title: China copper downstream activity expanded for a 4th straight month in December-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM survey data show Chinese copper downstream activity expanded for a fourth straight month in December, led by stronger electronics, home appliances and auto output/restocking, despite slower growth and weather/smog disruptions. New export orders improved amid US-China trade-talk progress. Copper purchasing prices rose as copper rallied on demand optimism and Beijing stimulus.

title: Copper rises on China policy easing, trade deal hopes
summary: London copper rose about 1% after China cut bank reserve requirements to release liquidity and support slowing growth. Investors also cheered hopes for a Jan. 15 U.S.-China Phase 1 trade deal. Chilean copper output fell, while nickel gained and aluminium was flat, reflecting mixed base-metals sentiment.

title: China copper outlook brightens with miners likely to shine most
summary: Chinese copper stocks are regaining favour as demand prospects brighten. The piece attributes earlier copper weakness to factors that have eased, including progress toward a US-China interim trade deal and stabilising Chinese economic data. Jiangxi Copper is highlighted for strong performance, suggesting improved near-term market sentiment for copper.

title: Union rejects restructure of nickel company in New Caledonia
summary: A New Caledonian union rejected Vale’s planned restructure of its nickel operations, arguing against redundancy plans and proposed nickel ore exports if refinery closure proceeds. Vale faces losses, has flagged closure of its nickel refinery, and put its stake up for sale, with speculation of Chinese interest in assets.

title: Utah copper mine seeks extension despite potential groundwater contamination
summary: A Utah copper mine (Lisbon Valley) is seeking permits to extend operations by using an experimental acid-based extraction process involving diluted sulfuric acid pumped underground. The company argues it is safe and could add at least 25 years of mine life, while environmentalists warn about possible groundwater contamination risk.

title: Mianhu Copper's 100,000 mt/year of copper rod capacity to come online in Jan-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: Jiangmen Mianhu Copper plans to begin batch charging and trial production of its 100,000 mt/year copper rod project on January 7, with facilities switched on in late December. The plant is currently in furnace drying, indicating incremental copper processing supply coming online shortly.

title: Shanghai aluminum slips to 2-week low; nickel dives
summary: Shanghai aluminum fell to a more-than-two-week low as Chinese consumer stocks rose, with inventories up and LME cash discounts widening on weaker near-term demand signals. Nickel also plunged, with London briefly down sharply and ShFE nickel hitting a multi-day low, reflecting broad risk-off metal pressure into January.

title: Shanghai aluminum slips to 2-week low; nickel dives
summary: Shanghai aluminum prices fell to a more than two-week low as Chinese aluminum inventories rose 18,000 tonnes and weak near-term demand signals appeared (wider cash-to-forward discount). Nickel “dived,” with ShFE nickel down around 2% to its lowest since mid-December. Copper was also slightly lower.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose 3,750 mt on week-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: Shanghai bonded-area copper inventories rose for a third straight week, up 3,750 mt from a week earlier to 247,750 mt as of Jan 3, according to SMM data. Higher stocks suggest improved near-term supply/availability in the physical market, which is typically a negative signal for copper prices.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports declined to 14.06 million wmt-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories across Chinese ports fell by 40,000 wmt to 14.06 million wmt in the week ended Jan 3. Stocks at seven major ports also declined to 11.19 million wmt. In metal content terms, inventories dropped to 120,300 mt.

title: Evening Comments (Jan 3): Copper dropped to 3-week low as Middle East tensions flared-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: Shanghai copper prices fell to a three-week low as Middle East tensions flared after a US air strike killed an Iranian official, prompting a risk-off move. The dollar strengthened and gold rose. SHFE nonferrous metals declined: copper -1%, nickel -2.9%, and aluminium -0.2%, with comments on inventories and technical levels.

title: Canada's First Quantum weighs $1 billion Zambian copper mine expansion -document
summary: First Quantum is weighing a roughly $1 billion expansion at Zambia’s Kansanshi copper mine to extend mine life and raise output over time to about 300,000 tonnes from 235,000 tonnes. Approval may hinge on changes to Zambia’s tax regime amid disputes and arbitration involving the state miner ZCCM-IH.

title: First Quantum weighs $1-billion copper mine expansion in Zambia
summary: First Quantum is considering a roughly $1 billion expansion at Zambia’s Kansanshi copper mine to extend mine life and lift production toward 300,000 tonnes from about 235,000 tonnes expected last year. Board approval may be delayed or require Zambia tax changes, but the planned output increase is copper-supportive.

title: First Quantum weighs $1-billion Zambian copper mine expansion, document reveals
summary: First Quantum is considering a roughly $1-billion expansion of Zambia’s Kansanshi copper mine to avert declining output, but board approval is likely hindered by a tax/royalty regime that includes higher copper royalties and new surcharges at high prices. Analysts expect investment may stall unless Zambia changes policy.

title: Here's Why Shares of Southern Copper Climbed 12% in December
summary: The article says Southern Copper shares rose in December largely alongside higher copper prices, with December’s average copper at $2.77 (highest since April). It also notes easing U.S.-China trade tensions, which analysts expect could support copper demand and prices, and a Peruvian permit for the Tia Maria project.

title: Exclusive: Canada's First Quantum weighs $1 billion Zambian copper mine expansion
summary: First Quantum is considering ~$1 billion to expand Zambia’s Kansanshi copper mine, which would raise output over time and extend mine life. However, disputes with the Zambian government over taxes/royalties and assets, including higher copper royalty taxes and new price-linked levies, could delay or prevent approval.

title: Copper near 8-month high on China data and trade deal hopes
summary: Copper prices rose to their highest since May on stronger China industrial profits and hopes of a phase-one US-China trade deal, supporting expectations for metals demand. LME copper stocks fell to the lowest since mid-March. Aluminium was also higher, while nickel showed a softer tone amid rising LME stocks.

title: £10m aluminium manufacturing process validated for high-volume automotive OEM applications
summary: A UK-funded 30-month project (RACEForm) validates Hot Form Quench technology for high-volume manufacturing of complex, lightweight aluminium automotive parts such as A-pillars and chassis assemblies. The process targets faster cycle times and enables greater use of highly recycled aluminium, potentially reducing smelting needs and embedded emissions.

title: SKC to complete takeover of world's top copper foil maker for $1b
summary: SKC Inc. said it will complete a $1 billion takeover of KCFT, the world’s top copper foil maker used as the negative electrode current collector in lithium-ion batteries. With major customers in EV battery supply chains, the acquisition is expected to expand mobility exposure and support copper-foil-linked demand outlook.

title: Evening Comments (Jan 3): Copper fell to 3-week low as Middle East tensions flared-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: Shanghai metals sold off on Friday as Middle East tensions flared after a US air strike killed a senior Iranian official. Investors moved to risk-off, lifting the dollar and safe havens. SHFE copper fell to a three-week low, nickel dropped nearly 3%, and aluminium slid slightly lower amid growing expected inventories.

title: China nickel downstream activity improved in December-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM says China’s nickel downstream manufacturing recovered in December: the downstream PMI rose to 49.51, with new orders in expansion (51.17) and stronger production. Stainless steel producers restocked on falling feedstock prices, supporting nickel demand and contributing to nickel and stainless-steel price stabilisation. January PMIs point to continued weakness.

title: London copper rebounds as Sino-U.S. trade deal nears
summary: London copper rebounded after a sharp prior drop, with gains linked to expectations that a U.S.-China Phase 1 trade deal is imminent and could lift demand. China policy easing and stronger December manufacturing also supported sentiment. The LME complex was mixed, with aluminium slipping while nickel was flat.

title: LME copper rebounds on China policy, Sino-U.S. trade truce
summary: London copper rose 0.5% as markets priced in China’s policy easing and the expected U.S.-China Phase 1 trade deal. China’s RRR cut and steady inflation target support hopes for firmer economic activity and metal demand, offsetting earlier declines tied to Middle East tensions and weak U.S. manufacturing data.

title: Atlantic Nickel Announces First Sale of Nickel Concentrate From Santa Rita
summary: Atlantic Nickel announced its first sale of nickel concentrate from the Santa Rita project. The news is interpreted as the start of concentrate deliveries, implying additional nickel supply potential. This can weigh on near-term nickel sentiment if the market expects a gradual build in availability.

title: PLN needs to triple electricity supply in Sulawesi to power nickel smelters
summary: PLN says it must nearly triple electricity supply in Central and Southeast Sulawesi to power nickel smelters being built under Indonesia’s domestic refinement rules. The utility plans major new coal power and grid integration to meet 1,556 MW additional demand, aiming to support timely smelter commissioning and nickel output growth.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 6): Copper fell on US-Iran tensions, China's weak service data-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous closed mixed: copper fell 0.63% as US-Iran tensions boosted safe-haven sentiment and China Caixin services data disappointed; aluminium rose 0.64% on slower primary aluminium inventory build and Inner Mongolia shipment disruptions. Nickel lagged down 1.8%, hovering near support/average with expectations of rangebound trading.

title: Copper rattled by soft China data and U.S.-Iran tensions
summary: Copper fell on Monday as softer China services growth signaled weaker demand and U.S.-Iran tensions drove a risk-off move, weighing on cyclical base metals. Aluminium weakened with cash discounts deepening and LME warehouse stocks rising, while nickel edged lower after a recent low.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 6): Copper fell on US-Iran tensions and China's weak service data-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM reports mostly lower SHFE nonferrous prices on Jan 6. Copper fell 0.63% as US-Iran tensions boosted safe-haven demand and China’s weak Caixin services data hurt sentiment. Aluminium rose 0.64% with weaker-than-expected primary inventory build from Inner Mongolia disruptions. Nickel edged down 1.8% and is seen rangebound.

title: USTKE union wary of New Caledonia nickel restructure
summary: A New Caledonian union warned about Vale’s planned restructure and sale of its nickel plant in New Caledonia. Vale intends to close the refinery and focus on nickel hydroxide cake for EV batteries, while selling assets and exporting nickel ore subject to approvals, increasing near-term supply and labor uncertainty.

title: CRU: USMCA Should Support Regional Aluminium Demand but not Without Complications and Risks
summary: The US Senate approved the USMCA trade agreement with Mexico and Canada by a large margin, sending it to President Trump for signature. CRU expects the pact to support regional aluminium demand, but notes potential complications and risks, implying only moderate, not guaranteed, near-term support for aluminium prices.

title: Atlantic Nickel to sell first concentrate from Brazil's Santa Rita project
summary: Atlantic Nickel has signed an offtake contract for part of production from its restarted Santa Rita nickel sulphide project in Brazil. The mine has completed refurbishment, ramped commissioning, and is set to deliver its first concentrate shipment this month, supporting higher near-term nickel supply.

title: Copper edges higher as investors take stock and look to China
summary: Copper prices edged higher as investors looked to China for continued stimulus and as U.S.-Iran tensions eased, stabilizing broader markets. LME copper inventories have fallen sharply to the lowest since March 2019. Aluminium was the only tracked metal down, with a wider cash discount suggesting ample near-term warehouse supply.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 7): Copper advanced on an absence of escalation in Middle East tensions-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM reports most SHFE nonferrous metals ending higher after no further US–Iran escalation reduced safe-haven demand; copper rose 0.41% and nickel 1.21%. Aluminium slipped slightly (-0.21%) but is described as supported by a softer US dollar and an elevated LME aluminium, keeping near-term prices high.

title: Copper closes higher as investors take stock and look to China
summary: Copper prices rose on easing U.S.-Iran tensions and expectations that China will extend stimulus to support growth and investment. LME three-month copper gained 0.2% and inventories fell sharply. Aluminium finished lower with a wider cash discount, while nickel rose 0.8% on the day.

title: Copper price unlikely to rebound even if trade tensions subside -Chile trade group
summary: Chile’s Sonami head says copper prices are unlikely to rebound in 2020 even if U.S.-China trade tensions ease. He expects demand not to rise significantly through 2020, keeping major miners cautious about boosting supply. Electric vehicle manufacturing is viewed as supportive in the mid-term, not immediately.

title: Copper output slumps at Codelco, BHP's Escondida in November
summary: Chile’s Cochilco said copper output fell at Codelco and BHP’s Escondida in November, amid riots and mass protests. Codelco output dropped 11% year-on-year to 155,200 tonnes. As major Chilean supply is disrupted, near-term copper availability expectations worsen, typically pressuring prices lower.

title: Atlantic takes third run at Santa Rita nickel
summary: The piece reports that Atlantic is making a third attempt related to the Santa Rita nickel project. Renewed progress on a nickel supply project can improve near-term expectations for future production, offering some support to nickel sentiment, though the exact timing and output impact are uncertain.

title: MEE: Examination over standards on recyclable copper, brass, aluminium raw materials has ended-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China’s MEE says its review of national standards for recyclable copper and aluminium scrap has ended. The rules reclassify eligible scrap that replaces solid-waste scrap, with compliant imports allowed without restrictions as solid-waste scrap import bans near end-2020. This should ease supply tightness for copper and aluminium.

title: MEE: Examination over standards on recyclable copper, brass, aluminium raw materials has ended-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China’s MEE says a review of standards for recyclable copper and aluminium scrap has ended. Scrap meeting the new criteria is expected to be allowed into China without restrictions, replacing “solid waste” treatment amid an end-2020 import ban. The change should affect scrap supply expectations and prices.

title: Review completed over standards on recyclable copper, brass and aluminium raw materials-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China’s ecology ministry says the nonferrous standards for recyclable copper and aluminium scrap have been reviewed, enabling scrap that meets the new criteria to enter China without restrictions as solid-waste imports are banned. This reclassification should improve near-term scrap supply for domestic processing, supporting copper and aluminium sentiment.

title: Review completed over standards on recyclable copper, brass and aluminium raw materials-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China’s environmental authorities said standards reviewing recyclable copper and aluminium scrap have been completed. The draft rules reclassify qualifying scrap as recyclable materials rather than “solid waste,” allowing foreign scrap that meets standards to be imported without restrictions, supporting scrap inflows ahead of the earlier broader waste import ban.

title: Copper price unlikely to rebound in 2020 forecasts Chile's mining union
summary: Chile’s Sonami leader says copper is unlikely to rebound meaningfully in 2020 even if US-China trade tensions ease. He expects prices around about $2.80/lb, citing weak demand prospects and miners’ caution on ramping supply. Electric vehicle demand is seen as supportive only mid-term.

title: Indonesia approves environmental study for battery-grade nickel plants -minister
summary: Indonesia approved environmental impact studies for battery-grade nickel chemical plants in Morowali, allowing investors to proceed with high-pressure acid leaching construction. The move supports expansion of Indonesia’s integrated nickel industry and follows a prior stop to unprocessed nickel ore exports, reinforcing nickel supply and demand expectations.

title: Auroch off and running on nickel hunt near Leinster
summary: Auroch Minerals reports further nickel assay results from its Saints project near Kalgoorlie, including 6.87m at 0.77% nickel and a higher-grade interval, with conductive zones identified by DHEM yet to be tested. The company plans additional drilling, alongside exploration at Leinster.

title: Arc Minerals intersects wide copper mineralisation in maiden drill programme at mine in Zambia
summary: Arc Minerals says its maiden drill programme at a Zambia mine intersected wide copper mineralisation. The reported results can strengthen market expectations for the project’s prospective copper resource and near-term supply outlook, typically supportive for copper sentiment over the coming days to weeks.

title: Max Resource Identifies Visible Copper Oxide Mineralization at Cesar
summary: Max Resource Corp. reports visible copper oxide mineralization (chrysocolla, malachite, azurite, etc.) at its Cesar copper-silver project in Colombia and expects assay results for chip samples. Prior grab samples ranged up to 4.2% copper. Phase II drilling is planned after assays, suggesting ongoing exploration but no production impact.

title: Excelsior Mining Announces Positive Initial Wellfield Results at the Gunnison Copper Project
summary: Excelsior Mining announced initial wellfield results at its Gunnison in-situ copper project, saying copper recovery grades exceed feasibility expectations. Pregnant leach solution copper measurements are ahead of schedule, with acid injection ramping toward full rate and first copper cathode sales expected in Q1 2020.

title: China issued 2nd batch of copper scrap import quotas for 2020-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China’s environmental authorities approved a second batch of 2020 copper scrap import quotas (26,566 mt of high-grade scrap), adding to first-quarter allowances and easing concerns of supply disruption before end-year solid waste import restrictions. Additional standards to ease qualified scrap imports and shifts to remelt ingot also support copper availability.

title: A visit to Germany′s only remaining aluminum factory | Business| Economy and finance news from a German perspective | DW
summary: DW visits Germany’s only remaining aluminum-oxide plant in Stade, which ships bauxite from Guinea. It notes aluminum-oxide production is highly energy-intensive and raises concerns that further energy-price hikes from Germany’s renewables transition could threaten domestic aluminum output. It also describes competition from abroad.

title: Q&A: making nickel mining greener with Norilsk
summary: The Q&A discusses Nornickel’s efforts to reduce sulphur dioxide emissions by cutting back and eventually shutting old nickel smelting operations, and to capture emissions at its copper facilities while shutting a copper smelter without production loss. It also plans to supply nickel/cobalt for BASF-made EV batteries, aiming for more demand diversification.

title: DEQ fines The Dalles aluminum recycler $1.3 million
summary: Oregon DEQ fined Hydro Extrusion USA, part of Norsk Hydro, $1.3 million for air quality permit violations at an aluminum recycling facility. The plant processed prohibited “unclean” scrap and failed monitoring and recordkeeping. DEQ ordered it to stop and improve compliance, while penalty includes avoided pollution-control costs.

title: State regulators issue largest-ever air pollution fine to The Dalles aluminum recycler
summary: Oregon regulators fined Hydro Extrusion USA, an aluminum recycler owned by Norsk Hydro, $1.3 million for air pollution permit violations tied to improper melting of coated “unclean charge” materials. The firm must stop the prohibited processing, upgrade monitoring, and improve emissions controls, with an appeal deadline.

title: Strengthening dollar curbs Copper rebound | Regina Leader-Post
summary: Copper was set for about a 1% weekly gain as fears of U.S.-Iran conflict eased and LME/SHFE inventories continued to fall, supporting prices. However, a strengthening dollar reduced demand and limited upside momentum. The piece also notes smaller weekly moves in aluminium and nickel without new drivers for them.

title: Oregon DEQ Issues Its Largest Air Quality Fine To Aluminum Recycler
summary: Oregon DEQ fined Hydro Extrusion, an aluminum recycling plant in The Dalles, $1.3 million for air-permit violations. The facility melted unpermitted coated scrap and failed to properly track incoming recycled material. The company may appeal within 20 days, but no broader market disruption is stated.

title: 3 Canadian Copper Stocks Set to Shine in 2020?
summary: Canaccord Genuity highlights a promising 2020 environment for industrial commodities, citing global monetary/fiscal stimulus and progress toward a U.S.-China Phase 2 trade deal. It favors copper and lists Canadian copper stocks as top picks. Turquoise Hill, First Quantum, and Ero Copper are discussed, including Ero’s nickel-copper “super-pods” samples.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 10): Copper rose on bullish outlook for US non-farm payrolls-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous prices mostly higher: copper +0.06%, nickel +1.07% and aluminium +0.5%. Gains are attributed to improved risk appetite ahead of US non-farm payrolls and expectations of stronger Chinese demand after a US-China preliminary trade deal is to be signed next week.

title: 42-year-old man arrested, charged with TPCO copper theft
summary: A man was charged with stealing copper from TPCO Industries after authorities received a tip about large copper-wire sales at salvage yards. Police seized about 6,000 pounds of copper valued around $93,000. The sheriff said copper theft is a costly, widespread problem for U.S. businesses.

title: Portland man accused of stealing $93K of copper from TPCO near Gregory
summary: Authorities accused a Portland man of stealing about 2,000 pounds of thick-gauge copper worth roughly $93,000 from TPCO America near Gregory. Investigators linked the alleged theft to salvage yard sales and confirmed the loss through an inventory check, along with finding related spools at the suspect’s home.

title: Authorities search for copper thief
summary: Craighead County authorities in Arkansas are investigating theft of wire from a Craighead Electric substation after reports of a cut fence and stolen copper-infused wire. Deputies have no suspects and believe the theft occurred within two weeks. The case may affect local replacement needs, but likely not wider copper pricing.

title: Emirates Global Aluminium signs deal with Indonesian competitor
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) signed an agreement with Indonesia’s Inalum/PT Indonesia Asahan Aluminium to license smelting technology and cooperate on a new “greenfield” aluminium smelter and upgrades. Cooperation includes secondment for reduction cell modelling and potential wider use of EGA technology in Indonesia, supporting aluminium supply expectations.

title: Copper eases ahead of U.S.-China trade deal signing
summary: Copper prices edged down as investors stayed cautious ahead of the Wednesday signing of the U.S.-China Phase 1 trade deal that should ease the 18-month trade dispute. LME copper fell 0.1%, while LME aluminum declined and nickel rose slightly, indicating muted, sentiment-led moves rather than fundamentals shock.

title: London copper rises ahead of U.S.-China trade deal
summary: London three-month copper rose 0.4% to about $6,222/tonne, extending a six-day rally ahead of a U.S.-China Phase 1 trade deal. Gains were modest as investors awaited China macro data. Other base metals were mostly range-bound, with aluminium slightly down and nickel slightly up.

title: London copper rises ahead of U.S.-China trade deal | The London Free Press
summary: Copper prices rose on Monday on expectations of a forthcoming U.S.-China Phase 1 trade deal later in the week, extending LME copper’s gains. However, gains were limited as investors awaited China’s macro data. The base-metal complex was mostly range-bound, with aluminium slightly down and nickel up.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 13): Copper flat ahead of US-China trade deal signing-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM reports mixed SHFE nonferrous performance ahead of the US-China Phase One trade deal signing. Copper was flat as trade optimism was offset by weaker-than-expected US payroll data and ongoing US-Iran risks. Aluminium fell on increased social inventories. Nickel rose on aggressive long buildup and rising open interest.

title: Recyclable copper, brass, aluminium alloy casting raw materials standards to come into force in July-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China will implement from July 1 new national standards for recyclable copper, brass, and aluminium alloy casting raw materials. The rules reclassify eligible scrap away from “solid waste,” enabling compliant foreign copper and aluminium scrap to enter without restrictions ahead of a full scrap import ban by end-2020, with details due shortly.

title: Recyclable copper, brass, aluminium alloy casting raw materials standards to come into force in July-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China will implement national standards for recyclable copper, brass, and aluminium alloy casting raw materials from July 1. The rules reclassify scrap previously treated as solid waste, aligning with a complete ban on such imports by end-2020. Foreign copper and aluminium scrap meeting standards can enter without restrictions.

title: China's new copper, aluminium scrap standards to take effect from July 1
summary: China’s CMRA said new standards for high-grade copper and aluminium scrap will start on July 1. Scrap meeting the standards may be reclassified as a resource and enter China without restrictions, potentially easing import limits. Companies importing restricted scrap before then need quotas, and minimum metal content is unclear.

title: China's new copper, aluminium scrap standards to take effect from July 1
summary: China will implement new CMRA standards for high-grade copper and aluminium scrap from July 1, based on a market-regulator approved document. Scrap meeting the criteria could be reclassified as a resource and imported without restrictions, reducing solid-waste imports. Minimum metal content remains unclear and quotas are needed before July 1.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Announces 2019 Production and Provides Three-Year Guidance
summary: Copper Mountain Mining reported Q4 2019 and full-year 2019 copper production of 72.0 million pounds and issued 2020 guidance for 86–96 million pounds of copper, citing improved grades and lower strip needs. It also guided 2020 C1 cash costs of US$1.30–1.45 per pound and highlighted concentrator expansion.

title: High Purity Alumina Market Will Reflect Significant Growth Prospects during 2025
summary: The piece projects significant growth prospects for the high purity alumina market in 2025. Because high purity alumina is an upstream input feeding parts of the aluminium value chain, the outlook can influence short-term expectations for aluminium supply/demand balance. Directionally, it is supportive for aluminium prices.

title: MN court rejects 2 major permits for PolyMet copper-nickel mine
summary: A Minnesota court rejected two major permits for PolyMet’s planned copper-nickel mine. The decision likely delays development and increases uncertainty over future output, tightening near-term supply expectations. That typically pressures both copper and nickel prices downward in the following days as market participants reassess project timelines.

title: MN court rejects 2 major permits for PolyMet copper-nickel mine
summary: A Minnesota court rejected two major permits for PolyMet’s copper-nickel mine, raising the likelihood of delays or additional hurdles before production can proceed. The decision increases near-term supply uncertainty for copper and nickel, which typically pressures prices downward in the days following the news.

title: Standards for recyclable copper, brass, aluminium alloy casting raw materials to be in force in July-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China will implement national standards for recyclable copper, brass and aluminium alloy casting raw materials from July 1. The move reclassifies scrap previously treated as “solid waste,” aligning with an import ban scheduled by end-2020. Foreign copper and aluminium scrap meeting the standards can enter China without restrictions, potentially tightening supply concerns.

title: Standards for recyclable copper, brass, aluminium alloy casting raw materials to be in force in July-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China will implement from July 1 new national standards for recyclable copper and aluminium alloy casting raw materials and brass. The rules reclassify approved scrap to replace solid waste, enabling foreign compliant copper and aluminium scrap imports without restrictions, as China’s broader scrap import bans approach end-2020.

title: China copper concentrate imports rose 11.6% in 2019-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: China’s copper concentrate imports rose 11.6% in 2019, reaching 21.99 million mt versus 19.7 million mt in 2018. In December, concentrate imports were 1.93 million mt, down from November’s record 2.16 million mt but up 31.8% year-on-year. Unwrought copper imports also rose.

title: China's unwrought copper and copper product imports 6% lower in 2019-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: Shanghai Metals Market reports China’s December imports of unwrought copper and copper products were 530,000 mt, up 22.8% year-on-year versus December 2018 and higher than November. But total 2019 full-year imports were 4.98 million mt, 6% lower than 2018, signaling softer overall demand.

title: Court rejects PolyMet permits, inflaming fight over copper-nickel mining
summary: A court rejected PolyMet’s permits, intensifying legal conflict over a proposed copper-nickel mine. The decision raises the risk of delays or curtailed development, which can tighten expected near-term supply and therefore support bullish sentiment for both copper and nickel prices over coming days.

title: China Dec copper imports hit highest since March 2016; annual shipments fall
summary: China’s December unwrought copper imports rose 9.1% to 527,000 tonnes, the highest since March 2016, aided by improved industrial activity, power/auto demand, favorable price arbitrage, and tighter scrap imports that may require additional copper inputs. Annual copper imports fell, but concentrate imports increased, supporting smelter demand. Aluminium exports also rose.

title: Clean Water Advocates Applaud Halt of Key PolyMet Permits For Copper-Nickel Mine
summary: Clean water advocates say they have halted key Polymet mine permits. The Polymet project is associated with both copper and nickel production, so permit delays can push out development timelines and increase near-term uncertainty about future supply, a backdrop that would typically pressure copper and nickel prices.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 14): Copper rose ahead of US-China trade deal-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM says SHFE nonferrous prices were mixed: copper rose 0.8% on hopes for a US-China phase-one trade deal and eased US-Iran concerns, plus bullish positioning; aluminium fell 0.54% as downstream production suspensions worsened demand pessimism; nickel slumped 3.19% on long exits and technical weakness.

title: Emirates Global Aluminium inks MoU with INALUM to build aluminium smelter
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) signed an MoU with Indonesia’s INALUM to license EGA aluminium smelting technology and support expansion of INALUM’s existing smelter and construction of a new one in Indonesia. The deal signals potential future supply growth, but it is non-binding and near-term output is unclear.

title: Rockcliff to Complete 70,000 Metre Drill Program on Copper Properties in 2020
summary: Rockcliff Metals says it has recommenced a fully funded 2020 drill program, targeting 70,000 metres across advanced-stage and exploration copper projects (Tower, Rail, Talbot, and other properties). Samples from 2019 drilling are awaiting assays, and results are expected as they become available. No near-term production impact is stated.

title: The Northern Miner Podcast – episode 169: Prospects for nickel industry better than ever, ft  Atlantic Nickel CEO Paulo Castellari
summary: The Northern Miner podcast discusses Atlantic Nickel’s Santa Rita nickel project in Brazil. Atlantic Nickel has sold its first nickel concentrate and signed a three-year offtake deal with Trafigura. The episode contrasts current prospects with the mine’s prior shutdown in 2015 due to low prices and high costs.

title: Another spin of the giant LME aluminum stocks carousel: Andy Home
summary: LME-registered aluminium stocks jumped 58% to 1.49 million tonnes, with hundreds of thousands of tonnes earmarked for physical load-out and rising daily departures. The piece links the inventory carousel to tightening cash–three-month spreads, futures/physical incentives, and upcoming LME warehousing reforms including load-out queues, rental terms, and off-warrant reporting.

title: Metro Train Delayed? Don't Rule Out Copper Bandits Stealing Wiring From The Tracks
summary: Los Angeles Metro reports thieves are damaging signal and traction power equipment to steal copper wiring, causing service disruptions and costly, time-consuming repairs. The agency has increased security, improved copper traceability, and alerts scrap yards, but officials call the crimes occasional, limiting likely global copper price impact.

title: M&As in the copper space could surge in 2020, especially if Chinese companies come to the party
summary: The article says copper prices are rising to an eight-month high as the U.S. and China prepare a trade deal. It also notes copper open interest is increasing rapidly and analysts expect more copper-sector M&A, while supply is seen as relatively weak, supporting near-term bullish sentiment for copper.

title: London copper falls as U.S. to keep tariffs on Chinese goods
summary: London copper fell after investors retraced a rally tied to hopes for a U.S.-China Phase 1 trade deal, as Mnuchin said tariffs will remain. Traders cited profit-taking and doubts about demand recovery. Three-month copper dropped 0.7% while LME aluminium was slightly lower and nickel slightly higher amid mixed inventory signals.

title: Why Europe must safeguard and promote a greener, circular and innovative aluminium value chain
summary: The article urges Europe to safeguard its aluminium value chain by expanding recycling, maintaining primary smelting capacity, and reducing reliance on higher-carbon imports. It highlights high EU electricity costs driving capacity loss and calls for state aid/ETS indirect cost compensation and trade measures, which could support near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Initial drilling confirms presence of high-grade bauxite occurrence at Lindian Resources' Gaoual project
summary: Lindian’s drilling at the Gaoual bauxite project in Guinea confirmed high-grade conglomerate bauxite, with indicative average aluminium oxide grades above 60% from partially completed holes. Rig issues are delaying depth confirmation, but spare parts and a second rig are expected within the fortnight, supporting positive aluminium feedstock sentiment.

title: Can Alcoa Beat Consensus For FY 2019 Amidst the Fall In Alumina And Aluminum Prices?
summary: The piece says Alcoa’s FY2019 revenue is expected to fall due to sharp declines in alumina and aluminum prices. It attributes alumina weakness to excess supply and lower demand, while aluminum pricing is pressured by Chinese export growth of semi products despite a deficit. These factors link directly to aluminum price trends.

title: China-invested Letpadaung copper mine brings tangible benefits to Sagaing Region, Myanmar
summary: China’s Wanbao Mining’s Letpadaung copper mine in Myanmar is described as one of Asia’s largest copper hydrometallurgy projects, with cathode output exceeding 100,000 tonnes in 2018 and reaching about 120,000 tonnes in 2019. The report emphasizes production capability and ongoing operations, supporting copper supply expectations.

title: Ero Copper produces 42,318 tonnes of copper in 2019 and provides 2020 production outlook
summary: Ero Copper reported 2019 copper production of 42,318 tonnes at its Curaçá Valley in Brazil, up 39% from 2018, exceeding guidance. It also issued 2020 guidance of 41,000–43,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate and reiterated low C1 cash cost assumptions, suggesting improving supply outlook and cost discipline.

title: Copper: Set to Shine in 2020 and Beyond - Investing Daily
summary: The piece forecasts a large copper demand surge from renewables and electric vehicles, citing higher copper intensity per unit of power and charging infrastructure. It also warns that declining ore grades make copper production more energy-intensive, potentially tightening supply. It concludes copper prices are likely to rise.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 15): Caution over US-China trade deal capped copper increase-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM reports SHFE copper edged up but gains were capped as US-China trade deal concerns persist: Mnuchin said tariffs remain, potentially limiting upside. Aluminium rose slightly, but the outlook is pressured by weaker pre-holiday demand and rising aluminium ingot inventories as producers switch to ingot output.

title: Aluminum Association Applauds Phase One China Trade Deal; Calls for Addressing Structural Subsidies in Phase Two
summary: The Aluminum Association praised the U.S.-China Phase One trade deal but urged Phase Two talks to tackle China’s subsidized aluminum overcapacity. It cites OECD findings on large state subsidies, notes China’s aluminum overcapacity growth and expanding exports to third countries, and argues this distorts the global aluminum market.

title: It's a conglomerate ! Lindian unearths lucrative bauxite deposit
summary: Lindian Resources reports early drilling results confirming a high-grade “conglomerate style” bauxite deposit at its Gaoual project in Guinea, with aluminium oxide grades around 61% and low iron and silica. Drilling will resume after rig failure. If confirmed at scale, it could support aluminium supply sentiment.

title: Alcoa misses views, expects a global aluminum surplus for 2020
summary: Alcoa reported a larger-than-expected Q4 loss and weaker sales, and said it will close one alumina refinery. Importantly, the company projected a global aluminium surplus for 2020 and a balanced alumina market, with bauxite also expected to be slightly oversupplied, signaling softer aluminium fundamentals.

title: Sasol expands alumina spheres production capacity in Germany
summary: Sasol plans to expand its alumina spheres production capacity in Germany. Because alumina is a major feedstock for aluminium smelters, incremental alumina output can improve availability and potentially reduce input tightness. The article provides limited detail on timing or volumes, so the near-term effect is likely moderate.

title: Alcoa sees aluminum swing to surplus after fourth quarterly loss
summary: Alcoa says aluminum is set to swing into surplus after recording its fourth quarterly loss. The company’s outlook points to easing market tightness and potentially weaker demand/supply balances, which can pressure expectations for near-term aluminum prices.

title: Goldfields nickel-cobalt project now the firm focus for Ardea Resources
summary: The West Australian reports that Ardea Resources is making its Goldfields nickel-cobalt project the firm focus. The news is relevant to nickel via potential future supply, but the provided information does not indicate any immediate change in production timing, output, or constraints that would likely move prices in the next weeks.

title: Copper eases after U.S.-China trade deal as doubts linger
summary: Copper prices slipped after the U.S.-China Phase 1 trade deal as investors doubted it would materially lift metals demand. LME three-month copper eased 0.1% and ShFE copper 0.2%. LME inventories hit a 10-month low, but spreads widened, suggesting no urgent supply shortage. Aluminium rose slightly; nickel traded mixed across exchanges.

title: McCollum introduces bill to protect the Boundary Waters from sulfide-ore copper mining
summary: Minnesota Rep. Betty McCollum introduced a bill to permanently protect the Boundary Waters from sulfide-ore mining, targeting a ban on sulfide-ore extraction in parts of the Superior National Forest and the Rainy River Watershed. The concern is acid drainage harming water quality, with Twin Metals’ proposed mine facing opposition.

title: Primary aluminium inventories rose 20,000 mt on week-Shanghai Metals Market
summary: SMM data show China’s social inventories of primary aluminium across eight consumption areas rose by about 20,000 mt in the week ended Jan 16 to 630,000 mt. The increase reflects higher arrivals and broadly weaker consumption, following a small prior uptick after a longer downtrend.

title: Regulus Reports Additional Drill Results at the AntaKori Copper-Gold Project Including:
summary: Regulus reports new drill intersections at its AntaKori copper-gold project in Peru, including long intervals of ~0.4–0.6% Cu and sections with higher copper grades. The company says results extend and infill mineralization and open new targets, potentially supporting positive sentiment for future copper supply.

title: ETFs to play copper's expected comeback in the global shift to a low-carbon economy
summary: The piece highlights expected copper demand growth from the low-carbon transition, citing renewables and electric vehicles as copper-intensive. It notes past ETF availability and current limited ETP options tracking copper miners or futures, while stating copper has rebounded but remains volatile. Overall, the outlook is framed bullish for copper.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Update on Operations and Ramp-Up of Pumpkin Hollow Underground Mine
summary: The (partially provided) news item is titled as an operational update from Nevada Copper, describing a ramp-up at the Pumpkin Hollow underground mine. Such mine ramp-up typically influences expectations for near-term copper supply and may support copper prices, though specific production figures and timing are not shown in the text provided.

title: Copper Futures Unlock 8-Month High; Positive Momentum Increases
summary: Copper March futures rose to an eight-month high around 2.8794, breaking out of a squeeze Bollinger Band. Technical momentum is positive (RSI rising toward 70; MACD above its trigger). Resistance is noted near 2.9180, with further upside levels at 2.9645 and 2.9930; support sits near 2.8530 and 2.8194.

title: Bill would prohibit copper-nickel mining upstream of BWCAW
summary: Minnesota Rep. Betty McCollum introduced H.R. 5598 to permanently withdraw about 234,000 acres upstream of the Boundary Waters Canoe Area from mineral leasing for sulfide-based copper-nickel mining. The bill faces long odds and potential veto, but it would constrain potential output from projects like Twin Metals.

title: Bill would prohibit copper-nickel mining upstream of BWCAW
summary: Minnesota Rep. Betty McCollum introduced H.R. 5598 to permanently withdraw about 234,000 acres from federal mineral leasing for sulfide-based minerals in the Rainy River watershed upstream of the BWCAW. The measure targets copper-nickel mining plans such as Twin Metals, though passage and veto prospects are uncertain.

title: Column: LME stock surge grounds high-flying nickel, but for how long?
summary: LME registered nickel inventories have more than doubled to about 183,000 tonnes after earlier depletion, while the cash-to-3-months premium has shifted from extreme backwardation to contango. This weakens the nickel bull narrative by easing imminent shortage concerns, supported by strong Indonesia-related ore and ferronickel imports.

title: Zambia plans to compel copper miners to account for gold
summary: Zambia plans to require copper miners to declare the gold contained in copper blisters or cathodes to improve mineral revenue, arguing gold has been hidden and underreported. Only one major mine has declared gold so far. The move also includes investment and buying centres for gold.

title: Rio Tinto reiterates Tiwai position as aluminium prices stay weak
summary: Rio Tinto reiterated its position on the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter, lobbying for cheaper energy as the business struggles with low profitability. The company described challenging global conditions and noted aluminium prices staying weak, reinforcing bearish expectations for the metal in the near term.

title: China, Indonesia sign $695m deal for West Kalimantan alumina smelter
summary: China and Indonesia signed a $695m contract to build the Mempawah alumina refinery in West Kalimantan. The project is expected to produce 1m tons of alumina annually and feed Indonesia Asahan Aluminium for ingot production. It aligns with Indonesia’s ore export ban and import replacement goals.

title: CRU: Copper Concentrates - Key Themes for 2020
summary: CRU highlights 2020 themes for the copper concentrates market: elevated disruption risk in Chile due to strikes/labour negotiations and potential unrest, drought-driven cost/output impacts across mining regions, and Chinese smelter closures as losses mount. These factors point to tighter copper material availability and support copper prices.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks inched up 400 mt on week
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories rose by about 400 mt in the week to Jan 17 to 18,100 mt, while nickel briquettes slipped to 3,300 mt. Arrivals for December orders offset domestic deliveries, and several hundred tonnes of Sumitomo nickel entered domestic markets, with average import losses easing versus last week.

title: Rockcliff Expands Copper Mineralization Below the Rail Deposit with Results of 13.65% CuEq Across 2.40 Metres and 10.57% CuEq Across 2.03 Metres
summary: Rockcliff Metals reports additional drill core assays from its Rail polymetallic sulphide deposit in Manitoba, identifying expanded high-grade copper mineralization. It cites significant CuEq intercepts and notes a 2020 expansion drill program and a planned PEA in Q2 2020, supporting expectations for future copper supply.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose 7,000 mt on week
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose by 7,000 mt to 272,000 mt as of Jan 17, extending a five-week run of weekly gains. SMM data attributes the buildup to continued import losses and record December copper cathode imports, with more cargoes moved into bonded warehouses on low prices. Holiday-thinned trading should support further stock growth.

title: D. Mark Appleby: Early Warning Report Issued Pursuant to National Instrument 62-103 in Relation to Tartisan Nickel Corp.
summary: An early warning report states that D. Mark Appleby acquired additional shares of Tartisan Nickel Corp., increasing his stake from about 8.9% to 11.1%. The filing is for investment purposes and does not mention production, supply, or other fundamentals that would immediately move nickel prices.

title: Pacific Ridge Announces Gold-Copper Acquisition in British Columbia
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration signed an earn-in agreement to acquire up to a 75% interest in the Kliyul and Redton copper-gold porphyry projects in British Columbia, subject to regulatory approval. The release outlines geological potential and planned exploration spending but does not mention production or immediate supply impacts.

title: Trade War Has Copper Prices Artificially Low, Chile Minister Says
summary: Chile’s minister says the trade war has pushed copper prices “artificially low,” suggesting the market is mispricing copper relative to underlying conditions. That commentary can influence near-term expectations for copper demand/supply balance and prompt a modest upward price bias over the coming days.

title: Unions promote nationalism as copper miners strike approaches 100 days
summary: Unions say nearly 1,800 Asarco copper miners at five Arizona and Texas mines and a processing plant have been on strike for almost 100 days over pension and healthcare cuts. Asarco continues partial output with strikebreakers, but the disruption raises short-term supply concerns for copper.

title: GCC countries produced 5.7mln tonnes of aluminium in 2019
summary: GCC primary aluminium producers produced 5.77 million tonnes of high-quality primary aluminium in 2019, up about 363,600 tonnes year-on-year, mainly due to expansion at Aluminium Bahrain’s Line 6. The region exports a significant share of production, supporting its role in global aluminium demand.

title: London copper steady on solid China data; volumes dip ahead of long holiday
summary: London copper held steady near an eight-month high on firm China industrial output, retail sales and investment data, though volumes were thin before the Lunar New Year holiday. Copper on ShFE eased as trade slowed. LME aluminum and SHFE aluminum fell slightly; nickel declined on SHFE, implying limited net directional pressure.

title: Primary aluminium inventories rose 21,000 mt over weekend
summary: SMM data show China’s social inventories of primary aluminium across eight consumption areas rose 21,000 mt from Jan 16 to 651,000 mt as of Jan 20. The build was driven by concentrated arrivals and softer consumption ahead of Lunar New Year holidays, suggesting near-term bearish pressure for aluminium.

title: Indonesia tightens grip on nickel and coal exports
summary: Indonesia’s Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry regulation bans nickel ore exports starting in January and requires domestic processing before overseas shipments. The government also tightens oversight via digital monitoring systems. Given Indonesia’s role as a major exporter, the policy risks near-term nickel ore supply tightness and price support.

title: Budget 2020: Stainless Steel Sector Seeks Zero Duty On Ferro-Nickel, Scrap -
summary: India’s stainless steel industry group ISSDA is asking the government, ahead of the FY2020-21 budget, to set zero import duty on ferro-nickel and stainless steel scrap. It argues ferro-nickel isn’t produced domestically and must be imported; current basic customs duty is 2.5%.

title: Asarco strike poses need for international unity of US and Mexican copper miners
summary: Asarco’s 1,800 copper miners have been on strike for months at facilities in Arizona and Texas while opposing major health-care cost increases, pay freezes, and pension attacks. The work stoppage is expected to reduce near-term copper supply, supporting supportive price expectations in the coming weeks.

title: China, RI sign $695m deal for W. Kalimantan alumina smelter
summary: Indonesian and Chinese firms signed a $695m contract to build the Mempawah alumina refinery in West Kalimantan. The project is expected to produce 1m tons of alumina annually and replace part of Inalum’s alumina imports, supporting domestic refining and eventual aluminium output as export bans push value-add.

title: London copper steady around 8-month high on solid China data
summary: London copper rose to an eight-month high after solid China industrial output and retail sales data lifted demand sentiment, though volumes were light ahead of Lunar New Year. LME aluminium inched up, while LME nickel fell slightly. China’s scrap standards add detail but not an immediate shock.

title: 649m copper hit for Hot Chili in Chile
summary: Hot Chili reports a new 649-meter diamond drill intersection at its Cortadera porphyry copper-gold discovery in Chile, including 440 meters at 0.5% copper. The result extends the Cuerpo-3 zone and is part of an expanding drilling program toward a mid-year resource estimate.

title: Good morning Vietnam – Blackstone hits 60m nickel zone
summary: Blackstone Minerals announced its best drill results to date at the Ta Khoa nickel project in Vietnam, including 60m at 1.3% nickel and additional high-grade intersections. The zone is described as near-surface and large-scale, with copper also reported within the mineralised interval, boosting nickel outlook.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 20): Copper lower amid holiday-thinned volumes
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals mostly closed lower Monday as liquidity thinned ahead of the Jan 24 Chinese New Year holiday. Copper fell 0.47% with technical softness, though PBOC reverse repos supported sentiment. Aluminium dropped 0.49% on weakened demand, and nickel declined 1.44% and stayed rangebound.

title: Doubleview Capital Corp.: Doubleview Announces New Discovery at Hat Gold Copper Porphyry Located at South Extension of the Lisle Deposit
summary: Doubleview Capital reports a new mineralized zone south of the Lisle deposit at its Hat gold-copper porphyry project. Drill results show sulphide mineralization with chalcopyrite/magnetite intercepts and higher intensity with depth; assays for copper/gold/cobalt are pending. It’s an exploration discovery without production implications.

title: PolarX identifies extension to copper-gold skarn
summary: PolarX says fieldwork at Alaska’s Zachly East Skarn suggests a potential 600-metre extension to a copper-gold mineralised system. Trenching found anomalous copper zones and prior drilling intersected grades around 0.6% copper with gold. The work may support further exploration targeting across a broader corridor.

title: BHP and Chinese miner buy up Western Areas nickel supply
summary: Western Areas has won new short-term contracts to supply high-grade nickel concentrate from its Forrestania operations to BHP’s Nickel West and China’s Jinchuan. The tendering was driven by optimism that nickel prices will keep rising, supported by battery-related demand for nickel.

title: China nickel ore imports fell for 3 months
summary: China’s imports of nickel ore and concentrate fell for a third straight month in December, down 27.9% from November. Imports are set to keep declining in January as Indonesia’s export ban takes effect. Demand disruption followed an earlier Indonesian export halt, while Philippines supply also remains constrained by the rainy season.

title: Weir Minerals makes savings at Philippines gold and copper mine
summary: Weir Minerals installed 19 Cavex hydrocyclones at OceanaGold’s Didipio gold and copper mine in the Philippines. The retrofit reduced circulating load from about 620% to 374%, cutting power, grinding media, and maintenance costs by over US$815,000 annually while enabling higher throughput and maintaining grind size.

title: Group Ten Metals Inc.: Group Ten Drills 399 Meters of Continuous Palladium, Platinum, Gold, Nickel, Copper and Cobalt Mineralization from Surface in the Camp Target Area at Stillwater West
summary: Group Ten Metals reported 2019 drill results at its Stillwater West PGE-Ni-Cu project, including 399m of continuous nickel-equivalent mineralization with associated copper values. The company says the results expand known Platreef-style PGE-Ni-Cu-Co mineralization, supporting incremental short-term optimism for nickel and copper supply potential.

title: Max Resource Expands Footprint with 1.4 km Stratabound Copper-Silver Horizon Discovery Open in Both Directions
summary: Max Resource Corp. reports a new 1.4 km stratabound copper-silver horizon at its 100% owned Cesar project in Colombia, with highlighted rock chip assays including up to 2.7% copper over 0.5m. The company plans follow-up sampling to expand the horizon, but there is no production impact described.

title: Western Areas to supply nickel to BHP'S unit and Jinchuan
summary: Western Areas secured new contracts to sell 10,000 tpa nickel concentrate to BHP’s Nickel West and 10,000 tpa to China’s Jinchuan for two years with an extension option. It ends an existing Tsingshan supply by month-end. The agreements support smelter feedstock continuity for nickel.

title: Global output drop fails to disperse aluminum gloom: Andy Home
summary: Global aluminum production fell 1% in 2019, but LME prices stayed weak around a two-and-a-half-year low, reflecting poor demand and expectations that China’s production growth will resume. Analysts forecast renewed oversupply pressures, suggesting the market may need additional supply cuts to prevent further downside.

title: Centre agrees to restart Aluminum Park in Odisha
summary: The Centre agreed to restart the Angul Aluminium Park infrastructure upgrade project in Odisha after bottlenecks were addressed. Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan said the JV between NALCO and IDCO is expected to complete by July 2020, supported by central funding, aiming to boost aluminium industry competitiveness and jobs.

title: Atewa citizens stage demo, vow to sue gov't over bauxite mining in Atewa Forest
summary: Residents protest plans to mine bauxite in Ghana’s Atewa Forest Reserve and vow to sue the government if the project proceeds. They argue mining would harm water and livelihoods and call on authorities to exclude the area from the government’s Syinihydro deal, amid international criticism of the $2 billion Chinese infrastructure plan.

title: BHP ups copper output despite Chile social unrest
summary: BHP reportedly plans to boost copper production in Chile even as social unrest raises disruption concerns. By indicating output resilience or improved operations despite unrest, the update implies tighter near-term copper supply risk, which can reduce any upward risk premium and weigh on copper prices.

title: Bloc wants to slow down adoption of new NAFTA deal because of aluminum concerns
summary: The Bloc Quebecois plans to block fast-track ratification of the updated NAFTA deal, citing insufficient protections for Quebec’s aluminum industry compared with steel. Ratification could be delayed in Canada while the agreement is studied and debated. The U.S. and Mexico have already advanced their steps, raising near-term aluminum trade uncertainty.

title: RI tightens grip on nickel and coal exports
summary: Indonesia’s regulation bans nickel ore exports to force downstream processing, while monitoring is tightened via digital systems. However, the Philippines’ BARMM region has indefinitely suspended nickel extraction, potentially removing 100–150 kt of supply. With downstreaming delayed by execution, near-term nickel supply expectations look vulnerable.

title: Theft of copper cable: Humboldt RCMP
summary: Police in Humboldt RCMP report a theft of more than $5,000 worth of copper cable from construction equipment in Middle Lake, Saskatchewan. Two males allegedly stole the copper from a business yard. The incident is localized and involves a small volume, so it is unlikely to influence copper prices meaningfully in the near term.

title: Bloc won't fast-track new NAFTA deal due to aluminum concerns
summary: Canada’s Bloc Quebecois says it will not fast-track ratification of the updated NAFTA, citing insufficient protections for Quebec’s aluminum industry compared with steel. The party may stall approval in a minority Parliament while reviewing the agreement. The U.S. and Mexico have already moved forward, leaving Canada as the holdout.

title: Centre agrees to restart Angul Aluminum Park: Dharmendra Pradhan
summary: The Union government agreed to restart the infrastructure upgrade project for the Angul Aluminium Park in Odisha, after earlier delays and a decision to drop the project and refund the central grant. The upgrade is expected to enhance aluminium industry competitiveness and is targeted for completion by July 2020.

title: London copper hovers around 2-wk low as China virus spreads
summary: London copper stayed near a two-week low as LME-approved inventories jumped 38,700 tonnes and coronavirus fears spread beyond China. The benchmark three-month contract fell as much as 0.5% and was near unchanged by early trade. Aluminium fell slightly while nickel rose on the day, reflecting mixed macro impact.

title: Update: China nickel ore imports fell for 3 months
summary: China’s nickel ore and concentrate imports declined for a third straight month in December, down 27.9% from November, as buyers’ rush to ship before Indonesia’s export ban faded after an October halt. January imports are expected to keep falling due to the ban and ongoing rainy-season disruptions in the Philippines.

title: London copper hovers near 2-week low amid virus outbreak
summary: London copper hovered near a two-week low as the Wuhan coronavirus outbreak in China raised travel/consumption concerns and LME-approved copper inventories jumped by 38,700 tonnes to 162,925. LME three-month copper fell up to 0.5% and had a larger prior-session drop, reflecting bearish near-term sentiment.

title: London copper hovers around second week low as China virus spreads
summary: London copper hovered near a two-week low as LME inventories rose by 38,700 tonnes and coronavirus spread from China to other countries. LME three-month copper fell up to 0.5% and was near unchanged later, with overall metals sentiment weaker, while aluminium and nickel also moved amid risk concerns.

title: Antofagasta hit top end of copper guidance for 2019, backs 2020 targets
summary: Antofagasta reported operationally strong 2019 results, producing 770,000 metric tons of copper, at the top end of its revised guidance. The higher output came from increased production at its Los Pelambres, Centinela and Zaldivar mines. The company also backed its 2020 targets.

title: Antofagasta 2019 Copper Production Up 6.2%; Backs 2020 Copper Production View
summary: Antofagasta reported 2019 copper production of 770,000 tonnes, up 6.2% year-on-year, citing higher output at Los Pelambres, Centinela and Zaldívar. Q4 volumes fell due to planned maintenance, lower grades and disruptions from Chilean fuel deliveries and a strike. 2020 copper guidance calls for 725-755 kt, 2-6% lower.

title: CRU: Future of Mount Isa Copper Smelter Open to Question
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says Kamoa Copper awarded Nerin Engineering the basic engineering contract for a planned 500,000 tpa direct-to-blister flash smelter at Kamoa-Kakula in the DRC. The project uses Metso Outotec technology and aims to process most of the complex’s concentrate, boosting in-country copper processing capacity.

title: AB InBev Boss Carlos Brito On Aluminum Tariffs
summary: AB InBev CEO Carlos Brito said progress on trade deals supports consumers, but “aluminum tariffs aren’t welcome.” Because beer cans use aluminum, tariffs act as an added tax on consumers and disadvantage domestic U.S. can purchasers. The headline implies weaker aluminum demand sentiment.

title: Copper touches 2-week low as virus death toll rises in China
summary: Copper fell to a two-week low as China’s virus death toll rose, reviving fears of weaker economic growth and reduced metals demand. The drop was reinforced by higher LME-approved copper inventories and a widening cash/three-month discount, signaling plentiful immediate supply and weighing on sentiment.

title: Pembridge to appoint third-party operator for copper-gold mine in Canada
summary: Pembridge will appoint a third-party operator to run its Minto copper-gold-silver mine in Canada’s Yukon. The company says the move should address operating inefficiencies from time-zone differences and reduce management costs. It also reports 14,000m of diamond drilling across multiple copper deposits to expand and upgrade resources and reserves.

title: Copper falls to a near 3-week low as virus death toll rises in China
summary: Copper fell to a near three-week low as China’s coronavirus death toll rose, renewing concerns about weaker economic growth and base-metals demand. The move was reinforced by rising LME copper inventories and wider signals of plentiful supply (cash discounts). Aluminium and nickel also closed lower amid the same risk sentiment.

title: Indonesia 2019 nickel ore output surges, 2020 output to slow - official
summary: Indonesia’s official said 2019 low-grade nickel ore output rose and exports jumped, but ore exports are expected to be cut in early 2020 after a policy change favoring higher-grade feed for smelters. Ferronickel and nickel pig iron production increased sharply while matte fell, keeping nickel supply dynamics in focus.

title: Indonesia 2019 nickel ore output surges, 2020 output to slow -official
summary: Reuters reports Indonesia’s 2019 nickel ore output rose to 52.8 million tonnes, more than double 2018. Nickel ore exports also increased to 30.2 million tonnes in 2019. However, the country stopped nickel ore exports at the start of 2020, likely prompting lower output from low-grade miners and tightening supply for nickel processing.

title: Copper steadies as production closures offset China virus fears
summary: London copper steadied in early Asia as fears over a China virus weighed on demand, but looming African production closures supported prices. LME three-month copper inched up, while China contracts fell. Reuters cites care-and-maintenance at Zambia’s Chambishi refinery and plans to halt Namibia’s Tschudi mine.

title: Anglo American Q4 Copper Equivalent Production Rises; Maintains FY20 View
summary: Anglo American said Q4 copper equivalent production rose 4% mainly from successful ramp-up at the Minas-Rio project in Brazil. Group copper equivalent was slightly lower excluding Minas-Rio. However, copper production declined overall due to drought-driven reductions at Chile’s Los Bronces, while 2020 copper guidance stayed unchanged.

title: Copper hits 6-week low on rising inventories, China virus scare
summary: Copper prices fell to a six-week low as LME-approved inventories jumped 20% and Shanghai inventories rose, while concern over a spreading flu-like virus in China raised fears of weaker demand growth. Trading activity also weakened ahead of Lunar New Year. The broader base-metals complex fell, including aluminium and nickel.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks jumped 20,500 mt in the pre-CNY week
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose by 20,500 mt to 292,500 mt between Jan 17 and Jan 23. The build followed muted trades during the closed import arbitrage window and arrivals under bill of lading, with gains continuing for six weeks, including 44,500 mt cumulative growth over three weeks.

title: Centre Agrees To Restart Angul Aluminum Park: Dharmendra Pradhan -
summary: The Centre agreed to restart infrastructure upgradation work at Odisha’s Angul Aluminium Park, a JV involving NALCO and IDCO. Dharmendra Pradhan said renewed focus on removing bottlenecks should enable completion by July 2020, funded partly by a central grant, and restore support to the aluminium cluster, boosting the sector’s outlook.

title: Copper slides further as China virus fears grow | The London Free Press
summary: Copper prices fell to a six-week low as coronavirus fears in China intensified, with two cities locked down and liquidity disrupted by the Lunar New Year. The drop was reinforced by rising LME warehouse inventories and technical selling. Other industrial metals also declined, including aluminium and nickel, reflecting broad risk-off demand expectations.

title: Private equity fund GSOL eyes takeovers to expand ferronickel business
summary: Private equity fund GSOL is in talks for four or five potential acquisitions to expand its ferronickel production, a stainless-steel input combining nickel and iron. It already revived and ramped operations in the Dominican Republic and North Macedonia, and targets further capacity and cost improvements.

title: Copper slides further as China virus fears grow
summary: Copper prices fell to the lowest in six weeks as coronavirus fears in China intensified, driving concerns about weaker economic activity and metal demand. The move was reinforced by speculators cutting long positions, rising LME inventories, and broader selloffs in industrial commodities, with nickel and aluminium also trading lower.

title: Peru: Copper exports total US$12.260 billion in Jan-Nov 2019 | News | ANDINA
summary: Peru’s SNMPE reported that copper exports totaled US$12.260 billion in Jan–Nov 2019, down 9.4% versus the prior year, with November shipments falling 17% y/y to US$1.131 billion. Copper accounted for 29% of total exports, with China, Japan, and South Korea as main destinations.

title: ZAF Energy Systems Deploys First Data Center to Run on Nickel Zinc Batteries
summary: ZAF Energy Systems, with Capitol Power Group, is deploying nickel-zinc (NiZn) batteries in a data center operator in Atlanta, replacing VRLA backup power systems. The announcement highlights NiZn’s performance and economics for UPS/telecom use, implying incremental nickel demand for battery production. Battery scale is unspecified.

title: World's biggest nickel miner has a plan for its crisis-ridden border town: here could come a hub for Arctic tourism
summary: Russia’s Nornickel faces a crisis in Nikel as the local nickel smelter is closing and hundreds of jobs will be dismissed. Authorities plan to attract new industries, including a planned tourism investment. The smelter shutdown is the key immediate implication for nickel supply.

title: U.S.-China trade deal boosts copper prices even as doubts linger
summary: Copper jumped to an eight-month high after the U.S. and China agreed an initial trade deal, lifting hopes for stronger metals demand. LME copper prices rose about 0.7% with declines in warehouse inventories. The article also reports aluminium and nickel up modestly, reflecting positive broader sentiment.

title: Greece to sell troubled nickel producer Larco's assets – minister
summary: Greece plans to liquidate troubled nickel producer Larco and sell its smelting plant and mines in separate chunks. The move follows long-running financial distress and Greece’s obligation to recover illegal state aid. Larco faces large unpaid bills to PPC and fines for environmental violations, raising risks to nickel processing availability.

title: Copper heads for sharpest weekly drop in nearly 19 months on virus fears
summary: Copper steadied but was still set for its biggest weekly drop in 19 months as China’s coronavirus controls raised fears of slower growth and weaker metals demand. LME-approved copper stocks rose sharply and China inventories increased. The broader complex also weakened, with aluminium and nickel heading for weekly declines.

title: Beer Institute Highlights Transparency Issues in Aluminum Market on Beer Can Appreciation Day
summary: The Beer Institute says aluminum costs for U.S. brewers have surged due to 10% aluminum tariffs and the Midwest Premium pricing system. It claims brewers pay a full “tariff-paid” premium despite using recycled or Canada-origin metal. The institute urges leaders to demand more transparent aluminum benchmarking and pricing.

title: Copper posts steepest weekly drop since 2015 on virus fears
summary: Copper prices posted the biggest weekly drop in five years as coronavirus spread raised fears of weaker Chinese growth and reduced metals demand. China’s lockdown measures and holiday disruptions heightened the outlook risk, while LME-approved and China inventories rose sharply. Nickel and aluminium also fell alongside copper.

title: Copper Sees Worst Losing Streak Since 2018 on Virus Fears
summary: Copper is seeing its worst losing streak since 2018 as virus fears intensify market risk. The headline suggests the selloff is driven by expectations of weaker near-term economic activity and demand, putting downward pressure on copper prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: Trump expands tariffs on steel and aluminum imports
summary: Trump signed a proclamation expanding tariffs on U.S. imports of steel and aluminum derivatives, adding 25% to derivative steel products and 10% to derivative aluminum products, effective Feb. 8, with some country exemptions. The move targets circumvention of existing duties and aims to protect domestic production and security needs.

title: Trump Expands Aluminum, Steel Tariffs to Some Imported Products
summary: The article headline says Trump is expanding aluminium and steel tariffs to some imported products. Such tariffs can raise the landed cost of imported aluminium, tightening near-term supply availability and supporting aluminium price expectations over the coming days to weeks.

title: Trump expands import tariffs to include derivative aluminium and steel products
summary: The Trump administration expanded Section 232 tariffs to downstream derivative aluminium products, adding a 10% duty on some items such as nails, staples, electrical wires, and parts used in cars and tractors. Some countries are exempted. By increasing tariff costs on aluminium inputs, the policy is likely to support aluminium prices near term.

title: Trump announces higher tariffs for steel and aluminum derivates
summary: Trump signed a proclamation raising U.S. tariffs on derivative steel products by an additional 25% and on derivative aluminum products by an additional 10%, with some country exemptions. He cited national security goals and said imports of base metals fell while derivative imports rose to circumvent duties. The changes take effect Feb. 8.

title: Trump increases tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum products from some countries
summary: The article headline reports Trump increasing tariffs on derivative steel and aluminium products from selected countries. Higher tariffs can discourage imports and alter short-term trade flows, potentially reducing downstream demand for aluminium products and placing downward pressure on aluminium prices within the next days to four weeks.

title: Trump expands aluminum, steel tariffs
summary: Trump’s administration expanded steel and aluminum tariffs to cover additional imported downstream products, including some derivative aluminum articles facing an extra 10% duty. By increasing the cost of imported aluminum products and highlighting potential national-security justifications, the move is likely to support near-term US aluminum pricing.

title: Trump to raise tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum imports - Xinhua
summary: Trump signed a proclamation raising U.S. tariffs on derivative steel imports by 25% and derivative aluminium imports by 10% from Feb. 8 to stop circumvention of prior duties. The move follows claims of national-security justification but studies warn tariffs hurt manufacturing, lift input costs, and trigger retaliation—negative for aluminium demand expectations.

title: Trump to raise tariffs on derivative steel, aluminium imports
summary: Trump signed a proclamation raising US tariffs on derivative aluminium imports by an additional 10% from Feb 8 and increasing derivative steel tariffs by 25%, citing national security and claiming circumvention. The piece highlights likely damage to manufacturing employment, GDP, and input costs, with retaliation risks weighing on industrial metals sentiment.

title: Trump to raise tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum imports
summary: Trump signed a proclamation raising U.S. tariffs on derivative steel imports by 25% and derivative aluminum imports by 10% from Feb. 8, claiming foreign producers shipped downstream items to circumvent existing Section 232 duties. Some countries are exempt. Research cited by the article says such tariffs hurt manufacturing via higher input costs and retaliation.

title: Trump increases tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum products | THE DAILY TRIBUNE
summary: Trump increased US tariffs on derivative steel products by an additional 25% and raised duties on derivative aluminum products by an additional 10%. Several countries receive exemptions, but the broader tariff lift is likely to curb demand for imported aluminum products and weigh on aluminium price expectations in the near term.

title: AT A GLANCE: Peru's Buenaventura misses 2019 guidance; copper, zinc output down
summary: Peru’s Buenaventura missed its 2019 guidance and reported that copper (and zinc) output fell. A decline in copper production can reduce near-term supply expectations, increasing downward pressure on copper prices over the coming days as markets reassess inventory and output outlooks.

title: Futures File: Coronavirus outbreak in China affects copper, oil and more
summary: The report headline says China’s coronavirus outbreak is impacting copper (along with oil and other assets). Such an outbreak can disrupt industrial activity and logistics in the short term, reducing near-term demand expectations and pushing copper futures lower as markets price slower consumption.

title: Palladium One Reports Highly Anomalous Nickel and Copper in Soil Sampling on the Tyko Ni-Cu-PGE Property, Canada
summary: Palladium One reports anomalously high nickel (up to 238 ppm) and copper (up to 108 ppm) in fall 2019 soil sampling along the Smoke Lake EM anomaly on its Tyko Ni-Cu-PGE property in Ontario. The results confirm the target, but no immediate supply or production implications are provided.

title: Palladium One Reports Highly Anomalous Nickel and Copper in Soil Sampling on the Tyko Ni-Cu-PGE Property, Canada
summary: Palladium One reports strongly anomalous nickel (up to 238 ppm) and copper (up to 108 ppm) in soil samples along an untested airborne EM anomaly at its Tyko Ni-Cu-PGE property in Ontario. Results are described as confirming a drill target; drilling is expected later in February 2020.

title: Escalating Global Demand & Increased Consumption of Copper to Drive Revenues in 2020
