summary: The piece projects copper demand growing about 4.2% per year through 2019 to 36.0 million tonnes, citing higher construction, power-grid upgrades, manufacturing output and transport equipment use. It also notes ongoing copper mining activity and an $8m royalty financing for a Chilean project to advance studies and development.

title: Financial News Media |   Escalating Global Demand & Increased Consumption Of Copper To Drive Revenues In 2020
summary: The release projects rising global copper demand driven by construction, infrastructure and manufacturing, and highlights Los Andes Copper’s $8m NSR royalty financing to advance its Chile Vizcachitas project (PFS and permitting). It also references company production updates forecasting higher 2020 nickel output, supporting sentiment for both metals.

title: SSY Futures Ltd Arranges The First Options Trade In Mid Western Aluminium Delivery Premium
summary: SSY Futures Ltd arranged the first options trade tied to a mid-western aluminium delivery premium. The coverage is directly connected to how regional aluminium premiums are priced and hedged, but it does not describe any immediate change in supply, demand, inventories, or production. Net near-term price impact is therefore limited.

title: Advertisement: Can copper be the metal of the future with large deficits?
summary: The advertisement argues global copper supply will face deficits over the next two years as major mine production wanes, while demand is expected to rise with renewables and EVs. It promotes Trigon Metals’ Kombat restart readiness in Namibia and the Silver Hill project in Morocco, but offers no immediate supply shock.

title: Copper Slides Under Coronavirus Concerns
summary: Copper prices slid further as China’s coronavirus lockdown of tens of millions intensified worries about slower growth. March copper in New York fell 7.2% over seven straight down sessions to a seven-week low. Analysts link the demand outlook deterioration to China’s central role in global copper imports.

title: Colombia approves studies for Jericó copper project
summary: Colombia has approved studies for the Jericó copper project. While the decision relates directly to copper development and could support longer-term supply expectations, it does not indicate imminent production, exports, or disruptions. Therefore any near-term effect on copper prices is likely small and mostly expectations-driven.

title: Aluminum Market 2019-2023 | Increasing Demand for Aluminum Cans in the Beverage Industry to Boost Growth
summary: Technavio’s press release forecasts growth in the global aluminum market, citing increasing demand for aluminum cans in the beverage industry. It also highlights that high volatility in LME aluminum prices could hinder growth. The piece is descriptive and does not provide concrete short-term supply or policy shocks.

title: Nickel prices go from red hot to ice cold
summary: Nickel fell to its lowest level since July on the London Metals Exchange, after previously trading above $8. Indonesia reversed an earlier export ban, while China-US trade war fears and, most recently, coronavirus spread raised concerns about weakening Chinese demand, a key driver for base metals including nickel.

title: Uptick in world growth, supply constraints to lift copper prices
summary: A Reuters poll expects copper prices to rise on improving global growth and less seamless supply return, projecting a 2020 copper deficit. It also expects nickel support from Indonesia’s nickel ore export ban. Conversely, analysts foresee an aluminium surplus in 2020, implying LME prices will decline.

title: Copper crashes as virus chills the China recovery story: Andy Home
summary: Wuhan coronavirus fears are driving risk-off sentiment and sharply weakening China’s expected industrial recovery. LME copper is cited as falling ~10% since mid-January, with liquidity losses during holidays and fund positioning reversing. Analysts expect demand weakness to persist for weeks, creating bearish near-term price pressure.

title: President Trump Imposes Additional Tariffs on Downstream Aluminum and Steel Products | Clark Hill PLC
summary: President Trump imposed additional duties on imports of downstream aluminum articles—10% for aluminum products—effective February 8, 2020, under Section 232 national-security findings. Tariffs target derivative goods where aluminum is a major input and import volumes rose after prior tariffs, likely tightening supply and supporting aluminum demand/prices.

title: Uptick in world growth, supply constraints to lift copper prices: poll
summary: A Reuters poll expects copper to rise in 2020 due to improving global growth and less seamless supply returns, with a projected market deficit. It also expects nickel support from Indonesia’s nickel ore export ban, implying tighter supply. In contrast, aluminium is forecast to swing to surplus, weighing on prices.

title: Copper crashes as virus chills the China recovery story
summary: Coronavirus fears in Wuhan are driving a sharp risk-off move and disrupting China’s production and return-to-work expectations. LME copper falls about 10% from mid-January highs, with reduced Chinese liquidity and sharply unwound speculative longs. Citibank expects very weak Chinese demand for 4–6 weeks, delaying recovery.

title: Copper Fox Announces 2019 Fourth Quarter Operating and Financial Results
summary: Copper Fox Metals filed audited annual financial statements and provided 2019 Q4 highlights, including continued development and exploration spending on its Schaft Creek, Van Dyke, Mineral Mountain, and Sombrero Butte copper projects. The company expects an updated Van Dyke resource estimate in Q2 2020 and cites sensitivity to copper prices and M&A activity.

title: Copper rebounds as investors assess virus impact
summary: London copper rebounded from a four-month low as investors reassessed the coronavirus outbreak’s economic impact in China, where virus containment measures extended holidays and threatened factory output. The report notes factory shutdown fears for copper demand and also shows smaller gains in aluminum and stronger gains in nickel on day-to-day sentiment shifts.

title: Sandfire disappointed by Black Butte copper project delay
summary: Sandfire Resources’ managing director criticized delays in receiving US approvals needed for mining permits for the Black Butte copper project in Montana. The delay comes while the company continues to progress its DeGrussa mine in Western Australia and still waits to decide on this high-grade undeveloped copper asset.

title: Need customs duty hike on aluminium: AAI's response to ASMA
summary: Aluminium Association of India (AAI) urges the Prime Minister to raise customs duties on imported aluminium metal and scrap, arguing imports have increased due to global trade disputes and scrap policy changes. AAI disputes claims by ASMA that such a hike would harm small downstream firms, but the proposed tariff is price-supportive for aluminium.

title: Illinois man pleads guilty to stripping copper from over 80 cellphone towers
summary: An Illinois man pleaded guilty to a federal charge alleging he shut down power to more than 80 cellphone towers across Missouri to steal copper from the sites. The report is about copper theft at telecom infrastructure, but it provides no evidence of broad supply disruption or market-wide impact.

title: Proactive Investors China - The web's leading portal for China stocks - Panoramic Resources awards underground mining contract for Savannah Nickel Mine
summary: Panoramic Resources has awarded an underground mining contract for the Savannah Nickel Mine, as described in the article title. The update is directly related to nickel mining activity, but it appears operational rather than a clear, immediate supply disruption or demand catalyst. Net impact on near-term nickel prices is likely limited.

title: Examining The Milestone Guinea Alumina Corporation Project
summary: The article reviews the $1.4bn Emirates Global Aluminium Guinea Alumina Corporation bauxite project, including rail capacity expansion and financing structures. It highlights Guinea’s bauxite as feedstock for alumina and aluminium smelting. While relevant to the aluminium value chain, it provides no clear new short-term operational or policy shift.

title: Challhuahuacho kicked off new round of strike against Peru's Las Bambas copper mine
summary: Residents of Challhuahuacho launched a 48-hour strike against MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine over unmet government and company social commitments. An indefinite strike could follow from Jan 27, threatening disruption of copper concentrate shipments. Reduced supply of concentrate is likely to pressure treatment charges and support copper prices.

title: KAZ Minerals Q4 Copper Production Rises
summary: KAZ Minerals reported Q4 copper production rose to 80.9 kt versus 77.9 kt a year earlier. The company also increased gold output but saw lower quarterly silver production. The data points to higher copper supply, though the article lacks market, delivery, or cost context.

title: Copper Strong Sell-Off Towards 4-Month Low
summary: Copper delivery in March 2020 is in a strong bearish trend, falling from recent highs and hitting a four-month low. Technical signals such as RSI below 30, a bearish MACD and a bearish SMA crossover suggest further negative momentum. Downside support is cited near 2.4780 and 2.4000.

title: Highland Copper Provides Corporate Update
summary: Highland Copper announced extensions to its loan maturity (to May 31, 2020) and the deadline to complete its acquisition of the White Pine North copper project (to June 30, 2020). The closing depends on environmental obligations and bonding arrangements. No production changes are reported, but project timelines shift.

title: Egypt Aluminum swings to losses in H1-19/20 unaudited financials
summary: Egyptian aluminium producer reported H1 2019/20 net losses of EGP 595.7m versus prior-year profit, citing higher electricity and production costs and a decline in the LME basic aluminium price. Revenues fell sharply, and currency moves and investment exits also weighed on results, underscoring aluminium price weakness.

title: Indiana bill would require all schools to test water for lead, copper
summary: An Indiana bill (HB 1265) passed the House to require statewide school drinking-water testing for lead and copper by 2023, with remediation if results exceed federal action levels. The measure follows concerns from prior Marion County testing and aims to protect children and seek grant funding for costs.

title: Nickel and copper are bull stand-outs in base metals poll
summary: Reuters poll shows analysts expect nickel and copper to outperform on supply deficits (Indonesia export ban for nickel; copper shortfalls), but the coronavirus outbreak is weakening China demand expectations and funds are unwinding longs, with nickel and copper already down 12% and 9% since early January. Aluminium views are mixed.

title: Nickel and copper are bull stand-outs in base metals poll
summary: A Reuters poll expects higher nickel and copper prices over the next two years, driven by projected supply deficits (Indonesia’s nickel ore export ban; copper shortfalls). However, the coronavirus outbreak is undermining demand assumptions in China, and the article notes nickel (-12%) and copper (-9%) have already dropped since early January as longs are unwound.

title: UPDATE:  Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Derivatives List Extremely Limited | Kelley Drye & Warren LLP
summary: Trump issued a Section 232 proclamation imposing duties on imports of certain steel and aluminum derivatives. The Federal Register publication shows the covered product list is extremely limited, and additional annexes may expand coverage later. Near term, the aluminum duties raise import costs and may worsen demand/supply expectations for aluminium.

title: SMM survey: Most copper processors to postpone resumption to February 10 due to coronavirus outbreak
summary: An SMM survey reports Chinese coronavirus measures extending the CNY holiday and ordering many copper processors in key provinces to resume no earlier than Feb 9 (or Feb 10) and cut output. Downstream consumption is also hit by transportation and control measures, while smelting is less disrupted, implying bearish spot pressure.

title: China's 2019 nickel ore imports from Indonesia jump 72% on year
summary: China’s nickel ore imports from Indonesia rose 72% year-on-year in 2019, according to the article. The increase suggests more raw material entering China’s supply chain for nickel processing, which can lift expected supply and create downward pressure on nickel prices over the short term.

title: Copper on course for biggest monthly fall in over 4 years
summary: London copper, though up slightly on Friday, is set for its biggest monthly fall in over four years as the coronavirus outbreak raises fears of weaker Chinese demand. WHO declared a global health emergency, factory activity softened, and prices have fallen ~10% since headlines began. Aluminium and nickel also moved lower/flat with the risk backdrop.

title: CRU: Coronavirus: Assessing the Likely Impact on Copper Smelting
summary: CRU assesses coronavirus disruption risk to Chinese copper smelting. Hubei, including Wuhan lockdowns and extended Chinese New Year holidays, is seen as limited for copper (3.9% of blister output). Nearby provinces may matter more, but impacts are highly speculative; travel cancellations and a postponed CSPT meeting add uncertainty.

title: Nevada Copper taps Redpath to boost production at US underground mine
summary: Nevada Copper has hired Redpath USA as principal underground mining contractor to ramp up its Pumpkin Hollow project in Nevada. The processing plant started last month, and the company aims to reach full commercial production. The mine is a long-life copper development, with ongoing exploration to support output growth.

title: Alcoa's Australian aluminium smelter hit by power cut amid heatwave
summary: Alcoa’s Australian aluminium smelter reportedly faced a power cut during a heatwave. The outage can force production to slow or halt, reducing short-term aluminium output and tightening immediate supply expectations. Such disruptions usually pressure aluminium prices lower until operations normalize and capacity utilization recovers.

title: Men accused of stealing car, copper and generator from Cullman Electric Co-op
summary: Two men were arrested for stealing a generator and about 152 pounds of copper from the Ryan’s Creek substation of Cullman Electric Co-op, after investigating leads and recovering items, including a vehicle. Copper was reportedly taken to a recycling business. The incident is local and small versus global copper markets.

title: Copper miner looks to life after DeGrussa
summary: Sandfire Resources’ DeGrussa mine in Western Australia is entering its final years, leaving the company needing replacement copper tonnes. The piece frames the challenge as finding new supply quickly. That near-term production outlook can add downside pressure to copper expectations as markets assess potential shortfall risk.

title: China's imports of Indonesian nickel ore rose 72% in 2019
summary: China significantly increased Indonesian nickel ore purchases in 2019, with imports up about 72% to 23.9 million mt as traders bought ahead of Indonesia’s nickel ore export ban from Jan. 1, 2020. December imports also surged, highlighting short-term supply-tightening expectations for nickel processing.

title: Smaller coal, nickel miners concerned over proposed omnibus bill incentives
summary: Indonesia’s proposed omnibus bill includes fiscal and non-fiscal incentives to help miners build downstream industries, but smaller nickel miners worry the incentives may not be scalable. With Indonesia already banning nickel ore exports since January, stalled smelter projects could affect near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: Shanghai copper falls to lowest since late 2016 on virus concerns
summary: Shanghai copper sank to a more than three-year low as coronavirus concerns drove investors to sell futures. China’s market closure during Lunar New Year meant prices caught up with London declines. ShFE also showed aluminium and nickel falling, reflecting broad risk-off demand worries.

title: Shanghai copper falls to over 3-year low as market reopens
summary: Shanghai base metals fell as China reopened trading after the Lunar New Year break, amid coronavirus fears that could reduce demand. ShFE copper sank 7% to a more-than-three-year low; aluminium and nickel also declined by about 3–4%. The outbreak and market reopening pushed prices lower despite some support from LME copper.

title: Shanghai copper drops to lowest since late 2016 on virus concerns
summary: Shanghai copper fell to the lowest level since late 2016 as investors sold futures over escalating coronavirus worries in China. China’s Lunar New Year closure and virus-related uncertainty drove ShFE copper down the daily 7% limit, while ShFE aluminium and nickel also dropped sharply amid softer activity and disrupted trading.

title: Copper social stocks rose 65,000 mt over CNY holiday
summary: China’s major copper trading markets saw social inventories rise by 65,000 mt from Jan 23 to 280,000 mt by Feb 3. Deliveries to social warehouses were disrupted by the domestic coronavirus outbreak impacting logistics. SMM warns the near-term shipment hit may increase smelter inventory backlog risk.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports inched up 42,000 wmt during CNY holiday
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports increased to 14.43 million wmt as of Feb 3, up 42,000 wmt from Jan 23, as coronavirus and the CNY holiday slowed shipments. Stocks at seven major ports rose to 11.52 million wmt, indicating improved near-term ore availability.

title: Over 240 Senior Aluminium Executives to Gather in London in April at the CRU World Aluminium Conference
summary: CRU announced its World Aluminium Conference in London (20–21 April 2020), highlighting sessions on aluminium market outlook, supply/demand, premiums, sustainability, EV-driven demand, Chinese sector perspectives, trade impacts, recycled aluminium, and raw material/price discussions. It is an industry meeting announcement without new figures or concrete immediate catalysts.

title: Copper theft causing damage, high costs | Saskatoon StarPhoenix
summary: Copper theft in Saskatoon is damaging rental properties and city utility infrastructure, with thieves removing copper pipe and wire and causing flooding and heat outages. title: Copper flashes red warning light on virus hit to growth
summary: Copper prices fell about 10% in January as the coronavirus outbreak in China undermined growth and metals demand expectations. The article cites lockdown-driven postponements in work and state grid tenders, possible inventory builds, and anticipates smelter maintenance, contributing to bearish market positioning and further downside risk.

title: Copper prices could be sending up a warning flare for investors
summary: Copper has fallen over 12% since mid-January, with the coronavirus outbreak worsening and threatening global growth. Traders cite copper’s high sensitivity to China and uncertainty over China’s growth trajectory. Analysts warn the downtrend could continue, potentially breaking support near $2.50 toward $2.25.

title: Copper theft causing damage, high costs | Regina Leader-Post
summary: Copper pipe and wire thefts in Saskatoon are damaging rental homes and affecting Saskatoon Light and Power. Utilities and landlords face costly repairs and retrofits, while thieves target older copper-plumbed properties. Police note limited ability to trace sold copper, prompting advice to secure or remove visible copper.

title: Copper Hits Five-Month Low With Virus Threatening China Growth
summary: Copper prices fell to a five-month low as concerns grew that a virus outbreak could undermine China’s economic growth. The implied impact is weaker industrial activity and metal demand expectations, which generally weighs on copper sentiment in the near term over the coming days and weeks.

title: Copper hits five-month low with virus threatening China growth
summary: Copper is reported to have fallen to a five-month low, with a virus raising concerns about weaker economic growth in China. The development points to reduced near-term expectations for industrial activity and power/infra demand, pressuring copper prices.

title: Nickel plant in New Caledonia nears sale - report
summary: Vale’s board approved $US120 million for restructuring its New Caledonia nickel plant, which is for sale, with a buyer expected by end of next month. After losses, Vale is moving away from closure fears and prioritising nickel hydroxide cake for EV battery demand, though refinery closure may cut staffing and output.

title: China coronavirus hammers copper prices
summary: The report headline says China’s coronavirus situation is hammering copper prices. title: Glencore fourth-quarter copper output down 9%
summary: Glencore reported that its fourth-quarter copper output was down 9%. Reduced production points to weaker near-term supply availability from one of the major global producers, which can influence copper market expectations over the following days and weeks.

summary: China extended manufacturing and city shutdowns due to the coronavirus, with travel restrictions and delayed factory restarts. Copper futures in Shanghai hit multi-year lows, falling for 13 straight days.

title: Glencore's 2019 cobalt up, copper down; share price rises
summary: Glencore reported 2019 output with copper down 6% and cobalt up 10% after boosting production at its Katanga mine and shutting Mutanda early due to falling cobalt prices and rising costs/taxes. The firm also noted slightly lower nickel output and kept 2020 outlook unchanged, driving shares higher.

title: Glencore sees copper output drop in 2019 after African shutdowns
summary: The (title) article says Glencore expects copper output to drop in 2019 after African shutdowns. The rest of the provided text is unrelated advertising/content.

title: Max Resource Reports 4.3% Copper and 26 g/t Silver Over 3m by 3m at Cesar Copper-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: MAX Resource Corp. reports rock chip panel sampling at its Cesar copper-silver project in Colombia, including 4.3% copper over 3m by 3m at Outcrop-1, with additional copper-bearing intervals and pending results from other outcrops. summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) secured a US$600mn syndicated revolving credit facility priced at a competitive margin, replacing prior uncommitted lines. No direct production or export change is stated.

title: Chile's Escondida copper mine halts use of groundwater
summary: Chile’s Escondida copper mine is reported to be halting use of groundwater. The change in water sourcing could disrupt day-to-day operations and affect copper output in the near term. Any production risk at a major mine would likely weigh on copper price expectations over the coming days.

summary: Braidy Industries ousted CEO Craig Bouchard amid controversy over $2 billion financing for a Kentucky aluminum rolling mill. title: SMM Morning Comments (Feb 5): Copper continued its rally amid global rebound
summary: SMM reports copper extending its rally after China’s central bank pumped large liquidity and trimmed lending rates to stabilize markets amid the coronavirus outbreak. title: Updated independently verified Indicated Mineral Resource again increases the Kamoa Copper Discovery to 256 million tonnes grading 4.15% copper, at a 3% cut-off
summary: Ivanhoe Mines announced an independently verified update to mineral resources at the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Project in the DRC. Kakula resources were also updated.

title: US -CBP issues guidance on Sec. 232 duty on derivatives of aluminum and steel articles
summary: US CBP issued guidance on Section 232 additional duties for “derivative aluminum” articles under Proclamation 9980, effective for entries on/after Feb 8, 2020. title: Aluminium Bahrain discusses business opportunities with Italian firms
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) joined a Bahraini delegation to Italy and signed agreements with Italian firms including Fluorsid, FATA and Techmo Car. The deals relate to supply of aluminium fluoride, EPC work for Alba’s port/Line 6 expansion and related equipment collaboration, suggesting ongoing aluminium production activity but no immediate price shock.

title: Spot copper trades subdued in Shanghai amid virus fears
summary: Spot copper trading in Shanghai stayed subdued as virus fears limited consumer participation despite some post-holiday demand. summary: SMM says China’s downstream nickel manufacturing contracted in January for the tenth consecutive month. title: Coronavirus Sickens Crude Oil and Copper - Investing Daily
summary: The piece argues coronavirus-driven demand weakness is pressuring both crude oil and copper, calling copper “Dr. Copper” but highlighting a negative near-term outlook. title: Copper jumps to one-week high after China stimulus
summary: Copper rebounded to a one-week high after China’s central bank stimulus, prompting investors to unwind bearish positions on coronavirus-hit demand. LME three-month copper rose about 2%. title: Orion to Purchase Mills Following Positive Results at Copper-Zinc Project
summary: Orion Minerals says value engineering at its Prieska copper-zinc project has led to securing an option to purchase SAG and ball mills, long-lead items typically ordered later. title: Winter Drilling is Underway at VR's Ranoke Copper-Gold Property in Ontario TSX Venture Exchange:VRR
summary: VR Resources said winter drilling has resumed at its Ranoke copper-gold project in Ontario, targeting geophysical anomalies for a hydrothermal iron oxide breccia body with potential copper and gold. title: SMM Evening Comments (Feb 5): Copper extended rally on eased risk aversion
summary: SMM said SHFE nonferrous prices ended mixed, with copper (+1.09%) and nickel (+1.43%) rising and aluminium climbing modestly (+0.29%). The rally was linked to eased risk aversion after China’s central bank injected 400 billion yuan to support the economy and offset coronavirus disruption.

title: Copper jumps to one-week high after China stimulus | The London Free Press
summary: Copper rose to a one-week high after China’s central bank announced stimulus, prompting investors to unwind bearish positions tied to the coronavirus’s demand impact. title: Virus Hits Copper Trade With China Asking Chile to Defer Cargoes
summary: The headline reports a virus-related disruption to copper trade, with China requesting Chile to defer copper cargoes. The expected effect is slower shipments and tighter near-term supply into China, which typically supports copper prices in the coming days as market participants adjust delivery expectations.

title: Primary aluminium inventories rose 61,000 mt in the week after CNY holiday
summary: SMM data show China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots across eight consumption areas increased 61,000 mt from Feb 3 to 945,000 mt by Feb 6, after a 194,000 mt stock jump during the CNY holiday. Arriving deliveries and logistics bottlenecks deterred warehouse outflows, pointing to softer near-term supply tightness.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Feb 6): Copper on track for a third day of gains
summary: SMM says copper is on course for a third day of gains, with LME copper hitting a one-week high before settling higher. Nickel rose 1.4% on SHFE and gained strongly on LME. Aluminium also climbed, supported by Tomago smelter production cut reports and China demand offset steps.

title: Raw material supply troubles underpinned nickel prices
summary: Nickel futures edged higher as concerns rose over China NPI output and Philippine nickel-ore supply. NPI plants in Inner Mongolia are operating at low levels or shutting due to shortages and epidemic-related labor constraints. Philippine port measures restrict crews disembarking, tightening ore availability and supporting prices.

title: Ex-Century Aluminum property deeded to West Virginia | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Owners of the former Century Aluminum property in West Virginia deeded the site to the state to prevent foreclosure after default on a loan tied to the former smelter assets. The plant is long shut due to aluminum prices and utility costs, and the state plans to market the site for redevelopment.

title: Saudi miner Ma'aden says China supply, coronovirus dampen aluminium outlook
summary: Ma’aden CEO Darren Davis told Reuters that coronavirus-related disruption and longer China Lunar holiday will hit aluminium demand, while China is also set to increase supply, reinforcing a surplus outlook. He characterized the 2020 aluminium price outlook as “more negative” than at the start of the year, weighing on prices.

title: China issued import quotas for another 1,440 mt of aluminium scrap
summary: China’s environmental authorities issued another 1,440 mt of aluminium scrap import quotas, bringing 2020 allowances to 284,449 mt, with Q1 likely below 300,000 mt. The outbreak delays secondary aluminium producer restarts, reducing scrap demand, while market supply looks adequate in February, pushing scrap prices to track refined aluminium lower.

title: Pent-up demand amid virus outbreak to support near-term alumina price rally
summary: SMM reports China’s alumina market is temporarily imbalanced: upstream supply is relatively sufficient but transport curbs and logistics delays restrict shipments of bauxite/caustic soda/lime. Smelters’ feedstock inventories are running short, prompting SMM to expect a two-week alumina price rally, with continuity tied to transport policy changes.

title: North American Nickel Announces Loveland Nickel Exploration Program Underway
summary: North American Nickel announced mobilization for a 2020 drill program (1,085m in three holes) at its Loveland nickel property near Timmins, Ontario. The mineralization targets higher-grade nickel with reported associated copper, using BHEM/VTEMMAX-directed targets. This is exploration activity without immediate supply impact.

title: Excelsior Mining Releases Production Update for Gunnison Copper
summary: Excelsior Mining provided a production update for its Gunnison copper project in Arizona, noting optimization work on the wellfield. Preventive maintenance, retrofitting injection wells for recovery use, and reconfiguring wellheads/piping are being implemented during ramp-up to improve breakthrough and push first copper production to Q2 2020. The company says capex impact is not material.

title: Getec Industrial Offers Expanded Thermal Management Solutions including Extruded Aluminum Heatsinks
summary: Getec Industrial says its Thermal Management Solutions division increased sales in 2019 and is expanding for 2020 with upgraded CAD workstations and 12 new CNC milling machines. It also added friction stir welding to manufacture large, seamless extruded aluminum heatsinks, potentially supporting incremental near-term aluminum demand.

title: Woodmac: Copper "Well Below" Expectations Due to Coronavirus
summary: Wood Mackenzie says the coronavirus outbreak in China is slashing copper demand and disrupting logistics. Copper prices are described as trading well below expectations, with smelter acid inventories rising due to shipping constraints and construction delays reducing copper-intensive consumption.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Feb 7): Copper stemmed its rally
summary: SMM says copper’s rally is losing momentum as coronavirus concerns linger, with processors delaying operations and February consumption expected to fall. LME and SHFE copper face moderating gains from seasonally rising inventories. Aluminium is marginally firmer, while nickel edges up slightly despite pullbacks.

title: U.S. Imposes Tariffs On Derivative Steel And Aluminum Imports
summary: The Trump administration announced additional Section 232 tariffs on specified downstream steel and aluminum articles effective Feb. 8, 2020. Aluminum derivative products face 10% duties and steel derivatives face 25%, with exemptions for select countries. Commerce will consider product exclusions via its 232 exclusions portal.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 260,000 wmt in the first week after CNY holiday
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 260,000 wmt from Feb 3 to 7 to 14.17 million wmt, with metal content down 2,200 mt to 120,600 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also declined by 19,000 wmt to 11.33 million wmt, indicating tighter near-term feedstock.

title: Copper Prices Hit an Almost Three-Year Low. The Worst Is Yet to Come.
summary: Copper prices fell to an almost three-year low, attributed to coronavirus-driven economic slowdown in China. The article cites risks of further demand deterioration for copper and notes some analysts expect the downside to continue. Overall, expectations skew toward weaker near-term copper demand and lower prices.

title: Copper Prices Hit an Almost Three-Year Low Because of Coronavirus. The Worst Is Yet to Come.
summary: Copper prices are reported at an almost three-year low as coronavirus-related disruptions and an economic slowdown in China raise fears of weaker industrial activity and copper demand. Analysts cited in the article warn further downside could follow if the demand impact worsens, keeping downward pressure on prices in the near term.

title: Aluminum Market Procurement Intelligence Report | Supply Shortage of CTP Will Propel Aluminum Market Price
summary: A SpendEdge procurement report argues the aluminum market faces a CTP shortage, noting CTP is a key ingredient in carbon anodes and that China’s steel production has increased CTP demand. The report also points to higher oil and gas prices raising aluminum producers’ fuel and electricity costs, supporting higher aluminum prices.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Feb 7): Copper halted increase on worries about coronavirus risks
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals mostly closed lower as renewed coronavirus concerns raised worries about near-term economic impact. Copper fell 0.54% after investors paused a rally amid outbreak escalation ahead of post-holiday travel. Nickel edged down 0.11%. Aluminium rose 0.48% on short-covering and downstream resumption expectations.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks flat from pre-holiday
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks in the bonded area stayed unchanged at about 18,500 mt before the Chinese New Year holiday despite an extended shutdown from coronavirus-related delays. Import arbitrage remained closed with losses, and LME cash vs three-month discounts widened, signaling ample nearby supplies. Resumption of deliveries and warehouse activity is expected next week.

title: Copper prices may still have more to lose, even after touching a nearly 3-year low
summary: Copper prices fell to a nearly three-year low as coronavirus fears spur concerns about China’s economic slowdown and potential weaker industrial demand for the metal. Analysts quoted warn that prices could drop further if the outbreak intensifies and investors reduce risk exposure, extending bearish near-term pressure.

title: Japan's Mitsubishi Materials buys 30% stake in Chile copper mine
summary: Mitsubishi Materials bought a 30% stake in Chile’s Mantoverde copper mine and project for $236 million to secure more copper concentrates for its smelters. The mine has about 2.1 million tonnes of copper reserves, and ownership sits with a consortium led by Audley Capital and Orion Mine Finance.

title: More than 7000 sue Papua New Guinea miner Basamuk nickel refinery for environmental damage | Companies
summary: More than 7,000 plaintiffs in Papua New Guinea are suing Ramu Nico, operator of the Basamuk nickel refinery, claiming years of environmental damage. The suit cites alleged spills contaminating land and water, and seeks declarations of public nuisance and damages for injuries to local rights.

title: U.S. tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum imports take effect - Xinhua
summary: U.S. tariffs on downstream “derivative” steel imports rose 25% and derivative aluminum imports rose 10%, taking effect amid opposition and claims of circumvention. Some countries received exemptions. Economists warn the cascading duties raise input costs, reduce competitiveness, and may hurt manufacturing, weighing on industrial metal demand.

title: US tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum imports take effect - World
summary: The US began applying additional tariffs on derivative steel (+25%) and aluminum (+10%) imports, citing national security and downstream coverage. Some countries were exempt. Economists argue tariffs raise costs, disrupt supply chains, and reduce GDP, with potential negative pressure on aluminum demand and prices.

title: U.S. tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum imports take effect--China Economic Net
summary: U.S. tariffs on derivative aluminum imports (and derivative steel) took effect, with rates increased by 10% for aluminum downstream products. The move is framed as extending earlier Section 232 duties and aims to stop circumvention. Economists warn cascading tariffs raise input costs, hurt manufacturing, and could pressure metals markets downward via weaker demand and uncertainty.

title: U.S. tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum imports take effect
summary: U.S. tariffs on derivative steel and aluminum imports—25% on derivative steel and 10% on derivative aluminum—took effect. The move targets downstream items like nails and staples aimed at curbing circumvention. Exemptions apply for some countries. Analysts warn costs and uncertainty could rise.

title: US tariffs on derivative steel, aluminum imports take effect
summary: US tariffs on derivative steel and aluminum imports increased by 25% (steel) and 10% (aluminum) and took effect Saturday, with partial exemptions for some countries. The policy aims to counter shipments that circumvent prior duties. Economists argue cascading tariffs raise input costs and hurt manufacturing and jobs, creating mixed near-term price signals, especially for aluminum.

title: US tariffs on derivative steel, aluminium imports take effect
summary: US tariffs on “derivative” aluminium imports rise by 10% and take effect immediately, with some country exemptions. The administration frames the move as national-security related and to close loopholes from prior duties. Economists warn cascading tariffs could raise costs and weaken manufacturing activity, but the article gives no copper-specific signals.

title: Copper Under Pressure as Optimism About Coronavirus Dwindles
summary: Copper prices have been pressured as coronavirus-related optimism fades. The selloff is tied to concerns over weaker Chinese demand and factory restart uncertainty, alongside transport restrictions and expectations that some Chinese melters may cut output if disruptions persist. A negative reaction on Friday follows renewed panic over rising deaths and cases.

title: Chinese Copper Buyers Cancel Orders Around The Globe As Economy Grinds To A Halt
summary: The article headline says Chinese copper buyers are cancelling orders worldwide as the economy grinds to a halt. This implies weaker near-term demand, reduced order flow to suppliers, and less spot buying activity globally, which would likely weigh on expectations for copper prices over the coming days.

title: Proactive Investors China - The web's leading portal for China stocks - Castillo Copper gets boost from government body for Mt Oxide Project
summary: The article’s headline says Castillo Copper’s Mt Oxide Project received a boost from a government body. Such support can improve confidence in project progress and future copper supply plans. This can modestly strengthen copper sentiment in the near term, assuming the measure is timely for development.

title: Spot aluminium trades improved as processors scheduled to reopen
summary: Spot aluminium in east and south China strengthened from last week as traders increased stockpiling ahead of factory reopenings after an extended holiday. Shanghai aluminium futures rose in morning trade, helped by better-than-expected January inflation data. Prices were higher versus Friday, though social inventories of primary aluminium ingots rose to 1.04 million mt.

title: Primary aluminium inventories exceeded 1 million mt amid virus outbreak
summary: SMM reported that China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots rose to about 1.04 million mt as rail deliveries arrived and shipments out of social warehouses were limited amid the epidemic outbreak. Inventories increased roughly 90,000 mt from Feb 6 to Feb 10 across eight consumption regions.

title: SMM Webinar Series: Coronavirus Special Impact on the China metals market-Macro overview with Copper and Zinc
summary: SMM’s China metals webinar notes coronavirus impacts on physical markets. It says the outbreak is set to take a toll on copper demand, while supply effects remain unclear, implying near-term oversupply in China. It cites expected February copper cathode output falling to 701,300 mt and year-on-year declines.

title: BHP in Talks to Delay Copper Shipments to China Due to Virus
summary: BHP is reportedly in talks to delay copper shipments to China because of a virus-related disruption. A shipment delay can reduce immediate supply availability and disturb copper trade flows, potentially affecting near-term pricing as the market recalibrates expectations for deliveries into China over the coming days.

title: Mitsubishi to acquire 30% stake in Chile's Mantoverde copper mine
summary: Mitsubishi Materials will buy a 30% stake in Chile’s Mantoverde copper mine for $263m and receive matching offtake rights for copper concentrate. Mantoverde holds substantial reserves and is set for expansion, supporting copper concentrate supply and near-term sentiment.

title: Auryn Gets Environmental Permit for Sombrero Copper-Gold Project
summary: Auryn Resources said it received an environmental permit from Peru’s Ministry of Energy and Mines for its Sombrero copper-gold exploration project. The permit covers 1,031 hectares and allows drilling up to 33 holes from 23 platforms at the Ccascabamba Sombrero target, supporting upcoming drilling programs.

title: Auryn Secures DIA for Initial Drill Program at Sombrero Copper-Gold Project in Southern Peru
summary: Auryn Resources said it received Peru’s environmental permitting approval (DIA) for its Sombrero copper-gold project, allowing up to 33 drill holes from 23 platforms, with start-of-activities and community consultation next. The news is a positive permitting milestone but does not imply near-term copper production.

title: President Trump Expands Section 232 Tariffs on Aluminum and Steel; Calls for New Product Exclusion Application Process | Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP
summary: The update says President Trump expanded Section 232 tariffs to additional aluminum “derivative” products, keeping the 10% ad valorem rate and applying duties from Feb. 8, 2020. It also discusses a new, potentially retroactive exclusion process and added CBP compliance risk, which may affect near-term aluminum import flows and pricing.

title: Critics Say Proposed Copper Mine In Minnesota Threatens Pristine Water
summary: A company proposes an underground copper mine near Minnesota’s Boundary Waters, sparking concerns about water pollution and lawsuits. Supporters argue modern controls could protect the wilderness, but regulatory hurdles remain. The project is years from opening, limiting immediate effects on copper and nickel supply expectations.

title: Max Resource Discovers a Second Extended High-Grade Copper-Silver Zone at the CESAR
summary: Max Resource Corp. reports a second high-grade copper-silver zone at its 100% owned CESAR project in Colombia, with rock chip assays up to 4.4% copper. The company says the strike length is open and more assays are pending. It remains an early exploration update.

title: Court ruling presents another obstacle for Arizona copper mine
summary: A U.S. judge overturned another government approval for the planned Rosemont copper mine in Arizona, requiring federal wildlife agencies to redo their endangered-species analyses. The decision follows a prior ruling that halted construction. The remand likely delays development, weighing on near-term expectations for incremental copper supply.

title: Judge Overturns Agency's Approval Of New Copper Mine In Southern Arizona
summary: A federal judge in Tucson overturned the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s approval of the $1.9 billion Rosemont open-pit copper mine in southeastern Arizona. The legal reversal halts progress after a prior court ruling stopped work. The decision delays future copper supply, potentially weighing on prices.

title: Nicola Mining Announces Positive Copper and Magnetite Recovery Results on Historic Mine Terraces Material
summary: Nicola Mining announced positive laboratory flotation and magnetic separation tests using historic waste-rock material. Results show production of a copper concentrate grading 29.6% Cu with 73.1% copper recovery from initial 0.34% Cu feed. The company plans further testing to optimize recovery and grades.

title: Braidy Industries wants 'more progress, faster' to build Kentucky aluminum mill, new CEO tells lawmakers
summary: Braidy Industries’ new CEO told Kentucky lawmakers the aluminum mill in northeast Kentucky still needs roughly $500 million to start construction, with the build potentially beginning late 2020 and commissioning in late 2022/early 2023. The project depends on funding plans and Rusal-linked supply, though scope appears limited for near-term global prices.

title: Braidy executives give update on plans for aluminum plant
summary: Braidy Industries told Kentucky lawmakers it still needs to raise $500 million to build a planned $1.7 billion aluminum plant/rolling mill in Appalachia. After a leadership shakeup, executives cited $65 million on hand and $200 million financing commitments, projecting jobs and future production if funding is secured by year’s end.

title: Why Mexico drew the line on including aluminum in tougher auto rules under new NAFTA
summary: Mexico refused to include aluminum in tougher auto sourcing requirements under the new NAFTA, citing inability to compete in supplying the metal because it lacks aluminum smelting capacity. The pact still raises North American purchase content to 70% for vehicles, supporting demand for regional aluminum supply versus cheaper imports.

title: BHP Takes The Crown As World's Top Copper Miner
summary: BHP became the world’s top copper miner after Chile’s Codelco reported lower output. Codelco’s copper production fell 5.6% to about 1.706 million tonnes, the lowest since 2008, due to declining ore grades. BHP’s own copper output rose, led by Escondida, keeping 2020 guidance steady.

title: Virus another wild card in nickel's year of uncertainty
summary: Nickel has fallen about 8% since January as coronavirus-driven curbs weaken Chinese manufacturing and stainless steel demand, with rising LME stocks and weaker spreads reinforcing bearish sentiment. The article also notes copper has seen similarly hard hits from coronavirus positioning, keeping downside bias near term.

title: Red River Posts January Copper Production Update
summary: Red River Resources reported January production at its Thalanga copper-zinc-lead operation in Northern Queensland. Copper concentrate output rose to a record 860 tonnes versus 655 tonnes in December (+31%). The update also includes higher zinc and lead concentrate production, alongside increased ore mined and processed.

title: Poseidon Nickel: 106-Percent Increase of Reserves at Silver Swan
summary: Poseidon Nickel says Silver Swan ore reserves increased 106% to 130,000 tonnes grading 5.2% nickel (6,800 tonnes contained nickel). The company also reports ongoing exploration at Black Swan and drilling results at Windarra, including 5m at 0.75% nickel and higher-grade intervals, supporting nickel resource prospects.

title: Purdue's biggest donation ever? Grad's nickel mine gift has that potential
summary: Purdue President Mitch Daniels highlighted a donation-related 1% net smelter return interest in FPX Nickel’s British Columbia mine. The article frames potential long-term output and returns for Purdue at current nickel prices, but it does not indicate any near-term operational disruption or demand shift.

title: Braidy Industries still needs $500 million for Kentucky aluminum mill, new CEO tells lawmakers
summary: Braidy Industries’ new CEO told Kentucky lawmakers the company still needs about $500 million to start construction of a planned aluminum mill, with potential startup pushed to end-2020 and commissioning not until late 2022 or early 2023. The update highlights financing turmoil and pledged commitments, but timing limits immediate aluminum price impact.

title: Virus slows Rio Tinto copper sales
summary: Rio Tinto said coronavirus measures in Mongolia, including a state of emergency in Khanbogd where its Oyu Tolgoi mine operates, are delaying copper deliveries to customers. The disruption reflects slowed Australian-to-China product flows as the virus spreads into China’s border province, likely worsening near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Coronavirus logjam hits Rio Tinto copper deliveries
summary: Rio Tinto said coronavirus containment measures have slowed copper concentrate imports crossing the Mongolia–China border, while BHP also delayed shipments as Chinese plants shut. The disruption and heightened uncertainty about demand and supply chains triggered falls in key commodity prices, including copper, nickel, and aluminum.

title: Coronavirus slows down Rio Tinto copper deliveries in Mongolia
summary: Rio Tinto said coronavirus containment measures are slowing copper concentrate deliveries from its Oyu Tolgoi mine in Mongolia to Chinese customers. Border logjams tied to local restrictions have delayed imports crossing the Mongolia-China border, and the company is working with authorities to restore regular safe crossings as China’s outbreak worsens.

title: Rio Tinto reviewing viability of ISAL aluminum smelter in Iceland | 12 February 2020
summary: The news headline says Rio Tinto is reviewing the viability of its ISAL aluminium smelter in Iceland. This kind of review can signal potential changes to operating status or output, which may tighten or loosen perceived aluminium supply expectations and weigh on prices if closure becomes more likely.

title: Rio Tinto reviews unprofitable aluminum smelter in Iceland
summary: Rio Tinto said it may cut operations or shut its Iceland aluminium smelter after it remained unprofitable due to high power costs and tough market conditions. Production has already been reduced to 85% of capacity. Rio will review options with Icelandic partners, while weak demand strains the broader aluminium market.

title: Zambia's GDP to exceed 3% as copper-producer steps up spending
summary: Zambia’s copper growth outlook is affected by drought-related electricity shortages that reduce hydropower generation and lift electricity and fuel costs. The government plans to diversify power supply via solar and wind, while focusing on fiscal consolidation and debt sustainability. These developments influence expectations for Zambia’s near-term copper production.

title: Endangered species throw roadblock in path of Rosemont Copper mine | Cronkite News
summary: A federal judge overturned environmental permits for Hudbay’s proposed Rosemont open-pit copper mine, finding the Fish and Wildlife Service used an improper endangered-species assessment. The case is remanded for further review, potentially delaying a major U.S. copper supply project. Opponents cite groundwater and habitat damage, while the company vows to continue.

title: Will ISAL Aluminum Smelter Close?
summary: Rio Tinto plans a strategic review of its ISAL aluminum smelter in Iceland, considering options including reduced production or possible closure. Output is already cut to 85% due to unprofitable operations from uncompetitive energy costs and historically low aluminum prices. Discussions with Iceland’s government aim to restore profitability.

title: Copper makes modest gains as coronavirus infections drop
summary: Copper rose modestly on easing coronavirus figures in China, reducing fears for demand and lifting LME stocks. Analysts said the sell-off may have been exaggerated but risks remain for factory activity. Rio Tinto also reported slower copper concentrate shipments and possible aluminum smelter curtailments, while aluminium traded slightly weaker.

title: Copper and other metals make modest gains as coronavirus infections drop
summary: Copper rose about 0.6% after China reported its lowest new COVID-19 cases since late January, improving sentiment for demand from the biggest metals consumer. LME aluminum also edged up, while nickel stocks climbed to a multi-year high. Rio Tinto flagged shipment slowdowns and potential aluminum smelter cuts, keeping caution.

title: SMM Webinar Series: Coronavirus Special Impact on the China metals market- Aluminium supply chain
summary: SMM outlines COVID-19’s impact on China’s aluminium supply chain, noting demand concerns and significantly higher aluminium ingot social inventories (up 37% vs pre-holiday) that could further rise over the next ten weeks. It reports aluminium futures fell 3.5% on the first trading day after CNY, despite some alumina price increases from logistics constraints.

title: U.S. Imposes Tariffs on Derivative Steel and Aluminum Imports | Jones Day
summary: The Trump administration announced additional U.S. Section 232 tariffs on certain downstream (derivative) aluminum imports (10%) and steel derivatives (25%), effective Feb. 8, 2020, with country exemptions. Commerce cites circumvention of existing duties. The move may pressure aluminum supply-demand dynamics and also affect industrial metals sentiment, including copper.

title: COLUMN-Virus another wild card in nickel's year of uncertainty: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist Andy Home says LME nickel is down sharply in early 2020 amid coronavirus concerns about weaker Chinese manufacturing and stainless steel demand. Rising LME nickel stocks and collapsing spreads worsen sentiment and price outlook. The same virus-driven hit to sentiment is said to have affected copper as well, both pressured by crowded long positions.

title: Primary aluminium inventories jumped as demand remained subdued
summary: China’s social inventories of primary aluminium rose sharply in the second week after CNY, increasing to 1.09 million mt (up 148,000 mt WoW). Rail arrivals boosted supply while demand stayed subdued amid the ongoing coronavirus outbreak. The inventory build signals near-term pressure on aluminium prices.

title: President Trump Expands Section 232 Tariffs On Aluminum And Steel; Calls For New Product Exclusion Application Process
summary: President Trump expanded Section 232 tariffs by adding derivative aluminum articles to the existing aluminum tariff schedule, effective Feb. 8, 2020. The new coverage includes certain aluminum stranded wire/cables/plaited bands and vehicle/tractor bumper-body stampings. A new exclusion application process is authorized, but duties also apply retroactively and to some FTZ entries.

title: Mongolian copper concentrate exports 13% down in January
summary: Mongolian copper concentrate exports reportedly declined 13% in January. A drop in concentrate shipments can reduce near-term availability of copper feedstock to smelters, potentially tightening supply expectations and providing support for copper prices in the short term.

title: AA Metals, Inc. and International Dominican Aluminum announce Joint-Venture partnership to extrude aluminum products in the Dominican Republic
summary: AA Metals and International Dominican Aluminium (IDA) formed a joint venture to extrude AA’s aluminum product range at IDA’s Dominican Republic facility. IDA highlights expansion and increased workforce, aiming for significant sales over the next three years, suggesting higher aluminum product throughput and associated material demand.

title: Copper Fox Announces $1,800,000 Non-Brokered Private Placement
summary: Copper Fox Metals announced a proposed non-brokered private placement to raise up to C$1.8 million, partly to acquire the Eaglehead project and fund exploration. The financing is for a copper-focused company, but the release does not signal immediate changes in copper production or market supply/demand, limiting short-term price impact.

title: Operating rates across secondary aluminium makers to slip to record low in February
summary: SMM estimates China’s secondary aluminium operating rates will fall to a record low of 33% in February. Production resumption is delayed by 7–15 days and only limited firms were operating by Feb 10, with slower worker return and weaker downstream demand after the holiday, driven by a coronavirus outbreak.

title: Copper Enrichment in Soil Enhances Aurania's Tsenken N3 as a Porphyry Copper Target
summary: Aurania Resources reports copper enrichment in soils over the Tsenken N3 geophysical target at its Lost Cities–Cutucu project in Ecuador, consistent with a porphyry copper system like nearby Tsenken N2. Soil sampling and shallow drilling are planned pending water-use permits, with no production or resource estimates provided.

title: China nickel downstream activity improved in December
summary: SMM says China’s nickel downstream sectors recovered in December, with PMIs rising for production and new orders (still below 50 overall) and inventories of raw materials rebounding. Stabilisation in nickel and stainless steel prices encouraged buyers to restock, while January PMI points to lingering weakness despite better order sentiment.

title: Max Resource Reports Expansion of the High-Grade Copper-Silver Zones to 4.9- km in Length at the CESAR Copper-Silver Project
summary: Max Resource Corp. reports that the high-grade copper-silver outcrop zone at its CESAR project now extends 3.5 km, with rock chip assays including multiple intervals around 1.5–2.4% copper. The company expects more assays and notes the zone remains open, but this is exploration results only.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Provides Exploration Update for Falcon Nickel Project
summary: ALX Resources reported an exploration update for its Falcon Nickel Project, including plans for up to 1,000 metres of drilling starting in early March 2020 and geophysical/geochemical work to refine drill targets. Historical trenches showed grades up to 3.17% nickel and 0.40% copper, but no production or supply impact was stated.

title: Rio Tinto says coronavirus slows copper exports from Mongolia to China
summary: Rio Tinto said coronavirus containment measures have slowed copper concentrate shipments from its Mongolian Oyu Tolgoi mine to China, citing border/transport restrictions. Reuters also reports Mongolia halted coal deliveries and China’s Yunnan Copper cut output at its Chifeng smelter after reduced concentrate arrivals.

title: Decommissioning Copper Networks: 6 Operator Case Studies
summary: A ResearchAndMarkets report highlights operator case studies on migrating from copper networks to fiber or fixed-wireless. It estimates substantial potential OPEX savings and “cash release” from decommissioning copper assets. The copper-free transition suggests weaker copper consumption expectations, though timelines may be slow and scrap effects are unclear.

title: FPX Nickel Corp: Developing Canada's Next Nickel District
summary: FPX Nickel is advancing its Baptiste Nickel Project in British Columbia, aiming for low-cost, low-emission nickel concentrate production. The company highlights prefeasibility work, government funding, and partnerships, including stakeholders supporting the project’s development. The news is nickel-focused but describes ongoing development rather than near-term supply changes.

title: First Quantum posts surprise profit on higher copper sales, output
summary: First Quantum reported a surprise profit as output and copper sales rose, driven by ramp-up at its Cobre Panama mine and completion of its mill. However, average realized copper price fell and demand weakness from China was cited. Overall, stronger production/sales likely provides short-term bullish sentiment for copper markets.

title: Bids in for Vale nickel company in New Caledonia
summary: Vale’s New Caledonia nickel unit has received three bids for Vale Brazil’s 95% stake. A $120m approved restructure includes closing the refinery, job losses, prioritising production of NHC for EV batteries, and exporting two million tonnes of nickel ore annually subject to amendments to New Caledonia’s mining code.

title: Fabled Copper Corp. Provides Results of 2019 Exploration Program
summary: Fabled Copper Corp. reported results from its 2019 exploration at the ChurchKey and Muskwa properties in British Columbia, including surface sampling up to 22.69% Cu and drilling intersections targeting the Neil vein. Some drill intervals intersected chalcopyrite but initial assays recorded no copper, prompting analysis verification.

title: London copper eases as virus toll continues to rise
summary: London LME copper fell as the coronavirus death toll in China continued rising, weakening the near-term demand outlook. The article also shows declines in LME aluminium and nickel. It cites Hubei’s rising cases and notes potential disruption fears for LME’s Hong Kong event, reflecting risk to industrial activity.

title: Anglo American's nickel production up 1% in 2019
summary: Anglo American said nickel output met its 2019 full-year target: 11,700 mt in Q4 (up 3% YoY) and 42,600 mt for 2019 (up 1%). 2020 guidance remains 42,000-44,000 mt. Operations include Minas-Rio ramp-up, partially offset by Chile drought and other mine transitions.

title: Minim-Martap bauxite deposit : Canyon Resources announces launch of exploitation for 2022
summary: Canyon Resources says it expects to launch exploitation of the Minim-Martap bauxite deposit in Northern Cameroon in 2022. The project involves road and rail logistics to move ore to Douala/Kribi for export, targeting about 3 million tons annually then scaling up, potentially improving future aluminium raw-material supply expectations.

title: SDK Develops AI-Based Image Analysis System To Improve Spherical Alumina Production
summary: Showa Denko (SDK) developed an AI-based image analysis system with BLUE TAG to inspect and quantify spherical alumina sphericity defects. The system will be deployed at an SDK line in April and targets faster, more consistent quality control by matching skilled operators’ judgments and improving inspection accuracy over time.

title: Endangered species throw roadblock in path of Rosemont Copper mine
summary: A federal judge overturned environmental permits for Hudbay Minerals’ proposed Rosemont open-pit copper mine, citing failures to assess impacts on endangered species. The ruling delays the project and raises uncertainty about future copper supply timelines, supporting a modest bullish bias for copper prices over the coming weeks.

title: FPX Nickel: Developing Canada's Next Nickel District
summary: FPX Nickel reports leach testing of Baptiste concentrates with 98.8–99.5% nickel recoveries, producing high-purity chemical solution suitable for battery-grade nickel sulfate and cobalt sulfate. The company is advancing an updated PEA for its Decar Nickel District project, positioning it as potentially low-cost and large-scale.

title: EU launches anti-dumping investigation on China aluminium products
summary: The EU launched an anti-dumping investigation on Chinese aluminium products following a complaint from European Aluminium representing seven producers. The Commission cited negative impacts from import volumes and prices. Supporters called for urgent duties, while China’s industry association opposed the move and said it would respond. Aluminium extrusions face existing duties elsewhere.

title: First Quantum says no expansion at Zambia copper mine until 2024
summary: First Quantum says it will not expand its Zambia copper mine until 2024. The decision delays incremental copper supply growth, which can reduce near-term expectations for future output and keep the market tighter than previously assumed, typically exerting downward pressure on copper prices over coming days to weeks.

title: EU launches anti dumping investigation on China aluminum products | Politics
summary: The European Commission opened an anti-dumping investigation into whether China is dumping aluminium extrusions into the EU. The EU said evidence indicates import volumes and prices have negatively impacted the market. European Aluminum welcomed the move and urged rapid launch of anti-dumping duties, which could tighten supply.

title: India Has Now Become a Net Importer of Copper. What Comes Next?
summary: India’s refined copper balance has flipped from net exports to net imports, driven largely by the May 2018 closure of Vedanta’s Tuticorin smelter, cutting national refined output and exports. The article notes rising import volumes and emphasizes downstream and policy costs, implying tighter copper supply conditions.

title: Aluminium Bahrain's profit drops 91% YoY to $14.31m in FY 2019
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba), the world’s largest smelter outside China, reported FY2019 profit of $14.31m, down 91% YoY. Results were driven by higher metal sales volume from Line 6 ramp-up, but partly offset by lower LME prices, which declined 15% YoY.

title: EU's potential anti-dumping duties could take a toll on China's aluminium extrusion exports
summary: The European Commission launched an anti-dumping investigation into Chinese aluminium extrusion exports after complaints from EU producers. The article notes China’s sizable shipment volumes to the EU and that duties may be imposed provisionally within about seven to eight months, potentially reducing Chinese availability and supporting aluminium-focused prices.

title: Ample supplies weighed on spot copper premiums
summary: Shanghai spot copper premiums fell sharply as sellers and cargo holders destocked amid ample supply. High-quality premiums narrowed to 40-50 yuan/mt over the SHFE February contract, while standard premiums declined and hydro-copper discounts deepened. Expectations of further inflows and slow downstream recovery after COVID weighed on the near-term market.

title: Global xEV Battery Market: Nickel Deployment Up 39% In 2019
summary: Adamas Intelligence data show nickel usage in passenger xEV batteries rose 39% in 2019, with China up 56% despite only modest EV sales growth. The market is shifting toward high-nickel cathodes like NCM 811, and Tesla was a major driver in Europe, implying stronger nickel demand.

title: Pacific Rim receives registration approval for nickel-cobalt project
summary: Pacific Rim Cobalt said Indonesia has approved the registration of its Cyclops nickel-cobalt project licence, a step toward transferring it to a foreign investment licence under central government administration. The project in Papua has extensive drilling, permits, and positive drilling and scoping test results for nickel-rich material processing.

title: Comet Resources' Capital Raising Provides Strong Endorsement for Barraba Copper Project Acquisition
summary: Comet Resources says it secured firm commitments for a $2M capital raising to acquire the Barraba copper exploration project in NSW and will seek shareholder approval. The company plans drilling and geophysics on the project, which targets VMS copper zones, potentially supporting copper sentiment despite no near-term production impact.

title: Indonesia issued benchmark nickel ore prices for February
summary: Indonesia’s Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources issued February benchmark nickel ore prices, higher than prevailing market levels, to raise domestic nickel ore pricing after it banned exports from January. Benchmarks for various nickel grades were set at $28.37–$31.71/wmt FOB, aiming to rebalance profits toward miners.

title: More copper smelters to cut output in February on sulphuric acid storage capacity shortages
summary: Sulphuric acid storage shortages have led more Chinese copper smelters to cut output in February. SMM estimates copper cathode output falls about 3–5% month on month, while logistics disruptions from COVID-19 restrictions affect sulphuric acid movements and inventories.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong hit record high
summary: Copper cathode inventories at four Guangdong warehouses rose to a record 96,600 mt on Feb 18, up 4,800 mt from the prior year’s peak, with expectations to breach 100,000 mt soon. Transport restrictions between Guangdong and Guangxi are largely lifted, enabling faster smelter shipments into Guangdong. Warehouse supply and demand recovery appear to support inflows.

title: Coro Mining Corp. Announces Changes to its Board and an Update on  Progress for its Flagship Marimaca Copper Project
summary: Coro Mining announced board leadership changes and updates on its Marimaca copper project in Chile, including an updated oxide copper mineral resource and an ongoing PEA expected in early 2020. The company highlights low-cost open-pit and SX-EW processing prospects, but no immediate production or market-impacting decisions are stated.

title: China's copper imports and aluminium consumption to drop again in 2020 -Antaike
summary: Antaike forecasts China’s refined copper imports to fall 12.7% in 2020 and says coronavirus logistics and high sulphuric acid inventories have led smelters to cut output, narrowing but still leaving a market surplus. For aluminium, it projects slightly lower consumption alongside new smelting capacity additions, pressuring balances.

title: China's copper imports and aluminium consumption to drop again in 2020 -Antaike
summary: Antaike projects China’s refined copper imports will fall 12.7% in 2020, with coronavirus-related logistics and high sulphuric acid inventories forcing recent smelter production cuts. The market is seen in surplus. Aluminium consumption is expected to dip slightly while capacity additions, including Yunnan, raise supply.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Feb 18): Shanghai copper steadied at 2-week high as investors weighed coronavirus impact
summary: SMM reports Chinese reopening and falling new COVID-19 cases calmed markets, lifting Shanghai nonferrous closes mostly higher. SHFE copper and nickel rose less than 0.1%, while aluminium gained about 0.3%. Lingering worries about the epidemic’s economic impact capped further gains in base metals.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Announces Q4 and Full Year 2019 Financial Results
summary: Copper Mountain Mining reported Q4 and full-year 2019 results and said 2020 copper output should rise 20–33% versus 2019. The company also expects C1 cash costs to fall about 28% to $1.30–$1.45/lb and AISC to be near $2.00. Overall, operating improvements are highlighted.

title: Minim-Martap and Ngaoundal bauxite deposits: New estimates could make them the largest deposits in the world
summary: Canyon Resources’ Camalco subsidiary released early results expanding its estimates for the Minim-Martap and Ngaoundal bauxite deposits in Cameroon, identifying more bauxite-bearing plateaux and raising total potential. The new estimate includes significant high-grade bauxite for aluminium production, supporting improved supply expectations and boosting sentiment toward aluminium.

title: Coro Mining Releases Update on Marimaca Copper Project
summary: Coro Mining updated its Marimaca copper project in Chile, reporting a significantly larger oxide mineral resource estimate and identifying additional near-deposit oxide targets. The company is advancing a Preliminary Economic Assessment using a stand-alone open-pit and SX-EW processing approach, citing low development and operating costs, which is mildly supportive for copper sentiment.

title: EMX Royalty Executes Agreement to Sell Three Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Projects in Norway to Pursuit Minerals
summary: EMX executed an option agreement with Pursuit Minerals over three Norwegian nickel-copper-cobalt projects, with EMX receiving a 3% NSR royalty plus advance and milestone payments. The assets are described as historic Ni-Cu-Co sulfide systems, but no near-term production or supply changes are indicated.

title: Copper picks up as new coronavirus cases fall for 2nd day
summary: Copper rose modestly as China’s reported new coronavirus cases fell for a second straight day, easing concerns about demand from the world’s top metals consumer. The piece also notes updated LME/SHFE prices for aluminium and nickel, reflecting broader risk sentiment rather than a specific new supply or policy shock.

title: With Scrap Aluminum Value In The Tank, Hambro Looks To Bring Recycling To Klamath, Gasquet, Smith River
summary: Hambro Forest Products says the value of scrap aluminum paid for California CRV containers has fallen substantially—about 25% since 2018, with recent deliveries dropping from 41 cents/lb to a processor-reported 27 cents/lb. The lower scrap prices threaten recycling-center profitability, prompting proposals for expanded local buy-back services.

title: BHP Leans into Copper, Warns of Coronavirus Impact
summary: BHP reported higher copper output for the six months ended Dec. 31, 2019, and kept 2019–20 guidance unchanged. CEO Henry said coronavirus-related uncertainty is weighing on Chinese demand and could reduce near-term copper demand, though BHP sees underlying copper fundamentals as sound and expects demand growth with caveats.

title: Alumina prices to extend near-term rally on coronavirus impact
summary: SMM says China’s coronavirus outbreak is expanding alumina refinery capacity cutbacks to 4.6 million mt/year and leaving demand-supply imbalance largely unresolved. Logistics recovery is gradual, while smelters face falling alumina inventories. Some producers raise purchase prices and switch sourcing, supporting firmer near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: Sudbury, Vale Superstack, reduced carbon pollution, Copper Cliff
summary: Vale’s Copper Cliff smelter stack (“Superstack”) is nearing retirement and being replaced by two smaller chimneys. Emissions controls (e.g., lower SO2 and particulate) and reduced natural gas consumption are expected to cut maintenance costs and fuel use. This could modestly support copper supply margins in the near term.

title: Copper rises on China stimulus hopes, drop in virus cases
summary: Copper prices rose as hopes for additional Chinese stimulus lifted risk sentiment and as new coronavirus cases declined. The outlook for China’s economy and metal demand improved; firms in Hubei received temporary social-insurance relief. The article also notes gains in LME aluminum and nickel alongside copper.

title: Copper advances on China stimulus hopes, drop in virus cases
summary: Copper prices rose on hopes of additional Chinese stimulus and signs the virus outbreak is stabilizing, improving sentiment for the world’s top metals consumer. The piece cites policy relief for firms in affected areas and possible financial support. It also notes small concurrent moves in LME aluminium and nickel and mentions copper production/inflow fundamentals.

title: February aluminium plate, strip producer operating rates to hit three-year low
summary: SMM expects aluminium sheet, plate and strip producers’ operating rates in February to fall by over 10 percentage points versus January, the lowest level for the same month in three years. COVID-19 shutdowns and delayed approvals, travel restrictions, and slow end-user reopenings are cited.

title: Egypt Aluminum announces public tender for engineering consultants
summary: Egypt Aluminum (EGAL) plans to announce a public tender for engineering consultancy specialized in managing aluminum smelter projects. The move supports its seventh line project aimed at increasing primary aluminum production. While it signals future supply expansion, the tender and project timing are not immediate enough for a clear short-term price effect.

title: Indonesia Consolidates Nickel Production to Feed Growing EV Battery Market
summary: American Manganese begins feed testing for its RecycLiCo demonstration plant, processing lithium-ion battery cathode scrap to optimize leaching and chemical consumption and improve extraction efficiency for lithium, nickel, manganese, and cobalt. The update is focused on staged testing rather than commercial-scale output or immediate supply changes.

title: Century Aluminum Launches New Line of Low-Carbon Aluminum Products
summary: Alcoa announced expansion of its Sustana line with EcoSource, a low-carbon smelter-grade alumina brand with a maximum 0.6 t CO2e/t alumina. The company says it outperforms the industry average and cites lower-refinery emissions, which may support demand for compliant alumina feedstock and bolster aluminium sentiment.

title: Golden Arrow Commences Drill Program at Indiana Gold-Copper Project
summary: Golden Arrow Resources began a diamond drilling program at its Indiana gold-copper project in Chile within an IOCG belt. The company plans initial drilling of at least 2,500 metres in twelve holes to confirm grades and widths of high-grade vein targets, with additional drilling if results warrant.

title: In Amarillo, Copper Workers' Strike Enters Fourth Month with No End in Sight
summary: A copper workers’ strike at Asarco’s Amarillo refinery has entered its fourth month with no end in sight, alongside additional mine strikes in Arizona. Workers cite disputes over wages, health costs, and pensions. The stoppages likely cut near-term copper output, tightening supply expectations despite limited strikebreaking.

title: Copper Futures 2-Week Pullback from the Low Loses Steam
summary: Copper futures show renewed selling interest, with support near 2.5780 (23.6% Fibo) and the 100-period SMA around 2.5740. Indicators (MACD near/just below zero, RSI in bearish territory) suggest negative momentum. A breakdown below 2.5740 could drive a move toward 2.5360 and 2.4839 support.

title: Primary aluminium inventories extended gains as demand has yet to recover
summary: SHANGHAI Feb 20 (SMM): China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots rose again, increasing 137,000 mt in the week to Feb 20 to 1.23 million mt. The build is attributed to demand not yet recovering amid the coronavirus outbreak, suggesting weaker near-term aluminium fundamentals.

title: Freeport Indonesia Sets Date for New Copper Smelter Construction
summary: Freeport Indonesia says it expects to start construction of a new East Java copper smelter in August, with site prep nearly complete. The project is required to secure Grasberg mining rights and is aimed at producing 500,000–600,000 tonnes of copper cathode annually.

title: China to offer tariff exemptions on US copper concentrate, scrap imports
summary: China will allow applications from March 2 for tariff exemptions on US-origin copper concentrate and scrap (25% duty under Section 301).
