The move is expected to matter more for concentrate than scrap, potentially expanding feedstock supply to Chinese smelters amid tight ore supply, while quota limits temper scrap effects.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 22,500 mt on week
summary: SMM data in China showed 6063 aluminium billet inventories rose for a second consecutive week, increasing by 22,500 mt from Feb 13 to 193,100 mt as of Feb 20. The build was reported across major consumption areas including Foshan, Wuxi, Changzhou, Huzhou and Nanchang.

title: Tariff exemptions to have little impact on China's aluminium scrap imports
summary: China will allow one-year tariff exemptions for 25% duties on US aluminium scrap starting March 2, but US scrap will remain subject to the 25% tariff before entering China. Importers are expected to keep using processing trade to avoid duties. Quotas and import restrictions mean volumes should barely change, limiting aluminium price impact.

title: Castillo Copper : Formal Share Sale Agreement Signed
summary: Castillo Copper says it has signed a formal share sale agreement to acquire four copper projects in Zambia from Zed Copper, following ASX waiver conditions. It will issue shares and performance shares tied to JORC resource and feasibility milestones, plus a 2% net smelter return royalty. Near-term copper price impact appears limited.

title: $26mln Islamic financing for Oman copper-gold project
summary: Al Hadeetha Resources secured RO 10 million Islamic financing to develop its Washihi-Mazzaza copper-gold project in Oman. The funds will support mine-site infrastructure for a planned 1 mtpa copper concentration plant. The company also named CGM as EPC contractor and formalized a mining contractor arrangement, maintaining development momentum.

title: Max Resource Reports 2.2% Copper and 12g/t Silver Over 15-metre Open-Ended, Composite Grab at the CESAR Project, Colombia
summary: Max Resource Corp. reported open-ended rock chip intervals from its 100% owned CESAR copper-silver project in Colombia, including grades up to 2.2% copper over 15 metres and additional higher-grade samples. The company cautions grab samples may not be representative and is awaiting further assays from a new zone.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Feb 20): Shanghai copper edged higher as gains capped by strong US dollar
summary: SMM says Shanghai base metals closed mostly higher, but gains were capped by a stronger US dollar after FOMC minutes signaled steady US rates. China’s PBOC cut LPR to support firms amid the coronavirus impact, supporting sentiment. Copper edged up, nickel fell slightly, and aluminium dropped ~0.3%.

title: Pacific Rim Featured in Publication Spotlighting Dramatic Growth in Nickel Market
summary: Pacific Rim Cobalt says it received Indonesian government approvals for its Cyclops nickel and cobalt project after a revised registration process, citing favorable policy support tied to EV battery demand. The editorial link emphasizes Indonesia consolidating nickel production, implying improved supply prospects that can be bullish for nickel prices.

title: Century Aluminum Company Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2019 Results
summary: Century Aluminum reported Q4 and full-year 2019 results, noting higher primary aluminium shipments driven by ongoing Hawesville restart and Sebree returning to full production. Net sales declined mainly due to lower LME prices. Management said improved industrial activity and low inventories supported sentiment, but near-term weakness reflected the virus outbreak.

title: THEMAC Resources Group Receives Important U.S. Army Corps Authorization for the Copper Flat Mine
summary: THEMAC Resources said the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers authorized its Copper Flat Mine under Nationwide Permit 44, allowing mining activities subject to Clean Water Act requirements. The approval follows earlier BLM and state permits, moving the copper project toward full permitting and eventual production.

title: Trump Labor Board Could Determine Outcome Of Monthslong Amarillo Copper Strike
summary: Copper workers at ASARCO (Amarillo, with additional Arizona strikes) have been on strike for months over benefit and health-cost changes. The NLRB will decide if it’s an unfair-labor-practices strike or an economic strike, which affects replacement hiring. The ongoing dispute creates near-term uncertainty around copper refinery output.

title: Vale Reports 4Q Net Loss of $1.56 Billion After Impairment Charges on Nickel, Coal Mines
summary: Vale reported a fourth-quarter net loss of $1.56 billion, citing impairment charges linked to nickel and coal mines. Such write-downs typically reflect weaker expected cash flows and can raise market concerns about nickel production economics, potentially weighing on near-term nickel price expectations.

title: Pursuit Minerals pursues European nickel targets to meet growing battery metal demand
summary: Pursuit Minerals is pursuing additional European nickel sulphide projects in Norway, targeting battery-metal demand tied to rapidly expanding lithium-ion production for EVs. The company frames the move as enabling supply to battery manufacturers, which could reinforce bullish sentiment for nickel due to tighter future availability expectations.

title: Latin Resources and First Quantum re-confirm Peru copper joint venture
summary: Latin Resources and First Quantum’s Peruvian joint venture will remain on track after an extension linked to delays in permitting. Government approval received this week allows drilling permitting to proceed at Latin’s Pachamanca copper asset. Antares can earn majority via surveys and 4,000m of drilling, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks flat amid sluggish trades
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories were flat at about 19,000 mt with no new port arrivals. Import arbitrage remains closed, with losses widening to around 1,500 yuan/mt and warrant premiums near $200/mt. LME nickel cash discounts versus three-month expanded, pointing to sufficient nearby supply.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Feb 21): Shanghai base metals mostly lower on renewed virus fears; copper fell to 1-week low
summary: Shanghai base metals mostly fell as renewed coronavirus concerns in South Korea and other Asian economies revived risk aversion. On SHFE, copper dropped about 0.86% to a one-week low, aluminium fell 0.69% to the lowest close since Feb 4, and nickel slid 1.49% on short-position buildup.

title: Alizz Islamic Bank to lend on Omani copper-gold mine | News
summary: Alizz Islamic Bank plans to sign a $26 million loan for Alara Resources’ Al Hadeetha copper-gold project in Oman. Financing of a copper development project can bolster expectations for potential future copper supply and support market sentiment. The impact is likely modest because details on production timing are limited.

title: As Indonesia Looks to Expand Nickel Production, Companies Involved in Process Stand to See Substantial Benefit
summary: Indonesia’s earlier nickel ore export ban to January 2020 is expected to disrupt Chinese NPI feedstock flows and tighten global refined nickel supply despite existing deficits. The piece also highlights COVID-19-driven logistical and mine/HPAL-related uncertainty outside China, implying additional short-term support for nickel prices.

title: Garibaldi Drills 9.3 Meters Grading 7.2% Nickel, 3.6% Copper and 4.8 G/t Palladium-Platinum-Gold as Lower Discovery Zone Expands and Thickens to the North
summary: Garibaldi Resources reported drilling intercepts at its Nickel Mountain project, including 9.83 meters of massive sulphides grading 7.2% nickel and 3.6% copper, plus additional nickel-copper zones. The company says the Lower Discovery Zone expands and thickens north, but no production impacts are mentioned.

title: Coronavirus is double shock for China's giant aluminum sector: Andy Home
summary: Coronavirus measures are hitting China’s aluminum demand hard just as the market expects a post-holiday recovery. Fabricators are delayed in lockdown zones, while smelters keep running, pushing up ShFE stocks. Supply chain disruptions to bauxite and alumina refining add further instability, reinforcing bearish aluminum price pressure and limiting rebounds.

title: West Musgrave Copper and Nickel Project, Australia
summary: West Musgrave is a planned open-pit copper-nickel sulphide project in Western Australia (Nebo-Babel deposits) expected to produce about 41,000t copper and 35,000t nickel annually in the first five years. It is under construction since Nov 2022 and aims to start in Q2 2026, with a processing plant for separate concentrates.

title: Base Metals Weekly Round-Up: Nickel Squanders Recovery
summary: Nickel slid on the LME after earlier gains from six-month lows faded amid COVID-19 and broader market uncertainty. Copper moved sluggishly, only slightly above recent lows. Wood Mackenzie cited likely Chinese shutdowns affecting base metals supply, refining and demand, weighing sentiment across the complex.

title: Automotive Parts Aluminum Die Casting Market - Growth, Trends, and Forecast (2020
summary: The piece promotes a report on aluminum die casting for automotive parts, arguing EPA/CAFE pressure for lighter cars and rising EV production should boost aluminum die-cast demand. It also flags aluminum price volatility from sanctions/trade wars as a hindrance. Overall, impacts are mixed and not immediate for prices.

title: Copper falls on fears of coronavirus spread and strong dollar
summary: Copper prices fell as fears grew that China’s coronavirus outbreak could spread and curb global growth and metals demand, despite earlier support from China’s rate cut. A stronger U.S. dollar further pressured prices. LME also ended lower for aluminium and nickel, reflecting broad risk-off sentiment.

title: EU aluminum firms' dumping complaints groundless, Chinese association says
summary: China’s nonferrous industry association says an EU anti-dumping probe into Chinese aluminium extrusions is groundless and that there is no dumping or damage to EU industries. The statement follows the European Commission opening an investigation after complaints by European Aluminium. It also threatens potential countermeasures.

title: Aluminum bottled water going mainstream; Chicago company at the forefront
summary: A Chicago-based startup says bottled water in aluminum containers is moving into mainstream retail despite early skepticism that consumers wouldn’t pay more than for plastic packaging. The story frames wider adoption of aluminum bottles as growing demand for aluminium packaging materials.

title: EU aluminium firms' dumping complaints groundless, Chinese association says
summary: China’s nonferrous industry association said an EU anti-dumping probe into Chinese aluminium extrusions is groundless and that there is no dumping or damage to EU industries. The EU opened the investigation after a complaint, and China signaled possible countermeasures, though no final ruling was reported.

title: Copper bounces despite rise in virus cases, dollar slips
summary: Copper rebounded on Friday as U.S. data weakened the dollar, prompting late speculative buying despite rising coronavirus cases in China and concerns over demand. The piece notes broader LME moves: nickel fell and aluminium edged up slightly, reflecting mixed risk sentiment across industrial metals.

title: Primary aluminium inventories increased 84,000 mt over weekend
summary: SMM data show China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots increased by 84,000 mt from Feb 20 to Feb 24, reaching 1.314 million mt. The build occurred across multiple consumption areas, as demand recovered only slowly amid the ongoing coronavirus outbreak, implying weaker near-term tightness.

title: Spot copper trades revived on reduced futures prices, returning of downstream producers
summary: Shanghai spot copper activity improved on Feb 24 as downstream buyers increased purchases after SHFE futures eased and discounts narrowed versus the March contract. Sellers held firmer offers but cut discounts to stimulate trades. SHFE 2003 fell 0.61% by noon, while spot discounts moderated and trading volumes recovered.

title: China bauxite imports exceeded 100 million mt in 2019, up 21.91%YoY
summary: China imported 100.66 million mt of bauxite in 2019, up 21.9% year-on-year, with Guinea, Australia and Indonesia supplying over 94%. SMM notes refinery preferences for specific bauxite types and expects imports to remain above 100 million in 2020, with volumes sensitive to logistics and exporter stability.

title: Indonesia's Weda Bay nickel project to put two RKEFs under operation
summary: Indonesia’s Weda Bay nickel project plans to commission two 42,000 kVA RKEFs for nickel pig iron, targeting first output in March at the earliest. Once stabilised, the units are expected to produce around 1,800 mt of NPI per month. Indonesia’s January NPI Ni-content production rose month-on-month.

title: Funds sell copper as coronavirus hits physical supply chains: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist Andy Home reports funds have cut long positions and turned bearish on CME copper as 2019-nCoV freezes China’s manufacturing recovery and disrupts physical supply chains. Goldman and Citi forecast a meaningful near-term demand shock, surging stocks (ShFE) and pressures from logistics and smelter constraints.

title: Lindian hits high grade bauxite in Guinea
summary: Lindian Resources’ maiden auger drilling at its Gaoual bauxite project in Guinea reportedly hit consistently high-grade conglomerate-hosted bauxite, with drill results exceeding 60% aluminium oxide across much of the Bouba Plateau. Management says the findings are a major step toward resource definition and future processing.

title: Century Aluminum (CENX) Q4 Earnings and Sales Top Estimates
summary: Century Aluminum’s Q4 results beat estimates despite lower revenues, with primary aluminium shipments up 7.3% year over year due to the Hawesville restart. The company cites improved industrial activity, support from the U.S.-China trade agreement, normalized alumina costs, declining carbon prices, and lower power costs.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ahead of Schedule at Kakula Copper Project
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said underground development at its Kakula copper mine is advancing ahead of schedule, with over eight kilometres completed and monthly progress for February expected to beat plan. The company cites progress on access drives and high-grade ore zone development using large mining equipment, indicating improved future throughput potential.

title: Garibaldi Reports 7.2 percent Nickel at Nickel Mountain
summary: Garibaldi Resources reported that recent 2019 drill holes at its Nickel Mountain magmatic nickel sulfide system intersected significant near-surface massive sulfides. One hole returned 9.83m grading 7.2% nickel and 3.6% copper, suggesting expanding high-grade mineralization and improving future supply prospects.

title: United States adjusts steel and aluminum tariffs | Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE)
summary: The U.S. maintains a 10% tariff on aluminum imports and adds a tariff framework covering aluminum derivatives, citing national security concerns. Commerce says domestic capacity hasn’t met removal thresholds. A White House proclamation updates the tariff schedule and grants exemptions for certain countries, potentially reducing U.S. aluminum imports and supporting prices.

title: The Copper Market Is A Coiled Spring
summary: The article attributes early-2020 copper price volatility to coronavirus disruptions to global supply chains and trade uncertainty. It notes a rebound driven by concerns over refined metal shortages, while arguing that structural demand growth (EVs, grids, infrastructure) will outstrip supply, implying a bullish outlook for copper.

title: Alumina profit halves on less China demand
summary: Australian alumina miner profits halved as weaker Chinese demand reduced alumina prices and earnings. The US-China trade war hurt aluminium demand and pushed prices down in 2019. The firm expects improvement in 2020 as trade friction eases and demand grows, helping balance the alumina market and absorb surplus.

title: Evertiq - Lotte Aluminium to set up manufacturing in Hungary
summary: Lotte Aluminium will invest EUR 133 million to build a plant in Tatabánya, Hungary, producing aluminium anode foils for batteries. The facility is slated to begin production in June 2021 and create 107 jobs. The expansion supports incremental aluminium demand tied to Europe’s growing e-mobility manufacturing.

title: EU's last nickel smelter heads for the gallows, or an afterlife
summary: Greece’s EU’s last nickel smelter, Larco, is at risk of shutting down after the state stops funding it and sets a deadline for a buyer before bankruptcy. High electricity/emissions costs and unresolved illegal state-aid repayment restrict investment, threatening reduced nickel output in the EU.

title: Greece: Europe's only nickel factory facing closure
summary: Greece’s state-owned Larco, Europe’s only nickel processor, faces closure and may halt production as it sells under financial distress. With large debt and over a thousand jobs at risk, the shutdown threatens nickel supply in Europe, supporting tighter market expectations in the near term.

title: Pacific Rim Cobalt Corporation: Pacific Rim Featured in Publication Discussing Indonesia's Strategy to Ramp Up Nickel Supply
summary: Pacific Rim Cobalt is featured in coverage of Indonesia’s strategy to consolidate and expand nickel production and chemical processing capacity to feed the growing EV battery market. The piece cites government support and exploration success, implying increased nickel supply expectations that could influence near-term nickel prices.

title: EnGold Engages SRK to Complete Resource Estimates at Spout and G1 Copper Zones
summary: EnGold engaged SRK Consulting to update Mineral Resource estimates for the Spout Lake deposit and to create a maiden resource estimate for the G1 copper zone at its Lac La Hache property in BC. The release highlights higher-grade copper intervals targeting underground extraction but no near-term production or supply disruption changes.

title: Copper drifts as investors worry about virus hitting demand
summary: Copper prices slipped into negative territory as investors feared coronavirus-related demand losses beyond China and potential disruptions to producer supply and labor. Copper treatment/refining charges rose amid virus-hit smelters. Nickel rebounded on Indonesia project-delay expectations, while aluminium was marginally higher as most LME prices stabilized.

title: Copper eases as coronavirus spread raises pandemic fears
summary: Copper prices fell after coronavirus spread worsened outside China, raising fears of a bigger hit to global growth. The article frames copper as a gauge of economic health. It also notes nickel project delays in Indonesia, while LME aluminium rose marginally and nickel gained, reflecting mixed metal responses amid risk-off sentiment.

title: Using surplus heat to pre-heat carbon anodes for aluminium electrolysis
summary: The study tests using surplus waste heat to pre-heat carbon anodes before they are inserted into Hall-Héroult aluminium electrolysis cells. Preheated anodes reach up to 150°C internally and >250°C on the surface, cutting energy consumption by up to 0.018 kWh/kg Al and reducing frozen bath formation with longer preheating.

title: London copper rises on hopes of stimulus to counter virus impact
summary: London copper edged up as investors hoped central-bank stimulus would offset coronavirus damage, though prices were capped amid accelerating spread beyond China. A Reuters poll suggests wider economic slowing. It also says nickel project development in Indonesia could be delayed; aluminium was largely flat on LME and ShFE.

title: Spot copper trades weakened on coronavirus fears, thinned enquires at month-end
summary: Spot copper transactions in Shanghai fell on Feb 26 as heightened coronavirus concerns dampened risk assets and month-end downstream enquiries. Offers for nearby February invoices stayed at large discounts versus the SHFE March contract, while March cargoes saw limited buying interest as discounts widened. SHFE 2003 fell 0.33% by morning.

title: India made final anti-dumping determination on aluminium and zinc coated flat products from Vietnam, Korea and China
summary: India’s Commerce Department issued final anti-dumping duties on aluminium and zinc coated flat products imported from Vietnam, South Korea and China. Duty levels for China range roughly from $56.48/mt to $128.93/mt, while South Korea and Vietnam face $13.07–84.47/mt and $23.63–173.1/mt, respectively.

title: Copper falls as spreading virus sparks pandemic fears
summary: Copper prices fell on coronavirus pandemic fears as the outbreak threatened global economic growth, with China—the biggest copper user—expected to slow. Hopes of stimulus partly limited losses. The same risk-off move pressured LME copper and also pulled down LME aluminium and nickel prices.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Feb 26): Shanghai base metals mostly fell as virus fears mounted; copper hovered at 2-week lows
summary: SMM reports most SHFE base metals fell amid escalating COVID-19 fears after new case spikes outside China and weak end-user consumption from travel/transport restrictions. On SHFE, nickel dropped about 1.5%, copper fell over 0.5% to two-week lows, and aluminium edged slightly lower. LME copper stocks jumped sharply.

title: Rio Tinto Updates Progress on Forum's Janice Lake Copper Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals reports Rio Tinto Exploration Canada’s progress on the Janice Lake sedimentary copper project in northern Saskatchewan. The winter access road is about 50% complete and preparations for drilling and surveys are underway. Rio Tinto has met its initial $3 million exploration commitment ahead of schedule and made option payments.

title: CanAlaska Options North Thompson Nickel Project in Manitoba to Fjordland Exploration
summary: CanAlaska entered a letter of intent with Fjordland Exploration to let it earn up to 80% in the North Thompson sulphide nickel project in Manitoba. The work involves staged exploration expenditures and payments, with CanAlaska operating early stages. The release is exploration-focused, not production-related.

title: Copper slides to 3-week low, inventories reinforce demand fears
summary: Copper prices slid to 3-week lows as LME warehouse stocks jumped nearly 40% in one day, strengthening fears of weaker demand amid coronavirus spread beyond China. Global equities fell and safe havens rose. The outbreak is also expected to delay Indonesian nickel projects, while aluminium was slightly lower.

title: Fjordland and CanAlaska Announce Agreement to Explore North Thompson Nickel Project
summary: Fjordland Exploration and CanAlaska announce a non-binding LOI giving Fjordland an option to acquire up to an 80% interest in the Hunter and Strong properties of the North Thompson Nickel project. The program targets Ni-Cu-PGE sulphide deposits near Vale’s Thompson mine, with drill-ready exploration targets and planned expenditures.

title: Peru's copper production grew 97% from 2008 to 2019 | News | ANDINA
summary: Peru’s copper production rose from 1.27 million tons in 2008 to 2.46 million tons in 2019, and EY projects output could reach nearly 3 million tons in 2020 (over 20% growth). Peru remains a major supplier, with most shipments going to China.

title: Canada asks U.S., Mexico to clamp down on offshore aluminum
summary: Canada is urging the U.S. and Mexico to strengthen monitoring of offshore aluminum imports into the USMCA free-trade zone, fearing China/Russia dumping and trans-shipment via Mexico. Quebec, home to most Canadian aluminum production, seeks faster identification and possible USMCA amendments if tariff circumvention is proven.

title: Critics blast State Department copper mine report
summary: U.S. lawmakers and environmental critics are challenging Twin Metals’ proposed sulfide copper-ore mine in northeastern Minnesota, citing risks of acid mine drainage and violations of the 1909 Boundary Waters Treaty. Rep. Betty McCollum drafted legislation to stop the project, pending congressional and Trump approval, raising potential supply uncertainty for copper.

title: China's nickel ore imports dropped 38% in January as Indonesia banned exports
summary: China’s nickel ore and concentrate imports fell 38% in January amid Indonesia’s nickel ore export ban from Jan 1. Imports from Indonesia dropped 44%, with further declines expected in February due to wet-season effects and no Indonesian supply. Ferronickel and NPI imports rose, but ore tightening is still bearish for nickel.

title: LME copper inventories jumped as coronavirus dampened demand in China
summary: LME-approved copper inventories surged 38.17% (61,175 mt) to 221,425 mt in one day, the highest since November. SMM links the buildup to coronavirus-driven demand weakness in China, disrupted transport, stranded cargoes, and reduced imports, which weakened spot prices and delayed demand recovery into mid-April.

title: Max Resource Reports AM North Discoveries with Values of 10.4% Copper + 88 g/t Silver at the CESAR Project, Colombia
summary: Max Resource Corp. reports two stratabound discoveries at its CESAR copper + silver project in Colombia. Initial AMN-1 results include 10.4% copper plus 88 g/t silver from a 1-metre rock chip sample, with AMN-2 assays pending. The company interprets findings as supporting a large copper system concept.

title: Aluminum Curtain Wall Market Size, Share & Trends Analysis Report By Type, By Application, By Region And Segment Forecasts, 2020
summary: The news release promotes a report projecting strong growth for the aluminum curtain wall market through 2027, citing increasing commercial construction and green-building regulations such as EPBD. It argues curtain wall systems can reduce HVAC costs and improve energy efficiency, supporting rising demand for aluminum building components.

title: Coronavirus to hit nickel and copper markets says Nornickel
summary: Russian miner Norilsk Nickel says China’s COVID-19 outbreak is a downside risk for both nickel and copper markets. Mobility restrictions and extended holidays disrupt supply-chain operations and may delay mine/smelter staffing and Indonesia NPI ramp-ups. The firm also expects slower demand recovery in Q1, creating short-term uncertainty.

title: Coronavirus to hit nickel and copper markets says Nornickel
summary: Russian miner Norilsk Nickel says the COVID-19 outbreak in China is a downside risk for early-2020 demand recovery and assumptions for both nickel and copper. It points to disruptions from mobility curbs, extended holidays and closures, slower mine/smelter ramp-ups, and possible delays to Indonesia NPI project staffing and construction.

title: Rockcliff Updates Talbot Deposit to 2.19M Indicated Tonnes at 4.44% Copper Equivalent
summary: Rockcliff Metals announced an updated mineral resource for its Talbot Property in Manitoba, reporting 2.19M tonnes indicated at 4.44% copper equivalent (and additional inferred tonnes at 2.98% CuEq). The company says tonnage increased and grades improved, supporting the next phase of work and potential future copper supply.

title: Sphinx Resources Ltd.: Sphinx's Results Support the Extension of the Shea Copper-Gold Zone and its Correlation with Geophysical and Geochemical Anomalies in Metavolcanic Rocks on the Calumet-Nord Property, MRC Pontiac, Quebec
summary: Sphinx Resources announced channel sampling, soil geochemistry, and induced polarization results on its Calumet-Nord property in Quebec. Data supports extending the Shea copper-gold zone across a 95-metre exposed outcrop and finding a sharply defined copper-gold soil signature tied to geophysical anomalies, prompting plans for drilling.

title: Argentina made final anti-dumping determination on Chinese aluminium sheet
summary: Argentina has issued its final anti-dumping determination on Chinese-origin aluminium sheet, setting duties of 80.14% of FOB value for specified 3xxx-series unalloyed/aluminium sheet thicknesses and sizes. Duties will be effective for five years from the announcement date, following higher temporary measures.

title: Exclusive: Aluminum smelter resurrected on Trump tariffs may close as losses mount
summary: Reuters reports that the Magnitude 7 Metals aluminum smelter in Missouri may close within 60 days due to mounting losses. Despite Trump-era aluminum tariffs protecting generic output, competitors’ value-added products are undercutting the firm. Weak demand amid coronavirus fears coincides with LME aluminum falling to the lowest level since 2016.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks grew slower on port congestion, fewer arrivals
summary: Shanghai bonded copper inventories rose to 337,300 mt in the week ended Feb 28, but the increase slowed versus the prior week. Port congestion and fewer arrivals delayed deliveries to bonded warehouses. More copper was delivered to LME-approved warehouses, suggesting subdued Chinese consumption tied to COVID-19 and helping ease bonded stock build-up pressure.

title: Aluminum smelter resurrected by Trump tariffs may close amid losses
summary: A Missouri aluminum smelter (Magnitude 7 Metals) reopened after U.S. aluminum tariffs but is losing money rapidly and may close within 60 days. Tariffs are described as failing to protect value-added output, while coronavirus-driven recession fears coincide with LME aluminum prices falling to the lowest since 2016.

title: Aluminum smelter resurrected on Trump tariffs may close as losses mount
summary: Magnitude 7 Metals’ reopened aluminum smelter in Missouri is losing money and could close within 60 days as tariffs protect only generic aluminum while foreign value-added products undercut U.S. shipments. Reuters cites LME aluminum dropping to a six-year low and plant prices sliding, intensifying recession-demand fears.

title: DGTR recommends antidumping duty on aluminium, zinc coated items from 3 nations
summary: India’s DGTR has recommended antidumping duties on aluminium (and zinc-coated) items from three nations. The move is intended to counter suspected dumping, likely increasing import costs and reducing competitive pressure on domestic supply. That tightening effect can support higher aluminium prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports extended decline by 750,000 wmt
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell by 750,000 wmt to 12.59 million wmt in the week to Feb 28, accelerating versus the prior week’s decline. In metal content, stocks dropped to 106,500 mt. Seven major ports saw inventories shrink by 660,000 wmt to 9.86 million wmt.

title: Apache tribe marches to protect sacred Arizona site from copper mine
summary: Hundreds of Apache tribe members marched to protect Oak Flat in Arizona from Resolution Copper’s planned development, citing cultural destruction and potential water pollution. The project would extract 1.9 billion tons of copper using block caving. The dispute raises risk of delays or constraints on future copper supply.

title: Aluminium and zinc hit multi-year lows as coronavirus spreads
summary: Industrial metals hit multi-year lows as coronavirus fears triggered risk-off sentiment and weaker Chinese demand. Copper fell with construction demand delayed, while LME aluminium dropped to a 40-month low amid Rusal expectations of a supply surplus. Nickel prices eased as LME stocks reached the highest since 2018.

title: Chibougamau Independent Mines Extends C-3 Copper-Gold Zone to  515 metres Vertical Depth
summary: Chibougamau Independent Mines reports that drilling extended the C-3 copper/gold zone to 515 m vertical depth and intersected two copper-gold mineralization zones, while a nearby shallow hole found no copper-gold values. Further drilling is planned to test additional zone edges and an IP anomaly on land.

title: Aluminium, zinc bounce after hitting multi-year lows on virus
summary: Industrial metals hit multi-year lows as coronavirus fears escalated and WHO risk was raised. Copper and zinc weakened on expected demand erosion from delayed China construction and rising China inventories. Aluminium fell to a 40-month low citing Rusal’s view of a supply surplus, while nickel also faced record-high LME stocks.

title: Second copper mine could tap massive ore reserve near Yerington
summary: Hudbay Minerals acquired the Ann Mason site near Yerington and is assessing feasibility to develop a very large, near-surface copper deposit (1.4 billion tons at 0.32% Cu). Pre-production could take 3–5 years and development would be open-pit, implying limited immediate impact on copper prices.

title: Western Copper and Gold Closes Private Placement and Announces CFO
summary: Western Copper and Gold closed a private placement raising about $1.95 million, with proceeds intended for development of its Casino Project and general corporate purposes. The project is a copper-gold mine in Canada. The financing and progress support modestly bullish near-term copper supply expectations. CFO appointment is non-price-relevant.

title: Canada Nickel Company Announces Maiden Resource at Crawford and Drilling Highlights
summary: Canada Nickel Company announced a maiden resource estimate and new drilling results at its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project in Ontario, highlighting nickel grades around 0.23–0.25% Ni and openness for further expansion. The update may slightly influence medium-term nickel supply expectations, but no near-term production changes are stated.

title: Pictou County residents charged with copper thefts | Local | News
summary: RCMP charged two residents for allegedly stealing copper wire from Nova Scotia Power substations across Pictou County and other areas. Police arrested them while attempting theft near live electrical equipment. The utility said significant live copper wire was stolen, posing safety risks and implying copper scrap supply disruptions.

title: THEMAC Resources Group Ltd Announces Update of Project Economics and Permitting for Copper Flat Project  - Press Release
summary: THEMAC Resources Group Ltd issued a press release updating the economics and permitting progress for its Copper Flat copper project. Better project economics and advancement of permits can strengthen expectations for eventual copper supply, typically supporting near-term copper price sentiment, though the magnitude depends on timelines and feasibility details.

title: Indonesia to issue rules on nickel ore price around late March
summary: Indonesia’s minerals ministry plans rules by late March to set a monthly benchmark floor for nickel ore prices, allowing only a limited buffer below it. The rules target smelters paying too-low prices and relate to royalty calculations amid Indonesia’s earlier nickel ore export ban and push for integrated processing.

title: Police charge suspects in copper wire thefts in Pictou County | Canada | News
summary: RCMP and local police in Nova Scotia charged two suspects in copper wire thefts from power substations across Pictou County and other areas. Officers arrested them near live NSP equipment and recovered evidence of theft. Charges include break and enter and possession of stolen property; the company warns of safety risk.

title: SaskPower warns of dangers of stealing copper wire from power poles
summary: SaskPower warns that people stealing copper grounding wire from power poles is dangerous and can destabilize the grid. The utility says it happens weekly in Saskatchewan and replacement costs are substantial, though copper theft is also met with police concern. The copper theft risk and replacement demand are modestly supportive for copper prices.

title: Smelters buying nickel ore below floor price will get sanction: ESDM Ministry
summary: Indonesia’s ESDM Ministry plans a March regulation to set and monitor a floor price for nickel ore following the January export ban. Smelters buying below the floor will face sanctions. The floor will be adjusted to international prices and miners’ operating costs, aiming to ensure fair ore prices.

title: Nickel rebounds on global policy stimulus hopes
summary: Nickel prices rebounded after an eight-month low, rising up to 3.5% on the LME as investors viewed recent sell-offs as excessive and increased expectations of government stimulus to counter coronavirus fallout. The piece also cites Indonesia’s plan to start a nickel ore benchmark floor by late March and reports concurrent copper/aluminium gains.

title: Nickel rises as virus cases in Indonesia spark supply concern
summary: Nickel prices rebounded from eight-month lows as Indonesia reported its first coronavirus cases, raising concerns that disruptions could reduce nickel ore and nickel pig iron output. Analysts noted production risk if the situation worsens, while stimulus hopes and a planned late-March price benchmark supported gains across LME and ShFE contracts.

title: Aluminium and nickel return to fundamentals with sanctions on Rusal in flux
summary: The piece suggests aluminium is moving back toward fundamentals as sanctions targeting Rusal remain in flux. By threatening or disrupting Rusal’s aluminium output and shipments, the news raises near-term supply risk and supports a bullish bias for aluminium pricing. Nickel is mentioned, but the shock centers on aluminium.

title: Spot copper concentrate TCs fall further in Q2, in line with SMM expectation
summary: Spot copper concentrate treatment charges (TCs) are falling further in Q2, matching SMM expectations. The update points to continued weakening in concentrate pricing and smelting contract economics, which can affect market sentiment around copper supply/demand balance and near-term refined copper expectations.

title: Aluminium and nickel return to fundamentals with sanctions on Rusal in flux
summary: The piece says aluminium and nickel are moving back toward fundamentals as sanctions on Rusal are in flux. Any interruption or uncertainty in Rusal’s ability to produce, ship, or sell metal can tighten prompt supply expectations, typically supporting higher prices in the near term for aluminium and possibly nickel.

title: China nickel manufacturing contracted for eleventh consecutive month in February
summary: SMM says China’s nickel downstream sectors saw an 11th straight month of contraction in February. The nickel downstream PMI fell to 41.24, driven by production cutbacks at stainless steel firms, persistent closures in electroplating, and weaker new orders across stainless, alloy and battery supply chains amid COVID-19.

title: SMM 101- Shanghai nickel rallies on renewed concerns over Indonesia export ban
summary: SMM reports Shanghai nickel rallied as renewed fears about an Indonesia export ban resurfaced. The renewed uncertainty raised expectations of tighter outbound nickel supply, improving the near-term supply/demand balance for traders. The move points to fresh risk premium in nickel pricing ahead of any policy decision.

title: Copper rebounds on hope for stimulus after dire factory data
summary: Copper and other industrial metals rebounded after dire factory data revived hopes of central-bank stimulus. China’s February factory contraction fueled recession fears, but markets priced imminent U.S. rate cuts. Nickel gains were also supported by uncertainty over Indonesia’s ore supply after its first COVID cases; aluminium rose modestly as well.

title: Ghana could lose collateral to Sinohydro in bauxite-backed-loan – IMF warns
summary: The IMF warns Ghana may struggle to repay a US$2 billion bauxite-backed loan to Sinohydro, with collateral potentially at risk. The repayment terms require rapid increases in bauxite output and refining. The report highlights risks to resource-financed production, affecting near-term alumina/bauxite expectations and sentiment.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Announces Start of Drilling at the Falcon Nickel Project
summary: ALX Resources says drilling has commenced at its Falcon Nickel Project in Saskatchewan, targeting magmatic nickel-sulphide mineralization. The company references historical and recent assays showing elevated nickel (and some copper) and ongoing EM and geochemical work to define drill targets, but no production impact is reported.

title: Federal Circuit Upholds President's Authority To Impose Section 232 Tariffs On Steel And Aluminum | Husch Blackwell LLP
summary: A Federal Circuit ruling affirmed the constitutionality of U.S. Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum, meaning the 25% steel and 10% aluminum tariffs remain in force. The court cited binding Supreme Court precedent and declined to overturn the delegation framework, leaving tariffs as the near-term policy driver.

title: Can Congo Become The World's Top Producer Of Copper Again?
summary: Ivanhoe Mines’ founder argues the DRC could regain top copper-producer status, citing 17% higher 2019 output and the ramp-up potential of the Kamoa-Kakula project starting in 2021. The piece highlights strong expected copper demand from EVs, power, wind and solar, despite current coronavirus-driven volatility.

title: London copper hits over 1-week high on stimulus hopes after poor Chinese data
summary: London copper rallied to a more-than-one-week high as grim Chinese manufacturing data triggered hopes of stimulus to offset coronavirus damage. LME three-month copper rose up to 1.4%. Broader risk sentiment improved alongside moves in nickel and aluminium, suggesting supportive near-term demand expectations despite the ongoing disruption.

title: Robert Friedland: Copper is the EV Story, Demand to Rise 900 Percent
summary: Robert Friedland of Ivanhoe Mines argues electrification will sharply raise metal demand, claiming copper demand for EVs could grow 900% and highlighting nickel as the biggest beneficiary because EV batteries are high in nickel. He frames this as part of governments’ stimulus and EV rollout plans, supporting bullish sentiment for copper and nickel.

title: EPA concludes Venturex copper-zinc project assessment
summary: Australia’s EPA has concluded its assessment of Venturex Resources’ Sulphur Springs copper-zinc project in Western Australia and has begun consultation on implementation conditions toward ministerial approval. The project has a stated mineral resource with significant copper, and moving closer to approval improves perceived future copper supply prospects.

title: NovaCopper High-Grade Copper Mineralization | Aktienforum | Aktien Forum | Diskussionsboard
summary: NovaCopper announced additional diamond drilling results from the South Reef Zone of its Bornite Property, reporting multiple drill holes intersecting high-grade copper mineralization (e.g., up to ~5% Cu over several meters). The update suggests improved prospects for future copper resources, but it is unlikely to affect near-term global copper prices materially.

title: Trigon Extends Agreement to Acquire High Potential 'Silver Hill' Copper and Silver Project for Three Months TSX Venture Exchange:TM
summary: Trigon Metals extended its memorandum of understanding by three months to negotiate and enter a definitive agreement to acquire the Silver Hill copper-and-silver exploration project in Morocco. The company cites early exploration showing high-grade copper mineralization and is preparing a NI 43-101 technical report, subject to further diligence and approvals.

title: How Did Bloomberg Get His Riches?; Alaska Copper Mine Threatens Fishing
summary: The segment reports that communities in southwestern Alaska are divided over a proposed copper mine, citing threats to the sockeye salmon ecosystem. The long-running dispute raises the risk of project delays or additional constraints on development, which could reduce near-term copper supply expectations and weigh on copper prices.

title: SPONSORED: Galileo, Next Fraser Range Nickel Success Story?
summary: The sponsored piece highlights Galileo Mining’s newly commenced reverse-circulation drilling at the Lantern Prospect in Australia’s Fraser Range nickel belt. It frames potential “good” or “outstanding” results as catalysts similar to Legend’s Mawson and Nova discoveries, boosting sentiment around future nickel discoveries and supply prospects.

title: Adavale Resources granted ex-BHP tenements near Kabanga nickel project
summary: Australia’s Adavale Resources received new nickel sulphide tenements adjoining Tanzania’s Kabanga project. The company plans field testing of historic targets near a large high-grade nickel deposit previously advanced by major operators. While it may improve long-term supply expectations, no production timelines or immediate supply changes are indicated.

title: Global aluminium producers offer second quarter premiums of $98-$105/Tonne - sources
summary: Japanese buyers and global aluminium producers are negotiating Q2 primary aluminium premiums of $98-$105/t over the LME cash price, up from $83/t in Q1. Producers cite firmer regional spot premiums in South Korea and a stronger Europe. Buyers argue coronavirus-driven demand faltering warrants lower bids.

title: Fed's rate cut interpreted as a positive, copper gains
summary: Copper rose 0.9% on the LME after traders interpreted the Fed’s emergency rate cut as easing liquidity conditions. Sentiment remained tied to coronavirus-driven demand worries in top consumer China, with investors watching China inventory trends. Aluminium and nickel also increased on the day, while broader growth concerns persisted.

title: Max Resource Reports Values of 24.8% Copper + 230 g/t Silver Over 4m by 1m Interval at the CESAR Project, Colombia
summary: Max Resource Corp. reported high-grade outcrop/rock-chip assays from its CESAR copper + silver project in Colombia, including 24.8% copper plus 230 g/t silver over 4m by 1m. The company says zones are open-ended and continues surface sampling ahead of drilling, but it remains early-stage exploration.

title: BRIEF-Anhui Fuhuang Steel Structure Signs Contract Worth 1.5 Bln Yuan For Nickel Project In Indonesia
summary: Anhui Fuhuang Steel Structure reportedly signed a contract worth 1.5 billion yuan for a nickel-related project in Indonesia. The deal could improve expectations for nickel demand tied to the project’s execution, providing mild near-term support to nickel prices, though timing and physical output impacts are unclear.

title: High grade bauxite strike blows out by 3.5km for Lindian
summary: Lindian Resources says it has expanded its Guinea Bouba bauxite strike length and found high-grade bauxite, with samples showing over 62% alumina and low contaminants. Guinea is a major bauxite region feeding alumina and aluminium. The update is exploratory, with drilling planned next month.

title: Ghana looking to AfDB for investment in an integrated aluminium industry
summary: Ghana’s vice-president says the AfDB has supported infrastructure and other projects and that the country is seeking further AfDB investment to develop an integrated aluminium industry. The plan would use Ghana’s bauxite deposits. The piece provides broader macro and infrastructure context without citing near-term aluminium production shifts.

title: Ball Corporation Achieves Global First With Aluminium Sustainability Certification
summary: Ball Corporation said it became the first aluminium beverage can maker to achieve Aluminium Stewardship Initiative (ASI) certification for its EMEA plants and is moving to 100% renewable electricity for beverage operations in several EU countries, Serbia and the UK. The company also highlights higher recycling and sustainable packaging growth.

title: CRU Group: Decline in Chinese Copper Demand Hard to Make Up
summary: CRU Group says Beijing’s stimulus may not prevent China’s copper demand from declining about 22% in Q1 y/y, making it difficult to recover later in 2020. CRU also downgraded 2020 from a deficit to a 200,000 ton surplus as demand falls, weighing on copper sentiment and price.

title: Exemption of port construction dues reduces costs at Chinese nickel ore importers
summary: China exempted foreign trade vessels from port construction dues and cut other port charges from March 1 to June 30 to reduce operating costs amid COVID-19 disruptions. Nickel ore importers benefit, with estimated savings per mt. However, seaborne nickel ore trades remain weak due to delayed demand recovery.

title: Here's Why Southern Copper (SCCO) Stock Holds Potential
summary: The article discusses Southern Copper’s growth prospects but highlights coronavirus-related disruption to industrial activity in China, the biggest metals consumer. It states the virus has caused a fresh plunge in copper prices and that global economic concerns are weighing on copper (and other metals) in the near term.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks dipped as Feb rate cut drove copper import financing
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell 3,500 mt to 333,800 mt in the week ended March 6 after a prior build. The decline followed Fed rate cuts that reduced import-financing costs, encouraging imports, while easing port congestion sped deliveries to bonded warehouses and domestic markets, potentially increasing near-term supply.

title: Copper Down on Economic Slowdown Fears
summary: Markets tumbled as COVID-19 uncertainty increased, raising fears of slower global growth and possible recession. Copper fell sharply and is down over 11% since mid-January, with CRU projecting a large year-on-year Chinese demand decline in Q1. Nickel also dropped, though it rose this week on Indonesia supply worries.

title: Trump Leaves Brazil Stranded on Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: Trump declined to promise whether the US will impose new steel and aluminum tariffs on Brazil, after prior comments suggested no new tariffs. The meeting with Bolsonaro highlights ongoing trade uncertainty. Any tariff action would shift US aluminium import expectations, but the article provides no clear near-term decision.

title: Trump: No Promises on Brazil Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: President Trump declined to promise continued delays on potential tariffs targeting Brazilian imports of steel and aluminum. Commenting at a dinner with Brazil’s Jair Bolsonaro, Trump said he would not commit to holding off. The tariff risk raises uncertainty around aluminium trade flows and pricing expectations in the near term.

title: China unwrought aluminium, aluminium products exports dropped 25% YoY in January-February
summary: China’s exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium products fell 25.2% YoY in January-February, reflecting COVID-19 shutdowns at aluminium processors and production resumption delays of up to 20 days. Deliveries were also suspended ahead of Lunar New Year, slowing export recovery and potentially tightening near-term supply.

title: Copper scrap consumption in China dipped 18% in January
summary: SMM says China’s copper scrap consumption fell 18.1% month-on-month in January to 157,500 mt, led by lower processor and smelter intake due to an earlier Chinese New Year holiday. A prior copper price rally widened the refined-scrap spread, supporting scrap-made copper rod output, while blister processing charges edged higher, easing scrap tightness.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong shrank for three days
summary: SMM reports that copper cathode social inventories in Guangdong fell for a third straight day as of March 9, reaching 115,900 mt, down 430 mt from March 6. Although inventories rose 13,600 mt over the week to March 6, SMM expects a near-term turning point supported by steady consumption recovery.

title: EGA signs deal with Vinacomin that extends supplies of Vietnamese alumina to the UAE until 2023
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) extended a three-year contract with Vietnam’s Vinacomin to supply up to 300,000 tonnes of alumina annually to the UAE. Alumina is the feedstock for aluminium smelters. The deal supports EGA’s continued intake and helps secure aluminium production requirements through 2023.

title: Copper inventories in Shanghai slowed increases for 4 weeks
summary: SMM data show Shanghai, Guangdong and Jiangsu copper cathode social inventories rose to 539,600 mt by March 6, but the pace of increase has slowed for four consecutive weeks. Improved downstream operations and logistics recovery supported consumption, narrowing Shanghai spot discounts as futures remain pressured by macro uncertainty.

title: Exploration firm Oroco Resource completes Altamura Copper acquisition
summary: Canadian explorer Oroco completes its acquisition of full ownership of the Altamura Copper asset, including the Santo Tomás porphyry copper project in northwest Mexico. The deposit contains fracture and disseminated copper and molybdenum sulphides. The deal is described as accretive, with no immediate production or supply shock mentioned.

title: U.S. Aluminum Industry Files Unfair Trade Cases Against Imports of Common Alloy Aluminum Sheet from 18 Countries
summary: The Aluminum Association filed AD/CVD petitions against imports of common alloy aluminum sheet from 18 countries, alleging dumping and subsidy-driven unfair pricing that has hurt U.S. producers and devastated domestic sheet prices. It cites China export diversion and rising low-priced volumes, after prior U.S. measures on Chinese sheet in 2019.

title: EGA extends deal with Vietnam's state-owned mining firm to procure alumina
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) extended a three-year deal to buy up to 300,000 tonnes of alumina annually from Vietnam’s Vinacomin. Alumina is the key feedstock for aluminium smelters. The contract continuation supports EGA’s production inputs as its Al Taweelah refinery ramps up.

title: Output In World's Largest Copper Mine Is Falling
summary: Chile’s Codelco reported another fall in January copper output to 118,600 tonnes, down 6.8% year-on-year, citing lower ore grades, water scarcity and social unrest. Chile’s copper exports also declined 2.3% in February due to weak Chinese demand and protests, while some private mines posted gains.

title: Xanadu Mines extends Stockwork Hill deposit with broad high-grade copper discovery
summary: Xanadu Mines says drilling at its Kharmagtai project in Mongolia has extended the Stockwork Hill copper zone beyond the current resource, including a 62.8m interval grading 1.16% copper. The company calls results pivotal and suggests a potentially significant copper-gold system may exist eastward.

title: China issued import quotas for another 100 mt of aluminium scrap
summary: China’s environmental authorities approved an additional 100 mt batch of aluminium scrap import quotas, lifting 2020 allowances to 284,549 mt. While earlier quota declines tightened supply and kept scrap prices elevated, SMM expects new seaborne inflows and virus-hit downstream demand to pressure scrap and secondary aluminium ingot prices in coming weeks.

title: Mining company plans cobalt, nickel and scandium project at Greenvale
summary: Australian Mines plans a major expansion of its Greenvale tenements and is building a demonstration-scale processing plant expected to start producing small quantities of cobalt, nickel, and scandium from November. It also has a feasibility study for a much larger project, but near-term output is limited.

title: MEED | Emirates Global Aluminium extends Vietnam contract
summary: MEED reports that Emirates Global Aluminium has extended its contract for deliveries to Vietnam. While full details are not provided, an extension generally suggests continued aluminium offtake and can support near-term aluminium demand expectations, potentially providing mild upward pressure on aluminium prices in the coming days to weeks.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Mar 10): Shanghai base metals rebounded after global rout amid oil, virus fears; nickel jumped more than 4%
summary: Shanghai base metals rebounded as coronavirus fears eased and expectations of more Chinese stimulus improved sentiment after a global rout driven by an oil price war. On SHFE, nickel jumped 4.2%, copper gained 1.8%, and aluminium rose 0.5%, reflecting risk-on trade and short-covering.

title: Amid market turmoil, Doctor Copper isn't panicking... yet
summary: Copper fell to a three-year low on market turmoil but quickly rebounded above $5,600 as short positions were largely already off and funds appeared to avoid further de-risking. The article links moves to China-related coronavirus recovery expectations; aluminium and nickel also bounced, indicating broadly supportive sentiment.

title: Petition Summary: Common Alloy Aluminum Sheet From Various Countries | Husch Blackwell LLP
summary: Petitioners filed for antidumping and countervailing duties on common alloy aluminum sheet (CAAS) imported from numerous countries, including Bahrain, Brazil, India, Turkey, and others. The scope covers specific thickness/roll forms and exclusions. If imposed, duties could lift costs and expectations for aluminum sheet availability.

title: Ambatovy 'exit' will not affect nickel, cobalt output in Madagascar, Sherritt says
summary: Sherritt says the Ambatovy “exit” will not affect nickel (and cobalt) output in Madagascar. The excerpt provides limited operational detail, but the key implication is reduced disruption risk to nickel supply, which should support expectations for near-term nickel prices. Other Fastmarkets text focuses on pricing corrections.

title: Ambatovy 'exit' will not affect nickel, cobalt output in Madagascar, Sherritt says
summary: Sherritt says Ambatovy’s planned “exit” will not affect nickel output in Madagascar, implying no immediate loss of supply from the operation. By lowering expectations of near-term production disruptions, the news is likely to support nickel sentiment and price direction in the short term.

title: Blackstone Intersects Massive Sulfide Nickel at King Cobra Discovery
summary: Blackstone Minerals announced new drilling results at its Ban Phuc project, including massive sulfide nickel mineralisation and high-grade disseminated nickel sulfide near surface (e.g., 39m @ 1.1% Ni and 28m @ 1.2% Ni). The discovery remains open and drilling continues, supporting bullish nickel sentiment.

title: Copper rises on stimulus hopes, unabating virus spread caps gains
summary: Copper prices rose Wednesday on stimulus hopes aimed at cushioning coronavirus fallout, though gains were limited as the outbreak worsened outside China. Reuters reports three-month LME copper up 0.6% and ShFE copper up 0.3%. LME nickel also rose 1.5% while virus spread risks remain.

title: Copper prices ease as stimulus promises fail to calm virus fears
summary: Copper prices eased as doubts about coronavirus stimulus effectiveness failed to calm virus fears, increasing economic damage concerns. The piece cites rising Italy deaths and new China cases. It also reports LME aluminum down and ShFE nickel lower on the day, indicating broad industrial-metal risk-off pressure.

title: JPMorgan Reaped $100 Million as China Squeezed Niche Nickel Market
summary: The piece’s headline says JPMorgan profited as China squeezed a niche nickel market, suggesting tighter availability and firmer pricing conditions. This would typically raise expectations for near-term nickel prices, though the missing body text limits certainty about magnitude and timing.

title: GLOBAL ALUMINIUM WRAP: Brazil main ports premium moves for first time in three months; backwardation dents Rotterdam premiums
summary: An Aluminium “global wrap” reports that Brazil’s main ports premium moved for the first time in three months, while backwardation dented Rotterdam premiums. title: Coronavirus Fears, Oil Price Plunge Send Copper to 3-Year Low
summary: Copper is reported to have fallen to a three-year low as coronavirus fears intensify and oil prices plunge. The combination suggests worsening near-term economic/demand expectations and a broader risk-off environment that typically weighs on industrial metal prices, especially copper.

summary: Imperial Metals announced partial results from two drill campaigns at the Red Chris copper mine in British Columbia. Intercepts include several copper-bearing zones, with select sections reporting high grades such as 1.7% and 2.5% Cu, and up to 4.7% Cu. The company is progressing resource definition and brownfields exploration.

summary: Copper Mountain Mining revised its British Columbia mine plan due to weak copper prices and coronavirus-related uncertainty. title: Copper Mountain Trims Plans on Coronavirus "Uncertainty"
summary: Copper Mountain Mining revised its Copper Mountain mine plan in Southern British Columbia, cutting the mining rate by 25% for the remainder of 2020, deferring construction and re-sequencing production in response to coronavirus-driven copper price uncertainty. The company also schedules some high-grade ore for 2021, aiming for better future copper pricing.

title: Ball Corporation Agrees to Acquire Tubex Aluminum Aerosol Packaging Facility in Brazil
summary: Ball Corporation agreed to acquire Tubex’s aluminum aerosol packaging facility near Sao Paulo, adding eight extruded aluminum can lines and expanding supply for personal care packaging in Brazil. The company cites growing demand for sustainable aluminum packaging, implying increased aluminum feedstock demand, but likely limited overall near-term price impact.

title: Copper Mountain Trims 2020 Plans as Coronavirus Ravages Market
summary: Copper Mountain Mining cut 2020 capex and delayed parts of its plan, slowing mining of copper-rich material and pushing higher-grade ore to 2021. It revised 2020 copper-equivalent production to 86-94 million pounds from 100-113 million, citing COVID-19-driven low copper prices and uncertainty.

title: Blackstone racks up more solid nickel sulphide hits in Vietnam
summary: Blackstone Minerals announced additional nickel sulphide drilling intercepts at its King Cobra and Ta Khoa projects in Vietnam, including higher-grade nickel zones and massive sulphide. It says results could improve economics for restarting the mothballed Ban Phuc concentrator and advancing downstream nickel sulphate plans for lithium-ion batteries.

title: Ball Corp. To Buy Tubex Aluminum Aerosol Packaging Facility In Brazil
summary: Ball Corp. agreed to buy Tubex, an aluminum aerosol packaging business near São Paulo, Brazil, for $80 million plus an earnout. The facility is expected to expand Ball’s aluminum aerosol packaging capacity, supporting aluminum demand expectations.

title: Excelsior Mining Completes Copper Cathode Offtake Agreement
summary: Excelsior Mining says it has completed a copper cathode offtake agreement. Secured offtake typically signals demand visibility and can provide modest near-term support for copper prices. The provided text includes no contract volume, terms, or timing details, limiting confidence on the magnitude.

title: Copper hits over 3-year low as growth fears deepen after U.S. travel curbs
summary: Copper prices slid to over three-year lows as U.S. suspended travel from Europe to curb coronavirus spread, intensifying fears of an external demand shock and weaker global growth. LME three-month copper fell around 2.2%, while LME aluminum eased and nickel declined, reflecting broad risk-off demand expectations.

title: FPX Nickel Closes Private Placement for $1,500,000
summary: FPX Nickel closed a $1.5 million non-brokered private placement at $0.18 per share and expects final exchange acceptance shortly. Proceeds will fund working capital and early settlement of up to $687,000 of long-term debt. The news is financing-related, with no stated nickel production or market-impact changes.

title: Future Market Insights: Demand for Aluminum Cans Continues to Move on an Upward Trajectory, 2-Piece Cans Remain Highly Preferred
summary: Future Market Insights says demand for aluminum cans is rising, supported by stricter packaging/environmental rules and strong beverage demand (including 2-piece cans). The report points to increasing production and adoption across Europe, North America, and East Asia, suggesting higher near-term aluminum consumption despite competition from PET/glass alternatives.

title: China's $570 Billion Stimulus Is A Boon For Copper
summary: The article says China’s $570 billion stimulus, focused on infrastructure and restarting factories, should support industrial metals. It notes China is a major share of global copper consumption and highlights relatively resilient copper prices despite the pandemic shock, implying stimulus-driven demand optimism.

title: Canada Nickel Company Receives Positive Initial Mineralogy Results
summary: Canada Nickel said initial mineralogy results from its Crawford Nickel-Cobalt sulphide project show most nickel is contained in nickel sulphide and nickel-iron alloy minerals, with 97% of nickel in sulphides in the higher grade core. This supports potential higher recoveries as work continues.

title: Vedanta expects output at Lanjigarh alumina refinery to increase to 1.8 MT in 2019-20
summary: Vedanta said it expects output at its Lanjigarh alumina refinery to rise to 1.8 million tonnes in 2019-20. Higher alumina supply can ease feedstock constraints for aluminium smelters, supporting expectations for steadier or increased aluminium production in the near term.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong declined 5,800 mt on week
summary: SMM data show copper cathode social inventories in Guangdong fell 5,800 mt week-on-week to 110,500 mt as of March 13. This marks the first weekly decline after COVID-related demand weakness had boosted stocks since the Chinese New Year holiday. Inventories had risen 13,600 mt in the prior week.

title: Shanghai nickel drops to 8-month low as virus panic grips markets
summary: Industrial metals fell as coronavirus panic deepened recession worries. Shanghai nickel slid as much as 4.2% to an eight-month low, with LME nickel on track for its steepest weekly drop since 2017. Copper and aluminum prices also dropped, and copper smelting weakened as disruptions spread.

title: Copper Prices Fare Better Than Oil, Other Assets
summary: Copper futures have declined since a January peak as coronavirus spread triggered weakness across commodities and other risk assets. While copper is “faring better” than oil, it still “suffered” alongside the broader market move, pointing to near-term macro-driven demand concerns for industrial metals.

title: Section 232 Update: Challenges to Steel and Aluminum Derivative Tariffs Are Succeeding
summary: Importers are seeing success in court actions enjoining Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum derivative products, largely due to procedural timing issues under the statute. While the administration retains general tariff authority, the ruling increases the odds of relief for targeted importers, potentially easing aluminum price support.

title: Oak Flat copper mine: Activists take worries to Congress subcommittee
summary: Activists and tribal representatives testified before a House subcommittee opposing the Oak Flat land swap that would enable Resolution Copper’s underground mine. Speakers cited concerns over water use, tailings, and environmental process flaws, and lawmakers discussed bills to stop the exchange, raising risk to copper project timelines.

title: Resource Big News Roundup: Blackstone Intersects Massive Sulfide Nickel at King Cobra Discovery, Lake Resources Partner Lilac Solutions Takes Delivery of 20,000 Litres of Kachi Brine for Pilot Plant Testing, Nexus Gold to Expand Newfoundland Holdings Through Acquisition of Dorset Gold Project
summary: The news roundup cites Blackstone intersecting massive sulfide nickel at the King Cobra discovery, boosting sentiment for future nickel supply. title: Black Butte Copper Achieves Two Key Permitting Milestones
summary: Sandfire Resources announced two permitting milestones for its Black Butte copper underground project in Montana: release of the Final Environmental Impact Statement and a preliminary determination on water-right modifications. Both steps are needed before a Mine Operating Permit Record of Decision, potentially advancing construction plans.

title: DEQ, DNRC advance copper mine project in Meagher Co.
summary: Montana’s DEQ issued a final Environmental Impact Statement and DNRC issued preliminary water-permit determinations for Tintina’s proposed Black Butte copper mine. The analysis found potential impacts to Coon Creek flows and requires mitigation, with DEQ to issue a final decision at least 15 days after EIS publication.

title: 2 Montana agencies advance copper mine project in Meagher County
summary: Montana agencies advanced the proposed Black Butte copper mine by issuing a final Environmental Impact Statement and preliminary water permit determinations. The DEQ found potential impacts to nearby Coon Creek flows and required mitigation. DEQ must still issue a final decision after a 15-day publication wait before work can proceed.

title: London copper falls after surprise Fed rate cut, dire China data
summary: London copper fell 0.7% after a surprise Fed rate cut and emergency stimulus that failed to calm investor panic, alongside sharp contraction in China’s industrial output. The same risk-off backdrop coincided with declines in LME aluminium and nickel, while copper inventories rose at Shanghai Futures.

title: Copper falls after surprise Fed rate cut, dire China data
summary: Copper prices fell after a surprise Fed rate cut and emergency stimulus plans failed to calm investor panic. Dismal China industrial output data and rising SHFE copper inventories supported a demand- and supply-balance bearish view. LME aluminum and nickel also declined, reflecting broad industrial metals risk-off selling.

title: Coronavirus slows development at Rio Tinto's Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia | 16 March 2020
summary: The article title reports that coronavirus has slowed development at Rio Tinto’s Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia. title: Press Metal raises $300m for Bintan Alumina stake buy
summary: Malaysia’s Press Metal Aluminium raised $300m via dual-tranche financing to fund its acquisition of Bintan Alumina Indonesia (BAI). Securing alumina capacity/ownership is supportive for aluminium production prospects by improving access to refining feedstock, which can underpin short-term expectations for aluminium demand-supply balance.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Intersects Nickel-Copper Mineralization at Falcon Nickel Project, Northern Saskatchewan
summary: ALX Resources reported that its second drill hole at the Falcon Nickel Project intersected sulphide mineralization containing nickel and copper, with assays pending. title: ALX Resources Corp. Intersects Nickel-Copper Mineralization at Falcon Nickel Project, Northern Saskatchewan
summary: ALX Resources said its second drill hole at the 100%-owned Falcon Nickel Project in northern Saskatchewan intersected sulphide mineralization with visible pyrrhotite and chalcopyrite, indicating potential nickel-copper mineralization. Assay results are pending, and the release is primarily exploration-focused without production or near-term supply changes.

title: New Trade Case on Imports of Common Alloy Aluminum Sheet from 18 Countries | Clark Hill PLC
summary: Clark Hill PLC reports a U.S. antidumping (“AD”) petition filed March 3, 2020 by major U.S. aluminium sheet producers against imports of common alloy aluminum sheet from 18 countries. The ITC will assess injury within 45 days; if confirmed, Commerce would calculate preliminary AD duty margins with deposits required on entry.

title: NBS: China primary aluminium output increased 2.4% YoY in January-February
summary: China’s primary aluminium output rose 2.4% YoY to 5.85 million tonnes in January–February, according to NBS data. The report also notes total production of 10 nonferrous metals increased, but only aluminium has a specific upturn detailed. Higher aluminium supply can pressure prices near term.

title: Chengtun Mining wrapped up 500 million yuan acquisition of Nzuri Copper
summary: Chengtun Mining’s subsidiary Xuchen has completed its acquisition of Nzuri Copper for A$114 million, securing 100% ownership of two DRC copper-cobalt projects. Kalongwe is nearer to development with expected long-run copper output after construction, but no near-term disruptions are mentioned.

title: London copper rebounds from 40-month low on demand hopes
summary: London copper rose 0.6% from a 40-month low on hopes U.S. Fed liquidity measures will eventually boost longer-term metal demand. The Fed cut rates and pledged balance-sheet expansion. LME nickel climbed 1.8% while aluminum edged down 0.5%, reflecting mixed but mostly supportive macro sentiment.

summary: Anglo American said Peru’s 15-day national quarantine has led it to withdraw most employees and contractors from the Quellaveco copper project. Only critical activities continue, slowing construction significantly. The project’s start-up is expected in 2022, with initial output around 300,000 tonnes per year.

title: Oil price plunge to lower 90th percentile C1 copper costs to $5,180/mt
summary: Oil prices fell sharply on OPEC+ talk collapse and COVID-19 fears, cutting diesel-related costs for copper miners. SMM estimates global copper mining costs drop 2.25% and 90th percentile C1 costs fall to $5,180/mt (from $5,300/mt), supporting copper’s cost outlook.

title: Prospect of excess supply pushes copper towards 40-month lows
summary: Copper slid toward 40-month lows as slowing demand raised expectations of surpluses and pushed deliveries into LME-approved warehouses. summary: Vale said it is reducing activity and output at its Voisey’s Bay copper mine in Canada by placing the site into four weeks of care-and-maintenance to protect nearby indigenous communities from COVID-19 travel exposure. title: Copper Prices Plummet As China Faces First GDP Drop In 44 Years
summary: Copper prices fell more than 5% on Monday after China reported record declines in industrial production and fixed asset investment. title: Copper Price Tumbles, Miners Take Coronavirus Precautions
summary: Copper prices continued to tumble as markets worried coronavirus would curb demand, especially from China and globally. Lockdowns and risk aversion pressured base metals. title: Anglo American slows Peru copper project construction due to national quarantine
summary: Anglo American said it is slowing construction of its Quellaveco copper project in Peru after a 15-day national quarantine imposed to curb COVID-19 spread. summary: Spot copper trading in Shanghai improved on Mar 18 as copper futures fell, prompting downstream consumers to restock and sellers to narrow spot discounts. summary: Nornickel’s Kola MMC will invest about $34.6 million (2.6 billion rubles) in 2020 to upgrade mines and nickel electrolysis/refining operations, including new equipment for a nickel electrolysis shop and sulfuric acid department. summary: A judge has backed Twin Metals’ copper-nickel mine by rejecting environmental groups’ legal challenges. summary: A Minnesota judge backed the Twin Metals copper-nickel mine, rejecting environmental groups’ legal challenges. title: Pattrick Smellie: How to close an aluminium smelter

summary: BHP plans to exclude contractors at its Chilean copper mines for 15 days. Such a labor/contractor restriction can disrupt planned output and raise short-term supply risk, likely tightening market expectations for near-term copper availability and supporting copper prices over the following days to weeks.

title: Ecuador's largest gold and copper mines scale back as Coronavirus cases rapidly grow
summary: Ecuador’s largest gold and copper mines are reportedly scaling back operations as coronavirus cases rise rapidly. The production curtailment may reduce near-term copper supply from the country, potentially supporting copper prices over the following days as markets price tighter availability.

title: Copper's steepest weekly fall since 2011
summary: The piece highlights copper’s sharp weekly decline, its steepest since 2011, reflecting bearish near-term momentum. It also links broader market stress to surging oil prices from Middle East risks and expectations of tighter Australian monetary conditions, which can pressure industrial metal demand sentiment.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Mar 23): Base metals opened broadly lower; Shanghai copper briefly hit 'limit down'
summary: Base metals fell broadly at the open as coronavirus-related economic fears and a firmer US dollar weighed on sentiment. SHFE May copper hit limit down, while LME aluminium dropped sharply and tested multi-year lows. US stimulus uncertainty and collapsing futures/crude reinforced risk-off conditions; nickel was comparatively firm.

title: 'At least' $7.8b more needed to complete Rio's Mongolian copper mine
summary: Rio Tinto’s Turquoise Hill Resources said it needs at least a further US$4.5 billion to complete the underground expansion at Mongolia’s Oyu Tolgoi copper mine, after requiring far more funding than previously assumed. The shortfall raises execution and timing/cost risks that can weigh on near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Shanghai copper hits 11-year low as virus curbs raise demand concerns
summary: Shanghai and LME copper prices fell to multi-year lows as expanding coronavirus lockdowns and business closures increased concerns about weakening industrial and economic activity. LME three-month copper dropped about 5% intraday, while other base metals also fell, including aluminum and nickel, reflecting a broad risk-off demand selloff.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong extended slide on weekend
summary: Guangdong social inventories of copper cathode fell further, reaching 100,500 mt on March 23, down from March 20. The weekly drop accelerated as smelters scaled back shipments and imported arrivals declined. Lower prices reduced downstream buying, but prospects of stabilizing prices and resumed shipments support steadier spot offers.

title: Copper concentrate TCs dropped on supply concerns
summary: Treatment charges for spot copper concentrate fell to $68.35/mt as COVID-19 restrictions prompted mine slowdowns or care-and-maintenance in Chile and Peru, raising fears of shipment delays for April delivery. Trading eased as sellers cut back sales, while smelter production recovery in China added demand-side support.

title: China February nickel ore imports dropped 32% YoY due to Indonesian ban
summary: China’s February nickel ore and concentrate imports fell sharply as Indonesia’s export ban from the start of the year constrained supply. Imports declined versus both January and a year ago, with Indonesia shipments collapsing. Philippine and New Caledonia flows also faced weather and coronavirus-related disruptions, likely reducing March arrivals further.

title: Aluminium lurches to 45-month low on fears of global recession
summary: London LME aluminium fell to a 45-month low amid recession fears from coronavirus lockdowns and a broader sell-off. Copper also dropped sharply, with Shanghai copper hitting a multi-year low. The piece attributes moves to collapsing demand sentiment and reports nickel also weakening during the same session.

title: Freeport-McMoRan suspends dividend, could cut copper production
