summary: Freeport-McMoRan suspended its quarterly dividend and said it will pursue aggressive cost and capital-spending cuts, which may temporarily reduce copper production in the Americas. The firm cited low commodity prices. The article notes high grade copper futures down 20% over a month, indicating weak near-term sentiment.

title: LME ring goes dark as aluminum lurches to 45-month low
summary: LME open-outcry went dark as the market shifted to full electronic trading, while aluminium slid to a 45-month low and copper dropped to multi-year lows amid fears of a severe global recession. The sell-off spread to nickel as well, reflecting sharply weaker demand expectations and thin liquidity.

title: Rupture of copper demand to fuel surplus as industry hit by virus
summary: Coronavirus disruptions are expected to cut copper consumption more than supply, shifting the market from balance to a potential surplus of up to around one million tonnes in 2020. Analysts cite cancelled orders and weaker manufacturing, while mine halts and lower oil-driven costs only partially offset demand losses.

title: China Moly to isolate TFM copper mine in Congo due to coronavirus – note
summary: China Molybdenum said it will isolate its TFM copper and cobalt mine in the DRC starting Tuesday noon due to coronavirus precautions. Only essential services and on-site staff will continue to maintain production, potentially limiting throughput in the near term and pressuring copper supply expectations.

title: Japan's JX to cut operations at Chile's Caserones copper mine by 40% amid pandemic
summary: Japan’s JX Nippon Mining & Metal said it will cut operations at Chile’s Caserones copper mine by 40% by reducing workers from March 22 to comply with COVID-19 movement limits. The duration will depend on local virus conditions and government instructions, lowering short-term copper output prospects.

title: Congo's Copper, Cobalt Mining Province in Coronavirus Lockdown
summary: The DRC imposed a two-day COVID-19 lockdown on Haut-Katanga, key copper- and cobalt-mining areas, and closed public markets in neighboring Lualaba. Reuters sources expect the disruption to weigh heavily on copper output, citing potential smelter or logistics bottlenecks that prevent mines from shipping concentrates.

title: Copper prices rise on supply worries, Fed's stimulus
summary: Copper rose on Tuesday as coronavirus containment in key mining countries raised supply concerns, while Fed stimulus improved financial sentiment. Three-month LME copper gained about 2% and ShFE copper about 4%. The report also notes higher nickel and lists aluminium prices rising, suggesting supportive broader metal momentum.

title: China alumina exports plunged 83% YoY in January-February
summary: China’s alumina exports in January–February fell about 83% YoY to 30,000 mt, while exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis dropped 25% YoY. In contrast, aluminium imports surged 115% YoY. The data implies shifting trade flows that may influence near-term aluminium market balances.

title: Copper rebounds on Fed stimulus, supply concerns
summary: Copper prices rebounded as investors welcomed U.S. Fed stimulus measures to ease credit stress. At the same time, virus containment in major mining countries, including a Democratic Republic of Congo lockdown, raised near-term supply concerns. Chile’s Codelco warned low prices risk projects, and Freeport-McMoRan cut output.

title: Section 232 Update: Challenges To Steel And Aluminum Derivative Tariffs Are Succeeding - International Law
summary: Importers have been largely successful in court enjoining collection of Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum derivative products, arguing the administration missed statutory procedural deadlines. The ruling preserves the president’s broad Section 232 authority, but continued challenges could limit tariff costs, supporting aluminum sentiment in the short term.

title: Deemed essential, the aluminium industry participates in the united and collective effort of Quebec
summary: Quebec’s government recognizes aluminium as strategic. The Aluminium Association of Canada says it will suspend activities deemed non-essential until April 13 in response to COVID-19 mobilization, while maintaining essential operations requiring continuous molten-tank handling. This temporary output disruption could affect near-term primary aluminium supply expectations in North America.

title: China aluminium smelters start to reduce output as virus sends prices tumbling
summary: Chinese aluminium smelters are reducing operating capacity by an estimated 240,000–300,000 tonnes as coronavirus disruptions crush downstream demand and send aluminium prices tumbling, with Shanghai prices hitting the lowest since 2016. Smelters also face higher alumina costs, yet continued losses and weak consumption keep prices under pressure.

title: Macarthur set to advance Moonshine nickel prospect with EIS co-funded drilling
summary: Macarthur Minerals received an $85,000 Western Australian EIS grant to co-fund diamond drilling at its Moonshine North nickel prospect within the Lake Giles Iron Project. The drilling targets a historical high-grade nickel horizon and a deeper EM conductor. Results so far are non-economic, so near-term nickel market impact appears limited.

title: U.S. Gold Corp. Announces Updated Copper King Economics Showing NPV of $321.6 Million and IRR of 52%
summary: U.S. Gold Corp. announced updated “Copper King” project economics, reporting an NPV of $321.6 million and IRR of 52%. The update is intended to highlight project viability. No immediate mine output, permitting, financing, or supply disruption details are provided in the provided text.

title: Supramaxes sit at anchor as virus spread halts nickel ore cargoes
summary: Supramaxes are anchored as a virus spread disrupts operations and halts nickel ore cargoes. The delay hits Philippines’ attempt to replace Indonesia as a go-to mineral supplier, tightening near-term nickel ore availability and likely weighing on nickel prices in the coming days and weeks.

title: Copper Gains on Supply Shortage Fears Amid Coronavirus Outbreak
summary: The article headline says copper is rising as investors worry about supply shortages linked to the coronavirus outbreak. Such fears can imply reduced production or logistics disruptions for copper, tightening market availability and supporting higher copper prices in the near term over the following days to weeks.

title: U.S. Gold Corp. : Announces Updated Copper King Economics Showing NPV of $321.6 Million and IRR of 52%
summary: U.S. Gold Corp. updated the Copper King deposit economic model, switching assumptions to $1600 gold and $2.80 copper (from prior PEA assumptions). It reports higher NPV/IRR and discusses throughput and CAPEX changes, but no immediate production or supply changes are announced.

title: Copper bounces 6% on U.S. stimulus, but gains seen short-lived
summary: Copper jumped more than 6% after U.S. Fed stimulus boosted dollar liquidity and a weaker dollar, while coronavirus shutdowns raised concerns about reduced mine output. But analysts said demand collapse outweighs supply constraints, making the rebound likely temporary. The piece also notes high aluminium warehouse supplies and a widening nickel surplus.

title: Nordex wins massive corporate wind order for aluminium giant Alcoa
summary: Nordex has won a large corporate wind order tied to Alcoa, with electricity from Eolus’ 400MW Øyfjellet wind array earmarked to power an Alcoa metal smelter plant in northern Norway. The development improves the supply of electricity for aluminium production, which can be slightly supportive for near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: San Juan County copper mine shuts down, leaving behind unpaid workers, environmental fears
summary: San Juan County’s Lisbon Valley Mining Company copper mine shut down abruptly on March 18, leaving unpaid workers and prompting emergency action by Utah regulators. The sudden stoppage and related environmental and operational concerns point to reduced copper output, a factor that can influence near-term copper supply expectations.

title: BLP meeting closed to public foot traffic | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: The article discusses the Lisbon Valley Mining Company’s copper mine facility, including heap-leach pads, and notes that the operation shut down abruptly on March 18, 2020. Such a shutdown can tighten short-term copper supply expectations, adding downside pressure to copper prices over coming days or weeks.

title: Century Aluminum Company Announces Hawesville Labor Contract Extension and Provides Update on COVID-19 Response
summary: Century Aluminum extended its Hawesville, Kentucky smelter labor contract and outlined COVID-19 response measures to keep employees safe and sustain continuous primary aluminum operations. The company cited no current impediment to running plants and implemented cost and liquidity actions while monitoring evolving conditions with suppliers and customers.

title: Copper rises on U.S. stimulus hopes, supply worries
summary: Copper prices rose on U.S. stimulus hopes and concerns that coronavirus lockdowns in mining countries could disrupt supply, despite capped gains from demand worries as more regions impose self-isolation. The piece also notes Chinese aluminium smelters cutting capacity due to the price collapse, implying tighter supply conditions.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Mar 25): Base metals mixed following a historic rebound on Wall Street; Shanghai copper extended its gains
summary: SMM reports base metals opening mostly higher after a Wall Street rebound driven by hopes for an unprecedented US stimulus package and Fed unlimited bond buying, lifting risk sentiment and oil while weighing on the dollar. LME copper and nickel surged, and near-term ranges skew higher, though aluminium ended weaker amid volatility.

title: Nickel import disruption amid South Africa's lockdown to little impact China's downstream
summary: China importers have delayed talks with South African mining companies ahead of a 21-day lockdown starting March 26, raising short-term uncertainty around South African nickel supply. SMM expects minimal effect on Chinese downstream because steel mills’ nickel needs are met largely via other sources (e.g., Russian nickel).

title: China Jan-Feb nickel ore imports fall 5.1% y/y as Indonesia ban begins
summary: China’s nickel ore imports in Jan-Feb fell 5.1% y/y to 4.32 million tonnes as Indonesia’s export ban took effect on Jan. 1. Indonesia-origin ore dropped 18.1% y/y, while Philippines volumes rose 39.6%. Nickel pig iron imports increased, but overall ore supply appears tighter for near-term processing.

title: Recovered copper futures lifted spot trades
summary: Shanghai spot copper trading revived on March 25 as SHFE copper futures continued recovering losses from earlier in the week. Downstream buyers returned and spot discounts to the April contract narrowed (from wider levels to around 30 yuan/mt standard and 20 yuan/mt high-grade), supporting brisk early activity despite a later slowdown.

title: Copper and COVID-19: Who's Reacting and How?
summary: INN compiles copper-focused COVID-19 responses as shutdowns, quarantines, and health protocols disrupt mining and construction across key producing countries. Examples include production cuts at Codelco, temporary suspension at Freeport’s Cerro Verde, and reduced operations or slowed expansions for multiple projects. Uncertainty about demand also weighs on copper pricing.

title: NORNICKEL ANNOUNCES MEASURES TO PROTECT EMPLOYEES AND PARTNERS DURING COVID-19 PANDEMIC
summary: Norilsk Nickel announced COVID-19 protection measures to safeguard employees and ensure business process continuity, including remote work, medical equipment funding, extended shifts at Bystrinsky GOK until April 30, travel bans, and customer guidance to avoid visits. The company says operations remain functioning normally.

title: DUBAL Holding plans to make low carbon aluminium, EV batteries in the UAE
summary: DUBAL Holding says it is pursuing UAE projects including a low-CO2 aluminium rolling facility and a battery storage plant, with additional scrap recycling and cast aluminium wheel manufacturing under study. Its aluminium unit EGA produces and exports substantial volumes, and the plan aligns with UAE green and EV localisation goals.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Intersects Additional Nickel-Copper Mineralization at Falcon Nickel Project, Northern Saskatchewan
summary: ALX Resources announced drill hole FN20-003 at its Falcon Nickel Project in northern Saskatchewan intersected two zones of sulphide mineralization containing nickel and copper (with visible pyrrhotite, chalcopyrite, and pentlandite). Further exploration was suspended due to COVID-19, and geochemical analyses are pending.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Intersects Additional Nickel-Copper Mineralization at Falcon Nickel Project, Northern Saskatchewan
summary: ALX Resources said its FN20-003 drill hole at the Falcon Nickel Project intersected nickel- and copper-bearing sulphide mineralization, with core samples sent for base-metals analysis later in March 2020. The company also suspended further exploration due to COVID-19 precautions, including temporarily closing its Vancouver office.

title: Talon Metals Completes Initial Pre-Concentration Test Work and Increases Lower Grade Mineralization by 107% to 1.18% Nickel
summary: Talon Metals reports successful pre-concentration tests at its Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in Minnesota, upgrading low-grade nickel to 1.18% Ni and increasing copper grade to 0.79%, with reported recoveries of ~70.6% Ni and ~71.8% Cu. Results may expand resources, but production timing remains uncertain.

title: First Quantum eyes stake sale in Cobre Panama copper mine
summary: First Quantum Minerals is reportedly considering selling a minority stake in its 90%-owned Cobre Panama copper mine to reduce heavy debt. The company also disclosed coronavirus infections among contractor workers and implemented quarantine and salary cuts. These steps raise short-term supply and operational risk for copper.

title: Copper Fox Announces Updated Mineral Resource Estimate for the Van Dyke Project
summary: Copper Fox announced an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate for its Van Dyke oxide copper project in Arizona. The update increases contained recoverable soluble copper (RecCu) versus the 2015 estimate, with the deposit open for potential strike extension. The release also notes economic assumptions used in the resource wireframe.

title: Coronavirus death toll crosses over 20,000; 3 bn under quarantine
summary: The article reports a rapid rise in COVID-19 deaths and mass lockdowns across Europe and India, disrupting transport and services, alongside US and EU efforts to stimulate the economy. Such macro demand and supply disruption can influence copper, aluminium, and nickel sentiment, but no direct metal-specific fundamentals are provided.

title: UAE Business: Dubal plans low-carbon aluminium, EV battery units
summary: Dubal Holding said it is studying projects in the UAE including a low-carbon aluminium rolling facility, cast aluminium wheels production, and integrated scrap recycling. It also highlighted EGA’s refinery and bauxite output and ongoing power/desalination projects. Officials emphasized EGA’s premium aluminium sales and expansion efforts despite challenging markets and lower aluminium prices.

title: China bauxite imports expanded 9.6%YoY in January-February
summary: China’s bauxite imports rose 9.64% year-on-year to 18.4 million mt in January–February, with Guinea remaining the largest supplier at 8.93 million mt. Higher bauxite inflows suggest increased alumina feedstock availability in China, which can ease near-term aluminium supply constraints.

title: Latest on the spread of the coronavirus around the world
summary: Reuters updates global COVID-19 case and death counts and notes increasing restrictions, including lockdowns in New Zealand and curbs on movement in several countries. It also cites economic disruption, jobless-claims worries, and stimulus measures. Overall, the risk of shutdowns and weaker growth is negative for industrial metal demand.

title: Ultra-high-voltage projects to limitedly drive copper consumption in 2020
summary: China State Grid plans only a moderate rise in investment for 2020, including large UHV spending. However, UHV overhead lines are expected to use ACSR conductors rather than copper cables, limiting incremental copper demand. Transformer substations would consume copper only if copper-containing cables are used. Projects are resuming post-virus disruption.

title: EGA reports lower earnings in 'challenging' year for aluminium sector
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium reported a 43% earnings drop in 2019, citing a challenging aluminium market and a global alumina supply shortage. Curtailment at a major Brazil refinery spiked alumina costs in early 2019, while aluminium prices fell sharply from an April peak, reinforcing weak demand and pressure on sentiment.

title: Copper eases as hit to economy and metals demand outweighs U.S. stimulus
summary: Copper prices eased 1.3% as coronavirus-driven demand weakness outweighed a $2 trillion U.S. stimulus package. The piece cites higher China refined copper imports, Codelco project suspensions to curb virus spread, rising LME aluminium warehouse stocks, and nickel disruptions from Sumitomo’s planned mine suspensions, leading to mixed short-term signals.

title: Ecuador's largest gold and copper mines scale back as Coronavirus cases rapidly grow | The Mighty 790 KFGO
summary: Ecuador says its Mirador copper mine is reducing staffing and suspending transport of copper concentrate to ports as COVID-19 cases surge. It also imposes curbs on visitors and other operational controls. Fruta del Norte gold output is temporarily paused, while mining continues at bare minimum.

title: Global Bauxite Mining Market Latest Rising Trend & Forecast to 2025 - Top Companies Access Industries, Tata Steel Europe, Halco Mining
summary: The piece describes the bauxite mining market, noting bauxite’s role as the primary ore for aluminium and projecting continued growth. It also references increased global primary aluminium production and a generally positive aluminium industry outlook amid tariff and trade uncertainties. Overall, it supports expectations for aluminium supply tightness/price support.

title: Copper slips as coronavirus hit to metals outweighs U.S. stimulus
summary: Copper prices fell as coronavirus-driven demand hits outweighed support from a $2 trillion U.S. stimulus. The piece cites virus containment measures, Codelco project suspensions, mine shutdowns, and DRC/Zambia export terminal closures. It also notes aluminium inventory increases and a nickel decline, reinforcing near-term downside pressure across metals.

title: South African port closures to hit global copper supply - SABC News - Breaking news, special reports, world, business, sport coverage of all South African current events. Africa's news leader.
summary: South Africa’s bulk mineral export terminals are set to close for a 21-day coronavirus lockdown, disrupting overland transport of Zambian copper to ports such as Durban and others. Transnet says non-essential cargo handling will stop, while firms reroute exports. The supply disruption is expected to pressure copper markets higher.

title: Copper slips as coronavirus hits metals
summary: Copper prices are reported to be slipping as coronavirus-related concerns weigh on the broader metals complex. The news signals weakening sentiment and potential near-term demand risk, which typically translates into downward pressure on industrial metal prices such as copper over the following days to weeks.

title: Malaysia launched anti-dumping probes into aluminum & zinc coated flat steel products from China, South Korea and Vietnam
summary: Malaysia launched anti-dumping probes into aluminium- and zinc-coated flat-rolled/non-alloy steel products from China, South Korea and Vietnam, following a complaint by NS Bluescope Malaysia. The investigation may constrain imports of aluminium-coated steel into Malaysia near term, potentially lifting sentiment for aluminium demand versus alternative supplies.

title: Material Matters: Copper, Lithium & Closures
summary: The piece says COVID-19 has reduced activity and base-metal demand, with only limited short-term improvement. It notes elevated copper treatment charges, possible inventory builds, and coronavirus shutdowns at some Peruvian copper mines (Cerro Verde, Constancia). It also flags nickel/aluminium margin pressure and potential closures, keeping downside risk.

title: Woodmac: Copper Supply at Risk as Coronavirus Measures Tighten
summary: Wood Mackenzie warns COVID-19 quarantines in Chile and Peru risk escalating disruptions to copper mine supply, with potential broader effects across mining regions. It also links lower copper prices to reduced restart incentives and accelerated project delays. Refining output may fall, supporting prices versus weaker demand assumptions.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks shrank as arbitrage window briefly opened
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories fell during the week ended March 27 as an import arbitrage window briefly opened earlier in the week. Pure nickel stocks dropped 500 mt to 19,300 mt and briquettes fell 200 mt to 2,000 mt, with reduced arrivals also attributed to COVID-19 disruptions.

title: Forum's ROV to support Indonesia's largest copper and gold mine
summary: Forum Energy Technologies will supply an ROV to Amman Mineral for subsea operations at Batu Hijau, Indonesia’s second largest copper and gold mine. The system will replace an earlier unit and support deep-sea tailing monitoring and inspections. The order supports continued operations but is unlikely to materially affect copper prices short term.

title: Aluminium surplus to balloon as producers resist output cuts
summary: Reuters reports aluminium prices have plunged to 4-year lows as coronavirus weakens demand. Producers are reluctant to cut output because input costs (notably electricity, carbon and alumina) have also fallen, sustaining margins, while restarting shutdown capacity is slow and costly. The market is expected to swing to a large surplus.

title: Copper steadies near 4-year lows as supply shutdowns mount
summary: Copper steadied near four-year lows as worsening supply disruptions from mine and shipping shutdowns began to counter the sharp coronavirus demand shock. South African port closures and Glencore mine slowdowns disrupted shipments, while demand weakness and surplus expectations limited upside, keeping copper near $4,785/ton.

title: Pakistan claims 400% increase of copper products exported to China--China Economic Net
summary: Pakistan reports a 400% increase in copper product exports to China over the past two years, citing expanded production from the Saindak copper-gold project and potential additional output if the Reko Diq dispute resolves. China is described as a major copper buyer with favorable tariffs, supporting continued growth in exports.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports extended decline by 400,000 wmt
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell by 400,000 wmt in the week to March 27 to 10.26 million wmt. In metal content terms, stocks dropped 3,600 mt to 85,000 mt, with inventories at seven major ports down 290,000 wmt to 8.37 million wmt.

title: Amman Mineral to use ROV at Batu Hijau copper-gold mine
summary: Amman Mineral ordered a remotely operated vehicle for Indonesia’s Batu Hijau copper-gold mine to support subsea mining operations and routine deep-sea tailings monitoring. The ROV will be delivered in the first quarter next year and is framed as an environmental stewardship and safety measure. No production change is specified.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Files an Updated NI 43-101 Technical Report for the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Project
summary: Ivanhoe Mines filed an updated NI 43-101 technical report for the Kamoa-Kakula copper project in the DRC, providing an updated independently verified mineral resource estimate (effective Jan. 30, 2020). The company also notes no changes after a review of inputs for the Kakula deposit. No near-term production impact is stated.

title: China smelter Yuguang to put its copper system under maintenance for 20 days
summary: Henan Yuguang Gold and Lead will conduct routine maintenance on its copper system for about 20 days starting early April. SMM expects copper cathode output to fall by 6,000–7,000 mt, roughly 60% of normal monthly production, likely tightening near-term supply conditions for copper.

title: China's nickel supply to feel little impact from halt of Sumitomo's mine in Madagascar
summary: Sumitomo temporarily suspended its Ambatovy nickel project in Madagascar due to COVID-19 curbs. With China’s nickel briquette inventories low, the reduced supply may be only slightly limiting but increases China’s dependence on other imports. Imports have tariff-free access and inventory fell in Shanghai bonded areas.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong accelerated decline on weekend
summary: SMM reports that copper cathode social inventories in Guangdong accelerated their decline over the weekend. Stocks at major warehouses fell to 89,200 mt as of March 30, down 8,750 mt from March 27. Inventories have decreased for three consecutive weeks, with larger weekly drops recently.

title: Month-long maintenance to affect nickel sulphate output in north China
summary: A nickel sulphate producer in north China plans about a month of annual maintenance starting in early April. The shutdown is expected to reduce battery-grade nickel sulphate output by 3,000–4,000 mt. The supply curtailment could support tighter nickel-related markets over the next few weeks.

title: Three civilians injured as rebels attack gold, copper mining firm in Indonesia's Papua
summary: Rebels attacked the administration of PT Freeport Indonesia in Papua, where both gold and copper are mined, injuring three civilians including two foreigners. The incident highlights security risk for the mine site at Kuala Kencana, Timika, potentially affecting near-term expectations for copper supply.

title: 3 civilians injured as rebels attack gold, copper mining firm in Indonesia's Papua
summary: Rebels attacked PT Freeport Indonesia’s administration at Kuala Kencana in Papua, wounding three civilians and prompting the company to alert workers to halt operations and seek shelter. Police and military closed the compound. The incident targets a major copper mining firm, increasing short-term output and supply disruption fears.

title: 3 civilians injured as rebels attack gold, copper mining firm in Indonesia's Papua - Xinhua
summary: Rebels attacked PT Freeport Indonesia’s Kuala Kencana administration in Papua, injuring three civilians and prompting the company to issue an incident alert asking workers to halt activities. Security forces closed the mine compound. The disruption risk is relevant for copper, given Freeport’s major copper operations in the region.

title: Lindian adds 1km of strike to bauxite conglomerate in Guinea
summary: Lindian says drilling has confirmed and extended the Bouba plateau bauxite conglomerate in Guinea by about 1 km, with reported thickness and encouraging visual indicators of high-grade bauxite. Samples are due from the lab, potentially improving near-term expectations for bauxite supply feeding aluminium.

title: Andy Home, industrial metals demand, nickel prices, COVID-19 pandemic
summary: Recylex is temporarily closing smelting and battery-recycling capacity citing a sharp demand drop tied to coronavirus lockdowns and weaker metal prices. The column argues auto production and sales are collapsing, reducing demand for industrial metals used in vehicles—especially aluminum, and also copper and nickel via EV and battery-related applications.

title: Global copper miners head for worst quarter since 2008
summary: The piece flags that global copper miners are set for their worst quarter since 2008. That signals worsening operating conditions and/or output for copper producers, which typically undermines sentiment around near-term supply and can weigh on copper prices over the coming days.

title: Rio Tinto to scale back New Zealand aluminium smelter due to virus
summary: Rio Tinto said it will reduce production at its New Zealand aluminium smelter because of a virus-related disruption. The cut to output would likely lower near-term aluminium supply, affecting market expectations for prompt availability and refining/smelter utilization over the coming days.

title: Rio Tinto to scale back NZ aluminum smelter operations due to virus
summary: Rio Tinto’s NZAS will close pot line 4 at its Tiwai aluminum smelter in New Zealand due to coronavirus-related government restrictions. The company will wind down operations this week, reallocate workers, and cut electricity demand via Meridian Energy. The action reduces aluminum output from the loss-making facility.

title: Copper rebounds as China's factories unexpectedly return to growth
summary: Copper prices rose on Tuesday after China’s March factory PMI unexpectedly expanded to 52 from 35.7 in February, beating forecasts. Shanghai and London copper contracts climbed, reversing recent losses. The upbeat China growth signal also coincided with modest gains in aluminium and nickel, though coronavirus-driven longer-term pressure remains.

title: LME copper rises on China data, but set for worst month since 2011
summary: LME copper rose up to 2.2% after China’s PMI improved, boosting confidence in commodity demand. Despite the daily rally, copper is set for the steepest monthly fall since 2011 due to coronavirus-driven demand uncertainty. Aluminium and nickel were slightly higher, indicating mild supportive tone.

title: LME copper rises on China data, but set for worst month since late 2011
summary: LME copper rose up to 2.2% after China’s March factory PMI unexpectedly expanded, boosting demand confidence, though the metal remains set for its worst monthly decline since 2011 amid worsening coronavirus spread. Aluminium edged down and nickel fell, but a Philippines nickel mine suspension was also reported.

title: Philippines' nickel mining hub to suspend operations due to coronavirus
summary: Philippine nickel mining operations in Surigao del Norte will be suspended from April 1 due to COVID-19 containment measures, affecting two of the country’s largest nickel ore miners that supply over half of output. The disruption threatens ore shipments to China and may reduce near-term nickel availability.

title: Spot copper premiums moved higher with futures prices amid brisk trades
summary: Spot copper trading in Shanghai was active as premiums over SHFE April rose sharply on March 31, supported by upbeat China manufacturing data that improved sentiment and lifted copper futures. Premiums for standard and high-grade copper increased versus early session, though purchases later cooled and elevated prices weighed on spot demand.

title: Virus-hit copper heads for worst quarter since 2011
summary: Copper prices rose intraday on a surprise rebound in China factory activity, but the article warns the coronavirus shock will drive copper to its worst quarter since 2011. Analysts expect demand to fall more than supply. It also cites aluminium smelter closures and nickel mine suspensions amid lockdowns.

title: Rockcliff Announces Significant Increase to Rail Resource: 1.17M Indicated Tonnes at 3.52% Copper Equivalent and 0.73M Inferred Tonnes at 4.09% Copper Equivalent
summary: Rockcliff reported an updated Mineral Resource Estimate for its Rail deposit in Manitoba, showing a 42% rise in indicated tonnage and a 27% increase in contained indicated copper (to 70.2M lbs), with higher copper-equivalent grades. The company plans a Preliminary Economic Assessment after Q2 2020.

title: Copper heads for worst quarter since 2011 as coronavirus damps demand
summary: Copper is headed for its worst quarter since 2011 as coronavirus shutdowns reduce global industrial demand. Even with some mine closures and China manufacturing improving, analysts expect demand damage to dominate and potential oversupply. The piece also flags an aluminum smelter line closure and nickel mine suspension risks.

title: China copper downstream PMI returned above 50 in March
summary: China’s copper downstream PMI rose sharply in March, returning above 50 with improved production and new orders after a deep February contraction tied to Covid restrictions. The NBS also reported a manufacturing PMI rebound. Despite weak exports and raw material purchasing, the demand recovery is supportive for copper prices.

title: Copper suffers worst quarter since 2011 as coronavirus crushes demand
summary: The article’s headline says copper has its worst quarter since 2011 as the coronavirus pandemic crushes demand. It links the downturn to retailers closing stores and cutting hours, signaling weaker industrial and economic activity. Such demand shock would likely weigh heavily on copper prices in coming days.

title: Analysis: COVID-19 impacts on Indonesia's nickel industry - Wed, April 1 2020
summary: The analysis says COVID-19 has driven a sharp decline in global nickel prices, citing LME moves and YTD weakness. It forecasts a larger 2020 nickel surplus as demand grows slowly and supply/export disruptions rise in Indonesia, including smelter output reductions and an ore-shipment policy, weighing on price expectations.

title: U.S. launches probes into imports of aluminium sheet from 18 countries
summary: The U.S. has launched probes into imports of aluminium sheet from 18 countries. Such anti-dumping/countervailing-type investigations can slow or limit inbound supply to the U.S. in the coming days, tightening availability for buyers and typically providing upward support for aluminium prices.

title: Nickel Miners in the Philippines Hit by COVID-19 Prevention Measures
summary: Surigao del Norte in the Philippines ordered suspensions of nickel mining operations (Taganito and Hinatuan) from April 1 to curb COVID-19 spread. Nickel Asia and Global Ferronickel reported shipment-target cuts and appeal for continued operations. With Indonesia’s earlier nickel export ban tightening supply, the near-term output disruption is supportive for nickel prices.

title: LME copper falls on grim demand outlook as coronavirus paralyzes markets
summary: London copper prices fell 1.7% as the coronavirus pandemic worsened demand sentiment, with the article citing recession risk and deteriorating global growth expectations. Nickel was also lower on the day. The broader market context includes falling stocks and oil, typically pressuring industrial metals, including aluminium.

title: Copper falls as fast-spreading coronavirus threatens demand
summary: Copper prices dropped sharply as coronavirus spread and recession fears threatened near-term demand. The piece cites contracting factory activity across Asia and expectations that stimulus demand support may take until late Q2/Q3. It also notes declines in nickel and aluminum prices, reflecting broad industrial metal risk-off sentiment.

title: U.S. launches probes into imports of aluminum sheet from 18 countries
summary: The U.S. has launched probes into imports of aluminum sheet from 18 countries. Such investigations can result in tariffs or anti-dumping measures, potentially reducing import volumes and tightening near-term supply expectations. That typically provides upward price support for aluminum in the coming days to weeks.

title: Vietnam lockdown to add pressure on China's aluminium exports
summary: Vietnam imposed a 15-day nationwide lockdown, limiting consumption and business operations and weighing on demand for Chinese aluminium. China customs data show Vietnam received a meaningful share of Chinese aluminium products. With global lockdowns also shrinking China’s aluminium exports and delaying production, near-term aluminium supply/demand expectations turn bearish.

title: High premiums sidelined spot copper downstream consumers
summary: Shanghai spot copper trading moderated as downstream buyers hesitated due to elevated premiums and higher SHFE futures. Sellers kept offers slightly higher, but weak transaction support caused high-grade premiums to slip to 130–140 yuan/mt. Standard-grade premiums stayed around 120 yuan/mt, while overall volumes softened. Futures were modestly higher early.

title: Chinese nickel sulphate producers facing raw material supply woes as Papua New Guinea bans vessels at ports
summary: Papua New Guinea’s port vessel ban due to Covid-19 has delayed exports of nickel wet-processing intermediate products to China, threatening nickel sulphate feedstock supplies. Chinese producers are lifting quotes for battery-grade nickel sulphate amid uncertain delivery timing, with May production potentially affected if disruptions persist.

title: China nickel manufacturing returned to expansion in March after contracted for 11 months
summary: SMM says March activity in China’s nickel downstream sectors returned to expansion after 11 months of contraction. The downstream PMI rose, driven by higher production (stainless steel and electroplating especially), stronger new orders, and some restocking of nickel pig iron as base-metal prices fell.

title: Chilean state copper miner Codelco confirms fifth case of coronavirus among workers
summary: Codelco, Chile’s largest copper miner, confirmed a fifth coronavirus case among workers at its Ministro Hales mine and previously reported cases across Andina, El Teniente smelter, and Salvador. The company has stalled some updates and reduced staffing to maintain operational continuity, increasing near-term copper supply disruption risk amid falling copper prices.

title: Shanghai aluminum hits 4-year low on gloomy demand outlook
summary: Shanghai aluminum prices plunged to a four-year low as forecasts of falling demand grew, driven by rising coronavirus infections, tighter lockdowns, and weak global factory activity. The most-traded ShFE contract fell about 2.6%, reflecting deteriorating near-term demand for aluminum used in transport and packaging.

title: Shanghai aluminum hits 4-yr low as virus clouds demand outlook
summary: Shanghai aluminum prices plunged to a more than four-year low on weak factory data and rising coronavirus infections, with the benchmark ShFE contract down as much as 2.6% on Thursday. The article links the move to deteriorating manufacturing activity and demand uncertainty from pandemic-related disruptions.

title: Shanghai aluminum hits 4-yr low, coronavirus clouds demand outlook
summary: Shanghai aluminium prices on the ShFE fell to a more-than-four-year low after poor factory data and worsening coronavirus infections raised concerns about weak demand. The contract dropped as much as 2.6% before a small rebound from bargain buying, but sentiment remains bearish amid broader manufacturing slowdown.

title: COVID-19: Copper Mines Impacted by Coronavirus Measures
summary: COVID-19 measures have disrupted copper mining across Peru, Chile, Brazil and Mexico, including temporary shutdowns, reduced workforces, delayed projects and care-and-maintenance at several major operations. Analysts cited at least month-long disruptions and falling TCRC terms, while copper demand is described as near-nonexistent, implying bearish near-term price pressure.

title: A Chinese copper smelter entered month-long maintenance for April
summary: A copper smelter in south-west China has started month-long scheduled maintenance, expected to last until late April. SMM sources estimate the outage will cut copper production by about 6,000 mt. The reduced output is likely to tighten near-term supply expectations and support copper prices.

title: US officials investigating aluminum sheet subsidies from 18 nations, including Turkey, Germany, Oman, Bahrain
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department launched investigations into imports of common alloy aluminum sheets from 18 countries, checking for dumping and subsidies and possible U.S. injury to domestic producers. If preliminary findings turn positive, tariffs could be imposed, tightening supply prospects. An ITC preliminary decision is due by April 23.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 2): Shanghai base metals mixed on Thursday, copper advanced on oil price rally
summary: Shanghai base metals closed mixed: copper rose 1.02% on a crude oil rebound tied to expectations of Saudi-Russia output talks, nickel edged up 0.16%, while aluminium fell 0.56% as oversupply persisted. SMM notes primary aluminium inventories kept expanding this week and highlights key support/resistance levels.

title: Indigenous leaders alarmed that Glencore given green light to develop Aurukun bauxite deposit
summary: Queensland has appointed Glencore as the preferred proponent to develop the multi-billion-dollar Aurukun bauxite deposit in Cape York. Indigenous leaders criticized the process and consultation, but the decision supports progress toward bauxite production, which may increase perceived aluminium supply prospects.

title: Copper Supply Disruptions Not Enough to Offset Lack of Demand
summary: The interview says coronavirus-related copper mine closures and project delays are not enough to offset the immediate collapse in demand. Supply disruptions will have limited short-term price impact because demand is lacking globally. Copper has trended lower and could stay below key levels for weeks or months, though the analyst views it as not sustainable.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong speeded up decline on week
summary: SMM reports Guangdong social inventories of copper cathode fell for the fourth straight week to 82,700 mt as of April 3, down 10,300 mt from March 27. The weekly decline accelerated, suggesting improving supply tightness and potentially supportive near-term sentiment for copper.

title: London copper eases but on track for first weekly gain in six
summary: London copper eased 0.2% on Friday amid weaker investor sentiment as Covid-19 spread, though it remained on track for its first weekly gain in six weeks after better-than-expected Chinese factory data earlier. The piece also flags grim demand outlook and mentions LME aluminium rebounding from recent lows after a four-year low.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks extended decline on deterred arrivals
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell for a second week, down 5,200 mt to 333,800 mt, driven by limited seaborne arrivals amid COVID-19 disruptions and reduced warehouse inflows. Meanwhile, tax-cut stimulus expectations encouraged stockpiling, while improved import arbitrage increased warrant-related trades and inflow.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks continued to fall as pandemic reduced arrivals
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell for a second week as coronavirus measures reduced logistics and constrained arrivals. Inventories of pure nickel dropped by 700 mt to 18,600 mt, with cathode down 600 mt to 16,700 mt. With consumption recovering and arbitrage reopening later, bonded-area trades are expected to pick up.

title: Global Aluminum Market Huge Growth Opportunity between 2020-2025
summary: A market research report discusses expected 2020 growth changes for the global aluminum market, attributing near-term outcomes to COVID-19 disruptions and a supply-chain recovery that may begin around Q2 as quarantines and travel bans ease. It provides general demand/supply scenario framing through 2025 but no concrete near-term pricing trigger.

title: Chilean copper miners 'considering production cuts' – industry association
summary: Chile’s National Mining Society (Sonami) said copper miners are considering production cuts as coronavirus containment measures disrupt operations, halting projects and prompting companies to contemplate lower output. With Chile the world’s top copper producer, the move signals tighter near-term supply conditions and potential upside price pressure for copper.

title: Chile's Cochilco sees copper price down 45 cents to $2.4 per pound in 2020
summary: Chile’s Cochilco revised its 2020 copper price forecast down 45 cents to $2.4 per pound, citing a major demand slump driven by weaker Chinese purchases amid the coronavirus outbreak. The estimate marks a downgrade from January’s $2.85 and signals less supportive near-term copper demand conditions.

title: Chilean copper miners 'considering production cuts' -industry association
summary: Chile’s mining association Sonami says copper miners are considering production cuts amid COVID-19 restrictions. Some mines have already reduced manpower, while others have suspended projects or temporarily closed operations. With Chile the world’s largest copper producer, the potential supply reduction is likely supportive for copper prices in the near term.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports extended decline by 270,000 wmt
summary: SMM data show Chinese nickel ore inventories declined by 270,000 wmt in the week ended April 3, bringing total stocks to 9.98 million wmt. In metal content terms, nickel stocks fell 2,500 mt to 82,900 mt, with inventories at seven major ports dropping to 8.25 million wmt.

title: Chilean copper miners "considering production cuts" - industry association
summary: An industry association says Chilean copper miners are considering production cuts. The market implication is lower near-term mine output, which would tighten copper supply and likely improve the near-term balance for buyers. Such signals commonly support copper prices over the next days to a few weeks.

title: Alumina manufacturer in Ascension Parish temporarily laying off 300 workers in May
summary: LAlumina LLC, a specialty alumina producer in Ascension Parish, plans layoffs for 302 workers over late May into early June, with a full shutdown after limited inventory runs out. Management blames a coronavirus-driven slump in alumina prices. Plant disruptions and demand weakness may pressure nearby aluminium prices.

title: NEVADA COPPER PROVIDES UPDATE ON BALANCE SHEET STRENGTHENING FINANCING PACKAGE
summary: Nevada Copper updates its balance-sheet strengthening financing, fixing the conversion price for a C$ convertible loan and detailing potential share issuance/dilution tied to fees, a backstop, and capitalized interest. It reiterates Pumpkin Hollow is in production. The news is primarily corporate financing, not a direct copper supply/demand change.

title: Chemaf halts copper-cobalt processing plant over coronavirus
summary: Chemaf (Congo), a Shalina Resources subsidiary, put its Usoke plant on care and maintenance and stopped work at the Mutoshi copper-cobalt processing plant because travel restrictions and border closures made it impossible to source enough oxide ore. It also shut artisanal cobalt mining, likely extended beyond two weeks.

title: Philippines' Nickel Asia to resume ore shipment as local mining ban lifted
summary: Nickel Asia plans to restart nickel ore shipments to markets after a local mining ban in the Philippines was lifted. The resumption of outbound supply should improve near-term availability and weigh on nickel sentiment as inventories and prompt supply expectations adjust over coming days.

title: Copper rises as Chilean miners consider output cut | The London Free Press
summary: London copper rose 1.1% as Chile’s top miners consider production cuts during strict coronavirus measures. The report cites recession fears but highlights supply restraint from Chile. Nickel edged higher and aluminium was flat, reflecting mixed metal-specific sentiment despite broad pandemic-driven uncertainty.

title: Copper rises on lower exchange stocks, potential output cut in Chile
summary: Copper rose as exchange-tracked inventories declined, with Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks falling for a third straight week and LME stocks easing from recent highs. Support also came from Chile considering output cuts amid COVID-19 containment measures, though sustainability depends on export and demand conditions.

title: Copper firms on slowing coronavirus infections and inventory drop
summary: Copper prices firmed as coronavirus deaths and new infections eased in several European countries and LME/SHFE copper inventories fell, after factory data in China improved sentiment. At the same time, Antofagasta said it will suspend work on a Chile expansion for four months, raising supply disruption concerns.

title: Chemaf halts copper-cobalt plant, shuts artisanal mine site over coronavirus
summary: Chemaf, Congo subsidiary of Shalina Resources, halted operations at its Usoke copper-cobalt processing plant and paused construction at Mutoshi because COVID-era travel restrictions prevented sourcing enough oxide ore, leaving Usoke loss-making. It also shut the Mutoshi artisanal cobalt site, likely extending closure, while Etoile continues producing.

title: Funds cut copper exposure amid fast-changing fundamentals: Andy Home
summary: Funds cut both long and remaining short exposure in CME copper over two weeks as coronavirus-driven demand fears and supply disruptions rapidly changed. Shorts were reduced and the copper price steadied from LME’s four-year low, with open interest falling and traders reacting to accelerating mine and smelter disruptions.

title: Coronavirus-linked nickel shutdowns to help cut surplus
summary: Coronavirus-linked shutdowns at Glencore’s Raglan, Vale’s Voisey’s Bay, and Sumitomo’s Ambatovy, plus broader disruptions to ferronickel production and nickel pig iron logistics, are expected to shrink nickel supply. Despite weaker stainless demand, analysts project only a small surplus, supporting LME nickel prices after a sharp YTD decline.

title: Copper firms on slowing coronavirus infections, inventory drop
summary: Copper rose 0.8% as coronavirus deaths and new infections eased in parts of Europe, improving risk sentiment, while LME-approved copper inventories fell and SHFE stocks declined further. It also flagged coronavirus-related operational suspensions for copper and possible aluminum output cuts, alongside expectations of nickel supply tightening.

title: Global Energy Metals Reports Very High Recovery Rates for Cobalt, Copper and Gold from The Millennium Project in Queensland, Australia
summary: Global Energy Metals announced exceptional metallurgical recoveries from its Millennium Project, including 93% copper recovery into flotation concentrates and successful extraction of 95% of copper during subsequent processing. The results support producing clean saleable copper concentrate, improving project outlook, though no immediate production or supply change is indicated.

title: Russian firm Rusal and Glencore agree $16.3bn aluminium deal
summary: Russian aluminium producer Rusal has approved a $16.3bn long-term supply deal with Glencore to sell up to 6.9Mt of primary aluminium from 2020-2024 (plus an option to extend). The contract replaces an expiring agreement and supports primary aluminium sales at market price.

title: Canada Nickel Company Announces Discovery of New Palladium-Platinum Zone and Latest Nickel Intersections at Crawford, Provides Update on Transaction with Noble Mineral Exploration Inc
summary: Canada Nickel reported new drilling results at its Crawford project in Ontario, extending higher-grade nickel mineralization (including 0.34% Ni across 44m and 1.07% Ni across 1.5m) and identifying an additional near-surface palladium-platinum zone. It also updated a proposed property transaction with Noble, subject to approvals.

title: Copper Demand to Remain "Incredibly Weak" in Q2, Prices to Go Up in H2
summary: Capital Economics expects virus-related disruptions to keep copper demand “incredibly weak” in Q2, with demand growth negative in early data and demand not recovering until containment measures are lifted. The firm projects further price declines in Q2, potentially near US$4,000, with a rebound only in H2 under easing scenarios.

title: RPT-COLUMN-Funds cut copper exposure amid fast-changing fundamentals: Andy Home
summary: A Reuters column says funds have slashed copper exposure over two weeks, with short positions reduced and short-covering dominating amid a steadier copper price after March’s sharp collapse. The author links moves to pandemic-driven demand fears, supply hits from lockdowns, and exhaustion with fast-changing fundamentals, leaving traders cautious.

title: Copper scales near 3-week high on slowing coronavirus death toll
summary: Copper rallied to a nearly three-week high as slower coronavirus death tolls and easing-lockdown expectations boosted investor sentiment. LME three-month copper rose to around $5,025/t, with support from lower exchange inventories and possible supply disruptions. The piece also mentions gains in aluminium and a nickel supply-tightness offset.

title: Blackstone Minerals and Korean cathode supplier in Vietnam nickel processing alliance
summary: Blackstone Minerals will receive A$6.8 million from EcoPro to develop downstream nickel processing in northern Vietnam, using output from the planned revival of the Ta Khoa nickel-PGE mine. The project includes the Ban Phuc mine and a 450,000 tpa plant, targeting nickel/cobalt materials for lithium-ion batteries.

title: Nickel mining in Surigao del Norte, Philippines, remains suspended as the region recorded its first COVID-19 case
summary: Mining in Surigao del Norte in the Philippines remains suspended after the region reported its first COVID-19 case. Nickel Asia said its units would resume ore shipments only after local government approvals, but shipments are unlikely before April 30. The disruption follows a suspension that began April 1.

title: Antalya Mining profit falls as lower copper prices bite | 7 April 2020
summary: The article reports Antalya Mining’s profit falling as weaker copper prices reduce revenue and earnings. The connection is direct but it is primarily company-performance coverage, not a new policy, supply disruption, or inventory change. The news may reinforce near-term bearish sentiment for copper rather than trigger a fresh move.

title: Copper strides higher on hopes of slowing pandemic, stimulus
summary: Copper prices jumped about 4% to a near three-week high on hopes that the coronavirus outbreak is slowing and that stimulus will offset economic damage. The same relief/risk rally lifted other industrial metals, with aluminium also firmer. Aluminium premiums fell on weak demand, while nickel rose modestly.

title: Zambia says Glencore declares force majeure at Mopani Copper Mines
summary: Zambia said Glencore declared force majeure at Mopani Copper Mines and plans to shut operations in Kitwe and Mufulira, placing them on care and maintenance for three months due to coronavirus-related impacts. Zambia said it will block the move, citing legal notice and that mining is not impossible.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Acquires Airborne Geophysical Survey Data for Stu Copper-Gold Project
summary: Granite Creek Copper announced it acquired airborne magnetic and radiometric survey data for its Stu copper-gold project in Yukon and is processing it to refine drill targets. Limited past drilling reported copper-gold-silver mineralization, but no production, supply, or market-structure changes are described.

title: Zambia says Glencore declares 'force majeure' to shut copper mines, will block move
summary: Zambia says Glencore/Mopani has declared force majeure and will place its Kitwe and Mufulira copper mines into care and maintenance for three months, citing coronavirus pressures and staff movement restrictions. Zambia says it will block the move and claims insufficient notice, while 11,000 jobs are at risk.

title: Government Rejects Mopani Copper Mines' Plans To Place The Mine Under Care And Maintenance
summary: The article says the government has rejected Mopani Copper Mines’ request to put the operation into care and maintenance. By blocking the potential shutdown, the decision implies continued copper output and reduced risk of a supply pullback, which can support near-term copper prices over coming weeks.

title: Zambia says Glencore declares 'force majeure' to shut copper mines, rejects move
summary: Zambia rejected Glencore’s declared force majeure to place Mopani Copper Mines in care and maintenance for three months, citing legal and notice issues. The firm cited COVID-19 and staff movement limits amid weaker demand; copper benchmarks have already fallen ~17% this year.

title: Copper higher on hopes of slowing pandemic and economic stimulus
summary: Copper prices jumped to the highest in nearly three weeks as reports suggested COVID-19 cases may be slowing and markets bet on substantial economic stimulus. LME three-month copper rose about 3%. Aluminium also edged up, while spot premiums fell and cash discounts widened, reflecting still-weak physical demand.

title: Glencore's Mopani Copper Mines shutters Zambia mines due to coronavirus
summary: Glencore’s Mopani Copper Mines will shut its Zambia mining operations on April 8 amid COVID-19 travel and supply-chain disruptions, while continuing limited smelting/refining of on-site material. The miner cites a rapid copper price decline but the shutdown still signals reduced near-term copper output, tightening supply expectations.

title: Zambia says Glencore declares "force majeure" to shut copper mines, will block move - SABC News - Breaking news, special reports, world, business, sport coverage of all South African current events. Africa's news leader.
summary: Zambia says Glencore has declared force majeure and plans to shut Mopani Copper Mines in Zambia by placing operations into care and maintenance for three months, citing the coronavirus outbreak and staff movement limits. Zambia’s minister rejects the move and says notice and legality are inadequate, risking jobs for 11,000 workers.

title: Coronavirus impact sees Glencore Zambian unit shut copper mines
summary: Glencore’s Mopani in Zambia is moving to put mines in Kitwe and Mufulira on care and maintenance, citing COVID-19 mobility, transport and supply-chain disruptions plus contract force majeure arguments. Zambia’s government rejects the move. The firm also reviews spending after benchmark copper prices fell ~17% this year.

title: Glencore's Mopani Copper to shutter Zambia mines from April 8
summary: Glencore’s Mopani Copper Mines in Zambia will shut its mining operations on April 8, though it will keep processing material already on site in its smelter and refinery for now. Zambia’s minister suggested the shutdown could last three months, with talks ongoing with government and unions.

title: ATO escalates aluminium smelter dispute with Rio Tinto
summary: Australia’s ATO escalated its transfer-pricing probe into Rio Tinto’s aluminium division, moving to a formal amended assessment. The probe adds pressure to ongoing negotiations with the federal government over a rescue package for Rio’s three loss-making Australian smelters, raising near-term production and supply uncertainty for aluminium markets.

title: Further Downside Risk to Copper Prices "Unlikely" in Q2
summary: The interview says COVID-19 has pushed copper below US$5,000/t due to miner slowdowns in Chile and Peru and disrupted concentrate supply. Demand is also hit by 15–30% in Q1. However, the analyst believes prices are near the bottom, implying limited additional downside into Q2 as infection rates stabilize and TC/RCs guide tightness.

title: Philippines' No. 2 nickel ore exporter halts mining operations amid coronavirus concerns
summary: Philippines’ No. 2 nickel ore exporter reportedly stopped mining as coronavirus concerns mount. The halt reduces near-term nickel ore supply from a key producer/exporter, worsening availability expectations for market participants and weighing on nickel price sentiment over the coming days to weeks.

title: London copper eases as pandemic hits demand, supply worries cap losses
summary: London copper prices eased from a three-week high as coronavirus concerns dampened demand sentiment, including higher Spain and New York death figures. Losses were capped by mine shutdowns in Africa and Latin America (e.g., Mopani, Minera Panama) raising supply-disruption fears. Nickel is also supported by a Philippines mine suspension.

title: Strongbow Finds High-grade Copper-Tin Mineralization at United Downs
summary: Strongbow Exploration announced assay results from diamond drilling at its United Downs project in Cornwall, reporting high-grade copper mineralization (7.46% Cu over 14.69m) alongside tin. While further drilling is needed to confirm the extent, the discovery is supportive for near-term copper sentiment.

title: China copper smelters failed to agree on floor TC for Q2 2020
summary: China’s copper smelters did not agree on Q2 2020 floor treatment and refining charges (TC/RCs). The expected floor TC could drop to $60–65/mt versus $67/mt in Q1. Spot China concentrate TC/RCs fell to $62.5/mt, reflecting pressure tied to byproduct sulfuric acid and potential concentrate tightness.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 8): Shanghai base metals closed mixed; copper rebounded on lingering ore supply concerns
summary: SMM reports SHFE base metals ended mixed, with copper and nickel up and aluminium slightly down. Copper rebounded on stronger oil prices and recent mine closures/curtailments tied to virus containment, keeping ore-supply concerns. Nickel rose on aggressive long buying and short covering. Aluminium recovered but finished marginally weaker.

title: Glencore subsidiary MCM to shut Zambia copper mines
summary: Glencore’s Mopani Copper Mines (MCM) subsidiary in Zambia declared force majeure and plans to suspend operations for three months, citing COVID-19 disruption and lowered copper prices. Zambia’s mines minister says the government rejected short-notice layoffs and questions whether mining is impossible, leaving copper supply uncertainty.

title: Kodiak to Fly Airborne Geophysical Survey at MPD Copper-Gold Porphyry Project in Preparation for Drilling
summary: Kodiak Copper announces an airborne ZTEM geophysical survey over its MPD copper-gold porphyry project to guide a larger Phase II drilling program. The company aims to extend and better define copper-gold mineralization at depth and along strike. No production or supply disruption is mentioned.

title: Coronavirus-wrecked demand pushes aluminium to 4-year low
summary: Aluminium prices fell to a four-year low on coronavirus-linked demand weakness and renewed expectations of a sizeable 2020 surplus. LME warehouse stocks rose sharply, cash discounts widened, and analysts cited auto sector slumps and ongoing production growth, indicating increased glut risk and further near-term downside.

title: Glencore Shuts Zambia Copper Mine Over Coronavirus, Prices
summary: Glencore shut Mopani’s Zambia copper operations in Mufulira and Kitwe for three months, citing rapid declines in copper prices and Covid-19 disruptions to transport and supply chains. The move puts about 11,000 workers out of work and draws criticism from the Zambian government and unions.

title: Nickel Asia : Philippines' top nickel miners halt operations to contain coronavirus
summary: Philippines’ top nickel miners halted operations in Surigao del Norte until April 30 after local authorities requested a quarantine-driven stoppage. The province hosts the country’s biggest nickel mines supplying ore to China’s nickel pig iron and smelters. Existing stockpiles may still be transported, but ore exports face April disruption.

title: Copper belt miners turn to Tanzania
summary: South Africa’s COVID-19 lockdown hobbled ports, prompting Zambia and DR Congo copper belt miners to reroute shipments to Tanzania’s Dar es Salaam and also Walvis Bay. Dar copper cathode/concentrate exports rose 20–25% as some refineries shut, but capacity and processing delays raise near-term uncertainty.

title: Victory Nickel Inc.: Victory Nickel Provides Update of Activity at Minago and the 7P Plant
summary: Victory Nickel reported completion of two diamond drill holes at its Minago sulphide nickel project in Manitoba, noting assay results may be delayed due to COVID-19 movement restrictions. The company also stated its 7P sand plant in Alberta remains an essential service and continues selling sand to customers. No aluminium-specific information was provided.

title: Century Aluminum employee dies during incident at Sebree smelter
summary: Century Aluminum is investigating a fatal incident at its Sebree smelter in Kentucky, where an employee died after injuries in the anode production facilities. The worker was treated on scene and transported to a hospital. The company has not provided downtime details, but the incident may disrupt near-term aluminium production.

title: Chile´s Codelco says copper production, sales meeting targets amid coronavirus outbreak
summary: Chile’s Codelco said its copper production stayed in line with plans and it met 100% of sales targets despite coronavirus prevention measures at its operations. The statement to Reuters suggests no immediate disruption to copper supply or demand expectations in the near term.

title: Chile's Codelco says copper production, sales hitting targets amid coronavirus outbreak
summary: Codelco, Chile’s state copper miner, says it is maintaining production plans and meeting sales targets despite coronavirus measures. However, it will temporarily suspend around 30% of third-party contract work for 30 days as movement restrictions prevent contractors from completing jobs, with renewals possible as the outbreak evolves.

title: Copper Supply Cuts Seen Gaining Pace and Magnitude
summary: CRU Group says COVID-19 has already caused copper mine supply cuts and delays, but expects the pace to increase. However, it argues demand will fall faster, potentially leading to a 1 million tonne surplus and weaker prices despite some price rebound as markets await signs the downturn is easing.

title: Nickel at 3-week high as Philippines' top miners halt some operations
summary: Nickel rose to near three-week highs after Philippines’ top nickel ore miners halted some operations in a major mining province to meet virus containment measures. The article cites LME three-month nickel up about 1% and ShFE up up to 1.8%, reflecting supply risk from one of the world’s leading producers.

title: Nickel hits near 3-week high on Philippine supply disruption
summary: Nickel prices rose to near three-week highs as Philippine nickel ore producers suspended operations to contain the COVID-19 pandemic. Analysts said reduced Philippines supply would tighten ore availability for China’s NPI producers, prompting expectations of lower April output. LME nickel and ShFE nickel both jumped on the day.

title: Nickel climbs to highest in nearly 3 weeks on Philippine supply disruption
summary: London and Shanghai nickel prices rose to the highest levels in nearly three weeks as the Philippines suspended parts of its nickel ore mining operations to contain the coronavirus. Analysts cited tighter ore supply for China’s nickel pig iron producers, supporting nickel bullish moves.

title: Primary aluminium inventories fell for the 1st time since Lunar New Year holiday
summary: Shanghai-based SMM data shows China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots across eight consumption areas fell 69,000 mt to 1.607 million mt in the week ended April 9, the first weekly decline since Lunar New Year. Lower prices prompted smelters to hold back sales and cut warehouse deliveries, while demand improved.

title: Aluminium billet inventories shrank 4,100 mt on week
summary: SMM data show China’s aluminium billet inventories fell for a fifth straight week. In five major consumption areas, 6063 billet stocks dropped 4,100 mt in the week ended April 9 to 170,100 mt after an 18,500 mt decline the prior week, indicating tighter near-term availability.

title: Ventilator orders breathe life into Chinese copper demand
summary: Reuters reports that surging ventilator orders during the coronavirus outbreak have boosted Chinese copper demand. Traders cite increased production by car and AC makers supplying ventilators and delayed overseas shipments due to logistics jams and lockdowns in Peru and South Africa. This has tightened the market and lifted Chinese copper import premiums.

title: MMG declares force majeure on supply from Las Bambas copper mine – sources
summary: MMG declared force majeure on copper concentrate shipments from its Las Bambas mine in Peru after lockdown measures to contain COVID-19 and an extended state of emergency. Transportation restrictions are preventing delivery to customers, including major Chinese smelters, raising near-term copper supply concerns.

title: Three Elstree men jailed after copper theft in Staffordshire
summary: Police in Staffordshire stopped a gang attempting to steal copper cable from a business in Lichfield, seizing cut wiring and cable cutters. Six men were sentenced after pleading guilty, including three from Elstree. The case is copper-specific but appears limited in scale and unlikely to move copper prices.

title: BHP confirms first two cases of coronavirus at Chile's Escondida copper mine
summary: BHP confirmed two COVID-19 cases at its Escondida copper mine in Chile, with one employee and one contractor testing positive and several contacts placed in preventative quarantine. While many Chilean mines have maintained operations, the incident increases short-term concerns over copper supply continuity.

title: Copper price to grind lower as coronavirus hits industrial demand
summary: A Reuters poll expects copper, aluminium and nickel to weaken as coronavirus lockdowns reduce industrial activity, including autos and construction. Analysts forecast copper prices grinding lower, with a large surplus. Aluminium surpluses are set to expand further, while nickel faces delayed stainless demand despite supply constraints.

title: Copper set for biggest weekly rise in 14 months as risk appetite improves
summary: Copper is set for its biggest weekly gain in 14 months as signs of slowing coronavirus spread improve risk appetite and equities. China copper import premiums rise and LME price strength follows. Offsets include higher LME warehouse inventories and a copper concentrate force majeure from Las Bambas, but near-term tone stays bullish.

title: Black Butte Copper Project permit approved by DEQ
summary: Montana DEQ approved the Record of Decision for the Black Butte Copper Project, a proposed Tintina copper mine. The permit requires extensive groundwater/flow mitigation and strict wastewater treatment, including advanced reverse-osmosis and seasonal discharge limits. Development spans years, implying only modest immediate copper price pressure.

title: Base metals poll: Copper price to grind lower as coronavirus hits industrial demand
summary: A Reuters poll says coronavirus lockdowns have frozen industrial activity, hitting copper, aluminium and nickel demand. Analysts expect large surpluses—especially for aluminium—and forecast sharply lower prices, including new lows for copper in Q2. Nickel demand from stainless steel and construction is also weakening.

title: Glencore to shut Zambia copper mines | Medafrica Times
summary: Glencore’s Mopani Copper Mines in Zambia will shut its mining operations due to COVID-19 disruptions, while continuing to process existing on-site material. The company cites a rapid decline in the copper price and supply-chain disruptions. Zambia’s government is reported to seek to block the shutdown.

title: Montana environmental officials approve disputed copper mine near tributary of popular Smith River
summary: Montana environmental officials reportedly approved a disputed copper mine near a tributary of the Smith River. The decision potentially lowers permitting uncertainty for additional copper supply, which can weigh on copper prices in the near term by improving expectations for future production. The article content is not fully available to confirm details.

title: DEQ approves permit for Black Butte Copper Project
summary: Montana DEQ approved the Record of Decision for Tintina’s Black Butte copper mine. The review addresses groundwater flow reductions and strict water-quality requirements, including advanced treatment and no discharges during July–September. The permit enables project development over 19 years and could mildly support copper supply expectations near term.

title: MT DEQ approves permit for Black Butte Copper Project
summary: Montana DEQ approved a Record of Decision for Tintina Inc.’s Black Butte copper mine, subject to stringent water-quality and flow-mitigation requirements. The permit limits discharges, requires advanced treatment, mandates monitoring and seasonal restrictions, and can trigger further permit updates based on algae studies on the Smith River.

title: Refineries struggle to stay cash positive with alumina prices at Feb 2016 low
summary: The piece says aluminium refineries are finding it difficult to stay cash positive because alumina prices are at the lowest levels since Feb 2016. It frames weak alumina economics as a near-term stress for the aluminium refining chain, which can weigh on aluminium price sentiment.

title: State approves permit for copper mine near Smith River
summary: Montana approved a permit (“record of decision”) for the proposed Black Butte copper mine, allowing the developer to begin construction once a reclamation bond is posted, possibly this summer. Opponents may challenge the decision in court over environmental and cumulative expansion impacts, but approval supports copper supply expectations.

title: Montana DEQ gives approval for the Black Butte copper mine
summary: Montana’s DEQ issued a Record of Decision approving Tintina/Sandfire’s Black Butte underground copper mine near White Sulphur Springs. The permit includes mitigation measures for groundwater and surface-water impacts, including treated water discharges and tailings controls. Approval reduces project delay risk, modestly supportive for copper supply expectations.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks unchanged on week
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks were largely unchanged week-on-week, with refined nickel around 18,600 mt. Seaborne nickel arrivals were minimal due to COVID-19 logistics constraints, and although a Shanghai nickel price rebound narrowed import losses, import arbitrage still didn’t reopen, keeping foreign cargo trading muted.

title: NORNICKEL'S 2019 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT REPORT: REDUCING EMISSIONS AND SETTING NEW GOALS
summary: Nornickel’s 2019 sustainable development report highlights emission-reduction plans, including shutting down smelting operations in the town of Nickel on Russia’s Kola Peninsula to bring cross-border SO2 emissions with Norway to zero. The decision could reduce near-term nickel output, tightening supply expectations.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports extended decline by 430,000 wmt
summary: SMM data show Chinese nickel ore inventories fell 430,000 wmt in the week ended April 10 to 9.55 million wmt, with metal content down 3,900 mt to 79,000 mt. Stocks at seven major ports declined 313,000 wmt to 7.94 million wmt, extending the drawdown.

title: Chile's Codelco copper miner says it may have to slow investment plan
summary: Codelco said it may need to slow its investment plan. The news implies potential delays in future copper supply development, which can reduce market expectations for growth in availability and pressure sentiment toward copper in the coming days as investors adjust forward supply outlooks.

title: China issued 5th batch of copper scrap import quotas for 2020
summary: China’s environmental authorities issued a fifth batch of 2020 copper scrap import quotas, with high-grade copper scrap allowances jumping to 222,020 mt versus 3,520 mt in the prior batch. While the larger quota may help domestic supply, COVID-19 disruptions and supplier lockdowns keep scrap tightness concerns elevated.

title: Shanghai copper hits near 4-week high on supply woes
summary: Shanghai copper futures jumped to a near four-week high as supply worries mounted. ShFE copper inventories fell for a fourth straight week to the lowest since late February, while Freeport suspended operations at its Chino mine due to COVID-19. Pandemic-related logistics disruption and improving Chinese demand also supported prices.

title: MMG nixes Peru copper mine guidance
summary: The article’s headline says MMG has “nixed” (scrapped) Peru copper mine guidance. If production guidance is withdrawn, markets generally reduce expectations for near-term copper output, which can add bearish pressure to copper prices over the following days to weeks.

title: Sandfire's Black Butte copper mine in US achieves key permits
summary: Sandfire Resources America says Montana has issued the Record of Decision and related air quality and discharge permits for its Black Butte copper mine. The permits allow development of the Johnny Lee deposit and move the project toward bond calculation, construction, and eventual production, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Glencore's Kamoto Copper in Congo sends 350 contractors home
summary: Glencore’s Katanga Mining repatriated 350 Indian contractors after halting commissioning of the Kamoto Copper Company’s acid plant in DR Congo. The acid project was already delayed to the second half due to Covid-19 travel restrictions. The stoppage suggests near-term constraints on copper processing capacity.

title: Centaurus acquires Brazilian nickel sulphide mine from Vale
summary: Centaurus Metals acquired the Jaguar nickel sulphide project in Brazil from Vale after securing BNDES approvals, taking 100% ownership and enabling development. The project sits in the Carajás mineral province, with drilling already completed. The deal supports sentiment for future nickel supply, though output is not immediate.

title: Nornickel's investments in ecology projects up 21.6% in 2019 -  Business & Economy
summary: Norilsk Nickel said it raised 2019 investments in environmental projects 21.6% to 39.5 billion rubles and cut emissions by 16% to 2.2 million tonnes. The company is upgrading facilities and targeting large sulphur dioxide reductions under Russia’s Clean Air program, which may affect near-term nickel supply conditions.

title: MMG withdraws 2020 copper production guidance for Las Bambas
summary: MMG has withdrawn its 2020 copper production guidance for the Las Bambas mine. By signaling lower expected output, the update can reduce near-term supply expectations and lead traders to reprice the copper balance, typically weighing on prices in the short term over the following days to weeks.

title: Antamina copper, zinc production suspended amid Covid-19
summary: Antamina’s copper (and zinc) production has been suspended due to Covid-19. For copper, the temporary shutdown raises near-term supply disruption risks, likely tightening expected availability in the coming days and putting downward pressure on copper prices as markets price the output loss.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong shrank 4,300 mt over weekend
