summary: SMM says social inventories of copper cathode in Guangdong fell to 70,059 mt as of April 13, down 4,300 mt from April 10. The decline extends the fifth consecutive week, with stocks down 8,400 mt week-on-week, attributed to decent consumption and limited arrivals.

title: China unwrought aluminium, aluminium products exports dipped 5% YoY in March
summary: China’s exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium products fell around 5% YoY to about 518,600 mt in March, with total first-quarter exports down 17.5% YoY. The report expects further YoY declines in Q2 as coronavirus containment measures weaken overseas demand.

title: Copper Supply Cuts to Protect Prices, Prevent Major Surplus
summary: Refinitiv’s Karen Norton says copper prices may have bottomed, with further volatility likely. She expects China demand to recover modestly but decline year-on-year, while COVID-19 has driven miners to suspend operations and delay projects. Refinitiv projects a small surplus (~200,000 tonnes) due to supply cuts limiting downside.

title: Coronavirus crisis: Panoramic Resources shutters Savannah nickel mine to protect Aboriginal communities as Kimberley COVID-19 cases rise
summary: Panoramic Resources shut the Savannah nickel mine in response to the COVID-19 crisis, citing rising cases in the Kimberley and resulting travel bans and border closures. The shutdown is expected to disrupt near-term nickel output, tightening supply expectations in the next days to weeks.

title: China's copper ore, concentrate imports dipped 0.5%YoY in Q1 2020
summary: China’s copper ore and concentrate imports totaled 1.78 million mt in March, the lowest monthly level since September 2019, bringing Q1 volumes to 5.55 million mt, down 0.5% YoY. Unwrought copper and copper product imports rose 13% in March, but overall concentrate supply eased slightly.

title: Copper eases from 4-week high on global recession warnings
summary: Copper prices eased from a four-week high as investors grew more anxious about the global economy, citing IMF warnings of a deep 2020 recession tied to coronavirus activity collapse. LME three-month copper fell 0.1% and ShFE copper dropped 0.5%, despite China easing funding rates amid supply-risk support.

title: Black Butte Copper Project Completes Permitting
summary: Sandfire Resources said Montana’s environmental regulator issued a Record of Decision granting the Mine Operating Permit for its Black Butte copper project. With the permit in hand, the company can advance the feasibility study and financing for underground mining of the Johnny Lee deposit, though project timing may slip due to COVID-19.

title: Zambia plans to revoke Glencore's Mopani Copper Mines licenses
summary: Zambia intends to revoke Mopani Copper Mines’ large-scale licenses after the company allegedly failed to give sufficient notice before suspending operations and breached labor laws. Mopani shut mines on April 8 but continued processing material on site. Glencore has seven days to respond as Zambia reviews Nkana and Mufulira licenses.

title: Blackstone exercises option to acquire 90 per cent of nickel project
summary: Blackstone exercised an option to acquire 90% of the Ta Khoa nickel project in Vietnam for AUD$1m, including the mothballed Ban Phuc nickel mine and a nickel concentrator. The article cites strong drill results and plans for a maiden resource and scoping study toward nickel sulphate for lithium batteries, implying longer-term potential.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Announces Results of 2020 Winter Drilling at Falcon Nickel Project, Northern Saskatchewan
summary: ALX Resources reported analytical results from a 2020 winter drilling program at its Falcon nickel project in northern Saskatchewan. Nickel-bearing sulphide mineralization was intersected in two holes, with assays also including copper. Drilling was partially suspended due to COVID-19. The release is exploration-focused, not production-related.

title: Covid-19 impact: Panoramic suspends Savannah nickel mine operations
summary: Panoramic Resources has suspended operations at the Savannah nickel-copper-cobalt mine in Western Australia due to Covid-19 disruptions, including transport limits, workforce availability/costs, and equipment/supply accessibility. The company withdrew guidance and paused trading, citing cash preservation and planning for a safe restart.

title: Blackstone Acquires the Ta Khoa Nickel-PGE Project
summary: Blackstone Minerals has exercised an option to acquire 90% of the Ta Khoa Nickel-PGE Project in northern Vietnam from AMR Nickel. The project includes an existing modern nickel mine and 450ktpa processing plant, with scoping studies and metallurgical testing aimed at restarting operations as nickel prices stabilize.

title: Zambia plans to revoke Glencore's Mopani Copper Mines licenses -letter
summary: Zambia’s Mining Licensing Committee plans to revoke Glencore subsidiary Mopani Copper Mines licenses because the company allegedly failed to give sufficient notice and breached labor laws during its COVID-era shutdown. Mopani suspended mining April 8, though it continues processing onsite material in its smelter/refinery.

title: OZ Minerals Avoids Virus Damage As BHP Halts Copper Mine In Peru – ShareCafe
summary: OZ Minerals says COVID-19 has caused no material production impacts so far, though it deferred growth spending to preserve liquidity. In contrast, BHP and partners temporarily closed Peru’s Antamina copper-zinc mine due to COVID-19, moving it to care and maintenance and expecting a restart in roughly two weeks.

title: How The Pandemic Will Affect Global Aluminum Trade Probe
summary: Law360 reports that the U.S. industry filed new anti-dumping and countervailing duty petitions for common alloy aluminum sheet imports from 18 countries despite COVID-19 disruptions. The article notes pandemic-related demand declines and argues lower net prices and low-priced import inventories will intensify pressure on aluminum sheet markets.

title: Comet Resources: Capital Raising of $650,000 closed and Barraba Copper Project Acquisition Completed
summary: Comet Resources closed a $650,000 placement to fund the amended acquisition of the Barraba Copper Project in NSW, with initial drilling planned once travel restrictions ease. The release discusses copper demand outlook from emissions-reduction and renewables, but provides no immediate supply impact.

title: Potline 1 of Wenshan Aluminium's 500,000-mt project to come online at end-April
summary: Wenshan Aluminium’s 500,000-mt aluminum smelting and hydropower project in Yunnan will bring its first potline online by end-April. The company also runs an alumina refinery. The region has additional under-construction/built aluminium smelting capacity, implying rising near-term supply and potential downward pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Shanghai aluminum hits near 4-week high as China inventories dip
summary: Shanghai aluminium futures jumped to a nearly four-week high as China aluminium inventories fell for multiple weeks and social stocks hit a five-week low. Analysts cited increasing expectations of supply cuts. LME three-month aluminium also rose, though LME warehouse stocks increased, suggesting abundant prompt supply.

title: Spot copper sellers firmed up offers after declines in futures prices
summary: On Apr 16 in Shanghai, spot copper cathode sellers maintained firmer offers even after SHFE May copper futures slipped. Premiums for high-grade copper moved up to 200 yuan/mt earlier, then eased to 180-190 yuan/mt; standard-grade premiums fell to 170 yuan/mt. Trading remained tepid, with hydro-copper premiums at 140-150 yuan/mt.

title: GlobalData: Global Copper Mining to 2023 – coronavirus impact
summary: GlobalData expects global copper production growth in 2020 to slow sharply due to COVID-19 disruptions. Lockdowns reduce output in major supply markets Chile and Peru, with only partial offset from Cobre Panama and Grasberg. The outlook also reflects falling demand, reinforcing near-term bearish pressure for copper prices.

title: Group Ten Metals Inc.: Group Ten Reports Wide, Continuous Palladium, Platinum, Gold, Nickel, Copper, and Cobalt Mineralization Starting from Surface at the Chrome Mountain Target Area of the Stillwater West Project in Montana, USA
summary: Group Ten Metals reported drill results from its Stillwater West project, highlighting wide intervals of palladium/platinum and also nickel and copper sulphide mineralization. The release supports potential future resource development but provides no immediate changes to production or supply affecting copper or nickel prices in the next days-to-weeks.

title: Bonnell Aluminum Protecting Workforce in Five States While Producing Critical Items in Covid-19 Fight
summary: Bonnell Aluminum said it is protecting worker health across five states while continuing production and shipment of custom aluminum extrusions used in critical infrastructure and other essential products during the COVID-19 response. The company emphasizes no disruption to supply and rapid fulfillment despite supply-chain challenges.

title: Copper gains on China data but recession concerns cloud outlook
summary: Copper firmed on Thursday after China data suggested gradual recovery in the property sector, while LME inventories eased. However, recession concerns and anticipated metals demand destruction capped gains. Aluminium also rose for multiple sessions on expectations of supply cuts and improving Chinese market conditions.

title: Rio slashes copper target as iron ore exports underwhelm
summary: Rio Tinto said Australian iron ore exports missed analyst expectations and, more importantly for metals, it cut its copper production target. The company also warned that additional delays are hitting its troubled Mongolian copper project, implying tighter near-term copper supply expectations and potential downside pressure on copper prices.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Apr 17): Shanghai base metals opened higher across the board Friday, copper rebounded 2%
summary: SMM reports SHFE base metals opened higher as worries eased amid tentative US steps to restart the economy. Copper rose over 2%, supported by supply disruptions and an accelerated copper inventory draw in China, plus Rio Tinto cutting 2020 copper production targets. Aluminium edged up, while nickel steadied after losses.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong fell for 6 weeks amid rising consumption
summary: SMM data shows copper cathode social inventories in China’s major consumption regions declined for the sixth consecutive week. In Guangdong, stocks fell to 64,122 mt as arrivals stayed limited and consumption strengthened. Total major-area inventories also dropped, indicating tighter prompt supply conditions.

title: Global copper mine production dipped 0.3% in 2019
summary: SMM data shows global copper mine output fell 0.3% in 2019 to 20.37Mt, with Chile the largest producer. China’s production rose but still relies heavily on imported concentrate amid expanding smelting capacity. It also flags that, as the pandemic worsens, some miners are reducing output or suspending operations.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports dipped 50,000 wmt on week
summary: SMM data showed nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell further this week, dropping 50,000 wmt to 9.5 million wmt as of April 17, after a 430,000 wmt decline the prior week. Nickel-metal-content stocks fell 600 mt to 78,400 mt, suggesting tightening local availability.

title: Cornish village could become richest square mile on Earth after discovery of huge copper reserves
summary: A company says early drilling in Gwennap, Cornwall, found high-grade copper mineralisation (over 20%) at depths up to 330 feet and is seeking funding for further drilling. If confirmed, it would add potential supply of copper, supporting near-term bullish sentiment despite being preliminary.

title: LME copper set for best week since Feb 2019 on U.S. plans to reopen economy
summary: LME copper was set for its best week since Feb 2019 as Trump outlined a staged U.S. reopening plan. Copper rose up to 1.9%, with reports of strong Chinese physical premiums and tight scrap/concentrates. The article also notes LME aluminium and nickel gains alongside improved market sentiment.

title: Frozen pay and frosty relations: ASARCO's copper mine strikes
summary: ASARCO’s copper operations in Arizona and Texas are hit by a prolonged USW strike at five facilities, involving a 72,000 tpy smelter and a large open-pit mine. With roughly 2,000 workers out since October and no settlement, copper output is disrupted, tightening near-term supply expectations and supporting prices.

title: Zambia plans to revoke licenses of Mopani Copper Mines
summary: Zambia plans to revoke Mopani Copper Mines’ mining licences, citing insufficient notice before placing operations on care and maintenance during COVID-19, alleged labor-law breaches, and noncompliance around service contracts. Mopani had cited disruptions and a sharp copper price drop. Glencore has seven days to respond.

title: Eskom employee and accomplice bust for possession of stolen copper cables
summary: Police in Limpopo arrested an Eskom employee and a scrap-recycling company owner for allegedly stealing and selling copper cables. Authorities acted on information, found hidden copper cables valued at over R100,000, and later arrested an accomplice. The case is expected to proceed in court as investigations continue.

title: Brazil's Vale slashes 2020 production forecast for iron, copper, nickel
summary: Vale has reduced its 2020 production forecast for iron, copper, and nickel. While details are not provided in the excerpt, a lower copper and nickel output outlook would weaken near-term supply expectations and likely pressure prices as traders reassess market balances over the coming days to weeks.

title: Brazil's Vale slashes 2020 production forecast for iron, copper, nickel
summary: Vale has reportedly slashed its 2020 production forecast, including for copper and nickel. The revision suggests weaker output and potentially tighter near-term supply expectations, which usually weighs on prices for industrial metals over the coming days to weeks.

title: Zambian official says Glencore reverses plan to shutter copper mines
summary: Zambia’s Mines Ministry said Glencore has told the government it wants to keep operating Mopani Copper Mines in Zambia rather than shut down under “care and maintenance.” The government previously threatened license action over notice. Talks with Glencore are set for Monday, easing near-term copper supply concerns.

title: Primary aluminium inventories fell 60,000 mt over weekend
summary: Social inventories of primary aluminium ingots in China kept falling over the weekend. SMM data show stocks across eight consumption areas declined by 60,000 mt from April 16 to about 1.435 million mt by April 20, with demand described as strong, suggesting tighter near-term availability for aluminium.

title: Tightening supply to deter copper scrap discount from further widening
summary: Stringent coronavirus containment measures in March have reduced the flow of imported copper scrap into China, tightening supply across traders and processors. SMM expects foreign scrap shortages to persist for at least 1.5 months. Despite a recent domestic price rally, scrap discounts have widened and production remains constrained, supporting copper.

title: Weak car consumption to weigh on battery-grade nickel sulphate prices after April
summary: Battery-grade nickel sulphate prices in China have rallied, supported by improved precursor orders and low inventories, but SMM expects weaker downstream demand under COVID-19 to curb upside momentum in April. Producers limited cargoes; two plant suspensions may cut output, yet falling overseas orders could depress demand soon.

title: Shanghai nickel jumps over 4% as Vale cuts output forecast
summary: Shanghai nickel prices jumped more than 4% as Vale slashed its 2020 nickel production forecast due to the coronavirus. The cut intensified concerns about nickel supply shortages after Philippines mining disruptions, while China’s rate cuts boosted sentiment for stainless-steel demand, lifting ShFE and LME nickel to recent highs.

title: First Quantum Minerals : Zambian official says Glencore reverses plan to shutter copper mines
summary: Zambian officials said Glencore reversed its plan to shutter Mopani Copper Mines and wants to keep operating the Zambian copper mines after earlier care-and-maintenance plans sparked government backlash. Ministers will meet Glencore to discuss licenses and the way forward, affecting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Glencore reverses plan to shutter Zambia copper mines - Zambian official
summary: Glencore’s reversal of a plan to shutter Zambia’s copper mines (MCM) has prompted a dispute with the Zambian government, which threatened to revoke mining licences over insufficient notice before suspending operations. Ministers will meet Glencore via video conference to resolve the issue, affecting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Nickel prices supported by supply cuts as Vale trims annual output
summary: Vale slashed its 2020 nickel output forecast due to COVID-19, along with additional mine shutdowns, pushing LME nickel up about 2.6% to a one-month high. Vale also cut copper output estimates, though copper eased. Aluminium is weighed by a large rise in LME stocks and oversupply expectations, with prices down.

title: Nickel prices jump after Vale trims output target | The London Free Press
summary: Nickel prices rose sharply after Vale slashed its 2020 nickel output forecast amid coronavirus-related mine disruptions. Other nickel producers also shut or cut production. The article cites ongoing concerns about demand weakness and a projected market surplus, but near-term supply expectations still supported nickel. Vale also trimmed copper forecasts, while copper eased.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 20): Shanghai base metals closed mostly higher; nickel soared more than 4%
summary: Shanghai base metals closed mostly higher after China cut lending rates for the second time this year and stimulus expectations increased. Nickel surged 4.4% on the SHFE and LME. Copper and aluminium also posted gains, with copper supported by ongoing ore-supply concerns and aluminium stabilizing after strong weekly moves.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 20/04: Strong buying in LME nickel futures sees price climb 3.7%; copper dips below $5,200/t
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures recap shows strong buying in LME nickel futures, with prices up 3.7%, pointing to short-term bullish pressure for nickel. In contrast, copper is reported to have dipped below $5,200/t, suggesting bearish near-term momentum for copper. Aluminium is discussed but not repriced.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 20/04: Strong buying in LME nickel futures sees price climb 3.7%; copper dips below $5,200/t
summary: The live futures report shows strong buying in LME nickel futures, lifting prices 3.7%. Copper is reported to have dipped below $5,200/t. It also notes procedural corrections and delayed European low-carbon aluminium differential assessments, alongside commentary on aluminium supply and shipping disruptions, suggesting mixed near-term effects.

title: Nickel prices jump after Vale trims output target
summary: Nickel jumped on the LME to a more-than-a-month high after Vale slashed its 2020 nickel production forecast due to COVID-19 impacts. Other nickel mine shutdowns were cited. Despite supply cuts, a poll expects a market surplus. Vale also lowered copper output guidance, while copper fell on the day.

title: BHP iron ore on track but copper target set to fall
summary: BHP said its iron ore output remains on track, but it cut guidance for copper, nickel and thermal coal, citing coronavirus and other disruptions. With copper and nickel targets revised lower, market expectations for near-term supply weaken, which can pressure both copper and nickel prices over the coming weeks.

title: Tanga onto wide copper intercepts at Hagenhof
summary: Tanga Resources announced expanded drilling results at its Hagenhof copper project in Namibia, including wide breccia and copper-sulphide intercepts (up to 1m at 2.78% Cu within longer intervals around 0.56–0.71% Cu) and a large open strike zone. The company sees potential for hydrothermal copper deposits.

title: Copper prices drop as Glencore plans to reopen Zambian mine operations
summary: Copper prices fell on Monday as Glencore said it may reopen its Zambia Mopani Copper Mines if it reaches an agreement with the government, easing supply-disruption concerns. LME three-month copper fell 1.2% and ShFE copper dropped 2%. Sentiment was also weighed by broader risk-off moves, including negative oil.

title: Copper cathode inventories in Guangdong shrank despite greater arrivals
summary: SMM data show Guangdong social inventories of copper cathode fell to 59,741 mt by April 20, down 4,381 mt from April 17, extending a six-week decline. Stocks dropped despite increased arrivals, while consumption remained robust, indicating tightening near-term physical supply.

title: NBS: China refined copper output in March fell to 10-month low as COVID-19 disrupted production
summary: China’s refined copper cathode output fell 2.5% year on year in March to a 10-month low of 771,000 mt, with COVID-19 disruption cited as the cause. Daily output also declined versus Jan-Feb. China’s alumina production fell 3.6% y/y, which may modestly affect aluminium supply expectations.

title: BHP maintains iron ore guidance, but copper guidance under review | 21 April 2020
summary: The article headline says BHP maintained iron ore guidance but that its copper guidance is under review. This points to uncertainty in near-term copper production or outlook, which could affect market expectations. The excerpt itself provides no details on volumes or drivers, so price direction is unclear.

title: How US dumping duties will affect Egypt's aluminum industry
summary: AL-Monitor’s piece focuses on US anti-dumping duties and their impact on Egypt’s aluminum industry. Such trade measures can alter demand for Egyptian aluminum exports to the US and/or shift regional supply and pricing expectations, creating near-term downside pressure for aluminium. Details are not provided in the excerpt.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Apr 22): Shanghai base metals fell on Wednesday morning, nickel lost 4%
summary: SHFE nonferrous metals opened lower as oil prices collapsed, weighing on sentiment and prompting renewed demand and cash-crunch concerns. LME base metals fell overnight; nickel led with a 2.86% drop and copper fell 2.85%, while aluminium declined 1%. Traders expect continued weakness amid crude weakness.

title: South32's Cerro Matoso records 10% y-o-y increase in nickel output in Jan-Mar [CORRECTED]
summary: South32’s Cerro Matoso reported a 10% year-on-year increase in nickel output for January–March. The higher production rate implies improved near-term supply availability, which can reduce expectations of nickel tightness and weigh on prices in the coming days to weeks, assuming demand and inventories are unchanged.

title: Spot aluminium premiums continued to expand amid brisk trades
summary: China’s spot aluminium premiums over SHFE May continued widening as trade stayed brisk. Prices in east China were about 30–50 yuan/mt above May, higher than Tuesday. Social inventories of primary aluminium fell by over 100,000 mt week-on-week, with deeper backwardation and stronger demand indications.

title: Spot nickel trades picked up as SHFE nickel fell below 100,000 yuan/mt
summary: Spot nickel trading in Shanghai was brisk but prices fell sharply. SHFE June nickel dropped more than 4% to around 96,560 yuan/mt after a second day of heavy losses, with 1# refined nickel slipping to 97,200-99,300 yuan/mt. Brent oil fell to a record low, dragging nonferrous prices lower.

title: St George eyes nickel-copper targets at depth
summary: St George Mining reports early success from a magnetotelluric (MT) geophysical survey at its Mt Alexander project, identifying deeper conductive zones that could host nickel-copper sulphide mineralisation. The company plans additional MT lines and an extensive drilling program once modelling is complete, but no near-term supply changes are stated.

title: India probes alleged dumping of flat rolled copper products from China, 5 other Asian countries
summary: India is investigating allegations that Chinese and five other Asian countries are dumping flat-rolled copper products into its market. The probe could result in anti-dumping duties or other trade actions, potentially lowering import supply and easing downward pressure on domestic and regional copper pricing over coming weeks.

title: Copper steadies as supply fears and China demand support prices
summary: Copper prices steadied after an oil-driven selloff as miners warned coronavirus would reduce output and financial markets stabilized. China’s reopening, higher import premiums, and falling treatment charges suggest tightening supply. Antofagasta and Teck actions reinforced supply concerns. Aluminium demand in China rose on scrap shortages, supporting prices modestly.

title: New aluminium crisis looms as output rises in demand void: Andy Home
summary: Global aluminium production rose 2.1% in the first quarter, while usage/demand failed to keep pace. LME CMAL3 hit a four-year low around $1,455/t earlier in March and remains near $1,490. Producers are restarting and ramping capacity, while LME stocks have surged and spreads have loosened.

title: U.S. probe into aluminum sheet imports from 18 countries moves forward
summary: A U.S. investigation into aluminum sheet imports from 18 countries is moving forward. Such probes can result in tariffs or other import barriers that tighten supply entering the U.S., often lifting expectations for near-term aluminum prices as buyers anticipate reduced import availability.

title: Cornish copper find raises hopes for once 'richest square mile'
summary: Strongbow Exploration says engineers exploring geothermal springs in Cornwall for lithium instead found high-grade copper, averaging about 8% versus the global mined average near 0.5%. Further drilling will define the size and depth of the zone at Gwennap. The potential copper revival could support near-term sentiment toward copper supply prospects.

title: Copper firms as supply fears, China demand support prices
summary: Copper strengthened after two days of heavy selling as miners warned coronavirus would cut output and China began reopening, easing demand shock. Indicators such as falling Chinese treatment charges and higher Yangshan import premiums signaled tighter supply. LME aluminium also rose on reported growth in China’s primary demand driven by scrap shortages.

title: Trump to restore Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminium for Brazil, Argentina
summary: The headline says Trump will restore Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminium for Brazil and Argentina. Tariffs on aluminium imports are expected to tighten regional supply into the tariff-receiving market and lift import costs, which typically adds upward pressure to aluminium prices over the next days to weeks.

title: Alcoa halts aluminum, alumina estimates amid coronavirus pandemic
summary: Alcoa said it halted its global quarterly supply-and-demand projections for alumina, aluminium and bauxite because of the coronavirus pandemic, while keeping all bauxite mines, alumina refineries, aluminum smelters and rolling mills operational. The move pauses market guidance but does not indicate immediate production cuts, suggesting limited net price impact.

title: Withdraw export duty on non-metallurgical grade bauxite: FIMI
summary: The headline says FIMI is seeking withdrawal of an export duty on non-metallurgical-grade bauxite. If adopted, it would likely ease export economics and improve near-term availability of bauxite feedstock connected to the aluminium value chain, supporting aluminium price expectations over the coming days to weeks.

title: WBMS: World copper market recorded a 98,000 mt surplus in January to February
summary: WBMS reported the world copper market recorded a 98,000 mt surplus in January–February 2020 after a 197,000 mt deficit in 2019. Reported copper stocks increased by 263,000 mt. Copper mine and refined production rose year on year, while demand growth was not enough to offset supply, supporting bearish pricing bias.

title: Henan Zhongfu's aluminium smelting project in Sichuan to reach 250,000 mt/year in June
summary: Henan Zhongfu’s aluminium smelting and hydropower project in Sichuan is expected to bring potline 2 online in June, with full capacity reaching 250,000 mt/year. Potline 1 has been operating since November 2019. The new plant replaces an old smelter in Linzhou, Henan.

title: Anglo American Q1 Copper Production Down 9%; Reduces FY20 Capex Guidance
summary: Anglo American said Q1 copper production fell 9% to 147,000 tonnes, mainly from reduced output at Los Bronces as drought persists in central Chile, partially offset by strong performance at Collahuasi. The firm also cut FY20 capex guidance amid COVID-19, highlighting near-term operational pressure.

title: Spot aluminium premiums held firm despite a jump in futures
summary: Oil’s rebound lifted SHFE aluminium futures, but spot aluminium premiums over futures stayed firm. East China A00 premiums were about 40–50 yuan/mt, while Guangdong widened to 100–120 yuan/mt. Strong demand, weak arrivals, aggressive buying, and weekly inventory declines supported prices.

title: WBMS: World primary aluminium surplus expanded to 684,000 mt in January to February
summary: WBMS reported the global primary aluminium surplus widened to 684,000 mt in January–February 2020 versus 492,000 mt for all of 2019. Demand rose 4.1% YoY, but production increased faster (+8.3%). LME-approved stocks fell, yet surplus growth dominates the near-term balance outlook.

title: MMG's copper production falls 20% in Q1 on weak output from Las Bambas
summary: MMG said its Q1 copper production fell 20% year over year to 91,911 tonnes, mainly due to weak output from the Las Bambas copper mine in Peru. The decline was attributed to coronavirus-related restrictions, though the firm reiterated expectations for ~2 million tonnes over 2021-2025.

title: Renewed mistrust of foreign labor tests Indonesia-China relations
summary: Indonesian regional authorities are tightening controls on Chinese foreign workers during COVID-19, ordering some workers to return and denying others entry. The restrictions include Chinese technicians expected to repair nickel smelters at PT Gunbuster Nickel Industries. Separate cases also involve an aluminium producer denied foreign-worker access.

title: State regulators require reclamation of San Juan County copper mine by September 2021
summary: State regulators required Lisbon Valley Mining Company to complete full reclamation of its San Juan County copper mine by September 2021. The order effectively constrains ongoing operations and could lead to earlier mine closure or reduced output, tightening expectations for copper supply and exerting bearish pressure on prices.

title: USITC Votes To Continue Investigations Concerning Common Alloy Aluminum Sheet From Various Countries | Husch Blackwell LLP
summary: The US International Trade Commission found a reasonable indication of material injury to a U.S. industry from imports of common alloy aluminum sheet from multiple countries, alleging dumping and subsidization. Commerce will continue antidumping and countervailing duty investigations with preliminary rulings scheduled for June 3 and final determinations later in 2020.

title: President Rouhani Opens Iran's Largest Aluminum Plant
summary: Iranian President Rouhani inaugurated the country’s largest, modern aluminum production complex in Lamerd, with 300,000 tons/year capacity and about $1.2 billion investment. Officials said it will raise Iran’s aluminum output by over 63% in the current year and that output should further jump with the nearby SALCO smelter opening.

title: Rockcliff Discovers At Tower Deposit High Grade Copper Extensions Along Strike Including 4.88% CuEq Across 13.53 Metres and at Depth Including 5.87% CuEq Across 1.12 Metres
summary: Rockcliff Metals reported results from its 2020 winter drilling at the Tower Property, intersecting high-grade copper mineralization south of existing limits and at depth. Highlights include 4.88% CuEq over 13.53m and multiple high-grade intersections tied to conductive anomalies, suggesting expanded copper resources.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Apr 24): Shanghai base metals opened mixed Friday, nickel extended rally
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel extending gains, driven partly by Philippines’ decision to extend capital-region lockdowns until May 15, covering Zambales—an important nickel ore mining area. SMM expects 2–3 nickel-ore vessels affected, with other regions resuming May 1, supporting a bullish nickel tone.

title: RPT-COLUMN-New aluminium crisis looms as output rises in demand void: Andy Home
summary: Reuters column argues a looming aluminium “crisis” as production rose 2.1% in Q1 while aluminium usage fell much less, reflecting a demand shortfall from COVID-19 lockdowns. It cites LME prices hitting a four-year low and notes most smelters continued operating, worsening oversupply risk.

title: Miners seek export duty withdrawal on bauxite mined in Guj, Maha
summary: Indian miners urged Finance Minister to withdraw the 15% export duty on non-plant grade bauxite from Gujarat and Maharashtra because low-grade ore is not viable for domestic refiners/smelters. They cite declining exports and request duty removal to keep bauxite exports competitive during Covid-19 and shipping risks.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports dropped 302,200 wmt on week
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell sharply, down 302,200 wmt week-on-week to 9.2 million wmt as of April 24. Nickel ore stocks in seven major ports dropped 160,000 wmt to 7.81 million wmt, signaling potential near-term feedstock tightness for nickel production.

title: Philippines' Surigao del Sur to resume nickel ore shipments on May 8
summary: Philippines’ Surigao del Sur will resume nickel ore shipments on May 8, while Surigao del Norte (over 70% of exports) is expected to recover mid-May after a COVID-19 suspension. Quarantine extensions may still affect a few Zambales export vessels. Traders expect improved flows ahead.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks unchanged in closed import arbitrage window
summary: Shanghai bonded inventories of refined nickel remained unchanged week-on-week, with pure nickel at 17,900 mt and cathodes at 16,200 mt as of Apr 24. The import arbitrage window stayed closed, limiting inbound flows to bonded warehouses, while some arrivals cleared customs without entering bonded storage.

title: NPI smelting costs to rise as Indonesia puts floor price for nickel ore
summary: Indonesia will implement a floor price for nickel ore trades from May 14, using monthly mineral benchmark prices with up to a 3% discount. The higher ore-cost base is expected to lift NPI smelting costs for Chinese-backed smelters in Indonesia, pressuring margins and near-term nickel-linked output sentiment.

title: Copper eases on worries about recession, virus drug trials
summary: Copper fell 0.6% on recession worries and negative COVID-19 drug-trial sentiment, with demand pressure expected. The report cites mine shutdown-related supply expectations but says macro fears outweighed them. Nickel eased with on-warrant inventories at a multi-year high, while aluminum remained under pressure amid a ballooning surplus.

title: Indonesia sets price floor for nickel ore to protect small miners
summary: Indonesia’s ministry regulation sets a floor for nickel ore transaction prices using the government’s monthly benchmark price (HPM) derived from refined-price averages including LME. The policy aims to protect small miners as Indonesia pushes downstream processing and has already advanced its nickel ore export ban to 2020.

title: Aluminium Assn urges Centre to drop any move to increase tariff on import of chemicals
summary: The Aluminium Association urged India’s Centre to drop any proposed increase in tariffs on imported chemicals. The concern is that higher chemical input costs could weigh on aluminium production economics. By opposing the tariff hike, the industry signals reduced downside risk to short-term aluminium price expectations.

title: Vale, Glencore, Sudbury, nickel prices, COVID-19 pandemic, China
summary: The piece attributes nickel volatility to COVID-19 shuttering demand and Indonesia’s ban on nickel ore exports tightening supply for China. LME data show surplus narrowing but on-warrant inventories rising to the highest since 2018. Despite supply risks, analysts expect further near-term weakness, possibly to ~$4/lb, then later rebound.

title: Copper scrap supply in China shrank nearly 200,000 mt in Q1 as COVID-19 disrupted supply chain
summary: China’s Q1 copper scrap supply tightened as COVID-19 control measures disrupted import flows and Malaysia/Europe/US shipments slowed. Copper scrap imports to China fell sharply, while firms shifted toward copper cathode, lifting rod producer operating pressure and processing fees. Imports of scrap and remelt ingot are expected subdued in April-May, supporting copper prices.

title: China nickel inventories dipped 0.73% in the week ended April 24
summary: China’s refined nickel inventories fell 403 mt (0.73%) in the week ended April 24, driven by a drop in SHFE-approved on-warrant stocks. East China non-SHFE inventories rose on imported briquette arrivals, while bonded inventories were steady. Import arbitrage remained closed, keeping near-term supply tighter.

title: UAE-based Ridge Global Energy, Chinese firm sign five-year copper supply deal
summary: UAE-based Ridge Global Energy (Ridge Solutions) signed a five-year deal to supply 525,000 tonnes of Grade A, non-LME registered copper cathode to China’s Xinjiang Wal Optoelectronic. Procurement starts at 45,000 tonnes in year one and ramps up thereafter, with refining in Zambia and exports via South African ports.

title: Price floor for nickel ore to protect small miners
summary: Indonesia has issued a ministerial regulation setting a floor price for nickel ore transactions, using its monthly ore benchmark (HPM) derived from refined price references including the LME. The policy is intended to protect small miners during Indonesia’s intensified downstream push and nickel ore export ban.

title: Russia's Rusal Highlights Negative Effects of Coronavirus Pandemic on Aluminum Market
summary: Rusal said the coronavirus pandemic cut global aluminum demand by about 6% in Q1 2020, with transport and auto production hardest hit. It also reported rising aluminum supply and a 1.7 million tonne surplus. Rusal still increased output slightly, adding to bearish balance-sheet expectations.

title: SMM Copper Raw Materials Market Report- Keeping track of the China copper raw materials industry supply chain
summary: SMM’s report highlights China’s tightening copper raw-material supply. Coronavirus-related transport restrictions at South American mines constrain copper concentrate inflows, while China’s push to cut “solid waste” imports reduces copper scrap availability via lower quotas. The report expects an adverse demand/supply balance for copper feedstock into smelters.

title: Coal and alumina prices looking sick as virus takes hold
summary: The article says the early coronavirus-driven rally has reversed for Australian producers, with steep falls since February. It highlights significant declines in coal and alumina prices, and notes that aluminium (along with copper and zinc) is also suffering amid pandemic-linked demand concerns, pointing to near-term bearish pressure for aluminium.

title: London copper nears 6-week high as major economies prepare to reopen
summary: London LME copper rallied up to about 2.3% toward a nearly six-week high as major economies planned to reopen after pandemic lockdowns. The article also shows nickel rising ~2.1% and aluminium up ~0.5% alongside, indicating a broad, demand-sentiment-driven lift in industrial metals.

title: London copper nears 6-week high as economies reopen; stimulus measures eyed
summary: London copper rebounded toward a six-week high as investors expected reopening and factory restarts to revive industrial metals demand, supported by stimulus news. Aluminium stocks are still rising in warehouses, while China’s stockpiling plans and trade/import data bolster sentiment. Nickel also gained on the day.

title: Spot copper premiums fell as a futures rally sidelined consumers
summary: Shanghai spot copper cathode premiums eased on Apr 27 as sellers became more cash-in willing after long-term contract deliveries and a SHFE futures rally made buyers hesitant. With ample spot supply, premiums for standard and high-quality copper fell across the morning, and SMM expects softer support if futures strengthen further before May.

title: Lockdowns and low prices generate nickel supply shock: Andy Home
summary: COVID-19 lockdowns and low nickel prices are causing mine shutdowns and production cuts across major nickel supply sources, including Vale, Raglan, Ambatovy, and ferronickel producers. Chinese nickel ore and NPI output is falling and inventories are tightening, reducing the risk of large stock builds and supporting nickel prices near term.

title: China bauxite imports expanded 10.6%YoY in March
summary: China’s bauxite imports rose 10.6% year on year in March to 10.01 million tonnes, with Guinea the main supplier. Primary aluminium imports increased 35% to 5,409 tonnes and alumina imports climbed to 338,653 tonnes. Aluminium scrap imports fell 39% year on year to 76,672 tonnes.

title: En+ sees 'more visible' impact in Q2 from Covid-19 amid drop in aluminium demand, prices  | 27 April 2020
summary: En+ says it sees a more visible impact in Q2 from the COVID-19 disruption, citing a drop in aluminium demand and falling aluminium prices. The company’s outlook suggests reduced downstream consumption and weaker pricing pressure for aluminium over the immediate weeks ahead.

title: Copper hits six-week high on hopes for demand revival
summary: Copper rallied to a six-week high as investors bet easing lockdowns, factory restarts, and Japan stimulus would revive industrial demand. European plants and Chinese operations were resuming. LME nickel also rose, while aluminium inventories kept climbing and aluminium was marginally weaker.

title: Covid-19: MMG reports 24% drop in copper output for Q1 2020
summary: MMG said Las Bambas copper output fell 24% in Q1 2020 after Peru declared force majeure amid Covid-19 disruptions and a State of Emergency. The firm also withdrew 2020 guidance for Las Bambas, citing heightened uncertainty, which signals near-term copper supply shortfalls.

title: First Quantum cuts 2020 copper production guidance
summary: First Quantum announces a cut to its 2020 copper production guidance. The revision points to lower expected copper output in the near term, which can weaken market sentiment on available supply and lead to bearish price pressure for copper over the coming days to weeks.

title: COLUMN-Lockdowns and low prices generate nickel supply shock: Andy Home
summary: Reuters column says lockdowns and low prices are creating a nickel supply shock. It cites COVID-19-related production hits at mines and plants (Vale, Raglan, Ambatovy, Savannah) plus price-related ferronickel cuts totaling ~80,000 tonnes, supporting a recovery in LME nickel.

title: BHP joint venture Antamina copper mine in Peru reports 210 positive virus cases
summary: Antamina, a Peruvian copper mine jointly owned by BHP, Glencore, Teck and Mitsubishi, reported 210 positive COVID-19 cases after testing 600 workers and contractors. Two weeks ago it halted operations for at least two weeks to limit spread, raising short-term disruption risk for copper supply.

title: Copper falls after ICBC suspends some products to new investment
summary: Copper prices fell Tuesday after ICBC suspended new retail access to products linked to copper, citing extreme market volatility. Existing positions remain tradable, but new investment demand is curtailed. The most-traded ShFE June copper and three-month LME copper both declined, reinforcing bearish near-term momentum.

title: London copper edges up on supply shortage worries
summary: London copper edged up as production cuts by major miners and COVID-related shipping restrictions raised fears of tighter physical supply. Freeport’s El Abra will reduce processing by 40% and lay off workers, while lockdowns limit concentrate shipments and scrap availability. Demand uncertainty still weighs on prices, but supply fears support copper.

title: Philippines' top nickel ore miners to resume operations on May 1
summary: Nickel Asia and Global Ferronickel plan to gradually resume mining and shipping in Surigao del Norte from May 1 after COVID shutdowns. Easing restrictions should restart Caraga nickel projects, lifting Philippine ore supply to China, which has recently been disrupted and supporting nickel ore prices.

title: China's aluminium scrap imports jumped 30% in March
summary: China’s aluminium scrap imports rose about 30% in March as domestic secondary producers restarted after a COVID-19 shutdown, rushing to clear backlogged orders and boost processing-trade inflows. March imports reached 77,000 mt. Despite weaker export orders in April, scrap supply appears adequate for Q2.

title: Philippine nickel miners to restart coronavirus-shuttered sites
summary: Philippine nickel miners Nickel Asia and Global Ferronickel plan to gradually restart operations and shipments in Surigao del Norte from May 1 after COVID-19 restrictions ease. The prior shutdowns disrupted nickel ore supply and supported higher prices in China. Resumption should lift supply and weigh on nickel.

title: Copper falls as virus-led demand worries outweigh output cuts
summary: Copper prices fell as virus-led demand deterioration concerns outweighed output cuts announced by major miners. LME three-month copper dropped to $5,183/t and ShFE June copper fell to 42,300 yuan/t. Analysts cited severe supply constraints but said demand uncertainty and potential new lockdowns kept pressure on prices.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 28/04: LME base metals prices consolidate; copper supported by 7,300t fresh cancellation
summary: LME base metals prices were described as consolidating, with copper supported by 7,300 tonnes of fresh cancellations, implying improved near-term tightness versus outstanding supply. The text also mentions procedural corrections/delays to Fastmarkets aluminium assessments and commentary on aluminium supply conditions, but without a clear directional aluminium move.

title: First Quantum restarts Ravensthorpe nickel project
summary: First Quantum says it has restarted the Ravensthorpe nickel project. A restart generally increases near-term production and supply visibility, easing concerns about reduced output. That tends to lower the immediate nickel price risk premium, leading to bearish pressure over the following days to weeks.

title: Global Ferronickel : Philippine nickel miners to restart coronavirus-shuttered sites
summary: Nickel Asia and Global Ferronickel plan to restart operations in Surigao del Norte from May 1 as COVID restrictions ease after April 30. Previously shuttered mines in Caraga had disrupted nickel supply and supported prices. Reuters reports uncertainty around output and shipments, but resumption should restore supply.

title: SMM China Nickel Weekly and Nickel Downstream Sectors PMI Monthly – Keeping track of the nickel industry chain
summary: SMM reports volatility in China’s nickel chain. Indonesia’s ore export ban has shifted supply to the Philippines, but April imports were hit after Surigao del Norte mining suspended due to COVID-19. Meanwhile, China’s downstream nickel sector PMI rose above 50 in March as restrictions eased, indicating strengthening demand.

title: Southern Copper Corp (SCCO) - Insider Monkey
summary: BofA downgraded Southern Copper Corporation (SCCO) to Underperform from Neutral, though it raised its price target to $175 from $162. The update is equity-focused, but because Southern Copper is a copper miner, it may modestly affect near-term expectations for copper supply/profitability and sentiment.

title: Copper to Play Key Role in Post-COVID-19 World
summary: CopperBank’s CEO says post-COVID stimulus of over $10 trillion will largely fund modern infrastructure and electrification, which requires several times more copper per application (EVs, energy storage, grid and charging infrastructure). He also suggests copper’s role is strengthened by hospital demand ideas and constrained exploration appetite, supporting prices.

title: RPT-COLUMN-Lockdowns and low prices generate nickel supply shock: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist Andy Home says lockdowns and low prices are producing a “nickel supply shock.” COVID-19 disrupts operations at mines and plants (e.g., Vale guidance cut, mine closures/restarts), while low prices force ferronickel production cuts in several countries. Estimates cite large tonnes of market-driven cuts, supporting higher nickel prices.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Apr 29): Shanghai base metals opened mixed Wednesday, copper rebounded close to 1%
summary: SMM reports mixed nonferrous performance after Tuesday’s decline tied to falling oil prices. Copper rebounded, aluminium gained more than 1%, and nickel rose modestly (~0.5%). The note attributes gains mainly to macro optimism around economy reopenings and general market mood, plus some supply-related comments.

title: Spot copper premiums dipped amid holiday-thinned trading
summary: Shanghai spot copper cathode premiums fell sharply ahead of the Labour Day holiday as low-risk appetite reduced buying and downstream firms largely finished stockpiling. A rebound in SHFE May futures encouraged cargo holders to sell, further weighing premiums. Sellers resisted cutting below 100 yuan/mt, but anticipated holiday arrivals may cool trading.

title: Copper steady, focus on supply, demand developments
summary: Copper prices were steady on Wednesday as expected supply increases from producers easing lockdowns offset disruption concerns, while stronger demand signals from China were in focus. Analysts noted the market had not yet shifted to a surplus. Technical levels showed support near $5,050 and resistance around $5,288.

title: Indonesia rejects miners' proposal to end nickel ore export ban
summary: Indonesia rejected miners’ request to relax the nickel ore export ban. The coordinating ministry said processed nickel exports have grown and that allowing ore exports would likely cause world nickel prices to fall, especially amid weaker iron and steel demand. The ban began in January to expand domestic smelting.

title: Vale Indonesia's profit, nickel output drop in Q1 after export ban
summary: Vale Indonesia reported a sharp Q1 profit decline alongside a production drop and cites Indonesia’s nickel ore export ban plus weaker downstream demand from COVID-19. It notes slumping nickel demand lowered nickel prices in the first quarter and the trend may continue into Q2, signaling near-term bearish nickel pressure.

title: Rio Signs $51m Earn-in On Zambia Copper Deposits
summary: Rio has signed a $51m earn-in agreement for copper deposits in Zambia. The deal indicates additional investment and progress toward future copper supply, supporting bullish sentiment for copper. However, because it is not an immediate production or export change, the near-term price effect is likely modest and sentiment-driven.

title: Copper steady, focus on supply and demand developments
summary: Copper prices were steady as expected supply improvements from lockdown exits offset output disruptions, while potential stronger demand from China provided additional support. Analysts noted the surplus outlook has not materialized yet. Market focus remains on Chinese activity data and mine reopening frictions, with copper trading near key technical levels.

title: Chile copper industry largely unscathed by coronavirus – minister
summary: Chile’s mining minister says the country’s copper industry has been largely unscathed by COVID-19, with Cochilco estimating only ~1% output reduction (~63,300 tonnes). He contrasts this with other countries cutting production by 25–30%, suggesting a potential supply cushion that could support copper prices.

title: COVID-19 put Chile's copper industry in a tight spot
summary: The piece says COVID-19 put Chile’s copper industry in a “tight spot,” suggesting operational and market strain for the world’s leading copper supply hub. Such disruptions would likely reduce near-term output and/or exports while weakening sentiment, generally pressuring copper prices over the following days to weeks.

title: Chile copper industry largely unscathed by coronavirus
summary: The article headline says Chile’s copper industry has been largely unscathed by the coronavirus. That suggests limited disruption to mining, production, or related operations compared with market fears, which would reduce downside pressure on near-term copper supply expectations and potentially support copper prices.

title: Copper rises as China's factory activity data boosts demand hopes
summary: Copper prices rose after China reported expansion in manufacturing activity for a second straight month in April, improving demand hopes. LME three-month copper increased and ShFE June copper also gained. The report notes aluminum edging up and nickel rising, indicating broader risk-on sentiment across industrial metals.

title: Lundin cuts 2020 zinc, copper guidance, warns Neves-Corvo may not hit 2021 forecasts
summary: Lundin has cut its 2020 guidance for copper and warned that its Neves-Corvo operations may not meet 2021 forecast targets. The update implies weaker expected copper production/supply ahead, which typically weighs on copper price expectations in the near term.

title: London copper set for biggest monthly gain since Dec 2017 on improving demand
summary: London LME three-month copper is on track for its biggest monthly gain since Dec 2017, supported by improving China manufacturing activity. Copper premiums in Yangshan rose and bonded stocks fell, with ShFE stocks also declining. Optimism around demand and sentiment lifted prices despite export-order weakness.

title: Glencore Q1 Own Sourced Copper Production Down 9%
summary: Glencore said Q1 2020 own-sourced copper production fell 9% to 293,300 tonnes, with no production reported from Mutanda and Mopani. Nickel output rose 4% to 28,200 tonnes, reflecting disruptions and maintenance effects. Capex guidance was also lowered versus prior plans.

title: Glencore cuts guidance after fall in copper output
summary: Glencore cut production guidance across the board due to the coronavirus pandemic. The company reported first-quarter copper output of 293,300 metric tons, down from 320,700 a year earlier, alongside declines in cobalt and coal. The revised guidance implies weaker near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Copper social inventories fell for 6 weeks
summary: SMM data show China’s copper cathode inventories across Shanghai, Guangdong and Jiangsu (including SHFE-approved warehouses) fell for a sixth week. Stocks dropped 43,500 mt from Apr 24 to 308,900 mt as of Apr 30, reflecting a strong demand recovery despite still being above pre-Lunar New Year levels.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports dropped 347,000 wmt on week
summary: SMM data shows Chinese nickel ore inventories fell sharply, dropping 347,000 wmt from Apr 24 to 8.85 million wmt as of Apr 30, after a 302,200 wmt decline the prior week. Stocks in metal content and across major ports also decreased, suggesting tighter near-term supply.

title: KAZ Minerals Q1 Copper, Gold Production Up; Backs FY20 Production View
summary: KAZ Minerals reported Q1 copper production up 7% to 74.9 kt and confirmed all mines are operating with unchanged 2020 guidance. FY2020 copper guidance remains 280–300 kt, supported by higher ore throughput at Bozshakol. The update is specific to one producer, implying limited near-term copper price pressure.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks extended decline amid high import profits
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell for a sixth straight week, dropping 26,300 mt to 279,500 mt by April 30. Traders cited high import profits that encourage shifting cargoes to the domestic market. Downstream, especially power-sector demand, stayed strong, and SHFE backwardation kept premiums above 100 yuan/mt.

title: Copper set for biggest monthly gain since Dec 2017 on China recovery
summary: Copper is set for its biggest monthly gain since Dec 2017 as China’s recovery supports demand expectations. Official factory data improved, while Caixin weak demand tempered sentiment. Supply is supported by miner output cut forecasts and falling Chinese bonded and exchange inventories; aluminium sees smaller stock cancellations.

title: Rockcliff Makes Significant Nickel-PGE Discovery at the Tower Property 3.82% NiEq Across 2.4 Metres Including 6.79% NiEq Across 1.25 Metres
summary: Rockcliff Metals announced a new high-grade Nickel-PGE drill intersection at its Tower Property (up to 4.46% Ni over 1.25m; 3.82–6.79% NiEq). It is near the company’s copper-rich Tower Deposit. The release is exploratory and provides no production impact, making price moves unlikely.

title: Glencore's Sudbury Integrated Nickel Operations, COVID-19 pandemic
summary: Glencore reduced 2020 capex and cut production guidance amid COVID-19 operational disruptions and cost pressures. It reported weaker first-quarter copper output and lowered full-year copper guidance, and also trimmed expectations for nickel. The spending/output cuts imply near-term supply pressure and bearish sentiment for copper and nickel markets.

title: Copper dips on China factory data but hopes for recovery underpin prices
summary: Copper prices eased 1.3% after China private factory data unexpectedly shrank, reflecting COVID-related demand weakness, though official data and recovery hopes limited losses. The market also drew support from supply cut expectations, falling China bonded and ShFE stocks, and rising copper premiums. Aluminium slightly eased on LME stock dynamics.

title: Commerce Department Proposes New Aluminum Import Licensing System | Husch Blackwell LLP
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department proposes an Aluminum Import Monitoring and Analysis System requiring importers to obtain auto-generated licenses for basic aluminum shipments. It is designed to monitor and potentially limit import surges under Section 232 exemption reviews (e.g., Canada and Mexico). The rule would apply broadly, including FTZ entries.

title: Century Aluminum Co Q1 adjusted earnings Beat Estimates
summary: Century Aluminum Co reported improved Q1 adjusted earnings of $1.0 million (EPS $0.01) versus analysts’ expectations of -$0.09 per share. Revenue fell to $421.2 million from $490.0 million a year earlier, but the earnings beat may support sentiment around aluminium producer profitability and supply outlook in the near term.

title: Tsinghan, Eramet JV Weda Bay Nickel start production in Indonesia
summary: Tsinghan and Eramet’s joint venture at Weda Bay in Indonesia has started production. The ramp-up of new Indonesian nickel supply is likely to lift market expectations for availability, increasing downside pressure on nickel prices over the near term as traders factor in additional output.

title: Tsinghan, Eramet JV Weda Bay Nickel starts production in Indonesia
summary: Tsinghan and Eramet’s Weda Bay nickel joint venture in Indonesia has started production, according to the announcement. The start-up of additional nickel output can expand near-term supply expectations and likely pressure nickel prices over the coming days to several weeks, barring offsetting demand or disruptions.

title: Police arrest eight after violent protests at Indonesia's new nickel hub
summary: Police in Indonesia’s North Maluku have arrested eight people after violent protests at the Weda Bay Industrial Park (IWIP), where Eramet and Tsingshan operate a nickel project. Protesters destroyed property and looted food, raising short-term concerns about operational continuity and nickel supply risk.

title: Copper giant Peru to gradually ease restrictions on mining sector in May
summary: Peru said it will gradually ease May restrictions, allowing large-scale mining—including exploitation, storage, and transportation—to restart under strict health protocols after COVID-19 shutdowns. With Peru a major copper producer, the move improves expectations for copper output recovery over coming weeks despite ongoing virus risks at mines like Antamina.

title: London copper near 2-week low on oversupply concerns
summary: London copper slipped near a two-week low as markets worried about excess supply. Three-month LME copper fell up to 1% to around $5,061/t, with expectations for a 2020 surplus and coronavirus-linked demand deterioration. Supply eased sentiment after Peru signaled gradual mining restrictions relief in May.

title: Roskill: Indonesia to tighten grip on refined nickel supply
summary: Roskill says Indonesia will advance its nickel ore/concentrate export ban to January 2020, reducing feedstock availability for Chinese NPI producers and tightening global nickel supply in a market already in deficit. It also highlights COVID-related logistics and mine/refinery shutdown uncertainty that could further reduce supply near term.

title: Roskill Information Services Ltd: Roskill: Indonesia to tighten grip on refined nickel supply
summary: Roskill says Indonesia’s earlier nickel ore export ban (to January 2020) curtailed major NPI feedstock flows to China, forcing producers to draw down port stockpiles and increasing reliance on alternative sources. With COVID-19 causing further supply/logistics uncertainty and possible outside-China care-and-maintenance, nickel supply tightness risk rises.

title: London copper hits near 2-week low as some producers resume work
summary: London copper fell to a near two-week low, down about 1% on Monday, as some producers signaled they may resume operations while the coronavirus clouded global demand. Although production cuts previously supported prices, Peru eased mining restrictions in May. LME aluminium and nickel also declined.

title: Phoenix Copper ups resource estimate at Empire project in Idaho by 27% | AJ Bell Youinvest : 04/05/20 09:39
summary: Phoenix Copper said its resource estimate at the Empire project in Idaho was increased by 27%. The update is positive for the project’s potential resource base, which may lift sentiment around future copper supply prospects and support copper-related pricing expectations in the near term.

title: Lindian hits grade at conglomerate bauxite play in Guinea
summary: Lindian Resources says early XRF and digestion test work from its Gaoual bauxite project in Guinea shows high-grade conglomerate bauxite, with 56% alumina on average and low reactive silica. The company expects an easier processing flow sheet and will proceed toward resource work, but production timing is not yet defined.

title: Copper sinks to 2-week low as demand concerns resurface
summary: Copper prices fell to a two-week low as coronavirus-driven demand worries resurfaced, particularly around China’s ability to sustain base-metals consumption. The piece cites weak PMI data, potential oversupply signals, and Peru easing mining restrictions. Aluminium and nickel also declined on the same risk-off demand concerns.

title: Copper smelter Aurubis gets EU approval for Metallo takeover
summary: The European Commission approved Aurubis’s 380 million euro acquisition of Belgian-Spanish recycler Metallo. The deal combines Aurubis’s copper smelting with Metallo’s scrap processing capacity. Approval is unconditional, with consolidation starting June 1. The merger should not harm competition, but it is not a clear immediate copper supply shock.

title: U.S. Primary Aluminum Industry Lauds Import Monitoring Program; Calls for Immediate Action to Address Current Canadian Surge
summary: The U.S. primary aluminium industry praised an import monitoring program and urged immediate action to address a reported Canadian import surge. The push suggests expectations for tighter oversight or mitigations that could reduce unwanted inflows, supporting near-term aluminium market balance in the U.S.

title: Copper sinks to two-week low as demand concerns resurface
summary: Copper prices slid to a two-week low on the LME as coronavirus-linked demand concerns resurfaced, particularly around shrinking demand from top consumer China and other regions. The move followed easing of some lockdown restrictions by producers, but market focus stayed on potential demand softness, weighing on copper.

title: Aurubis : Copper smelter Aurubis gets EU approval for Metallo takeover
summary: Europe’s copper smelter Aurubis received EU antitrust approval to acquire Belgian-Spanish recycler Metallo for €380 million. Metallo processes substantial scrap volumes at plants in Belgium and Spain, mainly supporting copper recycling capacity. Approval reduces deal uncertainty and supports expectations for continued copper recycling throughput, with limited direct implications for prices immediately.

title: New aluminum billet company would bring 30 jobs to Richmond
summary: Richmond, Ind. approved tax abatements for Element 13 LLC to build a facility making aluminum billets by melting scrap and supplying extruder companies. The project includes abatements for real estate, manufacturing equipment, and IT. The expansion suggests incremental aluminum processing capacity, though the local scale may limit market impact.

title: Tanking aluminium prices don't bode well for Tiwai smelter
summary: Aluminium prices dropped to their lowest level in over a decade in April as demand weakened and Rio Tinto continues to consider the future of its Tiwai Point smelter. It also expects aluminium stocks to rise to record levels this year, signalling ongoing bearish fundamentals for aluminium.

title: Aluminium falls towards 4-year lows on fears of oversupply
summary: LME aluminium slid toward four-year lows as investors feared demand collapse could combine with rising output to create a large oversupply. ING projected a surplus of around 1.5 million tonnes for the year. LME cash discounts widened and warehouse inventories rose, reinforcing plentiful near-term supply signals.

title: Fjordland Executes Thompson Nickel Option with CanAlaska Uranium
summary: Fjordland Exploration entered an option agreement to earn up to 80% in CanAlaska’s North Thompson nickel project in Manitoba, with plans for staged exploration and possible joint venture participation. The belt is described as large-scale and drill-ready, near existing Vale nickel facilities.

title: Funds don't buy into Doctor Copper's recovery story: Andy Home
summary: Copper has rebounded from March lows, but the article says funds are not buying into the recovery. Net short positions on CME and LME have been trimmed mainly via bear covering, while outright longs haven’t built. Concerns over a COVID-19 second-wave demand hit and China’s “bao” scandal may suppress speculative buying.

title: Asiamet Resources continues to advance Indonesian copper projects
summary: Asiamet Resources reported improved FY results and detailed progress on its Indonesian copper projects, including a Beutong resource boost and advancement toward a bankable feasibility study for BKM. The company also discussed financing via placings and a strategic MOU. The updates are copper-specific but pre-production in nature.

title: Canada Nickel Company Inc. Closes Private Placement of $4.4 Million
summary: Canada Nickel closed a $4.4 million private placement, including flow-through financing, to fund advancement of its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide discovery and working capital. The release describes use of proceeds for exploration expenditures in Ontario. It does not announce production or supply changes, implying limited near-term impact on nickel pricing.

title: Copper Smelter Cuts Ahead, Mine Supply Will be Resilient
summary: The piece argues COVID-19 will continue to hurt demand for base metals, keeping the complex under pressure. For copper, concentrate supply has tightened as China ramps up while smelters face weak sulfuric acid revenue, suggesting possible smelter cuts and a floor for treatment charges. Overall direction remains bearish.

title: London copper nears 1-week high on prospects of demand recovery
summary: London LME three-month copper rose about 0.8% to near a one-week high, driven by hopes that easing coronavirus restrictions will improve global demand. The move is also linked to support from stimulus and earlier supply-shortage worries. China’s return from Labour Day holidays is mentioned as timing context.

title: Primary aluminium inventories dropped 32,000 mt over the holiday
summary: SMM data show Chinese social inventories of primary aluminium ingots fell 32,000 mt from April 30 to May 6, totaling 1.172 million mt, after a larger prior-week drop. The decline is attributed to strong demand and limited arrivals across major consumption regions including SHFE warrants.

title: Spot copper premiums edged up as major traders stockpiled
summary: Spot copper cathode premiums in Shanghai edged higher on May 6 after Labour Day, with traders replenishing inventories. Premiums for standard-grade copper rose to around 140 yuan/mt versus SHFE May, and 150–160 yuan/mt for high-quality. Downstream buyers stayed cautious as futures firmed slightly.

title: Factbox: Aluminium operations shuttered due to coronavirus
summary: Reuters factbox says the coronavirus is slashing aluminium demand while producers still add supply, implying a large annual surplus. However, several smelters and plants have been curtailed or shut due to lockdowns (e.g., Alcoa Intalco, Rio Tinto Tiwai Point pot-line, Aluar Puerto Madryn), and restarts are delayed.

title: Aluminium operations shuttered due to coronavirus
summary: Coronavirus lockdowns are sharply reducing aluminium demand, while analysts expect a major market surplus (2.6 million tonnes in 2020). Producers are idling capacity at multiple smelters and delaying restarts or launches (e.g., Alcoa, Rio Tinto, Norsk Hydro, Aluar, Rusal), but supply is still projected to exceed demand.

title: Aluminium billet inventories added 2,700 mt over holiday
summary: China’s aluminium billet inventories rose during the Labour Day holidays, adding 2,700 mt to 132,100 mt as of May 6. The increase follows an eight-week decline and was driven largely by Foshan, Guangdong (+5,200 mt), with other regions mixed. Wuxi and Changzhou were slightly lower.

title: Sharjah fire: Aluminium cladding blamed as authorities to probe towers across emirate
summary: Sharjah’s Abbco Tower fire spread faster due to banned aluminium composite panel cladding installed before a 2017 UAE prohibition. Authorities plan to assess how widely such cladding was used and whether it should be removed from older towers. Retrofitting and façade upgrades are cited as costly but feasible, implying potential aluminium-related demand.

title: Rare Metal Mining Discovers Large Gold and Copper Ore Bodies Near Oyu Tolgoi
summary: Rare Metal Mining says it discovered large gold and copper ore bodies near Mongolia’s Oyu Tolgoi region and signed a joint venture to develop the land. Drilling/extraction are expected mainly from 2021 onward, so the copper-supply upside is gradual. Nickel is mentioned only generally as a potential resource for Mongolia.

title: SMM Morning Comments (May 7): Shanghai base metals held onto gains from overnight, nickel added 2%
summary: SMM notes base metals strengthened after the post–Chinese New Year return to trading, with nickel adding over 2% and copper also rebounding, while aluminium is mixed but supported by falling domestic inventories. LME prices were broadly higher overnight; nickel and copper led gains, and aluminium outlook hinges on demand recovery concerns.

title: China unwrought aluminium, aluminium products exports fell 11.4% YoY in April
summary: China’s exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium products fell about 11.4% YoY to 441,000 mt in April, extending a worsening decline from March. April exports and the first-four-month total both dropped versus last year, attributed to weaker overseas demand as global lockdowns reduce consumption.

title: China's imports of unwrought copper and copper products increased 10.4%YoY in January-April
summary: China’s customs data show imports of unwrought copper and copper products totaled 1.75 million mt in January–April 2020, up 10.4% year-on-year. April imports were about 461,000 mt, up 4.3% from March and faster growth than the earlier Jan–Mar period, pointing to stronger copper demand.

title: China's copper ore, concentrate imports rose 4.9%YoY in January-April
summary: China’s copper ore and concentrate imports rose about 14% month-on-month in April to 2.03 million mt, and were up 4.9% year-on-year in January–April. Imports of unwrought copper and products also increased 4.4% month-on-month, suggesting firmer copper intake and supportive near-term sentiment for copper.

title: China April copper imports rise 4.3% month-on-month - Reuters calcs
summary: China’s unwrought copper imports rose 4.3% month-on-month in April to 460,952 tonnes, according to Reuters calculations from customs data. The increase is attributed to improving economic conditions post-COVID and favourable prices, suggesting stronger near-term demand that can support copper pricing.

title: China April copper imports rise as demand recovers; aluminium exports slump
summary: China reported April unwrought copper imports rising 4.4% month-on-month, helped by recovering manufacturing activity and arbitrage to Shanghai prices after LME declines, alongside refined copper inventory drawdowns. By contrast, aluminium exports fell 14.9% on weaker overseas orders amid COVID-19 disruptions, signaling softer external demand.

title: China April copper imports rise as demand recovers; aluminium exports slump
summary: China’s unwrought copper imports rose in April as manufacturing activity resumed, pricing encouraged arbitrage to Shanghai, and refined copper inventories in bonded warehouses were drawn down. Copper concentrate imports also increased. Meanwhile, aluminium exports fell to the lowest monthly level since October as overseas orders weakened during the coronavirus spread.

title: Trump's tariff wall breached by rising tide of aluminum: Andy Home
summary: The article says U.S. aluminum tariffs have failed to support domestic supply: Alcoa is putting the Ferndale smelter on care and maintenance and curtailing capacity due to uncompetitive conditions. Meanwhile imports and semi-manufactured aluminum inflows keep rising amid China’s overcapacity, weighing on LME aluminum prices near multi-year lows.

title: Chile anticipates a glut of some 200.000/300.000 tons of copper in 2020
summary: Antofagasta’s CEO said the global copper market could run a 200,000–300,000 ton surplus in 2020. He attributed the outlook to operating disruptions at some mines offsetting but not fully countering demand depression from the coronavirus, which should be reflected in weaker copper prices.

title: Trump's tariff wall breached by rising tide of aluminium: Andy Home
summary: Reuters column says U.S. 10% aluminium tariffs are not working, with rising aluminium product imports despite an exclusion system. It cites Alcoa putting the Ferndale smelter on care and maintenance and an LME aluminium price near a four-year low. The author blames China’s expanding overcapacity for ongoing pressure.

title: Chilean copper miner Codelco says it maintains production and shipments according to 2020 plan
summary: Codelco said it is maintaining production and shipments according to its 2020 plan despite coronavirus disruptions in Chile. The miner paused some construction and third-party contract work to balance worker health with operational continuity. The statement implies copper supply is being held steady in the near term, limiting immediate market impact.

title: Ero Copper Announces First Quarter Results, Improved Operating and Capital Cost Guidance for 2020
summary: Ero Copper Corp. reported Q1 2020 copper production of 10,657 tonnes and record low C1 cash costs of $0.71/lb, alongside improved operating and capital cost guidance. The company lowered full-year copper C1 cost guidance to $0.70–$0.85/lb, citing a weaker USD/BRL, and said production guidance remains unchanged.

title: Philippines' Nickel Asia Q1 ore shipments slightly down amid coronavirus disruptions
summary: The report says Philippines-based Nickel Asia’s Q1 ore shipments were slightly lower as coronavirus disruptions affected operations and logistics. A fall in near-term nickel ore availability can tighten supply expectations for refiners and trading, typically exerting downward pressure on nickel prices over the following days to weeks.

title: Nickel Asia : Philippines' Nickel Asia first-quarter ore shipments slightly down amid coronavirus disruptions
summary: Nickel Asia Corp said first-quarter nickel ore shipments fell 3.8% to 2.78 million wet metric tonnes as coronavirus disruptions cut shipments and prompted nearly a month of voluntary mine suspension. Taganito and Hinatuan mines restarted in June gradually. Ore prices supported revenue, but supply uncertainty remains for nickel.

title: Shanghai copper hits 3-week high on upbeat China demand, trade hopes
summary: Shanghai copper jumped to a three-week high, supported by China’s stronger copper import figures (unwrought and concentrate) and reports of tighter scrap rules plus South American mine disruptions. Trade-deal implementation hopes between the U.S. and China further boosted sentiment, while Chile and Peru supply updates added support.

title: Spot copper premiums fell on further rally in futures, cautious buyers
summary: On May 8 in Shanghai, sellers cut spot copper cathode offers as SHFE copper futures rallied further, sidelining downstream consumers. Spot premiums fell to about 90–110 yuan/mt from 120–140 earlier, with hydro-copper sold at even lower levels amid oversupply and subdued weekend trading.

title: Chile's Codelco copper output jumped 14.8% YoY in March
summary: Chile’s Codelco said its March copper production rose 14.8% YoY to 147,600 mt, lifting Q1 output to 386,600 mt (+4.2% YoY), per Cochilco. It also indicated production and shipments remain aligned with its 2020 plan despite coronavirus disruptions.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks extended decline on enticing import profits
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell another 14,500 mt to 265,000 mt as robust Chinese consumption and attractive import profits increased demand for imported copper.
