Copper rod producers’ operating rates moved toward record highs in April, while Yangshan premiums rose, keeping the import arbitrage window open and suggesting tighter supplies.

title: Western Copper and Gold Announces $3.36 Million Private Placement of Flow-Through Shares
summary: Western Copper and Gold announced a C$3.36 million non-brokered flow-through share private placement to fund Canadian exploration at its Casino copper-gold project in Yukon. Proceeds will be used for qualifying exploration expenditures. The release does not indicate any near-term supply disruption or production change.

title: Spot copper concentrate TC plunged to 8-month low as COVID-19 disrupted supply
summary: China’s spot copper concentrate treatment charges (TCs) fell to an 8-month low amid coronavirus lockdowns that disrupted mine operations and shipments, with some miners declaring force majeure. The SMM copper concentrate index dropped to $54.21/mt, indicating tighter concentrate supply and potential near-term support for copper prices.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 179,000 wmt on week
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories across Chinese ports kept falling, dropping 179,000 wmt from April 30 to 8.67 million wmt as of May 8. Stocks in metal content fell to 71,300 mt, reflecting tighter local ore availability after a larger prior-week drop.

title: China refined nickel output declined 7.6% in April
summary: SMM data show China’s refined nickel production fell 7.63% m/m to 14,400 mt in April. Smelters were mostly stable, but output dropped due to calculation differences and some planned adjustments tied to raw-material costs and profits. May production is expected to rise as nickel prices rally and COVID containment eases.

title: Phased capacity of Wenshan Aluminium's 500,000 mt/year project came online on May 5
summary: Wenshan Aluminium’s Phase I of a 500,000 mt/year Yunnan hydropower-supported smelter started up on May 5. The first phase includes 62 500KA integrated prebaked anode electrolytic tanks, while Phase II remains pending. The company also operates an alumina refinery, supplying the wider production chain.

title: Egypt Aluminum denies cancelling plans to set up new production line
summary: Egypt Aluminum in Egypt denied media reports that it would upgrade an existing sixth production line instead of building a seventh. The company said the tender for the new line is postponed to June 1 and targets an additional 250,000 tonnes/year of primary aluminium capacity.

title: China copper cathode production up 1.2% in April
summary: China’s copper cathode output rose 1.17% month-on-month in April as smelters restarted and new capacity ramped up amid slowing coronavirus spread. Yet reduced seaborne concentrate deliveries from Peru and other disruptions raised raw-material concerns, and planned Q2 maintenance could lower June-July cathode output, supporting copper prices.

title: China nickel sulphate production fell 6.9% in April
summary: China’s nickel sulphate output declined 6.9% in April to 44,500 mt as higher raw material costs and weak demand led producers to shut in capacity and clear inventories. About 5,000–6,000 mt of output was lost, and with fewer orders in May, sentiment is likely bearish despite a modest rebound planned.

title: London copper hits 8-week high as more countries restart economies
summary: London copper rose to an eight-week high on expectations that easing lockdowns will improve demand for metals. The article cites economic reopening in Australia, France, Spain and limited UK easing, with three-month LME copper up 1.8%. LME aluminum and nickel were also higher on the same risk-on demand outlook.

title: London copper hits 8-week high as countries ease restrictions
summary: London copper rose to an 8-week high as countries began easing COVID restrictions, lifting hopes for metal demand. LME three-month copper climbed up to 1.8% and was still higher at 1.2%. LME aluminum also rose and nickel in Shanghai edged higher amid improving economic signals.

title: Eurobattery Minerals Signs Investment Agreement With Option to Acquire the Hautalampi Nickel-cobalt-copper Mine
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. announced it acquired additional nickel-copper claims (Glatz and Night Danger) in Ontario. Historical sampling and drilling report nickel and copper grades, including intervals with elevated Ni and Cu. The company positions this as complementing its Kenbridge nickel project development plans.

title: Eurobattery Minerals Signs Investment Agreement With Option to Acquire the Hautalampi Nickel-cobalt-copper Mine
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. acquired 100% interest in additional nickel-copper claims near its Kenbridge project, describing historical assay results for nickel and associated copper. The release frames the acquisition as supportive of developing an operating mine, but provides no immediate production or supply disruption.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 11): Shanghai base metals closed mixed, aluminium and tin gained more than 1%
summary: SMM reports SHFE base metals closed mixed but copper and aluminium finished higher (copper +0.39%, aluminium +1.05%), supported by reopening-driven demand prospects and supportive technical/inventory signals. Nickel edged down slightly (-0.15%) yet remains supported by bullish indicators and a stainless-steel futures rally, limiting downside.

title: Freeport-McMoRan Needs Copper to Rally to Send the Stock Higher
summary: The piece argues Freeport-McMoRan needs copper strength to lift its stock. It cites Chile’s copper output resilience, China’s economy reopening, and recent copper futures gains driven by speculative short covering on the CME/LME. It notes that absent longer-term “buy-in,” copper upside may be limited.

title: Chile mining trade group sees copper supply glut of 200,000 tonnes in 2020
summary: A Chile mining trade group reportedly sees a copper supply glut of 200,000 tonnes in 2020. The expectation of an oversupplied market implies looser copper balances, which can weigh on copper prices as traders adjust forecasts for near-term availability and inventory buildup risk.

title: Guizhou to build 500,000 mt/year high-end special aluminium project
summary: Guizhou Zhengzhongyuan Mining plans to invest 600 million yuan to build a high-end special aluminium finishing project in Weng’an County. The project targets 500,000 mt/year capacity, with full operations expected to generate about 1.2 billion yuan in annual output value. The article does not specify near-term commissioning.

title: SMM Morning Comments (May 12): Base metals mixed after the release of China's inflation data; nickel jumped more than 1%
summary: SMM reports mixed SHFE/LME base metals after China’s April inflation data missed expectations: CPI rose 3.3% and PPI fell 3.1% y/y. Nickel jumped over 1% on SHFE and LME, copper fell on SHFE, and aluminium gained modestly, keeping overall price impact mixed.

title: Ex-Ravensthorpe nickel mine contractor fined for endangering workers lives
summary: The West Australian reports that an ex-contractor at the Ravensthorpe nickel mine was fined for endangering workers’ lives. The case highlights safety and compliance issues at the site, which can increase the likelihood of operational disruptions or added oversight, potentially weighing on near-term nickel production expectations.

title: Zambia shuts Tanzania border to fight COVID-19, delaying copper exports - SABC News - Breaking news, special reports, world, business, sport coverage of all South African current events. Africa's news leader.
summary: Zambia shut its border with Tanzania to curb COVID-19 spread in Nakonde, delaying copper exports that mainly transit through Dar es Salaam. Authorities prioritize essential-goods trucks, but closure duration is unclear. Zambia’s rising COVID-19 cases add further logistics risk, likely pressuring short-term copper supply expectations.

title: Ravensthorpe nickel mine contractor fined over accident
summary: A contractor at First Quantum Minerals’ Ravensthorpe nickel mine in Western Australia was fined $11,000 after a telehandler tipped while lifting a 3+ tonne pipe assembly, exposing workers to serious risk. The court found inadequate training and supervision. FQM faces related charges, but no immediate output impact is stated.

title: Copper falls on risks of rising coronavirus infections
summary: Copper prices fell as markets worried that a second wave of COVID-19 after reopenings could further pressure the global economy. The IMF signaled potential additional growth forecast cuts. LME copper fell 0.8%; aluminium rose slightly but nickel declined 0.8%, with broad risk-off sentiment.

title: Nespresso and Amcor win award for aluminium coffee capsule
summary: Nespresso and Amcor received an EAFA award for an aluminium coffee capsule using ASI-certified aluminium. The piece highlights sustainability, chain-of-custody certification, and responsible sourcing across the aluminium value chain. It does not report any supply disruption, quota, tariff, or demand shift that would affect near-term aluminium prices.

title: Copper prices extend losses on virus resurgence fears
summary: Copper prices extended losses as traders feared a second wave of coronavirus infections would delay global economic recovery. Three-month LME copper fell 0.6% and ShFE copper slipped 0.5%. The piece cites risk-off market moves and also shows smaller simultaneous declines in aluminum and nickel.

title: Operating rates at Chinese copper sheet/plate, strip, foil producers fell to 68.3% in April
summary: SMM survey data shows Chinese producers of copper sheets, plates, strips and foils saw operating rates drop to 68.3% in April, with COVID lockdowns denting demand and new orders plunging. May operating rates are expected to fall further to 64.83%. Copper rod producers fared better on infrastructure demand.

title: Copper Ore Grading 8% Currently Being Mined and Stockpiled at the Kakula Mine, with Underground Development Approximately 4.4 Kilometres Ahead of Schedule
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reports that COVID-19 measures have kept development at the Kakula copper project in DRC progressing uninterrupted, with underground drives intersecting a high-grade (>8% Cu) ore zone and high-grade ore stockpiled. Construction of the processing plant is advancing toward initial copper concentrate production in 3Q 2021.

title: Group Ten Metals Inc.: Group Ten Discovers Four New Kilometer-Scale Palladium, Platinum, Gold, Nickel, and Copper Soil Anomalies in the Boulder and Wild West Target Areas, Stillwater West Project, USA
summary: Group Ten Metals reported 2019 soil geochemistry results from its Stillwater West PGE-Ni-Cu project in Montana, identifying four new kilometer-scale anomalies with elevated nickel and copper, alongside PGE and gold. The update is exploratory and does not indicate imminent production or material supply changes, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Copper prices dragged lower by virus resurgence fears
summary: Copper eased on fears of a second COVID-19 wave in China and South Korea, prompting fresh restrictions and expected lower demand for base metals. U.S. warnings about lockdown rollbacks reinforced demand concerns. The selloff spilled into other industrial metals, with aluminium and nickel also falling on the day.

title: Blackstone Continues to Deliver Broad Nickel Sulfide at King Cobra Discovery
summary: Blackstone Minerals announced further broad disseminated nickel sulfide mineralisation at the King Cobra discovery within its Ta Khoa Nickel-PGE project in Vietnam, including multiple long intercepts of ~0.8–1.1% Ni and some higher-grade shallow intervals. PGE assays are pending and a maiden resource is due in Q3 2020, supporting potential restart.

title: Copper edges higher on China's demand, prolonged weak growth woes linger
summary: LME and ShFE copper edged higher as traders pointed to steady demand from China and factory restarts, with arbitrage helping prices. However, the outlook remains clouded by the Fed’s warnings of prolonged weak growth and pandemic-driven demand destruction. The piece also references moves in aluminium and nickel.

title: Copper falls as prolonged weak growth threatens demand
summary: Copper prices fell on LME and ShFE as fears of prolonged weak U.S. growth—stemming from the Fed’s comments on the coronavirus fallout—raised concerns over metal demand. The piece also cites pandemic-driven demand destruction and reports concurrent moves in nickel and aluminium prices, pointing to broadly bearish near-term sentiment.

title: Hardman & Co Research: Phoenix Copper (PXC): Potential world-class copper-gold-silver mine
summary: Hardman & Co Research discusses Phoenix Copper’s consolidated Idaho assets, including a first-stage shallow oxide copper mine and extensive copper-gold-zinc mineralisation. The research frames the project as potentially world-class, with valuation based on silver cashflows funding copper development. This can modestly support bullish sentiment for copper supply expectations.

title: LME copper inventories jumped 55,650 mt, the most in nearly three months
summary: LME-tracked copper stocks jumped 55,650 mt (+24.51%) to 282,675 mt on May 14, the largest one-day increase in nearly three months. The rise is linked to hit consumption beyond China due to COVID-19 lockdown restrictions. After the data, three-month copper prices accelerated losses and touched a one-week low.

title: King Cobra bites again with 38m @ 1.12 per cent nickel for Blackstone
summary: Blackstone Minerals announced strong drilling results at its King Cobra nickel-PGM project in Vietnam, including ~38m at 1.12% nickel from near-surface and additional thick, higher-grade intervals. The deposit remains open and the company is progressing scoping and resource work, supporting incremental bullish sentiment for nickel.

title: Atalaya Mining profit falls sharply as higher costs, lower copper prices weigh | 14 May 2020
summary: Atalaya Mining’s profit falls sharply as higher costs and “lower copper prices” weigh on performance. The article signals weaker copper price conditions impacting producer revenues and earnings, which can reinforce bearish near-term sentiment for copper demand/pricing expectations over coming days.

title: Copper falters for fourth day on somber U.S. economic outlook
summary: Copper prices extended declines for a fourth session as the Fed warned of prolonged weak U.S. growth amid coronavirus fallout. Concerns about a possible second COVID wave in China and renewed U.S.-China frictions weighed on demand sentiment. LME copper inventories jumped 25% and market structure stayed in deep contango.

title: Demand for Aluminum Castings Stagnant amid COVID-19 Pandemic; Reduced Workforce and Logistical Challenges to Prevail Through 2020, Reveals Fact.MR - Press Release
summary: A Fact.MR press release says aluminum casting demand is stagnant amid the COVID-19 pandemic. It attributes the weakness to reduced workforces and ongoing logistical challenges, projecting such conditions through 2020. The article implies near-term soft demand for aluminium castings, weighing on aluminium consumption expectations.

title: FactMR: Demand for Aluminum Castings Stagnant amid COVID-19 Pandemic; Reduced Workforce and Logistical Challenges to Prevail Through 2020, Reveals Fact.MR
summary: Fact.MR says aluminum castings demand is stagnant amid COVID-19, with the automotive industry facing major shocks. Oversupply from China plus travel restrictions, reduced workforce, and logistics issues are highlighted as concerns. The study expects a recovery by end-2020, but Q2 2020 demand remains weak.

title: Zambia Copper Miner Fights $132 Million Electricity Bill
summary: Zambia’s Konkola Copper Mines (Vedanta’s unit) is contesting a $132 million electricity bill dispute after Copperbelt Energy threatened to restrict power. KCM says curbs would irreparably damage facilities, while the court issued an interim order to prevent supply curbing pending a May 26 hearing.

title: En+ Group Supports the Publication of the Methodology to Define Low Carbon Aluminium by the Carbon Trust
summary: Australia’s government announced a long-term production credit to help aluminium smelters qualify for support while transitioning to reliable renewable electricity, targeting lower-carbon output. Rio Tinto said the scheme will help sustain and grow smelting operations and investment. The policy is intended to strengthen supply competitiveness for global low-carbon aluminium demand.

title: COMUNICADO: En+ Group Supports the Publication of the Methodology to Define Low Carbon Aluminium by the Carbon Trust
summary: En+ Group supports a Carbon Trust report proposing universal standards for labeling “low-carbon” primary aluminium, including a 4.5 tCO2/t threshold and cradle-to-gate accounting. The focus is transparency for buyers and potential product differentiation, but the note does not indicate any immediate supply or demand shock for aluminium prices.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 14/05: LME lead price pushes above $1,600; nickel slides 1.4%
summary: The LIVE FUTURES REPORT highlights LME market moves, noting that nickel is sliding by about 1.4%. While lead is also mentioned, the only clearly quantified price move tied to a tracked industrial metal is for nickel, pointing to bearish near-term momentum.

title: NBS: China primary aluminium output increased 2.4% YoY in January-April
summary: China’s NBS data show primary aluminium production of 2.97 million mt in April and 11.83 million mt in Jan–Apr, up 2.4% year-on-year. Production of 10 nonferrous metals (including copper and nickel) also rose to 4.93 million mt in April, suggesting supply is increasing, a bearish signal for prices.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 430,000 wmt on week
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell again in the week to May 15, down 430,000 wmt to 8.24 million wmt, after a 179,000 wmt drop the prior week. In metal terms, stocks fell to 67,600 mt, indicating tighter near-term ore supply.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks dipped 500 mt this week on outflow of cathode
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories fell by about 500 mt to 16,900 mt, driven by a temporary import arbitrage window that pulled nickel cathode product into China’s domestic market. Cathode stocks dropped to 15,200 mt, and no forward refined nickel arrivals were seen, alongside weaker SHFE/LME pricing.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc Provides Update On Joy Copper-Gold District And Files Project Technical Report
summary: Amarc Resources filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Joy copper-gold porphyry district in British Columbia, detailing drill-ready targets at PINE and MEX and planned core testing. The release cites historical intercepts and expansion potential but provides no near-term production or supply-change information, limiting immediate copper-price effects.

title: Copper Holds Above US$5,000, Volatility to Remain
summary: Copper holds above $5,000/tonne as China and other consumers gradually reopen, supporting demand expectations and lifting prices. Improved risk appetite and higher Chinese activity are cited, while treatment charges have fallen, signaling tight mine supply. However, Fed warnings about prolonged weak growth add volatility and risk of weekly pullbacks.

title: Derailed Train - Delayed Schedules and Spillage of Copper Concentrate - Novinite.com
summary: Two train derailments in Bulgaria are described, including a freight train carrying 25 wagons of copper concentrate to Burgas that derailed and spilled concentrate after hitting rocks from a landslide. Repair work is ongoing and some wagons are still obstructing the rail line, potentially disrupting copper concentrate deliveries.

title: Derailed Train in Bulgaria, Stara Zagora - Delayed Schedules and Spillage of Copper Concentrate - Novinite.com
summary: Two train derailments occurred in Bulgaria, including a freight train carrying 25 wagons of copper concentrate to Burgas. Ten wagons derailed and copper concentrate spilled at the scene while repair teams respond. The incident follows landslide/track obstruction, creating short-term logistics disruption for copper concentrate shipments.

title: Copper rises on demand hopes as economies reopen
summary: Copper prices rose about 1% on the LME and slightly on the ShFE as countries began reopening after coronavirus lockdowns, boosting hopes of a demand recovery. The report also cites reduced copper output in China due to outbreak disruptions and easing border controls for cargo in Zambia, supporting sentiment.

title: SMM Morning Comments (May 18): Base metals rose following gains in oil prices; LME nickel rebounded 1.3%
summary: SMM says nonferrous metals rose on Monday morning as oil prices jumped and the US dollar index slipped. The LME complex reversed a red week, with nickel rebounding and copper and aluminium also higher. SHFE positioning was mixed, but copper and aluminium showed recovery signals despite recent weakness.

title: Copper rises as economies reopen, but demand seen slowing in May
summary: Copper prices rose 1.3% on the LME as global equities improved with economies reopening after COVID lockdowns. However, China’s copper demand is expected to slow slightly in May. The article also notes increases in LME aluminum and nickel, signaling broader industrial metal support.

title: Traders stockpiling lifted spot copper premiums while copper futures rallied
summary: Shanghai spot copper cathode premiums rose as traders increased inquiries and purchases. High-grade premiums climbed to 160–170 yuan/mt versus the SHFE June contract, while standard premiums reached around 150 yuan/mt. Hydro-copper premiums held near 110 yuan/mt. SHFE June futures advanced above 43,100 yuan/mt and ended near 43,170 yuan/mt (+0.4%).

title: Franklin Mining to Begin Exploration of Copper Mine in Chile
summary: Franklin Mining entered a joint venture with Inversiones Mineras Scorpius Chile to explore the Los Totems copper mine in Chile. The release highlights potential high-grade copper and oxide copper shipments to Enami facilities, but it is chiefly an exploration initiative without near-term production changes.

title: China shifts policy tack to plug its copper scrap gap: Andy Home
summary: China is short of copper scrap after prior pollution-driven import restrictions and COVID-19 disruptions to scrap collection and processing. Beijing has partially relented by reclassifying some high-grade scrap as a “resource” and suspending a punitive U.S. scrap tariff. The resulting scrap gap likely increases demand for refined copper.

title: Hot Chili raises $5m to progress porphyry copper-gold strategy
summary: Hot Chili raised $5m via a placement plus $3.9m from a rights issue to restart drilling at its Chile Cortadera porphyry copper-gold discovery. Funds also include a $2m extension fee to complete acquisition payments. The company aims for a maiden resource and further drilling at Cortadera and nearby San Antonio.

title: Production remains on hold at Nevada Copper's Pumpkin Hollow Mine
summary: Nevada Copper’s Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine remains on hold as virus restrictions persist. The company says the mill is on standby because copper prices fell sharply (to around $2.10–$2.33/lb) and COVID limits underground access. Development continues; production is hoped to restart late summer or early fall.

title: Malaysia the new copper scrap hub
summary: The report says China is running short of copper scrap as restrictions on imports of copper scrap labeled as “waste” have tightened. China planned to ban copper scrap imports by end of the year, similar to other “foreign garbage” bans. The resulting supply shortfall is supportive for copper prices.

title: Copperstone explores the conditions for carrying out a directed share issue
summary: Copperstone Resources AB announced a directed share issue of about SEK 20 million via accelerated bookbuilding, with proceeds earmarked for intensified core drilling and studies at its Viscaria, Kiruna copper project, and further exploration and geophysical work at Arvidsjaur. The release indicates planned investment, not immediate production changes.

title: Lindian Resources confirms 'stunning' alumina grades at Gaoual bauxite project
summary: Lindian Resources reports “stunning” alumina grades from drilling at extensions (Bouba North and Bouba South) of its Gaoual bauxite project in Guinea, with many samples averaging above 50% and up to 58.5% alumina. Follow-up digestion tests are planned as the company prepares a JORC resource update.

title: Copper gains on vaccine optimism; U.S.-China friction looms
summary: London copper rose to a two-month high on optimism over very early COVID-19 vaccine data, supporting expectations of a faster economic recovery. China stimulus hopes also added support. U.S.-China tensions and yuan/equities pullbacks capped gains, but LME and Shanghai aluminum and nickel also edged higher.

title: Copper pulls back from two-month high on economic worries
summary: Copper prices retreated from a two-month high as investors weighed grim economic indicators (rising UK joblessness, expectations of a deep German contraction). Vaccine optimism helped Monday’s rebound, but Tuesday’s data and broader risk-off sentiment offset it. LME copper was slightly down while China futures eased from highs.

title: Seabridge to Drill New Gold-Copper Porphyry Target at Iskut
summary: Seabridge Gold plans drilling at its Iskut project to test a suspected gold-copper porphyry beneath the Quartz Rise lithocap, drawing parallels to its KSM system. The release outlines geophysical targets and planned meters but does not report any new copper resource estimates or production changes, limiting near-term price effects.

title: Chinese Aluminum Giant Causing Worries About Market Invasion
summary: Korean aluminum producers have jointly opposed a large Chinese aluminum manufacturer, Henan Mingtai Aluminum, which signed an investment plan in 2018 to build an aluminum products plant in South Jeolla’s Gwangyang Bay area. The project, opposed by local industry, raises concerns about Chinese supply entering Korea and affecting prices.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 19/05: 26.5kt inflow caps gains in LME aluminium; nickel gains 1.6%
summary: The live futures report says 26.5kt inflows are capping gains in LME aluminium, implying reduced upside pressure. It also states nickel is up 1.6%, indicating positive near-term momentum. The piece therefore signals offsetting short-term price pressure across aluminium and nickel.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 19/05: 26.5kt inflow caps gains in LME aluminium; nickel gains 1.6%
summary: The live futures report notes that LME aluminium gains are limited by a 26.5kt inflow, implying near-term supply/flow pressure weighing on upside. Nickel, by contrast, rises 1.6%, signaling stronger demand/positioning support for nickel prices over the same short horizon.

title: Revelo Signs Binding Letter of Intent to Sell 8 Copper-Focused Projects in Chile
summary: Revelo Resources signed a binding LOI to sell eight copper-focused projects in northern Chile to WPV, via an RTO of a public shell entity that will raise at least CAD$4 million for exploration. The transaction includes cash payments and contingent project payments tied to feasibility studies and production milestones.

title: Canada Nickel Company Announces Discovery of Multiple Palladium-Platinum Zones, Extends PGM Zone by 1.5 km, and Second Nickel Discovery Doubles Total Nickel Mineralization Along Strike by 1.7 km to 3.4 km at Crawford Nickel-Cobalt-Palladium Project
summary: Canada Nickel Company reported multiple palladium-platinum zone discoveries and extended a PGM zone by 1.5 km, plus a second nickel discovery that doubles total nickel mineralization along strike to 3.4 km at its Crawford project. The updates are likely supportive for nickel sentiment, but not an immediate supply shift.

title: Lindian hits uber-grade alumina numbers in Africa
summary: Lindian Resources reported ultra-high-grade alumina results from drilling at its Gaoual conglomerate bauxite project in Guinea, with alumina grades up to 58.5%. The company says resources have grown without grade loss and plans further digestion tests for silica classification ahead of a mid-year JORC resource estimate.

title: RPT-COLUMN- China shifts policy tack to plug its copper scrap gap: Andy Home
summary: Reuters column says China is short of copper scrap as prior pollution-driven import restrictions and COVID-related disruptions reduce scrap collection and processing. China reclassified high-grade scrap as “resource” to avoid an import ban, but available volumes are still far below prior years, likely tightening copper supply feedstock.

title: Rio Tinto and Forum Energy Metals Announce Exploration Plans at Janice Lake Sedimentary Copper/Silver Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Rio Tinto Exploration Canada and Forum Energy Metals announced 2020/2021 exploration work at the Janice Lake sedimentary copper/silver project in Saskatchewan, including completion of a winter haul road, permits for a drill camp, and planned diamond/RAB drilling and surveys. The article is exploratory and does not report production or disruptions.

title: Sulphur squeeze spells trouble for Congo's copper and cobalt miners
summary: Coronavirus lockdowns and border closures disrupting transport have raised sulphur and granulated sulphur prices and, by extension, sulphuric-acid costs for DRC miners. With sulphuric acid used to extract copper and cobalt, delayed reagent shipments may force mines into more expensive, potentially constrained operations, weighing on copper supply expectations.

title: Smelter owner Alumina says securing jobs vital as economy reopens
summary: Alumina says job retention is vital as governments consider another round of taxpayer support to keep Alcoa’s Portland aluminium smelter running after subsidies expire next year. The company cites ongoing low aluminium prices and challenging trading conditions, but highlights the need for reliable, lower-cost power and continued operation.

title: Satellite data shows copper smelting revival as China activity rebounds
summary: Satellite-based monitoring shows global copper smelting activity recovered in April and strengthened further in May, driven by rebounding operations at China’s smelters as COVID-19 lockdowns are lifted. The increase suggests rising refined copper supply, which may weigh on copper prices in the near term.

title: Aluminium job cuts will not help economy restart, say smelter owners
summary: Portland aluminium smelter owners say Australia’s economy restart needs better energy policy and avoiding further job losses as Alumina Limited and Alcoa seek a government-backed lifeline for the loss-making plant. The negotiations highlight operational risk from high power costs, affecting near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Photo Exhibition: Latpaudang Copper Mine - a 'Resources Curse'
summary: A photo exhibition and rights groups highlight controversy around Myanmar’s Latpaudang/Letpadaung copper mine, alleging coercive land seizures, excessive police force against protesters, and possible environmental damage from mine waste entering the Irrawaddy system. A government investigation is ongoing, with a final report due end-March.

title: Copper extends gains as economic recovery hopes boost risk sentiment
summary: Copper prices extended gains as hopes for a rapid global economic recovery lifted risk sentiment, pushing London copper to a more than two-month high. ShFE copper also rose sharply. The article adds that China’s copper smelting recovered in April and strengthened in May so far, supporting demand expectations.

title: China's nickel ore imports dropped 70% YoY in April due to COVID-19
summary: China’s nickel ore and concentrate imports fell 70.2% YoY in April as COVID-19 led to suspensions of Philippine mining operations and shipments. Imports totaled 1.36 million mt. Supplies from the Philippines, the main source, dropped sharply, with lower ore grades. Exports are expected to normalize in June.

title: SMM Morning Comments (May 21): Base metals seesawed ahead of 'two sessions;' SHFE nickel jumped more than 3%
summary: SMM notes volatile but generally firmer base-metals trading ahead of China’s “two sessions,” with oil prices rising and a slightly stronger dollar. LME copper and aluminium gained about 1.7%-1.8% on Wednesday; SHFE copper and aluminium rose too. SHFE nickel jumped more than 2%-3% before easing.

title: WBMS: World copper market recorded a 188,000 mt surplus in January to March
summary: WBMS reported the global copper market ran a 188,000 mt surplus in Jan–Mar 2020, after a 2019 deficit. Stocks rose ~316,000 mt, driven by net deliveries into LME-approved warehouses. Mine and refined output increased, while demand also grew, but not enough to offset supply.

title: Aluminium billet inventories accelerated decline on week
summary: SMM data shows China’s 6063 aluminium billet inventories fell further in the week to May 21, dropping to 92,800 mt from May 14. Stocks declined in four of five major consumption areas, with Foshan down sharply, while arrivals stayed limited. The drawdown suggests tighter near-term supply conditions for aluminium.

title: WBMS: World primary aluminium surplus came in at 709,000 mt for Q1 2020
summary: WBMS reported a 709,000 mt global primary aluminium surplus in Q1 2020 versus a 761,000 mt surplus for all of 2019. Demand rose 3.5% y/y but production grew faster (5.8%), and reported stocks rebounded to 2.17 million mt by end-March, suggesting near-term price pressure.

title: China's bauxite imports hit record high in Q1
summary: China’s bauxite imports hit a record 28.41 million mt in Q1, driven by higher demand and lower sea freight costs, supporting alumina feed supply for aluminium. However, the appeal of imported bauxite is fading as domestic ore losses widen, caustic soda/coal prices fall, and ~2 million mt/year of imported-bauxite alumina capacity went offline.

title: Rockcliff Identifies Near Surface High-Grade Copper and Zinc Mineralization at the Freebeth Property Including 5.28% CuEq Across 2.30 Metres and 4.00% CuEq Across 4.70 Metres
summary: Rockcliff reported successful phase one drilling at its Freebeth property in Manitoba, identifying high-grade near-surface copper-rich mineralization along the Last Hurrah Zone, with grades up to 5.28% CuEq across 2.30 metres. It remains exploration, with no production, smelting, or market-flow impacts described.

title: Chinalco exec proposes curbing China's copper capacity as lawmakers meet
summary: Chinalco’s general manager urged China to rein in “blind expansion” of copper smelting capacity during the Two Sessions, citing rapid output growth and low capacity utilisation amid oversupply. The proposal calls for faster supply-side reforms and revised standards, potentially tempering smelter growth in the near term.

title: Rusal expects all its aluminum to adhere to 'low carbon footprint' criteria by 2023
summary: Rusal said it expects all its aluminium to meet “low carbon footprint” criteria by 2023. The move is aimed at aligning output with buyer and policy preferences for lower-emissions aluminium. While it may support demand for compliant metal, the article does not signal immediate supply disruption or urgent price pressure.

title: Research Report with COVID-19 Forecasts-Aluminum Welding Wires Market 2020-2024 | Increasing Demand for Lightweight Vehicles to Boost Market Growth
summary: Technavio’s report forecasts growth in the aluminum welding wires market, attributing demand to stricter vehicle-emissions rules pushing lightweight, fuel-efficient vehicles and to investment in EV charging and power infrastructure. The press release expects COVID-19 effects to be most significant in Q1, with gradual easing.

title: FMI Revises Alumina Trihydrate Market Forecast, as COVID-19 Pandemic Continues to Expand Quickly
summary: FMI revised its forecast for the alumina trihydrate market, citing the continuing rapid expansion of the COVID-19 pandemic. Because alumina trihydrate is a key feedstock for aluminium refining, the update likely shifts near-term expectations for aluminium input availability and demand, weighing on prices.

title: Miner Hudbay Minerals expects delay to Peru copper expansion
summary: Hudbay Minerals said COVID-19 restrictions have delayed up to four months the start of mining an extension at its Constancia copper mine in Peru. The Pampacancha satellite deposit was expected to begin in late 2020, but slowed indigenous consultation has pushed mining to early 2021, with $70 million planned this year.

title: Initial bond for Meagher County copper mine set at $4.6M
summary: Montana will require copper miners in Meagher County to post a $4.6 million bond to begin construction for the Meagher County copper mine, the first of multiple bonds needed to proceed with mining near White Sulphur Springs. The new bond requirement increases upfront costs and may delay supply plans.

title: SMM Morning Comments (May 22): Base metals broadly lower with US-China tensions, 'two sessions' in focus; SHFE nickel hit 'limit down' overnight
summary: SMM reports broad declines in base metals amid US-China tensions, China’s “two sessions” and weaker economic data. SHFE nickel hit limit down, while SHFE copper slipped and SHFE aluminium rose slightly. LME copper fell and LME aluminium gained modestly. Moves largely reflect macro sentiment and positioning, not fresh fundamentals.

title: Tough Times Ahead for Nickel Producers as EV Demand Grows
summary: The article argues nickel producers face tougher conditions as EV demand grows but near-term nickel supply is disrupted. COVID-19 delays Indonesia operations and worker access, while expectations of dwindling Chinese nickel ore stocks may pressure NPI producers. It also highlights that EV batteries increasingly need Class 1 nickel for nickel sulfate.

title: Copper falls as China skips GDP goal, U.S.-Sino tension ramps up
summary: Copper prices fell 1.9% on the LME and 2.1% on the Shanghai Futures Exchange after China omitted an annual GDP target and U.S.-Sino tensions rose. Nickel dropped more than 4–5% and aluminium slipped slightly, reflecting risk-off sentiment, though contracts were still positioned for a weekly gain.

title: NZ's copper and fibre networks held up despite increased demand during lockdown
summary: New Zealand’s Commerce Commission reported that copper and fibre broadband connections maintained download speeds during COVID lockdown despite record demand. Fixed wireless saw a drop, while Fibre Max slightly declined but overall measured speeds increased versus the prior report. The report focuses on network performance, not copper market fundamentals.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell 25,000 mt on week
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell by 25,000 mt to 210,000 mt in the week ended May 22, the ninth straight week of decline. Traders moved bonded cargoes into the domestic market as import arbitrage remained open for a month. Consumption slowed and the arbitrage closed, but declines are expected to persist two weeks.

title: Chinalco's general manager: Blind copper smelting capacity expansion should be strictly curbed
summary: Chinalco’s general manager said China should curb “blind” copper smelting capacity expansion, warning that overcapacity is worsening. He cited low copper capacity utilization (about 77% in 2019), growing refined capacity (to 14.22m mt/year) and declining copper concentrate self-sufficiency. Sulphuric acid overcapacity is also mentioned.

title: Copper drops on fears of renewed U.S.-China tensions
summary: Copper prices slid about 2% as investors feared renewed U.S.-China tensions, possible sanctions, and renewed protests weighing on global growth sentiment. China’s lack of an annual growth target and demand concerns pressured copper. Aluminium and nickel also fell, with LME and SHFE declines reflecting broader selling and inventory signals.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks dipped 1,500 mt this week on outflow of cathode
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories fell 1,500 mt to 15,400 mt by May 22 as nickel cathode flowed out to the domestic market. A temporary import window and smaller import losses reduced replenishment, and Russian nickel arrived directly into China rather than entering bonded warehouses. Bonded stocks declined 2,000 mt month-to-date.

title: Canada Nickel Company Inc. Closes Property Transactions with Noble Mineral Exploration Inc.
summary: Canada Nickel announced it has closed property transactions with Noble Mineral Exploration, issuing 500,000 shares under a four-month hold. Both companies obtained the required disinterested shareholder approvals. The update is related to advancing nickel-cobalt projects tied to EV and stainless-steel demand, but offers no immediate supply impact.

title: 2020 was supposed to be copper's year to shine. Now everything is uncertain
summary: The article argues copper’s 2020 outlook deteriorated as COVID-19 shut mines, delayed Hudbay’s Constancia expansion, and clouded supply and demand. It cites copper price projections being revised lower and notes closures that impair output and financing. Possible fiscal stimulus in China and elsewhere may help, but near-term volatility persists.

title: Two fires at New Caledonia nickel mine site
summary: Two suspected arson attacks hit SLN nickel operations at Kouaoua, with the ore conveyor belt ablaze in two places. SLN’s firefighting and an investigation follow. The Kouaoua site supplies over a third of SLN’s ore and has faced prior disruptions, raising concerns about output and nickel viability.

title: FMG ups stake in Peru-focused copper play
summary: FMG increased its stake in a Peru-focused copper play. The move links the company more directly to future copper supply prospects and may support sentiment around the project’s development. While it could be mildly bullish for copper, the lack of operational or near-term output detail limits immediate price pressure.

title: Strong domestic demand supported operating rates at key aluminium processors, impact from weaker exports emerged
summary: SMM finds operating rates at 41 aluminium processors rose 1.3pp to 78.8% week-on-week, driven by strong domestic construction and medical demand and seasonal packaging/AC foil demand. Export orders weakened for plates/sheets, lowering those producers’ rates, but overall current orders keep utilization near highs into the week.

title: New Caledonia's Vale nickel plant eyed by Australian companies
summary: Australian bidders are reportedly contesting Vale’s nickel plant in New Caledonia. Vale said it would close a deal by end-June and has faced losses, while restructuring includes closing the refinery, prioritizing nickel hydroxide cake for EV batteries, and exporting 2 million tonnes of nickel ore annually. Jobs are expected to be cut.

title: New Century in talks with Brazil's Vale over nickel-cobalt mine sale
summary: New Century Resources is in exclusive talks with Vale to buy Vale’s troubled Goro nickel-cobalt mine in New Caledonia. The proposed deal could include Vale funding and possible French government support, addressing delays and costs. Continued operation supports nickel supply expectations tied to EV battery demand.

title: Australian miner set to acquire New Caledonia's Vale nickel plant
summary: Vale, in New Caledonia, has struck a tentative deal to sell its nickel assets to Australia’s New Century Resources, with financing due within two months. The plan includes restructuring, refinery closure, prioritising nickel hydroxide cake for EV batteries, and exporting two million tonnes of nickel ore annually.

title: Australian miner set to acquire New Caledonia's Vale nickel plant | Companies
summary: New Century Resources agreed to buy Vale’s stake/assets in New Caledonia’s Goro nickel plant after Vale put the 95% holding up for sale due to large losses. The plan includes restructuring, closing the refinery with job losses, prioritizing nickel hydroxide cake, and exporting up to two million tonnes of nickel ore annually.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 26/05: LME copper price up 1.5%; 25k inflow of aluminium at Port Klang
summary: LIVE FUTURES REPORT shows LME copper price up 1.5%, pointing to immediate bullish momentum. It also reports a 25k inflow of aluminium at Port Klang, which implies increased nearby aluminium supply/inventory and may limit upside for aluminium. Other items are mainly data/methodology updates.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 26/05: LME copper price up 1.5%; 25k inflow of aluminium at Port Klang
summary: A live LME futures update shows copper up 1.5%, pointing to near-term strength in copper prices. It also reports a 25k aluminium inflow at Port Klang, which generally increases available metal at the port and may weigh on aluminium pricing. Net impact is mixed across metals.

title: Quaterra Files Technical Report on Groundhog Copper-Gold Prospect, Alaska
summary: Quaterra Resources filed an independent NI 43-101 technical report for its Groundhog copper-gold prospect in Alaska, describing favorable geology and recommending additional geophysical processing and possible future IP and drilling. The update supports exploration planning but does not indicate any immediate production or supply changes affecting copper markets.

title: Trigon Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire the High Potential 'Silver Hill' Copper-Silver Exploration Project in Morocco TSX Venture Exchange:TM
summary: Trigon Metals agreed to acquire 100% of the Silver Hill copper-silver exploration project in Morocco, with exploration planned to begin after Morocco’s June 10 lockdown lift. The release describes transaction payments and conditions tied to a future resource estimate, but does not involve near-term copper production impacts.

title: Camino Minerals Corp. to Proceed with Resource Delineation Studies at its Los Chapitos Copper Discovery in Peru
summary: Camino Minerals will conduct resource delineation studies at its Los Chapitos copper discovery in Peru, using existing drilling results (58 of 61 holes with copper mineralization) and new 2019 channel samples to build grade/tonnage models. The work targets a potential manto deposit and supports future resource reporting.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 26): Shanghai base metals ended mostly higher Tuesday, copper recovered 1%
summary: SMM reported SHFE nonferrous prices were mostly higher on May 26. Copper recovered 0.94% and aluminium gained 0.9%, with copper bouncing above the five-day moving average and briefly testing session highs. Nickel edged slightly down (-0.01%). Gains were capped as US-China tensions kept investors cautious.

title: Three men charged in theft of copper from oil and gas sites
summary: RCMP charged three men for stealing 365 kg of copper wire from oil and gas worksites in southern Alberta. The copper was recovered at a Calgary residence and allegedly sold to a metal recycler. Police say continued buying of stolen copper sustains the theft market; the seized copper was valued at about CAD 2,500.

title: Copper range-bound as U.S.-China tensions dampen risk appetite
summary: Copper trades in a tight range as hopes for reopening are offset by renewed fears that U.S.-China friction could weaken global activity. Reports of possible U.S. action over Hong Kong heighten uncertainty. LME aluminium edges up, while nickel falls, indicating broadly mixed risk sentiment.

title: Impact of Covid-19 Outbreak on Aluminum Extruded Products Market Share
summary: The article states that the Covid-19 outbreak has affected the aluminium extruded products market, shifting market share. This implies reduced consumption and demand disruption for aluminium extrusions in the short term, which can pressure aluminium prices downward during the initial outbreak period.

title: Pacific Empire Minerals Acquires Rights to Large Copper Project
summary: Pacific Empire Minerals said it signed an option agreement to acquire a 100% interest in the Jean Marie copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry project in British Columbia. The release cites historical drilling intervals and copper geochemistry, but the news is an exploration acquisition with no immediate production impact.

title: Coronavirus to exacerbate copper surplus this year and next -IWCC
summary: The International Wrought Copper Council (IWCC) expects the global copper market to run a 285,000-tonne surplus in 2020 and a larger 675,000-tonne overhang in 2021. The forecast attributes the surplus to coronavirus-related demand destruction, projecting refined output above demand and weakness across regions.

title: Antamina copper, zinc mine resumes ops after Covid-19 suspension
summary: Antamina’s copper (and zinc) mine has resumed operations following a Covid-19 suspension. The restart should reduce the risk of continued supply curtailments and support near-term expectations for copper availability, likely helping copper prices by easing disruption-driven tightness over the coming days.

title: APAA Calls on Ambassador Lighthizer to Restore Tariffs on Surging Canadian Aluminum Imports
summary: APAA urges the Trump administration to restore Section 232 tariffs by repealing Canada’s exemption, citing a surge of Canadian aluminum imports hurting U.S. primary smelters. The group warns of potential shutdowns and requests reimposing a 10% tariff to reduce import pressure and protect domestic aluminum production.

title: Taseko inks deal on Yellowhead copper project in Canada
summary: Taseko signed an agreement with an Indigenous nation to support regulatory approval of its Yellowhead open-pit copper project in Canada. The large project (about 90,000 tpd) could become one of North America’s biggest. The step advances discussions and improves odds of future copper supply.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Extension of Main Zone by 1.5 kilometres and East Zone by 400 metres at Crawford Nickel-Cobalt-Palladium Project
summary: Canada Nickel said it is extending the Main Zone by 1.5 km and the East Zone by 400 m at its Crawford nickel-cobalt-palladium project. The update is directly tied to nickel resource definition, but the news lacks details on near-term production or supply changes, limiting expected price impact.

title: PRICING NOTICE: Correction to base metals arbitrage for nickel SHFE versus LME
summary: Fastmarkets issued a pricing notice saying it corrected and updated several base metal assessment entries due to procedural errors, including European low-carbon aluminium differentials and aluminium 6063 extrusion billet premium midpoint assessments. It also references nickel arbitrage methodology versus SHFE and LME, but no market-moving fundamentals were provided.

title: IWCC: COVID-19 to Increase Copper Oversupply in 2020
summary: IWCC expects COVID-19 to drive a copper surplus of 285,000 tonnes in 2020, rising to 675,000 tonnes in 2021. It forecasts refined demand falling about 5.4% in 2020 as construction and other uses weaken. Market fears of a slower recovery keep copper prices under pressure.

title: Amid the COVID-19 crisis and the looming economic recession, the Aluminum Castings market worldwide will grow by a projected US$32.1 Million, during the analysis period
summary: Reportlinker’s article forecasts growth in the global aluminum castings market amid COVID-19 and recession concerns, citing projected expansion in die casting and regional demand outlooks. It highlights drivers like lightweighting and automotive/electrical applications but provides no aluminum supply disruptions, inventory data, or pricing catalysts for the metal itself.

title: New Caledonia nickel ore sale plan labelled a disgrace
summary: New Caledonia faces a proposed law change that would let SLN and Vale export two million tonnes of nickel ore for local processing. Critics argue the plan undervalues ore and accompanies refinery closure. Prior approvals for large exports suggest increased nickel ore availability, weighing on near-term nickel prices.

title: New Caledonia nickel sale plan labelled a disgrace
summary: New Caledonia’s Palika party criticized a proposed law change that would let SLN and Vale export two million tonnes of nickel ore earmarked for local plants. They argue it sells ore at a fraction of value and cite refinery closures and past financing issues. Goro is suggested as an alternative processor.

title: Pan Global Extends Copper Mineralization with Step Out Drill Holes at the Escacena Project, Spain
summary: Pan Global Resources announced additional drill results at Spain’s Escacena project, extending a shallow copper mineralized zone and confirming multiple copper horizons associated with EM conductors. Intersections include notable copper grades, but it is an exploration campaign with no production timing, offering limited short-term impact on metal prices.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 28): Shanghai base metals ended mixed, aluminium rose to two-month high
summary: SMM says SHFE base metals ended mixed amid reopening optimism and US-China friction. Copper fell 0.34% after Peru’s Antamina resumed operations, raising oversupply worries, though China inventories supported prices. Aluminium rose 1.47% for a fifth day as Chinese primary ingot and billet inventories fell. Nickel added 0.13%.

title: Teck Resources resume operations at Antamina copper mine
summary: Teck Resources says Antamina mine operations in Peru have resumed with Covid-19 protocols and a reduced workforce targeting about 80% of full capacity, with gradual ramp-up to peak output in Q3. The restart follows a prior temporary suspension tied to Peru’s pandemic measures.

title: Copper Glut Continues To Grow | SafeHaven.com
summary: IWCC reports a widening copper surplus likely to grow as COVID-19 disrupts supply and demand. It forecasts supply exceeding demand by 285,000 tonnes this year and 675,000 tonnes next year, with demand down 5.4% in 2020. Copper prices have already hit multi-year lows, reinforcing bearish pressure.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 28/05:  LME copper price passes $5,300/t in 1.3% rise
summary: The report highlights a move in LME copper futures, noting copper passing $5,300/t in a 1.3% rise, signaling immediate upside momentum for copper prices. Other content focuses on Fastmarkets methodology/publication adjustments and general aluminium commentary, with no clear aluminium price move described.

title: Shanghai aluminum scales near 3-month high on China demand
summary: Shanghai aluminum futures rose to a near three-month high as demand recovered in top consumer China and aluminum stockpiles fell. ShFE’s most-traded contract hit 13,190 yuan/tonne. LME three-month aluminium also nudged higher, supported by inventory declines and demand-positive sentiment.

title: London aluminum set for strongest monthly gain in 16 months on China demand
summary: London aluminum prices rose and were set for the strongest monthly gain in 16 months, supported by a recovery in China demand. The move was also linked to a quick decline in ShFE aluminum inventories and improving sentiment. LME and ShFE aluminum contracts tested recent highs as trading increased.

title: China braces for aluminum import wave as coronavirus recovery upends trade
summary: China is preparing for record primary aluminum import volumes after post-coronavirus recovery creates a Shanghai–LME price spread. Traders say sizable inflows, including Russian metal, could enter in May-June. The extra supply may lift stocks and reduce the rally in Shanghai aluminum as the arbitrage narrows or closes.

title: Indonesia high-speed rail, nickel among US$ 97 billion priority projects
summary: Indonesia listed several priority projects for 2020–2024, including major nickel processing projects in Morowali, Konawe and Weda Bay. The government also plans rail and petrochemical upgrades, but the explicit inclusion of new nickel processing capacity is supportive for near-term expectations around nickel supply and sentiment.

title: China copper inventory shrank for 11 weeks
summary: SMM data show China’s copper cathode inventories in Shanghai, Guangdong and Jiangsu (including SHFE-approved warehouses) fell for an 11th straight week. Stocks dropped 32,500 mt week-on-week to 205,000 mt as of May 29, with declines mainly in Guangdong and Shanghai, suggesting tighter local availability.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 300,000 wmt on week
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell for the second consecutive week, dropping 300,000 wmt to 7.85 million wmt as of May 29. Stocks in seven major ports declined 230,000 wmt to 6.77 million wmt, suggesting tighter near-term supply for nickel production.

title: U.S. copper concentrate heads to China again after tariff relief
summary: The article headline says U.S. copper concentrate is heading back to China after tariff relief. Easing tariffs should restart cross-border shipments and improve availability for Chinese smelters/refiners, which can tighten near-term expectations for copper supply and support prices over the next few weeks.

title: Pandemic saps union clout as talks loom with Chile copper miners
summary: Chile’s copper unions face weaker bargaining power as COVID-19 hits miner profits and the global copper market. Contract talks may be delayed and miners seek to limit wage hikes, bonuses and benefits while companies push cost cuts. The piece follows falling copper prices to a four-year low in March, with only partial recovery.

title: Copper gets a warning the worst may be yet to come: Andy Home
summary: Commerzbank and the IWCC warn that COVID-19 optimism for copper may be premature. While China stimulus and imports support demand optics, IWCC forecasts demand falling more than supply (surplus of ~285k tonnes this year and ~675k next), with export weakness and trade risks limiting recovery.

title: Blackstone Commences Drilling On Regional Massive Sulfide Targets At Ta Khoa Nickel-PGE Project
summary: Blackstone Minerals has started drilling massive sulfide targets at its Ta Khoa Nickel-PGE project in northern Vietnam, expanding testing of district-scale prospects generated by in-house geophysics. Historic Ban Phuc results included high-grade nickel and associated copper, and drilling is expected to progress over coming months, supporting nickel supply expectations.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 29): Shanghai base metals mostly rose on Friday, copper rallied 1%
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals mostly rose on May 29. Copper gained 0.73% supported by decreasing domestic inventories; aluminium rose 0.84% amid tighter spot availability. Nickel edged down 0.13%. Broader support came from improved economic sentiment, though US-China tensions capped gains.

title: Doorknobs, handrails and shopping trolleys should be coated in copper to prevent spread of Covid-19
summary: The piece claims SARS‑CoV‑2 survives longer on steel and plastic but is killed on copper within hours, citing microbiologist William Keevil. It recommends copper coating for door handles, handrails, shopping trolleys and other shared surfaces. While supportive of copper adoption, it doesn’t quantify market-scale demand.

title: Dept of Commerce Wants Steel/Aluminum Industry Input on Section 232 Exclusion Process
summary: The US Department of Commerce opened a public comment period on the Section 232 exclusion process for US steel and aluminum tariffs and quotas, inviting industry input on factors, transparency, and potential revisions (e.g., blanket approvals/denials and tighter submission windows). Comments are due July 10.

title: Zambia's CEC to discontinue power supply to Konkola Copper Mines after talks fail
summary: Zambia’s Copperbelt Energy Corp will stop supplying power to Vedanta’s Konkola Copper Mines from Monday after talks failed to extend their agreement over $132m in debt. KCM will instead get electricity via Zesco, but power still flows through CEC lines at a fee. The risk is near-term supply disruption affecting copper production.

title: RPT-China braces for aluminium import wave as coronavirus recovery upends trade
summary: China is bracing for an aluminium import wave as coronavirus recovery disrupts and reshapes trade flows. The implied increase in inbound supply could ease near-term market tightness, weighing on aluminium prices over the coming days to weeks, unless offset by stronger concurrent demand signals.

title: RPT-U.S. copper concentrate heads to China again after tariff relief
summary: RPT-U.S. copper concentrate is reported to be heading back to China after tariff relief. The implication is improved cross-border trade conditions for U.S. concentrate exports, which may increase near-term availability and dampen copper market expectations over the next few trading sessions.

title: SKC to Spend 120 bln Won on New Copper Foil Plant
summary: SKC plans to spend 120 billion won on a new copper foil plant. The announcement points to incremental copper demand tied to producing copper foil, potentially supporting short-term copper sentiment as markets anticipate stronger usage needs from the new capacity.

title: 50,000km of new copper in national network
summary: NBN Co says it has purchased 49,620 km of copper wire for the National Broadband Network, including FTTC connections and replacing deteriorating copper lines. Labor questions costs and transparency to the Senate. The reported copper procurement points to ongoing demand, which can be mildly supportive for copper prices.

title: China nickel manufacturing expanded for 3rd consecutive month in May
summary: SMM reports China’s downstream nickel manufacturing PMI expanded for a third straight month in May, and raw-material inventory/purchasing sub-index rose on active nickel feedstock buys by stainless steel mills. NPI demand improved as fundamentals tightened, while some weakness persisted in battery/electroplating orders, suggesting net supportive near-term nickel demand.

title: Bank of America ups copper forecast as red metal rises for second month
summary: Copper prices finished a second month of gains as hopes for China-led fiscal and monetary stimulus lifted sentiment. U.S.-China tensions capped gains, but Bank of America raised its 2020 copper forecast by 5.4% to $5,621/t, citing a China activity rebound and easing lockdowns that could revive purchases.

title: The Global Aluminum Market is expected to grow by 1748.06 th tons during 2020-2024 progressing at a CAGR of 3% during the forecast period
summary: ReportLinker released a report forecasting growth in the global aluminum market for packaging from 2020-2024, citing rising demand for sustainable packaging and aluminum containers for liquid products. The piece is forward-looking and does not provide immediate supply, inventory, or pricing changes that could strongly shift near-term aluminum prices.

title: Zambia's CEC to discontinue power supply to Konkola Copper Mines after talks fail - SABC News - Breaking news, special reports, world, business, sport coverage of all South African current events. Africa's news leader.
summary: Zambia’s Copperbelt Energy Corp will discontinue power to Vedanta’s Konkola Copper Mines after failed talks over $132 million in unpaid debt. After Monday, KCM must source power directly from Zesco, though it still uses CEC lines. The disruption risk threatens near-term copper output.

title: Sicomines to use Outotec's copper solvent extraction technology
summary: Outotec secured a roughly €20m contract from Sicomines to deliver copper solvent extraction technology for a modular VSF®X plant near Kolwezi in the DRC. The scope includes engineering, equipment deliveries, installation, commissioning and start-up, supporting copper production progress.

title: Copper touches 11-week high on China recovery
summary: Copper rose to an 11-week high as signs of China’s economic recovery strengthened, including higher May vehicle sales and no new COVID cases in Wuhan. Analysts cited strong physical demand and tight scrap supplies prompting short covering. Per reports, LME aluminum and nickel also edged higher.

title: Material Matters: Met Coal, Iron Ore And Nickel
summary: The piece cites Morgan Stanley views that copper prices should remain resilient despite China-linked downside risk, forecasting strengthening later in 2020. For nickel, it highlights Indonesia’s ore export ban and pandemic mine closures tightening supply, but also weak end-demand, leading to a more mixed outlook.

title: Clive Palmer's Queensland Nickel traded while insolvent
summary: Court finds Queensland Nickel traded insolvently in the days before administrators were called in, and voided certain intra-group transactions involving China First and Waratah Coal. The ruling is about recovering funds from directors/liquidators after the 2016 refinery collapse, not current nickel production.

title: Chilean Govt to mine Hot Chili's copper-gold discovery
summary: Chile’s government agency ENAMI has agreed to help mine and process Hot Chili’s copper-gold ore from the Productora project using its nearby Vallenar facility. The deal is expected to start mining after permitting and proceeds will fund Hot Chili’s Cortadera work, including drilling and a planned maiden resource.

title: Blackstone Minerals intersects massive sulphide nickel at Vietnam project
summary: Blackstone Minerals reported successful maiden drilling intersections of massive sulphide nickel at its Ban Chang prospect in Vietnam’s Ta Khoa nickel-PGE district, using EM plates to target mineralisation. The project also plans scoping work for downstream nickel sulphate and has prior copper and nickel grades, but no immediate market-moving supply effects are stated.

title: Jharkhand: Maoists torch 11 vehicles engaged in bauxite mining in Lohardaga
summary: Maoist rebels in Jharkhand torched 11 vehicles, including nine excavators and other equipment, used in bauxite mining at Pakhar mines in Lohardaga district. The attack targeted operations of two private companies. Police said an investigation is underway, potentially disrupting local bauxite output and supply to aluminium production.

title: Blackstone nails new massive nickel sulphide veins in Vietnam
summary: Blackstone Minerals says drilling at its Ban Chang prospect in Vietnam intersected new massive sulphide nickel veins near its EM targets, while a second rig tests additional EM targets at Ta Khoa. The firm is also progressing a scoping study and assessing a restart of the mothballed Ban Phuc concentrator.

title: Inflow of seaborne copper weighed on spot copper premiums
summary: Shanghai spot copper premiums fell quickly after increased seaborne copper arrivals. Sellers cut premiums to 100 yuan/mt for high-quality and 90 yuan/mt for standard-grade versus earlier 130–140 yuan/mt. Hydro-copper premiums also eased. With imports not yet fully consumed, premiums may face further downside in a buyers’ market.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 03/06: LME copper price consolidates above $5,500/t; zinc slips below $2,000/t
summary: The live futures report highlights that LME copper is consolidating above $5,500/t, suggesting near-term price support. It also discusses aluminium market conditions—such as supply remaining broadly intact and earlier shipping disruptions—though the excerpt does not provide a direct aluminium price direction. Zinc is mentioned but not tracked here.

title: Kazakhstan Takes Another Economic Hit As Coronavirus Infects Oil Fields, Copper Mines
summary: Kazakhstan faces COVID-19 outbreaks at Tenghiz and mining sites including Kazakhmys. Kazakhmys reported a first case at its mining site and temporarily halted work at Nurkazgan mine except for limited repair and maintenance. Authorities warned production may be ordered to stop if infection rates grow further, threatening copper output and supply.

title: COVID-19 : Lanka Aluminium expects 40% market drop - Adaderana Biz English
summary: Lanka Aluminium Industries said Sri Lanka’s aluminium extrusion market could shrink about 40% due to COVID-19’s hit to the property and construction sector. Curfews forced the company to close its factory and sales reportedly stopped in April and May, with demand only starting to return partially by May.

title: Blackstone Intersects Massive Sulfide Nickel At Ban Chang
summary: Blackstone Minerals says it intersected massive nickel sulfide in two maiden drill holes at Vietnam’s Ban Chang prospect within the Ta Khoa Nickel-PGE project, with drilling continuing using EM plates. The company targets nickel-rich massive sulfide orebodies and downstream nickel sulfate production, but results are early and not immediate supply material.

title: Airbus contracts Constellium for aluminium products and solutions
summary: Constellium says Airbus has awarded a multi-year, multi-program contract worth a disclosed value to supply advanced aerospace aluminium rolled and extruded components, including wing and fuselage panels and aluminium-lithium solutions. Production is slated from plants in France and the US, reinforcing steady aluminium demand outlook.

title: Kakula Copper Mine Underground Development Now 4.7 Kilometres Ahead of Schedule; More than 15.4 Kilometres Now Complete
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says underground development at the Kakula Copper Mine is 4.7 km ahead of plan with higher-grade ore primarily grading ~8% copper. Equipment for the 3.8 Mtpa processing plant, including ball mills, is being shipped to site and commissioning milestones are scheduled for 2020-2021.

title: 15th China International Copper Industry Chain Conference 2020- Live broadcast for overseas delegates!
summary: SMM announces a July 16–17, 2020 Shanghai conference on China’s copper industry chain, focusing on copper smelting overcapacity, imported ore reliance, environmental constraints, and issues such as sulphuric acid supply for smelters and whether copper could rebound after COVID-19 lows. title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 04/06: LME copper price sinks 0.8% despite 20kt fresh cancelation; lead falls below $1,700/t
summary: The live futures update reports that LME copper prices are down 0.8% despite 20kt of fresh cancellations. It also notes moves in other metals (e.g., lead lower), and includes Fastmarkets methodology and assessment publication corrections, but the key price signal is copper’s decline.

title: Zijin's 200,000-tpy Serbian copper refinery to commence in 2022
summary: The article headline says Zijin plans to start a 200,000-tpy copper refinery in Serbia in 2022. title: Aluminum Billet Manufacturer Element 13 Eyes Manufacturing Plant in Richmond, Indiana
summary: Element 13 plans to build a 60,000 sq ft aluminum billet facility in Richmond, Indiana, using recycled aluminum scrap as its feedstock. The project involves about $15.8 million investment and a state/local tax grant to offset costs. The new capacity could modestly influence near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Fuel spill in river in Norilsk can be removed in 14 days — Nornickel top manager
summary: Nornickel says a diesel spill on the Ambarnaya River in Norilsk can be contained and removed in about 14 days with favorable winds. title: China's $700 Billion Infrastructure Package Sends Copper Soaring
summary: Copper jumped to a 12-week high after China launched a $700 billion infrastructure stimulus. Copper wire/cable output rates rose, while bonded stocks fell.

title: Groups seek to stop copper mine near popular Montana river
summary: Groups are seeking to halt a copper mine located near a popular river in Montana. summary: London copper was set for a third straight weekly gain as economies reopen and China demand recovers, supported by government stimulus and businesses rebuilding output after lockdowns. summary: Uncertainty over Vale’s sale of its New Caledonia Goro nickel plant is causing roadblocks and demands for talks from subcontractors and SAS Goro Mines. summary: Conservation groups sued to cancel approval of the Black Butte underground copper mine near Montana’s Smith River, alleging inadequate assessment of pollution risks. summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for a second straight week, expanding 1,000 mt to 213,000 mt by June 5. summary: Norilsk Nickel said it will host a conference call for investors about a fuel leak at Heat and Power Plant-3 in Norilsk. title: SMM Evening Comments (Jun 5): Shanghai base metals ended mostly higher Friday, nickel rallied 1%
summary: SMM says Shanghai base metals mostly closed higher, with copper up 0.96% and nickel up 0.98%, while aluminium edged up 0.08%. summary: The Kremlin dismissed calls to oust Norilsk Nickel President Potanin after an Arctic fuel spill. Shares in Nornickel have fallen amid Putin’s criticism of the state response. summary: China’s exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium products fell again in May, down 28.56% YoY to 382,900 mt, after a smaller decline in April. title: China's imports of unwrought copper and copper products dipped 5.5% in May
summary: China’s May imports of unwrought copper and copper products fell 5.51% month-on-month to 436,000 mt, attributed to coronavirus-related weakness in global manufacturing. summary: London copper slipped from a three-month high as data showed China’s exports weakened in May, raising short-term demand concerns. summary: China’s nickel sulphate production fell 3.9% in May (9,400 mt Ni content), driven by weak demand, existing inventories, and a fierce price war that pushed battery-grade material prices toward or below costs. summary: Chile’s central bank reported a $1.403 billion trade surplus in May. Total exports fell 15.2% y/y, but copper exports were $2.567 billion, down 11.8% y/y, reflecting the coronavirus disruption. The decline in copper export receipts points to reduced copper supply/export flows.

summary: Zijin Mining will pay $547.7m for a 50.1% stake in a Tibet copper miner, gaining access to three copper deposits totaling 7.95m tons. summary: Ames Copper Group will invest over $50 million to build a new U.S. copper smelter plant in Shelby, North Carolina, focused on recycling and purifying copper materials. title: Chile's biggest copper mines' output rises despite coronavirus: Cochilco
summary: Chile’s copper output rose in April despite coronavirus shutdowns. title: Shanghai aluminum hits 4-1/2-month high on solid China demand
summary: Shanghai aluminium surged to a 4-1/2-month high as strong China demand lifted the July contract on the SHFE. London aluminium posted a sixth straight gain. summary: Sandfire Resources reportedly faces a further environmental obstacle at its Black Butte copper project in the US. summary: East China spot aluminium ingot prices moved into wide discounts versus SHFE futures as foreign cargoes arrived and eased tightness.
