title: Centaurus Metals hits shallow, thick nickel sulphide mineralisation at Brazil project
summary: Centaurus Metals reported “exceptional” shallow, thick nickel sulphide intercepts at Brazil’s Jaguar Central and Jaguar North deposits, with multiple long intervals around 1.2–1.35% Ni and higher-grade sections. A maiden JORC resource is due later this month, with ongoing drilling to extend mineralisation down dip.

title: Capstone Expands MNFWZ Vein 20 M&I Resource by 118% at Cozamin to 13.1 Million Tonnes at 2.35% Copper and 52 g/t Silver
summary: Capstone Mining expanded the Vein 20 Measured & Indicated resource at its Cozamin copper-silver mine in Mexico, lifting contained copper by 127% to about 949 million pounds. The upgrade to Indicated status and higher contained metal expectations support near-term copper supply sentiment.

title: Blackstone extends massive nickel sulphide veins in Vietnam
summary: Blackstone says it has extended massive nickel sulphide mineralisation at its Ban Chang prospect within the Ta Khoa nickel-PGE project in Vietnam, threading new drill holes and intersecting thick sulphide intervals, with assays expected soon. The company frames results as supporting future mineability and possible supplementary feed into operations.

title: China Aluminium Processing Summit 2020: Substitution of recycled aluminium for primary metal is constant in long term
summary: SMM reports that recycled aluminium substitution for primary metal is expected to remain steady long term, but China’s aluminium users temporarily shifted back toward primary due to scrap import/policy changes, COVID disruptions, and sharp falls in aluminium prices. Secondary plants increased primary use, while later reductions occurred as premiums narrowed.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rebounded 900 mt on week
summary: China’s aluminium billet inventories rebounded in the week ended June 11, rising 900 mt to 74,000 mt. The increase was driven by growth in arrivals and reduced warehouse shipments. Stocks rose in Wuxi, Changzhou and Nanchang, while Foshan and Huzhou declined slightly.

title: 'Health, then production': Unions ramp up pressure on Chile copper miner Codelco | News
summary: Chile’s copper unions at state-run Codelco and BHP’s Escondida warned health should come before output amid an alarming spike in coronavirus cases, after a Chuquicamata death. Workers threatened walk-outs unless measures improve. Output so far looks steadier, but supply disruption risk increases.

title: Silkroad Nickel Ltd - An Emerging Nickel Player in Indonesia
summary: The piece describes nickel’s role in stainless steel and EV batteries, highlights Indonesia’s growing dominance in nickel supply after the 2020 ore export ban, and profiles Silkroad Nickel’s mine and planned NPI/ferronickel smelting projects. It supports a supply-growth narrative but provides limited immediate catalysts for prices.

title: London copper flat; set for fourth weekly gain on hopes of stimulus boost
summary: London copper was flat at $5,764.50/t and was on track for a fourth straight weekly gain, driven by hopes that central-bank stimulus could lift demand despite a gloomy global outlook. It notes a lack of Fed purchases, some USD support, and shows aluminum and nickel falling in separate moves.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for 3rd week
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for a third straight week, increasing by 3,200 mt to 216,200 mt by June 12. The rise was linked to weaker import demand during a closed arbitrage window. Spot copper premiums eased as consumption weakened, partly from increased switching to scrap on wider scrap discounts versus cathode.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks little changed in muted trades
summary: SMM reports Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories at 14,800 mt, unchanged week-on-week. However, muted trading follows worsening import losses as SHFE nickel underperforms LME nickel, with the SHFE/LME ratio near 8.0 and spreads averaging 3,350 yuan/mt. Russian nickel plates are still arriving into domestic warehouses.

title: HOTTER ON METALS: Section 232 and the Canadian aluminium 'surge'
summary: Fastmarkets/Fastmarkets-Metal Bulletin content notes procedural corrections and schedule changes to aluminium and other metal assessments, but also comments that aluminium has been “hard to move.” It references curtailed Gulf output, drawn-down inventories, and severely disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, implying some supply constraints without clear immediate price direction.

title: Aluminum glut revives financial crisis-era storage trade
summary: Banks and investors are joining commodity traders to stockpile aluminum amid a large surplus. Storage arbitrage is profitable because spot aluminum trades below three-month forwards, after the pandemic hit auto and aerospace demand. Discounting and hedging can increase apparent supply, weighing near-term aluminum prices.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rebounded 210,000 wmt on week
summary: SMM data show Chinese nickel ore inventories rose after prior declines: total port stocks rebounded 210,000 wmt to 8.04 million wmt as of June 12, with stocks in seven major ports up 200,000 wmt to 6.93 million wmt. Metal-content stocks rose to 65,900 mt.

title: Knives out for nickel market as restaurants close: Andy Home
summary: Citi warns nickel faces unfavorable end-use demand as hospitality closures increase stainless steel scrap and weaken broader stainless end-use. With demand down more than supply, inventories/overhang could grow and the market may see a first surplus since 2015. Short-term stainless weakness is expected to weigh on nickel.

title: Copper Stages a Comeback Riding on Strong Demand in China
summary: Copper is reported to be rebounding, with the move attributed to strong demand from China. The article implies that improving Chinese offtake is tightening near-term expectations for copper supply/demand, which typically creates upward pressure on copper prices over the following days and weeks.

title: Andy Home, nickel market, batteries for electric vehicles, Sudbury
summary: Citi warns nickel demand is weakening as stainless-steel end markets, including hospitality, aerospace and oil & gas, face prolonged recovery. With refined nickel overhang already forming and a likely first surplus since 2015, the article argues the nickel narrative is shifting from supply disruption to demand downside, keeping prices under bearish pressure.

title: Chilean copper miners labour group alleges 'alarming' rise in coronavirus cases
summary: Chile’s miners’ unions, including Codelco workers, warn of an “alarming” rise in COVID-19 cases and say existing health and isolation measures are not preventing contagion. They call for updated operational continuity plans and transparency, following prior threats of site walkouts/quarantines, increasing near-term output disruption risk for copper.

title: Chilean copper miners labor group alleges 'alarming' rise in...
summary: Chile’s copper miners’ unions said coronavirus cases among workers are “alarming” and urged Codelco and other operators to re-evaluate continuity plans, arguing safety and isolation measures aren’t preventing contagion. The unions also cite discussions of self-imposed quarantine/walkoffs, increasing near-term production risk for copper.

title: Chilean copper miners labor group alleges 'alarming' rise in coronavirus cases
summary: Chile’s copper miners’ union alleges an alarming rise in COVID-19 cases among workers at major mines, arguing current isolation and health protocols are failing. It signals possible quarantines and calls for more transparency and re-evaluated continuity plans, raising short-term supply disruption risk for copper.

title: Vale renews bid for nickel ore exports from New Caledonia
summary: Vale is lobbying New Caledonia to change the mining code so low-grade nickel ore can be exported rather than processed locally, as Vale restructures and sells assets. Opposition from pro-independence politicians could limit export volumes, while refinery shutdown raises concern over local nickel supply. EV battery demand boosts sentiment.

title: Chilean copper miners labor group alleges 'alarming' rise in coronavirus cases | The Mighty 790 KFGO
summary: Chile’s copper miners’ unions said COVID-19 cases among workers are rising “alarming[ly]” and that current health protocols are not preventing contagion at major mines, especially Codelco. The unions called for revised continuity plans and transparency, warning some sites may face quarantine or walkoffs.

title: Spot copper discounts expanded on last trading day of the SHFE June contract
summary: Spot copper cathode discounts widened on Monday as sellers sought to destock amid ample supplies. The June–July SHFE spread expanded up to 450 yuan/mt after shorts exited the June contract, pressuring downstream buying decisions. Discounts deepened versus the June futures, and SMM expects premiums unlikely to stay elevated.

title: NBS: China primary aluminium output dipped 0.1% YoY in May
summary: China’s primary aluminium output in May was 2.98 million mt, up 0.4% from April but down 0.1% year on year, per NBS data. January–May production rose 2.1% but slower than earlier months. This suggests slightly tighter YoY aluminium supply.

title: Chilean copper miners warn of alarming increase in Covid-19 cases and threaten to walk off the job
summary: Chilean copper unions at state miner Codelco say rising COVID-19 cases show safety protocols are failing and warn of walk-offs or self-imposed quarantines at some sites. The dispute raises near-term production disruption risk for Chile, while copper prices have already been pressured by weaker Chinese demand from the pandemic.

title: China copper scrap imports to fall between end-July and early August
summary: China is expected to cut copper scrap imports between late July and early August as European and US supply declines amid COVID-19 disruption and civil unrest. Scrap shipments from Europe/US are down 15–20% in June y/y. Malaysia supplies cover about a month, but import quotas limit the extent.

title: Copper slides as coronavirus worries resurface
summary: Copper prices fell 1.9% as renewed coronavirus worries raised uncertainty about how quickly demand will recover. China’s manufacturing recovery looked fragile despite increased production. Chile miner unions also sought updated continuity plans amid rising worker cases. Aluminium and nickel also dropped on weaker sentiment and global demand concerns.

title: Refinitiv: COVID-19 Putting Pressure on Copper and Zinc
summary: Refinitiv says COVID-19 has pressured base metal markets, citing Peru’s pandemic containment measures and broader mine disruptions across Canada, Africa and Mexico. It reports sizeable mine-level losses for copper, forecasting a ~4% supply decline vs 2019 and about an 800,000-tonne year-on-year drop.

title: Barraba Copper Project Update
summary: Comet Resources provides an update on its Barraba Copper Project, including appointing a geologist as project manager and planning site visits and surface exploration once permits are in place. The company targets initial field exploration in Q3 and notes copper demand drivers from renewables and EVs, but no near-term production changes.

title: Copper Bulls Ride On Increased Orders, Mine Disruptions
summary: Copper is described as rallying on increased orders and reopening demand, supported by Beijing’s infrastructure stimulus. Supply is tightening as COVID-19 threatens mine output in Chile (including Codelco disruptions) and mined output falls, while LME and global inventories decline, reinforcing upward price pressure.

title: Southern ramps up Peru copper production despite pandemic
summary: The piece reports that Southern is ramping up copper production in Peru despite pandemic conditions. The implication is greater near-term copper supply than previously expected, which can weigh on copper prices as the market adjusts for reduced disruption risk and higher output levels.

title: Copper rises as Fed's stimulus boosts sentiment
summary: Copper rose 1.1% on the LME as investors welcomed the Fed’s widened bond-buying program, boosting risk-on sentiment. LME/Shanghai aluminium and nickel also increased alongside copper. However, China spot copper remained at a widening discount to futures, hinting weaker physical demand.

title: Glencore to combine copper and zinc operations in Queensland
summary: Glencore plans to merge its Queensland copper and zinc operations under a single management structure. Politicians fear potential job losses, though Glencore says consultation will follow and declines to confirm job cuts. The restructure could influence near-term copper production expectations, but no concrete output changes are stated.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Jun 16): Shanghai base metals recovered on Tuesday morning, aluminium added over 1%
summary: SMM says SHFE nonferrous prices mostly rose after overnight recovery and supportive macro sentiment from the Fed. LME copper gained on optimism around OPEC+ cuts and crude demand, while Chile extended a coronavirus catastrophe, raising copper-ore supply concerns. Aluminium and nickel also rebounded, with aluminium supported by positioning and fundamentals.

title: Copper jumps as more Fed support whets risk appetite
summary: Copper prices rose after the Federal Reserve widened its corporate bond buying, supporting U.S. risk sentiment and coinciding with a weaker dollar. The LME and Shanghai contracts both gained. In Chile, labor union concerns add a potential supply disruption tailwind, while aluminium also firmed on tariff-quota expectations.

title: China approves import quotas for another 1,570 T of copper scrap
summary: China approved new 2020 import quotas for 1,570 tonnes of high-grade copper scrap and 5,840 tonnes of aluminium scrap. The small eighth batch highlights tight oversight as China targets zero scrap imports by year-end but allows compliant scrap under new July 1 standards, influencing near-term supply expectations.

title: Copper blind-sided by the strength of Chinese recovery
summary: Copper has rebounded sharply as China’s recovery boosts industrial activity. LME and ShFE inventories are falling and prompt premiums reflect low exchange stocks. The key driver highlighted is a major copper scrap supply squeeze from lockdown-related collection disruptions and stricter Chinese import rules, supporting higher refined copper demand.

title: Copper blind-sided by the strength of Chinese recovery: Andy Home
summary: Copper prices have rebounded sharply as China’s recovery boosts demand and inventories tighten. SHFE and bonded warehouse stocks have fallen quickly after a COVID-era surge, while Chinese refined imports remain robust. Supply is also constrained by a collapse in copper scrap availability amid trade restrictions, displacing demand into refined copper.

title: USMCA Uniform Regulations Clarify Scope and Application of Steel and Aluminum Purchase Requirements for Passenger Vehicles, Light Trucks, and Heavy Trucks | White & Case LLP
summary: The USMCA interim Uniform Regulations clarify how vehicle producers must meet Article 6 originating steel and aluminum purchase requirements, including eligible products, calculation methods, and documentation timing. The rules take effect July 1, 2020 with a six-month grace period, potentially boosting expectations for USMCA-compliant aluminium demand.

title: Copper rises on COVID-19 treatment hopes, strong U.S. retail sales
summary: Copper prices rose after trial results for dexamethasone improved COVID-19 treatment expectations and sentiment, alongside a sharp rebound in U.S. retail sales indicating economic recovery. The report cites higher LME and Shanghai copper prices and also shows aluminium rising, implying broader risk-on support for industrial metals.

title: New Caledonia nickel ore export bids hit impasse
summary: New Caledonia’s government faces a stalemate over proposed changes to permit nickel ore exports to Asia. Two smelter-running companies want the sales to offset losses from low nickel prices, but pro-independence parties oppose the law change, fearing waste of local resources and loss of onshore processing.

title: Copper up on U.S. recovery hopes; China virus outbreak caps gains
summary: London copper rose modestly on hopes for U.S. demand recovery and potential infrastructure spending, plus a COVID-19 treatment breakthrough. Gains were capped by a growing China coronavirus outbreak, raising second-wave fears. Aluminum prices also edged higher, but overall sentiment is mixed between U.S. stimulus optimism and China demand disruption risk.

title: Operating rates at large aluminium processors remained stable, new orders declined_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates at major aluminium processors are largely stable (avg ~79.4%), but high aluminium prices are cooling downstream buying. Finished inventories are expected to rise, and new orders slow—especially exports—while billet processing fees decline and substitution of scrap for primary likely weakens further in June.

title: 3 per cent nickel result cements new discovery for Blackstone
summary: Blackstone Minerals’ maiden drilling at the Ban Chang West prospect in Vietnam returned a high-grade massive sulphide zone, including 0.66% nickel over 5m and an interval up to 2.98% nickel plus 1.22% copper. Management says results could add high-grade feed near its Ban Phuc facility, boosting nickel and copper sentiment.

title: Copper up on U.S. recovery hopes, but China virus outbreak caps gains
summary: London copper rose on U.S. retail sales recovery hopes and expectations of a large U.S. infrastructure package, supporting demand outlook. However, a rising COVID-19 outbreak in China raised fears of a second wave that could curb consumption. LME gained modestly while Shanghai futures ended flat.

title: Alcoa to Begin Formal Consultation Process With Spanish Works Council Regarding San Ciprián Aluminum Smelter
summary: Alcoa will begin a formal 30-day consultation with Spain’s works council on collective dismissals tied to significant recurring losses at its San Ciprián aluminum smelter. The restructuring could retain part of the casthouse, but smelter output may be reduced, pressuring short-term aluminum supply expectations.

title: Spot aluminium premiums exceeded 200 yuan amid tight availability_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s east-coast spot aluminium premiums rose for a second day, reaching about 200–220 yuan/mt over the July SHFE contract, near May’s peak. Availability remains tight, with sellers holding firm and some delaying shipments. Downstream buying is weaker, while social inventories have fallen sharply.

title: Alcoa To Begin Formal Process For Collective Dismissal Of Employees At San Ciprin Aluminum Facility
summary: Alcoa says it will start a formal consultation process for collective dismissals at its San Ciprián aluminum smelter in Spain on June 25, following earlier talks with worker representatives. The restructuring would keep part of the casthouse running, but the plant has recurring losses, suggesting possible supply tightening for aluminium.

title: Some U.S. aluminum producers are again pushing for tariffs on Canada as others warn of 'great Canadian distraction'
summary: U.S. aluminum producers are again lobbying for tariffs on Canadian aluminum as the new NAFTA nears implementation. Analysts say Chicago aluminum futures have risen as markets price likely quotas or restrictions. Supporters cite a Canadian export surge harming U.S. smelters, while opponents argue the impact is overstated and consumer costs rise.

title: Nevada Copper set to resume concentrate production in Q3 2020
summary: Nevada Copper says it is progressing to restart concentrate production at the Pumpkin Hollow underground copper project in Q3 2020. Output was paused in early April due to COVID-19 travel and workplace restrictions in Nevada. The company is completing shaft work and remobilizing staff, targeting processing operations in August.

title: Alcoa could cut up to 534 jobs in aluminum facility in Spain
summary: Alcoa plans to start a formal consultation process from June 25 that could result in cutting up to 534 jobs at its San Ciprian aluminum smelter in Spain. The move follows May talks citing significant and unsustainable circumstances and continuing recurring losses. The alumina refinery is not affected.

title: Covid 19 coronavirus: Copper prices higher after trial of drug
summary: Copper prices rose overnight as traders increased buying on improving risk appetite following promising Covid-19 treatment trial results and strong US economic data. The shift in sentiment supported near-term demand expectations and helped push copper higher in the financial markets.

title: Chile copper mine workers seek dialogue as coronavirus outbreak explodes
summary: Chile copper mine workers are seeking dialogue as a coronavirus outbreak intensifies. The situation raises the risk of production slowdowns or disruptions at the mine, tightening near-term copper supply expectations. That supply concern can be supportive for copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: London copper falls on worries over fresh virus cases in China
summary: London copper prices fell as rising COVID-19 cases in Beijing renewed lockdown fears that could hit demand. China also signaled monetary easing support, but risk sentiment turned cautious. The article notes concurrent easing in LME nickel and weakness in ShFE aluminium, indicating broad metal pressure.

title: Exclusive: EY finds China copper smelter Fangyuan has misstated accounts - sources
summary: Reuters reports EY found China’s largest privately held copper smelter Fangyuan overstated profit and production while understating debt, based on creditor briefings. The findings intensify worries about repayment capacity after treatment charge declines. Fangyuan denies fraud. Foreign lenders are also seeking audits, with a July 9 court hearing pending.

title: Operating rates across secondary aluminium makers edged higher in May_SMM
summary: An SMM survey says China’s secondary aluminium operating rates rose to 48.69% in May, supported by moderately improving auto sales linked to stimulus. Meanwhile, foreign aluminium alloy ingot imports did not significantly pressure producers in May, though increasing imports in June may slightly reduce operating rates among smaller firms.

title: Jubilee Metals secures rights to copper tailings resource in Zambia | 18 June 2020
summary: Jubilee Metals announced it secured rights to develop a copper tailings resource in Zambia. Tailings reprocessing can add incremental copper supply over time, influencing expectations for copper production and availability, which may provide modest upward support to copper prices in the near term.

title: Aluminium billet inventories shrank 2,500 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China’s aluminium billet inventories fell 2,500 mt in the week ended June 18 to 71,500 mt, after a 900 mt build the prior week. Shipments increased from warehouses but arrivals were limited across major consuming regions, with Foshan showing the largest drop.

title: PolarX set to drill exciting US copper-gold play
summary: PolarX secured ~$3.76m in investor funding for ~3,000m of drilling at its US Zackly East gold-copper target in Alaska. Prior hits included copper-bearing gold intersections (up to ~0.6% Cu) plus additional copper anomalous zones. The company also plans metallurgical tests at Zackly Main.

title: Copper Pipe and Tube Market Report: Trends, Forecast and Competitive Analysis
summary: The PRNewswire piece reviews the copper pipe and tube market, forecasting a COVID-19 decline in 2020 followed by recovery in 2021 and growth through 2025. It cites HVAC, refrigeration, construction, and electric/hybrid vehicle demand as drivers, with emphasis on product and regional trends.

title: Vale to restart nickel mine in Canada after COVID-19 pause
summary: Vale plans to restart its nickel mine in Canada after a COVID-19 related pause. The move is likely to lift near-term production/supply expectations and increase market availability, which usually weighs on nickel prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: Barrick says there's 'absolutely no truth' to release claiming it sold Lumwana copper mine
summary: Barrick Gold said a social-media “press release” claiming it sold the Lumwana copper mine for $895 million is false. Zambia’s National Pension Scheme Authority also denied involvement, and Metalinvest said it has no knowledge of any deal. Barrick previously explored options for Lumwana, but sale details remain unconfirmed.

title: Vale to Restart Nickel Mine in Canada After Covid-19 Pause
summary: The article headline says Vale plans to restart its nickel mine in Canada after a Covid-19-related pause. A restart typically increases expected near-term nickel output and supply availability, which can pressure nickel prices in the days to a few weeks following the news.

title: Trump considering reinstating tariffs on Canadian aluminum and steel imports
summary: The Trump administration is considering reimposing tariffs on Canadian aluminum and steel imports after talks with Ottawa, citing surges in shipments. U.S. producers are lobbying for action under a 2019 tariff-reinstatement clause tied to export spikes. The possibility triggers market anxiety in Canada amid election-year uncertainty.

title: NORNICKEL DISPOSES OF HONEYMOON WELL NICKEL PROJECT IN AUSTRALIA
summary: Nornickel said it has signed a definitive agreement to sell its Honeymoon Well Nickel Project in Western Australia to BHP’s Nickel West unit. The deal completes Nornickel’s exit from Australian operations and remains subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions. The project is a greenfield nickel development.

title: China copper inventory shrank for the 14th week with a 20,500 mt fall in Shanghai_SMM
summary: China’s copper inventories declined for the 14th consecutive week as of June 19, with total cathode stocks down 19,000 mt to 179,900 mt. Shanghai fell sharply by 20,500 mt to 141,500 mt, attributed to tight domestic smelter supply and slower seaborne arrivals, implying tighter short-term supply.

title: London copper flat as concerns over fresh virus wave check recovery hopes
summary: London copper was little changed amid mixed sentiment: worries about a potential second COVID-19 wave offset by hopes for economic recovery. China copper premiums and spot-futures spreads rose, pointing to near-term tightness. The report also notes aluminium easing, with prices moving modestly in both directions.

title: CRU: European Aluminium Rollers in the Eye of the Storm Caused by Another US Dumping Investigation
summary: CRU reports US AD/CVD petitions against common alloy aluminium sheet from 18 countries, with preliminary AD set for Aug 17 and preliminary CVD decisions due Aug 7. Imports from in-scope countries are already down sharply year-to-date, and an affirmative ruling could remove most 2019 import volumes, tightening supply for US buyers.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks rose 800 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories rose by 800 mt to 15,600 mt, driven entirely by nickel cathode. The build was linked to wider US-dollar import losses of refined nickel (up to 3,500 yuan/mt), encouraging cargo holders to reroute seaborne arrivals into bonded warehouses. The SHFE/LME nickel ratio held near 8.0.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 50,000 wmt on week_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports increased for a second straight week. Total stocks rose by 50,000 wmt to 8.09 million wmt as of Jun 19, following a prior-week build. Stocks in metal content also climbed, adding 200 mt to 65,800 mt.

title: Norilsk Nickel says to sell last Australian asset to BHP Billiton | Companies
summary: Norilsk Nickel said its Australian unit (MPI Nickel) agreed to sell its Honeymoon Well nickel project to BHP Billiton for an undisclosed price, marking its exit from Australian operations. The deal is subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, affecting expectations for nickel supply and asset ownership.

title: Exploding cases of Covid-19 in Chilean copper mines, claim workers' union
summary: Chilean copper mine workers’ union says COVID-19 cases among miners are surging and asks companies and the government to hold a three-way dialogue. It urges stronger enforcement of safety rules and transparent reporting of inspections, amid fears operational continuity could be strained in the top global copper-producing country.

title: BHP agrees to buy new Norilsk's nickel tenements in Western Australia
summary: BHP agreed to buy Norilsk Nickel’s Australian tenements via MPI Nickel, acquiring the Honeymoon Well nickel project in Western Australia, including the Wedgetail sulphide deposit and interests in exploration JVs. The deal takes Norilsk’s exit from Australia and expands BHP Nickel West’s resource base, supporting nickel sentiment.

title: COVID-19 Impact and Recovery Analysis- Global Aluminum Alloy Wheel Market 2020-2024 | Growing Demand for Lightweight Vehicles to Boost Market Growth
summary: Technavio forecasts growth in the global aluminum alloy wheel market, attributing demand to lightweight automotive designs that improve fuel economy and meet emission standards. It also highlights continued adoption in autonomous vehicles. Overall, the report points to higher aluminum alloy wheel production, supporting aluminum consumption expectations in the near term.

title: Exploding cases of Covid-19 in Chilean copper mines, claim workers' union - Chile News
summary: Unionized workers’ federation in Chile says COVID-19 cases are rapidly increasing among miners and asks for a three-way dialogue with companies and the government to prevent further infections. It calls for stricter safety enforcement and more transparent inspections. Chile’s output has so far held up, but disruption risk remains.

title: BHP to acquire new nickel tenements in Western Australia
summary: BHP agreed to acquire nickel tenements in Western Australia, including the Honeymoon Well project and interests in exploration joint ventures near its existing Nickel West assets. The deal covers high-grade nickel sulphide resources and is subject to approvals. It adds prospective resources but does not signal immediate production changes.

title: Trigon Metals acquires copper-silver project in Morocco
summary: Trigon Metals agreed to acquire Technomine Africa’s 100% interest in Morocco’s Silver Hill copper-silver project. The deal involves cash and share payments plus contingent payments based on contained copper-equivalent estimates. While it supports longer-term copper supply expectations, the article lacks near-term production impact details.

title: Rio Tinto adds 15 new apprentices at Weipa bauxite operation
summary: Rio Tinto says 15 new apprentices have started at its Weipa bauxite operation, bringing the total to 48. Training covers diesel fitting, electrical and boilermaking over three to four years. The piece emphasizes local employment and community support, without any near-term change to bauxite output.

title: BHP grows nickel footprint as Russians exit WA
summary: BHP increased its nickel footprint in Western Australia by buying a tenement package from Norilsk Nickel. The acquisition gives BHP control of the Honeymoon Well project and expands its position in other exploration tenements previously held via a 50% stake. No immediate production impact is stated.

title: Billionaire Birla's Hindalco Plans to Sell 65% Aluminum Overseas
summary: The news headline says Birla Group’s Hindalco plans to sell 65% of its aluminum output overseas. Such an export reallocation can increase near-term aluminum market flows and availability, typically exerting downward pressure on prices over the next days to weeks, depending on broader demand and competitiveness.

title: London copper falls as coronavirus surge sparks demand worries
summary: London copper fell as accelerating COVID-19 cases raised worries about a quicker recovery and near-term demand. LME three-month copper eased to $5,846/ton. China prices were supported by low inventories and potential Chile supply disruption, while LME aluminum slipped and LME nickel declined.

title: Primary aluminium inventories fell 17,000 mt over weekend_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots fell 17,000 mt from June 18 to 737,000 mt as of June 22, across eight consumption areas including SHFE warrants. The ongoing decline signals brisk downstream demand and tighter near-term supply conditions, supportive for aluminium prices.

title: Copper gains on supply woes, virus-led demand hit fears cap gains
summary: Copper rose on Monday as inventories drew on the LME and in China and supply disruption risks increased in Chile, including COVID-19-related labor health policy threats at Codelco. However, gains were limited by fears of weaker industrial demand as global coronavirus cases accelerated, capping upside despite a tightening market surplus.

title: OZ Minerals catches nickel fever, snaps up Cassini
summary: OZ Minerals agreed to buy its joint-venture partner Cassini Resources for $3.37bn, seeking greater control over the West Musgrave nickel/copper project in Western Australia. The move reflects ongoing nickel consolidation and can bolster near-term sentiment toward nickel supply expectations, with limited secondary relevance for copper.

title: Copper gains on inventory draw and Chinese demand
summary: Copper prices rose as inventories declined in both LME and Shanghai-tracked warehouses to multi-month lows, while China’s imports and consumption stayed robust. The rally was further supported by worries about disruptions at Chile’s Codelco, though further upside likely needs demand recovery outside China.

title: Aluminum Curtain Wall Market Size to Reach USD 62.22 Billion by 2027; Heavy Investment in Aluminum Extrusion to Revivify Sales Prospects, states Fortune Business Insights™
summary: The report projects strong growth for the aluminum curtain wall market and highlights rising investments in aluminum extrusion capacity (e.g., a new 3300-ton press in Germany) plus new system launches. It also cites expanding construction demand in Asia Pacific, collectively suggesting improving near-term aluminum demand outlook.

title: Copper rises on inventory draw and Chinese demand
summary: Copper rose as inventories fell to multi-month lows on Shanghai and LME monitors and China’s unwrought copper imports signaled robust demand. Analysts cited improved sentiment and noted that further gains likely need wider (Western) demand recovery. Supply risk from Chile’s Codelco added support. Aluminium rose; nickel fell.

title: Blackstone Intersects Further Broad Nickel Sulfides at Ban Chang
summary: Blackstone reports it intersected a 15.4m wide zone of massive nickel sulphide mineralisation at the Ban Chang prospect within Vietnam’s Ta Khoa nickel-Cu-PGE district. Results include assays with meaningful Ni and associated Cu, supporting further drilling and potential future mining studies, but no near-term production change is stated.

title: Copper falls on worries about U.S.-China trade tensions
summary: Copper prices fell after a U.S. official said the U.S.-China trade deal is “over,” raising concerns about the global economic outlook and worsening sentiment as the dollar firmed. The LME copper contract reversed recent gains. The article also notes declines in LME aluminium and nickel amid broader risk concerns.

title: U.S. Set to Announce Aluminum Tariffs on Canada by End of Week
summary: The U.S. is reportedly preparing to announce aluminum tariffs on Canada by the end of the week. Such tariffs can increase the cost of Canadian aluminum imports, potentially disrupting trade flows and near-term market expectations for aluminum supply and pricing.

title: Blackstone Minerals intersects more nickel sulphide at its Vietnam project
summary: Blackstone Minerals says it has intersected a new, wide zone of massive nickel sulphide at the Ban Chang prospect of its Ta Khoa nickel-PGE project in Vietnam. Multiple drill holes returned substantial nickel (with some copper) and support bulk underground mining potential, with EM technology proving effective.

title: COVID-19 global disruption: Production update on global copper miners, smelters_SMM
summary: Worsening global COVID-19 conditions are driving containment measures that disrupt manpower, transport, and production. The piece compiles a survey update showing copper miners worldwide implementing production reductions or temporary shutdowns, following earlier China disruptions, implying weaker near-term copper supply and bearish price pressure.

title: Spot copper premiums fell as few consumers stockpiled before holiday_SMM
summary: Spot copper cathode premiums in Shanghai fell on June 23 as sellers destocked and downstream buyers showed limited willingness to stockpile ahead of the Dragon Boat Festival. Ample supplies and cautious restocking kept premiums pressured, with standard-grade premiums sliding as low as 150 yuan/mt by noon.

title: US set to announce aluminum tariffs on Canada: report
summary: A Bloomberg report says the Trump administration may reinstate a 10% tariff on aluminum imports from Canada unless Canada imposes export restrictions. An announcement could come by end of the week, with tariffs effective July 1, ahead of a new USMCA timeline. U.S. aluminum demand weakened during the pandemic, and prices fell.

title: US set to announce aluminum tariffs on Canada by end of week
summary: The headline says the US will announce aluminum tariffs on Canada by the end of the week. Such tariffs can reduce Canadian aluminum inflows and tighten near-term supply expectations for the US market, typically supporting higher aluminum prices over days to a few weeks.

title: U.S. plans to slap tariffs on aluminum imports from Canada, Bloomberg report says
summary: Bloomberg reports the U.S. plans to re-impose 10% tariffs on aluminum imports from Canada, potentially announced Friday and implemented by July 1. The move is linked to the Canada-U.S.-Mexico trade agreement timing and could strengthen U.S. aluminum pricing by reducing Canadian supply access.

title: Copper recovers after Trump says U.S.-China trade deal still intact
summary: Copper rose on expectations the U.S.-China trade deal remains intact and on stronger European PMIs, which boosted risk appetite and recovery hopes. The rally is supported by near-recovered Chinese demand, supply disruptions in Chile, falling LME on-warrant inventories, and higher Chinese import premiums. Aluminium tariff news is also cited.

title: U.S. planning to reimpose tariffs on imports of Canadian aluminum: report
summary: U.S. officials are considering reimposing tariffs on Canadian aluminum unless Ottawa agrees to export quotas by July 1. The threat comes amid renewed trade-war talk under USMCA timelines. U.S. aluminum producers are lobbying for action, while industry groups argue over whether imports have surged.

title: Copper gains as Trump, European PMIs bolster demand outlook
summary: Copper prices rose 0.4% to near a five-month high after Trump said the U.S.-China trade deal is intact and European PMIs beat expectations. Analysts cited Chile supply disruptions, falling LME copper inventories, and stronger Chinese demand and import premiums. Aluminium tariff re-imposition plans were also reported as a support factor.

title: Constellium Paris: Constellium announces the launch of Aheadd, its new aluminium powder offer for additive manufacturing market
summary: Constellium announced the launch of “Aheadd,” a new high-performance aluminium powder offering for additive manufacturing, and said it is working with Poly-Shape (AddUp) to develop components using these powders. The release targets aerospace, defense and other markets, implying incremental aluminium demand support but no major supply shift.

title: U.S. may announce aluminum tariffs on Canada by end of week
summary: The report notes the U.S. may announce aluminum tariffs on Canada by the end of the week. Such tariffs would likely reduce Canadian metal imports into the U.S. and disrupt near-term trade/demand expectations, typically pressuring aluminium prices in the following days as market participants reprice the outlook.

title: U.S. said to announce aluminum tariffs on Canada by end of the week
summary: The Trump administration is considering re-imposing 10% tariffs on Canadian aluminum imports by July 1 if Canada does not accept export restrictions. Officials cite import surges and cite stresses on U.S. aluminum producers. Industry groups are split, but the tariff threat is likely supportive for aluminum prices.

title: Blackstone hits 15.4 m of nickel sulphides in Vietnam
summary: Blackstone Minerals reported a wide 15.4 m intersection of nickel sulphides at the Ban Chang prospect in Vietnam, following earlier high-grade hits including nickel at 2.20% with copper. The company aims to fast-track resources for potential renewed mining, but no production changes are stated.

title: The Daily Chase: U.S. may announce aluminum tariffs on Canada this week
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports that the U.S. may announce aluminum tariffs on Canada this week. Such tariffs can restrict or reroute Canadian aluminum flows into the U.S., tightening available supply for U.S. buyers in the near term and potentially pushing aluminum prices higher.

title: U.S. set to announce aluminum tariffs on Canada by end of week
summary: The Trump administration is considering reimposing U.S. tariffs on aluminum imports from Canada, with an announcement possible by end of week. If Canada does not agree to aluminum export restrictions, the U.S. would impose 10% tariffs starting Friday and implement them by July 1, affecting trade and pricing expectations.

title: Canada firmly believes its aluminum exports do not harm the U.S. market: official
summary: Canada’s official said Ottawa believes its aluminum exports do not harm the U.S. market, after Bloomberg reported Washington planned to reimpose tariffs. Canada signaled it would defend its aluminum sector and emphasized the export impact to U.S. partners, highlighting renewed trade risk for aluminum flows.

title: U.S. Weighs Reimposing Tariffs on Canadian Aluminum
summary: The Trump administration is considering reinstating tariffs on Canadian aluminum amid concerns that Canadian exports to the U.S. are rising, ahead of the USMCA entering into force July 1. Companies are split, with some seeking protection while critics warn retaliation and another trade war could pressure aluminium sentiment.

title: Feds prepared to push back against any new U.S. tariffs on aluminum, Duclos says
summary: Canada’s Treasury Board President Jean‑Yves Duclos said federal officials would oppose any new U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminum, after a Bloomberg report claimed the U.S. could impose a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports. The threat is linked to worsening risks post‑COVID and prior reciprocal duties.

title: Feds prepared to push back against any new U.S. tariffs on aluminum: Duclos
summary: Canadian federal officials, via Duclos, are prepared to push back against any new U.S. tariffs on aluminum. By signaling resistance to potential tariff imposition, the news improves near-term expectations for aluminum trade conditions and limits the risk of demand destruction that tariffs could cause.

title: 'This is business, it's not personal': Trade lawyer on possible aluminum tariffs
summary: The article features a trade lawyer commenting on potential aluminum tariffs. Such tariff developments can quickly change expectations for cross-border aluminum supply, pricing, and downstream demand, influencing near-term aluminium market sentiment. Depending on scope and timing, tariffs could add costs or curb trade volumes, weighing on aluminium prices.

title: Canada denies its aluminum exports harm U.S. market, official says
summary: Canada denies that its aluminum exports harm the U.S. market while U.S. officials may reimpose tariffs on Canadian aluminium imports. The dispute follows complaints from U.S. primary producers about surging Canadian inflows. Canada argues industries are integrated; timing for possible measures is before July 1.

title: U.S. threatens new tariffs on Canadian aluminum unless metal exports curtailed
summary: U.S. trade officials are threatening to reimpose tariffs on Canadian aluminum unless Canada agrees to export quotas by July 1. Canada signals it would retaliate. The potential renewed trade war, alongside mixed industry lobbying, adds near-term uncertainty to aluminum supply and demand, pressuring prices.

title: U.S. poised to slap 10% tariff again on aluminum from Canada
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports the U.S. may slap a 10% tariff again on aluminium imports from Canada. Reimposing the duty would likely reduce Canadian shipments into the U.S., tightening near-term availability and supporting higher aluminium prices as markets price in the renewed trade barrier.

title: Canada will defend its aluminum industry, says official
summary: Canada’s government says it will defend its aluminum sector as Bloomberg/officials report the U.S. may reimpose 10% tariffs on Canadian aluminum if Canada does not restrict exports. The move could take effect around July 1 under the USMCA timing, amid disputes over import surges and tariff exclusions.

title: Liberal government nearing revived trade spat with U.S. as tensions mount over dairy, aluminum
summary: The Canadian government faces renewed U.S. trade pressure. U.S. officials accuse Canada of “shading” dairy rules and, separately, say a surge in Canadian aluminum imports conflicts with anti-dumping understandings. The U.S. is considering re-imposing aluminum tariffs, increasing short-term uncertainty over Canadian aluminum exports.

title: Experts Talk Gold, Copper and More in a Post COVID-19 World
summary: An expert panel discusses how COVID-19 easing and fiscal/monetary stimulus could lift commodity prices. Copper is highlighted as a likely winner due to improving demand after China’s lockdowns ended, declining inventories, and longer-run support from electrification and renewable grid demand.

title: Chalco to source bauxite from Africa - Chinadaily.com.cn
summary: Chalco said it will receive its first large bauxite shipment from Boffa, Guinea, and the project is on track to complete two months ahead of schedule. Management and analysts view the ramp-up as improving bauxite self-sufficiency and sustaining aluminum production during COVID-era supply disruptions.

title: U.S. Chamber opposes U.S. plans to re-impose tariffs on aluminum from Canada
summary: The U.S. Chamber opposes U.S. plans to re-impose tariffs on aluminum from Canada. If tariffs are less likely to be implemented, markets may anticipate steadier aluminum import flows into the U.S., supporting prices. Investors may adjust expectations for short-term supply tightness.

title: Coronavirus: Why the pandemic could spark a copper rally
summary: The article argues the COVID-19 downturn could be followed by a copper-led recovery as governments pursue green and digital stimulus. It cites forecasts of demand rebound and higher 2020–2021 price targets, linking electrification, EVs, 5G, and renewables to stronger copper consumption.

title: China copper inventory shrank for the 15th week with stocks in Shanghai dipping the most_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s copper cathode inventories kept shrinking for the 15th week, falling 17,900 mt to 162,000 mt as of June 24. Shanghai dropped the most to 127,000 mt, while Guangdong and Jiangsu also declined, signaling tighter near-term supply.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks expanded 400 mt from last Friday_SMM
summary: SMM reported that Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories rose by 400 mt week-on-week to 16,000 mt as of June 24. Nickel cathode accounted for the increase, with forward cargoes entering bonded warehouses and some imports bypassing the bonded area. Trades in the bonded zone remained muted, suggesting supply overhang.

title: Inside Iran's secret project to produce aluminum powder for missiles
summary: Reuters reports Iran’s secret facility near Jajarm produces aluminum powder for missile solid-fuel propellants from bauxite. The operation appears connected to Iran Alumina Company and faces US and UN sanctions that target Iran’s aluminum sector and missile activities. The revelation could increase enforcement risk and reduce near-term aluminium trade expectations.

title: Special Report: Inside Iran's secret project to produce aluminium powder for missiles | News
summary: Reuters reports Iran’s Revolutionary Guards-run secret facility at Jajarm produces aluminium powder for missile solid-fuel propellants from bauxite feedstock. It highlights existing U.S./UK/U.N. sanctions targeting Iran’s aluminium sector and missile activity, potentially increasing supply-chain disruption and market risk around aluminium procurement and prices.

title: Inside Iran's secret project to produce aluminium powder for missiles
summary: Reuters reports Iran is producing aluminium powder at a Jajarm complex near bauxite deposits for use in missile solid-fuel propellants. The story may intensify sanctions enforcement and UN scrutiny of Iran’s aluminium sector. Restrictions already target transactions related to Iran’s aluminium; new allegations could further constrain supply.

title: Special Report: Inside Iran's secret project to produce aluminium powder for missiles
summary: Reuters reports that an aluminium production complex near Iran’s Jajarm bauxite deposit also houses a secret IRGC facility producing aluminium powder used in missile solid-fuel propellants. While the article highlights aluminium-focused diversion and potential sanctions/security implications, it does not show immediate disruptions to global aluminium supply or prices.

title: U.S. weighs reimposing tariffs on Canadian aluminum, sources say
summary: Sources say the U.S. is weighing reimposing tariffs on Canadian aluminum. If implemented, the measure would likely curb Canadian imports into the U.S., tightening apparent supply and raising delivered costs. That would tend to support aluminium prices in the coming days as market participants reprice trade flows.

title: Post Lockdown Phase Would Witness Boost In Copper Sector
summary: Reuters and analysts expect copper to rebound after the pandemic, with government “green and digital” stimulus supporting demand for renewables, electric vehicles, and 5G. The article notes benchmark LME copper near five-month highs and forecasts price strength in 2020-2021 as stimulus and supply disruptions boost consumption.

title: Ottawa prepared to push back against any new U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: Canada’s Treasury Board President said Ottawa will oppose any new U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum, responding to a Bloomberg report of a potential 10% tariff on imports. Officials argue Canadian aluminum isn’t harming the U.S. market, while past tariff episodes led to reciprocal measures between both countries.

title: Special Report: Inside Iran's Secret Project to Produce Aluminum Powder for Missiles | Jewish & Israel News Algemeiner.com
summary: Reuters reports Iran’s aluminum complex near Jajarm produces aluminum powder used in missile solid-fuel propellants. The work appears tied to the Revolutionary Guards. The U.S. has sanctions targeting Iran’s aluminum sector and could intensify enforcement or investigations, potentially tightening aluminum supply and weighing on prices.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 100,000 wmt _SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell after two weeks of gains. Total stocks dropped by 100,000 wmt from June 19 to 7.99 million wmt by June 24, with metal content down 800 mt to 65,000 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also declined to 6.95 million wmt.

title: COVID-19 will tilt aluminium axis further towards China: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist says COVID-19 is tilting aluminium supply toward China as output recovers and new smelters come online, while demand weakens. LME inventories rise sharply, prices struggle to rebound from a four-year low, and Western smelters face margin stress and closures, implying bearish near-term price pressure.

title: Chilean copper miner Codelco hit by third coronavirus death – union
summary: Chile’s state miner Codelco reported a third COVID-19-related death of a worker at the Chuquicamata facility’s smelter, according to a Reuters-seen internal memo and union statements. Codelco said the death reflects a difficult health emergency period. The operational disruption risk can affect near-term copper supply expectations.

title: 19 will tilt aluminum axis further towards China: Andy Home
summary: China’s aluminum production is rebounding and growing toward its 45Mt capacity cap, with new smelters coming online. Western smelters face margin stress from low prices and rising LME inventories. Semi shipments are slower but supply remains ample as tariffs and limited multilateral action allow China’s output creep, bearish for aluminum prices.

title: Copper-nickel mining
summary: The piece criticizes Antofagasta’s Twin Metals proposal for an underground copper-nickel mine in Minnesota, claiming it cannot operate profitably at current copper ($2.68/lb) and nickel ($5.68) prices. It argues uncertainty and opposition are hurting the local economy and that the project’s viability depends on much higher future metal prices.

title: Record high copper grades during exploration at the Viscaria D-zone; VDD0213 intersects 4.6m at 5.3% copper incl. 0.6m at 20.1% copper
summary: Exploration results from the Viscaria D-zone (VDD0213) show 4.6 meters at 5.3% copper, including 0.6 meters at 20.1% copper. The “record high grades” finding improves perceived resource quality and could be seen as supportive for future copper supply expectations, nudging copper sentiment upward.

title: Copper rises amid low inventories, Chile supply risks
summary: Copper rose 0.3% as inventories tightened across LME on-warrant and ShFE-tracked warehouses, hitting multi-month lows. Supply risks also increased after Chile’s Codelco reported a third COVID-19 death. Even as macro concerns and a stronger dollar capped gains, copper sentiment remained supported by constrained stocks.

title: Constellium Paris: Constellium to lead £15 million ALIVE project for the development of new aluminium battery enclosures for electric vehicles
summary: Constellium will lead a £15 million ALIVE project to design, engineer, and prototype structural aluminium battery enclosures for electric vehicles. The work will use Constellium high-strength HSA6 extrusion alloys and new manufacturing concepts, with aluminium extrusions produced at Brunel University’s technology center. Prototypes are expected by end-2021.

title: Ofcom Consults on Openreach UK Copper Retirement Process
summary: Ofcom opened a consultation on changing the process for retirement of Openreach’s UK copper lines and shifting more customers to FTTP. By waiting until after its WFTMR final decisions, Ofcom aims to refine conditions for when copper charge controls can be lifted, with earliest removals discussed for 2022-2023.

title: Chile copper producer Codelco reports third Covid-19 death
summary: Codelco reported a third Covid-19 death of a worker, raising pressure on Chile’s copper mining operations amid union demands for stronger safety measures. The Chuquicamata open-pit mine was affected, and Codelco has previously suspended some projects and faced quarantine-related work threats, implying near-term supply risk for copper.

title: Aluminium industry seeks duty remission to compete with Chinese producers
summary: India’s aluminium industry has asked the government to implement/accelerate RoDTEP and raise MEIS benefits to offset about 15% extra cost versus China. The industry argues export duty/tax rebates would improve competitiveness, support higher aluminium exports, and is seeking reimbursement of domestic taxes on export products.

title: DIAS: Canada must oppose any reimposition of unfair aluminum tariffs
summary: The article argues Canada should oppose any U.S. reimposition of “unfair” aluminum tariffs. It says the Trump administration may add a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum exports unless Canada accepts export quotas, potentially announced as early as July 1. Dias warns tariffs would likely be costly and could force smelter closures.

title: Chilean copper miner Codelco halts Chuquicamata smelter and refinery amid coronavirus
summary: Codelco said it will temporarily halt operations at the Chuquicamata division’s biggest smelter and refinery to prevent further coronavirus spread. The shutdown reduces refined copper output during Chile’s worst pandemic weeks, including reported Codelco worker deaths, creating immediate supply risk for the market.

title: Mincor edges closer to reviving Kambalda's nickel mines with $60m investment plan
summary: Mincor is moving closer to reviving nickel operations at Kambalda, backed by a planned $60 million investment. The report suggests renewed focus on restarting/expanding mine activity, which can influence expectations for near-term nickel supply and related market pricing over coming weeks.

title: Copper extends gains, set for sixth weekly jump as supply fears escalate
summary: Copper prices extended gains for a sixth straight week as supply fears rose with coronavirus disruptions in key producing countries. Codelco suspended refinery and foundry operations at Chuquicamata, implying larger copper losses, while Peru’s closures affected about 2 million tonnes. Nickel and aluminium also climbed.

title: Copper heads for sixth weekly gain as supply fears grow
summary: Copper extended gains toward a sixth consecutive weekly rise as coronavirus-driven supply disruption fears grew. Codelco suspended refinery and foundry operations at Chuquicamata, suggesting potential production losses exceeding Chile’s estimate. Analysts also cite Peru capacity closures. Nickel and aluminium were also higher, supported by improving supply expectations.

title: Silver, Copper Look to Recoup Losses From Earlier This Year
summary: The piece says industrial metals have rebounded in recent weeks. It notes silver has erased its year-to-date losses and copper is aiming to recover most of the declines it suffered during the pandemic’s peak economic downturn. The tone suggests improving market conditions supporting copper prices in the near term.

title: Chile suspends copper refinery and foundry at giant mine following Covid-19 19 deaths
summary: Codelco suspended refinery and foundry operations at its Chuquicamata division in Chile after Covid-19 deaths, winding down processing gradually while keeping minor maintenance and production work. The action affects a major smelting facility supporting a significant share of Codelco output, implying near-term refined copper supply risk.

title: Copper strides to 5-month high on fears about Chile output
summary: Copper prices reached a five-month peak as investors feared worsening COVID-19 disruptions to Chilean supply. Codelco suspended operations at its Chuquicamata division, and analysts warned production losses could exceed government estimates. LME data also showed aluminium stocks rising, while nickel and other metals gained.

title: Garibaldi Begins Drilling at Nickel Mountain
summary: Garibaldi Resources begins its 2020 drill program at the Nickel Mountain project in British Columbia, targeting extensions of a nickel-copper-rich massive sulphide system identified by prior drilling and EM surveys. The release outlines exploration plans to expand the E&L deposit; no production or immediate supply changes are mentioned.

title: Norrlandsfonden invests in Copperstone
summary: Norrlandsfonden will invest 2 MSEK in a convertible debenture for Copperstone, providing working capital to reinforce momentum in the Viscaria Copper Project in Kiruna and another project in Arvidsjaur. The note carries Stibor-based interest and may convert to equity, with limited dilution.

title: Spruce Ridge Resources Limited: Spruce Ridge Gives an Update on Company Exploration Activities and Plans: Drilling to Commence at Great Burnt Copper-Gold Property, Newfoundland
summary: Spruce Ridge plans to commence 3,000 metres of infill drilling at its Great Burnt copper-gold property in Newfoundland to upgrade copper resources, with expected receipt of survey results and further metallurgical testing. The release is exploration-focused and does not signal near-term output or supply changes.

title: 19 hits tin and zinc supply but focus now on copper: Andy Home
summary: COVID-19 is disrupting metal supply via mine and smelter closures. The key focus shifts to copper in Chile: as Chilean cases rise, unions push safety measures and Codelco suspends smelting at Chuquicamata to redeploy manpower, raising uncertainty over refined copper output and potential second-wave closures.

title: COVID-19 hits tin and zinc supply but focus now on copper
summary: COVID-19 lockdowns have disrupted base metals, with attention turning to copper in Chile. Although Chilean copper output grew earlier in 2020, rising sector infections and Codelco’s decision to suspend smelting at Chuquicamata raise near-term refined supply risks, keeping a bearish tone.

title: Silver, copper prices mark an impressive recovery from March lows
summary: Copper prices have rebounded sharply from March lows, with the article noting that earlier declines from coronavirus-related economic stress are being partially recouped. It attributes the move partly to a drop in global mining production during shutdowns and says the strong price climb implies markets see the economic slowdown as short-lived.

title: U.S. plan to slap tariffs on Canadian aluminum faces a powerful adversary — the beer lobby
summary: U.S. policymakers are considering reinstating 10% tariffs or quotas on Canadian primary aluminium under Section 232 after concerns about export surges. Industry groups argue Canadian supply is needed to meet U.S. demand and note premiums have already jumped. Beer and automotive users oppose the move over cost and job impacts.

title: Black Butte Copper Mine/Montana Department of Environmental Quality: Trout Unlimited Complaint for Declaratory Relief Challenging Issuance of Environmental Permits | Mitchell, Williams, Selig, Gates & Woodyard, P.L.L.C.
summary: Trout Unlimited and other groups filed a June 4 court complaint challenging Montana DEQ’s approval of Tintina Montana’s permit for the Black Butte copper mine in the Smith River watershed. The lawsuit contests permitting legality for a project involving daily excavation of concentrated copper ore and substantial tailings and waste rock.

title: Aluminum Tariffs Would Make Mockery of NAFTA 2 and Ignore the Real Problem
summary: The United Steelworkers warns that re-imposed U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum exports threaten jobs and undermine a new North American trade deal. The union argues tariffs are unjustified and that the real issue is China’s subsidized aluminum overcapacity. The reported tariff risk could still pressure near-term aluminum prices through trade disruption.

title: Copper bucks sentiment with gains on supply woes
summary: Copper rose as supply risks from South America mounted. Chile’s Chuquicamata could shut for two weeks after worker deaths, while Peru’s output is still recovering from pandemic-related suspension. With reduced staffing, falling inventories, scarce scrap, and UBS projecting a large deficit, investors expect tighter availability despite demand fears.

title: Ellwood Aluminum makes first cast | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Ellwood Group’s new Ellwood Aluminum cast house in Pennsylvania produced its first test casts and is progressing through tooling qualification and customer certification. The company targets supplying some customers in September and broader output by January-February, aiming for 150 million pounds of aluminum castings annually, supporting incremental aluminum demand.

title: An alumina refinery in Shanxi cut 1 million mt/year of capacity due to equipment accident_SMM
summary: An alumina refinery in Shanxi, China, shut a production line after an equipment accident, reducing annualised output by 1 million mt. The restart date is uncertain. Prior to the accident, 2.0 million mt/year of the 2.2 million mt/year plant capacity was operating, implying a supply tightness risk for aluminium.

title: China's nickel ore imports rose 25% in May as lockdown restrictions eased in the Philippines_SMM
summary: China’s imports of nickel ore and concentrate rebounded in May, up 24.83% month-on-month to 1.68 million mt, as Philippines deliveries resumed after COVID-19 lockdown measures eased. Imports from the Philippines rose 22.4% from April. Indonesian supply also increased sharply on the month, improving near-term nickel feedstock availability.

title: Commodity Weekly: NatGas Slumps, Copper Jumps as Virus Maintain its Grip
summary: The weekly commodities note says copper is firm and has jumped as COVID-related supply disruptions emerge, with South American mines operating on skeleton staff. It highlights LME Copper regaining the $6,000/t level and High Grade Copper testing recent highs, implying near-term bullish expectations for copper supply and prices.

title: Chilean copper miners threaten strike over alarming increase in Covid-19 cases - Chile News
summary: Chile’s copper miners’ federation, representing workers at Codelco and other major mines, called for re-evaluation of operational continuity plans and warned of possible work stoppages/quarantines after rising COVID-19 cases and a worker death. Disruption risk to Chilean copper supply comes amid broader demand uncertainty from China.

title: Nornickel Says Took Measures to Stop Discharge of Industrial Liquid Waste in Norilsk
summary: Nornickel said it took steps to halt spillover of circulating water from the Talnakh plant sump in Norilsk, with regulators including Rosprirodnadzor and investigators inspecting and taking samples. Officials attributed the sump level rise to possible pipeline tests or heavy rains and confirmed the discharge was stopped.

title: Natural gas slumps, copper jumps as virus maintains grip: index
summary: Copper is highlighted as a standout, initially hit in March by pandemic-driven demand destruction, then supported by global stimulus expectations and improved demand in China. The article also cites supply risks as South American mines operate skeleton staffs. It notes LME copper back near $6,000/t and high-grade copper challenging recent highs.

title: Copper hits 5-month high on Chile fears
summary: Copper prices are rising to a five-month high as traders react to fears over Chile. The market interpretation is that Chile-related supply risk could reduce near-term copper availability, tightening expectations for fundamentals and supporting upward price pressure over coming days to weeks.

title: Shanghai copper hits over 5-month high on Chile supply risks
summary: Shanghai copper rose to a more than five-month high as traders feared Chilean supply disruptions after a surge in COVID-19 cases. Chile’s mines minister said output could fall by about 200,000 tonnes (3.5%). LME and SHFE copper gains reflect tightening near-term supply expectations.

title: Shanghai copper climbs over 5-month peak on Chile supply risks
summary: Shanghai copper rose to a more than five-month high as investors priced in looming supply risks from Chile, where COVID-19 could cut output and unions are more vocal. A weaker U.S. dollar and tight Chinese scrap availability also supported demand sentiment, pushing ShFE and LME copper higher.

title: Material Matters: Copper Concerns And Iron Ore
summary: The piece questions whether copper’s recent rally reflects true demand. While Citi notes improved China end-use signals and falling inventories, ANZ shows downstream demand still deteriorating and points to trader stockpiling. With supply constraints easing expected, analysts warn refined copper could come under pressure if stimulus-driven demand disappoints.

title: China's bauxite imports fell 4% in May_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: China’s May bauxite imports fell 3.98% m/m to 9.54 million mt, with Guinea volumes down as refiners cut output on cost concerns. At the same time, imported bauxite prices dropped 3.3% in May to $46.54/mt due to lower COVID-related sea freight, helping aluminium feedstock costs.

title: Spot copper premiums in Shanghai stayed at highs on strong copper futures_SMM
summary: Shanghai spot copper cathode premiums stayed at high levels after SHFE copper futures rallied. The move was linked to faster declines in domestic inventories, while cautious consumers limited month-end stockpiling. Traders reduced premiums on lower-priced cargoes, but offers of hydro-copper fell sharply, indicating tight near-term supply support.

title: Norilsk Nickel admits to pumping wastewater into Arctic, suspends employees | Companies
summary: Norilsk Nickel admitted improper wastewater dumping into Russia’s Arctic tundra and suspended employees after a gross violation of operational protocols. The company said it is cooperating with regulators to assess potential damage and claimed there is no threat of leakage. The report follows media allegations of heavy-metal contamination.

title: Nornickel: Russia probes new pollution at Arctic mining firm
summary: Russian authorities investigated Norilsk Nickel for pumping wastewater from an Arctic processing plant into tundra. The firm suspended staff and denied the presence of toxic tailings, but reporters allege heavy metals and acid. A large diesel spill involving 21,000 tonnes was also cited, raising near-term supply disruption risk.

title: LME aluminium stocks at highest since April 2017 on weak physical market
summary: LME aluminium stocks have risen to the highest level since April 2017, reflecting a weak physical market. With more metal available in warehouses, buyers face less urgency, which can dampen spot demand and weigh on aluminium pricing expectations in the near term.

title: Copper heads higher as coronavirus constricts Chilean supply
summary: Copper prices are edging higher as COVID-19 hampers Chilean supply, with mines potentially cutting output by about 200,000 tonnes. Meanwhile, stocks at LME and Shanghai warehouses have declined and cash-to-three-month spreads tightened, reflecting tighter near-term availability. China’s demand backdrop is described as solid.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jun 29): SHFE base metals closed mostly higher despite surge in coronavirus cases; copper hit 5-month peak_SMM
summary: SHFE base metals rose mostly higher after the Dragon Boat holiday despite renewed COVID-19 curbs. Copper hit a five-month peak on fears output could be disrupted in Chile, where Codelco suspended Chuquicamata refinery and foundry operations. Aluminium climbed alongside falling primary ingot inventories; nickel also ended higher.

title: Feds prepared to push back against any new U.S. tariffs on aluminum, Duclos says - MRO Magazine
summary: Canadian officials said they are prepared to oppose any new U.S. protectionist tariffs on steel and aluminum, responding to a report that the Trump administration may impose a 10% tariff on aluminum imports from Canada. Canada argues its aluminum exports are not harming the U.S. market.

title: Coronavirus cluster at aluminum plant rises to 74 people, most live in Oneida County
summary: A COVID-19 cluster at Keymark’s aluminum extrusion plant has grown to 74 positive cases out of 500 workers, with most cases among employees living in Oneida County. New results may increase. The plant remains closed, indicating an immediate production disruption that could support aluminum prices.

title: U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum to hurt both economies, Trudeau says
summary: U.S. officials are reportedly considering re-imposing a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum unless Canada limits aluminum exports. Trudeau warns tariffs would raise input costs for U.S. manufacturers and hurt both economies. The possible trade dispute is expected in coming weeks, affecting aluminum trade flows and prices.

title: LME copper set for best quarter in a decade on China factory recovery
summary: LME copper is set for its best quarterly performance in a decade as China’s June factory activity surprised to the upside, supporting demand expectations. title: Copper scales 5-month high on China recovery hopes, supply fears
summary: Copper prices climbed to a five-month high on renewed China recovery expectations and supply concerns. LME copper inventories fell to the lowest since mid-March, and cash–to–three-month premiums rose, signaling tighter near-term supply. China policy and economic data boosted sentiment, while aluminium edged lower and nickel rose.

title: Blackstone buys third rig to ramp up Vietnam nickel drilling
summary: Blackstone Minerals bought a third diamond drill rig to accelerate drilling at Vietnam’s Ban Chang nickel prospect near the mothballed Ta Khoa nickel processing plant. Recent holes returned sulphide nickel grades with associated copper, and studies aim for possible nickel sulphate downstream production for lithium-ion batteries.

title: Shanghai copper hits 2020 high on China revival hopes, supply fears
summary: Shanghai copper rose to a 2020 high as China economic recovery hopes combined with supply fears supported sentiment. LME copper inventories fell to a multi-month low and nearby premiums widened, indicating tight physical supply. The article also mentions easing aluminum spreads and a rise in ShFE nickel, reflecting broad support.

title: Chilean copper industry halts expansion to slow the spread of coronavirus among miners
summary: Codelco halted work on an expansion project at the El Teniente copper mine to curb COVID-19 spread, reducing workers and contractors on site. It also suspended construction and slowed refining at Chuquicamata. These measures increase the risk of near-term copper production disruption and could weigh on prices.

title: Demand hopes, supply worries propel copper to 5-month peak
summary: Copper rallied to a 5-month peak as optimism over economic recovery and China manufacturing demand offset concerns about Chile supply disruptions tied to COVID. Tight LME conditions—rising cash/3-month premiums and high cancelled warrants—fueled worries about nearby availability, supporting strong bullish near-term price pressure for copper.

title: Ivanhoe updates on DRC's Kakula copper mine underground development
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reported progress at its Kakula copper project in the DRC, saying more than 17km of underground development has been completed ahead of schedule. The ore conveyor started operations, large processing-plant components were fabricated and are shipping, and initial production is targeted for Q3 next year.

title: Chile putting mine workers' health over copper production, minister says
summary: Chile’s mines minister says COVID health measures are being prioritized over full output, with firms keeping workers home and altering shifts, suspending upgrades and some smelter operations as cases spike. Chile’s copper commission projects a large 2020 production drop if cases worsen, impacting near-term supply expectations.

title: Exclusive: Chile putting mine workers' health over copper production, minister says
summary: Chile’s mines minister says COVID-19 containment measures are taking priority over output, keeping workers at home, tightening testing, and suspending upgrades and some smelter operations as cases and deaths spike. Cochilco projects a 200,000–240,000 tonne 2020 production drop if cases don’t decline, adding near-term copper supply risk.

title: The latest in coronavirus shortages: Aluminum cans
summary: Reports from CBS8 and FOX26 say aluminum beverage-can availability is tightening as consumers shift toward canned beer, hard cider, and wine at home. Can sales rose sharply in March–April, manufacturers are near capacity, and suppliers face backorders, prompting demand-driven pressure while firms expand capacity.

title: Exclusive: Chile putting mine workers' health over copper production, minister says | WTAQ News Talk | 97.5 FM · 1360 AM
summary: Chile’s mines minister says copper output is taking a back seat to COVID-19 safeguards, with strict testing and about half the workforce kept at home. He warns production depends on case trends, citing Cochilco’s forecast of a 200,000–240,000-tonne 2020 drop if cases decline. Copper markets are viewed as stabilizing.

title: Shanghai copper at 6-1/2-month high as supply risk mounts in top miner Chile
summary: Shanghai copper rose to a 6-1/2-month high as worries grew that Chile, the world’s top copper producer, may face supply disruptions. Chile’s mining minister said worker health is being prioritized to prevent infections. Gains were partly limited by concerns over slower global economic rebound amid rising COVID cases.

title: Shanghai copper at 6-1/2-month high as Chile supply risk looms
summary: Shanghai copper prices rose to a 6-1/2-month high as markets worried about potential supply disruptions from Chile, the top producer. Chile is prioritizing workers’ health to prevent infection spread that could hurt operations. This kept copper under bullish support, though global COVID-case spikes limited gains.

title: Shanghai copper at 14-1/2-month high on supply risks, China's equity bull run
summary: Shanghai copper surged to a 14-1/2-month high as traders priced in potential supply disruptions from Chile, where authorities prioritize workers’ health amid coronavirus concerns. China’s equity rally boosted demand sentiment. The August SHFE contract and LME copper were supported, with premiums tightening versus a week earlier.

title: Copper punches towards January peak, lifted by Chile fears
summary: Copper prices jumped to the highest level since January as speculators bought on fears of COVID-19 disruptions in Chile, the world’s top producer. Demand sentiment also improved with firmer China. LME copper neared the January peak, reinforcing expectations of tighter near-term supply and supporting bullish flows.

title: National aluminum can shortage affecting central Pa. grocery stores
summary: Weis Markets and Karns report shortages of canned soda and beer, citing a national aluminium can shortage. Demand rose as restaurant and bar closures increased at-home consumption, while beverage companies struggle to obtain enough aluminium to meet ongoing can production needs.

title: First Quantum to restart operations at Cobre Panama copper mine
summary: First Quantum Minerals plans to restart full production at its Cobre Panama copper mine after MINSA lifted the temporary suspension imposed during COVID-19 controls. The reopening will be phased by increasing on-site staff as production ramps toward an 85 million tonnes per annum throughput. The miner holds a 90% stake.
