title: Copper Mountain Mining Announces Commissioning of Direct Flotation Reactors at the Copper Mountain Mine
summary: Copper Mountain Mining says it has begun commissioning direct flotation reactors at the Copper Mountain mine. If the new flotation system ramps up successfully, it can improve ore processing and recovery, supporting expected copper supply. That can be mildly bullish for short-term copper prices.

title: China's primary aluminium output rose 2.4%YoY in June_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s primary aluminium output rose 2.42% YoY to 3.0 million mt in June, with operating rates edging up to 89% as margins encouraged ramp-ups. July output is expected to increase further, while consumption growth slows as supply grows and demand weakens, pressuring aluminium sentiment.

title: Copper punches towards January peak, boosted by Chile fears
summary: Copper surged to the highest since January as speculators bet on further disruptions in Chile’s mines and solid demand from China. The move followed renewed COVID-19 production fears in top producer Chile. LME aluminium also rose, while nickel was flat, implying copper-led strength.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Samples 4.64% Nickel Over 0.65 metres at Lappvattnet
summary: Gungnir Resources reports re-sampling of archived drill core at its Lappvattnet nickel deposit in Sweden, including an interval of 4.64% Ni over 0.65 metres. The company also provides historical Ni and minor Cu context and plans a resource update, but no production impact is described.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 08/07: LME aluminium price rallies to three-month high in high-vol trading
summary: The live futures report notes that LME aluminium prices have rallied to a three-month high in high-volume trading. It also discusses corrections/delays to certain Fastmarkets aluminium assessment publications, but the headline market message points to immediate strength in aluminium.

title: APAA Calls on President Trump to Restore Tariffs on Surging Canadian Aluminum Imports
summary: APAA urged President Trump to restore a 10% tariff on Canadian primary aluminum, citing an 80% surge in imports over the past year and a May 2020 record volume from Canada. The group argues recent Canadian subsidies and production restart boosted flows, and seeks trade enforcement to support domestic producers.

title: Rio Tinto announces plans to close New Zealand aluminium smelter in 2021
summary: Rio Tinto said it plans to close the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in August 2021, and the New Zealand government appears to accept the decision. The smelter employs more than 1,000 people directly, indicating a meaningful production cut that can affect aluminium supply expectations.

title: Rio Tinto says it has started plans to wind down and close the Tiwai Point Aluminium Smelter - 09-Jul-2020
summary: Rio Tinto says it has begun plans to wind down and close the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter after giving Meridian Energy notice to terminate its power contract. Closing the smelter reduces aluminium output and supply availability, which can be bullish for aluminium prices in the near term.

title: More than a thousand jobs will be lost - with New Zealand's only aluminium smelter set to close - 09-Jul-2020
summary: Rio Tinto says New Zealand’s only aluminium smelter at Tiwai Point will wind down operations in August 2021. The plant employs about 1,000 workers directly and more in the wider community. The smelter chief executive says the focus is on helping staff transition after the closure announcement.

title: Trudeau 'concerned' by U.S. threat of tariffs on Canadian aluminum and steel
summary: Trudeau said he is concerned the U.S. may reimpose tariffs on Canadian aluminum and possibly steel, despite USMCA taking effect July 1. The U.S. industry debate centers on whether Canadian aluminum exports constitute a surge threatening domestic producers. Canadian officials are pushing against the tariff threat.

title: Rio Tinto to shut New Zealand aluminium smelter | Companies
summary: Rio Tinto said it will close its aluminium smelter in New Zealand because of high costs and a challenging market, affecting about 1,000 direct jobs and 1,600 indirect jobs. The closure reduces expected aluminium supply, creating potential support for aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Trudeau concerned by reported U.S. threat of tariffs on Canadian aluminum, steel
summary: Canadian PM Trudeau said he is concerned the U.S. may reimpose tariffs on Canadian aluminum and possibly steel. He stressed the U.S. relies on Canadian aluminum imports and said Canada is pushing against unjustified tariffs that could harm Canadian jobs. Potential tariffs raise near-term supply risk for aluminum markets.

title: NZ Aluminium Smelters says lower cost power could prompt it to keep its doors open, but the window of opportunity is closing quickly; Government won't provide subsidy
summary: New Zealand Aluminium Smelters (NZAS) told its power supplier Meridian it will terminate its electricity contract, with wind-down expected to be complete by August 2021. Management says it cannot secure competitively priced power needed for sustainability and cites a challenging aluminium market, raising the possibility of reduced aluminium output.

title: Trudeau 'concerned' with U.S. threat of tariffs on Canadian aluminum and steel – RCI
summary: Trudeau said he is concerned the U.S. may reimpose extra tariffs on Canadian aluminum and possibly steel despite the new USMCA taking effect. Canadian officials are pushing the U.S. to avoid unjustified tariffs. Industry groups cite past tariffs and argue about whether Canadian aluminum export “surges” threaten domestic producers.

title: Rio Tinto To Close New Zealand Aluminium Smelters; 1,000 Jobs Affected
summary: Rio Tinto said it will wind down and close New Zealand Aluminium Smelters (NZAS) because the business is no longer viable amid high energy costs and a difficult aluminum outlook. The power contract with Meridian Energy will end in August 2021, with shutdown completion expected then, affecting about 1,000 jobs.

title: Chile's copper mines under threat from virus spread, copper price jerks upwards
summary: Copper prices jump as COVID-19 threatens Chilean production. Codelco reports thousands of worker infections, halts expansion at El Teniente, and suspends construction at operations including Chuquicamata. With unions and politicians pressing for more curbs and China boosting demand and stockpiling, the market expects tighter concentrate supply.

title: Rio Tinto to close Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in 2021
summary: The article states that Rio Tinto plans to close the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in 2021. A shutdown of a major smelter reduces aluminium production, tightening supply conditions. That expectation would likely be supportive for aluminium pricing in the days following the announcement.

title: Shanghai copper hits 16-month high on Chile supply concerns
summary: Shanghai copper prices rose to a 16-month high and London copper neared a six-month peak on renewed Chile supply worries. Unions at Codelco reported nearly 3,000 workers infected with COVID-19, prompting calls for stronger safety measures. The market priced greater near-term disruption risk.

title: Rio Tinto to shutter NZ aluminium smelter, putting jobs and economy in peril
summary: Rio Tinto plans to shut down its New Zealand aluminium smelter, raising concerns about jobs and the local economy. The reported closure implies reduced aluminium production capacity, which can tighten supply expectations in the short term and provide support for aluminium prices.

title: Rio Tinto announcement on Tiwai Aluminium Smelter
summary: Trustpower notes Rio Tinto’s announcement to wind down operations at the Tiwai aluminium smelter (NZAS), with expected closure in August 2021. Trustpower expects the power sector to adapt via transmission investment and demand growth. The smelter shutdown implies reduced aluminium supply.

title: South Port (SPN) Statement on NZAS Tiwai Point Aluminium Smelter Closure
summary: South Port says the NZAS Tiwai Point aluminium smelter closure in August 2021 will end a major customer relationship and reduce smelter-linked cargo. The statement highlights financial impacts and an as-yet-unknown effect during the current year as operations wind down, signaling reduced aluminium output.

title: Trudeau concerned over US tariffs on aluminium, steel
summary: Trudeau said Canada is concerned by reports the US may reimpose tariffs on Canadian aluminium (and possibly steel). He noted the US relies heavily on Canadian aluminium imports and lacks sufficient domestic production. Canadian officials are urging the US not to proceed, warning of negative impacts and a renewed trade fight.

title: Shanghai copper hits 16-month high as Chile supply worries mount
summary: Shanghai copper rose to a 16-month high and LME copper neared a six-month peak as worries about Chile’s Codelco supply intensified. Unions reported nearly 3,000 workers infected with coronavirus, renewing calls for safety measures. Analysts said the South America situation tightens the copper supply backdrop, supporting prices.

title: MORNING VIEW: Metals stronger as supply fears dominate, especially for copper, zinc
summary: The morning view reports metals are stronger on supply-fear dynamics. It specifically highlights copper, and discusses aluminium having been “hard to move,” citing curtailed output, inventory buffer drawdowns/repositioning, and severe shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz—signals likely to support short-term aluminium prices.

title: Trudeau concerned by reported U.S. threat of tariffs on Canadian aluminum, steel | Politics
summary: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said he is concerned by reports the U.S. may reimpose tariffs on Canadian aluminum and possibly steel. He argued the U.S. relies heavily on Canadian aluminum imports for domestic manufacturing capacity. Canadian officials are urging the U.S. not to move forward with unjustified tariffs.

title: Bam Bam Drilling Returns Significant Copper and Silver at Majuba Hill
summary: The headline reports that drilling at Majuba Hill returned significant copper (and silver) results. If verified, the find can lift market expectations for future copper supply and development success, supporting near-term sentiment for copper prices. The supplied text itself lacks further operational and tonnage details.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 7,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows China’s primary aluminium ingot inventories fell for the second consecutive week. Social inventories across eight consumption areas, including SHFE warrants, dropped 7,000 mt to 712,000 mt as of July 9, after a 3,000 mt decline the prior week. The reduced days-in-inventory signals tighter supply.

title: Aluminium billet inventories fell in China on greater shipments in the east_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s 6063 aluminium billet inventories fell 900 mt week on week to 72,300 mt as of July 9. The decline followed a rise in east-China shipments, with stocks dropping in Wuxi, Changzhou, and Nanchang, while Foshan and Huzhou saw gains.

title: Rio Tinto to close New Zealand aluminium smelters
summary: Rio Tinto says it will wind down and eventually close New Zealand Aluminium Smelters (NZAS) at Tiwai Point after a strategic review. The company cites persistent losses, high energy costs, and inability to secure a lower power price. Meridian confirmed Rio Tinto will terminate the electricity contract effective 31 August next year.

title: Copper hits highest in 14-months on China demand, Chile supply cuts
summary: Copper prices jumped to a 14-month high, supported by hopes for faster Chinese recovery and fears from temporary but potentially sizable supply disruptions in Chile. LME inventories fell and cash/3-month spreads strengthened. The broader complex also rose, with LME aluminium hitting a four-month high.

title: Global Aluminum Conductors Market 2020-2024 | Expansion and Revamping of T&D Networks to Boost Market Growth
summary: Technavio’s report projects strong growth in the aluminum conductors market, citing transmission and distribution network upgrades and expanding renewable wind/solar generation as key drivers. It notes large-scale infrastructure replacement and renovation programs, implying rising demand for aluminium conductors, while expecting aluminium prices to remain stable.

title: Copper hits 14-month high on China demand, Chile supply cuts
summary: Copper prices rose to a 14-month high on hopes of a faster China recovery and concerns over disruptions in Chile, the world’s biggest producer. LME copper climbed on higher cash premiums and falling on-warrant inventories. China factory price softness was partly offset by improving sector signs; speculators increased net longs.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 09/07: LME copper rallies to $6,300 at close; nickel falls 1.5%
summary: The LIVE FUTURES REPORT notes LME copper rallied to $6,300 at the close, while LME nickel declined by 1.5%. It also contains Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin methodological and assessment correction notes and general commentary on aluminium supply conditions, but without a specific aluminium price move.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 09/07: LME copper rallies to $6,300 at close; nickel falls 1.5%
summary: The report cites LME settlement moves: copper rallied to about $6,300 at the close, while nickel fell by roughly 1.5%. The accompanying text is largely administrative/methodology updates and does not add specific new fundamentals. Overall, the price signals are mixed across copper and nickel.

title: Norilsk Nickel fined US$2.1bn for Arctic oil spill
summary: Norilsk Nickel was fined US$2.1bn by Russia’s environmental watchdog after a diesel spill near Norilsk. The leak followed a storage tank collapse likely linked to unusually warm Arctic conditions and has reached Lake Pyasino. Cleanup is ongoing, while the company contests parts of the fine amid Greenpeace/WWF scrutiny.

title: Prospects slim for Tiwai Point aluminium smelter workers set to lose jobs
summary: New Zealand’s Tiwai Point aluminium smelter is set to close, cutting about 1,000 jobs directly and 1,600 in supply chains, despite government subsidy support. Officials cite emissions credit and transmission pricing issues. While the shutdown is planned by next year, it signals falling aluminium production and supply constraints.

title: Question marks over future power prices in New Zealand, following the decision by Rio Tinto to close its Tiwai Point aluminium smelter - 10-Jul-2020
summary: New Zealand power companies are assessing where electricity prices will go after Rio Tinto plans to close its Tiwai Point aluminium smelter. Rio says high power costs and a poor sales outlook drove the shutdown decision, and retailers expect demand and grid impacts to be uncertain for about a year.

title: Tiwai Point aluminium smelter closure: Southland faces 'shattering impact'
summary: Community leaders in Southland say the announced closure of the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter—planned for next August—could be a major economic blow. The news indicates reduced aluminium refining capacity, which would tighten supply expectations and likely support aluminium prices over the coming weeks.

title: Nickel Mines Poised For Price Recovery
summary: Nickel Industries’ Nickel Mines completed a stake increase to 80% in Indonesian Morowali nickel projects producing nickel pig iron. Analysts cite catalysts including improving nickel prices from cyclical lows, EV-related demand growth, and potential dividends in 2021, despite policy/export-ban risks in Indonesia.

title: LME copper holds steady, poised for eighth straight weekly jump
summary: London copper was steady but poised for an eighth straight weekly gain as China’s demand improved and COVID-related mine disruptions cut supply, with visible inventories down sharply since March. Three-month LME copper held near recent highs. Aluminium also rose, supported by demand recovery and higher alumina costs.

title: Chinese nickel company promises to hire 5,000 locals amid backlash
summary: Indonesia’s VDNI pledged to hire 5,000 locals for its Konawe nickel smelter after protests over 500 Chinese workers. The first batch arrived, but later arrivals were delayed due to demonstrations. Authorities say the project should proceed, albeit slower, while employment ramps up in phases.

title: Japan buyers agree to pay third-quarter aluminium premium of $79 per tonne
summary: Japanese buyers agreed a July–September aluminium premium of $79/t over the LME cash price, down 3.7% from the prior quarter and the fourth straight quarterly decline. The drop reflects collapsed COVID-impacted manufacturing demand, weaker imports/rolled shipments, and rising port stocks, with buyers seeking lower pricing as demand remains uncertain.

title: China copper inventory grew for the second straight week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that China’s copper cathode inventories in Shanghai, Guangdong and Jiangsu continued to increase for a second straight week. Total stocks rose 1,400 mt to 200,600 mt by July 10, after subdued demand at high prices had already triggered the first weekly build since March 20.

title: Copper recovering strongly, and at its highest levels since January
summary: Copper prices jumped to the highest level since January as speculative funds increased longs, betting on potential disruptions in top producer Chile. The move is supported by firm demand signals from China and bullish technical momentum, with LME and Shanghai futures hitting multi-month highs amid pandemic-related production fears.

title: Small China copper smelters shut as big get bigger - satellite data
summary: Satellite and industry data show China’s copper smelting activity in June was only slightly lower despite many small smelter closures. Rising input prices are pressuring margins and pushing some capacity offline, while activity at major operators increased, suggesting demand remains robust.

title: Japan Q3 aluminum premium falls to $79/T as COVID-19 hits demand
summary: Japan’s Q3 aluminum premium was set at $79/tonne, down 3.7% from the prior quarter, as COVID-19-driven manufacturing weakness reduced demand. Japan’s shipments of rolled products and primary ingot fell, port stocks rose, and buyers pressed for lower supply levels.

title: Rockcliff Initiates Drill Program on its High-Grade TGR Nickel-PGE Prospect Additional PGE Assaying on Discovery Hole Identifies Significant Rhodium Values
summary: Rockcliff initiated a new drilling program at its TGR nickel-PGE discovery and reported additional assay results with higher nickel equivalent grades, including significant rhodium and other PGMs alongside nickel. The update supports improved resource potential at Tower property, which is likely to be a near-term sentiment tailwind for nickel markets.

title: Study: aluminum is both a climate-friendly and cost-reducing material choice for bridge building
summary: Norsk Hydro and partners published a study on using aluminium bridge girders for Norway’s Langenuen coastal highway project, proposing up to 1,250 meters of aluminium girders totaling roughly 8,000–10,000 tonnes. The report suggests cost and maintenance advantages versus steel, improving aluminium’s near-term application prospects.

title: Proactive Investors China - The web's leading portal for China stocks - Red River Resources sets new quarterly copper production record
summary: The (partial) article title says Red River Resources has set a new quarterly copper production record. That headline suggests stronger copper output versus prior quarters, which can shift short-term expectations for copper supply and sentiment. Details on volumes, guidance, and timing are not provided in the excerpt.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks rose to about 16,500 mt on July 10_SMM
summary: SMM says Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories rose to about 16,500 mt as of July 10, with nickel cathode stocks up 400 mt week on week to 14,800 mt. Foreign trading stayed subdued and only limited cathode entered bonded warehouses, while some cathode is expected later in July and briquette shipments may decline.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 200,000 wmt to 7.88 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 200,000 wmt from July 3 to 7.88 million wmt as of July 10. In nickel content, stocks dropped 1,700 mt to 63,800 mt. Inventories at seven major ports declined by 240,000 wmt to 6.67 million wmt.

title: Biggest Copper Producers Add to Growing Supply-Disruption Fears
summary: Peru’s ramp-up after a two-month lockdown is slower than expected due to worker illness, limiting production capacity. In Chile, unions at Antofagasta mines vote on wages and could reject offers, risking strikes. Together, the disruptions heighten supply fears, supporting copper prices toward a weekly gain.

title: WHO experts head to China, where copper appetite may show recovery in economy
summary: The alert notes that China’s copper production rose in June, pointing to signs the country’s economy is recovering after pandemic-related slump. With China being the biggest consumer of industrial metals, improved output/demand expectations are likely to support short-term copper pricing.

title: Tariffs on Canadian aluminum would hurt Wisconsin, Skana CEO says
summary: Skana Aluminum’s CEO argues proposed U.S. tariffs on Canadian primary aluminum imports would raise aluminum costs for processors and consumers, disrupting supply used by the Wisconsin rolling mill. The firm says domestic supply can’t meet U.S. demand and warns Canada may retaliate, risking broader trade-war spillovers.

title: Southland mayors hopeful Tiwai Point aluminium smelter can stay open
summary: Southland mayors are urging the government and Rio Tinto to keep the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter open, after Rio Tinto said it plans to close in August next year due to high energy costs and a difficult outlook. Mayors seek more information and a chance to negotiate potential retention options.

title: Calls for tariffs on Canadian aluminum come with a Glencore twist
summary: U.S. political pressure is reviving talk of reimposing tariffs on Canadian aluminum under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada framework. Glencore is a major trader and investor in a U.S. aluminum producer lobbying for tariffs. Market participants link the renewed tariff speculation to rising U.S. forward premiums despite weak physical demand from COVID.

title: Arctic Oil Spill: Norilsk Nickel Fined $2.1B for Environmental Damages
summary: Russia’s environmental watchdog fined Norilsk Nickel $2.1B over an Arctic diesel spill in May caused by a collapsed fuel tank near Norilsk. The cleanup and soil/water remediation costs were substantial, and authorities declared a regional emergency. The company says it may contest the fine in court.

title: Egypt Aluminum considers funding from international institutions
summary: Egypt Aluminum said it is still considering requests for funding from five international financial institutions, with no funding amount determined yet. The company also reported net losses of EGP 1.019 billion for the first nine months of FY19/20. No direct production changes are disclosed, limiting immediate aluminium price pressure.

title: Soda flavors disappear from store shelves due to aluminum can shortage: report
summary: The report says lockdown-driven stockpiling has increased demand for canned soda by about 30% in March-April. Producers struggled to secure aluminum cans, leading some retailers to run out of certain brands and prioritize popular flavors. Increased packaging demand for aluminum is a short-term bullish signal for aluminium.

title: Karen militia protest government's use of violence in copper mine crackdown
summary: Karen militia groups protested the Burma government’s crackdown during the Letpandaung copper mine protests, after monks and civilians were wounded. The DKBA demanded an apology and an end to military offensives, warning of continued protests if no action is taken against abusive police. The incident links directly to Letpandaung’s copper project.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Jul 13): Base metals mostly higher; Shanghai copper soared nearly 5% on mine supply concerns _SMM
summary: SMM says nonferrous metals traded mostly higher, with copper leading on growing mine-supply concerns, including strike action at Antofagasta’s Zaldivar mine in Chile. Nickel and aluminium also rallied on Friday and into Monday, supported by broader risk sentiment and tight east China aluminium spot availability.

title: Copper jumps to 2-year high on strike worries at Chile mine
summary: Shanghai and London copper jumped to 2-year highs on Monday due to supply concerns after workers at Antofagasta Minerals’ Zaldivar mine in Chile voted for strike action, with a potential walkout set for July 15 pending government mediation. The move coincided with gains in aluminium and nickel prices.

title: Copper hits over 2-year high on Chile mine strike, China flood worries
summary: Shanghai and London copper surged to multi-year highs as supply worries grew. Workers at Antofagasta’s Zaldivar mine in Chile voted for strike action starting July 15. China flood warnings raised concerns over logistics and refined output, especially in Jiangxi. The move also lifted aluminium and nickel to multi-month peaks.

title: Copper price hits 2-yr peak on Chile strike fears [UPDATED]
summary: Copper prices are reported to be hitting a two-year peak as strike fears in Chile intensify. Such labor action risk would threaten near-term mine output and concentrate supply expectations toward tighter availability. The article’s remaining text largely covers Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin website or assessment scheduling updates.

title: Copper prices hit their highest in two years, over a Chilean miners' strike
summary: Copper prices jumped to multi-month highs on Monday amid supply worries from Chile after workers at Antofagasta’s Zaldivar mine voted for potential strike action. London and Shanghai copper rose sharply, with LME prices also firming for aluminium and nickel, indicating spillover across industrial metals.

title: Supply angst helps copper scale two-year high
summary: Copper jumped to two-year highs on supply angst and tight LME conditions. Worries include possible strikes at Antofagasta’s Chile mines, Codelco disruptions from COVID-19, and flooding risks in China’s Jiangxi region. Falling LME stocks and canceled warrants widened the cash premium, supporting bullish momentum.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 13/07: Production woes put LME copper above $6,500/t on high vol; C/3M holds backwardation
summary: A live futures update reports that production woes are driving LME copper above $6,500/t on high trading volume, with the C/3M curve holding backwardation. It also discusses aluminium supply conditions, including curtailed output and severe shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz, supportive for near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: Nornickel reports second oil spill, adding to company woes
summary: Nornickel reported a second diesel pipeline burst near Norilsk, following the May spill that flooded rivers with over 20,000 tonnes of fuel. Regulators are seeking large “voluntary compensation” and the company disputes damage estimates. The escalation adds to operational and legal uncertainty for the group’s nickel supply.

title: Revival of North American economy will negate need for aluminum tariffs, Trudeau tells Trump
summary: Trudeau urged Trump not to impose new tariffs on Canadian aluminum, arguing the North American economy and aluminum smelters are recovering post-pandemic. He said renewed production for U.S. auto supply reduces the rationale for tariffs that emerged after COVID-era shipment disruptions. The tariff decision remains uncertain but risk appears to be easing.

title: Canada Nickel (TSXV:CNC) Investor Overview
summary: The piece outlines Canada Nickel’s Crawford project in Ontario as a potential long-life, low-carbon nickel source outside Indonesia and China, with very strong stated economics. It also cites robust nickel demand growth for EV batteries and stainless steel, arguing the market could remain in deficit—supportive for nickel prices.

title: Workers at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine in Chile vote to strike -union
summary: Workers at Antofagasta’s Centinela copper mine in Chile have voted to strike, according to a union report. The action increases the likelihood of short-term output disruption from one of Chile’s significant copper-producing sites, which typically supports expectations for tighter supply and firmer copper prices.

title: Canada Nickel Identifies Multiple Nickel Targets on Recently Acquired Option Properties
summary: Canada Nickel reports it has identified seven nickel-bearing target structures on option properties acquired in May 2020. Historical drilling showed nickel and some PGM-enriched mineralization across the targets, though most drilling was decades ago and did not fully test target widths. The update supports potential future nickel supply sentiment.

title: Call For Govt Buy-out Of Aluminium Smelter
summary: Social Credit urges New Zealand’s government to buy the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter, convert it into a state-owned enterprise, and invest in advanced emission controls and upgrades. The plan includes long-term supply and sales contracts and would avoid closure fallout, supporting expected aluminium production and supply stability.

title: Lundin's Chile copper mine cutting its workforce, union says
summary: The news headline says Lundin’s copper mine in Chile is cutting its workforce, according to a union. Layoffs at a producing copper asset can signal potential short-term production risk or operational disruption, which may tighten near-term copper supply expectations and support copper prices.

title: Business Scoop » Call For Govt Buy-out Of Aluminium Smelter
summary: A political press release urges the government to buy the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter for $1 and convert it into a state-owned entity, funding upgrades including emissions controls. It argues this would prevent closure-related economic damage and maintain aluminium supply, which could support near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: Chilean copper giant Codelco records 3,215 cases of COVID-19; nine fatalities
summary: Codelco, Chile’s largest copper producer, reported 3,215 COVID-19 infections and nine deaths, with hundreds of employees recovering and 37 still hospitalized. As cases rise, pressure mounts to strengthen safety measures, potentially affecting production despite unions urging operations to pause around Calama.

title: London copper snaps six days of gains on rising coronavirus cases
summary: London copper ended a six-day rally as coronavirus cases rose, renewing fears of further lockdowns and weaker global demand. LME three-month copper fell 1.7% to $6,457.5/tonne, while Shanghai August copper slipped. Shanghai aluminium also declined, and LME nickel fell amid risk sentiment.

title: Copper giant Codelco records 3215 coronavirus cases among staff
summary: Chile’s Codelco reported 3,215 COVID-19 infections and nine deaths among staff, with production pressure rising as case numbers climb. While output has largely continued, unions and social groups urged possible operation halts around Calama and stronger safety measures, potentially threatening near-term copper supply.

title: China's copper concentrate imports rose 3% YoY in H1_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s copper ore and concentrate imports continued to fall month-to-month in June, but remained 3% higher year-on-year in H1. June imports totaled 1.59 million mt versus 1.69 million mt in May. Unwrought copper/semi-products imports also rose, up 25.2% YoY in H1.

title: Copper retreats from two-year high as U.S.-China tension flares
summary: Copper prices retreated from a two-year high as renewed U.S.-China tensions sparked fears of economic retaliation and prompted profit-taking. The article notes that LME three-month copper fell 1.8%. It also reports declines in LME nickel and Shanghai aluminium, despite firmer Chinese demand and a Chile supply-risk overhang.

title: Copper retreats from 2-year high as U.S.-China tension flares
summary: Copper prices fell Tuesday after flaring U.S.-China tensions raised retaliation and growth worries, triggering profit-taking. Still, the correction may be short-lived because China demand is firm, physical premiums in China rose, and Chile supply disruption concerns (Centinela strike vote) remain. Nickel and aluminium also moved lower on the day.

title: Rusal seeks management changes at Nickel Arctic after fuel spill | Companies
summary: Russian Rusal requested changes at Norilsk Nickel’s board, including relocating headquarters to Norilsk and overhauling environmental and safety policies after a fuel spill and other ecological accidents in the Arctic. The move signals heightened operational and compliance risk at nickel facilities, potentially pressuring nickel supply expectations.

title: Copper retreats from two-year peak as market eyes virus risks
summary: Copper prices fell after a prior surge to a two-year peak as investors responded to rising coronavirus cases and new California restrictions, alongside US-China friction over South China Sea claims. LME three-month copper dropped 1.4% and LME aluminium and nickel also declined, reflecting broader risk-off sentiment despite firm demand signals.

title: China's record crude oil, copper imports are more history lesson than predictor: Russell
summary: China’s June unwrought copper imports rose to a record 656,483 tonnes, aided by an arbitrage window created by cheap international copper prices relative to Shanghai. The incentive is fading as London copper recovers, which may stabilize imports after July. Overall, the spike is described as temporary rather than predictive.

title: Funds buy into a copper rally fueled by China and Chile: Andy Home
summary: Hedge funds are adding long exposure to copper, with CME net positioning the most bullish since 2018 and LME copper at a two-year high. Support comes from record China unwrought/refined import data and strengthening demand, while Chile’s supply is disrupted by Codelco COVID cases and potential labor actions, tightening availability.

title: Western Copper and Gold Announces Significant Resource Increase at Casino
summary: Western Copper and Gold announced a significant resource increase and favorable feasibility for its Casino copper-gold project in Yukon, including government funding for an access road and strategic investments. The updated project economics and copper resource scale support improved expectations for future copper supply over time, modestly bullish near-term sentiment.

title: Another Awful Arctic Accident By Russian Metals Giant Norilsk Nickel
summary: Norilsk Nickel said about 45 tons of aviation fuel spilled from an Arctic pipeline on July 12, adding to a recent run of environmental incidents. The company previously reported a 21,000-ton diesel spill from a Norilsk-operated power plant in May, highlighting potential disruption and compliance risk for nickel output.

title: Canada Nickel: Delivering the Next Generation of Nickel Sulfide Projects
summary: Canada Nickel highlights its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulfide project in Ontario’s Timmins mining camp, including a maiden resource estimate (~263 Mt at 0.31% nickel) and commencement of a PEA. The piece also links nickel demand to electric-battery use, potentially supporting near-term market sentiment for nickel.

title: Copper pulls back from two-year peak as market eyes virus risks
summary: Copper prices slipped from a two-year peak as markets turned cautious on renewed coronavirus risks and heightened US-China tensions. The move coincided with California restrictions and comments about potential sanctions. While Chile supply concerns had driven the rally, prices eased; LME aluminium and nickel also fell.

title: Copper edges higher on solid China demand, Chile supply risks
summary: Copper prices edged higher as solid China demand was evidenced by record June imports of unwrought copper, while potential strikes in Chile (the top producer) raised supply worries. However, rising U.S.-China trade tensions and global COVID-19 case spikes capped gains and clouded demand expectations.

title: Demand for copper and cobalt set to see rapid growth
summary: China’s “new infrastructure” plan—including EV charging piles, 5G stations, ultrahigh-voltage grids and intercity rail—could raise copper demand. Bloomberg Intelligence estimates 150,000 tons of copper, while State Grid projects 90,000 tons for charging piles plus additional copper needs for 5G and grid/rail infrastructure, supporting a near-term bullish tone for copper.

title: New Zealand aluminium smelter to close, axing 1,000 jobs
summary: Rio Tinto will close New Zealand Aluminium Smelters’ Tiwai Point smelter within 18 months, citing high energy costs and a challenging outlook for aluminium. The closure follows a reported hit from falling global aluminium prices and comes amid broader COVID-19-driven industrial slowdowns, weighing on aluminium market sentiment.

title: Copper advances as Chinese demand, Chile supply risks lend support
summary: Copper prices rose modestly as record-high Chinese unwrought copper imports signaled firm demand and potential strikes in Chile raised supply concerns. Gains were capped by worsening U.S.-China tensions after Trump moves on Hong Kong and by rising COVID cases and movement restrictions weighing on demand outlook.

title: Some gold, bauxite mines in Venezuelan Amazon run by criminal gangs - U.N.
summary: A UN investigation reports that criminal gangs largely control some gold, diamond and bauxite mines in Venezuela’s Amazon and that workers face exploitation and violence. It also says security and military forces fail to prevent crimes. The bauxite finding implies potential disruption to supply affecting aluminium/alumina expectations in coming weeks.

title: Saindak Project smeltery resumes production of copper on Monday--China Economic Net
summary: Saindak Project’s MCC smeltery in Balochistan resumed on July 9 after a nearly 10-month shutdown tied to lockdown and COVID-19 constraints. By July 13 it produced the first batch of crude copper, indicating the project is restarting full mining–beneficiation–smelting flow. Apparatus overhaul and health controls were required.

title: Copper slips on profit taking triggered by U.S.-China tensions
summary: Copper fell 0.3% on the LME, attributed to profit-taking after a sharp rally. U.S.-China political tensions triggered selling ahead of Thursday Chinese economic data on industrial output and investment. While demand indicators were strong and Chile disruption concerns supported prices, further gains were viewed as unlikely.

title: Clean Air Metals Announces New Drill Results from the Escape Lake Intrusion at Thunder Bay North, including 27.9m of 3.39ppm (g/t) Platinum and 4.67ppm (g/t) Palladium, 1.67% Copper, 0.90% Nickel
summary: Clean Air Metals announced new drill intercepts at its Thunder Bay North Escape Lake intrusion, including 1.67% copper and 0.90% nickel over 27.9m. The company frames results as progress toward outlining mineralization for a future resource estimate, but provides no production or inventory data.

title: Copper's 50% Pandemic Rally Isn't Scaring Bulls Away Just Yet
summary: Bloomberg reports copper up ~50% since March as COVID-19 disrupts production at major South American mines and China’s lockdown recovery drives record imports. Analysts cite stimulus and possible strategic reserve stockpiling as further support. Some traders say the surge may be partially priced in as demand weakens at high prices.

title: Copper steady after earlier losses prompted by U.S.-China tensions
summary: Copper steadied after earlier losses tied to U.S.-China tensions, trading up slightly on the LME ahead of Chinese manufacturing data. The piece cites strong recent demand indicators but limits further upside. It also highlights Chile COVID-related disruption/safety concerns and mentions marginal aluminium and nickel moves.

title: Wolf Administration: Poland-Based Manufacturer to Establish Aluminum Can Manufacturing Facility and North American Center of Excellence in Lackawanna County, Create Over 400 Jobs
summary: Pennsylvania’s administration announced plans by a Poland-based manufacturer to establish an aluminum can manufacturing facility and a North American center of excellence in Lackawanna County, creating over 400 jobs. The project signals incremental aluminum consumption for can production, which can lend near-term support to aluminum price expectations.

title: China's economic growth to boost copper production in Peru | News | ANDINA
summary: Buenaventura CEO Victor Gobitz said China’s growth will increase demand for copper and that the current crisis in Chile is supporting tighter supply. He expects Peru’s copper production to recover gradually as pandemic containment measures ease. The piece also notes copper prices rising above earlier 2020 lows.

title: Nifty Copper Mine, Pilbara, Western Australia
summary: Metals X’s Nifty copper project in Western Australia is moving from care-and-maintenance toward an open-pit redevelopment. A feasibility study (A$10m) is planned with drilling, alongside recommissioning of heap leach/SX-EW. If approved, the mine could restart integrated production and generate annual copper concentrate output.

title: hold for comment-Some gold, bauxite mines in Venezuelan Amazon run by criminal gangs - U.N.
summary: A UN investigation found criminal gangs largely control some Venezuelan Amazon gold, diamond and bauxite mines in the Orinoco Mining Arc. It alleges violence and lack of safeguards, urging Venezuela to regularize operations and meet environmental standards. The report links increased criminal presence with rising gold prices and expanding activity since 2015.

title: Aluminum can shortage: Beer, soda companies can't keep up with demand
summary: Beer and soda makers say aluminum can supply is in very tight condition as demand shifts to at-home multi-packs during COVID-19. Companies are limiting niche drinks and canmakers are adding capacity and sourcing globally. Producers cite capacity constraints for can manufacturing, not shortage of aluminum metal.

title: There Are Already Nationwide Shortages Of Aluminum Cans, Soda, Flour, Canned Soup, Pasta, & Rice
summary: The piece claims nationwide shortages are already affecting products packaged in aluminium cans, alongside other pantry staples. Such packaging shortages suggest aluminium supply constraints and tighter near-term availability for canstock, which can support aluminium prices in the coming days as buyers adjust to limited supply.

title: Alcoa Corp. stock rallies after aluminum producer posts narrower Q2 loss
summary: Alcoa shares jumped after the aluminum and alumina producer reported a narrower Q2 loss, slightly beat sales expectations, and noted lower production costs, stable shipments, and improved liquidity. It kept 2020 bauxite/alumina/aluminum shipment guidance and flagged higher Q3 aluminum results, despite higher energy costs in Australia.

title: Copper Scrap Trading was Particularly Affected by the COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: The piece says COVID-19 disrupted copper scrap trading, creating a scrap metal shortage. To compensate, China increased imports of copper cathode. This offset helped copper futures rebound above $6,000 by end-June, though the author expects cathode demand to ease if scrap markets recover.

title: Woodmac: Nickel to See Surplus in 2020, Lower Prices Ahead
summary: Wood Mackenzie says nickel’s YTD rebound is mostly sentiment rather than fundamentals. COVID-19 cut global demand and surplus forecasts replace prior deficits due to relatively resilient mining supply and strong Indonesian output (NPI, HPAL progress). With limited demand improvement over six months, Woodmac expects lower nickel prices.

title: Blackstone Generates New High Grade Nickel-copper-pge Target "Ta Cuong" at Ta Khoa
summary: Blackstone mobilises geophysics and plans EM-assisted drilling at the newly generated Ta Cuong massive sulfide prospect in the Ta Khoa district. Historic unassayed holes returned notable grades including ~0.66% Ni and 0.6% Cu and higher-incl. intervals. Follow-up drilling continues at Ban Chang and King Cobra discovery.

title: Blackstone Generates New High Grade Nickel-copper-pge Target "Ta Cuong" at Ta Khoa
summary: Blackstone announced commencement of exploration at the Ta Cuong MSV target in its Ta Khoa nickel-copper-PGE district, following geophysics and historical unassayed drill results. Reported grades include 0.66% Ni and 0.6% Cu over 15.6m, plus higher intervals. Drilling will use EM targeting to refine MSV plans and complement Ban Phuc and King Cobra.

title: London copper flat ahead of China economic data
summary: London copper was little changed as investors awaited China’s urban investment, industrial output, and GDP data for June/Q2, which could signal near-term demand. U.S.-China tensions and rising COVID-19 cases kept sentiment subdued. ShFE copper moved lower intraday, reflecting uncertainty ahead of the release.

title: SMM Morning Comments (Jul 16): Shanghai base metals extended decline, copper led the losses and dipped more than 2% _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals opened lower and extended losses, driven by risk aversion over COVID-19 and US-China tensions. Copper fell as much as ~2.8% in early trade, with nickel down >1% and aluminium down ~1.2%. LME also closed mostly weaker for copper, nickel, and aluminium.

title: Copper extends losses as doubts linger over China economic recovery
summary: London copper extended losses as concerns about China’s economic recovery and demand durability weighed on prospects for a rebound. Rising COVID-19 cases and U.S.-China tensions reduced expectations for metal consumption, dragging the market. Nickel and aluminium also fell, reflecting broader bearish sentiment across base metals.

title: Coalition split over Tiwai Point aluminium smelter's fate
summary: New Zealand’s coalition partners are split over the fate of the Rio Tinto-owned Tiwai Point aluminium smelter. The plant said production ends in 14 months, risking job losses. New Zealand First urges government action to “save” it, while Ardern emphasizes transitions and avoiding bailouts. The uncertainty affects aluminium supply expectations.

title: Despite spike in aluminium demand, China still a threat for India
summary: The piece argues that despite some demand recovery signals, China is raising aluminium production and supported by low-cost finance and energy, while global demand remains weak. It warns India may face higher imports and price pressure as Chinese surplus is redirected to world markets, keeping aluminium prices low.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 4,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s primary aluminium ingot social inventories fell to 708,000 mt as of July 16, down 4,000 mt week-on-week across eight consumption areas, including SHFE warrants. The drawdown continued but at a slower pace than the prior week, suggesting modest tightening.

title: Aluminium billet inventories fell for the second straight week_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s aluminium billet inventories fell for a second straight week as arrivals were limited and deliveries stayed high. Stocks across five consumption areas dropped 7,200 mt to 65,000 mt by July 16, after a prior 900 mt decrease. Foshan, Wuxi and Nanchang fell, while Changzhou rose slightly and Huzhou was steady.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 16/07: LME nickel price sinks 2% in lackluster morning trading; copper corrects in 0.8% downturn
summary: A live futures update shows LME nickel slipping 2% on lackluster trading and copper easing about 0.8% in a downturn. The piece also contains administrative pricing database and methodology update notes, but the only immediate market-move signals are the cited nickel and copper declines.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 16/07: LME nickel price sinks 2% in lackluster morning trading; copper corrects in 0.8% downturn
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures recap reports LME nickel prices down about 2% in lacklustre morning trading and copper about 0.8% lower on the day. The piece also includes administrative pricing-methodology notes but the only explicit price moves for tracked metals are bearish for nickel and copper.

title: Copper prices seen rising more, but so are risks - HKEX Forum
summary: HKEX forum speakers said tight supply and improving Chinese demand, supported by global stimulus liquidity, are likely to keep pushing copper higher in the second half of 2020. LME three-month copper hit a 25-month high this week and some expect peaks near $7,000, though risks of a fast reversal are also highlighted.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Acceleration of May 2020 Warrants
summary: Canada Nickel accelerated the expiry of May 2020 purchase warrants to August 21, 2020 to enable warrant exercise and raise additional capital. Proceeds are earmarked to advance its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project and complete a Preliminary Economic Analysis by year-end. The filing is financing-focused rather than an immediate supply shock.

title: Chinese-Backed Copper Exploration Plans in Myanmar Rekindle Fears
summary: Myanmar approved expanded copper exploration by PanAust Services (Myanmar) in Sagaing, with China links, after prior exploratory rights. Residents fear repeating Letpadaung-style land and pollution disputes involving Chinese firms. The state and company say activities are limited to sampling and land will shrink after five years.

title: Canada asks U.S. for patience, warns of reprisal in aluminum tariff spat
summary: Canada urged the U.S. to refrain from reimposing tariffs on Canadian raw aluminium, warning it would retaliate with duties if the U.S. “pulls the trigger.” The dispute centers on whether Canadian unalloyed aluminium imports rose after tariffs were lifted, and whether additional tariffs would hurt manufacturing recovery.

title: London copper dips as U.S.-China tensions weigh
summary: London copper dipped as heightened U.S.-China tensions raised worries of retaliatory measures that could curb economic growth and metal demand. Despite the intraday dip, the contract remains up for the week and in a nine-week run of gains. LME aluminum also eased amid broader risk sentiment.

title: SK Invests Additional 100 bln Won in Chinese Copper Foil Maker
summary: SK Invest reportedly plans to add 100 billion won in funding to a Chinese producer of copper foil. The investment is associated with expanding or supporting copper-foil manufacturing capacity. This can modestly improve near-term expectations for copper demand, but the scale and timing of output impact are unclear.

title: London copper set for first weekly drop in 9 on virus fears, U.S.-China tensions
summary: London copper is poised for its first weekly decline in nine weeks as worsening U.S.-China relations and rising COVID-19 infections raise fears of slower economic growth and weaker industrial demand. Fitch flags demand-side risks despite bullish longer-term factors. LME copper fell 0.6%; LME aluminum eased 0.7% as risk sentiment deteriorated.

title: Rio Says Copper Squeeze Could Worsen Amid Patchy Virus Rebound
summary: Rio Tinto says COVID disruptions have already cut 3%-4% of annual copper supply and could worsen amid a patchy virus rebound. Its own copper output fell 3% in Q2, while some mines operate at reduced rates. It also highlights aluminum sector weakness tied to demand from the pandemic and smelter sustainability concerns.

title: London copper falls as virus fears, U.S.-China woes raise demand worries
summary: London copper fell 0.2% as U.S.-China tensions and rising COVID infections raised concerns about global economic recovery and industrial metal demand. The U.S. may consider restricting travel for Chinese Communist Party members. Fitch cited second-wave risks to commodity demand. Aluminium eased; nickel showed a surplus.

title: 15th China International Copper Industry Chain Conference: COVID to send global copper output into a 0.3% decline in 2020_SMM
summary: SMM’s Jianhua Ye said COVID-19 will reduce global copper mine production by 0.3% in 2020, cutting copper ore output by about 450,000 mt. Supply disruptions hit China’s smelters via falling treatment charges and lower scrap imports, while cathode output growth slows. Fundamentals point to higher copper prices.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for 2nd week in closed import window_SMM
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for a second consecutive week, increasing by 2,500 mt to 212,500 mt by July 17. The rise is attributed to limited flows into the domestic market while the import arbitrage window remained closed. Weaker cathode demand and softer sentiment toward tightness also contributed.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks rose 800 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks rose 800 mt to 17,300 mt as of July 17, the fifth straight weekly increase. The closed import arbitrage window and a domestic low season limited demand, while forward cargo arrivals drove the buildup, suggesting bearish near-term pressure for nickel prices.

title: Zambia rejects copper mine's suspension plan
summary: Zambia’s mines ministry rejected Glencore’s Mopani Copper Mines proposal to suspend operations due to low copper prices and COVID-19 disruptions. Mopani said it will appeal but continue mining. The minister stated the government wants Mopani running and noted steps to cut expatriate staffing and address high production costs.

title: Copper retreats on virus fears and U.S.-China friction
summary: Copper fell from two-year highs as concerns over rising coronavirus infections and worsening U.S.-China relations threatened demand and the recovery narrative. Three-month LME copper dropped 0.2%. The piece also notes aluminium easing 0.9% and nickel down 1.1%, reflecting broader risk-off sentiment.

title: Zambia's mines minister rejects Glencore copper mine's suspension plan
summary: Zambia’s mines minister rejected Mopani Copper Mines’ proposal to suspend operations due to low copper prices and Covid-19 supply-chain disruptions. Mopani says it will appeal and continue mining through the process. The decision follows prior shutdowns and government pressure to restart operations after criticism.

title: Copper steady but virus fears and U.S.-China friction weigh
summary: Copper held near two-year highs, supported by supply worries including Chile disruption and strong quarterly output from Rio Tinto, plus tight cash vs three-month pricing. However, soaring U.S. COVID-19 cases and potential U.S.-China travel restrictions pressured prices and risked overheating. Aluminium and nickel declined as sentiment weakened.

title: App Will Track Harmful Dust from Bauxite Mining in Guinea | Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory
summary: Columbia researchers are developing an app for Guinean communities to monitor fugitive dust from bauxite mining, transport, and processing. The article describes heavy bauxite export flows from Guinea’s Boké region and outlines dust-control practices, but the project is mainly aimed at accountability and data collection rather than immediate supply changes.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 50,000 wmt to 7.83 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories across Chinese ports fell by 50,000 wmt to 7.83 million wmt between July 10 and July 17. Nickel-in-content stocks dropped 400 mt to 63,400 mt. Stocks at seven major ports also fell 50,000 wmt to 6.62 million wmt.

title: Michael Cullen: No crocodile tears for Tiwai Point aluminium smelter
summary: The article discusses New Zealand politics in the lead-up to the election and specifically addresses the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter. By framing government/public reactions to the smelter, it signals potential operational implications for aluminium supply, which can influence short-term aluminium price expectations.

title: Big News Roundup: Western Copper and Gold Increases Casino Resource, Brixton Metals Reveals Drill Results at Hog Heaven, Nextleaf Solutions Granted 40th Patent, Amex Drills Bonanza-Grade Hole at Perron, RAMM Pharma Receives Approval for Epifractán In Peru
summary: Western Copper and Gold increased the resource estimate at its Casino copper-gold project, adding copper in measured/indicated categories alongside inferred gold. The roundup also references additional nickel-copper-PGE mineralization at another Swedish project, but no near-term production changes are described.

title: Financial condition of Hindustan Copper in 'dire straits', says CMD
summary: Hindustan Copper’s CMD said the PSU’s finances are in “dire straits,” worsened by COVID-19 and prior poor performance. The company aims to make up a 2020-21 production shortfall and pursue capacity expansion, with clearances sought for 12 MT as the first phase. It produced about four million tonnes of copper ore and reported quarterly losses in 2019-20.

title: Hindustan Copper needs optimisation, cost cutting to survive: CMD
summary: Hindustan Copper’s CMD said the company is in worse condition due to weak FY2019-20 performance and the Covid-19 pandemic. He urged optimization and cost cutting across operations, and employees to work to make up a FY2020-21 production shortfall and explore alternative revenue, for survival.

title: Copper falls on rising Chinese inventories, coronavirus fears
summary: Copper prices fell after Chinese warehouse inventories rose sharply, while WHO-reported record COVID-19 case growth raised concerns about economic recovery and demand. ShFE copper stocks climbed to a multi-month high. Nickel also declined on higher inventories, while LME aluminum rose slightly.

title: 2020 China Stainless Steel Forum: China's nickel ore imports from the Philippines to drop 20.4% in 2020_SMM
summary: SMM expects China’s laterite nickel ore imports from the Philippines to fall 20.4% in 2020 to 35 million wmt as COVID-19 delays deliveries. Lower supply, compounded by Indonesia’s 2020 export ban, is expected to reduce Chinese nickel ore stockpiles. Philippine ore prices rose to about $47.5/wmt.

title: Sumitomo posts $513 mln impairment loss for Ambatovy nickel, cobalt asset
summary: Sumitomo reported a $513 million impairment loss for its Ambatovy nickel, cobalt asset. The write-down suggests problems with the asset’s outlook and could imply tighter or less reliable nickel supply/investment plans, which may pressure near-term nickel price expectations downward.

title: Aluminum Cans Are In Short Supply Due To the Pandemic And This Is Why... | 98.1 The Breeze
summary: The article says aluminum cans may face a shortage as consumers shift from bars and restaurants to drinking at home during the coronavirus pandemic. Grocery and curbside sales of canned beer, cider and wine are reported to be growing faster than expected, with soda can sales up 30% in March-April.

title: Refinitiv: There's Still Upside Potential for Copper Prices in Q3
summary: Refinitiv says copper rebounded from March lows and still has upside potential in Q3. It attributes support to tight and tightening mine supply (especially Chile) and stronger-than-expected Chinese demand from restocking and scrap shortages, while flagging COVID-19 second-wave and trade-sentiment risks that could increase volatility or cause sharp pullbacks.

title: Shanghai copper rises on COVID-19 vaccine, stimulus hopes
summary: Shanghai copper advanced on Tuesday, with the most-traded August ShFE contract up 0.8% to 51,830 yuan/t, driven by hopes for EU stimulus and early positive COVID-19 vaccine trial data. It also cited rising case numbers as a risk, while other metals showed mixed moves.

title: Operating rates across secondary aluminium makers edged lower in June_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s secondary aluminium operating rate fell to 48.0% in June, down 0.7 pp m/m and 4.3 pp y/y, mainly due to more imported alloy ingot arrivals and weak downstream demand amid scrap shortages. July operations are expected to stay stable, supported by overseas demand recovery from Japan.

title: Copper edges up on EU stimulus deal, coronavirus vaccine hopes
summary: Copper rose on Tuesday after EU leaders agreed a major stimulus package and early coronavirus vaccine trial data boosted hopes for faster global recovery. LME August copper gained while aluminum and nickel also edged up. Gains were limited by rising virus cases and uncertainty over vaccine outcomes, keeping sentiment cautious.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 21/07: EU recovery fund bolsters LME base metals complex; nickel leads the way
summary: The live futures report notes that an EU recovery fund is supporting the LME base metals complex, with nickel outperforming. It also discusses conditions affecting aluminium supply and logistics, including disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, suggesting near-term support for aluminium and broader base metals sentiment.

title: Russian river turns orange from copper mine waste
summary: Drone footage shows a Russian Ural river turning orange from runoff linked to the former Levikhinsky copper pyrite mine, closed in 2004. Authorities are investigating potential environmental violations related to neutralizing acidic mining water. They say the contamination is not a threat to residents’ drinking supplies. Immediate copper price effects appear limited.

title: COVID-19 Impact and Recovery Analysis | Copper Mining Industry Procurement Intelligence Report Forecasts Spend Growth of Over USD 4 Billion
summary: SpendEdge’s press release forecasts spend growth in the global copper mining industry and discusses COVID-19 impacts on procurement, including potential inflation in suppliers’ operating costs from raw materials and wages. The article is more about procurement strategy and spend outlook than immediate, quantifiable changes to copper supply or demand.

title: Financialization of Copper Mining in Chile
summary: The article focuses on Chilean copper mining during Covid-19, highlighting COVID cases and conflict between unions and operators. It reports votes for strikes at Antofagasta’s Zaldivar and Centinela mines and argues labor action has helped lift copper prices to a two-year high, suggesting short-term supply concerns.

title: Roskill: Partial Demand Recovery to Support Nickel Prices in H2
summary: Roskill says COVID-19 disruptions reduced global nickel mining and refining in H1, implying slightly lower primary refined nickel supply in 2020. Despite surplus pressures and stock build earlier, it expects a partial nickel demand recovery in H2, especially from China, supporting prices while watching Indonesia NPI outbreak risk.

title: Copper rises on weaker dollar, EU stimulus
summary: Copper prices rose as the U.S. dollar weakened and after the EU approved a large stimulus package. LME three-month copper gained 0.8%. The International Copper Study Group cited a widening April refined copper deficit, while the cash-to-3-month spread widened, signaling tight nearby supplies. Aluminium premiums increased and nickel edged up.

title: Authorities seek identity of alleged copper thief
summary: Authorities in Shreveport, Louisiana are seeking an alleged thief accused of stealing copper parts from air-conditioning units at Northside Elementary School. The theft involved parts from 45 AC units and caused about $45,000 in damage. Crime Stoppers is offering rewards and sharing surveillance images.

title: Top Nickel-producing Countries | Indonesia is First
summary: The article discusses global nickel production, emphasizing Indonesia’s rapid rise to over half of output. It states nickel prices have been trending down since May 2024 due to weak usage paired with strong Indonesian supply, contributing to oversupply. It also notes quota cuts and market headwinds in the short term.

title: Spot copper premiums in Shanghai fell amid subdued trades, higher futures_SMM
summary: Shanghai spot copper cathode premiums fell sharply on subdued trading as sellers increased destocking to lock in profits on a two-day copper futures rally. Downstream buyers stayed cautious about restocking while standard-grade premiums dropped versus SHFE August. Hydro and lower-quality discounts widened, signaling weaker physical demand.

title: Copper advances as weaker dollar attracts buyers, EU pumps stimulus
summary: Copper prices rose after a weaker U.S. dollar attracted buyers and following the EU’s 750 billion euro coronavirus recovery stimulus. Reuters cites a larger refined copper deficit and tighter nearby supplies (higher cash-to-three-month spread). It also reports recovering aluminium demand via rising U.S. premiums, while nickel edged lower.

title: Antofagasta copper, gold production fall
summary: Antofagasta reported lower copper output for Q2, with copper production down 8.4% year-on-quarter to 177,700 mt and copper sales down 8.4% to 178,900 tons, attributed to pandemic-related mining disruptions. The company reaffirmed its annual guidance, but the near-term supply drop is bearish for copper.

title: OZ Minerals hikes copper, gold targets as prices run hot
summary: Oz Minerals raised its full-year copper production targets after better first-half results at Prominent Hill and Carrapateena. It attributes copper strength to China demand hopes and COVID-related supply problems across South America, where reduced workforce levels have raised concerns about output. Chile and Peru disruptions further support sentiment for copper.

title: Renforth Resources Inc.: Exploration Resumes on Renforth's Copper/Silver Discovery at Malartic West
summary: Renforth Resources says exploration has resumed on its Beaupré copper/silver discovery at the Malartic West property in Quebec. Management cites prior surface sampling extending mineralization to about 165m and plans further work. The release contains no data on production, inventories, or refined supply impacting copper near term.

title: Blackstone notches up more Vietnam nickel hits
summary: Blackstone Minerals reports further high-grade massive sulphide intersections at its Ban Chang deposit in Vietnam’s Ta Khoa nickel-copper-PGM project. Results show higher nickel grades with associated copper and by-products, potentially feeding its mothballed Ban Phuc concentrator. The company expects work to support upcoming scoping and resource studies.

title: Blackstone Intersects 200M Long High-Grade Nickel-Copper-PGE Zone At Ban Chang
summary: Blackstone Mineral reported high-grade intersections at Ban Chang in Vietnam, including ~0.92–1.6% Ni and ~0.69–1.09% Cu over drill intervals, confirming a 200m-long massive sulfide zone. Assays are pending for other holes as drilling expands across additional Ta Khoa targets.

title: Blackstone Intersects 200M Long High-Grade Nickel-Copper-PGE Zone At Ban Chang
summary: Blackstone reports maiden drill-hole results at Ban Chang showing a 200m-long zone of high-grade nickel-copper massive sulfide, including up to 0.92% Ni and 0.69% Cu over 4.1m. Additional drilling across the Ta Khoa nickel-copper-PGE district continues, improving future supply expectations.

title: Copper's scrappy post-collapse recovery - The Globe and Mail
summary: Copper prices have rebounded as demand improved and supply stresses persist, but the article highlights a major additional driver: a COVID-era collapse in copper scrap availability. With scrap collection, processing and shipping disrupted—and China’s import regime still restrictive—hundreds of thousands of tonnes of contained copper supply have effectively vanished.

title: Copper price surges to two-year high
summary: Copper futures surged to a two-year high after agreement on a major European economic stimulus plan and rising optimism around a Covid-19 vaccine. Trading also reflected continuing worries about pandemic-related supply disruptions from South America’s top producers, supporting expectations of tighter near-term availability.

title: Antofagasta copper output steady despite Covid-19
summary: Chilean miner Antofagasta said it delivered copper volumes in the second quarter 5% ahead of expectations, even while Chile grapples with Covid-19. The quarter’s output was still 8.4% lower than the prior period, but the beat versus forecasts supports near-term copper supply sentiment.

title: Norilsk Nickel to hold independent expert review of fuel spill
summary: Norilsk Nickel said it will appoint ERM for an independent expert review of a large diesel fuel spill at CHPP-3 in Norilsk, including causes, remedial actions, and other environmental issues. The spill involved 21,000+ tonnes after a tank collapse, with reports planned for internal stakeholders.

title: Copper Could Reach US$6,800 in 2020 as Fundamentals Improve
summary: Capital Economics forecasts copper could rise toward US$6,800/tonne in 2020, expecting slower but continued gains in Q3 after a 26%+ jump in Q2. The firm cites an improved fundamental outlook: resilient mined supply and a demand rebound led by China’s infrastructure stimulus, with second-wave risks mainly tempered.

title: Copper slips on rising U.S.-China tensions
summary: Copper prices fell as U.S.-China tensions raised fears of retaliation. LME three-month copper was down 0.3% and ShFE September copper slid 1%. The article also notes LME aluminum and nickel declined, consistent with broader risk-off market sentiment affecting industrial metals.

title: Copper declines as escalating Sino-U.S. tensions weigh
summary: Copper prices fell as rising U.S.-China tensions, sparked by moves to close consulates, dampened sentiment and increased concerns over retaliation. Reuters cites the September LME/Shanghai price decline and notes nickel weakened while aluminium edged higher, suggesting the primary immediate pressure was on copper.

title: 'Please mine more nickel,' Musk urges as Tesla boosts production
summary: Elon Musk urges increased nickel mining as Tesla ramps up production. The message implies higher near-term demand for nickel feedstock, typically used in battery supply chains, which can tighten expectations for availability and support nickel prices in the short run.

title: Copper falls as Sino-U.S. tensions rise
summary: Copper prices dropped as Sino-U.S. tensions rose after the U.S. moved to shut China’s consulate in Houston, prompting Beijing to consider retaliatory action. The September Shanghai contract fell 0.9% and LME copper eased earlier. Aluminium edged up, while ShFE nickel declined in the same session.

title: China's aluminium imports jump to 11-year high on lower overseas prices
summary: China’s June aluminium imports jumped over 490% year-on-year to the highest in 11 years, driven by cheaper overseas prices versus domestic values. The widening Shanghai-London spread created arbitrage flows into China, while exports fell, leaving China a large net exporter earlier in 2020. This import surge supports aluminium sentiment.

title: 'Please mine more nickel,' Musk urges as Tesla boosts production | Reuters | Business
summary: Elon Musk urged for more nickel mining as Tesla boosts production, according to the Reuters Business headline. The message suggests rising near-term nickel demand tied to EV battery supply, supporting expectations for tighter availability and upward pressure on nickel prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: 'Please mine more nickel,' Musk urges as Tesla boosts production | WTAQ News Talk | 97.5 FM · 1360 AM
summary: Elon Musk urged nickel miners to boost environmentally sensitive, efficient production to support Tesla’s growing EV and solar output, emphasizing nickel’s role in battery energy density. Despite the call for more supply, traders and analysts said the market is in surplus, so prices are unlikely to move meaningfully short term.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose after two weeks of decline_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM says China’s aluminium billet inventories rose to 68,600 mt as of July 23, up 3,600 mt from a week earlier after two straight weeks of declines. The increase was attributed to stronger arrivals and smaller warehouse shipments across major consumption regions, with only Changzhou declining slightly.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 6,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots across eight consumption areas fell 6,000 mt to 702,000 mt as of July 23. The decline followed a 4,000 mt drop the prior week, indicating continued drawdowns that may tighten short-term supply conditions.

title: Copper rises as declining LME stockpiles tighten market
summary: Copper prices rose after LME stockpiles fell to about one-fifth of their level two months ago. On-warrant inventories dropped to 55,950 tonnes and the cash-to-three-month spread jumped to a 16-month high, signaling tighter nearby supply. Macro commentary and production/union headlines were secondary supports.

title: Aluminum Mills, Can Makers at Odds Over Tariff Exemptions
summary: U.S. aluminum mills and can-sheet makers disagree over tariff exclusion rules that allow importers to bypass the 10% duty on aluminum when products are deemed unavailable domestically. Exclusions for billions of pounds have risen, lifting can-sheet and other product imports and sparking concern of weaker domestic pricing, amid pandemic-driven demand shifts.

title: Some U.S. Aluminum Mills Want Changes In Tariff Exclusion Policies
summary: U.S. aluminum mills are urging the Commerce Department to change or halt tariff exclusion policies. The department has granted exclusions on billions of pounds of imported aluminium, and producers say this is increasing imports and squeezing domestic margins. The process is under review amid rising can-sheet and other product imports.

title: Tesla pitches "giant contract" to responsible nickel miners – The Northern Miner
summary: Tesla boss Elon Musk is asking responsible nickel miners to produce more nickel and has offered a “giant contract” for a long period to firms able to supply it. The move is intended to secure battery-grade nickel demand for Tesla electric vehicles, supporting bullish nickel price expectations.

title: US launches anti-dumping probe into Vietnamese copper products | Tuoi Tre News
summary: Vietnam confirmed the US Department of Commerce launched an anti-dumping investigation on seamless refined copper pipes and tubes imported from Vietnam, with a stated dumping margin of 111.82%. A preliminary determination is expected in December. Potential duties or reduced imports can affect near-term copper product supply into the US.

title: First coins, now aluminum cans? Why some beer may be hard to find
summary: The article says beer and other drinks in aluminum cans could be scarce due to a shortage of aluminum cans. Breweries like Molson Coors are reportedly reducing variety to focus on top sellers. The can shortage is attributed to pandemic-era shifts toward at-home canned beverages and rising hard seltzer demand.

title: Rio suffers fresh blow to Mongolian copper project
summary: Rio Tinto said its Oyu Tolgoi Mongolian copper project received another setback after a review of mine plans raised concerns about the underground expansion. The revised plan cut copper reserves by 15% and gold reserves by 17%, adding to previously disclosed multibillion-dollar cost overruns.

title: 'Please mine more nickel,' Elon Musk urges as Tesla boosts production
summary: Elon Musk urged miners to produce more nickel as Tesla ramps truck and solar projects that use nickel-rich battery chemistry. While EV demand growth supports longer-term expectations, traders say prices likely won’t move soon because the market remains in surplus and miners may not add volumes quickly or profitably.

title: Tesla Looks To Incentivize Nickel Miners With Massive Contract
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk is offering a large long-term contract to secure additional nickel supply for electric-vehicle batteries, citing cell production as a growth constraint and moving toward reduced cobalt use. The move boosts expectations for nickel demand even as recent nickel prices are near historic lows, with tight supply risks discussed.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 250,000 wmt to 8.08 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports increased by 250,000 wmt to 8.08 million wmt between July 17 and July 24. In nickel content terms, stocks rose 1,900 mt to 65,300 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also climbed to 6.66 million wmt.

title: Tesla boss Musk's desire for more nickel could be a non-starter: Andy Home
summary: Elon Musk called for more nickel mines for EV batteries, briefly lifting LME nickel. However, the article argues the broader stainless steel market is weak, with large refined surpluses, plentiful LME stocks and contango, and declining stainless output. Net effect is continued bearish sentiment for nickel.

title: Elon Musk's call for more nickel production could be a non-starter
summary: Elon Musk urged more nickel mining for EV batteries, briefly lifting LME nickel prices, but the article stresses weak fundamentals. It cites a growing refined nickel surplus, abundant LME inventories and contango, and a coronavirus hit to stainless steel output, nickel’s dominant demand driver, supporting bearish near-term pricing.

title: Elon Musk pledges "giant contract" for sustainable nickel miners
summary: Elon Musk said Tesla would offer long-term “giant contracts” to companies that can sustainably and efficiently extract nickel for its battery supply chain. Reuters notes Tesla may prefer higher-grade nickel sulphide. The article links EV battery growth to rising nickel demand, even as nickel remains below past peaks.

title: Elon Musk sends nickel soaring after urging more production, offering 'giant' contract
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk urged nickel producers to mine and produce more nickel and floated a “giant” long-term contract for efficient, environmentally sensitive supply. The call triggered a sharp reaction in nickel markets, with LME nickel up 4.5% to close at $13,689/t, reflecting strong near-term demand expectations.

title: RPT-COLUMN-Tesla boss Musk's desire for more nickel could be a non-starter: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist Andy Home says Elon Musk’s push for more nickel mines for EV batteries met a reality check as nickel prices are pressured by expectations of refined oversupply. INSG data point to surplus, high LME stocks and contango, suggesting the stainless-steel-linked demand backdrop limits sustained price gains despite a brief market spike.

title: Zaldivar Copper Miners Accept Wage Deal, Averting Chile Strike
