summary: Zaldivar copper miners in Chile accepted a wage deal, preventing a planned strike. By averting a potential work stoppage, the update lowers expectations of near-term copper supply disruption. That reduction in tail-risk around output can pressure copper prices downward over the next days.

title: Workers, Antofagasta reach labor deal at Chile´s Zaldivar copper mine, strike averted
summary: Workers at Antofagasta’s Zaldivar copper mine in northern Chile reached a labor contract deal, averting a potential walk-off. The mediation followed salary and benefits disputes intensified during Chile’s coronavirus outbreak. The mine contributes roughly 2% of Chile’s annual copper production, lowering disruption risk.

title: UNION OF WORKERS AT ZALDIVAR COPPER MINE IN CHILE ACCEPTS ANTOFAGASTA´S CONTRACT OFFER, STRIKE CALLED OFF - UNION
summary: A union at Chile’s Zaldivar copper mine accepted Antofagasta’s contract offer, and the strike was called off. The development lowers the probability of near-term production stoppages at the mine, supporting expectations for steadier copper supply in the coming days and weeks.

title: Rise in canned beer sales puts local breweries in bind amid aluminum shortage
summary: Canned beer demand is rising, but local and major brewers report an aluminum can shortage. Molson Coors and others are cutting beer types to focus on top brands. Brewers and a retailer say aluminum can prices have climbed about 30% and 12-pack sales have doubled, reflecting constrained packaging availability.

title: China's June U.S. copper concentrate imports hit highest since Sept 2018
summary: China’s June imports of U.S. copper concentrate rose to 30,734 tonnes, the highest since Sept 2018, after exemptions allowed some cargoes despite earlier China-U.S. tensions. The escalation in trade and consulate actions coincides with new shipments reaching Zhejiang and Fujian, supporting near-term concentrate supply for smelting.

title: Nationwide aluminum can shortage could impact local breweries
summary: A WBRC report says demand for aluminum cans has surged as more consumers drink at home during the pandemic, disrupting beer distribution from kegs to retail. It cites a nationwide aluminum can shortage affecting breweries’ ability to launch new products, with potential spillover to soda cans as supply chains remain strained.

title: China's June U.S. copper concentrate imports hit highest since Sept 2018 | Reuters | Business
summary: China’s June imports of U.S. copper concentrate reportedly hit the highest level since Sept 2018, signaling a surge in Chinese demand for copper feedstock. Tighter concentrate supply can support higher copper prices over the coming days and weeks as smelters secure material.

title: Antofagasta : Supervisors at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine in Chile agree to extend negotiations - union
summary: Supervisors’ union at Antofagasta’s Centinela copper mine agreed to extend mandatory mediation for one business day, seeking a revised contract proposal. If no agreement is reached, a strike would begin the following Tuesday. Centinela produced 276,600 tonnes of copper last year, making output disruption a near-term risk.

title: Some beer varieties may take a hit due to aluminum can shortage
summary: A reported aluminum can shortage is affecting beer and soda makers, prompting brewers to reduce the number of smaller brands and focus output on their biggest labels to avoid can stockouts. The piece cites rising demand for canned beverages and storage preferences, linking aluminium packaging constraints to immediate market pressure.

title: Alaska Gold and Copper Mine Moves Ahead after Impact Study
summary: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers issued a final environmental impact statement clearing Northern Dynasty Minerals’ proposed Alaska mine, finding no measurable effect on fish numbers. The project would include copper production. Despite continued environmental opposition, the permit process progressing this year supports improved near-term outlook for copper supply expectations.

title: Wisconsin Breweries Dealing with Aluminum Can Shortage
summary: Wisconsin breweries and soda makers report a nationwide aluminum can shortage. Demand for canned beer and other drinks surged during COVID-era home consumption, while shipping and supply couldn’t keep up. Companies are producing more and sourcing cans from abroad, pointing to tighter aluminium demand conditions.

title: China buys more US copper concentrate
summary: The article headline says China bought more US copper concentrate. That implies higher near-term demand for copper feedstock, improving refiners’ material availability and tightening the concentrate market. Such buying typically supports expectations for copper supply tightness and can lift short-term copper prices, while having no direct effect on nickel or aluminium.

title: Alaska Gold and Copper Mine Project Moves Forward, Despite Environmentalist Objections
summary: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers issued a final environmental impact statement saying the proposed Alaska Pebble mine would not measurably affect fish, clearing the way for permits. The project is designed to produce copper and gold, easing supply-permitting uncertainty and supporting copper sentiment near term.

title: Don Lindsay: Copper's unusual antimicrobial property gives it a part to play in the battle against COVID-19
summary: An opinion piece says copper surfaces can inactivate COVID-19 and related pathogens, citing studies showing shorter survival on copper than on plastic or stainless steel. It describes copper antimicrobial installations in healthcare and public settings (e.g., hospitals, subways, an Ontario auto plant), potentially supporting near-term copper demand sentiment.

title: London copper gains as weaker U.S. dollar draws buyers
summary: London copper rose 0.3% to $6,431.50/tonne as a weaker U.S. dollar attracted buyers. Upside was limited by worries over potential Chile labor strikes, though Antofagasta avoided a strike and mediation continued. The piece also shows modest gains in LME aluminium and stronger nickel.

title: China primary aluminium imports in June surged more than 40 times YoY_SMM
summary: China’s primary aluminium imports jumped 4060% YoY to 123,500 mt in June as traders increased purchases on lower overseas prices. Imports rose 574% from May. Alumina imports also climbed to a multi-year high (422,600 mt) in June, indicating stronger input demand for aluminium production.

title: China copper inventory grew for four straight weeks_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that China’s copper cathode inventories in Shanghai, Guangdong and Jiangsu (including SHFE-approved warehouses) rose 15,700 mt from July 17 to 255,900 mt as of July 24. It was the fourth straight week of increases, though the weekly pace slowed. Separate regional moves offset each other.

title: London copper advances as investors eye U.S. stimulus bill
summary: London copper rose about 0.5% on U.S. stimulus relief-deal hopes, as investors anticipated improving economic and metals demand prospects. Gains were limited by signs of weak Chinese downstream purchasing and concerns over China demand. The report also shows smaller advances in LME aluminium and nickel.

title: 5 Top Weekly TSX Stocks: Musk Asks for Metal, Nickel Stocks Rise
summary: The article highlights large gains among TSX mining stocks tied to nickel, especially Talon Metals and Sherritt. It attributes the momentum partly to Elon Musk’s call for miners to “mine more nickel” for Tesla’s long-term supply of battery material, which may boost near-term expectations for nickel demand.

title: 'No compromise on nickel ban': Ministry puts foot down on nickel price floor - Business
summary: Indonesia’s ministry says it will not compromise on the nickel ore export ban and will sanction firms that fail to follow government-pegged nickel ore pricing rules (HPM). Nickel smelters must buy ore at HPM-linked prices while miners face export restrictions, increasing pressure to comply and potentially supporting nickel pricing.

title: Rising Copper Prices are a Double Edged Sword for UK Broadband
summary: The piece notes copper briefly hit a two-year high and argues the higher copper value could encourage UK telecoms to remove retired copper cables in favor of FTTP fibre. It also warns of metal theft risks and says removal is gradual, so copper price changes may be less central than migration planning.

title: Capstone to Expand Leaching at Pinto Valley; 300 to 350 MIbs of Low-Cost, Copper Cathode Production Potential
summary: Capstone says its Pinto Valley dump leach partnership with Jetti’s catalytic technology has improved economics, doubling copper cathode production per area irrigated in the first year. The company plans to expand leaching activity to access residuals and high-grade waste, targeting 300–350 million lbs of cathode over two decades and boosting use of underutilized SX-EW capacity.

title: En+ warns of hit to performance from weaker aluminium, power prices  | 27 July 2020
summary: En+ warned that performance could be hit by weaker aluminium and also cited power prices. This ties the near-term outlook for aluminium production costs and operating conditions to changing aluminium price expectations, which could weigh on sentiment for aluminium within coming days.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Samples Up to 2.43% Nickel and 8.34 Grams/Tonne Gold in the Northern Athabasca Region, Saskatchewan
summary: ALX Resources reports rock-sample results from its Falcon Nickel, Flying Vee, and Gibbons Creek projects in northern Saskatchewan, including up to 2.43% nickel and up to 0.43% copper, plus high-grade gold and associated minerals. The news is exploration-stage and does not indicate immediate production changes.

title: Auto parts makers shine spotlight on aluminum's role in electric vehicles
summary: The piece argues that EV adoption is quickly shifting auto supply chains toward aluminium for lightweight structures and battery housings. It cites growth expectations, large deliveries by Norsk Hydro, and specific vehicle-component contracts in Europe. Overall, the new aluminium demand outlook is portrayed as a near-term tailwind for prices.

title: Global Aluminum Extrusion Market Analysis Highlights the Impact of COVID-19 2020-2024 | Increasing Demand for Aluminum Extrusion in Automotive Industry to Boost Market Growth
summary: Technavio’s press release analyzes the aluminum extrusion market’s growth (CAGR ~4% for 2020-2024), highlighting rising demand from automotive and solar energy applications. title: Canada Nickel aims for zero-carbon emissions at Crawford nickel project
summary: Canada Nickel says it is targeting zero-carbon emissions at its Crawford nickel project. Together, the signals support improved nickel supply expectations and potential demand momentum, which can underpin near-term nickel prices.

title: Auto parts makers shine spotlight on aluminium's role in electric vehicles | News
summary: Reuters reports that aluminium’s role in electric vehicles is expanding, supported by lightweighting needs and growing production allocations by companies like Norsk Hydro, Constellium and Nemak. Analysts expect higher aluminium usage per EV versus ICE cars and rising demand estimates, creating supportive sentiment for aluminium prices as EV demand accelerates in Europe and China.

title: Elon Musk's nickel supply challenge for Tesla batteries answered by Canada miners
summary: Elon Musk urged miners to produce more nickel for Tesla’s battery supply, stressing efficiency and environmental standards. Canada Nickel said it plans a zero-carbon nickel processing facility in Ontario, powered by nearby hydro, aiming to meet this demand. The news ties near-term EV battery growth expectations to nickel demand.

title: Auto parts makers shine spotlight on aluminium's role in electric vehicles
summary: The piece argues EVs are rapidly increasing aluminium’s share in vehicles due to lightweighting needs and higher aluminium content versus internal combustion cars. It cites production ramp plans, large auto supply contracts, and estimates of rising EV-related aluminium demand, implying supportive near-term expectations for aluminium prices.

title: Freeport-McMoRan has strong year ahead thanks to copper, gold prices, analyst says
summary: An analyst said Freeport-McMoRan’s outlook is supported by increased copper production and anticipated longer-term strength in copper prices. After Q2 earnings beat expectations amid Covid-19 cost cuts, the note mentions U.S.-China trade tensions could modestly reverse copper prices, but expects limited duration beyond the short term.

title: Copper, base metals rise as U.S. stimulus hopes lift sentiment
summary: Copper and other industrial metals rose after U.S. stimulus hopes boosted risk sentiment and pushed the dollar to a two-year low, making dollar-priced metals cheaper for other-currency buyers. It also cites positive vaccine trial progress and reports nickel gains alongside copper increases.

title: China's nickel ore imports doubled in June as supply from the Philippines recovered_SMM
summary: China’s nickel ore and concentrate imports rose sharply in June, more than doubling month on month to 3.45 million mt. The Philippines recovery lifted supply, while New Caledonia also increased. Such higher inbound feedstock availability signals less near-term nickel ore tightness for refiners.

title: London copper advances as investors eye U.S. stimulus package
summary: London copper rose 0.5% on Tuesday as investors priced in a proposed $1 trillion U.S. coronavirus aid package, boosting risk sentiment and weakening the dollar. Vaccine trial progress added support. Chile’s Centinela copper mine avoided a strike through contract talks, reinforcing copper firmness.

title: Omaha brewery prepares for aluminum can shortage
summary: Brickway Brewery & Distillery in Omaha says increased home drinking is driving an aluminum can shortage. The brewery stopped buying pre-labeled grocery cans months ago and switched to sourcing generic cans for relabeling. The owner expects pre-labeled cans to run out within weeks, raising per-can costs.

title: Your Favorite Beer May Go Out of Stock Due To Aluminum Shortage
summary: The article says the US is facing an aluminum can shortage affecting beer availability. It attributes the problem to reduced keg supply during shutdowns and a shift toward retail cans, alongside a spike in alcohol sales that is tightening aluminum demand for packaging.

title: Elon Musk, Stan Sudol, Sudbury, nickel, Vale, Glencore, electric vehicles
summary: Stan Sudol urges Elon Musk/Tesla to invest or stockpile Class-1 nickel to avoid potential future shortages for EV batteries. The piece notes limited annual nickel supply and low incentive for miners to expand at low prices, referencing Sudbury-area projects and subsidies as precedents.

title: Rio Tinto plots 'agile' path for new WA copper, gold ambitions
summary: Rio Tinto said it is pursuing a small-scale, faster-start development approach for its Winu copper project in Western Australia’s Pilbara, targeting first production in 2023. title: P.E.I. brewery experiencing delays getting aluminum cans
summary: A Charlottetown brewery says aluminum can deliveries have shifted from weeks to up to three months for trailer loads. The Canadian Beverage Association confirms a national shortage, attributing disruptions to COVID-19-driven changes in consumer behavior and supply-chain pressures. The brewery warns the situation may worsen into late summer.

title: Chakana Copper to Commence Drilling at Soledad Project, Peru
summary: Chakana Copper announced it expects to restart a fully funded 15,000m drilling program at Peru’s Soledad copper-gold-silver project on Aug. 15, focusing on targets within breccia pipes. The release provides COVID-19 safety measures and notes the work will support future sampling and potential resource estimates.

title: Aluminum Aerosol Cans Market Reached US$ 3.5 in 2019; Demand Moderately Impacted as Automotive Applications are Suspended During Covid-19 Pandemic
summary: Future Market Insights says the aluminum aerosol can market saw demand downturn after COVID-19, with weaker personal care spending and suspended automotive activity, plus trade and raw-material supply disruptions. It notes aluminum’s recyclability supports demand longer term, but near-term consumption appears pressured, weighing on aluminium demand.

title: Copper dips as Chile mine workers decide against strike
summary: Copper eased 0.2% on Tuesday after Chile mine workers agreed a new contract, reducing strike risk at Antofagasta’s Centinela. title: Production starts at Celesta copper project in Brazil
summary: Production has begun at the Celesta copper project in Brazil. The start of output suggests incremental copper supply reaching the market, which may lead investors to price in higher availability. Within days to weeks, this can create downward pressure on copper as supply expectations improve.

title: Copper rises as stockpiles fall and industrial activity rebounds
summary: Copper rose as LME on-warrant warehouses declined sharply and cash copper traded at a premium over three-month metal, signaling tight nearby supply. summary: New Century Resources and Vale are progressing the potential acquisition of 95% of Vale New Caledonia, operator of the Goro nickel-cobalt mine. summary: A Reportlinker market research note forecasts growth in the global aluminum extrusion market and discusses COVID-19 impacts on demand, supply-chain routing, and government interventions. title: Near 40% decline in basic commodity exports to US: Canadian aluminium production and exports starting to rebalance
summary: The article’s title says basic commodity exports to the US from Canada have fallen by nearly 40%, and that Canadian aluminium production and exports are starting to rebalance. title: First Quantum cuts 2020 copper production guidance for Cobre Panama, group
summary: First Quantum is reported to have cut its 2020 copper production guidance for its Cobre Panama operation. summary: San Antonio breweries report difficulty obtaining aluminum beverage cans as at-home beer consumption rises during the pandemic. Demand is outpacing planned production, with shortages affecting sleek and printed cans and leading to longer lead times. The Aluminum Association cites unprecedented can demand, suggesting tightness in aluminum can supply.

summary: Copper Mountain reported strong Q2 2020 results, including 18.1 million pounds of copper production, improved margins, and lower C1/AISC costs versus Q2 2019. The company completed direct flotation reactors and plans further mill expansion if conditions allow. It reiterates 2020 copper guidance amid COVID-era uncertainty.

title: Nornickel announce real-time permafrost monitoring system
summary: Nornickel plans a real-time permafrost monitoring system after a Norilsk diesel spill caused by alleged permafrost softening, amid contested liability and regulatory pressure. Cleanup and audits are ongoing and compensation demands were issued. As a major nickel and copper producer, the event raises near-term operational and cost concerns.

title: 'No compromise on nickel ban': Govt acts firmly on price floor - Thu, July 30 2020
summary: Indonesia reiterated it will not compromise on a nickel ore export ban and threatened sanctions for companies failing to follow government-pegged nickel ore pricing. A monthly nickel ore price floor protects small miners, with disputes between miners and smelters. The tighter supply outlook and administered pricing are bullish for nickel.

title: Local Brewers Seeing High Demand for Aluminum Cans
summary: Breweries report unusually high demand for aluminum cans and canned beverages, driving canning lines to run almost nonstop and prompting some product timing and packaging adjustments. One brewery shifts to bottles temporarily due to capacity, but overall retail demand for packaged beer remains strong, potentially supporting aluminium can-sheet demand.

title: Canadian Premier Wants Retaliatory Sanctions Should US Proceed With Aluminum Tariffs
summary: Canada’s provincial and federal leaders warn that US tariffs on Canadian aluminum imports could harm jobs, with threats of Canadian retaliation against US products. Trudeau cautioned the US against unjustified duties, after reports of escalating contention around the aluminum tariff proposal.

title: Shanghai aluminum hits over 2-year high on solid China demand
summary: Shanghai aluminium prices jumped to a more-than-two-year high as lower inventories in China’s ShFE warehouses highlighted solid domestic demand. The September contract rose about 2.1% to around 14,765 yuan/t. Domestic aluminium prices also moved to a two-week high, reinforcing bullish sentiment for aluminium.

title: Shanghai aluminum hits over 2-year high on strong China demand
summary: Shanghai aluminum rose to a more than two-year high as a better-than-expected recovery in China boosted demand and hopes of sustained consumption. The piece cites infrastructure-related special bond issuance timelines and sharply lower ShFE aluminum inventories versus prior peaks, while LME copper and nickel also edged higher.

title: Local Central Coast brewery feels new effects of COVID-19 with nation-wide aluminum shortage
summary: A Central Coast brewery reports delays and shortages of aluminum beer cans due to a nation-wide aluminum shortage. With higher at-home beer consumption, shipments that usually take days now take about a month, leaving periods with no cans and lost sales opportunities. Demand-supply tightness suggests upward aluminium pressure.

title: KAZ Minerals H1 Copper Production Up 4%
summary: KAZ Minerals reported first-half copper production up 4% to 153.8 kt, driven by higher ore throughput and improved grades at Bozshakol. The company expects full-year guidance to be met, though Covid-19 risks may affect the second half. Gold output rose 25%.

title: Proactive Investors China - The web's leading portal for China stocks - Blackstone Minerals extends King Cobra discovery at depth with 47 metres at 1% nickel from 65 metres
summary: Blackstone Minerals said it has extended the King Cobra discovery at depth, reporting 47 metres at about 1% nickel from 65 metres. Such drilling results can lift market expectations for potential nickel supply from the asset, supporting near-term nickel sentiment.

title: Aluminium billet inventories fell 2,700 mt on week on smaller arrivals _SMM
summary: SMM data shows China’s aluminium billet inventories (6063 grade) fell 2,700 mt week on week to 65,900 mt as of July 30, after a prior week build. The drop was driven by lower arrivals at warehouses across major consumption areas, particularly in Guangdong.

title: Primary aluminium ingot inventories in China expanded 10,000 mt on week _SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots across eight consumption areas increased by 10,000 mt between July 23 and July 30, reaching 712,000 mt. Shanghai and Guangdong were the main contributors. The inventory build may imply softer near-term tightness for aluminium markets.

title: Canadian miner answers electric carmaker Elon Musk's call for zero-carbon nickel
summary: Canada Nickel Company says it is developing a near–Timmins, Ontario facility to mine serpentine nickel sulphide with near-zero net carbon emissions, using hydroelectric power and electric equipment. Tesla CEO Elon Musk urged miners to produce more nickel efficiently, boosting sentiment around nickel supply prospects.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 30/07: Thin volume sees downbeat LME complex consolidate lower; copper slides 0.8%
summary: A live LME futures report notes thin volume and an overall downbeat tone across the LME complex, with copper falling 0.8%. The piece frames the move as consolidation lower, implying short-term bearish pressure on copper prices rather than a specific supply/demand shock.

title: Troubled Copper Mine a 'Cautionary Tale' for Myanmar Investors*
summary: A China-Myanmar venture developing the Letpadaung copper mine says it gained community support and plans to expand, but the project is surrounded by violent protests, shootings, and Amnesty allegations of rights and environmental abuses. The report could hurt Myanmar’s investment prospects and add execution risk for copper supply.

title: Infill Drilling Continues to Highlight Potential of Higher-Grade Core at Canada Nickel's Crawford Nickel-Cobalt-Palladium Project
summary: Canada Nickel reported assay results from infill drilling at its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project, including higher-grade core intervals starting at 0.36% nickel over 249 metres and up to 0.33%–0.41% nickel over long intersections. The company also notes continued PGM and cobalt grades, with a delayed resource update.

title: King Cobra Discovery Extended At Depth - 47m at 1 Percent Nickel From 65m
summary: Blackstone Minerals announced down-dip extension results from the King Cobra nickel-rich discovery, including intercepts up to 7.44% Ni and associated copper credits. The discovery remains open and the company continues drilling and downstream nickel-sulfate scoping work. It signals potential future supply but not immediate market-level tightening.

title: Canadian nickel mining company looking to work with Elon Musk
summary: Canada Nickel Co says it has an approach to mine nickel with lower carbon emissions, using serpentine rock that reportedly reduces carbon when exposed to air and relying on Ontario hydro power. The company is engaging Elon Musk after Tesla’s call for greener nickel mining, but it still must build a large facility.

title: Copper set for 4th straight monthly gain, up on strong China factory data, weak dollar
summary: Copper prices rose in early trade on strong July China factory data and a weaker dollar, supporting demand expectations in the top consumer. LME three-month copper was up about 1% and on track for a fourth straight monthly gain. Nickel and aluminium were also higher, tracking base-metal strength.

title: Nickel Price Update: H1 2020 in Review | Supply, Demand, Prices
summary: Nickel prices declined through 2025 as persistent oversupply from Indonesia met soft demand growth. LME warehouse stockpiles rose materially, downstream stainless-steel demand stayed sluggish, and EV makers shifted toward lithium-iron-phosphate chemistries. Indonesia’s policy changes and higher royalties did not offset bearish supply-demand fundamentals.

title: Timmins firm aims to be major supplier as global demand for nickel grows
summary: Canada Nickel Company created a subsidiary to research and develop a “zero-carbon” processing facility near Timmins, targeting nickel for EV supply chains. CEO Mark Selby cites Tesla’s demand signal and contrasts it with high-carbon nickel pig iron from Indonesia, positioning greener nickel/cobalt as increasingly needed.

title: COVID-19 Impacts: Aluminum Welding Wires Market will Accelerate at a CAGR of over 6% through 2020-2024 | Increasing Demand For Lightweight Vehicles to Boost Growth
summary: Technavio’s press release forecasts growth in the aluminum welding wires market (including COVID-19 scenarios), supported by demand for lightweight vehicles and repair/maintenance welding. It cautions that fluctuating LME prices may hamper growth, but does not detail any concrete near-term aluminum supply, inventory, or policy changes that would clearly move prices.

title: Glencore production dips, lowers coal, nickel view
summary: Glencore said production across most commodities fell in the first half and it cut full-year guidance for nickel (and coal). Copper output dropped 11% year-on-year, while off-take for other metals including nickel declined. The revisions suggest weaker supply expectations, pressuring copper and nickel prices.

title: Glencore cuts nickel, coal guidance as output falls on virus-led disruptions    | 31 July 2020
summary: Glencore said it is cutting nickel (and coal) guidance as output falls due to virus-led disruptions. The update implies weaker near-term nickel supply, which would likely prompt the market to revise short-term balances lower and put downward pressure on nickel prices over the next days to weeks.

title: Shanghai bonded nickel stocks rose in closed import window_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM says refined nickel inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses rose by 1,000 mt in the week ended July 31 to 18,300 mt. The increase was mainly in plate-shaped products, reflecting seaborne arrivals moved into bond during a closed import arbitrage window. Stocks are expected to keep climbing in August.

title: Chile copper production falls in June for first time since coronavirus hit
summary: Chile’s copper production fell in June for the first time since the coronavirus shock, declining 0.6% to 472,172 tonnes, according to INE data. As the world’s top copper producer, the output drop signals slightly tighter supply conditions and could pressure copper prices near term.

title: Chile copper production dips in June for first time since coronavirus hit
summary: Chile’s copper output fell 0.6% to 472,172 tonnes in June, the first drop since the coronavirus hit, according to Chile’s INE. The decline coincides with an 8.3% plunge in manufacturing and worsening COVID outbreaks, suggesting supply constraints from reduced staffing could pressure near-term copper prices.

title: Chilean regulators charge BHP´s Escondida copper mine with water misuse
summary: Chile’s environmental watchdog said it will charge BHP’s Escondida copper mine for exceeding permitted water extraction by drawing too much from parched northern desert, tripling the limit in 2019. Regulators warn the violation could lead to permit revocation, closure or fines—raising supply risk for copper.

title: Chile's Codelco boosts copper output in first half 2020 despite coronavirus
summary: Chile’s Codelco said it increased copper output by 4.7% in the first six months of 2020 despite COVID-19 restrictions, relying on skeleton crews while maintaining operational continuity. Profits rose 20% and cash costs fell 9%, indicating resilient supply from the world’s top producer.

title: Chile's Codelco copper output up in first half 2020 despite coronavirus
summary: Chile’s Codelco said it increased copper output 4.7% to 744,000 tonnes in the first half of 2020 despite coronavirus constraints and skeleton staffing. The company cited improved processing and ore grades, with profits up 20% and cash costs down 9%, suggesting stronger supply continuity than feared.

title: Trump may make moves Friday on TikTok sale and aluminum tariffs: reports
summary: Reports say Trump may announce decisions on TikTok and could also impose new tariffs or other restrictions on Canadian aluminium as soon as Friday. Such actions would likely affect cross-border aluminium supply expectations and raise uncertainty, which can weigh on near-term aluminium prices.

title: Apple's low-carbon aluminum is a climate game changer | "Global Possibilities"
summary: Apple says some Macbook Pros will use low-carbon aluminum produced via an alternative smelting process with far fewer direct emissions. The story highlights scaling challenges for producers like Elysis and the role of electricity and inert anodes. Near-term adoption is limited, so immediate aluminum price effects are unclear.

title: Arizona siblings suspected in theft of 100,000 pounds of copper
summary: Arizona siblings were charged in a scheme to steal more than 100,000 pounds of copper from a power company site and sell most of it to a recycling facility in St. George, with only about 20,000 pounds remaining unsold. Investigators say the copper was taken in March and partially sold during July.

title: Japan"s Showa Aluminum Can inaugrates third plant in Vietnam
summary: Japan’s Showa Denko group via Hanacans inaugurated a third aluminium can plant in Vietnam (Ba Ria–Vung Tau) with 1.3bn can bodies/year capacity, plus an added can-ends line at Bac Ninh. Total system capacity rises to 3.3bn bodies and 3.3bn ends annually.

title: Arizona siblings suspected in theft of more than 100,000 pounds of copper sold in Utah
summary: Arizona siblings were charged after allegedly stealing over 100,000 pounds of copper from an Arizona power company and selling it at a Utah recycling facility. The copper had been stolen in March and was reportedly already mostly sold. Court documents cite copper buyers, payments, and estimated sale values.

title: Montana brewers battle shortages in aluminum as demand for packaged beer grows
summary: Montana brewers report shortages of aluminum cans as Americans shifted toward packaged beer during the pandemic. Restaurant alcohol sales fell, but packaged beer demand rose, tightening can availability. Brewers expect continued supply pressure, implying stronger near-term demand for aluminum canstock.

title: Material Matters: Copper, Gold & Iron Ore
summary: The piece notes copper has risen sharply over the past four months and examines drivers behind the move, including heavy financial participation via copper futures and links to China’s growth and macro variables. It argues these factors currently point to copper prices rising, despite “crowded” sentiment.

title: Copper falls to 3-week low as dollar firms, virus fears weigh
summary: Copper prices slid to a more than three-week low as the dollar firmed and coronavirus fears resurfaced, capping gains despite stronger-than-expected China factory activity. Three-month LME copper and SHFE September copper were down, while Chile’s June output fell, adding supply concern.

title: Shanghai Futures Exchange: Announcement On The Release Of Aluminum Futures Option Contract Specifications And Zinc Futures Option Contract Specifications
summary: Shanghai Futures Exchange announced the release of specifications for an aluminum futures option contract and zinc futures option contracts. While the aluminum contract update is directly tied to aluminium derivatives, the notice does not reference any change in production, inventories, tariffs, or demand, suggesting limited immediate price impact.

title: Copper rebounds from three-week lows on strong China data
summary: Copper prices bounced from three-week lows after strong China factory data boosted hopes for recovering demand. LME three-month copper rose 0.3% and the China Yangshan premium fell. The piece also reports small same-day moves in aluminium (+0.3%) and nickel (-0.4%), reflecting broader industrial metals sentiment.

title: Copper rebounds from three-week low on strong China data
summary: Copper rebounded from a three-week low after robust China factory data boosted hopes for renewed metals demand. The article highlights firmer euro-zone manufacturing too. It also reports aluminium rising 1.5% and nickel up 0.8% on Monday, reflecting broader investor risk sentiment tied to macro improvement.

title: Nornickel power plant fire kills 1; ops continue | American Metal Market
summary: The excerpt discusses aluminium market conditions, stating that while global supply remained technically intact, output was curtailed in parts of the Gulf and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was severely disrupted. These logistics constraints could reduce near-term flow and support aluminium price expectations.

title: Aluminum Is Bouncing Back In China
summary: The piece says aluminium is rebounding, especially in China. SHFE inventories have fallen sharply and SHFE/LME trading volumes are rising. It also notes firmer U.S. demand with reduced Canadian P1020 ingot shipments and smelters adjusting output for downstream needs, supporting near-term price strength.

title: London copper stays rangebound as investors eye next cue
summary: London copper stays rangebound after a sharp rally earlier in the year, with investors weighing mixed signals: U.S.-China tensions, COVID resurgences and weaker seasonal China demand versus stimulus hopes, a weaker dollar and some recovery. ShFE copper rises; LME aluminum dips and nickel gains, reflecting mixed risk sentiment.

title: London copper eases as investors eye next cue
summary: London copper slipped 0.5% and remained range-bound after a strong mid-2020 rally, with U.S.-China tensions, COVID resurgence, and weaker China demand limiting upside, while a weaker dollar and some economic recovery supported prices. The piece also reports concurrent moves in LME aluminum (down) and ShFE nickel (up).

title: SMM Evening Comments (Aug 4): Shanghai nonferrous metals were mostly higher, nickel surged more than 1%_SMM
summary: SMM reports most Shanghai nonferrous prices rose after upbeat US and Europe economic data. SHFE copper gained 0.94% on easing supply worries after Codelco restarted the Chuquicamata smelter. Aluminium ended up 0.69% and nickel surged 1.32%, reflecting broadly supportive near-term market sentiment.

title: Taseko Mines: Draft Aquifer Protection Permit for Florence Copper Project to be Issued this Week
summary: Taseko said Arizona’s environmental regulator notified it that a draft Aquifer Protection Permit for the Florence Copper in-situ project will be issued Aug. 6, after which a 30-day public comment period will follow. Management views this as confirming process environmental safety and supporting advancement toward copper cathode production.

title: Peru copper output plunges in first half of 2020 as coronavirus bites -govt
summary: Peru’s Energy and Mines ministry said copper output fell 20.4% in the first half of 2020 versus the same period in 2019 as coronavirus disruptions hit production. The report also noted declines in gold and zinc output, but copper supply weakness is the key driver for copper markets.

title: Rio Tinto to close New Zealand aluminium smelter
summary: Rio Tinto said it will wind down operations at its Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in New Zealand, citing high local energy costs and continued challenging aluminium conditions. It will terminate the Meridian power contract and close the plant, removing capacity and potentially supporting higher aluminium prices.

title: Peru copper and gold output nosedive in first half of 2020, ravaged by coronavirus -govt
summary: Peru’s Energy and Mines ministry said coronavirus restrictions severely reduced output. Copper production fell 20.4% in the first half of 2020 versus a year earlier, alongside declines in gold and zinc. Quarantine restrictions disrupted mining, with gradual normalization starting in May and June output partially recovering.

title: Now there's even an aluminum can shortage
summary: A local distributor reports an aluminum can shortage as bars and restaurants reopen and more consumers drink at home. Warehouse inventories are far below normal and suppliers deliver only a fraction of orders due to demand surging for canned beer. Recycling helps, but allocation and tight supply persist.

title: Highland Copper Announces Further Extension of Loan Maturity Date
summary: Highland Copper announced an extension of the maturity date for a US$4.5 million loan under its credit agreement to Aug. 15, 2020. The update concerns corporate debt timing rather than operations. Highland is focused on copper project development in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula.

title: Emergency crews contain fire at Goose Creek aluminum plant
summary: Emergency crews contained a fire at the JW Aluminum aluminum plant in Goose Creek, South Carolina. The facility was evacuated and firefighters/EMS responded. Officials reported no injuries and said the fire is contained, with continued assessment and an investigation to follow. Output disruption risk is likely in the near term.

title: Copper eases on output increases from top producers Chile, Peru
summary: Copper prices fell as increased output from major producers Chile and Peru reduced concerns over supply disruptions. Codelco reported higher Jan–Jun output, and expected strikes did not occur. Peru’s June output jumped sharply after mining resumed. LME and SHFE copper contracts eased, while premiums softened.

title: Copper edges lower as output from Chile, Peru rises
summary: Copper prices edged lower as production in Chile and Peru increased, easing concerns of supply disruptions that had pushed prices to multi-year highs. Codelco reported higher output and expected strikes failed, while Peru’s June output jumped. China’s copper premiums also fell, signaling weaker nearby demand for physical copper.

title: Brazil initiated an anti-dumping investigation on China's aluminum sheet products_SMM
summary: Brazil’s Secretariat of Foreign Trade launched an anti-dumping investigation into imports of Chinese aluminum sheet products, effective from an announcement published July 29. The probe covers multiple aluminum sheet HS codes. The move could tighten expected supply of Chinese sheet in Brazil and support aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Unthinking politics has led to India's copper shortage. It can't be aatmanirbhar without it
summary: The piece argues India faces a copper shortage after shutting down its largest smelting plant in Tuticorin (Sterlite), shifting India to net imports of refined copper. With EVs, wind/solar, grid upgrades, and charging infrastructure all copper-intensive, the article implies tighter near-term supply and potential price support.

title: United Steelworkers shuts down strike by Asarco copper miners
summary: United Steelworkers ended picket lines and instructed Asarco’s 1,800 copper miners to accept jobs or lose recall and unemployment benefits. The strike started Oct 13 and was tied to labor negotiations. The move suggests a resumption of mine output, reducing strike-related copper supply risk.

title: AAI urges govt to continue MEIS scheme for aluminium industry
summary: AAI urged India’s government to continue the MEIS export incentive for aluminium and raise the reward rate from 2% to 5%, warning exports worth about $5 billion are at stake. It also called for RoDTEP and product-linked incentives, noting capacity is high and domestic demand is weak amid Covid-19.

title: China nickel manufacturing remained in expansion in July_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s nickel downstream PMIs stayed in expansion in July, though growth slowed slightly. Production and new orders remained near/above 50, but raw-material inventory contracted as rising nickel (NPI) prices made buyers less aggressive. Electroplating was weakest, with lower operating rates due to higher base metals.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Aug 5): Shanghai nonferrous metals were mostly lower, nickel surged nearly 2% as the Philippines will extend lockdown_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals mostly fell, with nickel up 1.95% after the Philippines extended lockdown to Aug 18. Copper fell 0.66% and aluminium shed 0.44%, amid cautious trading ahead of US data and continued position building in aluminium. Overall near-term direction is mixed.

title: Aluminum Aerosol Cans Market Sales to Flatten Due to COVID-19 Pandemic; Key Market Players to Redesign Developmental Strategies
summary: The piece reports that the aluminum aerosol cans market’s sales are likely to flatten as the COVID-19 pandemic disrupts demand. It also notes key players will redesign strategies. Softer near-term consumption of aluminium-containing packaging suggests downside pressure for aluminium price expectations in the short term.

title: China produced 14,600 mt of refined nickel in July, output in Xinjiang and Shandong fell _SMM
summary: China produced 14,600 mt of refined nickel in July, down 3.1% from June. Xinjiang output fell 37% and some material output shifted into August classifications, while Shandong output dropped 16.7% as smelters cut operating rates. SMM expects higher August output, but Xinjiang COVID-19 disrupts raw-material transport.

title: Progressive Planet Solutions Inc.: PLAN Announces Anomalous Nickel Over a 500 Metre Strike Length at Heffley Creek Property in BC
summary: Progressive Planet Solutions announced further geochemical results from its Heffley Creek property in British Columbia, defining a nickel-in-soil anomaly over a just-over 500-metre strike length. Reported soil grades reach up to 3,330 PPM nickel. The company plans additional soil and rock sampling; no production or supply impact is stated.

title: Aluminium sector for MEIS scheme as exports at stake
summary: Indian aluminium producers urged the government to continue MEIS incentives and raise rates to support exports worth about $5 billion. The government’s possible MEIS funding cut and blockage of new applications may reduce export competitiveness amid COVID-19 demand weakness, keeping aluminium prices under pressure.

title: PLAN Announces Anomalous Nickel Over a 500 Metre Strike Length at Heffley Creek Property in BC
summary: Progressive Planet Solutions reports anomalously high nickel values in soil samples at its Heffley Creek property in BC, with a nickel-in-soil anomaly exceeding 300 PPM across just over 500 metres. Results are exploration-stage and do not imply immediate production or supply changes. Continued sampling is planned into fall 2020.

title: New Caledonia approves export of nickel ore
summary: New Caledonia has approved exports of nickel ore after lobbying by nickel companies to sell low-grade material amid financial stress at SLN and Vale’s restructuring. The policy requires amending the mining code and adds an export tax. The approval is likely to boost nickel supply expectations over coming weeks.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 9,900 mt on week on larger arrivals _SMM
summary: SMM reported that China aluminium billet inventories rose 9,900 mt WoW to 75,800 mt as of Aug 6, mainly due to larger arrivals in Guangdong and Jiangxi. Stocks increased in Foshan, Changzhou and Nanchang, while Wuxi and Huzhou declined.

title: Most of the large-scale copper mines saw year-on-year declines in output in H1_SMM
summary: SMM reports that most large copper mines saw year-on-year output declines in H1 2020, with Peru among the hardest hit due to COVID-19 disruptions. Second-quarter weakness persisted across many surveyed producers. Peru’s copper output fell 20.4% on year, while some gains in Chile and Zambia were smaller.

title: Primary aluminium inventories built up 13,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China primary aluminium ingot inventories rose by 13,000 mt on the week to 725,000 mt as of Thursday Aug 6. The increase covers eight consumption areas, including SHFE warrants, indicating a near-term build in available aluminium supply.

title: Ivanhoe Mines: Kakula Copper Mine Underground Development Far Ahead of Schedule and Surface Processing Plant Advancing Rapidly with 4,700-Strong Workforce
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says underground development at the Kakula copper mine in the DRC is 5.5 km ahead of schedule and surface ore stockpiles contain sizable copper grades. The processing plant commissioning and equipment shipments are progressing, with first copper targeted for Q3 2021, supporting bullish copper supply sentiment.

title: Copper drifts lower as surplus looms
summary: Copper prices drifted lower as investors questioned whether improving demand would be enough to prevent a surplus. Analysts cited negative demand growth outside China, expectations of continued surplus conditions, and only partial offset from Chinese demand. A cited suspension at Papua New Guinea’s Ok Tedi adds some supply uncertainty but net sentiment remains bearish.

title: METALS-Copper drifts lower as surplus looms
summary: Copper prices drifted lower as investors questioned whether improving demand would sustain the rally. Commentary cited negative demand growth outside China, expectations of continued surplus for 2020, and forecasts of weaker demand. Coronavirus supply disruption eased, while Papua New Guinea’s Ok Tedi suspended output briefly and aluminium was referenced.

title: Chile copper production to dip 1.2% to 5.718 mln tons this year - Cochilco
summary: Chile’s copper commission (Cochilco) expects 2020 copper production to decline 1.2% to 5.718 million tons versus the prior year. The report also projects copper prices averaging $2.62/lb in 2020 and $2.85/lb in 2021, signaling a softer near-term outlook.

title: Infill Drilling Further Strengthens Higher-Grade Core at the Crawford Nickel-Cobalt Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel reports infill drilling results from its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project, extending higher-grade nickel core and improving the definition of resource shells. All four infill holes intersect thick nickel mineralization, with additional assays expected soon. The company links results to an updated resource and mine-plan work.

title: Canadian Press NewsAlert: Trump slaps tariffs on Canadian raw aluminum
summary: The Canadian Press NewsAlert reports that Trump imposed tariffs on Canadian raw aluminum. Tariffs on imports generally increase the cost of Canadian supply into the U.S., potentially reducing purchases and weakening short-term demand. That could pressure aluminium prices downward in the coming days as market expectations adjust.

title: Trump to impose 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum
summary: Trump’s administration notified Canada it intends to impose a 10% tariff on unprocessed Canadian aluminum, expected to take effect Thursday or Friday. The move is tied to disputes over export quotas under a Trade Expansion Act framework. U.S. business groups warned the tariff would raise costs and invite retaliation.

title: Trump says aluminum tariffs reimposed on Canada
summary: Trump said the administration reimposed some tariffs on Canadian aluminum after prior reports suggested a move. The tariffs raise the cost of Canadian imports to the U.S., potentially tightening supply and influencing near-term aluminum price expectations. He also mentioned an executive order on essential drugs purchases, unrelated to metals.

title: Trump Signs Proclamation to Reimpose Tariffs on Canadian Aluminum
summary: Trump signed a proclamation reimposing a 10% tariff on aluminum imports from Canada, citing prior 2018 national-security concerns. The US Chamber of Commerce says the move will raise costs for US manufacturers and trigger retaliation. Canada warned it could respond with duties on US imports if tariffs are imposed.

title: Trump reimposing tariffs on Canadian raw aluminum
summary: Trump will restore a 10% tariff on Canadian raw aluminum starting Aug. 16, prompting Canada to plan dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs. U.S. primary aluminum firms say the move will protect domestic producers, while Canadian smelters argue exports are not surging and tariffs will raise costs for aluminum users in the U.S.

title: Trump reimposing tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: The article indicates Trump is reimposing tariffs on Canadian aluminum. Higher tariffs can deter U.S. purchases of Canadian metal, tightening near-term availability and raising effective aluminum costs. That typically supports aluminium price expectations in the short term, though the exact magnitude depends on market anticipation and alternatives.

title: Trump Poised to Reimpose 10% Tariff on Some Canadian Aluminum
summary: Trump will remove Canada’s exemption from a 10% U.S. tariff on some Canadian aluminum imports starting Aug. 16, citing a “flood” of exports that harms U.S. aluminum producers. Canada threatens retaliation. The move is expected to lift shipping costs and support near-term aluminum prices while raising end-user costs.

title: President Trump announces 10 per cent tariff on Canadian aluminum
summary: Trump announced 10% tariffs on most Canadian aluminum under Section 232, effective Aug. 16, with Canada planning dollar-for-dollar retaliatory measures. The U.S. argues imports surged, while industry says no surge exists. The tariff raises costs for U.S. buyers and may pressure aluminium price expectations near term.

title: U.S. slaps 10% tariff on aluminum imports from Canada
summary: The U.S. will restore a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports (Section 232) effective Aug. 16, citing national security concerns. Canada plans dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs. Industry groups say the move raises costs for U.S. manufacturers and could destabilize Canadian supply chains, with import dynamics already fluctuating.

title: Trump slaps tariffs on Canadian raw aluminum
summary: The article title says Trump slapped tariffs on Canadian raw aluminum. Such tariffs can alter trade flows and near-term supply expectations for aluminium, potentially affecting pricing quickly as import costs and procurement strategies adjust. The full page content wasn’t available, so details and tariff scope are uncertain.

title: U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum will raise costs for U.S. firms, U.S. Chamber of Commerce says
summary: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce warned that Trump’s decision to reimpose 10% tariffs on certain Canadian aluminum imports would raise costs for U.S. manufacturers. It argued the move is opposed by most U.S. aluminum producers and could trigger retaliation, potentially weighing on aluminum demand and prices soon.

title: Urgent: U.S. re-imposes 10 pct tariff on aluminum from Canada
summary: Trump’s proclamation re-imposes a 10% U.S. tariff on aluminum imports from Canada. The measure is likely to disrupt Canadian export flows into the U.S., affect near-term demand and pricing for physical aluminium, and introduce trade uncertainty that can weigh on aluminium benchmarks over the coming days.

title: Trump reimposes tariffs on Canadian aluminium
summary: The article says Trump has reimposed tariffs on Canadian aluminium. Such trade barriers can raise the cost of Canadian metal imports, alter supply flows, and worsen near-term pricing expectations for aluminium as markets reassess trade volumes and available supply.

title: APAA Hails Trump Administration Action to Address Canadian Aluminum Surge
summary: APAA praised the Trump Administration for reinstating Section 232 tariffs on Canadian imports of primary aluminium. It cites a 95% year-on-year surge and acceleration in June to a record 190,798 metric tons. The group says the action should curb imports and support U.S. primary aluminium jobs and pricing.

title: Taseko Mines: Draft Aquifer Protection Permit Has Been Issued for Florence Copper Project
summary: Taseko Mines said Arizona ADEQ issued a draft Aquifer Protection Permit for its Florence copper project, starting a public comment period. While it is only a draft step and not final approval, it improves permitting momentum for copper development and could modestly support near-term copper price expectations.

title: Evening Update: Trump announces 10-per-cent tariff on Canadian aluminum
summary: Trump announced a reimposed 10% U.S. tariff on Canadian non-alloyed unwrought aluminum, effective Aug. 16. The move follows an earlier trade agreement allowing targeted tariff renewals if imports surge. U.S. firms cite increased Canadian shipments, while Canadian and much of U.S. industry oppose the tariff.

title: Trump reimposes 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum
