title: U.S. District Court Denies Class Certification Motion in Aluminum Rate-Manipulation Case Based on Improper Use of Statistical Averages by Plaintiffs' Expert | King & Spalding
summary: A U.S. court denied class certification in an aluminum warehousing antitrust case, criticizing plaintiffs’ expert use of statistical averages and finding it insufficient to show classwide injury. The allegations involve manipulation of aluminum regional premiums, but the decision is procedural and not directly tied to short-term aluminum market fundamentals.

title: Premier Scott Moe worried U.S. could put tariff on steel after Canadian aluminum
summary: Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe said he fears the U.S. may extend tariffs from Canadian aluminum to steel after Washington reimposed a 10% import tax on raw aluminum from Canada. Canada plans $3.6 billion in retaliatory tariffs on U.S. aluminum-linked products, raising near-term trade and pricing concerns.

title: 'Disappointing news': Horgan criticizes US tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: British Columbia Premier John Horgan criticized the US decision to impose 10% tariffs on Canadian aluminum imports, warning it will make Canadian aluminum more expensive in the US. Canadian leaders said retaliation with dollar-for-dollar tariffs would follow, heightening trade friction and likely weighing on near-term aluminum prices.

title: U.S. aluminum tariffs 'disappointing' and 'unfortunate,' says Horgan
summary: B.C. Premier John Horgan criticizes U.S. tariffs on Canadian raw aluminium as “disappointing.” The statement argues Canadian exports don’t harm the U.S., while the 10% tariff could damage the U.S. economy. Canada plans to match the tariff cost, potentially targeting other U.S. imports, keeping aluminium markets unsettled.

title: S&P, Dow pick up small gains as tech stocks falter; Canada claps back at new aluminum tariffs
summary: Canada said it will impose tariffs totaling about $2.69 billion on U.S. imports in retaliation after the U.S. reinstated a 10% import tax on Canadian aluminum. The dispute follows prior aluminum tariff actions tied to trade negotiations, raising near-term uncertainty for aluminum supply and demand.

title: Ontario urging residents to buy local over Trump's tariffs against Canadian aluminum | Nation and World
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford urged consumers to buy Canadian products in retaliation for Trump’s decision to remove Canada’s exemption from 10% tariffs on aluminum, effective Aug. 16. Trudeau’s government plans countermeasures, and the move is driven by U.S. producers’ concerns about Canadian aluminum inflows.

title: Canada to slap $2.7bn counter-tariffs on US aluminum
summary: Canada plans C$3.6bn (US$2.7bn) counter-tariffs on US aluminum following Trump’s reimposition of a 10% duty on Canadian aluminum, alleging a surge in imports. Ottawa will consult for 30 days on targeted items. The dispute threatens aluminum costs and trade flows ahead of Aug. 16.

title: Canada to slap Can$3.6-billion counter-tariffs on US aluminum
summary: Canada announced Can$3.6 billion in counter-tariffs on US aluminum products after the US reimposed a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum from Aug 16. Ottawa cites “absurd” US levies and plans consultations. The dispute targets items linked to aluminum, creating trade-flow uncertainty and near-term demand pressure for aluminum.

title: Canada to levy huge tariffs against U.S. re-imposing duty on Canadian aluminum
summary: Canada will impose C$3.6bn of counter-tariffs on U.S. products after the U.S. re-imposed a 10% tariff on Canadian raw aluminum from Aug. 16. Canada’s measures take effect in 30 days post-consultation. The dispute raises near-term aluminum supply and trade-cost expectations.

title: Imposing Aluminum Tariffs on Canada Will Hurt Tens of Thousands of Auto Workers in Tennessee
summary: U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander criticized reimposed tariffs on aluminum imports from Canada, saying they will likely raise costs for automakers that must source at least 70% of aluminum production in North America under USMCA. He argues this could reduce car production and jobs in Tennessee.

title: Stokes County: Wieland Copper plant announces layoffs
summary: Wieland Copper Products, a copper tubing manufacturer, filed a WARN Act notice saying 120 workers will be permanently laid off at its Pine Hall, North Carolina plant. The company says it operates facilities worldwide, but the article doesn’t quantify output changes, limiting the expected short-term impact on copper demand and pricing.

title: Canada, local leaders criticize Trump's revival of aluminum tariffs | Business
summary: Canada’s government said it will respond with retaliatory tariffs after President Trump announced duties on Canadian aluminum. Deputy Prime Minister Freeland outlined over 60 U.S. aluminum-containing products that may face higher tariffs, promising retaliation dollar-for-dollar and targeting C$3.6 billion in goods. The dispute raises near-term aluminium trade risk.

title: Canada, local leaders criticize Trump's revival of aluminum tariffs | Nation and World
summary: Trump plans to impose new U.S. duties on Canadian aluminum, prompting Canada to announce retaliatory tariffs. Ottawa published a list of more than 60 aluminum-containing U.S. products that could face higher charges, with retaliation capped at a dollar-for-dollar equivalent totaling C$3.6 billion. The tariff dispute is framed as highly protectionist.

title: Ottawa's retaliatory tariffs on U.S.-made aluminum could hit everything from washing machines to golf clubs
summary: Ottawa plans 10% retaliatory tariffs on U.S.-made aluminum products starting Sept. 16, estimated at about $3.6B on imported raw aluminum and aluminum goods. The measures widen coverage into consumer and industrial aluminum items, potentially disrupting trade flows and pressuring near-term aluminum market sentiment.

title: Power outage planned for Sunday in Copper Cliff cancelled; one set for Aug. 16 will proceed
summary: A scheduled power outage in Copper Cliff for Sunday Aug. 9 was cancelled, but another outage planned for Aug. 16 (8 a.m.–2 p.m.) will proceed. Hydro One will interrupt transmission to the Clarabelle Transmission Station, and Greater Sudbury Hydro will use the outage to perform equipment maintenance.

title: It might not be all bad for the South - when the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter closes - 10-Aug-2020
summary: Rio Tinto plans to shut the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in Southland, causing 2,600 job losses but leaving a power-grid surplus of about 13%. The piece argues Southland may face cheaper electricity via lower transmission costs and improved local power sales, while smelter closure reduces aluminium supply.

title: U.S. imposes aluminum tariffs amid can shortage
summary: The U.S. imposed a 10% tariff on Canadian raw aluminum, prompting B.C. brewers to worry about higher aluminum can costs during an ongoing shortage. Industry sources cite reduced U.S. aluminum plant supply and increased demand for seltzers. Canada is set to consult before countermeasures, with uncertainty about effects on prices.

title: Aluminum tariffs could impact Michigan manufacturing
summary: Canada is retaliating with tariffs on $2.7 billion of U.S. goods after the U.S. reimposed aluminum duties (10%) and steel duties (25%). Trade groups warn the measures disadvantage Michigan manufacturers, and automakers cite higher prices hurting profits and jobs following the 2018 tariff round.

title: How copper's tumultuous year sets the stage for an uncertain future
summary: Copper is trading at its highest level since 2010, up ~38% from March lows, driven by a faster-than-expected demand rebound in China and escalating COVID-driven supply concerns in South America. Chile’s Codelco is curbing operations due to COVID cases, raising production disruption risk.

title: Biden vows to block Alaska copper/gold mine project if elected | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Democratic candidate Joe Biden said an administration would stop a proposed copper-and-gold mine in Alaska’s Bristol Bay region. The project faces potential EPA veto-style restrictions and awaiting Army Corps of Engineers permitting. Supporters cite environmental risks and oppose the project, threatening future copper supply expectations.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 10/08: China's consumer inflation rise boosts LME copper; lead below $1,900/t
summary: A live futures report notes that China’s consumer inflation increased, which boosted LME copper prices. The excerpt also mentions lead trading below $1,900/t, but provides no comparable copper-linked details for nickel or aluminium. Overall, the actionable metal-price signal is positive for copper.

title: Aluminum Tariffs Re-imposed
summary: The U.S. is re-imposing a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum, citing rising import concerns and alleged broken commitments. Canada plans dollar-for-dollar retaliation via countermeasures. The move is controversial, with downstream users warning of higher raw-material costs while supporters argue it supports struggling U.S. aluminum producers.

title: LME aluminium queue at Istim's Port Klang sheds rise to 68 days
summary: The article highlights LME aluminium delivery/warehouse queue conditions at Istim’s Port Klang, stating the aluminium queue has risen to 68 days. Longer queues typically indicate more congestion and reduced near-term availability, which can support upside pressure in aluminium prices over the coming days.

title: Canada's Teck says to re-start work at Quebrada Blanca 2 copper project in Chile
summary: Teck said it will reinitiate work on its Quebrada Blanca phase 2 copper project in Chile after closing it in March due to COVID-19. The company is coordinating with local authorities and targets full staffing within three months, contingent on health conditions. The restart follows prolonged suspension.

title: Canada´s Teck says to re-start work at Quebrada Blanca 2 copper project in Chile
summary: Teck said it will restart work at its Quebrada Blanca phase 2 copper project in Chile after shutting it in March due to COVID-related health concerns. The company is coordinating with local authorities and expects full staffing within about three months, improving outlook for copper output.

title: U.S. to reimpose 10% tariff on Canadian aluminium
summary: President Trump announced the U.S. will reimpose a 10% tariff on some Canadian aluminium imports effective Aug. 16. The measure is intended to affect trade flows and raises the cost of imported metal into the U.S., likely weighing on aluminium pricing in the near term.

title: Papua New Guinea's Ok Tedi copper mine halts output over COVID cases | Reuters | Business
summary: Papua New Guinea’s Ok Tedi copper mine halted output after COVID cases emerged among workers. The shutdown is expected to reduce near-term copper production and affect shipments. Such supply disruptions can quickly influence short-term market sentiment and pricing for copper.

title: U.S. aluminum tariffs are 'unjustified and unnecessary': Canadian manufacturers - MRO Magazine
summary: U.S. manufacturers and Canadian aluminum industry groups oppose a new 10% U.S. tariff on Canadian aluminum starting later in August. Firms expect higher costs, disrupted integrated supply chains, and potential retaliation tariffs. Industry notes the move may shift aluminum production to third countries, adding volatility after the prior trade dispute ended.

title: Premier Scott Moe worried U.S. could put tariff on steel after Canadian aluminum - MRO Magazine
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump reimposed a 10% tariff on raw aluminium imports from Canada, prompting Ottawa to announce $3.6 billion in retaliatory import tariffs. Canadian premiers worry the U.S. could extend tariffs to steel, raising uncertainty for regional manufacturing and potentially weighing on aluminium prices.

title: Commerce Sets Early Duties On Aluminum Sheets
summary: The report headline says Commerce has set early duties on aluminum sheets. Tariffs on aluminum sheet imports generally reduce competitive imported supply available to U.S. buyers, supporting pricing and encouraging suppliers to seek higher net prices. The near-term effect depends on duty level and coverage details.

title: China launches aluminum, zinc options to serve real economy
summary: China launched trading of aluminium options on the Shanghai Futures Exchange, alongside zinc options, to better hedge real-economy risks. The first-day activity was reported as active. The move improves the derivatives toolset for aluminium risk management, but the article does not cite immediate physical market imbalances, suggesting limited short-term price impact.

title: Copper rises on hopes of U.S. stimulus bill
summary: Copper climbed after investors focused on hopes of renewed U.S. COVID-19 stimulus negotiations. Three-month LME copper rose slightly, while September Shanghai copper gained more. However, gains were capped by a stronger U.S. dollar and worsening U.S.-China tensions. China auto sales and a Chile project restart were also cited.

title: Blackstone Minerals Continues to Intersect High-grade Nickel at Ban Chang
summary: Blackstone Minerals reported further high-grade nickel-copper-PGE intersections from its Ban Chang prospect at the Ta Khoa nickel-copper project in Vietnam. Results include multiple drill holes with up to ~2.5% Ni and ~1.4% Cu, and drilling continues to define resources and support scoping work for nickel sulfate production.

title: Copper edges higher as investors eye fresh U.S. stimulus
summary: LME copper trades with a slight uptick but is pressured by a stronger U.S. dollar and rising Sino-U.S. tensions, according to Reuters. The market also watches for fresh U.S. stimulus, which could support demand expectations, offsetting some of the immediate bearish influence from FX and geopolitical risk.

title: Operating rates at copper pipe producers to extend declines in August _SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates at Chinese copper pipe producers fell in July as air-conditioner orders dropped sharply and makers cleared inventories and delayed production to meet new energy-efficiency standards. August is expected to see further declines. Producers also cut feedstock inventories due to pessimistic consumption and high copper prices.

title: LME copper eases on stronger dollar, rising Sino-U.S. tension
summary: London copper eased as a stronger U.S. dollar reduced appeal for non-USD buyers and rising U.S.-China tensions increased fears of retaliation and weaker growth, hurting metals demand. A potential U.S. stimulus bill limited losses. The report also shows LME and ShFE aluminium prices slipping slightly.

title: Over half of Americans oppose Trump tariff on Canadian aluminum, survey suggests
summary: A survey highlights opposition to a Trump decision to reimpose a 10% tariff on Canadian raw aluminum. The U.S. cites alleged dumping, while Canada denies it and plans $3.6 billion in retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods containing aluminum. Tariff-driven trade frictions can affect near-term aluminium pricing.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 11/08: LME copper price holds below $6,400/t; C/3M spread flips to contango
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures report notes LME copper is holding below $6,400/t and that the 3M/nearby spread has turned to contango, implying softer near-term positioning. It also mentions procedural corrections and delays to certain low-carbon aluminium differential assessments, affecting publication accuracy rather than signalling a major aluminium market shock.

title: Copper dips as U.S.-China tensions simmer, economy weighs
summary: Copper fell on Tuesday as investors worried about simmering U.S.-China tensions, the economic fallout from COVID-19, and a stronger U.S. dollar. The piece cites geopolitics and macro concerns weighing on sentiment, with copper dropping toward key support levels, while aluminium and nickel also edged lower amid broader metal moves.

title: NORNICKEL REPORTS FIRST HALF 2020 INTERIM CONSOLIDATED IFRS FINANCIAL RESULTS
summary: Norilsk Nickel reported 1H2020 results and highlighted nickel market conditions. It notes nickel price resilience but argues the short-term outlook is negative due to an expanding surplus, COVID-related demand disruption across stainless and non-stainless sectors, and higher LME/SHFE inventories. It also describes production disruptions and Indonesia NPI ramp-up offsetting shortages.

title: Trump Administration to Reimpose 10 Percent Tariff on Canadian Aluminum Imports
summary: The Trump administration plans to end Canada’s exemption and reimpose a 10% Section 232 tariff on Canadian aluminum imports into the U.S. The change takes effect around Aug. 16. The administration cited a “flood” of aluminum imports as the justification, implying tighter supply and near-term market repricing for aluminum.

title: Russia's Nornickel H1 profit slides as it sets aside $2bln for fuel spill claim
summary: Russia’s Nornickel reported a sharp H1 profit drop after reserving $2.1 billion for potential environmental damage compensation tied to a major Arctic fuel spill. The company also reduced 2020 capex due to weaker rouble and COVID-19. It disputes the regulator’s requested compensation level.

title: Canada Nickel Announces $1.5 Million Non-Brokered Private Placement, Extends the Accelerated Expiry Date of its Common Share Purchase Warrants to September 14, 2020
summary: Canada Nickel announced a $1.5 million non-brokered private placement of flow-through shares to fund advancement of its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide exploration, plus an extension of warrant expiry to September 14, 2020. The release is primarily corporate funding and does not indicate near-term supply or inventory changes.

title: Trump's tariffs on Canada are about more than aluminum
summary: The US imposed a 10% national-security tariff on aluminum from Canada shortly after USMCA’s entry into force. Canada retaliated and is also concerned about broader protectionism. The dispute revives Section 232-style legal friction, likely pressuring near-term aluminum trade and sentiment.

title: Opinion: It's not me, it's you: Trump's aluminum tariffs are a byproduct of his re-election woes
summary: The opinion argues that President Trump’s renewed tariffs on Canadian aluminum are politically driven around the U.S. election. It notes the tariffs target Canadian supply used by U.S. manufacturers and highlights anticipated countermeasures from Canada, implying near-term trade disruption and higher aluminum import costs into the U.S.

title: Trump Administration Reinstates Tariffs on Canadian Aluminum
summary: The Trump administration reinstated a 10% tariff on specific Canadian aluminum products (non-alloy unwrought aluminum under subheading 7601.10). Canada proposed dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs on U.S. aluminum and aluminum-containing goods. The measures threaten broader trade conflict and likely tighten near-term aluminum supply to the U.S.

title: 'An own goal': Aluminum tariffs will hurt U.S. consumers
summary: The article argues that U.S. aluminium tariffs will harm consumers and downstream users by raising costs for industries such as autos. It interviews a Canadian vehicle industry representative on how the tariff policy is expected to affect production and pricing through tighter aluminium supply or higher domestic costs.

title: Over 50% of Americans oppose Trump tariff on Canadian aluminum: survey
summary: A survey highlights backlash to Trump’s reimposed 10% tariff on Canadian raw aluminum. The U.S. cited alleged dumping/flooding, while Canada denied it and said it would retaliate with $3.6 billion of tariffs. The trade dispute and expected retaliation are likely to weigh on aluminum market sentiment near term.

title: Insights on the Global Aluminum Foil Market 2020-2024 | COVID-19 Analysis, Drivers, Restraints, Opportunities and Threats
summary: Technavio’s report forecasts aluminum foil demand growth (~5% CAGR during 2020-2024), citing increased packaged food use and concerns over plastic packaging. It summarizes market size, segmentation, and vendor landscape (including Alcoa and Norsk Hydro) but provides no immediate supply shock, inventory, or pricing information for aluminum.

title: Canada´s Teck to re-start work at Quebrada Blanca 2 copper project in Chile
summary: Teck said it will restart work at its Quebrada Blanca 2 copper project in Chile after shutting it down in March due to COVID-19. The company aims to reach full staffing within three months, subject to health conditions. The restart supports expectations for copper output and future ramp-up.

title: Global Electrodeposited Copper Foils Industry
summary: The news promotes a report on the global electrodeposited copper foils market, citing growth forecasts by thickness and by regions such as the U.S. and China, including pandemic-related commentary. It profiles industry participants but does not mention any immediate supply, trade, policy, or inventory event that would likely move copper prices soon.

title: President Trump re-imposes tariffs on Canadian aluminum imports
summary: President Trump re-imposed tariffs on Canadian aluminum imports, citing Canada’s failure to meet commitments from a recent trade deal. Trudeau said Canada will respond dollar-for-dollar. The tariff action directly targets aluminum trade, likely increasing U.S. import costs and supporting near-term aluminum price strength.

title: Opinion: Trump's aluminum tariffs have Glencore's prints all over them
summary: The opinion piece says Trump has renewed a 10% tariff on Canadian primary aluminum, arguing it supports U.S. smelters despite claims imports were not surging. It highlights Century Aluminum and Glencore influence and states tariff speculation boosted prices linked to the LME, implying near-term bullish pressure for aluminium.

title: Copper dips as U.S. stimulus uncertainty weighs
summary: Copper prices fell after talks on U.S. coronavirus relief stalled, increasing uncertainty over additional fiscal stimulus. Investors also worried that U.S.-China tensions could trigger retaliation and further dampen global growth. LME copper dropped 0.6% and Shanghai copper slid 1.1%, reflecting weaker demand sentiment across metals.

title: Material Matters: Copper, Gold & LNG
summary: ANZ Bank warns copper is overvalued as global industrial production remains weak outside China and resurging COVID-19 risks threaten recovery. With pandemic-related supply disruptions expected to ease, the firm expects a copper surplus over the next 12–18 months, implying downside pressure for copper prices.

title: Aluminum can shortage causes breweries to slow beer production
summary: Breweries are slowing beer production because of an aluminum can shortage. The report suggests constrained availability of aluminum packaging supply is disrupting output plans, which can increase competition for aluminum can material and reinforce near-term support for aluminium prices as buyers scramble for supply.

title: Altus Strategies PLC: EIA Approved and Exploration Update at Agdz Silver and Copper Project, Morocco
summary: Altus Strategies announced approval of the Environmental Impact Assessment for its Agdz silver and copper project in Morocco, a milestone toward converting an exploration licence into a mining licence. It also reports predictive mapping and new high-grade copper results from priority prospects, but no production or supply changes.

title: Canadian Government's Consultation Process On Countermeasures To U.S. Aluminum Tariffs: 2018 Redux? - International Law
summary: Canada’s government is consulting on retaliatory 10% surtaxes targeting U.S. aluminum products after the U.S. imposed a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum exports. The measures are scheduled for mid-August and mid-September and total $3.6 billion, potentially disrupting aluminum trade flows and price expectations.

title: Aluminium sector struggles to adopt common standards to cut emissions
summary: Reuters reports the aluminium industry is struggling to agree on shared low-carbon standards for greener processing. Competing benchmarks and stalled guidelines—complicated by funding links to EN+ and buyer reluctance to pay premiums—mean “green” labelling remains inconsistent, limiting short-term pricing impact.

title: Our Views: Raising the price of aluminum in beer cans not good for Joe Sixpack, Mr. President
summary: The piece argues that Trump’s planned reimposition of a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum will increase costs for U.S. can makers and consumers. It also notes Canada retaliated with tariffs on U.S. products. Overall, the tariff-driven demand hit and trade-war uncertainty are framed as negative for aluminum pricing prospects.

title: Indigenous Peoples Of Russia's Far North March Against Nornickel
summary: Indigenous groups in Russia’s Norilsk area marched against Nornickel, citing alleged rights violations and environmental harm. The piece highlights major fuel spills from Nornickel assets, including a May diesel spill with estimated $2 billion damage, plus another aviation fuel spill. It raises potential operational and regulatory risks for nickel.

title: Chile's Codelco sees quick progress in ramping up Chuquicamata copper processing
summary: Codelco said it is making faster progress ramping up processing capacity at its Chuquicamata underground project after COVID measures forced a temporary suspension. Management expects the ramp-up to contribute more fine copper this year and aims to reach 140,000 tons per day of mineral processing sooner than planned.

title: Presidential Proclamation Reinstates Tariffs on Canadian Aluminum | Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath LLP
summary: The proclamation reinstates 10% U.S. tariffs on certain non-alloyed unwrought aluminum imports from Canada under Section 232 monitoring, citing a surge in Canadian volumes. Canada responded with retaliatory tariffs on U.S. aluminum and aluminum-containing goods, raising risk of broader trade escalation that could pressure aluminum markets.

title: What's going on with the shortage of aluminum cans?
summary: The article says COVID-related stockpiling increased take-home demand for canned beverages, driving a shortage of aluminum cans. Brewers and beverage brands cut back on offerings and report out-of-stocks, reflecting constrained container supply. This suggests near-term aluminum demand tightness, likely supportive for aluminium prices.

title: Peru's copper exports fall 26.3% in the first half
summary: Peru’s copper exports fell 26.3% in the first half, indicating reduced outbound shipments from a key global supplier. The decline can affect near-term supply expectations and buyer availability, typically weighing on copper market sentiment and pointing to potential downward pressure in copper prices over the coming weeks.

title: Aluminum Tariffs Tit-for-Tat Far Cry From Canada's Timid Response to Beijing's Aggression
summary: Canada plans to retaliate with $3.6 billion in tariffs in response to U.S. aluminum import tariffs beginning Aug. 16. Ottawa frames the action as protecting national and industry interests, while denying claims of aluminum flooding in the U.S. The tit-for-tat could reduce trade flows and support aluminium pricing.

title: Banks arranging US$325m for Horizonte's Brazil nickel project – The Northern Miner
summary: Horizonte Minerals said it is arranging up to US$325m in senior secured project finance for construction and development of its Araguaia nickel project in Para state, Brazil. The funding helps progress the nickel project, though no immediate production change is indicated, limiting short-term price pressure.

title: Blackstone Doubles Exploration Capacity at Ta Khoa Nickel-Cu-PGE Project
summary: Blackstone said it doubled exploration capacity at its Ta Khoa nickel-copper-PGE project in Vietnam by adding a second geophysics crew and three drill rigs (plus a fourth owned rig). The company aims to accelerate drilling for a maiden resource this quarter and advance a downstream nickel sulfate study.

title: Copper dips on tepid Chinese demand, U.S. stimulus uncertainty
summary: London copper fell 0.6% as China’s typically weak summer demand weighed and U.S. stimulus uncertainty plus U.S.-China trade tensions added downside risk. Analysts cited weaker July–August wire-rod consumption and near four-month-low Chinese premiums. Stocks rose in China, while LME inventory declines offered limited support. Aluminium edged up.

title: Canada and the United States resume aluminum tariff war
summary: Canada will impose C$3.6 billion in tariffs on US metal products in retaliation for a new US 10% tariff on Canadian non-alloyed, unwrought aluminum. The US aluminum industry would face higher input costs and the trade dispute is set to begin Aug. 16, with possible reciprocal targeting.

title: Aluminium billet inventories fell 6,400 mt on week on smaller arrivals_SMM
summary: SMM reported that China’s aluminium billet inventories fell 6,400 mt on the week to 69,400 mt as of Aug 13. Stocks declined across most major consumption areas, with Foshan posting the largest drop, while Wuxi slightly increased as arrivals rose at some warehouses.

title: Blackstone beefs up drilling fleet in Vietnam nickel hunt
summary: Blackstone Minerals added a second geophysics crew and three drill rigs to expand exploration at its Vietnam Ta Khoa nickel-copper-PGM project, doubling drilling capacity. The company targets massive sulphide vein prospects and plans an initial resource estimate this quarter, potentially increasing future nickel/copper supply expectations, not immediate prices.

title: London Metal Exchange plans low carbon aluminum platform
summary: The LME outlined plans to launch a low-carbon aluminum spot trading platform and an optional carbon data register (LMEpassport) to support sustainability characteristics. Because power can be up to 40% of smelting costs, the initiative aims to enable buyers and sellers to trade lower-emissions aluminum. It also plans cash-settled aluminum scrap contracts.

title: Alcoa Announces Agreement to Extend Consultation Period Regarding San Ciprián Aluminum Plant in Spain and Pursue Potential Sale
summary: Alcoa extended the consultation deadline for collective dismissal and is evaluating a potential sale of its San Ciprián, Spain aluminium smelter (228,000 tpy) to GFG Alliance. The plant will keep operating during the sale review. If no deal is reached, talks shift to a social plan or permanent layoffs.

title: Horizonte secures $325m in financing for Araguaia nickel project in Brazil
summary: Horizonte Minerals secured a $325m syndicated loan to fund construction and development of its Araguaia nickel project in Brazil. The financing supports pre-production capex for Stage 1 and moves the project toward construction, with funding closing expected by end-2020, subject to approvals and COVID-related delays.

title: Copper slips on weak Chinese demand, Chile turns on supply taps
summary: Copper eased 0.8% as worries about South American supply disruptions receded and attention returned to weak, seasonally softer Chinese demand. Miners in Chile and Peru ramped back up after COVID and lockdown effects. Analysts noted China’s stimulus impact was largely already felt, weakening sentiment.

title: Alcoa Extends Formal Consultation Period Regarding San Ciprin Aluminum Plant
summary: Alcoa and worker representatives agreed to extend the formal consultation period for potential collective dismissal at the San Ciprin aluminum plant in Spain to Sept. 28, 2020. The review includes evaluating a potential sale to GFG Alliance, covering a 228,000 t/yr smelter and casthouse, while the facility keeps operating.

title: Canada says big winners of Trump aluminum tariff are foreign
summary: The article headline says Canada claims the biggest beneficiaries of Trump’s aluminium tariff are foreign firms. Such statements relate to aluminium trade diversion and supply effects that can influence near-term pricing expectations, but the excerpt provides no specific data on volumes, retaliation, or immediate market impact.

summary: Horizonte Minerals says it is arranging up to US$325 million in senior secured project financing to fund construction and development of its Araguaia nickel project in Brazil’s Para state. The news supports progress toward future nickel production, but it is unlikely to significantly move near-term prices within weeks.

title: American tariffs on Canadian aluminum, Nickel Belt MP Marc Serre, Liberals
summary: A Nickel Belt MP criticizes renewed U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum, calling them “unjustified.” The article says Canada may counter with measures and that Ottawa will consult industry on aluminum products worth $3.6 billion over 30 days. The tariff threat targets tens of thousands of aluminum-linked jobs.

title: American tariffs on Canadian aluminum, Nickel Belt MP Marc Serre, Liberals
summary: Canada’s Nickel Belt MP Marc Serre criticizes renewed U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum, citing a 10% duty and potential $3.6B of targeted aluminum products over 30 days, alongside Canada’s planned countermeasures. The dispute threatens aluminum trade flows and near-term price expectations, weighing on sentiment.

title: Aluminum shortage affects Cape Girardeau County Businesses
summary: Cape Girardeau and Jackson-area businesses report frequent shortages of canned beverages due to limited aluminum supply. Convenience stores receive smaller shipments of canned drinks, while a local metal recycler sees aluminum inflows and customers increasing. The piece suggests manufacturers can’t produce cans fast enough amid pandemic-driven bulk buying.

title: London Metal Exchange plans low carbon aluminum platform | News
summary: The LME outlined plans for a low-carbon aluminum spot trading platform and a voluntary carbon-information register (LMEpassport), citing smelting’s high power-related emissions. title: United States re-imposes aluminum tariffs on certain Canadian aluminum products | Dentons
summary: The article states that the United States re-imposes aluminum tariffs on certain Canadian aluminum products. title: Shanghai copper on track for weekly loss as China data fails to lift prices
summary: Shanghai copper is set for a weekly decline as worse-than-expected China data failed to boost demand expectations and uncertainty persists over additional U.S. virus relief. The September ShFE contract falls, while LME copper is flat-to-higher intraday. Aluminium output is at records, and nickel trends higher.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 258,000 wmt on week_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose by 258,000 wmt to 8.45 million wmt in the week to Aug. 14. In nickel content, stocks increased 1,900 mt to 67,800 mt. Stocks also rose at seven major ports to 6.79 million wmt, suggesting weaker near-term tightness.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks rose 1,500 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows Shanghai bonded areas’ refined nickel inventories rose 1,500 mt week-on-week to 19,800 mt as of Aug 14.
