Scrutiny could lead automakers to curb purchases and delay approvals of new projects, tightening or disrupting nickel supply expectations.

title: Congo grants new export ban waivers for copper, cobalt, tin
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo granted indefinite export ban waivers for cobalt hydroxide/carbonate and certain tin concentrates, and also a waiver for copper concentrate with the duration still to be determined. The move reflects limited smelting/refining capacity and should ease short-term supply constraints, supporting copper and cobalt sentiment.

title: Expansion of Chile's Los Pelambres copper mine delayed 6 months
summary: Chile’s Los Pelambres copper mine expansion has been delayed by six months. The postponement pushes back incremental output timing relative to earlier plans, tightening the forward supply outlook. Such supply-schedule uncertainty typically supports copper prices as markets adjust expectations over the coming weeks.

title: China turns net aluminum importer in July amid rare buying spree
summary: China’s July aluminium imports jumped nearly sevenfold, turning the world’s biggest producer into a net importer for the first time since 2009. The spike followed a favourable arbitrage between lower LME prices and higher domestic prices in China, bringing in cheaper metal even after the window later closed.

title: Tiwai Point aluminium smelter closure: calls for managed transition
summary: Southland leaders urged political parties to support a managed transition for the planned August closure of Rio Tinto’s Tiwai Point aluminium smelter. The government is in talks with Rio Tinto and Meridian Energy, discussing a transition package to implement regional projects and employment support for affected workers.

title: London copper rises as inventories slip to 13-year low
summary: London Metal Exchange copper rose 0.9% to about $6,546/t as LME-approved inventories fell to a 13-year low, tightening near-term supply expectations. A weaker U.S. dollar also boosted demand for USD-priced copper. Fitch forecasts COVID-related declines in 2020 mine output, further supporting sentiment.

title: Cobre joins copper hunt in elephant country
summary: Cobre Limited is acquiring a controlling 51% interest in Kalahari Metals’ ground on Botswana’s Kalahari Copper Belt, expanding its copper exploration beyond Western Australia. The belt is seen as highly prospective for sediment-hosted copper. Drilling is already underway, supporting bullish sentiment for copper despite no near-term output.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Aug 24): Shanghai nonferrous metals declined for the most part, nickel advanced 1.34%_SMM
summary: SMM said Shanghai nonferrous prices were mostly lower in low downstream season: copper -0.83% and aluminium -0.44%, while nickel rose 1.34% as the dollar index fell. Copper was supported by PBOC liquidity injection, aluminium tracked positioning/arbitrage, and nickel focused on key resistance levels.

title: Jaguar Land Rover upcycles aluminium to cut carbon emissions by a quarter
summary: Jaguar Land Rover’s REALITY project develops a process to upcycle aluminium waste from vehicles and consumer products into premium automotive-grade alloys for prototypes. The company claims recycling cuts production CO2 emissions by up to 26% and can reduce virgin aluminium use via blending, supporting more recycled aluminium in automotive demand.

title: Copper rises as LME inventories dwindle to 13-year low
summary: Copper rose as LME warehouse inventories fell below 100,000 tonnes, the lowest since 2007, alongside a cash premium indicating tight nearby supply. Demand hopes in China and risk-on sentiment after an FDA COVID-19 plasma authorization plus a weaker dollar lifted prices. The piece also notes stronger aluminium import and premium expectations, with nickel up too.

title: Moscow Exchange Trading In Futures Contract On Norisk Nickel Ordinary Share
summary: Mondo Visione reports that the Moscow Exchange began trading a futures contract linked to Norilsk Nickel ordinary shares. Since Norilsk Nickel is a major nickel producer, the development is relevant to nickel sentiment and hedging, but it is not a direct supply-demand or pricing change, implying limited near-term price impact.

title: Nevada Copper Restarts Production
summary: Nevada Copper said it restarted milling operations at the Pumpkin Hollow underground project after a temporary COVID-19 suspension. The plant resumed processing on Aug. 20 and will ramp up using about 160,000 tons of stockpiled ore, supplemented by development and stope material, boosting near-term copper supply.

title: Aluminum Can Shortage Is Now Causing Beer Shortages!
summary: Nationwide shortages of aluminium beverage cans are causing beer shortages, with brewers reporting extended wait times for can orders and some smaller players unable to get orders fulfilled. Increased demand from beer and canned wines, plus limited manufacturing capacity until end-2021, suggests near-term aluminium supply tightness.

title: Elon Musk Is Going to Have a Hard Time Finding Clean Nickel
summary: Tesla and EV makers face trouble sourcing “clean” nickel as accidents and deep-sea tailings concerns in Indonesia and other regions draw scrutiny. Analysts note difficulty approving new nickel projects while prices are low and environmental risks persist, which could reduce compliant supply and support nickel prices.

title: Spot copper premiums in Shanghai fell amid thinned trades_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that Shanghai spot copper cathode premiums fell on Aug 25 as trading volumes were thin and downstream buying demand stayed sluggish. Standard-grade premiums dropped versus the SHFE August contract, while high-quality premiums also declined. The end of long-term contracts increased available supply, pressuring premiums further.

title: Canadian firm Midland signs nickel exploration funding deal with BHP
summary: Midland Exploration’s subsidiary secured a funding arrangement with BHP’s Rio Algom to finance 100% of its nickel exploration in northern Quebec (Nunavik) up to C$1.4m annually for at least two years, with potential further work and a later JV. The move aligns with rising EV battery metal demand, supporting nickel sentiment.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Aug 25): Shanghai nonferrous metals declined for the most part, nickel advanced 0.95%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous broadly fell as bullion prices dropped, with copper down ~0.25% and aluminium down ~0.48%, while PBOC liquidity easing supported copper. Nickel rose ~0.95% despite broader weakness, amid monitoring of price ranges and open interest changes. Overall signals are mixed and short-term.

title: Brazil outage buoys Alumina amid fruitful smelter talks
summary: Alumina producers warn that Brazil’s biggest refinery will run at reduced rates for at least three months, creating a projected global alumina shortage. Alumina expects the shortage to support prices. Talks with power generators aim to stabilize operations at Victoria’s Portland aluminium smelter, reinforcing tight supply expectations.

title: Rio Tinto enters option deal for ALX's nickel project in Saskatchewan – The Northern Miner
summary: ALX Resources entered an option deal with Rio Tinto for its Falcon nickel project in northern Saskatchewan. Rio may acquire up to an 80% interest, subject to terms. The news highlights continued investment interest in nickel supply, which can support near-term nickel sentiment despite likely limited immediate output effects.

title: Zambia's ZCCM-IH seeks to take control of Glencore's Mopani Copper Mines
summary: Zambia’s ZCCM-IH is seeking a controlling stake (potentially ~51%+) in Glencore’s Mopani Copper Mines after a dispute over Glencore’s plan to suspend operations citing low copper prices and COVID disruptions. Zambian authorities are negotiating to keep production running, despite prior care-and-maintenance expectations.

title: ALX signs option agreement with Rio Tinto for Canada's Falcon nickel project
summary: ALX Resources signed an option agreement with Rio Tinto to earn up to an 80% interest in the Falcon nickel project, renamed Firebird, via staged exploration spending. The deal covers a Canadian site with prior magmatic nickel-copper-cobalt drilling results, signaling renewed nickel-focused supply prospects and sentiment.

title: The hidden plants that 'bleed' nickel
summary: Researchers are searching Indonesia’s nickel-rich soils for plants that naturally accumulate high levels of nickel, enabling “phytomining” by harvesting shoots and burning them to recover nickel. Field work is preliminary and positioned as an alternative to open-pit mining, potentially affecting nickel supply prospects but not showing near-term production changes.

title: China's copper cathode imports increased in July_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s copper cathode imports rose to 555,000 mt in July (+14.24% from June, +89.93% y/y) as domestic demand recovered and smelter maintenance tightened supply. Imports helped cover the supply gap, while exports fell to 10,400 mt in July and declined year on year overall.

title: Canterbury Resources unveils maiden resource for historic Idzan Creek and Wamum copper-gold deposits
summary: Canterbury Resources released maiden inferred resource estimates for the Idzan Creek and Wamum copper-gold deposits in Papua New Guinea. Idzan Creek contains 288,000t at 0.28% copper plus gold; Wamum contains 281,000t at 0.29% copper. It remains early-stage, with approvals and further drilling pending.

title: Nickel price hits nine-month peak
summary: Nickel prices rose in Shanghai and London to their highest since November, with Shanghai up as much as 1.7% on Tuesday. The gain was linked to declining laterite ore inventories at Chinese ports and hopes for improving demand, though high stainless steel inventories and additional Indonesian supply temper the bullish outlook.

title: Copper rises as investors cheer trade talks, COVID-19 treatment
summary: Copper prices rose as investors cheered smoother U.S.-China trade talks and encouraging COVID-19 treatment news. Tightness supported the move: LME copper inventories fell to about 95,525 tonnes, lifting nearby spreads. The weaker U.S. dollar also helped demand; nickel prices rose as well.

title: China's imports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis in July exceeded exports for the first time since 2009_SMM
summary: China’s July imports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis (391,237 mt) exceeded exports (373,400 mt) for the first time since 2009. Import volumes surged as the SHFE/LME aluminium price ratio rose and arbitrage opened, alongside stable downstream demand and improved auto-sector operations.

title: Vedanta moves SC against Madras HC order on Sterlite copper plant
summary: Vedanta has appealed to the Supreme Court to challenge a Madras High Court decision that denied reopening of the Sterlite copper unit in Tuticorin, closed since May 2018 over pollution concerns. The Tamil Nadu government has filed a caveat, and the case turns on environmental and legal constraints to restarting copper production.

title: Rio Tinto eyes nickel near Stony Rapids
summary: Rio Tinto Exploration Canada signed an agreement with ALX Resources to take up to an 80% stake in a nickel project near Stony Rapids, Saskatchewan. Rio would spend up to $12 million on exploration over six years plus $125,000 in cash. The move is seen as endorsement of nickel potential.

title: Hannan Metals Ltd.: Hannan Provides Update On The Tabalosos Copper Silver Project, Peru
summary: Hannan Metals reports remote study results for its Tabalosos copper-silver project in Peru, defining target zones over a 30-km trend with reported high-grade copper and silver in selective grab samples, and outlines plans for further reconnaissance and airborne geophysical surveys. It also notes COVID-19 disruption in the district.

title: Nickel hits 9-month high on solid demand, supply worries
summary: Nickel prices rose to a nine-month high as steady demand from stainless steel supported sentiment, while supply risks increased after flooding in Indonesia’s Weda Bay Industrial Park forced parts of PT Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park to halt operations. Nickel futures on LME and ShFE climbed on tighter supply expectations.

title: Nickel hits 9-month high on demand boost, supply worries
summary: Nickel prices rose to a 9-month high as demand from the stainless steel sector stayed firm and improved China appliance exports and EV momentum boosted outlook. At the same time, supply concerns grew after flooding at Indonesia’s Weda Bay smelting facility forced operations to halt, tightening expectations.

title: China's copper concentrate imports rose 12.6% MoM in July _SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: China’s copper concentrate imports rose 12.6% month-on-month to 1.8 million mt in July, though they were down year-on-year. Improved logistics after local lockdowns eased lifted shipments from Chile and Peru, among others. SMM expects imports to peak in September, supporting near-term refined supply expectations.

title: Inventories of aluminium billet in China declined 3,800 mt on week_SMM
summary: SMM data showed Chinese aluminium billet inventories across five main consumption areas fell 3,800 mt week on week to 56,200 mt as of Aug 27. Drawdowns in Wuxi, Huzhou and Nanchang contributed most, while Foshan rose slightly and Changzhou was unchanged.

title: Technavio Research: COVID-19 Pandemic Impact on Global Aluminum Extrusion Market 2020-2024
summary: Technavio’s research release discusses COVID-19’s mixed impact on the global aluminum extrusion market (2020-2024), citing positive demand drivers such as solar/automotive and construction-related lightweight material use. The report emphasizes lockdown, supply chain disruption, and demand destruction scenarios but includes no concrete aluminum price or inventory data.

title: In terms of value, the aluminum rolled products market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 6.7% between 2020 and 2025
summary: Reportlinker projects aluminum rolled products market growth (CAGR 6.7% from 2020-2025) driven by automotive and construction demand, while noting COVID-19 is expected to impact the market severely. The piece is descriptive and forward-looking without concrete near-term supply, inventory, or price drivers for aluminium.

title: Copper price to extend rally on "signs of Chinese panic buying"
summary: Copper is expected to extend its rally as inventories fall and Chinese demand remains strong. The piece also cites pandemic-hit supply disruptions affecting sources in South America, the U.S. and Africa. With copper approaching $3/lb, market momentum is portrayed as supported by tightening supply.

title: Pacific Empire Signs Letter of Intent to Option the Pinnacle Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Empire Minerals signed a non-binding LOI granting an option to earn up to a 70% interest in the Pinnacle copper-gold project. The deal depends on exploration spending and cash/share payments. The release cites historical copper and gold anomalism and anticipates further diamond drilling, but no near-term production impact.

title: Class 1 Nickel & Technologies: Working Towards Nickel-Cobalt Sulfide Production
summary: Class 1 Nickel & Technologies is promoting its Alexo-Dundonald project in Ontario, describing past-producing high-grade nickel sulfide mines and plans to drill and restart production. The deposits also include nickel-copper-cobalt and PGEs, but the article provides no near-term output change, limiting price impact expectations.

title: Exclusive: Iranian vessel loads with Venezuelan alumina, amid closer ties - sources | News
summary: Reuters reports an Iranian-flagged vessel loaded alumina at Venezuela’s CVG Bauxilum port and is sailing toward Iran, amid escalating Iran–Venezuela trade under U.S. sanctions. Alumina is crucial for aluminum production, and Washington has sanctioned Iran’s metals sector, but the cargo’s final use is not confirmed.

title: Chinese Panic Buying Could Fuel A Copper Rally
summary: Copper prices near $3/lb on New York/LME amid sharply lower visible inventories (including 13-year low LME stocks) and strong Chinese demand with importing at record rates. Pandemic disruptions hit South American/US/Africa supply, scrap flows have fallen, and Roskill expects further upside.

title: Class 1 Surface Samples confirm high grade mineralization; Assays validate historic Nickel-Copper-Cobalt-Platinum-Palladium
summary: Class 1 Nickel reports verification results from surface samples and re-sampled core at the Alexo-Dundonald project, confirming high-grade Ni-Cu sulphide mineralization. Assays show nickel grades up to 20.9% and ranges of nickel from open-pit samples, with copper/cobalt mineralization reproducible in historical core.

title: Brixton Metals to Acquire the Trapper Gold-Copper Property and Related Royalties Further Expanding its Thorn Project
summary: Brixton Metals said it will acquire the Trapper gold-copper property and related royalties adjacent to its Thorn project, and terminate existing NSR royalty burdens. The Trapper mineralization is linked to a copper-gold trend, but the announcement is a portfolio/royalty transaction with no near-term production impact mentioned.

title: Falling production, increasing demand push nickel prices to a nine-month high
summary: The article headline attributes a rise in nickel prices to falling production alongside increasing demand, pushing nickel to a nine-month high. This points to near-term supply tightness and improved demand expectations, which would typically support upward nickel price pressure over coming days to weeks.

title: National commits to 'facilitating negotiations' to keep aluminium smelter at Tiwai Point open, as Rio Tinto says it could stage a longer exit if it gets a 'fixed and fair' electricity transmission price
summary: New Zealand’s National plans to facilitate negotiations to reduce Transpower’s electricity transmission charges for Rio Tinto’s Tiwai Point aluminium smelter. Rio says it could stage a longer exit only with a “fixed and fair” transmission cost. Government backs commercial talks to prevent an August shutdown.

title: Copper set for third straight weekly rise after Fed policy shift
summary: Copper prices are set for a third straight weekly gain after traders interpreted a Fed policy shift as keeping rates low and weakening the dollar. LME three-month copper rose 0.4% and SHFE October copper gained 0.6%. Nickel also edged higher, while nickel smelter restart and mine easing are cited.

title: Investment in nickel expansion at Boliden Harjavalta
summary: Boliden will invest EUR 40m to expand its Boliden Harjavalta nickel smelting operations, adding a new concentrate dryer, more electric smelting and granulation capacity, and automated tapping. Feed capacity is set to rise from 310 to 370 ktonnes raw material per year, mainly implemented in 2021, aimed at improved competitiveness and lower CO2 intensity.

title: Iranian Vessel Loads With Venezuelan Alumina, Sources Tell Reuters
summary: A Reuters report says an Iranian-flagged vessel loaded Venezuelan alumina at CVG Bauxilum and sailed toward Iran. Alumina is refined from bauxite and is used to produce aluminum. The shipment occurs amid U.S. sanctions on Iran’s metals sector, suggesting tightened feedstock conditions and potential upward pressure for aluminium prices.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 36,000 wmt to 8.35 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 36,000 wmt from Aug 21 to 8.35 million wmt by Aug 28. In nickel content, stocks dropped 300 mt to 67,000 mt. Stocks at seven major ports fell 226,000 wmt to 6.36 million wmt.

title: Copper hits fresh 2-year high on weak dollar, falling stocks
summary: Copper rose to a fresh two-year high as the dollar weakened and LME visible inventories continued drawing down, boosting the cash premium. The Fed’s policy stance and a Reuters poll pointing to improving Chinese factory activity also supported demand expectations. Indonesia mine/smelter disruptions ending further aided sentiment, lifting aluminium and nickel too.

title: Feds rule Santee Cooper can't stop Goose Creek from powering SC aluminum plant
summary: A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission order requires South Carolina’s Santee Cooper to grant the city of Goose Creek access to power lines feeding the Century Aluminum smelter. The city wants to source out-of-state electricity to lower costs. Santee Cooper may appeal, but the ruling is a near-term step favoring cheaper power access.

title: Trump Administration Re-imposes Sec. 232 Tariff on Canadian Primary Aluminum | Dorsey & Whitney LLP
summary: The Trump administration re-imposed a 10% Section 232 tariff on Canadian-origin primary aluminum imports after a surge in shipments since the May 2019 tariff truce. Canada retaliated with a 10% surtax on a range of U.S. aluminum goods. The move targets unwrought, unalloyed aluminum and can disrupt market flows.

title: Why America and El Paso are running out of aluminum cans
summary: The article reports a shortage of aluminum cans in the U.S., including El Paso, driven by unprecedented demand for canned beer and soft drinks during the pandemic. Breweries and distributors face extended wait times for can orders and some unfulfilled orders, prompting manufacturers to import billions of empty cans to boost supply.

title: Venezuela Reportedly Sends Ship Full of Aluminium to Iran Following Fuel Deliveries From Tehran
summary: A general cargo ship departing Venezuela is reported to carry about 23,000 tonnes of aluminium, after Iranian fuel deliveries to support Venezuela’s refinery restart under US sanctions. The move reflects tighter Caracas–Tehran trade links and shifts near-term aluminium export flows, potentially affecting physical aluminium availability.

title: Copper Prices Rally On Chinese Panic Buying
summary: Copper prices rallied above $3/lb as global visible stocks fell sharply and inventories in LME warehouses hit 13-year lows. The article attributes gains to booming Chinese buying, import demand for refined copper, and reduced scrap inflows after rule delays, alongside pandemic-hit South American, U.S., and African supply disruptions.

title: Officials quash plan to develop Philippines' biggest copper mine | News | Eco-Business
summary: Officials in Tampakan, Philippines, canceled a municipal agreement tied to Sagittarius Mines’ plan to develop the Tampakan project, Southeast Asia’s largest known undeveloped copper and gold reserves. Local lawmakers cite a lopsided deal and governance failures, increasing the risk of delays. Legal and permitting uncertainty may weigh on copper supply expectations.

title: China copper wire and cable operating rates fell sharply in August as projects construction slowed amid the hot weather and heavy rainfalls_SMM
summary: SMM says China copper wire and cable producer operating rates dropped to 97.02% in August, down 4.6 points m/m, as orders from State Grid and outdoor construction fell during hot weather and heavy rainfall. High copper prices kept inventories low. September rates may rise, but environmental inspections could weigh.

title: Intermediate products of nickel hydro-metallurgy imports decreased in July_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s imports of intermediate products for nickel hydrometallurgy fell to 21,200 mt in July, down 21% from June and 45% versus a year earlier. The decline is mainly attributed to much lower imports from Papua New Guinea. Inventories are adequate, suggesting no immediate supply tightness for nickel sulfate inputs.

title: It takes time for aluminium consumption to recover notably, despite upcoming peak season _SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium processor operating rates dipped to 77.2% but are likely to rebound slightly. Foil demand holds in peak season while extrusion/plate/sheet and alloy ingot demand shows mild recovery. Bullish sentiment stems from lower supply of imported scrap and alloy ingots and closures among scrap-based billet producers; exports stay weak.

title: Two under-the-radar ways to play the aluminum can shortage
summary: COVID lockdowns are accelerating demand for packaged food and drinks, triggering an aluminum can shortage. Beverage makers report tighter aluminum supply, pressuring their margins. Traders highlight can producers Ball and Crown as beneficiaries and analysts say aluminum charts suggest a retest of 2019 highs, implying bullish near-term price pressure.

title: Chile's copper output drops 4.6% y/y in July to 467,913 tonnes
summary: Chile’s copper output declined 4.6% year-on-year in July to 467,913 tonnes, according to the headline data. As Chile is a key global supplier, lower production can reduce near-term material availability, shifting expectations toward a tighter balance and typically pressuring copper prices lower in the coming days.

title: Beirut explosion creates boom in demand for glass, aluminium
summary: A Beirut port explosion shattered windows and doors across much of the city, triggering a surge in orders for glass and aluminium for repairs and reconstruction. The article notes production jumped and market prices for these materials rose rapidly, while supplies and affordability lagged amid Lebanon’s wider economic crisis.

title: Chinese aluminium company Zhongwang scales back European operation
summary: Zhongwang said it has scaled down its European aluminium sales operation due to EU anti-dumping investigations and pandemic-driven economic weakness. A restructuring in Europe includes staff reductions, with business from China uncertain. The EU opened two investigations into Chinese aluminium extrusions and flat-rolled products.

title: Copper price leaps to 26-month high on strong Chinese demand
summary: Copper prices rose sharply to a 26-month high as Chinese economic recovery gained momentum, boosting demand for the world’s largest copper-consuming nation. The move helped copper clear the US$3/lb threshold, indicating stronger near-term buying expectations in the physical and futures markets.

title: Aluminum Can Shortage Affecting Local Breweries - WCCB Charlotte's CW
summary: Local breweries report an aluminum can shortage as at-home drinking and spiked seltzer demand rise during COVID-19. A can producer cannot keep up with demand, pushing up beer can availability and procurement costs. Brewers are considering sourcing cans from Mexico to secure steady supply, indicating tight aluminum packaging demand.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper to Acquire Copper North Mining
summary: Granite Creek Copper Ltd. agreed to acquire all outstanding shares of Copper North Mining Corp. in an all-share deal, consolidating the advanced-stage Carmacks copper project with Granite Creek’s Stu copper-gold prospect in Canada’s Yukon. The release focuses on project synergies and potential drilling, not immediate copper market supply changes.

title: Sohar Aluminium hot metal production soars to new record in 2019
summary: Sohar Aluminium (Oman), a major aluminium smelter, reported record 2019 hot metal production of 390,516 tonnes and 390,449 tonnes of finished goods after efficiency improvements following a 2017 technical glitch. About 158k tonnes of hot metal were supplied to local processors, with expected higher local uptake later in 2020.

title: China nickel manufacturing expanded for sixth consecutive month in August _SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s downstream nickel sectors expanded for a sixth month in August, with the downstream PMI rising to 53.24 and production and new orders sub-indices improving. Raw materials inventories returned to expansion and buyers remained willing to accept high feedstock prices, suggesting supportive near-term nickel demand.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Sep 1): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, aluminium fell 0.27%_SMM
summary: SMM reports most SHFE nonferrous metals rose on Sept 1 as China’s Caixin/Markit manufacturing PMI beat forecasts and stayed in expansion. Copper gained 1.92% with optimism and earthquake-related worries about tight Chilean supply. Nickel rose 1.84%. Aluminium edged down 0.27%.

title: Mining Stocks Are Rising on Higher Gold and Copper Prices. There's More to Come.
summary: Mining stocks rose early Tuesday as the weaker U.S. dollar supported gold and Chinese manufacturing data lifted copper prices. The piece suggests further gains by implying copper price strength is driving equity performance, reflecting improved demand expectations tied to near-term macro signals.

title: Kakula Copper Mine Underground Development Exceeds 1,840 Metres in August; More than 20.6 Kilometres Now Complete
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says underground development at the Kakula Copper Mine reached 1,842 metres in August (over 20.6 km total) and is ahead of schedule, with stockpiles and planned transition to higher-grade zones (+5% to +8% copper) expected to improve. Processing plant construction and long-lead equipment deliveries are progressing for first production in 2021.

title: Tesla's Nickel Problem: The quest for sustainable sourcing
summary: Tesla’s CEO discusses securing a “giant contract” for nickel suppliers, noting Tesla may struggle to find environmentally and socially responsible nickel sources. Indonesia dominates expected nickel supply growth, driven by EV battery demand, but environmental impacts raise sourcing risks. The piece is mostly about sourcing sustainability, not immediate market disruption.

title: Electric Car Batteries Are Going to Need a Lot of Nickel
summary: The article says EVs will drive a major rise in nickel use because nickel-rich battery chemistries (NCM/NCA) contain large nickel shares, especially for larger battery packs. It notes Indonesia is expected to supply most of the incremental nickel but raises concerns about mining waste practices.

title: Canyon Resources raises about XAF6 bln for final feasibility studies of the Minim Martap bauxite project
summary: Canyon Resources raised about XAF6 billion by issuing new shares to fund definitive feasibility studies for its Minim Martap bauxite project in Cameroon. The investor cited bauxite/alumina contacts in Australia and China. The study refines earlier cost estimates and aims to move toward production in 2022, with no near-term output change.

title: Copper eases on stronger dollar, recovering Peru production
summary: Copper prices eased from a 26-month high as the U.S. dollar strengthened, making dollar-priced metals more expensive for non-dollar buyers. At the same time, output in Peru—copper’s second-largest producer—was reported to be almost fully recovered from COVID-19 impacts, limiting downside momentum.

title: Blackstone's Ban Chang discovery delivers broad nickel intercepts
summary: Blackstone Minerals reports continued drilling at its Ban Chang sulphide discovery in Vietnam, intersecting broad nickel mineralisation (e.g., 9.60m at 0.84% Ni and 14.65m at 0.74% Ni) with associated copper grades. The company aims for a maiden resource and potential feed for its mothballed Ban Phuc plant, citing strong current nickel prices.

title: Peru copper production falls 2.2% in July to 198,796 tons -official
summary: Peru’s copper output fell 2.2% year-on-year in July to 198,796 tons, according to the vice minister of energy and mines. The ministry said copper production is largely recovered from early-pandemic disruption, but July still shows reduced output, which can pressure near-term copper supply expectations.

title: China's aluminium import surge a sign of global disconnect: Andy Home
summary: China imported more aluminium than it exported in July, after a rare net-import turnaround since 2009. Primary imports rose sharply, driven by a wide arbitrage between higher ShFE and lower LME prices plus supply-chain disruption and stockpiling. Alloy imports also surged, amid scrap-flow realignment and export challenges.

title: Blackstone Intersects Broad Zones Of Nickel Sulfides At Ban Chang
summary: Blackstone reports additional high-grade massive sulfide Ni-Cu-PGE intersections at its Ban Chang prospect, including several drill results with elevated nickel and copper grades across broader intervals and an expanded target strike length. The company plans an aggressive drill-out to define resources and support downstream nickel sulfate studies.

title: China's aluminum import surge a sign of global disconnect
summary: China’s aluminum trade inverted into a rare net-import position, with primary aluminum imports jumping in June-July and alloy imports reaching unprecedented levels. The surge is attributed to an arbitrage gap between ShFE and LME and supply disruptions. Exports fall amid weak external demand and anti-dumping barriers, suggesting near-term aluminium strength.

title: Copper Prices at 2-Year High on Strong Manufacturing Data
summary: The article headline states copper prices are at a two-year high following strong manufacturing data. The implied market reaction is that better manufacturing activity expectations boost near-term demand for industrial metals, providing upward support for copper prices over the coming days.

title: Rio Tinto starts drilling Janice Lake copper-silver project in Canada
summary: Rio Tinto Exploration Canada has started drilling at Forum Energy Metals’ Janice Lake sedimentary copper-silver project in Saskatchewan. A rotary air blast drill will test historical and newly mapped copper showings over a 52 km property to define mineralisation extent and guide a future diamond drill program.

title: China's aluminium import surge a sign of global disconnect
summary: China imported more aluminium than it exported in July, an unusual outcome for the world’s largest producer, which accounted for about 57% of global output. The imbalance suggests China’s aluminium flows were tighter than usual, potentially boosting near-term support for global aluminium prices.

title: Copper edges up as data shows steady economic recovery in China
summary: London copper rose slightly as Reuters cited data showing China’s service sector and manufacturing recovery after COVID-19. The piece also notes a GEM deal to buy battery-grade nickel chemicals in Indonesia. Supportive macro demand expectations were the main driver, with nickel only indirectly boosted.

title: Copper eases as Chile, Peru supplies pressure prices
summary: Copper futures fell as supply disruptions eased in Chile and Peru, pressuring short-term prices. Three-month LME copper dropped 0.8% to $6,643.5/t, and October SHFE copper declined 0.8%. Despite depleted inventories, Reuters cited improving mine output and a stronger U.S. dollar.

title: New orebody boosts Western Areas' Leinster nickel mine development
summary: Western Areas says a newly discovered orebody at its Leinster nickel mine in Western Australia will boost mine development. The update strengthens expectations for future nickel feed and potential output ramp, which can increase short-term supply confidence and support nickel pricing over the coming days to weeks.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 4,000 mt on week on larger arrivals_SMM
summary: SMM data shows China’s aluminium billet inventories rose 4,000 mt week on week to 60,200 mt as of Sept 3, due to higher arrivals. Most consumption areas added stock (except Foshan, which fell), suggesting greater short-term supply and potential downward pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Aluminum can shortage hits local breweries, empties sparkling water aisles
summary: A local grocery retailer in St. Louis experienced empty shelves in the sparkling water aisle for weeks, attributed to an aluminum can shortage. The article notes A-B InBev’s large aluminum bottling/can plant in Arnold supplies cans and lids, indicating constrained packaging supply that can tighten aluminum demand.

title: EEPC urges govt to continue MEIS for aluminium industry exports sans ceiling
summary: India’s EEPC urged the government to continue MEIS for aluminium exports without a reward ceiling after a Sept 1 DGFT notice capped MEIS reward claims. The group says the reduction would hurt competitiveness amid weak global demand and already depressed LME aluminium prices, leaving aluminium exports and prices pressured.

title: Chile's copper output drops 5% in July on Codelco unit stoppages
summary: Chile’s copper output is reported to have dropped 5% in July as Codelco unit stoppages reduce production. The news points to a near-term supply interruption from one of the world’s largest copper producers, which typically raises expectations of tighter availability and supports downward pressure on copper prices.

title: Peruvian copper production down 2.2% in July; zinc output grows y-o-y
summary: The article’s title says Peru’s copper production declined 2.2% in July, while zinc output rose year-on-year. A drop in copper supply from a major producer would likely tighten availability expectations in the near term and weigh on copper prices. Zinc is not tracked here.

title: Backer of tariffs on Canadian aluminum confronts critics in Canada, U.S.
summary: A trade lawyer defending Trump-era fresh tariffs on Canadian aluminum argues the measure is essential to U.S. aluminum producers. He cites alleged earlier surges of Canadian exports into the U.S. and responds to criticism from industry groups in Canada and the U.S. The tariffs target aluminum trade flows.

title: New data casts doubt on Trump's basis for tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: The article says new data undermines Trump’s August claim that Canadian producers flooded the U.S. market with primary aluminium, showing imports and Canadian primary exports declined in May-July. It argues the situation reflects COVID-driven demand shifts and product switching, while tariffs have been contested as unjustified.

title: Copper scrap imports rebounded ahead of new import restrictions in September_SMM
summary: China’s copper scrap imports rose in July and are expected to keep gaining in August as buyers rush shipments before Sept. 1 solid-waste law penalties. Imports likely fall in September due to tighter quota compliance, while higher copper ingot imports have partially offset scrap shortages. Price spreads support demand.

title: Copper heads for historic squeeze with China's demand red-hot
summary: The article says the copper market may face a historic supply squeeze as China’s demand stays extremely strong and exchange inventories fall to the lowest levels in more than a decade. With spot reserves tightening, traders expect a further price surge after copper reached two-year highs above $US6,800/tonne this week.

title: 'Continue MEIS for aluminium industry exports sans ceiling'
summary: India’s EEPC urges the Commerce Minister to continue MEIS incentives for aluminium exports without a ceiling after a DGFT notification imposed a Rs 2 crore per IEC reward cap and a reduced overall MEIS allocation. It argues aluminium exports are already pressured by high duties and weaker LME prices and needs support.

title: Ball Corporation Locates Aluminum Packaging Plant in Pittston, Pennsylvania
summary: Ball Corporation plans to invest about $360 million over multiple years to build a state-of-the-art aluminum beverage packaging manufacturing plant in Pittston, Pennsylvania. The project includes job creation and public funding support. The announcement signals additional aluminum demand, but lacks near-term capacity details to strongly move prices.

title: Company behind tariffs on Canadian aluminum confronts critics in Canada, U.S.
summary: The article discusses U.S. national-security tariffs adding a 10% levy on Canadian aluminum exports, effective Aug. 16, and expected retaliatory measures against U.S. products. Advocates debate whether Canadian imports surged and contributed to falling aluminum prices, but the dispute itself signals near-term trade pressure.

title: This Company Has What Elon Musk Needs ... Nickel This Company Has What Elon Musk Needs ... Nickel
summary: The piece highlights EV and battery growth (higher nickel intensity) as a driver of sharply rising nickel demand, while noting underinvestment and slow ramp-up in nickel supply. It cites forecasts of large demand growth and a likely future supply deficit, suggesting upward price pressure for nickel as markets reprice.

title: Technavio Research: COVID-19: Aluminum Conductors Market 2020-2024 | The Expansion And Revamping Of T&D Networks to boost the Market Growth
summary: Technavio forecasts growth in the aluminum conductors market (2020-2024) driven by expansion and revamping of transmission and distribution networks and renewable generation. It also warns that volatile raw material prices could hamper growth, but the press release lacks specific, near-term aluminum supply or pricing shocks.

title: Copper rises on low stocks, solid Chinese demand
summary: Copper prices rose as low LME-approved stocks, disrupted ore supply, and solid Chinese demand supported the market. Fitch Solutions pointed to potential further inventory tightening through mid-October and noted ongoing year-on-year weakness in ore output growth. Funds’ net long positions were at record highs, adding bullish sentiment.

title: New Caledonia's SLN nickel company acts as insolvency looms
summary: SLN, New Caledonia’s major nickel employer, seeks court protection as insolvency looms and it runs down a remaining $600m loan. The firm applied for a permit to export two million tonnes of nickel ore for cash, but local opposition threatens raw-material sales. Eramet says it likely won’t provide more support.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 504,000 wmt to 8.85 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data showed nickel ore inventories across all Chinese ports rose by 504,000 wmt to 8.85 million wmt between Aug 28 and Sep 4. In nickel content, stocks increased to 71,000 mt, while seven major ports grew by 274,000 wmt to 6.64 million wmt, implying less near-term tightness.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks remained unchanged on week_SMM
summary: SMM data show Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories held steady at 20,800 mt. The import window for nickel plates and nickel briquettes stayed closed and foreign trading was limited. Although 1,000 mt of plates and 600 mt of briquettes arrived, further flows are destined for import/domestic rather than bonded warehouses. Nickel prices began declining after rising.

title: Some Japan aluminium buyers agree fourth-quarter premium at $88/T, up 11% on quarter - sources
summary: Japanese aluminium buyers reportedly agreed Q4 primary aluminium premiums at $88/t, up 11% from the previous quarter and above $79/t paid earlier. Producers initially sought $95–$98/t. Talks set the regional benchmark. Demand from autos and electronics is improving, and the LME aluminium rally may support premiums further.

title: Copper prices rise on low stocks, solid Chinese demand
summary: Copper prices rose as LME-approved warehouse inventories fell to their lowest in nearly 15 years, ore supply from South America was disrupted, and China’s manufacturing/services recovery supported demand. LME three-month copper gained, with Fitch citing room for further inventory tightening. Nickel also rose modestly.

title: Judge's ruling allows PolyMet copper-nickel mine to move ahead
summary: A judge ruled that PolyMet’s copper-nickel mine can move forward, clearing a key legal hurdle. The decision supports expectations that the project will advance toward production rather than face prolonged delays, which is typically constructive for sentiment and prices of copper and nickel.

title: Judge's ruling allows PolyMet copper-nickel mine to move ahead
summary: A judge ruled that PolyMet’s planned copper-nickel mine can move ahead, removing a legal obstacle that had threatened delays. The decision is likely to improve short-term expectations for future copper and nickel supply, adding modest bullish support to both metals’ prices.

title: Environment watchdog states "depressing" condition of number of Norilsk Nickel facilities
summary: Russia’s environmental regulator says inspections of Norilsk Nickel facilities show a “depressing” situation and notes a trend of transferring assets to smaller dependent companies. The checks follow a major CHPP-3 fuel spill in Norilsk, with Rosprirodnadzor estimating 148 bln rubles in environmental damages.

title: Work gets underway to create the Black Butte Copper Mine
summary: Construction has begun on the Black Butte underground copper mine in Montana, including a planned 5,000-foot access tunnel, treated water system, and future mill site. The project is described as environmentally responsible, with operations expected in 2022. Near-term production effects appear minimal for copper prices.

title: Copper rises on hopes of upbeat China trade data
summary: Copper rose on Monday as hopes grew for a sustained China economic recovery, supported by expectations for stronger August exports and imports, alongside a US unemployment rate falling to 8.4%. The report links the rally to improved employment data and anticipated trade momentum; aluminium was mixed.

title: Operating rates of copper rods are expected to decline in September with high inventories_SMM
summary: SMM says copper rod makers’ operating rates fell to 72.66% in August, with declines expanding into September expectations. Downstream cable orders weakened, shipments missed expectations, and finished inventories rose sharply from 12.91% to 17.51%. Producers plan maintenance or reduced output as peak-season demand remains sluggish.

title: Hot Chili eyes look-alike Cortadera copper-gold target in Chile
summary: Hot Chili says drilling and geochemical surveys at its Cortadera project in Chile have identified a new Cortadera North target with copper oxides and copper-bearing porphyry veins, potentially increasing the scale of mineralisation ahead of a maiden resource estimate. Ongoing RC and diamond drilling supports a copper-positive sentiment outlook.

title: Blackstone to drill new nickel sulphide target in Vietnam
summary: Blackstone Minerals begins drilling a new nickel sulphide target (Ta Cuong) at Vietnam’s Ta Khoa project, part of a push to define deposits near Ban Chang and Ban Phuc. The company highlights a mothballed Ban Phuc processing plant and prior production of nickel and copper, aiming to fast-track feasibility work as nickel prices stay firm.

title: Operating rates across major aluminium processor recovered slightly during peak season_SMM
summary: SMM said operating rates among major aluminium processors edged up to 77.4% week-on-week as September demand improved across sectors like autos, construction, electronics and packaging. While some segments softened, the outlook calls for slight further increases. Secondary alloy output rose on stronger orders and scrap availability, supporting near-term sentiment.

title: Copper rises as solid Chinese exports lift recovery hopes
summary: Copper prices rose after solid Chinese exports data signalled a faster, more balanced recovery, supporting demand expectations. Gains were tempered by lower-than-expected Chinese imports. The report also mentions LME aluminium edging higher and nickel slightly lower, while Chinese import easing and stimulus expectations shape near-term sentiment.

title: Company behind tariffs on Canadian aluminum confronts critics in Canada, U.S. - MRO Magazine
summary: A trade lawyer defending the White House’s new 10% tariffs on Canadian primary aluminium argues Canadian imports surged and contributed to a sharp aluminum price fall. Canadian and U.S. industry groups dispute the data, citing pandemic-driven demand collapse, while retaliation measures on aluminium-linked goods loom.

title: No New Century for New Caledonia nickel
summary: New Century Resources has withdrawn its offer to buy Vale’s New Caledonian nickel assets due to inability to secure funding. The cancellation leaves the Pacific nation’s nickel sector in disarray and shifts attention to IGO. The piece signals deal uncertainty but no confirmed immediate supply disruption.

title: Exclusive: China's refined nickel output declined 2.25% MoM to 14,300 mt in August_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s refined nickel output fell 2.25% month-on-month to 14,300 mt in August. Gansu declined, while Xinjiang rose after COVID restrictions eased. Tianjin and Guangxi smelters suspended production due to raw-material issues. SMM expects output to drop further to 13,700 mt in September, amid planned maintenance.

title: Sale of New Caledonia's Vale nickel plant fails
summary: New Century Resources failed to complete a deal to buy Vale’s Goro nickel plant in New Caledonia after negotiations couldn’t meet shareholders’ risk-reward needs. Vale is considering shutting the plant if no solution emerges, while the province resists closure to protect jobs. Nickel supply risk increases.

title: Exclusive: China's copper cathode output rose 8.14% on the month to 810,500 mt in August_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s copper cathode output reached 810,500 mt in August, up 8.14% from July, aided by minimal maintenance and sufficient scrap feedstock. With pandemic-related raw material constraints easing, smelters are raising scheduled production to meet annual targets. Output is expected to rise further in September.

title: London copper falls on U.S.-China tension, stronger dollar
summary: London copper slid as U.S.-China tensions escalated and the stronger U.S. dollar made greenback-priced metals more expensive for non-dollar holders. Three-month LME copper eased, while Shanghai’s October contract ended higher. Tight LME warehouse supplies supported fundamentals, but risk sentiment dominated.

title: Exclusive: China's nickel sulphate output jumped 15.69% on the month to 60,500 mt in August_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s nickel sulphate output rose 15.69% m/m to 60,500 mt (13,300 mt nickel content) in August, including higher battery-grade production. Nickel salts plant operating rates improved with recovering downstream demand, aided by new lines. September output is also expected to rise further.

title: Move aside robots, Tesla bets on aluminium casting
summary: Tesla plans to replace hundreds of robots at its new German plant with giant aluminium casting (“Gigapress”) machines, using cast modules to replace many riveted or glued chassis components on the Model Y. The move could increase near-term expectations for aluminium casting demand, though volumes are not specified.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Announces Outstanding Economic Results of the Independent Integrated Development Plan (IDP) for the Tier One Kamoa-kakula Copper Project
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reported strongly positive results from updated DFS, PFS, and PEA for its Kamoa-Kakula copper project in the DRC. The DFS confirms economics for the 6-Mtpa Kakula mine under construction, the PFS adds Kansoko feed, and the company says it is fully funded for first copper in under a year.

title: Copper dips as sizzling rally loses some of its heat
summary: Copper fell 0.8% amid rising U.S.-China tensions, softer stock markets and a stronger U.S. dollar, but prices stayed near two-year highs. Tight LME inventories (15-year low) and expectations for continued Chinese demand supported the rally. LME aluminium and nickel also edged down on macro sentiment.

title: GBML Announces LOI to Exclusively Negotiate an Option to Lease the Mineral Rights in the Michigan Based Sawyer Camp, a Prospective Nickel, Copper Property
summary: Global Battery Metals Ltd. announced a non-binding LOI to exclusively negotiate an option to lease mineral rights at the Sawyer Camp, a prospective nickel-copper property near Lundin’s Eagle Mine. The company plans a short due-diligence drill program (three core holes) pending permits, with no production or offtake details provided.

title: Funds collide with fundamentals in red hot copper cauldron
summary: Funds are piling into CME copper longs as China’s physical copper purchases surge, pulling refined metal into China and accelerating LME stock depletion. LME inventory is down about 70% since late May and backwardation/tighter spreads persist, reinforcing a marketwide physical tightness and bullish momentum.

title: Funds collide with fundamentals in red hot copper cauldron: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist Andy Home says copper has rallied as China’s unprecedented buying draws down Western supply, while LME stocks have fallen sharply since May. Funds have flipped to net longs and CME positioning is near a multi-year high. Backwardation and rising roll costs signal physical tightness and support higher prices.

title: Tech Talk: Move aside robots, Tesla bets on aluminium casting
summary: Tesla plans to reduce robot usage at its Brandenburg, Germany plant by using large aluminium casting (Gigapress) machines to produce simpler chassis modules for the Model Y. The approach replaces multiple glued/riveted parts with single cast aluminium modules, potentially boosting near-term aluminium demand expectations.

title: Camino to Commence Drilling in September at Its Los Chapitos Copper Project in Peru
summary: Camino plans to start drilling in September at its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru. The move suggests continued exploration/development progress that could improve longer-term copper supply expectations. In the near term, such development news typically provides modest support to copper sentiment, though immediate production impact is limited.

title: Blackstone Commences Drilling New Nickel Targets At Ta Cuong
summary: Blackstone Minerals has started drilling at the Ta Cuong nickel sulfide prospect using EM targeting. Historic unassayed holes reported include intervals grading ~0.66% Ni and up to ~4.47% Cu. The company plans further rigs across the Ta Khoa nickel-copper PGE district to expand potential supply.

title: NZ First leader Winston Peters to meet with Tiwai Point aluminium smelter workers
summary: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters met Tiwai Point aluminium smelter workers, reiterating a promised 20-year agreement with a fair electricity cost to keep the plant operating. Rio Tinto previously said it would end production, threatening 2,500 jobs. Peters criticized other parties’ shifting plans, aiming to reassure continued output.

title: Five Additional Infill Holes Continue to Expand Higher-Grade Core, Drilling of Additional Targets Now Underway at the Crawford Nickel-Cobalt Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel reported additional infill drilling results at its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project, including multiple wide intersections grading around 0.30–0.40% nickel and extending higher-grade mineralization in both western and eastern Main Zone areas. Updated resource incorporation is expected later in September, with further assays to follow.

title: Jamaica clears debt owed to alumina partner Noble Group
summary: Jamaica’s Clarendon Alumina Production (CAP) repaid Noble Group nearly US$136 million of outstanding loan and interest tied to the Jamalco alumina refinery. The settlement enables planned incorporation and an IPO. The piece links the original debt to depressed alumina markets and says Jamalco losses reflect weaker demand.

title: Shanghai metals drop on dollar strength, but London copper gains
summary: Reuters reports base metals in China fell broadly as a stronger U.S. dollar and weaker stocks and oil hurt risk appetite. London copper rebounded after prior-session losses. Aluminium and nickel were also lower in Shanghai, while LME nickel slipped slightly. Underlying drivers cited include shifting sentiment and inventory dynamics.

title: Saft's new Compact nickel batteries to streamline footprint and maintenance budgets for industrial sites - NEWS, POWER
summary: Saft launched Compact maintenance-free industrial backup nickel batteries designed as a drop-in replacement for VRLA systems, requiring only a single-step charging voltage and using existing cabinets/chargers. The product targets offshore oil & gas, utilities, manufacturing, and rail sites, touting lower maintenance and long life, which could modestly support nickel demand expectations.

title: Callinex Discovers Two High Grade Copper, Gold, Silver and Zinc Lenses in the Flin Flon Mining District of Manitoba
summary: Callinex reported discovery drilling at its Pine Bay Project in Manitoba, with drill hole PBM-111 returning high-grade copper (up to 4.12%) over short intervals and associated precious/other metals. The company is mobilizing further drilling after conductive BPEM results, but no production timeline is provided.

title: Adventus and Salazar Add Second Drill Rig To Exploration Program at the Pijili Project and Provide a Drilling Progress Update
summary: Adventus and Salazar report progress on drilling at the Pijili porphyry copper-gold-molybdenum project in Ecuador, adding a second rig and intersecting mineralized breccia and sulphide intervals. Copper grades are referenced from prior surface sampling, while new core assays are expected in October, limiting immediate market impact.

title: FPX Nickel Announces Positive Preliminary Economic Assessment for Baptiste Project with US$1.7 Billion After-Tax NPV, 35-Year Mine Life, 4-Year Payback and C1 Operating Costs of US$2.74/lb Nickel
summary: FPX Nickel said its preliminary economic assessment for the Baptiste nickel project delivers a US$1.7 billion after-tax NPV, a long mine life and a four-year payback, with C1 operating costs of about US$2.74/lb. The results are likely to bolster nickel market expectations and sentiment.

title: Thunderstruck Drills Turning at Its High-Grade Korokayiu Copper-Zinc Project
summary: Thunderstruck Resources began a funded 1,500-meter drill program at its Korokayiu VMS project in Fiji, following high-grade 2019 results that included meaningful copper grades alongside zinc. The company also plans geochemistry and an Induced Polarization survey. The release is exploration-focused with limited immediate supply impact but supports copper sentiment.

title: Maine governor concerned about US tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: Maine’s governor expressed concern about potential US tariffs on Canadian aluminum. Such tariffs can reduce imports from Canada, tightening near-term availability for US buyers and supporting higher aluminum prices. The effect is expected within days to weeks as trade expectations and pricing adjust.

title: FPX Nickel Announces Positive PEA for Baptiste Project
summary: FPX Nickel announced positive 2020 PEA results for its wholly owned Baptiste nickel project in central British Columbia. The study forecasts 35 years of mine life, ~99 million lb/year nickel, low C1 costs, and strong after-tax NPV/IRR metrics. Optimizations and potential low-carbon positioning are also discussed.

title: Scott, Sununu and Mills call on president to reverse tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: Vermont, New Hampshire and Maine governors urged President Trump to reverse newly reimposed 10% tariffs on non-alloyed unwrought aluminum imports from Canada, effective Aug. 16. They warn the trade tax will hurt US manufacturers and can affect industries such as aluminum-can packaging.

title: New England governors ask Donald Trump to repeal Canadian aluminum tariff
summary: Three New England governors urge Trump to repeal the 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum, arguing it will artificially inflate costs for aluminum goods and hurt manufacturers during the pandemic. The tariff reinstated on Aug. 16 prompted Canada to retaliate dollar-for-dollar with aluminum tariffs, raising pricing pressure.

title: Pacific Empire Commences Drilling at Weedon Copper-Gold Property with Assays Pending from Worldstock Drilling
summary: Pacific Empire Minerals begins reverse-circulation drilling at its Weedon copper-gold property, with assays expected later and reports geophysical/geochemical targets including copper-gold-molybdenum anomalies. At a separate Worldstock property, RC holes intersected sulphides and increased copper anomalism with depth, suggesting a porphyry system. No production impacts are announced.

title: Scott joins New England counterparts in denouncing aluminum tariff
summary: Gov. Phil Scott joined New Hampshire and Maine officials in urging the Trump administration to remove a reinstated 10% tariff on Canadian aluminium. The governors cite higher input costs for local businesses and consumers and warn of trade disruption. Canada has said it will retaliate with dollar-for-dollar countermeasures.

title: NNE governors ask for reversal of tariff on aluminum imports
summary: NNE governors have asked for the reversal of tariffs on aluminum imports. Easing or removing import duties would lower the landed cost of imported aluminum and potentially increase near-term supply availability, which can weigh on aluminum prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: London copper slips ahead of ECB meeting; Sino-U.S. rift weighs
summary: London copper edged down while Shanghai copper rose ahead of an ECB decision, as Sino-U.S. trade tensions kept investors cautious. LME copper stocks fell to multi-year lows, but Shanghai inventories rose. Nickel output increased, while aluminium and nickel were largely flat in Shanghai and LME aluminium rose slightly.

title: Bauxite Hills Mine to lose 240 jobs as Weipa facility struggles to land Chinese contracts
summary: Metro Mining plans to shut its Weipa Bauxite Hills bauxite mine for at least nine months after failing to secure Chinese contracts. The company attributes the problem to weaker aluminium prices and China’s reliance on onshore stockpiles. The cut in production and demand uncertainty could weigh on aluminium sentiment near term.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 3,400 mt on week on larger arrivals_SMM
summary: SMM said China aluminium billet inventories rose 3,400 mt week on week to 63,600 mt as of Sept 10, driven by larger arrivals. Stocks increased in most major consumption regions including Foshan, Changzhou, Huzhou and Nanchang, while Wuxi declined slightly.

title: Primary aluminium inventories rose 3,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that China’s social inventories of primary aluminium across eight consumption areas, including SHFE warrants, rose by 3,000 mt from a week ago to 764,000 mt as of Sept 10. The continued buildup suggests slightly looser near-term supply, a potential headwind for aluminium prices.

title: Russian watchdog says sues Norilsk Nickel unit for $1,965,440 | Companies
summary: A Russian natural resources oversight agency has filed a 148 billion ruble ($1.97 million) suit against Norilsk-Taimyr Energy Company, part of Norilsk Nickel, over damage from an emergency spill in Norilsk. The regulator assessed July environmental damage at 147.7 billion rubles, while Norilsk Nickel disputed the figure.

title: Sterlite Copper economically beneficial, but lacks local connect
summary: Vedanta’s Sterlite Copper smelter in Tuticorin has been shut since 2018, cutting about 40% of India’s copper smelting capacity. Domestic refined production fell, leading to higher copper imports and lower exports. Downstream reliance on sulphuric acid and logistics also declined, reinforcing supply tightness.

title: India plans to restrict copper, aluminium imports with an eye on China -sources
summary: Sources say India is considering restricting imports of copper and aluminium with an eye on China. If implemented, tighter cross-border supply would reduce availability for buyers in the near term and likely lift price expectations for both metals.

title: India plans to restrict copper, aluminium imports with an eye on China -sources
summary: Sources say India plans to restrict copper and aluminium imports as part of a strategy aimed at China-linked trade flows. If implemented, the measure would likely reduce near-term supply available to buyers, supporting domestic and regional price expectations for copper and aluminium over the next several weeks.

title: India plans to restrict copper, aluminium imports with an eye on China - sources
summary: India’s mines ministry plans tighter screening of copper and aluminium imports, moving them toward a restricted list requiring licenses for each shipment. The goal is better data to manage potential dumping and support self-reliance. With China a key aluminium supplier, controls could constrain short-term imports.

title: India plans to restrict copper, aluminium imports with an eye on China - sources
summary: India plans to require importers of copper and aluminium to register and likely obtain permits/licenses for each shipment as authorities consider adding the metals to a restricted list. title: India plans to restrict copper, aluminium imports with an eye on China
summary: India plans to raise surveillance and potentially require permits for every shipment of copper and aluminium, aiming to curb imports from China and other Asian exporters to protect domestic producers. title: India plans to restrict copper, aluminium imports with an eye on China
summary: India plans to increase surveillance and introduce permits for individual shipments of copper and aluminium imports, with the intent to restrict imports from China and other Asian suppliers. title: 2,600 g/t Silver and 1.4% Copper pop as VR completes an array of early-stage surveys across the Reveille property and CRD mineral system in Nevada
summary: VR completed early-stage survey arrays across the Reveille property/CRD mineral system in Nevada, prompting a market “copper pop” (cited as 1.4% copper) alongside silver values. While still early-stage, the drilling/survey update can lift near-term expectations for copper resource potential.

title: Russian watchdog files $2 bln lawsuit against Nornickel for fuel spill damage
summary: Russia’s environment watchdog filed a 148 billion rouble ($2.0bn) lawsuit against Nornickel over a May diesel spill near Norilsk. Nornickel had disputed the amount and set aside reserves, pressuring first-half profits. Analysts said the figure may not threaten stability but could affect debt and dividends, weighing sentiment.

title: India plans to restrict copper, aluminium imports - Malaysia a major exporter
summary: India plans to increase surveillance and impose tighter controls on copper and aluminium imports, including requiring importers to register and potentially obtain permits for individual shipments. summary: India plans to tighten copper and aluminium import controls by increasing surveillance, requiring importers to register, and introducing permits for individual shipments. The policy aims to curb inflows from China and other Asian nations to protect domestic producers, potentially reducing near-term market supply and supporting prices.

title: SK, ILJIN clash over battery copper foil plants in Malaysia
summary: SK Nexilis and ILJIN Materials dispute plans to build additional copper foil plants for EV batteries, with SK weighing Malaysia as one candidate location. ILJIN argues SK may “free ride” on its site-matching and infrastructure efforts. Both firms are also expanding elsewhere, indicating ongoing copper foil supply growth.

title: 2-month queue remains for aluminium at Istim's Port Klang LME sheds
summary: The article highlights that aluminium at Istim’s Port Klang LME sheds faces a 2-month queue. Such extended waiting times signal constrained warrant/warehouse availability and slower delivery through the port, which can tighten prompt supply expectations and provide near-term support for aluminium prices.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Announces C$2.4 million Private Placement Financing
summary: Granite Creek Copper Ltd. announced a C$2.4 million private placement, including flow-through proceeds, to fund exploration and development of its Stu Copper-Gold project and other working capital needs. The company highlights progression of its Yukon copper asset portfolio, but provides no immediate production or supply/cost shock.

title: Tesla in talks to buy low-carbon nickel from Canada's Giga Metals, sources say
summary: Tesla is in talks with Canada’s Giga Metals to secure low-carbon nickel (and possibly cobalt) for EV batteries from the Turnagain mine. The supply deal would likely be financed and backed by long-term offtake. While primarily a nickel story, it supports bullish sentiment toward battery metal demand and supply visibility.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 55,000 wmt to 8.91 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories across Chinese ports rose 55,000 wmt to 8.91 million wmt between Sept 4 and Sept 11, with Ni content up 400 mt to 71,400 mt. Stocks at seven major ports fell 285,000 wmt to 6.35 million wmt.

summary: Tesla is reportedly in talks to buy low-carbon nickel from Canada. summary: Reuters reports Tesla is in talks to buy low-carbon nickel from Canada. title: Nationwide aluminum can shortage has Michigan breweries scrambling
summary: Michigan breweries are scrambling as a nationwide aluminum beer can shortage limits deliveries through the rest of the year. The shortfall is linked to pandemic-driven shifts toward packaged beer and reduced can return/recycling. Breweries report running out soon, while suppliers like Ball expand output of can styles.

title: Exclusive: Tesla in talks to buy low carbon nickel from Canada - sources
summary: Tesla is reportedly in talks to buy long-term low-carbon nickel from Giga Metals’ Turnagain mine in Canada, potentially via financing and offtake arrangements. summary: Tesla is reportedly in discussions with Canada’s Giga Metals to develop and secure long-term low-carbon nickel (and possibly cobalt) for EV batteries. summary: Tesla ordering aluminium casting presses and the broader shift toward low-carbon aluminium are driving new market pricing. title: Copper Continues To Outperform | SafeHaven.com
summary: SafeHaven argues copper has outperformed other metals due to COVID-related supply-side fears in South America and a persistent market deficit. title: Copper slips on strong dollar, China demand hopes limit losses
summary: Copper prices slipped to a one-week low as a stronger U.S. dollar made metals costlier for non-dollar buyers. LME inventories ticked higher, reinforcing downside. Hopes for stronger China demand limited losses. Aluminium and nickel also fell on broader base-metal risk sentiment.

title: Tesla reportedly looking to source low-carbon nickel from Canada
summary: Tesla is reportedly in discussions to contract with Canada’s Giga Metals to source low-carbon nickel for EV batteries, using a lower-emissions mining process and Quebec/B.C. hydro power. The potential new supply agreement could affect near-term market expectations for nickel demand and sustainability-linked pricing.

title: Copper Prices Are Soaring On Growing Battery Metal Demand
summary: Copper prices are described as soaring, supported by battery/EV demand and a weaker U.S. dollar, with additional momentum from supply-side anxiety in South America amid COVID-related disruptions and mine suspensions. Aluminium is also higher, but more tied to currency moves and Chinese demand/import dynamics.

title: Tesla in talks to purchase nickel from Canadian mining firm, claims sources
summary: Tesla is reportedly in talks with Canadian miner Giga Metals about developing and purchasing nickel from a planned low-carbon mine. Reuters cites sources suggesting a long-term supply deal, while Musk urged miners to expand efficient, sustainable nickel production to win Tesla contracts. The news is supportive for nickel supply expectations.

title: FPX Nickel releases 'large-scale' PEA for Baptiste
summary: FPX Nickel has released results of a “large-scale” preliminary economic assessment for its Baptiste nickel project in British Columbia’s Decar nickel district. The company’s CEO says the work establishes Baptiste as a major development opportunity, which may support expectations for future nickel supply and valuations.

title: Tesla In Discussions To Source Low-Carbon Nickel From Canada
summary: Tesla is reportedly in discussions with Canada’s Giga Metals to help develop a nickel mine and source low-carbon nickel for battery production. Musk has urged higher-volume, environmentally sensitive nickel mining. The project’s lower emissions could help Tesla meet supply needs, supporting nickel demand expectations despite no final deal confirmed.

title: Norilsk Nickel estimates amount of fuel in soil at 12,000 tonnes at spill
summary: Norilsk Nickel says it has nearly finished collecting diesel fuel that entered water bodies near Norilsk after an accident at CHPP-3, estimating the fuel volume at around 12,000 tons and noting 188,000 tons of contaminated soil removed. Rosprirodnadzor estimates higher figures, and legal proceedings are underway.

title: Trilogy: Copper prospect still profitable at higher costs
summary: Trilogy Metals said its Interior Alaska Arctic hard-rock project remains profitable despite higher costs. A feasibility study estimated post-tax NPV of about $1.3 billion at current metal prices and over $1.1 billion using longer-term forecasts, supporting expectations for development of hard-rock copper (and associated metals).

title: Tariffs on Canadian aluminum are senseless and hurt American interests
summary: The article argues that the U.S. is re-imposing 10% tariffs on Canadian primary aluminum, despite prior temporary supply shifts during COVID-related shutdowns. It claims the move would reduce North American supply and push regional aluminum prices higher, while Canada’s $3.6 billion retaliatory tariffs would further disrupt trade.

title: 5 Top Weekly TSX Stocks: Positive Results Move Copper Mountain
summary: The article reports that Copper Mountain Mining’s drill results from its Ingerbelle copper-gold pit tested the depth of its copper project in British Columbia. The company’s shares rose 22% on the week. As a copper producer, the positive results may bolster near-term expectations for copper supply and sentiment.

title: Mothballed Mt Lyell copper mine in Queenstown offered for sale after coronavirus stalls restart plan
summary: Vedanta’s Mt Lyell copper mine in Tasmania is being offered for sale after COVID-19 delayed a planned restart. The mine has been in care and maintenance, with state funds spent on infrastructure to enable a quick recommencement. Local authorities view the sale as positive, but production timing remains uncertain.

title: Automobile sector replaced real estate as major driver of aluminium demand_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates at major aluminium processors rose to 77.7% and that orders across plate/sheet, strip and foil continue to recover, led mainly by automobiles. Aluminium foil demand is improving as AC peak ends, while extrusion remains weak. Primary and secondary alloy output and operating rates are also expected to rise.

title: Resurgent no more?:How Covid-19 put the brakes on nickel's great recovery
summary: The piece explains how Covid-19 derailed nickel’s 2020 recovery. Lockdowns reduced Chinese stainless steel demand and increased stocks. It also notes Indonesia’s nickel ore export ban remains, while production is expected to rise, creating a primary surplus and lowering prices versus the earlier ban-driven bullish outlook.

title: The Importance of Copper In China's Economy | Institutional Investor
summary: China’s strong manufacturing rebound is lifting copper demand, with imports surging to record levels. Supply is also constrained as Peru’s output fell and Chile’s Codelco temporarily closed/suspended operations. Stimulus, infrastructure spending, renewables, and EV ambitions are expected to further support prices.

title: Cerro Grande Mining Corporation Announces Finalization of Agreement to acquire the Assets relating to the Pimentón Copper Gold Mining Project
summary: Cerro Grande Mining announced it has finalized an asset purchase agreement to acquire concessions and related rights for the Pimentón copper-gold project in Chile, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The deal price is C$3.9bn across multiple installments. Near-term copper output changes are not specified, limiting impact.

title: Demand cheer helps copper hold near 26-month peak
summary: Copper prices rose as strong Chinese demand, historically low LME-approved inventories, and a weaker U.S. dollar supported sentiment. Cash copper traded at an 18-month high premium versus the three-month contract, while warehouse stocks hit the lowest since 2005. Aluminium and nickel also gained in the same session.

title: Canada to unveil retaliatory measures against United States this week in aluminum dispute
summary: Canada will announce retaliatory measures against the U.S. in response to U.S. Section 232 tariffs on Canadian aluminum imposed in August. The retaliation will be tariffs on U.S. imports containing aluminum, set to start Sept. 16. The dispute could disrupt aluminum trade volumes and weigh on prices short term.

title: Golden Arrow Provides Exploration Update, including First Program at Rosales Copper Project, Chile
summary: Golden Arrow says its first field program has begun at the Rosales Copper Project in Chile, including soil sampling and geological mapping, and cites historical copper grades from nearby targets. The release is an exploration update and does not indicate production, mine operations, or immediate supply changes for copper.

title: Tesla reportedly in talks to buy low-carbon nickel from Giga Metals
summary: Tesla is reportedly in discussions with Giga Metals to develop a large mine to access low-carbon nickel for EV batteries. Giga’s Turnagain project uses CO2 and hydropower to produce carbon-neutral nickel. While details are unconfirmed, the potential agreement supports near-term nickel demand expectations.

title: Second bid for New Caledonia's Vale nickel plant
summary: Byms plans a second bid to buy Vale’s nickel plant in New Caledonia, after an earlier Australian offer was withdrawn and concerns grew about potential closure. Management says operations could stop by end-October without a new owner, risking supply disruption. Local and government efforts aim to preserve 3,000 jobs and the plant.

title: Evening Update: Chinese firm amasses data on influential Canadians; Ottawa to reveal measures against U.S. in aluminum dispute
summary: Canada is preparing retaliatory measures against the U.S. following Trump’s August tariffs on Canadian aluminum. The announcement, expected this week, would target U.S. imports—many containing aluminum—amounting to C$3.6 billion and taking effect Sept. 16, potentially tightening trade and influencing aluminum prices.

title: Governors of Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont want Trump administration to reverse tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: Governors of Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont are asking the Trump administration to reverse tariffs on Canadian aluminum. If tariffs are rolled back, it would likely improve near-term aluminum import economics and expectations for availability and demand, providing upward support to aluminium prices over the coming days.

title: Construction work begins on copper mine project in Montana
summary: Construction began at Montana’s Black Butte Copper Project after the state issued permits for initial site work.
