Sandfire Resources America can build roads, pads and a reservoir while further permits for tunneling and processing continue. Opponents have a pending lawsuit, but progress on development is mildly supportive for copper supply expectations.

title: Will the prolonged state of catastrophe in Chile affect copper supply? _SMM
summary: Chile extended its coronavirus state of catastrophe by another 90 days. Despite prolonged restrictions, Chilean copper mine production has been barely affected: output in the first seven months rose year-on-year, and Codelco reports sharply falling infections. Copper production is expected to remain largely unaffected as anti-spread operations continue.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Expands Kenbridge Nickel Project Land Position and Finds Additional Nickel Targets
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. announced it staked additional claims adjacent to its Kenbridge Nickel Deposit and identified further nickel-related exploration targets using spectral and radar surveys. The company plans surface exploration and a definition program in autumn 2020 and winter 2021, but provides no new resource or production changes.

title: Response to U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum to come today, Trudeau says
summary: Trudeau says a response to U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminium is expected “today.” Such tariff actions can disrupt trade flows and change near-term expectations for aluminium supply and pricing. The announcement implies immediate market uncertainty, with tariff pressure generally bearish for aluminium prices in the short term.

title: Response to U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum to come today: Trudeau
summary: The U.S. Trade Representative’s office is tentatively lifting a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum, expecting Canadian exports to “normalize” over the rest of the year. The U.S. is effectively standing down in the dispute, reducing tariff-driven costs and supporting sentiment for aluminium prices.

title: Canada to unveil retaliatory action today for 'unjust' U.S. aluminum tariffs: Trudeau
summary: The U.S. called off a newly imposed 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum for now, withdrawing current penalties and substituting monthly import-volume terms to monitor flows until after the U.S. election. Canada suspended planned retaliation. Tariffs could return if volume limits are exceeded, keeping uncertainty in place.

title: Siberian Academics, Nornickel strike cooperation agreement
summary: Russia’s Siberian Branch of the Academy of Sciences signed a cooperation agreement with Norilsk Nickel covering environmental issues in the Arctic, including joint efforts to respond to an oil spill and study climate changes. The program includes scientific expeditions and lab work, with first results expected in late 2020—no clear supply impact signaled.

title: Atlantic Nickel's Santa Rita mine life extended to 34 years
summary: Atlantic Nickel released a preliminary economic assessment for its Santa Rita nickel-copper-cobalt open-pit mine in Brazil, extending projected mine life to 34 years. The update suggests more sustained availability of nickel (and associated copper) supply, which can influence market expectations over the coming weeks.

title: Response to U.S. aluminum tariffs to come today: Trudeau
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports that Canada (Trudeau) says a response to U.S. aluminum tariffs will come today. The announcement signals potential changes to aluminum trade terms, which can shift market expectations for near-term supply and demand. Details of retaliatory measures aren’t included in the excerpt.

title: U.S. backs down on aluminum tariffs directed at Canada
summary: The U.S. lifted 10% tariffs on Canadian aluminum retroactive to Sept. 1 after consultations, citing expected lower Canadian shipment volumes. It also outlined conditions to reimpose tariffs if shipments exceed quota thresholds in coming months. Canada threatened retaliation, keeping the outlook uncertain for near-term prices.

title: At 11th hour, U.S. abruptly reverses course, lifts tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: The U.S. drops a 10% tariff on $3.6 billion of Canadian aluminum exports, retroactive to Sept. 1, after a late-stage trade dispute with Canada. USTR says imports should normalize, though it retains a threat of reimposition under conditions, keeping some uncertainty for the future.

title: U.S. yanks Canada aluminum tariffs amid retaliation threat
summary: The U.S. ended a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum, effective retroactively to Sept. 1, citing expectations that Canadian exports will normalize. The move pauses a looming Canada retaliation package and reduces near-term trade friction, while a monitoring window could trigger retroactive tariffs if shipment thresholds are exceeded.

title: U.S. drops 10 percent aluminum tariff ahead of potential retaliation from Canada
summary: The U.S. trade office tentatively lifted a 10% tariff on imports of Canadian non-alloyed unwrought aluminum, expecting Canadian exports to normalize. Canada had threatened retaliation to protect its aluminum industry, but the U.S. is standing down in the dispute, modifying the tariff terms.

title: US Drops Tariffs On Canadian Aluminum Before Retaliation
summary: The headline reports the US is dropping aluminum tariffs on Canada before any retaliatory action. Easing tariff burdens on Canadian aluminum imports can reduce landed costs and affect near-term supply expectations in the US market, influencing aluminium pricing over the coming days.

title: U.S. stands down on aluminum tariff dispute
summary: The U.S. backed down on its tariff dispute with Canada, lifting a 10% levy on aluminum imports from north of the border retroactive to Sept. 1. The USTR expects Canadian exports to normalize, though it will monitor trade and could reimpose if aluminum import levels spike unexpectedly.

title: U.S. drops tariffs on Canadian aluminum ahead of countermeasure announcement
summary: The U.S. dropped tariffs on Canadian aluminum hours before Canada was expected to announce retaliatory measures against U.S. products. The tariffs had been reimposed after U.S. smelters alleged Canadian violations of a 2019 agreement. The dispute may continue, but removal of aluminum tariffs supports prices.

title: NewsAlert: U.S. standing down on aluminum tariffs
summary: The U.S. Trade Representative said it is tentatively lifting a 10% tariff on imported Canadian aluminum, expecting exports to “normalize” over the rest of the year. Easing the tariff reduces trade friction and should improve aluminum import prospects, supporting aluminum pricing in the near term.

title: U.S. Removes Canada Aluminum Tariffs Amid Retaliation Threat
summary: The U.S. is reported to have removed aluminum tariffs on Canada amid threats of retaliation. Easing tariff costs and improving prospects for steadier Canadian aluminum flows would likely support near-term aluminum price expectations by reducing friction in trade.

title: Canadian Press NewsAlert: U.S. standing down on aluminum tariffs
summary: The U.S. Trade Representative’s office said it is tentatively lifting a 10% tariff on imported Canadian aluminium, expecting Canadian exports to “normalize” over the rest of the year. Standing down in the dispute should ease supply frictions and reduce pricing pressure on aluminium in the near term.

title: U.S. Abruptly Reverses Course, Lifts Tariffs on Canadian Aluminum
summary: The U.S. reversed course in its tariff dispute with Canada, lifting a 10% levy on Canadian-made aluminium retroactive to Sept. 1. The change was made because Canadian exports are expected to normalize for the rest of the year, reducing import cost and supply disruption fears.

title: Trump drops aluminum tariffs, sets new trade thresholds just as Ottawa readies response
summary: The U.S. removed tariffs on Canadian aluminium but imposed new import quotas with low monthly thresholds and retroactive 10% tariffs if caps are exceeded. Canada withdrew its planned $3.6 billion retaliation. Analysts warn the quotas could constrain supply and raise uncertainty for aluminium producers and downstream users.

title: U.S. abruptly reverses course; lifts tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: The U.S. lifted a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum retroactive to Sept. 1, resuming duty-free treatment for non-alloyed, unwrought aluminum while imports are monitored. Canada avoided immediate countermeasures. The move is aimed at normalizing flows after a prior surge dispute, with potential near-term price support for aluminium.

title: US drops tax on Canada aluminum, heading off retaliation
summary: The Trump administration ended a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum a month after imposing it, citing that Canadian shipments have returned to normal and retaliation was averted. The US could reimpose if imports surge. The change is expected to reduce aluminum input costs for US buyers.

title: US Removes 10 Percent Tariff On Canadian Aluminum
summary: The US will remove a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports retroactive to Sept 1, following Ottawa’s retaliation threats. USTR expects non-alloyed unwrought aluminum trade to normalize in late 2020, while warning it may reimpose the tariff if monthly import shipments exceed listed maximums.

title: Canada Not Imposing Retaliatory Tariffs After US Lifts Aluminum Duties - Minister
summary: Canada will not retaliate after the US ends its 10% Section 232 tariff on Canadian aluminum retroactive to Sept. 1, 2020. The US resumes duty-free treatment for non-allowed unwrought aluminum, but imposes monthly shipment volume expectations and could reimpose tariffs if volumes exceed set thresholds.

title: The Trump administration drops its aluminum tariffs just hours ahead of Ottawa's planned retaliation
summary: The Trump administration is removing 10% tariffs on Canadian aluminum imports worth $3.6 billion, retroactive to Sept. 1, just before Canada outlines retaliatory measures. USTR expects imports will normalize later in 2020-21. Canada says there’s no deal, but producers welcome tariff relief.

title: U.S. standing down on aluminum tariffs against Canada
summary: The article headline says the U.S. is “standing down” on aluminum tariffs against Canada. Easing or delaying tariffs would improve aluminum import conditions and reduce cost uncertainty, supporting expectations for tighter demand-supply balance in the near term and thus likely providing upward pressure on aluminum prices.

title: Canada welcomes U.S dropping aluminum tariff, but won't back down if re-imposed again
summary: Canada welcomed the U.S. move to drop an aluminum tariff, a development that is likely to ease import costs and improve near-term expectations for aluminum supply and demand. Canada also warned it would not retreat if the tariff is re-imposed, adding some uncertainty for future pricing.

title: U.S. drops tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: The U.S. Trade Representative is lifting a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminium, retroactive to Sept. 1, citing expectations that Canadian exports will normalize. However, a safeguard rule would reapply retroactive tariffs if shipments exceed 105% in any month. Future review is planned later this year.

title: US announces it is dropping tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: The US Trade Representative has resumed duty-free treatment for Canadian non-alloyed, unwrought aluminum, reversing an August plan to reimpose a 10% tariff. The decision follows consultations showing imports should normalize in Q4 2020, with average monthly inflows projected to fall 50% versus earlier months.

title: U.S. scraps 10 pct tariff on Canadian aluminum with imports expected to decline sharply
summary: The U.S. Trade Representative announced duty-free treatment for Canadian aluminum, reversing a previously imposed 10% tariff on certain non-alloyed unwrought aluminum. The decision is linked to expectations that Canadian imports will fall sharply in the last four months of the year, supporting aluminum market sentiment.

title: U.S. Drops Tariff On Canadian Aluminium
summary: The article title says the U.S. has dropped a tariff on Canadian aluminium. Removing or reducing import frictions typically boosts aluminium availability in the U.S. market in the near term, which can pressure domestic and benchmark aluminium prices downward over days to a few weeks.

title: Evening Update: Stroke can be first symptom of COVID-19 in young patients, study shows; U.S. backs down on aluminum tariffs directed at Canada
summary: The U.S. has lifted 10% tariffs on Canadian aluminum, removed retroactively to Sept. 1, after consultations indicating Canadian shipments are set to decline. The U.S. warned tariffs could return if shipment volumes exceed thresholds in coming months, ahead of planned Canadian retaliation.

title: Canada Drops Counter-tariffs Threat After US Nixes Aluminum Levy
summary: Canada and the US avoided a trade war after Washington walked back a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports. Duty-free treatment is retroactive to September 1, though the USTR set shipment caps and warned the tariff may return if limits are exceeded. Canada dropped counter-tariffs.

title: Trump walks back aluminum tariffs on Canada
summary: Trump reversed the planned 10% U.S. aluminum tariff reimposed on Canada, replacing it with a monthly import quota (with limited tolerance) and potential retroactive charges if limits are exceeded. The move avoids renewed trade-war escalation, bringing relief to business groups and reducing tariff-related import uncertainty for aluminum markets.

title: U.S. Drops Tariff On Canadian Aluminum
summary: The headline says the U.S. has dropped a tariff on Canadian aluminum. Removing the tariff should lower landed costs for U.S. buyers and improve import competitiveness, supporting expectations for higher near-term aluminum supply and potentially firmer pricing versus a tariff-on environment.

title: Freeland offers few answers as Trump administration levels strict new quotas on Canadian aluminum
summary: The U.S. removed tariffs on Canadian aluminum but replaced them with strict import quotas and tariff reapplication triggers if monthly thresholds are exceeded. Canada dropped planned retaliation, yet observers warn quotas could constrain Canadian producers and restart trade uncertainty, pressuring aluminum supply expectations and pricing near term.

title: U.S. drops taxes on Canadian aluminum
summary: The Trump administration reversed a recently imposed 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum, ending the added cost for U.S. buyers. Reports say the tariff may be replaced by a monthly export quota. Canada had threatened retaliation if the tariff returned, while business groups opposed the tariff’s higher costs.

title: Canadian Vehicle Manufacturers' Association: CVMA Statement Regarding U.S. Decision to Resume Duty-Free Trade of Aluminum
summary: The Canadian Vehicle Manufacturers' Association welcomed a U.S. decision to resume duty-free trade of non-alloyed, unwrought aluminium retroactive to Sept. 1, 2020. The group said the prior trade issue added unnecessary costs for manufacturers and urged continued Canada-U.S. engagement to avoid further aluminium-related trade barriers.

title: Governors of Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont want Trump administration to reverse tariffs on Canadian aluminum
summary: Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont governors urged the Trump administration to reverse a 10% tariff on Canadian non-alloyed unwrought aluminum. They argue the tariff inflates costs for aluminum-consuming manufacturers and disrupts supply chains, potentially weakening competitiveness and raising prices for downstream goods.

title: EDITORIAL: Sanity prevails in aluminum trade war
summary: The editorial says the Trump administration called a ceasefire and repealed a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports, avoiding Canada’s planned $3.6 billion counter-tariff retaliation. It argues tariffs were unnecessary and could disrupt supply during the COVID-19 recession, implying aluminum prices face less near-term upward pressure.

title: Canada welcomes US decision to drop aluminum tariff
summary: Canada’s finance minister welcomed the US decision to remove a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports. The US will resume duty-free treatment for certain categories from Sept 1, 2020, while keeping a retroactive tariff trigger if shipments exceed expectations. Canada threatens dollar-for-dollar retaliation if tariffs return.

title: U.S. Drops Tariff On Canadian Aluminum Imports
summary: The Trump administration removed a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports, retroactive to Sept. 1, lowering trade frictions for aluminum shipments. Canada and U.S. border businesses praised the move. However, the U.S. warned tariffs could return if imports rise, with Canada indicating possible dollar-for-dollar retaliation.

title: Material Matters: Gold, Copper & Thermal Coal
summary: The piece reports that forward curves for copper (along with nickel and aluminium) are up as global growth improves. UBS notes mine disruptions from mobility restrictions have largely passed, and tight concentrate supply may ease later. Copper supply risk is said to have peaked in 2020, keeping a constructive tone.

title: US scraps 10 pct tariff on Canadian aluminum with imports expected to decline sharply
summary: The U.S. is removing a 10% tariff applied to Canadian aluminium. Despite the tariff removal, the article expects U.S. aluminium imports from Canada to fall sharply. That implies tighter near-term supply availability in the U.S., which would tend to support aluminium prices in the short term.

title: Canada to announce retaliatory measure against US aluminum tariffs
summary: Canada plans to announce retaliatory measures in response to US aluminum tariffs. The move could alter cross-border aluminum supply and pricing expectations by changing import/export flows between the US and Canada. Near-term impact on aluminum prices depends on the scope and form of retaliation, which is not detailed in the excerpt.

title: Copper giant Peru's economy contracted 11.7% in July
summary: Peru’s economy contracted 11.7% in July amid the COVID-19 downturn, with mining and hydrocarbons output down 6.2%. The report notes lower production of several metals, including copper, and highlights Peru’s large export reliance on mining. Weak activity and demand are likely bearish for industrial metal prices.

title: Celsius Resources diversifies into copper-gold in the Philippines
summary: Celsius Resources is acquiring advanced copper-gold projects in the Philippines, including a drilled high-grade copper deposit with long mineralised intervals and assays around ~0.77–0.82% Cu. A maiden JORC resource is planned after COVID restrictions ease. The move cites improved legislation, but has no immediate supply impact.

title: Canada drops counter-tariffs threat after US nixes aluminum levy
summary: Canada avoided a trade war as the US revoked a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports, making duty-free treatment retroactive to September 1. The USTR warned tariffs could be reinstated if imports exceed monthly shipment caps, creating conditional but net support for aluminium prices.

title: No More Tariffs on Canadian Aluminum
summary: The US will drop its tariffs on Canadian aluminum, with the change retroactive to Sept. 1. Canada will not counter with retaliatory measures. Freeland calls it positive for the aluminum industry, and notes the US will retain tariff proceeds accrued during August.

title: EDITORIAL: Sanity prevails in aluminum trade war | St Thomas Times Journal
summary: The editorial reports the Trump administration agreed to a ceasefire and repeal a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum products. It argues tariffs would have raised prices and triggered retaliation. While the dispute could return later, the immediate resolution should ease aluminum import costs and support sentiment for aluminum markets.

title: BeMetals Corp.: BeMetals Commences Phase 2 Underground Drill Program At High-Grade South Mountain Zinc-Silver-Gold-Copper Project
summary: BeMetals announced the start of Phase 2 underground drilling at its South Mountain zinc-silver-gold-copper project in Idaho, targeting extensions and infill in the Texas Zone, where copper-silver-gold targets are highlighted. The program aims to support an updated resource estimate and PEA in 2021; no results are reported now.

title: Tesla in discussions with Canadian mining company for low carbon nickel supply: report
summary: Tesla is reportedly in discussions with Canada’s Giga Metals to develop a mine supplying “low carbon” nickel for lithium-ion battery production. Tesla’s talks follow Glencore cobalt plans and a stated preference for environmentally sensitive sourcing. The project targets 40,000 tonnes of nickel annually for 20 years.

title: US rescinds latest 10% tariff on Canadian aluminium
summary: US rescinded the latest 10% tariff on Canadian aluminium. Removing the tariff should reduce landed costs for US buyers and support additional aluminium imports, easing supply tightness expectations over the coming days and weeks, which is generally supportive for aluminium prices versus a tariff-in place scenario.

title: Norilsk Nickel completes Talnakh concentrator upgrade project in Russia
summary: Nornickel says it has completed its Talnakh concentrator modernization in Russia, increasing throughput from 7.6Mtpa to 10.2Mtpa and reducing tailings losses. The upgrade met targets for nickel and copper recoveries and concentrate quality, potentially supporting near-term supply for nickel and some copper.

title: U.S. removes Canada aluminum tariffs amid retaliation threat
summary: The news says the U.S. removed aluminum tariffs on Canada after discussions involving a potential retaliation threat. Easing tariff barriers would likely increase Canadian aluminum’s competitiveness and raise import availability for the U.S., creating downward pressure on aluminum prices in the near term.

title: 'We are not playing that game': Canadian aluminum producers in tough spot as White House swaps tariffs for quotas
summary: The U.S. initially imposed a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum, then put the tariff on hold and replaced it with export quotas through December. If volumes exceed thresholds, tariffs could be applied retroactively after a review window. The uncertainty around potential re-imposition pressures aluminum supply expectations.

title: Union rally to be held in New Caledonia over sale of Vale nickel plant
summary: A union in New Caledonia called for a rally over the sale process of Vale’s nickel plant. Vale said it may close the facility end-October if no buyer is found. The union wants more time, citing job losses and an economic impact, with a sale attempt previously falling through.

title: Opinion: Score one for Canada: On aluminum tariffs, the U.S. bully blinks
summary: The article says the U.S. backed off planned aluminum levies on Canadian imports hours before Ottawa’s retaliatory tariffs were due. While the U.S. hinted quotas could trigger future reimposition, Canadian officials deny quota negotiations. Overall, the withdrawal reduces near-term aluminum trade risk and supports aluminum prices.

title: How Breweries Can Survive the Aluminum Shortage | Bowditch & Dewey
summary: The piece highlights a national aluminum can shortage blamed on an unprecedented demand surge and delayed deliveries. Breweries and some large producers are conserving can stock, and firms are seeking alternatives like growler refills. The tight aluminum can supply and strong demand are supportive for near-term aluminum sentiment.

title: Trump Administration Lifts Tariff On Aluminum Imported From Canada
summary: The Trump administration lifted a 10% tariff on aluminum imported from Canada after support from U.S. representatives and a request from governors in Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont. The move is described as a win for the regional economy and closer U.S.-Canada cooperation, implying improved aluminum import conditions.

title: Alexander Says Rescinding Aluminum Tariffs On Canada Will Help Tennessee Auto Workers
summary: Sen. Lamar Alexander praised the Trump administration for rescinding aluminum import tariffs on Canada, saying the move will reduce costs for U.S. buyers and help auto workers in Tennessee. By removing a trade barrier on aluminum, the article implies better aluminum availability and upward support for aluminum prices.

title: Copper dips, strong China demand limits losses
summary: London copper edged lower but stayed near a 26-month high as markets expected strong Chinese demand amid improving industrial output and retail sales. U.S. factory output rose but showed strain. China also reported higher aluminium production, reaching records, which affects aluminium supply expectations.

title: Wanbao Mining's DRC Pumpi project produces first batch of copper cathode
summary: Wanbao Mining’s DRC Pumpi project has produced its first batch of copper cathode. The milestone signals new near-term availability of refined copper, which can improve supply expectations and potentially tighten prompt market balances. Other text is mostly about Fastmarkets methodology and unrelated aluminium commentary.

title: China Hongqiao kicks off aluminium production in Yunnan
summary: China Hongqiao has begun first-phase production at a greener aluminium smelter in Yunnan with 1.0 Mt/year capacity, aiming to shift about one-third of output from coal-powered Shandong to hydropower-rich Yunnan amid environmental curbs. The project totals 2.03 Mt/year and targets completion by 2025.

title: Chakana Reports 15.2 Metres of 2.1% Copper at Paloma East
summary: Chakana Copper reported drill results from the Soledad Project’s Paloma East target in Peru, including copper-bearing intercepts such as 2.1% copper over 15.2 metres (within a broader mineralized interval). The release is exploration-focused and does not indicate immediate production, limiting expected near-term copper price impact.

title: Ivanhoe's Congo mine productivity peerless among copper giants
summary: The piece highlights Ivanhoe Mines’ Kamoa-Kakula project on the DRC/Zambia copper belt and notes its exceptionally high productivity among major copper operations. With fewer large-scale new deposits elsewhere, strong project performance can bolster near-term supply expectations, tending to support copper price sentiment.

title: USTR Rescinds 10% Tariff On Canadian Aluminum, Expecting Imports To "Normalize" | Husch Blackwell LLP
summary: USTR rescinded the 10% Section 232 tariff on Canadian non-alloyed, unwrought aluminum retroactive to Sept. 1, 2020, after negotiations. The agency expects aluminum imports to “normalize” in late 2020, though it may reinstate tariffs if monthly volumes exceed 105% of expected levels.

title: Strike threat in New Caledonia over Vale nickel plant plans
summary: Unions in New Caledonia threatened a general strike over Vale’s plans to close its nickel plant if no buyer is found after a failed sale. Vale said the plant could shut end-October, eliminating thousands of jobs. Local bidders have emerged, but acceptance remains unclear.

title: 'We are not playing that game': Canadian aluminum producers in tough spot as White House swaps tariffs for quotas — for now
summary: The U.S. initially imposed a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminium, but then placed it on hold and replaced it with monthly export quotas through December. If Canadian volumes exceed thresholds by more than 5%, tariffs could be reimposed retroactively. The episode increases near-term uncertainty and tightens U.S.-bound supply.

title: Mincor board approves Western Australia's nickel project development
summary: Mincor Resources’ board approved development of its Kambalda nickel project in Western Australia after a four-year hiatus. Secured $55m loan facilities from BNP Paribas and Société Générale and with permitting in place, it expects mobilisation and surface construction to ramp in coming weeks, targeting ore production in the December quarter.

title: Goose Creek and Santee Cooper face off in court over power supply for SC aluminum smelter
summary: Santee Cooper and the city of Goose Creek are in court over who can control the power supply to Century Aluminum’s smelter in Berkeley County. Goose Creek claims it can buy and resell power, while Santee Cooper says it has exclusive rights. Century warns potential closure if the city fails, adding supply risk.

title: U.S. to remove tariffs on Canadian aluminum if imports stay within limits
summary: The Trump administration reached an accord with Canada to cap raw aluminum imports into the U.S. If imports remain within agreed limits, the U.S. will remove the 10% tariff on non-alloyed, unwrought aluminum from Canada, allowing duty-free shipments retroactive to Sept. 1 and expected to normalize volumes.

title: Trump Administration Lifts Reimposed Canadian Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The Trump administration lifted a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports that had been reimposed in August. The move came before Canada’s planned retaliatory tariffs on Sept. 15, and the U.S. also set up monthly quotas for Canadian aluminum imports.

title: U.S.-Canada truce but aluminium is ever more politicised: Andy Home
summary: The U.S. will lift a 10% tariff on Canadian unalloyed primary aluminium after a short-lived reimposition linked to an earlier import “surge.” However, exemptions are conditional on quarterly flow limits, so U.S. aluminium premiums remain volatile, with politics driving regional prices more than supply/demand.

title: London copper hits over 2-year peak on weak dollar, China demand hopes
summary: London copper surged to a more than two-year high, up on a weaker dollar and strong fund buying amid hopes of Chinese stimulus boosting demand. U.S. data disappointed, keeping monetary easing expectations limited. China copper premiums fell, but the market reaction still points to near-term bullish sentiment. Aluminium also rose modestly.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks remained unchanged for four consecutive weeks_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories at 20,800 mt, unchanged for a fourth consecutive week. Nickel prices have also stayed flat. The US dollar premium eased to about $110–120/mt and import losses narrowed, while weaker foreign trade and storage policies support stable bonded stocks.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 43,000 wmt to 8.95 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose by 43,000 wmt to 8.95 million wmt between Sep 11 and Sep 18. In nickel content, stocks increased by 300 mt to 71,700 mt. Inventories at seven major ports rose 167,000 wmt to 6.52 million wmt.

title: Spruce Ridge Resources Limited: Spruce Ridge Resources to Begin Drilling the Great Burnt Copper/Gold Property in South Central Newfoundland
summary: Spruce Ridge Resources said it will begin a ~3,500-metre diamond drilling program on its Great Burnt copper-gold VMS property in Newfoundland. The release cites prior infill copper intersections and suggests drilling could increase mineral resources. It provides no production outlook, so near-term copper supply expectations likely change little.

title: Copper hits two-year peak on speculative buying and China hopes
summary: Copper rallied to a two-year high on speculative inflows as China’s industrial output improved and broader growth expectations rose, while a weaker dollar made metals cheaper. LME copper remained above $6,700 support. Physical premiums in China declined. Aluminium rose, but nickel fell, highlighting copper-led momentum.

title: Fortune Nickel and Gold Inc. Exploration Work on its Gowan Nickel Property
summary: Fortune Nickel and Gold plans to begin an expedited exploration program at its Gowan nickel property in Ontario, including re-drilling and geophysical surveys, with permits and future diamond drilling. The company cites prior high-grade nickel results and includes copper assays, but no near-term production or inventory changes are provided.

title: Zambia Seeks to Buy Bigger Stake in Glencore's Local Copper Unit
summary: Zambia is reported to be seeking to buy a bigger stake in Glencore’s local copper unit. The move could affect expectations around ownership, development and operating terms for copper production in Zambia, potentially influencing near-term copper supply sentiment and prices.

title: Tesla in talks to buy low carbon nickel from Canada, sources say
summary: Tesla is reportedly in talks with Canada’s Giga Metals to help develop and potentially finance a low-carbon Turnagain nickel mine, aiming to secure battery supply. The article links Tesla’s demand for nickel to EV growth and suggests long-term procurement could support nickel sentiment despite carbon-neutrality details not changing current output immediately.

title: Tanzania, Burundi plan to construct joint nickel processing plant
summary: Tanzania’s President said Tanzania and Burundi are in talks to speed up construction of a joint nickel processing plant. Both countries are described as nickel producers exporting unprocessed material. The proposed facility would add processing capacity and improve the nickel value chain, potentially supporting nickel market expectations in the near term.

title: Copper hits over 2-year high on Chinese demand recovery
summary: London and Shanghai copper prices rose to multi-month highs as China’s industrial production accelerated and retail sales turned positive, signaling improving demand after the virus slump. Physical copper premiums in China continued to fall, reinforcing market expectations of recovery. LME three-month copper climbed 0.6% and ShFE added 0.8%.

title: 5 Top Weekly TSX Stocks: Nickel Stocks Enjoy Momentum
summary: The TSX stock roundup highlights copper rising to a two-year high, attributed to speculators extending buying on improving top metals demand signals from China. It also features strong momentum in TSX nickel names, including a nickel-copper-cobalt project with recent drilling results, supporting near-term nickel sentiment.

title: Aluminium scrap import approvals for Q4 likely to decline 40% from Q3, supply to remain in shortages_SMM
summary: China approved 121,000 mt of aluminium scrap imports in its 12th approval batch, with total approvals at 818,000 mt this year. SMM estimates Q4 import quotas of 130,000–150,000 mt, about 60% lower than Q3, keeping scrap shortages. ADC12 secondary aluminium prices are expected to stay strong.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Sep 21): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, nickel fell 1.99%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals mostly rose, with aluminium up 0.58% and copper up 0.37%, while nickel fell 1.99% on Monday. Trading focused on coronavirus-relief bill progress, Fed speakers, and yields/US dollar. The note also references open-interest shifts and zinc inventory declines, but provides no new major nickel/copper/aluminium shock.

title: China Hongqiao kicks off aluminium production in Yunnan | Reuters | Business
summary: Reuters reports that China Hongqiao has kicked off aluminium production at facilities in Yunnan. The start of output suggests incremental primary aluminium supply entering the market in the coming days, which can weigh on near-term price expectations for aluminium despite any local operational ramp-up constraints.

title: Copper pulls back from two-year peak on resurgent coronavirus
summary: Copper fell from a two-year peak as surging COVID-19 cases in Europe and the U.S. threatened economic activity and metal demand, reinforcing risk-off sentiment. A stronger dollar also weighed. Nickel and aluminium were also weaker, with nickel tracking steel weakness and aluminium output declining in August.

title: Talon Metals Comments on Tesla "Battery Day" and its Critical Role in Meeting the Growing Demand for Green Nickel
summary: Talon Metals comments ahead of Tesla’s Battery Day, saying its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project in Minnesota is on track to become a U.S. source of “green nickel” for EV batteries. Management highlights battery-grade nickel timing and aims to meet expected nickel demand, implying supportive near-term nickel sentiment.

title: LME copper up on Chinese demand, new lockdown fears cap gains
summary: LME three-month copper rose 0.4% as traders expected stronger Chinese demand after improved industrial output and retail sales. The global refined copper market deficit widened in June. However, fresh coronavirus lockdown fears and a resurgent, stronger U.S. dollar limited upside and helped cap gains.

title: Global Aluminum Market 2020 Industry Analysis, Share, Growth, Sales, Trends, Supply, Forecast 2027
summary: The press release broadly analyzes the global aluminium market and highlights the COVID-19 impact. It notes the LME aluminium price falling to around $1,440/ton from $1,750/ton, and says disruptions have led to shutdowns and left many smelters unworkable without government support, suggesting bearish near-term pricing.

title: LME copper rises on demand prospects; lockdown anxiety caps gains
summary: London copper prices rose modestly as markets looked to strong Chinese demand and tightening global copper inventories. LME stocks available for purchase fell 25% and total stocks are near lows not seen since 2005. However, renewed European lockdown worries and a firmer dollar capped gains.

title: Ero Copper intersects 10.0 meters grading 4.50% copper, 0.68% nickel including 4.0 meters grading 8.53% copper, 1.25% nickel in newly discovered zone at the Siriema deposit
summary: Ero Copper reports drill results from its Bahia, Brazil property, including new Siriema and UG1 zones with copper and nickel grades (e.g., 10.0m at 4.50% Cu and 0.68% Ni). It also describes ongoing drilling to extend mineralization. Results are exploration updates, not yet resource changes.

title: Metal industry sees no need for LME green aluminium platform
summary: Reuters reports industry sources say the LME does not need a separate platform for low-carbon (“green”) aluminium, arguing existing aluminium LME contracts already allow buyers to pay premiums for sustainability and specifications. The LME had proposed a spot platform for low carbon aluminium, but feedback is due, and liquidity concerns are cited.

title: Copper prices plunged following a broad sell-off across stock markets, but prices likely to rise in Q4 amid ample liquidity and strong post-holiday consumption _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME copper fell after a broad stock sell-off and a rebound in the US dollar. It notes tight concentrate supply and expectations of improved Q4 demand from ample liquidity and post–National Day consumption, but also cites weak rod orders and rising domestic inventories, leaving near-term pressure mixed.

title: Mining Brief: Copper Mine Production Increasing While Gold Prices Rise
summary: The piece argues copper is outperforming amid rising demand and stimulus optimism, citing LME copper hitting a two-year high and hedge funds buying the rally. It also references Fitch expectations for steady growth in global copper mine output, implying improving supply/demand fundamentals for copper over the coming weeks.

title: Financial News Media | Mining Brief: Copper Mine Production Increasing While Gold Prices Rise
summary: The article highlights strengthening copper prices, including an LME two-year high, and links the rally to China demand optimism and fears of disruption in Chile output. It also references Fitch forecasts for steadily rising global copper mine production. Nickel is only referenced historically via a former Ni-Cu mine near QMC’s project.

title: Copper Fox Updates Mineral Mountain Project
summary: Copper Fox updated plans for its Mineral Mountain porphyry copper project in Arizona, including retaining consultants for an Environmental Assessment required by the BLM before geophysical surveys and describing geochemical analysis identifying a CuMoAuAgTe target. The work is preparatory, with no production or supply change reported.

title: Ero Copper Intersects 10 Meters Grading 4.5 Percent Copper, 0.68 Percent Nickel
summary: Ero Copper reported drill results from its Curaçá Valley projects in Brazil, including 10.0m at 4.5% copper and 0.68% nickel, plus other strong copper/nickel intercepts at Siriema and Pilar/Vermelhos areas. The company also notes stacked structures and ongoing drilling; results are exploration and pending resource updates.

title: Ero Copper Intersects 10 Meters Grading 4.5 Percent Copper, 0.68 Percent Nickel
summary: Ero Copper reported quarterly drill results from Bahia and associated zones, including newly discovered mineralized intercepts with high copper grades (e.g., 4.50% over 10m) and meaningful nickel (up to ~1.25% over 4m). The update also extends Pilar and Vermelhos targets. Overall, it is supportive for copper and nickel expectations but not immediate production.

title: Freeport-McMoRan aims to hit 'Copper Mark' at six operating sites
summary: Freeport-McMoRan said it will commit to the International Copper Association’s ‘Copper Mark,’ a framework intended to assure responsible production and trading across copper mines and refineries. The company says it supports customers’ responsible sourcing needs amid expected copper demand growth, but it does not imply a near-term supply shock.

title: GLENCORE'S HEAD OF AFRICA COPPER SAYS KAMOTO COPPER COMPANY EXPECTS TO PRODUCE 270,000 TONNES OF COPPER IN 2020
summary: Glencore’s Africa copper head said Kamoto Copper Company expects to produce 270,000 tonnes of copper in 2020. The update is directly tied to copper supply expectations, but it appears to be a production forecast rather than a disruption or policy change, suggesting limited immediate influence on near-term copper prices.

title: Qld govt props up Glencore copper refining
summary: Queensland’s government is said to be supporting Glencore’s copper refining operations, implying authorities are helping prevent or mitigate a potential disruption at a key refining facility. This should help maintain near-term supply of refined copper and support expectations for copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Mount Isa copper smelter gets three more years with 'one-off' incentive from Queensland Government
summary: Queensland will extend Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery operations for another three years, after the plants were due to close in 2022. The government provides a one-off incentive and the operator plans major investment, supporting local jobs and copper processing continuity.

title: China's remains net aluminum importer as August shipments surge
summary: China remained a net aluminum importer in August, with shipments jumping eight-fold year on year to 429,464 tonnes, the highest in over 11 years. Imports exceeded exports as traders exploited a Shanghai-London price arbitrage from lower overseas prices amid sluggish global demand.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Airborne Geophysical Survey Underway on Recently Acquired Option Properties
summary: Canada Nickel says airborne magnetic and gravity surveys have started on newly acquired option properties, targeting seven nickel-bearing structures. The company cites historic drilling results with nickel grades across several targets. The update is exploratory and does not indicate immediate production or supply changes.

title: Strengthening dollar sucks momentum from copper's rally
summary: Copper prices fell as the dollar strengthened to its highest since July, making copper costlier for other-currency buyers. The rally’s slowing pace and signs of weaker Chinese demand raised fears of a speculative sell-off. The piece also notes tighter LME cash supply but highlights overall momentum loss.

title: Alcoa Expands Sustana Line Of Products By Adding Low-carbon EcoSource Alumina
summary: Alcoa announced it is adding EcoSource, a low-carbon smelter-grade alumina brand to its Sustana line. The product targets up to 0.6 tons CO2e per ton of alumina, versus an industry average of 1.2. Alcoa says its refiners have among the lowest carbon footprints.

title: PROJECT 81 Exploration Update: Canada Nickel Company Announces Comprehensive Geophysical Survey Underway on Recently Acquired Option Properties from Noble
summary: Canada Nickel, using funds from a recent financing, is starting airborne magnetic and gravity surveys over seven nickel-bearing target structures within its Project 81 option properties. The company cites historical nickel drill intersections and expects improved targeting, but no production or confirmed reserves are reported.

title: Glencore's copper operations in North Queensland thrown another lifeline weeks before state election
summary: Queensland granted Glencore a “one-off” multi-million-dollar incentive to secure jobs and keep its Mount Isa smelter and Townsville refinery operating for at least three years. Glencore said the payment partially mitigates high costs. The decision came as copper prices surged and supply tightness concerns were raised.

title: COVID-19 case reported at Highland Valley Copper near Kamloops
summary: Teck said a contractor at Highland Valley Copper has tested positive for COVID-19. The worker was on site Sept. 8–11, with the positive result received Sept. 20 after a Sept. 18 test. The person is self-isolating as contacts are traced and work areas disinfected.

title: Lindian to pick up transformational bauxite assets in Guinea
summary: Lindian Resources agreed to procure the 847 Mt Lelouma bauxite project in Guinea, plus plans to acquire 75% of Woula, both high-grade bauxite assets near existing infrastructure and export routes. Such deals can improve expectations for aluminium feedstock supply while the article notes a rebound in aluminium prices.

title: The consumption affected the trend of aluminium prices before the National Day holidays_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices have been rangebound ahead of China’s National Day as the USD strengthens and macro sentiment stays weak. It cites rising domestic primary aluminium capacity and only modest inventory growth, while September consumption is flat vs August and slightly below expectations, leaving October outlook largely neutral.

title: Encounter Resources offers BHP 75% stake in Elliot Copper project
summary: Encounter Resources signed an option pact with BHP to potentially earn up to a 75% stake in its Elliot copper project in Australia’s Northern Territory after a validation programme. BHP may spend up to A$22 million over 10 years on exploration and could run further programmes before entering an earn-in JV.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 3,900 mt on week on larger arrivals_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s aluminium billet stocks rose 3,900 mt week on week to 71,500 mt as of Sep 24, driven by larger arrivals. Inventories grew in Foshan and Nanchang, while Wuxi, Changzhou, and Huzhou saw declines, indicating a net supply build.

title: BHP takes on copper project in Australia's Northern Territory
summary: BHP has signed an option agreement with Encounter Resources over the Elliott copper project in Australia’s Northern Territory. The deal gives BHP an option to enter an earn-in and joint arrangement, potentially advancing development of the copper asset. It supports bullish sentiment for copper via future supply expectations.

title: Management & Project Update for AEM Canada's High Purity Alumina, Cap Chat Plant
summary: AEM Canada announced progress in recommissioning its Cap Chat high-purity alumina (HPA) plant in Quebec, aiming to start production in November after engineering fixes and installation of a new furnace. HPA is used in aluminium-related refining, and its ramp-up could support supply expectations for the aluminium chain.

title: Class 1 Nickel Announces Commencement of VTEM™ Survey over Alexo-Dundonald and NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Upgrade Work Nears Completion
summary: Class 1 Nickel commenced an airborne VTEM survey and completed on-site validation sampling for an NI 43-101 mineral resource upgrade at its Alexo-Dundonald nickel-copper project. The company expects an updated resource by early October, citing increased tonnage/grade potential from nickel-bearing sulphides. No immediate production or market supply changes are indicated.

title: Glencore to extend life of its copper assets in Queensland
summary: Queensland will fund Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery to keep them running for an additional three years, after they were slated to retire in 2022. Glencore also plans A$500m to continue operations, securing hundreds of jobs. Extended refining capacity can support copper supply.

title: Sanity prevails in aluminum trade war | Kincardine News
summary: The Trump administration reportedly repealed a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports after a last-minute aluminum trade ceasefire. The planned U.S.–Canada tariff retaliation was linked to counter-tariffs and claims of excessive imports, but business groups and industry opposed it. Without tariffs, near-term aluminum trade risk eases.

title: Sanity prevails in aluminum trade war | Mayerthorpe Freelancer
summary: The Trump administration’s last-minute decision to end its trade war with Canada over aluminium imports is welcomed. The U.S. will repeal a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminium products, avoiding planned $3.6 billion counter-tariffs. The article notes claims of excessive imports were exaggerated and warns disputes could reappear later.

title: Sanity prevails in aluminum trade war
summary: The Trump administration called a ceasefire in its aluminum trade dispute with Canada by repealing a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum products. Canada had threatened $3.6 billion in counter-tariffs. Business groups opposed the tariffs, noting import levels were near normal, supporting a less restrictive trade outlook for aluminum.

title: Sanity prevails in aluminum trade war | Grande Prairie Daily Herald Tribune
summary: The piece reports the Trump administration is repealing a 10% tariff on Canadian aluminum imports, ending a threatened aluminum trade escalation. It notes Canada would have imposed large counter-tariffs, but both sides avert the conflict during the pandemic. The decision is presented as supportive for aluminum trade flows and prices.

title: Japan Q4 aluminium premium rises to US$88/T as demand recovers from COVID-19
summary: Japan’s Q4 aluminium premium for Oct–Dec was set at $88/tonne, up 11% from the prior quarter ($79) and the first quarterly increase in five, as buyers’ demand recovers post-COVID. The premium remains below producers’ initial $95–98 offers, implying renewed pricing momentum.

title: Class 1 Nickel Announces Commencement of VTEM Survey over Alexo-Dundonald and NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Upgrade Work Nears Completion
summary: Class 1 Nickel announced commencement of an airborne VTEM plus magnetic survey and near-completion of field work to upgrade its NI 43-101 mineral resources at the Alexo-Dundonald Ni-Cu-PGE project. Validation of historical nickel sulphide resources may increase tonnage and grade, but no near-term production changes were stated.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks added 5,700 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for the eighth week, adding 5,700 mt to 282,200 mt as overseas arrivals increased and domestic inflows stayed stable. With demand sluggish before the holiday, the Yangshan copper premium fell to a new yearly low. Traders shipped cargoes into bonded warehouses, boosting inventories.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 81,000 wmt to 9.03 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 81,000 wmt from Sept 18 to 9.03 million wmt by Sept 25. In Ni content, stocks increased 600 mt to 72,300 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also climbed 101,000 wmt to 6.62 million wmt.

title: BHP signs option agreement for Elliott copper project in Australia
summary: BHP signed an option agreement for Encounter Resources’ Elliott copper project in Australia’s Northern Territory. A 75/25 JV is expected after the earn-in, with upcoming data compilation, interpretation and modelling planned. The deal signals continued exploration activity but provides no immediate supply change.

title: Zijin's Serbia copper smelter suspended for reconstruction to lower SO2 emissions
summary: Zijin’s Serbia copper smelter has been suspended for reconstruction aimed at reducing SO2 emissions. The shutdown implies reduced smelting throughput and potential short-term constraints in refined copper supply. Such disruptions can support upward pressure on copper prices over the following days as market participants price tighter availability.

title: Trigon Completes Acquisition of 'Silver Hill' Copper-Silver Exploration Project in Morocco and Files NI 43-101 Technical Report TSX Venture Exchange:TM
summary: Trigon Metals reports completion of its acquisition of the Silver Hill copper-silver exploration project in Morocco and files an NI 43-101 technical report. The release describes surface copper/silver mineralization and no expected COVID-19 delays to sampling. It provides no production or policy details that would drive immediate copper price changes.

title: Nine employees in Indonesia's largest nickel industrial park tested positive for COVID-19_SMM
summary: Nine employees tested positive for COVID-19 at Indonesia’s Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP), the country’s largest nickel industrial park. Other throat swabs were still pending, while 77 were negative. An SMM survey says production is currently normal and output later is not expected to be affected, with monitoring continuing.

title: Copper processors' production arrangements for the National Day/Mid-Autumn Festival holidays _SMM
summary: SMM surveys 32 copper processors on National Day/Mid-Autumn Festival holiday plans. Many wire/cable, copper rod, and copper pipe makers will reduce output due to tepid orders and high finished-product inventories, though some plate/strip/foil firms plan normal operations and others stockpile inputs to sustain several days of production.

title: India opens dumping probe on Malaysia, Vietnam, Thai copper tube, pipe imports
summary: India has opened a countervailing duty dumping/subsidy probe into copper tubes and pipes imported from Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand, citing increased import volumes. The investigation may result in countervailing duties after reviewing shipments from April 2019–March 2020, potentially reducing imports and supporting copper-related demand expectations.

title: Shifting Trump tariffs on aluminum disruptive to CNY businesses
summary: U.S. aluminum businesses near the Canadian border say tariff reversals have been disruptive. While a recent decision avoids tariffs on Canadian aluminum, officials warn duties could return if import volumes exceed expectations. Shippers reduced large shipments to avoid tariffs, cutting port arrivals and complicating budgets.

title: Copper rises 1% on China demand, U.S. stimulus hopes
summary: London copper futures rose about 1% as markets expect firmer Chinese demand tied to improving manufacturing and infrastructure spending, alongside hopes for a large U.S. stimulus package. China industrial output accelerated, while other factors like a stronger dollar posed some risk. Zambia’s duty removal aims to boost copper processing.

title: India opens dumping probe on copper tubes from Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand | Politics
summary: India has opened a dumping investigation into copper tubes and pipes imported from Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand. The probe examines whether unfair subsidies were involved for shipments from April 2019 to March 2020. India cites customs data showing increased imports, with Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam accounting for over 90% of total imports.

title: Copper inventories in Guangdong to increase to a maximum of 100,000 mt post-holiday _SMM
summary: SMM reports Guangdong copper inventories are expected to rise during Oct 1–8 holidays, reaching up to 100,000 mt post-holiday from 85,600 mt. With weak downstream demand and post-holiday imported shipments, copper stocks may stay elevated into late October, keeping spot discounts from widening sharply, but weighing on premiums.

title: Renforth's Surimeau Interpreted to Be a Large-Scale Sulphide Nickel System
summary: Renforth Resources reports that its Surimeau Project in Quebec is interpreted as hosting a large-scale sulphide nickel-PGE system, with VMS mineralization and nickel-bearing ultramafic sills. Field and lab observations identified pentlandite in most samples and nickel grades up to ~0.49% in grab samples, suggesting potential nickel resources.

title: Nornickel signs support package with indigenous peoples
summary: Nornickel signed a RUB2bn indigenous support package in Russia’s North, but the firm faces criticism over environmental impacts, including a major Norilsk diesel spill and high sulphur dioxide emissions. An Aboriginal Forum letter urged Tesla to avoid buying Nornickel nickel for batteries until independent damage assessments are done.

title: Intl Aluminium Conf: Key discussion points | American Metal Market
summary: Fastmarkets proposed amendments to its Asian base-metal assessment publication times and holiday pricing schedule. It also delayed and corrected certain European low-carbon aluminium differential assessments due to procedural errors, including Aluminium 6063 extrusion billet premium midpoints for Italy and North Germany, with the pricing database updated.

title: Copper prices edge up, but steady U.S. dollar caps gains
summary: Copper prices inched up on Tuesday, with LME three-month copper rising 0.3% and Shanghai’s November contract up 0.2%, though gains were capped by a steady U.S. dollar. LME aluminium rose 0.3% while nickel slipped 0.2%, reflecting mixed, short-term currency-driven pressure.

title: CSPT released the floor price of copper concentrate treatment charges in Q4_SMM
summary: SMM reports CSPT finalized higher Q4 treatment and refining charges for copper concentrate at $58/mt and 5.8 cents/lb, above Q3. It cites marginal supply/demand improvement, specific mine output increases, and some smelting-side disturbances. Refineries have adequate inventories, but purchasing prices rose as spot needs were limited.

title: Jervois to Acquire the Sao Miguel Paulista Nickel and Cobalt Refinery in Brazil
summary: Jervois agreed to acquire Brazil’s Sao Miguel Paulista nickel/cobalt electrolytic refinery from CBA and plans feasibility work for a restart. SMP has 25,000 tpa refined nickel capacity and was on care and maintenance. Pending permits and study outcomes, Jervois expects restart timing aligned with planned feed deliveries, affecting nickel supply outlook.

title: India opens dumping probe into Malaysia, Vietnam, Thai copper tube, pipe imports
summary: India opened a countervailing duty investigation into copper tubes and pipes imported from Malaysia, Vietnam, and Thailand, citing subsidy concerns. Increased imports and potential duties may make importers hesitant and reduce order placement. The probe covers shipments from April 2019 to March 2020 and could affect short-term copper tube demand.

title: Azelio, Stena Aluminium to collaborate energy storage
summary: Azelio and Stena Aluminium plan a long-term collaboration to produce Azelio’s energy storage units by filling them with recycled molten aluminum at a dedicated line at Stena’s smelter. The company claims energy and emissions benefits from using recycled aluminum, but no near-term volumes are specified.

title: India probes alleged spike in subsidised copper tube, pipe imports from Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam
summary: India is investigating an alleged rise in subsidised copper tube and pipe imports from Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam. The probe could lead to anti-subsidy or anti-dumping measures that reduce import volumes and tighten copper-related supply, supporting near-term copper prices as market participants adjust expectations.

title: Refined nickel industry's production arrangements for the National Day/Mid-Autumn Festival holidays_SMM
summary: SMM surveyed China’s refined nickel industry for National Day/Mid-Autumn holidays. Most refined nickel smelters keep continuous production with rest/duty schedules, so monthly output should be stable. Some smelters previously shifted to producing nickel sulfate and may not revert before year-end. Alloy and stainless operations also run largely normally.

title: Consultation Period for San Ciprián Aluminum Plant Officially Ends Without Agreement; Alcoa Has up to 15 Days to Announce Decision
summary: Alcoa’s San Ciprián aluminum plant consultation ended without agreement with workers’ representatives. With no sale reached to GFG Alliance, Alcoa must announce a decision within 15 days, potentially involving curtailment or permanent dismissal for the smelter’s 228,000 tpy capacity. The alumina refinery is not affected.

title: NORNICKEL INCREASES INVESTMENTS IN INDUSTRIAL SAFETY
summary: Norilsk Nickel plans to increase investments by over 100 billion roubles (about USD 1.3 billion) in modernization of its fuel and energy complex in 2020-2024, including upgrades to power, grids, gas pipelines and fuel storage, with a focus on industrial safety and permafrost monitoring on the Taimyr Peninsula.

title: ABB completes commissioning of groundbreaking conveyor system at world's largest open-pit copper mine - Chemical Engineering
summary: ABB and TAKRAF completed commissioning of a high-power gearless conveyor system at Chuquicamata copper mine in Chile, adding 11 x 5MW synchronous motors and a 58MW total drive for a largely truckless continuous-mining transport setup. The upgrade is expected to extend mine operations for decades, but near-term copper price impact appears limited.

title: Jervois Mining to buy cobalt, nickel refinery in Brazil
summary: Jervois Mining will purchase a nickel and cobalt refinery in Brazil for 125 million reals from Companhia Brasileira de Alumínio. The deal is intended to expand Jervois into a producer and refiner serving battery supply chains. Added refining capacity could modestly support nickel market expectations.

title: India opens dumping probe into Malaysia, Vietnam and Thai copper tube, pipe imports
summary: India opened a dumping/subsidy probe into copper tube and pipe imports from Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand, which could lead to countervailing duties. The circular cites rising import volumes. Reuters reports Thailand expects little direct impact but said uncertainty may deter orders, potentially tightening copper tube/pipeline inflows.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 97,000 wmt to 9.13 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data shows Chinese nickel ore inventories rose by 97,000 wmt to 9.13 million wmt between Sept. 25 and Sept. 30. Ni-content stocks increased by 700 mt to 73,000 mt, and inventories at seven major ports also climbed, indicating improved near-term ore supply.

title: Copper claws higher on China data; inventories weigh
summary: Copper prices edged up but struggled as LME inventories rose, suggesting excess supply risk even as China’s factory activity improved. The article flags copper’s technical vulnerability after breaking its uptrend. It also reports softer LME aluminum and marginal moves in nickel, within a stronger U.S. dollar backdrop.

title: Jervois Mining to acquire cobalt and nickel refinery in Brazil
summary: Jervois Mining agreed to acquire a nickel and cobalt refinery in Brazil, aiming to restart operations after care and maintenance. The São Miguel Paulista facility previously produced 25,000 tpa nickel capacity. Jervois plans a feasibility study to restart refining, which may improve near-term expectations for nickel supply.

title: Chile says manufacturing, copper output fall in August
summary: Chile’s statistics agency INE said copper output in August fell 5.5% year-on-year to 489,461 tons, linked to lower mineral processing. The agency also reported an 8.2% drop in manufacturing output amid broader COVID-19 disruption. January-August copper production rose slightly, by 0.6%.

title: Copper edges to one-week high on stimulus hopes and China
summary: Copper futures edged to a one-week high as investors priced in hopes for China’s recovery and a potential U.S. stimulus inflow, while a weaker dollar supported dollar-priced metals. This optimism offset concerns after LME copper inventories more than doubled, suggesting physical demand uncertainty. Aluminium and nickel were slightly higher.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Reports Kamoa-Kakula Copper Project Sets Fresh Monthly Record for Underground Development with 2,069 Metres Achieved in September; More than 22.6 Kilometres Now Complete
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reported progress at the Kamoa-Kakula copper project: September underground development reached a new monthly record (2,069 metres), with the first 3.8 Mtpa concentrator construction over 52% complete and stockpiles rising. The project is still targeting first copper production in about a year, with higher-grade ore access improving.

title: Copper slips from one-week high on virus worries, high stocks
summary: Copper prices fell from a one-week high as virus worries and higher LME inventories raised doubts about physical tightness and demand, with China premiums also easing. Despite hopes for U.S. stimulus, copper slipped 0.7%. LME aluminum and nickel also weakened, reflecting broad risk-off metal sentiment.

title: Ivanhoe Reports Kamoa-Kakula Copper Project Sets Fresh Monthly Record for Underground Development with 2,069 Metres Achieved in September; More than 22.6 Kilometres Now Complete - 44% Ahead of Plan
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said underground development at the Kamoa-Kakula copper project hit a monthly record (2,069 metres in September) and is ~44% ahead of schedule. The Kakula concentrator and infrastructure are over half complete, with first production still targeted for Q3 2021 and access drives to join in November.

title: Copper & Crude Crashing As Growth Fears Re-Emerge
summary: The piece highlights copper falling alongside crude as renewed growth concerns resurface. The implication is weaker economic activity and associated demand worries for industrial metals, contributing to bearish near-term sentiment for copper prices.

title: After hitting pause on aluminum tariffs, Trump looks to collaborate with Canada on 35 'critical minerals'
summary: Trump signed an executive order to promote U.S. investment and collaboration with Canada on supply chains for 35 critical minerals, including aluminum, to reduce reliance on China. It follows a temporary pause on Canadian aluminum tariffs but with new import thresholds reviewed mid-November, when tariffs could return, leaving near-term direction uncertain.

title: Copper drops most since March with growth fears dimming outlook
summary: Copper prices are reported to have fallen the most since March, with growth fears easing or dimming the outlook. Weaker macro demand expectations generally pressure industrial metal sentiment in the near term, pointing to bearish pressure for copper markets over the coming days.

title: EMR Capital seeks concessions to develop $1 bln Zambia copper mine
summary: EMR Capital, owner of Lubambe Copper Mine in Zambia, is seeking government concessions to advance a $1 billion expansion potentially producing up to 160,000 tonnes of copper annually. Zambia’s Chamber of Mines argues royalties should be deductible to reduce double taxation and unlock delayed mine investment.

title: Aluminum can shortage affects local breweries
summary: Local breweries in Tucson report an aluminum can shortage that leaves many products out of stock and creates multi-month waitlists. Even when cans are obtainable, they cost more and lids/bottoms may be unavailable separately, increasing ordering costs. Breweries expect pressure to ease as conditions improve.

title: Surge Copper Corp.: Surge Copper Amends the Terms of Its Recently Announced Financing, While Ootsa Drill Preparations Are Underway
summary: Surge Copper Corp. amended terms of a C$6.5 million private placement, increasing the flow-through component and earmarking proceeds to expedite and expand drilling at its Ootsa copper property. The company plans to mobilize a drill rig next week to test targets, with no immediate production or supply impact stated.

title: Surge Copper Amends the Terms of Its Recently Announced Financing, While  Ootsa Drill Preparations Are Underway
summary: Surge Copper amended the terms of its recently announced financing, increasing the flow-through component, and plans to mobilize a drill rig to test a new geophysical target at its Ootsa copper property. Proceeds are earmarked for exploration and drilling, but no production or near-term supply change is stated.

title: Western Copper and Gold : September 2020 Technical Presentation
summary: Western Copper and Gold’s September 2020 technical presentation focuses on developing its copper-gold project and outlines progress in exploration and feasibility work. It also claims copper deficits are projected and notes very strong gold prices, supporting the narrative of tighter copper supply conditions.

title: Burnside alumina plant shuttered, hundreds laid off; future in limbo
summary: LAlumina’s Burnside, Louisiana specialty alumina plant closed, laying off hundreds of workers, after warning of indefinite layoffs due to slumping market conditions and COVID. The union claims unpaid benefits, while Noranda Alumina hired some workers. The shutdown reduces alumina output for aluminum-related materials.

title: Copper dips as global volatility shakes investors' confidence
summary: Copper fell as global volatility ahead of the U.S. election and reduced Chinese participation weighed on sentiment. The report cites a build-up in LME stocks, plunging China spot premiums, and a broad sell-off in risk assets. It also records declines in aluminum and nickel during the same session.

title: Tesla in talks with another potential nickel supplier from Canada
summary: Tesla is in discussions with additional nickel suppliers, with Vale saying it is “absolutely” talking to Tesla about environmentally friendly nickel supply for EV batteries. The report highlights Vale’s production at Voisey’s Bay and low-carbon initiatives, which could improve near-term demand expectations for nickel if deals advance.

title: Tesla in discussion for major investment in Indonesia, a key nickel producer: report
summary: Reports say Indonesia’s government has entered early discussions with Tesla about a major investment in the country, a top nickel producer. The article notes Indonesia’s move to curb exports of unprocessed nickel ore and ongoing battery-related projects, which could strengthen Tesla’s battery supply chain and lift near-term nickel demand expectations.

title: Rep. Stefanik supports decision to suspend U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports of aluminum
summary: Rep. Elise Stefanik said she supports the U.S. decision by USTR to suspend tariffs on Canadian aluminum imports. She argued that removing the tariffs will benefit the regional economy, including Alcoa’s Massena smelter, and help manufacturers with cross-border supply chains and competitiveness.

title: Avrupa Minerals : Announces Drilling Program at the Alvalade Copper-Zinc Project, Iberian Pyrite Belt, Portugal
summary: Avrupa Minerals announced a 7,000–8,000 meter diamond drilling program and an airborne EM survey at the Alvalade copper-zinc (VMS) project in Portugal. The work targets the Sesmarias and other massive sulfide zones to delineate additional drilling targets. No production or discovery results are provided.

title: Copper falls despite reports of improvement in Trump's health
summary: LME copper prices fell about 0.5% as signs of weakening demand and rising stocks outweighed broader risk-on optimism after reports that Trump’s COVID-19 condition is improving. China demand indicators softened, Yangshan premiums declined, and LME warehouse inventories increased, easing nearby supply tightness.

title: U.S. Government Invests in TechMet Nickel Mining
summary: The U.S. government plans a $25 million investment in TechMet’s nickel (and cobalt) mining project to reduce dependence on Chinese supply chains for electric vehicle batteries. The move supports strategic critical-material sourcing and may improve near-term expectations for nickel availability, offering modest upward pressure to nickel prices.

title: Avrupa Minerals Announces Drilling Program at the Alvalade Copper-Zinc Project, Iberian Pyrite Belt, Portugal
summary: Avrupa Minerals announced an October-start diamond drilling program and airborne EM survey at its Alvalade VMS project in Portugal. Work targets multiple massive sulfide zones, including the Sesmarias copper-zinc discovery and related prospects, to delineate new drill sites. The release is exploration-focused and does not imply near-term production changes.

title: Tesla To Consider Investing In Major Nickel Producer
summary: Tesla is considering an investment in Indonesia after contacting the country informally, where it may source nickel for battery production. Elon Musk has recently urged miners to increase nickel output for high-volume EV batteries, framing Indonesia as especially important. The report could lift near-term nickel demand expectations.

title: Sherritt CEO pins future on demand for nickel for electric-car batteries
summary: Sherritt CEO David Pathe says Battery Day reinforced expectations of significant growth in nickel demand for electric-car batteries, noting Tesla’s claims that EVs could consume a large share of annual nickel supply. Sherritt plans to scale Cuban nickel output, though analysts flag debt and U.S. sanctions risks.

title: Tesla in talks with Vale to buy Canadian nickel for electric cars
summary: Tesla is reportedly in talks with Vale to secure nickel from Vale’s Canadian operations for EV batteries. Musk previously urged miners to produce more nickel, and analysts warn of a potential nickel supply deficit. Vale is expanding output and discussing low-carbon production, keeping “environmentally friendly nickel” central.

title: Nevada Copper Delivers Copper Concentrate and Provides Operations Update
summary: Nevada Copper says it resumed concentrate deliveries after restarting milling operations at its Pumpkin Hollow Underground Mine in August 2020. The first shipment was 1,322 tons, with compliant specs and planned increasing volumes as mining ramps toward mill capacity. It also discusses operational milestones and liquidity support.

title: Copper rises on U.S. stimulus hope, Chile mining risks
summary: Copper prices rose as investors gained optimism for a U.S. coronavirus stimulus package, which could lift demand expectations. At the same time, Chile’s Candelaria mine faced higher disruption risk after workers rejected Lundin Mining’s contract offer, raising potential strike concerns.

title: Copper rises as Trump returns to White House
summary: London copper rose after Trump returned to the White House, easing political/COVID uncertainty and improving risk sentiment. The report also cites U.S. coronavirus economic relief talks that could support demand. Separately, a Chile mine contract rejection raised strike risk, reinforcing bullish near-term copper expectations; aluminium also advanced.

title: BeMetals Corp.: BeMetals Commences Exploration Program at the Pangeni Copper Project
summary: BeMetals Corp. begins a fully funded 2020 exploration program at its Pangeni Copper Project in Zambia’s Copperbelt, targeting extensions of copper mineralization found in 2019. The company plans shallow aircore and follow-up core drilling and expects initial aircore results in early December.

title: Copper edges higher on potential Chile mine disruption
summary: Copper prices edged higher as investors worried about potential strike action at Chile’s Candelaria mine, with broader negotiations at other large Chilean operations in the fourth quarter. This raised near-term supply risk, though trade flows and signs of weaker demand kept copper fragile amid inventory concerns.

title: Rio Tinto, AB InBev Partner To Deliver More Sustainable Aluminium Beer Cans
summary: Rio Tinto and AB InBev formed a partnership to produce sustainable beer cans made from low-carbon aluminium using renewable hydropower and recycled content. The initial focus is North America, with a pilot of one million cans in the United States, targeting over 30% lower emissions versus traditional cans.

title: Kaz Minerals suspends operations at Kyrgyz copper and gold mine
summary: Kaz Minerals suspended operations at its Bozymchak copper and gold mine in Kyrgyzstan amid post-election unrest. The company cited instability and the report also mentions attacks and protests at other mines. The halt in copper output tightens near-term supply expectations, supporting copper prices.

title: Tesla in talks with BHP over nickel supply pact – Bloomberg News
summary: Tesla is reportedly in talks with BHP to secure a nickel supply deal to support higher electric-car production and reduce the risk of a nickel supply crunch. Negotiations are stalled over pricing with no agreement yet. Tesla has also urged miners to increase nickel output amid battery cost concerns.

title: Tesla is in talks with top miner BHP over nickel-supply pact
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports Tesla is in talks with miner BHP over a nickel-supply agreement. If concluded, such a pact would signal stronger battery-related nickel demand and potentially tighter near-term supply. Markets typically react by repricing expectations for nickel balances and headline availability in the coming weeks.

title: FMI Updates Aluminium Aerosol Cans Market Forecast and Analysis as Corona Virus Outbreak Disturbs Investment Plans
summary: FMI updated its forecast and analysis for aluminium aerosol cans, citing that the coronavirus outbreak is disturbing investment plans. The disruption suggests weaker near-term spending and production activity related to aluminium can manufacturing, which can soften demand expectations for aluminium over the coming days to weeks.

title: China's import boom heralds deeper rift in aluminium: Andy Home
summary: China’s imports of unwrought and primary aluminium rose again in August, extending a rare inversion where it is a net importer. The author links this to faster COVID-19 recovery, infrastructure stimulus and a wider ShFE-LME arbitrage window that drives demand and smelter ramp-ups, reinforcing near-term bullish aluminium sentiment.

title: Copper slips as China absent from market
summary: Three-month LME copper fell 0.6% to $6,639/t after slipping from a near one-week high, attributed to China’s absence from the market during a major holiday (Oct. 1–8). Copper had earlier risen on expectations of improved growth and demand, alongside Chile strike concerns.

title: Canada Nickel's Final Three Infill Holes Confirm and Extend Higher Grade Mineralization at Crawford Nickel-Cobalt Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel announced final infill drill results at its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project in Ontario, highlighting higher-grade nickel intervals (e.g., ~0.33% Ni over long core lengths and 0.36% Ni).
