Results will be incorporated into an updated resource estimate expected in two weeks, potentially improving nickel project outlook.

title: Kodiak Copper Closes $12.7 Million Private Placement
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. closed a C$12.7 million private placement, including flow-through shares, to fund exploration at its advanced-stage copper porphyry projects in British Columbia and Arizona. The company says it is fully funded for 2020-into-2021 drilling at the MPD project and will follow up on its Gate Zone discovery.

title: How investors can benefit from 'COVID-19 and The New Age of Copper'
summary: A Globe and Mail roundup features a VoxEu paper arguing we are entering “a new age of copper.” It cites China’s rebound lifting copper imports and forecasts additional demand from the digital and green economy (electrification, EVs, 5G) plus healthcare uses. Overall implications are supportive for copper prices.

title: Peru copper output slips back 10% in August; zinc, tin production up
summary: Peru’s copper output reportedly slipped 10% in August, indicating weaker production volumes from a key supplier. The data points to near-term supply downside expectations, which can influence copper pricing over the coming days as markets adjust for reduced availability versus demand conditions.

title: Sumitomo to sell stake in Sierra Gorda copper mine
summary: Japanese miner Sumitomo Metal Mining is reviewing strategic options for its minority 45% stake in the Sierra Gorda copper mine in northern Chile, where KGHM is the majority owner. The company announced it is considering selling the holding, but no immediate production disruption is indicated.

title: Lundin copper miners begin strike in Chile after wage talks fail
summary: Lundin copper miners in Chile have begun a strike after wage negotiations failed. The stoppage raises the risk of disrupted near-term copper output and slower deliveries, which typically supports prompt copper prices. However, the exact duration and volume affected are not specified.

title: Union at Chile´s Candelaria copper mine begins strike
summary: Workers at Lundin Mining’s Candelaria copper mine in Chile went on strike after contract talks broke down. The union said the mine was largely paralyzed, while the company said operations weren’t materially affected. With Chile already a key supply risk for copper, the labor action raises short-term output concerns.

title: Norsk Hydro: Hydro resumes bauxite pipeline operation in Brazil
summary: Norsk Hydro resumed operations of its bauxite pipeline in Brazil, restarting transport from the Paragominas mine to the Alunorte alumina refinery. With the mine restarted and maintenance completed, alumina production is being ramped up after prior reductions to balance bauxite inventories.

title: US to impose tariffs on $1.96B worth of aluminum sheet goods: Wilbur Ross
summary: The U.S. Commerce Secretary says the U.S. will collect tariffs on $1.96B of aluminum sheet imports from 18 countries starting immediately after a preliminary anti-dumping determination. Rates are highest for Germany. The ITC’s final ruling is expected in February 2021, with deposits refundable if exporters prevail.

title: U.S. imposes tariffs on aluminum sheet from 18 countries
summary: The U.S. has imposed new anti-dumping tariffs on $1.96 billion of aluminum sheet products from 18 countries, with rates up to 52%–132% for Germany. Tariffs are immediately applied while final determinations are due in February 2021, aiming to curb dumped imports and support U.S. pricing amid higher demand.

title: US to collect tariffs on $1.96B worth of aluminum sheet goods: Wilbur Ross
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department will collect tariffs on $1.96B of aluminum sheet imports from 18 countries following preliminary anti-dumping findings. Duties begin immediately, with final rulings expected in February. Tariff rates are highest for Germany (52%-132%), aiming to curb unfairly low-priced imports and protect domestic producers.

title: Aluminum tariffs imposed: Trump administration targets $2B in imports
summary: The Trump administration imposes immediate antidumping tariffs on imported aluminum sheets totaling about $2B from 18 countries, with rates ranging from single digits to 52%–132% for Germany. The U.S. argues imports were “dumped,” while the Aluminum Association supports the action as it restricts unfair low-priced supply.

title: U.S. aid talks and Chile strike propel copper to two-week peak
summary: Copper prices climbed to two-week highs as U.S. aid talks restarted and the dollar weakened, alongside a strike at Lundin Mining’s Candelaria mine in Chile. The move lifted broader industrial-metals sentiment, with aluminium and nickel also gaining on the day.

title: The Trump administration adds tariffs on nearly $2 billion of imported aluminum.
summary: The Trump administration added tariffs on nearly $2 billion of imported aluminum. By raising the landed cost of aluminum imports, the measure is likely to reduce import flows and improve pricing for domestic supply, supporting near-term aluminum market expectations.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Closes First Tranche of Private Placement Financing and Launches Inaugural Drilling Campaign at Stu Copper-Gold Project in Yukon, Canada
summary: Granite Creek Copper closes the first tranche of a private placement, raising about C$1.85 million, and plans an inaugural drilling campaign of up to 1,500 meters at its Stu copper-gold project in Yukon. The news is primarily financing and exploration-focused, with no immediate supply or market fundamentals stated for copper.

title: How To Set Up A Lightning Network Node
summary: Camino Corp. says drilling has started on its Los Chapitos copper project in southern Peru, testing near-surface oxide copper and deeper high-grade sulphide mineralization. It plans a 3,000-meter program to expand targets and refine resource potential at Carlotta and Diva West, with prior sampling reporting copper grades up to ~2-3%.

title: Camino Commences Drilling on its Los Chapitos Copper Discovery
summary: Camino Corp. has begun drilling on its Los Chapitos copper project in southern Peru, starting a planned 3,000-meter program targeting near-surface oxide copper and deeper high-grade sulphides. The campaign aims to test new targets like Carlotta and Diva West to expand potential mineralization and a future maiden resource.

title: Supervisors at Chile's Escondida copper mine reject final labor deal, negotiations to continue
summary: Supervisors at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile rejected the company’s final labor offer and voted 78% against it, with strike timing not announced. BHP said it will meet again next week to avert a walkout. Chile strike risk has recently supported copper prices through supply concerns.

title: Trump administration hits 18 countries with aluminum tariffs
summary: The Trump administration is reported to have imposed aluminium tariffs on 18 countries. Such tariff actions can quickly affect expectations for aluminium import supply and trade flows, potentially changing near-term availability and pricing dynamics. The likely immediate market effect is bearish for aluminium as expectations shift.

title: US impose tariffs on aluminium sheet from Bahrain, 17 others | THE DAILY TRIBUNE
summary: The US Commerce Department announced immediate anti-dumping tariffs on aluminium sheet products from Bahrain and 17 other countries, with rates varying by country and based on preliminary findings. The move targets about $1.96 billion in imports and is expected to raise US aluminium sheet pricing while awaiting a final ITC decision.

title: US to impose tariffs on Croatian aluminium production
summary: The US will impose immediate tariffs on aluminium sheet imports worth $1.96 billion from 18 countries, citing dumping. Croatia’s aluminium sheet products face customs duties of 3.22%. Tariffs are preliminary pending a final Commerce/ITC decision in February 2021, excluding China as it is already tariffed.

title: Zambian Royalty Spat Halts $2 Billion of Copper Mine Investment
summary: Zambia’s royal­ties dispute is said to halt $2 billion in investment for a copper mine. By delaying or preventing new supply development, the announcement can weaken copper supply expectations, supporting bearish near-term pricing as traders adjust for the risk of lower future output.

title: New Caledonia launches consultation on nickel sector
summary: New Caledonia has launched a consultation on its nickel resources and future strategies. The territory’s nickel sector includes 35 mines and three processing plants and is a major employer. The article notes fears SLN’s smelter may approach insolvency and Vale may shut its Goro plant, suggesting potential nickel supply disruption.

title: Brian Fallow takes a look at the energy policies of the Labour, National, Green and ACT parties against the backdrop of uncertainty over the future of the aluminium smelter at Tiwai Point and the oil refinery at Marsden Point
summary: The piece discusses energy policy ahead of New Zealand’s election, with particular emphasis on uncertainty around the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter and its electricity transmission costs. Labour, National and others discuss targets and grid upgrades, while a possible agreement with Rio Tinto could extend output and lessen immediate supply risk for aluminium.

title: London copper rises for fifth day on hopes of China demand, U.S. stimulus
summary: London copper extended gains to a fifth straight session, rising about 0.1%, driven by expectations of improving China demand from major power-grid investment and hopes for additional U.S. COVID-19 stimulus. It also reported increases in LME aluminium and Shanghai nickel, suggesting supportive macro/industrial sentiment for base metals.

title: China copper smelters raise Sept cathode output m/m - Antaike
summary: China’s copper smelters increased refined copper cathode output 3% month-on-month in September to 747,100 tonnes, beating Antaike’s prior forecast. While production was slightly lower year-on-year, the higher supply versus expectations can pressure copper prices. October output is expected to decline on scheduled maintenance.

title: Chinese demand pushes copper back towards multi-year highs
summary: Copper rallied to a three-week high as solid Chinese demand and Chile strike risk pushed prices toward multi-month highs. The piece cites China stimulus for power grids, improving premiums, higher Chinese smelter cathode output, and stronger yuan. Aluminium and nickel also rose modestly, reflecting broad metal strength.

title: Hot Chili triples world-class copper-gold resource
summary: Hot Chili triples its reported resource at the Costa Fuego copper-gold project in Chile, citing 724Mt at 0.48% copper equivalent and an additional maiden resource for Cortadera of 451Mt at 0.46% copper equivalent. It also notes continued drilling and scoping studies, but no near-term production start.

title: US Imposes Anti-Dumping Tariff of 84% on Alro's Aluminum
summary: The US Department of Commerce has imposed an anti-dumping tariff of about 83.94% on aluminium sheets produced by Romania’s Alro SA, effective immediately. The move raises the landed cost of these imports into the US, potentially reducing supply and supporting near-term aluminium price sentiment.

title: Azure Minerals hits massive nickel sulphides at Andover
summary: Azure Minerals reports significant massive nickel-copper sulphide results at its 60%-owned Andover project in WA, including a 4m zone of massive nickel-copper mineralisation and high-grade nickel confirmed by pXRF. A conductor target is supported by drilling, but no resource or production update is provided.

title: Funds' faith in turbulent copper stirred, but not shaken: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist says funds trimmed copper exposure after an early-October mini selloff tied to Trump’s COVID news, alongside a large LME warrant delivery that widened spreads. However, CME net longs remain high, shorts are low, and China’s rapid demand recovery and potential green stimulus support a bullish copper outlook.

title: Bullish Signs: Copper and Silver Shine Anew | Chief Investment Officer
summary: The piece argues that industrial demand is stabilizing: US manufacturing has picked up after shutdowns, China’s rebound is increasing material needs, and low copper inventories from pandemic mining slowdowns support prices. It also cites global stimulus and infrastructure expectations as further upside catalysts for copper.

title: Goose Creek's plan to power SC aluminum plant gets slapped down in court, ruled illegal
summary: A South Carolina judge ruled Goose Creek’s plan to take over power supply for Century Aluminum’s Berkeley County smelter is illegal, keeping Santee Cooper’s exclusive electricity service rights. The decision disrupts efforts to form a municipal utility and potentially secure cheaper power, likely raising or maintaining smelter power-cost expectations for aluminium.

title: EU imposes tariffs on aluminium products from China | Reuters | Business
summary: Reuters reports the EU has imposed tariffs on aluminium products from China. The measure is likely to reduce Chinese import volumes into the EU and improve relative competitiveness for non-tariffed supply, tightening short-term availability expectations and providing upward support for aluminium prices.

title: Copper edges lower despite strong Chinese trade data
summary: Copper futures fell 0.4% on the LME despite strong September Chinese trade data, as a stronger U.S. dollar offset optimism and as coronavirus-related vaccine trial pause news weighed on sentiment. China’s copper imports remain high. Separately, EU duties on Chinese aluminum extrusions were reported.

title: Turquoise Hill's Oyu Tolgoi Awarded the Copper Mark for its Responsible Production
summary: Turquoise Hill Resources said its Oyu Tolgoi mine in Mongolia received the Copper Mark, an independently assessed responsible production program for copper. The company highlights environmental, health and safety, and ESG commitments and compliance with management standards. The announcement is certification-focused and does not indicate immediate production or supply changes for copper.

title: Hampton Roads breweries feeling the aluminum can crunch
summary: Brewer Smartmouth Brewing in Norfolk says aluminum beverage cans are harder to get as demand for canned drinks rises during the pandemic while supply cannot keep up. The brewery also faces higher can costs—up 30% since September—because can supply is limited to just two domestic manufacturers.

title: European Union imposes 48pc tariffs on Chinese aluminum
summary: The EU announced 48% tariffs on Chinese aluminum, aiming to curb imports from China. Higher landed costs for Chinese metal should reduce import volumes into Europe and support domestic supply conditions, creating upward pressure on aluminium prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: Exclusive: China's aluminium output rose 7.68% YoY to 3.11 million mt in September, alumina output stood at 5.91 million mt_SMM
summary: SMM survey data show China’s primary aluminium output rose 7.68% YoY to 3.11mn mt in September, with operating rates at 88.2% and more capacity starting in Yunnan and Inner Mongolia. October output is expected to rise to 3.24mn mt. Alumina output also increased modestly.

title: Exclusive: China's copper cathode output edged down 0.09% from August to 809,800 mt in September _SMM
summary: SMM reports China produced 809,800 mt of copper cathode in September, down 0.09% month on month, supported by higher output from concentrate-fed smelters and rebound in copper concentrate imports. Scrap-fed smelters reduced output as the cathode–scrap spread narrowed with tighter domestic scrap supply. October output is expected to rise.

title: Argentina's Aluar reaches 60% aluminium capacity
summary: Argentina’s Aluar is reported to have reached 60% aluminium production capacity. Changes in smelter operating rates affect near-term aluminium supply availability, which can influence prompt market pricing. The update is likely to be viewed as a modest supportive signal for aluminium prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: EU imposes tariffs on aluminium products from China
summary: The EU imposed provisional duties of 30.4% to 48.0% on aluminium products imported from China, effective from Wednesday, with possible continuation after an investigation through April. The measure targets Chinese supply in transport, construction and electronics, expected to lift aluminium prices by increasing EU import costs.

title: China to add 3mln T of aluminium capacity in 2021 - Antaike
summary: Antaike says China will launch about 3 million tonnes of new annual aluminium production capacity in 2021, with significant additions in Yunnan and other provinces, plus substantial alumina capacity growth. Despite consumption growth forecasts, the outlook notes severe export conditions, suggesting greater supply and potential downside price pressure.

title: Blackstone Positions Ta Khoa Nickel-Cu-PGE Project for Li-ion Battery Market with Positive Scoping Study
summary: Blackstone reported completion of a positive scoping study to restart Vietnam’s Ta Khoa nickel-copper-PGE project, with estimated ~12.7ktpa nickel production over ~8.5 years and downstream NCM precursor plans. The study increases confidence in future nickel supply, with copper credited as a by-product.

title: Blackstone delivers billion-dollar nickel baby
summary: Blackstone Minerals released a scoping study for its Ta Khoa nickel project in Vietnam, highlighting strong economics and a potential restart of its mothballed Ban Phuc mill. The plan forecasts about 12,700 tonnes per year of nickel and evaluates downstream concentrate processing for battery precursors, supporting bullish sentiment for nickel.

title: Indonesia focuses on nickel downstream industry to attract investors
summary: Indonesia’s minister said the government is pushing nickel downstream investments to attract foreign capital, citing interest from firms like CATL and LG Chem in a multibillion-dollar nickel supply-chain project. With Indonesia as the top nickel producer/exporter for EV battery inputs, the policy is supportive for nickel market expectations.

title: Alcoa narrows Q3 loss as aluminum prices improve
summary: Alcoa reported a narrower Q3 loss, citing stronger prices for its aluminum-related products and improved auto-sector demand after earlier COVID-related factory shutdowns. It posted a $49 million loss versus a year-ago $221 million loss, reflecting improved market conditions tied directly to aluminum pricing.

title: Aluminium billet inventories fell 3,200 mt on week on smaller arrivals_SMM
summary: SMM reported that China’s aluminium billet inventories fell 3,200 mt on the week to 102,500 mt as of Oct 15, driven by lower arrivals to major warehouses. Stocks increased slightly in Foshan and Changzhou, but declined in Wuxi, Huzhou and Nanchang.

title: Copper gains on supply risks from Chile, Chinese demand hopes
summary: London copper rose as markets priced in potential production disruptions from strikes-related negotiations at Chile’s Escondida mine and Candelaria deposit. Analysts also pointed to prospects of stronger Chinese demand and improving month-on-month physical buying, supporting bullish sentiment for near-term copper prices.

title: Copper gains as China demand hopes, supply risks eclipse virus woes
summary: Copper prices rose on Friday as expectations for strong Chinese demand and concerns over supply disruptions outweighed worries about renewed COVID-19 cases in Europe. Strategists cited pandemic-related mine issues in Chile and Peru and potential labor strike risks. LME and Shanghai copper contracts gained; most base metals rose too.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks added 21,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show Shanghai bonded copper inventories rose for the 11th straight week, increasing 21,000 mt to 330,000 mt. The import arbitrage window stayed closed due to sluggish export demand, and traders moved cargoes into bonded warehouses after production resumed, lifting bonded stock levels.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 202,000 wmt to 9.41 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 202,000 wmt from Oct 9 to 9.41 million wmt by Oct 16. In Ni content, stocks increased 1,500 mt to 75,100 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also grew, indicating improving supply visibility.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks rose 1,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories rose 1,000 mt to 23,800 mt by Oct 16. With the import window closed and limited ability to ship Russian nickel to China, stocks have kept building since June. The import loss narrowed as nickel prices rebounded, but bonded stocks are expected to keep accumulating.

title: Top copper producer Chile says it can run mines in the Andes without affecting glaciers
summary: Chile’s environment minister says the country can mine large Andean copper deposits while protecting glaciers that supply water. The government seeks rules balancing environmental safeguards with investment certainty. An opposition bill could impose blanket protections and restrict projects, potentially affecting mines like Codelco and Los Bronces.

title: Glencore in talks with car companies and battery makers about nickel, CEO says
summary: Glencore CEO Ivan Glasenberg said the company is discussing nickel supply with carmakers and battery makers, highlighting nickel’s role in EV batteries. Glencore produces nickel and runs nickel mines and a refinery, and it already supplies battery materials. The talks suggest firmer near-term nickel demand sentiment.

title: Indonesia sees China firms lead 'commitment' for $35bln nickel investments
summary: Indonesia expects nickel processing and related investments to reach $35 billion by 2033, led by major Chinese companies. CATL, Ningbo Lygend, Tsingshan and Delong plan to expand nickel processing capacity alongside lithium battery and stainless steel projects. The push supports shifting nickel supply expectations in the near term.

title: Zambia Copper Mine-Waste Dam Bursts, Destroying Crops, Mail Says
summary: The headline says a waste dam at a Zambia copper mine burst, destroying crops. Such an incident can force immediate operational stoppages, raise safety and regulatory risks, and threaten near-term copper output. That supply disruption concern is likely to weigh on copper prices over the coming days.

title: Ohio's craft brewers brace for aluminum can shortage
summary: Ohio craft brewers are bracing for an aluminum can shortage as packaged beer demand rises while can supply lags. Ball says the U.S. is short 8–10 billion cans this year and plans more capacity. Smaller breweries face the biggest sourcing problems, including higher minimums and limited vendor orders.

title: Trump Administration Hits 18 Countries With Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The US imposed new anti-dumping aluminum tariffs on imports from 18 countries, totaling nearly $2 billion, with immediate collection from importers. Tariffs are steep (up to ~353% for Germany). The Commerce Department cites dumping and displacement linked to Chinese excess capacity, likely tightening US supply.

title: Sustainable mining of bauxite needed for India to be global aluminium hub
summary: The piece says India lacks successfully auctioned metallurgical-grade bauxite mines, pushing domestic aluminium producers to import bauxite and causing major foreign-exchange losses. It links delays to the current bauxite ASP calculation regime that may make aluminium production unviable. Proposed policy changes aim to boost bauxite output and reduce imports, supporting aluminium.

title: China aluminum output hits daily record in September
summary: China’s primary aluminium output hit a daily record in September, rising to 3.16 million tonnes and driven by ramp-ups and restarts of new smelting capacity in regions such as Yunnan and Sichuan. Total nonferrous production also rose. The supply increase risks weighing on aluminium prices despite some recovery earlier.

title: China's exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis rose 7.7% MoM in September amid lower SHFE/LME price ratio and pre-holiday restocking_SMM
summary: China exported 426,000 mt of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis in September, up 7.7% MoM, supported by a lower SHFE/LME ratio and overseas pre- National Day restocking. However, exports fell 2.1% YoY amid weaker overseas demand and scrap import restrictions, and October gains look limited by COVID and anti-dumping.

title: Nickel Mines to develop Indonesia smelter and coal-fired | News
summary: Australia-based Nickel Mines plans to acquire a 70% stake in a nickel production line at Indonesia’s Weda Bay Industrial Park for $490 million. The development includes a smelter, which could affect expectations for nickel processing capacity and supply availability in the coming weeks.

title: China grants import quotas for another 5,980 T of copper scrap
summary: China published new customs codes for recycled scrap meeting revised standards that can be imported freely from Nov. 1, including 5,980 tonnes of high-grade copper scrap and related aluminium scrap categories. This follows a looming ban on importing foreign solid waste, which had previously limited shipments until quotas/codes were clarified.

title: Ivanhoe Mines: Underground Development at the Kakula Copper Mine Enters Zone of Ultra-High-Grade Ore
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said underground development at the Kakula copper mine has reached ultra-high-grade, chalcocite-rich ore zones, with access drives expected to connect next month to enable stoping. Construction on the Kakula concentrator is progressing, with first production expected in July 2021, supporting improved copper supply outlook.

title: Chile´s Candelaria copper mine says to suspend operations amid union strikes
summary: Chile’s Candelaria copper mine (Lundin Mining) said it will suspend operations from Oct. 20 after workers’ unions strike and reports of blockades and attacks on staff and facilities. The stoppage follows failed contract negotiations, likely lowering near-term copper output and supporting copper prices.

title: Nickel hits 11-month high on expectations of robust demand
summary: Nickel prices hit 11-month highs as buyers increased positions on expectations of strong stainless-steel demand, including better-than-expected recovery in China and Indonesian production of high-nickel 300-series grades. Delays to Indonesia capacity expansions were also cited as potentially narrowing surpluses into early next year.

title: Copper snapshot: Eight companies with promising assets to watch
summary: A copper-focused snapshot notes rising copper prices, a favorable supply-demand outlook, and limited progress on new mine development. It highlights eight companies with promising projects as potential future supply. The framing implies near-term tightness support, which is bullish for copper prices over coming weeks.

title: Mangaluru: MLA Rajesh Naik denies accusations by Ramanath Rai over illegal bauxite extraction
summary: A Bantwal MLA denies accusations that his kin are involved in illegal bauxite extraction and says he has halted laterite extraction on his land while calling for a probe. The district BJP president also cites information about relatives linked to a red bauxite company. The dispute may affect perceived bauxite supply and enforcement risk.

title: The new standard of imported scrap aluminum to be launched in November_SMM
summary: SMM says new standards and tariff codes will liberalize imports of recycled casting aluminum alloy raw materials (scrap aluminum), starting November. Traders expect a large overseas scrap stock release, which could lower ADC12 aluminum ingot prices and narrow domestic–overseas price gaps, increasing supply in Q4.

title: Is copper scrap import harder or easier after customs codes of secondary copper (brass) raw materials were unveiled _SMM
summary: China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment issued new rules effective Nov 1 clarifying customs treatment for standardized secondary copper (and secondary cast aluminium alloy). Standard materials can be imported freely under specific commodity codes, while non-standard feedstocks face restrictions. With quotas ending in 2020, the policy could boost copper and aluminium scrap availability and support prices.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Oct 20): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, aluminium fell 0.57%_SMM
summary: SMM said Shanghai nonferrous prices mostly rose after China’s October LPR was released unchanged, easing rate expectations. Copper finished +0.18% and nickel +0.17%, supported by a weaker USD. Aluminium was the exception, down 0.57% amid fourth-quarter demand and inventory concerns and election-related macro volatility.

title: Copper steady, waiting for outcome of U.S. stimulus talks
summary: Copper prices were steady as U.S. stimulus-talk uncertainty offset expectations of strong Chinese demand. Analysts pointed to a possible deal outcome by Wednesday, while China’s industrial output and GDP data supported metals demand. A weaker dollar helped, and Chile supply disruption concerns also offered support.

title: New policy on customs codes of secondary copper (brass) raw materials: Impact analysis on copper scrap import_SMM
summary: China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment announced that standardized secondary copper (and secondary cast aluminium alloy) meeting national specs are not treated as solid waste and can be imported freely under specified customs codes. Non-compliant materials face import prohibitions, except licensed scrap. The policy may raise scrap inflows and improve availability for copper inputs.

title: Lower dollar helps copper head towards 27-month peak
summary: Copper prices climbed 0.8% toward a 27-month high as a lower U.S. dollar and firmer China growth/industrial activity expectations boosted demand sentiment. U.S. stimulus timing uncertainty limited upside. The piece also reports aluminium easing while nickel rose, showing mixed moves across other metals.

title: Copper futures on track for settle at highest in over 2 years
summary: Copper futures rose Tuesday toward their highest settlement in over two years, helped by signs of strong Chinese demand, including a new quota allowing copper scrap imports. Optimism around U.S. stimulus and potential early vaccine availability also supported sentiment. December copper gained about 2% to $3.148/lb.

title: Copper futures head for highest finish in over 2 years
summary: Copper futures rose Tuesday to their highest close in more than two years, supported by signs of strengthening demand from China. The article also cites optimism around a potential COVID-19 vaccine as early as December, which helped boost sentiment for the industrial metal.

title: Century Aluminum threatens to close SC smelter over power costs — again
summary: Century Aluminum says it will shut the last pot line at its Mount Holly, South Carolina smelter by Dec. 31 if it cannot negotiate lower electricity rates from state utility Santee Cooper. A shutdown would cut supply capacity and jobs, reflecting power-cost pressure that can affect near-term aluminium output expectations.

title: Enduro Intersects 8.85m of 31.09 g/t Gold and 1.07% Copper in NE Extension of McLymont Fault
summary: Enduro Metals reported first drilling results at its Newmont Lake Project, including intervals with meaningful copper grades (1.07% Cu over 8.85m and 4.90% Cu over 0.59m) alongside gold. As an exploration update without current production or immediate supply disruption, it is unlikely to move copper prices materially in the next few weeks.

title: Canada Nickel Company Announces Significant Mineral Resource Update at Crawford Nickel-Cobalt Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel Company announced an updated mineral resource at its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project near Timmins, Ontario. Measured and inferred resources more than doubled, with higher-grade nickel in the Main Zone and an initial East Zone resource. The update improves longer-term supply expectations but doesn’t indicate immediate production changes.

title: Copper rises to 28-month high on stimulus hopes, stronger yuan
summary: Copper prices rose toward $7,000 per tonne, supported by US coronavirus stimulus hopes, a stronger yuan, expectations of healthy Chinese demand, and prospects of China stockpiling. Supply risks increased after strikes suspended operations at Chile’s Candelaria mine. LME aluminium also gained alongside broader macro sentiment.

title: Atalaya Mining bulks up on copper with Masa Valverde acquisition
summary: Atalaya Mining says it will buy the Masa Valverde polymetallic project in Spain for €1.4 million in cash. The acquisition is described as being “on copper,” implying added future copper exposure. The payment structure and project proximity are noted, but the deal is small and effects likely limited.

title: China's imports are soaking up the world's excess copper: Andy Home
summary: ICSG forecasts a small but meaningful refined copper supply-demand deficit after previously expecting a surplus, amid output disruption from COVID-19. It attributes ongoing tightness to China’s record refined copper imports and inventory accumulation, which absorb global excess. Prices surged to a fresh year-to-date high on the LME.

title: China Demand Helps Copper Defy Covid Demand Shock – ShareCafe
summary: Copper prices are rising sharply as China’s buying wave continues for refined copper and concentrates, helping offset earlier COVID demand weakness. Imports are well above 2019 levels and the ICSG projects a small refined-copper deficit versus last year’s surplus, tightening near-term supply-demand balances.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 21/10: LME copper price soars above $7,000; nickel down 1%
summary: The live futures report states that LME copper prices have surged above $7,000, signaling strong near-term bullish momentum. It also says nickel is down 1%, implying weaker pricing pressure there. Other text mainly covers Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin updates and background on aluminium market conditions without a clear price move.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 21/10: LME copper price soars above $7,000; nickel down 1%
summary: A live LME futures report notes LME copper soaring above $7,000, while nickel is down around 1%. The rest of the text mainly concerns Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin pricing methodology updates and corrected assessments, offering limited additional information on physical market drivers.

title: New bid expected for New Caledonia's nickel plant
summary: Markets in New Caledonia expect a bid to be finalised for Vale’s nickel plant after Vale reconfirmed plans to shut. Failed prior bids and job-loss fears highlight supply concerns, while EV battery demand is supporting nickel. Vale is negotiating different nickel/cobalt supply routes.

title: Anglo American Q3 Copper Production Up 4%
summary: Anglo American said Q3 copper production increased 4% to 165,700 tonnes, helped by strong performance at Collahuasi. The company tightened its annual copper production guidance to 630,000–660,000 tonnes versus 620,000–670,000 previously, suggesting improved near-term supply expectations.

title: Lindian scoops up Woula bauxite deposit
summary: Lindian Resources agreed to acquire a 75% stake in Guinea’s Woula bauxite project, adjacent to existing haul-road and export infrastructure. The company plans scoping and resource work, targeting potential near-term open-pit direct shipping ore and improving alumina supply prospects, which can support aluminium-linked prices.

title: P&G Beauty Announces the Launch of Its First Ever Reusable and Refillable Aluminium Bottle System at Scale, with its Brands?Head & Shoulders, Pantene, Herbal Essences and Aussie in Europe
summary: P&G Beauty will launch a reusable and refillable shampoo system across Europe’s Head & Shoulders, Pantene, Herbal Essences and Aussie brands. It replaces conventional bottles with reusable 100% aluminium bottles and recyclable refill pouches, aiming to cut virgin plastic usage and increase reuse as of 2021.

title: Freeport-McMoRan profit buoyed by copper, gold
summary: Freeport-McMoRan reported a third-quarter swing to profit of $329 million, up from a year-earlier loss, with higher revenue supported by selling more copper and benefiting from favorable realized pricing (copper-linked performance) alongside higher gold prices. The results suggest improved copper earnings visibility near term.

title: Chinese firms commit 35 billion USD investment in Indonesia's nickel processing | World
summary: Chinese firms plan to double investment in Indonesia’s nickel processing to about USD 35 billion by 2033, with additional projects for EV battery supply chains. The move builds on Indonesia’s January nickel ore export stop, signaling continued domestic processing capacity expansion. Nickel prices may face supportive supply expectations.

title: Copper falls as dollar firms ahead of U.S. election
summary: London copper prices fell 0.5% as investors grew cautious ahead of the U.S. presidential election, strengthening the dollar and making dollar-priced metals costlier for non-USD buyers. Three-month copper at the LME dropped to $6,885/t, while nickel also eased slightly amid fragile sentiment.

title: Battling Battery Giants to Tap Indonesia's Vast Nickel Reserves
summary: CATL and LG Chem are investing billions in Indonesia to develop end-to-end EV battery supply chains using Indonesia’s large nickel reserves. Deals with Antam cover nickel mining and processing via battery-grade chemical production, with further plans for recycling. Such moves can raise expectations for nickel demand and feedstock needs.

title: China approves international copper futures launch on Nov. 19
summary: China’s securities regulator approved the launch of an international copper futures contract on Nov. 19, traded on the Shanghai International Energy Exchange. The move will allow foreign investors to trade copper in the world’s top consumer market, potentially increasing participation and liquidity and supporting copper price sentiment.

title: TransAlta Renewables Executes 15-year Contract Extension in Western Australia with BHP Nickel West
summary: TransAlta Renewables said Southern Cross Energy extended a power purchase agreement with BHP Nickel West for 245 MW generation in Western Australia through 2038. The deal supports BHP’s emissions targets, including solar and waste-heat projects at Nickel West sites, but does not signal immediate production changes.

title: China to launch long awaited international copper futures on Nov. 19
summary: China’s regulator approved an international copper futures contract for launch on Nov. 19 on the Shanghai International Energy Exchange, giving foreign investors access to hedging in China’s top copper market. The yuan-quoted contract aims to improve liquidity and arbitrage versus LME and other benchmarks, but no physical supply or demand shock is cited.

title: Copper drifts lower as investors question recent rally
summary: Reuters reports copper drifting lower as investors question the extent of a recent rally, with prices down on Friday and traders awaiting stimulus developments. It also cites China’s shift back to net aluminum exports and shows slight declines in LME aluminum and nickel, suggesting limited net downside pressure.

title: Cobalt, nickel rally lifts EV Metal Index to 2020 high
summary: MINING.COM reports the MINING.COM EV Metal Index, tracking battery metals in newly registered EVs, recovered month on month in July and reached a 2020 high. The move is attributed to a rally in cobalt and nickel, signaling stronger demand sentiment for nickel used in EV batteries.

title: Global copper production to increase in 2021 after two years of declines: ICSG
summary: The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released its 2020–21 copper forecast, saying 2019 saw a small production fall and 2020 is expected to be the second consecutive year of decline. It anticipates production will increase in 2021, implying improving supply conditions.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Oct 26): Shanghai nonferrous metals declined for the most part, aluminium advanced 0.14%_SMM
summary: SMM reports most SHFE nonferrous metals fell on Oct 26 as US and Europe COVID-19 cases hit records, weighing risk sentiment and driving a US dollar rebound and weaker crude oil. Copper closed slightly down, nickel more sharply lower. Aluminium was the only gainer, up 0.14%.

title: INTERVIEW: Aluminium spot market, low-carbon interest to pick up in 'blurry' 2021 - Alvance COO
summary: The excerpt is an interview/commentary on the aluminium spot market, noting that while aluminium was “hard to move” earlier, low-carbon interest is expected to pick up amid a “blurry” 2021 outlook. It also references corrections to European low-carbon aluminium differential assessments due to procedural errors.

title: China's new international copper contract comes at the right time: Russell
summary: China’s regulators announced a new international copper futures contract on the Shanghai International Energy Exchange on Nov. 19, accessible to foreign traders and settled via bonded warehouses. The piece links this to China’s dominant production/import role and strong 2020 copper import momentum, suggesting supportive near-term demand and better price discovery versus LME.

title: Adventus and Salazar Identify Porphyry System at Pijili Project:  Initial Scout Drilling Results Include 65 Metres of 0.44% CuEq and 145 Metres Of 0.30% CuEq
summary: Adventus and Salazar reported preliminary scout drilling at the Pijili project in Ecuador, intersecting a porphyry copper-gold-molybdenum system. Results include long intervals with copper grades around 0.11–0.22% Cu (with CuEq highlights), plus sulphide mineralization and alteration, encouraging further drilling and targeting.

title: Alba Q3 results impacted by aluminium price fall
summary: The (now unavailable) article headline says Alba’s Q3 results were impacted by a fall in aluminium prices. This implies lower aluminium market pricing during the quarter and potential continued bearish sentiment for aluminium in the near term, as investors reassess revenue and margin outlooks.

title: Copper dips on virus fears, U.S stimulus aid uncertainty
summary: Copper prices dipped as investors grew cautious over record COVID-19 cases and uncertainty around a U.S. stimulus package before the election. The report also notes small, mixed moves in LME aluminum and ShFE nickel alongside broader risk-off sentiment. A Peruvian mine disruption is said to have normalized.

title: London copper rebounds on dollar weakness; virus, U.S. stimulus concerns cap gains
summary: London copper rebounded 0.4% on Tuesday after earlier losses, supported by a weaker U.S. dollar. Gains were limited by rising global COVID-19 cases and renewed uncertainty over a U.S. stimulus agreement ahead of the Nov. 3 election. Shanghai copper declined, reflecting mixed regional demand sentiment.

title: Nickel surplus looms as electric vehicle buzz fades: Andy Home
summary: The piece argues nickel’s recent rally is driven mainly by nickel-ore supply shifts to China’s stainless steel sector, but forecasts a coming refined nickel surplus (117,000 tonnes in 2020 and 68,000 tonnes in 2021). It expects Philippine ore costs to normalize after Indonesia’s ban climax and notes waning EV-focused sentiment.

title: Shanghai nickel nears 2-mth high as Philippine mine halted by virus
summary: Shanghai nickel prices rose toward a two-month high as Nickel Asia suspended its Hinatuan mine in the Philippines until Nov. 10 after COVID-19 cases were detected among employees. As the country’s leading nickel ore exporter, the halt prompted supply fears, lifting ShFE and LME nickel contracts.

title: Trump lifts tariffs on imports of aluminum from Canada
summary: Trump signed a proclamation lifting tariffs on US imports of aluminum from Canada, effectively restoring duty-free treatment (retroactive to Sept. 1) after USTR’s decision. He warned tariffs could return if Canadian aluminum imports surge. Given Canada’s dominance in North American supply, the change is likely near-term price bearish for aluminium.

title: Trump signs proclamation formally exempting Canadian aluminum from tariffs, for now
summary: Trump signed a proclamation exempting Canadian aluminum from tariffs for now. The move is expected to lower effective import costs and ease short-term concerns about tighter supply or higher landed prices for aluminum. This should be supportive for aluminum prices over the coming days as trade expectations adjust.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Oct 28): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, nickel fell 1.99%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous mostly rose on Oct 28 despite higher US COVID infections and falling oil. Copper ended +0.6% with mixed macro sentiment; nickel jumped +5.31% as Philippine typhoons were expected to reduce nickel ore exports; aluminium fell -1.15% with higher open interest for related markets.

title: Nickel hits near one-year high fueled by Philippine mine closure
summary: Nickel prices jumped to near a one-year high after Nickel Asia suspended operations at its Hinatuan mine in the Philippines following a COVID outbreak. The outage threatens nickel ore supply to China, where demand from stainless steel mills remains firm, lifting both ShFE and LME nickel contracts sharply.

title: Shanghai nickel jumps most in nearly 3 months after Philippine mine closure
summary: Nickel prices surged after Nickel Asia’s Hinatuan mine in the Philippines suspended operations following a COVID-19 outbreak. With the Philippines supplying much of China’s nickel ore for stainless steel feedstock, traders cited immediate supply-chain risk. ShFE December nickel rose up to 3.3% and LME three-month nickel gained as much as 1.2%.

title: U.S. lifts tariffs on imports of aluminum from Canada - Canadian Plastics
summary: The Trump administration signed a proclamation lifting 10% tariffs on U.S. imports of aluminum from Canada and resuming duty-free treatment retroactive to Sept. 1. However, it warns tariffs could be reinstated if imports surge in late 2020. Canada supplies about 80% of its primary aluminum exports to the U.S.

title: Nickel hits near one-year high fuelled by Philippine mine closure
summary: Nickel prices surged to near a one-year high after Nickel Asia suspended operations at its Hinatuan mine in the Philippines following COVID-related cases. As the Philippines is a key nickel ore supplier to China, the shutdown raised supply worries, pushing ShFE December nickel up 5.7% and LME nickel up as much as 2.5%.

title: KAZ Minerals Q3 Copper Production Declines
summary: KAZ Minerals reported that Q3 copper production fell to 76.2 kt from 78.9 kt in Q2 and declined from 82.9 kt a year earlier. The firm also saw lower gold and silver output. It expects to meet full-year guidance if no new COVID-19 disruptions occur.

title: Canadian copper miner results 'crush expectations'
summary: Globe/analyst coverage highlights First Quantum Minerals’ “Q3 Results Crush Expectations,” including copper production of 211kt above estimates and record output at Cobre Panama and Sentinel. It also notes improved 2020 consolidated copper guidance, which would raise expectations for near-term copper supply and underpin copper sentiment.

title: Small business advocate pitches message to help Century Aluminum
summary: A dispute between Century Aluminum and Santee Cooper over industrial power rates is threatening a potential shutdown at the Mt. Holly aluminium plant. Santee Cooper says rates are competitive and offers contract extension, while the chamber warns the cost and transmission constraints could devastate output. Aluminium prices are also noted as surging.

title: First Quantum raises 2020 copper production guidance after strong Q3
summary: The news says First Quantum increased its 2020 copper production guidance following strong Q3 results. A higher projected output level suggests improved copper supply expectations, which typically exerts downward pressure on prices in the near term as the market anticipates greater availability.

title: Glencore 9M Copper, Cobalt Production Down, Zinc Up; Maintains FY20 Production View
summary: Glencore said nine-month own-sourced copper production fell 8% to 934,700 tonnes and nickel production dropped 9% to 81,800 tonnes, while zinc rose. The firm cited Mutanda’s cobalt impact and progress at Katanga, but overall output declines for copper and nickel may pressure near-term prices.

title: Kanak groups push to take over Vale's New Caledonia nickel assets
summary: Kanak groups in New Caledonia protested Vale’s planned sale of its nickel plant to a Trafigura-led consortium, arguing for local processing and due diligence with Sofinor. Vale says it will shut the plant if no buyer by end-October. Opposition and failed prior sales add near-term nickel supply uncertainty.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 34,000 wmt to 9.42 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show Chinese nickel ore inventories across all ports rose by 34,000 wmt to 9.42 million wmt between Oct 23 and Oct 30. In nickel content terms, stocks increased to 75,100 mt. Meanwhile, inventories at seven major ports fell by 56,000 wmt to 7.07 million wmt.

title: Chile's Codelco, world's largest copper producer reports profits are back
summary: Chile’s Codelco reported an 86% profit jump for the first nine months, helped by higher output (up 4% to 1.165 million tons) and lower cash costs. The results point to improved productivity and continued copper sales, supporting sentiment for near-term copper supply and pricing.

title: Copper dips as dollar firms ahead of U.S. election
summary: Copper held steady as China factory data boosted demand expectations, but a firmer U.S. dollar and election-related uncertainty offset gains; lockdowns also threaten demand. Aluminium saw reduced worries about nearby LME supplies, narrowing the cash discount, though three-month aluminium fell slightly.

title: Market talks: China is considering banning imports of copper ore from Australia _SMM
summary: Market rumours and media reports suggest China may ban imports of Australian copper ore and concentrate starting this week. SMM contacts say no official notices have been received and smelters/importers question the likelihood due to reliance on seaborne concentrate. Australia’s share of concentrate imports is small but could tighten sentiment.

title: Manufacturing activity across nickel downstream sectors in China retreated to contraction in October_SMM
summary: SMM reported China’s nickel downstream PMIs fell into contraction in October, with the composite index at 49.68 and new orders at 49.23. Stainless steel new orders weakened sharply, and raw materials purchasing slowed, including reduced procurement at electroplating plants as nickel prices rose post–National Day holidays.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Announces Strong Q3 2020 Financial Results, Reduces All-in Cost Guidance
summary: Copper Mountain reported strong Q3 2020 copper output (18.9 million lb) and significantly lower costs, cutting 2020 all-in cost guidance to US$1.85–2.00/lb. The company expects higher copper grades and improved recoveries in Q4, targeting the top end of 70–75 million lb production guidance.

title: Ivanhoe Mines : Kamoa-Kakula Copper Project achieves another monthly record for underground development with 2,172 metres completed in October; more than 24.7 kilometres now complete – 7.9 km ahead of plan
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said underground development at the Kamoa-Kakula copper project reached a monthly record in October, with ore production 48% higher than September and pre-production stockpiles rising to about one million tonnes at ~3.47% Cu. The concentrator and infrastructure construction also progresses toward planned copper concentrate production.

title: Copper miners confident of life beyond China
summary: Chinese media speculation suggests Australia’s copper exports to China could face restrictions similar to those already applied to barley, lobsters, wine and coal. Sandfire says it can sell copper outside China, but the risk of reduced China demand/export flows drove Sandfire shares lower on Tuesday.

title: Aluminium scrap meeting the new standard can be imported freely_SMM
summary: SMM reports that Chinese Customs will treat aluminium scrap conforming to a new standard as general goods, allowing freer imports and removing requirements such as 100% package inspections, qualifications, and designated ports. Non-conforming scrap still needs approval. Market focus is now on possible tariff and secondary ingot constraints.

title: Funds place their bets on copper going into U.S. election: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist Andy Home says funds are turning bullish on copper ahead of the U.S. election, citing heavy net-long CME positioning. The rally is linked to China-driven demand and expectations for a Biden-led, green infrastructure stimulus, though election uncertainty is noted as a risk.

title: NORNICKEL BOARD OF DIRECTORS RECOMMENDS INTERIM DIVIDEND FOR 9M 2020
summary: Norilsk Nickel’s board recommended an interim dividend for nine months of 2020 totaling RUB 98.64 bn and set key shareholder meeting and record dates. The company is a major nickel and copper producer, but the announcement is a corporate payout decision rather than a direct supply or demand update for metals.

title: The benchmark price for 2021 imported copper was settled at $88/mt _SMM
summary: SMM reports Codelco set 2021 copper cathode long-term contract premiums for China at $88/mt, unchanged from 2020, but some domestic traders declined the benchmark and may shift toward floating pricing. Sentiment is cautious as weaker Q3 consumption and a new secondary copper import policy may reduce cathode demand.

title: China began to levy value-added tax on gold in imported blister copper from October _SMM
summary: China customs started levying VAT on gold contained in imported plate-shaped copper anodes from October, increasing costs for higher-gold anode and reducing buyer interest. VAT-exempt ingot-shaped blister copper was favored. Refining charges for blister copper adjusted, with domestic RCs stabilizing as scrap-derived supply concerns eased by renewable copper policy from Nov 1.

title: Global Aluminum Rolled Products (1xxx, 3xxx, 5xxx and 6xxx) Market 2020-2025 with Novelis, Constellium, Arconic Rolled Products, UACJ, and Norsk Hydro ASA Dominating
summary: PRNewswire/ResearchAndMarkets promotes a report on the aluminium rolled products market (1xxx/3xxx/5xxx/6xxx), forecasting growth to 2025 and noting automotive and construction as key demand drivers. It also mentions COVID-19 expected to severely impact end-use industries. No fresh price, inventory, or trade figures are provided.

title: Copper moves sideways in thin trade as U.S. election buzz fades
summary: Copper prices were flat in thin trading as U.S. election volatility faded and a softer U.S. dollar offered support. Despite a supply shock risk from a prolonged strike at Chile’s Candelaria mine, LME three-month copper was unchanged and ShFE copper fell marginally.

title: Copper dips in thin trade as U.S. election buzz fades
summary: Copper prices fell slightly in thin trade as U.S. election volatility tapered, with the dollar weakening to support metals but not enough to offset the easing sentiment. LME three-month copper was down 0.3% and Shanghai copper down 0.5%. Separately, a strike at Chile’s Candelaria mine threatens supply.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 4,400 mt on week on larger arrivals_SMM
summary: SMM reported that China’s aluminium billet inventories rose 4,400 mt week on week to 94,500 mt as of Nov 5, mainly due to larger arrivals. Stocks increased in Foshan, Changzhou and Nanchang, were flat in Huzhou, and declined slightly in Wuxi, indicating more supply availability.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 34,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s primary aluminium ingot inventories fell for the week, down 34,000 mt to 654,000 mt as of Nov 5. The decline across consumption areas, including SHFE warrants, is linked to stronger downstream demand and limited arrivals, suggesting tighter near-term supply conditions.

title: Kirkvine workers protest two-year wage-hike delay
summary: About 120 workers at the Kirkvine refinery in Manchester and St Ann, operated by UC Rusal, are refusing to work until a delayed two-year wage hike negotiation is concluded. The dispute is before the Ministry of Labour, raising the risk of short-term output disruption for Rusal’s alumina/aluminium-linked operations.

title: Nornickel invests $51 million in new port cranes in Dudinka in northern Russia
summary: Nornickel will invest about $51 million (4 billion rubles) to buy ten new Liebherr mobile port cranes for the Dudinka port in northern Russia, with deliveries during November and completion by end-2021. The upgrades are intended to improve port handling efficiency, replacing older cranes.

title: Chile copper output costs plunged in first half even as pandemic raged
summary: Chile’s mining ministry said cash costs for its copper producers fell 17% in the first half of 2020 to $1.21 per pound, down from $1.45 a year earlier. The decline was attributed to a stronger dollar and lower processing-input prices like sulfuric acid and diesel, while mines maintained output despite COVID-19.

title: What is at stake with Australia-China trade tensions over wine, lobster and copper?
summary: The piece describes Australia–China trade tensions and notes that threatened customs actions could ban Australian copper imports from November 6, alongside restrictions on other products. It highlights China’s role as Australia’s largest export destination and the resulting risk of disrupted mineral and commodity flows.

title: Copper dips on firmer dollar; U.S. election results eyed
summary: Copper prices slipped as a slightly firmer U.S. dollar reduced the appeal of dollar-priced metals. Traders also stayed cautious while U.S. election results and prospects for a large stimulus package remained unclear. LME aluminium and nickel also fell, reflecting broad risk-off pressure.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks added 6,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: Shanghai bonded copper inventories rose for the 14th straight week, gaining 6,000 mt to 366,500 mt as of Nov 6. The import loss narrowed to under 100 yuan/mt due to a high domestic copper premium, though declared imports remain relatively limited, contributing to continued inventory growth.

title: China's Australian copper ban seen hurting smelters in TC/RCs talks
summary: Reuters reports an unofficial Chinese ban targeting increased inspections of Australian copper concentrate imports from Nov. 6. Traders say shipments are being diverted, while South American supply is disrupted by COVID-19. Spot TC/RCs have fallen to an eight-year low, and analysts expect benchmark rates to drop, pressuring smelters and price expectations for copper processing.

title: Copper dips as dollar firms; investor focus remains on U.S. election results
summary: Copper prices edged lower as a slightly firmer U.S. dollar reduced demand for dollar-priced commodities, amid uncertainty while election results are finalized. Traders expect U.S. stimulus and green-energy investment (under a potential Biden win) to support sentiment next week. Nickel and aluminium also fell alongside broader risk moves.

title: China copper imports rose 43.4 y/y in Oct, set annual peak in just 10 months
summary: China’s October copper imports rose 43.4% y/y to 618,108 tonnes, reaching a new annual peak and reflecting rapid post-COVID demand recovery and prior arbitrage buying. Imports of copper concentrate also fell. Aluminum exports in October declined slightly, with China shifting between net importer and exporter positions earlier in the year.

title: Chile copper export revenue surges 24% in October - central bank
summary: Chile’s central bank reported copper export revenue rose 24% in October, with copper exports up to $3.211 billion and lifting the trade balance. The central bank attributed the surge to recovering global copper prices. As Chile is the world’s top copper producer, the data reinforces near-term copper demand/price expectations.

title: Doubleview Gold : Visible Gold Occurrence in Drill Core at Hat Gold Rich Copper Porphyry deposit
summary: Doubleview Gold reports visible gold and chalcopyrite (and possibly chalcocite) in drill core from its Hat porphyry deposit within the Lisle zone. Two 2020 holes intersected mineralized sections but were abandoned in a fault zone. Core samples are pending lab analysis; no copper assays or production changes are provided.

title: ALX Resources Corp. and Rio Tinto Locate Airborne EM Anomalies at the Firebird Nickel Project
summary: ALX Resources and Rio Tinto reported preliminary airborne electromagnetic VTEM survey results at the Firebird nickel project in Saskatchewan, identifying new high-conductivity targets for potential drilling. ALX expects additional processing over coming weeks to assess anomalies’ depth and viability. Current disclosure is exploration-focused, with no near-term production impacts mentioned.

title: Brazil alumina exports down 33% in October; Alunorte shipments drop
summary: Brazilian alumina exports reportedly fell 33% in October, with Alunorte shipments also dropping. The reduction in alumina availability can constrain aluminium smelter feedstock and weaken near-term production outlooks, typically exerting bearish pressure on aluminium prices over the coming weeks.

title: Copper hits 29-month high on vaccine hope and Biden win
summary: Copper surged to a 29-month high after news of promising COVID-19 vaccine results and investor optimism following Joe Biden’s election win, which supported hopes for better trade conditions. A weaker U.S. dollar helped dollar-priced metals. Aluminium and nickel also rose strongly in the same risk-on rally.

title: FPX Nickel Highlights New Geoscience BC Report Outlining the Potential for Significant Carbon Capture at Baptiste Nickel Project
summary: FPX Nickel highlights a Geoscience BC/UBC report suggesting ultramafic tailings at its Baptiste nickel-iron alloy project could sequester substantial CO2 through mineralization, potentially enabling low- or net-negative carbon nickel production. It also describes ongoing field tests, with findings expected in 2021.

title: Mitsui to Sell Its Interest in the Caserones Copper Mine in Chile and Dissolution and Liquidation of a Subsidiary Company
summary: Mitsui plans to sell its interest in Chile’s Caserones copper mine and dissolve/liquidate a subsidiary. While this is directly related to copper production, the provided information lacks specifics on any immediate production impact, output changes, or operational disruptions that would likely move copper prices in the next few weeks.

title: Copper eases as virus worries outweigh vaccine hopes
summary: Copper prices eased as worries about a COVID-19 resurgence and weaker near-term economic recovery outweighed optimism from positive vaccine trial news. Analysts cited potential renewed lockdowns in Europe and possible U.S. restrictions. China’s industrial upstream demand also appeared tepid, pressuring copper futures on both SHFE and LME.

title: A tense calm in Guinea – but trouble is on the horizon
summary: Guinea’s disputed election result has sparked clashes and ongoing instability. The piece notes Russia-backed support for President Conde is tied to aluminium supply, as Rusal sources part of its bauxite from Guinean mines. Conde’s victory may reassure investors, but violence and disruption risks offset that in the near term.

title: China refined nickel consumption to reach 5% growth in 2021 _SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Chinese alloy producers running at full capacity since August, supported by solid new orders. It expects demand to remain stable and potentially rise as infrastructure demand continues, with further support from automobile and home appliance sectors, pointing to higher refined nickel consumption growth of about 5% in 2021.

title: Copper slips from 29-month highs as dollar strengthens
summary: Copper eased from 29-month highs as the U.S. dollar strengthened, making the metal more expensive for non-dollar buyers. Benchmark three-month LME copper fell 0.3% to about $6,895/ton. Despite optimism from a COVID-19 vaccine and renewable-energy demand, October China weakness and maintenance reduced support.

title: TransLink to test anti-microbial copper on high-touch surfaces to reduce COVID-19 transmission
summary: TransLink will run a four-week pilot in Vancouver testing antimicrobial copper on high-touch surfaces in SkyTrains and buses to reduce COVID-19 transmission. Vancouver Coastal Health will evaluate copper and protective coatings twice weekly. Teck Resources reportedly funds the project (~$90,000). The copper demand is limited and local.

title: London copper hovers near 2-1/2-year high on vaccine, stimulus hopes
summary: London copper traded near a 29-month high as vaccine optimism and prospects for further U.S./European stimulus lifted expectations of a quicker global economic reopening. LME three-month copper rose 0.5% while LME aluminium gained 0.5% and Chinese aluminium prices firmed, reflecting supportive demand sentiment and easing tightness concerns.

title: Vaccine hopes help propel copper towards 29-month peak
summary: Copper prices climbed toward 29-month highs as vaccine optimism and signs of robust Chinese demand supported expectations. China copper imports rose year-on-year to a new annual peak, though traders questioned consumption versus imports. Aluminum gained modestly as LME supply concerns eased; nickel was slightly weaker.

title: Kakula Copper Mine's Northern and Southern Access Tunnels Successfully Connected
summary: Ivanhoe Mines announced the successful connection (“holing”) of Kakula’s northern and southern access tunnels in the DRC, opening high-grade drift-and-fill ore blocks. The milestone improves ventilation and enables immediate development toward feeding the concentrator plant, with Phase 1 copper concentrate production scheduled for July 2021.

title: Shanghai aluminum hits 3-year high on low China inventories, demand pick-up
summary: Shanghai aluminum jumped to a three-year high as China’s primary aluminum inventories fell and demand picked up in sectors including construction, automobiles and photovoltaics. The ShFE December contract gained up to 2.5%, while LME aluminum also rose, reflecting tightening fundamentals and supportive spreads.

title: Mirasol Resources Introduces Nandi Copper Project in Chile
summary: Mirasol Resources reports initial exploration results from its Nandi copper project in northern Chile, within the porphyry Cu belt and near BHP’s Escondida and Glencore’s Lomas Bayas. Early mapping and geochemistry show anomalous Cu and Au targets for potential porphyry Cu/Mo/Au mineralization, but no production changes.

title: London copper slips further from $7,000 on virus worries
summary: London copper eased from near $7,000 as rising COVID-19 cases and tighter restrictions reduced expectations for a rapid global economic recovery. Analysts flagged ongoing macro risks, including Europe and U.S. uncertainty. The report also shows LME nickel weaker and ShFE aluminium higher, suggesting mixed but overall risk-driven metal sentiment.

title: Zambia plans sale of copper mines owned by billionaire Anil Agarwal
summary: Zambia’s seizure and planned sale of Vedanta’s Konkola Copper Mines faces delays due to London arbitration and other legal challenges. With KCM cash-starved, high-cost operations and low output persist while investors wait for case outcomes, potentially weighing on Zambia’s copper supply outlook amid broader financial strain.

title: EGA signs deal with Colombian firm for the export of aluminium production technology
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) signed an agreement to license its aluminium smelting production technology and provide technical services for NEO Aluminio Colombia’s planned Colombian “Green Aluminium Transformation Complex.” The project targets 540,000 tonnes per year. The deal strengthens EGA’s technology sales pipeline and supports aluminium production prospects.

title: Industrial metals jump on China demand optimism, copper at 29-month high
summary: Industrial metals rallied as China demand optimism grew after faster-than-expected October industrial output. Copper hit 29-month highs, supported by falling Shanghai exchange inventories. Aluminium reached a three-year peak, with output at records and briefly positive import arbitrage. Nickel also rose in London and Shanghai amid the broader move.

title: Secondary aluminium prices lost upward momentum on eased supply concerns of imported aluminum scrap_SMM
summary: SMM reports secondary aluminium operating rates easing in October as downstream buyers wait after news of China’s scrap import liberalization. Export and imported ADC12 prices have softened, and traders have reduced new orders amid possible tariff changes and attempts to import aluminium alloy ingots duty-free, potentially increasing supply.

title: Copper hits 2-1/2 year high on upbeat China data
summary: Copper surged to a 29-month high after stronger-than-expected China factory output reinforced expectations of solid industrial metals demand. LME and Shanghai aluminium also hit multi-year peaks as consumption held firm. The piece attributes the move to demand recovery and easing supply concerns, with nickel rising in tandem.

title: Birdcall to Introduce the Ball Aluminum Cup™ to Cut Down on Plastic Cups
summary: Birdcall will replace single-use plastic cups at its Colorado restaurants with Ball Corporation’s recyclable “Ball Aluminum Cup.” The company frames the move as sustainability-focused and aims to increase aluminum beverage packaging, while noting the cup is reusable and recyclable like a can.

title: Nickel hits 1-week low, tracking Shanghai stainless steel losses
summary: Nickel fell to a one-week low on Tuesday, with LME three-month nickel down as much as 1.5% and Shanghai nickel sliding after Chinese stainless steel futures weakened. Analysts cite high input costs and flat demand. Copper and aluminium also edged lower in Shanghai and London amid subdued investor risk sentiment.

title: China's new copper futures add another card to global yuan deck
summary: China will launch a new internationally accessible yuan-denominated copper futures contract on the Shanghai INE, aiming to boost yuan adoption and gradually shift pricing influence away from London’s benchmark. Analysts expect improved liquidity and investor interest, though yuan convertibility and capital controls remain near-term barriers.

title: Copper surges on Peru protests, China futures launch
summary: Copper prices jumped to fresh multiyear highs as investors feared potential supply disruptions from Peru protests. Prices also gained support from optimism surrounding the launch of a China futures contract open to international investors, which may improve liquidity and demand expectations. The market cited Comex December copper strength.

title: Emirates Global Aluminium pens deal for Colombia's first aluminium facility
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) agreed to export its UAE-developed aluminium smelting technology to NEO Aluminio Colombia to support a planned low-carbon smelter in northwest Colombia. The Green Aluminium Transformation Complex (GALTCO) is intended to reach 540 ktpa and be hydro-powered.

title: Aluminium at highest in nearly 2 years on China demand
summary: Reuters reports aluminium prices jumped to the highest in nearly two years on Tuesday as speculators bought ahead of expected further tightness in China. China demand is said to be up sharply, while global supply remains oversupplied but China is tighter, supporting rising LME and Shanghai futures prices.

title: NBS: China's copper cathode output rose 5.4% year on year in October _SMM
summary: China’s NBS data show copper cathode output reached 914,000 mt in October, up 5.4% YoY, with 8.36 million mt produced in the first ten months. Alumina output fell to 6.39 million mt, while lead output hit 599,000 mt. Higher copper supply may weigh on prices.

title: Green light for bauxite mining in Cockpit Country
summary: An EIA has given a green light for Noranda Jamaica Bauxite Partners to mine 8,335 hectares of bauxite in Jamaica’s Cockpit Country (SML 173), with Jamaica holding 51% stake via NJBP II and New Day Aluminum holding 49%. The report highlights economic benefits and implies improved near-term bauxite supply.

title: Shanghai copper slips on virus worries; aluminium shines
summary: Shanghai copper eased 0.3% as investors worried about higher COVID-19 cases and renewed lockdowns in the US and Europe, though declines were limited by supply-side concerns. Copper demand sentiment was supported by China factory output data. Aluminium climbed to multi-year highs on expectations of supply tightness.

title: Shanghai copper slips on virus worries; aluminium shines
summary: Shanghai copper futures fell 0.3% as COVID-19 worries and new US/EU lockdowns raised demand concerns, while supply-side worries limited losses. Aluminium rose to multi-year highs on expectations of a supply crunch. The piece also mentions a reduction in Shanghai nickel futures margins, affecting trading conditions, though nickel direction was mixed.

title: Palladium One Discovers up to 0.41% Nickel in Boulders and Begins Drill Program at the Tyko Nickel-Copper-PGE Project in Canada
summary: Palladium One reports finding anomalous nickel and some copper in boulders and soils at its Tyko Ni-Cu-PGE Project in Ontario, with a drill program scheduled to begin Nov. 23, 2020. The update is exploration-stage and does not confirm production, so near-term price effects should be limited.

title: Global Water Atomizing Copper Powder Market 2020 Industry Emerging Trend, Top Players, Revenue Insights to 2025 – Business
summary: A press-release-style market report outlines trends and outlook for the global water atomized copper powder market through 2025, citing COVID-19 impact and expected post-crisis prospects. It discusses market structure, players, applications, and geography, but offers no specific near-term pricing or supply-demand shocks for copper.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Resources Tables 177 Million Pounds of Nickel in Sweden
summary: Gungnir reports updated mineral resource estimates totaling about 177 million pounds of nickel at two deposits in Sweden and notes potential upside from further drilling. The update is based on prior drill data and does not announce production changes, so near-term price impact on nickel (and minor copper) is likely limited.

title: EGA to establish Colombia's first aluminium production facility
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) agreed to license its UAE-developed aluminium smelting technology and provide technical services for Colombia’s proposed GALTCO low-carbon aluminium transformation complex. The hydro-powered project targets up to 540,000 tonnes per year. The deal supports future capacity, but timing is not immediate.

title: COVID-19 mine disruption causes copper concentrates crunch: Andy Home
summary: Reuters reports that COVID-19 mine lockdowns have resulted in a copper concentrates crunch, with smelters facing raw-material shortfalls. Treatment/refining charges in China have fallen to eight-year lows and smelter buying floors are extremely cheap, signaling tight concentrate availability and bullish near-term copper fundamentals.

title: This Month in PCB007 Magazine: The Copper Foil Market Is Anything But Flat
summary: The interview covers Denkai America, a U.S. copper foil and electrodeposition producer recently acquired by Nippon Denkai, and highlights manufacturing and customer-driven changes tied to PCB trends like smaller features and varied resin/substrate requirements. While it relates to copper foil supply, it doesn’t provide concrete near-term copper price signals.

title: UC Rusal workers take industrial action over wages
summary: UC Rusal Alumina Jamaica workers represented by UCASE have taken industrial action after wage talks at Jamaica’s Labour Ministry stalled. The union says the company proposes low increases and contract extensions with zero percent for later years. The disruption could affect alumina/aluminium production and lift short-term aluminium supply risk.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 18/11: Aluminium surpasses November 2018 high; zinc up 2%
summary: The live futures report states aluminium has surpassed its November 2018 high, signalling strong near-term momentum for aluminium prices. It also notes Fastmarkets corrected and updated certain low-carbon aluminium assessment specifications after procedural errors, implying data housekeeping rather than a negative demand/supply shock.

title: How is copper affected by the adjustment of catalogue of prohibited commodities in processing trade?_SMM
summary: China’s customs and commerce authorities adjusted the prohibited catalogue for processing trade, removing 199 commodity codes. Copper ore and copper concentrate were referenced, changing the prohibition method from outright import to an adjusted mode. However, SMM notes this is largely a wording clarification with no change in actual implementation.

title: China's new international copper futures slip in debut
summary: China’s Shanghai International Energy Exchange (INE) launched bonded copper futures open to overseas investors, but prices slipped on debut. Front-month copper for March 2021 fell about 1.2% to 47,090 yuan/tonne, with trading volumes far below the domestic ShFE contract. Traders cited a potentially high listing price and low initial liquidity.

title: Bonded copper futures starts trading on Shanghai exchange
summary: Bonded copper futures began trading at the Shanghai International Energy Exchange, allowing foreign investors to trade the contract with renminbi denomination and bonded delivery. The move expands international platform access via major overseas trading systems and brokers, potentially boosting liquidity and influencing near-term copper price expectations.

title: China's new copper contract off to a spluttering start
summary: China’s new global copper contract began trading with a sharp decline, falling about 1.4% at the open on the Shanghai International Energy Exchange. The move reflects broader downside sentiment in industrial metals as investors worry that additional coronavirus lockdowns could dampen copper demand.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 14,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Nonferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows China’s primary aluminium ingot inventories continued to fall, dropping 14,000 mt from last Thursday to 615,000 mt as of Nov 19.
