title: Copper hovers near 8-year high on stimulus hopes
summary: Copper prices rose to near an eight-year high on stimulus hopes after Democrats gained control of the U.S. Senate. Three-month LME copper and Shanghai futures climbed, with analysts saying potential investment in EV and renewable infrastructure would support copper demand in coming weeks.

title: Codelco will overhaul overhaul Copper Mine in Chile and start operation in the second half of next year_SMM
summary: Codelco approved $1.383 billion to overhaul its El Teniente “Rajo Inca” project, converting an aging underground mine to an open pit. The plan targets about 95,000 tpa and construction starts this year, with production expected in the second half of next year. Costs are said to be 33% lower than a prior estimate.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 14,900 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows Chinese inventories of 6063 aluminium billet across major consumption areas rose 14,900 mt from the prior week to 85,700 mt as of Jan 7. Stock increases were led by Guangdong (+9,100 mt to 41,600 mt), with additional gains in other regions, indicating softer near-term billet demand.

title: Copper Mountain Exceeds 2020 Production Guidance and Provides 2021 Guidance
summary: Copper Mountain Mining said its Copper Mountain mine exceeded 2020 copper guidance, producing 77.6 million pounds versus 70–75 million pounds, with strong Q4 output. It also guided 2021 copper production higher to 85–95 million pounds, citing higher grades and improved recovery/throughput from the mill expansion.

title: Forest Service To Initiate Oak Flat Land Swap For Copper Mine Jan. 15
summary: The U.S. Forest Service will release the final environmental impact statement for a land swap in Arizona on Jan. 15, a step needed for Resolution Copper (Rio Tinto) to obtain title to Oak Flat. The project would become one of the largest U.S. copper mines, boosting supply expectations despite controversy.

title: EnGold Mines Ltd.: EnGold Lac La Hache Drilling Returns 5.05 Metres of 2.75% Copper Equivalent at G1-South
summary: EnGold Mines reported drilling that extends its G1 copper zone at the Lac La Hache property, including hole G20-51 returning 5.05 metres at 2.75% CuEq within a wider 23.7-m interval at 0.51% CuEq. Results support continued exploration along the prospective trend.

title: Here To Serve Holding Corp.: Fortune Nickel and Gold Inc. Acquires Strategic Nickel and Gold Lands Near Timmins, Ontario
summary: Fortune Nickel and Gold Inc. acquired 75 mining claims near Timmins, Ontario in a nickel-bearing area, issued shares, and granted a 1% net smelter return royalty. The claims include historic drill intersections and reported nickel grades, complementing its existing Gowan nickel project.

title: Lockdown measures: Primary aluminium sector gets green light to keep operations running safely
summary: Quebec’s government approved measures that let Canada’s primary aluminium sector continue running safely during the next four-week lockdown. The Aluminium Association of Canada says smelters (largely in Quebec) maintained operations during the prior lockdown with strengthened sanitary controls, lowering shutdown risk.

title: Ball Announces New Aluminum End Manufacturing Facility in Bowling Green, Kentucky; Production Scheduled to Begin in Early-2022
summary: Ball Corporation plans to build and expand an aluminum end manufacturing facility in Bowling Green, Kentucky, with production scheduled to begin in early-2022. The facility will supply aluminum ends to Ball’s North American beverage can network, supported by long-term customer contracts amid demand for aluminum packaging.

title: Copper jumps to 2013 peak on Biden infrastructure, stimulus hopes
summary: Copper prices rose for a third straight day, reaching their highest since 2013 on optimism for Biden-era $2 trillion infrastructure spending after Democrats won Senate control. Nickel also rallied to multi-year highs on strength in Chinese stainless steel and lower inventories. Aluminium edged down slightly amid the broader reflation move.

title: First Notice: Aluminum relief; CPP eyes Finland; RAIC panel
summary: The Aluminium Association of Canada said it welcomes Quebec’s expanded-lockdown measures because they allow the province’s aluminium sector to keep operating for the next four weeks. By reducing shutdown risk and preserving production continuity, the announcement is supportive for near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Chile's copper export revenue rose 6.7% in December._SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chile’s central bank said December trade surplus was driven by higher copper export receipts. Copper export revenue rose 6.7% to $3.747 billion, and the article notes Chile maintained production through the COVID period. As the world’s largest copper producer, the update supports near-term copper market sentiment.

title: Australian state approves copper mine
summary: Australia’s Northern Territory approved KGL Resources’ A$200 million Jervois Copper Project. The developer says it will become a major supplier amid growing demand and a potential future copper shortage. Financing and concentrate marketing discussions have started, with initial concentrate transport to Alice Springs and calls for rail expansion.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 153,000 wmt to 9.14 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories across all Chinese ports fell 153,000 wmt to 9.14 million wmt as of Jan 8, with Ni content down 1,200 mt to 72,300 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also dropped to 7.12 million wmt, suggesting tighter near-term supply.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 200 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 200 mt to 22,800 mt week-on-week as overseas pandemic conditions limited arrivals. Despite this, a post–New Year drop in nickel plate import tariff to 1% reduced import loss, prompting flows into bonded areas and expectations of additional bills of lading next week.

title: Copper Mountain reports record Q4 production - The Northern Miner
summary: Copper Mountain Mining reported record fourth-quarter output and said it beat 2020 guidance. The company is also projecting a further 22% production increase this year from its Copper Mountain mine in British Columbia, which could affect near-term expectations for copper supply. The article provides operational updates without broader market context.

title: Glencore is close to selling troubled Zambian copper mine
summary: Glencore is reportedly close to selling a troubled copper mine in Zambia. Traders typically interpret such developments as reducing the probability of prolonged production disruption at the asset, easing short-term supply-risk perceptions and weighing on expectations for copper prices over the coming days.

title: Ero Copper files Technical Report for the NX Gold Mine
summary: Ero Copper Corp. filed its 2020 Technical Report for the NX gold mine, updating mineral reserves and resources previously announced in November 2020. While the report concerns gold/silver, the company is primarily focused on copper production from its Brazilian copper assets, which may marginally support copper sentiment.

title: Jindal Aluminium sees better export prospects on demand from emerging markets
summary: Jindal Aluminium says it saw no drop in exports and expects international demand to rise, especially from emerging markets, helping offset subdued US sales due to a 48% anti-dumping duty. The firm also calls for higher import duties on downstream aluminium and duty-free primary aluminium, implying supportive demand outlook.

title: 5 Top Weekly TSX Stocks: Copper Hits US$8,000, Stocks Surge
summary: The TSX materials-heavy index rose after a mid-session dip, with copper described as surging above US$8,100 per tonne—its highest level in eight years. The piece highlights TSX-listed copper-focused miners that gained sharply, reinforcing strong near-term bullish sentiment for copper prices.

title: Blister copper produced from copper scrap is expected to be sufficient in supply_SMM
summary: SMM reports blister copper refining charges: domestic RCs rose to 1,450–1,550 yuan/mt and imported CIF RCs increased to $155–165/mt in December. Scrap policy boosted overseas high-quality scrap inflows, raising scrap smelter output. Inventories at refineries remain abundant, keeping RCs high.

title: New proposal mooted in New Caledonia nickel plant sale
summary: New Caledonia’s Southern Province president proposed that local shareholders hold 51% of Vale’s nickel plant purchase, while Trafigura’s stake be cut to under 20%. Talks continue after prior sale efforts faced protests and arson at the Vale site, raising concerns over potential mothballing and jobs.

title: The impact on copper and steel sectors as Hebei announced a "state of wartime" _SMM
summary: Hebei announced a “state of wartime” as COVID-19 cases rose, closing expressways and making parts of Shijiazhuang a high-risk zone. Copper traders in Shijiazhuang worked from home and trades were suspended. Some copper producers and rod makers in Xingtai halted or reduced output due to transportation disruptions.

title: Six companies bid for Egypt Aluminum's car wheel rim production line project
summary: Egypt Aluminum says six consulting firms have submitted technical bids to produce a feasibility study for a new car wheel rim production line. The companies are from China, Italy, Germany, the UK, and a JV. While the project could support downstream aluminium demand, it remains early-stage and not tied to immediate output.

title: Mongolia considers terminating, replacing plan to develop Oyu Tolgoi copper mine
summary: Mongolia is considering terminating and replacing the development and financial plan for the Oyu Tolgoi copper mine, Turquoise Hill Resources said. The government is dissatisfied with the company’s plan to reach production for $6.75 billion in development capital. Oyu Tolgoi is a major copper deposit.

title: Castillo Copper hails 'major' copper discovery at Mt Oxide in Australia following assay results | 11 January 2021
summary: The article title says Castillo Copper has hailed a “major” copper discovery at Mt Oxide in Australia after receiving assay results. Positive exploration news can lift market sentiment about future copper supply prospects, potentially providing short-term support to copper prices, though the magnitude/timing of eventual production remains uncertain.

title: Canada Nickel mulls using Glencore's processing facility in Ontario
summary: Canada Nickel has signed an agreement with Glencore to explore using the Kidd concentrator and metallurgical site in Timmins, Ontario. The plan would let Canada Nickel process its material at Glencore’s facilities, potentially improving nickel processing capacity. However, it remains a potential, not finalized, arrangement.

title: Surge Copper Resumes Drilling at Ootsa and Expands Drill Program
summary: Surge Copper reported drilling resumed and expanded at its Ootsa project, adding at least 5,000 metres to target resource expansion at West Seel and East Seel. Assay results highlighted encouraging copper grades, and permitting is underway for future drilling at the Berg deposit. No production impacts are stated.

title: Canada Nickel signs deal to process at Kidd Met site
summary: Canada Nickel signed a non-binding MOU with Glencore Canada to potentially process material from its nearby Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project at the Kidd concentrator/metallurgical site. Using existing surplus capacity could speed production and reduce retrofit costs, with a study expected in late March.

title: Shanghai copper drops as China's COVID-19 cases stoke demand fears
summary: Shanghai copper fell as rising COVID-19 cases in China sparked fears of demand disruption ahead of Lunar New Year. The March contract dropped up to 2.5% to a one-week low, while ShFE aluminium and nickel also declined around 2% on weakened sentiment for the world’s biggest metals consumer.

title: Shanghai copper hits 1-week low as China imposes new virus curbs
summary: Shanghai copper fell to a one-week low after China imposed fresh virus curbs, renewing concerns over demand from the world’s largest metals consumer. ShFE copper slid 1.3%. Aluminium fell 1.4% and nickel was slightly lower, reflecting expectations of slower industrial activity and tempered recovery.

title: Libero Intersects 80.77 Metres of 0.43% Copper Equivalent at Big Red From Surface
summary: Libero Copper & Gold reported assay results from two holes at the Big Red project’s Terry porphyry copper-gold target in Canada, including near-surface copper intervals such as 0.36% Cu over 80.77 metres. Remaining holes are pending and a 2021 diamond program is planned. Likely limited near-term price impact.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Kicks off the New Year Intersecting 8.39 Meters (27.53 Feet) of Mineralization Grading 8.15% Nickel (9.83% NiEq) at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reported a new drilling intercept at the Tamarack nickel-copper project in Minnesota: 8.39 meters grading 8.15% nickel and 3.01% copper (plus cobalt and PGM/Au). The company says results increase confidence in continuous thick mineralization and plans more drilling and a pre-feasibility study.

title: Rusal America releases new line of sustainable, high-performance aluminum Additive Manufacturing powders
summary: Rusal America announced a new line of low-carbon aluminum powder alloys for additive manufacturing, including Al-Si casting alloys and specialty aerospace/automotive grades. It emphasizes pre-alloyed powders, atomization from Rusal’s low-carbon feedstock, and certification of carbon footprint. The release expands product scope but gives no volume or price impact.

title: Future Returns: Copper Plays a Leading Role in the Green Economy
summary: Barron’s highlights copper’s role in the green economy, citing that renewable power and EVs are copper intensive and that major initiatives (e.g., European Green Deal, China targets) are expected to lift demand. It also notes constrained recent supply growth and ongoing development timelines, implying bullish copper price pressure.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Upsize to Its Previously Announced Bought Deal Offering to $33 Million
summary: Nevada Copper upsized its bought deal offering to $33 million to meet funding needs for its Pumpkin Hollow Underground Project ramp-up, including $5 million for a cost overrun facility. The release links the funding to ramp-up progress in a “positive market for copper,” which may improve near-term supply expectations.

title: Talon Metals Kicks off the New Year Intersecting 8.39 Meters of Mineralization Grading 8.15% Nickel at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reports drill hole 20TK0273 intersected 8.39 meters of massive sulphide mineralization grading 8.15% nickel and 3.01% copper at the Tamarack project in Minnesota. The company says the thick, high-grade result improves confidence in continuous Ni-Cu mineralization and plans more drilling and a pre-feasibility study.

title: FPX Nickel Reports Potential to Achieve Production with Lowest Carbon Footprint in Global Nickel Industry
summary: FPX Nickel says its Baptiste project could produce 63% refined nickel with very low carbon intensity by using hydro power and bypassing smelting, with an estimated 2.40 tCO2/t refined Ni (potentially lower with tailings sequestration). The note is based on a PEA and positions the product for carbon-threshold buyers.

title: GLOBAL ALUMINIUM WRAP: Premiums mostly flat; Brazilian import premium dips
summary: Global aluminium wrap pricing is largely steady, with premiums mostly flat. However, the Brazilian import premium shows a dip versus prior assessments, indicating some localized softening in aluminium buying costs and differentials despite generally stable overall market conditions.

title: Native Americans sue Trump administration over Arizona copper project
summary: Native Americans, via Apache Stronghold and the San Carlos Apache tribe, sued the Trump administration to stop a land swap in Arizona that would transfer Oak Flat to Rio Tinto for the Resolution Copper project. The final environmental impact statement could be published Friday and land transfer planned for Jan. 15.

title: Apache group sues over land swap for Arizona copper mine
summary: Apache Stronghold sued the U.S. government to stop a land swap that would allow Rio Tinto’s Resolution Copper to develop the Oak Flat site in Arizona. Opponents argue the Forest Service is transferring land despite treaty protections, while officials plan to release a final environmental review that starts a 60-day transfer clock.

title: Apache group sues to stop a land swap at a copper mine site
summary: Apache Stronghold sued the U.S. Forest Service to block a final environmental impact statement that would enable a land swap for the Resolution Copper/Magma Mine at Oak Flat, Arizona. Opponents argue procedural failures and treaty-based limits. The suit seeks an injunction, potentially delaying copper output and weighing on supply expectations.

title: Los Andes Copper
summary: The piece argues copper demand is rising due to global electrification and suggests markets may stay in deficit through 2026. It profiles Los Andes Copper’s Vizcachitas project in Chile, noting financing and strong project economics tied to copper prices. Overall messaging is supportive of copper price sentiment.

title: MEED | Bahrain aluminium firm hits production milestone
summary: A MEED piece reports that a Bahrain aluminium firm has achieved a production milestone. While details are not provided in the excerpt, production milestones can signal progress in output/ramp-up, influencing near-term aluminium supply expectations and potentially supporting aluminium prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Native Americans seek to stop Rio Tinto, BHP copper mine plan
summary: Native American groups (Apache Stronghold and the San Carlos Apache Tribe) filed a lawsuit to stop the US government from transferring land at Oak Flat, Arizona, to Resolution Copper, a joint venture of Rio Tinto and BHP. The court action seeks to prevent final environmental steps that could enable a major new copper project.

title: Los Andes Copper Ltd. Receives Updated Rougher Flotation Assessment Results for the Vizcachitas Project
summary: Los Andes Copper reported improved rougher flotation recovery results for its Vizcachitas Chile copper-molybdenum project. Updated metallurgical testwork refined flotation conditions, increasing copper rougher recovery by about 2.8% versus prior PEA formulas. The improvement enhances project economics, supporting near-term bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Nickel prices rise on New Caledonian, Philippine supply worries
summary: Shanghai and LME nickel prices rose as traders feared supply disruptions in key ore-producing regions. Eramet warned its SLN unit in New Caledonia could face liquidation within weeks if protests continue. A Philippines nickel mining ban also boosted supply worries, though it excludes Caraga.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 12): Shanghai nonferrous metals all closed lower, aluminium weakened 1.35%_SMM
summary: SMM reports that Shanghai nonferrous futures closed lower across the board. Copper fell 1.26% and aluminium weakened 1.35%; nickel was slightly lower. The piece links the drop to higher US Treasury yields and a stronger US dollar, with China’s financing/M2 data due and the market watching key contract levels.

title: Mongolia is considering ending its cooperation with Rio Tinto involving the world's largest copper and gold ore reserves of up to 30 million tons._SMM
summary: Mongolia is considering ending or revising cooperation with Rio Tinto’s Oyu Tolgoi, citing dissatisfaction with updated expansion costs and benefits. Underground development estimates have risen to $6.75 billion, with production timing concerns and potential renegotiation of commitments. Such uncertainty around a large copper mine is bearish for copper.

title: Adventus and Salazar Announce Drilling Results at the El Domo Deposit Highlighted by 17.38% Copper Equivalent Over 5.70 Metres and Provide an Update on 2021 Exploration and Development Plans in Ecuador
summary: Adventus and Salazar announce additional infill drilling at the El Domo copper-gold deposit in Ecuador, including intervals with high copper grades and improved CuEq highlights. Results will be used to update the Mineral Resource and feed ongoing feasibility and development planning for a potential future mine. This supports near-term copper sentiment.

title: Blue Rhino Capital Corp: Blue Rhino Signs Letter of Intent to Acquire Zebediela Nickel Project
summary: Blue Rhino Capital signed a letter of intent to acquire entities controlling the Zebediela Nickel Project in South Africa. The transaction is conditional on financing and approvals and is aimed at exploration and development. Despite no near-term production, the deal can modestly improve nickel project sentiment and market expectations.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 13): Shanghai nonferrous metals were mostly higher, nickel surged 3.15%_SMM
summary: SMM reports most Shanghai nonferrous base metals rose on Jan 13. Nickel surged 3.15% and copper gained 0.72%, supported by a softer dollar and higher oil. Aluminium declined 1.11%. The note also includes contract closes, open-interest changes, and brief supply-demand commentary for other metals.

title: APAA Congratulates President-Elect Biden and Calls for the Preservation of the Section 232 Aluminum Tariffs
summary: APAA urged President-elect Biden to keep Section 232 aluminum tariffs, arguing they preserved thousands of U.S. aluminum jobs, boosted primary production, and restarted idled smelters. It warns that removing the measures before global balance improves could force remaining U.S. smelters to shut, raising vulnerability of supply chains.

title: Latin Metals Receives Positive Results from Mapping and Sampling at the Lacsha Copper Project, Peru
summary: Latin Metals reports positive mapping and rock sampling results from its Lacsha copper project in Peru, with copper values up to 6,410 ppm. The company plans additional stream sediment sampling, further mapping, and eventual drill permitting. The update supports exploration progress but provides no production or near-term supply impact.

title: Tiwai Point aluminium smelter to keep operating until end of 2024
summary: Rio Tinto’s Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in New Zealand will keep running through end-December 2024 after a new contract with Meridian that lowers power/transmission costs and makes the operation “economically viable.” The extension delays a planned shutdown, preserving aluminium supply while enhancing pricing certainty for 3–4 years.

title: Apache Group Sues Over Land Swap For Arizona Copper Mine
summary: Apache Stronghold sued the federal government over a land swap in Arizona tied to opening a major Rio Tinto copper mine. The Forest Service plans to release a final environmental review and finalize the land exchange Friday. Legal challenges raise the risk of delay or additional review, supporting copper price sentiment.

title: Bluff's Tiwai Point aluminium smelter will be operational for at least another four years - 14-Jan-2021
summary: Rio Tinto and Meridian Energy reached an agreement allowing New Zealand’s Bluff Tiwai Point aluminium smelter to operate for at least another four years, after a prior plan to close by August. The smelter’s chief cites a challenging year but emphasizes stable, safe operations under the extension.

title: GLOBAL COPPER WRAP: Southeast Asia premiums remain market high point, EQ levels shift
summary: The article describes a Fastmarkets methodology/assessment update and reports that Southeast Asia copper premiums remain at a high point, suggesting ongoing near-term tightness and bullish pressure for copper. It also references aluminium differential assessment delays/corrections and general aluminium supply conditions, implying limited immediate directional impact on aluminium prices.

title: Rio Tinto's NZ aluminium smelter
summary: Rio Tinto agreed with a power supplier to keep its Southland, New Zealand aluminium smelter operating for four more years. The deal follows talks on support for Rio’s Australian smelters and Alcoa’s forthcoming investor update on potential government-backed support and repowering for Portland, supporting aluminium supply outlook.

title: Southland leaders are wary of relying too heavily on the Bluff aluminium smelter - 14-Jan-2021
summary: Southland leaders discuss reliance on the Bluff aluminium smelter and note Rio Tinto’s decision to keep the Tiwai Point smelter operating until end-2024 rather than closing in August. Local officials highlight the smelter’s economic importance and consider adding power generation as additional stability.

title: Dr Copper's prognosis for the global economy is positive
summary: The article forecasts a positive global economic recovery and potential commodity “super cycle,” highlighting that demand for copper is highly sensitive to economic conditions. It notes copper’s strong year-on-year performance and claims decarbonisation (EVs, solar, wind) will drive additional copper demand amid supply constraints from declining grades and limited new mines.

title: Falling China aluminium scrap market drags down Asia ADC 12 prices
summary: The piece says a falling China aluminium scrap market is dragging down Asia ADC 12 prices. It points to softer scrap market conditions affecting aluminium alloy pricing in the region, implying near-term downside momentum for aluminium benchmarks tied to scrap availability and replacement demand.

title: NZ aluminium smelter operating through 2024 | News
summary: The news says Rio Tinto and Meridian Energy have agreed on the future of a South Island New Zealand aluminium smelter, allowing it to run through 2024 amid redevelopment plans. Continued operation implies steadier aluminium supply expectations, with no clear outage or ramp-up details to drive a strong short-term move.

title: Rio Tinto reaches agreement to extend the term of Tiwai Point aluminum smelter in New Zealand_SMM
summary: Rio Tinto agreed with Meridian Energy on electricity pricing to extend the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in New Zealand. Closure is now expected in December 2024 rather than August, supported by improved power economics. Discussions with the government continue on transmission costs and the smelter’s final site.

title: Primary aluminium inventories built up 20,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that primary aluminium ingot social inventories across eight Chinese consumption areas climbed 20,000 mt week-on-week to 684,000 mt as of Jan. 14, including SHFE warrants. The build-up suggests softer near-term tightness and may weigh on prompt aluminium prices.

title: Aluminium billet inventories fell 3,000 mt on week on larger shipments_SMM
summary: SMM reported that Chinese aluminium billet inventories fell by 3,000 mt week on week to 82,700 mt as of Jan 14, driven by decreases in Foshan, Huzhou and Changzhou, with the biggest drop in Huzhou (-2,000 mt). Wuxi and Nanchang rose, reflecting uneven regional flows.

title: Rio Tinto U-turns on Tiwai Point aluminium smelter closure by extending ops to 2024
summary: Rio Tinto has U-turned on the planned Tiwai Point aluminium smelter closure, extending operations to 2024. This delays potential loss of aluminium output, easing near-term supply tightness and supporting expectations for steadier or higher aluminium prices over the next several weeks.

title: Rio Tinto Deal Keeps New Zealand Aluminium Smelter...
summary: Rio Tinto said it reached an agreement with New Zealand electricity generator Meridian Energy to keep the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter operating until Dec. 31, 2024. The deal makes the smelter economically viable despite ongoing transmission-cost discussions, reducing closure risk and supporting aluminium supply expectations.

title: Salazar Resources Limited: Salazar Resources Gears Up for Busiest Ever Exploration Program, Drilling Four Copper and Gold Exploration Licences; Drilling Resumes at Los Osos
summary: Salazar Resources plans its busiest-ever exploration program in Ecuador, resuming drilling at Los Osos and preparing 3,000m drill programs at Rumiñahui and Los Santos targeting gold-copper mineralization. Geophysical work at Macara Mina is complete with drilling planned after permits. The release cites recent infill results showing copper equivalent quality.

title: Drill Targeting Advancing at the Kjøli High-Grade Copper Project, Norway; CARDS AI Technology to Assist with Target Prioritization
summary: Capella Minerals reported progress on drill target generation for its Kjøli high-grade copper VMS project in Norway, including ground magnetic and soil Ionic Leach surveys, new claim staking, and an AI-based CARDS analysis to prioritize drill sites. Permitting for initial drilling is expected to start in Q2 2021.

title: China Dec unwrought copper imports at 512,332 tonnes - customs
summary: China’s December unwrought copper imports fell to 512,332 tonnes, down from 561,311 tonnes in November and below a year earlier. Customs attributed the third consecutive monthly decline to weaker construction and manufacturing demand and the closure of an arbitrage window that had boosted shipments in 2020.

title: White Metal Resources Corp.: Drilling Underway at White Metal's Taranis Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Resources began a first reverse circulation drilling program at its 95%-owned Taranis copper-silver project in Namibia to update historical resources and prepare an NI 43-101 compliant estimate. Management cites positive copper price outlook, but the news is primarily exploratory with no immediate supply impact.

title: EU escalates WTO case against Indonesia over nickel ore export curbs
summary: The EU is escalating a WTO case against Indonesia over nickel ore export curbs by requesting a formal dispute panel. The complaint, launched in 2019, targets Indonesia’s restrictions on raw materials used to make stainless steel. A ruling or compliance pressure could change nickel ore export availability soon.

title: Rio Tinto to keep New Zealand aluminium smelter until 2024
summary: Rio Tinto has agreed a power deal with Meridian Energy that allows its New Zealand aluminium smelter in the South Island to keep running until December 2024. The agreement reduces the likelihood of an earlier curtailment and therefore supports ongoing aluminium supply expectations near term.

title: SDK to increase capacity of aluminum substrate for hard disks
summary: Showa Denko will expand capacity to produce aluminum substrates for hard disk (HD) media via its Yamagata subsidiary, boosting group output by 30%. The investment is subsidized to strengthen Japan’s supply chain. With demand growth for data-center HDDs, the plan should modestly support aluminium-related demand expectations.

title: Nickel batteries to keep wind farm operating at -35ºC
summary: A wind farm in western Kazakhstan will use Saft’s Uptimax nickel battery system to supply backup power during extreme winter temperatures down to -35°C. The batteries are used for monitoring and control equipment on remote turbines and are claimed to be reliable for over 20 years, supporting ongoing nickel battery demand.

title: Copper Fox Metals completes Van Dyke PEA - The Northern Miner
summary: Copper Fox Metals announced results from a preliminary economic assessment for its Van Dyke copper project in Miami, Arizona. The PEA outlines a potential 17-year mine life and total production of roughly 1.1 billion pounds of copper, which may modestly improve market sentiment toward future copper supply.

title: Minnesota lawmakers introduce anti-copper mining legislation
summary: Minnesota lawmakers introduced legislation to slow or ban copper-nickel mining in the northeastern Iron Range, including a proposed ban on copper mining on federal lands in the Rainy River watershed. Another bill would require proof of safe operations elsewhere. Local bipartisan opposition exists, but the policy is supply-restricting.

title: Copper rises towards 8-year highs as stimulus cheers markets
summary: Copper climbed toward eight-year highs as U.S. stimulus hopes lifted equities and boosted industrial-demand sentiment. A firmer dollar and worsening coronavirus cases in China posed risks. Nickel also rose sharply amid supply support from halted Philippines mining. Aluminium was slightly lower, indicating weaker net momentum.

title: U.S. judge denies Native American bid to block land swap for Rio Tinto copper mine
summary: A U.S. judge denied Native American efforts to block the Trump administration from publishing an environmental study that would enable a land swap for Rio Tinto’s proposed Resolution copper mine in Arizona. The ruling starts a 60-day countdown toward transferring land, improving near-term mine-development prospects despite no immediate final investment decision.

title: Aluminium inventories to increase January-February _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China’s domestic social aluminium inventories (including SHFE warrants) rose to 676,000 mt by Jan 11, up 80,000 mt, with notable builds in Wuxi and Nanhai. It expects continued inventory accumulation in January-February as cast aluminium ingot supply increases and downstream demand weakens seasonally.

title: 1.5% medium-grade nickel ore prices to remain stable in January _SMM
summary: SMM reports that 1.5% medium-grade nickel ore prices in late December fell to about $65.5/wmt CIF, but shipments from small Philippine mines were limited as bids lagged expectations. Due to rainy season and constrained resources, mines are reluctant to cut offers, so January prices are expected to stay around $65/wmt CIF.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 1,600 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories fell 1,600 mt week-on-week to 21,200 mt on Jan 15. SHFE nickel strengthened early week due to a domestic supply shortage, while recovering import losses later allowed more bonded goods into the market. Further inventory declines are expected.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 268,000 wmt to 8.87 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell by 268,000 wmt from Jan 8 to 8.87 million wmt as of Jan 15. In nickel content, stocks dropped 2,200 mt to 70,200 mt. Stocks at seven major ports also declined, suggesting tighter near-term supply.

title: C3 Metals Inc.: C3 Metals Core Resampling Programme Confirms Historic Copper-Gold Assays at Jasperoide Project, Peru
summary: C3 Metals reports completion of a core resampling programme at its Jasperoide copper-gold project in Peru, confirming historic copper intercepts across seven drill holes and planning further Phase 1 drilling of 3,500m. Results largely replicate prior grades, supporting confidence in the resource model.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 15): Nonferrous metals on the SHFE closed mostly higher, Nickel gained 1.19%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals mostly higher: aluminium rose 0.92% and nickel gained 1.19%, while copper edged down 0.09%. The commentary attributes moves to pandemic/rescue-plan and macro developments, plus market focus on near-term levels for copper and aluminium, with no specific supply disruption highlighted.

title: Apaches object to Forest Service review of huge copper mine
summary: The U.S. Forest Service is set to publish an environmental review that could trigger a 60-day process to transfer land enabling Rio Tinto’s Resolution Copper project near Oak Flat, Arizona. Apache Stronghold seeks to halt the publication, but a judge denied an injunction, keeping the review on track.

title: Huntsman Exploration Inc.: Huntsman to Commence Ground Electromagnetics Survey at Canegrass High-Grade Nickel Project, Western Australia
summary: Huntsman Exploration announced preparations and the start of an MLEM ground electromagnetics survey at its Canegrass nickel project in Western Australia, followed by an 18-hole RC/diamond drilling program to test EM anomalies. The project reports high-grade Ni-Cu mineralization historically, but the release is exploration-focused with no near-term supply change.

title: Silver Elephant Mining Corp.: Silver Elephant Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Minago Nickel Project in Thompson Nickel Belt Manitoba, Canada
summary: Silver Elephant signed a definitive agreement to acquire Victory Nickel’s Minago nickel sulphide project in Manitoba for US$11.675m, including consideration shares. The deal also has a nickel-price trigger, issuing additional shares if nickel exceeds US$10/lb for 30 consecutive business days. Timing is late 2020/early 2021.

title: Copper Output May Suffer If Pandemic Drags On, Chile Group Says
summary: The article’s headline says a Chilean group warns copper output may suffer if the pandemic persists. That would suggest reduced near-term supply availability from Chilean operations, tightening market expectations for copper and typically weighing on prices in the coming days to weeks.

title: Emirates Global Aluminium extends contract to process industrial waste
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium extended a 10-year partnership with Geocycle UAE/LafargeHolcim to pre-process and recycle spent pot lining from its Al Taweelah smelter. The renewed deal targets about 40,000 tonnes more material, improving toxic waste treatment for use in other industrial feedstocks. Immediate price effects are limited.

title: Is China nearing peak aluminum after record 2020 output? Andy Home
summary: World aluminium output rose 2.5% to a record 65.3 million tonnes, led by China lifting smelting run-rates. With seasonal demand weakening ahead of Lunar New Year, most analysts expect prices to fall as the market digests extra production. China’s potential output cap may matter later.

title: Analysis of primary aluminium replacing aluminium scrap amid nearing CNY _SMM
summary: SMM reports secondary aluminium producers are increasingly buying A00 primary aluminium to replace scrap as primary prices fall faster and the primary–scrap spread narrows. ADC12 makers may substitute when relative spreads support profits, while billet producers face tighter processing-fee economics. Some firms stockpile amid regional scrap shortages.

title: Weaker-than-expected substitution of copper cathode with copper scrap despite wide price spread_SMM
summary: SMM reports that although the cathode–scrap price spread hit a four-year high, substitution of copper cathode with copper scrap weakened. Drivers include reduced northern scrap consumption amid Henan environmental enforcement and COVID-19 disruptions, plus cathode inventory declines and supply disruptions, lifting spot premiums and supporting firm near-term copper prices.

title: Copper dips on demand worries as China's coronavirus cases rise
summary: Copper prices fell as demand worries grew from rising coronavirus cases in China, raising risk of wider lockdowns and reduced industrial activity, especially ahead of the Lunar New Year holiday. Copper dipped on the LME and Shanghai. The broader risk-off tone also pressured aluminum while nickel was mixed in quoted trade.

title: Copper edges higher on U.S. stimulus hopes, weaker dollar
summary: Copper prices edged higher on Monday as the dollar weakened and investors grew hopeful for additional U.S. COVID-19 stimulus. Three-month LME copper rose to $8,008/t and Shanghai March copper nudged up to 59,080 yuan/t. Gains were limited by worries over China’s rising COVID cases and pre-Lunar New Year demand slowdown.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Additional Positive Metallurgy Results at Crawford Nickel-Cobalt Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel reported additional positive locked-cycle metallurgical testing at its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project, citing 52% nickel recovery and the ability to produce a high-grade 37% nickel concentrate. The company plans further flowsheet optimization toward a feasibility study, improving near-term investor sentiment for nickel.

title: Sherritt forecasts higher output, costs at Cuba nickel mine
summary: Sherritt forecast higher output and higher costs at its Cuba nickel mine. The increased production can improve near-term nickel supply expectations, while rising costs may weigh on profitability and future output economics. The article’s mixed signals make the immediate net impact on nickel prices unclear.

title: European secondary aluminium ingot price retreats from five-year high on reduced Asian buying
summary: European secondary aluminium ingot prices fell back from a five-year high as Asian buyers reduced purchasing. The pullback in demand is directly linked to softer ingot market sentiment in Europe, suggesting near-term downward pressure on aluminium prices relative to recent peaks.

title: Santee Cooper approves 'experimental' power rate for Century Aluminum's SC smelting plant
summary: Santee Cooper approved an “experimental” temporary electricity rate to help Century Aluminum keep its Berkeley County smelter operating through end-2023, including using an aging coal boiler to meet demand. A new contract is still being negotiated after prior rate fights, while the utility claims other customers won’t be harmed.

title: Sumitomo reports further $289 mln impairment for Ambatovy nickel-cobalt asset
summary: Sumitomo reported an additional $289 million impairment related to the Ambatovy nickel-cobalt asset. While impairment is an accounting measure, it signals financial deterioration and potential operational risk for nickel supply, which can support higher near-term nickel price expectations versus otherwise.

title: Santee Cooper OKs 'experimental' rate for Century's SC aluminum plant
summary: Santee Cooper approved an “experimental” temporary electricity pricing structure for Century Aluminum to keep its SC smelting plant running, using power generation from nearby coal-fired units. The deal is meant to underpin a new three-year contract and may enable output restarts, supporting aluminium production prospects.

title: Canada Nickel achieves high-grade nickel concentrate
summary: Canada Nickel announced processing test results from its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project, reporting a 52% nickel recovery and details on how recovered nickel splits during processing. The update is aimed at demonstrating concentrate performance, which can support sentiment for nickel supply prospects.

title: City Power to replace copper cables as thefts get out of hand
summary: Johannesburg’s City Power is combating electricity-cable theft by replacing copper cables with aluminium bundle cables. Officials report many incidents and losses since January 2021, with police actions underway. The copper-to-aluminium substitution may increase short-term aluminium cable demand while reducing copper demand.

title: MMG:2020 's annual copper concentrate output of 310000 tons decreased by 18.6% compared with the same period last year._SMM
summary: MMG said its 2020 copper concentrate output fell 18.6% year-on-year to about 312,557 tons, mainly due to labour shortages and major logistics interruptions at the Las Bambas mine in Peru amid Covid-19 and local unrest. Copper cathode output rose slightly, and shipments resumed January 10.

title: Chile's copper output in 2020 was slightly higher than that of the previous year._SMM
summary: Chile produced slightly more copper in 2020 than in 2019 despite COVID disruptions, helping smelters maintain supply as copper prices rise. With infection rates increasing, mines including Escondida and Codelco are tightening restrictions and remote work to protect output. Fundamentals remain supportive, though second-wave risks linger if disruptions extend.

title: Imports of nickel ore and ferronickel declined significantly in December 2020_SMM
summary: China’s nickel ore imports fell in December 2020 (down 11.2% m/m) with shipments from the Philippines weaker due to adverse weather, and nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports declined by late January. Ferronickel imports in December were down m/m but up y/y, with November clearance delays normalizing.

title: SK Nexilis to build copper foil plant in Kota Kinabalu
summary: SK Nexilis will build its first overseas plant in Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, to produce 44,000 tons/year of copper foil for EV battery cells, aiming to triple output and expand total capacity to 100,000 tons/year. Operations are targeted for 2023, using renewable energy and cheap, stable power.

title: Copper eases on U.S. stimulus uncertainty
summary: Copper prices eased as investors grew uncertain about the outcome and timing of the $1.9 trillion U.S. stimulus package from President Biden, which is expected to support metals demand. Reuters reports three-month LME copper and March ShFE copper both fell about 0.6%, alongside a firmer dollar and vaccine rollout worries.

title: EGA upgrades third potline at its alumina refinery
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium completed refurbishment of its third potline at the Al Taweelah alumina refinery, replacing pot inner linings with steel collector bars containing copper inserts. The copper improves conductivity, enabling higher amperage and better pot performance. EGA also extended a contract to recycle spent pot lining, supporting sustainable operations.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Hits Record Length of Mixed Massive Sulphide Nickel Mineralization at the Tamarack Nickel Project with 21.73 Meters (71.2 Feet) of Nickel-Copper Mineralization
summary: Talon Metals announced a record 21.73-meter intercept of mixed massive sulphide mineralization at its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project in Minnesota, with assays pending. Management says the discovery could extend a high-grade massive sulphide unit. The update is exploratory and does not affect near-term supply or costs directly.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Hits Record Length of Mixed Massive Sulphide Nickel Mineralization at the Tamarack Nickel Project with 21.73 Meters (71.2 Feet) of Nickel-Copper Mineralization
summary: Talon Metals announced that drill hole 20TK0278 at its Tamarack nickel-copper project intersected 21.73 meters of mixed massive sulphide mineralization, setting a new record for the western limb of the Massive Sulphide Unit. Assays are pending, but the company expects the results to extend high-grade Ni-Cu mineralization.

title: FOCUS: Australia, Peru copper supply gap leaves Chinese smelters short of options
summary: Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin analysis highlights a copper supply gap involving Australia and Peru, leaving Chinese smelters with fewer sourcing options. This points to tighter near-term availability for smelting feed. The excerpt also comments that aluminium supply remains technically intact despite disruptions, suggesting weaker net influence for aluminium.

title: SK Nexilis to build RM2.3bil copper foil facility in Kota Kinabalu
summary: SK Nexilis will invest RM2.3bil to build its first overseas copper foil plant in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah. The facility will have 50,000 tonnes capacity, with construction starting in the first half and operations targeted for 2023. The announcement points to rising copper demand for EV supply chains.

title: World Copper Ltd.: World Copper Commences Trading on the TSX Venture Exchange and Provides Corporate Update
summary: World Copper begins trading on the TSX Venture and provides a corporate/project update for its Chilean porphyry copper assets. The company cites strengthening copper prices, tightening LME inventories, and supply disruptions. It also details updated Escalones resources and an upcoming drilling and metallurgical study program.

title: World's copper mines struggle to recover from COVID-19: Andy Home
summary: Reuters columnist says COVID-19 severely disrupted copper mine output in Peru and other producer countries, with recovery patchy. Treatment and refining charges and smelter purchase terms have hit decade lows, signaling inadequate concentrates for smelters. The market still shows no clear near-term relief, implying bearish pressure on copper prices.

title: Copper slips for a fourth day as rally loses momentum
summary: Copper prices edged lower for a fourth day as rally momentum faded on slow U.S. stimulus progress and concerns about China’s demand amid coronavirus disruptions and tighter liquidity. LME aluminum rose on firmer cash premiums suggesting tight nearby supply, while nickel declined slightly. Overall pressure is mixed across metals but copper softens near term.

title: SKC to spend $600 mn to build copper foil plant in Malaysia
summary: SKC plans to build its first overseas copper foil plant in Malaysia, investing about $600 million. The new facility is intended to more than quadruple its copper foil production capacity. Copper foil is a key component in EV batteries, implying higher near-term expectations for copper demand.

title: Lara Exploration Ltd.: Lara Exploration Ltd: Production Update for the Celesta Copper Mine in Brazil
summary: Lara Exploration reported that during the July–December 2020 ramp-up, its Celesta copper mine in Brazil shipped 1,195 tonnes of concentrate containing 457 tonnes of copper. Output is below target due to lower recoveries, but additional milling and flotation are scheduled for Q2 2021 to lift production and recoveries.

title: Talon Metals Hits Record Length of Mixed Massive Sulphide Nickel Mineralization at the Tamarack Nickel Project with 21.73 Meters of Nickel-Copper Mineralization
summary: Talon Metals announced record drilling results at its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project in Minnesota, reporting 21.73 meters of mixed massive sulphide mineralization in a new step-out hole. Assays are pending, but the company expects the intercept to extend its high-grade massive sulphide unit.

title: Atico Continues to Expand Footprint with High Grade Copper-Gold Intercepts Reporting 34.1g/t Au, 112 g/t Ag and 11% Cu over 3 meters at La Plata Project, Ecuador
summary: Atico Mining reports additional 2020 drilling results at its La Plata VMS project in Ecuador, highlighting copper-bearing intervals including 11% Cu over 3 meters and improved continuity toward the Guatuza extension. The company is restarting a 2021 two-rig program to test new targets and expand the mineral footprint.

title: Latin Metals Options Out Esperanza Copper Gold Project, San Juan Province, Argentina
summary: Latin Metals signed an agreement with Libero Copper and Gold giving Libero an option to acquire a 70% interest in the Esperanza copper-gold project in Argentina, subject to TSXV acceptance. Libero must pay cash and fund exploration over about two years. The project has prior drilling showing copper grades up to 0.57%.

title: Libero Options the Esperanza Porphyry Copper-Gold Project - Drilling Includes 232 Metres of 1% Cueq from Surface
summary: Libero Copper & Gold optioned the Esperanza porphyry copper-gold project in Argentina and reported drill-ready targets after historical intercepts of up to 387 metres of 0.78% copper equivalent (including 232 metres of ~1% CuEq). A 5,000-metre drill program is planned for Q2.

title: Talon Metals Hits Record Length of Mixed Massive Sulphide Nickel Mineralization at the Tamarack Nickel Project with 21.73 Meters of Nickel-Copper Mineralization
summary: Talon Metals said drill hole 20TK0278 at its Tamarack nickel-copper project intersected 21.73 meters of mixed massive sulphides, extending the western massive sulphide unit; assays remain pending. The update is exploratory and aimed at expanding resources, with no immediate supply or trade changes.

title: Biden commerce pick promises 'aggressive' stance against China when asked about aluminum, steel tariffs
summary: Gina Raimondo, Biden’s Commerce pick, promised an “aggressive” stance against China’s “anti-competitive” dumping, explicitly citing cheap steel and aluminum entering the U.S. She referenced using tariffs, countervailing duties, and entities-list style tools. The likely effect is reduced Chinese aluminum supply expectations and supportive near-term pricing.

title: Rio Tinto and BHP battle Apache tribes to build North America's biggest copper mine at sacred Oak Flat site
summary: Rio Tinto and BHP’s Resolution Copper project to build North America’s largest copper mine at Arizona’s Oak Flat faces a lawsuit from Apache groups seeking to halt the land transfer and alleging heritage and water pollution risks. Resolution Copper denies fast-tracking and says consultation continues, but legal uncertainty could delay supply plans.

title: Weakening dollar lifts copper as rally loses momentum
summary: Copper rose as the dollar weakened, but gains were capped by doubts around U.S. stimulus delivery and concerns over Chinese demand amid coronavirus and liquidity tightening. The LME cash-aluminium premium rose, signaling tight nearby supply, while nickel fell, highlighting mixed near-term price pressure across industrial metals.

title: Freeport sees rising copper demand boosting 2021 results
summary: Freeport reported a quarterly profit slightly above estimates, citing rising copper production and higher copper prices alongside improving demand as economies recover from COVID-19, especially in China. Management forecast continued growth in 2021 and said talks to expand and build smelters in Indonesia, supporting bullish near-term copper expectations.

title: Nickel Mines' Bumper Quarter Well Received
summary: Nickel Mines reported record Q4 output from its Indonesian RKEF projects, with realised nickel and nickel pig iron (NPI) prices beating broker forecasts and margins expanding. The company is also increasing its Angel Nickel stake and raising capital for expansion. It noted an NPI pricing change from LME nickel to Chinese NPI benchmarks.

title: NICKEL MINES LIMITED (ASX:NIC) - Share Price Analysis
summary: The piece is a share-price/financial overview for Nickel Industries/Mines, an Australian producer of nickel pig iron used in stainless steel. While it directly relates to nickel exposure, it lacks any specific news on nickel supply, demand, inventories, or pricing, making a clear short-term nickel price signal unlikely.

title: Material Matters: 2021 Demand, Nickel & Copper
summary: Citi expects focus on ex-China demand as developed-economy consumption rebounds, supporting copper demand. For nickel, Morgan Stanley highlights significant ongoing supply disruptions (e.g., Philippines issues and protests around New Caledonia operations) with rising stainless-steel and later battery-related demand. Copper faces potential labour-led and operational disruption risks, likely keeping a deficit.

title: Material Matters: 2021 Demand, Nickel & Copper
summary: Citi expects ex-China commodity demand to support metals consumption. For nickel, Morgan Stanley flags elevated supply disruption risks (Philippines issues; ongoing protests after Vale’s Goro mine sale), while stainless demand is expected to grow, supporting prices. For copper, labor disruptions and slower Chile/Peru ramp-ups imply a deficit and price support.

title: Hot Chili posts 382m Cortadera copper hit
summary: Hot Chili started a 40,000-metre drill program at its Costa Fuego copper-gold project in northern Chile and reported a 382-metre copper intercept at Cortadera, including 80m at 0.6% Cu. The firm plans to add a third rig soon, aiming to expand the high-grade core.

title: Hannan Metals Ltd.: Hannan Announces Copper-Gold Porphyry Discovery at Ucayali in Peru Samples up to 25.6% Copper
summary: Hannan Metals announced initial field sampling from its Ucayali, Peru project, identifying copper-gold porphyry target areas at Previsto and Belen. Float and stream sediment results show copper anomalies, including a best grab assay of 25.6% copper. The report is early exploration with no production impacts.

title: Nickel sulphate prices stood high amid tight spot supply, downstream restocking demand extended_SMM
summary: SMM says nickel sulphate prices remain high due to tight spot supply and strong downstream restocking ahead of CNY. China output rose in December, with most production battery-grade. Demand nearly doubled year on year, driven mainly by new-energy batteries and rising precursor orders.

title: Ball to build new $206m aluminum can plant in Czechia
summary: Ball plans a €170m ($206m) aluminum can plant in Pilsen, Czechia, with two production lines, intended to meet growing regional demand. The facility will begin operations in October 2022 and expand capacity via two construction phases, using automated equipment and 100% renewable energy for operations in Europe.

title: Pan Global Resources Inc.: Pan Global Resources Announces Accelerated 2021 Drill Program at Escacena Copper Project, Spain
summary: Pan Global Resources resumed drilling at its La Romana copper prospect in Spain, planning 20 core holes (~4,500m) to extend near-surface copper and deeper chalcopyrite targets based on geophysics. Results from prior holes are pending and the company cites sufficient funds to expand drilling, but no production impact is stated.

title: Ball plants to build new aluminium can plant near Pilsen, Czechia
summary: Ball Corporation plans to build a €170 million aluminium can plant near Pilsen, Czechia, with two production lines starting operations in October 2022. The facility expands regional output to meet growing demand for recyclable beverage packaging, implying incremental aluminium can supply and related aluminium input demand.

title: Pan Global Resources Announces Accelerated 2021 Drill Program at Escacena Copper Project, Spain
summary: Pan Global Resources announced Phase 4 of an accelerated ~4,500m drill program at its Escacena Project in Spain, targeting strike/dip extensions of copper mineralization at the La Romana prospect. Results from prior holes are pending and the firm expects expanded drilling based on the project’s open-ended mineralization and geophysics targeting.

title: Australia Copper Mining Report 2021-2024: Updated with Impact of COVID-19 Featuring Glencore, BHP, Oz Mineral Resources, & Newcrest Mining Ltd
summary: A new report covers Australia’s copper industry, including COVID-19-related mine closures that reduced output in 2020 and expected production through 2024. It highlights China’s role in exports (54%) and states China banned imports of category commodities including copper from Australia in November 2020, potentially weighing on demand.

title: Constellium and Novelis Establish Alumobility, an Initiative to Advance Automotive Aluminum
summary: Constellium and Novelis launched Alumobility, a non-profit ecosystem aimed at delivering implementation-ready technical solutions to expand use of aluminum automotive body sheet. It highlights completed studies for next-generation door and B-pillar designs and claims cost competitiveness, supporting expectations for aluminum uptake in vehicles, especially EVs.

title: Copper Mines Devastated During Covid
summary: COVID-19 lockdowns cut copper mine output in Peru and caused Chile production to slide after a strong first half of 2020. Copper concentrate tightness is reflected in decade-low benchmark treatment/refining charges and weaker smelter purchase floor terms. Imports from China also fell, indicating supply stress.

title: Freehill Mining readies to drill for copper and gold at El Dorado
summary: Freehill Mining plans to start drilling at its El Dorado copper target in Chile after receiving approvals, following high-grade surface copper (up to 2.5%) and strong IP survey results. The company is also advancing its Yerbas Buenas iron project; no near-term copper supply change is indicated.

title: EU envoy urges Biden to remove aluminum tariffs, settle aircraft subsidy dispute
summary: An EU envoy urged the Biden administration to immediately lift US Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminium imports from the EU. He said Brussels would also lift retaliatory tariffs if the US removes them, supporting sectors in both regions. The aircraft subsidy dispute was mentioned separately as a broader trade issue.

title: Primary aluminium inventories built up 13,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows China’s primary aluminium ingot inventories rose by 13,000 mt week-on-week to 682,000 mt as of Jan 28. Stock builds were concentrated in Wuxi and Gongyi amid holiday pre-stocking, while arrivals did not significantly increase in Xinjiang and Southwest China, suggesting near-term inventory pressure.

title: Chile increases estimate of 2021 average copper price to $3.3 per pound - Cochilco
summary: Chile’s copper commission (Cochilco) raised its 2021 average copper price estimate to $3.30 per pound from $2.90, citing earlier-than-expected COVID-19 vaccinations, strong projected Chinese growth, and perceived vulnerability in global copper supply. It also projects Chilean output around 6 million tons, up 3.6% year on year.

title: Grid Metals Corp.: Grid Metals Discovers Nickel Mineralization and Intersects Additional Pd-Rich Mineralization at East Bull Lake
summary: Grid Metals reports drilling results from its East Bull Lake property, including a four-metre interval of nickel-rich semi-massive sulfide and magnetite with accompanying copper assays. The company plans additional drilling to delineate Pd- and Cu-rich zones and test Ni-rich targets. No near-term supply or demand impacts are stated.

title: Excelsior Mining Corp.: Excelsior Mining Announces Sale of First Copper Cathode
summary: Excelsior Mining announced it sold the first copper cathode from the Gunnison Copper Project under an offtake agreement with Trafigura. The cathode purity is reported at ~99.998–99.999% and the company targets ramping to 25 million pounds per year later this year. Volume sold was 90,000 pounds.

title: Massive Deposit of Battery-Grade Nickel on Deep-Sea Floor Gets Confidence Boost With New Data
summary: DeepGreen Metals revised upward its polymetallic nodule resource estimate in the Clarion Clipperton Zone, increasing nodule quantity and boosting grades, including nickel by 6.1% (and higher manganese/cobalt). The company frames the deposit as battery-grade supply for EV demand growth, supporting bullish sentiment for nickel and some copper.

title: Silver Bull Announces Maiden NI 43-101 Resource of 2.33 Million Ounces of Gold & 476 Thousand Tonnes of Copper in the "Indicated" Category, and 1.56 Million Ounces of Gold & 220 Thousand Tonnes of Copper in the "Inferred" Category at the Beskauga Copper-Gold Project in Northeastern Kazakhstan Toronto Stock Exchange:SVB
summary: Silver Bull Resources reported a maiden NI 43-101 mineral resource for its Beskauga copper-gold project in Kazakhstan, estimating hundreds of thousands of tonnes of contained copper in open-pit constrained Indicated and Inferred categories. The resource uses a copper price assumption for pit optimization but no production timeline or output change.

title: Chile's Cochilco raises copper price forecast
summary: The article headline states that Chile’s Cochilco raised its copper price forecast. If the revision reflects a firmer near-term pricing outlook, it can support market sentiment and trading expectations for copper prices over the coming days or weeks.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jan 29): Shanghai nonferrous metals declined for the most part, aluminium advanced 1.32%_SMM
summary: SMM reports broad declines in Shanghai nonferrous prices, with copper (-0.78%) and nickel (-0.84%) falling on the day while aluminium rose (+1.32%). It cites weaker US growth signals, tight domestic liquidity, and positioning/“capital withdrawal before CNY” as sentiment drivers, with spot-to-futures monitoring for aluminium.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 2,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 2,000 mt to 16,600 mt as of Jan 29, the fourth consecutive weekly drop. Lower refined nickel inventories improved trading conditions, encouraging bonded nickel plates and some Russian/Australian arrivals to flow into China via customs clearance.

title: GLOBAL ALUMINIUM WRAP: Rotterdam duty-unpaid premium hits 3-month high; pre-holiday restocking boosts Taiwanese market
summary: Rotterdam duty-unpaid premium for global aluminium wrap has hit a 3-month high, reflecting tighter near-term availability and improved pricing. The report attributes strength to pre-holiday restocking activity that supports the Taiwanese market, suggesting continued upward pressure on aluminium premiums in coming days.

title: NORNICKEL ANNOUNCES PRODUCTION RESULTS FOR 4Q AND -2-
summary: Norilsk Nickel reported preliminary Q4 and FY2020 production results, including nickel output up q/q (via refinery ramp-up using new chlorine leaching) and copper output up q/q (driven by higher ore volumes and Bystrinsky ramp-up). The release reiterates 2021 guidance; no aluminium-specific information is provided.

title: NORNICKEL ANNOUNCES PRODUCTION RESULTS FOR 4Q AND FY2020
summary: Nornickel announced preliminary 4Q and FY2020 production results and 2021 outlook. Nickel output rose q/q on refinery ramp-up at Kola MMC with new chlorine-leaching technology. Copper output also increased q/q, driven by ramp-up at Bystrinsky (Chita) and higher grades/shipment. Guidance reiterated for 2021.

title: MMC Norilsk Nickel: Nornickel announces production results for 4Q and FY2020
summary: Norilsk Nickel announced its 4Q20 and full-year 2020 production results, noting it met 2020 guidance and reiterated 2021 outlook. Nickel output increased 13% q-o-q to 68 kt, while copper rose 8% q-o-q to 129 kt, driven by ramp-ups and operational factors at its Russian assets.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces 2020 Fourth Quarter Operating and Financial Results
summary: Copper Fox reports audited annual results and provides updates on its copper projects. It commissioned work for an updated PEA at Schaft Creek, highlights stronger PEA economics for Van Dyke, and notes ongoing progress toward permitting for the Eaglehead project. Delays affect other projects due to approvals and BLM authorization.

title: Copper Fox Announces 2020 Fourth Quarter Operating and Financial Results
summary: Copper Fox reported Q4 2020 financial results and project updates for its copper assets, including commissioning work on PEAs for Van Dyke and Schaft Creek and slower-than-expected progress on acquiring Eaglehead. It also noted delays in other projects due to approvals, and disclosed cash and warrant exercises to fund 2021 activities.

title: Chile's copper production fell to 506891 tons in December_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chile’s manufacturing output rose 0.4% YoY in December, but copper production declined. Chilean copper output fell 8.7% to 506,891 tons in December, per INE data. With Chile the world’s largest copper producer, the drop signals weaker near-term supply, which can pressure copper prices.

title: Copper giant Peru says mining allowed during new coronavirus lockdown
summary: Peru will impose a two-week COVID-19 lockdown but will allow mining to continue, including operations at major copper-producing regions such as Ancash, Apurimac, Pasco and Ica. This should support Peru’s copper output and lower the likelihood of short-term supply disruption.

title: Fight for Oak Flat: Mining company one step closer to building copper mine on sacred land
summary: A British-Australian consortium (Rio Tinto/BHP) is one step closer to building the Resolution Copper underground mine at Oak Flat, after a January 15 Final Environmental Impact Statement. Tribal and environmental groups challenge the land exchange, including an upcoming injunction hearing, potentially delaying copper output that is otherwise years away.

title: Shipments of copper from Chile to tighten after CNY due to coastal winds and waves_SMM
summary: Coastal winds and waves in northern Chile delayed copper exports in January, with multiple ports unable to load cathode on schedule. Chile’s exports to China fell in late 2020, tightening supply. The shipping backlog and potential lower arrivals in February–March increased trader pressure and supported higher post-CNY premiums.

title: Copper dips weighed by China factory activity slowing in January
summary: Copper prices edged lower as China’s January factory activity grew at the slowest pace in months, raising near-term demand concerns. LME three-month copper fell to $7,849/t and March ShFE copper declined to 57,870 yuan/t. Copper premiums into China rose, partly offsetting.

title: S&P Global Platts Launches World's First Daily China Clean Copper Concentrate Assessments
summary: S&P Global Platts launched daily Clean Copper Concentrate (CCC) spot price assessments on a CIF China basis, including treatment and refining charges (TC/RC) and differentials for major South American brands delivered to China. Platts says this adds transparency to copper concentrate pricing as China imports and demand remain strong.

title: Operating rates at aluminium processing enterprises continued to decline due to tighter logistics and CNY_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates for major aluminium processors fell 3.6pp to 71.8% as firms cut output ahead of Chinese New Year amid tighter logistics and weaker orders. Secondary aluminium rates dropped to 57.4% due to disrupted transport and reduced scrap supply. Operating rates are expected to fall further in February.

title: Aluminum can shortage: Northeast Ohio breweries bottling
summary: Northeast Ohio breweries report an aluminum can shortage as demand for canned beers and hard seltzers has risen faster than can manufacturers can produce. Breweries face reallocated allotments and forced format changes (16-ounce cans, bottles). Experts note limited capacity and a long lead time for new can facilities.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Kamoa-Kakula Copper mines 300,000 tonnes of ore in January grading 5.45% copper, including 82,000 tonnes grading 8.80% copper from the high-grade centre of the Kakula Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said the Kamoa-Kakula copper project mined 300,000 tonnes of ore in January at a 5.45% copper grade, up from December, and boosted contained copper in pre-production stockpiles. Underground development hit a record, with phase-1 concentrator construction progressing on schedule for July copper concentrate.

title: Indonesia's Antam targets 50,000-100,000 T nickel sulphate output a year by 2024
summary: Indonesia’s Antam aims to produce 50,000–100,000 tonnes/year of nickel sulphate from its planned HPAL plant in 2024, alongside 120,000–240,000 tonnes/year of battery precursors and cathodes. The metals and chemicals target domestic and export EV demand, supported by state-led ventures.

title: Forum Energy Metals Corp.: Rio Tinto Mobilizes Drills to Forum's Janice Lake Copper/Silver Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals says Rio Tinto Exploration Canada has begun mobilizing drills and supplies to the company’s 100% owned Janice Lake copper/silver project in Saskatchewan. Drilling is set to start mid-February on the Rafuse and Jansem copper targets, following a successful winter haul road and camp setup.

title: Business Scoop » Deal Struck To Speed Up Removal Of Aluminium Dross From Mataura Paper Mill
summary: New Zealand authorities reached an agreement to accelerate removal of aluminium dross (ouvea premix) stored at Mataura, citing hazardous ammonia risk if it gets wet. The government and New Zealand Aluminium Smelters will share additional costs (up to $500,000 each), sending material to Tiwai Point for processing and storage within months.

title: Biden to keep tariffs on aluminum imports from UAE, reversing Trump
summary: The White House said President Biden will keep U.S. tariffs on aluminum imports from the United Arab Emirates, reversing Trump’s decision to exempt UAE shipments from a 10% tariff. The exemption was set to start on Wednesday, but Biden cited national security interests for maintaining the levy.

title: Deal Struck To Speed Up Removal Of Aluminium Dross From Mataura Paper Mill
summary: New Zealand’s government agreed to speed removal of ouvea premix (aluminium dross by-product) from the Mataura site due to hazardous ammonia risk. Costs for accelerated removal are shared by the Ministry for the Environment and NZ Aluminium Smelters (up to $500,000 each). Material will be sent to Tiwai Point and processing capacity adjusted.

title: Commerce Tags Vietnamese Copper Pipes With 8% Duty
summary: The report says Commerce has tagged Vietnamese copper pipes with an 8% duty. Such a tariff can increase import costs, potentially reducing near-term purchases of copper pipe and associated copper demand. That shift may weigh on copper price expectations over the following days to weeks.

title: Scrap metal company must pay for buying stolen nickel worth millions, Manitoba judge rules
summary: A Manitoba judge ordered Urbanmine to pay Vale for buying and reselling nickel stolen from Vale’s site in Thompson, Man. The case involves about 483,396 pounds of nickel and prior resale to other metals traders. The ruling is restitution/liability focused, with no clear immediate nickel supply-market disruption.

title: Cost of ferronickel increased markedly amid rising procurement prices of raw and auxiliary materials _SMM
summary: SMM says high-grade NPI prices rose to 1,120 yuan/mtu, while the ferronickel market was quiet. Costs jumped as nickel ore in the Philippines stayed expensive and thermal coal/coke prices increased, lifting ferronickel costs ~50 yuan/mtu. Many ferronickel plants are losing money and some may halt output due to low ore inventories.

title: President of Myanmar was detained with a one-year state of emergency declared in Myanmar, the impacts on nickel and tin ore production in focus_SMM
summary: Myanmar’s military detained senior officials and declared a one-year state of emergency, with communication disruptions. SMM notes CNICO’s Dagonshan nickel project is currently in normal production, but political uncertainty and potential logistics disruption create near-term nickel supply risk. Tin ore flows are reported as stable with no impact so far.

title: In reversal of Trump move, Biden to keep levies on UAE aluminium
summary: The White House says President Biden will keep a 10% tariff on aluminium imports from the UAE, reversing Trump’s plan to exempt UAE shipments via a quota. Officials argue tariffs better protect domestic producers tied to national security. UAE aluminium is a major US import category by value.

title: BMW Group becomes first customer for EGA's CelestiAL aluminium, made with solar power
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) says BMW Group will buy 43,000 tonnes per year of CelestiAL aluminium produced using solar electricity from Dubai’s Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park. EGA claims the contract cuts BMW’s annual CO2 by 222,000 tonnes and covers nearly half of BMW’s Landshut casting needs.

title: BMW buys aluminum made with solar power to cut CO2
summary: BMW says it has signed a triple-digit million-euro deal with Emirates Global Aluminium to buy 43,000 metric tons of solar-powered, lower-emission aluminium in 2021. The volume is intended to cover nearly half of BMW’s annual needs for its Landshut light-metal foundry for vehicle parts.

title: Myanmar coup: Impact on nickel and tin ore production_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Myanmar’s military detained senior officials and declared a one-year state of emergency, accompanied by widespread communications interruptions. SMM notes CNICO’s Dagonshan nickel mining and ferronickel smelting project is currently producing normally, but instability could still affect near-term nickel supply expectations. Tin ore logistics appear stable for now.

title: SunLive - Deal struck to speed up removal of aluminium dross
summary: New Zealand’s government agreed to speed up removal of hazardous aluminium dross (ouvee premix) stored at the Mataura site due to ammonia risk if it gets wet. Costs are shared with New Zealand Aluminium Smelters. Material will be sent to Tiwai Point for container storage, with added staffing and truck capacity during remediation.

title: PROJECTS: Germany's BMW to source solar aluminium from the UAE
summary: BMW will source 43,000 tonnes of solar-produced aluminium from EGA, supplying nearly half of the aluminium foundry’s annual needs at its Plant Landshut. The move supports BMW’s CO2 reduction targets and highlights growing use of aluminium in electric vehicle components. Impact on broader aluminium prices appears limited.

title: BMW buys first aluminium made using solar energy from UAE's EGA
summary: BMW signed a triple-digit-million-euro contract with UAE’s Emirates Global Aluminium to buy 43,000 tonnes of solar-powered aluminium from EGA’s Dubai solar plant. The deal targets emission cuts and uses the aluminium in BMW components. It signals demand for low-carbon aluminium, though it may not materially shift short-term prices.

title: Nickel Rock Resources Completes Expansion of the Hard Nickel Project West of the Decar Nickel Project of FPX Nickel Corp.
summary: Nickel Rock Resources announced it completed expansion of the Hard Nickel Project by acquiring additional mineral claims and reporting highly elevated nickel-bearing samples on nearby ground with similar geology to the FPX Decar deposit. The company plans further 2021 exploration, aiming to advance potential battery-grade nickel-iron alloy awaruite.

title: BMW to use world's first solar-made aluminium from UAE's EGA
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) signed BMW to supply 43,000 tonnes per year of “CelestiAL” aluminium produced using solar power from Dubai’s Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park. BMW says the shift cuts emissions and covers nearly half of BMW’s Landshut light-metal casting needs in Europe.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Updating the Preliminary Economic Assessment on the Kenbridge Nickel Deposit, Kenora Mining District, Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. announced an update to the preliminary economic assessment and mineral resource estimate for its Kenbridge nickel deposit in Ontario, with work to be completed in Q2 2021 and a future bankable feasibility study planned. The release is focused on project evaluation rather than immediate output or trade flows.

title: Harnessing the power of the desert sun: BMW Group sources aluminium produced using solar energy
summary: BMW Group will begin immediately sourcing solar-generated aluminium from Emirates Global Aluminium, supplying 43,000 tonnes in 2021 to its Landshut foundry and aiming for more green-power sourcing long term. The release links aluminium smelting demand to energy-intensive production and e-mobility growth.

title: Glencore to supply 1,500 tonnes of aluminium to South Korea's PPS
