summary: Glencore plans to supply 1,500 tonnes of aluminium to South Korea’s PPS. In the short term, this provides incremental physical availability for buyers in South Korea and can tighten local supply expectations, offering mild upward pressure to aluminium prices.

title: Biden to Keep Tariffs on Aluminum Imports From UAE, Reversing Trump's Policy
summary: Biden issued a Feb. 1 proclamation keeping a 10% tariff on aluminum imports from the UAE, reversing Trump’s decision to end the levies. The stated rationale is national security. The tariff change is likely to affect near-term aluminium supply-demand expectations by altering import costs and trade flows.

title: Biden keeps aluminum tariffs on U.A.E., reversing Trump policy
summary: The Biden administration reversed Trump’s last-minute decision to exempt the UAE from a 10% U.S. aluminum import tariff scheduled to be lifted on Feb. 3. Tariffs on UAE aluminum, imposed in 2018, remain in place, maintaining higher costs for UAE shipments into the U.S. market.

title: Western Copper and Gold Announces Exploration Results from the Casino Project, Yukon
summary: Western Copper and Gold reported assay results from drilling at its Casino copper-gold project in Yukon, highlighting expanded mineralization and higher-grade copper-bearing zones (with intervals up to 0.30% CuEq and additional copper grades tied to the deposit core). The company plans to complete an updated PEA in Q2 2021.

title: Chile copper production falls 9.4% in December - Cochilco
summary: Chile’s copper production declined 9.4% in December, according to Cochilco. The drop from a key global producer raises expectations for reduced near-term supply, which typically supports copper prices as markets price in tighter availability over the following days and weeks.

title: Biden Reinstates Aluminum Tariffs in One of His First Trade Moves
summary: President Biden reinstated tariffs on aluminum exported from the UAE, reversing Trump’s last-day removal of the measure. The tariffs are meant to protect U.S. producers that have struggled against low-priced imports and shut down smelters. Industries expect higher costs, while unions support the move.

title: BMW buys aluminum made with solar power to cut CO2 - Energy Industry Today
summary: BMW says it signed a “triple-digit million-euro” deal with Emirates Global Aluminium to buy 43,000 metric tons of lower-emission aluminium in 2021. The metal is produced using energy from Dubai’s Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park. The supply would cover nearly half of BMW’s Landshut foundry needs.

title: BMW sources aluminum produced using solar energy to cut CO2 impact
summary: BMW will source 43,000 tonnes of aluminium produced using solar energy from Emirates Global Aluminum starting this year, supplying nearly half of the light metal foundry needs at Plant Landshut. BMW cites a 20% supplier-network CO2 reduction. The move targets low-carbon aluminium rather than overall market supply disruption.

title: GLOBAL COPPER WRAP: Japan, Chile supply hitches drive up Shanghai premiums; US, Europe stable
summary: The report’s “GLOBAL COPPER WRAP” says supply disruptions involving Japan and Chile increased Shanghai copper premiums, reflecting tighter local availability. It notes that US and Europe were stable, implying the price pressure is concentrated in Asia rather than broad global moves.

title: New Caledonia's government collapses over independence, nickel unrest
summary: New Caledonia’s coalition government collapsed as pro-independence politicians resigned amid riots over the sale process of Vale’s local nickel business. Protesters allege a locally led offer was overlooked. As the world’s fourth-largest nickel producer, the unrest and asset-sale uncertainty raise near-term nickel supply concerns.

title: Biden Reinstates Aluminum Tariffs, Reversing Trump's Decision
summary: President Biden reinstated tariffs on aluminum exports from the United Arab Emirates, reversing Trump’s recent removal. The administration aims to protect U.S. aluminum producers that have struggled against low-priced imports and smelter closures, which should reduce import competitiveness and provide short-term support to aluminum prices.

title: New Caledonia government falls apart over nickel deal and independence push
summary: New Caledonia’s multi-party government collapsed amid debate over the future of nickel mining and smelting, including the planned sale of Vale Nouvelle-Calédonie. The independence movement opposes the deal, and protests delayed the process, increasing near-term uncertainty over nickel industry plans and potentially supply continuity.

title: Biden annuls Trump's tariff waiver on UAE aluminium imports
summary: The White House said the US will maintain a 10% tariff on aluminium imports from the UAE, reversing Trump’s final-day waiver. Biden argued continued tariffs better protect domestic producers and national security than an “untested” quota. UAE shipments are a meaningful share of US imports, and the policy change takes effect immediately.

title: Shipment difficulties from South America pressured on copper concentrate TCs_SMM
summary: January shipment difficulties in Chile and Peru delayed copper concentrate exports from major mines (Las Bambas, Escondida, Chuquicamata). The supply disruption is cited as creating a concentrate supply gap, boosting restocking demand at Chinese smelters and driving a TC downward trend. Q1 imports are expected below 2 million mt.

title: Resurgence of COVID-19 and early closures of downstream producers and logistics firms affected copper scrap consumption_SMM
summary: COVID-19 resurgence in Hebei and other north-east provinces led factories to suspend production and logistics disruptions, limiting scrap copper rod deliveries and pulling forward the off-peak season, sharply reducing copper scrap consumption. Shipping closures also likely reduce south China scrap imports in early February, with a rebound after CNY.

title: Shanghai copper falls to 8-week low, China holiday dampens demand outlook
summary: Shanghai copper prices fell to an eight-week low as investors grew concerned about lower China demand ahead of the Lunar New Year holiday and amid recent COVID-related disruptions. Both Shanghai and LME copper declined, with analysts citing lockdown effects, softer PMI, and weaker credit conditions weighing sentiment.

title: Shanghai copper hits 8-week low on demand woes ahead of China holiday
summary: Shanghai copper slid to an eight-week low and London copper also fell as traders priced weaker near-term demand ahead of China’s Lunar New Year. A coronavirus outbreak dampened January economic activity, dragging output and services. Nickel declined as well, suggesting broader risk-off in industrial metals.

title: Glencore 2020 Copper Production Excl. Mutanda In Line With Prior Year
summary: Glencore said 2020 own-sourced copper production was 1.26 million tonnes, 8% lower than 2019, and nickel output fell to 110,200 tonnes, 9% lower. The company noted Mutanda is on care and maintenance and said 2021 guidance remains current, implying no immediate supply rebound.

title: 2021 CNY holiday plans at Chinese copper processors_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM surveyed 37 Chinese copper processors on 2021 CNY holiday plans. Many copper rod and wire/cable makers reduce output from mid/late January to early February, while cathode rod plants close about five days earlier and some avoid restocking raw materials, focusing on using existing inventories. Other segments keep production partly through robust orders.

title: Global $10 Billion Copper Foil (Value, Volume) Markets to 2025 - Industry is Facing Supply/Demand Imbalance with Low Production Capacity of Copper Foil
summary: A Research and Markets report says the copper foil market is seeing a supply-demand imbalance due to low production capacity, driven mainly by lithium-ion battery demand and electronics/EV growth. It also attributes 2020 weakness to COVID-19 and reduced Chinese activity, denting copper demand.

title: EBRD and TSKB to co-finance Turkish copper wire producer Mega Metal
summary: EBRD and TSKB will co-finance a €4 million loan to Turkey’s copper wire rod producer Mega Metal to cover working capital needs amid the coronavirus pandemic. The financing is intended to ease SME access to funding and support ongoing manufacture of oxygen-free electrolytic copper wire used by cable manufacturers.

title: Freeport, Tsingshan finalising $2.8 bln copper smelter deal
summary: Freeport and Tsingshan are reportedly finalising a $2.8 billion copper smelter deal. The news suggests new/expanded smelting capacity for refined copper, which can raise expectations for future supply and weigh on short-term copper prices, though the immediate price effect depends on commissioning and ramp-up timing.

title: BMW Group, Tetra Pak and Schüco International Express Concerns About Sourcing Aluminium from Gh
summary: BMW Group, Tetra Pak and Schüco said they will reject aluminium supplied from bauxite mined in Ghana’s Atewa Forest due to unacceptable environmental destruction and biodiversity risk. The release warns Ghana’s bauxite and aluminium could face outright rejection by aluminium users, potentially reducing near-term supply availability.

title: Freeport, Tsingshan finalising $2.8 billion copper smelter deal - Indonesia minister
summary: Indonesia’s coordinating minister says Freeport and Tsingshan are finalising a $2.8 billion copper smelter deal in Weda Bay, with production of copper pipes and wires and potential copper-derived battery components. Freeport’s unit says it remains committed but is still discussing cooperation with Tsingshan.

title: Camino Minerals Corporation: Camino Identifies Additional Mineralized Copper and Silver Veins at Plata Dorada with Channel Samples Grading up to 5.76% Cu and 1,500 g/t Ag; Increases Mineral Claims at Plata Dorada to 3,800 Ha
summary: Camino announced additional exploration results from its Plata Dorada copper-silver project in Peru, identifying up to 5.76% Cu and 1,500 g/t Ag across multiple veins over 4 km, and increasing claims to 3,800 ha. This could slightly improve copper sentiment, but no production or trade impacts are indicated.

title: Apaches' Fight Over Arizona Copper Mine Goes Before US Court
summary: A federal judge will hear arguments on a lawsuit by Apache Stronghold seeking to stop the U.S. Forest Service from moving ahead with Resolution Copper’s land swap at Oak Flat, Arizona. The plaintiffs seek an injunction over land rights and potential infringements on religious practices; the agency says mining is not imminent.

title: Electrocuted 'copper thief' was a 14-year-old boy
summary: A 14-year-old was electrocuted at the Pointe a Pierre refinery after police believed he entered to steal copper and contacted high-tension lines. Petrotrin and regulators investigated and issued a safety reminder against unauthorized interference with company electrical and mechanical assets. The report does not indicate broader copper supply impacts.

title: Century Aluminum Commends President Biden's Action to Maintain Section 232 Tariffs on the United Arab Emirates Nasdaq:CENX
summary: Century Aluminum praised President Biden for maintaining Section 232 aluminum tariffs on UAE imports. Biden reversed a Trump-era proclamation that would have exempted the UAE from relief, keeping tariffs in place. Century argues this will protect the U.S. aluminum industry, keep the “playing field level,” and support U.S. aluminum jobs.

title: Aluminium Composite Cladding (ACC) – banned by Victorian government in certain circumstances - Real Estate and Construction
summary: Victoria (Australia) banned the use of certain aluminium composite cladding with less than 93% inert content in future multi-storey residential and commercial buildings, with effect for building permit applications after 1 Feb 2021. This restricts a specific aluminium product demand stream, potentially weighing on aluminium-related consumption expectations.

title: Explainer: How the New Caledonia government collapse may affect the nickel market
summary: Riots and a New Caledonia government collapse, tied to disputes over Vale’s nickel asset sale, raise the risk of disruptions at a major (~9% of global) nickel supplier. With China already tight on stocks, analysts say further supply fears and supported demand could keep LME nickel prices well-supported in coming weeks.

title: Copper prices rise on stimulus hopes; firm dollar limits gain
summary: Copper rose as markets priced more potential U.S. COVID-19 stimulus and improving U.S. economic indicators. A firm U.S. dollar capped gains. The piece also notes LME aluminium, nickel (and zinc) moving higher, reflecting broader bullish industrial-metals sentiment tied to recovery hopes.

title: Primary aluminium inventories expanded 32,000 mt on week to 714,000 mt_SMM
summary: SMM reports that China’s social inventories of primary aluminium across eight consumption areas rose by 32,000 mt week-on-week to 714,000 mt as of Feb 4, the highest since Oct 15, 2020. Increases were mainly driven by stocks in Gongyi and Hangzhou.

title: Apache make emotional appeal to court to halt proposed copper mine | Cronkite News
summary: Apache Stronghold members urged a federal judge to halt the proposed Resolution Copper Mine at Oak Flat, arguing the land transfer was rushed and would infringe religious rights. They seek a preliminary injunction. The government opposed, saying the claims lack merit and public interest favors proceeding.

title: Bauxite test work stacks up for Lindian in Guinea
summary: Lindian Resources says further digestion test work on high-grade bauxite ores from its Bouba conglomerate deposit in Guinea confirmed the material suits both low- and high-temperature Bayer process digestion settings. The result follows earlier positive dry screening outcomes and improves confidence in refining performance, supporting aluminium-linked sentiment.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Announces Updated PEA on the Tamarack Nickel Project: After-Tax NPV Increases 96% to US$569 Million
summary: Talon Metals released an updated preliminary economic assessment for its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project, showing higher after-tax NPVs under three nickel offtake scenarios. The report highlights modeled nickel economics at specified nickel and copper prices and cites low costs, but it is a feasibility-stage update, not production.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Provides Update on Schaft Creek Project
summary: Copper Fox provided an update on the Schaft Creek project PEA, including progress on resource estimation, QP review, and a mine/processing plan assuming 133,000 tpd truck-shovel operations with flotation producing copper and molybdenum concentrates. The update is technical and preparatory, not indicating imminent production changes.

title: Margaret Lake Diamonds Inc.: Margaret Lake Announces Acquisition of Old Nick and Letain Nickel
summary: Margaret Lake Diamonds announced it will acquire the Old Nick and Letain nickel-cobalt projects in British Columbia, with scheduled milestone payments and regulatory approvals. The release is exploratory and does not indicate immediate production or supply disruption, so any effect on near-term nickel prices is likely limited.

title: Apache make emotional appeal to court to halt proposed copper mine
summary: Apache Stronghold urged a federal judge to halt progress on the proposed Resolution Copper mine at Oak Flat in Arizona, arguing due-process and religious-rights violations. The project follows a finalized environmental impact statement and land swap. Opponents seek an injunction to stop/slow copper production.

title: Blackstone Hits Massive Sulfide Nickel at King Snake
summary: Blackstone reports drilling success at the King Snake prospect, intersecting massive sulfide nickel mineralisation across multiple holes. The company is continuing resource work at several Ta Khoa project sites in Vietnam and notes that the Ban Phuc concentrator restart follows success at Ban Chang, supporting positive nickel supply outlook sentiment.

title: Nornickel to offer program to monitor water bodies near recent fuel spill
summary: Nornickel said it will run a 2021–2023 program to monitor water bodies and soils near a May 2020 fuel spill and to revegetate contaminated areas. It also plans to restore biological resources and dispose of contaminated sorbents and soils, with the plan filed with Rosprirodnadzor. No production impact is cited.

title: Nornickel plans to cut greenhouse gas emissions to levels below 10 million tonnes by 2030
summary: Nornickel said it plans to cut annual greenhouse gas emissions to below 10 million tonnes by 2030, using a technical upgrade program as part of its ecology strategy. The company is a major refined nickel producer and also produces copper. The announcement is sustainability-focused with no near-term operational change described.

title: Freeport to join hands with China's Castle Peak to build a copper smelter in Indonesia_SMM
summary: Freeport-McMoRan is reportedly close to a $2.8 billion deal with China’s Aoyama/Castle Peak to build a copper smelter in Veda Bay, Indonesia. The facility would make copper tubes, wires and battery-related components. Indonesia expects EV supply-chain support, complementing its existing nickel and battery efforts.

title: Rising copper price forces higher Kaz Minerals bid
summary: The headline reports that rising copper prices are leading bidders to raise their offer for Kaz Minerals. This reflects improved near-term value assumptions for the company’s copper exposure, which can reinforce bullish sentiment in copper markets over the coming days.

title: Operating rates at aluminium processing enterprises continued to decline due to tighter logistics and CNY _SMM
summary: Operating rates at major aluminium processing enterprises fell 3.6 points to 71.8% last week, driven by reduced activity ahead of Chinese New Year and tighter logistics. Construction extrusion, wire and cable, and secondary aluminium firms cut orders and production, while some foil/plate/strip producers stayed steadier.

title: Easpring signs 8-year contract to buy nickel, cobalt raw materials from Lygend subsidiary
summary: Easpring (per the headline) signed an 8-year contract with a Lygend subsidiary to purchase nickel and cobalt raw materials. While the excerpt lacks volume details, the long-term procurement suggests firmer demand outlook for nickel feedstock, which may support nickel prices in the coming days to weeks.

title: 2021 CNY holiday plans at Chinese secondary aluminium alloy and die-casting producers _SMM
summary: SMM surveys Chinese New Year holiday plans for secondary aluminium alloy and die-casting producers. Large secondary aluminium plants mainly shut Feb 9–11 and resume after Feb 16; some operate normally. Hebei plants halt earlier due to restricted raw-material transport from COVID resurgence. Die-casting plants largely pause after Feb 4 and restart after Feb 17.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 17,000 wmt to 8.08 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 17,000 wmt to 8.08 million wmt between Jan 29 and Feb 5. In nickel content terms, stocks dropped 100 mt to 63,700 mt. While inventories at seven major ports rose, the all-port total declined.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 05/02: Nickel up to $17,900/t; zinc set for weekly gain of 3%
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures report notes nickel rising to $17,900/t, implying bullish near-term price pressure for nickel. Most other text discusses publication timing changes and corrections to Fastmarkets’ aluminium-related assessment methodologies/differentials, without clear evidence of immediate aluminium price moves. Zinc is mentioned only in passing.

title: Russian environmental watchdog's $2 billion claim to Nornickel satisfied – court | Russian Legal Information Agency (RAPSI).
summary: A Russian court in Krasnoyarsk ordered JSC Norilsk-Taymyr Energy Company, a Nornickel subsidiary, to pay 146 billion rubles (~$2 billion) for environmental damages. Rosprirodnadzor cited urgent inspections, 139 violations, and equipment age/lack of monitoring, following earlier oil/product spills near Nadezhinsky facilities.

title: BMW will use aluminum produced by solar energy_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: BMW says it has started purchasing aluminum produced using solar power, supplied by UAE-based Emirates Global Aluminium. About 43,000 tons will be delivered this year to BMW’s Lanzhut foundry, representing nearly half of that facility’s demand. The program targets lower CO2 emissions, with no direct supply disruption stated.

title: Nornickel subsidiary faces record fine for environmental damage in Russian history
summary: Russia’s regulator upheld a multi-billion-ruble environmental penalty against Nornickel’s Norilsk-Taimyr Energy Company for a large fuel spill at Norilsk CHPP-3. More than 20,000 tonnes of oil products were released. The court awarded about 146.2 bln rubles, with Nornickel likely to appeal and disputed damage estimates.

title: Copper buoyed by vaccine and U.S. stimulus hopes
summary: Copper rose 1.4% on LME amid hopes that vaccine rollout and U.S. stimulus will lift industrial demand. The move was tempered by a stronger U.S. dollar. Copper inventories in LME warehouses are at multi-year lows. The article also notes gains in aluminium and nickel, reflecting broadly bullish sentiment.

title: Tesla Proposes Nickel Battery Project With Indonesia As Electric Vehicle Firm Expands Sales Globally
summary: Tesla proposed working with Indonesia to build EV battery supply chains, including potential cooperation on energy storage, and emphasized technology transfer beyond raw-materials extraction. Indonesia is highlighted as having the world’s largest nickel reserves. Such battery-supply expectations could increase near-term nickel demand sentiment.

title: Copper buoyed by sagging dollar and U.S. stimulus hopes
summary: Copper prices rose 1.9% on Friday, supported by a weaker U.S. dollar and hopes for stimulus-driven demand, alongside tight LME inventories. Warehousing stocks hit the lowest since 2008 and canceled warrants were elevated. LME aluminum and nickel also gained as broader metals sentiment turned bullish.

title: Norilsk Nickel fined nearly US$2 billion for massive fuel spill in the Arctic
summary: A Russian court ordered Norilsk Nickel to pay a record 146 billion rubles (about US$1.94 billion) for a massive Arctic fuel spill last May. The ruling adds significant financial and regulatory risk to the world’s largest nickel producer, potentially pressuring nickel sentiment, though no specific output reduction is cited.

title: Norilsk Nickel pays fine appointed by environmental watchdog after accident in Norilsk
summary: Norilsk Nickel’s unit was fined after an oil products spill at the Norilsk TPP-3. The watchdog confirmed the company paid a 1 mln ruble administrative fine, while a court partially satisfied a much larger 148 bln ruble damages claim against NTEK. Norilsk Nickel disputes the damage estimates.

title: Tesla Proposes Nickel Battery Project With Indonesia As Electric Vehicle Firm Expands Sales Globally - Energy Industry Today
summary: Tesla has proposed partnering with Indonesia to build EV battery supply chains, including potential collaboration on energy storage systems. Indonesia’s official notes Tesla’s battery technology transfer beyond raw materials and highlights Indonesia’s large nickel reserves. The engagement suggests incremental nickel demand expectations, though no volume details are given.

title: BMW Group Sources Aluminium Produced Using Solar Energy
summary: BMW will begin sourcing aluminium produced using solar electricity from Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA), supplying 43,000 tonnes that covers nearly half of BMW’s Landshut light-metal foundry requirements. The move targets lower CO2 emissions from energy-intensive aluminium smelting, including downstream use in vehicle components.

title: China aluminium sector must shut inefficient coal power to meet climate goals
summary: The piece reports that China’s aluminium sector must close inefficient coal power units to meet climate targets. Such closures can constrain aluminium production or raise electricity costs, tightening near-term supply expectations and likely weighing on aluminium prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: China aluminum sector must shut inefficient coal power to meet climate goals -report
summary: Ember says China’s aluminum sector must retire around 47 GW of inefficient captive coal power over the next decade to meet climate targets. With most smelting using self-generated coal electricity, policy push toward cleaner power and emissions trading could raise costs and limit output, weighing on near-term aluminum sentiment.

title: China aluminium sector must shut inefficient coal power to meet climate goals - report
summary: Ember says China’s aluminium output emitted more CO2 than some countries and that aluminium-linked inefficient captive coal power must be shut or replaced, amounting to about 47 GW over the coming decade. Smelters are urged to switch to cleaner electricity and improve efficiency and recycling, potentially constraining supply.

title: Rusal maintains aluminum output in 2020 at 3.755 million tonnes
summary: Rusal said 2020 aluminum production was 3.755 million tonnes, nearly unchanged from 2019, while sales fell 6%. The average sold aluminum price dropped 6% to $1,805/t. Rusal also cited a 1.7% decline in global aluminum demand to 63.9 million tonnes.

title: Copper rises as U.S. stimulus optimism raises demand, recovery hopes
summary: Copper prices rose around 1% after optimism over a potential $1.9 trillion U.S. COVID-19 stimulus package boosted expectations for metals demand and economic recovery. Tight nearby supply was suggested by a higher LME cash premium. Aluminium and nickel also increased modestly alongside copper moves.

title: Exclusive: China copper cathode output shrank 7.39% on the month to 798,300 mt in January_SMM
summary: SMM’s survey shows China produced 798,300 mt of copper cathode in January, down 7.39% from December, as smelter operating rates fell after completing annual targets and concentrate shipments from South America were delayed. February output is expected to rise modestly as maintenance ends, but early supply remains tighter.

title: Canada Nickel held talks with U.S. government on supplying metal for EV batteries
summary: Canada Nickel reportedly held talks with the U.S. government regarding supplying metal for EV batteries. Such discussions can affect near-term expectations for nickel supply and procurement demand linked to battery markets. With limited detail in the provided text, the likely market impact is modestly supportive for nickel.

title: Mongolia seeking pact with Rio Tinto to end copper mine expansion
summary: Mongolia’s government is seeking Rio Tinto’s agreement to mutually terminate the deal enabling the Oyu Tolgoi underground expansion project. A new Prime Minister has pushed against the expansion and the government wants a replacement of the underground development plan, raising near-term copper supply risk and bearish sentiment.

title: Canada Nickel CEO says company held talks with U.S. on supplying metal for electric-car batteries
summary: Canada Nickel’s CEO said the company has held talks with U.S. government officials about supplying nickel for electric-vehicle batteries amid concern over China’s dominance. U.S. agencies have sought input on the miner’s ability to supply critical minerals and offered introductions to financing. Nickel demand is expected to rise as EV adoption grows.

title: Chile copper export revenue up in January- central bank
summary: Chile’s central bank reported copper export revenue rose 9.3% in January as shipments increased and global copper prices climbed. The rise contributed to a trade surplus. The article also notes thinning inventories supporting continued price gains, implying stronger near-term demand signals for copper.

title: FactMR: High Purity Aluminium Demand to Sustain amid Rising Semiconductor and Aerospace Applications: Fact.MR Study
summary: Fact.MR’s report highlights recovery in high-purity aluminium demand and continued growth supported by semiconductor and aerospace use cases, including AI/IoT-driven chip penetration and demand for aircraft alloys. It notes supply normalization from China and Taiwan as restrictions ease, implying supportive near-term aluminium fundamentals.

title: En+ reports fall in aluminium sales on broadly unchanged output  | 8 February 2021
summary: En+ reported a decline in aluminium sales despite broadly unchanged output. That combination points to weaker buying/offtake in the near term rather than production cuts. With inventories not clearly addressed, the news could translate into softer aluminium demand expectations and downward price pressure over coming sessions.

title: Cameroon: Yearly aluminium exports drop by about 50% in 2017-2020 due to Alucam's financial problems
summary: Cameroon’s Alucam cut aluminium exports from about 62,000 tons (2018) to 52,000 (2019) and 49,000 (2020) amid financial problems after Rio Tinto’s divestment and a January 2018 energy disruption. Lower shipments and potential further power-payment issues could reduce supply, weighing on aluminium prices.

title: Peru's copper output falls in December; zinc production up again
summary: Peru’s copper production is reported to have fallen in December, indicating lower output from a major South American producer. The article also notes zinc production rose, but the tracked impact here is on copper, where weaker supply expectations can shift near-term market pricing.

title: Peru copper production in 2020 hammered by coronavirus pandemic - govt
summary: Peru’s Energy and Mines Ministry says copper production fell 12.5% to 2.15 million tonnes in 2020 as coronavirus restrictions reduced output in the world’s No.2 copper producer. Such production losses can support supply-tightness expectations for copper, though the data is historical.

title: Norden Crown Resumes Diamond Drilling at the Burfjord Copper-Gold Project, Norway
summary: Norden Crown Metals resumes diamond drilling at its Burfjord copper-gold project in Norway with Boliden funding. The program targets IOCG-style copper mineralization and continuity of new/legacy targets, based on geophysical anomalies and prior high-grade copper intercepts. The release is exploration-focused and lacks near-term supply impacts.

title: Turquoise Hill Resources : Mongolia seeks more tax revenue from Rio copper mine expansion - source
summary: Mongolia is seeking revised tax arrangements for the expansion of Rio Tinto’s Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold mine to increase government revenue rather than take a bigger stake. The government argues benefits were eroded by higher costs, and is negotiating amid a long-running development standoff that could influence copper supply outlook.

title: Mongolia seeks more tax revenue from Rio copper mine expansion - source
summary: Mongolia is seeking a revised agreement with Rio Tinto over expanding the Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold mine, aiming for higher tax revenue rather than a larger government stake. The government is dissatisfied with rising costs and low early dividends and corporate income tax payments.

title: Tanzanian nickel deposit project is world's largest
summary: UK-based Kabanga Nickel signed a landmark agreement with Tanzania to develop the world’s largest nickel deposit, forming Tembo Nickel Corporation to mine and process/refine Class 1 nickel with copper and cobalt by-products. The deal boosts investor confidence, but near-term production impacts appear limited, so nickel price effects likely small.

title: BMW buys solar aluminium as supply chains go green
summary: BMW signed a UAE deal to buy “green” solar-powered aluminium produced in Dubai, worth in the three-digit million euros, covering about half the aluminium needs of its Landshut foundry. The contract highlights accelerating low-carbon sourcing requirements likely tightening availability and supporting aluminium demand sentiment in the near term.

title: UPDATE 2-Mongolia seeking pact with Rio Tinto to replace copper mine expansion plan -FT
summary: Mongolia is reportedly seeking a deal with Rio Tinto to replace a copper mine expansion plan. The change could alter expected growth in copper supply, shifting short-term market expectations for availability. Traders may react by repricing supply risk, typically weighing on copper prices if expansion timing or scale is reduced.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Drills Thick Intercept of 110.65 Meters (363 Feet) of Semi-massive and Disseminated Sulphide Mineralization at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals said drill hole 20TK0277 intersected 110.65 meters of semi-massive and disseminated sulphide mineralization at the Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project in Minnesota, extending the semi-massive sulphide unit. Assays for this hole remain pending, though prior holes show Ni and Cu grades.

title: Renforth Resources Inc.: Renforth's Surimeau District Scale Nickel/VMS Prospect Assays 0.483% Ni over 1m with a 13m Interval of 0.156% Ni Starting at Surface
summary: Renforth Resources reported drill results from its Surimeau district Nickel/VMS prospect, including 0.483% Ni over 1m and 0.156% Ni over 13m, plus intervals with elevated Cu (and Zn). The release is an exploration assay update, not a confirmed production change, so near-term market effects are limited.

title: Nickel prices: How did we get here and what comes next?
summary: Nickel prices have gained substantially over the past year and are rising toward the US$9/lb or US$20,000/tonne level that analysts say could stimulate investment in new supply. Despite the climb, the piece notes nickel has faced ongoing issues, implying some uncertainty about continued gains.

title: District Copper Corp: District Acquires Copper Project in Central British Columbia
summary: District Copper announced it has executed an agreement to acquire a 100% interest in the Copper Keg porphyry copper exploration project in British Columbia. The company plans systematic exploration based on Highland Valley porphyry models, with historical indications of a buried leach cap. No near-term production or supply change is reported.

title: Scrap gap drives China's copper and aluminum import boom: Andy Home
summary: China imported record refined copper and unwrought aluminium as a “scrap gap” tightened secondary supply after restrictions on scrap/waste imports. Quarantine and mining disruptions mattered, but scrap was central. With new customs rules allowing higher-grade scrap, flows may rebound, supporting copper and aluminium prices amid competitive global scrap markets.

title: Scrap gap drives China's copper and aluminum import boom: Andy Home
summary: China’s scrap import curbs created a “scrap gap” that reduced copper scrap inflows to a new low in 2020 and tightened available secondary material, leading to heavier refined copper imports and a shift to primary and unwrought aluminium alloy imports. New rules may help, but supply-chain shifts keep pressure on prices.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28's Ramu Confirmed as One of Lowest Carbon Emitters Amongst Nickel Producers
summary: Nickel 28 says independent analysis confirms its Ramu nickel-cobalt operation is among the lowest GHG emitters in nickel production, with scope 1 and 2 intensity averaging 15.6 tCO2e/tonne of nickel in MHP. It also explores further reductions by eliminating on-site electricity generation with renewables.

title: White Metal Provides Update on Drilling Program on the Taranis Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal reports progress on its reverse-circulation drilling program at the Taranis copper-silver project in Namibia, aiming to update an NI 43-101 compliant resource estimate. Management cites the recent rise in copper prices as a reason to continue exploration, but no immediate copper supply or physical flows are changed.

title: A rival for Sudbury? Company hopes to turn Timmins into the new nickel capital
summary: Canada Nickel CEO Mark Selby says the Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project near Timmins could be the largest since the 1970s, citing a large resource estimate and ongoing feasibility and processing-site studies. He frames EV and stainless demand as strong, implying future nickel supply growth.

title: Scrap gap drives China's copper and aluminium import boom
summary: China imported record volumes of refined copper and unwrought aluminium last year, driven by a scrap gap and a quicker, stronger recovery in manufacturing after COVID-19 lockdowns. The import surge suggests higher near-term demand and potential tightness, which is generally supportive for copper and aluminium prices.

title: Scrap gap drives China's copper and aluminium import boom
summary: China imported record volumes of refined copper and unwrought aluminium, driven by a “scrap gap” and a rapid manufacturing rebound after COVID-19 lockdowns. The jump in imports suggests stronger short-term feedstock and consumption demand, which is supportive for copper and aluminium price expectations in coming weeks.

title: Could Timmins become Northern Ontario's new nickel capital?
summary: Canada Nickel’s Crawford sulphide project near Timmins is presented as a potential global-scale nickel discovery, with large resources, planned feasibility this year, permitting thereafter, and initial production expected in 2023 and ramp-up to commercial by 2025. The project’s low-carbon positioning and EV-driven nickel demand support a bullish nickel outlook.

title: Los Andes Copper: Developing One of the Largest Advanced Copper Deposits in Chile
summary: Los Andes Copper highlights its Vizcachitas copper-molybdenum project in Chile, describing sizable measured resources and plans to publish a PFS in late 2021. The company frames the project as positioned for rising copper prices, but the update does not indicate immediate production or policy changes affecting near-term copper supply-demand balance.

title: London copper near 8-year high on stimulus hopes, tight supply
summary: London copper rose to an eight-year high on Wednesday, driven by tight supplies, more buyers than sellers and low inventories, plus a reported copper concentrate shortfall. Optimism over further U.S. coronavirus stimulus improved sentiment for base metals demand. The article also notes increases in aluminum and nickel prices.

title: Primary aluminium inventories built up 61,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows China’s primary aluminium ingot social inventories across eight consumption areas rose by 61,000 mt from last Thursday to 775,000 mt as of Feb 10. Increases were mainly driven by stocks in Wuxi, Nanhai, Hangzhou, and Gongyi, indicating a larger supply cushion.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 37,400 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data for China shows aluminium billet shipments fell 13,300 mt to 14,000 mt for the week ahead of the CNY holiday. Aluminium billet inventories across key consumption regions rose 37,400 mt to 165,500 mt by Feb 10, with increases in major warehouses including Foshan and Wuxi.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 34,000 wmt to 8.04 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 34,000 wmt to 8.04 million wmt between Feb 5 and Feb 10. Stocks in nickel content declined 300 mt to 63,400 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also dropped 24,000 wmt to 6.44 million wmt.

title: Column: Scrap gap drives China's copper and aluminium import boom
summary: A Reuters column says China’s scrap import restrictions created a “scrap gap,” sharply cutting copper scrap and aluminium scrap inflows and forcing higher refined copper and unwrought aluminium imports. With new customs rules expected to boost scrap flows, the author expects renewed supply support and price resilience for both metals.

title: Column: Scrap gap drives China's copper and aluminium import boom
summary: Reuters columnist says China’s ban and restricted import rules on scrap (treated as “waste”) sharply reduced copper and aluminium scrap inflows, leaving a large gap that had to be filled with refined metal and driving record imports. Recent customs rule changes could help scrap volumes rebound, though competition for material may limit recovery.

title: Lindian eyes bauxite infrastructure plan with Guinea Govt
summary: Lindian Resources signed an MoU with the Guinean government to appraise joint development of the Dobali port and related logistics corridor to support its Lelouma, Gaoual and Woula bauxite projects. Better infrastructure planning could improve future bauxite handling and bolster aluminium supply expectations, albeit with limited near-term certainty.

title: Nickel Rock Resources Files Notice of Work Application for the Hard Nickel Project Next to the Decar Nickel Project of FPX Nickel Corp.
summary: Nickel Rock Resources announced it filed a notice of work application for the multi-year Hard Nickel Project, including trenching and diamond drilling. The claims are adjacent to FPX Nickel’s Decar project and target nickel-iron alloy mineralization. The release discusses EV demand and carbon-reducing processing prospects, but no output is provided.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Plans Expansive 2021 Copper Exploration Program on Its 100%-Owned Western Foreland Licences Adjacent to Kamoa-Kakula Copper Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines announced an expansive 2021 exploration program on its Western Foreland copper licences adjacent to the Kamoa-Kakula project in the DRC. It cited assay results extending the Kamoa North high-grade copper trend at Kiala Discovery and significant mineralization at Makoko Sud, alongside planned drilling, geophysics, and sampling.

title: Victory Nickel Inc.: Victory Nickel Sells Minago Property, Closes Private Placement, Positions Company to Move Forward in Nickel and Industrial Minerals Markets
summary: Victory Nickel announced it sold its Minago nickel property and restructured its secured debt with Silver Elephant, including a debt reduction and equity-based consideration. The company also plans to return to active nickel exploration. The news is company-specific and does not signal immediate global supply or demand changes.

title: Silver Elephant Mining Corp.: Silver Elephant Completes Acquisition of Minago Nickel Sulphide Project in Thompson Nickel Belt Manitoba, Canada
summary: Silver Elephant Mining completed its acquisition of the Minago nickel sulphide project in Manitoba from Victory Nickel. The project hosts the Nose nickel deposit and other drilled discoveries. Deal terms include consideration shares and a nickel-linked issuance trigger if nickel exceeds US$10. No immediate production changes are stated.

title: Strong performance by Hindalco led by aluminium and Novelis
summary: Hindalco reported inline Q3 results with a sharp rise in India profit and improving margins. Aluminium downstream sales rose to 80kt, above pre-COVID levels, aided by lower input costs and efficiencies. Copper cathode output fell due to maintenance, while Novelis posted record EBITDA. Overall, aluminium demand signals are stronger.

title: Platinum, copper rally to multiyear highs as bets on economic recovery lift industrial metals
summary: Industrial metals rose as markets bet on global economic recovery, boosting demand expectations. Copper reportedly hit its highest level since 2013/ eight-year high, while platinum also surged. The piece links the rally to supply-demand balance, citing LME/Comex copper stocks near decade lows.

title: Taseko Mines Completes Notes Offering and Moves Forward with Florence Copper Commercial Production Facility
summary: Taseko completed a $400m notes offering and will fund capital for its Florence Copper commercial production facility. The company says most funding is now in hand and it is moving ahead with design engineering and procurement for a project targeting 40,000 tonnes of cathode copper annually for the U.S. market.

title: Manufacturing group asks Biden to end steel, aluminum tariffs
summary: A manufacturing group is urging President Biden to end U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs. If tariffs are removed, import costs and trade barriers for aluminum would fall, increasing expected supply and weakening tariff support for prices. Markets would likely react negatively to the prospect of lower aluminium tariff-driven pricing.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Plans Expansive 2021 Copper Exploration Program on Its 100%-Owned Western Foreland Licences Adjacent to Kamoa-Kakula Copper Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines announced assay results extending the Kamoa North high-grade copper trend at its Western Foreland licences and plans a large 2021 exploration program (40,000m drilling, geophysics and sampling) near the Kamoa-Kakula project in the DRC. Results indicate strong copper mineralization continuity along strike.

title: Gold futures up a 4th session; platinum, copper rally to multiyear highs
summary: Gold rose for a fourth session as the U.S. dollar weakened and markets priced another U.S. stimulus package. The same optimism for economic recovery lifted industrial metals, with copper reaching an eight-year high and platinum hitting a multi-year peak, supported by expectations for stronger global demand.

title: Objection period ends in March for Tonto's proposed decision on copper mine
summary: An objection period ending March 1 is set for Tonto’s proposed Resolution Copper mine decision and related land exchange. The FEIS and draft Record of Decision were released in January 2021, and objections can be filed with the USDA. The piece is procedural, with no stated approval or denial outcome.

title: House Committee Advances Copper Theft Bill Honoring Fallen Tulsa Officer
summary: Oklahoma’s House Judiciary Committee advanced the Sgt. Craig Johnson Metal Theft Act to curb scrap metal theft. The bill requires ID/vehicle details and digital images for copper scrap sales, with records retained for two years. The proposal targets illegal copper wire sales that drive theft-related economic losses.

title: Material Matters: Iron Ore, Copper, Zinc & EVs
summary: ANZ Bank and Morgan Stanley expect copper tightness to persist: low inventories, declining bonded stocks, weak concentrate supply, and short-term Peru/Chile shipment disruptions could keep the market in deficit despite seasonal demand weakness. Separately, Macquarie’s EV sales recovery boosts expectations for higher nickel demand for batteries, supporting prices.

title: Queensland Coordinator-General approves alumina plant in central Queensland boasting world-first processing
summary: Queensland’s Coordinator-General approved Alpha HPA’s $300 million high-purity alumina plant in Gladstone. The project will use solvent extraction technology and leverage the port for export. Construction is expected to start this year, with production targeted from 2023 and higher run rates later, supporting future alumina supply sentiment.

title: Copper hovers near 8-year high on weaker dollar
summary: London copper hovered near an eight-year high, with prices supported by a weaker U.S. dollar tied to growth-relief hopes and softer inflation. Trading was thin due to China’s Lunar New Year. Aluminium fell, nickel slipped slightly, and nickel cathode and shipment fundamentals were also cited.

title: Aluminium Bahrain Posts $25.9 Million Profit in 2020
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) reported higher 2020 profit, with the statement attributing improved margins in Q4 to higher LME prices and top-line partly offset by lower metal sales volumes. The article highlights LME price movement versus 2019, which can sway near-term aluminium market expectations.

title: Copper hovers near eight-year high as Chinese holiday starts
summary: Copper is hovering near an eight-year high after several days of gains as China enters its Lunar New Year holiday, reducing trading activity. Falling LME and Shanghai inventories, a cash premium versus the three-month contract, and slowed Chile cathode shipments point to tight nearby supply and support bullish sentiment.

title: LME off-warrant lead stocks drop 70% in December; aluminium dips to 1.6mln tonnes
summary: The article notes a sharp decline in LME off-warrant lead stocks and states that aluminium inventories dipped to about 1.6 million tonnes. Inventory declines can affect near-term sentiment on physical aluminium availability, typically weighing on prices if perceived as reducing prompt demand support.

title: Gold Fields Acquires Shares of Chakana Copper Corp.
summary: Gold Fields Nazca Holdings purchased 5.81 million shares of Chakana Copper Corp., raising its ownership from about 16.8% to nearly 20% following an offering. The transaction is for investment purposes with potential future adjustments, but no immediate production, supply, or policy change is stated.

title: Foreign demand seen to boost nickel industry
summary: The Philippine Nickel Industry Association expects a strong 2021 for the local nickel sector, citing improving foreign demand despite COVID-19 disruptions in 2020. Export values rose even as output fell, attributed to steady world nickel prices led by China’s demand and growth across infrastructure, appliances and EVs.

title: Canaccord Genuity raises Q1 copper price forecast
summary: Canaccord Genuity mining analyst Dalton Baretto raised his Q1 copper price forecast to US$3.75/lb from US$3.50/lb, compared with an average quarter-to-date price of about US$3.61/lb. The update signals moderately higher expected copper prices for the coming quarter.

title: Investigation: Can China clean up after the aluminium king?
summary: The article describes China’s push to regulate captive coal power that supplies primary aluminium smelters, using Hongqiao/Weiqiao as an example. It cites prior environmental violations, ongoing compliance changes, and partial coal-plant retirements alongside government and carbon-policy pressure. It highlights potential effects on aluminium production costs and supply.

title: Mining company hopes to turn Timmins into the new nickel capital
summary: Canada Nickel says its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project near Timmins is the largest nickel sulphide discovery since the early 1970s and is being aggressively advanced. The company plans studies, explores use of Glencore’s Kidd concentrator for processing, and frames future demand from EVs, supporting bullish nickel sentiment.

title: China's copper industry sees steady performance in 2020
summary: China’s MIIT said copper product output in 2020 rose 0.9% year on year to 20.46 million tonnes. Copper import/export value totaled $88.9 billion (+9.1%), with imports up and exports down. The ministry pledged to curb disorderly smelting capacity expansion and boost copper use in infrastructure and buildings.

title: A rival for Sudbury? Mining company hopes to turn Timmins into the new nickel capital
summary: Canada Nickel’s CEO says the Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide discovery near Timmins is being aggressively advanced, potentially feeding a large open-pit mine and processing plans using existing Timmins infrastructure. The company frames nickel demand from EVs and stainless steel as growing, supporting upbeat nickel market sentiment.

title: ALUMINIUM FOUNDRY WRAP: Premiums climb in US, Eastern Europe
summary: Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin reports an aluminium foundry wrap with US and Eastern Europe premiums moving higher. It also notes delayed publication and corrections to certain European low-carbon aluminium differential and Aluminium 6063 extrusion billet premium assessments due to procedural errors, updating its pricing database.

title: Bam Bam Resources Corp.: Larry Segerstrom Joins Bam Bam Advisory Board and Completes Review of Majuba Hill, Nevada Porphyry Copper Project
summary: Bam Bam Resources reports an advisory board appointment and reviews drilling data from its Majuba Hill Nevada porphyry copper project. The 2020 program expanded oxide copper and extended hypogene/supergene sulfide mineralization, with assay results pending. No production or supply changes are announced.

title: ALUMINIUM BILLET WRAP: Premiums in US, Germany, Spain up to nearly 2-year highs
summary: Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin updates report that premiums for aluminium billet wrap in the US, Germany, and Spain have risen to nearly 2-year highs. The piece also notes procedural corrections and database updates to certain aluminium differential/premium assessments, but the headline points to firming physical pricing.

title: Possible link between sick koalas and Portland Aluminium emissions under microscope
summary: Scientists are examining koalas euthanised around the Portland Aluminium smelter to determine whether nearby fluoride emissions caused deformities. The plant operator Alcoa says the assessment will finish within months, and past wildlife studies prompted management actions. The report suggests environmental scrutiny of aluminium smelting emissions.

title: Bauxite leaves farmers in the red – report
summary: A Jamaica Environment Trust report says bauxite mining and alumina operations have delivered limited economic benefits while harming farmers, air quality, and water resources. It criticizes outdated air-quality standards, monitoring non-compliance, and inadequate soil rehabilitation, implying higher regulatory and remediation pressure on the local bauxite/alumina industry.

title: Rio Strikes Power Deal to Keep Iceland Aluminum Plant Running
summary: Rio Tinto said it reached a new power agreement to keep operating its ISAL aluminium smelter in Iceland. The deal addresses prior concerns about power costs that could have forced a shutdown unless terms changed. Rio also cited improved efficiencies, and noted a similar power deal in New Zealand earlier this year.

title: Copper hits highest since 2012 on inflation concerns and healthy demand
summary: Copper surged to its highest level since 2012 as investors bought on inflation/reflation concerns and improving Chinese demand, alongside evidence of tightening supply. LME three-month prices rose, cash premiums increased, and inventories fell 44% in two months. Nickel also climbed to multi-year highs; aluminium edged down slightly.

title: Botswana names Canadian firm as preferred bidder for copper mine
summary: Botswana has named a Canadian firm as the preferred bidder for a copper mine, signaling progress in developing new copper supply. Because this is an early procurement stage, it may not translate into immediate production, limiting any short-term effect on copper prices.

title: ASX to rise, European shares rally on copper, oil
summary: Australian shares are expected to open higher as European miners gain. The piece highlights copper trading at its highest level in eight years alongside rising oil prices, signaling strong bullish sentiment toward copper and supporting near-term price momentum.

title: Hopes for more US stimulus sees global markets rally as oil and copper make tracks
summary: Markets rallied on hopes for US coronavirus relief and vaccine rollouts. The piece notes stronger copper price performance alongside BHP’s record copper extraction from Escondida and overall higher commodity prices, supporting bullish expectations for copper within days. It also mentions iron ore and oil strength, but aluminium drivers are not specified.

title: Copper rises to near 9-year high on likely demand growth, tight supply
summary: Copper prices advanced to their highest level in nearly nine years, rising up to 0.5% in early trading and more than 9% from the February low. The rally was tied to optimism over global economic recovery supporting demand while supply is expected to remain tight, with a weaker U.S. dollar also boosting buying.

title: Doubleview Gold Corp.: Drill Hole H035 Extends Lisle Deposit: Intersected 1.00 g/t Gold EQ (0.73% Copper EQ) over 97.9m
summary: Doubleview Gold reported drill-hole H035 results from the Hat Project, including a 97.9m intercept averaging 0.73% copper equivalent. The company also notes possible cobalt and palladium in places, but provides no resource estimate or production outlook, making it more informative for copper-gold potential than immediate copper supply.

title: Azarga Metals Corp.: Updated PEA to be Prepared for Unkur Copper-Silver Deposit and Private Placement
summary: Azarga Metals announced an updated preliminary economic assessment to be prepared for its Unkur copper-silver project in eastern Russia, incorporating a new inferred resource and updated metallurgical test work over the next 4–6 weeks. The company also arranged a small private placement to fund the PEA and working capital.

title: Forum Energy Metals Corp.: Rio Tinto Commences Drilling at Forum's Janice Lake Copper/Silver Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Rio Tinto Exploration Canada has started drilling two rigs at Forum Energy Metals’ Janice Lake copper/silver project in Saskatchewan, testing an IP chargeability anomaly at the Rafuse target. The company highlights historical surface and near-surface copper intercepts and outlines further winter-accessible targets.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Drills 213 m of 0.65% Copper and 0.37 g/t Gold (1.00% CuEq) and 171 m of 0.62% Copper and 0.43 g/t Gold (1.03% CuEq)
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. reported new drilling at its 100%-owned MPD copper-gold porphyry project, including multiple long intervals around ~0.6% copper, and plans to expand drilling with up to 30,000 metres in 2021. The update improves geological expectations but does not signal immediate production or supply changes.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanplats Arranging Project-level Financing of up to US$420 Million to Advance Development of the World-scale Platreef Palladium, Platinum, Rhodium, Nickel, Copper and Gold Project in South Africa
summary: Ivanplats (Ivanhoe Mines) signed a non-binding US$300m gold/palladium/platinum streaming term sheet and arranged up to US$120m senior project debt to fund development of the Platreef project in South Africa. Shaft 1 changeover and detailed engineering progress toward eventual production of nickel and copper.

title: The impact of energy costs on industrial performance: identifying price and quantity effects in the aluminum industry using a data envelopment analysis approach
summary: The paper uses efficiency frontier methods to study how energy costs influence primary aluminum smelter performance and competitiveness. It finds energy-related effects on cost efficiency vary by region and technology, and notes other factors like market share and exchange rates. It does not report specific immediate market disruptions or new policy changes.

title: Russia's Nornickel 2020 profit sinks 39% as sets aside cash for fuel-spill fine
summary: Norilsk Nickel said 2020 net profit fell 39% after setting aside $2 billion for an environmental damage claim tied to a major Arctic fuel spill. The court fine over diesel leakage remains before being effective. Nornickel expects 2021 capex of $3.0–$3.4 billion, with final dividend later.

title: Norilsk Nickel fined record £1.4 billion for role in May 2020 oil spill | Crime
summary: A Russian court upheld a record 146 billion ruble (£1.4bn) fine on Norilsk Nickel tied to a May 2020 oil spill near its Nadezhdinski Metallurgical Plant. Authorities blamed operational failures and tank depressurisation. The company plans to review the decision and may appeal before paying within a month.

title: Premium Nickel Resources Corporation: Premium Nickel Resources Selected as Preferred Bidder in BCL Liquidation Process
summary: Premium Nickel Resources was selected as preferred bidder to acquire Botswana BCL’s former Selebi-Phikwe, Tati Phoenix, and Selkirk Ni-Cu-Co assets after a technical and government review. The deal moves to documentation and six-month exclusivity for due diligence, implying potential future supply but no immediate production changes.

title: Funds grow wary as red-hot copper hits nine-year highs: Andy Home
summary: Copper rallied to $8,437/t on the LME, its highest since May 2012, with low stocks, tightening spreads, and fund positioning flattening despite price gains. Options open interest shows increasing demand for downside puts as liquidity deteriorates, signaling correction risk. Nickel is mentioned as also being hedged via put structures.

title: Premium Nickel Resources Selected as Preferred Bidder in BCL Liquidation Process
summary: Premium Nickel Resources was selected as the preferred bidder to acquire Botswana Ni-Cu-Co assets from BCL’s liquidation process. The selection starts a six-month exclusivity period for due diligence and negotiations. This can modestly lift sentiment toward nickel and copper supply prospects, though no immediate production changes are confirmed.

title: Ivanplats Arranging Project-level Financing of up to US$420 Million to Advance Development of the World-scale Platreef Palladium, Platinum, Rhodium, Nickel, Copper and Gold Project in South Africa
summary: Ivanplats signed a non-binding term sheet for a US$300m gold/palladium/platinum streaming facility and arranged up to US$120m of senior project debt to advance the Platreef mine. The project development includes nickel and copper and targets initial production after engineering and shaft changeovers, supporting mild bullish sentiment despite non-binding terms.

title: Trimco Announces Strategic Partnership with Scranton Products for Industry-First Bactericidal Copper Partition Hardware
summary: Trimco and Scranton Products announced Healthy Hardware bathroom partition hardware made with EPA-registered bactericidal CuVerro copper alloys. The products are marketed to kill 99.9% of infectious bacteria when cleaned regularly, expanding Trimco’s copper touch-surface ecosystem for commercial buildings.

title: Searchlight Resources Inc: Searchlight Resources Granted Drill Permits for Beatty South Copper and Henning-Maloney Gold Targets
summary: Searchlight Resources said Saskatchewan granted drill permits for its Beatty South copper target and Henning-Maloney gold target, with mobilization expected within two weeks. The company plans to drill both targets in a single program, but provides no resource or production figures, making near-term copper price impact likely limited.

title: Searchlight Resources Granted Drill Permits for Beatty South Copper and Henning-Maloney Gold Targets
summary: Searchlight Resources received Saskatchewan Ministry of Environment permits to drill its Beatty South copper target and the Henning-Maloney gold target near Creighton/Flin Flon. Drilling is expected to mobilize within two weeks with a signed drilling contract. The release is an exploration milestone without stated production impact.

title: The Northern Miner Podcast – episode 226: Low-grade nickel deposits in the battery electric age, ft Selby, Muinonen, Carson and Pedlar-Hobbs at CIM Sudbury
summary: The Northern Miner Podcast episode features CIM Sudbury speakers discussing how Canadian low-grade nickel resources could help meet future electric-vehicle battery supply needs. It profiles companies and project experience around nickel-cobalt development, but provides no concrete near-term supply, policy, or inventory changes.

title: Copper drifts towards 9-year high on demand outlook, defies firm dollar
summary: LME benchmark copper edged higher toward a nine-year peak as optimism over global economic recovery supported metals demand despite a firmer U.S. dollar. Analysts at Goldman Sachs and Citi lifted copper targets. Smelting activity fell in January and China’s futures market reopened after Lunar New Year, reinforcing a tight supply outlook.

title: Rio Tinto Decreases Aluminium Pacific Operations Ore Reserve Estimate
summary: Rio Tinto said its Aluminium Pacific Operations ore reserve estimate fell by 305 Mt to 1,224 Mt, attributed to a routine review of price assumptions over the mine life. Mineral resources excluding ore reserves increased. It also reported major resource additions at Kennecott, boosting copper-equivalent resources but not near-term output.

title: Good news for Chile, copper price soaring on Chinese demand
summary: Chile’s main export, copper, surged to about $3.81/lb on the LME, the highest in eight years and nine months. Cochilco cited a steady climb from $3.63 last Friday, linked to a recovery in China and U.S. stimulus pledges, supporting strong copper demand and price momentum.

title: GLOBAL COPPER WRAP: Copper price nears 2012 level; US copper premium rises
summary: The article reports copper prices nearing a 2012 level and notes that the US copper premium has risen, indicating firmer near-term copper sentiment. It also mentions aluminium supply tightness and severe shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz, which can support aluminium differentials and cash prices despite limited specifics.

title: Canada Nickel Announces MacDiarmid Exploration Target - Approximately 15% Larger Than Crawford Main Zone
summary: Canada Nickel and Noble Mineral Exploration entered a binding LOI to option and consolidate additional properties around the MacDiarmid township nickel target. The exploration program identified a >1.8 km long, ~400 m wide target said to be similar quality to the earlier Crawford discovery and ~15% larger.

title: Grid Metals Corp.: Grid Metals Files NI 43-101 Report on Bannockburn Nickel Property: Historical Drilling Identifies Potential for Bulk Tonnage Nickel Deposit and High Grade Nickel Mineralization
summary: Grid Metals announced it received an NI 43-101 technical report for its Bannockburn nickel sulphide property near Timmins, Ontario. The report compiles 84 drill holes, highlights Mount Keith-type disseminated nickel mineralization and heazlewoodite-rich grades, and recommends further drilling and metallurgical work. No production or immediate supply changes were announced.

title: Russia's Norilsk Nickel hit with enormous fine over Arctic oil spill
summary: Norilsk Nickel faces a record $2.1 billion fine from Russia’s environmental regulator after a diesel spill caused damage to Arctic rivers and soil. The company says it will not appeal. The firm’s broader ecological overhaul includes shutting nickel smelting capacity and a planned copper smelter closure, affecting supply expectations.

title: USA Market Wrap - GLOBAL COPPER WRAP: Copper price nears 2012 level; US copper premium rises
summary: Copper prices near 2012 levels as the LME cash/three-month spread remains in backwardation. LME cash rises to the highest since May 2012 and on-warrant stocks fall week on week. The US copper premium also increases, indicating firmer demand and tighter nearby supply conditions.

title: Ongoing aluminum can shortage spurs packaging manufacturer to increase production
summary: Ongoing shortages of aluminum beverage cans continue to constrain beverage makers. Ball says it is capacity constrained and expects demand to outstrip supply into 2023, while Molson Coors reports improved availability toward end of Q1 after expanded global sourcing. Can producers are adding production, indicating sustained aluminum packaging tightness.

title: Copper prices hit 8-year high on pandemic-induced government spending and tightening supplies
summary: Copper futures hit an eight-year high as investors cite rebounding demand alongside a tightening supply picture. The piece points to China-related logistics bottlenecks (including shipping and migrant-worker quarantine effects) and analyst forecasts of a deficit, with some expecting further price gains in the near term amid speculative positioning.

title: GLOBAL NICKEL WRAP: US, Europe premiums steady amid Chinese holidays
summary: Fastmarkets’/Metal Bulletin coverage says US and Europe nickel premiums are steady amid Chinese holidays, suggesting muted immediate price movement. It also notes procedural delays and corrections to European low-carbon aluminium differential assessments and some aluminium billet premium data, mainly addressing publication errors rather than changing fundamentals.

title: US judge dismisses aluminum antitrust claims
summary: A U.S. judge narrowed a decade-old aluminum antitrust case, ruling many aluminum purchasers lacked standing and that smelters’ pricing played a key role in end prices rather than banks/defendants’ alleged conspiracy. Some plaintiffs can continue, but overall claims were dismissed for others, affecting legal expectations more than near-term supply.

title: Glencore records strong results; high nickel prices help
summary: Glencore reported strong 2020 results and reinstated a dividend, citing strong commodity prices and possible further payouts if prices remain firm. Its Sudbury operations produce nickel and copper, and Glencore’s trading benefited from strong copper and nickel markets. No specific new supply or inventory change is announced.

title: Peru reports sharp drop in 2020 copper production due to pandemic
summary: Peru’s Energy and Mines Ministry said 2020 copper production fell 12.5% to 2.15 million tonnes due to COVID-19 restrictions. Health authorities required staffing reductions across gold and copper mines from mid-March to May. Peru is the world’s second-largest copper producer, making the supply hit notable for markets.

title: Primary aluminium inventories built up 126,000 mt during CNY holiday_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s social inventories of primary aluminium across eight consumption areas rose by 126,000 mt during the Chinese New Year holiday to 901,000 mt as of Feb 18. Gains were mainly from stocks in Wuxi, Nanhai and Gongyi, suggesting higher near-term supply and potential price pressure.

title: Mining stocks climb as copper trades near decade high
summary: European mining shares rose as copper futures surged, with the LME copper contract hitting its highest level since April 2012. Rio Tinto and other copper-linked miners gained alongside nearly 4% growth in copper futures, reflecting bullish near-term pricing momentum for copper.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 169,000 wmt to 7.87 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 169,000 wmt from Feb 10 to 7.87 million wmt by Feb 18. In nickel content, stocks dropped 1,300 mt to 62,100 mt. Stocks at seven major ports also declined to 6.27 million wmt.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks remained unchanged during the CNY holiday_SMM
summary: SMM reports that refined nickel stocks in Shanghai bonded warehouses were unchanged at 17,600 mt as of Feb 18 during the CNY holiday. The import window stayed closed due to tepid foreign trade, and bonded warehouses suspended operations, with no arrivals under long-term contracts—supporting stable inventory levels.

title: Chakana Copper Corp.: Chakana Copper Accelerates Drill Program with Second Rig, Provides Exploration Update at Soledad, Peru
summary: Chakana Copper added a second drill rig and expanded its 2021 Soledad project drilling program in Peru, targeting resource definition and exploration at Huancarama and Paloma. The company says it is funded for a 26,000m drill program and will release further exploration results. It implies potential longer-run copper resource growth, not immediate output changes.

title: Teck Resources reports rise in quarterly profit boosted by robust copper business
summary: Teck reported a quarterly loss driven by non-cash writedowns tied to oil sands bitumen expectations, but highlighted improving copper performance. It said Quebrada Blanca Phase 2 copper expansion reached 40% completion and copper revenues and sales volumes rose year-on-year, supporting near-term copper supply outlook versus prior expectations.

title: White Metal Resources Corp.: White Metal Completes Drilling Program at the Taranis Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Resources said it completed a four-week reverse circulation drilling program at its 95%-owned Taranis copper-silver project in Namibia. The company plans to receive assay results by mid-March and publish an NI 43-101 resource estimate by April, based on the Okohongo deposit’s historical Cu grades.

title: Renforth Resources Inc.: Renforth Demonstrates 68% Average Sulphide Nickel Content within Surimeau Grab Samples
summary: Renforth Resources reports lab results on Surimeau grab samples showing an average of 68% sulphide nickel, with most samples indicating sulphide nickel as the dominant form and conventional milling recoverability. The company frames this as a large-scale, battery-grade nickel discovery and continues related assay work.

title: Teck's fourth-quarter adjusted profit soars on boost from copper business
summary: Teck Resources reported a big jump in Q4 adjusted profit driven by its copper business. Average realized copper prices rose about 26% to $3.42/lb and copper gross profit nearly tripled, while steelmaking-coal results weakened. Teck also said it met construction targets and is ramping Quebrada Blanca Phase 2 in Chile.

title: White Metal Completes Drilling Program at the Taranis Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Resources says it completed a four-week reverse-circulation drilling program at its 95%-owned Taranis copper-silver project in Namibia, submitting 727 samples for assay. The company plans an NI 43-101 compliant resource estimate after receiving results, offering limited short-term copper price signal as no assays are reported.

title: "Dr. Copper" ETFs look healthy even as stocks slump
summary: Copper-linked exchange-traded products rose Thursday even as global stocks fell. The United States Copper Index Fund and the iPath Bloomberg Copper Subindex Total Return ETN gained about 2% mid-morning, while a copper miners ETF rose over 0.8%. The piece reiterates copper as a proxy for global economic activity.

title: Zambia: IMF debt talks unlikely to stop Lungu from trying to pawn copper to China
summary: IMF debt talks in Zambia are unlikely to produce support before the election, increasing reliance on alternative financing. The article notes China’s role as a major copper consumer and investor in Zambia’s mines, potentially used as collateral for loans. This supports expectations of ongoing copper-linked funding and stability.

title: More Massive Sulfide Nickel at King Snake
summary: Blackstone Minerals reports continued drilling success at its King Snake massive sulfide prospect, with all five new holes intersecting MSV mineralisation and a defined strike length over 800m. The company sees significant potential for the project to add to nickel MSV inventory and potentially support restart of the Ban Phuc concentrator. Assays are due soon.

title: Trade unions call off strike at Alcoa aluminium giant in Spain
summary: Spain’s unions called off a four-month strike at Alcoa’s San Cibrao aluminium smelter, after opposing the closure and layoffs. The shutdown previously blocked shipments of over 50,000 metric tons of metal and reflects oversupply but near-term primary supply risk and disruption uncertainty for aluminium markets.

title: BHP Billiton: profit margin of 59% WAIO in the first half of 2021, Escondida copper production is a record._SMM
summary: BHP reports strong first-half 2021 performance, with record processing output at the Escondida copper concentrator and smooth start-up of the Spence copper mine expansion. The company says rising iron ore and copper prices boosted free cash flow and raised guidance, which can reinforce near-term positive sentiment for copper markets.

title: Outlook on the Automotive Aluminium Alloy Global Market to 2026 - Competition, Forecast & Opportunities
summary: The report forecasts strong growth for the global automotive aluminium alloy market through 2026, driven by increasing vehicle production and vehicle-weight reduction using aluminium components. It also cites environmental regulations and adoption in regions like Asia-Pacific and Europe. These points imply supportive near-term demand sentiment for aluminium.

title: NORNICKEL NOT TO APPEAL THE COURT'S RULING REGARDING DIESEL SPILL INCIDENT
summary: Norilsk Nickel said it will not appeal a Krasnoyarsk arbitrazh court ruling related to a diesel fuel spill at its HPP-3 in Norilsk in May 2020. Management will comply with the judgment, citing legal advice. The release does not mention penalties or operational effects, suggesting limited immediate impact on nickel and copper markets.

title: Copper prices top $4 a pound for the first time in over 9 years
summary: Copper futures surpassed $4 per pound for the first time in more than nine years. The move is linked to expectations of a recovering global economy and increased renewable (“green”) energy deployment, which should improve industrial demand prospects. Analysts cite continued upside for copper demand and prices as the transition accelerates.

title: Gold futures lose more than 2% for the week; copper rallies to a more than 9-year high
summary: The article notes copper rallied to its highest finish since September 2011, reaching a more than 9-year high as markets bet a U.S. COVID-19 relief package and economic recovery would boost demand. Copper rose about 4.4% on Friday and nearly 7.6% for the week.

title: Copper prices are soaring. Here's why that's good news for the recovery
summary: Copper prices climbed above $4/lb, the highest in nearly a decade. The article links the rally to optimism for stronger infrastructure and construction demand in the US and China, plus supply constraints and low Chinese inventories. It notes risks from potential COVID-related reopening delays but expects continued support.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Corporate and Operations Update
summary: Nevada Copper reported improved main-shaft hoisting performance and strong milling throughput with rising recoveries, but unplanned shaft mechanical stoppages have reduced 2021 ore production versus plan. Copper concentrate output is expected to be significantly lower in H1 2021, with higher rates and deferred steady-state output into Q3 after electrical/ventilation upgrades.

title: Aluminium premiums, prices rally in Europe amid tight supply across complex
summary: The piece says aluminium premiums and prices have risen in Europe, attributing the move to tight supply across complex market conditions. It also notes Fastmarkets’ procedural corrections to certain European low-carbon aluminium differential and billet premium assessments, consistent with recent premium strength.

title: Part of Nornickel's Arctic processing plant collapses, one killed
summary: Norilsk Nickel said part of its Arctic processing plant collapsed during renovation in Siberia, killing one worker and leaving two missing. The plant continues operating with restrictions while an investigation is opened. As a leading nickel producer, the disruption and constraints raise near-term supply risk and potential downside for nickel.

title: Part of Nornickel's Arctic processing plant collapses, one killed | News
summary: Norilsk Nickel said part of its Arctic processing plant partially collapsed during maintenance work in Siberia, killing one worker and leaving two missing.
