It cites US/EU sanctions and China countermeasures boosting risk-off sentiment, alongside a US green-infrastructure plan and trade/market developments.

title: White Metal Reports 1.54% Cu and 36 g/t Ag over 31 Metres from the Taranis Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Reports results from its Taranis Copper-Silver Project in Namibia, including 1.54% copper over 31 metres (and 36 g/t silver). The update is an exploration/grade announcement without any stated production, shipment, or permitting change, suggesting limited short-term influence on copper pricing.

title: 'Deficient' shipment of Chinese aluminium forces delay to Navy's Cape Class patrol boats
summary: A shipment of “materially deficient” Chinese aluminium was found by Australian shipbuilder Austal, forcing remediation of Cape Class patrol boats and delaying launch dates by four to 16 weeks. The supplier removed the mill and lab from approved lists and is replacing out-of-spec material, adding maintenance costs.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 23/03: Aluminium tumbles 2% on rumors of Chinese stockpile cuts
summary: Aluminium futures tumbled about 2% as markets reacted to rumors that China’s stockpiles would be cut. The article frames the move as a near-term sentiment shock affecting aluminium supply expectations, leading to immediate downside pressure in aluminium benchmarks and related futures.

title: Workers at Antofagasta's Los Pelambres copper mine in Chile accept contract offer
summary: Workers at Antofagasta’s Los Pelambres copper mine in Chile accepted a contract offer, ending a threat of strike. The union said the vote was 70.65% in favor. The resolution reduces the risk of immediate production disruption at a mine producing about 6% of Chile’s output.

title: Antofagasta Avoids Strike at Top Copper Mine With $27,000 Bonus
summary: Antofagasta reportedly avoided a strike at its main copper mine by agreeing on a $27,000 bonus. The resolution reduces the likelihood of short-term production outages, easing immediate supply disruption fears and providing modest support to expectations for copper output and near-term pricing.

title: Copper in Australia
summary: The piece describes Australia’s copper production and reserves, highlighting major mines such as BHP’s Olympic Dam and other producers across several states. It notes that most copper exports go to Asia, especially China, and frames copper’s long-term outlook, but offers no immediate market-moving event.

title: Mitsubishi Corp to acquire interest in bauxite project in Australia
summary: Mitsubishi will acquire a 30% interest in Glencore’s Aurukun bauxite project in Queensland, adding bauxite exposure to its existing aluminium smelting and trading operations. The mine is undeveloped and currently under feasibility assessment, so the agreement may support longer-term supply prospects for aluminium rather than immediate output changes.

title: Taseko Mines: Court of Appeal Decides in Favor of Florence Copper
summary: Taseko said an Arizona Court of Appeals decision confirmed Florence Copper’s mining rights, rejected the Town of Florence’s appeal, and upheld permit-related progress toward commercial operations. The company also cited capital secured via a bond offering and ongoing design, engineering and procurement for the in-situ facility, supporting its copper project outlook.

title: Copper cathode imports during January-February fell 9.09% year on year_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s copper cathode imports fell 9.09% YoY in Jan-Feb 2021, dropping to 268,500 mt in January and 263,400 mt in February. Closed import arbitrage and South American shipment problems reduced inflows, but March arrivals are expected to rise as Chile issues ease. Inventories are still increasing despite low LME stocks.

title: Prices of battery-grade nickel sulphate continued to decline_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports battery-grade nickel sulphate (crystal) quotations were cut to 34,000–34,500 yuan/mt, with active selling and most buyers staying sidelined. Despite tight spot availability, premiums narrowed and sellers expect further lower pricing. The article also cites shortfalls in intermediate raw materials and limited briquette dissolution capacity.

title: China's copper imports drop 9% in Jan-Feb on poor arb, holiday effect
summary: China’s copper imports declined 9% in Jan–Feb, the article attributes the drop to poorer arbitrage activity and holiday-related distortions. The lower import flow suggests weaker near-term physical demand and copper buying interest, which can pressure short-term market expectations for supply/demand tightness.

title: MAX Resource Corp.: Max Resource Assays 12.5% Copper and 120 g/t Silver from its New CONEJO Discovery at CESAR North, NE Colombia
summary: MAX Resource Corp. reports high-grade copper results (e.g., up to 12.5% copper) from rock panel samples in its new CONEJO discovery within the CESAR copper-silver project in northeastern Colombia. The release highlights exploration potential over a 1.6-km by 0.6-km zone but does not affect current supply or refining.

title: Surge Copper Significantly Expands West Seel with Step Out Hole Intersecting 585 Metres Grading 0.57% Copper Equivalent Including 164 Metres Grading 0.68% Copper Equivalent
summary: Surge Copper announced step-out drilling results at its Ootsa Property, with Hole S21-228 intersecting 585 metres grading 0.57% copper equivalent and higher-grade intervals including 0.68% copper equivalent over 164 metres. Management says the deposit is open for further expansion, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Copper falls on Europe coronavirus lockdowns, firmer dollar
summary: Copper prices fell as renewed European coronavirus lockdown fears boosted demand for the U.S. dollar and weighed on global growth sentiment. Three-month LME copper and Shanghai May copper dropped. Nickel also eased on the day, while aluminum premiums rose, indicating regional tightness despite broader macro headwinds.

title: China exported 153,200 mt of aluminium extrusions from January to February_SMM
summary: SMM cites China Customs data showing aluminium bars and extrusions exports in early 2021, with aluminium extrusion exports rising 35.9% year-on-year to 153,200 mt in January–February. February exports fell versus January. Destinations are scattered, with Southeast Asia and Guangdong as leading contributors.

title: Premium Nickel Resources Corporation: Premium Nickel Resources Awarded Exclusivity to Acquire Former BCL Assets in Botswana
summary: Premium Nickel Resources said it completed an exclusivity MOU for a six-month due diligence period to acquire former BCL Ni-Cu-Co assets in Botswana, with the company selected as preferred bidder. The work includes environmental, metallurgical, and legal reviews and negotiations for purchase agreements.

title: North American Nickel Inc.: North American Nickel Reports PNR Awarded Exclusivity to Acquire Former BCL Assets in Botswana
summary: North American Nickel reports that Premium Nickel Resources received exclusivity for six months to complete due diligence and negotiate purchase agreements for former BCL Ni-Cu-Co assets in Botswana. The company frames redevelopment as producing critical metals, potentially supporting nickel supply expectations, though timing depends on future agreement and development.

title: Damm and Ball launch world's first Aluminium Stewardship Initiative certified beverage cans
summary: Damm and Ball Corporation announced that Damm’s beer will use only ASI-certified aluminium beverage cans from March 2021. The ASI certification covers responsible sourcing and stewardship across the aluminium lifecycle, including can production and recycling. The news is about sustainability standards rather than a measurable near-term supply or demand shock.

title: Oil, copper concentrate and coal export increased
summary: Mongolia’s Ministry reported mining export statistics for Jan 1–Mar 21, 2021. Copper concentrate exports rose to 298.4 thousand tons (+7.7%). Coal and oil exports also increased, while iron ore declined. The copper concentrate rise suggests slightly higher concentrate supply, but without market-size detail.

title: Secondary aluminium: prices to lack upward momentum, orders improved slightly_SMM
summary: SMM reports weak demand and poor sales at secondary aluminium producers have pressured aluminium scrap prices. Tight supply from import restrictions keeps scrap tense supply limited, but secondary aluminium (ADC12) lacks momentum, with orders only slightly improving. Prices are expected to decline this week, with downstream losses expanding if aluminium rises.

title: Alumina: Prices in north China rose slightly, high sea freight curbed imports_SMM
summary: North China alumina trading was thin and prices stayed largely stable around 2,340–2,350 yuan/mt. Higher sea freight from Western Australia to China ($40/mt) curbed overseas buying and intensified losses on imports. FOB alumina fell to $289/mt, while smelters shifted toward domestic supply.

title: Bitterroot Resources Ltd.: Bitterroot Resources Intersects Additional Nickel-Copper-PGM Mineralization and Expands the LM Property
summary: Bitterroot Resources reports a new drill intersection (LM 21-10) of disseminated and blebby sulphides at its Michigan LM project, including chalcopyrite and associated nickel-bearing minerals, with assays expected in 8–10 weeks. It also expands the property via a memorandum. No production or inventory changes are indicated.

title: Westminster Resources Ltd. Identifies Roots to Copper Mineralization at Mostazal
summary: Westminster Resources announced it is reviewing past exploration at its Mostazal copper-silver property in Chile. The company says geophysical anomalies correlate with surface copper mineralization and suggests potential porphyry copper mineralization at depth. The release is exploration-focused and does not indicate near-term supply changes.

title: Mitsui Mining to exit from copper mining, selling stake in Collahuasi mine
summary: Mitsui Mining will exit copper mining by selling its 0.97% stake in Chile’s Collahuasi copper mine to Mitsui & Co. Terms are undisclosed and completion is expected by end-March. The move boosts Mitsui’s profit via a one-off gain but does not indicate any near-term copper supply disruption.

title: Copper line theft drains Openserve's pockets
summary: Openserve’s CEO says copper line theft and vandalism have cost the firm over R60 million in the past year and disrupted service for thousands of DSL customers across 800+ hotspot areas. Telkom estimates the wider telecom sector loses millions annually, and industry groups cite multi-billion rand annual costs.

title: Antofagasta : Workers at Antofagasta's Los Pelambres copper mine in Chile accept contract offer
summary: Workers at Antofagasta’s Los Pelambres copper mine in Chile accepted a contract offer after a union vote, averting a potential strike. Los Pelambres produced about 372,100 tonnes of copper in 2020 (around 6% of Chile’s total). The development lowers near-term disruption risk for copper supply.

title: Norway's Nussir considers share listing after Arctic copper mine agreement
summary: Nussir ASA may list shares in Oslo after signing a cooperation agreement with Norway’s Hammerfest municipality to build a fully electric Arctic copper mine. The deal follows local opposition, but the company cites community support and a 10-year copper tailings supply agreement with Aurubis. Electrification aims to cut emissions.

title: Grid Metals Corp.: Grid Metals Set to Drill at Bannockburn Nickel Property Completes 15 Drill Holes at East Bull Lake Palladium Property
summary: Grid Metals Corp. reports completion of additional drilling at its East Bull Lake palladium property and plans to commence ~2,000 meters of drilling at its Bannockburn nickel property in Timmins, targeting the B Zone. The company expects to confirm nickel grades and widths, but no assay results are provided now.

title: Mitsui Mining to sell stake in Collahuasi copper mine in Chile
summary: Mitsui Mining and Smelting will sell its 0.97% stake in Chile’s Collahuasi copper mine to its parent, Mitsui & Co, increasing Mitsui’s holding to 12%. The move is part of portfolio restructuring and is expected by end-March. MMS cites EV and renewable trends supporting copper demand.

title: Renforth Commences Drilling the Victoria Nickel Target on Surimeau District Property
summary: Renforth Resources begins a ~3,500m drill program targeting the Victoria nickel zone on its Surimeau property. Prior surface and sub-surface work indicated sulphide mineralization with nickel and other metals, including copper (and zinc). The update is exploratory with no immediate supply impact, limiting near-term price effects.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 7,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s primary aluminium ingot inventories fell during the week, dropping 7,000 mt from last Thursday to about 1.24 million mt as of March 25. The decrease was mainly driven by lower stocks in Wuxi, Nanhai, and Hangzhou, including SHFE-warranted supplies.

title: Aluminium billet inventories fell 34,700 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s aluminium billet stocks across key consuming regions fell 34,700 mt WoW to 198,200 mt as of Mar 25, driven by outbound activity, price volatility, and tepid but concentrated downstream restocking. With prices stabilized, inventories are expected to stay broadly stable next week.

title: Century Aluminum confirms Berkeley County plant's restart project on schedule
summary: Century Aluminum says it has finalized a new three-year power contract with Santee Cooper, rescinding a WARN notice tied to potential job losses if the Mt. Holly aluminium smelter could not restart. The contract takes effect April 1, supports rebuilding cells and restarting the potline, and runs through Dec. 2023.

title: London copper rebounds on optimism around global economic recovery
summary: London copper rose 1.1% after positive U.S. labor data and faster COVID-19 vaccination rollout boosted optimism for global recovery. However, both copper contracts remain set for weekly losses amid Europe’s COVID-19 wave, rising inventories, and a stronger dollar. LME aluminium and ShFE nickel also edged higher.

title: Tertiary Minerals records 'encouraging' results from maiden drill hole at Lucky Copper Project | 26 March 2021
summary: Tertiary Minerals says it has delivered “encouraging” assay results from a first (maiden) drill hole at its Lucky Copper Project. Positive early drilling outcomes can lift expectations for the potential size/quality of a copper resource, typically providing modest near-term support to copper-linked sentiment.

title: London copper rises on optimism around global economic recovery
summary: London copper rose 1.1% as equities climbed on optimism for global economic recovery, supported by positive U.S. labour data and faster-than-expected COVID-19 vaccination progress. The note cited metals tracking stock market gains. LME aluminium and ShFE nickel also advanced, though copper inventories were rising.

title: Mitsui Mining to sell Collahuasi copper mine stake
summary: Mitsui Mining and Smelting plans to sell its 0.97% stake in Chile’s Collahuasi copper mine to Mitsui & Co as part of an asset reshuffle. The deal should close by month-end and is expected to generate a one-off gain of 9.5 billion yen, with no production or shipment changes cited.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 1,500 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 1,500 mt week-on-week to 11,300 mt as of Mar 26. Nickel cathode and briquettes flowed into domestic markets, while import arbitrage is currently closed, leaving bonded stocks at low levels. Shipments from the bonded zone may slow next week.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Mar 26): Nonferrous metals on the SHFE closed mostly higher, nickel increased 1.93%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals mostly rose on Friday. Copper closed flat, but aluminium gained 1.52% and nickel rose 1.93%. The commentary cites supportive US policy signals alongside infrastructure/innovation rhetoric, consistent with improved sentiment for industrial metal demand in the near term.

title: Humble aluminum can shows a circular economy won't be easy: Andy Home
summary: The article says EU plans to toughen waste packaging rules could push aluminum can recycling toward 100% by 2030. It notes significant ongoing “metal loss” from not collected cans in Europe and the US, implying a scrap supply gap. Recycling is also framed as crucial for decarbonizing aluminum production.

title: Mincor signs $42m loan facility for Kambalda nickel operations
summary: Mincor Resources secured A$55m ($41.7m) loan funding to fully develop and restart Kambalda Nickel Operations in Western Australia. Management expects first drawdown late in the September 2021 quarter and targets early 2022 production of high-grade nickel sulphides, supporting nickel supply expectations; the project also includes some copper output.

title: NORNICKEL MAJOR SHAREHOLDERS AGREED ON A SPIN-OFF OF BYSTRINSKY PROJECT
summary: Nornickel reports that its major shareholders agreed to a spin-off of the Bystrinsky project. The move is likely to influence investors’ expectations for the timing and structure of future nickel supply from Nornickel’s asset base, which can affect near-term nickel pricing sentiment within weeks.

title: Russia's Rusal open for talks over Nornickel dividend - deputy CEO
summary: Rusal is open to talks with Nornickel’s other major shareholder, Interros, over a proposed change to Nornickel’s dividend policy. The board will review investment strategy and dividends on March 29. Rusal says it needs stronger arguments and wants discussions tied to recent accidents and related risks.

title: Tribal, Religious Groups Back Apache Bid To Halt Copper Mine
summary: Tribal and religious groups are supporting an Apache bid seeking to halt a copper mine. The legal action could delay or stop production, tightening near-term supply expectations. Such developments often influence copper price sentiment over the following days to weeks, depending on the likelihood and timing of the mine’s shutdown.

title: Copper Futures Jump On Strong Chinese Demand
summary: Copper futures are reported to have risen following expectations of strong demand from China. This points to improved near-term physical consumption and buying interest, which typically tightens market sentiment and supports higher copper prices over the coming days.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 9,000 mt over weekend_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s primary aluminium ingot inventories fell over the weekend. Social stocks across eight consumption areas declined 9,000 mt from last Thursday to 1.23 million mt as of March 29. Drops in Wuxi and Nanhai drove most of the decrease, while Hangzhou rose slightly.

title: Foreign trade copper premium continued to decline, the spread of warehouse receipt and bill of lading was smoothed_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums continued falling as the USD copper market stayed tepid. The spread between warehouse receipts and bills of lading narrowed and turned inverted. Slow domestic consumption, weak downstream buying, and rising Shanghai bonded copper stocks supported a bearish tone, with Yangshan premium expected to remain weak next week.

title: Copper falls on signs of slowing demand
summary: London copper fell 0.7% to around $8,900/ton, driven by higher LME exchange inventories and signals of weakening demand from China, the top consumer. The report also cites LME aluminum down about 1%. Nickel direction is mixed, with ShFE nickel up and ShFE tin higher.

title: BTU Metals Corp.: BTU Exploration Underway on Expanded Land Position Near TNT Copper Silver Discovery
summary: BTU Metals announced expanded land and ongoing IP geophysical surveying near its TNT copper-silver-gold discovery in Ontario’s Red Lake area. Early results suggest a significant sulphide-related chargeability target. The release mainly affects copper exploration sentiment, but it does not provide resource or supply changes, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Nornickel board calls on shareholders to discuss proposed change to dividend policy
summary: Norilsk Nickel’s board asked shareholders to discuss proposed changes to dividend policy as the company plans additional investment in production and environmental protection following a major Arctic fuel spill. The company faced a $2 billion fine and is considering paying dividends based on free cash flow, potentially altering near-term sentiment around nickel.

title: Nornickel plans to fully restore production at flooded mines in May - early June
summary: Nornickel said it has stopped water inflow at the flooded Oktyabrsky mine and is resuming production. Oktyabrsky is set to fully resume in early May, while Taimyrsky is expected to restart in early June. The firm previously cut 2021 nickel and copper output forecasts but the repair timeline improves near-term supply expectations.

title: Nornickel stops water inflow at two Arctic mines - The Northern Miner
summary: Nornickel stopped water flowing into two Siberian Arctic mines, saying the sites remain on track to fully resume production in the coming period. By mitigating immediate operational disruption at a key producer, the move can support nickel supply expectations in the next several weeks.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Announces Opportunities to Accelerate Future Expansions at the Tier-One Kamoa-Kakula Copper Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines announced US$575m convertible bond funding to accelerate Kamoa-Kakula copper mine expansions, including additional hydropower upgrades for power supply, a faster Phase 3 concentrator ramp, and possible downstream smelting. It also funds accelerated Western Foreland copper exploration. Overall, the project timeline and growth prospects are copper-bullish.

title: Crown Mining Corp.: Crown Mining Announces AGM Results and Name Change to US Copper Corp
summary: Crown Mining Corp. reported AGM results and a special resolution to change its name to US Copper Corp, with regulatory approvals expected within weeks. The company controls major copper claims in California and previously produced copper. No operational or supply-demand change was announced, suggesting limited near-term price impact.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces 2021 First Quarter Operating and Financial Results
summary: Copper Fox reported Q1 2021 financial results and highlighted progress on its copper projects: a Van Dyke PEA for in-situ copper recovery exceeding expectations, commissioning of a Schaft Creek PEA, receipt of a Mines Act permit for Eaglehead, and planned 2021 budgets for drilling, pilot testing, and metallurgical work. No production or market-impact details are given.

title: Hudbay Announces Significant New Discovery at its Copper World Properties Adjacent to Rosemont
summary: Hudbay announced significant new exploration results at its Copper World properties adjacent to the Rosemont copper project in Arizona, including multiple drill intercepts with ~0.70% to 1.38% copper and strong near-surface copper oxide/sulphide mineralization. The company doubled rigs to six, planning further drilling and resource definition.

title: Opening of Cassini mine marks start of new era for Kambalda's historic nickel mining industry
summary: WA’s Mines Minister will open Mincor’s Cassini underground nickel mine near Kambalda, the first new nickel development in two decades after low nickel prices caused prior mine shutdowns. The $98 million restart aims for first nickel in August and could expand output, boosting nickel market sentiment.

title: Russian nickel prices retreated while Jinchuan Nickel prices rose, inventories fell little amid sluggish trade_SMM
summary: SMM reports nickel prices swinging and then slipping as downstream purchasing stays sluggish and bonded-area demand fails to absorb imported Russian nickel. Shanghai bonded inventories fell to 11,300 mt by March 26. Russian premiums eased while Jinchuan prices rose on smelter financial closure; briquette premiums adjusted as trading remained weak.

title: Copper rises in tepid trade as investors eye Chinese demand
summary: Copper prices rose on the day as investors focused on stronger-than-seasonal Chinese demand entering Q2. Support also came from low treatment charges for copper concentrate and limited mined supplies. The piece notes investors awaiting U.S. infrastructure bill details that could further boost metals demand.

title: IN BRIEF: Taseko Mines extends copper price...
summary: Taseko Mines extended its copper price protection strategy by purchasing put options covering 41 million pounds of copper at a USD 3.75 strike for the second half of 2021. Management says the hedge secures minimum operating margin amid Covid-19 and metal market volatility, without capping cash flow if prices rise.

title: Mincor opens Cassini Nickel Mine in Kambalda
summary: Mincor has officially opened the Cassini nickel mine within its Kambalda Nickel Operations in Western Australia. The company says first nickel concentrate is on track for 1Q22 and production will ramp toward 16,000 tpy of nickel-in-concentrate. It supplies concentrate via BHP Nickel West for further processing into nickel sulfate.

title: Mincor Resources opens Cassini nickel mine in Western Australia
summary: Mincor Resources officially opened the Cassini nickel underground mine in Western Australia. The project is expected to provide about 56% of Mincor’s nickel output in its first five years, with first nickel concentrate targeted for early next year and production processed via BHP’s Kambalda concentrator.

title: Great Atlantic Resources Corp.: Great Atlantic Completes Maiden Diamond Drilling Program at Mascarene Copper, Cobalt, Nickel, Zinc, Gold Property Southwest New Brunswick
summary: Great Atlantic Resources completed a maiden diamond drill program at its Mascarene property in New Brunswick, intersecting narrow sulfide veins including copper sulfides plus magnetite intervals. The site is also associated with historical copper and inferred mafic intrusion-hosted copper-nickel-cobalt potential, but it remains exploratory with no immediate supply change.

title: Canadian copper miner Turquoise Hill declares force majeure on some Chinese contracts
summary: Turquoise Hill invoked force majeure on Chinese contracts for shipments from its Mongolian Oyo Tolgoi copper mine due to COVID-19 border delays between China and Mongolia and positive cases at the site. This is expected to delay copper concentrate exports, adding short-term downward pressure to copper supply expectations.

title: EU imposes tariffs on Chinese aluminium producers
summary: The EU has imposed anti-dumping duties of 21.2% to 31.2% on Chinese aluminium extrusions after finding they were sold at unfairly low prices. Duties are lower than provisional levels. The action targets products used in transport, construction and electronics and should reduce low-priced imports.

title: North American Nickel Inc.: North American Nickel Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement Financing of up to $1.5 Million
summary: North American Nickel Inc. announced a $1.5M non-brokered private placement to fund continued investments, including exploration tied to its nickel projects in Greenland and Ontario and further activities in Morocco. The release is exploratory in nature and does not indicate near-term production, supply disruption, or inventory changes for nickel.

title: Oyu Tolgoi declares force majeure due to delayed copper concentrate shipments to Chinese customers
summary: Oyu Tolgoi declared force majeure for concentrate contracts because shipments to Chinese customers were suspended due to COVID-19 health and safety precautions at Chinese-Mongolian border crossings. The concentrator operated uninterrupted, but underground work was temporarily halted during testing. The firm is working to resume deliveries as soon as possible.

title: Higher Chinese imports herald coming copper scrap surge
summary: China’s copper scrap imports rose 60% year-on-year to 191,720 tonnes in the first two months of 2021. The increase follows a November rule change that reclassified eligible scrap as a “resource” rather than “solid waste,” removing bans on high-grade copper recyclables and potentially boosting recycled copper supply.

title: Canadian miner declares force majeure as pandemic affects Mongolian copper deliveries
summary: Turquoise Hill Resources said its Mongolian Oyu Tolgoi mine’s operator declared force majeure after COVID-19 precautions suspended shipments of copper concentrate to Chinese customers at border crossings. Two COVID cases were reported at the site and underground development work was halted while testing and travel restrictions disrupted operations.

title: Ivanhoe working towards accelerating Phase 3 expansion at Kamoa-Kakula copper mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says proceeds from a recently completed US$575 million, 2.50% convertible notes offering will be used to accelerate Phase 3 expansion at the Kamoa-Kakula copper mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The update targets faster scaling of copper production capacity.

title: Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Duties Litigation Shifts Into High Gear | Arent Fox
summary: The update focuses on litigation and renewed legislative interest around Section 232 tariffs. It notes reinstatement of aluminum import duties from the UAE shortly after removal and highlights that the Commerce Secretary called the duties “effective.” With the U.S. defending duties in multiple court and WTO cases, near-term removal appears unlikely.

title: Taseko Mines clears legal hurdles at Florence; advances copper projects
summary: Taseko Mines said it can move forward with its Florence copper in-situ project after an Arizona Court of Appeals rejected arguments against the project by the Town of Florence. The ruling clears legal hurdles, improving near-term project certainty for future copper supply.

title: Suez Canal suspension to disrupt Chinese aluminium exports to Europe_SMM
summary: A container ship grounding has blocked two-way traffic through the Suez Canal, disrupting shipping between Europe and Asia. SMM links the disruption to delayed China aluminium semis exports (plate, strip, foil, extrusion, wire/cable), with detouring via the Cape expected to add about one month and affect April shipments if prolonged.

title: LME copper set for first monthly fall in 1 year
summary: LME copper is poised for its first monthly fall in a year, down around 0.5% on the day and nearly 3.8% month-to-date, pressured by a firmer U.S. dollar and renewed COVID-19 risks in Europe. The piece also cites copper concentrate force majeure and notes nickel weakness and flat aluminium.

title: Vedanta to set up new copper smelter plant; to exit Tuticorin?
summary: Vedanta plans a 500,000 tpa copper smelter in India and has asked coastal states to partner after requesting expressions of interest. The piece questions whether it is exiting the previously shut Tuticorin Sterlite copper smelter, with a Supreme Court case ongoing and the next hearing in August.

title: Papua New Guinea's Ok Tedi copper mine resumes operations after COVID-19 shutdown
summary: Papua New Guinea’s Ok Tedi copper mine will resume operations after a two-week COVID-19 suspension at the site. Startup will be gradual, ramping to full production within up to two weeks. Management expects revenue loss from the shutdown but remains upbeat on profit for the year.

title: Domestic alumina prices to rise slightly, high sea freight continues to suppress buying interest and prices overseas_SMM
summary: SMM reports muted domestic alumina trading with mostly steady prices, but limited upside due to a market shifting toward surplus. Overseas buying is inhibited by rising sea freight to China (Western/Eastern Australia), worsening importer losses. An FOB alumina deal from Western Australia to India fell $274/mt from $289/mt.

title: Copper rod processing companies to see improved consumption from power industry _SMM
summary: SMM reports low operating rates at copper rod plants and weak March orders, driven by soft power-sector demand. Production and sales fell over 25%, inventory rose, and secondary rod shipments were subdued. With power-grid order declines and sluggish downstream purchasing, copper consumption is expected to improve only slowly in April.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 31/03: Rewarranting of aluminium at LME warehouses in Malaysia fails to depress futures prices
summary: The article reports an LME Malaysia aluminium warehouse “rewarranting” event that did not lead to weaker aluminium futures. It describes Fastmarkets’ related publication/assessment corrections and broader commentary on how aluminium supply and inventories have behaved, but emphasizes that this specific change failed to pressure prices lower.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Provides an Update on Pre-Feasibility Study Fieldwork at the 100%-Owned Alacran Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals provided an update on progress at its Alacran copper-gold-silver project in Colombia, including ongoing PFS fieldwork, metallurgical drilling results correlations, and plans to deepen holes and design further exploration for porphyry sources. It also notes PTO/EIA schedule and no immediate production changes.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Consistently Intersects Nickel-Copper Mineralization in a New Zone Outside of the Tamarack Nickel Project Resource Area
summary: Talon Metals reports consistent drilling intercepts of shallow nickel-copper sulphide mineralization in the CGO East zone outside the Tamarack resource area. Multiple drill holes intersect nickel-copper mineralization with mixed and massive sulphides, but assays are pending. The company plans further drilling to delineate additional resources.

title: SPC Nickel Corp.: SPC Nickel Acquires the Outstanding 30% Interest in the Historic West Graham Ni-Cu Property, Sudbury Mining Camp, Ontario
summary: SPC Nickel Corp. announced it acquired the remaining 30% interest in the West Graham Ni-Cu property in Ontario, taking full control subject to a 1% net smelter return royalty. The release cites historic nickel and copper resource grades and discusses future evaluation of the Lockerby East portfolio.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Mar 31): Shanghai nonferrous metals fell for the most part, nickel plunged 2.19%_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai nonferrous prices fell broadly, with SHFE copper -1.1%, aluminium -1.32%, and nickel -2.19%. The decline is attributed to higher US bond yields lifting the dollar, weighing on copper futures. Contracts also saw lower or rising open interest depending on metal, indicating short-term bearish sentiment.

title: Vedanta plans to set up new copper smelter plant; to exit Tuticorin? (Ld)
summary: Vedanta says it is seeking partners to build a new 500,000 tpa copper smelter in a coastal location and may be shifting from its closed Tuticorin plant. It argues the Tuticorin shutdown has made India a net copper importer. The company’s new plant remains at partner-selection stage, not imminent supply.

title: Renforth Intersects Visible Nickel, Copper and Zinc Sulphides in Initial 1,350m Drill Step Out to the West at Victoria West
summary: Renforth Resources said it intersected visible nickel, copper, and zinc sulphides in an initial 1,350m drill step-out west at its Victoria West target in Quebec. The result supports expectations for potential copper and nickel mineralization, which may modestly lift short-term sentiment in those metals despite being early-stage.

title: Vale sells New Caledonia nickel assets to Trafigura
summary: Vale has completed the sale of its nickel (and cobalt) operations in New Caledonia to a consortium led by Prony, which includes Trafigura. The transaction could affect nickel supply expectations, but the provided excerpt does not disclose production impacts or timelines, making the near-term price effect unclear.

title: Chile says manufacturing, copper output down in February
summary: Chile reported its February copper production declined 4.8% to 430,100 tonnes, citing lower ore grades at aging mines. The drop in extraction and processing comes amid renewed COVID-19 restrictions, though mining has broadly held up. The supply shortfall is likely to weigh on copper prices in the near term.

title: Victory Nickel Inc.: Victory Nickel Engages Financial Advisor for Debt Restructuring
summary: Victory Nickel engaged a financial advisor to pursue restructuring of its unsecured debt. It also previously sold its Minago nickel property and notes a reduction of secured debt and liquidity from transactions with Silver Elephant. The release does not specify production changes, but links to the company’s nickel asset footprint.

title: Wisconsin Aluminum Foundry in Manitowoc acquires Wabash Castings
summary: Wisconsin Aluminum Foundry plans to buy Wabash Castings, adding about 100 workers and expanding its product lines serving EVs and consumer goods. The acquisition is an expansion of an aluminum casting business, potentially supporting incremental aluminum demand, but details on volumes or market pricing are not provided.

title: ITC Greenlights Duties On Aluminum From 16 Countries
summary: The article says the U.S. ITC has greenlit anti-import duties on aluminum shipments from 16 countries. Tariffs like these typically increase the landed cost of imported metal and can alter short-term supply flows, weighing on aluminum pricing expectations over the coming days and weeks.

title: Vale concludes sale of New Caledonia nickel plant
summary: Vale has completed the sale of its New Caledonia nickel plant to Prony Resources after political unrest over the deal. Terms were not disclosed, though $1.1 billion will be invested and Vale retains a long-term nickel supply contract. Vale cites support for EV-driven nickel demand; no output disruption is stated.

title: Vale sells New Caledonia nickel assets to Trafigura - Brazil Business Today
summary: Vale has completed the sale of its nickel and cobalt operations in New Caledonia to a consortium led by Prony, which includes Trafigura. The report does not suggest any immediate operational changes, so the transaction is unlikely to materially move nickel prices in the next few weeks, though it is supply-relevant.

title: Oman's Sohar Aluminium closes $600mln ln 7-year loan
summary: Oman's Sohar Aluminium, part-owned by Rio Tinto, secured a $600 million seven-year loan to refinance existing debt used for constructing its aluminium smelter and facilities. The refinancing with nine international banks helps manage financing costs and liquidity, but does not signal immediate capacity change.

title: Copper falls on slowing Chinese factory growth, Codelco wage deal
summary: Copper prices fell as China’s Caixin/Markit factory PMI slowed to its weakest in almost a year, signaling softer physical demand. Prices were also pressured by Chile’s Codelco clinching a labor deal at Radomiro Tomic, which reduces strike-related supply risk that previously supported copper.

title: Aluminium billet inventories shrank 4,300 mt to193,800 mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows China’s 6063 aluminium billet inventories across five major consumption areas fell 4,300 mt from the prior week to 193,800 mt as of Apr 1. Shipments rose slightly in the week. The report expects modest further stock shrinkage next week as downstream restocks only as needed.

title: Primary aluminium inventories rose 8,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China’s social inventories of primary aluminium across eight consumption areas increased 8,000 mt week-on-week to 1.25 million mt as of April 1. Stocks fell 7,000 mt in Nanhai but rose 6,000 mt in Hangzhou, leaving overall inventories higher.

title: Vedanta plans to build $1.4bn copper smelter in India
summary: Vedanta plans a $1.4bn copper smelter project in India, seeking state government partners to develop a 500,000 tpa coastal complex near a port. The move follows a Supreme Court challenge after the closure of its 400,000 tpa Thoothukudi smelter. The announcement signals expanded copper processing capacity.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Kamoa-Kakula Mines and Stockpiles a Record Number of Tonnes of Copper Ore in March
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said its Kamoa-Kakula copper project in the DRC mined and stockpiled a record number of tonnes of copper ore in March and set a new monthly development record. Final assay results are pending, and a detailed update is due April 6, with first ore into the mill expected in July.

title: Copper touches lowest in nearly a month on China demand worries
summary: Copper prices fell to their lowest in nearly a month as investors worried about slowing China demand amid debt deleveraging and reduced stimulus. China factory data showed weaker growth in small firms, and LME inventories rose. The piece also flags aluminum supply worries lifting physical premiums, while LME aluminum rose modestly.

title: Brazil's Vale completes sale of New Caledonia nickel operations
summary: Vale has completed the sale of its nickel operations in New Caledonia. The announcement is directly tied to nickel supply but contains no information on changes to production levels, disruptions, or near-term supply constraints, so the net effect on nickel prices within days-to-weeks is likely limited.

title: Kamoa-Kakula Mines and Stockpiles a Record Number of Tonnes of Copper Ore in March
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says its Kamoa-Kakula Copper Project in the DRC mined and stockpiled a record amount of copper ore in March and set a monthly development record. Assays are pending, with a detailed progress update due April 6 and first ore into the mill targeted for July, supporting copper output expectations.

title: Codelco agrees 3-year labor deal at Radomiro Tomic copper complex
summary: Codelco agreed a three-year labor deal for the Radomiro Tomic copper complex. By resolving potential labour tensions, the agreement lowers the risk of output disruption and stabilizes near-term copper supply expectations, which can underpin prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Vale offloads New Caledonia nickel asset to Prony Resources consortium
summary: Vale has sold its stake in Vale New Caledonia, covering the Goro nickel mine and processing plant, to the Prony Resources consortium. The deal includes major funding support, continued offtake for nickel production, and a long-term nickel supply agreement. The transfer is framed as preserving operational continuity and jobs, not changing output immediately.

title: Alcoa completes sale of Warrick Rolling Mill to Kaiser Aluminum for $670M
summary: Alcoa has completed the $670M sale of its Warrick rolling mill and related assets to Kaiser Aluminum. Alcoa keeps about 269,000 metric tons of smelting capacity, power generating units, and land at the Warrick site, along with new commercial agreements to manage the transition.

title: Hudbay makes copper discovery near Rosemont in Arizona
summary: Hudbay’s Rosemont copper project in Arizona is highlighted following a reported copper discovery near the site. The article notes the company’s past acquisition aimed at advancing Rosemont into a major U.S. mine. The news is supportive for copper sentiment, though any supply effect is likely limited in the near term.

title: UEX hits high-grade cobalt-nickel mineralisation at West Bear
summary: UEX reported drill results showing high-grade cobalt-nickel mineralisation at its West Bear deposit in Saskatchewan. Highlights from the Michael Lake zone include intersections such as 9.5% (partial figure shown) in drillhole MIC-007. The news may modestly improve expectations for future nickel supply, supporting nickel sentiment near term.

title: Copper Fox Metals CEO: Presenting Exciting Opportunities Through Advanced-staged Copper Asset
summary: Copper Fox Metals’ CEO discusses updates for the Schaft Creek advanced-stage copper project in British Columbia. The company plans to release a resource estimate in early 2021 and later a Preliminary Economic Assessment using data from a prior feasibility study, highlighting exploration value drivers within its Teck Resources joint venture.

title: Shanghai copper gains as smelting activities drop
summary: Shanghai copper edged up as global smelting declined to the lowest levels in at least five years, driven by a shortage of copper feedstock concentrates. The report notes the supply squeeze partially offset weaker-than-expected refined demand in China, where Q2 demand season is approaching.

title: Shanghai copper posts weekly gain as smelting activity drops
summary: Shanghai copper rose as data showed global smelting activity fell to multi-year lows, driven by concentrate feedstock shortages. The supply squeeze outweighed indications of softer-than-expected refined copper demand in China. Analysts also flagged risks if second-quarter destocking is weaker than expected.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose 3,600 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for the seventh straight week, increasing by 3,600 mt to 385,600 mt as of Apr 2, helped by larger arrivals. Import loss stayed around 500 yuan/mt, while demand for customs declarations remained weak and foreign trade purchases were limited.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 345,000 wmt to 5.74 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 345,000 wmt from March 26 to 5.74 million wmt by April 2, with Ni-content stocks down to 45,000 mt. Seven major ports saw a 250,000 wmt decline. The downward trend should reverse as shipments recover in ~half a month.

title: Nickel downstream PMI rose to 52.44 in March_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said downstream nickel industries’ PMI rose to 52.44 in March, with production and new orders in stainless steel and electroplating rebounding after the CNY. Raw-material inventories expanded, supported by tight high-carbon ferrochrome supply. The battery segment weakened on high nickel sulphate prices, but overall activity improved.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 1,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data showed Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories fell by 1,000 mt week-on-week to 10,300 mt as of Apr 2. The import window closed, with some nickel plates still clearing customs and entering directly rather than bonded warehouses, contributing to altered stock trends in the bonded area.

title: Gold Price Correction Still "Healthy," Biden Coming for Copper
summary: The piece highlights Biden’s US$2 trillion American Jobs Plan and notes CRU Group’s estimate that copper demand could rise by 110,000–170,000 tonnes per year and aluminium demand by 130,000–220,000 tonnes over five years, depending on congressional approval. This supportive demand outlook is expected to pressure prices upward.

title: 'Dr. Copper'-linked ETFs show healthy gains
summary: Copper-linked ETFs rose sharply on Monday as investors increased exposure to copper on expectations of an economic rebound. The U.S. Copper Index Fund was up about 3.3% midday and the Global X Copper Miners ETF gained roughly 2.8%. Strong U.S. jobs growth and a record services activity survey supported the rally.

title: Copper Fox Announces IP Survey for Mineral Mountain Copper Project
summary: Copper Fox announced an induced polarization (chargeability/resistivity) survey at its Mineral Mountain copper project in Arizona to map copper mineralization depth and advance toward drill-ready status. The release is exploration-focused and does not mention production, supply changes, or pricing-related developments.

title: Chile's Codelco upped copper production 2.1% y/y in February - Cochilco
summary: Codelco increased its copper production to 122,800 tonnes in February, up 2.1% year-on-year, according to Chile’s Cochilco. The update signals slightly higher near-term mine supply from the world’s largest copper miner, which can marginally affect copper market expectations over coming days.

title: Chilean copper production down 5% in February, Cochilco says
summary: Chile’s state mining agency Cochilco says February copper production declined 5% versus the prior reference period. As Chile is a key global supplier, a reduction in output can affect expectations for prompt supply and inventories, typically creating near-term bearish pressure on copper prices.

title: Copper Prices Jump After Leading Producer Chile Closes Its Borders
summary: Copper prices jumped about 4% after Chile closed its borders for April amid a COVID-19 surge. Restrictions could disrupt mining by delaying truck/equipment movements and slow operations; Chile’s output already fell in February. Investors reprice near-term supply risk as Chile remains the top exporter.

title: Claims highly toxic waste buried at Tiwai Pt aluminium smelter
summary: Investigators are probing claims that highly toxic waste has been buried in unmapped sites at the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter, including spent cell liner waste containing cyanide and toxic fluoride that is banned from being buried untreated. Potential enforcement actions could disrupt operations and affect near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Copper hits 2-week high as top producer Chile closes border
summary: Copper rose to a two-week high as Chile, the world’s top producer, closed its border amid rising COVID-19 cases, raising supply concerns in a tight market. Three-month LME copper gained up to 3.6%. Aluminium and nickel also increased on broadly supportive industrial-metals sentiment.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 06/04: Over 2% gains for most LME base metals prices; aluminium rewarrantings continue
summary: A live LME futures report shows over 2% gains for most base metals prices. It specifically mentions aluminium rewarrantings continuing, suggesting ongoing warehouse/physical market activity. Separately, Fastmarkets notes procedural corrections to certain assessment methodologies, but the headline is broadly bullish near-term price action.

title: CAVU Mining Corp.: CAVU Mining Announces Hopper Porphyry Copper Option Agreement and Forward Stock Split
summary: CAVU Mining announced an option agreement to earn a 70% interest in the Hopper Copper Project in Yukon, describing copper porphyry and skarn mineralization and permitted drilling plans. The deal includes cash/share payments and work expenditures. The stock split is unrelated to commodity fundamentals.

title: Panoramic Resources approves restart of Savannah Nickel Project
summary: Panoramic Resources approved restarting the Savannah Nickel Project in Western Australia after operational strategy reviews. Underground development and production are set to resume in August, with mobilisation in July. The mine will produce nickel and copper (and cobalt) in concentrate, supporting improved near-term supply outlook.

title: Hudbay Minerals stock surges toward 7th-straight gain, after double upgrade at BofA amid bullish copper view
summary: Hudbay Minerals shares jumped 8.4% after BofA upgraded the copper producer from underperform to buy and boosted its target, citing a greatly improved outlook. The analyst pointed to better-than-expected 2022–2023 copper production and higher reserve replacement, alongside expectations for rising copper prices.

title: Kamoa-Kakula Shatters Previous Production Records, Mining 400,000 tonnes of ore Grading 5.36% Copper in March, Including 100,000 tonnes Grading 8.70% Copper from the Centre of the Kakula Mine
summary: Kamoa-Kakula in DRC mined a record 400,000 tonnes of ore in March (5.36% Cu), up 18% from February, and grew pre-production surface stockpiles to 2.56 million tonnes at 4.60% Cu. Commissioning for Phase 1 is progressing, with first copper production targeted for July 2021.

title: Analysis of the impact of the EU's imposition of temporary anti-dumping duties on Chinese aluminium extrusion _SMM
summary: The EU launched and later imposed anti-dumping duties on Chinese aluminium extrusions and some aluminium structures, initially 30.4%-48% and later 21.2%-32.1%. Chinese EU export volumes fell, but producers reported strong orders and rising operating rates. SMM concludes the duties should have limited impact on the aluminium extrusion market.

title: Mason PEA from Hudbay suggests potential to double copper output
summary: Hudbay’s preliminary economic assessment for its Mason porphyry copper project in Nevada outlines a large open-pit mine that could become among the biggest copper producers in the U.S. The plan suggests copper output could more than double, increasing expectations for future supply.

title: Crown Mining Corp.: Crown Mining Announces Completion of Name Change to US Copper Corp
summary: US Copper Corp (formerly Crown Mining Corp) completes its name change effective April 8, 2021, and trades under a new ticker. The release reiterates its Moonlight-Superior copper project in California and prior historical copper production, citing potential benefits from U.S. critical minerals supply strategy, with no new operational actions announced.

title: Chile's Codelco secures nod to extend life of Radomiro Tomic copper mine
summary: Codelco obtained environmental approval to extend the Radomiro Tomic copper mine’s operations to 2030, enabling an $882m expansion and new resource additions. The mine had been planned for closure in 2022. Codelco plans upgrades including bioleaching for low-grade minerals, despite acknowledging difficult conditions ahead.

title: Press Metal to ride on 'supercycle' of aluminium prices
summary: The article says aluminium and related building materials are entering a “supercycle” with prices set to rise for a lengthy period. It attributes momentum to massive government stimulus and infrastructure project rollouts after pandemic lockdowns, boosting expected aluminium demand in construction and materials markets.

title: Copper prices dip as premiums fall, inventories rise
summary: Copper prices fell as China premiums dropped and LME/ShFE inventories rose, pointing to a weaker-than-expected demand pickup in a key consumption season. The move was accompanied by declines in LME and ShFE aluminium and nickel prices, reflecting soft industrial-metal sentiment while traders watch upcoming data and earnings.

title: New batteries with aluminium anodes can effectively store renewable energy, says study
summary: A study reports a rechargeable battery using low-cost aluminium and carbon electrodes to store renewable energy, with claims of 10,000 cycles and improved deposition behavior that addresses aluminium’s reactivity issues. While it is presented as a potential alternative to lithium-ion, the article does not specify near-term commercialization.

title: Copper prices fall on weaker-than-expected China demand
summary: Copper prices fell as China demand disappointed expectations. The Yangshan premium declined and inventories rose at LME and ShFE warehouses, signaling weaker physical demand. With copper still relatively high, downstream buying stayed subdued, while fears of tighter Chinese policy added to pressure on prices.

title: Aluminium scrap prices to lack upward momentum in the short term_SMM
summary: SMM reports that import restrictions have reduced aluminium scrap supply, but high and volatile primary aluminium prices are discouraging downstream buying. Attempts to route cargoes via Guangdong were mostly rejected. Scrap prices are expected to meet resistance near term, with potential for later gains if tight supply and price transmission improve.

title: Surge Copper Acquires Strategic Land Position at Berg Project
summary: Surge Copper announced it acquired additional mineral claims at the Berg and Ootsa properties, consolidating its exploration target that shows a large copper-in-soil anomaly and historic porphyry copper intersections. It plans surface mapping and potential induced polarization work, but no production or supply changes were disclosed.

title: Canada Nickel Signs Memorandum of Understanding with Taykwa Tagamou Nation  for Mine Fleet Financing for the Crawford Nickel-Cobalt Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel signed an MoU with Taykwa Tagamou Nation to pursue favorable financing terms for the mine equipment fleet for the Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project and enable related training and jobs. The company also references power-grid steps to supply the mine. Better project financing visibility is modestly supportive for nickel.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Drills Massive Sulphide Nickel Mineralization in First Three Holes Drilled in New Target Area at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reports that its first three drill holes in the CGO West target area at the Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project intersected massive sulphide nickel-copper mineralization at shallow depths. Assay results are pending and the work is early-stage exploration intended to potentially expand resources.

title: U.S. Spending Big Dollars On Infrastructure Should be a Huge Boon for Copper Metals Market
summary: The piece suggests that renewed U.S. infrastructure spending should be a major positive catalyst for copper. It notes copper’s extensive use in electrical wiring and how highways, bridges, ports, and digital communications rely on copper, implying stronger demand expectations for the copper market.

title: Ridgestone Mining Inc.: Ridgestone Highlights IP Anomaly and High-Grade Copper at Rebeico
summary: Ridgestone Mining announced induced polarization and resistivity survey results at its Rebeico project in Sonora, Mexico, highlighting strong chargeability anomalies and surface copper assays up to 3.77% Cu plus additional high-grade intersections from previous drilling. The release is exploration-focused with no immediate supply impact data.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 7): Shanghai nonferrous metals declined for the most part, nickel advanced 0.37%_SMM
summary: SMM reports most SHFE nonferrous metals declined after overnight Wall Street losses: copper fell 0.49% and aluminium 0.46%, while nickel rose 0.37%. It cites stable market sentiment despite IMF upgrades and US job-vacancy data; monitoring of US trade continues. Mixed moves suggest limited net pressure.

title: Copper slips as inventories climb and China premiums dip
summary: Copper prices fell as inventories in LME warehouses rose sharply and premiums into China declined. Analysts linked the stock build and lower China pricing to weaker demand expectations and producer sell/hedging activity, while investor net longs were reduced. The report flags no immediate deficit support.

title: Top Copper Miner Is Boosting Output Amid a Chile Covid Surge
summary: The headline reports that the top copper miner is boosting output despite a COVID surge in Chile. The implication is that operations are being maintained or ramped up in the near term, affecting expectations for copper supply and production levels over the coming days to weeks.

title: Canada Nickel signs mine fleet financing agreement with Taykwa Tagamou Nation
summary: Canada Nickel signed an MOU with Taykwa Tagamou Nation to seek favourable financing for the mine’s electric heavy equipment fleet at the Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project. The partnership is intended to reduce initial capital requirements and support earlier startup alongside work with Glencore on processing routes.

title: Clean energy? The world's demand for copper could be catastrophic for communities and environments
summary: The piece argues the energy transition will require record copper but warns of a potential supply shortfall, implying higher copper prices. It also highlights sustainability and permitting risks—public opposition, lower-grade deeper mines, and sensitive locations—that could slow projects and affect future supply.

title: Codelco chief bullish on copper price
summary: Codelco’s chairman said copper prices are likely to remain strong, though new COVID-19 variants could bring volatility. Copper has reached near-decade highs, rising again after Chile tightened lockdowns due to infection spikes, with some analysts linking the move to supply-related concerns.

title: Indigenous advantages to be hammered out in Glencore bauxite mine deal for Aurukun
summary: Queensland officials discuss appointing Glencore as the preferred proponent to lease and develop an Aurukun-area bauxite deposit. The government emphasizes short-term job creation and community presence ahead of surveys and environmental work before any production phase. Content does not indicate near-term output changes.

title: Material Matters: Iron Ore, Gold & Copper
summary: The piece notes copper fell ~8% over the past month due to COVID-related lockdown risks, stronger USD, and tighter credit in China. However, Citi expects a deficit to become clearer within weeks, with inventory likely drawn down and physical prices supported in May-June.

title: Shanghai copper near 1-week low on signs of weakening demand
summary: Shanghai copper prices fell to their lowest in nearly a week as rising inventories and falling premiums in top consumer China signaled weakening demand. The most-traded May contract dropped as much as 1.2% to about 66,310 yuan/ton, with LME prices slightly higher amid a softer dollar.

title: Biden Commerce Secretary Says Trump's Steel and Aluminum Tariffs Saved American Jobs
summary: Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo said the Trump-era 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum helped “save American jobs” in the U.S. steel and aluminum industries. The remarks imply tariffs improved domestic producers’ competitiveness by reducing imports, which can support short-term aluminum market expectations. Copper effects are not mentioned.

title: MAX Resource Corp.: Max Resource Reports a Second New Copper Discovery at CESAR North, NE Colombia
summary: MAX Resource Corp. announced a second newly discovered copper zone (URU) within its Cesar North copper-silver project in northeastern Colombia, with mineralization over 3.7 km and assays pending. The release reinforces exploration progress but offers no production, pricing, or inventory impact for copper in the near term.

title: London copper picks up on weak dollar, U.S. infrastructure stimulus
summary: London copper rose 0.7% as the dollar weakened, supporting dollar-priced commodities. Prices were also lifted by hopes for higher U.S. industrial metals demand from Biden’s $2 trillion infrastructure proposal. Chinese concerns capped sentiment, while LME aluminum edged up and ShFE nickel rose.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 23,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows China’s primary aluminium ingot social inventories fell 23,000 mt week-on-week to 1.23 million mt as of April 8. The drop was mainly driven by declines in Gongyi and Nanhai. SHFE warrants and inventories across eight consumption areas decreased, signaling tighter nearby supply.

title: Emgold Mining Corporation: Kennecott Commences Diamond Drilling at the New York Canyon Copper Property, NV
summary: Emgold Mining said Kennecott Exploration has commenced diamond drilling at Emgold’s New York Canyon copper property in Nevada under an earn-in/joint-venture agreement. The program includes five holes targeting several copper-related targets, plus UAV magnetic surveying, but no resource or production changes were announced.

title: Calibre Mining Corp.: Rio Tinto Exploration and Calibre Mining Initiate 2021 Exploration Program Including 5,500 Metre Drilling Campaign Prioritizing Prospective Near-Surface Copper and Copper-Gold Mineralization
summary: Calibre and Rio Tinto initiate a 2021 exploration program at the Borosi project in Nicaragua, planning 5,500 metres of drilling to test near-surface copper and copper-gold porphyry/skarn targets, including Primavera-linked areas. The release discusses drilling plans and prior geochemical results but no production or supply impact.

title: Canada Nickel initiates the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment of the Crawford Nickel Cobalt Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel says it has begun the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment for its Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project, hiring Golder/Wood for environmental studies and TES for community engagement. The company expects a feasibility study later and is progressing permitting, but no operational or supply update is provided.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Kamoa Copper Appoints Ben Munanga as Chairman of the Board Ahead of First Production at the Tier-One Kamoa-Kakula Copper Mine in The DRC
summary: Ivanhoe Mines’ Kamoa Copper appoints Ben Munanga as board chairman as the Kamoa-Kakula copper mine approaches first production in July 2021. The release also references hydropower plant upgrades supplying Phase 1/2 output, but provides no new disruption or capacity guidance beyond planned development timelines.

title: Copper climbs on supply concerns, lower dollar
summary: Copper rose 0.8% to about $8,988 as concerns over mine supply disruptions tightened concentrate treatment charges and a weaker U.S. dollar supported demand. LME inventories have doubled since early March, capping gains, while markets await China trade data. Aluminium and nickel also rose.

title: Torq Resources Inc.: Torq Commences Exploration on its Margarita Iron-Oxide-Copper-Gold Project in Northern Chile
summary: Torq Resources began a three-month exploration program on its Margarita iron-oxide-copper-gold project in northern Chile, using mapping, induced polarization geophysics, and soil sampling to define drill targets. The company plans to seek drill permits and start drilling in Q3 2021, aiming to locate copper sulphide sources.

title: Salazar Resources : Adventus And Salazar Provide Pijili Project Exploration Update – Preparing For New Copper-Gold Drill Targets At The Rosa De Oro And Carmen De Pijili Concessions
summary: Adventus and Salazar provided an exploration update at Ecuador’s Pijili project (Rosa de Oro and Carmen de Pijili), reporting regional copper results from grab and soil sampling and identifying drill-ready targets later in 2021. The work focuses on defining copper porphyry potential; no production or supply disruptions are announced.

title: Fabled Silver Gold Corp: Fabled Amends and Restates Copper Option Agreements and Acquires Additional Claims
summary: Fabled Silver Gold Corp. amended and restated option agreements for its Neil and Toro copper properties in northern BC and gained the right to acquire additional claims to form the expanded Muskwa copper property. The amendment reduces total costs by removing advance royalty payments and consolidates control of the district’s copper occurrences.

title: Copper climbs on supply concerns and lower dollar
summary: Copper prices rose about 1% as concerns over tighter available supply—driven by mine disruptions that cut treatment charges—combined with a lower U.S. dollar to boost bullish sentiment. LME inventories increased and rising cash-vs-3-month premiums capped gains, while China trade data was awaited.

title: White Metal Resources Corp.: White Metal Reports 45 Metres Grading 2.02% Cu and 33 g/t Ag from Second Set of RC Drill Hole Results, Taranis Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Resources announced additional RC drilling results from its Okohongo Cu-Ag deposit in Namibia, including 45 metres grading 2.02% copper. The company plans to update resources and seek a partner to advance the project. The article is an exploration update without any stated near-term production impact.

title: Chile's border shutdown won't affect China's copper imports from Australia: analysts
summary: The article says analysts expect Chile’s border shutdown to have no meaningful effect on China’s copper imports from Australia. While it references a copper rally above $9,000/ton and a broader jump in base metals, the key takeaway is that the Chile disruption should not tighten China’s copper supply.

title: White Metal Reports 45 Metres Grading 2.02% Cu and 33 g/t Ag from Second Set of RC Drill Hole Results, Taranis Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Resources reported assay results from additional RC drill holes at its Taranis Copper-Silver project in Namibia, confirming historical Okohongo Cu-Ag targets. The samples include 2.02% Cu over 45 metres in one hole, supporting continued confidence in copper potential and plans to update the resource.

title: China's CNGR to make nickel matte in Indonesia as battery demand grows
summary: CNGR said it will build a nickel matte joint venture in Indonesia, with production capacity of 30,000 tonnes per year across an initial phase of 10,000 tonnes. Nickel matte is an intermediate product for battery-grade nickel. The move adds supply expectations as Indonesian nickel ore export bans support smelting demand.

title: COVID-19: Top copper supplier boosts output amid COVID surge
summary: Codelco said Chile’s COVID resurgence and tighter restrictions will not disrupt its copper operations, and first-quarter output rose. However, fresh border measures for truck drivers and citizens sparked supply jitters, briefly lifting copper to a two-week high. Strong export revenue further supports bullish sentiment near term.

title: Rio Tinto Exploration and Calibre Mining Initiate 2021 Exploration Program Including 5,500 Metre Drilling Campaign Prioritizing Prospective Near-Surface Copper and Copper-Gold Mineralization
summary: Calibre Mining and Rio Tinto announce a 2021 5,500-metre drilling and orientation survey at the Borosi project in Nicaragua, targeting near-surface copper and copper-gold porphyry/skarn mineralization. The update is exploratory with reconnaissance drilling planned, offering limited immediate implications for copper supply or demand.

title: Copper on track for weekly rise as dollar weakens
summary: Copper was on track for a weekly rise as the dollar weakened, making greenback-priced metals cheaper. LME three-month copper rose and SHFE May copper gained, while LME aluminium edged lower and Shanghai nickel and aluminium increased. The dollar fell on European data strength, weak U.S. jobs, and a dovish Fed.

title: Gianni Kovacevic: Is Copper Headed for its Biggest Bull Market?
summary: Gianni Kovacevic of CopperBank Resources says copper is positioned for an unusually strong bull market, driven by electrification and US infrastructure plans. He cites electricity use as a growing share of copper demand and suggests supply may struggle to keep up, supporting expectations of much higher copper prices.

title: China's CNGR to produce nickel matte in $243mln Indonesian project
summary: CNGR plans to produce nickel matte at a $243 million project in Indonesia. By expanding nickel upstream production capacity, the move is expected to bolster supply expectations for nickel and may support prices in the near term as markets anticipate improved availability.

title: The main force of Shanghai Copper opened low and rebounded as a whole._SMM
summary: Shanghai copper (2105) opened lower and rebounded, closing slightly down (~-0.07%), with LME copper up modestly. Market focus includes Fed/infrastructure expectations and weaker Chile copper output. Spot and inventories show tight supply but demand remains weak, keeping near-term price pressure mixed and mostly neutral.

title: Copper falls as China inflation fuels fears of credit tightening
summary: Copper fell for the day on the LME, reversing some weekly gains, as China’s inflation beat expectations and raised fears that Beijing could tighten monetary/credit policy. The piece cites weaker macro sentiment and reports LME aluminum down and nickel mixed, indicating broader pressure on industrial metals.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell 300 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell 300 mt week-on-week to 385,300 mt as of April 9, driven by smaller inbound arrivals. With the import window closed and Yangshan premium easing, some cargoes were shifted into bonded warehouses. Stocks are expected to trend upward later.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 255,000 wmt to 5.48 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 255,000 wmt to 5.48 million wmt between April 2 and April 9, with Ni content stocks down to 43,000 mt. Stocks remain in a downward trend and are near historically low levels, implying tighter feedstock supply.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 300 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories fell by 300 mt from the prior week to 10,000 mt as of April 9, marking the sixth consecutive weekly decline. Russian nickel imports were lower, though nickel briquettes and some LME flows continued into bonded warehouses.

title: Auginish Alumina secures approval for Foynes expansion
summary: Aughinish Alumina received approval to fast-track planning for expansions at its Foynes, Ireland alumina plant, including additional bauxite residue disposal capacity to prevent capacity limits and extended salt-cake disposal. The move supports continued alumina refining, a key input into aluminium production, and could be mildly supportive for aluminium prices.

title: Reality check for copper bulls as Chinese demand growth slows
summary: Copper bulls face pullback risk as Chinese demand growth in the traditional Q2 industrial season is delayed. Speculators have cut long exposure after the Feb peak, while premiums and end-user purchasing sentiment weaken. Analysts cite rising supply expectations and scrap substitution, with some forecasting prices falling toward ~$6,000-$7,000 before support.

title: Huntsman Exploration Inc.: Huntsman to Host Investor Webcast to Discuss Recent Results at Canegrass Nickel Sulphide Project In Australia and Upcoming Exploration Activities
summary: Huntsman Exploration will host an investor webcast to discuss recent high-grade nickel and copper assay results from its Canegrass nickel sulphide project in Australia and plans for the next phase of drilling. The article is primarily a company update with no explicit changes to near-term production or supply flows.

title: Huntsman to Host Investor Webcast to Discuss Recent Results at Canegrass Nickel Sulphide Project In Australia and Upcoming Exploration Activities - Press Release
summary: Huntsman will host an investor webcast to discuss recent results from its Canegrass nickel sulphide project in Australia and plans for upcoming exploration. Project updates can affect expectations for future nickel supply, but the snippet does not include material production, cost, or reserve details.

title: Copper heads for weekly gain despite dip on China policy fears
summary: Copper eased 0.3% on Friday as strong China inflation fueled fears of tighter monetary policy and a stronger dollar, weighing on metals. However, expected supply tightness and infrastructure/electrification demand supported a weekly gain. The piece also notes weaker China aluminum inflows and shows LME aluminum and nickel slightly lower.

title: District Copper Corp: District Provides Update on Copper Keg Project, Kamloops Mining District
summary: District Copper provides an update on expanding and advancing exploration at its Copper Keg porphyry-style copper project in British Columbia. The company will mobilize crews for prospecting, mapping, and a deep IP survey. The release outlines historic copper indications but no production or immediate supply impact.

title: Aluminium batteries take a step closer
summary: Cornell researchers report a way to prevent short-circuiting in aluminium batteries by using oxidised carbon fibres (and related coatings for stainless steel) to regulate aluminium electrodeposition morphology. Cells show over 99% aluminium return over many cycles, improving prospects for large-scale energy storage.

title: Tesla's Biggest Competitor Is Ditching Nickel And Cobalt
summary: BYD confirmed it will go all-in on LFP batteries and drop NCM (nickel-cobalt-manganese) across its model lineup, citing safety and cost advantages. BMO said the move is a net negative for nickel and cobalt demand. This should weigh on nickel demand expectations in the near term.

title: Material Matters: Nickel, Oil, Silver, Iron ore, Copper
summary: The piece covers market views on nickel and copper. Citi trimmed nickel price forecasts after Tsingshan expanded conversion into “class 2,” indicating more supply and lower medium-term prices, though it still expects some near-term upside. Copper is described as rallying ~3% on stronger US growth optimism, despite rising LME stocks that could temper gains.

title: Material Matters: Nickel, Oil, Silver, Iron ore, Copper
summary: Citi trimmed nickel price forecasts by 6–15% after Tsingshan’s move into “class 2” conversion weakened the medium-term nickel bull case, projecting lower prices into 2022 and beyond. Separately, copper rose nearly 3% on US jobs/infrastructure optimism, though LME stockpiles rising may temper gains.

title: Vedanta signs MoU with research institutes for value-creation from bauxite residue
summary: Vedanta signed an MoU with CSIR-NML, IMMT, and JNARDDC to develop technologies for valuing bauxite residue (red mud), including REE enrichment and recovery of alumina, iron, titanium and related elements. The project targets circular-economy waste reduction and downstream value, potentially supporting aluminium producer sentiment.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 12/04: LME nickel price falls 2.8%; zinc stocks up 5% following deliveries in Asia
summary: A live LME futures report notes nickel down 2.8%. It also includes Fastmarkets methodology and database updates, including corrections to certain low-carbon aluminium and aluminium 6063 billet premium assessments. While aluminium adjustments are procedural, the only clear immediate price move described is bearish for nickel.

title: CATL to acquire stake in Kisanfu copper-cobalt mine in DRC for $137m
summary: CATL’s unit will buy a 25% stake in CMOC’s Kisanfu copper-cobalt mine in the DRC for about $137.5m, with joint plans to fund project capex. The mine is undeveloped and is expected to supply copper and cobalt long term, implying limited immediate price impact.

title: Limited orders at copper rod companies using copper cathode as feedstock_SMM
summary: SMM says April copper rod consumption initially looked promising, but orders turned unexpectedly weak after the Qingming Festival. Wires and cables demand remains insufficient, cathode-based rod plants cut rates or delay restart, and buyers shift toward secondary-copper rods as the cathode vs scrap price gap stays around 2,000 yuan/mt. A near-term pickup is unlikely.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 12): Shanghai nonferrous metals fell across the board, nickel dropped 3.58%_SMM
