summary: SMM reported broad declines in Shanghai nonferrous metals on April 12. Copper fell 1.76%, nickel dropped 3.58% and aluminium slipped 0.66%, tracking weaker global sentiment. The piece attributes bearish tone to subdued bullish market expectations amid macro factors and upcoming Eurozone retail sales data.

title: BHP to ride EV, green power revolution as copper, nickel demand set to soar
summary: BHP forecasts copper demand could double and nickel could quadruple as faster EV adoption and renewable energy rollouts increase consumption of these metals. It cites favourable EV policy signals and mentions copper strength, attributing gains to growth and infrastructure/decarbonisation spending, supporting bullish sentiment for copper and nickel.

title: BHP to ride EV, green power revolution as copper, nickel demand set to soar
summary: BHP says net-zero policies and EV, solar and wind expansion will drive much higher copper and nickel demand. It links EVs to higher copper intensity and infrastructure needs, and notes copper prices have surged. It also highlights BHP’s increased nickel/copper exposure and favorable policy signals.

title: Abu Dhabi Mubadala invested record amount in 2020, eyes aluminium IPO -CEO
summary: Abu Dhabi state investor Mubadala said it invested a record amount in 2020 and is close to deciding on an IPO for Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA). The CEO called EGA a mature, low-cost business, noting the listing had been delayed previously. The news supports aluminium sentiment via improved growth prospects.

title: Copper loses ground on fears of Chinese commodities price caps
summary: Copper fell 0.6% as markets feared China may implement commodity price caps to contain inflation, while demand concerns and rising inventories added pressure. Chinese PPI inflation data and Premier Li’s comments reinforced regulatory fears. Nickel also eased on Nornickel restarting a flooded mine earlier than expected.

title: Analysis of the future development direction of secondary aluminium industry_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s carbon-neutrality push and secondary aluminium’s energy intensity put recycled output in focus. It outlines two development paths: better recycling of wrought alloys and improved casting alloy performance. It notes most secondary casting remains dominant short term and flags policy risks (imported raw material, ash treatment, tax invoices).

title: Arizonans attend board meeting of international company proposing copper mine at Oak Flat
summary: Activists and coalitions opposed Rio Tinto’s proposed Resolution Copper project at Oak Flat, highlighting lawsuits over religious freedoms and environmental concerns such as groundwater use and contamination risk. The opposition and legal actions could delay copper supply development, supporting near-term expectations for tighter copper availability.

title: China March copper imports rise as demand holds firm
summary: China’s March copper imports rose 25% year-on-year to 552,317 tonnes, customs data showed, up 34.7% from February’s 13-month low. The increase suggests demand held up despite disruptions to shipments from top producer Chile, which could reinforce bullish near-term expectations for copper supply-demand tightness.

title: China March copper imports rise 25% from year ago on firm demand
summary: China’s March copper imports rose 25% year on year to 552,317 tonnes and first-quarter imports hit 1.44 million tonnes, the highest since at least 2008. Copper concentrate imports also reached record levels amid globally tight supply. China’s unwrought aluminum exports fell 14.5% year on year.

title: Prices of nickel sulphate stabilised, narrower premiums over nickel briquette_SMM
summary: SMM says nickel rose slightly last week due to macro factors, supporting battery-grade nickel sulphate, which stabilized around 31,000–32,000 yuan/mt. Spot trades were quieter and premiums of nickel sulphate over first-grade nickel narrowed further, with profit margins for nickel sulphate produced via MHP and briquettes falling.

title: Nickel prices supported by macro sentiment, forward surplus and short-term stable consumption is expected_SMM
summary: SMM reports nickel prices rose last week mainly on easing US Treasury yields and stronger macro sentiment, but nickel fundamentals remain weak: sluggish spot trading, NPI price softness, and expectations of continued April surplus. LME briquette inventories fell, yet domestic transactions weakened. CNGR’s supply expansion is seen bearish for forward balance.

title: Proactive news headlines including Walkabout Resources, Peninsula Energy, Castillo Copper and Alto Metals
summary: Proactive reports that Castillo Copper is preparing to resume drilling at its Mt Oxide copper project in the Mt Isa Copper Belt after reviewing historical data to enhance exploration potential. Other headlines cited (graphite, titanium, uranium, gold, gold-silver) do not directly involve tracked copper market fundamentals.

title: Copper falls on rising inventories, fear of China's price control
summary: Copper prices fell as LME-approved inventories rose, pressuring sentiment. Market worries that China may introduce price-control measures for inflation/cost management added to the decline. Although Q1 copper imports were strong, traders viewed the news as largely priced in, anticipating further downside before potential buying opportunities.

title: Surge Copper Appoints Paul Chawrun and Steve Blower to Technical Advisory Committee for the Advancement of its Ootsa & Berg Projects
summary: Surge Copper Corp. announced appointments to a technical advisory committee to support exploration and development at its Ootsa and Berg projects. Both projects are advanced-stage copper porphyry systems with pit-constrained copper resources adjacent to the Huckleberry copper mine. The update is operational but does not signal imminent supply or policy changes.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 13): Shanghai nonferrous metals declined for the most part, aluminium advanced 1.87%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous prices mostly fell on April 13: copper ended slightly lower, nickel dropped 2.23%, while aluminium advanced about 1.87%. It cites muted US sentiment, cautious market positioning, and contract-by-contract open interest changes. Overall moves are mixed across the three metals.

title: EU slaps import duties on Chinese aluminium; accuses Beijing of dumping
summary: The EU has slapped import duties on Chinese aluminium after accusing Beijing of dumping. The measures are intended to counter unfair pricing and curb Chinese supply into the European market, potentially reshaping near-term aluminium import flows and benchmark price expectations over coming days.

title: NORNICKEL TO EXPAND SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION AT NN HARJAVALTA IN FINLAND
summary: Nornickel said it will expand its NN Harjavalta nickel refinery in Finland, boosting output from 65 ktpa to 75 ktpa in 2023 and to over 100 ktpa by early 2026. The project targets growing European demand for battery metals and is powered by renewable energy and recycling.

title: Nornickel to boost output of nickel products in Finland for EV battery market
summary: Nornickel plans to boost production of nickel products, including nickel sulphate solution, at its Harjavalta plant in Finland to serve a growing EV battery materials cluster. Output is slated to rise from 65,000 tonnes to at least 75,000 tonnes by 2023 and over 100,000 tonnes by 2026, including higher sulphate volumes.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Intersects 138.18 Meters (453.35 Feet) Grading 2.26% Nickel Equivalent at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reported drill hole 20TK0277 at its Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in Minnesota intersecting 138.18m grading 1.66% nickel and 1.02% copper, including a higher-grade core above 3% nickel. The company expects improved resource grade/length but provides no near-term production update.

title: Nornickel expands environmentally friendly Harjavalta plant production
summary: Norilsk Nickel (Nornickel) plans to gradually expand its Harjavalta refinery in Finland, using renewable power and high-yield hydro-metallurgical processes to increase battery-grade nickel output. Capacity is targeted to rise from 65,000 tpa to 75,000 tpa in an initial phase and to over 100,000 tpa by 2026, supporting EU demand for low-carbon battery materials.

title: Pan Global Reports New Drill Results and Extends near Surface High Grade Copper at Escacena Project, Southern Spain
summary: Pan Global reported additional drill results at its Escacena (La Romana) project, extending near-surface high-grade copper mineralization over a ~700m strike length and confirming continuity to the east. Several intervals show elevated CuEq grades, with drilling ongoing and assay results pending for more holes.

title: Talon Metals Intersects 138.18 Meters Grading 2.26% Nickel Equivalent at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reported drill hole 20TK0277 at its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project intersecting 138.18 meters grading 1.66% Ni and 1.02% Cu, including a higher-grade 39 meters at 3.12% Ni and 1.60% Cu. Management says results exceed expectations and require follow-up drilling.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 13/04: Lower Dollar Index pushes aluminium close to 2021 high; zinc up 1%
summary: A LIVE futures market recap notes that a lower Dollar Index is supporting aluminium prices, pushing the metal close to the 2021 high. The piece also mentions zinc rising, but zinc is not tracked here. It contains Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin operational update items beyond the price move.

title: Chile to reap benefits of multibillion-dollar copper investment
summary: Chile’s mining minister expects copper output to rise to 5.9 million tonnes in 2021 and exceed six million tonnes in 2022 as Codelco and private projects ramp up. The government says existing mining taxes are adequate, citing regulatory stability and increased exploration activity.

title: Billionaire Investor Sees Copper as a National Security Issue
summary: Billionaire Robert Friedland says copper is vital for electrification and “national security,” pointing to years of underinvestment and the difficulty of replacing fossil-fuel supply with adequate metal inputs. He notes deteriorating ore quality and the need for major grid spending, implying supportive demand and tighter supply for copper.

title: Mayor Of Superior Says Town Needs Copper Mine, Urges Bill Rejection
summary: Superior’s mayor urges Congress to reject a bill that would halt Resolution Copper’s planned mine near Oak Flat. The project faces opposition from tribes over potential desecration of a sacred site and a proposed land-exchange rescission. Blocking the mine would tighten projected copper supply, potentially lifting copper prices.

title: Shanghai aluminum near 10-year high on Chinese production curb fears
summary: Shanghai aluminium rose, with the May contract near a 10-year high, as traders feared China could curb aluminium output in Xinjiang to meet pollution-control environmental targets. LME aluminium also hit multi-year highs. Inventories have fallen, though remain elevated versus early-year levels.

title: Bauxite prices in north China to rise on environmental inspections in Shanxi and Henan_SMM
summary: SMM reports bauxite prices in northern China may rise as environmental inspections tighten mining requirements in Shanxi and Henan, shifting “mine while treating” to “mine after pollution treatment.” Supply is expected to tighten in Q2, while alumina production is set to resume, boosting bauxite demand and supporting prices.

title: Shanghai aluminium near 10-year high on Chinese production curb fears
summary: Aluminium prices rose sharply, with Shanghai near a 10-year high, driven by fears China will limit output to meet environmental targets. Traders discussed possible Xinjiang curbs for energy-intensive aluminium, while inventories fell at LME/ShFE despite still-elevated levels, reinforcing short-term supply-tightness expectations.

title: Shanghai aluminum near 10-year high on Chinese supply fear
summary: Shanghai and LME aluminium rose toward multi-year highs as traders flagged fears China may curb aluminium output, particularly in Xinjiang, to meet green/pollution targets. The report links price gains to constrained expansion of energy-intensive capacity, expectations of a market deficit, and falling combined inventories despite higher stockpiles year-to-date.

title: Indonesia mulls another copper smelter with Enfi | News
summary: Indonesia’s government has tapped China Enfi Engineering to develop a new copper smelter in Fakfak Regency, West Papua. The plan would expand Indonesia’s copper refining capacity, which may bolster expectations for copper supply and processing, supporting near-term copper price sentiment over the coming weeks.

title: Shanghai aluminium near 10-year high on Chinese supply fear
summary: Shanghai aluminium surged toward a near 10-year high as traders feared China’s green-policy drive could limit aluminium output, particularly in energy-intensive regions such as Xinjiang. LME prices also advanced. The move was supported by falling combined aluminium inventories, even though stockpiles remain above early-year levels.

title: Copper smelter terms at rock bottom as mine squeeze hits: Andy Home
summary: Copper’s rally has stalled, but physical tightness is shifting upstream: lack of mine concentrates has driven treatment and refining charges to record lows and squeezed smelter margins. Chinese smelter maintenance downtime is set to rise, potentially reducing refined copper output during a seasonally strong demand period.

title: Aluminum Extrusion Market Latest Trends On The Basis Of  Product, Application, Region And Forecast To 2028
summary: The article discusses latest trends in the aluminum extrusion market by product, application, region, and a forecast to 2028. While it signals ongoing demand for extruded aluminium products, the provided excerpt contains no concrete near-term data on inventories, production disruptions, or pricing that would clearly drive spot moves within days.

title: BeMetals Corp.: BeMetals Returns Further Positive Drilling Results from Pangeni Copper Project
summary: BeMetals announced additional positive drilling intersections at its Pangeni Copper Project in Zambia, including grades around 0.39%–0.37% Cu over shallow intervals, plus newly identified targets for follow-up drilling. The company also notes accelerated 2021 exploration funding via JOGMEC. The news is exploration-focused and not a near-term production supply event.

title: Forum Energy Metals Corp.: Rio Tinto Completes Winter Drill Program at Forum's Janice Lake Copper/Silver Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals said Rio Tinto Exploration Canada completed winter drilling at its 100% owned Janice Lake copper/silver project in Saskatchewan, with first assay results expected in May. Drilling was cut short due to late winter, and results are pending, implying no immediate supply disruption.

title: Playfair Mining Ltd.: Playfair Prepares for Drilling at RKV Copper Project, Norway
summary: Playfair Mining says it has filed drill notifications and will drill seven targets at its RKV copper project in South Central Norway. The targets show strong MMI Cu anomalies (multiple readings above 6,000 ppb and up to 53,300 ppb), suggesting likely weathering copper sulphides and improving exploration expectations for copper.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 14): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, nickel fell 0.35%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous trading on Apr 14: aluminium rose 1.82% and copper gained 0.47% on the day, while nickel fell 0.35%. Coverage notes open-interest changes but offers no major new supply/demand driver, implying only mild, already-contained price pressure for copper, aluminium, and nickel.

title: FOCUS: High-stakes labor negotiations await Chile's copper miners in H2 2021
summary: The piece highlights that Chilean copper miners face high-stakes labor negotiations in H2 2021. Such negotiations can increase near-term uncertainty over potential disruptions to mining output. This supply-risk sensitivity typically weighs on copper price expectations over the following days to weeks.

title: Rio Tinto Completes Winter Drill Program at Forum's Janice Lake Copper/Silver Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals says Rio Tinto Exploration Canada completed winter drilling on the Janice Lake copper/silver project in Saskatchewan. Nine holes totaling 2,330 metres were drilled at the Rafuse target, investigating down-dip mineralization. Assay results are expected in May, with a potential June drilling resumption. No assay results are released now.

title: Shortage Of Copper Wiring Impacting Utah's Already Hot Housing Market
summary: Utah home builders face an acute shortage of construction materials, with copper wiring highlighted as particularly constrained. An electrical contractor says the issue is the worst he has seen in 20 years. Reuters notes copper is expected to rise toward record levels due to strong demand and limited supply, pressuring prices.

title: London copper declines on rising inventories
summary: London copper fell as LME-approved warehouse inventories extended higher, weighing on the three-month contract. Nickel dipped on the day, while aluminium climbed to multi-year highs amid concerns about potential China output cuts for carbon-emissions reasons. A weaker dollar also capped gains.

title: Huntsman Exploration (TSX.V: HMAN) takes control of the Canegrass Nickel Sulphide project in Australia
summary: Huntsman Exploration exercised an option to take 100% control of the Canegrass nickel sulphide project in Western Australia. The article highlights near-surface and deeper drill intercepts with high-grade nickel and associated copper, plus ongoing drilling and surveys. It also frames nickel demand/EV drivers as supportive for prices.

title: Aluminum Jumps to Highest Since 2018 on Strong China Trade Data
summary: Aluminium prices rose to the highest level since 2018, with the move linked to strong China trade data. The implication is that better trade readings support expectations for near-term industrial and construction demand for aluminium, pressuring prices upward over the coming days.

title: Supply woes in China, Russia fuel aluminum prices to multi-year highs
summary: Aluminum prices surged to near multi-year highs as supply worries intensified. China’s carbon/energy curbs in Inner Mongolia prompted closures and shutdowns of smelting and some plants, while investors tracked potential renewed U.S. sanctions on Russia’s major producer Rusal. The reduced supply outlook boosted both Shanghai and LME aluminum contracts.

title: Brodrick's Bets: How to Play Aluminum
summary: The piece argues that global stimulus measures are boosting demand expectations for aluminum. It explains aluminum’s energy-intensive smelting, major production regions, and investment vehicles including an aluminum-focused base-metals fund and Alcoa. It also notes that copper may move similarly within a basket, suggesting broadly bullish sentiment.

title: Aluminium billet inventories shrank 15,800 mt to 165,200 mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows China’s social inventories of 6063 aluminium billet fell 15,800 mt WoW to 165,200 mt by Apr 15. Shipments rose, downstream restocked as demand improved, while railway container shortages in northwest China and higher transport fees in Guangxi reduced billet arrivals. Inventories are expected to decline slightly next week.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 15): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, nickel fell 0.26%_SMM
summary: SMM says most SHFE nonferrous contracts rose on Apr 15, with copper up 2.64% and aluminium up 2.78%. Blast-furnace operating rates improved versus a week ago, while 6063 aluminium billet stocks in major consumption regions fell to 165,200 mt, supporting tight supply and bullish sentiment. Nickel was slightly down.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Royalty Options the Copper Warrior Project in Utah to Warrior Metals Inc.
summary: EMX Royalty executed an option agreement with Warrior Metals for the Copper Warrior copper project in Utah, providing cash/share payments and exploration work commitments. EMX will retain a 2% NSR royalty if the option is exercised. The project is in the Paradox Basin near the Lisbon Valley copper mine.

title: EMX Royalty Options the Copper Warrior Project in Utah to Warrior
summary: EMX Royalty executed an option agreement with Warrior Metals for the Copper Warrior copper project in Utah. The earn-in requires payments and exploration expenditures, after which EMX retains a 2% NSR royalty. The geology resembles nearby Lisbon Valley copper operations, but no near-term production impact is stated.

title: Huntsman Exploration Inc.: Huntsman Discusses Canegrass Nickel Sulphide Project Results with Newexco on GlobalMeet Webcast
summary: Huntsman Exploration hosted a webcast reviewing recent drilling on its 100% owned Canegrass nickel sulphide property in Australia and discussed upcoming activities. The company described strong results and optimism about the project. The release focuses on exploration progress, with no immediate production or inventory data provided.

title: Serbia orders Zijin Mining to cease work at copper mine
summary: Serbia has ordered Zijin Mining to stop work at the RTB Bor copper mine over environmental non-compliance and to fast-track a wastewater treatment plant to protect the River Pek. The action follows prior orders affecting parts of the operation, raising near-term copper supply disruption risk.

title: Times of Zambia   |  Zambia's rating, high copper prices can turn economic fortunes – Siliya
summary: Zambia’s government says Fitch Ratings’ improved sovereign rating to CCC, alongside high copper prices internationally, could help reverse the country’s economic fortunes. The piece highlights the role of copper price strength in Zambia’s outlook, but does not describe a new copper supply or demand event.

title: Resolution Copper mine would help solve America's copper crunch
summary: The opinion piece says proposed federal legislation could overturn a 2015 land-exchange authorization and effectively shut the Resolution Copper mine in Arizona. It presents the mine as vital to easing a U.S. copper crunch for clean-energy infrastructure, implying reduced future supply would be supportive for copper prices.

title: Alcoa Q1 Profit Trumps Street View As Aluminum Shipments And Prices Rise
summary: Alcoa’s Q1 profit more than doubled as aluminum and alumina shipments and realized prices rose. The company cited higher aluminum and alumina prices and increased shipment volumes as key drivers of revenue. It also signaled stronger demand expectations for 2021, supporting near-term sentiment for aluminum prices.

title: Peru Candidate Seeks More From Mining But Not State Control
summary: Peru’s presidential winner Pedro Castillo is said to seek renegotiated mining contracts and a bigger government/profit share without nationalizing companies. Investors’ concerns about higher fiscal take and project risk could reduce future copper supply growth. Analysts note Peru’s importance in global mined copper and expect potential price support.

title: Nornickel to Expand Sustainable Production at NN Harjavalta in Finland
summary: Nornickel plans to ramp up production at its NN Harjavalta nickel refinery in Finland, which is powered largely by renewable energy. Capacity is expected to rise from 65 ktpa to 75 ktpa in 2023 and exceed 100 ktpa by early 2026 to meet growing European EV battery raw-material demand.

title: Material Matters: Gold, Thermal Coal & Alumina
summary: The article reports broker optimism for copper and aluminium, citing Goldman Sachs upgrades and forecasts for higher 2022 prices and long-term deficits on renewables-driven demand. For aluminium/alumina, it discusses freight-driven alumina weakness but expects China demand to rise, potentially supporting alumina and influencing aluminium market sentiment.

title: London copper dips but set for weekly gain
summary: London copper fell slightly after China growth and manufacturing data came in weaker than expected, but it remains on track for a weekly gain. Banks including Goldman Sachs and Citi turned more bullish, raising/endorsing copper targets for the next few weeks. Aluminium prices are also reported amid China output dynamics.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell 1,800 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said Shanghai bonded copper stocks fell 1,800 mt to 383,500 mt over the past week, extending a two-week decline. With the import window closed and import-loss costs mostly above 400 yuan/mt, customs demand did not lift inflows. Lower inbound volumes and weaker foreign trade demand reduced inventories; some shipments were redirected abroad.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 135,000 wmt to 5.62 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data shows nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 135,000 wmt to 5.62 million wmt between April 9-16, with Ni content up to 44,000 mt. It cites resumed shipments from Surigao and potentially higher Philippine flows, alongside sharply lower nickel ore prices and expectations of further stockpiling.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 16/04: LME nickel, lead rise, while copper consolidates after Thursday surge
summary: Live futures coverage reports that LME nickel rose on 16/04, signaling near-term bullish pressure for nickel. Copper is described as consolidating after a Thursday surge, suggesting the immediate post-rally move is slowing or stabilizing rather than trending higher or lower.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 16/04: LME nickel, lead rise, while copper consolidates after Thursday surge
summary: A live LME futures report notes that nickel futures are rising, while copper is consolidating following Thursday’s surge. It also includes procedural updates to Fastmarkets’ metal assessment publications, but the immediate market call is the mixed near-term price action between nickel strength and copper digestion.

title: Chilean Metals, Inc.: Chilean Metals Arranges $2 Million Financing To Explore Nisk Nickel Project
summary: Chilean Metals arranged $2 million in equity financing to fund an initial drill program at the Nisk nickel project in Quebec, aiming to expand a historical Ni-Cu resource and develop potential nickel-sulfate processing. It signals exploration progress rather than near-term production, so price impact on nickel/copper is likely minimal.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 16): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, aluminium fell 0.36%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous prices mostly higher after China’s Q1 GDP slightly missed expectations. Copper closed up 1.69% and nickel up 1.25%, supported by macro sentiment and market positioning, while aluminium fell 0.36% despite higher open interest. Nickel supply signals cite increased Chinese port ore inventories.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 700 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 700 mt week-on-week to 9,300 mt as of April 16. The decline reflects nickel plates flowing out of the bonded area, even as Norwegian nickel and LME briquettes entered China after customs clearance. Stocks have dropped for seven consecutive weeks.

title: Chilean Metals Arranges $2 Million Financing To Explore Nisk Nickel Project
summary: Chilean Metals arranged $2m financing to fund an initial drill program at its Nisk nickel-copper project in Quebec, including work toward an updated NI 43-101 resource. The company positions the project for a market improving for battery metals, but it remains exploration with no current production impact.

title: The Case for Investing in Copper, the Go-To Metal for Renewable Energy Projects
summary: The piece highlights Goldman Sachs’ view that copper will surge as renewable energy deployment accelerates and the metal remains in a tight market, with China demand returning. It argues prior underinvestment in mines could lead to a future supply gap, supporting bullish near-term price expectations.

title: Copper heads for biggest weekly gain since February
summary: Copper is positioned for its biggest weekly gain since February after solid U.S. and Chinese data lifted stocks and improved short-term demand sentiment. China’s factory activity was mixed but still supportive. Goldman raised its 12-month copper target and Citi advised bullish exposure over coming weeks. Aluminium is pressured by record output despite capacity-curb expectations.

title: Chinese Aluminum Price Soar To 11-Year Highs As Decarbonization Efforts Slash Energy To Smelters
summary: Chinese aluminium prices reportedly surged to 11-year highs as decarbonization policies cut energy supply to smelters. The resulting reduction in primary aluminium output is expected to tighten near-term supply and bolster spot prices quickly.

title: Southland iwi meet with officials over Tiwai Point aluminium smelter clean-up for first time
summary: Southland iwi met officials for the first time on cleanup of the contaminated Tiwai Point aluminium smelter. The Environment Ministry had been talking with the Rio Tinto-owned operator, but talks were halted over missing environmental monitoring data. No new data emerged at the meeting.

title: China March aluminium imports rise 40.8% from prior month
summary: China’s March aluminium imports rose 40.8% from February to 206,556 tonnes, and were up 70.9% year-on-year. Q1 imports jumped 118.8%. The increase follows a brief mid-March reopening of Shanghai–London arbitrage as the price spread widened.

title: NORNICKEL AGREED WITH JOHNSON MATTHEY ON CRITICAL SUPPLY OF NICKEL AND COBALT
summary: Norilsk Nickel (Nornickel) signed a term sheet with Johnson Matthey for long-term supply of critical metals for battery materials in Finland and plans to ramp nickel and cobalt production at its Harjavalta refinery. The agreement supports expected nickel supply into European EV cathode production, adding bullish near-term sentiment.

title: SMM survey on the impact on primary aluminium alloy industry from automaker shutdowns caused by chip shortage_SMM
summary: SMM reports that chip shortages have forced automaker shutdowns or suspensions, reducing orders from downstream wheel hub users. About 90% of A356.2 primary aluminium alloy in China goes to wheel hubs. Surveyed producers saw weaker March orders, and expect operating rates to fall toward ~50% in April if shutdowns persist.

title: Copper prices faced pressure from fundamentals last week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports copper prices dipped early then rose as the dollar index eased, supported by stronger US retail sales/jobs data and Chinese liquidity injections. However, smelter maintenance and eased inventories are offset by weak downstream demand (postponed power grid projects, lower automaker orders, delayed April-May consumption). Spot discounts widened on higher Shanghai inventories and are expected to narrow with imported supplies.

title: Johnson Matthey Partners With Finnish Minerals; Agrees With Nornickel, SQM For Raw Materials Supply
summary: Johnson Matthey said it will commercialise eLNO cathode materials via a second plant in Finland with Finnish Minerals. The project includes treating sodium sulphate by-products and pre-treatment of nickel/cobalt sulphates. It also signed a term sheet for nickel and cobalt supply from Nornickel, supporting nickel demand.

title: Nornickel to supply nickel, cobalt to Johnson Matthey for battery materials
summary: Nornickel signed a long-term deal to supply nickel (and cobalt) to Johnson Matthey for EV battery precursor and cathode active materials production in Finland and Poland. The news follows Nornickel’s plan to boost nickel output at its Harjavalta refinery, alongside future supply expansion discussions.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 19): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, nickel fell 1.28%_SMM
summary: SMM reports most Shanghai nonferrous metals rose on Apr 19 except nickel, which fell 1.28% while copper gained 1.22% and aluminium edged up 0.05%. The piece attributes moves to softer USD and strong economic data/risk sentiment, with no major new nickel or aluminium supply-demand event.

title: Kodiak Expands MPD Project Through Acquisition of Axe Copper-Gold
summary: Kodiak Copper agreed to acquire 100% of the Axe copper-gold property contiguous with its MPD project in British Columbia. The release cites historic drill results and permits for future drilling, expanding the copper-gold land position. It signals exploration upside but offers no immediate production or supply changes.

title: Gold and Copper Sold Ahead of Breakouts
summary: Saxo Bank’s COT review shows money managers cut copper net-long positions by 20% to 38.2k lots, the lowest in nine months, while gold selling also occurred before technical breakouts. The article notes breakouts would likely attract momentum flows, but the lead positioning shift for copper is net bearish.

title: NORNICKEL ANNOUNCES PRODUCTION RESULTS FOR 1Q 2021
summary: Norilsk Nickel said recent incidents in Norilsk temporarily shut its Norilsk Concentrator and two mines (Oktyabrsky and Taimyrsky) and reduced output at Kola MMC. As a result, 1Q21 nickel fell to 47 kt (-10% q-o-q) and copper to 91 kt (-21% q-o-q), signaling tighter near-term supply.

title: NORNICKEL ANNOUNCES PRODUCTION RESULTS FOR 1Q 2021 -2-
summary: Norilsk Nickel said accidents in Norilsk—temporary suspension of the Norilsk Concentrator and flooding-related shutdowns of Oktyabrsky and Taimyrsky mines—cut 1Q21 nickel output by 10% q-o-q and copper by 21% q-o-q. Recovery is guided toward later in 2021, increasing near-term supply downside risk.

title: Agreement reached for 350 Century Aluminum workers; 60 jobs added
summary: Century Aluminum announced a new five-year collective bargaining agreement for its Hawesville, Kentucky aluminum smelter, ratified by USW Local 9423. The contract covers about 350 hourly workers and the company plans to add roughly 60 jobs as the expansion continues, citing a competitive aluminum market.

title: Bullish investors push copper towards 10-year highs
summary: Copper prices rose on Monday, supported by record global stock markets and a falling U.S. dollar. LME benchmark copper was up about 1.8% to near $9,380/t after briefly topping $9,436, the highest since late February, as analysts expect further upside toward 10-year highs.

title: Rio Tinto Commences Exploration on Solwezi Copper | The Kingston Whig Standard
summary: Rio Tinto begins a 2021 exploration campaign on Midnight Sun’s Solwezi copper licences in Zambia, including drilling across several prospects and a $3.2 million program to late June. The work targets high-grade copper anomalies on the Solwezi copper belt, but no results are provided.

title: Nickel News Roundup_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM’s nickel industry roundup says Nornickel restarted mining at the Oktyabrsky copper-nickel mine after an April 12 flood, targeting full production by end-April. It also highlights Norilsk/Harjavalta plans to expand nickel sulphate output and deals to supply high-grade NCA/NCM ternary precursor materials for EV batteries in 2021-2023.

title: Copper rises to near 10-year high on a weaker dollar
summary: Copper prices rose to near a decade high, with three-month LME copper up to around $9,453/t, driven by a weaker U.S. dollar making dollar-priced metals cheaper. The piece also notes modest moves in LME aluminum and tin, while nickel is mixed amid an expanding surplus and production updates at Nornickel.

title: Norilsk Nickel and Johnson Matthey sign terms of long-term supply of nickel and cobalt
summary: Norilsk Nickel and Johnson Matthey agreed on long-term supply terms for nickel (and cobalt) for Johnson Matthey’s Finland plant producing ultra-high energy cathode materials for EV batteries. The arrangement supports Norilsk’s planned expansion of sustainable nickel/cobalt output at Harjavalta to meet growing European battery demand.

title: Singapore prosecution files more charges over nickel trading scandal
summary: Singapore prosecutors filed five additional cheating charges against a businessman tied to a nickel trading scandal, alleging investors’ funds were used for bogus forward nickel contracts. The case involves Envy Global Trading and ongoing court oversight, with assets seized. Fraud and reduced trading confidence can pressure short-term nickel market sentiment.

title: Why copper and lithium could be 'the new oil'
summary: The piece argues copper is central to meeting climate targets, citing its use in renewable power transmission. It says the market is already tight, with copper prices up sharply over the past year and mine expansion timelines extending supply constraints. It projects higher prices ahead, implying near-term bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Cardero Resource Corp.: Cardero Enters into Letter Agreement to Merge with World Copper
summary: Cardero agreed to merge with World Copper, where WCU would acquire Cardero’s shares in exchange for WCU stock and finance the combined entity with $10 million. The combined portfolio is focused on copper projects (Zonia in Arizona; projects in Chile). The transaction is subject to approvals and has no stated immediate production impact.

title: Forum Energy Metals Corp.: Forum Plans Electromagnetic Survey at Love Lake Nickel-Copper-Palladium Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals plans a large-scale airborne electromagnetic survey at its Love Lake nickel-copper-PGM project in Saskatchewan to refine targets for possible feeder pipes or ‘reefs.’ The company is moving toward a drill program later in summer, but the announcement is exploratory with no near-term supply impact.

title: Quaterra Resources Inc.: Quaterra Announces Drill Program at MacArthur Copper Oxide Property: Core Drilling to Begin in Early May
summary: Quaterra Resources announced a 7,000–10,000-foot core drilling program beginning in early May at its MacArthur copper oxide project in Nevada. The drilling supports resource upgrades and sulfide exploration ahead of a prefeasibility study. The company highlights sensitivity to copper and acid prices but provides no near-term supply impact.

title: North American Nickel Inc.: North American Nickel Closes Oversubscribed Non-brokered Private Placement Financing Raising $1.99 Million
summary: North American Nickel Inc. closed an oversubscribed non-brokered private placement raising about $1.99 million. Proceeds are intended for continued investment in Premium Nickel Resources and further exploration at projects in Morocco and Greenland, plus general corporate use. The release is nickel-related but does not signal immediate production changes.

title: Chilean peso at over 4-mth high on copper gains, Peru's sol stable
summary: Chile’s peso and Peru’s sol strengthened as copper prices rose toward 10-year highs, reflecting optimism about recovering global demand. The move improved emerging-market sentiment amid shifting expectations for U.S. yields and dovish Fed signals. Most other Latin currencies traded flat, while Latin American equities were mixed.

title: Supercycle or China cycle? Funds wait for Dr. Copper's call
summary: Funds cut net long exposure in copper futures, while Chinese officials warn they will “stabilise prices,” prevent hoarding/panic buying, and crack down on speculation and monopolies. The piece notes copper remains dependent on China’s cycle and that slowing China growth could pressure industrial metal demand, weighing on prices near term.

title: Copper price boost? Peru's socialist swerve worries miners
summary: Peru’s election has heightened risk for miners, with frontrunner Pedro Castillo proposing nationalization and constitutional changes affecting copper among other minerals. Industry warnings cite “mining nationalism” and a likely increase in the Peru risk premium, potentially reducing investment and future supply, supporting higher copper prices.

title: Forum Plans Electromagnetic Survey at Love Lake Nickel-Copper-Palladium Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals plans a May airborne electromagnetic survey on its Love Lake nickel-copper-PGM project in Saskatchewan to refine conductive targets for potential future drilling. The release reiterates historic copper and nickel grades and aims to make the project drill-ready, but provides no immediate production or trade changes.

title: Forum Plans Electromagnetic Survey at Love Lake Nickel-Copper-Palladium Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals plans an airborne electromagnetic survey in May at its Love Lake nickel-copper-PGM project in Saskatchewan to refine conductive target areas for possible drilling later this summer. The work is exploratory and aimed at better defining anomalies, with no production or supply impact reported.

title: Talon Metals Unveils Platform for Building a Domestic USA Supply Chain from Mine to Battery the "Smart" Way at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals presented its “Green Nickel” traceable supply-chain concept using the Tamarack Nickel Project, proposing a US-based refinery and integration from mine to EV battery materials. It argues US refinery capacity is missing for nickel destined for cathodes, especially after Eagle Mine closure, supporting tighter domestic nickel sentiment.

title: 7 A-Rated Retirement Stocks to Buy: DKS, GSBD, TGT
summary: The piece lists retirement stock picks and includes Southern Copper, describing copper as increasingly critical for electrification and construction. It references Goldman Sachs warning of a historic copper shortage driven by demand from China and green initiatives. The article implies copper demand is strong and should support higher prices.

title: BHP lifts copper guidance, iron-ore output falls
summary: BHP said it will likely produce more copper than previously expected this fiscal year and raised its annual copper production forecast, despite quarterly copper output falling 9% year-on-year to 391,400 tonnes. The company also reported lower iron-ore output due to weather and maintenance.

title: Copper slips on virus surge, weak dollar limits losses
summary: Copper prices fell as investors grew concerned that a COVID-19 resurgence in India and Japan could slow the global recovery and reduce metals demand. A weaker U.S. dollar limited losses. Reuters also noted LME aluminium up, while nickel slightly rose and aluminium fell on the Shanghai market.

title: Domestic alumina prices rose slightly on improving purchase by traders and aluminium smelters _SMM
summary: SMM reports slightly stronger spot alumina trading in China, with Shanxi prices edging up and more buying by traders and downstream users. Overseas alumina deals were recorded and imports remain costly. Outlook is mixed: rigid demand and lower freight support, but resumed production may add supply; prices expected to stabilise or rebound slightly.

title: China aluminium scrap imports fell 44.9% in February_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s aluminium scrap imports dropped to 38,100 mt in February, down 44.9% month-on-month and 35.5% year-on-year. January-February imports totaled 107,200 mt (-12.3% y/y). Rumours easing at Sanshan Port may lift March volumes slightly, but inspections at other ports remain tight.

title: Antofagasta copper production declines 5%
summary: Antofagasta said its copper production declined 5% in the first quarter versus the fourth quarter of 2020. The miner produced 183,000 metric tons of copper in the three months to March 31, down from 192,600 tons in October-December, implying reduced near-term supply.

title: Aluminium prices remained high and fluctuated in March_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices stayed high and fluctuated in March. A00 spot reached about 17,760 yuan/mt, trading mostly 17,000–17,500. Weak demand replaced earlier supply tightness, while import restrictions kept scrap supply reduced. Transmission of high prices to downstream was slow, with secondary market activity expected later.

title: Copper foil maker raises $700 mn funding to build Europe plant
summary: SKC Ltd. plans its first overseas copper-foil plant in Malaysia, investing roughly $588 million (650 billion won) to expand capacity for copper foil used in EV battery components. The announced funding and production scaling are likely to support near-term expectations for incremental copper demand, though impacts are not immediate supply-related.

title: Freeport-McMoRan Stock Gets Downgraded. An Analyst Sees Risks for Copper Demand.
summary: A news item says Freeport-McMoRan shares were downgraded, with an analyst warning about risks to copper demand. While broader commodity prices are rising, the downgrade highlights potential near-term demand weakness, which could weigh on market expectations for copper over the next days to a few weeks.

title: Century Aluminum Publishes its Inaugural Annual Sustainability Report
summary: Century Aluminum published its inaugural sustainability report highlighting renewable power use at operations, redesign of an anode facility to optimize energy use, and new pot technology aimed at reducing power consumption and improving current efficiency. It also references “green aluminum” products and safety initiatives, but provides no concrete cost or output figures.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Operations Update
summary: Nevada Copper reported progress at its Pumpkin Hollow underground mine: first stope mining is expected to start this week, ventilation fan installations are underway to raise development rates, and lateral development improved after electrical upgrades. The mill is batching at ~4,700 tpd average with higher concentrate grades and a 5,000 tpd steady-state target in Q3.

title: Copper dips as physical buyers shun high prices
summary: Copper prices fell as physical buyers reduced demand after a 21% London rally this year. Three-month LME copper dropped 0.5% to $9,397.50/t. Softer USD provided limited support. Weaker-than-expected demand in China due to high prices and slower recovery pressured sentiment; nickel and aluminium moved modestly.

title: AT A GLANCE: Anglo American copper volumes up 9% on output rise in Chile
summary: The piece highlights that Anglo American’s copper volumes rose 9% due to higher output in Chile. This points to improved production levels from a major supplier, which can influence near-term expectations for copper supply availability and related market sentiment, potentially supporting copper prices over the coming days.

title: Daily Authority: Greener aluminum with Apple's help, and more
summary: Apple is backing a joint venture (Elysis) formed by Alcoa and Rio Tinto to develop “green aluminum” smelting without direct carbon pollutants. The piece highlights Elysis’ carbonless process and emissions reduction potential, but emphasizes commercialization remains uncertain, implying limited immediate impact on near-term aluminum prices.

title: Nobel29 Resources Corp. Announces Values up to 36% Copper and 27 G/T Gold From Underground and Surface Sampling at Its Algarrobo Copper-Gold Project, Chile
summary: Nobel29 Resources reported chip-channel sampling from its Algarrobo copper-gold project in Chile, with copper grades up to 36.22% and gold enrichment, ahead of an upcoming drill program. The company also notes artisanal production feeding a smelter via direct shipping. No immediate supply disruption or policy change is indicated.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Reports Excellent Grades at Shallow Depths Extending 300 Meters Outside of the Tamarack Nickel Project's Resource Area
summary: Talon Metals reported drill results from the CGO West area of the Tamarack nickel-copper project in Minnesota, highlighting shallow massive sulphide intercepts with grades up to about 5.86% Ni and 2.35% Cu. The company says this extends mineralization outside the current resource area and planning continues.

title: Shanghai aluminium soars as China's production stalls: Andy Home
summary: Shanghai aluminium prices hit the highest since 2010 as Chinese supply stalls and demand approaches a seasonal peak. Smelter output has risen only modestly, with energy-efficiency closures in Inner Mongolia and rail delays tightening physical availability. Imports are re-accelerating, while LME prices also reach fresh highs.

title: Talon Metals Reports Excellent Grades at Shallow Depths Extending 300 Meters Outside of the Tamarack Nickel Project's Resource Area
summary: Talon Metals reported assay results from three shallow drill holes in the CGO West target outside its current Tamarack resource area in Minnesota. Intersections include high-grade nickel and copper massive sulphides, suggesting potential extension of nickel-copper mineralization. The announcement is exploration-focused and does not imply near-term production.

title: Copper dips as Chinese physical buyers shun high-priced metal
summary: London copper dipped 0.2% as Chinese physical buyers stayed sidelined due to poor downstream acceptability after a 21% YTD rally. Softer dollar provided some support, but sluggish end-user demand left trading largely stalled. Nickel and aluminium movements are mentioned but the demand-driven move centers on copper.

title: Antofagasta reduces workforce, postpones copper mine maintenance due to Covid-19 wave
summary: Antofagasta will cut its workforce and postpone copper mine maintenance because of a Covid-19 wave. The changes signal near-term production and operational disruption risks, which can reduce effective copper output and weigh on short-term copper price expectations over coming days to weeks.

title: Freeport still in talks on Indonesia copper smelter | American Metal Market
summary: The article headline says Freeport remains in talks on an Indonesia copper smelter, which could influence near-term expectations for copper refining capacity and supply balance. The rest of the excerpt focuses on Fastmarkets’ procedural publication corrections for aluminium assessments, with no clear new physical shock.

title: Aluminum commands record premium in U.S. as economy recovers
summary: U.S. aluminum is reportedly trading with a record premium as the economy recovers. A higher premium generally signals stronger demand and/or tighter supply in the regional market, raising expectations for near-term aluminum tightness and supporting upward pressure on prices in the coming days.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 322,000 wmt to 5.3 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show Chinese nickel ore inventories at ports fell 322,000 wmt to 5.3 million wmt between April 16 and April 23. Seven major ports saw a 302,000 wmt drop to 3.94 million wmt. Ni-content stocks rose modestly, but near-term availability appears tighter.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Apr 23): Shanghai nonferrous metals ended mixed, nickel fell 0.22%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous markets ending mixed: aluminium +0.99% and copper +0.35% after higher arrivals lifted Shanghai bonded copper stocks, while nickel slipped 0.22% with bonded nickel inventories unchanged. Open interest mostly rose in copper/aluminium but fell in nickel, suggesting mild, offsetting near-term pressure.

title: McIlvenna Bay set to become first carbon neutral copper development project
summary: Foran Mining says its McIlvenna Bay deposit will be developed as a “carbon neutral” copper project by measuring and offsetting greenhouse-gas emissions tied to past exploration activities and using renewables/electric equipment for future work. The announcement is ESG-focused and does not indicate immediate copper supply changes.

title: Copper prices post highest finish in more than 9 years
summary: Copper futures posted their highest weekly finish in more than nine years, with prices rising for the third straight week. The article attributes the bullish momentum to Biden administration infrastructure plans and a green-energy push, which is expected to lift demand for copper used in renewable energy systems.

title: Green Spending Reignites Industrial-Metal Rally Led by Copper
summary: Industrial metals rallied to multi-year highs on pandemic-driven industrial recovery, Biden’s infrastructure and climate push, and green-energy demand expectations. Copper climbed to a multi-year London high amid shrinking inventories and stockpiles. Aluminum also rose on expectations for further China supply curbs and supply-side stress from COVID-related mine risks.

title: Vietnam ups anti-dumping duties on Chinese aluminium - VnExpress International
summary: Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade raised anti-dumping duties on certain Chinese extruded aluminium products from 18 firms, with duty rates varying by producer. The ministry said prior dumping hurt domestic producers, causing output halts and job losses. Import volumes reached 62,000 tons in 2018, and the revised duties aim to curb underpriced imports.

title: Flavonoids Market and Ferronickel Market Size 2021 Movements by Key Findings, Progression Status, Emerging Demands, Recent Trends, Business Opportunity, Covid-19 Impact Analysis, and Revenue Expectation till 2026
summary: A report covers the global ferronickel market (a nickel ferroalloy used mainly in stainless steel). It says nickel ore is the key input and that export restrictions by Indonesia and the Philippines have driven up raw-ore prices. It also discusses COVID-19 effects and market growth through 2026.

title: Analysis of China's aluminium extrusion exports in March amid anti-dumping by the EU_SMM
summary: China’s aluminium extrusion exports in March fell, with EU shipments down sharply. EU final anti-dumping duties on Chinese aluminium extrusions (21.2%–32.1%) were imposed on March 30, driving producers to cut EU orders. The article expects exports to the EU to drop further in April, pressuring aluminium demand.

title: Copper concentrate: Quotes and counter-offer inched higher_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says the Imports Copper Concentrate Index rose to $30.2/mt on April 23. Sellers’ quotes are limited and smelters are preparing purchases for June+ amid maintenance periods. Spot concentrate TCs are below $30/mt. It also notes port strikes in Chilean politics with no disruption.

title: Copper Jumps to Highest Since 2011 as Demand Bets Reignite Rally
summary: Copper surged to its highest level since 2011 as global recovery, stimulus and decarbonization plans revive demand expectations. Analysts cite tightening supply conditions and rising LME/SHFE/Comex positioning. Aluminum is also surging on broader commodity strength, while COVID and potential China interventions add short-term risk.

title: Copper marches towards 10-year high on weaker dollar, supply concerns
summary: Copper prices rose toward a nearly 10-year high on a weaker U.S. dollar and renewed supply concerns. A potential strike in Chile, a leading copper producer, threatened an already tight concentrate market. The article also records gains in LME aluminum and nickel, reflecting supportive industrial-metals sentiment.

title: Copper's Large Role in Growing Electric Vehicle Production
summary: The piece contends EV growth will raise copper demand versus internal combustion vehicles, citing higher copper usage in hybrids/BEVs and additional copper in charging infrastructure wiring and cables. It notes global EV sales have risen and projects many more charging points, implying supportive demand expectations for copper.

title: Sterlite Copper smelter will not be opened at all: Stalin
summary: DMK leader M.K. Stalin said Tamil Nadu’s permission for Vedanta’s Sterlite Copper plant to run temporarily to produce medical oxygen will not lead to the copper smelter reopening if his party comes to power. The facility previously was shut after protests over pollution and deaths, and the restart lasts four months.

title: Surge Battery Metals Acquires Quesnel Nickel Project
summary: Surge Battery Metals announced it negotiated an option agreement to acquire an 80% interest in the Quesnel Nickel Project in British Columbia, targeting nickel alloy/mineralization (awaruite) in ultramafic/serpentinite rocks. The company plans to file permits and start work this summer, but no production impacts are indicated.

title: Nickel Mines acquires additional stake in Angel Capital
summary: Australia’s Nickel Mines completed a further 20% stake acquisition in Angel Capital, bringing its interest in Indonesia’s Angel Nickel project to 50%, with rights to raise to 80%. The project includes RKEF lines and a 380MW power station under construction, but the update is mainly ownership-related and not linked to near-term output changes.

title: Copper Hits Highest Since 2011 as Global Recovery Powers Metals
summary: Copper is reported to be hitting its highest level since 2011 as expectations for a global economic recovery strengthen. The article’s framing suggests improving near-term demand and risk sentiment for industrial commodities, which is generally supportive for copper prices in the coming days.

title: Aluminum Extrusion Market Size to Reach $118.7 Billion by 2027
summary: The piece forecasts growth in the global aluminum extrusion industry and notes that COVID-19 caused temporary demand declines (automotive, construction) and disrupted alumina/bauxite supply chains via import/export restrictions. It also highlights ongoing lockdown effects. These factors could influence near-term aluminium supply-demand expectations.

title: Proactive news headlines including PlantX Life, FPX Nickel, Safe -T Group and PsyBio Therapeutics
summary: Proactive headlines include FPX Nickel Corp launching a metallurgical pilot test program at its Baptiste nickel project in British Columbia. The item is development-focused, but improved metallurgy work can slightly support expectations for nickel production potential, which may provide limited upward sentiment for nickel-related equities and prices.

title: Global recovery powers metal boom as copper and steel prices soar
summary: The piece says investors can track the strength of the global recovery through metals markets: copper is at its highest in a decade, aluminium is surging, and iron ore/steel prices are also rising. It frames the move as driven by recovery expectations, implying supportive near-term price pressure for copper and aluminium.

title: Copper hits near-decade high as metals prices boom
summary: Copper rose about 2% to a near-decade high, driven by US and China recovery plus green-infrastructure demand for electrification, alongside supply tightness from emission-linked curbs. Aluminium is also gaining support from China’s green push halting new projects and potential regional production restrictions.

title: SDK's Full-scale Marketing of ST60-HSM Aluminum Alloy Board with High Heat Conductivity and High Strength, uses On-board Bus Bar
summary: Showa Denko began full-scale marketing of an aluminium alloy board (ST60-HSM) for use as automotive on-board bus bars, highlighting higher heat and electric conductivity and lower cost versus conventional copper bus bars. The company frames the move as part of the industry shift from copper to aluminium in EV wiring and power distribution.

title: SDK's Full-scale Marketing of ST60-HSM Aluminum Alloy Board with High Heat Conductivity and High Strength for On-board Bus Bar
summary: Showa Denko began full-scale marketing of a high heat- and electric-conductivity aluminum alloy board for EV on-board bus bars. It notes aluminum bus bars can replace copper ones, offering weight reduction and cost benefits. This supports incremental demand expectations for aluminum, with indirect downside for copper.

title: Vietnam raises anti-dumping duties on some Chinese aluminium products
summary: Vietnam raised anti-dumping duties on certain aluminium products from China, effective April 25, with rates revised to 4.39%-35.58% from 2.49%-35.58%. The government cited ongoing threat of damage to domestic manufacturing. The change is expected to curb Chinese aluminium import flows in the near term.

title: Bitterroot Resources Ltd.: Bitterroot Resources Intersects Additional Nickel-Copper-PGM Mineralization
summary: Bitterroot Resources reported assays from drill hole LM 21-10 at its LM nickel-copper-PGM project, including 0.93% Ni and 0.77% Cu over 2.3 metres and a basal interval grading up to 2.74% Ni and 0.43% Cu. Drilling is expected to resume in late May.

title: Bitterroot Resources Ltd.: Bitterroot Resources Intersects Additional Nickel-Copper-PGM Mineralization
summary: Bitterroot Resources reported assays from a third drill hole (LM 21-10) at its LM nickel-copper-PGM project in Michigan, including disseminated sulphides grading 0.93% nickel and 0.77% copper and a basal interval with higher nickel. Drilling is expected to resume in late May; funds come from a private placement.

title: Pancontinental Resources Corporation: Pancon Reports Significant Copper in Discovery Holes 4 and 5
summary: Pancon reports assay results from diamond holes at its Brewer Gold & Copper Project, highlighting holes 4 and 5 with about 0.95–0.97% copper over 7.6 m and copper-gold correlation. Phase 2 drilling is underway, but the news is an exploration find with no immediate production or supply change.

title: Grid Metals Corp.: Grid Metals Commences Drilling at Bannockburn Nickel Project
summary: Grid Metals Corp. started drilling at its Bannockburn nickel sulphide project, aiming to better define nickel grades and test depth and metallurgical performance for potential high-grade nickel concentrates. The release is exploration-focused with no immediate production, export, or supply disruption, so near-term nickel price impact is likely limited.

title: SHFE copper and aluminium registered new ten-year highs_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE copper and aluminium hitting ten-year highs as broader non-ferrous prices rise early this week. Copper strength is linked to improved US/EU manufacturing, weaker USD from strong European currencies, and ample liquidity. Aluminium upside is supported by limited April supply (cuts/maintenance and import delays) despite some demand softening from high prices.

title: SHFE copper and aluminium registered new ten-year highs_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SHFE copper and aluminium both reached nearly/ten-year highs as non-ferrous stocks rallied. Drivers cited include improving European/American manufacturing, weaker US dollar and ample liquidity. For copper, potential disruption from a Chilean port workers strike is a risk to exports. Aluminium is supported by limited April supply, low inventories, and output cuts.

title: MEED | UAE aluminium firm raises Abu Dhabi smelter output
summary: MEED’s headline says a UAE aluminium firm has raised output at its Abu Dhabi smelter. The change points to increased near-term aluminium supply in the region, which can weigh on aluminium prices by improving availability for buyers.

title: Copper reaches decade high near $10,000
summary: Copper rallied to a decade high near $10,000/t on the London Metal Exchange, driven by strong Chinese demand and tight availability. Analysts cite Chile strike action involving port workers and mining unions, alongside a weaker dollar, and intensifying demand for wiring, including electrical vehicles.

title: Mining giant Chile flush with cash as copper price soars
summary: Chile’s finance minister says soaring copper prices will boost growth and help fund nearly $16 billion in pandemic-related stimulus. The government forecasts copper averaging $3.99/lb in 2021 versus $3.35 earlier, with higher taxes/royalties per price point and stabilizing debt, reinforcing bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Materials Edge Lower As Copper Rally Continues -- Materials Roundup
summary: Metal-related shares edged lower, but copper led gains: U.S.-traded copper futures jumped more than 6% in the biggest one-day rise in over seven years. The rally was driven by strike risks in Chile, strong momentum, and improving Chinese demand, including higher Q1 imports of key inputs.

title: Copper surges toward US$10,000 as bulls bet on global rebound
summary: The piece centers on copper rising toward US$10,000, with traders described as bullish and expecting a global rebound. This framing suggests improving short-term demand expectations and market momentum supporting higher copper prices over the coming days.

title: Tiwai Point aluminium smelter to lower its electricity consumption
summary: New Zealand’s Tiwai Point aluminium smelter agreed to cut electricity use by up to 30.5MW until end of May due to low rainfall pressuring hydro generation and a natural gas shortage that drove wholesale power prices sharply higher. The temporary load reduction likely reduces aluminium supply, supporting prices.

title: Copper prices hit 10-year high as rising commodity prices, aside from gold, lift TSX
summary: The article headline reports that copper prices have surged to a 10-year high. It attributes the strength to rising commodity prices broadly (excluding gold) and notes the positive lift to the TSX. Overall, the news signals strong upward momentum for copper.

title: Records tumble as iron ore, copper exports boom
summary: Australia’s mineral exports hit record highs as China-driven demand and renewable-energy momentum boost shipments. The report says metalliferous ores reached a record and highlights copper ore exports up 62% in March. This suggests stronger near-term demand flow, likely supporting expectations for copper prices.

title: Imports of intermediate products of nickel hydro-metallurgy increased 5% month on month in March_SMM
summary: China imported 28,800 mt of nickel hydro-metallurgy intermediate products in March, up 5% month-on-month and 79% year-on-year, with total imports up 87% to 85,500 mt. Unit import prices excluding taxes rose, and SMM expects strong Q2 demand for nickel sulphate, keeping intermediates in high demand.

title: Kenadyr Signs Letter of Intent to Acquire Kamkor Copper Deposit
summary: Kenadyr Mining announced a binding letter of intent to acquire 100% of the Kamkor copper project in Kazakhstan via purchase of Kamkor-Saryarka. The release cites historical resources and flotation-based processing to produce copper concentrates, but provides no immediate production or supply impact.

title: Vietnam continues to impose anti-dumping duties on Chinese aluminum imports
summary: Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade has decided to continue anti-dumping duties on selected Chinese non-alloy aluminium products (bars, rods, extruded and surface-treated/unprocessed) with duty rates from 4.39% to 35.58%. The measures follow a first review and reflect claims that imports were dumped and harmed domestic producers.

title: Total export volume of aluminium wires and cables declined in March declined in March_SMM
summary: China exported about 10,600 mt of aluminium wires and cables in March, down 4.1% m/m and 61% y/y, with weaker overseas demand despite improved domestic operating rates. High domestic aluminium base prices narrowed overseas order profitability. Suez Canal effects and customer resistance also reduced export orders; April exports may remain around 10,000 mt.

title: The import loss expanded rapidly, refined copper exports increased_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums (warehousing receipt) fell sharply, reflecting weak domestic demand and oversupply from rising smelting capacity. Import losses widened to about 1,000 yuan/weekend, suppressing customs declarations and boosting bonded inventories. Domestic smelters are shifting toward export profits, raising refined copper exports and potentially narrowing the import-loss spread.

title: Premiums of nickel sulphate averaged 21,000 yuan/mt with metal content over nickel briquette_SMM
summary: SMM reports slightly weaker SHFE nickel but stabilised battery-grade nickel sulphate at 31,000–32,000 yuan/mt amid quiet trading and tight spot supply. Monthly purchasing may raise trades this week, while prices could fall if SHFE nickel stays low. Premiums over first-grade nickel rose, but are expected to shrink.

title: Copper climbs towards record as market frets about supply
summary: Copper is climbing toward record levels as traders fret about potential supply tightness. The market’s focus on whether inventories or production could fall short supports higher pricing expectations in the near term. (Article excerpt provided contains only the headline/snippet, but the stated driver is supply-related.)

title: Chakana Copper Corp.: Chakana Reports High-Grade Intersects
summary: Chakana Copper Corp. reported high-grade drill intercepts at its Soledad Project, including intervals with meaningful copper grades (e.g., 0.54% Cu over 125m and 1.27% Cu over 15m) plus gold and silver. It also outlines an ongoing, fully funded 2021 drilling program aimed at future resource estimation.

title: Palladium One Mining Inc.: Palladium One Intersects Massive Sulphides in Multiple Holes at Tyko Nickel-Copper Project, in Ontario
summary: Palladium One reported multiple massive to semi-massive sulphide intersections at its Tyko Ni-Cu project in Ontario, linking upper and lower EM conductors and expanding the known nickel-copper mineralized zone. Drilling was suspended due to equipment and spring conditions, with assay results pending; no production changes are announced.

title: Palladium One Mining Inc.: Palladium One Intersects Massive Sulphides in Multiple Holes at Tyko Nickel-Copper Project, in Ontario
summary: Palladium One reports multiple massive sulphide intersections and continuity along a 350-meter strike length at its Tyko Ni-Cu project in Ontario. The company links upper and lower sulphide conductors and plans further EM surveys before resuming drilling. It is early-stage exploration with assays pending.

title: Teck profit jumps 247% as COVID-19 vaccine rollout boosts copper prices
summary: Teck says vaccine rollout and stimulus have lifted China’s copper demand above pre-pandemic levels, helping its quarterly earnings. It cites rising copper prices and notes limited new mine supply, implying investors may need higher prices to spur new production. Teck’s realized copper price rose sequentially.

title: Imports of secondary copper increased sharply in March_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China imported 172,000 mt of secondary copper scrap in March, up sharply m/m and y/y, driven by holiday timing and deferred shipments. Strong demand for secondary smelting and high-quality scrap lifted active overseas buying, firm quotes and a wider cathode-scrap spread, suggesting supportive near-term copper price pressure.

title: Nickel prices soared amid positive macroeconomic environment_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported SHFE 2106 nickel jumped 3.61% to close at 126,560 yuan/mt, with rising open interest. The move was linked to easing financial conditions (lower US yields, softer dollar) and potential near-term Russian nickel supply disruption after a Norilsk mine accident, plus stronger nickel briquette and nickel sulphate-related demand expectations.

title: Investors 'unlikely to recover funds' in billion-dollar Singapore nickel fraud case
summary: Singapore court documents say investors in a billion-dollar nickel trading fraud involving Envy Group are unlikely to recover losses, with large receivables owed and possible inability to pay. The scheme purportedly involved discounted nickel purchases and on-sales under allegedly forged contracts, prompting judicial management and forensic review.

title: CanAlaska Stakes Fourth Thompson Nickel Belt Project
summary: CanAlaska Uranium stakes 12 new claim blocks at Resting Lake in Manitoba’s Thompson Nickel Belt, targeting ultramafic sulphide nickel horizons south of nearby Wabowden nickel mines. The release cites prior nickel drill intersections and highlights infrastructure access, positioning for upcoming exploration drilling and potential JV activity.

title: Alianza Minerals Acquires Additional Data for Yanac Copper Porphyry Project, Peru
summary: Alianza Minerals reports it acquired additional drill-log data from prior reverse-circulation drilling at the Yanac copper porphyry project in Peru. One hole intersected copper and molybdenum with potential untested potassic core. The company is evaluating data and seeking a partner for follow-up drilling. No near-term production changes are mentioned.

title: Copper, 'the new oil,' leads metals surge amid global economic rebound
summary: Copper prices are surging toward record highs on LME levels near $9,965/tonne, driven mainly by Chinese demand and lingering supply constraints after COVID shutdowns. The piece also notes strong year-on-year growth in China’s consumption of copper and aluminium, suggesting supportive near-term demand and tight supply conditions.

title: Teck Resources profit soars 247% on higher copper prices
summary: Teck Resources reported a 246.8% rise in first-quarter adjusted profit, driven by higher copper prices. The average copper price realized increased 54% to US$3.92 per pound, while sales declined to 67,000 tonnes. The results were linked to stronger investment demand as COVID-19 vaccine rollouts progressed.

title: Copper Mountain Mining reports record revenues in Q1 2021
summary: Copper Mountain Mining reported record Q1 2021 revenues and gross profit, citing increased sales and higher metal prices. The quarter included copper sales of 27.5M lb at an average realized copper price of $3.90/lb and production guidance for strong output. The update is copper-positive via improved earnings and demand assumptions.

title: Can Copper Prices Continue To Break Records?
summary: Copper prices are again nearing the $10,000/tonne mark in New York, rising to about $9,940/tonne as bullish sentiment and renewed supply worries in the world’s top producing region support the rally. The piece links upside to expectations of demand growth from decarbonisation, though forecasts vary widely.

title: Demand poised to drive oil, copper prices sharply higher: Goldman
summary: Goldman Sachs said the magnitude of an upcoming commodity demand shift, which supply cannot match in the short run, should not be underestimated. It highlighted near-inelastic supply dynamics in months, suggesting upward pressure for commodities including copper, though details on the specific demand driver are limited.

title: Sherritt Reports Strong First Quarter Nickel and Cobalt Production
summary: Sherritt reported stronger Q1 nickel production (finished nickel up 9% to 4,188 tonnes) and said this reflected improved nickel market conditions, with NDCC at the Moa JV at US$3.83/lb (lowest since Q4 2019) and better realized nickel prices. The article also reviews broader nickel volatility and inventories.

title: Glencore Q1 Own Sourced Copper Production Up 3%
summary: Glencore reported Q1 own-sourced copper production of 301,200 tonnes, up 3% year-on-year, citing productivity improvements and mine plan sequencing at South American operations like Collahuasi, Antamina and Antapaccay. Nickel output fell 11% (maintenance at Koniambo). Guidance remains within its stated range.

title: Copper Extends Rally to Top $10,000 With All-Time High in Sight
summary: The article headline says copper is extending its rally to above $10,000, with expectations of an all-time high. That framing indicates market participants are bidding up copper prices, suggesting continued near-term bullish sentiment toward copper.

title: Ero Copper reports new copper zone below Vermelhos mine in Brazil
summary: Ero Copper says it has identified a new zone of mineralization below the Vermelhos mine at its underground project in Brazil. Vermelhos is part of the MCSA complex that includes the Pilar underground mine. The update is discovery-focused and could improve outlook for future copper supply sentiment.

title: Ero Copper reports new copper zone below Vermelhos mine in Brazil - Brazil Business Today
summary: Ero Copper said it identified a new zone of mineralization below the Vermelhos mine at its underground project in Brazil, part of its MCSA complex. The discovery may strengthen confidence in future copper resources and output, typically lending modest bullish support to copper prices over the near term.

title: Camino Minerals Corporation to Raise $5M to Commence Copper Discovery
summary: Camino Minerals plans to raise up to $5M via a private placement to fund exploration drilling at its Peruvian copper projects, including Los Chapitos and the Maria Cecilia porphyry complex, as well as related permitting milestones. The financing supports future resource discovery rather than any immediate output change.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 29/04: LME copper cash price hits $10,000/t; 64kt aluminium delivery in Port Klang
summary: Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin’s live futures report highlights market pricing and logistics. It notes LME copper cash reaching $10,000/t and records 64kt aluminium delivery in Port Klang. It also includes procedural/methodology update notes for other assessments. Overall it functions as a price update, not a clear new catalyst.

title: Copper rally to run out of steam in second half of year: poll
summary: A Reuters poll suggests copper’s strong rally may lose momentum in the second half of the year. Copper has risen over 25% in 2023 on expectations of China’s metal-intensive support during COVID recovery, but respondents expect Beijing to curb stimulus spending, weighing on demand outlook and sentiment.

title: Max Resource Reports a Fifth New Copper Zone at CESAR North, NE
summary: Max Resource Corp. reports discovery of a fifth new copper zone (SP) within its CESAR North copper-silver project in Colombia, with soil/rock sampling and assay results pending in June. It also updates prior discoveries (URU, CONEJO, AMN, AMS). No production or supply disruptions are mentioned.

title: US recovery gathers pace; copper hits $10,000; UK household wealth soars – as it happened
summary: The article summarizes a pickup in US growth in early 2021, supported by stimulus spending and consumer demand, alongside stronger stock sentiment. It notes copper trading around $10,000, consistent with bullish industrial demand expectations. UK and Eurozone optimism is also cited, though no direct nickel or aluminium specifics are given.

title: Copper extends rally to top $US10,000, with all-time high in sight
summary: Copper prices extended their rally above $10,000 per tonne on the LME, nearing the 2011 all-time high. The surge is attributed to stimulus, near-zero rates, reopening-driven demand recovery, and supply constraints as mines struggle to meet higher consumption tied to the energy transition.

title: Copper climbs to US$10,000, a new high
summary: The article headline reports that copper has climbed to US$10,000, a new high. While the excerpt provides limited context, the move itself signals improving short-term market expectations for copper pricing, typically reflecting tighter supply and/or stronger demand sentiment in response to current data.
