title: Copper slips below $10,000 as rally stalls ahead of holidays
summary: London and Shanghai copper prices edged lower after topping levels above $10,000 and recent records. The report links the pullback to investors assessing how high prices may curb demand, alongside slower-than-expected China factory activity and earlier supply concerns. It suggests the rally may stall, not reverse sharply.

title: Los Andes Copper Ltd. Receives Environmental Approval by Regional Environmental Committee for Upcoming Drilling Campaign at Vizcachitas
summary: Los Andes Copper reported unanimous environmental approval for drilling at its Vizcachitas copper project in Chile. The permit covers up to 350 holes and allows the company to complete its PFS. The update reduces permitting risk and supports development progress for a copper project tied to copper price assumptions.

title: Nornickel plans to adopt new ecology strategy in 2021
summary: Nornickel plans to adopt a new ecology strategy in 2021 with investments exceeding $5.5 billion, including cuts to emissions and remediation after a May 2020 diesel spill. The company also reports studies and cleanup steps and notes it has paid a large environmental fine. The capex could affect nickel and copper supply expectations.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks expanded 7,000 mt on week _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose 7,000 mt week-on-week to 396,700 mt as of April 30. Tepid domestic consumption and weaker pre-holiday restocking lifted inventories. Quieter foreign trading and roughly 1,000 yuan/mt import spot losses encouraged shifting port stocks to bonded zones, while smelters increased export plans.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 77,000 wmt to 5.37 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories across Chinese ports rose 77,000 wmt to 5.37 million wmt by April 30, with nickel-content stocks up 600 mt to 42,400 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also increased. Demand for low-nickel, high-iron ore fell as stainless mills shifted grades amid poor profits.

title: Chile says manufacturing up, copper output down in March
summary: Chile’s INE said manufacturing output rose 3.9% year-on-year in March, but copper output fell 1.3% to 491,720 tonnes. With Chile a major global copper producer, weaker March output signals tighter near-term supply conditions, typically pressuring copper prices downward in the short term.

title: Scientists: Bacteria Could Be Used To Source Copper
summary: US and Brazil-based researchers report that a copper-resistant bacterium can transform copper sulfate ions into zero-valent, single-atom copper. The study suggests a potentially cleaner, less labor-intensive route than current synthetic methods. While it may address future copper supply challenges, there’s no immediate production impact implied.

title: Copper extends its rally to top US$10,000 per tonne
summary: Copper rallied to above US$10,000 per tonne, nearing the 2011 all-time high, as stimulus and reopening raise demand expectations while producers struggle to keep up. Investors increased long positions and open interest. Aluminum was also cited higher, while nickel was lower, but the dominant price pressure is bullish for copper.

title: Mining industry 'booming' as copper jumps to highest level in 10 years
summary: The article’s headline highlights that copper has jumped to the highest level in 10 years and describes mining activity as “booming.” This directly points to near-term bullish sentiment and price pressure in copper markets, implying tighter perceived supply or stronger demand expectations ahead.

title: Green Economy Investment Strengthens Copper Outlook – Business
summary: The piece links stronger green-economy investment to rising copper demand from EVs, charging infrastructure, renewables and storage. It warns supply is underprepared after years of oversupply and delays in mine development, with output expected to peak soon. It concludes copper prices have already surged and may rise further.

title: Copper's surge toward record high hits Chinese industry as plants idle units
summary: Copper has surged toward record highs, but Chinese end-users are struggling with the spike. Some wire producers have idled units and delayed deliveries; rod and pipe orders slump. Physical indicators show weaker demand, including larger spot discounts and lower Yangshan premiums.

title: Copper Bonanza Challenge For Top Producer Chile
summary: Copper prices are near a ten-year high, supported by strong demand and infrastructure spending, but Chile’s political and labor disruptions add supply fears. Protests, a port strike backed by mining unions, and COVID-related delays to Codelco expansion raise concerns about continued output, alongside possible new mining taxes and regulatory uncertainty.

title: Bacon And Copper Lead Commodity Price Surge
summary: Global raw-material prices are surging, with copper “Dr Copper” topping $10,000/tonne and reaching a 10-year high. The rally is linked to strong Chinese demand, Chile labor protests disrupting mines and ports, a weaker US dollar, and accommodative Fed policy plus inflation/liquidity-driven commodity buying.

title: Weekly Financial Wrap: Rental Cars Prices, Copper and Job Scams Rise As Video Game Stocks Decline
summary: The piece mainly discusses rental car shortages and job scams, but it also flags a “copper boom.” It claims copper demand is rising as manufacturing revitalizes, attracting investors. With no detailed supply or inventory changes cited, the article supports a modest bullish expectation for copper prices in coming weeks.

title: Column: Indonesia, the puzzle of nickel's competing narratives
summary: INSG data shows nickel is in surplus (108,000 tonnes last year; further surplus expected), with LME forecasts pointing to refined supply exceeding demand and cash pricing below earlier levels. The article highlights Indonesia’s role and uncertainty in output growth and processing, keeping a bearish supply-demand narrative intact.

title: Indonesia, the puzzle of nickel's competing narratives: Andy Home
summary: INSG data and a Reuters poll point to continued nickel market oversupply, with refined supply exceeding demand and sizable LME warehouse inventories weighing sentiment. Indonesia is the key uncertainty as NPI and new processing moves accelerate, leaving supply-demand balance fluid and sustaining a bearish price narrative.

title: Rio Tinto executive meets Southland iwi over Tiwai Point aluminium smelter closure
summary: Rio Tinto executives met Southland iwi about Rio’s plan to close the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter by end-2024. The government suspended cleanup talks in March, and Rio provided a pollution assessment plan while adjusting power consumption as hydro lake levels stay low. Meetings aim to resolve cleanup information gaps.

title: Copper Looks Like an Investment With a Bright Future - SavingAdvice.com Blog
summary: Copper futures have surged, and the blog points to bullish drivers: China buying demand, infrastructure and green-energy plans in the US calling for substantial copper use, and electrification/EV growth. It also argues copper supply is tighter due to pandemic-related mining reductions, supporting expectations of higher prices.

title: Los Andes Copper Announces Investment By Queen's Road Capital and Appointment of Non-Executive Director
summary: Los Andes Copper announced a US$5 million convertible debenture investment to fund general purposes, specifically completion of the Vizcachitas project pre-feasibility study, after drilling approval. The company is developing a copper-molybdenum porphyry in Chile, potentially advancing toward production and supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Provides a Western U.S. Copper Portfolio Update
summary: EMX Royalty Corp. announced it has optioned four additional Western U.S. copper projects and extended its alliance with South32 for 2021–2022 work programs. The release details exploration plans, drilling targets, and EMX’s retained royalty interests across several Arizona and New Mexico properties.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Kamoa-Kakula to Begin Copper Production Within a Month
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says the Kamoa-Kakula Phase 1 concentrator is nearly complete and has advanced commissioning, with first copper concentrate production expected by end-May or early June. It also details rising mined ore and contained copper in pre-production stockpiles, increasing near-term expectations for copper supply.

title: Kamoa-Kakula to Begin Copper Production Within a Month
summary: Ivanhoe Mines’ Kamoa-Kakula project in the DRC advanced Phase 1 concentrator commissioning, targeting first copper concentrate by end-May/early June rather than later in the year. April ore and stockpile growth raise contained copper volumes, increasing near-term supply expectations and supporting copper sentiment.

title: The world risks 'running out of copper' — and here's how high prices may rise as the economy reopens, BofA warns
summary: Bank of America warns the world risks “running out of copper” as demand rises with economic reopening. It notes inventories near 15-year lows, covering roughly 3.3 weeks of demand, and forecasts continuing inventory declines and market deficits. Strategists suggest copper prices could spike toward $13,000/ton.

title: Aluminum shortage forces DMV to hit brakes on plate replacement program :: WRAL.com
summary: North Carolina’s DMV indefinitely suspended an expanded license-plate replacement program due to a worldwide aluminum shortage. Prison inmates produced 400–500 plates daily, but the program scaled output much higher. Available aluminum covers only a fraction of planned replacements, so officials pause until supplies improve, potentially delaying further demand.

title: NCDMV suspends replacement of older license plates due to aluminum shortage
summary: North Carolina’s DMV indefinitely suspended replacement of older license plates due to a worldwide aluminum shortage. The agency said the vendor has aluminum for ~160,000 plates and another shipment is expected by mid-May. The disruption may delay the state’s replacement schedule, but volumes are limited.

title: Aluminum Shortage Impacts License Plate Industry
summary: North Carolina’s DMV is indefinitely suspending its license-plate replacement program due to a worldwide aluminum shortage. The replacement effort had increased production demand roughly 10-fold versus normal first-time plates, with 640,000 replacements already made and 1.4 million more projected for 2021.

title: Scrap Copper Prices NI
summary: The piece is a short update for scrap copper prices in Northern Ireland, noting that scrap rates depend on metal availability and fluctuating market rates. It references a scrap price website but provides no specific figures or external catalysts, making the immediate price pressure direction uncertain.

title: BeMetals Corp.: BeMetals Announces Substantial Increase to Mineral Resource at the High-Grade South Mountain Zinc-Silver-Gold-Copper Project in Idaho
summary: BeMetals announced an updated NI 43-101 mineral resource for its South Mountain zinc-silver-gold-copper project in Idaho, increasing measured/indicated and inferred resources. The grades include copper alongside zinc and precious metals, but the news is exploration/resource-oriented rather than a near-term supply or demand change for copper.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Reports More High-Grade Massive Sulphide Intercepts Outside of the Resource Area at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon reports additional shallow, high-grade massive sulphide intercepts in the CGO East area of its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project in Minnesota. Results show strong Ni and Cu grades and could extend the mine plan, but there is no production update, so near-term price impact is likely modest.

title: Los Andes Copper secures environmental nod for drilling at Chilean mine
summary: Los Andes Copper received Chilean environmental approval to drill up to 350 holes at its Vizcachitas copper-molybdenum project. The campaign enables completion of a prefeasibility study and includes infill drilling and geophysical testing. Production is targeted for 2025/26, with PFS due in Q4 this year.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Pacific Ridge Continues to Build Its Portfolio of BC Copper Gold Projects with the Acquisition of the RDP Project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration announced it will acquire 100% of the RDP copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia and plans mapping, sampling, and geophysics for the 2021 season, with drilling expected later in the year. The release provides historical copper-gold grades from RDP targets but no production or supply changes.

title: Aluminum shortage forces DMV to hit brakes on plate replacement program
summary: The article says an aluminium shortage is leading the DMV to slow or stop its license-plate replacement program. The pause points to constrained aluminium supply for plate production or procurement, which typically reinforces tightness perceptions and can provide short-term support for aluminium prices.

title: How copper could double to $9
summary: A Globe and Mail roundup cites BofA research suggesting copper could spike on tight fundamentals and low inventories. It notes scrap supply is critical and projects potential inventory depletion if secondary supply fails to rise, implying violent price swings and higher upside versus current ~$4.50/lb.

title: Talon Metals Reports More High-Grade Massive Sulphide Intercepts Outside of the Resource Area at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reported high-grade shallow nickel-copper sulphide intercepts in the CGO East area outside its current resource at the Tamarack project, including up to 4.99% Ni and 1.66% Cu over 5.1m. The company says results support potential inclusion in the mine plan and resource expansion, potentially improving future supply expectations.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp. Updates Announcement to Acquire Punitaqui Copper-Gold Mine and Concurrent Financing of up to C$15,000,000
summary: Battery Mineral Resources says it is nearing closing of a financing and acquisition of the Punitaqui copper-gold mine in Chile, including settlement of a US$10m indebtedness and up to US$5m milestone payments. The company plans equity funding to support acquisition and restart/exploration activities, subject to regulatory approvals.

title: Chile's copper output falls 1.2% in March on lower Escondida volumes
summary: Chile’s copper output fell 1.2% in March, attributed to lower production volumes from Escondida. The reduction from one of the world’s largest copper operations is a direct supply signal, potentially worsening near-term market balance and contributing bearish pressure on copper prices in the short horizon.

title: Chile's copper output falls 1.2% in March | American Metal Market
summary: American Metal Market reports that Chile’s copper output fell 1.2% in March. As Chile is a key supplier to global markets, weaker near-term production can reduce supply expectations and influence short-term copper pricing. The news is supply-side and likely to weigh on copper sentiment over the next days.

title: Brigadier Intercepts 7.63 g/t Gold, 11 g/t Silver and 0.26% Copper Across 0.5 Metres at Picachos
summary: Brigadier Gold reported additional drill and trench assay results from its Picachos gold-silver project in Sinaloa, including copper-bearing intercepts (notably 2.12% Cu over 1.7 m and 0.26% Cu over 0.5 m). The update is exploratory, with no production or supply commitment, limiting near-term copper price influence.

title: Material Matters: Nickel, Aluminium & Iron Ore
summary: Macquarie expects nickel to stay in deficit into the June quarter after a March production shortfall; disruptions reduced briquette output and port stocks fell, supporting nickel tightness. Morgan Stanley warns semiconductor shortages may cut vehicle demand, with aluminium exposed to automotive output declines and potential weaker demand/scrap prices.

title: Material Matters: Nickel, Aluminium & Iron Ore
summary: Nickel: Macquarie expects a deficit to persist into the June quarter, citing below-expected March production, briquette supply disruptions, falling port stocks and rising briquette premiums. Aluminium: Morgan Stanley flags semiconductor shortages and vehicle-output cuts could reduce Q2 aluminium demand (~5%), with scrap demand also weakening.

title: Ero Copper reports record first quarter copper production and financial results
summary: Ero Copper reported record Q1 copper production of 12,638 tonnes from its MCSA complex, driven by higher-than-budget grades and strong metallurgical recoveries, and reiterated 2021 copper production guidance. The press release emphasizes improved operational performance and cost metrics, potentially supporting near-term market sentiment for copper supply.

title: Windfall Geotek Delivers AI Targets for Capella Minerals Copper - Zinc - Gold - Silver Kjoli VMS Project In Norway
summary: Windfall Geotek says it delivered 13 high-probability copper-zinc exploration targets and 11 gold-silver targets for Capella Minerals’ Kjøli VMS project in Norway. Targets are near past-producing Killingdal mines, reducing the exploration area by 90% to guide upcoming summer 2021 field drilling.

title: Barrick Gold reports Q1 profit up as higher gold and copper prices help boost revenue | iNFOnews
summary: Barrick Gold reported higher Q1 profit, attributing revenue growth to higher gold and—especially—copper prices. The CEO said copper’s share of Barrick’s gold-equivalent ounces will rise as spot pricing tops $4.50/lb. Copper realized pricing and copper revenue increased quarter over quarter despite lower production volumes.

title: Barrick Q1 profit up as higher gold, copper prices help boost revenue
summary: Barrick reported higher Q1 profit and revenue, attributing the improvement to higher gold and copper prices. The report suggests copper is currently trading firmer than earlier levels, which can support near-term market sentiment around copper demand and pricing, though it is not a new supply-demand shock.

title: Barrick Gold reports Q1 profit up as higher gold and copper prices help boost revenue
summary: Barrick Gold reported Q1 profit rising to US$538 million, helped by higher realized gold and especially copper prices. Realized copper averaged US$4.12/lb versus US$2.23 a year earlier, while copper production fell. The results point to stronger copper pricing conditions supportive of near-term copper sentiment.

title: CARDS AI Analysis Identifies 13 Priority High-Grade Copper Targets at Kjøli
summary: Capella Minerals reports CARDS AI analysis identifying 13 priority copper-zinc target areas at its Kjøli high-grade massive sulfide project in Norway and plans near-term evaluation and drill testing after permitting. The release focuses on exploration pipeline updates rather than any immediate production or trade changes.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Provides Ground and Borehole Electromagnetic Update for the Kenbridge Nickel Project, Kenora Mining District, Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. reported TDEM geophysical results at its Kenbridge North and Kenbridge Deposit areas, identifying stronger conductors and indicating nickel-hosting material continues at depth and along strike. The company plans a first-pass drilling program to test extensions, aiming to upgrade resources and improve nickel and copper grades.

title: Barrick Q1 profit up as higher gold, copper prices boost revenue
summary: Barrick reported higher Q1 profit, attributing the improvement to higher prices for gold and copper. The headline implies copper has been trading stronger, which would generally reinforce near-term market expectations for copper demand and price direction over the coming days.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Pledges Net-zero Greenhouse Gas Emissions at the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines pledges net-zero operational greenhouse gas emissions (Scope 1 and 2) at its Kamoa-Kakula copper mine by electrifying its underground fleet using battery or hydrogen-powered equipment. The mine already uses renewable hydropower and is expected to start producing copper concentrates soon, supporting positive copper outlook.

title: Surging copper prices boost Barrick's profit as miner weighs bigger move into the metal
summary: Barrick CEO Mark Bristow says copper’s rebound has boosted profits and highlights a strong rise in the company’s realized copper price to $4.12/lb in Q1. The discussion of potential deals is secondary, while the main takeaway is that copper prices are moving higher on demand and speculation.

title: China's super-charged buying reshapes the copper market
summary: China’s refined copper net imports surged 38% to a record 4.4 million tonnes last year, driving LME copper from $4,371 to above $10,000. However, imports are already plateauing and expected to slow as state stockpiling fades and commercial restocking diminishes, reshaping supply-demand expectations.

title: Barrick Gold 1Q Profit Rises 35%, Higher Copper And Gold Prices Boost Revenue
summary: Barrick Gold reported a 35% rise in first-quarter profit. The company said the improvement was boosted by higher copper and gold prices, which increased revenue. The news therefore directly reflects stronger copper price conditions, which can support sentiment around industrial metals in the near term.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Pledges Net-zero Greenhouse Gas Emissions at the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines pledged net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions at its Kamoa-Kakula copper mine by electrifying the mining fleet using electric batteries or hydrogen fuel cells. The project is already powered by renewable hydropower, and the company expects first copper concentrates soon, with expansion targeting up to 800,000 tonnes/year.

title: Century Aluminum Co Q1 adjusted earnings of -$0.54 per share
summary: Century Aluminum Co reported Q1 results with a large adjusted loss (-$52.5 million, -$0.54 per share) and weaker overall performance versus the prior year. The earnings deterioration can affect expectations for aluminium producers’ operating outlook and industry sentiment, potentially putting downward pressure on aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Calgary man faces charges after police investigation into copper wire thefts at oil lease sites
summary: Alberta RCMP arrested a Calgary man accused of breaking into southern Alberta oil lease sites and stealing copper wire, metal signs, and tools. Authorities cite damages and stolen property over $85,000 and note copper wire theft is rising in rural commercial sites, potentially increasing replacement demand.

title: NC DMV suspends replacement of older license plates due to aluminum shortage
summary: North Carolina’s DMV will suspend replacement of older license plates because of an aluminum shortage. The move signals constraints in aluminum availability for producing plate replacements, which can tighten near-term supply expectations for aluminum and provide mild price support in the next few weeks.

title: Barrick Gold : expects growing exposure to copper as price escalation boosts Q1 profits
summary: Barrick Gold said copper is becoming more important to its earnings after copper hit 10-year highs, lifting Q1 copper revenues 31% as realized copper prices rose to about $4.12/lb. The CEO plans to expand copper exploration, with copper expected to form a growing share of gold-equivalent output.

title: Copper Holds Near $10,000 as China's Return Puts Focus on Demand
summary: Copper is reported to be holding near $10,000, with market attention turning to demand as China returns. This framing suggests traders are weighing near-term demand support for copper prices, implying a modest positive bias rather than a clear reversal.

title: Shanghai aluminum hits 11-yr high as China-Australia tensions stoke supply woes
summary: Shanghai aluminum prices surged to an 11-year high, with the June contract up about 2% after China-Australia tensions sparked worries over reduced supply from Australia, a key source of bauxite and alumina. LME three-month aluminum also rose, reflecting bullish sentiment for physical availability.

title: Zambia Shuts Seized Copper Mine as Prices Soar Toward Record
summary: The report says Zambia has shut down a seized copper mine as copper prices climb toward record highs. The action reduces expected near-term copper output, tightening supply expectations and adding upward pressure to copper prices within the coming days and weeks.

title: Primary aluminium inventories remained unchanged on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data says China’s primary aluminium ingot inventories stayed unchanged at 1.12 million mt as of May 6. Stocks were steady overall, with slight increases in Shanghai, Nanhai and Tianjin and a small decline in Gongyi due to smaller arrivals, implying limited near-term supply pressure.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 5,100 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show Chinese aluminium billet stocks across key consumption regions rose 9% week-on-week to 139,100 mt as May 6, driven mainly by Labor Day holiday effects. Shipments increased, but downstream buying sentiment remained lukewarm despite fears of high prices, suggesting inventories may not fall next week.

title: Zambia denies report it shuttered Konkola Copper Mines
summary: Zambia denied a Bloomberg report that it shuttered Konkola Copper Mines, saying the operations are currently running and not being placed on care and maintenance. The denial counters earlier claims that production was halted due to lack of funds, easing expectations of near-term copper supply disruption.

title: US$953mil Singaporean fund ensnared by alleged nickel fraud
summary: A Singapore investor, Vickers Venture Partners, is implicated in a suspected nickel trading fraud involving Envy Global Trading and businessman Ng Yu Zhi. Authorities are reviewing the case after claims of fake nickel trades and falsified bank transfers and account statements totaling hundreds of millions. The news points to financial misconduct, not clear physical market disruption.

title: Analysts: Copper Prices Could Double To $20,000 Per Ton
summary: Analysts argue copper prices could surge toward $20,000/ton due to strong demand from energy transition technologies and insufficient new mine/project supply. The IEA highlights a supply gap by 2030 and declining ore grades, while Bank of America notes upside if inventories deplete. Aluminium is cited as needed for electricity networks.

title: MORNING VIEW: Copper, aluminium upbeat, other metals tread water in high ground
summary: A morning market wrap notes three-month copper up 0.6% and aluminium up 0.4%, with other base metals mostly weaker. SHFE copper also rises (June +1.3%). The piece links the upbeat tone to easing bond yields and a weaker/flat dollar backdrop, implying upside support for industrial metals.

title: MORNING VIEW: Copper, aluminium upbeat, other metals tread water in high ground
summary: The note says three-month copper and aluminium were up on the morning, alongside stronger SHFE copper and generally positive base-metals tone. It attributes support to easing bond yields, a weaker dollar, and bullish expectations tied to stimulus and potential infrastructure spending, while other metals were flatter or mixed.

title: Chile copper miners cry foul as royalty bill advances to Senate
summary: Chile’s lower house approved an opposition-led bill imposing a progressive royalty on copper sales, increasing the rate as prices rise (up to very high marginal rates at higher copper prices). Chilean miners warn it could chill investment and slow supply. The measure now moves to the Senate.

title: Aluminium extends rally as China-Australia tensions add to supply fears
summary: Aluminium prices extended their rally toward $2,500/t, helped by China–Australia tensions and fears over supply of bauxite/alumina. Investors also anticipate China’s crackdown on polluting smelters will tighten output. LME cash conditions improved, supporting further upside despite some notes that near-term supply remains adequate.

title: Copper Price Hits All-Time-High In Commodities Bull Run
summary: Copper futures jumped to a record high after China’s five-day holiday, with July copper up about 1.7%. The rally is linked to reopening-driven demand and improving sentiment, while forecasts from major banks point to continued strength amid tight inventories and supportive decarbonization demand themes.

title: Monster Beverages reports Q1 miss, warns of aluminum-can shortage
summary: Monster Beverage shares fell after a Q1 earnings miss and guidance concerns. The company warned it is operating amid an aluminum-can shortage across North America and Europe. Tighter availability of aluminum packaging demand could support near-term aluminum market expectations as can makers compete for supply.

title: In Top Copper Nation Chile, a Giant Tax Hike Moves a Step Closer
summary: Chile’s lower house approved a progressive tax on copper sales that adds marginal rates as copper prices rise, topping at 75% for prices above $4/lb. The bill could sharply increase mining royalties, possibly deterring investment. While higher copper prices may offset some effects, higher expected costs are bearish for copper near term.

title: Chile Lawmakers Take First Step Towards New Copper Mining Tax
summary: Chile’s lower house approved a bill proposing an additional 3% royalty on copper sales, alongside lithium, to fund social plans and environmental compensation. The proposal is opposed by the president and mining industry, citing existing heavy taxes. It now moves to the Senate, against a backdrop of recent copper strength.

title: VTB lends Russian Copper Company RUB 40 billion, EUR 82.7 million
summary: VTB Bank provided Russian Copper Company (RMK Group) a RUB 40 billion and EUR 82.7 million loan for five years to fund expenses for a copper processing plant (Mikheevskiy GOK) and acquire a 100% stake in Invest Razvitie LLC, plus refinancing existing debt. VTB becomes the sole creditor.

title: Tiwai Point aluminium smelter chief executive Stew Hamilton resigns
summary: Tiwai Point aluminium smelter CEO Stew Hamilton resigns to join Mercury Energy. The smelter had a planned shutdown this year but received power-deal extensions until at least 2024. It consumes 13% of New Zealand’s power and has complained about high power costs amid depressed global aluminium prices.

title: Zambia denies previous reports of closing the Konkola copper mine_SMM
summary: Zambia’s Ministry of Mines denied foreign reports that the Konkola copper mine (KCM) had been closed due to lack of funds. Officials said operations continue with no evidence of suspension or stagnation, and the interim liquidator also indicated no maintenance plans. The news eases short-term supply concerns for copper.

title: Copper climbs to all-time high of US$10,232 in London
summary: London copper is reported to have climbed to an all-time high of US$10,232. The update points to strong spot-market demand or supply tightness expectations, implying upward near-term price pressure for copper relative to other industrial metals.

title: China April copper imports fall 12.2% on month as high prices deter purchases
summary: China’s April copper imports fell 12.2% month-on-month to 484,890 tonnes as decade-high copper prices discouraged purchasing, though logistics delays are easing and May arrivals may remain elevated. Copper manufacturing activity also slowed. Aluminum exports fell 1.4% as high Shanghai aluminum prices deterred overseas demand.

title: China April copper imports fall 12.2% on the month as high prices deter purchases
summary: China’s April copper imports fell 12.2% month-on-month to 484,890 tonnes as record-high prices deterred purchases. Copper concentrate imports also declined. The report notes aluminium exports down 1.4% as decade-high Shanghai prices discouraged overseas buyers, suggesting weaker demand for both metals.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose 900 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported Shanghai bonded-area copper stocks rose 900 mt to 397,600 mt as of May 7, driven by larger arrivals and overseas inbound goods plus domestic smelter exports into bonded warehouses. Demand for customs declarations was sluggish before the holiday, and further increases are expected after warehouse operations fully recover.

title: MORNING VIEW: Base metals prices mixed; aluminium lurches higher with copper, lead following
summary: Fastmarkets’ morning view reports mixed base metals performance, highlighting that aluminium “lurches higher” and that copper is moving higher as well, with lead following. The article also notes procedural delays/corrections to some assessment publications, but the headline takeaway is an aluminium-led upside move.

title: UK construction grows rapidly amid surging costs; iron ore and copper at record highs – business live
summary: UK stocks are rising as miners outperform, with investors expecting profits from a surge in iron ore and copper. The piece notes copper trading at an all-time high and highlights stronger-than-expected Eurozone economic data, supporting construction and industrial demand outlooks. Sentiment is broadly risk-on for commodities.

title: Copper, Iron Ore Hit Records As Demand Surges But Stocks Mixed
summary: US weak jobs data boosted hopes for continued fiscal/monetary support, pressuring the dollar lower and lifting commodities broadly. With economies reopening and production ramping up, copper broke above $10,300/ton and analysts expect further gains. Infrastructure and decarbonization trends are cited as additional demand drivers.

title: Copper hits record high on industry and speculative buying
summary: Copper surged to a record high on the LME, supported by industrial and speculative buying alongside rosy economic data. The piece notes supply tightness and weak warehouse stocks. It also reports LME aluminium rising to a multi-year high and nickel moving higher, signaling broad bullish momentum across industrial metals.

title: Copper jumps to record as growth bets supercharge commodities
summary: Copper surged to a record high as markets priced a global pandemic rebound. Bloomberg links the rally to stimulus and vaccine rollouts that raise demand expectations and could strain supply. Copper’s role as an economic bellwether and in the green-energy transition is cited as supporting continued gains.

title: LME copper hits all-time high on tight supply, demand hopes
summary: LME three-month copper surged to record highs on tight supply and hopes for strong demand tied to global recovery and energy-sector growth. Shanghai copper also climbed sharply. The piece notes LME aluminium rose with copper, with traders pointing to supply worries as a China-Australia spat deepens.

title: Copper, Iron Ore Hit Records As Demand Surges
summary: US jobs data disappointed, but investors saw continued fiscal/monetary support and a weaker dollar, helping lift commodity prices. With global economies reopening and production ramping, copper “broke to an all-time high” above $10,300/ton and analysts expect further upside on supply tightness concerns.

title: Copper looks to set fresh record Friday as economic recovery, electric-cars drive rise in metal's price
summary: Copper futures were near a new record, up about 2.4% on the day and set for a strong weekly rise. The move is linked to global economic recovery and growing popularity of electric vehicles, which are expected to boost demand for copper in the near term.

title: Atlas Mining swings to profit on higher copper prices
summary: Atlas Mining reported a first-quarter profit turnaround, saying results were driven by a 55% jump in copper prices to $3.93 per pound. While its Carmen Copper subsidiary saw weaker production due to lower ore grades and concentrate shipments, the company linked performance to improved copper market conditions.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 7): Nonferrous metals on the SHFE rose across the board, aluminium surged 2.93%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals mostly higher on May 7, with copper up 2.63%, aluminium up 2.93%, and nickel up 1.2% versus prior levels. The move is attributed to positive US jobless claims data and broader supportive macro sentiment, alongside open-interest changes reflecting renewed trading interest.

title: Quaterra Resources Inc.: Quaterra's Previously Announced Drill Program Now Underway at MacArthur Copper Oxide Property
summary: Quaterra Resources began a 7,000–10,000 ft core drilling program at its MacArthur copper oxide property in Nevada, aiming to upgrade resources and support a prefeasibility study. The company highlights that the project is acid-leach sensitive to copper prices and acid costs, but no near-term production or supply changes are announced.

title: 'Doctor Copper' In Rude Health But US Jobs Growth Anaemic
summary: Disappointing US jobs growth pushed stimulus and continued accommodative monetary policy hopes, weakening the dollar and lifting broad commodities. The article explicitly says copper surged to an all-time high above $10,300/ton on Friday, attributing gains to global reopening, supply concerns, and longer-term electrification demand.

title: Mining stocks climb in London, as copper surges to all-time highs
summary: London’s FTSE 100 rose Friday, with mining stocks gaining as copper surged to all-time highs. The piece attributes equity strength to record copper prices driving performance for mining companies, alongside unrelated Barclays movement after an activist sold its stake. Macro noise from U.S. jobs data was secondary.

title: Copper, iron ore hit record highs - Taipei Times
summary: Copper surged to an all-time high above $10,200/ton amid a strong global economic rebound and worries about supply constraints after COVID disruptions. Analysts expect prices to remain supported by decarbonization-driven demand, while China’s copper ore imports fell and some buyers slow production or extend delivery times due to costs.

title: Copper soars to all time high on economic recovery optimism
summary: Copper prices surged to an all-time high on global recovery optimism, with stimulus and vaccine rollouts boosting expected demand. The piece cites disrupted trade, lack of mine investment, and tight supply conditions implying a growing deficit. Chile’s proposed copper sales taxes also raise future supply-investment risks, reinforcing bullish sentiment.

title: Tight supply is still expected to strengthen copper prices into a long-term bull market?_SMM
summary: The article argues copper remains strongly supported by tight mine supply from Peru and Chile epidemic disruptions, which may reduce output and tighten concentrate availability. It notes copper prices hitting a decade high and breaking $10,000/LME. Analysts expect continued bullish pricing, though macro and monetary policy could affect timing.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 110,000 wmt to 5.48 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show Chinese nickel ore inventories across ports rose by 110,000 wmt to 5.48 million wmt from April 30 to May 7, with Ni content at 43,300 mt. Stocks at major ports rose 170,000 wmt to 4.15 million wmt. A slow near-term inventory increase is expected.

title: Copper Just Smashed Past a Record. Here's What You Need to Know
summary: Copper prices surged to an all-time high, with London futures reaching about $10,440/ton. The rally is attributed to investors’ bets on rising demand from green energy, EVs, and infrastructure, while new mine supply is slow and expensive. Spot demand is starting to cool, but expectations still support higher prices.

title: MIDAS SHARE TIPS: Copper-bottom mining returns with Trident
summary: The piece highlights rapidly rising industrial metals prices, saying copper has topped $10,000 per tonne and is expected to continue climbing. It also notes aluminium and nickel have jumped since last spring, attributing strength to fast economic recovery and government infrastructure spending. It promotes Trident Royalties as benefiting from this demand.

title: China Copper Smelters to Cut Concentrate Purchases in Green Push
summary: China’s largest copper smelters plan to reduce concentrate purchases this year by about 1.26 million tons (~300,000 tons of copper) as part of China’s emissions-reduction drive. The move reflects a shift toward limiting new capacity and using more scrap, lowering demand for mined concentrate and weighing on copper.

title: Exclusive: China's primary aluminium output rose 9.87% YoY to 3.25 million mt in April_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s April primary aluminium output rose 9.87% YoY to 3.25Mt, with operating rates around 91.3% and additional restarts planned in May (Gansu Zhongrui, Shanxian Hengkang). Alumina production also remains solid. While demand supports lower inventory days, higher supply outlook is likely pressure on aluminium.

title: Copper hits record high on demand hope, tight supply
summary: Copper prices surged to record highs on both the LME and Shanghai markets, driven by improving demand hopes and tight concentrate supply. Investors cited global economic recovery and green-energy investment, while reports said Chinese smelters plan to cut raw concentrate purchases, tightening feedstock and supporting higher prices.

title: Copper hits record high on higher demand hopes, tighter supply
summary: Copper prices hit record highs on the LME and Shanghai after hopes for stronger economic and green-energy demand coincided with tighter concentrate supply. Three-month copper on the LME climbed to an all-time high. Chinese smelters agreed to cut concentrate purchases, reinforcing scarcity sentiment; aluminium also rose.

title: Copper sprints to record high as investors fear missing out
summary: Copper surged to record highs on the LME and Shanghai as investors chase momentum and some physical buyers capitulate after waiting for lower prices. Support came from tight copper concentrate supply and reports that Chinese smelters agreed to cut 2021 concentrate purchases. Aluminium also hit fresh peaks; nickel was slightly down.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 10): Shanghai nonferrous metals rose broadly, copper soared 4.81%_SMM
summary: SMM says Shanghai nonferrous metals broadly rose, with SHFE copper jumping 4.81% and aluminium up 3.68% as the USD index weakened. It notes high copper prices cooled consumption and some smelters halted production for maintenance, while nickel was nearly unchanged.

title: Castillo Copper provides update
summary: Castillo Copper says approvals allow it to restart exploration at the Mt Oxide Project in Australia, with geophysics and planned drilling at the Big One and Arya targets, plus continued work across Zambia and NSW assets. Management notes copper’s rise on fears of forward supply deficits, supporting bullish sentiment.

title: Stocks cheer prospects for low rates, copper shines
summary: World stocks and copper hit new peaks as markets bet interest rates will stay low and the economy recovers. Copper rallied to record highs on the LME and SHFE, driven by improved demand expectations amid tightening supply and a weaker dollar after disappointing U.S. nonfarm payrolls data.

title: 199-day queue for aluminium at Istim warehouses in Port Klang
summary: The headline reports a 199-day queue for aluminium at Istim warehouses in Port Klang, suggesting significant delays in metal availability and constrained warehouse throughput. Such physical-market tightness can support higher aluminium premiums and near-term prices as buyers face longer delivery/handling times.

title: FPX Nickel Provides Exploration Update and Prepares Drilling Programs at Decar Nickel District in Central British Columbia
summary: FPX Nickel provided plans for maiden drilling at the Van Target and infill drilling at the Baptiste Deposit within the Decar Nickel District. The programs aim to convert inferred to indicated resources and test for new nickel-iron alloy (awaruite) mineralization. No near-term production or supply disruptions are indicated.

title: Hot commodities: Iron ore surges 10%, copper extends record run
summary: Copper prices extended their record run, rising to a fresh LME high on optimism for environmental-driven demand and potential tightening in Chinese concentrate flows, alongside expectations of supportive central-bank policy. The piece also links the broader commodities boom to inflation concerns and notes aluminium slipped after earlier gains.

title: Copper hits record high amid broad-based surge in commodities
summary: Copper rose to a new record $4.90/lb, with gains attributed to a rebound in Chinese demand, supply-side jitters (Chile producer tax risk and stricter Chinese emissions targets for smelters), and accommodative monetary policy. The broader industrial-commodity rally also lifted aluminium alongside copper.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Federal government considering plan to repurpose alumina refinery for fuel storage
summary: Sky News reports the Australian federal government is considering repurposing an alumina refinery for fuel storage. Such a change would reduce alumina refining capacity, potentially constraining feedstock for aluminum smelters. That supply risk could weigh on aluminium price expectations over the next several days to weeks.

title: Escondida and Spence copper mines in Chile, owned by BHP Billiton, face the threat of strike_SMM
summary: Workers’ union at BHP’s Escondida and Spence copper mines in Chile is asking members to vote on a strike after stalled contract talks. A strike threat is already affecting operations amid tight concentrate supply and rising prices. Even with mediation required, near-term production risk boosts bullish copper expectations.

title: Copper eases from record high as weak China demand stalls rally
summary: Shanghai copper prices slipped 1.5% after a rally to a record high, as tepid demand from China’s industrial buyers weighed. The Yangshan copper premium fell to the lowest since February 2016, indicating subdued appetite for imported copper. Nickel and aluminium also fell amid cautious sentiment.

title: London copper rises as traders bet on bullish demand outlook
summary: London LME copper rose about 0.9% as traders bet on stronger demand from renewable energy and EV sectors alongside gradual economic recovery and stimulus. The piece also notes rising copper related supply tightness and speculative positioning. Aluminium also increased, while nickel fell on Shanghai data.

title: MAX Resource Corp.: Max Resource Significantly Expands the CONEJO Copper-Silver Zone at CESAR North, Colombia
summary: Max Resource reports new assay results expanding the CONEJO copper-silver zone in Colombia’s CESAR North project by 500% to 3.2 km by 1.6 km, with multiple panels returning >1% and highlights up to ~3% copper. The company frames the find as scalable and open.

title: Max Resource Significantly Expands the CONEJO Copper-Silver Zone at CESAR North, Colombia
summary: Max Resource reports expanded assay results widening the CONEJO copper-silver zone at its CESAR North project in Colombia, with multiple high-grade copper and silver intercepts and the zone remaining open in all directions. It indicates growing potential for a large copper-silver system, but remains exploration-stage.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Provides Update on Drill Program at MPD Copper-Gold Porphyry Project in Southern British Columbia
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. provided an update on its fully funded 2021 drill program at the MPD copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia. Up to 30,000 metres are planned, with drilling progressing and assaying expected late Q2/Q3. Intercepts at the Gate Zone continue and an expanded permit supports further drilling.

title: BTU Metals Corp.: BTU Defines New Base Metal Drill Targets East and South of the TNT Copper-Silver-Gold Discovery and Provides Drilling Update
summary: BTU Metals reports results from geophysical survey reinterpretations at its Dixie Lake TNT copper-silver-gold discovery, identifying additional conductive targets to drill this month and suggesting potential base-metal bearing sulphide mineralization. The company also updates on drilling at Pakwash North and expects further sampling and lab results soon.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 11): Shanghai nonferrous metals fell across the board, nickel declined 1.35%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals fell across the board on May 11. Copper eased 0.96%, aluminium weakened 0.72%, and nickel declined 1.35% as contracts closed lower with declining open interest. The note links the move to broader market softness and demand/supply conditions, with inventories cited for aluminium support and weakness still dominating.

title: Signs of investor vertigo as copper hits record highs
summary: Copper extended its rally, breaking the LME three-month record to around $10,747/tonne, with funds rebuilding long exposure after strong technical closes and options/hedging related short-covering. However, Chinese trading volumes/open interest and refined import momentum are weakening, while premiums hit multi-year lows, adding caution.

title: Copper load of this: Openreach outlines 77 new locations where it'll stop selling legacy phone and broadband products
summary: Openreach says it will stop selling legacy copper-based phone and broadband services in 77 UK exchange locations from April 29, 2022, encouraging switches to fibre-delivered products. It cites cost of running parallel networks and plans to end new analogue copper products nationwide by 2025.

title: Completion of Acquisition of Highly Prospective Copper Projects in Northern Territory
summary: Comet Resources says it has completed the acquisition of a portfolio of copper-gold and related base-metal projects in Australia’s Northern Territory. The assets include multiple prospects with reported copper assays (up to 1%+ and higher in rock chips). Management frames the deal as adding to copper exposure amid strong prices.

title: Copper bounces back as bullish investors bet on shortages
summary: Copper prices rebounded on the LME, with three-month copper up 0.8% to about $10,465/t by 1600 GMT after a volatile session. Investors renewed buying, betting that supply constraints and stronger demand could drive the market toward fresh highs, following a prior pullback.

title: 'Don't stop buying now': Investors bet billions on copper's bull run continuing
summary: Investors are continuing to buy copper aggressively through ETFs/ETPs and leveraged futures/CTA positioning, after copper has already doubled and reached record highs. Wall Street strategists argue higher levels are possible if supply falters and green/EV demand grows. The inflow-driven financial demand narrative supports a bullish near-term outlook.

title: Copper's Key Role in Europe's Green Energy Plans
summary: Europe’s green energy and EV electrification plans are framed as a growing source of copper demand, including for vehicles, public charging cabling/power electronics, and energy storage. The article notes Europe may struggle to grow mine supply, relying on imports and scrap, supporting a bullish near-term copper outlook.

title: Aluminium Industry reiterates urgency for 5% RoDTEP rate for economic sustainability
summary: India’s Aluminium Association urged the government to implement at least a 5% RoDTEP remission rate, saying delays and ambiguity in notified sector-wise rates are harming aluminium exporters. It also cites MEIS withdrawal/blocking and high unrebated taxes raising production costs, threatening competitiveness and near-term export flows.

title: Operating rates at copper plate, strip and foil producers continued to rise in April amid strong demand from the automobile and electronics industries_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates for copper plate, strip and foil producers rose to 85.59% in April, supported by improving new-energy vehicle battery demand and strong electronics orders. Raw-material stockpiling stayed limited due to high copper prices. For May, rates are expected to ease as copper prices prompt slower processing.

title: Operating rates at copper rod producers using copper cathode as raw material registered a new low in April _SMM
summary: SMM survey data show copper rod producers using copper cathode saw operating rates rise slightly month-on-month but fall sharply year-on-year to 70.59% in April, the lowest since 2016. High copper prices curbed wire and cable consumption, forcing output reductions to manage finished inventory. May rates are expected to dip further.

title: High copper prices weighed on copper tube operating rates, a low season may come earlier_SMM
summary: SMM reports copper tube producer operating rates rose in April but copper’s high price weighed on processors. Rising costs and cautious restocking reduced raw-material inventory. Orders for May reportedly fell over 15% versus April, with small producers hit harder; operating rates are expected to drop in May.

title: Copper prices hit new high on post-pandemic recovery hopes
summary: Copper futures hit fresh highs as post-pandemic recovery hopes boost demand expectations and global shortages/declining inventories tighten supply. The rebound is linked to China’s heavy refined-copper buying and imports. Separately, possible union strikes at major Chilean mines add near-term supply risk, reinforcing bullish copper sentiment.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc Forms Alliance With Freeport-McMoRan Mineral Properties Canada Inc. To Advance Its JOY Copper-Gold Porphyry District, British Columbia
summary: Amarc Resources said Freeport-McMoRan can earn up to 70% of Amarc’s JOY copper-gold porphyry district in British Columbia by funding staged work, including a $4 million first-year exploration program. Drilling and geophysical permits are in place, with plans to advance delineation and targets.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 12): Shanghai nonferrous metals rose for the most part, copper increased 1.62%_SMM
summary: SMM says Shanghai base metals rose broadly on May 12. Copper increased 1.62% and nickel 1.42%, while aluminium added 0.25%. Commentary cited improving US economic expectations and suggested aluminium import arbitrage intermittently opened, which could slow inventory declines, supporting prices in the near term.

title: Aluminium Associations in the US, Europe, Canada and Japan Urge G7 Governments to Take Concrete Steps to Deliver More Free, Fair and Open Trade
summary: US, Europe, Canada and Japan aluminium associations urge G7 governments to tighten trade rules on state support and below-market finance. Citing an OECD report, they argue China’s subsidized financing expanded aluminium capacity and depressed global prices, harming unsubsidized competitors. They call for fair, open markets to restore competitiveness.

title: Nicola Mining Inc.: Nicola Mining Commences Phase 1 Exploration at the New Craigmont Copper Project
summary: Nicola Mining commenced Phase 1 drilling at its 100% owned New Craigmont copper project in British Columbia. The program targets magnetic anomalies and known copper-iron mineralization, building on prior intercepts of about 1.1–1.3% Cu. It is an exploration update with no immediate production or supply impact.

title: Copper crunch drives record prices
summary: Copper prices are hitting record highs as traders bid amid tight supplies. The curve is backwardated, above-ground stocks are depleted from heavy Chinese buying and EV demand, and inventories cover only about 3.3 weeks. Bank of America expects the deficit to keep prices elevated, potentially pushing copper higher further.

title: From gold, copper and rare earths -- Taliban controls over half of Afghanistan's treasure trove
summary: A report says the Taliban earned about $1.6 billion last fiscal year through mining-related revenues and controls numerous Afghan mining sites, including copper. It describes insecurity, extortion, and smuggling of minerals out of Afghanistan, with mining often untapped or poorly managed, creating supply-risk conditions.

title: Sama Resources Intersects 9.30 metres at 2.68% Nickel and 1.47% Copper at Samapleu Main
summary: Sama Resources reported early drilling results from the Samapleu deposit, including 9.30m grading 2.68% nickel and 1.47% copper within a broader 81.35m mineralized zone. The company is also drilling at Yepleu using DHTEM targets. This is exploration-focused with no immediate production changes.

title: Sama Resources Intersects 9.30 metres at 2.68% Nickel and 1.47% Copper at Samapleu Main
summary: Sama Resources reported preliminary drilling results from its Samapleu deposit, including a 9.30 m intercept grading 2.68% nickel and 1.47% copper within a broader 81.35 m mineralized zone. The company is continuing drilling at Yepleu, with further assays pending for additional metals.

title: Nicola Mining Commences Phase 1 Exploration at the New Craigmont Copper Project
summary: Nicola Mining began Phase 1 exploration drilling (~2,000m) at its New Craigmont Copper Project near Merritt, BC, targeting two magnetic anomalies associated with prior copper intercepts and near-surface chalcopyrite/magnetite skarn mineralization. The press release discusses step-out drilling aims but provides no production changes or resource updates.

title: Aluminium industry reiterates urgency for 5% RoDTEP rate
summary: India’s Aluminium Association of India urges the government to implement RoDTEP export duty remissions for aluminium, targeting at least a 5% rate and faster notification of sector-wise rates. It argues delays and withdrawn MEIS support weaken competitiveness versus China and create export uncertainty, potentially boosting aluminium export demand.

title: San Lorenzo Commences Exploration on It's 100% Owned Large Scale Copper - Gold Porphyry Salvadora Project, Chile
summary: San Lorenzo Gold announced it has begun magnetometer and subsequent induced polarization geophysical surveys on its 100% owned Salvadora copper–gold porphyry project in Chile, near the El Salvador copper–gold mine. The company cites encouraging copper grades from prior drilling and plans a large diamond drill program.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp. Closes Book for C$15,000,000 Equity Financing to Acquire Punitaqui Copper-Gold Mine
summary: Battery Mineral Resources closed a C$15m equity financing to fund its acquisition and restart activities for the Punitaqui Mining Complex, a prior-producing copper-gold mine in Chile. The proceeds support settlement of obligations, exploration, and development toward mid-size copper production within about 12 months. Effects point to copper-positive sentiment.

title: Copper eases as U.S. inflation data sparks liquidity concerns
summary: Copper prices fell as U.S. CPI came in hotter than expected, raising fears of monetary tightening that could curb liquidity flowing into commodities. The June ShFE contract eased 0.3% and LME three-month copper was flat to slightly down, while markets digested the inflation surprise.

title: Chilean National Copper Corporation's $1.4 billion Salvador copper project will break ground_SMM
summary: Codelco, Chile’s state copper producer, said it will begin work in the next few weeks on its $1.4 billion Rajo Inca/Salvador project to convert the old Salvador mine to an open-pit operation. The company targets 90,000 tons in the first half of 2023, supporting future output.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Provides Update on Schaft Creek PEA
summary: Copper Fox updates the Preliminary Economic Assessment for the Schaft Creek porphyry project, highlighting a revised mine plan with reduced strip ratio, lower operating and capital costs, and planned throughput producing copper concentrate (average ~28% Cu). The news improves project economics and can bolster near-term copper supply outlook sentiment.

title: Copper Fox Provides Update on Schaft Creek PEA
summary: Copper Fox updates progress on its Schaft Creek Preliminary Economic Assessment, a large undeveloped porphyry deposit with copper as the primary metal and gold/molybdenum/silver by-products. The PEA work includes improved mine design, lower operating costs, and cash-flow modeling using copper-price assumptions, supporting bullish sentiment for copper-linked project economics.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Provides Update on Pre-Feasibility Study Work at the 100%-Owned Alacran Copper-Gold-Silver Project
summary: Cordoba Minerals updated its Alacran copper-gold-silver project pre-feasibility work, reporting metallurgical tests with ~90% copper recoveries and ~83% gold recoveries, plus ongoing drilling to convert resources and support feasibility study progress. The news is project-specific, with limited immediate supply-market impact beyond sentiment.

title: NORNICKEL HAS RECOVERED ORE MINING AT THE OKTYABRSKY MINE TO FULL CAPACITY
summary: Nornickel said ore mining at the Oktyabrsky mine has recovered and is operating at full capacity. The update points to improved near-term nickel ore supply conditions, which can increase market expectations for greater availability and put downward pressure on nickel prices over the next days to weeks.

title: Codelco to start work soon on $1.4bn copper project in Chile
summary: Codelco plans to start work soon on its $1.38bn Rajo Inca project to overhaul the Salvador copper mine in Chile, switching to open-cast operations. The company targets 90,000t production in the first half of 2023 after pre-stripping and concentrator ramp-up, with equipment largely sourced internally.

title: Firm dollar, slowing China loan data weigh on copper
summary: Copper fell 1.8% as a firmer dollar and weaker China TSF/loan growth pointed to slowing demand. Traders also worried Chinese authorities may cap commodity prices. The Fed/dollar reaction reduced purchasing power, and higher LME copper margins encouraged selling. Aluminium and nickel also dropped on the same market risk-off move.

title: Zambia Shutters Seized Copper Mine as Prices Soar Toward Record
summary: Zambia has shut down a seized copper mine, tightening near-term copper supply. With copper prices already surging toward record levels, the disruption is likely to add further upward pressure by increasing concerns over availability and shipments in the short horizon.

title: SHANGHAI'S MOST ACTIVE COPPER CONTRACT FALLS 3.2%
summary: Shanghai’s most active copper contract in China fell 3.2%, as reported by Reuters. A sharp drop in the front-month futures price signals strong near-term bearish sentiment and suggests market expectations for copper demand/supply or risk appetite moved lower within the trading day.

title: Oxygen production at Sterlite Copper smelter hits technical snag
summary: Vedanta said oxygen production at its Sterlite Copper smelter in Thoothukudi was paused due to a technical snag in the cold box of its oxygen plant. A team has been stationed to resolve the issue and resume stabilized output soon. The oxygen supply is intended for medical use, and overall plant operations remain linked to the smelter.

title: Appian announces US$23m Caserones copper royalty sale
summary: Appian Capital Advisory announced it will sell its US$23 million royalty interest over the Caserones copper mine in Chile to Nomad Royalty Company. The royalty is 0.28% NSR, with dividends payable in 2021. The deal is subject to regulatory approvals and provides long-life copper exposure, but no operational changes are noted.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose 4,300 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for the fourth straight week, up 4,300 mt to 401,900 mt by May 14, attributed to larger arrivals and weak demand for inbound goods. With Yangshan copper bill of lading prices continuing to decline, unclaimed imports moved into bonded warehouses, increasing availability.

title: Barksdale acquires Arizona copper projects from Kennecott
summary: Barksdale Resources will acquire 100% of two copper exploration projects in Santa Cruz County, Arizona, from Kennecott. The deal expands Barksdale’s footprint in the Patagonia mining district and adds copper porphyry drill targets, but it is an exploration-stage transaction with limited immediate supply impact for copper prices.

title: Production of the top ten copper mining companies in the world is expected to rise in 2021. Freeport is expected to increase production by 18.5%._SMM
summary: GlobalData reports copper output from the world’s top 10 miners rose slightly in 2020 and expects a rebound in 2021. Freeport is projected to lift production 18.5% on expanded Grasberg, alongside growth from First Quantum and others. First-quarter 2021 data show Freeport and Freeport rising.

title: Silver Elephant Mining Corp.: Silver Elephant Proposes a Return to Pure Silver Miner with Nickel and Vanadium Spin-Outs
summary: Silver Elephant plans to spin out its nickel (Minago) and vanadium projects, returning to a pure silver vehicle focused on its Pulacayo silver asset. It notes nickel prices are near multi-year highs and details EIA renewal and prior investment, but the article does not imply near-term nickel supply changes.

title: Aluminium giant China Hongqiao to move more smelting capacity to Yunnan - sources
summary: China Hongqiao plans to shift additional aluminium smelting capacity from Shandong to hydropower-reliant Yunnan, adding a further 1 million tonnes to the Wenshan/Honghe projects. The move reflects cheaper, cleaner power economics and carbon policy pressures. Timing is unclear, but capacity relocation can affect near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Copper heads for weekly loss, retreating from record high
summary: Copper was set for its first weekly decline since early April as inflation fears pressured markets and the dollar, while China demand indicators weakened. Yangshan import premiums fell to record lows and LME cash copper shifted to a discount versus the three-month contract, signaling ample near-term supply. Aluminium and nickel were comparatively steadier.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks fell 600 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories fell 600 mt from a week earlier to 8,700 mt by May 14. The import window narrowed but premiums for duty-free nickel briquettes and plating nickel plates were moderate, with some volumes entering China after customs clearance. Stocks are expected to keep declining.

title: Barksdale to buy two copper projects in US from Rio Tinto
summary: Barksdale Resources agreed to buy two early-stage copper exploration projects—Goat Canyon and Canelo—in Arizona from Rio Tinto’s Kennecott Exploration. The deal includes upfront cash plus a 2% NSR royalty and potential future milestone payments. It expands Barksdale’s copper project footprint, but not near-term production.

title: O2 production at Sterlite Copper smelter hits technical snag
summary: Vedanta said a technical snag in the cold box at the oxygen plant at its Sterlite Copper smelter in Thoothukudi has caused a temporary pause in oxygen production. The company expects to resume stabilized output soon, after dispatching oxygen tankers earlier in May.

title: Deep-South Appoints Knight Piesold to Produce Scoping Studies on the Haib Copper Project in Namibia
summary: Deep-South Resources appointed Knight Piésold to run scoping studies for its Haib copper project in Namibia, covering water supply, alternative power, ESIA planning, and heap-leach pad conceptual design. The release reiterates strong copper economics, including returns at $3.00/lb and $4.00/lb, boosting copper development sentiment.

title: Go Metals Mobilizes for Quebec Nickel | The Kingston Whig Standard
summary: Go Metals says it has mobilized crews in Quebec to start early-season exploration on its Havre-Saint-Pierre nickel and copper project, aiming to ground-truth geophysical conductors and assess subsurface continuity. It also plans follow-on work for gold claims. The update concerns exploration, not production or supply changes.

title: BHP Remote Copper Operators Move Closer to Strike in Chile
summary: BHP remote copper operators in Chile are reportedly moving closer to a strike. The potential work stoppage would increase the risk of near-term copper supply disruptions from mines in the country, often weighing on sentiment and futures pricing over the coming days and weeks.

title: Union at BHP's Escondida, Spence copper mines in Chile reject contract offer
summary: A union at BHP’s Escondida and Spence copper mines in Chile rejected the company’s contract offer, increasing the risk of a strike. The union president said the rejection heightens potential work stoppage at two major producing assets, which could disrupt near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Gold Holds Above US$1,800, Copper Breaks Records
summary: The piece highlights copper breaking to record levels, topping $4.90 per pound for the first time. It links the surge to higher Chinese demand and supply-side concerns, while noting copper’s expanding role in green energy applications such as EVs and charging infrastructure. Battery metal commentary is secondary.

title: LG Chem to Invest 40 bln Won in Chinese Copper Foil Firm
summary: LG Chem says it will invest 40 billion won in a Chinese firm that makes copper foil. The announcement points to increased upstream capacity for copper foil used in industrial and battery supply chains, which could improve near-term expectations for copper demand and support copper pricing over coming weeks.

title: LG Chem invests W40 billion in Chinese battery copper foil company
summary: LG Chem plans to invest 40 billion won in Jiujiang DeFu Technology, a major Chinese battery copper foil producer. The move targets expansion of battery materials for EVs as battery copper foil demand rises. Defu plans to grow annual copper foil capacity, which can support copper demand expectations.

title: Local consortium proposes to develop Pakistan copper and gold mine after arbitration case
summary: A Reuters report says a local consortium proposed developing Pakistan’s Reko Diq after Pakistan’s Supreme Court previously blocked the Antofagasta–Barrick venture and arbitration led to large damages. The consortium would start with Tanjeel reserves, then expand Reko Diq. The Balochistan government is reviewing terms.

title: Supply worries lift copper prices
summary: The article headline reports that supply worries are boosting copper prices. While other listed items are macro or news briefs, the only direct metal-specific signal is the claim of tightening/concern in copper supply, which typically raises near-term expectations for higher prices.

title: Local consortium proposes to develop gold, copper mine
summary: A Pakistani consortium (NRL) proposed developing the Tanjeel and Reko Diq copper reserves in Balochistan after court/arbitration actions blocked the prior Tethyan Copper Company plan. BMEC will review the proposal and it remains at investigation/approval stages, making any short-term impact on copper supply expectations uncertain.

title: SHFE aluminium to continue to fluctuate at highs in the high season_SMM
summary: SMM reports the SHFE most-traded aluminium contract fell 2.7% last week, while LME aluminium dropped 3.8%. Despite weaker liquidity sentiment from higher US PPI and the Fed’s policy stance, domestic fundamentals remain positive and the peak season continues. SHFE aluminium is expected to stay high in a defined range this week.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 17): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mostly higher, copper fell 0.07%_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai nonferrous markets mostly higher on May 17 on improved China economic data and ongoing monitoring of Covid conditions. SHFE copper slipped 0.07%, while nickel rose 1.98% and aluminium gained 1.39%. Commentary links aluminium support to falling ingot stocks and nickel/copper to broader sentiment.

title: Northern Dynasty Minerals Ltd.: US Green Energy Policies Drive Unprecedented Demand for Copper
summary: Northern Dynasty says U.S. green-energy and offshore wind targets (e.g., 30,000 MW by 2030) will require substantially more refined copper, citing higher copper intensity in offshore wind and broader electrification needs. It argues domestic copper supply may not meet demand, supporting bullish expectations for copper prices.

title: USW: US-EU Talks Must Strengthen Domestic Steel and Aluminum Production and Employment
summary: The USW urged US-EU trade talks to strengthen domestic steel and aluminum, citing foreign dumping, subsidies, and global overcapacity. It notes existing unfair trade relief measures against EU steel and aluminum and supports solutions that deliver measurable relief for producers and US workers. No new aluminium policy details are announced.

title: Western Copper and Gold Announces C$25.6 Million Strategic Investment by Rio Tinto
summary: Western Copper and Gold said Rio Tinto will invest C$25.6 million to fund studies, feasibility and permitting for the Casino copper-gold project in Yukon. The financing and Rio Tinto’s involvement are supportive for project progression and future copper supply expectations, which can modestly lift near-term copper sentiment.

title: Copper turns higher as strike risk offsets weak China data
summary: Copper rebounded toward the prior week’s record as investors weighed strike risk at Chile’s Escondida and Spence mines against weak Chinese factory data. The LME copper price rose 0.4% near $10,283/t. LME aluminium and nickel also increased, supported by broader nonferrous output.

title: Northern Dynasty: US Green Energy Policies Drive Unprecedented Demand for Copper
summary: Northern Dynasty says U.S. clean-energy and offshore-wind targets imply a large step-up in copper demand, citing high copper intensity for offshore wind (e.g., ~8 t/MW or more). It projects additional tonnes of refined copper needed through 2030–2035 as power generation, grids, EVs, and electrification expand.

title: Offshore Wind Requires 63,000lbs Of Copper Per Turbine
summary: Oilprice.com says offshore wind can require about 63,000 lbs of copper per turbine, implying structurally higher demand for copper. It links recent price swings to supply chain disruptions and reports a potential strike by most Chilean workers at BHP, raising prospects of copper supply disruption and tighter markets.

title: Peru Leftist Copies Chile's Proposal for Tax on Copper Boom
summary: Peru is considering a move patterned after Chile’s proposal for a tax on profits during a copper boom. Such measures typically increase government take from copper producers, potentially raising costs or investment uncertainty and pressuring near-term copper market sentiment despite the boom conditions.

title: Copper shortage sparks worry of metal thefts in Suffolk | East Anglian Daily Times
summary: Suffolk police warn residents and businesses about potential increases in copper thefts as copper prices rise. Officers cite surging demand and a global copper deficit, plus post-Covid economic recovery and construction demand. The piece focuses on security and forensic marking advice rather than any new supply disruption.

title: Copper shortage sparks worry of metal thefts in Suffolk
summary: Suffolk police warn residents and businesses about rising metal theft risk as copper prices increase and shortages grow. Copper is cited as rising on surging demand and a global copper deficit, with construction demand recovering post-Covid. Authorities urge better security to protect stored scrap and cabling.

title: Rio Tinto takes strategic stake in Western Copper and Gold
summary: Rio Tinto Canada plans to invest $25.6 million for an 8% stake in Western Copper and Gold, funding economic studies and permitting for its Casino copper-gold project in Yukon. The move can provide positive sentiment for copper development, but near-term price effects are likely limited since activities are pre-production.

title: U.S. and Europe to Begin Talks on Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The U.S. and EU began talks to resolve their dispute over steel and aluminum tariffs. The Trump-era duties included 25% on steel and 10% on aluminum. Easing or preventing tariff escalation would lower expected aluminum import costs and likely weigh on near-term aluminum prices.

title: Massive Sulfide Nickel Drilling Update
summary: Blackstone Minerals reported assay results from drilling at its Ta Khoa nickel-copper massive sulfide project, including continuous mineralisation with significant nickel and copper (plus PGEs). Results from the King Snake prospect suggest potential resource extensions and support restarting a 450 ktpa concentrator, improving near-term supply expectations.

title: Edgemont Gold Corp.: Edgemont Plans Summer Drill Program for Dungate Copper/Gold Porphyry Project Near Houston, B.C.
summary: Edgemont Gold plans a fully funded 3,000 m summer Phase I drill program at its Dungate copper/gold porphyry project in B.C., pending final permitting. The release cites historic chalcopyrite, quartz-pyrite breccia, and outcrop copper grades, targeting untested IP and magnetic anomalies.

title: Century Aluminum Announces CEO Succession
summary: Century Aluminum announced CEO succession: Mike Bless will retire July 1, 2021, and Jesse Gary will become President and CEO. The company cites continuity and industry knowledge, referencing prior operational expansions and pandemic leadership, but provides no new production, capacity, or cost guidance that would immediately affect aluminium market pricing.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Operations Update; Announces Filing
summary: Nevada Copper reported Q1 operational progress at its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine, including initiation of stope mining, completion of key hoisting and electrical upgrades, improved processing recoveries, and concentrate production. The company expects sustainable 3,000 tpd by end-Q2 and continued ramp-up, subject to dike grouting and COVID-related shipping delays.

title: Copper prices gain as dollar weakens, Chinese premium rebounds
summary: Copper prices rose on Tuesday as Treasury yields stalled and a weaker U.S. dollar made dollar-priced metals cheaper. At the same time, the Yangshan/Chinese premium rebounded, suggesting improving demand from China, the top copper consumer. LME three-month copper rose 0.7% and SHFE June copper gained 1.4%.

title: Tight secondary copper supply as higher copper prices drove sellers to hold back cargoes _SMM
summary: Secondary copper suppliers held back cargoes after copper prices rose, tightening scrap availability. The cathode-to-scrap spread narrowed sharply and inventories at rod plants using scrap dropped to 2–5 days, prompting higher plant pricing. Later restocking improved trading, but copper prices remained elevated despite weaker optimism.

title: Copper prices to have downward room_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM expects SHFE copper to fall further, citing US CPI beating forecasts and a rebound in the US dollar index that limits further dollar weakness.
