China’s financing missed expectations, sentiment stayed depressed, and demand is weak with off-season approaching and low plant operating rates.

title: Copper cable thieves get violent and deadly
summary: Security officers were killed while protecting substations from armed copper cable thieves in South Africa, amid repeated thefts causing outages. title: Copper rises; ShFE zinc at 13-1/2-year high on supply concerns
summary: Copper prices rose on a weaker U.S. dollar. The report also mentions aluminium smelters in Yunnan being asked to test power-consumption staggering ahead of celebrations, supporting tight supply expectations, while LME and SHFE nickel both climbed. Overall, the news signals broad bullish pressure for copper, aluminium, and nickel.

title: Deep probe proves Cortadera a copper monster
summary: Hot Chili says deep drilling at its Chile Cortadera project hit 836m grading 0.5% copper-equivalent, extending the Cuerpo 3 porphyry and linking Cuerpo 2 and 3 at depth, with assays pending. The update strengthens the project’s copper resource outlook but does not imply immediate supply.

title: Peruvian presidential candidate plans to emulate Chile in imposing copper surtax_SMM
summary: A Peruvian presidential candidate said he would add copper sales taxes and renegotiate mining tax stabilization contracts, inspired by Chile’s approved progressive copper royalty (up to 75% when copper exceeds $4/lb). Mining firms warn of competitiveness and investment delays, weighing on sentiment toward copper.

title: DLP Resources Inc.: DLP Resources Signs Letter of Intent to Option 100% of the Advanced Stage Aurora Porphyry Copper-Molybdenum Project, Peru and Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement
summary: DLP Resources signed a letter of intent to option 100% of the Aurora porphyry copper-molybdenum project in Peru and plans to use proceeds from a non-brokered private placement to fund cash payments and exploration. title: Inomin Mines Inc.: Inomin Starts Beaver Nickel-Cobalt Exploration Program
summary: Inomin Mines reports a ground magnetic survey and an airborne EM test at its Beaver nickel-cobalt project in British Columbia to delineate drill targets for later 2021. title: EU Halts Tariffs on US Steel, Aluminium Exports to Resolve Metal Trade Dispute
summary: The EU and US began talks to resolve their steel and aluminium trade dispute, with the EU temporarily suspending an increase in tariff rebalancing measures on US 232 steel and aluminium. The move aims to address market distortions and global excess capacity. It should support near-term aluminium pricing sentiment.

title: Missouri manufacturers join call for Biden to lift Trump aluminum, steel tariffs
summary: Missouri manufacturers and other U.S. metal users urge President Biden to lift Trump-era Section 232 tariffs on foreign aluminum, saying tariffs raise costs and extend delivery lead times amid strong demand for metals tied to autos and appliances. They warn tariffs could worsen shortages and delay infrastructure spending; Raimondo says tariffs remain.

title: Exclusive: Glencore to restart operations at Mutanda copper, cobalt mine in 2022
summary: Glencore plans to restart production at the Mutanda copper/cobalt mine, which has been offline since late 2019. Worker recruitment is ongoing, with no specific restart date given.

title: Slumping US$ boosts metals, including tin and aluminium
summary: Industrial metals rose as investors shifted toward riskier assets on bets for an extended period of low interest rates, lifting global equities. title: Power pole plea after Manawatū copper cabling thefts
summary: Manawatū police are asking residents to report suspicious activity near power poles and lines after copper cabling thefts. Inspector Ross Grantham says about 10,000 metres of copper cabling stolen from Powerco’s network in the year to date. The report is focused on theft prevention.

summary: SMM reports China’s April 2021 nickel apparent consumption at 120,451 mt and expects primary nickel demand to rebound to a new Q2 high. summary: Nickel prices continued to fall, but purchases of nickel plates turned active after prices dropped below 130,000 yuan/mt. summary: Vedanta restarted oxygen production at its Sterlite Copper smelter in Thoothukudi after a technical snag in the cold box halted output on May 14. summary: Vedanta’s Sterlite Copper unit in Tamil Nadu resumed medical oxygen production after a technical disruption halted operations. title: Why 2021 Could Be The Biggest Bull Market For Copper… Ever
summary: The piece argues 2021 could be a major copper bull market, citing copper’s strong Q1 rally to multi-year highs. title: Posco buys stakes in Ravensthorpe Nickel in Australia for $240m
summary: POSCO agreed to buy a 30% stake in Australia’s Ravensthorpe Nickel Operation for $240m and obtain a long-term offtake for 7,500 tons per year of nickel in MHP starting in 2024. It also plans possible nickel-sulfate cathode precursor production, supporting EV battery-related nickel demand.

title: POSCO Buys Stakes in Ravensthorpe Nickel in Australia for US$240 mln
summary: POSCO plans to buy stakes in Australia’s Ravensthorpe nickel project for US$240 million. The transaction is directly tied to expanding or securing exposure to nickel production capacity in the near-term outlook, which can be mildly supportive for nickel price expectations, though immediate supply impact is likely limited.

title: Deal puts billion-dollar value on BHP's nightmare nickel mine
summary: POSCO has agreed to buy a 30% stake in Western Australia’s Ravensthorpe nickel mine, valuing the BHP-linked asset at roughly $1 billion. POSCO will pay about $US240 million, with the deal motivated by rising battery materials demand, reinforcing bullish expectations for nickel supply and pricing.

title: Aluminium billet inventories fell 16,600 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Chinese aluminium billet stocks fell 16,600 mt (down 15.8%) to 88,600 mt as of May 20, while outbound shipments rose sharply. With aluminium prices easing, downstream buying increased on fears of a rebound. SMM expects inventories to decline slightly next week, keeping prices tangled.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 41,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s primary aluminium ingot social inventories fell 41,000 mt from last Thursday to 1.02 million mt as of May 20. Stocks declined across seven of eight consumption areas, with the exception of Chongqing. The drawdown signals tighter near-term availability for the market.

title: Operating rates at secondary aluminium makers lost 0.25 percentage point in May_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates at China’s secondary aluminium producers fell to 41.35% in April and are expected to decline further in May. Reasons include squeezed downstream die-casting margins, weak orders from the ongoing auto “core shortage,” and tighter scrap supply after rapid aluminium price rises plus environmental inspections reducing output.

title: POSCO invests $240 million to acquire stake in nickel mine
summary: POSCO agreed to buy a 30% stake in Australia’s Ravensthorpe nickel operation for $240m via First Quantum. The deal secures supply of mixed nickel-cobalt hydroxide (MHP) for EV battery cathodes, with 7,500 tons of nickel per year expected from 2024, supporting nickel-demand expectations.

title: Copper up on dollar, strike possibility in Chile
summary: Copper rose 0.6% on a softer U.S. dollar and worries about a potentially lengthy strike at Chile’s Escondida mine. The union is preparing to strike if BHP fails to reach a fair contract. China’s commodity-price management and other factors capped gains, limiting the rally’s strength.

title: Trigon Metals, Inc.: Trigon Announces High Grade Copper Results From Drilling At Silver Hill, Morocco
summary: Trigon Metals announced assay results from drilling at its Silver Hill copper project in Morocco, including a highlight of 31 metres at 0.74% copper. The results suggest strong ongoing mineralization at the western extent of the campaign. This may mildly support copper sentiment, though the announcement is still exploration-stage.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 20): Nonferrous metals on the SHFE fell broadly, nickel tumbled 3.7%_SMM
summary: SMM reports broad declines across SHFE nonferrous metals, with copper down 2.02%, aluminium down 1.85%, and nickel down 3.7%. The move is linked to Fed minutes suggesting possible earlier debt-purchase reduction and higher rate expectations, plus China’s guidance to curb unreasonable commodity price increases.

title: Alcoa Exploring Technology to Further Reduce Carbon Emissions in Alumina Refining
summary: Alcoa said Australia’s ARENA will fund tests of renewable-energy Mechanical Vapor Recompression (MVR) in alumina refining. If successful, Alcoa plans a three-megawatt MVR module at the Wagerup refinery. The project targets large carbon-footprint reductions for alumina, supporting low-carbon aluminium supply.

title: Copper: HCL, Hindalco rally on Chinese demand, supply mismatch. But how long can copper retain the shine?
summary: The piece says copper has returned to the USD 10,100/ton area after about a decade, citing a rally driven by strong Chinese demand and a supply mismatch. It also highlights major Indian copper/aluminium-linked equities (Hindustan Copper, Hindalco) outperforming, and questions whether a broader “super cycle” is forming.

title: iTWire - ARENA allocates $11.3m to Alcoa for low emissions alumina investigation
summary: ARENA has allocated $11.3m to Alcoa for a low-emissions alumina investigation at the Wagerup refinery. The project will test renewable-powered MVR to supply process heat and, if feasible, deliver a 3 MW MVR module. It aims to decarbonise energy-intensive alumina refining and support competitiveness.

title: LME copper eyes worst week since Sept 2020 on China price curb fears
summary: London copper is set for its biggest weekly drop since Sept 2020 as fears grow that China will curb a commodity price rally. Beijing’s plan to manage supply and prevent “unreasonable” price increases worries markets. The piece also shows lower nickel and aluminium prices, pointing to bearish broader metal sentiment.

title: Adam Rozencwajg: Copper in for a "Very, Very Strong Bull Market"
summary: An interview argues copper still has room to rise, potentially up to $10–$15/lb. It points to prior strength driven by demand from China and India and increasing demand for green energy, but says the next phase will be driven by supply risks, including declining head grades and low discovery activity.

title: China NiCoLi Summit 2021: Expectations over new energy market drive nickel price volatility_SMM
summary: SMM reports that new energy demand is becoming a key driver of nickel prices as pure-nickel substitution by NPI weakens. Analysts expect China’s NPI output to fall while Indonesia’s NPI and hydromet intermediate product supply to rise, with growing imports in 2021 alongside precursor production growth.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 21): Nonferrous metals on the SHFE closed mixed, nickel plunged 3.21%_SMM
summary: SMM said SHFE nonferrous metals closed mixed, with copper down 1.25%, aluminium down 1.76%, and nickel down 3.21% on the day. The note attributes the backdrop to US data showing very low jobless claims and a Philly Fed survey where accelerating input costs and rising prices squeeze profits, pressuring sentiment.

title: China LiCoNi Summit 2021: Recycled nickel metal is expected to reach 62,000 gold mt in 2030_SMM
summary: SMM’s analyst at the China International Lithium Cobalt Nickel Summit forecasts strong growth in battery recycling, including recycled nickel reaching 62,000 metric tons by 2030. The piece outlines bottlenecks in recycling policy and pricing but provides no near-term supply shock or policy action affecting nickel prices immediately.

title: NEW Economic Policy Institute White Paper Launch on Section 232 Aluminum Tariffs: A Virtual Discussion
summary: The American Primary Aluminum Association announces a webinar introducing an Economic Policy Institute white paper analyzing the impacts of Section 232 aluminum tariffs on the primary aluminum sector and downstream users. The piece is directly tied to policy affecting aluminum trade and supply expectations, which can move aluminium prices in the near term.

title: First Quantum to offload 30% stake in Australian Nickel mine for $240m
summary: First Quantum agreed to sell its 30% stake in the Ravensthorpe nickel/cobalt operation in Western Australia to POSCO for $240m, while keeping a 70% operating role. POSCO will receive 7,500 tpa of nickel in mixed nickel-cobalt hydroxide precipitate under an offtake deal.

title: Chile's Codelco says 40% of its copper output at risk if glacier bill passes -media
summary: Codelco told Chilean lawmakers that a proposed glacier protection bill could jeopardize as much as 40% of its copper output, citing “absolute prohibitions” that overlap with activity at its major mines. The review is happening alongside a royalty bill that would raise taxes, increasing uncertainty around Chilean supply.

title: Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, Emirates Global Aluminium discuss industrial sector decarbonisation
summary: UAE climate officials toured Emirates Global Aluminium and discussed industrial decarbonisation toward net zero. The company cited investments in lower-emissions smelting and casting, reduced PFC emissions, and transferring carbon dust as cement fuel. DEWA will supply solar power to its smelter, positioning UAE as producing solar-powered aluminium.

title: Peruvian presidential candidate Fujimori wants to speed up the development of copper projects in Peru_SMM
summary: Peru’s presidential candidate Keiko Fujimori says she would speed up energy and mining approvals, including promoting Tia Maria and Conga while avoiding contract renegotiations. Polls suggest a close race with potential market impact, as Peru is a major copper supplier, supporting near-term bullish sentiment for copper.

title: 5 Top Weekly TSX Stocks: Western Copper Up After Rio's Investment
summary: A TSX stocks recap says Western Copper and Gold shares rose after Rio Tinto Canada made a C$25.6 million strategic investment to advance the Casino copper-gold project. Other listed miners also rose on broader market moves, but the Rio-related update directly supports copper-linked development expectations.

title: China and Green Energy Drive Copper Prices to Record High
summary: Nikkei Asia reports copper hitting a record LME level above $10,000, driven by China’s faster post-COVID recovery and decarbonization demand for power, EVs, wind, and solar. Analysts highlight strong copper imports and limited new mine development, with nickel and aluminium also rising.

title: S & P: new discoveries of global copper mines hit a 30-year low_SMM
summary: S&P Global Market Intelligence analysis finds that major copper mine discoveries have fallen to a 30-year low, with only three such discoveries in the past three years and a risky project pipeline. Most resources come from older deposits, while many projects are not yet feasible, suggesting a looming copper supply squeeze.

title: China's Huayou, Eve Energy Surge After Investing in USD2.1 Billion Nickel Plant in Indonesia
summary: Huayou and Eve Energy plan a USD 2.1 billion joint venture in Indonesia to process laterite nickel ore on Halmahera, producing about 120,000 tons of nickel annually and also cobalt. Investors’ confidence rose after the deal, which aims to secure battery raw materials and reduce exposure to nickel price fluctuations.

title: China's Huayou, EVE Energy to set up nickel smelter in Indonesia
summary: Huayou, partnering with EVE Energy and others, plans a US$2.08 billion nickel and cobalt smelter in Indonesia, targeting about 120,000 tonnes of nickel annually. The investment could expand future Indonesian supply, but near-term production additions are unlikely, so immediate nickel price pressure is modest.

title: Oyu Tolgoi mined copper production from open pit 29% up in Q1
summary: Oyu Tolgoi’s Q1 performance scorecard says open-pit mined copper production was up 29% versus Q1 2020, helped by higher grades improving head grade and copper recovery. Copper guidance expands slightly (150,000–180,000 tonnes) while gold guidance is reduced due to COVID-19 and prior wall failure.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 24): Shanghai nonferrous metals fell across the board, aluminium dropped 3.52%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals fell broadly, led by aluminium (-3.52%) with copper (-1.36%) and nickel (-1.82%) also lower. Sentiment weakened amid inflation concerns and Fed policy taper/normalization talk that strengthened the US dollar, while domestic regulation-control commentary reduced confidence for bulk commodities.

title: China's Huayou invests in $2.1 billion Indonesia nickel project
summary: Huayou will partner EVE Energy and others in a $2.08 billion Indonesia nickel-and-cobalt smelting venture at Weda Bay, targeting about 120,000 tonnes of nickel and 15,000 tonnes of cobalt annually. It also buys a stake in a battery materials firm, expanding its battery supply-chain exposure.

title: US$2.1bil Indonesia nickel project aims to produce 120,000 T nickel, 15,000 T cobalt a year
summary: Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt confirmed a US$2.08 billion nickel and cobalt project in Indonesia, partnering with EVE Energy and others. The project targets about 120,000 tonnes of nickel per year, alongside 15,000 tonnes of cobalt, and includes additional investment in battery-materials firms.

title: China's Huayou invests in $2.1 bln Indonesia nickel project
summary: China’s Huayou plans to invest $2.08 billion in an Indonesia nickel-and-cobalt project at Weda Bay, aiming for 120,000 tonnes of nickel annually. The project adds capacity in a key Indonesian processing hub and follows Huayou’s related nickel sulfate ventures and investments upstream in battery materials.

title: Chile's Codelco strikes deal with Microsoft to extend automation at its copper mines
summary: Codelco in Chile struck a deal with Microsoft to extend automation at its copper mines. The move is aimed at further improving operational efficiency and technology use in production. That can support expectations for steadier or higher copper output over the coming weeks, though the exact impact timing is uncertain.

title: Chile's Codelco strikes deal with Microsoft to extend automation at its copper mines | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: Codelco said it reached a deal with Microsoft to fast-track digitization and automation at its Chilean copper mines, aiming to improve analytics, efficiency, safety, and traceability. The program includes worker training and is framed as a cost-and-sustainability upgrade, potentially improving near-term production outlook and sentiment for copper.

title: BHP and Encounter Resources sign farm-in deal for Elliott copper project
summary: BHP has exercised its option to enter a farm-in deal with Encounter Resources for the Elliott copper project in Australia’s Northern Territory. BHP will fund $17m over 10 years to gain a 75% interest, with a JV exploration program including seismic surveys and drilling. No near-term production is cited.

title: Rescheduled: Economic Policy Institute White Paper Launch on Section 232 Aluminum Tariffs: A Virtual Discussion
summary: The Economic Policy Institute will host a virtual white paper launch analyzing how the U.S. Section 232 aluminum tariffs affect the primary aluminum industry and downstream producers and consumers. The session includes the American Primary Aluminum Association and union leadership, signaling ongoing attention to tariff impacts on aluminum market conditions.

title: Global Ferronickel to take 20% stake in Chinese ore processor
summary: Global Ferronickel Holdings approved buying a 20% stake in China’s Guangdong Century Tsingshan Nickel Industry (GCTN), aiming to enhance synergy between its nickel ore supply and GCTN’s processing operations. The deal is expected to support consistent trade flows and diversification; no financial terms were disclosed.

title: Material Matters: Iron Ore, Gold, Nickel & LNG
summary: The piece highlights nickel fundamentals: stainless-steel price strength and an International Nickel Study Group data point showing a renewed supply/demand deficit (consumption +18.9% in Q1 vs production +7.9%), implying tighter near-term conditions. Copper is only briefly referenced for valuation, while aluminium receives no mention.

title: Copper rises to US$10,021
summary: The provided content includes a headline indicating copper has risen to US$10,021. The surrounding news links mention broader market and macro developments, but there is no direct nickel or aluminium-specific information. Overall, the immediate copper signal points to bullish price pressure.

title: Operating rates across major aluminium processors extended slight increase, driven by continuous growth in extrusion segment _SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates across major aluminium processors rose to 77.1%, mainly from a higher extrusion segment. Construction extrusion and aluminium formwork orders improved with a recovering real estate sector. Plate/strip stayed full, while primary alloy rates eased due to weaker auto orders, but overall aluminium demand looks supported into May-June.

title: Refinery expansions, franking credits back on Alumina agenda
summary: Alumina Limited reports that demand for alumina could soon outstrip supply and is again considering ways to expand capacity, including potential refinancing of franking credits. With Western Australian refinery expansion on the agenda, expectations for tighter upstream alumina supply are supportive for aluminium prices.

title: No commodities 'super-cycle' but copper demand from green economy bright | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: Experts at an LME Asia Metals seminar said there’s unlikely to be a broad “super-cycle,” but the energy transition should support demand for industrial metals. Copper was highlighted as benefiting most, with EVs and renewable grid investment driving consumption. Nickel and low-carbon aluminium were also expected to gain from decarbonisation trends.

title: China's Zhejiang Huayou to form venture for Indonesia nickel project
summary: Zhejiang Huayou plans a $2.08bn Indonesia JV for a nickel and cobalt project, with Huayou holding 20% and partners including EVE Energy and Yongrui. The venture targets 120,000 tpa of nickel at Weda Bay, adding to Indonesia’s nickel supply pipeline and supporting nickel sentiment.

title: Secondary copper supply tightened at week-end_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports tightened secondary copper availability at week-end: suppliers held back cargoes during a late-week copper selloff, while restocking and aggressive scrap purchases limited declines. The cathode–scrap price spread widened, and some users paid higher prices with cash-flow constraints. SMM expects improved cargoes this week amid volatility risk.

title: Shortages of lumber, glass, copper and more impacting construction
summary: Pennsylvania homebuilders face widespread construction shortages, including unavailable or expensive copper products and items made with aluminum. Builders report they cannot get materials “no matter what you’re willing to pay,” causing delays and higher costs passed to buyers. Shortages are expected to persist, supporting near-term price strength.

title: Forum Energy Metals Corp.: Rio Tinto Intersects 1.78% Copper and 9.25 g/t Silver over 3.1 Metres Within 48 Metre Copper Zone at Forum's Janice Lake Copper/Silver Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals reported initial drill results from Rio Tinto Exploration’s Rafuse target at the Janice Lake copper/silver project in Saskatchewan. Intercepts included thick copper mineralization, with a higher-grade section over a few metres. Rio Tinto plans further drilling and follow-up on remaining targets. No production change is described.

title: Codelco partners Microsoft to digitise copper mining operations
summary: Codelco signed a deal with Microsoft to digitise and automate its Chilean copper mining operations, aiming for improved analytics, remote production, safety and productivity, plus employee training. The move accompanies plans for the near-term Rajo Inca overhaul of the Salvador mine, while unions warned about job risks.

title: Canada Nickel Preliminary Economic Assessment Confirms Robust Economics of Crawford Nickel Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel reports a preliminary economic assessment for its Crawford sulphide project in Ontario, with $1.2 billion after-tax NPV8% and 16% IRR, plus low projected nickel costs (C1 ~$1.09/lb). The company is advancing to feasibility, potentially supporting bullish sentiment for nickel supply.

title: Commodities Prices - No commodities 'super-cycle' but copper demand from green economy bright
summary: Experts polled said commodities are unlikely to see a “super-cycle,” but they cited bright copper demand from the green economy. The piece also notes efforts by Chinese authorities to keep commodity prices stable, which may dampen broader moves. Net effect is supportive but not strongly directional beyond copper.

title: Roskill Information Services Ltd: Roskill: Multiple factors at play as the dynamic nickel market undergoes further transformation
summary: Roskill highlights the evolving nickel market as battery demand grows and supply routes change. Tsingshan’s plan to supply high-grade nickel matte from NPI-based production to Chinese battery cathode makers helped weaken the bull narrative, with LME nickel dropping over 8.5% on 4 March. Indonesia project ramps add more supply optionality.

title: Rising copper price inflicts pain on downstream industries in China
summary: China is feeling the impact of a sharp copper surge, with prices rallying above $9,000 a tonne. The higher cost is hurting downstream industries, reflecting tightness or strong demand expectations that are pushing copper prices higher globally.

title: International Aluminium Institute: Post-consumer Aluminium Scrap Tops 20 Million Tonnes for the First Time
summary: The International Aluminium Institute reports record post-consumer aluminium scrap intake of 20 million tonnes in 2019, with post-consumer scrap reaching nearly 60% of total scrap intake. The IAI says recycling reduces greenhouse emissions and could supply up to 50% of aluminium demand by 2050, via better collection and recycling tech.

title: Aluminum Can Manufacturer To Build Large Facility In Delaware County, Bringing Over 300 Jobs
summary: CanPack plans a $380 million facility in Delaware County, Indiana, to produce aluminum beverage cans, citing a current US shortage of about 10 billion cans. The project’s scale and timeline suggest rising aluminum input demand for coil-to-can production, potentially supporting short-term aluminum sentiment.

title: Rio Tinto Intersects 1.78% Copper and 9.25 g/t Silver over 3.1 Metres Within 48 Metre Copper Zone at Forum's Janice Lake Copper/Silver Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals reported initial drill results from Rio Tinto Exploration Canada at its Janice Lake copper/silver project in Saskatchewan. Assays on the Rafuse target included 0.325% copper over 48m and 1.78% copper over 3.15m within broader mineralized intervals open at depth. Additional results are expected soon.

title: Want to Bet on Copper? Buy This Top Canadian Mining Stock
summary: The piece argues copper has been soaring due to restricted supply and strengthening demand, including support from EV and battery growth. It recommends Teck Resources as an overlooked Canadian way to gain copper upside. While it provides bullish drivers, it does not cite new operational or policy changes.

title: Lawsuit Claims Tesla Fired Employee To Cover Up Copper Theft At Nevada Battery Plant
summary: A former Tesla employee claims the company fired him to cover up alleged copper wire theft at its Nevada battery plant. The complaint cites millions of dollars’ worth of copper wire removed and unaccounted losses. While theft could influence perceptions of copper supply security, the lawsuit is unlikely to move broader copper prices.

title: SK nexilis to Build Copper Foil Factory in Poland
summary: SK nexilis says it will build a copper foil factory in Poland. New production capacity for copper foil typically signals higher downstream copper demand (e.g., for industrial/energy applications), which can provide modest near-term support to copper pricing expectations, though the timing and scale are not specified.

title: Copper Weakness Persists Despite Chilean Unrest – ShareCafe
summary: Copper prices continue to slide despite a threat of strike action at BHP’s Escondida and Spence mines in Chile over a new labor award. Reuters reports talks failed and workers may vote on striking. Traders appear to wait for the outcome, while Chinese and macro reports weigh on copper demand expectations.

title: Lack of Reliable Energy Forces NSW Aluminium Smelter to Power Down
summary: Power shortages have forced the NSW Tomago Aluminium smelter to halt operations several times in the past month. The smelter, a major Australian primary aluminium producer, is affected by insufficient dispatchable energy, implying reduced near-term aluminium output and likely tighter supply conditions.

title: SK nexilis to build copper foil factory in Poland
summary: SK nexilis, part of SK Group, plans to build a copper foil factory in Europe (likely Poland) to supply lithium-ion battery demand. It aims to raise copper foil capacity to over 200,000 tons/year by 2025 from 43,000 tons currently, with construction targets in 2024 after ground-breaking this year.

title: London copper rises as Chile labor strike woes stoke supply fears
summary: London three-month copper rose as a potential strike in top producer Chile threatened supply from BHP’s Escondida and Spence mines. A union rejected the contract offer and called for a walkout from Thursday. Analysts cited supportive fundamentals and supply-risk concerns despite weak demand.

title: London copper rises as labor strike woes in Chile stoke supply fears
summary: London copper rose as concerns about a potential strike at Chile’s Escondida and Spence mines threatened supply from the world’s top producer. A union rejected BHP’s contract offer and could start a walkout from Thursday. Analysts cited supportive fundamentals and supply disruption fears driving price strength.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Begins New Era of Commercial Copper Production
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says Kamoa-Kakula in the DRC began producing copper concentrate on May 25, ahead of schedule, with the concentrator ramping using initial ore grades and targeting ~57% copper concentrate. The company provides 2021 contained copper-in-concentrate guidance and discusses potential further expansion acceleration.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: AMARC: Surging Global Copper Demand Through 2030 to Benefit Canadian Explorers and Producers
summary: Amarc says global copper demand is surging on renewable energy, electrification, and EV/battery needs, while copper supply growth faces constraints like depleted ore grades and limited new mine pipeline. Referencing Goldman Sachs forecasts, it highlights a widening supply gap, supporting expectations for higher copper prices through 2030.

title: Copper boosted by potential labor strikes at Chile mines
summary: Copper prices rose as a planned labor strike threatened output from BHP’s Escondida and Spence mines in Chile, with unions calling for a walkout from Thursday. Analysts cited already low supplies and broader South American political risks, supporting a near-term bullish price reaction in copper markets.

title: Brigadier Gold Limited: Brigadier Makes Copper Discovery at Picachos
summary: Brigadier Gold reports bulk-tonnage copper mineralization at its Picachos gold-silver-copper project in Mexico, with trench samples returning copper grades up to 1.34% (and silver up to 284g/t). Additional phase-one assay results are pending. The update is exploration-focused without any immediate supply change.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Begins New Era of Commercial Copper Production
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says Kamoa-Kakula Phase 1 has begun commercial production ahead of schedule, with first hot commissioning in late May and expected production of 80,000–95,000 tonnes of contained copper in concentrate for the rest of 2021. The concentrator is ramping with guidance and planned Phase 3 acceleration.

title: Ivanhoe's Kamoa-Kakula mine starts copper production
summary: Ivanhoe says its Kamoa-Kakula project in the DRC began producing copper concentrate ahead of schedule after first ore was fed to the concentrator. Initial ramp-up targets 80,000–95,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate this year and higher output at peak, reinforcing bullish near-term supply expectations.

title: Groundbreaking Economic Policy Institute Study Finds That Section 232 Aluminum Tariffs Created Thousands of New American Jobs
summary: The Economic Policy Institute study claims Section 232 aluminum tariffs introduced in 2018 boosted U.S. aluminum production and employment, with negligible consumer impact, despite global overcapacity. Speakers urged maintaining and even strengthening the import restraints to stabilize and expand primary aluminum output, implying supportive near-term aluminium price pressure.

title: USW: EPI Report Demonstrates Continuing Need for Aluminum Section 232 Measures
summary: The United Steelworkers (USW) cites an Economic Policy Institute report and urges the U.S. to keep Section 232 measures on aluminum. It claims global overcapacity and illegal trade practices strain domestic production. Retaining the measures is said to help the industry regrow, protect jobs, and avoid destabilizing prices.

title: White Metal Partner Noronex Outlines Wide-Spread Copper Targets, Dorwit Copper-silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Resources outlines Noronex’s ongoing airborne EM, geochemistry compilation, and planned IP and reverse-circulation drilling at the DorWit copper-silver project in Namibia. The work aims to test multiple untested copper soil anomalies and define mineralisation, but no production or resource impact is quantified.

title: Brigadier Makes Copper Discovery at Picachos
summary: Brigadier Gold reports bulk-tonnage style copper mineralization discovery at its Picachos gold-silver-copper project in Sinaloa, Mexico. Trenching returned preliminary copper grades of 0.05%-1.34% (plus silver) from initial samples, while additional assay results from further drilling are pending.

title: Biggest copper project in decades begins production
summary: Ivanhoe Mines began producing copper concentrate at its Kamoa-Kakula project in the DRC months ahead of schedule. The start-up comes as copper trades near all-time highs, implying a faster-than-expected increase in supply that could pressure prices in the coming days to weeks.

title: EMERGING MARKETS-Chilean peso bounces as copper prices rise; Mexican peso buoyed by data
summary: Reuters reports Chile’s peso rebounded as copper prices rose on a planned labor strike at BHP’s Escondida and Spence mines. A union rejected BHP’s contract offer and urged a walkout, threatening already tight global copper supply. Other EM currency moves were tied to Mexico’s GDP data and Brazil’s sentiment.

title: Allied Copper Corp.: Allied Copper Enters into Definitive Agreement to Acquire 1269280 B.C. Ltd and Announces Leadership Changes
summary: Allied Copper Corp. announced a definitive agreement and reverse takeover to acquire BCCo, which holds an option on the Silver King project in Nevada. The project is described as a porphyry copper-gold exploration target. The deal is mainly exploratory and financing/approvals are required, with no near-term output impact mentioned.

title: BHP Chile Control Staff to Strike in Threat to Copper Supply
summary: BHP Chile control staff are threatening to strike, creating uncertainty around continued operations and near-term copper supply. The disruption risk is likely to tighten expected availability and weigh on market sentiment for copper in the coming days as traders price higher short-run supply risk.

title: Canada Nickel completes PEA for Crawford nickel project
summary: Canada Nickel says it has completed a preliminary economic assessment for its Crawford nickel sulphide project in Ontario. After drilling began in mid-2022, the PEA is meant to outline project economics, which can raise market expectations for future nickel supply and support nickel-related sentiment in the near term.

title: SK Nexilis building copper foil plant for EV batteries in Poland
summary: SK Nexilis plans to build a copper foil plant for EV batteries in Poland. Copper foil is a key input for battery production, so new supply intended for EV demand can improve near-term expectations for copper demand and bolster copper price sentiment over the next several weeks.

title: Hot Chili fast-tracks Costa Fuego copper feasibility
summary: Hot Chili is fast-tracking feasibility at its Costa Fuego hub in northern Chile, aiming to expand copper output from the Productora mine and evaluate the Cortadera porphyries. The company cites strengthening copper near $10,000/t and improved economics from higher prices as it continues drilling.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 58,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that China’s social inventories of primary aluminium across eight consumption areas fell by 58,000 mt week-on-week to 962,000 mt as of May 27. The decline is attributed mainly to seasonal high demand, which suggests improved physical absorption and potential short-term price support.

title: Exclusive: KPMG managers back liquidation of Singapore firms in $1 billion nickel scandal
summary: KPMG interim judicial managers in Singapore recommended liquidating firms accused in a $1.1 billion bogus nickel trading scheme. The report said investor money was used for alleged fraud, not real nickel trades, and assets are insufficient for creditors. Authorities said forged documents and fake shipment inspections misled investors.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 27/05: LME zinc up 1.6%, copper above $10,000 over morning
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures-style update says LME zinc is up 1.6% and copper is trading above $10,000 over the morning. The excerpt provides an explicit near-term copper price level, pointing to bullish pressure, while it does not give clear immediate price direction for nickel or aluminium.

title: KPMG managers back liquidation of Singapore firms in $1bln nickel scandal
summary: Singapore interim judicial managers at KPMG say firms linked to a $1.1 billion nickel trading scandal should be liquidated, citing insufficient assets. Authorities allege funds from about 1,000 investors were used for non-existent nickel deals, with forged documents and staged shipment inspections.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 27/05: LME zinc up 1.6%, copper above $10,000/t over morning
summary: Fastmarkets/Fastmarkets-style live futures coverage reports copper trading above $10,000/t over the morning, signaling near-term bullish price momentum. The article also references aluminium market conditions (supply disruptions and inventory dynamics) and low-carbon aluminium differential assessment updates, which may influence short-term aluminium pricing expectations.

title: Record high aluminium prices drive Press Metal earnings higher
summary: Press Metal Aluminium Holdings reported a Q1 profit doubling, attributing gains to record high aluminium prices. The company expects global economic recovery to continue supporting demand, helping keep aluminium selling prices elevated. The update reinforces market expectations of sustained strength in aluminium pricing over the near term.

title: Enduro Samples 1,277 g/t Silver & 4.51% Copper on Surface at Cuba - Outlines a 1,800m Long Anomaly
summary: Enduro Metals reports discovery of the Havana vein system on the Cuba Trend at its Newmont Lake Project in BC, with surface samples assaying 4.51–5.34% copper alongside high silver and zinc. Induced polarization data support a chargeable conductor, and management plans expanded drilling and further study of linkages to Chachi.

title: Ivanhoe begins production at Congo's Kamoa-Kakula copper mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines has started copper production at the Kamoa-Kakula mine in DRC after commissioning of the concentrator plant. Phase one targets about 200,000 tpa copper, with later expansion to 400,000 tpa. The JV includes Ivanhoe, Zijin, and the DRC government.

title: Aurubis AG: First copper anodes produced with hydrogen
summary: Aurubis AG reported producing its first copper anodes using hydrogen. The update links to copper refining production processes and could influence expectations about costs or emissions over time. But the announcement does not indicate substantial near-term changes in anode output or market supply, limiting short-term price impact.

title: Canpack to build US aluminum beverage can body manufacturing plant in Muncie
summary: Canpack plans a $380m US aluminum beverage can body manufacturing plant in Muncie, Indiana, creating about 345 jobs and expanding to 425 jobs later. Construction is expected to begin mid-2021 with operations starting in Q4 2022, boosting its end-making capacity and potentially supporting aluminum demand.

title: SPC Nickel Commences Drilling at Its High-Grade Ni-Cu-PGM Janes | The Kingston Whig Standard
summary: SPC Nickel commenced a 2021 drill program at its Janes Ni-Cu-PGM project in Sudbury, targeting continuity of surface mineralization (Trench 1) and an IP anomaly (“Target B”). The release references historic and channel-sample Cu and Ni grades, but involves only exploration drilling with no immediate production impact.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28 Announces Proposed Normal Course Issuer Bid
summary: Nickel 28 Capital Corp. announced a proposed normal course issuer bid to repurchase up to 8.7% of its shares for cancellation after TSXV approval. The company is a nickel-cobalt producer via its Ramu joint venture, but the filing does not indicate any immediate change to nickel output or market fundamentals.

title: Materials Climb With Copper Prices Amid Infrastructure-Bill Optimism
summary: Metals and raw-materials rose on optimism for a U.S. congressional infrastructure compromise. Copper futures surged 2.9% and neared record highs as investors bet lawmakers’ plans—especially “green energy” transition spending—would strengthen copper demand. Miners such as Freeport McMoRan are cited as key beneficiaries.

title: KPMG managers back liquidation of Singapore firms in $1b nickel scandal
summary: KPMG interim managers backed liquidating Singapore firms tied to a $1.1 billion bogus nickel trading scheme, saying investor funds were not used for any nickel trades and documents were forged to sell “nickel shipment” stories. Investigators may recover assets; authorities say at least $1 billion was raised from nearly 1,000 investors.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 78,500 wmt to 5.69 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories across all Chinese ports fell 78,500 wmt to 5.69 million wmt from May 21 to May 28. Stocks in nickel content were 44,500 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also declined to 4.2 million wmt, despite slower unloading and export-peak conditions.

title: SMM Evening Comments (May 28): Nonferrous metals on the SHFE rose across the board, nickel soared 4.85%_SMM
summary: SMM reports broad gains in SHFE nonferrous metals on May 28. Copper closed up 2.22%, aluminium rose 1.47%, and nickel jumped 4.85% on the most-traded SHFE contracts. Open interest also increased for copper and nickel, suggesting strengthening near-term bullish momentum.

title: Shanghai bonded refined nickel stocks rose 1,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows Shanghai bonded refined nickel inventories rose 1,000 mt on the week to 9,700 mt by May 28. Nickel plates and briquettes arrived from LME Asia warehouses, and about 1,000 mt moved into bonded storage because the import window is still in a loss state, leaving domestic stocks low.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Responds to Media Reports Regarding Copper Concentrate Exports from the Democratic Republic of Congo
summary: Ivanhoe Mines responded to reports that DRC provincial authorities issued an order banning copper and cobalt concentrate exports, but noted that companies with minister-approved derogations can still export. The firm says Kamoa-Kakula has applied and is discussing a derogation due to in-country smelting limits. Kamoa-Kakula began production in March 2021.

title: Rio Tinto begins drilling work at Madison copper gold project in US
summary: Rio Tinto has started drilling at the Madison copper-gold project in Montana, with additional diamond drills added to the updated program totaling up to 4,000m. The permitted project is under an earn-in JV, and exploration targets are being drill-tested based on prior work.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Responds to Media Reports Regarding Copper Concentrate Exports from the Democratic Republic of Congo
summary: Ivanhoe Mines responds to DRC media reports of an order banning copper concentrate exports, confirming it received guidance on derogations for firms with Minister of Mines approvals. Ivanhoe says Kamoa-Kakula has applied and is discussing a derogation due to limited in-country smelting capacity, supporting continued copper concentrate flows.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Logjams at Malaysian warehouses exacerbate aluminium shortages
summary: Logjams at LME-registered warehouses in Malaysia, owned by ISTIM UK, are worsening difficulties for US and European buyers to source aluminium. Reuters says strong demand and tight supply are already lifting US physical prices to record highs and keeping Europe near post-Rusal-sanctions peaks, suggesting further bullish pressure.

title: DRC concentrate export ban may tighten global copper, cobalt supply
summary: The DRC reinstated an export ban on copper and cobalt concentrates, while allowing shipments from companies holding waivers. As the world’s top cobalt producer and Africa’s major copper source, the ban may tighten global copper concentrate availability and alter short-term supply expectations for copper markets.

title: DRC backtracks on copper, cobalt export ban | American Metal Market
summary: The report focuses on DRC’s reversal (“backtracks”) on an export ban covering copper (and cobalt). If an export restriction is withdrawn or softened, copper supply expectations improve in the near term, typically pressuring prices as the market adjusts toward higher availability.

title: Electronics exporters seek copper standard review
summary: Philippines electronics exporters (SEIPI) are asking DENR to review tightened wastewater guidelines that lower dissolved copper discharge limits to 0.04 PPM from 1 PPM. The proposed revision awaits DENR/Environment Secretary signature, amid recent cease-and-desist orders for Manila Bay dischargers. The change could affect copper-related industrial demand.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp. Concludes Agreement to Acquire Punitaqui Copper-Gold Mine and Closes First Tranche of Concurrent Financing
summary: Battery Mineral Resources completed the acquisition of the Punitaqui Mining Complex, a recently producing copper-gold mine in Chile, financed partly via a private placement. It plans a low-capital restart program with operations targeted to resume within 4–6 months after drilling and permit updates, adding near-term copper production potential.

title: Copper has become the new gold
summary: The piece argues copper is effectively constrained supply against rapidly rising demand from clean energy, EVs, and related industries. It cites few new mines in development, existing mines nearing peak output, and recycling unable to fully cover the gap. Bank of America projects further major upside.

title: The strike at BHP Billiton's Chilean copper mine continues to unionize against alternative workers._SMM
summary: Union remote operators at BHP’s Escondida and Spence copper mines in Chile entered a second day of strike while BHP brought alternative workers to keep production running. Union leaders say disruption and legal disputes continue, adding uncertainty to global copper supply from the world’s largest copper producer.

title: GOF cripples Simpang Renggam copper-smelting syndicate with arrests of eight
summary: Police arrested eight men for allegedly smelting copper illegally in Simpang Renggam. The GOF said the arrests involved locals and several foreign nationals. By interrupting an illicit copper-smelting syndicate, the operation’s near-term output could be reduced, marginally tightening copper supply expectations.

title: Shanghai copper registers second monthly gain on supply concerns
summary: Shanghai copper rose for a second month as strike activity at BHP’s Escondida and Spence mines in Chile raised supply concerns, while U.S. infrastructure spending plans boosted demand expectations. ShFE nickel and aluminium also advanced, though LME was closed for a holiday. Additional supply bottlenecks were noted in warehouse logistics.

title: Yangshan copper premiums fell to record low_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Yangshan copper premiums for June fell to record lows, with warrants quotes around $29–45/mt and B/L around $20–35/mt. Trades were quiet as oversupply grew, demand for near-term arrivals stayed near absent, and Shanghai bonded copper inventories rose for a sixth week, weighing on import pricing despite weaker cost pressure.

title: Shanghai copper set for monthly gain on U.S. spending plans, Chile strike
summary: Shanghai copper rose toward a second straight monthly gain as traders expect Chilean supply disruption from a BHP mine strike. U.S. plans for massive infrastructure spending boosted concerns of global metals shortages. ShFE nickel and aluminum also climbed, while LME closure limited trading activity.

title: Stratabound Minerals Corp.: Stratabound Reports Anomalous Gold and Copper Results from McIntyre Brook Soil Sampling Program
summary: Stratabound reports 2020 soil sampling from the McIntyre Brook project showing multiple broad copper-in-soil anomalies (>15 ppm, up to the reported anomalous zone patterns) alongside gold anomalies, plus plans for follow-up trenching and expanded sampling. It also notes assay delays due to lab backlogs.

title: Trudeau's EV Ambitions Need Strategic Shift, Nickel CEO Says
summary: Nickel producer Sherritt’s CEO says Canada should coordinate policy to build a North American EV battery hub, not just supply raw materials. With U.S. supply-chain reviews covering large-capacity batteries and critical minerals, and EV growth expected to sharply raise battery-grade nickel demand, sentiment turns supportive for nickel, with some potential spillover to copper.

title: Lower expenses, higher aluminium price, better results
summary: Reykjavík Energy reported strong Q1 2021 results partly driven by significantly higher aluminium prices versus Q1 2020. The firm notes that some power purchase agreements are connected to aluminium pricing, so the aluminium price rebound improved its calculated financial items and overall earnings year-on-year.

title: Rio Tinto closes deal to buy stake in Western Copper and Gold | iNFOnews | Thompson-Okanagan's News Source
summary: Western Copper and Gold said Rio Tinto Canada completed a $25.6 million investment, buying 11.8 million shares at $1.27 each for an 8% stake. The funding will help advance its Casino project in Yukon, a copper-and-gold development. The deal supports copper project progress.

title: Strike enters fifth day at 2 BHP copper mines in Chile
summary: Workers strike at BHP’s Escondida and Spence copper mines in Chile entered a fifth day. The union challenges BHP’s use of substitute workers amid Chilean labor-law concerns, while BHP cites contingency plans to keep operations within legal limits. Production status has not been reported, increasing near-term supply risk.

title: Byron King: Copper is Hot, What's the Best Way to Make Money?
summary: The interview argues copper prices are at new highs due to strong demand beyond China and declining output from the world’s largest mines. It suggests major copper miners and some junior/exploration firms could benefit, and links the supply-demand setup to potential continued price strength and consolidation.

title: London copper rises to US$10,328 a ton
summary: London copper is reported to have risen to US$10,328 per ton. The article excerpt does not detail specific supply-demand drivers or policy developments, but the headline itself directly reflects an upward move in copper prices, indicating bullish near-term sentiment for the metal.

title: Mineração Vale Verde completes construction at the Serrote copper-gold mine ahead of schedule and under budget
summary: Mineração Vale Verde says construction of the Serrote copper-gold mine and processing plant is finished ahead of schedule and under budget in Brazil. Ramp-up is planned for the second half of 2021, with first copper-gold-silver concentrate shipments targeted for November 2021, supporting expectations of additional copper supply.

title: Bam Bam Resources Corp.: Bam Bam Announces Expanded Soil Sampling Underway at Majuba Hill Nevada Copper Project
summary: Bam Bam Resources announced expanded soil sampling and additional geophysical work at its Majuba Hill copper project in Nevada. The company cites geochemical and geophysical indications of copper/silver mineralization and provides shallow intercepts with ~0.6% copper grades, but no immediate production changes or supply impacts are reported.

title: FLSmidth A/S: FLSmidth receives significant order for a range of key equipment for greenfield Chilean copper mine
summary: FLSmidth received a DKK ~200m order to supply mineral processing equipment (crushers, SAG/ball mills, flotation cells, thickeners, pumps) for Ausenco’s Mantoverde greenfield copper project in Chile. Delivery is targeted for end H1 2022. The mine is expected to produce 106,000 tons of fine copper annually.

title: Copper prices to fall initially before rallying_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM expects mixed LME/SHFE copper moves last week, with initial pressure from US infrastructure and dovish Fed comments plus month-end cash-flow issues. It also highlights reduced smelter output, lower arriving imports, declining social inventories, and uncertainty from a Chile BHP mine strike that could tighten global supply and support a rally.

title: Manufacturing activity across nickel downstream sectors in China returned to expansion in May_SMM
summary: SMM data shows China’s downstream nickel-sector PMI rose to 50.67 in May, signaling renewed expansion. Production and raw-material inventory sub-indices recovered, while tighter ferronickel supply encouraged stainless steel firms to stockpile. Battery orders improved, partially offset by seasonal weakening in alloy and electroplating.

title: Nickel prices rebounded sharply after plunging_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports nickel rebounded sharply after a plunge, gaining nearly 5% as a new US $6 trillion infrastructure plan boosted capital-market enthusiasm for commodities. The rally is linked to expected nickel demand from high stainless-steel production schedules and new energy products. SHFE and LME nickel are expected to fluctuate within provided ranges.

title: FLSmidth receives significant order for a range of key equipment for greenfield Chilean copper mine
summary: FLSmidth says it has won a large DKK200m order to supply mineral processing equipment—crushers, SAG/ball mills, flotation cells, thickeners, cyclones and pumps—for the Mantoverde greenfield copper project in Chile’s Atacama region. Mantoverde is projected to produce 106,000 tons of fine copper annually. Delivery is scheduled by mid-2022.

title: UPDATE 1-Some Japan buyers agree to pay 24-25% higher Q3 aluminium premium of $185/T
summary: Japan buyers agreed to pay a 24–25% higher Q3 aluminium premium of $185/ton. A higher premium typically signals improved demand/availability balance for physical aluminium, which can support nearby aluminium pricing through stronger expectations for Q3 supply costs.

title: Emgold Mining Corporation: Emgold's Partner Kennecott Exploration Expands Diamond Drill Program at the New York Canyon Copper Property, NV
summary: Emgold Mining said its JV partner, Kennecott Exploration (Rio Tinto subsidiary), is expanding a diamond drilling program at the New York Canyon copper property in Nevada. Drilling results from several holes are pending, with no mineral output or supply changes reported. The update is exploratory and mainly sentiment-driven for copper.

title: BeMetals Corp.: BeMetals Commences 2021 Exploration Program at the Pangeni Copper Project
summary: BeMetals begins its 2021 exploration program at the Pangeni Copper Project in Zambia, expanding work around D and SW copper prospects. The plan includes an AEM survey plus ~4,000m of aircore and ~1,500m of core drilling to test continuity and higher-grade zones based on encouraging prior copper intercepts.

title: Brunswick Exploration Inc.: Brunswick Exploration Announces Multiple Copper-Gold-Silver Discoveries at the Fundy Gold Project
summary: Brunswick Exploration announced new outcrop grab sample discoveries at its Fundy Gold Project, including high copper grades (up to ~12% Cu) alongside gold and silver. The company suggests potential IOCG mineralization and plans further prospecting. As this is early exploration with no production changes, near-term copper price impact is likely limited.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Announces Drilling to Date Intersects Nickel-Copper Mineralization in More than 60 Holes, All Located Outside of the Resource Area at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reported additional drilling at its Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in Minnesota, intersecting nickel-copper mineralization in more than 60 holes at shallow depths, including continuous trends in CGO East and additional mineralization in CGO Bend. Assays remain pending and no production or trade changes were announced.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Announces Drilling to Date Intersects Nickel-Copper Mineralization in More than 60 Holes, All Located Outside of the Resource Area at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals announced that drilling at the Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project intersected nickel-copper mineralization in more than 60 holes, including shallow and wide intervals outside the current resource area. Assays for the latest holes remain pending, and a new resource estimate is planned later this year or early next year.

title: US Copper Corp.: US Copper Corp Announces Commencement of Drilling Program
summary: US Copper Corp says drilling has begun at the Superior deposit of its Moonlight-Superior copper project in California. The 7,000–10,000 ft core program aims to verify historic copper assays, test for silver/gold credits, and upgrade resources from inferred to indicated. The company links progress to a copper price recovery and electrification demand.

title: Wedgemount Resources Corp.: Wedgemount Announces Closing of Strategic Red Copper Property Acquisition
summary: Wedgemount Resources announced the closing of an option agreement to acquire a 100% interest in the Red Copper property in British Columbia’s Toodoggone copper belt, subject to 2% NSR. The company plans further exploration with stated cash, share issuance, and budget commitments, but no near-term production or supply disruption is described.

title: CopAur Minerals Inc.: CopAur Minerals Outlines Upcoming Exploration Activities at Williams Copper-Gold Project in BC
summary: CopAur Minerals outlines a 5,000-metre exploration program at its Williams copper-gold project in British Columbia, including drilling to test a GIC porphyry copper-gold target and additional geophysics and soil sampling. The release is exploratory and does not affect current copper supply, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp.: Tartisan Files Enhanced Disclosure and (Amended) Technical Report and Updated Mineral Resource Estimate of the Kenbridge Nickel Project, Kenora, Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. filed an amended technical report and updated mineral resource estimate for the Kenbridge nickel project in Ontario. The update includes revised disclosures and reports pit-constrained and out-of-pit resources totaling 95 Mlb contained nickel and associated copper. It outlines expansion plans and potential depth continuity from geophysics.

title: Why Copper Prices Are at All-Time Highs – ShareCafe
summary: Copper prices are described as at all-time highs, supported by supply constraints (COVID-related dislocation, slower scrap response, declining ore grades, limited new discoveries) and demand strength from stimulus and clean-energy/renewables electrification. The piece flags inventory drawdowns and China purchasing/speculative positioning as key near-term swing factors.

title: Giga Metals Corporation: Test Results Support Potential Carbon Neutrality of Giga's Turnagain Nickel Project
summary: Giga Metals reported University of British Columbia testwork showing CO2 mineral sequestration in tailings from its Turnagain nickel project, supporting a “carbon neutral” goal. The company cites lower expected emissions under electrified hauling and potential incentives from carbon policies, but provides no near-term production impacts.

title: Century Aluminum Jobs Announcement and Ceremonial Restart at South Carolina Aluminum Smelter with Governor Henry McMaster
summary: Century Aluminum will hold a ceremonial restart at its Mt. Holly, South Carolina primary aluminum smelter alongside Governor Henry McMaster. The company cites significant capital investment to increase production capacity and create new jobs. The restart and capacity expansion are likely to affect near-term supply expectations for aluminium.

title: Funds cut copper exposure as Chinese impetus fades: Andy Home
summary: Funds have sharply reduced net long positions in copper on both CME and LME as China’s buying impetus fades and the market shows signs of glutted supplies and de-stocking. Speculative longs are at the lowest levels since last year, suggesting rising caution and potential near-term bearish pressure on copper.

title: Brunswick Exploration Announces Multiple Copper-Gold-Silver Discoveries at the Fundy Gold Project
summary: Brunswick Exploration said it has announced multiple copper-gold-silver discoveries at its Fundy Gold Project. The announcement can improve market expectations for potential future copper supply, supporting a bullish sentiment toward copper. However, the impact is likely limited without confirmation of resources size, development timeline, or near-term output changes.

title: Pacific Aluminium writes off Tiwai value
summary: Pacific Aluminium has taken a $223m impairment charge tied to the pending closure of its Tiwai aluminium smelter. The majority owner’s write-down signals imminent or likely reduction in primary aluminium production, tightening supply expectations and potentially supporting nearby aluminium prices.

title: BHP says Chile's copper operations 'normal' despite strike
summary: BHP said its Escondida and Spence copper operations in Chile were running normally despite a union walkout at the Integrated Operations Center. A second union at Spence is in government-mediated talks to avoid a strike. Escondida on-site workers may begin bargaining soon as copper prices rise.

title: Material Matters: Coal, Nickel And Aluminium
summary: The piece reviews bullish expert views on nickel and aluminium. For nickel, Indonesia’s new high-pressure acid leach project and existing capacity buildout raise output, while Macquarie warns of weaker fundamentals in 2H as supply ramps. For aluminium, Citi expects structurally higher prices as China adds less capacity and demand eventually catches up.

title: Material Matters: Coal, Nickel And Aluminium
summary: The piece highlights Indonesia’s expansion plans for nickel/cobalt and warns that rising Indonesian supply could weigh on nickel fundamentals in the second half. Separately, Citi is bullish on aluminium, arguing China’s slower supply additions may eventually tighten the market, pushing prices higher in 2022.

title: Peru's Castillo has copper tax deals in his sights; Chinese firms at risk
summary: Peru presidential contender Pedro Castillo is seeking to renegotiate copper mining tax stability agreements and proposes materially higher royalties and state take. Reuters analysis says Chinese miners (including MMG and Chinalco) would be hardest hit. The policy uncertainty could weigh on copper investment sentiment as Peru remains a major supply source.

title: Peru's Castillo has copper tax deals in his sights; Chinese firms at risk | WTVB | 1590 AM · 95.5 FM
summary: Peru’s presidential frontrunner Pedro Castillo proposes royalties and renegotiating copper miners’ tax stability deals, threatening changes in taxation for large Chinese-linked producers. The move could unsettle markets in Peru’s top copper region and affect output/investment expectations, adding political risk that investors typically price bearish for copper.

title: Copper eases on weak China demand, stronger dollar
summary: Copper prices eased as signs of weakening demand in China emerged, while a firmer U.S. dollar increased the cost of dollar-priced metals for other currency holders. LME and Shanghai copper contracts fell slightly. The article also notes aluminium in Shanghai declined, pointing to overall softness in industrial metals.

title: Copper concentrate imports dropped slightly in April_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s copper concentrate imports fell to 1.92m mt in April, down 11.5% MoM, driven by Peru road blockages and an indefinite truckers strike that disrupted Antapaccay and hindered Las Bambas/Constantia logistics. Chile and Mongolia supply were also hit. Disruptions eased, and May imports may stabilise, but April weakness is a near-term negative for copper.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Kamoa-Kakula Phase 1 Concentrator Plant Produced First Copper Concentrate on May 25; Ramp Up Toward Nameplate Capacity of 3.8 Million Tonnes of Ore per Year Progressing Smoothly
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said the Kamoa-Kakula Phase 1 concentrator produced its first copper concentrate on May 25 and is ramping toward nameplate capacity. Ore grades and mined tonnages in May were detailed, with first concentrate deliveries to the Lualaba Copper Smelter on June 1, supporting near-term copper supply.

title: Ethos Gold Corp.: Ethos Commences Drilling at Perk-Rocky Copper-Gold Porphyry Project
summary: Ethos Gold commenced a maiden drilling program at the Perk-Rocky copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia. The company targets multiple porphyry centers within an extensive alteration footprint, funded for ~2,000 metres of drilling. The news is copper-relevant but does not imply immediate supply changes.

title: Over 10% of world's copper and zinc in 2020 produced in Peru | News | ANDINA
summary: Peru’s energy and mines ministry says 10.7% of global copper output in 2020 came from Peru (2.15 million FMT) and highlights strong post-COVID recovery, plus reserve shares. The data is mainly historical and does not signal an immediate supply or policy change affecting near-term copper prices.

title: GLOBAL COPPER WRAP: Premiums fall in China and other Asian markets; Europe, US unchanged
summary: Global Copper Wrap reports that copper premiums declined in China and other Asian markets, while Europe and the US remained unchanged. It also includes procedural corrections and methodology-related updates to some aluminium and steel assessments, but the only clear price-direction signal for tracked metals is the fall in Asian copper premiums.

title: Mineração Vale Verde completes Serrote copper-gold mine build
summary: Privately held Mineração Vale Verde and funding partner Appian Capital Advisory have completed the Serrote copper-gold mine construction in Alagoas, Brazil, ahead of schedule and under budget. The project is expected to produce about 22,000 tonnes on average at full capacity, supporting copper supply expectations.

title: Ivanhoe's Congo copper JV inks 10-year processing deal with nearby smelter
summary: Ivanhoe’s Congo copper JV, Kamoa-Kakula, has started production and signed a 10-year processing/tolling deal to send part of its copper concentrate to the nearby Lualaba smelter owned by CNMC. The agreement follows the DRC’s continued concentrate export ban requiring waivers, supporting domestic supply flows.

title: Why Pan Global Resources is at the forefront of the copper space
summary: Pan Global Resources says its drilling at the Escacena project in Spain’s Iberian Pyrite Belt is “hitting copper with every hole,” with multiple holes reporting near-surface copper and high-grade intersections. The firm plans expanded 2021 drilling and potential work at the Al Andalus permitting stage, aiming to grow discovery size.

title: Chilean copper output falls 2% in April on lower Codelco, Escondida volumes
summary: Chile’s copper production reportedly declined 2% in April, attributed to lower output from Codelco and Escondida. Reduced Chilean mine supply can weaken near-term copper availability expectations, likely pressuring prices lower over the coming days as markets adjust to the slower production pace.

title: Top Copper Nation Chile 'Pretty Confident' of Tempering Tax Bill
summary: Chile’s mining minister said the government is “pretty confident” of tempering a copper royalty/tax bill as the senate debates it. The lower house version could raise copper company taxes to 70–80% from about 40%. A smaller increase, potentially up to ~45%, is viewed as more reasonable.

title: Nickel price: Fitch upgrades forecast on long-term uptrend
summary: Fitch Solutions raised its long-term nickel price forecast to US$16,500/t from US$15,750/t for 2021, arguing the global nickel market will remain in deficit and the price will trend gradually higher. The update is supportive for nickel bulls, though effects may be more sentiment-driven than immediate.

title: Libero Copper & Gold Chief Executive Officer Ian Harris
summary: Libero Copper & Gold CEO Ian Harris says the company is mobilizing fieldwork and preparing a 5,000-meter diamond drill program at its Big Red porphyry copper-gold project in British Columbia. Work includes geophysics (3D induced polarization) and follow-up drilling on the Terry copper discovery, starting in early-to-mid June.

title: Century Aluminum Jobs Announcement and Ceremonial Restart at South Carolina Aluminum Smelter with Governor Henry McMaster and Majority Whip Jim Clyburn
summary: Century Aluminum will hold a ceremonial restart and jobs announcement at its Mt. Holly, South Carolina primary aluminum smelter. The company describes a significant capital investment underway to increase production capacity and create jobs. The event is tied to raising smelting output, a factor that can influence near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: BHP says operations at Escondida, Spence copper mines in Chile 'normal' despite strike
summary: BHP said operations at its Chilean copper mines Escondida and Spence are “normal” even with a strike underway. The statement suggests no meaningful near-term production disruption, easing concerns about copper supply tightness and potentially putting downward pressure on prices over coming days.

title: Copper edges up as supply fears outweigh weak Chinese demand
summary: Copper prices edged higher as supply risks outweighed softer Chinese demand. Three-month LME copper rose to $10,165/t. Strikes at BHP’s Escondida and Spence mines and a landslip at Rio Tinto’s Bingham Canyon mine disrupted production, while Vale plans to suspend Sudbury operations in Canada.

title: Copper scrap held back as copper prices rose sharply _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports a bullish mood as copper prices jumped after Labour Day. Scrap outlets and traders held cargoes, creating tight spot availability and leading scrap users to cut orders or lower operating rates. Regulatory announcements later eased prices, but scrap re-flow and import dynamics were mixed, with April scrap imports down MoM and set to fall in May.

title: London copper rises to US$10,165 a ton
summary: London copper is reported higher at around US$10,165 per ton. Other listed items are mainly broader macro and market headlines (e.g., trade deficit, financial conditions, policy/geo concerns) without specific metal supply or demand details. The only direct metal signal in the article is the copper price gain.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 1,100 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows aluminium billet stocks across five major consumption areas in China rose 1.2% to 89,400 mt as of June 3, after prices weakened and downstream adopted a wait-and-see stance. Logistic and consumption disruptions from Guangdong pandemic measures and power curtailment reduced raw-material demand.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 8,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s social inventories of primary aluminium ingots fell 8,000 mt week-on-week to 954,000 mt as of June 3. Declines continued in areas such as Wuxi, Shanghai, and Gongyi, while Nanhai increased slightly. Lower inventories suggest tighter short-term supply conditions.

title: RCs for blister copper rose further_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says domestic blister copper RCs rose to 1,800–2,000 yuan/mt in May (+100 month-on-month) and imported blister copper RCs increased to $185–205/mt cif (+$15). Quotes diverged by region, with southern prices lifted amid smelters restocking despite oversupply and thinning trades for imports.

title: Spruce Ridge Resources Limited: Spruce Ridge Reports the Start of Updated Mineral Resource Estimate and PEA on Great Burnt Copper Property
summary: Spruce Ridge announced progress on a PEA for its Great Burnt copper deposit, including an updated mineral resource estimate and ongoing metallurgical testing following 2020 drilling. Management notes rising market interest in copper for electrification and expects potential benefit from higher copper prices, but no immediate supply-impact is stated.

title: China's primary aluminium output seen peaking in 2024
summary: Antaike said China’s primary aluminium output may rise into 2024 before slowing as consumption plateaus and recycled secondary aluminium takes a larger share. Policy aims to cap smelting capacity amid emissions pressure, with plans to reduce reliance on coal and expand cleaner electricity. Chalco also issued green bonds for wind power.

title: Grizzly Discoveries Inc.: Grizzly Advances Its New Copper Targets with Planned Fieldwork at Its Robocop Project, Southeastern British Columbia, Canada and Closes First Tranche of Its Private Placement
summary: Grizzly Discoveries announced planned June 2021 fieldwork and IP/geochemical follow-up on copper targets at its Robocop project in southeast British Columbia, citing historical copper grades in prior drilling and trenches. The release is exploration-focused and does not indicate production or supply disruptions, limiting near-term copper price impact.

title: Wedgemount Signs Option Agreement to Acquire Friendly Lake – Deer Lake Copper-Gold Property in South-Central B.C.
summary: Wedgemount Resources signed an option agreement to acquire the Friendly Lake–Deer Lake copper-gold property in south-central British Columbia, involving cash, share issuance, and planned exploration. The release discusses prior copper mineralization and future field work plans, but provides no near-term production or supply disruption details.

title: Copper Discovery which is at all time highs. Brigadier Gold (OTC Markets: BGADF) Makes Copper Discovery at Picachos
summary: Brigadier Gold said its Picachos project in Mexico has discovered bulk-tonnage type copper mineralization. Trenching results reported copper grades from 0.05% to 1.34% (field XRF) and silver assays, with additional assays pending from phase-one drilling. The update is copper-focused, supporting mildly bullish sentiment.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jun 3): Shanghai nonferrous metals declined for the most part, nickel advanced 0.07%_SMM
summary: SMM reports that SHFE nonferrous metals mostly fell on June 3 after investors reacted to China data. Copper slid 1.28% and aluminium fell 1.37% with lower open interest, while nickel edged up 0.07%. The note links moves to macro outlook and ongoing monitoring of US data.

title: Century Aluminum Hosts Ribbon Cutting Ceremony with South Carolina Governor Henry McMaster and U.S. House Majority Whip James E. Clyburn
summary: Century Aluminum held a ribbon cutting for the planned restart and expansion of its Mount Holly, South Carolina primary aluminum smelter, highlighting a 50% capacity increase after a restart and a $60+ million investment. The company also expects 100 new aluminum jobs. It credits Section 232 support in remarks.

title: Timmins mine aims to cash in on global demand for nickel
summary: Canadian Nickel’s CEO says the Crawford nickel deposit could be developed on aggressive timelines to supply anticipated EV-driven nickel demand and reduce reliance on Indonesia. The company discusses feasibility, permitting, and potential use of the Kidd Creek mill for early de-risking, supporting bullish sentiment for nickel.

title: Taseko expects 'money-maker' Florence Copper's draft permit this month
summary: Taseko Mines says it expects the draft permit for its Florence Copper project in Canada this month. As the company views Florence as a potential “money-maker” and a contender to add new copper supply over the medium term, the permitting update may lift near-term expectations for copper production.

title: Century Aluminum expanding S.C. smelter operations
summary: Century Aluminum announced a $60+ million expansion of its Berkeley County smelter operations, aimed at creating 100 new jobs. The project increases primary aluminum production capacity, which can pressure market expectations for aluminum supply and weigh on prices over the next several days to weeks.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 252,000 wmt to 5.95 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 252,000 wmt to 5.95 million wmt from May 28 to June 4, with Ni content at 46,800 mt. Stocks increased further at major ports. Bad weather in the Philippines delayed shipments, though new China ferronickel lines may slow inventory growth later.

title: Copperstone Resources AB: Copperstone opens the gates to the Viscaria mine in Kiruna after 25 years, for further environmental studies
