summary: Rosprirodnadzor said fines paid by Nornickel for a Taimyr Peninsula fuel spill will be used for Arctic cleanup and remediation of ecological damage. The Krasnoyarsk court ordered a 146 billion ruble fine after a 20,000-ton fuel release in May 2020, and Nornickel has settled it.

title: Copper rises on weaker dollar ahead of Fed chair's testimony
summary: Copper prices rose as the dollar paused before U.S. Fed Chair Powell’s testimony, making greenback-priced metals cheaper. LME three-month copper and Shanghai July copper both gained slightly. The note also pointed to active downstream buying if prices stay below 70,000, while supply pressures remain.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jun 22): Shanghai nonferrous metals rose across the board, nickel advanced 3.58%_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals rising across the board after Fed Chair Powell’s updated inflation projections and a less aggressive path for rate hikes. Nickel led (+3.58%), while copper (+0.85%) and aluminium (+1.58%) also climbed. Aluminium support comes from production cuts in key regions and falling social inventories.

title: India's huge bauxite import bill needs to be diverted to develop local supply chains
summary: India’s aluminium industry relies on imported bauxite, driving substantial forex losses and rising imports over the past six years. The article argues that delayed domestic bauxite mine auctions and pricing rules inflate ex-mine costs. It calls for faster auctions to expand supply, attract investment, and strengthen the aluminium value chain.

title: Western Copper and Gold Announces Positive PEA on Casino
summary: Western Copper and Gold released a positive Preliminary Economic Assessment for its Casino copper-gold-molybdenum project, citing base-case copper at US$3.35/lb and showing project returns depend significantly on copper prices. The release is about project economics and permitting, with no immediate change to copper supply or demand.

title: China to release 20,000 mt of copper, 30,000 mt of zinc, and 50,000 mt of aluminium reserves_SMM
summary: China’s National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration will release a first batch of metal reserves: 20,000 mt of copper and 50,000 mt of aluminium. The copper release is small versus monthly consumption (~2%), limiting impact. Aluminium is expected to meet expectations and SHFE aluminium may rise slightly overnight.

title: China to release 20,000 mt of copper, 30,000 mt of zinc, and 50,000 mt of aluminium reserves_SMM
summary: China will release the first batch of national metal reserves: 20,000 mt of copper and 50,000 mt of aluminium (with zinc also included but not tracked here). The copper amount is only ~2% of monthly consumption, while aluminium is described as lower than expected and SHFE aluminium is expected to rise slightly overnight.

title: The Northern Miner Podcast – episode 244: 'There's only a few smelters in the West' — Battery makers 'worried' about nickel supply, ft Ken Hoffman
summary: Northern Miner Podcast episode 244 features Ken Hoffman discussing the nickel market and battery makers’ worry about securing reliable, ESG-friendly nickel supply. The conversation emphasizes limited Western smelters and the challenge of ensuring steady output for EV batteries, which can influence near-term nickel supply expectations and pricing sentiment.

title: Jaguar Land Rover at risk of running out of aluminium
summary: Liberty Aluminium Technologies (LAT) is in last-ditch talks to avoid administration, with reports it could collapse within days. If its UK sites close, aluminium supply to Jaguar Land Rover could be disrupted, affecting vehicle production. No buyer or outcome is confirmed, but the risk adds near-term strain.

title: China to release 50,000 tonnes of aluminum reserves
summary: China will release 50,000 tonnes of aluminium from national reserves via open bidding starting July 5, restricted to processing/manufacturing users and intended for prompt production use. Officials also said additional nonferrous metal reserve releases, including copper, may occur in response to market price changes.

title: Ford Working on Int'l Grants to Empower Women in Copper & Cobalt
summary: Ford is partnering with nonprofits to run a pilot empowering women in the DRC’s copper and cobalt artisanal mining supply chains. The program aims to improve financial access, formalize small mines, and reduce child labor. The DRC is a dominant cobalt exporter, but the article offers no direct pricing or production impact details.

title: Operating rates at secondary aluminium plants continued to decline in May_SMM
summary: SMM says secondary aluminium producers’ operating rates fell to 59.56% in May, down 5.44 points MoM, with die-casting firms cutting output as auto demand weakens amid chip shortages. Scrap supply is still in deficit, but power curtailment and weaker orders reduced production. ADC12 fell toward 18,500 yuan/mt in June, with bearish sentiment and expected further declines.

title: Scarce supply and strong demand pushed up nickel ore prices_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports tight nickel ore supply and strong demand in China, keeping 1.5% CIF nickel ore prices elevated (around $64/wmt) and suggesting further increases to $65–70/wmt this week. Most sellers are sold out for July, while shipping rates, freight capacity constraints, and higher oil costs lift delivered costs.

title: Los Andes Copper Ltd. Receives Final Molybdenum Assessment Results and Concentrate Specifications for the Vizcachitas Project
summary: Los Andes Copper reported metallurgical results for its Vizcachitas copper-molybdenum project, confirming molybdenum recovery assumptions and producing “clean” copper concentrates. The company cites projected final copper concentrate grades of ~22.9%–24.4% copper and specifies no major penalty elements, supporting copper project economics.

title: Los Andes Copper Ltd. Receives Final Molybdenum Assessment Results
summary: Los Andes Copper reported final molybdenum flotation results and copper concentrate specifications for the Vizcachitas PFS in Chile. The metallurgical work confirms improved molybdenum recovery versus the PEA and projects copper concentrate grades of about 22.9–24.4%, supporting cleaner concentrates without penalty penalties. Copper project economics sentiment improves.

title: BSTDB provides 40 million USD loan to aluminium producer ALRO
summary: BSTDB is providing a $40 million seven-year corporate loan to Romanian aluminium producer ALRO for capital investment. The funding will target improved energy management and higher value-added production capacity, aligned with ESG and emissions-reduction goals. ALRO is a large European aluminium producer with exports to 50+ countries.

title: Emirates Global Aluminium in talks to refinance $6bln loan - sources
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) is in talks with banks to refinance and reprice a roughly $6.5 billion syndicated loan from 2019, seeking longer tenor and lower interest costs. The move is aimed at better financing conditions after the 2020 downturn, supporting the company’s aluminium production outlook.

title: NPI cost based on nickel ore inventory purchased 25 days earlier fell slightly in May_SMM
summary: SMM reports May actual cash costs for RKEF and EAF high-grade NPI producers were mixed, falling partly because raw material inventory prices dropped, but offset by higher coal/coke costs. Despite lower May costs, the article says profits likely shrink in June as ore prices follow NPI price movements.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Main Zone Extension and Additional Drilling Results at Crawford Nickel Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel announced that drilling at its Crawford nickel sulphide project extended the Main Zone mineralization north and northwest, reported new higher-grade PGM intersections within dunite, and discovered/extended PGM and nickel zones at North and East Zones. Results define broader nickel mineralization and remain open for further expansion.

title: Palladium One Mining Inc.: Palladium One Drills 7.4% Ni_Eq (164 lbs/tonne) over 4.5 Meters Including 10.2% Ni_Eq (224 lbs/tonne) over 1.7 Meters at Tyko Nickel-Copper Project, in Ontario, Canada
summary: Palladium One reported Phase II drilling results at its Tyko nickel-copper project, including intercepts grading up to 10.2% nickel equivalent (with copper-equivalent also stated) and a continuous 350-metre strike length. The release highlights exploration plans (VTEM survey, fieldwork) but provides no near-term mine or production update.

title: Goldplay Strengthens Portuguese Portfolio - Signs Definitive Agreement To Acquire Past Producing Copper Mine and Highly Prospective Gold Projects
summary: Goldplay Mining agreed to acquire a Portuguese company holding past producing copper projects, including the Aparis underground copper mine, plus prospective gold assets. The plan is further drilling over multiple years to expand copper zones. The announcement is exploration-focused with no near-term production or supply change stated.

title: China is planning to release 50,000 tonnes of aluminium from its reserves
summary: China’s reserves administration will release 50,000 tonnes of aluminium from national reserves via open bidding starting July 5, aiming to curb commodity price increases. The aluminium must be used promptly for production. China also signaled multi-batch reserve releases of nonferrous metals, including copper.

title: Copper edges up after Fed chief vows to keep rates low
summary: Copper prices edged higher as investors reacted to U.S. Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s vow to keep interest rates low to support economic recovery. This reduced fears of imminent monetary tightening after last week’s sharp selloff. LME three-month copper rose 0.4% and China’s July contract also gained.

title: Battery Minerals to acquire Russell copper project in Australia
summary: Battery Minerals agreed to buy the Russell Copper Project in Western Australia from iCopper, with cash and share payments and further contingent consideration after tenement control. The project lies near a Savannah nickel-copper-cobalt asset, and initial drilling and sampling are planned, but no production is imminent.

title: Copper's Rising importance in Growing Infrastructure & Technology Needs Causing the Supply and Demand to Remain High
summary: The article argues copper’s importance for infrastructure and technology and highlights Ridgestone Mining’s maiden RC drill program on its El Cobre copper target in Mexico, with permitting expected within weeks. It also references major copper producers’ output and higher commodity prices, supporting a mildly bullish copper sentiment.

title: Trafigura and Mubadala plan to divest Spanish copper miner MATSA
summary: Trafigura and Mubadala reportedly plan to divest Spanish copper miner MATSA in a deal potentially valued up to $2bn, with offers due by week-end. MATSA operates mines in Huelva and runs processing facilities producing over 300,000t of copper concentrate annually, but the report provides no immediate production impact.

title: Mubadala acquires 2.6% stake in Russian aluminium company En+
summary: Mubadala acquired a 2.6% stake in Russia’s En+, increasing its total ownership to 2.86%. En+ controls Rusal, a major aluminium producer, and the company expects primary aluminium demand to grow 5–6% this year. The news is supportive but likely too small to move near-term prices.

title: EU envoy sees 'plenty of time' to resolve U.S.-EU dispute over steel, aluminum tariffs | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: The EU’s top diplomat in Washington said there is sufficient time to resolve the U.S.-EU dispute over steel and aluminum tariffs, citing progress from last week’s summit. He referenced an agreement to suspend tariffs related to aircraft subsidies for five years and said Brussels is pressing for broader resolution.

title: Deep-South Met with The Minister of Mines and Energy of Namibia on HAIB Copper Licence Renewal
summary: Deep-South says Namibia’s Minister of Mines refused to renew its Haib copper exploration licence, citing inability to advance to pre-feasibility and complete planned drilling. After meetings, the Minister will review information, but the company has suspended work on site and hopes retrenchments can be avoided.

title: Copper prices decline on U.S. rate hike fears
summary: Copper prices fell as U.S. Fed officials’ comments increased fears of a sooner-than-expected rate hike, raising concerns about reduced liquidity and slower global recovery. The three-month LME copper contract dropped 1.2%. LME aluminium fell 0.9% and nickel rose 0.4%, reflecting mixed but broadly macro-driven metal sentiment.

title: Copper prices fall on firm dollar, supply pressure
summary: Copper prices fell 1.5% as a firm dollar and fears of a sooner-than-expected U.S. rate hike pressured metal demand. Traders also cited expectations of more copper concentrate in coming months and rising inventories, while mentioning China’s smaller-than-expected reserve release. LME aluminium and nickel also eased.

title: This Copper Miner Is Facing New Taxes in Chile. The Stock Is Already Taking a Hit.
summary: Chile’s political shift to the left is raising expectations of higher taxes on resource companies, pressuring copper miner Antofagasta. The article also points to recent declines in copper prices, suggesting weaker near-term sentiment for copper and potential downside for related market pricing over coming days.

title: EnGold Mines Ltd.: EnGold Commences Drilling at Lac La Hache Copper Gold Project
summary: EnGold Mines began diamond drilling at its 100% owned Lac La Hache copper-gold project in British Columbia, targeting porphyry and skarn-style prospects including Ann North. Management expects an active exploration season and mentions strong metals markets and a pending $8 million financing, but provides no production changes.

title: Indonesia drawing plans to restrict nickel pig iron, ferronickel smelters
summary: Indonesia’s mining ministry is considering restricting new smelter construction for nickel pig iron and ferronickel to better utilize limited nickel ore reserves for higher-value products. Existing and under-construction plants are exempt. The plan could curb incremental supply of nickel intermediates, supporting near-term nickel market expectations.

title: Decks cleared for Midhani's aluminium alloy plant in Nellore
summary: Regulatory and land compensation obstacles were resolved for Midhani’s planned aluminium alloy plant in Nellore, with APIIC settlement negotiations leading to acceptance by affected land holders. Construction is expected to recommence, pending environment clearance and consent for establishment. The project could expand future aluminium alloy supply.

title: Large brush fire sparked by wires downed by copper thieves: police
summary: Police say a brush fire at the former Ford auto plant in Elgin County was triggered when copper thieves cut down a utility pole with three transformers. Stolen copper wire downed the lines, sparking and igniting grass. Crews extinguished the fire quickly; the story signals localized copper theft only.

title: German economy minister: EU, U.S. can resolve differences over steel and aluminum tariffs by end of year
summary: Germany’s economy minister says EU and U.S. can likely resolve differences over steel and aluminum tariffs by year-end. Talks in Washington opened a window to settle tariff disputes, which would improve expected aluminum trade conditions and reduce downside pricing pressure for the metal versus an escalated tariff outcome.

title: Material Matters: Coal, Oil & Gas, and Copper
summary: A commodities outlook highlights Macquarie’s 13–14% upgrades to copper price forecasts for 2022–25 and expects a ~250kt copper deficit in 2021, with deficits persisting structurally thereafter. The broker’s base-metals stance implies improving copper fundamentals despite a cyclical June-quarter pullback.

title: Tongling Nonferrous Metals : China copper smelters set Q3 treatment charge floor at $55/T
summary: China’s top copper smelters (CSPT) set Q3 treatment and refining charges at a $55/tonne and 5.5 cents/lb floor. Charges function as smelter revenue tied to copper concentrate volumes. After low spot TC/RCs squeezed smelter margins, the new floor suggests firmer concentrate terms going forward.

title: China copper smelters set Q3 treatment charge floor at $55/T
summary: China’s top copper smelters via the CSPT set a Q3 floor for treatment and refining charges at $55/t and 5.5 cents per lb after a meeting in Tongling. TC/RCs are paid by miners to smelters for refining copper concentrate and influence smelter margins when concentrate markets are tight.

title: China Baowu, Brazil's Vale Partner on Nickel Project in Indonesia
summary: China Baowu and Vale will partner to develop a nickel pig iron/smelting project in Indonesia’s Sulawesi Tengah. The plan includes eight smelting lines and expected output of 73,000 tons of nickel per year, powered by natural gas to cut emissions. The deal targets future nickel feedstock for Baowu’s stainless steel.

title: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 137,000 wmt to 5.1 million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 137,000 wmt to 5.1 million wmt by June 25, with Ni content at 40,200 mt. Stocks at seven major ports also increased. Despite high domestic demand, some ports unloaded slowly, limiting further sharp gains.

title: Copper Fox Announces 2021 Second Quarter Operating and Financial Results
summary: Copper Fox reports its Q2 2021 operating and financial results, including updates for several copper projects in Arizona and British Columbia. It notes a Van Dyke PEA, a Schaft Creek drilling program, permitting progress, and an Eaglehead project transaction. The news is project-focused and not a direct supply shock.

title: FRES Headlines - Strategic Minerals announces update to Leigh Creek Copper Mine
summary: Strategic Minerals said its Leigh Creek Copper Mine received notification from South Australia’s Department of Energy and Mining. While this is directly tied to copper mine operations or approvals and could influence near-term supply expectations, the provided text contains no clear production, ramp-up, or shutdown details.

title: Vale Indonesia and partners to build nickel processing facility
summary: Vale Indonesia, Baowu (TISCO) and Xinhai will build and operate the Bahodopi nickel processing facility in Morowali, Central Sulawesi, with eight kiln-electric furnace lines targeting 73,000 mt/year of nickel production. The JV uses gas-fired power instead of coal, aligning with Indonesia’s local processing push after export bans.

title: Cause of fire at the center of SC aluminum maker's $100M insurance fight
summary: A fire at JW Aluminum’s plant caused over $100 million in damages and disrupted production, delaying an expansion phase. The case centers on insurers disputing whether the loss is capped under a ‘molten material’ clause ($10 million) versus broader fire coverage. Fire is the direct trigger, but market-scale impact is unclear.

title: Energy Insider: Chinese SOE profits up 170% in first five months; Baowu and Vale launch Indonesia nickel project
summary: China Baowu and Vale plan to launch Indonesia’s Bahodopi FeNi project in Morowali, targeting 73,000 tons of nickel production annually. The agreement covers joint ventures and FeNi smelting powered by natural gas-fired electricity to cut emissions. The supply outlook can support near-term nickel sentiment.

title: ​​​​​​​Commerce Solidifies Duties On Copper Pipe From Vietnam
summary: The piece reports that U.S. trade authorities have solidified duties on copper pipe imports from Vietnam. Such tariffs typically reduce competitive import supply and can tighten near-term availability for copper pipe buyers, improving outlook for copper-linked demand and supportive price pressure over coming days to weeks.

title: Five Questions with Sarasota manufacturer Mullet's Aluminum Products
summary: Mullet’s Aluminum Products says demand for windows, doors, metal roofing, and aluminum railing has been strong, helped by remote work and earlier condominium/HOA projects. It warns that material costs are rising rapidly and supplier lead times have stretched to months, prompting customers to buy sooner.

title: Copper eases as dollar firms on U.S. inflation fears
summary: Copper fell as the dollar firmed on U.S. inflation fears, raising expectations for sooner Federal Reserve tightening. LME three-month copper dropped 0.6% and SHFE copper slid 0.9%. The piece also reports LME nickel and aluminium declining on the same broader dollar/risk backdrop.

title: London copper drops to US$9,354.50 a ton
summary: The news headline states that London copper has fallen to US$9,354.50 per ton. The accompanying market wrap mentions broader risk sentiment and trade-related concerns, but the key actionable detail is the reported decline in copper prices, implying bearish near-term price pressure.

title: Copper edges higher as dollar gives up gains; U.S. bill in focus
summary: Copper rose slightly after a softer dollar reduced support for the greenback. Traders also awaited U.S. employment data and progress on an infrastructure bill. Separately, LME nickel fell and aluminium slipped, while Shanghai’s aluminium edged higher, indicating mixed short-term pressure across base metals.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 28/06: LME base metals prices hold on to Friday levels; aluminium stocks continue to fall
summary: A live futures report says LME base metals prices are holding around Friday levels, while aluminium stocks continue to decline. It also references Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin publication corrections and methodology updates. The key market signal is persistent aluminium inventory drawdowns, usually supportive for short-term aluminium prices.

title: Singapore files 13 more charges in massive nickel trading fraud
summary: Singapore prosecutors filed 13 additional charges over an alleged scheme that raised over S$1 billion by promoting non-existent forward nickel contracts. Prosecutors say investors were cheated and at least S$201.2 million misappropriated from EGT’s DBS account. The case may raise nickel trading counterparty concerns but lacks confirmed physical market disruption.

title: Russia's Nornickel sees impact of new export duties at $0.5 bln - RIA
summary: RIA reports Nornickel expects about $0.5 billion impact from new Russian export duties. Russia introduced temporary export taxes on steel products plus nickel, aluminum and copper, costing producers $2.3 billion between Aug. 1 and Dec. 31. The added costs may reduce exports and weigh on prices.

title: China's National Carbon Trading Market to Include Cement, Aluminum Next Year, Expert Predicts
summary: China’s national carbon trading market is expected to expand beyond the power sector. An expert says cement and electrolytic aluminum will be included next year, with the ETS running by end-June and covering more sectors during the 14th Five-Year Plan. The policy expansion could increase compliance costs for aluminum producers.

title: Dale Corman To Retire as Executive Chairman of Western Copper and Gold
summary: Western Copper and Gold announces executive chairman Dale Corman’s retirement and interim leadership changes. The company also reiterates its Casino Project is expected to become a premier copper-gold mine. However, no specific near-term operational or supply changes are disclosed, limiting immediate price impact.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Commences 10,000 Meter Drill Program at the Kenbridge Nickel Deposit and on the Kenbridge North Target
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. mobilized two rigs for a 10,000-meter drill program at its Kenbridge nickel project in Ontario, targeting additional nickel sulphide mineralization and a separate EM conductor at Kenbridge North. The release cites high-grade nickel and associated copper results, but no near-term production change or disruption.

title: Freeport to Acquire Yandera Copper Project
summary: Freeport Resources signed an agreement to acquire Carpo, which controls the Yandera Copper Project in Papua New Guinea. The project is described as a copper porphyry system with historical resource and reserve estimates. The transaction is pending TSX Venture approval, and no immediate development or production changes are indicated.

title: US DOJ backs land swap deal for Rio Tinto's Arizona copper project
summary: The US DOJ is supporting a land swap needed for Rio Tinto’s Resolution Copper project in Arizona, despite opposition from native tribes. The agreement would transfer land to the government in exchange for national forest where the mine would be built. The project is expected to supply a sizable share of US copper demand.

title: Low inventories to give strong support to aluminium prices _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME aluminium rising over the prior week, attributing gains to continued declines in social aluminium inventories and slower production resumption in Yunnan, with new projects in several provinces delayed. A planned SRB release of 50,000 mt may pressure spot premiums, but low inventory should keep aluminium supported.

title: Nickel prices to hover at high levels_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports easing inflation panic after Powell’s dovish tone and cites strong nickel fundamentals. SHFE nickel backwardation widened as bullish raised positions amid low inventories and limited warrants. LME nickel also shifted to backwardation on expectations of higher Russian export tariffs, supporting prices. With SHFE near-month positions falling, nickel should still trade at high levels.

title: Aluminium rises as Russia's new export tax fuels supply concerns
summary: London aluminium prices rose 1.4% as Russia announced new export taxes affecting aluminium supply, on top of existing production curbs in China’s Yunnan province. US licensing requirements to import aluminium also supported demand. The report notes export taxes for nickel and copper too, with other metals weaker on a firmer dollar.

title: Rusal gives start to environmental upgrade of aluminum smelter
summary: Rusal has started the first phase of an environmental upgrade at its Novokuznetsk aluminum smelter in Kuzbass. The project includes a new electrolysis facility using Russian technologies and targets major emission cuts: fluorine down tenfold, sulfur dioxide halved, and benzopyrene to zero.

title: Ball Corporation Announces New Sustainability Goals, Shares Vision to Achieve a Circular Economy for Aluminum Beverage Packaging
summary: Ball Corporation announced 2030 sustainability goals aimed at a circular aluminum beverage packaging system, including higher recycled content and increased recycling rates, plus investments in low-carbon roadmaps and recycling infrastructure. It highlights that recycled aluminum uses far less energy than virgin. The release is more directional than immediate for aluminum prices.

title: Yangshan copper premiums rebounded_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Yangshan copper premiums for July rebounded, supported by an improved SHFE/LME copper ratio that boosted import demand. Trades picked up, with low cancelled warrants and LME contango around $30/mt. However, higher quotes for late-June/early-July cargoes and some late-week softening could limit further gains.

title: Copper prices to fluctuate in narrow range this week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Powell’s inflation/employment optimism and steady ECB rates improved sentiment. With the dollar index fluctuating tightly, focus shifts to June PMI and US non-farm data. Supply factors (spot TCs unchanged, smelter maintenance, declining Shanghai inventories) support copper, but rising LME inventories and contract turnover keep prices rangebound.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 29/06: Tin and aluminium firm on supply bottlenecks, other prices mixed
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures report says tin and aluminium prices are not uniformly moving, but aluminium is “firm” on supply bottlenecks. It notes global aluminium supply conditions remained technically intact while output in parts of the Gulf was curtailed, inventories were repositioned, and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted.

title: Canada Nickel Makes Significant Discovery at Nesbitt and Announces Additional Results on Regional Properties
summary: Canada Nickel reports a significant discovery at the Nesbitt project and provides additional results from regional properties. Exploration success can improve expectations for future nickel supply development. That outlook may reduce near-term nickel price pressure as markets factor in potential additional supply beyond current balances.

title: FPX Nickel Commences Drilling Programs at Decar Nickel District in Central British Columbia
summary: FPX Nickel says it has started drilling programs at its Decar Nickel District in central British Columbia. The announcement is directly related to nickel exploration progress and potential future resource development, but it is unlikely to materially change near-term nickel fundamentals within days to a few weeks.

title: CanAlaska Uranium Ltd.: CanAlaska Provides Update on Manitoba Nickel Projects
summary: CanAlaska provided an update on staged option arrangements, government-funded airborne magnetic surveys, and renewed permitting for nickel projects in Manitoba’s Thompson Nickel Belt. It also resumed control of Hunter/Strong projects after terminating an option deal. The release is focused on exploration progress, not production or supply changes.

title: Copper prices fall for fourth day on stronger dollar
summary: Copper fell for a fourth straight session on a stronger dollar, driven by rising COVID-19 cases and concerns about slower economic recovery, alongside plentiful-supply signals (contango and still-high LME inventories). It also cites Russia preparing export taxes for copper, nickel and aluminium, while aluminium rises on supply concerns.

title: CanAlaska Provides Update on Manitoba Nickel | The Kingston Whig Standard
summary: CanAlaska provided updates on its Manitoba nickel exploration portfolio, including a staged option agreement for the Manibridge project, completion of magnetic surveys funded via Manitoba’s mineral development fund, and resumption of control of Hunter/Strong after terminating an option deal. The news is exploration-focused without immediate production impacts.

title: CanAlaska Provides Update on Manitoba Nickel Projects
summary: CanAlaska provided updates on Manitoba nickel exploration projects, including a staged earn-in option for its Manibridge project, completion of funded airborne magnetic surveys at Resting Lake and Halfway Lake, and resumption of control after terminating the Hunter/Strong option. The company highlights drilling readiness following permit approvals.

title: China First Heavy Industries Gains by Limit on Plan to Buy Indonesian Ferronickel Assets
summary: China First Heavy Industries plans to buy a 23% stake in an Indonesian ferronickel producer, acquiring exposure to Delong Nickel Indonesia’s laterite refining and ferronickel exports to China. The deal is expected to boost CFHI profits and increase secured ferronickel supply feeding stainless steel and battery-related demand.

title: Copper producer Aurubis installing largest solar power plant in Bulgaria for own needs
summary: Aurubis is installing a 10 MW solar PV plant near its Bulgarian copper production site to supply some of its own electricity, covering about 2.5% of consumption (up to 12% at peak hours). The project, built on a recultivated landfill, supports the company’s carbon-neutral goal and aims to cut CO2 emissions.

title: ATOZ reached agreement over TCs for long-term contract of copper concentrate with Chinese mainstream copper smelters_SMM
summary: Antofagasta and Chinese mainstream copper smelters reached an agreement after four rounds of talks on treatment charges (TCs) for long-term copper concentrate contracts for H1 2022. The negotiated TC terms can affect smelting margins and concentrate supply expectations, potentially supporting short-term copper price sentiment.

title: Copper Industry News Roundup_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM’s copper news roundup says Glencore intends to restart the Mutanda copper project in Congo before year-end after two years of idleness. It also cites ICSG preliminary data: Q1 global copper mine output rose 3.7% and concentrate output increased 5.5%, while SX-EW fell 3.5%.

title: Copper set for weakest quarterly gain since March 2020 on China curbs
summary: Copper is set for its weakest quarterly gain since March 2020 amid China’s efforts to cool a red-hot metals rally and a firmer US dollar. China released state reserves including copper and aluminium, weighing prices. The piece also flags aluminium supply pressures and a tight nickel market, but copper sentiment remains bearish.

title: Hannan Metals Ltd.: Hannan Commences Groundbreaking 2,782 Line Kilometre Lidar Survey Over the San Martin Jogmec JV Copper-Silver Project in Peru
summary: Hannan Metals reports it has started a large airborne LiDAR survey over its San Martin JOGMEC JV sediment-hosted copper-silver project in Peru, aiming to improve geological mapping, drill targeting, and planning. The work is pre-production exploration and does not signal near-term copper supply or demand changes.

title: Torq Resources Inc.: Torq Obtains Drill Permit for the Margarita Iron-Oxide-Copper-Gold Project in Northern Chile
summary: Torq Resources announced it received an environmental permit for its Margarita iron-oxide-copper-gold project in northern Chile, allowing drilling across multiple platforms and targeting copper sulphide beneath known oxide mineralization. The first drill program is expected in Q3 after IP and geochemical surveys, with results anticipated in coming weeks.

title: Vale strike at Canadian mine strains battery nickel supply
summary: The headline reports that a Vale strike at a Canadian mine is straining battery nickel supply. Reduced production during the stoppage can tighten near-term supply of battery-grade material, typically supporting nickel prices in the following days and weeks as buyers anticipate shortages.

title: Vale to invest $121m to extend life of Manitoba nickel mines
summary: Vale plans to invest $121m to extend the life of its Manitoba nickel mines by 10 years and fund phase one of expansion at the Thompson Mine. The work includes ventilation, backfill capacity, and power upgrades targeting a 30% increase in production capacity, alongside exploration drilling.

title: Metallum Resources provides update on drilling at its Superior Zinc and Copper Project, Ontario; announces proposed $302,500 flow-through financing
summary: Metallum Resources reports Phase 1 drilling completion (2,100m) at its Superior zinc-copper VMS project in Ontario, with core logging ongoing and initial assay results expected in 2-4 weeks. The company also announces flow-through financing to fund exploration. No copper assay or market-moving developments are provided.

title: Missouri Cobalt Nears Completion Of Key Facility, Advancing Its Leadership Goal In Domestic Battery-Grade Cobalt And Nickel
summary: Missouri Cobalt says it is nearing completion of a new hydrometallurgical facility that will enable large-scale production of battery-grade cobalt and nickel, quadrupling run-rate volumes. It also cites ongoing concentrate production and potential copper output from its Missouri assets, which could improve near-term supply expectations.

title: Antofagasta reached agreement over TCs for long-term contract of copper concentrate with Chinese mainstream copper smelters_SMM
summary: Antofagasta agreed after four negotiation rounds with major Chinese copper smelters on treatment charges (TCs) for long-term copper concentrate contracts for H1 2022. The deal affects smelter concentrate economics, but the article does not indicate a clear bullish or bearish impulse for copper prices in the near term.

title: LIVE FUTURES 01/07: Aluminium premium futures firm on Russia news, flat price futures lightly traded
summary: The live futures update says aluminium premium futures were firm on Russia news, while broader price futures were flat and lightly traded. It also details Fastmarkets corrections and delayed publication of certain aluminium differential and billet premium assessments due to procedural errors, with database updates completed.

title: South Korea's PPS awards 12,000 tonnes of aluminium in June
summary: The article notes South Korea’s PPS awards 12,000 tonnes of aluminium for June and includes additional Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin methodology and assessment-update information. While tenders can influence short-term aluminium demand sentiment, no explicit price or spread change is described, making the net impact on prices uncertain.

title: Primary aluminium inventories increased 2,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s social aluminium inventories rose by 2,000 mt on the week to 876,000 mt as of July 1. Stocks fell in Wuxi and Hainan, but increased in South China Sea regions due to higher arrivals and reduced outbound shipments, indicating near-term inventory build-up.

title: Aluminium billet inventories up 14,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium billet outbound volumes rose to 51,100 mt, while inventories in five major consumption areas increased to 111,200 mt (+14.35%). Transportation restrictions eased and restocking improved slightly, but SMM expects downstream orders to decline in July. National reserve release next week may loosen spot liquidity, pressuring sales and likely raising inventories.

title: Metso Outotec delivers grinding package for NALCO alumina refinery in India - Chemical Engineering
summary: Metso Outotec won an engineering and delivery contract for a bauxite grinding package for NALCO’s Damanjodi alumina refinery expansion in Odisha, India. The scope includes basic design, ball mills and related equipment for a new stream. The project is booked in Q2/2021 orders, with no immediate disruption signals mentioned.

title: Rio Tinto studies using hydrogen to make greener alumina
summary: Rio Tinto is funding a study to test hydrogen as a feedstock to replace natural gas in alumina calcination, aiming to cut refining emissions. Work includes lab-scale reactor simulations and preliminary engineering at its Yarwun refinery. The project could support “green aluminium,” but it’s not an immediate production shift.

title: EPA Delays Lead and Copper Rule Revision Again More Changes Likely
summary: The EPA delayed revisions to the Lead and Copper Rule, pushing the effective date to Dec. 16 from June. Water systems get more time to plan compliance, including monitoring lead levels and potentially adding corrosion-control chemicals. The 15 ppb lead-service-line replacement trigger remains.

title: Copper eyes weekly decline as firmer dollar, weak China demand weigh
summary: Copper is set for a weekly decline as a firmer U.S. dollar and weakening demand in China (a top consumer) weigh on prices. LME and Shanghai copper contracts fell. The piece notes related price weakness in other metals and cites pressure from slower destocking.

title: Castillo Copper to commence geophysical campaign across Zambia projects
summary: Castillo Copper Limited will begin induced polarization (IP) geophysical surveys over its Luanshya and Mkushi projects in Zambia’s copper-belt. The IP work follows prior soil sampling that outlined copper-related anomalies and is intended to prioritize drill targets. The update supports exploration advancement but not immediate supply.

title: Chile's Antofagasta inks copper ore supply deals with China smelters, sources say
summary: Chile’s Antofagasta signed contracts to supply copper concentrate to Chinese smelters covering at least half of next year. Deals were struck amid a tight concentrate market, with TC/RCs around mid-$50s per tonne versus a $60 level a year ago and a spot TC floor at $55.

title: High Grade Copper & Silver Results from Three New Projects in Morocco
summary: Altus Strategies reports high-grade copper (up to 8.37% Cu and 3.41% Cu with associated silver) from initial prospecting at three newly granted projects in Morocco’s western Anti-Atlas. Results include copper-bearing breccia and sediment-hosted occurrences; exploration is ongoing with follow-up sampling planned.

title: Global High Purity Alumina Market Overview 2021 with Company Profiles of 16 Major Players & Industry Guide with Contact details for 77 Companies
summary: PRNewswire promotes a ResearchAndMarkets report on the global high purity alumina (HPA) market, used in LEDs and lithium-ion batteries. It cites growth projections, regional demand shares, and company/capacity developments in alumina processing. However, it provides no specific aluminium metal pricing or immediate supply shocks.

title: Chile's May copper production up 5.8% yr/yr in May – Cochilco
summary: Chile’s state copper commission Cochilco said Codelco’s May copper production rose 5.8% year-on-year to 152,500 tonnes. Output fell at the Collahuasi mine (-3.7% to 57,900 tonnes) and at BHP’s Escondida (-9.2% to 84,800 tonnes).

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 02/07: Aluminium, copper edge up while market awaits cues from data releases
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures report says aluminium and copper prices are “edging up” as traders await cues from upcoming data releases. It also notes procedural corrections to some aluminium differential and premium assessments. The piece does not mention nickel.

title: LIVE FUTURES REPORT 02/07: Aluminium, copper edge up while market awaits cues from data releases
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures report says aluminium and copper prices edged up as the market awaited cues from upcoming data releases. It also mentions procedural delays/corrections to certain aluminium differential and billet premium assessments, but these were publishing errors rather than changes in underlying supply-demand fundamentals.

title: Three reasons why a Carbon Border Adjustment Measure will not work for aluminium
summary: The piece argues Europe’s planned carbon border adjustment measure cannot adequately protect aluminium producers from carbon leakage, especially due to indirect electricity-related costs under the ETS and likely circumvention/source-shifting. It warns CBAM could raise costs and remove regulatory certainty for EU producers until at least 2030.

title: Antofagasta : Copper prices climb as U.S. job data boosts demand prospects
summary: Reuters reports copper prices rose after U.S. job data showed faster hiring, improving demand expectations for metals tied to the economic recovery. It cites higher LME/SHFE copper prices, declining LME/SHFE copper stocks, and simultaneous gains in ShFE aluminium and nickel amid mixed inventory signals in China.

title: Copper prices climb as U.S. job data boosts demand prospects
summary: Copper prices rose on Monday after U.S. job data signaled faster hiring and easing labor shortages, improving demand prospects for metals used in durable goods. LME three-month copper and SHFE August copper both gained. The story also cites advances in SHFE aluminium and nickel alongside the copper rally.

title: Fundamentals shaky, but funds fuel copper's rise to 2-week peak
summary: Copper prices climbed 1.3% to a two-week high as the dollar’s uptrend stalled and funds bought, though China’s slowing growth, building inventories, and rising mine supply capped gains. Aluminium rose slightly. Nickel premiums for cash over the three-month contract reflected tight stocks and disruption factors.

title: When Will Copper Go Up? | Supply and Demand Dynamics
summary: The piece argues copper can still rise, citing mine disruptions that tightened supply and keep the market in deficit through 2026, including Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula outages. It also discusses tariff-related uncertainty and demand drivers from electrification and AI, supporting bullish copper price expectations.

title: SHFE aluminium fell amid increased social inventory, while LME aluminium rose on Russian tariffs _SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium declined after off-season demand and transportation restrictions lifted social inventories, with the 2108 contract ending the week slightly lower. In contrast, LME aluminium rose on Russia’s decision to impose additional tariffs on aluminium products. The report expects SHFE to range 18,400–19,000 yuan/mt and LME 2,480–2,550.

title: Copper rises to 3-week high on fund buying; Fed minutes eyed
summary: Copper prices rose to a three-week high as fund buying gained momentum after a softer-than-expected China stocks release and strong U.S. jobs data boosted demand expectations. LME three-month copper and Shanghai August contracts climbed. China is also set to auction 20,000 tonnes of copper, adding support ahead of Fed minutes.

title: London copper rises to US$9,546 a ton
summary: London copper is reported to have risen to US$9,546 per ton. The accompanying snippets reference broader market factors but do not provide specific supply-demand developments for nickel or aluminium. Overall, the only clear immediate signal is an increase in copper prices, consistent with bullish short-term momentum.

title: US non-farm data to give directional guidance to copper prices_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says SHFE copper prices traded in a tight range around 68,300 yuan/mt. US dollar strength and upcoming Fed inflation/employment data, plus this week’s China/Europe/US PMIs, may guide direction. Fundamentals are mixed: maintenance ends and imports are weak, while downstream buyers stay cautious and low season pressures prices.

title: Nickel prices to fluctuate in wide range, stainless steel contract prices to have limited downside room_SMM
summary: SMM says upbeat US non-farm payrolls strengthened the dollar and pushed nickel lower, though prices rebounded toward 136,000 yuan/mt. It expects nickel to trade in a wide range this week, with limited upside due to shifting international macro policy expectations and tighter domestic regulation. Stainless steel contracts are seen rangebound.

title: NPI trades weakened, weekly average discount of high-grade NPI shrank to 140.7 yuan/mtu against refined nickel_SMM
summary: SMM reports NPI prices in China and Indonesia rose versus last week, while the discount of high-grade NPI to refined nickel narrowed to 140.7 yuan/mtu. NPI sentiment improved on expectations of tight supply and a sharp rise in nickel ore, though higher costs may pressure short-term profits.

title: MUX Creates McEwen Copper Which Announces $80 Million Series B Private Placement to Advance the Los Azules Copper Project
summary: McEwen Mining’s subsidiary, McEwen Copper, announced an $80 million private placement to fund pre-feasibility, road access, exploration drilling, permitting and corporate purposes for the Los Azules copper project in Argentina. This is a project-financing step to advance development; it is not an immediate macro supply shock.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces Positive IP Results for Mineral Mountain Copper Project
summary: Copper Fox announced positive induced polarization results outlining a large chargeability and resistivity anomaly correlated with copper-molybdenum mineralization at its Mineral Mountain project in Arizona. Management says the data supports planning diamond drilling targets. The news is exploration-stage and does not affect near-term supply.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jul 6): Shanghai nonferrous metals rose for the most parts, aluminium fell 0.65%_SMM
summary: After an OPEC+ production increase deadlock, oil prices jumped on expectations of tighter supply, lifting most SHFE nonferrous contracts. Copper and nickel rose (copper +1.85%, nickel +1.2%). Aluminium fell about 0.65%, with bulls’ open interest declining and attention on macro-driven price moves.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Announces First Assays for Newly Discovered Pool of Massive Nickel-Copper Mineralization: 13.92 Meters (45.5 Feet) Grading 5.54% Ni, 2.14% Cu (6.70% NiEq)
summary: Talon Metals reported first assays from drill hole 21TK0313 in the Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project’s CGO West area, intersecting thick nickel-copper sulphide mineralization (up to 5.54% Ni and 2.14% Cu over 13.92 m). Management says the mineralization pool is high-grade and remains open.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Announces First Assays for Newly Discovered Pool of Massive Nickel-Copper Mineralization: 13.92 Meters (45.5 Feet) Grading 5.54% Ni, 2.14% Cu (6.70% NiEq)
summary: Talon Metals reported first assay results from drill hole 21TK0313 at its Tamarack nickel-copper project, intersecting thick mineralization grading 5.54% Ni and 2.14% Cu over 13.92 meters in the CGO West area. Drilling remains ongoing to define the extent of the new sulphide pool.

title: Pan Global Resources Inc.: Pan Global Drills Further Wide Copper-Tin Intercepts with High Grades from near Surface at Escacena Project, Southern Spain
summary: Pan Global Resources reports additional near-surface high-grade copper (including copper-tin equivalent) drill intercepts at the La Romana discovery in Spain, with mineralization extended along strike and open in multiple directions. While supportive for longer-term copper project potential, the release has no direct aluminium-related market impact.

title: CAVU Mining Corp.: CAVU Mobilizes Drilling Team to Hopper Copper-Gold Project in Yukon
summary: CAVU Mining announced mobilization of a 1,500m diamond drilling program at its road-accessible Hopper copper-gold project in Yukon, targeting skarn and porphyry anomalies. The news outlines drill collars and geological context but does not indicate production changes or supply disruptions, limiting immediate price impact on copper.

title: Russia levies export duty on aluminium [corrected] | American Metal Market
summary: American Metal Market reports that Russia has levied an export duty on aluminium. The measure is expected to reduce Russian aluminium exports and affect supply flows, adding downward pressure to price expectations for aluminium in the near term as market participants re-price availability and trade economics.

title: Copper wire stolen near Carrickmacross
summary: Gardaí are investigating three incidents of theft of Eir copper wire from telephone poles near Carrickmacross between June 26 and July 1. The report cites prior local copper-cabling thefts in 2019, 2018 and 2017, including damage and losses, but no material production or market-wide impact is described.

title: Camino Geophysics Survey Targets Known High-grade Copper and Gold Mineralization at the Northern Extension of Los Chapitos
summary: Camino announced the start of a 257.8 line km magnetic geophysics survey at its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, targeting high-grade copper zones near known artisanal workings. Results due in July will guide drilling starting August to test the northern extension and subsurface continuity of mineralization.

title: Talon Metals Announces First Assays for Newly Discovered Pool of Massive Nickel-Copper Mineralization: 13.92 Meters Grading 5.54% Ni, 2.14% Cu
summary: Talon Metals reports initial drill-hole assays from the CGO West area of the Tamarack nickel-copper project in Minnesota, including 13.92 m grading 5.54% nickel and 2.14% copper, with follow-up holes also intersecting mineralization. The company says the massive sulphide pool remains open for expansion, suggesting upside to resources.

title: Pan Global Drills Further Wide Copper-Tin Intercepts with High Grades from near Surface at Escacena Project, Southern Spain
summary: Pan Global Resources reported additional Phase 4 drilling results at its La Romana copper target in Spain, including multiple wide, near-surface high-grade intercepts and further extension of strike length to ~800m, with remaining potential to expand. Results are supportive of longer-term copper resource growth sentiment.

title: Talon Metals Announces First Assays for Newly Discovered Pool of Massive Nickel-Copper Mineralization: 13.92 Meters Grading 5.54% Ni, 2.14% Cu
summary: Talon Metals reported first assays from a newly discovered zone at the Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in Minnesota. Drill hole 21TK0313 returned 13.92 meters grading 5.54% nickel and 2.14% copper, with additional intersections nearby. Mineralization remains open for expansion as drilling continues.

title: Copper industry news roundup_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Zijin Mining expects much higher first-half 2021 profits, driven by higher output of gold, copper and zinc. It cites commissioning of the Kamoa-Kakura copper mine and further ramp-up at other copper projects, boosting near-term copper supply outlook. It also notes growth at a Finland cobalt-nickel-copper project.

title: Yangshan copper premiums continued to fall amid quiet trades_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Yangshan copper import premiums under warrants and bill of lading declined over early July, while trades stayed quiet due to pessimistic buyers and expectations of further premium falls. SHFE/LME ratio weakened and Shanghai bonded copper inventories rose for a fourth week, suggesting near-term copper price pressure.

title: Puma: Creation of a New Active Player for Copper Exploration and Development in New Brunswick, Canada
summary: Puma Exploration announced it will transfer its copper projects into a new entity (Melius Capital 3) to create a standalone copper exploration company in New Brunswick. The deal includes share and optional cash payments, with existing historical copper resources at the Chester project. It is exploration-focused with no production impact.

title: Tight supply pushes higher nickel ore prices, shipping rates unlikely to fall in short-term_SMM
summary: SMM says tight availability of 1.5% nickel ore pushed CIF prices to about $73.5/wmt, up $4.5/wmt week-on-week. Weather-related shipment delays and cargoes sold through early August tightened inventories at NPI plants, boosting production amid high profits. Freight remains elevated, reducing near-term downside risk.

title: London copper rebounds as dollar rally pauses
summary: London copper rose 0.6% as the dollar’s rally paused, easing pressure on dollar-priced metals, while investors awaited Fed minutes. China’s recycling push and state metal reserve auctions supported copper and aluminium sentiment. However, SHFE copper and aluminium declined, and nickel fell, indicating mixed near-term pricing pressure.

title: London copper prices rebound at US$9,370 a ton
summary: The news notes a rebound in London copper prices, lifting the metal to around US$9,370 per ton. While broader market drivers are not detailed in the excerpt, the reported price movement itself implies near-term support for copper rather than weakness.

title: US Copper Corp.: US Copper Corp Expands Drill Program
summary: US Copper Corp announced an expanded diamond drilling program at its Moonlight-Superior copper project in California, increasing the number of holes to 12–15 and advancing in-fill drilling to upgrade resources. The company cites full funding and aims to quantify silver and gold credits. No direct production or trade impact is stated.

title: McEwen creates subsidiary to advance Los Azules copper project
summary: McEwen Mining created McEwen Copper to fund Argentina’s Los Azules copper project, raising $80m via a private placement. Shares will support pre-feasibility work, access road construction, drilling, and permitting, aiming to avoid dilution of McEwen’s core equity. The news is copper-specific but unlikely to move near-term prices materially.

title: Malaysian blockade extension hampered secondary copper imports_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Malaysia extended its COVID lockdown indefinitely, delaying secondary copper (scrap) exports to China. Persistent port congestion across Hong Kong/Shenzhen/Guangdong and global shipping disruptions have destabilized schedules, tightened container supply, and raised freight costs. With domestic scrap supply already tight, the article cites higher weekly #1 bright copper and a contracting cathode–scrap spread.

title: Aluminium billet inventories rose 12,600 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data for China shows aluminium billet inventories in five major consumption areas rose 11% (+12,600 mt) to 123,800 mt by July 8, while outbound shipments fell. Downstream buyers were less willing to restock amid price fluctuations and weak consumption, with extrusion orders weakening, suggesting inventories may keep building next week.

title: Primary aluminium inventories shrank 18,000 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s primary aluminium ingot inventories fell by 18,000 mt from last Thursday to 858,000 mt as of July 8. The drop was driven partly by continued declines in Wuxi. The reduction across major consumption areas and SHFE warrants suggests tighter short-term supply conditions.

title: China releases national reserves of copper, aluminum, zinc
summary: China’s reserves authority said it released 100,000 tonnes of copper and aluminium from national reserves to maintain market order and stabilize prices of bulk commodities. The action follows a State Council decision to ensure supply amid soaring raw material costs, with further releases expected to relieve enterprise pressure.

title: China releases national reserves of copper, aluminum, zinc
summary: China will release 100,000 tonnes each of copper and aluminium (and zinc) from national reserves to maintain market order. The action, authorized by the State Council, aims to ensure supply and stabilize prices amid soaring raw material costs, with additional releases expected to relieve enterprise pressure.

title: Sandfire secures licence for Motheo copper mine in Botswana
summary: Sandfire Resources received Botswana approval for the Motheo copper mine licence, the final permitting step before full-scale construction. Mining work is planned to start in early 2022 with first production early 2023. The company has ordered long-lead equipment and began construction of the process plant and infrastructure.

title: Iran opens 50,000-tonne copper cathodes project
summary: Iran inaugurated a new 50,000-tonne-per-year copper cathodes project using industrial-scale bioleaching at Shahr-e Babak (Kerman). The plant is intended to expand Iran’s copper cathode output and uses an alternative, “environment-friendly” extraction method. The announcement is a direct supply-capacity catalyst for copper.

title: Sandfire secures mining licence for Motheo Copper Mine
summary: Sandfire said Botswana has granted the final mining licence for its Motheo copper mine. Site works have started and, after the licence approval, the company will mobilise crews to begin full-scale construction of the process plant and infrastructure. Production is slated for early 2023, supported by long-lead equipment orders.

title: Copper piping worth R30m looted at Charlotte Maxeke hospital after fire
summary: Charlotte Maxeke hospital was looted after a fire, with copper piping worth R30m stolen. The loss left parts of the hospital without hot water as it reopens and clears a cancer-treatment backlog. Replacement efforts are underway, but stolen pipes add costs, creating a hurdle for the Gauteng health department.

title: Spruce Ridge Resources Limited: Spruce Ridge Reports Updated Mineral Resource Estimate at Great Burnt Copper Property
summary: Spruce Ridge reports an updated mineral resource estimate for its Great Burnt copper-gold property, showing higher indicated copper grade (2.66% to 3.21%) and increased contained copper. The company plans a Preliminary Economic Assessment and notes higher copper demand and a higher copper-price deck supporting the cut-off.

title: TNR Gold Corp.: TNR Gold Announces McEwen Copper $80 Million Private Placement to Advance the Los Azules Copper Project
summary: McEwen Copper plans a private placement of up to US$80 million to fund advancement of the Los Azules copper project in Argentina, including pre-feasibility, infrastructure access road, drilling, and permitting. TNR holds a royalty on the project. The news is supportive for copper development but not near-term supply.

title: Braveheart Resources Inc.: Braveheart Intersects Additional Copper Mineralization at Bull River Mine Project
summary: Braveheart Resources reported additional high-grade copper mineralization from its H1 2021 drilling at the Bull River Mine, including intersections up to 5.60% copper over 1.0 m. Management says results could expand resources and increase mine life, supporting forward copper supply expectations.

title: Universal Copper Ltd.: Universal Copper Closes Private Placement for $1,437,000
summary: Universal Copper Ltd. announced it closed a private placement totaling $1.437 million, including flow-through funds, to advance its Poplar copper exploration project and for working capital. The financing supports ongoing drilling/exploration plans but provides no immediate changes to supply, demand, or metal trade affecting short-term copper prices.

title: Rob McEwen: New Copper Venture, Gold Price Tipping Point
summary: Rob McEwen discusses forming McEwen Copper to house the Los Azules project and raising $80 million. He cites broker forecasts of upcoming copper deficits and expects demand growth from Asia, EVs, and regenerative energy. He also comments on inflation-driven gold strength.

title: Small-scale Chilean Miners Left Out Of Copper Price Bonanza
summary: AFP reports small-scale miners in northern Chile are not sharing in record copper prices despite higher sales proceeds. It notes Chile’s copper dominance and that Enami has reactivated many small operations. The piece also covers proposed higher taxes on resource extraction, which could affect future investment and output.

title: China releases national reserves of copper, aluminum, zinc--China Economic Net
summary: China’s National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration announced the release of 100,000 tonnes of copper and aluminium (and zinc) from national reserves to maintain market order and stabilize bulk commodity prices. Further releases are expected to ease enterprise pressure from rising raw material costs.

title: China releases national reserves of copper, aluminum, zinc--China Economic Net
summary: China’s National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration said it released 100,000 tonnes of copper and aluminium (plus zinc) from national reserves to maintain market order and stabilize bulk commodity prices. The authority expects further releases to ease enterprises’ pressure from rising raw material costs.

title: London copper rises as dollar retreats; Shanghai copper slips
summary: Reuters reports London copper edged up after the U.S. dollar retreated, but gains were limited by worries that the Delta variant could derail global recovery and demand. Shanghai copper slipped slightly. Nickel rose sharply on inventory tightness, while LME aluminium also increased modestly.

title: Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose 4,200 mt on week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said Shanghai bonded copper stocks rose for the fifth straight week, up 4,200 mt to 439,800 mt as of July 9, driven by larger inbound arrivals. Limited terms-of-trade repair, weak customs-declaration demand, and about 300 yuan/mt import loss kept buyers cautious, allowing inventories to build.

title: Fort St. James Nickel Corp.: Fort St. James Closes Financing
summary: Fort St. James Nickel Corp. announced it has closed a private placement totaling $370,400, with proceeds allocated to general working capital and exploration at its property in New Brunswick. The release contains standard warrant terms and does not indicate any immediate production, supply, or trading impacts for nickel markets.

title: Nickel hits four-month high; strike in Sudbury continues
summary: LME nickel jumped 2.2% to a four-month high as investors turned more bullish and nickel inventories fell to their lowest since last year. The move is also linked to a continuing Sudbury labor strike that keeps Vale’s and Glencore’s major nickel operations idle. Citi raised its near-term forecast.

title: Small-scale miners left out of Chile's copper bonanza
summary: The piece says small-scale copper miners in Chile are not sharing in record copper prices. It highlights that Chile may raise extraction-related sales taxes to 70%, and officials warn investment and production could fall. Since Chile is the top global copper supplier, the policy risk is likely bearish for copper sentiment.

title: EV Laggard Australia Supplies Tesla's Lithium & Nickel: Ironic?
summary: Australia, an EV-policy laggard, supplies substantial battery materials: roughly three quarters of lithium and one third of nickel used in Tesla EVs. Tesla-linked investment and incentives for refining are framed as a growing opportunity, implying firmer EV-driven demand expectations for nickel, even though no immediate supply shock is cited.

title: Copper News Roundup_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports a Shandong copper smelter suffered equipment failure over the weekend, with repairs expected to take at least a month. The disruption is estimated to lift spot copper concentrate treatment charges and drive a continuous decline in domestic refined copper inventories. Separately, the commissioning of Daye Nonferrous’ large cleaner project is delayed.

title: Panoramic starts underground mining at Australian nickel project
summary: Panoramic Resources has begun underground development and ore production at its Savannah nickel project in Western Australia ahead of schedule. Mining contractor Barminco is now producing ore, with first concentrate shipment planned for later this year. The mine targets annual output of nickel and copper in concentrate under an offtake deal.

title: London copper eases on doubt over Chinese rebound
summary: London copper fell 0.8% after China’s reserve-cutting steps to support growth raised doubts about a V-shaped rebound, the world’s top metals consumer. The prior Friday rally faded Monday. The piece also notes LME nickel easing and mixed aluminium moves across exchanges, indicating broadly softer sentiment.

title: Cameroon: ALUCAM exposes the aluminium market to speculation with an 8% price increase
summary: Cameroon’s ALUCAM raised prices effective July 12, 2021, by about 8%, citing a 52.5%+ increase in international alumina costs and higher transport expenses from COVID supply-chain disruptions. The firm’s move is expected to lift roofing sheets and utensil retail/wholesale prices, reflecting cost pressure on aluminium production.

title: Copperstone's exploitation concession Viscaria k no. 7 confirmed by the Swedish Government
summary: Swedish authorities confirmed Copperstone’s exploitation concession for Viscaria k no. 7. The approval supports continued development of the Viscaria project, improving expectations for future copper supply availability. In the coming days, this typically provides modest bullish sentiment for copper as supply prospects become clearer.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Further Progress With Underground
summary: Nevada Copper reported continued progress ramping up its Pumpkin Hollow underground mine and processing plant, including completion of underground ventilation commissioning and successful process plant testing. It expects a dike crossing to be completed within two weeks, which should increase development rates and support higher copper production toward steady state.

title: Lower social inventory to offer solid support to aluminium prices, eyes on macro front in the short term _SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium trading steadied after a brief rise, with SHFE and LME prices pressured by hawkish Fed comments. West Inner Mongolia’s renewed power curtailment had limited plant impact, while ingot inventories are expected to decline slowly. PBoC’s planned RRR cut may boost liquidity, keeping prices relatively firm this week.

title: Copper prices to remain in downward trend this week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says copper prices are likely to remain in a downward trend. China’s liquidity easing boosted sentiment, but expectations of Fed tightening and stronger USD cap upside. Fundamentals include lower inventories from dip buying, yet smelters’ scrap supply, recovered TC and expected output point to oversupply and inventory rebuilding.

title: Copper rises as positive China data boosts demand outlook
summary: Copper gained as stronger-than-expected Chinese trade data improved the near-term demand outlook. Imports and exports beat expectations, supporting sentiment even though physical demand was tepid due to record-high prices and weaker downstream margins. LME aluminum and nickel also rose, suggesting spillover strength from the China macro news.

title: Vedanta Aluminium Business recycles 16.5 bn litres of water in FY21
summary: Vedanta Aluminium Business says it recycled 16.5 billion litres of water in FY20-21, saving about 700 million litres via projects across its alumina refinery, aluminium smelters and power plants. It cites SCADA monitoring, enhanced ETP/UF/RO and zero-discharge efforts, plus rainwater harvesting and community water programs.

title: Scarce available nickel ore kept quotes at high levels, shipping rates unlikely to fall in short-term_SMM
summary: SMM says nickel ore CIF quotes stayed high and stable, with mainstream traded prices around $72–75/wmt and some deals at $76/wmt. Tight supply and high demand keep prices elevated despite slowing NPI-profit momentum. Shipping delays and resilient freight rates from the Philippines to China also limit declines, supporting nickel prices.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Begins Airborne Survey at the Cannon Copper Project, Ontario
summary: ALX Resources began a helicopter-borne VTEM Max airborne electromagnetic survey over its 100%-owned Cannon Copper Project in Ontario, which includes the historic Cannon (Crownbridge) copper mine. The program will generate new geophysical targets for prospecting and potential future diamond drilling, with no immediate production changes.

title: Copper eases as U.S. inflation data stokes policy tightening fears
summary: Copper fell after U.S. inflation data triggered fears of faster Fed tightening, strengthening the dollar and making USD-priced metals less attractive. The article also notes concurrent declines in LME aluminium and nickel, indicating broader macro-driven downside pressure across industrial metals markets.

title: Saudi Ma'aden signs deal for calcined petroleum coke for aluminium plant
summary: Ma'aden Aluminium Company signed a five-year deal to buy 100,000 tonnes/year of calcined petroleum coke for its Ras Al Khair aluminium smelter. The contract supports output from commercial production expected end-2024 and forms part of Ma’aden’s plan to source more coke domestically, aligning with Saudi Vision 2030.

title: The performance of copper cathode rod operating rate remained poor in June_SMM
summary: SMM says copper cathode rod producers’ operating rate was 68.68% in June, sharply lower year on year, amid cautious downstream ordering as copper prices declined. Maintenance shutdowns, power curtailment in South China/Yunnan/Guizhou, and COVID-related transport restrictions reduced sales and output. July operating rate is expected to improve with steadier copper prices.

title: Bam Bam Resources Corp.: Bam Bam Resources' IP Survey Discovers New Zones at Majuba Hill Copper District
summary: Bam Bam Resources announced completion of a deep IP survey at its Majuba Hill copper district in Nevada, identifying a new “789 Zone” with enhanced sulfide/chargeability signatures and a drill intersection (MHB-8) containing 0.35% copper over 19.8 m, plus broader copper-silver intervals. Further drilling is planned.

title: Copper eases as dollar firms on U.S. inflation jitters
summary: Copper prices eased slightly as the U.S. dollar firmed following U.S. inflation data, which increased expectations for faster monetary tightening. The article notes copper’s reaction was mild and fundamentals were unchanged, while nickel fell and aluminum dropped on trading concerns, pointing to broad macro-driven downside.

title: Aluminium scrap prices fluctuate within a narrow range amid off-season and fewer imports _SMM
summary: Aluminium scrap price ranges in China narrowed in June, with weak supply and demand as the processing off-season began. Aluminium scrap imports fell sharply after stricter customs inspections. Scrap prices are expected to stay in a tight range in July, rising slower than primary aluminium.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Jul 13): Shanghai nonferrous metals closed mixed after surging US CPI in June, Aluminium gained 1.72%_SMM
summary: Shanghai SHFE nonferrous metals closed mixed after June US CPI hit a 30-year high, boosting expectations of Fed tightening and pressuring USD/debt conditions that weigh on copper. Aluminium rose 1.72%, nickel nearly unchanged, while copper fell 0.36%, keeping overall near-term impact mixed for the tracked metals.

title: Canada Nickel Expands New Nesbitt Nickel Discovery by 1.8 kilometres
summary: Canada Nickel announced results from its Nesbitt drill program, reporting that drill hole NES21-03 intersected 302 metres of nickel mineralization with visible disseminated sulphides, consistent with prior holes. Management highlights scale potential of a 3.7-kilometre target and notes potential higher-grade feed for its Crawford mill.

title: Rockridge Resources Ltd.: Rockridge Intersects Additional Copper Mineralization and Plans Upcoming Summer Exploration Program at the Knife Lake Copper Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Rockridge Resources announced assay results from 2,043 metres of drilling at its Knife Lake copper project in Saskatchewan, highlighting copper-bearing VMS mineralization at the Knife Lake and Gilbert targets. The company also plans a funded summer exploration program and notes continued progress in a rising copper price environment.

title: Phoenix Copper Limited Announces Empire Mine Deep Sulphide Drilling Programme
summary: Phoenix Copper Ltd. reported sulphide-rich mineralisation intercepted below the Empire Mine oxide pit during its Deep Sulphide drilling programme. The company plans 4,500m of core drilling in 2021 and has submitted a plan for permitting, targeting initial copper and zinc production for late 2022. Immediate supply effects are not indicated.

title: Eagle Plains Resources Ltd: Eagle Plains' Partner Rockridge Resources Intersects Additional Copper Mineralization and Plans Upcoming Summer Exploration Program at the Knife Lake Copper Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Eagle Plains announced Rockridge’s final drill assay results from Saskatchewan’s Knife Lake copper project, including anomalous copper intercepts and further follow-up exploration plans. It highlights VMS-style copper mineralization at targets beyond the main deposit and notes continued drilling later this year. Copper market sentiment could strengthen modestly.

title: Margaret Lake Diamonds Inc.: High-Grade Awaruite Obtained During Site Visit to Letain Along 1 km X 1.3 km Known Nickel-Cobalt Mineralization Zone
summary: Margaret Lake Diamonds reported high-grade awaruite from the Letain property and plans further SGS Davis Tube magnetic separation testing and assays for Ni, Co and related elements. The article discusses metallurgy work and potential future drilling permits, but provides no production or near-term supply changes to affect nickel prices directly.

title: Rockridge Intersects Additional Copper Mineralization and Plans Upcoming Summer Exploration Program at the Knife Lake Copper Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Rockridge Resources reported final assay results from a 2,043m diamond drilling program at its Knife Lake copper project in Saskatchewan and highlighted additional copper mineralization. The company also plans a permitted summer VTEM and follow-up drilling program. The release is primarily sentiment/expectations for copper, without near-term nickel or aluminium effects.

title: MEED | UAE aluminium firm brings expansion phase online
summary: The article headline reports that a UAE aluminium firm has brought an expansion phase online. If capacity ramps up as planned, it can increase near-term supply and reduce price pressure for aluminium. However, the piece provides no volume, timing, or commissioning details due to paywall access.

title: St. James Parish alumina smelter investor buys much bigger stake; gobbling up Jamaican mine
summary: Concord Resources became the majority owner of New Day Aluminum’s Noranda bauxite mine operations in Jamaica and the Noranda Alumina refinery in Louisiana, acquiring more interest from DADA. The deal supports plans for a nearly $1 billion rare-earth extraction facility using alumina residue, boosting confidence in regional alumina supply and processing continuity.

title: EU duties on aluminum import to result in price growth — Rusal
summary: Rusal told TASS that EU duties on aluminum imports will automatically lift average aluminum market prices in Europe, given the EU’s heavy reliance on primary aluminum imports (local supply covers about 25% of needs). The company expects the downstream processing sector to be most affected and competitiveness to change.

title: Travelling through deep time to find copper for a clean energy future
summary: The piece argues that net-zero commitments will drive sharply higher copper demand and warns—citing the IEA and Goldman—that supply could become increasingly strained. It describes new software and AI methods to identify likely copper-bearing subduction zones, potentially improving future discovery efforts.

title: Trading House Concord Buys Alumina Plant in Bet on U.S. Revival
summary: BNN Bloomberg’s headline says Trading House Concord bought an alumina plant as a bet on a U.S. revival. Because alumina is a key feedstock for primary aluminium production, the deal could imply improved upstream supply and tighter near-term expectations for aluminium.

title: ATEX Resources Inc.: ATEX Defines Opportunity to Extend Porphyry Mineralization Closer to Surface at Its Valeriano Copper Gold Project
summary: ATEX reports an updated geological interpretation at its Valeriano copper-gold project in Chile after relogging and mapping, suggesting copper-gold porphyry mineralization may extend closer to surface in a southwest area and expand targets for the next drill season. No production or timing is provided, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Horizonte Minerals PLC Announces Araguaia Nickel Project Operational Update
summary: Horizonte Minerals provides an operational update on its Araguaia nickel project in Brazil, citing progress on procurement tenders for key processing equipment and EPCM services, permits in place for construction, and senior debt credit committee approval expected in Q3 2021.
