summary: Udokan Copper says it has completed installation of a gyratory crusher at its coarse crushing plant for rougher ore from the Zapadniy open pit. The company is building a mining and metallurgical plant targeting copper cathodes and concentrate, with construction of conveyors and related infrastructure ongoing.

title: The Demand for Copper
summary: Interview with Nippon Denkai on copper market conditions. Demand for copper far exceeds current manufacturing, with copper foil supply tightening in Asia. Electronics recovery and rising lithium-ion battery/EV orders are straining capacity and driving allocations away from PCB use. Copper prices rose sharply earlier in 2021, later eased after China reserve releases.

title: Codelco Miners Vote to Strike as Copper Disruption Threats Mount
summary: Codelco miners have voted to strike as disruption threats mount, raising the risk of near-term copper supply interruptions from one of the world’s largest producers. Markets typically react quickly to strike risk, with reduced output expectations weighing on copper prices over the first days of any labor action.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventories Up to 117,600 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium billet stocks in major consumption areas rose 14,400 mt to 117,600 mt (+14%) on the week, while outbound shipments fell 4,900 mt to 41,200 mt amid quiet downstream purchasing. Downstream orders are sluggish and SMM expects demand to soften and supply to improve, with possible restocking next week.

title: Primary Aluminium Inventories Increased 7,000 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data showed China’s social aluminium inventories rose 7,000 mt on the week to 739,000 mt as of Aug 12. Shortage of arrivals eased in Wuxi and outbound volumes declined, while Hainan received more ingot from north-west regions. Rigid downstream demand continued despite high prices.

title: LIVE FUTURES 11/08:Tin set to hit new high of $36,000, nickel up 2%
summary: Fastmarkets/Fastmarkets-Metal Bulletin live futures commentary reports nickel is up 2% and highlights ongoing aluminium market conditions. The aluminium section stresses supply has been technically intact despite some curtailments and logistics disruption, suggesting mixed near-term momentum versus nickel’s clear gains.

title: Interra Copper Corp. Appoints Mr. Jason Nickel, P. Eng as Chief Executive Officer & Extends Drill Program
summary: Interra Copper Corp. appointed Jason Nickel as CEO and reported its Thane Project drilling program is on schedule and has been extended after promising early results at the Cathedral Area. Core samples have been sent for analysis with initial results expected soon, supporting potential copper development upside.

title: Interra Copper Corp. Appoints Mr. Jason Nickel, P. Eng as Chief Executive Officer & Extends Drill Program
summary: Interra Copper Corp. appointed Jason Nickel as CEO and reported that its drilling program at the Thane copper project is on schedule. Initial core samples from the first drill holes were sent for lab analysis, with results expected soon. The company extended drilling after promising early shows in the Cathedral Area.

title: World Copper Ltd.: World Copper Samples High-Grade Oxide Copper and Provides Exploration Update
summary: World Copper released exploration results from its Chilean Escalones project, reporting high-grade copper in oxide targets (including assays around 16.95–18.2% Cu and native copper confirmation) and delineating the extent of the Mancha Amarilla lithocap. Management says results support stronger resource potential and a possible heap-leach pathway.

title: Nickel prices again surging
summary: Nickel prices jumped to their highest in two weeks after softer U.S. inflation revived risk-on sentiment and expectations around Fed policy. Strong stainless-steel demand, falling refined output in China, and reduced nickel stocks in both LME and Shanghai supported the rally, with analysts citing a potential market deficit.

title: Analysts: copper prices are expected to rise in the short term_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Analysts expect copper to rise short term as macro conditions eventually tighten less than feared while liquidity easing and stronger fundamentals improve. Supply is constrained by smelter maintenance and power restrictions, electrolytic output may fall in August, and scrap availability tightens. Demand looks supported by grid and post-flood projects and accelerating destocking.

title: Shanghai Bonded Copper Stocks Fell 11,400 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show Shanghai bonded copper stocks declined 11,400 mt to 380,700 mt over Aug 6–13, falling for five straight weeks, though destocking slowed. Smelter output disruptions and refined copper replacing scrap reduced availability, while favorable price ratios and inflows of godown warrants after customs clearance further lowered bonded inventories.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Shrank 255,000 wmt to 5.512 Million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM data show Chinese nickel ore inventories fell 255,000 wmt to 5.512 million wmt between Aug 6 and Aug 13, with Ni content at 43,300 mt. Stocks at seven major ports also declined. Despite strong demand, stricter pandemic controls slowed unloading, keeping inventories tight.

title: Copper rises on Chilean supply risk as workers go on strike
summary: London copper prices rose 0.4% after strikes at two Chilean mines (Codelco’s Andina and JX Nippon’s Caserones) heightened supply disruption risk. Escondida approved a contract, limiting upside. Fitch cited tightened copper and aluminum markets from supply constraints, while weaker China demand weighed sentiment.

title: Peruvian copper miner Cerro Verde pays $245 mln tax debt 'under protest'
summary: Peruvian copper miner Cerro Verde paid $245.5 million in a disputed tax debt “under protest,” as arbitration over Peru’s tax calculations continues. With President Pedro Castillo seeking higher taxes on miners, similar disputes affecting large producers (including Buenaventura) can increase near-term cost and supply-risk expectations for copper.

title: Copper steady as Escondida deal takes edge off supply fears
summary: Copper prices were steady as a deal between management and workers at Chile’s Escondida mine eased supply fears, offsetting strikes at other operations and a weaker dollar. LME copper was up slightly and poised for a weekly gain. Aluminium rose and nickel was flat, reflecting broader sentiment rather than specific shocks.

title: Agreement Reached To Avoid Strike At World's Largest Copper Mine In Chile
summary: A labor union at Chile’s Escondida mine reached an agreement with BHP, canceling a planned strike after union approval of a new collective contract. The deal prevents potential production disruptions at the world’s largest copper operation, reducing near-term supply risk and supporting copper sentiment.

title: Temporary Suspension of Highland Valley Copper Operations due to Evacuation Order
summary: Teck announced it has temporarily suspended operations at its Highland Valley Copper mine in British Columbia because a wildfire evacuation order was issued nearby. Workers are demobilized while maintaining safety and environmental protection. Production impact depends on how long the suspension lasts, with restart planned once the order is lifted and safe.

title: Aluminium Downstream Operating Rate Extended Decline amid Deepening Impact of the Pandemic and Power Curtailment _SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates for large aluminium processing firms fell due to spreading pandemic disruptions and increasing power curtailment, especially in Henan, with many plants cutting output or shutting. Off-season weakness in real estate and automotive reduces demand, while higher aluminium prices further pressure orders, limiting production in coming weeks.

title: CATL Leading the Capacity Expansion of Copper Foil_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: CATL’s growth and related lithium-battery supply-chain expansion are boosting copper foil demand. Jiayuan Technology plans acquisitions and to build high-performance electrolytic copper foil capacity in Guangdong, while other foil makers expand in Qinghai and Huizhou. With copper-foil supply tight, processing fees and demand outlook remain strong, supporting copper sentiment.

title: Copper falls as China data dents demand outlook
summary: Copper prices fell as China economic data (slower factory output and retail sales, weaker exports, COVID-19 disruptions) raised worries about reduced near-term demand. LME copper dropped 1.6% and ShFE copper eased. The report also notes China aluminium output slipped amid power shortages, keeping aluminium under pressure.

title: LG Energy Solution secures stable supply of nickel, cobalt
summary: LG Energy Solution signed a six-year offtake agreement with Australian Mines to buy 71,000 tons of nickel (and 7,000 tons of cobalt) starting end-2024 from Queensland’s Sconi Project. The deal is intended to secure stable EV battery raw-material supply and may tighten near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: Funds unimpressed by mounting copper supply disruption: Andy Home
summary: The columnist cites escalating copper supply disruptions from Chile strikes and a Canada wildfire suspension, yet LME three-month copper is steady around $9,500/t. Funds’ speculative interest is low, with positioning at lows, while weaker China growth indicators and Delta-related demand worries outweigh micro supply hits in the near term.

title: LG Energy Solution to have 6-year access to nickel, cobalt from Australian Mines amid heated competition over raw materials
summary: LG Energy Solution signed a binding long-form offtake with Australian Mines for 71,000 tonnes of battery-grade nickel over six years starting end-2024, plus cobalt. The deal supplies mixed hydroxide precipitate from the Sconi Project, aimed at securing EV battery material supply amid raw-material competition.

title: Copper retreats on demand worries after Chinese data
summary: Copper prices fell as weak Chinese economic data intensified demand worries and drove broader risk-off sentiment, pulling LME three-month copper down 1.3% to $9,442/t. Aluminium rose slightly after China’s aluminium output slipped for a third month, but copper’s macro-demand pressure outweighed in the near term.

title: Freeport Completes Acquisition of Yandera Copper Project
summary: Freeport announced it has completed the acquisition of the Yandera copper project. The deal is expected to strengthen its copper asset base and supports market expectations for future copper supply. In the near term, the news is more likely to be sentiment-positive than to change physical balances quickly.

title: Azarga Metals Announces Updated Resource and PEA on Unkur Copper-Silver Project
summary: Azarga Metals reported an updated PEA for its Unkur copper-silver project, proposing ~11.7ktpa copper production over 14 years with SART heap leaching for oxide material and flotation for sulphides. Economics are shown at $3.86/lb copper (and $4.54/lb spot), but no immediate aluminium linkage is provided.

title: Latin Metals Discovers Outcropping Copper Mineralization at Lacsha, Peru
summary: Latin Metals reports outcropping copper-molybdenum mineralization at its Lacsha South project in Peru, with composite rock-chip results including ~0.20–0.22% copper over continuous channel sections and anomalous molybdenum. The release outlines further surveys to define drill targets but provides no resource or production figures.

title: India to receive first aluminium bodied coaches early next year
summary: Indian Railways expects to receive its first aluminium-bodied metro coaches in early 2022 after delays in a $17.3m contract with Dawonsys. Plans to use aluminium coaches for premium services due to lower haulage cost and corrosion resistance could lift expectations for incremental aluminium demand in the near term.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Acquires Royalty on Caserones Copper-Molybdenum Mine in Northern Chile
summary: EMX Royalty Corp. will acquire a 0.418% net smelter return (NSR) royalty on the operating Caserones copper-molybdenum mine in northern Chile for $34.1 million, alongside Altus. The royalty value can vary with LME copper price thresholds, but the deal mainly transfers royalty ownership, not production.

title: Shanghai aluminium hits 13-year high on supply concerns
summary: Shanghai and LME aluminium prices hit multi-year highs as China’s aluminium output faces ongoing power curtailment and declines in electrolytic production. The state planning review limits for high energy-consuming projects in major producing provinces adds supply concern. Higher alumina costs from reduced refinery output further supports bullish sentiment.

title: [Clara Ferreira Marques] Reality is dragging Russia toward climate acceptance
summary: Putin’s administration is moving toward emissions reporting and an emissions-reduction plan as the EU’s carbon border tax raises costs for carbon-intensive Russian exporters. The piece cites EU levy exposure and mentions Rusal separating “green” metal, implying near-term aluminium competitiveness pressure despite longer-run adaptation efforts.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces Desktop Study of Van Dyke Project
summary: Copper Fox announces a desktop data gap analysis to support EPA and ADEQ permitting for its Van Dyke in-situ copper recovery project in Arizona. The study will review hydrogeological information, refine permitting guidance, and scope field work. No production changes are reported, suggesting limited immediate impact on copper prices.

title: Aluminum Shapes of Pennsauken cites impact of pandemic, competition
summary: Aluminum Shapes LLC filed for Chapter 11 and is operating at about 10% capacity. It cites pandemic effects, increased overseas competition, supply chain issues, and the “skyrocketing price of metal” alongside inadequate cash flow. It plans a sale or liquidation of its aluminum window/door fabrication business.

title: Kamoa Copper Extends Existing Financing Agreement With DRC's State-Owned Power Company To Facilitate The Upgrade Of Turbine 5 At The Inga II Hydropower Complex
summary: Ivanhoe Mines’ Kamoa Copper extended financing with DRC’s SNEL to upgrade turbine 5 at the Inga II hydropower complex, expected to add 162 MW of renewable electricity. This, combined with Mwadingusha output, will provide priority clean power for Kamoa-Kakula copper Phase 3 and future expansions.

title: SMM: SHFE Aluminium Recording New Highs in Thirteen Years_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says SHFE aluminium surged to 13-year highs after NDRC signals on dual-control, carbon reduction and power restriction. Spot prices in East China hit record levels, with tight cargo availability and only mild discounts. Delayed shipments are arriving, but power curbs in east Inner Mongolia and off-season inventory shifts keep aluminium supported.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Copper Temporarily Pauses Drill Program at MPD Due to Wildfire Risk
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. temporarily pauses drilling at its MPD copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia due to wildfire risk and safety concerns. Workers are demobilized and work will resume once deemed safe. The company says it does not expect a material impact on its fully funded drill program.

title: Nova Royalty Acquires Producing 1.0% Net Smelter Return Royalty on the Aranzazu Copper Mine Owned by Aura Minerals Inc.
summary: Nova Royalty Corp. agreed to buy a 1.0% net smelter return royalty on Aura Minerals’ Aranzazu copper-gold-silver mine in Mexico. Royalty payments depend on copper prices versus an LME threshold and on ongoing copper concentrate production, but the transaction itself is unlikely to move copper fundamentals in the next weeks.

title: Fabled Continues To Define New Gold System, Hits Lower Feeder, which Returns 580.01 g/t Silver Eq, PLUS 19.90% Lead, 5.18% Zinc and 1.29% Copper
summary: Fabled Silver Gold reported drill assay results from the Santa Maria property in Mexico, describing a “lower feeder” zone with significant silver-equivalent and listed grades including copper (28.38 lb/tonne) alongside lead and zinc. The news is drilling-focused and provides no explicit copper supply impact or trade disruption.

title: Sombrero Resources Inc.: Sombrero Resources Options the High-Grade Takana Copper-Nickel District in Southeastern Peru
summary: Sombrero Resources signed an option agreement to acquire Peru’s Takana copper-nickel district, highlighting high-grade copper and nickel occurrences and plans to advance the project to drilling. The announcement is exploration-focused with no established resource or production, implying limited immediate impact on near-term copper or nickel prices.

title: U.S. Gold Expanding Wyoming Copper and Gold Projects; Names Francis to Lead its Exploration
summary: U.S. Gold says it is expanding its Wyoming copper and gold projects and appointing Francis to lead exploration. The update is supportive for longer-term copper supply expectations, but without details on near-term output, it is unlikely to meaningfully move copper prices within days to four weeks.

title: MMG : Residents block road near Peru's Las Bambas copper mine after two-week truce
summary: Residents near MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine in Peru restarted a road blockade, halting use of the mining corridor after a two-week truce. Communities accuse MMG of failing to attend a scheduled dialogue. Las Bambas produces about 400,000 tonnes of copper annually, and the disruption may impede shipments.

title: Copper rebounds from sell-off, Peru supply threat supports
summary: Copper prices rebounded after two days of losses as investors turned to “buy the dip.” Support came from concerns that ongoing labor strikes in Chile and road blocks near Peru’s Las Bambas mine could disrupt copper supply. LME three-month copper rose 0.6% to $9,305.50/ton.

title: Copper hits lowest in almost two months as concerns linger
summary: Copper prices fell for a third day to the lowest in almost two months, driven by weak economic data reinforcing demand concerns and nervousness ahead of central bank messaging at Jackson Hole. The selloff is echoed by declines in LME aluminum and nickel, reflecting broader risk-off pressure on industrial metals.

title: Copper prices spike with fears of supply disruption at Las Bambas mine
summary: Copper surged after fears of renewed supply disruption at Peru’s Las Bambas mine. Residents resumed road blockades involving the MMG-owned operation, following a prior truce break under President Castillo. With Las Bambas producing about 400,000 tonnes annually, the market priced higher near-term copper tightness; LME three-month rose 0.8%.

title: SM Lab develops cathode with 98% nickel, industry's highest density - The Korea Economic Daily Global Edition
summary: POSCO plans to spend about $200 million (230 billion won) to build a nickel sulfate refining facility to supply growing electric vehicle battery material demand. It also recently acquired a 30% stake in Australia’s Ravensthorpe Nickel Operation, reinforcing its nickel supply and refining expansion plans.

title: White Metal Announces New Mineral Resource Estimate Containing 7.7Mt at 1.82% CuEq, Using a 0.30% Cu Cut-off, Taranis Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Resources announced an updated Inferred mineral resource estimate for the Okohongo Cu-Ag project in Namibia. Using a 0.30% copper cut-off, it reports ~7.7 Mt grading 1.55% Cu (CuEq 1.82%). The news relates directly to prospective copper supply growth expectations.

title: EU CBAM for Iron, Steel, Cement, Fertilisers, Aluminium, Electricity
summary: The EU proposes a CBAM on certain imports to prevent carbon leakage, phasing in from 2023 and fully implemented from 2026. It would require importers to buy and surrender certificates based on embedded emissions, using EU ETS auction prices. Aluminium is explicitly in scope; carbon-costs may raise import costs and weigh on demand.

title: Three unions on strike at world's top copper producer
summary: Three CODELCO unions began a strike at the Andina division after rejecting a labor agreement. The strike involves 1,300 of 1,437 workers and affects underground Rio Blanco and open-pit Sur Sur mines that produced over 184,000 tonnes of copper last year. The labor action increases near-term Chile copper supply risk.

title: Copper slips to over 4-month low on firm dollar, easing supply pressure
summary: Copper prices fell to a more than four-month low as a stronger U.S. dollar weighed on sentiment and investors saw easing supply disruptions. Blockaded transport near MMG’s Las Bambas mine in Peru reopened and operations resumed at Teck’s Highland Valley Copper after evacuations ended. The piece also shows aluminium down and nickel slightly higher.

title: China Imported 9.25 Million mt of Aluminium Ores and Concentrates in July, Down 15.7% YoY_SMM
summary: China Customs data show July imports of aluminium ores and concentrates at 9.25 million mt, down 15.7% YoY, and YTD imports down 7.1% YoY. July exports of alumina rose sharply YoY, while imports of unwrought aluminium/products fell. The weaker ore inflow may tighten aluminium feedstock expectations.

title: Antofagasta H1 Profit Surges On Strong Copper Demand, Prices; Adjusts FY Production View
summary: Antofagasta reported sharply higher H1 profit as revenue rose on higher realized copper prices and strong copper demand. Despite lower sales volumes, results supported copper strength. The company adjusted FY copper production guidance for 2021 to 710–740 kt, while maintaining cost guidance at $1.25/lb.

title: SMM: Understanding Copper Rod Market based on Weekly Operating Rates_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates for copper rod (made of concentrate) companies averaged about 71% in July, above expectations, helped by stronger cable/wire demand and a narrower concentrate–scrap spread. Early August rates fell on COVID-19 transport and production disruptions, but SMM expects recovery in the second week with continued pandemic influence.

title: Nickel Sulphate Prices Stood Stable This Week, Likely to Weaken Next Week_SMM
summary: Battery-grade nickel sulphate prices were stable this week amid scarce supply and not-yet-peaked consumption, with upstream quotations staying high. However, downstream users are reluctant to buy at elevated prices. Precursor inquiry prices and coefficients fell, demand for high-grade ternary batteries is weak, and nickel sulphate prices are expected to weaken next week.

title: Antofagasta's H1 earnings soar, drought erodes copper output
summary: Antofagasta reported strong H1 earnings and raised interim dividends, but said Chile’s 12-year-driest conditions could erode copper output. A desalination plant redesign at Los Pelambres may trigger about 50,000 tonnes of production at risk next year, cutting 2022 estimates and weighing on near-term supply expectations.

title: Copperstone Resources : interim report January - June 2021
summary: Copperstone’s interim report highlights the Swedish government’s final decision to confirm the Viscaria exploitation concession (No. 7) and the reopening progress, with plans for further drilling, permitting, and potential increased mining and processing. It also notes support from Norrlandsfonden and an expectation of higher annual copper production.

title: Chile Drought Forces Copper Output Cuts in Top Producing Nation
summary: The report says drought conditions in Chile are forcing copper production cuts in the world’s top producing country. The immediate effect is lower mine supply, which can tighten the market and raise near-term expectations for copper prices over coming days to weeks.

title: Teck Resources resumes operations at Highland Valley copper mine
summary: Teck Resources resumed operations at its Highland Valley copper mine in British Columbia after an evacuation linked to wildfire threats. The company had restarted an oxygen plant to address smelting idling from poor air quality, but warned further smoke could cause outages. It may update guidance once wildfire risk eases.

title: DGAP-News: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Hits Massive Sulphides at Lappvattnet Nickel Deposit
summary: Gungnir Resources said ongoing drilling at its Lappvattnet nickel sulphide project in Sweden intersected massive and semi-massive sulphides, including a 10-metre interval. Samples have been submitted for priority nickel (and PGEs) assays in the next couple of weeks; mineralization includes chalcopyrite indicating potential copper.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Hits Massive Sulphides at Lappvattnet Nickel Deposit
summary: Gungnir Resources reported drilling at its Lappvattnet nickel deposit in Sweden intersecting massive and semi-massive sulphides, including a 10-metre core interval. Samples have been submitted for priority assaying for nickel (and PGEs); copper and cobalt are also planned, with assays expected within weeks.

title: Three Valley Copper Reports 2021 Second Quarter Results (all amounts expressed in US dollars)
summary: Three Valley Copper reported Q2 2021 results, including 1,035 tonnes of copper cathode production and revised 2021 guidance due to Chilean COVID restrictions, equipment shortages, and labor competition impacting construction and ore delivery. An offtake amendment increases 2021–2022 sales at prevailing spot prices, improving near-term cash flow.

title: Tesla Shareholders Point to Human Rights Risks in Sourcing Nickel From Russian Nornickel
summary: Tesla shareholders raise human-rights and environmental concerns about sourcing nickel from Russia’s Nornickel after a May 2020 Arctic fuel spill affecting Indigenous communities. The piece notes Tesla has no agreement stated by the board and Nornickel cites compensation and ongoing programs. No direct supply disruption is reported.

title: Primary Aluminium Inventories Rose 2,000 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data said China’s social aluminium inventories across eight consumption areas rose by 2,000 mt on the week to 741,000 mt as of Aug 19. The gain was mainly in Gongyi, while Wuxi inventories declined due to lower arrivals, suggesting net near-term supply loosened.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Aug 19): Shanghai Nonferrous Metals Closed Mostly in the Negative Territory with Copper Leading the Losses_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nonferrous metals closing mostly lower as a higher US dollar and hawkish Fed meeting minutes hurt risk appetite. Copper fell 3.27% and LME copper declined. Aluminium dropped 1.68% on soft macro and slowing de-stocking, while nickel slid 2.09% amid weaker stainless steel prices.

title: Copper and iron ore tumble as growth fears roil metals markets
summary: The piece reports that copper prices are tumbling alongside iron ore as worries about economic growth roil metals markets. The negative macro sentiment implies weaker near-term demand expectations for industrial commodities, creating downward pressure on copper prices over the following days.

title: Copper slides as China, Fed and COVID-19 trigger sell-off
summary: Copper fell 2.9% to the lowest in more than four months as China dampened growth measures, the Fed signaled reduced bond buying (supporting a stronger dollar), and COVID-19 cases spurred demand worries. The sell-off also weighed on aluminium and nickel, with both down on the day.

title: Emerita Intersects 3.8% Copper, 30.5% Zinc, 15.6% Lead and
summary: Emerita Resources reports high-grade drill hole results from the Infanta Deposit in Spain, including copper mineralization (reported as 3.8% copper in the title) over 86.2–112.8 meters. The company describes step-out drilling to extend strike length and depth, with further results expected.

title: UAE-based Emirates Global Aluminium refinances $5.5bln debt
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) said it has refinanced $5.5bn of corporate debt, reducing leverage and cutting scheduled repayments by about two and a half years. The new terms lower the cost of debt, improving the company’s balance sheet, but the article does not indicate near-term production or market supply changes.

title: Copper Prices Just Fell to a Dangerous Level. What That Means for the Economy.
summary: The piece reports that copper prices have dropped to a “dangerous” level and characterizes the move as a negative signal for economic recovery. While it provides no specific drivers, the clear focus on an abrupt copper price decline implies near-term bearish pressure on copper.

title: There's gold in this hill near Princeton but is there copper too? | iNFOnews | Thompson-Okanagan's News Source
summary: Sego Resources reports gold assay results at its Miners Mountain project near Princeton and says the geology may represent a gold-copper porphyry system. Further drilling is planned, contingent on wildfire conditions, to assess deposit size and determine whether mineable copper is present. Copper assay data is not yet provided.

title: Tiger Finance Provides $15.5 Million D-I-P Financing to Aluminum Shapes LLC
summary: Tiger Finance provided $15.5 million in debtor-in-possession financing to Aluminum Shapes LLC, a New Jersey aluminum extruder and distributor, to fund Chapter 11 restructuring and a potential going-concern sale. The liquidity is intended to keep production and sales running, lowering near-term disruption risk for aluminum supply.

title: Fabled Silver Gold Corp: Fabled Silver Gold Announces Closing of $6.9 Million Private Placement in Connection with the Proposed Spin-Out of Copper Assets
summary: Fabled Silver Gold closed a C$6.9 million private placement to support the planned spin-out of its Muskwa copper project into a separate listed entity. Proceeds are earmarked for working capital and flow-through exploration expenses. The news focuses on corporate structuring, financing terms, and exploration plans rather than copper fundamentals.

title: Copper Inventory in Shanghai Bonded Zone down 12,200 mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says Shanghai bonded-zone copper inventories fell 12,200 mt to 368,500 mt by Aug 20, the sixth straight weekly decline. The improved SHFE/LME copper price ratio, electricity curtailment, scrap shortages, and limited imported cargo inflows boosted customs clearances, sending Yangshan premiums above $50/mt and likely pushing inventories lower.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 8,900 mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says copper inventories across major Chinese markets fell 8,900 mt by Aug 20 to 150,800 mt, driven mainly by declines in Shanghai and Guangdong. Limited imported-copper arrivals and improved demand from lower prices reduced stocks. With strong cathode consumption and no surge in inflows, SMM expects continued inventory drops next week.

title: Drought in Chile forces Antofagasta to lower its copper production target_SMM
summary: Antofagasta said Chile’s worsening water shortage forced it to lower its 2022 copper production target to 710,000–740,000 tonnes versus a prior 730,000–760,000 range. It also warned desalination redesign delays at Los Pelambres could endanger about 50,000 tonnes of copper output.

title: London copper set for steepest weekly loss in 2 months
summary: London copper is set for its steepest weekly loss in two months despite a Friday uptick, as China’s slowing growth, COVID-19 outbreaks, and U.S. bond-buying taper worries dent metal sentiment. Copper hit four-month lows on weak data. The piece also reports day moves in nickel and aluminium amid China reserve release uncertainty.

title: Copper bounces, but demand concerns dominate mood
summary: Copper prices bounced on the day but remain headed for the biggest weekly fall since June. Traders cite worsening demand concerns: slower growth in China, tighter U.S. monetary-policy expectations boosting the dollar, and rising global COVID/Delta infections. Technicals look oversold, but negatives still dominate sentiment.

title: Tight Domestic Supply of Nickel Plates Bolstered SHFE/LME Nickel Price Ratio_SMM
summary: SHFE/LME nickel ratio rose this week as tight spot supply of nickel plates boosted spot premiums. Lower nickel prices prompted downstream restocking, while the opening import window increased bonded-zone inflows. Port congestion delayed expected plate shipments, keeping warrant premiums high; briquette premiums are less likely to improve.

title: Marubeni : Japan's Marubeni starts selling carbon-neutral aluminium ingot
summary: Marubeni began selling a carbon-neutral aluminium ingot (“Neutr-Al”) for Japanese buyers seeking lower emissions in transport, packaging and construction. It offsets GHG from bauxite, alumina, smelting and shipping using carbon credits. Pricing is variable by customer needs, with no fixed rate, and no supply disruption noted.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Increased to 5.92 Million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM reported Chinese nickel ore inventories at major ports rose 410,000 wmt to 5.92 million wmt as of Aug 20, with nickel content totaling 46,500 mt. COVID-19 quarantines at Tieshan and Lianyungang slowed offloading, extending shipping schedules. Imports are expected to weaken as the Philippines enters wet season, reducing accumulation risk.

title: Nomad increases royalty stake in Caserones copper mine in Chile
summary: Nomad Royalty agreed to buy an additional 0.351% net smelter return royalty on Chile’s Caserones copper mine for $27.25m cash, raising total exposure to 0.63% NSR. It will also acquire CMC shares and expects closing in Aug/early Sep 2021, mainly to boost cash flow, not change production materially.

title: Copper rebounds, but demand concerns dominate market
summary: Copper prices rebounded 0.4% but are still headed for the biggest weekly drop since June, driven by concerns over slowing Chinese demand, expectations of U.S. monetary tightening boosting the dollar, and rising COVID-19 Delta cases. Aluminium and nickel also edged up slightly, reflecting mixed market sentiment.

title: LIVE FUTURES 17/08: Copper at one-month low on LME, nickel down 1.6%
summary: The article is a “live futures” update noting copper at a one-month low on the LME and nickel down 1.6%. This implies immediate bearish price pressure for both metals. Other content focuses on Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin assessment methodology, timing, and corrections, with no clear new supply-demand catalyst.

title: LIVE FUTURES 17/08: Copper at one-month low on LME, nickel down 1.6%
summary: The piece is a live futures update noting copper at a one-month low on the LME and nickel down 1.6%, signaling near-term bearish sentiment. The rest of the article mostly covers Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin publication timing and procedural corrections to specific assessments, with limited new fundamental impact detail.

title: Nickel miner Noront reiterates support for $325 million BHP takeover
summary: Noront Resources reiterated its board’s recommendation that shareholders accept BHP’s $325 million cash offer, following a dispute with largest shareholder Wyloo Metals. Noront’s main asset is its Eagle’s Nest nickel-and-copper deposit. While the outcome may influence nickel supply expectations, deal scale likely limits broad near-term price impact.

title: New dawn for copper in Zambia
summary: Zambian copper producers are preparing $2bn expansion plans next year contingent on agreeing mineral royalties and tax rules with President-elect Hakainde Hichilema’s administration. Companies held back capital since 2019 amid tax changes. Producers seek royalty deductions and sliding-scale taxes, aiming for a more stable policy environment.

title: Rising copper prices help Poongsan, hit LS-Nikko
summary: Rising LME copper cash prices are boosting Poongsan’s operating profit through higher inventory valuation and healthy demand for copper products. In contrast, South Korea’s LS-Nikko refining business is hit by falling refining margins as Chinese competitors expand refining capacity, intensifying price competition and pressuring long-term contract terms.

title: Risen Energy expands Power Purchase Agreement with BHP to further cut Nickel West's emissions
summary: Risen Energy expanded its 10-year renewable PPA with BHP, increasing solar electricity deliveries to Nickel West operations. The added 30MW will supply the Kalgoorlie smelter and cut Scope 2 emissions by 30%, building on earlier supply to the Kwinana refinery. The update is focused on decarbonization, not output changes.

title: SHFE Aluminium to Remain at Highs, Despite Increasing Inventory_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME aluminium volatility amid stronger USD and Fed hawkishness, which pressured prices. However, power curtailment and energy controls have already removed significant capacity and further cuts are possible. The peak-season recovery could reverse rising social inventories, offering support and upward momentum for aluminium.

title: A Chinese Smelter Suspended Refined Nickel Production, Affecting Output by 4%_SMM
summary: SMM says a north China smelter has recently suspended refined nickel production because of high production costs. The plant’s refined nickel output is about 4% of China’s August total, with the overall impact considered limited. Resumption timing is not set. Nickel salt production continues on separate lines.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Completes Initial Closing on the Royalty Acquisition on the Caserones Copper-Molybdenum Mine in Northern Chile
summary: EMX Royalty Corp. completed the initial closing of its purchase of an NSR royalty interest on the Caserones copper-molybdenum mine in northern Chile, acquiring 0.418% effective NSR royalty for US$34.1 million. Further closing is expected by September 1. The deal is presented as improving cash flows, not changing copper supply.

title: Copper prices advance as traders hunt for bargains
summary: Copper prices rose on Monday as risk-on sentiment returned, supported by signs China’s COVID outbreak is tapering and bargain hunting after recent weakness. Additional support came from a labor contract rejection at Chile’s El Teniente mine, raising supply concerns. Nickel and aluminum also increased alongside broader base-metal strength.

title: Global bauxite production to grow by nearly 4% in 2021
summary: GlobalData forecasts global bauxite production to rise about 3.8% in 2021 to 372.8 million tonnes, citing higher output in Australia and Guinea and return to pre-COVID levels. It also highlights mine restart/expansions and a new railway improving freight volumes, plus plans for alumina refining in Boke.

title: Copper climbs as investors return to market after slump
summary: Copper jumped 2% on the LME as investors returned after a recent slump, attracted by lower prices and hopes for improving global growth and electrification-driven demand. The piece also references improving euro-zone activity and fewer China COVID cases, alongside a May refined-copper surplus shift. Aluminium and nickel rose too.

title: Domestic Copper Consumption Still Have Support but Copper Prices to Dip Further_SMM
summary: SMM expects SHFE and LME copper prices to dip further despite supportive domestic supply-demand fundamentals. July data disappointed and Fed minutes signaled tapering, weighing sentiment. Electric restrictions eased slightly but cathode supply limits still linger, while falling scrap and weaker price momentum constrain rod makers and reinforce bearish price expectations.

title: Playfair Mobilizes for Drilling at RKV Copper Project, Norway
summary: Playfair says core drilling is expected to begin in early September on its 100%-owned RKV copper project in Norway. Permits are approved, drill targets have been defined, and prior sampling showed strong mobile metal ion copper anomalies (with values >6,000 ppb).

title: Playfair Mining Ltd.: Playfair Mobilizes for Drilling at RKV Copper Project, Norway
summary: Playfair Mining announced mobilization of a core drilling program for its RKV Copper Project in Norway, with permits approved and a lightweight, hand-carried drill machine arriving for September drilling. The project targets multiple high-grade copper soil anomalies (MMI Cu) consistent with potential weathering copper sulphides.

title: Edgemont Prepares to Commence Drilling at Dungate Copper-Gold Porphyry Project near Houston, B.C.
summary: Edgemont Gold Corp. said drilling equipment is on site and Phase I drilling is about to start at its Dungate copper-gold porphyry project in B.C., targeting IP anomalies and a quartz-pyrite breccia zone reported in older drilling. It is an exploration update without assays or production impact, limiting immediate price effects.

title: Norden Crown Commences Drilling at the Burfjord Copper-Gold Project, Norway
summary: Norden Crown Metals, with Boliden, has started ~2,500 metres of diamond drilling at the Burfjord copper-gold project in Norway, targeting IOCG-style mineralization and following up prior drill intercepts. The release details target zones and planned exploration activities, but signals no near-term mine output changes.

title: Congo seeks revaluation for China Moly's copper and cobalt mine
summary: DR Congo has formed a commission to re-evaluate reserves and resources at China Molybdenum’s Tenke Fungurume copper-cobalt mine to verify compliance and potentially renegotiate contract terms and extensions. The review may affect perceived future copper supply, but no immediate production changes are confirmed.

title: Metals Creek Resources Corp. Receives 1,250,000 Shares of Class 1 Nickel and Technologies Limited for PGE Claims in The River Valley Area of Ontario
summary: Metals Creek Resources announced it will receive 1.25 million shares of Class 1 Nickel and Technologies Limited in exchange for a 100% interest in 500 hectares of PGE/nickel-related claims in Ontario, plus a 2% net smelter returns royalty. It also mentions exposure to copper/nickel/PGE exploration, without production.

title: Class 1 Nickel Announces Execution of Definitive Agreement to Acquire Strategic Portfolio of Mineral Claims in Ontario and Quebec
summary: Class 1 Nickel agreed to acquire additional mineral claims in Ontario and Quebec, expanding its Alexo Dundonald and Somanike (including the Marbridge Nickel Mine) property portfolios. Consideration includes cash and share issuance. The deal is subject to approvals and closing conditions, with no stated immediate production impact.

title: McEwen Mining : Copper Inc. Closes $40 million Private Placement with Rob (Form 8-K)
summary: McEwen Mining announced its subsidiary McEwen Copper closed the first tranche of a $40 million private placement to fund the Los Azules copper project in Argentina, including permitting, access road construction, and drilling. A second tranche is expected by Sept. 30. No immediate production or trade changes were stated.

title: Six Southern California Companies Convicted of Scheming to Avoid Payment of $1.8 Billion in Duties on Imported Chinese Aluminum
summary: Six Southern California companies were convicted for allegedly scheming to avoid paying $1.8 billion in duties on imported Chinese aluminium. The case implies tighter compliance and enforcement of aluminium tariff obligations, potentially increasing effective import costs and reducing near-term inflows to the US market.

title: London copper falls on caution ahead of Fed symposium
summary: London copper slipped 0.5% as traders turned cautious ahead of a U.S. Fed symposium that may clarify stimulus tapering timing. A potential tightening outlook could support the dollar and hurt demand expectations. LME aluminium eased slightly, while ShFE nickel rose, showing mixed regional reactions.

title: China Copper Cathode Imports Down Further in July on Closed Import Window_SMM
summary: China’s copper cathode imports fell further in July as the closed Q2 import window continued to suppress customs declarations and trading. Premiums weakened and traders slowed import pace, shifting or warehousing cargoes. The SHFE/LME ratio improved from mid-July, but a demand boost is expected mainly in August.

title: Pandemic sends alumina exporters up ship creek
summary: Australia’s leading alumina exporter says pandemic disruptions have surged shipping rates for moving alumina to China to about $50/t versus ~$18/t historically. The firm expects margins to be squeezed until shipping normalizes, though strong Chinese demand for aluminium end products provides some offset.

title: LIVE FUTURES 24/08: LME prices rise slightly, cancellations of copper, zinc, tin continue
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures report says LME prices rose slightly while cancellations of copper (and other metals) continued. It also covers Fastmarkets’ procedural corrections to certain European low-carbon aluminium differential and extrusion billet premium assessments. The net near-term signal is mild upward pressure, mainly via the copper/LME move.

title: Nickel target Western Areas plays hard to get
summary: Takeover target Western Areas says it will keep leverage over its next Australian nickel supply by limiting long-term supply contracts with traditional industrial customers. Management is seeking new battery and auto-making customers as electrification reshapes demand. The story implies stronger near-term nickel demand support and potential supply tightening effects.

title: Copper claws higher on physical demand, but jittery on rates
summary: Copper prices rose for a third session on renewed physical demand, with buyers seeking physical metal and China’s Yangshan premium improving. Gains were restrained by uncertainty ahead of U.S. Fed comments at Jackson Hole affecting the dollar. Separately, alumina hit six-month highs after a Jamalco refinery blaze, supporting aluminum.

title: Secondary Aluminium Alloy Quotations Trended Higher_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices fluctuating but trending higher, with A00 up 50 yuan/mt and secondary aluminium offers rising 100 yuan/mt. Scrap prices increased, imported ingots thinned and immediate import losses rose slightly. Oxygen and ADC12 costs continued to climb, and secondary plants raised quotes, though deals were subdued.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Intercepts 105 Meters of 1.18% Copper Equivalent Including 21.22 Meters of 2.55% CuEq at the Carmacks Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Yukon, Canada
summary: Granite Creek reported diamond drill results at its Carmacks project in Yukon, including 105.52 meters of 1.18% copper equivalent and a higher-grade 21.22 meters of 2.55% CuEq. The company says results extend Zone 2000S below the current model and may support an updated resource estimate.

title: Australian aluminium smelter aims to switch to renewables
summary: Tomago, Australia’s largest aluminium smelter, plans to source 100% renewable electricity by 2029 after its current power contract tied to AGL’s Bayswater coal plant ends in 2028. The shift raises doubts about Bayswater’s extended operation and signals lower-carbon, potentially lower-cost aluminium production going forward.

title: Quaterra Resources Inc.: Quaterra Announces the Advancement of the MacArthur Copper Oxide Project with Key Appointment and Metallurgical Progress
summary: Quaterra Resources announced a key appointment to lead the MacArthur oxide copper project and completion of a metallurgical sampling program ahead of its pre-feasibility study. The company drilled over 1,355 meters for representative samples, with assays from additional oxide and sulfide drilling expected soon. It also filed a judicial review petition on water permits.

title: Capella Continues Scandinavian Focus and Strategy with the Acquisition of Gold-Copper Projects in Finland
summary: Capella Minerals signed a binding LOI to earn-in to Cullen’s Katajavaara and Aakenus gold(-copper) projects in northern Finland, requiring upfront and multi-year exploration payments. The release frames the geology and permits but does not indicate immediate production changes, supply disruptions, or policy actions impacting base-metal prices.

title: Quaterra Announces the Advancement of the MacArthur Copper Oxide Project with Key Appointment and Metallurgical Progress
summary: Quaterra Resources announced a key appointment to lead its MacArthur oxide copper mine PFS and reported completion of a metallurgical sampling program, with assays from further oxide and sulfide drilling expected soon. It also filed a judicial review petition regarding forfeiture of Nevada water permits. No immediate production or supply impact is stated.

title: MMC Norilsk Nickel: Nornickel's Global Palladium Fund Reduces the Cost of Its Gold ETCs to Take Advantage of Investor Interest
summary: Global Palladium Fund cut the TER on its gold ETC and cited research expecting European pension funds to increase gold allocations. It also notes it launched physically backed copper and nickel ETCs and claims it is the only provider for both. The implied fundraising/inflow outlook is modestly supportive for copper and nickel sentiment.

title: Blackstone Intersects 375m of Nickel Sulfide from 2m
summary: Blackstone Minerals reports final infill drilling at its Ban Phuc DSS deposit in Vietnam, intersecting 375m of nickel sulfide and improving confidence in its JORC nickel resource. The results are expected to underpin its Ta Khoa UBU PFS and potentially increase mine inventory, supporting near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: Aluminum Near Three-Year High as Disruptions Tighten Market
summary: The piece headline states aluminium is trading near a three-year high as disruptions tighten the market. This suggests near-term supply constraints are improving aluminium price expectations, with bullish pressure likely in the coming days as market tightness outweighs any near-term demand weakness.

title: London copper edges down as investors eye Fed meeting
summary: London three-month copper fell 0.3% to $9,350/t as investors stayed cautious before the Fed’s Jackson Hole meeting, weighing possible tapering and its impact via the US dollar and growth expectations. LME aluminium edged up 0.2%, with alumina prices rising after a Jamalco refinery blaze, suggesting limited near-term pressure.

title: SMM Analysis of Chinese Unwrought Aluminium Alloy Import in July_SMM
summary: China Customs data show July 2021 imports of unwrought aluminium alloy at 88,000 mt, down 48.5% year-on-year and 2.3% month-on-month, while exports also fell. The decline is linked to last year’s scrap restrictions, COVID-driven lower overseas demand, and closed import profits, plus Malaysia lockdown curbing shipments.

title: Altus Strategies commences IP survey at Adgz Copper-Silver project
summary: Altus Strategies began a 135 line-km induced polarisation (IP) and gradient array geophysical survey at its Agdz copper-silver project in Morocco. The survey will refine targets for trenching and drilling across several prospects with prior rock-chip copper grades up to 8% and other encouraging results.

title: Rising Bauxite Prices in Henan Boosted Dependence on Imported Bauxite_SMM
summary: Henan bauxite production is declining amid environmental/safety checks, flooding, and COVID-19, leaving local supply unable to meet alumina demand. Operating rates are recovering, but tighter bauxite availability has pushed bauxite prices higher. Alumina plants are increasing imported bauxite use, which can tighten costs and supply conditions for aluminium.

title: Global Aluminum Extrusion Market Analysis & Trends -
summary: ReportLinker’s market report highlights growing demand for aluminum extrusion from automotive/EV penetration, construction and green buildings, and increased use of recycled/value-added aluminum, supported by sustainability and BIPV incentives. It also notes COVID-19 disruptions but expects gradual improvement, implying supportive near-term aluminum sentiment.

title: Ignore Copper's Gyrations. Demand Is Strong, Top Supplier Says
summary: Codelco’s chairman said copper’s recent dip is temporary, citing strong demand for wiring and clean-energy infrastructure. China’s Covid containment boosted sentiment after earlier slowdown worries. Codelco begins a $1.4 billion Salvador investment and expects slightly higher output, though a strike at Andina is ongoing.

title: Taliban sitting on $1 trillion in iron ore, copper and gold
summary: The article says the Taliban controls Afghanistan and holds deposits worth over $1 trillion, including copper (and iron ore and gold). It argues improved stability could enable much greater mineral development over time, but it does not describe imminent production or export changes, limiting near-term price implications.

title: Copper Slips as Dollar and Yields Rise, Virus Concerns Simmer
summary: Copper is slipping as the dollar and bond yields rise, while virus-related concerns continue to simmer. The piece frames these macro moves as weighing on near-term risk appetite and copper demand expectations, creating downward price pressure in the immediate market window.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.24% Higher at $4.2650 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper’s front-month contract settled 0.24% higher at $4.2650 per pound, gaining 1.00 cent. The market rose for four consecutive sessions, with the largest four-day dollar and percentage gain since late July and the highest settlement value since Aug. 16, 2021.

title: Geophysical IP Survey at Agdz Copper-Silver Project, Morocco
summary: Altus Strategies started a 135 line-km induced polarisation geophysical survey at its Agdz copper-silver project in Morocco to prioritize targets for trenching and drilling. The release reiterates historical rock-chip copper grades up to 8% and additional positive results, but provides no direct aluminium-related market impact.

title: Royalty bill will put pressure on private copper miners in Chile_SMM
summary: Chile’s Congress is reviewing a royalty bill that would levy a 3% royalty on copper sales. Private miners warn the rates could pressure operations and even cause some mines to shut down, while supporters cite social spending needs. The bill’s progress and potential supply impact are bearish for copper.

title: Aluminium Prices Pulled Back Slightly, Secondary Aluminium Prices Stood Firm_SMM
summary: SMM reports that Chinese aluminium prices fluctuated at high levels. A00 aluminium eased by 60 yuan/mt to 20,540 yuan/mt, while secondary aluminium prices remained firm. Imports of aluminium ingots thinned, and die-casting demand stayed relatively rigid despite high production costs. Secondary aluminium is expected to fluctuate.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventories Fell 6,200 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data showed China’s social aluminium billet inventories fell 6,200 mt week-on-week to 124,400 mt as of Aug 26, led by declines in Foshan, Wuxi and Nanchang. Downstream restocking reflected high aluminium prices, but billet demand weakened; inventories are expected to stay muted next week due to low arrivals.

title: Subdued Trades in Copper Import Market amid Wider Import Losses_SMM
summary: SMM reports subdued trading in Shanghai’s imported copper market as import losses widen to 200 yuan/mt. Backwardation in LME cash versus the three-month contract remains $6.5/mt, while near-term arrivals see lower quotes and purchases remain scarce, indicating weaker physical demand conditions.

title: Silver Elephant Mining Corp.: Silver Elephant Announces Execution of Plan of Arrangement and Spin-Out of Nickel and Vanadium Assets
summary: Silver Elephant executed an arrangement spinning out its Minago nickel project into a separate SpinCo for shareholders, alongside other vanadium and royalty interests. The release discusses nickel resource details and ongoing steps to finalize environmental license documentation for Minago’s open-pit operations, but provides no immediate production change.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Copper Restarts Drill Program at MPD
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. said it is remobilizing staff to restart its drill program at the MPD copper-gold porphyry project in Southern British Columbia. The company attributes the restart to improved conditions and reduced wildfire risk, expects continued drilling and to provide updates later in the season.

title: UAE's Emirates Global Aluminium considering IPO for H1 2022 -sources
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) is considering an IPO for H1 2022 and is weighing valuations and investor appetite. Sources say recent record aluminum prices in Europe and the US could influence the decision. EGA has smelters in the UAE and a bauxite mine in Guinea, valued by banks at $16–19B.

title: Aluminium smelters in China's Xinjiang told to cut output
summary: Reuters reports that Changji prefecture in China’s Xinjiang ordered several aluminium smelters to limit production from August, cutting monthly output by about 10% versus Jan–Jul levels. Xinjiang is a key global supply hub, so the supply restriction is supportive for short-term aluminium pricing.

title: Copper Prices Slip Below Scrap For First Time Since April 2020
summary: Copper prices have reportedly fallen below scrap for the first time since April 2020. This suggests spot copper is trading at weaker levels relative to scrap metal values, pointing to deteriorating near-term pricing sentiment and potential pressure on copper demand or tightness expectations.

title: Alumina handling operator set to benefit from Siwertell Ship Unloader Technology.
summary: Bruks Siwertell won an order for a road-mobile Siwertell unloader to discharge dry alumina at Marseille for Trimet France. The equipment claims dust-free, low-spillage handling with minimal material degradation and low energy use. The operator says reduced fines can lower energy needs in aluminium smelting.

title: ThreeD Maintains 9% Ownership In Premium Nickel Resources
summary: ThreeD Capital says it participated in a private placement to maintain its ~9% ownership in Premium Nickel Resources, which is pursuing acquisition of the former BCL Limited and TNMC assets in Botswana. The projects target development of separate Ni-Co and Cu concentrates, though completion is not assured.

title: London copper dips as investors await Jackson Hole meeting
summary: London copper slid 0.1% as investors stayed cautious ahead of the Jackson Hole Fed symposium, where expected plans to cut stimulus could boost the dollar and make greenback-priced metals costlier. Copper also faced softer Chinese industrial profit growth. Aluminium rose on Xinjiang smelter output-limit risks.

title: Aluminium Downstream Operating Rate Continued to Pick up after Power Curtailment in Henan was Lifted _SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium processing operating rates rose after Henan power curtailment was lifted and transport recovered, with Guangxi also improving. However, aluminium and silicon price surges lifted input costs and weighed on some secondary producers due to raw material shortages. Wire/cable and extrusion face pressure from higher aluminium prices, while demand expectations are mixed into peak season.

title: Aluminium Inventory Growth in Shanghai Bonded Zone Slowed Down Significantly  _SMM
summary: SMM reported that aluminium inventories in Shanghai’s bonded zone increased by just 1,700 tonnes week-on-week to 102,800 tonnes as of Aug 27. The weekly inventory growth rate was much slower than the previous week, suggesting less rapid accumulation and potential support for near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: China curbs propel aluminum to highest since April 2018
summary: Aluminum prices jumped to their highest since April 2018 after Xinjiang imposed output limits on five smelters and curbed electricity usage, reducing domestic supply. Benchmark aluminum rose about 1.5% and ShFE prices hit multi-year highs. The piece also mentions upcoming Chinese metal reserve auctions, including aluminum.

title: SRB to Release the Third Batch of Copper, Aluminium and Zinc into the Market _SMM
summary: SMM reports the State Reserve Bureau will release the third batch of state metals soon: 30,000 mt of copper and 70,000 mt of aluminium, alongside 50,000 mt of zinc. The added official supply is likely to weigh on copper and aluminium prices over the coming days as inventories rise.

title: SRB to Release the Third Batch of Copper, Aluminium and Zinc into the Market _SMM
summary: SMM reports that China’s State Reserve Bureau will begin releasing its third batch of strategic metals into the market soon, including copper (30,000 mt) and aluminium (70,000 mt), alongside zinc. The added government supply likely increases short-term availability expectations and pressure prices downward for copper and aluminium.

title: Second Q4 MJP aluminium producer offer at $250/t - sources
summary: Sources cite a “Second Q4 MJP aluminium producer offer” at $250/t. The piece also notes procedural timing and database corrections for several aluminium (including low-carbon) premium assessments and publication schedules in Europe and Asia. No copper or nickel pricing information is provided.

title: Canyon partners China's MCC to develop Cameroon bauxite project
summary: Canyon Resources partnered with China’s MCC-CIE to develop Cameroon’s Minim Martap bauxite project. The deal supports financing, off-take, and technical work for Stage 1, targeting direct shipping of about five million tonnes per year via Douala port. The partnership also links MCC groups to alumina/aluminium operations.

title: Copper Inventories in Shanghai Bonded Zone Dip on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Shanghai bonded-zone copper inventories fell by 23,400 mt to 345,100 mt as of Aug. 27, the seventh consecutive week of decline. The import window opened recently, and cargoes booked under warrants amid import profits were brought in after customs clearance, further reducing bonded inventory.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Grow on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 154,000 wmt week-on-week to 6.076 million wmt as of Aug 27, with Ni content at 47,700 mt. While broader port stocks at seven major ports fell, the overall increase suggests stranded cargoes are building and easing supply tightness.

title: LIVE FUTURES 27/08: Aluminium nears $2,700/t, most LME prices buoyant at week's end
summary: A Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin live futures wrap says aluminium is nearing $2,700/t and most LME prices are buoyant at the week’s end, implying supportive near-term sentiment for aluminium. The rest of the content focuses on methodology and procedural corrections to some aluminium pricing assessments.

title: Two charged with Iowa copper thefts that caused power outages
summary: Two people were charged with stealing copper from grounding rods at electrical substations in northwest Iowa, triggering fires, several power outages, and damage estimated in the hundreds of thousands of dollars. Authorities say utility workers found removed copper components, prompting costly repairs and service disruptions.

title: Chilean national copper company calls on strikers at Andina mine to return to the negotiating table_SMM
summary: Codelco urged miners at its Andina copper mine in Chile to return to negotiations after a 16-day strike that has cut operations to minimum safe levels. Unions say contract terms lag historical benefits despite high copper prices and cite rising costs. The strike reduces output from Andina’s earlier production base.

title: Oman's Ghuzayn copper project offers paradigm for engagement with local community
summary: Oman’s Ministry of Energy and Minerals says progress has been made on Mawarid Mining’s Ghuzayn underground copper project after addressing local community concerns under Oman’s Mineral Wealth Law. The firm plans about RO 43 million in initial investment and milestones for studies/approvals in 2021, with production beyond the near term.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 4,500 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM data show copper inventories across major Chinese markets fell 4,500 mt over the weekend to 130,000 mt. Declines in Guangdong and Tianjin reflect low arriving shipments tied to smelter maintenance and strong downstream offtake. Shanghai rose on higher imported arrivals. Weekly inventories depend on future import shipment flows.

title: SHANGHAI'S MOST ACTIVE NICKEL CONTRACT RISES 3%
summary: Reuters reports that Shanghai’s most active nickel contract rose 3%. The move signals stronger near-term price momentum for nickel, likely reflecting shifting short-term trading expectations and market sentiment around nickel supply-demand conditions in Asia.

title: UAE's Emirates Global Aluminium swings to profit in first half
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium reported a return to profit in the first half of 2021, attributing gains to higher aluminium prices as economies recovered from COVID-19. The LME aluminium benchmark averaged $2,245/tonne in the first half versus $1,592 a year earlier, boosting revenues and earnings.

title: Short-Term Alumina Price Outlook Remains Bullish on Rising Cost and Supply Disruptions Overseas_SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices rising week-on-week, supported by higher production costs and tighter supply. Overseas shipments were also disrupted after a Jamalco fire and Alcoa’s Alumar technical problems reduced output. With high ocean freight and limited supply, overseas buyers pulled forward purchases, lifting CIF-equivalent prices.

title: Nickel Prices Unlikely to Hit a New High for Lack of Fundamental Support _SMM
summary: SMM says nickel remains supported by tight NPI and nickel-ore supply and declining nickel briquette stocks, but falling ferrochrome and lower stainless-steel costs limit upside. NEV demand is uncertain due to chip shortages, so nickel prices are expected to be rangebound rather than make new highs. Weekly SHFE and LME ranges are given.

title: UAE's Emirates Global Aluminium posts strongest H1 profit; CEO talks IPO plans
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium reported its strongest H1 profit since reporting began, citing global demand and higher aluminium prices amid an economic recovery. Production was affected by upgrades and logistics constraints, but output remained substantial. The CEO hinted at potential IPO plans, alongside progress toward solar-powered aluminium production.

title: Aluminium industry stares at critical coal shortage
summary: Coal India has reduced coal and railway rakes for aluminium captive power plants, creating an acute coal crunch. Aluminium smelting is highly power-dependent; shortages or outages can freeze molten metal and shut plants for months. Imports are not feasible on short notice, likely tightening supply and supporting aluminium prices.

title: C3 Metals Identifies Significant Porphyry and Epithermal Copper-Gold Potential at the Bellas Gate Project, Jamaica
summary: C3 Metals reports a comprehensive review and recent field mapping at its Bellas Gate copper-gold project in Jamaica, highlighting multiple porphyry and epithermal targets with historical drill intersections of copper grades. The company plans to advance several targets toward drill testing in coming weeks, mainly supporting longer-term copper prospects.

title: Inside the latest Indigenous push to stop a massive copper mine
summary: Alaska Native groups and conservation organizations have secured a conservation deal that places a large portion of Pedro Bay Corp. land off-limits to industrial development, blocking routes needed for the Pebble open-pit copper/gold mine. The move is an immediate setback that could delay copper supply, supporting copper prices.

title: China Hongqiao : aluminium smelters meet to address 'irrational' price spike
summary: Chinese aluminium prices surged to a highest level since 2008 on Shanghai Futures and hit a 10-year peak on the LME amid smelter production curbs in key regions tied to power-grid constraints. CNIA smelters including Chinalco and Hongqiao met, saying there’s no obvious supply gap and they will improve efficiency and stabilise expectations.

title: EGA delivers "strongest-ever half-year financial performance" amid high demand for aluminium
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) reported its strongest half-year performance, with higher adjusted EBITDA and record output at its Al Taweelah alumina refinery. It ramped bauxite exports, commissioned more reduction cells, and is adding solar-powered aluminium production and a more efficient power block, amid high global aluminium demand.

title: SHFE Aluminium Soared Once Again to Record High amid Rumours of Further Output Cut _SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium surged to record highs as rumours and policy signals pointed to further output cuts and tighter dual control of energy consumption in regions such as Guangxi, alongside existing output controls in Xinjiang. Spot premiums stayed firm, national reserve releases looked insufficient, electricity pricing for aluminium tightened, and inventories remained low.

title: Cashed-up Forrest trumps BHP in nickel bidding war
summary: Andrew Forrest has raised his bid for Canadian nickel explorer Noront Resources, topping BHP’s $C325 million offer. Forrest also wants Noront to remain publicly listed instead of being absorbed by his Wyloo Metals. The heightened competition for nickel assets may modestly bolster expectations for nickel supply and support prices.

title: Sandfire dividend: copper miner cashes in on red-hot prices
summary: Sandfire Resources reported record profit and revenue and announced its biggest final dividend, attributing it to red-hot copper prices and higher earnings from its DeGrussa mine as it transitions into decline. The company also says it is positioned to build a new Botswana copper project as decarbonisation boosts demand.

title: Fathom Nickel Inc.: Fathom Reports Second Quarter Results and Share Listing on the OTC
summary: Fathom Nickel reports Q2 results and timelines for an exploration program at its Albert Lake Project, including survey work and planned drilling. The company targets high-grade nickel sulfide and notes the deposit is recognized for nickel and copper. The update is mainly sentiment-oriented with no direct supply or inventory impact mentioned.

title: Battery blitz: 'Twiggy' Forrest fights BHP for Canadian nickel miner
summary: Mining billionaire Andrew “Twiggy” Forrest’s Wyloo Metals seeks to outbid BHP for Canadian nickel explorer Noront, citing growing demand for electric-vehicle battery raw materials. Noront’s Ring of Fire assets and Wyloo’s higher offer keep attention on future nickel supply prospects, supporting near-term nickel sentiment.

title: China's Exports of Aluminium Plate/Sheet and Strip Up 11% MoM in July_SMM
summary: China’s aluminium plate/sheet and strip exports rose to 262,400 mt in July, up 11% MoM and 53% YoY, with higher shipments across key product codes and destinations. Domestic and overseas orders are described as abundant, though Henan’s late-July power curtailment and flooding may weigh on August exports.

title: Industrial Conference Held to Prevent Malicious Speculation and Irrational Price Hikes of Aluminium_SMM
summary: China’s Nonferrous Metals Industry Association held a video conference with major aluminium producers to prevent malicious speculation and irrational aluminium price hikes. Participants said off-season demand is stable, no obvious supply shortage exists, and firms will continue ensuring supply while managing higher environmental and production costs.

title: Aluminum Hits 10-Year High With Demand Roaring, Supply Squeezed
summary: Aluminum jumped to a 10-year high on the LME as demand surged and Chinese supply was squeezed by pollution rules, power consumption caps, and provincial production cuts. Tightening conditions, limited ability to ramp output, and rising orders supported the rally, lifting related base metals including copper and nickel.

title: Aluminum Hits 10-Year High as Demand Roars, China Supply Curbed
summary: Aluminium is said to hit a 10-year high as demand strengthens and China’s supply is being curtailed. The headline framing points to tighter market conditions and reinforcing buy-side momentum, suggesting aluminium prices face immediate upside pressure in coming days as supply constraints meet robust demand.

title: Pancontinental Resources Corporation: Pancon Intersects 25 Meters of 0.96 g/t Au and 0.2% Cu, Further Extending Gold-Copper Zone at Brewer
summary: Pancon reports new drilling results from its Brewer Gold & Copper Project, including copper-bearing intervals (up to ~0.21% Cu) and chalcopyrite-bornite mineralization. The company frames results as extending a gold-copper zone and potential porphyry copper prospects, using copper spot pricing for AuEq. No nickel or aluminium linkage or supply impact is stated.

title: Aluminium Bahrain marine facility upgraded
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) inaugurated upgrades to its marine jetty and alumina storage, enabling larger Panamax alumina vessels and higher annual alumina intake. The project supports post–reduction line 6 commissioning output, which increased overall production by more than 50%, potentially improving aluminium supply expectations.

title: China aluminum smelters meet to discuss 'irrational' price spike
summary: China’s top aluminium smelters, via CNIA, discussed an “irrational” aluminium price surge after Shanghai prices hit a 13-year high. The move follows production curbs in key smelting regions aimed at easing power-grid strain, sparking tight-supply fears. LME aluminium also hit a 10-year peak.

title: Aluminum hits 10-year high as demand roars, China supply curbed
summary: The article says aluminum has hit a 10-year high as demand “roars” while China supply is being curtailed. The combination implies tighter near-term availability and stronger consumption support, which should continue to put upward pressure on aluminium prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Sanatana Resources Inc.: Sanatana Commences Exploration at its Newly Optioned Oweegee Dome Porphyry Copper-Gold Project in British Columbia's Golden Triangle
summary: Sanatana Resources announced it has begun exploration at its optioned Oweegee Dome Cu-Au porphyry project in British Columbia. The work includes 3-D IP/RES geophysics, mapping, and sampling that confirm copper-bearing mineralization at the Delta and Malloy zones and define drill targets for the 2022 field season.

title: Times of Zambia   |  'Benguela Railway will ease copper haulage between Zambia, DRC'
summary: Angola’s Benguela Railway opening to private firms is expected to ease copper haulage from Zambia to the DRC. By improving regional transport and enabling exports through the Port of Lobito, the route could facilitate quicker copper shipments to global markets.

title: Aluminum hits 10-year high as demand roars, China supply is curbed
summary: Aluminium prices rose to a 10-year high as demand strengthened sharply while Chinese supply was curtailed. The combination of higher consumption and constrained near-term availability is expected to tighten the market and support upward price pressure in the coming days.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Drills 7.38% Nickel Within 4.25 Metres Grading 3.19% Nickel
summary: Gungnir Resources reports initial drill assay results from Sweden’s Lappvattnet nickel deposit, including 3.19% Ni over 4.25 metres and a peak of 7.38% Ni. Drilling continues with additional holes and pending assays. The release is positive for nickel exploration, but does not indicate near-term supply changes.

title: LME launches sustainability register for aluminium and other metals
summary: The LME announced the LMEpassport, a digital register to store sustainability credentials and quality information for metals trading, starting with energy-intensive aluminium. It includes ESG disclosures such as carbon footprint and launches a spot platform for lower-carbon aluminium. Producer access begins Oct. 1 and disclosure is initially voluntary.

title: Congo copper sales increase 10% in H1, cobalt up 15%
summary: Democratic Republic of Congo mines ministry said copper sales rose 10% in H1 2021 to 871,956 tonnes, with exports and local sales increasing, while cobalt sales climbed 15%. Congo is Africa’s top copper producer, so higher output/sales suggests improved near-term supply that may weigh on copper prices.

title: Interra Copper Completes Drill Program at Cathedral Area on Thane Property and Commences IP Surveys
summary: Interra Copper reported completion of its drilling program at the Thane Property, with additional holes at the Cathedral/Pinnacle zones. Early core logging described arsenic-associated mineralization and chalcopyrite-bearing breccia, consistent with a porphyry-style model. It also began IP and other surveys; assay results are pending.

title: Sanatana Commences Exploration at its Newly Optioned Oweegee Dome Porphyry Copper-Gold Project in British Columbia's Golden Triangle
summary: Sanatana Resources announced initial exploration at its Oweegee Dome Cu-Au porphyry project in British Columbia, including mapping, sampling, and starting a 3-D IP/RES survey to define 2022 drill targets at the Delta and Malloy zones. The release is exploration-stage with no near-term supply changes, limiting price impact.

title: Consumers will demand ethically sourced drinks cans, says aluminium expert
summary: An aluminium industry expert says consumers will increasingly demand ethically and low-carbon aluminium for products like drinks cans. EN+ Group’s chairman expects energy-driven onshoring and expanding low-carbon supply, noting that most current output in China uses coal. A recent EN+ deal with Ball supports the demand trend.

title: Aluminium prices lifted to 10-year high by China concerns
summary: Aluminium prices surged to a more-than-10-year high as China tightened energy consumption controls for smelters, particularly in Guangxi. Production caps—kept at 80% of recent output—signal reduced aluminium supply. With supportive demand and already tight inventories, benchmark aluminium rose sharply on the LME/Shanghai.

title: Aluminum Prices Hit Decade High Amid China's Drive To Cut Carbon Emissions
summary: Aluminum prices are reported to have climbed to a decade high as China accelerates efforts to cut carbon emissions. The policy drive likely affects near-term aluminium production and costs through regulatory/compliance requirements and emissions-driven constraints, supporting a bullish price outlook over the coming weeks.

title: Aluminum prices soar as supply worries mount
summary: Aluminum prices rose for a seventh day to near a decade high on the LME after Chinese power-and-emissions curbs prompted output cuts. Guangxi and Xinjiang are reported to reduce energy-intensive metals, including aluminum, raising fears of a supply shortfall as smelters pledge supply.

title: Copper Royalty Bill Clears Another Hurdle in Chile
summary: The piece’s headline says a copper royalty bill is clearing further hurdles in Chile. Because Chile is a major driver of global copper supply, progress on royalty changes can shift market expectations toward higher costs and weaker investment incentives, generally pressuring copper prices in the near term.
