title: Chilean Environmental Court approves Environmental Compliance Plan for Caserones Copper Mine_SMM
summary: Chile’s environmental court approved JX Nippon’s Caserones copper mine compliance plan after SMA charged it in 2019 over alleged overpumping and tailings leaks. The $42 million plan includes returning desalinated water to the Copiapo River to address drought. Farmers challenged scope, but the court upheld SMA’s approach.

title: BHP holds its ground as Andrew Forrest fights for Canadian nickel miner
summary: BHP is defending its $C325 million bid for Canadian nickel explorer Noront Resources against a competing approach from Andrew Forrest’s Wyloo Metals. The contest underscores investor efforts to lock in nickel exposure tied to the Ring of Fire, ahead of expected EV-driven demand growth.

title: Benjamin Cooper Acquires Securities of Class 1 Nickel &
summary: Benjamin Cooper acquired 7,940,908 common shares of Class 1 Nickel & Technologies Limited at a deemed price of $0.56 per share. The shares relate to a mineral-claims acquisition by the company. The announcement concerns ownership changes and does not describe any near-term changes to nickel supply or production.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Operations and Financing Updates Corrected Version
summary: Nevada Copper reported completion of a key underground development crossing at its Pumpkin Hollow project, enabling faster development and scheduled backfilling, plus ongoing installation of ventilation fans. Financing updates include a KfW waiver extension and added liquidity via an amended promissory note to support the mine ramp-up.

title: Copper falls as Chinese factory activity slows
summary: Copper prices fell as China’s factory activity data pointed to slowing demand. August factory activity entered contraction due to COVID-19 containment, supply bottlenecks and high input costs. With China consuming roughly half of global copper, the weaker outlook weighed on both LME and Shanghai copper futures.

title: Aluminum Steadies on Warning Rally Not Supported by Fundamentals
summary: Aluminum pulled back after hitting its highest level since 2011. China Nonferrous Metals Association warned the rally isn’t supported by tight fundamentals and that high prices may quickly reduce demand via substitutions. It stressed supply isn’t in a notable shortfall and pointed to softer China data and broader policy tightening risks.

title: China's Exports of Aluminium Wheel Up 28.15% MoM in July_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Customs data cited by SMM show China’s aluminium wheel exports rose to 84,800 mt in July, up 28.15% month-on-month. Key destinations included the US and Japan, where shipments increased with improving downstream demand. Exports were expected to rise steadily into September’s peak season.

title: Murchison Minerals Ltd.: Murchison Confirms Multiple Highly-Prospective Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Targets at Its 100%-Owned HPM Project
summary: Murchison Minerals reports final assay results confirming near-surface nickel and copper mineralization at multiple targets (Syrah and 4048) within its HPM project in Quebec, with high NiEq/CuEq grab sample grades. The company plans additional prospecting and an upcoming ~3,500 m drilling program to test further mineralization.

title: Copper falls from two-week highs as factory activity slows
summary: Copper prices dropped more than 2% as global manufacturing slowed, with China reporting contraction for the first time in nearly 1.5 years. China’s state reserves also released 150,000 tonnes via auctions to curb prices. LME copper, aluminum and nickel were all lower in trading despite nickel’s stronger cash premium.

title: High Court of Namibia Interdicts the Ministry of Mines to Grant Any Mineral Licences Over Haib Copper Licence In Namibia
summary: Namibia’s High Court interdicts the Ministry of Mines from granting mineral licences over the Haib Copper project area until a court review of the denied EPL renewal is finalized. The company says work was halted after non-renewal. A further hearing is scheduled for Sept. 16.

title: Vedanta says keen to open dialogue with Zambia's ZCCM; reiterates commitment to invest USD 1.5 bn in Konkola Copper Mines
summary: Vedanta said it wants to open dialogue with Zambia’s ZCCM and reiterated its commitment to invest $1.5bn in Konkola Copper Mines, including payments to local suppliers and funding for ESG and community projects. The comments follow a partial final arbitral award involving disputes with ZCCM and Zambia.

title: Prices Pulled Back Slightly, Secondary Aluminium Prices Stood Firm_SMM
summary: SMM reports that primary aluminium (A00) prices fell slightly to 21,160 yuan/mt, while secondary aluminium prices were unchanged and remained supported by high production costs. Imported aluminium ingot availability tightened, and silicon stayed strong. Die-casting demand was rigid but plants reduced output due to losses.

title: Nobel Resources Provides Next Phase Diamond Drilling Plan, Algarrobo Copper-Gold Project, Chile and Announces Marketed Offering and Concurrent Non-Brokered Private Placement
summary: Nobel Resources announced a 10,000–12,500 meter diamond drilling program starting September 10, 2021 at its Algarrobo copper-gold (IOCG) project in Chile. The company targets multiple geophysical anomalies associated with near-surface copper mineralization, alongside a marketed offering and private placement to fund exploration.

title: China battles with aluminium's decarbonisation paradox: Andy Home
summary: Aluminium prices surged on the ShFE and LME as China’s decarbonisation drive runs into power constraints. Smelters face curtailments from energy-efficiency rules, drought-hit hydro supply, and production cuts in provinces like Xinjiang. Inventories fell and China increased primary imports, tightening supply and supporting higher prices.

title: Norden Crown Completes Phase I Airborne Magnetic Geophysics at the Burfjord Copper-Gold Project, Norway
summary: Norden Crown completed Phase I (~400 line km) of UAV airborne magnetic geophysics over its Burfjord copper-gold project in Norway and plans Phase II in coming weeks. The results aim to refine and prioritize drill targets, building on prior high-grade copper intercepts from earlier drilling. Exploration continues via a Boliden-funded option.

title: Aluminum Prices Hit 10-Year High As China Looks To Cut Emissions
summary: Aluminum prices jumped to a 10-year high on the LME as China’s government and regional authorities tighten energy-consumption and emissions controls on energy-intensive smelters. Reuters cites production curbs and capacity limits in Guangxi and spillover from Yunnan, alongside firm demand, keeping supply worries elevated.

title: Sheriff: copper theft, damage reported at rural Mower County wind turbines
summary: Mower County authorities report multiple incidents of copper theft and damage to EDF Renewable Services wind turbines. Five turbines were damaged and copper wire stolen, with eight additional turbines damaged. Estimated damage for eight turbines is about $38,000, and high-voltage conditions make wire removal dangerous. Police request public help identifying vehicles.

title: Chile needs $150 bln to boost green copper output, minister says
summary: Chile’s mining minister said the country needs about $150 billion in investment to nearly double copper output by 2050, supported by a new mining blueprint aimed at boosting traceability, reducing water use and shaping future royalties. Chile’s target depends on investment approvals for 49 projects.

title: Negotiations over major copper mine contract kick off in Panama
summary: Panama has begun talks with First Quantum’s local unit to renegotiate the contract for the Cobre Panama copper mine, aiming for higher royalties and stronger environmental conditions. The government indicates a “completely new” deal and possible operator change if no agreement is reached, creating near-term uncertainty for copper supply.

title: Aluminium hits more than 10-year high as supply worries grow
summary: Aluminium jumped to a 10+ year high as traders priced in rising supply risk. Concerns intensified as several Indian power plants neared coal exhaustion, threatening energy input for primary smelters. China’s smelting output curbs also supported tightness fears, while the State Reserve released a modest batch of ingots.

title: Chilean Minister of Mining: $150 billion needed to increase Green Copper production_SMM
summary: Chile’s mining minister said about $150 billion is needed for a blueprint to expand “green copper” production, aiming for record output targets and requiring large project approvals and investment. The plan targets environmental measures and traceability, with current projects and royalties/regulatory constraints influencing investor expectations for copper supply.

title: Aluminum Ingot Social Inventory Declined 5,000 mt in the Week Ended September 2_SMM
summary: SMM reported that China’s aluminum ingot social inventory fell by 5,000 mt week-on-week to 749,000 mt as declines in Shanghai, Wuxi and Gongyi outweighed a small rise in Nanhai tied to poor demand. The market will watch downstream consumption and incoming supplies at consumption hubs.

title: Aluminium hits 10-year high as supply fears grow
summary: Aluminium prices hit a 10-year high as investors worry that China production restrictions will tighten supply. Analysts cite over 2 million tonnes of annual capacity shut this year amid electricity/pollution limits and potential further curbs. LME inventories are drawing down and alumina prices have surged, reinforcing bullish expectations.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Positive Initial Drill Results from Its Recently Acquired Punitaqui Copper Mine in Chile
summary: Battery Mineral Resources announced encouraging initial assays from drilling at its Punitaqui copper-gold mine in Chile, including copper grades up to 2.06% over 9m (and other intercepts). Three drills are active and the company expects resumption of copper production mid-2022, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventory Increased by 14,600 mt in the Week Ended September 2_SMM
summary: SMM reports China domestic aluminium billet inventories rose to 139,000 mt on Sept 2, up 14,600 mt (+11.7%) from a week earlier. The increase was driven by strong arrivals and weaker downstream demand as extrusion firms cut purchases amid poor orders and peak aluminium prices, with expectations for further inventory growth next week.

title: Gramercy alumina refinery in US to restart this week after surviving Hurricane Ida
summary: Gramercy alumina refinery in the US is set to restart this week after surviving Hurricane Ida. The restart suggests alumina supply disruption is being unwound, which can reduce near-term aluminium feedstock tightness fears and support expectations for steadier aluminium availability over the coming days.

title: Maiden Drill Program Intersects 147m of Disseminated Nickel Sulfide at the New Ban Khoa Prospect
summary: Blackstone Minerals reported assay results from its maiden drilling at the Ban Khoa disseminated sulfide prospect within the Ta Khoa nickel–copper–PGE project in northern Vietnam. Highlights included 147m of disseminated nickel sulfide and potential to extend operations and complement nearby mining, supporting optimism for nickel and copper resources.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Positive Initial Drill Results from Its Recently Acquired Punitaqui Copper Mine in Chile
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reports positive initial drill core assays from the Punitaqui complex in Chile, including intercepts such as 9m at 2.06% copper and other zones grading above 1% copper. Punitaqui is slated for production resumption, and these results may support near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Sber, Gazprombank to provide $2.7 bln loan to Russian Copper Company
summary: Sber, Gazprombank and the Russian Copper Company signed a $2.7 bln syndicated loan to fund the Malmyzhskoe copper deposit development in Russia. The project is expected to increase Russian copper concentrate output by nearly 30%, supporting regional economic growth and boosting future copper supply expectations.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Completes Final Closing on the Royalty Acquisition on the Caserones Copper-Molybdenum Mine in Northern Chile
summary: EMX Royalty Corp. completed the final closing to acquire an additional interest in an NSR royalty on the Caserones copper-molybdenum mine in northern Chile. The transaction is for US$34.1 million cash and increases EMX’s royalty cash flow tied to copper production, but it does not cite operational or market changes.

title: Copper edges higher on weak dollar, U.S. jobs report eyed
summary: Copper prices edged higher as the dollar weakened and markets looked ahead to U.S. non-farm payrolls, seen as guiding Fed taper timing. Aluminium was virtually flat near a decade high on tight-supply fears, while nickel was slightly lower. The jobs data and currency move supported near-term copper demand sentiment.

title: Aluminum Prices Hit Fresh Decade High As China Pledges More Support For Ailing Economy
summary: Aluminum prices are reported to have reached a fresh decade high as China pledged more support for its ailing economy. The market implication is improved near-term growth and industrial activity expectations, which can lift demand forecasts and strengthen aluminum price momentum in the coming days.

title: Nickel Inventory in Bonded Zone Declined amid Wider Import Profits_SMM
summary: SMM reports pure nickel bonded-zone inventories fell by over 1,400 mt as tight domestic spot supply raised the SHFE/LME nickel price ratio. Higher import profits encouraged traders to pull nickel from bonded stocks, with the SHFE/LME contango shifting toward backwardation. Import premiums peaked around $350/mt; more cargoes are expected next week.

title: CHILE: Copper strike ends as key bill advances in senate
summary: The article headline says Chile’s copper strike has ended as a key bill advances in the Senate. A strike ending typically improves near-term mine operations and reduces supply risk, which can weigh on copper prices in the coming days as markets recalibrate disruption expectations.

title: Nickel Rock Issues An Update On Its Exploration Program -Nickel Properties In British Columbia
summary: Nickel Rock Resources reported completion of phase 2 exploration on its British Columbia nickel claims, including soil and rock sampling and on-site pXRF readings showing elevated nickel values. The company plans additional trenching, assays, and survey work to meet its 2021 flow-through commitments, targeting awaruite mineralization.

title: Chilean copper output falls 0.02% y-o-y in July - Cochilco
summary: Cochilco data cited by the article show Chilean copper output fell 0.02% year-on-year in July. As Chile is a key driver of global supply expectations, the small decline can modestly pressure pricing lower, though the change is minimal and likely limits immediate market movement.

title: Copper boosted by declining dollar after weak U.S jobs data
summary: Copper climbed 0.6% on the LME after weak U.S. jobs data pushed the dollar down, boosting optimism that stimulus tapering may be more gradual. Copper support also came from falling visible inventories. The article notes aluminium up 1% and nickel up 1.5% in the same risk-on, softer-dollar move.

title: Peru's copper production falls in July but grows in first 7 months
summary: Peru’s copper output fell in July but remains higher over the first seven months of the year. The decline in the latest month can reduce near-term mine supply expectations for the market, potentially pressuring copper prices in the short run, even though year-to-date production is still growing.

title: Aranjin Resources Ltd: Aranjin Resources Announces Closing of Acquisition of Sharga Copper Project
summary: Aranjin Resources said it closed the acquisition of the Sharga copper project in Mongolia, paying US$1.5 million and issuing shares, financed via a convertible debenture. The Sharga technical report cites copper assay intersections and outlines early-phase exploration surveys and drilling plans.

title: Copper boosted by declining dollar after weak USjobs data
summary: Copper prices climbed as the dollar fell following weak U.S. jobs data. The weaker currency and improved sentiment suggested optimism for a more gradual stimulus taper. Benchmark LME copper was reported up about 0.6% to $9,439 per tonne by 1600 GMT, indicating near-term bullish pressure.

title: Gold gains as US jobs data ease taper woes; nickel, aluminum lead base rally
summary: US jobs data showed slower hiring, easing worries about Fed stimulus tapering and pushing the US dollar lower, which supported base-metal prices. Nickel led gains, while copper rose and aluminium advanced to a 10-year high. Aluminium’s rally was linked to constrained Chinese supply from electricity-saving measures.

title: Gold gains as US jobs data ease taper woes; nickel, aluminum lead base rally
summary: US non-farm payrolls rose less than forecast, easing concerns about earlier Fed tapering and pushing the US dollar lower. The weaker dollar lifted investor demand and helped base metals rally, with aluminium up on constrained Chinese supply under electricity-saving measures. Copper and nickel also rose on the day.

title: Mutinous Guinea military unit seizes power and suspends the constitution
summary: Guinea’s military seized power and suspended the constitution, raising security and supply-risk concerns for bauxite shipments. As Guinea is a major source of bauxite for alumina and aluminium, the event could disrupt production and shipments. Analysts cited note potential near-term speculative pressure on aluminium and stronger exposure for alumina.

title: Africa resources: Guinea military unit seizes power, suspends constitution
summary: Guinea’s military seized power and suspended the constitution, imposing a curfew. As a key source of raw material for aluminium, the instability increases near-term risks of bauxite supply and transport disruptions, which can lead to tighter expected aluminium availability and price weakness over coming days.

title: Lumina Copper reaches deal to end strike at Chile's Caserones mine
summary: Lumina Copper agreed with workers at Chile’s Caserones mine on a three-year contract, ending an almost month-long strike that began in early August. The deal followed mediation and wage negotiations. Caserones produced about 127,000 tons of copper in 2020, making the strike an immediate local supply risk.

title: Aluminum Surges as Guinea Coup Attempt Fuels Supply Concerns
summary: The piece highlights that aluminium prices are surging as a coup attempt in Guinea raises supply concerns. The market implication is greater risk to bauxite shipments and aluminium feedstock availability, which can lift near-term aluminium price expectations over the coming days.

title: Aluminum Jumps as Guinea Coup Attempt Fuels Supply Concerns
summary: Aluminum prices are rising as fears grow that an attempted coup in Guinea could disrupt bauxite and related aluminium supply chains. The market is repricing near-term supply risk, which increases expected tightness in aluminium availability and supports upward price pressure over the coming days.

title: Bauxite Supply to be Affected by Political Turmoil in Guinea_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Guinea’s political crisis, including border closures and detention of top officials, raises concerns about bauxite supply disruption. Guinea is China’s biggest bauxite source, and the article notes higher freight and CIF Guinea ore prices. Expectation is that rising bauxite costs could lift aluminium-related pricing soon.

title: Aluminium prices hit over 10-year peak on Guinea bauxite worry
summary: Aluminium prices surged to a 10+ year peak as fears grew after a coup in Guinea, the world’s largest bauxite supplier used to make aluminium. Reports of borders being closed and government dissolved heightened supply-disruption risk, lifting Shanghai and LME aluminium contracts sharply on Monday.

title: JV Article: Battery Mineral Resources acquires Punitaqui copper complex in Chile, drill program underway
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reports early drill core assay results at its newly acquired Punitaqui copper complex in Chile and outlines plans to revise resources and restart the mill around mid-2022. The program confirms copper grades near 2% in intersections, but current details suggest no immediate output change.

title: SHFE Aluminium to Continue to Outperform LME Aluminium on Supply Disruptions_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium is set to keep outperforming LME as power curtailment in China continues to disrupt aluminium operations. Xinjiang tightens capacity in operation and Guangxi has increased curtailment, raising supply risk. Slower consumption recovery at high prices should also slow social inventory decline.

title: News Roundup for Overseas Copper Markets_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM’s roundup highlights labor and contract developments for major overseas copper producers. Chile’s Andina strike was ended via new union agreements, and Codelco reached an early bargaining deal for El Teniente. Panama is negotiating royalties and environmental terms for First Quantum’s Cobre Panama, supporting expected supply stability.

title: Copper Cathode Output Down 1.3% MoM in Aug amid Tight Scrap Supply and Falling RCs_SMM
summary: SMM data show China copper cathode output fell 1.3% MoM in August to 819,400 mt, driven by power curtailment and some maintenance, while tighter domestic scrap supply and sharply lower RCs squeezed smelter profits. September output is forecast to rise 1.6% MoM, as maintenance winds down and some plants ramp up.

title: Aluminium prices hit over decade high as Guinea unrest sparks supply fears
summary: Aluminium surged to a decade high after unrest in Guinea, a major bauxite supplier to China, raised concerns about raw material shortages. With borders closed and government dissolved, traders reacted by bidding up ShFE and LME aluminium contracts, reflecting immediate supply-risk pricing. Copper and nickel moved less overall.

title: Reports of Guinea unrest send aluminium prices to 10-year high
summary: Reports of Guinea unrest, including a military seizure of power, raised concerns that bauxite shipments could be disrupted. As Guinea supplies a large share of global and Chinese bauxite imports, aluminium prices surged to 10-year highs in London and also jumped in China futures.

title: Guinea coup attempt sparks concerns for bauxite, iron ore miners
summary: A Guinea coup attempt has raised fears of disrupted bauxite exports from the West African nation, where major miners operate. Since bauxite is a key input for alumina and aluminium, the uncertainty supported a rally in aluminium prices to a 10-year high. Iron-ore project timelines were also questioned.

title: LIVE FUTURES 06/09: New highs for LME aluminium price on further supply issues, nickel down 1%
summary: The live futures update reports LME aluminium reaching new highs on further supply issues, indicating upward near-term pressure. It also states nickel is down around 1%, reflecting downward momentum. The surrounding context references aluminium supply disruption and inventory/shipping impacts, supporting near-term price sensitivity.

title: LIVE FUTURES 06/09: New highs for LME aluminium price on further supply issues, nickel down 1%
summary: Live futures updates show LME aluminium hitting new highs attributed to further supply issues, implying upward near-term pressure. In the same report, nickel is down about 1%, indicating downward price pressure. Overall effects are mixed between aluminium and nickel within the immediate trading horizon.

title: Press review: Can Guinea's coup impact Rusal and G7 invites Russia to discuss Afghanistan -  Press Review
summary: Vedomosti says Guinea’s coup has succeeded and President Alpha Conde is held by special forces, raising questions about UC Rusal’s Friguia bauxite/alumina and bauxite mines. However, experts argue Guinea has seen prior regime changes and that Rusal’s position is likely secure, implying limited net aluminium market impact.

title: Guinea turmoil pushes aluminum to 10-year high
summary: Aluminum prices jumped to a 10-year high after reports of a coup in Guinea, raising fears of interruption to bauxite supply used to make aluminium. Although no disruption is confirmed and Chalco says its Guinea project runs normally, traders cite tight supplies and higher risk.

title: Aluminum Prices Skyrocket on News of Guinea Coup
summary: Guinea’s military coup triggered sharp gains in aluminum prices because Guinea holds major bauxite reserves, a key input for aluminum. Reuters notes market worries about potential bauxite shipment shortages. October aluminum futures in Shanghai jumped over 3%, and LME aluminum rose as well, reflecting near-term supply risk fears.

title: China Hongqiao : aluminium smelters meet to discuss 'irrational' price spike
summary: China Hongqiao and other major Chinese aluminium smelters held a CNIA meeting after aluminium prices surged to multi-year highs on production curbs in smelting regions. The group said there was no obvious supply-demand gap and urged efforts to improve efficiency while stabilising costs and market expectations, aiming to contain further price spikes.

title: Chalco's Shares Rise Amid Aluminum Supply Concerns
summary: Chalco shares jumped as concerns grew that a coup in Guinea could disrupt global bauxite supply, a critical input for aluminum production. Guinea is the largest bauxite exporter. LME aluminum cash rose to the highest level since April 2011, with banks expecting further price gains amid tightening supply.

title: Aluminum prices hit decade high as coup threatens supplies from Guinea
summary: Aluminum reached a decade high after a coup in Guinea threatened bauxite supplies. Guinea is a major bauxite producer and supplies more than half of China’s imported bauxite. With borders shut and operations possibly halted for days to weeks, LME aluminium futures jumped about 1.8% on Monday.

title: Guinea bauxite prices rise on political turmoil, mines report no immediate impact
summary: Guinea’s coup sparked buyer concern about bauxite supply after a political upheaval in the world’s second-largest producer. Guinean bauxite prices for China hit their highest in 18 months, while aluminium prices extended to decade highs. Operators reported normal or stable output and minimal disruption, but market risk premium rose.

title: Aluminum price hits ten-year highs amid Guinea unrest
summary: Aluminium prices reportedly hit ten-year highs at about $2,761/t after reports of an attempted coup in Guinea. The unrest raises concerns over bauxite supply, with Guinea accounting for roughly 20% of global bauxite. Rusal’s Guinea operations and shares rose sharply on the perceived supply disruption risk.

title: Aluminum prices reach decade high after Guinea coup
summary: Aluminum prices jumped to a decade high after a military coup in Guinea, a major mineral producer. The report says the coup threatened to disrupt Guinea’s aluminium supply chain, lifting three-month LME forward contracts by 0.9% to $2,757/mt, the highest since early 2011.

title: Guinea Coup Sends Aluminum Prices Soaring To Fresh Decade Highs
summary: The headline reports that the coup in Guinea has driven spot aluminium prices sharply higher, reaching fresh decade highs. It suggests markets are reacting quickly to perceived disruptions or supply risks tied to Guinea’s role in the aluminium value chain, leading to strong upward pressure on prices.

title: Benchmark capesize bulker rates tumble amid political unrest in bauxite powerhouse Guinea
summary: Capesize bulker rates fell sharply as Guinea’s political unrest following an overthrow of President Alpha Conde disrupted bauxite-related shipping. With Guinea the world’s top bauxite producer, analysts say the turmoil is weighing on spot freight rates and raising near-term supply disruption concerns for aluminium feedstock.

title: Coup fuels aluminum supply concerns
summary: Guinea’s coup and ensuing political instability have sparked fears of bauxite shipment disruptions, the key feedstock for alumina and aluminium. Guinea supplies over half of Chinese bauxite imports. LME aluminium and China futures jumped to multi-year highs, reflecting near-term supply anxiety.

title: OZ Minerals halts Australia copper mine after fatality
summary: OZ Minerals halted operations at its Prominent Hill copper-gold mine in South Australia after a contractor was killed in an underground machinery incident. The stoppage follows police and Safework SA investigations. Prominent Hill is a major part of the company’s copper production, raising short-term supply concerns for copper.

title: Capesize rates tumble over bauxite amid Guinea's political unrest
summary: Capesize freight rates are falling as Guinea’s political unrest disrupts bauxite-related shipping. With Guinea the leading global bauxite producer, market participants expect logistics and delivery risk to weigh on near-term bauxite flows, which can translate into bearish pressure for aluminium pricing over coming days to weeks.

title: Miners keep digging as Guinea coup ignites aluminium prices
summary: Guinea’s miners were allowed to continue working despite curfews after a military coup. With Guinea supplying roughly half of China’s imported bauxite, market fears that the coup could disrupt bauxite shipments pushed aluminium (bauxite’s end product) to a 10-year high on Monday.

title: Aluminium jumps as Guinea coup attempt fuels supply concerns
summary: Aluminium surged to the highest level in more than a decade after Guinea’s coup attempt and political unrest raised fears about disruption to the supply of raw materials used to make aluminium. The article reports military action and suspended constitution, which heightened near-term supply concerns and supported prices.

title: Does the coup in Guinea have a short-term impact on aluminum prices? The local military has promised to guarantee the export of minerals._SMM
summary: Guinea’s coup initially pushed aluminium prices to a 10-year high, driven by higher bauxite delivery prices and market concerns about potential supply disruptions. The military later promised mining and exports would remain normal, and no major operational disruptions were reported, but the immediate aluminum reaction was still strongly upward.

title: Aluminium Prices Fluctuated Rangebound, Second Aluminium Prices Stabilised_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices are fluctuating within a range but with a mild upward tone: A00 rose to 21,710 yuan/mt. Secondary aluminium quotes were mostly stable, though some firms lifted prices. Thinner import arrivals and about 400 yuan/mt import profits coincide with higher silicon costs, sustaining upward room despite muted downstream demand.

title: Copper Mining Fight in Santa Ritas Continues After Feds Protect Jaguars / Public News Service
summary: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service rejected a request by Hudbay Minerals to remove critical-habitat protections for jaguars tied to the proposed Rosemont open-pit copper mine in Arizona. The decision continues opposition to mining in the Santa Rita Mountains, potentially delaying mine development and copper supply.

title: Chakana Reports Significant Intercepts at Soledad, Peru Including 46m of 5.64% Copper, 592.9 g/t Silver, and 0.36 g/t Gold Provides Update on Resource Drilling
summary: Chakana reported significant drilling intercepts at its Soledad property in Peru, including 46 meters grading 5.64% copper, along with elevated silver and gold values. The company provided an update on resource drilling. The news may improve the project’s long-term potential but is unlikely to materially move near-term copper prices.

title: Ubique Minerals Limited: Ubique Minerals Withdraw from Discussions to Acquire up to 80% of the Port Loko Bauxite Mine in Sierra Leone
summary: Ubique Minerals said it withdrew from non-binding discussions to earn in up to an 80% stake in Alumina Ventures’ Port Loko bauxite mine in Sierra Leone. The company cited AVL’s inability to meet due diligence and contractual requirements and is now discussing repayment terms for funds advanced.

title: Brigadier Gold Limited: Brigadier Expands Precious Metal Rich Copper Discovery at Picachos
summary: Brigadier Gold reported additional trench and channel sampling at its Picachos project, expanding a copper-silver discovery and adding high-grade gold-silver-copper results at the historic La Gloria mine. Reported copper assays (e.g., ~0.54% Cu over 0.72 m) may modestly bolster copper sentiment.

title: Camino Minerals Corp.: Camino Commences Discovery Drilling at the Los Chapitos Copper Project, Peru
summary: Camino Minerals begins discovery drilling at its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru after receiving permits. The company targets extensions of the Lidia Zone and reports early trace chalcopyrite and alteration assemblages, with historical chip samples up to 5.1% copper. It is an exploration update without near-term production impact.

title: Mincor secures loan as nickel arms race escalates
summary: Mincor, an early-stage Australian nickel explorer, secured a mix of equity and debt funding as capital flows into nickel stocks. The funding round included a $30 million equity purchase and a supportive $30 million debt facility from BNP Paribas. The story also references intensifying nickel deal competition among major players.

title: Aluminum Hovers at Decade High as Guinea Coup Fuels Supply Angst
summary: The article headline says aluminum is hovering near a decade high as a coup in Guinea fuels supply worries. Because Guinea is tied to the upstream aluminum supply chain, the disruption risk can tighten expectations for metal availability and lift prices in the near term.

title: Camino Commences Discovery Drilling at the Los Chapitos Copper Project, Peru
summary: Camino Corp. announced it has started core discovery drilling at its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, targeting mineralization extensions at the Lidia Zone. The company notes trace chalcopyrite and historic rock samples with up to 5.1% copper, suggesting potential for new copper discoveries.

title: High Grade Sampling Results at Karibib Copper and Gold Project
summary: Arcadia Minerals reported grab-sampling results from its Karibib Copper-Gold Project in Namibia, confirming mineralisation across a 20 km by 2 km structural feature. Skarn and vein samples returned average copper grades of about 4.32% and 1.94%, supporting upside to copper prospectivity. It remains exploration, not production.

title: How Does Malaysian Higher Aluminium Scrap Standards Affects China's Imports_SMM
summary: Malaysia postponed implementation of tighter standards for imported metal scrap to Oct 31. SMM expects limited impact overall but potential effects on imported aluminium scrap flows to China, especially Guangdong, where supply could dip until alternative Southeast Asian sources replace Malaysia. Some secondary producers may face higher export/input costs.

title: Material Matters: Cobalt, Nickel, Gold, Kaolin & HPA
summary: The piece discusses commodity outlooks, highlighting nickel: after a deficit earlier in 2021, Macquarie expects rapid Indonesia-led supply growth and reduced demand momentum to flip the market into substantial oversupply from 2022 onward (reducing the bullish supply-demand gap). This outlook is likely negative for nickel pricing.

title: Shanghai aluminum near 13-year high as Guinea unrest stokes supply woes
summary: Shanghai and LME aluminum prices stayed near 13-year highs as traders worried that unrest in Guinea—China’s biggest bauxite supplier—could disrupt supply. Tightness in China and shipping/logistics delays further supported rallies, with the October ShFE contract up about 0.8% and LME three-month slightly higher.

title: Interpretation of the Tightening of Malaysian Copper Scrap Import Standards and its Impact_SMM
summary: Malaysia extended by two months the grace period for tighter metal scrap import standards. The new rules require high copper content and cap impurities, effectively blocking low-grade copper scrap categories. If implemented after October 31, Malaysia’s secondary copper scrap exports to China may contract, tightening China’s scrap supply and supporting copper prices.

title: BTC trial launches in El Salvador & aluminum price spike on Guinea coup
summary: The segment reports that aluminium prices are soaring following a coup in Guinea. Guinea is a key West African supplier to the aluminium supply chain, so political disruption raises near-term concerns about bauxite and related logistics, tightening expectations for metal availability. Other topics mentioned do not directly affect metals.

title: China may turn to Australia for bauxite after Guinea coup stokes fears of supply disruptions: analysts
summary: Guinea’s coup raised fears of bauxite supply interruptions, prompting analysts to suggest China may source more bauxite from Australia. Although disruption hasn’t yet hit mining and transport, rising political and investment risks lifted aluminium prices on the LME to a 10-year high, reflecting tight supply expectations for alumina inputs.

title: SunSirs: Nickel Prices Fell Slightly on September 7 - Top Chemical News from ChemNet.
summary: SunSirs reports spot nickel edged down to 147,566.67 yuan/wet ton on Sept. 7. Macro factors such as a rising US dollar pressured metals, while epidemics disrupted automotive and downstream stainless output. Offsetting supports include tight nickel fundamentals, very low domestic inventories, and higher sea freight before the Philippines rainy season. Nickel likely fluctuates narrowly.

title: Vale Indonesia eyes 2026 completion for nickel HPAL plant
summary: Vale said it is amending environmental studies and aiming to obtain permits so construction of its Pomalaa, Indonesia nickel HPAL plant can start next year, targeting mechanical completion in 2026. The project is expected to produce 40,000 tonnes of mixed sulphide precipitate for EV batteries, supporting nickel supply expectations.

title: LIVE FUTURES 08/09: Base metals mixed on LME - aluminium close to $2,800/t; nickel up 1.7%
summary: Live LME base metals futures are mixed: aluminium closes around $2,800/t while nickel is up about 1.7%. The rest of the text focuses on Fastmarkets/Metal Bulletin platform and methodology publication corrections rather than new fundamentals, limiting the ability to infer a fresh directional price move.

title: LIVE FUTURES 08/09: Base metals mixed on LME - aluminium close to $2,800/t; nickel up 1.7%
summary: Fastmarkets’ live futures wrap says base metals were mixed on the LME. Nickel was up about 1.7%, while aluminium closed near $2,800/t. The remainder of the update focuses on procedural corrections to certain assessment methodologies and publication schedules rather than a new physical market catalyst.

title: C3 Metals Inc.: C3 Metals Intersects 235 metres of 0.67% Copper, 0.34 g/t Gold at Jasperoide
summary: C3 Metals reported assays from further drilling at its Jasperoide copper-gold project in southern Peru, including multiple long intercepts with copper grades and visible copper sulphides, plus continued drilling at the Cresta Verde Zone. Results suggest extensive skarn continuity, but they are exploratory.

title: SPC Nickel Corp.: SPC Nickel Announces Remaining Drill Results from its Janes Ni-Cu-PGM Project
summary: SPC Nickel announced final drill assay results from the Janes Ni-Cu-PGM Project, highlighting continuity of high-grade Trench 1 mineralization. The company reports Ni and Cu-bearing sulphides and notes potential for high-grade mineralization close to surface. As exploration news, it may modestly lift sentiment for nickel and copper.

title: Guinea-Bissau Plays a Crucial Role in Global Bauxite Supply Chain (By Miguel Artacho)
summary: The piece highlights Guinea’s (and Guinea-Bissau’s) role in bauxite supply, noting how disruption fears in Guinea have recently lifted LME three-month aluminium forward contracts by 1.3% to the highest in a decade. It attributes the concern to potential disturbance in aluminium’s supply chain from major bauxite exports.

title: Eagle Plains Resources Ltd: Eagle Plains' Partner Rockridge Resources Commences Exploration Program at the Knife Lake Copper Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Eagle Plains said its option partner Rockridge has started a helicopter-borne EM and magnetic geophysical survey at the Knife Lake Cu-Zn-Ag-Co VMS project in Saskatchewan. Prior drilling results show meaningful copper and other metals grades, but the release does not change resources, production, or near-term supply.

title: Soul Patts mulls copper spin out
summary: Washington H. Soul Pattinson is considering an IPO of its wholly owned Round Oak Metals unit, with Mick Wilkes as chairman. The subsidiary has operating mines in Western Australia and Queensland plus non-operating growth projects. The news signals copper asset monetization, but no immediate supply impact is specified.

title: C3 Metals Intersects 235 metres of 0.67% Copper, 0.34 g/t Gold at Jasperoide
summary: C3 Metals announced additional assay results from the Jasperoide copper-gold project in southern Peru, reporting broad, laterally extensive copper mineralization (including intervals with ~0.67% and higher Cu) and visible copper sulphide in newly drilled zones. The update is exploration-focused with no production change, so near-term copper price effects are likely limited.

title: Teck and BCIT Partner to Make Burnaby Campus Safer Using Antimicrobial Copper Patches
summary: Teck and BCIT announced installation of more than 1,000 Health Canada-certified antimicrobial copper patches on high-touch surfaces across five BCIT buildings. Funded through Teck’s Copper & Health program, the initiative highlights copper’s antibacterial properties based on prior trials on transit vehicles. Teck notes copper quantities are small and mainly for safety.

title: U.S. decision on Minnesota copper mine awaits Interior Dept opinion
summary: The U.S. Agriculture Secretary says a decision on approving Minnesota’s Twin Metals copper mine is pending a legal opinion from the Interior Department, which controls the underground deposit. Approval would add a potential major U.S. copper supply, while environmental opposition could delay or block the project.

title: More Massive Nickel Sulfide at Ban Chang
summary: Blackstone Minerals reports infill drilling at its Ban Chang massive sulfide target within the Ta Khoa nickel–copper–PGE project in Northern Vietnam, including 5.35m of massive sulfide nickel. The company says drilling supports a forthcoming maiden resource and mine-plan inputs, but no immediate production or trade disruption is stated.

title: Aluminum Hits 13-Year High as Supply Woes Build, Demand Booms
summary: The article headline reports that aluminium prices have reached a 13-year high as supply issues build and demand booms. The stated drivers—tightening availability and accelerating consumption—imply stronger near-term fundamentals and likely continued upward pressure on aluminium prices over coming days to weeks.

title: Aluminum Notches Fresh 13-Year High on Supply Woes, Demand Surge
summary: Aluminum prices hit fresh multi-year highs as markets tighten on supply risks. Guinea’s coup raises concerns over bauxite disruptions, while China’s power conservation and pollution crackdowns constrain aluminum production. The article also notes strong demand recovery and reports aluminum rallying around 1.6–2.1% in LME and Shanghai.

title: SEC takes aim at Coinbase & China's search for alternative aluminum — RT Boom Bust
summary: The segment highlights Guinea unrest affecting aluminium markets, implying potential supply disruption and heightened sourcing risk. It also points to China searching for alternative aluminium supply. These developments are likely to tighten expectations around near-term aluminium availability and support price momentum.

title: Aluminium hits 13-year peak on China and Guinea supply fears
summary: Aluminium prices surged to 13-year highs as China’s output curbs reduced stockpile availability and political turmoil in Guinea raised bauxite disruption risk. LME three-month aluminium rose up to 1.9% and ShFE contracts gained over 3%, with analysts forecasting a sizable global deficit this year.

title: The high price of copper forces air-conditioning manufacturers to switch to aluminum? But aluminum is also soaring at the moment._SMM
summary: Record-high copper prices are pushing air-conditioning makers (e.g., Daikin) to consider replacing some copper with aluminium to reduce costs, though timelines are longer-term. It also notes aluminium prices are rising even faster due to supply concerns in Guinea and China’s smelting constraints, offsetting any near-term aluminium demand boost.

title: The high price of copper forces air-conditioning manufacturers to switch to aluminum? But aluminum is also soaring at the moment._SMM
summary: Surging record copper prices are pushing air-conditioning makers (e.g., Daikin) to plan increased aluminum use in heat exchangers to cut costs. Yet LME aluminum is also rising sharply on Guinea-related supply concerns and China’s emission-reduction actions that strain energy-intensive smelting, creating offsetting price pressures.

title: Golden Lake Exploration Inc.: Golden Lake Samples Return Up to 9,920 g/t Silver in Grab Samples Returned From West Copperview Property Adjacent to Kodiak Copper Corp.'s MPD Property
summary: Golden Lake Exploration reported initial assays from grab samples at its West Copperview property near Kodiak’s MPD claims, including up to 0.95% copper and high silver values. The release is early-stage exploration with limited grab samples and pending soil results, implying no immediate copper market supply impact.

title: Guinea coup threatens to further inflate aluminium prices
summary: The article headline says the Guinea coup could further inflate aluminium prices. That suggests market concern over potential disruption or risk to aluminium-related supply in the near term, likely via interruptions to bauxite/inputs or logistics, creating an expectation of tighter availability and higher prices.

title: NorthWest Copper Announces New High-Grade Drill Results at
summary: NorthWest Copper reported assays from initial and expansion-confirmation drilling at its Kwanika project in British Columbia, highlighting consistently high-grade copper equivalent intervals (e.g., ~1%+ CuEq starting near bedrock surface). Management says results expand the near-surface high-grade footprint supporting an updated Q4 2021 resource estimate.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventories Up to 145,500 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium billet inventories in five consumption areas increased 6,500 mt to 145,500 mt (+4.7%) week-on-week, driven mainly by Foshan. South China arrivals exceeded deliveries, while downstream extrusion firms remained sluggish and avoided buying on high prices, suggesting inventories may rise further, pressuring aluminium prices.

title: SMM: Copper Cathode Inventory in Guangdong Kept Falling, and When Will it Come to an End?_SMM
summary: SMM says Guangdong copper cathode inventories have fallen for 10 sessions, dropping to around 21,400 mt, close to a multi-year low. Tightening supply (limited smelter restarts, lingering effects of power restrictions, constrained imports) plus strong downstream replenishment ahead of Mid-Autumn/National Day is expected to keep inventories declining until after National Day.

title: Copper Mountain Announces Continued Positive Drill Results at New Ingerbelle, Doubles Vertical Extent of Mineralization
summary: Copper Mountain Mining reported positive drill results from 18 holes at its New Ingerbelle copper-gold open pit, including long intercepts and doubled vertical extent of mineralization. The company plans to add two drill rigs and continue drilling to expand and potentially increase copper resources and reserves, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Copper's Long-Term Bullish Potential Remains
summary: The piece highlights aluminum strength driven by political unrest in Guinea, a major bauxite supplier, raising expectations of tighter supply and a larger deficit. For copper, it notes the market remains range-bound amid slowing growth momentum, weaker macro data, and reduced speculative positioning, keeping near-term upside limited.

title: Updated PEA Commences on the Cañariaco Norte Copper Project
summary: Candente Copper announces Ausenco has been awarded a contract to start an updated 12-week Preliminary Economic Assessment for its Cañariaco Norte copper project in Peru. The study will develop updated mining, process plant, and infrastructure concepts to improve project economics and cost competitiveness, potentially supporting copper market sentiment.

title: Aluminium prices reach decade high after Guinea coup
summary: Aluminium prices jumped to a decade high after Guinea’s president was detained in a coup. Analysts expect bauxite operations and export flows to be disrupted for days or weeks, tightening supply for China, the top aluminium producer. LME aluminium futures rose, reflecting immediate bullish market pressure.

title: EPA moves to block gold and copper Pebble Mine project in Alaska
summary: The EPA is moving to block the Pebble Mine project in Alaska, targeting a development that includes copper alongside gold. The decision raises risk to planned copper output, tightening market expectations for future supply and providing upward support to copper prices in the near term.

title: Goldman, Citi See Aluminum Rally Raging On as Bears Flag Caution
summary: The piece suggests Goldman and Citi see aluminium prices set for a continued rally, with bears flagging caution. While the excerpt doesn’t provide specific figures or drivers, the headline indicates a bullish re-rating of near-term aluminium outlook by major banks.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Dipped 700 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s major copper inventories fell 700 mt from Monday to 126,900 mt, driven mainly by declines in Shanghai and Guangdong. Shipments may not quickly lift warehouse stocks due to downstream routing, while smelter maintenance keeps arrivals weak. Inventories are expected to decline further ahead of Mid-Autumn Festival.

title: Copper Prices Dipped below Copper Scrap Prices, Raising Operating Rates at Copper Cathode Rods Plants by 3.06 Percentage Points in August_SMM
summary: SMM reports August operating rates for domestic copper cathode rod producers rose 3.06 percentage points MoM, despite weaker orders from Yangzhou lockdowns. The key driver was copper falling below scrap prices, improving the cathode-vs-scrap spread and encouraging downstream purchases and restocking of cathode rods, even as inventory willingness stayed low.

title: Shanghai nickel hits record high on low stocks, strong demand
summary: Nickel prices surged to record highs in Shanghai and a seven-year peak in London, driven by strong demand and dwindling inventories. It also reports aluminium hitting its highest since 2008 on China and Guinea supply worries, while copper rose on improving smelter output and byproduct returns, keeping sentiment firmly bullish.

title: RUSSIA-CHINA-GUINEA Conakry coup troubles Moscow and Beijing aluminum supplies
summary: Guinea’s coup d’état has raised concerns about disrupted bauxite output, a key feedstock for aluminium. The article says Russian and Chinese investors are heavily involved in Guinean mining, particularly linked to Rusal and Chinese Baowu. It frames the event as potentially unsettling aluminium supplies and therefore pressuring prices.

title: Shanghai nickel hits record high on low inventories, solid demand
summary: Nickel surged to record highs in Shanghai and above London’s seven-year peak as inventories dwindled and demand stayed strong, with refined nickel expected to remain in short supply in September. The same piece also highlights elevated prices in aluminium (supply worries in China and Guinea) and copper, reinforcing a broad bullish tone.

title: SMM Analysis of Four Important Drivers Behind Soaring Alumina Prices_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s alumina prices hit new highs, rising sharply into early September, driven by higher bauxite/coal/caustic soda costs, alumina output cuts, overseas outages, and firmer plant offers. It also links the move to aluminium strength, but elevated alumina input costs can pressure aluminium margins.

title: Commerce Ministry recommends anti-dumping duty on certain aluminium items from China
summary: India’s DGTR has recommended definitive anti-dumping duties on certain flat-rolled aluminium products imported from China, saying dumped imports have caused material injury to domestic producers. Proposed duties are USD 65/tonne and USD 449/tonne, with the finance ministry to take the final decision, potentially lifting aluminium prices.

title: Nickel prices hit 7-year highs as demand creates shortages
summary: Nickel prices surged to the highest level in more than seven years, topping $20,500/tonne (about $9 a pound). The rally is attributed to a supply shortfall as demand from stainless steel mills and EV battery makers rises while exchange-monitored stocks fall sharply, driving a market deficit.

title: Exports of Russian aluminum see tenfold surge in July
summary: Russian aluminum exports reportedly surged tenfold in July, reaching about $7.4bn and over three million tons. The piece notes export taxes on aluminum (and a tariff framework covering other non-ferrous metals). With China running deficits and Guinea bauxite risks, the incremental Russian supply likely adds near-term pressure on aluminum prices.

title: SC aluminum smelter, adding jobs for first time since 2015, sets goal at full production
summary: Century Aluminum’s Mount Holly, S.C. smelter is ramping back after lower power costs, targeting 75% capacity now and 100% later. Repairs are bringing idled electrolytic pots back online. The company also notes supportive conditions: aluminum near 10-year highs, driven by China power/pollution constraints and solid end demand.

title: Aluminum industry frets over supply snarls
summary: Aluminum prices have surged to a 13-year high as supply snarls persist, including shipping bottlenecks, China’s production curbs, worker shortages, and limited trucking capacity. Producers and traders at a North American conference expect tight availability to last, with contract delays and uncertain Russia export taxes adding upside risk to prices.

title: Rio and BHP's Arizona copper mine hits new hurdle
summary: US legislators passed an amendment that adds the Save Oak Flat Act to a Biden spending package, creating fresh doubt over Rio Tinto and BHP’s planned Arizona copper mine. The proposed legislative hurdle raises the risk of delays or cancellation, weakening near-term copper supply expectations and weighing on prices.

title: North Korea says it will continue to fight for the Pebble copper and gold project._SMM
summary: North Korea says it will continue backing the Pebble copper-and-gold project as U.S. policy and court actions evolve over environmental veto authority affecting Bristol Bay. The dispute centers on mining licensing and discharge protections. The project could expand domestic copper supply, but timing uncertainty limits short-term price impact.

title: Aluminum Powers Toward $3,000 as Supply Snarl Supercharges Rally
summary: Aluminum hit $3,000/ton in London for the first time in 13 years as supply snarls intensify. China’s Yunnan province plans production curbs for energy intensity goals, while EU smelters face record carbon and power costs. Rising demand adds momentum, pushing prices sharply higher in both regions.

title: Copper Inventories in Major Trading Markets Down 3,700 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM says copper social inventories in China’s major trading markets fell 3,700 mt to 123,200 mt over the weekend, led by declines in Shanghai and Guangdong. Downstream quickly consumed imports, and SMM expects domestic inventories to likely fall further this week on restocking demand before the Mid-Autumn Festival, absent higher imports.

title: China's Jiangxi Copper to develop Afghanistan copper mine when situation allows
summary: Jiangxi Copper and MCC said they are monitoring Afghanistan after Taliban control and will proceed with the Mes Aynak copper mine once conditions allow; substantial construction has not started. Mes Aynak is estimated to hold 11.08 million tonnes of copper, with Jiangxi holding 25%. Near-term output impact is unclear.

title: Aluminium price hits $3,000 a tonne on tight supply
summary: The article headline says aluminium prices have hit $3,000 per tonne as tight supply tightens availability in the near term. This implies prompt market support from constrained inventories/production capacity, increasing the likelihood of further upward price pressure over coming days.

title: China's Jiangxi Copper to develop Afghanistan copper mine when situation allows | The Asahi Shimbun: Breaking News, Japan News and Analysis
summary: Jiangxi Copper and MCC say they are monitoring Afghanistan after the Taliban takeover and will proceed with the Mes Aynak copper mine only when conditions allow. The mine has large estimated copper reserves, but construction is not yet substantial. Jiangxi links benefits to current high copper prices, not new immediate supply.

title: LME aluminium hits $3,000 for first time since 2008
summary: LME benchmark aluminium rose to $3,000/tonne for the first time since 2008, up around 1% on Monday, as China’s smelters face output limits from power shortages and environmental rules. Guinea-related bauxite project delays add supply risk, with analysts estimating over 1 million tonnes disrupted this year.

title: China's Yunnan imposes output curbs on aluminium, steel, cement makers
summary: Yunnan province in southwest China ordered hydropower-powered “green” aluminium smelters to run at no higher than August output for Sept–Dec amid drought-linked power shortages. It also maintained broader energy-intensity curbs. The supply cut adds to existing capacity shutdowns, supporting aluminium price strength.

title: Copper Prices to Fluctuate Rangebound This Week, Upward Room for Spot Premiums to be Limited_SMM
summary: SMM expects copper to remain rangebound this week. LME copper bounced after a USD-driven dip, supported by macro liquidity and less restrictive ECB stance, while upcoming US CPI/retail sales are watched. Fundamentals remain mixed: tighter scrap supply due to smelter inspections, but large late-September imports from LME warehouses weigh spot quotes.

title: Aluminum Hits $3,000 for First Time in 13 Years on Supply Snarl
summary: Aluminium hit $3,000/ton in London for the first time in 13 years as supply risks intensify. Production curbs in China’s Yunnan smelters and record-high EU carbon and power costs are cited, alongside expectations of lingering logistical disruptions. The market has surged sharply over recent weeks.

title: LME aluminum hits $3,000 for first time since 2008
summary: LME aluminium rose above $3,000/tonne for the first time since 2008, driven by concerns about near-term supply. Yunnan ordered green aluminium smelters to keep September–December output no higher than August. Analysts also pointed to Chinese power and environmental limits and Guinea political turmoil threatening bauxite project timelines.

title: USA Market Wrap - Commodity wrap on September 13: Crude oil, aluminium futures rise; agri pack struggles
summary: The market wrap reports that in commodity trading on September 13, crude oil and aluminium futures rose on demand, while nickel experienced notable selling. No specific catalysts such as inventory changes, production disruptions, or policy moves are cited, limiting conviction about follow-through beyond the immediate price action.

title: Aluminium breaks $3,000 on supply concerns, equities mixed
summary: Aluminium rose above $3,000/tonne for the first time in 13 years as investors priced tighter supply conditions. The move was linked to concerns over bauxite disruption from a coup in Guinea and low Chinese output. Broader markets were pressured by record US inflation and trade worries involving China.

title: Energy leads stock gains; aluminum at 13-Year high
summary: The provided market wrap mentions that energy leads stock gains and specifically notes aluminium is trading at a 13-year high. While no detailed driver is included in the excerpt, the reference to aluminium reaching multi-year levels points to bullish near-term pricing pressure for the metal.

title: Aluminum hits US$3,000 for first time in 13 years on supply snarl
summary: Aluminium prices reportedly hit US$3,000 for the first time in 13 years as a supply snarl tightens near-term availability. The move suggests traders expect less aluminium to reach the market soon, supporting higher prices over the following days as supply constraints dominate.

title: SMM Evening Comments (Sep 13): Shanghai Nonferrous Metals Closed with Mixed Performance, with Aluminium Leading the Gains_SMM
summary: SMM reports mixed Shanghai nonferrous closes, but aluminium led gains (+4.38%) amid rumours/notice of tighter Yunnan output and energy-driven curbs in other provinces. Copper also rose (+2.52%) with falling inventories and tight scrap. Nickel fell (-2.24%) as supply-demand signals conflicted.

title: China copper giant monitoring Afghanistan situation to resume mining work
summary: Jiangxi Copper says it and MCC are monitoring Afghanistan’s situation and will push forward with the Mes Aynak copper mine when possible, after instability prevented substantial construction. The mine holds large copper reserves and the company notes recent high copper prices, supporting expectations for sustained strength.

title: Horizonte Minerals obtains financing approval for Brazil nickel project
summary: Horizonte Minerals reports it has obtained financing approval for a nickel project in Brazil. While this supports the project’s progression and could influence longer-dated nickel supply expectations, the provided information is limited and does not clearly indicate near-term production changes. Overall impact on nickel prices is likely negligible.

title: Nickel Prices Continue To Rise | OilPrice.com
summary: The piece argues nickel prices have swung from earlier oversupply to a bullish demand story. It cites low SHFE inventory, falling LME stocks, strong physical demand and rising imports, plus constrained refined supply and backwardation. It also notes speculators and arbitrage drawing metal toward China.

title: Cruz Battery Metals Corp.: Cruz Drills Broad Zone of Anomalous Silver-Copper Mineralization at the Hector Cobalt-Silver Property in Cobalt, Ontario
summary: Cruz Battery Metals reported three diamond drill holes at its Hector cobalt-silver property, including a broad silver-copper zone with assay ranges over tens of metres and additional cobalt-copper intervals. Nickel is mentioned only in the analytical scope, with no nickel results provided, limiting near-term price relevance.

title: Soaring aluminium hits $3,000 for first time in 13 years
summary: Aluminium futures topped $3,000/t for the first time in 13 years as China— the world’s biggest producer— imposed output restrictions. The tighter supply outlook drove a rapid rally, with prices up about 50% year-to-date and nearly 15% in three weeks, alongside increased speculative inflows.

title: Is Aluminium Pivoting Towards A Structural Bull Market?
summary: The article argues aluminium is moving toward a structural bull market. It points to power-related curtailments of Chinese smelting, disruptions at Alcoa’s Alumar refinery and Jamaica’s Jamalco, and heightened Guinea bauxite risk. Multiple brokers forecast major 2021 deficits, higher aluminium and alumina prices, and persistence into 2022.

title: Aluminum Tops $3,000 For First Time Since 2008 On Supply Woes
summary: The report highlights that aluminium spot prices have risen above $3,000 for the first time since 2008, linking the rally to worsening supply conditions. Tighter availability is expected to underpin near-term demand for physical material and support further upside in aluminium prices over coming days.

title: China's Tight Supply of Copper Scrap to be Further Intensified by Malaysia's Import Restrictions_SMM
summary: Malaysia extended a grace period for stricter copper scrap import standards until Oct 31, requiring at least 94.75% metal content. This blocks lower-grade Category Seven and some Category Six scrap from entering Malaysia. With limited substitution sources, scrap supply available for China tightens further, likely supporting firmer copper prices.

title: Rob McEwen: Keep the Faith — Buy Gold, Silver and Maybe Copper
summary: Rob McEwen discusses inflation concerns and expects stronger prices in gold and silver, but he also turns bullish on copper. He references McEwen Copper’s vehicle and a US$80 million financing tied to the Los Azules copper property, suggesting improving outlook and potential upward sentiment for copper.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX to Receive Initial Royalty Payment from the Caserones Copper-Molybdenum Mine in Northern Chile
summary: EMX Royalty Corp. said it expects an initial quarterly after-tax royalty payment of about US$974,000 from its 0.418% net smelter return interest in Chile’s Caserones copper-molybdenum mine. The payment is based on Q2 distributions for copper and molybdenum production, reflecting royalty cash flow.

title: Yunnan Tightens Aluminum Production Curbs in Green Push
summary: Yunnan province ordered local aluminum producers to slash output about 30% and further cap average monthly production from September to December below August levels amid energy-use and emissions controls. Power curbs and earlier reductions have already lowered utilization, implying additional near-term supply restraint and affecting aluminum prices.

title: US Copper Corp.: US Copper Provides Update on Superior Drill Program
summary: US Copper reports that evacuation orders from the Dixie Fire are being lifted, but access to its Moonlight-Superior copper property remains restricted. Although the drill rig wasn’t damaged, the drill contractor is moving off-site, power was interrupted, and drilling is unlikely to resume fully this season, delaying assay progress.

title: China Company Reportedly Hoping to Revive Stalled Plans to Mine Vast Afghan Copper Deposit
summary: Jiangxi Copper and MCC are reportedly working to revive stalled development of Afghanistan’s Mes Aynak, a large high-grade copper deposit, by negotiating amid Taliban rule. The project remains constrained by security instability and lack of substantial construction, but efforts to restart mining improve forward copper supply expectations.

title: Latin Metals Discovers Additional Copper Mineralization at Lacsha Project, Peru
summary: Latin Metals reports additional rock chip sampling results from its Lacsha project in Peru, highlighting broad copper and molybdenum mineralization (e.g., 72m at 0.2% Cu) and expansion of the mineralized footprint across Lacsha North and Lacsha South. The update is exploration-stage and not tied to production.

title: Aluminium hits decade high after supply disruptions
summary: Aluminium surged to a decade high on the LME, driven by industry-wide supply disruptions. A coup in Guinea, China’s production curbs, and electricity rationing in hydropower-reliant Yunnan are cited. Chinese smelters urged market stabilization and analysts raised aluminium targets, suggesting continued bullish price momentum.

title: Cyprium Metals Ltd (ASX:CYM) Nifty Copper Project Drilling ...
summary: Cyprium Metals reports ongoing drilling at its Nifty Copper Project in Western Australia, including eastern limb RC drilling, metallurgical diamond holes, and assessment of waste dump material for heap leach restart. It also starts infill and extension drilling at the nearby Maroochydore project. First assay results are expected soon.

title: World's Top Copper Supplier Trims Price Forecast as China Slows
summary: The article’s headline says the world’s top copper supplier reduced its copper price forecast as China slows. That points to softer near-term demand expectations from the main end-market, which typically pressures copper prices downward over the following days as market sentiment adjusts.

title: Chile's Cochilco revises copper price estimate downwards
summary: Chile’s Cochilco revised its copper price estimate downwards. The downward revision can signal weaker expected copper pricing for the upcoming period, potentially reducing near-term support for copper futures as investors adjust expectations around supply-demand balance and realized copper revenues.

title: Prince George aluminum maker plans $102 million expansion in county
summary: Service Center Metals, an aluminum products maker in Prince George County, plans a $101.7 million expansion with two new plants: an aluminum extrusion plant and a compact remelt facility. The company says the move will increase capacity due to growing demand, creating 94 jobs. Construction timing was not announced.

title: Mealtop shareholder of Kosdaq listed Melfas signed with DR Congo to supply Cobalt & Copper, valued at US$1.52B over 3yrs
summary: Mealtop, via a local partner in the Democratic Republic of Congo, signed contracts to supply finished copper (and cobalt) to buyers over three years. The release highlights EV-driven demand and claims early fulfillment starting in late 2021, suggesting improved near-term availability expectations for copper.

title: China Aug aluminum output falls for 4th month as supply cuts mount
summary: China’s August primary aluminium output fell for a fourth straight month to the lowest in over a year, as smelters faced power-usage limits and production restrictions in major hubs. Xinjiang ordered 10% output cuts across five smelters for August–December, keeping aluminium supply tight.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Drills 21.65 Metres of 1.09% Nickel at Lappvattnet
summary: Gungnir Resources reports new drill assays expanding near-surface nickel mineralization at its Lappvattnet project in Sweden, including 1.09% Ni over 21.65 metres in hole LAP21-02. The release updates the drill program and resources but provides no production or shipment changes, limiting short-term price impact.

title: Where Does the Increment of Copper Cathode Come from in Q1-Q3 2021?_SMM
summary: China’s copper cathode output rose in Jan–Aug 2021, mainly from blister copper tied to higher concentrate demand. In the second half, copper scrap supply tightened as high prices increased scrap consumption, while imports were limited by pandemic port controls. Next four months depend on restricted anode and scrap imports.

title: Why some benchmark aluminum prices have soared to a record
summary: Aluminum benchmark prices have surged to records in the U.S. Midwest and hit a 13-year high on the LME. The jump is linked to disruptions to global supply, including COVID-related slowdowns, elevated transportation costs, U.S. import restrictions, and labor shortages, tightening availability and boosting prices.

title: Three Valley Copper Initiates Exploration Drilling Program
summary: Three Valley Copper announced the start of 2021 near-mine exploration drilling on its Minera Tres Valles property in Chile, targeting high-potential copper occurrences between existing Don Gabriel and Papomono deposits. The first phase plans about 6,000–8,000 meters of drilling, aiming to define new near-surface copper mineralization.

title: Aluminum prices soar in new construction headache
summary: Aluminum prices are reported to have surged 47% this year, reaching $2,907/tonne on the LME three-month offer, raising construction material costs and project pricing. The article links higher aluminum (and other inputs like copper) to increased builder expenses and reduced confidence, but does not suggest near-term relief.

title: Industry Watch | tight supply overlaps demand peak season analysts: aluminum prices or high upside_SMM
summary: Aluminum prices rose more than 10% in September as analysts point to tight electrolytic aluminum supply under power/"double control" limits and stricter autumn-winter production curbs. Political turmoil in Guinea raised bauxite supply concerns. Spot inventories fell ahead of the “Golden Nine Silver Ten” demand peak, supporting higher prices.

title: Universal copper : mobilizes drill rig and field crew to poplar project
summary: Universal Copper announced that it has mobilized drill rigs and geological staff for a planned 3,000-metre 2021 drilling program at its Poplar copper project in British Columbia. The company aims to expand mineralization and higher-grade limits, citing prior resource growth and expecting value gains if copper prices strengthen.

title: Will there be an oversupply of copper? Chile, the world's largest copper producer, issued an early warning._SMM
summary: Chile’s Cochilco lowered its copper price forecasts for this year and next, warning of a possible oversupply as global growth slows and stimulus is phased out. It expects supply to grow faster than demand. The end of a BHP Billiton labor shutdown in Chile may add supply. Investors are split on the outlook.

title: FTSE avoids big drop as oil and copper prices rise
summary: European indexes were mostly down, but the FTSE 100 avoided a bigger fall as oil and commodity prices rose. The article notes gains for mining companies such as Antofagasta and Glencore that benefited from higher copper prices, implying near-term bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Nickel Ore Imports Up 7.2% MoM in July, Philippine Shipments Continued to Increase in August_SMM
summary: China’s nickel ore imports rose in July, with Philippines shipments up sharply and overall volumes staying high into August. While the wet season and pandemic conditions may slightly reduce August offloading, typhoons could delay September cargoes and wet-season effects are expected to worsen later.

title: Azure Minerals: Nickel sulphide hits with both grade and length
summary: Azure Minerals says drilling at its Andover project in Western Australia intersected nickel sulphide with both higher grade and longer mineralised intervals, describing the results as the highest grades yet. The update also references nickel-copper drill numbers, supporting modest upside sentiment for both nickel and copper markets.

title: NDRC: To Keep Launching Copper, Aluminium, Zinc as National Reserves to the Market_SMM
summary: China’s NDRC said the State Food and Material Reserves Bureau released a third batch of national reserves (starting Sept 1) including copper and aluminium, totaling 150,000 mt for copper, aluminium and zinc, with 420,000 mt accumulated across batches. Authorities will continue releasing reserves to stabilize prices and move them back to a reasonable range.

title: Aluminium rises on talks of fresh output curbs in China
summary: Aluminium prices rose as talks in China about fresh production/output curbs heightened concerns about supply disruption. LME and Shanghai aluminium contracts gained, supported by news that a major Chinese producer faces a 50% September output reduction under energy consumption controls. China’s output also fell for a fourth straight month.

title: TCs for Imported Copper Concentrate Up $7.45/mt MoM in Aug, But the Weekly Increase Sarply Slowed Down_SMM
summary: SMM reports August imported copper concentrate TCs rose to $58.55/mt, but weekly gains slowed as spot TCs moved above $60. While labor negotiations, strikes, and Peru logistics disruptions add uncertainty, expected mine output and smelting restart/support improve supply-demand for buyers. Copper prices remained rangebound.

title: NDRC: To Keep Launching Copper, Aluminium, Zinc as National Reserves to the Market_SMM
summary: China’s NDRC said the State Food and Material Reserves Bureau launched a third batch of national reserves, including copper and aluminium (plus zinc), totaling 150,000 mt, and plans further reserve sales. Officials aim to ensure supply and curb high prices, implying near-term downward pressure on copper and aluminium.

title: Hind Copper OFS 2021, Hindustan Copper Offer For Sale Price, Hind Copper Share Price, Hind Copper News
summary: India’s government will sell up to 10% of its stake in Hindustan Copper via an offer-for-sale over two days, raising about Rs 1,120 crore. The filing sets a specific sale price and includes a greenshoe option. The article is about equity divestment, not copper supply or demand changes.

title: Shanghai aluminum rises on supply fears and high coal prices
summary: Shanghai aluminum rose on supply fears in China’s key aluminum regions as power consumption restrictions force output cuts and heighten disruption risk. Surging thermal coal prices lifted energy costs for coal-fired smelting. Despite some mixed moves in other metals, the market’s focus remained on tightening aluminum supply.

title: EU to Suspend Planned Tariffs on Chinese Aluminium, Lobby Group Says
summary: The EU is expected to impose duties on Chinese aluminium from October but may suspend them for nine months, following an investigation into aluminium flat-rolled products. Provisional duties were previously set in 2021. The tariff stance is likely to shift near-term European aluminium pricing and import economics.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventories Up to 148,800 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported aluminium billet stocks in five major consumption areas rose to 148,800 mt, up 3,300 mt week-on-week, driven by higher arrivals in Foshan and Wuxi. Downstream activity remains wait-and-see, with sluggish orders and news of off-peak production amid power rationing, implying weaker billet demand ahead and bearish pricing pressure.

title: Power Rationing May Strengthen in Guizhou and Guangxi, Over 4.4 Million Mt Annual Aluminium Production Capacity to Be Affected_SMM
summary: SMM reports notices tightening orderly power usage in Guizhou, affecting 4.4 million mt of alumina capacity and all five aluminium plants, and renewed reports of stronger restrictions in Guangxi. News cites potential cuts of 35% for aluminium plants and 70% for alumina plants, implying lower near-term output.

title: Copper drifts lower as focus turns to U.S. Fed meeting
summary: Copper fell 2% as markets focused on the upcoming U.S. Fed meeting for signals on stimulus tapering, a macro driver that can pressure metals. The article also cites China’s plan to release copper and other metals from state reserves. Aluminium softened amid China supply issues and higher LME inventories.

title: BeMetals Corp.: BeMetals Extends Option Agreement for High-Grade South Mountain Zinc-Silver-Gold-Copper Project in Idaho
summary: BeMetals extended an option agreement to allow further surface drilling at the South Mountain polymetallic (zinc-silver-gold-copper) project in Idaho.
