title: Brazil's Vale resumes production at nickel mine
summary: Vale resumed production at its nickel mine in Brazil, signaling a potential normalization of supply after disruption. Such restarts can quickly shift expectations for near-term nickel availability, influencing prices depending on how much output was lost and whether inventories or shipping schedules were tightened during downtime.

title: Playfair Mining Ltd.: Drill Moving to Second Target at Playfair's RKV Copper Project, Norway
summary: Playfair Mining reports successful drilling at its RKV copper project in Norway, moving from the Rødalen target to a second target at Storboren. Four short holes intersected sulphide-bearing amphibolite and strong MMI copper anomalies, suggesting potential copper mineralization. Samples are pending analysis; no production or concrete supply impact is announced.

title: 'Patience could run out': Mongolia warns Rio Tinto over copper mine
summary: Mongolia’s Justice Minister warned Rio Tinto that patience may run out unless it makes progress on the Oyu Tolgoi copper mine. The government cited delays and cost blowouts, and said it was surprised by Rio’s response to an independent July report disputing reasons for a two-year schedule slip and $1.45 billion overrun.

title: The Heavy Rain in Shanxi Has Caused Bauxite Mines to Stop Production, Affecting Alumina Plants_SMM
summary: Heavy rain in Shanxi has shut central open-pit bauxite mines and cut alumina factory output to about half, with some plants facing <10 days of ore inventory and transport disruptions for raw materials. A production line at Xinfa is paused. Alumina prices in China rise and overseas supply remains tight, supporting aluminium prices.

title: The Highest Tender Price of the Four Batch of Government Stockpiles of Aluminium Ingots over 22,000 yuan/mt_SMM
summary: Bids for government stockpile aluminium ingots began Oct 9. The highest tender prices rose across regions, with the spread versus east China spot narrowing to 389–543 yuan/mt. Baotou tender peaked at 22,087 yuan/mt and Maanshan at 22,241 yuan/mt, against 22,630 yuan/mt spot.

title: SMM Exclusive: Distribution of Chinese Copper Downstream Processing Companies Affected by Electricity Shortage and Dual Control of Energy Consumption in 2021_SMM
summary: SMM says electricity shortages and energy consumption controls in several Chinese provinces have forced many copper downstream processors (rods, cables, enamelled wire, sheets/strips) to suspend or limit output for days in September–October. With sizable share of national copper production affected, copper cathode demand is hit.

title: Copper Prices Dip As The Energy Crunch Sparks Demand Doubts
summary: Copper benchmark prices fell as the Fed moved toward tapering and rate hikes boosted the U.S. dollar, pressuring copper. China’s power crisis restricted production and manufacturing, weakening factory activity, while Evergrande-related demand concerns persisted. LME three-month and Chinese cash prices declined, reflecting bearish sentiment.

title: Dutch aluminum producer Aldel suspends production due to electricity price problem_SMM
summary: Dutch primary aluminium producer Aldel will suspend production at its Delvzel plant due to high electricity costs. Management says output is shutting down and will stop from Monday until at least early 2022. Aldel is the Netherlands’ only primary producer, with 110,000 tons/year primary capacity, implying reduced supply.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Added 1,400 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s mainstream copper inventory rose 1,400 mt to 112,400 mt from Oct 8 to Oct 11, mainly due to higher cathode stocks and imported arrivals, especially in Shanghai. Downstream shipments stayed sluggish on power rationing in parts of the region. A weekly drawdown is expected later.

title: Aluminum price surpasses $3,000 per tonne at LME first since July 2008
summary: Aluminum prices on the LME surpassed $3,000 per tonne for the first time since July 2008. Trading data show the metal at about $3,014.5/tonne and $3,010/tonne shortly after, up roughly 1.5% versus the prior close. Related Russian shares in En+ and Rusal rose.

title: Copper falls on firmer dollar as Fed tapering looms
summary: Copper fell 0.3% on the LME as a firmer dollar strengthened on expectations the Fed will begin tapering stimulus in November. Separately, the article cites aluminium production halts from high electricity prices and a nickel shutdown due to higher energy costs, but LME nickel and aluminium were up on the day.

title: Glencore : Nickel jumps to 2-week high as power shortage fuels supply fears
summary: Nickel prices rose to a two-week high as power shortages and higher electricity costs in China and Europe raised supply fears. Nickel inventories fell on the LME and ShFE, while a ferro-nickel producer shut output and smelters faced possible curtailments. Higher energy costs were also cited for aluminium production cuts.

title: Valor unearths widespread copper in Peru
summary: Valor Resources reported widespread high-grade copper sampling at its Picha (Peru) copper-silver project, including channel results up to 35.6m averaging 1.3% Cu and a 13.39% Cu grab sample at Maricate. The news may be sentiment-supportive for copper, but it is exploration-stage and not near-term supply-relevant.

title: China's Aluminium Output Saw the First Drop in 21 Months in September_SMM
summary: SMM data shows China’s aluminium output declined to 3.11 million mt in September, the first drop in 21 months, due to power shortages and energy-consumption “dual control” in late September. With further capacity reductions expected in October and only limited recovery, output and liquid share stay soft and inventories may rise modestly.

title: China's Alumina Output Stood at 6.20 Million mt in September_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows China’s September alumina output at 6.20 million mt, including 5.99 million mt of metallurgical grade. Metallurgical grade output rose year-on-year, helped by higher prices and weaker impact from power rationing in Guangxi. October output is forecast at 6.08 million mt with surplus still present.

title: SMM Forecast: Copper Prices to Trend Lower in October amid Power Rationing_SMM
summary: SMM forecasts copper prices to trend lower in October as intensifying power rationing disrupts production and weakens downstream demand. The power cuts are expected to pressure the consumption side more, keep imports of secondary copper from rising sharply, and leave scrap demand stronger than supply.

title: Aluminium Tops $3,000 Per Tonne for First Time Since 2008
summary: Aluminium prices jumped above $3,000 a tonne for the first time since 2008, with three-month LME shipments up 2.24% to $3,035.50. The metal has risen for nine consecutive months, and the article links the earlier $3,000 push to China’s restrictions on aluminium output.

title: Habakkuk Trust Launches Documentary on Copper Cable Thefts – Kubatana.net
summary: Habakkuk Trust launched a documentary on copper cable thefts in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, linking the crime to recurring power cuts. It says thieves increasingly target both underground and overhead copper cables almost daily. Residents often replace stolen copper with aluminum cables due to shortages and the power utility’s limited capacity.

title: Codelco offers Europe physical copper at $128/T premium, sources say
summary: Codelco is offering Europe physical copper premiums of $128/tonne for 2022 versus $98 in 2021, the highest since 2015, seen as a market benchmark likely to be followed by others. Aurubis also set a high premium. Tightness is supported by deficit expectations from the ICSG.

title: Bam Bam Resources Corp.: Bam Bam Adds Second Drill at Majuba Hill Porphyry Copper Project
summary: Bam Bam Resources added a second drill rig at the Majuba Hill Porphyry Copper Project in Nevada to expand the drill footprint and test in-fill/expansion of oxide copper mineralization. Drilling targets a copper-gold zone, with ongoing results driving the expanded program, potentially supporting copper supply expectations.

title: Aluminium hits highest since 2008 as power shortages escalate
summary: Aluminium prices jumped to the highest since 2008 as escalating power shortages and higher energy/raw-material costs forced output cuts, especially in China. Production disruptions also hit other producers due to outages and soaring costs. Alumina prices surged, adding cost pressure, while analysts forecast a growing market deficit.

title: Vale Joins the International Copper Association
summary: Vale International S.A. was added as a member of the International Copper Association (ICA). The release frames the move around ESG and decarbonization efforts, with ICA working on a roadmap to decarbonize copper processes. No new production, supply, or demand shock is announced.

title: Global energy crisis piles pressure on aluminum supply
summary: A global energy crisis is said to be piling pressure on aluminum supply. Because aluminum smelting depends heavily on electricity and energy input, higher energy costs or reduced operating rates can quickly tighten availability. That usually lifts short-term market expectations for aluminum prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Codelco Raises Europe Copper Premium by 31% in Bullish Signal
summary: Codelco reportedly increased the Europe copper premium by 31%, a bullish signal for the regional physical market. A larger premium generally reflects tighter availability or stronger demand in Europe, which can raise expectations for near-term copper pricing. The move would likely support copper sentiment over the coming days.

title: Kosovo's NewCo Ferronikeli stops ferro-nickel production
summary: Kosovo’s NewCo Ferronikeli is forced to temporarily stop ferro-nickel production because European electricity prices have surged to record highs. Separately, the Netherlands’ primary aluminium producer Aldel has idled its Delfzijl plant amid an unhedged power-cost squeeze. Both shutdowns reduce near-term supply.

title: Tribes, Activists' Fight Against Proposed Minnesota Copper Mine Bolstered by Legal Victories
summary: Activists and the Fond du Lac Band won multiple federal and state rulings affecting PolyMet’s proposed NorthMet copper-nickel open-pit mine in Minnesota. EPA “may affect” findings and court decisions suspend permits and require further review, heightening delays and potential supply constraints for copper and nickel.

title: Copper bulls get an electric shock
summary: A global energy crisis is weighing on copper sentiment. Investors worry that power shortages and factory slowdowns will curb near-term demand, even as long-term bullish views persist. Rising natural gas and electricity costs could contribute to stagflation-like conditions, with demand weakening while input costs stay elevated.

title: Chile's Codelco copper production will exceed expectations despite the strike [LME WEEK]_SMM
summary: Codelco said copper production this year will be about 2% higher than previously estimated even after a strike cuts output at the Andina project. August production at Codelco fell year-on-year due to the strike. The firm cites strong cash flow and confidence in planned mine developments.

title: President of Antofagasta: temporary bottleneck drop increases Chilean Copper miners' costs_SMM
summary: Antofagasta’s CEO said global transport and energy bottlenecks have temporarily increased production costs for copper miners, including higher logistics and shipping/airfreight expenses. He expects energy and shipping costs to normalize as Chile’s seasonal demand changes, while maintaining that copper market fundamentals remain strong despite supply tightness.

title: Aluminum Retreats From 13-Year High as Stagflation Worries Mount
summary: Aluminum prices are pulling back from a 13-year high as worries about stagflation grow. The piece frames the move as a market reaction to macro-economic uncertainty, suggesting investors are scaling back expectations for near-term demand and price momentum in aluminium.

title: Newcrest expects production costs to fall and copper production to increase_SMM
summary: Newcrest said it expects production costs to halve over coming years and higher copper output from its Australian and Canadian mines, projecting a 37% rise to about 175,000 tonnes by the end of the decade. The firm’s gold-focused model includes copper as a by-product and signals growing exposure to green-energy demand.

title: Taseko Reports Significant Increase in Quarterly Copper Production
summary: Taseko said its Gibraltar Mine produced 34.5 million pounds of copper in Q3, up 29% from Q2, supported by improved grades and recoveries, and efficient processing of new ore during a transition into the Gibraltar pit. The company also links results to improved unit costs and financial performance.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Announces Positive Drill Results at Cameron Copper Project in Australia, Three Large Mineralized Zones Identified
summary: Copper Mountain Mining reported positive drill intercepts from 48 holes at its Cameron Copper Project in Australia, identifying multiple large mineralized zones and potential for a larger copper-gold system. The release supports longer-term resource potential but provides no immediate evidence of supply disruptions or production changes.

title: Surge Copper Intersects 495 metres of 0.54% CuEq including 126 metres of 0.85% CuEq  at West Seel and Previews Upcoming News Flow
summary: Surge Copper Corp. announced assay results from resource definition drilling at its Ootsa Property in British Columbia. The company reports a 495-metre intercept grading 0.54% CuEq, including 126 metres at 0.85% CuEq, and outlines progress and upcoming pending results, which may support copper sentiment.

title: Aluminium price hits 13-year high
summary: Aluminium jumped to a 13-year high on the LME as deepening energy stress raised smelting costs and squeezed output. The article links gains to aluminium’s heavy electricity needs, China’s cap on future capacity, and Guinea supply concerns for bauxite. Demand is also expected to rise with ‘green’ technologies.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Kamoa-Kakula's Phase 2 Expansion, Doubling Production to over 400,000 Tonnes of Copper per Year, Ahead of Schedule and Now on Track to Begin Full Operations in Q2 2022
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reports Kamoa-Kakula copper operations progressing ahead of schedule: Phase 2 concentrator construction is over 50% complete and expected to begin operations in Q2 2022, while Phase 1 throughput exceeds design and a second filter press produced a daily record 721 tonnes of copper concentrate.

title: GCC Non-Ferrous Metals Markets Report 2021 - Opportunity Assessment of the Aluminum and the Copper Value Chains, and Evaluation of Future Impact and Go-to-Market Strategies
summary: A GCC non-ferrous metals market outlook report links Vision 2030 to higher aluminum demand from construction, packaging and EV-related lightweighting, plus copper value-chain initiatives such as secondary smelting, recycling, and reduced cathode import dependence. The piece is mainly strategic and forecast-based, implying limited immediate price impact.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Transformative Balance Sheet
summary: Nevada Copper announced extensions to its KfW senior project facility and consolidation of shareholder loans, adding about US$41 million liquidity and deferring loan repayments to support ramp-up of its underground copper operations and progress toward open-pit and exploration milestones. Closing is subject to approvals and conditions precedent.

title: Kamoa-Kakula's Phase 2 Expansion, Doubling Production to over 400,000 Tonnes of Copper per Year, Ahead of Schedule and Now on Track to Begin Full Operations in Q2 2022
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says Kamoa-Kakula’s Phase 2 concentrator expansion is progressing ahead of schedule, targeting full operations in Q2 2022. Phase 1 throughput and a second filter press are exceeding design parameters, with record filtered concentrate output. The project aims to double copper output to over 400,000 tonnes annually.

title: Indonesia starts to build world's largest copper smelter
summary: Indonesia has begun construction of what President Joko Widodo calls the world’s largest copper smelter, with capacity to process 1.7 million tons of concentrate per year. Built by PT Freeport Indonesia, the project is part of Indonesia’s downstream push, with an investment of $3 billion and an initial copper metal output of about 480,000 tons annually.

title: Groundbreaking: President Joko Widodo kicks off construction of the world's largest copper smelter in JIIPE
summary: President Joko Widodo has kicked off construction of what is described as the world’s largest copper smelter in JIIPE. A new smelter project can signal increased future refined copper capacity, which may support copper prices through improved supply expectations, even if production gains are not immediate.

title: Pre-Feasibility Study Completed on Red Chris Block Cave Gold and Copper Mine
summary: Newcrest completed a pre-feasibility study for the Red Chris block cave gold and copper mine in Northern BC and approved moving to feasibility. The study estimates reserves of 2 million oz copper and projects about 80k tonnes of copper per year from 2028 onward, which can signal future supply despite the long ramp-up.

title: Canada Nickel reports positive results
summary: Canada Nickel says metallurgical performance at its Crawford project improved, delivering higher nickel recovery (62%, +19% vs prior) alongside better iron and cobalt recoveries. Management links nickel recovery gains to increased project value and continues feasibility work, though assay results are delayed. The news is supportive for nickel sentiment.

title: Tesla : Prony Resources says Tesla has agreed to a multi-year nickel purchasing deal
summary: Prony Resources, the nickel producer in New Caledonia previously acquired from Vale, said Tesla agreed to a multi-year nickel supply deal for battery material. Prony aims to raise output to about 44,000 tonnes by 2024. Tesla is Prony’s largest customer; negotiations were via Trafigura.

title: China Sept copper imports snap 5-month fall as delayed shipments arrive
summary: China’s September copper imports rose 3% month-on-month after five months of declines, as delayed cargoes cleared port congestion following eased COVID curbs. However, Q3 imports fell to a two-year low. Shanghai bonded refined inventories dropped sharply, and copper concentrate imports increased.

title: Prices of Aluminium Varieties Remained Firm amid Power Rationing and Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices stayed firm after Guinea’s early-September coup raised concerns about bauxite supply. Tight power from energy-consumption controls and higher coal prices constrained downstream production, while reported cuts/shutdowns in China and Guinea supported tight global supply expectations. SHFE aluminium surged to records and LME hit new highs.

title: Freeport begins construction of $3bn Indonesian copper smelter
summary: Freeport has started building a $3bn copper smelter in Gresik, Indonesia, targeting 600,000t/year of copper cathode and up to 1.7Mt/year of concentrate processing. The project, near existing operations, is scheduled to start in late 2023 or early 2024 and would shift value-added output to Indonesia.

title: The New Development Era of Secondary Aluminium under China's Carbon Strategy_SMM
summary: The article says China’s secondary aluminium output has grown to about 14 million mt (around 30% of global) and relies mainly on domestic scrap. It also forecasts secondary aluminium production rising and primary shrinking as policy and economic factors evolve, implying greater recycled supply over time.

title: Freeport Indonesia begins construction on $3bn copper smelter complex
summary: Freeport Indonesia began building a $3bn copper smelter and precious metals refinery in East Java with 1.7 million tonnes/year concentrate capacity, producing copper cathodes, pipes and wires. The project, in a Gresik industrial zone, is linked to Freeport’s Grasberg supply and targets commissioning in 2024, supporting copper downstream growth expectations.

title: Nobel Signs Option Agreement to Acquire La Salvadora Copper
summary: Nobel Resources announced it signed an option agreement to acquire 100% of the La Salvadora IOCG copper-gold project in Chile, including scheduled option payments and a future NSR royalty. The release highlights copper mineralized zones and adjacent operations, but provides no near-term production impact, limiting broader price effects.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Intersects 25.5 metres of 1.13% Ni, 0.61% Cu, Including 4.5 metres of 2.96% Ni, 1.66% Cu, and 1.5 metres of 4.17% Ni, 2.14% Cu at the Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project, NW Ontario.
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. reported additional drilling results at its 100% owned Kenbridge nickel-copper project in Ontario, including strong Ni grades over 25.5 metres (with associated copper) and additional zone intercepts. TDEM surveys support conductive zone continuity, guiding further drilling toward down-dip and along-strike extensions.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Intersects 25.5 metres of 1.13% Ni, 0.61% Cu, Including 4.5 metres of 2.96% Ni, 1.66% Cu, and 1.5 metres of 4.17% Ni, 2.14% Cu at the Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project, NW Ontario.
summary: Tartisan Nickel reported additional drilling results from its Kenbridge Ni-Cu project in Ontario, including 25.5 metres of 1.13% Ni with 0.61% Cu, plus higher-grade nickel-copper intervals. Interpretation is based on TDEM-conductive zones and supports ongoing down-dip/along-strike drilling, aiding sentiment for nickel and copper.

title: Norilsk Nickel endager BCL deal
summary: Norilsk says Botswana has not implemented an agreed settlement and the dispute over liquidation and sale of BCL’s assets remains in London arbitration. Observers warn PNRB’s plan to acquire and restart the Selebi nickel-copper-cobalt assets may fall through without a resolution, affecting near-term supply outlooks.

title: District Copper Corp: District Announces Fall Field Program at the Copper Keg Project, Kamloops Mining District
summary: District Copper announced a fall induced polarization geophysical survey over its Copper Keg project in British Columbia and completed a one-week mapping and geochemistry program. Historic interpretations suggest a buried porphyry copper system; grab samples showed copper values up to 124.5 ppm. It remains early exploration with limited immediate market impact.

title: 2 Copper Stocks to Buy on the Dip
summary: The article argues copper should rebound, pointing to declining LME inventories and a potential supply squeeze after copper fell on COVID-19 Delta-driven economic worries and weaker China output. It expects EV and renewable grid growth to raise demand, supporting a near-term rally in copper prices.

title: Fathom Nickel Inc.: Fathom Announces Preliminary Interpretation of 2021 Soil Geochemistry Results at the Albert Lake Property and Approval of DTC Eligibility for OTC Trading
summary: Fathom Nickel reported preliminary interpretation of 2021 soil geochemistry from its Albert Lake property, showing multiple anomalous Ni zones with associated Cu and other elements, and noted drilling is ongoing with assays pending. It also received DTC eligibility approval for OTC trading, mainly impacting investor access rather than metal fundamentals.

title: Bitterroot Resources Ltd.: Bitterroot Resources Intersects High Nickel Grades in Massive Sulphide Mineralization
summary: Bitterroot Resources reported assay results from two holes at its LM Project, stating massive and semi-massive sulphides are enriched in nickel and copper, with disseminated mineralization in one hole. The company continues drilling toward additional targets, but no near-term production or supply disruption is indicated.

title: New Caledonia's Prony to Supply Nickel to Tesla in Multi-Year Deal
summary: Prony Resources said Tesla agreed to buy about 42,000 tons of nickel in a multi-year deal, positioning Prony as a key supplier to the U.S. EV maker. Prony also plans to produce around 44,000 tons of nickel by 2024, doubling its expected 2021 output.

title: Boatbuilders could face big rise in aluminium costs
summary: The piece suggests marine boatbuilders could experience a large rise in aluminium costs while demand conditions improve in parts of Europe. Such a warning points to increasing aluminium input prices and near-term cost pressure, which is typically supportive for aluminium price expectations over the coming weeks.

title: Copper Production at Gibraltar Up, Expansion Continues
summary: Copper output at Taseko Mines’ Gibraltar facility near Williams Lake rose 29% this quarter to over 34 million pounds. The company has mobilized drilling to continue spring expansion and will investigate geophysical anomalies, while operations transition smoothly to the Gibraltar Pit. Management cites strong copper costs and $50M credit acquisition for the year ahead.

title: South32 buys $2.8b stake in Chilean copper mine
summary: South32 is buying a 45% stake in Chile’s Sierra Gorda copper mine for up to $2.05 billion (about $2.8 billion). Management says the mine’s reputation helped secure a “cheap” price. The deal expands South32’s copper exposure, but the article doesn’t mention immediate production changes.

title: SkyTEM Aerial Survey Confirms Prospective Nickel-Copper-PGE Targets at the Coates Project
summary: Charger Metals announced SkyTEM aerial survey results over its Coates Ni-Cu Au-PGE project near Perth, delineating 22 potential sulphide conductor targets and anomalous Ni-Cu-Au-PGE values near Target T1. The findings support forthcoming drilling, but no production impacts are described.

title: SkyTEM Aerial Survey Confirms Prospective Nickel-Copper-PGE Targets at the Coates Project
summary: Charger Metals reported SkyTEM helicopter EM survey results at the Coates Ni-Cu Au-PGE Project near Perth, delineating multiple sulphide-conductor targets, including strong Ni-Cu-Au-PGE anomalies at the northern end of target T1. The update supports drilling plans but does not indicate immediate production or supply changes.

title: Aluminium Social Inventories Rose 25,000 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China’s social aluminium inventories across eight consumption areas increased by 25,000 mt on the week to 887,000 mt as of Oct. 14. The rise was driven mainly by higher arrivals in Wuxi and Hainan versus the previous session, suggesting more near-term supply pressure.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventories Up 7,600 mt from Last Friday_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says aluminium billet stocks in five major consumption areas rose 7,400 mt to 184,400 mt versus the previous week, with most regions increasing and only Huzhou declining. Downstream extruders remain wait-and-see as orders have not improved much, despite easing power rationing, and inventories may rise further next week.

title: LIVE FUTURES 14/10: LME zinc price at highest since 2007; copper cash/3-month spread in backwardation
summary: Metal market coverage highlights that the LME zinc has risen while focusing on copper and aluminium. Copper cash/3-month trading is described as being in backwardation, implying tighter prompt conditions. For aluminium, the text references supply curtailments and disrupted shipping (Strait of Hormuz) but suggests pricing moves have been limited.

title: Tesla Signed a Big Contract with Prony Resources to Buy over 42,000 mt of Nickel_SMM
summary: Prony Resources said Tesla signed a multi-year nickel supply agreement to purchase over 42,000 mt of nickel. Tesla is prioritizing nickel supply for batteries, alongside prior contracts. Prony also plans to expand output after Vale’s unit sale, while acknowledging future oversupply risk. LME nickel has risen ~20% over a year.

title: Indonesia builds copper smelter worth 3 billion USD | World
summary: Indonesia’s President attended the groundbreaking of PT Freeport Indonesia’s 3 billion USD copper smelter in Gresik, East Java. The project, backed by the government’s 51% stake, is planned for 1.7 million tonnes of annual copper capacity, potentially increasing domestic processing. Timing is construction-stage, limiting immediate price effects.

title: Chakana Copper Corp.: Chakana Reports 268m of 1.17 g/t Gold, 0.55% Copper and 19.2 g/t Silver (1.48% Cu-Eq) in Breccia Pipe 5 from Surface at Soledad, Peru
summary: Chakana Copper reported 14 resource definition drill holes at its Soledad Project in Peru’s Breccia Pipe 5, including copper-bearing intersections (e.g., 0.55% Cu and 1.17 g/t gold) and continued IP geophysical surveys. The update is early-stage and does not signal immediate production or supply changes.

title: Eagle Plains Resources Ltd: Eagle Plains' Partner Rockridge Resources Completes VTEM Geophysical Program at the Knife Lake Copper Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Rockridge completed a helicopter-borne VTEM Plus geophysical survey at the Knife Lake VMS project in Saskatchewan, targeting copper-bearing mineralization. The release summarizes prior drilling copper grades and notes planned follow-up work for future diamond drilling. It is a development-stage exploration update without any immediate production or trade effects.

title: Surging aluminium price squeezing processors' profits - Nanshan exec
summary: Chinese aluminium processors face margin pressure as aluminium prices rise more than 50% this year, helped by strong demand and output cuts from an energy crisis, flooding, and record electricity costs. Power curbs are expected to hurt power-intensive smelting. China’s aluminium reserve sales are too small to ease prices materially.

title: Tianshan Aluminum: Net profit in the First Three Quarters to Up 163.5%, the Average Price of Aluminium Ingots Up 35% YoY_SMM
summary: Tianshan Aluminum forecast Q1–Q3 net profit up 163.5% YoY, citing bullish market sentiment, strong demand for aluminium ingots, and tight supply. The report says aluminium prices increased further due to capacity limits and power rationing, with average ingot prices up about 35% YoY in Jan–Sep.

title: Bam Bam Resources Corp.: Bam Bam Announces Copper, Silver, and Gold from Soil Geochemistry Expands Targets at Majuba Hill Porphyry Copper Project in Nevada
summary: Bam Bam Resources reports expanded soil geochemical anomalies at its Majuba Hill project in Nevada, identifying larger copper/silver/gold target zones, including an extended DeSoto oxide copper/silver anomaly and a new copper-gold target. Core drilling is planned in late October, but no production or supply impacts are indicated.

title: Quebec Nickel Corp. - Exploration Update
summary: Quebec Nickel Corp. provided an update on exploration at its 100%-owned Ducros Ni-Cu-PGE property in Quebec. It staked additional claims, completed stripping and till sampling preparation, and expanded an airborne VTEM survey to identify new nickel targets, with potential follow-up work and drilling planned for later.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Punitaqui Drilling Update Continues to Deliver Encouraging Copper Results
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reported additional assay results from ongoing drilling at the Punitaqui project in Chile, highlighting multiple copper intercepts in the San Andres target. The company says results demonstrate continuity and grade and could add to copper ore sources as it aims for potential resumption of operations in 2022.

title: Sumitomo to exit Chilean copper project | News
summary: Sumitomo plans to sell its entire 45% stake in the Sierra Gorda copper mining project in Chile to a preferred purchaser. The deal is an ownership exit rather than an explicit production change, so it is unlikely to drive immediate copper supply expectations materially.

title: Copper prices setting up for record surge
summary: Bank of America technical analysis says copper is poised for record highs as traders rotate from oil into copper, with CME copper futures jumping and breaking key resistance. The article adds that contractors report copper material shortages and producer inflation, reinforcing bullish fundamentals despite some near-term oil correction signals.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Punitaqui Drilling Update Continues to Deliver Encouraging Copper Results
summary: Battery Mineral Resources announced additional drill-core assay results from the Punitaqui mine complex in Chile, including multiple copper intercepts with grades up to ~2%+ Cu over substantial intervals. The company says results support continuity and grade and may help resume operations and cash flow, which could be supportive for copper sentiment.

title: Alcoa Pays First Dividend Since 2016 Revamp as Aluminum Soars
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports Alcoa has paid its first dividend since 2016 after revamping, attributing the turnaround to surging aluminum prices. The message is that higher aluminum pricing has improved earnings and cash generation, reinforcing bullish sentiment toward the aluminum market near term.

title: Rusal (Rusal) plans to increase aluminum supply to China next year_SMM
summary: Rusal said it will raise aluminium sales to China in coming periods, including 300,000–400,000 tonnes in 2021 and more thereafter via expanded production. China’s smelting curbs have caused shortages and record imports, pushing prices higher. Planned additional supply and a continuing supply gap outlook influence near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: Rusal Plans to Supply More Aluminium to China in the Following Year_SMM
summary: Rusal plans to supply 300,000–400,000 mt of aluminium to China in 2021, similar to 2020, and plans significantly higher sales next year. China’s import needs rose after COVID demand recovery. Despite a market shortage lifting prices, Rusal’s production ramp and smelter commissioning add supply expectations.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 7,200 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says mainstream Chinese copper inventories fell 7,200 mt from Oct 11 to 105,200 mt, led by declines in Guangdong, Shanghai, and Jiangsu. The drop reflects fewer imported copper arrivals and tighter domestic smelter output. While Tianjin rose due to processing curbs, overall supply remains tight and could stay so next week.

title: South32 to acquire Sumitomo's stake in Chilean copper mine for $2bn
summary: South32 agreed to buy a 45% indirect stake in Chile’s Sierra Gorda copper mine from Sumitomo for up to $2.05bn, with payments tied to copper production thresholds and prices. The mine is large and long-life, but the deal is primarily ownership transfer, not immediate production change.

title: Prioritise aluminium industry for immediate coal supply to avert collateral damage
summary: Aluminium industry bodies in India urge Coal India to immediately resume continuous domestic coal supply. They report critically low coal stocks at aluminium plants and warn that any power outage could force shutdowns taking at least 12 months to recover. The supply crisis would damage operational continuity of major capacity.

summary: Indigenous advocates seek to stop a proposed copper mine at Oak Flat in Arizona through federal court action. summary: The article highlights Granite Creek Copper’s Carmacks project in Yukon, citing a copper resource and ongoing drilling aimed at expanding and upgrading reserves. It claims the world is short of copper due to green-energy needs and suggests prices will rise, making the project more valuable.

title: Rusal shares plummet 5% on Hong Kong Exchange as aluminum prices decline
summary: Rusal shares on Hong Kong’s exchange fell over 5% as world aluminum prices declined. The LME aluminum price dropped below $2,600/tonne (first since late August) to about $2,547/tonne by Friday morning, following a peak above $3,200 in October.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Surged 60,000 wmt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 60,000 wmt to 9.05 million wmt (71,000 mt Ni content) as of Nov 5, with the Guangxi port driving most of the increase. Despite a recent rise, nickel ore shipments may be ending with the monsoon season in the Philippines, so inventories are expected to fall.

title: Bam Bam Resources Corp.: Bam Bam Samples 0.89% Cu and 0.638 g/t Au at Majuba Copper Project
summary: Bam Bam Resources reported chip sampling results from the Majuba Hill Project in Nevada, with several samples returning above 0.2% copper and additional gold assays. The company is expanding and infilling known copper oxide mineralization via reverse circulation drilling. The release is exploratory and not a production update.

title: Aluminium Prices Plummeted as Russia Plans to Cancel Aluminium Export Tariffs_SMM
summary: Russia’s plan to cancel aluminium export tariffs for Rusal triggered a sharp sell-off: SHFE aluminium fell over 7% and LME aluminium about 5% overnight. The removal of a prior 15% tariff is expected to raise global supply, pushing down Yangshan and overseas spot premiums.

title: CEO of Peru's largest copper miner seeks 'common ground' after protests
summary: Antamina’s CEO in Peru held a town-hall after last week’s blockade forced the mine to suspend operations. He signaled a shift toward dialogue with rural protesters, and residents expect a formal agreement later Friday. The de-risking of near-term output disruption is supportive for short-term copper supply expectations.

title: Sherritt to boost output of nickel, cobalt in Cuba for EV battery demand
summary: Sherritt said it will boost production of battery-grade nickel at its Moa joint venture in Cuba by 15% to 20%, extending the mine’s life beyond 2040 to meet EV battery demand. It highlighted processing and U.S. embargo risks but expects construction/equipment orders and follow-up next quarter.

title: Tiwai Pt aluminium smelter: preliminary closure study expected this year
summary: New Zealand’s Environment Ministry expects a preliminary closure study for the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter by year-end. Cleanup and legal enforceability are uncertain, with Rio Tinto pledging removal of 200,000 tonnes of toxic waste and negotiating liabilities. The timeline and closure risk may influence short-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Peru: Copper production up 10.9% in Jan-Sep 2021 | News | ANDINA
summary: Peru’s Ministry of Energy and Mines reported copper production up 10.9% from January to September 2021 versus the same period last year. The rebound is attributed to higher output at operations including Antamina, Cerro Verde and Southern companies, alongside additional project production such as Mina Justa.

title: First Cobalt Unveils Strategic Shift to Make Battery Precursor and Nickel Sulfate; Changes Name to Electra Battery Materials
summary: First Cobalt (renaming to Electra Battery Materials) announced plans to expand a hydrometallurgical refinery and assess a North American battery-grade nickel sulfate project, including recycling and later precursor manufacturing. It highlights future nickel output and studies, but near-term volumes and timelines suggest limited immediate price impact for metals mentioned.

title: Alcoa to restart long idled capacity at Australian aluminium smelter
summary: Alcoa plans to restart long-idled capacity at an Australian aluminium smelter. The restart would raise aluminium production/supply expectations in the near term, affecting market tightness. Traders may adjust positions based on the timing and pace of ramp-up, influencing aluminium price sentiment over coming days to weeks.

title: Alcoa to Restart Aluminum Lines in Australia Idled Since 2009
summary: Alcoa plans to restart aluminum lines in Australia that have been idle since 2009. The reopening signals additional primary aluminum supply returning to the market, which can weigh on near-term expectations for aluminium balance and push prices lower in the coming days.

title: Malaysia Postponed Implementation of Metal Scrap Import Standards, Domestic Copper Scrap Supply Is Generally Tight_SMM
summary: Malaysia postponed implementation of planned metal scrap import standards to next year, leaving details unclear and potential scrap-flow impacts uncertain. Separately, Chinese copper scrap supply was tight as sellers held cargoes after price falls and COVID-related transport risks reduced scrap availability, forcing some Hebei copper-rod plants to pause production.

title: U.S. Secretary Of Commerce Raimondo to Visit Japan and Discuss the Cancellation of Tariffs on Japanese Steel and Aluminium_SMM
summary: U.S. Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo will visit Japan and, with USTR representatives, discuss the possible cancellation of U.S. tariffs on Japanese steel and aluminium. The talks are aimed at strengthening trade and cooperation and restoring supply chains, which could ease aluminium import costs and support aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Alcoa to restart Portland Aluminium smelter after 12 years
summary: Alcoa plans to restart the Portland aluminium smelter after 12 years of inactivity. The restart is expected to bring additional aluminium output back into the market, improving supply expectations and likely pressuring prices in the near term as traders price in reduced tightness.

title: Nobel Provides Update on La Salvadora and Algarrobo Copper Projects, Chile
summary: Nobel Resources plans to commence drilling at its newly acquired Salvadora copper project in Chile after receiving a drill permit around Nov. 15. It will continue testing its Algarrobo copper target despite earlier mechanical and logistics issues, including establishing water infrastructure. The updates signal exploration progress, not near-term production.

title: / R E P E A T -- First Cobalt Unveils Strategic Shift to Make Battery Precursor and Nickel Sulfate; Changes Name to Electra Battery Materials/
summary: First Cobalt, renamed Electra Battery Materials, outlined expansion of battery-grade nickel and cobalt production for North American EV supply chains. It is running a nickel market study for a future battery-grade nickel sulfate plant (targeted 2024-25) and evaluating recycled feeds, potentially supporting nickel demand expectations.

title: Kintavar Begins Drilling on Wabash Copper Project
summary: Kintavar Exploration began drilling on its Wabash copper project in Quebec, targeting multiple mineralized zones along an 8 km corridor. The program of up to 3,000 meters aims to test mineralization at depth and lateral extent, with first results expected early 2022 based on prior high-grade copper assays.

title: Aluminum Declines as Chinese Auto Sales Drop, Power Crunch Eases
summary: Aluminium prices are falling as China’s auto sales weaken, signaling softer downstream demand for the metal. The report also says the power crunch is easing, reducing constraints on aluminium production and potentially easing supply pressure. Together, the developments create downward near-term price bias for aluminium.

title: Goldplay Mining Inc.: Goldplay Begins Drilling on past Producing Copper Mine in Portugal
summary: Goldplay Mining began an approximately 1,000m underground drilling campaign at the historical Aparis copper mine in Portugal. The project targets expanding and defining a copper-rich shear zone (>1% Cu) with existing underground development and flotation mill on site. It signals potential future copper development but no near-term production changes.

title: Goldplay Begins Drilling on past Producing Copper Mine in Po...
summary: Goldplay Mining began drilling at the historical Aparis underground copper mine in Portugal. The release cites extensive existing development, prior high-grade copper sampling, and plans to expand delineate a copper (>1% Cu) shear-zone target. It discusses exploration potential, but does not indicate near-term production impacts.

title: Guatemala advances community consultation at Fénix nickel mine
summary: Guatemala is reported to be advancing community consultation steps for the Fénix nickel mine. The notice suggests ongoing engagement tied to approvals for the project, which may affect near-term certainty around operational timing and output. This can influence market expectations for nickel supply in the coming weeks.

title: LSE Shares - Katoro Gold Update – Haneti Nickel Project
summary: The article reports on a Katoro Gold update focused on the Haneti Project, where Power Metal is eager for drilling to begin. The project targets a large-scale nickel and PGE discovery. As an exploration milestone, it may modestly improve expectations for future nickel supply.

title: Copper up on robust China data and falling inventories
summary: Copper rose about 1.2% as China’s export growth beat forecasts, LME-registered copper inventories fell sharply, and canceled warrants suggested further stock declines. Sentiment was reinforced by passage of a $1 trillion U.S. infrastructure bill, though traders remain cautious about potential Chinese demand weakness.

title: Wabash National signs long-term deal for aluminum
summary: Wabash National says it has signed a 10-year deal with Hydro for aluminum extrusions, giving it more reliable access to aluminum materials. The company expects the arrangement to support increased production of dry van and refrigerated trailers and truck bodies. The agreement runs through 2031.

title: Nickel added to US critical minerals list
summary: The US has updated its critical minerals list by adding nickel, highlighting its use in battery alloys, electronics, military hardware, and energy technologies. With Australia producing about 24% of global nickel supply, the article argues Australia is positioned to benefit, potentially lifting nickel sentiment.

title: LME aluminium on-warrant stocks at lowest levels since Dec 2005; small uptick in prices
summary: LME aluminium on-warrant stocks are at their lowest since Dec 2005, signalling very tight near-term availability. The piece also mentions a small uptick in prices. Together, the inventory drawdown/buffer compression and stock scarcity are supportive for aluminium sentiment over the coming days.

title: How the rise of copper reveals clean energy's dark side | Mining
summary: The piece describes community concerns around Freeport-McMoRan’s proposed expansion of New Mexico’s Tyrone-area copper mining, while stressing that clean energy and EV/renewables growth are driving sharply higher copper demand. It argues copper is essential for electricity grids and electrification, supporting a bullish copper price narrative despite environmental risks.

title: Global Copper Pipes and Tubes Markets, 2021-2026 - As Key End-Use Industries Take a Hit, Pandemic Affects Demand for Copper Pipes & Tubes
summary: A ResearchAndMarkets report on copper pipes and tubes cites that demand fell in 2020 as non-critical construction, residential building, manufacturing output, and automotive demand were disrupted by COVID-19. It projects recovery and growth later via HVAC, plumbing, and heat exchange uses, but the pandemic shock is demand-bearish.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28 Announces Q3 2021 Financial Results
summary: Nickel 28 reported Q3 2021 results from its 8.56% stake in the Ramu nickel-cobalt project in Papua New Guinea. The company highlighted strong nickel and cobalt output, solid sales and cash costs per pound, improved payability, and a received cash flow payment, supporting nickel supply sentiment.

title: Nickel 28 Announces Q3 2021 Financial Results
summary: Nickel 28 reported Q3 2021 results for its 8.56% interest in the Ramu nickel-cobalt operation in Papua New Guinea. The company cited strong nickel/cobalt commodity prices, improved MHP payability, higher Q3 nickel sales, and a US$3.2 million cash-flow receipt following repayment of operating debt.

title: World Copper Ltd.: World Copper to Host Conference Call and Provides Update on Arrangement
summary: World Copper Ltd. announced an upcoming management conference call and an interim court order supporting a planned arrangement with Cardero Resource Corp. Shareholders will vote on the deal at a scheduled meeting, with completion targeted for about December 20, 2021. The company is focused on copper projects in Chile and Arizona.

title: Fluor JV to install new grinding mill at copper and gold mining project in Indonesia - Chemical Engineering
summary: Fluor’s JV with Petrosea will install a new third semi-autogenous grinding (SAG) mill at PT Freeport Indonesia’s Grasberg underground copper and gold district in Papua. The expansion aims to increase milling capacity as underground output ramps up post-2019 open-pit completion. Construction is scheduled to start later in 2021 and finish in 2023.

title: Russia Considers Lifting Its Aluminum Export Tax
summary: The Reuters report says Russia may let its 15% aluminum export tax lapse in December, potentially increasing primary aluminum supply to Europe. That expectation is already weighing on LME prices and especially physical delivery premiums like Rotterdam, which have fallen sharply, with further declines anticipated despite still-tight availability.

title: DNR opens comment period on rules for copper mining near BWCA
summary: Minnesota’s DNR is accepting public comments as it reviews rules governing nonferrous (copper-nickel) mining restrictions near the BWCAW after a lawsuit sought to expand protections to the Rainy River Watershed. Comments are due Dec. 8. The process relates to the proposed Twin Metals mine near Ely.

title: Copper skids on worries over Chinese property crisis
summary: Copper prices fell on fears that China’s deepening property debt crisis will reduce demand. The article links the turmoil to liquidity stress for developers and highlights China’s large share of global copper consumption. Energy shortages and higher electricity prices add to downside risk, though falling inventories limit losses.

title: US Relaxes Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum from Europe, Looking Next to UK and Japan | Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner
summary: The US and EU agreed to ease Trump-era Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum, replacing aluminum tariffs with tariff-rate quotas effective Jan 1, 2022. The lower effective tariff burden should improve access for EU aluminum imports into the US, likely weighing on nearby aluminum prices.

title: LME copper futures fall back due to concerns about the outlook for Chinese demand_SMM
summary: LME three-month copper fell 0.88% as traders flagged uncertainty over Chinese demand. Concerns center on ongoing real-estate stress, China’s energy shortages and higher electricity prices in Europe, plus a risk-off warning from the Fed. Copper stocks fell sharply, but the demand outlook dominated. Aluminum warehouse receipts also dropped.

title: 'Candemic': Supply chain issues hit breweries, causing aluminum can shortage
summary: Breweries in Nevada report a “can shortage” as pandemic-era supply chain disruptions continue. CraftHaus says it is struggling to source enough aluminum cans for packaging, leading to size changes and relabeling. Breweries expect costs to rise, which could translate into higher aluminum-related pricing pressure over the near term.

title: China Company to Speed up Investments in High-Nickel Ternary Capacity in Europe_SMM
summary: Dang Sheng Technology signed a letter of intent with FMG and its subsidiary to form a Finland JV to build high-nickel ternary cathode capacity (100,000 mt/year total; first 50,000 mt/year by 2024). The project targets overseas demand for high-nickel batteries, supporting nickel demand expectations.

title: [Spoiler] SMM China Aluminium Industry Chain Annual Report  2021-2025_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s “dual carbon” policy and an energy crisis caused frequent aluminium smelter production limits and power rationing in late 2021. Costs rose from higher coal and natural gas, but rationing cut output, spread to downstream plants, increased peak-season social inventories, and weighed on aluminium prices.

title: Tinka Resources Ltd.: Tinka Samples 6 Metres @ 12.8 Grams/Tonne Gold and 2.7% Copper at Silvia
summary: Tinka Resources announced new trench results from its Silvia NW copper-gold skarn target in Peru, including intervals with up to 2.7% copper (with gold co-mineralization) and an expanded outcrop strike footprint. The news is exploration-focused and does not indicate near-term production or supply disruption, so broader copper price impact is likely limited.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Drills 44.90 g/t platinum over 0.65 metres, 13.65 metres of 0.83% nickel, 8.00 metres of 1.03% nickel, Peak Assay of 5.12% nickel at Lappvattnet
summary: Gungnir Resources reported additional 2021 drill results from Sweden’s Lappvattnet nickel deposit, including 13.65 metres of 0.83% Ni and 8.00 metres of 1.03% Ni, with a peak of 5.12% Ni. These improved assays may modestly boost nickel market sentiment despite no near-term supply change.

title: British company agrees Indonesia nickel mining JV
summary: Altilium Group agreed with Indo Mineral Research/Sebuku Group to promote and accelerate the DNi hydrometallurgical process in Indonesia. Plans discussed include constructing plants delivering about 20,000 tonnes/year of nickel in MHP and producing co-products such as aluminium hydroxide, supporting EV battery supply and cleaner nickel output.

title: Tight Supply, Rising Demand and Low Interest Rate Creates Bullish Case for Copper
summary: Commentary highlights tight copper supply, rising demand (China emissions goals and US decarbonization goals), and fears of shortages as drivers for higher copper prices. It also discusses feasibility studies, resource expansion, and ongoing drilling/exploration at several copper projects, reinforcing bullish sentiment.

title: Drilling Completed on Second Target at Playfair's RKV Copper...
summary: Playfair reports completion of drilling on targets at its RKV Copper Project in Norway. The Storboren hole intersected multiple sulphide zones and samples were submitted for analysis. Results are supported by strong MMI Cu anomalies (up to 53,300 ppb) suggesting weathering copper sulphides, but no development impacts are stated.

title: Cook Children's asking for donations of aluminum crutches amid shortages
summary: Cook Children’s Home Health in Fort Worth is asking for donations of new or gently used aluminium crutches as a “national” aluminium shortage leads to hospital backorders. The hospital says it currently has a two-month supply and is not yet facing a shortage, but is stockpiling ahead of demand.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Retains SGS for 43-101 Mineral Resource Update on Carmacks Deposit in Yukon, Canada
summary: Granite Creek Copper retained SGS to prepare an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate for its Carmacks copper-gold-silver deposit in Yukon. The company also notes Yukon’s Carmacks Bypass road/bridge contract to improve access for mining activities, with work expected to complete in 2024. The news is development-oriented, not production-related.

title: Canada Nickel Demonstrates Carbon Sequestration Potential of Tailings from the Crawford Nickel Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel reports lab tests showing its Crawford nickel project tailings can mineralize CO2 at rates up to 17.5 kg per tonne, potentially exceeding the 4.6 kg/tonne needed to offset projected emissions. The work supports future carbon-credit opportunities and a NetZero initiative, with next pilot tests planned later.

title: Ero Copper third quarter production and financial results
summary: Ero Copper reported Q3 2021 copper output of 10,057 tonnes from its MCSA Mining Complex, with mill maintenance completed to support higher Q4 throughput. It also announced an optimized feasibility study for the Boa Esperança project, doubling expected life-of-mine copper production. Overall guidance is toward the high end of 2021 ranges.

title: After Copper Chaos, LME Mulls Rules to Keep From Running Out of Metal
summary: The piece’s headline says that after “copper chaos,” the LME is mulling rules aimed at preventing metal shortages. While such measures could reduce short-term supply risk and support sentiment, the article text provided lacks details on the proposals, making the net price impact unclear.

title: Ero Copper third quarter production and financial results continue to position the Company for growth - Brazil Business Today
summary: Ero Copper reported Q3 2021 copper production of 10,057 tonnes from the MCSA complex and completion of mill maintenance to support higher throughput in Q4. It also announced an optimized feasibility study for the Boa Esperança project that doubles life-of-mine copper output, reinforcing growth-oriented copper supply expectations.

title: Ero Copper third quarter production and financial results co...
summary: Ero Copper reported Q3 2021 results including 10,057 tonnes of copper production at its MCSA complex, completion of mill maintenance, and guidance to achieve the high end of 2021 copper-in-concentrate output. It also discussed capex inflation impacts and growth projects aimed at higher future throughput.

title: Copper Fox Metals CEO: Developing an Asset and Monetizing it at the Right Time
summary: Copper Fox Metals’ CEO discusses the preliminary economic assessment for its Schaft Creek copper-molybdenum-gold-silver project and plans to collect metallurgical samples to cut processing costs. The interview highlights copper-price sensitivity of project economics, but provides no new supply or trade factors that would materially shift near-term copper prices.

title: Landslides at Codelco's Minstro Hales Copper Mine did not affect operation_SMM
summary: Codelco said a landslide occurred on the eastern slope of its Ministro Hales open-pit copper mine in Chile, but it did not impact worker safety, equipment, or ongoing operations. The company attributed this to early warning and slope monitoring, with the area quarantined. No production disruption was reported.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Overnight Marketed Public Offering
summary: Nevada Copper announced a marketed public offering and related private placement, raising about C$75 million, to fund ramp-up of its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine and repay related bridge loans. The release also details credit-facility deferrals/extensions. It’s financing-focused, with only indirect near-term copper supply impact.

title: Cabinet introduces moratorium on licensing activities for development of gold, silver and copper
summary: The Cabinet of Ministers introduced a temporary moratorium on licensing activities for geological exploration, prospecting, and development of gold (placer), silver, and copper subsoil use, with exceptions for technogenic formations. The policy may delay copper project development, increasing near-term supply uncertainty and weakening copper sentiment.

title: Aluminium Social Inventories Dropped 6,000 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s social aluminium inventories across eight consumption areas fell by 6,000 mt week-on-week to about 1.007 million mt as of Nov 11, with declines mainly in Nanhai, Shanghai and Gongyi. Wuxi rose, and the article flags possible transport disruption from a north-China blizzard.

title: US Relaxes Tariffs On Steel And Aluminum From Europe, Looking Next To UK And Japan - International Law
summary: The US and EU agreed to relax Trump-era Section 232 tariffs on European steel and aluminum. For aluminum, the US replaces tariffs with a tariff-rate quota effective Jan. 1, 2022, with only higher-than-allowed volumes subject to the tariff. Similar deals are pursued with the UK and Japan.

title: Trigon Metals, Inc.: Trigon Reports 8m of 6.56% Copper Extending Open Pit Mineralization, Namibia
summary: Trigon Metals reported geotechnical/assay drill results from Namibia’s Kombat copper project, finding multiple copper intersections, including 8m of 6.56% Cu (with a higher-grade subinterval). The company suggests the mineralization could expand pit tonnage, grade, and mine life, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Peru has yet to decide how much to hike takes on miners – finance minister
summary: Peru’s finance minister said the government has not decided how much to raise taxes on miners, though it plans rate adjustments while seeking IMF input. The mining sector is a major tax source in the No. 2 copper-producing country. Industry groups warn higher taxes could hurt competitiveness and affect copper supply outlook.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Upsize and Pricing of Overnight
summary: Nevada Copper upsized a C$114 million overnight unit offering, citing strong demand, to fund ramp-up of its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine and open-pit exploration, plus debt repayment. The company plans to close around Nov. 29, with over-allotment possible. No immediate production change is specified.

title: London copper eases as dollar firms on rate hike bets
summary: London copper eased slightly as the dollar firmed on expectations of an earlier U.S. rate hike after strong inflation data, which can slow global recovery and raise dollar-priced metals. LME aluminium fell while nickel rose; losses were partly offset by tight exchange inventories.

title: How will the supply and demand of SMM: copper scrap be interpreted in the later stage of the epidemic [SMM Annual meeting]_SMM
summary: SMM’s copper analyst discusses how China’s zero solid-waste import policy, stricter customs checks, and tightening scrap-metal standards in Malaysia/EU affect flows of recycled copper/brass scrap into China. Despite some flexibility for standards-met scrap, overseas supply is expected to stay tight, supporting copper scrap and copper market prices.

title: SMM Annual Conference 2021– Development Trend and New Solutions in Copper, Aluminium, New Energy Industries_SMM
summary: At SMM’s 2021 Nonferrous Metals Industry Chain conference, speakers said China faces a prominent copper resource shortage, with copper processing capacity exceeding smelting and smelting exceeding concentrate supply. It also noted RUSAL’s ambition to produce most aluminum with carbon-free energy by 2025 and growing secondary-aluminum demand, affecting aluminum supply expectations.

title: Copper Inventory in China Bonded Zone Dipped 10,700 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported China’s domestic bonded zone copper inventories fell 10,700 mt from Nov 5 to 216,200 mt by Nov 12, the fifth straight weekly decline. Shanghai bonded inventories dropped 8,700 mt and Guangdong fell 2,000 mt, attributed to low port arrivals and ongoing smelter exports.

title: Europe's Aleastur announces GCC's first aluminium grain refiners plant in Bahrain | THE DAILY TRIBUNE
summary: Aleastur will launch the GCC’s first aluminium grain refiner and master alloys plant in Bahrain, a $15 million hub exporting about 85% of production. The facility will supply aluminium smelters and cast-houses, reducing lead times and strengthening regional supply chains as construction activity resumes.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Surged 190,000 wmt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chinese ports’ nickel ore inventories rose by 190,000 wmt to 9.24 million wmt, with Ni content at 72,500 mt. Demand for nickel ore was weaker than normal as NPI production in some areas hasn’t fully recovered and buyers restocked only to cover until year-end. Inventories are expected to fall later.

title: Copper prices slip after U.S. inflation boosts dollar
summary: Copper gained after U.S. inflation-related weakness in consumer confidence eased the dollar, supporting dollar-priced metals; tight LME/shanghai inventories also helped. China power curbs cut 7% of aluminium capacity, supporting aluminium. Nickel faces Indonesia export-pricing scrutiny, with nickel quoted lower on the day.

title: U.S. to ease import tariffs on Japanese steel and aluminum in effort to reset trade relations
summary: The Biden administration plans to begin negotiations with Japan to ease U.S. import tariffs on steel and aluminum. The goal is an arrangement that would allow some Japanese metals to enter the U.S. tariff-free. Tariff relief could shift near-term aluminum trade flows and influence pricing expectations.

title: U.S., Japan to Start Steel, Aluminum Talks Over Excess Capacity
summary: The U.S. and Japan are set to begin talks regarding excess capacity in steel and aluminum. Such discussions can affect market expectations around aluminum supply and potential trade responses, but without details on specific measures or timelines, the near-term effect on aluminum prices is uncertain.

title: UPDATE 1-U.S. will open talks with Japan on import steel, aluminum tariffs
summary: The U.S. will open talks with Japan regarding import steel and aluminium tariffs. Easing or renegotiating tariff conditions would likely affect aluminium import expectations and supply risk premiums in the near term, potentially pressuring aluminium prices downward versus a scenario of confirmed higher tariffs.

title: U.S., Japan to start steel, aluminum talks over excess capacity
summary: The U.S. and Japan will start talks aimed at resolving global steel and aluminum excess capacity and U.S. tariffs on Japanese product exports. Officials cite distortions from China-driven overcapacity and seek mechanisms similar to the EU tariff-rate quota, which could affect near-term aluminum import supply.

title: U.S. will open talks with Japan on import steel, aluminum tariffs
summary: The U.S. plans talks with Japan that could ease steel and aluminum import tariffs, aiming to address global excess capacity and restore market-oriented conditions. It follows the U.S.-EU deal that maintained Section 232 tariff rates but reduced costs via limited duty-free volumes. Japan seeks abolishment of Section 232.

title: US Launches Talks With Japan to Address Steel, Aluminum Excess Capacity - US Trade Office
summary: The USTR said the US and Japan have begun consultations to tackle global excess capacity in steel and aluminium and to address related tariff issues. The talks focus on restoring market-oriented conditions and countering trade-distorting policies, particularly those linked to China’s persistent overcapacity in aluminium.

title: U.S. will open talks with Japan on import steel, aluminum tariffs | The Asahi Shimbun: Breaking News, Japan News and Analysis
summary: The U.S. will open talks with Japan that could ease tariffs on steel and aluminum imports, targeting “global steel and aluminum excess capacity” and restoring market-oriented conditions. The piece notes existing Section 232 rates (25% steel, 10% aluminum) but suggests possible relief via a tariff-exclusion/adjustment process.

title: Egypt scraps import tariffs for billets, rebar and aluminium products
summary: Egypt’s trade ministry said it has scrapped import duties for steel billets, rebar and aluminium products, citing high global inflation and energy prices. Previously, duties were imposed in 2019 (16% on billets and 25% on rebar). The aluminium duty removal could add supply pressure.

title: Operating Rates at Copper Plate and Strip Producers Slid Further in October and Expected to Improve in November_SMM
summary: SMM reports copper plate/sheet and strip producers’ operating rates fell to 74.19% in October as power rationing tightened after September energy controls, expanding to more provinces. Small and mid-sized firms faced production hindrance amid high copper prices and maintenance. November operating rates are expected to rise to 75.51% with easing rationing intensity and slightly better downstream demand.

title: [Spoiler] China Copper Industry Chain Annual Report  2021-2025_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports copper concentrate supply shocks (roadblocks in Peru, Chilean port high tides), China power rationing causing smelter suspensions, and tighter inventories (falling SHFE stocks, rising LME cancelled warrants) alongside a weaker import window early in 2021. These shortages and squeeze dynamics lifted copper treatment charges and Chinese premiums, supporting bullish copper pricing.

title: Japan, U.S. ministers meet over steel, aluminum tariffs
summary: Japan and U.S. ministers agreed to begin negotiations to resolve a trade dispute over higher U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminum imports imposed under the Trump administration. Talks raise the prospect of reduced tariff pressure on aluminum shipments, improving near-term expectations for aluminum import flows and pricing.

title: Japan, U.S. agree to start talks on extra tariffs on steel, aluminium
summary: Japan and the U.S. agreed to begin talks on additional U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminium imports from Japan. No specific measures were set in the meeting, but the U.S. said talks could lead to easing tariffs, a longstanding irritant. This may support aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Solus Advanced Materials buys copper foil plant site in Canada
summary: Solus Advanced Materials will restart a previously owned copper foil plant site in Quebec, Canada, with 60,000 tons annual capacity. The company plans to convert it into a battery foil production line for North American customers from battery and auto industries, aiming for mass production by 2024.

title: U.S., Japan Agree to Talks on Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The headline says the U.S. and Japan have agreed to hold talks on steel and aluminum tariffs. Any move toward higher tariff barriers could reduce or reroute aluminum imports, tightening expected supply and supporting near-term aluminium price sentiment over the coming days to weeks.

title: Impact of SMM: China's Energy Saving and carbon reduction Policy on Global Electrolytic Aluminum Industry [SMM Annual meeting]_SMM
summary: The piece argues China’s energy-saving and carbon-reduction policies affect electrolytic aluminum output by driving “double control” limits tied to electricity and coal tightness, citing significant shutdown capacity. It also notes aluminum demand/inventories softened after coal price falls, but overall policy-driven supply pressure should be supportive.

title: FPX Nickel Reports Van Target Drilling Results Confirming Significant Lateral Extension of Higher-Grade, Near-Surface Nickel Mineralization
summary: FPX Nickel announced new drill intersections at its Van target in the Decar Nickel District, extending strong awaruite nickel mineralization and reporting broad, high-grade near-surface intervals. Assays for additional holes are pending. The positive results may improve expectations for future nickel supply potential.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Drills 6.94% Nickel within 31 Metres Grading 0.93% Nickel Starting 20 Metres Below Surface at Lappvattnet
summary: Gungnir Resources reported additional near-surface drilling at its Lappvattnet nickel deposit in Sweden, including a 6.94% Ni intercept over 31 metres in hole LAP21-12. Assays are pending for nearby holes and the company expects these results to feed future resource upgrades.

title: Japan, US Agree to Start Talks on Additional Steel, Aluminum Tariffs
summary: Japan and the U.S. agreed to start talks in Tokyo to address potential additional U.S. tariffs on Japanese steel and aluminum imports. No specific measures were discussed and no talks timetable was set. The tariff focus directly targets aluminum trade, which can pressure near-term aluminum prices.

title: Bahrain to host GCC's first plant for aluminium grain refiners - Construction Week Online
summary: Aleastur will launch the GCC’s first aluminium grain refiners and master alloys hub in Bahrain, investing $15m and exporting about 85% of output to regional smelters and cast-houses. The facility aims to shorten lead times and strengthen downstream aluminium supply chains as construction activity resumes.

title: One Planet:  How the copper & zinc Ambler Road project threatens Alaska's Native communities & wildlife
summary: A proposed 211-mile industrial access road to Alaska’s Ambler mining district is described as enabling extraction of over 43 million tons of copper (and zinc). The report emphasizes environmental and Native community opposition and notes the Biden administration has not interrupted approvals, but it doesn’t indicate imminent production start.

title: Copper falls on Chinese property market weakness, strong dollar
summary: Copper prices fell as China’s property sector showed weakness, reducing expectations for metals demand. Coal prices dropped, easing smelter energy costs, but a stronger U.S. dollar lifted metal prices for non-dollar buyers. The LME warehouse squeeze eased. LME aluminium and nickel also fell on the same risk backdrop.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Provides an Update on Development Planning for Its San Matias Copper-Gold-Silver Project
summary: Cordoba Minerals provided updates on its San Matias project in Colombia, including expected completion of a pre-feasibility study and submission of a mining technical work plan permit application, alongside ongoing environmental impact assessment work. The company is advancing the Alacran copper-gold-silver deposit toward construction.

title: Talon Commends U.S. Action on Battery Supply Chain as President Biden Signs Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill, Adds Nickel to Critical Mineral List
summary: The article says Talon commends U.S. action on the battery supply chain as President Biden signs a bipartisan infrastructure bill and adds nickel to the U.S. critical mineral list. The move signals stronger policy attention to nickel sourcing and battery-related industrial activity, potentially supporting nickel prices in the near term.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Commends U.S. Action on Battery Supply Chain as President Biden Signs Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill, Adds Nickel to Critical Mineral List
summary: Talon Metals says President Biden signed the U.S. Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, providing funding for EV adoption and EV battery materials processing, including nickel. It also notes the administration added nickel to the U.S. Critical Minerals List, aiming to prioritize nickel mining and processing for supply security.

title: Copper rises as risk sentiment improves after Xi-Biden summit
summary: Copper prices rose 0.5% on the LME and edged up on the SHFE after improved risk sentiment following a Biden-Xi summit. The meeting supported wider market confidence, with the yuan strengthening. In the same snapshot, nickel was up while aluminium and zinc fell, showing mixed effects across metals.

title: New method recovers cobalt and nickel from NMC batteries
summary: A research team at UIUC developed a tunable liquid electrolyte and polymer coating to recover metals from spent NMC battery waste, reporting ~94% nickel purity and ~96% cobalt purity. By making recycling more efficient and less wasteful, the method could boost expectations for secondary nickel supply, though timing and scale remain unclear.

title: Solus buys back its Canadian copper foil plant
summary: Solus Advanced Materials reacquired its Quebec copper foil plant with capacity of 60,000 tons of copper foil for lithium-ion battery negative electrodes. The firm plans investments to expand the facility and target mass production in 2024, aiming to grow exposure to North America’s EV market.

title: Power Nickel Inc.: Power Nickel Starts 4000 Metre Drilling Program
summary: Power Nickel started a ~4,000-metre drilling program at its Nisk project to expand a historic nickel-copper mineralization and produce a new NI 43-101 resource estimate. The company expects assay results in January and discusses potential nickel sulphate for EV batteries, but provides no new production or assay data.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Continues to Deliver Encouraging Copper Results at Punitaqui Mine
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reports encouraging San Andres drill results at Chile’s Punitaqui copper project, including multiple intercepts around ~0.7–1.4% copper and wider zones like 28.1m at 0.98% Cu. The company highlights progress toward restarting mine production mid-to-late 2022, potentially supporting copper supply expectations.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Continues to Deliver Encouraging Copper Results at Punitaqui Mine
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reported assay results from the San Andres drill program at its Punitaqui copper project in Chile, with several intercepts grading around ~0.5% to 1.4%+ copper over multiple meters. The company also cites progress toward a mid-to-late-2022 restart, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: United States Set to Rollback Existing Section 232 Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum from the European Union | Husch Blackwell LLP
summary: The US and EU agreed to modify Section 232 tariffs on EU steel and aluminum imports by replacing tariff requirements with tariff-rate quotas (including 18,000 metric tons for aluminum) starting January 1, 2022 and halting EU retaliation. The aluminum tariff rollback should lower import costs and support aluminum price expectations.

title: Unit of China's CNCEC Lands USD2 Billion Contract to Build Alumina Refinery in Guinea
summary: CNCEC’s unit won a USD2 billion EPC contract to build a bauxite project and an alumina refinery in Guinea with 1.5–2.0 million tons annual alumina output. Alumina is a feedstock for aluminium smelting. The project could lift supply expectations and support aluminium market sentiment despite long construction lead times.

title: Palladium One Mining Inc.: Palladium One Tyko Copper-Nickel Project Update
summary: Palladium One provided updates on its Tyko copper-nickel exploration project, including geophysical EM surveys, additional exploration permit applications, and expectations to resume drilling after permits are received. The release also cites recent high-grade Ni and Cu intercepts used in Ni-equivalent calculations, but offers no near-term production impact.

title: Palladium One Mining Inc.: Palladium One Tyko Copper-Nickel Project Update
summary: Palladium One provides updates on its Tyko copper-nickel project, including ongoing EM surveys, new exploration permit applications, and plans to schedule drilling after permits are received. It reiterates earlier drill intercept grades (Ni and Cu) and notes nickel-equivalent calculations, but no immediate production or supply impact is stated.

title: Smelter in Copper Cliff placed in standby mode
summary: Vale has ramped down its Copper Cliff Smelter into a “hot” standby state for two weeks to optimize concentrate stock levels after an incident halted production at the Totten Mine. The move pauses ore smelting temporarily, with refinery operations continuing and no customer impact expected in the article.

title: Updated Nifty Copper Mineral Resource Estimate
summary: Cyprium Metals announced an updated Mineral Resource estimate for its Nifty copper deposit, reporting higher contained copper, including a larger heap-leachable component.
