The company says the increase supports its Nifty Heap Leach Restart Study and future SX-EW cathode potential. The update is project-focused rather than supply-impacting immediately.

title: Fire Broke Out at Nickel Smelter in Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia_SMM
summary: A fire broke out in a ferronickel smelting furnace at a nickel smelter in Konawe, southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia. The incident affects only one smelting furnace production line, with expected capacity of about 650 mt/month in Ni content under normal operations. The article says the impact is not significant.

title: Aluminium Futures Plunged over 3% amid Bearish Factors and Increased Short Positions_SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium has dropped for four straight days as SMM social inventories rose, short positions expanded, and weakening coal and alumina prices reduced cost support. Weak downstream consumption and a stronger US dollar further weighed on sentiment. Spot prices in East China widened to large discounts, reinforcing expectations of more declines.

title: Why Overseas Aluminium Capacity Expands so Quickly amid Strict Energy Consumption Control?_SMM
summary: SMM describes several overseas aluminium capacity additions entering November, including Alcoa’s restart in Australia (35,000 mt/yr), Alcoa/South32’s Brazil Alumar restart, and EGA’s Al Taweelah smelter expansion (78,000 mt/yr). It attributes expansion to higher prices, import expectations, and low-carbon supply demand.

title: SPC Nickel Corp.: SPC Nickel Announces Major Land Acquisition Covering the Highly-Prospective Muskox Intrusion (Ni-Cu-PGM) and the Acquisition of a Large Comprehensive Database
summary: SPC Nickel announced staking of a large land package covering Nunavut’s Muskox Ni-Cu-PGM intrusion and acquisition of an extensive historical geoscience database. The release emphasizes future evaluation and potential for feeder-dyke mineralization, but it does not change near-term production, inventories, or trade flows for nickel or copper.

title: EUROFER welcomes EU and USA statement on steel and aluminium
summary: EUROFER welcomed a joint EU-US statement to address carbon intensity and global overcapacity in steel and aluminium. The plan replaces the US Section 232 25% tariff on EU steel with a tariff-rate quota based on historical volumes, aiming to prevent tariff escalation and reduce trade frictions affecting industrial metals demand.

title: Global need for copper, nickel will multiply over next 30 years -BHP
summary: BHP’s executive said a decarbonised world will require much higher metal supply, projecting nearly double copper demand and about four times nickel demand over the next 30 years. The comments were presented as modelling results supporting the long-run investment case, potentially boosting short-term sentiment.

title: Rio Tinto invests to increase low-carbon AP60 aluminium production in Canada
summary: Rio Tinto will invest US$87 million to add 16 smelting cells at its AP60 aluminium smelter in Quebec, expanding output by ~45% to 86,500 tonnes per year. The company cites growing demand for low-carbon aluminium and expects works from spring 2022 to end-2023.

title: Rio Tinto Adds New Aluminum Production to Hot Metals Market
summary: The piece headline says Rio Tinto is adding new aluminum production to the “hot metals” market, implying additional supply entering the aluminum market. Such additions can influence short-term expectations for aluminum availability and pricing within days to a few weeks. The provided text lacks further specifics on volume, timing, or constraints.

title: Iran aluminum output rises 23% in March-October: Report
summary: IMIDRO data show Iran’s aluminium production rose 23% in the seven months to late October, with major smelters (IRALCO, SALCO, Al Mahdi) expanding output. Alumina powder slightly declined but bauxite output increased. Overall higher supply from Iran could weigh on aluminium prices in the coming weeks.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Copper Temporarily Pauses Drill Program at MPD Due to Flooding and Road Closures
summary: Kodiak Copper temporarily paused its 2021 drilling program at the MPD copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia after an evacuation order for Merritt due to flooding and related road closures. The program is largely completed, with demobilized personnel and no damage risk, and drilling will resume after orders lift.

title: Gold, copper drilling operations resume in Sagay
summary: Mayor Alfredo Marañon III said Tambuli Mining Company has resumed diamond drilling in Sagay City, targeting gold and copper under an environment permit. Drilling restarted after a 2012-2017 period, with seven holes totaling about 4,400 meters under new management. No production or near-term output changes are mentioned.

title: Surge Battery Metals Inc.: Surge Closes Acquisition of Nickel Claims with Nickel Rock Resources
summary: Surge Battery Metals announces it has closed an option acquisition to earn an 80% interest in nickel claims (HN4 and N100) in Northern British Columbia from Nickel Rock Resources. The company issued shares and plans $200,000 in exploration expenditures over two years, with further joint-venture steps pending.

title: Rio Tinto To Invest US$87 Mln To Increase Low-carbon AP60 Aluminium Production In Canada
summary: Rio Tinto will invest US$87 million to expand low-carbon aluminium production at its AP60 smelter in Quebec by adding 16 new smelting cells. The project should raise output by about 45% to 86,500 tonnes/year, with work starting in spring 2022 and completion by end-2023.

title: Chairmen's egos main threat to nickel merger: analyst
summary: Merger talks between IGO Ltd and nickel producer Western Areas showed no progress at annual meetings, with the deal now past three months. Despite the lack of signs of resolution, both companies’ shares rose modestly, implying limited near-term optimism related to nickel and some exposure to copper markets.

title: [SMM Annual Summit] The Alumina Market Maintains Tight Balance, and Market Sentiment Volatility Amplifies the Fluctuation of Spot Prices_SMM
summary: SMM says the alumina market is temporarily unlisted, with spot price discovery driven by supply tightness and sentiment. Prices rose in Q2-Q3 on an estimated long-term shortage. For the short term, it expects declines as the shortage view unwinds, sellers increase, and falling aluminium prices reduce rigid demand.

title: [SMM Annual Summit] Imported Bauxite Prices to Increase in 2022 Amid High Ocean Freight In 2021 and Limited Marginal Demand Increments_SMM
summary: SMM reports that imported bauxite volumes fell 7.5% y/y in Jan–Sep and notes constrained cost-effectiveness under high 2021 ocean freight. With freight expected to ease, demand to grow, and domestic prices to rise, imported bauxite prices and related supply expectations are projected to improve in 2022, affecting alumina feedstock costs.

title: Analysis of Long-Term Contracts in Copper Industry Chain 2021-2022_SMM
summary: SMM says copper concentrate transport/commercial terms (TCs) have fallen to 10-year lows, signaling tightening concentrate supply since 2015. It expects contract terms and copper cathode premiums for 2022 to rebound (e.g., Codelco higher). Logistics recovery, limited refined supply, and stronger cathode demand support firmer copper.

title: Korea's SKC to build $761 mn copper foil plant in Poland - The Korea Economic Daily Global Edition
summary: SKC plans to invest about $761 million to build a copper foil plant in Poland as part of expanding its EV battery materials business. The project, tied to SK Nexilis production, is intended to grow corporate value substantially by 2025, implying higher future copper demand from battery supply chains.

title: Kamoa Copper Awards China Nerin Engineering Contract for Direct-to-Blister Copper Smelter
summary: Kamoa Copper awarded China Nerin a basic engineering contract for a planned 500,000 tpa direct-to-blister flash smelter at the Kamoa-Kakula complex. The facility will use Metso Outotec technology and renewable power, processing most site concentrate into blister copper and improving in-country beneficiation.

title: Kamoa Copper Awards China Nerin Engineering Contract for Dir...
summary: Ivanhoe Mines’ Kamoa Copper awarded China Nerin a basic engineering contract for a planned 500 ktpa direct-to-blister flash smelter at Kamoa-Kakula in DR Congo. The project targets on-site beneficiation and sulphuric-acid byproduct output, but timing is months away, implying limited near-term copper price impact.

title: SKC to Invest 900 bln Won for Battery Copper Foil Factory in Poland
summary: SKC plans to invest 900 billion won in a battery copper foil factory in Poland. Producing copper foil for battery applications adds to projected industrial copper demand, which can be supportive for copper prices over the coming weeks. Details on start date and output ramp are not provided.

title: SKC to invest W900 bil. for battery copper foil factory in Poland
summary: SKC will invest 900 billion won ($761m) to build a battery copper foil plant in Poland, targeting 50,000 tons of annual capacity by 2024. The copper foil is used as an anode current collector in lithium-ion cells for EVs, supporting expectations of stronger copper demand in Europe.

title: Usha Resources Ltd.: Usha Resources to Resume Exploration at Lost Basin Gold-Copper Project
summary: Usha Resources said it has resumed exploration planning for its Lost Basin gold-copper project in Arizona after receiving a notice to excavate trenches. The company reports anomalous gold and “Copper Blowout” chip samples above 1% Cu and plans subsequent core drilling to define copper mineralization later in 2022.

title: Kamoa Copper Awards China Nerin Engineering Contract for
summary: Kamoa Copper awarded China Nerin Engineering a basic engineering contract for a planned 500 ktpa direct-to-blister flash smelter at the Kamoa-Kakula complex in the DRC. The facility is designed to process most concentrate output, produce blister copper and sulphuric acid, and use clean hydropower and sulphur capture technology.

title: Ridgestone Mining Inc.: Ridgestone Receives Permit for Drill Program on El Cobre Copper Target at Rebeico Project
summary: Ridgestone Mining says it has received permits from Mexico’s SEMARNAT to begin a maiden reverse-circulation drill program targeting the El Cobre copper structure at its Rebeico copper-gold project. The program follows surface sampling with reported copper grades up to 3.5%, supporting potential future copper resource definition.

title: Experts Forecast Rise For Copper As Demand is Expected to Jump Resulting from Infrastructure Bill
summary: Experts forecast higher copper prices, citing that an infrastructure bill should boost demand for copper used in power generation, transmission, and energy storage. The piece also references low copper inventory concerns and analysts’ expectations for LME prices returning toward/above $10,000 per tonne by year-end.

title: Experts Forecast Rise For Copper As Demand is Expected to Ju...
summary: Experts forecast a copper price rise as demand is expected to jump from an infrastructure bill. The piece cites copper’s role in energy transmission, generation and storage, and references low copper inventory concerns alongside optimistic banking targets and mining developments, reinforcing near-term bullish expectations for copper.

title: Fireweed Intersects 1.54% Copper, 5.42% Zinc, and 5.7 g/t Silver over 2.00 m and 2.35% Zinc, and 4.6 g/t Silver over 203.05 m in Step-Out Hole at Boundary Zone
summary: Fireweed Zinc reported step-out drill results at its Macmillan Pass (Yukon) Boundary Zone, including a copper-rich intersection grading 1.54% Cu over 2.0 m and 2.35% Zn over 203.05 m. The update highlights a new copper-zinc mineralization style but is unlikely to materially shift near-term metals prices beyond copper expectations.

title: Nornickel resolves dispute with Botswana, gets compensation
summary: Nornickel said it settled a dispute with Botswana’s government and BCL Group tied to its aborted Africa asset sale, including a 50% stake in the Nkomati joint venture mine. The company received agreed cash compensation and both sides waived claims. The resolution may lessen near-term nickel supply uncertainty.

title: Copper price rebounds from lowest in a month on upbeat US data
summary: Copper rebounded after hitting a month low, turning positive as buoyant U.S. data improved sentiment and raised hopes for stronger demand. The move followed risk-asset selling earlier, but thin inventories limited downside and supported the reversal, bringing prices back into gains on Thursday.

title: All eyes on China as LME copper spreads collapse
summary: The report says market calm has returned to the LME after last month’s action to protect short holders. The LME cash premium for copper collapsed from an extreme US$1,103.50/t before the intervention to about US$15.50/t at Tuesday’s close, indicating normalization in the copper market.

title: Will Copper Market See Resource Exhaustion amid Continued Declines in Global Copper Inventory?_SMM
summary: SMM reports global copper cathode inventories have fallen 56.8% since Q2 2021 to 519,000 mt by Nov 12, alongside strong LME backwardation reflecting tight supply. It cautions that “resource exhaustion” is unlikely as smelter output should rebound after power rationing, with a potential inventory pivot in December.

title: Copperstone Resources : Q3 2021 | MarketScreener
summary: Copperstone Resources’ Q3 2021 interim report says Sweden confirmed the Viscaria exploitation concession and the company is scaling up plans to reopen the mine in Kiruna. It highlights drilling positives, plans for higher production and concentrator capacity, and emphasizes copper demand/supply tightness.

title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zones Decreased 9,700 mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says domestic bonded copper inventories fell 9,700 mt to 206,500 mt by Nov 19, including declines in Shanghai and Guangdong zones. With the import window reopened and invoice restrictions boosting domestic spot premiums to a record 2,200 yuan/mt, importers transferred goods from bonded warehouses, tightening supply and supporting prices.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Dipped 4,800 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM reports Chinese copper inventories fell 4,800 mt to 79,500 mt by Nov 19, with declines in Guangdong and Jiangsu and first time below 80,000 mt this year. Late-week import arrivals slowed, though the import window may reopen next week. Overall inventory is expected to rise only marginally, supporting copper.

title: Chile′s economy benefits from worldwide copper prices | Business | Economy and finance news from a German perspective | DW
summary: DW reports that Chile benefits because higher worldwide copper prices lift revenues from its mining sector. It notes Chile’s position as the world’s largest copper producer and highlights the financial gains to public coffers, including due to state ownership in major mining.

title: Korea copper foil makers on bull run amid demand hopes
summary: Korea’s SKC plans to invest $761 million to build its first European copper foil plant in Poland. Produced by its battery-focused subsidiary SK Nexilis, the facility will make copper foil for electric vehicle batteries, indicating expanded output and potentially stronger copper demand expectations.

title: Silver Elephant Mining Corp.: Silver Elephant's Flying Nickel Spinout Has Upsized its Private Placement to $8.6 Million Including a $2.975 Million Lead Order From Strategic Investor
summary: Silver Elephant’s subsidiary Flying Nickel upsized its private placement to CAD 8.6 million, with Blackstone investing CAD 2.975 million. Proceeds (held in escrow pending approvals) will fund exploration and advancement of the Minago nickel project, supporting near-term nickel development prospects.

title: SKC finalises copper foil investment plans in Poland
summary: SKC finalized plans with the Polish government to build a copper foil manufacturing facility in Stalowa Wola, targeting Europe’s EV battery supply chain. Copper foil is used as anode current collectors in lithium-ion cells. The KRW 900bn investment aims for 50,000 tons/year capacity, with construction starting next year and completion in 2024.

title: New Warren County aluminum can manufacturer spotlighted in economic development update
summary: An economic update highlights Crown Cork & Seal’s new aluminum beverage-can manufacturing operation at Kentucky Transpark in Warren County. The plant began in June and is sized to produce 2.6 billion cans per year across two high-speed lines, boosting packaging output and expected aluminum demand in the near term.

title: Peru PM sparks controversy with mining sector by ruling out timeline extensions
summary: Peru’s Prime Minister said four mines in Ayacucho will not be allowed any extensions to their operational or shutdown timelines amid community protests. The mining industry protested, arguing it expects to keep investing and extend plans. With Peru a major copper producer, earlier closures weigh on near-term copper supply expectations.

title: MMC Norilsk Nickel: Nornickel settles dispute with botswana Government and BCL
summary: Nornickel (MMC Norilsk Nickel) said it settled its dispute with Botswana’s government and BCL Group related to the sale of its African asset interests, including a 50% stake in JV Nkomati. The parties waived claims and Nornickel received cash compensation, withdrawing legal actions. No production or supply changes were cited.

title: The inflection point is coming? A brief Analysis of the recent trend of Copper Market_SMM
summary: The analysis argues copper prices are supported in the near term by stagflation-leaning macro conditions, looser mine supply but strong smelting/secondary conditions, and—most importantly—a sustained 20-week inventory draw driven by disruptions, container shortages, and the energy crisis. It expects future policy tightening to temper upside into late-year.

title: The market is still short of spot copper transactions around long order negotiations [SMM Copper Weekly selection]_SMM
summary: SMM reports scarce spot copper turnover and continued difficulty seeing mining-trader transactions, with activity mainly in January–February shipment and long-order negotiations. It notes Antamina restarting and a Kamoa-Kakoula flash smelter engineering commission, but suggests these have limited immediate impact on the short-term copper concentrate balance.

title: Indonesia PM Jokowi vows to 'fight in any way' EU lawsuit over nickel export ban
summary: Indonesia’s President Jokowi vowed to defend the country’s nickel ore export ban as the EU escalates its challenge via the WTO. Indonesia imposed the ban from January 2020 to promote local processing. The dispute could introduce near-term uncertainty over nickel supply flows to global markets.

title: Cyprium Metals : Significant Copper Intersections from Nanadie Well Drilling
summary: Cyprium Metals reports assay results from final diamond holes at Nanadie Well, highlighting extensive copper sulphide mineralisation with several high-grade intercepts and confirming the deposit remains open. The company also notes elevated nickel values associated with some copper intervals, but provides no near-term production or supply impact.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Dipped 300 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM data show Chinese copper cathode inventories fell 300 mt week-on-week to 76,500 mt, the lowest level this year. The drawdown occurred in Guangdong and Tianjin as copper was shipped to higher-premium East China (Shanghai, Jiangsu). With premiums normalizing and import invoicing easing, inventories may tick up slightly by Friday.

title: Copper Rod Producers Using Copper Cathode Suspended Production amid High Premiums of Copper Cathode _SMM
summary: SMM reports spot copper cathode premiums rising above 2,000 yuan/mt as social inventory falls and customs tariffs are suspended. Downstream orders weaken under high premiums, while copper rod producers facing bearish shipments and higher finished-stock levels suspend or cut output. Persistent high premiums could further lower copper rod operating rates.

title: Nickel Prices to Fluctuate Rangebound amid Eased Market Pessimism_SMM
summary: Nickel prices recently fell due to pessimism on real-estate demand, then rebounded as sentiment improved. Lower coal prices and weaker demand failed to drive sharp nickel losses. Discounts to NPI narrowed, nickel sulphate demand stayed steady, inventory is low, and customs tax-control issues may raise spot premiums.

title: copper-fox-metals--ceo-elmer-stewart - Investing News
summary: Copper Fox Metals’ CEO discusses the Schaft Creek copper-molybdenum-gold-silver project and its preliminary economic assessment. The company highlights efforts to reduce processing costs and improve recoveries, and notes project economics are highly sensitive to copper price movements and exchange rates. No near-term supply shock or policy action is mentioned.

title: Nickel Investing News | Your Trusted Source for Investing Success
summary: The piece gives a nickel market review, arguing that Q1 2026 trends point to continued oversupply through 2026. It attributes the surplus to high nickel output from Indonesia and weaker demand from manufacturing and battery-related uses. It also discusses several nickel project and portfolio developments.

title: FOB Prices of Nickel Ore Stood Firm amid Tight Supply, CIF Prices Unchanged due to Weak Demand_SMM
summary: SMM says CIF nickel ore prices were flat, but FOB prices firmed as supply tightened. Philippines rainy season impeded mining and cargo handling, sharply reducing nickel ore exports, with further declines expected into December holidays. NPI plants buy cautiously due to weak NPI/stainless prices, keeping near-term volatility high but supportive for nickel.

title: Jobs saved at Liberty Aluminium Technologies in Kidderminster after take over
summary: Evtec will take over Liberty Aluminium Technologies’ plants in Kidderminster and Coventry after Liberty Steel’s sale process, saving over 170 jobs. The intervention follows Jaguar Land Rover backing of its supply-chain role. A separate Witham site will still close, with about 64 redundancies, reflecting ongoing restructuring pressures.

title: Mosaic Minerals Intersects 70 Meters Anomalous Nickel Zone
summary: Mosaic Minerals reports drilling intersected a 70-meter anomalous nickel zone (Pike Nickel East) and nearly 80 meters of nickeliferous mineralization, extending a nickel corridor by about 3.4 km and prompting plans for further drilling. Copper is also mentioned on the property, but aluminium appears only in risk wording.

title: Copper Prices Trend Upwards Following Xi-Biden Talks
summary: Copper prices rose following positive Xi-Biden virtual talks, with a weaker dollar and improved investor risk sentiment. The commentary frames the move as a potential rebound from the prior month’s decline and highlights copper producers likely to benefit. The piece also references a feasibility study using high base copper assumptions.

title: NORNICKEL BOARD OF DIRECTORS RECOMMENDS INTERIM DIVIDEND FOR 9M 2021
summary: Norilsk Nickel’s board recommended an interim dividend for nine months of 2021 totaling RUB 232.84 bn, with EGM set for Dec. 27 and dividend record date Jan. 14. The company is a major producer of nickel and copper, but the announcement does not change metal supply or demand expectations.

title: Extruded Aluminum Expands Ionia County, Michigan, Production Plant
summary: Extruded Aluminum Corporation (EAC) is expanding its Ionia County, Michigan extrusion plant by acquiring adjacent land to add production, handling, and processing equipment. The project is supported by a state grant and workforce training. Management cites growing demand for extruded aluminium products, reinforcing near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Ridgestone Mining Inc.: Ridgestone Announces Maiden Drill Program on Its High-Grade El Cobre Copper Property, Sonora, Mexico
summary: Ridgestone Mining announced a maiden RC drill program (about 14 holes/2,700 m) at its El Cobre high-grade copper property in Sonora, Mexico. The company cites past and recent surface sampling with copper grades up to 3.5%, targeting down-dip extensions under historical workings.

title: Cyprium Metals Ltd Significant Copper Intersections from Nanadie Well Drilling
summary: Cyprium Metals reported extensive copper sulphide intersections across all diamond drill holes at Nanadie Well, with mineralisation open along strike and across strike. The results will support a mineral resource estimate for a scoping study and preliminary metallurgical work. Elevated nickel and palladium values were found with key copper intervals.

title: Noble Options its Properties in Mann, Hanna, Duff and Reaume Twps and Sells its Patents in Kingsmill and Mabee Twps to Canada Nickel
summary: Noble Mineral Exploration entered a Letter of Intent with Canada Nickel to option mining claims and sell MRO patents. The properties cover a 20 km strike length with evidence of nickel, cobalt, PGM’s, rhodium and rare earths. The plan is to move toward a joint venture and fund exploration over four years.

title: Canada Nickel Expands Timmins Nickel District - Acquires 13 Additional Highly Prospective Nickel Properties in Timmins Region
summary: Canada Nickel reports acquiring 13 additional properties in the Timmins Nickel District, adding multiple ultramafic targets with historical nickel (and some copper) intercepts. The company highlights district-scale exploration potential, including twinning and updating historical resources, which can support improved expectations for future nickel supply.

title: Errawarra Resources : - Acquisition of Outstanding Nickel Prospect
summary: Errawarra Resources agreed to acquire an 80% interest in the AndoverWest nickel project adjacent to Azure’s Andover nickel sulphide discovery. The deal supports exploration funding through a share placement and outlines planned EM reprocessing and drilling on nickel sulphide targets, conditional on shareholder and regulatory approvals.

title: China NPI and Ferronickel Imports Dipped 2.42% in October and will Remain at This Level without Output Growth at New Production Lines in Indonesia_SMM
summary: SMM says China imported 299,000 mt of NPI and ferronickel in October, down 2.42% m/m but up 10.09% y/y, with Ni content at 46,000 mt. Despite a mid-November Indonesian plant fire, damage is limited, no major new Indonesia production lines were added, and Nov imports are expected to stay roughly unchanged.

title: China Aluminium Extrusion Exports Declined in October, But Likely to Increase in November amid Higher Profits_SMM
summary: China’s aluminium extrusion exports fell in October on the National Day holiday, but November is expected to rise as the SHFE/LME aluminium price ratio drops (to ~7.07) and export profits improve. Higher profitability and active trader interest suggest export volumes may reach or exceed prior highs in 2018.

title: Monsoon Season in Philippines Drove Declines in China Nickel Ore Imports in October_SMM
summary: SMM cited Chinese customs data showing nickel ore imports fell 21.3% m/m in October, with Philippines shipments down 22.8% m/m amid monsoon rainy-season disruptions to mining and shipments. Imports of nickel sulphide ore also dropped sharply. SMM expects declines to continue in November as more areas in the Philippines enter rainy season.

title: Universal Copper Continues to Advance the Poplar
summary: Universal Copper reports progress at its Poplar copper exploration project, including drilling, a mineral resource estimate update, and additional target work plus property acquisitions. It also reiterates that rising global demand for copper (EVs and electronics) should support higher copper prices, but no immediate supply or production change is announced.

title: Aluminium Spot Discount Shrinks to 60 yuan/mt amid Increasing Bonded Inventory_SMM
summary: SMM says Shanghai bonded-area aluminium ingot inventory has increased for four straight weeks and is expected to keep rising, widening import losses. Yangshan bonded premiums have fallen and holders have moved spots into bonded areas. Meanwhile aluminium imports keep falling while downstream restocks. Spot discount versus SHFE 2112 shrank to about 60 yuan/mt.

title: Operating Rates at Copper Processing Plants in Guangdong Hit a Low as Premiums Skyrocketed Amid Low Copper Inventory_SMM
summary: Guangdong copper cathode inventories fell to 6,527 mt (below 10,000 mt), driving Guangdong spot premiums to multi-year highs on Nov 22. Elevated premiums led downstream rod plants to cut output: six halted production and operating rates dropped to 65.8%. Firms expect further rate declines this week if premiums stay high.

title: White Metal Resources Corp.: White Metal Partner Noronex Continues Drilling at DorWit Copper-Silver Project, Namibia with Two Rigs at Witvlei Property and Initial Results Confirming Soil Anomalies
summary: White Metal Resources says its partner Noronex is drilling the DorWit Cu-Ag project in Namibia with two rigs and reports initial anomalous copper from the first 10 RC holes at Otjiwaru, including an intercept of 7.0 m at 0.5% Cu. Further drilling is ongoing at other targets.

title: DRC's Kamoa-Kakula to build blister copper smelter
summary: DRC’s Kamoa-Kakula mine signed contracts to build a 500,000 t/yr blister copper smelter to process concentrate from its concentrators into blister copper. The project also includes a 10-year processing deal to route early-phase concentrate to local smelting. Expansion plans target over 800,000 t/yr concentrate supply.

title: Approval of New Infrastructure Bill Sparks Enthusiasm for Copper
summary: The article says the approved U.S. infrastructure bill will fund electrification, transit and EV charging stations, expected to increase demand for industrial metals. It links this to copper and mentions battery materials such as nickel. It also highlights Kutcho Copper’s feasibility study as supportive for future copper supply.

title: U.S., European Union to lower tariffs on steel, aluminum
summary: The U.S. and EU plan to lower tariffs on steel and aluminum. By reducing trade frictions for aluminum, the decision is likely to improve import flows and raise near-term supply expectations, which generally puts downward pressure on aluminum prices. Copper is not directly addressed.

title: Aluminum Inventories Have Fallen To Critical Levels
summary: The piece says global aluminum is in deficit and that inventories are running down sharply, with LME depots in places like Detroit and Vlissingen virtually empty and total China stocks around about two weeks of demand. It cites shortages and rising risk of consumers competing for limited supply.

title: Material Matters: Iron Ore, Copper, Coal, Lead & Nickel
summary: Morningstar cuts iron ore assumptions but lifts average copper price expectations, citing potential US infrastructure-driven demand growth. Credit Suisse estimates the infrastructure bill could add 50–250ktpa copper demand and see supply risks easing. Nickel pig iron in China is said to have softened after exchange nickel price declines.

title: Material Matters: Iron Ore, Copper, Coal, Lead & Nickel
summary: Morningstar highlights US infrastructure stimulus as a potential demand tailwind for copper, estimating additional demand of 50–250ktpa. Separately, Credit Suisse notes nickel pig iron prices in China have softened after nickel declines on exchanges, with expectations of a surplus as production recovers—signaling mixed near-term pricing forces for both metals.

title: China's import of aluminum scrap increased by 82.4% in October compared with the same period last year._SMM
summary: China imported 86,265.32 tons of waste aluminum scrap in October, down month-on-month but up 82.4% versus a year earlier. Malaysia remained the top supplier at 23,969.92 tons. The larger scrap inflow suggests more recycling feedstock, potentially pressuring aluminium prices near term.

title: EU Steel/Aluminum Imports Quota Free of Section 232 Tariffs
summary: The U.S. and EU agreed to replace Section 232 tariffs on EU steel (25%) and aluminum (10%) with tariff-rate quotas effective Jan. 1, 2022. Eligible EU products enter the U.S. duty-free up to quota volumes; above-quota shipments face remaining tariffs. Quota administration and exclusions rules add some uncertainty.

title: Zijin Mining Approved Kamoa-Kakula Copper Constructing 500,000 mt/year Copper Smelter Project_SMM
summary: Zijin Mining approved internally the construction of a 500,000 mt/year copper smelter at the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Project in the DRC. The investment totals about $769 million, with $699 million for construction, funded from the project’s cash flow and planned over three years, boosting expectations for future copper processing capacity.

title: Will the Suspension of Exports of Indonesian Commodity Raw Materials Affect Domestic Aluminium Markets? _SMM
summary: Indonesia’s president reiterated plans to halt exports of commodity raw materials, including suspending bauxite exports in 2022 and copper in 2023. The article argues short-term bauxite supply impact is limited because imports from other regions and large domestic port stocks provide about three months of feed. The policy targets alumina output, supporting aluminium-linked sentiment; copper effects are more future-oriented.

title: What is the impact of Indonesia's president's reaffirmation of the ban on the export of tin, copper and bauxite?_SMM
summary: Indonesia’s president reiterated possible export bans: tin may stop in 2024, bauxite in 2022, and copper in 2023. SMM argues bauxite restrictions should have little short-term effect because inventories at ports are large and supply can be covered by other regions, limiting immediate aluminium disruption; copper effects are still pending assessment.

title: Aluminium Bahrain B S C : Alba Chairman of the Board of Directors Tours Reduction Line 6
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (ALBA) reported that its chairman visited Reduction Line 6, an aluminium smelting line inaugurated in late 2019. The company said Line 6 added 540,000 tonnes of capacity and is operating at 477.5 kA, supporting record financial performance. No new disruption or policy change was announced.

title: Surge Copper Corp.: Surge Copper Intersects 422 metres of 0.52% CuEq including 200 metres of 0.60% CuEq at West Seel and Provides Update on Resource Estimate
summary: Surge Copper Corp. announced assay results from a drill hole at its Ootsa Property, including 422 metres grading 0.52% CuEq and 200 metres at 0.60% CuEq, plus ongoing work toward an updated resource estimate. Investors awaited remaining drill results and the updated resource; the release is copper-focused.

title: Rockcliff Metals Corp.: Rockcliff Identifies Near Surface High-Grade Copper and Zinc Mineralization at the Copperman Property Including 4.35% CuEq Across 6.00 Metres and 3.33% CuEq Across 8.3 Metres
summary: Rockcliff Metals reported phase-one drill results at its Copperman property in Manitoba, highlighting near-surface, high-grade copper mineralization (e.g., several intervals above ~2% CuEq). The company cites encouraging widths and VMS-hosted copper-zinc potential, with an ongoing drill program planned.

title: Zijin sanctions $769m investment in Congo copper smelter
summary: Zijin and Ivanhoe approved a $769m direct-to-blister copper smelter adjacent to the Kamoa-Kakula concentrators in the DRC. The 500,000 tpa facility is designed to process most Kamoa-Kakula concentrates and reduce reliance on third-party smelters. Construction is expected to take about three years.

title: Indonesia plans to stop exports of raw materials following nickel ore shipment ban
summary: Indonesia plans to stop exports of raw materials after its nickel ore shipment ban, aiming to shift trade toward semi-finished and finished goods to boost downstream investment. The explicit nickel restriction is the immediate driver, while copper export shutdown is mentioned as a next-step possibility; aluminium is not addressed.

title: LME copper prices rise to an one-month high as demand is expected to improve_SMM
summary: LME copper futures closed about 1.3% higher at an one-month high, supported by China’s plan to increase real estate credit lines and signs of tighter supply, with falling warehouse inventories and premiums for fast delivery. Nickel also rose more than 2%, with receipts falling sharply, indicating tighter availability.

title: China Exports of Aluminium Wheel Fell Sharply in October, Unlikely to Recover Significantly in November and December_SMM
summary: SMM cites customs data showing China’s aluminium wheel exports fell 25.8% m/m to 65,400 mt in October, with most regions and key destinations declining. SMM attributes weakness to a late-August silicon price surge, higher processing fees, reduced alloy (A356) output, and lower customer purchases.

title: Production Capacity of High-Grade Nickel Matte to Increase 40,000 mt in Indonesia_SMM
summary: Weiming Group and Indigo signed an agreement to jointly develop and construct a 40,000 mt high-grade nickel matte project in Indonesia. The $400 million venture targets processing low-grade ore and tailings technology. Capacity in Indonesia would rise to 300,000 mt nickel content, reflecting expanded future nickel supply expectations.

title: Copper Cathode Premiums Plunged by 85% from Historical High Recorded Last Friday_SMM
summary: SMM reports China spot premiums for 1# copper cathode have fallen about 85% to around 350 yuan/mt from a historical high of ~2,200 yuan/mt. SHFE backwardation weakened as well. Causes cited include slower domestic inventory drawdowns, easing of VAT invoice issues for imports, and reduced downstream processing amid weak terminal demand.

title: Rio Tinto CEO and Mongolian Prime Minister discuss Oyu Tolgoi Copper and Gold Mine_SMM
summary: Rio Tinto’s CEO met Mongolia’s prime minister over unresolved issues threatening the expansion of Oyu Tolgoi, Mongolia’s major copper project. Delays, cost overruns, and investigations have led to potential contract renegotiations and possible restructuring. Uncertainty over timelines and financing may weigh on near-term copper supply expectations and sentiment.

title: Showa Aluminum, a Portfolio Company Owned by Apollo Funds, t...
summary: Showa Aluminum Can (Apollo Funds’ portfolio company) has agreed to acquire Mitsubishi Aluminum’s aluminum rolled & extruded products business and shares of Universal Can. The deal aims to create a more integrated aluminum packaging and engineering group, potentially supporting aluminum downstream demand and production utilization as closing nears.

title: Zijin approves investment of US $769 million in Congo copper smelter_SMM
summary: Zijin approved a US$769 million investment for a smelter tied to its Kamoa-Kakula copper project in the DRC. The plant (blister copper) is intended to process more concentrate internally, reducing third-party smelter reliance. First phase output is underway, with construction expected to take about three years.

title: Indonesia plans to stop exports of raw materials following nickel ore shipment ban | Politics
summary: Indonesia plans to halt exports of raw materials as it moves toward downstream processing. After implementing a nickel ore shipment ban, President Widodo suggests bauxite export limits next year, copper exports later, and further restrictions thereafter. The policy aims to force exports of semi-finished/finished products.

title: SMM: Expanding Application of Secondary Aluminium Will Boost the Demand of Silicon_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s secondary aluminium production is concentrated and increasingly makes silicon-aluminium cast alloys such as ADC12 and A356.2. It links higher silicon prices to higher aluminium alloy/ingot values versus primary aluminium and describes expanding secondary aluminium applications in autos and communications, supporting growing demand for silicon-aluminium feedstock and alloys.

title: Three Valley Copper Corp. Announces Closing of Bought Deal O...
summary: Three Valley Copper closed a bought-deal equity offering to fund advancement and exploration of its Minera Tres Valles copper project in Chile, including plans for first caving operations in January 2022 and rising production in 2022. The release also cites supportive copper-price conditions and EV/infrastructure demand.

title: Horizonte Minerals arranges US$633mn funding package to fully finance Brazil nickel project
summary: Horizonte Minerals reportedly arranged a US$633mn funding package to fully finance its nickel project in Brazil. The financing reduces uncertainty around project completion and can support sentiment for nickel supply prospects, potentially exerting upward or stabilizing expectations for nickel prices depending on construction timelines.

title: Puma Exploration Updates on Copper Transaction With Melius M...
summary: Puma Exploration reports progress on its transaction with Melius Metals to unlock value from Puma’s copper projects. Melius has advanced approvals, completed technical reports, funded additional activities, and started a 2,000-meter drilling program at the Chester copper deposit, with claims transferred to Puma.

title: Puma Exploration Updates on Copper Transaction With Melius
summary: Puma Exploration reported progress on its transaction with Melius Metals, granting Melius an option to acquire Puma’s copper projects. Melius completed technical reports, closed financings, and started a 2,000-meter drilling program at the Chester copper deposit, including additional payments and related corporate approvals for listing and financing.

title: Nickel prices boosted by low inventories and China outlook
summary: Nickel neared seven-year highs as LME on-warrant inventories fell to 62,304 tonnes from over 200,000 in April, signaling tighter supply. The rally was reinforced by expectations that China may provide fiscal support despite property-sector distress, boosting demand outlook; prices later eased slightly from peaks.

title: Nickel, Industrial Metals Rise As China Property Optimism Returns
summary: Nickel and other industrial metals rose as optimism about China’s property sector returned. The headline implies improved demand expectations for construction-related materials, providing near-term support to prices. By extension, the move is likely to affect copper and aluminium alongside nickel.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 114,000 wmt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chinese nickel ore inventories at major ports fell 114,000 wmt week-on-week to 9.35 million wmt as of Nov 26, with Ni content at 74,300 mt. The decline is linked to fewer shipments during the Philippines wet season, alongside recovering NPI production. Further near-term inventory declines are expected from slower supply and stronger demand.

title: Secondary Copper Rod Plants in Henan Xinxiang to Suspend Production_SMM
summary: SMM reports that Xinxiang, Henan issued a red heavy-air-pollution warning, prompting local secondary copper rod plants to suspend production from Nov 25 to Nov 29. The temporary shutdown aims to curb pollution peaks and likely tightens short-term copper rod supply expectations, providing upward support for copper prices.

title: Is the weather going to change in Peru, the world's second-largest copper producer? The opposition proposes to impeach the left-wing president_SMM
summary: Peruvian opposition lawmakers submitted a bill to impeach President Pedro Castillo. The article notes Castillo had promised higher taxes on mining and oil, which previously alarmed investors about stagnant copper production. The impeachment effort is framed as a potential boon for miners, easing perceived policy risk for Peru’s copper market.

title: Forum Energy Metals Corp.: Rio Tinto Reports Final Results at Rafuse Target; Exploration Update at Forum's Janice Lake Copper/Silver Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Forum Energy Metals reports final drill assay results from Rio Tinto’s 2021 program at the Janice Lake copper/silver project in Saskatchewan, highlighting expanded high-grade copper at Rafuse and related targets, plus copper boulder discoveries. It also notes Rio Tinto will not fund 2022 exploration and a $100,000 payment is due to complete the earn-in.

title: Evertiq - Indonesia's export restrictions on nickel likely to impac...
summary: TrendForce reports Indonesia intends to end exports of unprocessed nickel ores (and also mentions copper and tin), which could disrupt global raw-material supply chains for EV batteries. With rising nickel demand for NCM cathodes, potential tightening supports expectations for higher nickel prices within weeks, though copper effects are less direct.

title: South32 to buy $1.55bn stake in South Gorda copper mine
summary: South32 will buy a 45% stake in Chile’s Sierra Gorda copper mine for $1.55bn upfront, plus up to $500m contingent payments, after KGHM Polska failed to exercise pre-emptive rights. The project is expected to produce about 180kt of copper this year, but closure is planned for early 2022.

title: Chile's election may affect 1/3 of the world's copper supply_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chile’s election could determine the fate of a proposed royalty tax reform that would base Chile’s copper royalty on output rather than profits and could rise up to 75% when copper prices exceed $4/lb. Industry warns this may force mine closures and cause investment delays, pressuring copper supply expectations.

title: Guinea bauxite can make up for Indonesia ban, China's Antaike says
summary: Indonesia may ban bauxite exports from 2022 to boost domestic processing, but China’s Antaike says the impact on China’s aluminium industry should be limited. It argues Guinea’s large bauxite capacity surplus, mostly shipped to China for alumina production, can replace Indonesia’s shortfall, with room to increase imports further.

title: Guinea bauxite can make up for Indonesia ban, China's Antaike says | 1450 AM 99.7 FM WHTC
summary: Indonesia may restrict bauxite exports from 2022, threatening China’s aluminium ore supply. Antaike says Guinea’s bauxite capacity surplus—mainly shipped to China for alumina production—could fully replace Indonesian volumes. China’s bauxite imports remain heavily reliant on Guinea and Indonesia, supporting expectations of minimal disruption to aluminium supply.

title: Guinea bauxite can make up for Indonesia ban, China's Antaike says | Kat Country 98.9
summary: Indonesia may restrict bauxite exports from 2022, threatening aluminium ore supply to China. Antaike says Guinea’s bauxite capacity surplus—largely shipped to China for refining into alumina—can offset Indonesia’s potential shortfall. China’s bauxite imports remain heavily sourced from Guinea, supporting stable near-term aluminium expectations.

title: Guinea bauxite can make up for Indonesia ban, China's Antaike says | WTVB | 1590 AM · 95.5 FM
summary: Reuters reports Antaike says a possible Indonesia bauxite export ban from 2022 would have little impact on China’s aluminium industry because Guinea has ample spare capacity. China would increase bauxite imports from Guinea to replace Indonesian supply. Indonesia’s share is 15% of China bauxite imports.

title: Nickel prices rise emotionally and fall back into a volatile market after cooling down [selection of SMM Nickel Weekly]_SMM
summary: SMM’s nickel weekly report says nickel rebounded from below 150,000 yuan/ton to above it this week, driven mainly by improving macro sentiment and low inventories rather than a major change in fundamentals. Supply is stable and demand growth is not negative; import inflows may stay limited, keeping volatility high.

title: LME copper and other industrial metals plummeted and the market was in safe-haven mode._SMM
summary: LME copper and other industrial metals fell sharply as fears about a potentially vaccine-resistant COVID variant drove risk aversion, tighter travel restrictions, a higher dollar, and lower oil and equity prices. Analysts cited tight copper fundamentals and low inventories, but overall demand concerns outweighed, pressuring prices for weeks.

title: Xinchang Copper: Cai Yunlei, the "Invisible Champion" of Guangming_SMM
summary: The piece profiles Henan Xinchang Copper Group, highlighting its recycled-copper processing (low-oxygen copper), high utilization recovery rates, and energy-saving upgrades at its continuous casting/rolling lines. It also cites ongoing cooperation with downstream users and plans for higher-end conductor products, but no immediate market-changing event.

title: Indonesia is considering a ban on the export of copper concentrates from 2023_SMM
summary: Indonesia is considering a ban on exporting copper concentrates from 2023 to boost domestic processing. Traders expect limited impact because China relies only slightly on Indonesian concentrate imports and new smelter capacity in Indonesia should absorb concentrates by 2024, keeping supply sufficient and reducing urgency for price moves.

title: The planned Minnesota high-grade nickel mine will be rare in the United States._SMM
summary: Aitkin County’s Tamarack project in Minnesota, a planned high-grade nickel mine (with copper by-product potential), is entering the licensing process amid environmental opposition. The U.S. is investing to expand nickel refining capacity, and demand for nickel in stainless steel and EVs is rising, supporting bullish sentiment despite uncertain permitting timelines.

title: Indonesia Contemplates Implementing Ban on Copper Concentrate Exports in 2023_SMM
summary: Reports say Indonesia is considering a ban on copper concentrate exports from 2023. Yet analysts expect limited effect on China because Indonesian concentrate is only a small fraction of China’s imports and supply should remain sufficient. Planned smelter capacity (Grasberg and others) would process most domestic concentrate after 2024.

title: Second Round of Long-Term Copper Concentrate Contract Negotiations Began_SMM
summary: SMM reports a second round of 2022 long-term copper concentrate contract negotiations among major Chinese smelters and miners, with parties largely agreeing on next-year supply/demand but differing on treatment charges (TCs). Lower proposed TCs and smelter reluctance to purchase—linked to Olympic Games environmental controls affecting Q1 operating rates—signal near-term weakness for copper demand.

title: SSR Mining Announces Positive Exploration Results At Copper Hill And Increases Ownership To 70%
summary: SSR Mining reported positive exploration results at its Copper Hill project and increased its ownership stake to 70%. The news is copper-related via project prospects, but it is early-stage exploration rather than operating or production guidance, so any impact on near-term copper market supply expectations is likely limited.

title: Rio Tinto to take majority stake in Janice Lake copper-silver project
summary: Rio Tinto Exploration Canada will acquire a 51% majority stake in Forum Energy’s Janice Lake copper-silver project after funding additional exploration. The move follows prior earn-in conditions and drilling that expanded high-grade copper mineralisation. Forum will pay $100,000 cash to fulfil obligations, but no production change is indicated.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Dalmacia Drilling Delivers Encouraging Initial Copper Results at Battery Mineral Resources Punitaqui Mine
summary: Battery Mineral Resources said drilling at its Punitaqui mine complex’s Dalmacia target returned encouraging assay results, including multiple high-grade copper intercepts. The company expects Punitaqui to resume copper concentrate production in mid-to-late 2022, implying improved prospects for future copper supply and supporting copper sentiment.

title: NORNICKEL 2021 ANNUAL CAPITAL MARKETS DAY: NAVIGATING THE TRANSITION TO A NET ZERO WORLD
summary: Norilsk Nickel’s Capital Markets Day highlights a large increase in capex, including upgrades to concentration and smelting capacity in Russia and capacity expansions for nickel refining and copper refining. The company also raised long-term production growth targets for nickel and copper, reinforcing expectations of future supply.

title: Russia's Nornickel ups investment forecast by $6 billion over next decade
summary: Nornickel raised its 2021-2030 investment estimate by $6 billion to $35 billion, citing higher construction costs and additional energy and production infrastructure upgrades. Management also pushed out the peak spending period to 2028 and increased its long-term output forecast, implying potential future nickel capacity. The note mentions energy upgrades after accidents.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Drills Deepest Hole To Date at The Kenbridge Nickel Project and Intersects 3.18% Ni, 0.19% Cu Over 1.05 Metres. Updates Progress at The Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project, NW Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. announced that drilling at its Kenbridge nickel project reached the deepest hole to date and intersected 3.18% nickel over 1.05 metres, with 0.19% copper. It also updated progress at a nickel-copper-cobalt project in NW Ontario, supporting positive sentiment for nickel.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Drills Deepest Hole To Date at The Kenbridge Nickel Project and Intersects 3.18% Ni, 0.19% Cu Over 1.05 Metres. Updates Progress at The Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project, NW Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. announced drill results at its Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in northwestern Ontario, including a 3.18% Ni intersection and a small associated copper grade (0.19% Cu) over 1.05 metres. The update signals exploration progress but does not mention production changes or market supply disruption.

title: Nornickel 2021 Annual Capital Markets Day: Leading the
summary: Norilsk Nickel outlined an expanded 2021-2030 capex plan, raising investment by $6bn to $35bn with significant allocations to ESG and energy modernization. The company also raised strategic production growth targets for 2030+ including 25-35% higher nickel volumes and 25-35% copper growth, supporting demand-linked sentiment.

title: Smaller batches, rotating selections give craft breweries leg up on aluminum can supply issues
summary: Craft breweries say they’re struggling to obtain aluminum beverage cans as shortages persist since COVID-era demand increases. The problem worsens because Ball Corporation requires large minimum orders of pre-printed cans and storage capacity for bulk deliveries. Brewers respond with smaller batches, rotating can usage, and sticker label printing.

title: Golden Deeps : Very High-Grade Copper-Lead-Silver Intersections at Nosib
summary: Golden Deeps reports diamond drilling at its Nosib project intersected thick copper-bearing mineralisation, including semi-massive bornite with chalcopyrite grading up to ~6% Cu on spot XRF, with overall intervals up to ~1% Cu from surface to ~46m. Results are pending lab assays.

title: Where will Russia's plan to abolish aluminum export tariffs and increase the global supply of aluminum prices?_SMM
summary: Russia’s plan to abolish aluminium export tariffs on alloys for Rusal is expected to raise global aluminium supply. The article links the announcement to a sell-off in European and US spot markets, lower premiums, and falling LME/Shanghai prices. It also notes ongoing regional inventory pressure.

title: Global Nickel Demand to Increase, Battery Industry Becomes the Main Driving Force for Consumption _SMM
summary: SMM reports DISER expects global nickel finished products consumption to reach 2.7 million mt in 2021 (+15%), rising further in 2022-2023. While stainless steel remains the main user, the electric vehicle battery industry is described as the future growth driver, supported by decarbonisation measures and rising EV demand to offset COVID impacts.

title: Russia: Norilsk Nickel production is expected to be 20.5-215000 tons in 2022_SMM
summary: Norilsk Nickel forecasts nickel production of 205,000-215,000 tons in 2022 and higher output for 2023-2024, while estimating a global nickel surplus of 60,000 tons in 2022. This points to increased near-term nickel supply. The firm also mentions copper output guidance and sizable capex plans.

title: Norilsk Nickel Company of Russia has raised its investment forecast for the next decade by 6 billion US dollars._SMM
summary: Norilsk Nickel raised its 2021-2030 investment forecast by $6 billion to $35 billion due to higher construction costs and added spending on energy and production infrastructure upgrades. The firm expects its capex peak to shift from 2026 to 2028, supporting improved nickel production plans after recent accidents.

title: Capstone Mining Corp.: Capstone and Mantos Copper Combine to Create Capstone Copper, a Premier Copper Producer With Transformational Near-Term Growth
summary: Capstone Mining and Mantos Copper announced a definitive merger to form Capstone Copper, positioning the combined company as a premier copper producer. The release highlights large near-term growth ramp-ups at Chilean operations (including Mantoverde and Mantos Blancos) and provides output, reserves, and funding details that can influence short-term copper market expectations.

title: Capstone and Mantos Copper Combine to Create Capstone Copper, a Premier Copper Producer With Transformational Near-Term Growth
summary: Capstone Mining and Mantos Copper agreed to combine, forming Capstone Copper, a larger copper producer focused on Chilean assets. The deal highlights near-term production ramp-ups and growth plans at Mantoverde and Mantos Blancos, aiming for higher annual output by 2024. The transaction is presented as transformational for copper supply expectations.

title: Copper under pressure on Omicron uncertainties
summary: Copper prices fell 0.9% as Omicron uncertainties raised concerns about near-term demand and growth. China manufacturing data was stronger, and LME copper stocks are falling, limiting losses. Nickel also eased with low stocks and high cash premiums, while aluminium slipped slightly amid broader logistics and supply tightness worries.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28 Files Q3 2021 Financial Statements
summary: Nickel 28 reported strong Q3 2021 results from its 8.56% interest in the Ramu nickel-cobalt operation. It repaid an operating-debt tranche and triggered a cash distribution, citing higher nickel prices versus quarter economics, strong production and sales, and improved margins and payability.

title: Nickel 28 Files Q3 2021 Financial Statements
summary: Nickel 28 reported Q3 2021 results, highlighting strong performance from its 8.56% Ramu nickel-cobalt operation in Papua New Guinea. It notes operating debt repayment and a US$3.2 million cash distribution, higher quarterly nickel margins, and sales of 8,085 tonnes of contained nickel.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: US EV Battery Supply Chain: Drilling Continues to Deliver High-Grade Nickel and Copper Intercepts at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reported new assay results from 11 drill holes at its Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project, including thick intersections with high nickel and copper grades outside the main resource area. The company expects the results to expand the size and extent of known resources, but it provides no immediate production or supply changes.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: US EV Battery Supply Chain: Drilling Continues to Deliver High-Grade Nickel and Copper Intercepts at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals reported continued high-grade nickel and copper assay intercepts from new drill holes at its Tamarack Nickel Project in Minnesota, particularly in the CGO West area outside the main resource zone. Management says results may expand nickel-copper resources, but no immediate production or supply-impact data is provided.

title: Copper hits two-week low on Omicron uncertainty and Fed comments
summary: Copper fell to a two-week low as Omicron uncertainty hurt demand and growth expectations and Powell’s comments suggested faster Fed tapering. LME copper stocks are declining, but further selling followed the U.S. open. The piece also highlights tight nickel inventories and easing aluminium prices amid the same macro backdrop.

title: Aluminum can change could have costly impact at local breweries  :: WRAL.com
summary: WRAL reports Ball Corp. will raise the minimum can-order quantities and increase prices for some customers, starting Jan. 1. Brewers say the changes could raise costs and force smaller breweries to find alternative suppliers due to higher cash outlays and logistics constraints. This implies firmer near-term aluminum can demand/pricing.

title: Capstone Mining and Mantos Copper merge_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Capstone Mining and Mantos Copper will merge to form Capstone Copper, an Americas-focused copper producer. The company plans to expand output by about 45% to 260,000 tonnes per year by 2024 via ongoing projects and stakes in mines in the US, Mexico, and Chile. Deal closure is targeted for Q1 2022.

title: Turquoise Hill agrees to Oyu Tolgoi's transitional budget of $75 million for copper and gold mines_SMM
summary: Turquoise Hill approved a US$75 million transitional budget to keep Oyu Tolgoi’s underground expansion moving amid ongoing negotiations with Mongolia and Rio Tinto. The deal reduces delay and funding risk for the project’s copper output, which had faced cost overruns and possible contract disputes.

title: Aluminum can distribution change could drastically impact local Utah breweries
summary: Ball Corporation is raising minimum orders for non-contract customers to about five truckloads (~1 million cans) per beverage, from one truckload. It also stops warehousing those customers’ cans and increases price-per-can by nearly 50% for some. Utah breweries report margin pressure and potential retail price hikes.

title: China Nickel Downstream Sectors PMI Remained in a Contraction Range in November_SMM
summary: SMM data shows China’s nickel downstream PMI remained in contraction in November (49.92) with weak new orders (48.33). Despite improved production after power rationing eased, nickel sulphate entered short-term oversupply and purchase-price sub-index fell with weakening nickel prices, suggesting bearish near-term nickel demand.

title: A Philippine Nickel Mine Will be Decommissioned in End-2021, Global Nickel Supply May Tighten Further_SMM
summary: DMCI Holdings said its Berong nickel mine in the Philippines will run out of resources and be decommissioned and repaired before end-2021. As the Philippines is a key nickel ore supplier to China, the suspension could further tighten global nickel supply amid an ongoing INSG-noted supply gap.

title: Altamira Gold Corp.: Altamira Gold Discovers Copper-Gold Porphyry- Style Stockwork Mineralization at the Santa Helena Project
summary: Altamira Gold Corp. started an initial drill program at its Santa Helena porphyry copper-gold project in Brazil. Surface quartz stockwork shows copper- and gold-bearing mineralization over at least 100m with IP chargeability/resistivity anomalies extending to depth. Drilling aims to test the porphyry-style copper-gold potential.

title: Copper rebounds as virus concerns fade
summary: Copper rose about 1% on the LME as Omicron demand concerns eased and investors regained risk appetite. The piece cites low warehouse inventories as extra support. It also flags Chile royalty bill progress, nickel mine depletion, and aluminium’s tight nearby supply via 14-year-low stocks and a cash premium.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Pacific Ridge Intersects 437 Metres of 0.61% CuEq or 0.96 g/t AuEq, Including 291.7 Metres of 0.75% CuEq or 1.18 g/t AuEq, in First Drill Hole at Kliyul Copper-Gold Project; Best Kliyul Interval Ever
summary: Pacific Ridge announced assay results from its first drill hole at the Kliyul copper-gold project, reporting 437m of 0.61% copper equivalent and including higher-grade intervals. Management highlights the best results from the project to date and discusses plans for expanded drilling, with no near-term production changes.

title: Capstone Mining signs merger deal with Mantos Copper
summary: Capstone Mining will merge with Mantos Copper to form Capstone Copper, targeting copper expansion across operations in the US, Mexico and Chile. The combined firm is planned to raise production from 175,000t (2021 base) toward 260,000tpa by 2024, and potentially 380,000tpa after Santo Domingo.

title: SMM Outlook: Copper Prices Likely to Stay Weak in December_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM expects copper prices to remain volatile and weak in December. It cites low LME/SHFE inventories providing some support, but notes bearish demand risks from COVID lockdowns and sluggish real estate, while smelters plan year-end output catch-up, premiums normalized, and support weakened.

title: Adyton hits significant copper at Feni Island 6.4m @ 5.1%
summary: Adyton Resources announced significant copper intersections from its Feni Island drill hole ADK004, including 5.1% Cu over 6.4m and higher-grade sub-intervals. The results confirm a potential copper system at the Kabang corridor, but remain early exploration with no immediate supply change.

title: Craft brewery owners sound alarm on rising cost of aluminum cans due to inflation
summary: Craft brewery owners report aluminum can prices are skyrocketing due to inflation and higher energy costs, making cans harder to source and forcing some businesses to raise prices. Ball Corp. increased can pricing and minimum orders, indicating supply tightening and supportive near-term demand/cost pressures for aluminum.

title: Betting against coal, Rio Tinto taps Quebec's hydro power to produce green aluminum
summary: Rio Tinto plans a $110 million expansion of its Quebec AP60 aluminum smelter, adding 16 smelting cells and using Quebec hydro power to cut emissions versus industry norms. The company frames it as a bet against coal-based smelting and expects growing aluminium demand, amid market tightness mainly linked to China.

title: Carbon brakes aluminium supply response to booming prices
summary: China, the world’s largest aluminium producer, continues to face a shortage of primary metal. It imported an additional 140,000 tonnes in October, lifting year-to-date imports to 1.27 million tonnes. The headline indicates aluminium supply tightness responding to previously booming prices, supporting near-term price expectations.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventories Down 7,200 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium billet stocks in five major consumption areas fell 7,200 mt (down 9.14%) to 71,700 mt, extending seven straight weeks of decline. The drop is attributed to weaker billet arrivals, led by Foshan. North-west transport remains disrupted, so inventories may fall but more slowly, with possible week-to-week reversal.

title: Huayou Cobalt Commissioned Hydrometallurgical Nickel Smelting Project in Indonesia_SMM
summary: Huayou Cobalt commissioned its hydrometallurgical nickel smelting project in Indonesia at PT. Huayue Nickel Cobalt after completing equipment installation and testing. Using laterite ore, it targets 60,000 mt of nickel and 7,800 mt of cobalt annually. The first batch has been produced and performance indicators are qualified.

title: Fujifilm increases surcharge for aluminum offset plates
summary: Fujifilm said it will raise by 0.39 GBP per sqm the surcharge for aluminum offset printing plates from Jan 1, 2022. It attributes the move to unprecedented aluminum price increases plus higher energy, logistics, chemicals, and packaging costs, and adds a UK order charge to offset local logistics expenses.

title: Copper slips as Omicron spreads and China slowsows
summary: Copper prices slipped as Omicron fears and slowing China growth reduced demand outlooks. LME copper was down 0.3% on the day and around 4% on the week, despite strong year-to-date performance. China growth and property guidance stayed cautious, while aluminium inventories rose 16% and other base metals moved mixed.

title: Successful trial production of Huayue Wet process Nickel Project Huayu Cobalt Industry Nickel Plate achieves a key breakthrough from 0 to 1_SMM
summary: Huayou Cobalt announced that its Indonesia Morowali laterite nickel wet-smelting project (60,000 t/y nickel) has completed installation, entered trial production, and produced a first batch of products with qualified indicators. The update is expected to improve the company’s nickel self-supply and integration, lifting nickel sentiment.

title: Trial production of Indonesian Nickel Joint Venture of Huayou Cobalt Co., Ltd._SMM
summary: Huayou Cobalt said its Indonesian smelting joint venture reached first trial production, with product quality meeting requirements and producing mixed hydroxide precipitate that can be processed into nickel and cobalt battery chemicals. It plans large annual nickel output using HPAL, but no full-production timeline was given.

title: Canada Nickel Continues to Demonstrate Significant Improvements in Metallurgical Performance at Crawford Nickel Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel reported metallurgical testwork at its Crawford nickel sulphide project, achieving 61% nickel recovery and 37% nickel concentrate grade from lower-grade samples, above PEA modeled performance. The company says the optimized flowsheet improves recovery and will proceed with variability testing for feasibility.

title: China's Chengtun to invest US$245m in Indonesian nickel matte project
summary: China’s Chengtun plans to invest US$245 million in an Indonesian nickel matte project. The move points to future processing capacity for nickel feedstock in Indonesia, which can increase expectations for supply and likely pressure nickel prices in the near term as traders price in potential output growth.

title: US delays removal of UK tariffs on steel, aluminum due to post-Brexit fears
summary: The US Commerce Department is delaying removal of Trump-era tariffs on UK steel and aluminum, citing UK threats to trigger Article 16 of the Northern Ireland protocol. The 25% steel and 10% aluminum tariffs remain, while negotiations with the UK stall, adding uncertainty over future trade terms despite UK denial of protocol linkage.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Drills 6.52% Nickel over 0.8 Metres within 4.5 Metres of 2.04% Nickel plus 12 Metres of 1.13% Nickel at Lappvattnet
summary: Gungnir Resources announced final 2021 drill results from its Lappvattnet nickel deposit in Sweden, reporting high-grade nickel intersections including 6.52% Ni over 0.8 metres within a wider mineralized zone. The company also notes surface EM geophysics underway and expects new assays to feed future resource updates.

title: Nornickel lifts up investment plans by billions of dollars
summary: Russia’s Nornickel increased its investment guidance by billions of dollars, citing construction cost inflation and expanded modernization for energy and production assets in the Arctic. It plans upgrades including new/expanded concentrators and smelter capacity, plus a new copper production facility in Monchegorsk, alongside Arctic logistics debottlenecking.

title: US$5-billion hoard of aluminum in Vietnam may never be seen again
summary: Vietnam’s customs holds about 1.8 million tonnes of seized aluminium worth roughly $5bn, but it’s unlikely to be released soon amid an ongoing investigation. With China curbing supply and global inventories drawn down rapidly, the hoard’s inaccessibility reinforces a tight aluminium market and supports higher prices.

title: Chinese Mining Company to Construct a High-Grade Nickel Matte Project with Capacity of 40,000 mt/year in Ni Content in Indonesia_SMM
summary: Hongsheng International Resources, a Chengtun Mining Group subsidiary, plans to form Chengmai Nickel in Indonesia via a JV. The project targets a high-grade nickel matte output of 40,000 mt/year in nickel content, with total investment of $350m. Funding will be staged based on requirements.

title: Montana craft brewers navigate a crunch in aluminum can supply chains
summary: Montana craft brewers report severe shortages and much higher prices for aluminum beverage cans. Supply-chain clogs, increased can-maker minimum order requirements, and longer lead times force breweries to use intermediaries, raising can costs. The story cites aluminum rising to a decade high and says beer price increases may follow for customers soon.

title: London copper falls on fears of Sino-U.S. tensions, China inventory glut
summary: London copper eased as Asian markets turned risk-averse on renewed Sino-U.S. tensions. Reuters cited signs of a China copper inventory glut: ShFE stockpiles hit the highest since late October and the Chinese refined copper spot premium fell from a record. LME copper fell about 0.5% to $9,460/t.

title: 1.566 billion! Shengtun Mining Industry plans to build a high nickel matte project with an annual production capacity of 40,000 tons in Indonesia._SMM
summary: Shengtun Mining plans to build a high-nickel matte project in Indonesia’s Weidabe Industrial Park with 40,000 tons/year capacity, investing about $350 million. It is intended to supply battery-grade nickel sulfate for ternary batteries, with product underwritten by JV partners. This expands nickel-related output and feedstock expectations.

title: The Output of Copper at Codelco Declined YoY in October_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Cochilco data cited by SMM show Codelco’s October copper output fell 9.9% YoY to 144,100 mt. BHP’s Escondida output dropped 15.2% to 84,700 mt, while Glencore/Anglo American’s Collahuasi rose 17.3% to 49,500 mt.

title: Copper Cathode Inventory in Guangdong Hit Lowest for the Year. When Will the Inventory Bottom?_SMM
summary: SMM data shows Guangdong copper cathode inventories at 5,900 mt on Dec 3, the lowest for the year and near historical lows. A smelter’s output is still recovering and import invoice issues limit arrivals, while downstream restocking resumed in December. Inventories likely stay low into late December, supporting copper prices.

title: Copper Inventory in China Bonded Area Dipped 5,700 mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported China’s domestic bonded copper inventories fell 5,700 mt to 183,500 mt by Dec 3, the eighth straight week of decline. Shanghai and Guangdong inventories also dropped. Warrant-related inflows were smaller and stronger customs quarantine plus slower port efficiency reduced incoming shipments, tightening near-term supply expectations.

title: Zinc leads LME base metals' ascent; nickel edges over $20,000/t
summary: The piece notes that nickel is edging above $20,000/t, implying improving near-term sentiment for nickel. It also references aluminium supply staying intact despite output curtailments and mentions severe shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz, factors that can affect aluminium transport and pricing.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 169,000 wmt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported Chinese port nickel ore inventories fell 169,000 wmt to 9.18 million wmt (72,100 mt Ni content) by Dec 3. Seven major ports combined declined 129,000 wmt. Backlogs and slow shipments at Lanshan and shipping difficulties at Jingtang reduced arrivals, and inventories are expected to continue sliding short-term.

title: HK-listed MMG to cease copper operations at Peru mine
summary: HK-listed MMG said it will stop copper production from its Las Bambas mine in Peru by mid-December, citing unresolved demands from the Chumbivilcas community despite government meetings. The mine has faced prior shipment blockades, and concentrate stockpiles have risen, but output loss threatens near-term copper supply.

title: China's Chengtun to invest $245m in Indonesian nickel matte project
summary: China’s Chengtun plans a $245m investment in an Indonesian nickel matte project (PT ChengMach Nickel), producing about 40,000 tpa on a nickel-content basis. The JV, with Chengtun majority ownership, adds to Indonesia’s nickel feedstock pipeline, potentially improving supply expectations for nickel processing.

title: SHFE/LME Nickel Price Ratio Rallied_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports the SHFE/LME nickel price ratio rose this week after prior weakness. Renewed COVID-19 fears have raised concerns about overseas nickel demand, while China’s demand stays stable and nickel arrivals fall. Inventories declined, but planned shipments of nickel briquette and plate could lift supply, limiting upside.

title: HSBC Securities Analyst Predicts Copper Consumption Will Drive These Stocks to New Highs by 2024
summary: HSBC’s analyst argues copper demand is being driven by manufacturing, residential/construction, EVs, and renewable power, which require substantially more copper. On the supply side, Peru and Chile (large producers) face political/regulatory risks, keeping the market tight and potentially in deficit, supporting a bullish copper outlook.

title: Las Bambas Copper Mine in Peru to close production by mid-December_SMM
summary: Las Bambas in Peru will stop copper production in mid-December after road blockades. Executives say operations have already been suspended for most of the past year due to transport disputes with communities. While a freight railway has been approved, it may not run until 2028, leaving near-term disruption risk high.

title: Belgium's Copper Imports Jump to $1.5B, with Rising Supplies from Bulgaria and Spain
summary: Belgium’s copper imports rose in 2020, reaching about 175K tonnes and $1.5B, with higher purchases from Bulgaria and Spain. Bulgaria remained the largest supplier (~48% share). The average import price increased to $8,266/tonne (+11% y-o-y), reflecting country-level pricing differences.

title: 'Good prospect' Tiwai smelter will delay closure if aluminium prices stay high - govt officials
summary: New Zealand officials say the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter may operate beyond its end-2024 planned closure if aluminium prices stay high. While electricity contract details and decarbonisation risks are discussed, the key signal is that strong aluminium prices could extend output, affecting short-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Geophysics point to copper drill targets for Valor in Peru
summary: Valor Resources reports preliminary results from a ground geophysics program (magnetic and induced polarization/IP) at its Picha copper-silver project in southern Peru, identifying chargeability/resistivity anomalies that correlate with surface copper mineralisation and may extend at depth. The company plans a drilling campaign, but no near-term output change is indicated.

title: Drill results add to Ambler-area copper prospect's high-grade reputation
summary: Alaska drilling at Ambler Metals’ Ambler-area hard rock prospect identified multiple mineralized zones near the proposed open pit, including a 19.9-meter interval with over 6.7% copper.
