title: Nickel Climbs After U.S. Renews Warning of Russian Invasion
summary: Nickel is reported to be climbing after the U.S. renewed warnings about a potential Russian invasion. The renewed geopolitical risk is likely prompting market participants to price in disruptions or supply tightness related to Russia, increasing nickel’s risk premium and supporting higher prices in the near term.

title: Sixth smelter won the bid Indonesia OBI Nickel Cobalt Wet process Phase III Project_SMM
summary: SMM reports China Nonferrous Metals Industry No. 6 Metallurgical Construction won bids for two sections of Indonesia OBI Nickel-Cobalt Wet Phase III. The project includes laterite nickel wet smelting and nickel-cobalt refining activities (smelting and nickel/cobalt hydroxide processing), signaling incremental refining capacity buildout.

title: Xinhu Futures: overseas interference factors still exist short-term aluminum price still has support_SMM
summary: Xinhu Futures (SMM) reports LME three-month aluminum rising to about $3,282/ton and Shanghai night trading lifting the main contract, supported by renewed fears of overseas supply disruptions linked to Russia-Ukraine. Spot activity is improving but bargain-driven; downstream restocking is cautious. Overall, aluminum retains short-term support.

title: Huatai Futures: the overseas situation is not yet clear. Zinc and aluminum continue to fluctuate._SMM
summary: SMM notes Shanghai aluminum was strong and volatile after the holiday, with improving downstream procurement and better spot offers in South China. LME aluminum inventories fell, while Europe’s ongoing gas/electricity uncertainty threatens electrolytic output capacity into early spring, supporting bullish expectations despite macro and rate-hike concerns.

title: Red seas and no fish: nickel mining strains Indonesia's spice islands | News | Eco-Business
summary: Fishermen in Indonesia’s Obi Islands say declining fish catches stem from expanding nickel mining and smelting, citing pollution from waste disposal plans and alleged heavy-metal contamination near fishing grounds. Trimegah previously backed down on deep-sea tailings dumping but seeks a tailings dam instead, with ongoing approval uncertainty and environmental risk.

title: Restored Social Order in Baise Ensures Stable Aluminium Supply _SMM
summary: Baise held a COVID-19 control press conference stating the city has large aluminium reserves and has restored “internal circulation” of aluminium supply and demand. It notes workers returning to production and faster commissioning of 200,000 mt aluminium capacity, with over 75% of scaled plants operating normally, keeping aluminium supply stable.

title: LME aluminium's $45/t backwardation – bullish or bearish for premiums?
summary: The piece discusses LME aluminium showing $45/t backwardation and frames this as a sign that aluminium is “hard to move” despite being available. It also notes Fastmarkets corrections/delays to certain aluminium premium assessments, but the core signal is tight near-term supply conditions supportive of aluminium premiums.

title: Develop to buy Heron's zinc-copper project in Australia for $21.5m
summary: Develop has agreed to buy Australia’s Woodlawn underground copper project in NSW for $21.5m, including cash and shares to Heron’s creditors. The asset includes a redeveloped processing plant but previously faced ramp-up and Covid-related issues. Develop also expects the acquisition to expand its base metals business.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 400,000 wmt on Week_SMM
summary: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell by 400,000 wmt week-on-week to 7.88 million wmt as of Feb 18, with lower Ni content total. Laterite inventories kept dropping amid weak Philippine shipments, while downstream demand improved after environmental restrictions were lifted, suggesting faster inventory declines.

title: SHFE Copper Prices Rose Sharply to 72,000 yuan/mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE 2203 copper futures rising sharply to around 72,000 yuan/mt, with trading interest increasing. It attributes the move to macro risk sentiment and a weaker dollar, while noting copper inventory builds domestically but continued LME stock declines and solid downstream support, keeping prices supported.

title: Supply concerns send nickel to three-week high
summary: Nickel prices rose to three-week highs as traders flagged tight LME-registered inventories and potential sanctions against Russia. LME stocks fell sharply and cancelled warrants suggest more nickel will leave warehouses. The cash nickel premium over the three-month contract widened, reflecting immediate supply fears amid strong battery and stainless demand.

title: Native Americans protest proposed copper mine in Arizona
summary: Native Americans in Arizona protest a proposed Resolution Copper mine at Oak Flat, as a federal appeals court is expected to rule imminently on whether the project can move forward. The story highlights reliance on domestic copper for clean-energy demand and ongoing legal/environmental uncertainty affecting mine progress.

title: The international situation is tense and the copper price maintains a wide range of volatility [selected from SMM Copper Weekly]_SMM
summary: SMM says geopolitical tensions involving Ukraine and Russia fueled risk aversion and sharp moves in oil and gold, briefly pushing copper volatility. It also points to Fed minutes showing no more hawkish signals and mixed expectations for March rate hikes, with domestic inflation easing, suggesting copper may remain volatile without a clear directional trend.

title: Supply concerns send nickel prices soaring; cracks $11 a pound
summary: Nickel rallied to the highest since Jan. 21, topping $11/lb, driven by fears of tight LME supply. Stocks in LME warehouses have fallen sharply and canceled warrants imply more nickel will exit. Traders also cite potential sanctions on Russia, plus ongoing EV-battery demand.

title: Eskom security guards bust at scrapyard with stolen copper cables
summary: Security guards and scrap dealers were arrested after police and stakeholders raided suspected scrap outlets in Free State and recovered stolen Eskom copper and aluminium cables, along with other telecom and municipal cables worth over R60,000. Separate cables worth about R8,000 were also found with guards arriving at the scrapyard.

title: SPARKLING NICKEL
summary: Nickel prices rose to three-week highs as traders worried about low inventories and potential sanctions targeting Russia, a major nickel producer. Reuters reported LME benchmark nickel up 0.6% at $24,035/t after earlier hitting $24,140. Supply risk drove the upside move.

title: AuKing Mining reports wide copper intersections at flagship Koongie Park project
summary: AuKing Mining reported new diamond drilling results from its Koongie Park copper-zinc project in Western Australia, including 105.3m at 1.94% copper and a 16.6m interval grading above 10% copper. The company highlights significant copper potential and expects remaining assays within a week, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Mitsubishi Materials and the expansion of Copper smelter capacity in Freeport, Indonesia_SMM
summary: PT Smelting (Mitsubishi Materials and Freeport Indonesia JV) started construction of a $223 million copper smelter expansion in East Java. Cathode copper capacity is set to rise from 300,000 to 342,000 tons and concentrate processing from 1.0 to 1.3 million tons, targeting completion by Dec 2023.

title: Western Mines appoints exploration manager ahead of drilling at Mulga Tank nickel-copper-PGE project
summary: Western Mines appointed an exploration manager ahead of a planned 30-hole diamond drilling program at its Mulga Tank nickel-copper-PGE project. The company is completing an MLEM survey and logistics for an exploration camp. This is activity-focused with no production or resource results, limiting near-term price influence.

title: China Starts to Build a New Hydrometallurgy Project with Nickel Production Capacity above 50,000 mt in Indonesia_SMM
summary: China MCC 20 Group began construction (Jan 21) of a hydrometallurgy project in Indonesia’s Central Sulawesi, within Tsingshan Industrial Park. The plant targets at least 50,000 mt nickel metal capacity and 4,000 mt cobalt, with related infrastructure works. Completion could support nickel supply for batteries.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese markets Added 5,600 mt over Weekend _SMM
summary: SMM said copper inventories in major Chinese markets rose 5,600 mt from Feb 18 to 217,400 mt, the smallest weekend increase in weeks. Growth was mainly from domestic smelters, while downstream recovery and higher exports reduced cathode inflows. This week, social inventory growth is expected to slow, contingent on COVID-19 effects on production.

title: The Nickel Prices will be High due to the Tight Supply_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: The piece argues nickel will remain high due to tight supply conditions. It cites strong downstream demand, export disruption linked to conflicts affecting Norilsk Nickel, rising transaction premiums that ease only partly, and tight nickel sulphate/requirements for additional matte output. It expects SHFE and LME nickel to fluctuate at elevated levels this week.

title: Japanese shareholders seek to sell stake in LS-Nikko Copper joint venture
summary: Japanese firms in JKJS are considering selling their 49.9% stake in LS-Nikko Copper, a copper smelting joint venture, for about 800 billion won. LS Corp., which already holds 50.1% and manages the business, says the stake sale should have limited impact on operations, implying minimal near-term copper price effects.

title: Mitsubishi Materials and Freeport Indonesia expand copper smelter capacity with US$223 million  joint venture
summary: Mitsubishi Materials and Freeport Indonesia’s PT Smelting launched construction of a $223 million expansion to its East Java copper smelter in Indonesia. Cathode capacity is expected to rise to 342,000 tonnes from 300,000 tonnes currently, which should support refined copper supply outlook over the coming weeks.

title: London nickel hits highest in over a decade as supply tightens
summary: London nickel surged to the highest level in more than a decade, with three-month LME nickel up and reaching multi-year highs. The move is attributed to low inventories and tightening supply, plus EV-related demand for battery metals. Ukraine-Russia tensions also add supply-risk and volatility.

title: 56.5% of Aluminium Fabrication Capacity in Baise City, Guangxi Province Was Still Affected by Local COVID_SMM
summary: Baise City in Guangxi reported that COVID-19 suspended 39 of 68 aluminium fabricators, affecting 56.5% of local fabrication capacity. Several smelters and alumina producers also faced shutdowns, with processing firms largely offline. The interruptions point to near-term output disruptions for aluminium supply chains.

title: Aluminium Ingot Import Losses Recorded Two-Year High_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says aluminium ingot import losses are near 1,500 yuan/mt, close to early-2020 levels, as import swap costs rise and the import window stays closed. With the SHFE/LME copper price ratio falling and Yangshan copper spot prices low, aluminium ingot imports face further pressure, likely weighing on aluminium pricing.

title: Copper Prices Fluctuated in a Wide Range amid Tense International Situation_SMM
summary: Copper prices fluctuated amid worsening Ukraine–Russia tensions that boosted risk aversion and moved oil and gold, alongside macro focus on Fed minutes and mixed rate expectations. Fundamentals cited low inventories and weaker-than-expected domestic cathode supply, but consumption gains look limited post-CNY, keeping prices rangebound.

title: IGO eyes acquisition of Glencore's CSA copper mine in Australia
summary: IGO is negotiating with Glencore to acquire the CSA copper mine in western New South Wales. The mine produces about 50,000 tonnes per annum of copper, processed on-site and exported for smelting. Talks are incomplete and due diligence continues, making it a potential near-term supply-sentiment factor for copper.

title: Aluminium shortages to deter blanket sanctions on Rusal: analysts
summary: Analysts say the US/EU likely will not impose blanket sanctions on Rusal in a Russia-Ukraine invasion scenario because it would worsen aluminium shortages. Rusal supplies about 6% of global output. With inventories already very low, any sanctions-related supply disruption could push aluminium to new record prices, above tight physical premiums.

title: PT Smelting embarks on copper smelter expansion in Indonesia
summary: PT Smelting has started construction on a $231m expansion of its Gresik, Indonesia copper smelter/refinery. Capacity is expected to rise for copper cathode and concentrate processing, with added sulphuric acid and electrolysis capacity. The project is positioned to deepen Indonesia’s copper downstreaming cluster.

title: Norsk Hydro Expects To Restart Aluminium Plant Albras, Brazil In Early Q2
summary: Norsk Hydro said its part-owned Albras aluminium plant in Brazil expects to restart the first pots in early Q2 after a power distribution failure shut one of four potlines on Feb. 19. The incident cut output by about 25%, while the other lines kept running normally.

title: Bauxite: Sonamines partners with CREC 5 to develop the Ngaoundal and Makan deposits
summary: Sonamines (Cameroon) signed a memorandum with CREC 5 to develop the Ngaoundal and Makan bauxite deposits. The plan includes feasibility and environmental studies, construction of a bauxite-to-alumina refinery, and alumina-to-aluminum production and by-products plants, subject to permits. This supports aluminium supply expectations.

title: Hydro's Albras aluminium smelter cuts 25% capacity after power failure [UPDATED]
summary: Hydro’s Albras aluminium smelter has reportedly reduced output by about 25% after a power failure. The capacity cut is expected to lower near-term aluminium production, tightening supply expectations and supporting prices over the next days to weeks.

title: JV Article: Metal Energy advances its nickel-copper-PGE projects in Manitoba and Ontario
summary: Metal Energy promoted its Manibridge nickel-copper project in Manitoba and the Strange nickel-copper-PGE project in Ontario, citing high-grade nickel drill intersections and launching new drilling campaigns. While no production is starting, the positive exploration progress can modestly improve sentiment toward nickel and copper prices over coming weeks.

title: Key Trends & Developments in the Chinese Aluminium Market 2022-2026: Growing Popularity of Recycled Aluminium and Growing Application in Power Grid & Power Generation Industries
summary: A ResearchAndMarkets report outlines China’s aluminium market outlook, citing demand growth from construction, EVs, electronics, and power grid/power generation applications, alongside increased use of recycled aluminium. It also notes headwinds from tighter environmental rules and slower new capacity additions. The piece is forward-looking, not a near-term supply disruption.

title: JV Article: Newly public Zacapa Resources focuses on US copper-gold exploration with drill-ready targets in prolific belts
summary: Zacapa Resources, newly public, is drilling in Arizona’s Laramide porphyry copper belt at its Red Top project and reports discovery of porphyry copper mineralization in an initial drill hole. The article highlights portfolio expansion and planned further drilling, but provides no immediate supply or production change.

title: Opponents of Resolution copper mine converge on Oak Flat for march
summary: Protesters converge on Oak Flat in Arizona to oppose Resolution Copper’s planned mine beneath sacred Indigenous land. The article cites risks of ground collapse and groundwater contamination and notes the Forest Service withdrew a prior decision and is restarting tribal consultations, alongside ongoing legal challenges.

title: Healthy demand, shortages spur nickel's climb to decade highs
summary: Nickel surged to decade highs as LME inventories fell sharply, with draws from warehouses and fewer warrants due to leave the system. Strong Chinese EV demand supports tightness in nickel suitable for battery nickel sulfate, while sanctions risk around Russia adds a supply risk premium.

title: Mining firm reports promising results for Timmins-area nickel sulphide project
summary: Canada Nickel reports higher nickel sulphide concentrate grades and improved recoveries from locked-cycle tests at its Crawford nickel project near Timmins. Results show high-grade concentrate targeting 40–50% nickel versus a 35% target and recoveries above 60%. The company frames this as confirmation of flow-sheet improvements.

title: The increase in Electroweb investment will boost copper and aluminum consumption [Agency Review]_SMM
summary: The article says China’s Electroweb investment is set to rise sharply in 2022, with more UHV projects starting construction. It estimates 2022 copper consumption up 47–600k tons and aluminium up 60–800k tons, translating into projected copper price gains (~2.1%) and stronger aluminium price gains (~6.63%).

title: The increase in Electroweb investment will boost copper and aluminum consumption [Agency Review]_SMM
summary: China’s Electroweb investment is expected to rise in 2022, with more UHV lines starting construction. The article estimates incremental demand of copper and aluminium for power grid equipment and conductors, predicting copper consumption up ~3.3% and aluminium ~1.7% in 2022, with corresponding price increases.

title: Ferronickel smelter of ANTAM Company in Indonesia will be put into operation soon._SMM
summary: Indonesia’s Mind ID signed an MoU with Guodian to supply 75 MW of electricity to ANTAM’s ferro-nickel smelter. Commentators expect the Jokowi-linked smelter to start production soon, boosting Indonesia’s processing capacity and improving near-term nickel supply expectations, which could support nickel prices.

title: Earnings wrap: Alumina, AMA Group, ARB, AUB, Cochlear, Coles, Costa, Deterra, Estia, G8 Education, HomeCo Daily Needs, Hub24, Humm, Ingenia, Johns Lyng, Jumbo Interactive, Judo Bank, Macquarie Telecom, Macmahon, Monadelphous, Nanosonics, Perenti, RAM Essential, Regis Resources, Seven Group, Superloop, Uniti, Virtus, Whispr
summary: An “earnings wrap” highlights that Alumina increased its dividend after profits rose by a quarter. While the piece is company-focused rather than macro, improved Alumina earnings can support expectations for refining economics and availability feeding aluminium production over coming days to weeks.

title: Russian Aluminum Giant Rusal Tumbles on Fresh Sanction Fears
summary: Rusal, a major Russian aluminium producer, is reportedly tumbling on fresh sanction fears. If new sanctions hinder the company’s operations or exports, market supply expectations for aluminium could worsen quickly, likely weighing on near-term aluminium prices.

title: LME Aluminium Reached a New Height in more than 13 Years due to Tense Ukrainian-Russian Geopolitics_SMM
summary: Tense Ukrainian-Russian geopolitics drove a sharp early rise in aluminium prices. LME aluminium hit a 13+ year high ($3,342/mt) as sanctions risk could disrupt Russian supply to Europe and the US and higher oil/gas prices lift production costs. Domestic demand is improving while supply constraints ease.

title: Steady Demand and Low Supply Sent LME Nickel Prices to a Ten-year High_SMM
summary: SMM reports LME nickel prices surged on low inventories and steady EV battery demand, with heightened concerns about potential sanctions limiting Russian nickel supply. LME three-month nickel hit a more than 10-year high, premiums rose sharply, and nickel registered warrants and cancelled warrants signals intensified fears of further tightness.

title: GFG Alliance launches high court action to reclaim aluminium smelter
summary: GFG Alliance has filed a London High Court action to reclaim control of the Dunkerque aluminium smelter in France from US private equity fund AIP, citing loan agreement issues and “unlawful expropriation.” AIP has been operating the plant since October, while broader AML and fraud investigations add uncertainty.

title: Alumina warns freight costs to remain high for 2022
summary: Alumina says freight costs will stay high for the rest of 2022, pressuring margins. This follows strong prior profits but signals weaker cost conditions going forward. The company also announced a slightly lower final dividend, reinforcing the squeeze from logistics expenses and transport disruptions.

title: Spot Copper Premiums Narrowed to Small Discounts because of the Large Quantities of Arrivals_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE copper cathode spots moved from prior wider discounts to smaller discounts (30–0 yuan/mt vs average 15 yuan/mt) as large arrivals of high-quality copper increased supply and reduced high-quality/standard differentials. Weaker downstream consumption in Jiangsu and smelter shipments to Shanghai are cited as keeping premiums suppressed.

title: Transactions in Yangshan Copper Market were Slack_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports slack trading in the Yangshan copper import market. Warrant and bill of lading premiums show mixed moves, but imports remain loss-making versus LME 03 and hydro-copper quotes were cut sharply due to weak buying. Traders struggled to complete deals, and overall premiums faced downward pressure.

title: Forged documents and misled banks: ED&F Man awarded US$282mn in nickel fraud case
summary: A UK court awarded ED&F Man US$282mn in a nickel warehouse receipts fraud case. The judgement found forged receipts were used to obtain financing from banks including ANZ, ING and Natixis, with nickel held at LME warehouses. The fraud surfaced in 2017; the ruling is now the focus, not new nickel supply.

title: Nickel Prices Surge To Decade High Amid Soaring Battery Demand And Ukraine Crisis
summary: Nickel prices are reported to have surged to a decade high, attributed to soaring demand tied to batteries and added risk from the Ukraine crisis. The combination of robust end-use demand and geopolitical supply concerns is expected to increase near-term pricing pressure for nickel.

title: Gardaí search scrap yards for missing copper cables
summary: Gardaí and PSNI raided scrap yards to investigate theft of missing copper telecommunications cables under “Operation Moselle”. It cites about 12 km of copper wire stolen and thousands of households affected, with raids in multiple counties and inspections at licensed facilities. The thefts’ value is tied to copper scrap resale.

title: Aluminium and nickel hit multi-year highs on Russian supply threat
summary: Aluminium and nickel prices jumped to multi-year highs after Russia deployed troops in eastern Ukraine, increasing fears of sanctions that could disrupt Russian exports. With already tight fundamentals—low LME inventories and record/high cash premiums—market sentiment turned strongly bullish for both metals.

title: Antofagasta annual profit jumps as rising copper prices boost growth | 22 February 2022
summary: The article headline says Antofagasta’s annual profit increased as rising copper prices boosted growth. This indicates copper price strength in the near term, supporting market expectations for continued cash-flow improvement for a major copper producer. The rest of the provided text does not add further copper-specific details.

title: Aluminium and nickel hit multi-year highs on Russian supply threat
summary: Aluminium and nickel prices surged to multi-year highs after Russia ordered troops into eastern Ukraine, raising fears of sanctions and supply disruptions. Russia accounts for meaningful shares of global aluminium and mined nickel. The move compounds already tight markets, with LME inventories down and cash premiums near records.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Kamoa Copper to Expand Processing Capacity of Kamoa-Kakula's Phase 1 and Phase 2 Concentrators by 21%, to a Combined Total of 9.2 Million Tonnes of Ore per Year
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says Kamoa-Kakula will de-bottleneck its Phase 1 and Phase 2 concentrators, increasing combined processing capacity by ~21% to 9.2 Mtpa. The plan should lift annual copper output to exceed 450,000 tonnes by Q2 2023. Phase 2 commissioning is on track for April 2022.

title: Huntsman Exploration Inc.: Major Drill Program Commenced at Canegrass Nickel Project in Western Australia
summary: Huntsman Exploration says it has started a major ~5,000m drilling program at its Canegrass nickel project in Western Australia, using RC and diamond rigs. The company plans to follow up prior “exceptional” intercepts, including high-grade nickel with associated copper, aiming to expand several targets and test new EM anomalies.

title: South32 buys 45% stake in Sierra Gorda copper mine in Chile
summary: South32 completed its $1.9bn purchase of a 45% stake in Chile’s Sierra Gorda copper mine. Payments to Sumitomo include an upfront $1.4bn plus contingent amounts tied to copper production and prices over 2022–2025, highlighting increased copper exposure and near-term earnings contribution.

title: Nickel Surges to $25,000 a Ton for First Time Since 2011
summary: Nickel prices reportedly surged to $25,000 per tonne for the first time since 2011. That level implies strong near-term bullish repricing by the market, typically reflecting tightening expectations around nickel supply and/or demand fundamentals, which can quickly pull physical and derivatives prices higher.

title: Stocks of Russian Aluminum Giant Rusal Fall Amid Fears of Over Sanctions
summary: Rusal shares fell as investors watched tensions with Ukraine that could lead to further sanctions on Russian firms. Rusal is a top aluminum producer outside China and a significant supplier to global markets. Any sanctions threatening exports or operations would likely tighten supply and support aluminum prices.

title: Russia's Move Into Luhansk and Donetsk Sends Nickel, Aluminum Prices Soaring
summary: Nickel and aluminum surged after Russia declared parts of eastern Ukraine—Luhansk and Donetsk—independent and sent troops. The report attributes the jump to Russia’s major role in producing both metals, raising expectations of supply risk. Aluminum rose about 3.7% and nickel about 3.9% on Feb. 22.

title: Russia's Move Into Luhansk and Donetsk Sends Nickel, Aluminum Prices Soaring
summary: Nickel and aluminum prices jumped after Russia declared Luhansk and Donetsk independent regions and sent troops into Ukraine. The article attributes the move to heightened supply risk because Russia is a major producer of both metals, with aluminum up about 3.7% and nickel up about 3.9% in a day.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Continues to Deliver Favorable Drilling Results at Punitaqui Copper Mine
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reports favorable drill core assay results from the San Andres zone at Chile’s Punitaqui copper mine. The company says the project is slated to resume copper concentrate production in 2H 2022, and the results support additional copper ore potential and a resource update.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Continues to Deliver Favorable Drilling Results at Punitaqui Copper Mine
summary: The headline reports that Battery Mineral Resources continues to deliver favorable drilling results at the Punitaqui copper mine. Such positive exploration updates can improve expectations for future copper supply and bolster market sentiment toward copper prices, though the article content provided contains no additional supply-demand details.

title: Coast Copper Stakes New Claim to Expand Red Chris Area Operations
summary: Coast Copper says it has staked new claims to expand operations around its Red Chris-area properties, including a Gin property expansion of over 726 hectares, plus expansions at Knob Hill NW and Empire Mine on northern Vancouver Island. The updates are largely about property scope rather than near-term output.

title: Soaring Battery Demand And Ukraine Conflict Sends Nickel Prices To Decade High
summary: Nickel prices jumped to the highest level in more than a decade as electric-vehicle demand tightened lithium-ion battery cathode supplies. The Ukraine conflict raised additional supply-flow concerns, with Russia a top nickel producer. The article also notes Russia’s aluminum production role and suggests aluminum prices are nearing new highs.

title: Nickel and aluminum hit multi-year highs on Russian supply threat
summary: Nickel and aluminium surged to multi-year highs after Russia’s troop move in eastern Ukraine raised fears of sanctions and export disruptions. Russia supplies a meaningful share of global production. With inventories tight and LME premiums/stocks deteriorating, the market expects near-term supply risk, supporting higher prices.

title: Nickel and aluminum hit multi-year highs on Russian supply threat
summary: Nickel and aluminium reached multi-year highs after Russia’s move into eastern Ukraine raised concerns about sanctions and interruptions to Russian exports. Russia accounts for about 7% of mined nickel and 6% of global aluminium. With already undersupplied markets and falling LME stocks, prices rose sharply.

title: Russia May Sharply Increase Refined Nickel Exports to China If US Imposes Sanctions_SMM
summary: SMM reports that the US may impose sanctions on Russia. If so, refined nickel previously destined for the US could instead be redirected to China. Russian Nornickel output is steady near 210,000 mt, and Russia already supplies sizable volumes to China, so redirected flows could increase supply and weigh on nickel prices.

title: Indonesia Exported 6,087 mt of High-Grade Nickel Matte in Jan_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data shows Indonesia exported 6,087 mt of high-grade nickel matte in January (4,748 mt in metal content), mainly to Japan with a smaller flow to China. The volume was below previous years’ typical 7,500–8,500 mt/month range, suggesting tighter near-term nickel matte supply.

title: NORNICKEL Nickel Is Likely to Flow into Chinese Market or LME warehouses, Pushing Up Premiums of Other Nickel Brands in Europe and US markets_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME nickel diverging and notes wider import losses. It argues that if US sanctions target Russia, Nornickel refined nickel could reroute toward China and/or enter LME warehouses, tightening US/Europe supply while boosting LME stocks, premiums, and opening import windows for nickel.

title: C3 Metals Inc.: C3 Metals Drills 32.4m at 3.75% Copper at Jasperoide Drilling on Deeper Targets Underway
summary: C3 Metals reported assay results from drilling at its Jasperoide copper-gold project in southern Peru, including thick intervals with high copper grades and an enrichment zone. A larger rig is now drilling deeper targets for stacked skarns and porphyry copper-gold mineralization to guide future development priorities.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: South African Mining Veteran Riaan Vermeulen Appointed as Kamoa Copper's New Managing Director
summary: Ivanhoe Mines announced that Riaan Vermeulen will become Managing Director of Kamoa Copper and that Zhang “Frank” Xingxun will join as Executive Director. The release highlights ongoing Kamoa-Kakula copper production and expansion plans, but provides no immediate change to output, exports, or pricing drivers.

title: LME aluminum hovers near a 13-year high. Investors worry about supply._SMM
summary: LME aluminium stayed near a 13-year high as investors worried that western sanctions and the halted Russia gas pipeline could disrupt Russian metal exports. Russia supplies ~6% of aluminium production and 7% of nickel mining. Nickel also hit multi-year highs amid tight inventories and higher spot premiums, with copper modestly higher.

title: C3 Metals Drills 32.4m at 3.75% Copper at Jasperoide Drilling on Deeper Targets Underway
summary: C3 Metals announced drilling at its Jasperoide project, reporting 32.4 meters at 3.75% copper on deeper targets, with additional drilling underway. Stronger grade/intercept results can lift sentiment around future copper supply potential, modestly supporting expectations for copper prices over the coming weeks.

title: Aluminium and nickel rally falters but Russia sanctions support
summary: Aluminium and nickel eased after recent multi-year highs, but prices stayed elevated as the US, EU and UK consider tighter sanctions on Russia. With Russia producing key shares of global aluminium and mined nickel, traders fear supply impairment. Tight inventories and widening nickel/cash premiums further support bullish sentiment.

title: Aluminium and nickel rally falters but Russia sanctions support
summary: Aluminium and nickel pulled back from recent highs, but Western sanctions efforts against Russia are boosting prices by raising fears of impaired Russian metal supply. Russia accounts for about 6% of aluminium and 7% of mined nickel. Tight markets persist, with higher nickel premiums and falling LME inventories.

title: Atacama Copper Announces the Expansion of Its License Area on the El Cofre Copper Project
summary: Atacama Copper announced an expansion of its license area covering the El Cofre copper project. The update suggests progress toward future project development and potential reserve expansion, but it does not signal any immediate output or supply disruption, so any near-term impact on copper prices is likely muted.

title: C3 Metals Drills 32.4m at 3.75% Copper at Jasperoide Drillin...
summary: C3 Metals reported assay results from the Jasperoide (southern Peru) Jasperoide drilling program, including 32.4m at 3.75% Cu and 15.1m at 2.02% Cu in oxide copper-gold zones. The company is also starting deeper drilling to test porphyry and stacked skarn potential.

title: Ivanhoe approves de-bottlenecking plan for Kamoa-Kakula copper project
summary: Ivanhoe Mines approved a de-bottlenecking plan at the Kamoa-Kakula copper project in the DRC to raise concentrator processing capacity by about 21% versus current throughput. The company expects higher copper output, including over 450,000 tonnes annually by Q2 2023, supporting near-term copper supply sentiment.

title: Global Aluminium Cans Market (2022 to 2027) - Industry Trends, Share, Size, Growth, Opportunity and Forecasts
summary: The piece promotes a report on the global aluminium cans market (2022–2027). It highlights demand support from replacing plastics with recyclable aluminium cans and mentions COVID-19 considerations. However, it lacks concrete near-term supply, trade, or aluminium price catalysts, implying limited immediate price impact.

title: Supply chain hiccup leaves craft breweries scrambling for aluminum can alternatives
summary: Ball, the dominant maker of aluminum beer cans, is dropping some customers and raising minimum order requirements due to high demand and supply-chain constraints. Breweries are forced to source cans elsewhere, often at higher cost, delaying production and raising prices, indicating tighter aluminum can availability.

title: Prospect of sanctions hits Russian part-owner of Queensland alumina refinery
summary: Prospect of sanctions tied to Russia is pressuring Rusal, part-owner of Australia’s Queensland Alumina alumina refinery. Rio Tinto warns escalating tensions could cause disruption to its aluminium operations and supply chain. Authorities signal more sanctions if escalation continues, raising near-term aluminium supply risk expectations.

title: Europe Is Desperate for Aluminum and Traders Are Getting Creative

The article links the actions to concerns that alumina exports to Russia could be used in munitions. Asset freezes, business restrictions, and travel bans raise the likelihood of reduced Russian-linked alumina flows, supporting aluminium-related supply expectations.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Decreased 34,400 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says Chinese copper inventories across major markets fell 34,400 mt to 172,500 mt versus Monday, with sharper declines in Shanghai and Guangdong. The drop is linked to reduced smelter delivery efficiency from COVID-19, limited imported copper, logistics frictions, and only marginal expected improvement next week, implying supply remains tighter than demand.

title: Philippines to Open 12 New Metal Mines in 2022, Mostly Nickel Mines_SMM
summary: Philippines’ regulator expects about 12 new metal mines to enter commercial operation in 2022, mostly nickel projects. Philippine nickel production rose 17% in 2021 to 386,359 mt, boosting its role as a key nickel ore supplier to China. The outlook is positive, but rising fuel, labor, and freight costs pressure miners.

title: There will be 12 new metal mines in the Philippines this year, mostly nickel mines._SMM
summary: Philippine regulators expect about 12 new metal mines to start commercial operations this year, mostly nickel. Nickel output rose 17% in the prior year to the highest in six years. While high prices persist, producers face higher fuel and logistics costs. A policy shift could also lift a copper opencast ban, but timing is unclear.

title: Hindalco maintains sheen as aluminium prices remain high
summary: Hindalco shares fell about 2% over the week as LME aluminium prices eased from the 4 March peak and declined around 3% over the past week. Despite the weekly softening, aluminium remains up sharply year-to-date (up roughly 19% in CY22 to mid-month), suggesting recent bearish pressure.

title: Nickel Drops 12% in Another Glitchy Start to London Trading
summary: The article headline reports that nickel dropped 12% in an “another glitchy start” to London trading. Despite limited details in the provided text, the framing clearly points to sharp near-term weakness in nickel prices, which would be expected to pressure related market sentiment and pricing.

title: LME aluminum inventory continues to decline by 9475 tons. Klang inventory has dropped the most._SMM
summary: SMM reports that LME aluminum inventories continued to fall on March 18, down by 9,475 tons in total. The largest decrease occurred at the Klang warehouse. Lower tracked aluminum stock levels generally indicate tighter near-term supply conditions, which can be supportive for aluminium prices.

title: Universal Copper Ltd.: Universal Copper Closes Second & Final Tranche of Private Placement for Proceeds of C$355,500
summary: Universal Copper Ltd. reports closing the second tranche of an oversubscribed private placement, raising C$355,500, to fund 2022 exploration at its Poplar copper deposit in British Columbia and some working capital. The company issues flow-through and non-flow-through units with warrants; no direct supply or demand impact is described.

title: Magna Mining Inc.: Magna Mining Files Technical Report for the Shakespeare Nickel Project
summary: Magna Mining filed an independent NI 43-101 technical report for its Shakespeare Nickel Project near Sudbury, Ontario. The report supports a previously described feasibility study and is dated March 17 with an effective date of January 31. The release is a regulatory disclosure with no new production or supply changes cited.

title: Nickel hits lower circuit in early trade on LME
summary: LME nickel saw a major selloff in early trade, with the three-month contract down 12% to hit the lower circuit at about $36,915/t. CNBC cited heavy selling in international metal markets. The report recalls prior March surges and LME trading interruptions due to pricing system issues.

title: Glencore to sell Australia's CSA copper mine to Metals Acquisition
summary: Glencore agreed to sell the CSA copper mine in New South Wales to Metals Acquisition for $1.05bn plus a $50m stake and a 1.5% NSR royalty. MAC will take full operational control and secure an offtake for 100% of copper concentrate, implying ongoing production. Completion awaits approvals.

title: The Nickel Markets Are a Mess - The New York Times
summary: The New York Times reports that nickel trading has been effectively frozen after a rapid price surge following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. London Metal Exchange trading was suspended and trades were canceled, with daily-limit plunges restarting volatility. Analysts expect nickel prices to drop from the spike, though likely stay above a year ago.

title: Nickel tumbles 12% in latest glitchy start to London trading
summary: Nickel prices are reported to have tumbled 12% in the latest glitchy start to London trading. The sharp drop signals strong near-term bearish pressure on nickel, reflecting market repricing during the early trading session, even though the excerpt does not provide the underlying cause.

title: Peruvian community lifts blockade affecting Las Bambas copper mine -govt
summary: Peru’s government said a community blockade affecting MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine was lifted after three days of talks. The disruption had begun March 1 and prevented shipments. With road access restored, Las Bambas can resume trucking concentrate to ports, easing near-term copper supply tightness.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Resources Announces $1-Million Strategic Investment from Altius Minerals, Including Equity Financing and Royalty Option on Nickel Assets
summary: Gungnir Resources announced a $1.0 million strategic investment from Altius, including equity financing and a royalty option tied to nickel-focused projects in Sweden. Net proceeds will fund continued exploration drilling concentrating on its nickel resources. The news may be modestly supportive for nickel sentiment but is unlikely to alter near-term market fundamentals.

title: Pandemic Paralysed Chinese Aluminium Scrap Market _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: In early week, Chinese aluminium prices moved within a narrow range with a midweek drop, but then rebounded sharply on Thursday and Friday. As aluminium scrap recyclers’ sentiment improves, pandemic-related transport disruptions and paralysed recycling parks still limit shipments. The article expects transaction volumes to rise if control improves next week.

title: LME's Copper Industry Group Recommends Banning Russian Metal
summary: LME’s Copper Industry Group has recommended banning Russian metal. The proposal implies a reduction in the availability of Russian copper for international trading and settlement, which can tighten near-term supply expectations and provide upward support for copper prices over the next days to weeks.

title: How the Ukraine Crisis Led to ... Nickel Hoarding
summary: The article says the Ukraine crisis created a nickel supply shock as Western buyers avoided Russian nickel, shifting demand to other suppliers and pushing nickel prices up sharply on the LME. It describes a record surge in nickel and consequential public hoarding of nickels as the metal’s melt value rose.

title: Nickel market tumult continues: What investors need to know
summary: Nickel is in turmoil following supply concerns linked to the Russia-Ukraine war. The LME suspended nickel trading on March 8 after prices more than doubled, and although trading resumed on Wednesday, prices continued to fall to expanded daily price limits for three straight sessions, signaling ongoing bearish pressure.

title: LME nickel extends its slide as bugs still hit trading
summary: LME nickel continues falling to about $36,915/t as trading volumes remain thin and LMEselect technical glitches hinder order entry. Nickel has faced suspension and tight daily price limits, and the exchange has not issued official settlement prices, affecting physical contract references and raising concerns over liquidity and venue risk.

title: A wild ride for global nickel market
summary: Russia’s role as a major nickel supplier is cited as a key driver of extreme volatility after the invasion of Ukraine. Nickel prices surged, and the LME stopped trading nickel for days before a rocky reopening. The piece highlights how supply fears and market disruption are affecting near-term nickel moves.

title: China's Exports of Alumina May Increase Rapidly on Opened Export Window_SMM
summary: China’s alumina export window has been expanded and exports are expected to rise, with transaction pricing up and a widened domestic-to-abroad price spread. Higher shipping costs and logistics constraints limited earlier exports, but abundant export supply may grow. Domestic smelter and trader procurement is suppressed, potentially weighing on aluminium prices.

title: China exploiting Ukraine invasion - Taipei Times
summary: The Taipei Times article says China is increasing financing and stakes in Russia’s energy and commodities sector amid sanctions, citing talks with state-owned firms. It specifically mentions Gazprom and Rusal, suggesting possible Chinese investment/involvement in Russian aluminium production and assets.

title: Inauguration of the certified CSA S37-18 Aluminum Telecommunications Towers
summary: REMAC inaugurated a CSA-certified 100ft aluminum telecommunications tower and plans to deliver six similar towers to Nova Scotia for improved cellular and high-speed internet coverage. The release highlights aluminum’s corrosion resistance and reduced installation time, indicating incremental aluminum demand, but it lacks volume data to affect prices materially.

title: Rio Tinto told to sweeten $3.6b copper takeover bid
summary: Rio Tinto is urged to sweeten its $US2.7b offer to acquire full control of Turquoise Hill Resources after a major shareholder said the bid undervalues its stake. The move is linked to simplifying ownership of Mongolia’s Oyu Tolgoi mine, projected to be among the world’s top copper mines.

title: LME hikes daily nickel price limit to 15% from Monday
summary: The LME resumed nickel trading after a rare shutdown caused by extreme volatility and introduced 15% daily price limits starting Monday. The same limits were applied to other base metals, including aluminium and copper. The measure restricts outright contract moves, potentially dampening volatility across these markets.

title: Goldman Bids for Nickel Off-Exchange About 32% Below LME Price
summary: The piece reports that Goldman is making off-exchange bids for nickel at roughly 32% below the LME price. Such a deep discount suggests nickel physical markets are trading weaker versus the benchmark, which can pressure near-term expectations and support bearish pricing for nickel.

title: LME boss says banks are partly to blame for nickel short squeeze
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports that the LME boss said banks were partly to blame for a nickel short squeeze. The comments suggest price moves were driven by market positioning rather than fundamentals, increasing the likelihood of a near-term unwind and bearish pressure on nickel.

title: London Metal Exchange outcry after nickel trading halted again
summary: LME nickel trading was halted again for a third consecutive day after heavy selling triggered the circuit breaker. Nickel fell about 12% to $36,915/t, and attempts to reopen with wider trading ranges failed, driving further declines. Traders cite chaos and loss of market credibility, shifting near-term nickel expectations.

title: The industrial chain of "Devil Nickel" in Castle Peak War is very hurt._SMM
summary: Castle Peak/Castle Peak Group’s large short positions amid tight LME deliverability led to a nickel short squeeze: LME nickel briefly surged from about $65,000 to $100,000/ton on March 8, prompting emergency trading suspension and later reopening with stricter nickel limits and delayed deliveries. The disruption affects hedging and industry pricing benchmarks.

title: Golden Arrow Purchases the San Pietro Iron-oxide Copper Gold Project, Chile
summary: Golden Arrow Resources agreed to buy 100% of the San Pietro IOCG project in Chile for $3.35M. The property shows historic drill results with meaningful copper grades (plus gold/iron/cobalt). The release discusses planned 2022 exploration and resource delineation, not any near-term production or supply changes.

title: Australia bans alumina exports to Russia, sources coal for Ukraine
summary: Australia has imposed an immediate ban on alumina and bauxite-related exports to Russia, saying Russia relies on Australian alumina for about 20% of its needs. The government expects reduced Russian aluminium output. The move also aligns with broader sanctions. This supply disruption is likely supportive for aluminium prices.

title: Australia live news update: Labor's landslide SA election win 'a team effort'; Australia bans aluminium ore exports to Russia; at least four Covid deaths | Australia news
summary: Australia’s foreign minister said the government is banning aluminium ore and alumina exports to Russia alongside a major Ukraine aid package. Cutting Russian-linked alumina feedstock supply can tighten refinery inputs and raise near-term expectations for aluminium availability, likely supporting aluminium prices over coming days and weeks.

title: Australia bans exports of aluminium ores to Russia over 'illegal' aggression towards Ukraine | Australia news
summary: Australia bans exports of alumina and aluminium ores to Russia, targeting feedstock used to produce Russian aluminium exports and citing aggression toward Ukraine. The move affects Queensland Alumina/Rio Tinto’s Russian-linked operations, with Russia relying on Australia for a portion of its alumina needs. The sanction aims to reduce Russia’s aluminium production capacity.

title: Australia bans alumina exports to Russia, steps up Ukraine aid
summary: Australia bans alumina (and bauxite) exports to Russia, saying Russia depends on Australia for nearly 20% of its alumina needs. The government expects the measure to limit Russian aluminium production. The sanctions expansion follows recent targeting of Rusal-linked interests and aims to pressure Russia during the Ukraine war.

title: Australia bans exports of alumina, aluminium ores, bauxite to Russia | Politics
summary: Australia has banned exports of alumina, aluminium ores and bauxite to Russia, cutting off a source of roughly 20% of Russia’s alumina needs. The action reduces Russian access to key aluminium feedstocks and is expected to tighten aluminium supply dynamics, supporting downside pressure on aluminium prices.

title: World's Top Alumina Supplier Australia Bans Exports to Russia
summary: Australia’s top alumina supplier has banned exports to Russia, according to the article headline. Reducing alumina deliveries to Russia can tighten near-term feedstock availability for aluminium smelters, increasing downside pressure on aluminium prices as markets price in potential supply disruptions.

title: Alcoa wins $470m aluminium sheet supply deal from Embraer
summary: Alcoa won a $470m long-term deal to supply aluminium sheet and plate for Embraer’s E2 aircraft, including use in wing skins and fuselage sheet/structural components. The contract supports ongoing aircraft production demand, but it is long-term and does not imply immediate supply constraints for aluminium markets.

title: Provisional liquidator of Zambia's Konkola Copper Mines resigns | Kat Country 98.9
summary: Reuters reports the provisional liquidator of Zambia’s Konkola Copper Mines (KCM) has resigned, amid an ongoing dispute between Vedanta (80%) and the Zambian government (20%). The resignation follows suspensions over alleged mismanagement and leaves KCM’s near-term management uncertain, potentially disrupting copper production expectations.

title: Australia bans the export of aluminum ores to Russia
summary: Australia bans exports of alumina and bauxite to Russia to raise the Kremlin’s economic costs. Officials cited Russia’s reliance on Australian alumina (about 20%) for aluminium production. The restriction prevents a planned shipment, which should tighten aluminium supply expectations in the near term.

title: Soaring Nickel Will Drive Tesla, EV Players to Do This With Batteries
summary: The article says inflation is pressuring the EV supply chain as metal inputs into batteries—especially nickel—soar. It notes that while higher costs are challenging, EV makers may innovate faster to reduce costs over time. The key immediate signal is ongoing upward pressure around nickel used in batteries.

title: Provisional liquidator of Zambia's Konkola Copper Mines resigns | WTVB | 1590 AM · 95.5 FM
summary: Zambia’s provisional liquidator of Konkola Copper Mines (KCM) resigned, Reuters reported. The move follows a dispute between Vedanta (80%) and the Zambian state (20% via ZCCM-IH) and a suspension attempt over alleged mismanagement. The outcome for KCM operations remains unclear, raising short-term supply uncertainty for copper.

title: Those Electric Cars Biden Wants You to Buy? Many Are Made with Russian Aluminum

summary: Aluminium prices are reported to have jumped after Australia imposed a ban on alumina exports to Russia. summary: Jiangxi Copper said its 100,000 mt lithium copper foil project in Shangrao has cleared key preparations, with Phase I (50,000 mt/year) starting construction in February 2022. summary: Culpeo Minerals will acquire up to 80% of the high-grade Lana Corina copper project in Chile’s Coquimbo region, paying staged cash and shares. title: SMM Analysis on Impact of Australia's Immediate Ban on Alumina and Bauxite Exports to Russia_SMM
summary: Australia announced an immediate ban on alumina and bauxite exports to Russia under additional sanctions. title: SMM China Aluminium Social Inventory Dropped 28,000 mt from Last Thursday_SMM
summary: SMM said China aluminium social inventory fell 28,000 mt from last Thursday to 1.06 million mt as of March 21, with declines mainly in Gongyi, Nanhai and Wuxi. Arrivals were delayed due to COVID-related transport disruptions, while output lagged last year. The market will track aluminium price and inventory changes.

title: Low Inventory Will Continue to Support Aluminium Prices at Highs_SMM
summary: SMM expects SHFE and LME aluminium to stay supported as aluminium ingot social inventories in China keep falling and COVID-related transport disruptions reduce arrivals. title: Copper Prices Continued to Rise amid Favourable Policies in China and the Turning Point of Inventories_SMM
summary: SMM says copper prices kept rising as China’s macro data and supportive policy stance stabilized expectations. Chinese copper inventories in major markets fell sharply, with reduced smelter delivery efficiency under COVID-19 and fewer imports after the SHFE/LME import window reopened. Falling arrivals boosted Shanghai spot premiums, expected to stay 300–400 yuan/mt.

title: China Hongqiao's net profit in 2021 increased by 53% compared with the same period last year, and its aluminum output reached 5.633 million tons._SMM
summary: China Hongqiao reported 2021 net profit up 53% and aluminum output of 5.633 million tons. The company attributes results to steady demand from vehicles, infrastructure, electronics and power, while China faces aluminum supply tightness from energy and power constraints, plus higher coal-linked production costs. Prices for aluminum products remain high.

title: LME Aluminium Jumped Over 4% on Low Inventory and Australian Sanctions on Russia_SMM
summary: LME aluminium jumped over 4% after Australia announced an immediate ban on alumina and bauxite exports to Russia, limiting Russia’s ability to produce aluminium. The move coincided with low aluminium inventories in China and overseas and recent losses of overseas production, supporting elevated short-term aluminium prices.

title: SMM Analysis on How Battery Recyclers Respond to Volatile Nickel Prices _SMM
summary: LME nickel trading resumed then was suspended again after a 46% slump beyond the daily downside limit, while SHFE prices remain volatile. title: LME Nickel Drops by 15% Limit, Narrowing Gap With Shanghai Price
summary: The article’s headline reports that LME nickel fell by 15% to its daily limit, tightening the price gap with Shanghai. title: Thiess Khishig Arvin JV secures contract extension at Oyu Tolgoi copper mine
summary: Thiess Khishig Arvin JV secured an extension for underground works at Rio Tinto’s Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia. The update reinforces operational continuity at a major copper project, but does not indicate a market-wide supply shock.

title: Nickel's tumble hurts hopes of Western Areas bump
summary: Nickel’s sharp decline is affecting Western Areas’ takeover prospects, with IGO Ltd facing pressure to adjust its $3.36/share offer after global nickel price moves. The headline suggests falling nickel has weakened deal hopes and market expectations in the near term.

title: Ukraine conflict: Australia bans alumina exports to Russia

title: Barrick gets to restart huge gold and copper project in Pakistan
summary: Barrick has reportedly reached a position to restart a large gold and copper project in Pakistan. title: First Quantum to Power Zambia Copper Mines With Wind, Solar
summary: First Quantum plans to power its Zambia copper mines using wind and solar. The shift toward renewables can reduce reliance on conventional power and potentially lower operating costs, supporting mine economics and short-term supply expectations for copper.

summary: Bloomberg reports First Quantum plans to fund a $500 million solar and wind installation to power its Zambia copper mines. summary: Nickel prices on the London Metal Exchange fell 15% to about $31,380/ton, repeatedly hitting limit-down for a third straight session. title: Aluminium jumps on Russian supply worries, nickel down
summary: Australia banned exports of alumina and aluminium ores to Russia, following sanctions. The ban, plus disrupted shipments from Ukraine, raised expectations of a raw-material shortfall for Russian smelters, pushing aluminium prices more than 5% higher. Separately, nickel fell to lower trading limits amid selling pressure and adjusted LME limits.

title: Latest News | Aluminium Association of India Seeks PMO Intervention as Coal Supply Deteriorates
summary: Aluminium Association of India urged PMO intervention after state-run Coal India curtailed road and rake coal dispatches to non-power users. The non-power sector, including aluminium captive power plants, faces dwindling coal stocks (below four days vs 15 days). The coal shortage is expected to worsen power supply for smelters.

title: Russia-Ukraine war: Rio Tinto's Russian partner under pressure over alumina export ban
summary: Australia ordered an immediate ban on exporting alumina and alumina ores to Russia, aiming to limit Russia’s aluminium-making capacity. title: Zambia's Mopani halts copper mining at a shaft after accident
summary: Zambia’s Mopani has suspended all operations at the South Ore Body (SOB) mine shaft after an accident during weekly maintenance. The suspension lasts until further notice as the company investigates the cause with safety officials and authorities. The halt reduces copper output in the near term and may weigh on copper prices.

title: Australian export ban pushes up aluminum prices
summary: Australia’s ban on alumina exports to Russia blocks shipments to Rusal’s supply chain, prompting Rio Tinto to comply with Canberra’s directions and raising concerns about Rusal’s ability to source alumina for its plants. The disruption coincides with a sharp jump in LME aluminum prices.

title: Glazed Aluminum Door and Window Systems from Insulgard Security Products™ Certified by UL to meet the ICC 500-2020 Standard and FEMA P-361-2021 Guideline
summary: Insulgard’s STORMDEFEND storm-shelter door and window systems, made with glazed aluminum, received UL certification to meet ICC 500-2020 and updated FEMA P-361-2021 guidance. With IBC-2021 requiring storm shelter components in 250 mph wind zones for certain buildings, the certification may support near-term demand for aluminium security glazing.

title: US Midwest aluminium premium falls from peak
summary: Fastmarkets assessed the US Midwest P1020A aluminium premium at 37–39 cents/lb, down from 38–40 cents/lb earlier and ending a record run. The fall follows weaker spot buying, lower P1020 offers, declining mill-grade scrap prices, and easing LME aluminium futures after a March peak amid Russia supply concerns.

title: District Copper Corp: CORRECTION FROM SOURCE: District Copper Identified Two Large Chargeability Targets on Copper Keg Property, Completes Airmag Survey
summary: District Copper reported results from a 19.3 km induced polarization survey at its Copper Keg porphyry copper project, identifying two large chargeability anomalies correlated with altered host rocks and sporadic copper mineralization. An airborne magnetometer survey has also been completed; interpretations are underway.

title: Aluminum shortage leads to walker supply issue
summary: SaskAbilities says a lack of available aluminum has created challenges obtaining folding walkers for loan to patients after hip and knee surgeries. The organization is urging people to return stored walkers to improve supply. The reported issue points to short-term aluminum availability constraints, but appears localized.

summary: The article focuses on nickel after a brief short squeeze that drove prices near quadruple within 48 hours. title: Automotive Aluminum Market Type Is Anticipated to Grow Faster Till – 2030
summary: The article, via an Allied Market Research report, forecasts faster growth in automotive aluminum usage through 2030, driven by urbanization and eco-friendly measures, especially in Asia-Pacific and LAMEA. title: Aussie export ban pushes aluminium prices up
summary: Australia will ban alumina exports to Russia, increasing supply pressure for alumina and affecting Moscow-based Rusal operations. title: Aluminium prices dip as China's COVID cases dampen growth outlook
summary: Aluminium prices edged lower as rising COVID-19 cases in Shanghai clouded China’s growth outlook. Losses were limited by supply concerns, including Australia’s export ban of alumina/ores to Russia and planned production cuts tied to higher energy prices. The piece also notes copper easing and nickel weakening into deeper downside limits.

title: Company ordered to clean up toxic copper waste mine site in Santa Fe National Forest
summary: A Florida company, Williams Express LLC, agreed to remediate a 19th-century Nacimiento copper mine site in/near the Santa Fe National Forest by removing about 80,000 cubic yards of tailings, relocating them to a disposal area on federal forestland, and capping the material. The action is environmental compliance, not operating mine supply.

title: Customs Data on China's Alumina Import and Export in February 2022 _SMM

title: Yunnan Shenhuo to Put 900,000 mt of aluminium Capacity into Operation by the End of April after Power Shortages Ease_SMM
summary: SMM says Yunnan’s aluminium smelters are ramping up as power shortages ease after higher-than-usual water supply. Yunnan Shenhuo restarted 220,000 mt and recently commissioned an additional 150,000 mt. The company plans to bring total aluminium capacity of 900,000 mt online by end-April.

title: SMM Morning Minutes: Fundamental of Nickel Remained Weak, SHFE nickel in Declining Fluctuations_SMM
summary: SMM reports fundamentals for nickel remain weak. summary: INSG reported that the global nickel market was oversupplied by 6,000 mt in January 2022, compared with a 5,300 mt supply shortage in January 2021. It also expects a 157,100 mt nickel supply shortage for 2022 versus a 103,700 mt surplus in 2021, signaling shifting balances.

title: LME Nickel Inventory Hit A New Low in Over Two Years, SHFE Nickel Inventory Hit Four-Month High_SMM
summary: SMM reports that LME nickel stocks plunged since late April, falling about 72% to a new two-plus-year low at 73,600 mt. Meanwhile, SHFE nickel inventories rose 16.15% over three weeks to a four-month high of 7,509 mt, indicating mixed but tighter global availability.

title: Zambia's 2021 copper production falls by 4.5% - statistics agency
summary: Zambia’s 2021 copper production fell 4.5%, according to ZAMSTATS. title: LME three-month nickel falls around 10%, doesn't hit limit down

summary: The article headline says nickel is trading higher on the LME “as buyers return after squeeze.” That suggests the prior dislocation from short-covering or tight supply-demand balance is easing and new demand is supporting upward price pressure in the very near term.

title: Spot Premiums were Weak amid High Copper Futures Prices_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says Shanghai copper cathode spot premiums fell to 240–310 yuan/mt over the 2204 contract, averaging 275 yuan/mt, down 55 yuan/mt day-on-day. summary: Meridian reports multiple zones of high-grade copper-gold at the Cabaçal project.
