It also notes copper supply disruptions and policy factors (e.g., Peru’s mining emergency) while warning that high overseas inflation and stock increases may limit upside.

title: Western Mines Group to drill bedrock conductors at Mulga Tank nickel-copper-PGE project
summary: Western Mines Group will drill nine holes at the Mulga Tank nickel-copper-PGE project in Western Australia after an MLEM survey identified bedrock conductor anomalies. Early holes target an electromagnetic plate and follow geochemical vectoring. Work is planned to start next week, with results guiding further drilling.

title: Chile's Copper Production Fell Sharply in February_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chile’s copper production fell sharply in February, according to Cochilco. Total output dropped 7.5% year-on-year to 394,700 mt. Escondida fell 14.3% to 69,900 mt and Collahuasi declined 11.2% to 46,900 mt, despite a slight rise at Codelco.

title: Aston Minerals extends nickel-cobalt strike at Bardwell prospect
summary: Aston Minerals says drilling at its Edleston project extends nickel-cobalt sulphide mineralisation to 1 km of strike, with multiple intercepts including up to ~0.44% nickel. The company also raises funds to accelerate resource-definition drilling and metallurgical testing, but no production impact is stated.

title: Nickel Prices Are Likely to Remain High_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says LME nickel has limited liquidity and prices remain elevated ($31,700–$33,600/mt). Russia-Ukraine tensions and China’s worsening COVID controls have prolonged pure nickel spot transport and warehouse delivery, tightening supply. Nickel sulphate discounts persist but are expected to narrow, keeping nickel prices deviation from fundamentals elevated.

title: LME to independently conduct Nickel Market Review Nickel Price wide volatility [Agency Review]_SMM
summary: The report highlights LME’s independent nickel market review after nickel price anomalies and volatility, alongside concerns about funds risk and potential financing/customer stress. It provides spot nickel ranges in yuan and notes low global inventories and ongoing cost/demand swings, suggesting continued high volatility but an unclear net price direction.

title: Peru Is Mulling Over Tax on Excess Profits from Mining, Freeport-Mcmoran Projects a Surge in Copper Demand _SMM
summary: Peru is mulling taxes on excess mining profits to address social protests, with the government still assessing the rate. As Peru is a major copper producer, policy uncertainty could affect near-term supply expectations. The piece also cites tighter market conditions and rising clean-energy demand, though tax risk dominates.

title: Decline in Overseas Alumina Prices Expanded amid Spillover Effect from Australian Ban on Alumina Exports to Russia_SMM
summary: SMM reports overseas alumina FOB Western Australia prices fell 8% to $440/mt on April 6 after Australia’s ban on alumina exports to Russia redirected material into the spot market. The overseas-China price spread narrowed, reducing exporter profits, while domestic alumina stayed mostly stable.

title: SMM March Aluminium Downstream Composite PMI in Contraction Range with Less-Than-Expected Operating Rates_SMM
summary: SMM’s March composite PMI for China’s aluminium downstream processing came in at 49.1 (down y/y), reflecting COVID-related logistics and production disruptions, lower-than-expected operating rates, and weaker orders. Several segments remain in contraction, with rising finished-product inventories. Easing is hoped in April, but near-term demand looks soft.

title: Inventory of LME Aluminium Dropped to a New Low of More than 16 Years_SMM
summary: LME data show aluminium inventories fell further after a prior surge, reaching 623,325 mt and a new 16-year low. SHFE inventories in Shanghai also declined for a third straight week, down 1.02% to 305,805 mt. The falling stocks suggest tighter near-term availability for aluminium.

title: Chinese Aluminium Smelters' Costs Increased to 18,000 yuan/mt amid Sharply Rising Prebaked Anode Prices _SMM
summary: SMM reports Chinese aluminium smelters lifted April prebaked anode bids by 850 yuan/mt, pushing total smelter costs up to 18,317 yuan/mt from last week. Meanwhile aluminium prices fell, cutting profits. While coal prices eased in some regions, cost volatility from alumina, freight rates, and anodes remains high.

title: Copper Import Market Stagnated due to Weak Price Ratio and Deterioration of Pandemic_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai copper import premiums for warrants are stable but remain low, while transactions are scarce. Deteriorating COVID-19 conditions have limited logistics operations, kept key warehouses closed, and reduced downstream willingness to collect goods. Traders are mostly inactive, awaiting unsealing, supporting a near-term bearish tone for copper.

title: JPMorgan is Assessing Commodity Exposure Following a Short Squeeze in Nickel Market _SMM
summary: JPMorgan is reviewing its commodity client relationships after a short squeeze in LME nickel futures last month. Management has ordered renewed due diligence and risk assessments, including on metals traders/refiners and financing units. The bank is already reducing nickel exposure and may scale back commodities business, tightening financing conditions.

title: BHP Australian nickel operation secures clean power from Italy's Enel | Kat Country 98.9
summary: BHP signed a 12-year contract with Enel Green Power for wind electricity for two Nickel West operations in Western Australia. The wind farm will supply power for the Kalgoorlie smelter and concentrator from 2024. Combined with other solar deals, BHP expects nearly 60% lower Scope 2 emissions, supporting “green” nickel branding.

title: MAX Resource Corp.: Max Resource Reports New High-Grade Copper-Silver Discovery at URU
summary: Max Resource Corp. reported new high-grade copper-silver discovery results at its URU area within the Cesar copper-silver project in Colombia. Channel sampling returned multiple open-ended intercepts around 8–12% copper and high silver grades, with mineralization extending over strike and vertical ranges.

title: BHP Australian nickel operation secures clean power from Italy's Enel
summary: BHP will use electricity from Enel Green Power’s Flat Rocks Wind Farm to cover all power needs for two Nickel West operations in Western Australia. Enel will build the A$200 million wind project, with output matching power requirements from 2024. Combined renewables deals cut Nickel West Scope 2 emissions by ~60% versus 2020.

title: Blackstone kicks off Vietnam nickel refinery pilot
summary: Blackstone Minerals delivered nickel-cobalt sulphide feed to ALS for Ta Khoa refinery pilot trials after restarting the Ban Phuc nickel concentrator in Vietnam. The company processed ore to produce sulphide flotation product, plans a 400kt refinery capacity, and is developing high-purity NCM811 nickel precursor products for batteries.

title: April 6th LME aluminum inventory decreased by 3450 tons the largest drop in Klang warehouse_SMM
summary: SMM reports that LME aluminum inventories fell by 3,450 tons on April 6, marking the largest drop in the Klang warehouse. Lower visible exchange stocks can signal tighter near-term availability and improve market sentiment for aluminium prices.

title: Oligarch linked to Aughinish Alumina could face EU sanctions
summary: Oleg Deripaska, a major shareholder in Aughinish Alumina via Rusal, is under consideration for EU sanctions. The EU is also preparing wider measures against Russia, including bans on certain imports and restrictions on banks, vessels, and procurement. Such steps could disrupt Russia-linked alumina/aluminium supply.

title: Markets Plunge as Trump Plans Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum
summary: The article reports Trump plans 25% tariffs on steel and 10% tariffs on aluminum starting next week, with markets falling sharply on the policy. Aluminum is directly targeted, likely tightening import supply. The broader risk-off tone could weigh on industrial demand, creating offsetting forces for copper.

title: Oligarch linked to Aughinish Alumina set to be sanctioned by EU
summary: EU is considering sanctions on Oleg Deripaska, a major shareholder in Aughinish Alumina via Rusal, alongside broader measures targeting Russia’s financial sector and trade. Proposed bans on coal, limits on bank transactions, port access restrictions, and potential further action on fossil-fuel revenues increase supply-chain and risk concerns for industrial metals.

title: China Aluminium Ingot Social Inventory Rose as Pandemic Undermined Consumption _SMM
summary: China’s aluminium ingot social inventory rose to 1.05 million mt on Apr 6, up 13,000 mt week-on-week. Growth came mainly from Wuxi after buyers couldn’t collect cargos due to truck shipment hindrances. SMM links the rise to reduced transport efficiency during the pandemic and will monitor effects on prices.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 800 mt during Tomb-sweeping Day_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventory across major Chinese markets fell 800 mt from Apr 1 to 136,900 mt, with destocking slowing during the Qingming holiday. Pandemic-related logistics delay picking up goods, while south China consumption stayed weak as rod factories were on holiday. Overall, inventory is expected to rise slightly this week.

title: Sun Summit Minerals : Discovers Zone of Strong Copper and Silver Mineralization West of Buck Main and Provides Update From Current Drill Program
summary: Sun Summit Minerals announced results from ongoing drilling and rock-chip sampling at its Buck Property, central British Columbia, including assays up to 0.47% copper in newly discovered mineralized zones. It outlines further planned follow-up work and geophysics, but remains exploration-stage and unlikely to move near-term copper prices.

title: Open consultation on aluminium billet and P1020A assessments submitted for IOSCO audit
summary: Fastmarkets opened an IOSCO-compliant consultation to review methodologies used for publishing aluminium premiums, including MB-AL-0302 and MB-AL-0300 6063 extrusion billet premiums (DDP terms) and the MB-AL-0316 aluminium P1020A premium. The update adds an Italy FCA premium as part of the audited pricing framework.

title: CORRECTING and REPLACING: Core Assets Discovers Additional Mineralized Copper Occurrence During Successful Winter Accessibility Assessment at the Blue Property
summary: Core Assets reports an additional mineralized copper occurrence found during a successful winter accessibility assessment at its Blue property. The update increases confidence in the site’s copper potential, which can be marginally supportive for near-term copper market sentiment, though details on size and economics are not provided here.

title: Current Views on Gold, Copper and Crude Oil
summary: The article highlights copper’s supportive near-term backdrop: Chile reported a 7% YoY decline in February output and tight supply is expected to underpin prices. It also notes China’s draconian COVID lockdowns may weaken growth, but maintains a bullish copper view while price holds above the 200-day moving average.

title: Rusal exports first Guinea bauxite in nearly a month, data shows
summary: Reuters reports Rusal exported its first Guinea bauxite shipment in nearly a month, after disruption from the war in Ukraine. Using shipments via Kamsar port, ore feeds Rusal’s Aughinish refinery in Ireland. With Australia having banned bauxite exports to Russia, any resumed Guinea supply supports aluminium refining availability.

title: Aluminum demand affecting beverage, pet food packaging in NH
summary: The article links a growing aluminium can “can-demic” to higher demand from craft beer and pet food packaging alongside tighter supply. It notes China cutting production and suppliers raising purchase minimums, leaving smaller firms relying on third parties. Can prices nearly doubled pre-pandemic, suggesting bullish aluminium price pressure.

title: Consumer News: Aluminum shortage could affect canned beer and cat food, tips to get a deal on your next flight
summary: CNN reports shortages affecting grocery items like canned beer and cat food are linked to an aluminum shortage ahead of peak demand. The article attributes the gap to labor and broader supply-chain disruptions and notes China’s pollution crackdown reducing aluminum manufacturing. Experts expect the issue to persist for months.

title: There may be a gap in the supply and demand of nickel resources around 2024. The prospect of nickel price continues to rise [institutional review]_SMM
summary: The piece expects nickel prices to rise, citing a potential future supply-demand gap in nickel resources around 2024. It links demand growth to high-nickel ternary lithium battery benefits (energy density and battery life), and notes beneficiaries across the ternary precursor and cathode chain, including Philippine nickel producers.

title: Widening gap between global supply and demand of aluminum [institutional research report]_SMM
summary: Rising European off-season electricity prices are expected to keep some European aluminium capacity offline, with 100k–250k tonnes of smelter production at risk. Higher energy and cash costs could also pressure output. China and Russia may partially offset, but the global supply-demand gap is seen widening.

title: Canada Nickel raises $51.6 million to bring Timmins deposit to mine-ready stage
summary: Canada Nickel raised $51.6 million via flow-through shares to advance technical studies for its Crawford nickel sulphide project and pay some debt. It also reported strong infill drilling results, including a high-grade nickel intercept. The company plans further step-out drilling, an updated resource estimate mid-year, and a feasibility study by year-end.

title: SMM Detailed Analysis of Chinese Aluminium Smelters' Costs and Profits in March and Forecast for Q2_SMM
summary: SMM reports Chinese aluminium smelters were profitable in March, with average full costs easing QoQ amid cheaper coal and power in some regions. It forecasts Q2 cost uncertainty: coal/power costs may fall somewhat, but overall costs likely rise due to energy and petroleum-coke volatility and high anode prices, supporting aluminium.

title: SMM Comments: INE Bonded Copper Contract Fell under the Pressure of Fed Rate Hikes_SMM
summary: SMM reports the INE bonded copper contract dropped sharply overnight to around 66,000 yuan/mt, falling below the daily moving average with bulls reducing positions. The move is attributed to Fed minutes signaling potential faster tapering and at least one 50 bp hike, lifting the dollar and weighing on copper.

title: COVID Lockdown in Shanghai Paralysed Local Copper Market While Boosting Premiums in Neighbouring Regions  _SMM
summary: A Shanghai COVID lockdown suspended warehousing logistics, leaving the spot copper market stagnant in the city. Downstream firms diverted purchases to smelters and warehouses in bordering Jiangsu and Zhejiang, where inventories were limited. With demand rising, local copper premiums jumped from about 300 yuan/mt before Qingming.

title: CITIC Securities: Nickel Resources to See Supply Deficit around 2024, Nickel Price Outlook Remains Bullish _SMM
summary: SMM cites CITIC Securities saying nickel prices may be influenced by non-fundamental factors in the short term, but the longer outlook is bullish. Fewer new nickel resources are expected over the next five years, and high-nickel NMC battery demand should rise, potentially leading to a supply deficit around 2024.

title: Aughinish Alumina unlikely to be hit by EU's new Russia sanctions, says Coalition
summary: The Irish government says Aughinish Alumina’s immediate parents Rusal and EN+ are unlikely to face the next EU Russia sanctions. However, EU sanctions on Deripaska raise concerns that counterparties could stop trading. Aughinish converts bauxite to alumina for European aluminium smelters, so disruptions could pressure aluminium supply and prices.

title: Georgia reveals its main export destinations for copper ore
summary: Georgia’s copper ore exports rose 65% year-on-year in January–February 2022 to $156.2 million. Bulgaria and China increased purchases sharply, with China taking $73.8 million (+73.6%). The report points to stronger export flows that may bolster short-term expectations of copper supply.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Retains Ausenco and Provides Update for Van Dyke Project
summary: Copper Fox provided an update on its 100%-owned Van Dyke in-situ copper recovery project, including completion of initial ADEQ/EPA meetings and steps toward UIC and aquifer protection permits for Class III wells. The company retained Ausenco for process and hydrogeological services and plans further work programs pending approvals.

title: Japanese buyers agree to pay $172 per tonne for aluminum premium in the second quarter_SMM
summary: Japanese buyers agreed to pay a $172/tonne premium for aluminum shipments in Q2 (April–June), down 2.8% from the prior quarter. The premium decline reflects weak demand in Japan and China, offsetting concerns about possible supply disruptions in Russia. Premiums are linked to LME spot pricing.

title: April 7 LME aluminum inventory reduction of 100t Kaohsiung warehouse increase was largely offset by decreases in Kaohsiung and Singapore_SMM
summary: SMM reports LME aluminium inventory levels across major warehouses on April 7. A 100t Kaohsiung warehouse inventory reduction occurred, but was largely offset by decreases in Kaohsiung and Singapore. The resulting headline points to slightly tighter aluminium availability in the near-term warehouse system.

title: Pandemic Delivers Demand Shock in East China Aluminium Market_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM’s survey says East China’s aluminium plate/sheet, strip and foil demand is hit by the severe pandemic, with falling orders and disrupted shipments. As a result, some producers in Henan are cutting operating rates, indicating weaker near-term aluminium consumption and likely bearish price pressure.

title: Goldman Sachs Says the Reduction in Global Copper Inventories Will Trigger A Supply Shock_SMM
summary: Goldman Sachs says global refined copper inventories are set to decline faster than expected, warning of a potential supply shock. It raised its 2022–2024 shortfall estimates materially, suggesting visible inventories could be depleted by Q4. Despite only modest price gains so far, analysts view fundamentals as tightening.

title: End-users Production was Hindered by Firm Copper Scrap Prices_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Shandong bare bright copper prices holding at 66,700-66,800 yuan/mt while copper scrap prices remain firm. Pandemic-related transport restrictions have hindered scrap supply, worsening after Tomb-Sweeping Day. Downstream recycling and end-user production cannot run at full capacity due to difficulty obtaining scrap, likely supporting nearby copper sentiment.

title: BHP Nickel West secures wind power for Southern nickel operations
summary: BHP Nickel West signed a power purchase agreement with Enel Green Power for the Flat Rocks Wind Farm, expected to supply 100% of power needs for several nickel operations in Western Australia from 2024. The deal supports decarbonization and reliability but does not imply near-term output changes for nickel.

title: Moxico considers $100m investment to expand Zambia copper mine
summary: Moxico Resources plans to invest $100m to expand its majority-owned Mimbula copper mine in Zambia. The project would create jobs and increase tax revenues for the Zambian government. The copper-rich oxide and sulphide deposit on the Copperbelt underpins expectations of higher future copper supply.

title: Rio Takes Full Control of Rusal Alumina Partnership in Australia
summary: Rio is set to take full control of its Rusal alumina partnership in Australia. The move is linked to upstream alumina supply, an input for aluminium smelting, which can affect production expectations. However, the provided text lacks specifics on output, disruptions, or delays, limiting near-term price direction.

title: Go Metals Corp.: Go Metals 2.4 KM Drill Program at Nickel-Copper Sulphide Project
summary: Go Metals Corp. contracted an operator for a 2,400m summer diamond drill campaign at its Quebec nickel-copper sulphide project. Targets include near-surface nickel-copper sulphides (with reported grab-sample grades) and permitting for up to 20 holes. The release is exploratory and does not indicate immediate supply changes.

title: Go Metals Corp.: Go Metals 2.4 KM Drill Program at Nickel-Copper Sulphide Project
summary: Go Metals Corp. announced a contracted 2,400m summer diamond drill program at its Quebec nickel-copper sulphide HSP project. Targets are surface-proven for nickel-copper sulphide mineralization with stated Ni (0.3–1.8%) and Cu (0.3–4.0%) grades, with permitting underway for up to 20 holes.

title: Japan buyers agree to Q2 aluminium premium of $172/T, sources say
summary: Japan agreed a Q2 aluminium premium of $172/t over the LME cash price, down 2.8% and below initial producer offers. Sources cite weak auto demand and ample Asian supply as China exports more aluminium. Russia disruption concerns eased as Rusal kept shipments, though traders may divert supply.

title: DEEP-SOUTH TO ACQUIRE UP TO 80% OF THREE COPPER EXPLORATION LICENCES IN THE HEART OF THE ZAMBIA COPPER BELT
summary: Deep-South Resources signed an earn-in agreement to acquire up to 80% of three copper exploration licences in Zambia’s Copper Belt. The deal includes payments and share issuance subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval, with soil sampling and potential drilling plans. No resources or economic viability are estimated yet.

title: Rio freezes Russian links at Queensland alumina
summary: Rio Tinto says it will no longer need to consult its Russian partner, Rusal, on operational decisions at a shared Queensland alumina refinery after taking “step-in” rights tied to sanctions. Rusal keeps its 20% ownership, but loses influence over maintenance and operations, potentially supporting supply confidence for aluminium-linked markets.

title: Rio Tinto takes full control of Queensland alumina refinery after Russian oligarchs sanctioned
summary: Rio Tinto took full control of Queensland Alumina Limited after Australia sanctioned Deripaska and Vekselberg and banned export of bauxite products to Russia. Rio will run 100% of QAL capacity and governance until further notice, aiming for uninterrupted operations. Activists welcomed the move, reducing uncertainty for aluminium-related inputs.

title: Bunting Establishes New Castle, Pennsylvania, Aluminum Extrusion Mill
summary: Bunting will open a new aluminum extrusion mill in Pennsylvania, redeveloping a large facility and investing in equipment and workforce via state incentives. The expansion targets construction, automotive, and transportation markets, suggesting incremental aluminum consumption from extrusion production.

title: Azure Minerals: Exquisite timing – a new nickel/copper resource in WA
summary: Azure Minerals’ managing director discusses a newly defined nickel/copper/cobalt resource in Western Australia. The piece frames the discovery as arriving while nickel and copper prices are “booming,” which could boost sentiment around future supply prospects and provide a modest near-term supportive effect for nickel and copper.

title: SMM China Aluminium Social Inventory Added 25,000 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China aluminium social inventory reached 1.07 million mt as of April 7, up 25,000 mt on the week. Wuxi rose most (+36,000 mt) due to pandemic-related transportation constraints limiting warehouse shipments. Other regions were mostly flat or down, including Nanhai (-7,000 mt).

title: DADA, CONCORD AND INVITALIA ACQUIRE ITALIAN ALUMINIUM ROLLING BUSINESS
summary: DADA Holdings, Concord Resources and Italy’s Invitalia acquired the business unit of Slim Fusina Rolling in Venice, Italy, including a vertically integrated cast house and rolling mills. The operation has about 75,000 t/year rolling capacity, and production and deliveries were maintained through its prior insolvency process.

title: SMM Comments: Prices of Secondary Copper Stabilised at a High Level among Fluctuations_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shandong secondary/copper-related self pickup prices (bare bright copper) at 66,700–66,800 yuan/mt, unchanged from April 7. Supply tightness worsened after Qingming, but secondary copper prices stayed stable despite slight overall copper declines. Poor recycling and transport efficiency may reduce secondary copper rod operating rates this week.

title: Shanghai aluminium, tin extend losses on demand concerns
summary: Shanghai aluminium prices fell to a three-week low as fresh China lockdowns and expectations of tighter monetary policy raised worries about weaker growth and metals demand. A stronger dollar pressured dollar-priced commodities, pulling LME and ShFE copper lower too, with nickel trading/infrastructure concerns adding sentiment drag.

title: East London commuters bear brunt of cost as copper gangs strip railway
summary: Organized gangs are stripping copper cables from Prasa’s electrified East London railway line, forcing commuters to switch to costly taxis. Police report seizures including 47kg of copper cables and arrests over infrastructure theft. The losses reduce accessible copper cable supply, potentially supporting copper prices.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 150,000 wmt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM said nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 150,000 wmt week-on-week to 5.737 million wmt (45,100 mt Ni content). Inventories at seven major ports also declined. The decline is slowing, but as the Philippines rainy season ends, imports may rise, potentially moderating tightness.

title: LME aluminum inventory decreased by 4025 tons on April 8th, with the biggest drop in Klang and Singapore warehouse_SMM
summary: SMM data shows LME aluminium inventories fell by 4,025 tons on April 8, with the biggest reductions in the Klang and Singapore warehouses. The inventory draw suggests tighter available supply in key shipping regions, which can support aluminium pricing over the following days.

title: SMM Data: Operating Aluminium Capacity Stood at 40 Million mt in March with Monthly Output of 3.315 million mt_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s March aluminium output at 3.315 million mt with no production cuts and operating rates around 90.8%. Capacity in Yunnan and Guangxi is resuming smoothly, lifting expected April output. Recurring pandemic disruptions are hurting transport and demand, leaving a supply-demand mismatch and rising social inventories through late April.

title: North American Nickel Inc. Announces Upsize of Previously-Announced Best Efforts Private Placement to $10 Million
summary: North American Nickel Inc. upsizes a private placement to about $10m via subscription receipts that will be used for exploration, development, working capital and general purposes. The company also outlines a proposed reverse takeover with Premium Nickel Resources to advance nickel assets. No direct production or trade changes are stated.

title: Michigan Capitol visitor center: Aluminum shortage delays opening
summary: Michigan’s Capitol visitor center opening was delayed because the project could not source aluminum for curtain wall glass frames. The Capitol Commission expects a late-June opening, with delays linked to broader supply-chain constraints and possible access issues to Russian-origin aluminum, though officials cite unknown factors.

title: Glencore may take over Aughinish Alumina from Russian parent
summary: EU discussions to separate Aughinish Alumina from its Russian parent have reportedly progressed toward a Glencore takeover. Deripaska is being sanctioned, but Aughinish is expected to be outside scope. The government wants uninterrupted alumina supply for European aluminium, easing supply-chain and trading concerns.

title: Fan Shunke: seize the opportunity to promote the high-level export of China's aluminum and aluminum products_SMM
summary: The article urges China’s aluminium processing industry to expand high-end aluminium exports, arguing that overseas aluminium prices are currently stronger than domestic prices and overseas processing fees are rebounding. It cites supportive policies (tax rebate/no tariffs in most cases) and recent trade-relief outcomes, aiming to raise exports and shift toward higher-value products.

title: Weak pure nickel supply and end demand Shanghai nickel weak volatility [SMM Nickel Weekly report]_SMM
summary: SMM’s nickel weekly report notes nickel supply remains weak, with domestic epidemic worsening spot transport and delivery of pure nickel. Nickel sulfate supply is relatively tight as raw material shortages transmit downstream. Shanghai nickel trends slightly lower but tight fundamentals still provide support; next week is forecast 202,000–222,000 yuan/ton.

title: Metals Acquisition Corp's acquisition of Glencore's CSA copper mine sparks guesses on who is next
summary: Metals Acquisition Corp agreed to buy Glencore’s CSA copper mine for about $US1.1 billion and will receive a 1.5% copper net smelter royalty. Investors are speculating about further portfolio deals in NSW’s Cobar region, which can bolster near-term copper market sentiment.

title: Guinea: Foreign Mining companies ordered to process bauxite on site
summary: Guinea’s junta ordered foreign mining firms to propose by end-May a timetable to build bauxite refineries in-country and to produce raw materials locally, warning of penalties for delays. With China relying heavily on Guinean bauxite, the move could disrupt or raise costs in feedstock supply for aluminium, lifting near-term price expectations.

title: IGO boosts nickel bid by 15pc as market surges
summary: IGO Group increased its bid by about 15% for nickel miner Western Areas after its takeover attempt was overtaken by soaring nickel prices. An independent expert previously said IGO’s last $3.36-per-share offer was not fair. The revised offer reflects the improved nickel-price environment.

title: St-Georges Eco-Mining Corp.: Discovery of a High-Grade Nickel & Palladium Ore Body
summary: St-Georges Eco-Mining disclosed additional core assay results from Quebec’s Manicouagan Project, including high-grade nickel (up to 9.49% Ni) and copper values (up to 2.2% Cu), along with significant palladium and other PGEs. The company is re-logging unsampled core to extend the Ni–Cu–PGE discovery corridor.

title: Aluminum crunch hits Las Vegas craft breweries
summary: Las Vegas craft breweries face an aluminum can crunch as global supply is disrupted, especially after China lockdowns reduced output of the world’s largest aluminum producer. Can costs are reported nearly 125% higher, forcing bigger orders and warehousing three months ahead, delaying expansion.

title: Domestic spot strength temporarily supports copper price [institutional review]_SMM
summary: The report cites temporarily stronger China spot support for copper: domestic warehouse receipts fall and spot premiums versus futures remain firm, while mine supply disturbances in Chile and Peru are increasing. It also notes weak recycled copper supply and logistics disruption from epidemics, but net near-term fundamentals are price-supportive.

title: SHFE Aluminium Still under Downward Pressure amid Regional Supply-Demand Imbalance_SMM
summary: SHFE 2205 and LME aluminium are down on the week after Qingming, with the macro backdrop bearish (hawkish Fed, strong USD, volatile energy amid Russia sanctions). Fundamentals cite higher China output and capacity growth, weaker consumption, and rising social inventories, extending pandemic-related supply-demand imbalance.

title: Overseas Alumina Prices Erased Previous Gains, While Domestic Prices Inched Higher_SMM
summary: Overseas alumina prices fell sharply after Australia banned alumina exports to Russia, easing supply tightness as material entered the spot market. Domestic alumina prices edged higher on bauxite shortages in Guizhou and restocking by resuming aluminium production, but new capacity release could push the market toward surplus, keeping a mixed outlook.

title: Spot Copper Concentrate TCs Targeted $80/mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports the Imported Copper Concentrate Index at about $79.28/mt, above the prior week, with buyers’ inquiries above $80/mt. Peru’s curfew and transport strikes, plus some Chilean port disruptions, challenge copper cathode logistics. Smelters and abundant inventories still keep TCs near $80/mt.

title: Chile's Copper Output Dropped Sharply in February_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Cochilco said Chile’s copper output fell sharply in February. While Codelco output rose slightly year-on-year to 123,600 mt, other major mining companies’ production dropped materially. The report implies weaker Chilean supply into the coming weeks, which is generally bearish for copper prices.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 5,000 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM said copper inventories in major Chinese markets fell 5,000 mt from Friday to 135,300 mt, dropping on Mondays for six straight weeks. COVID-19 traffic and testing rules limited warehouse arrivals (e.g., Shanghai loading/unloading delayed until April 15), and arrivals are expected to stay subdued, keeping weekly stocks declining.

title: Russian nickel, palladium, chromium exports a headache for Germany | Business | Economy and finance news from a German perspective | DW
summary: DW reports Germany relies significantly on Russian nickel, with Russia a major supplier of high-grade “class 1” nickel. With EV-driven nickel demand rising, fears of Russian export or EU/Moscow sanctions have previously sparked price spikes and suspended LME trading, keeping supply anxiety elevated. Copper is mentioned but less central.

title: LME aluminum stocks fell 5900 tons on April 11th, the lowest level since November 2005._SMM
summary: SMM reports that LME aluminum stocks declined by 5,900 tons on April 11, reaching the lowest level since November 2005. The piece details stock changes across major global warehouses. Lower visible exchange inventories suggest tighter near-term supply conditions, which can support aluminium prices.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay Reports Over 53% Copper for Direct Shipping Product from Storm Copper Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay announced that ore-sorting tests at its Storm Copper Project in Nunavut produced a very high-grade direct shipping product, with a reported 53.9% Cu grade (chalcocite). A June 2022 diamond drilling program is planned to define resources and new zones, but no production or market supply changes are stated.

title: NORDEN CROWN INTERSECTS HIGH-GRADE COPPER AT BURFJORD JV COPPER-GOLD PROJECT
summary: Norden Crown reported results from 12 diamond drill holes at its Burfjord copper-gold project in Norway, including several copper intercepts (up to 1.27% Cu over 12m). The company says the follow-up drilling outlines broad copper zones and notes discrete cobalt and nickel mineralization, but no production changes.

title: Kamoa Copper Achieves Record Quarterly Production of 55,602 Tonnes of Copper in Q1 2022, with a Record 19,605 Tonnes of Copper Produced in March
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says its Kamoa-Kakula complex in the DRC set a record Q1 2022 copper-in-concentrate output of 55,602 tonnes, including a record March and daily production. Phase 2 achieved commercial production on April 7 and is exceeding throughput, supporting higher 2022 copper guidance.

title: INSTALLED BUILDING PRODUCTS : ANNOUNCES THE ACQUISITION OF CENTRAL ALUMINUM SUPPLY CORPORATION - Form 8-K
summary: Installed Building Products announced the acquisition of Central Aluminum Supply (and Central Aluminum Supply of North Jersey), a distributor of gutter supplies and accessories used in residential and retrofit construction. The deal adds about $45 million of annual distribution revenue. Potentially modest incremental demand support for aluminum-containing building products.

title: Taxpayers to pump money in trial of low carbon alumina
summary: Taxpayers will fund 44% of a $19.7 million trial aimed at reducing the carbon footprint of Australia’s alumina refining. ARENA will contribute $8.6 million for emissions reductions at Alcoa/Alumina Ltd’s Pinjarra refinery in Western Australia. The move targets refining sustainability rather than immediate output changes.

title: Judge says Montana officials unlawfully approved copper mine
summary: A judge in Montana ruled that state officials unlawfully approved a copper mine. The decision could overturn or delay the project, potentially affecting near-term copper supply plans and tightening market expectations. That supply-risk angle is supportive for copper prices, while no evidence of nickel or aluminium effects is indicated.

title: Montana Judge says DEQ unlawfully approved construction of Black Butte Copper Mine
summary: A Montana judge ruled the state DEQ unlawfully approved construction of the Black Butte copper mine near the Smith River. Environmental groups alleged inadequate environmental analysis and disregard for public comments. DEQ says it will appeal and the operator reviews the decision, leaving uncertainty around timing and output.

title: Judge says MT DEQ unlawfully approved construction of Black Butte Copper Mine
summary: A Montana judge ruled the state DEQ unlawfully approved construction of the Black Butte Copper Mine, citing inadequate environmental analysis and failure to consider alternatives. The DEQ plans to appeal, while the mine operator reviews the decision. The outcome could delay or disrupt project progress, affecting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Playfair Begins Review of 100% Owned Nickel-Copper Assets at...
summary: Playfair Mining begins a review of its RKV Norway nickel-copper occurrences. The article notes nickel has surged to a 15-year high and argues EV demand growth plus an extended Russian (Norilsk) embargo likely tightens Class 1 nickel supply near term. It cites historical drilling results and plans further data review.

title: Playfair Begins Review of 100% Owned Nickel-Copper Assets at...
summary: Playfair Mining begins reviewing its RKV nickel-copper assets in Norway, focusing on historical Vakkerlien, Kaltberget and Olkar showings. The release reiterates that nickel prices have surged and argues Class 1 nickel tightness may worsen if Russian supply is embargoed. No new drilling or production changes are announced.

title: Montana judge: DEQ unlawfully approved construction of Black Butte Copper Mine
summary: A Montana judge ruled the DEQ unlawfully approved construction of the Black Butte copper mine, finding deficiencies in environmental review and failure to consider alternatives. DEQ plans to appeal and the operator is reviewing the decision. Legal uncertainty could delay operations, potentially tightening near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Montana judge says DEQ unlawfully approved construction of Black Butte Copper Mine
summary: A Montana judge ruled the DEQ unlawfully approved the Black Butte Copper Mine’s permit, saying required environmental analyses and consideration of alternatives were not properly done. DEQ plans to appeal and Sandfire Resources will review the decision. The legal challenge could delay or disrupt copper project timelines, affecting supply expectations.

title: Crude oil tumbled 4% in internal and external trading, metal fell in both markets, aluminum and nickel dived together [overnight market]_SMM
summary: Oil prices fell about 4% on concerns about weakening Chinese demand and expectations of additional IEA strategic reserve releases. The stronger dollar and macro data focus contributed to risk sentiment. Industrial metals dropped, led by aluminium (-3.64% offshore; SHFE -3.09%) and nickel (-2.37%), while copper also fell (~-1.61%).

title: Crude oil tumbled 4% in internal and external trading, metal fell in both markets, aluminum and nickel dived together [overnight market]_SMM
summary: Oil prices dropped 4% on worries about falling Chinese demand and plans to release strategic reserves. In line with weaker macro sentiment, industrial metals fell: aluminium dropped ~3–3.6% and nickel fell ~2–2.4% on demand-slowdown fears. Zinc was the only gainer on production cuts and lower European inventories.

title: Guinea asks bauxite miners to present local refinery plans by May
summary: Guinea’s interim government asked major bauxite miners to submit by May plans to refine bauxite into alumina domestically, with penalties if deadlines are missed. The country is a leading bauxite supplier, so the move could affect near-term alumina supply expectations and support aluminium-linked sentiment.

title: Lunnon Metals adds two historical nickel mines to Kambalda project
summary: Lunnon Metals will acquire rights to two historical nickel mines (Silver Lake and Fisher) in Western Australia from Gold Fields’ subsidiary, adding 19 mining leases to its Kambalda project. The company will raise up to $30m for exploration and re-entry plans, potentially strengthening nickel supply expectations.

title: AEX Gold Inc.: 2021 Sava Exploration Results Indicate Iron Oxide, Copper, Gold Style Mineralisation
summary: AEX Gold published 2021 exploration results from its Sava IOCG/porphyry-copper target in Greenland. Historical assays reported up to 3.4% copper, and 2021 rock chips found anomalous copper up to 0.9%. The company highlights coherent multi-element anomalies supporting further copper-focused exploration in 2022.

title: April 12 LME aluminum inventory increased for the first time recently by 925t Singapore warehouse increased by 3725 tonnes_SMM
summary: SMM reports LME aluminum inventory distribution as of April 12, noting aluminum stocks rose for the first time recently, including a 3,725-ton increase at the Singapore warehouse. The inventory build suggests soft prompt demand or improving supply balance, which is generally bearish for near-term aluminum prices.

title: Southern California firms to pay $1.8 billion for avoiding aluminum import duties
summary: Six Southern California firms linked to China Zhongwang were ordered to pay nearly $2 billion in restitution for evading U.S. anti-dumping/countervailing duties on aluminum extrusions by misrepresenting them as finished pallets. The metals sat in warehouses with no actual sales, leading to fraud charges and potential supply disruptions.

title: Ivanhoe's Congo copper mine achieves record production levels
summary: Ivanhoe said its Kamoa-Kakula copper mine in the DRC set a production record in Q1 2022 and that Phase 2 achieved commercial production quickly, supporting expectations of higher output through 2022–2023. Copper market coverage noted Comex-LME premiums and rising U.S. cathode imports from Chile.

title: Fabled Copper Corp.: Fabled Copper Locates New Copper Discovery Based on Geophysics and Increases Land Package by an Additional 2,924.43 Hectares
summary: Fabled Copper Corp. reports geophysical and surface prospecting results at its Muskwa Project, identifying an EM-1 copper anomaly and collecting float samples assaying up to 10.55% Cu. The company increased land holdings by 2,924.43 hectares and plans further work, but no production impact is mentioned.

title: Fabled Copper Locates New Copper Discovery Based on Geophysics and Increases Land Package by an Additional 2,924.43 Hectares
summary: The article headline reports that Fabled Copper has identified a new copper discovery using geophysics and expanded its land position by about 2,924 hectares. Exploration upside can improve expectations for future copper supply, typically supporting copper sentiment in the near term despite details being limited here.

title: BMW Group to use 100% sustainably produced aluminium for wheels from 2024
summary: BMW will use 100% sustainably produced cast aluminium wheels from 2024, with production powered by green power, and suppliers required to meet these conditions. BMW also expands secondary aluminium use (e.g., 70% in some Mini models), positioning demand toward lower-carbon aluminium supply and potentially supporting aluminium market sentiment.

title: Mining: Altus gets new license for copper & silver project in Morocco
summary: Altus Strategies said Morocco’s Ministry of Energy Transition granted a 10-year mining license for its Agdz copper and silver project near the Bou Skour Cu-Ag mine. The license gives long-term tenure security for the company’s copper prospects. No production schedule or output figures were provided.

title: Availability of Nickel reserves, Tax Incentives, and Increasing Favorability of EVs will drive the growth of Indonesia EV Charging Equipment Industry at a CAGR of 44% during 2022-26: Ken Research
summary: Ken Research says Indonesia’s EV charging equipment market will grow rapidly, citing tax incentives and “availability of nickel.” It notes Indonesia holds over 22% of the world’s nickel reserves and government plans to expand EV infrastructure, implying stronger battery-related nickel demand as investment grows.

title: Mining Licence Granted for Agdz Copper-Silver Project in Morocco
summary: Altus Strategies said Morocco’s ministry granted a 10-year mining licence for its Agdz copper-silver project. The licence provides long-term tenure for the company’s 100% owned assets, supporting development of multiple copper and silver prospects in the eastern Anti-Atlas. The announcement is copper-relevant but not an immediate production catalyst.

title: Candente Copper receives second financing offer for up to $10 Million to Advance the Cañariaco Copper Project
summary: Candente Copper said it received a second financing offer for up to $10 million to advance the Cariaco copper project. The update is directly tied to copper project development, but it provides no timeline for production or supply changes, implying limited near-term influence on copper prices.

title: SoCal Companies Ordered to Pay $1.83B Restitution in Aluminum Fraud Case
summary: Six Southern California companies tied to a fugitive Chinese aluminum billionaire were ordered to pay $1.83B in restitution for disguising imported Chinese aluminum extrusions to evade 2011 anti-dumping duties. Aluminum extrusions were reshaped into pallet-like forms and stockpiled at multiple warehouses, mainly via Los Angeles and Long Beach ports.

title: Nickel regulation passed despite pushback | The Quebec Chronicle Telegraph
summary: A Quebec province passed a controversial regulation that raises the allowable level of nickel in the atmosphere, overcoming local pushback. The regulation is set to come into effect later, implying changes to nickel emissions compliance for affected operations. Such rules can influence nickel production costs and short-term supply outlooks.

title: SoCal Companies Ordered to Pay $1.83 Billion Restitution in Aluminum Fraud
summary: Six Southern California companies were ordered to pay $1.83 billion in restitution for allegedly evading anti-dumping duties on imported aluminum extrusions from China. Prosecutors said aluminum was disguised to resemble pallets to avoid 2011 duties. The case may reduce duty evasion and tighten effective aluminum supply.

title: What has happened to the global aluminum market since the conflict between Russia and Ukraine? [institutional Research report]_SMM
summary: The report argues that since the Russia-Ukraine conflict escalated in Feb 2022, European power costs have surged, pushing aluminium smelters into production cuts and tightening spot supply. It also highlights growing sanctions and shipping worries around Russian producer Rusal, with knock-on effects from alumina logistics disruptions.

title: Demand weakens, supply releases, aluminum prices fall under pressure [institutional research report]_SMM
summary: The report attributes aluminum price declines to epidemic-related weakness in downstream processing starts and delayed demand, alongside expanding supply and only small inventory buildup. It also cites LME governance/clearing reviews after nickel-market events as adding pressure to Lun aluminum. It expects stabilization only if epidemic conditions improve.

title: 【SMM Morning Comments】The Supply of Refined Nickel Remains Tight, and the Nickel Prices are Expected to be Hard to Decline _SMM
summary: SMM reports refined nickel supply remains tight as pandemic conditions reduce China’s refined production, limit customs clearance, and disrupt south-market transport. North tightness and high SHFE–LME spread raise spot premiums and keep downstream restocking constrained. SMM expects domestic nickel prices to be hard to decline near term.

title: Alumina Price Difference between China and Overseas Began to Narrow, Export Window Likely to Close_SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices stable in China but falling overseas; the China–FOB spread narrowed sharply as export profits eroded and exporters turned cautious amid COVID disruptions. Tightness from ore shortages and rising aluminium capacity supports demand, but incoming alumina supply and weaker aluminium prices could push the market toward surplus.

title: SMM Monthly Aluminum Price Forecast for April 10-May 10 _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME aluminum prices fell in early April as macro conditions worsened (hawkish Fed, stronger USD). Domestically, supply rose with restarted and new smelting capacity and profits, while pandemic disruptions reduced downstream production and logistics, leading to inventory accumulation. Prices may stay pressured unless demand rebounds.

title: Major Battery Makers Raised the Share of LFP Battery in their Product Portfolio Further in Q1, and the Proportion of High-Nickel Battery also Rose_SMM
summary: SMM reports that major battery makers increased the proportion of LFP batteries, but also saw a rise in high-nickel NMC share in Q1. Lithium price strength raised procurement costs, leading to slower LFP purchasing, while advance orders boosted high-nickel NMC allocations. NEV demand was only slightly higher.

title: Nickel Sulphate Market Saw Significant Supply Deficit in March  _SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s nickel sulphate market ran a 4,825 mt (nickel content) supply deficit in March, extending three consecutive months of deficits. High raw-material costs reduced in-house briquette dissolution, forcing producers to cut output. Battery-grade prices are expected to stay supported in April as tight supply and high demand persist.

title: China March copper imports down 8.8% y/y on sluggish demand
summary: China’s March unwrought copper imports fell 8.8% year-on-year to 504,009 tonnes for the third straight monthly decline, attributed to sluggish manufacturing demand and COVID disruptions. Manufacturing PMI slipped below 50. The article also mentions aluminium exports rising in March, but the copper demand weakness is the key signal.

title: For the first time ever! Copper stocks actually fell in March Goldman Sachs: "Dr. Copper" has changed_SMM
summary: Goldman Sachs says copper fundamentals have tightened as global exchange inventories fell for the first time in a decade. It points to reduced Chilean output from water shortages and rising mine costs, plus sanctions-driven risks to Russian exports and freight. The firm forecasts larger refined supply gaps and higher copper prices.

title: Gold prices warm up to stimulate capacity expansion! GOLD.US plans to restart a copper and gold project at a cost of $7 billion_SMM
summary: Barrick Gold says it has revised plans with Pakistan to restart the large Reko Diq copper-gold project, estimating copper output of about 200,000 tons per year and investment around $7 billion. The company positions it as timely amid global copper shortages, which is likely to support near-term copper sentiment and pricing.

title: Recovery of Copper Consumption was Slow after the CNY Holiday, and the Operating Rates of Copper Cathode Rod Producers were less than Expected_SMM
summary: SMM says copper cathode rod producers’ average operating rate rose in March but remained below normal historical levels. It attributes the shortfall to late production resumption and high copper prices, plus mid-March COVID outbreaks in major regions that reduced downstream output, disrupted procurement and transportation, and forced some output cuts.

title: Infinitum Copper Reports 9.15 Metres of 16.45 g/t Gold, 1.90% Copper and 3.50 g/t Silver in Trenching at La Adelita Project
summary: Infinitum Copper reported trench results from its La Adelita project in Mexico, including intervals averaging 1.90% copper and additional copper-bearing skarn samples up to ~1.34% copper. The company is advancing geophysics and a new drilling program, but provides no near-term production or supply disruption details.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: US EV Battery Supply Chain: Talon Metals Purchases Three Additional Drill Rigs to Accelerate Battery Mineral Exploration at the Tamarack Nickel Project in Minnesota, USA
summary: Talon Metals purchased three additional drill rigs to expand exploration outside the main resource area at its Tamarack nickel-copper project in Minnesota. The new drilling targets multiple zones to find high-grade nickel-copper mineralization for potential battery supply, but current output is not reported as changing.

title: CopperBank Resources Corp.: CopperBank Confirms Historic, High-Grade Copper Intercepts and Identifies Mineralized Zones in Previously Unsampled Core at Copper Creek Project in Arizona; Update on Drilling Program
summary: CopperBank reports initial drill core re-sampling and assays from its Copper Creek project in Arizona, confirming historic high-grade breccia-hosted copper and identifying mineralization in previously unsampled core. Over 2,800 metres of a 5,000-metre drilling program are completed; additional assays are pending for broader evaluation and resource work.

title: A solid-state electrolysis process for upcycling aluminium scrap
summary: Nature reports a solid-state electrolysis (SSE) process using molten salts to upgrade aluminium scrap into high-purity aluminium comparable to primary metal, with projected energy consumption less than half of primary production. It frames rising demand for high-grade aluminium (e.g., EVs) and reduced demand for low-grade recycled aluminium.

title: Warnings sounded over Xinjiang-made aluminium in global supply chains
summary: Research warns that Xinjiang-made primary aluminium may be exposed to expanding US forced-labour enforcement under the UFLPA. Some Xinjiang producers are linked to alleged forced labour programmes. If customs restrictions grow or audits tighten, imports and downstream supply chains could face delays or denials.

title: Southwest Copper Industry strives to make a good start in the first quarter._SMM
summary: Southwest Copper (Yunnan) reports first-quarter progress in copper smelting output, cost reduction, and “green development” measures, including ongoing optimization of energy consumption per unit and amoeba-style performance management across branch plants. It highlights safety and environmental spending but offers no specific capacity or trade change affecting short-term copper pricing.

title: Southern Copper says Peru mine remains halted despite latest deal to end protests
summary: Southern Copper said its Peruvian Cuajone copper mine is still closed after six weeks of protests, with production halted since Feb. 28. A deal to end protests required withdrawal of complaints, but a railway blockade persists and the government has not ensured security. Peru’s copper production disruption is weighing on the economy.

title: The High Abroad and Low Domestic Aluminium Prices Drove the Export Volume of Domestic Unwrought Aluminium and Aluminium Semis Increasing Significantly YoY in March [SMM analysis]_SMM
summary: SMM reports China exported 594,400 mt of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis in March, up 34% YoY, driven by policy support, a low domestic price vs high overseas prices (SHFE/LME), weak Southeast Asia processing output, and overseas supply constraints. It forecasts high export levels despite Shanghai port disruptions and higher sea freight.

title: Consumption expectations are more optimistic. Shanghai Aluminum is strong and volatile. [closing comments]_SMM
summary: SMM says Shanghai Aluminum rebounded and remained volatile, closing up 1.42%. Exports are strong and overseas supply tightness is supported by new US sanctions/tariffs on Russian raw aluminum, potentially redirecting flows to Asia. Domestic production resumes and inventories are stable, but optimistic consumption expectations underpin support.

title: Net Imports of Nickel Sulphate Fell 16.7% MoM to 681 mt in Ni Content in February_SMM
summary: SMM cites customs data showing China’s nickel sulphate imports fell 16.7% month-on-month to 681 mt in nickel content in February, despite strong year-on-year growth. Exports were very small. The article expects March net imports to drop to 440 mt (-35.3% MoM) due to lower natural days and wider market price spreads.

title: Some Chinese Aluminium Plate/Sheet and Strip Producers Stopped Production due to the COVID-19 outbreak_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates for China’s aluminium plate/sheet and strip producers were 79.22% in March, with late-March COVID outbreaks disrupting purchasing, shipping and capital turnover. In April, more firms cut or stop production due to raw-material shortages and weaker downstream demand, with operating rates expected near ~74%.

title: The seasonal High of the Domestic Aluminium Wire and Cable Industry in March Brought a Recovery Operating rates _SMM
summary: SMM reports March operating rates for China’s aluminium wire and cable sector rebounded sharply as orders increased and production resumed, aided by grid-related UHV demand. April is expected to rise further. Pandemic disruptions affected some regions, but overall demand remains supportive, with weak exports due to high aluminium prices.

title: NPI Prices Fluctuated at High Levels in March due to the Extreme Price Moves of Nickel_SMM
summary: SMM reports that high-grade NPI prices in March rose with extreme LME and SHFE nickel moves, expanding the nickel-vs-NPI spread and causing downstream to pause purchases. After LME rules and falling nickel prices, the spread narrowed and NPI stabilized in early April. Weak demand suggests NPI may stay range-bound.

title: Alcoa begins to restart Alumar aluminum smelter in Brazil_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Alcoa has begun restarting its Alumar aluminum smelter in Brazil by electrifying the first 20 electrolytic cells, with full capacity targeted later this year. It also notes Hydro restarting capacity at Albras after power outages. Together, the moves suggest improving aluminum output supply and potential near-term price pressure.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventory in China Declined _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says China domestic aluminium billet inventories fell to 146,400 mt on Apr 14, down 8.02% week-on-week. Destocking accelerated in Foshan as downstream producers resumed restocking after aluminium prices dropped to 20,000 yuan/mt. East China flows remain disrupted by the pandemic, while Nanchang inventories rose on weak demand.

title: China's Yinbang Jumps After France's Valeo Orders USD314 Million of Aluminum
summary: Yinbang Clad Material’s shares rose after Valeo Thermal Systems placed a large order worth about USD314 million for aluminum alloy sheets. Deliveries are planned over three years and prices are linked to aluminum ingot costs. The deal is described as boosting earnings, but it is company-specific rather than a sector-wide shock.

title: Metal up, more down, less Shanghai nickel up 2.39%, Shanghai zinc down nearly 2% [SMM Daily Review]_SMM
summary: SMM’s daily review shows industrial metals mixed on LME but generally higher in China, led by Shanghai nickel (+2.39%) and Shanghai aluminium (~+1.5%). The piece attributes nickel strength to tighter pure nickel supply amid Shanghai epidemic disruptions and weaker demand, while LME copper is slightly up (~+0.45%).

title: Alcoa Announces Deal to Supply Low-Carbon EcoLumTM Aluminum to Speira; Sees Strong Growth in Sustainable Product Portfolio
summary: Alcoa announced a supply agreement to deliver low-carbon EcoLumTM aluminum to Speira and said it expects strong growth in its sustainable product portfolio. The news points to incremental contracted demand for aluminum, which can mildly support nearby aluminum price sentiment, though the contract size is not specified.

title: White Metal Resources Corp.: White Metal Partner Noronex Provides Update from Drilling at the DorWit Copper-Silver Project, Namibia
summary: White Metal Resources reports Noronex drilling updates from the DorWit Cu-Ag project in Namibia’s Kalahari Copper Belt. Results include numerous high-grade copper intercepts (e.g., 27m at 1.6% Cu) and mineralized strike-length extensions, with infill sampling underway. Overall, it supports bullish sentiment toward copper.

title: Mining company seeks to expand alumina production by a fourth
summary: Vinacomin is seeking government approval to expand bauxite mining at its Tan Rai and Nhan Co complexes by 23%, which would raise alumina production by 150,000 tons per year. Higher alumina availability could support aluminum smelting output and improve near-term supply expectations, affecting aluminium prices.

title: Aughinish Alumina plant in Limerick 'not impacted' by EU sanctions imposed on Russian oligarch
summary: EU sanctions on Russian oligarch Oleg Deripaska were reported to raise fears for Aughinish Alumina, but the Irish minister confirmed the Limerick alumina plant faces no direct impact. Aughinish is the EU’s largest alumina producer (used for aluminium), with Deripaska described as only a limited shareholder and not receiving dividends.

title: Chile's Cochilco raises 2022 copper price forecast to $4.40 per pound
summary: Chile’s Cochilco increased its 2022 copper price forecast to $4.40/lb, attributing the revision to lower inventories and concern that global supply may not meet expectations amid the Russia-Ukraine conflict. It also projected Chilean copper production rising 2.6% to 5.78 million tonnes.

title: Aluminum Ingot Social Inventory in China Declined when Compared to last Thursday _SMM
summary: SMM reported China’s aluminium ingot social inventory at 1.06 million mt on April 14, down from last Thursday, with some markets rising due to restricted shipments. COVID transport controls reduce logistics efficiency and increase costs, while downstream restocking after price pullbacks and spot premiums in Foshan suggest firmer aluminium sentiment.

title: EMX Acquires Additional Royalty Interest on Caserones Copper-Molybdenum Mine and to Complete US$10 million Financing with Franco-Nevada
summary: EMX Royalty Corporation acquired an additional 0.3155% NSR royalty on Chile’s Caserones copper-molybdenum mine for US$25.74 million, increasing its effective NSR to 0.7335%. Financing is completed via a C$12.58 million private placement with Franco-Nevada. Caserones produces copper and molybdenum concentrates and copper cathodes.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Acquires Additional Royalty Interest on Caserones Copper-Molybdenum Mine and to Complete US$10 million Financing with Franco-Nevada
summary: EMX Royalty acquired an additional effective 0.3155% NSR royalty on the Caserones copper-molybdenum mine in northern Chile for US$25.74 million and will be financed via a C$12.58 million private placement with Franco-Nevada. The update increases royalty exposure to copper output but does not change production or supply.

title: LME nickel prices: The short squeeze
summary: The piece reviews March events in LME nickel trading, noting that trading was suspended and then resumed amid disruption. Framed as a “short squeeze,” the episode likely drove unusual price dynamics. It also describes how these disruptions affected publication and display of LME nickel data on Fastmarkets.

title: Victory Nickel Inc. Update
summary: Victory Nickel filed a proposal to restructure unsecured debt under Canada’s Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, aiming to continue operating. The company also received bonus shares from Silver Elephant Mining related to the Minago Project, which become freely tradable later in 2022. The update is company-specific with no direct nickel supply impact details.

title: Metal floating red Shanghai nickel up more than 3.4% aluminum prices in the two markets are up more than 1.7% [overnight market]_SMM
summary: SMM’s overnight wrap says oil rose on possible action to ban Russian exports and the dollar strengthened. Despite macro headwinds, the article cites expectations of China stimulus supporting metals demand. It reports Shanghai copper up about 0.3%, nickel up about 3.49%, and aluminium up about 1.73%.

title: Lun Copper rose slightly as the market looked forward to China's stimulus measures._SMM
summary: LME three-month copper rose slightly as markets looked for further Chinese stimulus measures to support demand from the world’s largest copper consumer. The piece also cites a sharp year-to-date fall in LME copper stocks, which tightens supply expectations. Chile’s forecast lift reflects supply crunch concerns.

title: SMM Analysis：The Problems Faced by Copper Processing Companies in Jiangsu and Zhejiang under the Pandemic_SMM
summary: SMM reports copper rod and other copper-processing firms in Jiangsu/Zhejiang face logistics bottlenecks under Shanghai’s pandemic controls, limiting access to copper cathode and increasing costs. At the same time, State Grid infrastructure bids are postponed, terminal demand weakens, and April operating rates are expected to fall, pressuring copper consumption.

title: Metal general rally Shanghai Nickel rose more than 3.5% black line down [SMM afternoon review]_SMM
summary: SMM reports an overall metal rebound on April 15, despite a firmer dollar pressuring prices. Shanghai nickel led gains, up about 3.5%, supported by tight pure nickel supply and consecutive rises. Shanghai copper rose 1.14% and aluminium rose 1.92%, with spot market support cited for aluminium.

title: JP Morgan takes $524m XVA loss on nickel, Russia trades
summary: JP Morgan reported a $524m XVA loss in Q1 as surging nickel prices and sanctions against Russian banks hit counterparties. The loss widened sharply versus Q4 2021, highlighting heightened trading and valuation stress tied to nickel-linked exposures and sanctions-related risk transmission in derivatives.

title: SMM Research: Extrusion Drove up the Operating rates of Aluminium Downstream, the Pandemic Supressing Downstream Consumption_SMM
summary: SMM said major aluminium processors’ operating rates rose to 67.8% (+1.2pp) as pandemic-related suspensions recovered and some transport curbs eased. Aluminium extrusion operating rates increased to 75.5%. Some segments still faced weak orders and logistics limits, but the near-term trend supports aluminium demand and output.

title: SMM Research: Extrusion Sector Drove up the Operating rates of Aluminium Downstream, the Pandemic Supressing Downstream Consumption_SMM
summary: SMM says aluminium leading processing operating rates rose overall, helped by improving extrusion production after pandemic-related suspensions. Extruders increased to 75.5%, while some sheet/plate/strip and foil were stable. Demand and logistics remain constrained, especially for alloy, wire/cable, and secondary alloy. Recovery depends on easing transport restrictions.

title: SMM China Copper Inventory across Major Market Dropped 1,000 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s copper inventory across major markets fell slightly week-on-week to 139,300 mt, despite some regional gains. Logistics blockages are improving, but freight costs surged, limiting downstream restocking from Shanghai. With transport expected to normalize, inventory may drop again and downstream production could resume.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports fell 163,000 wmt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 163,000 wmt to 5.574 million wmt as of Apr 15, with seven major ports totaling 2.352 million wmt. Destocking is slowing because Philippine shipments remain unstable and mine supply is unlikely to rise soon, while NPI plant demand stays strong.

title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zone up 3,600 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s domestic bonded copper inventories rose 3,600 mt from April 8 to 310,100 mt by April 15, with increases in Shanghai and Guangdong. Even as the SHFE/LME ratio improves slightly, imports remain loss-making and demand for customs-declaration imports is weak, limiting copper circulation.

title: Aluminum plant to expand wind farm in Argentine Patagonia
summary: Argentine aluminium producer Aluar plans a US$130 million expansion of its wind farm in Patagonia, adding 81 MW by December 2023. The extra renewable electricity is intended to supply its primary aluminium plant, support a broader sustainable energy mix, and enable reactivation and value-chain development with higher production and exports.

title: UK Financial Regulators' Statement on Suspension of Nickel Trading on London Metal Exchange | Shearman & Sterling LLP
summary: UK financial regulators (FCA, PRA, and Bank of England) issued a joint statement on the LME’s suspension of nickel trading between March 8–16, 2022, citing challenging market conditions after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. They plan reviews of LME suspension/resumption processes and LME Clear risk governance, and may take further steps.

title: Copper wire theft a growing issue in Las Vegas area
summary: A Las Vegas-area report says copper wire theft is increasing, affecting agencies’ traffic communications equipment and streetlights. The RTC and Clark County cite significant repair hours, dozens of affected locations, and backlog-limited staffing, with areas added to wire replacement lists. The immediate implication is disrupted supply of installed copper wire and replacement needs.

title: Analysts: Chilean copper production stagnant, the world's largest copper producer may change ownership_SMM
summary: BMO analysts warn Chile’s copper output is stagnating and fell 7.5% year-on-year in January to the lowest in 11 years, citing ore quality and water shortages. They also note ongoing cathode declines and policy uncertainty (royalties/nationalization proposals), dampening investment prospects. Expansion hopes are uncertain.

title: The supply of pure nickel is tight and the demand is weak. Expected nickel shock operation in Shanghai [selected SMM Weekly report]_SMM
summary: SMM’s weekly nickel report says pure nickel supply remains tight while demand is weak. High Lunni prices and difficult contract implementation reduce willingness to hold inventory. Nickel sulfate supply is also tight, but high matte output disappoints. Overall, supply tightness supports prices, while weak demand pressures them.

title: Internal metal general rise Shanghai nickel rose more than 2% black generally fell back [Friday night trading]_SMM
summary: SMM reports broad gains in Shanghai industrial metals after macro/energy moves. Shanghai nickel rose 3.8% by the day close and another 2.42% in night trading. Shanghai aluminium gained over 2%. Shanghai copper also rose more than 1% during the day and 0.44% at night.

title: The central bank cut the reserve requirement to improve the short-term copper price [institutional review]_SMM
summary: China’s central bank cut reserve requirements by 25 bps, boosting risk sentiment and the article expects near-term support for copper. It notes low domestic copper warehouse receipts and rising spot, while highlighting constraints like mine supply disturbances, smelter outages/overhauls, and weak recycled supply.

title: Copper Prices Rose Rapidly amid Low Inventory_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports copper prices rose after a weak USD and improving SHFE/LME ratio. Macro inflation data fueled earlier dollar strength, but stimulus expectations—RRR cut—and anticipated normalization of logistics supported demand sentiment. Copper inventories across major Chinese markets edged down, and spot premiums were expected to stay firm, underpinning prices.

title: RRR Cuts and Expectations for Demand Recovery to Support SHFE Aluminium at Highs  _SMM
summary: China’s State Council and PBOC signaled and implemented RRR cuts, alongside expectations for demand recovery as COVID-related controls and local logistics improve. SMM expects aluminium supply to be higher but spot tightness persists from disrupted smelter shipments. Together, these factors are seen underpinning SHFE/LME aluminium prices near current highs.

title: Profits of Aluminium Smelters Dropped Significantly amid Volatile Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium smelter profits fell sharply as costs rose amid volatile prices. Freight rates increased, transportation costs were higher, while thermal coal prices eased slightly. Even with some benefit from captive power, alumina and auxiliary material volatility and rising freight are expected to keep aluminium production costs elevated, weighing on margins.

title: Alumina Prices Likely to Find Solid Support in the Short Term, But May Face Downward Pressure in the Long Run_SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices have firmed slightly week-on-week, while the export window is nearly closed and FOB Western Australia prices have reversed gains. Shanxi shutdowns impede cross-province transport, reducing supply, while smelters seek alumina from Henan and demand in southwest China supports prices. Oversupply risk is flagged longer term.

title: Metal in early trading more than red Shanghai nickel rose more than 2.4% black series have risen one after another [SMM afternoon review]_SMM
summary: SMM’s afternoon review says the dollar firmed and metal markets saw early pressure, but by midday Shanghai nickel surged 2.43%. Shanghai aluminium also trended higher on improving epidemic outlook and a reserve requirement cut, while North China electrolytic copper was slightly higher with limited downstream transactions.

title: Copper and aluminum: China's steady growth hedging risk of non-ferrous copper and aluminum is not easy to sell short [institutional review]_SMM
summary: The piece notes firm Chinese copper futures and flat aluminum prices, alongside recent sentiment stabilization from stimulus expectations. It stresses low LME inventories and market volatility, with LME reportedly considering measures against extreme zero-inventory conditions, implying inventory tightness risk but no clear net directional catalyst.

title: Copper and aluminum: China's steady growth hedging risk of non-ferrous copper and aluminum is not easy to sell short [institutional review]_SMM
summary: The piece notes firmer domestic copper futures and roughly flat aluminium, alongside China-led stimulus improving sentiment but geopolitical risks increasing volatility. It warns that LME inventories in major non-ferrous metals are at dangerous lows and could amplify swings, prompting LME to consider steps to avoid zero-inventory extremes.

title: Aluminium Ingot Inventory in China Extended Decline_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s social inventory of aluminium ingots fell to 1.04 million mt on April 18, extending a decline across most regions. Wuxi saw a limited uptick tied to logistics, while other areas dropped on sales and pickup. With production rising but downstream rates improving, spot demand is active and RRR cuts are expected to support near-term SHFE aluminium prices.

title: Cochilco lifts 2022 copper price projection amid Ukraine conflict
summary: Chile’s Cochilco lifted its 2022 copper price projection to $4.40/lb from $3.95 in January, citing scarcity concerns after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The Mining Minister warned some gains may be offset by higher fuel, steel, maritime transport and mining inputs. Cochilco also flagged risks from reduced Russian copper supply and higher energy costs.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets up 300 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventories across major Chinese markets rose 300 mt over the weekend to 139,600 mt. Guangdong and Jiangsu increased due to imports and domestic supply, while Shanghai and north China fell on logistics constraints and pandemic-related hindered shipments. SMM expects inventories to fall this week with logistics recovery and downstream restart.

title: China's primary aluminum production rose 1.8% in March compared with the same period last year due to recovery in output and huge profits._SMM
summary: China’s primary (electrolytic) aluminium output rose 1.8% year-on-year in March to 3.3 million tons, the highest since May last year, supported by higher profits and recovery. COVID outbreaks and anti-epidemic transport/blockade measures disrupted aluminum demand, while April production restarts in Yunnan/Guangxi may keep supply growing.

title: Guinea: Doumbouya orders mining companies to process local bauxite
summary: Guinea’s President Doumbouya ordered bauxite mining firms to submit proposals and timetables by end-May to build local alumina/aluminium refineries, threatening penalties for non-compliance. Guinea holds the world’s biggest bauxite reserves and supplies about half of China’s bauxite needs, making policy enforcement potentially supply-impacting for aluminium.

title: China Likely to Speed up Construction of Alumina Projects in Guinea after the Country Requires International Mining Companies to Build Alumina Refineries Locally_SMM
summary: Guinea’s interim government has asked international mining firms to provide production plans and construction schedules for alumina refineries from bauxite by end-May. The policy is intended to deepen the aluminium value chain and reduce bauxite exports, encouraging faster Chinese alumina project investment and potentially supporting aluminium market sentiment.

title: Alumina Prices in Henan Inched Higher amid Prolonged Supply-Demand Mismatch Caused by COVID-19 Outbreak_SMM
summary: SMM reports that COVID-19 controls reduced truck transport capacity, forcing alumina refineries to rely on slower train shipments and worsening supply-demand imbalance in north China. Aluminium smelters in northwest China increased stocking and turned to Henan suppliers, lifting Henan alumina prices by 10 yuan/mt versus last Friday.

title: The Information of RRR Cut and the Relief Impact of the Pandemic Boosted the Market and the SHFE Aluminium Operated High Before Noon [SMM Afternoon Comment on Aluminium Spot]_SMM
summary: Shanghai’s RRR cut and improving pandemic outlook boosted sentiment, pushing SHFE aluminium higher and keeping spot transactions stable above 21,800 yuan/mt, at times near 21,900. East China spot discounts stayed about 40 yuan/mt. Tight low-cost supply and declining Gongyi inventory supported firmer prices as holders maintained demand for holding.
