title: Condor Resources Inc.: Condor and Chakana Copper extend Soledad Project Option Agreement
summary: Condor Resources announced a binding agreement with Chakana Copper to extend the option period for its Soledad copper concessions in Peru to June 23, 2022. Chakana paid US$200,000 and will make additional payments of US$2.8m plus shares to complete transfer, with further scheduled consideration options.

title: Dow Technology recruits 2.2 billion yuan for Indonesia's high nickel matte project_SMM
summary: Guangdong Dow Technology plans to raise up to 2.2 billion yuan via convertible bonds to fund high-performance ternary precursor capacity and an Indonesia high-nickel matte/resource expansion project. The firm cites rising high-nickel battery demand and China’s limited nickel resources, implying improved nickel feedstock supply outlook.

title: Thieves steal hundreds of feet of copper wire in Swatara Township, Pa., police say
summary: Swatara Township police said thieves broke into Bitner Electric and stole about 540 feet of MCM THHN copper wire, 180 feet of 1/0 THHN copper wire, and 30 feet of 4/0 copper wire, along with a chainsaw. The incident is a localized copper theft with limited market-wide impact.

title: Trading metals is still a mess. It's not just about nickel
summary: CNN reports metals trading turmoil after Russia’s Ukraine invasion and sanctions, with energy-led scarcity breaking pricing. Nickel saw an LME price surge, trading suspension, cancellations, and subsequent volatility. It also notes record-low inventories for copper and aluminium, implying ongoing tightness and higher near-term price risk.

title: MMG's Las Bambas copper mine in Peru suspends operations following protest -SNMPE
summary: MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine in Peru suspended operations after local residents entered company property to protest, SNMPE’s Raul Jacob said. The mine is described as supplying about 2% of global copper, so the shutdown likely tightens near-term supply and weighs on copper prices.

title: Material Matters: Copper, Lithium, Gold, Russian Coal and Oil
summary: ANZ says copper remains supported by a tight supply situation that could worsen with potential renewed COVID disruptions affecting China’s port traffic, while anticipating demand resilience from electricity grid investment. It also notes Russia’s role as a major producer could pressure inventories lower. Overall, near-term copper price momentum looks positive.

title: Culpeo Minerals firms up 'compelling' targets at Quelon copper-gold project
summary: Culpeo Minerals completed induced polarisation surveys at its Quelon iron oxide-copper-gold project in Chile, identifying large geophysical anomalies and stating three zones are compelling drill targets. The company is pursuing earn-in stakes and plans a maiden drilling program. The update is exploratory and does not change near-term copper supply.

title: Minmetals Said Las Bambas Mine Will Be Unable to Sustain Copper Production_SMM
summary: Minmetals disclosed that Las Bambas will halt its ability to sustain copper output from April 20 (Peru time) for safety reasons amid ongoing community protests over social investment commitments. Authorities and stakeholders have not resolved the impasse, with a follow-up meeting expected in coming days.

title: LME copper, zinc climb on supply woes, China stimulus hopes
summary: LME copper rises 1.7% to a two-week peak as low inventories and China stimulus hopes coincide with supply worries. MMG’s Las Bambas mine plans to suspend operations after a local protest begins. Aluminium stabilizes near $3,214 per tonne on technical support, suggesting near-term resilience.

title: Tight Supply and Falling Demand to Keep Nickel Prices Rangebound _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel has continued rising but expects prices to stay rangebound. Scarce local supply, poor transportation, and tight nickel briquette and nickel sulphate keep premiums elevated. However, pessimism over downstream demand and weak liquidity/hedging on LME cap upside gains.

title: LME Aluminum Inventory Hit 17-Year Low, SHFE Aluminum Inventory Fell to Two-Month Low_SMM
summary: LME data show aluminum inventories fell again after a prior spike, with last week’s level reaching the lowest in 17 years. SHFE aluminum inventories also decreased 2.46% week-on-week to 299,855 mt, the lowest in two months. The inventory draw suggests tightening supply and price support for aluminum.

title: Import Market was Still Sluggish due to the Rising LME Copper and the Weakened Price Ratio_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums for warrant and B/L trades stayed flat but import market liquidity remained sluggish. Weak customs clearance and logistics efficiency, plus rising LME copper prices that worsened the price ratio, discouraged offers. Traders cited inability to transfer documents, limiting order pickup and sustaining wider losses for imports.

title: There was Shortage in Market Pure Nickel Supply, and the Futures Prices Rise Significantly as the Premium was Firm[SMM Afternoon Comment on Nickel]_SMM
summary: SMM reports a shortage of domestic pure nickel supply and temporarily suspends certain premium/discount quotes due to futures diverging from spot. Spot prices for Jinchuan and NORNICKEL nickel rose sharply, supported by reduced production and import losses. SHFE nickel futures increased for six straight days, aiming to reopen the import window.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Provides Schaft Creek Update
summary: Copper Fox provided an update on the Schaft Creek copper-gold-molybdenum-silver project, operated by Teck, including preparation for a planned 5,000m summer drill program and progress on geotechnical, metallurgical testing, environmental baseline work, and indigenous engagement. It is mainly a near-term development planning update.

title: African copper, cobalt logistics chain under pressure as truckers avoid DRC
summary: DRC border delays, truck shortages and congestion are making it far costlier and slower to move copper cathodes and raw materials to export ports (Durban, Dar es Salaam, Beira). With Kamoa-Kakula starting early and offering 30–50% higher trucking fees, producers face mounting logistics costs and potential delivery disruptions, supporting higher copper pricing.

title: Portugal: New contribution over disposable plastic and aluminium packages from meals ready to consume
summary: Portugal will introduce a contribution from 1 July 2022 on disposable plastic or multi-material food packages and in 2023 on packages made of aluminium or multi-material with aluminium. The charge is paid by producers/importers via a customs/e-DIC process and is meant to be passed to final consumers, potentially weighing on aluminium packaging demand.

title: Watchdog blasts London Metal Exchange over nickel trading debacle
summary: The IMF criticized the LME for cancelling trades during last month’s nickel “pickle” after Russia-Ukraine fears drove nickel to record highs. The cancellations limited losses for Tsingshan but removed gains for other counterparties, prompting investigations by UK regulators and calls to strengthen LME governance.

title: AuKing Mining raising $7.1m to lock-in ownership and advance Koongie Park copper-zinc project
summary: AuKing Mining raised $7.1m to fund drilling and exploration at the Koongie Park copper-zinc project in Western Australia, including buying Anglo Australian Resources’ remaining 25% stake. The funds will support the planned program, but the timeline is exploration-focused, implying limited immediate impact on copper prices.

title: NBS Released China March and Q1 Copper Semis Output_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s NBS reported copper semis output of 1.9 million mt in March (+4.6% YoY) and 4.83 million mt in Q1 (+6.8% YoY). Higher production from processors suggests stronger near-term copper consumption demand, which can be supportive for copper prices.

title: Import Losses Shrank after SHFE Nickel Rose for Six Consecutive Days, Loss-Making Nickel Salt Plants Curtailed Production  _SMM
summary: SHFE nickel rose for a sixth straight day, with refined nickel spot prices also climbing sharply. The report attributes gains to domestic smelter production reductions, declining pure nickel inventories, and weaker nickel salt plant output amid losses. Higher SHFE/LME spreads are expected to open the import window, though a pullback is possible if supply improves.

title: Inventory of Nickel Fell at LME and SHFE, SHFE Nickel Stocks down over 10%_SMM
summary: The article cites LME data showing nickel inventories declining sharply to about 72,600 mt, near a two-year low, after a mid-April peak. It also notes SHFE nickel stocks fell 11.96% week-on-week to 7,668 mt. Lower exchange inventories are generally supportive for nickel futures.

title: China Zijin invests in Xanadu to ink copper-gold resources in Mongolia
summary: Zijin Mining agreed to buy stakes in Xanadu Mines, including a path to a 45.9% interest in Mongolia’s Kharmagtai copper-gold mine via its subsidiary Khuiten Metals. The Kharmagtai resource includes sizable copper, but the transaction signals investment rather than immediate production, implying limited near-term copper price pressure.

title: LME copper edges higher as stimulus hopes offset firm dollar, growth woes
summary: London copper edged up as hopes for additional China stimulus offset a firm dollar and growth concerns. A suspension at Peru’s Las Bambas mine added a copper supply-tightness risk. Aluminium and nickel in LME and Shanghai were broadly softer, reflecting uneven sentiment tied to China lockdown-related demand worries.

title: IMF says LME governance needs strengthening after nickel fiasco
summary: The IMF urged strengthening London Metal Exchange governance after a nickel-market short squeeze last month. The event triggered a six-day suspension, a 250% price surge in under two days, and billions of dollars in cancelled trades linked to Chinese producer Tsingshan. The IMF cites governance lessons for commodity-market volatility.

title: China's March alumina exports to Russia soar as sanctions over Ukraine bite | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: China’s alumina exports to Russia rose more than 90x in March after sanctions over Ukraine reduced Russia’s traditional supply routes. Shipments to Russia reached 9,949 tonnes, while total alumina exports jumped 180% year-on-year. Australia’s alumina and aluminium-ore ban to Russia is cited as the driver.

title: China's Primary Aluminum Imports Fell by 55.1% year-on-year in March _SMM
summary: China’s primary aluminium imports fell 55.1% year-on-year in March to 39,433 mt, though they rose 115% month-on-month. Q1 imports totaled 96,551.5 mt, down 71% year-on-year. The shift in import flows could influence short-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: SHFE Aluminium Did Not Move, and the Spot Aluminium Ingot Transactions Continued to be Slightly Discounted [SMM Afternoon Comment on Aluminium Spot]_SMM
summary: SMM reports early-session SHFE aluminium plate trading around 21,800 yuan/mt with narrowed ranges. Spot ingot transactions in East China stayed slightly discounted, reflecting cautious longs and weaker holder pricing after declines. Demand improved modestly with downstream pandemic recovery, but upstream refined output resumed, adding supply pressure.

title: Alumina Prices FOB Western Australia declined_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports a deal for 30,000 mt of alumina sold at $371/mt FOB Western Australia, down $7/mt from the prior transaction. The shipment is scheduled for late May and the destination is undisclosed. The pricing drop suggests weaker near-term alumina market sentiment, a key input for aluminium smelting.

title: Aluminum Casting Market Size Worth $135.20 Billion By 2030: Grand View Research, Inc.
summary: Grand View Research says the global aluminum casting market should grow to $135.2B by 2030, citing rising demand for lightweight vehicles and equipment. It expects steady use of aluminum components, despite some impact from electrification. China’s scale in primary aluminum and manufacturing growth underpin demand for casting inputs.

title: SHFE Nickel Fell over 3%, Will Tight Supply and Downstream Production Cuts Drag down the Prices? _SMM
summary: SHFE nickel reversed after consecutive gains, dropping 3.04% as spot refined nickel prices also fell. Despite tight pure nickel supply, reduced downstream production from higher raw-material costs and sluggish demand are weighing on prices. The piece expects further weakness once the import window opens and supply improves.

title: Las Bambas: Peru copper mine halts operations amid protests
summary: MMG said it will suspend Las Bambas operations in southern Peru from Wednesday due to safety concerns amid local protests demanding higher financial contributions and accusing MMG of unmet compensation agreements. Las Bambas is a major copper producer (~2% of global supply), so the halt points to near-term supply losses.

title: Tight supply sends Rotterdam aluminium premium to record high
summary: Tight aluminium availability pushed Rotterdam duty-unpaid premiums to an all-time high near $500/t, alongside stable but elevated Midwest US premiums at record levels. LME warehouse stocks fell and energy costs remained high, while sanctions-fear around Russian supply supported demand for physical material.

title: SolGold says it can create one of the world's lowest-cost copper mines
summary: SolGold says its Cascabel copper project in northern Ecuador, supported by major shareholders BHP and Newcrest, could become one of the world’s lowest-cost and lowest-carbon copper mines. The feasibility study underpins a $2.7 billion development plan and notes potential gains if a second nearby deposit is successfully developed.

title: Hawaiian Airlines Partners with Jason Momoa's Water Company Mananalu, Featuring Infinitely Recyclable Aluminum Bottles
summary: Hawaiian Airlines will replace plastic water bottles on certain routes with Mananalu’s 16-ounce BPA-free aluminum bottles, aiming to remove about 142,000 plastic bottles annually from transpacific operations. The move increases demand for recycled aluminum packaging but offers limited, localized market impact.

title: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Reports First Quarter 2022
summary: Kaiser Aluminum reported Q1 2022 results with strong demand in general engineering and packaging and improving aerospace recovery, while automotive remained muted. Higher freight and inflationary costs were partially offset by contained-metal surcharges. It also cited lingering supply-chain issues affecting magnesium and timely metal supply at its Warrick facility.

title: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Q1 Profit Increases, Inline With Estimates
summary: Kaiser Aluminum reported Q1 profit of $8 million (EPS $0.51), up from $5 million a year earlier and matching analysts’ expectations (adjusted EPS $0.66). Revenue rose sharply to $949 million from $324 million. With results inline with estimates, the impact on near-term aluminium price expectations appears limited.

title: Alcoa Sinks as Aluminum Shipments Fall in Sign of Waning Demand
summary: The article headline says Alcoa’s aluminum shipments are declining, a sign that demand is waning. Falling shipments suggest reduced orders and weaker consumption for aluminum in the near term. This points to a looser demand outlook for the aluminium market, likely weighing on aluminium prices over the coming days.

title: Latin Metals Discovers High-Grade Copper Mineralization, Auq...
summary: Latin Metals reported positive soil sampling at its Auquis copper project in Peru, outlining a 3km x 2km area of anomalous high-grade copper (up to 2,300 ppm) with coincident molybdenum. The company plans additional rock-chip sampling and mapping, but no production or near-term supply impact is indicated.

title: Drilling is underway at the Hecla-Kilmer copper-gold breccia...
summary: VR Resources says drilling has started on its Hecla-Kilmer copper-gold breccia target in northern Ontario, with 4–6 holes planned and assay results expected by June/July. The company previously intersected “copper and gold locally,” but this update contains no new copper assay, production, or supply-impact information.

title: BHP's copper and nickel output hit by labour shortages
summary: BHP said labour shortages forced it to downgrade output at its Australian nickel business and its Chilean copper operations. The company’s iron ore division is still tracking its full-year target, but the specific nickel and copper production cuts point to near-term supply constraints that could weigh on copper and nickel prices.

title: BHP's copper and nickel output hit by labour shortages
summary: BHP said labour shortages have forced it to downgrade output from its Australian nickel division and its Chilean copper division, even as its iron ore operations remain on track. The update signals near-term supply constraints for nickel and copper, which can weigh on short-term price expectations over coming weeks.

title: Mining protests halt 20% of copper output in world's No. 2 producer Peru
summary: Mining protests in Peru are reportedly halting roughly 20% of output in the world’s No. 2 copper producing country. The disruption reduces near-term supply, tightening market availability and supporting higher copper prices over the coming days as traders price the production loss.

title: Peru declares state of emergency to restore copper production at Cuajone mine
summary: Peru will declare a state of emergency near Southern Copper’s Cuajone mine after protests halted roughly 20% of the country’s copper output. Peru, the world’s No. 2 copper producer, faces disruptions across major mines including Las Bambas and Antapaccay, raising short-term copper supply expectations.

title: BHP cuts copper output outlook over Chile protests, environmental concerns
summary: BHP reportedly cut its copper output outlook amid Chile protests and environmental concerns. The update suggests potential disruption or slower ramp-up at copper operations, lowering expected supply in the near term. Such developments can influence copper balances and prompt short-term price moves as traders reassess production expectations.

title: WBMS: Global Nickel Market Saw a Supply Deficit of 17,400 mt from January to February 2022_SMM
summary: WBMS reported that the global refined nickel market ran a supply deficit of 17,400 mt from January to February 2022, with apparent demand exceeding production. Refined nickel output totaled 447,600 mt versus 464,900 mt demand. Chinese and Indonesian smelter output increased, but demand rose faster.

title: Peru Declared A State of Emergency of Cuajone Copper Mine, China-Funded Mines Also Suspended the Production_SMM
summary: Peru declared a state of emergency around Southern Copper’s Cuajone mine after protests and water cutoffs disrupted output, while MMR suspended production at Las Bambas for safety. The article cites disruptions affecting about 20% of Peru’s copper production, a notable supply risk.

title: BHP Q3 Copper Production Down, Cuts FY22 Copper Production View; Stock Down
summary: BHP shares fell after the miner said Q3 copper output dropped 6% to 369.7 kt and it cut FY22 copper guidance to 1,570–1,620 kt from 1,590–1,760 kt, citing lower Escondida volumes. BHP also lowered nickel guidance to 80–85 kt due to COVID-19 labor constraints.

title: Novelis adds capacity to supply growing market for coffee capsules made of recycled aluminium
summary: Novelis will invest over $30 million in Germany to add a continuous annealing line at its Plettenberg-Ohle facility, doubling capacity for aluminium used in coffee capsules. The expansion targets growing demand for sustainable, high-recycled-content packaging and supports recycled aluminium supply from its Ohle and Nachterstedt operations.

title: China Unwrought Aluminium Alloy Imports Surged 50% YoY in Mar_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China imported 120,600 mt of unwrought aluminium alloy in March, up 54.5% YoY and 31.3% MoM. Customs data also shows strong Q1 growth. The report links expectations of aluminium supply shortage to a deepening overseas energy crisis, supporting LME aluminium and lifting ADC12 prices, with fewer new orders.

title: Anglo American Q1 Copper Equivalent Production Down; Diamond Production Climbs
summary: Anglo American said Q1 copper equivalent production fell 10% year on year, with copper output down 13% amid Covid-related absenteeism and high rainfall disrupting operations in South Africa and Brazil. Company guidance for copper remains unchanged, but the weaker recent production supports a bearish near-term supply outlook.

title: Antofagasta Q1 Copper Production Declines
summary: Antofagasta said Q1 copper production fell to 138,800 tonnes, down 24.2% year-on-year, mainly because drought reduced throughput at Los Pelambres and lower grades at Centinela Concentrates affected output. Full-year guidance remains unchanged, but the Q1 decline may pressure near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Aluminium Ingot Destocking in China Accelerated_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says China’s aluminium ingot social inventory fell to 1.02 million mt on April 21, down 42,000 mt week over week, helped by higher warehouse shipments and stronger demand in some regions. Poor transport temporarily lifted Wuxi inventories, while improved post-pandemic conditions boosted downstream restocking.

title: SMM Comments: Prices of SHFE Nickel Fell with Improved Spot Inquiries _SMM
summary: SMM reports that SHFE and spot nickel prices drifted lower as spot fundamentals and futures diverged. It suspended nickel premium/discount quotations but kept 1# nickel assessments normal. Spot Jinchuan and Norilsk nickel averages fell about 2,750 yuan/mt, while inquiries improved slightly but trades remained thin; prices may be hard to fall further without higher inventories.

title: Inventory of Aluminium Billets Declined 15,300 mt as of April 21_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s aluminium billet inventory fell to 119,100 mt as of Apr 21, down 11.37% from a week earlier, with declines across major regions. Logistics and pandemic controls continue to weigh on transport efficiency, while destocking and rigid/seasonal demand support expectations of further inventory reductions into Labour Day.

title: Gold State Finalizes Acquisition of the Panteria Copper-Gold Porphyry Project in Peru
summary: Gold State Resources finalized acquisition of the Panteria copper-gold porphyry project in Peru. Prior drilling reported long porphyry-related copper intervals (via copper-gold grades and copper-equivalent assumptions). The deal involves exploration-stage milestones and a net smelter return royalty, with no immediate production impact.

title: White Gold Corp. Identifies Significant Copper, Gold &
summary: White Gold Corp. reports broad, zoned soil anomalies at its Hayes and Pilot properties, including anomalous copper and a potential Cu-Mo porphyry core. The findings are based on geochemistry with no drilling yet, but they may slightly improve expectations for future copper supply in the region.

title: MMC Norilsk Nickel: UPDATE FOR HOLDERS OF AMERICAN DEPOSITARY RECEIPTS
summary: Norilsk Nickel notified ADR holders that Russian federal law will require termination of depositary receipt programs. From April 27, 2022, shares underlying ADRs will become non-voting and no dividends will be paid on those shares. ADR holders face restrictions on trading their ADRs for entitlements.

title: Analysis-Peru's Castillo hardens stance on mining protests as economy stumbles
summary: Peru’s President Pedro Castillo hardened his stance on mining protests, mobilizing the army as tensions with communities against mining firms escalated. Mining has been halted at Southern Copper’s Cuajone since late February, demanding compensation and profit sharing, raising near-term disruption risk for Peru’s copper supply.

title: Woman allegedly stole more than $150,000 of copper wiring from Rockdale site
summary: A North Texas woman was indicted for allegedly stealing over $150,000 worth of copper wiring from an abandoned Alcoa site in Rockdale. Authorities say deputies tracked a van leaving the property after wires were cut and stacked. The case is criminal in nature with localized supply impact.

title: Lunnon Metals unveils new nickel resource as it probes historical Foster mine
summary: Lunnon Metals announced a first-time resource estimate for its N75C surface prospect at the former Foster mine within Australia’s Kambalda nickel district: 412,700 tonnes at 2.3% nickel (about 9,500 tonnes contained nickel). The company is continuing historical core work and progressing dewatering/permitting for re-entry.

title: The Pandemic Sent the Operating Rates of Aluminum Processing Enterprises to a Two-Month Low This Week_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates for major aluminium processing enterprises fell 3.3 percentage points to 64.5% as East China’s pandemic situation suppressed demand. Downstream firms cut production, finished-product inventories rose, and transportation disruptions made it harder to source inputs and ship output. Rates could rebound if infections ease.

title: Nickel Prices Went Upward, and the Import Window Has not been Opened[SMM Morning Meeting] _SMM
summary: SMM says nickel prices have trended upward but imports remain unprofitable and tight supply persists due to losses and production reductions by refined nickel enterprises. Demand is mixed—transactions are weak—yet nickel salt raw material costs rose, causing losses and shutdowns. Without clear inventory build, nickel is hard to fall.

title: Will Nickel Prices Extend Rally amid Falling Supply and Demand? _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel rebounded after two down days, rising over 2% intraday and closing up 1.64%. It attributes strength to falling pure nickel supply from reduced domestic refined output, losses and output cuts at nickel salt factories, and supportive high-grade NPI pricing amid low inventories. Nickel likely won’t drop soon.

title: LME copper set for third weekly fall on China's COVID woes
summary: LME copper is on track for a third weekly decline as China’s COVID lockdowns cloud demand, while LME-approved inventories have risen to the highest since last October. Rising inventories and a stronger U.S. dollar add pressure. Limited support comes from hopes of Chinese stimulus and supply disruptions, but overall bias remains down.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports up 90,000 wmt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose by 90,000 wmt to 5.664 million wmt as of Apr 22, with total Ni content around 1,000 mt. Seven major ports inventory also increased week-on-week. Supply easing from southern Philippines and weak downstream demand prevented further inventory declines, weighing on nickel sentiment.

title: Antofagasta revises Chilean copper project expansion cost to $2.2bn
summary: Antofagasta raised capex for its Chile Los Pelambres expansion by $900m to $2.2bn, citing revised Covid-19 costs, general inflation (wages, labor incentives, logistics), and contingency. The company said delivery schedules are unchanged and copper output guidance remains, but higher costs can support near-term copper pricing expectations.

title: Proposal to launch bauxite cif China price assessment, discontinue fob bauxite prices
summary: Fastmarkets proposes launching a monthly bauxite CIF China price assessment (from accepted origins including Guinea, Australia, Indonesia, and Brazil) and discontinuing existing FOB bauxite assessments for Guinea and Brazil, subject to market feedback. The change is methodological/benchmarking, not an explicit physical market shock.

title: Nickel Inventory in Shanghai Bonded Zone Remained almost Unchanged this Week_SMM
summary: SMM reports volatile LME nickel and rising SHFE nickel, despite imports remaining at losses. Shanghai bonded nickel inventory was little changed at 8,200 mt, with nickel briquettes and plates flat. COVID-19 slowed operations, LME liquidity remains weak, but SHFE’s high prices reflect tight Chinese supply; profitable imports may follow if prices persist.

title: Alcoa draws downgrade from Citi on aluminum prices
summary: Citigroup downgraded Alcoa to neutral from buy, citing aluminium price assumptions (around $2,800 mid-spot versus a long-term $2,500) and a more balanced near-term risk-reward after a large stock rally. The move reflects expectations for aluminium rather than a clear new supply or demand shock.

title: ArcWest Exploration Inc.: ArcWest Provides an Exploration Update for its Oxide Peak Copper-Gold Project, Toodoggone District, B.C.
summary: ArcWest Exploration provided an exploration update for its Oxide Peak Cu-Au project, including planned 2022 drilling of an untested porphyry target and prior geophysical/geochemical results indicating copper anomalies. The release is company/project specific with no immediate changes to mine output, inventories, or pricing mechanisms for copper, nickel, or aluminium.

title: Open consultation on nickel sulfate ex-works mainland China going through IOSCO audit
summary: Fastmarkets has opened an IOSCO audit/consultation on its nickel sulfate ex-works mainland China price assessment (MB-NI-0244). The review updates price specifications and may shift assessment timing from within seven days to within 30 days, with weekly publication. The move is methodology-focused rather than a market-balance shock.

title: Prolonged Peru mine protest ends after dispatch of soldiers
summary: Peru lifted an indigenous protest against Southern Copper’s Cuajone copper mine after deploying soldiers. The shutdown lasted 52 days and caused large export and tax losses. Southern Copper says installations, including a rail line, were damaged by residents, and plans to restart once repairs are completed.

title: The state enterprise "Nebitmaş" is allowed to gradually conclude contracts with JSC "Tajik Aluminum Company"
summary: Turkmenistan’s President authorized the state enterprise Nebitmaş to gradually sign contracts with TALCO for purchases of 7,000 tons of drawn aluminum and 3,000 tons of cast aluminum billets. The deal is aimed at building processing capacity and supplying domestic markets with import-substituting aluminum products, likely supporting aluminium demand expectations.

title: Chile recommends denying extension for Anglo American copper mine
summary: Chile’s environmental regulator has recommended denying an extension permit for Anglo American’s Los Bronces copper project, which is linked to a $3.3 billion investment plan. The decision could delay or limit project expansion, increasing concerns about future copper supply and weighing on copper price expectations in the coming weeks.

title: Bahrain 'stable' as oil, aluminium prices keep current account robust: Moody | THE DAILY TRIBUNE
summary: Moody’s revised Bahrain’s outlook to stable, citing higher oil prices and a rebound in aluminium prices that help keep the current account robust. Aluminium accounts for more than 25% of Bahrain’s merchandise exports (2020). The improved external balance supports stronger reserves and reduced financing pressure.

title: Alcoa shares plunge as aluminum shipments fall
summary: Alcoa shares fell after the company reported lower quarterly sales as prolonged supply-chain disruptions reduced aluminum shipments. The firm cited higher inventories caused by shortages of train cars and vessels, particularly in North America, and noted that Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has worsened the crisis, affecting demand.

title: MSP investigating theft of copper wiring from an agricultural pivot in St. Joseph County
summary: Michigan State Police are investigating reports of copper wiring theft from an agricultural irrigation pivot in St. Joseph County, Michigan. Several feet of copper were cut from pivot towers between November 2021 and April 15, causing damage. The incident is local and unlikely to affect broader copper pricing.

title: Expectations for Consumption Recovery and Falling Social Inventories Will Support Aluminium Prices at Highs_SMM
summary: SMM expects short-term aluminium prices to hold near highs, citing improving downstream consumption, falling social inventories from limited ingot transportation to consumption areas, and active restocking by downstream producers. It also notes overseas smelters are unlikely to resume due to high energy prices, supporting aluminium supply balance despite some operating-rate softness.

title: Overseas Alumina Prices Continued to Fall, While Domestic Prices Inched Higher amid Improved Trades _SMM
summary: SMM says China’s alumina prices edged up domestically, but overseas alumina FOB Western Australia fell to $371/mt as previously Russia-bound material entered the spot market. The China–overseas premium shrank sharply, and about 180,000 mt already entered China; future import-window reopening could add more supply and pressure prices.

title: Aluminium Costs Likely to Increase Due to Potential Rise in Alumina and Prebaked Anode Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports that alumina prices edged up while auxiliary materials were stable, and smelter full costs rose to 18,255 yuan/mt. Despite some relief from falling thermal coal, the article warns aluminium costs are unlikely to decline due to potential increases in alumina and anode prices, plus higher freight rates.

title: Base metals drop on China lockdown, prospects of bigger Fed hikes
summary: Industrial metals fell as China’s COVID-19 lockdown restrictions raised fears of weaker demand and economic growth. Copper hit its lowest level in over a month, while expectations for larger Fed rate hikes supported a stronger dollar, pressuring dollar-priced metals. Additional headlines include a negative outlook for copper projects and Peru mine restart.

title: China's Bauxite Imports Exceeded 10 Million mt Again in March. Will Record High Imports from Guinea Sustain? _SMM
summary: China imported 11.7 million mt of bauxite in March, a record and mostly from Guinea, as Indonesia’s export ban uncertainty and rainy-season disruptions keep Indonesian supply unstable. Chinese alumina refineries shifted toward Guinean ore to maintain production and stockpiles, supporting more stable alumina supply and potentially aluminium output.

title: Increase in Spot Copper Concentrate TCs was Hindered by the Overseas Supply_SMM
summary: SMM reports higher imported copper concentrate prices and TCs, with trading concentrated on May–June shipments. Protests force Las Bambas to stop production from April 20, while Peru considers a state of emergency near Cuajone; Chile is also reshaping mining rules. The market worries about long-run concentrate supply despite short-term easing.

title: Scrap iron dealers urge public to help end copper theft
summary: Trinidad and Tobago scrap dealers urge the public and authorities to curb copper wire theft after viral incidents. The association says theft harms livelihoods and has been linked to fires and past deaths. It calls for faster regulation, arrests, and refusing to buy stolen items, aiming to reduce theft-driven scrap supply.

title: Review of Changes in Domestic Aluminium Production Capacity in the First Quarter and Prospect for the Second Quarter [SMM Analysis]_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s aluminium operating capacity climbed in Q1 with higher operating rates and resumption of previously shut plants, and expects further capacity growth in Q2 to about 40.94 million mt. It also cites capacity replacements reducing net output less than planned, implying supply support and potential near-term price pressure.

title: Yunnan's Aluminium Output Surged 43.6% MoM in March _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Yunnan Statistics Bureau data cited by SMM show aluminium output rose to 377,000 mt in March, up 43.6% month-on-month. By end-March, around 80% of aluminium capacity in the province had been released, implying increased near-term supply and potential pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 12,400 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM says Chinese copper inventories fell 12,400 mt to 114,900 mt over the weekend, with declines across Shanghai, Guangdong, Jiangsu and others. The drawdown is attributed to downstream restocking after sharp price drops and improving inter-provincial logistics. SMM expects inventories to keep declining into the week before May Day.

title: Export Outlook for Chinese  Aluminum Plate/Sheet and Strip Enterprises Is Pessimistic Following Sharp Increase in March_SMM
summary: China’s aluminum plate/sheet and strip exports rose in March, but companies report April export orders have slumped month-on-month. They attribute weaker shipments partly to pandemic disruptions and also to improving overseas capacity in Western countries as COVID-19 restrictions ease, reducing dependence on Chinese supply.

title: Will SHFE Nickel Extend Decline after More than 6% Drop?_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SHFE nickel fell 6.23% to 224,000 yuan/mt. The piece links the move to limited imported nickel inflows and low refined smelter operating rates tightening supply, while high prices and pandemic conditions reduced downstream demand, with alloy/battery/electroplating output cut. Net expectation: high-level fluctuation.

title: NORNICKEL ANNOUNCES CONSOLIDATED PRODUCTION RESULTS FOR 1Q 2022
summary: Norilsk Nickel reported preliminary 1Q22 production: consolidated nickel output rose 10% y/y to 52kt, driven by recovery of Oktyabrsky and Taimyrsky mines and ramp-up of the Norilsk Concentrator. Copper production stayed roughly unchanged at 91kt, with logistics and geopolitical issues not disrupting operations.

title: Bears tip-toe back into copper market as demand fears grow: Andy Home
summary: Copper fell on Monday, dropping below $10,000/t on the back of demand fears. Funds increased bearish CME copper bets, while China’s lockdowns and weaker PMI readings signaled slowing manufacturing. Supply issues remain, but attention is shifting toward weaker near-term consumption, driving bearish sentiment.

title: Zambia 'very close' to picking investor for Mopani copper mine - president
summary: Zambia’s president said the government is very close to selecting a private investor for Mopani Copper Mines to increase output, following the state’s purchase of the mine from Glencore and ongoing need for investment. He also denied plans to return KCM to Vedanta.

title: Vedanta Aluminium intensifies campaign against malaria at Lanjigarh
summary: Vedanta Aluminium’s Lanjigarh unit in Odisha runs a week-long malaria awareness and prevention campaign for local communities, citing reduced malaria cases from prior efforts. The piece mainly covers health outreach and surveillance/testing improvements, with only background details on Vedanta’s alumina refinery and aluminium smelting operations.

title: Atacama Copper Announces Commencement of a Trenching Program...
summary: Atacama Copper began a four-week trenching and channel-sampling program at its El Cofre copper-gold project in Chile. Approximately 3,000 meters of trenching will follow up geochemical and mapping targets, with initial XRF results expected in May 2022 and lab assays in June 2022.

title: Russia's Nornickel Q1 nickel output up, palladium down
summary: Nornickel said Q1 nickel production rose 10% year-on-year to 51,534 tonnes after the recovery of its two mines from 2021 flooding. Copper output was stable at 91,414 tonnes. Despite Western sanctions-related logistics challenges, the company kept its 2022 nickel forecast unchanged, citing uninterrupted operations.

title: Russia's Norilsk Nickel Keeps Pumping Out Metal
summary: The piece focuses on Russia’s Norilsk Nickel, saying it continues to pump out metal. Persistent output from a major nickel producer can reduce fears of near-term supply disruption and ease market tightness expectations, which is generally supportive for inventories and mildly bearish for nickel prices in the short term.

title: Amid China's funding to Myanmar Junta's resistance groups, call for halting Chinese copper mines
summary: Resistance groups tied to Myanmar’s civil disobedience movement warn Chinese-run copper mines in Salingyi to halt operations by May 5. The timing and potential for mine disruption raise supply risk for copper, though it is unclear if the call will be implemented immediately.

title: Russia's Norilsk Nickel Keeps Pumping Out Metal
summary: The piece headlines that Russia’s Norilsk Nickel is “keeping” production levels steady, continuing to pump out nickel metal. Continuous supply from a major producer tends to add availability to the market and can pressure nickel prices in the near term, absent signs of disruption or demand acceleration.

title: China Becomes Driving Force In Hot Aluminium Market
summary: Europe’s aluminium semis market is described as extremely tight due to tariffs and sanctions limiting Russian deliveries, with further EU restrictions (including possible import/payments limits) under consideration. At the same time, China is expanding semi-finished output and improving primary smelting, making it the key swing supplier. Premiums remain high.

title: Working class struggles explode in Peru
summary: Weeks of Peru-wide protests over fuel and fertilizer costs spread to mining communities. The Chinese-owned Las Bambas copper project was disrupted after community members invaded the site, prompting Las Bambas to stop producing copper. The government deployed the army, worsening uncertainty over Peru’s copper output near term.

title: LME copper rebounds on China stimulus hopes, dollar retreat
summary: London copper rebounded 1.4% after hitting a more-than-two-month low, driven by hopes for additional China economic stimulus and a slight retreat in the U.S. dollar. The piece also notes lingering COVID lockdown worries and broader macro uncertainty, with aluminium and nickel referenced via markets and related company updates.

title: CME Group to Launch an Aluminum Option Contract on May 23
summary: CME Group said it will launch a COMEX-listed aluminum option contract on May 23, pending regulatory approval. The exchange highlighted higher aluminum futures trading volumes and positioned the new contract as additional risk-management and hedging flexibility. The announcement is about derivatives access, not immediate changes to aluminum fundamentals.

title: Metallic Minerals Corp.: Metallic Minerals Defines 985 Million Pounds of Copper Equivalent in Inaugural NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate for the La Plata Project in Colorado, USA
summary: Metallic Minerals reported an inaugural NI 43-101 inferred resource at its La Plata project, centered on the Allard copper-silver porphyry deposit. The estimate includes 115.7 Mt at 0.39% copper equivalent (0.35% Cu, 4.02 g/t Ag) and plans for follow-up drilling, but no production or inventory change.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Intercept of 34 Meters of 1.35% Copper from the Cinabrio Norte Target at Its Punitaqui Copper Mine in Chile
summary: Battery Mineral Resources said it intercepted 34 meters of 1.35% copper from the Cinabrio Norte target at its Punitaqui copper mine in Chile. The result is an exploration success that modestly improves expectations for future copper resources, offering limited near-term bullish sentiment for copper prices.

title: Global copper market drivers push and pull
summary: The article reviews copper market drivers: a still-large but narrowing refined deficit, Chinese demand slowing tied to real estate weakness, European consumption pressure from high energy costs, and uncertainty from Russia-related sanctions and financing. It also notes limited copper-aluminium substitution, leaving copper volatility high but directionally mixed.

title: Tesla's Elon Musk meets with delegation from Indonesia at Giga Texas to discuss potential nickel deal
summary: Elon Musk met an Indonesian delegation at Tesla’s Gigafactory Texas to discuss potential cooperation on Indonesia’s nickel deposits for Tesla battery supply and processing. Officials said the goal is to involve nickel in ESG-aligned battery-cell production, which could lift near-term expectations for nickel demand.

title: Peru loses more than US$110mn in copper exports due to illegal occupation of Las Bambas
summary: Peru is losing over US$110mn in copper export value due to an illegal occupation affecting the Las Bambas operation. The disruption limits copper shipments from the mine, reducing near-term export flows from one of the country’s key producers and likely worsening short-term supply expectations.

title: The Northern Miner Podcast – episode 288: A brief history of aluminum and Alcoa conference call highlights, ft CEO Roy Harvey and CFO Bill Oplinger
summary: This podcast episode reviews Alcoa’s earnings call and the company’s weaker stock reaction. Speakers cited rising energy costs, disruptions tied to leaving Russia, shipping challenges, and environmental initiatives toward zero-carbon smelters. The operational and cost pressures discussed are likely to weigh on near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Copper rebounds as China vows additional support for economy
summary: Copper is reported to be rebounding as China vows additional support for its economy. The implication is improved near-term economic activity and demand expectations for industrial metals, which tends to lift sentiment and prices for copper, the benchmark industrial metal, over coming days.

title: Insight - Bears tiptoe back into copper market
summary: Copper prices were under pressure Monday, with LME three-month copper slipping below $10,000 per tonne for the first time in a month. After weeks of stalled trade—too high for buyers and too tight for sellers to short—bears are moving back in, indicating renewed bearish momentum.

title: LME copper eases on China's COVID lockdowns, Fed rate-hike bets
summary: LME copper fell as concerns grew that COVID lockdowns in top consumer China will curb demand, while expectations for large U.S. rate hikes lifted the dollar to multi-year highs. The stronger dollar increased costs for non-dollar buyers. China stimulus hopes limited declines. Global risk-off also pressured industrial metals.

title: Aluminum Holds Near Three-Month Low on China Demand Concerns
summary: Aluminum prices are reported to be holding near a three-month low as concerns about China’s demand weigh on market sentiment. The implication is softer near-term consumption from China, which can pressure aluminium prices over the coming days as traders reassess demand outlook.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Kept Rising amid Improved Price Ratio_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says Yangshan copper premiums under warrants rose to $20–45/mt, with averages up $8.5/mt versus the previous day. Quotes under B/L for May also increased. The improved price ratio supported import transactions, while traders held firm due to high US-dollar pledge costs and related financing frictions.

title: SHFE Nickel Rebounded Slightly with Weak Inquires and Transactions_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel rebounded slightly and spot nickel prices rose. Jinchuan nickel averaged 231,550 yuan/mt (+4,050 yuan/mt) and Nornickel averaged 227,650 yuan/mt (+5,950 yuan/mt). Nickel briquette also increased. The rise was linked to late trading recovery and higher Shanghai premiums, though inquiries and transactions were weaker.

title: SHFE Nickel Remained High, and Spot Transactions Improved Slightly, but the Overall Supply and Demand Remained Weak [SMM Morning Meeting]_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel remained high as tight domestic pure nickel supply persisted, with poor customs clearance, low operating rates, and high spot premiums. NPI and nickel sulphate supplies were also described as tight. Although pandemic-related demand weakened and stainless transactions were poor, SHFE nickel is expected to stay elevated.

title: SHFE Nickel to Fluctuate at Highs after Gaining More than 3% amid Tight Supply_SMM
summary: SHFE nickel rebounded more than 3% after a brief slump, with SMM 1# refined nickel spot prices averaging 225,600 yuan/mt. Tight domestic refined nickel supply persists, smelter operating rates remain weak, NPI imports are short, and nickel sulphate supply is constrained by producer losses. Demand is mixed amid pandemic weakness, but tight supply supports prices at highs.

title: Teck Resources profit jumps five-fold as copper, coal prices surge
summary: Teck Resources reported profits jumping five-fold, attributing the increase to higher copper and coal prices. The headline implies copper prices are firming, which can support short-term sentiment and expectations for further strength in copper markets over the coming days.

title: Copper edges higher buoyed by China stimulus hopes
summary: Industrial metals rose as hopes for further Chinese stimulus outweighed COVID-related demand worries and fears from potential aggressive U.S. rate hikes. LME three-month copper edged up and LME aluminium gained. Nickel also rose, with investors weighing China’s monetary support amid lockdown impacts on industrial activity.

title: Golden Rim and Teck sign option agreement for porphyry copper project
summary: Golden Rim Resources signed an option and joint venture agreement with Teck Chile to explore the Loreto porphyry copper project in northern Chile. Teck may earn up to 75% via cash payments and US$17m exploration spending. The deal targets potential deeper copper mineralization, but is not a production change.

title: Chilean watchdog starts sanction process against Glencore's copper mine
summary: Chile’s SMA has launched a sanctions process against Glencore’s Lomas Bayas copper mine for failing to meet required water and flora/fauna monitoring standards, including missing observation-well records and improper aquifer measurement records. The charges could pressure operations or raise compliance costs in the near term. The mine produced 64,300t copper last year.

title: SHFE Aluminium Rallied, but Market Confidence Remained Fragile _SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium rebounded after two days of declines, rising 0.51% to 20,765 yuan/mt. Moves were mainly driven by macro sentiment, including a rising US dollar that pressured base metals. While smelter output resumed and social inventories fell, the article expects weak fluctuations because consumption recovery lags.

title: Transactions of Aluminium Scrap this Week were Poor amid Dropping Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices fell sharply over Apr 25-27, reaching around 20,730 yuan/mt. Falling prices suppressed trader shipments and, with weaker downstream alloy consumption, reduced aluminium scrap trading volumes. Even as transport pressure eased in some areas, scrap demand is expected to stay weak due to poor demand and long settlement periods.

title: Six Aluminium Smelters in Guangxi Were Not Subject to Tiered Electricity Prices in 2021_SMM
summary: Guangxi’s DRC issued guidance on tiered electricity prices for aluminium smelters. It said six named smelters in 2021 were not subject to tiered rates because their average electricity use in aluminium liquid production stayed below 13,700 kWh per metric ton, implying their power cost structure was unchanged.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Announces Start of Second Phase Drill Program at Lappvattnet High-Grade Nickel Project
summary: Gungnir Resources announced the start of a second-phase drill program (about 4,000 metres) at its Lappvattnet high-grade nickel project in Sweden. Drilling aims to expand and upgrade the existing nickel resource and test an additional EM conductor target, using results from phase one drilling.

title: GNRI weighs sale of Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana
summary: GNRI is exploring a sale of its Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana, which produces about 60,000–65,000 tonnes of copper annually. The reported possible deal value (~$1.5bn) is uncertain and no operational changes are announced, limiting immediate impact on near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Can You Invest in Nickel? 7 Stocks to Consider.
summary: The piece promotes nickel investing, highlighting the recent surge in nickel futures on the LME and linking upside to potential EV battery demand growth. It also notes supply risks from rapid Indonesian production expansion that could pressure prices. Overall, the narrative implies bullish near-term expectations for nickel despite volatility.

title: Callinex Commences Drilling to Define High-Grade Copper Rainbow Deposit and Test Priority Targets in the Flin Flon Mining District of Manitoba
summary: Callinex began a 20,000-meter drilling program at its Pine Bay Project in Manitoba, focusing on infill and step-out drilling to define the high-grade Rainbow copper deposit ahead of a 43-101 resource estimate. A second rig will test geophysical targets along the district trend for additional mineralized zones.

title: GNRI exploring sale of Khoemacau copper-silver project in Botswana
summary: GNRI is exploring options, including a possible sale, of its Khoemacau copper-silver mine in Botswana. Bloomberg reports advisers are identifying potential suitors, valuing the asset at nearly $1.5bn. While buyers may expand copper portfolios, no final decisions or operational changes are indicated.

title: Proactive news headlines including Fabled Copper, Avalon
summary: Proactive lists investor-focused headlines including Fabled Copper reporting an airborne survey identified new anomalies at its Muskwa copper project in British Columbia, and Quebec Nickel mobilizing a second drill rig at its Ducros property after VTEM data revealed new targets. Other items are unrelated to industrial metals.

title: Teck Resources reports record first-quarter profit; Chile copper mine nearly finished
summary: Teck reported record first-quarter profit and higher copper revenue, noting that its QB2 copper mine in Chile is over 80% complete. Management expects first copper from Line One in Q4, subject to no further COVID disruptions, and frames 2022 as transformational for copper production and cash generation.

title: Peru police enter Las Bambas copper mine to evict protest camp -sources
summary: Peruvian police evicted indigenous protesters from MMG’s Las Bambas open-pit copper mine after the camp led the company to suspend operations. MMG said production remains suspended for safety reasons and restart timing is unclear. The stoppage at a ~2% global supply mine may tighten copper supply expectations.

title: SMM to Resume the Quotations for Premiums and Discounts of 1# Jinchuan Nickel and 1# Imported Nickel _SMM
summary: SMM suspended quotations for premiums and discounts of 1# Jinchuan nickel and 1# imported nickel from Mar 25, 2022 due to extreme LME nickel volatility and weak guidance for spot pricing. With SHFE nickel stabilizing and manufacturers requesting resumption, SMM will resume from Apr 28, 2022.

title: European Union: Rules for Batteries Should Cover Bauxite, Copper, Iron
summary: The EU’s proposed batteries regulation would require battery makers and importers to source bauxite (linked to aluminium) and copper responsibly, if included in the final list of regulated raw materials. A coalition argues the rules should cover bauxite, copper, and iron. Negotiations are ongoing with differing positions in EU institutions.

title: European Union: Rules for Batteries Should Cover Bauxite, Copper, Iron
summary: An EU batteries regulation proposal would require battery importers and manufacturers to ensure responsible sourcing of key raw materials used in batteries. A coalition argues the final list should include bauxite (for aluminum) and copper, alongside iron, citing human-rights and environmental risks in mining and refining.

title: INSG: Global Demand for Nickel will Rise to 3.02 Million mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: INSG forecasts global nickel demand to rise to 3.02 million mt in 2022 from 2.78 million mt in 2021, while production increases to 3.08 million mt from 2.61 million mt. The market is expected to move from a 168,000 mt deficit in 2021 to a 67,000 mt surplus in 2022.

title: Glencore cuts output guidance for copper, zinc, cobalt
summary: Glencore has reduced its output guidance, according to the headline, covering copper (and also zinc and cobalt). A lower near-term production outlook for copper suggests reduced supply availability, which can tighten market balance and provide upward price pressure over the following days to weeks.

title: Glencore Q1 Own Sourced Copper Production Down 14%
summary: Glencore reported Q1 own-sourced copper production of 257,800 tonnes, down 14% versus Q1 2021, citing temporary geotechnical constraints at Katanga and other changes. Nickel output rose 22% to 30,700 tonnes mainly from Koniambo. The mixed supply signals imply limited net near-term price pressure.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventory Declined 11,600 mt _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Shanghai-area aluminium billet social inventories at 105,900 mt on Apr 28, down 9.88% from a week earlier. Inventory fell across most major regions as downstream producers restocked ahead of the Labour Day holiday, though sluggish demand in Foshan slowed the decline. Stocks are expected to drop further after the holiday.

title: CRISIL Research: Aluminium prices could average 25% higher on-year
summary: CRISIL Research forecasts aluminium prices to average about 25% higher year-on-year, linked to LME contract pricing. Despite recent declines from conflict-era highs, the report expects a supply deficit in 2022 supported by extended cuts and robust demand, with demand and export dynamics limiting downside.

title: Protesters tear gassed at copper mine in Peru
summary: Protesters were tear-gassed at a copper mine in Peru, signaling unrest at the operation. Such disruptions can hinder production and exports in the near term, reducing supply visibility and supporting expectations for higher copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Osisko Metals Announces Maiden Resource at Gaspé Copper - Inferred Resource of 456Mt Grading 0.31% Copper
summary: Osisko Metals said it has announced its maiden resource at the Gaspé copper project: an inferred resource of 456 Mt grading 0.31% copper. While not immediate production, the update can strengthen expectations for future copper supply, supporting bullish sentiment toward copper-linked markets.

title: American Resources Corporation Secures Worldwide Rights to New Provisional Patent for Producing Battery-Grade Lithium, Cobalt and Nickel
summary: American Resources secured worldwide rights to a provisional patent from Purdue University for multi-mode chromatography to isolate and purify battery-grade lithium, cobalt and nickel (plus manganese) from various feedstocks including end-of-life batteries. The firm highlights high purity, yields, low energy and costs, and plans for a new production train.

title: Los Andes Copper Ltd.: Los Andes Copper Announces Notice of Planned Payment of US$ 5,000,0000 to the Company Under the 2020 Royalty Agreement
summary: Los Andes Copper Ltd. says RCF has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its 2% NSR royalty on the Vizcachitas copper project in Chile. If the sale closes, RCF will pay Los Andes a contingent US$5 million under the 2020 royalty agreement, subject to fundraising and closing conditions.

title: Aluminium prices likely to come under pressure on excess supplies
summary: The article says aluminium prices rose to ₹300/kg in March but are likely to ease in the second half of the fiscal due to excess supply. It forecasts average domestic prices around ₹225–235/kg and links these to three-month LME contracts, where March’s average was $3,537/tonne.

title: Large consignment of stolen copper cables found in Devland scrapyard
summary: City Power said police recovered stolen copper cables from a scrapyard in Devland near Soweto and plans to intensify raids on scrapyards to curb cable theft. City Power and other utilities joined enforcement actions, citing reduced lost revenue and public inconvenience from stolen copper cables.

title: CME to launch options contract on aluminium physical futures
summary: CME says it will launch options on aluminium physical futures after successful physical trades in March and April. It cites record aluminium futures volumes and rising client use, positioning CME as an alternative to the LME. The move supports aluminium hedging and liquidity, potentially providing modest near-term upside sentiment.

title: Century Aluminum Company Reports First Quarter 2022
summary: Century Aluminum reported Q1 2022 results highlighting higher shipments and net sales driven by higher LME aluminum prices. It cited a global ~1 million tonne aluminum supply deficit and the lowest LME inventory levels since 2005, plus restart projects at Mt. Holly and Hawesville, supporting tightening sentiment for aluminum.

title: Century Aluminum Co Q1 Earnings Summary
summary: Century Aluminum Co reported a sharp Q1 improvement, with earnings rising to $16.6 million from a loss a year earlier and revenue increasing to $753.6 million. Adjusted earnings were $60.7 million ($0.59 per share). The update can affect near-term sentiment on aluminium producers.

title: Vale Takes Hit From Nickel Hedging Amid Record Price Spike
summary: Vale reported pressure from nickel hedging during a record nickel price spike, per the article headline. The framing implies nickel prices are rising rapidly and could stay supported by current market conditions, which may influence short-term trading sentiment for nickel.

title: Century Aluminum Company Reports First Quarter 2022 Results
summary: Century Aluminum reported Q1 2022 results, highlighting stronger shipments and higher net sales driven by higher LME aluminium prices. The company emphasized a global ~1 million tonne aluminum supply deficit and record-low LME inventories, suggesting tight supply conditions and supportive near-term pricing for aluminium.

title: SMM Forecast for Short-Term Alumina Price Outlook_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports alumina prices have been flat, with spot buying weak ahead of the Labour Day holiday. Pandemic-related logistics disruptions tightened supply and raised bauxite/auxiliary material and refinery costs. However, new capacity release and a potentially reopening import window for ~150,000 mt imported alumina are bearish. Cost support limits downside.

title: Logistics Problems Still Hinder the Production of Copper Processing Enterprises_SMM
summary: SMM says pandemic control and logistics problems are still disrupting copper processing enterprises, reducing return rates, pressuring sales and funds, and extending holiday downtime. Terminal demand is weakening and producers hold low raw material inventory. The outlook depends on May improvement, but traditional power grid, real estate, and appliances remain sluggish.

title: SMM Survey of Copper Cathode Rod Makers _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports cathode rod makers are still affected by pandemic-linked logistics problems, with Zhejiang producers short of raw materials and constrained production. Downstream demand is weak, new orders have declined, and firms have barely restocked ahead of Labour Day. More producers are expected to close than in previous years, extending the holiday break.

title: SMM Survey of Copper Wire and Cable Producers _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM survey says COVID outbreaks in some regions have left copper wire and cable producers with finished-product inventory backlogs and under financial stress, prompting lower output and longer Labour Day holidays. Demand also weakened as pandemic controls reduced end-user operating rates and slowed State Grid/China Southern Power Grid ordering.

title: Las Bambas Copper Mine Enters State of Emergency as Government Expels Protesters_SMM
summary: Peru expelled protesters from the Las Bambas copper mine after a two-week production halt, deploying hundreds of police and tear gas amid clashes. The government declared a 30-day emergency, temporarily suspending free assembly. Las Bambas accounts for nearly 400,000 mt/year capacity and has suffered shipment losses from road protests.

title: Huayou Cobalt to Cooperate with Vale Indonesia to Expand Production of Nickel-Cobalt Hydroxide_SMM
summary: Huayou Cobalt said it signed a framework agreement with PT Vale Indonesia to develop an HPAL project using limonite from Vale’s Pomalaa mine. Huayou will use its hydrometallurgy to produce nickel-cobalt hydroxide (MHP) with planned annual capacity up to 120,000 mt in nickel content, implying higher nickel supply expectations.

title: Sumitomo Metal Mining Withdraws from Indonesia Nickel Project, which May Exacerbate Battery-Grade Nickel Supply Tightness _SMM
summary: Sumitomo Metal Mining exited its planned HPAL nickel project with PT Vale Indonesia over disagreements on construction timelines and costs. The change may delay the project and worsen supply risks for already tight battery-grade nickel. The piece notes HPAL is key to expanding battery-grade supply, with capacity growth expected later this decade.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports up 213,000 wmt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported Chinese nickel ore inventories at ports rose 213,000 wmt to 5.877 million wmt as shipments from the Philippines increased after the rainy season. Transport issues from the pandemic and weaker NPI demand slowed consumption. With sufficient supply expected, port inventories are projected to keep rising in the short term.

title: Aluminium production industry
summary: The piece says Iran is expanding aluminium production, with aluminium ingot output “skyrocketing” over recent years and doubling in two years. It also attributes the growth to more than a 13% surge in bauxite production. Overall, it signals rising alumina/aluminium supply.

title: Copper climbs on China support but COVID clouds demand outlook
summary: Copper rebounded 1.4% after China’s Politburo pledged more economic support and the dollar eased, making copper cheaper for overseas buyers. However, a renewed COVID wave and tighter lockdowns are expected to hurt Chinese factory activity, with copper still headed for a sharp monthly fall. Aluminium and nickel also fell on China demand worries.

title: China's Huayou Cobalt Jumps After Joining With Vale to Build Indonesia Nickel Plant
summary: Huayou Cobalt surged after partnering with Vale to build an Indonesia plant that processes Vale’s Pomalaa limonite into nickel products (including mixed hydroxide precipitate) for electric vehicle batteries. The project is expected to reach up to 120,000 tons annually, with construction already underway and definitive agreements forthcoming.

title: Rio Tinto invests in copper developer Arizona Sonoran
summary: Rio Tinto will invest in copper producer Arizona Sonoran Copper through a $23.7m private placement, taking a 7.4% stake. Proceeds fund drilling and studies for the Cactus Mine Project and metallurgical testing, including Nuton leaching technologies aimed at unlocking additional copper recovery with lower waste.

title: Zambia's ZCCM-IH to appoint adviser to restructure Mopani Copper Mines
summary: Zambia’s ZCCM-IH said an adviser and restructuring for Mopani Copper Mines is imminent, with the government “very close” to finding an investor. Zambia bought Mopani from Glencore in 2021 and needs new capital for output increases, while ZCCM continues servicing loans and funding inputs in the interim.

title: Aluminum Orders Stall as U.S. Buyers Fear Looming Recession
summary: The article headline says aluminum orders are stalling because U.S. buyers are increasingly concerned about a looming recession. That signals weakening near-term demand and softer order flow, which usually weighs on industrial metals sentiment and can pressure aluminum prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: European aluminium market tightness worsens as logistics issues plague ports
summary: European aluminium premiums are at record highs as Rotterdam infrastructure bottlenecks and staff shortages prevent imports from easing physical tightness. Warehouses lack units for May, shipments are delayed, and swaps are difficult. Logistics issues compound already low stocks, with falling LME inventories and a growing deficit outlook.

title: Copper is top performer in Friday morning rebound for LME base metals
summary: Fastmarkets says China’s stimulus sparked a risk-on rebound in LME base metals, lifting copper and other contracts early Friday. Traders also cite ongoing supply tightness in 2022, including mining/logistics challenges and Glencore’s lower copper guidance and force majeure on African copper deliveries.

title: Hydro Aluminum Metals Plans Cassopolis, Michigan, Operations
summary: Hydro Aluminum Metals plans to start operations in Cassopolis, Michigan, bringing a new product line backed by recycling technology aimed at the EV market. The project receives local and state support including grants, tax exemptions, and a property tax abatement, potentially boosting aluminium-related output expectations.

title: Aluminum orders stall as US buyers fear recession
summary: US aluminum buyers are holding off on new orders as recession fears rise amid inflation, weakening manufacturing activity, and supply-chain uncertainty. Spot deals have slowed and shipping costs fell, indicating reduced market activity. Semiconductor shortages are also limiting auto output, a major aluminum demand driver, despite packaging and aerospace strength.

title: Chile's March copper production falls 7.2%, manufacturing output up 3.3%
summary: Chile’s March copper output fell 7.2% year-on-year to 462,360 tonnes, according to INE. While manufacturing output rose 3.3% due to higher food production, the key update is weaker copper production from the world’s largest supplier, which can worsen near-term supply expectations.

title: What The War In Ukraine Means For Efforts To Cut Emissions
summary: Russia’s war and sanctions are disrupting emissions-reduction and industrial upgrade projects. For aluminum, Rusal faces logistical challenges and an alumina shortfall linked to the war and a ban on Australian exports, potentially delaying smelter upgrade investments. That raises risks to aluminum supply continuity.

title: Culpeo Minerals unearths broad copper zones in first hole at Lana Corina
summary: Culpeo Minerals reported first drilling assays at its Lana Corina copper project in Chile, confirming broad copper intervals (104m at 0.74% Cu) and additional intercepts with molybdenum credits. The firm is continuing a nine-hole, 4,000m program and awaiting assays for subsequent holes.

title: Vedanta Aluminium announces long-term sourcing of 380 MW renewable power
summary: Vedanta Aluminium said it has signed a long-term power delivery agreement to source 380 MW of renewable energy for its aluminium smelters—180 MW for Jharsuguda and 200 MW for BALCO’s Korba plant. The renewable supply aims to lower emissions and stabilize costs, but commissioning timing is not given.

title: Zambia seeks financial adviser to restructure Mopani Copper Mines
summary: Zambia’s ZCCM-IH is hiring a financial adviser and searching for a private investor to restructure and support Mopani Copper Mines. The firm aims to raise production and address funding needs after taking on $1.5bn debt in 2021. Government and company officials expect investor announcements within months.

title: Five Reasons Copper Prices Have Risen
summary: CME Group argues copper prices have risen because copper supply growth has been exceptionally slow and demand has improved, especially alongside China’s manufacturing rebound. It also links copper to higher energy and crude prices and to accelerating energy-transition and EV demand, though it notes consumer spending may eventually soften manufacturing demand.

title: Critical minerals: Lithium teething problems can't sate IGO Group's nickel processing hunger
summary: IGO Group’s lithium processing teething issues haven’t reduced its push to go deeper into the value chain. It vows to start studies for a battery-grade nickel sulphate plant if shareholders approve a $1.26 billion takeover. The plan also follows political promises in Australia to boost mineral value-adding investment.

title: Arizona Sonoran Announces Additional High-Grade Copper from Cactus and Completes PFS Drilling Program
summary: Arizona Sonoran Copper (ASCU) announced completed infill drilling results from its Cactus PFS program, including several copper-rich intercepts and improved resource confidence. The company aims to convert inferred to indicated resources and support a future mine plan/reserve update. It signals potential supply upside but no immediate production change.

title: Myanmar's junta vows to defend China-backed copper mine after PDF threats — Radio Free Asia
summary: Myanmar’s junta vows to secure the restart of the Letpadaung copper mine after opposition groups threatened to destroy it, creating supply-disruption risk alongside potential output resumption. The report also cites earlier PDF attacks that damaged infrastructure including a nickel plant, adding nickel downside risk.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Launches Clean Nickel Strategy And Initiates Research Into Decarbonizing Nickel Production
summary: EV Nickel launches its “Clean Nickel” strategy and trademark, outlining plans to electrify mining, use bioleaching, and evaluate carbon mineralization for CO2 capture in ultramafic tailings. The company reports ongoing funded research and sample testing, but provides no near-term production or supply changes affecting nickel prices.

title: Enough nickel, lithium for 14 million EVs in 2023 – European climate group
summary: A European climate group using BloombergNEF data argues there is enough battery-grade nickel and lithium for millions of EVs, while warning that the rapid EV ramp-up could still cause short-term battery-material supply bottlenecks. It highlights soaring nickel prices after Russia’s invasion and urges Europe to secure nickel supplies.

title: Blackstone Minerals appoints contractor for upstream DFS at Ta Khoa nickel project
summary: Blackstone Minerals appointed GRES to deliver an upstream definitive feasibility study for its Ta Khoa nickel project in Vietnam, covering process infrastructure, metallurgical testwork, and tailings storage, alongside mining studies. The project includes an existing nickel mine and planned refinery, supporting continued de-risking toward a future investment decision.

title: Vow ASA: VOW SUBSIDIARY C.H. EVENSEN SECURES CONTRACT WITH LEADING ALUMINIUM PRODUCER
summary: Vow ASA’s unit C.H. Evensen won a nearly EUR 1.3 million contract to deliver an electric preheating furnace for aluminium ingots to a leading, undisclosed producer. The company highlights energy efficiency and emissions reduction. The award suggests continued aluminium production investment, with limited but positive near-term demand signaling.

title: LME chief: bourse could revamp margining after nickel kerfuffle
summary: The LME chief said the exchange may end its unusual netting of initial and variation margin calls after heavy criticism of how it handled extreme price moves in nickel following Russia’s war. Removing the margin netting could increase funding costs for hedgers and weigh on nickel sentiment.

title: DGAP-News: Goldplay Mining Inc.: Goldplay Drills 12.2m of 1.18% Copper, Including 5.5m of 2.33 % Copper at Aparis Mine, In Southern Portugal
summary: Goldplay Mining announced Phase 1 drill results at the Aparis Copper Mine in southern Portugal, including 12.2m at 1.18% Cu and 5.5m at 2.33% Cu. The company says the mineralized system appears wider than historical workings and is planning further drilling.

title: Goldplay Drills 12.2m of 1.18% Copper, Including 5.5m of 2.33 % Copper at Aparis Mine, In Southern Portugal
summary: Goldplay drills at Aparis Mine in southern Portugal, reporting 12.2m of 1.18% copper, including 5.5m at 2.33% copper. Such positive drilling results typically strengthen expectations for potential resource quality and future copper supply, which can provide near-term support to copper prices.

title: Blackstone beefs up engineering muscle for nickel play
summary: Blackstone Minerals hired GR Engineering Services to support a definitive feasibility study for its upstream Ta Khoa nickel project. The work includes process and metallurgical testing and tailings design, aiming to de-risk development and improve financing confidence. The move may modestly boost expectations for future nickel supply.

title: London copper, aluminum sink to 3-months lows on demand concerns
summary: London copper and aluminum dropped to three-month lows as COVID-19 restrictions in China and expectations of aggressive U.S. rate hikes raised fears of weaker global growth. The Fed meeting and potential half-point hike, along with recent weak Chinese data, intensified demand worries, pressuring LME prices.

title: London copper, aluminum sink to 3-months lows on demand concerns
summary: London copper and aluminum slid to three-month lows as COVID-19 curbs in China and expectations of aggressive U.S. rate hikes raised fears of weaker global growth and metals demand. Copper fell 1.7% and aluminum 0.9% on LME, with the dollar firmer and macro data also weighing.

title: Group Ten Metals Inc.: Group Ten Reports 13.2 Meters of 3.33% Nickel Equivalent Within 401 Meters Continuous Mineralization from Resource Expansion Drilling at Stillwater West Critical Minerals Project in Montana, USA
summary: Talon Metals reported assay results from new drill holes at its Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project in Minnesota, highlighting thick, high-grade nickel and copper intervals in the CGO West area. The company plans continued drilling and feasibility work toward first production in 2026, with updates expected as new targets are drilled.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Retains SGS Canada for Updated Preliminary Economic Assessment on High-Grade Carmacks Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Yukon Canada
summary: Granite Creek Copper retained SGS to update a Preliminary Economic Assessment for its Carmacks Cu-Au-Ag project in Yukon, using a 2022 resource estimate with 651 Mlb contained measured/indicated copper. The study includes potential sulphide processing benefits and revised pit modeling and economics based on specified metal prices.

title: Enough nickel, lithium for 14 mln EVs in 2023 - European climate group
summary: A European climate group (T&E) says BloombergNEF-based data show enough nickel (and lithium) to support production for up to 14 million EVs in 2023. It argues Europe should secure more raw materials to speed the shift away from oil, but the “enough supply” framing may reduce immediate nickel price tightness.

title: Here To Serve Holding Corp.: Fortune Nickel and Gold Completes High Resolution Drone Magnetic Surveys that Identify New Priority Targets at Beck-Lennox Properties in Northeast Ontario
