summary: Fortune Nickel and Gold reported results from low-altitude drone magnetic surveys at its Beck-Ottaway-Lennox properties near Timmins, identifying magnetic anomalies coincident with EM conductors in mafic-ultramafic rocks. The company plans priority drilling to test potential Crawford-style nickel sulfide mineralization.

title: Couloir Capital Ltd. is Pleased to Announce the Initiation of Research Coverage on SPC Nickel Corp.
summary: Couloir Capital announced it is starting research coverage on SPC Nickel Corp., a Canadian nickel exploration company focused on Sudbury and other projects. The report highlights favorable macro conditions supporting the nickel outlook and potential future demand growth, but provides no concrete near-term supply or trade impacts that would directly move nickel prices.

title: One Year Later, Targeted Trade Enforcement Driving Aluminum Investment
summary: A white paper from the Aluminum Association says Commerce AD/CVD duties on common alloy aluminum sheet imports from 16 countries have cut imports sharply and increased U.S. producer shipments by about 24% in 2021. It cites $300 million+ in U.S. plant upgrades and expands capacity, supporting bullish aluminum sentiment.

title: One Year Later, Targeted Trade Enforcement Driving Aluminum
summary: A white paper from the Aluminum Association says U.S. AD/CVD orders on common alloy aluminum sheet from 16 countries have reduced unfair imports by two-thirds and boosted domestic producer shipments in 2021. It cites investment and cites injury findings from the USITC, suggesting improved supply-demand balance for aluminum.

title: Kamoa-Kakula on Track to Become the World's Third-largest Copper Mining Complex by Q4 2024, with Copper Production of Approximately 600,000 Tonnes per Year
summary: Digital Journal reports Kamoa-Kakula is on track to become the world’s third-largest copper mining complex by Q4 2024, targeting about 600,000 tonnes of copper production per year. The ramp-up implies rising supply expectations, which can pressure nearby copper prices despite the forward-looking timing.

title: LME credibility after nickel saga now top of Chamberlain's 'to do' list
summary: The LME’s nickel contract was suspended after March volatility drove prices above $101,000/tonne, triggering FCA and other regulatory reviews of the exchange and clearing house. The CEO will remain, and the priority is restoring credible, orderly nickel price discovery. Market impact is mostly confidence-related, not a direct nickel supply shock.

title: Southern Copper Mine Back to Full Output as Protester Talks Loom
summary: The article headline says Southern Copper’s mine is back to full output as talks with protesters are expected. This suggests an end (or easing) of production disruption, improving near-term supply visibility. The likely near-term market effect is supportive for copper prices as output constraints diminish.

title: QS Stock: Nickel Is About to Take a Back Seat at QuantumScape HQ
summary: The article says QuantumScape may be “cathode-agnostic,” with CEO Jagdeep Singh suggesting a switch from nickel to iron-based cathodes alongside lithium-metal anodes. The piece frames iron as potentially cheaper and more energy efficient, implying reduced nickel usage in future battery designs and pressuring nickel sentiment.

title: Fabled Copper Corp.: Fabled Copper Reports on the Davis Keays Eagle Vein Area with 6 Additional Parallel Veins Discovered and Values as High as 6.73% Copper
summary: Fabled Copper Corp. reported 2021 surface fieldwork at its Muskwa Copper Project’s Davis Keays Eagle vein area, including new parallel vein discoveries and rock assays up to 6.73% copper. The article is focused on exploration sampling and prospecting results, with no production or project-scale timeline changes.

title: Copper Fox Metals : Provides Update on Eaglehead Copper Project
summary: Copper Fox Metals updates its 100%-owned Eaglehead polymetallic porphyry copper project in British Columbia. It describes progress toward 2022 drilling (contracts executed, NoW pending), geological modeling, and age dating supporting a copper system. The release is exploration-stage with no production or immediate supply change.

title: Aranjin Resources Ltd: Aranjin Commences Exploration at the Baavhai Uul Copper Nickel Discovery
summary: Aranjin Resources began follow-up auger geochemical drilling at the Baavhai Uul copper-nickel discovery in Mongolia under an agreement with ION Energy. Early results reported anomalous nickel (up to 2,150 ppm) and copper (up to 677 ppm), with plans to upscale auger drilling and geophysics in coming weeks.

title: Copper steadies near 4-1/2 month lows but demand worries linger
summary: Copper prices steadied near 4-1/2 month lows as traders weighed rising interest rate risk, China COVID outbreaks and slowing factory activity that could weaken demand. The dollar’s strength further pressures dollar-priced metals. Speculators shifted toward price-fall bets. LME aluminium and nickel also posted declines.

title: Aranjin Resources Ltd: Aranjin Commences Exploration at the Baavhai Uul Copper Nickel Discovery
summary: Aranjin Resources commenced follow-up auger drilling at the Baavhai Uul copper-nickel discovery in Mongolia under an earn-in agreement. Early results cited up to 2,150 ppm nickel and 677 ppm copper from shallow samples, with additional auger, geophysics, and other copper project work planned.

title: Camino Minerals Corp.: Camino Signs Drilling Contract for its New Permitted Copper Exploration Targets at Los Chapitos, Peru
summary: Camino Minerals announced a contract to drill 1,500 metres of core at its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, targeting newly permitted high-grade oxidized copper outcrops at the Lourdes–Condori zones. Mobilization is planned for May 15, 2022, with results expected to follow later.

title: Mountain Boy Announces Progress on Telegraph Copper-Gold Project in BC's Golden Triangle
summary: Mountain Boy reports progress on its Telegraph copper-gold project in BC’s Golden Triangle, citing renewed geological prospectivity, anomalous copper values (including a 17.95% grab sample), and planned hyperspectral, IP/MT, and soil programs to refine drill targets for the 2022 field season. No production or resource update is provided.

title: Canadian Ingenuity: Booming copper mine, major community disasters
summary: The piece describes the history of Britannia Mines near Vancouver, focusing on copper ore concentration, output, disasters, and later environmental remediation. While copper mining and historical production are emphasized, the article contains no present-day supply, policy, or demand event that would likely affect short-term industrial metal prices.

title: Russia's Potanin dodges politics and sanctions to flourish
summary: Reuters reports that Potanin’s Interros and its key holding in Nornickel have avoided US/EU sanctions, while Western firms exit Russia. Since Nornickel is a leading refined nickel producer, being spared from sanctions should ease fears of disruption and weigh on nickel’s near-term risk premium.

title: Bitterroot Resources Ltd.: Bitterroot Resources Updates the LM Magmatic Nickel-Copper Project
summary: Bitterroot Resources provided results from a winter drilling program at its LM magmatic nickel-copper project in Michigan. Nickel-copper sulphide mineralization was intersected in 10 of 26 holes, including disseminated to semi-massive sulphides. The company plans further down-plunge drilling after additional land acquisition.

title: Bitterroot Resources Ltd.: Bitterroot Resources Updates the LM Magmatic Nickel-Copper Project
summary: Bitterroot Resources updated on a completed winter drilling program at its LM nickel-copper-platinum group metals property in Michigan, reporting sulphide mineralization in 10 of 26 holes, including chalcopyrite, pyrrhotite and pentlandite. The company plans further targeting after additional land acquisition, signaling ongoing exploration progress.

title: TSTT: Police held 161 for copper cable theft
summary: TSTT says copper cable theft has risen during the pandemic, leading to significant costs and service outages. Police have brought 161 people to court. TSTT argues it is transitioning customers to wireless and fibre but still serves active copper users. It condemns scrap buyers and notes penalties under telecom law.

title: Copper: Short Term Pain, Long Term Gain
summary: Report discusses Comex copper futures at $3.88/$3.50 support and $5.17 resistance, noting daily/weekly/monthly downtrends but arguing buyers may return. It cites corrective Elliott structure, oversold conditions, and a bullish breakout level above ~$5.06, with a long position and stop at $4.12.

title: SHFE/LME Copper Price Ratio Continued to Improve amid Favourable Policies in China and the Frequent Tightening Cycles Overseas_SMM
summary: SMM reports the SHFE/LME copper price ratio improved as China’s policy support for infrastructure and demand recovery, alongside a sharp drop in SHFE copper inventories, helped stabilize prices. Earlier, a strong US dollar and rising LME inventories pressured copper. After the USD impact eases, copper is expected to firm.

title: NickelX receives drilling grant for Cosmos South nickel project
summary: NickelX received a $180,000 WA government grant to start drilling four holes at its Cosmos South nickel prospect near major producers. The project is progressing permitting and using geophysical data to define drill targets. Given the small exploration scale, it likely has limited effect on near-term nickel prices.

title: Southern Copper's Cuajone mine resumes full operations; Las Bambas still suspended
summary: Southern Copper’s Cuajone mine has resumed full operations, improving Peru copper supply availability, while Las Bambas is still suspended, which continues to constrain supply elsewhere. The net effect is an improvement in near-term copper supply expectations, typically supportive for copper prices over the next few weeks.

title: Domestic Aluminium Inventory Increased After The Labour Day Holiday, But Fell YoY_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s eight major markets recorded aluminium ingot social inventories of 1.03 million mt as of May 5, up 46,000 mt week-on-week but down 82,000 mt year-on-year. Holiday arrivals lifted inventories in Gongyi and Nanhai; logistics restrictions eased. Suppliers face selling pressure, while downstream buying stays cautious, weighing on aluminium prices.

title: Slow Recovery of Consumption and US Interest Rate Hike Will Put Pressure on Short-Term Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium futures have fallen sharply on the week amid a likely US rate hike, stronger USD and weaker risk appetite. Downstream operating rates remain low with order declines in auto and real estate. Although inventories dropped, they fell due to delayed arrivals, so higher post-holiday arrivals may raise stocks and pressure prices.

title: Domestic Alumina Prices Remained Flat amid Declining Trading Activities _SMM
summary: SMM reports domestic alumina prices were flat week-on-week despite easier north-China transport after improved pandemic conditions and some COVID recurrence in Guangxi. Smelters stockpiled on logistics concerns, but weak aluminium prices and adequate long-term supply muted upward momentum. Support may be temporary, while future oversupply and imports loom.

title: Aluminium Smelters' Profits Shrank to 2,500 yuan/mt amid Sharply Falling Aluminium prices _SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium smelters’ full costs eased slightly but profits fell sharply as aluminium prices declined. Thermal coal costs dropped after cancelled import tariffs, while power tariffs were mostly stable short term. However, prebaked anode prices are seen rising in May and freight rates increased, implying higher aluminium costs ahead.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices will Remain Rangebound at High Levels Supported by the Strong Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SMM reports LME nickel fluctuated between $32,000–$33,880/mt with weaker liquidity and SHFE nickel remaining rangebound at high levels. A pullback from macro factors was offset by persistent supply shortage, tightening nickel sulphate supply. Poor demand pressured prices, so the outlook is rangebound: SHFE 218,000–238,000 yuan/mt.

title: Aguila Copper Corp.: Aguila Copper Begins Geophysical (IP) Survey at the Lida Copper-Silver Project, Nevada
summary: Aguila Copper Corp. began an induced polarization (IP) survey at its Lida copper-silver project in Nevada, using a deep-penetrating geophysical system to guide potential drilling later in 2022. The release highlights copper-oxide/carbonate mineralization from recent sampling, but provides no immediate production or supply effects.

title: SMM Sees Little Upward Momentum for Aluminium Prices in May amid Extended Regional Imbalance_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices lost momentum through April, with SHFE and LME both falling. It attributes weakness to rising domestic supply from capacity restarts, muted downstream demand/PMI and higher inventories due to pandemic logistics, plus bearish sentiment from US rate hikes. Aluminium is expected to stay pressured in May.

title: Inventory of Aluminium Billets in China Rose 22,700 mt to 128,600 mt after the Labour Day Holiday_SMM
summary: China’s domestic aluminium billet inventory rose 22,700 mt to 128,600 mt on May 5 after Labour Day. Large arrivals from Yunnan and stagnant trading boosted stocks, especially in Foshan. Downstream buying stayed cautious due to ongoing consumption disruption/pandemic rumours, creating near-term inventory pressure and price downside risk as buyers wait.

title: BHP says bid for Canadian nickel miner 'tip of the iceberg' for growth ambitions
summary: BHP says its bid for a Canadian nickel miner is only a “tip of the iceberg” as it pursues broader growth ambitions. The report implies continued focus on expanding nickel exposure and may affect near-term sentiment around nickel supply and production prospects.

title: Chile's copper output falls 6.36% in March, Cochilco says
summary: Chile’s copper output declined 6.36% in March, according to Cochilco. As Chile is the key source of global supply, lower monthly production can signal tighter availability and support near-term copper price expectations. Other content is largely unrelated fastmarkets/assessment process updates.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Closes Upsized C$20 Million Equity Offering
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. closed a C$20 million upsized private placement at $0.80/share and plans to use net proceeds to advance its Copper Creek and Contact Copper projects, plus working capital. The article is about financing for exploration/development rather than any immediate production or supply change affecting copper prices.

title: Victory Nickel Inc. Restructuring Proposal Update
summary: Victory Nickel updated investors on its bankruptcy-related debt restructuring proposal and held a creditor vote, later adjourned to address concerns from its largest creditor. The company is a sulphide nickel resource holder, and the distress raises near-term uncertainty around its nickel operations, typically bearish for nickel sentiment.

title: TSTT slams  rogue dealers  for copper theft
summary: TSTT in Trinidad and Tobago condemned “rogue scrap iron dealers” for a rise in theft and vandalism of the firm’s copper overhead line network since the start of the Covid-19 pandemic. The company warned of penalties and said copper theft drives illicit scrap purchases and causes outages and safety risks.

title: The 'nickel king' is still Russia's ultimate survivor
summary: The piece argues Potanin has largely avoided US/EU sanctions, despite Western pressure after Ukraine. It stresses Nornickel’s size in refined nickel production and notes its apparent exemption from sanctions, suggesting reduced nickel supply disruption risk versus previously sanctioned Russian producers.

title: Aluminium Prices May Stay Weak as Aluminium Ingots Arrived during Holiday_SMM
summary: Aluminium futures and LME prices fell over May 5-6. SMM data show social aluminium inventories rising and spot premiums weakening, with domestic downstream procurement described as weak and processing operating rates down. Despite some shipments and faster plant resumption, the net view is that aluminium fundamentals remain pressured and prices may stay rangebound at low.

title: SMM Weekly Survey: Aluminium Downstream Operating Rates Down 7.5 Percentage Points due to Holiday Factor and Pandemic _SMM
summary: SMM says major aluminium processing operating rates fell 7.5 percentage points to 57.3% week-on-week, hurt by Labour Day shutdowns and pandemic disruptions. Extrusion and secondary producers saw the sharpest declines, with higher transport costs and inventory build. Rates may improve only as holiday effects fade and pandemic improves.

title: Nickel Spot Market was Sluggish due to the Pandemic in China_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports sluggish Chinese nickel trading, with SHFE nickel and spot premiums softening versus the prior day. It links the decline in pure nickel quotes mainly to China’s pandemic-driven lower manufacturing operating rates, which weakened demand. It also notes relative price differences between nickel briquette and nickel sulphate and slightly rising quotes.

title: ALUMINIUM INDUSTRY: Looking outside the box: Record high in 2021 on sustained recovery of demand in Europe / Deliveries grow 3.9% / Exports decline 15%
summary: The article reports a record high for the aluminium industry in 2021, attributed to sustained recovery of demand in Europe. It notes deliveries rising 3.9% while exports fell 15%, implying stronger domestic/contract demand versus weaker outward shipments, which is generally supportive for near-term aluminium pricing sentiment.

title: Copper Importers Continuously Raised the Premiums due to the Rising Profits _SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums under warrants rising to $33–68/mt, with B/L premiums also increasing, reflecting higher import profits. It cites LME inventories rising but notes low Chinese social inventory supporting SHFE/LME ratios. Rising profits have led importers to keep lifting premiums for pyro- and hydro-copper cargoes.

title: Aluminium Scrap Prices Followed Aluminium Prices Down _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices fell 420 yuan/mt to 20,300 yuan/mt. Corresponding aluminium scrap prices also dropped: extrusion scrap by 200–300 yuan/mt and tense scrap by 100–200 yuan/mt, with some areas like Shandong seeing declines up to 400 yuan/mt. Drops varied by local COVID severity.

title: Copper Inventories across Major Chinese Markets up 9,400 mt after the Labour Day Holiday_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s mainstream copper inventories rose 9,400 mt to 120,000 mt after the Labour Day holiday, driven by less-than-expected downstream activity and cathode stagnation from transport problems, alongside smelters shipping directly to downstream. With improved consumption expected next week, inventory may fall, but the near-term signal is bearish.

title: Nickel Inventory in Shanghai Bonded Zone Slightly Increased_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that LME nickel fell through the week while SHFE nickel stayed rangebound at high levels. Shanghai bonded nickel inventory rose to 8,800 mt, up 600 mt WoW, with nickel plate inventory increasing on long-term orders awaiting customs clearance. The buildup points to weaker near-term nickel tightness.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 235,000 wmt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 235,000 wmt to 5.642 million wmt (44,300 mt Ni content) versus last week. Demand improved as pandemic easing let NPI plants restock. Philippines shipments rose after the rainy season, but supply gains remain limited. Port inventories are expected to stay steady short term.

title: Copper, aluminium, other metals crash on Chinese Covid curbs
summary: Copper, aluminium, nickel and other commodities have fallen as China tightened Covid controls. The lockdowns reduce activity in end-use industries, cutting near-term metal demand and weighing on broader sentiment toward the metals complex. The price declines over the past couple of weeks reflect this demand shock.

title: Copper, aluminium, other metals crash on Chinese Covid curbs
summary: Copper, aluminium, nickel and other metals have fallen over the past couple of weeks as China tightened Covid curbs. The lockdowns reduce demand from the world’s largest metal consumer and dampen sentiment toward the metal complex, creating negative price pressure across industrial commodities in the near term.

title: Tesla Confirms Vale Nickel Deal, Lifts Veil on U.S. Race Data
summary: The headline says Tesla has confirmed a nickel supply deal with Vale, suggesting additional demand visibility for nickel in the near term. If the agreement affects contracted volumes or timing, it may tighten market expectations and provide modest upward support to nickel prices over the next few weeks.

title: Brazil's Vale signs long-term deal to supply Tesla with nickel
summary: Vale signed a long-term agreement to supply Tesla with nickel sourced from its Canada operations. The contract increases visibility of nickel demand from a major EV manufacturer, potentially tightening near-term supply expectations and supporting nickel prices. The announcement is directly linked to nickel market fundamentals.

title: CME explores nickel contract after LME trade chaos -sources
summary: CME Group is exploring a cash-settled nickel contract, including a possible nickel sulphate product, after the LME suspended nickel trading and cancelled billions in deals in March amid extreme price swings. LME volumes fell post-suspension. The move targets better hedging access, but the article cites no immediate supply-demand shift.

title: Shanghai bonded base metals stocks diverge in April amid Covid-19 controls; copper build-up slows
summary: Shanghai’s Covid-19 controls affected bonded metals flows. Copper bonded stocks kept increasing in April but more slowly as transport improved and import arbitrage turned profitable. Aluminium and nickel bonded stocks declined due to closed or loss-making arbitrage windows and limited inflows/outflows, with weak trading and constrained logistics.

title: BHP's unsuccessful nickel bid 'tip of iceberg' for growth ambitions, top executive says
summary: BHP says its failed bid for Noront Resources is “almost the tip of the iceberg” for future Canadian nickel growth, setting up teams to seek projects in Ontario’s Ring of Fire. The executive also notes focus on copper and investing in opportunities, but provides no deal or supply disruption.

title: Brazil's Vale signs long-term deal to supply Tesla with nickel | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: Vale said it signed a long-term deal with Tesla to supply nickel from its Canada operations. The agreement links Vale’s nickel production to EV battery demand, which can improve near-term market sentiment about nickel demand. The article does not quantify volumes or timing, limiting precision on magnitude.

title: 7 Oversold Stocks That Shouldn't Be. Buy Them Now.
summary: The piece lists oversold stocks to buy, including Southern Copper (SCCO). It notes copper prices pulled back after a spike post–Ukraine invasion, with worries that higher rates may slow demand. It counters that EV growth could sustain copper demand, implying copper may avoid further declines.

title: Copper Inventory Growth Fell Short of Expectations, Despite Falling Downstream Operating rates_SMM
summary: SMM reported that most copper downstream enterprises had lower operating rates after the Labour Day holiday and many paused for 3–5 days. However, copper inventory growth after the holiday missed expectations, as smelters shipped directly to downstream and transportation disruptions stranded copper at smelters, tightening near-term availability.

title: Vale signs deal with Tesla for Canadian nickel
summary: Vale signed a long-term deal to supply Tesla with low-carbon Class 1 nickel from its Canadian operations, including the Long Harbour plant. Vale targets a growing share of Class 1 nickel sales to the EV sector. The agreement reinforces EV-linked demand expectations for nickel despite limited deal details.

title: Peruvian protesters agree to attend talks over MMG's shut copper mine | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Peruvian indigenous communities protesting MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine agreed to attend talks with the government and company. The dispute has already forced the project’s temporary closure, and production disruptions have previously occurred due to roadblocks. Negotiations could reduce near-term supply risk for copper.

title: Peruvian protesters agree to attend talks over MMG's shut copper mine | Kat Country 98.9
summary: Peruvian Indigenous communities protesting MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine agreed to attend talks with the government and the company. The dispute has led to a temporary closure. Talks are planned for Saturday outside the emergency area, after prior eviction attempts and a state of emergency in late April suspended protests.

title: Aluminium Fell by More Than 2% Due to the Demand Concerns_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: LME aluminium slid 2.54% to a four-month low on May 6 as a rising US dollar and concerns over slower manufacturing demand—especially from China—pushed selling. The Fed’s large rate hike and weaker/global growth signals weighed on base metals. The piece also cites rising LME copper inventories pressuring copper prices.

title: Aluminium Inventory in Shanghai Bonded Zone Increased_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that aluminium inventories in Shanghai’s bonded zone rose to 77,800 mt on May 6, up 2,000 mt from a week earlier. Higher bonded inventories suggest easing physical tightness in the near term, which is generally bearish for aluminium price expectations over coming days to weeks.

title: Supply Tightness of Copper Cathode in East China Gets Eased_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that copper cathode supply tightness in East China has eased substantially. Raw material procurement for copper cathode rod producers in Jiangsu and Zhejiang has returned to normal following the Labour Day holiday as most firms resumed production. Logistics are not fully normalized, and transport costs from Shanghai remain relatively high.

title: SHFE Nickel Inventory Dropped over 20%, Creating a New Low in Nearly Two Months_SMM
summary: SMM reports that nickel inventories have been falling. LME nickel inventory has declined since late April, while SHFE nickel inventory dropped for three straight weeks. On May 5, LME inventories rose but remained low; SHFE weekly inventories fell 22.29% to 5,354 mt, the lowest in nearly two months.

title: Copper in Worst Run Since 2020 as Covid Dims China Outlook
summary: Copper is experiencing its worst run since 2020 as Covid-related developments dim China’s outlook. Weaker expectations for Chinese economic activity and industrial demand tend to reduce near-term buying interest for copper, placing downward pressure on prices over the coming days.

title: Tesla Confirms Vale Nickel Deal, Lists Battery Material Suppliers
summary: Tesla confirmed a long-term supply deal with Vale to provide Class 1 nickel into the United States, naming Vale among its direct battery-material suppliers. Nickel is used in cathode chemistries for Tesla’s longer-range EVs, which can support incremental near-term demand expectations.

title: Vedanta offers Zambia investment commitments in return for copper-mine control
summary: Vedanta offered Zambia increased investment and infrastructure spending for Konkola Copper Mines (KCM) in exchange for resuming control. The proposal follows a long-running legal dispute after Zambia put KCM under liquidation in 2019. Vedanta also pledged to pay suppliers and raise salaries, aiming to boost KCM output.

title: First Quantum Minerals Ltd.: First Quantum Announces Board Approval of the Kansanshi S3 Expansion and Enterprise Nickel Project
summary: First Quantum’s board approved Zambia’s Kansanshi S3 expansion to boost copper output (including higher smelter capacity for copper anode) and approved the Enterprise nickel project using the Sentinel processing circuit. Work starts immediately, but first production is expected in 2025 for S3 and 2023 for nickel.

title: First Quantum Announces Board Approval of the Kansanshi S3 Expansion and Enterprise Nickel Project
summary: First Quantum reports board approval for the Kansanshi S3 expansion and the Enterprise Nickel project. The decision signals progression toward additional nickel production capacity, which can improve forward supply expectations and weigh on nickel price sentiment over the coming days to weeks, absent any offsetting disruptions.

title: First Quantum Approves $1.25 Billion Zambia Copper Expansion
summary: First Quantum reportedly approved a $1.25 billion copper expansion project in Zambia. Such investment signals future capacity growth and can influence market expectations for copper supply timelines, with the immediate price reaction depending on perceived project speed, ramp-up risk, and timing versus current market tightness.

title: Cyprium Metals propelling Nifty reopening as huge copper deficit forecast
summary: Rystad Energy forecasts a growing global copper deficit driven by electrification demand. The article highlights Cyprium Metals’ planned restart of Australia’s Nifty mine, showing costs well below the recent copper price and potential free cash flow. It also notes analyst expectations of Chinese demand recovery later in 2022, supporting copper prices.

title: Output of Aluminium Stood at 3.298 million mt in April in China_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s April aluminium output rose to 3.298 mln mt and capacity utilization stayed high. Demand was weaker in April due to repeated COVID-related logistics issues, leaving delayed ingot arrivals and a clearer backlog. May output and capacity are expected to rise, but improved transport could lift downstream use and reduce inventories later.

title: SMM Outlook for Aluminium Scrap  Market in May_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says Linyi (Shandong) had strict pandemic freight controls since April, reducing aluminium scrap supply, but shipments rose after the Ministry of Transport allowed compliant drivers to pass through. Despite eased transport elsewhere, recyclers are cautious for May due to lower prices and demand and higher inflows of non-standard ADC12 secondary aluminium.

title: Customs: Aluminium Semis Exports Rose 29.2% YoY in Jan-Apr, While Steel Exports Dropped 29.2% YoY_SMM
summary: China’s customs data show total exports and imports rising year-on-year. Specifically, exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis increased 29.2% in Jan–Apr, while copper ore and concentrates imports rose 4.5% over the same period. These trade-flow shifts can influence short-term supply expectations for aluminium and copper.

title: China Produced 12,900 mt of Refined Nickel in April and Normal Output can be restored in May_SMM
summary: SMM reports China produced 12,900 mt of refined nickel in April (+2.62% MoM, -0.65% YoY). Output matched expectations, supported by more stable LME nickel and resumed operations as raw-material import issues eased and March maintenance ended. May refined nickel production is expected to rise to ~13,400 mt.

title: China's Output of Nickel Sulphate Declined to 21,600 mt in Metal Content in April and Some Nickel Salt Plants Began to Return to Work in May_SMM
summary: China’s nickel sulphate output fell 12.46% on the month in April as nickel salt factories faced high costs and weak demand with near-negative profits, prompting production cuts to support prices. In May, some plants resumed and output rose, but demand for precursors and batteries remains poor, keeping production subdued.

title: China Unwrought Aluminium and Aluminium Semis Exports Largely Unchanged in Apr Partly due to COVID_SMM
summary: China’s April exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis were about 596,900 mt, largely unchanged MoM but up sharply YoY, with COVID-impacted transport limiting further gains. April export profits improved as the SHFE/LME ratio recovered. With logistics improving, May exports are expected to stay up about 35% YoY.

title: China Aluminium Ingot Social Inventory Dropped Slightly and Varied by Region _SMM
summary: SMM reported China’s aluminium ingot social inventories at 1.03 million mt on May 9, down 3,000 mt from a week earlier and 72,000 mt versus a year earlier. Some regions rose (e.g., Gongyi) on delayed arrivals, while others fell (e.g., Wuxi, Hangzhou) as arrivals slowed.

title: First Quantum approves US$1.25B Zambia copper expansion
summary: First Quantum approved a $1.25 billion expansion project in Zambia, increasing plans for copper output. The decision is likely to shift expectations toward greater copper supply, which can pressure prices in the coming days as traders start repricing the near-term supply outlook, despite construction ramp-up uncertainty.

title: SHFE Aluminium to Remain Pressured by Poor Fundamentals after Refreshing a New Low in Four and a Half Months_SMM
summary: SMM says SHFE aluminium slid to a four-and-a-half-month low near 19,575 yuan/mt after weak fundamentals. April unwrought aluminium and semi exports rose sharply YoY, while output also increased and consumption remains inhibited by severe COVID conditions. Fed-tightening and recession/sanctions fears further pressured LME base metals.

title: Pacific Ridge Acquires Chuchi Porphyry Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration announced it will acquire up to a 75% interest in the Chuchi porphyry copper-gold project in British Columbia. The release outlines historical drilling, copper grades, and plans for an airborne survey and summer exploration to define drill targets. It implies future supply potential, not near-term production changes.

title: Jokowi plans to meet Elon Musk over nickel, says minister
summary: Indonesia’s President Jokowi plans to meet Elon Musk during a US visit, as the country seeks to accelerate development of its nickel industry to supply EV batteries. Tesla representatives have visited Morawali’s nickel production hub, and Indonesia is targeting a full domestic nickel-to-batteries supply chain. The news is supportive for nickel sentiment.

title: Brazil's CBA posts record Q1 Ebitda on higher aluminium prices, premiums
summary: Brazil’s CBA reported record Q1 EBITDA, attributing the result to higher aluminium prices and premiums. While the piece is largely platform/assessment-related, the key financial linkage highlights recent aluminium price strength, which can bolster expectations for further short-term aluminium pricing.

title: China's COVID Lockdowns Push Copper Prices Lower
summary: China’s lockdowns and zero-COVID stance are keeping demand weak. Shanghai remains under restrictions and Beijing cases are rising, while Caixin Manufacturing PMI hit a two-year low. The contraction coincides with falling copper prices and an 8.8% drop in copper imports from February to March, with demand likely soft through May.

title: Nickel 28 Releases Ramu Q1 2022 Operating Performance
summary: Nickel 28 reported Q1 2022 Ramu production of 8,756 tonnes of contained nickel and lower cash costs of $1.48/lb net of cobalt by-product credits. Management said production is at expected levels as Asia reopens, while sales were temporarily hit by export restrictions and the Olympics, expected to normalize in Q2.

title: Emmerson Resources reveals visual copper at Hermitage prospect
summary: Emmerson Resources reports visual confirmation of “very high-grade” copper at the Hermitage prospect, with drill intersections including 38m of mineralisation containing native copper, malachite and chalcopyrite, and a second hole with 57m of native copper-bearing intervals. The company plans further drilling and awaits assay results.

title: Far East Gold begins revised scoping study for Wonogiri copper-gold project
summary: Far East Gold started a revised scoping study for its Wonogiri copper-gold project, commissioning metallurgical test work and updating a prior study based on current commodity prices. It reports early gold and copper metallurgical results and outlines additional exploration at another Indonesian copper-gold project.

title: SHFE Nickel Fell for Four Consecutive Days and Once Fell by 6% Today and the Spot Fell by 9.5% in 5 Days [SMM Comment]_SMM
summary: SHFE nickel has fallen for four consecutive days, with the spot refined nickel down sharply over five days amid weak downstream demand. NPI prices weakened as steel mill transactions slowed and profits were squeezed by oversupply in stainless steel. Supply remains tight for pure nickel, but demand weakness dominates near term.

title: Mongolia's export of copper concentrate up by 23% in a week
summary: Mongolia exported 492.8 thousand tons of copper concentrate between April 29 and May 5, up 23.1% from the same period a year earlier. It also exported copper cathode since the start of the year. Faster concentrate exports can raise near-term supply expectations for copper.

title: The Short Position Increased, and Upward Trend of INE Bonded Copper Contract was Under Pressure_SMM
summary: SMM reports that the INE bonded copper 2207 contract trended slightly upward but finished near 63,500 yuan/mt, up only 0.05%, with short positions increasing. It notes pandemic-affected near-term demand and investor worries over growth, while the INE-SHFE price spread widened.

title: Copper concentrate export grows by 23.1 percent
summary: Mongolia exported 492.8 thousand tons of copper concentrate during April 29–May 5, up 23.1% versus the same period last year. The report also notes copper cathode exports and broader shipments of coal and iron ore, indicating greater copper feedstock availability in the near term.

title: Pacific Ridge agrees to buy Canadian porphyry copper-gold project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration agreed to buy up to a 75% stake in Canada’s Chuchi porphyry copper-gold project from AuRico Metals. The earn-in requires cash, share issuance, and $10m-plus exploration spending, pending regulatory clearance. As an exploration-stage transaction, it is unlikely to affect near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Peru copper production hit amid ongoing protests
summary: Protests in Peru have suspended MMG’s Las Bambas mine and halted work at Southern Copper’s Cuajone, with stoppages removing about 20% of Peru’s copper output. Authorities report major daily losses in royalties and exports, while unrest raises fears of wider mine disruptions beyond these sites.

title: New Caledonia's green nickel plan to stand out in global market
summary: New Caledonia plans more environmentally friendly nickel production, aiming to power nickel factories with increasing renewable energy and build solar generation for Prony Resources. The project is tied to cutting emissions and costs versus lower-cost Indonesian and Filipino producers. Output is scheduled over 2023–2025, implying limited immediate price impact.

title: High Profits Drive Aluminium Smelters to Stick to Output Increase Plans _SMM
summary: SMM reports Chinese aluminium smelter costs averaged 17,320 yuan/mt in April, with only a portion of capacity above higher cost thresholds. Despite recent aluminium price declines, smelters remain profitable and may stick to output increase plans. Meanwhile, east China spot discounts persist amid increasing supply and weak demand, keeping prices weak and volatile.

title: SHFE Nickel Stopped Declining? The Import Window Remained Closed!_SMM
summary: SMM reports that pure nickel supply remains tight because the SHFE/LME spread keeps the nickel import window closed, and NPI output declines. However, SHFE nickel and spot prices fell, with weaker stainless steel demand after renewed COVID cases in Wuxi. Macro factors also continue to pressure nickel downward.

title: Africa: Renewed interest in copper mining
summary: The article says high copper prices and rising demand are driving renewed exploration and mine expansion across Africa. It cites the DRC’s Kamoa-Kakula ramp-up to 600,000 tonnes by Q4 2024, Zambia’s Mimbula expansion and Mopani/Uganda’s Kilembe restart plans, reinforcing a bullish copper outlook.

title: LME Aluminium Inventory Hit 17-Year Low, While SHFE Aluminium Inventory Increased Following Continuous Decline _SMM
summary: LME data show aluminium inventories have resumed falling after a February spike, reaching 560,275 mt on May 10, the lowest in nearly 17 years. SHFE aluminium inventories ended three weeks of decline but still rose only 1.72% to 295,137 mt as of May 6, remaining low versus recent months.

title: LME Aluminium Slumped to Five-Month Low as Funds Bet Slowing Demand Will Drag Aluminium Prices Lower_SMM
summary: LME three-month aluminium slid to a five-month low as funds bet slowing demand will weigh on prices. Upcoming China lending and social financing data may confirm demand weakness. Higher U.S. interest rates boosted the dollar, pressuring dollar-priced metals, though tight supply concerns from Europe’s high electricity costs may offer limited support.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Rebounded as Import Profit Window Remains Open_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai bonded-zone imported copper premiums under warrants rising to $70/mt on average and bill-of-lading premiums up to $57.5/mt. The SHFE/LME copper ratio increase keeps the import profit window open versus spot and SHFE 2205, with firm offers but thin trading as buyers balk at premiums.

title: Marimaca Copper infill drilling continues to encounter higher grades
summary: Marimaca Copper reported results from 10 RC infill holes at its Marimaca oxide deposit in Chile, finding broad near-surface copper oxide mineralisation with grades exceeding the resource model in several zones. Extensions outside the prior resource block and potential expansion of the high-grade MAMIX zone were highlighted.

title: Metals Generally Rose with 3% and 5% Increase in SHFE Nickel and Iron Ore Respectively_SMM
summary: SMM reports that SHFE metals broadly rose on May 11, with SHFE nickel up about 3%, SHFE aluminium up 2.61%, and SHFE copper up around 0.3%. LME copper and aluminium also increased, while nickel declined, reflecting mixed global signals amid a weaker dollar and higher crude.

title: SMM Analysis: SHFE Aluminium Has Returned to above 20,000 yuan/mt, but still Lack Support from Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium returning above 20,000 yuan/mt, up 2.61% on the day. It cites LME inventory drops to the lowest levels in nearly 17 years and lower Chinese social inventories. Rising smelter costs also support prices, though SMM says fundamentals haven’t materially improved and risks remain.

title: Copper gains as China's COVID-19 cases ease, but demand still at risk | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Copper rose 1.4% as China’s slowing COVID-19 infections eased near-term demand concerns, though “zero-COVID” restrictions remain. The report notes lockdowns and macro worries had pressured prices recently. It also cites disruptions affecting cobalt, nickel, lithium logistics and shows aluminium up while nickel falls.

title: Blackwolf Copper and Gold Ltd: Blackwolf Copper and Gold's Niblack and Hyder Projects Exploration and Permitting Update
summary: Blackwolf Copper and Gold provides an exploration and permitting update for its Niblack (Cu-Au-Ag-Zn VMS) and Hyder-area projects (including Cantoo with Cu/Ag/Zn plus gold-silver). The company anticipates permits and plans multi-phase drilling, potentially expanding resources, which may modestly influence near-term copper expectations. No nickel or aluminium impacts are stated.

title: Governor Ivey: Novelis Plans to Invest $2.5 Billion to Open Alabama Aluminum Plant, Creating 1,000 Jobs in Baldwin County
summary: Governor Kay Ivey said Novelis will invest $2.5B to build a low-carbon integrated aluminium recycling and rolling plant in Alabama, with an initial 600 kilotonnes of finished goods capacity and 1,000 jobs. Construction is underway and commissioning is expected mid-2025, targeting beverage can demand.

title: Copper gains as China's COVID-19 cases ease, but demand still at risk | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: Copper prices rose about 1.4% as China’s COVID-19 infections slowed, easing immediate demand concerns, though partial “zero-COVID” restrictions still suppress activity. The piece notes April vehicle and cathode output weakness from lockdowns and logistics disruption, while LME aluminium also gained and nickel fell on the day.

title: ALX Resources Corp. Completes Inaugural Drilling Program at Electra Nickel Project, Ontario
summary: ALX Resources said it completed six of eight planned holes in its Electra nickel-copper project in Ontario, intersecting sulphide mineralization and detecting nickel, copper and zinc via portable XRF. Additional lab results are pending and the update is exploratory, with no production or definitive resource revision.

title: Golden Arrow options Argentina copper-gold project to Syndicate Minerals
summary: Golden Arrow Resources agreed to option up to 85% of its Mogote copper-gold project in Argentina to Syndicate Minerals. Syndicate can earn 80% through $5m exploration spend and $1.9m cash over five years, with a further 5% after feasibility and JV formation. No immediate supply disruption is cited.

title: Vedanta Agrees to Suspend Lawsuits Over Zambia Copper Mines
summary: Vedanta agreed to suspend lawsuits connected to its copper mining operations in Zambia. Easing legal pressure can lower the probability of immediate operational disruptions or delays, improving near-term expectations for copper supply. This usually provides supportive sentiment for copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Utah copper mining company to produce rare mineral
summary: Rio Tinto and Utah officials said the Kennecott refinery in Utah will begin producing tellurium, a critical mineral used in solar panels, from materials previously discarded as tailings. The U.S.-based plan targets about 20 tons/year and aims to reduce reliance on China, offering limited near-term impact on copper or aluminium prices.

title: Nickel has been whacked, but is poised to bounce back faster than other battery metals
summary: Nickel fell alongside a broader mining sell-off, but the piece argues it is positioned to recover sooner than other battery metals. It points to EV battery demand plus existing stainless-steel use, Australian class-one premium supplies, and China’s grade dislocation where NPI and nickel sulphate trade at deep discounts to LME.

title: Rio Tinto Starts Producing Tellurium At Kennecott Copper Operation In Utah
summary: Rio Tinto says it has started producing tellurium at its Kennecott copper refinery in Utah, with refining by 5N Plus and primary supply to First Solar. About 20 tons per year will be produced via a new circuit. The update is focused on critical minerals/semi supply rather than copper market fundamentals.

title: Aluminium Prices Rebounded to 20,000 yuan/mt and Will Move Rangebound_SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium rebounded toward 20,000 yuan/mt, with the LME aluminium contract also rising. The piece attributes the move to improved market activity as enterprises resumed work, narrower spot discounts, stronger downstream purchases, and lower secondary aluminium operating rates, outweighing bearish positioning.

title: Weak Demand Limited the Rapid Growth in Aluminium Scrap Trading in Linyi_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium scrap throughput at Linyi’s nonferrous metals city rose week-on-week in early May, helped by improved logistics and a small aluminium price increase. However, falling prices and weak downstream alloy demand reduced recycler activity and trading volumes, despite a May 11 rebound in aluminium and taint prices.

title: Copper Drops Below $9,000 as Metals Slide on Global Demand Fears
summary: Copper traded below $9,000 as broader industrial metals weakened on global demand fears. The framing suggests investors reduced expectations for near-term consumption, driving selling pressure in copper prices over the immediate period referenced.

title: US Federal Reserve may Continue to Raise the Interest Rate and the INE Bonded Copper Prices Fell_SMM
summary: SMM reports INE bonded copper 2207 declining to close at 62,480 yuan/mt, down 0.97%, with rising open interest mainly from shorts. It cites macro pressure: US CPI missed expectations, leading to expectations the Fed may keep raising rates, weighing on copper gains. The INE–SHFE premium narrowed.

title: Monthly Review and Analysis of Pure Nickel Spot Market_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports tight pure nickel supply in April, with overseas sources driving availability and import losses persisting due to weak SHFE/LME spread. Downstream alloy and battery demand softened after renewed pandemic impacts. May is expected to keep supply and demand relatively weak, with limited upward momentum in SHFE nickel prices.

title: Copper Sinks Below $9,000 as Metals Slide on Global Demand Fears
summary: The headline reports copper dropping below $9,000 as broader metals weaken on concerns about global demand. This suggests investors are cutting near-term expectations for industrial consumption, creating immediate downward pressure on copper prices relative to other metals.

title: Canada Nickel Takes Important Step in Crawford Nickel Project Permitting Process
summary: Canada Nickel announced it submitted a preliminary draft Initial Project Description for the Crawford nickel project to Canada’s Impact Assessment Agency after signing impact assessment process agreements with local Indigenous communities. The step initiates a review period and supports regulatory certainty for the project’s development.

title: Wrexham: 'Significant' amount of copper cable stolen
summary: Police in Wrexham are investigating four theft incidents over 10 days involving “significant amounts” of underground copper cable, including roughly 700–800 metres per event. Victims reportedly lost telephone and broadband service. Authorities request information, indicating localized copper loss rather than wider market supply disruption.

title: Anglo American to return to Zambia with Arc Minerals copper deal
summary: Arc Minerals said Anglo American will take majority control (70%) of its Zambia copper-cobalt exploration licences, its first new investment in Zambia in 20 years. The agreement is likely to support copper market sentiment, though it is tied to exploration rather than near-term production.

title: Russia Allows Norilsk Nickel to Keep ADRs Traded Abroad
summary: Russia has allowed Norilsk Nickel’s ADRs to remain traded abroad. The move can improve market access and sentiment toward the company, a key nickel producer. While it does not directly change nickel supply or demand, the policy easing may provide mild near-term support to nickel pricing.

title: Aluminium Bahrain B S C : Alba Discloses its Financial Results for the First Quarter of 2022
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (ALBA) reported Q1 2022 profit of BD146.8m, up 181% YoY, citing higher LME prices driving revenue (LME up 56% YoY) and low LME inventories (~0.6m MT). It also notes demand recovery and improving supply-demand balance, reinforcing positive near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: Anglo to return to Zambia with Arc Minerals copper deal
summary: Arc Minerals’ shares jumped after Anglo American agreed to take 70% control of a JV tied to Arc’s Zambia copper-cobalt licences in the North-Western province. Anglo will fund exploration over seven years and make cash payments. The move supports longer-term copper supply confidence, but not immediate output.

title: Novelis Plans Minette, Alabama, Recycling And Aluminum Rolling Plant
summary: Novelis plans a Bay Minette, Alabama, integrated aluminum recycling and rolling plant, positioning it to serve beverage can and automotive markets. The company expects to start commissioning in mid-2025 and discusses future capacity expansion above 600kt, signaling longer-dated aluminum supply and demand changes rather than immediate pricing pressure.

title: 10 Gold Stocks that Pay Dividends - Insider Monkey
summary: The piece is mainly about dividend-paying gold stocks and a mild rise in gold after US CPI eased rate-hike fears. It also describes Rio Tinto taking full control of an Australian alumina refinery where Rusal faces sanctions, potentially tightening alumina supply and supporting aluminium prices.

title: Why the 'shocking' price of aluminium matters
summary: The piece highlights aluminium volatility: energy-price pressures and Russia-Ukraine supply tightness have reduced European smelting output and pushed aluminium can and container costs up sharply. It also warns recession fears could cool demand and slow production, creating uncertainty for near-term aluminium availability and pricing.

title: Appeals court upholds previous ruling overturning Forest Service's permit approval for southern Arizona copper mine
summary: A U.S. appeals court upheld a decision overturning the Forest Service’s approval of a Toronto-based company’s permit for the Rosemont open-pit copper mine in southern Arizona. The court found the permit exceeded legal allowances and noted issues around waste-rock storage and mineral value. Conservationists welcomed the ruling.

title: Capstone Copper Reports First Quarter 2022 Results and Provides Consolidated Production and Cost Guidance for the Remainder of 2022
summary: Capstone Copper reported Q1 2022 results and provided consolidated guidance for 2022, forecasting 136,000–150,000 tonnes of copper output at C1 cash costs of $2.55–$2.70/lb. It also detailed ramp-up progress at the Mantos Blancos concentrator and construction of the Mantoverde sulphide project.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Reports First Quarter 2022 Results and Provides Consolidated Production and Cost Guidance for the Remainder of 2022
summary: Capstone Copper reports Q1 2022 results with consolidated copper output of 22,500 tonnes and C1 cash costs of $2.31/lb. The company also outlines progress on ramp-ups and major construction and reiterates 2022 guidance for 136,000–150,000 tonnes of copper at C1 costs of $2.55–$2.70/lb.

title: Inventory of Aluminium Billets Rose 10,100 mt as of May 12_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says China’s domestic aluminium billet inventories rose to 138,700 mt as of May 12, up 10,100 mt week-on-week (+7.84%). Smelter restarts in Yunnan boosted shipments to Foshan, while high conversion margins weighed on demand. Some areas saw poor consumption and inventory growth, though sentiment improved.

title: Aluminium Ingot Inventory Extended Decline_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China’s aluminium ingot social inventory fell to about 1.0 million mt as of May 12, down on the week and sharply vs a year earlier. Shipments were smooth, traders sold more, and inventories dropped in several regions (e.g., Wuxi, Foshan, Hangzhou), reflecting relatively strong demand.

title: Copper Wavers Near $9,000 After Fear-Filled Week For Metals
summary: The article headline says copper is “waving” near $9,000 after a fear-filled week for metals. This points to recent risk-off sentiment and weaker momentum in the copper market, which typically exerts downward pressure on prices in the immediate days following the selloff.

title: The NPI Supply will be Gradually Surplus and the Pure Nickel Supply was still Tight_SMM
summary: SMM says overseas pure nickel remains tight due to import losses, with premiums rising, but it also expects NPI supply to move toward surplus as Indonesia ramps up output. Weak stainless demand and reduced steel mill production are pressuring NPI, with NPI prices and nickel outlook leaning downward.

title: Production and Sales Of Aluminium Plate/Sheet and Strip Likely to Recover From Pandemic in May-June _SMM
summary: SMM says China’s aluminium plate/sheet and strip producers ran at 76.7% in April as COVID restrictions hurt shipping, purchasing, and downstream consumption. Export orders fell as overseas buyers shifted away. With easing in east China, firms expect production and orders to recover in May-June, potentially tightening near-term sentiment for aluminium.

title: The Domestic Alumina Prices Continue to Quote Flat while Overseas Prices Gradually Declined_SMM
summary: SMM says alumina prices are flat domestically but have eased overseas, with FOB Western Australia dropping to about $365/mt. With newly added domestic capacity gradually coming on stream, the market increasingly expects a surplus and further price declines, pending large-scale transaction guidance.

title: The Macro Front and Fundamentals Are Both Relatively Bearish, Aluminium Prices in May May Continue to Be Pressured_SMM
summary: SMM expects bearish near-term aluminium price pressure in May. China’s macro indicators deteriorated and the Fed raised rates by 50 bps. Fundamentals are negative: record operating capacity and higher output, closed import window, and downstream disruption from COVID lower consumption. Marginal power costs provide limited support.

title: SMM Forecast: There Are Signs of Opening of Alumina Import Window, New Production Capacity Will Gradually Be Put into Production, Capping Alumina Prices _SMM
summary: SMM forecasts alumina prices will remain supported as import economics improve (FOB Western Australia decline narrows China–abroad spread) and new capacity ramps in gradually. Pandemic-related transport constraints in northern China disrupted supply, while southwest demand rose with resumed aluminium smelter operations, lifting alumina locally. Prices expected to hold higher-cost support.

title: Discounts of Nickel Salt against Nickel Briquette Narrowed in May as Prices of the Former Were More Resilient to Decline than the Latter_SMM
summary: SMM reports that discounts of battery-grade nickel sulphate versus nickel briquettes narrowed in May. Nickel prices stayed relatively high in April, but nickel salt weakened on poor demand, leading some factories to cut briquette use. Entering May, tighter nickel salt supply reduced the downside more than nickel prices, supporting the spread.

title: Aluminum Warehouse Stocks at Record Low as Tight Supply Persists
summary: The piece highlights that aluminium warehouse stocks are at record lows, reflecting persistently tight physical supply. With inventories strained, market participants face higher near-term availability risk, which tends to lift prompt aluminium premiums and support higher aluminium prices over the coming days.

title: The Fiji Times » Peru community wants its land back, threatening Chinese copper mine
summary: Community protesters occupied Peru’s Las Bambas copper mine near the open pit, forcing production to halt and stretching into a third week with no restart in sight. The mine is cited as supplying about 2% of global copper; expansion plans face further conflict, raising near-term copper supply disruption risk.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 272,000 wmt to 5.37 Million wmt_SMM
summary: SMM reports Chinese nickel ore inventories fell 272,000 wmt to 5.37 million wmt by May 13, with Ni-content stocks down to 42,200 mt. The decline is linked to poor Philippine weather affecting mines and delaying shipments, keeping port inventories historically low and likely limiting near-term supply.

title: Torr Metals Inc.: Torr Acquires All Crown Grants on the Latham Copper-Gold Project
summary: Torr Metals announces it completed the purchase of undersurface crown grants covering the Dalvenie Zone within its Latham Copper-Gold Project in northwest BC. The company touts a kilometer-scale copper-gold-silver exploration target tied to a regional copper-gold porphyry trend and plans near-term data compilation for the 2022 field program.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 2,600 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM data show copper inventories across major Chinese markets fell 2,600 mt WoW to 118,900 mt by May 13, and down versus a year ago. The decline is linked to reduced processor operating rates from pandemic/transport issues and weaker end-week restocking, while supply should rise next week.

title: Copper Inventory in Bonded Area Decreased 2,100 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports domestic bonded copper inventories fell 2,100 mt week-on-week to 327,000 mt as of May 13, with Shanghai down 2,800 mt to 290,000 mt while Guangdong rose slightly. SMM expects further declines due to large import profits and reduced pandemic-era port piles.

title: Aluminum inventories hit a record low and bears didn't blink
summary: The piece flags that aluminium inventories have reached a record low, suggesting tightened near-term physical availability. This type of inventory squeeze often supports prompt pricing as market participants anticipate less stock to draw from in coming days.

title: Aluminum rises on low supply as base metals end fear-filled week
summary: The piece reports that aluminium prices moved higher, attributing the rise to low supply conditions in the market. It frames the move as part of broader base-metal trading after a fear-driven week, suggesting improved short-term supply tightness supported aluminium upward momentum.

title: Chile's climate scientist minister eyes tougher rules for top copper mining nation
summary: Chile’s environment minister Maisa Rojas will push tougher environmental regulation, including new climate legislation with emission caps and mandatory reporting, with added scrutiny on mining operations. As Chile is the leading copper producer, stronger enforcement and adaptation requirements could pressure mining output and increase costs, weighing on copper prices.

title: Mixed Result for Rosemont Copper in Appeals Court Decision
summary: A federal appeals court partially blocked Rosemont Copper’s bid to develop a large open-pit copper mine near Tucson by restricting its ability to dump nearly two billion tons of waste rock on additional Forest Service land. The company can mine on land it owns, but must pursue an alternate compliant plan.

title: Aluminum rises on tight supply signs at end of fear-filled week
summary: The piece highlights that aluminum is rising as the market reads signals of tighter supply at the end of a fear-filled week. Tight supply conditions typically reduce availability and support higher prices over the coming days, keeping near-term sentiment bullish for aluminum.

title: Investors returning to Africa's copper region
summary: The piece says mining investors are returning to the Zambia–DRC border region, an area highlighted as rich in minerals, especially copper used for wires and cables (and cobalt for batteries). Renewed investment appetite can lift short-term copper sentiment by easing risk around future supply projects.

title: Interview with Marcelo Castillo, spokesperson of the Coordinating Committee for the renationalization of Copper and Big Mining in Chile
summary: An interview with Marcelo Castillo discusses Chile’s constitutional process and calls for renationalisation/nationalisation of copper, rejection of mining concessions, and state-led exploration/exploitation with majority state participation. It argues private miners extract profits while causing social and environmental harm, and seeks constitutional norms enabling these changes.

title: The Fiji Times » Chile's climate scientist minister eyes tougher rules for top copper mining nation
summary: Chile’s Environment Minister Maisa Rojas is pushing stronger climate and pollution regulations for mining, including emissions caps and mandatory reporting, in the world’s top copper producer. The plan also ties into drought and water-code changes, potentially increasing compliance burdens and production constraints for miners.

title: Peru: Copper, tin and molybdenum production up in 1Q 2022 | Noticias | Agencia Peruana de Noticias Andina
summary: Peru’s Mining Ministry reported Q1 2022 production rose for copper, with output up 4.2% year-on-year to 553,749 fine metric tons, supported by Antamina, Cerro Verde and Las Bambas. Copper remained the country’s main export metal, with shipments contributing 29.7% of total mining exports.

title: Peru: Copper, tin and molybdenum production up in 1Q 2022 | News | ANDINA
summary: Peru’s Ministry of Energy and Mines reported that 1Q 2022 copper production rose 4.2% year-on-year to 553,749 fine metric tons, driven by Antamina, Cerro Verde and Las Bambas. Copper remains Peru’s main export, with 29.7% share, and higher mining exports supported by stronger demand.

title: Indonesia's Jokowi meets Tesla's Musk after nickel talks
summary: Indonesia’s President Jokowi met Tesla CEO Elon Musk following nickel-related discussions. The meeting implies continued political and business engagement around nickel, relevant to battery supply chains. While the article details are not provided here, such talks are generally supportive of near-term expectations for nickel demand or investment.

title: Indonesia's Jokowi meets Tesla's Musk after nickel talks | Kat Country 98.9
summary: Indonesia’s Jokowi met Tesla CEO Elon Musk in Texas after working-level discussions on potential Tesla investment in Indonesia’s nickel industry and EV battery supply. The talks follow recent large planned investments by LG Energy Solution and CATL, suggesting continued momentum for Indonesia’s nickel-to-batteries value chain.

title: Indonesia's Jokowi meets Tesla's Musk after nickel talks | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Indonesia’s President Jokowi met Tesla CEO Elon Musk in Texas to discuss potential investments, following working-level talks on Tesla’s battery supply plans and Indonesia’s nickel industry. The story cites prior big-ticket deals to expand nickel refining and EV battery cell production, supporting expectations of higher near-term nickel demand.

title: Peru economy grows 3.79% in March, weighed down by mining protests
summary: Peru’s March GDP grew 3.79% y/y but the mining sector shrank due to social conflicts. Protests by indigenous communities have disrupted production, and Southern Copper’s Cuajone mine was halted throughout March. Since Peru is the world’s No. 2 copper producer, the output hit is copper-relevant near term.

title: Jokowi meets Musk after nickel talks
summary: Indonesia’s President Jokowi met Tesla CEO Elon Musk in Texas after working-level talks on potential investments in Indonesia’s nickel industry and EV battery supply. The Indonesian government says the discussions focused on technology and investment, which could support nickel demand/supply outlook and boost nickel prices.

title: Chile copper mines dodge radical changes
summary: Chile’s Constitutional Convention failed to include a proposal that would replace the investor-friendly mining concession model with temporary, revocable permits. With the plan falling short of the two-thirds threshold, immediate political risk to Chile’s copper mining regime appears reduced ahead of a Sept 4 referendum.

title: Operating Rates of Major Aluminium Processing Enterprises Rebounded Slightly amid Recovery of End Demand and Eased Cost Pressure_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates of major aluminium processors increased after Labour Day as pandemic-related logistics improved and downstream end demand started recovering. Extrusion and secondary alloy saw notable gains; wire, cable, and foil also stabilized or rose. Despite weak auto demand in places, expectations are for further rate increases in the coming days.

title: SHFE Aluminium Likely to Rebound Following Digestion of Bearish Events and Accident at a Smelter _SMM
summary: SMM reports bearish macro signals (high US CPI, strong dollar, mixed PMI) have largely been digested. Aluminium fundamentals show easing pressure: downstream resumes post-holiday, buyers restock after spot lows around 19,640 yuan/mt, and inventories keep declining. An aluminium smelter accident could further tighten near-term supply, supporting a rebound in prices.

title: Alumina Prices to Stay at a High Level in the Short Term _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports alumina prices in China remaining high, with the domestic index around 3,016 yuan/mt and a narrowed domestic-versus-FOB WA gap. April imports are expected to stay near 180,000 mt, and sporadic COVID-19 slowed port operations. Smelter restart in Yunnan supports local demand, keeping short-term prices elevated.

title: Aluminum workers furious over USW's last minute deal with Arconic
summary: USW workers at Arconic/Alcoa facilities in Iowa, Tennessee, Indiana and New York are angry at a proposed four-year contract that they view as cutting real wages by removing a pay-for-performance scheme. Workers authorized a strike (May 12) at Davenport Works, raising risk of aluminum production disruption.

title: Copper Prices Bore Pressure from the Macro Factors_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports copper prices under pressure from a rising US dollar and tightening Fed signals. In China, weaker manufacturing/credit and pandemic disruptions hurt terminal demand (cables, construction). Supply appears tight in May but imports are beginning to flow, LME inventories rose, and inventories visible support pessimism. Prices likely trend lower.

title: Aluminium Ingot Social Inventory Extended Decline, Led by Wuxi and Gongyi_SMM
summary: China’s eight major markets reported aluminium ingot social inventories of 984,000 mt on May 16, down on the week and month. Wuxi pickup recovered while Gongyi saw more shipments. Downstream demand is improving, and Yunnan smelter output cuts after an accident helped aluminium prices rebound.

title: Aluminium Smelters' Profits Shrank to 2,000 yuan/mt amid Sharply Falling Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium smelters’ profits fell as aluminium prices dropped sharply. Electricity costs in Yunnan eased slightly with the rainy season, while anode prices rose and overall smelter full costs increased. Alumina faces downward pressure from growing supply, but falling aluminium prices dominate near-term sentiment.

title: Spot Copper Concentrate TCs Dropped from High Levels amid Rising Demand from Domestic Smelters_SMM
summary: SMM reports weekly spot copper concentrate TCs eased to around $79/mt as trading was slack and smelters drew down in-plant inventories amid resuming output at Xiangguang and Fangyuan. Las Bambas remains suspended for community disputes, reducing exports, but high port inventories cap further TC downside, keeping copper impact limited.

title: Arc Minerals forms copper-cobalt JV with Anglo American
summary: Arc Minerals agreed with an Anglo American subsidiary to form a copper-cobalt JV for a project in Zambia. Anglo plans to fund exploration and pay cash totaling up to $88.5 million while retaining up to 70% ownership. The deal is subject to due diligence and definitive agreements, implying limited immediate supply impact.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets up 7,900 mt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s major-market copper inventories rose 7,900 mt WoW to 126,800 mt as arrivals increased over the weekend. Guangdong and Shanghai saw the largest jumps, attributed to higher smelter deliveries and delayed unloading due to weather/logistics. SMM expects inventories may keep rising this week with more imports and stable consumption.

title: OZ Minerals to earn 75% stake in Resolution's Australian copper project
summary: OZ Minerals agreed to earn up to a 75% stake in Resolution’s Benmara copper project in Australia’s Northern Territory via staged exploration spending (initial $1m over two years, then $3m over three years for 51%). A JV would follow if spending targets are met, but no immediate production changes are cited.

title: UPDATE 1-Philippines removes last hurdle for stalled Tampakan copper-gold project
summary: Philippines authorities removed the final regulatory hurdle blocking the stalled Tampakan copper-gold project. The decision improves the likelihood the project can move forward, shifting expectations toward eventual copper supply. While production start dates are not immediate, the news is supportive for copper sentiment in the coming weeks.

title: Canadian North Resources Inc. confirms high-grade nickel-copper massive sulfides and high-grade palladium-platinum low-sulfide mineralization zones at Ferguson Lake Project
summary: Canadian North Resources reports re-sampling and re-assaying results from historic drill cores at its Ferguson Lake project, confirming high-grade copper-nickel massive sulfides and wide low-sulfide PGM mineralization. The findings support resource-estimation confidence, but do not indicate near-term supply changes, implying limited immediate impact on copper and nickel prices.

title: "9th Circuit Keeps Massive Ariz. Copper Mine On Ice"
summary: A U.S. appeals court upheld a ruling invalidating a Forest Service approval for Hudbay’s proposed Rosemont open-pit copper mine in Arizona. The decision halts the mine’s permitting pathway, raising uncertainty over future copper supply and potentially supporting nearby copper price expectations.

title: Nevada Copper Achieves Key Development Milestones: Paste
summary: Nevada Copper reported progress at its Pumpkin Hollow project, including ramping underground hoisting/production, paste plant commissioning with expected throughput by end-June, and higher copper concentrate output in Q1 2022. The prefeasibility study for the permitted open pit project is advancing. Overall, near-term copper production expectations improve.

title: IGO's 'unfair but reasonable' nickel bid approved by proxies
summary: IGO’s proxy advisers urged shareholders to back its $1.26 billion bid to acquire nickel producer Western Areas. The offer was raised to $3.87 per share, though it remains below the fair-value range cited by KPMG’s independent expert. The update may modestly influence nickel sentiment but is not clearly market-moving.

title: London Copper Inventory at a Nearly Seven-Month High, SHFE Copper Inventory Increased slightly_SMM
summary: LME copper inventories climbed for over two months from a 16-year low to a seven-month high of 177,000 mt, then eased slightly to 176,550 mt by May 16. SHFE copper inventories rose 5.89% week-on-week to 55,372 mt, a two-month low, suggesting improving supply levels.

title: Crude Oil Prices Declined and Copper Prices Rose Slightly_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports the INE bonded copper 2207 contract rose overnight, closing at 63,280 yuan/mt (+0.80%). Copper strength was linked to a crude oil rebound and concerns about policy-driven growth risks as US Treasury yields fell. Prices are expected to trade around 63,300–63,600 yuan/ton today.

title: Will Recent Rally Sustain After SHFE Aluminum Recorded Five Consecutive Days of Gains?_SMM
summary: Favourable COVID policies and improving Shanghai conditions boosted market confidence. Falling aluminium ingot social inventories in China’s major markets and a Yunnan smelter cutting production after an accident supported sentiment. SHFE aluminium recorded five straight gain days, with expectations of further short-term rebound, though longer-term upside depends on consumption recovery.

title: Nickel Prices May Be Pressured in the Short Term Despite Supply Tightness_SMM
summary: SMM reports pure nickel supply stayed tight in April but downstream demand weakened due to COVID-19 disruptions. Spot activity improved only when prices fell at end-month, while nickel briquette remained scarce yet trades stagnated. For May, tight supply persists but weak demand and macro factors are expected to pressure prices downward.

title: Domestic Alumina Market Remained in a Deadlock _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s domestic alumina prices staying flat at 3,014 yuan/mt as negotiations stall. North China supply increased, while buyers sought significantly lower prices, but sellers resisted due to rising costs. With supply and pricing expectations stuck, trading volumes and the regional weighted index showed no day-on-day change.

title: Emirates Global Aluminium starts up DX+ Ultra reduction cell technology
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium says it has successfully started up DX+ Ultra reduction cell technology at 500kA, a first for the Middle East. Higher amperage is expected to lift production by about 5% versus current operating limits, supporting potline upgrades and future capacity expansion.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Targets Large Scale Nickel Potential of Carman-Langmuir Area
summary: EV Nickel reports extensive historical exploration at its Carman–Langmuir area near Timmins, identifying long dunite–peridotite units with nickel grades above 0.25% and thickness to at least 250m depth in records. The company plans late-spring surface sampling and expects drilling permits in coming weeks.

title: LME Aluminium Inventories Hit a New Low in Nearly 17 Years, SHFE Aluminium Inventories Fell to a Seven-Month Low_SMM
summary: LME data shows aluminium inventories declining steadily since mid-February, reaching 532,500 mt on May 16—the lowest in nearly 17 years. SHFE aluminium inventories also fell 16.33% week-on-week to 246,931 mt as of May 13, the lowest in seven months, signaling tighter supply.

title: NBS: China's April Primary Aluminium Production Hit a Record High_SMM
summary: China’s April primary aluminium production rose to 3.36 million mt, a record high, as eased power rationing allowed smelters to expand to full capacity by month-end. Domestic operating capacity is expected to rise in May with plans to resume and new capacity coming online, supporting higher supply despite early-2024 output weakness.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums were Stable with some Downward Potential amid Closed Import Window_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums at $62–84/mt, averaging $73/mt, slightly lower day-on-day, with import losses near 600 yuan/mt on the 2206 contract. A closed import window and low price ratio reduced offers and inquiries, and transactions were limited as market participants wait for logistics to resume in June.

title: EnGold Mines Ltd.: EnGold Drills 655 Metres of 0.14% Copper Equivalent at Ann North, Deep Hole at Aurizon Gold at 1200 Metres and Still Underway
summary: EnGold Mines reported assays from deep drilling at its Lac La Hache property in BC, including hole AN22-05 intersecting 655m of 0.14% CuEq with chalcopyrite and bornite, plus indications of copper-bearing mineralization at depth in another hole. Results are exploration-focused with assays pending elsewhere.

title: After legal setbacks on Rosemont mine, copper company starts work
summary: Hudbay Minerals began site work at its Copper World and Rosemont copper projects in Arizona after recent legal setbacks, including surrendering a Clean Water Act permit.
