Opponents allege it is illegal and await further court decisions. Hudbay says it plans to extract copper, supporting potential near-term supply expectations.

title: Nickel: How Government Alchemists Turned a Base Money "Hard" and Now Are Expected to Kill It.
summary: The article links recent nickel market “chaos” and extreme price spikes to US government actions, including increased nickel demand from war footing and sanctions reducing supply, alongside tighter credit/liquidity conditions tied to Federal Reserve policy. It frames nickel as both an industrial metal and a monetary metaphor, with no clear near-term directional call.

title: Leading Edge Materials Signs Exploration License for Romanian Nickel and Cobalt Project
summary: Leading Edge Materials says it has signed an exploration license for its Romanian nickel and cobalt project. The news is a development toward potential future supply, but as it concerns exploration rather than production, it is unlikely to materially alter near-term nickel market balances or pricing expectations within days to four weeks.

title: Lion Copper and Gold Announces Agreement for Stage One Work Program with Rio Tinto and Commencement of Permitting Process
summary: Lion Copper and Gold announced final Stage 1 agreement with Rio Tinto, including $3.75m funding for permitting, studies, metallurgical testing, and a planned 6,500-ft drill program at its MacArthur and Yerington copper deposits. The company also started environmental permitting with the U.S. Bureau of Land Management.

title: Lion Copper and Gold Corp.: Lion Copper and Gold Announces Agreement for Stage One Work Program with Rio Tinto and Commencement of Permitting Process
summary: Lion Copper and Gold announced a final Stage 1 work program agreement with Rio Tinto for its Mason Valley MacArthur and Yerington projects. Rio Tinto will fund US$3.75 million for permitting, studies, metallurgical testing, and a 6,500-ft drill program, supporting progress toward copper production.

title: Decks cleared for Midhani to set up aluminium alloy plant in Nellore
summary: Legal issues over land acquisition have been resolved for MIDHANI to set up an aluminium alloy plant at Bodduvaripalem near Nellore with NALCO. The project investment is Rs 2,500–3,000 crore and construction can start. It signals additional aluminium processing demand, mainly a medium-term support factor.

title: The INE Bonded Copper Contract Prices Rebounded amid Improved Market Sentiment_SMM
summary: SMM reports the INE bonded copper 2207 contract rose overnight, closing at 63,420 yuan/mt (+130). It links the rebound to improved Shanghai pandemic conditions boosting market confidence and to expectations of additional government policies to stimulate growth. Trading saw modest volume and slightly lower open interest.

title: Imported Copper Market in Shanghai Bonded Zone Was Subdued amid Closed Import Profit Window, But Traders Held Offers Firmly _SMM
summary: Shanghai bonded zone imported copper trading was subdued as the import profit window closed. Yangshan premiums were below prior levels (under warrants $62-84/mt; under B/L $49-70/mt) and import losses were about 500 yuan/mt vs SHFE 2206. With logistics expected to recover, sellers held offers, while buyers avoided deals.

title: Spot Transactions of Nickel were Poor amid Weak Downstream Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports weak spot nickel trading, with lower activity tied to declining procurement expectations from alloy plants. Jinchuan nickel premiums rise slightly, but NORNICKEL prices and briquette premiums are firmer or falling, and nickel briquette transactions are nearly absent due to weaker economy versus intermediate products.

title: OZ looks to buy Havilah's South Australian copper project for $144m
summary: OZ Minerals signed a terms sheet to option Havilah’s Kalkaroo copper project in South Australia for A$205m over 18 months, including required drilling or a shortfall payment. The deal includes copper price-linked contingent payments and a copper exploration alliance, supporting near-term copper market sentiment.

title: Copper prices fall on lingering global slowdown worries
summary: Copper fell 1.1% as markets renewed worries about global slowdown after hawkish Fed signals and weak China data tied to Shanghai COVID lockdown impacts. The stronger dollar pressured dollar-priced metals. LME aluminum and nickel also declined, reflecting broad risk-off sentiment toward industrial metal demand.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: US EV Battery Supply Chain: Talon Metals Releases Record Length of High-Grade Nickel Mineralization at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals announced additional infill drilling results at its Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in Minnesota, including a record 23.44 m massive sulphide intercept of nickel and copper (assays pending). The company plans to complete infill drilling for a pre-feasibility study and references a Tesla nickel supply agreement.

title: China CNGR expands nickel investments in Indonesia to meet EV demand
summary: CNGR will invest $1.26 billion in three nickel-matte projects in Indonesia’s Weda Bay, raising annual capacity by 120,000 tonnes (40,000 tonnes nickel content each). Nickel matte is processed into battery-grade nickel for EV batteries. Investments are meant to secure inputs and lower costs, likely affecting nickel supply expectations.

title: Update of Mining Activities at TVIRD's 60% owned Agata Nickel/Iron Mine, Agata Mining Ventures Inc.
summary: The page content appears to be a privacy/cookie notice rather than the operational update itself. The title references an update to mining activities at TVIRD’s Agata nickel/iron mine. Operational changes at a nickel asset can influence short-term nickel supply expectations, but no directional production details are shown here.

title: 2 men charged in Natchitoches plywood mill copper theft
summary: Two men were arrested for allegedly stealing copper wire from Roy O. Martin Plywood Plant in Louisiana. Supervisors found trespassing at an area where copper wiring and metal items are stored; police seized about $750 worth of copper wire and equipment used to strip it. The theft investigation continues.

title: Copper premiums in Asia, Europe increase; US market flat amid quiet conditions
summary: The article notes that copper premiums in Asia and Europe have increased, while the US market is flat amid quiet conditions. It also describes delays and corrections to Fastmarkets’ European low-carbon aluminium differential and certain aluminium billet premium assessments due to procedural errors, implying data housekeeping rather than a clear new supply-demand shock.

title: Demand Recovery from Pandemic to Drive a Rally in SHFE Aluminium _SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium fell for two days amid pessimistic sentiment, weak spot demand, and a rising US dollar. Costs were steady as alumina talks stalled. A smelter reduced output after an accident, helping prices rebound, but demand remains subdued. Prices may rise again if pandemic-linked demand recovers.

title: The Decline of Aluminium Ingot Inventory Drives Bulls to Enter the Market and SHFE Aluminium Rebounded by 1%_SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium rebounded about 1% and prices rose above 20,600 yuan/mt as east China spot aluminium ingot inventories fell by 38,000 mt to 965,000 mt and billet stocks declined. The Zhongyuan spot discount narrowed sharply on lower ingot supply and steady downstream acceptance demand, drawing new long positions.

title: CNGR, Rigqueza Invest USD1.3 Billion to Hike Nickel Ore Processing Capacity in Indonesia
summary: CNGR and Rigqueza plan to invest $1.3 billion in Indonesia to build three nickel-processing plants at Weda Bay, producing 40,000 tons of high-grade nickel matte annually each. The matte is used to make nickel sulfate for battery precursors. No construction timetable was provided.

title: Aluminium Billet Inventory Recorded Weekly Decline of 2,300 mt as of May 19_SMM
summary: SMM reported domestic aluminium billet inventories at 136,400 mt as of May 19, down 2,300 mt (1.66%) on the week. Regional inventories were mixed, with notable declines in Wuxi and Foshan. Downstream buyers increased purchases after aluminium price and conversion-margin drops, supporting destocking.

title: SMM Analysis: How Will the Prices of Nickel Briquette Move amid Fierce Competition for Nickel Sulphate Raw Materials? _SMM
summary: SMM reports that high raw-material costs are stressing nickel sulphate manufacturers using dissolving nickel briquette and imported MHP. When nickel briquette prices trade above nickel sulphate, some sulphate plants cut briquette sales, lowering briquette spot premiums versus NORNICKEL nickel. Demand use in stainless/alloys appears limited, muting price signals.

title: EGA site recertified to Aluminium Stewardship Initiative
summary: EGA reports that one of its aluminium production sites has been recertified to the Aluminium Stewardship Initiative. The update is likely to strengthen sustainability credentials and market access for the aluminium produced, which can modestly support expectations for aluminium demand or pricing, though no direct supply shock is mentioned.

title: Alcoa Announces Long-Term Contract for Renewable Power to Support 2024 Restart of San Ciprián Aluminum Smelter
summary: Alcoa signed a long-term renewable power purchase agreement with Greenalia to support the planned 2024 restart of its San Ciprián aluminum smelter in Spain. The deal would supply up to 183 MW for baseload electricity (~45% of needed power at full capacity), helping replace curtailed operations.

title: Chakana Copper Corp.: Chakana Announces Private Placement, Gold Fields to Follow Its Participation Rights
summary: Chakana Copper Corp. announced a non-brokered private placement to fund exploration and development of its Soledad copper-gold-silver project in Peru, plus working capital. It also notes an inferred resource including 130 million pounds of copper. The financing is unlikely to materially affect near-term copper supply.

title: China Primary Aluminium Net Imports Stood at 2,842 mt in Apr, down 98.2% YoY_SMM
summary: China’s primary aluminium net imports fell to 2,842.6 mt in April, down 98.2% year-on-year. April imports declined sharply versus last year, while exports were also lower month-on-month but higher versus a very low base. The reduced net import flow may limit near-term supply.

title: Aluminium Downstream Operating Rates Recovered Slightly from the Pandemic, but Some Sectors Reported Insufficient Orders _SMM
summary: SMM says major aluminium processing operating rates rose slightly week-on-week to 59.1%, helped by improving COVID conditions and transport in eastern China. However, many sectors remained stable due to insufficient orders and cautious downstream ordering, with some producers expecting limited gains. Auto demand weakness and logistics/frieght pressure persist.

title: Column: Nickel demand boomed in 2021; this year it will be supply
summary: The article says nickel demand surged 16.2% in 2021, creating a 168,000-tonne supply shortfall. For 2022, usage is expected to rise 8.6% but global production is forecast to jump 18.2% on Indonesia’s new capacity, moving toward a modest surplus and likely lower LME prices, though Class I supply remains disputed.

title: Russia Exported 2.93 million mt of Primary Aluminium in 2021_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Russia exported about 2.938 million mt of primary aluminium in 2021, mainly to Europe and Asia. With Rusal as a major producer and low-carbon output supported by hydropower, Russia’s export flows are highlighted as influential to global aluminium supply expectations. The piece links broader 2022 trade frictions and tight market sentiment.

title: Declining Aluminium Inventory across China and Indonesia's Banning of Export Bauxite Boosted SHFE Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium prices stabilized higher on the day, helped by a week-on-week decline in China social inventories and firmer spot demand. The article also cites Indonesia’s planned 2022 ban on bauxite exports as a catalyst expected to increase alumina costs, though noting the policy is not yet fully implemented and timing is uncertain.

title: Outraged Arconic aluminum workers speak out against USW's contract proposal: "It's a bad deal!"
summary: Arconic aluminum workers at several plants express anger over a below-inflation USW contract proposal, arguing raises do not keep up with high inflation and bonuses are inadequate. Workers signal readiness to strike, with heightened protest activity around the Davenport Works plant, raising short-term supply disruption risk for aluminum.

title: All Metals Prices Rose and SHFE Nickel Rose by more than 5% _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that in early Shanghai trading, SHFE nickel rose 5.36%, while SHFE aluminium gained 1.69% and SHFE copper rose 0.66%. The broader move coincided with a firmer US dollar, expanding Fed balance sheet, hawkish Fed comments, and crude oil weakness tied to growth concerns.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 6,900 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM data shows copper inventories in major Chinese markets fell 6,900 mt to 119,900 mt week-on-week, with declines in Guangdong and Tianjin outweighing slight rises in Shanghai and Zhejiang. Supply was constrained by logistics/rail issues, though next week imported arrivals may increase.

title: SHFE Aluminium Rose Again and the Short-term Market Improved_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE 2201 aluminium opened at 20,850 yuan/mt and closed at 20,820 yuan/mt, up 0.94%. The rise is linked to a recent decline in the US dollar index and domestic demand stimulus that encouraged restocking, improving short-term sentiment.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums were Stable with some Downward Potential amid a Dropping Price Ratio_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums of $69–85/mt under warrants, averaging $77/mt, down $1 from the prior day. Import losses widened as LME copper inventories fell and carrying fees rose. The market remains sluggish, despite warrant traders’ willingness to ship; no transactions were reported.

title: The Exports of Aluminium Wheels were Weak amid Pandemic and Sluggish Demand_SMM
summary: China’s aluminium wheel exports fell in April 2022, down 10% month on month and 15% year on year, per customs data. Demand from the automotive sector stayed weak and pandemic disruptions in east China hurt production and shipments. SMM expects May-June exports to drop further and annual volumes to remain relatively low.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports down 7,000 wmt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 7,000 wmt week-on-week to 5.363 million wmt (total Ni content -50 wmt). The decline stems mainly from reduced Philippines shipments due to poor weather, alongside faster consumption by low-inventory NPI plants. Further Philippines shipment developments are watched.

title: Copper edges up on China mortgage rate cut and lockdown easing
summary: Copper prices inched higher as China cut mortgage rates by more than expected and continued progress on easing COVID lockdowns, boosting optimism for a demand rebound. LME three-month copper rose slightly and was on track for a weekly gain, reversing earlier declines tied to fears over China’s growth and global recession.

title: Work suspended at Botswana's Khoemacau copper mine after accident kills two
summary: Operations were suspended at Botswana’s Khoemacau Zone 5 underground copper-silver mine after an accident killed two workers. The company said investigations are ongoing and that output will be halted temporarily. Given it is the country’s only operational copper mine, the disruption can reduce near-term copper supply expectations.

title: What Might Tesla's Nickel-Mining Deals Suggest About Future Strategy?
summary: Tesla’s new long-term contract with Vale to secure Class 1 nickel supply for EV battery production, plus a published list of nickel (and cobalt) suppliers, signals tighter, more contracted nickel sourcing. This can support nickel demand expectations in the near term, especially as EV growth raises battery-material competition.

title: UK may impose duties of up to 29% on Chinese aluminium extrusions
summary: Britain’s Trade Remedies Authority may impose provisional anti-dumping duties up to 29% on Chinese aluminium extrusions, citing price undercutting and “damage” to domestic producers. Chinese exporters would need bank guarantees from May 28 while the investigation continues, with recommended duties varying by company and dumping margin.

title: Aston Minerals produces saleable concentrate from Boomerang nickel-cobalt samples
summary: Aston Minerals says metallurgical testing of nickel-cobalt sulphide samples from its Boomerang target produced saleable concentrate using conventional flotation. The head grades were ~0.51% nickel and 0.016% cobalt, with concentrate grading up to 11.29% nickel. Further optimization work is planned as analysis continues.

title: Nickel Prices will Probably Drop this Week due to the Customs Clearance of Spots_SMM
summary: SMM says nickel is likely to fall this week. Weak demand and limited bonded-zone customs clearance have kept pure nickel tight, but the import window should lead to more customs clearances. NPI and nickel-sulphate input costs are pressured by lower LME nickel, while stainless-steel downstream activity remains subdued.

title: Sales of Copper Wires and Cables in Japan Decreased by 3.1% in April YoY_SMM
summary: Japan’s Electric Wire and Cable Makers’ Association data show April sales of copper wire and cables (domestic plus exports) fell 3.1% year-on-year to 52,100 mt. The drop signals softer demand for copper inputs in the short term, which can weigh on copper price expectations over the next few weeks.

title: China Aluminium Imports Fell 73.1% YoY in April, While Exports Surged 640%_SMM
summary: China’s primary aluminium imports fell sharply in April (down 77.6% YoY) while exports surged (up ~640% YoY). Limited European aluminium supply from energy problems and constrained Rusal exports boosted overseas demand. With import windows loss widening and reduced orders from COVID, tighter flows supported repeated LME aluminium record highs.

title: Koba Resources moves closer to maiden drilling at Blackpine cobalt-copper project
summary: Koba Resources has started an induced polarisation survey at its Blackpine cobalt-copper project to generate targets for maiden drilling. The soil and historical drilling results show cobalt-copper anomalism and high-grade intersections. The company also plans drilling at its Colson project. No production or supply impact is specified.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 10,100 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s major market copper inventories fell 10,100 mt on the week to 109,800 mt, with declines in Shanghai and Guangdong attributed to reduced imported arrivals and stronger downstream pickup, while Guangdong fell on transport disruptions. Inventories are expected to drop slightly further as imports and domestic supply improve.

title: SHFE Aluminium to Move up amid Continued Decline in Social Inventory   _SMM
summary: SMM says SHFE and LME aluminium are likely to rise this week as social inventories in China keep falling and downstream activity recovers slightly. It notes a Yunnan smelter shutdown and restarts, Rusal ingot inflows, and growing concern over a potential Indonesia bauxite export ban that may lift alumina and aluminium costs.

title: Aluminium Costs Remained High_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports average aluminium smelter costs fell slightly to 18,239 yuan/mt as alumina prices eased, while profits rose. Lower power costs from Yunnan’s rainy season helped, but an upcoming electricity-demand peak in east and south China may lift coal/energy prices. Overall, aluminium costs are expected to rise short term.

title: IAI: Global Primary Aluminium Production in April was 5.599 Million mt_SMM
summary: SMM cites International Aluminium Institute (IAI) data showing global primary aluminium production of 5.599 million tonnes in April, with China accounting for about 3.29 million tonnes. The figures inform short-term supply expectations for aluminium markets, but the excerpt lacks comparison to prior months or demand context.

title: Alumina Prices Diverged between North and South China, with Eyes on the Amount and Sustainability of Exports _SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s alumina prices slightly down week-on-week, with declines in north China but stability in parts of southwest China. April exports jumped sharply, and continued high exports could reduce domestic surplus and slow further price drops. North supply improved post-transport recovery, while some bauxite tightness raised costs.

title: Weak dollar, China demand hopes lift copper to over 2-week high
summary: Copper prices climbed to a more than two-week high on a weaker U.S. dollar and improving China demand expectations as lockdown easing and mortgage rate cuts were seen supporting property activity. Shanghai copper also rose amid falling SHFE inventories. LME aluminium gained as well, suggesting broader industrial-metals uplift.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums were Stable with some Downward Potential due to the Import Losses_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums at about $70–83/mt, averaging ~$77/mt, with slight softness versus the prior day. Import losses estimated around 550 yuan/mt over the 2206 copper contract suppressed buying interest, keeping premiums stable but with some downward potential amid backwardation.

title: SHFE Aluminium Hovered at a High level with Spot Premiums Falling_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium staying elevated around 20,800-21,000 yuan/mt. Aluminium ingot inventories fell to 941,000 mt (down 24,000 mt from May 19), with sharp declines in Wuxi and Gongyi. Spot prices remained discounted but discounts narrowed and then widened modestly as rigid producer buying outpaced weaker downstream demand.

title: Alumina Market Tilted Further to a Buyer's Market amid Continued Price Drop in Shanxi_SMM
summary: Shanxi alumina prices continued falling, pushing the market further into a buyer’s mode. SMM attributes weakness to export disruptions, including Australia’s ban on alumina exports to Russia, which diverted supply into overseas markets. The article notes falling FOB Western Australia prices and domestic alumina index declines.

title: China's Primary Aluminium Exports in April Fell 24.2% on the Month, up 64 Times on the Year_SMM
summary: China’s April primary aluminium exports fell 24.2% month-on-month to 32,034 mt, with tariff 76011010 exports at 333.8 mt and tariff 76011090 imports at 31,700.3 mt. January–April exports rose sharply year-on-year, but the April drop points to reduced export flows.

title: LME Aluminium Inventories Kept Falling and Refreshed the Lowest in 17 Years_SMM
summary: LME data cited by SMM shows aluminium inventories have steadily fallen since mid-February, reaching 504,275 mt on May 20—the lowest level in 17 years. SHFE aluminium inventories also declined to 288,801 mt, a two-and-a-half-month low, indicating ongoing destocking that can tighten near-term supply.

title: Rising Supply Of Nickel Intermediary Products Could Ease Tig...
summary: China’s imports of nickel intermediaries MHP and matte hit record levels in April, helped by faster NPI-to-matte conversion and ramped MHP supply from Indonesia. With supply feeding sulphate production and incentives to convert into exchange-deliverable Class 1 nickel rising, availability could improve and LME nickel prices/spreads face downside pressure.

title: Chile to Cushion the Blow of Glacier Ban on Giant Copper Mines
summary: The piece signals Chile will take measures to offset a glacier ban that would constrain operations at large copper mines. Any near-term limits on mine access, production, or permitting can raise concerns about reduced copper supply, shifting market expectations toward tighter availability and price pressure on copper.

title: Primary Nickel May Enter Supply Surplus amid Market Weakness_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says some spot pure nickel from SHFE 2205 deliveries eased China’s supply tightness, causing NORNICKEL premiums to drop sharply and Russian nickel prices to fall. NPI supply is also rising with Indonesia’s Delong ramp, while demand remains weak under pandemic recovery. Downward pressure persists despite low inventories.

title: LME Copper Climbed to the Highest Level in Nearly Two Weeks amid Falling US Dollar Index_SMM
summary: LME copper rose to its highest level in nearly two weeks, closing up 1.17%, while SHFE also gained. Support came from a weaker US dollar, improving consumption expectations, tighter Chinese cathode spot supply, and declining LME/SHFE and regional inventories. Spot premiums are expected to stay firm.

title: Taruga Minerals confirms ionic adsorption clay REE at Mt Craig copper project
summary: Taruga confirms ionic adsorption clay rare earth mineralisation at its Mt Craig copper project and plans further REE drilling. Separately, at the Meekatharra nickel-copper project, Peak completed an aircore program that intersected broad, “highly encouraging” nickel zones, including 17m at 0.29% Ni and 10m at 0.32% Ni.

title: Minister: TSTT to complete shift from copper to wireless by end of August
summary: Trinidad and Tobago’s TSTT faces rising theft and vandalism of copper cables, which the minister says intensified alongside higher international copper prices. TSTT plans to shift all remaining customers from its copper network to wireless/fibre by end-August, having moved about 100,000 so far, and begins removing disused copper lines.

title: Pure Nickel Premiums Dropped amid Weak Downstream Purchasing_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says pure nickel spot premiums weakened: Jinchuan nickel averaged 9,500 yuan/mt, down 1,500 yuan/mt from the prior day, due to soft downstream buying. Nornickel premiums were steady. Nickel briquette quotes rose on firmer nickel futures, but cost-efficiency issues for nickel sulphate weighed on trading.

title: SMM is Pessimistic over Aluminium Plate/Sheet and Strip Export in May-June after Mild MoM Growth in April_SMM
summary: SMM cites customs data showing China’s aluminium plate/sheet and strip exports at 329,000 mt in April (+1% MoM, +52% YoY). Despite April growth, SMM surveys indicate export orders fell from April because of pandemic disruptions in east China and softer overseas demand, suggesting May–June exports may be below April.

title: Global Battery Metals Granted Four New Mineral Leases to Expand its Michigan Nickel-Copper Project
summary: Global Battery Metals was granted four new surface and mineral leases in Michigan, expanding its Sawyer Camp nickel-copper exploration area. The company plans electromagnetic surveys to guide drilling targeting mafic-ultramafic intrusions potentially hosting nickel and copper mineralization. No production or reserve update is provided.

title: Benjamin Hill Mining Corp.: Benjamin Hill Announces Initial Drill Results from the Sonora Project Indicating a High-Grade Copper System near Surface
summary: Benjamin Hill Mining reported initial diamond-drilling results from its Sonora Copper Zone in Mexico, including multiple copper-bearing intercepts (e.g., up to 1.2% Cu over 6m and 0.55% Cu over 26.54m) confirming continuity of mineralized veins. The company expects further assays to support copper potential.

title: Drones and micro-dotting proposed for fighting rampant copper theft
summary: Gauteng authorities say rampant infrastructure theft is rising as demand for copper pushes prices higher. Copper is allegedly smelted, mixed with legitimate supply, and exported with manipulated customs declarations. The city is considering drones and micro-dot tracing to curb theft amid rolling blackouts.

title: New Long-Lasting Tesla Battery Now Being Studied; LFP To Have a New Nickel-Based Power Cell Competitor
summary: Tesla is studying a long-lasting nickel-based EV battery (NMC) with research results published in May, claiming longevity up to 100 years and comparable performance to LFP cells. While still experimental and not tied to immediate scaling, the work implies potential future nickel demand and supports a mild bullish bias for nickel prices.

title: TG Metals makes ASX debut to advance nickel exploration at Lake Johnston
summary: TG Metals begins trading on the ASX to fund exploration at its Lake Johnston Greenstone Belt projects in Western Australia. The company plans aggressive geophysical work and drilling to define nickel-cobalt oxide resources, including a near-term Bremer Range laterite target and other nickel prospects over the next two years.

title: Domestic Aluminum Demand Continues to Grow; Up 5.3% in First Quarter
summary: The piece reports that domestic aluminum demand continues to grow, rising 5.3% in the first quarter. The implied increase in near-term consumption supports expectations of tighter aluminum supply-demand conditions, which typically provides upward price pressure for aluminum in the short run.

title: Hudbay Receives Favourable U.S. District Court Ruling on Copper World
summary: Hudbay said a U.S. District Court ruled in its favor over the Copper World project in Arizona, dismissing a preliminary injunction request and clarifying that the Army Corps of Engineers has no obligation to include Copper World in Rosemont’s NEPA review. Hudbay continues early works, drilling, and expects a PEA in Q2 2022.

title: After nickel-gate, Esma may seek data from more non-EU CCPs
summary: EU supervisor ESMA says it may request more granular exposure data from additional non-EU CCPs after the March “nickel-gate” episode on the London Metal Exchange, when all nickel contracts were cancelled. It warns current oversight could leave regulators unprepared for future LME-style disruptions affecting nickel markets.

title: Gold Fields Acquires Units of Chakana Copper Corp.
summary: Gold Fields’ acquisition of units of Chakana Copper Corp suggests increased ownership and development focus on copper assets. While deal-specific production timing is not provided, the transaction can improve market expectations for copper supply prospects and support copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Copper: Longer Term Bullish
summary: A technical report on Comex copper argues for a longer-term bullish bias, citing shallow consolidation and improving chart structure. It highlights a bullish trigger above ~$5.06 and confirmation above $5.17, with expectations for a breakout toward $7.00 and potentially beyond, framing the move as a constructive setup.

title: SHFE Aluminium Moving Downwards, The Market Purchased Aluminium Ingot Spot on Rigid Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports LME aluminium down over 2% and SHFE aluminium falling to around 20,400 yuan/mt. East China spot remains at a small discount, while central China prices rebound on tighter arrivals and rigid downstream demand, with premiums. Overall, futures weakness dominates the immediate tone.

title: SMM Forecast for Short-Term and Long-Term Aluminium Prices amid Low Inventory and Growing Supply _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium down 1.99% after three gains, while inventories continue to fall. China social aluminium inventories and LME stocks hit recent lows, providing support. Supply grew more slowly, despite a Yunnan smelter shutdown, and stable smelter operations persist. Short-term low inventories are expected to underpin prices.

title: Brazil lowers import duties by another 10%; steel cut to 9.6%, aluminium to 4.8%
summary: Brazil reduced import duties for steel and aluminium, with aluminium duties cut to 4.8% from 5.4% (for included product types) effective June 1 through year-end. The move aims to curb inflation and broaden Mercosur trade. Lower duties can lift aluminium import competitiveness, pressuring near-term prices.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Receives Exploration Permit for Phase 3 Drilling and Initiates Surface Sampling in Carman-Langmuir Area
summary: EV Nickel says it received an exploration permit for Phase 3 drilling and started surface sampling at its Carman-Langmuir ultramafic targets near Timmins, Ontario. Historic work shows elevated nickel grades, and the company plans further drilling in summer. The update is exploration-focused with no near-term output impact stated.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Commences Construction on All Season Access Road for the Kenbridge Nickel Project, Kenora Mining District, Northwestern Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. announced it has begun construction of an all-season access road into the Kenbridge Nickel Project in northwestern Ontario, with permits allowing maintenance and upgrades such as brushing, ditching, graveling, and culverts. Completion is expected by September 2022, supporting project development and future nickel operations.

title: Nine Mile Metals Ltd.: Nine Mile Metals Announces Completion of Drill Program (Phase 1) and Reports Visible, Massive High-Grade Copper VMS Mineralization at Its Flagship Nine Mile Brook VMS Project
summary: Nine Mile Metals announced completion of its Phase 1 drill program at the Nine Mile Brook VMS project, reporting visual high-grade VMS mineralization in drill core with copper (chalcopyrite) plus lead/zinc. The company plans BHEM surveys and ALS-certified assays shortly; no confirmed production or supply impact is stated.

title: Shadowbriar Acquires Benada Aluminum Products
summary: Shadowbriar Capital Partners’ affiliate acquired controlling ownership of Benada Aluminum Products, a Florida-based aluminum extruder with three extrusion lines and a paint line. The deal terms were not disclosed. The update is about ownership and potential growth, without specific near-term capacity or market impact details.

title: Low Inventories Still Underpin Nickel Prices Despite Sluggish Downstream Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports weak downstream demand and declining nickel sulphate prices due to softer raw-material costs and limited alloy buying. However, short-term pure nickel inventories remain low and support prices, while Indonesian Delong NPI commissioning is progressing and some supply restarts. Overall, nickel is expected not to drop sharply.

title: China Primary Nickel Supply Surplus Estimated at 140,000 mt in Ni content in 2022_SMM
summary: SMM reports CITIC Futures’ view that China’s nickel market has faced weak demand amid high LME nickel prices and pandemic-related drag. However, with improving nickel affordability and rising Indonesia NPI and nickel-salt feedstock supply, primary nickel is expected to run a ~140,000 mt Ni-content surplus, suggesting bearish near-term pricing pressure.

title: Spot Premiums of Aluminium Ingot Rose in Some Areas amid the SHFE Most-Traded Contract Delivery_SMM
summary: SMM reports the SHFE most-traded aluminium contract moving with tight early-session fluctuations. LME aluminium fell and spot prices in east China stayed slightly discounted, but in central China aluminium ingot premiums rose. Thin arrivals and a 26,000 mt inventory decline supported rigid downstream demand, keeping premiums stable.

title: Biden administration announces effort to stop Pebble copper and gold mine from being built
summary: The Biden administration announced efforts aimed at preventing the Pebble copper and gold project from being built. If the mine is blocked, markets may price in tighter long-run copper supply expectations, which typically turns sentiment bearish for copper over the coming days to weeks.

title: SMM Weekly Survey of China Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventory as of May 26_SMM
summary: SMM’s survey shows China aluminium ingot social inventories at 936,000 mt, down 29,000 mt WoW, helped by lower arrivals in Wuxi and slower declines elsewhere, with tight transport capacity limiting future inflows. Aluminium billet inventories also fell WoW, though Foshan arrivals stayed high amid weak consumption.

title: Chinese alumina exports to Russia surge in April
summary: Chinese alumina exports to Russia jumped more than 12-fold in April, with Russia likely to keep buying as sanctions limit alternative raw-material sources. Rusal has lost about 40% of its alumina supply since Ukraine’s invasion, and Australia banned alumina/bauxite exports to Russia, tightening feedstock availability.

title: Alumina Prices in Shanxi still in Downward Trajectory amid Growing Market Pessimism _SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanxi logistics largely recovered, but alumina prices still slid another 5 yuan/mt to 2,890–2,950 yuan/mt due to high inventories and market pessimism. North China remains a buyers’ market; further falls are possible if exports disappoint. In the southwest, alumina is supported by aluminium smelter production resumption.

title: Prices Spreads Continued to Expand and the INE Bonded Copper Contract Remained High_SMM
summary: SMM reports that most INE bonded copper 2207 trading trended downward on May 26, finishing at 63,380 yuan/mt. Macro concerns about inflation and interest-rate hikes hurting economic growth kept copper under pressure. The INE after-tax equivalent versus SHFE 2207 widened, with the spread expanding to about 539 yuan/mt.

title: Camino Minerals Corp: Drilling Commences at New Lourdes-Condori Copper Zones at Los Chapitos, Peru
summary: Camino Minerals says core drilling has started on newly permitted Lourdes-Condori copper zones at its Los Chapitos project in Peru. The company reports near-surface high-grade copper targets, visible copper oxides in road cuts, and additional access work for other copper prospects, potentially supporting future resource delineation and discoveries.

title: Manna Capital Partners to Broaden Access to U.S. Aluminum Can Sheet Production and Recycling in Alliance with Ball
summary: The headline says Manna Capital Partners plans to broaden access to U.S. aluminum can sheet production and recycling through an alliance with Ball. If capacity or supply access increases, it could ease near-term aluminum supply expectations, but the article body provides no capacity/timeline details, limiting confidence in any price direction.

title: Federal agency can't regulate pollution rules on Copper World project
summary: A federal court ruled that Hudbay Minerals can continue stream filling for its Copper World copper project because it surrendered its Clean Water Act permit, removing Army Corps regulatory authority over the permit itself. Conservation groups and tribes may still sue Hudbay directly for Clean Water Act violations, but the ruling shifts enforcement burdens.

title: Rusal calls strike at Guinea bauxite mine 'illegal'
summary: Workers at Rusal’s Guinea bauxite mine COBAD went on strike, halting production, with Rusal calling the strike illegal. Guinea is the world’s second-largest bauxite producer and a key supplier to China. The disruption could reduce bauxite availability for alumina and aluminum output, pressuring aluminum prices.

title: Fastmarkets to launch cif China bauxite price, discontinue fob Guinea, extend fob Brazil consultation
summary: Fastmarkets said it will launch a CIF China bauxite price, stop publishing the fob Guinea format, and extend consultation on fob Brazil. It also delayed and corrected several aluminium-related assessment methodologies (differentials and billet premiums) due to procedural errors, updating its pricing database accordingly.

title: Chinese Companies Seize Indonesian Nickel Resources Amid New Energy Battery Opportunities
summary: CNGR and RIGQUEZA plan to invest $1.26 billion to expand nickel matte production in Indonesia, targeting 40,000 tons per year, building on a prior 60,000 ton cooperation. The new battery-related energy investment focus highlights additional nickel supply capacity, likely weighing on nickel prices.

title: High Grade Copper Intersected in "Deep Zone" at Globex's NewMetal Royalty Property
summary: The piece reports that Globex’s NewMetal royalty property intersected high-grade copper in a “deep zone.” The information is an exploration milestone that may modestly improve perceptions of future copper resources and supply potential, offering slight near-term support to copper prices, though it is not yet production data.

title: Nickel North Exploration Corp.: Nickel North Closes Final Tranche of Private Placement and Announces a New Flow Through Private Placement
summary: Nickel North Exploration closes a private placement tranche and announces a new flow-through private placement to fund 2022 field exploration at its Hawk Ridge Ni-Cu-PGE project. The release is about equity financing and exploration plans, not production, shipments, or disruptions affecting near-term nickel supply.

title: US Dollar Index Closed Down, and Copper Futures Prices Rose in Overnight Trading_SMM
summary: Overnight, LME and SHFE copper futures rose modestly, with spot cathode premiums in China improving. The weaker US dollar (after Fed minutes) and supportive infrastructure-growth expectations supported risk assets. Falling LME/SHFE inventories and tight China supply further limited downside, keeping near-term copper bullish.

title: China's Bauxite Imports Exceeded 10 Million mt in April, with Market Attention Centred on Potential Export Ban by Indonesia_SMM
summary: China imported 11.13m tonnes of bauxite in April, with faster demand driven by concerns over Indonesia’s potential bauxite export ban. Buyers increased imports from Guinea, which rose to 5.83m tonnes, while Indonesia’s volumes fell MoM. Chinese alumina refiners seek alternative feedstock to mitigate supply uncertainty.

title: Alumina Prices Stabilised amid Subdued Trades_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports a quiet domestic alumina market with traders taking a wait-and-see approach. In the southwest, aluminium smelter production resumed in Yunnan, encouraging local alumina sellers to keep offers firm. The SMM weighted alumina index was 2,995 yuan/mt, unchanged versus the prior day.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell 2,200 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventories in major Chinese markets fell 2,200 mt to 107,600 mt by May 27, with a 12,300 mt drop versus last Friday. The decline follows lower supply and higher demand, though Shanghai rose due to more imports and logistics delays. Next week’s arrivals may lift inventories slightly.

title: Copper rebounds after 3-day slump as dollar weakens
summary: Copper rose after a three-day slump as the dollar weakened, while worries about China’s economic slowdown persisted. Nickel on the Shanghai Futures Exchange climbed up to 5% after three days of declines. Separately, a strike at Rusal’s Guinea bauxite mine raised supply disruption concerns for aluminium-linked markets.

title: Copper rebounds from 3-day slump as weak dollar supports
summary: Copper rose after a three-day slump, supported by a weaker U.S. dollar, but the article says copper was still set for weekly losses due to worries about China’s demand amid slowing growth. It also references an aluminium-related Rusal mine strike and low Chinese nickel inventories lifting nickel prices.

title: SMM Analysis: SHFE Aluminum Recorded Two Days of Gains amid Rising Downstream Operating Rates and Extended Destocking _SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium rose 1.22% to 20,775 yuan/mt as downstream operating rates improved and aluminium ingot social inventory fell across major Chinese markets. Billet inventory also declined. Destocking is supported by smelter output dynamics, though auto demand remains weak and macro pessimism could limit further gains.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Lack Upward Momentum amid Oversupply and Import Losses_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums slipping amid oversupply and import losses. Premiums are weaker under warrants and bill-of-lading ahead of June QP, with sluggish trading and minimal buyer inquiries. The SHFE/LME ratio decline and falling SHFE copper relative pricing likely weigh on near-term copper sentiment.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports up 37,000 wmt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose 37,000 wmt to 5.4 million wmt, with Ni content up 300 mt to 42,400 mt. The increase follows improved Philippines shipments after bad weather. Demand is supported by falling NPI prices, but overall the supply build may weigh on nickel sentiment short term.

title: Bonded Zone Inventory of Pure Nickel Dropped Sharply due to the Import Profits_SMM
summary: SMM reports spot pure nickel imports stayed profitable, but falling pure nickel premiums boosted customs clearance. Shanghai bonded zone nickel inventory fell to 7,900 mt, down 700 mt weekly, including 2,900 mt nickel briquettes and 5,000 mt nickel plates. Traders expect premiums to be further lowered, implying continued near-term supply tightening.

title: Copper breaks three days of losses on China hopes, weak dollar
summary: Copper rebounded after three sessions of losses as a weaker U.S. dollar and hopes of China easing COVID curbs boosted demand expectations. China’s copper futures also rose. The piece also cites an illegal strike at Rusal’s Guinea bauxite mine, supporting aluminium, while aluminium and nickel prices gained on the day.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Announces Diamond Drilling Results at Its 100%-Owned San Matias Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals reported diamond drilling results from its 100%-owned San Matias project in Colombia, including copper-bearing intervals at the Alacran deposit and related targets. Intercepts showed grades consistent with the resource model, but no clear evidence of a deeper porphyry source was found. No immediate market supply disruption was indicated.

title: Tesla team visited nickel plants in Indonesia, negotiations still ongoing
summary: Indonesia’s officials say Tesla’s team visited nickel processing plants and that talks over a potential battery/EV factory are still ongoing, after earlier claims of agreement were tempered. The news points to possible near-term demand for Indonesian nickel supply for the battery supply chain, supporting expectations of firmer nickel prices.

title: C3 Metals Inc.: C3 Metals to Commence Drilling Copper-Gold Porphyry Targets in Jamaica
summary: C3 Metals says it will commence a 5,000-metre drilling program at its Bellas Gate copper-gold porphyry project in Jamaica, starting at the Epidote Ridge target and then testing additional porphyry and epithermal prospects. The release is exploration-focused with historic copper-gold grades but no immediate supply impact.

title: C3 Metals to Commence Drilling Copper-Gold Porphyry Targets in Jamaica
summary: C3 Metals says it will start a 5,000-metre drilling program at its Bellas Gate copper-gold porphyry targets in Jamaica, beginning with the Epidote Ridge area and then moving to other porphyry and epithermal targets. The release is exploration focused and does not indicate immediate changes to copper supply or demand.

title: Manna and Ball to develop aluminium can facility in New Mexico
summary: Manna Capital Partners plans, with Ball, to develop an advanced aluminium can sheet rolling mill and recycling centre in New Mexico. The project targets up to 1.3 billion pounds annual capacity, with construction starting late next year and production in 2026, supported by state incentives and renewable-energy framing. It could bolster aluminium supply chain sentiment.

title: Manna Capital Partners-Ball Corporation Plan Valencia County, New Mexico, Aluminum Can Sheet Rolling Mill
summary: Manna Capital Partners and Ball Corporation plan to build a state-of-the-art aluminum can sheet rolling mill in Los Lunas, New Mexico, with construction starting late 2023 and manufacturing in 2026. The project includes a long-term supply agreement, renewable power plans, and up to 1.3 billion pounds annual capacity with high recycled content.

title: US judge rejects request to block work for new copper mine
summary: A federal judge rejected a request to block Hudbay Minerals from preparing a planned new copper mine site near Tucson. Opponents sued on environmental grounds, but the court cited Hudbay’s surrender of a suspended Clean Water Act permit for the nearby Rosemont Mine as removing the legal basis. Copper supply timeline risk eased.

title: St. Paul Public Works takes steps to deter copper thefts from street lights
summary: St. Paul Public Works is using measures such as leaving street lights on during the day to deter theft of copper wire from street lights. The city reports a backlog of thefts from the winter, worsened by supply chain issues, and says it is working to catch offenders and reduce neighborhood impacts.

title: Domestic Economic Stimulus Policy and Extended Inventory Decline Are Expected to Shore up SHFE Aluminium in the Short Term _SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s stabilising-growth stimulus and accelerating production resumption. Fundamentals show slower domestic aluminium supply growth in May, higher liquid-output mix by some smelters, and continued destocking in Wuxi/Gongyi, with consumption improving. Overall, aluminium prices should gain near-term momentum despite medium-term supply/demand constraints.

title: The Average Aluminium Cost Remained around 18,000 yuan/mt_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says average aluminium smelter cost fell 34 yuan/mt to 18,205 yuan/mt due to lower alumina prices. Spot aluminium averaged 20,800 yuan/mt and smelter profits rose 64 yuan/mt to 2,594 yuan/mt. Electricity tariffs fell in multiple provinces, likely keeping costs easing, though power shortages in peak season are a risk.

title: Copper Prices will be Supported by the Fundamentals in the Short Term_SMM
summary: SMM expects copper prices to be supported short term. Weak US/Europe growth backdrop is balanced by China stabilization measures. Smelter restarts lift output slightly, while copper scrap supply remains tight despite improved selling willingness. Demand looks firmer with State Grid orders and lower wire/cable inventories, keeping spot premiums stable.

title: How Will the High Ocean Freight Affect Domestic Bauxite Import?_SMM
summary: High ocean freight rates are keeping shipment costs elevated for China’s bauxite imports. Traders report booking difficulties and shortages of available spot supply. Rising imported bauxite prices squeeze alumina refineries’ margins in Shanxi, Henan and Guizhou, prompting possible output cuts, lifting near-term aluminium supply concerns.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Rose Slightly and Spot Imports Turned into Profits_SMM
summary: SMM says Yangshan copper premiums rose to around $68–83/mt under warrants, with spot imports in China shifting to profit-making levels. Importers raised premiums for small orders, but expected further increases are constrained by poor demand and oversupply, with limited inquiries and no bill-of-lading transactions.

title: Chinese Aluminium Ingot Market still in Destocking Cycle, with Cumulative Reduction of 64,000 mt in May_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s aluminium ingot social inventories fell to 923,000 mt as of May 30, down 14,000 mt week-on-week, and 64,000 mt cumulatively since May. Regions like Wuxi and Foshan saw faster declines. With downstream production resuming, inventory is unlikely to rise soon, supporting sentiment for aluminium.

title: Alumina Prices in Shanxi Extended Decline _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says Shanxi alumina prices fell another 15 yuan/mt to 2,860-2,950 yuan/mt, lowering the weighted alumina index to 2,989 yuan/mt. Flooding in Guangxi did not disrupt local supply, while southwest alumina stayed firm as aluminium smelters resumed production.

title: Copper Inventories across Major Chinese Markets down 300 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventories across major Chinese markets fell by 300 mt to 107,300 mt over the weekend. Guangdong dropped rapidly, while others saw smaller moves. With logistics recovery, stranded imported copper is being shipped, but near-term arrivals may not be enough, so inventories could keep declining.

title: SHFE Nickel Continued to Rise amid the Weak Supply and Demand_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel (2206) gaining and closing higher after short funds covered, with price support from tight pure nickel supply and low inventories/warrants. While nickel sulphate and NPI prices soften due to weaker demand and supply conditions, overall nickel is seen as hard to fall sharply in the near term.

title: Los Andes Copper Announces Additional Copper Intercepts at Vizcachitas Copper Project Chile
summary: Los Andes Copper reported additional copper intercepts at its Vizcachitas copper project in Chile. News of new mineralization can improve perceptions of resource potential and future output, typically providing modest near-term support to copper prices through improved supply expectations and investor sentiment.

title: Los Andes Copper Ltd.: Los Andes Copper Announces Additional Copper Intercepts at Vizcachitas Copper Project Chile
summary: Los Andes Copper announced additional high-grade drilling intercepts at its Vizcachitas copper-molybdenum project in Chile, including long copper-equivalent intervals. Management says results expand a Tier 1 advanced copper resource and support progress on a pre-feasibility study amid expectations of limited development projects and a looming supply deficit.

title: Fragmentation of the copper supply chain
summary: The piece argues the copper supply chain is fragmented, with concentrated mining (e.g., Peru) and concentrated processing/smelting (notably China). It cites disruptions like strikes at Las Bambas and recent import declines, and warns of a projected copper supply shortfall versus demand, supporting bullish price expectations.

title: "Tribal Request To Halt Arizona Copper Mine Work Is Denied"
summary: A federal judge denied Native American tribes’ request to halt Hudbay Minerals’ preparations for a planned copper mine in Arizona. The ruling dismissed the lawsuit after Hudbay surrendered a previously suspended Clean Water Act permit for the Rosemont project. Hudbay’s effort pivots to the Copper World project on private land.

title: Copper steadies near 3-week high on China demand optimism
summary: LME copper held near a three-week high as China demand optimism rose. Better Chinese factory data and easing COVID-19 lockdowns, including Shanghai reopening, improved near-term consumption expectations. The U.S. dollar’s limited strength provided support, while copper was steady near $9,537/tonne and other metals were mixed to slightly higher.

title: China gains from Russia-Ukraine war, increases aluminium exports to Europe
summary: China is expanding aluminium shipments to Europe amid the Russia-Ukraine war, with exports rising far above imports. The article notes US and European criticism of these shifting trade dynamics. More Chinese aluminium supply into Europe is likely to weigh on short-term aluminium pricing through improved availability and weaker local balance.

title: Decline in NPI Prices to Have Limited Impact on Nickel Prices _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports NPI prices may stay volatile around 1,500–1,550 yuan/mtu, tracking NPI plant costs that could fall with more nickel ore supply and lower ore prices. It says the NPI-to-nickel linkage is weaker due to a large spread since March, so NPI declines should not greatly pressure nickel in the short term.

title: Pure Nickel Premiums Fell Sharply_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports sharp declines in Shanghai spot nickel. Jinchuan nickel averages about 4,000 yuan/mt (down sharply), while NORNICKEL averages 5,400 yuan/mt (down 850). The drop is linked to traders shipping as the pure nickel import window opened, falling premiums, and weaker nickel briquette quotes as futures fell.

title: SHFE Nickel Inventory Set a New Record Low_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that LME nickel inventories have fallen to a two-year low, with May 20 seeing a new low around 71,898 mt. SHFE data show nickel inventories dropped further last week, down 9.61% to 2,877 mt on May 27, a record low.

title: China Takes Advantage of Russia-Ukraine War, Increases Aluminium Exports to Europe
summary: China is increasing exports of aluminium to Europe, exploiting the Russia-Ukraine war-driven reconfiguration of supply. The article cites higher VAT rebates for exports and a larger export gap versus imports, alongside April growth in aluminium output after power-production curbs eased. ING warns supply growth may exceed soft demand.

title: SMM Analysis: SHFE Aluminium to Remain Rangebound amid Eased Oversupply Pressure and Expected Demand Recovery  _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium and spot prices were largely flat in May. It cites slowing growth in domestic aluminium supply, a modest decline in social inventories, and expectations of downstream consumption recovery alongside improved market sentiment from China’s financial-support meeting. Overall, SMM expects aluminium to remain rangebound.

title: The US Dollar Continued to Decline and the INE Bonded Copper Contract Remained Volatile_SMM
summary: SMM reports the INE bonded copper 2208 contract trended higher on May 31, closing up 0.30% at 64,430 yuan/mt. It attributes the move to a continued decline in the US dollar index and expectations around the next Fed rate-hike and balance-sheet shrink timeline.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Announces Feasibility Study is Underway at its 100%-Owned San Matias Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals begins feasibility-study technical work and a 40,000-metre infill drilling program at its San Matias copper-gold-silver project in Colombia. The company cites prior PFS economics using US$3.60/lb copper and notes the current spot copper price, but provides no new supply or demand changes that would move prices. Nickel/aluminium not mentioned.

title: SCCO stock Pays High Dividends but too many Problems in the Industry
summary: Peru protests disrupted copper mining for nearly two months, cutting production and hurting revenues for Southern Copper. The article notes rising demand drivers (EVs, infrastructure) while supply remains constrained, implying potential tightening. It also highlights a concurrent increase in copper prices during the quarter.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Begins Environmental Baseline Studies at the Kenbridge Nickel Project, Kenora Mining District, Northwestern Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. says it has started environmental baseline studies for the Kenbridge Nickel Project to support permitting and approvals. It retained consulting firms for time-sensitive Spring 2022 work and plans further updates on a summer work program. The release is a development/permitting step, not imminent nickel production.

title: Novelis Joins First Movers Coalition to Accelerate Decarbonization of Aluminum Industry
summary: Novelis joined the First Movers Coalition to accelerate decarbonization of the aluminum industry, pledging by 2030 to source 10% near-zero primary aluminum and at least 50% aluminum from recycled inputs (it already has 57%). The move targets clean-energy technologies for lower-carbon aluminum production and recycling.

title: Prasa worker who stole copper cables worth R1m gets 12 years in prison
summary: A South African court sentenced a PRASA worker to 12 years for stealing copper cables worth R1m (about 192kg) from a railway line. Prosecutors said cable theft harms service delivery and stressed renewed enforcement, but the incident appears localized with no clear broader effect on copper supply or pricing.

title: Four holes drilled at the newly discovered Grata prospect in Ivory Coast returned thick intersections of nickel-copper-palladium mineralization including holes GR-08 and GR-11 with 298 meters and 212 meters respectively
summary: Sama reports four holes at the Grata prospect in Ivory Coast returning long, thick intersections of nickel-copper sulphide mineralization, including GR-08 (297.6m) and GR-11 (212m). Grades include ~0.2–0.3% Ni and ~0.2–0.3% Cu. Assays for additional holes remain pending, with no near-term production impact stated.

title: Four holes drilled at the newly discovered Grata prospect in Ivory Coast returned thick intersections of nickel-copper-palladium mineralization including holes GR-08 and GR-11 with 298 meters and 212 meters respectively
summary: Seahawk-like news highlights new drilling at the Grata prospect in Ivory Coast, with multiple holes intersecting long widths of Ni-Cu rich sulphide mineralization (notably high Cu/Ni in GR-06 zones) and additional narrow stringers. Results for further holes are pending; the company aims to fast-track resource definition.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Stayed Stable due to the Poor Demand_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums under warrants were steady at $69–83/mt, averaging $76/mt, with no transactions yet. Bill-of-lading premiums averaged $71/mt. Import losses against the SHFE 2206 contract persisted, while buying interest remained weak due to poor demand and traders’ caution over follow-up policies.

title: Spot Premiums of Pure Nickel Continued to be Lowered when the Market Started to Quote Premiums over SHFE 2207 Nickel Contract_SMM
summary: SMM reports pure nickel spot premiums shifted to trade over the SHFE 2207 nickel contract, but premiums for Jinchuan and NORNICKEL fell versus the prior day. It attributes declines to spot inflows into the market and higher supply, with nickel briquette prices dropping on weaker trading and cost-efficiency.

title: Copper premiums slide in China, rise in Italy, Netherlands
summary: The report notes copper premium movements: premiums slid in China but rose in Italy and the Netherlands. It also contains Fastmarkets methodology/assessment publication timing and procedural-error corrections for aluminium differentials and related price assessments. Overall, the only clearly supported metal price signal is softer copper premiums in China.

title: Resource Mining to drill long nickel-cobalt zone at Kabulwanyele project in Tanzania
summary: Resource Mining Corporation plans a six-week maiden RC drilling program at its Kabulwanyele nickel-cobalt project in Tanzania, targeting massive sulphides beneath nickel laterite and testing a 2km strike area. The company is also progressing due diligence for its Massive Nickel acquisition, citing a sharply stronger nickel market and competition for assets.

title: Vedanta Aluminium's Restora is India's First Low Carbon 'Green' Aluminium - Energy Industry Today
summary: Vedanta Aluminium launched its Restora brand of low-carbon ‘green’ aluminium in India, claiming much lower GHG intensity via renewable energy and ultra-low carbon products made from recovered dross. The move targets growing demand from climate-conscious manufacturers, but no short-term supply or trade change is mentioned.

title: Chile's Copper Output in April Dropped by 9.8% YoY_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chile’s National Bureau of Statistics reported that copper output fell 9.8% YoY in April to 421,742 mt. The article notes Chile’s production has been below last year’s levels due to factors including lower ore grades, insufficient water supply, and temporary operating problems.

title: Global Bauxite Market Report (2022 to 2030)
summary: A ResearchAndMarkets report projects bauxite demand growth through 2030, citing rising aluminium-linked consumption such as aluminum foil packaging and investment in new foil production capacity. Since bauxite is the key feedstock for alumina and primary aluminium, the outlook is supportive of aluminium demand expectations.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Selects Independent Consultants for the Copper Creek Project Mineral Resource Estimate Update and Mine-to-Mill Assessment
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. selected consultants to update the Mineral Resource Estimate and complete a mine-to-mill assessment for its Copper Creek porphyry copper project in Arizona. The company expanded drilling, but no assay results or production decisions were provided. The work will feed a planned PEA timeline into 2023.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28 Announces Financial Results and Large Debt Repayment
summary: Nickel 28 reported results and significant debt repayment linked to cash generation from its Ramu nickel-cobalt operation. The release highlights strong nickel production and notes market tightness, with LME nickel trading above $12.50/lb. These factors are supportive for near-term nickel sentiment and expectations.

title: Ball Corporation and Novelis Join World Economic Forum's First Movers Coalition, Encourage Value Chain Collaboration to Drive Decarbonization in Aluminum Sector
summary: Ball Corporation and Novelis joined the World Economic Forum’s First Movers Coalition for aluminum decarbonization, committing to buy 10% of primary aluminum annually as near-zero carbon by 2030 and to source at least 50% recycled aluminum by 2030. The piece emphasizes circularity and clean energy needs rather than near-term price moves.

title: Duty-free Import Of UK Steel And Aluminum To US Comes Into Force
summary: The UK-US deal removes Trump-era Section 232 tariffs on UK steel and aluminium entering the US, replacing them with tariff-rate quotas. UK aluminum exporters can ship specified volumes tariff-free each year. Cheaper access for suppliers and improved trade conditions are expected to support the near-term aluminum market.

title: Nickel price chaos triggered $2bn margin breach at LME
summary: LME Clear reported a record $2 billion initial margin breach in March tied to soaring nickel prices after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The peak breach reflects a worst-case scenario for the largest clearing member default. The event underscores the severity of nickel market volatility and stressed clearing finances.

title: Chile starts sanction process against Los Pelambres copper mine
summary: Chile’s environmental regulator (SMA) initiated sanction proceedings against Antofagasta Minerals’ Los Pelambres copper mine for deficiencies in tailings management and incident communication protocols. While there were no air- or water-quality standard breaches, serious sanctions could include fines up to about $9 million or even permit loss/closure.

title: Two fires break out at copper projects in Peru amid protests -sources
summary: Two fires broke out at Southern Copper’s Los Chancas project and MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine in Peru amid intensified protests. Las Bambas operations have been halted since April 20, and Southern suspended Cuajone earlier. Companies attribute parts of the fires to artisanal miners; clashes caused injuries and infrastructure damage.

title: Rebounded US Dollar Put Pressure on Copper Prices, and Buying Interest of Spot Trading was not High_SMM
summary: SMM reports modest copper price gains in LME and SHFE, while spot premiums fluctuate and import buying interest remains weak due to import losses and poor demand. LME and SHFE inventories fall slightly. Macro signals are mixed: US dollar rebound/rate-hike expectations weigh, while China policy support and Shanghai demand recovery are supportive.

title: Blackstone Minerals explores new massive sulphide opportunities around Ta Khoa nickel project
summary: Blackstone Minerals’ Ta Khoa (Vietnam) drilling identified new sulphide prospects, including intersections with reported nickel up to ~20% and gossan assays up to 5.9% Ni, plus copper values in nearby infill results. The news is exploration-focused with no near-term supply change.

title: Market Still Pessimistic on Demand Recovery Despite Improved Pure Nickel Sales_SMM
summary: SMM says pure nickel spot prices maintained a downward trend, with nickel sulphate and NPI prices falling and limited willingness to cut due to high costs. Demand for stainless steel and NPI remains weak, with high stainless inventory and tight mill margins. Despite improved operating rates for some alloy factories, the chain stays bearish and low stocks support only modestly.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Added 3,100 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM reported that China’s major-market copper inventories rose 3,100 mt to 110,400 mt from Monday (and 2,800 mt from last Friday). The increase was linked to resumed smelter output, more imported cathode, and weaker restocking ahead of the Dragon Boat Festival. Consumption is expected to remain soft post-holiday.

title: SMM Weekly Statistics of Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventory in China as of June 2_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s aluminium ingot social inventories fell to 882,000 mt as of June 2, down 55,000 mt week-on-week, driven by warehouse cargo pickup after collateral-related incidents and improved buying from wider spot discounts. Billet inventories also declined, supported by a price correction and recovering downstream demand, suggesting ongoing destocking next week.

title: Aluminium Ingot Inventory Plummeted as Collateral Scandal Triggered Panic Cargo Pick-Up_SMM
summary: Rumours of aluminium ingot batches being repeatedly pledged as collateral sparked panic among SHFE warehouse participants in Foshan, Guangdong. Cargo pick-up was suspended, police are investigating, and risk aversion intensified. SHFE aluminium fell more than 3% and spot discounts widened as sellers rushed to sell and downstream buyers stayed cautious.

title: Shanghai copper gains on demand hopes as China eases COVID curbs
summary: Shanghai copper rose after China eased COVID-19 curbs, lifting hopes for demand recovery as Shanghai reopened and business activity improves. The upside was tempered by a stronger U.S. dollar. The report also shows Shanghai aluminium and nickel climbed, reflecting broader metal support from improved Chinese sentiment.

title: Where Will SHFE Nickel Head after Ending Four-Day Winning Streak?_SMM
summary: SHFE nickel ended a four-day winning streak, falling about 2.15%, with LME nickel down similarly. Spot SMM1# refined nickel averaged lower and premiums for Jinchuan and Norilsk declined amid improving domestic supply. Despite tight pure nickel, weak stainless steel demand and ample NPI supply suppressed buying and limited upside.

title: Pure Nickel Spot Prices Rose as Futures Prices Rebounded_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that pure nickel spot premiums rose, with Jinchuan nickel averaging 7,500 yuan/mt and NORNICKEL averaging 7,750 yuan/mt. The increase was attributed to a sharp rebound in nickel futures and improved overseas nickel customs clearance affecting spot premiums and shipment demand.

title: Yangshan Copper Market was slack amid Closed LME Trading_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Yangshan copper premiums under warrants were $69–83/mt, largely flat, while LME 0–3 premiums were about -$2/mt. Import losses against the 2206 contract were ~300 yuan/mt as LME trading paused for a UK holiday. Weak spot premiums and poor demand reduced quotes, especially for small orders.

title: Copper Inventory in China Bonded Zone Dropped by 8,600 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s copper inventories in domestic bonded zones fell 8,600 mt to 294,800 mt as of June 2. Shanghai dropped 9,700 mt to 265,300 mt, while Guangdong rose 1,100 mt to 29,500 mt. With customs pick-up demand cooling and logistics improving, the drawdown may slow.

title: Imports of Pure Nickel Spots Remained Profitable, and Bonded Zone Inventory Dropped Slightly_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel fell slightly, but pure nickel spot imports remained profitable due to falling premiums. Bonded zone nickel inventory was 7,400 mt, with nickel briquette and plate inventories down week-on-week. Eased COVID impacts improved demand while supply stayed tight, limiting downside and supporting short-term import buying.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 343,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said Chinese nickel ore port inventories fell 343,000 wmt WoW to 5.057 million wmt (Ni content down to 39,800 wmt). Seven major ports’ inventories also declined. Philippine shipments improved with weather, but arrivals lagged expectations as NPI plants increased purchases. Inventories are seen rangebound short term.

title: Bearish Sentiment Dominated Alumina Market amid Continuous Release of New Capacity _SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices were steady but sentiment remained bearish as new alumina capacity came online (Hebei Wenfeng, Chongqing Bosai, and Tiangui Phase II), increasing supply and causing a surplus. Some Shanxi refineries face losses, with SMM monitoring high-cost operations as a headwind for any rebound.

title: SHFE Nickel Rose Supported by the Low Inventories_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Ni 2207 rose 1.38% on June 2, citing low nickel inventories as support for short-term trading. Spot premiums narrowed as pure nickel supply increased and transactions improved. However, downstream acceptance for briquettes is weak and nickel sulphate/NPI face falling prices, implying volatile conditions.

title: Nickel Sulphate Prices Continued to Fall along with Costs in the Absence of Strong Demand Recovery_SMM
summary: Battery-grade nickel sulphate prices in China fell to about 42,800–44,500 yuan/mt, down 850 yuan/mt week-on-week, with limited trading volumes. Producers’ quotations varied due to cost differences, while integrated suppliers’ lower-cost output increased volumes. NEV demand recovery remained slow, so nickel salt prices are expected to stay weak.

title: C3 Metals Inc.: C3 Metals Discovers High Grade Copper - Silver at Arthurs Seat, Jamaica
summary: C3 Metals reported surface reconnaissance results at the Arthurs Seat project in Jamaica, including samples with up to 13.8% copper and 492g/t silver, plus plans for continued mapping and future geophysics and drilling. The company is exploring for copper-gold mineralization; no production changes or shipments are mentioned.

title: G3 Enterprises Offers Craft Brewers, RTD Cocktail Producers and Beverage Companies a New, Dedicated Aluminum Can Supply
summary: G3 Enterprises says it has secured additional aluminum can and lid supply and is building a new can plant in Nashua, New Hampshire (KJ Can USA) expected to complete within months. The company aims to end aluminum can shortages affecting craft brewers and RTD drink makers across New England and the East Coast.

title: Valor Resources : Significant Copper & Silver sampling results in Peru
summary: Valor Resources announced significant copper-bearing rock chip and channel sampling results from its Peru Picha Project (including assays up to ~2.69% Cu and ~2.82% Cu) and Charaque Project targets. It also outlines further drilling plans subject to approvals. The findings are exploratory and do not indicate near-term supply changes.

title: Information sought following theft of scrap copper from field close to Limerick/Tipperary border
summary: Gardai are investigating the theft of a large quantity of scrap copper stockpiled in a field near the Limerick/Tipperary border, stolen sometime between May 12 and May 26. The scrap is valued at €1,500–€2,000, and local police seek information to recover it.

title: Desktop Metal, Inc.: Aidro Becomes Qualified Supplier of Leonardo Helicopters for Additive Manufacturing of Aluminum Flight Parts
summary: Desktop Metal’s subsidiary Aidro (via Aidro/Aidro-AM) says it became a qualified supplier for Leonardo helicopters, producing 3D-printed aluminum flight parts. The qualification enables supply of aluminum components for rotorcraft lightweighting. This can marginally support aluminum demand expectations, though the overall market impact is likely limited.

title: Here To Serve Holding Corp.: Fortune Nickel and Gold Defines Strong Exploration Targets at its Property in Ontario, Canada.
summary: Fortune Nickel and Gold reports completion of IP and magnetic surveys over its Beck-Ottaway-Lennox property in Ontario, outlining conductor anomalies consistent with nickel sulfide targets and some copper-bearing sulfides (chalcopyrite). The company plans near-term drilling. It provides exploration updates, not operational or supply-demand changes.

title: Possible buyout of Limerick's Aughinish Alumina plant by British politician
summary: Reports say Aughinish Alumina’s Russian owner is considering carving out Rusal’s international business and a British politician may be involved in talks with non-Russian investors to buy Rusal’s European operation, including Ireland. The aim is to preserve jobs and maintain operations at the Askeaton site amid post-war sanctions.

title: C3 Metals Discovers High Grade Copper, Silver at Arthurs Seat, Jamaica
summary: C3 Metals announced high-grade copper (up to 13.8%) and silver assay results from surface reconnaissance at the Arthurs Seat Project in Jamaica and described ongoing mapping and plans for geophysics and drill testing. The update is exploratory, with no production or near-term supply impact described.

title: Tamkeen backs first aluminium grain refiner project in the Gulf | THE DAILY TRIBUNE
summary: Tamkeen, Bahrain’s labour fund, signed an agreement with Spanish aluminium alloy/refiner Aleastur to establish the first Gulf plant for producing aluminium alloys. The project is positioned to meet rising regional and global demand and enable substantial exports, with government and ALBA-linked support.

title: Govt not to impose countervailing duty on certain aluminium products from Malaysia
summary: The finance ministry rejected DGTR recommendations and the government will not impose countervailing duties on certain aluminium products imported from Malaysia. Without the added tariff protection, import competition is expected to continue, potentially increasing effective supply and weighing on near-term aluminium prices.

title: Russia's Rusal launches legal action against Rio Tinto over alumina refinery-report
summary: Rusal sued Rio Tinto in Australian federal court, arguing Rio’s April step-in control of Queensland Alumina Ltd unjustly sidelined Rusal and breached obligations. Rio’s move followed sanctions on Russian oligarchs. Australia previously banned alumina/aluminium ore exports to Russia.

title: SHFE Aluminium to Fluctuate Rangebound amid Basically Balanced Supply and Demand _SMM
summary: SMM forecasts rangebound aluminium prices this week, with SHFE aluminium expected at 20,000–21,300 yuan/mt and LME at $2,700–2,900/mt. Improved COVID conditions support demand recovery in east China, while tight inventories and a supply slowdown counterbalance a temporary “collateral scandal” shock.

title: Alumina Prices Fell amid Strong Bearish Sentiment _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports alumina prices in China falling week-on-week, with bearish sentiment dominating spot trading. It cites reduced spot buying by aluminium smelters, potential output ramp-ups from new alumina capacity, and expected supply glut.
