Caustic soda and bauxite costs may limit downside, but near-term pressure remains bearish.

title: Copper hits over 1-month high on easing curbs in China, U.S. tariff cut hopes
summary: London copper prices climbed to the highest level in over a month as China began relaxing COVID-19 lockdowns and sentiment improved ahead of possible U.S. tariff easing. The piece links the move to expectations of a faster demand recovery, alongside a broader positive tone in industrial metals.

title: Copper Concentrate Market was Slack Last Week, and the TCs Remained Stable_SMM
summary: SMM reports sluggish copper concentrate trading and stable treatment charges, but market focus is on supply risk: Peru’s Las Bambas copper mine has been suspended for over a month with renewed conflict, and authorities extended a state of emergency. Negotiations and concentrate availability keep pricing coefficients steady, with tighter supply concerns supportive for copper.

title: Russia's Rusal files suit against Rio Tinto over alumina refinery
summary: Rusal filed a lawsuit against Rio Tinto seeking to regain its 20% access to alumina output at Queensland Alumina Ltd in Australia. Rio took sole control after sanctions triggered by Russian oligarch links following Ukraine. The case challenges whether conditions for the step-in existed and asks for restoration of Rusal’s rights.

title: Elliott Associates sues LME for $456 million over nickel trading halt – HKEX
summary: Elliott Associates has sued the London Metal Exchange for $456 million after the LME suspended and cancelled nickel trades in March. HKEX said LME and LME Clear were named in a UK judicial review filed in June. The case centers on the trading halt’s handling rather than nickel supply or demand.

title: Report: Both LME and SHFE Aluminium Inventories Fell, LME Aluminium Inventory Hitting a New Low of More than 21 Years_SMM
summary: LME data show aluminium inventories kept declining last week to 453,875 mt, the lowest in more than 21 years. SHFE aluminium inventories also fell for four straight weeks, dropping 2.25% to 279,128 mt in the week of June 2. The trend is supportive for futures.

title: Aluminium Costs Increased Slightly due to Rising Prebaked Anode Prices _SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices fell 5-10 yuan/mt, while prebaked anode prices rose, lifting smelter full costs by 84 yuan/mt to 18,289 yuan/mt. Spot aluminium averaged 20,540 yuan/mt, but smelter profit fell 344 yuan/mt. Near term, electricity is stable and alumina could drop on surplus, weighing on aluminium prices.

title: Copper Prices Continued to Rebound under the Support of Government Policies in China_SMM
summary: SMM reports copper prices rebounded last week as China rolled out economy-stabilizing policies, firms resumed work, and downstream wire/cable and cathode rod demand improved with grid project start-ups and restocking. Supply tightness is supported by Las Bambas suspension and delayed Daye output, despite some regional flows pressuring spots.

title: Nickel Prices Remained Rangebound at High Levels Last Week due to the Recovery of Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports nickel prices stayed rangebound at high levels, with spot premiums drifting down and trading volume improving. Nickel sulphate cost differentials pressured market expectations, while weak NPI terminal demand and limited stainless steel consumption restrained gains. Downstream alloy purchasing improved, but primary supply/demand recovery is still absent; low inventory supports prices.

title: Rio Tinto arm begins farm-in drilling program at Alderan Resources' copper project
summary: Rio Tinto’s subsidiary Kennecott Exploration has started farm-in drilling at Alderan Resources’ Frisco copper project in Utah, targeting porphyry and high-grade copper at the Copper Gulch prospect. Prior drilling and historical assays show substantial copper grades, strengthening near-term optimism for copper discovery and development.

title: London Metal Exchange sued for $456m over cancelled nickel trades
summary: Elliott Associates sued the LME and LME Clear for $456m after the exchange cancelled nickel trades on 8 March when nickel prices surged. HKEX said the market became disorderly and trading was suspended for over a week. The case and wider regulatory scrutiny could weigh on near-term nickel sentiment.

title: Aluminium Ingot Inventory Dropped to 874,000 mt, Led by Wuxi_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s social aluminium ingot inventories fell to 874,000 mt as of June 6, down 8,000 mt from the previous Thursday, led by a 20,000 mt drop in Wuxi. Warehouse shipments rose to 188,000 mt after a collateral scandal prompted cargo pickup. Inventories may decline more slowly due to upcoming arrivals to Gongyi.

title: Subsidiary of Russian company sues Rio Tinto for cutting it out of Queensland alumina operation
summary: A Rusal subsidiary is suing Rio Tinto, saying it was frozen out of a Queensland alumina joint venture after Australia sanctioned Deripaska. Rio moved to take full control to avoid breaches, while ABC seeks reinstatement and damages. The sanctions process is disrupting alumina supply and governance at Gladstone.

title: Rusal Sues Rio Tinto to Restore Its Fair Share of Alumina Supply_SMM
summary: Rusal sued Rio Tinto to restore its 20% alumina production share in a Queensland joint-venture refinery. The claim follows Australia’s sanctions on Russia, including bans on supplying alumina and bauxite to Rusal, after which Rio Tinto assumed 100% capacity and management, potentially tightening alumina—and aluminium—supplies.

title: 3,000 Workers of Las Bambas Were Laid Off due to Shutdown of the Mine, Tcs of Imported Copper Concentrate Soared 166% in more than A Year_SMM
summary: MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine in Peru has been suspended for over 40 days due to indigenous community protests, with about 3,000 contractor workers laid off. Meanwhile, treatment charges for imported copper concentrate jumped 166% to $78.66/mt by June 2, reflecting tightening concentrate availability and bullish copper sentiment.

title: New Alumina Capacity Ramped up as Scheduled, Talks between Buyers and Sellers in A Deadlock _SMM
summary: SMM reports sluggish alumina transactions and little price movement, despite supply pressures: Hebei Wenfeng output was released in May and Chongqing Wanbo has further capacity ramping. Rising caustic soda prices and high costs erode refinery profits, leading sellers to stick to long-term orders. With weaker smelter demand after the Dragon Boat Festival, alumina prices face downside risk.

title: London Metal Exchange sued over cancelled nickel contracts
summary: Elliott Management sued the London Metal Exchange for more than $456 million over the exchange’s suspension and cancellation of nickel trades earlier this year, after dramatic nickel price swings. The claim alleges unlawful conduct and human-rights violations, with the case filed in England’s High Court.

title: SHFE Nickel Rose by More Than 3% and How Long can Low Inventories Support Nickel Prices?_SMM
summary: SHFE nickel extended gains, at one point rising more than 3%, while LME nickel was up after opening. SMM notes premiums narrowing amid higher absolute prices and weaker near-term transactions, but still-low nickel inventories and gradual downstream restocking are expected to keep nickel prices supported and elevated.

title: Elliott Sues London Metal Exchange for $456 Million Over Nickel Crisis
summary: Elliott Management has sued the London Metal Exchange for $456 million, alleging losses tied to nickel trades being suspended and canceled earlier this year. The dispute highlights market-function disruptions around nickel contracts, which can pressure short-term nickel pricing through liquidity, hedging uncertainty, and investor sentiment.

title: SMM Analysis: SHFE Aluminium Outperformed Other Base Metals, but Tug-of-War between Bulls and Bears Remains Intense_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium gained over 3% on the first day after the Dragon Boat Festival, reaching the highest level in more than a month. It links the move to improving China downstream activity post-COVID lockdown, higher processing operating rates, stronger export demand, and slight declines in social inventories, though near-term volatility remains.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Dipped 1,500 mt during the Dragon Boat Festival_SMM
summary: SMM said copper inventories in major Chinese markets fell 1,500 mt to 108,900 mt as of June 6, with most regions declining after the Dragon Boat Festival. Shanghai and Guangdong dropped, while Jiangsu and Tianjin rose slightly. Outlook: supply should keep rising, but weak consumption may rebuild inventories.

title: LME faces Elliott International's US$456 million lawsuit for suspending nickel futures trading, cancelling trades
summary: The news reports that the LME faces a US$456 million lawsuit from Elliott International after it allegedly suspended nickel futures trading and cancelled trades. The dispute highlights trading-market disruption and potential legal/operational uncertainty, which can shift near-term nickel price expectations through liquidity and risk-premium effects.

title: Elliott Management Sues the London Metal Exchange Over Nickel Fiasco
summary: Elliott Management sued the London Metal Exchange over its March 2022 suspension of nickel trading and cancellation of nickel trades after the price surged above $100,000/ton during a Russian-sanctions-driven short squeeze. The LME and its owners dispute wrongdoing and regulators launched a nickel market review. Nickel later traded far lower.

title: WESTERN COPPER AND GOLD COMMENCES EXPLORATION AND DRILLING PROGRAM AT CASINO
summary: Western Copper and Gold announced its 2022 exploration and drilling program at the Casino copper-gold project in Yukon. The company plans to drill and scan core to evaluate a deep MT low-resistivity copper-gold anomaly and conduct geotechnical/hydrological work for project facilities. No production impacts or copper price drivers are specified.

title: Vedanta Aluminium's largest smelter reduces GHG emissions intensity by 12% in FY222
summary: Vedanta Aluminium says its largest smelter cut GHG emissions intensity by ~12% in FY22 versus FY21 while raising production volume by 20%. The company also expands renewables via a power delivery agreement for 380 MW, launches lower-carbon “green” aluminium, and highlights energy-efficiency gains and climate targets.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Kamoa Copper Achieves Record Monthly Copper Production of 29,800 Tonnes
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says Kamoa-Kakula set a record May output of 29,800 tonnes of copper in concentrate, despite brief planned maintenance. Phase 2 ramp-up and commissioning of a filter press support higher throughput and keep 2022 guidance toward the upper end, reinforcing near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Hedge Fund Elliott Sues LME for $456 Million Over Nickel Trading Halt
summary: U.S. hedge fund Elliott Associates is suing the LME for $456 million after the exchange cancelled nickel trades and suspended its nickel market during chaotic trading in March. The lawsuit adds pressure amid regulator probes and efforts to restore volumes, potentially worsening near-term nickel liquidity and sentiment.

title: Nickel Prices Rose as the Tight Supply Improved_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Nickel prices on the SHFE Ni 2207 contract rose about 1.33% on June 6 after an intraday high. The report links the move to improved pure nickel supply from Nornickel circulation, higher domestic inventories, better spot premiums, and a gradual demand recovery, suggesting nickel remains supported this week.

title: Three Drillholes Completed at Camino's Los Chapitos Copper Project in Peru
summary: The news reports that Camino has completed three drillholes at its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru. Positive drilling progress can modestly lift sentiment around the project’s potential size and development outlook, which may support copper price expectations in the near term. No direct details on nickel or aluminium are provided.

title: TT Scrap Iron Dealers beg Gov't to shut down copper industry
summary: Trinidad and Tobago’s Scrap Iron Dealers Association urged the Ministry of Trade to shut down the copper export industry, arguing it is the only way to stop theft of copper wires and fixtures. The group claims licensed exporters are limited and wants police to inspect export containers, potentially reducing copper export flows.

title: Chilean copper production falls 8.9% in April, Cochilco says
summary: Chile’s April copper output fell 8.9% to about 420,000 tonnes versus April 2021, with declines attributed to lower refining rates and worse ore grades. Cochilco also flagged tighter concentrate supply as Chinese smelter maintenance nears end, pressuring copper concentrate TC/RC charges and refining expectations.

title: Infinitum Copper: Invitation to PDAC 2022 Booth | The Kingston Whig Standard
summary: Infinitum Copper invites investors to visit its PDAC 2022 booth and describes its copper exploration assets, including the La Adelita copper project in Mexico and the Hot Breccia property in Arizona. The piece is promotional and does not report new discoveries, production changes, or supply-demand shocks affecting copper prices.

title: Scrap dealers: Ban copper trade until thieves are found
summary: Scrap dealers in Trinidad and Tobago are calling for a two-to-three month suspension of copper exports until suspected theft networks are identified. The proposal includes stricter export licensing, container checks at the port, and tighter scrapyard controls on purchase of scrap, aiming to reduce the market that enables theft.

title: Explainer-Why the London Metal Exchange is fighting a lawsuit for cancelling nickel trades
summary: Elliott Associates sued the LME for $456 million over the exchange cancelling nickel trades during March chaos that led to an LME nickel suspension. The dispute comes as regulators probe the LME and it struggles to rebuild nickel volumes and trust. Nickel prices had earlier surged on short-cover expectations.

title: LME hit with £363m lawsuit from hedge fund Elliott over nickel debacle
summary: Elliott Management has filed a £363m lawsuit against the LME, alleging the exchange’s cancellation of nickel trades on March 8 was unlawful. The dispute followed a disorderly nickel surge, with regulators and the IMF criticizing conflicts of interest. The case reintroduces uncertainty for nickel trading and market structure.

title: Infinity Stone Ventures Corp.: Infinity Stone Announces Work Program at Zen-Whoberi Copper-Cobalt-Platinum-Palladium Project
summary: Infinity Stone Ventures begins a reconnaissance exploration program at its Zen-Whoberi copper-cobalt-(plus platinum/palladium) project in Quebec. The work aims to confirm historical results, including reported copper intercepts, before potential drill work later in 2022. The release does not suggest immediate production effects for metals markets.

title: Jane Street Global sues LME for $15.3 million for cancelling nickel trades
summary: Jane Street Global sued the LME for $15.3 million after the exchange cancelled nickel trades in March amid severe volatility when nickel prices doubled to over $100,000/t within hours. The LME is also facing a larger lawsuit from Elliott Associates and regulator probes over its suspension and cancellations.

title: SMM China Copper Cathode Output Declined by 1.0% MoM and 3.6% YoY to 819,200 mt in May_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s copper cathode output fell in May because of intensive smelter maintenance, with delayed maintenance and some raw-material tightness in the spot market. Blister copper supply remained tight, imports were disrupted, and blister TCs kept declining. June output is forecast higher but most smelters stay in maintenance.

title: Pure Nickel Prices Remained High Today and the Spot Transactions were Poor_SMM
summary: SMM reported that China’s nickel spot market stayed at a high level but prices edged down: Jinchuan and NORNICKEL nickel were quoted around 6,500–7,000 yuan/mt, averaging 6,750, down 500 yuan from the previous day. Premiums narrowed slightly as SHFE remained high, but spot trades were poor.

title: How Is the Alloy Sector Performing after Pure Nickel Imports Turned Profitable?_SMM
summary: SMM reports pure nickel spot import premiums turned profitable from May 16 to June 1, prompting a drop in Shanghai bonded nickel inventories despite ongoing concern about weak downstream demand. Demand is improving after customs clearance and easing COVID impacts. With tight visible supply and warrant shortages, near-term nickel prices are expected to keep rising.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Operating and Financial Update
summary: Nevada Copper said geotechnical issues at its Pumpkin Hollow underground mine have delayed access to East South stopes, reducing expected concentrate production in Q2 2022 and pushing most stope ore production to August. It also details progress in East North development and seeks additional funding.

title: SKRR Exploration Inc. enters into Definitive Agreement to acquire a 100% interest in the Nickel Peak Claim Group, Omineca mining district of British Columbia
summary: SKRR Exploration Inc. has signed a definitive agreement to acquire full ownership of the Nickel Peak Claim Group in British Columbia’s Omineca mining district. The asset is described as a nickel prospect, which can modestly improve sentiment on future nickel supply, though it is not immediate production.

title: Tsingshan Group Planned to Commission a Project with 50,000 mt Refined Nickel in Indonesia_SMM
summary: SMM reports Tsingshan Group plans to commission a project in Indonesia producing 50,000 mt of refined nickel. The refinery uses Tsingshan nickel matte as raw material to make nickel plate and refined output. Start-up timing is not confirmed, but the project adds upside to supply expectations for nickel.

title: The INE Bonded Copper Contract was under Pressure as the US Bond Yields Continued to Rebound_SMM
summary: SMM reports INE bonded copper 2208 trending downward, closing at 64,980 yuan/mt (down 170 yuan/mt). The drop is attributed to higher US bond yields from inflation worries and a slight rebound in the US dollar index, which weighed on copper prices and encouraged shorts.

title: Canada Nickel Completes Additional Property Acquisitions
summary: Canada Nickel announced it has agreed to acquire a 100% interest in the Bannockburn Nickel Property near Matachewan, Ontario, and to share more details on other recently acquired properties. The news is limited to land acquisitions and does not indicate near-term changes to nickel output or supply.

title: Bell Copper Corporation: Bell Copper Reports Big Sandy Assays
summary: Bell Copper announced full assay results from drillhole BS-3 at its Big Sandy porphyry copper project in Arizona, including 200 meters grading 0.42% copper and metallurgical scoping work for chalcocite recovery. The company states future drilling will test supergene enrichment; no resource is yet defined.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Launches 2022 Exploration Program at the High-Grade Carmacks Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Yukon, Canada
summary: Granite Creek Copper announced it is starting a 2022 Induced Polarization (IP) survey at its Carmacks Cu-Au-Ag project in Yukon, Canada, to improve targeting of deeper and offset mineralization. The release focuses on exploration planning and resource/PEA work; it does not indicate production or supply changes.

title: Grid Metals : and Canada Nickel Announce Sale of Bannockburn Nickel Property
summary: Grid Metals and Canada Nickel announced a deal under which Canada Nickel will acquire the Bannockburn nickel property, paying Grid with 2 million shares. The company highlights drilling intersections and processing work indicating potential to produce a nickel concentrate, improving near-term perceptions of nickel resource development prospects.

title: SHFE Nickel Rose As the Low Inventories Provided Support for the Nickel Prices_SMM
summary: SHFE nickel (ni 2207) rose modestly on June 7, supported by historically low LME and SHFE nickel inventories despite slight customs clearance improving supply. Domestic supply remained tight, and improving expectations for new-energy vehicle demand boosted nickel sulfate demand, though downstream remained cautious, capping upside.

title: Goldman Sachs Predicts Extreme Copper Supply Crunch
summary: Goldman Sachs metals strategist Nick Snowdon warns that predictions of copper supply constraints could prove correct, potentially driving copper to $15,000/ton. The outlook rests on sharply rising demand over the next decade from electric vehicles, power and renewable projects, while supply remains insufficient to meet that growth.

title: US traders sue London Metals Exchange over nickel market disruption
summary: US traders sued the LME over how it handled the March nickel disruption, alleging unlawful cancellation of trades before suspension. The nickel market had spiked after a short position by Tsingshan-linked activity amplified the move. The FCA is investigating the episode, adding uncertainty for nickel pricing.

title: Exchange execs clash over LME nickel closure
summary: ICE Futures Europe president Stuart Williams criticizes the LME’s March closure of the nickel market and cancellation of trades following extreme price swings. He argues circuit breakers might have prevented the shutdown, warning of knock-on effects for participants. An LME executive defends the action as a “tough decision.”

title: Shape Corp and Hydro Aluminium Metal enter partnership to develop automotive products utilizing 75% recycled aluminum scrap
summary: Shape Corp partnered with Hydro to bring to the US automotive components using Hydro CIRCAL® recycled aluminum with at least 75% post-consumer scrap. The materials are positioned as lower-carbon and suitable for vehicle lightweighting. Shape also references expanding extrusion capacity in Ohio, supporting ongoing aluminum demand.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces 2022 Second Quarter Operating and Financial Results
summary: Copper Fox reported interim financial results and outlined continued exploration work across its copper projects, including metallurgical drilling updates and planned 2022 field programs. Management expects further results that could support future resource estimates, but no production or supply commitments were changed, implying limited near-term impact on copper pricing.

title: Report: LME Copper Ended Lower as Demand Concerns Affected Market Sentiment_SMM
summary: LME copper ended lower on June 7, falling 0.47% to $9,699/mt, as a stronger US dollar reinforced concerns about China’s demand. While LME copper inventories dropped by 20,200 mt to a multiweek low, aluminium inventories fell to a 21-year low, yet aluminium futures still slipped.

title: Second US trading firm sues LME over nickel trading shutdown
summary: A second US trading firm, Jane Street, sues the LME over the exchange’s cancellation of nickel trades in March, alongside a larger Elliott Management claim. The cancellations followed a nickel price surge amid Ukraine invasion-related volatility, and the lawsuits target the legality of the cancellations.

title: KCM Seeks Investors for Konkola Copper Mine, Planning to Shut down Nchanga Smelter for Maintenance_SMM
summary: KCM’s provisional liquidator said it will seek equity investors to fund Zambia’s Konkola Deep Mining Project and announced the resumption of open-pit mining. KCM also plans $17 million in annual maintenance shutdowns at the Nchanga copper smelter (311,000 mt capacity) alongside measures to expand production at other operations.

title: Pure Nickel Premiums Narrowed Again but the Transactions were still Poor_SMM
summary: SMM reports Jinchuan and Nornickel nickel in Shanghai quoted at 5,000-5,500 yuan/mt, averaging 5,250, down 1,500 yuan from the prior day. Premiums narrowed and nickel briquette prices fell to 222,500-223,500 yuan/mt, but transactions remained poor because futures prices were still high.

title: Cyprium Metals extends resource potential of Maroochydore copper-cobalt deposit
summary: Cyprium Metals said initial reverse-circulation drilling at its Maroochydore copper-cobalt deposit in Western Australia extended near-surface mineralisation to 3,000m. Several intervals reported significant copper grades (up to 1.92% Cu) alongside cobalt, supporting prospects and potential future development, mildly bullish for copper sentiment.

title: SHFE Aluminium Fell Slightly and the Spot Market of Aluminium Ingots was Weak_SMM
summary: On June 8, SHFE aluminium fluctuated around 20,800 yuan/mt and slipped below the daily moving average. The east China aluminium ingot premium stayed around 50 yuan/mt, but warehouse-related issues kept transactions weak. Zhongyuan ingot prices were quoted at discounts of 70–80 yuan/mt to SMM A00, with some at larger discounts.

title: S.Korea's LG Energy Solution launches nickel processing plants in Indonesia
summary: LG Energy Solution broke ground on nickel processing plants in Indonesia, including a $3.5 billion smelter producing nickel sulfate and a $2.4 billion cathode/precursor facility for EV batteries. It also plans a joint $300 million nickel mine with Antam. Indonesia’s ongoing nickel downstream push bolsters demand outlook.

title: Afghanistan: Chinese company demands revision of contract in Aynak Logar copper mining project
summary: A Chinese firm is demanding revisions to its contract for the Aynak Logar copper mining project near Kabul, Afghanistan. The Logar deposit is described as the world’s second-largest copper deposit. The contract dispute could delay development, weighing on expectations for future copper supply.

title: Chile's Copper Exports in May Totalled $3.76 billion, down 18.3% YoY_SMM
summary: Chile’s central bank said copper exports in May totaled $3.76 billion, down 18.3% year on year. Despite the decline, Chile posted a $851 million trade surplus. Overall exports rose and imports increased as well, but the YoY fall in copper export receipts is a negative copper supply-demand signal.

title: The Aluminium Scrap Throughout of East China Nonferrous Metal City in Linyi Declined_SMM
summary: SMM says aluminium scrap throughput at East China Nonferrous Metal City in Linyi fell sharply in late May/early June and again for the week. The drop is linked to reduced supply as aluminium’s price shock triggered wait-and-see sentiment and some upstream traders took a holiday. Monitoring A00 inventories is urged.

title: CanAlaska Uranium Ltd.: CanAlaska Announces 10,000 Metre Phase 2 Drill Program Started on Manibridge High-Grade Nickel Project
summary: CanAlaska, via partner Metal Energy, has started a 10,000-metre phase two drill program at the Manibridge nickel project in Manitoba, targeting nickel-copper sulphide mineralization near a past-producing mine. The release cites prior drilling success and notes a strengthening nickel market, but no assays or production changes are provided.

title: Bell Copper Corporation: Bell Copper Results of its Special General Meeting, Approval of Shareholder Rights Plan, 2022 Stock Option Plan and Grant of Stock Options
summary: Bell Copper reports shareholder approval of a shareholder rights plan and a new 2022 fixed stock option plan, including granting 10 million incentive stock options. The company is focused on exploring copper projects in Arizona, but the release is mainly governance/compensation with no direct change to copper production or trade flows.

title: CanAlaska Announces 10,000 Metre Phase 2 Drill Program Started on Manibridge High-Grade Nickel Project
summary: CanAlaska’s partner has started a 10,000-metre phase-two drilling program at the Manibridge high-grade nickel project in Manitoba, targeting extensions near a past-producing mine. The program aims to define nickel-copper sulphide mineralization; earlier drilling intersected nickel mineralization and copper/nickel were confirmed with assays pending.

title: Dispute between artisan gold miners in Peru leaves 14 people dead
summary: Fourteen people were killed in an armed dispute between small-scale miners in southern Peru. Reuters notes the violence follows earlier unrest, including a fire allegedly set by wildcat copper miners at Southern Copper Corp’s Los Chancas project, raising risks of disruption to copper supply.

title: London copper eases ahead of ECB meeting; demand recovery hopes support
summary: London copper prices eased 0.4% ahead of the ECB meeting, with analysts citing muted trading until the policy outcome. Better-than-expected Chinese economic data and falling LME inventories (down 3,875 tonnes) supported hopes for a demand recovery, but the near-term direction reported was lower.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Royalty Announces Q1 Royalty Distribution from the Caserones Copper-Molybdenum Mine in Chile
summary: EMX Royalty will receive about US$2.7 million in Q1 royalty distributions from Chile’s Caserones copper-molybdenum mine, based on copper output and NSR terms. The company attributes higher payments to strong copper prices and robust production throughput, reinforcing bullish copper expectations.

title: Luminex Expedites Drilling at the El Hito Copper-Molybdenum Porphyry Target at Central Condor
summary: Luminex Resources announced expedited drilling at the El Hito copper-molybdenum porphyry target in Ecuador, citing a newly identified 320-metre zone where rock chips mostly exceed 0.4% copper. A 1,500-metre drill program is expected to start next week, while assays are pending from other holes.

title: EV Nickel Phase 2 Drilling Results- 48.6 metres Grading 1.31% Nickel from W4, Samples Submitted for Met Testing
summary: EV Nickel Phase 2 drilling returned 48.6 metres grading 1.31% nickel (from W4). Samples are submitted for further met testing. The reported assay results strengthen confidence in the project’s potential resource quality and prospective nickel supply, which is typically supportive for short-term nickel sentiment.

title: Rockridge Resources to Commence Fully Funded Drill Program at its High-Grade Knife Lake Copper Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Rockridge Resources says it will start a fully funded drill program at its high-grade Knife Lake copper project in Saskatchewan. While it does not change production immediately, the announcement can lift expectations for future resource definition and copper supply prospects, providing modest bullish sentiment for copper prices.

title: Wind, solar to replace coal-fired power for Rio Tinto aluminium
summary: Rio Tinto will invest in large-scale wind and solar projects in Queensland to supply electricity for its aluminium operations in the Gladstone region. The company issued a call for proposals to meet energy demand for the Boyne smelter and its Yarwun and Queensland Alumina refineries, replacing coal-fired power.

title: Miners are Increasing Operations In Copper, Lithium & Cobalt Projects Owing To Rising Demand
summary: Fitch Solutions expects miners to increase investments in copper and nickel projects because demand is rising from renewable energy, batteries, and electric vehicles. While companies focus more on developing existing assets than launching new ones, the outlook supports constructive near-term sentiment for copper and nickel supply-demand fundamentals.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Intercept of 23 Meters of 1.55% Copper from Dalmacia Target at Its Punitaqui Mine
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reports high-grade drill results at its Dalmacia target within the Punitaqui copper project in Chile, including multiple copper intercepts above 1.5% and up to 2.5%. The company links results to planned mine resumption in late 2022 and potential increased confidence in future copper supply from the site.

title: Production cost rise is a concern for alumina refining in China as downturn deepens
summary: China’s alumina refineries face higher production costs as bauxite and caustic soda prices jumped in April and northern supply tightened. With alumina prices softening amid oversupply, traders say Henan refineries may trim output, but cuts are uncertain and not yet reflected in prices. Possible aluminium cost/supply effects remain mixed.

title: Eagle Plains Resources Ltd.: Eagle Plains' Partner Rockridge Resources to Commence a Fully Funded Drill Program at the High-Grade Knife Lake Copper Project, Saskatchewan
summary: Eagle Plains and partner Rockridge plan to start a fully funded diamond drill program in mid-July at the Knife Lake copper VMS project in Saskatchewan, targeting VTEM anomalies and down-dip extensions. Prior drilling reported high-grade copper intervals, but the news is exploratory rather than production or supply-related.

title: LG begins building nickel processing plants in Indonesia
summary: LG Energy Solution has begun building two nickel processing plants in Indonesia, including a smelter targeting 150,000 tonnes of nickel sulfate annually, plus precursor and cathode facilities. The investment also includes a joint nickel mine with Antam, supporting nickel supply-chain demand as Indonesia pushes downstream development.

title: China Produced 3.435 million mt of Aluminium in May and the Production Capacity will Continue to Increase_SMM
summary: SMM data show China aluminium production rose in May and more capacity is expected to resume in June, lifting operating capacity and output. Demand remains modest despite easing transport/pandemic issues, with social inventory falling by less than usual. Billet inventory edges higher, implying near-term price pressure for aluminium.

title: China Metallurgical-grade Alumina Output Increase to 6.595 million mt in May_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s metallurgical-grade alumina output rose in May, with new capacity driving higher production and shifting fundamentals from shortage to surplus. It notes net imports were negative and alumina prices corrected. More capacity is expected to ramp in Q3, keeping long-term alumina surplus while potentially easing smelter feed costs.

title: Timmins suggested at Mining Expo to be a potential hotbed for nickel
summary: Canada Nickel’s CEO says the Timmins area could become a major nickel district, building on the Crawford Project—described as the largest nickel sulphide discovery since the early 1970s. The company expects to advance a feasibility study, seek permitting, and potentially find additional deposits. The narrative supports nickel supply growth for EV demand.

title: Peruvian Community Allows Las Bambas Copper Mine to Restart after Shutdown for 51 Days_SMM
summary: Peruvian indigenous communities agreed on June 9 to lift protests against MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine after a shutdown lasting over 50 days. The communities have approved a 30-day truce and reopening negotiations, easing disruption risk. With Las Bambas among the top copper producers, copper supply expectations should improve.

title: Operating Rates of Aluminium Billet Producers Using Aluminium Liquid to Extend Upward Trend in June_SMM
summary: SMM survey data show aluminium billet producers’ operating rates using aluminium liquid rose to 71.2% in May, aided by better aluminium-liquid availability and improving regional supply. North China disruption is expected to improve. Output and downstream demand are forecast to recover in June, lifting operating rates to ~72%.

title: China Produced 14,300 mt of Refined Nickel in May amid the Production Resumption_SMM
summary: SMM reports China produced 14,300 mt of refined nickel in May, up 10.59% month-on-month and 15.11% year-on-year. Output rose as smelters and some salt factories resumed or started production due to low LME nickel prices and attractive profits. June production is expected to increase further.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Stopped Falling and Stabilised due to the Rising Domestic Premiums and the Narrowed Import Losses_SMM
summary: SMM says Yangshan copper premiums under warrants were $45–60/mt, stabilizing after stopping their fall as domestic premiums rose and import losses narrowed. Importers slowed dumping and buyers preferred domestic copper. Traders showed weak willingness for only small orders, limiting sharp premium upside.

title: DRC: False alarm says China Moly, denies Tenke copper-cobalt mine take over
summary: Congo’s state mining firm Gecamines and China Moly dispute over Tenke Fungurume (TFM) led to a temporary court-appointed administrator taking charge. China Moly denies any management change and says production continues normally. The enforced ruling and royalty/reserve concerns create copper risk, though impact seems limited short term.

title: SMM Analysis: Production Growth and Consumption Recovery to Keep Aluminium Prices Volatile_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium rose then fell to close up 0.36% and highlights May’s year-on-year increase in aluminium output. Despite higher production and some capacity gains, social inventories of aluminium ingots kept declining, supporting prices. Net effect is a tug-of-war, implying continued volatility rather than a clear trend.

title: Castillo Copper provides strategic update
summary: Castillo Copper outlined strategic updates across its Australian and Zambian projects, emphasizing drilling campaigns and efforts to formalize off-take and processing paths for deposits including Big One and Cangai. The company is also advancing copper targets in Zambia via potential joint-venture funding and continued exploration.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 188,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Chinese nickel ore port inventories fell 188,000 wmt WoW to 4.869 million wmt as Ni content dropped to 38,300 mt. Seven major ports also saw declines. Although shipments from the Philippines resumed after rains eased, ship supply is tight and NPI plants drew down stocks, keeping inventories low.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Provides Update on 2022 Exploration Program at MPD Copper-Gold Porphyry Project in Southern British Columbia
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. provided an update on its fully funded 2022 exploration program at the 100% owned MPD copper-gold porphyry project in southern British Columbia. The company restarted drilling in March, added a second rig, completed 11 holes, and plans further drilling and 3D IP/soil geochemistry, with assays expected in late June.

title: Kodiak Provides Update on 2022 Exploration Program at MPD Copper-Gold Porphyry Project in Southern British Columbia
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. provided an update on its fully funded 2022 exploration at the MPD copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia. The company reported drilling progress at the Gate Zone, a new 3D IP survey underway, and planned assay results in late June, with further drilling across multiple targets.

title: MMG to restart copper concentrate production at Las Bambas, Peru
summary: MMG plans to restart copper concentrate production at Las Bambas in Peru. The restart should lift near-term concentrate availability and reduce outage risk, which can improve expectations for copper supply/demand tightness over the coming days to weeks.

title: China Moly denies DRC takeover of its Tenke copper-cobalt mine
summary: China Moly denies the DRC has taken control of its Tenke Fungurume copper-cobalt mine. Congo authorities said a court-appointed administrator assumed charge amid a shareholder dispute tied to suspected reserve underreporting and royalty payments. China Moly says management and production continue normally as talks proceed.

title: Nickel North Invites Shareholders and Investment Community to Visit Company at Booth 2919 at PDAC 2022 in Toronto, June 13-15, 2022
summary: Nickel North Exploration invites investors to PDAC and discusses an updated NI 43-101 resource at its Hawk Ridge Ni-Cu-PGE project, including grades for inferred deposits and a newly intersected massive sulfide zone. The release references historical and May 3, 2022 LME nickel prices, but provides no immediate supply or demand shock.

title: Aluminum ingot manufacture increases 4 percent in first 2 mo...
summary: Iran’s IMIDRO said aluminium ingot production rose 4% year-on-year in the first two months of the Iranian calendar year (March 21-May 21), reaching 89,718 tons versus 86,216 tons a year earlier. Output increases at major producers like IRALCO are highlighted.

title: The LME Is Facing $500 Million In Lawsuits Over Nickel Short Squeeze
summary: The LME faces nearly $500 million in lawsuits from Jane Street and Elliot Management over how it handled March 8’s nickel short squeeze, including cancellation of trades. The piece highlights persistent low liquidity and falling open interest on both LME and SHFE, keeping nickel sentiment pressured.

title: Chile and Ecuador Restart Copper Talks After Yearslong Impasse
summary: Bloomberg/BNN highlights that Chile and Ecuador have restarted copper talks after a yearslong impasse. The development could affect market expectations around copper supply, trade arrangements, or related policy decisions. The excerpt provides no details, making direction and magnitude of any short-term copper price move uncertain.

title: SHFE aluminium Likely to Remain Rangebound amid Strong Wait-and-See Sentiment _SMM
summary: SMM expects SHFE/LME aluminium to remain rangebound. ECB policy signals and US inflation concerns weigh on sentiment, while China’s aluminium supply slightly rises after a capacity restart and output increases. A collateral scandal triggered trader selling and wider spot discounts, but low inventories and possible consumption recovery support prices.

title: Decline in Alumina Prices Accelerated amid Deteriorating Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s metallurgical alumina prices declining across provinces and overseas benchmarks stabilizing around $360/mt FOB WA. Output rose in May and net exports turned to a surplus, shifting the market from deficit to oversupply. Profit erosion from bauxite and caustic costs limits dumping, while smelters’ near-term alumina demand is subdued.

title: Aluminium Costs Dropped Slightly due to Decline in Alumina and Electricity Prices _SMM
summary: SMM reports domestic alumina prices fell again and Guangxi will apply preferential grid tariffs, potentially lowering electricity costs by about 0.1 yuan/kwh. Aluminium smelter weighted average power costs dropped, reducing smelting costs and expanding profits. In the near term, falling alumina amid excess supply supports softer input costs for aluminium.

title: Iran's alumina powder output increases 11 percent in first 2...
summary: Iran’s IMIDRO reported that alumina powder production rose 11% to 42,406 tons in the first two months (March 21–May 21) versus about 38,000 tons a year earlier. Higher alumina supply can support aluminium refining capacity and weigh on aluminium prices short term.

title: Aluminium hits 6-month low as demand prospects deteriorate
summary: LME aluminium slid to a six-month low as investors feared weaker Chinese demand from COVID lockdowns, higher inflation and interest-rate hikes, and a stronger U.S. dollar. Inventories are at low levels, but macro-driven demand concerns outweighed support. Copper and nickel also declined during the sell-off.

title: Thesis Gold Inc.: Thesis Gold Discovers New Gold & Copper Zone near the Bingo Occurrence; Drills 35.57 Metres of 1.76 g/t Gold Equivalent
summary: Thesis Gold reported five-hole assay results from the Bingo Zone at its Ranch Gold Project in British Columbia, including intervals with gold and copper mineralization (up to 0.45% Cu). While this indicates potential copper-bearing high-sulphidation/porphyry-related system at depth, it does not signal near-term production supply changes.

title: Aluminium Ingot Inventory Maintains Downward Trend_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s social aluminium ingot inventories totalled 825,000 mt on June 13, down from last Thursday and end-May, with declines led by Wuxi, Shanghai and Foshan. Some warehouses/outlets are missing in stats after a collateral scandal, and arrivals may slow destocking.

title: China Nickel Sulphate Output Rebounded from Lows in May_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s nickel sulphate output rose in May as some producers restarted and tolling increased. Demand stayed weak, but raw material costs fell, easing nickel salt prices and improving plant margins. For June-July, recovery in precursor production should lift nickel sulphate prices from lows, though abundant feed supply may cap upside.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Prepares for Drilling Program on Eaglehead Copper Project
summary: Copper Fox provided an update on its Eaglehead polymetallic porphyry copper project, including preparations for a 2022 drilling program in early July pending Notice of Work approval and permits. The work focuses on geological model verification and testing continuity of porphyry mineralization between zones, with no results or supply changes reported.

title: Chile, Ecuador resume talks over stalled Llurimagua copper project
summary: Ecuador and Chile resumed talks over the stalled Llurimagua copper-molybdenum project after Ecuador’s National Mining Company won a suspension of two arbitration processes from Codelco. The project remains in advanced exploration and faces environmental opposition, making any near-term copper supply effect uncertain within days to weeks.

title: DGAP-News: Hot Chili Limited: Stunning 17m Visual Drill Intersection Extends High Grade Copper Zone by 120m at Valentina
summary: Hot Chili Limited said diamond drilling at Chile’s Valentina deposit extended the high-grade copper zone by 120m, including a 17m visual estimate of 2–3% Cu from 22m and 8m at 4–5% Cu from 28m, with assay results pending. Additional holes and PFS/port workstreams are progressing.

title: AVINO ET AREA DRILLS HIGH GRADE SILVER & COPPER IN MULTIPLE HOLES
summary: Avino Silver & Gold Mines announced deep drill results from its ET area in Mexico, reporting significant copper-bearing intercepts alongside silver. The company says drilling confirms downdip continuity of the vein to at least 290 metres below Level 17 and suggests higher copper mineralization at depth.

title: Manitou Gold Intersects 0.25% Nickel over 48 m and Update
summary: Manitou Gold announced discovery of a nickel-bearing ultramafic complex at its Goudreau project and reported diamond drilling results including a 0.25% Ni intersection over 48 m. It also notes ultramafic intrusions along a deformation zone analogous to Crawford/Dumont nickel deposits. The release is early exploration and not production-related.

title: Seabridge to Begin Drilling a Cluster of Gold-Copper Porphyry Targets
summary: Seabridge Gold says drilling will start at its 100%-owned Iskut project in British Columbia, testing gold-copper targets at Bronson Slope and Quartz Rise, supported by magnetotelluric surveys. The release describes copper-bearing mineralization in resource targets but does not indicate production or near-term supply changes.

title: Anteros Metals Provides Update on Airborne Geophysical Surveying at the Hopedale Nickel Project, Labrador
summary: Anteros Metals updates that Phase One VTEM airborne electromagnetic surveying is underway at its Hopedale nickel project in Labrador, aiming to detect deep conductivity anomalies tied to nickel mineralization and possibly Ni-Cu-Co sulphides. The company is awaiting results to guide future surface work and potential drilling, with no production impacts stated.

title: Aluminum Prices Are Taking A Beating
summary: Aluminum prices weakened in May as China’s Shanghai lockdown returned, curbing manufacturing and reducing aluminum imports, while primary output stayed high. At the same time, LME inventories fell and oil/energy prices rose, supporting costs. Overall direction remains unclear amid competing demand and supply signals.

title: Osisko Metals Announces Filing of Technical Report on Gaspé Copper; Update on Previously-Announced Private Placement
summary: Osisko Metals announced it has filed a technical report related to its Gaspé copper project and provided an update on a previously announced private placement. Such corporate/technical milestones can influence expectations for future copper resources, though the provided content lacks details on production timelines.

title: Lunnon Metals reports maiden resource estimate for Baker Shoot target within Kambalda nickel project
summary: Lunnon Metals reported a maiden JORC mineral resource at the Baker Shoot target in its Kambalda nickel project: 568,000 tonnes at 2.8% nickel for 15,800t contained nickel. The discovery lifts the project’s total contained nickel to 64,300t and prompts further drilling, studies, and permitting.

title: The Tight Domestic Bauxite Mines Supply Affected the Production of Some Alumina Plants_SMM
summary: Bauxite mine supply in China tightened sharply, worsening after Indonesia announced a bauxite export ban. Alumina plants in Shanxi, Henan and Guizhou faced shortages and had to buy imported ore at high prices. Rising ore costs and reduced output are expected to keep bauxite prices firm, supporting aluminium via constrained alumina supply.

title: LME Aluminium Hit a Six-Month Low As Demand May Fall_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: LME aluminium fell to a six-month low on June 13 amid concern over possible additional China lockdowns and a sell-off linked to rising inflation and interest rates. Demand for industrial metals is expected to weaken. The piece also notes falling LME copper prices, while aluminium inventories are at a multi-year low.

title: Three Valley Copper Announces MTV Files for Creditor
summary: Three Valley Copper’s 95.1% Chilean subsidiary Minera Tres Valles (MTV) commenced Chilean judicial restructuring to seek creditor protection. The filing is expected to trigger an immediate demobilization and a temporary halt in third-party ore processing, with curtailed operations and cash extending only through August 2022, increasing near-term copper supply risk.

title: Argentina offers tax sweeteners to encourage fledgling copper sector
summary: Argentina will introduce a voluntary, optional tax regime for new copper investments that can replace the current 4.5% export duty with a variable rate between 0% and 8% tied to the copper price. The move aims to stimulate production and exports while improving fiscal and foreign-currency outcomes.

title: Vietnam reviews anti-dumping measure imposed on Chinese aluminium
summary: Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade announced a second review of anti-dumping measures on specified aluminium product imports from China. The review covers several HS-coded items and will reassess the duties’ application, potentially sustaining protection for domestic sellers and influencing aluminium import flows in the near term.

title: Operating Rates of Secondary Aluminium Alloy Plants Increased Slightly in May Thanks to Improved Pandemic, But Its Prices Fell Further amid Weak Demand _SMM
summary: SMM says China’s secondary aluminium alloy plant operating rates rose in May, but prices fell further. Weak auto-related demand, declining die-casting orders, and profit erosion from high scrap and freight costs reduced production and quotes. Import volumes eased as the aluminium price ratio worsened, extending downward pressure.

title: Ministry reviews anti-dumping measure imposed on Chinese aluminum
summary: The Ministry of Industry and Trade announced a second review of anti-dumping measures on specified aluminum product codes imported from China. Initial duties imposed in 2020 and continued after a first review in 2021 remain under assessment, with the investigation citing dumping and harm to the domestic aluminum industry.

title: Spot Premiums Increased amid the Tight Pure Nickel Supply_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that spot premiums for pure nickel increased as the future price corrected sharply and spot supply tightened. Traders bought on dips when premiums were low, lifting pre-nickel premiums. Nickel briquette prices fell mainly because premiums narrowed, and demand/transactions were weaker versus mainstream nickel plate feedstocks.

title: Copper Concentrate Imports Rose Sharply in May, and the Monthly Import Volume Hit a Record High_SMM
summary: China’s copper concentrate imports rose to 2.189 million mt in May, up 16.2% month-on-month and 12.5% year-on-year, with January–May imports hitting a record. April fell due to the Xiangguang shutdown and weaker purchasing. Peru restart and limited port impacts helped May recover.

title: Upside Room of Copper Prices to be Limited, with Eyes on Domestic Consumption_SMM
summary: SMM says Fed and ECB rate-hike expectations strengthened the US dollar and weighed on base metals, limiting copper’s upside. China’s stimulus and improving cathode output, plus a large LME inventory drop, support copper prices. However, weaker demand signals (PMIs, soft orders) suggest gains may be capped into June.

title: AIP BECOMES OWNER OF ALUMINIUM DUFFEL
summary: American Industrial Partners acquired 100% ownership of the Aluminium Duffel aluminium rolling mill in Belgium from Ecnavla 8 UK Ltd. The deal follows administration and court decisions related to refinancing defaults. AIP expects no operational disruption and plans additional capital, including working capital and investments.

title: Ministry reviews anti-dumping measure imposed on Chinese aluminum - Economy - Vietnam News | Politics, Business, Economy, Society, Life, Sports
summary: Vietnam’s MoIT announced a second review of anti-dumping duties on specific aluminium product codes imported from China. The original duties (2.49%–35.58%) were imposed after an investigation found dumping and harm to the domestic industry. After the first review, duties were continued, and the second review may keep them in place.

title: Opinion: LME nickel lawsuits are about principle as much as money
summary: The Reuters opinion says lawsuits over the LME nickel meltdown highlight disputes over the exchange’s handling of an “orderly market” during March 8’s trading halt and trade cancellations. It argues confidence may be damaged and liquidity may shift to OTC, pressuring nickel participation and sentiment soon.

title: Argentina launches flexible copper export tax regime
summary: Argentina has launched a flexible export tax regime for copper exports. By altering exporter incentives and potentially reducing physical shipments abroad, the policy can affect near-term global supply expectations for copper and may therefore exert downward pressure on copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Nickel Prices may be Kept at the Current Level amid a Sufficient Supply of Pure Nickel_SMM
summary: SMM reports that after May’s Fed-driven rate hikes, SHFE nickel fell while LME liquidity remained thin and prices could stay volatile. Domestic policies and improving downstream operations boosted mid-May prices, but strong pure nickel supply and higher refined output in China should limit gains in June. Warrant scarcity warrants caution for shorts.

title: Nickel debacle weakens UK's case on clearing supervision
summary: The LME cancelled roughly $4 billion of nickel trades in early March after a disorderly move following Russia’s invasion, prompting lawsuits and criticism of the clearing house’s decision-making. The piece also highlights margin behavior, lack of circuit breakers, and UK supervisory scrutiny—raising near-term nickel market uncertainty.

title: Nickel drama highlights Tsingshan's role in energy transition | News | Eco-Business
summary: Russia’s invasion sparked a rapid nickel market disruption, sending LME prices up about 250% and leading the LME to suspend trading after a major short squeeze and margin calls. The piece also argues buyers may shun Russian nickel for EVs, increasing reliance on Chinese/Indonesian supply amid energy-transition demand growth.

title: ZCCM: ZCCM-Investments Holdings Plc_Market Announcement Engagement of Rothschild and Co to Assist with the Strategic Review of Mopani Copper Mines Plc.
summary: ZCCM Investments Holdings engaged Rothschild & Co to assist with a strategic review aimed at ensuring sustainability and optimal operation of Mopani Copper Mines. The review is expected to conclude in about six months (extendable). No immediate production or supply change is stated, limiting short-term copper price pressure.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement of up to C$2.0 Million
summary: EV Nickel Inc. announced a non-brokered private placement of up to C$2.0 million to fund Phase 3 exploration on its Langmuir and Shaw Dome projects in Ontario. The flow-through proceeds are earmarked for “Canadian exploration expenses” and mining expenditures, with no direct production or supply change disclosed.

title: China aluminium fraud allegations suggest lessons not learned from Qingdao
summary: China-wide allegations of financing fraud at aluminium warehouses—showing physical stocks below reported levels and suspected double pledging of the same aluminium stocks—have raised concerns about collateral risk and potential forced unwinding. The article links the emergence of irregularities to recent aluminium price weakness and tighter liquidity conditions.

title: Fabled Copper Corp.: Fabled Book 6 Copper Occurrence reports up to 7.73% Copper in Chip Sampling
summary: Fabled Copper Corp. announced additional 2021 surface fieldwork results from its Muskwa Copper Project, detailing chip sampling along the Book 6 vein target. Samples reported multiple intervals with elevated copper, including up to 7.73% Cu in a chip sample. The release is exploratory and does not signal immediate production.

title: Salina grain elevator sees theft of over $30K in copper wire
summary: Salina police are investigating the theft of over $30,000 worth of copper wire from a grain elevator. Authorities say scrap metal thefts aren’t rising locally, noting copper theft slowed when prices fell. The article quotes local scrap prices and emphasizes the incident rather than any broader copper supply disruption.

title: European aluminium billet premiums fall following surge of overseas imports
summary: European aluminium 6063 extrusion billet premiums in Germany, Italy and Spain have fallen as a rise in overseas imports creates “extreme oversupply.” Demand has weakened with poor automotive activity and consumers delaying purchases. With aggressive low offers and ample stocks, traders expect billet premiums to continue trending down.

title: Opinion: Aluminum tariffs increase inflation, costs to consumers
summary: The article claims Section 232 aluminum tariffs are contributing to high inflation by raising aluminum costs faced by U.S. beverage canmakers that rely on imported and taxed aluminum inputs. It urges Senators Toomey and Warner to repeal the tariffs, arguing this would lower aluminum prices and consumer costs.

title: London Metal Exchange Faces Complaint from US Hedge Fund Group Over Cancelled Nickel Trades
summary: Elliot Management filed a lawsuit against the LME in English High Court seeking $456 million after the exchange suspended nickel futures contracts and cancelled trades in early March. The case highlights controversy around LME handling of nickel contracts, which can contribute to near-term uncertainty and downside pressure for nickel pricing.

title: Doré Copper Files Technical Report for Its Preliminary Economic Asessement of Hub-and-Spoke Operation in Chibougamau, Quebec
summary: Doré Copper Mining filed an NI 43-101 technical report for a preliminary economic assessment of its Chibougamau hub-and-spoke complex in Quebec. The PEA covers multiple copper projects feeding the Copper Rand mill, supporting plans for subsequent feasibility work and permitting. It is mainly a forward-looking copper development signal.

title: Doré Copper Files Technical Report for Its Preliminary
summary: Doré Copper Mining Corp. filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Chibougamau hub-and-spoke complex (Corner Bay, Devlin, Joe Mann) feeding its Copper Rand mill. The release reiterates a PEA and plans for feasibility and permits, but provides no immediate operational or supply change.

title: How Are Australian Aluminium Smelters Performing amid Power Supply Shortage?_SMM
summary: Australia faces power shortages after AEMO capped wholesale electricity prices, leading to shutdowns of some coal and gas plants and restricting supply. SMM says aluminium smelters are currently producing normally, but high power costs and spot-market exposure could trigger future production cuts, weighing on aluminium sentiment as LME aluminium falls.

title: Will China's nickel sulfate price bottom out amid increased feedstocks and weak demand?
summary: Fastmarkets reports China nickel sulfate prices falling and likely pressured by increased availability of feedstocks such as MHP and nickel matte, including higher imports and expanded Indonesian production. Weak domestic demand and some contract renegotiations are weighing on payables and supporting further downward risk, with LME nickel also declining.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Dipped 5,800 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM said Chinese copper inventories across major markets fell to 109,900 mt on June 17, down 5,800 mt from Monday. Shanghai and Jiangsu declined sharply as copper prices dropped and downstream firms restocked with pandemic-related consumption recovery. Next week’s arrivals may rise, but further inventory falls are possible if demand improves.

title: Aluminium Ingot Collateral Scandal Led to Wild Swings in Spot Premiums and Discounts _SMM
summary: Rumours that the same SHFE-approved aluminium ingot batches were repeatedly pledged as collateral triggered panic to ship out cargoes from warehouses in Foshan and other regions. This boosted spot aluminium scarcity and drove large swings, including Gongyi premiums rising from earlier discounts to ~200–280 yuan/mt after the scandal.

title: China Prebaked Anode Production Hit 2022's New High in May, Driven by Rising Aluminum Production _SMM
summary: China’s May 2022 prebaked anode output rose to 1.88mn mt, with operating rates at 77%. Pre-baked anode prices increased further in June, supported by a petroleum coke rebound. Aluminum smelters are ramping production, boosting anode demand, though carbon profits face pressure from weaker aluminum prices.

title: Nickel Spot Prices Dropped by 8% within Eight Trading Days_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports nickel prices falling sharply: SHFE nickel dropped for five days and spot refined #1 nickel fell about 8% since June 8 to 207,200 yuan/mt. The declines are linked to US Fed rate-hike concerns. Despite some premium strength from rare sources, demand remains slack and SMM expects nickel to stay rangebound at low levels.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 11,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says Chinese nickel ore inventories fell 11,000 wmt week-on-week to 4.88 million wmt as of June 17. Ni content totals 38,000 wmt, with declines across seven major ports. The supply gap persists after Philippines weather disruptions, keeping nickel ore tight and supporting nickel demand and prices.

title: NORNICKEL EXPANDS PARTNERSHIP WITH THE MURMANSK REGION GOVERNMENT
summary: Nornickel and the Murmansk Region government signed a memorandum to support local investment and “Big Copper,” a green roast-leach-electrowin copper production facility in Monchegorsk. The project includes high sulphur recovery and zero-discharge water management, plus capacity reconfiguration at Kola MMC to raise non-ferrous output.

title: Analysis of Global New Copper Concentrate Capacities and the Distribution_SMM
summary: SMM data estimates global copper mines will add up to 164,000 mt of new copper capacity in 2022, alongside further expansion lifting total new concentrate output to about 1.023 million mt. Major contributors include projects in Chile, Peru, Russia, Indonesia and Zambia, signaling rising supply expectations.

title: SHFE Nickel Fell Below 200,000 yuan/mt and will Gradually Return to the Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel dropped below 200,000 yuan/mt despite a brief rebound after the Fed rate hike boosted sentiment. However, growth worries persisted and prices weakened. LEM and SHFE nickel fell on increased short selling, with demand for alloys and stainless steel still poor and supply expected to ease early next week.

title: Copper edges up ahead of possible Chile strike
summary: Copper prices edged up as traders priced in strike risk at Chile’s Codelco, the world’s largest copper producer, alongside slightly better China activity data. LME copper rose 0.4% on the day, while aluminium weakened on a firmer dollar and softer China prospects; nickel rose modestly.

title: Aluminum Extruders Council Calls for Biden Administration
summary: The Aluminum Extruders Council urged the Biden Administration to defend CBP’s EAPA findings that Kingtom avoided U.S. aluminum extrusion duties by transshipping Chinese-origin extrusions via the Dominican Republic. The group also seeks CBP action to halt imports tied to forced-labor violations, potentially tightening supply and supporting aluminum prices.

title: Mainland aluminium imports drop by over 16 percent
summary: Mainland aluminium imports reportedly fell by more than 16%. A drop in import volumes usually signals reduced near-term buying/procurement (or weaker demand), which can ease supply tightness and pressure aluminium prices over the next days to a few weeks, assuming the change is not immediately offset elsewhere.

title: Aurubis Richmond recycled-copper smelter will be the nation's first
summary: Georgia officials backed Aurubis Richmond, a $340 million recycled-copper smelter in Augusta slated to start in January 2024. The plant will process about 90,000 tons of complex recycling materials annually and extract roughly 35,000 tons of blister copper, supporting the EV supply chain.

title: Reducing aluminum tariffs can ease inflation
summary: The article says Colorado’s inflation has been worsened by Section 232 tariffs that have pushed aluminum prices higher. It argues that repealing the tariffs would ease inflation by lowering aluminum input costs and helping supply. It references bipartisan U.S. Senate legislation aimed at ending the tariff regime.

title: Chinese firm's hopes of resolving royalties row at massive DR Congo copper and cobalt mine hits political hurdle
summary: A Chinese firm seeking to settle a royalties dispute tied to a major DR Congo copper-and-cobalt mine faced a political hurdle. The unresolved issue increases uncertainty around mine stability and potential supply disruptions, creating near-term bearish risk for copper prices as markets price timing and operational continuity.

title: Are Aluminum Prices About To Break Out?
summary: The piece says LME aluminum inventories fell in early 2022, but pricing has stayed bearish. It cites a WBMS surplus of ~400k tonnes for Jan–Apr 2022, rising physical delivery premiums, and European smelter closures from high energy costs. It expects inventories to fall further and aluminum prices to ease.

title: LME tightens rules around nickel trading
summary: The LME approved new rules requiring members to report OTC positions weekly, effective in one month, with large position holders providing rationale. The change follows the March nickel trading chaos and LME suspension tied partly to a large OTC short. The reporting also covers copper and aluminium.

title: Domestic Alumina Market Was Quiet amid Deadlock between Buyers and Sellers _SMM
summary: SMM says domestic alumina prices were quiet but slightly down, with spot prices falling on abundant supply after new capacity commissioning and worsened cash flows leading traders/refineries to dump cargoes. Overseas prices rose moderately as smelters increased purchases to keep production stable. Some refinery cuts slowed declines, but an outright rebound depends on costs vs. prices.

title: Culpeo Minerals discovers new copper zone at Lana Corina project
summary: Culpeo Minerals reports high-grade copper drilling results at its Lana Corina project in Chile, including a new breccia-hosted copper zone aligned with a major magnetic target and multiple high-priority intercepts. Drilling continues to test near-surface breccia pipes and potential to expand copper and molybdenum mineralisation.

title: Expectations for US Interest Rate Hike and Economic Recession Weighed on SHFE Aluminium _SMM
summary: SMM reports that a 75 bp US Fed hike and additional rate increases abroad have pressured commodities, including SHFE and LME aluminium. Domestically, supply growth is accelerating, with some smelters turning loss-making and traders shifting/cancelling orders, limiting support despite declining ingot inventories.

title: Output Cuts Slowed down Decline in Alumina Prices _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says alumina prices in China fell but the decline slowed as overseas buying picked up, tightening supply and lifting FOB Western Australia prices. Domestic pressure eased where cash-flow stress forced some refineries to cut output. Smelters relied on long-term supply, limiting spot demand, but costs remain high.

title: Domestic Bauxite Prices Rose Slightly, Guinea Pressures Mining Companies to Build Alumina Refineries Locally _SMM
summary: SMM reports a slight rise in China’s domestic bauxite prices due to tighter bauxite availability for alumina refineries. Guinea’s military government asked bauxite miners to submit alumina-refinery construction timetables, considers a bauxite reference price, and raises export uncertainty, potentially lifting imported bauxite costs and widening refinery cost disparities.

title: Smelters' Profits Declined amid Plummeting Aluminium Prices_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports alumina costs edged lower while thermal coal was slightly firmer, leaving electricity prices largely unchanged for aluminium smelters. Despite anode prices staying high, smelters’ average costs fell but profits dropped sharply as aluminium spot prices plunged. Raw material costs may fall further, though electricity-driven coal strength could keep costs elevated.

title: Copper Prices Declined Last Week as Global Liquidity Tightened_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Copper prices fell last week as tighter global liquidity, aggressive rate expectations, and a stronger US dollar pressured industrial products. Although Las Bambas resumed production and China’s smelters restarted, weak demand, low processor operating rates, higher overseas inflows, and rising domestic output suppressed spot premiums. Fundamentals remain bearish and sustainability of consumption is key.

title: Nickel Prices Continued to Fall due to the Macro Factors_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports nickel prices continued to fall, with spot supply easing from higher purchases and sufficient NPI supply. NPI prices weakened as steel mills pressured raw material costs. Nickel sulphate saw more long-term orders but slack spot trading. Sluggish downstream demand and Fed rate-hike macro pressure keep SHFE nickel rangebound with downward potential.

title: Ronbay Technology Expects Nickel Prices to Fall Back Rapidly Next Year as Battery Supply Chain Stabilises_SMM
summary: Ronbay’s chairman says nickel prices will drop rapidly as the battery supply chain stabilises, forecasting a nickel metal surplus above 400,000 mt in 2023. He expects nickel to fall from about $20,000/mt to below $15,000/mt next year. Battery mix and recycling could affect future costs.

title: Huayou Cobalt Plans to Raise No more than 17.7 Billion yuan to Invest in Nickel Hydrometallurgy and Lithium Processing Business_SMM
summary: Huayou Cobalt said it will raise up to 17.7 billion yuan to fund a nickel-cobalt hydroxide hydrometallurgy project in Indonesia, targeting 120,000 mt/year of nickel metal, along with a lithium salt project. The financing also includes working-capital replenishment, signaling expanded nickel processing capacity.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Decreased 6,300 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventory in major Chinese markets fell 6,300 mt over the weekend to 103,600 mt, and is far below last year. The drop is linked to lower prices last week and downstream restocking, plus smelters shipping output directly. Spot trading is cautious, and further restocking hinges on demand.

title: Vedanta to sell off its Tuticorin copper facility, invites expressions of interest
summary: Vedanta invited expressions of interest to sell its Tuticorin Sterlite Copper smelter, closed since 2018 after a Tamil Nadu injunction. The plant produces a large share of India’s copper and sulfuric acid, and bids are sought by July 4. Any path to restart could support refined copper supply expectations.

title: Aluminium Inventory in China Maintained Downward Trend _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s aluminium ingot social inventories in eight major markets were 757,000 mt as of June 20, down 28,000 mt week-on-week and 165,000 mt from end-May. The decline was led by Wuxi and Foshan, aided by cargo transfers and stronger downstream purchases after price pullbacks, with limited arrivals helping inventories fall.

title: Vedanta shares decline 10 pc after it puts Tamil Nadu copper plant on sale
summary: Vedanta shares fell after the firm issued an expression of interest to sell its shut Sterlite copper plant in Tuticorin, Tamil Nadu. The move highlights reduced copper refining capacity from an idled smelter, which can worsen near-term sentiment around copper supply and inventories.

title: Vedanta puts its copper smelter plant in Tuticorin on sale
summary: Vedanta is putting its 400,000 tpa Sterlite Copper smelter and refining complex in Tuticorin up for sale, calling for expressions of interest. The move comes while a Supreme Court appeal over reopening is pending amid local environmental opposition. Vedanta argues it affects supply, with India becoming a net importer.

title: Huayou Cobalt to Raise Up to USD2.6 Billion for Indonesia Nickel Project
summary: Huayou Cobalt plans a CNY17.7 billion private placement, allocating CNY12.2 billion to its Indonesia JV to build a nickel-cobalt hydroxide production base using nickel laterite ore. The expansion targets 326,000 tons of hydroxide products annually from 2025, reinforcing nickel supply prospects.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Provides Update on Drilling at Lappvattnet High-Grade Nickel Project
summary: Gungnir Resources reported progress on drilling at its Lappvattnet high-grade nickel project in northern Sweden, completing eight holes and sending core for assay, with results expected in late July/early August. The company cites prior high-grade nickel intercepts and existing inferred nickel resources, but provides no new market-moving assay data.

title: China's Imports of Copper Cathode will Increase Slightly in June Thanks to the Flowing of the Cancelled Warrants of LME Asian Warehouses_SMM
summary: China’s copper cathode imports rose in May (up MoM and YoY), with increases from Congo (DRC) and Russia supported by improved logistics and post-crisis shipments. The inflow also reflects cancelled LME Asian warehouse warrants entering China. SMM expects June imports to increase slightly as exports decline further.

title: Official Data from NBS Showed A Month-on-Month Rebound in China Copper Cathode Output in May_SMM
summary: China’s NBS reported copper cathode output of 912,000 mt in May (+4.7% y/y). SMM attributes slightly higher output to delayed smelter overhauls from pandemic and transportation disruptions. Despite some recovery, June remains intensive maintenance, so cathode production is expected to rise only slightly.

title: Pollution from 100 years of copper mining in Keweenah Peninsula in UP is now a crisis
summary: The article describes ongoing pollution from 100 years of copper mining in Michigan’s Keweenaw Peninsula, where storm-driven “stamp sands” are migrating into Lake Superior and smothering aquatic life. It notes elevated and sometimes toxic copper levels and a cleanup plan expected in July, potentially costing about $1 billion.

title: 1844 Resources Inc.: 1844 Extends Its Position to 299 Claims on Native Copper Project
summary: 1844 Resources says it has acquired four additional claims to complete its 299-claim land position on its Native Copper Project in Quebec, adding known copper showings and previously collected high-grade grab/trench/drilling results. It also postpones a Vortex drill program for wildlife reasons and shifts focus to the copper project.

title: Copper Markets On Edge As Chile Adopts New Constitution
summary: Copper sentiment remains choppy as investors weigh the Fed’s aggressive rate-hike backdrop and Chile’s constitutional referendum. While earlier drafts avoided outright nationalization, a new constitution could tighten environmental and water-related mining obligations, raising investment uncertainty for major producers, with potential downstream pressure on global copper supply expectations.

title: EMERGING MARKETS-Record-low for Chile's peso as copper slides; Petrobras recovers
summary: Chile’s peso hit a record low as copper prices slid. The move suggests deteriorating near-term market expectations for copper, likely tied to weaker demand and/or improving supply outlook perceptions. The currency reaction reinforces that investors are adjusting risk and commodity pricing downward for copper in the coming days.

title: Record-low for Chile's peso as copper slides; Petrobras recovers
summary: Chile’s peso weakened to a record low as global recession worries pushed copper to nine-month lows. The piece attributes the move to expectations of further central-bank tightening and softer industrial growth, alongside broader EM risk sentiment. It notes additional macro volatility across Latin America and markets, reinforcing copper’s near-term downside.

title: Vedanta decides to sell troubled copper smelter
summary: Vedanta said it is seeking buyers for its closed 400,000 tpa Sterlite copper smelter in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, with expressions of interest due July 4. The shutdown followed deadly 2018 protests over pollution claims. Vedanta is also disputing the permanent closure at India’s Supreme Court.

title: Alcoa celebrates 120th anniversary in Massena; employs 450 making aluminum
summary: Alcoa marked the 120th anniversary of its Massena, New York aluminum smelter, noting 450 employees and long-term production for transportation, construction, defense, and aerospace. The facility is described as the oldest continuously operating aluminum smelter and recently earned ASI certifications, with an emphasis on ESG performance rather than output changes.

title: SMM Analysis: China Primary Aluminium Imports Fell 61% YoY While Exports Soared 7047% YoY in May_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s primary aluminium ingot imports fell 61% YoY in May while exports surged, leaving small net imports.
