The SHFE/LME ratio rose in June as domestic prices held up versus LME, narrowing import losses and suggesting the import window may reopen, while weaker overseas orders may reduce semis exports.

title: Japanese Companies Adopted Other Materials Instead of Copper Due to the Soaring Prices_SMM
summary: Japanese firms are reportedly substituting away from copper as copper prices surge. Daikin plans to cut copper usage by about 60% in 2023, and Panasonic is considering air-conditioner models using aluminium instead of copper for core components. The shift may dampen copper demand and mildly lift aluminium demand.

title: NPI Supply Remained in Surplus, Pure Nickel Supply-Demand Balance Was Maintained_SMM
summary: SMM says nickel supply remained balanced to slightly surplus: Indonesia NPI imports grew and arrivals in China kept taking share from domestic NPI, while deliveries eased spot tightness. Downstream stainless demand is still weak and macro factors are bearish. The report expects near-term nickel prices to keep falling and remain volatile.

title: China's Ferronickel Imports Increased by 63.7% YoY in May_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s ferronickel imports rose to 492,059 mt in May, up 17.6% month-on-month and 63.65% year-on-year, according to customs data. Indonesia supplied most volumes (463,718 mt), also up sharply. The larger inflow suggests increased nickel availability, potentially weighing on nickel prices in the near term.

title: SMM Analysis: SHFE Aluminium Fell Again due to Bearish Macro Sentiment after Receiving Brief Boost from Falling Inventory _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium falling 0.84% to a six-month low amid bearish macro sentiment after multiple central banks’ rate hikes and recession fears, with expectations of further US hikes. Energy supply concerns in Europe and power price pressure add headwinds. Social inventories declined, but rising supply and weak demand cap rebounds.

title: Buyers of Imported Copper Held a Wait-and-See Attitude as the Import Profits Narrowed_SMM
summary: Yangshan imported copper premiums under warrants rose modestly, while import losses versus the 2207 contract narrowed slightly. Buyers adopted a wait-and-see stance as profits improved, but sellers kept quotes largely steady. Cathode continues to clear from bonded warehouses, including non-standard sources, supporting stable near-term supply pricing.

title: SHFE Nickel Rebounded Significantly and Spot Transactions were Poor amid the Decline in Premiums_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel rebounded sharply, and spot prices rose: Jinchuan nickel averaged 11,250 yuan/mt, up 5,400 yuan/mt, while premiums declined slightly as futures had surged. Nickel briquette prices fell on narrower premiums and weaker demand, but overall spot nickel levels increased.

title: IAI: Global Primary Aluminium Production Rebounded from A Low Level in May, But Daily Average Output Continued to Decline _SMM
summary: SMM reports IAI data showing global primary aluminium production (excluding China) rebounded to 2.21 million tonnes in May. The daily average still slipped to 713,900 tonnes, the lowest in about 1.5 years, signaling supply remained constrained but improved versus the trough.

title: Surge Copper Announces 96% Increase in Ootsa Measured & Indicated Resources to 439 Mt Grading 0.32% CuEq
summary: Surge Copper reported a 96% increase in Measured & Indicated resources at its Ootsa Property to 439 Mt grading 0.32% CuEq (plus inferred tonnage). The estimate supports potential future development near the Huckleberry Copper Mine, but the update does not signal immediate production changes.

title: No Word On Copper Export Shutdown
summary: The Scrap Iron Dealers Association is urging the government to shut down copper exports for three months to curb theft of TSTT copper cables. The government has not yet responded. The proposal, if implemented, could reduce copper export supply and be supportive for copper prices over the near term.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp.: Flying Nickel Completes Drilling Program at Minago Nickel Project in Thompson Manitoba
summary: Flying Nickel reports completion of its first drilling program at the 100% owned Minago nickel sulphide project in Manitoba, totaling 2,834 meters. Infill holes intersected disseminated nickel mineralization and metallurgical testing will support a feasibility study. Initial drill results are expected in early July.

title: Secondary Copper Throughout of East China Nonferrous Metal City in Linyi Fell Significantly as Copper Prices Dropped Greatly_SMM
summary: SMM data shows secondary copper throughput in Linyi (East China Nonferrous Metal City) fell sharply in June 13-19, while 1# copper cathode and bare bright copper weekly averages dropped materially. The decline is linked to weaker downstream scrap demand and upstream reluctance to ship, with further falls expected June 20-27.

title: China Bauxite Imports Hit Historical High in May with International Dynamics Turning More Complicated_SMM
summary: China’s bauxite imports hit a record high in May, rising sharply year-on-year, with large volumes from Guinea and Indonesia. Indonesia export-ban rumors and Guinea regime instability could restrict supply and lift imported bauxite prices. Higher feedstock costs are expected to pressure alumina costs and support aluminium prices.

title: China Imports of Nickel Ore Still Lower Than in Previous Years in May_SMM
summary: Customs data show China’s May nickel ore imports rose MoM but remain below previous years. Full-year-to-date imports are still down YoY, and port nickel ore stocks are at historical lows. Philippine weather disruptions slowed mine shipments, and supply-demand is unlikely to build a surplus, keeping nickel ore—and nickel—relatively supported.

title: Ancient Afghan Buddhist city threatened by Chinese copper mine
summary: Afghanistan’s Taliban is pressing to restart the Mes Aynak project, run by a Chinese consortium, tied to one of the world’s largest copper deposits. Security, contract and royalty disputes have delayed development for years. Talks are “80% finished,” but the timing, permitting and environmental demands remain uncertain.

title: Ancient Buddhist city threatened by Chinese copper mine
summary: Afghanistan’s Taliban and the Chinese consortium behind the Mes Aynak project are pushing to restart mining at a major copper deposit after years of delays. Negotiations are nearing technical settlement, with demands on local processing and infrastructure. Environmental and security concerns remain, but the push for faster execution supports copper supply expectations.

title: Short-term Nickel Ore Prices Are Unlikely to Fall Significantly Despite Palpable Import Growth in May_SMM
summary: China’s May nickel ore and concentrate imports rose sharply, with Philippines shipments recovering but still below last year. Despite sluggish domestic stainless/NPI markets and mild declines in ore prices, SMM expects nickel ore prices to hold near current levels. Tight Chinese port inventories and later-than-expected Philippines rainy-season impacts sustain supply.

title: China Primary Aluminium Imports Slumped 61% YoY in May 2022_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s primary aluminium imports in May 2022 totaled about 37,305 mt, up 6.96% month-on-month but down 61% year-on-year. Imports from January to May fell to 168,700 mt, down 71% YoY, indicating significantly reduced primary aluminium inflows.

title: Intraday SHFE Nickel Prices Dropped while the Spot Prices Declined_SMM
summary: SMM reports nickel spot prices weakening on June 22, with Jinchuan and NORNICKEL quotes down by 250 yuan/mt and nickel briquette prices falling sharply as premiums narrowed. The decline is attributed to softer nickel futures, weaker premiums, and poor spot transaction activity, indicating near-term bearish sentiment for nickel.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd.: Aston Bay Announces Drill Program for the Storm Copper Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay announced a July 2022 diamond drill program at its Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, targeting high-grade copper zones (noted intersections around 2.45–3.07% Cu) and additional EM conductors. The program includes bulk sampling for direct ship product and beneficiation test work, with results to be released over time.

title: The Fundamentals of Pure Nickel were Unchanged and Nickel Prices will Decline Slightly in the Short Term_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE Ni 2207 traded lower on June 22, with volume and open interest falling. Pure nickel supply tightened slightly improved due to overseas plate arrivals, but demand remained weak and alloy transactions were poor. SHFE warrants hit a historical low, providing some support, yet macro factors point to a slight near-term decline in nickel prices.

title: SHFE and LME Nickel Continued to Fell amid the Negative Effect of Macro Factors_SMM
summary: Nickel prices on SHFE and LME continued to fall after June 9 amid negative macro factors including US Fed rate hikes and weak demand/transactions. Spot nickel weakened as premiums and futures eased. Although SHFE warrants inventories are at a historical low, improved pure nickel supply from overseas arrivals keeps pressure bearish in the short term.

title: Three Valley Copper Announces Adjournment of Annual and
summary: Three Valley Copper said its 2022 annual and special shareholders’ meeting was adjourned due to insufficient quorum, rescheduled from June 22 to June 30, 2022. The company continues soliciting votes and will proceed with proposals at the adjourned meeting. No operational or production changes were disclosed.

title: Chilean miners strike at copper giant Codelco; government plays down impact
summary: Codelco workers in Chile launched a major strike after the Ventanas smelter was closed for environmental reasons. Unions expected 50,000 workers (including contractors) to stop, and say protests led to detentions and halted talks. The government says mining sites are continuing, but operational discontinuity raises near-term copper supply concerns.

title: Road to Peru's Las Bambas copper mine blocked again by residents
summary: Residents in Peru blocked the highway used by MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine, demanding payment for road use. The incident follows another protest that previously forced the mine to shut down for over 50 days. With Las Bambas having resumed only two weeks earlier, renewed disruption raises near-term copper supply risks.

title: Road to Peru's Las Bambas copper mine blocked again by residents | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: A community in Peru’s Mara district blocked a highway used by MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine, demanding compensation and citing delays in land appraisals. The disruption follows a prior protest that shut the mine for over 50 days. Reuters reports uncertainty about whether concentrate transport is affected, but supply risk remains.

title: Workers strike at world's largest copper producer, Chile's Codelco
summary: Workers at Chile’s Codelco, the world’s top copper producer, began an indefinite strike after the company planned to close its Ventanas foundry in Quintero/Puchuncavi. Unions say the shutdown and protests will cost output daily, while the government disputes the extent, but production access is disrupted.

title: Myanmar junta forces kill 2 militiamen, torch villages near copper mine
summary: Myanmar junta forces raided villages near the Letpadaung copper mine, torching homes and displacing thousands. Local PDFs retaliated with about 100 mortar rounds aimed at a power distribution site and acid tanks at the mine project, though damage is unclear. The attacks increase near-term disruption risk to copper output.

title: Workers in Chile strike at world's largest copper producer
summary: Workers in Chile are striking at the world’s largest copper producer, raising the risk of disrupted mine output. Any stoppage can reduce near-term copper supply and increase uncertainty for the market, potentially weighing on copper prices in the coming days and weeks.

title: Ancient Afghan Buddhist city threatened by Chinese copper mine - World
summary: Afghanistan’s Mes Aynak, threatened by the Taliban’s push for revenue, sits atop one of the world’s largest copper deposits mined by a Chinese consortium (MCC/MJAM). Despite a $3 billion 2007 contract, the mine remains delayed by security and contract disagreements. Ongoing talks could affect copper supply plans but near-term output is unclear.

title: Chilean gov't to reinvest in copper giant Codelco-Xinhua
summary: Chile’s government will reinvest 30% of Codelco profits (2021-2024) into company projects instead of turning over all profits to the state. Finance officials say it can reduce Codelco’s financing costs and improve indebtedness, supporting long-term copper production plans. Immediate production impact is not specified.

title: ALUMINIUM INDUSTRY: Looking outside the box: Strong demand within Europe / Exports slump
summary: The article discusses aluminium foil market conditions in Europe, noting first-quarter production fell marginally to 244,700 tonnes. It highlights strong demand within Europe but a sharp export slump, with shipments down by almost a third, suggesting weaker external sales that could pressure aluminium market pricing in the near term.

title: Aluminium Ingot and Billet Inventories both Extended Decline _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China aluminium ingot inventories fell to 751,000 mt by June 23, continuing declines in Wuxi and Foshan due to dip buying and fewer arrivals, though Gongyi saw accumulation. Aluminium billet inventories also dropped to 111,600 mt. Destocking and improved restocking are expected to extend into next week, supporting prices.

title: The US Remained the Top Destination of China's Copper Wire and Cable Exports _SMM
summary: SMM reports customs data showing China exported copper wire and cable to 174 countries in May 2022. The United States was the top destination at 11,300 mt (15% share), followed by Australia at 6,900 mt (6%). Export demand appears concentrated in the US, Australia, and Southeast Asia.

title: Inverted Price Gap between Copper Cathode and Copper Scrap Suppressed Consumption of the Latter_SMM
summary: SMM survey indicates scrap sellers held inventories as copper prices declined, tightening scrap availability for processors. The cathode-vs-scrap price spread narrowed and turned inverted, with cathode below scrap, which suppressed scrap consumption by processing firms.

title: INSG: Global Nickel Shortage Narrowed to 200 mt in April_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: INSG data reported by SMM shows the global nickel market deficit shrank dramatically to about 200 mt in April 2022 from 8,900 mt in March. The overall January–April deficit also remains sizable versus last year, but the sharp narrowing implies easing tightness and potential support for nickel sentiment.

title: SHFE Nickel Lost More than 4% due to Eased Supply Tightness and Poor Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports nickel prices correcting down since June 9, with SHFE nickel falling over 4% in a day to 190,010 yuan/mt and LME nickel around $25,000/mt. Deliverable-brand and imported nickel inflows eased supply tightness, while poor demand reduced premiums. With inventories at lows, support exists, but macro factors are expected to pressure short-term prices.

title: Century Aluminum idling Hawesville smelter
summary: Century Aluminum plans to idle its Hawesville smelter (as stated in the headline). Smelter idling reduces primary aluminium production in the near term, altering supply expectations. The impact on prices depends on whether the outage is supply-driven or reflects weaker demand; the headline implies a net negative near-term effect.

title: Road to Peru's Las Bambas copper mine blocked again by residents | WTVB | 1590 AM · 95.5 FM
summary: Residents in Peru’s Apurimac region blocked a highway used by MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine, demanding compensation and citing delays in land appraisals. The blockade follows a prior 50+ day shutdown after protests. It is unclear immediately how much concentrate transport is affected, but renewed disruption raises near-term supply concerns.

title: China's imports of copper concentrates hit record high in May; supplies from Peru decline
summary: China’s copper concentrate imports reportedly hit a record high in May, while Peru’s concentrate supply declined. The combination suggests tighter near-term concentrate availability and stronger feedstock demand for China’s smelters, which can lift expectations for copper supply balance and support copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Castillo Copper grants option to sell Zambia copper projects
summary: Castillo Copper granted Hyperion a 12-month option to acquire its Zambia copper-belt assets via Zed Copper, including Luanshya and Mkushi projects. Payments include an option fee and consideration in Hyperion shares tied to copper resource milestones. Hyperion would assume a 2% net smelter return royalty on concentrate.

title: Recession fear stalks oil, copper and stocks
summary: Global markets rose as Treasury yields eased, but copper fell sharply to 16-month lows on the London Metal Exchange. Investors feared a slowdown as tightening financial conditions and soft factory activity boosted recession risks and weakened expectations for copper demand.

title: Recession Fear Stalks Oil, Copper and Stocks
summary: Global markets declined as investors feared further interest-rate hikes to fight decades-high inflation could push economies into recession. Germany’s and France’s recent Purchasing Managers’ Index data showed weaker activity, reinforcing slowdown concerns. This demand outlook weighed on risk assets and industrial commodities such as copper and likely other metals.

title: Aluminum Plant Scheduled To Close
summary: Century Aluminum’s Hawesville plant is scheduled to stop operations for roughly a year, starting in August, citing high global energy costs. The shutdown is expected to trigger 628 temporary layoffs (about 500 union members) at the Hawesville smelter. Reduced output may support aluminium prices.

title: Gold prices slip, copper tumbles to 16-month lows on recession fears
summary: Gold fell and copper tumbled to its lowest level since early February 2021 as recession fears weighed on industrial metals. Copper for July delivery dropped 20 cents (5.2%) to $3.739/lb, reaching 16-month lows. The selloff reflects weakening demand expectations alongside macro pressure.

title: Chile workers strike at Codelco, world's largest copper producer | Mining News
summary: Codelco workers in Chile launched an open-ended strike after the government decided to shut the Ventanas foundry to curb pollution following sulphur dioxide poisonings. Workers blocked entrances at multiple facilities and unions said production was paralysed, though the finance minister said mining sites were not fully stopped.

title: Copper dips below $4, suggesting the global economy is in trouble
summary: Copper briefly fell below $4/lb, signaling weakening demand expectations as interest-rate hikes and recession fears curb demand. The market is also weighing whether electrification can offset a projected surplus. The piece notes Chilean labour/smelter disruptions could threaten future supply, but near-term pressure is bearish.

title: ASX to slip, copper drops, Wall St mixed
summary: Australian equities are set to edge lower as commodity prices weaken. The article highlights recession worries that are deflating metals, with copper falling to a 16-month low. Oil and gold also slip, suggesting broader risk-off sentiment that typically pressures copper prices further in the near term.

title: Century's Hawesville smelter to close as energy soars, Aluminium prices slump
summary: Century will begin idling its Hawesville, Kentucky aluminium smelter on June 27 because US power costs have more than tripled. The closure is expected to reduce US Midwest primary supply, potentially reversing some declines in aluminium premiums. Aluminium prices and US premiums have already fallen sharply amid global sell-off.

title: Chile workers end strike at world's largest copper producer
summary: Workers have ended a strike at the world’s largest copper producer in Chile. The resolution is expected to restore normal operations and reduce near-term supply disruption risk, which can ease market concerns over copper availability and typically puts downward pressure on copper prices over the following days.

title: U.S. stocks rise as yields hit two-week low; copper falls
summary: U.S. stocks rose as Treasury yields fell, but copper declined to 16-month lows. The report links copper’s slump to higher interest rates and softer factory activity across major economies, with recession fears growing amid tightening policy and supply-chain disruptions from China’s curbs and the Ukraine war.

title: Copper thieves target Port of Spain businesses' a/c units
summary: Port of Spain businesses report copper thieves hacking copper lines from rooftop air-conditioning units, with repeated theft within 24 hours and occasional full condenser theft. DOMA cites record-high international copper prices and urges protective measures. A scrap dealers leader blames authorities and calls for action on copper trade; police are investigating.

title: Copper dives to 16-month low as recession alarms blare
summary: Copper prices plunged to a 16-month low as investors grew more concerned that aggressive central-bank tightening will spur a recession. LME benchmark copper fell 4.2% to $8,409/tonne, down about 14% from early-month peak, reflecting expectations of reduced industrial demand for metals.

title: 50,000 Chilean copper miners launch strike against Boric government
summary: Chile’s copper miners (about 50,000) have launched an indefinite strike at mines and refining facilities after the Boric government announced the permanent closure of the Ventanas copper refinery and planned layoffs. The work stoppage threatens near-term copper supply from Chile, a key global producer, adding upside support to prices.

title: Century Aluminum plant in Hancock County to shut down, laying off over 600 employees
summary: Century Aluminum will shut down its Hawesville, Kentucky smelter, cutting over 600 jobs. The company cites energy costs nearly tripling due to the war in Ukraine. The closure is expected to last 9–12 months and comes after prior temporary shutdowns blamed on Chinese overcapacity, implying reduced near-term aluminum supply.

title: Bearish Macro Expectations Outweigh Positive Impact from Overseas Aluminium Output Cuts_SMM
summary: SMM reports sharp declines in SHFE and LME aluminium prices, citing US rate-hike expectations and weaker manufacturing data as bearish for demand. Despite lower Chinese aluminium ingot and billet inventories, spot transactions stay weak. Rising domestic operating capacity and overall macro tightening are expected to keep aluminium prices pressured in the near term.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Decreased 1,300 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM said copper inventories across major Chinese markets fell 1,300 mt to 102,300 mt vs Monday, and 7,600 mt vs last Friday, with the sharpest decline in Guangdong linked to higher rod-plant operating rates. However, end-June fund withdrawals are expected to bring more sellers, less buyers, and inventories to bottom out and rise next week.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices Continued to Drop while the Spot Prices Declined_SMM
summary: SMM reports that SHFE nickel and related spot prices declined further, citing weak macro sentiment and the arrival of overseas pure nickel. Jinchuan nickel averaged 10,500 yuan/mt (with spot plate correcting) while Nornickel was flat at 5,500 yuan/mt. Nickel briquette premiums narrowed and transactions weakened.

title: SMM's Detailed Analysis of Factors behind the Continuous Decline in Aluminium Ingot Inventories _SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s aluminium ingot social inventories fell to 751,000 mt by June 23, down 172,000 mt in a month, driven by sharply lower imports, increased exports of ingots and semis, more smelting output as aluminium liquid, and dip buying by downstream users. Smelters also reduced warehouse shipments after a collateral scandal, aiding destocking.

title: HKEX's London Metal Exchange names Oliver Wyman to review nickel trading chaos amid investor lawsuits
summary: HKEX’s London Metal Exchange appointed Oliver Wyman to review nickel trading “chaos” following investor lawsuits. The announcement is directly tied to nickel market functioning and potential reforms, which can affect short-term trading expectations, but no clear supply/demand or production impacts are described in the provided text.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports up 283,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says Chinese nickel ore port inventories rose by 283,000 wmt to 5.163 million wmt (Ni content up 2,000 mt). While imports from the Philippines are recovering, total inventories remain historically low due to earlier rainy-season import shortfalls. Near term inventories should rise gradually, but tight supply likely persists.

title: Stock Markets Today: Shares up After Powell Pledge, Copper Drops
summary: Global stocks rose after Powell reiterated a fight against inflation, but risk-off factors lingered. The dollar eased and Treasury yields moved, yet copper slid to a 16-month low near $3.7/lb. The drop is attributed to recession fears, despite a strike at Chile’s Codelco, the biggest producer.

title: Markets pare back inflation expectations as copper slides
summary: Global stocks rebounded while copper continued to slide. Reuters notes LME copper was down 0.5% to $8,367/t after earlier touching $8,122.50. The move is linked to easing inflation expectations and a growing recession outlook from aggressive central-bank rate hikes, lowering demand expectations for commodities.

title: Chinese Aluminium Plate/Sheet and Strip Companies Were Plagued by Poor Domestic and Overseas Demand  _SMM
summary: SMM’s survey finds aluminium plate/sheet and strip demand remains subdued. Many Chinese producers report new orders falling by more than 50% year-on-year, while both domestic sales and foreign trade are sluggish. This indicates weaker near-term aluminium consumption and potential downward pressure on prices.

title: Bonded Zone Inventory Increased Slightly due to Weak Demand for Pure Nickel_SMM
summary: SMM says macro factors kept nickel prices falling in domestic and overseas markets, with profitable imports supporting activity. Bonded zone inventory for pure nickel rose to 7,700 mt, while nickel briquette and plate inventories fell WoW. SMM expects profitable spot imports to continue, bringing more overseas nickel plate into bonded warehouses next week.

title: Gold prices slip, while recession fears drive copper to biggest weekly loss in a year
summary: Gold slipped for a second week as recession fears weighed on risk sentiment. Copper was highlighted for posting its biggest weekly percentage loss in a year, with the most-active contract down 6.8% and Thursday settling at the lowest level in about 16 months. Macro factors and the dollar drove moves.

title: TNR Gold Corp.: TNR Gold Update - NSR Royalty on McEwen Mining's Los Azules Copper, Gold and Silver Project
summary: TNR Gold highlights its 0.4% NSR royalty on McEwen Mining’s Los Azules copper project in Argentina. McEwen’s update includes multiple long copper intercepts (up to 1.38% Cu over 54m) and progress on drilling, modeling, and site access, supported by additional project financing.

title: Stocks Temper Their Inflation Expectations on Copper Pounding
summary: World stocks were set for a weekly gain as investors hoped falling commodities, led by copper, would curb runaway inflation. The week saw steep commodity declines amid concerns the global economy is shaky and rate hikes could hurt growth, prompting traders to reduce inflation expectations and bets on hike size.

title: Stocks temper their inflation expectations on copper pounding
summary: Stocks rallied as investors tempered inflation expectations, but benchmark LME copper fell further, down 0.5% on Friday and near multi-month lows. The move reflects easing recession worries from commodity price slides; however, the article still highlights continued downside pressure on copper versus recent peaks.

title: Copper Is in a Bear Market — Like Before the Last 4 Recessions
summary: Copper has fallen more than 20% from its peak, entering a technical bear market, alongside intensifying recession fears. The piece attributes weakness to rapidly rising interest rates and inflation choking global growth, with analysts saying copper’s sensitivity to recession risk is rising and could weigh on demand.

title: Kentucky aluminum plant cuts off production, lays off 600 workers due to high energy costs
summary: Century Aluminum plans to temporarily halt its Hawesville, Kentucky smelter for nine to 12 months starting in August, laying off about 600 workers. The company cites dramatically higher power costs. The Hawesville plant is its largest U.S. smelter and a major high-purity primary aluminum producer.

title: Gold edges lower for the week; copper suffers worse weekly fall in a year
summary: Gold was slightly firmer on Friday but down for the week, with traders waiting for inflation data to gauge Fed rate-hike expectations. The key point is copper’s large weekly drop, losing 6.8%, driven by recession fears and expectations for weaker copper demand.

title: Chile Copper Strike Highlights Volatility of Green Economy
summary: CODELCO workers in Chile launched and then ended a nationwide strike over plans to shut the Ventanas foundry/refinery. The disruption threatened significant daily costs and production alterations at the world’s largest copper producer, highlighting near-term supply volatility for copper that is heavily tied to China-driven demand.

title: U.S. court upholds Arizona land swap deal for Rio Tinto copper mine
summary: A U.S. appeals court upheld the federal government’s land swap in Arizona that would transfer thousands of acres to Rio Tinto for the Resolution Copper project. The decision rejects Native American objections and defers to prior Congressional/Obama authorization, lowering permitting risk for copper output.

title: Exclusive-Copper giant Codelco sees 'very firm' copper price ahead despite recent drop – chairman | Kat Country 98.9
summary: Codelco’s board chairman said the copper market may face short-term turbulence but fundamentals remain favorable, with a strong supply-demand balance supported by limited new deposits. The comments follow a sharp weekly copper drop tied to central bank inflation-fighting and weaker growth expectations. Codelco plans to maintain output goals.

title: EXCLUSIVE Copper Giant Codelco Sees 'very Firm' Copper Price Ahead Despite Recent Drop - ... - Latest Tweet by Reuters
summary: Reuters reports Codelco’s chairman said the copper price outlook is 'very firm' despite a recent drop. The statement signals stronger near-term sentiment around copper fundamentals. Though not an explicit production or trade action, such guidance can affect short-term market expectations for copper prices.

title: Exclusive-Copper giant Codelco sees 'very firm' copper price ahead despite recent drop – chairman
summary: Codelco’s chairman said copper price fundamentals remain favorable despite a sharp recent drop, citing limited new supply and strong demand outlook. He said production targets would be maintained and costs kept in check. Chile also plans to let Codelco retain 30% of profits to fund major investments.

title: Exclusive-Copper giant Codelco sees 'very firm' copper price ahead despite recent drop – chairman | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Codelco’s chairman said the copper price outlook remains “very firm” based on favorable supply-demand fundamentals, despite a sharp recent decline and worries that central bank actions may slow growth. Codelco plans to maintain 1.7 million tonnes annual output and keep costs competitive, while Chile allows it to retain profits to fund investments.

title: No cop-out on copper
summary: The article warns that copper theft is rising in Trinidad and Tobago, targeting copper lines and tubes from businesses and utility infrastructure. It links the increase to high export scrap values and a 125% copper price rise since March 2020. It discusses tougher policing and proposals to restrict scrap copper sales.

title: Bearish Macro Factors and Fundamentals to Pressure SHFE Aluminium in the Short Term_SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium fell 4.22% on the week and LME was also down, reflecting bearish macro pressure from Fed/ECB rate-hike expectations. Fundamentals are soft: domestic aluminium capacity is set to rise, but processing sectors receive limited orders and July-August is an off-season. Inventories are low, limiting downside.

title: Alumina Prices Have Stabilised for Now, but Will Remain in A Downward Trajectory in the Long Run_SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices roughly flat week-on-week, with most Chinese regions holding within set ranges. Some Shanxi/Henan losses from higher caustic soda and imported bauxite prompted production cuts, while ore-related outages are gradually resuming elsewhere. Tight balance from stable exports and returning aluminium output underpins current prices, despite long-run surplus risk.

title: Aluminium Smelters' Profits Shrank Rapidly amid Plummeting Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium smelters’ profits shrinking sharply as spot aluminium prices fell to a new year low (19,160 yuan/mt as of June 24). Despite a drop in smelting costs, bearish aluminium market factors and potentially sticky coal costs near peak power demand could push aluminium prices lower and risk losses.

title: SMM Insights on Nickel Sulphate Raw Material Market that You Cannot Miss _SMM
summary: SMM analyzes why nickel sulphate feedstock prices and nickel briquette demand persist despite falling nickel prices. It compares cost performance across raw materials (MHP, crude sulphate, black powder, high-grade nickel matte, briquette), discusses smelter operating rates and Indonesia imports, and notes capacity bottlenecks and inventory that may keep briquette usage stable into the second half.

title: Vimetco Extrusion, ALRO's downstream subsidiary, opened new automatic line for aluminium profiles following 10 million Euro investment – The Diplomat Bucharest
summary: ALRO’s Vimetco Extrusion installed and tested a new automated extrusion press line after a ~€10m investment. The 7” line aims to produce higher value aluminium profiles with lower energy and gas use, adding 11,000 tonnes of annual capacity to reach 35,000 tonnes by end-2022.

title: Aluminium Inventory Decline Slowed down, Some Areas Saw Inventory Accumulation  _SMM
summary: China’s eight major markets recorded aluminium ingot social inventories of 746,000 mt as of June 27, down slightly on the week but sharply less than end-May. Destocking slowed materially. Wuxi outflows fell as collateral-scan-dal effects eased, while Gongyi inventory rose on arrivals and weak downstream buying.

title: Codelco: Copper Prices Will Strengthen in the Future, Despite Recent Dip_SMM
summary: Codelco President Máximo Pacheco said recent weakness in copper prices may be temporary, with fundamentals and supply-demand balance remaining favorable. He noted Codelco’s stable annual production target and cost competitiveness, alongside Chile allowing the firm to retain profits to fund a large investment plan. Copper fell sharply on global growth fears.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Added 13,500 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s copper inventory across major markets rose 13,500 mt to 115,800 mt over the weekend—the biggest increase since March. The rise was driven by higher arrivals as the import window reopened and smelters cleared in-plant stock, while downstream demand weakened after sharp price falls.

title: JV Article: US Copper aims to develop Moonlight-Superior in California into a major new source of copper
summary: US Copper says it aims to advance the Moonlight-Superior copper project in California toward production, citing large historical resources, existing infrastructure, and an upcoming drilling program targeting open-pit grade material. With the US a net copper importer and demand rising from clean-tech, the initiative is framed as added supply potential.

title: Chile copper giant Codelco eyes green shift as environment pressure grows
summary: Codelco says Chile’s tightening environmental and water regulations will force strategy changes, including recirculating water, cutting emissions, shifting to renewables, and previously closing its Ventanas smelter. The drought is still affecting output, while permitting delays and potential glacier rules add uncertainty for future projects.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Surged before Falling with the Improvement of the Price Ratio_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums under warrants and bill of lading rose slightly amid profitable spot imports. The Fed’s 75 bp hike and hawkish tone pressured copper prices and the SHFE/LME ratio, though China demand/import activity and low social inventory supported premiums. Bonded-zone inventories increased, with shipping and inflows rising.

title: Copper Prices could not Stop Falling under the Pressure of the Potential Global Economic Recession_SMM
summary: SMM reports copper prices continued falling as recession risk intensified after weaker US/Europe data and Fed rate-hike concerns. LME copper dropped below technical support and overseas prices declined for 12 straight days. Fundamentals were mixed: slightly lower concentrate TCs, some restocking, but weak demand and ample spot supply pressured premiums.

title: Criminals eye water meters, copper pipes
summary: A Nelson Mandela Bay security firm says theft of water meters and copper pipes has risen sharply over the past few weeks. Copper units are targeted because they can be sold for cash at scrapyards, while newer plastic meters are less affected. The firm advises residents to deter thefts.

title: Gold futures settle lower; copper gains following a sharp loss last week
summary: Gold futures fell as markets digested potential G7 restrictions on new Russian gold. Copper, however, recouped part of last week’s sharp loss, with July futures settling higher after worries about an economic slowdown drove its biggest weekly percentage drop in about a year.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Intercept of 48 Meters of 1.31% Cu From the Cinabrio Norte Target at Its Punitaqui Copper Mine in Chile
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reports high-grade copper assay results from the Cinabrio Norte target at its Punitaqui copper mine in Chile, including 48 meters at 1.31% Cu. The release links the drilling to potential additional copper mineralization as feed for the concentrator and ongoing plans to restart operations in 2H 2022.

title: Vimetco Extrusion, ALRO's Downstream Subsidiary, Opens New Automatic Line For Aluminium Profiles In EUR10M Investment
summary: ALRO’s downstream unit Vimetco Extrusion has completed a new automatic press extrusion line for aluminium profiles, following nearly EUR10m investment since March 2021. The added extrusion capacity may increase near-term demand for aluminium billets/feedstock, supporting expectations for aluminium consumption in the period.

title: Short-Term SHFE Aluminium Expected to Move Between 18,900-19,600 yuan/mt amid Bullish Macro Front and Cost Support_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium moving in a broad range amid recession worries but notes cost support and supply tightening. Alcoa’s Hawesville smelter and Century’s Kentucky plant closure were cited, alongside falling LME and domestic inventories. The piece expects SHFE aluminium to trade between 18,900-19,600 yuan/mt near term.

title: SMM Semi-Annual Review of China Copper Rod Market _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reviews China’s copper rod market in H1 2022. COVID lockdowns in Shanghai and other cities sharply lowered cathode rod operating rates and hurt downstream demand. A March VAT policy and a narrowing copper-cathode/scrap spread constrained recycled supply and margins, weakening secondary rod output. Power and real-estate demand also slowed.

title: SHFE Nickel Rebounded Yesterday but the Long-term Nickel Prices are Unlikely to Remain Positive amid Weak Demand and Loose Supply_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel rebounded after several days of declines, but overall demand remains weak with poor downstream spot transactions. Supply appears to be improving due to resumed refined nickel production and profitable overseas imports, while Indonesia NPI output may add pressure. The article expects longer-term nickel prices to keep falling.

title: Will SHFE Aluminium Maintain Upside Momentum amid Bullish Macro Factors?_SMM
summary: China’s policy briefings and additional measures to stabilize the economy are portrayed as turning the macro outlook more optimistic, lifting non-ferrous prices. SHFE aluminium is reported up 2.34% and spot A00 prices higher, with firmer seller pricing/cost support and some rebound after shorts covered.

title: Copper price dives due to dollar volatility, market instability, say Chilean experts-Xinhua
summary: Xinhua reports Chilean experts say copper has fallen about 9% week-on-week to $375.6/lb, the lowest in 16 months. They link the drop to higher U.S. Fed rates boosting the dollar and recession fears that reduce global demand for copper. Brief Codelco strike news failed to support prices.

title: WESTERN COPPER AND GOLD ANNOUNCES POSITIVE FEASIBILITY ON CASINO
summary: Western Copper and Gold reported positive feasibility results for its Casino copper-gold-molybdenum project, including project economics that depend on assumed base-case copper prices. The article details processing design, recovery improvements, and inflation-driven cost increases, but it does not indicate imminent production or supply disruptions that would move metal prices soon.

title: Mutilated body found near China-Myanmar copper venture
summary: Fighting between Myanmar junta forces and anti-junta militias has escalated around the Chinese-owned Letpadaung copper mine near Sagaing, with nearby villages raided and residents displaced. Wanbao says production has been suspended for over 16 months, while rebels accuse the company of supporting the military. Supply disruption risk weighs on copper.

title: 9th Circuit court denies appeal to stop copper mine at Oak Flat
summary: A U.S. appeals court denied Apache Stronghold’s bid to halt construction of the Oak Flat copper mine, affirming the site’s sacred status but ruling religious arguments under federal law and the First Amendment were insufficient to overturn the land swap. The ruling reduces legal risk for Resolution Copper’s project timeline.

title: Copper: Buyers Required - FNArena
summary: An FNArena technical note on Comex copper futures (US$/lb) shows daily/weekly/monthly trends down and highlights support around $3.50 and $2.85 (Sep 2022) versus resistance near $4.08 and $5.17. It calls for buyers to re-enter if $3.50 holds, recommending a long only on confirmation.

title: L.A. pilot program aims to protect street lights from copper thieves
summary: Los Angeles is launching a $60,000 pilot to protect municipal street lights from copper-wire theft that has caused outages and costly repairs. City officials plan measures like camouflaging boxes, burying and reinforcing them, and welding access points. Theft leads to higher replacement demand for copper wire but volumes seem localized.

title: Copper Concentrate TC/RC Set at $76/mt and ¢7.6/lb Respectively for the First Half of 2023_SMM
summary: SMM says copper concentrate TC/RC for the first half of 2023 was fixed at $76/mt and 7.6 cents/lb in long-term negotiations among Jiangxi Copper, Tongling Non-ferrous, Jinchuan and Antofagasta. It compares with about $54-55/mt a year earlier and follows an earlier June 20 deal.

title: SHFE Nickel to Remain Volatile amid Ample Supply after Ending Four-Day Losing Streak _SMM
summary: SHFE nickel rebounded after a four-day losing streak, but refined nickel spot prices continued falling. The report cites ample supply of high-grade nickel matte and MHP, weaker demand from stainless steel and alloy sectors, and conversion of some lines to refined nickel, leading SMM to expect volatile nickel prices near term.

title: LME and SHFE Nickel Inventories both Fell, with the Latter Hitting A New Record Low_SMM
summary: LME data shows nickel inventories have trended lower since end-May, falling again last week to 66,936 mt by June 28, a lowest level in more than two years. SHFE inventories also dropped, down 21.18% weekly to 2,021 mt on June 24, setting a new record low.

title: SHFE Nickel Declined Slightly and the Transactions were Poor as the Premiums Changed Little_SMM
summary: SMM reports that on June 28 Jinchuan nickel averaged 10,000 yuan/mt, down 1,500 yuan/mt, while NORNICKEL averaged 5,850 yuan/mt, down 400 yuan/mt. Jinchuan premiums fell due to high futures prices and weak downstream buying. Nickel briquette premiums narrowed but trading remained poor.

title: Copper Prices to Plummet, Throughput of Secondary Copper in East China Nonferrous Metal City Dropped Significantly _SMM
summary: SMM says copper prices dropped sharply in June 20-26, with weekly average 1# cathode down about 5%. Secondary copper throughput in East China fell 12% to 19,666 mt as traders faced losses, inventory stayed high, and cathode-to-scrap spreads narrowed, reducing scrap substitution and shipments. Demand for secondary copper is expected to keep declining.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Reports Infill Drilling from Southern Gate Zone: 0.44% CuEq Over 114 m, Within 0.28% CuEq Over 501 m
summary: Kodiak Copper reported infill drilling results from its MPD copper-gold porphyry project, confirming copper mineralization continuity in the southern Gate Zone (e.g., weighted Cu intervals and CuEq). The company also outlines continued drilling and upcoming geophysical/soil work, but provides no near-term supply or production-impact signals.

title: BeMetals Corp.: BeMetals Commences 2022 Aircore Drilling Program at Pangeni Copper Project
summary: BeMetals commenced a 2022 aircore (4,000 m) and diamond drilling (1,400 m) program at its Pangeni Copper Project in Zambia’s Copperbelt, following prior copper intercepts (e.g., 4.14 m at 0.62% Cu). The company aims to expand Q and D prospect mineralization for future drilling targets.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Announces Q2 2022 Results Conference Call Date
summary: Copper Mountain Mining announced the date and webcast details for its Q2 2022 results conference call. The company’s main asset is a 75%-owned copper mine producing about 100 million pounds of copper equivalent annually. However, no operational or financial updates are included here.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Field Crews Mobilized to Pacific Ridge's Kliyul and RDP Copper-Gold Porphyry Projects
summary: Pacific Ridge announced mobilization of field crews and camp construction for a 6,000 m drilling program at its Kliyul copper-gold project and a partner-funded 1,500 m drill program at the RDP copper-gold project. The news is exploratory, with no immediate changes to copper supply, production, or trade.

title: Romios Gold Resources Inc.: Romios Gold Reports High-Grade Copper & Silver Assays Up to 7.39% Cu and 192 g/t Ag from Previously Undocumented Au-Cu-Ag Prospects On the Kinkaid Project, Nevada
summary: Romios Gold reported new assay results from its Kinkaid, Nevada property, including high-grade copper values (up to 7.39% Cu) alongside gold and silver. The release describes exploratory chip and grab sampling at previously undocumented prospects and planning for mapping and potential diamond drilling. It provides no production or supply guidance.

title: Alumina Producer Alum Tulcea Suspends Production as of August
summary: Romanian alumina producer Alum Tulcea plans to suspend production starting in August, according to its activity plan. Because alumina is a key feedstock for aluminium smelting, the shutdown raises concerns about tighter supply of refining inputs, which can pressure expectations for near-term aluminium prices.

title: Sanatana Resources Inc.: Sanatana Prepared for Drilling at Triassic Age Oweegee Copper-Gold Porphyry Project, Golden Triangle BC
summary: Sanatana Resources reports the start of drilling at its Oweegee copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia. A recent ASTER survey and new copper-bearing altered intrusion discovery inform targeting of the Molloy monzonite. Results are pending, with no production, inventory, or export changes described.

title: Investors Dump Copper As Demand Stumbles
summary: Copper prices plunged to 16-month lows, with the article citing an 11% drop over two weeks as evidence that global growth is slowing and investors are turning bearish. It includes Codelco’s view that fundamentals remain supportive, but recession fears and broader risk sentiment weigh on prices near term.

title: LME Copper Hovered around a 16-month Low due to the Worry about Demand_SMM
summary: LME copper stayed near a 16-month low as investors weighed hawkish central bank signals and potential rapid rate hikes that could hurt growth and demand. LME nickel futures rose after UK sanctions involving Norilsk Nickel’s major shareholder. Aluminium premiums for July–September were agreed lower, suggesting softer near-term aluminium pricing.

title: Nine killed in junta raids on Myanmar villages near China-backed copper mine
summary: Nine civilians were killed and dozens missing after junta raids on villages near Myanmar’s Letpadaung copper project in Sagaing. Sources link operations to a China-backed mine site run by Wanbao Mining. Heavy fighting and attacks—including earlier power-line destruction—have displaced thousands, raising near-term disruption risk for copper production.

title: The Spot Copper Concentrate TC/RC Guidance Price was $80/mt and￠8.0/lb in Q3 2022 by China Smelters Purchase Team_SMM
summary: SMM reports that China Smelters Purchase Team (CSPT) finalized Q3 2022 spot copper concentrate TC/RC guidance at $80/mt and ￠8.0/lb, unchanged from Q2. The SMM Imported Copper Concentrate Index averaged $78.68/mt in Q2, indicating little fresh momentum for copper prices.

title: Resumed Pure Nickel Capacity Starts to Yield Output, While Purchase Are Muted_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel rising and spot refined nickel higher, while nickel premiums compress. The supply outlook improves as pure nickel capacity resumes and some imports may arrive, but demand remains muted with quiet buying in Wuxi/Foshan. Overall, SMM expects nickel to stay rangebound with limited further change.

title: The Latest SMM Analysis of Nickel_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports sufficient nickel intermediate supply from Indonesia (nickel matte and hydrometallurgy intermediates) with inventories rising slightly as consumption lags. Nickel sulphate cost is expected to fall due to supply surplus, and NPI prices are projected to keep declining, dragging stainless steel costs. Nickel prices are expected to decline short term.

title: Explainer-Nuts And Bolts Of The LME's Cancelled Nickel Trades Legal Case
summary: Elliott Associates and Jane Street are suing the LME after it cancelled nickel trades on March 8 during chaotic spikes above $100,000/t. The LME cited systemic risk from large margin calls. The explainer details margin mechanics, Tsingshan’s cash constraints on a large nickel short, and potential default losses.

title: Aluminium traders brace for possibility of more smelter cuts amid rising energy costs
summary: Rising European energy costs, intensified by geopolitical tensions and strikes (including at TotalEnergies), are squeezing aluminium smelter margins and raising expectations of further curtailments. Traders say losses exceed profitability thresholds, limiting supply and supporting Rotterdam aluminium premiums despite declines in the LME aluminium cash price.

title: Candente Copper Provides Update on Implementation of
summary: Candente Copper reported that directors receiving withheld votes offered resignations under its majority voting policy. Between 96% and 98% of withheld votes were cast by Fortescue’s affiliate, Nascent Exploration. The company said the board will consult parties and decide within 90 days, with no operational or production updates disclosed.

title: Chinese Mining Giant CMOC to Invest Over USD1.8 Billion to Develop Copper-Cobalt Mine in DRC
summary: China Molybdenum plans to invest over $1.8 billion in the Kisanfu/KFM copper-cobalt project in the DRC, including spending on engineering and construction. The mine is expected to supply about 90,000 tons of cathode copper annually after full output, starting production in the first half of next year.

title: SMM Survey of Output Cuts by Alumina Refineries across Shanxi and Henan_SMM
summary: SMM reports a surge in newly commissioned Chinese alumina capacity, pushing alumina prices into a downward trend since May 16. Inland, high-cost refineries in Shanxi and Henan face bauxite shortages and reduced profits, cutting operating rates or shutting furnaces. Falling alumina and ongoing supply tightness may ease smelter costs.

title: Aluminium Price Rally Turned out to Be Transitory due to Growing Supply Pressure and Weak Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports that an aluminium rally proved temporary: SHFE aluminium fell 1.42% after improving but still mixed macro data. Weak end demand ahead of the off-season and slower destocking coincide with higher domestic operating capacity (up to ~41mn mt) and only modest inventory declines, weighing on prices.

title: SMM Semi-Year Review of Lithium-Battery Copper Foil_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reviews China’s lithium-battery copper foil expansion, estimating large capacity additions in 2H2022 and a higher likelihood of oversupply as COVID hits demand. Processing fees for 6μm/8μm/4.5μm foils have fallen, and SMM forecasts 6μm and 8μm power-battery foil prices will drop below 40,000 and 30,000 yuan/mt in 2022.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Added 10,400 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM said copper inventories across major Chinese markets rose 10,400 mt to 126,200 mt from Monday, up 23,900 mt week-on-week. The build was driven by smelters shipping to ease mid-year pressure and continued imported inflows amid weaker restocking as downstream funds tighten. SMM expects inventories to dip slightly next week.

title: Bonded Zone Inventory of Nickel Stayed almost Unchanged this Week as the Price Ratio Narrowed_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai bonded-zone nickel inventory at about 7,700 mt, unchanged week-on-week. The price ratio tightened as overseas nickel prices fell while USD premiums rose in the bonded zone. Weak downstream demand for pure nickel and delays in overseas arrivals supported the flat inventory level.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 120,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says Chinese port inventories of nickel ore fell 120,000 wmt week-on-week to 5.044 million wmt on July 1. Total Ni content dropped to 39,700 mt. Supply is described as tight and likely driven by NPI plant activity, keeping short-term inventories at low levels.

title: Copper Bear Market Worsens As Price Dips Below $8,000 Amid Growth Fears
summary: London copper dropped as much as 3.6% to around $7,959/ton, extending a bear market and marking the lowest level since early 2021. It fell nearly 20% in the quarter amid recession and growth fears, with similar weakness cited for aluminium and nickel.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Further Operational and Financial Update
summary: Nevada Copper provides an operational update at its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine, citing restricted stope access caused by weak rock structures. Liquidity constraints and creditor/vendor non-payments have led the company to suspend most underground mining activities while seeking additional funding, increasing near-term risk of reduced copper output.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Further Operational and Financial
summary: Nevada Copper provides an update on its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine. Restricted stope access from weak rock conditions required curtailment, and liquidity/default concerns have led to suspension of most mining activities. Further funding is uncertain, risking inability to complete ramp-up and maintain planned copper production.

title: Copper stumbles to 17-month low as inflation data fans slowdown fears
summary: Copper prices reportedly fell to a 17-month low after inflation data increased concerns about a slowing economy. The market reaction suggests traders expect weaker industrial demand ahead, putting downward pressure on copper despite no specific supply or inventory shock being cited in the prompt.

title: Chile plans to raise copper mining royalties and reform tax system
summary: Chile’s finance minister introduced a tax reform bill that raises copper mining royalties for large producers and adds profit taxes that vary with copper prices. Given Chile’s position as the world’s top copper producer, higher government take could pressure investment and near-term supply expectations, weighing on copper sentiment.

title: Prices of Oil, Wheat, and Copper are Falling. What It Means.
summary: The article says oil, wheat, and copper prices are falling as recession fears increase. It argues that a weaker economy would reduce demand: construction activity slows, lowering copper use in wiring and plumbing, and sales of electrical goods weaken. The immediate takeaway is softer copper demand expectations.

title: Economic barometer copper sinks deeper into a bear market after worst quarter in a decade amid global slowdown fears
summary: Copper is described as worsening into a deeper bear market after the worst quarter in a decade, with the move linked to fears of a global economic slowdown. The article frames deteriorating growth outlook and demand prospects as the driver for near-term selling pressure in copper markets.

title: Nickel Prices Surge As UK Sanctions Major Russian Miner
summary: UK sanctions added Norilsk Nickel chairman Vladimir Potanin to the sanctions list, freezing UK dealings and limiting access tied to his holdings. As Norilsk provides about 7% of global nickel supply, markets feared supply disruptions and logistics constraints, and LME nickel reportedly jumped roughly 6% after the announcement.

title: Falling copper prices increase concerns over recession
summary: Copper prices on the LME fell 12.8% in June, reaching $8,240/ton and a 17-month low, driven by widening recession worries. The drop is linked to higher U.S. interest rates and China’s extended lockdowns, pressuring demand expectations. Aluminum prices also declined during the gloomy outlook.

title: Santee Cooper power deal helps SC aluminum smelter avoid fate of Ky. plant
summary: Century Aluminum’s three-year power contract with Santee Cooper helps its Mount Holly, South Carolina smelter avoid idling despite rising electricity prices. In contrast, Century will idle its Hawesville, Kentucky smelter for up to a year as power costs tripled. The deal stabilizes Mount Holly’s costs through 2023 and supports output.

title: Bauxite miners want to clear seven Rottnest Islands' worth of WA forest
summary: Two major bauxite miners in Western Australia seek approvals to clear large areas of forest to expand bauxite mining feeding Perth refineries and raise alumina production. Environmental reviews by the EPA and opposition could constrain or delay supply expansion, affecting near-term aluminium/alumina availability and market expectations.

title: Topic | Bauxite | WAtoday
summary: The piece describes intensified Western Australia oversight of Alcoa’s bauxite mining, including an unprecedented $55 million forest-clearing fine and ongoing investigations over approvals and exemption conditions. It also notes regulator actions that could add stricter constraints, with knock-on concern for alumina output, affecting aluminium supply expectations.

title: Alcoa Announced the Suspension of One Production Line at Warrick Aluminium Smelter _SMM
summary: Alcoa said it will begin immediately curtailing one of three smelting lines at its Warrick, Indiana aluminium smelter because of operational challenges. Each line is about 54,000 mt annual capacity. Alcoa plans to protect output from the remaining two lines while reducing total capacity safely.

title: Alumina prices Stabilised Thanks to Output Cuts by High-Cost Refineries in north China _SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices are largely stable week-on-week as high-cost refineries in north China cut output due to bauxite shortages and shrinking margins. Regional prices are steady and overseas alumina transactions fell, suggesting falling CIF levels. Aluminium smelters find prices acceptable, so near-term aluminium impact looks limited.

title: Aluminium Inventory Stopped Falling _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says China’s eight major markets’ aluminium ingot social inventories were 734,000 mt on July 4, flat from last Thursday, indicating the destocking cycle has paused. Foshan and Gongyi rose (Gongyi above 100,000 mt for four straight weeks). Spot trading softened as the off-season nears, and inventories may edge higher.

title: Copper Prices are Unlikely to Rebound in the Short Term amid the Global Economic Recession_SMM
summary: SMM reports weaker-than-expected PMIs in Europe and the US and continued worries about Fed rate hikes, keeping recession sentiment bearish for copper. While spot supply is tight and concentrate TCs are stable, downstream order growth is limited and buyers stay cautious. The piece expects copper to struggle in the short term.

title: Short-Term Copper Prices may Rebound, while the Prices will Probably Fall to around 57,000-60,000 yuan/mt in the Medium and Long Term_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s copper consumption remains weak despite supportive macro policies. Traditional demand sectors (appliances, autos, infrastructure) lag, while overseas consumption shrinks. Scrap supply is tight and inventories are low, supporting spot/backwardation, but the report expects only a slight short-term rebound and overall price decline later.

title: First nickel from Brazilian Nickel's Piauí Nickel Project
summary: Brazilian Nickel Plc announced first continuous production from its Piauí Nickel laterite heap-leach project, producing nickel hydroxide product (NHP). Initial output is set to ramp toward guidance of 300 t nickel in 2022 and 1,400 t nickel in 2023 (plus small cobalt volumes), marking the company’s entry as a producer.

title: SHFE Aluminium Crashed below 19,000 yuan/mt amid Multiple Bearish Factors and Will still Have Room to Fall _SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium fell below 19,000 yuan/mt amid bearish macro signals from Powell and expected ECB rate hikes. Meanwhile China’s aluminium supply expanded with new capacity coming online. Downstream demand weakened (construction, auto, and wire/cable orders), inventories destocking slowed, and the market risk shifts toward surplus, pressuring prices further.

title: New Study from StrategyR Highlights a $10 Billion Global Market for Aluminum Composite Panels by 2026
summary: A StrategyR/GIA market study projects the global aluminum composite panels market to grow to about $10B by 2026 from $7.1B in 2020, with steady growth by segment and region. While it suggests rising end-demand for aluminium inputs, it contains no short-term supply or pricing triggers.

title: CMOC's KFM copper-cobalt mine scheduled to start production in 1H23
summary: CMOC says its KFM copper-cobalt mine in the DRC will start producing in 1H23, targeting average output of about 90,000 tpy copper metal (and 30,000 tpy cobalt) at full production. The company argues the additional cobalt supply helps EV demand, but near-term price effects are limited.

title: With prices skirting a 17-month low, Dr Copper's prognosis about the global economy is downbeat
summary: Copper prices are hovering near a 17-month low, and “Dr Copper” is giving a downbeat assessment of the global economy, urging that it “must do better.” Because copper demand tracks activity in appliances, power generation and cars, the gloomy growth outlook is framed as a headwind for copper.

title: TABLE-Japan aluminium buyers to pay lower premiums for July-September imports
summary: Japan-based aluminium buyers are set to pay lower premiums for July–September imports. Falling import premiums generally indicate less tightness in the physical market and/or softer demand conditions, which can weigh on aluminium price expectations in the near term by improving availability and reducing buyer urgency.

title: New Glasgow Regional Police charge two men Stemming from the theft of Copper Wire from Nova Scotia Power
summary: Nova Scotia Regional Police arrested two men accused of stealing copper wire from Nova Scotia Power substations and poles in Trenton. Police found copper wire and tools in the vehicle and charged the suspects with trespassing and theft-related offenses. The article emphasizes safety hazards from live wires, not any large-scale market impact.

title: Outlook on copper prices amid move into bear market territory
summary: Copper has fallen about 26% from recent highs and is now more than 20% below them, entering bear-market territory. The decline is attributed to softer demand from renewed China lockdown measures, plus a stronger USD tied to faster US monetary tightening and recession fears.

title: Proactive news headlines including SpaceX, Amazon, Sonoro Gold, Nevada Copper and Sassy Resources
summary: Proactive lists several company headlines. The only directly metal-linked item is Nevada Copper agreeing non-binding terms for a loan of up to US$70M to maintain its underground mine. If financing keeps production running, it can ease short-term copper supply concerns and be mildly supportive for copper.

title: Lunnon Metals reports more nickel hits at Warren
summary: Lunnon Metals says drilling at its Warren nickel target in Western Australia returned stronger nickel mineralisation, including assays up to 5.28% Ni, plus smaller copper and cobalt grades. The results are expected to show Warren may host substantially more contained nickel than estimated, leading to a revised mineral estimate in coming quarters.

title: Scrap iron dealers call on govt to stop copper theft, not embolden criminals
summary: Trinidad and Tobago scrap dealers say copper theft from utilities and buildings has worsened, disrupting water, electricity and communications. They urge the government to stop copper exports temporarily, arguing export demand fuels theft. The piece cites vandalism incidents and calls for stronger enforcement to curb the trade.

title: Aluminium Prices under Mounting Pressure as Approaching Off-Season Suppresses Tepid Consumption Recovery_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE aluminium up slightly but under mounting pressure as bearish macro concerns suppress demand ahead of the traditional off-season. Aluminium processing rates tick up while social inventories stop falling and may accumulate. Alumina refinery cuts due to bauxite shortage and higher petroleum coke costs provide some cost support.

title: Copper Concentrate TCs and RCs to Face Further Pressure in Q3 due to Tight Supply and Growing Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports copper concentrate demand in Asia should stay supported in Q3 by high smelter margins and increased Chinese capacity, while clean concentrate supply remains tight. Chile export declines and Peru mine strikes disrupt concentrate availability, and delays in replenishment and new mine shipments extend tight conditions. This is expected to weigh on Chinese TC/RCs.

title: Russian Tycoon Potanin to Start Nornickel-Rusal Merger Talks
summary: The title says Russian tycoon Potanin plans to begin merger talks between Nornickel and Rusal. Nornickel is closely tied to nickel output and Rusal to aluminium. While deal talks can affect market expectations for supply and corporate risk, the snippet lacks details, limiting clear direction in the near term.

title: Russian Tycoon Potanin to Start Nornickel-Rusal Merger Talks
summary: The piece says Russian tycoon Potanin plans to begin merger talks between Nornickel and Rusal. These companies are major producers of nickel and aluminium, respectively, so consolidation could affect expectations for supply. But without details on timing or capacity changes, the short-term price direction is unclear.

title: Russia's Potanin says he is ready to discuss possible Nornickel-Rusal merger | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: Vladimir Potanin, largest shareholder in Nornickel, said he is ready to discuss a potential merger with aluminium producer Rusal. While Nornickel has not been directly targeted by sanctions, Britain recently sanctioned Potanin, and Potanin cited diversification and possible state support as motives for talks, Reuters reported.

title: Alleged copper thieves bust in Durban
summary: Police in Durban raided two illegal scrapyards and recovered 682kg of stolen copper, arresting three suspects. The operation involved Transnet, Prasa and Telkom and also found aluminium cables and lids. Authorities said further arrests would continue to stop tampering with infrastructure in eThekwini.

title: Russia's Potanin says he is ready to discuss possible Nornickel-Rusal merger | Kat Country 98.9
summary: Vladimir Potanin, largest shareholder in Nornickel, said he is ready to discuss merging Nornickel with aluminium producer Rusal. The idea is driven by shareholder diversification to withstand sanctions; Britain recently sanctioned Potanin. The proposal comes from Rusal’s management, with no immediate response from Rusal.

title: Outlook for Nickel Prices amid Weak Expectation of Interest Rate Hikes and Poor Demand _SMM
summary: SMM reports refined nickel spot prices rising, with higher Jinchuan and NORNICKEL premiums due to scarce Jinchuan supply in Shanghai and weaker expectations of sustained US rate hikes. However, NPI transaction prices fall, NPI plants face losses, and alloy demand remains weak amid Wuxi pandemic disruption, keeping nickel rangebound.

title: SMM Review: Aluminium Stocks May Accumulate in Q4 despite Recovering Demand in the Second Half of the Year_SMM
summary: SMM says non-ferrous metals are under pressure from recession fears after Fed/ECB rate hikes. For aluminium, overseas demand (real estate/auto) is weak, while domestic output is set to rise quickly with new capacity, likely leading to stock accumulation in Q4. Overseas supply may be vulnerable in winter.

title: UK sanctions will not affect Norilsk Nickel stability — chief executive
summary: UK sanctions expanded to include Vladimir Potanin and cover entities linked to Norilsk Nickel. The CEO says the company’s stability should not be harmed, but it may need to repay some loans early due to exposure to UK banks. He also says supplies will be redirected without leaving core markets.

title: Vladimir Potanin: we are ready to discuss merger of Nornickel and Rusal
summary: Vladimir Potanin said Norilsk Nickel is ready to begin talks to merge with Rusal, citing shareholder diversification, sustainability/green agenda, and increased resistance to sanctions. Norilsk produces nickel and copper, while Rusal produces aluminium with low-carbon power. The update is only about initiating merger discussions.

title: Worldwide Copper Switch-Off Initiatives Industry 2022 - Cases Studies on China Telecom, Orange, Telenor, Telefonica, Telia and Openreach
summary: A ResearchAndMarkets report examines “copper switch-off” initiatives by telecom operators across Europe, Asia, and North America, focusing on decommissioning aging copper networks and migrating customers to fiber. The article highlights rising maintenance costs for copper infrastructure and planned decommissioning timelines, implying shifting near-term copper demand dynamics.

title: Copperstone Resources AB: Copperstone updates on the environmental permit application for the Viscaria mine
summary: Copperstone Resources said it has received feedback from Swedish authorities and consultation bodies on environmental permit additions needed for the Viscaria mine’s reopening. The company will submit supplements in September, with a court assessment afterward, aiming for an announcement in autumn 2022.

title: Copper Prices Plunge to 17-Month Low on Recession Fears
summary: Copper prices plunged below $8,000/ton on the London Metal Exchange to a 17-month low, down about 2.3% Tuesday and nearly 20% in the prior quarter. The drop is attributed to global recession fears and rate hikes. Aluminum and nickel also declined amid the broader metals rout.

title: THE FINAL HEARING ON THE HAIB COPPER LICENCE REVIEW OF THE DECISION OF THE MINISTER OF MINES WILL BE HELD ON OCTOBER 3 AND 4, 2022
summary: Deep-South Resources reports a court-ordered schedule for the final hearing of Haib Minerals’ copper licence review, with filings due in September and the hearing on Oct. 3–4, 2022. The release also notes the Minister’s prior refusal to renew the licence and the company contesting it in court.

title: Copper spirals to 19-month low as recession fears dominate
summary: Copper is falling to a 19-month low as recession fears take center stage. The market appears to be pricing weaker near-term industrial demand, which would reduce expectations for copper consumption and weigh on sentiment for the metal over coming days.

title: Copper: 16-Month Low Price for Metal Could Indicate Looming Recession
summary: Copper prices dropped to a 16-month low, with analysts warning it can signal impending recession. The article links weaker demand to China’s industrial slowdown and extended COVID lockdowns, including near-zero Tesla production. Since EVs use far more copper, reduced manufacturing implies softer copper consumption ahead.

title: Beer CEOs have had it with Trump-era aluminum tariffs
summary: Major beer CEOs urge President Biden to suspend Trump-era US aluminum tariffs, saying they have cost the industry over $1.4 billion since 2018. Beer producers rely heavily on aluminum cans, and the tariffs reportedly raise end-user production costs through the supply chain, pressuring consumer prices.

title: Black Butte Copper Project set to continue construction despite legal challenges
summary: A Montana district court permitted Tintina Montana Inc. to continue phase-one construction of the Black Butte Copper Project under an existing permit, despite earlier findings of environmental violations. The decision allows work to proceed while the company appeals an April order, leaving broader regulatory outcomes unresolved.

title: NickelX completes magnetic survey at Cosmos South project
summary: NickelX completed a close-spaced magnetic survey at its Cosmos South nickel project in Western Australia and is processing the data to refine subsurface lithology and targets. It has commenced permitting for 1,500m diamond drilling at CS1, with results expected in coming weeks and support from a state grant.

title: SHFE Aluminium Hit A 15-Month Low amid Strong Pessimism and Poor Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium (2208) hit a 15-month low and LME aluminium fell below $2,400/mt. Weak downstream orders, poor spot trades, destocking ending, and continued capacity/operating momentum are cited. Pandemic curbs, softer oil, and tightening monetary conditions add macro pressure, keeping aluminium bearish in the near term.

title: Copper Scrap Handling Volume in East China Nonferrous Centre Slumped as Copper Prices Fell Steeply_SMM
summary: SMM reports East China copper scrap handling volume fell 47% week-on-week as 1# copper cathode and bright copper prices dropped about 6%. Traders cleared stocks anticipating further declines, while downstream scrap users reduced or suspended output, cutting scrap demand. More declines are expected in the coming week.

title: Copper crash deepens as recession fears dominate metals trading
summary: Copper extended its retreat as investors priced in worsening recession risks, pointing to weaker demand prospects from Europe’s energy/gas problems, a US slowdown and renewed COVID flare-ups in China. After a 4.2% drop to a 19-month low, copper and aluminium fell again, reflecting broad metals risk aversion and demand concerns.

title: Copper Crash Deepens as Recession Fears Dominate Metals Trading
summary: The article reports that copper prices are falling sharply (“copper crash”) as recession fears drive sentiment across metals. The implied market mechanism is weaker near-term industrial demand expectations, leading traders to reduce exposure to copper until economic risks ease.

title: Global nickel, copper smelting slips in June
summary: Satellite surveillance indicated global copper smelting activity fell in June, driven by a maintenance shutdown at Codelco’s Ventanas smelter/refinery and reduced output at other Chilean sites, plus weaker activity in China and Europe. Nickel smelting also declined due to downtime at major smelters in China, South Africa and Canada.

title: Global nickel, copper smelting slips in June
summary: Satellite surveillance shows global copper and nickel smelting activity declined in June. Copper was hit by Codelco’s Ventanas smelter and refinery shutdown for maintenance and below-capacity operation at other Chile smelters, plus weak activity in China and Europe. Nickel downtime at key smelters including Jinchuan and Sudbury reduced output.

title: SMM Analysis: Chinese Aluminium Smelters Struggled to Break even amid Steadily Falling Prices _SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium (2208) fell over 4% to 17,975 yuan/mt as prices have trended down since March. Resumed and newly commissioned smelter capacity is set to lift operating supply, while downstream demand is still weak and spot transactions sluggish. Aluminium inventories are stabilizing/increasing, and many smelters face losses near 18,000.

title: June Copper Cathode Output Rose Despite Centralised Maintenance of Smelters_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s copper cathode output rose to 857,000 mt in June despite maintenance at many smelters, aided by resumed production from two Shandong smelters. Some maintenance is delayed into July–October. Concentrate supply looks relatively sufficient as benchmark TC stabilizes; July output is still forecast high.

title: SMM Analysis: SHFE Nickel Once Lost 5.72% on Poor Fundamentals _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel declining further, with refined nickel prices falling on the day. The weakness is linked to increased pure nickel supply, profitable imports, and oversupplied nickel pig iron pressured by weak demand. Alloy purchases also missed expectations as pandemic resurgence caused steel market operations to suspend.

title: Oil, Lumber, Copper Signal a Recession Is Likely in 2022: Strategist
