summary: A strategist says falling commodity prices signal a likely US recession in 2022, tied to aggressive Fed rate hikes and slowing demand. He points to oil and especially copper, which has slipped to a 17-month low and is in a bear market, implying continued weakness if recession-driven demand destruction persists.

title: Camino Minerals Corp.: Camino Intercepts 31 metres of 1.23% Copper and 7.95 g/t Silver in New Discovery at the Los Chapitos Copper Project
summary: Camino Minerals announced initial drill results from its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, including a new discovery at the Lourdes zone. Highlights include 31 m grading 1.23% oxidized copper from 27 m and additional copper- and silver-bearing intervals, with further drilling ongoing and assays expected in September.

title: Alcoa will cut alumina production by up to 15% at San Ciprián on high gas prices
summary: Alcoa said it will reduce alumina production by up to 15% at the San Ciprián refinery in Spain to mitigate rising natural gas costs. The plant has 1.5m tpy alumina capacity and says output can be adjusted. The move follows prior San Ciprián aluminium suspension and pressures alumina prices.

title: Camino Intercepts 31 metres of 1.23% Copper and 7.95 g/t Silver in New Discovery at the Los Chapitos Copper Project
summary: Camino reports intercepting 31 metres grading 1.23% copper in a new discovery at the Los Chapitos copper project. The announcement highlights potential resource growth and can lift expectations for future copper supply, typically providing modest near-term support to copper market sentiment.

title: Aluminium mating season: Three reasons why the 2023 negotiations won't be like any other
summary: European aluminium supply is described as tight due to capacity cuts, logistics bottlenecks (e.g., Rotterdam port backlogs, trucking shortages, strike-related disruption), and reduced availability including less Russian-origin material. Premiums in Europe have risen to all-time highs, implying sellers hold leverage and negotiations remain supportive for prices.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Announces Updated Mineral Resource Estimate for the Copper Creek Project in Arizona; Measured and Indicated Mineral Resources Exceed 3.9 Billion Pounds of Copper
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. reported an updated mineral resource estimate for its Copper Creek project in Arizona, stating measured and indicated resources exceeding 3.9 billion pounds of copper. The company notes additional drilling not included in the estimate and that results will feed a forthcoming preliminary economic assessment. No production or supply timing changes were announced.

title: Quebec pressured to cut arsenic emissions from copper factory
summary: Quebec is reportedly pressuring a copper plant to reduce arsenic emissions while aiming to preserve about 650 jobs. More stringent environmental requirements can raise operating costs and risk output limits at the smelter, potentially reducing near-term copper supply expectations and exerting downward pressure on prices.

title: Recession Barometer Copper Continues Its Sharp Sell Off
summary: Copper prices plunged below $7,500/ton on July 6, down 7.1% week over week, as escalating global recession fears weighed on industrial metals sentiment. The sell-off follows record highs earlier in the year and signals near-term demand downgrades for copper.

title: Oil, copper tumble on recession fears - Newspaper
summary: Recession fears triggered a sharp sell-off in industrial commodities. Copper prices on the LME tumbled to their lowest in nearly 20 months, with three-month copper down as much as 4.9% before trimming losses. The move was attributed to persistent worries about weaker metals demand.

title: How Does the Copper Foil Market Stand amid Drastically Falling Copper Prices?_SMM
summary: SHFE copper fell below 68,000 yuan/mt and consolidated around 67,000, down about 9% week-on-week. Demand in lithium-battery copper foil picked up slightly, but buyers shifted to restocking then waiting, leaving suppliers with excess finished goods. SMM expects conversion margins for multiple foil types to drop 500–1,000 yuan/mt.

title: Rising Nickel Sulphate and NPI Supply May Weight on Nickel Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports rising Indonesia nickel sulphate supply via new high-grade nickel matte and hydromet intermediate capacity, while China demand for intermediates remains below incoming volumes, risking stock accumulation. With intermediate operating rates near full and NPI prices falling, the article expects nickel sulphate costs and overall nickel prices to trend lower.

title: Peru's Copper Production in May Fell by 11.2% YoY_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Peru’s copper production in May fell 11.2% YoY to 174,258 mt, with Las Bambas suspended from April to early June and ore grades declining. Cuajone was also suspended due to protests. January–May output was slightly down, with sharper declines at Southern Copper.

title: Recession Alarm: Copper Prices Are Sinking. That's Big Trouble.
summary: Copper prices have fallen sharply, recording their largest quarterly percentage decline in over a decade and trading at the lowest levels since November 2020. The piece frames the move as a recession warning that could still allow further downside, even though renewable-energy demand is cited as longer-term support.

title: SMM Aluminium Ingot and Billet Inventory Data as of July 7_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China aluminium ingot social inventories at 723,000 mt as of July 7, down week-on-week and sharply versus last year. Billet inventories also fell weekly. Dip buying increased as aluminium prices dropped and buyers brought forward purchases amid COVID-related transport uncertainty, though demand is weakening into the off-season.

title: Canada Nickel Co. updates Crawford MRE
summary: Canada Nickel Co. updated the mineral resource estimate for its 100% owned Crawford nickel sulphide project in Ontario. Total measured and indicated resources more than doubled to 1.43 billion tonnes at 0.24% nickel, with contained nickel rising to 3.48 million tonnes. Company says the feasibility study remains on track.

title: Torr Metals Inc.: Torr Commences 2022 Field Program with IP Survey at the Latham Copper-Gold Project
summary: Torr Metals announced the start of a 2022 induced polarization (IP) survey at its Latham Copper-Gold project in northern BC. Historical rock grabs reported multiple assays above 1% copper, including up to 8.86% Cu. The work aims to define drill targets for future exploration, not immediate production changes.

title: Deep-South closes deal for majority stake in Zambian copper projects
summary: Deep-South Resources agreed to acquire up to an 80% stake in three copper exploration licences in Zambia’s Copper Belt. The deal involves cash, share issuance, and work expenditures over five years, with additional payments for remaining interest. It signals development interest but no immediate output increase.

title: HG00 | Copper Continuous Contract Overview
summary: The article provides an overview of the Copper Continuous Contract (HG00US), including the latest close ($5.6815), day range, and open interest. It notes a +0.62% move on the day, but contains no fundamental news explaining drivers, so no clear forward price impulse is evident.

title: Dutch group Aloft moves in on Alcoa's Portland Aluminium
summary: Aloft Holdings, a Dutch company planning to buy and manage aluminium assets globally, is in advanced talks to acquire Alcoa’s Portland Aluminium Smelter. The buyer has completed due diligence and discussed a potential deal for months, but the article provides no immediate operational or production changes.

title: Copper prices trade near a 2-year low, but may not have hit bottom yet
summary: Copper is trading near a two-year low and at the lowest level since November 2020 after its steepest quarterly decline in more than a decade. Analysts warn it may not have hit bottom yet, emphasizing recession-driven demand destruction. Renewable-energy support is viewed as longer term, leaving near-term downside risk.

title: Copper bounces on China stimulus hopes
summary: Copper prices jumped 4.5% to $7,858/t after Bloomberg reported China is considering $220bn in stimulus, helping offset bets on lower prices and forcing position buybacks. Analysts still warn rising rates and recession risks could push copper further down, with aluminium higher too.

title: Kaiser Aluminum (KALU) Declares Force Majeure at its Warrick Rolling Mill Due to Limited Availability of Magnesium
summary: Kaiser Aluminum declared force majeure at its Warrick rolling mill due to limited availability of magnesium used in aluminum beverage and food packaging. US Magnesium deliveries stopped after partial supplies, forcing Kaiser to cut output 30%–40% in July and about 50% in the rest of Q3 until supplies resume.

title: EV Nickel Closes Oversubscribed Private Placement of $2.2M
summary: The article headline says an EV nickel-related company has closed an oversubscribed private placement raising $2.2M. While details are limited, the implication is stronger investor demand and potential acceleration of activities linked to nickel for EV applications, which can provide modest near-term support to nickel prices.

title: Commodities including copper and oil rebound on renewed China stimulus hopes
summary: Commodities rebounded after reports China may let local governments issue 1.5 trillion yuan of special bonds to support growth. The rally lifted copper by about 4.5% to around $7,860/t. The stimulus narrative typically boosts near-term industrial demand expectations, supporting base metals.

title: SKC's Largest Battery Copper Foil Plant Breaks Ground in Poland
summary: SKC has broken ground on its largest battery copper foil plant in Poland. The project is aimed at expanding supply of copper foil used in batteries, implying higher future copper demand. The near-term market impact may be limited because construction has just started, but sentiment could turn slightly supportive for copper.

title: SKC's largest battery copper foil plant breaks ground in Poland
summary: SKC and its copper foil unit SK Nexilis broke ground on a 50,000-ton battery copper foil factory in Poland, costing 900 billion won, aimed for mass production in late 2024. The facility supports EV lithium-ion batteries and can expand substantially, implying higher future battery-copper demand.

title: Operating Rates across Major Aluminium Processing Enterprises Dropped Slightly amid Off-Season and Collapse of Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SMM says operating rates at major aluminium processing enterprises fell to 66.5% (down 0.2pp), with primary and secondary aluminium alloys particularly weak due to off-season demand softness and bearish sentiment from sharply falling aluminium prices. Secondary alloy ADC12 fell sharply on inventory pressure, further hurting downstream purchases.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Decreased by 8,300 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventory across major Chinese markets fell 8,300 mt to 118,100 mt over the week, with declines mainly in Shanghai and Guangdong. The drop is attributed to reduced smelter arrivals and downstream restocking after price declines. Next week supply may rise slightly as the import window closes later.

title: Copper Inventory in China Bonded Zone Dropped by 7,600 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM reports China bonded-zone copper inventories fell 7,600 mt week-on-week to 286,400 mt as imports slowed and copper was moved out of bonded warehouses to customs after the import window reopened. The import window then closed, making trading slack, and inventories are expected to increase soon.

title: Copper retreats as China's COVID woes dampen demand prospects
summary: Benchmark LME copper fell about 1.7% and was set for a fifth straight weekly loss as fresh China COVID-19 restrictions raised fears of slower infrastructure spending and weaker metal demand. The piece also notes declines in LME aluminium and nickel, reflecting broader recession/risk-off sentiment toward industrial metals.

title: Mountain Boy Minerals: Field Work Is Underway on the Telegraph Copper-Gold Project in BC's Golden Triangle
summary: Mountain Boy Minerals reports June fieldwork underway at its Telegraph copper-gold project in BC’s Golden Triangle, using IP/MT and SWIR to define drill targets around a previously overlooked trend. Historic results include multiple surface samples above 1% copper (up to 17.95%). The survey aims to support upcoming drilling target selection.

title: Bonded Zone Inventory of Nickel Decreased Slightly as the Price Ratio Narrowed_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai bonded zone nickel inventory at 7,600 mt, slightly lower week-on-week, including decreases in nickel briquette and nickel plate stocks. The drop is attributed to poor downstream demand and weaker-than-expected port arrivals, as the nickel price ratio narrowed due to lower overseas nickel prices and higher US dollar premiums.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Rose by 227,000 wmt WoW_SMM
summary: SMM said Chinese nickel ore inventories rose 227,000 wmt to 5.271 million wmt as Indonesian NPI arrivals and weak stainless-steel demand pressured NPI production, cutting nickel ore consumption. While earlier poor weather delayed shipments, arrivals haven’t yet caught up fully; nickel ore inventories may keep rising in coming weeks.

title: Hydro announces new investments to meet growing low-carbon aluminium demands from auto sector
summary: Hydro began producing low-carbon forged aluminium (HyForge) at its Rackwitz recycling plant, adding 25,000 tpy using more post-consumer scrap, and is investing in a new extrusion press in Tønder for EV and automotive components. The move coincides with rising European aluminium scrap prices and higher low-carbon premiums.

title: Alumina market grapples with rising costs, Atlantic differential may switch direction
summary: Fastmarkets reports alumina price volatility amid rising costs, weaker Chinese domestic demand, and reduced refinery output. The Atlantic premium may narrow if Century’s Hawesville smelter closes, but Alcoa’s San Ciprian and Romania cuts could offset. The LME aluminium price falling below $2,400 trims margins, pressuring aluminium sentiment.

title: Analysts Just Turned Bearish on These 10 Stocks
summary: The article lists analyst downgrades, including Southern Copper. Wolfe Research cut Southern Copper to Underperform, attributing the move to dropping commodity prices and weaker near-term demand from China. The commentary suggests analysts expect softer copper pricing conditions, which can pressure copper futures in coming weeks.

title: Exclusive-Peru's Las Bambas copper mine revives after protest; but deal talks stall – data, sources | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: Peru’s Las Bambas copper mine resumed normal output after ending a two-month protest shutdown, with power usage data showing activity returning to historical levels by mid-June. However, community talks remain stalled under a truce running to July 15, leaving risk of renewed disruptions.

title: Nolan Speaks For Land Swap To Accommodate State Copper Mine
summary: U.S. Rep. Rick Nolan supports legislation approving a land swap required for the proposed PolyMet copper mine in northeast Minnesota. The Forest Service would trade about 6,500 acres for private land, and PolyMet owns the mineral rights—without approval, the mine would not proceed. Supporters cite economic benefits, critics question impact.

title: Clean energy demand to drive copper price higher in future, despite recent falls
summary: Copper fell to a 19-month low amid recession fears, but the article argues clean-energy electrification will support demand and potentially worsen supply scarcity. It notes structurally harder-to-find deposits and weaker recent output, suggesting volatility near term while the medium-to-long outlook remains very positive for copper.

title: Copper prices, seen as economic barometer for centuries, give recession warning
summary: The piece says “Doctor Copper” is flashing recession warnings as copper falls to about $3.57/lb, down roughly 28% from March’s peak. It links the decline to weakening U.S. GDP forecasts and recession risk, suggesting softer industrial demand and bearish near-term copper price pressure.

title: New World Resources identifies US$2b in potential revenue from Antler copper project
summary: New World Resources’ scoping study for the Antler copper project in Arizona forecasts about 15,350 tpa of copper in-concentrate and estimates US$2b revenue over 10 years, with low C1 cash costs. Drilling continues and a pre-feasibility study is underway, but first production remains future.

title: Low Inventory and Marginal Cost Allowed SHFE Aluminium to Rebound Briefly, But Weaker Consumption Will Continue to Pressure Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SMM says SHFE and LME aluminium rebounded briefly due to low inventories and marginal costs, but downstream demand is weakening as operating rates fall and new orders stay insufficient. With operating capacity still rising and destocking slowing, the market risks a future surplus, compounded by overseas rate hikes.

title: Alumina Market in North China Began to Outperform that in the South_SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices in north China firming slightly as high-cost refineries cut output due to tighter bauxite and high raw-material costs. In the south-west, new alumina capacity release is increasing supply and weighing on prices. Overall alumina is in the “tightening then rebound” phase.

title: Overseas Monetary Tightening Policy Continued to Advance, and the Shorts still Controlled the Copper Market_SMM
summary: SMM reports that overseas monetary tightening strengthened the dollar and weighed on industrial prices, pushing copper to low levels with shorts still controlling. Demand was mixed: infrastructure and wiring orders improved, but terminal consumption weakened and inventories stayed elevated. Meanwhile tight supply and stabilizing spot premiums suggest copper remains rangebound.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Dropped under Pressure due to the Closed Import Window and the Weak Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports Yangshan copper premiums fell sharply under both warrants and bill of lading, as the import window stayed closed and import losses reduced buying appetite. Bonded-zone copper inventories declined briefly but are expected to rise as import trading remains slack and supply surplus grows.

title: Copper drops as China COVID worries dull demand outlook
summary: Copper prices fell as new COVID-19 restrictions in China and worries about faster Fed rate hikes heightened fears of slower global growth and weaker metals demand. LME three-month copper slid 1.3% and Shanghai August copper fell 2%. Aluminium also declined, reflecting a broader risk-off demand outlook; nickel was mixed.

title: Alumex first in Sri Lanka to commit to Aluminium Stewardship Initiative for sustainable society - Adaderana Biz English
summary: Alumex, Sri Lanka’s aluminium profiles exporter, joined the Aluminium Stewardship Initiative (ASI) and will pursue ASI Performance and Chain of Custody standards. The firm also expanded aluminium waste collection and upgraded its recycling facility, targeting higher scrap recycling volumes as commercial operations begin in 2022.

title: China Metallurgical-grade Alumina Output in June was 6.74 million mt and the Alumina Market is Experiencing the Replacement of Old Capacity_SMM
summary: SMM reports China metallurgical-grade alumina output fell in June due to tight raw-material supply and high prices, prompting cuts in high-cost capacity in Shanxi and Henan. Other regions partially increased output. Net imports were slightly negative and a modest surplus is expected, with supply-demand balance easing as old capacity is replaced.

title: China  Aluminium Output Increase in June Due to the Production Resumption and the New Capacity_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s June aluminium output rose 4.48% y/y to 3.361 Mt as production resumed and new capacity (e.g., in Guangxi, Gansu, Yunnan) added ~450,000 tonnes. July capacity and output are expected to keep increasing despite weakening prices, demand, exports, and inventories likely staying firm.

title: China Refined Nickel Output Rose to 15,500 mt in June and is Expected to Further Increase in July_SMM
summary: SMM says China refined nickel output rose to 15,500 mt in June (+8.74% MoM) and is expected to reach about 15,600 mt in July, with further increases as salt-plant lines are commissioned. Demand improvements support some orders, but the overall near-term supply outlook is larger.

title: SKC begins construction of copper foil plant in Poland
summary: SKC has started construction of what it describes as Europe’s largest copper foil plant in Poland. The new facility, part of SK Group’s materials business, implies higher future copper foil output and associated copper demand, potentially supporting short-term copper market sentiment within weeks as the project ramps.

title: EV Nickel Phase 2 Drilling Results: Reports 5.4 Metres Grading 2.96% Ni From "W4 Extension"
summary: The article title says EV-related nickel Phase 2 drilling at the “W4 Extension” intersection returned 5.4 metres grading 2.96% nickel. Positive assay results can lift market expectations for future nickel supply, providing a modest near-term support to nickel prices, though details are limited.

title: Global demand fears slam copper prices
summary: Copper prices dropped 3% on Monday as worries about China’s demand from new zero-COVID restrictions intensified, reinforced by higher interest-rate expectations, a soaring U.S. dollar, and rising warehouse stocks. Aluminium also slid 2.4% in the broader base-metals complex amid recession fears.

title: Chile currency plunge, inflation rattle Latin America's copper king
summary: Chile’s peso has plunged and inflation has surged, while officials attribute currency stress partly to weakening copper prices. Reuters also flags rising recession risk and slowing Chinese demand that has pulled global copper prices sharply from recent highs. Chile’s role as the world’s top copper producer heightens immediate sensitivity.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Added 1,100 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM says Chinese copper inventories across major markets rose 1,100 mt to 119,200 mt as Shanghai gained 3,300 mt from imported inflows. Downstream restocking was limited after price declines. Ahead of the 2207 delivery week, smelter shipments and tighter customs clearance may keep inventories inching up, implying bearish near-term sentiment.

title: The first Norilsk Nickel's icebreaker in Finland awaits a building license
summary: Finland’s Helsinki Shipyard is waiting for an export construction license for Norilsk Nickel’s first icebreaker because of sanctions against Russia. The pending license is delaying construction and pushing key schedule milestones back. The vessel is intended to secure shipping access to Dudinka and support Norilsk Arctic logistics.

title: Material Matters: Copper, Aluminium, Iron Ore, Lithium & Bauxite
summary: Credit Suisse’s recession scenarios point to downside for copper and aluminium: copper could drop for longer amid incoming supply, while aluminium faces negative demand pressure despite possible support from constrained supply and higher energy/input costs. It also discusses broader iron ore resilience and a bauxite outlook that is mainly longer-term.

title: Material Matters: Copper, Aluminium, Iron Ore, Lithium & Bauxite
summary: Credit Suisse analysis flags recession scenarios as negative for copper and aluminium: copper could fall longer due to incoming supply, while aluminium faces demand weakness though it may get support from constrained supply and higher energy/input costs. The piece also discusses bauxite supply prospects, which could ultimately support aluminium demand.

title: Canada Nickel says latest analysis doubles mineral resource potential
summary: Canada Nickel says its Crawford Nickel Sulphide Project’s updated resource estimate has doubled, now indicating 1.4 billion tonnes at 0.24% nickel plus additional inferred resources. The feasibility study remains on track for year-end, and the company expects potential for further regional discoveries, targeting future nickel supply.

title: China Nickel Sulphate Output in June Stood at 26,500 mt in Metal Content and is Expected to Increase in July_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s nickel sulphate output rose in June and is expected to increase further in July, supported by higher self-production/toll manufacturing and recovery in downstream demand. Despite early-July demand improvement, market supply is projected to grow, reinforcing the recent decline in nickel sulphate and nickel prices.

title: Meridian Mining UK S: Meridian Reports Further Significant Copper-Gold-Silver Results From Cabaçal
summary: Meridian Mining reported further high-grade drill results at its Cabaçal copper-gold VMS project in Brazil, including intervals with copper grades and copper-equivalent calculations, plus extensions of gold-silver zones. The update is exploration-focused, with further results pending and a resource statement planned later, limiting immediate impact on copper prices.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Provides Positive Preliminary Economic Assessment for the Kenbridge Nickel Project, Kenora Mining District, Northwestern Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. released a positive preliminary economic assessment for its Kenbridge underground nickel project, projecting 9 years of production centered on nickel with copper as a byproduct. The PEA relies on forecast metal prices and contains project-economics metrics, but it does not indicate immediate supply disruption or large inventory changes.

title: Australia ends anti-dumping duties on Vietnamese aluminum products
summary: Australia’s Anti-Dumping Commission recommended ending low-level (1.9%) anti-dumping duties on Vietnamese aluminum extrusions, citing evidence that dumping had little or no impact on the domestic industry in the inquiry period. Duties imposed on June 27 are expected to expire, likely increasing import competition and weighing on aluminum prices.

title: Australia ends anti-dumping tax on aluminum extrusions imported from Vietnam
summary: Australia’s anti-dumping authority concluded that aluminum extrusion imports from Vietnam and Malaysia were not causing significant harm to the domestic industry. The 1.9% duty on Vietnamese extrusions is set to expire from June 27, 2022, implying reduced import cost pressure for buyers and potentially more competition for local producers.

title: Allied Copper Mobilizing for Drilling at the Klondike Property, Colorado in mid-July
summary: Allied Copper says it is mobilizing for drilling at the Klondike property in Colorado, scheduled for mid-July. The move suggests continued exploration activity that could support longer-term copper supply prospects, which can modestly underpin sentiment for copper prices in the near term.

title: Copper Prices Plummet To Lowest Levels Since 2020
summary: Copper prices are falling to the lowest levels since 2020, with the article linking the downtrend to worsening COVID conditions in Shanghai and broader demand worries from China’s stalled recovery. Potential economic slowdown and limited stimulus effectiveness are cited as risks that could accelerate further declines.

title: Major Spike in PVC, Steel, & Copper Prices in 2021 Leads to Record Year for Pipe Market
summary: Freedonia Group reports that US pipe market values surged in 2021 alongside 38% PVC, 48% steel, and 49% copper price increases driven by inflation and supply-chain shortages. It also notes pipe usage rebounded in oil & gas and construction. Forecasts through 2026 expect average metal prices to moderate.

title: China Bauxite Imports Hit A New Record High in May, While Imports from Mainstream Supply Countries Diverged _SMM
summary: China’s bauxite imports in May reached 11.97 Mt, a new record, led by Guinea and also higher Australia/Indonesia-linked volumes. With Indonesia repeatedly rumored to ban exports and Guinea’s regime instability, supply uncertainty persists. Strong refinery demand is expected to push up bauxite costs and support aluminium prices.

title: Alumina Prices Bottomed out on the back of Output Cuts by High-Cost Refineries _SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices have bottomed out as high-cost refineries cut output amid losses. In northern China, supply tightens and local spot prices hold firm, while the south-west faces renewed buyer-favourable pressure from new capacity. Overall, alumina downside is limited in the short run due to curtailments.

title: Aluminium Prices May Continue to Decline in the Short Term amid Increasing Supply and Weakening Consumption_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices falling sharply as domestic supply rises with resumed production and new capacity, while demand weakens due to July seasonality, high southern temperatures, and sluggish real estate. Inventory declines are slowing, and overseas semi exports growth may fade. SMM expects SHFE aluminium to drop further in July-August.

title: Premiums of NORNICKEL Nickel Fell Slightly amid the Recovery of SHFE/LME Price Ratio_SMM
summary: SMM reports that NORNICKEL nickel premiums on the spot market fell to an average of 13,500 yuan/mt, down 500 yuan/mt day-on-day. The decline is linked to customs clearance of some supply and a recovery in the SHFE/LME price ratio. Nickel briquette prices also eased as premiums narrowed.

title: Copper Prices Rebounded, But the Throughout Increase of East China Nonferrous Metal City was Limited_SMM
summary: SMM says July 4-10 secondary copper throughput in Linyi rose 2.9% to 10,795 mt, but 1# cathode and bare bright copper average prices fell sharply versus the prior week. Cargo holders shipped more after a rebound, yet tight secondary supply and weak downstream demand kept market activity low, with throughput expected to stay limited.

title: Operating Rates of Billets Made from Molten Aluminium Fell Slightly amid Weak Consumption_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s molten aluminium casting billet operating rates fell to 72.4% in June, with weaker terminal consumption and lower order volumes in several regions. Billet social inventory rose amid supply-demand tension, conversion margins were pressured, and conditions are expected to deteriorate in the July off-season.

title: Metso Outotec to deliver grinding mills to Kansanshi copper mine
summary: Metso Outotec will supply two very large horizontal grinding mills for First Quantum Minerals’ Kansanshi copper mine expansion in Zambia. The order supports an expanded processing plant and includes power and wear-life features. While it signals ongoing copper investment, it does not indicate an immediate supply disruption or large short-term output change.

title: Copper sinks to 20-month low on economic slowdown fears
summary: Copper prices fell to a 20-month low as economic slowdown fears intensified. A stronger U.S. dollar, renewed COVID-19 curbs in China, and expectations of aggressive U.S. rate hikes ahead of inflation data reduced demand outlook. China’s growth cuts and market caution before China data reinforced selling pressure. Aluminium also fell; nickel was mixed.

title: US Dollar Index Recorded a New High Overnight while SHFE Nickel Rose Against the Trend_SMM
summary: The US Dollar Index hit a new high overnight, and most nonferrous prices fell early, but SHFE nickel (Ni 2208) rebounded and closed up about 0.9%. Spot imports were profitable, increasing overseas pure nickel supply, while low inventories and limited stainless demand keep nickel volatile.

title: Manitou Gold Identifies Nickel-Iron Alloy in Drill Core,
summary: Manitou Gold reports finding awaruite (nickel-iron alloy) in drill core at its Goudreau project in Ontario, with 0.25% Ni over 48 m, and identifies additional ultramafic structures with nickel potential. The update is exploratory, without production or supply changes.

title: Copper Fox Metals : Announces Plans to Advance Van Dyke Project
summary: Copper Fox Metals announced plans to advance its 100% owned Van Dyke in-situ copper recovery project in Arizona via a two-phase 2022 program. Phase I focuses on hydrogeological monitoring, well rehabilitation, and baseline water data to support regulatory applications, followed by Phase II drilling and pump testing toward preliminary feasibility.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: US EV Battery Supply Chain: Talon Metals Announces Thick High-Grade Nickel-Copper Assay Results from the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals released assay results from the Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project, reporting thick mineralized intervals with high nickel and copper grades in the CGO East area. The drilling suggests potential resource expansion outside the current resource boundary, but no near-term production or supply disruption is announced.

title: Indonesia to Leverage Nickel Reserves for Green Transition, Says Commerce Chief
summary: Indonesia’s commerce leadership says the country will leverage its abundant nickel reserves to attract investment in domestic supply chains for the “green energy” transition. It specifically targets nickel use in ternary lithium batteries for EVs, following recent high-profile progress on local electric vehicle launches.

title: New Recycling Pilot Program Launches in Florida, Targeting 6M Pounds of Aluminum
summary: Proud Source Water, Ball Corporation, and Replenysh launched a Florida pilot to improve aluminum recycling infrastructure, targeting recovery of at least six million pounds of aluminum over 12 months. The program places schools as collection “host locations” to divert aluminum cans from landfill, increasing recycled supply.

title: South32 to offload copper and nickel royalty portfolio to Anglo Pacific
summary: South32 agreed to sell a portfolio of royalties over advanced development-stage copper and nickel projects to Anglo Pacific for $185m plus up to $15m contingent payments. Royalties include NSR and realised value stakes across projects in Australia, Chile, and the US, with quarterly cash follow-ons and share issuance.

title: South32 to offload copper and nickel royalty portfolio to Anglo Pacific
summary: South32 agreed to sell a $185m copper and nickel royalty portfolio to Anglo Pacific, including royalties on producing Carlota copper and Nifty copper and advanced-stage copper/nickel projects in Australia and Chile. Payments include cash, share issuance, and quarterly contingent payments. The transaction shifts ownership of royalties, not physical supply.

title: Chile Wants Higher Taxes For Copper Miners
summary: Chile’s Finance Minister proposed higher taxes/royalties for copper miners, potentially replacing the current mining profits tax. Analysts expect earnings and asset-value pressure for BHP (Spence/Escondida) and Rio Tinto, with possible project approval delays. Though timing depends on stability agreements, the reform is negative for copper sentiment into 2023.

title: Boosting copper output 'the biggest contribution Australia could make' to hitting net zero
summary: S&P energy experts urge Australia to expand copper output to avoid a looming supply deficit tied to rapid electrification and clean-energy deployment. The report projects a growing shortfall that could start in 2025, citing stagnant mine output and long project lead times. Copper is central to electricity, EVs and renewables.

title: Net zero climate target could fail without more copper supply – report
summary: Reuters reports S&P Global data suggesting copper demand from solar, electric vehicles and renewables will rise sharply, while projected supply may fall short without more recycling and mining. The gap of 2.7 million tonnes by mid-century, plus rising U.S. import reliance and mine opposition, points to tightening copper fundamentals.

title: Operating Rates of Secondary Aluminium Continued to Rose in June, But were Under Pressure in July Due to Low New Order Volume_SMM
summary: SMM reports secondary aluminium operating rates rose 4.3% in June to 43%, supported by easing pandemic effects and improving auto supply chains. However, low new order volumes and weak die-casting demand left downstream purchasing cautious. Inventories increased and firms cut prices, suggesting operating rates may fall in July.

title: Review and Forecast of Nickel Spot Market_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports non-ferrous markets under pressure after Fed tightening but notes some demand recovery from downstream alloys and batteries as pure nickel spot prices fell. It forecasts higher refined nickel supply in July as salt factories normalize output, while domestic demand remains weak, leading to relatively sufficient supply and likely further LME nickel weakness.

title: Review and Forecast of Nickel Futures Market_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reviews nickel futures, noting a June downward trend amid macro pressure and Fed rate hikes. Despite this, nickel is relatively resilient due to low inventories. Demand for pure nickel is mixed: military/aviation improved while civilian alloy demand weakened. Upcoming Indonesia NPI/intermediate ramp-ups may lead to future surplus and long-run pressure.

title: SMM Aluminium Ingot and Billet Inventory Data as of July 14_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s aluminium ingot social inventories fell to 697,000 mt as of July 14, driven by downstream dip buying, reduced warehouse arrivals due to pandemic impacts, and active cargo outflows. Billet inventories also eased overall, though arrivals rose in some regions. Lower prices boosted purchasing sentiment.

title: China's Import and Export of Copper Tube_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s copper tube is the only copper product category showing net exports, with exports far exceeding imports. Imports declined 10.1% y/y Jan–May, while export volumes have been steady around 280,000–290,000 mt, with 2022 exports expected near 300,000 mt. Article flags vulnerability to trade barriers.

title: EU Copper Wire Market Report: Prices, Industry Trends and
summary: IndexBox publishes an EU copper wire market summary, detailing 2021 production (about 2.6M tons), trade (exports 1.1M tons; imports 936K tons) and trade prices. Average EU export and import prices for copper wire increased sharply in 2021, but no immediate 2022 catalyst is provided.

title: Looming Copper Supply Shortfalls Present a Challenge to Achieving Net-Zero 2050 Goals, S&P Global Study Finds
summary: S&P Global’s study projects copper demand nearly doubling by 2035 as electrification and renewables expand, while new mine supply cannot come online fast enough. It forecasts large and persistent deficits even under optimistic recycling and capacity-utilization assumptions, pointing to sustained upward pressure on copper prices.

title: Barrick produces 1.04 million ounces of gold and 120 million pounds of copper in Q2 | iNFOnews
summary: Barrick Gold reported Q2 copper production of 120 million pounds and copper sales of 113 million pounds, citing improved output driven by its Lumwana mine. It said the average Q2 copper price was $4.32/lb, but realized copper price is expected 13–15% lower due to provisional pricing adjustments after a late-quarter price drop.

title: Horizonte Minerals buys US$135mn in equipment for Brazil nickel project
summary: Horizonte Minerals said it has purchased US$135mn in equipment for its Brazil nickel project. The spend is directly related to developing future nickel output, but it is mainly a longer-dated capex milestone rather than an immediate production or supply disruption, so near-term nickel pricing impact is likely limited.

title: Anglo American begins copper production from Peru's Quellaveco project
summary: Anglo American has begun producing copper concentrate at its Quellaveco mine in Peru, starting the testing period for the processing plant and ramping mining work toward commercial operations after regulatory clearance. The project is expected to average about 300,000 tonnes of copper annually once fully running, adding to near-term supply expectations.

title: Barrick produces 1.04M ounces of gold and 120 million pounds of copper in Q2
summary: The article says Barrick produced 1.04 million ounces of gold and 120 million pounds of copper in Q2. Copper output figures can influence short-term supply expectations, but the provided information lacks context on changes versus forecasts or demand, implying limited immediate price impact.

title: Archer to acquire Wallbridge Mining's nickel assets
summary: Archer Exploration agreed to acquire Wallbridge Mining’s nickel assets in Quebec and Ontario, including a 100% stake in the Grasset nickel sulphide project, for about C$53.6m in an all-share deal. Wallbridge will focus on its Detour-Fenelon gold properties, while Archer builds a nickel-focused exploration platform.

title: Barrick sees lower prices for copper in Q2
summary: The article headline says Barrick expects lower copper prices in Q2. If credible, this outlook can weaken near-term expectations for copper demand and pricing, creating bearish sentiment in the copper market over the coming days and weeks.

title: Barrick produces 1.04M ounces of gold and 120M pounds of copper in Q2
summary: Barrick reported Q2 production figures, including 120 million pounds of copper alongside 1.04 million ounces of gold. Quarterly output updates can shift near-term expectations for copper supply, but the provided excerpt lacks context versus estimates or prior trends, so directional effects appear limited.

title: Hudbay Announces Filing of Technical Report for its Copper
summary: Hudbay announced it filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Copper World Complex in Arizona, summarizing a preliminary economic assessment. The PEA outlines staged copper cathode capacity targets and project economics using an assumed $3.50/lb copper price, but it remains preliminary with permitting and development timelines ahead.

title: Hudbay Announces Filing of Technical Report for its Copper World Complex
summary: Hudbay announced it filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Copper World Complex in Arizona, including results of a preliminary economic assessment for the Copper World and Rosemont deposits. The PEA outlines planned copper cathode production capacity, mine life, and cost metrics, supporting expectations for future U.S. copper supply.

title: CORRECTION – Class 1 Nickel and Technologies Limited
summary: Class 1 Nickel reports results from a 32.85 line-km ground TDEM survey in Quebec, identifying 10 new EM anomalies near the historical Marbridge nickel mine and indicating potential continuity of nickel sulphide mineralization. The company is reviewing results for a diamond drill program; prior ore also included trace copper.

title: US Dollar Hits 109 Causing LME Copper to Fall 4.0% _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: The US dollar hit an all-time high as markets leaned toward Fed rate hikes, pressuring LME copper. LME copper fell about 4.0% to $7,104/mt and SHFE copper also weakened, closing down 1.65%. Spot premiums remain elevated, limiting further premium growth near term.

title: Copper set for biggest weekly loss since March 2020
summary: London and Shanghai copper prices are set for their biggest weekly loss in over two years, pressured by a stronger US dollar and weak demand outlook tied to slowing growth and imminent rate hikes. China’s COVID-hit activity also weighs. Nickel sharply falls too; aluminium edges up slightly.

title: Rio Tinto says cost for development of copper mine in Mongolia $300 million higher than expected
summary: Rio Tinto said the Oyu Tolgoi underground copper mine development in Mongolia will cost about $300 million more than expected, with total project cost now $7.06 billion. The schedule has also been pushed, with shafts 3 and 4 commissioning expected in H1 2024 after COVID-19 disruptions.

title: Prices of Spot Pure Nickel Fell Significantly Today due to the Sharp Decline in Futures Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports that spot pure nickel premiums were largely unchanged despite a significant drop in nickel futures. Jinchuan nickel premiums averaged 21,000 yuan/mt, while NORNICKEL averaged 13,500 yuan/mt. Nickel briquette prices fell 12,500 yuan/mt, mainly as premiums narrowed and demand weakened versus nickel plate.

title: Copper Selloff Deepens, Drops Below $7,000 First Time Since 2020
summary: Copper prices are falling sharply, with the metal dropping below $7,000 for the first time since 2020, signaling a deepening selloff. The move implies worsening sentiment and near-term downside price pressure in copper markets. No specific supply-demand driver is detailed in the provided text.

title: Copper Drops Below $7,000 as Rout Deepens on Recession Fears
summary: Copper is reported to have dropped below $7,000 as the selloff accelerates on growing recession fears. The market reaction points to concerns about slowing industrial activity and reduced near-term demand for copper, creating downward pressure on prices in the coming days.

title: Copper Slips Below $7,000, Potentially Signaling a Recession
summary: Copper slid below $7,000 a ton on the LME, down 1.52% on Friday and 27.4% year-to-date. Analysts cite recession concerns tied to weak Chinese activity from COVID lockdowns and slowing global growth. Goldman and others say pricing weakness may persist until confidence in Chinese stimulus improves.

title: Copper Prices Fall Lowest in 20 Months. This Miner Just Warned of Earnings Hit.
summary: Copper prices dropped to the lowest level in about 20 months as one of the world’s biggest miners warned of significant headwinds that could hurt earnings. The earnings warning is treated as a negative signal for near-term industry conditions, reinforcing downward pressure on copper market sentiment.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell 61,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 61,000 wmt WoW to 5.21 million wmt (41,000 mt Ni content). Inventories were historically low, though Lianyungang rose on local pandemic impact and others fell on restocking rhythm. With weak downstream demand and falling ore prices, imports are unlikely to rise; inventories may stay rangebound.

title: Copper selloff deepens, drops below US$7,000 first time since 2020
summary: Copper prices are falling sharply, with the selloff deepening to levels below US$7,000 for the first time since 2020. The move signals renewed market selling and weakening near-term price expectations for industrial copper.

title: On World Youth Skills Day, Vedanta Aluminium reaffirms commitment to empowering rural youth
summary: Vedanta Aluminium announced on World Youth Skills Day it is expanding training and placement-linked skill programmes for rural youth in Odisha and other states. It highlights work near its alumina refinery and aluminium smelter operations, including farmers’ training and rural women’s cooperatives, but no direct production, pricing, or trade changes are cited.

title: Copper price at lowest level since 2020 as fears over global economy grow
summary: Copper hit its lowest level since 2020, with three-month LME copper down about 2.8% and a steep weekly plunge. The selloff is attributed to growing recession fears, tighter monetary policy, and weaker China demand, reinforced by Rio Tinto warnings of slowing growth and pressured commodity prices.

title: Copper suffers worst week in a year on recession fears
summary: Copper prices are reported to have suffered their worst week in a year as recession fears grow. The market narrative points to weakening economic outlook and demand expectations, which typically pressures industrial metals, especially copper used in construction and manufacturing demand cycles.

title: 2050 net-zero goals are dead in the water because of copper
summary: S&P Global says copper is the bottleneck for 2050 net-zero, projecting demand rising sharply and supply failing to meet it due to long mine lead times and constraints on expanding production and recycling. With limited substitution—including insufficient aluminium and recycling—near-term expectations for tight copper supply could support higher prices.

title: Recession Barometer Copper Drops Below $7,000 per Ton in Ominous Sign for World Economy
summary: Copper fell below $7,000 per ton on the LME on July 15 for the first time since November 2020. The move followed China data showing slower Q2 growth, with only 0.4% year-on-year expansion. Investors linked the slowdown to increased recession risk and weaker near-term metal demand.

title: Nickel Prices Plummet To 6-Month Low
summary: Bloomberg reports the Tsingshan owner behind the March nickel squeeze limited his losses, helped by LME trading suspensions and canceled transactions. However, the article says the squeeze’s fallout persists: damaged LME reputation, lawsuits, lower open interest, thin liquidity, and nickel contract volumes cut roughly in half as nickel prices fall to a six-month low.

title: Copper prices sink, flashing another recession warning
summary: Copper fell sharply on the LME, posting its worst weekly drop since early COVID-19 and deepening recession concerns. The move is tied to hotter inflation data and expectations the Fed may deliver another large rate hike in July, tightening credit and weakening economic outlooks that drive copper demand.

title: Three Valley Copper Provides Update on MTV's Filing for
summary: Three Valley Copper says Chile’s court response to MTV’s judicial restructuring procedure is delayed, with an initial order (stay of creditor claims) expected by late July. Failure to receive the order could force liquidation or sale, potentially disrupting copper production and increasing near-term supply risk.

title: Copper shortage keep green energy, tech ventures grounded
summary: S&P Global warns that copper demand from electrification could double by 2035 and remain far above supply, even under optimistic assumptions, due to slow mine development and production constraints. The report argues recycling and substitution (including aluminum) won’t close the gap, implying a looming copper shortage.

title: Copper Falls Below $7,000 a Ton for the First Time in 2 Years, Flashing a Potential Recession Signal
summary: Copper fell below $7,000 a ton on the LME for the first time in about two years, down 1.52% on Friday and 27.4% year-to-date. The decline is attributed to China’s near-stalled Q2 growth amid COVID lockdowns and broader recession worries tied to slower global growth and rate hikes.

title: Serbia to delegate processing of copper mines to Iran | Politics
summary: Serbia’s Minister of Mining and Energy said Serbia is ready to delegate processing of its copper mines to Iran, following discussions and proposed terms reviewed by a working group. The talks also covered oil/petrochemical derivatives and renewable energy supply. The article does not specify near-term output changes for copper.

title: New Exports Suspended From Congo's Tenke Copper and Cobalt Mine
summary: Bloomberg/BNN reports that exports have been suspended from Congo’s Tenke copper and cobalt mine. The suspension is a direct supply disruption for copper, reducing expected near-term deliveries and tightening availability, which typically supports higher copper prices over the next several days.

title: Aluminium Prices to Remain in Downward Trajectory amid Bearish Macro Front and Fundamentals _SMM
summary: SHFE 2208 and LME aluminium prices extended declines, with contracts down about 6.6% on the week. The report attributes the fall to bearish macro—US CPI and higher rate-hike odds—and aluminium fundamentals: many smelters are loss-making, downstream orders remain weak, and destocking slows, keeping prices pressured.

title: Aluminium Ingot Inventory Extended Decline amid Dip Buying _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s aluminium ingot social inventories at 682,000 mt as of July 18, down from last Thursday and significantly lower than a year earlier. Shipments from warehouses increased, and downstream buyers became more willing to purchase after prices dipped near 17,000 yuan/mt. Arrivals in Wuxi should normalize after pandemic disruption.

title: Central Copper Resources plans Australia/Canada listing for DRC financing
summary: Central Copper Resources plans an Australia/Canada listing to raise funds for the Mbamba Kilenda copper project in the DRC. The company is in discussions with brokers and aims to complete the listing by end-2022, potentially into early 2023, depending on market conditions, to fund production and exploration.

title: Aluminium Smelters Suffered Losses amid Falling Aluminium Prices and High Costs  _SMM
summary: SMM reports that aluminium smelters face higher power costs as coal supply tightens during peak summer electricity demand. Electricity prices rose 1.6% to 0.439 yuan/kwh, pushing real-time smelter costs up 58.6 yuan/mt. Meanwhile, A00 aluminium prices fell 5.5%, expanding smelter losses and risking further short-term deterioration.

title: Alumina Prices Continued to Diverge between North and South China due to Different Fundamentals _SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices diverging across China as ocean FOB Western Australia prices fall on abundant supply, while north China gets partial refinery recoveries but bauxite costs constrain output. South-west prices weaken with new capacity releases. Record aluminium smelter operating rates suggest only a slight alumina surplus, limiting sharp aluminium moves.

title: Nickel Prices will not Rise Sharply due to the Bearish Macro Factors_SMM
summary: SMM assesses nickel market conditions in Shanghai, noting steady spot import profitability despite high bonded-zone premiums and improved SHFE/LME ratio. NPI producers raise quotes but reduce output due to high earlier ore costs. Demand weakens with steel mills’ production cuts and off-season, though some special alloy and battery buying increases. Overall, prices should not rise sharply.

title: Copper Concentrate TCs Dropped Slightly in the Sluggish Market_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said imported copper concentrate TCs slipped to about $71–72/mt after sluggish spot trading. Buyers stayed cautious and sellers held higher offers, reflecting weak momentum. Supply looks more sufficient after Anglo American’s Quellaveco started earlier than expected, while no new Chile turbulence progress emerged.

title: Blister Copper Rcs to Remain under Pressure amid Tighter Supply _SMM
summary: SMM reports blister copper RCs in south and north China and imported blister copper CIF have fallen since July. Smelters lowered TCs amid tighter scrap supply and raw-material shortages, while some blister capacity is under maintenance. LCS’s overhaul and smelter maintenance are expected to keep RCs under downward pressure into Q3 if copper doesn’t rebound.

title: SMM Nickel Supply-Demand Forecast in 2022-2026, with Pure Nickel Expected to Be Oversupplied in H2_SMM
summary: SMM’s report attributes nickel price volatility to extreme earlier moves and highlights ongoing weakness. It expects pure nickel to be oversupplied in H2 and also anticipates oversupply in nickel sulphate and related precursor segments. Higher Indonesia NPI output and weaker demand signals are likely to pressure nickel prices lower.

title: SMM Survey of Orders in Copper Processing Industry amid Continuous Drop in Copper Prices _SMM
summary: SHFE copper fell sharply, and an SMM survey finds downstream processors responded with bearish sentiment. Copper wire/cable improved only partly via order shifting and PV/wind demand. Enamelled wire and copper pipe orders weakened amid restocking restraint and sluggish end-demand. Copper rod held above 70% rates due to cable recovery and cathode–scrap spreads.

title: Copper hits worst rate since November two years ago
summary: Copper fell 7.8% over the week to $3.2 per pound, its worst rate since November two years ago. Nickel declined 11% and aluminium dropped 3% (zinc also down). The move is linked to recession fears and wider commodity weakness, alongside European gas supply concerns from Gazprom.

title: Copper bounces on short-covering as China supports property sector
summary: Copper jumped 3.3% on LME after investors covered shorts following Chinese government support for the property sector and signs of monetary easing, helped by a weaker dollar. CMOC’s Tenke Fungurume suspended exports. Aluminium rose 3.8% and nickel gained 6.5%, reflecting broad industrial metals strength.

title: Copper Prices Drop To Lowest Level In A Year
summary: Copper prices fell 7.9% last week to the lowest level in a year, briefly below $7,000/t, amid growing recession worries for Europe and continued China lockdowns. Goldman Sachs forecasts copper may drop to $6,700/t in three months, citing demand slowdown and higher mining costs.

title: Culpeo Minerals confirms extension of copper mineralisation at Lana Corina project
summary: Culpeo Minerals says assays from the seventh drillhole at its Lana Corina copper project in Chile extend high-grade copper mineralisation by 100 metres to depth and shows strong copper (>2%) and molybdenum intersections. Drilling continues on nearby breccia pipes. The update is exploration-focused, with no immediate production impact.

title: China Aluminium Ore and Concentrate Imports Drop 7.5% YoY_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China imported 9.42 million tonnes of aluminium ore and concentrate in June, down 7.5% year-on-year, while first-half imports rose. Alumina exports jumped to 190,000 tonnes in June, up sharply YoY, with much higher first-half exports, suggesting shifting supply balances that may support aluminium prices.

title: Nickel Futures Rebounded and the Spot Prices Rose Sharply_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: On July 19, SMM reported nickel futures rebounded and spot nickel prices rose sharply. Jinchuan nickel premiums increased by about 500 yuan/mt to an average 21,000 yuan/mt, while NORNICKEL averaged 12,650 yuan/mt. Nickel briquette prices jumped mainly due to premium narrowing, though deal activity was weaker.

title: Frequent COVID Outbreak Weighed on Nickel Fundamentals_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports nickel fundamentals are weak as demand sentiment is muted despite improved supply conditions in parts of China. Premiums for Jinchuan nickel are slipping, NPI plants hold firm amid losses and thin transactions, and market expectations point to continued near-term spot price declines for nickel and NPI-related products.

title: Transactions of Nonferrous Metal City in Linyi Decreased as Aluminium Prices Fell Sharply by 1,040 yuan/mt_SMM
summary: SMM reports that East China Nonferrous Metal City in Linyi saw aluminium scrap throughput fall sharply while aluminium prices dropped by 1,040 yuan/mt last week. After aluminium rebounded by 320 yuan/mt on Monday, aluminium scrap prices rose (taint +300, tense +200). Demand stayed weak, limiting transaction recovery.

title: Barrick allies with Pakistan on Reko Diq copper-gold project
summary: Pakistan’s finance minister and Barrick confirm renewed development of the Reko Diq copper-gold deposit, previously on hold since 2011. The partnership framework and ownership structure were agreed, with definitive legal documents being finalized and updated feasibility work underway. First copper production is targeted for 2027/2028.

title: Prices of INE Bonded Copper Renounced amid a Bullish Market_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that the most-traded INE bonded 2209 copper contract rose on Jul 19, rebounding after falling earlier in the day. It closed at 49,560 yuan/mt, up 1.18%. The gain is attributed to Fed comments reducing expectations of a 100 bps rate hike and restoring market sentiment.

title: Copper Prices Further Declined and the Throughout of East China Nonferrous Metal City was Low_SMM
summary: SMM reports that from July 11-15 the weekly average 1# copper cathode price fell to 56,965 yuan/mt and bare bright copper in Linyi declined to 52,170 yuan/mt. Secondary copper throughput rose but market supply remained tight, while scrap users bought less amid weak demand and poor orders, keeping volumes low into July 18-24.

title: Power Nickel Inc.: Power Nickel Releases Initial NI 43-101 Compliant Mineral Resource Estimate on the Nisk Project
summary: Power Nickel released an initial NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate for its Nisk nickel sulphide project near James Bay, reporting indicated and inferred tonnes based on nickel-equivalent grades. The company’s mineralization is described as nickel-copper PGE style, but the release does not imply near-term production changes.

title: Steel Dynamics To Construct $1.9 Bln State-of-the-Art Low-Carbon Aluminum Flat Rolled Mill
summary: Steel Dynamics authorized construction of a $1.9–$2.2 billion low-carbon recycled aluminum flat-rolled mill with 650,000 tonnes capacity, plus two recycled aluminum slab centers, mainly using aluminum scrap. Production is targeted for Q1 2025. The project is expected to expand aluminum processing and scrap utilization.

title: Callinex Provides Update on Drilling to Define High-Grade Copper Rainbow Deposit and Test Priority Targets in the Flin Flon Mining District, MB
summary: Callinex reported progress on its 2022 drilling program at the Pine Bay Project near Flin Flon, focusing on delineating the high-grade Rainbow copper deposit. One rig completed 11 holes and a second began testing EM/IP targets; assays are pending for multiple holes and results will inform an upcoming NI 43-101 resource estimate.

title: Demand fears return to haunt copper prices
summary: Copper prices fell 1.7% as investors returned to demand concerns tied to China’s growth slowdown and rising inventories. Reuters notes China lockdown/control measures are not fully over, with growth prospects deteriorating. A weaker dollar offered some support, but expectations for further Fed tightening remain a headwind.

title: Steel Dynamics to build new aluminum mill
summary: Steel Dynamics will invest $2.2 billion to build a recycled aluminum flat-rolled mill and two satellite slab centers, aiming to address a reported 2+ million ton North American supply deficit in aluminum flat roll. The facilities will rely on the company’s scrap aluminum recycling platform and ramp from 2024-2025.

title: SMM: Copper Market to be Pressured in H2 amid Contracting Liquidity and Weak Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SMM expects copper to face downward pressure in H2 2022. It cites contracting liquidity and recession fears from aggressive Fed/ECB tightening, weak demand from construction/real estate and electronics, while copper cathode supply is set to rise significantly, potentially outpacing demand.

title: Aluminum Cable Market Growth Analysis and Industry Forecast by 2030
summary: The piece forecasts growth in the aluminum cable market, citing increased use of aluminum wire in lightweight vehicles, power distribution, and electric/hybrid vehicles in Asia-Pacific. It describes aluminum’s lightweight and corrosion-resistant properties as drivers. It acknowledges copper’s substitutability but presents it as a dampener, not the main theme.

title: SMM: Alumina Oversupply Likely to Ease in H2 with Prices Hovering Around the Cost Level_SMM
summary: SMM expects China’s alumina oversupply to ease in H2 as supply-demand balances improve and new capacity timing shifts economics. It forecasts domestic alumina prices to fluctuate around production costs despite high bauxite/energy/caustic soda inputs. Overseas, weaker cost support may pressure prices.

title: NorthWest Copper Announces First Drill Results From 2022
summary: NorthWest Copper announced assay results from the first three holes of its 2022 Kwanika drilling program, reporting multiple intervals of significant copper-gold mineralization (CuEq ~0.61% to 1.21%). The company says results expand mineralized footprint and increase confidence in its resource model, supporting longer-term copper potential.

title: Vale cuts 2022 iron ore output forecast amid lower prices, including for nickel
summary: Vale cut its 2022 iron ore output forecast citing lower market prices, but also lowered its copper production estimate and reported weaker nickel performance. Nickel output fell 16.1% in the quarter, while copper production dropped 23.9% year-on-year. Analysts expect weaker results to weigh on base metals sentiment.

title: Canada Nickel Identifies New Method for Accelerated CO2 Capture
summary: Canada Nickel reports lab test results for accelerated CO2 capture at its Crawford nickel-cobalt project using in-process tailings carbonation. The company claims near-term net-zero emissions in 36 hours at lab scale and significant CO2 credit potential. It may improve future nickel project economics, but no immediate production impact is stated.

title: Volkswagen to build nickel processing plant in Indonesia this year-Xinhua
summary: Volkswagen plans to build a nickel ore production and processing plant in Indonesia this year, with sites in Batang regency and Sulawesi. The project is still under negotiation, including incentives and reserve capacity. The news highlights Indonesia’s large nickel resources and rising nickel exports, supporting nickel demand sentiment.

title: Russia's Nornickel Increases Supplies to Finland, Plans to Increase Production
summary: Russia’s Nornickel increased deliveries of nickel matte to its Finnish unit and plans to raise production to 100,000 tonnes. The report cites a 72% rise in April export value and ongoing plant operations, while noting logistics and potential further sanctions risks.

title: Europe's Power Crunch Cuts Zinc and Aluminum Capacity in Half
summary: Europe’s power crunch is reportedly cutting aluminum capacity by half. Reduced operating rates from high energy costs can tighten near-term aluminum supply expectations, affecting producer output and sentiment across the aluminum market.

title: Brazil's Vale lowers iron ore, copper guidance
summary: The article headline says Brazil’s Vale has lowered its guidance, including for copper. Lower company guidance usually implies a less favorable near-term outlook for copper volumes or market conditions. This can weigh on sentiment and expected price levels for copper in the coming days to weeks.

title: Why history provides a cautionary tale for aluminium | Hotter on metals
summary: The article argues that aluminium smelting is highly sensitive to power and gas prices. It cites Europe idling over 900,000 tonnes of primary capacity due to soaring energy costs and warns some curtailments may become permanent. It compares past energy shocks in the US and Japan that led to closures.

title: SDI makes $2.2-billion move into aluminium business
summary: SDI will invest $2.2bn to build an aluminium rolling mill (650,000 tpa) plus two recycling facilities supplying aluminium slab, targeting beverage can and automotive sheet. The firm cites a growing North American flat-rolled aluminium supply deficit and says the projects will start from 2024/2025.

title: Volkswagen to build nickel processing plant in Indonesia this year
summary: Volkswagen said it will build its first nickel ore production and processing plant in Indonesia this year, in Batang regency. The minister noted negotiations are ongoing regarding investment value, incentives, and nickel ore reserve capacity. The move signals incremental Indonesian refining demand for nickel.

title: Japanese firm shifts copper foil plans from South Carolina to Georgia
summary: The (expired) article title says a Japanese firm is shifting planned copper-foil manufacturing from South Carolina to Georgia. However, the provided content lacks details on production volume, startup timing, or any change in total capacity. With only a location change, short-term copper price effects appear minimal.

title: Japanese copper foil maker, Denkai America, to build plant in Augusta
summary: Japan’s Denkai America plans a $150 million initial investment and up to $430 million for a North American headquarters and manufacturing plant in Augusta, producing copper foil for printed electronics and lithium-ion batteries. The buildout implies incremental near-term demand for copper materials, which can be mildly supportive for copper prices.

title: SMM: Rising Supply and Slow Consumption Recovery Likely to Weigh on Aluminium Market in H2_SMM
summary: SMM expects aluminium prices to face downside risk in H2 as China’s operating capacity resumes and supply grows faster than downstream demand recovery. It notes slower consumption post-pandemic, rising ingot/billet supply with inventories likely turning up, and cost support from high costs, but net supply-demand pressure dominates.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices Stayed Strong with Increasing Pure Nickel Spot Prices_SMM
summary: SMM says SHFE nickel spot markets stayed strong on July 21. Jinchuan nickel carried premiums of 16,000–16,500 yuan/mt versus NORNICKEL at 12,500–13,000, both up from the prior day. Nickel briquette prices also rose with futures, though nickel-sulphate cost efficiency was poorer and deal activity remained muted.

title: SMM Aluminium Ingot and Billet Inventory both Dropped on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China aluminium ingot social inventory fell to 668,000 mt on July 21, down from both the prior week and a year earlier, as delayed arrivals and deliveries resumed selectively. Billet inventory also dropped to 95,400 mt, helped by weaker north-west smelter shipments and downstream restocking, likely continuing to fall next week.

title: Volkswagen to build nickel processing plant in Indonesia this year | Companies
summary: Volkswagen said it will build its first nickel ore production and processing plant in Indonesia this year. Indonesian officials cited large local nickel reserves and rising exports, with VW negotiating investment value and incentives. The news points to additional downstream processing activity, supporting near-term nickel demand expectations.

title: AngloAmerican Q2 production falls 9% on lower copper grades
summary: Anglo American said Q2 output fell 9% due to likely lower copper grades and lack of water availability in Chile, alongside planned maintenance at its Minas-Rio iron ore mine. The update implies weaker near-term copper production prospects, which can increase expectations of tighter supply and bearish copper price pressure.

title: Copper prices decline as weak U.S. data stokes demand worries
summary: Copper prices fell after bleak U.S. housing data raised recession and demand worries, with mortgage-rate pressures hurting affordability. The article links copper’s move to weakening global growth expectations and softer Chinese demand confidence amid COVID-19 restrictions, driving bearish sentiment in near-term pricing.

title: Los Andes Copper Ltd.: Los Andes Copper Announces Decision by the Environmental Court Reinstating Drilling Permit
summary: Los Andes Copper Ltd. said Chile’s Second Environmental Court revised a prior injunction and reinstated its drilling permit for the Vizcachitas Copper Project, allowing drilling to continue with restrictions for the first 12 months. The company submitted studies to show environmental compatibility and plans to advance exploration and a prefixed feasibility study.

title: Freeport-McMoRan misses on profit and revenue amid a 'precipitous' fall in copper prices
summary: Freeport-McMoRan reported second-quarter profit and revenue below expectations, attributing weak performance to a precipitous fall in copper prices. Average realized copper price fell 7.1% to $4.03/lb despite higher production. The company cited higher U.S. rates, a strong dollar and global economy concerns, pressuring copper sentiment.

title: Los Andes Copper : Announces Decision by the Environmental Court Reinstating Drilling Permit
summary: Los Andes Copper said Chile’s Second Environmental Court revised an injunction and reinstated its drilling permit for the Vizcachitas Copper Project, with operational restrictions for the first 12 months. The decision allows drilling to continue and expand its program toward a prefeasibility study in Q4 2022.

title: Vale Indonesia, China's Huayou sign agreement with Ford for nickel plant
summary: Vale Indonesia, Huayou and Ford signed a non-binding memorandum to build an Indonesia plant producing 120,000 tonnes per annum of nickel chemicals for EV batteries. The project builds on prior Huayou/Vale framework rights and comes amid Indonesia’s push to process nickel domestically after the unprocessed ore export ban.

title: Steel Dynamics, Unity, former Braidy Industries plans aluminum plant
summary: Steel Dynamics will build a $1.9 billion low-carbon flat rolled aluminium plant in the Southeast, with 650,000 metric tons/year capacity, starting production in early 2025, and will own most of the joint venture with Unity. The project also includes two supporting recycled slab centers, expanding North American supply.

title: Freeport-McMoRan Misses Profit Estimates On Lower Copper Prices
summary: Freeport-McMoRan reported a Q2 profit miss driven by lower realized copper prices ($4.03/lb vs. $4.34/lb). Copper fell about 20.4% in April–June amid recession fears and China COVID lockdowns. The miner warns current prices may not fund new mines, worsening supply tightness.

title: Rio Tinto signs with Ford for carbon-free aluminium
summary: Rio Tinto signed an exploratory memorandum with Ford to develop and potentially supply low-carbon materials for next-generation vehicles, including battery and lightweight components. The deal explicitly mentions aluminium and copper, and supports expectations of increased demand as EV and truck production expand in North America, Europe and China.

title: World Copper Ltd.: World Copper Closes First Tranche of $2.5 Million Non-Brokered Private Placement And, Retains Paradox Public Relations Inc. to Provide Investor Relations Services
summary: World Copper Ltd. reports closing the first tranche of a $2.5 million private placement, raising gross proceeds of about $1.28 million. Funds are intended for exploration and development of its Escalones and Zonia copper projects, plus working capital. The article also covers investor relations arrangements and warrant terms.

title: Surging Natural Gas Prices Create 'Complicated Situation' for Aluminum Giant Alcoa
summary: Alcoa executives say surging natural gas prices have forced European smelters to cut capacity, including a two-year curtailment at its San Ciprian smelter in Spain and a 15% drop in refinery production. With spot-driven costs, operations are loss-making and aluminum supply remains under pressure despite demand growth.

title: Governor seeks to salvage aluminum mill deal promised to Kentucky
summary: Kentucky’s Gov. Andy Beshear is trying to salvage a deal for a proposed aluminium mill after the previous plan to locate the plant in Kentucky failed. His administration is reaching out to Steel Dynamics, which will build the mill with Unity Aluminum but has not specified a Kentucky site. Financing issues are cited.

title: Peru indigenous communities say no progress in talks with Las Bambas mine
summary: Peruvian indigenous communities protesting MMG’s Las Bambas copper mine say there has been no progress after a month of talks and the 30-day truce has ended without a clear next step. The earlier protests shut operations for over a month, so renewed disruption risk is increased.

title: Another twist in the Ashland aluminum mill saga raises fresh questions about $15 million state investment
summary: The Unity Aluminum/Braidy project in Kentucky is in dispute, with Gov. Andy Beshear criticizing the state investment and saying it has received nothing so far. Steel Dynamics is scouting for a planned $1.9 billion plant with Unity, but no site commitment is confirmed. The outcome could influence aluminum supply expectations.

title: China's Nickel Ore Imports Stood at 4.3106 million mt in June amid the Poor Demand_SMM
summary: China’s nickel ore imports totaled 4.31 million mt in June, up MoM but down YoY, with weak first-half demand. Philippine laterite imports were constrained by negative sentiment as NPI and nickel ore prices fell through transmission from a poor stainless steel market. Stainless output cuts further reduced ore demand into July-August.

title: Limerick's Aughinish Alumina under energy cost pressures
summary: Aughinish Alumina in Limerick avoided Deripaska/Rusal sanctions but faces rising energy costs. The article notes Romanian alumina producer Alum was forced to halt output for 17 months, laying off 70% of staff, while Alro Group (a major aluminium smelter) warns energy-driven production cost damage affecting calcined alumina and electrolytic aluminium.

title: Romanian alumina producer to halt production, lay off 500 | Companies
summary: Romanian alumina producer ALUM plans to temporarily suspend its Tulcea alumina operations from Aug. 1 for about 17 months, citing very high and scarce electricity and natural gas, plus rising CO2 certificate prices. The shutdown follows losses and cost escalation and implies lower alumina supply for aluminium production.

title: BASF and TODA to further expand their Japanese joint venture's capacity for high nickel cathode active materials
summary: BASF and TODA will expand their Japanese joint venture’s capacity for high-nickel cathode active materials at Onoda. BTBM’s capacity targets up to 60,000 tons by 2025, supported by subsidies under a supply-chain program. The project responds to fast-growing lithium-ion battery demand, boosting expected nickel consumption.

title: Crawford Nickel Sulphide Project, Ontario, Canada
summary: Canada Nickel Company’s Crawford nickel sulphide project in Ontario is progressing with an ongoing feasibility study and defined open-pit mining and processing plans, targeting long-term nickel supply (and other by-products). The report does not indicate imminent production or disruptions, so near-term effects on nickel pricing appear limited.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Decreased by 15,300 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventories across major Chinese markets fell by 15,300 mt from Monday to 94,500 mt, and by 26,200 mt versus last Friday. The largest drop was in Guangdong, driven by lower import inflows and shipments into warehouses, while downstream demand was steady, supporting firm spot premiums.

title: Copper Inventory in China Bonded Zone Dropped by 2,000 mt on Week_SMM
summary: SMM said copper inventories in China’s bonded zones fell by 2,000 mt to 276,300 mt as of July 22, continuing a four-week decline but at a slower pace. Shanghai was flat while Guangdong declined. Poor import trading, limited warrant shipments, and steady inflow into bonded warehouses kept the drawdown modest.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports up 375,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
