It also notes copper-nickel-cobalt occurrence context and anomalous nickel/cobalt, but no production impact.

title: Great Atlantic Resources Corp.: Great Atlantic Drilling Intersects 6.74% Copper, 34.5 G/T Silver and .6 G/T Gold over .4 Meters as well Nickel and Cobalt also Anomalous Mascarene Property New Brunswick
summary: Great Atlantic Resources reports new drill core results from its Mascarene Property in New Brunswick, including a 0.40m intercept grading 6.74% copper and anomalous nickel (plus cobalt) and gold/silver. The findings support copper-bearing veins, but the update is early exploration without production implications for metal prices.

title: China's Output of Nickel Sulphate is Expected to Increase in August due to the Considerable Profits_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s nickel sulphate output rose in July, with battery-grade production increasing and inventories for battery-grade further declining, tightening retail supply. Due to strong MHP profits, August output is expected to rise ~4% month-on-month, mainly from high-grade nickel matte lines, suggesting easing nickel sulphate supply that can weigh on nickel prices.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Reports Results from Continuing Drilling at Lappvattnet Nickel Deposit and Highlights Eastern Potential
summary: Gungnir Resources reports first 2022 assays from continuing drilling at its Lappvattnet nickel deposit in Sweden, including wide zones up to 19m at 0.80% Ni and peak grades above 4%. Drilling is progressing to the eastern area and a new EM target, suggesting resource expansion potential.

title: Tesla Reportedly Signs $5 Billion Nickel Supply Deal In Indonesia
summary: Tesla reportedly signed about $5 billion in five-year nickel supply contracts with Indonesian processing companies. The nickel will be used in Tesla’s lithium batteries, according to a cabinet minister. With Indonesia the largest nickel producer and export curbs intended to support downstream supply, the deal signals stronger nickel demand.

title: MHP emerges as preferred route to sulfate for international nickel market
summary: Fastmarkets says MHP (from Indonesian laterite) is increasingly the preferred feedstock for nickel sulfate producers. Despite rapidly rising MHP output, China’s conversion capacity is still tight, keeping nickel sulfate supply constrained since late July. Producers cite rising offer prices and an MHP payable uptrend as demand picks up.

title: Copper Prices Slide Sideways As Bulls And Bears Battle It Out
summary: Copper prices are described as moving sideways after earlier gains, with recession fears weighing on the market despite a stronger US labor report (unemployment down to 3.5%). Demand themes include China/US infrastructure support, while risks include China’s property crisis and possible Chile supply-investment uncertainty.

title: Hudbay Files Early Warning Report for American Copper
summary: Hudbay Minerals filed an early warning report related to an asset/share transaction with American Copper Development, involving issuance of consideration shares for acquisition of a 100% interest in a New Mexico property. The release mainly covers share mechanics and securities disclosure, with no direct near-term copper supply or demand impact stated.

title: SMM Outlook for Aluminium Market in the Third Quarter_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM’s Aug 10 outlook says aluminium prices face two pressures: new domestic supply/resumed idle capacity and weaker overseas consumption concerns. Costs remain firm (cash ~16,500 yuan/mt) while inventory is low but ingot/billet stocks have risen recently and may rise through late August, limiting upside.

title: Copper Cathode Supply Concerns Triggered by Sudden COVID Lockdown in Guixi City_SMM
summary: Guixi City in Jiangxi Province was locked down from 5:30am Aug 10 with no end time announced. The city hosts China’s largest copper cathode smelter (1mn mt/yr), prompting supply tightness concerns despite limited reported production disruption and normal rail flows, with truck transport somewhat affected.

title: Horizonte awards Copa industrial civil works contract at Araguaia Nickel Project
summary: Horizonte Minerals awarded Copa an industrial civil works contract for its Araguaia Nickel Project in Brazil, covering process plant foundations and concrete structures to accelerate construction toward furnace shell installation in 4Q22. The update supports ongoing project development but provides no direct near-term production or supply shock details.

title: Tesla Giga Nevada will soon source copper foil from Redwood Materials
summary: Redwood Materials will begin producing recycled copper foil in 2026, with Panasonic at Tesla’s Gigafactory Nevada among the first customers. The company claims the recycled copper foil cuts CO2 versus an Asia-based battery supply chain and plans to ramp output over time. The near-term news supports copper demand but likely not price materially.

title: Go Metals Corp.: Go Metals Begins Drilling at HSP Nickel-Copper PGE Project
summary: Go Metals began diamond drilling at its HSP nickel-copper PGE project in Quebec, testing six EM/geophysical targets after confirmed nickel-copper sulphide mineralization at surface. The initial program plans about 2,000 metres of drilling. This is exploration with no production impact reported.

title: Go Metals Corp.: Go Metals Begins Drilling at HSP Nickel-Copper PGE Project
summary: Go Metals Corp. began its 2022 diamond drilling program at the HSP nickel-copper PGE project in Quebec. Surface targets were previously confirmed with nickel-copper sulphides and PGE. The company plans about 2,000 metres of drilling for initial testing, with samples sent for independent analysis.

title: Copper gains after U.S. inflation data undershoots, dollar slides
summary: Copper rose about 1% after U.S. inflation came in weaker than expected, easing fears of aggressive rate hikes and supporting a weaker dollar. Comex futures also climbed. The article notes aluminium fell on the same day, while nickel gained sharply, suggesting mostly supportive macro demand sentiment for copper.

title: Second-Largest U.S. Aluminum Mill Idles Due to 'Untenable' Energy Prices, Laying Off 600 American Workers
summary: Century Aluminum idled its Hawesville, Kentucky aluminum smelter for 9–12 months, laying off about 600 workers, citing “untenable” electricity and energy prices after power costs tripled. Alcoa is also curtailing smelting at its Warrick, Indiana plant, with broader energy-driven industrial slowdown implied.

title: Review of Alumina Market in July-August: Prices of Alumina Varied between North and South China_SMM
summary: SMM reviews July–August alumina pricing in China, with northern output reduced at times due to high costs and tight spot supply, while later expectations of cuts were not fully met. Southern China saw new capacity ramping up in Guangxi/Chongqing, leading to steadier but slightly softer alumina prices, pressuring deals toward lower levels.

title: Pure Nickel Transactions were Poor as SHFE Nickel Prices were High_SMM
summary: On Aug 11, SHFE nickel prices were high and spot trading was poor. Jinchuan nickel premiums rose to 7,000-8,000 yuan/mt, while Nornickel premiums fell to 4,000-4,500 yuan/mt. Nickel briquette prices increased mainly from narrowed premiums, but spot demand remained weak due to lower product appeal.

title: Alpha Copper Provides Indata Project Drill Campaign Update
summary: Alpha Copper reports results and ongoing drill progress at its Indata copper-gold project, targeting vein gold and porphyry copper-gold mineralization with associated molybdenum. It describes chalcopyrite mineralization and encourages copper-bearing intercepts, which can affect near-term copper market sentiment. No nickel or aluminium impacts are indicated.

title: Operating Rate of Aluminium Billet Producers Dropped Steadily in July_SMM
summary: SMM’s survey shows domestic aluminium billet producer operating rates fell to 71.3% in July and are expected to decline further in August. Downstream extruder rates dropped, and Sichuan faced power rationing and an aluminium smelter accident disrupting 190,000 mt of aluminium and 40,000 mt of billets, hurting demand.

title: SMM Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventory as of August 11 _SMM
summary: SMM says aluminium ingot social inventories across eight Chinese markets rose to 693,000 mt as of Aug 11, accumulating for three straight weeks, while downstream demand remains weak and the price rebound curbs buying. Aluminium billet inventories also increased for five consecutive weeks, suggesting further inventory growth next week.

title: Tesla to invest in Indonesia as country bets on nickel reserves
summary: Tesla has signed nickel-containing product supply contracts with two Indonesian companies, including a reported $5 billion deal for five years, as Indonesia positions itself as a hub for battery-related green industries. The announcement supports expectations of higher nickel demand linked to EV and battery growth.

title: Copper speculators anticipate downturn for market and the world
summary: Reuters reports LME and COMEX speculative positioning is net bearish for copper, with funds holding large short positions and buying put options targeting lower prices. The backdrop is concerns over growth slowdown in China and aggressive interest-rate hikes that raise recession risk, threatening further declines in demand and copper prices.

title: Copper Speculators Anticipate Downturn For Market And The World
summary: Speculators are increasingly positioning for a global downturn, building bearish exposure in copper on the LME and COMEX and buying downside put options. With copper still pressured by recession risks from China growth slowdown and aggressive rate hikes, the article highlights potential for prices to fall further toward marginal production-cost levels.

title: Kentucky Aluminum Mill Laid Off Hundreds of Workers Due to 'Untenable' Energy Prices
summary: Century Aluminum laid off hundreds at its Hawesville, Kentucky primary aluminum plant, citing “untenable” energy prices. The plant will stay idle for nine to 12 months until power costs are expected to normalize. The curtailment tightens supply forecasts for primary aluminum and is likely bearish for near-term prices.

title: Aluminum Spacers Market to Garner $866.4 Million, Globally, By 2031 at 4.7% CAGR, Says Allied Market Research
summary: The PRNewswire piece summarizes an Allied Market Research report on global aluminum spacers demand, citing substitution from metal, construction and transport end-use, and manufacturing emphasis in Asia-Pacific. It also notes feedstock availability at reduced prices but provides no short-term supply disruption or policy shock that would materially move aluminium prices immediately.

title: AUD/USD Targets 200-Day SMA As Copper And Coal Prices Surge ...
summary: Copper prices gained around 1.56% in New York as the US dollar pulled back, supporting a firmer Australian dollar. The piece also highlights higher energy prices and a weak Rhine water level affecting coal transport and stockpiling, reinforcing broader commodity strength that can lift industrial metals sentiment.

title: How Strong of a Rebound Will We See? Copper Price Where to?
summary: The piece attributes copper’s rebound to softer inflation (falling CPI) and visible effects of Fed rate hikes easing financial pressure. It notes copper has recovered nearly 15% and highlights domestic inventories at record lows, focusing on how tight supply and demand dynamics may sustain further gains.

title: Glencore Halts Supplies to Chinese Trader Over $500 Million of Copper Missing, Financial Times Reports
summary: Glencore and IXM reportedly stopped supplying Huludao Ruisheng after $500 million worth of copper went missing. Glencore also moved some stock from Qinhuangdao to other ports to reduce similar risks. Traders said Western exposure is limited, but the incident still threatens short-term copper supply confidence.

title: Imports of Bauxite Dropped Sharply by 2.56 Million mt in June with Reductions Observed in All Countries _SMM
summary: China’s bauxite imports fell to 9.42 million mt in June, down 21.4% MoM, with declines from Australia and Guinea and a steep drop from Indonesia amid export-ban fears. Weather reduced production and shipments in Australia/Guinea, while Indonesia supply looks tighter, potentially pressuring alumina availability and supporting aluminium prices.

title: Thomson Geer confirms role in $205m proposed sale of Kalkaroo copper-gold project
summary: Thomson Geer confirmed its involvement in Havilah Resources’ proposed $205m sale of the Kalkaroo copper-gold project to OZ Minerals. OZ will evaluate for 18 months and may buy 100% subject to milestones, with potential extra payments. An alliance also targets copper exploration in the Curnamona Province.

title: Alumina Prices Will Fluctuate in A Narrow Range amid Resonance of New Projects and Production Reduction _SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices in China are largely stable within a narrow range as northern refineries face high-cost pressure and production reductions, tightening spot supplies, while new capacity in the southwest adds supply and pressures prices. Overall transaction activity is thin, with expectations of stable prices in the north and slight declines in the south.

title: Aluminium Prices Likely to Move in A Wide Range with Supply Inconsistency and Seasonal Low in the Consumer Market_SMM
summary: SMM reports volatile aluminium trading, with SHFE prices rising despite sluggish consumption. Supply is supported by unexpected Sichuan smelter cuts and ongoing Europe energy-related capacity limits, while downstream operating rates remain weak and inventories keep rising. Exports are strong but overseas semi demand is expected to stall, keeping prices range-bound.

title: Operating Rates of Aluminium Plate/Sheet And Strip Producers Fell in July amid Poor Orders_SMM
summary: SMM says Chinese aluminium plate/sheet and strip producers’ average operating rate fell to 74.99% in July amid sluggish end consumption and insufficient new orders. Producers cut output or margins. Although inventories fell after late-July price rebound, firms expect continued weak off-season demand, potentially worsened by power rationing in August.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Decreased by 2,100 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says Chinese copper inventories across major markets fell to 70,700 mt, down 2,100 mt from Monday, though still above last Friday. Shanghai dropped but Guangdong rose. Power rationing clouded east-China supply/demand, while falling SHFE premiums may boost demand elsewhere, making next week’s trend uncertain.

title: Bonded Zone Inventory of Nickel Dropped Slightly this Week amid the Poor Demand_SMM
summary: SMM says China bonded zone inventory fell to 6,500 mt, with nickel briquette and plate down WoW, helped by slightly improved spot trading early in the week. However, after SHFE nickel prices rebounded, demand for pure nickel weakened, pointing to bearish near-term sentiment for nickel.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fell by 40,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Chinese nickel ore inventories fell by 40,000 wmt WoW to 6.289 million wmt as of Aug 12, with total Ni content at 49,000 mt. Although demand for raw materials is described as poor, tight market supply and mines holding back shipments suggest short-term nickel ore levels may stay steady, supporting nickel.

title: Sky-high Energy Costs To Fan Fire Under Aluminium And Zinc Prices
summary: Sky-high European energy costs are forcing aluminium smelters to cut output further, potentially reducing winter capacity. LME aluminium inventories are at very low levels, adding supply-fear support. While recession-driven demand risks are noted, the supply contraction from energy constraints is expected to be price supportive in the near term.

title: Finnish shipyard to build icebreaker for Norilsk Nickel — TV
summary: Finland’s Arctech Helsinki Shipyard plans to build a large LNG-powered icebreaker for Norilsk Nickel. An export license application under sanctions has been filed and a decision is expected in coming months, with an exception possible for a pre-sanctions contract. The vessel would escort Norilsk ships on the Yenisei River.

title: Sky-high energy costs to fan fire under aluminium and zinc prices
summary: Sky-high European energy costs are pressuring aluminium and zinc smelters, with analysts warning of further capacity cuts this winter and already low LME inventories. The resulting tighter supply deficits could outweigh demand worries, supporting expectations of relative price outperformance, particularly for aluminium, if power curbs occur.

title: Codelco Turns to AI to Squeeze Out More Copper From Aging Mines
summary: Codelco says it is using AI to squeeze more copper from aging mines. The move is aimed at improving extraction from existing deposits rather than starting new projects. If it translates into incremental output, markets may expect tighter supply conditions easing, which can lift near-term copper sentiment.

title: Have Nickel Prices Hit A Bottom?
summary: Nickel prices appear to have rebounded mid-July but then resumed declining in August, with movements staying tight and direction unclear. Indonesia’s proposed export taxes on nickel intermediates (NPI and ferro-nickel) have not yet lifted prices, and any market response is expected closer to a levy start in Q3 2022.

title: Offshore firm links BBC chair to sanction-hit Russian 'Nickel King' | Richard Sharp
summary: A BBC chair’s offshore investment connects to Vladimir Potanin, a UK-sanctioned Russian oligarch known for nickel through Nornickel. The crypto firm involved trades commodities, especially metals produced by Nornickel. While sanctions and association may be relevant, the article gives no new immediate supply or trade disruption for nickel.

title: Operating Rates of Molten Aluminium Casting Billet Enterprises Continued to Fall in July amid Sharp Decline in Orders_SMM
summary: SMM reports domestic molten aluminium casting billet firms operated at 71.3% in July, down for a second month. Downstream extruder rates fell sharply, prompting billet output cuts, while Sichuan power rationing and an accident disrupting 190,000 mt smelter capacity and 40,000 mt billet capacity may weigh further in August.

title: Alumina Prices Fell Across both North and South China, Market Transactions Increased _SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices fell across North and South China, with weaker bids and a gradual tilt toward a buyer’s market. Overseas FOB Western Australia prices also declined. Supply risk is tempered near term, but new capacity is set to ramp up in September-October, reviving oversupply concerns.

title: Unexpected Production Cuts and Seasonal Low to Keep Aluminium Prices Moving in A Wide Range_SMM
summary: SMM reports Sichuan’s aluminium smelter was shut after an accident, and 285,000 mt of capacity was cut due to power rationing. Despite some easing oversupply, downstream demand remains weak, social inventories keep rising, and overseas demand falls amid high energy prices and rate-hike expectations. Aluminium seen ranging widely this week.

title: Copper Prices Continued to Rebound amid the Declining Domestic and Overseas Inventory_SMM
summary: SMM reports copper prices rebounded after softer-than-expected US CPI cooled rate-hike expectations and weakened the dollar. Fundamentals are mixed but supportive: tight blister/scrap, July smelter maintenance leading to low cathode output, then expected August rebound. Demand from infrastructure and wire/cable orders strengthened, with some inventory trend stability.

title: TCs of Spot Copper Concentrates Rose to Nearly $74-75/mt with the Improvement of Spot Trading_SMM
summary: SMM says spot copper concentrate trading improved, with the Imported Copper Concentrate Index rising to about $74.38/mt. Traded spot TCs increased to $71-72/mt and a smelter bought at nearly $74-75/mt. Rumoured Qinhuangdao resales had limited spillover, as most smelters rely on long-term orders.

title: Rio Tinto copper target freezes takeover talks
summary: Rio Tinto would have needed to raise its offer to Turquoise Hill minority shareholders to win board endorsement for a full takeover. Turquoise Hill’s chairman says talks ended, potentially blocking the plan to lift Rio’s stake to 100%. The news implies deal uncertainty rather than direct copper supply or demand changes.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices may Remain High Thanks to the Favourable Macro Factors_SMM
summary: SMM expects SHFE nickel to remain high, citing supportive macro data: US CPI and PPI growth both came in below expectations, boosting commodity prices in China. Supply is rising (domestic pure nickel, Indonesian NPI oversupply), while demand is cautious, but demand for nickel sulfate may support briquette demand and tighten inventories.

title: Imperial Aluminum eyes for industrial site for expansion in Minerva
summary: Imperial Aluminum in Minerva seeks to expand by reactivating a nearby former industrial building. Because the structure contains lead and asbestos, officials are pursuing state grant funding to pay for hazardous-material cleanup before demolition and site use. The project is expected to support Imperial’s operations and potential hiring.

title: Rio Tinto's Offer to Take Over Giant Copper Mine Is Rebuffed
summary: Rio Tinto’s proposed takeover of a large copper mine was rebuffed, according to the article headline. The rejection likely introduces uncertainty about future ownership and development timelines for the asset, which may negatively affect near-term expectations for copper supply and thereby pressure copper prices.

title: Aluminium Inventory maintained the upward trend _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says China’s aluminium ingot social inventories totaled 698,000 mt on Aug 15, up 5,000 mt week-on-week but down 44,000 mt year-on-year and still at a low level. Wuxi fell on fewer arrivals; Foshan declined with higher shipments. Sichuan production is cut due to power issues, potentially reducing southbound arrivals.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets down 400 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventory in major Chinese markets fell 400 mt to 70,300 mt from Friday, and is far lower than last year. Low imported arrivals and reduced east-China smelter output contributed to the draw, while some flow shifted to Guangdong. Resumption of smelters may later increase stockpiles.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28 Releases Update on Giga Royalty: Secures Mitsubishi as Development Partner
summary: Nickel 28 updates its 2% NSR royalty on Giga Metal’s Turnagain nickel/cobalt deposit after Giga formed a joint venture with Mitsubishi to pursue development in British Columbia. The company highlights EV demand growth support for nickel and cobalt and says the JV clears a key hurdle toward development.

title: Quebec allows copper smelter in northwest to emit arsenic levels five times norm
summary: Quebec’s environment minister set a new arsenic emission limit for the Horne copper smelter in Rouyn-Noranda at 15 nanograms per cubic metre, lower than its current 100 and above the provincial norm. The measure responds to health concerns, including higher lung cancer rates in local residents.

title: Quebec allows copper smelter to emit arsenic levels five times norm
summary: Quebec has allowed a copper smelter in Rouyn-Noranda to emit arsenic levels up to five times the norm. The regulatory decision may reduce compliance pressure and help sustain smelting throughput, supporting near-term copper supply expectations and potentially aiding copper prices in the coming days.

title: Quebec allows copper smelter in northwest to emit arsenic levels five times norm | iNFOnews
summary: Quebec’s environment minister approved a new arsenic emissions cap for Glencore’s Horne copper smelter in Rouyn-Noranda, lowering the limit to 15 nanograms per cubic metre over five years from 100. Updated rules will also address nickel and other pollutants, with no immediate closure announced.

title: Australian Dollar Falls Alongside Copper And Iron Ore Ahead ...
summary: The piece attributes pressure on the Australian dollar to stronger USD and recession fears, citing weak U.S. data and China’s softer retail sales and industrial production. It specifically says copper prices came under pressure, weighing on risk sentiment. RBA minutes and wage expectations are also in focus.

title: Bravo Intercepts High-Grade Nickel/Copper Massive Sulphide Mineralization at Luanga
summary: Bravo Mining announced high-grade results from the Luanga drill hole DDH22LU047, including 11.04m at 2.04% nickel and 1.23% copper (with higher-grade inclusions). The company is starting downhole electromagnetic surveying and continuing a multi-rig Phase 1 diamond drill program, with PGM results pending.

title: Bravo Intercepts High-Grade Nickel/Copper Massive Sulphide Mineralization at Luanga
summary: Bravo Mining announced high-grade intercepts from diamond drilling at its Luanga project in Brazil, including 11.04m at 2.04% nickel and 1.23% copper, with additional high-grade copper/nickel sub-intervals. DHTEM surveying and further drilling are planned, with PGM results pending, supporting positive sentiment for Ni and Cu.

title: DLP Resources Inc.: DLP Resources Announces Receipt of Water Permit for the Aurora Copper-Molybdenum Project in Peru, Drilling to Commence
summary: DLP Resources said it received a water permit for its Aurora porphyry copper-molybdenum project in Peru and has started a first-phase ~5,000m drilling program to test copper enrichment and primary copper-molybdenum mineralization. The article is exploratory and does not imply near-term production changes.

title: 10 Copper Stocks to Buy Now as Recession Fears Recede

summary: Reuters reports Shanghai aluminium prices rallied on supply concerns tied to European and China production disruptions. title: Antofagasta's Twin Metals sues Biden administration over Minnesota copper project | 100.7 MIX-FM | Today's Hit Music
summary: Antofagasta’s Twin Metals sued the Biden administration to challenge the cancellation of Minnesota mineral leases for its proposed underground copper and nickel mine. Twin Metals said the January decision was illegal and should allow its project to be assessed under regulatory standards, potentially improving near-term supply expectations.

title: Culpeo Minerals confirms large-scale copper mineralisation at Lana Corina
summary: Culpeo Minerals reported expanded high-priority drill targets after mapping confirmed large-scale copper oxide and breccia mineralisation at the Lana Corina project in Chile. Recent drilling returned multiple substantial copper and molybdenum intercepts, and the mineralised footprint increased to 500m by 400m. The update is exploration-focused.

title: China Primary Aluminium Import and Export in Jul_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM cites China customs data showing primary aluminium imports of 51,037.4 mt in July, down 82.1% MoM and 97.2% YoY. Exports reached 7,588.4 mt, up 14.6% MoM and 16x YoY, with much higher export totals from January to July.

title: China's Ferronickel Imports Continued to Decline in July, with Imports from Indonesia down Significantly_SMM
summary: China’s ferronickel imports fell to 387,400 mt in July for a second straight monthly decline, with Indonesian-origin shipments down 16% month-on-month. Meanwhile, China’s NPI inventories are in surplus, leading to production curtailments. Indonesia is also said to consider nickel export tariffs targeting NPI and ferronickel.

title: China's Copper Scrap Imports Increased 4.02% Year-on-Year in July_SMM
summary: China’s copper scrap imports rose 4.02% year-on-year to 155,168.64 mt in July, though they fell 6% versus the previous month. The US remained the biggest supplier at 26,559.12 mt, down 15.21% month-on-month but up 16.55% year-on-year.

title: Clearance Volume of Pure Nickel Decreased 6.48% MoM amid the Weak Downstream Demand after Mid-July_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s customs clearance volume of pure nickel fell to 9,517 mt in July, down 660 mt vs June, driven by weaker downstream demand after late-July restocking. Import profitability was pressured by rising bonded premiums and poor terminal demand, and spot imports are expected to remain loss-making in August.

title: China Nickel Ore Imports Rise Fractionally MoM in Jul, the Lowest in Five Years_SMM
summary: China’s nickel ore imports were 4.37 million mt in July, up slightly month-on-month for two months but at the lowest level in recent years. Imports from the Philippines increased, while Indonesia and New Caledonia declined. Gains were muted by weak Chinese demand and a lacklustre market.

title: Spot Transactions were Poor and the Spot Premiums of Jinchuan Nickel Declined_SMM
summary: SMM reports that on Aug 23, Jinchuan nickel spot premiums fell to 3,500–5,500 yuan/mt (avg 4,500), down 900 from the prior day, while Nornickel premiums rose slightly. Despite futures remaining high, downstream demand stayed weak, spot transactions remained poor, and physical pricing weakened for nickel.

title: Alumina says unit costs have peaked as commodity price slides
summary: Alumina Limited’s managing director says the inflationary pressures that raised its unit costs by 32% over the past year have likely peaked. The firm notes alumina prices have fallen from an average of about $398/tonne over six months to roughly $330/tonne recently, easing cost pressures and supporting the aluminium value chain.

title: Aluminum Rally Pushes Top Gulf Producer EGA to Record Profit
summary: BNN Bloomberg notes that an aluminium rally has helped Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) achieve record profits. This suggests favourable aluminium price levels and/or demand conditions for the producer in the near term, supporting market expectations for aluminium.

title: Secondary Copper Supply Keeps Improving with Copper Cathode Prices Remaining High_SMM
summary: SMM reports East China copper scrap throughput rose sharply week-on-week as cargo holders sold some high-priced inventories, while downstream secondary rod firms urgently restocked. Copper cathode prices stayed high, spreads to scrap widened, imports fell, inventories were extremely low, and power rationing restricted output—supporting bullish near-term copper sentiment.

title: Impact of High Temperature on the Output of Nickel Sulphate_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: High temperatures triggered stronger power consumption controls and rationing across multiple regions, including Zhejiang. SMM says power curtailment severely impacted nickel sulphate producers, cutting Zhejiang nickel sulphate output from 5,388 mt Ni in July to 4,416 mt in August (down 18% m/m), with only minimal growth domestically.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay Announces Major New Copper Discovery at Storm Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay announced that drilling at its Storm Copper Project in Nunavut intersected over 68m of stratiform copper sulfide mineralization linked to a large EM conductor plate, with six other similar deeper anomalies still untested. The discovery suggests a potentially major sedimentary copper system; assays are expected next month.

title: Wildpack Beverage Inc: Wildpack Announces Supply Agreement for Aluminum Packaging with Ball Corporation
summary: Wildpack Beverage announced a long-term purchase and supply agreement with Ball Corporation for sustainable aluminum beverage packaging. The deal expands Wildpack’s printed can and warehousing services across its U.S. locations, supporting ongoing demand for aluminum packaging and potentially improving near-term sentiment for aluminium prices.

title: German Aluminum Smelter Considers Halving Output on Energy Costs
summary: A report says a German aluminum smelter is considering halving production because energy costs are too high. If implemented, lower primary aluminum output could affect regional supply expectations and market pricing in the near term, depending on how quickly alternative production or inventories can offset the reduction.

title: Imports of Unwrought Aluminium Alloy Fell MoM, while Exports Increased Nearly 50% MoM_SMM
summary: China’s unwrought aluminium alloy imports fell 13% MoM in July but rose strongly YoY, while exports surged nearly 50% MoM. Import losses were easing as aluminium prices rallied since mid-July. An opened import window in early August pushed Malaysia ADC12 quotes up, despite losses widening to 300–400 yuan/mt.

title: Speira is Considering Reducing the Production of its German Aluminium Smelter to Cope with the Soaring Energy Prices_SMM
summary: Speira is considering reducing output at its German aluminium smelter to about half to cope with soaring electricity and natural-gas costs, deciding in September. With many European smelters already curtailing, the risk of tighter regional aluminium supply is rising, which supports near-term LME aluminium price strength.

title: When Energy Crisis, Strikes and Production Cuts Plague Aluminium Market_SMM
summary: Aluminium markets are pressured by Sichuan power rationing that is pushing more Chinese smelters to cut or suspend output, while overseas producers face strikes (Hydro Sunndal, Alcoa Mosjoen) and energy-price-driven reductions. Despite some eased supply, weak downstream demand limits upside, keeping prices volatile but supported by supply tightness.

title: Global Net Zero Target Faces Copper Shortage
summary: S&P Global/IHS Markit research warns a copper supply gap will open by 2025, with demand surging from electrification and recycling/substitution not closing the shortfall. It argues higher prices are the likely market response to persistent deficits, potentially constraining the net-zero energy transition. Aluminium substitution is limited to about 1% of demand.

title: Continuous Inflow of Imported Copper Threw Cold Water on the High Spot Premiums_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai spot copper premiums for cathode versus the SHFE 2209 contract fell to around 520 yuan/mt, down from the prior day, as imported copper inflows rose. Improved east/central China smelter output after power rationing also pressured premiums, though declines were moderated by still-high levels in Guangdong.

title: Blackstone ticks more boxes for Vietnam nickel project
summary: Blackstone Minerals says it has advanced its Vietnam green nickel project, completing bench tests, commissioning pilot unit operations, and converting mixed hydroxide precipitate into battery-grade nickel sulphate. The company is also progressing nickel mine pilot work and feasibility studies, which should support improving near-term sentiment for nickel processing.

title: Aluminium falls as grim demand outlook overshadows smelter closures
summary: Aluminium prices saw a modest rise as smelter closures and temporary shutdowns—driven by high energy costs in Europe and drought/heatwave in China—tightened supply. However, Reuters notes worsening macro data, high rates and inflation are weakening demand, likely capping further upside despite falling LME inventories.

title: Fluor Announces First Copper from Anglo American's Quellaveco Mining Project in Peru
summary: Fluor announced first copper output from Anglo American’s Quellaveco mining project in Peru. The start of production suggests incremental copper supply is beginning to reach the market, which can weigh on near-term copper price expectations, though full volume ramp-up may limit the magnitude.

title: Monster struggles to shift aluminum can sourcing to US
summary: Monster says port congestion and high freight costs have pushed it to continue importing aluminum cans to avoid stockouts, despite aiming to shift more sourcing to U.S. suppliers. The company incurred higher aluminum can costs in Q1 and Q2 and expects cost-of-sales relief via more domestic can usage, while raising prices Sept. 1.

title: QC Copper and Gold aims to shore up Opemiska resource in Quebec
summary: QC Copper and Gold reported new drill assay results from the Opemiska property in Quebec, with multiple holes intersecting wide in-pit mineralization zones including grades up to about 1.49% copper. The program aims to upgrade inferred to indicated copper resources via strip-ratio reduction, with no immediate production impact.

title: Rio Tinto steps up efforts to take control of Mongolian copper mine
summary: Rio Tinto raised its offer to buy the remaining 49% stake in Turquoise Hill Resources, which controls the Oyu Tolgoi project in Mongolia. Rio already operates the mine and holds 51%. The move aims to secure full value and control over a major copper asset, potentially supporting copper supply expectations.

title: South32 (S32) posts bumper profit as coal, aluminium prices shine
summary: South32 posted record profit, saying higher realised prices—especially aluminium and metallurgical coal—boosted earnings. The company also highlighted moves to low-carbon metals, adding copper exposure via Sierra Gorda and expanding aluminium capacity through Mozal and a restarted Brazil smelter. No direct near-term price shock is announced.

title: Rio Tinto raises stakes in bid for copper target
summary: Rio Tinto increased its offer to $3.1 billion to buy out minority shareholders of copper developer Turquoise Hill Resources, after Turquoise Hill rejected an earlier $2.7 billion bid and halted talks. Rio is seeking full control, raising its stake from 50.79% to 100%, in a bid-driven corporate process.

title: Advanced alumina ship unloading delivers wide ranging benefits
summary: Trimet France upgraded its Marseille alumina import unloading system, replacing an older pneumatic method with a new electric Siwertell next-generation road-mobile unloader. The equipment reduces berth time, meets strict dust/noise/emissions rules, and is reaching about 150t/h discharge, improving operational efficiency for aluminium production.

title: Impacts of Production Reduction in European Aluminium Smelters on China's Primary Aluminium Imports_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s July primary aluminium imports jumped MoM as price spreads narrowed, but expects imports to slow in August (net ~30,000 mt) due to further price declines, bearish macro after US rate hikes, weak downstream consumption, and higher inventory. European energy costs also weigh on smelter output, affecting semis demand.

title: Overview of Current Overseas Aluminium Production Cuts and Distribution of Global Aluminium Production Capacity_SMM
summary: SMM outlines global aluminium capacity and reports production cuts: Europe (about 1.16m mt) and North America (about 0.304m mt) hit by high energy costs and strikes, while Sichuan sees near-total smelter suspensions (~1.0m mt). Overall supply is tighter, potentially lifting aluminium prices short term.

title: Clean Air Metals Reports Drill Results including 13m grading 5.06g/t Platinum, 5.14g/t Palladium, 1.27% Copper and 0.71% Nickel in Hole CLM22-07; Advances Prefeasibility Study at Thunder Bay North
summary: Clean Air Metals reported 2022 drill assay results from the Thunder Bay North Current deposit, including copper grades up to ~0.98% and nickel up to ~0.56%, and it is advancing a prefeasibility study with metallurgical testing and resource updates. The news is exploration-focused with no immediate production impact, limiting near-term price effects.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Commences Trading on the OTCQX Under the Symbol CPPKF
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. announces that its shares began trading on the OTCQX in the U.S. under symbol CPPKF, improving visibility and liquidity for U.S. investors. The company remains listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange and continues developing its U.S.-based copper projects.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay Announces Additional Near Surface Copper Mineralization and Expansion of High Grade 2750N Zone at Storm Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay announced further near-surface copper mineralization from three diamond drill holes at the Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, expanding the high-grade 2750N zone and leaving mineralization open along strike and at depth. Assays are pending, and no immediate supply or production changes were stated.

title: Aranjin Resources Ltd: Aranjin Announces the Victory Copper Nickel Discovery
summary: Aranjin Resources announced follow-up auger drilling at its Baavhai Uul copper project in Mongolia, reporting extensive geochemical anomalies at the “Victory” copper-nickel discovery, including up to 1,252 ppm copper and 494 ppm nickel. The anomaly remains open and further drilling is planned to outline extensions.

title: Aranjin Resources Ltd: Aranjin Announces the Victory Copper Nickel Discovery
summary: Aranjin Resources announced results from initial follow-up auger geochemical drilling at its Baavhai Uul Copper Project in Mongolia, highlighting a large copper-nickel discovery (“Victory”) under shallow alluvial cover. Reported results include up to 1,252 ppm copper and 494 ppm nickel, with the anomaly remaining open for further drilling.

title: American West Metals Limited Announces Results for Diamond Drill Holes Completed at the Storm Copper Project
summary: American West Metals reported further visual results from diamond drilling at its Storm Copper Project on Nunavut’s Somerset Island. Holes ST22-07 and ST22-08 intersected thick intervals of massive chalcocite-dominant copper sulphides, and ST22-09 tested an EM anomaly. The copper mineralization remains open along strike and at depth.

title: China's energy shortage could boost copper and aluminium demand - ANZ
summary: Reuters (Aug 25) cites ANZ analysts saying China’s energy shortage could accelerate grid and renewable projects, lifting demand for copper used in solar/wind and power cabling. It also expects aluminium benefits from ultra-high-voltage line and electrical cable needs. The report forecasts deficits that could pressure prices higher.

title: China's energy shortage could boost copper and aluminium demand - ANZ
summary: ANZ says China’s energy shortage and power constraints may accelerate grid and renewable projects, increasing demand for copper used in solar, wind and cabling. The report also expects higher aluminium demand from ultra-high-voltage transmission lines and electrical cables, widening deficits and supporting higher prices.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Restart Plan and Significant Proposed Financing Package
summary: Nevada Copper said it has agreed non-binding terms for up to US$93 million of liquidity to restart and ramp up its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine. The plan includes de-bottlenecking and mill restart timing, targeting higher hoisting rates in 2023, improving expected copper output despite current production pause.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Restart Plan and Significant Proposed Financing Package
summary: Nevada Copper announced non-binding terms for up to $93 million in liquidity to restart and ramp up its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine. The funding package supports de-bottlenecking and mill restart planning, with working capital deferrals until copper deliveries resume. Overall, it reduces restart risk and supports copper supply expectations.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Restart Plan and Significant
summary: Nevada Copper agreed non-binding terms for up to US$93 million to fund and de-risk the restart and ramp-up of its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine. The plan includes de-bottlenecking, capital works, and a scheduled mill restart, targeting higher underground production rates from 2023 onward.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Restart Plan And Significant Propose...
summary: Nevada Copper announced non-binding financing of up to $93m to restart and ramp up its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine in Nevada. The liquidity package and creditor deferrals are intended to de-bottleneck operations and enable mill restart, with copper production targeted to rise through 2023 as deliveries resume.

title: Market Concerns over Copper Supply Eased amid Subsiding Impact of Power Rationing and Increased Customs Clearance _SMM
summary: SMM reports that as summer heat cools, copper smelters in eastern and central China are resuming output after earlier power-rationing cuts. This is complemented by higher customs clearance and increased imported copper inflows, easing spot-market worries about tightening supply.

title: Triple Flag Reaches Terms with Nevada Copper to Participate in Proposed Financing Package for Restart Plan at Pumpkin Hollow
summary: Triple Flag agreed to provide up to US$30 million in financing to support Nevada Copper’s restart plan for the Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine. The liquidity is intended to fund and ramp up production, improving short-term supply expectations, though closing depends on definitive documentation and regulatory approvals.

title: Peruvian Ministry of Economy and Finance: Copper Prices to Fall to $3.40/lb in 2023_SMM
summary: Peru’s Ministry of Economy and Finance predicted copper prices could fall to $3.40/lb in 2023 from $3.90/lb this year. Peru is a major copper producer and mining taxes depend heavily on copper output. Quellaveco’s planned ramp is cited as an offset, but the outlook remains pessimistic.

title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zones Dipped 18,900 mt from Last Friday_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s domestic bonded copper inventories fell 18,900 mt to 175,100 mt as of Aug 26, with nine straight weeks of declines. The drop is linked to shipments from warehouses as the import window opened, limited Guangdong port arrivals, tighter social inventories, and higher spot premiums drawing more metal into bonded zones.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Added 9,800 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventories across major Chinese markets reached 68,300 mt as of Aug 26, up 9,800 mt from Monday. While Guangdong fell, Shanghai rose sharply due to greater imported arrivals. Total inventories remain far below last year, but SMM expects weekly inventories to keep rising as power rationing eases and demand may weaken.

title: Copper Anode Supply Remained Tight despite Rising Imports in Jul_SMM
summary: China imported 96,000 mt of copper anode in July, up MoM, but spot blister copper transactions remain scarce and logistics from Africa (including Zambia) is still unsmooth. African supply is tight due to maintenance and incidents (LCS, CCS boiler leakage). Lower scrap availability also limits blister output as smelter demand rises.

title: Copper scales 2-week peak on China demand optimism, low stocks
summary: London copper rose to a two-week high as China demand optimism grew after new stimulus measures and infrastructure plans. Prices also found support from tight supply and very low inventories. US and Germany data improved broader demand sentiment. The LME three-month contract and SHFE copper futures ended higher.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Royalty Options the Mesa Well Copper Project in Arizona to Intrepid Metals
summary: EMX Royalty announced an agreement for its Mesa Well porphyry copper project in Arizona, where Intrepid will fund earn-in payments and exploration. EMX will retain a 2% NSR and receive advance and milestone royalty payments. The update supports future copper optionality but offers no near-term market supply shock.

title: Nevada Copper unveils restart and US$93M financing plan for Pumpkin Hollow
summary: Nevada Copper plans to restart and ramp up its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine in Nevada, citing de-bottlenecking and completion of critical work. The company also agreed non-binding terms for up to US$93 million in financing to support the restart, affecting expectations around future copper supply rather than immediate output.

title: Traverse City's Right Brain Brewery Reacts to Rising Aluminum Costs
summary: Right Brain Brewery says rising aluminum costs have made sourcing local beer cans difficult, with prices up about two cents per can. It also notes CO-2 shortages and supply chain strain that have squeezed smaller breweries, forcing some can sourcing to Asia when local supply is unavailable.

title: Engineer Who Freed Chilean Miners Takes Helm At Top Copper F...
summary: Andre Sougarret will replace Octavio Araneda as CEO of Chile’s state-owned Codelco, the world’s top copper producer. The leadership transition comes as the company faces operational setbacks, logistical disruptions, and ballooning costs, while it continues large spending to upgrade aging deposits.

title: The Fiji Times » Usamate positive on bauxite export
summary: Fiji’s mineral minister says bauxite exports are expected to resume. Fiji has not exported for a few years as the company waited for favourable world prices and because Indonesia had slowed bauxite exports to China. With Indonesia resuming, Fiji’s small market faces renewed demand, supporting bauxite/alumina availability.

title: Local Opinion: Copper World is coming for beloved Santa Rita Mountains
summary: An opinion piece argues that Hudbay’s “Copper World” copper mining project in Arizona should be halted, citing alleged Clean Water Act violations and environmental opposition. It outlines planned pits and processing facilities and ongoing court and regulator disputes, but does not quantify near-term production changes affecting copper prices directly.

title: Chinese copper giant seeks help with liquidity issues
summary: Chinese commodities trader Maike Metals International, led by founder He Jinbi, is seeking government and lender support after liquidity problems. The cash crunch led to delays in payments for imported copper, potentially disrupting short-term copper trade flows and adding bearish pressure to copper demand expectations.

title: Brewers across the country are dealing with an aluminum can shortage
summary: Brewers in the U.S. say they face an aluminum can shortage that began as demand rose during the 2020 shift toward at-home drinking, combined with delivery delays. Domestic aluminum demand is up over 5% in the first quarter, prices stay high, and availability is only slowly improving.

title: Short-Term Copper Prices may Fluctuate with some Upward Potential Supported by the f Fundamentals _SMM
summary: SMM expects near-term copper prices to fluctuate but with upward potential. It cites strong support from low home and overseas inventories, a higher share of cancelled LME copper warrants, and expanding backwardation. It also expects smelter restarts to ease extreme supply pressure while consumption from infrastructure and new energy remains solid.

title: Exports of Domestic Aluminium Extrusions Continued to Rise MoM in July, with Countries in Southeast Asia the Major Destinations_SMM
summary: China’s aluminium extrusion exports rose 12.8% month-on-month in July to 93,300 mt, driven by lower domestic aluminium prices improving import affordability in Southeast Asia and Africa. Overseas processing faced supply constraints and COVID-related restrictions, supporting demand. August prices’ rally may slightly reduce exports. Impact on aluminium price appears limited and mostly offsetting.

title: Trading Activities in Alumina Market Declined amid Output Cuts by Aluminium Smelters _SMM
summary: SMM reports weaker trading in the alumina market, with domestic prices edging down. Power shortages in Sichuan nearly shut aluminium smelters (about 1 million mt capacity), cutting alumina demand. Pandemic-related transport restrictions and potential output curbs add uncertainty, but market pessimism keeps prices under pressure.

title: Sohar Aluminium and GE Sign 10 Year Power Services Contract in Sultanate of Oman
summary: Sohar Aluminium in Oman signed a 10-year power services contract with GE to maintain and supply parts for gas turbines and generators that provide electricity to its aluminium smelter. The deal aims to improve reliability, turbine availability, cost efficiency, and reduce operational risks, supporting sustained output over the decade.

title: Domestic and Overseas Supply Disruptions to Sustain the Short-Term Aluminium Price Rise _SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices have risen over the week amid energy-driven production cuts. In China, Sichuan shutdowns and Chongqing power rationing reduce operating capacity, while European smelters plan output reductions due to the energy crisis. Downstream rates weaken but supply constraints still support near-term aluminium gains.

title: Aluminium Costs to Remain High amid High Energy Prices_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that rising coal prices increased thermal power costs, while grid-power aluminium smelters face stable tariffs settled monthly. Smelter real-time costs rose week-on-week, and profits expanded. With peak power demand and declining thermal coal supply, electricity prices are unlikely to fall soon, keeping aluminium smelting costs high.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Added 5,000 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM says Chinese copper inventories rose 5,000 mt over the weekend to 73,300 mt, with gains across multiple regions and stronger supply as power rationing eases, boosting domestic cathode availability. At the same time, consumption may soften due to high premiums and copper prices plus month-end effects, supporting further inventory growth this week.

title: Cannindah Resources Limited  High Grade Copper Hits in Hole 12
summary: Cannindah Resources reported high-grade copper intercepts from drilling at the Mt Cannindah copper-gold-silver project in Queensland, including multi-meter zones around 1.0–1.3% Cu and some higher-grade intervals above 3–4% Cu. The company says this extends the copper breccia further north-east and deeper.

title: Cannindah Resources Ltd (ASX:CAE) High Grade Copper Hits In...
summary: Cannindah Resources announced assay results from drilling at its Mt Cannindah copper-gold-silver project, including multiple high-grade copper intercepts (e.g., 126m at ~1.01% Cu and zones up to ~1.53% Cu, plus strong CuEq). The company says the results extend high-grade breccia deeper and further north-east.

title: Social Inventory of Nickel Plates Decreased only Slightly last Week due to the Slack Transactions_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s pure nickel social inventory fell 295 mt to 7,397 mt last week, with nickel plate inventory down to 6,447 mt. Nickel briquettes were flat. Despite futures direction uncertainty, rigid buying for high-temperature alloys supported prices, and bonded-zone inventory fell on salt-plant purchases.

title: TNM Drill Down: Top Ten best nickel drill results year to date
summary: The article discusses the increasing urgency to discover large, economic nickel deposits as clean-energy technologies rely on nickel-based batteries and nickel-containing steel. It features top nickel drilling results year to date, implying improved prospects for future supply, which can buoy nickel market sentiment in the near term.

title: American Copper Development Corporation (Formerly Known as Cirrus Gold Corp.): American Copper Development Corporation to Resume Trading Following Acquisition of Lordsburg Property
summary: American Copper Development Corporation says its shares will resume trading after completing the acquisition of the Lordsburg Property in New Mexico. The company describes ongoing geophysical programs and planned drilling aimed at finding a major copper discovery in porphyry country. The update is exploratory and does not affect near-term copper supply or demand directly.

title: Aluminium canning demand outlook positive amid high energy cost concerns
summary: Hulamin says aluminium canning demand is positive as consumers and brands shift from energy- and water-intensive glass/plastic packaging. It expects firm demand for aluminium can material despite capacity additions. The company also benefited from higher aluminium prices and a weaker rand, supporting near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: Domestic A00 Aluminium Prices Stopped Rising and Throughput pf Aluminium Scrap at Linyi Non-Ferrous Metal City Increased Significantly_SMM
summary: SMM says aluminium scrap throughput at Linyi Huadong rose sharply to about 15,300 mt in Aug 22-28. Domestic A00 aluminium prices increased to 18,860 yuan/mt and added another 100 yuan to 18,960. Scrap recyclers sold more amid weak momentum, but downstream demand—especially for tense scrap—remains strong.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices Fell while Spot Premiums Stabilised_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: On Aug 30, SHFE nickel prices fell, and nickel spot premiums largely steadied after futures weakness, with Jinchuan premiums averaging higher but still reflecting the day’s softer price tone. Nickel briquette prices dropped, attributed to narrowed premiums and weak trading versus intermediate products and nickel plate.

title: A new study presents cuprous oxide-based marine antifouling coatings with controlled release of copper ion mediated by amphiphilic copolymers.
summary: The study develops Cu2O-containing marine antifouling coatings that use amphiphilic diblock copolymers to control and prolong copper-ion release in seawater. It reports strong antifouling performance in marine field tests and comparable results to commercial self-polishing coatings. Overall, it suggests niche copper use but no immediate market impact.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Announces Private Placement
summary: Granite Creek Copper announced a non-brokered private placement to raise up to $640,000 for exploration and development. Funds target its Carmacks copper-gold-silver project and a newly acquired Star copper-nickel-PGE project in Canada. The company positions these projects for future copper output, but it doesn’t indicate immediate production changes.

title: Aluminium prices set to rebound as global deficit looms: Report
summary: CRISIL Research says aluminium prices have likely bottomed and are set to rise as a global deficit looms. It attributes the rebound to limited additions to smelter capacity and a pickup in demand, which should tighten supply and support higher aluminium prices over the coming weeks.

title: Construction begins on new aluminum plant – WLKM Radio 95.9 FM
summary: Construction is underway for a new Hydro Aluminum plant in Cassopolis. The facility will use raw aluminum and recycled scrap to produce aluminum bars, targeting demand including the automotive sector. Hydro says the project will create about 100 jobs and expects operations to start in fall 2023, implying limited immediate pricing impact.

title: Aluminium billet premiums remain under pressure globally
summary: Fastmarkets reports that aluminium extrusion billet premiums in the US and Europe declined as demand weakened and supply stayed ample. Underlying primary aluminium premiums eased too, while producers faced higher energy costs that compressed margins. Thin spot activity and cautious buying further pressured premiums across multiple regions.

title: Key talking points ahead of Fastmarkets' International Aluminium Conference
summary: Fastmarkets’ preview highlights ongoing European aluminium smelter cuts from high energy costs and Ukraine-related disruption, while demand remains uncertain and consumers are not buying against full order books. Aluminium premiums have fallen from record highs, and LME stocks are low, with macro recession fears adding bearish sentiment toward near-term prices.

title: Proactive news headlines including Facebook, Nextleaf Solutions, Valeo Pharma, Naturally Splendid Enterprises, Arrow Exploration and Québec Nickel
summary: Proactive’s news roundup cites Québec Nickel reporting impressive assay results from step-out drilling at its Ducros project. Such positive exploration updates can lift sentiment around future nickel resource potential, supporting modest near-term bullish expectations for nickel prices. Other items mention zinc concentrates, but zinc is not tracked here.

title: Copper Scrap Transactions Pick up Substantially with Copper Prices Stabilising above 63,000 yuan/mt_SMM
summary: SMM reports East China copper scrap throughput rose 29% WoW to about 22,000 mt as copper prices stabilized above 63,000 yuan/mt. The cathode vs scrap spread widened, improving scrap economics and raising secondary rod operating rates to 43.51%. Demand may cool slightly, but improving logistics should support supply.

title: Sandfire goes ahead with copper mine expansion in Botswana
summary: Sandfire Resources plans to invest $71.9m to expand the Motheo copper mine in Botswana, following completion of a feasibility study for the A4 deposit and processing plant upgrades. Copper output is expected to grow toward a 5.2 Mtpa hub. Botswana can take up to a 15% interest.

title: Sandfire announces Motheo Copper Project expansion DFS
summary: Sandfire says it has completed a definitive feasibility study to expand its Motheo copper mine in Botswana from 3.2 mtpa to 5.2 mtpa, including development of the A4 deposit and a larger processing plant. Construction is scheduled to start March quarter FY23 with higher throughput from FY24, subject to approvals.

title: Officials asking for public's help to find copper thieves tampering with Louisville highway lights
summary: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet officials say copper thieves have damaged thousands of Louisville highway light poles, stealing roughly 66,000 feet of copper wire (about $45,000) across Interstates 64, 65 and 264. Crews and police are responding to deter theft, but the local volume is unlikely to move copper prices meaningfully.

title: Rio Tinto Plans Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean, Quebec, Aluminum Recycling Plant
summary: Rio Tinto plans a new aluminum recycling plant in Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean, Quebec, aiming to remelt locally sourced post-consumer aluminum scrap into billets at the Arvida smelter. The facility is expected to start in Q2 2024 with 30,000 tons/year capacity, boosting low-carbon recycled supply.

title: Codelco's Copper Output Likely to Fall Further in 2023_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: El Mercurio reported that Codelco’s output outlook will likely deteriorate further next year because of project delays and lower ore grades at Chuquicamata. Codelco cut its 2022 production estimate to around 1.5 million mt from 1.61 million mt, citing difficulties implementing investment projects.

title: Chile's Copper Production Fell 8.6% Year-on-Year in July_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chile’s National Statistics Institute reported that copper production fell 8.6% year-on-year in July to 430,028 metric tons. As Chile is the world’s largest copper producer, reduced output can signal tighter copper supply expectations, typically exerting downward pressure on nearby copper price sentiment.

title: An Alumina Refinery in Shandong Has Shut down One 900,000 mt/Year Alumina Production Line Following An Accident _SMM
summary: SMM reports a Shandong alumina refinery shut one 900,000 mt/year alumina line after an accident, removing an estimated 70,000–75,000 mt of alumina output. Production is expected to resume mid-to-late September. The temporary alumina supply tightening is likely supportive for aluminium prices over the next several weeks.

title: Pure Nickel Demand Recovered Slightly with Spot Premiums Trending Toward Different Directions_SMM
summary: SMM reports mixed spot pure nickel premiums in China: Jinchuan premiums rebound on rigid demand, while NORNICKEL premiums stay pressured due to weak demand. For NPI, oversupply and high inventories with ongoing Indonesia inflows cap prices. Transactions in stainless/alloys are mostly muted, leading SMM to expect nickel to fall further.

title: Copper Extends Worst Losing Streak Since 2008 on Growth Fears
summary: Copper is reportedly extending its worst losing streak since 2008, with prices pressured by renewed growth fears. The news framing points to deteriorating near-term demand expectations for industrial metals, supporting the view that copper faces continued downside pressure in the immediate trading window.

title: Rio Tinto wins over copper target Turquoise Hill
summary: Rio Tinto won approval for its $3.3 billion takeover of Turquoise Hill Resources, clearing the way to partner with Mongolia’s government on developing the Oyu Tolgoi copper mine. The deal supports ambitions for the mine to become one of the world’s top copper producers by 2030, boosting sentiment toward copper.

title: SMM Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventory as of September 1_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s social aluminium ingot inventories rose to 683,000 mt (+4,000 mt WoW) but remain lower vs a year ago, led by gains in Wuxi and transfers from Foshan. Billet inventories slightly fell (-500 mt WoW). Demand is weak, and Sichuan smelter output remains constrained, limiting further accumulation.

title: Sandfire's additional investment in Botswana's Motheo copper mine will boost output – The North Africa Post
summary: Sandfire plans to spend an additional $71.9 million to expand its under-construction Motheo copper mine in Botswana, adding a new processing plant and open pit mine. Output is expected to ramp up after environmental and mining approvals, raising long-run copper supply expectations in the Kalahari Copper Belt.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay Announces 41 Metres of 4.18% Copper Intersected at Storm Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay announced initial assay results from drilling at its Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, highlighting 41 metres at 4.18% copper and narrower intervals exceeding 20% Cu, with mineralization remaining open for expansion. Further assays and planned metallurgical work are expected over coming days and weeks.

title: Investigation Of Potential Copper Porphyry Systems Now Under...
summary: First Tellurium Corp. says work is underway to investigate potential copper porphyry targets at its Deer Horn property in west-central British Columbia, following earlier copper showings and a prior PEA suggesting a hidden porphyry system. The company aims to define drill targets for future exploration.

title: Macdonald Intersects 0.41% Copper Equivalent (Cueq) Over 90....
summary: MacDonald Mines reported Phase 1 drill results at its SPJ property, including a 0.41% CuEq (with copper values and associated gold/silver) over 90.44m at the Alwyn trend and cobalt anomalies. While it highlights potential for broader polymetallic systems including nickel, no nickel/aluminium results are given.

title: Aluminum Buyer Novelis Excludes Russian Metal in Key Supply Deal
summary: Novelis has excluded Russian metal from a key supply deal, signaling reduced availability of Russian-origin aluminum material for customers. This kind of sourcing shift can tighten regional supply in the near term and support expectations of firmer aluminum prices over coming days to weeks.

title: SMM Analysis of the Impact of Power Shortages in Yunnan on Chinese Aluminum Supply_SMM
summary: SMM says Yunnan’s aluminium smelters are mostly operating normally, but hydropower shortages and lower reservoir water raise concerns of power rationing and output curtailment after the dry season. Yunnan’s growing smelter capacity could be cut if 20–30% of capacity is curtailed, easing domestic supply pressure.

title: As Investment in Power Supply Speeds Up, Average Operating Rate of Copper Wire and Cable Producers in September Expected to Rise_SMM
summary: SMM reports copper wire and cable producers’ operating rate is expected to rise in September as power rationing eases and government investment in power supply and non-fossil energy (especially PV) increases. Pandemic-related disruption and weak real estate/state grid demand limit the upside, but copper-linked production should improve.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Added 1,700 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says Chinese copper inventories across major markets totaled 75,000 mt, up 1,700 mt from Monday, with increases in most regions except Shanghai. Shanghai fell due to fewer imported arrivals, while Guangdong rose on higher imported and domestic inflows. Consumption is expected to improve next week as prices decline, but near-term inventories are supportive.

title: Copper Prices Fell amid Resonating Macro and Fundamentals Fronts with Firm Rate Hike Stance in US and Europe_SMM
summary: Copper prices fell as hawkish ECB and Fed messaging supported higher interest rates, pushing up bond yields and the US dollar and pressuring USD-priced commodities. Fundamentals also weakened: power-restricted smelters resumed production and cathode supply rose, while downstream demand/order flow stayed sluggish despite softer supply conditions.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports up 300,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Chinese nickel ore port inventories rose 300,000 wmt week-on-week to 6.53 million wmt (51,300 mt Ni content). Inventories at seven major ports increased too. With weak supply-demand, sluggish transactions, slack stainless steel and NPI output, and pressured NPI prices, the buildup is seen as bearish for nickel despite limited further gains expected.

title: Los Andes Copper Ltd.: Los Andes Copper Announces Closing of Further US$ 5 million Investment by Queen's Road Capital
summary: Los Andes Copper announces closing an additional US$5 million convertible debenture investment by Queen’s Road Capital. Proceeds will fund expansion drilling at the Vizcachitas copper project in Chile and related studies. Management says drilling will commence soon, supporting progress toward potential future copper production.

title: Copper touches one-month low on China lockdowns, recession fears
summary: Copper prices touched a one-month low earlier amid China’s extended COVID restrictions in Shenzhen and a lockdown in Chengdu, raising recession and demand concerns; potential smelter shutdowns could reduce supply. Risk sentiment improved after U.S. jobs data eased Fed hike fears. Aluminium support came from Aldel mothballing capacity due to energy costs.

title: Protesters demand reopening of Sterlite Copper plant
summary: Pro-Sterlite protesters in Tamil Nadu demand the immediate reopening of Vedanta’s Thoothukudi copper smelting plant, arguing the closure caused major livelihood losses and a sharp drop in India’s refined copper exports, making it a net importer. The article implies reopening would ease copper supply constraints and support prices.

title: Copper Price Decline: Good Sign for Low Inflation, Bad Omen for Economy
summary: Fairlead Strategies’ Katie Stockton expects copper to extend its decline, projecting another ~11% drop toward $3.14 per pound, citing loss of momentum and technical support levels. The fall is framed as easing inflation but signaling weaker economic activity, with historical recession links to sharp copper drops.

title: Crescat, Delphi to Fund Additional Drilling at Pacific Ridge's Kliyul Copper-Gold Project
summary: Crescat and Delphi will fund additional drilling at Pacific Ridge’s Kliyul copper-gold project. The announcement supports exploration progress and could improve long-term resource expectations for copper, but drilling activity usually has limited immediate effect on supply, inventories, or prompt pricing within the next few weeks.

title: Nickel Prices Fell amid the Supply Surplus of Primary Nickel_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Nickel prices fell as macro sentiment worsened on hawkish Fed expectations and overseas primary nickel weakened. Fundamentals pointed to supply surplus: NPI plant inventories rose, Indonesia NPI inflows increased, and NPI prices were unlikely to rise. Demand showed only modest improvement, leaving net bearish pressure on nickel.

title: Copper export from Udokan to start in 2023, mainly to China
summary: Udokan Copper plans to begin copper product exports in 2023, mainly to China. The company says volumes are small and Far Eastern port throughput should be sufficient, citing Ministry of Transport projects to expand port capacity. The note also highlights increased 2022 transport loads from Russia’s shift to Asian exports.

title: Alumina Output Cuts Are Accompanied by Production Resumptions, Demand at Risks of Falling_SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices were slightly lower week-on-week amid mixed supply moves: some Chongqing and other plants resumed after power restoration, while others cut output due to accidents, ongoing bauxite shortages, or delayed availability. Aluminium smelters are restarting in Sichuan, but Yunnan hydropower concerns may curb output and raise risks for alumina demand.

title: Aluminium Prices Likely to Be Volatile amid Weak Fundamentals and Bearish Macro Environment _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME aluminium prices fell on the week amid hawkish rate expectations and stronger USD, plus weak macro demand signals. While Sichuan power is restored, Yunnan reservoir declines may trigger smelter load cuts and supply uncertainty. Overall, aluminium is expected to remain volatile with support and downside risks balancing.

title: Aluminium Ingot Social Inventory Dropped Slightly_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Shanghai (SMM) said China’s aluminium ingot social inventories in eight major markets fell to 681,000 mt on Sep 5, down slightly week-on-week and more than last year. Regional moves were small. Despite Sichuan smelter shutdowns in August, inventory didn’t drop sharply, but downstream purchases improved after price declines, supporting demand.

title: Goldman Sachs Expects Copper Prices to Rise in H1 2023_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that Goldman Sachs expects copper prices to rise from about $7,200/mt in the second half of 2022 to $8,000/mt in the first half of 2023. The update reflects bullish market expectations for copper, which may support near-term sentiment and price pressure in coming weeks.

title: NICIC discovers 1B tons of additional copper assets
summary: NICIC’s managing director says drilling at Iran’s Sungun copper mine found about one billion tons of additional copper assets, lifting in-place reserves from roughly four billion to over five billion tons. The company says it will begin development actions, valuing the reserves at more than $50 billion.

title: Some Aluminium Capacity in Europe May Be Gone Forever amid Ongoing Energy Crisis_SMM
summary: European aluminium producers face potential smelter shutdowns as an energy crisis—linked to Gazprom supply cut-offs and soaring electricity costs—makes production uneconomic. Norsk Hydro’s Slovak plant is at risk, with European output at the lowest since the 1970s and analysts expecting large capacity closures, some permanent.

title: Downstream Buyers Reluctant to Purchase Aluminium Scrap, and Throughput of Aluminium Scrap in Linyi Non-Ferrous Metal City Began to Decrease _SMM
summary: SMM reports weaker downstream appetite for aluminium scrap in Linyi, with aluminium scrap throughput falling sharply week-on-week due to reluctance to buy after September stocking. Aluminium scrap prices and overall aluminium prices dropped last week, reflecting bearish sentiment and inventory dynamics.

title: Culpeo Minerals confirms shallow, high-grade potential of Lana Corina copper system
summary: Culpeo Minerals reports maiden drilling at its Lana Corina project in Chile returned shallow, high-grade copper intercepts (up to 4.01% Cu over 2m) plus molybdenum. Management says the grades support an open-pittable resource potential and follow a recent large-scale copper discovery, with multiple drill targets designated.

title: Peru's July copper output falls 6.6% after mines underperform
summary: Peru’s July copper output fell 6.6% year over year to 195,234 tonnes, after Antamina and Southern Copper underperformed. With Peru supplying about 60% of its shipment exports through mining, renewed protests and potential supply risks following the Las Bambas truce raise bearish near-term expectations for copper.

title: Power Rationing in Yunnan Shall Stay on the Radar of Aluminium Market Players_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium fundamentals turning supportive: potential power rationing in Yunnan could reduce aluminium output and support SHFE prices. It also notes weaker bauxite/alumina supply stability concerns, overseas producer capacity cuts (Alcoa, Aldel), slightly falling aluminium inventories, and wider spot discounts despite thin transactions.

title: Spot Copper Premiums Rose amid Narrowing SHFE Contract Spread and Failed Copper Import Expectations_SMM
summary: SMM reports spot copper cathode premiums rising to 380-440 yuan/mt over SHFE 2209, up 10 yuan/mt, as SHFE 2209/2210 spreads narrowed. Failed customs clearance for imported copper and low transaction sources supported higher premiums, though some traders were cautious due to still-expected imports and SHFE 2209 delivery.

title: Copper prices increase on weaker dollar, China stimulus
summary: Copper futures rose on a weaker dollar and expectations that China will accelerate infrastructure spending. Reuters cites the shift as the main driver for improved metals demand. LME cash/three-month and Shanghai copper gained, alongside price increases in aluminium and nickel, reflecting broad bullish sentiment across industrial metals.

title: Proactive news headlines including Kaiser Reef, Chalice Mining, New Century Resources and Poseidon Nickel
summary: Proactive lists several company headlines, including Chalice’s work on a polymetallic nickel-copper deposit extension, Poseidon’s partnership while refocusing on restarting its Black Swan nickel project, and Caspin’s “significant” nickel-copper-PGE drilling results. These updates are sentiment-supportive for nickel and co-product copper near term.

title: Mundoro Capital Inc.: Mundoro And JOGMEC Announce New Copper Project from the Generative Alliance
summary: Mundoro Capital and JOGMEC announced the start of an exploration program on the newly approved JOGMEC-Mundoro copper project in western Bulgaria, following government approval and an earn-in/option structure. The release focuses on geology and historical production but does not signal any near-term production or supply impact.

title: Australian Foreign Investment Review Board Approves Metals Acquisition Corp's Acquisition of the CSA Copper Mine
summary: Australia’s Foreign Investment Review Board has approved Metals Acquisition Corp’s acquisition of the CSA copper mine. The decision clears a key regulatory hurdle for the ownership transfer of a copper-producing asset, which can reduce disruption risk and provide mild near-term support for copper supply expectations.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Phase 2 Results: Continued High-Grade Mineralization Including 8.5 Metres Grading 2.14% Ni from the W4 Extension, Now Applying for Mining Lease
summary: EV Nickel reports final assays from Phase 2 drilling on the W4 Extension at its Shaw Dome nickel project, including 20.6m at 1.23% Ni and 8.5m at 2.14% Ni, plus additional high-grade intercepts. The company is applying for a mining lease and planning further drilling.

title: PNG Copper Inc: Announcement of Assay Results
