summary: PNG Copper Inc. announced assay results from the first three drillholes at its Doriri nickel–palladium–platinum prospect in Papua New Guinea. Results intersected significant nickel grades and continued mineralisation, prompting plans to accelerate drilling and extend along strike. Copper and aluminium are not addressed in the release.

title: McEwen Copper Options Elder Creek Project to Rio Tinto
summary: McEwen Copper said it entered a binding term sheet with Rio Tinto’s KEX for an option to earn a 60% interest in the Elder Creek porphyry copper project in Nevada by spending $18 million over up to seven years. Afterward, a 60:40 joint venture would form. No near-term production timeline was given.

title: Electric Royalties Ltd.: Electric Royalties Closes Zonia Copper Royalty Acquisition
summary: Electric Royalties closed its acquisition of a 0.5% gross revenue royalty on the Zonia copper oxide project in Arizona, with options to acquire additional royalty interests. The transaction involves cash and shares and is tied to future prefeasibility work. It is a project-funding event, not an immediate supply shift.

title: World Copper Ltd.: World Copper Announces Closing of Zonia Project Royalty Sale
summary: World Copper announced the closing of a royalty sale for its Zonia copper oxide project, receiving cash and equity and allowing Electric Royalties options to increase the royalty and acquire similar rights on Zonia Norte. The release reiterates that project economics are sensitive to copper prices and plans a PEA update.

title: Mundoro And JOGMEC Announce New Copper Project From The Gene...
summary: Mundoro Capital and JOGMEC announced an exploration program for the JOGMEC-Mundoro copper project in western Bulgaria, following government approval and an earn-in agreement. The project targets sediment-hosted stratiform copper(-silver) mineralization with historical production and many copper-lead-zinc occurrences, but no near-term production changes are stated.

title: Kaiser Aluminum Lifts Force Majeure At Warrick Rolling Mill
summary: Kaiser Aluminum lifted force majeure at its Warrick rolling mill after magnesium shortages constrained production of certain aluminum packaging products in 2022. Its largest supplier, US Magnesium, stopped deliveries in June 2022, but Kaiser secured qualified magnesium from alternative sources and aims to return to full production.

title: BHP And Riverside Resources Extend Sonora Mexico Exploration with Budget of US$1,600,000 in Funding Focused on Four Copper Properties and Llano De Nogal
summary: BHP and Riverside extend their exploration funding agreement for a fourth year, directing about US$1.6M toward five copper properties in Sonora, Mexico. The program emphasizes derisking and preparation for future drilling and drill decisions, with additional potential budgets in later operational phases if projects advance.

title: Exclusive-EU, U.S. Step Up Russian Aluminium, Nickel Imports Since Ukraine War
summary: EU and U.S. imports of Russian aluminium and nickel rose sharply in March–June, despite wartime logistical issues and sanctions. Trade data show aluminium and nickel shipments increasing up to ~70%, with supply still reaching ports. Continued Russian export availability likely reduces supply-risk premiums and pressure for higher prices.

title: Exclusive-EU, U.S. Step Up Russian Aluminium, Nickel Imports Since Ukraine War
summary: Reuters data show EU and U.S. boosted Russian aluminium and nickel purchases by up to ~70% in March–June despite logistical issues and sanctions threats. Ports and traders report continued deliveries because metals are largely spared. The near-term supply outlook improves, weighing on expectations for aluminium and nickel prices.

title: Europe's Top Aluminum Plant Will Cut Output 22% on Energy Costs
summary: Europe’s top aluminum plant plans to cut output 22% because energy costs make production uneconomic. The supply reduction is expected to tighten aluminium availability in the near term, supporting aluminium prices over coming days to weeks as buyers anticipate less production and potential restocking.

title: Exclusive-EU, U.S. step up Russian aluminium, nickel imports since Ukraine war
summary: EU and U.S. boosted purchases of Russian aluminium and nickel since Russia’s invasion, with imports rising as much as 70% in March–June versus a year earlier. Russian shipments continued despite war-related logistics issues and broad sanctions, suggesting supply pressures have eased, weighing on price expectations.

title: Exclusive-EU, U.S. step up Russian aluminium, nickel imports since Ukraine war
summary: EU and U.S. have increased purchases of Russian aluminium and nickel since the Ukraine war despite sanctions and logistics concerns. Reuters trade data show EU/U.S. Russian aluminium and nickel imports rising as much as 70% in March–June. Analysts attribute steady flows to workable deals mainly driven by price.

title: Europe's Top Aluminum Plant Will Cut Output 22% on Energy Costs
summary: Europe’s top aluminum plant plans to reduce production by 22% because higher energy costs make operating uneconomic. The output cut should lessen near-term aluminum supply in the region, tightening availability and providing upward support to aluminum prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Taseko Mines Limited (TGB) Stock Struggled as Copper Prices Fell From Recent Highs
summary: The piece says shares of Taseko Mines, a copper miner, were weak because copper prices retreated from prior highs. It also notes commodities spiked earlier on supply concerns tied to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, implying that easing concerns and/or supply expectations contributed to softer copper.

title: Dunkerque, Largest Aluminium Smelter in Europe, Plans to Cut Output 22%_SMM
summary: Aluminium Dunkerque Industries France, Europe’s largest aluminium smelter, plans to cut output by 22% as high electricity prices threaten profitability. The shutdown begins next Monday and should finish before October 1, amid broader European smelter curtailments and uncertain restart timing without losses.

title: China August copper imports up on year amid lower prices, stocks
summary: China’s August unwrought copper and copper product imports rose year-on-year as July-August price declines prompted producer buying and arbitrage between Shanghai and London increased inflows. Electricity rationing during a heatwave tightened domestic supply and lowered SFE stocks, supporting copper availability, though overall demand remained soft amid property weakness.

title: EU, U.S. step up Russian aluminium, nickel imports since Ukraine war
summary: Reuters data show EU and U.S. imports of Russian aluminium and nickel rose sharply from March to June, with U.S. aluminium up 21% and nickel up 17% year-on-year and some increases up to ~70%. The shift reflects ongoing sanctions-driven trade rerouting after the Ukraine war.

title: EU, U.S. step up Russian aluminium, nickel imports since Ukraine war
summary: EU and U.S. imports of Russian aluminium and nickel rose markedly in March–June, with values up to $1.98 billion and monthly aluminium imports up around 21% (U.S.) and nickel imports up 17% (top destinations). Analysts link the shift to lessons from disruption after earlier sanctions, suggesting increased supply into Western markets.

title: Nickel Prices Hovered at Highs with Poor Trades_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Jinchuan nickel spot premiums eased to 11,000–10,500 yuan/mt (down from the prior day) and NORNICKEL premiums averaged lower as high futures prices and improved tight supply weighed on trading. Nickel briquette prices also fell. Demand may improve as steel mills resume, but near-term sentiment remains weak.

title: Palpable Overseas Stainless Steel Production Cuts Sustain Nickel Prices at a High Level_SMM
summary: SMM reports that overseas stainless steel mills are expected to shut down in September, likely reducing overseas supply and lifting domestic stainless sentiment. NPI supply is expected to be flat, while rising stainless purchasing supports NPI firming. These factors keep nickel prices high despite weak near-term pure nickel demand.

title: German Aluminum Smelter Halves Output on Soaring Power Costs
summary: A report says a German aluminum smelter has cut production by half because power costs have surged. The output reduction points to immediate curtailments in primary aluminum supply, which can tighten near-term availability and likely provide upward pressure on aluminium prices over the next several weeks.

title: Vale and partners to invest in nickel project in Indonesia
summary: Vale and partners (Shandong Xinhai and Baowu via TISCO) signed a JV to develop the Bahodopi nickel processing plant in Sulawesi, targeting ferronickel output of about 73,000–80,000 tonnes of nickel content annually. Cost is around $2.1bn, with completion targeted by 2025 at latest.

title: China Customs Released August Rare Earth Export and Copper Ore Import Data _SMM
summary: China Customs data show copper ore and concentrate imports of 2.27 million mt in August and 16.64 million mt in Jan-Aug, up 9% year-on-year. This suggests higher feedstock supply for Chinese processing, which can support near-term copper market sentiment. Rare earth flows are also reported but are not directly tracked here.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Intersects 1.05% Copper over 165.8 Metres, Including 2.61% Copper over 34.0 Metres at Copper Creek in Arizona
summary: Faraday Copper announced assay results from five drill holes at its Copper Creek Arizona project, reporting multiple copper intercepts including 1.05% Cu over 165.8 m and 2.61% Cu over 34.0 m. The company plans to incorporate results into an updated resource estimate and PEA, aiming to advance project development.

title: Infinitum Copper Announces Geophysical Interpretation Reveals Strong, Untested, Conductive Anomalies at La Adelita Project
summary: Infinitum Copper reports completion of an MT geophysics interpretation at its La Adelita project in Mexico, identifying untested conductive anomalies aligned with copper-gold-silver skarn mineralization at Cerro Grande and Las Trancas. Diamond drilling results and assays are pending, and Phase 2 drilling is planned once rain improves conditions.

title: Boeing says it stopped buying aluminum from Russia in March
summary: Boeing said it stopped buying aluminum from Russia in March after suspending operations in the sanctions-hit country. It follows an earlier pause on Russian titanium sourcing. Boeing cited widespread aluminum sourcing but the move, alongside Russia’s major role via Rusal, may tighten near-term supply expectations for aluminium.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Drills 2.14% Nickel over 3.3 Metres, 5.15% Nickel over 0.73 Metres, 9.8 Metres of 0.82% Nickel and 349 g/t Silver over 1.72 Metres at Lappvattnet
summary: Gungnir Resources reported additional assays from drilling at its Lappvattnet nickel deposit in Sweden, including 2.14% Ni over 3.3 metres and 0.82% Ni over 9.8 metres, plus a high-grade silver interval. The company is defining nickel shoots and aiming to upgrade its resources.

title: Chinese Waste Handler Weiming Teams Up With GEM on Second Nickel Plant in Indonesia
summary: Chinese waste handler Weiming and GEM will build a USD 448 million laterite nickel smelting JV in Indonesia, producing about 50,000 tons per year of high nickel matte for battery supply chains. The partners will prioritize purchases by stake. A similar project has been underway and additional nickel projects were announced this year.

title: Green light for expansion plans at Aughinish Alumina plant in west Limerick
summary: Irish regulator approved Aughinish Alumina’s plan to expand by-product storage at its Askeaton alumina refinery, raising red mud pond and salt cake storage heights. The expansion supports deposition of about one million cubic metres per annum and helps avoid a projected 2030 operational stop, supporting alumina supply continuity.

title: Camino Minerals Corp.: Camino Intercepts Satellite High-Grade Copper with 55.5m at 0.93% Cu from Surface, including 7.5m of 2.58% Cu at Los Chapitos, Peru
summary: Camino Minerals reported final results from its 2022 drilling at the Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, including multiple high-grade copper oxide intercepts such as 55.5m at 0.93% Cu from surface and 7.5m at 2.58% Cu. The company plans solubility testing and more drilling for potential heap-leach development.

title: Panama copper exports lifted by Cobre Panamá surge
summary: The report (via its headline) states that Panama’s copper exports rose as Cobre Panamá increased production. Higher output and export availability can add near-term supply to the market, which generally puts downward pressure on copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp.: Flying Nickel Drills 113.55 Meters Grading 0.41% Nickel, 0.13 g/t PGM at Minago's North Limb in Thompson Nickel Belt
summary: Flying Nickel reported initial drill results from its Minago nickel sulphide project, with assays averaging 0.41% nickel over 113.55 meters and trace copper. Management says results support down-dip nickel mineralization expansion, with continuous Pt/Pd intercepts. The update is exploration-focused with no production changes.

title: Gungnir Drills 2.14% Nickel over 3.3 Metres, 5.15% Nickel over 0.73 Metres, 9.8 Metres of 0.82% Nickel and 349 g/t Silver over 1.72 Metres at Lappvattnet
summary: Gungnir reports drill assay results at Lappvattnet, including multiple intervals with nickel grades (e.g., 2.14% over 3.3m, 5.15% over 0.73m, and 0.82% over 9.8m) and associated silver results. Such exploration updates can influence market expectations for future nickel supply.

title: Brazilian alumina exports rise 62% in August
summary: Brazil’s alumina exports rose 62% year-on-year in August to 908,008 tonnes, with higher shipments via São Luís and Belém. Export revenues nearly doubled and average FOB prices jumped to $386.14/t. Fastmarkets’ fob Brazil alumina index also increased, indicating firmer alumina pricing that can support aluminium cost expectations.

title: The Energy Transition Could Be Derailed By A Looming Copper Shortage
summary: The piece argues that copper is central to decarbonization and highlights projected shortfalls: demand is expected to nearly double by 2035 and rise further, while primary copper production growth is much smaller. It suggests higher prices may suppress demand but still implies tightening fundamentals.

title: Vale sees 44% increase in global nickel demand by 2030
summary: Vale forecast global nickel demand to rise 44% by 2030 on strong EV-battery growth, alongside an increase in Vale’s own medium-term production. It also expects copper demand to grow about 20% by 2030 and projects a copper structural deficit due to insufficient supply, supporting bullish sentiment for both metals.

title: Tesla strikes $5B deal to purchase nickel products from Indonesia: report
summary: Tesla reportedly signed about a $5 billion, five-year deal to buy nickel products from Indonesia for lithium-ion batteries, with deliveries already started. The contract involves processing companies in Morowali, and Indonesia has sought to secure battery-industry supply by restricting nickel ore exports.

title: FORCE MAJEURE: Massive global shutdowns are now under way for METALS SMELTING operations covering iron, copper, nickel, aluminum, zinc and STEEL
summary: News describes widespread force majeure and shutdowns across metals smelting and fabrication, citing sky-high energy prices and weak demand. Examples include an aluminum smelter closure in Montenegro and primary aluminum cutbacks in Slovenia, plus copper mine/smelt-related disruptions (e.g., Cuajone suspension, Kennecott force majeure), implying near-term supply tightness.

title: FORCE MAJEURE: Massive global shutdowns are now under way for METALS SMELTING operations covering iron, copper, nickel, aluminum, zinc and STEEL
summary: The article says several copper and aluminium production sites worldwide have halted or declared force majeure, citing high electricity costs, weak demand, and disruptions such as protests, earthquakes, or strikes. Examples include an aluminium smelter shutdown and copper cathode/ mine curtailments, implying reduced near-term supply.

title: FORCE MAJEURE: Massive global shutdowns are now under way for METALS SMELTING operations covering iron, copper, nickel, aluminum, zinc and STEEL
summary: Multiple metals smelting and production operations are shutting down worldwide under force majeure and citing very high electricity prices and weak demand. Examples include an aluminium smelter closure in Montenegro, copper mine/smelter disruptions in Peru and Chile, and an electrochemical strike affecting a nickel refinery in Europe.

title: Aluminium Sector in Chinese Stock Market Saw Broad Rise Following Production Cuts by Europe's Largest Aluminium Smelter _SMM
summary: Europe’s energy crisis is forcing aluminium smelters to cut output, highlighted by Dunkirk Aluminium’s 22% production reduction. Soaring electricity costs make production loss-making and lead to broader curtailments. The article notes domestic aluminium prices rose nearly 10% since mid-July, supporting bullish price pressure.

title: Workers at Chile's Escondida copper mine to strike over safety concerns | Kat Country 98.9
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile voted to strike over safety concerns. The action includes partial stoppages Sept. 12 and 14, then an indefinite stoppage until BHP reaches a deal. Escondida says it complied with obligations and temporarily closed affected areas, calling the strike unlawful.

title: Workers at Chile's Escondida copper mine to strike over safety concerns
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in northern Chile voted nearly unanimously to strike over safety concerns. The plan includes partial stoppages on Sept. 12-14 and an indefinite stoppage until a deal is reached. The company says it complied with obligations and temporarily closed affected areas, calling the strike unlawful.

title: China's August coal and copper imports not as strong as they look: Russell
summary: China’s August imports of unwrought copper rose 8.7% month-on-month and 28.2% year-on-year, while Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks fell to the lowest since January before rising only modestly by early September. The higher imports likely reflect arbitrage and only mild demand recovery, but falling inventories can still underpin copper.

title: SMM Analysis of Alternatives after Indonesia Reiterated Its Ban on Bauxite Exports _SMM
summary: SMM reports that Indonesia may halt bauxite exports, alongside earlier nickel ore export restrictions. Chinese alumina refineries relying on Indonesian ore are considering alternatives such as Guinea, Australia, Montenegro, Jamaica, and other sources. The move raises near-term expectations of tighter bauxite/alumina supply for China.

title: Aluminium Production Cuts in Europe Could Potentially Expand before Winter amid Sky-Rocketing Electricity Prices_SMM
summary: Europe faces soaring electricity costs after Russia’s Nord Stream 1 suspension, with natural gas power a key input to generation. European aluminium smelters are already cutting output—over 1 million mt curtailed—and additional cuts are expected before winter. Dunkirk, Alcoa Norway and Hydro plan sizable reductions, temporarily supporting prices.

title: Output of Refined Nickel in August Fell by 3.13% on the Month and is Expected to Increase Slightly in September_SMM
summary: SMM says China produced 15,500 mt refined nickel in August, down 3.13% m/m, with higher spot prices cutting transactions and increasing social inventories by 29%. Downstream demand also weakened. September output is expected to rise, and Indonesia NPI supply may weigh on nickel prices longer term.

title: Premiums of Pure Nickel Remained High, and the Spot Trading was Less than Expected_SMM
summary: SMM reports Jinchuan nickel premiums at 9,500–10,000 yuan/mt and NORNICKEL nickel premiums at 3,500–3,800 yuan/mt, both lower than the prior day. Pure nickel spot premiums fell, but nickel futures rose, keeping spot prices elevated and transactions scarce. Demand for nickel briquettes may improve as mills restart.

title: Aluminium premiums still under pressure in Japan, Europe, Brazil, but US market quiet
summary: Fastmarkets reports aluminium P1020A premia weakening across key regions. Japan’s MJP premium fell as traders noted low deliverability and heavy inventories. Europe and Brazil premiums continued downtrends amid weak spot demand and ample availability, despite reported energy-related smelter curtailments. US premia were flat but at very low levels.

title: Panama copper exports lifted by Cobre Panamá output
summary: The piece reports that Panama’s copper exports were lifted by increased output from Cobre Panamá. Higher production and export volumes can raise near-term supply availability, which typically weighs on copper prices over the short horizon as market expectations shift toward greater availability.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay Announces 48 Metres of 2.92% Copper Intersected at Storm Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay announced drilling results from its Storm Copper Project on Somerset Island, including 48m at 2.92% copper and other high-grade intervals. The company expects further assays and metallurgical tests for potential direct-shipping product development. It advances the 2750N Zone toward resource estimation.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: US EV Battery Supply Chain: Talon Metals Hits 29.39 Meters Grading 2.21% Nickel Equivalent at the Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals announced assay results from 13–14 new drill holes at its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project in Minnesota, including a 29.39-meter interval grading 1.71% nickel and 2.21% nickel equivalent. The company says drilling will continue to expand resources and supports ongoing feasibility planning for 2026 production.

title: York Harbour Metals Drills 14.77 Metres of 2.86% Copper, 6.95% Zinc, and 20.2 gpt Silver and 173.4 gpt Cobalt
summary: York Harbour Metals reports preliminary assays from Phase 3 drilling at its Newfoundland York Harbour Copper-Zinc Project, including a drill interval with 2.86% copper over 14.77 metres. Management says the discovery expands the D Zone and could extend along strike and downdip. Results for additional core are pending.

title: Boeing stopped buying Russian aluminum – the second time it ended sourcing a crucial metal from Russia since the Ukraine invasion
summary: Boeing has stopped buying Russian aluminum again, ending sourcing of a “crucial metal” from Russia for the second time since the Ukraine invasion. The move reduces demand for Russian aluminium supply, potentially tightening near-term availability and supporting aluminium prices as buyers shift away from Russia.

title: Scrap, secondary and recycled aluminium, from rescue to low-carbon gains
summary: The piece argues aluminium prices remain volatile as energy costs and inflation force many smelters in Europe and the USA to curtail or shut down due to uneconomic production. It examines scrap and secondary aluminium trends, noting recycling can cut energy use and emissions, but depends on local, sufficient scrap availability.

title: Speira to curtail 50% of aluminium smelter production at Rheinwerk plant; cites high energy costs
summary: Speira will curtail 50% of aluminium smelter production at Rheinwerk, Germany, cutting output to 70,000 tonnes/year from October through November, citing high European energy costs. The curtailed output will be replaced via external supplies. The move follows other energy-driven aluminium curtailments and occurs amid falling premiums.

title: European Energy Crisis Causes Major Aluminum Capacity Cuts
summary: Soaring European power and gas prices have driven widespread aluminum smelter curtailments, including cuts at Neuss (Germany) and Dunkerque (France). Despite the supply reductions, aluminum prices are still falling to a 17-month low, with recession fears and rising Chinese output capping upside. Eurometaux warns the crisis also affects copper and nickel.

title: NiCAN Reports High Grades in First Two Drill Holes at the Wine Project in Manitoba, Including 27.3 Metres of 2.61% Nickel Equivalent
summary: NiCAN reports “outstanding” assay results from its first two 2022 drill holes at the Wine project in Manitoba. Results include 27.3 metres grading 2.61% nickel equivalent. The company frames the findings as encouraging for thickness and orientation of mineralization encountered in historical drilling.

title: Newly listed junior NiCAN hits 27.3 metres of 2% nickel and 1.81% copper in Manitoba
summary: NiCAN Ltd. announced initial drill results from its Wine project in Manitoba shortly after listing on the TSX Venture Exchange. Hole 22-05 intersected multiple mineralized zones, including 27.3 metres grading about 2% nickel and 1.81% copper, supporting exploration optimism and mildly improving sentiment for both metals.

title: Comex Copper Settles 2.85% Higher at $3.5360 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex Copper for September delivery settled 2.85% higher at $3.5360 per pound, gaining 9.80 cents. The contract posted its largest one-day dollar and percentage gain since late July, rising on three of the past four sessions and reaching the highest settlement since Aug. 30, 2022.

title: Brazil's Vale looking to ramp up copper, nickel output
summary: Vale is reportedly looking to ramp up output of copper and nickel in Brazil. If investors expect higher near-term supply, it typically reduces price support for both metals. However, the provided excerpt lacks specifics on timing, capex, and expected volumes, keeping the price impact magnitude uncertain.

title: Osisko Announces Royalty Transaction With Marimaca Copper
summary: Osisko Gold Royalties said it acquired a 1.0% NSR royalty on the Marimaca copper project in Antofagasta, Chile for US$15.5 million. The release describes the project’s oxide heap-leach profile, resources, and plans for a resource update and definitive feasibility study, without indicating imminent production changes.

title: Copper Super Cycle Temporarily On Halt
summary: Forecasts for a copper “super cycle” are temporarily on hold as global demand weakens amid slowing economies. The copper spot price has fallen sharply since March, with China data, recession fears, and higher rates weighing on demand. Analysts cut forecasts, implying further near-term downside.

title: DGAP-News: Hot Chili Limited: Strong Copper-Silver Drill Results Delivered Ahead of San Antonio Resource Upgrade
summary: Hot Chili Limited announced strong copper-silver drill intercepts at its San Antonio resource with grades above current model, supporting an upgrade from Inferred to Indicated and enabling inclusion in open-pit reserve estimates. It also highlights promising Valentina results and planned follow-up drilling, boosting copper project outlook.

title: Strong Copper-Silver Drill Results Delivered Ahead Of San An...
summary: Hot Chili reported strong copper-silver drill intersections at Chile’s Costa Fuego, particularly upgrading the San Antonio deposit from Inferred toward Indicated status. Higher-grade results support adding ore to open-pit reserve estimates for the Pre-feasibility Study and planning further drilling at the adjacent Valentina prospect.

title: Aluminium Smelters in Yunnan Could Potentially Be Subject to Power Rationing after the Mid-Autumn Festival _SMM
summary: Yunnan has large, active aluminium smelting capacity and recently produced record-high output. Low reservoir water levels raise the risk of power rationing after the Mid-Autumn Festival. If implemented, electricity limits could reduce smelter operating rates, lowering near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Poseidon Nickel: Beats digging it up
summary: ASX-listed Poseidon Nickel’s MD Peter Harold says the company can generate revenue by re-treating older, previously idle gold tailings. The business focus is on extracting additional value from existing material rather than new digging, which can improve expectations for nickel processing and incremental supply.

title: TCs of Spot Copper Concentrate Rose to Above $80/mt Affected by the Qinhuangdao Port Incident  _SMM
summary: SMM reports spot copper concentrate trading improved, with imported copper concentrate TCs rising above $80/mt and Qinhuangdao port re-trading showing $84–85/mt levels. Inventories at the port fell week-on-week, while higher costs and potential stoppages/strikes at major mines raise concentrate supply risk.

title: Bonded Zone Inventory of Pure Nickel Dropped Slightly as the Terminals Picked up_SMM
summary: SMM says bonded-zone pure nickel inventory fell to 6,400 mt. Nickel briquette inventory was 2,150 mt and nickel plate 4,250 mt, both down slightly. The declines were linked to probable September steel mill production resumption and steady purchasing by salt plants, plus continuous nickel sulphate output release.

title: Mitsubishi Materials to buy out Onahama copper smelter partners
summary: Mitsubishi Materials will buy out remaining partners in the Onahama copper smelter in Fukushima, taking full ownership from March 31. The company says the change will improve decision-making to help the smelter handle rising electricity and fuel costs, and it plans recycled-material pre-processing.

title: Alumex introduces environmentally friendly low-carbon aluminium to grow export markets
summary: Alumex launched low-carbon aluminium billets (“Ozon”) backed by a new state-of-the-art melting facility at Sapugaskanda, with over Rs. 1 billion investment. The process claims much lower energy use for billet production and targets export demand from the USA, UK, Europe, and Australia, supporting improved aluminium market competitiveness.

title: Talon Metals' Tamarack nickel project continues to grow
summary: Talon Metals and Rio Tinto’s Tamarack nickel project in central Minnesota continues to expand as explorers find thicker, higher-grade nickel-copper mineralization outside the defined resource zone. The updated results improve perceived future supply prospects for nickel and, secondarily, copper, potentially supporting prices modestly.

title: South32 to switch fossil fuels at alumina refinery as coal ends
summary: South32 said it will transition its Worsley alumina refinery in Western Australia from coal to gas as the state moves out of coal-fired power. The firm expects a further shift to renewables only after viable alternatives emerge and dependent technologies develop, implying near-term production cost impacts for alumina-linked markets.

title: Rio Takeover of Giant Copper Mine Opposed by Top Investor
summary: The headline says Rio’s bid to take over a giant copper mine faces opposition from a top investor. Such disputes over control of a major copper asset can increase uncertainty around production and supply timing, potentially weighing on short-term copper market expectations over coming days to weeks.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 4.66% Higher at $3.5810 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex Copper front-month for September delivery ended the week 4.66% higher at $3.5810, up 15.95 cents per pound. The contract gained for multiple sessions, reaching the highest settlement since Aug. 29, and is up modestly month-to-date despite remaining far below recent highs.

title: Glencore reaches new deal with workers at Quebec nickel mine
summary: Glencore reached a new five-year deal with workers at Quebec’s Raglan nickel mine, ending a strike lasting over 100 days. The agreement includes wage increases and tighter subcontractor use, and production is set to restart Sept. 12. Prolonged closure had threatened global Class 1 nickel supplies.

title: Indonesia president says likely to lose WTO nickel dispute against EU
summary: Indonesia’s President Joko Widodo said the country is likely to lose its WTO dispute with the EU over a 2020 ban on exporting nickel ore. Regardless of the ruling, Indonesia plans to extend similar export bans to other raw commodities, but the likely WTO outcome raises expectations of easing nickel supply restrictions.

title: Copper Prices Are Trading Sideways, But Not For Long
summary: Copper is described as trading sideways but vulnerable to further declines amid high European energy costs and weak demand. Soaring electricity expenses raise producer input costs and can trigger shutdown risk. The Eurozone PMI remains in contraction, weighing on demand. Chile’s rejected constitution avoids bullish supply-restriction headlines.

title: Rise of lithium not seen threatening nickel demand - BusinessWorld Online
summary: BusinessWorld reports that rising lithium use in EVs is not expected to threaten nickel demand. Industry officials say nickel remains the preferred cathode metal and will be used alongside other materials, noting nickel-based cathodes powered most new plug-in EV battery capacity in 2021. Philippines nickel output exposure is highlighted.

title: Indonesia Leaving Australia In Its EV-Making Dust
summary: The article argues Indonesia is accelerating EV battery supply chains by expanding nickel mining and downstream processing (ferronickel/nickel pig iron, smelters and planned industrial capacity). It notes Indonesia already supplies about a third of global nickel and expects the market to move back toward surplus, adding bearish pressure. A potential 2% export duty is also mentioned.

title: Electricity restrictions in Yunnan may increase aluminum price
summary: Electricity restrictions in China’s Sichuan/Yunnan region have been extended, keeping industrial power cuts in place through Thursday. The disruption raises concerns of reduced aluminum smelting output in a major supply area, which can tighten near-term market balance and lift aluminum prices.

title: Camino Minerals Corp.: Camino Granted Drilling Permit in Central Area of the Maria Cecilia Copper Gold Porphyry Complex in Peru
summary: Camino Minerals said it received the DIA environmental permit for its Maria Cecilia copper-gold porphyry project in Peru, authorizing up to 23,000 metres of drilling. The company plans drilling on 20 platforms after additional start-of-operations permitting, aiming to test higher copper grades and extend mineralization.

title: C3 Metals Inc.: C3 Metals Intersects 309.0 Metres at 0.44% Copper and 0.33 g/t Gold in First Assays from Bellas Gate Project, Jamaica
summary: C3 Metals reported partial assay results from its Bellas Gate Project in Jamaica, including 309 metres grading 0.44% copper (from 15 metres downhole) and 0.33 g/t gold. Two additional holes were completed at Epidote Ridge with assays pending, supporting continued drilling on copper-gold targets.

title: Mitsubishi to take over Japanese copper smelter from JV partners
summary: Mitsubishi Materials will buy the remaining stakes in its Onahama Smelting and Refining copper JV to gain full ownership. The plan targets higher operating resilience amid rising electricity and fuel costs, including new pre-processing and e-scrap capacity. The smelter is a key eastern Japan copper supply source.

title: Yunnan aluminium producers ordered to cut output amid power rationing
summary: Yunnan aluminium smelters are ordered to cut output by about 10% initially due to power rationing, potentially rising to 20% and lasting until May next year. Given Yunnan’s role as China’s aluminium hub and power-driven production constraints, the market expects tighter aluminium supply and higher SHFE prices.

title: JV Article: Tartisan Nickel outlines low-cost underground nickel sulphide mine at flagship Kenbridge project
summary: Tartisan Nickel released a preliminary economic assessment for its Kenbridge underground nickel sulphide project in Ontario, citing low pre-production capital, expandable resources and potential early production in about 3.5 years. The PEA includes ore grades of ~0.97% nickel and ~0.52% copper, but no immediate supply impact.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.24% Higher at $3.6255 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for September delivery settled 1.24% higher at $3.6255 per pound, gaining 4.45 cents. The contract rose for three straight sessions, up 18.75 cents (5.45%) over that span and five of the past six days, with the highest settlement since Aug. 29, 2022.

title: Global Supply Disruptions Will Continue to Boost Aluminium Prices, Despite Hawkish Stance in Europe and the US _SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices surged on week amid continuing supply disruptions. Yunnan smelters are expected to cut output 10–20% after the Mid-Autumn Festival, while overseas cuts exceed 1.5 million tonnes this year. Social inventories are falling, and downstream restocking is improving, though demand remains softer.

title: SMM Survey: Aluminium Billet Operating Rates to Maintain the Downward Trend in September amid Pessimistic Outlook for Downstream Market _SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s molten aluminium casting billet operating rates fell to 67.84% in August, citing weaker downstream extruder orders, COVID disruptions, and power rationing. Higher silicon and magnesium costs raised billet costs, while some regions faced extended restart delays. September/October demand pessimism implies further operating-rate declines.

title: The Short-Term Alumina Prices to Fluctuate within A Narrow Range amid Disruptions to Both Supply and Demand Sides_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s metallurgical-grade alumina prices mostly range-bound, but overseas deals rose due to frequent smelter output cuts. In China, some refineries face pandemic-related closed-off management, potentially tightening supply, while aluminium smelters have already started small-scale output cuts. Demand weakening may cap further gains.

title: Russian aluminium giant cut out of Queensland operation to abide by sanctions, Rio Tinto says
summary: Rio Tinto cut Rusal out of its Gladstone, Queensland alumina refinery operations to avoid breaching Australian sanctions on Russian oligarchs linked to Rusal. Rusal’s subsidiary sued, but the dispute underscores an immediate disruption to Russian-linked alumina bauxite processing and alumina export flows, which can tighten aluminium-related supply.

title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zones Decreased 25,000 mt from September 2_SMM
summary: SMM data shows copper inventories in China’s domestic bonded zones fell 25,000 mt from Sep 2 to 134,700 mt as of Sep 9, the lowest level since tracking began. Shanghai and Guangdong bonded inventories dropped further, with ongoing inflows to the domestic market and expectations of continued declines this week.

title: Aluminium Ingot Social Inventory Accumulated after Three-Day Holiday _SMM
summary: SMM says China’s aluminium ingot social inventories rose to 696,000 mt on Sep 13, up from the prior week, driven by holiday arrivals and slower pickup. Downstream buyers stayed cautious given high aluminium prices. Sichuan smelters are restarting slowly, while Yunnan cut fears eased, adding supply clarity.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Added 19,100 mt from Last Friday_SMM
summary: SMM data shows copper inventories across major Chinese markets rose 19,100 mt to 89,800 mt, up versus last week’s level and higher across most regions during the Mid-Autumn holiday. SMM expects continued domestic supply-driven builds this week, while downstream restocking remains weak near SHFE 2209 delivery.

title: Lara Exploration Ltd.: Lara Intercepts 380.79 Metres at 0.57% Copper Equivalent at the Planalto Project
summary: Lara Exploration reported results from seven follow-up drill holes at the Cupuzeiro target within its Planalto Copper Project in Brazil, including a long sulphide-copper intersection of 380.79 metres at 0.575% copper equivalent and higher-grade zones. The company also drilled around the Homestead target, finding some copper potential.

title: Infinitum Copper Reports 20.60 Metres of 1.91% Copper, 2.00 g/t Gold and 40.91 g/t Silver in Drilling at La Adelita Project
summary: Infinitum Copper reported initial diamond drill results from the La Adelita project, including 20.60 m grading 1.91% copper (plus Au and Ag) in skarn mineralization at the Cerro Grande zone. Geophysics suggest mineralization may strengthen at depth, supporting continued exploration and potential future supply improvements.

title: Constellium SE: Constellium supplying aluminium Auto Body Sheet solutions to a premium car manufacturer
summary: Constellium said it will supply aluminium auto body sheet solutions for Mercedes-Benz C-Class vehicles produced in Europe, China, and South Africa, including hood, roof, tailgate and fenders, using plants in France and Germany. The update indicates ongoing aluminium demand from automotive, but provides no volume data to gauge price impact.

title: Copper Is The New Oil: Expected To Rise By More Than 50% by 2040
summary: The piece cites BloombergNEF projections of rising long-term copper demand and notes copper-focused corporate updates: Torq’s expanded drilling and funding for Chile projects and the EPA draft UIC permit for the Florence Copper Project. It also references company results affected by lower copper prices, outages, and higher costs.

title: Go Metals Intersects Wide Intervals of Nickel and Copper Sulphides
summary: Go Metals says initial drilling at its 100% owned HSP nickel-copper-PGE project in Quebec visually confirmed nickel-copper sulphides across five zones, including several wide intercepts. Assay results are pending, and the company plans more drilling as samples are sent for lab analysis.

title: Go Metals Intersects Wide Intervals of Nickel and Copper Sulphides
summary: Go Metals reported that drilling at its 100% owned HSP nickel-copper project in Quebec visually identified nickel and copper sulphides across five zones. The company sent initial samples for lab assays and noted wide mineralized intervals. The update is exploration-focused with no confirmed assay or production impact.

title: Three miners die at Peru copper mine run by Toronto's Sierra Metals
summary: Three miners died in a mudslide at Sierra Metals’ Yauricocha copper-zinc mine in Peru, prompting a temporary suspension until conditions are safe. The company produces significant copper from Yauricocha. Given Peru’s large role in copper supply, the outage may pressure near-term copper prices downward.

title: Premium Nickel Resources Ltd. Reports Additional Assay Results at Its 100% Owned Selebi Mine in Botswana: 6.40 metres of 0.52% NI, 2.63% CU, 1.51% NIEQ
summary: Premium Nickel Resources Ltd. released additional assay results from its 100% owned Selebi mine in Botswana, reporting 6.40 metres of 0.52% nickel and 2.63% copper. Improved assay information can strengthen market expectations for future nickel output, with a smaller positive signal for copper.

title: Aluminum Prices Slip Despite Smelter Shutdowns Chipping Away At Supply
summary: Aluminum prices have slipped as European energy costs force additional smelter cuts (e.g., a 22% capacity reduction at Dunkerque and halving Speira output), and production hits multi-decade lows. However, weakening demand, falling premiums, and rising LME inventories alongside lower prices suggest net bearish pressure.

title: Bucks County man allegedly stole copper wire from decommissioned power plants, causing millions in damage
summary: Prosecutors allege a man broke into shuttered coal-fired power plants in Pennsylvania and Maryland to steal copper wire for resale at scrap yards, causing substantial local damage. Copper theft increases scrap availability and regional supply into recyclers, but reported volumes appear too limited for broader copper price moves within weeks.

title: Multiple Adverse Factors Restricted Recovery in Operating Rates of Copper Cathode Rod Enterprises in August _SMM
summary: SMM reports copper cathode rod producers’ operating rates rose slightly MoM but fell YoY to 74.44% in August. Pandemic in Jiangxi, power rationing in parts of East China, and high south China cathode premiums reduced or suspended production. September operating rates are expected to recover as disruptions fade.

title: Spot Prices of Pure Nickel Fell Slightly, with No Significant Improvement in Transactions_SMM
summary: SMM reports spot nickel weakness in China. Jinchuan nickel premiums fell to about 6,750 yuan/mt and NORNICKEL premiums to around 3,100 yuan/mt. Nickel futures dipped on softer demand, while spot prices stayed near 195,000 yuan/mt. Nickel briquette prices also declined, with fewer trades as nickel sulphate economics deteriorated.

title: China's Huayou Teams Up Again With Vale to Build Second Nickel Plant in Indonesia
summary: Huayou Cobalt and Vale will build a second HPAL nickel processing plant in Indonesia to produce 60,000 metric tons per year of nickel in mixed hydroxide precipitate (MHP) from Vale’s Sorowako limonite. The joint venture may expand if feed supply grows, bolstering nickel supply expectations.

title: Terminal Electronics Sector Improved Marginally, and Operating Rates of Copper Foil Enterprises Rebounded in August as Expected_SMM
summary: SMM says copper foil producers’ average operating rate rose to 86.19% in August, helped by restocking when copper prices retreated and improved lithium-battery and some electronics demand. However, September operating rates face downward pressure as COVID outbreaks delay capacity commissioning and weaken electronics consumer sentiment.

title: Highland Copper Provides Update on Key Projects
summary: Highland Copper provided an update on its Copperwood and White Pine projects in Michigan, including an expected feasibility study update, permitting progress, and potential production of copper concentrates and possibly cathodes via on-site leaching. The company cites strong EV/renewables-driven copper demand and higher expected input costs.

title: Fabled Copper Corp.: Fabled Wraps Up 2022 Muskwa Exploration Discusses Accomplishments for the Season
summary: Fabled Copper Corp. reports completion of its 2022 exploration program on the Muskwa Copper Project in northern British Columbia. The company completed extensive field days, sampling, mapping, geophysics, and permitting progress toward future drilling and potential 43-101 work. No production or near-term supply changes are announced.

title: Highland Copper Provides Update On Key Projects
summary: Highland Copper updates on its Copperwood and White Pine projects in Michigan, including plans to issue an updated feasibility study, ongoing permitting (incl. federal pumping-station approval), and potential process/cost improvements. The company cites strong copper demand for electrification but no immediate production or supply shock is announced.

title: Analysis-Industrial Users Flee LME Nickel, Deepening Market Fissures
summary: LME nickel trading volumes have fallen sharply and participants are increasingly avoiding the contract after a March suspension and explosive price move. Low liquidity reinforces volatility. The shift toward cheaper Indonesian nickel pig iron (NPI) and related feedstocks reduces reliance on deliverable LME nickel, weighing on nickel sentiment.

title: Proactive news headlines including Majuba Hill Copper, KULR Technology, American Battery Technology Company, Kainantu Resources, Valeo Pharma and Renforth Resources
summary: Proactive’s article is a roundup of investor news including copper and nickel exploration updates. It notes Majuba Hill Copper’s Nevada drilling completion and Fabled Copper’s Muskwa exploration results, while Copper Fox delays drilling. It also cites Nickel North Exploration expanding mineralization and other battery-metal project work, implying mixed signals.

title: Chinese Miner Joins Vale in Building Second Nickel Refining Plant in Indonesia
summary: Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt and PT Vale Indonesia plan to build a second nickel refining plant in Sorowako, using HPAL to convert low-grade limonite laterite into MHP, an intermediate product for EV battery materials. The project expands Indonesia’s nickel processing capacity and improves refined-output prospects.

title: Alumex introduces environmentally friendly Low-Carbon Aluminium to grow export markets
summary: Alumex PLC (Sri Lanka) launched a low-carbon aluminium billet brand (“Ozon”) backed by a new state-of-the-art melting facility at Sapugaskanda. The firm claims major energy reductions and capacity expansion to grow exports to the USA, UK, Europe and Australia, supporting higher aluminium billet demand.

title: Alcoa Squeezed by 'Stubbornly High' Costs, Lower Aluminum Prices
summary: BNN/Weekend Edition reports that Alcoa is being squeezed by stubbornly high costs while aluminum prices are lower. The coverage implies ongoing weakness in the aluminum market and potential margin pressure for producers, which can weigh on near-term sentiment toward aluminum prices.

title: Pure Nickel Demand Remained Poor, and Nickel Prices Deviated from the Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SMM reports that China’s energy-consumption controls tightened nonferrous supply, lifting nickel prices into early September, but pure nickel demand remains weak due to high futures prices. With strong macro uncertainty and weak downstream orders, prices may fall in the short term. Indonesia’s NPI/intermediate projects could add supply surplus.

title: Magmatic Resources: A monster copper drill hit in elephant country!
summary: Magmatic Resources says it has achieved a very large copper drill hit, described as half a kilometre long and still being extended, in an “elephant country” setting. The announcement relates directly to potential copper resources, which can slightly lift sentiment, though it does not confirm near-term output.

title: Supply in the Spot Market was Tight, and the Heightened Production of Integrated Enterprises Failed to Fully Address the Supply Tightness of Nickel Salt_SMM
summary: SMM reports battery-grade nickel sulphate prices rose in August as spot supply tightened, despite slight overall oversupply, because integrated producers’ output is not fully available in spot circulation. September demand is picking up and utilization is higher, so prices should stay supported though spot tightness may ease.

title: Orange given go-ahead to decommission copper telephone lines in France
summary: France’s regulator Arcep has cleared Orange to begin decommissioning copper telephone lines in selected communes from end-2024, with full country disconnection by 2030. Orange cites €500m annual savings and says copper won’t be cut without fibre or other alternatives, though critics warn rural fibre delays.

title: Prices of Domestic Bauxite in North China Fell Slightly, but to Remain High in the Long Term_SMM
summary: SMM says domestic bauxite prices in northern China fell slightly in mid-September, with lower bids attributed to August reductions in alumina refinery production (high costs) and weaker bauxite demand. Nevertheless, it expects alumina output to grow while domestic bauxite remains tight, so prices should stay high.

title: Copper Alloy Wire Market Research Report by Technavio predicts USD 18.16 Bn growth -- APAC to have significant share
summary: Technavio’s report forecasts growth for the copper alloy wire market (about USD 18.6B incremental growth) driven by electrical/electronics demand and APAC’s large market share. It describes longer-term market expansion but provides no concrete near-term supply disruptions, inventory changes, tariffs, or contract price impacts for copper, nickel, or aluminium.

title: Aluminium Plate/Sheet and Strip: The Production was Contained by Seasonal Low and Power Rationing in August, and is Expected to Recover to Some Extent in September_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium plate/sheet and strip producers ran at 71.97% in August, down MoM/YoY, due to seasonal low demand and power rationing amid an energy shortage. SMM expects September operating rates to recover as rationing eases and overseas energy pressure may boost Chinese exports, though a worsening pandemic could offset gains.

title: Copper's Outlook for 2022 Amid Stressed Macro and Mild Fundamentals
summary: The piece examines China’s copper spot tightness, explaining what is tightening the market and the likely duration. It also assesses whether China’s copper consumption will improve and what factors drive demand. The discussion centers on copper market balance, implying near-term price support from supply tightness.

title: SMM Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventory as of September 15_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium ingot social inventories across eight China markets at 675,000 mt on Sep 15, slightly up week-on-week but down sharply versus Tuesday and year ago. Aluminium billet social inventory fell to 114,900 mt. Reduced arrivals from Sichuan/Yunnan and potential further Yunnan smelter cuts may support higher spot prices.

title: Key topics ahead of Fastmarkets international Copper Conference 2022
summary: Fastmarkets’ pre-conference report highlights tight refined copper fundamentals in 2022: low on-warrant stocks on COMEX and SHFE, recovering but still constrained LME availability, and persistently elevated physical premiums in Europe and China. It links supply frictions and limited warrant deliverability, including some Russian cathode restrictions, to supportive near-term copper pricing.

title: MMC Norilsk Nickel: FIRE AT KOLA MMC EXTINGUISHED. NICKEL AND PLATINUM GROUP METALS PRODUCTION UNAFFECTED
summary: Norilsk Nickel says a fire in the cobalt section of its Kola electrowinning shop-2 was extinguished and the platinum group metals production chain remains intact. The company reports the main building, finished products storage, and nickel electrowinning sections were not affected, with a test run showing normal nickel output.

title: Copper Could See A Supply Shortfall By 2025
summary: Rio Tinto’s increased control of the Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold mine faces opposition from minority shareholders, led by Pentwater, after additional stake purchases. The project is expected to reach large-scale copper output, but investor disputes raise near-term uncertainty as experts still forecast a copper supply shortfall by 2025.

title: To Buy Or Not To Buy: Russian Aluminium Dilemma For Europe's Buyers
summary: Europe’s aluminium buyers face power shortages and high electricity costs, but some still plan to purchase Russian Rusal metal despite war-related moral concerns. Others refuse Rusal supply for next year due to reputational risk. With Rusal reportedly offering $100-$150/tonne discounts amid threatened supply, pricing pressure intensifies for aluminium contracts.

title: Aluminium rises, but other metals slip on recession fears
summary: Aluminium prices rose as Europe’s power crisis forced about half of EU aluminium capacity offline and analysts warned shortages could worsen in winter. Copper fell amid recession demand fears and a sharp jump in LME on-warrant stocks; nickel dropped even more with broader risk-off sentiment and tighter economic prospects.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.62% Lower at $3.5235 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for September delivery settled 0.62% lower at $3.5235 per pound, dropping 2.20 cents. It marked three consecutive down sessions, with the biggest three-day decline since Sept. 2, 2022. The settlement was also the lowest since Sept. 7, 2022.

title: Automakers and Aluminum Producers Prepare to "Transform Mobility and Electrification Through Collaboration"
summary: The Aluminum Association’s Aluminum Transportation Group hosted an automotive-electrification panel linking automakers with aluminum producers. Speakers discussed joint work on manufacturing processes, advanced alloys, and joining technologies, along with aluminum-clad vehicles displayed at NAIAS and related industry outreach aimed at accelerating aluminium penetration in transportation.

title: Copper Prices to Stay High amid Tight Supply, even as Hawkish Stance of the US Fed is in Favour of the US Dollar_SMM
summary: Report expects copper to remain high due to tight supply: LME inventories continue to fall (~100,000 mt), cash-to-3-month backwardation hits multi-month highs, and SHFE warrant stocks are very low. It flags possible Escondida strike risk and easing power rationing, while warning hawkish Fed/firm USD adds volatility and medium-term pressure.

title: Constellium to keep buying aluminium from Rusal - executive
summary: Constellium’s executive said Rusal accounts for under 5% of its aluminium purchases and that, with no sanctions currently in place, the company sees no reason to avoid buying. The article contrasts other buyers turning away from Russian metal and mentions discounts tied to potential export-sanction risk.

title: Shanghai aluminium supported by fears of wider production cuts
summary: Shanghai aluminium rose up to 2% on fears of wider and longer China production cuts as power restrictions in Yunnan could expand and remain in place amid low rainfall and hydropower supply. Gains were capped by record August output and global macro worries, which also weighed on copper and nickel.

title: CME Group Announces Record Volume as Participation in Aluminum Futures Accelerates
summary: CME Group said aluminum futures trading has hit record volume, with average daily volume up sharply and growing open interest and accounts. Participants, including Bonnell Aluminum, are using the contracts for hedging and referencing prices in downstream contracts. The release highlights market liquidity rather than physical aluminum fundamentals.

title: SMM Analysis: Alumina Prices still Vulnerable to Decline, despite Aluminium Price Rally_SMM
summary: SMM says aluminium prices have recently rebounded, but alumina remains vulnerable: regional alumina prices are weak and demand risk is rising as hydropower shortages in Yunnan cause smelters to reduce output. Although Sichuan curbs eased and some capacity resumes, Yunnan’s production risk keeps downside pressure on alumina.

title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zones Dipped 19,300 mt from Last Friday_SMM
summary: SMM data show copper inventories in China’s domestic bonded zones fell by 19,300 mt from Sept 9 to 115,400 mt as of Sept 16, the lowest in SMM records and the twelfth straight weekly drop. Shanghai declined sharply on sustained warrant outflows, later slowed by a weaker SHFE/LME ratio; further narrowing is possible next week.

title: Aluminium has challenges in short term but a 'great future' – Alcoa's Harvey
summary: Alcoa’s Harvey says short-term aluminium markets face volatility from high European electricity prices, with some smelters offline and Alcoa cutting output at its Lista facility. Despite tighter energy conditions, demand remains weak and recession fears weigh, reducing European aluminium premiums (P1020A) versus earlier peaks.

title: Infinity Stone Ventures Corp.: Infinity Stone Discovers 15.5% Copper from New Zone at Zen-Whoberi Project
summary: Infinity Stone Ventures announced new assay results from its Zen-Whoberi Project, identifying a Centauri Zone where one grab sample returned 15.5% copper, alongside anomalous silver, gold, nickel and cobalt. Additional samples show lower copper grades. The update is exploration-focused, with no production or inventory changes stated.

title: Nickel ore Inventories at Chinese Ports up 426,000 wmt on Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said Chinese nickel ore port inventories rose 426,000 wmt to 7.06 million wmt as of Sep 16, driven by approaching rainy-season restocking and recovering downstream demand. Inventories increased across seven major ports as shipments improved. The outlook is further growth, with NPI plants’ nickel-ore demand expected to rise as well.

title: ​Agnico Eagle, Teck Resources teaming up on Mexico copper-zinc mine
summary: The article headline says Agnico Eagle and Teck Resources are partnering on a Mexico copper-zinc mine. The development supports copper supply expectations, but without details on start dates, output changes, or disruptions, it is unlikely to create immediate pricing pressure over the next days to weeks.

title: Copper heads for weekly fall as China's yuan slumps
summary: Copper is set for a weekly decline as a weaker yuan and stronger dollar make dollar-priced metals costlier for Chinese buyers. Investors also fear slowing growth amid a deepening China property slump and broader recession risks. Aluminium on the LME is also down, consistent with risk-off macro pressure.

title: Teck sells half of Mexican copper project to Agnico Eagle as it shifts focus to larger ventures
summary: Teck agreed to sell half its San Nicolás copper project in Mexico to Agnico Eagle, with Agnico contributing $580 million to fund development. The mine is expected to start production in 2026, and copper is projected to be a smaller part of Agnico’s revenue. Overall, near-term copper effects seem limited.

title: U.S. And EU Nickel Imports From Russia Surge
summary: U.S. and EU imports of Russian nickel rose sharply after March, with shipments to the U.S. up 70% (March–June) and to the EU up 22%. The influx of discounted Russian material suggests overstated disruption fears and increased supply availability, which can pressure nickel prices despite some earlier upside momentum.

title: Thieves turning to copper pipe, wire thefts
summary: The news reports that theft of copper pipe and wire is rising, as criminals target these materials for resale. This could slightly increase near-term demand for copper and raise concerns about local availability or security costs, but the article lacks data on volumes or broader market impact.

title: Tertiary, FQM partner to jointly explore two Zambian copper projects
summary: Tertiary Minerals and First Quantum Minerals agreed to jointly explore two copper projects in Zambia (Mukai and Mushima North), including sharing historical exploration data and coordinating a technical committee to advance exploration and development. The licences are near FQM’s Trident Project, which includes nickel and copper assets, but timing is exploratory.

title: COVID-19 couldn't stop Dajcor Aluminum Ltd. from growing
summary: Dajcor Aluminum says COVID-19 slowed operations early on but the company doubled in size over the pandemic period. It expanded via automation and opened a new plant in Kentucky, which has restarted after flooding. The Kentucky site adds extrusion capacity, supporting expectations of rising aluminum product demand across automotive and construction.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 0.56% Lower at $3.5610 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex Copper for September delivery ended the week 0.56% lower at $3.5610 per pound, down 2.0 cents, following two down weeks in the past three. It gained 1.06% on the day, snapping a three-session losing streak. Broader performance vs highs/lows is also cited.

title: China's August aluminium imports fall 19% on-year as domestic output rises
summary: China’s August aluminium imports fell 19% year-on-year to 200,440 tonnes as domestic production rose to record monthly levels after relaxed power restrictions. Easing local supply “jitters” reduced import volumes, while demand for imported material stayed supported by changes in power-linked production. European cuts and a closed SHFE-LME arbitrage window also weighed on flows.

title: Far East Gold starts first ever drilling program at historic Anak Perak copper-gold prospect
summary: Far East Gold started its first drilling at the Anak Perak copper-gold prospect within Indonesia’s Woyla project, after securing a borrow-use licence for advanced exploration. The program will test the vein system and support a future maiden resource estimate, but no assay or production changes are reported.

title: Transactions between Mines and Smelters were Active, and TCs of Spot Copper Concentrate Kept Rising_SMM
summary: SMM reports active spot copper concentrate trading and higher Imported Copper Concentrate Index levels. Clean concentrates from the Americas flowed into China, and some copper concentrates were rerouted to China after a South Korea smelter accident, lifting TCs. Mine safety issues in South America and Peru add supply risk, while port inventories fell.

title: Overseas Alumina Prices Rose amid Improved Trading Activities, While Domestic Prices Fell due to Weaker Demand _SMM
summary: SMM reports domestic alumina prices fell across most provinces on weaker demand and thin trading, despite firmer overseas prices. It highlights widening domestic/overseas differentials supporting exports, but warns Yunnan power rationing may reduce aluminium output by 20–30%, putting alumina demand at risk and possibly pressuring prices further.

title: Aluminium Price Volatility to Intensify amid Bearish Macro Environment against Bullish Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SMM reports volatility in aluminium prices: SHFE fell on the week while LME rose. Macro factors like hotter US CPI, higher Fed hike probabilities, and weaker RMB are seen pressuring aluminium. Offsetting supports include Yunnan smelter production cuts (10% possibly to 20%), slow Sichuan ramp-up, and domestic demand stimulus.

title: Tight Supply Will Keep Nickel Sulphate Prices at Highs_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Battery-grade nickel sulphate prices followed nickel slightly higher last week. SMM says insufficient MHP-based nickel sulphate capacity will be hard to resolve through the rest of the year. While high-grade matte-based capacity has grown, spot supply remains tight, and despite weak restocking demand, prices are expected to stay at highs this week.

title: The Inventory of Aluminium Ingots Remained Low, Withdrawals from Warehouses Declined Significantly_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s aluminium ingot social inventories at 685,000 mt, still around a low level despite minor week-to-week uptick. Warehouse withdrawals fell sharply to 113,800 mt amid holiday disruptions and weaker billet demand after imported inflows. With National Day stocking and Yunnan production reductions ahead, inventories are unlikely to build in September.

title: Copper prices fall on bleak demand outlook pressures
summary: Copper prices fell as markets turned more pessimistic about global growth, raising concerns of weaker metals demand; the weak U.S. dollar limited declines. Fitch Solutions cut its copper forecast. Aluminium also weakened on lower Chinese import volumes tied to strong domestic production, while nickel moved higher amid mixed signals.

title: Callinex Intersects 33.67m of 4.29% Copper and Other High-Grade Intervals at the Rainbow Deposit located in the Flin Flon Mining District, MB
summary: Callinex reported intersections of 33.67 meters grading 4.29% copper at its Rainbow Deposit in Manitoba’s Flin Flon Mining District, plus other high-grade intervals. The update is supportive of potential future copper supply, but is unlikely to materially move copper prices in the near term on its own.

title: Nickel Ore Prices Varied Approaching the Rainy Season_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Ni 1.5% ore averaging $67.5/wmt CIF on Sep 16, flat on week, while low-grade FOB/CIF prices rose on scarce supply ahead of the rainy season. Medium-grade deals were disputed. Limited stainless demand and high NPI inventories cap upside, but a slight seasonal rise in ore is expected ($68–72).

title: Agnico Eagle to buy stake in Teck's Mexican copper-zinc mine
summary: Agnico Eagle agreed to buy a 50% stake in Teck’s Minas de San Nicolas, forming a JV to develop the San Nicolás copper-zinc project in Zacatecas, Mexico. Investment terms include $580m subscription and further shared costs, but the project remains undeveloped and scheduled to close in H1 2023.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Intersects Additional High-Grade Copper-Gold Veins Within the Alacran Deposit at its 100%-owned San Matias Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals reported additional infill drill results at its 100%-owned San Matias/Alacran copper-gold-silver project in Colombia, including 30.48m of 1.87% copper and other high-grade intervals. Results confirm higher-grade domains and CBM vein continuity, supporting bullish sentiment toward copper prospects.

title: JV Article: Battery Mineral Resources accelerates path to production at Punitaqui copper complex in Chile
summary: Battery Mineral Resources says Chile’s environmental authority has approved the environmental impact declaration for mining at its Punitaqui copper complex. The company cites positive drill results, a resource update, strong metallurgical recoveries, and expects copper concentrate production to start in Q1, supporting incremental near-term supply sentiment.

title: JV Article: Doré Copper Mining on track to develop Quebec's first copper mine
summary: Doré Copper’s PEA outlines restarting the Chibougamau copper camp in Quebec, centered on the Corner Bay deposit feeding the Copper Rand mill. The plan targets about 492 million lb of copper over 10.5 years and includes feasibility, mill refurbishment, and ongoing infill drilling. This supports bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Callinex shares jump on strong copper intervals at Rainbow
summary: Callinex Mines shares jumped more than 15% after drilling results from its Pine Bay project in Manitoba, including work at the Rainbow copper deposit. The update was strong enough to lift the company’s outlook, which can improve market expectations for future copper supply and sentiment in the near term.

title: Aluminium Prices Supported by Potential Production Cuts and Rising Cost_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices are supported by expected power-related production cuts in Yunnan and rising electricity costs, while actual restriction levels remain uncertain. Sichuan smelters are resuming, slightly easing supply. Demand remains sluggish and inventories are low, leaving aluminium pressured by weak transactions but structurally supported.

title: Aluminium Scrap Circulation Improved ahead of September US Rate Hike_SMM
summary: East China aluminium scrap throughput in Linyi rose 43% WoW to 14,200 mt, while spot A00 stayed volatile and fell to 18,770 yuan/mt on Sept 19. Traders shipped more amid Fed rate-hike worries, social ingot inventories eased slightly, and the scrap market is expected to remain oversupplied, bearish for aluminium prices.

title: Imported Nickel in US and EU from Russia Saw Significant Increases _SMM
summary: SMM reports Western countries continued importing nickel from Russia despite sanctions, with US Russian nickel imports rising 70% from March to June and EU up 22%. Russia supplies about 10% of global nickel and Nornickel provides key battery-grade supply. The increased inflows suggest added near-term supply pressure on nickel prices.

title: Canada lags behind world nickel producers, says mining exec
summary: A nickel mining executive says Canada has fallen behind global nickel output and processing is dominated by Indonesia and China. She argues Canada needs many new mines and refineries by 2030 to meet growing battery-driven demand. She also cites U.S. Inflation Reduction Act incentives boosting nickel sulphate eligibility.

title: China Primary Aluminium Net Imports Totalled 43,200 mt in Aug_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s customs data show primary aluminium net imports of 43,200 mt in August 2022, down 0.43% MoM and sharply lower versus a year earlier (-58.9% YoY). Total imports fell to 49,300 mt (down 53.4% YoY) and exports rose to 6,100 mt (+1,365% YoY).

title: China Nickel Ore Imports Fell in Aug despite Expected Restocking ahead of Rainy Season_SMM
summary: China’s nickel ore imports fell in August to 4.34mn mt, below expectations, with laterite ore weaker and total domestic imports down 13.1% YoY. Poor stainless/NPI demand reduced smelter restocking, while weather limited flows from the Philippines and New Caledonia. Imports may rise into the rainy season restocking period.

title: 2022 Phase II Exploration Program Commences  on Come by Chance Copper-Gold Porphyry Target
summary: Belmont Resources began its Phase II 2022 exploration program on the Come By Chance copper-gold porphyry target in southern British Columbia. Ground truthing and geophysical interpretation aim to refine drill targets ahead of a planned drill program before year-end, supported by prior propylitic alteration and pyrite anomalies.

title: Tertiary Minerals announces agreement on Zambia copper projects
summary: Tertiary Minerals announced an agreement with FQM covering exploration interests at Zambia’s Mukai and Mushima North licences. The Mukai area is adjacent to FQM’s Sentinel copper mine and includes an enterprise nickel mine nearby. The parties will collaborate via a technical committee and exchange historical exploration data.

title: Golden Dawn Minerals Inc.: Golden Dawn Commences Drilling On the Phoenix Copper Gold Mine
summary: Golden Dawn Minerals announced it has started drilling at its Phoenix Copper-Gold mine in southeastern British Columbia, targeting VTEM conductivity and magnetic anomalies linked to historic skarn copper-gold mineralization. The news is an exploration update with no production or supply impact, so any copper price effect is likely minimal.

title: Demand worries fuel bearish sentiment at Fastmarkets' International Aluminium Conference
summary: Fastmarkets’ International Aluminium Conference in Barcelona highlighted bearish sentiment and demand worries for the rest of the year. European aluminium P1020 premiums fell to $400–440/t, with additional downside expected. High energy costs have led to smelter cuts (including Hydro and Alcoa) and may squeeze margins and downstream demand.

title: Europe upstages China as main driver for copper outlook
summary: Europe is expected to become the main driver of copper’s outlook as surging gas and power prices (stemming from Russia-linked supply cuts and sanctions) may force higher power consumption cuts. Citi and Macquarie forecast a seasonal surplus and regional demand decline, implying bearish pressure on LME copper toward the winter period.

title: Russian aluminium giant Rusal mulls selling directly on LME - Bloomberg News
summary: Bloomberg reports that Rusal is considering selling aluminium directly on the LME by shipping some metal from Vladivostok to LME warehouses in Asia. Rusal is cautious about large inventory inflows that could depress prices, implying near-term bearish pressure on aluminium if deliveries proceed.

title: Rio Tinto CEO Says Copper Outlook 'Challenged' in Near Term
summary: Rio Tinto’s CEO said the near-term copper outlook is “challenged,” indicating a more difficult near-term balance for copper than previously expected. Such guidance typically weighs on market sentiment and can reduce short-term copper price expectations as traders adjust to potentially weaker conditions.

title: Rio Tinto CEO makes clear that offer is final on giant copper mine
summary: Rio Tinto’s CEO reportedly said its offer for a major copper mine is final, signaling closure on a potential takeover or deal renegotiation. The news may influence near-term expectations for copper supply continuity, but the excerpt provides no operational or timing specifics to gauge a strong price reaction.

title: China's GEM Teams With Aussie Nickel Industries for Raw Materials in Indonesia
summary: China’s GEM, via its QMB unit, partnered with Australia’s Nickel Industries to secure annual limonite laterite ore supply from Hengjaya’s Indonesian mine. The deal aims to back long-term production of battery materials, with yearly pricing agreements, potentially supporting near-term expectations for nickel feedstock tightness.

title: Global Aluminium Production outside China Continued to Increase in August, with Daily Average Output Rebounding from 20-Month Low_SMM
summary: SMM reports IAI data showing ex-China aluminium production increased to 2.22 million tonnes in August. Daily average output outside China rebounded from a 20-month low to 71,480 tonnes. Higher ex-China supply points to potential short-term pressure on aluminium prices as availability rises.

title: FLSmidth A/S: FLSmidth to supply overland conveyor system for a major copper-gold mine in Southeast Asia
summary: FLSmidth will supply a 5km-plus overland conveyor for a major copper-gold mine in Southeast Asia, building on earlier 2022 orders for gearless SAG and ball mills and thickener technology. The project is valued at about DKK 330 million and is designed to cut energy use and OPEX, supporting mine expansion.

title: First Tellurium Plans October Drill Campaign to Investigate Copper Porphyry Target at Deer Horn Property
summary: First Tellurium plans a mid-October drill campaign at its Deer Horn property in British Columbia to investigate the Pond copper porphyry target, following a prior copper porphyry investigation and awaiting new assays. The update is exploration-focused without production or supply changes, making copper price impact likely limited near term.

title: Man charged in theft of valuable copper wire from Athens site
summary: Athens-Clarke police charged a suspect in thefts of copper wiring from an AT&T facility in Athens, recovering nearly 2,000 pounds of wire and citing multiple losses over August and September totaling about $80,000. No forced entry was reported, and cameras later helped identify the suspect.

title: Six things we learned at the 2022 Fastmarkets International Aluminium conference in Barcelona
summary: Fastmarkets conference takeaways were that high European energy costs are driving some aluminium smelter curtailments and weighing on end-user demand, keeping the supply-demand balance fragile. European aluminium premiums have fallen to new 2022 lows, while spot liquidity remains weak, though low warehouse stocks cap downside.

title: Copper Prices Remain Resilient As Uncertainty Persists
summary: The article says copper has remained resilient but highly volatile, trading near resistance after breaching short-term ranges. It attributes swings to smelter shutdowns (notably China), weak European demand from energy strain, rising LME warehouse stocks, a strong U.S. dollar, and core inflation/Fed-hike fears weighing on prices.

title: China Bauxite Imports above 10 million mt again in Aug, Some Indonesian Mines Obtained Extra Export Quotas?_SMM
summary: China imported 10.75 million tonnes of bauxite in August, with Guinea the largest source. Indonesia export-ban uncertainty and some mines receiving extra quotas sustain demand, while supply is not expanding. Bauxite prices have surged (Guinea +28% YTD, Indonesia +21%), implying higher alumina feedstock costs.

title: Both Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventory Fell amid Pre-Holiday Restocking_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s aluminium ingot social inventory fell to 666,000 mt, with declines concentrated in Wuxi, Nanhai and Hangzhou. Arrivals were limited by pandemic-related rail restrictions, and Nanhai dropped on Yunnan production cuts. Billet inventory also declined, supported by pre-holiday restocking, likely keeping supply tight next week.

title: China Aluminium Extrusion Exports Fell for Third Month in a Row in Aug_SMM
