Nickel briquette prices declined and the economics of in-house dissolution deteriorated, limiting buying interest.

title: C3 Metals Inc.: C3 Metals Expands Epithermal Gold-Copper Vein System by 1.5 Kilometres at Arthurs Seat, Jamaica
summary: C3 Metals reports expanding the Arthurs Seat epithermal gold-copper vein swarm in Jamaica by 1.5 km east, with rock chips assaying up to 11.1% Cu alongside high gold and silver. A drill permit application is progressing and drilling is planned after permits, but this remains early-stage exploration.

title: Murchison Minerals Ltd.: Murchison Expands BDF Zone; Intersects Shallow High-Grade Nickel-Sulphide Mineralization Including 3.67 m Estimated at 3.74% pXRF NiEq or 11.14% pXRF CuEq
summary: Murchison Minerals reports additional drill intersections at its Barre de Fer project, expanding near-surface nickel-copper(-cobalt) sulphide mineralization. Highlighted pXRF results include metres of high-grade NiEq/CuEq and deeper/greater modelled zones. Exploration progress can modestly support expectations for future nickel and copper supply.

title: Russian copper builds up in LME warehouses -sources
summary: Sources say Russian copper is accumulating in LME warehouses, suggesting inventory builds. Additional near-term stock availability can reduce tightness in the physical market, typically pressuring copper prices downward over the following days as traders adjust expectations for prompt availability and deliverable supply.

title: Solis Minerals Ltd.: Solis Minerals: Project Tenements Granted at Cinto
summary: Solis Minerals reports granted tenements for its Cinto copper project and highlights ongoing remote-sensing and field work at Ilo Este and Ilo Norte in Peru’s copper belt near the Toquepala mine. The company plans mapping, sampling, and drill permitting, with no immediate production changes.

title: Russian Copper Builds Up In LME Warehouses -sources
summary: Russian-origin copper has accumulated in LME warehouses in Germany, the Netherlands and Taiwan since mid-September, with stocks rising sharply. Some consumers reportedly reject Russian copper, turning LME storage into a last-resort outlet. LME also discussed possible bans on Russian aluminium, nickel and copper.

title: GM to collaborate with Queensland Pacific Metals for nickel and cobalt supply
summary: GM will invest up to $69 million in Queensland Pacific Metals’ TECH facility to produce nickel and cobalt sulfate for NMC batteries, using nickel sourced via laterite processing. The deal targets secured, cost-competitive supply for GM’s EV ramp, amid recent pressure on nickel sulfate prices.

title: White House Weighs Ban on Russian Aluminum Over Ukraine War Escalation
summary: The article reports that the White House is weighing a ban on Russian aluminum in response to Ukraine-war escalation. Such a restriction could limit Russia’s access to export markets and reduce available supply, increasing expectations of tighter global aluminum availability and supporting prices in the near term.

title: GM Strikes $69M Deal to Source Nickel and Cobalt from Australia
summary: General Motors will invest $69M in Queensland Pacific Metals to secure long-term nickel (and cobalt) supply for Ultium battery cells. The nickel laterite ore will be processed at a TECH project using the DNi process with high acid recycling and no tailings dam. The deal strengthens near-term nickel demand expectations for EV production.

title: U.S. considering complete ban on Russian aluminum -Bloomberg
summary: The Biden administration is weighing an outright ban, punitive tariffs, or sanctions targeting Russian aluminum producer Rusal to respond to Moscow’s escalation in Ukraine. If implemented, reduced Russian supply would likely tighten global availability and boost aluminum prices in the coming days and weeks.

title: Québec Nickel Corp. Adds Third Drill at Its Ducros Ni-Cu-PGE Project, Abitibi Québec
summary: Quebec Nickel Corp. plans to expand drilling activity at its Ducros Ni-Cu-PGE project in Abitibi, Quebec, adding a third drill. The update suggests ongoing progress in exploration for nickel (and related metals), generally supportive for nickel sentiment, though no immediate supply change is stated.

title: Aluminum Price Surges After White House Weighs Ban On Russian Metal
summary: The article headline says aluminium prices are surging after the White House weighs a ban on Russian metal. Such a policy move would likely reduce near-term Russian aluminium availability and increase supply risk, supporting firmer spot pricing over the coming days.

title: Global Nickel Supply Shifts Into Surplus
summary: The piece argues Indonesia’s strong nickel mine output (up 41% YoY in the first seven months of 2022) shifted global supply from deficit to surplus (~29,000 tons). It notes this oversupply, alongside demand destruction fears and a firm U.S. dollar, should pressure nickel prices downward, though liquidity remains low and volatile.

title: Rusal to Meet With LME Over Opposition to Possible Metal Ban
summary: Rusal says it will meet with the LME to oppose a possible metal ban. Because Rusal is a leading aluminium producer, an LME restriction could reduce deliverability or participation in the aluminium market, tightening supply expectations and supporting aluminium prices in the coming days.

title: Biden administration weighs a ban on Russian aluminum in response to Putin's escalation in Ukraine
summary: The Biden administration is considering a total ban or equivalent punitive tariffs/sanctions targeting Russian aluminum after renewed missile strikes on Ukraine. Russia supplies about 10% of U.S. aluminum imports and Rusal is a major producer. Any restriction would likely tighten supply and support higher aluminum prices near term.

title: US Reportedly Considers to Impose Complete Ban on Russian Aluminum
summary: Bloomberg reports the US is considering a complete ban on Russian aluminum, alongside potential tariff increases and sanctions on Rusal. Discussions have been ongoing for weeks. Blocking Russian supply would reduce availability in the near term and likely support higher aluminium prices.

title: U.S. may block Russian aluminum imports -source
summary: Reuters reports the Biden administration is considering restricting Russian aluminum imports, including a possible ban, punitive tariffs, or sanctions on Rusal. The measure is expected to boost global aluminum prices by tightening supply, with no finalized decision yet. Alcoa shares rose and related stocks moved on the news.

title: US May Block Russian Aluminum Imports: Source
summary: The report states the US may block Russian aluminum imports. Such a measure would cut Russian-origin supply entering the US, potentially tightening availability for downstream consumers and helping support aluminum prices in the near term. Copper and nickel are not indicated as directly affected.

title: Overseas Aluminium Smelters Buckled under the Weight of Soaring Energy Prices and Strike_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium production has been constrained as soaring energy prices and strikes led to 1.67 million mt of capacity cuts since August in Europe and North America. The cuts include 1.36 million mt in Europe and 304,000 mt in North America. The market is also concerned about a possible LME ban on Russian metals.

title: Some Copper Scrap Traders Sold Their Goods when Copper Prices Stood High_SMM
summary: SMM reports that copper scrap traders have become more willing to sell their inventory as copper prices have risen and they still maintain a bullish outlook. Downstream scrap users entered and bought selectively, favoring sellers with lower prices, indicating active but price-sensitive demand.

title: Pure Nickel Supply Tightens, and NPI Downstream Demand Robust_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says pure nickel premiums for Jinchuan and NPI-related products rose due to tight supply and active market inquiries. Downstream demand from stainless steel producers and alloy consumers remains robust, while NPI output increases are limited by pandemic impacts and lower-than-expected Indonesia supply. Overall, nickel-chain prices are supported.

title: SMM's Latest Update on China Social Inventory of Aluminium Ingots and Billets as of October 13 _SMM
summary: SMM said China’s social inventories of aluminium ingots fell to 655,000 mt by Oct 13, down from Oct 8, while billet inventories dropped to 97,600 mt. Declines were linked to delayed shipments from Xinjiang and pandemic-related transport disruptions, though rail recovery may raise arrivals later in October.

title: Swedish startup offers reusable nickel metal hydride batteries for renewables storage
summary: Swedish startup Nilar International began manufacturing reusable ReOX nickel metal hydride batteries for renewable energy storage. The company says aging is reversible and capacity can be restored multiple times. Production followed an order from Enequi for 800 batteries, potentially providing incremental nickel demand, though likely at a relatively small scale.

title: Québec Nickel Corp. Adds Third Drill At Ni-Cu-PGE Project In...
summary: Quebec Nickel Corp. reports adding a third drill at its Ni-Cu-PGE project in Quebec’s Abitibi region, expanding work around high-grade results. The update relates to exploration rather than production, so it is unlikely to materially change nickel supply expectations in the next few weeks.

title: OpenGate Capital Combines Extol and Aluminium France Extrusion to Form Aluminium Solutions Group SAS
summary: OpenGate Capital is combining Extol and Aluminium France Extrusion into Aluminium Solutions Group SAS, a major European aluminum extruder, and plans to improve its ESG profile with investments to facilitate recycled materials. The deal increases extrusion scale, but offers no disclosed terms or immediate capacity figures affecting global aluminum balances.

title: Yangshan Copper Premiums Surged to a New High amid the Shortage of Supply_SMM
summary: Yangshan copper premiums rose to new highs (warrants $130–145/mt; bills of lading $117–140/mt) as bonded-zone inventory stayed low and warrant transactions were absent. Overseas shipments fell and South African port strikes hurt logistics, reinforcing a supply deficit. Traders expect premiums to keep rising short term.

title: Copper Road Resources Inc. drills significant intervals of
summary: Copper Road Resources announced results from a 3,000-metre diamond drilling campaign at its Tribag Mine Zone, reporting near-surface copper mineralization continuity and grades in multiple breccia zones. The company plans further exploration and validation work. The update is exploration-focused and unlikely to alter near-term copper supply materially.

title: Aluminum Stocks Boom as Biden Administration Mulls Ban on Russian Metal
summary: Reports say the Biden administration is considering an outright ban, tariff increases, or Rusal-specific sanctions on Russian aluminium imports. U.S. aluminium producers’ stocks jumped on expectations of more domestic business, while officials warn sanctions could raise prices; aluminium reportedly spiked about 7% after the news.

title: VALE MARKS OFFICIAL OPENING OF THE COPPER CLIFF COMPLEX SOUTH MINE PROJECT
summary: Vale Canada officially opened the first phase of its CDN$945 million Copper Cliff Complex South Mine project in Sudbury. The expansion is expected to nearly double ore production and add about 13,000 tonnes/year of copper and 10,000 tonnes/year of contained nickel, supporting supply and regional investment sentiment.

title: Vale announces official opening of $945M Copper Cliff Complex South Mine Project
summary: Vale announced the official opening of its $945M Copper Cliff Complex South Mine Project. The development signals increased copper supply capacity from a major producer. While this may take time to fully impact shipments, it can still weigh on near-term copper price expectations by improving supply outlook.

title: Vale announces official opening of $945M Copper Cliff Complex South Mine Project | iNFOnews
summary: Vale Canada opened the first phase of its $945M Copper Cliff Complex South Project at Sudbury, adding tunnels and ventilation for expanded underground handling. The phase is expected to increase contained production by about 13,000 tonnes/year of copper and 10,000 tonnes/year of nickel, supporting supply expectations.

title: Alcoa calls for U.S. to halt Russian aluminum imports: report
summary: Alcoa urged the White House to halt U.S. imports of Russian aluminum and support sanctions on Russian aluminum, citing Russia’s intensified attacks on Ukraine. The request follows reports that Washington is weighing limits on Rusal’s ability to sell aluminum in the U.S., which could reduce near-term supply.

title: Alcoa asks White House to block U.S. imports of Russian aluminum
summary: Alcoa urged the White House to block U.S. imports of Russian aluminum after Russia’s escalation in Ukraine. Biden’s administration reportedly considered options including restricting Rusal. Alcoa also asked the LME to delist Russian aluminum, arguing it distorts price discovery and supply-demand signals.

title: Material Matters: Oil, Iron Ore, Aluminium & Lead
summary: The piece links an OPEC-driven recession risk to weaker demand across commodities, but focuses on aluminium. It says US sanctions on Russia’s Rusal (via sanctions, tariffs, or a ban) could disrupt supply, citing a prior 2018 sanction-induced 25% aluminium jump and increased upside for prices. Lead and iron ore are discussed but not tracked here.

title: US Mulling Sanctions against Russian Aluminium Could Aggravate Chaos in Global Aluminium Supply_SMM
summary: The US is considering a blanket ban or sanctions on Russian aluminium, including Rusal, potentially blocking imports or restricting warehouse deliveries. Such actions would tighten Western supply amid existing disruptions, with analysts warning of sharp aluminium price increases as Russian volumes reroute to China and other exporters.

title: SMM Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Added 11,500 mt from October 9_SMM
summary: SMM said Chinese copper inventories across major markets rose to 94,200 mt, up 11,500 mt from Oct 9, though south China declined slightly. Downstream firms took a wait-and-see stance as SHFE spreads widened post-holiday, pressuring consumption. Inventories may fall slightly after 2210 delivery, but imports should keep supply supported.

title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zones Dipped 13,600 mt from October 9_SMM
summary: SMM reported copper inventories in China’s domestic bonded zones fell 13,600 mt from Oct 9 to 38,100 mt by Oct 14. The Shanghai and Guangdong bonded zones declined by 11,600 mt and 2,000 mt. Warehouses resumed normal operations and import profits rose, boosting customs declarations and reducing stocks.

title: Operating Rates of Copper Cathode Rod Enterprises Fell Short of Expectations in September due to High Spot Copper Premiums and Holiday Factor  _SMM
summary: SMM survey shows copper cathode rod enterprises’ operating rates averaged 73.84% in September, below expectations, citing high spot copper premiums, weak demand from enamelled wire plants, and maintenance during Mid-Autumn and National Day holidays. After the holidays, a wide SHFE price gap made firms cautious on orders.

title: Nickel Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zones Dropped 400 mt from October 9_SMM
summary: SMM said bonded-zone nickel inventories fell 400 mt to 3,900 mt, including 1,250 mt of nickel briquettes and 2,650 mt of nickel plate. Despite a weaker RMB, spot pure nickel imports still found some profit margins. Demand for briquettes stayed firm due to expected higher nickel sulphate output and bullish stainless steel.

title: Port Inventories of Nickel Ore Added 321,000 wmt Compared with those before the National Day Holiday_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s nickel ore port inventories rose by 321,000 wmt to 7.94 million wmt by Oct 14 versus pre–National Day levels, with Ni content about 62,000 mt. Further arrivals are expected next week (possibly >8 million wmt), after which inventories fall once Philippines rainy season fully starts.

title: After Spate Of Gangster Heists, Chile Boosts Security On Copper Trains
summary: Chilean authorities will add specialized police, air support, and better communications to protect trains carrying copper cargoes after a wave of violent heists. FCAB previously suspended copper shipments, and security is being restored to resume flows amid concerns about further disruptions and theft quantities.

title: After spate of gangster heists, Chile boosts security on copper trains
summary: Chile is boosting police security for copper freight trains after repeated armed heists linked to organized crime. FCAB suspended copper shipments earlier this week, prompting mines to consider alternative routes. Authorities say specialized personnel, air support and better communications will resume protected transport, but theft frequency and violence remain high.

title: Vale opens Copper Cliff Complex South Mine Project in Canada
summary: Vale Canada began the first phase of its C$945m Copper Cliff Complex South Mine Project in Sudbury, adding about 13,000 tonnes of contained copper and 10,000 tonnes of contained nickel per year for Vale’s Copper Cliff operations. The phased launch supports future supply, but immediate market price effects likely limited.

title: Vale Canada opens phase I of Copper Cliff Complex South Mine Project
summary: Vale Canada has inaugurated phase I of its $945m Copper Cliff Complex South Mine Project in Sudbury, expanding underground ore and waste handling and ventilation. The project is expected to nearly double Copper Cliff output, adding about 13,000 tonnes of copper and 10,000 tonnes of contained nickel per annum, supporting supply sentiment.

title: Record European copper premiums as buyers shut out Russia: Andy Home
summary: European copper buyers face record term premiums for 2023 as they self-sanction against Russian metal following UK actions affecting UMMC-linked brands. Aurubis, Codelco and Montanwerke Brixlegg quote much higher premiums amid low visible stocks and potential benchmark concerns. The piece warns Russian copper could redirect to China, affecting regional pricing.

title: Vale opens first phase of $945M copper complex expansion in Sudbury
summary: Vale opened the first phase of a $945 million expansion at its Copper Cliff Complex South Mine in Sudbury, Ont. The initial phase is expected to nearly double some output at the project. As new copper capacity ramps, the news is modestly supportive for copper market expectations.

title: "Two headframes, one mine." Vale opens Copper Cliff South Mine
summary: Vale has officially opened the initial phase of its $945m Copper Cliff Mine South expansion, involving re-opening a dormant mine and rebuilding key shafts and infrastructure. Vale forecasts nearly double output at Copper Cliff, adding about 10,000 tonnes of nickel and 13,000 tonnes of copper annually, supporting low-carbon mineral supply.

title: GM enters collaboration agreement with Queensland Pacific Metals for nickel from Australia | Companies
summary: General Motors invested in Queensland Pacific Metals to secure cost-competitive nickel feedstock for Ultium battery cells. The planned TECH facility will process high-grade nickel laterite ore imported from New Caledonia and produce high-purity nickel and cobalt for EVs, with construction expected to start in 2023.

title: Business News | Railway Minister Inaugurates India's First Aluminium Freight Rake Made from Bhubaneswar
summary: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw inaugurated India’s first aluminium freight rake in Bhubaneswar, built with an all-aluminium superstructure and designed to carry more freight with lower empty-weight. The statement credits collaboration including HINDALCO and says it supports the Make in India programme and local aluminium industry.

title: Aluminium Costs Remained High amid Rising Prebaked Anode and Energy Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports firm electricity costs keeping aluminium smelter costs high. Hydropower costs in Sichuan and Yunnan are expected to rise with the dry season, while prebaked anode prices increased. Smelter full costs edged up and profits expanded as aluminium prices stayed firm, limiting short-term downside.

title: Should the LME Ban Russian Aluminium, How Will the Aluminium Market Be Affected?_SMM
summary: SMM reports the LME is considering limiting or banning new Russian aluminium deliveries after UK sanctions related to UMMC’s co-founder. Russia supplies a meaningful share of global and LME flows, with heavy exports to Europe. If a delivery ban occurs, overseas circulation could tighten and prompt supplier price/output adjustments.

title: Alumina Prices in China and Overseas both Declined, High-Cost Alumina Capacity Began to Withdraw_SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices fell across Chinese regions and overseas in mid-October, with the weighted average index down 16 yuan/mt. Higher costs did not support prices, and weak profitability plus new capacity reduced bargaining power. Pandemic-related transport disruptions and refinery curtailments could further pressure near-term aluminium-linked costs.

title: Short-Term Aluminium Prices to Still Have Upside Room amid Positive Domestic Fundamentals and Overseas Supply Disruptions _SMM
summary: SMM says both SHFE and LME aluminium rose after the holiday as US consideration of a ban on Russian aluminium imports raised supply-shock expectations, while Chinese fundamentals improved. Domestic operating capacity declined, downstream processing rates recovered, orders improved, and social inventories stayed low, supporting further gains in the coming week.

title: Weekly Ratings, Targets, Forecast Changes - 14-10-22
summary: A weekly broker-rating roundup highlights Citi’s view of short-term headwinds for base-metals demand from sluggish China, higher US interest rates and a stronger USD. Citi trims near-term price forecasts for aluminium, copper and nickel (while being comparatively more bearish on copper). Some company ratings are upgraded on valuation, but metal-price expectations lean weaker.

title: India's first aluminium freight rake introduced by Hindalco for Indian Railways; details inside
summary: Hindalco says it has launched India’s first all-aluminium freight rail rakes for Indian Railways. The move supports freight transport modernization and is positioned to deliver carbon savings. By increasing aluminium railcar demand through Hindalco’s deliveries, the news could add modest near-term bullish pressure to aluminium prices.

title: Copper prices subdued as demand uncertainty offsets supply woes
summary: Copper prices were subdued as demand uncertainty from China’s continued zero-COVID curbs and global recession fears offset worries over tight supply. LME and Shanghai copper prices gave back gains. Aluminium and nickel also declined as risk sentiment weakened, despite lower Chile output and tight inventories.

title: Copper prices rise on global supply worries
summary: Copper rose on tightening global supplies: LME/COMEX/ShFE stocks fell and Chilean production dropped sharply. China demand improved at the margin via premiums, but gains were capped by ongoing zero-COVID uncertainty and global recession fears. Aluminium and nickel fell in the same session, showing mixed risk appetite.

title: TCs of Spot Copper Concentrate Continued to Rise amid the Slack Demand from Smelters_SMM
summary: SMM says spot copper concentrate trading stayed sluggish, but the weekly Imported Copper Concentrate Index rose to $86.38/mt. Clean concentrate TCs for smelters moved to about $88–89/mt, while trader-smelter deals were scarce at $81–85/mt. Higher TCs and negotiation dynamics support copper sentiment despite limited transactions.

title: Copper Prices Soared last Week due to the Short Squeeze_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM attributes last week’s copper surge to a stronger US dollar from hotter CPI and Fed expectations, alongside tight copper fundamentals in China: open import window, rising cancelled LME warrants, low inventories, and sharp SHFE backwardation. With spot premiums also seen improving, SMM expects SHFE 2211 copper to rise this week.

title: SHFE Nickel Remained Rrangebound last Week amid Pressure from the Macro Front_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel stayed rangebound, with upside pressure from strong downstream pure nickel demand and occasional drops in stainless steel prices. US CPI and core CPI exceeding expectations weighed on nickel. Chinese refined output was slightly lower MoM, and near-term price outlook for SHFE 2211 is 172,000–192,000 yuan/mt.

title: City installs aluminium instead of copper in bid to curb cable theft
summary: Nelson Mandela Bay’s electricity department is replacing copper cables with cheaper aluminium to deter cable theft and vandalism. Officials report repairing hundreds of street lights daily and arresting cable thieves, while also targeting scrapyards. The substitution is demand-shifting at the city level for copper versus aluminium.

title: City installs aluminium instead of copper in bid to curb cable theft
summary: Nelson Mandela Bay’s electricity department is replacing copper cables with cheaper aluminium to reduce cable theft and vandalism. The city reports ongoing streetlight repairs and arrests of cable thieves, and says aluminium cables are installed higher to deter removal. This may modestly shift demand from copper to aluminium locally.

title: Imports of Nickel Ore May Rise and Remain High Before the Rainy Season _SMM
summary: SMM estimates China’s nickel ore port arrivals rose to 1.27m wmt (Sep 30 week) and 1.69m wmt (Oct 7 week). With the Philippines rainy season approaching, early-purchased ore is arriving now, keeping imports high. Increased NPI demand helped stabilize and lift nickel ore prices.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Added 16,100 mt over the Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM data shows copper inventories across major Chinese markets rose by 16,100 mt to 110,300 mt, with increases in all regions. title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces Completion of Metallurgical Drilling Program for Schaft Creek Project
summary: Copper Fox reports completion of 4,688 meters of metallurgical drilling at its Schaft Creek copper-gold-molybdenum-silver project, aimed at improving geometallurgical data for planned metallurgical testwork. Analytical results are pending. The update is operational but lacks production or market-impacting findings in the near term.

title: Downstream Aluminium Scrap Recyclers Had Higher Demand for Scrap, and Throughput of Aluminium Scrap in Linyi East China Nonferrous Metal Market Increased Significantly_SMM
summary: SMM reports Linyi East China scrap market throughput surged in Oct 10-16, especially aluminium scrap, reaching 19,200 mt (+83.6% WoW). This coincided with rising A00 aluminium prices and improved downstream recycler buying after the holiday. Aluminium supply fell on trader risk concerns, while inventories declined; prices were expected stable this week.

title: Copper subdued as demand uncertainty offsets supply woes
summary: Copper prices were subdued as demand uncertainty outweighed supply woes. LME copper gave up gains and hovered around $7,535/t while inventories fell and Chile production dropped sharply. China’s reiterated zero-COVID stance and recession fears limited upside, with aluminium and nickel also slipping.

title: India's First Aluminium Freight Rake introduced by Ashwini Vaishnaw at Bhubaneswar
summary: India’s Railways Minister inaugurated the first domestically built aluminium freight rake made with Hindalco collaboration. The lighter, corrosion-resistant design is intended to improve payload and reduce maintenance while lowering emissions. The new rake supports incremental aluminium demand through fabrication and purchases, potentially modestly bullish for aluminium prices.

title: JV Article: Element 29 Resources defines first copper-moly resource in mineral-rich Peru
summary: Element 29 Resources reported its first resource estimate for the Elida copper project in Peru, with inferred tonnes grading 0.32% copper and small molybdenum credits, and plans further drilling and metallurgical studies. It also plans to update resources at Flor de Cobre. Overall, it’s copper-positive for sentiment, not a direct near-term supply driver.

title: Aluminium price drops on jump in LME stocks, Russian metal
summary: Benchmark LME aluminium fell about 2.3% as warehouse stocks surged by roughly 65,825 tonnes to 433,025. Traders cited concern that Rusal-linked Russian metal could be delivered into the LME system, distorting prices. Despite ongoing sanctions on some Russian finance, buying Russian metal remains unrestricted.

title: Copper Remains Range-Bound As Bears And Bulls Duke It Out
summary: The piece says copper is range-bound after a rebound, with macro pressure from Fed rate hikes weighing on demand. title: Comex Copper Settles 0.14% Higher at $3.4555 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures for October delivery settled 0.14% higher at $3.4555 per pound, gaining 0.50 cent. The piece summarizes recent trading—up four of six sessions, near-term month-to-date up slightly, and year-to-date still down. No fundamental catalyst is discussed.

title: GM secures nickel supply in Australia
summary: General Motors partnered with Queensland Pacific Metals to secure increased long-term nickel supply for its Ultium battery cells, investing up to $69 million to develop a high-purity battery materials refinery in Australia. The deal supports GM’s EV production ramp and EV tax-credit eligibility, reinforcing contracted demand for nickel.

title: Pure Nickel Price Drop Slowing amid Hindered Release of NPI Output_SMM
summary: SMM says pure nickel price declines in September were mainly driven by macro expectations around Fed hikes, but downside is now slowing. title: Sanctions/Export Highlights [As Of October 13, 2022] - Export Controls & Trade & Investment Sanctions

title: Transactions of Nickel Briquette Performed Well as the Cost Efficiency of Nickel Briquette Improved_SMM
summary: SMM reports higher Jinchuan and NORNICKEL nickel premiums in Shanghai and stable but volatile pure nickel conditions. title: Biden preparing to tank US manufacturing with ban on importation of all Russian aluminum
summary: Biden is reportedly considering an executive order banning imports of Russian aluminium, either via a direct ban, expanded tariffs, or sanctions targeting Rusal. title: Iran's aluminum ingot production surges 23 percent in first ...
summary: The piece says Iran’s aluminum ingot production rose 23% in the first part of the year, indicating increased domestic output. summary: Faraday Copper announced additional drill results from its Copper Creek, Arizona project, including 36.0 metres at 3.02% copper and longer intervals averaging 0.87% copper. The company says mineralization remains open and could expand the resource, feeding into an updated MRE/PEA.

summary: Power Nickel Inc. announced a C$3 million non-brokered private placement of flow-through and non-flow-through units to fund Canadian exploration eligible for a critical mineral tax credit, plus debt settlement and working capital. title: SHFE Copper will still Bear the Possibility of a Short Squeeze amid the Low Inventory in October_SMM
summary: SMM links US CPI and a stronger dollar with softer global growth expectations, while noting LME copper inventories rose to about 140,000 mt and cash-to-3M premiums narrowed before later warrant-related tightening. It expects abundant concentrate supply and steady smelter output, with demand improving for State Grid but not lasting, leaving copper weak-balance and prone to short squeezes.

title: LME and SHFE Nickel Inventories Increased, but may Fall amid the Strong Demand_SMM
summary: SMM data show SHFE and LME nickel inventories have increased from recent lows, with mixed movements across product types. title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Drills 9.0 metres of 2.35% Nickel Including 5.66 metres of 3.02% Nickel at Lappvattnet
summary: Gungnir Resources reported partial results from drill hole LAP22-19 at its Lappvattnet nickel deposit in northern Sweden, including 9.0 metres at 2.35% nickel (with 5.66 metres at 3.02% nickel). The company continues drilling toward 2022/23 resource upgrading with assays pending.

title: Excelsior Mining Corp.: Excelsior Mining Announces Well Stimulation Modelling Results for the Gunnison Copper Project
summary: Excelsior Mining says well-stimulation modeling for its Gunnison Copper Project in Arizona shows pre-existing fractures could be inflated by significant volumes, improving connectivity and copper production. The company expects EPA approval for field trials in Q1 2023, but notes results may differ from modeling.

title: Sumitomo Metal sees global nickel market staying in deficit next year
summary: Sumitomo Metal Mining expects the global nickel market to remain in deficit in 2023 for the third straight year, though the shortfall will narrow due to higher Indonesian NPI supply. Strong demand for batteries and industrial uses should keep prices supported despite improving supply.

title: Canada's top firm reaches out to Baloch people with eye on rich gold, copper deposits
summary: Barrick Gold’s CEO visits Baloch communities regarding the Reko Diq copper-gold mine in Pakistan’s Balochistan. While the company discusses local socio-economic work, the article reiterates separatist opposition and past attacks on regional infrastructure and CPEC-linked projects, implying ongoing operational and development risks for copper.

title: DEEP-SOUTH UPDATES COPPER EXPLORATION PROJECTS IN THE HEART OF THE ZAMBIA COPPER BELT
summary: Deep-South Resources provides an update on exploration programs for three large copper exploration licences in Zambia’s Copper Belt. It describes environmental brief submissions awaiting approval from ZEMA and planned geochemical soil sampling to identify drilling targets. No resources are estimated and no immediate production impact is indicated.

title: Canada Nickel Closes Previously Announced US$10 Million Loan Facility with Auramet International, Inc.
summary: Canada Nickel closed a US$10 million secured loan facility with Auramet to fund post-feasibility permitting and detailed engineering over the winter. The project is focused on nickel-sulphide development at the Crawford Nickel-Cobalt site. The financing improves near-term development prospects, mildly supportive for nickel sentiment.

title: Supply of Pure Nickel was Scarce, but may Increase after the Goods of SHFE 2210 Contract are Released_SMM
summary: SMM reports spot pure nickel supply turned scarce again on Oct 19, lifting NORNICKEL premiums to about 5,000 yuan/mt (+200). Jinchuan premiums averaged 10,250 yuan/mt (flat). Nickel briquette prices rose, but liquidity weakened. Supply may improve after SHFE 2210 contract goods are released.

title: New tests boost US copper potential for American West
summary: American West Metals says new metallurgical tests at its West Desert Utah project show 78% copper recovery from oxide material using traditional sulphuric acid heap leaching, with low acid consumption. The results support improved recoverability and potential low-cost extraction, strengthening near-term sentiment for copper supply prospects.

title: Meridian Mining UK S: Meridian Reports New Trends of Gold and Copper Mineralization at Cabaçal
summary: Meridian Mining UK S reports new drill assays from the Cabaçal gold-copper VMS deposit, including multiple intervals with high-grade copper (e.g., up to 6.2% Cu over 0.7m and 1.9% Cu over 4.8m). The results expand copper-rich trends ahead of a planned 2023 resource update.

title: BHP and Antofagasta uphold yearly outlook for copper production
summary: BHP and Antofagasta kept annual guidance after strong quarterly copper output, including higher volumes from expanded production and improved mine conditions. The piece notes global economic uncertainty has weighed on copper prices, but the maintained outlook and supply growth support expectations for near-term copper availability.

title: Copper pushes lower on fears about inflation, recession
summary: Copper prices fell further as soaring inflation, recession worries and expectations of more rate hikes pressured global demand sentiment, while a stronger dollar weighed on metal prices. LME aluminium also slipped amid additional inflows into approved warehouses and rising inventories. Nickel rose slightly, but the overall tone remains bearish.

title: PETITION FOR FURTHER APPEAL OF NEW MEXICO COPPER CORPORATION'S GROUND WATER DISCHARGE PERMIT DENIEDPOSTED
summary: New Mexico’s Supreme Court denied a petition to further appeal a decision upholding the groundwater discharge permit for New Mexico Copper Corporation’s Copper Flat Mine (DP-1842). With appeals exhausted, the permit remains in effect, lowering regulatory uncertainty for the project and modestly supporting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Federal grant awarded for construction of nickel processing facility in ND's Mercer Co.
summary: North Dakota’s Mercer County will host a $433 million Talon Nickel ore processing and management facility, backed by a $114 million U.S. federal cost-share grant. The plant will process ore from Talon’s Tamarack mine for battery minerals. The policy aims to strengthen domestic supply chains, reducing reliance on foreign nickel sources.

title: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Q3 Earnings Summary
summary: Kaiser Aluminum reported Q3 earnings of $2.5 million (EPS $0.16), versus a loss of -$2.3 million and -$0.14 EPS in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted earnings were $9.6 million or $0.60 per share. Revenue was $749 million, slightly below last year.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: US Battery Supply Chain: Talon Metals Announces Significant Increase to Mineral Resource Estimate at Tamarack Nickel Project
summary: Talon Metals announced a near-doubling of indicated resources at its Tamarack Nickel Project, including a 570% rise in high-grade massive sulphide contained nickel. The update strengthens expectations for future nickel concentrate supply potential from the Tamarack nickel-copper deposit, with limited secondary implications for copper.

title: Federal grant awarded for construction of nickel processing facility in ND's Mercer Co. | The Mighty 790 KFGO
summary: North Dakota’s Mercer County will host Talon Nickel’s $433 million ore processing and management facility, funded partly by a $114 million U.S. grant. The plant will process nickel ore from Talon’s Tamarack mine to support U.S. EV and grid battery supply chains, creating about 150 jobs.

title: Minnesota-based Talon Nickel To Build $433 Ore Processing Plant In N.D.
summary: Talon Nickel will build a $433 million ore processing and management facility in Mercer County, North Dakota, funded in part by $114 million from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. The plant will process raw ore from Talon’s Tamarack nickel mine to support domestic battery mineral supply for EVs and the power grid.

title: Alcoa Posts Surprise Loss as Aluminum Woes Deepen
summary: BNN Bloomberg highlights Alcoa posting a surprise loss as “aluminum woes” deepen. The framing implies continued pressure on aluminium economics—likely reflecting weak pricing or demand—making near-term aluminium sentiment more negative for prices over the coming days.

title: In the News: Supply Chains, Aluminum, Mexico, Green Trade Pact | Sandler, Travis & Rosenberg, P.A.
summary: The piece covers trade and logistics updates. It notes that U.S. shipping costs and port backups have eased, but highlights a key risk: the Biden administration may block Russian aluminum imports, which could boost global aluminium prices and potentially reverse an earlier stance on sanctions’ market effects.

title: Alcoa Calls On US, Allies to Sanction 'Cheating' Russian Metal
summary: Alcoa urged the US and allies to sanction “cheating” Russian metal. Such measures would likely disrupt Russia-linked metal supply or trading, particularly in aluminium markets given Alcoa’s exposure, and therefore could lift near-term aluminium price expectations over the coming days to weeks.

title: WBMS: Global Copper Market Saw a Supply Deficit of 657,000 mt from January to August, 2022_SMM
summary: WBMS reported a 657,000 mt global copper supply deficit in January-August 2022, following a 283,000 mt deficit in 2021. LME stocks rose vs. end-2021, but mine and cathode output increased less than demand (up 4.3% YoY). August balances also show demand above production.

title: SMM Updates on China Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventories as of October 20_SMM
summary: SMM reports China aluminium ingot social inventories at 636,000 mt as of Oct 20, down week-on-week, with transportation disruptions limiting cargo arrivals and Gongyi Railway Station suspending loading/unloading. Aluminium billet inventories also fell to 71,900 mt. Smelter output cuts and unstable logistics tightened supply.

title: Indian-made aluminium wagons enter service
summary: India’s railways put its first rake of aluminium-bodied wagons (61 bottom-discharge cars) into service to improve freight efficiency. The wagons were produced with Hindalco supplying high-strength alloy plates and extrusions. The lighter design and expected CO2 savings support ongoing domestic aluminium demand and modernization of freight transport.

title: MINTO METALS REPORTS 2.20% COPPER OVER 20 METRES TO EXTEND MINTO NORTH; 3.52% COPPER OVER 7.26 METRES AT CU KEEL SOUTH DISCOVERY
summary: Minto Metals reported copper intercepts of 2.20% over 20 metres and 3.52% over 7.26 metres from the Minto North and Cu Keel South discovery areas. The update is copper-focused, indicating promising resource potential, but it is unlikely to materially shift near-term copper prices by itself.

title: Freeport-McMoRan profit more than halves on weak copper prices
summary: Freeport-McMoRan reported a sharp profit drop as recession fears and COVID-19 lockdowns in China pressured copper prices. Reuters notes LME copper has fallen about 30% from March highs and is trading in a $7,200–$8,000 range since late August. Copper production rose year-on-year, but realized prices fell.

title: 'Strikingly Tight' Copper Market Belies Price Drop, Miner Says
summary: The piece centers on a copper market that a miner describes as “strikingly tight,” suggesting supportive near-term supply conditions. The title also notes a concurrent price drop, implying either other offsetting factors or that the tightness signal may not be translating into higher prices immediately.

title: Nearctic Nickel Mines Inc.: Statement of Defense Received from Attorney General of Quebec
summary: Nearctic Nickel Mines Inc. says its Quebec affiliate, Ungava Mineral Exploration, received a Statement of Defense in an ongoing Quebec Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources action. The company notes amendments to a Motion for Damages filed in 2015 and updated in May 2022. No operational or production changes are described.

title: Gravita India climbs ~4% on starting aluminium recycling plant in Senegal
summary: Gravita India’s share price rose after it started an expanded aluminium recycling plant in Senegal. The project cost about Rs3.5 crore, expected to add ~Rs60 crore annual revenue and improve the group’s aluminium sales mix. The plant will process local scrap for die-casting component demand in China, Japan, and Vietnam.

title: Strike Copper Corp. Announces an Exploration Agreement with the Lac La Croix First Nation
summary: Strike Copper Corp. announced an exploration agreement with the Lac La Croix First Nation for its Sungold property near Thunder Bay in Ontario. The deal includes consultation, cultural/heritage protections, and compensatory benefits. The news is supportive of continued copper exploration but lacks details on near-term production or supply impacts.

title: Iran's aluminum output up 22.5% in H1 fiscal year: IMIDRO
summary: Iran’s state metals firm IMIDRO says Iranian aluminum smelters produced 318,091 mt of aluminum ingot in six months to late September, up 22.5% from the prior year. Salco accounted for over 43% of output. Alumina rose only 2% y/y, while bauxite fell.

title: What happens if more buyers refuse metals like aluminum from Russia? The LME doesn't want to find out
summary: Speculation that the U.S. may ban Russian aluminium helped trigger a brief price spike last week. Some buyers have already voluntarily avoided Russian metal, prompting the LME to consider ways to prevent trading distortions from possible stockpiles in its warehouses. Tightened effective supply supports near-term aluminium upside.

title: Sanctions on Russia Aluminum Could Send Ripple Effects Through Global Supply Chains
summary: The piece says sanctions and alleged dumping of Russian aluminum are pressuring the market. It notes LME warehouse stocks jumped, raising concerns about more Russian-origin supply, while global demand is weakening and operational costs are rising, contributing to aluminium price declines this quarter.

title: Aluminium Processing and Raw Material Procurement in Shanxi Were Disturbed by the Pandemic and Environmental Protection Checks_SMM
summary: Environmental inspections in Beijing and its surrounding areas and pandemic-related disruptions in Shanxi have reduced raw-material spot purchases for aluminium processors, causing intermittent production suspensions and order-delivery delays. Transport restrictions limit supply inflows, while aluminium ingot and billet social inventories fell, tightening availability and supporting prices.

title: Copper Prices Pressured on Looming Recession Fears_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports copper is pressured by heightened recession fears after the Fed’s hawkish signals and weakening global PMIs. Offsetting this, supply growth is capped by lower South American output and tight scrap/power rationing, while global inventories are at 20-year lows with high China premiums.

title: DTE Secures $1.85m Contract for its Unique Real-Time Liquid Metal Intelligence Solution With Century Aluminium's Nordural Site to Support New Low-Carbon Products
summary: DTE won a $1.85m contract to install real-time chemical composition analysis on Nordural’s new low-carbon aluminium billet casthouse in Iceland. The system monitors molten aluminium quality to optimize furnace throughput and reduce emissions/energy use. Nordural’s expanded capacity is expected to start in 1Q 2024.

title: China Nonferrous Metal Jumps on USD2.3 Billion Deal to Build Copper Processing Plant in Kazakhstan
summary: Shares of NFC jumped after it signed a USD2.3 billion contract to build a copper processing plant in Kazakhstan for Kaz Minerals’ Baimskaya project. The plant is planned to start construction in December 2023 and open years later, implying limited immediate impact on short-term copper prices.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports up 328,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Chinese nickel ore port inventories rose 328,000 wmt WoW to 8.26 million wmt as NPI plants restocked before the Philippines rainy season. Total nickel content was 65,000 mt. With rainy-season conditions in southern Philippines expected to lift inventories short term, ore prices get some support.

title: Recharge Resources intends to spin-out Canadian nickel project
summary: Recharge Resources plans to spin out its 100% owned Pinchi Lake nickel project in Canada into a new subsidiary, NextCharge Battery Metals Corp., subject to conditions and regulatory approval. The announcement is procedural and does not change near-term output or supply, implying limited immediate impact on nickel prices.

title: EQS-News: Aurubis AG: Decarbonizing production - Aurubis begins test series for the use of blue ammonia in copper rod production Seite 1
summary: Aurubis began a pilot at its Hamburg copper wire rod production site using blue, low-carbon ammonia shipped from the UAE by ADNOC. The company says ammonia can cut natural-gas use for production by up to 20% and supports its decarbonization goals. The project is presented as practically feasible to build a UAE–Germany ammonia value chain.

title: Aurubis tests ammonia for low-carbon copper product output
summary: Aurubis, Europe’s largest copper smelter, is starting tests to use ammonia for low‑carbon copper rod production. A first shipment of blue ammonia arrived at its Hamburg plant. The report indicates an emissions-reduction pilot rather than a near-term change in copper output or supply, limiting near-term price effects.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 2.10% Higher at $3.5230 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures (front-month October) settled at $3.5230/lb, up 2.10% for the week after gaining 7.25 cents per pound. Prices rose for two consecutive weeks and sessions, with the settlement at the highest level since Oct. 5, 2022.

title: Vale CEO says iron ore miner will spin-off copper, nickel unit
summary: Vale CEO Eduardo Bartolomeo said the company may spin off and ring-fence its copper and nickel unit from iron ore, potentially taking the base-metals business public at a later date. He cited strong long-term demand for copper and nickel from EVs and clean-energy infrastructure, but gave no timing.

title: Vale CEO says iron ore miner will spin-off copper, nickel unit
summary: Vale’s CEO said the company will ring-fence its copper and nickel unit from its iron ore business, with an eventual plan to grow the base-metals unit and take it to public markets. The CEO pointed to strong long-term EV/renewables demand for copper and nickel, but offered no near-term timing details.

title: Chilean copper miners' costs hit by inflation, lower output
summary: The article headline says Chilean copper miners are seeing inflation raise operating costs while output falls. For a major global copper supplier, cost inflation and reduced production can tighten short-term supply expectations, increasing downside pressure on copper pricing over the coming days to weeks.

title: Aluminum rebound buoys Alcoa, muting worries on global slowdown
summary: Alcoa, the largest U.S. aluminum producer, reported a quarterly loss amid worries that heavy-industry demand is weakening and had previously warned it was squeezed by higher costs and falling aluminum prices. However, shares rose after a rebound in aluminum prices, offsetting some global slowdown concerns.

title: Silver prices up 1.80 pc, copper rises 0.96 pc: MCX
summary: Silver prices rose 1.80% to Rs 57,670 per kilo on Sunday morning, according to MCXindia.com. The report also notes copper was up 0.96% versus its closing level in the prior session. This signals immediate upward momentum in copper prices.

title: Copper disconnect: The world has a problem as it drives towards net-zero
summary: The piece argues copper is “disconnecting” from net-zero expectations: copper prices have fallen ~30% since March despite lower refined-stock coverage. It cites recession risk, China’s weakening copper-intensive property demand, Europe’s energy/war effects, and a stronger US dollar from higher US rates as reasons for price weakness.

title: TCs of Spot Copper Concentrates were Supported by the Slack Demand from Smelters_SMM
summary: SMM reports slack spot copper concentrate trading as smelters hold sufficient inventories and the market enters a negotiation period for 2023 long-term TCs. Reported TC ranges and weekly concentrate port inventories are cited alongside quarterly copper output updates, but no clear immediate directional price shock is indicated.

title: First Quantum bets on Zambia to address global copper, nickel shortage
summary: First Quantum Minerals says it will apply for new exploration licenses in Zambia late 2022 or early 2023, citing improved business conditions under President Hakainde Hichilema after years of stagnant copper output. The planned exploration targets copper and nickel, aimed at easing global shortages, though timing limits near-term price effects.

title: China's September copper imports up more than 25% on year ago | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: China’s September unmanufactured and semi-finished copper imports rose 25.6% year-on-year to about 510,000 tonnes and increased from August. Reuters attributes the pickup to infrastructure stimulus plans and seasonal demand, alongside supply tightness from lower output and importer liquidity issues, supporting copper prices.

title: Unwrought Aluminium and Aluminium Semis Exports in September Increased 0.8% and That in January-November Increased 27.8%_SMM
summary: China exported 496,000 mt of unwrought aluminium and aluminium semis in September, down 8.22% month-on-month but slightly up 0.8% year-on-year. Cumulative exports in January–September rose 27.8% versus the prior period, according to customs data, implying stronger outward supply flows.

title: Low Inventory and High Cost to Sustain Aluminium Prices at Highs_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME aluminium prices fell on the week, with SHFE at 18,535 yuan/mt and LME near $2,212.5/mt. Supply recovered slightly, but Yunnan power risks persist and COVID disruptions reduced arrivals and social inventories. Consumption was hit by COVID and downstream plant shutdowns, while hawkish Fed views weigh sentiment.

title: Will US Ban on Russian Aluminium Promote China Aluminium Semis Exports?_SMM
summary: Alcoa is reportedly lobbying the Biden administration to curb Russian aluminium imports from Rusal, with options including a full ban, higher tariffs and sanctions. The piece notes that prior Rusal sanctions lifted LME aluminium and increased China aluminium exports. A new ban could tighten supply and support aluminium prices amid mixed demand outlook.

title: High Spot Premiums Greatly Suppressed the Pure Nickel Trading_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that on Oct 24 spot premiums for pure nickel were sharply lower: Jinchuan nickel premiums fell to 8,000–8,500 yuan/mt (down 400). NORNICKEL premiums also declined (down 500). Month-end shipping activity and weaker spot transactions followed prior futures-driven premium spikes.

title: Arrivals of Nickel Ore at Chinese Ports Totalled 752,000 wmt as of October 21_SMM
summary: As of Oct 21, nickel ore arrivals at Chinese ports were 752,000 wmt, down 34% week-on-week. Shipments from the Philippines (Surigao) were constrained by rainy-season weather restrictions. With NPI prices supported by tight short-term supply, ports are likely to see smaller imports going forward, tightening balances.

title: China's Sept Copper Imports Jump On Infrastructure Spending
summary: China’s September unwrought and copper-product imports rose 25.6% year-on-year as local governments and power utilities ramped infrastructure spending to counter economic slowdown. Lower prices and favorable import parity encouraged buying, while tighter domestic supply from power curbs and liquidity issues at Maike Group reinforced support for copper demand.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices Declined After Rising amid the Pandemic Outbreak in Many Places_SMM
summary: SHFE nickel prices fell after an earlier rise. Pandemic-related transport restrictions delayed spot pure nickel arrivals. NPI shipments in October were steady and inventories eased, while Indonesia NPI supply was tight with high prices. Despite rising stainless steel demand, nickel is expected to trade volatile this week.

title: Nickel Ore Shipments from the Philippines will be Restricted by the Rainy Season_SMM
summary: SMM reports September 2022 China nickel ore imports rose, but port inventory is only slightly higher and the market remains tight. With the Philippines rainy season approaching, nickel ore shipments face weather restrictions, likely reducing laterite nickel ore imports. The article expects imports to trend downward during the rainy season.

title: Rusal accuses Potanin of breaching Nornickel shareholder pact
summary: Rusal filed a London lawsuit alleging Norilsk Nickel CEO Vladimir Potanin breached a decade-old shareholder pact that was meant to protect Nornickel’s dividend formula. The dispute renews tension between Rusal and Potanin-controlled Interros, with the agreement set to expire and merger talks postponed.

title: China's Primary Aluminium Imports Rose 31.13% MoM in September, with Russia Being the Top Supplier _SMM
summary: China’s primary aluminium imports rose 31.13% month-on-month to 64,685.05 mt in September, though they fell year-on-year. Russia supplied the most, with imports of 45,666.12 mt, up 8.79% month-on-month and 447.23% year-on-year, indicating stronger near-term inbound supply.

title: China's September Bauxite Imports down 23.57% MoM, with Guinea Being Top Supplier _SMM
summary: China’s September bauxite imports fell to 8.21 million mt, down 23.57% month-on-month. Guinea remained the top supplier, with volumes from Guinea at 4.15 million mt, down 33.7% MoM. The decline suggests reduced upstream raw material inflows for China’s alumina/aluminium sector.

title: 400,000-mt High-Purity Copper Cathode Clean Production Project Led by Daye Nonferrous Metals Now in Production_SMM
summary: SMM reports that Daye Nonferrous (Yangxin Hongsheng Copper) began operations on a 400,000 mt high-purity copper cathode clean production project on Oct 23, 2022. The $8.7 billion investment uses a double-flash smelting process and is running smoothly, adding copper cathode supply capacity in China.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Phase 3 Drilling Preliminary Results: Confirms New Large-Scale Nickel Zone at CarLang
summary: EV Nickel reported initial assay results from four holes of Phase 3 drilling at its Shaw Dome CarLang A Zone, confirming thick dunite-hosted, large-scale nickel mineralization (e.g., 297 m at 0.25% Ni and 201 m at 0.22% Ni). Remaining assays are pending and expected over coming weeks.

title: Net-zero: Copper disconnect a problem in world's drive to emissions target
summary: An opinion piece argues there is a disconnect between net-zero copper expectations and current market pricing. Copper has fallen ~30% since March even as refined inventories drop to very low days of consumption. It attributes weakness to recession fears, China’s property slump, Europe’s energy shock, war and a stronger USD.

title: The Fiji Times » China's September copper imports up more than 25% on year ago
summary: China’s September unwrought and copper product imports rose 25.6% year-on-year to 509,954.1 tonnes, up from August. The report links stronger demand hopes to planned infrastructure spending and stimulus, plus supply tightness from summer power curbs and importer liquidity issues, supporting a bullish outlook for copper prices.

title: Copper Buyers Want Longer-Term Deals on Supply Concerns, Codelco Says
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports that copper buyers are pushing for longer-term supply agreements as Codelco points to ongoing supply concerns. The emphasis on securing future material points to tighter near-term availability expectations, which typically supports copper pricing in the coming days to weeks.

title: Los Andes Copper on track to deliver Vizcachitas prefeasibility by year-end, says CEO
summary: Los Andes Copper says it is working to publish a pre-feasibility study for the Vizcachitas porphyry copper-molybdenum project by year-end while preparing to restart drilling. The planned advancement suggests continued development momentum for future copper supply, which can provide modest bullish sentiment.

title: The Fiji Times » China Sept aluminium output rises 9.3% y/y as power restrictions ease
summary: China’s primary aluminium output rose 9.3% y/y in September to 3.42 million tonnes after authorities relaxed power restrictions for smelters. Production was still down 2.5% month-on-month because Yunnan cut power from Sept. 10 due to tight hydropower. Overall supply trends point to bearish near-term price pressure for aluminium.

title: Cash-for-copper trade grinds to a halt
summary: The report says cash-for-copper trading has “grinded to a halt” around Shanghai’s free-trade zone warehouses that historically anchor global physical copper pricing. It notes traders track flows in and out of the bonded copper stockpile, implying liquidity/physical exchange conditions are deteriorating, but no specific price impact mechanism is stated.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.23% Lower at $3.4795 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for October delivery settled 1.23% lower at $3.4795 per pound, losing 4.35 cents. The move snapped a two-session winning streak. The contract remains down from recent highs and slightly up month-to-date, signaling near-term bearish price pressure for copper.

title: Resurging Pandemic in Henan Pressures Shipment of Secondary Aluminium Enterprises_SMM
summary: A resurgence of COVID in Henan is disrupting secondary aluminium (remelted billets/ADC12) producers. Lockdowns and transport restrictions delay shipments, increase freight costs, and limit access to aluminium scrap/raw materials, narrowing margins and reducing production or output. Firms are generally bearish on near-term downstream order recovery.

title: Copper falls as Chinese yuan weakens further against dollar
summary: Copper fell on Tuesday on the LME after the Chinese yuan weakened further against the dollar. A weaker yuan makes dollar-priced commodities costlier for China, the largest copper consumer. Three-month LME copper dropped about 0.5% to around $7,516/t as the market adjusted to FX-driven demand concerns.

title: Supply of Spot Jinchuan Nickel is Tight and Decline in Premiums is Limited_SMM
summary: SMM says spot Jinchuan nickel premiums averaged 8,250 yuan/mt, staying flat, while NORNICKEL premiums fell. Although pure nickel premiums continue to drop, spot Jinchuan supply is generally tight in October and the premium decline is limited due to severe pandemic conditions. Nickel briquette prices rose slightly, but trades were weak.

title: CME Group and Marex to Expand Client Access to CME Group Aluminum Futures
summary: CME Group and Marex will expand clients’ access to CME’s base metals markets, starting with CME COMEX Aluminum futures, offered on Marex’s Neon Metals platform. CME cites rising aluminum futures volumes and record open interest. The move is aimed at improving market access and risk management rather than changing fundamentals.

title: Johor Customs foils bid to smuggle nearly 74,000kg of aluminium scraps
summary: Johor Customs in Malaysia stopped a shipping company from exporting about 73,696kg of aluminium scrap in three containers. The shipment, valued at RM819,000, included export duties. The seizure removes a small but immediate amount of aluminium scrap from outgoing trade flows, which can modestly support prices.

title: Falcon Gold Corp: Falcon Increases Land Position by 70% at HSP South, Nickel-Copper-Cobalt-Project Next to Go Metals, Quebec
summary: Falcon Gold expands its HSP South project by staking additional claims, increasing its land position by 70% in Havre St. Pierre’s anorthosite complex. The area is described as newly recognized nickel source and contiguous to Go Metals’ recent nickel-and-copper sulphide discovery, with airborne surveys planned.

title: Falcon Gold Corp: Falcon Increases Land Position by 70% at HSP South, Nickel-Copper-Cobalt-Project Next to Go Metals, Quebec
summary: Falcon Gold reported a 70% increase in its land position at the HSP South property in Quebec, adjacent to Go Metals’ drilling and discovery of wide intervals of nickel and copper sulphides. Falcon plans airborne EM surveys and expanded staking across prospective contact, potentially boosting near-term sentiment for nickel and copper.

title: Delfzijl aluminium smelter hit by high energy prices, seeks new money
summary: Aldel’s aluminium smelter in Delfzijl has been granted creditor protection while seeking new financing after shutting down due to high energy prices and lack of government support. It previously stopped processing imported aluminium, and since then has remained in care-and-maintenance, prompting curators to find a buyer.

title: Throughput of Aluminium Scrap Drops Slightly due to the Pandemic Control Measure_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium scrap throughput in Linyi, Shandong fell 11.8% WoW to about 16,900 mt as pandemic controls disrupted logistics. Secondary producer operating rates rose only slightly and Linyi market was shut temporarily. Spot A00 aluminium prices dipped and SHFE aluminium (2211) weakened, indicating bearish near-term aluminium pressure.

title: Clearance Volume of Pure Nickel Grow 11% MoM in September amid the Better Demand_SMM
summary: SMM cites customs data showing China’s clearance volume of pure/nickel-related products rose about 11% MoM in September while remaining low YoY. Imports of nickel briquettes and powder jumped MoM, attributed to higher nickel sulphate demand for ternary precursors. Output and bonded inventories should stay supportive into October.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28 Releases Ramu Q3 2022 Operating Performance
summary: Nickel 28 reported Q3 2022 operating performance from its Ramu nickel-cobalt JV in Papua New Guinea, including higher contained nickel production and substantially higher nickel sales. It discusses earthquake-related curtailment and cash-cost impacts from input commodity pricing that is reportedly easing, which affects short-term nickel sentiment.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Reports Shallow High-Grade Copper-Gold Intercepts Within the Alacran Deposit at Its 100%-Owned San Matias Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals reported shallow high-grade copper (0.69–0.74% Cu over 152–175 m) from infill drilling at its San Matias Alacran deposit in Colombia, with copper-gold-silver intercepts to be included in an updated mineral resource estimate. The update is sentiment-supportive but not near-term production-changing.

title: Aluminium Supply Still Expected to Decline Despite Falling Alumina Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports falling aluminium spot prices with low south China arrivals, firm spot premiums, and improving inventory only slightly after a recent LME surge. Demand is weak as PMI signals deteriorate and processing rates decline. Yunnan power shortage could reduce output; alumina prices fall, weakening cost support, while high energy costs keep aluminium rangebound.

title: Nickel processing plant moving to ND because of environmental, tribal concerns in MN
summary: Talon Metals plans to move components of its proposed Tamarack, Minnesota nickel processing plant to North Dakota to address environmental and tribal concerns. The company says this reduces land disturbance and permitting scope. The project remains focused on nickel and has a $114 million DOE grant, but no production change is specified.

title: Elemental Altus Royalties Corp.: Elemental Altus Divests Copper Subsidiary, Generates 16 New Royalties
summary: Elemental Altus completed the sale of its Morocco-focused copper subsidiary Aterian Resources to Eastinco, generating a 2.5% NSR royalty over 15 copper-focused projects. The company also received Eastinco shares and warrants, retaining 25% equity exposure. The release is mainly a royalty/corporate transaction with indirect copper impact.

title: Battery Makers Can't Escape Rising Nickel Costs
summary: Battery OEMs are facing rising nickel costs as supply terms have shifted from fixed long-term off-takes to spot pricing for nickel salts. The piece cites nickel-salt premiums over LME nickel and a move toward lower-grade intermediates, increasing input cost volatility and exposure for manufacturers.

title: Nickel North Exploration Corp.: Nickel North Confirms High-Grade Ni-Cu Sulfide Mineralization up to 400m Long at Gamma Zone and Grants Stock Options
summary: Nickel North Exploration reports 2022 sampling and backpack drilling confirming high-grade, up to 400m-long Ni-Cu sulfide mineralization at the Hawk Ridge Project’s Gamma Zone in Northern Quebec. Reported intercepts and outcrop/backpack results include strong nickel and copper grades, supporting further 2023 drilling plans.

title: Nanadie Well drilling returns broad copper-nickel-PGE zones for Cyprium Metals
summary: Cyprium Metals’ reverse-circulation drilling at the Nanadie Well project in Western Australia intersected broad anomalous copper-nickel-PGE zones, including multiple strong copper intervals and sections with meaningful nickel. The company plans follow-up work to test an expanded 1.6 km corridor, improving sentiment for future supply.

title: Weekly Throughput of Copper Scrap Declined Under Influence of Multiple Factors_SMM
summary: SMM says East China copper scrap throughput fell 6.7% in Oct 17–23, with pandemic-driven lower secondary rod operating rates and weaker shipments. Cathode and scrap prices also declined slightly WoW. SMM forecasts a steeper drop in Oct 24–30 due to a Linyi lockdown, while scrap remains tight and imports limited.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices are High, and Spot Transactions are Thin_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that on Oct 26 Jinchuan nickel premium fell to 8,000 yuan/mt (down 250) and NORNICKEL premium to around 2,400 yuan/mt (down 500). Despite active near-month SHFE contract shifting, spot premiums declined, while thin spot trading and higher nickel briquette prices weakened deal activity.

title: Spot Nickel Premiums Resilient on Supply Tightness_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports resilient Jinchuan nickel spot premiums in October amid supply tightness, with imports pressured by a weaker SHFE/LME ratio. Nickel demand remains supported by downstream stainless steel, and low inventory is cited. For NPI, demand is robust and the market expects slight short-term upward room, unless Indonesian flows surge.

title: Reasons for Huge Fluctuations in Spot Copper Premiums in Shanghai_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai #1 copper spot premiums fell nearly 50% to 425 yuan/mt in two days. The decline is linked to eased warehouse congestion, weaker downstream demand after rising copper prices, wider cathode-scrap spreads shifting purchases to secondary material, more imported copper entering, and warrant drawdowns after SHFE 2210 delivery.

title: SHFE Nickel Rise for Three Consecutive Days amid Low Inventory_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel rising for a third consecutive day (+1.35%) with spot refined nickel up to about 195,050 yuan/mt. Tight Jinchuan supply, limited premium declines, weaker import economics, relatively strong NPI demand, low inventories, and supportive stainless-steel demand should limit downside.

title: T2 Metals Corp.: T2 Metals Receives Drill Permit for the Lida Copper
summary: T2 Metals received a permit from the Bureau of Land Management to construct five drill sites and begin drilling at its Lida copper-silver project in Nevada. The company describes high-grade copper oxide/carbonate mineralization and strong IP anomalies, aiming to advance toward potential economic skarn-style mineralization.

title: Clean Air Metals Reports Drill Results including 10m grading 3.31g/t Platinum, 3.16g/t Palladium, 0.61% Copper and 0.43% Nickel in Hole CLM22-058; Advances Prefeasibility Study at Thunder Bay North
summary: Clean Air Metals reported infill drill results at its Thunder Bay North PGE-Cu-Ni project, including copper (0.61%) and nickel (0.43%) in a 10m interval, and said it is advancing prefeasibility engineering and metallurgical testing. The update is exploration-focused with no immediate production or supply disruption signals.

title: Clean Air Metals Reports Drill Results including 10m grading 3.31g/t Platinum, 3.16g/t Palladium, 0.61% Copper and 0.43% Nickel in Hole CLM22-058; Advances Prefeasibility Study at Thunder Bay North
summary: Clean Air Metals reported 2022 drill results from its Thunder Bay North Current deposit, including 10.0m grading 0.61% copper and 0.43% nickel, and said it is advancing a prefeasibility study with metallurgical optimization and resource validation. The update may support longer-term supply expectations, but no immediate production impact is cited.

title: Traders Bet Big in Aluminum Options as LME Weighs Russia Ban
summary: Traders are reportedly placing large bets in aluminum options as the LME considers imposing a Russia-related ban. The market implication is tighter near-term aluminum availability and increased risk of supply disruption, which typically pushes expectations for higher aluminum prices in the following days.

title: Copper Miner Freeport Is in Talks to Buy Arizona Smelter
summary: The article headline says copper miner Freeport is in talks to buy an Arizona smelter. If the deal progresses, it could expand or secure copper refining capacity, improving expectations for treatment and concentrate processing and near-term copper supply availability, generally supportive for copper prices.

title: SMM Review and Analysis of China Aluminium Extrusion Import and Export in the First Three Quarters of 2022_SMM
summary: SMM reports China aluminium extrusion imports rose 12.4% YoY in Jan–Sep 2022, driven by higher inflows from Taiwan, while exports rose slightly 2.57% despite anti-dumping actions. Europe’s energy crisis and a low SHFE/LME ratio supported exports, but later rate hikes and weaker demand pressured shipments.

title: SMM Updates on China Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventories as of October 27_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s aluminium ingot social inventories were 621,000 mt, slightly down WoW, but sluggish transactions and transport disruptions led to local accumulation, with more arrivals expected after Gongyi railway restores. Aluminium billet inventories fell WoW to 55,800 mt due to reduced arrivals from logistics issues and Yunnan smelter cuts, but SMM expects inventory growth once controls ease.

title: Osisko Metals Reports Additional Infill Drill Results at Gaspé Copper Including 102.0 m of 0.57% Copper and 2.20 gpt Silver
summary: Osisko Metals reported additional infill drill results at its Gaspé copper project, including 102.0 m of 0.57% copper and associated silver grades. Updated drilling information can support the resource outlook and future development expectations, which may modestly underpin copper sentiment, though no immediate production or supply disruption is indicated.

title: Freeport in early discussions to extend copper mine rights in Indonesia
summary: Freeport-McMoRan says it is in early talks with Indonesia to extend Grasberg mine operating rights beyond 2041. The Grasberg district is a major copper source, and extending permits would lower long-run supply disruption risk. Freeport is also building a smelter and expanding the mine in Indonesia.

title: New Research Shows Tariffs on Aluminum Have Cost the U.S. Beverage Industry $1.7 Billion
summary: A study for the Beer Institute says Section 232 aluminum tariffs since March 2018 have cost the U.S. beverage industry $1.714 billion on 8.203 million metric tons of aluminum, largely charged through end-user pricing by mills and smelters. Brewers use aluminum heavily for cans, and the report urges tariff relief.

title: New Research Shows Tariffs on Aluminum Have Cost the U.S.
summary: Research for the Beer Institute estimates U.S. beverage producers paid $1.714 billion in Section 232 aluminum tariffs between 2018 and August 2022. It argues rolling mills and smelters pass through tariff-burdened costs to brewers, raising production costs even when specific shipments are not tariffed.

title: Nickel mine could open in Minnesota amid rising electric vehicle demand, raising concerns: "It's going to devastate the land"
summary: Talon Metals is advancing the Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project in Minnesota to supply nickel for electric-vehicle batteries, citing test results and a Tesla supply deal. Local groups raise concerns about wetlands and potential runoff, but the company says processing occurs out of state. The prospect supports nickel sentiment more than near-term supply.

title: Midland and Soquem Announce New Results on Their Recent Copper-Gold Discovery in Nunavik
summary: Midland and Soquem announced new results from their recent copper-gold discovery in Nunavik. Updated exploration outcomes can strengthen confidence in potential copper resources, which may translate into near-term support for copper prices if investors perceive improved supply prospects. Gold relevance is not assessed here.

title: Sinkhole at Lundin's Chilean mine set to impact copper output
summary: A sinkhole at Lundin’s Chilean mine is expected to disrupt operations and reduce copper output. The outage could tighten near-term supply expectations for copper, potentially weighing on prices over the coming days as markets adjust to the production loss and related logistics or repair timing risks.

title: Nevada Copper restart financing may close Oct. 28
summary: The headline indicates that financing for restarting Nevada Copper could be finalized by Oct. 28. A restart typically increases expected copper supply from the mine, which can reduce tightness and pressure copper prices in the near term, depending on the timing and likelihood of actual restart.

title: Sinkhole at Lundin's Chilean mine to impact copper output
summary: A sinkhole at Lundin’s Chilean mine is expected to disrupt operations and reduce copper output. The immediate effect is lower near-term supply from the site, which can tighten market availability in coming days and weeks and generally exerts downward pressure on copper prices.

title: Roughly 228,000 mt/Year of Aluminium Capacity Will Have Been Commissioned through Capacity Replacement by the End of 2022_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s tightening aluminium capacity-approval regime has encouraged smelters to secure or trade quotas to commission new projects. It highlights Shanxi Zhongrun’s 65,000 mt/year capacity replacement project scheduled for December. Overall, 228,000 mt/year of aluminium capacity is expected to be commissioned in the year through replacements.

title: SHFE Nickel Fall in Early Trading and Spot Transactions Perform Well_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel fell in early trading. In the spot market on Oct 28, Jinchuan nickel premiums averaged 6,250 yuan/mt, down 400 yuan/mt, while NORNICKEL premiums averaged 1,550 yuan/mt, down 350 yuan/mt. Spot supply rose and shipments increased; nickel briquette prices also dropped as demand remained weak.

title: Glencore 9-month Own Sourced Copper Production Down 14%
summary: Glencore said its own-sourced copper production for the first nine months fell 14% to 770,500 tonnes versus the prior year. The decline was attributed to land access, geotechnical and processing constraints at Katanga, basis changes after a sale, and lower ore mined at Collahuasi, reducing copper units.

title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zones Dip 4,800 mt from October 21_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s copper inventories in domestic bonded zones fell 4,800 mt from Oct 21 to 29,700 mt as of Oct 28, with Shanghai and Guangdong declines. Limited arrivals of imported copper and importers shifting stock from bonded warehouses to the domestic market amid low social inventories support a tighter supply outlook.
