He cited that 98.8% of copper and 87% of aluminium are exported abroad due to lack of available domestic inputs, prompting concern from processing enterprises.

title: Teck's new CEO looks to tap cash from coal to fuel copper expansion
summary: Teck’s new CEO is looking to generate and redeploy cash from coal to fund copper expansion. The announcement is relevant to copper supply expectations through changes in investment priorities, but it is unlikely to materially affect near-term (days to weeks) physical supply or inventories.

title: Copper retreats on worries over China demand, rate hikes
summary: Copper fell on the LME and Comex as concerns grew that China’s economy will weaken due to spreading COVID cases and ongoing factory curbs. Uncertainty over whether the Fed and other central banks will slow rate hikes added pressure. The same macro concerns weighed on aluminium and nickel.

title: Indonesia appeals WTO ruling in nickel dispute against EU
summary: Indonesia has appealed a WTO ruling that backed the EU in a dispute over Jakarta’s ban on nickel ore exports and related domestic processing requirements. The EU argued Indonesia’s restrictions harmed its stainless-steel industry, while Indonesia banned nickel ore exports from early 2020. The appeal could prolong uncertainty over supply restrictions.

title: Glencore and MMG copper mines ride out unrest as Peru promises early polls
summary: Unrest in Peru has threatened planned strikes and disruptions at copper mines operated by Glencore and China-controlled MMG. After President Dina Boluarte promised elections two years early in 2024, it was unclear whether protesters would back down. Easing unrest would support short-term copper supply expectations.

title: Bauxite Imports Added 9.27% Mom In October, and Some New Suppliers Emerged  _SMM
summary: China imported 8.98m mt of bauxite in October, up 9.27% month-on-month. Shipments rose from Guinea and Australia, with improved Guinea weather aiding output and traffic. Australia volumes increased on higher demand and better cost efficiency. New suppliers also emerged, supporting alumina feedstock availability.

title: Copper buoyed by China property shares, but COVID woes weigh
summary: London copper edged up 0.2% to $8,393/tonne, supported by China property shares and data on weekly new home sales. However, surging COVID-19 infections raise concerns about manufacturing disruption. SHFE January copper fell. Peru protests near Las Bambas add supply uncertainty as markets watch central banks.

title: SMM Forecast: Alumina Prices Bottomed out in November, to Trend Higher in the Short Term _SMM
summary: SMM reports alumina prices have bottomed in November and are expected to trend higher in the short term. Output was curtailed by heating-season pollution warnings and refinery shutdowns/equipment issues, while logistics disruptions tightened supply. With limited arbitrage and improving trade activity, alumina prices are projected to edge up.

title: Aluminium Prices i December Will Rise First and then Drop amid Bullish Macro Policies in China and the Off-Season _SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME aluminium prices edged higher in late November and expects December to be supported by China’s property/policy stimulus, easing COVID controls, a weaker US dollar, and low aluminium inventories. However, rising domestic capacity and off-season demand are expected to pressure prices later, implying a rise first, then fall.

title: Copper Prices to still have Upward Momentum amid Favourable Policies in China and Low Global Copper Inventory_SMM
summary: SMM says copper prices should maintain upward momentum as dovish Fed expectations weaken the dollar and China loosens COVID and supports real estate. Fundamentals remain supportive: copper concentrate TCs/RCs rose, domestic and LME inventories fell to tight levels with higher cancelled warrants. Off-season demand risks limit upside but do not negate bullish tone.

title: Indonesia Appeals WTO Ruling on Nickel Ore Export Ban Dispute
summary: Indonesia has appealed a WTO ruling related to a dispute over its nickel ore export ban. The appeal keeps uncertainty around whether and when export restrictions will change, which can alter near-term nickel ore supply flows to refiners and thereby influence nickel price expectations over coming days to weeks.

title: Capella Provides Exploration Update for the Løkken Copper Project, Norway
summary: Capella Minerals provided an exploration update for its Løkken copper-cobalt project in Norway, highlighting ground surveys, soil geochemistry, and a drill-ready Åmot target with permits issued. Work focuses on advancing drill targeting around the former Løkken mine; no production or supply changes are reported.

title: ERG, Gécamines restart copper-cobalt producer Boss Mining at time of market weakness
summary: ERG and Gécamines are restarting the Boss Mining operation in the DRC, producing copper cathodes and cobalt hydroxide. The phased restart adds copper supply (around 1,800 tonnes/month) as demand—especially in related end-use sectors—is described as weak, reinforcing near-term price pressure.

title: Angkor Confirms 108 Metres of 0.53% Copper Equivalent at Andong Bor, Cambodia
summary: Angkor Resources announced assay results from core samples at its Andong Bor copper/gold license in western Cambodia. Two 2016 drill intervals reportedly grade 0.53% copper equivalent over 108 metres and 0.51% over 46 metres, indicating a robust porphyry copper system and potential for larger scale follow-up exploration.

title: Lion Copper and Gold Corp. Announces Positive Mason Valley Exploration Results
summary: Lion Copper and Gold reported positive assay results from trenching at its Mason Pass copper oxide prospect in Nevada, including multiple intervals averaging up to 0.28% TCu and bedrock zones with copper oxide veins. The company says mineralization remains open and will consider further exploration to expand targets at depth and laterally.

title: Copper rises on weaker dollar; China COVID woes persist
summary: Copper edged higher on the LME after the U.S. dollar weakened following softer-than-expected U.S. inflation. China’s reopening raises short-term COVID infection risks that could hurt industrial recovery, with a falling spot premium suggesting weaker demand. Still, the article reports copper up versus prior levels.

title: Metso Outotec Oyj : receives orders for four copper anode casting shops
summary: Metso Outotec said it received orders worth about EUR 18 million for four copper anode casting shop projects from major copper producers in the USA, China and Africa. The equipment supports the casting of copper anodes used in smelting, and is booked in Q4 orders received.

title: Nickel Ore Prices still Supported by Low Arrivals at Ports Despite Sluggish Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports that mid- and high-grade nickel ore prices rose slightly in November on low arrivals and scarce supply, partly offset by lower ocean freight. However, poor demand and falling NPI prices have weakened momentum. For December, SMM expects nickel ore prices to fall slightly, with Ni 1.5% ranging $70–75/wmt.

title: Orion secures $87m for South African copper-zinc mine
summary: Orion Minerals secured an $87m funding package (including a precious-metals stream) to advance development of its Prieska copper-zinc mine in South Africa. Funds will support feasibility work and commissioning of dewatering and water-treatment systems, subject to approvals and additional financing conditions.

title: Peru Copper Mine Running Out of Storage Space in Threat to Production
summary: A report says a Peruvian copper mine is running out of storage space, creating a risk to continued operations. If stockpiles cannot be handled and production is curtailed, near-term copper supply expectations may weaken, likely weighing on copper prices over the coming days.

title: Billionaire-backed KoBold Metals to invest in Zambia copper mine
summary: KoBold Metals will invest $150 million to develop the Mingomba copper project in Zambia, a deposit described as high-grade and among top-tier potential mines. The deal with EMR Capital and ZCCM-IH supports Zambia’s push to raise copper output, which can bolster copper sentiment near term.

title: Pan Global Expands La Romana Deposit and Intersects 3.9 Meters of 1.04% Copper and 5.2 g/t Silver in New Upper Horizon
summary: Pan Global reported assay results from 14 drill holes at its Escacena Project in Spain, expanding La Romana near-surface copper mineralization and identifying a new copper horizon (e.g., 3.9m at 1.04% Cu). The update is exploration-focused, with no stated near-term production or supply impact.

title: Chinese Aluminum Stocks Gain After Power Cut to Guizhou Producers
summary: China Southern Power Grid’s Guizhou branch cut electricity load by 20% for five electrolytic aluminium smelters, prompting gains in shares of firms not directly affected. The cut could shut 200,000–300,000 tons of capacity. Inventories are near recent lows, supporting a modest bullish outlook despite weak winter demand.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.92% Higher at $3.8750 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for December delivery settled 0.92% higher at $3.8750, up 3.55 cents/lb. Prices rose for two consecutive sessions and gained 2.01% over the past two sessions, the largest two-day increase since Dec. 2, 2022, while year-to-date remains down.

title: China Nov aluminium output rises as power controls ease
summary: China’s primary aluminium output rose to 3.41 million tonnes in November, the ninth straight year-on-year increase, after electricity usage restrictions eased. Smelters saw higher profits on lower coal prices and production ramped up in several regions, partially offsetting cuts elsewhere. SMM/Shanghai Futures pricing rose modestly as markets digested supply.

title: SMM Analysis: Xinjiang Accounted for 15.3% of China Aluminum Production from January to November, Ranking Second_SMM
summary: Xinjiang released its first list of emission-reduction compliance enterprises, affecting multiple aluminium smelters. With pandemic controls largely cancelled, smelters have ended closed-loop management and operated normally during the prior 100-day period. Although earlier shipments were delayed, improved coal/logistics should raise arrivals, with limited transit volumes limiting inventory pressure in consumer markets.

title: Nickel Salt Supply Likely to still Be in A Small Surplus in December_SMM
summary: SMM reports that in November nickel sulphate supply was in a small surplus despite sluggish downstream demand. A battery-grade deficit turned into a surplus due to weaker demand and delayed downstream purchases alongside ternary producers dumping inventories. For December, precursor output is set to fall and nickel salt output only slightly, leaving a surplus that pressures prices.

title: Norsk Hydro to supply Mercedes-Benz with low-carbon aluminium
summary: Norsk Hydro will supply Mercedes-Benz with low-carbon aluminium for multiple models, including electric vehicles, as Mercedes expands decarbonisation goals. Hydro’s REDUXA 3.0 targets under 3.0 kg CO2/kg aluminium from 2023 and uses Norwegian scrap recycling. Mercedes called it a major milestone, suggesting meaningful volumes.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Receives FIRB Approval and Anticipates Imminent Completion of the Sale of the Eva Copper Project and the Australian Exploration Tenements
summary: Copper Mountain Mining said Australia’s FIRB approved the sale of its Eva Copper Project and exploration tenements to Harmony, completing the final condition for the transaction. The company expects closing imminently after receiving cash. The news is copper-asset related but does not detail immediate production changes.

title: Canada Nickel Appoints Financial Advisors, Reaches Next Permitting Milestone
summary: Canada Nickel says it has filed the Detailed Project Description and related responses to advance the federal impact assessment process for its Crawford nickel sulphide project, following prior permitting steps and consultations. The company also hired Deutsche Bank and Scotiabank to advise on equity financing alternatives, targeting permits by mid-2025.

title: SMM China Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventories as of December 15_SMM
summary: SMM said China’s aluminium ingot social inventories fell to 482,000 mt as of Dec 15, the lowest in nearly five years, helped by smelter output cuts and more shipments to downstream buyers. Billet inventories also declined to 61,400 mt, driven by better conversion economics and reduced shipments. Overall supply looks tight.

title: SHFE Nickel Fell for Two Consecutive Days amid Poor Demand and Favourable Macro Front_SMM
summary: SHFE nickel prices continued to decline, with spot refined nickel and briquettes lower as demand remained weak. Inventories rose in some areas and LME stocks increased. While macro improved modestly after weaker-than-expected US CPI, downstream stainless steel and alloy consumption stayed soft, limiting upside.

title: KoBold Metals commits $150m investment in Zambia copper mine
summary: KoBold Metals plans a $150m investment in Zambia’s Mingomba copper-cobalt project, including a $115m payment tied to stakes and $35m for exploration. It aims to develop the high-grade deposit using AI-enabled drilling analysis. Zambia targets much higher copper output by 2032, but near-term production impact is unclear.

title: US Sanctions Russia's Richest Tycoon, Nornickel Chief Potanin
summary: The report’s headline says the U.S. sanctioned Russia’s richest tycoon and Nornickel chief Potanin. Because Nornickel is a key nickel supplier, the sanctions could disrupt operations, financing, or trade-related access, likely tightening perceived near-term nickel availability and weighing on nickel prices.

title: First Quantum Panama copper mine deadline passes without a deal
summary: Panama rejected First Quantum Minerals’ last-minute proposal to amend its US$375 million/year royalty agreement for the Cobre Panama copper mine. With no deal in place, the mine’s continued operation is now uncertain, raising near-term supply disruption risk and likely weighing on copper prices.

title: Coming flood of demand from energy transition will cause copper prices to rise again
summary: The note says copper has already fallen ~20% from its 2022 high, but demand from the energy transition will eventually lift prices again. It cites higher copper intensity in EVs and wind, and warns supply growth is constrained by long mine timelines and permits, implying future tightening.

title: Aluminium Follows Iron Ore In China-Fueled Price Rally
summary: Aluminium prices broke higher as China lifted zero-COVID lockdowns, boosting hopes of returning base-metal demand. The piece flags added volatility from an “exit wave,” and suggests China’s energy demand revival could raise production costs, setting a higher price floor for energy-intensive aluminium. WTO ruling against U.S. tariffs is unlikely to change duties.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Completes Sale of the Eva Copper Project and the Australian Exploration Tenements
summary: Copper Mountain Mining says it has closed the sale of its Eva Copper Project and Australian exploration tenements for up to US$230 million, including contingent payments tied to copper prices (e.g., 10% of incremental revenue above US$3.80/lb). Proceeds fund bond buybacks and working capital, with no immediate production-supply change described.

title: Deadline for copper mine agreement has passed
summary: Panama’s government missed a midnight deadline to agree with Minera Panamá on the contract terms for operating the Cobre Panamá copper mine, after the company rejected the initial proposal and later submitted changes to economic terms such as royalties. The government will brief the public on negotiations and efforts to sign a deal.

title: Panama Shuts Down First Quantum Copper Mine After Talks Fail
summary: Panama is reported to have shut down First Quantum’s copper mine after talks failed. The move signals an abrupt supply disruption for mined copper, which can quickly change near-term market tightness expectations and push copper prices lower in the following days.

title: Panama shuts down huge copper mine in contract dispute
summary: Panama ordered First Quantum Minerals to stop work at its large Donoso copper mine after the deadline for a new concession contract expired. Only maintenance will continue while the contract payment and terms are renegotiated. The mine supplies most of Panama’s exports and producing 300,000 tons of concentrate annually.

title: Panama moves to oust Vancouver miner after fight over revenue from copper mine
summary: Panama ordered First Quantum Minerals to pause operations at its Cobre Panamá copper mine after missing a deadline to sign a $375 million/year payment agreement. Talks over tax/royalty terms continued, but legal protections for termination and stability were not agreed. The mine could produce ~340,000–350,000 tonnes of copper in 2022.

title: Spot Pure Nickel Supply is Tight and the Premiums Rebound_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports tight spot pure nickel supply in Shanghai as the import window remains closed. Jinchuan nickel premiums rise to 8,000–8,500 yuan/mt and NORNICKEL premiums to 6,000–6,500 yuan/mt. Nickel briquette prices also tick up, though spot trading remains weak due to relative pricing.

title: Press review: Potanin blacklisted, but Nornickel spared and Erdogan rival gets jail time
summary: The press review says the US blacklisted Vladimir Potanin and related entities, but spared Norilsk Nickel via a special clause to avoid disrupting the global non-ferrous metals market. It notes that analysts expect limited near-term effects on nickel prices, with demand support from stainless and batteries in China.

title: China Nonferrous Metal Group and Jiangxi Copper Reach an Agreement on RCs for Imported Blister Copper in 2023 _SMM
summary: China Nonferrous Metal Group and Jiangxi Copper agreed benchmark refining charges (RCs) for imported blister copper for 2023 at $125/mt CIF, down from $155/mt in 2022. The sharp decrease signals lower refining economics and may weigh on expectations for copper-linked pricing in the near term.

title: Bonded Zone Inventory of Nickel Adds 1,800 mt from December 9_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says bonded-zone nickel inventory rose to 8,100 mt as of Dec 16, with nickel briquette at 1,370 mt and nickel plate at 6,730 mt. From Nov 1, spot imports suffered amid a low SHFE/LME nickel ratio. The export window then opened, prompting nickel plate shipments to ports and lifting bonded stocks this week.

title: Mercedes To Introduce 70% Greener Aluminum Into Its Vehicles Next Year
summary: Mercedes signed a letter of intent with Norway’s Hydro to supply aluminum with a 70% smaller carbon footprint, potentially starting next year. The deal targets lower emissions in aluminum production by using more renewable power and recycled inputs. It may influence expectations for low-carbon aluminum premiums, but no near-term supply shock is described.

title: Eldorado to restart construction at Greece gold-copper project
summary: Eldorado Gold approved a full restart of construction at the Skouries gold-copper project in Greece after permit delays, contingent on the first drawdown of an €680m project finance facility expected in Q1 next year. The feasibility study targets 67 million pounds of copper annually, supporting supply expectations.

title: First Quantum Clings to Hope of Last-Minute Panama Copper Deal
summary: The piece focuses on First Quantum maintaining hope for a late-stage copper-related deal in Panama. While details are limited in the excerpt, the implication is improved project or supply certainty. That kind of development risk reduction typically supports near-term copper sentiment and may pressure prices upward over days.

title: NORNICKEL APPROVES BUDGET FOR 2023
summary: Norilsk Nickel’s board unanimously approved its 2023 budget, with CAPEX projected to rise 10% to about $4.7bn. The investment programme supports mining, infrastructure maintenance in the Norilsk Industrial District, equipment replacement and capital repairs, alongside initiatives to address operational challenges from partner refusals.

title: Panama shuts down First Quantum's giant copper mine
summary: Panama’s government ordered First Quantum Minerals to halt operations at the Cobre Panama copper mine after contract negotiations failed. The temporary shutdown represents an immediate reduction in copper supply from a major producer, likely weighing on near-term market sentiment and expectations for copper prices.

title: Eldorado Gold board okays Skouries gold-copper project restart
summary: Eldorado Gold said its board approved an investment decision to fully restart construction activities at the Skouries gold-copper project in northern Greece. The company’s proposed mine has reserves of 3.7 million oz., and the restart implies progress toward bringing copper supply online.

title: Hedge Funds Say They Lost $95 Million in LME Nickel Crisis
summary: The report says hedge funds suffered $95 million in losses amid an LME nickel crisis, indicating significant stress in nickel trading. While the excerpt does not provide underlying fundamentals or price moves, the reference to a “crisis” implies near-term negative sentiment and risk to nickel prices.

title: Harmony Gold buys Copper Mountain's Eva copper project in Australia
summary: Harmony Gold completed the purchase of Copper Mountain’s Eva copper project in north-west Queensland for up to $230m. The deal adds 1.72 billion pounds of copper reserves and expands Harmony’s copper exposure. Harmony will review feasibility over up to 12 months before deciding execution and financing.

title: Canadian firm blames Panama for closure of copper mine
summary: A Canadian company says Panama is responsible for the closure of a copper mine. The report implies a near-term reduction in copper production and potential supply tightening, which would likely drive expectations of higher copper prices in the short run, barring details on size or duration.

title: Rocky Mountain substations damaged; copper wire stolen
summary: Rocky Mountain Power reported vandalism at three substations in Sandy, Utah, including missing copper ground wire and stolen copper wire from two sites. Crews rerouted power after quick repairs, briefly cutting electricity to about 3,500 homes. Officials may add security measures after multiple similar incidents nationwide.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 2.95% Lower at $3.7615 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper ended the week 2.95% lower at $3.7615, losing 11.45 cents per pound for the week. The contract also fell over the last two sessions, dropped for two consecutive days, and hit the lowest settlement since Nov. 30, 2022, signaling bearish momentum.

title: Rio Tinto wins fight for control of copper miner
summary: Rio Tinto has completed its multi-billion-pound takeover of Turquoise Hill, securing full control of its 66% stake in Mongolia’s Oyu Tolgoi project. The mine contains major copper deposits, and the deal may increase confidence in project development despite prior delays, cost overruns and disputes with the Mongolian government.

title: Ero Copper Corp.: Ero Copper Increases Revolving Credit Facility to $150 Million and Extends Maturity to December 2026
summary: Ero Copper Corp. amended its senior secured revolving credit facility, increasing commitments to $150 million and extending maturity to December 2026, with updated SOFR-based interest and reduced standby fees. The company cites improved borrowing terms and expects closing by late December, supporting liquidity for its copper operations in Brazil.

title: Analysis-Bumper Green Aluminium Output Is Good News For Carmakers, And Climate
summary: The piece says global “green aluminium” output is set to rise about 10% in 2023, increasing to more in subsequent years. With robust supplies and higher volumes from hydro- and recycled-based production, low-carbon premiums have largely disappeared, weighing on the prices producers can charge buyers, especially in spot markets.

title: Bumper green aluminium output is good news for carmakers, and climate
summary: Reuters reports aluminium makers plan to boost low-carbon output by about 10% in 2023 and more afterward, adding to existing surpluses. It notes green aluminium premiums have largely disappeared, with spot premiums for billet sliding to zero, pressuring price levels even as limited EU-driven demand could support some premiums regionally.

title: China Nov aluminium imports fall amid rising domestic supply
summary: China’s November aluminium imports are reported to have declined while domestic supply increased. The mix suggests reduced need for imported metal into China in the near term, which can weigh on market sentiment and support lower aluminium prices as buyers look more to local supply.

title: Commodities: Chinese companies flock to Indonesia for its nickel
summary: Chinese firms have invested heavily in Indonesia’s Sulawesi and Halmahera, building nickel smelters and refineries and securing supply from the world’s largest known nickel reserves. The report cites $3.2 billion of investment this year and $14.2 billion over 10 years, implying greater future nickel availability.

title: China's aluminium imports decline in November amid rising domestic supply
summary: China’s aluminium imports fell 35.7% year-on-year in November as domestic smelters ramped production and easing power restrictions boosted output. The COVID-hit economy weakened demand for aluminium used in transport, construction and packaging. Despite higher prices in October, weak fundamentals and supply-led import contraction point to downside for aluminium.

title: Forrest takes stake in nickel miner to takeover brink
summary: Andrew Forrest’s Wyloo Metals increased its stake in nickel miner Mincor Resources to 19.9% after supporting a $60 million capital raising. The move places the investor near the takeover-offer threshold, potentially accelerating acquisition talks. It is primarily company-level news, with only indirect implications for nickel prices.

title: Fading Bullishness and Weakening Fundamentals to Put Aluminium Prices at Risk of Downward Corrections  _SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium bearish risk from fading macro support and weak demand: China’s COVID spike suppresses activity, while US/Europe rates remain hawkish. On the supply side, Guizhou smelters face power-load reductions with some potline shutdowns. Aluminium processing operating rates fall and inventories drop on weak arrivals.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Dips 12,400 mt over the Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM said copper inventories across major Chinese markets fell 12,400 mt to 81,900 mt over the weekend, a new year-on-year low. The drop was driven by fewer imported arrivals and downstream restocking after prices fell, while Guangdong rose slightly on weaker consumption. Inventories are expected to fall further if arrivals don’t increase.

title: Spot Copper Concentrate TCs are Under Pressure amid the Shrinking Supply_SMM
summary: SMM says spot treatment charges for imported copper concentrates are under pressure as tight spot supply persists for three straight weeks. Peru road blockages near Cusco threaten Las Bambas warehousing limits and raise odds of output cuts. Port inventories slipped and parties miss 2023 TC benchmarks, weighing on copper sentiment.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices Weaken and Spot premiums are Unlikely to Fall in the Short Term_SMM
summary: SMM reports pure nickel futures on SHFE have declined, but spot nickel premiums stayed broadly stable because spot supply remains tight. Jinchuan and Nornickel premiums increased slightly day-on-day, while nickel briquette prices dropped and remained higher than nickel sulphate, weakening briquette spot transactions.

title: Nickel Ore Prices Remain High amid the Supply Tightness in the Rainy Season, which is Unacceptable for the Downstream Companies_SMM
summary: Nickel ore trading was flat but held at high levels as rainy-season supply tightness persisted. Philippine mines maintained high FOB asking prices, while NPI spot prices rose with raw-material tightness. Downstream nickel processors reduced output in December, tempering demand, yet Ni 1.5% ore is expected to remain around $68–72/wmt short term.

title: ITOCHU : Announces Agreement with Emirates Global Aluminium for Procurement of Environmentally Friendly Raw Materials for Aluminum
summary: ITOCHU said it has agreed with Emirates Global Aluminium to sell environmentally friendly aluminum raw materials produced using solar power to Kobe Steel in Japan. The deal targets demand for low-carbon aluminum as smelting is electricity-intensive and supports carbon-neutrality goals, potentially influencing aluminum pricing expectations and premiums.

title: Strong turnout for copper explorer Cobre's equity raising
summary: Copper explorer Cobre returned from equity capital markets fundraising, securing $5 million in fresh funds, including investment from Sprott Asset Management and its largest shareholders. The news is tied to copper exploration funding, but no immediate operational changes or supply disruptions are mentioned.

title: EGA To Supply Celestial Solar Aluminium To Kobe Steel
summary: EGA said it will supply “Celestial Solar Aluminium” to Kobe Steel. The announcement signals an aluminium supply arrangement that may support near-term aluminium sentiment by improving delivery expectations for buyers, but the provided excerpt does not include contract size, delivery schedule, or broader supply impacts.

title: Canada Nickel Acquires Past Producing Texmont Mine, Highlights High Grade Potential of Regional Land Package
summary: Canada Nickel announced it will acquire the past producing Texmont nickel property and reported early drilling at Texmont and higher-grade targeting at Sothman, with assays pending. Historic resources include 3.2 Mt at 0.9% nickel and Sothman at 1.24% nickel, implying potential for near-term open-pit production.

title: Nickel Mining Market Analysis including Reserves, Production, Operating, Developing and Exploration Assets, Demand Drivers, Key Players and Forecasts, 2021-2026
summary: The PRNewswire piece promotes a report on global nickel mining, citing historical and forecast nickel mine production by country (e.g., growth in Indonesia, Colombia, New Caledonia) and declines in South Africa, the Philippines, and Finland. It also discusses reserves, major projects, and demand drivers, but lacks near-term market-moving events.

title: Are Copper Prices Poised To Climb Higher In 2023?
summary: The piece argues copper is poised to rise as softer U.S. CPI data eases Fed tightening expectations and the U.S. dollar weakens. It also highlights Peru’s protests disrupting mine logistics and shipments from major copper operations, tightening near-term supply and supporting bullish price momentum.

title: Nickel Creek Platinum is innovating in a local supply location
summary: Nickel Creek Platinum says nickel prices should rise amid a perceived nickel supply shortage for EV growth. It highlights the Nickel Shäw Project in Yukon, recent drilling intersecting near-surface massive/semi-massive nickel-copper sulphides, and completed studies toward saleable nickel/copper concentrate. It anticipates a prefeasibility study in 2023.

title: Canada Nickel acquires former Texmont nickel mine near Timmins
summary: Canada Nickel will acquire a 100% interest in the former Texmont nickel property near Timmins, Ontario, between its Deloro and Sothman assets. The company frames the move as providing near-term smaller scale opportunities, which can modestly improve near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: Panama orders First Quantum to halt copper mine operations
summary: Panama has ordered First Quantum to halt operations at a copper mine. A sudden suspension of mining output can quickly reduce expected near-term copper supply, tightening availability in the days ahead. Markets typically react to such disruptions through higher prompt copper pricing expectations.

title: SHFE Aluminium Inventory Ends Eight Consecutive Weeks of Decline and Is at A Relatively Low Level in Six Years_SMM
summary: LME aluminium inventories rose sharply last week but remained around 477,650 mt as of Dec 16, which is relatively low. SHFE aluminium inventories also rebounded after eight straight weeks of decline, up 1.24% to 92,373 mt, yet still sits at a six-year low.

title: SMM Analysis of Reasons for Three Consecutive Weeks of Decline in Copper Concentrate TCs_SMM
summary: SMM reports three straight weeks of declines in the Imported Copper Concentrate Index to $87.67/mt, citing tight spot supply. Production and transport risks at Peru’s Las Bambas (road blocks; near-full inventory) are worsening availability, while Cobre Panama faces operational uncertainty after failed talks with the Panamanian government.

title: Secondary Copper Rods Remain Unpopular, Despite Expanding Price Difference between Copper Cathode and Copper Scrap_SMM
summary: SMM reports Guangdong 1# bare bright copper at 60,500–60,700 yuan/mt with unchanged quotes, while the cathode-to-scrap spread widened to 1,462 yuan/mt. Secondary copper rod prices in Jiangxi were mostly 65,400–65,600 yuan/mt, up 100 yuan/mt, but trading stayed muted.

title: Supply of Spot Pure Nickel was still Tight and Spot Premiums Rose Sharply_SMM
summary: SMM reports that spot pure nickel supply remained tight on Dec 20, pushing Jinchuan premiums to an average of 10,250 yuan/mt (+1,900) and NORNICKEL premiums to 7,750 yuan/mt (+1,300). Despite rigid demand, transactions stayed thin, reinforcing bullish short-term nickel tightness.

title: LME and SHFE Nickel Inventory Polarised, with LME Inventory Hitting a 3.5-Month High_SMM
summary: LME data showed nickel inventories increased to 54,360 mt, a three-and-a-half-month high after a prior decline. SHFE nickel inventories fell sharply on Dec 16 but overall fluctuated. The piece notes that declining inventories usually support futures, implying the LME build is a short-term bearish signal for nickel.

title: Emerita Intersects 25.1 Meters Grading 0.3% Copper, 1.5%
summary: Emerita Resources reported additional 2022 delineation drilling assays at the La Romanera deposit in Spain, including multiple copper-bearing massive sulphide and stockwork intercepts (notably ~0.3% Cu to ~1.0% Cu over varying widths). The company plans an NI 43-101 resource estimate around Q1/Q2 2023.

title: Canada Nickel agrees to buy Texmont Mine in Canada
summary: Canada Nickel agreed to acquire the past-producing Texmont mine in Canada for cash and a promissory note, with the option to restart operations. The company is drilling to update resources and assess whether output could support a restart by 2025 or provide higher-grade feed for its Crawford nickel project, lifting nickel sentiment.

title: 1844 Resources Inc.: 1844 Resources Completes Its First Reconnaissance Program on Native Copper Project, Gaspesie, Quebec
summary: 1844 Resources announced completion of its 2022 reconnaissance program at the Native Copper project in Quebec, including prospecting, trenching, sampling, and road rehabilitation. The compilation and sampling highlight copper mineralization in multiple sectors with assay values up to ~10% Cu, but no near-term production impacts are stated.

title: Sortera Alloys Hits Above 95% Accuracy Milestone Sorting Mixed Aluminum Scrap into High-Quality End Products
summary: Sortera Alloys says its new sorting facility will process up to 150 million lbs. of mixed aluminum scrap annually and has achieved >95% accuracy sorting aluminum pre-production material by alloy and composition. The upgraded recycled feedstock is recirculated into manufacturing, expanding domestic secondary supply and reducing reliance on virgin metal.

title: Russian Mining Giant Nornickel Mulls Cutting Output 10% Next Year
summary: Russian miner Nornickel is considering a 10% output cut next year. Because Nornickel is a key nickel producer, the prospect of lower supply can tighten expected market balances and lift nickel price sentiment within weeks as traders price in reduced future availability.

title: Copper smelter Aurubis plans 530 million euros in new investments
summary: Aurubis, a major copper smelter, reported higher FY operating earnings and said it will invest about 530 million euros. Its CEO attributed gains to strong copper demand from renewables and electric vehicles, offsetting weaker construction demand. The company did trim its 2022/23 earnings forecast corridor.

title: Taseko and Mitsui partner to develop Florence copper project in Arizona
summary: Taseko shares jumped after it announced a partnership with Mitsui to develop the Florence copper project in Arizona. Mitsui committed an initial US$50 million investment to support the project’s development. The deal is a constructive supply-development signal for copper markets and can lift near-term sentiment.

title: UAE's EGA to supply CelestiAL solar aluminium to Japan's Kobe Steel
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) agreed to supply its CelestiAL solar aluminium to Japan’s Kobe Steel for Nissan automotive body sheet. EGA already supplies thousands of tonnes annually and plans to expand CelestiAL output using more grid/renewable power. The solar smelting case may support aluminium demand visibility.

title: Chinese Primary Aluminium Imports up 64.1% MoM in Nov_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s primary aluminium imports rose 64.1% month-on-month to 110,700 mt in November, but were down 51.7% year-on-year. Exports increased strongly on the month, while net imports fell 52.7% YoY to 108,300 mt. Overall flows point to volatile near-term supply-demand dynamics for aluminium.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices Stand High with No Downward Potential for Spot Premiums_SMM
summary: SMM says SHFE spot premiums for Jinchuan nickel averaged 10,750 yuan/mt on Dec 21, up 500 yuan/mt, while NORNICKEL premiums were flat at 7,750 yuan/mt. It attributes strength to tight pure nickel supply and traders awaiting the import window, with nickel briquette premiums also increasing.

title: Indonesia Bans Bauxite Exports in Latest Protectionist Move
summary: Indonesia’s latest protectionist step, as stated in the headline, bans bauxite exports. Because bauxite is a key raw material for alumina production, the policy can reduce global supply of aluminium feedstock and increase expected costs or shortages, supporting higher aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Xanadu secures Zijin support for Mongolian copper project
summary: Xanadu Mines executed further investment agreements with Zijin for its Mongolian projects, including funding earmarked for the Kharmagtai pre-feasibility study and potential construction. Kharmagtai has an estimated resource and expected copper output of about 37,000 tonnes per year, which may support bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Indonesia bans bauxite exports in latest protectionist move
summary: Indonesia will ban bauxite exports starting mid-2023, including bleached bauxite, to force more domestic processing. The move could disrupt supply to China, where Indonesian bauxite is a meaningful share of imports, boosting short-term aluminium price expectations despite possible diversification toward Guinea.

title: Weak Supply and Demand Suppressed Imports of Laterite Nickel Ore in Nov_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s November nickel ore imports fell 12% MoM to 4.17 million mt, with laterite nickel ore down 12.5% MoM, driven by rainy-season restrictions on Philippine mine ROM output. NPI prices slid toward cost, pressuring producers and limiting ore buying. December imports are expected to decline further.

title: Chinese Aluminium Extrusion Exports Rose Seasonally in Nov_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM cites Chinese customs data showing aluminium extrusion exports rose to 82,200 mt in November, up 10.9% month-on-month but down 6.7% year-on-year. Exports rebounded seasonally, with Vietnam, the Philippines, and Israel as key destinations, while anti-dumping risks persist and may keep growth limited.

title: Indonesia plans to ban bauxite ore exports starting from June 2023-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia’s President Joko Widodo said the country plans to ban bauxite ore exports starting June 2023 to expand downstream manufacturing, jobs, and foreign exchange. The government expects higher state revenue from bauxite processing. The article also notes a prior nickel export-ban case ruled on by the WTO.

title: Indonesia plans to ban bauxite ore exports starting from June 2023
summary: Indonesia’s President Joko Widodo said the country plans to ban bauxite ore exports starting June 2023 to boost downstream manufacturing jobs and revenue. By restricting exported bauxite feedstock, the policy is likely to tighten expectations for alumina supply and support aluminium prices. Nickel is only referenced historically.

title: Aluminum Cost Rising as Indonesia Decides to Halt Bauxite Ore Exports From June 2023
summary: Aluminum prices rose about 1% after Indonesia said it will ban exports of bauxite ore from June 2023 and push for more processed bauxite domestically. Because bauxite is a key input for aluminum production and Indonesia is a major global bauxite supplier, the policy tightens supply expectations and supports higher aluminum prices.

title: Azerbaijan Sends Another Batch Of Aluminum Products To Turki...
summary: The article title says Azerbaijan sent another batch of aluminum products to Turkey. Such shipments typically increase near-term supply availability in the region, which can weigh on aluminum prices. However, the provided excerpt lacks shipment quantities, contract terms, or any production or policy disruption details.

title: Chakana Copper Corp.: Chakana Provides Corporate Update
summary: Chakana Copper Corp. modified payment terms for its Aija Option Agreement and is advancing environmental permitting to drill south targets at its Soledad project in Peru. The project’s inferred resources include copper alongside gold and silver. The update is primarily corporate/permitting and unlikely to impact copper supply or demand immediately.

title: Indonesia Will Ban Bauxite Ore Exports in June 2023
summary: Indonesia’s president announced a planned ban on bauxite ore exports starting June 2023 to push domestic processing and refining. The policy follows a prior nickel export ban and is expected to increase state revenue. Because bauxite is a key input for alumina and aluminium, the move could tighten supply and support aluminium prices.

title: Vior, Inc.: Vior Signs Letter of Intent With Soquem To Advance Its District-Scale Skyfall Nickel Project
summary: Vior signed a letter of intent with Soquem for a 50% option interest in its Skyfall nickel project in Quebec, including $2.5 million in exploration spending and $350,000 in cash payments over two years. The update supports ongoing nickel exploration but signals no near-term production impact.

title: Vior Signs Letter of Intent With Soquem To Advance Its District-Scale Skyfall Nickel Project
summary: Vior signed a letter of intent with Soquem to advance its district-scale Skyfall nickel project. The update is geared toward progressing the development pipeline, which can modestly improve market expectations for future nickel supply. That typically supports nickel sentiment in the coming days as supply risks ease.

title: Indonesia to ban bauxite exports next year to boost processing at home
summary: Indonesia announced it will ban bauxite exports starting next year to expand domestic processing, similar to its nickel ore restrictions. Bauxite is used to produce alumina and aluminum. The policy could reduce near-term bauxite flows to importers and potentially tighten aluminum feedstock supply, supporting prices despite expected WTO challenges.

title: Copper thieves strike again at Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital
summary: Copper thieves cut and stole about three metres of copper piping at Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital, compromising sterilisation steam and cooling systems in two operating theatres. The incident follows Monday’s theft of 10 metres of copper cable affecting ICU oxygen supply. Authorities say the hospital is targeted; alternative arrangements were made.

title: Copper market in 46,000 tonne surplus in October –ICSG
summary: ICSG reported the world refined copper market had a 46,000-tonne surplus in October, reversing the prior month’s 85,000-tonne deficit. October output was 2.2 million tonnes versus 2.16 million tonnes consumption. For the first 10 months, the market remained in deficit.

title: Foran's US$150M loan helps nearly cover McIlvenna Bay copper project cost
summary: Foran Mining said it will use a US$150 million loan from Sprott Resource Lending, alongside about US$200 million proposed by Ontario, to help fund construction of its McIlvenna Bay copper project in Saskatchewan. The update supports future supply but does not indicate immediate output changes.

title: Vior Inc. signs letter of intent with SOQUEM on Skyfall nickel project
summary: Vior Inc. signed a letter of intent with SOQUEM regarding its Skyfall nickel project in Quebec’s Abitibi Greenstone Belt. The deal suggests forward progress on developing new nickel supply. Although the announcement is at the LOI stage, it can still provide modest near-term support for nickel pricing sentiment.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Closes C$1 Million Private Placement
summary: EV Nickel Inc. closed a C$1.03 million non-brokered private placement, issuing flow-through units to fund exploration at its Shaw Dome nickel project in Ontario. Proceeds will be used for Canadian flow-through mining expenditures. The release signals ongoing exploration but does not indicate any near-term production or supply change.

title: Thousands flee troop deployment near Chinese-run copper mine in Myanmar
summary: More than 6,000 residents fled after troops entered villages near China’s Wanbao-run Letpadaung copper mine in Myanmar. Mine operations were cut by over 80% after workers walked off post-coup, and locals report renewed attempts to restart. The heightened security risk and unrest threaten copper output continuity.

title: Palmer offloads Qld nickel refinery to Swiss-based investors
summary: Clive Palmer has sold Queensland’s Yabulu nickel and cobalt refinery to Swiss-based Zero Carbon Investek for an estimated $1–2 billion. The buyer plans to restart operations, aiming to employ hundreds and later add solar and battery power to decarbonize production. Sale is subject to regulatory approvals.

title: Chinese Copper Imports Reach a Monthly High in November 2022 as the Import Window is Wide Open in October_SMM
summary: China imported 358,300 mt of copper cathode in Nov 2022, a monthly high, as the import window stayed open and import profits exceeded 1,500 yuan/mt. Tight supply and low inventories kept spot premiums elevated despite expected Dec imports near 320,000 mt.

title: Clearance Volume of Pure Nickel Falls 13% MoM in November 2022_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China imported about 14,521 mt of refined nickel in Nov 2022, but customs clearance volumes for refined/pure nickel fell 13% month-on-month. The decline is linked to nickel import losses after the SHFE/LME ratio dropped, and rising bonded inventories. SMM expects further clearance decreases in December.

title: Xanadu locks in gas supply deal for Mongolian copper project
summary: Xanadu Mines signed a non-binding gas offtake MoU with Jade Gas Holdings to supply cleaner, low-cost natural gas to power its Kharmagtai copper-gold project in Mongolia. The near-field gas supply option supports progress toward binding commercial terms and potential construction decisions, improving outlook for copper project development.

title: Imported Copper Transactions are Sluggish Owing to the Low SHFE/LME Copper Price Ratio_SMM
summary: SMM says Yangshan copper premiums for LME-warrant and bills of lading cargoes were $30-50/mt and $25-45/mt, respectively, with little change. Import losses versus SHFE were about 700 yuan/mt as the SHFE/LME ratio stayed steady, causing sluggish demand, subdued trading, and delayed spot settlements.

title: Spot Holders Insist on High Premiums amid the Low Copper Inventory_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai spot copper premiums over SHFE 2301 rose to about 570 yuan/mt, supported by low copper inventory and cargo holders insisting on high quotes. SHFE 2301 was volatile but ended higher, while small imported arrivals and suppressed downstream demand failed to ease supply tightness. Spot prices likely stay firm next week.

title: Black & Veatch to Deliver Seawater Desalination Plant in Indonesia Saving Precious Fresh Water Resources at World's Largest Designed Single Line Copper Smelter
summary: Black & Veatch will design and deliver a seawater desalination plant beside PT Freeport Indonesia’s Manyar copper smelter in East Java. The plant will supply desalinated water to support processing of concentrates from Grasberg and improve operational efficiency and reliability for the planned 1.7 MTPA smelter.

title: Premium Nickel Resources Ltd.: Premium Nickel Resources Ltd Announces Assay Results at Its 100% Owned Selebi Mine in Botswana Including: 6.80 Metres of 2.06% NiEq (1.28% Ni, 2.35% Cu, 0.04% Co), 4.65 Metres of 1.55% NiEq (1.10% Ni, 1.24% Cu, 0.04% Co)
summary: Premium Nickel Resources announced additional assay results from its Selebi Ni-Cu-Co sulphide mine in Botswana, including multiple drillhole intervals with reported nickel and copper grades and NiEq calculations based on LME prices. The update is exploratory/resource-expansion oriented and does not change near-term production or inventories, limiting short-term price impact.

title: Palmer hits pay dirt, scooping over $1b for Qld nickel refinery he bought for $1
summary: Clive Palmer’s Queensland Nickel/Yabulu refinery was sold for an estimated $1–$2 billion to Zero Carbon Investek, with plans to restart operations and employ hundreds. The deal is framed as happening in more favourable conditions for nickel tied to battery demand, supporting near-term nickel sentiment.

title: Premium Nickel aims to re-open Selebi mine in Botswana
summary: Premium Nickel Resources reports drill results at its Selebi nickel-copper-cobalt project in Botswana support the idea that past-producing deposits connect at depth. The company is working to reopen the Selebi mine, which could improve perceived future nickel supply and modestly affect copper expectations due to co-product potential.

title: Expectations of Pure Nickel Prices in 2023 amid High Prices and Supply Surplus_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel futures rising to a new high, tracking LME nickel’s gain after news that Norilsk Nickel may cut 2023 production by 10%. With low LME warrant inventories and the pure nickel import window still closed, supply concerns intensified and lifted nickel prices.

title: Copper struggles for momentum under recession risks, China uncertainty
summary: Reuters reports copper trading in a narrow range as recession fears and uncertain demand from China pressure prices, despite support from Chinese liquidity measures and easing COVID restrictions. China’s infection spike disrupts logistics and lowers operating rates. Strong U.S. data lifts the dollar. Aluminium and nickel also slip modestly.

title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zones Stay Flat from December 16_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventories in China’s domestic bonded zones were flat from Dec 16 to Dec 23, including Shanghai and Guangdong. Slower customs clearance in Shanghai from rising COVID-19 cases supported unchanged stock levels. With only three LME copper trading days and cautious downstream buying, bonded-zone inventories may rise, but near-term net impact looks limited.

title: Factors Contribute to the Burgeoning Spot Premiums of Copper Cathode in the Shanghai Market_SMM
summary: SMM reports that Shanghai copper cathode spot premiums have surged about 400 yuan/mt versus SHFE 2301, staying firm despite a small dip. COVID-19 outbreaks disrupt processing and downstream buying, while a closed import window, declining social inventories, and hindered north-to-Shanghai transfers tighten spot supply, lifting premiums.

title: Nickel Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zone Grow Slightly from December 16 amid the Huge Import Losses_SMM
summary: SMM says Dec 23 bonded-zone nickel inventories reached 8,300 mt, with nickel briquette and plate inventories rising, while the SHFE/LME price ratio failed to improve. Import losses stayed around 10,000 yuan/mt, limiting pure nickel clearance. Salt makers dumped briquettes and demand weakened, increasing plate inventory.

title: Mining magnate Palmer offloads Yabulu nickel refinery for $1.3bn
summary: Clive Palmer has sold Australia’s Yabulu nickel and cobalt refinery to Zero Carbon Investek for $1.3bn, raising funds and positioning a planned restart. The refinery has been on care-and-maintenance since 2016 and is expected to resume operations in about 18 months, with additional investment and renewable energy upgrades.

title: Class 1 Nickel announces the first update of its Drill
summary: Class 1 Nickel reported progress on its Somanike drilling program in Quebec, with two active drills and assays pending. Drilling intersected sulphide mineralisation in 18 holes and identified geophysical anomalies for follow-up near the historic Marbridge nickel mine. Positive results may support near-term nickel and copper sentiment.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Down 81,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 81,000 wmt week-on-week to 9.04 million wmt, with total Ni content near 71,000 mt. Inventories at seven major ports also declined. Supply tightness from restricted Philippine shipments and cautious NPI buying are cited, with expectations for a slow inventory decline.

title: Copper edges higher on hopes for better demand next year
summary: Copper prices edged higher as low inventories and hopes for economic recovery next year offset weaker near-term demand in China from a surge in COVID-19 cases. LME copper rose 0.5% on the day. ShFE copper stocks fell, limiting downside if demand improves. Nickel rose; aluminium fell.

title: Hedge Funds Lose Court Fight for LME Disclosure of Nickel Crisis Communications
summary: The article headline says hedge funds lost a court fight seeking LME disclosure of communications tied to a nickel crisis. While this is directly connected to nickel market sentiment and transparency, the excerpt provides no specific new supply, trading, or regulatory information to indicate a clear short-term price move.

title: Nickel metal still has key role to play in 2023 battery grade market
summary: Fastmarkets says demand for nickel for EV batteries is set to rise sharply and is a key driver for the nickel sulfate battery-grade market. The article describes high nickel price volatility and production shifts in China toward intermediates like MHP, while briquette remains important for LME hedging access, reinforcing nickel’s near-term tightness expectations.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 1.10% Higher at $3.8030 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper ended the week up 1.10% to $3.8030 per pound, with the front-month contract also rising sharply on the day. The piece is primarily market data recap (daily/weekly gains and declines vs prior highs and lows) and does not mention new fundamental drivers.

title: Titan Minerals Maiden Drilling Delivers Shallow Copper-Gold-...
summary: Titan Minerals’ maiden drilling reportedly delivered shallow copper-gold results at its project. Such exploration success can raise market optimism about future copper resources and development timelines, offering mild near-term support to copper sentiment, though it does not confirm production or immediate supply.

title: What's next for WA aluminum manufacturing? The fight goes on
summary: The article reports that the push to reopen a “green” aluminum manufacturing plant near Bellingham has stopped this month. While it is not described as permanent closure, the halted reopening likely delays additional aluminum supply coming to market and could weigh on nearby aluminium price expectations.

title: Setback for hedge funds amid London Metal Exchange nickel battle
summary: A High Court judge dismissed a case by hedge funds seeking information about the LME’s decision to cancel nickel trades in March, when nickel surged on fears related to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The cancellations helped some shorts but hurt others, prompting ongoing lawsuits and appeal considerations.

title: Eight drums of copper cable stolen from Coneybury Road
summary: West Mercia Police said eight drums of copper cable were stolen from a nearly finished new-build site on Coneybury Road in Worcester, between Monday 19 December (4:30pm) and Tuesday 20 December (7am). Police are seeking witnesses; the incident is localized and not linked to broader market supply or demand.

title: SHFE Nickel Prices Fluctuated with some Ups Affected by News Front_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel stayed high after news that Norilsk may cut 2023 nickel output by ~10%. Stronger US GDP and lower jobless claims supported tighter Fed expectations, bearish for commodities. Domestically, import losses and elevated spot premiums tightened supply, while demand restocking and weak briquette trading limited direction; prices are expected rangebound.

title: Bank of Japan's Raising YCC Last Week Hit the US Dollar, and Copper Prices Rise First and then Fall_SMM
summary: Bank of Japan’s expansion of YCC weakened the yen and the US dollar, lifting risk assets; the article notes SHFE copper briefly surged above 66,000 yuan/mt. Fundamentals also supported prices: China inventories fell sharply, spot premiums rose, and COVID-19 outbreaks kept consumption weak.

title: China Aluminium Extrusion Exports Increased 10.9% MoM in November, and Showed Seasonal Characteristics of Previous Years_SMM
summary: SMM cites customs data showing China’s aluminium extrusion exports at 82,200 mt in November, up 10.9% month-on-month but down 6.7% year-on-year. Shipments were led by Guangdong and focused on Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand. Despite seasonal recovery, anti-dumping measures may keep export growth restrained.

title: China's Bauxite Imports in Nov Exceeded 10 Million mt Again, with Indonesia's Ban Taking Effect in Next June_SMM
summary: China imported 11.79 million mt of bauxite in November (+31% MoM, +53% YoY), with Guinea hitting a record 7.28 million mt. Indonesia’s export ban from June 2023 is expected to be partly offset by other suppliers (Guinea, new entrants) and ongoing alumina projects, keeping impacts controllable, though high bauxite prices could pressure alumina margins.

title: Spot Copper Concentrate TCs Drop under Pressure Owing to the Disturbances on the Supply Side_SMM
summary: SMM reports spot copper concentrate trading was sluggish as COVID-19 and overseas holidays reduced activity. Treatment charges (TCs) for clean concentrates fell as Chile’s Ventanas port fire, Peru’s Matarani riots, US trucking strikes, and operational constraints at Las Bambas disrupted shipments, lowering expected concentrate supply.

title: Chile's Codelco Unveils Austerity Plan after Cutting Copper Output Forecast_SMM
summary: Chile’s Codelco announced an austerity plan and cut its copper output target for 2022 to 1.435–1.465 million tonnes versus 1.49–1.51 million previously. It cited lower ore grades and weaker prices. Codelco will cut spending on materials and services to improve earnings and optimize production through 2027.

title: Alumina Price Rise Slowed Down amid Declining Market Activities_SMM
summary: SMM says the alumina weighted index rose modestly but the pace of gains slowed. Prices remain elevated across Chinese provinces, while overseas FOB weakened slightly. The rise was supported by north China output cuts and high-cost closures, but smelters’ stockpiling reduces fresh demand, and year-end refinery suspensions should stabilize prices.

title: Historically Low Inventory and Mild Production Growth May Put A Brake on Further Decline in SHFE Aluminium_SMM
summary: SMM reports historically low Chinese aluminium ingot inventories (475,000 mt) and tight spot supply with elevated premiums. More than 200,000 mt of aluminium capacity has been cut in Guizhou, and additional capacity transfers/shutdowns are underway. Production growth is muted by off-season demand risks and power rationing, supporting SHFE aluminium stabilization.

title: Tight Spot Pure Nickel Supply Improved and the Premiums Fell Slightly_SMM
summary: SMM said pure nickel spot supply improved as traders were more willing to ship near month-end. Jinchuan nickel premiums fell to around 10,250 yuan/mt, while Nornickel premiums were slightly higher. Nickel briquette prices eased and weaker briquette spot activity was noted versus nickel sulphate.

title: Aluminium Ingot Social Inventory Begin to Accumulate After Continuous Fall_SMM
summary: Shanghai-based SMM says China’s aluminium ingot social inventories reached 484,000 mt on Dec 26, up 9,000 mt from the prior week, as cargo arrivals slowed destocking and demand weakened. Some local inventories rose (notably Wuxi), while other areas declined amid output cuts elsewhere. Downstream planned closures before Chinese New Year may support an inventory uptrend.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Add 3,500 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM said copper inventories across major Chinese markets were 79,700 mt as of Dec 26, up 3,500 mt from last Friday. Increases occurred in Shanghai and Guangdong, while Jiangsu fell. COVID-related factory rate declines and smelter “inventory dumping” boosted shipments; SMM expects further inventory growth, weighing on copper.

title: Aluminum's Booms and Busts: Is More Volatility Ahead? | Institutional Investor
summary: The piece argues aluminum prices may face near-term downside risk as demand softens and excess pandemic-era inventory could lead to a supply glut, pressuring producers to cut prices. It also notes possible volatility from potential U.S. sanctions on Russian aluminum, but focuses mainly on surplus concerns.

title: Imports of Unwrought Aluminium Alloy in Nov Gained Slightly MoM, but Continued to Drop YoY_SMM
summary: China’s imports of unwrought aluminium alloy rose slightly month-on-month in November but fell year-on-year. Exports increased sharply. Demand weakened due to ongoing off-season and COVID-related production disruptions in secondary aluminium and die-casting plants, leading traders to sign fewer orders and expecting lower December port arrivals.

title: LME Aluminium Inventory Refreshes the Lowest Level in More Than Two Months, SHFE Aluminium Inventory Continues to Increase_SMM
summary: LME data show aluminium inventories fell again to 466,600 mt as of Dec 23, the lowest in over two months after a brief rebound. SHFE inventories rose 3.43% WoW to 95,539 mt but remain a six-year low. Overall, tighter LME supplies likely support prices.

title: SHFE/LME Lead Price Ratio Rose Rapidly, and Import Loss of Refined Nickel Dropped Sharply_SMM
summary: SMM reports that between early and mid-December the SHFE/LME lead ratio for lead/related spreads rose as refined nickel import losses narrowed sharply. Improved import window effects from a weaker dollar and slightly alleviated tight domestic pure nickel supply supported prices, while LME nickel warrant accumulation kept upside expectations.

title: Spot Premiums of Copper Cathode in North China Drop Greatly Near the Year-End_SMM
summary: North China copper cathode spot premiums versus SHFE 2301 fell sharply, with discounts widening to 400–160 yuan/mt (avg 280 yuan/mt). Higher rangebound futures and suppressed downstream restocking, alongside year-end fund withdrawals, forced cargo holders to cut quotes. Smelters also shipped more to the east to manage north supply.

title: China Nickel Ore and Concentrates Import Report 2022: In
summary: The piece summarizes a ResearchAndMarkets report on China’s nickel ore and concentrate imports. It highlights strong 2021 import growth and higher average import prices, plus rising demand from EVs and stainless steel. With China’s limited local resources and heavy import dependence, nickel ore imports remain sizable into 2023.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.80% Higher at $3.8335 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper front-month futures settled 0.80% higher at $3.8335 per pound, up 3.05 cents. The contract was up for two consecutive sessions, rising 8.20 cents over the last two sessions and posting its highest settlement value since Dec. 14, 2022.

title: Short-term Nickel Price Likely to Remain High on Relatively Tight Supply and Slightly Improving Downstream Demand_SMM
summary: SMM expects SHFE nickel to remain supported as pure nickel supply stays tight, keeping spot premiums high and Indonesian NPI nearly fully booked. Downstream demand for stainless steel/alloys is only slightly improving, and some restocking occurs ahead of Chinese New Year, supporting a bullish tone for nickel in the near term.

title: Nickel Prices Remain High and spot Transactions were Thin_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Dec 27 spot nickel premiums: Jinchuan at about 8,500 yuan/mt and NORNICKEL around 7,150 yuan/mt, both lower than the prior day. Premiums eased as traders became more willing to ship late month, but spot transactions were thin because high futures prices and weak briquette liquidity limited buying.

title: Copper hits 2-week high on China recovery optimism
summary: London and Shanghai copper prices rose, with LME three-month copper hitting a two-week high, as China signaled it will end inbound quarantine from Jan. 8 and resume overseas visas. Optimism over demand and falling SHFE copper inventories supported prices, though analysts warned near-term demand weakness from cases and holidays.

title: Indonesia to Ban Bauxite Exports from June 2023: An Explainer
summary: Indonesia announced a bauxite export ban from June 2023, stopping exports of bauxite ore and bleached bauxite to push domestic downstream processing. Since bauxite is the key input for alumina and aluminium, the tighter supply outlook—especially for China—could support higher aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Imported Copper Transactions are in a Stalemate Near the Year-End_SMM
summary: Yangshan copper premiums under warrants stayed around $30-50/mt and were flat, while bill-of-lading premiums were $25-40/mt. Import losses rose to about 720 yuan/mt amid a weaker SHFE/LME ratio. Domestic spot premiums fell further (avg -135 yuan/mt), leaving buyers offering very low prices and trading near-stalled.

title: Negotiations to resurrect Ferndale aluminum plant fall apart
summary: Negotiations to restart the Alcoa Ferndale aluminium smelter failed, mainly over BPA electricity pricing terms. The plant needs large power loads and high upgrade costs, and electricity rate transfer rules constrain the desired “industrial” rate. If not revived, US supply expectations for aluminium are lower.

title: Copper hits two-week high on easing China COVID controls
summary: Copper prices rose to a two-week high as China began easing zero-COVID rules, boosting market mood and prompting buying. Reuters notes that recession risks and expectations of weaker demand limited upside, while supply concerns offered some support. The focus is primarily on near-term copper demand expectations.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28 Letter From the Chairman
summary: Nickel 28’s chairman provides a year-end update tied to its Ramu Nickel operation and nickel sulphide royalties. It discusses 2022 nickel market dynamics, higher sulfur costs, expected nickel/cobalt production, and that debt repayment timing depends on nickel prices. It also references progress at Dumont and Turnagain projects.

title: Chinese Imports of Copper Concentrate from the Americas Burgeon Sharply MoM in November 2022_SMM
summary: China’s copper concentrate imports rose sharply in Nov 2022, but December saw frequent supply-side and port disruptions. A fire at Chile’s Ventanas port, Peru unrest impacting Matarani port and roads, Las Bambas warehousing constraints, and a US truck strike likely hinder Americas shipments, weighing near-term supply and supporting copper prices.

title: A Production Accident in a Large Nickel Project in Indonesia Affects the Operation of Some Production Lines_SMM
summary: PT GNI in North Morowali, Indonesia, faced a smelter incident after coal dust exploded, causing deaths and shutting two production lines for overhaul. Workers protested over safety and pay demands. The first phase of GNI is planned to reach production with multiple lines, but the accident implies short-term output losses.

title: Nickel Price Forecast: Top Trends that Will Impact Nickel in 2023
summary: The article argues nickel is likely to stay oversupplied through 2026 due to strong Indonesian output and weaker demand for stainless steel and nickel batteries. It notes quota changes have only stabilized prices, inventories are mixed (LME up, SHFE down), and soft China steel/EV trends weigh, despite risks from US-Iran energy bottlenecks.

title: Shrinking Demand amid the Spread of COVID-19 Outbreaks Offers Limited Support to the High Nickel Prices_SMM
summary: SMM links the COVID-19 spread to softer overall demand, noting suppressed pure nickel demand because nickel prices remain high. Spot transactions are thin and Jinchuan and NORNICKEL nickel premiums fell. While NPI supply is relatively tight and SS futures rose, pure nickel demand cannot support prices.

title: CSPT Sets the Spot Copper Concentrate TCs for the First Quarter of 2023 at $93/mt_SMM
summary: CSPT set spot copper concentrate treatment charges for Q1 2023 at $93/mt ($0.093/lb), according to SMM. The TC level is unchanged from Q4 2022. Since treatment charges impact smelter economics but this update is flat, any near-term copper price effect is likely limited.

title: Review of Refined Nickel Market in 2022 and Outlook_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reviews 2022 nickel volatility and outlines 2023 risks. It cites falling LME inventories early in the year, later demand weakness, tight spot supply from a closed import window, and then expects a significant refined nickel and overall primary nickel surplus. Rising NPI supply and pessimistic macro could keep nickel prices downward.

title: Pure Nickel Premiums Trend Lower, while the Transactions are Slack_SMM
summary: SMM reports spot premiums for Jinchuan nickel fell to 7,000–8,000 yuan/mt, with the average down 1,000 yuan/mt day-on-day. Nornickel premiums also declined. Traders ship more as month-end approaches, but spot transactions stay thin due to high futures prices and weak demand for nickel briquettes.

title: Copper Is Sliding. Where Inflation Could Send Prices.
summary: The piece says copper could fall nearly 20% over the next 12 months. It attributes the expected decline to demand cooling amid a likely economic slowdown, while supplies are described as staying stable. The message points to weaker copper demand and downside price pressure.

title: Copper slides as focus shifts to poor demand prospects
summary: Copper prices fell as markets focused on poor near-term demand prospects. Surging COVID infections in top consumer China and recession fears raised expectations of slower industrial activity. Traders looked to upcoming Chinese manufacturing PMIs for clues. LME copper ended down 0.2% and technical levels were highlighted.

title: Norsk Hydro : Hydro investing in the green transition and Norwegian aluminium plants
summary: Norsk Hydro outlines NOK 3 billion of investments to upgrade Norwegian primary aluminium plants, adding recycling, carbon capture, and green-hydrogen-related technologies to produce low/zero-carbon aluminium. It also cites demand growth for low-carbon metal. Management says the current aluminium market is challenging with high inventories.

title: Altiplano Metals Inc.: Altiplano Reports November 2022 Results at Farellon with Copper Grade at 2.10%
summary: Altiplano Metals reported November 2022 operating results from its Farellon copper-gold mine in Chile. Copper grade improved to 2.10% from 1.87% in October, with higher production, processing, and copper sales of 131,153 pounds. Revenue rose to about US$308,000 after costs, alongside stockpiling and ongoing ramp-up.

title: SMM Updates on Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventories as of December 29_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s social inventories of aluminium ingots rose to 493,000 mt (+18,000 w/w) and aluminium billets to 60,900 mt (+5,100 w/w). Demand is weak in the off-season, billet supply remains abundant, and seasonal accumulation is likely, which could pressure aluminium prices.

title: SMM Sees Limited Impact from China's Aluminium Export Tariff Hike Next Year_SMM
summary: SMM reports China will increase the export tariff on primary aluminium from 15% to 30% from Jan 1, 2023. Despite this, SMM expects limited short-term effects because aluminium exports have already fallen sharply, with monthly volumes below 3,000 mt in recent months. Longer-term effects may depend on overseas price premiums.

title: China Leaves Import and Export Tariffs Untouched for Copper Products in 2023_SMM
summary: SMM reports that China’s 2023 import and export tariff settings for copper-related products will remain unchanged from 2022, effective Jan 1. The update indicates no new tariff shock for cross-border copper product flows, likely stabilizing expectations rather than adding bullish or bearish near-term price pressure.

title: Review of Copper Cathode Rod Market in H2 2022_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: An SMM survey says copper cathode-rod operating rates improved in H2 2022 due to restocking when copper prices fell and tight copper scrap supply that lifted scrap prices above cathode. Still, September-October season weakness, high premiums, COVID disruptions, and price spread swings hurt consumption and orders, weakening Q4 output.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Subject to Ransomware Attack and Implements Risk Management Systems and Protocols
summary: Copper Mountain Mining said its Copper Mountain Mine and corporate IT systems were hit by ransomware on Dec. 27. Operations were isolated, manual processes used, and the mill preventatively shut down to assess control-system impact. The company expects temporary disruption and additional safeguards, with no safety or environmental incidents reported.

title: Nevada Copper Receives US$20 Million from Closing of Second Tranche of Restart Financing Package and Provides Update
summary: Nevada Copper said a second US$20 million tranche of restart financing was released from escrow, enabling progress on ramp-up at its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper mine. The company also outlined continued capital and development work. The funding and restart momentum may modestly improve near-term expectations for copper supply.

title: Local company in billion dollar deal for copper mine
summary: Osisko Bermuda agreed to a revised deal involving a silver stream and a backstop copper stream to help fund Metals Acquisition Corp’s $1.1B purchase of the CSA copper-silver mine in New South Wales. The financing structure and copper-focused stream support near-term copper supply expectations and sentiment.

title: China's Primary Aluminium Imports in November Increased 64.1% on the Month But Fell 51.7% on the Year_SMM
summary: China imported about 110,678 mt of primary aluminium in November 2022, up 64.1% month-on-month but down 51.7% year-on-year. Imports totaled 540,400 mt in January–November, down 66% year-on-year. The monthly jump suggests improved near-term supply flows into the domestic aluminium market.

title: SHFE Aluminium Fell For Two Consecutive Days amid A Lack of Support From Fundamentals_SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium fell again as macro sentiment faded and aluminium fundamentals weighed on prices. Social inventories in major markets rose, with more ingot arrivals and weaker off-season/pandemic demand. Spot discounts widened and power rationing in Guizhou was reported to expand further, renewing fears of additional production disruption. Prices are expected rangebound near term.

title: SMM Analysis on Impact of Adjustment to Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Export Tariffs in 2023 _SMM
summary: China announced higher export tariffs on primary aluminium from Jan 1, 2023, replacing provisional duties with a 30% export levy. SMM expects export volumes—especially high-purity primary aluminium—to decline and the export window to remain largely closed, potentially tightening domestic availability and supporting aluminium prices.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Adds 18,200 mt from Monday_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventory across major Chinese markets rose to 97,900 mt, up 18,200 mt from Monday, the highest in three weeks. The build reflects suppressed downstream buying from higher prices and COVID-19-driven consumption disruptions. SMM expects limited imported arrivals and only a gradual further inventory increase next week.

title: Key Takeaway from SMM Nonferrous Metals Industry Annual Conference: Domestic Aluminium Output in 2023 to Increase Further with Demand Returning to Positive Growth _SMM
summary: SMM says aluminium output in 2022 rose despite Q3 power-tightness that shut/squeezed smelters in Sichuan and Yunnan, with further curtailments into early 2023. For 2023, production should keep increasing but demand is expected to recover via PV and NEVs, while inventories stay low, supporting prices.

title: Port Inventory of Nickel Ore Up 141,000 wmt from December 23_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports rose by 141,000 wmt to 9.18 million wmt by Dec 30, with Ni content around 72,000 mt. Arrivals increased, and Philippine rainy-season shipments were reduced, but downstream demand remained weak. NPI plants ran at low rates, consuming ore slowly.

title: 'Join the joyride': the mystery syndicate behind Clive Palmer's nickel payday
summary: Clive Palmer’s Queensland Nickel refinery is set to be acquired by Switzerland-based Zero Carbon Investek for about $1.5 billion, contingent on Queensland port access and pending Foreign Investment Review Board approval. The move could enable restart-related supply improvements for nickel, supportive for near-term nickel market sentiment.

title: Battery metal binge outweighs cost hikes at PolyMet copper-nickel project in Minnesota
summary: The Northern Miner reports that surging demand for battery metals is offsetting higher construction costs for PolyMet Mining’s copper-nickel NorthMet project in northeastern Minnesota. Updated estimates suggest the first phase of the open-pit operation remains economically supported despite cost inflation, which can improve near-term sentiment for both copper and nickel.

title: Battery metal binge outweighs cost hikes at PolyMet copper-nickel project in Minnesota
