summary: Quebec plans to kick off its 2023 drilling program at the Ducros nickel project. The update relates to ongoing development and exploration activity for nickel supply prospects. While not an immediate increase in output, it can offer modest positive sentiment for nickel markets over the coming weeks.

title: UPDATE 1-Trafigura plans to take large amounts of LME copper -sources
summary: Trafigura plans to withdraw large amounts of copper from LME-registered warehouses, likely keeping the metal in Europe. LME registered stocks are low and cancelled warrants have surged, raising supply concerns. The cash discount to the three-month contract has narrowed, alongside a sharp LME copper price rally.

title: Nickel Prices Face Bearish Production Forecasts
summary: The piece discusses nickel’s post-squeeze volatility and reports negotiations where Tsingshan may switch inputs with Chinese copper producers to boost refined nickel output, potentially raising global supply. It also cites expected higher nickel production from Indonesia efforts, implying surplus risk and possible downside pressure on prices.

title: China-owned nickel smelter in Indonesia resumes production after deadly riot
summary: Production restarted at PT Gunbuster Nickel Industry (GNI) in Indonesia after a deadly weekend riot damaged parts of the plant and followed labor unrest over wages and safety. Management reported 2,963 employees, including 350 Chinese workers, returning to work. Security remains heightened while authorities investigate causes.

title: Bullish Catalysts Are Mounting For Copper
summary: Copper prices surged above $9,000/t as China abandoned zero-Covid and markets anticipated a demand rebound after Lunar New Year. The piece cites supportive China property/economic stimulus, low LME/SHFE/COMEX inventories, and a weaker US dollar easing monetary-tightening concerns, offering bullish near-term upside despite COVID-case risks.

title: Production resumes at nickel smelter after deadly clash
summary: Production has resumed at PT Gunbuster Nickel Industry (GNI), a nickel smelter owned by Jiangsu Delong Nickel, after operations were suspended following weekend protests and rioting that killed two workers. With production restarting, near-term nickel supply risk eases, which can be supportive for nickel prices.

title: BASF, Eramet to finalise $2.6 billion partnership on Indonesia nickel smelter -Indonesia
summary: BASF and Eramet are set to finalise a $2.6 billion partnership to build/operate a nickel smelter in Indonesia. The planned investment increases expectations for future nickel refining supply, which can weigh on nickel prices as markets anticipate more availability.

title: Why LME Copper Prices Outpace SHFE Copper Prices? Views on Direction in Short-Term_SMM
summary: LME copper rebounded to a 7-month high while SHFE lagged. The piece links LME strength to low global visible inventories and overseas traders pricing in expectations of stronger Chinese demand after zero-Covid disruptions. It also notes SHFE stock build-up and earlier holiday closures hurting near-term domestic demand.

title: BASF, Eramet Plan $2.6 Billion Nickel Smelter in Indonesia
summary: BASF and Eramet plan to invest about $2.6 billion in a nickel smelter in Indonesia. The project would ultimately increase nickel refining capacity and influence longer-run supply expectations, but the article provides no near-term commissioning timeline, suggesting limited immediate (days-to-weeks) price pressure.

title: Stellantis and Terrafame Agree on Low-Carbon Nickel Sulphate Supply for Electric Vehicle Batteries
summary: Stellantis and Terrafame signed a five-year supply agreement beginning in 2025 for low-carbon nickel sulphate used in EV batteries. Terrafame will provide a significant portion of Stellantis’ sustainable nickel needs for its electrification plans, reinforcing demand expectations for nickel battery inputs.

title: Antofagasta Plc FY22 Gold, Copper Output Fall, But In Line With Expectations
summary: Antofagasta reported lower FY22 gold and especially copper production versus 2021, citing drought-linked throughput reductions at Los Pelambres and reduced concentrate pipeline availability. Fourth-quarter copper output and sales improved. The company said the FY22 decline matched expectations and forecast 2023 copper output of 670,000–710,000 tons.

title: Stellantis strikes nickel sulphate supply deal with Terrafame
summary: Stellantis has signed a nickel sulphate supply deal with Terrafame, Reuters reports. Nickel sulphate is used to produce battery materials for EVs, so the agreement is likely to bolster expectations for near-term nickel demand and strengthen sentiment around nickel prices over the coming weeks.

title: Fabled Copper Corp.: Fabled Copper Reports 0.90% Copper over 22.90 meters and 2.09% copper over 6.10 meters On the Ringarooma Copper Occurrence
summary: Fabled Copper Corp. reported 2022 surface sampling results from the Muskwa Project’s Ringarooma copper occurrence in northern British Columbia. Results include contiguous chip sampling of 0.90% copper over 22.90 meters and higher-grade intervals. The update is exploration-focused with no production or supply commitments.

title: African Energy Metals Inc.: African Energy Acquires Mali Project with Uranium, Copper and Silver Resources and Announces Financing
summary: African Energy Metals will acquire GoviEx’s Malian subsidiary holding the Falea uranium project, with disclosed copper resources (including indicated and inferred copper grades) and additional exploration upside. The deal and related equity financing are subject to TSXV approvals, but there are no immediate production changes affecting copper demand or supply.

title: BASF nears $2.6bn deal with Eramet for Indonesian nickel project
summary: BASF is nearing a $2.6bn deal with Eramet to invest in an Indonesia Weda Bay HPAL plant producing mixed hydroxide precipitate (MHP) for EV batteries. The project targets up to 67,000 tpa nickel (and ~7,000 tpa cobalt). Decisions are expected in early 2023; commissioning is planned for early 2026.

title: Ero Copper Achieves Record Full-Year Copper and Gold Production and Provides 2023 Guidance
summary: Ero Copper reported record 2022 copper output at Caraíba and issued 2023 guidance for copper in concentrate (44,000–47,000 tonnes). It also entered zero-cost collars for 3,000 tonnes per month of copper, establishing a $3.50/lb floor. The update is mildly supportive but not market-moving.

title: American Copper Development Corporation (Formerly Known as Cirrus Gold Corp.): American Copper Development Corporation Completes 134 line-km Titan 160 DCIP and MT Survey Over the Lordsburg Property, New Mexico
summary: American Copper Development Corp. reports preliminary 3D DCIP/IP and MT survey results at its Lordsburg, New Mexico property, pointing to a district-scale porphyry signature and copper-bearing potential at depth. The company plans a 5,000m Phase I drill program in mid-February to test targets identified by the survey and historic mines.

title: Chile rejects $2.5bn iron and copper mine planned near penguin reserve
summary: Chile’s government rejected the $2.5bn Dominga open-pit iron and copper mine and port project near the Humboldt penguin reserve, citing insufficient mitigation for marine and nature impacts. The decision removes a potential copper supply development in a key producer region, likely tightening near-term expectations.

title: EVs need nickel: Minnesota metal company digs for the solution with new mine
summary: Talon Metals, in partnership with Rio Tinto, plans to develop a nickel mine in Tamarack, Minnesota, expected to operate in 2026, while also striking a Tesla deal for nickel for EV batteries. It highlights depleting global supply and the closure of Michigan’s nickel mine, suggesting nickel tightness risk. Community objections are noted.

title: Stellantis signs nickel sulphate deal for EV batteries
summary: Stellantis said it has signed a supply agreement to secure nickel sulphate for electric vehicle batteries, sourced from Finland-based Terrafame. The deal signals additional committed demand for battery-grade nickel compounds, which can tighten market expectations and provide bullish support for nickel prices in the near term.

title: Canada Nickel confirms major discovery larger than flagship Crawford project in Ontario
summary: Canada Nickel says assay results confirm the Reid property is a major discovery, with a target footprint larger than its flagship Crawford nickel-cobalt project in Ontario’s Timmins-Cochrane camp. The news highlights expanding resource potential, which may lift near-term market sentiment for nickel supply expectations.

title: Indonesia bauxite ban: Aussie miners to gain as Jakarta defies global trade rules
summary: Indonesia says it will stop exporting bauxite from June, aiming to expand domestic refining into alumina and higher value manufacturing. The policy shifts bauxite supply away from global traders, likely tightening feedstock availability for alumina producers and weighing on near-term aluminium market sentiment and prices.

title: Nickel Prices Rebounded and Spot Transactions were Thin_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports a rebound in Shanghai spot nickel. SHFE nickel rose as funds supported prices; Jinchuan nickel premiums increased to about 11,500 yuan/mt. NORNICKEL premiums declined, but spot prices still rebounded. Nickel briquette prices rose sharply, though briquette trading remained weak versus nickel sulphate.

title: Domestic Alumina Prices are Stable and Overseas Prices Remain High_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s domestic alumina prices are stable as cold weather and the approaching Chinese New Year disrupt logistics and finished-product deliveries, while air-pollution controls and natural-gas shortages reduce north China alumina plant output. Overseas prices remain high; Brazil alumina was sold at $390/mt FOB, up $10/mt from Jan 9.

title: Aluminum price forecasts surge due to higher demand in Europe and China
summary: Goldman Sachs raised its aluminium price forecast amid visible global inventories at about 1.4 million tons, the lowest since 2002. Europe has cut production by 1.4 million tons, and sanctioned Russian supply is diverted to Asia. With deficit risks and easing macro/dollar headwinds, analysts expect higher aluminium prices into spring.

title: Alumina stock slumps 6pc on inflation and low demand
summary: Alumina Ltd’s shares fell 6.7% after Alcoa’s downbeat results. The companies’ refinery margins were hit as inflation increased unit costs while alumina prices stayed subdued, constraining Alcoa’s fourth-quarter cash flow and affecting near-term sentiment around alumina supply economics.

title: Copper's Rally Keeps Rolling Along. China Will Drive the Comeback.
summary: Copper prices have rebounded sharply early in the year, regaining much of the prior-year losses. The article attributes the strength to prospects for higher demand from China as Beijing eases Covid-19 restrictions, suggesting improved consumption that supports copper prices in the coming weeks.

title: SMM Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventories in China as of January 19_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s aluminium ingot social inventories rose to 744,000 mt on Jan 19, up 15.8% on the week, and may add over 160,000 mt during the CNY holiday, reaching ~920,000 mt. Aluminium billet inventories also climbed to 131,900 mt, with further increases expected.

title: Alcoa's Bauxite, Alumina, and Aluminium Production All Declined in 2022_SMM
summary: SMM reports Alcoa’s 2022 output fell: bauxite -11.6% YoY to 42.1 Mt, alumina -5.4% to 12.54 Mt, and primary aluminium -8.3% to 2.01 Mt. The lower upstream and primary output points to reduced aluminium supply, which could be supportive for near-term aluminium prices.

title: BASF, Eramet 'near $2.6b deal to process nickel for EV batteries'
summary: BASF and Eramet are in final stages of a roughly $2.6b partnership to build a hydro-metallurgical facility in Indonesia to produce battery-grade nickel (MHP) from Eramet’s Weda Bay mine. Officials cite potential investment approval in early 2023, boosting expectations for future nickel supply into EV batteries.

title: Union Budget: Ficci seeks increase in import duty of aluminium, aluminium products
summary: India’s Ficci asked for a rise in import duty on aluminium and aluminium products to at least 12.5% (from 10%) to curb low-quality dumping-heavy imports, mainly from China. It also seeks rationalised duties and reduced coal cess to cut costs for power-intensive aluminium producers, supporting domestic demand.

title: Budget 2023: FICCI backs higher duties on imported aluminium products to boost domestic manufacturing
summary: FICCI’s pre-Budget 2023 proposals urge the government to raise duties on imported aluminium products to encourage domestic manufacturing. The policy direction implies reduced import inflows and stronger support for the local aluminium supply chain, which can translate into near-term upward pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Alcoa Drops on Hit From Aluminum Prices
summary: Alcoa shares fell after the company reported lower prices for its aluminum products at the end of 2022. The article also highlights a potential margin squeeze in 2023, implying pressure on aluminum pricing and profitability. Overall, the piece is more company-specific than a clear new aluminum market catalyst.

title: Copper Clad Laminates Market worth $21.6 billion in 2027 - Exclusive Report by MarketsandMarkets
summary: PRNewswire/MarketsandMarkets projects rapid growth for the copper wire and cable market through 2032, citing electrification, grid modernization, renewable integration, EV charging, and underground power projects. While the piece is a long-run market forecast, it signals improving copper demand expectations that could support copper prices over coming weeks.

title: Is Zambia's drive for 3m tonnes of copper a year by 2031 a shiny dream?
summary: The piece discusses Zambia’s goal to triple copper output to nearly 3m tonnes per year by 2031, attributing the outlook to improved investment conditions under President Hakainde Hichilema and supportive policy direction. Copperbelt Energy Corporation says opportunities are perking up, but the timeline is largely long term.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: US EV Battery Supply Chain: Talon Metals Confirms Potential New System of High-Grade Nickel Mineralization at Tamarack Nickel Project in Central Minnesota
summary: Talon Metals announced new drilling results at its Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project, identifying a “Raptor Zone” with high-grade nickel-copper massive sulphide intersections in multiple holes outside the current resource area. The company frames this as evidence of district-scale potential, which could affect near-term nickel sentiment and, secondarily, copper.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Drilling Recommences at Amarc's Duke Copper-Gold District, BC
summary: Amarc Resources said core drilling has resumed at its Duke porphyry Cu-Au district in central British Columbia after a holiday break, with one rig now drilling and a second joining soon. The 2023 program tests the Duke deposit and nearby IP anomaly under a Boliden earn-in funding plan.

title: Business News | Budget 2023: FICCI Backs Higher Duties on Imported Aluminium Products to Boost Domestic Manufacturing
summary: FICCI’s pre-budget proposal calls for increasing import duties on aluminium and aluminium products to at least 12.5% to curb dumping, especially from China, where it accounts for most downstream imports. It also seeks changes to coal/cess treatment and inverted duty structures, aiming to boost domestic aluminium manufacturing.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Announces Positive PEA with Net Present Value of $324M on Carmacks Copper-Gold Project in Yukon, Canada
summary: Granite Creek Copper reported positive Preliminary Economic Assessment results for its Carmacks copper-gold-silver project in Yukon, including NPV/IRR sensitivity to copper prices and planned open-pit processing. The news highlights project viability and expansion potential but provides no near-term production or supply impact for the copper market.

title: What's behind copper's impressive rise?
summary: Copper has rebounded sharply at the start of the year, recouping most losses from 2022. Analysts link the move to expectations of higher Chinese demand as Covid-19 restrictions end and the economy recovers, alongside a shift toward macro tailwinds from a less hawkish Fed.

title: The Power Play by The Market Herald Releases New Interviews with Blockmate Ventures, Zinc8 Energy, Fabled Copper, Datametrex AI and iMining Technologies Discussing Their Latest News
summary: The article compiles interviews covering multiple companies. The copper-relevant item is Fabled Copper’s report of 2022 surface work results at its Muskwa copper project in British Columbia. The other announcements concern equity listings, zinc-air funding, and AI or power-plant plans, with no direct impact on copper prices.

title: Peru Unrest Threatens to Choke Off Almost 2% of Global Copper Supply
summary: The piece highlights that unrest in Peru may threaten to disrupt copper output, potentially affecting close to 2% of global supply. Such a supply-shock risk typically tightens near-term availability expectations, helping support copper prices in the coming days.

title: Chile rejects permit for $2.5bn Dominga copper project
summary: Chile rejected the permits for Andes Iron’s $2.5bn Dominga project near ecological reserves, citing water, wildlife, air quality and marine-protected area impacts. The project included two open-pit mines and was expected to produce 150,000tpa of copper, effectively reducing future supply expectations and supporting copper prices.

title: Talon Metals finds new nickel and copper zone several kilometres from Tamarack
summary: Talon Metals says it has identified a new nickel and copper mineralization zone about 3.2 km from its Tamarack project in central Minnesota. The discovery is expected to boost sentiment around potential future output. Near-term effects are likely limited pending further drilling, assays, and resource definition.

title: Talon Metals finds new nickel and copper zone several kilometres from Tamarack
summary: Talon Metals says it has discovered a new system of nickel and copper mineralization about 3.2 km from its Tamarack project in central Minnesota. The company describes the new zone’s location and potential significance, but the announcement is not tied to immediate production changes or inventories.

title: Domestic and Overseas Alumina Prices both Rose _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports alumina prices rising: the domestic weighted index reached 2,945 yuan/mt (+12) and overseas prices climbed to $355/mt FOB Western Australia. Gains were attributed to a 30% Kwinana refinery output cut. Cold weather, transport limits, and natural gas shortages constrained roasting capacity.

title: Thieves dressed as municipal officials steal copper cabling
summary: Thieves posing as municipal officials stole about 25 meters of copper cabling worth R200,000 from a transformer substation in Struandale while workers were absent. Police are investigating, and authorities warn against buying illegal copper. No outages occurred, suggesting mainly localized disruption rather than broader market supply changes.

title: Optimism over Demand Recovery to Sustain Further Rise in SHFE Aluminium after the CNY Holiday_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME aluminium rose over the week, attributing gains to a softer US dollar and growing expectations that China’s demand will recover after the CNY holiday. It also cites power rationing-induced capacity cuts in southwest China as supply support, though inventories remain elevated and the market surplus persists.

title: Spot Nickel Trading to Pick up Post-Holiday_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel prices fell despite China’s GDP growth being at a normal level. Markets focus on upcoming US core PCE data and potential Fed tightening, which could strengthen the dollar and pressure commodities. Fundamentals show weak import clearance, weaker spot transactions, and tight deliverable refined nickel, suggesting limited near-term support.

title: SHFE Nickel Price Drop this Week amid Shrinking Demand for Pure Nickel_SMM
summary: SHFE nickel prices fell this week despite China’s 2022 GDP growth normalizing. Market support was limited as upstream sellers offered less and NPI producers kept low finished-product inventories. Downstream demand stayed soft due to CNY holiday rest. Ahead, potential US Fed tightening risks remain bearish for commodity prices. Nickel expected to drop further pre-CNY.

title: Copper drifts lower as China kicks off Lunar New Year holiday
summary: Copper prices edged lower as China’s Lunar New Year reopened trade demand expectations but near-term consumption signals stayed weak. Analysts cited soft onshore physicals, negative import arbitrage and a sharp jump in SHFE copper inventories, with smelter production outpacing holiday demand.

title: China's Copper Costs Driven Up By Maike's Woes, Output Glitches
summary: China’s refined copper buyers face much higher costs as Maike’s financial woes reduce import availability and domestic smelters undergo maintenance. This has lifted Guangdong and Shanghai local premiums to multi-year highs, potentially pressuring users’ margins while expectations for recovering Chinese demand support global copper.

title: China's copper costs driven up by Maike's woes, output glitches | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Reuters reports China’s copper buyers face higher costs as Maike’s financial woes cause import supply disruptions and domestic smelters undergo maintenance. Copper premiums over Shanghai futures have surged to multi-year highs, suggesting tighter refined supply. Analysts also flag uncertainty around import volumes despite improved demand expectations.

title: China's copper costs driven up by Maike's woes, output glitches | Kat Country 98.9
summary: Reuters reports China’s copper buyers are facing sharply higher costs as Maike Group’s financial problems disrupt refined copper imports and domestic smelter maintenance reduces output. This has pushed China’s domestic copper premiums over Shanghai futures to multi-year highs, potentially straining demand from construction and renewables.

title: China's copper costs driven up by Maike's woes, output glitches
summary: The article headline reports that China’s copper costs are being driven higher by problems at Maike and associated output glitches. This suggests reduced supply or production disruptions in the short term, which typically tightens availability and increases cost pressures for copper.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Dip 96,000 wmt WoW from Last Friday_SMM
summary: SMM says Chinese port nickel ore inventories fell 96,000 wmt WoW to 8.58 million wmt, with Ni content down 1,000 mt to about 67,000 mt. Arrivals were pressured by rainy conditions in the Philippines, while NPI and steel mills suspended output for overhauls. Inventory may decline faster after Chinese New Year.

title: FICCI Demands Higher Import Duty On Aluminium, Aluminium Pro...
summary: FICCI is calling for higher import duties on aluminium. The proposed tariff would likely reduce imports and constrain near-term aluminium availability, supporting domestic prices. The impact is expected within days to weeks as traders price in the likelihood of higher duties and related demand for local supply.

title: Glencore's Antapaccay copper mine in Peru faces new attack as fire lit on grounds -source
summary: Protests reportedly sparked a fire at Glencore’s Antapaccay copper mine in Peru, seen in the workers’ housing area, with video footage showing flammable material near the site. The incident raises the risk of short-term operational disruption, supporting expectations for tighter copper supply and potentially higher prices in the coming days.

title: Glencore's Antapaccay copper mine attacked, fire breaks out – source | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: Protesters allegedly set flammable material near fences at Glencore’s Antapaccay copper mine in Peru, causing a fire to spread through nearby worker housing. The incident follows prior disruptions when the mine was operating at restricted capacity due to anti-government protests.

title: Glencore's Antapaccay copper mine attacked, fire breaks out – source | The Mighty 790 KFGO
summary: Glencore’s Antapaccay copper mine in Peru faced another disruption after a fire spread through nearby worker housing, believed to have been started by protesters. The mine was already running at “restricted” capacity earlier this week due to anti-government unrest following the president’s ouster. Such interruptions heighten near-term copper supply risk.

title: Glencore's Antapaccay copper mine attacked, fire breaks out - source
summary: Reuters reports protesters attacked Glencore’s Antapaccay copper mine in Peru, with a fire breaking out near worker housing and possibly started by demonstrators. The mine had been operating at restricted capacity earlier in the week due to unrest, indicating continued supply disruption risk for near-term copper output.

title: Glencore's Antapaccay copper mine attacked, fire breaks out – source
summary: A fire at Glencore’s Antapaccay copper mine in Peru spread through nearby worker housing, believed to be sparked by protesters, after weeks of anti-government unrest. The mine had already been running at restricted capacity due to protests earlier this week, implying further short-term copper supply disruption.

title: LS C&S expands aluminum material biz for EV components
summary: LS C&S, via affiliate LS Alsco, is expanding its high-strength aluminum materials for EV components, with alloy AA8031 approved and already used in Hyundai and Kia vehicles since 2019. The firm projects aluminum will increasingly replace copper in weight-sensitive automotive wiring, supporting aluminium demand growth.

title: Tertiary Minerals receives EPB approval for Zambian copper project
summary: Tertiary Minerals says ZEMA has approved the EPB for its Mushima North copper project in Zambia, following prior EPB approvals for other projects. With approval, field exploration can proceed as the company plans assays on recovered historical drill core and continues work ahead of the next exploration season.

title: Access to Almost 2% of Global Copper Supply Under Threat Over Peru Unrest
summary: Peru’s political unrest threatens nearly 2% of global copper supply as major mines cut output or fail to dispatch concentrate. Glencore’s Antapaccay suspended operations after attacks, and Las Bambas shut down and halted shipments. With inventories at historical lows, the disruption could tighten supply and lift copper prices.

title: PACRO discusses nickel and site cleanup
summary: Paducah Area Community Reuse Organization officials discussed 10,000 tons of nickel held at the DOE Paducah site and said a major battery company is interested in partnering. The piece focuses on site cleanup and collaboration plans, without specifying timing or any confirmed nickel sale or release into markets.

title: Glencore's Antapaccay copper mine attacked, fire breaks out – source | WTVB | 1590 AM · 95.5 FM
summary: Reuters reports that protesters are believed to have started a fire near Glencore’s Antapaccay copper mine in Peru, spreading through nearby worker housing. The mine had already been operating at restricted capacity earlier due to protests. The disruption increases near-term copper supply uncertainty.

title: Indonesia's Bakrie Group seeks nickel mine, partners up for $9 billion EV project
summary: Bakrie Group, with Envision and Glencore, plans a $9 billion industrial park and seeks to acquire a nickel mine in Sulawesi to supply nickel smelting and EV battery precursor production. The consortium targets nickel-based precursor output by 2026, supporting Indonesian battery-material demand expectations.

title: The Fiji TimesGlencore copper mine in Peru suspends operations after another attack
summary: Glencore suspended operations at its Antapaccay copper mine in Peru after protesters attacked the site again, following other disruptions all month. Road blockades prevented concentrate supply and reduced workforce presence. The company cited unacceptable risk and halted mineral concentrate transport temporarily, implying near-term copper supply tightness.

title: Topic | Bauxite | The Sydney Morning Herald
summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports that Alcoa is fined $55 million and faces further scrutiny over alleged environmental breaches tied to its WA bauxite mining exemptions, including potential tighter mining approvals. It also notes South32’s WA alumina business faces proposed environmental protections, threatening operational viability and supply.

title: Topic | Bauxite | Brisbane Times
summary: Multiple reports describe Alcoa being fined $55 million and facing further scrutiny over clearing and bauxite mining approvals in Western Australia, alongside concerns that stricter environmental protections could threaten operations. South32’s WA alumina business valuation is cut amid proposed protections, implying potential production disruption.

title: Potanin says sanctions constrain Nornickel, force it to adjust strategy
summary: The piece (based on the title) says that sanctions are constraining Nornickel and forcing the company to adjust its strategy. This implies potential near-term disruptions to nickel output, refining or shipments, which would likely tighten effective supply and weigh on nickel prices.

title: Copper firms on China demand hopes; Lunar New Year break curbs trading
summary: London copper rose 0.58% as hopes grew for China’s post-COVID reopening demand recovery and the dollar weakened. Trading stayed subdued due to Lunar New Year closure. The piece also flags potential copper supply risk from social unrest in Peru. LME aluminium fell 0.56% at the same time.

title: Metal Energy Corp.: Metal Energy Drills Three Holes with Broad Nickel Intersections Including 85.3 m of 0.67% NiEq at Manibridge Project
summary: Metal Energy announced assay results from three drill holes at its Manibridge nickel project in Manitoba, reporting broad high-grade nickel intersections including 85.3m of 0.67% NiEq and additional intervals with similar NiEq grades. Results extend mineralization down dip and support improved confidence in the nickel resource at Manibridge.

title: ATAC Discovers Additional High-grade Copper and Gold Mineralization at Catch Property, Yukon
summary: ATAC says it has discovered additional high-grade copper (and gold) mineralization at its Catch Property in Yukon. The finding may slightly improve perceived future copper resource potential, but it is unlikely to affect immediate supply and therefore should have only a modest, short-term supportive effect on copper sentiment.

title: Deposits of gold, coal, iron and copper returned to state fund of Kazakhstan
summary: Kazakhstan terminated 115 contracts and 198 licenses for solid mineral resources in 2022 and returned related deposits to the state fund, including copper (alongside gold, coal, and iron). The headline suggests changes to mining rights that could introduce near-term supply or investment uncertainty for copper.

title: Capella Initiates Scout Drilling at the Kjøli Copper-Cobalt Project, Norway
summary: Capella Minerals started a 1,250m scout diamond drill program at its Kjøli copper-cobalt-zinc VMS project in Norway, targeting Kjøli Deeps, mine extensions, and nearby geophysical anomalies. Assays are expected by early April, potentially improving outlook for future copper resource growth, which can slightly support copper sentiment.

title: Official: Iran ramping up alumina production with Chinese help
summary: Iranian officials say the country is studying to expand annual alumina output to 500,000 tonnes with Chinese support, improving self-sufficiency and reducing costly imports. Alumina is converted into aluminium metal, and the Jajarm refinery is already operating, with plans for higher capacity.

title: Jarrah forests get small reprieve after Alcoa drops bauxite export plan
summary: Alcoa has scrapped plans to increase bauxite mining for export from WA’s Northern Jarrah Forest. The company will preserve bauxite output for its three West Australian alumina refineries, prioritizing value-add. WA regulators are reviewing future mine footprint options amid rising environmental scrutiny.

title: Clive Palmer's companies gain port access for Queensland nickel refinery
summary: Port of Townsville has approved arrangements to restart nickel ore imports and nickel product exports for the mothballed Queensland Nickel refinery in Queensland, which has been tied up in legal and financial hurdles. The renewed port access is expected to support plans to revive output, influencing nickel supply expectations.

title: Marimaca Copper infill drilling yields best results to date at oxide deposit in Chile
summary: Marimaca Copper released final reverse-circulation drill results from an infill program at its Marimaca oxide deposit in northern Chile, highlighting the best copper intersection drilled to date. The upbeat drilling outcome can improve expectations for the project’s copper resources and feedstock potential, supporting near-term copper sentiment.

title: Extremely Tight Market Could Push Copper Prices To Record Highs
summary: A Bloomberg MLIV Pulse survey and subsequent commentary highlight copper’s strong rebound and expectation of a record high, driven by China reopening, policy-driven energy-transition demand, and minimal supply response. Goldman and Glencore warn of an emerging supply crunch and large deficits, while new data shows rising net bullish positioning.

title: Osisko Metals Reports Additional Drill Results at Mount Copper Including 1011.0 Metres Grading 0.46% Copper and 3.19 g/t Silver
summary: Osisko Metals said it has received additional drill results from its Mount Copper project, highlighting intercepts of 1011.0 metres at 0.46% copper and 3.19 g/t silver. The update improves project quality and future resource expectations, which can modestly support near-term copper sentiment.

title: Copper inches up in lacklustre trade; U.S. data in focus
summary: LME three-month copper edged up 0.34% to $9,388 per tonne as the dollar weakened, with weaker Chinese demand during Lunar New Year keeping trade lacklustre. Investors await U.S. flash PMI and growth data for direction on Fed policy. Aluminium was also slightly higher at $2,638.50.

title: MAX Resource Corp.: Drill Results of Max Resource Confirm High-Grade Copper Silver at the CESAR Project in NE Colombia
summary: MAX Resource Corp. released drill results from its CESAR project in NE Colombia, confirming continuation of copper-silver mineralization at depth, including intervals of 3.4% Cu over 10.6m and 18.5% Cu over 0.8m. The update may support copper exploration sentiment but does not change near-term supply.

title: India's Copper Demand Bounces Back; Grows 27 per cent in FY22
summary: The report says India’s copper demand rebounded sharply in FY22, rising about 27.5% year-on-year to 12.5 lakh tonnes versus 9.78 lakh tonnes in FY21. The growth is attributed to power infrastructure, real estate, consumer durables, and industrial activity, according to ICA India.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay Announces Accelerated 2023 Exploration and Resource Delineation Program at Storm Copper Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay announced an accelerated 2023 drilling and geophysics program at its Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, targeting expansion and resource delineation of near-surface high-grade copper mineralization and potential direct shipping product mining. The update supports future copper development but does not signal immediate market supply changes.

title: SPC, Vale to consolidate Sudbury nickel/copper deposits in Canada
summary: SPC Nickel and Vale Canada agreed to consolidate adjacent Sudbury deposits, granting SPC Nickel the right to acquire full interest in the Crean Hill 3 nickel-copper property in exchange for development work and a C$1m payment at a feasibility deadline. Vale retains rights/royalties on the combined project.

title: SPC, Vale to consolidate Sudbury nickel/copper deposits in Canada
summary: SPC Nickel and Vale Canada agreed to consolidate adjacent West Graham and Crean Hill 3 deposits in Ontario’s Sudbury camp. SPC can earn full rights to Crean Hill 3 by delivering a feasibility study by June 2026, paying C$1m and granting Vale certain royalties. It targets higher-grade nickel-copper growth.

title: Norilsk Nickel solves problem with feedstock delivery to Harjavalta — Senior VP
summary: Norilsk Nickel says it has overcome complications in feedstock deliveries to its Harjavalta plant in Finland. A contracted Finnish operator is transporting by rail. The company expects possible logistical interruptions later, but has planned conservatively to meet client demand for contracted Finnish volumes versus production capacity.

title: SPC Nickel enters agreement with Vale to consolidate deposits in Sudbury camp
summary: SPC Nickel and Vale Canada signed a cooperation agreement to consolidate SPC Nickel’s West Graham and Crean Hill 3 nickel-copper deposits into a single property in the Sudbury camp. The deal is aimed at streamlining the asset footprint, but it does not indicate any near-term production supply impact.

title: York Harbour Metals Drills High-Grade Intercept of 8.97 Metres of 4.7% Copper, 10.2% Zinc, and 22.7 gpt Silver in a New Area Adjacent to Previous Mine Workings
summary: York Harbour Metals reported new diamond drill assay results from its York Harbour copper-zinc project in Newfoundland, including 8.97 m grading 4.727% copper. The company highlights multiple high-grade copper intercepts and plans to restart drilling for further delineation. The update is sentiment-positive for copper but not near-term supply-changing.

title: BHP to earn 100% stake in three Serbian copper properties
summary: BHP signed an agreement with Mundoro Capital to earn 100% interest in three exploration areas in Serbia’s Timok region: Borsko Jezero, South Timok and Trstenik, targeting porphyry copper deposits. The options require about $1.7m cash and $7.5m exploration over three years, with a 2% NSR royalty retained by Mundoro.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.20% Lower at $4.2455 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures for January delivery settled 0.20% lower at $4.2455 per pound, snapping a two-session winning streak. LME copper cash was also slightly down (about 0.27%). The piece is a market-data recap with no accompanying new fundamentals, so impact is limited.

title: Copper lines worth $78,600 stolen – Times News Online
summary: Police in Tamaqua are investigating theft and criminal mischief at a Lehigh Anthracite property where three utility poles were cut down and stripped of about 90 feet of 3/4-inch copper wire per pole, destroying three transformers. The reported theft and damage value is about $78,600.

title: Brazilian aluminium import market to take a backseat: 2023 preview
summary: Fastmarkets reports Brazilian aluminium import markets are set to shrink as domestic producers raise premiums and the government tightens trade rules (ending duty-free quotas and imposing countervailing duties on Chinese rolled aluminium from April 2023). Aluminium P1020A premiums in São Paulo rose versus earlier weeks, indicating firmer local pricing versus imports.

title: MineHub Technologies Inc.: MineHub and Capstone Copper Enter into Commercial Agreement for Use of the MineHub Platform
summary: MineHub Technologies said Capstone Copper will use its platform and enterprise applications for metals marketing. A first live shipment of roughly 10,000 MT of copper concentrate was initiated from the U.S. to Japan via the MineHub system. The release focuses on digital supply-chain visibility, not a market-wide supply shift.

title: Freeport-McMoRan quarterly profit falls on lower copper price
summary: Freeport-McMoRan reported a quarterly profit decline attributed to a lower copper price. The headline suggests copper prices have recently weakened, which can reinforce bearish sentiment and expectations for near-term pricing pressure in copper markets, even if no explicit supply or demand change is stated.

title: Exclusive-Chile mine delays to slow copper growth; peak seen lower, later -regulator
summary: A Chilean regulator says mine delays will slow copper growth, with the market’s expected peak occurring lower and later. The guidance points to weaker near-term copper production/supply than previously expected, which can tighten sentiment and pressure copper prices lower in the coming days to weeks.

title: Exclusive-Chile Mine Delays To Slow Copper Growth; Peak Seen Lower, Later -regulator
summary: Chile’s regulator Cochilco expects slower copper growth, with output peaking later (around 2030) and lower than previously projected due to delays in mining projects and permitting uncertainties. It flags continued growth to 2033 but anticipates supply tightening versus earlier forecasts, which could support global copper prices.

title: China eyeing nickel market of Indonesia
summary: Nikkei Asia reports China is seeking Indonesia’s large nickel market. It notes protests in Sulawesi, Indonesia’s mineral-rich region, turned violent after disputes tied to a high share of Chinese workers in local companies. Such unrest raises risks of interruptions to nickel production or flows.

title: EXLCUSIVE-CHILE LIKELY COPPER PRODUCTION 5.345 MLN T IN 2022, RI…
summary: Reuters reports COCHILCO’s outlook that Chile’s copper production is likely 5.345 million tonnes in 2022, rising to 5.647 million tonnes this year and 5.891 million tonnes in 2024. The supply outlook implies greater near-term availability, which can pressure copper prices.

title: Iran's aluminum ingot production rises 19 percent in 9 month...
summary: MENAFN reports that Iran’s aluminium ingot production rose 19% over the past nine months. The output increase suggests greater upstream supply of ingot material, which could ease tightness in aluminium availability and put downward pressure on aluminium price expectations in the coming weeks.

title: Critical Metals plc. announces first copper production from Molulu project in DRC
summary: Critical Metals plc says it has started copper ore production at the Molulu project in the DRC, with expectations for increased activity and higher monthly copper ore output as the rainy season ends. The restart follows prior funding for project redeployment, supporting a near-term copper supply-positive narrative.

title: Sudbury-based exploration company hopes to soon become nickel producer
summary: SPC Nickel agreed with Vale to consolidate the Crean Hill 3 nickel-copper property with its Lockerby East assets in Sudbury. The deal enables a combined evaluation and potential open-pit development, starting with a 2023 feasibility study. Production is not expected until years later, limiting near-term price effects.

title: Palladium One Mining Inc.: Palladium One Initiates 2023 Exploration Program and Expands the Tyko Nickel
summary: Palladium One Mining reports staking an additional 4,520 hectares and expanding the Tyko nickel–copper district. A high-resolution airborne magnetic survey is being flown across the expanded property to refine feeder dyke/chonolith structures and improve drill targeting. The release describes exploration activity, not any output or supply disruption.

title: Panama not willing to expand First Quantum's copper mine operations
summary: Panama’s deputy environment minister said the country will not allow First Quantum to expand its Cobre Panama copper mine operations, amid ongoing contract negotiations and environmental disputes. The government also wants tighter monitoring and highlights limited reforestation and pending environmental cases, while considering additional funding via possible fossil-fuel taxes.

title: Panama Not Willing To Expand First Quantum's Copper Mine Operations
summary: Panama told First Quantum it will not allow expansion of the Cobre Panama copper mine’s operating area amid an environmental dispute and negotiations over a new contract. The government also seeks tighter monitoring and higher annual payments tied to environmental spending, raising the risk of output constraints or delays.

title: Suspects steal copper cables in front of Vaal police station – WATCH
summary: Police in Ekurhuleni are investigating alleged digging and theft of copper cables in front of a police station. Abandoned digging tools and copper cables were found. City Power also reports prior foiled incidents and highlights increased spending to curb cable theft and vandalism.

title: Mongolia Calls On Rio Tinto To Keep Budget For Giant Copper Mine In Check
summary: Mongolia asked Rio Tinto not to increase the $7.06 billion budget for the Oyu Tolgoi underground expansion, after cost overruns and delays. Mongolia highlighted reforms such as domestic metal exchange trading and proposed changes to copper royalties. Oyu Tolgoi is expected to deliver first underground copper by mid-2023.

title: Mongolia calls on Rio Tinto to keep budget for giant copper mine in check
summary: Mongolia urged Rio Tinto to keep the budget for its large copper mine in check. The move is intended to control costs and protect project discipline, which can slightly improve confidence in the mine’s development outlook and therefore provide modest support for copper supply expectations over coming weeks.

title: Panama not willing to expand First Quantum's copper mine operations | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Panama’s deputy environment minister says the country will not permit First Quantum to expand its Cobre Panama copper mine operations, citing environmental concerns and failed commitments. Negotiations for a new contract involve taxes and tighter monitoring. Panama is also reviewing other concession requests, but stresses current mining is already large enough.

title: Stillwater expands resource, nickel by more than half at Montana project
summary: Stillwater Critical Minerals increased the inferred resource tonnage for its Stillwater West battery and platinum metals project in Montana, highlighting a large expansion in nickel resources. The company aims to mirror its neighbor Sibanye-Stillwater. The update is supply-related sentiment, but not immediate production, limiting short-term price impact.

title: Workers At Chinese-Serbian Copper Mine Block Roads To Press Wage Demands
summary: Hundreds of workers at Zijin’s joint Chinese-Serbian copper mine in Bor blocked four entrance gates to demand higher wages and a new collective bargaining agreement. Road blocking targeted heavy trucks, risking interruptions to mining and smelting operations. The stoppage comes as similar protests occurred earlier this month.

title: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Announces Date of Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2022 Earnings Release and Conference Call and Changes to Presentation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures
summary: Kaiser Aluminum (KALU) announced its Q4/full-year 2022 earnings release date and updated non-GAAP financial measure presentation, including renaming VAR to “Conversion Revenue” and changing the inclusion of alloy costs within Hedged Cost of Alloyed Metal from Jan. 1, 2022. No new production or pricing action was stated.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp.: Flying Nickel Announces Private Placement Offering of up to 5,000,000 Units for Gross Proceeds of up to $800,000
summary: Flying Nickel Mining Corp. announced a non-brokered private placement raising up to $800,000 to fund a Minago PGM assay/drilling program and general corporate purposes. The company is developing its 100% owned Minago nickel project. The release is financing-focused with no immediate supply or production impact stated.

title: Biden administration moves to protect Boundary Waters wilderness in northern Minn. from proposed copper-nickel mine
summary: The Biden administration ordered a 20-year closure of parts of Minnesota’s Superior National Forest to mineral and geothermal leasing, blocking the Twin Metals proposed underground copper-nickel mine near Ely. The move follows prior disputes over lease reinstatement and threatens project viability, increasing perceived supply risk for copper and nickel.

title: Biden administration moves to protect Boundary Waters wilderness in northern Minn. from proposed copper-nickel mine
summary: The Biden administration ordered a 20-year closure of Superior National Forest land in Minnesota to mineral and geothermal leasing, protecting the Boundary Waters and stopping the Twin Metals proposed copper-nickel mine. The move followed rescission of key mineral rights, shifting outlook toward lower future supply of copper and nickel.

title: China reopening: ANZ, Morgan Stanley and Perennial fund managers' investment strategies to play the big reopening
summary: Fund managers expect strong resource-sector returns as China’s reopening accelerates economic activity. The article says traders have repositioned in response, lifting prices of raw materials, explicitly mentioning copper, and implying wider support for industrial metal demand that could also benefit aluminium.

title: A Copper Mine Could Advance Green Energy but Scar Sacred Land
summary: A proposed Arizona copper project called Resolution by Rio Tinto and BHP faces strong opposition from Apache tribal groups at Oak Flat. Companies argue the added copper supply for batteries and electric cars will cut emissions. Despite cultural and legal concerns, the prospect of more supply is supportive for copper sentiment in the near term.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.64% Higher at $4.2670 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper front-month futures settled 0.64% higher at $4.2670 per pound, gaining 2.70 cents. The move ended a two-session losing streak and marked the largest one-day dollar and percentage gain since Jan. 12, alongside strong recent outperformance and a month-to-date increase.

title: Nickel briquette premiums decline in US, Europe; cathode premiums mixed
summary: Nickel premiums fell across the US, with nickel briquette and 4x4 cathode premiums dropping after China returns from Lunar New Year. Reports show demand improving but price opinions easing, leading to lower assessed ranges. In Europe, briquette premiums decreased on weak stainless demand, while uncut cathode premiums rose slightly amid tight high-purity supply.

title: EPA to decide whether gold and copper mine in Alaska moves forward
summary: The EPA is expected to issue a final decision in January on whether the proposed Pebble Mine in southwest Alaska can proceed. Residents fear it would harm salmon habitat. Because the mine is described as producing copper and gold, the regulatory timeline could influence short-term copper supply expectations.

title: Demonstrators Shut Down Serbian Copper Mine Over Wage Dispute
summary: Hundreds of workers blocked entrances to Zijin Copper’s Bor mine and smelting complex in eastern Serbia on a wage dispute, demanding a 14.3% pay rise and a new collective bargaining agreement. The access disruption could delay mining and processing, raising near-term supply risk for copper.

title: Peru's Violent Protests Imperil 30% of Its Copper Output
summary: Weekend Edition coverage flags that Peru’s violent protests may imperil roughly 30% of the nation’s copper output. Such a large, near-term supply disruption risk would likely worsen short-term availability expectations, driving sharp price moves in copper markets as traders reprice production risk.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 0.58% Lower at $4.2240 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper ended the week down 0.58% to $4.2240 per pound, snapping a five-week winning streak. The front-month contract fell 2.45 cents this week and was down again on the day, with settlement at the lowest level since Jan. 17, reflecting bearish near-term momentum.

title: Québec Nickel to Showcase High-Grade NI-CU-PGE Drill Core at VRIC on January 29-30
summary: Québec Nickel Corp. announced it will showcase high-grade NI-CU-PGE drill core from its Fortin Sill Zone at a January 29-30 conference and reported strong 2022 Ni and Cu intersections. It also launched its 2023 winter drilling program at the Ducros property, with a second drill expected soon.

title: What is Doctor Copper? Investing Explained
summary: “Doctor Copper” refers to copper’s role as an economy indicator. The article says LME copper has surged to above $9,300, citing China’s easing lockdowns boosting demand, fears of supply tightness, weaker USD supporting commodity prices, and investor reluctance to source Russian copper. Forecasts are for further upside.

title: Russia's Largest Nickel Producer Nornickel Produced 59,735 mt of Nickel in Q4 2022_SMM
summary: Russia’s Nornickel, the largest nickel producer, reported Q4 2022 nickel production of 59,735 mt and forecast 2023 output of 204,000–214,000 mt. The figures influence near-term expectations for nickel supply and potential market balance, though the Q4 portion is historical.

title: Aluminium Ingot Inventory Accumulation after 2023 CNY Holiday Far Outpaces that in Same Period Last Year _SMM
summary: SMM said China’s social inventories of aluminium ingots in eight major markets rose to 929,000 mt on Jan 28, up 185,000 mt from pre-CNY and higher than last year. Arrivals were concentrated in Gongyi, Wuxi and Nanhai, with more in transit, and SMM expects inventory to reach ~980,000 mt next Monday.

title: SMM Review of Aluminium Market during CNY Holiday and Post-Holiday Outlook _SMM
summary: SMM reviews aluminium prices during the CNY break: SHFE and LME aluminium rose modestly after the holiday closure. Fundamentals show normal smelter output overall but continued power rationing in southwest China and limited capacity resumption, while downstream demand is expected to recover as firms restart production and spot activity picks up, despite rising ingot inventories.

title: China's Primary Aluminium Imports Fell 58% YoY in 2022_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s primary aluminium imports fell to 668,000 mt in 2022, down 58% from a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data. In December, imports totaled about 127,646 mt, rising 15.3% month-on-month and 55.2% year-on-year, indicating variability but weaker full-year demand for imports.

title: Copper Prices to Be Subject to Follow-up Consumption post CNY Holiday_SMM
summary: SMM reports LME copper stayed relatively high through the CNY holiday but fell on Friday after US PCE, consumer confidence, and GDP supported the dollar. At the same time, LME inventories kept falling to 73,975 mt. China’s cathode inventories remained high, potentially capping gains.

title: Ferronickel and NPI Imports Stood at 619,000 mt in December, with 28.7% MoM increase in FeNi Imports_SMM
summary: SMM cites customs data showing China imported 619,000 mt of ferronickel and NPI in December, with FeNi imports up 28.7% MoM and nickel-content imports rising. Firms attribute higher demand to stronger nickel prices and stainless steel substitution needs, while tight FeNi supply held prices firm. Early January demand also looks constructive for February.

title: SMM Imported Copper Concentrate Index Falls for Eight Consecutive Weeks amid Frequent Disruptions on Supply Side_SMM
summary: SMM reports its weekly Imported Copper Concentrate Index at $83.56/mt, down for eight consecutive weeks, driven by a troubled spot market. Supply disruptions include a fire at Ventanas port in Peru, Antapaccay mine disruption from protesters, ongoing Las Bambas issues, and Cobre Panama risks from taxes/fees, alongside temporary shipping constraints.

title: Iran's alumina powder output surpasses 176,000 tons in 9 mon...
summary: Iran’s alumina powder production reportedly exceeded 176,000 tons over the first nine months. As alumina is a primary input to aluminium smelters, higher output can reduce supply tightness and feedstock cost pressures, which may support near-term expectations for aluminium prices.

title: Global Copper Prices are Expected to Increase Further as Output Growth in Chile is Lower than Expected_SMM
summary: Cochilco expects Chile’s copper output growth to slow versus prior projections, with peak timing delayed, citing delays in mining projects. Peru violence has disrupted copper mine production. Political uncertainty in Chile and licensing/tax concerns add risk to supply, suggesting global copper prices may rise further.

title: Conversion Margins of Aluminium Billets in South China May Rebound As Aluminium Inventory Accumulation Misses Expectations_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium inventories in South China and nationally rose during the CNY period but the stock buildup missed expectations. With current billet conversion margins at very low levels pre-holiday, SMM expects margins to rebound after production resumes as extrusion demand recovers, and flags φ120 margins likely above 200 yuan/mt.

title: Prismo Metals Inc.: Prismo Metals Announces Definitive Agreement to Acquire Majority Interest in Hot Breccia Property in the Arizona Copper Belt
summary: Prismo Metals signed a definitive agreement to acquire a 75% stake in the Hot Breccia porphyry copper-skarn project in Arizona, paying cash, issuing shares, and assuming earn-in obligations. The release cites historic drill intercepts with copper exceeding 1% and plans exploration/drilling, supporting a near-term positive copper outlook.

title: Minmetals Resources Says Its Las Bambas Copper Mine May Suspend Production from February 1_SMM
summary: Protests in Peru have blocked transportation for weeks, disrupting southern access routes to mines. Minmetals says Las Bambas may gradually slow operations from now and could suspend copper production from Feb 1 (Peru time) if disruptions continue, following other attacks including Glencore’s Antapaccay halt.

title: Aluminium Ingot Social Inventory in China Still in Seasonal Accumulation Cycle  _SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s aluminium ingot social inventory reached 986,000 mt on Jan 30, up sharply versus before and after CNY. Inventories increased as trades stagnated while cargoes kept arriving and withdrawals remained limited, suggesting the accumulation cycle may continue.

title: Spot Prices of Pure Nickel Climb amid Expectations for Improved Consumption_SMM
summary: SMM reports nickel spot premiums rising on Jan 30: Jinchuan nickel premiums against SHFE increased to around 10,500 yuan/mt (+750), while optimism over consumption after the Chinese New Year holiday supported the move. Nickel briquette prices also rose, though trading remained relatively slack.

title: Pure Nickel Customs Clearance Volume Fell 13% MoM in Dec 2022_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s December 2022 customs clearance for refined/pure nickel fell 13% MoM, with refined nickel imports largely flat MoM but pressured by persistent import losses. Lower nickel sulfate output and weaker 300-series stainless steel demand reduced need for nickel briquettes, weighing on near-term nickel demand.

title: Iran's copper cathode output surpasses 200,000 tons in first...
summary: The report states that Iran’s copper cathode production has surpassed 200,000 tons in the first period. Higher cathode output implies greater copper supply entering the market, which typically weighs on prices in the short term unless offset by stronger demand or tighter inventories.

title: Oz Minerals' Quarterly Copper Output Hit A Record High, Brent Futures Rose
summary: Oz Minerals reported a record-high quarterly copper output, a factor that can increase near-term supply expectations. The broader market tone is also supportive, with China reopening, stronger Lunar New Year consumption growth, and firmer energy prices. These opposing forces likely offset, keeping copper price impact mixed.

title: Overseas Alumina Prices Continue to Rise While Domestic Prices Remain Firm_SMM
summary: SMM says overseas alumina deals rose to $408/mt FOB Brazil (+$18 on Jan 17), implying a large premium over China domestic spot. After the CNY holiday, truck transport efficiency returned and aluminium smelters restocked as inventories ran low, while refineries prioritized long-term contract deliveries. Trading activity is expected to pick up and lift spot transactions.

title: In race for EV metals, BHP casts wider net to locate copper, nickel
summary: BHP launched its Xplor accelerator to fund and mentor early-stage explorers targeting copper and nickel, receiving hundreds of applications. The article also cites BHP’s binding $9.6bn takeover of Oz Minerals and an option to take a stake in copper exploration leases in Serbia, strengthening supply outlook sentiment for both metals.

title: Peru Protests Put Huge China-Owned Copper Mine on Brink of Halt
summary: Peru protests are escalating pressure on a large China-owned copper mine, reportedly putting it on the brink of a halt. The risk of an output stoppage or slower production increases near-term supply concerns, which typically supports upward pricing in copper markets over the coming days.

title: SHFE Aluminium Pulls Back as Poor Fundamentals Outweigh Macro Tailwinds _SMM
summary: SHFE aluminium gained early after CNY but fell back, with spot discounts widening as supply exceeded demand. Guizhou output may slowly recover after power rationing impacts proved smaller than expected. Meanwhile, social aluminium inventories rose sharply due to continued cargo arrivals and limited warehouse withdrawals, keeping prices rangebound to weaker.

title: Philippines May Tax Nickel Exports to Follow Indonesia's Success
summary: The headline says the Philippines may tax nickel exports following Indonesia’s reported success. Such export taxes can reduce outbound supply and tighten availability in the near term, potentially lifting nickel prices as market expectations shift toward lower export flows.

title: NorthWest Copper Announces Increase to Non-Brokered Private
summary: NorthWest Copper increased the size of its non-brokered private placement to fund working capital and exploration (including the Lorraine property). The company describes itself as a copper-gold explorer. The announcement is financing-related and does not mention production changes, supply disruptions, or project economics that would move near-term copper prices.

title: 'China's economic slowdown could dampen its demand for copper and lithium'
summary: The piece notes that China’s economic slowdown could dampen demand for copper. A weaker Chinese growth outlook typically lowers expectations for industrial activity and infrastructure spending, which can reduce projected copper consumption in the near term. Lithium is mentioned but is outside the tracked metals set here.

title: Trigon Confirms Acquisition of Copper King Extension at Kombat in Namibia
summary: Trigon Metals confirmed it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire exclusive prospecting licence EPL 8529, known as the “Copper King Extension,” surrounding its Kombat and Gross Otavi projects in Namibia. The land position covers 35 km of prospective strike and will be targeted in planned surface drilling for copper resources later in 2023.

title: Galapagos of Asia at Risk Because of Nickel Mining
summary: Residents of Sibuyan Island in the Philippines are asking authorities to pause APMC’s nickel mining exploration, arguing it threatens local ecosystems and livelihoods. The company has received an export license for bulk testing and ore shipments are reported, but protests and required environmental clearances raise the risk of delays.

title: What China's reopening means for markets as traders bet on copper, iron ore and Chinese tech stocks
summary: China’s reopening after the zero-COVID policy is framed as a catalyst for economic recovery. Traders are already positioning for stronger demand, including copper, alongside iron ore and Chinese tech stocks. The report cites a sharp rise in China’s CSI 300 index, reinforcing bullish sentiment for commodities exposed to Chinese demand.

title: The Global Nickel Industry Could Another Shock as the Second Largest Supplier of Nickel Ore Is Mulling over Export Tax _SMM
summary: Philippines officials are considering imposing an export tax on nickel ore to shift the country from exporting raw material to developing domestic nickel processing. With the Philippines a leading global nickel ore supplier, the policy could tighten upstream availability for overseas supply chains, supporting nickel price expectations in the near term.

title: China's Imports of Copper Concentrate from Some American Countries Declined in December 2022_SMM
summary: China’s copper concentrate imports in December 2022 fell MoM, attributed to Peru’s political protests disrupting Las Bambas and Antapaccay deliveries and US port truck driver strikes reducing exports to China. Chinese smelter winter stockpiling also ended, with fewer scheduled inbound shipments in December, tightening supply visibility.

title: U.S. EPA to block Pebble Mine copper/gold mine project in Alaska
summary: The U.S. EPA plans a final determination under the Clean Water Act to prevent Northern Dynasty from storing mine waste for the proposed Pebble copper/gold project in Alaska’s Bristol Bay. The decision would halt future development if it causes similar harm, reducing potential copper supply.

title: The Philippines Plans to Levy Taxes on Nickel Ore Exports_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: The Philippines is considering taxes on primary nickel ore exports, or even a broader ore export ban, inspired by Indonesia’s success with export restrictions since 2020. The policy aims to drive local processing and boost downstream revenue. Philippine nickel ore shipments are expected to improve despite a 17% production fall.

title: Aluminium Smelters in Yunnan Maintain Stable Operation_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium smelters in Yunnan are maintaining operating rates near pre-holiday levels despite power rationing introduced in Q3 last year. Total operating aluminium capacity in Yunnan is about 4.04 million mt. Some producers warn further power-cut production declines are possible, but no formal notice has been issued yet.

title: SMM Expects Aluminium Prices to Remain in Upward Trajectory as Demand Optimism Prevails, Despite Fundamentals-Driven Bumps along the Way_SMM
summary: SMM expects aluminium prices to remain on an upward trajectory despite near-term bumps. Analysts cite possible pressure from January inventory accumulation, large transit cargoes, and weaker coal cost support. However, they say seasonal inventory effects are priced in and demand optimism from post-Covid reopening and stimulus will support higher prices, unless destocking disappoints.

title: An Aluminium Giant in Shandong Lowers February Benchmark Purchase Price of Prebaked Anode_SMM
summary: SMM says a major aluminium smelter in Shandong lowered its February benchmark purchase prices for prebaked anodes by 660 yuan/mt versus January, to 5,920 yuan/mt in cash and 5,955 yuan/mt by acceptance. The move signals lower anode procurement costs for aluminium production.

title: Copper Cathode Imports in Dec Declined as Expected_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China imported 347,400 mt of copper cathode in Dec 2022, down MoM and sharply YoY, citing a continued closure of the import window, slower year-end customs clearance, and COVID disruptions. SMM expects January imports to fall further, while exports rise, with logistics delays pushing volumes into February.

title: SHFE Nickel Gained Ground, Spot Nickel Prices Rose in Tandem_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SHFE nickel stayed elevated on Jan 31 and spot pure nickel prices rose. Jinchuan premiums averaged 8,500 yuan/mt (down from yesterday), while Nornickel premiums averaged 8,250 yuan/mt (up). Nickel briquette prices climbed 2,650 yuan/mt to about 228,700–229,200 yuan/mt, despite weaker spot transactions.

title: Vedanta Is Said to Scrap Plans to Sell Mega Indian Copper Smelter
summary: Vedanta is reported to be scrapping plans to sell its “mega” copper smelter in India. The decision could affect expectations for copper refining capacity and operational continuity. Near-term sentiment may be mildly supportive for copper, though the headline alone provides limited detail on timing or production impact.

title: Teck's Copper Output in FY 2022 Missed Guidance, But to Increase in FY 2023_SMM
summary: Teck Resources produced 270,500 mt of copper in FY2022, below guidance, citing the December 2022 closure of its Highland Valley copper mine in Canada after an engineering accident. The issue has stabilized. Teck forecasts higher FY2023 copper output of 390,000–445,000 mt, adjusting supply expectations.

title: Philippines' proposed tax on nickel ore exports could 'kill' industry - group head
summary: Philippines lawmakers are considering a tax on raw nickel ore exports (initially 10%) to push miners toward local processing. Industry groups warn it would “kill” the sector, citing low processing capacity versus ore output. The proposal follows Indonesia’s nickel ore ban model, affecting near-term nickel export supply expectations.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Reports 33.77 metres at 3.43% Copper within 65.20 meters at 1.88% Copper at Copper Creek in Arizona
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. reported drill results from its Copper Creek Project in Arizona, including 33.77m at 3.43% copper (and a longer 65.20m at 1.88% copper) and additional lower-grade copper intervals. The company says Phase II drilling could expand mineralization and the resource.

title: EPA blocks major Alaska gold and copper mine over effects on salmon fisheries
summary: The Biden EPA blocked Alaska’s Pebble Mine from advancing, rejecting developers’ plan under the Clean Water Act due to unacceptable impacts on the Bristol Bay salmon ecosystem. By halting a major proposed gold and copper project, the decision reduces potential copper supply, weighing on copper price expectations. Broader mining actions are mentioned for other minerals.

title: Prismo to purchase majority stake in Infinitum Copper
summary: Prismo Metals agreed to acquire a 75% interest in Infinitum Copper’s Hot Breccia porphyry-copper skarn project in Arizona, including a $350,000 payment and share issuance. Prismo plans to begin exploration and drilling soon, but near-term copper output impact is limited.

title: Vietnam Issued The Results Of The Second Review Of The Application Of Anti-dumping Measures On Some Aluminum Products From China - International Trade & Investment
summary: Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade issued Decision No. 74/QD-BCT confirming/adjusting anti-dumping measures on several Chinese-origin aluminum product categories (HS 7604). Anti-dumping duty rates for 17 firms range from 2.85% to 35.58%, with an official rate of 35.58% for others, effective March 11, 2023.

title: Feds use rare veto to block Alaska copper, gold mine plan
summary: The article headline says U.S. federal authorities used a “rare veto” to block an Alaska mine plan involving copper (and gold). Denying the project can delay future copper supply and worsen short-term supply expectations, which generally creates bearish price pressure for copper markets.

title: The Forced Labor Wheel Spins to Aluminum
summary: The article notes that the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act enforcement appears to be expanding to aluminum, identified by U.S. Customs as high risk. Importers are urged to compile extensive documentation and origin/proof records, suggesting increased inspections and potential import friction that could affect aluminum supply in the near term.

title: Feds veto plan for gold, copper mine in Alaska
summary: The article headline says federal authorities veto a plan for a copper mine in Alaska. If the veto delays or blocks the project, market expectations for near-term copper supply may worsen, supporting higher copper prices over the following days to weeks. (Gold is mentioned but isn’t tracked here.)

title: US vetoes proposed AK copper, gold mine to support world's largest sockeye salmon fishery
summary: The U.S. EPA used Clean Water Act veto authority to prohibit activities linked to the proposed Pebble Mine in Alaska, effectively ending the project. The mine is aimed at developing copper and gold. The decision cites risks to Bristol Bay salmon habitat and removes a potential future copper supply source.

title: United States Notifies Intent to Appeal WTO Panel Reports on Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Measures | Wiley Rein LLP
summary: The United States notified the WTO of its intent to appeal panel reports on Section 232 tariffs and quotas for steel and aluminum, arguing Article XXI security exceptions should not be questioned. Because appellate review is deadlocked, disputes are effectively on hold, implying no near-term requirement to remove or change measures.

title: China's Low Aluminum Production Worsens Supply Chain Challenges
summary: The article argues that low aluminum production in China, shutdowns or limited capacity at smelters, energy shortages, and historically low aluminum inventories are worsening supply chain constraints. It also notes U.S. scrap/U​BC availability challenges for sheet mills. Overall, aluminum supply remains tight, supporting a short-term uptrend.

title: Candente Copper Announces Voting Results From Special
summary: Candente Copper reports shareholder approval of a $4 million private placement with Fortescue’s unit, via issuance of 22.2 million shares at $0.18, expected to close around Feb. 6 subject to TSX approval. The funding supports development of its Cañariaco copper project in Peru.

title: Teck misses copper guidance, expects more extreme weather events
summary: Teck missed its 2022 copper guidance, producing 270,500 tonnes versus the estimate of 273,000–290,000, citing geotechnical issues, unplanned maintenance, and extreme weather. It also trimmed QB2 copper startup output expectations for 2023 (150–180,000 tonnes), worsening near-term copper supply outlook.

title: EPA uses rare veto to block Alaska copper, gold mine plan
summary: The U.S. EPA blocked the proposed Pebble Mine in Alaska, citing unacceptable impacts on Bristol Bay’s salmon ecosystem. The project is described as the world’s most significant undeveloped copper and gold resource. The decision deals a heavy blow to future copper supply development, likely pressuring copper prices lower.

title: Vale's nickel sales volume soars by 30 per cent in 4th quarter of 2022
summary: Vale SA said Q4 2022 nickel production fell 1.3% to 47,400 tonnes, while nickel sales volumes jumped 30.2% to 58,200 tonnes by drawing on pent-up stocks to meet contracts. The company also noted weaker iron ore output and ongoing expectations for 2023 nickel production.

title: RPT-UPDATE 1-Japan buyers agree to pay Q1 aluminium premiums of $85-$86/T, sources say
summary: Japan buyers have agreed to pay Q1 aluminium premiums of $85-$86/T, according to sources. While not the cash price itself, agreed premiums reflect stronger physical-market conditions and demand expectations, which usually lend near-term support to aluminium prices.

title: An Alaska gold and copper mine project blocked over environmental impact
summary: US EPA blocked the proposed Pebble Mine in Alaska under the Clean Water Act due to expected damage to Bristol Bay salmon habitat. The mine was a large undeveloped copper (and gold) resource; blocking it reduces prospective copper supply, which can support near-term copper price expectations despite possible appeals.

title: The Philippines Mulling over Taxing Exported Nickel Ore May Raise China's Procurement and Smelting Cost_SMM
summary: The Philippines is considering taxing exported nickel ore to attract investment in domestic nickel processing. Analysts warn tariffs would increase supply uncertainty and raise Chinese smelters’ nickel-ore procurement costs (Philippines ore is largely used). While potential future smelting capacity could expand, the near-term effect is cost pressure for primary nickel.

title: Jinchuan Successfully Increased Refined Nickel Output by 600 mt in January_SMM
summary: SMM reports Jinchuan Group boosted refined nickel production by 600 mt in January. The plan targets 6,000 mt higher refined nickel output in 2023 and relies on capacity and balance improvements across nickel smelters, using high-grade nickel matte as feedstock, with most incremental output from existing lines.

title: Pure Nickel Spot Prices on the Rise, Premiums Decline with Suppliers Keen on Selling_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel prices rising on Feb 1 while spot trade activity is slack due to high spot levels. Jinchuan and Nornickel spot premiums fell day-on-day as suppliers were keen to sell. Nickel briquette spot prices edged higher, but nickel sulphate production economics remained unattractive, limiting demand.

title: Chile's 2022 Copper Production Continues to Decline on Lower Ore Grade_SMM
summary: Chile’s copper production rose slightly month-on-month in December 2022 but fell year-on-year, with output down across the year. The report attributes the decline to worsening ore grades, limited water resources, and maintenance issues. It also notes lower concentrate recovery and weaker performance at major mines like Escondida.

title: United States Notifies Intent To Appeal WTO Panel Reports On Section 232 Steel And Aluminum Measures - International Trade & Investment
summary: The U.S. notified it intends to appeal WTO panel decisions on its Section 232 tariffs and quotas for steel and aluminum imports. With the Appellate Body deadlocked, the disputes are effectively paused, meaning the U.S. will not be required to remove the aluminum measures soon, supportive for aluminum prices.

title: Atlantic Nickel announces another record financial and operational performance in 2022
summary: Atlantic Nickel reports record 2022 performance at its Santa Rita nickel-copper sulphide mine in Brazil, including higher concentrate output and details of hedging for 2022-2023. Realized prices were about US$12.23/lb Ni and US$3.70/lb Cu, but the release is mainly historical, limiting immediate price pressure.

title: FTSE 100: Glencore sticks to targets despite copper production drop
summary: Glencore said it will keep its 2023 output guidance despite a 12% copper production plunge in 2022, citing issues at Katanga and disruptions including an Antapaccay suspension after protests. Nickel production rose 5% on improved operations, but overall guidance stayed unchanged, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Achieves 9-Month 2022 Production and Cost Guidance and Provides 2023 Guidance
summary: Capstone Copper reported 2022 nine-month copper production of 136.3 kt with lower C1 cash costs and provided 2023 guidance. It expects declining C1 costs overall, with Mantoverde ramp-up timing and sulphuric acid price assumptions reducing costs, while Cozamin costs rise from new tailings/paste-backfill commissioning.
