title: Camino Minerals Corp.: Camino Signs Earn-in and Joint Venture Letter of Intent with Nittetsu Mining for the Los Chapitos Copper Project, Peru
summary: Camino Minerals signed a non-binding earn-in and joint venture letter of intent with Nittetsu for Peru’s Los Chapitos copper exploration project. Nittetsu can earn 35% through CAD $10.1 million in payments and expenditures over three years. Camino remains operator while due diligence proceeds toward a definitive agreement.

title: Spectra7 to Showcase 200 and 400Gbps Connectivity using Active Copper Cables at DesignCon
summary: Spectra7 says data center operators are shifting toward active copper cables as switches move to 56G PAM4 signaling, since passive copper has length limits. It highlights GaugeChanger chips enabling 100–800Gbps copper connectivity, expecting continued growth in PAM4 interfaces. This points to incremental copper interconnect demand, though it’s a marketing release.

title: Copper Mountain Mining Announces Q4 2022 Results Conference Call Date
summary: Copper Mountain Mining said it will release its Q4 and full-year 2022 results on March 27, 2023, and host a conference call. The company produces copper from its southern British Columbia mine, which could affect near-term expectations for copper supply, but no new production or guidance figures were provided.

title: Vedanta ditches Indian copper smelter divestment plan
summary: Vedanta dropped plans to sell its Sterlite Copper smelter in Tamil Nadu and is considering restarting the idled facility shuttered in 2018. A reopening would boost Indian copper output and reduce import needs, amid peak local demand tied to electrification and renewables.

title: EPA blocks Alaska gold, copper Pebble Mine to protect salmon fishery
summary: The EPA used its Clean Water Act veto to block the proposed Pebble Mine in Alaska, citing potential harm to Bristol Bay’s salmon fishery. The project is described as a major undeveloped copper resource. Companies and state officials condemn the decision, and legal challenges are expected, increasing copper supply uncertainty.

title: MMG shuts Las Bambas copper mine amid Peru protests
summary: MMG has placed its Las Bambas copper mine in Peru on care and maintenance after protests linked to the impeachment and arrest of a former Peruvian president escalated community opposition. The shutdown removes a large share of near-term copper supply from the world’s second-largest copper-producing country.

title: US Details Chinese Aluminum, a Suspected Product of Forced Labor
summary: The article’s headline says the U.S. is detailing certain Chinese aluminum products suspected of being made with forced labor. If this leads to tighter import enforcement or restrictions, it would likely curb near-term availability from China and support aluminium pricing through reduced supply and higher compliance costs.

title: Glencore 2022 copper output falls, co sticks to 2023 outlook
summary: Glencore said it produced 1.06 million tonnes of copper in 2022, implying a decline versus prior expectations. Despite the weaker output, the company kept its 2023 copper outlook unchanged. The news highlights supply performance but suggests limited additional near-term impact from guidance.

title: Will the Philippines' Potential Ban of Nickel Ore Export Overturn Global Nickel Market?_SMM
summary: The Philippines is considering increasing export taxes or banning nickel ore exports to support local processing and EV battery supply chains. The piece argues this could disrupt nickel ore supply flows—especially to China, Japan, and South Korea—raising input costs and potentially supporting nickel prices in the near term despite implementation uncertainties.

title: Alaska gold, copper mine blocked over environmental worries | Chattanooga Times Free Press
summary: AP reports the U.S. EPA blocked the proposed Pebble Mine in Alaska over environmental concerns, dealing a heavy blow to a major undeveloped copper resource. By removing potential future copper supply, the decision is likely to raise short-term expectations of tighter supply and support copper prices.

title: Strong copper demand underpins New Century's Mt Lyell plan
summary: New Century’s Mt Lyell copper mine restart is presented against a backdrop of surging battery and renewable demand and tight physical copper inventories (around 12 days), with risks to supply from unrest and potential tax-related mine closures. The article frames copper as poised for sustained upward movement.

title: Indonesia plans to ban copper exports in 2023
summary: Indonesia’s president said the government will soon consider halting exports of unprocessed copper ores to encourage domestic processing. The plan follows Indonesia’s earlier bauxite export ban and nickel ore export restrictions that boosted processing activity, which can tighten expected copper supply and support higher prices.

title: Canada's Power Nickel to Use Fleet Space Satellite-Based Mineral Exploration System
summary: Fleet Space Technologies will partner with Canada’s Power Nickel to deploy its satellite-based ExoSphere exploration system at the company’s NISK nickel project in Quebec. The technology aims to accelerate, lower-impact discovery of high-grade nickel deposits needed for EV battery supply, supporting a modest positive outlook for nickel.

title: Indonesia Relaxes Restrictions on Foreign Ownership of Nickel Mines and Pricing of Low-grade Nickel Ore Attracts Attention_SMM
summary: SMM reports Indonesia has relaxed restrictions on foreign ownership in local nickel mines from 49% to 70%, strengthening foreign participation. With stainless-steel and intermediate-product investment, competition for nickel ore is intensifying. Indonesia is also promoting benchmark pricing for low-grade nickel ore, drawing market attention.

title: Camino and Nittetsu team up on Peru copper exploration project
summary: Canada’s Camino and Japan’s Nittetsu plan to partner to advance Nittetsu’s Los Chapitos copper exploration project in Peru, with Nittetsu earning 35% via payments and expenditures over three years. The funding supports exploration, drilling, and studies. The deal is exploration-stage, offering minimal immediate copper supply impact.

title: Umicore signs long-term agreement with Terrafame for the supply of sustainable low carbon nickel
summary: Umicore has signed a long-term agreement with Terrafame to supply low-carbon, high-grade nickel sulphate for EV cathode materials. Commercial deliveries have started, with volume ramp-up planned in 2023. The contract covers a substantial part of Umicore’s planned nickel sulphate needs, supporting demand expectations for nickel.

title: Nickel Prices Pull Back after Surging High in the First Week post CNY Holiday _SMM
summary: After China’s New Year, nickel prices jumped on hopes of stronger consumption and a potential Philippines nickel-ore export ban, but the high level curbed buying. The article says the ban is unlikely due to power and rainy-season constraints. With weaker fundamentals and thin spot trades, SHFE nickel prices pulled back.

title: WESTERN COPPER AND GOLD'S CASINO PROJECT TO HAVE SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ON YUKON'S ECONOMY
summary: Western Copper and Gold announced an updated economic study for its Casino copper-gold project in Yukon, estimating large GDP, employment, tax, and wage contributions. While it signals future copper supply potential from a major project, the article does not confirm near-term construction start or production, so near-term copper price effects appear limited.

title: MONGOLIAN METALS CORPORATION (MMC) identifies new targets in the Khongor Copper & Gold District
summary: Mongolian Metals Corporation provides an exploration update for its Khongor copper-gold district in Mongolia, highlighting a new Copper Hill target with rock-chip results up to 3.69 wt% Cu and describing geochemical/geophysical work for 2023 drilling. The release is exploration-focused and does not imply immediate copper supply changes.

title: Aluminium sector vies for 'critical' status amid green tech rush
summary: Australia’s aluminium producers are urging the government to recognize bauxite, alumina and aluminium as “critical minerals” tied to the clean-energy transition. The sector cites demand growth for solar and wind and EVs, and promotes Australia’s downstream value chain. The proposal could improve sentiment toward aluminium prices and investment.

title: Allied Copper Announces Termination of Klondike Option Agreement
summary: Allied Copper Corp. announced it terminated its option agreement to acquire a 100% interest in the Klondike copper property, effective immediately. The company must still maintain the mineral claims for two years at an estimated cost of about $43,000. The announcement does not signal any broader copper supply or demand change.

title: Aluminium Bahrain B S C : Alba Reports its Financial Results for the Fourth Quarter and 12 Months of 2022
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) reported Q4 2022 and full-year results, with lower Q4 profit amid challenging conditions. The release reiterates 2022 aluminium market pressures from higher European energy costs, curtailments, and low LME inventories, but it mainly covers FY performance and general 2023 outlook rather than a new near-term supply shock.

title: Aluminium industry backs push to be on list of 'critical minerals'
summary: Australia’s Aluminium Council is urging bauxite, alumina and aluminium to be added to the country’s “critical minerals” list. It argues these materials are essential for infrastructure supporting Australia’s emissions-reduction targets, though it says no shortage exists currently. The policy push could influence investment expectations, but no immediate market shock is cited.

title: Emerita Intersects 24.3 Meters Grading 5.1% Zinc, 2.0% Lead, 0.2% Copper, 1.16 g/t Gold and 100.5 g/t Silver, Including 7.1 Meters Grading 12.4% Zinc, 3.1% Lead, 0.2% Copper, 0.80 g/t Gold And 67.7 g/t Silver at La Romanera Deposit
summary: Emerita Resources reported assay results from additional drill holes at the La Romanera massive sulfide deposit in Spain. Intercepts include polymetallic mineralization with chalcopyrite and copper grades around 0.1–0.4% Cu in most holes, alongside higher zinc and lead. The company is preparing a NI 43-101 resource estimate.

title: Copper Development Association Releases New Report, Urges
summary: The Copper Development Association released a report saying copper’s USGS supply risk score exceeds the 0.40 threshold for automatic inclusion on the U.S. Critical Minerals List. It highlights rising net import reliance and urges the Interior Secretary to add copper immediately to enable streamlined regulation and faster new supply development.

title: Anglo American Chile's copper output flat due to water scarcity, falling grades
summary: Anglo American Chile’s copper output is reported to be flat as operations face water scarcity and declining ore grades. The operating constraints suggest weaker production efficiency and potential short-term supply risk for Chilean copper, which can weigh on expectations for nearby copper availability and pricing.

title: Peru's political crisis cuts off access to 2% of the world's much-needed copper supply
summary: Peru’s political crisis is reported to cut off access to roughly 2% of the world’s copper supply. With supply tightening from a key origin, market expectations for near-term availability worsen, likely increasing copper prices over the coming days and into the next few weeks.

title: Philippines pushes for nickel exports in latest development plan
summary: The Philippines’ trade chief said the country will prioritize exporting processed nickel ore and develop downstream processing aligned with EV battery supply chains. The plan also follows earlier consideration of banning raw ore exports to force processing. Community opposition exists, but the policy direction is supportive for nickel sentiment.

title: SHFE Nickel Ends Seven-Day Winning Streak as Poor Fundamentals Dominate after Bullish Impact from the Philippines Mulling over Tax on Nickel Ore Exports Fades _SMM
summary: SHFE nickel reversed after seven gains, dropping 3.68% on Feb 2, with LME nickel also weaker. The earlier bullish support from the Philippines considering nickel ore export taxes faded. Ample supply during CNY, massive social inventories, and cautious restocking by alloy plants due to high nickel prices point to further downside.

title: Premiums of NORNICKEL Nickel are Nearly 1,400 yuan/mt Higher than Jinchuan Nickel_SMM
summary: NORNICKEL nickel spot premiums in Shanghai rose to nearly 1,400 yuan/mt above Jinchuan, leading to poor spot shipments as downstream pure-nickel demand stayed weak. Nickel futures climbed on post–CNY production resumption, but market sentiment was less bullish and the SHFE/LME ratio improved, suggesting premiums may ease next week.

title: SMM Forecast on Refined Nickel Market in 2023_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM forecasts 2023 refined nickel as volatile but trending lower. It expects Chinese and overseas refined nickel output to keep rising, while demand growth is uneven (stainless steel and nickel sulphate weaker; alloy demand supported). It also anticipates a supply surplus and higher inventories, with Indonesian export-tax risk possibly increasing oversupply.

title: Aluminium Capacity in China to Peak as Energy Consumption Ceilings Are Imminent_SMM
summary: China’s regulators issued energy consumption ceilings for aluminium and alumina production, effective Jan 1, 2024. The policy targets a highly energy-intensive industry, potentially constraining capacity utilisation as capacity nears limits under “dual carbon” goals. The article also cites strengthening demand after reopening, implying upward pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Port Inventories of Nickel Ore Dip 484,000 wmt from January 20_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s port nickel ore inventories fell 484,000 wmt to 8.1 million wmt by Feb 3, with Ni content down to about 64,000 mt. The drop is linked to slack holiday trading and weaker Philippines shipments due to rainy season, supporting expectations of further declines.

title: Taseko in talks regarding potential deal to up stake in Gibraltar copper mine
summary: Taseko says it is in talks with Sojitz to buy the 12.5% effective interest it does not already control in the Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia. Any deal would include an upfront payment and five years of annual payments tied to minimum and contingent payments based on Gibraltar copper revenues.

title: Taseko in talks regarding potential deal to up stake in Gibraltar copper mine | iNFOnews
summary: Taseko Mines said it is in confidential discussions with Sojitz Corp. about buying Sojitz’s effective interest linked to Taseko’s Gibraltar copper mine stake. title: Filo's longest copper cuts in Argentina boost takeover appeal
summary: Haywood Securities says Filo Mining’s new drill results from its Filo del Sol project in Argentina show the longest interval yet, improving perceived project potential. This can strengthen takeover appeal and bolster sentiment around the company’s future copper supply outlook, offering a mild bullish signal for copper-linked markets.

title: Future Metals Unearths More Nickel-Copper Hits At Panton
summary: Future Metals reports additional nickel-copper assay “hits” at its Panton project. The update is interpreted as improved potential resource prospects for both nickel and copper. Such discovery-related news can modestly support short-term market sentiment by raising expectations for future supply, even without immediate production details.

title: Employees at Alcoa's San Ciprián facility in Spain vote to endorse improved restart plan for aluminum smelter
summary: Alcoa says a majority of workers at its San Ciprián Spain aluminium smelter endorsed an improved restart plan starting in phases from January 2024. The update raises capital commitments (including a new anode plant), supported by long-term wind PPAs pending permitting. Alcoa plans full restart by late 2025 and minimum 75% capacity in 2025-2026.

summary: Sojitz will sell its 12.5% stake in Canada’s Gibraltar copper-molybdenum mine to Taseko. Output is sizable, so supply-risk concerns may weigh on copper.

title: Sinema and Kelly urge designation of copper as critical mineral
summary: Arizona senators Sinema and Kelly urged the Interior Department to classify copper as a critical mineral to secure domestic supply for the power grid and clean energy buildout. title: Copper play AIC Mines readies $30m cash call
summary: AIC Mines plans a $30m equity raising to fund expansion of its Eloise mine near Cloncurry in Queensland. The update is a direct supply-side development for the miner’s copper operations, though the article doesn’t indicate delivery timing or production magnitude relative to market size.

title: Cyprium Metals raises $35m to help fund Nifty copper project restart
summary: Cyprium Metals secured firm $35m capital-raising commitments to fund the restart of its Nifty copper project in Western Australia. title: Domestic Alumina Prices Held Steady amid Prevailing Wait-and-See Sentiment among Aluminium Smelters_SMM
summary: SMM reports the domestic alumina weighted index at 2,947 yuan/mt, barely higher WoW after the CNY holiday. Overseas alumina rose slightly, but the China import window stayed closed. title: Copper falls on stronger dollar
summary: Copper prices declined as a firm U.S. dollar following a strong jobs report made dollar-priced commodities more expensive. title: Like Musk, nickel-rich Indonesia has high electric vehicle ambitions
summary: Indonesia’s export ban on nickel ore and push to build EV battery supply chains underpin expectations for rapidly rising nickel demand and sustained market prominence. title: Aluminium Inventory in China Exceeds 1.1 Million mt by Adding Another 96,000 mt_SMM

summary: SMM says battery-grade nickel sulphate prices rose to 38,000–39,000 yuan/mt on supply tightness. Integrated firms are restocking amid concerns over future raw-material supply.

summary: ANZ forecasts nickel will face a large supply surplus of about 55,000 mt in 2023. summary: SMM reports nickel prices rose after post-CNY production resumed, supported by refined output increases and concerns over possible Philippines nickel-ore export bans. Fundamentals seen as offering weaker support going forward.

title: Nickel-rich Indonesia aims high over EVs
summary: Indonesia, the world’s top nickel producer, is pushing EV battery investment and leveraging its 2020 nickel ore export ban to expand onshore processing. title: Nickel Ore Prices are Stable as Wait-and-See Sentiment Fills the Market_SMM

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Initiates Drilling on the High-Grade W4 Zone, focused on the East Side of the Mineralization, to be Incorporated into the Upcoming Resource
summary: EV Nickel began Phase 4 drilling at its Shaw Dome W4 Zone, targeting the eastern expansion of previously defined high-grade nickel mineralization and collecting metallurgical samples. Assay results are expected in early Q2. The company says results could materially impact the upcoming updated resource estimate.

title: Anglo American to buy minority stake in Canada Nickel
summary: Anglo American agreed to buy a 9.9% stake in Canada Nickel for C$24m and will provide technical support for the Crawford nickel project in Ontario. The equity funding is meant to complete permitting, and Anglo gains rights related to recoveries of nickel concentrate and related carbon credits.

title: Commodity Trading Giant Faces $577 Million Loss From Nickel Fraud: Report
summary: Trafigura says it faces a $577 million loss after discovering nickel shipment fraud, with some purchased cargoes missing the nickel they were supposed to contain. The fraud was detected through inspections and legal action has started, while most shipments remain in transit awaiting further checks.

title: Trafigura accuses TMT Metals, others of "systematic" US$577mn nickel trading fraud
summary: Trafigura says it may lose up to $577mn after suing parties including TMT Metals over an alleged “systematic fraud” in containerised nickel shipments during 2022. Some containers inspected since late Dec 2022 were found not to contain nickel. Most shipments remain in transit pending inspection.

title: GM Expresses Interest in Acquiring a Portion of Vale's Base Metal Division and Becoming Tesla's Nickel Provider
summary: Bloomberg reports GM is in advanced negotiations with Vale for a stake in Vale’s newly established base metals division, which supplies nickel and copper for EV batteries. With automakers scaling EV production, Vale expects sizable growth in nickel and copper demand, and GM’s bids could tighten expectations despite no deal being finalized.

title: Mixed Fundamentals to Keep Aluminium Prices Rangebound _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports mixed drivers for aluminium. Yunnan smelters face power rationing, while spot activity improves as downstream buying picks up, supporting prices. However, aluminium ingot inventories continue accumulating without an inflection point. SHFE and LME trade volatility ends without a breakout, pointing to rangebound pricing.

title: SMM A00 Aluminium Prices Fell Sharply on January 10_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that Shanghai A00 aluminium spot prices fell to 18,550–18,590 yuan/mt on Jan 10, down 310 yuan/mt from the previous day. Spot discounts versus the SHFE 2302 contract were stable at 30–70 yuan/mt. The update signals short-term weakening aluminium pricing.

title: Aperam & Econick have formed a JV called Botanickel to become a world leader in the responsible and sustainable production of biosourced nickel for the stainless steel industry.
summary: Aperam and Econick formed a JV, Botanickel, to produce biosourced nickel by extracting nickel from hyperaccumulator plants and feeding it into stainless-steel recycling and processing routes. The company claims pilot production has started and aims to cover part of primary nickel demand, potentially reducing exposure to nickel volatility.

title: SUPPLY CHAIN SILLINESS: Biden to slap 200% tariff on Russian aluminum to "commemorate" Ukraine invasion anniversary
summary: The U.S. is considering a proposed 200% tariff on Russian aluminum to counter alleged dumping and punish Russia over Ukraine. The target is Russia’s supply into the U.S. LME aluminum briefly rose then fell 1.7% to $2,526.5/mt, reflecting a shifting near-term outlook for aluminum flows.

title: Catastrophic Earthquake in Turkey Barely Disrupted Local Aluminium Industry Chain due to Long Distanc_SMM
summary: Turkey’s catastrophic earthquake killed thousands, but the sole primary aluminium smelter (Eti Aluminium in Seydisehir) and downstream processing plants are located far from the epicenter and were reportedly unaffected. SMM says the event has little near-term impact on Turkey’s aluminium chain, while monitoring any future changes in China’s exports.

title: Copper slips on demand concerns; Shanghai nickel jumps
summary: Copper eased on China factory-gate price weakness and weaker U.S. employment data that raised demand and recession worries, while Las Bambas in Peru maintained reduced output after road blockades. Nickel surged after Trafigura disclosed a large nickel-fraud-related loss and rising expectations around low-stock liquidity. Aluminium also edged lower.

title: Copper slips on demand concerns; Shanghai nickel jumps
summary: Copper fell as China factory-gate prices and weaker U.S. unemployment claims revived demand and recession worries. Nickel jumped after Trafigura disclosed a large charge tied to alleged systematic fraud involving nickel cargoes. Aluminium also eased on the day, indicating a mixed but mainly risk-driven tape across industrial metals.

title: LS C&S joins hands with HAI to produce aluminum components for EVs
summary: LS Cable & System and Hammerer Aluminium Industries plan a joint venture investing 67.5 billion won to produce aluminum EV components such as battery cases from 2025. The companies cite rising EV supply and market growth, positioning the project as demand support for high-strength aluminium used in autos.

title: Trafigura books $577m charge for nickel shipments fraud
summary: Trafigura will record a ~$577m impairment after discovering missing nickel in containerized shipments from suppliers allegedly involved in document misrepresentation. The issue is described as isolated and under review, with inspections ongoing for remaining in-transit loads. Trafigura initiated legal proceedings against those parties.

title: Getting nickel going again | Hotter on metals
summary: The piece reviews the LME’s efforts to restart and stabilize nickel trading after the March 2022 volatility suspension, including possible permission to resume Asian hours, reworking margin/15% daily limits, improved OTC oversight, and clearing access proposals. Ongoing sanctions-related nerves around Russian deliverable nickel also shape sentiment.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports Fall 267,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Chinese nickel ore inventories fell 267,000 wmt WoW to 7.83 million wmt, with Ni content down 2,000 mt to about 62,000 mt. Shipments from the Philippines were constrained by rainy-season conditions, and rising February NPI output is expected to lift ore consumption.

title: Copper heads for third straight weekly loss on weak Chinese demand
summary: Copper is set for a third straight weekly loss as weak Chinese demand and soft Chinese inventory/factory data weigh on prices. The dollar firmed after strong U.S. employment data and investors wait for U.S. inflation signals. LME copper fell, and LME aluminium also declined on the broader negative sentiment.

title: EV Off-Roading, BMW, Nickel, And Tesla's Master Plan: Top EV News Feb 10
summary: The piece discusses Indonesia’s dominant nickel position—21 million tonnes of proven reserves, an ongoing nickel ore export ban, and rapidly expanding processed nickel and battery/EV deals. It also notes efforts to persuade Tesla to produce EVs or batteries in Indonesia, reinforcing expectations for nickel-linked demand.

title: Daily on Energy: A lot is at stake in the push to have copper named a critical mineral
summary: Lawmakers and copper industry groups are lobbying Interior/USGS to add copper to the formal US critical-minerals list. Copper is currently excluded despite rising supply-risk and rising import dependence. A designation would enhance domestic-sourcing benefits under IRA EV tax credits and potentially increase demand expectations for copper.

title: Fraud Findings Force Trafigura To Fire Head Of Nickel And Cobalt Trading
summary: Trafigura announced a $577 million impairment after discovering that some purchased containers did not contain nickel as contracted, firing its head of nickel/cobalt trading and pursuing legal action. With a portion of shipments already inspected and failing checks, while others remain in transit, uncertainty around nickel supply quality increases.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 0.87% Lower at $4.0275 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for February delivery settled 0.87% lower at $4.0275/lb, falling for three consecutive weeks and down 10 of the past 14 sessions. LME copper cash was also lower (-0.27%). The day’s move was particularly weak, with a steep one-day percentage decline.

title: Scrap Iron dealing to resume: Copper ban remains
summary: Authorities will allow a partial reopening of the scrap-iron industry, but the prohibition on exporting copper will continue for at least another year. Only limited by-product copper manufacturers are exempt. A transitional period before full licensing applies restricts new scrap-dealer participation, keeping export supply constraints in place.

title: Aluminum Dynamics set to break ground in Lowndes County March 7
summary: Aluminum Dynamics is scheduled to break ground on a $2.5 billion aluminum mill in Lowndes County, Mississippi, on March 7. The plant near Golden Triangle Regional Airport includes co-located customers and is owned by Steel Dynamics. The project is expected to create about 1,000 jobs, but no near-term production details are given.

title: Scrap iron trade resumes February 24, copper ban remains - Trinidad and Tobago Newsday
summary: Trinidad and Tobago will partially restart scrap iron trading Feb 24 under the Scrap Metal Act, but trading in copper remains illegal for most dealers. The copper export ban ends Feb 23 only as to the act’s partial enactment, while export of copper is still prohibited, limiting scrap copper availability.

title: Anglo American investment a 'game changer' for Canada Nickel Co: CEO
summary: Anglo American plans a $24 million minority stake in Canada Nickel and gains an exclusive right to buy about 10% of nickel from its Crawford project. The move supports expectations for low-carbon nickel supply for EV battery demand, potentially tightening sentiment for nickel over the next weeks.

title: Aluminium Prices to Remain Rangebound amid Mixed Factors _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE 2303 aluminium fell 1.2% to 18,515 yuan/mt and LME aluminium dropped 2.07% to $2,455/mt. Yunnan production cuts have not yet started and expectations for output curbs have weakened. With mixed bearish and bullish factors, aluminium prices are expected to remain rangebound short term.

title: Copper Futures Edged Lower Overnight as US Dollar Index Rebounded_SMM
summary: Copper futures edged lower as the US Dollar Index rebounded ahead of upcoming US inflation data, raising investor caution. LME and SHFE copper finished down. Domestic copper inventories fell modestly, mainly on stronger Guangdong consumption, but east China stocks still rose. With demand still weak, prices may drift lower.

title: Aluminium Inventory Exceeds 1.2 Million mt _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says aluminium ingot social inventories in China’s eight major markets rose to 1.22 million mt by Feb 13, up from Feb 6 and last Thursday, and indicating a seasonal accumulation phase. Growth is slowing as lower prices and production recovery spur downstream buying, likely keeping further buildup gradual over coming weeks.

title: Copper Stocks in Mainstream Chinese Markets Increased 3,400 mt over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s mainstream copper stocks rose 3,400 mt to 316,300 mt over the weekend. The increase is tempered by limited imported arrivals and smelters slowing shipments to Shanghai amid spot-premium levels. Consumption in Shanghai is improving, while downstream replenishment may increase if prices stop falling.

title: London copper prices rise amid caution ahead of U.S. inflation data
summary: London copper edged up 0.2% but stayed near a one-week low as traders were cautious ahead of U.S. CPI. The dollar’s rise weighed, but China bank-loan data supported demand hopes. LME aluminium also rose 0.4%, while SHFE nickel fell 3.4% amid weaker sentiment.

title: Aluminium Smelters with Captive Power Plants Benefited from Falling Coal Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports that aluminium smelters using captive power saw electricity costs fall as coal prices dropped, with weighted electricity price slipping to 0.44 yuan/kwh by Feb 10. Smelting full costs declined, but profits narrowed due to lower aluminium prices (A00 at 18,570 yuan/mt). Further coal declines could keep aluminium costs falling.

title: A Mix of Bullish and Bearish Factors to Keep Aluminium Prices Rangebound in the Short Term_SMM
summary: The piece cites mixed drivers for aluminium: bullish Chinese macro support and improving downstream demand, plus lower coal and anode costs, offset by bearish US dollar/risk appetite after strong non-farm payrolls and Fed rate-hike comments. Yunnan output cuts are not yet enforced, while potential Russian aluminium tariff increases raise supply worries. Prices likely rangebound.

title: Sellers Lowered Copper Concentrate TCs Further amid Tepid Spot Trades_SMM
summary: SMM reports the Imported Copper Concentrate Index falling to $79.38/mt, with further TCs reduced amid tepid spot activity. Improving logistics at American mines is offset by South America shipment issues affecting contract deliveries. Deals show lower clean ore TCs (e.g., $75/mt and $65/mt), tempering buyer inquiries and sentiment for copper.

title: Copper scrap supply remained ample_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: After the Chinese Lantern Festival, copper scrap sales picked up as sellers moved aggressively amid high copper prices and inventories built before the CNY holiday due to weak consumption. Scrap supply is described as adequate, with still-large volumes available at Ningbo port, despite prior loss-making conditions late December to January.

title: Nevada Copper Corp.: Nevada Copper Provides Update on Production Restart at Pumpkin Hollow and Identification of Additional Copper Targets
summary: Nevada Copper said its Pumpkin Hollow underground mine restart is progressing, with completed dike crossings, definition drilling/assays of initial EN Zone stopes, and a construction contract for key mill/ore-handling and dewatering systems. The company targets a mill restart in Q3 2023 and ramp-up toward nameplate capacity, supporting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Nickel sulfate price rebounds in China; market participants skeptical amid subdued EV demand
summary: Fastmarkets reports nickel sulfate prices in China rebounded 3.45% week-on-week after Tsingshan began producing nickel full plate using nickel sulfate, boosting sentiment and pressuring futures. But traders remain skeptical that EV-driven demand will strengthen, citing slowing battery metal demand and expectations of ample spot supply.

title: Nickel market reacts to Trafigura's 'shocking' fraud allegations
summary: Trafigura alleges large-scale containerized nickel fraud by traders connected to Prateek Gupta, involving 20,000 tonnes of uncut nickel cathode and potential $577m losses. After the release, LME three-month nickel saw sharp volatility and a temporary spike, then eased, while participants fear wider pricing and trade-finance impacts.

title: Reports we're edging closer to knowing a certain future of the Tiwai Point Aluminium Smelter - 14-Feb-2023
summary: Contact Energy’s CEO says majority owner Rio Tinto is ready to negotiate a long-term power contract for the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter near Bluff. The move follows earlier concern the power price was too expensive. As a result, expectations for aluminium production stability improve.

title: DADA Holdings Acquires Majority Stake In Aluminum Rolling Facility Near Venice, Italy
summary: DADA Holdings acquired a majority stake in Niche Fusina, an Italian aluminum rolling facility near Venice with cast house and rolling capacity (about 75,000 tons/year rolling and 95,000 tons/year slab). The plant uses substantial recycled aluminum and sustainability initiatives, supplying multiple industries across Europe and beyond.

title: Trilogy Metals to Release Updated Feasibility Study for the Arctic Copper-Zinc-Lead-Silver-Gold Project on Tuesday, February 14, 2023
summary: Trilogy Metals will publish updated feasibility study results for its Arctic copper-zinc-lead-silver-gold project in Alaska, and hold an investor call/webinar. The project is copper-dominant, which can affect market expectations about future copper supply, but no immediate production change is indicated.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.48% Higher at $4.0870 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for February delivery settled up 1.48% at $4.0870 per pound, gaining 5.95 cents. The contract was up on two of the past three sessions and remains above recent lows, though still below its 52-week high and off its 2023 settlement peak.

title: How Citigroup helped lift the lid on Trafigura's nickel nightmare
summary: Bloomberg reports that Citi stopped financing Trafigura’s nickel “transit finance” trades on Oct. 27 after concerns over alleged fraud tied to a counterparty. Trafigura’s inspections found containers labelled as nickel did not contain nickel, and it previously sold some of these cargoes onward, potentially amplifying nickel market disruption fears.

title: Copper Prices Rose amid Falling US Dollar Index_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: LME and SHFE copper rose overnight as the U.S. dollar index fell, with traders focused on upcoming U.S. CPI and interest-rate expectations. Chinese tracked copper stocks increased, but inventory growth slowed due to reduced smelter shipments to warehouses and scarce imported arrivals, while downstream demand remained tepid.

title: Copper rises on weaker dollar ahead of U.S. inflation data
summary: Copper edged higher as the U.S. dollar weakened ahead of U.S. inflation data. LME three-month copper rose 0.2% and Shanghai March copper gained 0.7%. Gains were also supported by Freeport-McMoRan cutting its copper sales forecast after rains and landslides shut the Grasberg mine until end-month.

title: Xanadu on the edge of new copper-gold frontier in Mongolia
summary: ASX-listed Xanadu Mines advances its Kharmagtai copper-gold deposit in Mongolia near Rio Tinto’s Oyu Tolgoi, citing a large resource, PEA economics and new exploration and funding steps with Zijin. Approval-driven funding supports longer-term supply expectations, but first copper concentrate is targeted for 2027, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Import Volume of Bauxite Remained at around 10 milion mt in December 2022_SMM
summary: China imported 10.15 million mt of bauxite in December 2022, down 13.9% MoM but up 16.3% YoY, with major sources including Guinea, Australia and Indonesia. Full-year imports reached a record 125.67 million mt (+16.9% YoY), suggesting steady bauxite supply for aluminium/alumina production.

title: Aluminium Ingot Inventory Kept Rising in January, with Inventory Accumulation during and after CNY Holidays Exceeding Same Period of Previous Years_SMM
summary: SMM reports aluminium ingot social inventories rose sharply in January and continued increasing after the CNY holidays. By Feb 10 inventories climbed from 740,000 mt to 1.19 million mt, the highest versus the past three years, and is projected to exceed 1.3 million mt by end-February, delaying destocking.

title: High Inventory and Costs Weighed on Aluminium Prices in February Despite Low Domestic Operating Capacity_SMM
summary: SMM reports that in January Chinese refined aluminium output fell and operating capacity declined further, with potential short-term output cuts in Yunnan. However, downstream consumption weakened during the off-season and CNY, and overseas semis demand deteriorated, driving higher social inventories and weighing on SHFE aluminium, expected to stay low before rebounding in mid-February.

title: Imports of Nickel Ore Fall in December 2022 as the Rainy Season in the Philippines Restricts Ore Shipments_SMM
summary: China’s nickel ore imports fell to 2.76 million mt in Dec 2022, down 33.9% MoM, while port stockpiles continued declining. Philippine ore shipments dropped 22.7% MoM due to rainy-season disruptions. Sulphide ore imports also declined. January import levels are expected to stay low despite lower ocean freight and a NPI price rebound.

title: China's Refined Nickel Imports Totalled 14,441 mt in Dec 2022_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s refined nickel imports totaled 14,441 mt in Dec 2022, down 0.55% MoM and 46.41% YoY. Most volume came from other unwrought alloy nickel, which fell sharply year-on-year. Russia was the largest supplier. Separate categories showed mixed MoM/YoY movements.

title: Meridian Mining UK S: Meridian Uncovers Cabaçal's Most Significant Copper Anomaly at Alvorada
summary: Meridian Mining UK reported that georeferenced historical BP archives uncovered the strongest copper stream anomaly at its Cabaçal Alvorada prospect (peak 164 ppm Cu) and plans additional mapping/geochemical/ground geophysics followed by diamond drilling. The company also restarted near-mine programs and is progressing a PEA for the project.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Inc.: Ivanhoe Electric Announces Significant Resource Upgrade at the Santa Cruz Copper Project in Arizona, Including Resource Additions at the East Ridge and Texaco Deposits
summary: Ivanhoe Electric announced a major resource upgrade at its Santa Cruz copper project in Arizona, increasing indicated tonnage and contained copper, adding resources at East Ridge and Texaco, and reporting high potential recovery from metallurgical leach-float tests. The update is intended to underpin an initial economic assessment later in Q3 2023.

title: Possible Forced Labor Enforcement Remedies on Aluminum Products | Husch Blackwell LLP
summary: Reports say CBP enforcement under the UFLPA is now targeting aluminum, including issuing detention notices and investigating aluminum products (notably automotive and Chapter 76 items). With no de minimis allowance, compliance and supply-chain disruptions could raise costs and reduce near-term availability in the U.S.

title: Copper Prices Flatline As Chinese Demand Struggles To Recover
summary: Copper prices have stalled since early February as China’s demand recovery disappoints. CME data show copper futures near recent lows. The bearish tone is reinforced by rising SHFE inventories, a stronger dollar, weaker manufacturing, and disruptions including strikes and temporary mine shutdowns in Peru alongside Chile’s output decline.

title: New Energy Metals Corp.: New Energy Metals Announces Approval of Troitsa Copper Option Agreement and Provides an Update on Roslyn Lithium Option
summary: New Energy Metals announced TSX Venture Exchange approval for its Troitsa Copper property option, outlining cash and share payments to potentially acquire a 100% interest. It also provided an update on a Roslyn lithium option agreement, but the only direct tracked-metal item is the copper property approval, with no near-term production impact described.

title: Two workers killed in protest at Indonesian nickel smelter
summary: A deadly protest at Indonesia’s Gunbuster Nickel Industry (GNI) smelter in Morowali led to a strike, violent clashes, police arrests, and the suspension of production at the facility. Management and authorities investigated while heavy security presence continued, raising near-term supply disruption risk for nickel.

title: Aluminum price on LME down below $2,400 per ton first since Jan. 9
summary: LME aluminum prices fell below $2,400 per ton for the first time since Jan. 9, according to trading data cited by TASS. Losses extended to around $2,398/ton shortly after, with the price around $2,400 again by 9:10 a.m. Moscow time.

title: Premiums of Yangshan Copper Continued to Fall amid Import Losses_SMM
summary: Yangshan copper premiums under warrants and bill of lading fell further into February, with import losses widening to 500–700 yuan/mt as the SHFE/LME ratio failed to recover. Slow post-holiday demand and trader cash selling increased oversupply and bonded-zone inventories. A PPC Naoshima smelter maintenance period may spur restocking.

title: Operating Rates of Copper Cathode Rod Producers Plummeted in January on Multiple Factors_SMM
summary: SMM says copper cathode rod producers’ average operating rate fell to 36.39% in January, far below expectations, driven by post-Covid employee infections, the traditional downstream off-season, and early closures for CNY holidays causing order/backlog issues. February is expected to rebound, though orders remain weaker than hoped.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Reports Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2022 Financial Results
summary: Capstone Copper reported Q4 and full-year 2022 results, including copper production volumes (45.5 kt in Q4) and C1 cash costs. It attributes lower quarterly performance to a lower realized copper price and higher costs such as sulphuric acid and diesel. The update also notes ongoing Mantoverde ramp-up and development milestones.

title: Here's Where Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) Stands in a Copper-Constrained World
summary: Diamond Hill Capital’s investor letter highlights Freeport-McMoRan, arguing its Q4 copper producer stock advance reflected a rebound in copper prices. It attributes the rebound to recognition that copper inventories are low versus historical norms, suggesting ongoing leverage for the company in a “copper-constrained world.”

title: Diamond Drill Mobilization Commences at York Harbour Metals' High-Grade Copper-Zinc-Silver Project in Newfoundland
summary: York Harbour Metals says diamond drilling has begun at its York Harbour Copper-Zinc-Silver VMS project in Newfoundland, with drilling expected to start in about a week. The company aims to delineate extensions of the A Zone and test additional targets identified by IP/EM surveys and geochemical anomalies.

title: PolyMet Mining Corp.: PolyMet closes NewRange Copper Nickel joint venture with Teck Resources
summary: PolyMet and Teck closed the NewRange Copper Nickel joint venture covering the NorthMet and Mesaba deposits in Minnesota. The owners committed funding for permitting and engineering (initial work program) and PolyMet announced a ~$200m rights offering to fund its share and repay debt. This is a modest bullish signal for copper and nickel.

title: PolyMet Mining Corp.: PolyMet closes NewRange Copper Nickel joint venture with Teck Resources
summary: PolyMet and Teck closed their 50:50 joint venture, NewRange Copper Nickel LLC, covering the NorthMet and Mesaba copper-nickel deposits. PolyMet will raise about US$200 million via a rights offering to fund its share of an initial work program and repay Glencore-related debt. Permits remain partly dependent on litigation clearance.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Announces Significant Resource Upgrade At the Santa Cruz Copper Project in Arizona, Including Resource Additions At the East Ridge and Texaco Deposits
summary: Ivanhoe Electric announced an updated Mineral Resource Estimate for its Santa Cruz copper project in Arizona, adding initial resources at the East Ridge and Texaco deposits and increasing project-wide Indicated contained copper. Higher cut-off grades boosted Indicated contained copper, with strong emphasis on high-grade oxide/exotic domains for an upcoming IA/PEA.

title: Cascada Silver Corp.: Cascada Options Angie Copper Molybdenum Project
summary: Cascada Silver Corp. announced it signed an option agreement to acquire 100% of the Angie Copper-Molybdenum Project in Chile. The target shows a defined molybdenum anomaly linked to a probable porphyry system, with plans for mapping and reverse circulation drilling in 2023. No near-term production impacts are described.

title: NewRange Copper Nickel LLC: NewRange Copper Nickel poised to supply critical minerals for clean energy transition
summary: PolyMet and Teck’s joint venture, NewRange Copper Nickel LLC, has been formed to advance the NorthMet and Mesaba projects in Minnesota. These deposits are cited as major copper and nickel resources. The company plans permitting and pre-construction studies, which can modestly lift near-term sentiment for copper and nickel supply prospects.

title: NewRange Copper Nickel LLC: NewRange Copper Nickel poised to supply critical minerals for clean energy transition
summary: NewRange Copper Nickel LLC was formed via a JV between PolyMet and Teck, controlling the NorthMet and Mesaba deposits in Minnesota. The projects are geared toward developing domestic copper and nickel supply for North America’s clean-energy transition, with permits pending for NorthMet and ongoing pre-development work for Mesaba.

title: Freeport-McMoran (FCX) Receives Copper Mark at PT Freeport Indonesia
summary: Freeport-McMoRan said PT Freeport Indonesia received the Copper Mark, validating conformance at all 12 of its eligible copper producing sites globally. The company also noted Molybdenum Mark awards for its primary molybdenum mines. The announcement focuses on ESG assurance and revalidation requirements, not production or shipment changes.

title: U.S. Weighs 200% Tariff On Russian Aluminum
summary: The U.S. is considering a unilateral measure that could tariff Russian aluminum by up to 200%, potentially cutting U.S. access to ~200,000 tons/year. The piece links this to rising European duty-paid premiums and tightness indicators, raising the risk of shortage and margin pressure, which should support aluminium prices.

title: U.S. Steel And Aluminium Tariffs Ruled WTO-Inconsistent But U.S. Refuses To Remove The Measures Citing National Security Concerns | Bennett Jones LLP
summary: Bennett Jones reports WTO panels found U.S. Section 232 tariffs (25% on steel, 10% on aluminium) inconsistent, but the U.S. refused to remove them, appealing “into the void” to keep cases in limbo. Canada may face further U.S. security-based tariff actions. Aluminium trade costs remain the immediate focus.

title: Teck Announces Completion of NewRange Copper Nickel Joint Venture Agreement with PolyMet
summary: Teck announced it has completed the NewRange copper–nickel joint venture agreement with PolyMet. The deal headline suggests improved forward supply expectations for copper and nickel, which can support prices in the near term. The excerpt contains no project specifics, so immediate impact is uncertain.

title: Rio Tinto and Marubeni partner to create stronger and more responsible Aluminium supply chains
summary: Rio Tinto and Marubeni agreed a collaboration in Japan to sell Rio Tinto’s “Responsible Aluminium” products, including RenewAlTM high purity aluminium from New Zealand Aluminium Smelters. The deal uses Marubeni’s trading and carbon-credit mechanism to help downstream customers meet ESG and traceability requirements, aiming to secure reliable supply amid risks.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.41% Lower at $4.0520 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex Copper for February delivery settled 1.41% lower at $4.0520, down 5.80 cents per pound. The move ended a two-session winning streak and leaves copper weaker month-to-date, despite remaining up versus some prior lows. LME copper cash also declined modestly.

title: SMM ADC12 Secondary Aluminium Alloy Prices on January 15_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that ADC12 secondary aluminium alloy prices in Shanghai were 19,550–19,750 yuan/mt on January 15, unchanged versus the previous day. The flat reading suggests limited near-term price momentum for secondary aluminium supply and related aluminium market expectations.

title: SMM A00 Aluminium Prices Fell on January 15_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that Shanghai spot A00 aluminium prices fell to 18,410–18,450 yuan/mt on January 15, down 60 yuan/mt from the prior day. Spot discounts were broadly stable at 50–90 yuan/mt against the SHFE 2303 contract, pointing to modest bearish sentiment in the aluminium market.

title: SMM Detailed Analysis of Aluminium Smelters' Cost Changes in January and February _SMM
summary: SMM reports January 2023 aluminium smelter costs fell to about 17,200 yuan/mt as coal prices eased, electricity costs were stable, and prebaked anode prices declined. Smelter profits rose. It estimates costs may fall further in Feb–Mar as anode benchmarks drop, supporting aluminium sentiment.

title: SMM Alumina Prices Dipped on February 15_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that alumina prices averaged 2,949 yuan/mt on February 15, down 2 yuan/mt from the previous day. The note appears to be a pricing snapshot for alumina rather than a major supply/demand shock. Any effect on aluminium would be limited and likely insufficient for strong short-term price moves.

title: China Copper Foil Output to Decline in February amid Sluggish Market Performance _SMM
summary: SMM estimates China’s copper foil output will fall 1.16% MoM to 65,400 mt in February, despite strong YoY growth from lithium battery copper foil capacity expansion. However, NEV market sluggishness and the end of subsidies have left battery foil firms with poor new orders, with some considering switching products.

title: SMM #1 Copper Cathode Prices Tumbled on Feb 16_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that #1 copper cathode prices fell by 575 yuan/mt on Feb 16 to 68,280–68,460 yuan/mt. The direct reporting of a large daily decline signals near-term bearish pressure for copper cathode markets.

title: Qingdao Zhongcheng's Subsidary in Indonesia Focuses on NPI Production, Giving no Consideration to Refined Nickel_SMM
summary: Qingdao Zhongcheng’s Indonesian operations are said to be producing nickel ore subject to Indonesia’s export restrictions. The ore will be smelted in Indonesia, where the company’s smelters will prioritize NPI production rather than refined nickel for now, while monitoring further policy changes.

title: SMM Aluminium Ingot and Billet Social Inventories as of February 16_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s aluminium ingot social inventories rose to 1.22m mt, but weekly growth slowed and accumulation is expected to be only mildly positive. Aluminium billet inventories fell to 202,300 mt on warehouse outflows, with demand improving. Yunnan smelters face power-driven curtailment risk.

title: Aluminium Billet Market Maintains Destocking _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
