summary: SMM says China’s aluminium ingot social inventories were 1.267 million mt on March 9, slightly down on the week but still much higher year-on-year, with prices rangebound as demand recovers slowly. summary: TNR Gold’s update relays McEwen Copper’s drilling results from the Los Azules porphyry project in Argentina, highlighting copper intercepts such as 1,052 m averaging 0.29% Cu and 236 m of 1.39% Cu, supporting continued resource de-risking and potential expansion toward feasibility in 2024.

title: First Quantum, Panama seal draft concession deal on copper project
summary: First Quantum’s Minera Panamá and Panama agreed to settle a profit-sharing dispute for the Cobre Panamá copper mine, with payments covering taxes and royalties. The draft concession contract requires approval and public consultation, and Minera expects permits to resume copper concentrate loading at Punta Rincon port after a long suspension.

title: Large copper cathode plant to be launched in East Kazakhstan region
summary: Kazakhstan’s Prime Minister discussed plans to build a copper cathode smelter in East Kazakhstan with capacity of about 300,000 tons per year. The project is intended to attract foreign investment and technology, meet tax and power-supply considerations, and boost exports. State agencies were tasked to support investor implementation.

title: KAM and Granges Powder Metallurgy Form Partnership to Expand DISPAL® High Performance Aluminum Alloy Solutions in US
summary: KAM and Granges Powder Metallurgy formed a partnership to expand US production of DISPAL® high-performance aluminum alloy solutions for additive manufacturing. summary: Stellantis’ multimillion-dollar investment in McEwen’s Los Azules copper project is reported in connection with a royalty and project financing update. summary: US copper scrap exports shifted toward China and India while some other destinations fell. Sources describe depressed domestic demand and sluggish end-market activity, particularly in China. summary: BHP expects China’s demand recovery to support overall growth in copper demand this year, but highlights a short-term copper supply glut. summary: German metal processor Speira will close its aluminium smelting operations at the Rheinwerk plant because energy prices are too high. title: Copper Inventories in Domestic Bonded Zone Add 10,300 mt from March 3_SMM
summary: SMM says copper inventories in China’s domestic bonded zones rose 10,300 mt to 195,500 mt from March 3, with most gains in Shanghai. More arrivals are expected mid-March, keeping inventories rising slightly.

title: Bonded Zone Inventory of Nickel Drops Slightly from March 3_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported bonded zone nickel inventory fell 500 mt to 5,100 mt as of March 10. Nickel plate stock declined more amid weak downstream demand, reflecting dropping nickel prices. summary: ArcWest announced an earn-in partnership with Freeport to advance its Todd Creek copper-gold project in British Columbia. title: HAIB COPPER: THE RULE OF LAW PREVAILS IN NAMIBIA. THE HIGH COURT RENDERS VERDICT IN FAVOR OF DEEP-SOUTH

summary: ArcWest shares surged after announcing an earn-in deal with Freeport-McMoRan on its copper-gold property in British Columbia’s Golden Triangle. summary: SMM forecasts March aluminium prices as the Fed stays hawkish and downstream demand improves. Domestic supply recovery is expected to be partial due to output cuts in Yunnan and Guizhou, leading to declining social inventories. High current inventories may cap gains, so SHFE aluminium is projected to trade within 17,500–19,200 yuan/mt.

title: China's Alumina Import Window Has Remained Closed since January 18_SMM
summary: Alcoa reduced output at its Kwinana alumina refinery in Australia by 30% because of natural gas shortages, and the plant stayed closed through March 10 with restart timing unknown. The cut kept overseas alumina prices elevated, while China’s alumina import window has been closed since January 18.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Reports 100.12 Metres at 0.69% Copper at Copper Creek in Arizona
summary: Faraday Copper reported drill intercepts at its Copper Creek project in Arizona, including 100.12 metres at 0.69% copper and other copper-bearing zones outside the current mineral resource shell. Management says results support potential open-pit resource expansion. The news is exploration-focused and does not imply immediate production changes.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp.: Flying Nickel Signs Landmark Impact and Benefit Agreement with Norway House Cree Nation to Advance the Minago Nickel Project in Manitoba
summary: Flying Nickel Mining signed an Impact and Benefit Agreement with Norway House Cree Nation to advance the Minago nickel project in Manitoba. The IBA includes jobs, contracting, board participation, share subscription, and revenue-sharing based on nickel revenues, improving certainty around development.

title: Alumina Refineries Favoured Domestic Bauxite in March Following Steep Drop in Caustic Soda Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanxi alumina refineries cut liquid caustic soda purchase prices in March after a steep MoM decline in caustic soda. The lower caustic soda eases refinery losses, prompting some refineries to reduce imported bauxite and buy more domestic ore. Domestic bauxite remains supported by persistent shortages.

title: Alumina Prices in Guangxi Bear the Brunt of Demand Shock_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Power rationing in Yunnan hit aluminium smelters, cutting output by about 65,000 mt monthly from 780,000 mt capacity and threatening roughly 130,000 mt of alumina demand per month. With demand sagging, alumina prices in Guangxi fell to 2,830 yuan/mt by March 10 and price spreads widened.

title: SMM Monthly Alumina Price Forecast from Supply-Demand Perspective_SMM
summary: SMM expects alumina prices to fall further as oversupply persists and north China cost support is weakening. Tight north-south spreads limit arbitrage, but any widening could shift surplus south alumina north, accelerating declines. Reduced demand in south-west and refinery resumptions (Bosai, Guanglv, State Power Investment) further worsen supply-demand balance.

title: Rising Operating Rates Shifted Alumina Market to Supply Surplus in February_SMM
summary: SMM said operating rates at China’s alumina refineries rose in February, shifting the alumina market to an estimated supply surplus of about 265,000 mt. A surplus implies easing alumina availability and input pressure, which can weigh on expectations for aluminium prices over the coming weeks.

title: Alumina Refineries Slashed March Liquid Caustic Soda Purchase Prices_SMM
summary: Alumina refineries in Shanxi lowered March liquid caustic soda purchase prices by 800 yuan/mt to 2,700 yuan/mt. SMM estimates this cuts alkali costs for producing 1 mt of alumina by about 200 yuan/mt (domestic ore) and 90 yuan/mt (imported ore), potentially supporting alumina economics.

title: Short-term Aluminium Fluoride Prices to Rangebound_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that in March, purchase prices of aluminium fluoride offered by major aluminium factories are expected to generally fall. However, market supply for aluminium fluoride remains not high, allowing producers to quote higher. Overall, short-term aluminium fluoride prices are expected to stay rangebound, implying limited net direction.

title: Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe and Allies Call on Minnesota Officials to Prioritize Clean Water Over Nickel Mining
summary: The Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe and allies launched the “Water Over Nickel” initiative opposing Minnesota plans for the proposed Tamarack nickel mine by Talon Metals. They cite risks to local water, watersheds, and cultural sites and urge officials to prioritize clean water over nickel mining.

title: Aluminium Smelter Shutdowns Threaten Europe's Green Transiti...
summary: The article headline reports that aluminium smelter shutdowns are threatening Europe’s green transition. If smelters curtail production, near-term aluminium supply tightens, which can raise price expectations and support aluminium prices in the coming days to weeks, barring an offsetting rise in inventories or demand.

title: Canada's ban on Russian aluminium imports | Hotter Commodities
summary: Canada bans imports of all Russian aluminium products from March 10, building on earlier tariff measures that already largely halted Russian flows. The move follows US plans for a 200% tariff and LME warranting suspensions for Russia-origin metal. Attention now turns to Europe/UK for possible further restrictions.

title: Rio Tinto Starts Digging Copper From Oyu Tolgoi Mine
summary: Rio Tinto says it has started digging copper from the Oyu Tolgoi mine in Mongolia after years of delays and disputes with the government. CEO Jakob Stausholm argues the project is well-positioned to meet rising copper demand tied to electric vehicles and renewable energy, supporting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.45% Lower at $4.0105 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for March delivery settled 1.45% lower at $4.0105, down 5.90 cents per pound. The move marks the largest one-day dollar and percentage decline since March 7, with copper down two of the past three sessions and at its lowest settlement since then.

title: Quellaveco proves insufficient to offset Peru's January copper output drop
summary: Quellaveco’s production was insufficient to compensate for a reported drop in Peru’s copper output in January. The shortfall points to weaker near-term supply conditions from one of the world’s key copper-producing countries, which can increase expectations of tighter inventories and weigh on copper prices in the coming weeks.

title: Nickel Ore Mines Hold Their Prices Firm, which was Unacceptable for Downstream Companies_SMM
summary: SMM reports Ni 1.5% nickel ore at about $71/wmt CIF, slightly lower WoW. Philippine rainy-season conditions keep nickel ore supply tight. NPI demand from stainless producers has been weaker, pressuring NPI prices and prompting wait-and-see restocking, though limited supply suggests nickel ore may stabilize with occasional drops.

title: Copper flat as investors gauge demand uncertainty
summary: London copper fell as investors reassessed China demand prospects after early 2020s factory data grew more slowly than expected and property investment stayed weak. A steadier U.S. dollar also dampened buying interest. In parallel, LME aluminium and nickel were slightly lower on the same day.

title: Brazil Cancels Import Tariffs on Six Products, Covering Steel and Aluminium Plate/Sheet_SMM
summary: Brazil has canceled import tariffs on six products effective March 10, including aluminium plate/sheet categories previously taxed at 12-16%. The policy change is expected to alter near-term trade flows and supply conditions for aluminium flat products, influencing pricing expectations within days as import demand and availability adjust.

title: Costs of Chinese Aluminium Smelters Fall Drastically_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that Chinese aluminium smelter costs dropped sharply in March, with average cost falling to 17,200 yuan/mt as of March 12, down 500 yuan/mt from early February. The decline points to improved smelter economics and may support near-term aluminium prices.

title: American Creek Resources Ltd.: American Creek's JV Partner Tudor Gold Announces Significant Upgrade to Mineral Resource Estimate for the Goldstorm Porphyry Deposit at the Treaty Creek Project, British Columbia with Increased Gold, Copper and Silver Grades
summary: Tudor Gold updated the Mineral Resource Estimate for its Goldstorm porphyry deposit at the Treaty Creek project, increasing grades and total copper contained to over 3 billion pounds, alongside gold and silver improvements. The release is resource-focused and does not announce production or immediate supply changes.

title: Alcoa Corp. Says Portland Aluminium Joint Venture Smelter To Cut Production To 75%
summary: Alcoa said its Portland Aluminium joint-venture smelter in Victoria will cut production to about 75% of capacity immediately because of operational instability, including rodded anode production issues. Output remains reduced until stability is restored. The change lowers the site’s 358,000 mtpy capacity utilization, supporting aluminium prices.

title: Iran targets one million tons of copper production, USD10B i...
summary: The article headline says Iran plans to target one million tons of copper production with a USD 10B initiative. This is directly tied to prospective copper supply and could influence market expectations, but the provided text lacks near-term output timing or concrete production changes.

title: Energy transition: Rio Tinto wants the Albanese government to support aluminium smelters under safeguard changes
summary: Rio Tinto urged Australia’s Albanese government to increase decarbonisation spending and provide special treatment for its unionised aluminium smelters under reforms to the safeguard mechanism. Labor has allocated $600 million in grants, which Rio argues should be much higher, implying less near-term smelter disruption and supportive aluminium supply outlook.

title: Canada Nickel reports high nickel recoveries at Reid project
summary: Canada Nickel says its first metallurgical test at the Reid ultramafic nickel project near Crawford in Ontario produced a head grade of 0.35% nickel, 0.10% sulphur, and 6.2% iron, alongside reported high nickel recoveries. The results support improved prospects for future nickel output.

title: Beer Institute Reacts to ITC Report on Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The Beer Institute reacts to a new ITC report saying U.S. companies faced most costs from Section 232 aluminum tariffs, raising production expenses for brewers and contributing to higher consumer prices. The group urges repeal of the tariffs, citing WTO rulings that challenged the tariffs’ basis.

title: TASEKO CLOSES ACQUISITION OF 12.5% INTEREST IN GIBRALTAR COPPER MINE
summary: Taseko says it completed its acquisition of an additional 12.5% interest in the Gibraltar copper mine, raising its effective ownership to 87.5%. The deal includes C$60 million minimum payments and contingent amounts linked to Gibraltar copper revenues and copper prices over the next five years.

title: Aluminium Scrap Prices Remain Firm in Feb_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that in February, SMM A00 aluminium prices fell overall, but aluminium scrap prices in south China remained relatively firm due to supply tightness. Taint scrap dropped 300-500 yuan/mt, while tense scrap fell 100-300 yuan/mt, reflecting softer aluminium-linked demand despite tighter availability.

title: Macro Headwinds to Leave Aluminium Prices Vulnerable _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports broad non-ferrous weakness driven by macro sentiment. Aluminium led declines: SHFE 2304 fell about 1.6% and LME aluminium dropped roughly 3%, reflecting heightened liquidity/systemic-risk concerns after Silicon Valley Bank and Credit Suisse turmoil. Aluminium demand is recovering, but bearish macro sentiment keeps prices vulnerable.

title: Aluminium Prices Trend Lower in Feb_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that primary aluminium prices trended lower in February, while aluminium scrap prices stayed firm, narrowing the primary–scrap spread. In south China, spreads for Foshan extrusion and shredded tenses fell sharply, while in east China (Shanghai) spreads narrowed only slightly.

title: China's Major Copper Concentrate Suppliers in Dec 2022, with Chile Ranking First_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s copper concentrate imports by origin in Dec 2022, including 740,600 mt from Chile (+6.34% MoM) and 573,100 mt from Peru (-1.81% MoM). Other flows (Canada, US, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Indonesia) are also detailed, indicating shifting near-term concentrate supply for Chinese smelters.

title: Glencore Won't Renew $16 Billion Aluminum Contract With Rusal
summary: Glencore reportedly will not renew a $16 billion aluminum contract with Rusal. The non-renewal signals a potential disruption or reduction in previously agreed aluminum supply, which can alter near-term market expectations for availability and logistics. Such a change typically weighs on aluminum prices in the following days to weeks.

title: Increase in RCs of Blister Copper in South China in February Hit the Highest Since the Second half of 2022_SMM
summary: SMM reports that blister copper RCs in South China rose 250 yuan/mt in February to 900–1,300 yuan/mt, the highest since mid-2022, driven by sufficient scrap supply and high blister inventories. Imported RCs fell slightly. Smelters restocked before March maintenance, reducing near-term blister demand.

title: Rising Copper Prices in February Led to Sufficient Copper Scrap Supply_SMM
summary: After the Lantern Festival, Chinese copper scrap supply resumed as suppliers shipped more scrap amid high copper prices. While weekly operating rates rose, secondary copper rod plants’ incremental scrap demand stayed limited because wire and cable orders were weak and they relied on existing inventories. Net impact on price appears offsetting.

title: China's Copper Anode Imports Decreased 7,000 Mt in December 2022_SMM
summary: China’s copper anode imports fell in December 2022 to 84,400 mt (down 7.62% MoM, 6.86% YoY). The MoM drop was mainly due to lower Zambian anode shipments (down 24.49% to 30,800 mt). Imports from Congo rose, while South Africa volumes increased in January.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Inc.: Ivanhoe Electric Identifies Visible Soluble Copper Mineralization at Texaco Ridge Step-Out Exploration Drill Hole
summary: Ivanhoe Electric reports visible soluble copper mineralization at its Texaco Ridge step-out drill hole, intersecting oxide/chalcocite/chalcopyrite zones, and highlights recent infill drilling at the Santa Cruz deposit (e.g., 55m at 3.10% Cu). The company advances an initial assessment for underground development.

title: The Metals Company: TMC Enters into MOU with Leading Nickel Processor PAMCO to Evaluate the Processing of Polymetallic Nodules into Battery Metal Feedstocks
summary: TMC entered a non-binding MOU with Japan’s PAMCO to evaluate toll processing 1.3 million tonnes/year of polymetallic nodules from 2025. PAMCO would use existing Hachinohe smelting infrastructure to produce nickel-copper-cobalt alloy and manganese silicate, with further study on upgrading to matte. Near-term effects are uncertain due to study-only terms.

title: SMM China Weekly Aluminium Inventory (Mar 16, 2023) _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported China’s aluminium ingot social inventories at 1.21 million mt on March 16, down week-on-week, with declines led by Foshan on better consumption and downstream buying, aided by Yunnan output cuts. Billet inventories rose, with smoother arrivals and weaker buying interest due to firm margins.

title: SMM A00 Aluminium Prices Fall Sharply on Mar 16_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that on Mar 16 the SMM A00 aluminium price in Shanghai fell sharply to 18,120–18,160 yuan/mt, down 180 yuan/mt from the prior day. The move signals immediate bearish momentum in aluminium spot pricing, with no comparable changes cited for copper or nickel.

title: Aluminium Ingot Social Inventories Fall Considerably after Two Months of Seasonal Accumulation _SMM
summary: Shanghai-based SMM reports China aluminium ingot social inventories at 1.21m mt as of March 16, down 56,000 mt on the week. The decline follows two consecutive weeks of destocking, led by Foshan amid stronger downstream buying and tighter supply after late-February output cuts in Yunnan.

title: Average Operating Rate of Copper-zinc Alloy Billet Producers Rises in Feb_SMM
summary: SMM reported that copper-zinc alloy billet producers’ average operating rate rose to 60.35% in February, up 29 percentage points month-on-month and 17.13 percentage points year-on-year. The higher utilization indicates improved production activity and likely stronger short-term demand for copper alloy feedstock.

title: TNR Gold Corp.: TNR Gold NSR Royalty Update on McEwen Los Azules Copper, Gold & Silver Project - Rio Tinto's Nuton and Stellantis now Shareholders of McEwen Copper
summary: TNR Gold reports progress on McEwen Mining’s Los Azules copper project in Argentina, where TNR holds a 0.4% NSR royalty. The update highlights continued exploration drilling, road improvements, and further funding/strategic stakes by Nuton (Rio Tinto venture) and Stellantis, aimed at advancing the project toward a future feasibility update.

title: TNR Gold NSR Royalty Update on McEwen Los Azules Copper, Gold & Silver Project - Rio Tinto's Nuton and Stellantis now Shareholders of McEwen Copper
summary: TNR Gold reported that Rio Tinto Venture’s Nuton and Stellantis became shareholders of McEwen Copper, funding additional stake increases to advance the Los Azules copper project in Argentina. The release highlights ongoing drilling, updated studies/PEA timing, and a planned heap-leach/ SX-EW approach to produce LME Grade A copper cathodes.

title: Aluminum Association Requests Ruling that Certain Imports from Korea are Circumventing Unfair Trade Orders on Common Alloy Aluminum Sheet from China
summary: The Aluminum Association asked the U.S. Department of Commerce to investigate whether Korean imports of common alloy aluminum sheet, made using Chinese inputs, are circumventing existing AD/CVD duties on similar Chinese-origin products. Commerce has 45 days to decide on initiating the inquiry, which could raise costs and limit import competition.

title: Glencore won't renew $21b Rusal deal
summary: Glencore will not renew its large aluminum supply deal with Russia’s Rusal when it expires next year, citing its policy against new business with Russia after the Ukraine invasion. The decision signals reduced Russian aluminum trade, which can support near-term aluminum pricing sentiment via tighter supply expectations.

title: Aluminum company Speira closes down German plant
summary: Speira will place its Rheinwerk aluminum plant in long-term care after an earlier 50% production cut, citing damage from Europe’s energy crisis. The closure highlights smelters’ reluctance to restart amid uncertain gas prices and weak primary output. Analysts see further supply pressure for aluminum despite some offset via external sourcing.

title: European nickel uncut cathode and briquette premiums rise but premiums steady elsewhere
summary: European nickel refined premiums for uncut cathode and briquettes rose sharply, especially in-whs Rotterdam, amid tighter regional availability and higher offers/assessments. LME nickel weakness encouraged some consumer return, but liquidity remained limited at top range levels. Cathode premiums stayed high, while US premiums were mostly flat.

title: SMM Copper Concentrate Index Dip $4.94/mt MoM in Feb on Disrupted Production and Hindered Concentrate Shipments at Overseas Mines_SMM
summary: SMM said its monthly Copper Concentrate Index fell to $78.28/mt in February, down $4.94/mt month-on-month, with the decline linked to disrupted mine production and hindered concentrate shipments in America and Southeast Asia. The index was down for 14 straight weeks as of March 10.

title: RCs of Domestic Blister Copper Add 250 yuan/mt MoM in Feb on Eased Supply Tightness_SMM
summary: SMM said domestic blister copper RCs increased 250 yuan/mt MoM in February, while imported CIF RCs fell $5/mt. Copper was near highs, as higher scrap availability grew after CNY. Improved COVID-19 logistics and faster dismantling eased blister copper supply tightness in China.

title: Alcoa Announces Closure Of Intalco Aluminum Smelter In Washington State
summary: Alcoa said it will permanently close its Intalco aluminium smelter in Washington State, which has been fully idle since 2020. The firm will record restructuring charges in Q1 2023 and expects cash outlays over three years. AltaGas has rights to redevelop the site, including transport and utility infrastructure.

title: China Imports 87,800 mt of Nickel Hydrometallurgy Intermediate Products in Dec 2022_SMM
summary: China imported 87,800 mt of nickel hydrometallurgy intermediate products in Dec 2022 (17,700 mt Ni content), down 13% MoM. Nickel matte imports were 30,000 mt in Dec, down 7% MoM. Tsingshan shifted some matte-based lines to NPI, cutting matte output by 9,000 mt in Jan, potentially tightening intermediate supply.

title: Aughinish owner Rusal may face end of $16bn aluminium contract
summary: Glencore is reportedly willing to end a $16bn aluminium supply contract with Russia’s Rusal, the owner of the Aughinish alumina/aluminium business. Glencore’s Russia-biz policy introduced after the Ukraine invasion suggests reduced Russian aluminium trading. The potential contract termination could tighten market availability and support aluminium prices.

title: Both Copper Semis Import and Export Posted Seasonal Recovery in February_SMM
summary: SMM estimates China imported 41,000 mt of copper semis in February, +78% MoM, and exported 61,000 mt, +54% MoM. The year-on-year increase is attributed to CNY holiday effects, though Jan-Feb volumes fell YoY. Softer US/EU durable demand is linked to weaker exports and lower freight rates.

title: Operating Rates at Copper Semis Plants Recovered and Topped Expectations in February_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s copper semis output rose sharply in February, and operating rates jumped to 64.63%, slightly above expectations. Gains were strongest in the copper pipe industry and supported by improved orders from transformers, new energy, and home appliances post–Chinese New Year, while overseas demand stayed lukewarm.

title: SMM Forecast of Copper Semis Import and Export in March_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM expects China’s domestic consumption to be in peak season in March, with government support boosting demand for copper semiconductors. This should increase copper semi imports. Overseas demand recovery is expected to be slow, so exports should remain low with no significant rise, supporting domestic market tightness.

title: SMM Views on Copper Price Direction in March_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says copper prices in March will be heavily influenced by changing expectations for Fed rate hikes, as softer US growth may still support a stronger USD. Import losses have narrowed but continue to weigh on seaborne copper clearance. At the same time, peak season and policy stimulus should lift consumption.

title: SMM Forecast of Production at Copper Semis Plants in March_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM forecasts March operating rates for copper semi-processing in China to average 72.59%, up 7.96 percentage points month-on-month, driven by the traditional peak season. Sector-specific rates are expected at 83.55% for copper pipe, 76.61% for plate/sheet and strip, and 69.24% for cathode rod.

title: Mistango River Resources Inc.: Mistango Updates on Manibridge's Drill Intersections Including 1.13% Nickel Equivalent over 36.55 Metres
summary: Mistango (15% interest) updates Manibridge drilling results, highlighting over 1% nickel mineralization and a highest-grade continuous intersection of 19.45m at 1.69% NiEq, with assays also incorporating Cu and Co components. These are exploration findings rather than production changes, so near-term metal price effects are likely limited.

title: Glencore to not renew $16bn aluminium contract with Rusal
summary: Glencore said it will not renew a $16bn aluminium supply contract with Russia’s Rusal, citing compliance with policies after the Ukraine conflict. Although existing deals remain honored, non-renewal could shift Russian metal flows to the market and potentially increase LME warehouse deliveries, adding price pressure for aluminium.

title: EU adds copper, nickel and manganese to list of critical materials
summary: The European Union published its Critical Raw Materials Act and designated copper and nickel as critical raw materials. The framework aims to simplify permitting and strengthen access to supply. While potentially supportive for medium-term investment certainty, the excerpt provides no immediate trade or supply shock likely to drive near-term prices.

title: 10 Best Copper Stocks To Buy For 2023 - Insider Monkey
summary: The article argues copper should benefit from supply tightness, historically low inventories, and ongoing disruptions, reinforced by EU legislation classifying copper and nickel as critical raw materials. It also expects aluminum to remain above historical averages into early 2024. Nickel is framed as having a 2023 surplus despite EV-driven demand.

title: FCA Statement London Metal Exchange Nickel Market
summary: The FCA confirmed it has opened an enforcement investigation into the LME’s conduct and controls related to the LME’s 2022 suspension of nickel trading. The review follows the disorderly nickel market after Russia’s invasion and price spikes, and aims to assess governance and lessons for future market structure and risk management.

title: China Jan-Feb aluminium imports rose 11.3% on year - Stock market news
summary: China’s aluminium imports in Jan–Feb 2023 rose 11.3% y/y to 374,321 tonnes as demand expectations improved after reopening. Domestic primary aluminium output grew 7.5%, and bauxite imports increased 12.8%. Despite higher volumes, high global prices in early 2023 made imports less attractive and LME prices eased in February.

title: Iran's Alumina Powder Production Reaches 206,887 Tons in Fir...
summary: The article reports that Iran’s alumina powder production reached approximately 206,887 tons in the referenced period. Alumina is a primary feedstock for aluminium smelting, so increased alumina output can improve supply conditions along the aluminium value chain and provide modest bullish support to aluminium prices.

title: SMM Aluminium Morning Comment (Mar 20, 2023)_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that aluminium prices fell slightly last week but stayed relatively resilient as improving downstream demand and a sharp drop in social aluminium ingot inventories offset macro headwinds. The outlook for this week is positive, with expectations of further inventory declines and stronger spot transactions potentially lifting aluminium prices.

title: Aluminium prices to rebound on sharply falling inventories_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports aluminium prices were resilient last week amid macro uncertainty, but highlights sharply falling inventories and improving spot transactions. With better fundamentals counteracting macro headwinds, aluminium is poised to rebound. It expects SHFE aluminium to trade around 18,000–18,800 yuan/mt and LME aluminium at $2,250–2,450/mt this week.

title: Copper Prices Rebounded Slightly as Market Awaiting Fed Interest Rate Decision_SMM
summary: LME copper closed higher on the week, with SHFE futures also up slightly. The move is attributed to eased worries about the banking crisis after bank stocks fell, alongside a large drawdown in Chinese copper inventories and increased downstream procurement as prices dropped. Overall, prices are expected to trade narrowly.

title: Lower Spot Copper Prices Can Keep Sellers Reluctant to Sell in Shanghai_SMM
summary: SMM reports Shanghai copper spot premiums fluctuated, with premiums rising on downstream buying as prices fell, but subsequently dropping. It expects more imported copper inflows due to a favorable domestic SHFE/LME ratio and strong premiums, plus increased warrant sales after delivery, pressuring intraday spot quotes.

title: SMM Views on Copper Price Direction This Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM expects panic sentiment to fade as overseas liquidity injections reduce systemic risk, while consumer demand and fundamentals stay broadly bullish. Copper market structure remains backwardated, with rebounding premiums and improving import losses. However, rising imported-copper inflows may pressure domestic supply and slow inventory depletion, weighing on spot premiums.

title: Copper Inventory Across China's Major Trading Markets Decreased Last Week_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s copper inventory across major trading markets fell 44,900 mt to 226,200 mt as of March 17. Copper semi-processing companies replenished stock after prices tumbled. The article argues that downstream recovery and lower inventories should underpin copper prices over the near term.

title: Spot Copper Prices in Shandong to Fall Back_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that Shandong spot copper discounts had stabilized early in the week but moved up and down with copper price volatility after a banking crisis. Downstream procurement increased during price drops but eased after rebounds. This week demand is improving slightly, yet discounts are expected to fall back toward 100 yuan/mt.

title: Copper concentrate Supply continued to recover_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports active spot copper concentrate transactions and recent improvement in logistics for Las Bambas in Peru after a roadblock removal, with gradual inventory reduction and possible late-March shipments. Port congestion persists, but inventories at Chinese ports fell, while smelters expect TCs to rebound in April and into Q2.

title: Copper falls in volatile market as fears over banking crisis persist
summary: Industrial metals prices fell as investors worried that a banking crisis could worsen and hurt global economic growth. Copper eased on both LME and SHFE. Nickel also declined. Aluminium was mixed but broadly pressured, reflecting risk-off positioning as liquidity promises and a Credit Suisse rescue deal failed to calm markets.

title: China Jan-Feb aluminium imports from Russia more than triple on-year
summary: China’s aluminium imports from Russia more than tripled in January–February, reflecting stronger Chinese demand and reduced Western trading of Russian metal after sanctions. Russia supplies most Chinese primary aluminium. US and Canada measures and Glencore’s non-renewal of a Rusal deal reinforce the diversion toward China.

title: Aluminium Ingot Stocks May Have Entered Seasonal Destocking Cycle_SMM
summary: Shanghai-based SMM data shows China’s social aluminium ingot inventories at 1.17 million mt, down week-on-week and indicating seasonal destocking. Cargoes in transit are limited, arrivals are normalizing, and smelters increasing molten output implies continued declines in ingot supplies. Warehouse outflows rose, supporting tighter availability.

title: China's Tianshan Aluminum to Build New Plant in Indonesia for USD1.6 Billion
summary: Tianshan Aluminum will invest nearly USD1.6 billion to build a 2 million t/year aluminum oxide plant in Indonesia’s Riau Islands, including logistics infrastructure. An initial phase targets 1 million t/year. The firm expects improved bauxite/coal-based raw material supply, following earlier bauxite mine rights purchases.

title: ADVENTUS AND SALAZAR ANNOUNCE ADDITIONAL EL DOMO UNDERGROUND DEPOSIT DRILLING RESULTS INCLUDING 14 METRES OF 4.44% COPPER EQUIVALENT
summary: ADVENTUS and Salazar announced additional drilling results at the El Domo underground deposit, reporting 14 metres at 4.44% copper equivalent. The update is a positive exploration/resource signal for the project and can provide modest support to expectations for copper supply, though likely with limited immediate price impact.

title: Automotive Aluminum Market is expected to display a steady growth of 9% due to the incorporation of green aluminum
summary: A UnivDatos report projects the automotive aluminum market to grow about 9% CAGR from 2022–2028, citing increased vehicle production, lightweighting, and adoption of “green aluminum.” It describes aluminum’s automotive use in body and powertrain components but provides no near-term supply, trade, or price catalyst for metal markets.

title: Access World and the non-nickel stones | Hotter Commodities
summary: Access World, once owned by Glencore, allegedly shipped over $1.2 million of fake nickel from Rotterdam, with LME warrants totaling 54 tonnes equivalent discovered as non-deliverable under contract specifications. The small quantity (0.14% of live stock) still raises nickel-industry fraud and liquidity concerns, likely pressuring nickel sentiment.

title: Economic Worries Weigh On Nickel Prices
summary: The article says nickel prices have fallen significantly from February to March and remain range-bound, with lower lows needed to confirm a downtrend. It notes South Africa’s load shedding threatens ferrochrome supply for stainless steel, but overall direction for nickel is unclear, with potential for stabilization.

title: Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe Launches Initiative Opposing Multi-Billion Dollar Nickel Mine
summary: The Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe launched an initiative opposing a multi-billion-dollar nickel mine. By challenging the project, the action raises the risk of delays, permitting hurdles, or reduced near-term supply prospects for nickel, which may support prices. However, timing and project outcome remain uncertain.

title: Financial Conduct Authority Updates its Statement on the London Metal Exchange's Suspension of the Nickel Market | Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft LLP
summary: The FCA confirmed it has opened an enforcement investigation into the LME’s decision to suspend the nickel market after disorderly conditions in March 2022, when nickel prices spiked sharply following the Russia-Ukraine invasion. The probe targets LME conduct, systems, and controls, with implications for nickel market governance.

title: Nevada Copper Files Financial Statements, MD&A and AIF for
summary: Nevada Copper filed audited financials and provided an update on Pumpkin Hollow’s underground mine restart. It says vent shaft stripping, ore-handling excavation, and development toward higher-grade stoping are underway and it expects to ramp to nameplate milling capacity by end-2023, with mill restart in late Q3 2023.

summary: Copper held a tight range but posted small gains as falling inventories and improving demand outweighed macro worries. title: Copper climbs on lower supply; LME nickel resumes Asian hours trading - Stock market news
summary: Reuters reports LME/SHFE copper trading slightly higher on lower inventories and improving demand sentiment despite macro concerns. summary: SMM reports that despite volatility in spot coal, long-term contract coal prices at thermal power plants are mostly stable. summary: SMM reports that while macro sentiment is stabilising, aluminium markets expect near-term support from robust destocking. Despite rising domestic supply and imported ingot inflows, downstream demand is in peak season and social aluminium inventories have declined sharply. This should help aluminium prices this week, though longer-term supply pressure and weaker costs may cap gains.

summary: The International Aluminium Institute launched “Aluminium Forward 2030,” a coalition of primary producers and downstream companies aiming to decarbonise and improve circularity across end-use sectors. title: Majuba Hill Copper to Acquire Copper King and Desert Mountain Claims and Leases Including the Historical Cayote Mine SW of Tintic Mining District
summary: Majuba Hill Copper Corp. announced it will acquire the Copper King and Desert Mountain claims near Utah’s Tintic Mining District, adding prospective greenfield copper targets and the small Coyote Mine. title: Copper climbs on lower supply; LME nickel resumes Asian hours trading
summary: Copper traded in a tight range but was slightly higher, supported by falling inventories, improving demand, and expectations around a possible pause in U.S. rate hikes. title: Copper climbs on lower supply; LME nickel resumes Asian hours trading
summary: Copper prices were steady to slightly higher on Monday, supported by falling inventories, improving demand, and a potential pause in U.S. interest-rate hikes. summary: SMM reports that alumina prices in North China face downside risk as perceived supply increases and South China shipments are expected to fill a persistent local supply deficit. summary: SMM says Guizhou and Sichuan smelters continued resuming production, lifting China aluminium operating capacity to 40.2m mt. Ingot inventories fell and processing orders improved.

title: LS constructs nickel sulfate plant in Asan to bolster EV battery materials output
summary: LS Group completed construction of a nickel sulfate plant in Asan, operated via affiliate Toricom, producing 5,000 tons for EV batteries. The company plans to expand nickel sulfate capacity to 270,000 tons by 2030 using additional feedstocks, supporting LS MnM’s battery materials value chain and potential nickel demand.

summary: Copper prices are edging lower as investors weigh easing worries about banking troubles against expectations of a credit squeeze that could curb lending, growth, and metals demand. summary: Palladium One Mining reports discovery of the “Ember Zone,” a new high-grade nickel–copper mineralized zone at its Tyko project in Ontario, adjacent to interpreted feeder dyke/chonolith structures. title: Gaoneng Xinke Yielded First Batch of Copper Cathode as Scheduled_SMM
summary: Jiangxi Xinke began output from its polymetallic resources recycling project and produced over 99.95% copper cathode on March 29. The company says the full 310,000 mt/year production capacity is now in operation, alongside additional hazardous waste recycling capacity beyond 1 million mt/year.

title: Ample Copper Scrap Supply Emerged Last Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Copper scrap supply rose last week as sellers shipped more actively. Downstream demand weakened from copper semi producers, and rod plants could run 5–6 days on inventories that increased ~300 mt. With real-estate consumption slow, orders lagged, potentially reducing high-grade scrap demand and shipments, capping copper price gains.

title: Copper slips on firm dollar, slower China factory activity growth - Stock market news
summary: Copper prices fell Monday as a firmer U.S. dollar—supported by renewed inflation worries and potential Fed rate hikes—curbed buying demand. Weaker China manufacturing activity, with the Caixin PMI slipping to 50.0, also weighed on sentiment. Refined copper premiums rose ahead of a holiday, but overall pressure prevailed.

title: Meridian Announces Filing of its PEA Technical Report for Cabaçal Gold-Copper Project, Brazil
summary: Meridian announced it has filed the PEA technical report for its Cabaçal gold-copper project in Brazil. While the resource update could influence longer-term copper supply expectations, a PEA filing typically does not change near-term production or inventories, suggesting only limited immediate effects on copper prices.

title: Dollar, weak China industrial activity pressure copper
summary: Copper prices eased on a stronger dollar after higher oil prices revived inflation and potential U.S. rate-hike fears. China’s Caixin/S&P manufacturing PMI fell to 50.0, suggesting demand slowdown. LME warehouse stocks declined, offering some support, but copper still traded lower. Aluminium rose on electricity-cost worries.

title: Surge Battery Metals Inc.: Surge Battery Metals Announces the Acquisition of the Remaining 20% Interest in the Surge Nickel Project BC
summary: Surge Battery Metals announced it can acquire the remaining 20% interest to reach 100% ownership of its HN4 and N100 mineral claims in central BC, a nickel/iron alloy (awaruite) project. The company also closed a private placement. The update is modestly supportive for nickel sentiment, not immediate supply.

title: Osisko Metals Reports Additional Drill Results at Mount Copper  Including 300.0 Metres Grading 0.55% Copper and 3.59 g/t Silver
summary: Osisko Metals announced final drill results from its 2022 program at the Gaspé Copper Project’s Mount Copper open pit. Multiple holes intersected hundreds of metres of copper mineralization (e.g., 300m at 0.55% Cu), supporting potential in-pit resource expansion ahead of a June drilling resumption.

title: Surge Battery Metals Announces the Acquisition of the Remaining 20% Interest in the Surge Nickel Project BC
summary: Surge Battery Metals announced it can acquire the remaining 20% interest in the HN4 and N100 mineral claims of its Surge Nickel Project in British Columbia, paying consideration in shares and consolidating to 100% ownership. The project targets nickel-iron alloy (awaruite), but remains exploration-focused with no immediate supply change.

title: Glencore Eyes $1 Billion Gain on Teck Copper Combo in Chile
summary: BNN Bloomberg’s item says Glencore is looking to secure about $1 billion in gains via a “Teck copper combo” in Chile. Such a copper-focused transaction can affect near-term expectations for copper output and financing, supporting sentiment toward copper prices even without detailed operational figures in the excerpt.

title: Redx confirms Jounce deal lapses, Tirupati seals deal
summary: The article rounds up company updates including Kefi Gold and Copper’s maiden resource estimate at Al Godeyer with copper grades and planned drilling, and Great Southern Copper’s discovery of mineralised structures at Victoria with assays up to 6.9% copper. These exploration updates may modestly support copper sentiment but are not near-term supply shocks.

title: New federal budget good for Sudbury-Nickel Belt, Serre says
summary: A federal budget targeted inflation relief and clean-economy investments. The Nickel Belt Liberal MP, Marc Serré, said the budget’s clean technology and critical-minerals incentives (including investment tax credits and strategic-fund support) will benefit mining projects in the Sudbury-Nickel Belt region, improving expectations for nickel supply.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.10% Lower at $4.0595 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper’s front-month contract settled 1.10% lower at $4.0595 per pound, down 4.50 cents. The session marked consecutive weakness with the metal declining two of the past three sessions and reaching the lowest settlement since March 21, signaling bearish short-term momentum.

title: Glencore launches $22bn copper raid as battle for battery resources explodes
summary: Glencore reportedly plans a $22bn move targeting battery-related resources, described as a major “copper raid.” The deal narrative is linked to copper supply and strategic investment, which can tighten perceived near-term availability and lift copper price expectations over the next few weeks.

title: Workers Struggles: The Americas
summary: Jamaica’s Industrial Disputes Tribunal issued a no-strike order for over 600 workers at UC Rusal Alumina Jamaica, requiring normal operations while the dispute is heard. The stoppage had been planned over wages and benefits after failed talks, lowering immediate risk to aluminum supply.

title: SMM Overview of Recent Copper Ore Supply and Demand in Overseas Markets_SMM
summary: SMM says overseas production was stable with no major negative shocks, but supply risks are building. Antofagasta’s Los Pelambres desalination project is postponed again. Lundin signed a stake purchase agreement for Lumina Copper Chile. Codelco plans to close Ventanas’ last refining link in May-June, and Kansanshi smelter struggles delivering blister copper.

title: China Copper Anode Imports from Italy Sky-Rocket in February after A Slump in January_SMM
summary: SMM data show China’s copper anode imports from Italy fell to 500 mt in January but then surged 299.47% month-on-month to 1,900 mt in February. The turnaround suggests renewed demand for refining inputs in the near term, potentially providing support for copper prices.

title: China Copper Concentrate Imports from US and Canada Soared in February_SMM
summary: SMM reports that China’s copper concentrate imports surged in February, with shipments from the US rising 192.5% MoM to 85,300 mt, and imports from Canada increasing 91.0% MoM to 18,600 mt. Larger concentrate inflows can bolster smelter supply expectations, tending to support copper.

title: China Copper Anode Imports from Asia by Country in January and February  _SMM
summary: SMM reports that China’s copper anode imports from Asia rose. In January, imports from South Korea increased to 3,100 mt, and from Thailand to 1,600 mt. In February, imports from South Korea rose further to 3,700 mt on a month-on-month basis, indicating stronger anode supply inflows.

title: Several Factors Point to Sharp Rise in Spot Copper Concentrate TCs_SMM
summary: SMM reports several drivers that point to a sharp rise in spot copper concentrate treatment charges (TCs): smelter maintenance starting in late March, better production and shipments from overseas mines, guidance TCs adjustments, and new mine commissioning in Chile. The combined supply and smelting-input outlook is expected to lift spot concentrate TCs.

title: China Copper Anode Imports from Africa by Country in February_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports February China imported 33,000 mt of copper anode from Zambia, down sharply on the month and year. Imports from Chile rose 42.8% MoM and 20.3% YoY, while flows from the DRC were roughly flat MoM. These shifts alter expected anode supply for Chinese smelters.

title: MAX Resource Corp.: Max Resource Evaluates 6 Priority Targets on its CESAR Copper-Silver Project, NE Colombia
summary: Max Resource provided an exploration update for its CESAR copper-silver project in northeast Colombia, including sampling, new target identification, and drilling/metallurgical test results. The release confirms stratiform and structurally controlled copper-silver mineralization and starts geophysical orientation work. No production or shipment impacts are announced.

title: Copper wire thieves moving west, Roma police suspect | Queensland Country Life
summary: Queensland police and Ergon Energy report a statewide rise in copper wire theft from overhead and underground electricity networks, with incidents increasing from 119 in 2020 to 338 in 2022 and 51 so far this year. Copper is stolen by damaging infrastructure, causing outages and fires.

title: Taseko Mines : NI 43-101 TECHNICAL REPORT FLORENCE COPPER PROJECT - Form 6-K
summary: Taseko filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Florence Copper ISCR/SX-EW project in Arizona. The report updates life-of-mine plan, reserves, and economics, projecting ~85 million pounds per year of LME Grade A copper cathode. Production is based on conservative long-term copper price assumptions; permitting remains in progress.

title: Explainer: Glencore's vision to be "biggest, best" copper producer through bid for Teck
summary: Glencore proposed acquiring Teck to form MetalCo, targeting a large “tier-1” copper asset portfolio and significant copper output growth, while separating coal assets. Teck rejected the offer, and Glencore’s strategy is tied to accelerating copper supply. The news primarily influences copper sentiment, with only indirect relevance to nickel.

title: Alcoa Expands its EcoSource™ Low-Carbon Alumina Brand to Include Non-metallurgical Grade Alumina
summary: Alcoa announced it is expanding its EcoSource™ low-carbon alumina brand from smelter-grade applications to include non-metallurgical alumina grades such as hydrates and calcined materials. The company says EcoSource is sourced from its refining system with low CO2e intensity, aiming to attract more customers and reduce emissions.

title: TSLOTS Aluminum Framing System to Expand Operations into Southeastern U.S.
summary: Bonnell Aluminum (Tredegar subsidiary) plans to expand TSLOTS aluminum structural framing operations by adding a new manufacturing and distribution facility in Newnan, Georgia, to better serve the U.S. Southeast. The project aims to improve access, reduce shipping costs, and shorten lead times, implying higher aluminum processing demand.

title: 'Mighty Quest: Rogue Palace' Releases Next Month, 40 More Netflix Games Titles Slated for This Year – TouchArcade
summary: Bonnell Aluminum, a Tredegar subsidiary, plans to expand TSLOTS aluminum structural framing operations by adding a new manufacturing and distribution facility in Newnan, Georgia. The move is intended to increase market access, reduce shipping costs, and shorten lead times, following prior investments in the Midwest.

title: Sandvik to supply automation solutions for Chilean copper mine
summary: Sandvik was selected to supply automation solutions to Codelco’s El Teniente underground copper mine in Chile, including autonomous loaders and AutoMine Fleet traffic control, with deliveries starting this year. The multi-year contract aims to digitise and automate operations, but the article does not cite immediate output changes.

title: Two nickel IPOs this month point to downstream industry potential
summary: Indonesia’s nickel sector is highlighted through two major planned IPOs by nickel mining/processing and EV-battery materials firms. Analysts link the fundraising to scaling opportunities in the nickel supply chain, supported by expected EV adoption and incentives. The news is sentiment-positive for nickel, with no immediate supply disruption cited.

title: Blackwolf Copper and Gold Ltd: Blackwolf Announces Closing of C$8.5 Million Private Placement
summary: Blackwolf Copper and Gold closed an C$8.5m private placement, using proceeds partly to advance its Niblack copper-gold-zinc-silver VMS project and for exploration and working capital. The release is mainly a securities-financing update with no immediate mine output or supply change indicated for copper.

title: Teck (TECK) Produces First Copper at QB2, Rejects Glencore Offer
summary: Teck said it produced its first copper at the QB2 project. The article also notes Teck rejected a Glencore offer. The key price-relevant element is the project’s early output milestone, which can slightly increase near-term expectations for copper supply and pressure prices.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.87% Lower at $3.9835 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for April delivery settled 1.87% lower at $3.9835 per pound, down 7.60 cents. The move marked the largest one-day dollar and percentage decline since mid-March, and copper has fallen for two consecutive sessions, with the lowest settlement since March 20, 2023.

title: Copper held down by global growth worries
summary: Copper prices struggled to hold gains as investors worried that OPEC+’s surprise output target cut could reignite inflation, while global growth remains weak. Analysts cited strong mine supply and easing Chinese demand, alongside credit concerns in the U.S. and Europe. Aluminium and nickel also slipped modestly.

title: Chile copper production down 3.4% in February- Cochilco
summary: Chile’s copper production fell 3.4% in February to 381,000 tonnes, according to Cochilco. Codelco output dropped 14.8% year-on-year to 105,400 tonnes, while Escondida rose 4% and Collahuasi fell 6%. The decline highlights softer near-term supply from a key exporter.

title: Canada Nickel Continues Rapid Progression of Crawford Nickel Project Federal Permitting
summary: Canada Nickel reports continued rapid progress in the federal permitting process for its Crawford nickel project, including advancement through the impact assessment and submission-related phases. The development could shape future nickel supply expectations, but the news does not indicate near-term production changes, limiting immediate spot price effects.

title: Meridian, Tiwai Point sign deal to allow aluminium smelter electricity demand flexibility
summary: Meridian and NZ Aluminium Smelters agreed to give the Tiwai Point smelter flexibility to reduce electricity demand when the New Zealand grid is under stress. As the smelter uses about 12% of current generation, such demand curtailment implies potential production adjustments that could pressure aluminium prices.

title: Copper Shortage Scare Is 'Clickbait' But More U.S. Mining Would Be Better For The Environment, Say Mining Experts
summary: Reports of a looming copper shortage are linked to supply problems: Peru mine blockades from political unrest and Chile posting its lowest output in six years. Demand is also rising for electrification and renewables. Experts argue shortages may spur more investment, but the immediate supply news is supportive for copper prices.

title: Analysis: Inalum to focus on aluminum smelting after MIND ID spin-off
summary: Indonesia’s Inalum has been separated from the MIND ID holding structure and is now focused on aluminium smelting and developing the national aluminium industry. The split follows government regulations transferring controlling shares. While it strengthens governance and planning, the article does not cite near-term changes to aluminium output or supply.

title: Copper inches higher in thin trade; China closed for holiday - Stock market news
summary: Copper prices fell toward a one-week low on weak U.S. economic data and worries about demand, but a further drop looked limited due to thin liquidity from China’s Qingming holiday (SHFE closed). Analysts cited a potentially stronger demand/d tighter supply outlook, while LME aluminium and nickel were also slightly lower.

title: New Zealand Aluminium Smelter and Meridian strike power demand deal, subject to approval
summary: New Zealand Aluminium Smelter (NZAS) and Meridian agreed to a demand-response deal allowing Meridian to request up to 50 MW reductions during grid stress or hydro shortages, with Meridian paying fees per reduction. The agreement is subject to Electricity Authority approval and aims to maintain reliable smelter power supply through next winter.

title: ArcPacific Resources Corp.: ArcPacific Acquires TL Nickel North Property
summary: ArcPacific Resources announced it will acquire the TL Nickel North property, adding 96 mineral claims in Labrador with reported elevated nickel values and EM anomalies. The release cites historical nearby drilling showing nickel and some copper grades, but no production or near-term supply changes. It remains subject to exchange approval.

title: Mincor-Wyloo Metals takeover: BHP's secret nickel clause provides termination rights
summary: Mincor confirmed its nickel supply contract with BHP contains a “change of control” clause allowing BHP to terminate the deal under certain takeover-related circumstances, potentially triggering default on Mincor’s debt. The disclosure followed a $760 million bid by Wyloo Metals, raising nickel supply uncertainty.

title: Vedanta records 5,74,000 tonnes of aluminium production in Q4FY23
summary: Vedanta said its aluminium production in Q4FY23 rose to 574,000 tonnes, slightly above the prior year. However, alumina output at its Lanjigarh refinery fell 7% QoQ and 18% YoY due to a planned calciner shutdown. The update is specific to aluminium production levels.

title: Foreign investors eye nickel industry in Indonesia | World
summary: Reuters reports growing foreign and corporate interest in Indonesia’s nickel sector as EV-battery demand rises. Ford plans a $4.5 billion nickel-processing alliance, and Merdeka Battery will build two processing facilities totaling 240,000 tonnes annually, funded via an IPO and with Tsingshan involvement. These moves bolster nickel supply expectations and sentiment.

title: McEwen Copper: Los Azules – New Assay Results
summary: McEwen Copper reported new drill assay results from Los Azules, Argentina, highlighting thick “enriched/supergene” copper intervals such as 0.92% Cu over 276 m and 1.00% Cu over 282 m. Management says drilling is progressing toward planned meters and aims to support resource upgrades and feasibility work.

title: Copper prices down with global growth concerns - Stock market news
summary: Copper prices rose on LME support from falling inventories, lower cancelled warrants, and drawdown dynamics, despite worries over weaker U.S. and China manufacturing and a stronger dollar. It also cites reduced global smelting activity and lower Chile production. Aluminium was reported lower during the session, and macro sentiment weighed broadly.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Appointment of Project Debt Advisor, Provides Corporate Update
summary: Canada Nickel appointed project debt advisors to help assemble a financing package for its Crawford nickel sulphide project as it advances toward production. It also updates board leadership and discusses carbon-credit related ambitions. The release is tied to future nickel development, which can modestly support nickel sentiment.

title: Fabled Copper Corp.: Fabled Copper Reports Multi +10% Copper Values Including 29.30% Copper on West Side of the Eagle Creek Copper Occurrence
summary: Fabled Copper Corp. released 2022 surface fieldwork results from the Muskwa Project’s Eagle Creek copper occurrence on the west side. Out of 12 float samples, most assayed above 0.5% copper, with several very high-grade results (up to 29.30% copper). This is an exploration assay update, not production guidance.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Reports Q1 2023 Production of 93,603 Tonnes of Copper from Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said its Kamoa-Kakula complex produced 93,603 tonnes of copper in concentrate in Q1 2023, with record March output after Phase 1 and 2 debottlenecking. The company cites improved recoveries and maintains 2023 guidance of 390,000–430,000 tonnes.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Reports Q1 2023 Production of 93,603 Tonnes of Copper from Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reports Kamoa-Kakula produced 93,603 tonnes of copper in concentrate in Q1 2023, including March records for daily, weekly, and monthly output and improving recovery rates. The debottlenecking program raised processing capacity and supports ongoing production guidance for copper.

title: Diamonds, gold, uranium, copper still rock exports
summary: Namibia’s mineral exports still dominate the economy, but copper exports slowed to about N$707 million in February versus over N$1.4 billion a year earlier. The overall trade deficit widened and exports were mainly destined for regional and international markets. The copper decline suggests weaker near-term copper export flows.

title: Copper prices turn to growth amid support from lower inventories
summary: Copper prices in London rose 0.5% to around $8,790/tonne as LME inventories continued to decline, with warehouse stocks down almost 15% over two weeks and on-warrant stocks at the lowest since late 2021. Despite weak U.S. and China manufacturing signals, supply disruptions and inventory drawdowns are supporting downside protection.

title: Hudbay's Copper World Project Receives Positive Permitting Update
summary: Hudbay said the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers formally accepted and revoked the surrendered Section 404 Clean Water Act permit for the former Rosemont project and reaffirmed jurisdictional determinations that no U.S. waters exist on the site. The company is progressing Arizona state permits and site work for the Copper World copper project.

title: Freeport CEO Sees More Copper Deals After Glencore's Teck Bid
summary: The piece highlights that Freeport’s CEO expects more copper-focused deals after Glencore’s bid for Teck. Such signals can lift near-term sentiment on copper as investors anticipate transaction-led supply and production expectations shifting. The immediate effect is sentiment-driven rather than a confirmed physical supply change.

title: Mining Stock News - ArcPacific (TSXV: ACP) Acquires TL Nickel North Property
summary: ArcPacific Resources acquired the TL Nickel North property (claims with elevated nickel values and EM anomalies) near Newfoundland/Labrador’s Voisey’s Bay nickel region. The company plans further evaluation with the anticipated field exploration program. The deal is subject to TSX-V approval and includes an NSR, but no near-term production changes are described.

title: McEwen Mining: McEwen Copper: Los Azules - New Assay Results
summary: McEwen Copper reported new Los Azules drilling assay results, including multiple long intercepts of enriched-zone copper grading roughly 0.5%–1.4% Cu over hundreds of meters, and said drilling density is being increased for future resource upgrades and a feasibility study. The news supports the project’s potential but not near-term output.

title: Colossus Resources Signs Letter of Intent with Austral Gold Limited to Acquire the Calvario and Mirador Copper Porphyry Projects in Chile
summary: Colossus Resources signed a letter of intent to acquire Austral Gold’s Calvario and Mirador copper porphyry projects in Chile. The news may support sentiment about future copper supply pipelines, but it does not indicate immediate production changes, outages, or inventory shifts, so near-term price impact is likely small.

title: Ero Copper Demonstrates Significant Near-Term Growth in Updated 5-Year Outlook
summary: Ero Copper Corp. released an updated five-year outlook showing a major planned increase in consolidated copper production, with 2025 output expected to rise to 100,000–110,000 tonnes. The company attributes gains to higher mined and processed grades from infill drilling and stockpile optimization at Tucumã and improved grades at Caraíba.

title: Chile Copper Output Falls in February, Dragged Down by State-Owned Giant Codelco_SMM
summary: Chile’s February copper output fell 3.4% year-on-year to 381,000 mt, driven by a 14.8% decline at state-owned Codelco to 105,400 mt, according to the Chilean Copper Commission. The production drop from a key supplier can tighten short-term supply expectations.

title: Chile Central Bank Raised Copper Price Forecast for 2023 _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Chile’s central bank lifted its copper price forecast for 2023, projecting an average of $3.85 per pound versus the prior $3.55. The update implies stronger expectations for copper demand/supply conditions and can bolster investor sentiment toward copper prices in the near term.

title: Copper climbs on tightening inventory, but recession fears cap gains - Stock market news
summary: Copper prices rose as LME warrant stocks fell to the lowest since 2021, supporting the market, and China demand/price premiums offered additional support. However, the rally was capped by global recession fears and macro concerns tied to U.S. jobs data, with aluminium up and nickel down.

title: SMM A00 Aluminium Prices Rise on Apr 6, 2023_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports the daily changes of Shanghai A00 aluminium prices for Apr 6, 2023. The quoted range is 18,590–18,630 yuan per metric tonne, up 20 yuan/mt on the day. The note indicates SMM’s data are for reference and not trading recommendations.

title: Low Inventory to Limit Downside Trend of Copper prices_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM notes that concerns about economic development domestically and overseas are pressuring sentiment, but current low copper inventories are expected to limit further downside in copper prices. The balance between macro worries and inventory support suggests near-term price resilience rather than a clear selloff.

title: Arizona Metals Corp. Announces Step-Out Exploration Drilling Intersects A Potential New Zone of Copper-Gold-Zinc VMS Mineralization
summary: Arizona Metals announced step-out and extensional drilling at the Kay Mine Project intersected potential new VMS mineralization, including intervals grading up to 0.5% CuEq and 4.8% CuEq in defined extensions. The company is fully funded for further drilling and plans to test additional target extensions, implying incremental copper upside.

title: Copper bounces on optimism over China and technical buying - Stock market news
summary: Reuters reports copper rose 0.3% on LME as optimism grew for improving China demand, supported by a stronger Caixin/S&P composite PMI showing the fastest expansion since June and improved consumption in power, construction and air conditioning. Recession fears from recent U.S. data limited gains. Technical buying also helped after lows.

title: Govt may let Freeport export copper beyond deadline
summary: Indonesia’s government is considering allowing PT Freeport Indonesia to keep exporting copper concentrate after a June export ban deadline. The Mining Law would end such shipments on July 1 unless smelting/refining capacity is ready. A quota of 2.3 million tonnes and smelter progress are cited as conditions.

title: Copper Fox Provides Update on the Van Dyke Copper | The Kingston Whig Standard
summary: Copper Fox updated progress on its 100% owned Van Dyke in-situ copper recovery project in Arizona. The company is rehabilitating historical drill holes and conducting hydrogeologic, mineralogical solubility, and geotechnical UCS testing ahead of future monitoring and underground access planning. No near-term output changes are indicated.

title: Teck and Agnico Eagle Announce Completion of the San Nicolás Copper-Zinc Project Joint Venture
summary: Teck and Agnico Eagle say the San Nicolás copper-zinc joint venture closed, with Agnico Eagle funding a 50% interest for US$580 million via study and development costs. The partners plan to submit an environmental impact assessment and permit application and complete feasibility studies in early 2024, supporting copper project timelines.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 1.91% Lower at $4.0260 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for April delivery ended the week down 1.91% at $4.0260 per pound, snapping a two-week winning streak and marking the largest one-week decline since mid-March. The metal later rose for two consecutive sessions, up 0.70% on the day and 1.07% over two days.

title: Copper Thieves Target Iconic Windmills Near Palm Springs
summary: Copper thieves are damaging windmills near Palm Springs, stripping copper wiring to obtain small amounts of scrap. The founder of WinTec Energy said a $30,000 windmill can be destroyed to retrieve about $500 worth of copper, highlighting losses tied to high copper prices but not broader market supply impacts.

title: Copper rises on softer dollar, but set for weekly loss amid demand worries - Stock market news
summary: Shanghai copper rose 0.2% on a softer dollar ahead of U.S. non-farm payrolls, but was set for a weekly loss due to weak economic data and recession demand fears. Tight Chinese inventories and improved demand provided support. SHFE aluminium and nickel also gained in the session.

title: Copper rises on softer dollar, but set for weekly loss amid demand worries
summary: Shanghai copper rose on Friday with a weaker dollar ahead of US non-farm payrolls, but the metal is on track for a weekly loss. Weak US economic data have intensified recession and demand concerns, despite tight inventories and improved Chinese consumption providing some support.

title: Mallee Resources to study potential Avebury Nickel Mine expansion | The Advocate
summary: Mallee Resources plans a study for potentially expanding the Avebury nickel mine near Zeehan, with limited prior exploration and a gravity survey to find additional high-grade nickel and copper sources. Management frames the project as battery-grade, low-emissions supply and cites strong nickel demand from EV and battery manufacturing plans.

title: Copper Cathode Price Advanced on Apr 7_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that #1 copper cathode prices rose on April 7. The range increased by 30 yuan/mt to 68,800–68,940 yuan/mt, with an average of 68,870 yuan/mt. The note is a spot pricing update reflecting day-of-day bullish movement in copper cathode.

title: Shanghai copper rises on softer dollar, but set for weekly loss amid demand worries - Stock market news
summary: Shanghai copper rose slightly on a softer dollar ahead of U.S. non-farm payrolls, but remains on course for a weekly decline as weak economic data revive recession and demand concerns. The LME is closed for Good Friday. SHFE aluminium gained and nickel rose on the day, indicating mixed sentiment across metals.

title: Shanghai copper set for weekly losses amid economic headwinds - Stock market news
summary: Shanghai copper edged up but was set for a slight weekly loss as macro economic headwinds, including weak US data and upcoming non-farm payrolls, weighed sentiment. SHFE copper stocks fell more slowly, while tighter inventories and steadier Chinese demand supported. LME copper declined weekly; aluminium rose modestly and nickel stocks plunged sharply.

title: SMM Daily Comments (Apr 7): Most SHFE Base Metals Gained Ground with Nickel Surging over 3%, Silver Refreshed New High_SMM
summary: SMM notes mild US dollar movement but reports SHFE base metal prices rising overall. Nickel surged 3.39%, copper gained over 0.6%, and aluminium advanced 0.51% during the session. Zinc was marginally higher, while tin fell. The broader tone is bullish for industrial metals.

title: Teck, Agnico Eagle close JV for San Nicolás copper project in Mexico
summary: Teck and Agnico Eagle closed their JV for Mexico’s San Nicolás copper project, with Agnico taking a 50% governance stake in the holding subsidiary. They plan permitting/impact assessment soon, feasibility in early 2024, and production in 2026. Initial output is expected at 63,000 tpa copper.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Down This week but will Grow Next Week_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s major copper inventories fell early this week but are still above last year in several regions. As prices declined, downstream buying briefly strengthened inventories’ drop. Looking ahead, smelters are expected to step up warehouse shipments while next week’s consumption may lag, pushing inventories higher.

title: Copper Inventories in Shanghai and Guangdong Bonded Zones to Decline Further_SMM
summary: SMM expects copper inventories in Shanghai and Guangdong bonded zones to keep falling next week, though at a slower pace. After traders sold and locked in profits, shipments from bonded stocks rose, but seaborne shipments should slow due to import losses and weak domestic spot quotes, while bill-of-lading arrivals grow.

title: Copper Inventory in China Bonded Zone Fell This Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s bonded-zone copper inventories fell by 9,500 mt to 163,100 mt in the week to April 7. Guangdong rose while Shanghai declined. Traders shipped from bonded stocks after the import window opened, but import losses and weak domestic quotes may slow shipments, with inventories likely to keep edging lower.

title: Hot Topics in International Trade - April 2023 - Recent U.S. Actions Affecting Imports of Aluminum Products and More from Russia | Braumiller Law Group, PLLC
summary: The U.S. issued new Presidential Proclamations increasing duties on imports of Russian-origin and Russia-smelted/cast aluminum articles, including extending a 200% ad valorem tariff to aluminum products regardless of origin if any primary aluminum was smelted or cast in Russia. Additional Russian product tariffs raise Column 2 rates, increasing landed costs.

title: Austral intends to divest copper projects in Chile to Colossus
summary: Austral Gold signed a LOI to sell its non-core copper exploration projects in northern Chile to Colossus Resources. Austral receives $100,000 upfront for an option and will earn equity in Colossus while Colossus funds exploration over two years subject to pre-feasibility studies. Likely limited near-term market impact.

title: On National Beer Day, New Data Show Tariffs on Aluminum
summary: The Beer Institute, citing new research, says Section 232 aluminum tariffs have cost the U.S. beverage industry $1.893 billion over five years as producers face higher aluminum prices through mills and smelters. The group urges lifting the tariffs, warning higher input costs feed into consumer prices.

title: On National Beer Day, New Data Show Tariffs on Aluminum Have Cost the U.S. Beverage Industry Nearly $1.9 Billion
summary: New data cited by the Beer Institute say five years of U.S. Section 232 aluminum tariffs have cost the beverage industry nearly $1.893 billion, with most tariff burden paid via upstream aluminum pricing. The report suggests tariffs raise consumer and producer costs across the supply chain, potentially damping aluminum end-demand.

title: Native Americans call copper mine plan 'environmental catastrophe'
summary: Native American groups and tribal leaders are challenging plans to move forward with environmental review and a land swap that would allow Resolution Copper’s Oak Flat mine in Arizona. Officials may publish the final environmental impact study soon, accelerating approvals, which implies greater copper supply potential and likely bearish price pressure.

title: Government may let Freeport export copper beyond deadline
summary: Indonesia’s government is considering letting PT Freeport Indonesia continue exporting copper concentrate despite a copper export ban scheduled to start after June/July 1. Continuation would depend on progress toward its smelter readiness. Officials cite large lost revenue if exports stop, while delays place 51.7% smelter progress in focus.

title: Shanghai copper edges higher; stronger dollar limits gains - Stock market news
summary: Shanghai copper prices rose marginally as improved Chinese demand expectations supported the market, but gains were limited by a stronger U.S. dollar after robust U.S. jobs data. SHFE aluminium edged higher and nickel was nearly unchanged, reflecting modest, mostly offsetting near-term forces.

title: Codelco's Copper Output to be Largely Steady in 2023_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Codelco CEO Andre Sougarret said the firm expects copper production to be roughly flat in 2023 at about 1.35–1.45 million mt versus 1.446 million mt in 2022. Pre-tax profit fell and direct costs rose, but no clear immediate production cut was signaled.

title: Chile's Copper Output in February Dropped, Codelco Output Down 14.8%_SMM
summary: Chile’s regulator Cochilco reported that Codelco’s February copper output fell 14.8% to 105,400 mt. Chile’s total copper output also declined 3.4% year-on-year to 381,000 mt and dropped 12% month-on-month, the lowest since early 2017, suggesting tighter near-term supply.

title: Alumina Offers FOB Western Australia (Apr 10, 2023)_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that daily alumina offers FOB Western Australia are unchanged at $358/mt on Apr 10, 2023. Because alumina is the main input for aluminium production, the lack of change suggests no new near-term signal for aluminium costs or price direction.

title: Price Spread between Copper Cathode and Copper Scrap Remained High_SMM
summary: SMM reports that consumption of copper rod made from copper scrap is recovering slowly, weakening scrap demand. Scrap sellers therefore held back from raising prices, causing copper scrap prices to fall more than copper cathode prices and widening the cathode–scrap price spread slightly.

title: NORNICKEL Nickel Prices Hover at Highs on Apr 10_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports April 10 premiums for Jinchuan and Nornickel nickel: Jinchuan premiums were flat at an average 8,750 yuan/mt, while Nornickel premiums averaged 7,750 yuan/mt, down 250 yuan/mt.
