summary: SMM reports spot #1 copper cathode premiums versus SHFE contracts widened earlier and spot quotes rallied midweek on pre-Labour Day restocking. Copper futures fell but import losses shrank, boosting arrivals and adding about 1,500 mt to social warehouse inventories. After the holiday, downstream raw-material inventories will run low, supporting higher spot pricing.

title: Kutcho Copper Corp.: Kutcho Copper Announces Closing of $4,063,050 Million Financing
summary: Kutcho Copper Corp. closed a $4.06 million non-brokered private placement, issuing common and flow-through units to raise funds for exploration at its Kutcho copper-zinc property in British Columbia and for working capital. The release does not indicate production changes; it mainly supports future project development.

title: Nickel Exploration 2022
summary: Headlines indicate nickel-focused activity: FPX Nickel reports confirmatory geotechnical drilling results at the Baptiste nickel project, receives funding support from Natural Resources Canada, and Ontario accelerates the C$5 billion Crawford nickel project under a new framework. Separately, NiCo Resources is noted as rising amid surging nickel prices.

title: Stellantis, Australia's Alliance Nickel ink deal for battery elements supply | Companies
summary: Stellantis and Australia’s Alliance Nickel signed a binding offtake agreement for about 170,000 tons of nickel sulphate over an initial five-year period, plus a smaller cobalt sulphate quantity. Stellantis also buys new equity in Alliance Nickel, funding work on the NiWest project feasibility study.

title: More workplace casualties as two workers die in collapsed dump site at Indonesia nickel plant
summary: Indonesia officials said two workers died after a nickel waste dump site collapse at the Sulawesi Chinese-owned nickel smelting complex operated by PT IMIP. Workers operating dump trucks were engulfed by sludge-like material tied to ferronickel processing, indicating potential operational disruption and supply risk.

title: Another workplace disaster in Indonesia - Two killed as nickel waste disposal site collapses
summary: Indonesia’s Sulawesi nickel smelting complex saw another accident as a nickel waste disposal site collapsed, killing two workers operating dump trucks. Officials said the victims were engulfed by sludge-like material associated with ferronickel burning waste removal, indicating ongoing operational disruption at a major nickel facility.

title: Macro Headwinds and Poor Fundamentals to Expose Aluminium Prices to Downside Risk after the Labour Day Holiday_SMM
summary: SMM flags macro headwinds and potential post-holiday build in Chinese social aluminium inventory, warning of downside risk for aluminium next week. It points to weak downstream ordering and lower operating rates after Labour Day, while noting capacity additions and possible minor inventory accumulation.

title: Series Of Power Cuts Disrupt Aluminum Production In Yunnan
summary: Power cuts in China’s Yunnan—home to around 12% of national aluminum capacity—have forced electrolytic smelters to cut power usage amid low rainfall. As a result, aluminum production growth slows and some capacity is offline. Warehouse SHFE stocks fell, but analysts still warn supply constraints.

title: Largest Supply Glut In A Decade Crashes Nickel Prices
summary: Nickel prices have fallen sharply as Indonesia’s output continues to outpace global demand, creating the largest supply surplus in at least a decade (INSG: 239,000 tonnes). Despite some growth in EV demand, it is insufficient to absorb new production, intensifying bearish sentiment.

title: Stellantis' nickel, cobalt offtake deal puts Alliance Nickel shares in fast lane
summary: Stellantis is taking an 11.5% stake in Alliance Nickel and has agreed an offtake that could supply up to 170,000 tonnes of nickel sulphate from the NiWest project for five years. The deal covers about 40% of annual output, signaling secured EV battery demand and supporting nickel sentiment.

title: Reconnaissance Discovers New Zones of Porphyry Copper Mineralisation at the Cobrasco Project, Colombia
summary: Reconnaissance work at Colombia’s Cobrasco project reportedly identified new zones of porphyry copper mineralisation. Such findings can strengthen expectations for future copper resource growth and potential supply expansion, though the discovery likely has limited immediate effect on current production and inventories within the next few weeks.

title: Reconnaissance Discovers New Zones of Porphyry Copper
summary: Rugby Resources reports continued reconnaissance at the Cobrasco copper project in Colombia, finding strongly mineralised porphyry float ~2 km from drilling and extending the copper-molybdenum geochemical anomaly northward. Over 600 soil samples and additional rock chips were collected, supporting further drill testing plans; no production changes are mentioned.

title: Aston Bay : Intersects Copper Mineralization in First Drill Holes at Storm Copper Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay reports early RC drill holes at the Storm Copper Project in Nunavut all intersected thick copper sulfide intervals, with portable XRF indicating copper and MLEM identifying additional conductors. Assay results are pending and the work is aimed at defining maiden resources, not production.

title: Aston Bay Intersects Copper Mineralization In First Drill Holes At Storm Copper Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay says its first drill holes at the Storm Copper Project in Nunavut have intersected copper mineralization. The news is an early-stage exploration update, not yet affecting mined output or inventories, but it can support short-term sentiment around prospective copper supply.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.21% Higher at $3.9170 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for May delivery settled 1.21% higher at $3.9170, gaining 4.70 cents per pound. The contract rose for a fourth consecutive session and marked the highest settlement value since April 24, 2023, reflecting stronger momentum in copper prices on the day’s data-driven move.

title: Zeb Nickel Corp.: Zeb Nickel Issues Clarifying Press Release
summary: Zeb Nickel Corp. issued a clarifying press release after regulatory review, retracting prior references to a “current” preliminary economic estimate/resource for its Zebediela nickel project. It says there is no current mineral resource estimate and the historical estimate lacks NI 43-101 support, with planned 2023 drilling to update resources.

title: New World Resources releases enhanced scoping study evaluating 48% larger resource base at Antler copper deposit
summary: New World Resources released an updated scoping study for its Antler Arizona copper deposit, expanding the resource 48% and increasing planned concentrate output, including 190,300t of copper-in-concentrate over the initial period. It also improved project economics using assumed copper pricing, but no immediate supply shock is indicated.

title: IGO to farm-into Venus Metals' Henderson nickel and lithium project
summary: IGO agreed to farm into Venus Metals’ Henderson nickel-lithium project in Western Australia, funding exploration through a pre-feasibility study and potentially acquiring up to 70% of the tenements. The deal, including a $1m reimbursement, reinforces near-term development activity for nickel targets and could support sentiment.

title: Former work friends busted stealing copper from Bathurst business | Western Advocate
summary: Two men were caught stealing copper from a Bathurst business, cutting it with a hacksaw and attempting to remove scrap through a fence. Police estimated the stolen copper at about $5,300. The case led to community corrections orders, but the volume is too small for market-moving price effects.

title: ASCENDANT RESOURCES CONFIRMS SALEABLE GRADE CONCENTRATES ACHIEVED FOR COPPER, LEAD AND ZINC WITH STRONG RECOVERIES AND PRECIOUS METAL CREDITS AT ITS LAGOA SALGADA VMS PROJECT, PORTUGAL
summary: Ascendant Resources reported metallurgical optimization test results from the Lagoa Salgada VMS Project in Portugal, including saleable-grade copper concentrates with strong recoveries and precious-metal credits. The results will feed into the feasibility study for the Venda Nova deposit, targeted for completion in May 2023.

title: C3 Metals Receives Drill Permit for Main Ridge Copper-Gold Project in Jamaica
summary: C3 Metals said it received a drill permit for its Main Ridge copper-gold project in Jamaica. The approval advances exploration and potential development timelines, which can modestly improve expectations for future copper supply. However, no production is implied, so the near-term impact on copper prices is likely limited.

title: Copper touches one-week high, but Chinese factory data weighs
summary: Copper edged to a one-week high, driven by speculative short-term bullish signals after a prior drop, but gains were capped by China’s unexpectedly weak April factory data. Analysts also pointed to possible policy support (EV subsidies, infrastructure) and Fed rate-hike timing uncertainty, suggesting the rally may fail.

title: IGO signs farm-in deal for Venus' WA nickel-lithium project
summary: IGO will fund exploration for Venus’ Henderson project in WA under a farm-in/JV arrangement, with potential to acquire up to 70% after a pre-feasibility study. The project is nickel- and lithium-bearing, but remains at exploration stage, so near-term nickel price impact is likely limited.

title: 6K Additive and Cumberland Additive Announce Partnership and Sign Long Term Supply Agreement for Nickel 718
summary: 6K Additive and Siemens Energy signed a long-term supply agreement for Siemens to deliver spent nickel alloy powder (revert streams) to 6K Additive. 6K Additive will upcycle the material into additive-manufacturing-ready nickel alloy powders via its UniMelt microwave plasma system.

title: Alumobility Study Illustrates Why Last Mile Delivery Vehicle (LMDV) Fleets Should be Comprised of Aluminum-Intensive Vehicles
summary: A study by Alumobility promotes aluminum-intensive electric/battery-electric last-mile delivery vehicles as lighter, cheaper to operate, and lower-carbon than steel ICE options. It claims aluminum reduces vehicle mass and battery requirements and lowers cost per mile, aligning with US/EU sustainability initiatives. The message implies supportive incremental demand for aluminum.

title: Nicola Mining Prepares for 2023 Drilling Exploration at New Craigmont Copper Project
summary: Nicola Mining announced finalized planning for 2023 diamond drilling at its New Craigmont copper project near Merritt, BC, with drilling expected to start mid-May. The program targets untested extensions of skarn and porphyry-style copper zones adjacent to Teck’s Highland Valley Copper. No immediate production or supply changes are indicated.

title: Nicola Mining Inc.: Nicola Mining Prepares for 2023 Drilling Exploration at New Craigmont Copper Project
summary: Nicola Mining announced it has finalized 2023 exploration drilling plans for its New Craigmont copper project in British Columbia, including mid-May diamond drilling and geophysical/IP work to test untested extensions and porphyry targets. The release describes geology and prior results but does not indicate near-term production changes.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.76% Lower at $3.8480 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for May delivery settled 1.76% lower at $3.8480 per pound, losing 6.90 cents. The move snapped a four-session winning streak and marked the lowest settlement since April 25, highlighting near-term bearish momentum in copper futures.

title: The Power Play by The Market Herald Releases New Interviews with Strategic Resources, Rush Rare Metals, ARway Corp, SPC Nickel, Liberty Defense Holdings, Adamera Minerals and Candente Copper Discussing Their Latest News
summary: The Market Herald released interviews featuring multiple companies, including SPC Nickel reporting positive new assay results from its West Graham nickel-copper drilling in Sudbury and Candente Copper outlining 2023 plans for its Cañariaco copper project in Peru. These updates are supportive for near-term expectations around copper and nickel supply prospects.

title: The Power Play by The Market Herald Releases New Interviews with Strategic Resources, Rush Rare Metals, ARway Corp, SPC Nickel, Liberty Defense Holdings, Adamera Minerals and Candente Copper Discussing Their Latest News
summary: The Market Herald publishes interviews featuring multiple companies. Of note, SPC Nickel reports positive assay results from drilling at its West Graham Nickel and Copper project in Sudbury, supporting nickel and copper development sentiment. Candente Copper also outlines plans for its 100% owned Cañariaco Copper Project in Peru.

title: Codelco Sees Copper Production Slump at Aging Mines in Chile
summary: Codelco expects a copper production slump as its Chile mines age. The report points to declining output from older operations, raising concerns about near-term supply and production stability. title: Shanghai copper rebounds on low inventory
summary: Shanghai copper rose 0.8% after three weeks of declines, helped by low SHFE inventory levels despite weaker-than-expected China demand. Analysts cited smelter maintenance in May and possible demand improvement post-Labour Day, plus copper’s cheaper price. Aluminium and nickel also increased modestly.

title: Taking a Look at Investment in Nickel Production and Nickel Smelting Facilities in Indonesia
summary: The article examines new Indonesian listings in 2023 related to nickel production and nickel smelting/refining, suggesting improving investment conditions for expanding nickel supply. It explains nickel’s uses and production routes (sulfide vs laterite) and notes growing demand linked to stainless steels and EV lithium-ion batteries, implying supportive sentiment for nickel.

title: An Aluminium Plant in Guizhou Province Plans to Stop Production_SMM
summary: An SMM survey says an aluminium factory in Guizhou plans to completely stop production in mid-May. It previously cut output at the start of the year due to local power shortages and resumed slowly. The plant has 130,000 mt built capacity and about 50,000 mt operating capacity as of late April, implying a near-term supply squeeze.

title: Shanghai copper rises on low stockpiles, hope for better demand
summary: Shanghai copper rose 1.3% on low SHFE inventory levels that cushioned recent falls amid weaker-than-expected Chinese demand. The report cites May smelter maintenance and potential demand improvement after Labour Day, alongside cheaper prices. Aluminium and nickel also increased on Monday.

title: Red metal rising: Argentina sets lofty sights on global copper top 10
summary: Argentina is targeting a major expansion of copper production from currently zero output, with a pipeline of projects including Lundin’s Josemaria and Glencore’s El Pachón. The government cites high reserves and progress on environmental approvals and infrastructure, aiming to eventually bridge demand gaps tied to energy transition.

title: Merdeka Battery to acquire a $75m share in a China-owned nickel-processing facility
summary: Merdeka Battery plans to buy a 60% stake in PT Huaneng Metal Industry (HNMI), a nickel-processing facility in Indonesia’s Morowali Industrial Park. Valued at about $75 million, it targets completion mid-year and refines low-grade nickel matte into ~70% nickel product.

title: SMM Updates On China Aluminium Ingot Social Inventories As Of May 8_SMM
summary: SMM says China’s aluminium ingot social inventories were 816,000 mt as of May 8, down 19,000 mt on the week and 214,000 mt year-on-year. The decline is linked to smelters increasing molten output and cutting ingots, with regional variations. Downstream orders and shipments are key to watch.

title: Indonesia to allow exports of copper concentrate until 2024 | World
summary: Indonesia will allow Freeport Indonesia and Amman Mineral Nusa Tenggara to continue exporting copper concentrate until May/2024 despite an export ban starting June. The government cites smelter construction delays from the pandemic and expects smelters to complete by May 2024, issuing a regulation on the export leniency.

title: This aluminum producer's shares can rally nearly 50%, JPMorgan says
summary: CNBC reports JPMorgan initiated coverage on Alcoa with an overweight rating, arguing aluminum’s price outlook is improving due to supply constraints and strong secular demand for energy-transition uses. It notes bauxite permitting delays may keep costs elevated and cap near-term alumina output, but views Alcoa positioned to benefit from low-carbon smelting developments.

title: Terra Balcanica Confirms Epithermal Gold And Porphyry Copper Targets At Ceovishte In Serbia And Closes First Tranche Of Financing
summary: Terra Balcanica confirmed epithermal gold and porphyry copper targets at Ceovishte, Serbia, and closed the first tranche of financing. The update is related to potential future copper supply from a new project, but it provides no near-term operational changes, limiting immediate copper price impact.

title: Terra Balcanica Resources Corp.: Terra Balcanica Confirms Epithermal Gold And Porphyry Copper Targets At Ceovishte In Serbia And Closes First Tranche Of Financing
summary: Terra Balcanica reports assay results from its Ceovishte license in Serbia, identifying a large Au-Ag-Cu hydrothermal system with copper-bearing mineralization. Soil and rock sampling show elevated Cu (including up to ~2.47% Cu in rock and up to ~424 ppm Cu in soil) and defines drill-ready targets for upcoming drilling.

title: Copper Shortage Is Irreparable Even after Biggest Mergers and Acquisitions, Here's Why_SMM
summary: The piece cites views that new copper supply is insufficient for energy-transition demand over the next decade, even after large M&A deals. It highlights commissioning progress at Oyu Tolgoi and Glencore’s incentives to expand capacity, concluding global copper supply-demand balance remains tight despite transactions.

title: Copper Inventory in Major Chinese Markets Fell over Weekend_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China’s copper social inventories across major markets fell 700 mt from Friday, with Shanghai and Jiangsu declining while Guangdong rose. The drop reflects weaker weekend arrivals and active warehouse departures amid tight scrap supply. Destocking is expected to narrow this week as arrivals and imported inflows increase.

title: Mexico Copper Project Has 'Significant Potential,' Analyst Says
summary: Infinitum Copper reported assay results from La Adelita in Mexico, with several drill holes returning high copper-equivalent grades over meaningful widths and indicating mineralization continuity. The company is working toward a resource estimate, and the article highlights rising copper demand for electrification, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.20% Higher at $3.9180 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for May delivery settled 1.20% higher at $3.9180 per pound, gaining 4.65 cents. The move marks the largest one-day dollar and percentage gain since May 1, continues three consecutive sessions of gains, and lifts prices to the highest settlement since April 24, 2023.

title: SSR Mining Announces The Acquisition Of An Up To 40% Ownership Interest And Operatorship In The Hod Maden Gold-Copper Project Through An Earn-In Structured Transaction
summary: SSR Mining agreed to acquire up to 40% interest and operatorship of the Hod Maden gold-copper development project in Türkiye, paying $120m upfront and $150m in milestone earn-in payments. The deal includes copper production and copper-based economics but no direct near-term supply or demand change.

title: Copper crisis threatens future of "clean" energy – there's not nearly enough of this metal available for the world to go "green"
summary: The piece warns that the global energy transition faces a copper shortage, citing insufficient new discoveries and slow, costly mine development (e.g., Oyu Tolgoi) against rising demand. It claims supply growth lags refined copper appetite and declining grades/aging mines add pressure, implying tighter copper availability ahead.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Inc.: Ivanhoe Electric Subsidiary Cordoba Minerals Announces Closing of Milestone Agreement with JCHX for Joint Development of the Alacran Copper Project in Colombia
summary: Ivanhoe Electric’s subsidiary Cordoba Minerals closed an agreement with JCHX to jointly develop Colombia’s Alacran copper project, with JCHX paying US$40m initially and funding a feasibility study and permitting milestones. Cordoba repays Ivanhoe’s US$17.3m short-term loans and plans ongoing exploration and feasibility work, supporting copper project development sentiment.

title: Ero Copper Reports First Quarter 2023 Operating and
summary: Ero Copper reported Q1 2023 results showing 9,327 tonnes of copper produced in concentrate at Caraíba and reaffirmed full-year 2023 guidance of 44,000–47,000 tonnes. The company cited progress on the Caraíba mill expansion and new external shaft commissioning, supporting expectations for improved throughput and copper output later in 2023.

title: SHFE Nickel to Remain Rangebound Today_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SHFE nickel traded rangebound as downstream firms were cautious about restocking after Labour Day. NPI holders stayed slower to ship despite profits. Mild gains in stainless steel spot and HRC aided demand, but #316L fell sharply. Overall tight domestic and abroad nickel spot supply keeps prices supported, so SHFE nickel should remain rangebound.

title: China April copper imports at 407,294 tonnes  - customs
summary: China imported 407,294 tonnes of unwrought copper and copper products in April, down 12.5% versus a year earlier, according to customs data. The report also notes aluminium exports of 461,782 tonnes. The copper import decline points to softer demand that can pressure copper prices in the near term.

title: Material Matters: Iron Ore, Copper, Lithium & Nickel
summary: Brokers flag pressure across industrial raw materials. Citi turns bearish on copper, expecting slower China demand and weaker US/Europe consumption amid high inventories and disappointing orders, trimming the 0–3 month copper forecast. Macquarie expects a large global nickel surplus, with nickel pig iron and sulphate oversupply widening discounts versus LME.

title: Material Matters: Iron Ore, Copper, Lithium & Nickel
summary: Citi turns bearish on copper, citing softer global PMI readings, weaker China consumption expectations, high/rising inventories in the US and Europe, and continued order disappointment, cutting its near-term copper estimate. Separately, Macquarie expects a large nickel production surplus, with nickel pig iron and sulphate in oversupply and trading at discounts.

title: Metso Outotec Oyj : awarded a major concentrator plant equipment order for Zijin Mining's copper project in China
summary: Metso Outotec was awarded an EUR 85m order to supply concentrator plant equipment for Zijin Mining’s Julong copper project in China’s Tibetan region. The scope includes high-power SAG/ball milling, crushers, flotation cells, thickeners and filters, supporting copper processing capacity build-out.

title: Massive Aluminium Capacity In China To Be Resumed Or Put Into Operation In H2 2023_SMM
summary: March operating rates for aluminium smelters in key Chinese provinces were high. By April 20, 930,000 mt of capacity was resumed and 212,000 mt newly commissioned, nearly offsetting earlier cuts. Yunnan smelters could restart after power shortages ease, with further resumption/new capacity later this year, likely weighing on prices.

title: Copper Prices Went Up As Market Awaiting US Inflation Data, to Move at Lows amid Lingering Banking Crisis_SMM
summary: LME was closed, while SHFE copper rose 0.91% to 67,640 yuan/mt as markets looked ahead to US inflation data for Fed rate guidance. Chinese tracked inventories fell 700 mt from two Fridays ago, driven by limited arrivals and active shipments amid tight scrap supply, though downstream demand hasn’t improved much. Banking stress caps upside.

title: Doré Copper Announces Up to $3 Million Non-brokered Private
summary: Doré Copper Mining Corp. announced a non-brokered private placement raising up to about $3.0 million, including flow-through shares, to fund exploration, development and working capital. The company is targeting future copper production, but no near-term supply change or disruption is specified.

title: China April copper imports fall on sluggish economy, property woes
summary: China’s April unwrought copper and copper product imports fell to 407,294 tonnes, reflecting sluggish economic activity, continued property weakness, and softer industrial demand. Producers cut output due to weaker orders and profits, while less use of copper as collateral is reducing financing-driven demand.

title: Mercedes Benz : to integrate aluminium with almost 70 per cent CO2 reduction into series production
summary: Mercedes-Benz says it has passed validation tests and will integrate low-CO2 aluminium into large-scale production this year. Supplied by Hydro, the alloy includes at least 25% recycled content and cuts carbon footprint by about 70% versus the European average. Mercedes plans use in multiple EV models and structural parts.

title: FLSmidth to deliver grinding mills to a Chilean copper mine
summary: FLSmidth says it received an order worth about DKK 270 million to supply a Chilean copper mine with one SAG mill and two ball mills, plus installation support. The project expands grinding capacity at an existing site. Equipment delivery is scheduled for 2024.

title: FLSmidth A/S: FLSmidth to deliver grinding mills to a Chilean copper mine
summary: FLSmidth said it won an order worth about DKK 270 million to deliver SAG and two ball grinding mills to a copper mine in northern Chile. The project expands grinding capacity and uses energy-efficient drives. The order was booked in Q2 2023 and deliveries are scheduled for 2024, with site start-up support included.

title: Aluminium Bahrain B S C : Alba Receives ASI Chain of Custody Standard Certification for Responsible Production
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) said it received Aluminium Stewardship Initiative (ASI) updated Chain of Custody Standard V2 certification for its smelter and calciner/marine plant. The voluntary certification enables ASI-certified aluminium traceability across the value chain. It reflects responsible sourcing commitments, without indicating immediate supply changes or price impact.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Reports Additional In-fill Drilling Results from the Alacran Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals reported additional in-fill drilling results from its Alacran copper-gold-silver project in Colombia, including long intercepts with copper grades and copper-equivalent calculations. The company says results confirm the resource model and expected life-of-mine grades, with ongoing drilling focusing on peripheral infill areas.

title: Chile Agrees to Lower Tax Hike for Copper Producers Ahead of Senate Vote
summary: Chile has agreed to reduce a proposed tax increase for copper producers ahead of a Senate vote. A lower tax burden would likely support copper producers’ economics and sentiment, easing concerns about production incentives and near-term supply, which can add upward pressure to copper prices over coming days.

title: Copper steady, but China demand fears shackle sentiment
summary: Copper steadied but sentiment weakened as China data pointed to softer growth and demand, with April imports down 12.5% and manufacturing activity slipping. LME-approved copper inventories rose 40% since April 18 and a firmer dollar weighed on prices. Nickel fell on rising supplies; aluminium edged up modestly.

title: Koala 'massacre' in Portland, VIC leaves 152 marsupials dead as aluminium smelter Alcoa admits fault
summary: Alcoa, the aluminium smelter operator in Portland, Victoria, admitted euthanising 152 koalas after they showed illness from fluoride exposure tied to smelting waste. The company implemented a Koala Management Plan including closing an affected area and planting 16,000 eucalyptus trees, though no production disruption is reported.

title: Mining Stock News - Cordoba Minerals (TSXV: CDB) Reports Additional In-fill Drilling Results from the Alacran Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals reported additional in-fill drill results from its Alacran copper-gold-silver project in Colombia, with intercepts such as ~0.42–0.47% copper and ~0.60–0.70% copper equivalent over long intervals. Management says results support the resource model; it does not indicate imminent production changes or supply shocks.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.74% Lower at $3.8890 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for May delivery settled 0.74% lower at $3.8890 per pound, falling 2.90 cents. The report notes a break in a three-session winning streak and links to concurrent weakness in LME copper cash. It provides price context without new fundamental drivers.

title: Nickel Mining Puts Indonesian Fishers On Edge
summary: Environmental group WALHI and others urge Tesla to stop or limit direct investment and use of Indonesia’s nickel, citing pollution, smelter emissions, and alleged rights violations affecting fishing communities. With Indonesia a major nickel supplier, the scrutiny could increase compliance or disruption risk, weighing on nickel market sentiment.

title: Nevada Copper Announces Significant Financing Package Supporting Completion of the Underground Mine Ramp-Up; Significant Debt Reduction
summary: Nevada Copper announced up to $115 million in equity and debt/stream financing to complete the ramp-up and restart of its Pumpkin Hollow underground mine, targeting 5,000 tons per day by end-2023. The deal also repays about $82 million of debt via warrant exercises and improves liquidity for continued copper production.

title: Chile Senate Committee Passes New Tax Limit for Copper Producers
summary: The piece says Chile’s Senate committee has passed a new tax limit for copper producers. Such fiscal changes can influence producer economics and near-term supply expectations for Chilean copper. But the provided article content lacks specifics on the tax direction or magnitude, so net price impact is uncertain.

title: Copper up as dollar eases, but demand woes cap gains
summary: Copper prices rose on a weaker U.S. dollar ahead of U.S. inflation data, but gains were limited by expectations of subdued demand in Q2 and rising supply. Peru’s March copper output jumped 20.4% after mine stoppages. Aluminium and nickel were roughly steady to mixed as traders waited for CPI.

title: Global Aluminium Inventory to Plunge Further amid Supply Headwinds, LME Aluminium Prices to React Fast_SMM
summary: Century Aluminum’s CEO said supply-side headwinds are expected to keep shrinking global aluminium inventories in the short term. The report adds that regional premiums and LME aluminium prices should respond quickly as demand picks up, indicating potential upside pressure to aluminium prices over coming days.

title: Peru's March Copper Production up 20% YoY After Copper Mine Resumes Production_SMM
summary: Peru’s March copper production increased 20.4% YoY to 219,275 mt, with Q1 output up 11.2% YoY. The gains follow February shutdowns tied to local protests, including Las Bombas and Antapaccay. Production recovered as Southern Copper, Antapaccay, and Cerro Verde posted strong growth.

title: US Debt Ceiling Negotiations Deadlocked, SHFE, LME Copper Prices Closed Mixed, Prices to Move at Lows_SMM
summary: US debt-ceiling talks remain deadlocked, lifting the dollar and weighing on risk sentiment ahead of US CPI. Spot activity for copper stays muted, downstream buying fades after a brief rebound, and China’s April copper imports fall 12.5% y/y. Analysts expect copper prices to remain low.

title: Refined Nickel Output Rises Slightly in Apr, and to Continue to Grow in May_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s refined nickel output at 17,600 mt in April, slightly higher month-on-month, after offsetting shutdown/overhaul effects with production increases in Jiangsu. May output is forecast to rise to 17,900 mt, supported by continued Jiangsu ramp-ups and normal operations in Guangxi, suggesting added supply pressure.

title: Chinese buyers anticipate end to soft ban on Australian copper
summary: China is expected to ease unofficial restrictions on Australian copper ore and concentrate after trade talks, with some buyers reportedly applying to customs to import. Smelters want additional Australian feedstock amid a tight global market. If talks resolve trade impediments, Australian shipments could resume quickly, supporting copper sentiment.

title: Hardman & Co Research on Anglo Asian Mining (AAZ): Growth in copper production poised to explode
summary: Hardman & Co’s research on Anglo Asian Mining (AAZ) says the company is expanding beyond Gedabek into copper-focused projects. It cites copper deposits in concessions (Xarxar, Garadag, Demirli) and estimates ~50kt per year of copper output from staged developments “Copper 1” and “Copper 2,” supporting a bullish copper outlook.

title: Spot Nickel Transactions Remain Weak Today_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported that May 10 spot nickel transactions were sluggish. Jinchuan nickel premiums rose slightly, but NORNICKEL premiums fell, with nickel prices moving down. Nickel briquette trades were slack and priced at premiums over nickel sulphate, reflecting weaker near-term demand conditions for nickel.

title: Nickel Prospect Update Early Indications of Significant Mineralisation
summary: Macarthur Minerals provides an update on the Lake Giles tenements, where ultramafic komatiite-type rocks and serpentinised olivine/talc-carbonate formations are viewed as having high potential for nickel sulphides. The company plans nickel-targeted drilling, EM surveys, and assaying to refine prospects, indicating improved exploration focus.

title: Québec Nickel Initiates Metallurgical Test Program at Fortin Sill Zone
summary: Québec Nickel Corp. initiated scoping metallurgical tests at its Ducros project to assess whether the Fortin Sill Zone can produce a saleable Ni-Cu-Co-PGE+Au concentrate. SGS will run grindability, flotation, and separation tests using 150 kg of drill core, with results expected later in Q4 2023.

title: Trigon Metals Restarts Mining At The Kombat Copper Project Ahead Of Schedule
summary: Trigon Metals restarted mining at its Kombat copper project ahead of schedule, indicating production will resume sooner than planned. The development improves near-term supply expectations for copper and may weigh on spot and short-horizon copper pricing as markets adjust for earlier output.

title: TUBEX creates mono-material aluminium tube for product refills
summary: TUBEX launched a mono-material aluminium refill tube made largely from 100% recycled aluminium and high post-consumer recycled content, designed for easy closed-loop recycling. It highlights energy savings from recycling and growing interest from brands, while industry groups note concerns about PCR material availability and transition costs.

title: Nevada Copper secures $115m to support copper project in US
summary: Nevada Copper secured a $115m financing package to restart and ramp up its Pumpkin Hollow underground mine in Nevada toward 5,000 tpd capacity. Funds support mining restart, development, and working capital. KfW drew $15m first tranche; others fund remaining amounts, with ramp-up expected in 2H 2023.

title: Times of Zambia   |  2022 copper output setback on 10-year target
summary: Zambia’s copper production in 2022 dropped to about 763,550 tonnes from 803,747 tonnes in 2021, down roughly 4.2% (around 40,000 tonnes) due to heavy downpours and lower copper grades at Kansanshi, with additional declines at other major mines. Investment needs are highlighted to meet Zambia’s long-range target.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.57% Lower at $3.8280 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex Copper front-month for May delivery settled at $3.8280, down 6.10 cents (1.57%) on the day. The contract fell for two consecutive sessions, with the latest settlement the lowest since Jan. 5, 2023, signaling renewed bearish momentum in copper prices.

title: Asiamet says BKM copper project study shows "excellent" economics
summary: Asiamet Resources said its feasibility study for the Beruang Kanan Main (BKM) copper project in Indonesia delivered “excellent” economics, with 40.8 million tonnes of ore at 0.7% total copper and planned production up to 20 ktpa of copper cathode. The company called it a de-risking milestone and expects development to capture supply gaps.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Pacific Ridge Acquires 100% Interest in Kliyul and Redton Copper-Gold Projects
summary: Pacific Ridge agreed to acquire 100% interest in the Kliyul and Redton copper-gold porphyry projects and budgets a 7,000 m drilling program. The release discusses expanding the KMZ mineralized body and exploration targets in British Columbia. It signals future copper potential but not immediate supply changes.

title: Under The Spotlight: Brad Aelicks On Exploration And Development Of Max Resource Copper-Silver CESAR Project In Colombia
summary: MENAFN reports an interview on Brad Aelicks discussing exploration and development for Max Resource’s CESAR copper-silver project in Colombia. The news is copper-linked through project progress, which may marginally improve expectations for future supply, but it is not a near-term supply shock.

title: Century Aluminum Company (NASDAQ:CENX) Q1 2023 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Century Aluminum’s earnings call highlights stronger aluminum market conditions in Q1: rising LME prices and regional premiums, driven by additional European and Chinese smelter curtailments and reduced supply. Inventories are below 50 days of consumption, while US energy costs fell. The company expects modestly higher Q2 pricing and EBITDA.

title: Faces for 2020 senatorial race - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news
summary: Century Aluminum’s Q1 call reports aluminum market improvement: LME prices and regional premiums increased, supported by European and China supply curtailments and easing input costs (notably power). The company also highlights low global inventories and continued curtailment risk, alongside an acquisition of Jamalco alumina/bauxite to secure feedstock.

title: TSX Mining Stock News - American Eagle (TSXV: AE) Receives 5-Year Drill Permit for NAK Copper-Gold Project
summary: American Eagle Gold reports it has received a five-year drill permit for the NAK copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia and expects a 6,000-metre 2023 drill program to begin in coming weeks. The company aims to expand mineralized footprint and delineate high-grade copper-gold zones.

title: Josh Harder writes to FBI director amid surge in copper theft
summary: The news reports that Josh Harder has written to the FBI director amid a surge in copper theft. The move suggests concern over rising theft of copper assets, which can disrupt local availability and scrap flows. Any resulting supply tightness would be supportive for short-term copper prices.

title: China's GEM to build a $500 million joint nickel project in Indonesia
summary: China’s GEM plans a $500 million joint project in Indonesia’s Morowali Industrial Park to produce 20,000 tonnes per year of nickel intermediate product for the new energy sector. GEM holds 51%, CAHAYA JAYA INVESTMENT 26%, and Weiming 18%. The announcement links directly to nickel supply expectations.

title: Western Metallica Reports Drill Program Results Including 26 Metres at 1.5% Copper From Its Nueva Celti Copper Project
summary: Western Metallica announced encouraging drill results from its Nueva Celti Copper Project in southern Spain, including an intercept of 26 metres at 1.5% copper and confirmation of copper sulfide mineralization across multiple intervals. The findings support continued drilling and potential future discoveries, but do not imply immediate supply changes.

title: Spot Pure Nickel Trades Fall Short of Expectations on Poor Demand_SMM
summary: SMM reports May 11 nickel market weakness. Jinchuan nickel premiums averaged 8,900 yuan/mt, while NORNICKEL premiums fell to about 6,100 yuan/mt. Nickel price pressure is linked to poor downstream demand and recession-hit trading, with higher nickel warrants and slack briquette transactions pushing premiums down.

title: Alcoa and United Steelworkers Reach Tentative Agreement for U.S. aluminum smelters in Indiana and New York State
summary: Alcoa said it reached a tentative three-year labor agreement with the United Steelworkers for workers at its Warrick (Indiana) and Massena (New York) aluminum smelters. The pact covers about 860 employees and will be voted on by union members, with the prior contract expiring May 15, 2023.

title: PAN GLOBAL SECURES SURFACE ACCESS TO EXPLORE A 680 HECTARE AREA WEST OF THE LA ROMANA COPPER-TIN DISCOVERY AT THE ESCACENA PROJECT, SPAIN
summary: Pan Global said it has secured surface access to begin drilling immediately at the Romana West target within its Escacena project in Spain, aiming to test an on-strike extension of the La Romana copper-tin-silver discovery. Two rigs will mobilize and 25–30 holes are planned, with results pending.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Inc.: Ivanhoe Electric to Acquire 6,205 Acres of Private Land at the Santa Cruz Copper Project Near Casa Grande, Arizona
summary: Ivanhoe Electric said it signed an agreement to acquire 6,205 acres and associated water rights at its Santa Cruz underground copper project in Arizona, with mineral rights contingent on future payments through 2024. The company plans to use solar power but provides no near-term production or delivery timeline.

title: Credit Suisse says this aluminum producer's stock could rally more than 35% as the metal rebounds
summary: Credit Suisse upgraded Alcoa, saying the stock could gain over 35% as LME aluminum prices rebound. The note cites recovering global demand, supportive U.S./EU physical premiums, improving Chinese outlook, and supply dynamics tied to hydro challenges and an expected Spain smelter restart, despite noted risks.

title: Copper Futures Collapse to a Fresh 2023 Low
summary: Copper July futures have fallen steadily since a mid-January peak and experienced a sharp Thursday selloff, breaching the 200-day SMA and printing a fresh 2023 low. Technical indicators like MACD and RSI also turned bearish, suggesting downside pressure could extend despite oversold conditions.

title: ATEX Resources Announces Drilling Completion for ATXD-22A and ATXD-23 at Valeriano Copper-Gold Project
summary: ATEX Resources announced completion of drill holes ATXD-22A and ATXD-23 at its Valeriano copper-gold project in Chile. The company reports significant chalcopyrite and early porphyry mineralization and plans future assay releases and a revised NI-43 101 resource estimate, with assays expected by late May and July.

title: Copper Co. Partners With Major on Colombia Project's Design
summary: Libero Copper and Gold partnered with Anglo Asian Mining on design and financial modeling for its Mocoa copper project in Colombia. The company highlights future copper supply for green industries and details large copper resources, while emphasizing environmental mitigation. Overall, the development supports bullish sentiment toward copper prices.

title: Comex Copper Settles 3.41% Lower at $3.6975 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures for May delivery settled 3.41% lower at $3.6975/lb, falling 13.05 cents. The contract declined for three straight sessions, marking the largest one-day dollar and percentage drop since mid-March 2023, and the lowest settlement since Nov. 29, 2022.

title: Silver and gold futures decline; copper settles at lowest since November
summary: Gold and silver fell on a rebound in the U.S. dollar and concerns over China. The weak China inflation data intensified worries about demand. Copper also dropped sharply, settling at the lowest finish since Nov. 29, down 3.4% to $3.71 a pound, reflecting immediate risk-off sentiment.

title: Silver, copper futures drop after 'benign' China inflation data
summary: Copper futures fell to their lowest since November after China released “benign” inflation data that dulled demand expectations for industrial metals. Analysts cited a rebound in the U.S. dollar and concerns over China as key drivers. The move translated into a broader risk-off tone for copper (and silver).

title: Green Copper - Sustainable Copper from Brixlegg
summary: The piece explains that LME-traded copper cathodes require low impurities and links copper demand to the energy transition. It highlights Motanwerke Brixlegg’s “green copper” approach using recycled scrap, claiming large carbon savings versus primary copper. No immediate trade, supply, or pricing shock is described.

title: Pressenachricht: Green Copper - Sustainable Copper from Brixlegg
summary: Montanwerke Brixlegg AG promotes “green copper” produced from 100% recycled raw materials and 100% renewable energy, positioning it as sustainable copper with regulated impurity levels similar to LME-traded cathodes. It highlights recycling’s lower energy needs versus primary copper but gives no concrete near-term volume or price signals.

title: Mallee Resources Limited's progress at Avebury Nickel Mine | The Advocate
summary: Mallee Resources says its Avebury nickel mine has exited care-and-maintenance and is ramping up. By end of March it had about 210 staff and produced and sold the first 10,000 tonnes of nickel-cobalt concentrate. Output is building toward nameplate capacity (900,000 tpa), supporting higher near-term supply.

title: SMM Forecast on SHFE Nickel Prices Today_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel weakened on poor downstream demand and recession-driven trades, with rising nickel warrants and falling spot premiums. NPI supply is increasing as more Indonesian shipments arrive, while low-inventory holders delay sales. Stainless steel futures slid with nickel, pulling spot slightly lower. SMM expects nickel to trade rangebound today.

title: Copper plummets on China outlook, may drag down AUD/USD
summary: Copper prices fell sharply as China’s copper import data contracted (-7.9% yoy in April; first four months ~-13% vs 2022 pace) alongside weak CPI (0.1% yoy) and deeply negative PPI (-3.6%). Manufacturing PMI also pointed to contraction, reinforcing bearish near-term demand outlook and technical downside.

title: Copper heads for weekly losses as demand fears loom
summary: London and Shanghai copper prices edged higher on the day but were set for the biggest weekly decline since November. Reuters attributes the move to demand fears from China’s sluggish recovery and subdued industrial consumption, plus rising supply from surveyed smelters, alongside supportive currency/dollar effects weighing sentiment.

title: Sterling Hit by BoE Bailey; Aussie Suffers Amid Copper Price Decline
summary: The piece links a precipitous copper sell-off to China’s weak trade and inflation/macro data, including a sharp contraction in copper import volumes, softer CPI, and plunging PPI, plus manufacturing contraction. It also notes broader risk-off sentiment pressuring the Australian dollar.

title: Macro Sentiment Suddenly Turns Bearish, Chinese Aluminium Market to Face Supply Shock_SMM
summary: Macro sentiment turned bearish, driven by renewed expectations of US rate hikes, banking crisis worries, and debt-ceiling negotiations. SMM reports aluminium ingot inventories falling, but downstream operating rates remain mediocre and billet inventories rise. Smelter output and operating rates increased in April, with further growth expected in May.

title: Weekly Updates on China Aluminium Billet Inventory_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s aluminium billet social inventory reached 168,600 mt as of May 11, up 10,900 mt from a week earlier. SMM attributes the build to continued cargo arrivals, weak downstream demand, and more molten aluminium being converted into billets. With extrusion moving into off-season, billet inventories face further accumulation risk.

title: Weekly Updates on China Aluminium Ingot Inventory_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China aluminium ingot social inventories at 787,000 mt as of May 11, down 48,000 mt week-on-week and 216,000 mt year-on-year. Destocking remains fast and stocks are near five-year lows. Lower premium levels and fading arrivals are driving withdrawals, suggesting inventories stay low near term.

title: SMM Daily Aluminium Market Review And Forecast_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports SHFE 2306 aluminium ended down 1.21% and LME aluminium fell 2.49%. It notes improving conversion of molten aluminium into billets could affect end-demand transmission to inventories. If demand remains weak, smelters may shift to more ingot output, but low ingot inventories may limit downside. Watches macro and Yunnan supply.

title: Copper set for weekly fall as demand outlook darkens
summary: Copper was up on Friday but set for its biggest weekly drop since November as weak global economic data darkened demand expectations and rising supplies pressured prices. LME copper inventories rose toward a two-month high and a stronger dollar hurt sentiment, weighing on the broader metals complex including nickel and aluminium.

title: Copper Futures Prices Fall Sharply Amid Concerns over Economic Outlook_SMM
summary: Copper futures fell sharply: LME copper down 3.48% and SHFE copper down 2.76%. The move is tied to a stronger US dollar and concerns that economic data have worsened the global growth/monetary policy outlook. Downstream orders remain limited, so firms are cautious despite some dip-buying.

title: Nickel Ore Inventories at Chinese Ports down 243,000 wmt WoW_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Nickel ore inventories at Chinese ports fell 243,000 wmt WoW to 6.36 million wmt as of May 12, with total Ni content at 50,000 mt. Ore prices rose slightly. Buyers returned to rigid-demand purchases, while mines planned higher quotes; Philippine spot shipments resume despite poor weather, keeping supply expectations tighter.

title: Spot Nickel Trading Remains Average Today amid Low Futures Prices_SMM
summary: SMM said May 12 Jinchuan nickel premiums rose on supply tightness, but spot trading was average because futures prices are low. NORNICKEL premiums also edged up. Nickel briquette prices declined and deal activity was slack, with briquettes still trading at premiums over nickel sulphate.

title: Demand blues push copper to lowest in more than five months
summary: Copper hit the lowest level in over five months as fears of slowing demand in China, rising LME warehouse inventories, and a stronger U.S. dollar pressured prices. The sell-off was reinforced by recent Chinese inflation data. Aluminium was slightly higher on the day, while nickel’s gains reflected short-covering amid expected surpluses.

title: Commodities Prices - Iron ore and copper prices plunge as the commodity supercycle ends
summary: Iron ore and copper prices have fallen sharply, with copper dropping to about $3.70, the lowest since January. The move is linked to concerns that China’s economy is not recovering as quickly as expected, pressuring expectations for near-term copper demand.

title: Granite Creek Copper Ltd.: Granite Creek Copper Announces $1.35 Million Private Placement Financing
summary: Granite Creek Copper announced a $1.35 million private placement to fund exploration and development at its Carmacks copper-gold project in Yukon, plus working capital. The financing includes common and flow-through units, with proceeds earmarked for critical mineral exploration expenses. Shares are subject to a statutory hold; closure is expected in tranches.

title: Altamira Gold says Santa Helena project shows potential for porphyry-related copper mineralization
summary: Altamira Gold CEO updates exploration at the Santa Helena project in Brazil, noting copper-in-soil anomalies and magnetic features consistent with a porphyry intrusive setting. The company says this suggests potential for porphyry-related copper mineralization, though it does not indicate near-term development or output.

title: Nornickel continues selling nickel through Rotterdam port
summary: Norilsk Nickel said Rotterdam has allowed it to continue selling nickel through its transshipment hub after earlier disruptions. The company is also using the Tangier port in Morocco for product logistics. Continued nickel deliveries point to easing supply constraints, likely supporting nickel prices in the coming days.

title: LME to Require Warehouses to Feel Their Nickel Bags After Heist
summary: The article says the LME will require warehouses to verify (“feel”) their nickel bags following a heist. The change targets accountability and reduces uncertainty about physical nickel availability against LME warrants. Such operational disruptions can tighten deliverable supplies and support short-term nickel prices.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 4.00% Lower at $3.7165 -- Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for May delivery settled 4% lower for the week at $3.7165/lb, the biggest one-week percentage decline since late 2022. It was down three of four weeks but rose slightly on the day, snapping a three-session losing streak. No new catalysts beyond price data are cited.

title: LME to tighten rules for nickel handling by warehouses -Bloomberg News
summary: The LME plans tighter rules for how licensed warehouses handle nickel, including magnet/metal-detector tests, “touch inspections,” and weighing bags before delivery out of the LME system. The move follows cases where nickel delivered to traders proved to be stone and earlier irregularities in LME-warranted stocks.

title: GIADEC will ensure value-addition to bauxite to prevent raw exports – Akufo-Addo
summary: Ghana’s Akufo-Addo says GIADEC will add value to bauxite by building alumina refining and aluminium smelting, aiming to stop raw bauxite exports within about five years. The announcement frames value-add policy and local processing, which could shift expectations for alumina/primary aluminium supply and support aluminium prices.

title: Charleston-area aluminum maker edges closer to final SC business park sale
summary: Century Aluminum said it is nearing completion of the sale of the final parcel at Mount Holly Commerce Park near its Berkeley County smelter. The process includes minor zoning issues and a lower sale price than first expected, while the smelter operations are unchanged. The update follows a net loss in Q1.

title: China's copper woes dampen traders' spirits
summary: Traders at an LME Asia event in Hong Kong are cautious as China’s post–zero-COVID recovery shows slipping momentum. Data point to weaker consumption: factory activity contracted, copper imports fell, and Yangshan port premiums halved. With copper prices already down on the LME, margins and smelter exports remain stressed, supporting bearish near-term sentiment.

title: HAL To Replace Aluminium Control Rods Of Advanced Light Helicopters With Ones Made Of Steel
summary: HAL plans a replacement programme for Advanced Light Helicopter control rods after multiple crashes traced to aluminium rod problems. The armed forces’ fleet currently uses aluminium control rods, but HAL will replace them with steel rods, beginning shortly and taking about a year. This implies reduced aluminium component demand.

title: Russian Supply Glut Forces LME Aluminum Prices Lower
summary: Aluminum prices drifted lower in early May, pressured by rising Russian aluminum dominance in LME warrants. The article notes Russian brands’ share of primary aluminum inventory surged to about 53% in March, raising concerns over benchmark reliability. Despite this, LME and CME prices track closely, but downside risk remains.

title: London copper falls on stronger dollar, China demand worries
summary: Benchmark London copper prices fell in Asian trading as the U.S. dollar firmed to a five-week high and investors worried about weaker China demand ahead of industrial activity data. Rising inventories and a slowdown in global growth pressured sentiment. LME aluminium and nickel also declined.

title: Copper Futures Prices Rebound, Market Concerns over US Recession Grew_SMM
summary: LME copper rose slightly and SHFE copper increased, but the backdrop is weakening US confidence tied to debt-ceiling and monetary policy concerns, pressuring risk appetite and prices. Meanwhile, Chinese copper inventories fell and falling cathode-vs-scrap spreads encouraged wire and cable plants to boost rod purchases, supporting cathode consumption.

title: Shandong Nanshan may expand Indonesia site into $6 billion aluminium complex
summary: Shandong Nanshan’s Bintan SEZ alumina plant is running at full capacity, using Indonesian bauxite, and the company plans to build a 250,000 tpy aluminium smelter later this year, targeting a 1 million tpy aluminium plant by 2028. The SEZ also benefits from long tax waivers and renewable power plans.

title: China's refined copper imports to rebound in 2023 -Trafigura analyst
summary: Trafigura’s analyst says China is likely to import more refined copper later in 2023 as domestic inventories gradually fall. With the import arbitrage window mostly closed earlier and overseas stocks relatively low, declining in-China inventories could flip arbitrage, support Yangshan premiums, and raise near-term demand for imports.

title: 3.4 Million Mt/Year of New Alumina Capacity In China To Come Online In May_SMM
summary: SMM reports one 1 mt/y alumina refinery in Inner Mongolia fully closed in early May after halting in April, while three new alumina projects totaling 3.4 mt/y begin operating in May, boosting Q2 supply. Aluminium capacity in Yunnan remains curtailed. Alumina costs eased, but alumina prices kept falling and profit margins shrank.

title: Brazen copper thieves terrorising Walmer residents
summary: The article reports rising theft of copper cables and water pipes in Walmer and Nelson Mandela Bay, often involving illegal scrap dealers that create a market for stolen metal. Officials and police are working to close illegal dealers and prosecute cable thieves, which could disrupt near-term copper scrap flows and supply expectations.

title: Macro Headwinds And Bearish Fundamentals To Put Downward Pressure SHFE Aluminium Prices_SMM
summary: SMM reports worsening macro conditions and bearish fundamentals for aluminium. Despite declining Chinese social inventories, demand is viewed as pessimistic, downstream operating rates are unlikely to improve, and domestic operating capacity is expected to rise above 40.9 Mt. Falling anode and captive power costs add pressure. SHFE and LME aluminium seen with downside.

title: Aluminium Costs Fell Sharply Last Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that aluminium smelter costs fell sharply last week as coal prices dropped and ample captive power reduced electricity costs. Prebaked anode prices also declined, lowering real-time full smelter cost to about 16,383 yuan/mt and boosting profits. Aluminium A00 prices eased to 17,890 yuan/mt, but margins improved.

title: Aluminium Costs Will Still Have Room To Fall In The Short Term_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that alumina and coal prices remain unstable, implying aluminium production costs still have room to fall in the short term. Although some smelters are already experiencing small losses due to weaker aluminium prices and relatively high electricity costs, the ongoing input cost weakness points to continued downward pressure on aluminium.

title: Improved import Losses Kept Yangshan Copper Premiums Firm_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Yangshan copper premiums rose week-on-week, with import losses shrinking into profits. Better SHFE/LME ratios and contango dynamics increased import demand and firmer warrant and bill-of-lading pricing. Meanwhile, domestic bonded-zone inventories fell, and this week’s bill-of-lading arrivals are expected to be lower, supporting copper premiums.

title: Chile's Short-Term Disruptions Unlikely To Change Ample Supply, SMM Imported Copper Concentrate Index Rose Further_SMM
summary: SMM reports Chile protests starting April 21 disrupted day and night shifts at several copper mines, with infrastructure risk to Codelco assets. Despite this, SMM expects only a limited impact and “hardly” any change to ample copper concentrate supply. Imported concentrate TCs rose further and inventories at Chinese ports increased.

title: Copper Inventories to Fall This Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM expects total supply and downstream demand to increase in Guangdong this week as smelters deliver toward the SHFE May contract and customs clearance improves. Inventory in Guangdong should fall slightly, pushing spot premiums up. Lower copper prices are also said to support improving consumption.

title: SMM Survey of Trades in China Major Copper Markets _SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China spot #1 copper cathode premiums versus SHFE moving from 50-90 yuan/mt to lower levels, then rising again as SHFE spreads/backwardation widened. Market uncertainty kept buyers cautious, but downstream dipped into buying on price drops. Social inventories fell, with weaker arrivals and faster warehouse outflows.

title: NUCLIDIUM and PharmaLogic Form Strategic Partnership for Sustainable Development of Novel Copper-based Theranostics to Diagnose and Treat Solid Tumours
summary: NUCLIDIUM and PharmaLogic announced a strategic partnership to produce and supply 61Cu radionuclides in the US for clinical trials and future radiopharmaceutical products. The agreement expands domestic 61Cu production capacity via PharmaLogic facilities, aiming for reliable copper isotope availability for oncology theranostics.

title: World's Biggest Gold Miner Bets Big on Copper -- Commodities Roundup
summary: The article reports Newmont’s $17.5 billion deal to acquire Australia’s Newcrest, highlighting that Newcrest’s gold assets also produce substantial copper. It frames a broader wave of mining M&A tied to commodities needed for EVs and renewables, supporting near-term copper sentiment.

title: Teck receives regulatory approval for Zafranal copper project
summary: Teck said Peru’s SENACE granted regulatory approval for its Zafranal copper project. Located in the Arequipa porphyry copper belt, the mid-sized mine is expected to produce copper-gold concentrates, with initial years targeting about 133,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate. Teck aims for formal sanction in H1 next year.

title: Atalaya Mining profit falls on higher costs, copper sales up revenue
summary: Atalaya Mining reported lower quarterly profit due to higher input costs, while revenue rose slightly on higher copper concentrate volumes. Realised copper prices fell to about $4.00/lb from $4.50/lb last year. The company cited lower electricity prices aiding costs and stayed on copper production guidance.

title: Short-term copper price forecasts in 2023
summary: The piece argues China’s post-reopening economic recovery should lift refined copper demand and tighten global fundamentals, supporting higher highs and lows near term. It notes April copper weakness despite strong China macro data, attributing it to buy-the-rumor/sell-the-news and LME long liquidation, but expects copper gains in coming months.

title: Copper prices rise after last week's slump with China liquidity injection
summary: Copper rebounded after a five-month low as China’s PBOC injected liquidity, signaling support for economic growth and improving base-metal sentiment. The weaker dollar and “bargain hunting” aided prices. Aluminium rose on lower LME on-warrant stocks, while nickel weakened on vulnerability concerns and forecast cuts.

title: China Copper Mine Halted After Incident Leaves Six Missing
summary: The headline reports that a copper mine in China was halted after an incident in which six people are missing. A mine stoppage typically disrupts near-term mine output, raising concerns over reduced copper supply and supporting expectations for firmer copper prices over the next days to weeks.

title: Emerita Intersects 4.2 Meters Grading 1.4 % Copper; 6.9 % Lead; 14.7 % Zinc; 0.31 g/t Gold and 63.7 g/t Silver, at La Infanta Deposit and Granted Permit to Further Explore IBW with Addition of Infanta Sur
summary: Emerita Resources reported assay results from 21 drill holes at its Iberian Belt West La Infanta deposit, highlighting polymetallic massive sulphide intervals including ~1.4% copper over 4.2m in one hole. The company also received a permit for Infanta Sur to start exploration. No nickel or aluminium impact is indicated.

title: Copper Inventory across Major Chinese Markets Plunged Over Weekend_SMM
summary: SMM shows China’s major-market copper inventories fell to 141,100 mt as of May 15, down 10,900 mt on Friday and 26,300 mt versus two Mondays ago. Drops in Shanghai, Jiangsu, Chongqing and Chengdu reflect fewer domestic arrivals and dip-buying, while Guangdong rose slightly. Inventories may keep declining, supporting copper.

title: Funds sell copper as China's recovery disappoints :  Andy Home
summary: Reuters reports funds have turned increasingly bearish on LME three-month copper as China’s manufacturing recovery disappoints. CME positioning has swung to a larger net short, LME inventories have risen, Chinese refined imports have slumped, and the market shows weak spot demand, reinforcing near-term downside pressure.

title: Copper prices rebound with China liquidity injection
summary: Copper prices rose about 1% on Monday after China’s central bank injected liquidity, supporting the Chinese economy and improving base-metal sentiment after a five-month low. A Tibet copper mine stopped production after an accident. The weaker U.S. dollar added support. Aluminium also climbed as LME on-warrant stocks fell.

title: Kincora Copper : First Quarter 2023 Financial Statements and Management Discussion & Analysis
summary: Kincora Copper Limited released its Q1 2023 financial statements and MD&A, describing ongoing drilling and exploration progress at Trundle and other Australian projects, with recent visuals/assays including copper grades. It also discusses Mongolia-related legal developments and planned drilling. No production changes or market-moving supply impacts are stated.

title: Shandong Nanshang to invest $6bn in aluminium expansion in Indonesia
summary: Shandong Nanshang plans to invest $6bn in expanding aluminium operations in Indonesia’s Bintan SEZ, including building a 250,000 tpa aluminium smelter and targeting additional capacity by 2028. The project is supported by new power generation plans, potentially lifting regional aluminium supply expectations.

title: Nickel Asia Q1 earnings down 8%
summary: Nickel Asia reported Q1 net income down 8%, citing foreign exchange losses and a lower weighted average nickel ore price. The move suggests weaker nickel ore pricing during the quarter, which can influence short-term sentiment about nickel supply/demand and producer cost conditions.

title: Aluminum flat-rolled products (FRP) market size to grow by USD 17.84 billion from 2022 to 2027; APAC to account for 65% of the market growth
summary: Technavio projects growth in the global aluminum flat-rolled products (FRP) market, with APAC driving most gains and demand tied to packaging (beverage cans/films), construction, and transportation. It cites green-building initiatives and mass transportation as drivers, but offers no immediate supply disruption or policy action.

title: Alcoa and Emirates Global Aluminium sign major, long-term alumina supply agreement
summary: Alcoa and Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) signed an 8-year, multi-year alumina supply agreement starting in 2024, with options up to 15.6 million tonnes from Western Australia. EGA will source smelter-grade alumina for its Abu Dhabi/Dubai smelters, with low-carbon EcoSource options, reducing near-term uncertainty on alumina availability.

title: Copper Mining Co. Moves Forward With Acquisition of Key Project
summary: Granite Creek Copper announced a small private placement and additional details on acquisitions and upcoming metallurgical and exploration work for its Carmacks copper-gold-silver project. The update is primarily company-specific, with no clear near-term production, inventory, or trade impact that would materially move copper prices within weeks.

title: Alcoa Inks Eight-Year Supply Deal With Emirates Global Aluminium
summary: Alcoa has agreed to an eight-year supply deal with Emirates Global Aluminium. The contract links a major producer’s deliveries with a key downstream aluminium player, which can improve visibility on contracted demand and supply tightness, supporting expectations for aluminium prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: Alcoa signs 8-year alumina supply deal with Emirates Global Aluminium
summary: Alcoa signed an eight-year alumina supply agreement with Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA), starting in 2024, to deliver up to 15.6 million tonnes of smelter-grade alumina from Western Australia. Alumina is a key aluminium raw material, and the contract secures feedstock and supports aluminium production planning.

title: Silvercorp Metals targets Philippines copper with Celsius Resources merger move
summary: Silvercorp Metals has launched a ~$56m bid to acquire Philippines copper developer Celsius Resources, including interim $5m funding for the MCB copper-gold project. The merger targets development and exploration, but it is a relatively small corporate transaction with limited immediate production impact on global copper prices.

title: Copper Futures Prices Rebounded On Falling US Dollar_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: LME copper rose modestly as the US dollar retreated from a five-week high, but the market is still focused on Washington’s debt-ceiling resolution and recession/default risk. An opened import window increased copper cathode inflows and supply, while downstream demand remained soft, suggesting copper stays relatively low short term.

title: RCs of Blister Copper In South China Will Fall In May_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that smelter maintenance demand improved as inventories fell. At the same time, copper scrap supply declined amid lower copper prices, narrowing the cathode–scrap spread. With tighter blister copper supply in south China, the article expects lower RCs for blister copper in May.

title: SMM Copper Concentrate Index Rose Further in April_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM says the April Copper Concentrate Index rose $5.88/mt to $83.38/mt. It notes ample offers but higher pricing for seaborne clean ore and trading TCs around $85/mt for June delivery, while blister copper RCs stayed relatively firm/flat. Overall, copper concentrate economics improved.

title: China Copper Concentrate Imports Increased In April, Imports from Chile Plunged_SMM
summary: China imported 2.1 million mt of copper ore and concentrate in April 2023, but SMM expects May imports to fall to about 2.076 million mt due to reduced smelter raw-material demand during maintenance. The article also shows mixed regional flows, including a sharp fall from Chile.

title: Imported Copper Concentrate TCs Seen Rising in Second Quarter_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM forecasts imported copper concentrate treatment charges (TCs) will keep rising in Q2. It attributes the increase to planned intensive maintenance at major Chinese smelters, which is expected to weaken concentrate demand. The report links the expected TC trend to near-term supply-demand conditions for copper processing.

title: Qianhai Mercantile Exchange plans battery metals, green aluminium contracts
summary: Qianhai Mercantile Exchange plans to launch contracts for lithium carbonate, nickel sulphate, and possibly one other battery metal, alongside considering a low-carbon “green aluminium” physical contract in China. The move targets EV-battery demand and rising preferences for lower-emissions aluminium, but no near-term supply or inventory change is cited.

title: Copper subdued as China activity data highlights patchy recovery
summary: Copper prices stayed subdued after China’s April industrial output and retail sales growth missed analyst forecasts, pointing to an uneven recovery for the world’s top metals consumer. Reuters notes funds turning more bearish on copper. Aluminium also edged higher as China’s aluminium output fell on power curbs, though net price pressure was still limited.

title: China April aluminum output up 0.8% on year
summary: China’s aluminium output in April increased 0.8% y/y to 3.33 million tonnes as some smelters resumed operations, raising daily production versus March. Power curbs in Yunnan still constrained supply, but the larger supply print and weaker Shanghai prices (vs March) point to bearish near-term aluminium pressure.

title: Nickel Ore Shipments From The Philippines Rose In April, Shipments To Grow Further In May_SMM
summary: SMM reports that Chinese ports received 2.67 million wmt of nickel ore in April, up 42% month-on-month, while Philippine exports rose to 2.36 million wmt, up 52%. The monsoon disruption eased and mining recovered, with demand picking up at the same time. May shipments are expected to rise further.

title: Nickel Ore Imports Rebounded In March On Fading Impact Of The Monsoon Season In The Philippines_SMM
summary: China’s nickel ore imports rebounded in March to 2.12 million mt (+42.9% MoM), with laterite ore and higher shipments from the Philippines after monsoon disruptions. Nickel sulphide ore imports also rose. Domestic port inventories increased, and April imports are expected to grow as NPI supply tightens.

title: Is nickel mining for EVs fuelling abuses in Southeast Asia?
summary: A Thomson Reuters Foundation report warns that nickel mining for EV battery supply chains in Indonesia and the Philippines involves environmental damage and alleged human-rights abuses. It notes Indonesia’s nickel ore export restrictions, Philippines mine closure/resumption history, and recent pledges to improve monitoring—raising reputational and compliance risks for nickel producers.

title: Indonesia Determined to Ban its Bauxite Exports in June, but China's Imports of Bauxite in March Still Stood High_SMM
summary: China’s March bauxite imports rose, but Indonesian bauxite flows fell sharply as Indonesia plans a June export ban. Alumina refineries reportedly seek alternative sources to offset the disruption, yet the policy is expected to weigh on bauxite prices and reduce refinery profits, likely pressuring aluminium-linked sentiment.

title: Funds sell copper as China's recovery disappoints: Andy Home
summary: Funds are turning more bearish on LME three-month copper after China’s manufacturing recovery disappoints. The article cites growing net short positions, shrinking Chinese refined import flows, rising LME inventories, and relaxed spreads/weak spot demand. With copper breaking technical support, short-covering appears unlikely near term.

title: Refined Nickel Imports Totalled 4,443 mt in March, and Imports of Nickel Powder Stood at 1,310 mt_SMM
summary: China’s nickel imports fell sharply in March. Refined nickel totaled 4,443 mt, down 52% MoM and 77% YoY, while nickel powder and flake reached 1,310 mt, down 35% MoM and 58% YoY. Nickel briquettes rose MoM but fell YoY; Russia nickel plate imports dropped to zero.

title: China April aluminium output up 0.8% on year
summary: China’s April aluminium output rose 0.8% year-on-year to 3.33 million tonnes as some smelters resumed operations, though Yunnan power curbs limited production. Despite supply constraints, aluminium prices received little support; Shanghai futures averaged lower than March. May output is expected to rise slightly, adding bearish supply tone.

title: China Hydrometallurgical Intermediate Nickel Products Grew Significantly in March_SMM
summary: China imported 129,000 mt of hydrometallurgical intermediate nickel products in March, up 13% month-on-month (equivalent to 24,600 mt Ni). High-nickel matte imports reached 20,000 mt and were up year-on-year, with Indonesia driving most growth. This suggests firmer nickel material inflows for processing.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Intersects 45.89 Metres at 1.68% Copper, 0.33 g/t Gold and 5.55 g/t Silver Near Surface
summary: Faraday Copper reported six drill-hole results at its Copper Creek project in Arizona, including 45.89m at 1.68% copper and additional long intervals with copper mineralization. The company also notes ongoing gold/silver assays and continued Phase II drilling to expand resources and delineate high-grade zones.

title: Enriching society through aluminium products: Jindal Aluminium upholds its no.1 position as India's largest aluminium extrusion company
summary: Jindal Aluminium reports record aluminium extrusion production of 106,000 metric tons, 16% revenue growth, and 100% renewable energy use. It also acquired and restarted a Bhiwadi unit and plans to add further capacity, targeting extrusion capacity growth from 1.30 to 1.50 lakh MTPA and supporting exports.

title: Mirasol Resources begins drilling at copper project Sobek in Chile
summary: Mirasol Resources began drilling at its 100%-owned Chile copper project, Sobek, targeting the Central Breccia Zone in the Vicuña copper-gold-silver district. The company cites airborne Mobile MT survey results and surface geochemical samples to refine drilling orientations. The work continues until winter weather limits access.

title: Emirates Global Aluminium and Alcoa sign alumina supply agreement
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium signed an eight-year agreement with Alcoa to supply 15.6 million tonnes of smelter-grade alumina from Western Australia starting in 2024. The contract boosts EGA’s alumina security beyond its refinery output and offers low-carbon EcoSource options, supporting aluminium production continuity.

title: Alcoa and Emirates Global Aluminum sign major, long-term alumina supply agreement
summary: Alcoa and Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) signed an eight-year agreement starting in 2024 for Alcoa to supply smelter-grade alumina, with options for up to 15.6 million tonnes from Western Australia. EGA’s Abu Dhabi refinery met 47% of its needs in 2022, and the pact strengthens long-term alumina security, including low-carbon EcoSource.

title: Palladium One Identifies Additional Chonolith / Feeder Dyke Structures, Field Season Initiated on the Tyko Nickel Project, Canada
summary: Palladium One Mining announced initial results from 2023 exploration at its Tyko nickel-copper project in Ontario, using updated airborne magnetic survey data to refine chonolith/feeder dyke targeting and begin field mapping and sampling. The release is exploratory with no immediate production or supply disruption mentioned.
