summary: Russian aluminium registered with London Metal Exchange warehouses rose to 68% of total holdings in May (from 52% in April), with 263,125 tonnes in warehouses. The LME said Russian metal continues to flow and be accepted. Concentrated stocks raise concerns about price distortion, likely weighing on aluminium sentiment.

title: Glencore, automakers to back US$1-billion nickel and copper SPAC deal in Brazil
summary: Glencore, Stellantis and PowerCo back a $1-billion SPAC deal in Brazil to buy the Santa Rita nickel sulphide and Serrote copper mines. Nickel concentrate will be refined in Glencore facilities and supplied into EV battery production. The expanding hydropower-based mines do not signal an immediate supply shock, limiting price impact.

title: Glencore, automakers to back US$1-billion nickel and copper SPAC deal in Brazil
summary: Glencore, Stellantis, and PowerCo back a $1-billion SPAC deal in Brazil to buy the Santa Rita nickel and Serrote copper mines. Nickel concentrate will be refined at Glencore facilities and feed EV battery production. Hydropower use and planned expansions further support investment sentiment.

title: Rio Tinto to expand its AP60 low-carbon aluminium smelter in Quebec
summary: Rio Tinto will invest $1.1 billion to expand its AP60 low-carbon aluminium smelter in Quebec, adding 96 new AP60 pots and about 160,000 tonnes of primary aluminium capacity per year. The project offsets closures at Arvida and aims to meet demand for low-carbon aluminium, with commissioning starting in H1 2026.

title: Rio Tinto Will Invest $1.1 Billion to Increase Capacity at Aluminum Site in Canada
summary: Rio Tinto will invest $1.1 billion to expand its low-carbon aluminium smelter at Complexe Jonquiere, Canada, adding about 160,000 tonnes/year and offsetting capacity lost from potroom closures. The project runs over two-and-a-half years and fully ramps by end-2026, supported partly by Quebec.

title: Rio Tinto to invest $1.1 billion to expand aluminum smelter in Canada
summary: Rio Tinto will invest $1.1 billion to expand its low-carbon aluminium smelter at Complexe Jonquière in Quebec, with up to $113 million from Quebec government support. The expansion will align with potroom closures at Arvida. Construction runs 2.5 years, with new pots commissioning in 1H 2026.

title: Copper under pressure ahead of China data, Fed decision
summary: Copper fell 0.7% as traders worried about China’s demand outlook and awaited U.S. Fed and inflation data. Earlier gains were linked to covering shorts and Chinese stimulus optimism. Falling LME stocks offer some support, but expectations of elevated rates and China uncertainty weigh on copper and aluminium.

title: FS of Nickel Project Expected in 9/23
summary: Canada Nickel said it has improved in-process tailings technology to capture carbon during ore processing at its Crawford nickel project, potentially lowering capital and operating costs and qualifying for refundable carbon-capture tax credits. The integrated feasibility study is now expected in September 2023, with no change to the overall schedule.

title: CanAlaska Proposes to Spinout Five Nickel Properties
summary: CanAlaska Uranium proposes to spin out five nickel properties (including the Mel nickel deposit) into a new vehicle, Core Nickel, via a statutory plan of arrangement. The company says completion is conditional on approvals, financing, listings and market conditions, with no operational or supply change detailed.

title: Copper dips after hitting strong cluster resistance
summary: Copper dipped as traders grew cautious ahead of the FOMC rate decision and awaited Chinese investment and production data for demand signals. The market faced a resistance cluster near 3.8229–3.8511; rejection could deepen losses toward 3.5393, while only a sustained breakout would turn outlook bullish.

title: Markets Mixed ahead of Fed and ECB; Aussie Extending Rally With Eyes on Copper and China
summary: Copper is reported to dip as traders turn cautious ahead of the FOMC decision and look to upcoming China data for demand signals. The piece cites rejection at a key resistance cluster and outlines a bearish technical path if support fails, implying further downside risk.

title: Rio Tinto to invest $1.4 billion to expand Quebec aluminum smelter
summary: Rio Tinto will invest $1.4 billion to expand its Quebec aluminum smelter by adding 96 AP60 pots, with Quebec funding up to $150 million. The project targets lower greenhouse-gas emissions and is expected to take about 2.5 years to build, boosting aluminum supply capacity.

title: Cdn. government signs MoU with Rio Tinto for aluminum manufacturing
summary: Canada signed a MoU with Rio Tinto to expand its Complexe Jonquière aluminum smelter by investing CAD $1.4 billion. The project will scale low-carbon AP60 electrolysis and deploy ELYSIS technology, adding new Western smelting capacity and increasing jobs during construction.

title: Rio Tinto invests $1.4-billion to expand Quebec aluminum manufacturing operations
summary: Rio Tinto will invest $1.4 billion to expand its Quebec aluminum smelter, adding AP60 pots and raising primary aluminum capacity to about 220,000 tonnes per year. The project is supported by a Quebec loan and includes plans to partially close older lines while adding recycling capacity.

title: Glencore, carmakers back $1bn nickel and copper mines deal
summary: Glencore and automakers back a $1bn SPAC deal to buy two Brazilian mines: a nickel sulphide site in Santa Rita and a copper mine in Serrote. The output will be refined at Glencore refineries and used for EV batteries, with $100m equity from Glencore and $100m nickel prepayment from PowerGo.

title: Glencore, carmakers back $1bn nickel and copper mines deal
summary: Glencore and automakers backed a $1bn SPAC deal to buy Brazilian nickel sulphide and copper mines, with Glencore handling nickel refinement at its Western and North American refineries. The metals are intended for EV battery use by Stellantis and PowerGo, reinforcing near-term supply-demand expectations.

title: Rio Tinto to expand aluminum smelter with $1.4B investment using greener technology
summary: Rio Tinto said it will invest $1.4 billion to expand its aluminium smelter complex in Saguenay, Quebec, adding 96 new pots using low-carbon AP60 technology. The move targets greener aluminum production capacity at the Jonquiére/Arvida site, which may support longer-run supply expectations but is unlikely to strongly move prices immediately.

title: Aluminum Extruders Council says unfair import rules have lead to massive rise in imported aluminum
summary: The Aluminum Extruders Council says U.S. Department of Commerce rules grant tariff-free treatment to foreign extruded aluminum via broad exclusions, while domestic producers face higher proof burdens. It claims untariffed imports rose 82% and penetration exceeded 25%—a record—prompting calls to revoke the General Approved Exclusion process.

title: Arizona Metals probes copper-gold deposit expansion at decades dormant Kay Mine
summary: Arizona Metals’ drill results at the long-dormant Kay Mine in Arizona indicate potential expansion of a high-grade copper-gold system, including strong copper-equivalent intercepts and additional drilling continuity. The news highlights exploration progress and future phase planning but does not signal imminent production affecting near-term copper supply.

title: Rio Tinto to expand aluminum smelter with $1.4B investment using greener technology | iNFOnews
summary: Rio Tinto will invest $1.4B to expand its Jonquière aluminum smelter in Quebec with 96 new low-carbon AP60 pots, targeting 220,000 tonnes of primary output and replacing jobs affected by the Arvida closure in 2025. Quebec will provide support contingent on job retention and emissions targets.

title: Appian sells Brazilian companies, Atlantic Nickel and Mineração Vale Verde, to ACG for US$1.065 billion
summary: Appian agreed to sell its Brazilian battery-metals portfolio—Atlantic Nickel (Santa Rita) and Mineração Vale Verde (Serrote copper-gold asset)—to ACG for $1.065 billion cash. The deal positions a London-listed nickel sulphide producer and targets expanded supply to Western EV partners, but it is mainly ownership transfer.

title: Mining Stock News: Drilling Underway at American Eagle's (TSXV: AE) (OTCQB: AMEGF) NAK Copper-Gold Project
summary: American Eagle Gold says drilling has started at its NAK copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia, with a planned 7,000 metres through October to expand and test copper-gold mineralization. The program is fully funded via Teck Resources’ strategic investment, supporting bullish sentiment for potential copper resource growth.

title: Iran discovers largest porphyry copper deposit in region
summary: Iranian media reports a major porphyry copper discovery in the Sarcheshmeh area of Kerman province, estimating billions of tonnes of high-copper-ore content and planning further exploration. It also notes recent copper production progress via a new smelter at Sungun, implying longer-term supply potential rather than immediate changes.

title: The Monday Report (On Tuesday) - 13 June 2023
summary: Market wrap notes metals were mixed: nickel shares surged after Nickel Industries announced a conditional capital placement with an Indonesian mining conglomerate at a premium to fund its nickel/cobalt project in Indonesia. The report also discusses macro CPI/Fed expectations, but the only metal-specific company news is nickel.

title: Rio Tinto to expand aluminum smelter with $1.4B investment using greener technology - MRO Magazine
summary: Rio Tinto will invest $1.4B to expand its Jonquiere, Quebec aluminium smelter, adding 96 AP60 low-carbon pots and increasing capacity by roughly 220,000 tonnes per year. The project is intended to replace jobs as the older Arvida plant closes in 2025, supported by Quebec funding.

title: Copper edges higher as China's rate decision lifts appetite
summary: Copper and other base metals in London climbed after China cut a key borrowing rate for the first time in 10 months to support growth. Traders expected improved industrial demand, while a weaker dollar also made greenback-priced metals cheaper for non-dollar buyers. LME aluminium, nickel, and copper rose modestly.

title: Replicating Indonesia's success in the nickel sector isn't likely with its bauxite exports: Analyst
summary: An analyst discusses how Indonesia’s decision to ban bauxite exports creates policy uncertainty for mining and metals investors. Because bauxite is a key input for alumina and then aluminium production, reduced export availability is likely to tighten feedstock supply and support aluminium prices over coming weeks.

title: Replicating Indonesia's success in the nickel sector isn't likely with its bauxite exports: Analyst
summary: The article examines how Indonesia’s ban on bauxite exports could affect metals markets. Analysts note investor concern over policy uncertainty in Indonesia’s mining and metals sector. Because bauxite is crucial for alumina and aluminium production, the export restriction is expected to tighten supply and pressure aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Alumina Supply Surplus In China Is Far Below Previously Predicted_SMM
summary: SMM reports China’s alumina supply surplus in May was only 78,000 mt, well below earlier 200,000 mt expectations, helped by refinery maintenance and slower new project output releases. Prices stabilize as hydropower in Yunnan supports potential aluminium smelter restarts in late June, boosting alumina demand expectations.

title: Copper Prices To Move Rangebound As Market Remains Cautious_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: LME and SHFE copper prices edged lower overnight as markets stayed cautious ahead of key policy decisions, especially the Fed rate outlook. China copper inventories fell due to concentrated smelter maintenance and limited imports, but downstream buying was weak from delivery timing and high premiums. Net effect expected: rangebound copper prices.

title: Copper rises as China's rate cut boosts risk sentiment
summary: Copper prices rose after China cut borrowing costs for the first time in 10 months, supporting growth expectations and risk sentiment. A softer dollar also helped. The Reuters snapshot showed LME aluminium and nickel moving higher alongside copper, though China’s total copper demand remained weaker month-on-month.

title: Boliden halts production at Ronnskar copper smelter due to fire
summary: Boliden halted production at its Ronnskar copper smelter in Sweden after a fire damaged the cell house. The disruption affects a major smelting unit and can tighten nearby copper supply.

summary: Rio Tinto said it will invest $1.1 billion to expand aluminium production at its Complexe Jonquiere smelter in Canada, supported by up to $111.3 million in Quebec funds. The capacity increase implies greater aluminium supply, which may pressure near-term aluminium price expectations.

title: Breakthrough: American West detects large copper target at Storm project
summary: American West Metals reports gravity and geophysical results indicating a much larger sediment-bound copper system beneath near-surface mineralization at its Storm project in Nunavut, Canada. title: Chile Prevents Lundin from Reopening Its Alcaparrosa Copper Mine_SMM
summary: Chile’s environmental court has ordered a stoppage that blocks Lundin from reopening its Alcaparrosa copper mine. The mine was previously closed after a sinkhole emerged in a nearby village. summary: The article argues macro optimism and policy support (debt-ceiling deal, lower recession odds, softer dollar) are boosting copper sentiment. summary: SMM forecasts that Guangdong’s spot copper premiums will fall this week. summary: The LME aluminum contract is increasingly backed by Russian-origin metal: its warehouse share rose from 52% in late April to 68% by end-May. summary: T2 Metals and the Kiciwapa Cree Nation signed an exploration agreement for the Sherridon copper-zinc project in Manitoba. The release supports renewed exploration activity but provides no immediate production or supply-impact details for copper prices.

summary: Aston Bay reported new gravity and inversion results at its Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, identifying large, shallow (to ~200m) anomaly targets coincident with historical IP/EM signals and known copper mineralization. summary: Golden Arrow reported Phase 1 drill results from its San Pietro IOCG project in Chile, including 34m at 0.41% Cu and high cobalt intercepts, plus additional shallow cobalt targets. summary: Latin Metals reported rock chip sampling results from its Tillo Copper Project in Peru. summary: Trigon Metals has closed the acquisition of the “Copper King Extension” prospecting licence surrounding its Kombat and Gross Otavi projects in Namibia, after ministerial approval. summary: Rio Tinto will invest CAD 1.4bn to expand its AP60 aluminium smelter at Jonquière, adding 96 AP60 pots and about 160,000 tonnes of primary aluminium capacity per year, alongside commissioning a recycling facility. The company highlights lower-carbon production supported by Quebec.

summary: Vedanta’s Sterlite Copper invited EoIs to support restart and restoration work at its Thoothukudi plant, which has been shut for over five years after pollution-related actions. summary: Hudbay and Copper Mountain report overwhelming shareholder approval for their planned arrangement, subject to final court approval and closing conditions around June 20, 2023. summary: Codelco’s CEO Andre Sougarret will step down by end-August amid operational frustration, accidents, adverse weather and delayed structural projects. Sources warn production may fall short of 2026 copper targets. As the world’s largest copper producer, the leadership and output concerns raise expectations for reduced near-term copper supply.

title: Surge Battery Closes Acquisition with Grid Battery and now owns 100% of Surge Nickel Project
summary: Surge Battery Metals says it has closed its transaction to acquire 100% of the Surge Nickel Project in Northern British Columbia, completing an option agreement with Grid Battery Metals. The press release describes claim ownership and related transaction terms, but provides no near-term production or market-supply impact details for nickel.

title: Hudbay Minerals, Vancouver's Copper Mountain shareholders approve merger
summary: Hudbay Minerals’ and Copper Mountain Mining’s shareholders approved their merger, handing Hudbay the Copper Mountain copper mine in British Columbia. The combined firm becomes Canada’s third-largest copper producer, targeting operating cost reductions and improved efficiencies, with closure expected around June 20 and a potential valuation re-rating.

title: Golden Mile Resources intersects 'spectacular' nickel-cobalt, appoints new MD
summary: Golden Mile Resources announced “spectacular” nickel intersections at its Quicksilver project in Western Australia, including 49m at 1.74% nickel from 30m depth and higher-grade intervals. The company also noted potential for direct shipping from higher-grade zones. The update is sentimentally supportive for nickel markets.

title: Spot Trades of Imported Copper Concentrate Recovered and TCs Rose_SMM
summary: SMM says the Imported Copper Concentrate Index rose to $89.93/mt, with weekly spot trading in copper concentrate picking up. Smelters bought sizable volumes from seaborne ore and Mexico’s Buenavista mine, and July inquiries/offers firmed as TCs increased to around $88–$90/mt.

title: Disruptions to Increase As "Peruvian Armed Protection Period" of Las Bambas Copper Mine Will "Expire" At End-June 0r Early July_SMM
summary: SMM reports the armed protection period for BHP’s Las Bambas copper mine in Peru will expire end-June/early July, with potential community road blockages and strikes likely to recur and disrupt production. It also cites a 100-hour suspension at Escondida in Chile after a fire damaged the ore conveyor.

title: Norsk Hydro : World's first batch of recycled aluminium using hydrogen fueled production
summary: Norsk Hydro says it has produced a first industrial batch of recycled aluminium using hydrogen-fueled production instead of natural gas. The hydrogen switch test, run at a casthouse in Navarra, Spain with Fives, is aimed at decarbonizing energy for recycling and studying effects on metal quality.

title: Norway Firm Produces World's First Aluminum Using Green Hydrogen
summary: Norway is reported to be producing the world’s first aluminum using green hydrogen. The development points to potential reductions in carbon and energy costs versus conventional smelting pathways. Even if ramp-up is limited, it supports bullish sentiment toward aluminium production economics in the near term.

title: Power Nickel Inc.: Power Nickel Announces Broad Nickel Intercepts From Remaining Drill Holes at Nisk
summary: Power Nickel reported new drill results from the Nisk project, including multiple intersections of higher-grade nickel (and accompanying copper) over drill intervals, supporting resource expansion efforts ahead of an NI 43-101 resource estimate expected in late Q3. The company also plans further geophysics and a funded drilling program.

title: Anglo American works with Chinese copper firm on sustainable mining
summary: Anglo American signed a memorandum of understanding with China’s Jiangxi Copper to support more sustainable copper mining, processing and smelting, including renewable energy use and emission reduction. Anglo American highlighted copper’s role in China’s decarbonisation. The piece is partnership-focused without near-term supply or demand disruptions.

title: BMW Group first to source CelestiAL-R, solar aluminium with recycled metal, from EGA
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium says BMW Group is the first customer for CelestiAL-R, EGA’s solar-powered blend of primary and recycled aluminium. BMW has sourced CelestiAL-R since 2023 for electric drivetrain and structural parts. The product lowers carbon intensity and requires longer, more rigorous production and testing.

title: Anglo American To Support Jiangxi Copper's Decarbonisation Efforts
summary: Anglo American said it signed an MoU with China’s Jiangxi Copper to improve assurance over how copper is mined, processed and delivered. The collaboration is aimed at supporting Jiangxi Copper’s decarbonisation and ethical supply-chain goals, aligned with Anglo American’s sustainable mining plan.

title: Red floods near giant Indonesia nickel mine blight farms and fishing grounds – ICSF
summary: Red floods and river overflow in Kolaka district (Southeast Sulawesi) have inundated hundreds of hectares of rice fields near a giant Indonesia nickel mine area. The “red mud” resembles mining tailings from processes used for aluminum extraction and nickel operations. Damage is reported, but no direct output disruption is stated.

title: EGA begins supplying aluminium made using solar energy and recycled metal to BMW
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) says it has begun supplying BMW with CelestiAL-R, an aluminium product made using solar energy and blended with recycled metal. EGA highlights significant CO2 reductions versus typical production and mentions a UAE recycling initiative and plans for a new recycling plant.

title: Drop in coal price to ease nickel production cost this year, Merdeka Copper says
summary: Merdeka Copper Gold says a drop in coal prices should lower electricity and nickel processing costs this year, improving profitability. It also notes high nickel ore costs may ease if nickel prices fall. The immediate market implication is better nickel production economics due to cheaper energy inputs.

title: Drop in coal price to ease nickel production cost this year, Merdeka Copper says
summary: Merdeka Copper Gold said a drop in coal prices should reduce nickel processing costs this year by cutting the cost of electricity used in its rotary kiln electric furnace. It expects easing pressure from high nickel ore costs and better profitability as input costs improve.

title: Mirasol Terminates Agreement to Option Coronación Copper-Gold Project, Chile
summary: Mirasol terminated an option/farm-in agreement with First Quantum and regained 100% control of the Coronación copper-gold project in Chile. The release cites prior exploration funding and describes copper-molybdenum/geochemical targets, with plans to resume community engagement and drilling subject to approvals.

title: Russia's Rusal to build new alumina refinery near St Petersburg -Kommersant
summary: Kommersant/Reuters says Rusal will build a 4.8 Mt/year alumina refinery near St Petersburg to reduce reliance on imported alumina (65% of needs, mostly from China). Recent disruptions, including Ukraine supply halts and Australia’s alumina/bauxite export ban, have pushed Rusal’s first-half aluminium production costs up 33%.

title: Canadian North Resources Inc. Starts the Summer Phase of its 20,000-meter Drill Program at the Ferguson Lake Nickel, Copper, Cobalt, Palladium and Platinum Project in Nunavut, Canada
summary: Canadian North Resources restarted summer diamond drilling at its Ferguson Lake project in Nunavut after a short pause, continuing a planned 20,000-meter program targeting near-surface Ni-Cu-Co-Pd-Pt massive sulphides and PGE disseminated mineralization. Assay results are pending, and there are no operational or supply changes.

title: Copper mine case goes to Montana Supreme Court
summary: A Montana judge ruled that the state environmental agency (DEQ) erred in issuing a mine operating permit for the Black Butte Copper Project. The issue will be argued before the Montana Supreme Court in June, with the case potentially delaying or constraining permitting for the proposed copper mine and affecting near-term supply expectations.

title: Kintavar Announces Maiden Copper and Silver Mineral Resource Estimate at Sherlock Zone, Mitchi Project
summary: Kintavar Exploration reported a NI 43-101 maiden resource estimate for the Sherlock zone at its Mitchi copper-silver project, including Measured+Indicated copper of about 2.99 Mt at ~0.40% Cu, with a shallow open-pit concept and forthcoming PEA. The release is development-stage and not an immediate supply change.

title: Weaker dollar pushes copper back to 5-week high
summary: Copper rallied to a five-week high on a weaker dollar and hopes that China will add economic stimulus after disappointing May output data. LME warehouse stocks fell and warrant cancellations suggest supply could leave the exchange soon, supporting tightness. Aluminium dipped, while nickel rose modestly.

title: Aluminum Prices Flatline As LME Grapples With Russian Inventory
summary: Aluminum prices are range-bound, with the article emphasizing LME’s growing Russian inventory problem: Russian-origin primary aluminium rose to 68% of LME warehouse stocks in May. The LME has not restricted inflows despite sanctions, keeping supply ample and pressuring LME pricing versus CME.

title: Rio Tinto Expands Quebec, Canada, Aluminum Smelter
summary: Rio Tinto will expand its Quebec, Canada aluminum smelter, adding 96 AP60 pots and increasing primary aluminum capacity by about 160,000 metric tonnes per year (full ramp-up by end-2026). The project targets low-carbon “green” aluminum and follows potroom closures at the Arvida smelter site.

title: Canada One Submits Permit to Drill at 100% Owned Copper Dome Project, Princeton, British Columbia
summary: Canada One Mining submitted a drilling permit for its 100% owned Copper Dome copper project in British Columbia, targeting conductivity anomalies similar to the nearby Copper Mountain mine. The company expects permit review by September and possible fall drilling after First Nations consultation.

title: Nevada Copper Provides Positive Operational Update
summary: Nevada Copper said its Pumpkin Hollow underground copper restart is advancing: a key ventilation raise is fully commissioned with fans, development mining is ahead of schedule, and a ~50,000-ton surface ore stockpile is ready for crushing. The company also tested mill/process systems and expects restart processing next quarter.

title: Copper poised for 3rd weekly gain on softer dollar, China stimulus bets
summary: Copper hovered near a five-week high and was set for a third weekly gain as the dollar weakened and investors bet on additional China stimulus. Better U.S. retail-sales data boosted sentiment. The piece also notes rises in Shanghai and LME aluminium and nickel, reflecting supportive demand expectations.

title: Expected Supply Increase And Weak Consumption Will Keep SHFE Aluminium In Check_SMM
summary: SMM reports SHFE and LME aluminium fell modestly. It links the tone to weak domestic real estate/industrial data and tighter macro conditions. Fundamentals cite rising water levels in Yunnan, enabling potential smelter production resumption, but argues short-term output gains are limited and oversupply may build in Q3 amid weak consumption.

title: Glencore sells Cobar copper mine for up to USD1.1 billion
summary: Glencore sold its stake in Cobar Management Pty Ltd, owner of Australia’s Cobar copper mine, receiving USD775 million in cash and USD100 million in shares plus deferred and contingent payments linked in part to future copper prices. Metals Acquisition will run the mine and Glencore will offtake 100% of concentrates.

title: Glencore Sells Cobar Copper Mine for $875 Million Cash-and-Share Consideration
summary: Glencore closed the sale of its 100% stake in the Cobar Management entity that owns the Cobar copper mine in New South Wales. The deal is valued at $875 million (including cash and shares) with Metals Acquisition taking operational control, while Glencore retains offtake of 100% of the copper concentrate produced.

title: Copper Inventory In China Bonded Zone Fell This Week_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM data show China’s bonded-zone copper inventories fell 8,900 mt to 78,900 mt after shipments under warrants ahead of SHFE June delivery. Trade was quiet as import losses exceeded 1,000 yuan/mt. Next week arrivals may rise and inventories could accumulate amid weaker SHFE/LME ratios.

title: Metals Acquisition Limited Closes Purchase of the CSA Copper Mine
summary: Metals Acquisition Limited and Glencore closed the sale of Glencore’s 100% interest in the CSA copper mine in Australia. MAC assumes operational control, with Glencore retaining offtake for copper concentrate. Deal terms include cash plus payments contingent on future copper prices, tightening near-term copper focus.

title: Copper pulls back from five-week high as inventories rise
summary: Copper prices eased from a five-week high as LME data showed rising stocks. Over 16,350 tonnes arrived in warehouses, lifting total inventories by 14%, suggesting improving supply and reducing upside momentum. The piece notes a broader rally driven partly by speculation and soft manufacturing demand.

title: Environmental Court Authorizes Los Andes Copper to Restart Drilling
summary: Chile’s Second Environmental Court authorized Los Andes Copper to restart drilling at its Vizcachitas copper project after finding it met previously imposed conditions. Drilling was suspended by an earlier injunction in 2022. The company says it can proceed with planned technical optimizations following required government filings and approvals.

title: Gold muted on mixed Fed cues, copper boosted by China rate cuts
summary: Gold was muted on mixed Fed rate-hike signals, but copper strengthened. The piece attributes copper’s strong weekly performance to China’s further interest-rate cuts and expectations for an upcoming LPR cut, which markets see as boosting economic activity and China’s demand for resource imports.

title: Romios Gold Resources Inc.: Romios Reports Potential for Porphyry System at Depth on the Kinkaid Gold-Silver-Copper Property in Nevada, USA
summary: Romios reports improved geological understanding at its Kinkaid Nevada property, including alteration zones and skarn packages that may indicate porphyry Cu-Au mineralization at depth. The article cites prior assays with notable copper grades but provides no development or production updates, so near-term copper price impact is likely minimal.

title: Copper Prices: A Forecast on When to Expect a Rise in 2023
summary: The piece discusses copper’s market state and seasonality, noting winter typically brings higher prices and summer lower, with a winter rally usually running from October to February/March. It argues current consolidation may give copper “more room to rally,” while stressing macro and China/US demand risks.

title: Boliden's Ronnskar smelter declares force majeure on copper deliveries after fire
summary: Boliden’s Ronnskar copper smelter in Sweden stopped output after a fire damaged its cell house and issued force majeure on copper deliveries. Resumption timing is uncertain but the firm aims to restart within weeks. With limited available copper inventories in Europe, the disruption is likely to tighten supply and boost prices.

title: Firm owned by tycoons Reuben Brothers sues Trafigura in nickel fraud - source
summary: Hyphen Trading, linked to the Reuben brothers, sued Trafigura over claims said to be tied to an alleged nickel fraud case. Trafigura previously booked a $590 million impairment for purported systematic fraud involving nickel cargoes. The dispute suggests wider fallout and heightened risk concerns for nickel buyers and traders.

title: Anglo American, Jiangxi join hands on responsible copper
summary: Anglo American and China’s Jiangxi Copper signed an MoU to collaborate on responsible copper production, focusing on advanced mining, processing and smelting technologies and emission-reduction initiatives. The article highlights demand in China and notes Anglo American’s ongoing Chile Los Bronces project permitting, without near-term supply changes.

title: The world's most feared investor heads for showdown with the LME
summary: Hedge fund Elliott, led by Paul Singer, is taking the LME to London High Court after the exchange suspended trading and retrospectively canceled nickel trades on March 8 during a sharp nickel rally. Elliott had built bullish nickel call positions that profited before the cancellation, prompting a legal challenge over the LME’s decision-making.

title: Claim of 'irreparable harm' from Noranda bauxite mining 'speculative' – Court of Appeal | News
summary: Jamaica’s Court of Appeal dismissed residents’ bid to keep an injunction against Noranda Jamaica Partners II and New Day Aluminium from mining bauxite under SML 173. The court found the claimed “irreparable harm” unproven and accepted arguments on stronger permit conditions. Mining restart potential could support near-term aluminium-linked supply sentiment.

title: London Metal Exchange fires back in nickel legal row
summary: The London Metal Exchange is defending itself in court against lawsuits claiming it unlawfully cancelled nickel trades during a March 8, 2022 price surge that led to a trading suspension. LME says actions were lawful to prevent clearing-house defaults. The dispute may influence market sentiment, but no new nickel fundamentals are cited.

title: Shanghai alumina contract rises as much as 3.8% on debut
summary: Shanghai alumina futures on the SHFE jumped up to 3.8% on debut, driven by high alumina production costs and improved demand outlook. Analysts cite elevated conversion costs versus the SHFE base and Indonesia’s June 10 bauxite export ban, while smelter activity in Yunnan is expected to lift demand.

title: London copper snaps 3-week rally on higher output, dollar strength
summary: London copper fell after a three-week rally as a firmer U.S. dollar reduced demand and data showed higher China refined copper production and rising LME inventories. SHFE stocks rose less, while aluminium and nickel prices also eased in LME and SHFE trading on the day.

title: London copper slips amid demand uncertainty
summary: London copper fell as investors assessed tepid near-term demand despite record-level production in China. LME stockpiles rose, offset by tight SHFE supplies and limited downside room cited by some analysts. Aluminium and nickel also declined on Monday, reflecting softer overall sentiment across industrial metals.

title: World's first alumina futures with physical delivery starts trading in China-Xinhua
summary: Shanghai Futures Exchange began trading the world’s first physically delivered alumina futures. Eight contracts were traded on the first day, with benchmark pricing reported. Alumina, mainly used for aluminium smelting, is central to aluminium production; the contract is intended to improve risk management amid volatile market prices.

title: ASX HGO: Hillgrove Resources has Australia's newest underground copper mine and is hoping some of the copper glow from BHP and OZ Minerals will shine on it.
summary: Hillgrove Resources is developing Australia’s newest underground copper mine near Kanmantoo, aiming for first copper production in January-March. It highlights lower labor logistics due to proximity to Adelaide and seeks investment following BHP’s $9.6bn OZ Minerals takeover. The news is copper-specific but unlikely to move prices immediately.

title: World's first alumina futures with physical delivery starts trading in China
summary: Shanghai Futures Exchange listed the world’s first physically delivered alumina futures, starting with benchmark trading around 2,665 yuan/ton. Since alumina is the main feedstock for aluminium smelting (about 95% use), the launch may influence aluminium risk pricing and hedging, though no immediate supply or demand disruption is cited.

title: Glencore, Volkswagen Lead $1 Billion Takeover Of Appian Nickel-Copper Mine In Brazil _SMM
summary: Appian Capital Advisory is selling two Brazilian subsidiaries, Atlantic Nickel and Mineração Vale Verde, associated with a nickel-copper mine. The acquisition is funded partly by Glencore and Volkswagen as well as other backers, totaling about $1 billion. The transaction could influence supply expectations but lacks short-term output implications.

title: Glencore, Volkswagen Lead $1 Billion Takeover Of Appian Nickel-Copper Mine In Brazil _SMM
summary: Appian Capital Advisory is selling its Brazilian mine subsidiaries Atlantic Nickel and Mineração Vale Verde to ACG Acquisition, funded in part by Glencore and Volkswagen. The assets are described as a nickel-copper mine in Brazil, linking the transaction to expectations for future supply of both metals.

title: Chile's Codelco must kick-start lithium industry while reviving copper output
summary: Chile’s President Boric tasked Codelco with developing Chile’s long-stalled lithium sector while also reviving copper output after copper prices slid to a 25-year low. Sources expect lithium to be handled largely via negotiations with private partners, while Codelco focuses resources on copper.

title: FOCUS-Chile's Codelco must kick-start lithium industry while reviving copper output
summary: Chile’s President Boric tasked Codelco to lead lithium development while boosting copper output, as copper prices remain near multi-decade lows. Codelco’s internal turmoil after CEO Andre Sougarret’s resignation and uncertainty over whether lithium negotiations will absorb resources cloud near-term copper production prospects.

title: R8m worth of copper cables found buried at Durban scrap dealer's yard
summary: Durban metro police seized about R8m worth of buried copper cables linked to eThekwini municipality, Transnet, Telkom and Prasa during a joint operation. Two suspects were arrested and charged, including for possession of burnt copper cables. Cash was also recovered. The action targets theft, but scale beyond local markets is unclear.

title: China demand angst pressures copper prices
summary: Copper prices fell as traders cited uncertainty over China’s economic stimulus and expectations of weak industrial demand, reinforced by a firmer U.S. dollar. LME copper declined to around $8,546/ton. Support came from sharply lower stocks tracked by Shanghai Futures Exchange, though volumes were thin during holidays.

title: Copper miner Amman Mineral raised $715 mln in Indonesia's biggest IPO this year
summary: Indonesian copper miner Amman Mineral raised about $716 million in the country’s biggest 2023 IPO. The firm plans to use proceeds to pay down debt and complete its copper smelter project in Sumbawa. Shares are due to debut July 5, potentially improving near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Chile's Codelco must kick-start lithium industry while reviving copper output | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Reuters reports President Boric tasked Codelco to expand Chile’s stalled lithium industry, while Codelco also seeks to revive copper output after copper hit a 25-year low. Concerns persist over internal challenges, including CEO Andre Sougarret’s resignation, raising uncertainty about near-term production recovery despite focus on lithium talks.

title: Platinex Receives Exploration Permits for W2 Copper-Nickel-PGE Project and Provides Update on Shining Tree and Heenan Mallard Gold Projects
summary: Platinex announced exploration permits for twelve drill pads and authorization for Phase 1 work on its W2 copper-nickel-PGE project near Ontario’s Ring of Fire. The company frames the permits as enabling efforts to prove Cu-Ni-PGE potential. Assays and drilling results are pending, with no immediate production impact mentioned.

title: HAIB COPPER: LICENCE RENEWAL UPDATE | MarketScreener
summary: Deep-South Resources said Namibia’s Ministry reinstated the Haib Copper licence EPL 3140 as “pending renewal” after a court-ordered process restart. The application is well advanced and a final decision is expected soon. The Ministry invited exploration resumption, though management plans to wait for renewal approval.

title: Platinex Receives Exploration Permits for W2 Copper-Nickel-PGE Project and Provides Update on Shining Tree and Heenan Mallard Gold Projects
summary: Platinex said Ontario issued exploration permits for 12 drill pads at its W2 copper-nickel-PGE project near the Ring of Fire, enabling Phase 1 drilling. The company also updated sampling and permit steps for its gold projects. No production changes or immediate supply figures were provided.

title: HAIB COPPER: LICENCE RENEWAL UPDATE
summary: Deep-South Resources said Namibia has reinstated its Haib copper licence renewal application procedure, with the EPL status set to “pending renewal.” Management expects a final decision in coming weeks, and officials invited resumption of exploration, though the company plans to wait for renewal approval.

title: Drilling commences at Liparamba nickel project in Tanzania
summary: Resource Mining Corporation begins its maiden reverse-circulation drilling program at the Liparamba nickel project in Tanzania, targeting nickel sulphide mineralisation along a southern corridor. The program is expected to run four to five weeks, with results in the next quarter. The news is exploration-focused with no production figures.

title: World's 1st alumina futures with physical delivery starts trading
summary: Shanghai Futures Exchange listed the world’s first physically delivered alumina futures, with Glencore buying in the first trade. Alumina is the key raw material for aluminium smelting, and China dominates alumina production and trade. The launch aims to improve risk management; no immediate production or demand shock is cited.

title: LME readies for court showdown over voided nickel trades
summary: The LME will face a court showdown over voided nickel trades from March 2022, when it annulled about $12 billion in deals after a record nickel price surge. FCA scrutiny preceded the case. Elliott Associates and Jane Street seek damages, while LME argues its actions were lawful and systemic-risk driven.

title: Indonesia braces for possible WTO case over bauxite export ban
summary: Indonesia said it is prepared to defend its bauxite export ban, potentially facing a World Trade Organization case, with China the biggest importer. Because bauxite is the key raw input for alumina and aluminium production, uncertainty over enforcement and legal outcomes may tighten near-term supply expectations and support aluminium prices.

title: Four firms shortlisted in race to buy Zambia's Mopani Copper Mines
summary: Reuters reports four firms have been shortlisted to buy Zambia’s Mopani Copper Mines and smelter complex. Candidates include Zijin and Norinco, plus Sibanye and an ex-Glencore-linked vehicle. Zambia aims to attract investment and potentially boost output, which can improve near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Toronto Stocks Slide; Deep-South Resources Soars on Copper License Renewal Progress in Namibia
summary: Toronto stocks were slightly lower on Monday, while Deep-South Resources surged after reporting that its Namibia copper mine license renewal application is moving forward. The company expects the license to be reinstated within weeks, improving prospects for copper supply development and supporting sentiment toward copper.

title: Opinion: Why copper miners can just keep saying no to takeover offers
summary: The opinion discusses tensions in mining M&A, especially among copper producers. It notes boards’ reluctance to accept low-ball offers and expectations of stronger copper demand from electrification and declining mine supply. Reports that First Quantum and Teck rejected takeover talks underscore likely premium bids and bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Government braces for possible WTO case over ban on bauxite exports
summary: Indonesia is enforcing a bauxite export ban and says it is ready to fight any WTO challenge from China, its biggest bauxite buyer. The ban leaves about 17 million tonnes of bauxite idle due to limited smelter capacity, raising expectations of tighter alumina feedstock availability and potential aluminium price support.

title: World's first alumina futures with physical delivery starts trading in China-- Beijing Review
summary: China’s SHFE began trading the world’s first physically delivered alumina futures on June 19. SHFE reported an initial benchmark around 2,665 yuan/tonne and trades between Glencore and a Chinese seller. As alumina is the main input for aluminium smelting, the listing supports hedging but may not immediately shift prices.

title: China demand concerns pressure copper prices
summary: Copper prices fell on concerns about the lack of clear economic stimulus in China, alongside a firmer U.S. dollar and thin trading during a U.S. holiday. Falling Shanghai Futures Exchange-monitored stocks provided limited support. Aluminium and nickel also dropped on the same day’s demand sentiment.

title: LME had options to avoid quashing nickel trades, hedge fund tells High Court
summary: Reuters reports that Elliott Associates and Jane Street Global Trading are suing the LME over the cancellation of nickel trades on March 8, 2023 after nickel’s benchmark price doubled within hours. They seek $472 million in damages, arguing the exchange had less disruptive options to manage margin calls and market disorder.

title: Indonesia to Ban Copper Exports Once Freeport, Amman Plants Open
summary: The headline says Indonesia plans to ban copper exports after Freeport and Amman’s plants start operations. Such a policy would likely reduce outward shipments and tighten global copper supply expectations in the short term, supporting price gains. The exact impact depends on the ban’s start date and any exemptions.

title: Mayville Engineering Company Announces Definitive Agreement to Acquire Mid-States Aluminum Corp.
summary: Mayville Engineering Company agreed to acquire Mid-States Aluminum, a vertically integrated aluminum extrusions and fabrication manufacturer, for about $96 million. The acquisition is expected to be accretive and expand MEC’s lightweight materials capabilities. The release does not mention aluminum pricing, inventories, or supply disruptions, so near-term market impact appears limited.

title: Copper slips as China rate cuts disappoint
summary: Copper prices slipped on Tuesday as disappointing disappointment with China’s rate cuts hurt industrial-metal sentiment. The softer U.S. dollar provided some support, but copper still fell on the LME. Aluminium and nickel were also down, reflecting weaker broad risk appetite ahead of upcoming Chinese data and technical levels.

title: LME Fueled Nickel Chaos by Lifting Circuit Breakers, Says Elliott
summary: The piece’s headline claims LME trading “chaos” in nickel following the lifting of circuit breakers. Such actions usually reflect stressed market conditions and can amplify volatility, with a risk of short-term bearish price pressure as participants react to unstable liquidity and repricing.

title: Aluminium: The Critical Raw Material Act's Blind Spot – EURACTIV.com
summary: EURACTIV reports criticism that the EU’s Critical Raw Materials Act omits aluminium, despite expected demand growth from EVs, solar and power networks. The piece urges including aluminium in the strategic list to attract investment, support recycling, and stem EU primary smelter closures, implying improved supply outlook.

title: PAN GLOBAL COMMENCES DRILLING AT ROMANA WEST COPPER-TIN-SILVER TARGET IN THE ESCACENA PROJECT, SPAIN
summary: Pan Global Resources began diamond drilling at the Romana West Cu-Sn-Ag target within Spain’s Escacena Project. The company cites gravity, IP chargeability, and pXRF soil copper-tin anomalies supporting potential westward extension of the La Romana mineralization. Assays for additional holes are pending; no production changes are reported.

title: Centaurus acquires nickel offtake rights from Vale
summary: Centaurus Metals agreed with Vale Base Metals to acquire offtake rights for the Jaguar nickel sulphide project in Brazil. Vale will waive its rights in exchange for higher net operating royalties linked to nickel sulphate and nickel concentrate. Centaurus cites rising battery-material demand and expects improved control over offtake options, mainly affecting nickel, with no clear immediate supply impact.

title: Indonesia To Stop Exports Of Copper Concentrates In 2024
summary: Indonesia’s President Joko Widodo said the country will stop exporting copper concentrates in 2024 once major domestic smelters (Freeport Indonesia and Amman Mineral) begin processing, targeting domestic cathode production. Indonesia recently allowed continued concentrate exports until smelter startups, implying near-term tightening for copper supply flows.

title: Rio Tinto (RIO) invests to strengthen copper supply in US
summary: Rio Tinto will invest about $498 million in its Kennecott copper operation to expand underground development and infrastructure, plus $300 million to rebuild the smelter and additional refinery upgrades. Management says the work supports stronger U.S. copper supply and processing capacity, with incremental mined output ramping after 2024.

title: Rio Tinto invests to strengthen copper supply in US
summary: Rio Tinto will invest about $498 million in Kennecott’s Utah operations, expanding underground development and upgrading smelting and refining capacity to strengthen US copper supply. The North Rim Skarn ramp-up begins in 2024, with further copper from Lower Commercial Skarn. A major smelter rebuild is also underway.

title: Rio Tinto Approves $498 Million Investment in Utah Copper Operation
summary: Rio Tinto approved a $498 million investment to develop underground infrastructure at its Kennecott (North Rim Skarn) copper operation in Utah. The project is set to begin production in 2024 and ramp over two years, adding about 250,000 metric tons of mined copper over the next decade, alongside earlier underground expansions.

title: Rio Tinto to Invest Almost $1 Billion in Utah Copper Mine
summary: Rio Tinto said it will invest almost $1 billion in its Utah copper mine. The announcement is tied to future copper production capacity, but such capex does not usually change near-term mine supply or inventories immediately, limiting likely prompt price effects.

title: Rio Tinto Invests In Kennecott Operation To Strengthen Copper Supply In US
summary: Rio Tinto said it will invest $498 million in its Kennecott mine near Salt Lake City to develop underground infrastructure (North Rim Skarn). Production is due to start in 2024 and ramp over two years, targeting about 250,000 tonnes of additional mined copper over the following decade, strengthening U.S. supply.

title: Hudbay Minerals Inc.: Hudbay Completes Acquisition of Copper Mountain to Create a Premier Americas-Focused Copper Producer
summary: Hudbay Minerals says it has completed its court-approved acquisition of Copper Mountain, making it a wholly owned subsidiary. The combined portfolio is positioned as a major Americas-focused copper producer with expected 2023 copper output above 150,000 tonnes and estimated $30m annual operating synergies, enhancing cash flows and copper price exposure.

title: Field Work Underway Ahead of Drilling on the Telegraph Copper-Gold
summary: MTB Metals has begun field work to prepare drilling at its Telegraph porphyry copper-gold project in British Columbia’s Golden Triangle, using geophysics, hyperspectral analysis, and on-site XRF to rank targets. The update is exploratory and does not indicate production disruptions or supply changes, implying limited near-term price impact.

title: Co. On Way To Supplying Nickel, Cobalt to EV Market
summary: Australia’s Alliance Nickel says its NiWest nickel-cobalt project in Western Australia is positioned to meet EV battery demand. The report highlights high-grade resources, improving drilling and planning toward production, and offtake agreements (including Stellantis) that support future nickel sulfate sales, though financing remains a hurdle.

title: China's Stimulus Measures Prop Up Copper Prices
summary: China’s stimulus—marked by central bank interest-rate reductions and expectations of further infrastructure and property-support measures—helped reverse bearish momentum in copper. The copper index rebounded after late-May lows, aided by a weaker U.S. dollar. However, the uptrend needs confirmation as LME inventories remain elevated.

title: Decarbonization must be across value chain, not just copper competition, Aurubis CEO says
summary: Aurubis CEO argues decarbonization must cover the whole copper value chain and says copper demand is rising due to electrification and transition technologies. Market sources expect low-carbon copper could trade at a premium, with producers already receiving premiums. He downplays a permanent “green premium,” but demand support remains bullish.

title: LME cancelled nickel trades to 'save' Tsingshan, London court told
summary: A London High Court hearing revisits the LME’s decision to cancel $12 billion of nickel trades on March 8, 2022 during extreme price volatility tied to a Tsingshan-related squeeze. Plaintiffs claim the cancellations unlawfully protected specific participants; LME cites margin and systemic-risk prevention.

title: Chile's Antofagasta seeks copper mine extension with $1.2 billion investment
summary: Antofagasta is seeking regulatory approval to extend operations of its copper mine by 26 years, with a $1.2 billion investment for a base metals project. The firm says the request would not change previously approved production capacity. Its environmental permit expires in 2025 and closure is planned afterward.

title: London Metal Exchange faces £370m legal showdown over nickel debacle
summary: The LME faces major legal claims over cancelling nickel trades after prices surged about 250% in two days in March 2022. The exchange froze billions of dollars in trades and shut nickel for over a week, citing margin and systemic risk. Ongoing legal and regulatory scrutiny may weigh on nickel sentiment.

title: Mallee Resources reports on Avebury Nickel Mine progress | The Advocate
summary: Mallee Resources reports that clay-like minerals disrupted ore processing at its Avebury nickel mine, reducing concentrate production rates in April and May and causing downtime in the tertiary crusher. Repairs are complete and June processing is at or above targeted concentrate output. Additional filtration capacity is planned to sustain nameplate production.

title: Rio Tinto allocates $920M to Utah's Kennecott for underground copper mining
summary: Rio Tinto plans a $920 million investment in the Kennecott Copper Mine, including $498 million for underground development, $300 million for the smelter rebuild, and upgrades to the refinery and molybdenum flotation. Management says underground production will start in 2024 and deliver about 250,000 tons over 10 years, supporting U.S. copper supply.

title: Rio Tinto invests US$498 million to boost US copper supply
summary: Rio Tinto plans a US$498 million upgrade at its Kennecott operation in Utah to expand underground development at the North Rim Skarn. The company targets copper production startup in 2024 and expects additional mined copper alongside existing operations. It also funds smelter and refinery upgrades to improve processing.

title: Rio Tinto makes $800m bet on US copper mining
summary: Rio Tinto plans to invest more than $800 million in Utah to raise copper production and processing. The miner will expand the Kennecott underground mine, upgrade processing, and rebuild a smelter near Salt Lake City. The company frames the spending around rising demand and tight copper supply.

title: China's Innovation New Material Falls on Plan to Build USD191 Million Aluminum Alloy Plant in Vietnam
summary: Innovation New Material said it will invest nearly USD191 million to build and operate an aluminum alloy sections plant in Vietnam via a local unit. The project targets Southeast Asia 3C electronics demand and leverages low labor and logistics. Shares fell 2.3%, while capacity growth could influence aluminum alloy supply expectations.

title: Yukon government raised red flags about copper mine before owner abandoned site
summary: The Yukon government issued warnings after inspecting Minto Metals’ MNTO-X copper mine and finding inadequate contaminated-water storage and multiple spills. Minto abruptly ceased operations in May, leaving the site to the territory for water treatment and cleanup. The shutdown raises near-term copper supply concerns as production stops.

title: NorthWest Copper Identifies Kwanika Central Zone Transfer
summary: NorthWest Copper announced it identified a “Transfer Target” near the Kwanika Central Zone based on reinterpretation of geophysical surveys and geological models. The company says the target could add shallow, open-pittable copper-gold mineralization and will be tested with a small number of relatively shallow drill holes.

title: Fading China stimulus hopes and stronger dollar dent copper
summary: Copper prices in London fell as optimism faded over the scale of potential Chinese stimulus to spur demand for power and construction metals. The stronger US dollar ahead of Fed-related remarks further weighed on dollar-priced metals. LME copper stocks declined. Aluminium also dropped on weak technicals and falling inventories.

title: POSCO to Build 1.5 tln-won Nickel, Precursor Factories in S. Korea with China's CNGR
summary: POSCO plans to build large-scale nickel and nickel-precursor factories in South Korea together with China’s CNGR, with a stated investment scale of roughly 1.5 trillion won. The project signals expanded nickel-precursor supply and processing capacity, which can be supportive for near-term nickel market sentiment.

title: LME dropped the ball in Asia trading as nickel rocketed -lawyer
summary: A Reuters report says a lawyer told London court that the LME had no senior management monitoring during Asian hours when nickel prices surged, before cancelling billions of dollars of trades after nickel doubled within hours in March 2022. Hedge funds seek large damages, highlighting disputed LME risk and oversight actions tied to nickel volatility.

title: Emerita Intersects 13.0 Meters Grading 0.2% Copper; 3.6%
summary: Emerita Resources reported additional drilling assay results from the La Romanera deposit at its Iberian Belt West project, including intervals with 0.2% to 0.6% copper over significant drillhole lengths. The company is expanding the deposit at depth via ongoing drilling, but no immediate production or supply disruption is noted.

title: Crown Holdings, Inc.: Crown Holdings: Aluminum Beverage Can Manufacturers Ardagh Metal Packaging and Crown Holdings Fund Additional Can Capture Grants at Recycling Sortation Facilities
summary: Ardagh and Crown Holdings fund additional grants for aluminum can-capture equipment at U.S. material recovery facilities. The program targets improved recovery of used beverage cans that are valuable in recycling. Reported results indicate materially higher annual can capture, supporting more recycled aluminum supply into canmaking.

title: Marimaca Copper Corp.: Marimaca Announces C$20 Million Strategic Investment from Mitsubishi Corporation
summary: Marimaca Copper announced a C$20 million strategic equity investment from Mitsubishi to fund the Marimaca flagship copper project in Chile, including work toward a definitive feasibility study and permitting. Mitsubishi also highlighted the project’s potential to add copper supply in the near term, but no output changes are stated.

title: Crown Holdings: Aluminum Beverage Can Manufacturers Ardagh Metal Packaging and Crown Holdings Fund Additional Can Capture Grants at Recycling Sortation Facilities
summary: Ardagh Metal Packaging and Crown Holdings are funding additional grants to install aluminum can capture equipment at MRF recycling facilities. Performance data shows nearly 140 million aluminum beverage cans captured annually, improving recycled aluminum availability and carbon savings. The program targets better sorting to reduce missorted can losses.

title: New copper supply offset by multiple hits to existing operations
summary: Copper is supported by supply tightness: new mine output (DRC, Peru, Chile) is being offset by operational and geotechnical problems at existing operations. ICSG forecasts further deficits in 2023, while Chile and Peru face production risks from ore quality, water constraints, and unrest. China/financial stimulus is cited as demand support.

title: Roundup: Indonesia pushes ahead with bauxite export ban despite controversy-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia will keep its bauxite ore export ban despite controversy and potential lawsuits. The policy aims to force downstream processing, but only four of 12 targeted bauxite smelters are operating, leading miners to cut output. The ban may reduce exports while adding value via refining capacity.

title: Rio Tinto reveals $918m investment in Kennecott copper mine in US
summary: Rio Tinto disclosed a $918m investment in its Kennecott copper mine near Salt Lake City, funding underground development, smelter rebuilding, and refinery upgrades. The North Rim Skarn project is set to start in 2024 with ramp-up over two years, adding additional mined copper alongside existing operations.

title: Indonesia to stop exporting copper concentrates in 2024 | World
summary: Indonesia plans to halt exports of copper concentrates in 2024 but has advised Freeport Indonesia and Amman Mineral to continue shipping until their new smelters start in May. With Indonesia also producing large volumes of nickel and expanding processing for batteries, the move suggests near-term tightening for copper and nickel feed, supporting prices.

title: Nuts and bolts of the LME's canceled nickel trades legal case
summary: Reuters details a legal case involving the LME’s cancellation of nickel trades on March 8, 2022 after nickel prices surged above $100,000/t. Elliott and Jane Street sue for damages, while the LME argues margin-call risks. The piece explains margin mechanics and default handling at LME Clear.

title: Talon Metals seeks regulatory permit for Minnesota nickel mine
summary: Talon Metals applied to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for an environmental review of its proposed Tamarack underground nickel mine. The project targets boosting U.S. nickel supply for battery use, reducing reliance on China and Russia. Tesla has an initial U.S. nickel supply deal with Talon.

title: Nuts and bolts of the LME's cancelled nickel trades legal case
summary: Reuters reports Elliott Associates and Jane Street suing the LME over its March 2022 cancellation of nickel trades during a spike above $100,000/t. The piece details how LME Clear margin calls and defaults work, including variation margin timing and member/clearing default procedures, framing the cause of the nickel benchmark disruption.

title: Sarnia man sentenced for role in $700K copper-wire theft back in jail for drug possession
summary: A Sarnia man involved in a large copper-wire theft at Sarnia Bay Marina, valued around $700,000, is back in jail after pleading guilty to meth possession. The theft required months of repairs, but the report does not indicate wider supply impacts that would move copper prices.

title: Roundup: Indonesia pushes ahead with bauxite export ban despite controversy
summary: Indonesia will keep pushing a bauxite ore export ban introduced June 10, despite controversy and possible legal challenges. With only four of 12 targeted bauxite smelters operating, miners may cut output. The policy restricts bauxite feedstock supply while aiming to increase downstream processing and investment in refining capacity.

title: Indian bands in Similkameen Valley share public grievance with Copper Mountain Mine acquisition
summary: Upper and Lower Similkameen bands say negotiations broke down over Hudbay’s acquisition of Copper Mountain Mining’s Copper Mountain Mine near Hedley. They cite serious impacts on the Similkameen River and say the deal proceeded without updated agreements, potentially raising friction, compliance concerns, and near-term operational uncertainty for the mine.

title: Nickel mining proposal in Minnesota could help produce Tesla batteries
summary: Minnesota’s DNR is reviewing Talon Metals’ proposed Tamarack Nickel Mine, an underground project that would produce nickel potentially used in Tesla battery supply under an MoU. The mine would transport ore to North Dakota for processing. The proposal still requires an Environmental Impact Statement.

title: Mining Stock News: Talon Metals (TSX: TLO) Submits Environmental Assessment Worksheet for Proposed Underground Nickel Mine to Produce Domestic Supply of Minerals for US Battery Supply Chain
summary: Talon Metals submitted an Environmental Assessment Worksheet to start Minnesota’s environmental review for the Tamarack underground nickel mine, including mine design changes and planned rail loading and water treatment. The project is linked to domestic battery supply inputs. The news is early-stage permitting, offering limited immediate supply impact.

title: Proposed MN nickel mine begins environmental review
summary: Talon Metals filed with Minnesota regulators to start an environmental review for its proposed underground nickel mine, aimed at supplying nickel for Tesla battery production. The project also received a DOE grant for an ore processing plant in North Dakota. Opposition cites possible water and community impacts, adding timeline uncertainty.

title: Montana Supreme Court hears arguments on Black Butte Copper project permit
summary: Montana’s Supreme Court hears arguments on whether the state improperly issued a permit for the Black Butte Copper Project. Environmental groups cite inadequate analysis of mining impacts, especially tailings and water-quality risks. The mine’s operator says DEQ conducted extensive review and plans safety-focused tailings design. Legal uncertainty could delay mine activity.

title: Mitsubishi Corporation Announces New Participation in the Marimaca Copper Project in Chile
summary: Mitsubishi Corporation plans a CAD20 million strategic investment in the Marimaca Copper Project in Chile, supporting feasibility work and environmental permitting. The project could produce copper cathode from oxide resources. While production is expected around 2030, the funding and development momentum are supportive for copper supply expectations.

title: Copper: It's Now Or Never - FNArena.com
summary: A copper-focused technical report (Comex futures) argues conditions may “revert to bullish” if the market holds support around $3.54 and breaks and sustains above resistance near $4.38. It warns a loss of $3.54 could send prices lower toward $3.16, but the base case favors upside.

title: Mitsubishi Corporation Announces New Participation In The Marimaca Copper Project In Chile
summary: Mitsubishi Corporation said it is taking new participation in the Marimaca copper project in Chile. The update is directly tied to copper project development and funding, which can modestly influence near-term sentiment around future copper supply, though the impact is likely gradual rather than immediate.

title: Copper eases in thin Chinese holiday trade
summary: Copper prices eased in thin Chinese holiday trade as China had no fresh stimulus news and its market was closed for June 22-23. Reuters notes 3-month copper down while aluminium and nickel were slightly higher, with traders citing disappointment versus expectations and some support from a weaker dollar.

title: For EV batteries, lithium iron phosphate narrows the gap with nickel, cobalt
summary: Reuters reports accelerating adoption of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) EV batteries as automakers target lower-cost vehicles. LFP is cheaper than nickel- and cobalt-based chemistries, and new U.S. production commitments support supply diversification. The shift implies reduced future need for nickel inputs, weighing on nickel demand sentiment.

title: Max Resource : Reports High-Grade Copper & Silver Assays from AM-7, at the CESAR Project
summary: Max Resource Corp. reported channel-sample assays from the newly identified AM-7 target at its CESAR copper-silver project in Colombia, including multiple intervals above 4% and up to 18.3% copper. The company describes stacked horizons and ongoing additional sampling, which improves exploration prospects for future copper supply.

title: Copper rises on weaker dollar and falling inventory
summary: Copper prices rose in tepid Chinese holiday trade as a weaker dollar and falling LME inventories supported tight supply. Three-month copper gained on the London Metal Exchange. Aluminium and nickel were also higher, reflecting broadly supportive currency and inventory dynamics despite concerns over insufficient Chinese stimulus.

title: Analysis: For EV batteries, lithium iron phosphate narrows the gap with nickel, cobalt
summary: Reuters discusses growing adoption of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) for EV batteries as automakers seek cheaper options. The piece notes LFP is less expensive than cobalt and nickel and can be sourced in North America with lower logistics costs, implying potential substitution away from nickel-linked battery demand.

title: Available LME copper stocks fall to the lowest since 2021
summary: LME copper stocks total 80,400 tonnes, down to the lowest since 2021, with 62.5% set aside or cancelled for delivery. Fresh warrant cancellations reached 19,200 tonnes, mainly in New Orleans. Such cancellations can signal tighter near-term availability and boosted benchmark copper prices by 0.8%.

title: LME failed to probe Tsingshan before nickel chaos, London court hears
summary: A London court heard that the LME did not investigate Tsingshan’s large nickel positions before the March 2022 nickel surge and subsequent cancellation of billions of dollars of trades. LME says voiding deals prevented defaults and systemic risk, while claimants seek $472 million in damages.

title: Copper hits seven-week peak as LME stocks plunge
summary: Copper rose to a seven-week peak after LME-registered warehouse stocks plunged to the lowest since 2021. Cancelled warrants reduced available material, reinforcing tightness. Chinese SFE-monitored inventories also fell. The weaker dollar added support, while traders cited bullish near-term targets amid constrained supply.

title: Proposed nickel mine in northern Minnesota moving forward with first phase of EIS process
summary: Minnesota’s DNR is advancing the first phase of the EIS process for the proposed Tamarack Nickel Mine by Talon Metals, with ore processed in North Dakota. The project remains pre-permit and not yet producing. Because production timing is uncertain, it is unlikely to move nearby nickel prices materially.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay and American West Metals Announce 8% Copper Intersected at the Storm Copper Project, Nunavut
summary: Aston Bay and American West report additional reverse-circulation drilling at the Storm Copper Project, Nunavut, intersecting thick, high-grade near-surface copper mineralization, including up to about 8% Cu. The company says results expand the 4100N Zone and support continued drilling and resource confidence, boosting copper-focused sentiment.

title: Morgan Stanley says sell this aluminum giant
summary: Morgan Stanley downgraded Alcoa (a major global aluminum producer) to underweight, citing sluggish global growth, a stronger dollar, and concerns about weaker commodity demand. The firm also adjusted its outlook for U.S. and global growth, expecting continued pressure on mining equities and related aluminum fundamentals.

title: Drilling Underway at Pacific Ridge's Kliyul Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration says drilling has started on its 100% owned Kliyul copper-gold project in British Columbia, planning 7,000 m of diamond drilling to expand mineralized zones and test multiple porphyry targets. The release is exploration-focused with no immediate production or supply impact for copper markets.

title: Canada Nickel Reports Encouraging Initial Metallurgical Results from its Texmont Project, Announces Consolidation of Texmont Region
summary: Canada Nickel announced encouraging initial metallurgical test results from its Texmont project, showing high nickel recoveries (79–84%) and high-grade nickel concentrates (18–28%), alongside strong cobalt recoveries. The company also consolidated additional claims in the Texmont region and plans further metallurgical testing toward a PEA later in 2023.

title: Indonesia to stop exporting copper concentrates in 2024
summary: Indonesia’s President said the country will stop exporting copper concentrates in 2024 once Freeport Indonesia and Amman Mineral complete smelters and begin local processing. Current guidance allows exports until their new smelters operational timing, reducing near-term copper concentrate availability and supporting copper prices.

title: Copper hits two-month peak on LME stocks and weak dollar
summary: Copper hit a two-month peak as LME-registered warehouse inventories fell sharply to the lowest since 2021 and cancelled warrants reduced available material. The move was reinforced by the dollar near a one-month low, improving commodity appeal. China inventories also declined. Aluminium and nickel rose modestly alongside copper.

title: Omico develops modern copper mine at Omitiomire
summary: Omico Mining is developing the Omitiomire copper project in Namibia, reporting a 95.8 Mt resource at 0.59% Cu and progressing metallurgical testing for chloride leaching and SX-EW refining. The article cites a feasibility study underway and design work completed, improving expectations for future copper supply.

title: What really happened the night the nickel market broke
summary: The piece recounts the events around March 7, when nickel prices surged sharply and the market later “broke,” leading LME CEO Matthew Chamberlain to write a late-night memo to the UK financial regulator. It focuses on the nickel market’s extreme volatility, but the excerpt doesn’t show the net direction after the break.

title: LME casts doubt on Elliott's nickel damages claim in judicial review
summary: Elliott and Jane Street seek damages totaling about $471.7 million, claiming the LME unlawfully cancelled nickel trades on March 8, 2022 when nickel prices surged above $100,000/mt. The LME argues cancellations prevented systemic risk from $19.7 billion margin calls, and disputes Elliott’s loss calculations and reference pricing.

title: Gold Stock News: Drilling Underway at Pacific Ridge's (TSXV: PEX) Kliyul Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration reports diamond drilling is underway at its Kliyul copper-gold project in British Columbia, planning 7,000 m to expand the Kliyul Main Zone and test new porphyry targets. The release includes prior copper-equivalent intersections but no operational changes to near-term copper supply.

title: Proposed Minnesota nickel mine begins environmental review — Would supply Tesla if approved
summary: Talon Metals filed for an environmental review to start its proposed Tamarack underground nickel mine, tied to EV-battery supply plans with Tesla and supported by a U.S. DOE grant for processing. The review faces environmental concerns and parallels delays to other Minnesota copper-nickel projects, making near-term supply impact uncertain.

title: Anglesey Mining Could Be Pulling Out Some Very Very Significant Copper Intersections
summary: Anglesey Mining is reported to be pulling out “very very significant” copper intersections. The news is framed around promising exploration results, which typically boosts market sentiment for copper supply prospects, though it does not by itself guarantee production timing or volume in the near term.

title: QC Copper and Gold Inc: QC Copper Updates on Opemiska Resource
summary: QC Copper and Gold reports it is nearing completion of the Mineral Resource Estimate for the Opemiska Copper Project in Quebec. The company cites extensive drilling and assay work and says the update may not be published this quarter. The release is mainly development-oriented without any immediate production or trade impact.

title: $20M CopperString contract and vanadium battery trial announced | North Queensland Register
summary: Queensland’s government announced $20m in early works for CopperString 2.0, a 1,100-km transmission line linking the North West minerals province to the grid, plus a vanadium battery trial. The transmission build is likely to boost near-term copper demand expectations, while broader grid investment supports sentiment.

title: Copper on track for first weekly fall in four as dollar firms
summary: Reuters reports London copper is on track for its first weekly fall in four, with the three-month contract down around 0.5% after a firmer dollar and hawkish central-bank signals boosted recession fears. Nickel and aluminium are also flagged for their biggest weekly declines, reflecting broader base-metal pressure.

title: Copper set for first weekly fall in four as dollar jumps
summary: Copper was set for its first weekly decline in four weeks as the dollar jumped, making dollar-priced metals costlier. LME three-month copper fell, while nickel also dropped and aluminium slid. The moves were driven by hawkish central-bank comments, risk aversion, and weak China consumer stimulus expectations post-COVID lockdown slowdown.

title: LME faced 'death spiral' with as many as a dozen firms at risk of default amid nickel chaos: lawyer
summary: The article’s title says the LME faced a “death spiral,” with up to a dozen firms at risk of default during a period of “nickel chaos.” Counterparty stress and reduced market confidence can worsen liquidity and elevate risk aversion, weighing on short-term nickel pricing expectations.

title: Nerves on edge as exchanges, funds await ruling in LME nickel case
summary: Exchanges and funds are awaiting a court decision in a $472 million lawsuit against the LME over the cancellation of $12 billion in nickel trades following the March 2022 nickel surge. Outcomes could shape confidence in London’s market governance and crisis actions, keeping nickel sentiment volatile until a ruling in at least a month.

title: Copper heads for weekly drop on hawkish rate hikes, strong dollar
summary: Copper prices are set for a weekly drop as hawkish rate-hike expectations and a stronger U.S. dollar weigh on growth-sensitive commodities. LME stocks keep falling, but price weakness dominates. Aluminium and nickel are also down on the week, indicating broad risk-off pressure across industrial metals.

title: Reheating The Economy: Kosovo Nickel Plant Fires Up After 20-Month Closure
summary: Kosovo’s Newco Ferronikeli ferronickel plant restarted June 21 after a 20-month closure caused by soaring European energy prices. The facility had been idle since Oct 2021, with partial wage payments during downtime. The restart boosts near-term nickel production and exporter activity, though environmental concerns remain.

title: Copper Needs to Be Classified as Critical Metal
summary: Billionaire mining investor Robert Friedland urges the U.S. to classify copper as a critical material, citing the IRA’s China-reduction goals, lack of new U.S. mines, and rising net-import reliance. The piece highlights warnings of an upcoming copper deficit from majors and notes the EU already classifies copper as critical.
