Historical production included copper and some nickel.

title: City of Casa Grande Approves Rezoning for Arizona Sonoran Copper's (TSX:ASCU) MainSpring Property, Company Acquires Mineral Exploration Permit
summary: Casa Grande approved industrial rezoning for Arizona Sonoran Copper’s MainSpring Property north parcel and the company secured a 2.5-acre mineral exploration permit from Arizona State Lands. These steps allow drilling and exploration at the Parks/Salyer deposit, supporting expectations for incremental copper resource growth at the Cactus Project.

title: Barrick earmarks $2 billion for copper 'super pit' in Zambia
summary: Barrick plans to spend nearly $2 billion to expand Zambia’s Lumwana copper mine into a “super pit,” targeting about 240,000 tonnes of annual copper output and doubling prior production. The project is intended to raise Zambia’s declining output. Investment commitments in Zambia bolster copper supply expectations.

title: American Producers of Aluminum Extrusions File Trade Petitions to Combat Illegal and Unfair Dumping and Subsidies from 15 Countries, Wiley Rein LLP Reports
summary: U.S. aluminum extrusion producers and the USW filed antidumping and countervailing duty petitions against imports from 15 countries, alleging high dumping margins and government subsidies. The Commerce Department is set to decide on initiating investigations, with USITC injury findings later, potentially leading to duties that raise import costs.

title: Sibanye CEO says Zambia's Mopani Copper Mines investment not 'onerous'
summary: Sibanye Stillwater said the investment needed to expand Zambia’s Mopani Copper Mines is not “onerous,” citing about $1 billion over four to five years. Mopani’s expected output increase to around 200,000 tonnes per year by 2027 supports market expectations for copper supply, despite ongoing sale processes.

title: Nickel from Ring of Fire could supply half million cars
summary: Wyloo’s CEO says Ring of Fire nickel could supply up to 500,000 EVs to North America, highlighting strong nickel demand for batteries and Canada’s lower-carbon nickel processing. The project’s ambitious 2030 timeline reduces immediate supply influence, keeping near-term nickel price impact limited.

title: Copper Falls to Lowest Since May as Traders Mull Dollar Strength
summary: Copper prices dropped to their lowest level since May as traders considered expectations for a stronger U.S. dollar. The move suggests near-term downside pressure, as currency strength can weigh on dollar-priced metals demand and pricing sentiment. No direct nickel or aluminium supply-demand details were provided in the excerpt.

title: Goldman Sachs: China's Demand For Oil And Copper Is Booming
summary: Goldman Sachs reports China’s demand for major commodities is rising robustly, highlighting copper. China’s copper demand is up 8% year-on-year and “green copper” demand rose 71% in July, driven by renewables, grid, and property completions. The update reinforces expectations of stronger near-term copper demand.

title: Commodities : Copper heads for fourth straight fall on high inventory - Today
summary: Copper is set for a fourth straight daily fall as rising LME inventories weigh on sentiment, while trading volumes remain thin because China is on holiday. Reuters reports three-month copper down 0.2%. Aluminium and nickel also declined modestly, reinforcing a cautious near-term tone despite earlier intraday gains.

title: Battery metals: BHP braces for Indonesian supply surge as nickel hits two-year low
summary: BHP says EV makers are not paying a “green premium” for sustainably mined Australian nickel while Indonesian laterite nickel volumes are unexpectedly large. This additional Indonesian supply has pushed nickel to a two-year low. BHP plans to invest in sulphide geology but anticipates further Indonesian nickel growth.

title: Ford, GM, Pepsi, Ball Corp., Rivian, SunPower, and 8 more leading companies call for federal investment in clean aluminum
summary: Ford, GM, Pepsi, Ball Corp., Rivian, SunPower and others urge the DOE to invest IRA funds to revive U.S. primary aluminum production. They cite electricity-price volatility, lack of low-cost power and six smelters “on the brink,” and warn demand will rise with clean-energy buildout, implying supportive supply-side expectations for aluminium.

title: Commodities : Copper set for 4th straight fall on high inventory, firm dollar - Today
summary: Copper is poised for a fourth straight session of declines as LME inventories rise and the dollar stays firm, pressuring dollar-priced metals. Aluminium also fell. Nickel slipped and the piece cites a deeper supply surplus from production ramp-ups in Indonesia and China, reinforcing bearish sentiment across base metals.

title: Sumitomo Metal sees global nickel supply surplus widening in 2024
summary: Sumitomo Metal Mining said the global nickel market should remain in surplus in 2024, with the surplus widening to 36,000 metric tons from 24,000 this year. The view is based on Indonesia’s growing NPI output and rising supply outpacing demand, despite expected increases for stainless steel and batteries.

title: Noronex stretches out Namibian copper project
summary: Noronex extended mineralisation at its Fiesta copper prospect in Namibia’s Kalahari copper belt, reporting multiple intercepts with meaningful copper grades and awaiting further assays. The company then moved to a nearby Blowhole target near the Botswana border, highlighting the belt’s prospectivity amid current weak sentiment and talk of future copper tightness.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Reports Gold Assay Results from the Childs Aldwinkle Breccia at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona
summary: Faraday Copper reported new gold fire-assay results and re-assayed copper from the Childs Aldwinkle breccia at its Copper Creek project in Arizona, including examples of intercepts with both copper and gold. The news mainly supports exploration/resource development and metallurgical testing, not immediate changes to copper supply or demand.

title: Australia's Nickel Industries' HPAL smelter plan to enter FID stage soon - Companies
summary: Australia’s Nickel Industries plans to enter final investment decision within weeks on an Indonesia Morowali HPAL smelter producing MHP, nickel sulfate and nickel cathode. With ~72,000 tonnes annual MHP capacity and large investment, the project strengthens expectations for future nickel output, supporting nickel market sentiment.

title: OMC inks pact with Hindalco to supply raw minerals to alumina refinery
summary: Odisha Mining Corporation (OMC) signed a long-term raw material linkage pact with Hindalco to supply feedstock for a planned two-million-ton alumina refinery in Rayagada. The state also has a mineral linkage policy and the project is part of major aluminum-industry investment, supporting alumina availability expectations.

title: Aurubis to Keep European Copper Premium at Record High Next Year
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports that Aurubis expects to maintain the European copper premium at record highs next year. A higher, sustained premium typically signals tighter regional availability and stronger demand/supply balance for physical copper, which can support copper prices through the near-term pricing window.

title: With copper plant's maintenance on course, Thoothukudi awaits new dawn
summary: Sterlite Copper at Thoothukudi is progressing with maintenance requirements, evacuating gypsum and preparing for possible restart pending Supreme Court proceedings. The closure has already tightened India’s copper supply and raised costs. A favourable ruling could restore output and improve near-term copper balance and sentiment.

title: AI Technology Identifies Multiple Nickel-Copper-PGE Sulphide Targets at QNI's Ducros Project
summary: Québec Nickel Corp. reports AI-driven exploration results at its Ducros property, generating multiple new nickel-sulphide (and Ni-Cu-PGE) targets and updating geological interpretations to guide further work. The company also continues deep drilling at the Fortin Sill target, aiming to extend mineralization at depth.

title: Copper drifts lower on disquiet about China as inventories rise
summary: Copper fell for a fourth straight session as investors sold on worries over China’s demand momentum, uncertainty about interest rates and growth, and rising LME stocks. The piece also cites CTA-driven selling that pressured aluminium and nickel, while nickel/lead saw losses and nickel’s surplus outlook worsened sentiment.

title: Bonnell Aluminum Commenting on Recent Trade Filing from Aluminum Extruders Coalition and United Steelworkers Union
summary: Bonnell Aluminum, through support for the Aluminum Extruders Coalition and USW, backed October 4 antidumping and countervailing duty petitions against aluminum extrusion imports from multiple countries. The filing aims to curb dumped and subsidized volumes harming U.S. extruders, potentially reducing import competition and supporting aluminum market conditions.

title: Marula Mining says Kinusi assays show high-grade copper
summary: Marula Mining said assay results from the Kinusi copper mine confirm high-grade copper at the Sasimo prospect. Reported grades range up to 15.48% copper, with an average of 2.68% across 51 samples. The results enable phase 2 exploration, including geophysics and mine planning.

title: Western Copper and Gold : October 2023 Presentation -October 05, 2023 at 02:58 pm EDT
summary: Western Copper and Gold’s October 2023 investor presentation describes its Casino copper-gold project in Canada’s Yukon, including past feasibility work, ongoing permitting, and strategic investments. It explicitly references a “strong copper market,” supporting positive sentiment toward copper, but provides no immediate production or policy change.

title: Trafigura Sees Potential $12,000 High For Copper
summary: Trafigura forecasts copper could rally to $12,000/ton, citing renewed Chinese demand linked to green-energy and equipment manufacturing. Goldman Sachs also projects China’s copper requirements rising 8% YoY. The piece acknowledges recent dips, inventory gains, and surplus risk, but overall forecasts are price-supportive.

title: Deadline Looms for U.S.-EU Steel, Aluminum Deal: Here's What Businesses Should Know
summary: The U.S. and EU face an October 31 deadline to finalize an arrangement on sustainable steel and aluminum to avoid renewed transatlantic tariffs. It also addresses CBAM reporting for aluminium imports (starting now) and CBAM-driven tariff effects beginning in 2026. The focus is emissions rules and competitiveness, not immediate price shocks.

title: US Extruded Aluminum Imports Actions
summary: U.S. aluminum extruders and USW filed AD/CVD petitions against imported extruded aluminum as allegedly dumped and subsidized from many countries. The case moves to ITC preliminary injury review and then DOC preliminary AD/CVD findings, with potential duties (including possible retroactivity). Reduced imports should support aluminum price expectations.

title: INSG forecasts a third consecutive year of nickel surplus : Andy Home - Today
summary: INSG forecasts nickel production exceeding demand for the third straight year, with the surplus rising to 239,000 tonnes next year and growing larger each year. Despite rising EV-related demand, output growth is faster, especially from Indonesia and China. Bears are heavily short, and surplus may increasingly reach LME/ShFE deliverable nickel.

title: Commodities : Copper set for worst week in nearly 11 months - Today
summary: Copper prices eased and were set for their steepest weekly decline in nearly 11 months as a firm dollar and high LME inventories weighed on sentiment. Aluminium rebounded slightly but remained on track for its biggest weekly drop since February. Nickel also extended losses for a fourth straight session.

title: Attempt to smuggle 28 tons of copper scrap from Uzbekistan to Kyrgyzstan foiled
summary: Customs authorities in Kyrgyzstan foiled an attempt to smuggle 28 tons of copper scrap from Uzbekistan into Kyrgyzstan, according to the State Customs Service. By stopping the shipment, the move likely prevents additional copper scrap supply from entering the local market in the near term.

title: Copper set for steepest weekly decline in almost 11 months
summary: LME copper was set for its biggest weekly drop in nearly 11 months, down about 4.5% week-on-week. A firm dollar and high LME inventories weighed on prices, while China’s market closure reduced near-term demand. Analysts also cited destocking of trapped DRC cathode after a temporary export ban.

title: LME WEEK-Resilient China demand supports copper prices, boosts local aluminium prices
summary: Reuters says China’s copper and aluminium demand has stayed robust despite housing stress, supported by appliances, EVs and renewables. Smelter inventories reportedly halved seasonally and procurement increased after a copper drop. Aluminium demand grew from solar and grid projects, lifting Chinese prices, though global macro demand risks persist.

title: LME WEEK-Resilient China demand supports copper prices, boosts local aluminium prices
summary: Reuters reports that unexpectedly resilient Chinese demand for copper and aluminium—supported by appliances, EVs, solar/wind and some property stimulus—has steadied otherwise weak global copper prices and lifted Chinese aluminium prices. Copper smelter inventories reportedly fell to about half normal, and aluminium demand rose for renewables and grids.

title: Japan's Pan Pacific sees 0.3% rise in H2 consigned copper output y/y
summary: Japan’s Pan Pacific Copper (PPC) expects H2 consigned copper output of 291,900 tonnes, up 0.3% year-on-year. The company scheduled about a month of maintenance at the Saganoseki smelter/refinery from late October and a short turnaround at Mitsui’s Tamano smelter in early December.

title: Asiamet Resources shares rise on progress at BKM copper project
summary: Asiamet Resources reported progress on financing for its BKM copper project in Indonesia. An independent expert is finalising its review after a site visit, and the company received an indicative term sheet for copper cathode offtake prepayment financing. It is also negotiating bank financing and EPC arrangements.

title: LME WEEK-LME nickel liquidity claws higher, full recovery may take years
summary: Reuters reports that LME nickel contract volumes are improving after the 2022 trading crisis, with August volumes up year-on-year. However, liquidity remains below early-2022 levels and brokers stay wary due to low LME warehouse stocks and market fragmentation. Nickel prices are down for the year amid surpluses from Indonesia.

title: Copper heads for the LME week with steep weekly decline
summary: Reuters reports copper rose Friday but is set for its biggest weekly drop in five months due to sustained high interest rates, a firm dollar, and elevated LME inventories. It links the fall to weaker-than-expected demand growth and CTA fund selling, while aluminium and nickel prices track the broader base-metal mood.

title: Metra purchases Belding's Extruded Aluminum Corp.
summary: Metra S.p.A. completed the acquisition of Extruded Aluminum Corp. (Belding Machinery and Equipment Leasing LLC and subsidiaries) for undisclosed terms. EAC manufactures custom extruded aluminum profiles used in sectors including solar, transportation, and construction. The deal expands Metra’s North American extrusion and fabrication footprint; no capacity or policy changes are specified.

title: Copper Study Group expects big supply surplus in 2024 : Andy Home - Today
summary: ICSG said the copper market shifts from balance/deficit in 2023 to a major supply surplus in 2024, with production forecast to exceed usage by 467,000 tonnes. Western demand is expected to weaken while Chinese apparent usage and smelting output rise, increasing the oversupply risk. Copper prices have broken below $8,000.

title: London-Codelco Chairman Says Copper Output Will Recover In 2024…
summary: Codelco’s chairman said copper output should recover in 2024 as the company ramps up operations at the Chuquicamata mine and faces fewer disruptions than previously expected. The Reuters update points to improving supply prospects, which can support copper market sentiment in the near term.

title: Codelco Plans to Borrow More as Copper Giant Reviews Major Projects
summary: Codelco plans to borrow more as it reviews major projects, according to the article headline. Because Codelco is a key copper supplier, financing and project-review decisions can influence near-term expectations for copper output. However, the excerpt provides no clear details on timing or volume changes.

title: London-Codelco Chairman Says Copper Output Will Recover In 2…
summary: Codelco’s chairman told Reuters that copper output will recover in 2024, supported by ramp-up at the Chuquicamata mine and reduced disruptions. The statement improves expectations for future copper supply, which tends to support copper prices by easing fears of prolonged production shortfalls.

title: Ruben Fernandes and Paul Gait presentation at the Deutsche Bank Virtual Copper CEO conference: Script -October 06, 2023 at 11:02 am EDT
summary: Anglo American executives present at a Deutsche Bank Virtual Copper CEO conference, emphasizing copper demand growth from decarbonisation and economic development, while arguing new copper supply is harder to bring online due to higher costs, permitting delays, and longer project timelines. They highlight operating ramp-ups and expansions, projecting a positive copper price outlook.

title: Petition Seeks Antidumping and Countervailing Duties on Aluminum Extrusion Imports from Fifteen Countries | Dorsey & Whitney LLP
summary: U.S. producers and unions filed a petition to impose antidumping and countervailing duties on aluminum extrusion imports from 15 countries, with potential margins above 100% for some origins. The scope is broad and could expand coverage beyond a prior 2011 China order, while existing Section 232/301 duties already apply.

title: Armenia's production of copper concentrate slashes by 16.5% in January-August 2023
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate production fell 16.5% in January-August 2023 versus the same period a year earlier to about 181,420 tons. The report also notes lower zinc and higher molybdenum concentrate output. The copper decline points to reduced near-term copper concentrate availability.

title: Codelco CEO Simplifies Management in Bid to Fix Growing Copper Mine Woes
summary: Codelco’s CEO is reportedly simplifying management as part of a bid to fix worsening issues at copper mines. The focus on “growing mine woes” implies potential near-term disruptions or weaker production prospects, which can increase perceived supply risk and weigh on copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Information regarding the antidumping and countervailing duty petitions on Aluminum Extrusions from 15 countries | White & Case LLP
summary: US Aluminum Extruders Coalition filed an antidumping (ADD) petition and an additional countervailing duty (CVD) petition regarding aluminum extrusions from 15 countries, alleging dumping and subsidies. The filing seeks remedies for material injury/threat of injury to domestic producers, which could lift near-term US import costs and support aluminum prices.

title: New Antidumping Duty and Countervailing Duty Petitions on Aluminum Extrusions From 15 Countries | Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath LLP
summary: A coalition of U.S. aluminum extruders and the United Steelworkers filed antidumping and countervailing duty petitions on aluminum extrusions from 15 countries. The petitions allege dumping and subsidies and could lead to U.S. duties, raising import costs, reducing supply availability, and increasing purchase prices in the near term.

title: New Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Petitions Target Aluminum Extrusions from 15 Countries | Husch Blackwell LLP
summary: U.S. industry groups filed new AD/CVD petitions covering aluminum extrusions from 15 countries. The scope may include certain downstream products previously excluded, with duties determined by the extrusion origin. Rates are cited from 28% to 256%, potentially imposed as early as late December, raising import costs.

title: BSE : Margin Framework for newly launched Aluminium, Copper & Zinc futures contract -October 06, 2023 at 05:26 pm EDT
summary: BSE (via ICCL/RMS margin framework guidance) issued a notice outlining margin parameters for newly launched non-agri futures in aluminium and copper, with high volatility category requiring minimum initial margin of 10% and minimum MPOR of 3 days. It is a risk-management/trading framework update rather than a demand-supply shock.

title: BSE : Margin Framework for newly launched Aluminium, Copper & Zinc futures contract -October 06, 2023 at 05:26 pm EDT
summary: BSE/ICCL issued a margin framework notice for newly launched non-agri futures on Aluminium and Copper (also Zinc), specifying high-volatility category initial margin of 10% and minimum MPOR of three days. The update affects trading/risk management for the contracts but not the metals’ underlying fundamentals.

title: London Listed Critical Metals signs landmark deal to buy copper ore processor
summary: Critical Metals plc says it will immediately lease and then purchase the Kastro hydrometallurgical processor in Lubumbashi, DRC, to process copper oxide/cobalt ore from its Molulu mine. The plant targets LME-grade 99.99% copper cathode output and improved value capture, potentially supporting near-term copper availability expectations.

title: Blackwolf Copper and Gold Ltd: Blackwolf Announces $2,500,800 Private Placement
summary: Blackwolf Copper and Gold Ltd. announced a non-brokered private placement to raise up to C$2.5M to fund exploration at its projects, including its 100% interest in the Niblack copper-gold-zinc-silver VMS deposit, plus general working capital. The news is financing-focused and does not cite near-term production changes.

title: Insider Buyers Lose Additional AU$72k As True North Copper Dips To AU$74m
summary: The piece highlights that insider buyers in True North Copper have lost an additional AU$72k as the company’s value/unit falls to AU$74m. The headline implies deteriorating sentiment toward copper-linked assets, suggesting expectations for copper prices have softened in the near term.

title: Copper - the winner in electric vehicle transition
summary: EV sales surged in Q2 2023, supporting an electrification trajectory that increases demand for copper through greater vehicle wiring and grid/energy storage uses. The piece highlights improving copper demand forecasts versus constrained supply and notes recent strength in LME copper. It also flags LFP batteries as potentially reducing nickel exposure.

title: LME CEO Says Stability Has Returned as Nickel Crisis Recedes
summary: BNN Bloomberg’s weekend headline says the LME CEO expects stability to have returned as the nickel crisis recedes. This points to easing shortages/market stress and a likely reduction in the risk premium, which typically pressures nickel prices downward over the next days to weeks.

title: Commodities : China demand supports copper, but Fed rate fears weigh - Today
summary: Copper opened higher after a weekly decline as China’s demand remained resilient, supporting both copper and aluminium despite property weakness. However, expectations of further U.S. Fed rate hikes weighed on overall sentiment. The piece reports nickel falling while other base metals rose slightly.

title: Material Matters: Iron Ore, Sector Downside, Copper & Oil
summary: The piece discusses a range of commodities but highlights analysts’ outlooks for industrial metals. Morgan Stanley and Citi expect copper to perform strongly medium-term, supported by decarbonisation demand, while also flagging cyclical macro headwinds. It suggests investors may selectively add copper and aluminium exposure despite near-term pressure.

title: Commodities : Copper climbs on robust China demand - Today
summary: Copper prices rose on Monday, supported by surprisingly robust demand in China despite the property sector crisis, with demand linked to appliances, electric vehicles, solar and wind. The firmer U.S. dollar limited gains, but copper still added 1.2%. Aluminium demand in China is also described as robust, though prices barely moved.

title: New Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Petitions on Aluminum Extrusions from 15 Countries
summary: U.S. producers filed major antidumping and countervailing duty petitions on aluminum extrusions imported from 15 countries, seeking expanded scope versus prior China orders. If preliminary findings are affirmative, importers would post cash deposits under country-specific AD/CVD rates, potentially reducing U.S. aluminum extrusion supply and supporting prices.

title: Copper firm, but demand outlook remains gloomy
summary: Copper rose to a one-week peak as Chinese buyers returned after a holiday, but further gains look unlikely. Traders cite weak China demand, trouble in the property sector, a strong dollar, and sharply higher LME warehouse inventories, which widen the cash discount versus the three-month contract.

title: Copper Markets Set For Shortages In The Long Term
summary: Executives warn that weak near-term copper prices and surplus expectations may discourage new mine development, potentially leading to a future supply gap for energy-transition demand. The article also cites inventory and manufacturing slowdown concerns and China demand uncertainty, keeping short-term prices pressured despite brighter medium/long-term outlook.

title: Critical Metals to sell copper oxide ore to OM Metal & Resources
summary: Critical Metals PLC signed an offtake agreement to sell at least 20,000 tonnes of copper oxide ore from its Molulu project in the DRC to OM Metal & Resources. The gross price is about $91.20/tonne. Management said the deal provides near-term cashflow while meeting oxide output targets.

title: Codelco 2024 copper premium offer matches 2023's record $234/T for European customers
summary: Codelco plans to sell 2024 copper to European customers at a $234/mt premium over the LME, matching the 2023 record. Europe’s reduced Russian imports after the Ukraine invasion, plus earlier high energy and logistics costs, supported premium levels. Aurubis also keeps a $228/mt premium.

title: FORD JOINS LEADING COMPANIES TO CALL FOR FEDERAL INVESTMENT IN CLEAN ALUMINUM
summary: Ford, GM, PepsiCo, Ball and others urge the DOE to use Inflation Reduction Act funding to secure affordable clean electricity and expand U.S. primary aluminium production. They cite plummeting primary output and curtailments from high power/fuel costs, warning demand is set to rise, implying tighter supply and price support.

title: First copper shipment marks Kombat cash flow
summary: Trigon Metals says its first copper concentrate shipments have begun from the Kombat Mine in Namibia, with more than 100 tonnes sent and shipments continuing as onsite storage fills. The company reports strong September mill performance, improving recoveries, and plans to declare commercial production in October, aiming for over four million pounds of copper by March.

title: LME WEEK-New Abaxx exchange to expand EV metals offering beyond nickel
summary: Abaxx Commodities Exchange in Singapore plans to launch a physically settled futures contract for nickel sulphate used in EV batteries and aims to add additional battery-metal contracts after nickel. Executives say delivery mechanics differ from the LME, and regulatory approvals are needed for timing. Nickel is the direct linkage; other metals are unspecified.

title: Farmers' group eyes gains from Tampakan Copper-Gold project
summary: A farmers’ federation in Mindanao voiced support for the Tampakan copper-gold project, saying operations are planned to begin in 2024 and that the firm already invested in local humanitarian programs. The group urges Malacañang to approve the venture, which could modestly improve expectations for future copper supply.

title: Copper Executives Warn Of Mine Shortage Amid Energy Transition
summary: Copper executives warn that the low-carbon energy transition could be slowed by a lack of new copper mines. They argue that rising renewable/EV and grid demand will outpace supply despite price. Producers are cautious amid weak demand signals and an uncertain investment climate, suggesting future supply tightness.

title: 'Alumina dust' plant emissions concern Goose Creek community
summary: South Carolina regulators are investigating complaints that an aluminum smelter (Century Aluminum’s Mount Holly plant) is emitting alumina dust that coats nearby properties. DHEC is using air sensors while Century attributes it to baghouse filter failures or high pressure events, and says fixes are planned by Oct. 17.

title: Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Petitions on Aluminum Extrusions
summary: US Aluminum Extruders Coalition and USW filed AD/CVD petitions on certain aluminum extrusions from multiple countries, alleging dumping and subsidies and requesting duties up to ~256%. If Commerce/ITC find dumping/subsidization and material injury, importers face AD/CVD liabilities. The dispute targets US aluminium extrusion supply and pricing.

title: Copper Extends Gains as Metals World Gathers in London
summary: The piece is headlined “Copper Extends Gains,” indicating copper prices are continuing to rise as metals gather in London. While the excerpted body includes unrelated headlines, the copper-specific title suggests positive near-term price momentum for copper rather than a reversal.

title: London copper set for 3rd straight gain on easing dollar, bullish bet
summary: London copper is set for a third straight daily gain as a weaker dollar and bullish sentiment lift LME prices, with LME Seminar showing copper as the top upside bet for 2024. China demand is cited as robust despite property stress. Aluminium edges up; nickel is also higher in SHFE trading.

title: Nickel Sulfate Price Expected to Remain Stable_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports battery-grade nickel sulfate trading around 32,100–32,800 yuan/ton, with slight week-on-week increases but weaker demand transmission from high prices. Manufacturers cite tight raw-material supply and high raw-material coefficients supporting prices, while electro-nickel-side purchasing slows. Post-holiday, nickel sulfate is expected to stay stable.

title: Copper boss warns of supply shortage in race to net zero
summary: Industry bosses, including Freeport-McMoRan’s president, warn the energy transition could be delayed by insufficient new copper mine development to meet growing demand. They argue higher prices alone won’t overcome non-price constraints on ramping supply, raising expectations of tighter copper availability ahead.

title: Chinese Copper Trader Detained For Questioning
summary: China’s police reportedly detained the founder of Maike Metals, a major copper trading house, amid investigations, while the firm is said to be nearly inactive after a prior liquidity crunch. The article also links earlier-month declines in Chinese copper demand and a real-estate slowdown to prices falling to a four-month low.

title: Chinese copper tycoon goes missing, believed to be detained by police
summary: Executives at Maike Metals International, China’s largest importer of refined copper, have lost contact with founder He Jinbi, believed detained by police. The company has faced a liquidity crisis and has been largely absent from copper trading, weighing on China’s copper trade liquidity amid ongoing creditor legal actions.

title: Nickel Sulfate Prices May Increase_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that China’s battery-grade nickel sulfate index rose to 32,182 yuan/ton on Oct 9. Spot activity remains weak after holidays, but inquiries persist. Tight raw-material supply and low shipping willingness support costs, while downstream demand continues, leaving potential upside for nickel sulfate prices.

title: European Investor to Build Nickel Smelter in Indonesia: Gov't
summary: Indonesia’s government says a European company is negotiating a large nickel smelter investment to supply batteries and electric vehicles. Since Indonesia’s 2020 ban on raw nickel ore exports, the policy has driven downstream investments despite an EU WTO dispute. New smelter plans are likely to support nickel supply expectations.

title: China's top copper buyers expect a 36% cut in Codelco premium, sources
summary: China’s largest copper buyers expect to pay a Codelco premium of about $90/mt next year, nearly 36% lower than this year, according to four sources. Copper premiums are paid over the LME benchmark and influence physical contract pricing, signaling softer physical copper pricing expectations.

title: Is Goose Creek's alumina dust issue getting resolved? Century Aluminum explains
summary: Residents in Goose Creek report weeks of alumina dust from Century Aluminum. The company attributes emissions to accelerated bag failures and says it will replace failed bags, with an action plan taking about 10 days. DHEC deployed air sensors, reporting very low readings so far.

title: LME WEEK-China's top copper buyers expect a 36% cut in Codelco premium -sources
summary: China’s top copper buyers expect to pay about a $90/ton premium next year for Codelco copper, 36% lower than this year. Premiums are set over LME benchmarks. Sources cite weaker Chinese demand and cheaper freight to Shanghai. The ICSG forecasts a larger refined copper surplus next year.

title: Copper slides as China property market jitters resurface
summary: Copper prices fell as renewed jitters over China’s property demand intensified after Country Garden warned of significant challenges meeting offshore debt. The move was reinforced by sharply higher LME warehouse inventories, widening a surplus outlook and weakening cash premiums. Aluminium and nickel also declined amid broader industrial-metals risk sentiment.

title: Potential for Sediment-Hosted Copper Identified in Drilling at Whisky Creek Project
summary: CopperCorp reports that review of historical drilling and drill core at its Whisky Creek project in northern Tasmania confirms strong potential for sediment-hosted copper mineralization. It cites past drill hole intersections (up to 1m at 4.1% Cu) and describes planned core resampling and field exploration, with no production impact stated.

title: There is a huge shortage of copper mines: another major obstacle to energy transition -October 10, 2023 at 07:21 am EDT
summary: The piece warns of a copper mine shortage as new mine permits hit their lowest level in a decade and projects require 10–20 years to develop. It cites labor and discovery difficulties and says recycling won’t meet demand. With electrification demand rising, Goldman expects higher copper prices.

title: Share of Russian aluminium in LME-registered warehouses falls to 76%
summary: Russian-origin aluminium on LME warrants fell to 76% in September from 81% as  cancellations occurred in Gwangyang, with Russian aluminium tonnage dropping to 132,475 from 183,650. Russian copper share fell to 23%, while nickel rose to 22.5%. Aluminium was up on the day, Reuters said.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Announces DRC President, Félix Tshisekedi, Visited the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex and Formally Opened the Kamoa Centre of Excellence
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reports DRC President Félix Tshisekedi visited the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex and opened the Kamoa Centre of Excellence. The delegation also toured concentrators and the site for a 500,000 tpa direct-to-blister copper smelter under construction. The release focuses on training and facilities rather than new copper output.

title: China's copper tycoon missing, presumed taken by police
summary: China’s Maike Metals International’s founder He Jinbi is reported missing and believed detained by police for questioning. The firm is a major refined-copper importer that previously struggled with liquidity and creditor legal action. Maike’s continued absence has weighed on copper trade liquidity, suggesting near-term bearish pressure for copper.

title: Zambia to decide on new Mopani Copper Mines investor in October - source
summary: Zambia is expected to decide in October on a new investor for Mopani Copper Mines, bought from Glencore in 2021, after delays from complex negotiations. Bids include Sibanye, an IHC-linked UAE investor, and China’s Zijin. Zambia aims to boost output, but no near-term production change is confirmed.

title: Tribeca Resources Recommences Drilling at its La Higuera Copper-Gold Project in Northern Chile
summary: Tribeca Resources announced it has recommenced Phase 2 diamond drilling at its La Higuera copper-gold project in northern Chile, targeting extensions and new IP/gravity targets at the Gaby IOCG discovery. The 4,000m program will take about four months, with results expected progressively. No production or supply impact is cited.

title: Great Southern Copper hails encouraging Especularita results
summary: Great Southern Copper reports encouraging drone-magnetics results at its Especularita project in Chile, identifying Abundante and Teresita copper-gold prospects and multiple targets along a magnetic corridor. The company plans to start scout RC drilling after permitting and drill-rig availability, pending follow-up ground-truthing.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Pacific Ridge Intersects 103.5 M of 0.63% Copper Equivalent Within 388.5 M of 0.42% Copper Equivalent in Kliyul North Zone at Kliyul Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge reported additional drilling at its Kliyul copper-gold project, including 103.5 m of 0.63% CuEq (0.18% copper) in the Kliyul North zone and expanded known extents of the porphyry system. The release is exploration-focused with no near-term production or infrastructure impact.

title: Low Embodied Carbon Architectural Aluminum Furnished to U.S. Market in Landmark Deal Without Cost Premium
summary: Reflection Window + Wall says it has secured a landmark deal to furnish U.S. markets with low-embodied-carbon architectural aluminum without a cost premium. The release highlights large potential emissions reductions versus typical aluminum production, positioning the product as broadly available for building facades and sustainability-driven demand.

title: Freeport Seeks to Extend Permit for Exporting Indonesian Copper
summary: The article (headline) says Freeport is seeking to extend an Indonesian permit that allows exporting copper. If the extension succeeds, it would likely reduce the risk of near-term export curbs from Indonesia and help sustain market supply expectations, offering modest support to copper prices.

title: At It Again: New Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Petitions on Aluminum Extrusions from Fifteen Countries | ArentFox Schiff
summary: US Aluminum Extruders Coalition and USW filed antidumping and countervailing duty petitions on certain aluminum extrusions from 15 countries. The petition alleges dumping and subsidies and requests AD/CVD duties ranging from 28% up to 256%. Duties would apply if Commerce and the ITC find dumping/subsidization and material injury.

title: New Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Petitions on Aluminum Extrusions from 15 Countries | Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP
summary: U.S. aluminum extruders filed antidumping and countervailing duty petitions covering aluminum extrusions from 15 countries. If the Commerce Department and ITC issue preliminary affirmative rulings, importers must post cash deposits of estimated duties. The expanded scope targets additional extrusion types beyond prior AD/CVD orders.

title: New Trade Case on Imports of Aluminum Lithographic Printing Plates from China and Japan | Clark Hill PLC
summary: U.S. antidumping and countervailing duty petitions were filed against imports of aluminum lithographic printing plates from China (AD and CVD) and from Japan (AD). The ITC will first assess injury/threat, then Commerce would set preliminary duty margins and require deposits, potentially affecting near-term import demand for aluminum plates.

title: Outstanding rock chip assay results of up to 11% Copper, 21g/t gold and 3% Zinc - Augustus Polymetallic Project, Arizona
summary: Advance Metals announced “outstanding” rock chip assay results from its Augustus polymetallic project in Arizona, including up to 11.97% copper and economically viable copper grades in ~40% of samples, plus gold and zinc. The update is exploration-related and unlikely to change near-term physical metal balances.

title: Copper Prices Decline As Global Renewable Hopes Fall Short
summary: Copper prices declined and broke below key price levels in early October. The piece cites softer demand expectations (notably China), delays in U.S. renewables, and ICSG forecasts of a developing surplus alongside rising LME inventories and investor positioning turning net short—together reinforcing downside pressure.

title: Firm demand for cement and aluminium
summary: Analysts are optimistic that supportive fundamentals will sustain aluminium demand. They point to tight supply conditions, rising demand, and strong prices, with ongoing infrastructure projects and construction activity expected to continue supporting the market. The report frames the outlook as positive going forward.

title: Copper supported by a weaker dollar, China demand hope
summary: Copper prices rebounded as the U.S. dollar weakened and investors hoped China could restart demand via potential infrastructure-focused stimulus, including possible sovereign debt issuance. The piece also notes mixed moves across other metals: LME aluminium rose while nickel edged lower, reflecting uneven market impact.

title: Key Takeaway From LME Week: China Fights Back By Upgrading Alumina And Primary Aluminium Trade With Russia_SMM
summary: SMM’s LME Week recap says China has tightened semiconductor-related exports of gallium/germanium after U.S. curbs, but the key aluminium point is that China and Russia have deepened trading links. China is upgrading alumina trade and importing more Russian primary aluminium, potentially increasing supply in the near term.

title: Key Takeaway From LME Week: China's Sustained And Rapid ODI Growth Will Add 11% To Demand For Steel, 46% More Demand For Copper And 55% More Demand For Aluminum_SMM
summary: SMM’s LME Week takeaway expects Chinese manufacturing restocking in Q4 due to housing completions, energy investment and ODI-related exports. It also claims China’s rapid ODI growth will raise demand for copper and aluminium via industrialization and urbanization in ASEAN/BRI countries, suggesting upward pressure on prices.

title: Key Takeaway From LME Week: China's Sustained And Rapid ODI Growth Will Add 11% To Demand For Steel, 46% More Demand For Copper And 55% More Demand For Aluminum_SMM
summary: SMM’s LME Week takeaway says China’s manufacturing should restock in Q4, supported by housing completions, energy investment and ODI-linked exports. It highlights electrification and energy shortages. Most directly, it projects ODI growth will add substantially to copper and aluminum demand in ASEAN/BRI via urbanization.

title: Nickel Sulfate Spot Supply Holds Tight_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports battery-grade nickel sulfate spot prices rising to around 32,203 yuan/ton, with expectations of further daily increases. Spot supply is described as tight, salt producers are worried about raw material availability and hold back goods, strengthening support for prices. Demand inquiries are active but trades remain weak.

title: Downstream Mineral Processing Set to Enhance Merdeka Copper's Performance
summary: Indonesia’s Merdeka Battery Materials (MBMA), linked to Merdeka Copper Gold, is expanding nickel processing via HPAL and other routes, including an agreement with GEM to build an HPAL plant at IMIP. The strategy targets EV battery supply chains, potentially boosting expectations for nickel demand and downstream utilization.

title: Copper edges higher on retreating bond yields, hopes for China
summary: Copper prices edged higher as U.S. bond yields fell from recent peaks and markets looked for China to announce more stimulus. The housing-demand outlook remains a concern and LME inventories rose toward a 17-month high, reflecting a likely surplus. Aluminium rose slightly, while nickel eased.

title: C3 Metals Extends Copper-Gold Porphyry Mineralization 150m at Provost at Bellas Gate, Jamaica; Drill Hole Ended in 1.1m at 1.27% Copper and 4,090 g/t Silver
summary: C3 Metals reported assay results from a new drill hole at its Bellas Gate, Jamaica Provost target, extending copper-gold mineralization by 150m and including 1.27% copper over the final 1.1m. The release discusses continued step-out drilling, but provides no immediate production, trade, or supply changes.

title: Rio Tinto Venture Makes Further $10 Million Investment in McEwen Copper
summary: Rio Tinto Venture (Nuton) and Stellantis increased investment in McEwen Copper, lifting stakes to 14.5% and just over 19%, respectively. The transactions value McEwen Copper at about $800 million. Proceeds will fund development of Argentina’s Los Azules copper project, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Canada Nickel to host Feasibility Study Conference Call on Thursday, October 12, 2023
summary: Canada Nickel Company will host a webcast and conference call to discuss its Definitive Feasibility Study for the Crawford nickel sulphide project. The update could affect market expectations for future nickel supply from the Timmins-Cochrane camp, providing modest near-term support to nickel pricing sentiment.

title: Intrepid Metals Highlights Additional High-Grade Shallow Mineralization at Its 100% Controlled Corral Copper Project in Arizona
summary: Intrepid Metals said it has identified additional high-grade, shallow mineralization at its 100% controlled Corral Copper Project in Arizona. The update is a positive development for the company’s copper resource profile, potentially supporting near-term expectations for future copper supply and project value.

title: McEwen Copper Closes ARS $42 Billion Investment by Stellantis
summary: McEwen Copper said Stellantis closed an additional ARS 42 billion investment to buy shares in McEwen Copper, with proceeds funding the Los Azules copper project in Argentina. Stellantis also secured minimum copper cathode offtake rights and defined market-price terms, supporting copper project progress and demand expectations.

title: McEwen Mining: McEwen Copper Announces an Additional US$10 Million Investment by Nuton, a Rio Tinto Venture
summary: McEwen Copper announced Nuton (Rio Tinto venture) will invest US$10m via a two-part share transaction expected to close Oct. 19. Proceeds will fund development of the Los Azules copper project in Argentina and corporate purposes. The parties also extended exclusivity for copper heap-leach technologies to Feb. 1, 2025.

title: Miners seek partners for copper assets as M&A heats up
summary: Reuters says copper miners are seeking partners and deal structures (M&A and joint ventures) for multiple copper projects in Argentina, Chile and Peru as development costs rise ~50% and securing new supply grows harder. Deals and stake sales (e.g., Glencore projects, First Quantum and others) signal sustained investment in copper supply.

title: Copper edges higher on retreating bond yields, China stimulus hopes
summary: Copper edged higher on the London Metal Exchange as U.S. bond yields fell from recent highs and investors looked for more China stimulus. However, concerns persist about China’s housing slowdown, while evidence of rising copper inventories and mine ramp-ups points to a potential surplus.

title: Stellantis, Rio Tinto Raise Bets on Copper Mining in Argentina
summary: The headline suggests Stellantis and Rio Tinto are ramping up plans for copper mining in Argentina. Such project-boosting news can lift market sentiment by improving expectations for future copper supply, though it is unlikely to change near-term spot availability within days to a few weeks.

title: Anglo American and Mitsubishi Materials to work on copper value chain
summary: Anglo American will collaborate with Mitsubishi Materials to develop copper product offerings with strong provenance traceability and sustainability indicators. The partnership also explores decarbonisation steps to lower the copper’s carbon footprint. It does not cite near-term changes to copper supply, inventories, or trade flows.

title: Zambian gov't rues rising pollution levels in copper mining province
summary: Zambia’s Minister of Green Economy and Environment visited the Copperbelt Province to inspect firms after concerns about increased pollution linked to mining and related activities. Officials will assess whether companies are complying with environmental regulations. The report signals regulatory scrutiny but does not mention immediate output cuts.

title: Zambian gov't rues rising pollution levels in copper mining province-Xinhua
summary: Zambia’s Ministry of Green Economy and Environment inspected mining-related firms in the central Copperbelt amid rising pollution. Officials found non-compliance with environmental rules, including emissions into open areas and untreated waste into a river. Some companies were ordered to halt operations and compensate affected farmers.

title: Alta Copper Announces Non-Brokered Financing
summary: Alta Copper announced a non-brokered private placement raising about C$766,645 for working capital and community initiatives in Peru, intended to support advancement of its 100% owned Cañariaco copper project. Management cited ongoing discussions for funding a 2024 drilling program and targeting preliminary economic assessment results in Q1 2024.

title: Copper falls as rising inventory outweighs China stimulus hopes
summary: Copper prices edged lower as London inventories rose to the highest since May 2022, with LME copper down and the copper premium signaling resilient Chinese imports. The drop was partly offset by a soft U.S. dollar and hopes for further China stimulus. Nickel and aluminium moved modestly.

title: Critical Metals signs copper oxide ore offtake deal with OM Metal
summary: Critical Metals signed an offtake deal to sell at least 20,000 tonnes of copper oxide ore from its Molulu project in the DRC to OM Metal & Resources from 4 Oct to 31 Dec, with possible renewal. The first load was delivered via ten trucks, supporting short-term copper supply monetisation.

title: Copper rises on softer dollar, Chinese stimulus hope
summary: Copper rose on Thursday as a weaker U.S. dollar made dollar-priced commodities cheaper and as investors looked for further Chinese stimulus. Chinese infrastructure-debt expectations lifted demand signals, including a higher Yangshan premium. However, gains were capped by sharply higher LME copper inventories, while aluminium stayed flat and nickel rose.

title: Copper Hovers Above $8,000 With Help From Fed Comments and China
summary: Copper is holding above $8,000, according to the article, with support attributed to recent Fed comments and China-related factors. These signals can affect short-term macro outlook and metal demand expectations, providing upward price pressure for copper over the next days to weeks.

title: EU to investigate Chinese steel and aluminium sectors, with tariffs looming, in deal with US
summary: The EU plans to investigate China’s steel and aluminium sectors, with tariff measures expected as part of a deal involving the US. The looming tariffs could affect cross-border aluminium flows by raising import costs and shifting expectations for near-term supply and demand dynamics, weighing on aluminium prices.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Initiates Phase III Drill Program at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. started a Phase III 20,000-metre diamond drill program at its Copper Creek copper project in Arizona. The program targets new discoveries, expansion of an open-pit resource, and higher-grade underground zones, with assay results to be released as received. No production or marketable supply changes are stated.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Positive Bankable Feasibility Study For its Crawford Nickel Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel reported a positive bankable feasibility study for its Crawford nickel sulphide project, highlighting higher after-tax NPV/IRR and production of about 48 ktpa nickel. The update strengthens expectations for future long-life development (permits/financing) and improves sentiment for nickel demand-supply balance over coming months.

title: Barrick Preliminary 3Q Gold, Copper Production Rise
summary: Barrick reported preliminary Q3 output of 112 million pounds of copper, up from 107 million in Q2, driven largely by higher production at its Lumwana mine in Zambia. Management cited delays at Pueblo Viejo affecting gold. It does not indicate sudden supply cuts or export constraints.

title: Barrick Gold's third-quarter gold, copper output rise
summary: Barrick Gold said its third-quarter copper production rose 4.7% sequentially to 112 million pounds, driven largely by Zambia’s Lumwana mine. The company also outlined investment to extend Lumwana’s life and gave cost outlooks, while gold output increased nearly 3%. The copper output beat is the key near-term datapoint.

title: Romios Stakes New Claims at the Kinkaid Copper-Gold-Silver Property in the Walker Lane Trend, Nevada, USA
summary: Romios Gold reported staking 22 new claims and finding mineralized boulders with high copper grades (up to 13.3% Cu, average ~5%) near its Kinkaid copper-gold-silver property in Nevada. The company plans further mapping and sampling; the release does not indicate near-term mining output.

title: Copper prices rise on China demand hopes
summary: Copper prices rose on LME as investors priced China demand support, stronger physical buying signals and stockpiling interest. The Yangshan premium climbed to the highest since Dec 2022, while cancellations reduced on-warrant supplies. A weaker U.S. dollar also improved appeal, though some analysts warned demand remains bearish into Q4.

title: Midland Exploration Inc. Reports New Nickel-Copper Assay Results from A Drilling Campaign Completed to Follow Up on the New Ni-Cu Discovery Named Santos
summary: Midland Exploration released new assay results from drilling at its Santos nickel-copper discovery on the Tete Nord property. The latest hole intersected mineralized zones with grades including 0.33% Ni and 0.12% Cu over 39.73 metres. Additional drilling is planned after permits in November.

title: Advanced Energy Minerals Breaks Ground On its High-Purity Alumina Plant Expansion in Cap-Chat, Quebec, Canada
summary: Advanced Energy Minerals is expanding its high-purity alumina plant in Cap-Chat, Quebec, with the project set to increase capacity over about two years using latest technology. High-purity alumina is an aluminium-related input, and the investment/production ramp could modestly influence near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Advanced Energy Minerals Inc.: Advanced Energy Minerals Breaks Ground On its High-Purity Alumina Plant Expansion in Cap-Chat, Quebec, Canada
summary: Advanced Energy Minerals started works to expand its high-purity alumina plant in Cap-Chat, Quebec, aimed at increasing output of aluminium derivative products over about two years using latest technology. The release frames it as capacity growth for customer demand, but it is not an immediate supply shock to aluminium prices.

title: Deep-South Hires Ferrodrill to Drill the Haib Copper Project in the South of Namibia
summary: Deep-South has hired Ferrodrill to carry out drilling for the Haib Copper Project in southern Namibia. The announcement points to continued exploration progress and potential future copper supply development, which can offer mild support to near-term copper sentiment. No direct near-term production or inventory data is provided.

title: Grizzly Reports the First Sample Results for the New Work at the Midway, Imperial and Copper Mountain Areas of the Greenwood, BC Precious and Battery Metals Project
summary: Grizzly Discoveries reports first sample results from work at the Greenwood District targets (Midway, Imperial, Copper Mountain). Results highlight gold and silver, with some base-metal grades including copper (up to 0.475%) alongside lead/zinc. The article is exploration-focused and contains no immediate supply or market-impact details.

title: The Watchlist by The Market Herald Releases New Interviews with Leveljump Healthcare, Kootenay Silver, Sendero Resources, Nextech3D.ai, and Canada Nickel Company Discussing their Latest News
summary: The Market Herald releases interview content covering multiple companies. The only clear industrial-metals link is Canada Nickel’s positive bankable feasibility study for its Crawford nickel sulphide project, reporting improved economics versus the preliminary analysis. Better project economics can support expectations for future nickel supply and sentiment.

title: LME Copper Stockpiles Rebound to Hit Highest in Nearly Two Years
summary: LME copper stockpiles are reported to have rebounded to their highest level in nearly two years. Higher warehouse inventories typically signal looser near-term physical supply, which can weigh on expectations for copper price direction in the coming days as market participants adjust for reduced urgency to buy.

title: China Sept copper imports slide amid strong domestic production
summary: China’s September unwrought copper and copper product imports fell 5.8% year-on-year to 480,426 tonnes, Reuters reported. Strong domestic refined production reduced need for overseas supplies, while weaker demand growth from the housing-led slowdown and flat October consumption limited appetite. Ore and concentrate imports rose, reflecting higher feedstock use.

title: Nickel Sulfate Supply&Demand Weak_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports that on Oct 12 the Shanghai battery-grade nickel sulfate index was unchanged day-on-day at 32,202 yuan/ton, with the average also stable. Supply remains tight due to unresolved raw material issues, but demand is soft with weak inquiries and transactions, leaving overall nickel sulfate market conditions weak.

title: Anglo, Mitsubishi team up on responsible copper value chain
summary: Anglo American and Mitsubishi Materials signed an MoU to develop a responsible, traceable copper value chain with enhanced provenance transparency and decarbonisation efforts. The deal targets sustainability credentials sought by consumers but does not mention near-term production, supply, or tariff impacts. Price effects are likely negligible in the coming weeks.

title: London copper edges up on weaker dollar, but set for weekly fall
summary: London copper edged up as a softer dollar supported USD-priced metals, but it was still set for a weekly decline amid weaker industrial demand sentiment tied to “higher-for-longer” rates. Copper was pressured by rising LME warehouse inventories. The article also notes minor moves in aluminium and nickel on the day.

title: Instant view: China's soybean and copper imports fall on year, crude oil up | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: Reuters reports China’s September copper imports rose 1.5% month-on-month to 480,426 mt but fell 5.8% year-on-year. Analysts attribute the m/m rise to improved import conditions and copper moving from bonded warehouses into China, while the y/y decline is linked to higher US interest rates raising financing costs and reducing import demand.

title: London Metal Exchange tries to move on from nickel crisis
summary: LME Week highlights that last year’s nickel crisis still lingers: lawsuits over canceled nickel trades remain pending, and the exchange is still rebuilding confidence in its nickel contract. Nickel volumes and participation lag, while rivals expand nickel trading and other venues gain EV-battery-related traction, pressuring sentiment.

title: Residents concerned about Century Aluminum's dust | News
summary: Goose Creek residents met DHEC and Century Aluminum after three Sept. dust-release incidents from the plant. DHEC said filtration failures released aluminium oxide but sensor readings Oct. 3-6 showed no air-quality standard violations. Century cited malfunctioning dust-holding devices and said repairs will be completed by mid-October.

title: Squarepoint Follows Citi Buying Russian Aluminum on the LME
summary: The item notes that Squarepoint is following Citi’s lead by buying Russian aluminium on the LME. This points to additional market demand/positioning for aluminium tied to Russian supply, which would likely support near-term aluminium price expectations over the coming days.

title: Peru copper production grows 7.5% in August
summary: Peru’s ministry reported copper production rose 7.5% year over year in August to 223,178 tonnes, though it was below July’s 229,728 tonnes after a 17.7% jump. Higher output from a key global source can pressure prices by increasing short-term supply expectations.

title: Peru's Copper Production Grows 7.5% Year-On-Year In August To 22…
summary: Peru’s Ministry of Energy and Mines reported that copper production increased 7.5% year-on-year in August to 223,178 tonnes. As a key South American supplier, the higher output can boost near-term availability and weigh on copper market expectations over coming weeks.

title: Peru's copper production up 7.5% in August
summary: Peru’s copper production increased 7.5% year-over-year in August to about 223,000 metric tons, though it was below July. The ministry attributed the gain to strong performance from miners Freeport-McMoRan and Cerro Verde. Peru is the world’s second-largest producer and raised output since earlier unrest disruptions.

title: Copper thefts in Louisville are leaving many highways dark
summary: Kentucky’s transportation officials say copper wiring theft has disabled nearly 1,000 highway light poles in Louisville, with damages estimated at $750,000. Authorities say thieves sell the copper for scrap and thefts have surged in recent years. A reward is offered as crews work to restore lighting.

title: AD and CVD Petitions on Aluminum Extrusions
summary: U.S. aluminum extrusions producers filed AD and CVD petitions covering imports from 15 countries and expanding existing China coverage. If Commerce and ITC issue preliminary affirmative rulings (likely early March 2024), importers must post cash deposits on covered aluminum extrusion products, raising landed costs and disrupting near-term supply.

title: B.C. First Nations ask B.C. to review Copper Mountain mine extension
summary: B.C. First Nations and conservation groups are urging the province to order an environmental assessment for the Copper Mountain Mine’s proposed open-pit expansion near the Similkameen River. They cite Indigenous rights and tailings-dam breach risks, including claims of prior pollution. The province is reviewing the request, potentially affecting copper supply timelines.

title: Frog Bikes to reduce carbon emissions using of recycled aluminium
summary: Frog Bikes received a £150,000 green loan to produce children’s bike frames and forks using 25% post-consumer recycled aluminium, which they say is stronger and lowers CO2 per bike. The funding supports scaling production and the company’s broader shift toward more recycled aluminium and emissions cuts.

title: Copper gains US 'critical material' designation
summary: The U.S. Department of Energy designated copper a “critical material,” enabling new federal tax incentives for copper projects. The policy aims to support clean-energy supply chains for EVs, solar and grid upgrades, particularly benefiting copper-heavy Arizona. Environmental groups oppose the move, but it may improve copper demand/investment expectations.

title: London Metal Exchange tries to move on from nickel crisis: Andy Home -October 15, 2023 at 07:00 pm EDT
summary: Reuters reports LME Week with lingering fallout from last year’s nickel crisis, including pending lawsuits over cancelled nickel trades and continued efforts to strengthen trading/clearing systems. It says nickel trading volumes and participation remain weaker than other metals and nickel lags the broader LME recovery, implying cautious near-term market sentiment.

title: Copper climbs on China demand; rising supplies cap gains
summary: Copper prices opened higher on resilient Chinese demand and signs of stabilizing growth, with imports at an intra-year high. However, gains were capped by rising LME inventories and a firmer dollar ahead of a Powell speech, limiting the net near-term upside. Aluminium was steady; nickel rose modestly.

title: Nickel Sulfate Prices Are Under Upward Pressure_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM said China’s battery-grade nickel sulfate index rose to 32,202 yuan/ton and has stabilized under upward pressure after the holiday. Tight raw-material supply persists with low spot circulation and reluctant selling. Demand weakened on slower electro-nickel and precursor purchasing, but cost-side support remains strong, supporting nickel.

title: China's Nanshan Aluminum to Spin Off Indonesian Business for Hong Kong Listing
summary: Shandong Nanshan Aluminum plans to spin off its Indonesian assets into a Hong Kong-listed entity to fund expansion. It already operates an Indonesian alumina plant and plans a 250,000-ton electrolytic aluminium project, but commissioning is targeted for 1H 2026, implying limited immediate supply impact.

title: RAMU NICKEL PROJECT DEVELOPER INVITED TO GET INTO DOWNSTREAM PROCESSING IN PNG – EMTV Online
summary: Papua New Guinea’s PM Marape urged MCC, developer of the Ramu nickel/cobalt project, to expand into downstream processing, and MCC said it would seriously consider such expansion in its PNG investment plans. The project is MCC’s biggest investment outside China, supporting nickel-focused sentiment.

title: New Trade Cases Filed on Imports of Aluminum Extrusions From 15 Countries | Clark Hill PLC
summary: Fifteen U.S. antidumping and four countervailing duty petitions were filed against imports of aluminum extrusions from multiple countries. The ITC will assess whether imports injure or threaten injury, and the Commerce Department will later set preliminary duty margins. Proposed duties would likely lift import costs and support aluminium pricing.

title: Copper propped up by weaker dollar, but nervous over Mideast
summary: Copper edged higher on Monday as the dollar weakened, reversing two sessions of losses, supported by stronger-than-expected Chinese physical demand and infrastructure spending. However, nerves over the Middle East and weaker global growth sentiment weighed on metals, with traders still net short. Aluminium dipped, while nickel rose.

title: TSX futures kick off week on copper boost, Middle East conflict weighs
summary: Reuters reports TSX futures rose modestly as copper prices edged upward, supported by a weaker dollar. The piece also notes Middle East conflict concerns that limit risk appetite and watches for energy market moves. Overall, the near-term market signal is a copper-led boost to materials sentiment.

title: TNR Gold NSR Royalty Update - Los Azules Copper, Gold and Silver Project - McEwen Copper Closes ARS $42 Billion Investment by Stellantis
summary: TNR Gold reported McEwen Copper’s Los Azules copper project secured an additional ARS $42 billion Stellantis investment, increasing Stellantis’s ownership. The deal includes amendments to copper cathode purchase rights, defining “market price” and a minimum 10,000 tonnes per annum cathode offtake. Proceeds will advance project development.

title: Benton Intersects Copper-Rich Massive Sulfides in Early Drilling at Great Burnt Copper-Gold Project, Newfoundland
summary: Benton Resources said drilling at Newfoundland’s Great Burnt Copper-Gold Project intersected semi-massive and massive sulfides with significant chalcopyrite in four holes, including multiple thick intervals of copper mineralization. Drilling is continuing (GB23-05 underway). The company highlights strong expansion potential for its main copper zone.

title: Flying Nickel Closes Private Placement for Proceeds of $600,705 with Norway House Cree Nation as Minago's Strategic Partner
summary: Flying Nickel Mining closed a non-brokered private placement raising about $600,705 at $0.079/share, with Norway House Cree Nation as sole investor and strategic partner. Proceeds fund exploration and working capital for the Minago nickel project in Manitoba. The announcement may modestly support near-term nickel sentiment via development progress expectations.

title: Alaska Energy Metals Intersects Nickel Sulfide Mineralization Over Significant Widths, Nikolai Nickel Project, Alaska
summary: Alaska Energy Metals reported assay results from initial holes at its Nikolai Nickel Project, intersecting long, persistent nickel sulphide mineralization (about 0.23% Ni over ~341m and ~296m) with accompanying copper. The company says results validate historical drilling and may accelerate a maiden resource.

title: Wisconsin Aluminum Foundry to Expand its Manufacturing Facility, Remodel Office Space
summary: Wisconsin Aluminum Foundry plans to expand its Manitowoc manufacturing facility by adding 50,000 square feet and renovate office space. The firm makes aluminum and copper-based alloy castings and expects the expansion to open in March. Financing includes $11 million in New Markets Tax Credits, supporting ongoing production capacity.

title: Copper slips as upbeat dollar, high inventories weigh
summary: Copper prices slipped on Tuesday as the U.S. dollar strengthened ahead of Powell’s speech and as elevated LME inventories weighed on sentiment. Reuters notes weaker demand indicators, including falling Chinese copper imports. LME aluminium also fell slightly and nickel eased, reflecting broader industrial-metals softness.

title: Nickel Sulfate Supply and Demand Weak_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports the October 16 battery-grade nickel sulfate index at 32,236 yuan/ton, up 36 yuan/ton from the prior day, with the market broadly flat. Battery-grade nickel sulfate is quoted at 32,100–33,000 yuan/ton. Supply and demand remain weak and quotations unchanged, indicating muted near-term pressure.

title: Jubilee Metals : to process Mopani Copper Mine slag after JV agreement -October 17, 2023 at 03:07 am EDT
summary: Jubilee Metals Group said it won a “large” Mufulira slag-processing contract with Mopani Copper Mines via a joint venture. The JV targets about 13 million tonnes of historical slag with estimated copper content (plus cobalt), expanding recovery from the existing MCM facility at Mufulira.

title: American Eagle Drills 900 Metres of 0.50% Copper Equivalent from Surface in the North Copper Zone at NAK
summary: American Eagle Gold reported drill hole NAK23-12 intersecting 900m of 0.50% copper equivalent from surface in its North Copper Zone, including higher-grade intervals (e.g., 540m at 0.61% CuEq) and notable copper grades.
