title: 'How valuable is it?': Barrick CEO questions worth of Teck Resource's key copper project as costs mount
summary: Barrick CEO Mark Bristow questioned Teck’s value for its Chilean QB2 copper project as capital costs were raised again to about $8.6–$8.8 billion due to delays and engineering changes. Teck defended QB2’s long-life outlook. The piece also notes Cobre Panama political uncertainty.

title: Cemac: export prices for ores and metals are up 2%, despite a fall in gold and aluminum prices
summary: Bank of Central African States data show Cemac export commodity prices up 2% QoQ in Q3 2023, driven by higher iron and manganese. However, aluminum export prices fell 2.5% after a 5.8% drop in Q2, indicating local aluminum pressure. Gold also declined, but only aluminium is tracked here.

title: Glencore exits Australian copper but future still bright for nation's critical minerals sector, expert says
summary: Glencore will close its remaining Australian copper operation at the Mount Isa mine in 2025, but it will keep running the Mount Isa smelter. The piece highlights Australia’s copper demand backdrop, continued investor interest, and government funding to accelerate critical-minerals projects, supporting bullish near-term copper sentiment despite the mine exit.

title: Ricoh and Siemens Collaborate to Advance Industrial Aluminium Binder Jetting for Mass Production
summary: Ricoh and Siemens are collaborating to develop binder-jetting for serial mass production of aluminium alloy components using inkjet printing and sintering. The technology is currently proof-of-concept, with trials involving European automotive firms for EV parts, aiming to cut costs and waste and support early commercialization.

title: Gunmen Free Former Dictator From Prison in Bauxite-Rich Guinea
summary: Gunmen freed a former dictator from prison in bauxite-rich Guinea, highlighting security and political disruption in a major aluminium raw-material region. Such events can threaten or delay bauxite production and logistics, tightening near-term supply expectations and typically weighing on aluminium prices in the coming days.

title: Suriname seeks to attract investors to develop bauxite in country's west
summary: Suriname’s government is inviting investors to develop new bauxite projects in the Bakhuis area in western Suriname, aiming to improve access, training, and maritime accessibility. Bauxite is the primary source of aluminum. While projects have previously failed, the initiative may bolster expectations for future aluminum supply and sentiment.

title: The amplitude of world prices for nickel in 2023 remains unstable — Stanislav Kondrashov — Пресс-релизы
summary: The piece attributes nickel price weakness to China’s recession-driven lack of demand and persistent global oversupply. It cites Indonesia’s rising nickel output, China shifting toward lower-grade intermediate nickel, and a sharp drop in Class 1 refined nickel imports, leading Kondrashov to forecast prices staying under pressure near term.

title: Chinese companies are investing billions in Indonesia's nickel industry — but working conditions can be deadly
summary: Chinese investment in Indonesia’s nickel refining has been linked to deadly workplace accidents and alleged forced-labour practices. Indonesia’s Human Rights Commission is investigating conditions at major refining hubs. The risks of regulatory action, production interruptions, and added compliance costs could worsen nickel supply expectations in the near term.

title: Chinese companies are investing billions in Indonesia's nickel industry — but working conditions can be deadly - 05-Nov-2023
summary: The story says Chinese companies are investing billions in Indonesia’s nickel industry, highlighting both the scale of capital inflows and concerns about deadly working conditions. While labor risks may pose longer-run regulatory or safety costs, the main near-term takeaway is expanded investment in nickel supply.

title: Police Blotter: Woman Thinks Someone Switched Her Electrical Box; Copper Cable Stolen From Utility Poles
summary: A facility technician for AT&T reported about 60 feet of copper cable stolen from utility poles, likely over the weekend, with an estimated replacement cost around $800. The incident appears localized with no broader supply or demand disruption, making near-term copper price impact unlikely.

title: Trends in global nickel production and use – Stanislav Kondrashov — Пресс-релизы
summary: The piece attributes last year’s nickel price rise to geopolitical factors, but says Indonesia boosted nickel output by 54%, reaching 3.3 million tons and about half of global supply. It notes spot prices eased below $20,000/mt, while EV battery demand is expected to keep growing, tightening long-term supply.

title: Copper holds steady as higher supply offsets dollar support
summary: Copper prices held in a tight range as investors balanced higher supply and uncertain demand against support from a weaker U.S. dollar. China’s slower winter consumption and uneven recovery added demand uncertainty. The report also shows mild easing in LME aluminium and a decline in LME nickel, alongside small overall moves.

title: London copper climbs on dollar support
summary: London copper rose 0.4% as a weaker U.S. dollar supported commodity prices and China stimulus improved risk appetite. The move was limited by slower seasonal winter demand in China and slowing destocking/inventory rises. LME aluminium and nickel edged higher, reflecting the same supportive financial backdrop despite mixed demand signals.

title: Nickel Ore Prices Dip Amid Softening Demand, Indonesia Has Granted Temporary Quotas For Nickel Ore Mining To Address Supply Crunch _SMM
summary: Ni 1.5% nickel ore prices reportedly fell to $59/wmt CIF, down $2 on the week. SMM attributes the dip to weakening demand and Indonesia’s temporary nickel ore mining quotas for Q4 2023, which alleviates the prior supply crunch. Indonesian local plants also plan fewer purchases from the Philippines.

title: Chinese Electrowinning Nickel Rivals Norilsk Nickel, Discouraging Some Traders From Signing Long-Term Agreements For The Latter_SMM
summary: China’s electrowinning nickel output is ramping up, with domestic product priced cheaper than Norilsk nickel of similar quality. This weakens Norilsk’s spot competitiveness and contributes to growing Norilsk inventory accumulation. SMM research also says some domestic nickel plate traders are reluctant to sign long-term Norilsk contracts due to electrowinning nickel.

title: The future of the global nickel market: growing demand for batteries and sustainable production — Stanislav Kondrashov — Пресс-релизы
summary: The piece argues nickel demand is rising from both EV batteries and stainless steel, highlighting Indonesia, the Philippines, and Russia as top production countries. It cites rapidly increasing Indonesian output, large nickel reserves, and new EV-battery processing plants, suggesting tightening fundamentals could underpin near-term nickel price strength.

title: SK Nexilis starts copper foil production in Malaysia
summary: SK Nexilis started commercial production at a new copper foil plant in Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, aimed at demand from electric-vehicle battery makers. The facility is the company’s first overseas plant and is expandable with a second line planned. Malaysia capacity is slated to rise substantially in 2024.

title: SMM data: Copper concentrate shipments and arrivals data  SMM spot copper concentrate TC & shipments and arrivals (Unit:1,000 mt)   _SMM
summary: SMM presents copper concentrate shipments and arrivals data and spot copper concentrate TC information (units in 1,000 mt). The excerpt is mainly a data-source/processing disclaimer and does not include the actual shipment or TC changes, so near-term directional price impact cannot be determined from the text alone.

title: As of 15:00 CST November 6, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease98.83, a decrease of 47.46 from the day before _SMM
summary: SMM data as of 15:00 CST on Nov 6 shows the copper cathode spot trading intensity index decreased 98.83, down 47.46 from the previous day. The update is presented as reference data, implying reduced copper cathode trading activity in the immediate market.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay and American West Metals Expand the Extensive Near-Surface Copper Mineralization at the Storm Copper Project, Canada
summary: Aston Bay and American West report further RC drilling assays at the Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, identifying thick, high-grade near-surface copper intervals and defining an expanded footprint at the 4100N Zone. Management says mineralization remains open and potential exists to extend north-east, supporting copper discovery and resource expectations.

title: Copper hits one-month high ahead of key China data
summary: Copper rose to one-month highs as a weaker U.S. dollar and China’s commitment to boost imports encouraged fund buying ahead of key Chinese economic data. Aluminium also hit a one-month high on low Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks, falling LME-approved inventories, and China Yunnan output cuts from power curbs.

title: Universal Copper Receives Poplar Exploration Permit for a Further Five Years
summary: Universal Copper announced a five-year renewal of its exploration permit for the Poplar copper project and added additional drill sites, with further work planned (including IP surveying and a second peripheral permit). The release is development-focused and does not indicate near-term production changes, so immediate copper price impact is limited.

title: Panama's congress lets First Quantum continue copper mining contract
summary: Panama’s congress struck a clause that would have revoked First Quantum’s Cobre Panama copper mining contract and instead sent the matter to the Supreme Court. The company said production is uninterrupted, though protests caused some on-site disruptions. Analysts expect the mine to keep operating through the uncertainty, easing supply-risk fears.

title: Chile copper miner Codelco's production dips 5.3% in September - Cochilco
summary: Chile’s state-run copper miner Codelco reported a 5.3% year-over-year production decline in September, according to Cochilco. Reuters notes operational issues and high debt, with production having reached a 25-year low last year. The drop implies reduced near-term copper output from a key supplier.

title: Chile copper production uneven in September - Cochilco
summary: Chile’s copper production in September was uneven, with state-run Codelco slipping 5.3% year-over-year to 116,700 tonnes due to operational issues. Escondida rose 25.5% and Collahuasi increased slightly. Overall Chile output still climbed 2.2% to 444,000 tonnes, per Cochilco.

title: Taseko Mines Limited - Taseko Receives Additional Financing for Florence Copper
summary: Taseko said it received approvals for two US$50m financing transactions for its Florence Copper Project in Arizona: a royalty from Taurus and a senior secured project loan from Societe Generale. Funds are intended to support construction and development of the commercial production facility, following permitting completion.

title: Billionaire-owned Vedanta seals Zambian copper assets deal
summary: Vedanta and Zambia sealed an agreement returning Konkola Copper Mines (KCM), including the smelter, to Vedanta after the 2019 state seizure and lengthy legal disputes. The government’s 20% stake remains. Vedanta plans around $1.2 billion in investment, enabling board reappointments and withdrawal of court challenges.

title: Vedanta seals Zambian Konkola copper assets agreement
summary: Vedanta and Zambia signed an agreement that returns Konkola Copper Mines (KCM) to Vedanta, ending a years-long state seizure and ownership dispute. Zambia’s ZCCM-IH officially handed back the copper assets in Lusaka. The resolution is expected to unlock investment and improve copper supply outlook, supporting sentiment.

title: USMW low-carbon aluminium differentials at zero, with growing interest
summary: Fastmarkets assessed its US Midwest low-carbon aluminium differential P1020A at zero on Nov. 3, with demand for low-carbon units in the US described as sluggish and no premium being paid. Some customer inquiries exist, mainly for beverage cans, automotive and construction, but near-term pressure is limited.

title: Kingston council motion calls for consequences for copper thieves | Brockville Recorder & Times
summary: Kingston council plans to consider a motion to curb copper thefts by tightening salvage-yard licensing and regulation, improving reporting requirements, reducing cash sales, and seeking more court resources. The city cites $1.5 million repair costs and safety impacts from theft of copper wiring and piping components.

title: Ero Copper Announces US$105 Million Bought Deal Financing
summary: Ero Copper announced a US$105 million bought-deal financing to fund growth initiatives at its Brazilian copper operations, including the Tucumã Project and Caraíba Operations, plus exploration and general corporate purposes. The news is primarily about capital raising, not near-term changes to production or physical copper flows.

title: Kingston council motion calls for consequences for copper thieves | Kingston/Frontenac This Week
summary: Kingston council will consider a motion to curb copper thefts by tightening licensing and regulation of salvage yards, improving reporting and cash-transaction limits, and seeking more resources for prosecutions. The city cites about $1.5 million in repair costs and reduced theft incentives as the core rationale.

title: Vancouver's Taseko Mines raises US$100M for Florence copper project
summary: Taseko Mines secured two financing deals totaling US$100 million for its Florence copper project in Arizona. Tarus will fund a 1.95% gross-revenue royalty and Société Générale provides $50 million in senior debt. Power and transport infrastructure are in place, but first copper is expected late next year/early 2025.

title: Taseko receives approvals for additional financing for florence copper
summary: Taseko says it has secured US$100 million in additional project financing for its Florence Copper Project in Arizona, including a US$50 million royalty investment approval and a US$50 million senior secured debt credit approval. Proceeds are intended to fund construction toward commercial copper production in coming months.

title: US launches anti-dumping probe into aluminum imported from Vietnam
summary: U.S. petitioners filed with the Department of Commerce seeking antidumping duties on aluminum extrusions imported from Vietnam. Fourteen Vietnamese firms were accused of dumping, with margins cited around 41.84%. Vietnam’s authorities warned exporters to cooperate with the probe, which could reduce imports and support aluminium prices.

title: US launches anti-dumping investigation of aluminum products from Việt Nam
summary: The US Department of Commerce launched an anti-dumping investigation into aluminum extrusions and products from 15 countries, including Vietnam. The alleged dumping margin for Vietnam is 41.84%. Duties would follow only if the ITC finds injury to the US industry. The process may constrain imports over coming weeks.

title: US launches anti-dumping investigation of aluminum products from Vietnam
summary: The US Department of Commerce launched an anti-dumping investigation into aluminum extrusions and products from Vietnam and 14 other countries, prompted by US labor union petitions. Vietnam’s alleged dumping margin is 41.84%. Duties are possible only if the ITC finds injury, affecting near-term aluminum import expectations.

title: China's October copper imports jump amid low stocks, solid demand
summary: China’s October copper imports rose 23.7% year on year to 500,168 tonnes, supported by low domestic inventories and solid end-demand from construction, transport and power sectors. Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks hit a 13-month low, while stimulus measures and a higher Yangshan copper premium point to stronger buying and bullish copper sentiment.

title: Copper concentrate production in Armenia down 13.4% in 9 months of 2023
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate production fell 13.4% year-on-year to about 208,740 tons in January–September 2023, according to the National Statistics Committee. The country also reported lower zinc concentrate output, while molybdenum production rose. The copper slowdown points to weaker supply momentum.

title: LX International to acquire 60% stake in Indonesian nickel mine
summary: LX International said it will invest 133 billion won to acquire a 60% stake in Indonesia’s AKP nickel mine and secure management rights and the entire offtake. It plans phased production increases and aims to more than double annual output over time, shifting toward battery minerals like nickel.

title: NorthWest Copper Provides Update on Exploration Plans
summary: NorthWest Copper Corp. updated plans for its 2024 exploration program, including drilling and geologic work across multiple copper-gold prospects (e.g., Kwanika-Stardust and Lorraine). Work is conditional on funding and final budgets. The news supports future resource pipeline but does not indicate immediate supply changes.

title: Key Takeaway From SMM Metal Industry Annual Conference : Global Aluminum Market's Current And Future, Driven By New Energy Demand_SMM
summary: SMM’s conference takeaway highlights persistent domestic aluminum supply fluctuation risk, including an expected 1.15 million mt Yunnan capacity cut. It links fast-growing photovoltaic power and aluminum PV frames/extrusions demand to higher aluminum usage, while noting tight 2023 supply-demand balance and rising spot prices and profits in September.

title: Codelco Significantly Slashes 2024 Copper Premiums To Chinese Buyers_SMM
summary: Codelco has set 2024 copper premiums for its major Chinese contract buyers at $89/mt, down 36% from $140/mt in 2023. The sizable reduction signals weaker pricing for copper delivered to China under long-term terms, likely pressuring market expectations for near-term copper prices.

title: PAN GLOBAL INTERSECTS 1.04% COPPER OVER 15.9 METERS AT WESTERN EXPANSION OF LA ROMANA COPPER-TIN-SILVER DISCOVERY
summary: Pan Global reports high-grade copper intersections at its La Romana copper-tin-silver discovery, including 15.9m at 1.15% CuEq1 (1.04% Cu) from 79m, and says mineralization remains open and extends over more than 1.35 km. It also notes pending results and plans more drilling, but no production impact.

title: EU, US fail to reach agreement on Global Arrangement on Sustainable Steel and Aluminium
summary: EU-US talks on GASSA collapsed without agreement on measures to limit high-carbon steel and aluminium contributing to overcapacity and to support lower-carbon production. Sources expect negotiations to be stalled and any year-end outcome to be partial, likely focused on the tariff-rate quota framework rather than carbon provisions.

title: Pacific Ridge Intersects 113.0 M of 0.48% Copper Equivalent or 0.71 g/t Gold Equivalent Within 485.7 M of 0.27% Copper Equivalent or 0.40 g/t Gold Equivalent at the Kliyul Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration reported diamond drilling results from its Kliyul copper-gold project, including 113 m grading 0.48% copper equivalent and other intervals with similar CuEq levels. The release is an exploration update expanding mineralized zone extents, with no production or supply changes, so near-term copper pricing impact is likely limited.

title: Firm dollar and China angst weigh on copper
summary: Copper fell 1% from a one-month high as a stronger U.S. dollar pressured dollar-priced commodities and China’s trade data pointed to uneven recovery. The article also notes aluminium down 1% and nickel down 2.5%, indicating broad industrial-metals weakness tied to demand concerns.

title: Closure Plan Approved for Generation Mining's Marathon Palladium-Copper Project – Major Milestone Met
summary: Ontario accepted and filed the Closure Plan for Generation Mining’s Marathon palladium-copper project. The company cites progress on additional environmental permits and expects further approvals. The project is forecast to produce sizable payable copper, so permitting progress is supportive for copper sentiment, though near-term output won’t change immediately.

title: Copper, cobalt supplies from Congo stranded by truckers' strike
summary: Truckers’ strike in DR Congo is stranding roughly 2,700 trucks carrying about 89,000 tons of copper in Kolwezi and halting exports from major mines, raising near-term supply tightness. Reuters notes expectations for a small copper surplus could turn to a deficit if the strike persists.

title: Peru Mine Spending at Eight-Year Low Signals Copper Tightening
summary: The piece (via its headline) says Peru’s mine spending is at an eight-year low, suggesting producers may be underinvesting. That can translate into slower capacity additions or reduced output maintenance, tightening near-term copper supply expectations and supporting higher copper prices over the coming weeks.

title: Zambia, Indian firm sign agreements to revitalize Konkola Copper Mines
summary: Zambia’s ZCCM-IH and India’s Vedanta signed agreements for the operation of Konkola Copper Mines (KCM), moving the restructuring toward a scheme of arrangements and a return of Vedanta’s control. The government said it aims to restart activity, boosting payment to suppliers and workers, which supports near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Peru miners say copper output could climb without impact from protests
summary: Peru’s copper producers expect output to rise in 2024 if next year’s operations proceed without social conflicts. Early-2024 protests caused stoppages that hurt supply, and the government’s investment outlook is weaker. SNMP says projects could be worth $3-3.5 billion and licensing should be granted this year.

title: Congo Trucker Strike Blocks Exports of Copper and Cobalt
summary: A trucker strike in Congo is said to be blocking copper exports. By disrupting transport and outbound shipments, the move is likely to reduce near-term available supply in the market, tightening inventory conditions and supporting higher copper prices in the short run.

title: Aluminium Deutschland reports 'sharp decline' in German aluminium production in Q3 2023
summary: Aluminium Deutschland says German primary aluminium production nearly halved in Q3 2023, while raw aluminium output fell and semi-finished volumes declined sharply, citing weak orders and high energy costs. It warns energy-market tension and poor industrial competitiveness, pointing to demand headwinds in construction and automotive sectors.

title: AD/CVD Extruded Aluminum ITC Preliminary Injury Investigation
summary: Parties argue before the U.S. ITC over a preliminary injury investigation into allegedly subsidized/dumped aluminum extrusions. Petitioners cite surging accused imports and urge cumulation and broad coverage, while respondents argue limited injury due to other constraints. The process may ultimately lead to AD/CVD duties affecting aluminum extrusion import flows and pricing.

title: LNG And Offshore Energy Projects Face Delays As Nickel Prices Soar
summary: The article says aerospace demand has rebounded strongly, boosting procurement of corrosion-resistant nickel alloys and extending lead times. This is tightening supply for high-nickel materials, pushing nickel spot prices higher in Europe and the US and raising near-term pricing risks despite lower raw-material costs.

title: Suriname bauxite project may attract interest from Indian, Chinese companies
summary: Suriname’s presidential commission says Indian, Chinese and Middle East firms have informally shown interest in a bauxite concession in the Bakhuis region, with deposits estimated at 324 million tons. The government plans to award the concession by November 2024, with detailed power and logistics proposals due late January.

title: Zambia, Indian firm sign agreements to revitalize Konkola Copper Mines-Xinhua
summary: Zambia’s investment arm and Vedanta signed agreements to restart operations at Konkola Copper Mines (KCM). The government says the deal will help regulate the business and resolve outstanding issues, aiming to revive production and ensure workers, suppliers and contractors are paid. Vedanta holds 80% of KCM.

title: Protests against the exploitation of a copper mine show the clash between two environmentalisms in Panama
summary: Thousands protest in Panama against extending a contract for First Quantum Minerals’ copper mine in a protected biological corridor. Congress fast-tracked the extension and the Supreme Court is expected to rule after appeals. Given Panama’s importance and possible production interruption risk, near-term supply uncertainty could support copper prices.

title: Copper under pressure on dollar strength, hazy demand outlook
summary: Copper prices were subdued, with the article citing a stronger U.S. dollar and a hazy, weaker demand outlook for the metal used in power, construction and transport. It also references softer expectations for China’s 2024 copper growth. Some supply disruptions were noted but did not offset bearish drivers.

title: Muted copper concentrate trading, TCs awaiting guidance from CIIE_SMM
summary: SMM reports muted spot trading of imported copper concentrates in China, with spot purchases by smelters slowing and spot TCs easing. Concerns over pricing awaiting guidance from the CIIE/CESCO meeting are offset by expectations of improved trading. Copper concentrate inventories at seven ports fell week-on-week. Panama’s revised law raises mine uncertainty.

title: U.S. Virgin Islands declares state of emergency after lead and copper found in tap water in St. Croix
summary: The U.S. Virgin Islands declared an emergency after tests found lead and copper in tap water on St. Croix, warning residents not to ingest or cook with it. Authorities froze bottled-water prices and are continuing testing and monitoring. Water use is limited to showering and cleaning while resources are mobilized.

title: Paradigm Change in Copper Metal_SMM | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Copper prices are starting a new uptrend supported by historically low global inventories. The piece attributes gains to easing global liquidity post-epidemic and to rising labor, fuel, and other production costs, while electricity costs and sustaining capex are expected to ease. It also notes long mine production cycles limiting supply growth.

title: Trident Royalties PLC Announces Acquisition of US Copper Rich Polymetallic Royalty
summary: Trident Royalties PLC said it acquired a U.S. copper-rich polymetallic royalty. The transaction increases corporate exposure to copper-linked future revenues, which can modestly improve copper sentiment. However, the excerpt provides no details on near-term production impact, mine timing, or supply changes.

title: Russia's Nornickel : Some Clients Which Previously Rejected Buyin… - 2023-11-08
summary: Reuters/Interfax reports that some customers who previously rejected buying from Russia’s Nornickel are now in discussions about purchasing metals in 2024. The shift suggests renewed willingness to source Nornickel output, potentially improving expectations for nickel demand and pricing over the near term.

title: As of 15:00 CST November 8, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 80.72, a decrease of 14.18 from the day before _SMM
summary: SMM data show that as of 15:00 CST on Nov 8, the copper cathode spot trading intensity index fell to 80.72, down 14.18 from the previous day. The report is presented as reference data, but the lower trading activity suggests weaker immediate copper spot demand sentiment.

title: Kodiak Drills From-Surface Copper at Man Zone: 0.45% CuEq Over 116 m within 0.24% CuEq Over 338 m -November 08, 2023 at 06:05 am EST
summary: Kodiak Copper reported drill results from its MPD copper-gold porphyry project in southern British Columbia. Two Man Zone holes returned broad copper-bearing intervals, including 0.34% Cu over 116 metres and 0.25% Cu over 75 metres, confirming mineralization from surface to near 995 m depth.

title: Highland Copper Initiates Copperwood Site Activity and Provides Project Update
summary: Highland Copper announced it has initiated site activity at its Copperwood project in Michigan, completing required wetland impacts and starting environmental mitigation and pre-construction works while keeping permits in good standing. The company highlighted potential copper price sensitivity, technical optimizations, and progress toward project financing.

title: Highland Copper Initiates Copperwood Site Activity and
summary: Highland Copper says it has initiated site activity at its Copperwood project in Michigan, completing required wetland impacts and starting environmental mitigation/pre-construction work under state permits. The company notes the project is sensitive to copper prices and continues technical optimizations and potential funding efforts, but no near-term output change is described.

title: Benjamin Hill Announces Start-Up of Inaugural Diamond Drill Program at Alotta Copper-Gold Project in West-Central Yukon
summary: Benjamin Hill Mining announced the start of an inaugural diamond drill program at its Alotta copper-gold project in Yukon, targeting IP chargeability anomalies coincident with copper/gold geochemical signals. No production or supply changes were reported; the news mainly reflects early exploration progress and does not directly affect near-term market fundamentals for copper.

title: ArcWest Exploration Inc.: ArcWest Provides an Exploration Update for its Oweegee Porphyry Copper-Gold Project in B.C.'s Golden Triangle
summary: ArcWest Exploration reports completion of a 2023 deep IP survey for its Oweegee porphyry copper-gold project in British Columbia, expanding a “Junction” chargeability anomaly to a 1 by 2 km drill target. The release also references prior Delta Zone drilling with copper grades, but provides no production or supply impact.

title: Rio Tinto, Codelco partner up to find more copper in Chile
summary: Rio Tinto and Chile’s Codelco formed the Nuevo Cobre joint venture to explore and potentially develop copper assets in Chile’s northern Atacama region. The announcement is directly tied to future copper production prospects, but it is not expected to materially shift near-term supply or inventories in the next few weeks.

title: Mining Stock News: Benjamin Hill (CSE: BNN) Announces Start-Up of Inaugural Diamond Drill Program at Alotta Copper-Gold Project in West-Central Yukon
summary: Benjamin Hill Mining Corp. announced the start of an inaugural diamond-drilling program at its Alotta copper-gold project in Yukon, targeting a chargeability anomaly coincident with copper/gold geochemical results. The program will test two 500-metre holes, but the release does not update resources or production, so near-term copper supply impact is limited.

title: Material Matters: The Outlook For Aluminium and Copper & Stock Picks
summary: Morgan Stanley turns bullish on aluminium, citing risks of tighter winter supply in China and declining LME inventories, alongside energy/production constraints. For copper, Citi/others flag near-term demand vulnerability (slower cyclicals, China property and EV uptake) with a widening surplus, though short-covering risks could support dips.

title: Material Matters: The Outlook For Aluminium and Copper & Stock Picks
summary: Morgan Stanley expects aluminium to outperform, projecting higher LME prices supported by declining LME inventories and possible winter supply cuts in China amid constrained power availability. It also notes a potential supply deficit re-emerging later. For copper, demand headwinds persist, but short-covering and potential supply downgrades could limit downside.

title: $115 million allocated to proposed nickel processing facility in Mercer County
summary: The U.S. Department of Energy allocated nearly $115 million for a proposed nickel processing facility in Mercer County, North Dakota. Talon Metals would ship nickel ore by rail from Minnesota for processing, with supply linked to Tesla. The project uses fly ash from coal processing to extract more nickel.

title: Rio Tinto, Codelco form JV for copper exploration in Chile
summary: Rio Tinto and Codelco have formalised a JV for Chile’s Agua de la Falda copper exploration project after Rio Tinto bought a 57.74% stake from PanAmerican Silver. The JV, “Nuevo Cobre,” aims to focus on prospective copper discoveries, but the news is exploration-focused rather than production.

title: Over 127,000 tons of copper produced from underground mine of Mongolia
summary: Mongolia’s Oyu Tolgoi underground copper-gold mine has produced over 127,000 tons of copper since starting in March, according to local media. The report highlights the project’s role in Mongolia’s long-term plans, but the production output also points to greater copper supply in the near term.

title: India's NALCO posts Q2 profit rise on strong aluminium demand
summary: NALCO reported a Q2 profit rise, driven mainly by its aluminium segment where pre-tax profit increased nearly 14%, supported by strong aluminium demand. The company benefits from India’s ramped-up infrastructure spending ahead of general elections. Revenue fell due to higher raw material costs, while Hindalco is set to report next.

title: Over 127,000 tons of copper produced from underground mine of Mongolia-Xinhua
summary: Mongolia’s Oyu Tolgoi underground mine has produced more than 127,000 tons of copper since it began in March, according to local media. Prime Minister Oyun-Erdene highlights the project’s importance for national development. Oyu Tolgoi is expected to average about 500,000 tons of copper per year from 2028–2036.

title: As of 15:00 CST November 9, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 29.75, a decrease of 50.97 from the day before _SMM
summary: SMM reported that its copper cathode spot trading intensity index fell by 29.75 as of 15:00 CST on Nov 9, down 50.97 from the prior day. The data suggests reduced spot trading activity in the copper cathode market versus the previous session.

title: More public input needed on changes to aluminum smelter emissions, EPA says
summary: The EPA said South Carolina’s DHEC must seek more public input before the Mt. Holly Century Aluminum plant can raise emissions limits, after environmental groups challenged permit changes processed as “minor modifications.” The changes would have increased particulates by ~50% and sulfur dioxide by ~one-third, but the process is now under scrutiny.

title: China's Jiangxi Copper boosts First Quantum stake after stock rout
summary: Jiangxi Copper raised its stake in First Quantum to 19.5% after buying 1.35 million shares. The move follows Panama actions to revoke the contract for First Quantum’s Cobre Panama flagship mine, but Reuters notes operations are continuing and the company is on track to meet next fiscal-year production.

title: Hot Topics in International Trade - November 2023 - New Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Investigation Initiated Covering Aluminum Extrusions from 15 Countries | Braumiller Law Group, PLLC
summary: U.S. authorities initiated antidumping and countervailing duty investigations covering aluminum extrusions from 15 countries, expanding prior AD/CVD scope and reducing exclusions, including for further-processed extrusions. Estimated dumping margins for some countries are very high, with preliminary rulings due later in 2023–2024, which could raise near-term aluminum costs.

title: Hudbay Is in Talks to Draw Partner for Arizona Copper Project
summary: Hudbay said it is in talks to draw a partner for its Arizona copper project. Such partnership discussions can be viewed as a positive step toward advancing development and financing, which may support near-term expectations for future copper supply and bolster copper market sentiment.

title: Century Aluminum Company (NASDAQ:CENX) Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Century Aluminum’s earnings call discusses Q3 falling LME and regional premiums, low inventory positioning for potential recovery, and China deficits versus smelter curtailment risks. It also highlights higher-than-expected power costs, Jamalco outage recovery, and the IRA Section 45X aluminum production tax credit, pending Treasury guidance.

title: Jiangxi Copper boosts First Quantum stake on Cobre Panama hit
summary: Jiangxi Copper, First Quantum Minerals’ largest shareholder, increased its stake in the Canadian miner. First Quantum is still dealing with heavy losses tied to uncertainty over the future of its flagship Cobre Panama copper mine in Panama. The mine outlook uncertainty can influence near-term copper supply expectations and sentiment.

title: Global Ferronickel net income dips to P1.5B - BusinessWorld Online
summary: Global Ferronickel Holdings reported higher revenues, driven by increased volume of high-grade nickel ore from its Palawan mine and an improved sales mix. The average realized nickel ore price rose to $31.93/WMT. Costs increased, but improved pricing and output are likely supportive for nickel market sentiment.

title: Nickel Shaw Project, Canada
summary: Nickel Shaw is a planned open-pit mine in Yukon producing nickel and copper concentrates (along with PGMs). The pre-feasibility study was completed in August 2023, with 19.1 years of mine life and $1.68bn pre-production capex. The article lacks any new short-term operational or supply-shift catalyst.

title: Indian aluminium producer Hindalco misses Q2 profit view on lower prices, demand
summary: Hindalco missed Q2 profit expectations as LME aluminium prices fell 5.1% sequentially and alumina declined 4.1%. India’s aluminium factory activity grew, but at the slowest pace in five months. Hindalco’s U.S. unit revenue dropped, while its copper revenue rose on higher shipments.

title: As of 15:00 CST November 10, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 32.63, a decrease of 2.88 from the day before _SMM
summary: SMM data show the copper cathode spot trading intensity index as of 15:00 CST on Nov 10 fell to 32.63, down 2.88 from the previous day. The report is reference data and implies reduced copper spot trading activity, which can weigh on short-term copper prices.

title: SMM social inventories of copper in China's major trading markets (1kt) _SMM
summary: SMM reports “social inventories” of copper in China’s major trading markets (1kt data series), based on publicly available information and SMM’s internal model. Such inventory readings can influence short-term copper price expectations by signaling near-term supply tightness or looseness, though the excerpt lacks the actual inventory levels or change direction.

title: Inflation is retreating and stocks are recovering. So why is copper in the dumps?
summary: Copper is sliding about 15% from a January high to around $3.62/lb, with producers underperforming. The article cites persistent demand risks (China property weakness, weak Europe, high U.S. rates, slower EV adoption) and “unprecedented” supply growth from expansions and new projects, suggesting further bearish pressure into coming months.

title: Hudbay seeks partners for copper project in Arizona, US
summary: Hudbay Minerals is seeking partners for its Copper World copper project in Arizona, starting informal discussions on potential minority stake divestment or joint venture to fund development. The mine is projected to produce about 85,000 tonnes of copper annually. Company expects strong partner interest from smelters and trading houses.

title: CEO.CA's Inside the Boardroom: Latest News From Emperor Metals, Doré Copper and Baselode Energy -November 10, 2023 at 07:35 am EST
summary: CEO.CA interviews executives including Doré Copper Mining. Doré recently announced positive “Lock Cycle” flotation test results from its Corner Bay copper-gold project, citing high copper recoveries (98.2% and 96.8%) and high concentrate grades (27.0% and 29.6%). Other featured items relate to gold and uranium exploration.

title: 'We are powerless': Indian villagers live in fear of torture in fight against bauxite mine  | Mining
summary: Villagers in Odisha’s Rayagada protest Vedanta’s planned Sijimali open-pit bauxite mine, alleging police violence, intimidation, arrests, and pressure to halt resistance. Activists also cite recent forest-law changes weakening community consent. The disputed bauxite project could face delays, tightening bauxite supply expectations for aluminium.

title: Shortage of Raw Materials Challenges the Copper-Clad
summary: A market report on copper-clad laminates says manufacturers face a growing shortage of copper foils, with strained supply chains from strong demand for notebooks, handsets, and automotive electronics. The copper-foil constraint is expected to hamper production, potentially supporting tighter conditions for copper prices near term.

title: 'We are powerless': Indian villagers live in fear of torture in fight against bauxite mine
summary: Villagers in Banteji, Odisha, say police raids and violence by company officials have occurred as they fight a proposed bauxite mine. The conflict threatens operations and local approvals for bauxite extraction. Any near-term disruption to bauxite supply could tighten alumina inputs and support aluminium prices.

title: SC aluminum smelter eyeing expansion with new power deal | Business
summary: Century Aluminum secured a new three-year electricity deal with state utility Santee Cooper to restart the remaining 25% of its Mount Holly aluminum pots. The contract provides enough power to lift annual capacity to about 225,000 tons, subject to market conditions and permitting steps. Company also plans further investments using sale proceeds.

title: Olympics-Decision on aluminium surfing judges' tower by end November – Paris 2024 | WTVB | 1590 AM · 95.5 FM
summary: Paris 2024 will decide by end-November whether to build an aluminium judges’ tower and related infrastructure for surfing events in Teahupo’o, Tahiti. Local residents and a petition oppose it due to potential reef damage, while officials consider alternatives like reusing prior foundations or reverting to a wooden tower.

title: Killings of striking teachers in Panama fuel mass protests against major copper mine
summary: Protests in Panama have escalated after Congress approved a renewed 40-year deal for First Quantum’s Minera Panama copper mine despite court and environmental concerns. Roadblocks and brief port disruptions threaten logistics. The government also signals possible future mining restrictions, increasing the risk of near-term copper supply strain.

title: Indonesia seeks U.S. partnership on nickel for EV batteries
summary: The U.S. and Indonesia plan talks on a potential EV-battery minerals partnership focused on nickel, with discussions tied to U.S. IRA tax-credit rules and environmental requirements. Indonesia has large nickel reserves and seeks export-coverage and an EV supply chain, which could lift near-term expectations for nickel demand and pricing.

title: Copper Thefts Warning | Scoop News
summary: Electricity Networks Aotearoa warns that copper theft from power lines is increasing, driven by cost-of-living pressures. ENA chief executive Tracey Kai says cutting cables is extremely dangerous and can disrupt power supply for local households. ENA urges public vigilance and reporting suspicious activity to police.

title: London copper edges higher on firm equities; demand woes linger
summary: London copper edged higher to about $8,052/t, supported by firmer equities, but stayed near a two-week low as a stronger U.S. dollar and China demand uncertainty weighed. LME aluminium dipped and nickel rose, reflecting mixed sentiment. Chile’s Codelco production guidance added minor context.

title: Copper subdued as firm dollar, demand worries dominate mood
summary: Copper hovered near a two-week low as a firm U.S. dollar and uncertainty about China’s and Europe’s recovery weighed on demand expectations. Investors awaited U.S. inflation for rate outlook clues. China stimulus needs also raised concerns. Aluminium was steady and nickel rose modestly, but copper sentiment remained bearish.

title: Panama court likely to revoke First Quantum copper mine contract
summary: Reuters reports Panama’s top court is likely to rule against First Quantum over its Cobre Panama copper mine contract. Lawyers cite precedent and note a government bill banning new mining concessions and extensions, which could prevent renegotiation. Revocation risks output disruption and investor concerns, supporting upside copper sentiment near term.

title: Eramet Earmarks $2 Billion for Nickel and Lithium Expansion
summary: Eramet earmarked about $2 billion for expansion focused on nickel (and lithium). While full production ramp-ups may take longer, the announcement can support market sentiment by improving prospects for future nickel supply, influencing expectations over the next several weeks.

title: Copper gains as bearish traders cancel short positions
summary: Copper prices rose on Monday after bearish traders covered shorts, lifting three-month LME copper about 1% to $8,115/t. Gains were limited by uncertainty over economic growth, high interest rates, and weaker China demand signals. Aluminium rose slightly; nickel fell, reflecting broader mixed base-metal sentiment ahead of data.

title: Trafigura brings Australian mined copper back to China -sources
summary: Trafigura is assisting Chinese smelters with customs clearance for Australian copper concentrate shipments, suggesting an informal ban on Australia-origin concentrate is being lifted. A reported 10,000 tonnes cargo from Western Australia is en route to Shandong. The easing of curbs may reduce smelters’ political and supply concerns.

title: Analysis-Panama court likely to revoke First Quantum copper mine contract
summary: A Yahoo analysis reports that Panama’s court is likely to revoke First Quantum’s copper mine contract. The prospect of disrupted or halted operations increases near-term uncertainty over copper supply, tightening expectations for output and inventory levels and adding upward pressure to copper prices over the next days to weeks.

title: U.S. and Indonesia Discuss Nickel Trade Agreement Amid Biden's Push for Clean Energy
summary: The U.S. and Indonesia plan discussions aimed at a nickel-focused mineral trade agreement tied to Biden’s Inflation Reduction Act EV tax credits. IRA rules favor minerals processed in the U.S. or FTA countries, raising demand for Indonesian nickel. The U.S. may also seek exclusions for nickel processed in China.

title: First Quantum Workers At Panama Copper Mine Down By 25% On Monda…
summary: Reuters reports that First Quantum reduced workers at its Panama copper mine by about 25% to roughly 3,000 on Monday because protesters are blockading the port. The disruption is likely to curtail production and/or shipments, tightening near-term copper supply expectations and supporting prices.

title: EV Minerals Engages IOS Services Geoscientifiques for 2023 Exploration at EV Nickel Project in Saguenay- Lac- Saint-Jean Region, Quebec
summary: EV Minerals engaged IOS Services Géoscientifiques to oversee its 2023 exploration program at the EV Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in Quebec. Work includes desktop target refinement, confirmatory drilling on a historical nickel/copper resource, exploratory drilling on a TDEM anomaly, and metallurgical testing. Drilling has commenced.

title: Copper treads lower; US inflation data in focus
summary: Copper prices edged down as the US dollar firmed, while traders awaited key US inflation data to gauge whether the Fed may raise rates further. Powell’s recent comments have tempered hopes the hiking cycle is ending. LME aluminium and nickel showed only slight moves, suggesting mainly macro-driven effects.

title: Goldman Sachs advises going long on some commodities and is optimistic about copper and aluminum_SMM
summary: Goldman Sachs expects commodity prices to rise in 2024, citing a less hawkish Fed and lower recession risk. The note forecasts oil around $80–$100/bbl and is optimistic on industrial metals, projecting an average copper price of about $9,200/mt in 2024 and positive expectations for aluminium.

title: Goldman Sachs advises going long on some commodities and is optimistic about copper and aluminum_SMM
summary: Goldman Sachs advises a long stance on commodities, citing a less hawkish Fed and lower recession risks that should support demand. It expects crude oil to trade within $80–100/bbl in 2024 and is also optimistic on copper and aluminium, projecting average copper around $9,200/mt in 2024.

title: Si6 jags high-grade copper-silver in Botswana
summary: Si6 Metals announced jagged high-grade copper-silver drill intersections at its Dibete project in Botswana, including 2m at 4.2% copper and 268g/t silver, tied to geophysical anomalies. The results strengthen the perceived copper sulphide potential in early drilling, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: As of 15:00 CST November 14, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 27.37, a decrease of 2.08 from the day before _SMM
summary: SMM data shows the copper cathode spot trading intensity index as of 15:00 CST on November 14 decreased by 27.37, representing a 2.08 decline from the day before. This suggests reduced spot trading activity and weaker immediate copper cathode market momentum.

title: Canadian Copper Inc.: Canadian Copper Provides Regional Exploration and Caribou Mine Restructuring Update
summary: Canadian Copper reports trenching and exploration at its Murray Brook West project and updates on court-supervised efforts to restart the former Caribou Mine. The company notes existing toll-milling infrastructure and argues Murray Brook could extend mine life, but no clear near-term production or shipment figures are provided.

title: DLP Resources Inc.: DLP Resources Intersects 138m of 0.68 % CuEq* Within an 881.95m Interval of 0.46% CuEq* on the Aurora Project in Southern Peru and Discovers New Copper Oxide Zone to the East of the Current Drilling
summary: DLP Resources reported complete results for drillhole A23-012 at its Aurora copper-molybdenum project in southern Peru, including long intervals of copper-bearing mineralization and discovery of new copper oxide showings east of current drilling. The company plans further sampling and continued drilling, with results expected later this year.

title: New Antidumping And Countervailing Duty Investigation Initiated Covering Aluminum Extrusions From 15 Countries - International Trade & Investment
summary: U.S. Commerce initiated antidumping and countervailing duty investigations on aluminum extrusions imported from 15 countries. Petitioners allege widespread dumping and subsidization and seek expanded scope, including previously excluded alloys and third-country processed products. Potential affirmative AD/CVD findings could raise import costs and tighten aluminum extrusion supply.

title: Benton Resources Inc.: Benton Continues to Intersect Copper-Rich Semi-Massive/Massive Sulphides in Drilling, up to 25.42m Thick at Great Burnt
summary: Benton Resources reports continued drilling success at its Great Burnt copper-gold project in Newfoundland, including multiple wide intercepts of semi-massive/massive sulphides and high copper grades (up to 8%+ over substantial lengths). The update is exploration-focused with no immediate supply or production change.

title: VR receives NOI drill permit for New Boston, and prioritizes drill targets for the copper-moly-silver porphyry system in western Nevada.
summary: VR Resources says it received its first NOI drill permit for the New Boston property in Nevada, prioritizing the East Zone copper conductor for its first-pass drill program. The article describes DCIP survey results, planned drill targets, and prior copper intersections, but no production or supply disruption is mentioned.

title: Eramet plans to increase lithium and nickel output
summary: Eramet plans to invest €1.9bn from 2024-2026 to expand lithium and nickel capacity. It aims to double nickel output at Indonesia’s Weda Bay mine, rising from ~30 million wet metric tonnes this year to 60 million by 2026. The supply outlook is negative for nickel prices.

title: Nevada Copper Corp. Provides Updates on Recent Operational Developments At Its Pumpkin Hollow Underground Mine
summary: Nevada Copper Corp. provided updates on its Pumpkin Hollow underground mine, reporting ramp-up progress in lateral development, completion of ore stopes ready for extraction, and notes on concentrate deliveries in prior months. The company also reported preliminary drill results and emphasized priorities like cleaning stockpiled underground ore and waste.

title: Europe's Raw Materials Challenge: the Copper Industry is Ready to Contribute, but not alone! – EURACTIV.com
summary: EU Raw Materials Week coverage highlights policy measures to secure strategic raw materials for net-zero technologies. It emphasizes copper’s role and the need to streamline permitting and lower energy costs for electricity-intensive production. It also notes recycling regulation could benefit metals including nickel, supporting medium-term supply expectations.

title: Police shut down scrap metal business as part of a large-scale copper theft investigation
summary: Police shut down a scrap metal business and arrested suspects linked to more than 50 copper thefts valued at about $780,000. The group allegedly cut copper cabling at telecommunications pits using power tools. A second-hand dealer reportedly handled over $250,000 of stolen metal, now facing charges for handling stolen goods.

title: First Quantum's Panama copper drama another ESG flash-point for miners
summary: First Quantum has reduced processing at its Cobre Panama copper mine due to escalating protests, including port blockades affecting shipments to a power plant. Legal challenges may void the contract. The disruption threatens near-term copper concentrate supply from a large new project, adding downside risk to copper prices.

title: Environmental groups say either this Indiana aluminum plant cleans up its act or they'll sue
summary: Environmental groups (Sierra Club and Environmental Integrity Project) intend to sue Alcoa’s Warrick aluminum smelter for Ohio River water pollution permit violations. They cite repeated excesses, including mercury and other discharge limits (including aluminum, copper, nickel). The notice allows 60 days to comply, implying potential compliance costs but no shutdown detail.

title: Aluminum Prices Struggle As Demand Dwindles
summary: Aluminum prices are described as range-bound but facing bearish signals: global premiums have eased sharply, with U.S. Midwest and Europe duty premiums at multi-month lows. Norsk Hydro reported steep drops in aluminum sales, and LME dynamics show ample Russian material in warehouses amid weaker industrial and real-estate demand.

title: Scrap metal business shut down over copper 'heists'
summary: Police in Melbourne shut down a scrap metal business and arrested multiple suspects over copper thefts worth more than $780,000. The thefts involved cutting telecom cabling, disrupting services. Authorities also targeted a second-hand dealer allegedly receiving $260,000 in stolen copper, tightening disposal channels.

title: GIADEC, Rocksure International Presents MRE Results on Nyinahin Bauxite Resources to President
summary: Ghana’s GIADEC and Rocksure International presented updated MRE results for bauxite at Nyinahin Block B, with resources revised upward (at least ~375MMT vs prior ~250MMT). The government-linked initiative aims for local refinery and smelter development, improving investor confidence for the Integrated Aluminium Industry and supporting aluminium sentiment.

title: Gold, Copper Rise as Cool US CPI Eases Bets on More Fed Hikes
summary: The article headline says gold and copper are rising as US CPI cools, reducing market expectations for additional Fed rate hikes. The implication is a near-term tailwind for copper from improving macro/rates sentiment, likely via weaker yields or dollar support.

title: Houghton County Board of Commissioners supports Highland Copper Company's Copperwood Mine project
summary: Houghton County commissioners voted to support Highland Copper Company’s Copperwood Mine project. The resolution cites the company’s transparency, environmental commitment, and potential economic benefits. Highland Copper estimates the mine will produce about 6,600 tons of ore daily and plans to begin construction soon, boosting copper project sentiment.

title: Class-action lawsuit filed against aluminum plant after emissions incidents
summary: A class-action lawsuit was filed against the Mt. Holly Century Aluminum smelting plant over multiple alumina dust emissions incidents. The EPA recently ruled in favor of a petition to stop polluting and require more public input before permit changes. DHEC is investigating and may assess penalties if permit violations are found.

title: China Oct aluminium production at record monthly high
summary: Reuters reports China’s October primary aluminium production rose 6% year-on-year to a record monthly high of 3.62 million tonnes. Smelters benefited from much higher profits, cheaper power and firm demand, but the surge in output lifts near-term supply expectations for aluminium.

title: Goose Creek residents announce lawsuit against Century Aluminum over alumina emissions
summary: Goose Creek residents filed a class-action lawsuit against Century Aluminum, alleging increased alumina/aluminum oxide particulate emissions linked to malfunctions in emissions control systems on Sept. 3, 16, and 30 and earlier in 2023. The suit seeks damages, citing health impacts and property and pet harm.

title: City taking aim at copper and metal thieves | Chatham This Week
summary: Brantford is tightening scrap-yard bylaws to make it harder to sell stolen copper and other metals: scrap dealers must notify police within 24 hours, require traceable identification, and ban cash transactions. The city cites many theft reports since 2019 and expects reduced theft-driven metal flows, though effects may be local and limited.

title: Copper near 5-week high as dollar softens on dovish Fed bets
summary: Copper traded near a five-week high as the dollar weakened following softer U.S. inflation data, boosting dovish Fed rate-cut expectations. LME copper was steady-to-higher and Shanghai copper rose. The report also shows LME aluminium gaining slightly, while nickel fell on the day.

title: Two old mines set to build Hot Chili copper resources
summary: Hot Chili has entered option agreements to acquire two historically mined copper areas near its Costa Fuego hub in Chile and plans scout reverse-circulation drilling starting next week. The company aims to expand high-grade and bulk-tonnage copper resources feeding its production ramp ahead of a Costa Fuego prefeasibility study.

title: City taking aim at copper and metal thieves | Brantford Expositor
summary: Brantford plans tighter scrap-yard rules to curb copper and metal theft, including restricting accepted items, requiring police notification within 24 hours, and banning cash transactions without traceable identification. The city cites hundreds of copper theft reports since 2019, but notes thieves can divert material to outside-city or online markets.

title: City taking aim at copper and metal thieves | The Stratford Beacon Herald
summary: Brantford council is tightening scrap-yard bylaws to curb copper and metal theft by restricting accepted items, requiring police notification within 24 hours, and banning anonymous cash transactions. Officials cite hundreds of theft reports since 2019. The firm argues thieves can reroute supplies outside the city, so effects may be limited.

title: ASIA COPPER WEEK-Copper concentrate market to face concentration shortage by 2025 - Jiangxi Copper
summary: Jiangxi Copper’s vice president said Asia’s copper market will face a copper concentrate shortage by 2025 as smelting capacity expands faster than mining output. China’s smelters rely on importing about 70% of concentrate. CRU expects a surplus next year and a 342,000-ton deficit in 2025.

title: City taking aim at copper and metal thieves | The West Elgin Chronicle
summary: Brantford city council is tightening scrap-yard bylaws to curb copper and metal theft, including limits on accepting certain items, requiring police notifications within 24 hours, and banning cash transactions. Officials cite hundreds of theft reports since 2019, but acknowledge theft may shift to yards elsewhere.

title: City taking aim at copper and metal thieves | The Woodstock Sentinel Review
summary: Brantford’s city council plans to tighten scrap-yard bylaws to curb copper and metal thefts, including banning cash transactions, requiring traceable identification, and notifying police within 24 hours of certain purchase offers. The goal is to make stolen copper/metal harder to monetize, though thieves may use yards outside the city.

title: City taking aim at copper and metal thieves | St. Thomas Times-Journal
summary: Brantford plans to tighten scrap-yard bylaws to make it harder to sell stolen copper and other metals. Dealers must notify police within 24 hours of purchases of frequently stolen items, require traceable ID, and end cash transactions. The city links theft revenue to broader social harms, but rerouting may blunt impact.

title: Hydro, UK EV startup WEVC partner up on low-carbon aluminium
summary: Hydro and UK EV startup WEVC will explore using Hydro’s renewable-energy, low-carbon and recycled aluminium for WEVC’s electric van. The low-carbon aluminium has a much lower CO2 footprint than the global average, aiming to cut the van’s embedded emissions and enable end-of-life recycling. Testing starts in 2024, with production in late 2025.

title: ASIA COPPER WEEK-China to expand imports of scrap copper -industry association
summary: China plans to expand the scope and volume of scrap copper imports, targeting 1.9 million tonnes in 2023 versus 1.75 million in 2022, according to an industry association official. Increased scrap inflows raise near-term supply for Chinese recyclers, which can pressure copper prices in the coming weeks.

title: Ero Copper closes $111m financing to support Brazil projects
summary: Ero Copper raised $111m through a bought-deal share financing to fund the Tucumã project and Caraíba operations in Brazil, plus working capital and exploration. Tucumã remains under development toward copper production in 2H next year, implying future incremental supply rather than a near-term market shock.

title: The Engineer - Hydro Extrusions and WEVC enter low-carbon aluminium extrusions partnership
summary: Hydro Extrusions and WEVC partnered to supply low-CO2, recycled aluminium extrusions for WEVC’s planned eCV1 electric light commercial vehicle. WEVC targets a >50% reduction in embedded production carbon and plans to explore closed-loop recycling. The deal may support low-carbon aluminium demand, but near-term price impact appears limited.

title: Hot Chili Continues to Expand its Costa Fuego Coastal Copper Hub in Chile
summary: Hot Chili says it has entered option agreements to acquire 100% interests in two historical copper mine areas, Marsellesa and Cordillera, near its Costa Fuego copper-gold project in Chile’s Atacama Region. The move expands its copper hub plans, but no immediate production timeline is provided.

title: Copper Fox Reports Positive Results from Solubility Testwork Outlines
summary: Copper Fox reported positive mineral solubility testwork for its 100% owned Van Dyke in-situ recovery copper project in Arizona. 72-hour leach results show high recoveries of acid- and cyanide-soluble copper and PLS grades up to 15.30 g/l, supporting plans for further geotechnical work and PFS-level studies.

title: Hudbay Further Enhances Financial Flexibility with Redemption of Remaining Copper Mountain Bonds
summary: Hudbay said its Copper Mountain subsidiary will redeem the remaining $54.7 million of senior secured 8% notes (Copper Mountain Bonds) around Nov. 30, 2023, using its revolving credit facility. The company expects improved deleveraging and flexibility, with bonds otherwise maturing in 2026.

title: Chile: Increasing copper production while preserving vital groundwater -November 15, 2023 at 10:22 am EST
summary: Chile’s Codelco is moving forward with the Aguas Horizonte desalination and pipeline project to supply multiple northern mines, reducing reliance on scarce groundwater. The infrastructure is designed to enable production increases at Chuquicamata, Ministro Hales and Radomiro Tomic, supporting Chile’s copper output capacity and near-term supply outlook.

title: The Engineer - Hydro Extrusions and WEVC enter low-carbon aluminium partnership
summary: Hydro Extrusions is partnering with WEVC to supply recycled, low-carbon aluminium for the eCV1 electric light commercial vehicle chassis, aiming to cut embedded carbon by over 50% versus other LCVs. The firms will also explore closed-loop recycling, potentially supporting demand for low-CO2 aluminium, though volumes appear limited near term.

title: Codelco's copper premium offer to South East Asia client drops 29% -sources
summary: Codelco offered copper cathode to a South East Asia client at an $85/mt premium for next year, down 29% from this year, while its premium to China fell to $89/mt, down 36%. Premiums are paid over the LME benchmark, so reductions suggest weaker physical tightness outlook.

title: Hudbay Minerals Inc.: Hudbay Further Enhances Financial Flexibility with Redemption of Remaining Copper Mountain Bonds
summary: Hudbay Minerals said its Copper Mountain subsidiary redeemed the remaining $54.7 million of its 8% senior secured Copper Mountain Bonds, using its revolving credit facility at a call price of 104% plus accrued interest. The company expects improved deleveraging and flexibility, with bonds otherwise maturing in 2026.

title: Vedanta Group sets up new unit in Saudi Arabia for copper business | Indiablooms - First Portal on Digital News Management
summary: Vedanta Group, via subsidiary Malco Energy Ltd, incorporated “Vedanta Copper International” in Saudi Arabia to pursue its copper business. The move is linked to broader restructuring and potential separate listings. The report does not specify production capacity or timelines, so near-term copper price implications appear limited.

title: Atico Mining Corporation: Atico Mining Reports Results on Brownfield Drilling Campaign to Extend Mine Life at El Roble High Grade Copper/Gold Mine in Colombia, Continues to Expand Tonnage with Intercepts up to 24.7m of 4.19% Cu, 3.11g/t Au, and 5.0m of 4.
summary: Atico Mining reported positive brownfield drilling results at its El Roble underground copper-gold mine in Colombia, including intercepts such as 24.7m at 4.19% Cu. The company says results extend historic massive sulfide bodies and could increase confidence in additional copper mineralization, with a resource update planned after more assays.

title: Atico Mining Reports Results on Brownfield Drilling Campaign to Extend Mine Life at El Roble High Grade Copper/Gold Mine in Colombia, Continues to Expand Tonnage with Intercepts up to 24.7m of 4.19% Cu, 3.11g/t Au, and 5.0m of 4.84% Cu and 12.26 g/t Au -November 15, 2023 at 04:31 pm EST
summary: Atico Mining reported positive brownfield drilling at its El Roble underground copper/gold mine in Colombia, including intercepts up to 24.7m at 4.19% copper and 5.0m at 4.84% copper. The company says results extend mine life and expand tonnage, with mineralization open at depth and along strike.

title: Proposed Brantford bylaw would crack down on copper and scrap metal thefts
summary: A proposed Brantford bylaw would crack down on copper and scrap metal thefts. By reducing theft-driven scrap loss, the measure could improve scrap recovery and supply for recyclers in the local market. This may offer mild near-term support to copper sentiment, with limited scope beyond Brantford.

title: Atico Mining Reports Results on Brownfield Drilling Campaign to Extend Mine Life at El Roble High Grade Copper/Gold Mine in Colombia, Continues to Expand Tonnage with Intercepts up to 24.7m of 4.19% Cu, 3.11g/t Au, and 5.0m of 4.84% Cu and 12.26 g/t Au
summary: Atico Mining reported brownfield drilling results at its El Roble underground copper-gold mine in Colombia, including intercepts up to 24.7m at 4.19% copper. Management says the results extend historic massive sulfide bodies, expand tonnage, and support an updated resource estimate.

title: Copper treads lower as US dollar strengthens
summary: Copper prices eased from near six-week highs as a stronger U.S. dollar—supported by retail sales and cooling inflation data—reduced demand for dollar-priced commodities and reinforced expectations that the Fed will cut rates later. In the same report, LME aluminium and nickel also fell modestly.

title: Hot Chili to buy two historical Chilean copper mine areas
summary: Australian explorer Hot Chili entered option deals to acquire the Marsellesa and Cordillera historical copper mine areas in Chile’s Atacama region. First-pass RC drilling is planned next week. The deals involve staged option payments and NSRs, but there is no stated production or near-term supply increase.

title: As of 15:00 CST November 16, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 120.69, a decrease of 30.08 from the day before
summary: SMM data as of 15:00 CST Nov 16 shows the copper cathode spot trading intensity index fell to 120.69, down 30.08 from the previous day. The decline signals reduced spot trading activity in copper, typically consistent with softer demand expectations and potential near-term downside price pressure.

title: NorthWest Copper Provides Business Update on Financial,
summary: NorthWest Copper provides a financial and operational update, including limited cash, significant prior legal/proxy-contest costs, and consideration of future financing (debt, rights offering with private placement, and flow-through funding) to support exploration. The company focuses on exploration rather than development and provides project strategy updates for 2024.

title: Bauxite mining to begin in Nyinahin – GIADEC
summary: GIADEC says mining of about half a million tonnes of bauxite from the Nyinahin range in Ghana will soon begin after completing a Mineral Resource Estimate and social impact analysis. The corporation highlights reserve size and responsible mining measures. The project could improve near-term expectations for aluminium feedstock supply.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Intercepts High-Grade Nickel-Copper Mineralization in 14 New Holes Located Outside of the Tamarack Nickel Project Resource
summary: Talon Metals reported assay results from 116 new drill holes at the Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project, including 14 exploration holes with high-grade nickel-copper massive sulphide intercepts outside the current resource. The company highlighted continued resource growth potential, particularly in CGO East and CGO West areas.

title: Talon Metals Intercepts High-Grade Nickel-Copper Mineralization in 14 New Holes Located Outside of the Tamarack Nickel Project Resource
summary: Talon Metals reported results from 116 new drill holes at the Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project, including 14 exploration holes intersecting high-grade nickel-copper mineralization outside the current resource. The company cites significant potential for resource expansion, with assays showing strong Ni and associated Cu grades in multiple new intervals.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Intercepts High-Grade Nickel-Copper Mineralization in 14 New Holes Located Outside of the Tamarack Nickel Project Resource
summary: Talon Metals reports assay results from 116 drill holes at Minnesota’s Tamarack nickel-copper project, with 14 exploration holes intersecting high-grade nickel-copper massive sulphides outside the current resource. The company cites potential for resource growth in the CGO East and CGO West areas, supporting longer-term supply expectations.

title: Talon Metals Intercepts High-Grade Nickel-Copper Mineralization in 14 New Holes Located Outside of the Tamarack Nickel Project Resource
summary: Talon Metals reported results from 116 drill holes at its Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project in Minnesota, including 14 exploration holes intersecting high-grade nickel-copper mineralization outside the current resource. Intercepts include several thick massive sulphide zones with elevated Ni and Cu assays, indicating potential resource growth.

title: Northstar Drills Multiple Horizons of High-Grade Volcanogenic Massive Sulphides at Historic Cam Copper Mine
summary: Northstar Gold reported preliminary Phase I drilling results at the Cam Copper Mine, a historic VMS copper producer, with high-grade copper intersections (including very high Cu zones) and notes zones remain open for down-plunge/strike expansion.
