summary: SMM says CSPT set Q1 2024 spot copper concentrate guidance TCs at $80/mt and 8.0 US cents/lb, down from $95/mt and 9.5 cents/lb in Q4 2023. The lower guidance implies softer concentrate pricing/treatment conditions for copper smelting in the near term.

title: Copper hovers near five-month high on soft dollar
summary: Copper prices in London were steady near a five-month high as a softer U.S. dollar—driven by expectations for potential Fed interest rate cuts—supported dollar-priced metals. Three-month LME copper was almost unchanged while SHFE copper edged higher. LME aluminium was flat and nickel slightly lower, reflecting mixed but mostly mild macro effects.

title: Death toll rises in furnace at Chinese-owned nickel plant
summary: An explosion at a Chinese-owned nickel smelter in Indonesia’s Sulawesi killed at least 18 workers and prompted police to order the plant to stop operating pending investigation. The incident is part of Indonesia-China nickel processing expansion, potentially disrupting near-term nickel output and supporting prices.

title: Great Southern Copper interim loss widens as costs increase
summary: Great Southern Copper reported a wider half-year pretax loss, driven by higher administrative costs, while stating it is well funded for ongoing exploration in Chile. Management links its outlook to accelerating demand for critical minerals such as copper as the energy transition progresses, but no near-term supply disruption is cited.

title: As of 15:00 CST December 28, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 38.1, a decrease of 14.26from the day before
summary: SMM data show that, as of 15:00 CST on Dec 28, the copper cathode spot trading intensity index fell 38.1 points, down 14.26 from the previous day. The lower spot trading intensity suggests reduced near-term demand/activity in the copper cathode market.

title: Asiamet Resources makes "significant progress" in BKM copper project
summary: Asiamet Resources said it made “significant progress” on the feasibility stage BKM copper project in Central Kalimantan, including advancing lead-bank credit committee approvals, securing positive feedback from an Indonesian bank, and moving engineering and environmental work toward 2024. The update supports long-term supply prospects but signals no imminent output.

title: Copper pulls back from near 5-month high on profit-taking
summary: Copper retreated from a five-month high as investors took profits ahead of year-end, with concerns about Chinese growth/property. Aluminium fell after LME inventories built to six-month highs. Nickel was the largest decliner as LME nickel inventories rose to levels not seen since July 2022.

title: President Joe Biden: Determined specified volumes of eligible steel, aluminum articles imports from EU will no longer threaten national security
summary: Biden determined that specified volumes of eligible EU steel and aluminium articles imports will no longer threaten U.S. national security. The decision excludes those volumes from tariff coverage through Dec 31, 2025 while keeping current tariffs for other countries. This likely supports aluminium supply expectations and prices.

title: Biden extends EU access to US tariff rate quotas for steel, aluminum for 2 years
summary: Biden extended the EU’s access to U.S. tariff rate quotas for steel and aluminum for two more years, excluding qualifying EU imports from the tariffs under Proclamation 9705 up to a designated quota through Dec. 31, 2025. The policy lowers trade barriers for aluminum into the U.S.

title: Biden extends EU steel, aluminum tariff exemption for 2 years
summary: Biden extended the suspension of U.S. tariffs on EU steel and aluminium for two years, keeping a tariff-free quota for EU aluminium (384,000 tonnes) and applying tariffs only beyond that limit. The move supports continued EU import volumes while negotiations on overcapacity and low-carbon production continue.

title: Biden Again Extends Tariff Suspension for EU Steel, Aluminum Imports
summary: The Biden administration extended the tariff suspension for steel and aluminum imports from EU members for two years, excluding certain EU aluminum articles from tariffs through Dec. 31, 2025. Easing trade barriers likely boosts expected U.S. aluminum supply and weighs on domestic prices, contributing to bearish sentiment.

title: Kutcho Copper Increases Financing
summary: Kutcho Copper Corp. increased a non-brokered private placement to up to $1.375M to fund the Kutcho Project and working capital. The offering details include unit pricing and warrant terms, subject to TSX Venture approval. The release is financing-focused, not a change to near-term copper supply or demand.

title: Police catch 3 people stealing copper in southeast Oklahoma City
summary: Oklahoma City police arrested three people for allegedly stealing copper pipes and wire while digging up and cutting metal near Southeast 29th Street and High Avenue. Authorities said the suspects planned to load the copper into a truck and sell it to scrap/recycling channels. Police noted scanner use during the theft.

title: Fire at Indonesian nickel smelter leaves 19 dead
summary: A fire at an Indonesian nickel smelter in the Morowali industrial park killed at least 19 workers and injured others. The incident occurred during furnace repairs, and unions threatened potential strikes over safety demands. Production risk and operational disruption at a major nickel processing hub are likely near-term bearish for nickel prices.

title: Avebury Nickel Mine survival optimism | The Advocate
summary: Avebury Nickel Mine avoided an abrupt shutdown and continued operating safely and productively after Mallee Resources entered administration and receivership. Management added drilling equipment and trucks while a sale process for the going concern is reportedly close, suggesting steadier near-term nickel supply.

title: Copper climbs on dollar support, set for yearly gain
summary: London copper rose as the dollar weakened, while expectations of tighter copper concentrate supply and thin global inventories supported sentiment. The piece cites firm Chinese demand despite property weakness. LME aluminium and nickel were mostly flat or slightly lower, suggesting the strongest near-term upside is for copper rather than aluminium or nickel.

title: Avebury Nickel Mine continues operations under new owner | The Examiner
summary: Avebury nickel mine continues operations under a new owner as Mallee Resources moved into administration and receivership this year. Management says the mine remained safe and productive, added drilling and trucks, and expects sale completion soon. Restarted production last year after years in care and maintenance.

title: US Extends Suspension Of Tariffs On EU Steel, Aluminum For 2 Years
summary: The US extended for two years the EU’s access to tariff-rate quotas for steel and aluminum and maintained suspension of tariffs on EU goods while negotiations continue. For aluminum, the tariff relief likely preserves freer import conditions into the US, which can weigh on prices through steadier supply expectations.

title: As of 15:00 CST December 28, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 103.2, a increase of 65.1 from the day before
summary: SMM data for Dec 28 (15:00 CST) shows the copper cathode spot trading intensity index decreased to 103.2, described as a change of 65.1 versus the prior day. The report is limited to trading-intensity monitoring and does not detail supply/demand fundamentals beyond this market-activity signal.

title: IMF Sees Further Upside Room for Prices of Nickel, Cobalt, Lithium, Copper and Other Metals Necessary for Electric Vehicle Batteries, Echoing Forecasts by the IEA
summary: The IMF warns that after the Russia-Ukraine conflict pushed metals higher, nickel and copper (along with other EV battery minerals) could rise further. It echoes IEA demand forecasts and notes supply-chain concentration risks, such as cobalt dependence on Congo, which may tighten expectations for critical metals.

title: IMF Sees Further Upside Room for Prices of Nickel, Cobalt, Lithium, Copper and Other Metals Necessary for Electric Vehicle Batteries, Echoing Forecasts by the IEA
summary: The IMF warned that following Russia-Ukraine-related increases, prices of metals used in EV batteries—especially nickel and copper—could rise further. It cited IEA forecasts of sharply higher long-run demand and highlighted concentration risk in key producing countries, implying potential supply-chain fragility.

title: Copper dips, but heads for yearly rise on healthy Chinese demand
summary: Reuters reports copper dipped on a firmer dollar but expects a modest yearly rise supported by healthy Chinese demand and hopes for U.S. rate cuts, alongside tighter concentrate supply. Nickel fell after LME inventories hit 18-month highs, signaling excess supply. Aluminium edged higher with smaller market impact than copper.

title: Core Nickel Completes Over-Subscribed Flow-Through Private Placement Financing
summary: Core Nickel Corp. has closed an oversubscribed flow-through private placement, issuing 4.35 million units for about C$392k to fund exploration work on its Halfway and Resting Lake projects and other programs. The company is a junior nickel explorer, so the news is only indirectly connected to near-term nickel pricing.

title: EU Suspends Retaliatory Tariffs on U.S. Imports and U.S. Extends TRQs on Imports of EU Steel and Aluminum as Bilateral Negotiations Continue
summary: The EU and U.S. extend a trade truce that suspends retaliatory tariffs on each other’s imports and extend tariff-rate quotas for EU steel and aluminum into the U.S. until end-2025. The policy aims to provide price stability and time for a broader steel and aluminum arrangement addressing carbon and overcapacity.

title: Biden Extends Tariff Suspension on EU Steel and  Aluminum
summary: Biden extended the U.S. suspension of tariffs on EU steel and aluminum for two more years through Dec. 31, 2025. The TRQ framework keeps EU quotas tariff-free but tariffs apply above quota. Easing aluminum trade frictions should bolster near-term supply expectations for aluminum in the U.S.

title: AGNICO EAGLE ANNOUNCES INVESTMENT IN CANADA NICKEL COMPANY INC.
summary: Agnico Eagle Mines acquired 19.6 million units of Canada Nickel Company at $1.18 per unit, including common shares and warrants. Canada Nickel’s Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project is in northern Ontario near Agnico’s operations. The deal represents early-stage investment and potential future nickel supply development.

title: Nickel is year's biggest metals loser: Bloomberg
summary: Bloomberg reports nickel is the worst-performing industrial metal, down about 45% on the LME this year. It says nickel may not recover soon as supply keeps expanding—especially from Indonesia—and demand growth has faded, leaving the market with growing surplus despite earlier shortage hopes.

title: Nickel is year's biggest metals loser: Bloomberg | Elliot Lake Standard
summary: Bloomberg says nickel is the worst-performing industrial metal this year, with an annual LME drop of about 45%. It argues prices may not recover soon due to continued supply growth from Indonesia’s new output and lackluster demand, while copper shows only a small gain.

title: Automotive Industry Embraces Eco-Friendly Aluminum
summary: Hydro says its new Cassopolis, Michigan plant (opened Nov 16) will produce recycled aluminum billets and ingots, enabling growth into U.S. extrusion and serving automotive demand. The facility uses low-energy recycling, electrification, and logistics improvements (rail spur), supporting a “green aluminum” supply shift, though no capacity figures are given.

title: Copper edges higher on China data, stimulus hope
summary: London copper edged higher as China manufacturing improved and investors looked for fresh stimulus, while SHFE copper benefited from low warehouse inventories. Aluminium and nickel were weaker on the firm dollar. Overall, the piece signals supportive demand expectations for copper but mixed impacts for other industrial metals.

title: Mechanism to monitor steel, aluminium products export at concessional rates to US in the making
summary: India and the US are setting up an internal/joint monitoring mechanism for Indian steel and aluminium exports under the US 232 framework. The US will allow imports of certain aluminium products from India without paying extra 10% duties, boosting outbound shipments and potentially increasing supply pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Latest News | Mechanism to Monitor Steel, Aluminium Products Export at Concessional Rates to US in the Making
summary: India will set up a mechanism to monitor exports of steel and aluminium products to the US at concessional rates under the US 232 framework. The US will allow imports from India without extra duties, reflecting reduced tariff pressure and agreed monitoring for up to 3.36 lakh tonnes annually.

title: Closure of Sterlite copper unit in Tamil Nadu: SC to consider hearing plea of Vedanta
summary: India’s Supreme Court agreed to consider Vedanta’s plea regarding the closure of its Sterlite copper unit in Tuticorin. The case stems from earlier court and state directions after protests over pollution and a sealing order in 2018. The review could influence expectations for near-term copper output.

title: EPA Proposes Revisions To Lead And Copper Rule - Environmental Law
summary: The EPA proposed revisions to drinking-water rules for lead and copper, requiring public systems to replace all lead service lines and certain galvanized lines within ten years, update inventory tracking, and tighten sampling protocols. The government would fund compliance, potentially increasing near-term demand for plumbing materials such as copper.

title: Magnitude 7 aluminium smelter in Missouri mulling over closure
summary: Magnitude 7 Metals’ Missouri aluminium smelter may close by end-2023 unless a buyer or power-cost relief is found. High electricity costs threaten production, despite efforts involving Renew Missouri and lawmakers. Industry expects shortages may be manageable via Canada, and the US aluminium premium has already declined.

title: Copper under pressure from climbing dollar
summary: Copper prices fell as the U.S. dollar strengthened early in European trade, pressuring dollar-priced commodity demand. Losses were partly offset by improving China factory activity data and sharply lower Shanghai inventories, but cash discounts indicated doubts about near-term demand.

title: Canada Nickel Completes Private Placement of Flow-Through Units & Announces Agnico Eagle as an Investor
summary: Canada Nickel completed a C$34.7m flow-through private placement at C$1.77 per unit, with Agnico Eagle becoming about a 12% shareholder. Management says proceeds will fund continued advancement of its Timmins Nickel District and related initiatives. The deal may mildly improve sentiment on near-term nickel supply prospects.

title: Canada Nickel : Investor Presentation - January 2024 -January 02, 2024 at 07:27 am EST
summary: Canada Nickel’s investor presentation highlights the Crawford nickel sulphide project with detailed economics (NPV/IRR), expected nickel production, and a mid-2025 permitting target. It argues the nickel market is structurally tight outside Indonesia/China and suggests a new North American supply source could emerge, supporting nickel sentiment.

title: Ivanhoe Mines' Exports Commence from Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex Along Lobito Atlantic Rail Corridor
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says the first 1,100-tonne trial shipment of Kamoa-Kakula copper concentrate arrived at Angola’s Lobito port via the Lobito Atlantic Rail Corridor, cutting transit time versus road. The rail link is expected to lower logistics costs for future copper exports, supporting supply confidence.

title: Canadian North Resources Inc. Reports Results of Borehole Geophysical Surveys Indicating Extensions of Deep Nickel-Copper-PGM Sulfide Zones at the Ferguson Lake Project
summary: Canadian North Resources reported BHTEM results from deep drillholes at its Ferguson Lake project, indicating the West Zone extends more than 200 metres down-dip with high-grade Cu-Ni-PGM sulphides. The findings support prospects for continued expansion, but they do not imply near-term changes to metal supply.

title: Canadian North Resources Inc. Reports Results of Borehole Geophysical Surveys Indicating Extensions of Deep Nickel-Copper-PGM Sulfide Zones at the Ferguson Lake Project
summary: Canadian North Resources reported borehole geophysical survey results indicating the West Zone at its Ferguson Lake project extends further down-dip by more than 200 metres at depths around 650 to >850 metres. The mineralization is described as Cu-Ni massive sulphides plus PGE zones, but no near-term production or supply changes were announced.

title: Danieli & C Officine Meccaniche S p A : Azienda Metalli Laminati relies on Danieli for its new, copper-foil rolling mill -January 02, 2024 at 11:07 am EST
summary: Azienda Metalli Laminati is expanding its copper-foil production in Italy using Danieli Fröhling technology, adding about 10,000 tons/year capacity for brazed plate heat exchangers. Danieli will supply a new four-high reversing copper rolling mill. Startup is planned for autumn 2025, indicating limited immediate price impact.

title: White House Issues Presidential Proclamations Extending Section 232 TRQs on Steel and Aluminum Imports from the EU | Wiley Rein LLP
summary: The White House extended Section 232 tariff-rate quotas for EU aluminum imports in the U.S. until Dec. 31, 2025, keeping TRQ terms largely unchanged. EU aluminum shipments face extra duties only above specified quota thresholds. The EU also suspended some retaliatory tariffs, supporting continuity amid ongoing negotiations.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Announces the First Shipment of Copper Concentrate from the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex Has Arrived by Rail At the Atlantic Ocean Port of Lobito, in Angola
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said the first copper-concentrate trial shipment from the Kamoa-Kakula complex arrived by rail at the Port of Lobito, Angola. The Lobito corridor links the DRC Copperbelt to Lobito and should cut transit times and energy costs, supporting smoother copper exports.

title: GFNI, two units secure new nickel supply deal with China's Baosteel Resources
summary: GFNI said it has secured a new agreement with Baosteel for up to 1.5 million WMT of nickel ore for 2024, priced monthly based on prevailing market values. The ore will come from GFNI subsidiaries operating nickel mines in the Philippines, reinforcing nickel ore demand for Asia-Pacific buyers.

title: Gold miner Agnico Eagle Mines acquires minority stake in Canada Nickel
summary: Agnico Eagle acquired a 12% minority stake in Canada Nickel via a flow-through offering, supporting the development of the Crawford nickel-cobalt project in Ontario. The deal is an investment in critical minerals, but it does not directly change near-term nickel supply or demand conditions.

title: Gold miner Agnico Eagle Mines acquires minority stake in Canada Nickel | iNFOnews
summary: Agnico Eagle Mines bought a minority stake in Canada Nickel through a flow-through offering, purchasing 19.6 million units for about $23.1 million. Canada Nickel owns the Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project. The deal is framed as investment in critical minerals, but no near-term production change is indicated.

title: Agnico Eagle makes major investment in Canada Nickel
summary: Agnico Eagle completed a $34.7 million investment in Canada Nickel, buying 19.6 million flow-through units at $1.77. Canada Nickel says proceeds will fund work to advance its Timmins Nickel District and the Crawford Nickel Project, supporting development of future nickel supply.

title: Global Ferronickel renews supply deal with Baosteel - BusinessWorld Online
summary: Global Ferronickel said it will sell 1.5 million wet metric tons of nickel ore to Baosteel under renewed purchasing arrangements. The ore is sourced from its mines in Surigao del Norte and Palawan, with monthly pricing tied to prevailing market nickel prices, supporting nickel-related supply expectations in Asia.

title: Copper appears set to rally more than 75% by 2025, analysts say
summary: Copper is forecast to rally sharply as mining supply is disrupted and producers cut output, tightening the market. Demand support comes from renewable-energy expansion commitments and broader macro expectations, including potential Fed rate cuts and a weaker US dollar, improving affordability for foreign buyers.

title: Copper eases under dollar pressure, soft demand
summary: Copper prices eased as the U.S. dollar firmed on reduced expectations for early, aggressive rate cuts and as Chinese buying slowed with seasonal weak demand and strong domestic output. LME three-month copper and SHFE February fell, alongside a sharp drop in the Yangshan premium. Aluminium also slipped; nickel rose.

title: SMM analysis: Guinean ore is a key component in China's domestic alumina industry's ore mix
summary: A fuel depot explosion in Conakry triggered fuel sale restrictions and prompted worries about Guinean bauxite output and shipment stability. Guinea supplies most of China’s bauxite imports and is heavily used in alumina production. Alumina futures surged on the news, with analysts flagging higher alumina costs from feedstock price risk.

title: Strategic Expansion: PRM NETWORK Boosts Aluminum Scrap Supply in Korean Marketplaces
summary: PRM NETWORK says it is expanding and improving aluminum scrap deliveries into Korean marketplaces for aluminum casting and rolling firms. It highlights recycled aluminum’s energy savings and positions the firm as a standardized supplier through ISRI-aligned practices and regional distribution, aiming to boost supply availability for Korean producers.

title: Copper drops to two-week low on higher dollar, China doubts
summary: Copper fell to a two-week low as the U.S. dollar rose and China’s industrial demand worries intensified after weak December manufacturing PMI data. Expectations of surplus widened cash discounts. The article also shows softer LME prices for aluminium and nickel on the same risk-off, demand- and FX-driven backdrop.

title: Pacific Ridge Acquires 100% Interest in RDP Copper Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge exercised its option to acquire full (100%) interest in the RDP copper-gold project in northcentral British Columbia, after Antofagasta previously drilled and conducted surveys. The release highlights copper-gold intersections and future exploration plans, but provides no new production or supply/disruption changes for copper in the near term.

title: Teck signs option for Condor's Peruvian copper-gold project stake
summary: Condor Resources and Teck Perú signed an option/joint venture to advance Condor’s Cobreorco copper-gold project in Peru. Teck can earn 55% by investing $4m and paying $500,000, with additional spending to reach 75%. Drilling is contingent on obtaining permits, implying no immediate copper supply changes.

title: Benton Resources Inc.: Benton Intersects 5.51% Copper over 25.42m Including 8.31% over 9.78m in GB-23-12 at Great Burnt
summary: Benton Resources reported new drill results from its Great Burnt copper deposit in Newfoundland, including 25.42m at 5.51% Cu and other copper-rich intervals, with the high-grade lens expanded but still open. This is an exploration assay update with no immediate production changes.

title: Benton Intersects 5.51% Copper over 25.42m Including 8.31% over 9.78m in GB-23-12 at Great Burnt
summary: Benton Resources reported further assay results from its Great Burnt copper deposit in Newfoundland, including GB-23-12 grading 5.51% copper over 25.42m (with higher-grade sub-intervals). The company says the high-grade core is expanded along strike and down plunge and remains open.

title: As of 15:00 CST January 3, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 51.9, a increase of 36.27 from the day before
summary: SMM reports that, as of 15:00 CST on January 3, the copper cathode spot trading intensity index fell 51.9 versus the prior reading. The data is presented as a reference indicator, implying reduced spot market activity around copper cathodes that may weigh on near-term copper price sentiment.

title: Explosion at Indonesian nickel plant kills 19 workers
summary: An explosion at a Chinese-owned nickel smelter in Morowali, Sulawesi killed at least 19 workers and injured dozens. Operations were halted by police while investigations continue after a furnace accident involving molten metal residue and a subsequent fire. Workers protested demanding smelter shutdowns and better safety measures.

title: Benton Resources Inc. Intersects 5.51% Copper over 25.42M Including 8.31% over 9.78M in Gb-23-12 At Great Burnt
summary: Benton Resources announced assay results from Phase I drilling at its Great Burnt copper deposit in Newfoundland. The reported hole GB-23-12 intersected 25.42m at 5.51% Cu, including higher-grade intervals. Additional holes also returned copper-rich mineralization, supporting expansion potential of the high-grade lens.

title: Vedanta's aluminium production rises to 5,99,000 tonnes in December quarter
summary: Vedanta said its aluminium production rose 6% to 599,000 tonnes in the December quarter (up from 566,000 tonnes a year earlier). While zinc mined output fell and iron/steel output figures were also reported, the key development for metals markets is the higher aluminium output in India.

title: Indonesian Nickel Mining Firm AKP Unveils IPO and LXI Korea Acquisition
summary: Indonesian nickel miner AKP launches an IPO and after listing will sell 60% to South Korean buyer LX International via Energi Battery Indonesia. LX plans to expand nickel production capacity and supply battery-related offtake. The transaction value is about Rp 1.59 trillion, with AKP near Morowali.

title: Fire contained at Rusal-owned aluminium smelter in Siberia - agencies
summary: Reuters says emergency workers contained a small fire at Rusal’s Krasnoyarsk aluminium smelter in Siberia. The blaze started at a stand-alone electricity substation and produced smoke, but authorities reported no casualties and no impact on smelter operations. The incident may pose minor disruption risk given electricity dependence.

title: Operator of Morowali nickel plant may face penalties after deadly explosion
summary: Indonesia’s industry minister said the government may penalize ITSS, which operates a nickel smelter at Morowali’s IMIP, after a deadly explosion in late December 2023. Disciplinary steps would depend on an ongoing investigation, with criminal and safety violations handled by relevant ministries, raising near-term nickel supply risk.

title: Alba breaks annual aluminium production record
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba), one of the world’s largest aluminium smelters, reported record 2023 production of 1,620,665 tonnes, up 1.3% from 2022. The milestone indicates slightly higher aluminium output and potential supply pressure, but the retrospective annual framing suggests limited immediate impact on prices.

title: Alba breaks annual aluminium production record in 2023
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) says it produced a record 1,620,665 tonnes in 2023, up 20,554 tonnes (+1.3% YoY). As a large aluminium smelter, the higher output suggests greater supply than the prior year, which could pressure aluminium prices in the short term.

title: Aluminium slides on easing supply fears and revised rate expectations
summary: Reuters reports aluminium prices slumped after bauxite supply worries linked to a Guinea blast eased and investors reduced optimism for early U.S. rate cuts. Three-month LME aluminium fell about 1.5%. The piece also cites weaker LME copper and nickel prices, indicating broader metal correction tied to macro expectations.

title: Ivanhoe Mines ships copper concentrate by rail to Angola
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reports the first trial shipment of copper concentrate from the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex arrived at Angola’s Lobito port via the Lobito Atlantic Railway Corridor. The rail route is quicker and less energy-intensive than road shipments to other ports, aiming to cut logistics costs and carbon footprint for future copper exports.

title: How the copper plant in the Arctic city of Norilsk operates
summary: The piece explains how a long-running Norilsk copper smelter converts copper concentrate into anode copper, then refines it via electrolysis to produce pure copper sheets. It also mentions a planned sulfur-byproduct program that uses sulfur dioxide to make gypsum from 2026, with little detail on near-term output changes.

title: Ivanhoe Mines ships first copper concentrate by rail to Angola
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says the first trial shipment of Kamoa-Kakula copper concentrate has arrived at Angola’s Lobito port via the Lobito Atlantic Railway Corridor. The rail route is intended to cut logistics costs, transit times, and energy intensity versus road trucking, supporting more efficient copper exports from the DRC copperbelt.

title: Teck Resources says Quebrada Blanca copper production below guidance for 2023
summary: Teck Resources said copper production at its Quebrada Blanca mine missed 2023 guidance due to reliability and consistency issues in the fourth quarter. QB copper output totaled 56,200 tonnes versus guidance starting at 80,000 tonnes. Operations were ramping toward design capacity by end-Dec; updates expected Jan. 16.

title: Teck Resources says Quebrada Blanca copper production below guidance for 2023 | iNFOnews
summary: Teck Resources said copper production at its Quebrada Blanca mine in 2023 fell below guidance due to reliability and consistency issues in Q4. Output excluding copper cathode totaled 56,200 tonnes versus the bottom of the 80,000-tonne guidance range, with Q4 at 35,000 tonnes. Teck will report further results later.

title: Peruvian Miner Buenaventura Sees Antofagasta as Ally in Copper Growth Plans
summary: The piece suggests Peruvian miner Buenaventura sees Antofagasta as a partner for copper growth plans. While details aren’t provided in the excerpt, the collaboration framing is likely read as supportive for copper project momentum or supply expectations, which can modestly strengthen near-term copper sentiment.

title: First Quantum in talks with Jiangxi Copper on sale of stake in Zambian mines-source
summary: First Quantum said it is in talks with Jiangxi Copper to sell a stake in Zambian copper mines (Sentinel and Kansanshi) to raise finances after regulatory action against its Panama Cobre Panama asset. The potential transaction underscores shifting ownership/supply expectations for Zambia copper production.

title: First Quantum in talks with Jiangxi Copper on sale of stake in Zambian mines
summary: First Quantum is in talks with Jiangxi Copper to sell a stake in its Zambian copper mines to improve finances after Panama’s Cobre Panama was ordered shut. Fitch warned the shutdown could impair borrowing and trigger covenants. The possible deal could stabilize Zambia copper supply and sentiment.

title: Copper climbs on dollar strength; waning hopes of Fed rate cut cap gains
summary: Copper rebounded on Friday, supported by a weaker dollar and hopes tied to the Fed’s potential rate cuts, though gains were limited as December minutes suggested rates may stay high longer. Supply tension from low stocks in China supported prices. LME aluminium and nickel also rose modestly.

title: Copper edges up as supply headwind counters Fed rate cut outlook
summary: Copper prices edged up as supply concerns and thin Chinese stocks supported spot premiums, offsetting changes in investor expectations for U.S. Fed rate cuts. LME aluminium was stable and nickel slightly higher, but the main focus was copper’s supply-tightening backdrop and macro-driven risk appetite.

title: Copper exports to China cross $1b
summary: Pakistan’s copper exports to China have crossed $1 billion in the first 11 months of 2023, up 9% year-on-year. Officials expect shipments to keep rising as China produces more refined copper products and demand stays firm, supported by increased Chinese investment in copper projects.

title: Jubilee Metals set to cash in on Zambian copper venture
summary: Jubilee Metals Group approved a GBP13m equity raise to fund a Zambian “green copper” project using copper waste rock. Berenberg reiterated a “buy” rating, citing potential output from the dump and favorable margins under an $8,500/t copper assumption. The news is company-specific and not a major supply shock.

title: Phoenix Copper reaches final stage in bond issue to fund Empire mine
summary: Phoenix Copper says it is at an advanced stage in negotiations for a proposed bond financing to fund construction of its Empire open-pit copper mine in Idaho (80% interest). Bond issuance is contingent on investor discussions, and the company is also extending/enlarging a short-term loan for working capital.

title: European aluminium premiums trend upwards as other markets stabilize throughout holiday period
summary: European aluminium premiums rose over the two weeks to Jan 2, with higher liquidity at year-end and ongoing supply-side concerns linked to Red Sea shipping disruptions. LME spreads/contango were supportive, and duty-unpaid premiums increased. Italy premiums also rose, while demand was slower into January.

title: Aluminium P1020 premiums in Rotterdam rise 10% into new year after months of decline
summary: Rotterdam P1020A aluminium premiums rose about 10–15% since early December, supported by supply-side worries including UK sanctions on handling Russian metal and Red Sea shipment disruptions that lift freight costs. LME spreads and de-stocking ending also help, though demand is slower early in the year.

title: Stronger dollar pushes copper prices to three-week low
summary: Reuters reports copper at a three-week low as a stronger U.S. dollar and reduced odds of early Fed rate cuts pressured LME prices. It also notes nickel down on persistent surplus and improving LME warehouse stocks, while aluminium declined alongside broader weaker metals sentiment.

title: First Quantum in Talks to Sell Zambian Copper Mines Stake, Reuters Reports
summary: First Quantum Minerals is reportedly in talks to sell a stake in its Zambian copper mines to China’s Jiangxi Copper. Options discussed include buying Sentinel or Kansanshi or taking a stake. Details are not finalized and no transaction is confirmed, making any near-term copper price effect likely limited.

title: India News | Jindal Stainless Seeks Zero Customs Duty on Ferro Nickel, Ferro Molybdenum
summary: Jindal Stainless asked India’s Ministry of Steel for continued zero customs duty on stainless steel scrap, steel scrap and pure nickel, and for a long-term exemption on basic customs duty for ferro nickel and ferro molybdenum. It also sought measures against dumping and fixed tariff values for stainless steel.

title: First Quantum Mulls Stake Sale in Zambian Mines to Jiangxi Copper Amid Financial Strain
summary: First Quantum is reportedly negotiating to sell part or all of its Zambian Sentinel and Kansanshi copper interests to Jiangxi Copper to improve liquidity after Panama-related setbacks. The deal could secure financing and supply continuity for major copper assets, potentially supporting near-term copper market sentiment despite ongoing uncertainty.

title: Alaska Energy Metals Files NI 43-101 Technical Report for the Eureka Property, Nikolai Nickel Project, Alaska, USA
summary: Alaska Energy Metals filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Nikolai nickel project and plans updated resource estimation incorporating 2023 drill results. The report’s cut-off and pit shell were based on assumed nickel pricing, with copper included via Ni-equivalent calculations. No production or supply change is announced.

title: Automaker Thaco plans $4.1bn bauxite mining, alumina production complex in Vietnam's Central Highlands
summary: Vietnam’s Truong Hai Auto (Thaco) plans a $4.1bn circular complex in Lam Dong, including bauxite exploitation and a 4 Mt/y alumina factory, plus aluminum production. The project would expand alumina supply and follows existing Vinacomin bauxite/alumina operations. It’s multi-phase through 2033, but the announcement is sentiment-supportive for aluminium.

title: Copper dips on steady dollar ahead of US inflation data
summary: Copper prices opened lower as a steady dollar pressured dollar-priced demand ahead of upcoming U.S. inflation data that could shift Fed rate expectations. However, support came from signs of tighter supply, with Shanghai Metals Market’s copper ore/concentrate index falling, suggesting reduced availability. LME aluminium also dipped modestly.

title: Mount Isa Council's response to Glencore Copper mining closure | The North West Star
summary: Mount Isa Council is developing a response plan to Glencore’s announced closure of its Mount Isa copper mining operations and copper concentrator by late 2025, while keeping the refinery and smelters running. The council is pursuing projects like the CopperString powerline and critical minerals processing to mitigate local job losses.

title: FLSmidth to deliver Ball mills and HPGRs to a greenfield South American copper concentrator
summary: FLSmidth won a DKK 380 million order to supply ball mills and HPGR comminution technology for a greenfield copper concentrator in South America. The order is booked in Q1 2024 and equipment delivery is slated for 2025. The story supports copper project activity but offers no immediate supply impact.

title: American Eagle Intersects 302 Metres of 1.09% Copper Equivalent within 606 Metres of 0.74% Copper Equivalent
summary: American Eagle Gold reported drill hole NAK23-17 intersecting 302 m of 1.09% copper equivalent within 606 m of 0.74% copper equivalent at its NAK copper-gold porphyry project in B.C. The company plans a funded 2024 follow-up drill program to expand high-grade zones; no near-term production impact is stated.

title: QC Copper Presents Canada's Highest Grade Open Pit Copper Deposit with Opemiska's Updated Mineral Resource Estimate
summary: QC Copper announced an updated mineral resource estimate for its Opemiska open-pit copper project in Quebec, citing a 26% increase in copper grade and higher contained copper. The company says the updated resource supports upcoming economic studies, but the release does not indicate near-term production or supply changes.

title: American Eagle Gold Corp.: American Eagle Intersects 302 Metres of 1.09% Copper Equivalent within 606 Metres of 0.74% Copper Equivalent
summary: American Eagle Gold reported drill intercepts at its NAK copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia, including 302 m grading 1.09% copper equivalent and broad intervals of 0.74% CuEq. Results confirm continuity and potential expansion plans for 2024, but the update is unlikely to change near-term copper fundamentals.

title: QC Copper and Gold Inc: QC Copper Presents Canada's Highest Grade Open Pit Copper Deposit with Opemiska's Updated Mineral Resource Estimate
summary: QC Copper and Gold announced an upgraded mineral resource estimate for its Opemiska project in Quebec, citing higher copper grades and contained copper (and copper equivalent) within a conceptual open-pit starter framework. The release focuses on geology, metallurgy, and future economic studies, with no near-term production changes.

title: Leader of Ky. conservation group sees aluminum promise in tax credit opportunity
summary: Kentucky conservation and state lawmakers say a federal advanced manufacturing tax credit could help modernize and restart idle primary aluminum smelters, including Hawesville, which has been shut due to high energy costs. The piece argues aluminum demand is strong for batteries and vehicles, implying supportive near-term sentiment for aluminum.

title: Copper falls on firm dollar as market awaits steer on demand outlook
summary: Copper fell on the LME as the firm U.S. dollar pressured dollar-priced metals and traders awaited Chinese data for demand signals. Aluminium also declined as LME warehouse stocks hit their highest since June. Nickel retreated, with a short-term index-fund rebalancing window cited as a possible, limited offset.

title: Nickel 28 Releases Ramu 2023 Production and Provides 2024 Production Guidance
summary: Nickel 28 reports Ramu’s 2023 production of 33,604 tonnes of nickel and 3,072 tonnes of cobalt contained in MHP, and expects 2024 output of ~30,000 tonnes nickel and 2,700 tonnes cobalt. MCC plans a US$33 million upgrade with a 30-day September shutdown, while upgrades are expected to improve production performance.

title: PAN GLOBAL INTERSECTS 1.6% COPPER OVER 9.7 METERS CONFIRMING CONTINUITY OF LA ROMANA COPPER-TIN-SILVER DISCOVERY OVER 1.4KM
summary: Pan Global Resources announced new drill results from its La Romana copper-tin-silver discovery in Spain, extending near-surface copper mineralization over a 1.4 km strike length and identifying a higher-grade (1%+ and up to 7.7% copper) sector. Drilling will resume, supporting positive sentiment for future copper supply potential.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Provides 2023 Production Results and 2024 Production Guidance for the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reports Kamoa-Kakula produced 393,551 tonnes of copper in concentrate in 2023 (18% higher YoY, within guidance) and sets 2024 guidance at 440,000–490,000 tonnes, assuming Phase 3 concentrator completion in Q3 2024. The release also addresses power/grid upgrades to sustain operations.

title: Alumina price panic a sign of future aluminium volatility: Andy Home -January 08, 2024 at 07:45 am EST
summary: Chinese alumina prices surged after a Dec. 18 explosion at a Guinea oil terminal threatened bauxite shipments, jumping ~30% by early January. Even after panic eased, the higher alumina costs echoed into aluminium, lifting Shanghai primary and LME three-month aluminium, though prices later eased.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp.: Nickel 28 Releases Ramu 2023 Production and Provides 2024 Production Guidance
summary: Nickel 28 reports Ramu’s 2023 nickel production of 33,604 tonnes, above design capacity, despite earthquake-related downtime. For 2024, MCC plans a US$33 million upgrade requiring a 30-day shutdown in September, with guidance for about 30,000 tonnes of contained nickel in MHP.

title: Panoramic nickel mine in WA closes with 140 miners to lose jobs
summary: Administrators for Panoramic Resources in Western Australia have stopped mining at the Savannah nickel mine, with operations halting within days and about 140 company roles plus contractor jobs at risk. The decision is linked to further weakening in the nickel price, but the shutdown reduces near-term nickel output.

title: Blank-cheque firm ACG signs non-binding term sheet for copper mine
summary: ACG Acquisition signed a non-binding term sheet to seek a controlling stake in a copper mine in the EMEA region, estimated to produce 20-25 kt of copper annually. The transaction would require about $200 million in funding, but there is no certainty of a binding deal or financing.

title: Gunna Drinks founder opens aluminium bottling factory with £1m investment
summary: Gunna Drinks’ Sustainable Bottling Co has opened a new 8,000 sq ft aluminium bottling facility near Leicester, investing £1m and marketing it as a new UK/Europe capability for aluminium drinks bottles beyond water. The plant will supply Gunna and white-label aluminium bottling, implying incremental aluminium packaging demand.

title: Supreme Court denies Alaska's bid to revive the copper and gold Pebble Mine proposal blocked by EPA
summary: The Supreme Court denied Alaska’s bid to revive the Pebble Mine proposal, which had been blocked by the EPA. Because the project includes copper development, the decision reduces expectations for future copper supply, which can tighten near-term market outlooks and support copper prices.

title: LME copper cash to three month discount hits highest since 1992
summary: LME copper cash moved to a three-month discount at the highest level since 1992, reflecting expectations of ample supply. LME-approved copper stocks rose nearly 200% since July to 161,725 tonnes. Benchmark copper was slightly lower around $8,451/ton after hitting a recent low, consistent with bearish near-term pressure.

title: Supreme Court won't review EPA rejection of Alaska copper mine
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court will not review an EPA decision rejecting permits for an Alaska copper mine. With the legal challenge ended, the project is unlikely to proceed, reducing expectations for incremental copper supply and creating downward pressure on copper prices over the following weeks.

title: Metso to deliver primary gyratory crushers and apron feeders to two copper mines in Central Asia
summary: Metso signed contracts to deliver three Superior MKIII primary gyratory crushers and 18 apron feeders to copper processing plants in Kazakhstan and Mongolia. The EUR 30m+ order includes engineering and controls. Crushers are key to the mineral processing circuit, aimed at high throughput and reduced downtime for copper mines.

title: Alcoa to Curtail Output at Australian Alumina Plant to Cut Costs
summary: Alcoa said it will curtail output at its Australian alumina plant to cut costs. The move reduces alumina availability, which can affect input supply and operating costs for aluminium smelters, potentially tightening the aluminium market in the near term and supporting prices.

title: Supreme Court rejects Alaska's attempted revival of copper and gold mine
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected Alaska’s attempt to revive the proposed Pebble Mine in Bristol Bay, which was blocked by the EPA. The EPA cited risks to the aquatic ecosystem supporting major sockeye salmon. Alaska can still pursue lower-court challenges, but the ruling keeps copper-supply expectations constrained.

title: Nickel investments in Indonesia may slow on falling prices, geopolitical risk | 2024 preview
summary: The article says Chinese nickel investments in Indonesia are slowing as falling LME nickel prices, shrinking project economics, and FEOC/IRA rules threaten profitability and eligibility for US tax credits. Companies have scrapped or paused nickel capacity plans amid concerns of surplus, adding bearish pressure to near-term nickel sentiment.

title: Bahrain Business: Conexus opens $100m aluminium rod plant
summary: Conexus Resources inaugurates a $100m aluminium rod plant in Bahrain with 32,000 tonnes per year capacity, processing liquid aluminium supplied from Alba into rods for regional and international clients. The project is positioned as part of Bahrain’s aluminium downstream expansion, potentially increasing downstream utilisation rather than altering broader supply immediately.

title: It's not all boom in Australian mining – look at Panoramic, Alumina
summary: Panoramic Resources has shut its Savannah nickel mine in Western Australia, placing 340 jobs at risk. Administrators say the decision follows falling nickel prices that made the operation unviable. The closure is expected to tighten or curtail nickel supply in the near term, though the cited cause reflects bearish pricing pressure.

title: Alcoa announces curtailment of Kwinana Alumina Refinery in Western Australia
summary: Alcoa announced it will fully curtail production at its Kwinana alumina refinery in Western Australia starting in the second quarter, ending all alumina output by the third quarter of 2024. The company cites high costs and current market conditions. Pinjarra and Wagerup output are expected to remain unaffected.

title: Alcoa set to slow output at WA alumina plant to cut costs
summary: Alcoa is expected to announce cost-driven curtailment at its Kwinana alumina refinery in Western Australia, though it is not a full closure and currently runs around 80% capacity. The move suggests reduced output/input supply in the near term as the producer targets lower costs, weighing on aluminum market sentiment.

title: Aranjin Resources Ltd: Aranjin Resources Announces Closing of Its Australian Copper Project Acquisitions
summary: Aranjin Resources announced that it has closed in escrow its acquisition of an 80% interest in three Australian copper projects (Bangemall, Gawler, Western Wood). Shares were issued to counterparties under escrow pending final TSXV approval. Royalty terms were set via net smelter return royalties, but no production or near-term supply change is specified.

title: Alcoa Kwinana alumina refinery phased shutdown announced with around 1,000 job losses
summary: Alcoa announced a phased shutdown of its Kwinana alumina refinery in Western Australia, cutting production later this year and reducing staff sharply through 2025. The closure, justified as a cost decision, lowers alumina supply for aluminium output, potentially weighing on aluminium prices despite continued operation of other plants.

title: Alcoa to mothball Western Australia alumina refinery, up to 1050 staff at risk
summary: Alcoa said it will stop production at its loss-making Kwinana alumina refinery in Western Australia in the third quarter of 2024, cutting employment and aiming to save about $70 million annually. The shutdown is driven by challenging market conditions and the plant’s age, while associated port facilities and some refineries remain unaffected.

title: Aranjin Resources Announces Closing of Its Australian Copper Project Acquisitions
summary: Aranjin Resources announced the closing of its Australian copper project acquisitions. While the details needed to judge production or timing are not provided, the news supports sentiment that copper supply development is progressing, which can be mildly bullish for copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Copper rises as softer dollar lifts appeal
summary: Copper rose as a softer U.S. dollar reduced the cost of dollar-priced metals, following bets on imminent Fed rate cuts. Reuters also reported LME aluminium and nickel edging higher in the same session. Investors awaited upcoming U.S. inflation data for further base-metals volatility.

title: Alcoa's Kwinana Alumina Refinery to be shutdown, 750 of 800 jobs to be cut, company announces
summary: Alcoa will fully curtail production at its Kwinana alumina refinery near Perth, starting in Q2 2024, with all alumina production ending by Q3 2024. Jobs will be cut sharply, and the site will continue limited processes. Alcoa cites age, operating costs, bauxite grades, and market conditions; Pinjarra and Wagerup output is expected to remain unaffected.

title: Alumina price panic a sign of future aluminium volatility: Andy Home
summary: Chinese ShFE alumina jumped 30% after a Dec. 18 explosion at a Guinea oil terminal raised fears for bauxite shipments, with supply already tight and dependency rising. The spike boosted Shanghai and LME aluminium, lifting aluminium to multi-month highs, then easing as disruption concerns receded.

title: Alcoa Kwinana alumina refinery shutdown will lead to hundreds of job cuts in resources minister's electorate | Western Australia
summary: Alcoa will close its 60-year-old Kwinana alumina refinery near Perth, cutting about 800 jobs and ceasing all alumina production by the third quarter of 2024. The firm cites operating costs, bauxite grades and current market conditions; politicians dispute whether policy contributed. Supplies are said not to be affected.

title: Minneapolis' new strategy to thwart copper thieves targeting street lights
summary: Minneapolis is testing five miles of aluminum wiring in about 125 streetlights to prevent copper thieves from stripping light posts. The city previously spent $250,000 replacing stolen copper wiring. Aluminum is worth far less than copper on salvage markets, so officials hope theft declines and may expand the approach citywide if it works.

title: This billionaire used Indonesia's nickel to squeeze out Australia
summary: Tsinghsan founder Xiang Guangda is credited with expanding nickel processing in Indonesia, boosting ferro-nickel alloy exports. Indonesian ferro-nickel exports rose sharply in the first five months, driven by increased processing capacity that helps lower-cost producers compete against higher-cost Australian nickel supply.

title: China December Aluminium Output and Forecast for January | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports China’s December aluminium output at 3.562 million mt, with daily production down MoM due to previously closed Yunnan electrolytic cells not restarting. Operating rate rose to 92.9% and installed capacity increased slightly. For January, SMM expects stable production near 3.56 million mt, implying limited price impact.

title: As of 15:00 CST January 9, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 51.08, a increase of 20.61 from the day before
summary: SMM data state that, as of 15:00 CST January 9, the copper cathode spot trading intensity index decreased 51.08, up 20.61 versus the day before. The report is focused on copper cathode spot market activity levels, implying weaker near-term trading momentum.

title: Madeleine King voices 'disappointment' over shock closure of Alcoa's Kwinana Alumina Refinery in Western Australia
summary: Australia’s resources minister expressed disappointment after Alcoa announced it will cease production at the Kwinana alumina refinery near Perth, cutting at least 750 jobs. The refinery will stop producing alumina by late Q3 2024. Government officials say other refineries will continue and supply chains remain intact.

title: Fiercer competition in copper raw material market amid earlier-than-expected supply tightness in copper concentrate market | 2024 preview
summary: Fastmarkets says copper concentrate supply tightened earlier than expected after the indefinite suspension of First Quantum’s Cobre Panama mine and reduced 2024 output guidance from Anglo American and Vale. It forecasts a copper concentrate deficit and shows treatment charges falling, signaling tighter feedstock conditions supportive of copper pricing.

title: Orecap Portfolio Company, QC Copper, Delivers Canada's Highest-Grade Copper Open Pit
summary: Orecap’s portfolio company QC Copper & Gold announced an updated Mineral Resource Estimate for the Opemiska project in Quebec, citing a 26% increase in copper grade and higher contained copper, with over 1.75 billion lbs of copper in measured/indicated resources. The release frames strong expansion potential.

title: Orecap Invest Corp.: Orecap Portfolio Company, QC Copper, Delivers Canada's Highest-Grade Copper Open Pit
summary: Orecap portfolio company QC Copper reported an updated mineral resource estimate for the Opemiska open-pit copper project in Quebec, citing higher copper grade and increased contained copper (over 1 billion pounds) alongside favorable metallurgy and expansion potential. The news is supportive for copper sentiment but not an immediate supply change.

title: Aluminium prices rebound as stocks decline
summary: Aluminium prices rebounded on Tuesday after recent lows as LME-registered stocks fell from a seven-month high, suggesting reduced nearby supply and some consumer buying. The piece also notes wide copper contango and rising nickel stocks, reflecting mixed short-term balance across metals.

title: PAN ASX: Nickel miners brace for job losses after Panoramic ends production
summary: Australia’s nickel miners are preparing for more job losses after Panoramic ends production. The article says nickel faces a massive oversupply forecast this year and points to worsening Canberra–Indonesia tensions. It adds that Indonesian policies have boosted Chinese investment, increasing nickel production and likely weighing on prices.

title: Orecap Portfolio Company, American Eagle, Intersects 302 metres of 1.09% Copper Equivalent
summary: Orecap’s portfolio company, American Eagle Gold, reported drilling results from the NAK project: 302 metres of 1.09% copper equivalent within 606 metres of 0.74% copper equivalent. The company says results extend high-grade mineralization and plans a fully funded 2024 program to expand the South Zone.

title: Orecap Invest Corp.: Orecap Portfolio Company, American Eagle, Intersects 302 metres of 1.09% Copper Equivalent
summary: American Eagle Gold intersected 302 metres of 1.09% copper equivalent within 606 metres of 0.74% copper equivalent at the NAK project in British Columbia. The company plans a fully funded 2024 drill program to expand high-grade South Zone targets, potentially improving copper project prospects.

title: Asian buyers profit from record discounts for near-term LME copper
summary: Record near-term discounts (cash vs three-month) for LME copper have hit an all-time high, reflecting oversupply and weak demand. Asian buyers are exploiting the contango to negotiate cheaper purchases for power and construction wire cable. Disruptions and production guidance cuts have not derailed the discount trend yet.

title: Scrap availability in focus for Europe's secondary aluminium markets in 2024 | 2024 preview
summary: European secondary aluminium markets are focused on scrap availability. Rising scrap prices have supported ingot prices, while steady exports to Asia helped. Recent waning export activity and a stronger euro/pound may weigh, but Red Sea freight disruptions and low European stocks add support. Dealers expect aluminium ingot and scrap prices to rise near term.

title: UK aluminium bottling factory launched after £1m investment
summary: A UK bottling facility funded with about £1m will produce resealable aluminium bottles for soda brands such as GUNNA and offer white-label aluminium bottling to the drinks industry. The firm argues aluminium’s recyclability will reduce reliance on single-use plastic, implying modest incremental packaging demand.

title: Hundreds protest at First Quantum's Panama copper mine
summary: Hundreds protested at First Quantum’s Cobre Panama mine in Panama after the Supreme Court declared its operating contract unconstitutional. The mine has been effectively shut, with protesters seeking symbolic closure while the company seeks formal talks for safe closure. The court decision also worsened Panama’s near-term growth outlook.

title: Alcoa Kwinana alumina refinery shutdown to have significant impact on WA economy, costing $650m annually
summary: Alcoa announced it will close the Kwinana alumina refinery near Perth by late 2025, citing high operating costs, low-grade ore constraints, and current market conditions. The shutdown threatens hundreds of jobs and reduces alumina supply from a major Australian exporter, adding downside pressure to aluminium sentiment.

title: On-site staff at Panoramic Resources Savannah nickel mine made redundant as prices continue to fall
summary: Panoramic Resources says it will make 140 on-site roles redundant at its Savannah nickel mine in Western Australia after entering voluntary administration, citing a low prospect of near-term turnaround. The company references falling nickel prices (down over 44% in 12 months) and continued declining trends despite recent concentrate shipments.

title: Hundreds of Jobs Lost in WA With Alumina Refinery Closure
summary: Alcoa said it will curtail production at its 60-year-old Kwinana alumina refinery in phases and close it in 2025, cutting up to 1,000 jobs. The closure reduces regional alumina availability, raising concerns about aluminium production and supply, which is likely bearish for aluminium prices in the coming weeks.

title: Copper prices under pressure on slowdown, demand concerns
summary: Reuters reports copper prices under pressure as traders weigh global growth headwinds and weaker yuan dynamics that reduce Chinese buying interest. The World Bank’s forecast of slower growth adds demand concerns. Aluminium edged up modestly, while nickel slipped slightly, reflecting mixed risk sentiment beyond copper.

title: Canberra backs green premium for failing Australian nickel miners
summary: Australia’s Resources Minister Madeleine King supports a pricing structure that pays a premium for nickel meeting higher ESG standards in Australia versus “dirty nickel” from Indonesia. The move is aimed at rewarding compliant producers amid industry turmoil and job losses, potentially lifting expectations for cleaner nickel pricing.

title: Alumina price panic in China a sign of future aluminium volatility
summary: China’s alumina market has surged: SHFE alumina rose 30% in the last two weeks of December, hitting 3,838 yuan/tonne on Jan 3. Since alumina is the main feedstock for primary aluminium production, the spike signals higher input costs and potential aluminium volatility.

title: Copper slips on steady dollar, demand worries
summary: Copper prices fell as a steady U.S. dollar and worsening demand sentiment, reinforced by World Bank warnings on global and China growth, pressured risk appetite. Investors awaited U.S. inflation data for Fed rate-cut timing. LME aluminium and nickel also eased, reflecting broader macro-driven weakness in industrial metals.

title: Refinery shut down 'no threat' to supply chain of alumina in Australia
summary: Australia’s resources minister says the Western Australian Kwinana aluminium refinery shutdown by Alcoa poses “no threat” to the alumina supply chain, with only a minor decrease in alumina availability. However, the refinery closure risks reduced aluminium output and potential job losses, likely weighing on near-term aluminium prices.

title: Copper ticks higher on weaker dollar, investor pause
summary: Reuters reports copper edged higher as the dollar softened and investors paused after repeated bearish sessions. Analysts cite thin LME stocks and high spot premiums for support, while China demand is seasonally weak. In the same market check, LME aluminium and nickel dipped, showing mixed impacts across metals.

title: Aranjin Resources Announces Victory Nickel Copper Discovery Drilling Planned
summary: Aranjin Resources says it identified a high-priority drill target from auger geochemistry and geophysics at its Victory nickel-copper discovery in Mongolia, where both copper and nickel exceed 100ppm and align with a magnetic low. Six diamond core holes are planned for early 2024 after an ASX dual listing.

title: Aranjin Resources Ltd: Aranjin Resources Announces Victory Nickel Copper Discovery Drilling Planned
summary: Aranjin Resources reports strong auger geochemical and geophysical correlation at its Victory gabbro intrusive in Mongolia, identifying targets with copper and nickel above 100 ppm. Six diamond core holes are planned to start in early 2024 after an ASX listing. The update is exploration-focused with no production impact stated.

title: Share of Russian aluminium in LME warehouses rises to 90% after UK crackdown
summary: UK sanctions from Dec. 15 limit physical delivery of Russia-made base metals, while the LME reports monitoring market orderliness and that Russian metal continued flowing through its warehousing network. Russian primary aluminium warrant stocks rose sharply, lifting Russia’s LME warehouse share to 90% and increasing near-term aluminium availability.

title: Share of Russian aluminium in LME warehouses rises to 90% after UK curbs
summary: UK curbs from Dec. 15 limited UK entities’ ability to take physical delivery of Russian base metals, yet Russian aluminium continued to flow through LME warehousing. LME data show Russian primary aluminium warrant stocks rose to 338,375 tonnes in December from 154,775 in November, raising concerns for competing producers and Western buyers.

title: Hydro Reduces Carbon Footprint of Hydro CIRCAL Recycled Aluminum to 1.9 kg CO2e/kg
summary: Hydro says it has lowered the measured carbon footprint of its Hydro CIRCAL recycled aluminium to 1.9 kg CO2e/kg from 2.3 kg via improved sourcing, sorting and traceability of post-consumer scrap. The updated third-party certified EPD is intended to help customers meet climate targets and boosts low-carbon aluminium demand.

title: Taseko Mines Limited - Taseko Announces a 26% Increase in Annual Copper Production
summary: Taseko announced that its Gibraltar mine produced 123 million pounds of copper for 2023, up 26% year-over-year and above guidance. Q4 output totaled 34 million pounds of copper. The company attributes performance to strong ore grades and operational throughput, with concentrate inventories above normal.

title: Taseko hikes copper production in "strong finish" to year
summary: Taseko said its Gibraltar mine produced 34 million pounds of copper in Q4 2023 and 123 million pounds for 2023, a 26% rise vs. 2022 and above prior guidance. The company expects the “strong finish” to continue into 2024 as the Gibraltar pit supplies ore in early 2024.

title: Copper concentrate production in Armenia down 8.4% in 11 months of 2023
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate production declined 8.4% year-on-year to about 263,417 tons in January–November 2023, according to the National Statistics Committee. Reduced concentrate availability can signal weaker copper supply conditions, which is typically bearish for copper prices in the near term.

title: Vale BM says decision to merge Canada nickel ops with Glencore a priority
summary: Vale BM says a tie-up of its Sudbury nickel operations with Glencore is a priority, with talks to assess whether shared infrastructure and redeveloped areas could deliver savings. Glencore declined to comment. VBM plans major nickel expansion, while the Sudbury basin assets also produce copper and precious metals.

title: Arizona Sonoran Copper Company Inc Reports Additional Drill Assay Results from the Cactus West and Cactus East Deposits Within the Cactus Project, Arizona
summary: Arizona Sonoran Copper announced additional drill assay results from its Cactus West and Cactus East deposits in Arizona, highlighting thick, high-grade total and soluble copper intervals. The company says results support expanded infill and exploration drilling and will feed into metallurgical work for an updated pre-feasibility study.

title: Taseko Mines Limited Announces Copper Production from Gibraltar Mine for the Fourth Quarter and Year 2023
summary: Taseko Mines reported that its Gibraltar mine produced 34 million pounds of copper in Q4 2023 and 123 million pounds for the full year, above guidance. Production reflected strong grades and average mill throughput, with some throughput impact from additional ball mill downtime. The update pertains to realized copper supply.

title: Alcoa set to end 60 years of production at Kwinana alumina refinery, impacting 1,000 workers
summary: Alcoa plans to end production at its Kwinana alumina refinery in Western Australia, phasing down workforces from 800 to 250 and ceasing alumina output by Q3. The company cites costs and weak market conditions. While Pinjarra and Wagerup should continue, the curtailment tightens near-term alumina availability for aluminium production.

title: Nickel Price Hits New Low As Market Struggles Continue
summary: Nickel prices hit a new low, extending a deep downtrend, with only partial stabilization earlier in December. Producers and buyers report weak demand and limited inventory rebuilding. Surplus expectations persist, LME inventories have risen, and Indonesia’s output remains strong, weighing heavily on nickel sentiment going forward.

title: Decarbonisation in the spotlight following closure of Alcoa's Kwinana alumina refinery
summary: Alcoa’s decision to halt production at its Kwinana alumina refinery is expected to cut output and reduce bauxite supply to the Kwinana/Pinjarra refineries, alongside job losses. The piece frames this as part of a decarbonisation transition, but the immediate outcome is lower alumina feedstock, pressuring aluminium-linked supply.

title: Aluminum and Forced Labor Beyond the USMCA and Inflation Reduction Act
summary: The piece highlights tightening US trade measures affecting aluminum, including AD/CVD investigations on aluminum extrusions and expanded Section 232 tariffs that add a 200% tariff on certain Russian-processed aluminum and related derivatives. It also notes ongoing enforcement against transshipment and evolving tariff scope in 2024, implying import cost pressure.

title: NickelX Limited to Commence Drilling at the Dalwallinu Project in Late January 2024
summary: NickelX Limited says it will begin drilling at the Dalwallinu nickel-copper-PGE project in late January 2024. The update is primarily operational and relates to exploration activity and deal mechanics for an option arrangement. No immediate production, reserve, or supply disruption figures are provided.

title: First Quantum's closed Panama copper mine targeted in fresh protest
summary: Hundreds of workers and the Suntracs union demonstrated at First Quantum’s closed Cobre Panama copper mine, padlocking the gates and demanding the shutdown become permanent. Union leaders cite resource nationalism and past legal/political actions leading to closure, warning against any contract extension during Panama’s upcoming election.

title: NIC ASX: No green lifeline for Australian nickel miners, Nickel Industries warns
summary: Nickel Industries warns Australian nickel miners will not receive a “green premium” as the sector becomes uncompetitive. The company links the outlook to falling nickel prices and expects Indonesia to increase nickel supply for years, weighing on jobs and prompting concerns about sustained market oversupply and weaker nickel pricing.

title: As of 15:00 CST January 11, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 111.45, a increase of 64.37 from the day before
summary: SMM data for Jan 11 shows the copper cathode spot trading intensity index at 15:00 CST decreased by 111.45, with a reported increase of 64.37 versus the day before. The change suggests softer near-term spot market activity, which may weigh on copper price expectations.

title: Infinico Announces the Start of Drilling Operations at the Nicobi Nickel, Copper & Cobalt Project
summary: Infinico Metals said drilling has commenced at its Nicobi nickel, copper & cobalt project in Québec, with 1,000 metres planned and borehole EM support. The program aims to validate and test historic mineralization, with assays expected late Q1 2024. No results, production, or supply changes were reported.

title: Infinico Metals Corp.: Infinico Announces the Start of Drilling Operations at the Nicobi Nickel, Copper & Cobalt Project
summary: Infinico Metals announced drilling has started at its Nicobi nickel, copper and cobalt project in Québec, with 1,000+ metres planned to validate historic mineralization and test down-plunge targets. Assays are expected in late Q1 2024, but no sampling results or changes in production are reported.

title: Infinico Announces the Start of Drilling Operations at the Nicobi Nickel, Copper & Cobalt Project
summary: Infinico Metals says it has begun a diamond drilling program at its Nicobi nickel, copper and cobalt project in Quebec. The CAD$1.8m fully funded program targets historic Ni-Cu mineralization and uses BHEM alongside drilling to identify new conductive zones. Assays are expected in late Q1 2024.

title: Infinico Metals Corp.: Infinico Announces the Start of Drilling Operations at the Nicobi Nickel, Copper & Cobalt Project
summary: Infinico Metals started a ~1,000 m diamond drilling program at its Nicobi Ni-Cu-Co project in Quebec, targeting historic mineralization and new down-dip/along-strike zones using borehole EM. Assays are expected in late Q1 2024. The release does not indicate production, only exploration testing.

title: PAN GLOBAL DRILLS 1.48% COPPER, 0.65 G/T GOLD, 7.2G/T SILVER OVER 6.8M AND 2.63 G/T GOLD OVER 8.0 METERS AT CAÑADA HONDA, SPAIN
summary: Pan Global Resources reported its first drillhole results from the Cañada Honda Cu-Au discovery in Spain, including 6.8m at 1.48% copper and other high-grade intervals. The company says mineralization remains open and could expand with further drilling, supporting bullish sentiment for copper supply potential.

title: Pan Global Resources Inc.: PAN GLOBAL DRILLS 1.48% COPPER, 0.65 G/T GOLD, 7.2G/T SILVER OVER 6.8M AND 2.63 G/T GOLD OVER 8.0 METERS AT CAÑADA HONDA, SPAIN
summary: Pan Global Resources reports channel-sampling results at its Cañada Honda target in Spain, including 0.16% copper over 6m and indications of a larger copper-gold VMS-style system. The release is mainly exploration-focused, with no near-term changes to output or inventories.

title: Taseko's Gibraltar copper output up 26% in 2023
summary: Taseko said its Gibraltar copper mine produced 34 million pounds of copper in Q4 2023 and 123 million pounds for the full year, 26% above the prior year and above guidance. Q4 sales volumes were 36 million pounds, while year-end concentrate inventories stayed above expected levels.

title: Sonoran Desert Copper Corporation Completes Sampling Program at Cuatro Hermanos
summary: Sonoran Desert Copper Corporation says its sampling program at the Cuatro Hermanos porphyry copper-molybdenum project in Sonora, Mexico, returned assays up to 16.25% copper and shows a higher-grade South Conglomerate area (average 1.736% Cu). The company plans percussion drilling and development activities during 2024.

title: REPEAT – American Pacific Reports Most Significant Copper Drill Intersections To-Date at Its Palmer VMS Project, Including 43.8 Metres of 6.54% and 23.9 Metres of 9.03% Copper
summary: American Pacific announced its most significant copper drill intersections to date at the Palmer VMS project, including 43.8 metres grading 6.54% copper and 23.9 metres at 9.03% copper. The update highlights improved resource potential, which can bolster short-term market expectations for copper supply.

title: Exploration firm reports sizable nickel deposits near Paxson
summary: Alaska Energy Metals told residents it has positive results from prospecting its Nikolai Project near Paxson and plans to spend at least $15 million on further nickel sampling and surveys in 2024, with exploration resuming in June. The company also cites potential nickel demand for EV batteries and some copper alongside nickel.

title: Panamanian commission visits copper mine shut down after court invalidated concession
summary: A Panamanian commission reportedly visited a copper mine after it was shut down when a court invalidated the mine’s concession. The shutdown points to an interruption in copper supply, which can influence short-term market expectations and price direction depending on how quickly operations can resume.

title: Panamanian commission visits shut down copper mine
summary: A Panamanian commission visit led to a copper mine being shut down after a court invalidated the mine’s concession. The stoppage tightens near-term copper supply expectations and can raise price volatility as the market reassesses output and availability over the coming weeks.

title: China 2023 copper imports decline amid rising domestic output
summary: China’s copper imports declined 6.3% in 2023 to 5.5 million tons as domestic refined output rose 13.3% and post-COVID production ramped up. Imports of ore and concentrate hit record highs, but lower finished copper purchases and a stronger U.S. dollar restrained demand, pressuring copper sentiment.

title: Panamanian commission visits copper mine following after court invalidates concession
summary: Panama’s government inspected a large copper mine that has been shut down after the Supreme Court ruled its concession with a Canadian company unconstitutional. The closure follows prior protests and suggests reduced copper output, with officials noting the halt was unusual and requires additional planning before operations can resume.

title: Alcoa to shut down West Australian alumina refinery, destroying more than 1,000 jobs
summary: Alcoa announced it will shut its Kwinana alumina refinery in Western Australia, ending alumina production by Q3 and cutting jobs. The company cited age, operating costs, bauxite grades and market conditions. While the port continues to handle related flows, the closure may tighten near-term alumina availability impacting aluminium expectations.

title: SMM Analysis Of China Bauxite Imports In November 2023 | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: China’s November 2023 bauxite imports rose MoM and slightly YoY, led by higher shipments from Guinea as the rainy season ended. Australia increased in November but not strongly over Jan-Nov. The Guinea oil depot explosion initially boosted then eased alumina futures concerns, with SMM saying bauxite supply was not materially hit short term.

title: Copper Up From Lowest in Nearly a Month on China Stimulus Hopes
summary: Copper prices moved up from their lowest level in nearly a month, according to the article’s headline, as traders looked to China stimulus for support. The market reaction reflects improved expectations for near-term industrial demand in China, a key driver for copper consumption.

title: A major aluminum smelter in Shandong cut January prebaked anode benchmark purchase price by 150 yuan/mt MoM
summary: A major Shandong aluminum smelter cut its January prebaked anode benchmark purchase price by 150 yuan/mt to 3,878 yuan/mt. SMM said export anode prices fell about $15–20/mt as raw material prices declined, with east China anode prices closing around 3,878–6,410 yuan/mt.

title: Grupo Mexico mulls Spanish copper mine acquisition
summary: Grupo Mexico is reportedly among bidders for First Quantum’s Las Cruces copper mine in Spain, after Cobre Panama was ordered to shut, creating a financial crunch and triggering the asset sale. Las Cruces includes a refinery targeting about 72,000t of annual copper cathode, which could influence short-term copper supply expectations.

title: Canada Nickel Receives Equity Investment from Samsung SDI
summary: Samsung SDI will invest US$18.5m in Canada Nickel and gain rights tied to the Crawford nickel-cobalt project, including an option for a 10% equity interest and offtake of nickel-cobalt production upon a construction decision. This supports near-term confidence in nickel project funding and supply outlook.

title: Canada Nickel Receives $18.5 Million Investment from Samsung SDI for 8.7% Stake
summary: Samsung SDI will invest $18.5 million for an 8.7% stake in Canada Nickel, buying about 15.6 million shares, and has a right to purchase a further 10% equity in production from the Crawford nickel project in Ontario. The deal signals stronger future output backing for nickel-linked battery materials.

title: Pampa Metals Corp.: Pampa Metals Finalizes Follow-Up Diamond Drill Program at the Piuquenes Copper-Gold Porphyry Project
summary: Pampa Metals finalized a follow-up diamond drill program for its Piuquenes copper-gold porphyry project in Argentina, targeting depth and lateral extension of known mineralization. The update is likely to affect near-term expectations for copper-related supply and investor sentiment, though it provides no nickel or aluminium-specific information.

title: Vulcan Minerals Inc. – High Grade Copper Intersected at
summary: Vulcan Minerals announced high-grade copper (with gold credits) from drill intersections in the McNeily zone at its Colchester project in Newfoundland.
