summary: Arizona Sonoran Copper released drill results from the MainSpring property within its Cactus copper project, reporting long intercepts of near-surface copper mineralization (e.g., 1,053 ft at 0.20% CuT). The company highlights potential open-pit starter development and continued drilling to support future studies.

title: Anglo Asian climbs amid copper resource discovery at Xarxar
summary: Anglo Asian Mining reported significant copper resource results at its Xarxar deposit in Azerbaijan, with drill results to be incorporated into a forthcoming JORC mineral resource estimate. The company plans further infill/extension drilling and testwork before mine design and production planning, indicating improved longer-run potential rather than near-term output.

title: Smelter closure to wipe nearly 30% of US aluminum capacity
summary: A US primary aluminium smelter is expected to close, removing nearly 30% of US capacity, after high energy costs made operations unfeasible and cold weather impaired restart. The closure reduces domestic supply, tightening the market and pressuring aluminium premiums higher, amid limited spot activity and sluggish demand.

title: Copper firms, on track for biggest weekly gain in two months
summary: Copper rose to a three-week high and was set for its biggest weekly gain in two months as China cut bank reserves, injecting liquidity and supporting expectations for a construction rebound. Softer dollar and mining disruptions added support. LME aluminium also rose modestly while nickel slipped slightly.

title: Capstone Copper Corp. Announces Consolidated Production Results for the Fourth Quarter and Full Year Ended December 31, 2023
summary: Capstone Copper Corp. released its consolidated production results for Q4 and the full year ended Dec. 31, 2023. It reported Q4 copper production of 44,103 tonnes and full-year copper production of 164,353 tonnes. The update is company-specific and does not cite major supply shocks.

title: Aluminium Deutschland urges 'common sense' approach in German economic policy to strengthen aluminium production
summary: Aluminium Deutschland warns Germany’s aluminium industry is under pressure from over-regulation, high energy costs and recession. German primary aluminium output reportedly fell sharply in 2023 and smelters have been shutting down, with imports increasing. It argues current energy-transition policy is damaging competitiveness.

title: Slumping nickel prices are expected to fall further, expert warns
summary: The piece centers on expectations that nickel prices will continue to decline. It cites an expert warning of further downside, reflecting negative near-term market sentiment around nickel supply/demand conditions. The headline is directly about nickel, implying potential downward pressure on nickel pricing over coming days.

title: Universal Copper Announces Funding of Loan Agreement
summary: Universal Copper Ltd. said it received a $150,000 convertible loan to fund a cash option payment related to its Poplar Copper Project in British Columbia. The principal matures May 28, 2024. The financing supports continued project advancement but is modest, so near-term copper price impact appears limited.

title: Missouri Aluminum Plant, Saved by Trump's Tariffs, to Shut Down Again
summary: A southeast Missouri primary aluminum plant (Magnitude 7 Metals) is set to shut down again, with about 500 workers laid off. The closure follows earlier tariff protection under Trump and is linked to Biden’s aluminum tariff exemptions for the EU. The loss of a major smelter underscores renewed import pressure on U.S. aluminium prices.

title: What's behind the drastic downturn in nickel and lithium prices, and what does it mean?
summary: The article attributes the sharp downturn in nickel (down over 40%) and lithium to supply outpacing EV demand, with Indonesian cheap nickel adding competition. WA producers are mothballing mines and cutting jobs, including Albemarle scaling back a refinery expansion. Officials discuss royalty relief to stabilize teetering operations.

title: Tax break on table for beleaguered nickel, lithium miners
summary: BHP says an industry crisis meeting over collapsing nickel conditions was a wake-up call for Australia’s role in future critical-minerals supply. Nickel and lithium producers in Perth left separate meetings encouraged by the possibility of an Albanese government production tax credit for downstream processing of some minerals.

title: Jokowi aides defend nickel policy against Anies team's claims - Regulations
summary: Indonesian ministers defended Jokowi’s nickel downstream policy after Anies campaign claims questioned its logic. Thomas Lembong argued EV batteries increasingly use lithium iron phosphate and that downstream could flood global nickel supply and lower prices. Ministers countered these points, reinforcing confidence in Indonesia’s nickel strategy.

title: Foreign entities are lobbying for nickel ore exports, minister says - Politics
summary: Indonesia’s investment minister alleges foreign entities are lobbying to reopen nickel ore exports by persuading a presidential candidate to lift the 2020 ban. If exports resume, global nickel supply expectations could improve quickly, which would likely be supportive for nickel prices in the short term.

title: Phoenix Copper seeks to raise up to GBP2.4 million in equity
summary: Phoenix Copper has launched an equity offer to raise up to GBP2.4 million to fund mining and processing equipment for its Empire open-pit copper (and silver) project in Idaho. The company also discusses a proposed corporate copper bond. The financing supports development but is unlikely to move near-term copper prices.

title: One of nation's only aluminum smelters set to close in Missouri Bootheel
summary: A primary aluminium smelter (Magnitude 7 Metals) in southeast Missouri is reportedly set to curtail/close, with claims it represents about one-fifth of U.S. aluminum production. Explanations include energy and fossil-fuel dependence, pollution compliance costs, and cold-weather disruptions. Lawmakers urge intervention via energy support or the Defense Production Act.

title: As of 15:00 CST January 26, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 27.27, a increase of 1.75 from the day before
summary: SMM data for January 26 show the copper cathode spot trading intensity index at 15:00 CST was 27.27, down 27.27 versus the previous level, though it notes a +1.75 change from the day before. Overall, the reported decline points to reduced spot activity and potential copper price softness.

title: Copper slips on doubts over China's stimulus measures
summary: Copper prices dipped on investor skepticism about whether China’s recent stimulus steps—such as lower reserve requirements and potential market support—will revive demand. LME three-month copper fell modestly, while the story also highlights adequate global smelting capacity and copper mine output shortfalls, keeping broader metals sentiment cautious.

title: Indonesian miners brace for prolonged low nickel prices - Markets
summary: Indonesian nickel miners expect prolonged low nickel prices as a global glut continues to grow and demand growth has slowed. Even with announcements to cut production and close mines, analysts do not expect supply reductions to lift prices soon. Vale Indonesia will keep its production target while focusing on lowering costs.

title: China's refined nickel export volume soars in 2023
summary: China’s refined nickel exports surged to 36,754 tonnes in 2023 (+62.9% YoY), with December up nearly 198% YoY. The growth is attributed to new refiners converting Class 2 to Class 1 and LME deliverability approvals, helping export surplus from an oversupplied domestic market despite weak overseas demand.

title: 'Copper Thieves' are Turning American Cities into Third World Countries
summary: The piece claims copper thieves have repeatedly targeted streetlights, bridges, and EV charging/solar infrastructure in U.S. cities like Los Angeles and the Twin Cities, leaving many fixtures inoperable. It implies copper replacement needs for utilities and municipalities, but provides no data on volume relative to global supply.

title: Missouri aluminum smelter set to close
summary: The report says an aluminum smelter in Missouri is set to close. Such announcements can reduce near-term primary aluminum output and alter supply expectations for U.S. markets. The immediate effect is generally bearish for prompt aluminum prices, reflecting uncertainty about restart and production timing.

title: Josh Hawley Thinks the White House Can Force an Aluminum Plant To Stay Open
summary: The piece argues that the White House could force an aluminum plant to stay open. That would help preserve current production and reduce expectations of an immediate supply shortfall. Supportive supply prospects can lift or stabilize aluminum prices in the near term, assuming the intervention is credible.

title: Ghana to get new alumina refinery as Prez Akufo-Addo announces GIADEC's strategic partner for Project 3A
summary: Ghana’s President announced Project 3A with Mytilineos, including development of a bauxite mine and construction of an alumina refinery under GIADEC. The plan is to end raw bauxite exports by supplying alumina to VALCO’s smelter. It should strengthen the bauxite–aluminium supply chain expectations.

title: Ghana to get new alumina refinery as Akufo-Addo announces GIADEC's strategic partner for Project 3A
summary: Ghana plans to add an alumina refinery under Project 3A via GIADEC’s partnership with Mytilineos. The project includes a Nyinahin-Mpasaaso mine and refinery aimed at shifting from exporting raw bauxite to supplying alumina to the VALCO smelter, supporting the integrated aluminium value chain.

title: L.A. officials seek to stop rampant copper wire theft
summary: Los Angeles officials propose a task force and rewards program to curb copper wire theft, citing $17 million in repair costs and disruptions to Metro rail and streetlights. City actions also target buyers/recyclers and seek to reduce illegal copper sales, aiming to eliminate the market for stolen copper.

title: New Caledonia's Prony Resources faces cash crunch on nickel slump - Markets
summary: New Caledonia nickel producer Prony Resources is facing an “alarming” cash crunch after nickel prices fell about 40% in a year amid surging Indonesian supply. It is seeking short-term French support to keep operations running; France is negotiating investment-backed cost reductions.

title: High labour costs and dwindling demand slowing nickel production in Australia
summary: High labour costs and falling demand are reducing nickel output in Australia, according to the article. It also points to increased nickel availability from Indonesia. Together, slower Australian production, weaker end demand and incremental supply are likely to pressure nickel prices in the coming weeks.

title: Another US primary aluminium smelter bites the dust: Andy Home -January 28, 2024 at 07:00 pm EST
summary: Reuters reports curtailment of the New Madrid primary aluminium smelter in Missouri due to impaired operations from abnormally cold weather. The closure leaves only four U.S. primary producers and is expected to push national run-rates to historic lows, highlighting persistent pressure from high power costs and competition from China.

title: Copper dips as dollar steady, caution on China demand
summary: Copper opened lower as a steady dollar and softer demand expectations from China weighed on sentiment ahead of U.S. data. Three-month copper on the LME slid 0.2% and Shanghai prices were flat. The story also notes declines in nickel and aluminium, reflecting broader downside pressure in industrial metals.

title: Copper slides on dollar strength, caution over China demand
summary: Copper fell as a firmer dollar ahead of U.S. data and caution over China’s demand outweighed supply concerns. SHFE on-warrant stocks rose for a fifth week and spot trading weakened around early Chinese New Year. Aluminium and nickel also declined, reflecting broader risk sentiment.

title: Nickel and Stainless Steel Operates Stronger than Expected | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: The report says sentiment improved as US GDP beat expectations and rate-cut expectations eased. For pure nickel and nickel sulfate, it cites Indonesia policy concerns, stronger electrowinning costs, and a shortage of spot supplies as support. Indonesian RKAB approval disruption is seen as limited so far, implying nickel prices rebound.

title: 【SMM Mainstream Copper Inventory Weekly Data】 | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reported national mainstream copper inventories rose 6,800 tons to 92,000 tons week-to-date, with regional moves mixed but generally higher supply. Guangdong increased sharply amid domestic and imported arrivals, while downstream consumption weakened as firms entered semi-holiday mode. SMM expects inventories to keep rising this week.

title: 2023 Price Review: Global Pure Nickel Inventories Accumulate Nickel Prices Fall in 2023
summary: SMM’s review highlights weak 2023 demand for pure nickel and strong supply growth from newly released electrowinning capacity, alongside rising LME/warehouse receipts and accumulating deliverable inventories. With pure nickel surplus persisting and imports/clearances falling sharply, nickel prices softened from about 208,000 yuan/ton to ~140,000 yuan by November.

title: Freeport positive about permit extension for copper concentrate exports - Companies
summary: Freeport Indonesia (PTFI) says it is confident its copper concentrate export permit will be extended until the end of the year. The government links the extension to completion of the Manyar copper smelter by May 2024, after which approval should be mostly administrative.

title: Russia's Nornickel forecasts 2024 nickel output drop after 5% fall in 2023
summary: Nornickel expects nickel output to fall again in 2024 to 184,000–194,000 tons after a 5% decline in 2023. The company links the reduction to ongoing geopolitical risks affecting operations and also plans capital repairs at its Nadezhda flash smelting furnace. Reuters reported the forecast.

title: Copper slides, focus on China's property sector troubles
summary: Copper slid as traders reinforced concerns about China’s near-term demand, citing further stress in the property sector after Evergrande liquidation and weaker profit data. A firmer U.S. dollar and rising SHFE warehouse stocks also pressured prices. Aluminium and nickel also fell on demand-focused sentiment.

title: The challenging world of Russian aluminium sanctions | Hotter Commodities
summary: The article reviews pressure to sanction Russian aluminium more broadly, arguing LME delivery credibility is diverging from the physical market. It highlights existing LME warehouse restrictions, possible EU widening of sanctions, reduced EU Russian volumes, and rising European aluminium premiums, suggesting near-term tightness supportive for aluminium prices.

title: Lara Provides an Update on its Planalto Copper Project in Brazil
summary: Lara Exploration reported progress on its Planalto Copper Project in Brazil, including completion of a 2023 drill program, filings for resource estimates, and preliminary metallurgical testwork showing chalcopyrite-dominant copper with 88–92% recoveries. It also outlines license acquisitions and NSR royalty terms.

title: First Quantum to sell 120,000 tons of copper in Panama mine
summary: First Quantum Minerals says its Panama unit will sell 120,000 tons of copper concentrate stored near Punta Rincon port because it lacks financing to maintain preservation and safe operations after the government ordered a Cobre Panama mine shutdown. The company estimates preservation costs at $15-$20 million monthly.

title: Nickel Industries posts record quarterly output, unveils $100 million buyback plan -January 29, 2024 at 06:37 pm EST
summary: Nickel Industries reported record quarterly output and higher RKEF nickel metal production in the December quarter, though sales fell on softer contract prices. The firm cited a sharp nickel price slide from Indonesian supply and said early-2024 NPI prices show marginal improvement. It also announced a $100m buyback plan and dividend policy.

title: Australian shares hit over 3-week high; retail sales data in focus
summary: Australian shares rose as investors awaited retail sales data and watched U.S. Fed guidance. Mining stocks climbed as metal prices rose. The biggest nickel-related mover was Nickel Industries, up over 15% after record quarterly output and a share buyback, suggesting improved near-term nickel sentiment.

title: London copper eases ahead of Fed rate decision
summary: London copper eased slightly but stayed in a tight range ahead of the U.S. Fed rate decision, as traders waited for signals on potential rate cuts. LME aluminium fell, and nickel dropped further on continued supply-glut pressure and a streak of monthly declines, while overall market sentiment stayed cautious.

title: Capricorn Copper Mine production rises after major flooding | The North West Star
summary: 29Metals says production at the Capricorn Copper Mine rose in 2023 after flooding halted operations for four months. About 500mm of rain in March 2023 caused cleanup and production costs, but output later increased to 2.4kt from 1.1kt, aided by government support and approvals.

title: China's copper mining maintains momentum amid global production deficit
summary: China’s copper mining is gaining momentum as a global production deficit is expected after closures such as First Quantum’s Cobre Panama and forecasted lower output at South American mines. Zijin Mining reported over 1 million tonnes of mined copper in 2023 and is expanding major projects, supporting a tighter copper supply outlook.

title: Xanadu hits drilling paydirt with Mongolian copper-gold
summary: Xanadu says recent drilling at Mongolia’s Kharmagtai project, shared with Zijin, expanded higher-grade copper-gold mineralisation at White Hill and improved Golden Eagle resource grade. The company cites increases in copper contained and copper-equivalent core expansion, supporting improved future open-pit designs and potential copper production timelines.

title: U.S. bond yields fell, overnight copper prices upward. | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Overnight, copper prices rose after U.S. bond yields fell following a lower Treasury net borrowing estimate. However, the article flags potential copper supply arrivals this week, rising inventories, and holiday-season demand decline, suggesting limited room for further gains. The overall takeaway is muted net upside for copper.

title: Copper inventories in mainstream areas nationwide increased by 0.68 million tons at the end of the week [SMM Weekly Data].
summary: SMM data show China’s mainstream copper stocks rose 0.68 million tons to 92,000 tons week-on-week, with most regions increasing and Guangdong adding 0.64 million tons. Total inventories remain well below last year, but SMM expects more smelter warehouse supply and weaker downstream demand, implying further inventory growth this week.

title: SHFE Nickel Leads the Decline in Non-ferrous Metals | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: The piece reports weak performance in nickel and stainless steel. Pure nickel sees declining restocking and weak spot trading sentiment, while NPI transactions remain light near the holiday. Nickel sulfate has a persistent spot shortage that may support its price, but overall sentiment and trading activity suppress nickel.

title: White Cliff lands exploration permit for Coppermine project
summary: White Cliff Minerals received positive conformity determination from Canada’s Nunavut Planning Commission, fully approving licences for exploration at its Coppermine project. The programme is expected to begin with contractor selection, logistics planning and geophysical surveying to target high-grade copper mineralisation. No production impact is indicated.

title: NioCorp Developments Ltd.: NioCorp Collaborating with Leading UK-Based Research University to Develop Innovative Aluminum-Scandium Alloys for the Automotive Sector
summary: NioCorp said it is working with Brunel University London to develop aluminum-scandium alloys for automotive applications, aiming to improve strength, corrosion resistance, weldability, and recyclability. The company also discusses planned production of scandium from its Elk Creek project, but the initiative is mainly R&D with no near-term aluminum market impact details.

title: Canadian Copper Inc.: Canadian Copper Signs Offtake Agreement and Credit Facility with Ocean Partners
summary: Canadian Copper Inc. signed an offtake agreement for at least one-third of copper concentrate from its Murray Brook deposit and a one-year US$1.5m credit facility to meet acquisition and environmental bond conditions. The offtake is at market rates, but the scale is likely too small for near-term copper price impact.

title: Canadian Copper Signs Offtake Agreement and Credit Facility with Ocean Partners
summary: Canadian Copper Inc. signed an offtake agreement for at least one-third of production of copper concentrates from the Murray Brook deposit with Ocean Partners, plus a one-year, up to US$1.5m credit facility to support acquisition conditions. The update mainly affects expected copper concentrate sales, but likely at small market scale.

title: Benton Receives Further High-Grade Copper Results Including 5.81% Cu over 24.00 m at Great Burnt Project in Newfoundland
summary: Benton Resources said infill drill holes at its Great Burnt copper project in Newfoundland returned high-grade intercepts, including 5.81% Cu over 24.0 m, improving and expanding the deposit’s grade and width. The company plans more drilling in 2024, citing optimism for upgrading its mineral resource.

title: Lion Copper and Gold Corp. Announces Positive Pea Results for Its Yerington, Nevada Copper Project That Includes the Use of Rio Tinto's Nuton Technologies
summary: Lion Copper and Gold reported positive preliminary economic assessment results for its Yerington, Nevada copper project, using Rio Tinto’s Nuton catalytic bio-heap leach process to recover cathode copper without concentrators or smelters. The PEA shows favorable NPV/IRR at an assumed $3.85/lb copper price, but remains preliminary.

title: Premium Nickel Drills 30.45m of 2.88% NiEq and 9.55m of 3.94% NiEq at Selebi North Underground
summary: Premium Nickel Resources reports additional underground drill assays at Selebi North in Botswana, including 2.88% NiEq over 30.45m with Ni and Cu grades, plus 9.55m at 3.94% NiEq. Results suggest mineralization extends below prior intersections. Material applies mainly to nickel and copper, but global price impact is likely minimal.

title: Copper Lake Provides Exploration Update on Its Marshall Lake Copper-Zinc-Silver VMS Property, Northwestern Ontario
summary: Copper Lake Resources provides an exploration update for its Marshall Lake VMS copper-zinc-silver project in Ontario, reporting modelled magneto-telluric conductors and planning additional large-loop EM surveying. Due to unusually warm winter conditions, drilling depth targets are adjusted, but no near-term production impact or price-relevant supply change is announced.

title: Premium Nickel Resources Ltd.: Premium Nickel Drills 30.45m of 2.88% NiEq and 9.55m of 3.94% NiEq at Selebi North Underground
summary: Premium Nickel Resources reports additional underground drilling assays at the Selebi North Ni-Cu-Co sulphide deposit in Botswana, extending mineralization beyond a historic resource and indicating continuity down plunge via BHEM. Results include intersections with nickel and copper grades, but the update is exploration-focused.

title: Solaris Resources (TSX:SLS) Launches Major 2024 Exploration Program Aimed at Expanding Warintza into District-Scale Copper Hub
summary: Solaris Resources launched a major 2024 drilling and regional exploration program at its Warintza copper-gold project in Ecuador, including six rigs and plans for 30,000+ meters of additional drilling. A new resource estimate is expected by late Q2, supported by a $130 million Zijin Mining investment and expansion targets.

title: Copper claws higher on hopes for more Chinese support measures
summary: Copper rose on Tuesday as investors looked for more Chinese support measures to stabilise the economy and stock markets, offsetting weaker demand. Reuters cites Evergrande’s liquidation as a dent to confidence, with copper “holding up” pending further policy support, while mine disruptions have shifted expectations toward deficits this year.

title: Rob McEwen Seeks $100 Million for Argentina Copper Mine as Milei Boosts Prospects
summary: Rob McEwen reportedly seeks $100 million to support an Argentina copper mine, with Argentina’s political developments (Milei) framed as improving prospects. The news relates to potential copper supply over time, but because it focuses on financing rather than near-term output, the likely near-term price effect is limited.

title: Gold-Copper Miner Northstar Gold Corp. (CSE: NSG) Provides Exploration Update
summary: Northstar Gold Corp. provided an exploration update on its Miller Copper-Gold property, highlighting copper-rich VMS and chalcopyrite intersections (e.g., 14.8% Cu over 2.45m) and plans for further drilling and geophysics funded via a private placement. The article is exploration-focused with no immediate production or trade impact.

title: Budget Expectations: Jindal Stainless advocates long-term duty exemption on ferro nickel and ferro molybdenum for raw material access | Indiablooms
summary: Ahead of India’s 2024-25 Budget, Jindal Stainless urged a long-term exemption of basic customs duty on ferro nickel (and ferro molybdenum) to secure competitively priced raw materials. It also seeks continued zero duty on stainless/steel scrap and other trade measures tied to stainless steel imports.

title: Australia's IGO freezes nickel project, trims lithium forecast
summary: IGO will place its Cosmos nickel project in Western Australia into care and maintenance, citing low nickel prices and associated operational/financial risks. It also trimmed lithium guidance, but the key near-term signal for industrial metals is nickel project suspension amid continued weakness.

title: Lower Lisbon Valley residents fear copper mining proposal's effects on water
summary: Residents in Lisbon Valley oppose expansion of the Lisbon Valley Copper Mine, citing fears that in-situ leaching could threaten drinking-water wells and that hydrology and monitoring are insufficient. The project depends on an EPA aquifer exemption and a Bureau of Land Management environmental review, raising the risk of delays or restrictions.

title: IGO ASX: More nickel job losses as IGO flags near wipeout on $1.3b buy
summary: IGO will shut down its troubled Cosmos nickel project in Western Australia, following continued job losses and financial stress. The move comes as the WA nickel sector suffers from reduced employment amid a market oversupplied with cheaper Indonesian nickel. Overall, the Cosmos shutdown tightens nickel supply expectations near term.

title: Russia the driver behind China's aluminium import boom: Andy Home - 2024-01-30
summary: China’s imports of unwrought aluminium more than doubled in 2023, with Russian material’s share rising to 76%. Despite high LME warrant stocks of Russian aluminium, China’s demand is absorbing supply that might otherwise hit Western inventories. Sanctions are making Russian primary metal harder to sell to Western users.

title: Copper on hold ahead of Fed decision; set for slight monthly gain
summary: London copper was subdued ahead of a U.S. Fed decision, with investors watching clues on a potential March rate cut. Prices are also supported by a slight monthly gain as Panama’s Cobre mine closure and lower global miner guidance disrupt supply and prompt possible Chinese smelter production cuts.

title: What is the Impact of Frequent Shutdowns in Australian Nickel Mines?
summary: SMM says frequent shutdowns/maintenance at Australian nickel mines in early 2024 stem from low nickel prices. It also notes falling China nickel ore imports, reduced Philippine shipments during the rainy season, and weaker purchasing by smelters amid low NPI output and inventory. Nickel ore spot prices have stabilized around $41/wet ton.

title: Trafigura-Backed Nickel Mine Seeks New Partner to Secure Bailout
summary: A Trafigura-backed nickel mine is reportedly looking for a new partner to secure a bailout. The move signals financial stress and potential operational or supply-chain risk, which can tighten near-term nickel availability expectations and provide upward price support in the coming days.

title: Stocks of the Hour: Sunstone Metals, Select Harvests, True North Copper
summary: The article is mainly a stock roundup. Sunstone Metals reports gold-silver assays at Ecuador’s Limon project; Select Harvests expects an earlier, higher-yield grain harvest. True North Copper is the copper link: it secured a four-year USD28m loan facility, supporting bullish sentiment toward copper-related supply prospects.

title: China copper smelters advised to cut output given tight raw material supplies
summary: China’s copper smelters are advised to reduce output because copper concentrate supplies have tightened unexpectedly after a major mine closure in Panama. CNIA urged maintenance extensions or earlier maintenance and cautioned against expanding due to smelting capacity. Some smelters discussed cuts but no specific plan was agreed yet.

title: Aluminium Sheet Prices, Trends & Forecasts | Provided by Procurement Resource
summary: The report outlines recent aluminum sheet price trends across Asia, Europe, and North America, linking movements to fluctuating aluminum ingot prices, construction demand weakness, labor strikes, constrained supply, inventory levels, production costs, and improving automotive sentiment. It notes declines in Q1 and firmer prices in Q2 as inventories fall.

title: Copper prices dip as soft China data, Fed caution weigh
summary: LME copper slipped 0.2% on softer China manufacturing data and traders’ caution ahead of the Fed decision. Although copper consumption rose in 2023, analysts expect slower growth. Sentiment also weighed on metals as smelters were urged to cut production amid tighter raw-material supplies, partially supporting prices.

title: Nickel prices face four years of pressure
summary: A nickel forecaster says the market will remain oversupplied until 2028, with prices potentially having more room to fall. The bearish view is reinforced despite recent mine closures, including IGO’s planned halt of the Cosmos nickel mine, which Benchmark Mineral Intelligence argues will do little to improve prices.

title: Copper concentrate TCs index fall off a cliff, how about smelter production?
summary: SMM says copper concentrate TCs are extremely low, prompting concern about smelter output. It finds domestic smelters have about three weeks of available concentrate (down from 4.5, above a 2.5-week extreme low). Most cathode production in January–February stays normal; only two reduce feed. Risk concentrates in Q2 if inventories worsen.

title: Indonesian nickel boom claims another WA mine, and hundreds of jobs
summary: IGO will close its Cosmos nickel mine in WA and cut jobs after a nickel price plunge made full ramp-up uneconomic. Management cites rising costs and shorter mine life, while Indonesia’s low-cost nickel supply has driven Australian producers to halt or trim operations. The piece also notes wider volatility in critical minerals.

title: Trafigura-Backed Nickel Mine Seeks New Partner for Bailout
summary: The article title says a Trafigura-backed nickel mine is looking for a new partner to secure a bailout. Such rescue efforts suggest financial stress that could threaten continued output, raising near-term supply risk perceptions for nickel and potentially supporting prices over coming days to weeks.

title: As of 15:00 CST January 31, the SMM copper cathode spot trading intensity index was decrease 81.37, a increase of 22.85 from the day before
summary: SMM data show that the copper cathode spot trading intensity index, as of 15:00 CST on Jan 31, fell to a level described as a decrease of 81.37, while noting a 22.85 change from the day before. The move signals reduced spot market activity for copper.

title: Power Metal Resources up as it mobilises for nickel drilling at Molobo
summary: Power Metal Resources shares rose after it contracted drillers to mobilise for imminent nickel drilling at the Molopo Farms Complex project in Botswana. The target is a high-priority conductor linked to potential nickel sulphides, with drilling expected in coming days. A two-year licence extension was also granted to its unit.

title: Volta Energy Solutions, world's first manufacturer of copper foil for batteries, to expand business presence in North American EV market
summary: Volta Energy Solutions (VES) plans to expand its presence in the North American EV market, leveraging its technology in ultra-thin copper foil used in battery electrodes. The article cites rapid EV growth and rising expected copper-foil demand. It supports copper demand expectations over the coming weeks.

title: Alumina production in 2023 slightly down despite H2 bounce back
summary: International Aluminium Institute data show 2023 world alumina production slipped slightly, but H2 output rebounded, with December up month-on-month. Gulf alumina/feed supply expectations look supported by rising production and GCC capacity expansions and major investment, suggesting improved near-term aluminium supply outlook.

title: Michigan board mulls $50M grant for new Upper Peninsula copper mine
summary: Michigan’s Strategic Fund is considering a $50M performance-based grant to support Highland Copper’s proposed Copperwood copper mine in the Upper Peninsula. The board tabled the decision pending further review over financing, but permits and projected output could improve expectations for future copper supply and investor confidence.

title: Archer Exploration Commences 2024 Winter Drilling Campaign at Grasset Nickel Project
summary: Archer Exploration has commenced its 2024 winter drilling campaign at the 100% owned Grasset nickel sulphide project in Quebec. The program targets a new EM conductor (N9) and further tests the H1 discovery zone with planned downhole EM surveys. Prior 2023 holes reported high nickel grades, supporting bullish nickel sentiment.

title: True North Copper secures $28m financing deal
summary: True North Copper (TNC) secured a four-year A$42m ($28m) senior secured loan to fund working capital and refinance the Cloncurry Copper Project rehabilitation bond. Part of the facility is contingent on starting commercial sulphide ore production. This supports a proposed copper mine plan restart, but market-scale impact is likely limited.

title: IGO puts Cosmos nickel project on care and maintenance
summary: IGO has shifted its Cosmos nickel project to care and maintenance after a review found reduced mine life, delays to full processing capacity, and higher costs. The company will preserve assets and complete limited commissioning and ROM ore processing, while retaining optionality to restart if nickel market conditions improve.

title: Game changer in global nickel market: booming Indonesian nickel industry
summary: The article links the nearly halved LME nickel price over 13 months to rising Indonesian nickel supply. It cites Indonesia’s export ban, large investment in processing (HPAL/RKEF/OESBF), and growing NPI output, while Wyloo and BHP have moved mines/operations to care-and-maintenance due to weak prices.

title: Indonesian Ministry of Energy and Mines: There are still 1.2 million hectares of unexplored land with nickel mining potential in Indonesia's nickel mines
summary: Indonesia’s Geological Bureau says 2 million hectares have nickel mining potential, with most still unexplored, and cites large nickel reserves split between sapropel (pyrometallurgy/RKEF) and limonite (hydrometallurgy/HPAL). It notes mechanisms to grow reserves but no new exploration plans yet, limiting near-term impact.

title: Seasonal watch | Copper enters its brightest seasonal phase
summary: The piece argues copper is entering a typically strong seasonal window in February, citing average gains and higher odds of price increases in early February. It links the outlook to China’s 50bp RRR cut injecting liquidity and supportive US inflation trends, plus possible COMEX short-covering after speculators remain net short.

title: Vale posts big rise in iron and copper production
summary: Vale reported strong Q4 results with copper production up 50% year-on-year to 99,100 tonnes, driven by expansion at Salobo 3 in Brazil. Nickel output fell 5% in Q4 and 8% in 2023 due to transitions and planned furnace reconstruction. Overall, it signals mixed near-term supply impacts.

title: Australia Looks To Capitalize on China's Insatiable Copper Demand
summary: The article highlights stronger China-led copper demand, including record Australian exports of copper ore and concentrates to China and continued increases in China’s copper imports. It also points to record CCP stockpiling since 2018 and expectations of further 2024 growth driven by EVs, power-grid investment, and stimulus.

title: Canada Nickel virtual open house launches
summary: Canada Nickel launched a virtual open house to gather public feedback on its proposed Crawford Nickel Project north of Timmins. The project is under provincial and federal impact assessment and would develop a large open-pit nickel mine and processing facility. The consultation process reflects ongoing development toward future nickel supply.

title: Canada Nickel virtual open house launches | Elliot Lake Standard
summary: Canada Nickel has launched a virtual public open house for the Crawford Nickel Project near Timmins, inviting comments on the proposed open-pit nickel mine and processing facility. The project is under federal and provincial impact assessment, with outcomes informing the impact statement and environmental documentation.

title: Michigan Economic Development Corporation Proposes $50 Million Grant For Highland Copper's Copperwood Project -January 31, 2024 at 05:23 pm EST
summary: Michigan’s economic development corporation proposes a $50 million grant to Highland Copper for its Copperwood copper project after initial review by the Michigan Strategic Fund. The company expects further approvals and highlights the project’s role in U.S. domestic copper supply for electrification. The financing/progress signal may mildly support copper sentiment.

title: Russia the driver behind China's aluminium import boom
summary: China’s imports of unwrought aluminium more than doubled year-on-year in 2023, reaching about 1.54 million tonnes, the second-highest annual total this century. The increase suggests stronger Chinese demand for primary aluminium, with Russia cited as a key driver behind the import boom.

title: Canada Nickel virtual open house launches | Cochrane Times-Post
summary: Canada Nickel launched a virtual open house for public comments on the proposed Crawford Nickel Project, a new open-pit nickel mine and processing facility near Timmins, Ontario. The project is under provincial and federal environmental impact assessment, with feedback to be incorporated into impact documentation.

title: Canada Nickel virtual open house launches | Mid-North Monitor
summary: Canada Nickel launched a virtual open house for the proposed Crawford Nickel Project near Timmins, Ontario, seeking public input during its provincial and federal impact assessment. The project would develop an open-pit nickel mine and processing facility with 3.8 million tonnes of nickel reserves, supporting future supply expectations for nickel.

title: Highland Copper gives update on mine progression, opposition voices concerns for Lake Superior, Porcupine Mountains
summary: Highland Copper says its Wakefield/Ironwood mine is in reserve status with drilling and geology completed, permitting and a feasibility study done, and the project nearing financing after about $35m in treasury. The company sought a $50m Michigan grant, tabled for review. Environmental opposition cites tailings and water risks.

title: Hunter Valley Telstra outage triggered by copper and battery thieves, telco says
summary: Telstra says a three-week network outage in New South Wales’ Hunter Valley was caused by thieves stealing copper wiring and batteries. The theft damaged exchanges and a mobile facility, disrupting landlines, ADSL, and mobile services during a busy vintaging season. Service restoration has been completed.

title: Major automakers may be using Chinese aluminum produced with Uyghur forced labor, rights group says
summary: Human Rights Watch alleges major automakers’ China supply chains may include aluminum produced with forced labor in Xinjiang. With U.S. rules requiring proof against Xinjiang forced labor, buyers may avoid or re-source harder-to-trace Xinjiang material. That risk can tighten compliant aluminum supply and support aluminium prices.

title: Carmakers may be using aluminium made by Uyghur forced labour, NGO investigation finds
summary: Human Rights Watch alleges carmakers (Toyota, Volkswagen, Tesla, GM, BYD) may source aluminium linked to forced labour from Xinjiang smelters, where labour-transfer programs allegedly coerce Uyghurs. The report cites Xinjiang’s sizable aluminium output and warns of potential import restrictions and tougher sourcing scrutiny, which could disrupt demand.

title: Australian Court Dismisses Rusal Suit Over Rio Tinto Alumina Refinery
summary: An Australian court dismissed United Co. Rusal’s lawsuit seeking to restore its access to Rio Tinto’s Queensland Alumina refinery. The decision upholds Australian sanctions that restrict Rio Tinto/QAL from supplying bauxite and processing alumina for Rusal. As long as sanctions continue, Rusal’s alumina supply remains constrained.

title: Glencore reports lower 2023 copper, nickel, cobalt output
summary: Glencore said 2023 copper output fell to 1.01 million tonnes and nickel production slipped to 97,600 tonnes. It trimmed 2024 copper guidance to 950,000–1.01 million tonnes (linked to selling its Cobar mine) and expects nickel output of about 80,000–90,000 tonnes, signaling weaker supply outlooks.

title: Nordic Nickel advancing Pulju project with key partnerships in Europe's growing battery sector
summary: Nordic Nickel says it is in talks with multiple strategic partners, including BHP, to advance its Pulju nickel project in Finland. The firm plans a resource update later this quarter and further metallurgical and processing studies. It also points to Europe’s growing battery demand, contrasting with current nickel oversupply.

title: Nickel North Extends Outside Date of Option Agreement with 1844 to Sell up to 100% Interest in Hawk Ridge
summary: Nickel North Exploration extended the outside date of an option agreement with 1844 to sell up to a 100% interest in the Hawk Ridge Cu-Ni project in Quebec. The company is still working toward TSX Venture Exchange acceptance. The update is administrative and does not signal immediate supply changes for nickel or copper.

title: Glencore reports lower 2023 copper, nickel, cobalt output
summary: Glencore said 2023 copper output fell to 1.01 million tonnes and nickel output to 97,600 tonnes. It expects 2024 copper between 950,000 and 1.01 million tonnes after the Cobar mine sale, and nickel at about 80,000–90,000 tonnes, implying weaker near-term supply momentum for both metals.

title: Glencore reports lower 2023 copper, nickel, cobalt output, flags further falls
summary: Glencore said 2023 copper output fell to 1.01 million tonnes and 2023 nickel production declined to 97,600 tonnes. It cut its 2024 copper outlook to 950,000–1.01 million tonnes and expects nickel output of about 80,000–90,000 tonnes, reflecting mine changes and lower volumes.

title: Glencore reports lower 2023 copper, nickel, cobalt output, flags further falls
summary: Glencore said 2023 copper output fell to 1.01 million tonnes and reduced 2024 expectations to 950,000–1.01 million tonnes after the Cobar mine sale. Nickel output also declined to 97,600 tonnes, with 2024 guidance of 80,000–90,000 tonnes. The company flags further falls.

title: China accelerating green power aluminium development
summary: China is expanding “green-power” aluminium using renewable electricity, with certification enabling buyers to source low-carbon metal. However, Yunnan smelters—key producers—face seasonal hydro shortages in the dry season, requiring rate cuts. This tightens near-term supply expectations and supports aluminium premiums versus ordinary metal.

title: Intrepid Metals Signs Drill Contract and Mobilizes Crew For Comprehensive Drilling at Corral Copper Property in Arizona
summary: Intrepid Metals announced a drill contract and mobilization for a 5,000 m program at its Corral Copper Property in Arizona, with drilling expected to start within two weeks. The company aims to verify historical copper results and extend mineralized holes, but the news does not signal near-term production impact.

title: Major automakers may be using Chinese aluminum produced with Uyghur forced labour, rights group says
summary: Human Rights Watch says major automakers may be using aluminium linked to Uyghur forced-labour programs in China’s Xinjiang. It highlights US requirements for Xinjiang-related forced-labour proof since 2022 and notes tracing difficulty once aluminum is alloyed. The scrutiny may tighten access to certain aluminum supply chains.

title: Alcoa to supply Nexans with low-carbon aluminum, including metal from ELYSIS™ technology
summary: Alcoa said it will supply Nexans with low-carbon aluminium rod made using ELYSIS, a process that eliminates direct greenhouse gas emissions from smelting by emitting oxygen instead. Nexans will start qualifications for rod in various cable types across Western Europe and Scandinavia, supporting sustainable electrification demand.

title: Canadian Copper Inc.: Canadian Copper Completes Acquisition of Murray Brook Deposit
summary: Canadian Copper Inc. says it has completed acquisition of the Murray Brook open-pit VMS deposit in New Brunswick and published an updated mineral resource estimate, including higher NSR value. The company also approved a 3,000-metre drill program to test a new copper/gold zone. Anticipated title transfer awaits ministerial approval.

title: Copper retreats on changing interest rate signals
summary: Copper prices fell on the LME after stronger dollar moves and receding expectations of a March U.S. rate cut. Losses were partly limited by tighter supply and improved China factory/export-order data, but demand is still cautious (cash-3m discount near highs). Aluminium and nickel also declined.

title: Nickel prices are affected by fundamentals, and the Federal Reserve has no expectation of interest rate cuts in the short term.
summary: SMM reports Shanghai nickel fell on Feb 1, with bearish positioning more aggressive. It cites cooling spot transaction sentiment as downstream stocking ends and increased availability of pure nickel. Macros include the Fed keeping rates unchanged and signaling no short-term cuts, leading SMM to expect weak price fluctuations.

title: Nexans: contract with Alcoa for low-carbon aluminum -February 01, 2024 at 10:06 am EST
summary: Alcoa signed a supply agreement with Nexans to provide low-carbon aluminum for several of Nexans’ European sites. The aluminum will come from Alcoa’s Elysis electrolysis process, cutting direct emissions. Alcoa already supplies Nexans with EcoLum aluminum. Contract value was not disclosed.

title: Blackboxstocks's (BLBX) Acquisition Target Evtec Aluminium Receives New $67M Long Term Supply Contract
summary: Evtec Aluminium, the planned acquisition target of Blackboxstocks, received a $67M long-term supply contract from JLR to produce parts for Jaguar’s new electric vehicle line. Evtec will be a single-source supplier for key EV powertrain components, adding new sales and supporting anticipated aluminium demand.

title: Alcoa To Supply Nexans With Aluminum From ELYSIS Technology
summary: Alcoa said it will supply Nexans with low-carbon aluminum rods produced via ELYSIS technology, which eliminates direct GHG emissions from traditional smelting. The aluminum will be used in Nexans cable facilities across Western Europe and Scandinavia, spanning low to high-voltage cables.

title: Blackboxstocks, Inc. Acquisition Target Evtec Aluminium Receives New $67 Million Long Term Supply Contract with JLR
summary: Rio Tinto said Federal and NSW governments have begun assessing ways to secure stable, competitively priced power for the Tomago Aluminium smelter once its current electricity agreement ends in 2028. The decision follows ongoing talks about long-term energy planning for local manufacturing, supporting aluminium production cost outlook.

title: Copper Futures Slip after Failing to Break 50% Fibo
summary: Copper futures are retreating after failing to break the 50% Fibonacci retracement and the descending trendline, confirming a bullish pennant but with rejected advances. Momentum signals are mixed, so near-term bias is neutral. Support is cited near the 50-day SMA, while a breakout direction remains pending.

title: Comanche Chairman releases address over upcoming cobalt and nickel refinery
summary: Comanche Chairman Mark Woommavovah issued a public statement about an upcoming cobalt and nickel refinery planned for Lawton. He cites assurances from the city and the chamber regarding environmental safety and jobs, and says the tribe will raise concerns with Westwin Elements and Oklahoma’s environmental quality agency.

title: Automakers May Be Using Chinese Aluminum Produced With Uyghur Forced Labor – The Yeshiva World
summary: Human Rights Watch alleges automakers, including Tesla, GM, Volkswagen, Toyota and BYD, source aluminum tied to forced-labor practices in China’s Xinjiang region. With U.S. rules requiring proof goods are not made with forced labor, compliance uncertainty and potential scrutiny could disrupt aluminum flows and pressure prices.

title: Capstone Copper to sell 59.52 million shares to RBC Capital for $280 million
summary: Capstone Copper said it will sell 59.52 million shares to RBC Capital Markets for about C$280 million (nearly C$375 million). The deal is expected to close around Feb. 8. The news is primarily a funding transaction rather than an immediate operational or supply-demand change for copper markets.

title: Major automakers may be using Chinese aluminum made with forced labor, rights group says
summary: Human Rights Watch alleges major automakers, including Tesla, GM, Volkswagen and Toyota, may be using Chinese aluminium produced with Uyghur forced labor. The report highlights sourcing from China’s Xinjiang region and other areas, increasing the risk of compliance scrutiny and potential procurement curbs that could affect near-term aluminium flows and prices.

title: Indonesia's Ban on Bauxite Exports Leads to Negative Effects, Surplus Bauxite Difficult to Consume
summary: Indonesia’s bauxite export ban has led to a cash-flow squeeze as domestic alumina plants cannot absorb the surplus bauxite. Limited alumina capacity and bank reluctance to fund new smelters have caused some firms to cut output or pause production. Indonesia is trying to expedite additional alumina plants, but delays weigh on expectations.

title: Major automakers may be using Chinese aluminum produced with Uighur forced labor, rights group says | The Asahi Shimbun: Breaking News, Japan News and Analysis
summary: Human Rights Watch links major automakers to aluminum allegedly produced with forced labor in China’s Xinjiang region. With governments requiring proof goods aren’t from forced labor and tracing difficult after refining/alloying, automakers may tighten sourcing away from Xinjiang supply. That could support aluminum prices near term.

title: Copper thefts cause major internet, phone outages at Pokolbin | Great Lakes Advocate
summary: Telstra says copper cable thefts from telecommunications sites in Australia’s Hunter wine region caused weeks of mobile, phone and internet outages. About 50 arrests occurred over 12 months, and cables plus backup batteries were stolen. Services resumed after replacements, but copper theft remains an ongoing issue.

title: Copper thefts cause major internet, phone outages at Pokolbin | Manning River Times
summary: Telstra reports copper cable thefts in Australia’s Hunter wine region have disrupted mobile and some fixed-line internet and phone services. Police cite nearly 50 arrests in 12 months and multiple theft events at a local telecommunications facility. Services were restored after cables and batteries were replaced.

title: Copper thefts cause major internet, phone outages at Pokolbin | Muswellbrook Chronicle
summary: Telstra says copper cable thefts have caused internet and phone outages in Australia’s Hunter wine region, with nearly 50 arrests over 12 months. Outages began after copper and backup batteries were stolen from a local facility and multiple premises were impacted until cables were replaced and services restored in late January.

title: Zccm Investments Holdings Plc : 	 ZCCM-IH Transaction Announcement Regarding Mopani Copper Mines- 01.02.2024 	 	 -February 02, 2024 at 03:00 am EST
summary: ZCCM Investments Holdings announced a transaction with IRH/Delta committing up to US$1.1bn for a 51% stake in Mopani Copper Mines, including interim financing ahead of closing in Q1 2024. Funds will support Mopani’s project development plan, working capital, and debt restructuring, aiming to sustain operations and increase copper cathode production.

title: ZCCM-IH Transaction Announcement Regarding Mopani Copper Mines- 01.02.2024
summary: ZCCM-IH announced a strategic equity partner transaction with IRH/Delta to invest up to US$1.1 billion for a 51% stake in Mopani Copper Mines. Funds will support Mopani’s project development plan, working capital, and restructuring of Glencore-related debt and letters of credit, subject to conditions precedent and approvals.

title: Presidential Proclamations Extend U.S. Section 232 TRQs On E.U. Steel, Aluminum - Export Controls & Trade & Investment Sanctions
summary: Biden’s proclamations extend U.S. Section 232 tariff-rate quotas on EU steel and aluminum through Dec. 31, 2025, keeping quota volumes unchanged and reiterating eligibility rules for in-quota treatment (including primary aluminum certification). Some steel exclusion relief is extended; aluminum exclusions remain available. Copper is not addressed.

title: Closure of First Quantum's Panama copper mine threatens e-transition
summary: Panama ordered the closure of First Quantum’s Cobre Panamá copper mine after a Supreme Court ruling. The mine produced 350,000 tonnes of copper in 2022. The shutdown removes a supply source (~1.5% of global output in the article) and increases regional mining risk, which the piece suggests could lift mineral prices.

title: Freight is gradually stopped, and nickel prices are running weakly | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Shanghai nickel 2403 fell and the spot market turned colder ahead of Spring Festival as freight stops tightened pre-holiday spot supply. The article cites weak overall supply-demand and differentiated premiums (Jinchuan slightly higher, Russian weaker), while warehouse receipts rose and LME inventories declined, leading to expectations of weak, volatile nickel pricing.

title: Low-carbon aluminium to become requirement for beverage and packaging industry: Ball Corporation
summary: Ball Corporation said beverage and packaging customers will increasingly require low-carbon aluminium due to UN net-zero goals, SEC climate disclosures and the EU CBAM. It cites 85–90% recycled content and use of low-carbon primary aluminium via carbon-free smelting tech (e.g., Elysis, HalZero). The article notes Fastmarkets low-carbon aluminium differentials are trading higher in Europe.

title: Copper's demand-driven price fall limited by low LME stocks
summary: Copper prices fell as traders weighed weaker China demand signals and patchy global industrial activity, alongside expectations of higher-for-longer U.S. rates. China and LME-tracked inventories rose sharply, cash copper discounts widened to a record, and stocks in warehouses limited the selloff. Aluminium dipped slightly; nickel rose.

title: 8 suspects sought after $300G of industrial copper cable stolen
summary: Toronto police seek suspects after industrial copper cable worth about $300,000 was stolen from a downtown electrical station. The break-in occurred around Jan. 15, with suspects using multiple vehicles to remove copper cable. The incident is copper-specific but appears localized, limiting likely near-term price impact.

title: Vandals strip copper from light poles in Linwood Park
summary: Police are investigating vandalism in Linwood Park where copper wire was stripped from light poles, cutting nighttime lighting for users. The city also reported theft of copper wiring from a nearby cell phone tower, with an estimated value of $15,000. Public works installed additional security measures.

title: Timeline of minerals meltdown reveals rapidity of shock
summary: The piece outlines a fast “battery minerals meltdown,” noting nickel prices halved in 2023 and triggering voluntary administrations, mine suspensions, and care-and-maintenance moves in Australia. It cites BHP’s Nickel West review, Ravensthorpe shutdown, and calls for government support. It also foreshadows possible write-downs tied to copper/nickel assets.

title: UBS forecasts copper pricing amidst supply challenges
summary: UBS is forecasting copper pricing while highlighting continued supply challenges. Copper is reported to be trading above $8,200 per metric tonne, resisting weaker investor sentiment in China. The message implies that supply constraints are providing near-term price support for copper.

title: Nickel price: Indonesia's poll frontrunner doubles down on nickel boom
summary: Indonesia’s presidential frontrunner Prabowo Subianto says he will continue controversial nickel policies backed by Chinese investment. The article links these policies to a surge in global nickel supply, cheapening prices and triggering mine closures in Australia. Ahead of the Feb. 14 election, this outlook implies continued bearish pressure on nickel.

title: Adani's USD 1.2 bn copper plant to boost India's metal production
summary: Adani’s Kutch Copper is investing about $1.2bn in a greenfield copper refinery/smelting complex in India, targeting Phase-1 operations by March-end and 1 million tonnes/year full capacity by FY29. The project aims to expand refined copper supply and cut import dependence amid rising energy-transition demand.

title: Iran's output of aluminum ingot amounts to 472,418 tons in 9 months
summary: IMIDRO data shows Iran produced 472,418 tons of aluminium ingots from March 21 to Dec 21, 2023, slightly down from 474,601 tons in the prior-year period. SALCO was the largest producer (209,384 tons), followed by IRALCO and Almahdi; overall output trends fluctuate year to year.

title: Adani Group's $1.2 Billion Copper Plant To Boost India's Metal Production
summary: Adani Group is building a large copper manufacturing plant at Mundra, Gujarat, described as the world’s largest single-location copper facility. The project is framed as reducing India’s reliance on copper imports and supporting energy-related needs, potentially improving supply expectations and easing price pressure.

title: Adani Group to invest $1.22 billion to build largest copper manufacturing plant in Gujarat's Mundra | Indiablooms
summary: Adani Group will invest about $1.2 billion to build a large copper manufacturing plant in Mundra, Gujarat, aiming to cut India’s copper imports and support the energy transition. The first phase is planned for late March, with full capacity targeted by 2029, alongside Vedanta’s Tuticorin restart efforts.

title: Adani's USD 1.2 billion copper plant to boost India's metal production – Eastern Mirror
summary: Adani’s Kutch Copper is building a $1.2 billion Mundra copper smelting/refining complex, targeting 500,000 tonnes refined copper per year in phase I by March-end and 1 million tonnes after expansion. The project is meant to cut India’s copper import dependence amid rising energy-transition demand, though near-term price effects look muted.

title: Business.Scoop » Commission Amends Copper Withdrawal Code To Enhance Consumer Protection
summary: New Zealand’s Commerce Commission amended the Copper Withdrawal Code governing Chorus’s ability to stop supplying copper telecom services as fibre becomes available. The code specifies consumer notice, guidance, and ensuring fibre installation before copper is switched off. It targets consumer protection during copper-to-fibre transition, with no direct copper price supply impacts stated.

title: Billionaire-backed KoBold says open to partners as it plans $2 bln Zambian copper mine
summary: KoBold Metals says it may partner as it fast-tracks development of the $2 billion Mingomba copper mine in Zambia. Backed by Gates and Bezos, it highlights high copper grades and increasing demand for critical metals. The company could seek financing or listings, boosting sentiment toward future copper supply.

title: Adani Group's $1.2 Billion Copper Plant Elevates India's Metal Production
summary: Adani Group plans a $1.2 billion Kutch Copper project with Phase 1 capacity of 0.5 million tonnes of refined copper per year, expanding to 1 million tonnes. The article cites India’s rising copper demand from EVs and clean energy, and heavy reliance on imports, implying greater future local supply.

title: Shanghai INE to adjust trading limits for copper, crude oil and some other products
summary: Shanghai INE said it will adjust trading limits for international copper futures contracts to 8%, effective from the Feb. 7 settlement. The exchange also changed limits for crude oil and low-sulphur fuel oil, and the European container freight index. The move affects trading behavior more than underlying fundamentals.

title: Bill Gates-Backed Miner Finds World Class Zambian Copper Deposit
summary: The piece’s headline reports that a Bill Gates-backed miner discovered a world-class copper deposit in Zambia. Such a find can strengthen near-term market expectations for future copper supply. However, the excerpt lacks project size, timeline, and development details, limiting confidence on how quickly prices would react.

title: Sibanye CEO pushes on with copper hunt after failed Zambian bid
summary: Sibanye’s CEO said the company will continue hunting for copper assets in Africa after being outbid for Zambia’s Mopani Copper Mines, where a UAE-backed unit won a 51% stake. The firm expects copper to remain important but notes the market is overheated. It highlighted competition with Chinese-backed buyers.

title: Nickel prices fluctuated downward, falling for five consecutive days during the week
summary: Nickel prices fell for five straight days, with sentiment pressured after Fed comments reduced expectations for early rate cuts. Fundamentals are mixed: inventory is accumulated and spot transactions soften into the Spring Festival, while Indonesian RKAB approval is slowly improving supply. Ferronickel slightly rebounds, but nickel is still reported as trending lower.

title: Shanghai nickel fell 3.57% for five consecutive consecutive weekly lines The Indonesian general election during the Spring Festival may affect LME nickel prices
summary: Shanghai nickel and LME nickel have been declining week-on-week, with weak spot transactions ahead of the Spring Festival. Inventories are accumulating domestically and abroad. Supply/demand balance looks soft as output rises earlier but production suspensions approach. A stronger dollar and Indonesian election-related uncertainty are expected to keep nickel prices weak.

title: China's export of aluminium covered by EU carbon tax down 30% in 2023
summary: China’s exports of aluminium products to the EU that fall under the EU carbon border tariff (CBAM) fell 30% in 2023 to 689,000 tonnes. EU importers must report embedded emissions after CBAM’s launch in October, even though charges start in 2026, reducing Chinese shipment volumes.

title: Sumitomo cuts nickel output forecast in Madagascar due to system glitches
summary: Sumitomo reduced its Ambatovy nickel output forecast to about 30,000 tonnes for the year to March 31, from roughly 40,000 previously, citing equipment malfunctions and a utility plant glitch that is not yet clearly resolved. The downgrade coincides with weak nickel prices and worsened financial losses.

title: Bill Gates, mining and Zambia: Was AI used to find a massive Copper deposit
summary: KoBold Metals, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and others, says drilling in Zambia’s Mingomba project has discovered a large, high-grade copper deposit, likened to the Kakula mine. The firm has not yet published updated resource or feasibility studies, and first output is targeted early next decade.

title: Stronger dollar and China demand gloom weighs on copper
summary: Copper prices fell to their lowest in nearly two weeks as the dollar climbed and sentiment around China’s property sector worsened. Traders cited weak credit impulse and fading expectations of Fed cuts after strong U.S. jobs data. While mining issues offered some support, aluminium and nickel also edged lower.

title: Resource Mining acquires Tanzanian copper-gold projects
summary: Australia-based RMC acquired a 75% stake in Vancouver Mineral Resources, gaining the Mpanda and Mbozi copper-gold projects in Tanzania. The areas have a history of copper mining and are along strike from high-grade Singililwa copper operations. The deal expands RMC’s Ni-Cu exploration base but provides no immediate production impact.

title: Bill Gates-backed miner discovers large-scale copper deposit in Zambia
summary: KoBold Metals says it has discovered a Kakula-scale, high-grade copper deposit at its Mingomba project in Zambia. With Zambia already among top copper producers and demand supported by electrification, the find boosts expectations for future supply and investment in new copper capacity.

title: Adani to open $1.2bn copper refinery in Gujarat, India
summary: Adani’s subsidiary Kutch Copper is moving ahead with a $1.2bn greenfield copper refinery in Mundra, Gujarat, targeting a Phase I start by end-March and 0.5mtpa refined copper output. The project aims to reduce India’s copper imports and includes integrated sulphuric acid production, with a planned 1mtpa Phase II.

title: Gates, Bezos-backed KoBold says Zambia copper find largest in a century
summary: KoBold Metals, backed by Gates and Bezos, said its Mingomba asset in Zambia is the country’s largest copper deposit in a century and will be fast-tracked for development. The announcement is positive for copper sentiment by implying future supply, though output timing likely limits immediate physical impact.

title: AEROBAL reports 6% surge in aluminium can deliveries for 2023
summary: AEROBAL says global aluminium aerosol can shipments rose 6% in 2023 to about 6.4 billion units, with demand stronger across EU, the Americas, and Africa, and a high order backlog into early 2024. The outlook is positive, while Germany’s primary aluminium output decline and production cost/regulatory concerns add supply tightness risk.

title: MetalX Plans Defiance, Ohio, Aluminum Recycling Operations
summary: MetalX plans to build an aluminum recycling campus in Defiance, Ohio, featuring scrap shredding/sortation and an aluminum rolling-slab facility to convert scrap into slabs for sheet production. The project supports automotive, beverage, and building markets, with operations expected in the first half of 2027.

title: Bill Gates- and Jeff Bezos-backed startup discovers large-scale copper deposit in Zambia
summary: KoBold Metals, backed by investors including Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos, says it has discovered a large, high-grade copper deposit at its Mingomba project in Zambia. If developed at scale, it could expand future copper supply, but the news does not indicate immediate production that would move prices soon.

title: Adani group building 1 million tpa copper plant at Mundra, Gujarat
summary: Adani’s subsidiary Kutch Copper is investing about $1.2 billion to build a Mundra, Gujarat copper smelter and refinery, starting production by March with 500,000 tpa and scaling to 1 million tonnes by 2029. It is meant to address India’s copper import shortfall after Sterlite’s shutdown.

title: London copper advances on easing dollar, China stock boost
summary: London base metals rose Tuesday as the US dollar eased and risk sentiment improved after state-backed Chinese stock buying. Three-month LME copper gained 0.7%. LME nickel increased 0.7%, while LME aluminium edged up 0.1%. The article also cites pressure from weak SHFE demand ahead of Lunar New Year.

title: Analysis by region: Alumina Operating Rate Hits a New Low in the Past Months
summary: China’s metallurgical-grade alumina production rose year-on-year but fell modestly month-on-month, with several provinces cutting operating rates due to ore shortages and pollution warnings that restricted calcination capacity. Some plants resumed in early February. Overall, tighter alumina supply conditions are supportive for aluminium prices.

title: LME nickel price collapse forces Forrest to recapitalise Mincor's Kambalda mines
summary: Forrest’s Wyloo vehicle, owner of Mincor Resources, injected $31 million to recapitalise its Kambalda nickel operations after a significant nickel price slump. Mincor has announced mine closure, also citing product quality problems from higher-than-expected arsenic levels in nickel ore.

title: Copper Fox Provides Update on Sombrero Butte Copper Project
summary: Copper Fox reported hyperspectral survey findings and relogging/sampling at its Sombrero Butte copper project in Arizona, mapping alteration patterns and breccia-related anomalies consistent with a porphyry system. It also relays historical drill results with copper-bearing intervals, but the news is exploration-focused and unlikely to move broader copper markets soon.

title: KoBold intends to expedite $2bn Zambia copper mine
summary: KoBold Metals plans to expedite development of its high-grade Mingomba copper project in Zambia, estimated at about $2bn, using partnerships and investor support. The company expects shaft sinking to start around 2027, implying limited immediate supply impact. Nickel is referenced only generally via broader exploration interests.

title: Mosaic Intersects 135 Meters Grading 0.34% Nickel on Gaboury Including 0.48% Nickel on 33 Meters
summary: Mosaic Minerals reports drill results from the Gaboury project, including multiple nickel-bearing intersections: 135 meters at 0.34% Ni (and higher-grade intervals such as 33 meters at 0.48%), plus other long zones with grades up to ~0.40% Ni. The company says results confirm nickel potential and plans further drilling and surveys.

title: Mosaic Intersects 135 Meters Grading 0.34% Nickel on
summary: Mosaic Minerals reported drilling intersections at its Gaboury project, including multiple long intervals of nickel-bearing ultramafic units (e.g., 135 m at 0.34% Ni). The company says results confirm nickel potential over several kilometers and plans additional winter/spring drilling and surveys. Other metals are noted, but no production is affected.

title: Copper giant Freeport to handle Asian sales from Indonesia
summary: Freeport McMoRan said Asian sales will be handled from Indonesia, with its Indonesian arm localizing sales, logistics, and marketing teams based in Jakarta. The shift centers on Grasberg and the Manyar smelter, nearing completion in May, but no immediate volume or disruption changes are cited.

title: Pampa Metals Corp.: Pampa Metals Intersects Thick Supergene Copper Enrichment Blanket and Extends Primary Cu-Au Mineralization to Depth at Piuquenes, San Juan Province, Argentina
summary: Pampa Metals reports drillhole PIU-01 intersected a 160m thick supergene copper enrichment zone with overlapping primary porphyry Cu-Au mineralization at its Piuquenes project in Argentina. First assay results are pending and drilling continues to extend mineralization laterally and at depth. No production or supply changes are announced.

title: China's refined nickel trade signals new production trends: Andy Home - 2024-02-06
summary: Reuters reports China’s net refined nickel imports fell to a near-decade low in 2023 as demand for Class I waned and imports of intermediates (NPI, matte, MHP) from Indonesia rose. New Chinese conversion/export capacity boosted refined nickel shipments, lowering Class I import needs. Nickel sulphate trade is also expanding.

title: Yunnan Operation of Electrolytic Aluminum Remains Stable | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports Yunnan’s electrolytic aluminum operating capacity is about 4.49 million tons, unchanged. A dry season keeps hydropower contribution low, reducing expectations for higher industrial electricity demand. Enterprises have no immediate plans to restart production and await clearer power-sector policy.

title: Shanghai Nickel inventory continues to accumulate and reach a new high in over three years
summary: LME data cited in the article shows nickel inventories fluctuated but ended slightly higher, while Shanghai nickel stocks continued to build during the Feb. 2 week. Inventories rose 3.32% to 15,622 tons, the highest in over three years. The trend of rising stocks is generally bearish for nickel futures.

title: Miners call for government help as nickel prices crash, but analysts say taxpayer-funded bailout unnecessary
summary: Western Australian nickel miners seek urgent government support after nickel prices crash on oversupply, with closures including Wyloo Metals, Savannah Nickel and Ravensthorpe affecting jobs. Analysts say a taxpayer-funded bailout is unwarranted due to boom-bust dynamics and cheap low-cost supply from Indonesia, Philippines and China, keeping sentiment bearish.

title: Amendment to aluminium P1020A all-in price, delivered US Midwest
summary: Fastmarkets updated its methodology for the aluminum P1020A all-in price delivered to the US Midwest. The formula previously used LME unofficial cash PM bid prices, which were discontinued after a 90-day notice. The new benchmark uses LME cash AM bid plus a Fastmarkets Midwest premium, published daily.

title: EV Minerals Strengthens Exploration Portfolio with Acquisition of Two Nickel Exploration Properties near Sudbury, Ontario
summary: EV Minerals announced a binding LOI to acquire 100% of the Baldwin and Lunge nickel exploration properties near Sudbury, Ontario, with immediate sampling planned. The projects’ geology indicates potential nickel and copper sulphide mineralization. However, there is no near-term production change, so price effects are likely limited to sentiment.

title: Global carmakers may be using aluminum made with Uyghur forced labor: report
summary: Human Rights Watch alleges major automakers source aluminum that may involve Uyghur forced labor in Xinjiang, noting traceability difficulties as Xinjiang aluminum is mixed into broader supply chains. The report raises prospects of EU/US forced-labor import restrictions, but the article does not show immediate aluminum supply disruption.

title: KoBold Metals, Backed by Gates and Bezos, Unearths Massive Copper Deposit in Zambia
summary: KoBold Metals announced a large, high-grade copper discovery at the Mingomba project in Zambia, supported by Gates- and Bezos-linked investors. The company must complete feasibility studies before any $2 billion plant decision. The article frames it amid concerns about copper supply for EVs and renewables, but no near-term output is cited.

title: Chile copper miner Codelco's 2023 production declines, but recovery seen this year
summary: Codelco’s copper output has fallen to a multi-decade low due to operational issues and delayed projects, but the company expects a rebound, with production seen rising in 2024. It also plans capacity increases at Chuquicamata and a brief belt swap stoppage next year.

title: Aluminum Producers Urge EU To Sanction Russia's Metal Imports
summary: European aluminum producers are urging the EU to sanction Russia’s aluminum imports, noting Europe still buys about 9% of its aluminum from Russia. However, diplomats say a full ban is unlikely by February 24 because some EU industrial countries oppose measures that could raise prices and oppose fast agreement across member states.

title: A Jeff Bezos- and Bill Gates-backed metals company has discovered a massive copper reserve in Zambia
summary: The piece claims a metals company backed by Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates has found a massive copper reserve in Zambia. Such a discovery can affect market sentiment by pointing to potential future copper supply, which may support copper prices in the near term.

title: China's refined nickel trade signals new production trends: Andy Home
summary: China’s net imports of refined Class I nickel fell to a near-decade low in 2023 as imports weakened and Chinese operators increasingly convert Indonesian nickel intermediates into refined metal for export. Exports reached the highest monthly levels since 2019, and China is also building nickel sulphate flows for batteries.

title: Police investigate after suspected copper wire theft knocks out power in downtown Calgary
summary: Police are investigating suspected copper wire theft that knocked out power in downtown Calgary. The report indicates a local disruption tied to copper wiring, but it does not specify the quantity stolen or broader supply implications, making near-term effects on copper prices likely negligible.

title: Ivanhoe Mines' Kamoa-Kakula Signs Term Sheet to Export Copper Along Lobito Atlantic Railway Corridor
summary: Ivanhoe Mines’ Kamoa-Kakula reportedly signed a term sheet to export copper via the Lobito Atlantic Railway corridor. Easier/confirmed export routing can improve near-term supply flow expectations from the project, which may tighten effective supply views and lend mild bullish pressure to copper prices over coming days to weeks.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines' Kamoa-Kakula Signs Term Sheet to Export Copper Along Lobito Atlantic Railway Corridor
summary: Ivanhoe Mines’ Kamoa-Kakula signed a term sheet for reserved transport capacity on the Lobito Atlantic Railway Corridor, targeting 120,000–240,000 tonnes per year of copper concentrate/blister-anode from 2025 (with trial shipments extended in 2024). The deal is expected to cut export logistics costs versus trucking.

title: Copper concentrate production in Armenia down 5.8% in 2023
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate production fell 5.8% in 2023 to about 289,608 tons, according to the National Statistics Committee.
