summary: First Quantum Minerals said it expects to be able to remove and sell already mined copper from Panama’s disputed Cobre Panama mine after the May elections. The mine was shut over environmental protests and a nullified contract. The possible copper sales could support costs and improve near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Guinea's bauxite production increases for third consecutive year
summary: Guinea’s bauxite production rose over 19% year-on-year in 2023 to about 123 million tonnes, while exports increased 24.5% to about 127 million tonnes, Reuters reported. Guinea is the world’s largest bauxite producer, and investment plans by SMB-Winning could further expand shipments.

title: The Metals Company provides update on nickel sulfate derived from seafloor polymetallic nodules
summary: The Metals Company says SGS Canada completed bench-scale tests producing nickel sulfate from seafloor polymetallic nodules, including processing nickel-cobalt-copper matte into nickel sulfate. It also plans further work toward cobalt sulfate. The announcement is exploratory and does not signal immediate commercial nickel supply, so near-term price effects appear limited.

title: BlackRock Says $12,000 Copper Is Needed to Incentivize New Mines
summary: BNN Bloomberg’s headline cites BlackRock saying roughly $12,000 copper is needed to motivate new mine investment. The implication is that current incentives may be insufficient to bring on supply, supporting expectations of tighter availability and firmer copper prices over the coming weeks.

title: DRC Pauses Mining License at Zijin-Owned Copper and Cobalt Project Over Radioactivity Concerns
summary: DRC paused the mining license for Zijin Mining’s COMMUS copper and cobalt project after shipments to South Africa were rejected for elevated radioactivity. The halt raises near-term copper supply concerns, adding to broader disruption worries as Citi expects copper to rise and prices have recently pushed higher.

title: Lured by copper, major miners drawn to Quesnel Trough and Golden Triangle
summary: Copper prices rose to a two-year high as investors bet supply won’t keep pace with demand. The article cites falling LME warehouse stocks and multiple supply interruptions—Panama’s Cobre Panama shutdown, Peru shipping disruptions, output cuts in Chile and other regions—driving expectations of a widening 2024 deficit.

title: Capstone Copper to invest US$150mn in Chile's Mantoverde
summary: Capstone Copper plans to invest US$150 million in its Mantoverde project in Chile. The announcement is expected to influence market expectations for copper production capacity, supporting copper sentiment. While the full supply impact is likely longer term, project funding can still provide some short-term bullish bias for copper prices.

title: Lower iron, nickel and copper prices weigh on Vale's quarterly earnings
summary: Reuters reports Vale’s Q1 earnings were hurt by lower realized prices for iron ore, nickel, and copper. Copper’s average realized price fell 19% year on year and nickel’s fell 33%, despite higher volumes of copper and iron ore. Vale’s net profit and adjusted EBITDA both missed analyst expectations.

title: Lower iron, nickel and copper prices weigh on Vale's quarterly earnings
summary: Vale reported weaker Q1 earnings, attributing the decline to lower iron ore, nickel and copper prices versus the prior year. Realized copper prices fell 19% and nickel dropped 33%. Higher sales volumes partially offset the price weakness, but EBITDA still missed analyst expectations.

title: Senators, Union Workers Call On Joe Biden to Hike Aluminum Tariffs to Save American Jobs
summary: Republican and Democratic senators, alongside United Steelworkers, urge President Biden to increase U.S. tariffs on imported aluminum. They argue that cheaper foreign aluminum extrusions are threatening U.S. aluminum extrusion plants and jobs. The proposal implies reduced aluminum imports and likely higher near-term domestic aluminum prices.

title: Anglo American receives BHP buyout proposal, could reshape copper market
summary: BHP’s all-share buyout proposal for Anglo American would create the world’s largest copper producer, with combined copper output around 2.6 million tonnes (~10% of global supply). The potential consolidation, alongside existing copper demand and supply bottleneck narratives, supports near-term bullish sentiment for LME copper.

title: Copper rises on funds inflow, potential supply shortage
summary: Copper prices rose as investment funds extended inflows into the market, lifting LME and SHFE contracts. The move was further supported by analyst forecasts calling for a sizable 2024 refined copper deficit. A weaker dollar also helped, adding incremental near-term buying pressure for copper.

title: BHP to reshape copper market with Anglo bid
summary: BHP received an all-share buyout proposal for Anglo American, which would create the world’s largest listed copper producer. The deal would likely spur further mining M&A as firms seek exposure to energy-transition metals. Analysts cite BHP’s preference for copper and potential synergies, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: John Wood : Wood to develop major expansion of Antofagasta's Nueva Centinela copper mine project
summary: Wood was awarded an EPCm contract by Antofagasta to expand the Nueva Centinela copper mine in Chile, adding facilities such as a concentrating plant, ore crushing, conveyors, a seawater pipeline, tailings disposal and port infrastructure. Work starts May 2024, but first copper output is expected in 2027.

title: BHP Group makes $38.8 billion play for Anglo American, copper in focus
summary: BHP made an offer to buy Anglo American in a deal that would create the world’s biggest copper miner, with about 10% of global output. The proposal targets increased access to copper supply for the clean energy transition, boosting market expectations for copper-linked production and sentiment.

title: More Chinese Nickel Seen Flowing Overseas After LME's Russia Ban
summary: The headline reports that more Chinese nickel is being seen flowing overseas following the LME’s Russia ban. The implication is that buyers’ supply channels may shift away from Russia and toward alternative origins, potentially increasing available nickel supply and limiting upside pressure on prices in the near term.

title: Analysis-BHP's proposed bid for Anglo American is a big bet on copper
summary: Reuters says BHP’s bid for Anglo American would reshape copper supply expectations. The report links bullish demand with unexpectedly tight concentrate and refined availability, including the closure of Cobre Panama and Anglo production guidance cuts. Shortage forecasts and rising LME/Shanghai copper prices point to strong near-term upside pressure.

title: BHP Group makes $38.8 bln play for Anglo American, copper in focus
summary: BHP offered to buy Anglo American for about $38.8 billion, valuing the deal at 31.1 billion pounds. If completed, the combination would create the world’s biggest copper miner with around 10% of global output, boosting access to additional copper and supporting copper market expectations.

title: SMM: Spot copper concentrate TC near $0/mt, how will the copper market evolve in second and third quarters amid concentrated maintenance at smelters?
summary: SMM notes China’s copper concentrate output has been declining while smelting capacity grows, worsening raw-material shortages. Overseas disruptions (Panama mine closure, Zambia drought, Vale mine closures) cut concentrate availability. Spot treatment charges have fallen to near $0/mt, and smelter maintenance in Q2-Q3 should lift inventories, underpinning copper tightness sentiment.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Reports New Copper Porphyry Discovery at 1516 Zone and Final 2023 Drill Results
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. announced a new copper porphyry discovery at its 1516 Zone within the MPD project in southern British Columbia, along with final 2023 drill results from multiple zones. Intercepts show broad copper mineralization from surface to substantial depths, supporting follow-up drilling and positive copper sentiment.

title: Kodiak Reports New Copper Porphyry Discovery at 1516 Zone and Final 2023 Drill Results
summary: Kodiak Copper Corp. reports a new copper porphyry discovery at its MPD project (1516 Zone) with drill intercepts including 0.12% CuEq over 258 m and additional shallow high-grade Cu/Ag. Final 2023 results also confirm mineralization across West, South and Man zones, supporting further drilling plans.

title: Copper: BHP wants to acquire Anglo American
summary: BHP’s proposed acquisition of Anglo American would add copper mines in Chile and Peru, increasing access to a major share of global copper output (estimated 10%). The deal follows Anglo’s profit plunge and metal demand writedowns. It is conditional and under UK bid timelines, shaping short-term sector expectations.

title: Southern Copper : SCC reports 1Q24 results
summary: Southern Copper reported 1Q24 results, highlighting higher copper sales volumes and lower operating cash cost per pound, supporting company cash generation. It also notes LME copper was down versus 1Q23 (-5.4%) and compares copper price changes across quarters. Overall, it signals firm operating performance but mixed copper price context.

title: BHP makes US$39-billion offer for rival Anglo American in bid to create world's biggest copper producer
summary: BHP’s $39-billion bid for Anglo American to create the world’s biggest copper producer is likely to boost near-term copper price sentiment, given Anglo’s ~760,000 tonnes/year of copper output and the prospect of supply consolidation. Nickel is only indirectly affected via references to Anglo’s nickel assets and possible review.

title: Toronto Stocks Move Lower; Teck Resources Rises on Jump in Copper Output
summary: Toronto stocks were lower, but Teck Resources shares rose 7.5% after reporting higher quarterly copper output. The company said production at its Quebrada Blanca mine in Chile is ramping up, offsetting weaker-than-expected earnings. Softer coal volumes were cited, but copper production improved.

title: BHP's $39 Billion Bid for Anglo American Could Create World's Largest Copper Producer
summary: BHP launched a $38.8 billion bid for Anglo American, highlighting the deal’s potential to create the world’s largest copper miner. With BHP emphasizing Anglo’s copper assets and possible consolidation, markets view the move as supportive for copper supply expectations, contributing to a generally bullish near-term tone for copper.

title: Chile president wants copper output boost of 1 mln tons by 2026
summary: Chile President Gabriel Boric said he wants Chile to boost annual copper output by 1 million metric tons by the end of his term in 2026, referencing both state-run Codelco and private producers. The government’s stated supply expansion agenda could increase expectations of future copper availability.

title: Teck copper output shoots up on QB mine, profit disappoints
summary: Teck Resources reported copper output up 74% year-to-date, mainly from ramping up the extension at its Quebrada Blanca (QB) mine in Chile. While the company’s profits disappointed, the key market takeaway is increased near-term copper supply from the expansion, which can pressure copper prices.

title: Europe's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism to Impact Aluminium Market, Reports Wood Mackenzie
summary: Wood Mackenzie reports the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) will negatively affect the primary aluminium market by penalizing older EU smelters under a framework that counts only direct emissions. It expects higher costs for EU consumers and notes potential buyer shifts if Russian supply faces sanctions.

title: International Business: BHP Group makes $38.8 bln play for Anglo American, copper in focus
summary: BHP made an offer to buy Anglo American in a deal that would create the world’s biggest copper miner. The proposed combination values Anglo at 31.1 billion pounds and includes exchange components tied to other holdings. If completed, it would expand BHP’s copper access, boosting copper sentiment near term.

title: Lower CBA supply driving low-VAT aluminium premium higher in Brazil
summary: Brazilian traders report fewer deliveries of CBA’s low-VAT aluminium ingot despite no major demand/supply shift, raising concerns about production constraints or strategic holding. Fastmarkets assessments show the low-VAT aluminium premium in São Paulo narrowing upward, suggesting local aluminium supply tightness and bullish price pressure.

title: Copper concentrate traders 'gambling' on market tightness continuing into 2025
summary: Traders have locked in 2025 copper concentrate tonnages at “very low” treatment charges, betting on sustained tightness. TCs have collapsed to record lows amid supply disruptions and expanding smelter capacity, pressuring smelter margins and raising risks of curtailments or trader/smelter failures. Forecasts suggest only modest TC recovery.

title: Mining giant BHP Billiton makes $39 billion bid for Anglo American to expand copper operations
summary: BHP made an unsolicited, highly conditional $39 billion all-share bid for Anglo American to expand copper operations. The deal would create the biggest copper miner with ~10% of global output, boosting copper presence amid clean-energy demand. Anglo’s board is reviewing the offer and a formal bid is due by May 22.

title: BHP's proposed takeover of Anglo a validation of copper focus: Teck CEO
summary: The headline reports Teck CEO saying BHP’s proposed takeover of Anglo “validates” BHP’s focus on copper. That framing can influence expectations about future copper supply and development priorities, potentially supporting sentiment and short-term positioning in copper markets. Details are not shown in the provided text.

title: Mining Giant BHP Bets on Copper With Megabid for Anglo American
summary: BHP has offered nearly $39 billion to buy Anglo American, conditional on Anglo spinning off its platinum and Kumba iron ore units. The deal highlights Anglo’s copper assets and BHP’s existing stake in Chile’s Escondida mine, reinforcing near-term expectations for copper exposure as EV and renewables demand rises.

title: 6 copper stocks with reliable dividends as demand rises
summary: The article links copper stock dividends to improving copper fundamentals, citing rising demand drivers such as EVs (higher copper intensity), power-heavy AI data centres, and continued construction electricity needs. It also notes limited new mine supply in the near term. It further mentions BHP’s $39bn bid for Anglo American boosting copper miner sentiment.

title: BHP proposed bid for Anglo American spurs talk of Canadian copper mining M&A
summary: BHP’s proposed $39B bid for Anglo American has sparked talk of further Canadian copper miner M&A. Analysts cite extreme challenges in adding copper mines and low-carbon demand, supporting renewed deal activity. Copper has recently rallied on supply fears, and shares of Canadian copper miners rose on Thursday.

title: How Copper Is Defying Weakness in China to Make A Serious Bull Run
summary: Copper is rallying despite a weaker Chinese backdrop, reaching a two-year high near $10,000/t. Gains are attributed to investor positioning (CFTC COT), mine-supply downgrades and disruptions, and improving China GDP and higher refined imports. Offsets include rising SHFE inventories and soft spot premiums, limiting upside.

title: Mount Isa Mines copper smelter worker suffers burns to 60 per cent of his body in workplace incident
summary: A steam vent incident at Mount Isa Mines’ copper smelter in Queensland injured two contract workers, prompting authorities to isolate the scene and investigate. Glencore said smelter operations were currently suspended, indicating a near-term disruption to copper output that could pressure short-term copper supply expectations.

title: Copper Close to Testing $10,000 as BHP Bid Points to Supply Risk
summary: The piece frames copper as nearing $10,000, attributing the strength to BHP’s bid that signals potential supply risk. That narrative suggests markets may be discounting tighter copper availability or increased supply uncertainty in the near term, supporting higher prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Copper rises near $10,000/T on investment flows
summary: Copper prices edged higher, nearing the $10,000/ton resistance, supported by investment flows into funds. LME three-month copper was up about 1%, and SHFE June copper gained about 1.5%. Aluminium and nickel also rose on both LME and SHFE, reflecting broad base-metals sentiment.

title: Two workers seriously burnt at copper mine
summary: Two contract workers were seriously burned at Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter in Queensland when steam discharged from a pressure relief valve. Surface operations were suspended for 24 hours and an investigation is underway, creating at most a short-term copper supply risk unlikely to persist without further findings.

title: Copper Hits $10,000 a Ton as Bulls Predict Looming Deficit
summary: The article headline reports copper reaching $10,000 a ton and describes a bull scenario of a looming supply deficit. That narrative points to tightening near-term availability and stronger demand-supply balance, which typically supports higher copper prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: Copper hits two-year high, surpassing $10,000/T on investment flows
summary: Copper prices hit a two-year high, breaking above $10,000/mt on Friday as index funds and ETFs attracted retail money and momentum-based buying overcame resistance. LME copper rose ~1.1% and Shanghai June copper ~1.7%. Aluminium and nickel also edged higher, reflecting supportive broad metal sentiment.

title: BHP's $60b copper power play rejected by British rival
summary: BHP made a $60 billion bid to acquire Anglo American, arguing it would combine copper (and greater nickel exposure) assets to become a top copper producer. Anglo American rejected the offer, saying it undervalued prospects and created demerger and execution risks, likely limiting any immediate market expectations for copper supply changes.

title: Copper Hits $10,000 a Ton as BHP Bid Shows Tight Supply Pipeline
summary: Copper is reported to hit $10,000/ton, with the move attributed to BHP’s bid and expectations of a tight supply pipeline. The framing suggests near-term supply constraints are tightening, supporting buyers and encouraging upside price pressure over the coming days.

title: Copper hits $US10,000 as BHP's bid for Anglo American releases the bulls
summary: Copper surged to about $US10,000 a tonne after BHP unveiled a $59.6bn bid for Anglo American, prompting renewed confidence for the metal. Anglo rejected the offer, but LME copper futures still rose up to 1.4% on Friday to the highest level since April 2022, adding momentum to recent gains.

title: Commodities investment: Resources funds rebound as copper and gold prices rally
summary: Resources fund managers say the commodity rally that began last month signals a potential new period for mining stocks. They cite copper price strength as part of the rebound, implying improved near-term market sentiment for copper. The excerpt does not describe aluminium or nickel-specific developments.

title: Copper hits US$10,000 a ton as BHP bid shows tight supply pipeline
summary: Copper is reported to have reached US$10,000 a ton, with the rally attributed to BHP’s bid and concerns about a tight supply pipeline. The framing suggests near-term expectations of constrained copper availability, supporting upward price pressure in the immediate market outlook.

title: Copper price tops $10,000 for first time in two years
summary: Copper surged above $10,000/tonne on the LME for the first time in two years, driven by strong global demand tied to electrification and renewables and by tight supplies. The move followed BHP’s $38.8bn bid for Anglo American, though the offer was rejected, while strikes, geopolitics and tighter regulation add support.

title: Minera's Copper Subsidiary Acquires Suaqui Verde Copper Project in Sonora, Mexico
summary: Minera Alamos’ Mexican subsidiary will merge with Minera Gold Copper to acquire the Suaqui Verde copper project in Sonora, adding oxide porphyry resources alongside its Los Verdes and Potreritos assets. The company plans a new resource estimate and future development via open-pit/SX-EW to produce cathode, but no near-term output is specified.

title: Minera Alamos Inc.: Minera's Copper Subsidiary Acquires Suaqui Verde Copper Project in Sonora, Mexico
summary: Minera Alamos’ Mexican subsidiary Cobre 4H de Sonora acquires the Suaqui Verde copper project and related claims, adding to its Los Verdes and Potreritos copper assets. The deposit is described as oxidized porphyry copper potentially developable via open-pit/SX-EW, but no near-term output is provided.

title: Codelco Posts Fresh Output Slump, Underscoring Copper Struggles
summary: Codelco’s fresh output slump points to weaker copper production, tightening the expected near-term supply outlook. With Chile’s major producer not running at prior levels, market expectations for copper inventories and availability can shift lower, typically pressuring prices downward over the next days to a few weeks.

title: A new dash for copper is underway - how will it play out? Expert Q&A
summary: BHP’s $39bn bid for Anglo American and potential mining consolidation put copper in focus, with the companies together controlling about 10% of global copper. The expert links demand growth to electrification and renewables, and argues consolidation could improve miners’ pricing power, supporting copper bullish expectations.

title: Opinion: Copper is the new oil and Big Mining sees the metal as its life blood
summary: BHP’s proposed US$39bn bid for Anglo American—mainly to gain its copper mines in Chile and Peru—was rejected as undervaluing the company. The story suggests a likely higher re-bid and potential rival/Chinese bids, reinforcing tight copper supply expectations and ongoing investor demand for copper assets.

title: The U.S. dollar fell, metal fell, industrial silicon, Shanghai tin fell more than 1%, alumina rose 1.37% [SMM Afternoon Review]
summary: SMM reports a broad decline in LME base metals by midday, with London copper and London aluminum down within 0.5%, while London nickel rose. It also notes the Shanghai Futures Exchange adjusted margin ratios and price limits for copper and aluminum futures effective April 17, alongside mixed Chinese industrial metal price moves.

title: A New Dash For Copper Is Underway - How Will It Play Out? Expert Q&A
summary: The Conversation discusses copper after BHP made a bid for UK rival Anglo American, valuing it at about US$39 billion. By focusing on copper headlines tied to major producer deal-making, the piece implies market attention to copper-linked supply and producer valuations, which can support copper prices near term.

title: Stainless steel market sentiment fell ferronickel upstream and downstream game prices temporarily stabilized
summary: SMM reports stable high-nickel pig iron prices at 956 yuan/nickel point as Indonesia’s Ramadan/Eid disruptions and suspended RKAB approvals keep ferronickel raw materials tight. Production ramp-up is slow and some smelters remain shut. Demand improves near May, with stainless mills replenishing inventories, supporting short-term stability and strength.

title: The spot price of stainless steel is temporarily stable, the circulating resources of ferronickel are tight, and the price is stable and strong
summary: SMM reports the average spot price of 8–12% high-nickel pig iron rose slightly and remains supported. Indonesia faces holiday disruptions and slower approvals, smelter raw-material availability stays tight, and production ramp-up is slow, while domestic inventories are limited. Demand for stainless-steel raw material reserves improves, supporting stable, strong prices short term.

title: upstream was more willing to raise the price, and the price of ferronickel rose
summary: SMM reports the April 23 average price of 8–12% high-nickel pig iron rose to 956 yuan/nickel point (+4.5 yuan). Supply is constrained by Indonesia holiday effects, stalled RKAB approvals, tight smelter raw materials, and slow production ramp-up. Demand improves as stainless steel reserve buying lifts transactions, supporting short-term strength.

title: Copper juniors converge in BC, the Yukon
summary: The article argues that copper-focused junior exploration activity in British Columbia and the Yukon is set to rise, citing higher exploration spend and multiple copper project developments and drill plans. It suggests this could lead to new discoveries, later development, and M&A involving major miners—supportive for copper sentiment.

title: European Commodities: After Asian Supply Shock, What's Next for Nickel?
summary: The article focuses on nickel after the 2022 sanctions-driven supply shock and subsequent oversupply from China and Indonesia. It cites current production-curtailment initiatives, Australia closures (BHP’s Nickel West), and tentative price recovery. It also notes sanctions limiting Russian aluminium deliveries to LME/CME, tightening stocks and supporting aluminium.

title: BHP's $60 billion play for copper giant Anglo American was years in the making
summary: BHP’s CEO succession in 2020 followed years of missteps as it sought to reshape its portfolio. The news highlights BHP’s $60 billion bid for Anglo American, portrayed as a major copper producer. The deal narrative may affect market expectations for copper supply and investment, though details are limited.

title: China Minmetals completes acquisition of copper mine in Botswana-Xinhua
summary: MMG, a subsidiary of China Minmetals, has finalized its purchase of the Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana’s Kalahari Copper Belt. The long-life mine targets about 60,000 tonnes of copper annually and holds large reserves. The deal, worth $1.875 billion, aims to strengthen strategic resource supply.

title: China Minmetals completes acquisition of copper mine in Botswana
summary: China Minmetals’ subsidiary MMG has completed the $1.875 billion acquisition of the Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana’s Kalahari Copper Belt. The long-life mine has over six million tons of copper reserves and has been operating since June 2021, targeting about 60,000 tons of copper annually.

title: SunLive - Time running out for NZ's copper phone network
summary: New Zealand telco One NZ plans to finish decommissioning its copper landline exchanges next year as customers move to mobile and VOIP on fibre. The Commerce Commission is suing over emergency access during power cuts. VOIP uses fibre, requiring battery backup. The shift reduces copper landline demand, not linked to immediate global pricing.

title: Australia's Ardea Resources teams up with Sumitomo, Mitsubishi for nickel project
summary: Ardea Resources signed a binding deal with Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi to form a joint venture and fund a definitive feasibility study for the Kalgoorlie nickel project. The study will guide a final investment decision, with Sumitomo/Mitsubishi funding A$98.5 million for a 50% stake. Shares rose sharply.

title: Japan's giants commit to Aussie nickel joint venture
summary: Ardea Resources, with Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi, agreed on a 50:50 joint venture to accelerate a $3 billion nickel-cobalt project in Western Australia. The project is expected to produce about 30,000 tonnes of nickel annually, but completion is targeted for the September quarter 2024 amid a reported nickel glut.

title: Copper trends higher on tight supply; BHP-Anglo American deal in focus
summary: Copper prices opened higher as supply tightness (ore and concentrate shortages after Cobre Panama’s December closure) pushed processing fees into negative territory. Investors also focused on BHP’s potential improved bid for Anglo American, raising supply concerns and prompting fund buying as LME copper tested $10,000.

title: Infinitum Copper Updates C$450,000 Private Placement
summary: Infinitum Copper amended terms of a C$450,000 private placement after a 1:2 share rollback. Funds are intended for establishing mining operations at the La Adelita copper-silver-gold project in Mexico. The company states no investor-relations payments and confirms standard restricted resale terms.

title: Mount Lyell copper mining update, key study to help next stage | The Advocate
summary: Sibanye Stillwater is advancing a feasibility study to potentially reopen the historic Mount Lyell mine, which produced copper until 2014. The study targets three underground deposits and includes building a new concentrator plant and refurbishing a vertical shaft. Outcomes are expected to feed a preliminary project budget in the second half of 2025.

title: WA jobs losses: Job cuts at WA nickel miner First Quantum in Ravensthorpe
summary: First Quantum says it will put the Ravensthorpe nickel mine in Western Australia into care and maintenance, ending production by late May and cutting about 330 jobs. Management cites significant current and projected losses despite prior cost/strategy changes. The shutdown implies reduced near-term nickel supply.

title: How to estimate the future trend of nickel prices? [SMM analysis] | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: Nickel prices have stayed strong, peaking near 148,270 yuan/mt before slipping but holding above 140,000. SMM attributes gains to ore cost support and macro non-ferrous outperformance, plus delays/uncertainty around RKAB approvals that limit near-term oversupply. Sanctions reduce Russian nickel deliveries; refined surplus looks limited in H1.

title: First Quantum Minerals to close Ravensthorpe nickel project with loss of 330 jobs
summary: First Quantum says it will place its Ravensthorpe nickel operation in care and maintenance, with production ending by late May, citing projected lower nickel prices and high operating costs. The move follows other WA nickel cuts and implies a near-term supply reduction from a marginal producer.

title: Stanislav Kondrashov Telf AG: China is reducing nickel iron production due to profitability problems — Пресс-релизы
summary: Expert analysis says China’s ferronickel/nickel pig iron production is under strain: profitability challenges have led to some plant shutdowns, and nickel pig iron output is forecast to fall in April versus March. The suspension is described as a temporary supply-demand balancing measure, potentially tightening global nickel supply.

title: ASX BHP: Japan Inc backing for nickel mine has ramifications for BHP
summary: Japanese firms Sumitomo and Mitsubishi will fund Ardea Resources’ $3.1 billion nickel laterite and cobalt project in Western Australia. The backing could strengthen expectations for incremental nickel supply from the Kalgoorlie region, while also highlighting uncertainty around BHP’s need for support.

title: Nickel miner First Quantum Minerals axes 530 jobs as pressure builds for federal budget bailout
summary: First Quantum Minerals will axe 530 jobs and move its Ravensthorpe nickel operations to care and maintenance within days. The move follows mounting pressure on Australia’s nickel industry amid a surge in nickel supply from Chinese-backed Indonesian producers. The Albanese government faces renewed calls for a federal bailout in May.

title: Vedanta Seeks Deals With Traders to Help Fund Zambia Copper Mine
summary: Vedanta is reported to be seeking deals with traders to help fund its Zambia copper mine. By securing financing to support production and ongoing operations, the development could reduce near-term supply risk for copper, supporting expectations of steadier output in the coming weeks.

title: Towards the end of the month, the downstream stocking sentiment has risen, and the short-term ferronickel price is still running strongly.
summary: SMM reports that average SMM 8–12% high-nickel pig iron prices rose to 963.5 yuan/nickel point. Supply disruptions from Indonesia holidays, suspended RKAB approvals, and tight smelter feed reduce output. Meanwhile strong ferronickel cost support and steel mills’ earlier buying lift demand, supporting near-term prices.

title: Bears take the initiative to increase their positions, and the final intraday rise and fall of -0.4% [SMM Nickel Brief Comment]
summary: SMM notes that Shanghai’s main nickel contract opened at 145,000 yuan/ton and closed at 142,850 yuan/ton, down 3,020 yuan/ton versus the prior close. Intraday price fluctuated within a range, but bears increased positions, and the final daily move was about -0.4%.

title: European Green Transition takes option on copper remnants from Cypriot mine
summary: European Green Transition acquired an option to develop a copper tailings recycling project at Cyprus’ Limni mine. The target is copper remaining in mine backfilled tailings and potentially pit waters. The firm has 12 months for due diligence. It aligns with EU recycling rules, but no near-term output is specified.

title: Ardea locks in Japanese giants for Kalgoorlie nickel project
summary: Ardea Resources says Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi will join an incorporated JV for its Kalgoorlie Nickel (Goongarrie Hub) project, fully funding definitive feasibility study costs and supporting debt financing. The project targets about 30,000 tonnes of nickel annually, with an 18‑month DFS timeline.

title: GCC aluminium producers look to boost exports amid US ban on Russian metals
summary: GCC aluminium producers expect to gain market share after the US and UK banned Russian aluminium imports and restricted Russian trading on major exchanges, with similar measures for copper and nickel. Reports cite falling Russian exports and a likely shift in global trade flows, potentially supporting tighter supply and higher prices.

title: Copperstone Resources : Invitation to presentation of Copperstone Resources's first quarter report 2024
summary: Copperstone Resources announced the publication date and live presentation details for its Q1 2024 report, tied to its reopening and scaling of the Viscaria mine in Kiruna. The release includes no new production, cost, or guidance data, making near-term copper price impact likely minimal despite the company’s copper focus.

title: Arizona Sonoran Copper Company Inc. Reports Completion of Its Indicated Drilling Program on MainSpring, Within the 100%-Owned Cactus Project, Arizona
summary: Arizona Sonoran Copper reports completion of an inferred drilling program at MainSpring on its 100%-owned Cactus Project in Arizona, confirming enriched and primary copper mineralization. Results will feed an updated resource model and later PEA work, while additional infill drilling continues to upgrade inferred to indicated resources.

title: Minera Alamos bolsters Mexican copper foothold
summary: Minera Alamos announced a merger combining its Mexican copper subsidiary with Minera Gold Copper, consolidating the Los Verdes and Potreritos projects and adding the Suaqui Verde porphyry copper asset. Management plans updated resource estimates and cost-focused project design (including SX-EW cathode), but no immediate output changes were stated.

title: Copper prices at 2-year highs thanks to green energy transition
summary: Copper prices are near a two-year high and seen rising further as demand from electric vehicles, wind and solar, and related infrastructure increases. Supply is constrained by lower ore grades, long timelines to bring new mines online, and stricter regulations/environmental hurdles, supporting tighter market expectations.

title: NetNewsLedger - Solaris Resources Expands Project Potential As Global Copper Market Enters Age of Large Deficits
summary: Solaris Resources raises ~$100m to expand exploration for its Warintza copper project in Ecuador as investors track potential development and acquisitions. The broader piece argues global electrification and net-zero goals are lifting copper demand while supply is projected to lag, implying a growing deficit and bullish copper fundamentals.

title: BHP is betting big on a renewable energy future, and it has Anglo American's copper mines in its sights
summary: BHP’s $60 billion takeover bid for Anglo American is presented as part of a low-emissions strategy focused on expanding copper production, including South American mines. The article links copper demand to electrification, clean-energy transmission, AI, and EVs, and notes BHP’s earlier copper/nickel acquisition of OZ Minerals.

title: First Quantum to shut down Ravensthorpe nickel mine
summary: First Quantum Minerals will close its Ravensthorpe nickel operation in Western Australia this week. The shutdown will end production and eliminate about 330 jobs. By cutting near-term nickel output, the decision changes supply expectations and is likely to influence nickel pricing in the coming days and weeks.

title: Western sanctions against Russia causing more copper production to move to China, concentrating control over this critical metal in Chinese hands   – NaturalNews.com
summary: The article claims Western sanctions are pushing Norilsk Nickel to move part of its copper smelting production to China and to sell spot metal in yuan. It also highlights a planned China joint venture for copper smelting. By preserving Russia-to-China flows despite sanctions, it could ease copper tightness.

title: Top 20 Copper Producing Countries in The World
summary: The piece reviews global copper production by country and reiterates rising demand from the green/EV transition, alongside notes that supply may lag. It also mentions BHP’s all-share bid for Anglo American aimed at copper assets, but without new immediate constraints or price-moving policy changes.

title: Sandfire Resources America Inc. Reports High Grade Copper Intersections at the Black Butte Copper Project
summary: Sandfire Resources America reported high-grade copper drill results at its Black Butte Copper project, including 5.37 meters of 10.2% Cu and 6.26 meters of 10.7% Cu. The company aims to upgrade and expand the Johnny Lee Lower Copper Zone resource and extend mine life, supported by ongoing drilling and permitting progress.

title: Sumitomo Metal Mining : and Mitsubishi Corporation to Participate in Kalgoorlie Nickel Project - Goongarrie Hub
summary: Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi Corporation have signed a binding agreement with Ardea Resources to participate in developing the Kalgoorlie Nickel Project in Australia. The announcement indicates new investment and future nickel supply prospects, typically supportive for nickel market sentiment in the short term.

title: Imperial Drilling Intersects 270 Metres Grading 0.65% Copper and 0.48 g/t Gold at Mount Polley
summary: Imperial Metals reported partial diamond drill results from the Mount Polley 2024 exploration program, including a 270-metre intercept grading 0.65% copper (plus gold). Drilling is ongoing and designed to follow up prior results in the Springer zone, with potential to convert mineralization to reserves.

title: Copper just passed US$10,000 a tonne again – Now what?
summary: Copper has risen to near US$10,000/t after eight weeks of gains. The piece cites stronger China PMI readings and an April 13 LME/CME ban on Russian copper produced on/after that date, tightening supply dynamics. It also notes copper–aluminium substitution effects as copper stays expensive.

title: Canadian Miner Closes Nickel Mine in Australia Costing 330 Jobs
summary: First Quantum Minerals will close its Ravensthorpe Nickel Operation in Western Australia, eliminating 330 jobs. The closure removes a source of nickel supply from the market. With nickel used in EV lithium-ion battery supply chains and stainless-steel production, the action is likely to weigh on near-term nickel sentiment.

title: EV Minerals Corporation: EV Minerals Announces Initial Assay Results Including 0.96% Ni, 0.15% Cu, and 0.05% Co Over 0.75 Metres Near Surface at the EVM Nickel Project, Quebec
summary: EV Minerals reported initial assay results from first-pass drilling at its EVM Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in Quebec, including intercepts up to 0.96% Ni and 0.15% Cu near surface. The company says the drilling confirms historic mineralization and suggests expansion potential, but provides no production or inventory impact.

title: EV Minerals Announces Initial Assay Results Including 0.96% Ni, 0.15% Cu, and 0.05% Co Over 0.75 Metres Near Surface at the EVM Nickel Project, Quebec
summary: EV Minerals reported initial assay results from its EVM Nickel-Copper-Cobalt project in Quebec, with drill hole 883-23-004 returning 0.96% nickel and 0.15% copper over 0.75 m near surface, plus broader sulphide mineralization in multiple holes. This supports positive exploration outlook for Ni and Cu.

title: Glencore reports lower Q1 copper production
summary: Glencore reported Q1 copper production of about 239,700 tonnes, down 2% versus the prior year’s 244,100 tonnes. The company left its full-year production forecast unchanged, suggesting the temporary dip may not materially alter total 2024 supply expectations in the near term.

title: Glencore Backs Guidance After Declines in Copper, Coal Output
summary: Glencore reported slightly lower first-quarter copper output (down 2% to 239,700 mt) and higher nickel output (up 14% to 23,800 mt), while backing full-year production targets. With guidance maintained and changes modest, the update is more likely to be informational than to drive sustained price moves.

title: Copper Extends Rally as China's Factory Activity Boosts Optimism
summary: Copper prices extend their rally as optimism grows from stronger-than-expected Chinese factory activity. The improved industrial production outlook can increase expectations for near-term copper demand, providing upward price pressure in the short term.

title: Glencore's Coal, Copper Output Decline -- Commodity Comment
summary: Glencore confirmed full-year guidance after booking declines in copper, coal and cobalt, offset by higher lead, nickel and gold. Copper own-sourced output rose modestly like-for-like, but the company’s overall copper volume declined. Nickel production was up 14% year-on-year on supply-chain recovery, likely limiting a net directional price move.

title: Commodities Overview: Copper nears the USD 10,000 mark
summary: Copper is on an uptrend in London, trading near USD 9,965 and approaching USD 10,000. Gains are attributed to a weakening US dollar and a more negative supply outlook. Chile revised down expected production growth to 5.51m tonnes versus 5.63m previously, supporting bullish sentiment.

title: Copper prices slip after hitting fresh two-year high
summary: Copper prices in London eased 0.4% after a four-session rally, despite concerns about tight supply supporting a strong monthly gain. Softer manufacturing momentum in China and the Labour Day holiday raise demand and liquidity concerns. LME warehouse copper inventories fell, while aluminium and nickel were also slightly lower or flat.

title: Commodities Prices - Commodity Roundup: Copper retreats from recent highs on profit-taking; precious metals fall
summary: A commodities roundup reports that copper has retreated from recent highs on Tuesday as traders take profits. It also notes broad commodity weakness linked to inflation concerns, higher-for-longer rates and a stronger U.S. dollar, which generally dampens demand expectations and weighs on industrial metals like copper.

title: GT Resources Inc.: GT Resources Update - Kostonjarvi (KS) Copper-Nickel-PGE Project, Finland
summary: GT Resources updated work at its Kostonjarvi (KS) Cu-Ni-PGE project in Finland, citing Finnish Geological Survey findings that de-risk the feeder-dyke target with ultramafic intersections and modeled EM/MT conductors. Plans include additional MT and follow-on drilling, but no immediate production or supply impact is reported.

title: Hot Chili Secures Large Addition to its Costa Fuego Coastal Copper Hub in Chile
summary: Hot Chili announced it secured an option to acquire Chilean concessions (the “Domeyko cluster”) within the Domekyo copper-gold mining centre, expanding land holdings at its Costa Fuego copper-gold hub. The news highlights exploration plans and near-term project development work, but no immediate production or supply impact.

title: Bell Copper Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement
summary: Bell Copper Corporation announced a non-brokered private placement to raise up to CDN $500,000 to fund ongoing drilling and exploration at its Big Sandy and other copper projects, plus general working capital. The release is financing-focused and does not indicate immediate changes to copper production or supply flows.

title: Pampa Metals intersects Wide Interval of Intense Porphyry Quartz Veining and Copper Mineralization in Third Drillhole at Piuquenes, San Juan Province, Argentina
summary: Pampa Metals reports completion of drillhole PIU-03 at the Piuquenes porphyry project in Argentina, intersecting porphyry quartz veining with chalcopyrite-bornite mineralization and supergene copper enrichment. Assays are pending for dispatch to ALS. Results could support copper-resource prospects, but no immediate production impact is indicated.

title: Copper smelters in leading buyer China wary of BHP-Anglo American tie-up
summary: Chinese copper smelters fear BHP’s planned bid for Anglo American could reduce their negotiating power over annual terms and increase uncertainty if more volumes are sold under index pricing. The market is already tight after Cobre Panama’s closure and negative treatment charges, reinforcing sensitivity to copper supply expectations.

title: Ardea Resources signs agreement with SMM and Mitsubishi for WA nickel project
summary: Ardea Resources signed a cooperation agreement with Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi to fund and conduct a definitive feasibility study for the Kalgoorlie Nickel Project–Goongarrie Hub in Western Australia. The consortium will provide DFS funding, with potential stake increases post-FID, supporting progress toward nickel supply development.

title: Alta Copper Delivers a New Geological Model; Provides Update on the Optimized PEA; Drill Permit and Community Relations
summary: Alta Copper provided an update on its Cañariaco advanced-stage copper project, including a new geological model identifying drill targets, submission and expected approval of a 40-platform drill permit, and a revised Optimized PEA with results due by May 15, 2024. The company cites progress and upcoming drilling plans.

title: Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi Corporation to Participate in Kalgoorlie Nickel Project
summary: Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi will join a venture to fund the definitive feasibility study for the Kalgoorlie Nickel Project in Western Australia. The project is expected to produce ~30,000 tonnes of nickel per year long term, but the study runs through 2025, limiting immediate near-term price impact.

title: Anglo American shares recover on improvement, copper appeal
summary: Anglo American shares recovered as management highlighted improvements and the “quality and potential” of its copper portfolio. The chair said the copper price is beginning to reflect underlying supply-demand trends, while M&A speculation around BHP’s offer and the company’s rejected bid boosted investor sentiment.

title: Chilean govt to press ahead with plans to build copper smelters, increase state role in lithium production - minister
summary: Chile’s mining minister said the government will press ahead with building new copper smelters and replacing capacity lost at Enami and Codelco sites. The move comes as TC/RCs remain at record lows amid tight concentrate availability. Chile also plans a larger state role in lithium, not tracked here.

title: First Quantum to cease nickel operations in Australia
summary: First Quantum will shut its Ravensthorpe nickel mine in Western Australia, beginning the shutdown process on 1 May. Production halted in January, and the company cites persistent losses, higher operating costs and a weaker nickel price forecast. The closure reduces near-term nickel supply and may support prices.

title: Refined copper market had large surplus in February, ICSG says
summary: ICSG reported the global refined copper market swung to a 226,000 mt surplus in February versus a 30,000 mt deficit in January. Adjusted for Chinese bonded warehouse inventories, the surplus was 256,000 mt. Output and consumption figures imply continued oversupply, with a 162,000 mt surplus expected this year.

title: Canada Nickel Company Concludes Successful Participation in Washington, D.C. Summit on North American Critical Minerals Strategy
summary: Canada Nickel participated in a Washington summit on North American critical minerals, highlighting the Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project in Ontario and its expected role in supplying EV and stainless-steel markets. The CEO referenced US import policy impacts and supply-chain pressures, positioning increased nickel availability and trade collaboration as supportive for nickel sentiment.

title: ICSG forecasts copper supply pressures but cautious on demand: Andy Home
summary: Reuters reports ICSG reduced its copper supply surplus outlook after much lower mine production, including the closure of Panama’s Cobre Panama and a resulting concentrates squeeze. Smelters turned to spot concentrates, driving lower treatment charges and slower refined output growth. Demand forecasts were downgraded, especially in China, tempering upside but not outweighing supply tightness.

title: MIN ASX: Nickel minnow Poseidon blasts lithium heavyweight Mineral Resources
summary: Poseidon Nickel says Mineral Resources is trying to back out of terms for the sale of a nickel concentrator and tenements at Lake Johnston, WA. The dispute centers on deal commitments linked to a processing hub plan, potentially delaying or reducing nickel output prospects. Nickel sentiment may soften amid uncertainty.

title: Intrepid Metals Intersects 105.20 meters of 1.17% Copper (1.42% CuEq) and 48.85 meters of 2.24% Copper (2.58% CuEq) Near Surface in Its Initial Drill Program at its Corral Copper Property in Arizona
summary: Intrepid Metals reported early drill results from its Corral Copper project in Arizona, including long near-surface intercepts such as 105.20m at 1.17% Cu and 48.85m at 2.24% Cu, with additional higher-grade copper intervals. The company is continuing a 5,000m program across mineralized zones.

title: Near-record high LME prices a magnet for Chinese copper exports
summary: Chinese copper producers plan to export up to 100,000 tons to LME-registered warehouses, the largest monthly volume in 12 years, seeking to cool LME prices near record highs. The move is driven by LME–ShFE arbitrage and logistics planning, potentially adding near-term supply and weighing on copper sentiment.

title: Exclusive-Near-record high LME prices a magnet for Chinese copper exports
summary: The headline suggests LME copper is at near-record highs, prompting Chinese exporters to ship more copper. This behavior implies tighter near-term availability outside China and reinforces bullish sentiment toward copper, as producers respond to elevated benchmark prices.

title: How durable are ESG claims made for aluminium packaging?
summary: Virgin Atlantic and easyJet are trialing low-carbon aluminium 5cl bottles, with Diageo launching 70cl aluminium Baileys bottles at airports. The article links aluminium’s lighter weight and lower emissions to increased use of post-consumer recycled (PCR) aluminium, while stressing the need for transparency on recycled content to avoid greenwashing.

title: LME plans for aluminium producers to submit carbon emission data by 2025
summary: The LME launched a consultation requiring LME-deliverable aluminium producers to submit Scope 1 and 2 emissions data by March 2025 to align with the EU CBAM. Non-submitting brands risk delisting. Warehoused deliveries will include a CBAM reporting form, and a low-carbon aluminium product is being considered.

title: Is Copper Heading to $15,000? | OilPrice.com
summary: Three-month LME copper futures have reached $10,000/ton, prompting forecasts of further gains. The article attributes the rise to supply repeatedly lagging demand, citing tighter mining regulations, geopolitical tension, labor strikes, and concentrate concerns after the Cobre Panama closure, plus firmer China demand.

title: IG Global Group: IG ASIA Acquires Majority Interest in the Pribrezhniy Porphyry Copper Deposit in the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: IG Asia (IG Global) agreed to acquire 75% of Rio Tinto’s Pribrezhniy porphyry copper deposit in Kazakhstan, plus additional prospects. The project includes scoping-level studies, infrastructure access, and planned prefeasibility work by 2029. The release is copper-focused but does not imply immediate output changes.

title: 'They're gonna put me outta business': Copper thieves target business owner
summary: A New Iberia businessman reports a surge in thefts of A/C condenser units, taking the copper-rich core that thieves sell as scrap or on the black market. He estimates nine condensers stolen in a month, forcing costly replacements. The copper scrap flow may increase local supply.

title: Rio Tinto aiming to become world's top copper supplier
summary: Rio Tinto says it is expanding its copper footprint and is on track to become a leading copper supplier, citing progress at Oyu Tolgoi underground operations and plans at the Simandou project. While it comments on other commodities and M&A restraint, the copper production focus is supportive for near-term sentiment.

title: RIO ASX : Rio Tinto chairman quiet on Anglo American bid, eyes copper profits
summary: Rio Tinto’s CEO Dominic Barton declined to comment on whether the company would bid for Anglo American, after a shareholder asked at the annual general meeting in Brisbane. Separately, Rio said it is embarking on doubling its copper production, signaling a focus on copper profits.

title: Ardea Resources: Why are these massive Japanese companies putting $98m into this Aussie laterite nickel play?
summary: Ardea Resources says it has secured $98m from major Japanese companies to help fund its very large Aussie laterite nickel project. The deal is framed as enabling long-run production (40 years) and sizable earnings, supporting near-term optimism for nickel project development and supply expectations.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Receives Approval From the Bureau of Land Management for Its Notice of Intent To Conduct Drilling at Its Copper Creek Project in Arizona
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. said the U.S. BLM approved its Notice of Intent to drill at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona, including 11 drill pads. The company plans to test near-surface copper targets using new drilling, potentially expanding resources, but no production or immediate supply change is announced.

title: First publication of low-carbon nickel briquette premium reflects regional differences
summary: Fastmarkets launched and assessed an initial low-carbon nickel briquette premium (cif global $300–880/t) reflecting regional differences, alongside stable in-whs Rotterdam premiums. Market sentiment is mixed on whether buyers pay more for low-carbon attributes, but policy-driven transparency and potential liquidity improvements keep nickel premiums in focus amid bearish nickel sentiment from Indonesian supply.

title: Talon Metals Reports 14 New Holes Intersect Nickel-Copper Mineralization in the Raptor Zone
summary: Talon Metals announced 14 new drill holes intersecting nickel-copper mineralization in Minnesota’s Raptor Zone at its Tamarack project, with assays pending. The company also highlighted a strong borehole electromagnetic anomaly and thick (~up to 10m) mineralized accumulations, implying continued upside for nickel and copper prospectivity.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Reports 14 New Holes Intersect Nickel-Copper Mineralization in the Raptor Zone
summary: Talon Metals reported 14 new drill holes intersecting nickel-copper mineralization in Minnesota’s Raptor Zone, plus a strong borehole electromagnetic anomaly suggesting continuity and potential thicker sulphide zones. Assays are pending and no production or inventory changes are cited, limiting immediate effects on copper and nickel prices.

title: Talon Metals Reports 14 New Holes Intersect Nickel-Copper Mineralization in the Raptor Zone
summary: Talon Metals announced 14 new drill holes intersecting nickel-copper mineralization in the Raptor Zone at its Tamarack project in Minnesota, along with a strong borehole electromagnetic anomaly. Assays are pending and no production changes are stated, limiting immediate near-term impacts to nickel and copper prices.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Reports 14 New Holes Intersect Nickel-Copper Mineralization in the Raptor Zone
summary: Talon Metals announced 14 new drill holes intersecting nickel-copper mineralization in the Raptor Zone at its Tamarack project in Minnesota, with assays pending. The company also highlighted a strong borehole electromagnetic anomaly and thick mineralized intervals, supporting exploration prospects but without immediate production impact.

title: EGA hosts world leading alumina experts for global technical forum in Dubai
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) hosted the Alumina Quality Workshop in Dubai, focusing on decarbonisation and sustainability. It highlights Al Taweelah alumina refinery output of 2.48 million tonnes in 2023 and ongoing technical development following a $3.3 billion expansion. No immediate supply or policy shock is announced.

title: The world is poised on the edge of a new copper supercycle
summary: The piece contends copper faces a “supercycle” setup: structurally strong demand from renewables, electric vehicles and AI-driven data centers, alongside tight supply stemming from years of underinvestment and long project lead times. It cites weakening China-related demand recently but expects further price gains if deficits emerge.

title: IG Asia seals deal to buy 75% stake in Kazakhstan copper deposit
summary: IG Asia signed a conditional deal to buy a 75% stake in Kazakhstan’s Pribrezhniy copper deposit from Rio Tinto, investing $11m to reach prefeasibility by 2029 plus milestone-linked payments. The project’s infrastructure and prior studies support further development, mildly bullish for copper sentiment over coming weeks.

title: Collective Metals Inc: Collective Metals Provides Review of Trojan-Condor Target Area on its Princeton Copper Project in B.C.
summary: Collective Metals reports 2023 soil sampling and reprocessed geophysical review for the Trojan-Condor drill-ready area at its Princeton Cu-Au project in B.C. Elevated localized copper anomalies are identified, supporting potential alkalic Cu-Au porphyry mineralization and outlining next-step 3D IP and drilling plans.

title: LUCA REPORTS SUCCESSFUL METALLURGICAL TEST WORK FOR NEW COPPER CONCENTRATE AT CAMPO MORADO
summary: Luca Mining reports successful ALS metallurgical test work for a copper–lead separation process at its Campo Morado operation. Lab and bench-scale flotation results indicate copper recovery of 80–93% and potential copper concentrate grades up to 28% Cu (vs. 15–18% bulk). The company plans to implement the flowsheet in 2H 2024.

title: Gold production from Indian mines surges by 86 pc in Feb, copper output up 29 pc
summary: India’s Ministry of Mines data show gold output up 86% and copper output up 28.7% to 11,000 tonnes in February. It also reports bauxite production (aluminium feedstock) rising 21% to 2.414 million tonnes. Overall mining and quarrying mineral production rose 8%.

title: Zimbabwe's sole nickel mine placed under administration
summary: Zimbabwe placed its only operating nickel mine, the Trojan Nickel Mine, under administration after production was halted for equipment failure and low market prices. Output has already collapsed and restart plans were delayed due to low prices and high input costs. Administration could further delay supply, supporting nickel prices.

title: Zimbabwe's only operating nickel mine placed under administration
summary: Zimbabwe placed its only operating nickel mine, the Trojan mine, under administration after it halted production months earlier due to equipment failure and low prices. The mine’s output has fallen sharply, with restart delayed over low prices and high electricity/input costs, reducing expected near-term nickel supply.

title: Half of all copper mining is at drought risk with climate change
summary: The piece says about half of copper mining operations face drought risk from climate change. It connects these risks to production challenges and frames them against rising demand from electric vehicles, grid infrastructure, and data centers. Copper has already rallied above $10,000/ton on expectations of future shortages.

title: Canadian miner Hudbay sees BHP's bid for Anglo boosting copper assets
summary: Hudbay CEO said BHP’s $39 billion offer for Anglo increased valuations of copper assets and signals miners’ willingness to pay premiums for existing copper production. Hudbay plans a sale process for a minority stake in its Arizona Copper World project. The piece notes LME three-month copper prices hit a two-year high before easing.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Reports First Quarter 2024 Results
summary: Capstone reported Q1 2024 copper production of 42,121 tonnes and C1 cash costs of $2.88/lb, with higher output and ongoing cost efficiencies. It said Mantoverde’s grinding circuit commissioning is complete and first saleable concentrate remains on track for Q2 2024, supporting near-term copper supply expectations despite lower realized prices.

title: Capstone Copper Reports First Quarter 2024 Results
summary: Capstone Copper reported Q1 2024 results, with consolidated copper production of 42,121 tonnes and C1 cash costs of $2.88/lb. The company noted a lower realized copper price and advanced Mantoverde development, targeting first saleable concentrate in Q2 2024, with feasibility and expansion studies underway.

title: U.S. Aluminum Extruders Coalition Reports: Commerce Department Announces Affirmative Preliminary Dumping Determinations on Imports of Aluminum Extrusions from 14 Countries
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department issued affirmative preliminary dumping determinations on aluminum extrusions imported from 14 countries, setting preliminary antidumping duty rates. After Federal Register publication, U.S. Customs will suspend liquidation and collect cash deposits on entries. The duties aim to counter unfair pricing and are expected to support U.S. aluminum markets near term.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Reports First Quarter 2024 Financial Results
summary: Faraday Copper reported Q1 2024 financial results alongside progress at its Arizona Copper Creek Project, including Bureau of Land Management approval to drill and multiple drilling/metallurgical highlights with measured copper assays. The company remains an exploration stage firm and notes it will need additional funding, with no immediate production impacts mentioned.

title: Bonnell Aluminum Commenting on Preliminary Dumping Determinations
summary: Bonnell Aluminum said it is pleased with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s decision to institute preliminary dumping duties on unfairly traded imports of aluminum extrusions. The statement implies support for domestic producers as duties may reduce import competition and strengthen market pricing and demand expectations in the near term.

title: Amendment by Traeger MP to extend Mount Isa copper mine | The North West Star
summary: An amendment proposed by Traeger MP Robbie Katter would extend Queensland’s Mount Isa Mine Act to allow Queensland to re-tender the site if Glencore shuts down operations, preventing the operator from effectively blocking future activity. Glencore plans to close the mine next year, while supporters cite global copper demand.

title: The Overnight Report: Sigh Of Relief
summary: The overnight report says base metal prices are falling again as renewed Chinese stimulus fails to support prices, with China closed until Tuesday. It notes the US dollar is down with lower yields and the Australian dollar higher, but the overall base-metals tone remains bearish.

title: US Plans to Impose 2.42% Antidumping Tariff on S. Korean Aluminum Extrusions
summary: The US plans to impose a 2.42% antidumping tariff on aluminum extrusions from South Korea. The added duty is expected to raise the cost of imports, potentially reducing demand for those aluminum products and exerting downward pressure on aluminum prices and related trading expectations over the coming days.

title: EV production keeps demand and price for copper high
summary: EV and net-zero plans are expected to lift copper demand, while supply is tightening due to mine outages (e.g., Cobre Panama closure), reduced output forecasts from major miners, and Chinese producer cuts. COMEX copper prices have risen about 22% since early March, with a 2024 refined-copper deficit forecast.

title: US plans up to 43.5% anti-dumping tariff on Korean aluminum extrusion
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department made a preliminary anti-dumping decision imposing up to 43.5% tariffs on Korean aluminum extrusion imports, with smaller rates for one firm and zero for another. The move follows a broader extrusion investigation and will be finalized later this year, potentially affecting aluminum trade and prices.

title: U.S. Plans Up to 43.5 Pct Anti-dumping Tariff on S. Korean Aluminum Extrusion
summary: The U.S. is reported to plan anti-dumping tariffs of up to 43.5% on aluminum extrusion imports from South Korea. Such measures can curb import volumes, tighten availability for buyers in the U.S., and therefore support near-term expectations for aluminium prices.

title: Copper bounces on weak dollar but heads for weekly decline
summary: Copper prices bounced on Friday as the U.S. dollar weakened and forecast revisions pointed to diminished supply after mine disruptions. Reuters cited a sharper reduction in the International Copper Study Group’s global surplus estimate. The story notes nickel and aluminium were also higher, though the core impact drivers were tied to copper.

title: Copper concentrate benchmark structure at risk in current market
summary: Fastmarkets reports copper concentrate TC/RCs have fallen far below benchmark levels, raising questions about whether the 2025 benchmark structure will be followed. Miners seek very low annual TCs if spot stays weak, but smelters resist loss-making deals. The resulting impasse highlights concentrate-tightness amid rising Chinese smelter capacity, underpinning bullish copper sentiment.

title: IC Capitalight Corp.: Capitalight Plans Work at Copper Nickel Project in Quebec
summary: IC Capitalight plans initial onsite geologic work and grab sampling at its Blue Lake/Retty Lake exploration project in Quebec, which previously reported historical grades of ~0.85% Cu and ~0.52% Ni. The company notes no impact-causing exploration work requiring permits is planned, limiting immediate price impact.

title: Congo's $7 bln infrastructure deal with China will depend on copper prices
summary: Congo’s $7 billion infrastructure investment under a revised Sinohydro/China Railway minerals deal is conditioned on copper prices remaining high. The agreement finances roads from Sicomines profits only if copper stays above $8,000/t, and infrastructure funding stops if copper falls to $5,200/t or less.

title: Police seeking public's assistance in copper cable theft
summary: Ontario Provincial Police report theft of substantial copper telephone cable in Englehart/Charlton-Dack, disrupting cellular and internet services. The estimated value and repair cost is about $100,000. Police are investigating and asking for public tips to identify the thieves and recover the stolen copper cable.

title: Argentina Power Supplier Central Puerto Eyes Stake in McEwen's Copper Project
summary: The article headline says Argentina power supplier Central Puerto is looking to take a stake in McEwen’s copper project. If the investment moves forward, it would signal improved backing for copper development, modestly supporting expectations for future supply and potentially providing short-term support for copper prices.

title: Panama to bar First Quantum from mining copper during closure process
summary: Panama said it will bar First Quantum from extracting copper while it manages the closure of the Cobre Panama mine after the contract was voided. Officials are seeking ways to finance an ~$800 million shutdown, with care-and-maintenance planned and key ownership disputes over 121,000 tons of concentrate, awaiting election outcomes.

title: Panama to bar First Quantum from mining copper during shutdown
summary: Panama said it will bar First Quantum from extracting copper while the Cobre Panama mine is shut down after losing its contract. The move follows protests and a nationwide ban on metal mining, with an upcoming plan for care-and-maintenance and uncertainty over who owns 121,000 tons of copper concentrate.

title: Strong copper price reviving Peru's mining mojo, minister says
summary: Peru’s mining minister said strong copper prices are reviving investor interest, citing copper trading at two-year peaks around $10,208/ton and Goldman’s hike to a $12,000 year-end target. The outlook points to scarcity and a larger deficit tied to electrification, supporting renewed confidence and investment.

title: Hopetoun locals staying positive despite hundreds of job losses with closure of First Quantum nickel mine
summary: Hopetoun locals face the closure of First Quantum’s Ravensthorpe nickel operation, with over 300 jobs at risk. The company cites falling commodity prices and high costs for mothballing, while keeping a small care-and-maintenance team for a possible restart only if nickel prices improve.

title: Zimbabwe's Sole Nickel Mine Placed Under Administration
summary: Zimbabwe’s Trojan nickel mine, owned partly by the state via Bindura Nickel Corporation, was placed under administration after an official reconstruction order. Output has already fallen sharply after seismic damage and restart delays tied to low nickel prices and high input costs, raising near-term supply disruption expectations.

title: ARU ASX: This BHP old boy thinks copper and rare earths prices will spike
summary: A former BHP copper boss, now CEO of Arafura Rare Earths, says BHP is making long-horizon moves and draws parallels between copper and rare earths. He specifically expects copper prices to spike, but the piece offers no concrete new data on supply, demand, or inventories.

title: Decarbonization of Aluminum Industries: States Play Pivotal Role, Study Reveals
summary: A study urges Indian states to back aluminum decarbonization by waiving or reducing open access charges for renewable power and prioritizing right-of-way for transmission and evacuation infrastructure. It estimates aluminum plants need ~3.94 GW of round-the-clock renewables and calls for viability gap funding to maintain competitiveness.

title: Public has chance to comment on SC aluminum smelter's permit | Business
summary: State regulators will hold a hearing on May 28 to take public comment on proposed air-permit changes for Century Aluminum’s smelter. The plan would increase sulfur dioxide and particulate matter emissions. EPA required the public process after groups argued it should be treated as a major permit revision under the Clean Air Act.

title: EDITORIAL | Copper theft is a crisis, but army deployment may not be the way to deliver power to the people
summary: The editorial describes Johannesburg Power outages caused by thieves targeting copper cable in tunnels near Smit Street and the M1, stealing 300 metres and triggering substation trips. It frames copper theft as escalating and costly, warning infrastructure destabilisation and urging tougher legislation and policing to curb plunder.

title: Sale of copper-based phone and broadband services to stop in more areas
summary: Openreach says it will halt sales of traditional copper-based phone and broadband services in 84 additional UK exchange areas, affecting 880,000 premises. The company will give providers a year’s notice as full fibre becomes available, encouraging upgrades and reducing ongoing copper network operations.

title: Canadian miner exploring for gold and copper on Bougainville
summary: A Canadian company is running large-scale exploration in Bougainville targeting porphyry copper geology near the closed Panguna mine. Separately, Bougainville’s government ends transitional arrangements for mining without a tenement, making unauthorised mining—including gold and equipment—subject to penalties, potentially affecting small-scale activity.

title: Shanghai copper falls on first trading session after holiday
summary: Shanghai copper fell 0.7% in the first session after a holiday, tracking weaker London prices as the dollar rebounded and demand signals from China’s troubled property sector lacked improvement. Aluminium rose 0.7% and nickel gained 0.4% despite cautious copper supply-cut hopes.

title: Shanghai copper tracks LME lower after holiday break
summary: Shanghai copper fell 0.6% on SHFE, tracking LME losses, as the dollar rebounded and there was no clear demand improvement from China’s troubled property market. Smelter output-cut expectations were tempered by strong long-term smelting profits and limited evidence of large cuts. Aluminium rose and nickel gained.

title: NetNewsLedger - Canada Nickel Continues to Achieve Excellent Drill Results at Reid
summary: Canada Nickel reported new assay results from four drill holes at its Reid nickel property, including the best interval to date (687m of 0.27% nickel). The company highlights long intersections and some higher-grade intervals, with ongoing drilling. The release is exploration-focused and does not affect near-term nickel supply.

title: Indonesia looks to UAE to develop 'green aluminum' industry - Economy
summary: Indonesia is seeking UAE partners to develop downstream “green aluminum,” citing limited domestic smelting capacity and the need for alumina/refining and renewable power. An official said Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) is engaging with PT Inalum and private firms to establish a smelter, possibly in Sumatra or Sulawesi.

title: Hot Chili Arranges A$29.9 Million Funding to Accelerate Costa Fuego Copper Hub, Chile
summary: Hot Chili arranged A$29.9 million (A$24.9m placement plus up to A$5m SPP) to advance Chile’s Costa Fuego copper-gold project, including studies, environmental work, and drilling. The firm positions this as near-term, meaningful copper production potential amid a rising copper price environment, supporting copper sentiment.

title: Nickel prices fluctuated in the morning, and the price difference between nickel beans and nickel sulfate narrowed slightly [SMM nickel spot afternoon comment]
summary: SMM reported May 6 nickel premiums: Jinchuan at 1400-1500 yuan/ton (up 50), while Russian nickel premium remained deeply negative at -700 to -400 yuan/ton (down 50). Nickel bean prices were 139,900-140,700 yuan/ton, down 450 on day. Trading was light and buying restrained; bean–sulfate spread narrowed slightly (~755).

title: After the holiday, the purchasing sentiment of steel mills is relatively light, and the price of ferronickel remains stable under the support of cost [Nickel Pig Iron Daily Review]
summary: SMM reported May 6 high-nickel pig iron (8–12% Ni) at 963.5 yuan/nickel point, flat day-on-day. Indonesian supply improved from a new line, but ore costs are firm and smelter output rises slowly. Domestic smelters run low rates; demand after the holiday is cautious. Cost support keeps prices stable.

title: Commerce Department Announced Affirmative Preliminary Dumping Determinations on Imports of Aluminum Extrusions
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department issued affirmative preliminary anti-dumping determinations on aluminum extrusions from 14 countries and plans to start collecting preliminary duties via cash deposits. Duties may be added alongside existing countervailing duties for several countries. Preliminary results could be revised upward in final determinations later in 2024.

title: First Quantum seeks 'dialogue' with new Panama president over disputed copper mine
summary: First Quantum said it will seek talks with Panama’s newly elected president to resolve the dispute over its Cobre Panama mine, which the prior administration ordered closed after protests over environmental damage. Analysts view the leadership change as positive for the mine’s future, which is supportive for copper supply expectations.

title: Congo's $7 Billion Deal With China Linked to Copper Price Under New Contract
summary: The article headline says Congo has agreed to a $7 billion deal with China, and that it is linked to the copper market under a new contract. Such an agreement typically signals tighter near-term copper supply/demand expectations and can provide upward price pressure as traders price in the added contracting.

title: New Preliminary Dumping Determinations on Aluminum Extrusion Imports
summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce issued preliminary anti-dumping duty determinations for aluminum extrusion imports from 14 countries, with dumping rates ranging widely by country. The government will require Customs to suspend liquidation and collect preliminary duties via cash deposits from mid-May 2024, supporting U.S. aluminum extrusion prices.

title: Areas of Calgary without internet, phone service after attempted copper theft
summary: Calgary telecom services were disrupted after an attempted copper theft that severed telecom infrastructure. Shaw and Rogers reported more frequent vandalism tied to copper theft, citing rising scrap incentives as copper prices increase. Police are investigating, and industry experts call for stronger penalties and security as repairs are costly and slow.

title: Finning reports Q1 2024 results, 10% dividend increase, and significant copper deals awarded in Q2 2024
summary: Finning reported Q1 2024 results and highlighted strategically important equipment wins in Chile, including contracts with multiple copper mines and a large Codelco order. Management also attributes its South America outlook to growing global demand and strengthening copper prices, indicating supportive near-term copper demand expectations.

title: Minmetals solidifies copper supplies with new deal
summary: China Minmetals’ MMG unit has finalized its $1.875 billion acquisition of the Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana. Analysts say the deal strengthens China’s strategic copper supply, diversifies import sources away from Chile and Peru, and supports rising demand from EVs and clean energy. Smelter expansion and record imports reinforce the backdrop.

title: Copper back up above $10,000/T on Fed rate cut hopes
