summary: US producers filed antidumping and countervailing duty petitions against Chinese imports of disposable aluminum containers, pans, and trays, alleging high dumping margins and potential subsidies. The case proceeds via ITC preliminary injury review (June 28, 2024) followed by Commerce preliminary AD/CVD decisions, which could raise import costs.

title: Materials Slide With Copper Futures Amid Deal Speculation - Materials Roundup
summary: Copper prices fell about 5% to $4.87 a pound alongside broader materials weakness. The drop is attributed to uncertainty around the implications of a potential mega-mining merger after Anglo American and others agreed to enter takeover talks with BHP following a rebuffed $50 billion bid.

title: Koryx Copper Announces Fully Committed $2 Million Non-Brokered Private Placement and Share Consolidation
summary: Koryx Copper announced a fully committed CAD$2 million non-brokered private placement to fund its Haib copper project in Namibia and Luanshya West project in Zambia, plus working capital. The company also approved a 5-for-1 share consolidation, pending TSX Venture Exchange approval.

title: Record-high copper prices freeze Chinese spot trading
summary: Record-high copper futures have driven spot buying in China to a halt as buyers step aside. Shanghai grade A cathode premiums have fallen into a wider $5–20/tonne discount, SHFE inventories hit a four-year high, and smelter shipments abroad arrive slowly, pointing to weakening physical demand.

title: Nickel prices surge as political riots erupt in New Caledonia
summary: Nickel prices surged after political riots in French-ruled New Caledonia, where the country is a top global nickel producer. The unrest led to deaths, airport closures, curfews, and troop reinforcements, raising fears of supply and logistics disruption. Nickel jumped about 5% then added further gains to a multi-month high.

title: MACAU DAILY TIMES 澳門每日時報Violent unrest in French Pacific territory impacting global nickel prices
summary: Violent unrest in France’s Pacific territory of New Caledonia has followed constitutional voting changes and a 12-day state of emergency. New Caledonia supplies roughly 20–30% of world nickel reserves and most local exports, raising fears of disrupted production. The article says global nickel prices have surged.

title: Copper slips on hawkish Fed minutes, weak demand
summary: Copper prices fell after hawkish Fed minutes supported a firmer U.S. dollar, making dollar-priced commodities more expensive. The drop was reinforced by weakening Chinese demand as earlier price gains reduced end-user consumption and lifted inventories. LME and SHFE aluminium and nickel also declined, reflecting broad risk-off pressure.

title: What New Caledonia riots mean for the nickel industry - Markets
summary: Riots in New Caledonia have halted nickel mining operations and damaged/limited processing at SLN, reducing output to minimum levels. As New Caledonia is a major nickel supplier, analysts say disrupted production could erode a global surplus and supported a rally in LME nickel prices, though prices later eased.

title: Troubled Peru Copper Mine Starts Expansion Work in Supply Boost
summary: The report says a troubled copper mine in Peru has begun expansion work aimed at boosting supply. The market impact comes from expectations of higher copper availability, which can pressure short-term copper prices as traders adjust forecasts for future output.

title: Chinese Factories Recoil From Paying Record Copper Prices
summary: The article suggests Chinese factories are recoiling from paying record-high copper prices. That behavior points to reduced copper buying or slower procurement, which can weaken near-term demand expectations and add downside pressure to copper prices over the next days to a few weeks.

title: Washington state is giving $5 million to a massive aluminum production plant in Spokane. Why?
summary: Washington will provide nearly $5 million to Kaiser Aluminum’s Spokane-area plant to replace two aging steam boilers under the state’s Climate Commitment Act. The funding offsets emissions-reduction costs and requires Kaiser to match the amount. The retrofit is expected to cut the plant’s annual greenhouse gases by about 13,000 metric tons.

title: Copper Extends Decline as Record Prices Deter Buyers in China
summary: Copper prices extended their decline as record-high prices discouraged buyers in China. The report links the latest weakness to softer purchasing activity from Chinese demand, suggesting near-term demand restraint and reinforcing bearish sentiment for copper over the coming days.

title: Mining and Metallurgical Norilsk Nickel : Nornickel's Board of Directors recommends not to pay dividends for FY 2023 to shareholders
summary: Nornickel’s board recommends not paying dividends for FY2023, citing sanctions and geopolitical challenges that hit revenue and EBITDA and reduced free cash flow. The company already paid interim dividends in 9M 2023 and says it will not increase debt for dividends. Nornickel is a major nickel and copper producer.

title: Rio Tinto Faces Lawsuit Over Panguna Copper Mine in Bougainville
summary: Rio Tinto is facing legal action over the Panguna copper mine in Bougainville. The dispute could create uncertainty around mine operations and potential timelines, reducing visibility on copper supply. In the first days to weeks, this type of risk can pressure copper prices as traders price in disruption odds.

title: Analysis-How can Milei unlock Argentina's copper riches? Fix the economy
summary: Reuters reports Argentina’s major copper projects in the Andean north are stalled by capital controls, very high inflation and taxes, despite record copper prices and investor interest. President Milei’s reform bill—if passed—may ease currency access and taxes, helping advanced projects like Josemaria and Taca Taca move toward construction in coming months.

title: GPAC concludes acquisition of Tinga Valley Copper & Gold
summary: Great Pacific Gold completed its acquisition of the Tinga Valley copper-gold project in Papua New Guinea. The deal adds a drill-ready copper porphyry and skarn target portfolio, with exploration planned to begin in 2024. While copper is implicated, there is no immediate supply impact expected in the near term.

title: PAN GLOBAL ACCELERATES COPPER EXPLORATION WITH ADDITIONAL DRILL RIG AT THE ESCACENA PROJECT, SOUTHERN SPAIN
summary: Pan Global Resources announced it is adding a second drill rig to expand the 2024 drilling program at its Escacena copper-tin-silver project in southern Spain. Management links the step-up to positive results and “exceptionally strong” copper market conditions, aiming to accelerate hole drilling as data remains pending.

title: Copper dips for third straight day on profit-taking, weak demand
summary: Copper on the LME fell for a third straight session due to profit-taking and consumers shunning near-record prices. It notes elevated China inventories and a refined market surplus in March. The piece also shows aluminium and nickel easing on the session, alongside caution ahead of U.S. jobs data.

title: Indonesia's nickel mining quotas fall short of demand
summary: Indonesia approved 204 nickel RKAB work plans totaling 220.7mn t, but participants expect production approvals may not meet 2024 ore demand of about 220mn t. Supply concerns include lower approval rates outside Morowali and New Caledonia unrest disrupting nickel value-chain operations and transportation. Nickel prices have risen on tighter availability.

title: Copper set for a mini shake out - Fastmarkets
summary: Fastmarkets’ analyst says LME copper’s rally is still supported by bullish positioning (rising CFTC net longs and consecutive fund buying) and a weekly close above $10,000/t. However, momentum looks “frothy,” so a short two-to-four-week technical pullback is expected before dip-buying resumes in June and highs are retested.

title: Profit Inverted Salt Factory's Positive Price Sentiment Still Strong [SMM Nickel Sulfate Daily Review]
summary: May 23 SMM battery-grade nickel sulfate averaged higher (index 32,389 yuan/ton). The report attributes the rebound to limited nickel-salt supply, low finished-product inventories, and higher raw-material costs from elevated nickel prices. Downstream buying continued despite weaker demand due to replenishment needs and warehouse-building constraints.

title: In the morning, nickel prices plummeted significantly, and the price difference between nickel beans and nickel salts narrowed. [SMM Nickel Spot Review]
summary: SMM’s May 23 nickel spot review says prices fell sharply: nickel beans dropped to 149,000–149,800 yuan/ton (down 5,050 yuan/ton). Nickel sulfate traded about 2,582 yuan/ton below beans, narrowing the beans–sulfate spread. Jinchuan and Russian premiums also shifted, reflecting bearish market sentiment.

title: High nickel pig iron prices fluctuate upwards, stainless steel is weak, steel mills are on the lookout for procurement [Daily Review of Nickel Pig Iron]
summary: SMM reports that SMM 8–12% high-nickel pig iron averaged 978.5 yuan per nickel point, up slightly. Higher Indonesian ore approvals vs March are still far below demand; Indonesian smelter output remains weak, and China supply is low. Weak stainless steel demand limits acceptance, but cost-driven tight circulation supports a stable-to-slightly-firm near-term outlook.

title: First Quantum seeks to expedite copper projects in Peru
summary: First Quantum Minerals said it is pushing to accelerate its La Granja and Haquira copper projects in Peru after a Panama setback, including the annulment of its Cobre Panama mining contract. The move is aimed at speeding development, but no construction timelines were provided.

title: Faraday Copper to raise $15m in bought deal financing
summary: Canadian explorer Faraday Copper will raise C$20m (and potentially ~C$3m more via an over-allotment option) through a bought deal financing. Proceeds will fund exploration and development of the Copper Creek porphyry copper project in Arizona. The offering closes around May 30, subject to approvals.

title: 'Party over' for copper, prices fall notably following Monday's record high
summary: Copper prices dropped notably after Monday’s record high, falling to around $10,210/tonne and down about 8% on the week. Traders cited hedge-fund positioning and profit-taking in a risk-off environment, suggesting the prior spike was unsustainable. Copper fundamentals were noted as still supported by tight concentrate supplies and demand.

title: Administration Releases Details on Planned Increases to Section 301 Duties on Imports of Steel, Aluminum, Electric Vehicles, Semiconductors, Solar Cells, and Other Products from China | Wiley Rein LLP
summary: The USTR released a Federal Register notice outlining higher Section 301 tariffs on $18 billion of China-origin imports, with increases effective Aug. 1, 2024 (and later dates for 2025/2026). The targeted product list includes aluminum, and the notice also describes exclusion and comment processes.

title: OCEANIA Macron in rioting New Caledonia, to talk with local leaders and nickel companies
summary: French President Macron visited Nouméa amid clashes between separatists and loyalists in New Caledonia, hinting the state of emergency could be lifted. The unrest is tied to New Caledonia’s nickel-dependent economy and an industry downturn, with stalled rescue talks. Disruption risks likely weigh on nickel prices soon.

title: Rio Tinto Limited and Bougainville Copper Limited facing multi-billion dollar class action lawsuit
summary: Residents of Bougainville have filed a multi-billion class action against Rio Tinto and Bougainville Copper over alleged historical mismanagement of the Panguna copper mine, citing environmental and social harm. The claim seeks compensation, but the article provides no evidence of immediate mine output disruption, limiting near-term copper price effects.

title: Copper treads water as investors reassess recent rally
summary: Copper prices were nearly unchanged as investors reassessed the rally that recently pushed LME prices to record highs, supported by fund buying and a U.S. Comex short squeeze but offset by dampened Chinese physical demand. LME aluminium and nickel fell slightly, indicating limited immediate directional impact beyond copper’s cooling momentum.

title: Talon mining development company begins western U.P exploration for nickel
summary: Talon Mining begins nickel exploration in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula, backed by about $20 million in U.S. federal funding. The company acquired a large land package and cites prior findings of up to 7.4% nickel, aiming to drill once targets are identified. It frames results for domestic EV-related supply chains.

title: East Las Vegas neighborhood plagued by copper theft starts to see relief after repairs, theft prevention
summary: East Las Vegas streetlights are being repaired after copper wire thefts left parts of Lamb Road and side streets dark. Clark County says crews have installed anti-theft copper wiring caps and plans to hire a contractor to replace ~42,000 feet of wiring. Over 500,000 feet have been stolen since 2022.

title: Battle for Anglo's copper assets tests BHP's resolve as deadline looms
summary: Reuters reports BHP is racing to secure Anglo American’s copper assets in Chile and Peru, with Anglo investors seeking higher cash/price or a simpler deal structure. The copper mines targeted are expected to produce ~532,000 tons this year, but the dispute is about valuation and execution details, not immediate output changes.

title: India's Hindalco beats Q4 profit view as lower costs outpace weak aluminium prices
summary: Hindalco Industries reported Q4 profit above analyst expectations, saying lower costs outweighed weak aluminium prices. The better earnings from the major India producer of both aluminium and copper supports margin resilience sentiment. The news may help underpin near-term expectations for aluminium pricing and, to a lesser extent, copper demand and production outlook.

title: Hindalco beats Q4 profit view as lower costs outpace weak aluminium prices
summary: Hindalco reported Q4 profit above expectations, saying lower costs helped offset weak aluminium prices. The result suggests current aluminium pricing remains soft, but the article is primarily about company earnings rather than a direct market shock. Copper is mentioned only as part of the producer mix, with no specific copper impact.

title: Copper slips on interest rate worries, lacklustre demand in China
summary: Copper prices edged lower as investors scaled back on interest-rate worries and weak physical demand in China. Premiums for importing copper into China shifted to a discount since mid-May, reflecting high-price damping of demand. The move followed prior rally strength driven more by financial selling than physical buying.

title: Pierre Andurand Sees Copper Hitting a Record-High $40,000 in Four Years
summary: Pierre Andurand says copper could reach $40,000/ton over the next four years due to electrification, renewables, defense demand, and AI data centers, though supply response may take longer. The article notes copper hit record highs, then saw profit-taking and skepticism from strategists over short-term fundamentals.

title: Macron Caves To Rioters, Postpones Voting Reform In Nickel-Rich New Caledonia
summary: Macron postponed voting reform in New Caledonia after yielding to rioters, in a territory described as nickel-rich. The unrest could disrupt local mining or logistics feeding nickel production, tightening near-term supply expectations. That scenario is generally supportive for nickel prices over the next days to four weeks.

title: Copper Price Records Will Extend Another 288% Amid Supply Issues: Trader
summary: Trader Pierre Andurand says copper’s supply-demand gap is worsening as mining production lags, inventories run tight, and new mine development takes years. With demand rising from electrification, renewables, military use and data centers, he expects copper to extend record highs and potentially reach far higher levels over time.

title: Exclusive-Grupo Mexico's Asarco to reopen U.S. copper smelter amid surging prices
summary: Asarco, controlled by Grupo Mexico, plans to restart its Hayden U.S. copper smelter in Arizona and the Amarillo refinery amid record copper prices. Negotiations with unions and permit processes are underway. Reopening would add domestic smelting/cathode supply, easing U.S. smelting constraints.

title: SMM Analysis: Tight alumina supply has significantly pushed global alumina spot prices up
summary: SMM says China’s alumina spot prices jumped on tight bauxite availability and rising refinery utilisation constraints. Demand rose as Yunnan restart of aluminium smelting increased alumina needs. Globally, outages at Rio Tinto/NALCO/Alcoa tightened supplies, pushing Western Australia FOB alumina higher and curtailing China imports.

title: Hindalco predicts Robust Copper, Aluminium demand in FY25 in India
summary: Hindalco said India’s copper and aluminium demand should remain robust in FY25, citing rising electrification-led demand. It reported a 15% YoY increase in domestic refined copper demand in the latest quarter and higher copper and aluminium revenues/EBITDA, alongside favourable input costs, boosting sentiment toward both metals.

title: Robert Wares catches a copper wave at Osisko Metals
summary: Osisko Metals CEO Robert Wares continued buying shares. The company’s recent rally is attributed to a strengthening copper price and new project news: a May 6 updated mineral resource estimate for its Gaspé Copper Project’s Copper Mountain Deposit. The insider buying is presented as supportive sentiment.

title: Hindalco predicts Robust Copper, Aluminium demand in FY25 in India
summary: Hindalco’s management said Indian demand for refined copper rose 15% year-on-year to 225 KT in the latest quarter, helped by household electrification and other industrial uses. It also reported improved aluminium upstream revenue and EBITDA, expecting robust copper and aluminium demand in FY25.

title: Cameroon's Aluminum Export Revenues Rise 11% in 2023 - Business in Cameroon
summary: Cameroon’s aluminum export revenues rose 11% to CFA54.2 billion in 2023, but export tonnage stayed almost unchanged at about 43.9k tons. The improvement is attributed to higher revenues for Alucam, despite ongoing financial and cash-flow challenges after Rio Tinto exited and the firm became state-owned.

title: The 6 Best Copper Stocks to Own Now
summary: The piece promotes copper exposure, citing EV electrification as a major copper-consumption driver and forecasting higher electricity demand from emerging economies plus AI/data centers. It highlights copper’s recent record high and anticipates potential upside. It discusses copper-miner stocks, but the core market claim is increasing copper demand.

title: A bet on copper has paid off. But what can investors expect now that prices are soaring?
summary: Copper futures surged to record highs above $5/lb in mid-May and eased to about $4.77, still up strongly in 2024. The rally is attributed to better-than-expected global growth, China fiscal stimulus, and slow supply additions amid regulatory and cost hurdles, though the piece warns copper may be overextended.

title: Materials Decline as Copper Slide Continues - Materials Roundup
summary: Metals producers fell as copper’s decline persisted. Analysts attributed the weakness to softer Chinese demand, which outweighed improved copper sales in other markets and reduced optimism tied to electrification demand. The piece frames ongoing downside sentiment for copper and related materials, with no clear catalyst for nickel or aluminium.

title: Copper's boom story has some truth — and lots of hogwash
summary: Bloomberg argues copper’s recent LME rally above $11,000/t is largely financial momentum rather than fundamentals. It cites low inventories and mining supply downgrades supporting prices, but also points to weak Chinese physical demand and depressed premiums, questioning the bullish “copper is the new oil” narrative.

title: How is the violent unrest in New Caledonia impacting nickel prices?
summary: Violent unrest in New Caledonia, a major source of global nickel, has raised fears of supply disruptions. The article reports nickel prices surging on the LME (e.g., above $20,000/ton) after the violence began, alongside broader concerns about critical-material shortages tied to EV demand.

title: A Looming Copper Bottleneck Could Derail the Energy Transition
summary: A report warns copper supply may soon lag rapidly rising demand from clean-energy technologies like EVs, solar, offshore wind, and grid electrification. It highlights the long permitting timeline and insufficient new mine additions, projecting a bottleneck risk. The article links this to record copper prices on the London Metal Exchange.

title: Venus Metals Corporation Limited Copper Hills Highly Prospective Circular Magnetic Targets
summary: Venus Metals announced tenement E45-6437 (Copper Hills) granted in the Paterson Orogen and completion of 3D magnetic modelling targeting potential intrusive sources for magmatic/hydrothermal Cu-Au/Mo mineralisation. Historical rock chip assays reported very high copper grades, and drilling is planned, but no production changes are stated.

title: Shanghai aluminium rise on alumina price surge, firm demand
summary: Shanghai aluminium futures rose on Monday, driven by an 8.3% weekly rally in SHFE alumina amid limited supply and improving demand expectations. Analysts also cited firm consumption growth tied to solar and electric vehicles. July aluminium gained 0.4% to 20,960 yuan/ton.

title: Indonesia's unnecessary bid for nickel cartel crumbles - Academia
summary: The piece says Indonesia is trying to form a nickel-producing countries alliance akin to OPEC to influence global nickel supply and prices. Despite Indonesia’s large nickel reserves and production, approached countries have shown reluctance and the proposal’s value proposition remains unclear, reducing expectations for any immediate market effect.

title: King River bumps up cash balance for NT copper-gold push
summary: King River Resources received a ~$361,000 R&D tax rebate, boosting cash to fund a delayed reverse-circulation drill program at its Tennant Creek East copper-gold project in Australia’s Northern Territory. The company plans multiple holes over several prospects to test geochemical anomalies and potentially expand drilling based on results.

title: Shanghai aluminium rises on alumina price surge, firm demand
summary: Shanghai aluminium futures rose Monday, supported by a sharp rally in alumina prices (a key input), robust demand, and domestic tightness due to overseas supply disruptions, including Rio Tinto force majeure on Queensland alumina exports. Producers increased output, while analysts cited strong consumption from solar and electric vehicles.

title: Altiplano Reports Assay Results From its Santa Beatriz Copper-Gold-Iron Project of up to 2.45 m at 3.65 %Cu; 0.29 g/t Au; and 26.97 %Fe
summary: Altiplano reported underground and surface assay results from its Santa Beatriz copper-gold-iron project, highlighting 2.45 m at 3.65% Cu (with Au and Fe). The company plans further bulk sampling, geophysics, and drilling to support a development decision and potential incremental Cu-Au feed for the El Peñón mill.

title: BEV Initiative: the DRC government and Buenassa company to set up a cobalt and copper refinery in Lualaba | United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
summary: The DRC government, via its Industry Promotion Funds, granted US$3.5 million to Buenassa to develop a hydro-metallurgical copper and cobalt refinery in Lualaba. The project targets production of 30,000 tonnes of copper cathodes annually. This indicates advancing local copper refining capacity under the BEV/battery value-chain initiative.

title: Strength in Gold and Copper Continues – But for How Long? | Live Wire
summary: The piece says copper prices are stabilizing after easing from recent highs, with one-month futures up slightly. It attributes May’s surge to speculative trading and warns physical demand may not confirm tightness. China’s forthcoming stimulus financing and export effects are highlighted as the key near-term swing factor.

title: Study: The Amount of Copper Needed for EVs Is 'Impossible for Mining Companies to Produce'
summary: A University of Michigan study says copper production cannot keep pace with EV and renewable grid electrification needs, estimating EVs and grid upgrades require far more copper per vehicle. It projects copper demand would exceed current mine capacity, implying new mines must expand output significantly.

title: ALEX BRUMMER: Copper displaces diamonds as Anglo American puts De Beers up for sale
summary: Anglo American’s planned sale of De Beers is framed as being driven by a push into copper, linked to BNP’s bids for copper projects in Chile and Peru. The piece also notes copper has surged about 20% this year to a record ~$11,000/tonne, reinforcing bullish market sentiment for copper.

title: Sask RCMP investigate copper thefts from rural worksites, transformers
summary: Saskatchewan RCMP is investigating multiple copper thefts from rural worksites and electrical transformers. Authorities say thieves stole copper lines and wiring, damaging transformers and potentially causing outages. Investigations span February to May. RCMP highlights safety risks and asks the public to report suspicious activity, but no market-wide supply impact is cited.

title: Sask. RCMP investigate copper thefts from rural work sites and transformers
summary: RCMP are investigating a series of copper thefts from rural work sites and transformers in northwest Saskatchewan, including instances where transformers were opened and copper wiring removed. SaskPower says tampering is dangerous and can cause outages. The reports list multiple locations and dates over several months.

title: Gold, silver, copper rally has just taken a breather — new highs not far off
summary: Gold and silver narratives are included, but copper receives direct coverage: prices hit an all-time high and are still supported by supply tightness. The article cites reduced copper surplus forecasts by the ICSG on lower production, plus mine-related output disruptions and planned cuts, supporting bullish expectations.

title: Gladiator Metals Corp.: Gladiator Extends Cowley Park Geological Model to Include Additional High-Grade Copper Mineralization
summary: Gladiator Metals reports assay results from previously unassayed historic drill core at the Cowley Park prospect, extending and confirming high-grade copper skarn continuity (notably several meters grading around ~1–2% Cu) with mineralization open under cover and at depth. It does not indicate imminent production changes impacting copper markets immediately.

title: European Union critical minerals deal a boost for Australian 'green premium' nickel, says Trade Minister Don Farrell and Resources Minister Madeleine King
summary: Australia and the EU signed a critical minerals memorandum intended to smooth investment in new projects and build momentum for a “green premium” market. The article specifically cites nickel among targeted resources, which should support expectations for nickel demand and potentially tighten supply outlooks over coming weeks.

title: Copper climbs, but high China stocks suggest ample supplies
summary: Copper prices climbed 1.1% on Tuesday, supported by expectations of interest rate cuts, a weaker U.S. dollar and strong China activity data. Traders also cite robust industrial profits and demand themes (EVs, automation, AI). However, elevated China inventories and high refined output suggest ample supplies.

title: Intrepid Metals Completes Initial Drill Program at Its Corral Copper Property in Arizona
summary: Intrepid Metals said it completed an initial drilling program at its Corral Copper property in Arizona, reporting assay highlights with multiple long copper intervals. Results for eight remaining holes are expected soon, but the release is an exploration update without any production or supply commitments, limiting direct near-term price impact.

title: Gold Royalty : Announces Agreement to Acquire Vares Copper Stream - Form 6-K
summary: Gold Royalty said it will acquire a copper stream on the Vares Silver Project (Rupice deposit) for $50m, with ongoing payments linked to 30% of the LME spot copper price (effective payable copper fixed at 24.5%). It also cites production guidance for 2024–2026 but no immediate supply disruption.

title: Gold Royalty Announces Agreement to Acquire Vares Copper Stream
summary: Gold Royalty agreed to acquire a copper stream on the Vares (Rupice) silver project, covering 100% of copper production in the mining area. Stream payments are linked to 30% of the LME spot copper price with fixed payable copper at 24.5%, with first production in 2024 and commercial in 4Q24.

title: Canadian Copper Receives New Brunswick Ministerial Approval for Murray Brook Title Transfer
summary: Canadian Copper Inc. said New Brunswick approved the transfer of the Murray Brook mining lease and title. The company frames the event as supporting a potential Caribou restart by providing a nearby ore resource. The release cites spot pricing used in its resource valuation, but no immediate production impact is stated.

title: Fathom Nickel Inc.: Fathom Continues to Intersect High-Grade Mineralization and Expand the Historic Gochager Lake Deposit in All Directions
summary: Fathom Nickel reported new drill results from the Gochager Lake project, including multiple high-grade nickel intercepts with associated copper and cobalt, plus strong BHEM conductor evidence suggesting expansion to depth and along strike. The update is exploration-focused and does not indicate imminent production changes for nickel or copper supply.

title: Electric Royalties Ltd.: Electric Royalties Provides Seven Updates on Its Lithium, Graphite, Copper, Nickel, and Tin Royalties
summary: Electric Royalties reports updates across its royalty portfolio, including Zonia copper-oxide progress toward a feasibility study and Kenbridge nickel project baseline studies and permitting steps. While these developments may support longer-run supply expectations, the article does not indicate near-term production changes, implying minimal immediate impact on copper and nickel prices.

title: Northstar Signs Additional Boston Creek Copper Property Letter of Intent
summary: Northstar Gold signed an LOI to consolidate additional adjacent properties along the Boston Creek Copper Trend, targeting near-surface VMS copper conductors identified by EM surveys. The release outlines drill-test plans and summarizes historical copper grades, but no production or supply-impact decisions are announced.

title: Interview with Paul Lusty, head of battery raw materials at Fastmarkets | Fast Forward podcast episode 2 transcript
summary: The Fastmarkets podcast interview focuses on battery raw materials, including nickel. It explains how Indonesian nickel matte can feed nickel sulfate for China’s battery sector and notes that mixed hydroxide precipitate (MHP) production expansions depend on whether nickel economics remain viable. The piece links supply chains to sentiment but gives no definitive short-term nickel price direction.

title: New Caledonia Unrest Pushes Nickel Sector Deeper Into Crisis
summary: Unrest in New Caledonia since mid-May has halted nickel mining and processing, stopping operations at SLN and Prony, idling Koniambo, and depleting ore reserves. Fuel blockages and possible shipping risk premiums further threaten supply. Given New Caledonia’s large global reserve share, the disruption should support higher nickel prices.

title: EV transition targets mean huge ramp-up in copper mining needed - IEF
summary: The IEF says 100% EV adoption by 2035 would require an unprecedented acceleration in copper mining. It notes long mine lead times, permitting delays, and limited mine additions, warning EV battery demand could substantially raise copper prices. It cites a lack of new projects in North America as evidence of constrained supply.

title: Al Hadeetha Resources exports first copper concentrate
summary: Al Hadeetha Resources in Oman has announced the first export of copper concentrate from its Al Washihi–Al Majaza project. The company highlights new mining and processing facilities and government support. The start of exports implies incremental copper supply entering trade, which can modestly lift near-term copper price expectations.

title: Gold Royalty Falls 13% on Equity Offering, Copper-Focused Transaction for Vares Project
summary: Gold Royalty shares fell after announcing a bought deal equity offering and a $50 million copper-related transaction for the Vares silver project in Bosnia. The company says the deal will help it benefit from record copper prices, operated by a unit of Adriatic Metals. The headline suggests mostly corporate financing effects, not near-term copper fundamentals.

title: What's Behind the Recent Rally in Copper Prices?
summary: Copper prices surged above $11,000/ton to a record high, breaking a key psychological level. The article links the rally to supply concerns after the Cobre Panama mine closure, stronger Chinese demand expectations, and macro/positioning effects including US bond yield correlations and short-seller squeezes in New York.

title: US Copper Corp. Commences Discussions with Strategic Partners for Its Moonlight-Superior Project, One of the Most Advanced and Largest Undeveloped Copper Projects in the USA
summary: US Copper says it has started discussions with strategic partners to advance its Moonlight-Superior copper project in California toward a definitive feasibility study and development. The company links partner interest to copper prices moving above $10,000/t and to U.S. policies supporting domestic critical-metal supply, reinforcing bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Podcast: 'Copper famine', green metals and misaligned incentives, ft Clareo's Peter Bryant
summary: The podcast features commentary on mining supply shortfalls and frames concerns as a potential “copper famine,” suggesting future tightness in copper availability. It also discusses BHP’s bid for Anglo American and how “green metals” and circular-economy approaches could affect supply constraints, potentially supporting copper price expectations.

title: Not enough copper production to meet Biden's EV policy goals, study finds
summary: A University of Michigan study says existing copper mine production (~20 million tons/year) cannot be doubled to meet current EV policy goals (~40 million tons/year). More mines would be needed, taking decades. The article links slow EV charging progress to potential copper supply constraints, implying tighter copper markets ahead.

title: Decade Resources : ANNOUNCES DISCOVERY OF 3 NEW RED BED COPPER SHOWINGS, TERRACE BC.
summary: Decade Resources announced new red-bed copper showings at its Copper River project in Terrace, B.C., with copper-silver assays up to about 1.26% Cu and associated silver values. The company collected 20 grab samples and plans to mobilize a drill as snowmelt runoff allows further testing.

title: We're Not Mining Enough Copper to Meet Upcoming EV Projections: Report
summary: A report says copper mining is not sufficient for EV electrification goals, citing that EVs use far more copper than gasoline vehicles and that many new deposits and permitting approvals have lagged. It estimates large additional mining and new mines are needed, implying tighter copper availability and supportive sentiment for copper.

title: Public meeting to be held on Century Aluminum's air permits
summary: South Carolina DHEC held a public meeting on Century Aluminum’s two air permits, with comments open until June 3. The process involves re-notification after EPA findings on prior permit changes (PM and SO2) and ongoing alumina dust investigations, while the SO2 limit is stated as unchanged.

title: B.C. miners serve strike notice at Gibraltar copper pit in central Interior
summary: Unifor Local 3018 has issued strike notice for workers at Taseko’s Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia if a new contract is not reached by May 31. The union says bargaining has stalled. Given the mine’s size, the risk of disruption could pressure near-term copper supply expectations downward.

title: B.C. miners serve strike notice at Gibraltar copper pit in Interior
summary: Unifor has served strike notice for workers at Taseko’s Gibraltar copper mine in central British Columbia if a new contract isn’t reached by Friday. The collective agreement expires May 31, with 98% voting for strike authorization. Taseko says talks are ongoing, aiming for a fair deal.

title: B.C. miners serve strike notice at Gibraltar copper pit in central Interior | iNFOnews
summary: A union representing 550 workers at Taseko’s Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia served strike notice, saying workers may strike if a new contract is not reached by Friday. The collective agreement expires May 31. The mine is described as Canada’s second-largest open-pit copper mine, raising near-term supply risk.

title: Global aluminium producer seeks Q3 premiums of $175/T -sources
summary: A global aluminium producer is seeking Q3 premium offers of $175/ton for July-September primary aluminium shipments to Japanese buyers, up about 18%-21% from the prior quarter. Japan’s quarterly premium level benchmarks the region versus the LME cash price, suggesting tighter near-term conditions.

title: Copper climbs on China outlook; firm dollar, rising stocks cap gains
summary: Copper prices rose as expectations of stronger Chinese demand improved, supported by new property-sector measures and an IMF upgrade to China’s growth outlook. Gains were capped by a steady/firm U.S. dollar and higher Chinese inventories. Aluminium and nickel also ticked up on the broader metals sentiment.

title: Proposed ordinance seeks to curb sales of illegal copper across the Las Vegas Valley
summary: Clark County in Nevada proposes an ordinance to restrict purchases and sales of illegal copper at junk yards and recycling plants. The goal is to deter copper-wire theft from street lights and utilities by tightening seller verification, records, and transaction safeguards. Officials cite 500,000 feet stolen since 2022.

title: Camino Minerals Corp.: Camino to Commence the Inaugural Drilling Program at Maria Cecilia Porphyry with 0.7% Oxidized Copper Identified at Surface
summary: Camino Minerals will begin its inaugural drilling program at the Maria Cecilia copper porphyry project in Peru on June 1, targeting potential extensions of oxidized copper observed at surface (up to 0.7% Cu) and assessing whether it continues to primary sulphides at depth. Work is exploration-focused and not tied to production.

title: Mining licence issued for Luansobe Copper Project | Company Announcement
summary: Galileo Resources said Zambia has issued a 10-year small-scale mining licence for its 75%-owned Luansobe copper project in the Copperbelt. The licence covers areas with previously reported inferred copper resources and supports further development steps, potentially improving expectations for future copper supply.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Inc.: Ivanhoe Electric Announces Selection of Fluor Enterprises Inc. as the Principal Lead for the Santa Cruz Copper Project Preliminary Feasibility Study
summary: Ivanhoe Electric reported substantially completed infill drilling at its Santa Cruz copper project, including additional high-grade intercepts from the Verde Domain and other areas. The company selected Fluor and other engineering consultants to lead workstreams for the project’s preliminary feasibility study, which remains on track for completion by end-Q2 2025.

title: Transition Metals Corp.: Transition Metals Validates Copper Porphyry Potential at Pike Warden Project, Yukon
summary: Transition Metals Corp. reports petrographic and trace-element studies supporting epithermal-to-porphyry style alteration at its Pike Warden project in Yukon, including a referenced sample returning 2.3% Cu. The company plans geophysics and a summer field program. It is an exploration update without production or supply effects.

title: Copper miners consider counterparty risks selling into 2025 and beyond
summary: Fastmarkets sources say copper miners and traders are negotiating 2025-2027 concentrate contracts with specific TC/RC terms and factoring in counterparty reliability. Traders worry about margin and market-tightness changes (e.g., potential reopenings or smelter curtailments and contango narrowing). Reliance-based bids could limit aggressiveness if risk rises.

title: NetNewsLedger - SPC Nickel Reports High-Grade Channel Sampling Results at the West Graham Project, Including 0.94% Ni and 0.44% Cu over 17.0 metres
summary: SPC Nickel reported high-grade channel sampling from its West Graham Ni-Cu project in Sudbury, including results of 0.94% Ni and 0.44% Cu over 17 metres and 0.62% Ni and 0.31% Cu over 38 metres. The company says results correlate with prior drilling and support development potential, but no immediate production impact is stated.

title: Nine Mile Metals Ltd.: Nine Mile Metals Announces Drill Hole WD-24-03 Certified Assay Results of 1.58% Copper Equivalent (Cu-Eq) over 32.10m Including 2.60% Cu-Eq over 16.15m and 3.61% Cu-Eq over 8.15m
summary: Nine Mile Metals reported certified assays from drill hole WD-24-03 at its The Wedge VMS target in New Brunswick, including copper values of 0.60% Cu over 32.10m and a higher-grade zone. The company highlights copper-led, strong widths and uses May 13 metal prices to calculate copper-equivalent.

title: Aluminium hits almost two-year high as funds switch from copper
summary: Aluminium prices rose to a nearly two-year high on the LME as funds reportedly rotated from copper into aluminium. The move was supported by supply tightness, including alumina shortages from lower Chinese output and Australian export disruptions, alongside stronger physical demand shown by higher Japanese premiums for upcoming quarters.

title: Copper Lake Resources Ltd. Reports Results of Drilling at Marshall Lake Copper-Zinc-Silver VMS Property
summary: Copper Lake Resources reported winter drilling results from its Marshall Lake copper-zinc-silver VMS property in Ontario, highlighting high-grade copper and zinc intercepts and a persistent EM conductor with the deposit remaining open at depth. The update supports potential resource expansion but does not indicate near-term production.

title: Aluminium hits almost two-year high as funds switch from copper
summary: Aluminium prices rose to a nearly two-year high on LME, driven by supply tightness and funds switching from copper. Reuters cites tighter alumina availability from weaker China output and Australian export disruptions, alongside higher Japanese booking premiums, indicating firmer physical demand and continued fund inflows.

title: SGS : Working with The Metals Company to Produce High Purity Nickel Sulfate from Deep-Sea Minerals
summary: SGS says it was contracted by The Metals Company to test and optimize onshore processing flowsheets producing high-purity nickel sulfate from seafloor polymetallic nodules. Bench-scale work also targets cobalt sulfate and mentions copper cathode production from nickel matte, supporting future supply expectations for nickel battery chemicals.

title: LME brand approval cements Indonesian nickel ascendancy: Andy Home
summary: LME approved the first Indonesian refined-nickel brand (“DX-zwdx”) for delivery, adding a new source of Class I nickel. With Russia’s Norilsk constrained by sanctions and LME stocks rising to a two-year high, the shift toward Indonesian/Chinese deliverable supply is likely to weigh on nickel prices.

title: Abundant Clean Energy, New Tech Investment Key to Aluminum
summary: A new Aluminum Association/ICF roadmap discusses how North American aluminum can cut production emissions via low-carbon primary tech, electrification and clean power, and expanded recycling, enabled by policy such as the Inflation Reduction Act. It projects large long-term reductions and rising output demand but no immediate aluminum supply shock.

title: State lawmakers review $50M proposal to back Copperwood mine project
summary: State lawmakers reviewed a $50 million proposal to support Highland Copper’s Copperwood mine project in Gogebic County, including infrastructure upgrades and permitting readiness. Officials discussed maintaining supply to U.S. and Michigan industry. Votes are scheduled next week, with sponsors confident funding will be approved.

title: Shanghai aluminium climbs to 2-year high on strong fundamentals
summary: Shanghai aluminium jumped about 3% to a two-year high, with LME aluminium also near multi-year peaks. The report attributes the rally to strong China demand for aluminium used in solar and EVs, alumina supply disruptions, and higher premiums for primary metal shipments, supporting immediate bullish price pressure.

title: BHP : Nickel West Mt Keith Satellite Project Statement 1087 Compliance Assessment Report
summary: BHP published its Statement 1087 compliance assessment report for the Mt Keith Satellite Project, covering 28 Dec 2020 to 31 Dec 2021. The report states BHP Nickel West was compliant with all conditions, describing ongoing satellite mining operations as an extension to the Mt Keith Nickel Mine. No near-term operational disruption is indicated.

title: Aluminum Hits Two-Year High as China Capacity Limits Help Rally
summary: Aluminium is reported to be at a two-year high as China enforces or tightens capacity limits. The headline suggests these restrictions reduce nearby supply, lifting market expectations and supporting aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Shanghai aluminium at 2-year high; other base metals slump on firmer dollar
summary: Shanghai aluminium hit a two-year high on early trade, supported by supply constraints linked to western sanctions on Russian metals, tight availability (including higher premiums to Japan), and robust demand from solar and EV sectors. Meanwhile, copper and nickel slipped as a firmer U.S. dollar weighed on base metals priced in dollars.

title: Norsk Hydro : Hydro starts onsite renewable energy production with battery storage systems at aluminium plants in Sweden
summary: Norsk Hydro says it has started delivering power from onsite solar panels and battery storage at its aluminium plants in Sweden, with rooftop and ground-mounted PV plus 4.5 MW of batteries. Hydro expects lower energy costs and reduced carbon footprint as it transitions toward zero-emission extrusion.

title: Gladiator Metals Corp.: Gladiator Stakes New Copper Skarn Prospect at the Whitehorse Copper Project
summary: Gladiator Metals staked additional claims for a new copper-skarn prospect at its Whitehorse Copper Belt project and cited historical drilling/rock-chip results with high-grade copper. The company plans further summer mapping and geophysics. The release does not signal immediate supply changes; copper price references are only used for CuEq.

title: Copper Fox Updates Sombrero Butte Copper Project
summary: Copper Fox reported preliminary mapping results at its 100% owned Sombrero Butte copper project in Arizona, highlighting limonite/clay alteration zones and copper-molybdenum anomalies that match the nearby Copper Creek porphyry model. The company plans additional deep geophysical work, with no production changes or supply impacts mentioned.

title: LX Pantos, KSA partner up to ship coal, nickel, lithium from Indonesia
summary: LX Pantos and Indonesian shipping firm KSA plan a joint venture to transport coal and other minerals from Indonesia, including nickel. KSA already moves large volumes and the venture expects to secure barges and expand vessels and transshipment facilities in stages. This could improve Indonesian nickel export capacity and near-term supply expectations.

title: Copper stumbles as funds liquidate amid rate worries
summary: Copper fell 2.7% on the LME as funds unwound bullish positions amid concerns that high interest rates will damp metals demand, especially from China. A firmer dollar and higher yields added pressure. Aluminium and nickel also declined, reflecting broader industrial-metals risk-off sentiment.

title: BHP's bid for Anglo American fails but can high copper price increase supply?
summary: The piece highlights record LME three-month copper prices and all-time-low/negative copper TC/RCs, implying strong copper pricing power and tight processing economics. It links BHP’s failed Anglo bid to investor appetite for copper exposure and cites potential project expansions (Las Bambas, Tia Maria) and increased Chinese scrap supply, though risks remain.

title: Can Copper Prices and Nearshoring Restart Peru's Economic Dynamism?
summary: The piece argues Peru may regain dynamism because a “copper super-cycle” and upcoming Pacific port expansions could unlock mining project development. It notes Peru has major copper reserves and outlines a pipeline of mining investments. The thesis is that copper-linked growth prospects could improve sentiment.

title: New World secures option to acquire Pinafore Copper Deposit in US
summary: New World Resources secured a five-year option to acquire 100% of the Pinafore copper deposit in northern Arizona, with rights to explore exclusively. The deal involves an initial payment, annual option payments, and a buy-in price plus a royalty for ownership. The update supports longer-term copper resource expansion, not immediate output.

title: Eramet's New Caledonia nickel plant needs supply within days, CEO says
summary: Eramet’s CEO said SLN’s New Caledonia nickel furnaces need ore supplies in the coming days because mining has been halted by riots and the Doniambo plant is running at minimum capacity. Without re-supply within about 10 days, operations face risk, tightening near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: EU sanctions gap could allow Russian aluminium into UK
summary: A trade association warns the UK construction sector may inadvertently use Russian aluminium because the EU has not sanctioned aluminium slabs, ingots and billets, comprising most Russian aluminium imports to the bloc. The UK and London Metal Exchange previously limited Russian aluminium, but EU gaps could keep supply flowing.

title: Norilsk Nickel expects nickel market to have surplus
summary: Norilsk Nickel expects the global nickel market to remain in surplus, forecasting roughly 100,000 metric tons for 2024 and 2025. It says low-grade nickel will dominate the surplus. The company attributes persistence to supply growth from new Indonesian facilities and rising offerings of nickel and chemical compounds.

title: Faraday Copper Announces Closing of C$23 Million Bought Deal Financing
summary: Faraday Copper closed a C$23 million bought deal financing at C$0.80 per share. Net proceeds will fund advancement of the Copper Creek Project in Arizona, plus working capital and corporate purposes. The announcement could marginally improve perceived near-term copper supply outlook via project progress.

title: Copper's supply-demand gap - Funds Europe
summary: The piece links copper’s recent spike (~$10,000/tonne) to worsening supply tightness and active production disruptions in Zambia, Chile and Peru, plus firmer demand signals from China (strong industrial output and a higher Caixin PMI). It also cites energy transition and AI/data-centre demand supporting outlooks.

title: Behind Solaris Resources's (TSX:SLS) Milestone Agreement with Ecuadorian Communities for the Warintza Copper Project
summary: Solaris Resources signed an updated Impact and Benefits Agreement with Shuar communities for the Warintza copper project in Ecuador, following a government manual requiring prior consultation. The deal formalizes community consent and commitments for jobs, training, infrastructure, and compensation, aiming to reduce conflict-related delay risk and support project advancement.

title: Anglo starts formal divestment of coal, nickel after rebuffing BHP, CEO says
summary: Anglo American said it has started formal processes to divest coal and explore options for its nickel operations after rejecting BHP takeover bids. Management indicated nickel mines could be mothballed and processes will follow regulatory steps. Such actions may tighten near-term nickel supply expectations and support nickel prices.

title: Copper Stumbles As Funds Liquidate Amid Rate Worries
summary: Copper prices fell sharply on Thursday as funds cut bullish positions amid concerns that high interest rates will curb metals demand, with China highlighted as a top consumer. Three-month LME copper dropped about 2.9% to roughly $10,153/ton, retreating from last week’s record highs.

title: Norsk Hydro : Hydro invests USD 85 million in new technology to deliver high-quality, recycled aluminium products for the U.S. automotive industry
summary: Norsk Hydro plans an $85 million HyForge technology investment at its Henderson, Kentucky aluminium recycling plant, expanding capacity by 28,000 tonnes and adding 31 jobs. The move, supported by Kentucky tax incentives, targets low-carbon aluminium billets for U.S. automotive production, following related upgrades at the site.

title: Ed Husic calls for Hunter input on green steel, aluminium plans | Newcastle Herald
summary: Australia’s Industry Minister Ed Husic is opening public consultation on a green metals policy focused on decarbonised production, including alumina and aluminium. The discussion paper cites Australia’s renewable and mineral advantages and highlights the firm renewable power needed for aluminium. The move may lift expectations for aluminium industry investment.

title: Aluminum Prices Hit Two-Year High On Smelter Output Limits In China
summary: Aluminum prices reportedly reached a two-year high as Chinese smelters operated under output limits. The restriction on production tightens available supply in the near term, typically lifting spot prices. The move suggests market expectations for aluminium availability have worsened over the next days to weeks.

title: Long-term future for New Zealand's Tiwai Point aluminium smelter secured with new power deals
summary: New Zealand Aluminium Smelters secured 20-year electricity arrangements totaling 572 MW to power the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter, with possible demand-response curtailments of up to 185 MW. Contracts start July 2024, supporting stable, competitive low-carbon aluminium output. Rio Tinto also moves to full ownership of NZAS.

title: Mort Rosenblum: Copper World plan's details give pause
summary: An Arizona community meeting scrutinizes the proposed Copper World open-pit copper mine, with concerns about aquifer impacts, air pollution, and weak enforcement. Hydrologists and opponents cite potential risks to Tucson water and clean air. The piece notes copper prices near $5/lb and highlights demand pressure but emphasizes permitting uncertainty.

title: Copper is the holdup for the EV transition
summary: The piece says EV and green-energy targets (California and a Biden executive order) are unrealistic without significantly more copper. It cites EVs needing far more copper than gas cars and warns copper mining takes decades, with high capital costs and long lead times, implying prospective supply tightness and higher prices.

title: The operator of Southland's Tiwai Point Aluminium Smelter has signed a new electricity agreement to keep it operating for the next 20 years - 31-May-2024
summary: Meridian, Mercury, Contact Energy and New Zealand Aluminium Smelters have signed a new electricity agreement, securing operation of the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter for 20 years after 18 months of talks. Local officials described the decision as major economic support, implying more stable aluminium output.

title: Tiwai Point aluminium smelter to stay open until 2044
summary: New Zealand’s Tiwai Point aluminium smelter (NZAS/Rio Tinto) secured a fixed-price power contract with Meridian Energy through 2044, ending uncertainty about shutdown after this year. The deal supports ongoing low-carbon aluminium output and includes demand-response provisions, which can improve power system reliability.

title: Rio to Keep New Zealand Aluminum Smelter Open After Power Deals
summary: Rio says it will keep its New Zealand aluminum smelter running after power deals secured electricity on workable terms. The update lowers the near-term risk of shutdowns or reduced output tied to power costs, supporting aluminum supply expectations and likely providing modest upward price pressure for the metal.

title: Rio Tinto to Keep NZ Aluminum Plant Open for 20 More Years
summary: Rio Tinto said it will keep its New Zealand aluminium plant operating for 20 more years. The extension improves long-term supply certainty for aluminium, but because the horizon is far beyond the next few weeks, near-term price impact is likely limited.

title: A deal's been made with New Zealand's Aluminium Smelter to keep the smelter at Tiwai operating for the next 20 years - 31-May-2024
summary: New Zealand’s Tiwai Point aluminium smelter is secured for the next 20 years after Meridian, Mercury, Contact Energy and New Zealand Aluminium Smelters signed a deal following 18 months of negotiations. Local officials say the smelter’s continued operation is a major economic boost for Southland and the country.

title: New Zealand Aluminium Smelters Signs Long-Term Energy Deals for Tiwai Point
summary: New Zealand Aluminium Smelters signed 20-year electricity arrangements totaling 572 MW to power the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter, using renewable generation in the mix. Rio Tinto says the long-term future of the smelter is secured, and it will buy remaining minority stakes in NZAS after the deal.

title: Rio Tinto signs deal to become sole owner of New Zealand Aluminium Smelters
summary: Rio Tinto agreed to buy Sumitomo Chemical’s stake to become sole owner of New Zealand Aluminium Smelters, which runs the Tiwai aluminium smelter. The company also secured 20-year electricity supply and demand-response arrangements with NZ energy generators. Rio also plans to buy Sumitomo’s stake in Australia’s Boyne Smelters.

title: Sumitomo Chemical : Announces Sale of its Shares in Two Overseas Aluminum Smelting Companies
summary: Sumitomo Chemical said it will sell its shares in New Zealand Aluminium Smelters and Boyne Smelters to Rio Tinto, after required approvals. The company cited profitability volatility tied to international aluminum market conditions and is exiting the investment to strengthen its financial position, not to change smelter output immediately.

title: In Brief: Telcos, Wages, Tariffs & Aluminium
summary: A broker wrap flags tightening bauxite and alumina supply, citing disrupted Chinese domestic sources and ongoing refinery or mine constraints. With China importing most bauxite (mainly Guinea and Australia), the expected tighter alumina/bauxite balance should lift prices for longer, benefiting aluminium-linked producers and supporting aluminium sentiment.

title: The Overnight Report: Weaker Data Trumped
summary: Weaker US economic data revised GDP down and reinforced “higher-for-longer” rate concerns, dragging US risk assets. The report says base metals traded lower. It also mentions Rio Tinto keeping a New Zealand aluminium smelter running with new electricity supply agreements, but overall the tone is bearish for industrial metals.

title: Copper rises; monthly gains capped by profit-taking, weak China demand
summary: Copper rebounded on the LME, but gains were capped by profit-taking after May 20 record highs and by weaker physical demand in China. China’s May manufacturing PMI fell below 50. Aluminium and nickel also rose on the day, reflecting broader market moves rather than a single new metal-specific shock.

title: Copper LME: Commodites to set fresh records after 'violent price swings'
summary: Investors debate how durable the commodity bull market is as shortages could drive more frequent, violent swings in base metals. Copper on the LME has fallen about 6% from its May 20 record high, but brokers expect the strong rally to resume after the current profit-taking dip.

title: Copper set for monthly increase but weak China demand cap gains
summary: Reuters reports copper under pressure after China’s May manufacturing PMI fell below 50, worsening demand expectations for the top consumer. Despite earlier speculative gains and a modest monthly rise, profit-taking could push copper back below $10,000. LME aluminium eased, nickel edged up slightly.

title: Indonesia to Issue Copper Export Permits for Freeport, Amman, Official Says
summary: Indonesia will issue copper concentrate export permits for Freeport Indonesia and Amman as their current permits expire Friday. A trade ministry official said the permits will ensure exports are not disrupted, lowering the risk of a near-term supply interruption from Indonesia’s copper concentrate shipments.

title: South Greenland Copper Exploration Update
summary: Amaroq Minerals reported updated results from South Greenland exploration, confirming a copper-molybdenum porphyry system and identifying 24 additional copper targets for its 2024 field season. The company also references copper-nickel sulphide targets within the same belt, but provides no near-term production or supply impacts.

title: ENRG shareholders poised to cash in on Botswana copper hunt
summary: ENRG-linked shareholders are watching copper exploration progress in Botswana. Arc’s Virgo project found new drill targets after an IP survey, and Kavango is starting a first phase of diamond drilling at Karakubis. The story highlights copper’s recent volatility but involves only exploration, not near-term production changes.

title: Copper wire theft from street lights: Costly with little payout
summary: City of Bakersfield reports an uptick in copper wire theft from streetlights, leaving areas dark and creating repair costs far exceeding scrap value. Officials cite small stolen weights (often under $50) but high materials and labor bills. The city is considering more security and using aluminum alternatives for lower recycle value.

title: Posco breaks ground for W1.5t nickel and precursor plants
summary: Posco Group broke ground on a KRW 1.5 tn project with CNGR to build a nickel refining plant and a precursor cathode-material plant for EV batteries. The refining unit targets 50,000 mt/year of ~99.9% nickel and the precursor unit 110,000 tons/year. Production starts in 2026 to reduce import dependence.

title: POSCO, CNGR break ground for joint production of nickel, precursors
summary: POSCO and China’s CNGR held a groundbreaking ceremony for POSCO CNGR Nickel Solution’s nickel refinery and a C&P Energy precursor plant in Pohang. The joint ventures are intended to secure stable raw materials for rechargeable batteries, potentially supporting improved near-term expectations for nickel supply.

title: Rio Tinto to buy out New Zealand Aluminium Smelters
summary: Rio Tinto will take full control of New Zealand Aluminium Smelters (NZAS) by buying Sumitomo Chemical’s stake. The move keeps the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter running for at least two more decades, supported by long-term electricity supply deals. Rio also buys more in Australia’s Boyne smelter.

title: Indonesia to Delay Ban on Copper Concentrate Exports to Year-End
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports Indonesia will delay a ban on copper concentrate exports until year-end. By extending current export flows, the decision is expected to ease near-term concentration of supply risk for global smelters, providing support for copper market sentiment over the next several weeks.

title: Rio Tinto expands aluminium assets in New Zealand and Australia
summary: Rio Tinto agreed to acquire Sumitomo Chemical’s stakes in New Zealand Aluminium Smelters (NZAS) and Boyne Smelters, moving toward full control of NZAS and a larger share of BSL. NZAS also signed 20-year renewable electricity contracts, stabilizing power costs and supporting ongoing aluminium smelting operations.

title: Copper extends losses after weak factory data from China
summary: Copper prices fell after China’s weak manufacturing data raised concerns about near-term demand. The LME three-month contract dropped to about $10,112/ton and Shanghai July copper also eased. Analysts said the soft PMI could prompt revised demand forecasts, though further stimulus hopes limited losses.

title: Surge Copper : Announces Closing of $3.9M Strategic Placement and Commences Berg PFS Metallurgical Test Program
summary: Surge Copper closed a C$3.93 million strategic placement and began metallurgical test work for its Berg project to support a pre-feasibility study. The program includes comminution, flotation, and copper-molybdenum separation tests on drill-core samples. The article indicates advancement of copper project development, not a near-term supply change.

title: Exploration Marvels: Torr Metals Inc. (TSX.V: TMET) Surges Forward In A Shining Era For Copper ...
summary: The piece reports record-breaking performance in global copper contracts on the London Metals Exchange, alongside similar strength in New York and Shanghai. This suggests improving short-term price expectations for copper, even though the company mentioned (Torr Metals) is primarily focused on gold.

title: Why there's a massive copper shortage
summary: The article argues copper demand is accelerating for electric vehicles, wind, construction and the power grid, while mining capacity is struggling to keep up. It says existing and under-construction projects cover only about 80% of needs by 2030 and notes high costs deterring new mines—supportive of copper shortages and prices.

title: The copper supply-demand gap
summary: The piece argues copper is facing a widening supply-demand gap. It cites electricity shortages from drought in Zambia, falling output at Chile’s Codelco due to lower-grade ore, and renewed disruptions at Peru’s Las Bambas. Demand drivers include stronger Chinese industrial activity and copper demand running well above last year.

title: Surge Copper Announces Closing of $3.9M Strategic Placement and Commences Berg PFS Metallurgical Test Program
summary: Surge Copper closed a C$3.9m strategic placement and began metallurgical test work for its Berg Project PFS. The program includes copper assays and flotation and copper–molybdenum separation testing on drill-core samples to confirm recoveries and flow-sheet parameters. This is copper-relevant but mostly technical, not immediate market-moving supply.

title: Indonesia's Delay of Its Ban on Copper Exports Could Weigh on Prices
summary: Indonesia, a major copper producer, delayed its planned ban on copper concentrate exports from June 1 to December 31, 2024. Export permits continue until smelters reach full capacity. The change could weaken market sentiment after copper hit record highs and SHFE inventories rose counter-seasonally.

title: Latest News | Production of Iron Ore, Aluminium, Limestone Rises in April
summary: India’s mines ministry said aluminium production rose 1% in April to 3.42 lakh tonnes versus 3.39 lakh tonnes a year earlier. Iron ore and limestone also increased, indicating firmer activity in metals-linked user sectors, but aluminium output is the only directly cited tracked-metal driver.

title: Copper Leader Chile Posts Worst Monthly Output in Over a Year
summary: Chile, a leading copper producer, reportedly posted its worst monthly output in over a year. Such a development can shift near-term expectations for copper supply and inventories, influencing copper prices over the next days as traders assess whether the production shortfall is temporary or persistent.

title: Sprott Physical Copper Trust Announces Filing of Final
summary: Sprott Physical Copper Trust filed a final prospectus and is launching an IPO of 10 million transferable units at US$10 each, raising about US$100 million. Net proceeds will be used to buy physical copper, with trading expected to begin after a June 6 closing. Over-allotment could add funds.

title: How AI and EVs Are Making Copper the New Gold
summary: The piece argues copper is in a supply deficit driven by EV and AI-linked demand, citing a recent Comex short squeeze that pushed prices to records. It quotes higher UBS deficit forecasts and rising LME price expectations, and frames M&A activity (BHP’s failed Anglo deal) around elevated copper prices.

title: Deep-sea nickel hits battery grade for The Metals Co.
summary: SGS verification reports that nickel mined from the Pacific seabed by The Metals Company can be processed into high-purity, battery-grade nickel sulphate suitable for EV batteries. The Ontario lab reportedly produced the material from polymetallic nodules, potentially supporting longer-term nickel supply expectations and sentiment.

title: EU Increases Purchases of Russian Iron, Steel and Aluminum
summary: The EU increased purchases of Russian metals in March 2024, with Russian aluminium shipments rising 29% month-on-month to 91.4 million euros, the highest since Oct 2023. Import demand growth is cited from Germany, Spain, and Poland, implying more aluminium supply entering Europe.

title: Hundreds of workers on strike at Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia
summary: Operations at Taseko Mines’ Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia were suspended after unionized workers voted to strike and negotiations for a new contract ended without a deal. The company shut down mining and milling before midnight, leaving only essential staff. The mine is a major Canadian copper producer.

title: Hundreds of workers on strike at Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia | iNFOnews
summary: Hundreds of workers at Taseko Mines’ Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia are on strike after contract talks with the union failed. Taseko suspended mining and milling operations, leaving only essential staff. The Gibraltar mine is a major Canadian open-pit copper producer, implying a near-term supply hit for copper.

title: Operations suspended at British Columbia's Gibraltar copper mine due to worker strike
summary: Operations at British Columbia’s Gibraltar copper mine were suspended after a worker strike. The shutdown can disrupt near-term copper supply and production schedules, affecting expectations for availability over the coming days and potentially influencing copper pricing in the short term.

title: Rate cuts could crash copper prices, analysts warn
summary: Analysts at Liberum warn that potential US Federal Reserve rate cuts could unwind copper’s recent surge. With copper above $10,000/tonne, they forecast a fall to $7,000–$7,500 by year-end, contrasting consensus views that prices stay above $8,500.

title: Operations suspended at BC Gibraltar copper mine due to worker strike
summary: Taseko suspended mining and milling at its Gibraltar copper mine after contract talks with Unifor Local 3018 ended without a deal and workers voted to strike. The shutdown is immediate, leaving only essential staff on site, potentially tightening near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Operations suspended at British Columbia's Gibraltar copper mine due to worker strike | iNFOnews
summary: Taseko Mines suspended mining and milling at its Gibraltar copper mine in British Columbia after union negotiations for a new collective agreement ended without a deal. Unifor says workers voted to strike after the previous contract expired Friday. Only essential staff remain while operations remain shut down.

title: Beyond the Mines: 3 Stocks to Buy to Profit From the Surge in Copper Prices
summary: The piece highlights Bank of America’s view that tightening copper supply, alongside green investment and economic rebound, could lift copper prices to about $10,250/t by Q4. It argues that non-mining stocks with copper-linked exposure (equipment makers/dealers and copper royalties) would benefit as copper strengthens.

title: BHP-Anglo Debacle Shines Spotlight on Copper Scarcity
summary: BHP’s failed bid for Anglo American spotlights copper tightness. The piece cites record copper prices, Goldman forecasts for demand growth from AI and defense, and limited new mine investment due to poor returns and high capex. It notes only modest near-term surplus, but overall supply risk supports a bullish outlook.

title: Freeport Indonesia says yet to receive copper concentrate export permit extension
summary: Freeport Indonesia told parliament it has raised its 2024 copper concentrate and refined copper output guidance while awaiting an extension of its copper concentrate export permit and a promised continuation of its dispensation. The earlier permit lapsed May 31; further levies and smelter commissioning timing drive near-term supply expectations for refined copper and cathodes.

title: London copper rises on China, US data
summary: London copper rose 1.1% on supportive China and US data: China’s private manufacturing survey showed the fastest activity growth in about two years, and US inflation stabilization kept the Fed’s planned rate cuts on track. A tighter China copper import discount suggested improved physical demand, lifting copper and supporting aluminium and nickel.

title: Freeport Indonesia Says Yet to Receive Copper Concentrate Export Permit Extension
summary: Freeport Indonesia said it has not yet received an extension for its copper concentrate export permit from Indonesia’s government. The existing permit runs only until May 31. The lack of an extension adds uncertainty around near-term copper concentrate exports, potentially tightening supply expectations and pressuring copper prices.

title: Gladiator Highlights Large Scale Copper Magnetic Anomalies
summary: Gladiator Metals says drone-borne aeromagnetic surveys over Yukon’s Whitehorse Copper Belt identified large-scale, undrilled magnetic anomalies linked to magnetite-copper skarn mineralization. The company has expanded its claims and begun field follow-up and geophysics ahead of drilling later in 2024, but no output is yet affected.

title: BSE : Discontinuation of Copper and Zinc Futures Contract in Commodity Derivatives Segment
summary: BSE issued a trading notice that its Copper (and Zinc) futures contract in the commodity derivatives segment will be discontinued effective June 3, 2023. The announcement concerns exchange contract availability rather than underlying market fundamentals, implying limited direct impact on immediate copper price levels.

title: Copper climbs on Chinese data and hopes of Fed rate cuts
summary: Copper prices rose after stronger-than-expected Chinese factory activity and U.S. inflation data that revived hopes for Federal Reserve rate cuts. Lower expected rates could lift manufacturing and industrial-metal demand while a weaker dollar makes dollar-priced metals cheaper. Aluminium also moved higher in the same session.

title: Virtual Tour of Cobalt Blue Holdings Ltd's Cobalt-Nickel Refinery Testwork
summary: Cobalt Blue Holdings describes virtual tour coverage of pilot-scale feedstock testing at its technology centre for a planned cobalt-nickel refinery in Australia. The company reports high cobalt extraction recovery and ongoing optimisation toward producing cobalt and nickel sulphate. Policy support for critical minerals is cited, but commercial timelines are not provided.

title: Nickel 28 Announces Receipt of Management Cease Trade Order in Response to Voluntary Application
summary: Nickel 28 Capital Corp. announced it received a management cease trade order from the Ontario Securities Commission after a voluntary application tied to delays in filing audited annual financial statements. The order restricts certain insiders from trading the company’s securities but does not affect non-insider shareholders’ trading. No production impacts are stated.

title: Bell Copper Announces First Tranche Closing of Non-Brokered Private Placement
summary: Bell Copper closed the first tranche of a non-brokered private placement, issuing units at $0.08 and raising about $160.5k gross proceeds. Funds will support ongoing drilling at its Big Sandy and Perseverance porphyry copper projects and working capital, with a second tranche planned.

title: Funds keep faith with copper even as squeeze fades: Andy Home
summary: Reuters reports fund managers remain bullish on copper despite the CME squeeze fading and some profit-taking. Long positions are still elevated on CME and LME, but copper is consolidating near $10,000 on weakening momentum. China inventories are rising, challenging the supply-tightness narrative.

title: Kazakhstan signs agreement for $1.5bn copper smelter project
summary: Kazakhstan signed an agreement with China Nonferrous Metal Mining to build a $1.5bn copper smelter near Aktogay with planned capacity of 300,000 t/year. The plant will process concentrate from Bozshakol and Aktogay mines, adding domestic cathode supply, but commissioning is targeted for 2028.

title: North American aluminium industry needs $60 billion investment to reach net zero by 2050: Aluminum Association
summary: The Aluminum Association says North American primary aluminium needs about $60 billion investment to cut emissions and reach net zero by 2050, alongside major reductions milestones. It cites low-carbon smelting, expanding recycling, and policy support for a green smelter project under the BIL/IRA, but targets are long-term.

title: Spot copper concentrates trading limited as market focus shifts to mid-year supply talks
summary: Fastmarkets said the copper concentrate TC index (cif Asia Pacific) fell to a record low discount, indicating limited smelter buying and little spot TC rebound. Ample blister copper and anodes in China reduce concentrate usage, while Chilean Antofagasta begins concentrate supply talks with no figures yet.

title: Taseko halts BC copper mine Gibraltar as workers strike
summary: More than 500 workers have gone on strike at Taseko Mines’ Gibraltar copper operation in central British Columbia after contract negotiations failed. The work stoppage halts mine output, likely tightening near-term copper supply expectations and weighing on prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: Hydro Aluminum Metals USA Expands Henderson, Kentucky, Operations
summary: Hydro Aluminum Metals USA plans to expand its Henderson, Kentucky facility by adding 80,000 square feet to introduce its HyForge technology for automotive billets and components. The project is backed by state tax incentives tied to an $85 million investment and jobs targets. Completion is scheduled for 2026.

title: Low nickel prices exerting drag on Sudbury economy: Report
summary: A Conference Board of Canada outlook says Sudbury’s economy is being weighed by soft nickel prices. It links the fall in nickel to worries about electric-car demand and, importantly, rising Indonesian supply, noting nickel prices are about half of March 2022 levels. Lower prices have hurt Vale and Glencore profits.

title: China to build $1.5B copper smelter in Kazakhstan
summary: Kazakhstan’s government has agreed with China Nonferrous Metal Mining (NFC) to develop a copper smelter through KAZ Minerals Smelting.
