summary: Bell Copper announced the closing of the second tranche of a non-brokered private placement, raising about C$254,522. Proceeds will fund ongoing drilling and exploration at its Big Sandy and Perseverance porphyry copper projects and general working capital. The financing is not large enough to imply major immediate copper supply changes.

title: Metals Creek Resources Corp. Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement to Advance Tillex Copper Project and Shabaqua Corners Gold Project
summary: Metals Creek Resources Corp. announced a non-brokered private placement (flow-through and non-flow-through units) to raise up to $400,000, intended to fund drilling at its Tillex copper project. The rest of the release describes unit structure and prior drill results; no immediate production or supply changes are stated.

title: What Factors Affect Copper Supply and Demand? (Updated 2024)
summary: The article outlines key factors affecting copper prices: China’s outsized role in consumption and smelting, energy-transition demand (EVs/renewables), mine disruptions and supply risks, and inventory dynamics. It also notes weakening China property/manufacturing and rising ShFE stocks, creating offsetting bullish and bearish pressures for near-term copper.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces 2024 Second Quarter Operating and Financial Results
summary: Copper Fox reports interim financial results and provides progress updates on several copper projects, including advancing the Schaft Creek joint venture toward a prefeasibility study, permitting progress for Mineral Mountain drilling, and technical work at Van Dyke and Sombrero Butte. The article signals ongoing exploration spend rather than any immediate supply output changes.

title: Copper climbs on supply worries, China demand concerns limit gains
summary: Copper rose on the LME and SHFE, supported by supply worries including Anglo American’s planned pause of processing at Chile’s Los Bronces, while China demand concerns and higher exports capped upside. Soft U.S. dollar conditions also supported prices. Nickel and aluminium also edged higher as sentiment improved.

title: ENRG puts close watch on two-pronged African copper hunt
summary: ENRG Elements is monitoring JV partners Kavango Resources and Arc Minerals as they start separate drill campaigns in Botswana’s Kalahari Copper Belt. Kavango plans shallow drilling to test copper-silver targets, while Arc will drill IP-defined anomalies. The report supports potential future discovery but signals no immediate production impact.

title: China economy: Copper glut soars in sign of stuttering recovery
summary: China’s copper glut has surged in warehouse inventories, with Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks rising to the highest since 2020 at about 330,000 tonnes. The build-up follows a price spike and tepid consumer demand, prompting manufacturers to pull back on purchases. Stocks imply near-term downward pressure on copper prices.

title: Copper supported by supply shortages; demand concerns cap gains
summary: Copper prices firmed as ore supply shortages and mine maintenance plans (Los Bronces output expected to fall next year) supported the market. A softer U.S. dollar also aided prices, but China demand concerns—reflected in higher LME stockpiles and softer spot demand—capped further gains.

title: How will Saudia Arabia's 'Vision 2030' boost nickel demand and unlock investment in supply?
summary: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 is expected to lift nickel demand through new steel plants, EV/battery manufacturing and broader infrastructure “giga-projects,” areas that account for most nickel consumption. In parallel, investments such as Manara Minerals’ stake in Vale aim to raise nickel output, but demand growth is emphasized as the key driver for near-term market expectations.

title: Copper bounces, spotlight on inventory jump
summary: Copper prices bounced as investors shifted from growth concerns to potential shortages after Anglo American signaled lower output from its Los Bronces mine due to maintenance. However, rising LME-approved inventories in Asia and wide contango pointing to surpluses raised doubts about tightness, tempering the net bullish effect.

title: Along Peru's mining corridor, Big Copper faces a snarl of trucks
summary: Reuters reports surging truck traffic from Peru’s illegal/artisan copper mines is jamming the 482-kilometer mining corridor highway, causing accidents, roadway damage, and increased delays for copper concentrate shipments to the coast. With production tied to major mines, risks of near-term supply disruptions are rising.

title: Rio Tinto invests $165 million in its Grande-Baie aluminium smelter
summary: Rio Tinto will invest US$165 million to refurbish two furnaces at its Grande-Baie aluminium smelter in Canada, plus feasibility studies for replacing anode-related equipment. Work on anode baking furnaces is scheduled for 2025-2026, aimed at sustaining competitive anode supply to its plants for decades. Carbon offsets are planned.

title: Intrepid Metals Drills 6.22% Cu and 8.83g/t Au (10.71% CuEq) at Its Corral Copper Property in Arizona
summary: Intrepid Metals announced additional drill results from its Corral Copper Property in Arizona, including multiple high-grade copper intercepts (up to 6.22% Cu over short intervals) from massive sulphide and skarn/CRD styles. The company plans further phase-two drilling after integrating results, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Intrepid Metals Corp.: Intrepid Metals Drills 6.22% Cu and 8.83g/t Au (10.71% CuEq) at Its Corral Copper Property in Arizona
summary: Intrepid Metals reported additional near-surface drill intercepts at its Corral Copper property in Arizona, including multiple high-grade copper zones. The news may marginally affect sentiment around future copper supply, but it is exploration-only with no immediate production or trade/inventory impact. Nickel and aluminium are not addressed.

title: Sterling Metals exercises option to acquire Adeline Copper-Silver Project
summary: Sterling Metals exercised an option to acquire full ownership of the Adeline copper-silver exploration project in Labrador, Canada. The deal includes a C$200,000 payment and 8.5 million shares, with prior option terms from Chesterfield. Recent drilling confirmed copper mineralisation, but no production timeline is given.

title: Casa Minerals Receives Drill Permit for Arsenault Copper-Gold-Silver Project
summary: Casa Minerals announced it received a five-year exploration work permit to conduct geophysical surveys and drill from helicopter-access sites at its Arsenault VMS copper-gold-silver project in British Columbia. The drilling program supports testing copper-bearing VMS occurrences, potentially improving near-term sentiment for copper exploration potential.

title: Copper Surge Unleashes Freighter Frenzy: Peru's Mining Road Crisis
summary: Reuters reports that rising copper prices have driven a surge in trucks hauling copper concentrate from illegal/artisan mines in Peru, congesting a key 482-km mining corridor highway. The increased traffic causes delays, stoppages, accidents, and road damage, complicating logistics for major copper producers.

title: Analysis-Along Peru's mining corridor, Big Copper faces a snarl of trucks | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Reuters reports that surging illegal copper mining in Peru is increasing the number of trucks along a key Andean “mining corridor,” causing traffic jams, accidents, road damage and hazardous night travel. Mines like Las Bambas, Constancia and Antapaccay face delays and stoppages, prompting calls for stronger inspections and control.

title: London's FTSE 100 gains after CPI shows in-line inflation, copper prices boost
summary: London stocks rose as investors digested an in-line CPI report, while industrial miners climbed alongside higher copper prices, which reached seven-week highs. The CPI kept rate-cut expectations in focus, but miner gains were attributed directly to copper strength. Anglo American also moved on outlook for its Chile copper mine.

title: An ETF to play gold, silver, copper and everything in between
summary: The article promotes Direxion’s broad commodity ETF that can hold copper (and gold/silver) when price trends are favorable. It cites recent gains in copper and gold alongside persistent inflation and central-bank gold buying, but offers no new copper-specific fundamentals or immediate catalysts.

title: Aluminium premiums being supported in all key regions
summary: Fastmarkets reports aluminium premiums rising in key regions, including Japan’s MJP premium and South Korea cif/fca, supported by tight availability and higher quarterly negotiations. Logistics issues and expectation of high Q3 settlements bolster tender levels. Europe premiums edged up amid regional tightness, while scrap tightness supports US demand.

title: Copper, jewelry buoy RI exports amid weakness in coal, CPO - Economy
summary: Indonesia’s trade surplus rose in May, supported by sharply higher exports of copper ore (+60.1% yoy) and jewelry (+67.3% yoy). While coal and CPO exports fell in value terms, the copper ore growth points to steadier outbound supply flows that could support near-term copper sentiment.

title: Copper edges higher on China easing, demand pick-up and supply woes
summary: Copper prices edged higher as sentiment improved on China’s central bank reinforcing easing policy, alongside better end-user demand. The report also cites supply concerns, including expected sharp declines in Chile’s Los Bronces output and easing SHFE inventories. LME stock gains and subdued physical demand limited upside.

title: Orecap's Cuprum Intersects 114 metres of 1.1% Copper Equivalent within 171 metres of 0.98% Copper Equivalent
summary: Orecap/Cuprum announced new step-out and infill drill results at the Thierry copper project, highlighting long intervals with high CuEq grades (including near-surface and deeper extensions). The resource also contains nickel, though Ni recoveries need metallurgical improvement, supporting a generally bullish outlook for copper and a secondary nickel read-through.

title: Orecap Invest Corp.: Orecap's Cuprum Intersects 114 metres of 1.1% Copper Equivalent within 171 metres of 0.98% Copper Equivalent
summary: Orecap/Cuprum reported results from five additional drill holes at the Thierry copper project, highlighting long intercepts with copper-equivalent grades and reiterating the K1 open-pit inferred resource. The deposit also contains nickel, but the release is exploratory and does not indicate imminent supply changes.

title: Copper edges up on hopes of stronger demand, stockpiles cap gains
summary: Copper prices edged slightly higher on hopes of improved Chinese demand after recent declines, alongside supply concerns. Gains were limited by a stronger U.S. dollar and rising LME stockpiles to the highest level since January. China’s easing remains constrained, while aluminium and nickel also logged modest moves.

title: China's Copper Exports Jump To Record On 'Export Arbitrage'
summary: The article headline says China’s copper exports have risen to a record level, attributed to “export arbitrage.” If more copper is being shipped abroad from China due to price differentials, it can add to near-term market supply and typically pressures copper prices in coming days.

title: NevGold Samples 1.22% Copper and 8.19 g/t Gold And Defines 4-Km Long Copper-Gold-Silver Trend At The Zeus Copper Project in The Hercules Copper District, Idaho
summary: NevGold reports high-grade surface rock chip samples at its Zeus copper-gold-silver project in Idaho, including several results above 1% copper, supporting copper porphyry potential and plans for continued fieldwork and eventual drilling. The update is exploratory and does not imply immediate changes to copper supply.

title: NevGold Corp.: NevGold Samples 1.22% Copper and 8.19 g/t Gold And Defines 4-Km Long Copper-Gold-Silver Trend At The Zeus Copper Project in The Hercules Copper District, Idaho
summary: NevGold reported positive surface sampling at its Zeus copper project in Idaho, including multiple rock-chip results around ~0.86–1.30% Cu and several gold/silver anomalies, and mapped a 4-km copper-gold-silver trend. The company plans further geochemical/ geophysical work and potential drill testing over the coming months.

title: Vale sees higher 2026 copper, nickel output after investments
summary: Vale said asset reviews and investments at its Sudbury and Salobo mines could lift 2026 copper output about 5% above its baseline scenario and raise nickel production by around 10%. The guidance suggests improved future supply, which can support bullish sentiment in copper and nickel markets.

title: Vale sees higher 2026 copper, nickel output after investments
summary: Vale said investments and an asset review could lift its 2026 output. Copper production is projected to be about 5% higher than its baseline, with nickel production about 10% higher, citing potential gains from Sudbury and Salobo mine improvements. The update supports more favorable supply expectations.

title: Flow Metals Completes Induced Polarization Survey at New Brenda Porphyry Copper Target
summary: Flow Metals reports completion of an induced polarization survey over its New Brenda copper-silver-molybdenum project in British Columbia, identifying two chargeability anomalies interpreted as potential disseminated sulphide zones associated with a porphyry system. The company plans further prospecting and survey expansion toward drill-ready targets.

title: Europacific Metals Inc.: EuroPacific Announces Drill Plan Extension Down to 350 Meters Undercutting the High-Grade Copper Zone at Miguel Vacas Located in Southern Portugal
summary: Europacific Metals announced an extension of drilling at its Miguel Vacas copper project in southern Portugal, targeting higher-grade and deeper (“fresh”) mineralization beneath an oxidized blanket. Partial drill results include strong copper intercepts, while most assays are pending, with the campaign aimed at defining an open-pit oxide resource via hydrometallurgy.

title: China Turns to Cast-Off Copper in Battle to Feed Hungry Smelters
summary: The piece’s headline says China is increasingly using discarded/cast-off copper to feed smelters that need additional feedstock. That suggests heightened demand for scrap copper and potentially tighter near-term supply conditions, which can support copper prices over the next days to weeks.

title: Investigation into automotive model certification expected to dampen aluminium demand in Japan
summary: Toyota suspended production, sales and shipments of three models in Japan, while Mazda halted two models, pending a certification investigation; suspensions were extended to end-July. Auto is Japan’s largest aluminium demand sector, so demand may slow, but traders expect limited impact on aluminium prices amid regional supply tightness and supported premiums.

title: EuroPacific Announces Drill Plan Extension Down to 350 Meters Undercutting the High-Grade Copper Zone at Miguel Vacas Located in Southern Portugal
summary: EuroPacific Metals announced an extension of its Miguel Vacas drill program in southern Portugal, including an additional undercut hole down to 350 meters targeting fresh sulphide mineralization below an oxidized zone. The first hole returned strong copper grades (up to 7.49% Cu) and assay results are pending.

title: China's Secret Weapon in the Global Copper War
summary: The piece says China is “sitting pretty” as global copper shortages raise prices. It highlights near-record refined copper output supported by copper scrap, alongside stronger Chinese factory activity and stabilizing U.S. inflation, factors that lift expectations of Fed rate cuts and underpin a copper price rise.

title: Indonesia vows to invest more in aluminium supply chain in strategy for critical metals
summary: Indonesia says it will invest further in its aluminium supply chain as bauxite export restrictions remain in place. With more bauxite mining quotas and expansion plans for smelters like Inalum, the country aims to increase alumina and primary aluminium output, potentially shifting regional bauxite/alumina supply and supporting aluminium prices.

title: Vale Unveils $3.3 Billion Plan to Boost Copper and Nickel Output
summary: Vale is set to unveil a $3.3 billion investment plan aimed at boosting production of copper and nickel. The move suggests higher supply expectations for both metals, which can influence short-term market sentiment depending on the timing and scale of output increases relative to demand and inventories.

title: Vale Unveils $3.3 Billion Plan to Boost Copper and Nickel Output
summary: Vale unveiled a $3.3 billion plan aimed at boosting output of copper and nickel. The announcement is directly tied to changes in near-term supply expectations for both metals, which can feed into market pricing over the next several days to a few weeks as production capacity plans are digested.

title: Sprott Physical Copper Trust Announces Exercise of
summary: Sprott Physical Copper Trust announced the underwriters partially exercised the over-allotment option, buying 1,000,000 units at US$10 each, raising $10 million. Net proceeds will generally be used to purchase physical copper, with procurement and handling arranged by an advisor. No other metals are referenced.

title: Copper: China About to Secure a New Mine in Africa
summary: Reuters reports JCHX Mining is near closing its purchase of Zambia’s Lubambe copper mine after IRH exited the bidding. Zambia is a major copper producer, and the government seeks higher output via new investment. The deal implies continued/expanded copper supply prospects.

title: Canadian Critical Minerals Inc.: Canadian Critical Minerals Receives Update on Drill Results from Thierry Copper Project
summary: Canadian Critical Minerals received final drill results from the Thierry Copper Project near Pickle Lake, Ontario. The company says results are as good or better than expected and indicate the K1-1 open pit remains open on strike and down dip, supporting follow-up drilling to expand the resource.

title: Copper prices set for weekly gain on demand pick-up
summary: Copper futures were down on Friday due to a stronger dollar but were poised for a first weekly gain in five as physical demand picked up after prices hit a two-month low. LME copper found support around $9,500-$9,600/ton. Aluminium was nearly flat and nickel slightly lower.

title: Unexpected copper and gold find boosts Cleveland project | The Advocate
summary: Elementos Limited said a diamond drilling hole at its Cleveland Tin Project intersected untargeted high-grade copper and gold mineralisation near the former Cleveland mine site. The company will further evaluate the results while continuing drilling for tin, copper and tungsten targets, boosting exploration outlook for copper in the region.

title: DRILLING UPDATE, KONKOLA WEST COPPER PROJECT | Company Announcement
summary: Tertiary Minerals updates drilling at the Konkola West Copper Project: the first hole (KWDD001) has reached 1,341m and is continuing above the target horizon. Progress is slower due to a new drill rig and variable ground conditions. Drilling will continue; no further detail is expected until completion.

title: Copper Country's Conundrum | Interlochen Public Radio
summary: An Interlochen Public Radio segment examines a proposed new Copperwood copper mine in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula amid local environmental opposition and economic hopes. It cites projected annual copper output and the state’s partial approval of a $50 million grant, but timing toward production is not immediate.

title: FLOW recovers stolen copper in Riverton
summary: Telecommunications company FLOW says it recovered part of copper wires stolen from its network in Riverton, after losses linked to theft and vandalism. FLOW estimates significant copper-related damage and notes theft caused service outages. Police investigate an alleged premises with burnt copper cables, an illegal activity.

title: Copper resumes downtrend on supply overhang and weak demand
summary: Copper prices resumed their downtrend as concerns grew about surplus supplies and sluggish demand in China. LME three-month copper fell 1.5% and SHFE stocks surged, reinforcing an oversupply overhang. The Reuters piece also reported easing aluminium and nickel prices amid generally weaker industrial metal sentiment.

title: Vale to spend $3.3bn to grow copper and nickel production
summary: Vale plans to invest $3.3bn to expand copper and nickel production capacity in Brazil and Canada, targeting copper output around 500,000t by 2028. The program centers on upgrades at Salobo and Sossego mines and aims to boost productivity and lower costs, implying higher future supply and potential price pressure.

title: Vale to spend $3.3bn to grow copper and nickel production
summary: Vale plans to invest $3.3bn over four years to expand copper and nickel capacity, targeting about 500,000 tonnes of copper output by 2028 through upgrades at Brazil’s Salobo and Sossego mines. It also aims to lower costs via productivity improvements, but the timeframe limits immediate price impact.

title: How Saudi Arabia's plans to increase base metals production, consumption will affect markets
summary: The article says Saudi Arabia is ramping base-metals production and usage under Vision 2030. It cites Vale investment to lift copper production and plans for a copper smelter, possible nickel demand growth from steel/EV projects, and increasing aluminium consumption amid tight supply and Red Sea route disruptions that support higher aluminium premiums.

title: Blast at Italian aluminum-steel plant injures 8 workers
summary: An explosion at an aluminium-steel plant near Bolzano, Italy, injured eight workers and triggered a fire that was extinguished by responders. Investigators are determining the cause, while unions plan a strike to stress workplace safety. The incident may disrupt aluminium output in the near term.

title: Copper Market Rally Loses Steam as Demand Fails to Keep Up
summary: Copper prices retraced after a late-May peak, falling as demand failed to keep up. Funds reduced long positions per COT data, Chinese demand signals weakened with negative Yanshan premiums, and LME inventories rose to the highest since February. A contango/backwardation mix points to a well-supplied, softer demand environment.

title: Pro-Palestinian group wants Canada to ban nickel sales to Israel
summary: A Sudbury pro-Palestinian group has launched a petition urging Canada to ban nickel sales to Israel or to arms manufacturers supplying Israel, arguing Canadian nickel is used for military equipment. The petition could prompt policy scrutiny affecting perceived nickel export demand, despite criticism from Israel supporters.

title: Vale to spend billions to boost copper and nickel output, report says
summary: Vale plans up to $3.3 billion in improvements across mines in Brazil and Canada to boost copper output by about 5% and nickel by about 10% by 2026. The Sudbury initiatives focus on reducing idle capacity. Gains are projected into later years, so near-term price impact is limited.

title: Vale to spend billions to boost copper and nickel output, report says
summary: Vale plans up to $3.3 billion in improvements at its Brazil and Canada operations to boost copper and nickel capacity, including initiatives to reduce idle capacity at its Sudbury mine-mill. Vale projects output increases by 2026 and further expansion by 2028, but timing suggests limited immediate impact on near-term prices.

title: Surge Copper Announces Closing of Private Placement for $2.2M
summary: Surge Copper Corp. closed a C$2.2M non-brokered private placement of flow-through shares to fund Canadian exploration expenditures through 2025 for its Berg and Ootsa projects. The release does not cite production changes or supply disruptions, so it is unlikely to move near-term copper prices materially.

title: Premium Nickel Resources Announces Closing of Second Tranche of Private Placement of Units for Total Offering of C$27.5 Million
summary: Premium Nickel Resources closed a C$27.5 million private placement, using proceeds to fund ongoing underground infill drilling and surface drilling at Selebi and other projects in Botswana. The company says resource estimates are on track for release soon, supporting future development of its nickel and copper sulphide assets.

title: The mad scramble for copper
summary: The piece argues copper is in short supply and highlights near-term disruptions across major producing regions: Panama’s Cobre Panama closure, labor stoppages at Peru’s Las Bambas, reduced output/scheduled maintenance at Chile’s Los Bronces, drought-related production risks in Chile and Zambia, and weaker concentrate availability that may force smelter cuts.

title: Alcoa Corporation (AA): Will Its Alumina Limited Acquisition Make It Soar Even More?
summary: The article discusses Alcoa’s plans and reports progress after its strategic acquisition of Alumina Limited. It cites alumina production and shipping guidance and notes an upbeat analyst outlook. Since Alcoa is a key bauxite/alumina producer, the deal could modestly improve near-term expectations for aluminum feedstock supply.

title: Senate inquiry sought into Avebury Nickel Mine closure | The Advocate
summary: A Tasmanian businessman urges a Senate inquiry into the circumstances leading to the closure of the Avebury nickel mine. He argues an earlier bid could have kept operations running, but Mallee collapsed and the restart would take at least a year, with major capital needed and no current near-term production.

title: Global primary aluminium output in May soars to over 6m tonnes
summary: The page title reports that global primary aluminium output in May surged to over 6 million tonnes. If production is indeed higher than expected, it can increase near-term supply availability and weigh on aluminium prices, particularly over the following days and weeks as market balance shifts.

title: Chinese Copper Exports Are Flooding Global Markets
summary: Bloomberg customs data show May Chinese unwrought copper exports more than doubled to about 150,000 tons, reaching a level not seen since 2012. With exporters easing and export arbitrage continuing via bonded warehouses, analysts expect copper prices to stay under pressure unless China adds stimulus or smelters cut output.

title: Japan Starts Mining Cobalt And Nickel In Its Economic Zone In 2026
summary: Japan plans to begin producing cobalt and nickel in 2026 from deep-water ferromanganese nodules near the Ogasawara Islands. The estimated reserves could cover Japan’s cobalt demand for 75 years and nickel for 11 years. The project would involve foreign extraction technology and commercial supplies to Japanese users.

title: Chinese-funded aluminum industrial park will boost Angola's economic diversification: official
summary: Angola’s government says a Chinese-backed Huatong Aluminum Industrial Park will create an alumina-to-aluminium value chain, including electrolytic aluminum production. The first phase targets 120,000 tons annually and is expected to start in 2H 2025, with larger capacity planned across five phases over 8–10 years.

title: Chinese-funded aluminum industrial park will boost Angola's economic diversification: official-Xinhua
summary: Xinhua reports Angola’s groundbreaking of the Huatong Aluminum Industrial Park, backed by Chinese investors, with a planned first phase producing 120,000 tons/year of electrolytic aluminum from 2H 2025. The project covers alumina preparation, electrolysis, and aluminum products, aiming to boost industrialization and jobs, but near-term supply effects are limited.

title: Caution urged over copper broadband switch-off
summary: Ireland’s telecom regulator ComReg and operator SIRO are urging careful planning ahead of a future copper broadband switch-off, noting many devices (alarms, security monitors, emergency phones, etc.) rely on the copper network. The process is contingent on widespread fibre-to-the-home availability, making near-term copper price effects likely limited.

title: Calls for taskforce to prepare for copper broadband switch-off
summary: Siro urged creation of a taskforce to prepare for the EU-approved shutdown of copper broadband. ComReg has approved commencement and estimates millions of premises still connected. Siro warns security alarms and terminals may be affected, while Eir plans to migrate to avoid maintaining two networks.

title: Copper inches lower as traders assess dull China demand, strong dollar
summary: Copper futures inched lower as traders weighed a firmer dollar and concerns over dull demand from China. The piece cites rising SHFE copper stocks to 322,910 tons, suggesting ample supply. Aluminium slipped on the day, while nickel was slightly higher/lower across venues, reflecting mixed broader metal sentiment.

title: Commodity super-cycle: Copper junior with gold and silver kicker chomping at the bits!
summary: The piece promotes Prismo Metals and claims a copper “super-cycle” is emerging based on geopolitical and market trends, projecting a strongly bullish copper outlook. It highlights expected soon copper drill permits for the Hot Breccia project, along with parallel silver and gold exploration, framing positive near-term sentiment for copper.

title: Roll-out of Integrated Copper Strategy in Zambia | Company Announcement
summary: Jubilee Metals Group announced completion of civil/mechanical construction for the Roan copper upgrade with commissioning testing underway and ramp-up planned for July 2024. It also acquired two operating near-surface open-pit copper mines to expand feed for its expanded Sable refinery, supporting higher copper output targets in 2024.

title: LMEWEEK-Funds to retrench, magnifying copper's losses
summary: Reuters reports that sluggish Chinese demand and soaring copper inventories are likely to prompt funds to reduce speculative long exposure, adding pressure to prices. Copper has fallen sharply from recent highs amid weak property and manufacturing activity, with LME and SHFE warehouse stocks surging, keeping near-term bias bearish unless demand improves.

title: Copper steadies but spotlight remains on China demand
summary: Copper steadied but remained pressured by weak demand in top consumer China and a sharp increase in LME-approved warehouse deliveries, with LME stocks up over 60% since mid-May. The cash-to-three-month discount stays near record levels. Nickel also eased on rising LME stocks, while aluminium slid slightly.

title: Green Bridge Metals Acquires Option on World Class Copper-Nickel Exploration Portfolio in Duluth Complex Minnesota
summary: Green Bridge Metals said it acquired an option to earn an 80% interest in the South Contact Zone copper-nickel exploration project in Minnesota, funded by a June 19 private placement. The news is an exploration-stage development with no immediate production or market flow changes cited.

title: Grid Metals Corp. Files National Instrument 43-101 Technical Report for MM Copper/Nickel Project in Southeastern Manitoba
summary: Grid Metals filed its NI 43-101 technical report for an updated resource estimate at its MM copper/nickel project in Manitoba, describing contained copper and nickel resources and planned exploration drilling. The announcement is resource-technical and not tied to immediate production or supply changes, so near-term price impact is limited.

title: Adani, Hindalco show interest as Hindustan Copper plans to develop two mines, source says
summary: India’s state-owned Hindustan Copper plans to develop two copper mines in Jharkhand, with combined capacity of 3 million tonnes, after one mine (Rakha) has been closed for decades. Adani Enterprises and Hindalco reportedly attended a pre-bid conference, but no production changes are immediate, limiting short-term price impact.

title: Grid Metals Corp. Files National Instrument 43-101 Technical Report for MM Copper/Nickel Project in Southeastern Manitoba
summary: Grid Metals filed an updated NI 43-101 technical report for its MM copper/nickel project in Manitoba, detailing revised mineral resource estimates for Makwa (nickel-dominant) and Mayville (copper-dominant). The company plans exploration drilling to expand resources, but no immediate supply or market-altering development is announced.

title: Friedland, McEwen back Power Nickel's oversubscribed $20M funding
summary: Power Nickel closed an oversubscribed $20M financing to fund expanded drilling on its Nisk nickel property in Quebec, supported by Canadian critical-mineral tax credits. The company says results extend mineralization beyond nickel/cobalt to copper and other metals, which is sentiment-supportive for nickel and modestly for copper, though no near-term production change is indicated.

title: Eramet and BASF decide against joint investment in a nickel-cobalt refining complex in Indonesia
summary: Eramet and BASF decided not to proceed with a joint investment in a proposed nickel-cobalt refining complex in Indonesia’s Weda Bay. Eramet will continue evaluating other nickel-related investments, including the EV battery value chain. The cancellation affects expectations for incremental nickel refining capacity in coming years.

title: Copper eases on subdued Chinese demand and inventories jump
summary: Copper prices eased as China’s demand lagged and LME-approved warehouse deliveries rose sharply, pushing inventories higher. Cash copper traded at a record discount, reflecting limited supply concerns but weaker physical balance. Funds also shifted with dollar moves, while nickel and aluminium were also mixed.

title: LMEWEEK-Aluminium prices under pressure, but brighter prospects on the horizon
summary: Reuters reports aluminium prices are under pressure due to weak global manufacturing, but the physical market remains tight. In China, an expected deficit and shortages of bauxite/alumina feedstocks should support prices. Rising duty-paid premiums in the US and Europe, alongside supply constraints from sanctions and Red Sea logistics hurdles, underpin a bullish outlook.

title: BASF Won't Invest in Nickel-Cobalt Refining Complex in Indonesia
summary: BASF said it will not invest in a planned nickel-cobalt refining complex in Weda Bay, Indonesia, citing major changes in the global nickel market, including evolving supply options and the availability of battery-grade nickel. BASF now sees less need for the large capex to secure battery materials supply.

title: BASF to Exit $2.6 Billion Nickel Smelter Project in Indonesia
summary: BASF said it will exit its $2.6 billion nickel smelter project in Indonesia. The move likely reduces planned nickel refining capacity and can worsen expectations for future supply balance. With refining bottlenecks relevant to market tightness, the news is generally negative for nickel price sentiment near term.

title: Aluminum Prices Face Downward Pressure Amid Oversupply Concerns
summary: Aluminum prices are falling as oversupply concerns grow. The article points to China’s post–dry-season production rebound (Yunnan smelters returning, output at a two-year high) and a sharp rise in LME inventories, including large Trafigura shipments. It also notes copper-led declines across base metals and rate-linked demand pressure.

title: McEwen Copper Announces $70 Million Financing to Advance the Los Azules Copper Project
summary: McEwen Mining announces up to US$70 million in financing for its wholly owned McEwen Copper subsidiary to advance the Los Azules copper project in Argentina, including work toward a bankable feasibility study scheduled for Q1 2025. The funding supports longer-run copper supply development, aiding copper sentiment.

title: BASF Exits $2.6 Billion Nickel Project as EV Demand Eases (1)
summary: BASF said it is exiting its $2.6 billion battery-quality nickel project, noting improved global availability since the project began. It also pointed to easing EV demand, alongside BloombergNEF cutting battery-electric sales estimates, which together suggest reduced near-term nickel demand and supply expectations.

title: Copper edges higher; strong dollar and low China demand check gains
summary: Copper futures edged slightly higher, but gains were checked by a stronger U.S. dollar and subdued demand prospects in top consumer China. The piece also notes small daily moves in LME aluminium and nickel, with market participants expecting thinner summer volumes and prices to stay range-bound near term.

title: New Zealand Aluminium Smelters keeping an open mind on re-opening fourth potline at Tiwai Point
summary: New Zealand Aluminium Smelters is considering whether to re-open a fourth potline at its Tiwai Point smelter, which has been shut since early 2020 due to Covid-19. The statement suggests potential supply normalization from restart plans, which could weigh on aluminium prices in the coming weeks.

title: Tennant hammers NT copper-gold with one-two drill combo
summary: Tennant Minerals announced a two-stage drill program at its Barkly project targeting extensions to the Bluebird copper-gold discovery, with multiple high-grade copper intersections and strong metallurgical results. The company aims to grow the resource and progress toward a standalone development project, supporting copper bullish sentiment.

title: Faraday Copper Intersects 20.07 m at 1.20% Copper within 100.29 m at ...
summary: The release title indicates Faraday Copper intersected a 20.07 m interval grading 1.20% copper within a broader drill run (up to about 100.29 m). This is copper-exploration information that can influence longer-term project expectations, but it is unlikely to materially move near-term copper prices by itself.

title: Copper steady, but China demand angst dominates mood
summary: Copper steadied briefly on a softer dollar, but traders expect ongoing downside pressure. China’s weak manufacturing and sluggish property sector undermine demand, while LME inventories have surged to a six-month high and surpluses widen discounts. Copper likely trades in a $9,500–$9,900 range until new China data.

title: Faraday Copper Intersects 20.07 m at 1.20% Copper within 100.29 m at 0.42% Copper in the American Eagle Area
summary: Faraday Copper reported drill results from its Copper Creek Project in Arizona, including near-surface copper intercepts (e.g., 20.07 m at 1.20% Cu). Management says results support higher open-pit resource potential and ongoing Phase III drilling. The release is copper-focused with no clear nickel or aluminium linkage.

title: China's refined copper exports surge to 8-year peak and high exports continue
summary: China exported 73,860 tonnes of refined copper in May, nearly tripling from April and reaching an eight-year high, with ongoing exports expected in June. Smelters and traders sell into an export arbitrage window as LME copper rises, reflecting strong supply and slower domestic demand.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Identifies 30km Awaruite Nickel Trend From Data Compilation at its Atlantic Nickel Project in Central Newfoundland
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reports completion of a large-scale data compilation at its Atlantic Nickel Project in Newfoundland, identifying a 30 km trend of consistently anomalous nickel (awaruite) concentrations and outlining priority exploration targets for 2024 drilling. The update expands geological knowledge but provides no near-term supply impact.

title: Brixton Metals Begins Drilling at its Cirque Copper Porphyry Target
summary: Brixton Metals announced the start of its first drilling campaign at the Cirque copper porphyry target on its Thorn Project. The company cites surface chalcopyrite occurrences, elevated Cu geochemistry, and supportive geophysics, with some historic quartz-chalcopyrite samples grading 1.6% Cu. Assays from new sampling are pending.

title: Builders' Merchants News - Low-carbon heating systems mandatory in new-build homes from 2025: Where does copper piping fit in?
summary: UK’s Future Homes Standard will require low-carbon heating systems in new-build homes from 2025. The piece promotes copper piping as a suitable, recyclable material for heat pumps and solar thermal/water heating, citing efficiency and durability. It implies higher residential copper demand, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Corcel acquires Willow Copper Property in Canada
summary: Corcel Exploration acquired the Willow Copper Property in north-central British Columbia, near the Sustut Copper Deposit, and cited historical rock-sample copper grades up to 6.28. The firm plans to review historical data and conduct potential fieldwork, extending related exploration commitments via an option amendment.

title: Eramet, BASF abandon Indonesia nickel-cobalt refining project
summary: Eramet and BASF have abandoned their planned Weda Bay, Indonesia nickel-cobalt refining complex, citing slower EV sales growth and a changed global nickel market. BASF will stop all project activities and says it no longer needs the investment due to evolved supply options for battery-grade nickel.

title: Brixton Metals Begins Drilling at its Cirque Copper
summary: Brixton Metals began its maiden drill program at the Cirque copper porphyry target on its Thorn Project, highlighting surface chalcopyrite mineralization and geophysical and geochemical anomalies. While results are pending, the news is broadly supportive for copper sentiment but unlikely to affect near-term physical supply or prices.

title: Emerita Intersects High Grade Copper-Gold Mineralization at
summary: Emerita Resources announced new drilling at its Iberian Belt West El Cura deposit, reporting multiple high-grade intercepts including ~1.7–1.8% copper over several meters and deepening/thickening at depth. Follow-up drilling is being accelerated with an expanded program, but no production or near-term supply changes are stated.

title: Emerita Intersects High Grade Copper-Gold Mineralization at El Cura; Mobilizes Second Rig to Accelerate El Cura Drill Program
summary: Emerita Resources reported new drilling at its El Cura VMS copper-gold deposit, including intersections of ~1.7–1.8% Cu over 2.6–10.6m and other assays with zinc-lead values. A second drill rig was mobilized and the program accelerated, potentially supporting bullish sentiment for future copper supply.

title: Aluminium use in China's NEVs to surge by 2030, but challenges exist
summary: Fastmarkets reports China’s NEV output and sales are rising fast, implying aluminium use could jump to about 10 million tonnes by 2030 versus ~2 million in 2023. NEVs require lightweighting and use aluminium in bodies, chassis, and electric systems. Higher aluminium demand may support prices despite cost and technical constraints.

title: BASF halts nickel-cobalt refining investment
summary: BASF said it will not execute a proposed nickel-cobalt refining project in Weda Bay, Indonesia, and will stop further evaluation and negotiations. The company cited significant changes in the global nickel market and reduced need for a large investment for battery-grade nickel supply. Eramet is involved in the prior assessment deal.

title: Domestic Aluminum Demand Up 4.3% in First Quarter in Signs
summary: The Aluminum Association’s monthly report shows North American aluminium demand rose 4.3% year-over-year in Q1 2024. Shipments were higher for primary ingot (+16%) and sheet/plate (+6.1%), with net new orders up 4.8% YTD through April. Some product categories fell, but overall demand improved.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Announces First Saleable Copper Concentrate at MVDP in Chile
summary: Capstone Copper said first saleable copper concentrate was produced at its Mantoverde Development Project in Chile, with commissioning milestones completed and further ramp-up to nameplate rates expected during Q3 2024. The milestone improves near-term expectations for incremental copper supply from the project.

title: Capstone Copper Announces First Saleable Copper Concentrate at MVDP in Chile
summary: Capstone Copper announced it has produced the first saleable copper concentrate from its Mantoverde Development Project in Chile. The milestone supports the project’s ramp-up toward nameplate capacity and signals increasing near-term availability of copper concentrate for sale, a development that can be mildly supportive for copper prices.

title: String of copper wire thefts in Sussex, Kent Counties under investigation
summary: Delaware State Police are investigating multiple thefts of copper wire from farm irrigation systems in Greenwood and Houston, Delaware. Copper wiring lengths reportedly range from 50 feet to several hundred feet. The incidents occurred overnight over the past month, and authorities are seeking tips to identify suspects.

title: Copper and Nickel Face Cooling Demand
summary: The piece describes falling copper and nickel prices as the leading drivers of a July decline in the NAS 304 stainless surcharge. It notes nickel has fallen sharply since May and remains oversupplied with LME inventories rising. A short-term bearish outlook is emphasized, with rallies from Q2 fading.

title: Copper and Nickel Face Cooling Demand
summary: Nickel prices peaked in May and then fell sharply, with the NAS 304 stainless surcharge also retreating in July. The article attributes the surcharge decline mainly to weaker copper and nickel, noting bearish short-term outlooks, unraveling speculative rallies, and nickel oversupply outweighing potential supply-disruption fears.

title: 'Crimes of opportunity' | Louisville police say thieves target AC units for copper, other metals
summary: Louisville police say thieves are targeting copper-containing parts in rooftop AC units, causing businesses like an ice cream shop to close temporarily while HVAC components are replaced. The report cites similar copper wire thefts elsewhere in Kentucky and Indiana, and police advise security measures, with no suspects identified yet.

title: Copper stocks surge offers little relief for CME shorts: Andy Home
summary: LME and ShFE copper inventories have surged, with LME stocks rising above 500,000 tons and Chinese exports to LME reaching multi-year highs. This stock build coincides with LME pricing slipping below $10,000 and widening contango, pointing to supply overhang. COMEX inventories remain tight, but US relief is delayed.

title: Capstone Copper Corp. Announces First Saleable Copper Concentrate at MVDP in Chile
summary: Capstone Copper reported first saleable copper concentrate from its Mantoverde Development Project in Chile, confirming commissioning progress and the transition toward ramping to nameplate operating rates expected in Q3 2024. This points to improving future copper supply from the project as it moves through key milestones.

title: Copper edges lower on dollar strength, weak China demand outlook
summary: Reuters reports copper futures edged lower as a firmer dollar and weak demand expectations from China weighed on the market. It also points to poor manufacturing data and rising inventories for metals such as aluminium, copper and nickel, reinforcing bearish near-term sentiment across these industrial metals.

title: Metso Outotec Oyj : to deliver cathode stripping machines to two copper plants in South America
summary: Metso Outotec will deliver cathode stripping machines to Southern Peru Copper’s Ilo electrorefinery and Toquepala electrowinning plants in Peru. The order exceeds EUR 10 million and is booked in 2024 Q2 Minerals orders. The equipment will replace/upgrade cathode handling to support stable copper cathode production and efficiency.

title: ENEOS : Notice regarding transfer of partial shares in SCM Minera Lumina Copper Chile, Operator of Caserones Copper Mine（PDF：196.8 KB）
summary: ENEOS Holdings says JX Advanced Metals will transfer 19% of its shares in SCM Minera Lumina Copper Chile (operator of Chile’s Caserones copper mine) to a subsidiary of Lundin Mining, increasing Lundin’s stake to 70%. The company expects no material consolidated earnings impact, suggesting limited short-term influence on copper supply expectations.

title: GCC Aluminium Industry Report 2023-2024: Market to Witness a Surge in Demand
summary: ResearchAndMarkets preview of a GCC aluminium report says the region is well-positioned for a surge in aluminium demand, citing planned high-rise construction and broad end-use demand. The study estimates market size using local smelter capacities and LME aluminium price trends, implying supportive sentiment for aluminium prices in coming weeks.

title: Copper rises for the first session in four on algorithm-driven buying
summary: Copper prices rose modestly as algorithm-driven funds bought after a four-session drop, but gains were capped by concerns over China’s weak physical demand, rising LME inventories, and a stronger dollar. LME cash-to-3-month spreads widened sharply. Nickel edged up; aluminium slightly declined.

title: Copper concentrate price data and news
summary: Fastmarkets reports production problems reducing global mine output and forcing smelters to scramble for copper concentrates. Strong concentrate demand drives TC/RCs to record lows, while refined copper prices are at all-time highs on the LME. It also notes new supply deals and shipments affecting concentrate flows and pricing dynamics.

title: Capstone produces first copper concentrate at MVDP project in Chile
summary: Capstone said it has produced first copper concentrate at its MVDP project in Chile. The milestone suggests the mine is moving from development toward production, improving forward supply expectations for copper. In the near term, the price effect is likely modest because initial output volumes may be small.

title: Sterling Metals Corp.: Sterling Metals Advances Inaugural Field Exploration Campaign at the Copper Road Project
summary: Sterling Metals says Phase 1 exploration at its Copper Road copper-molybdenum project in Ontario is underway, including property-wide airborne geophysics, soil sampling, and modeling of VTEM/IP data to identify new targets. The release supports future drilling plans but does not indicate near-term supply changes impacting copper prices.

title: Sanatana Resources Inc.: Sanatana Announces Drill Program at Oweegee Copper-Gold Porphyry Project Golden Triangle, BC
summary: Sanatana Resources announced a 3,000-meter drill program at its Oweegee copper-gold porphyry project in BC, targeting a previously untested 1 km x 2 km IP anomaly. The company aims to test whether the anomaly is linked to the copper-gold mineralization seen in 2022 drill holes. No production impacts are stated.

title: Quetzal Copper Mobilizes Drill Rig to the Cristinas Project, Chihuahua Mexico
summary: Quetzal Copper began field and drill work at its Cristinas Project in Chihuahua, Mexico, including 1,500–3,000 m of drilling and downhole EM surveys to test down-dip continuity of high-grade copper intercepts. The program targets EM conductors linked to sulphide mineralization and potential expansion of resources.

title: Sanatana Announces Drill Program at Oweegee Copper-Gold Porphyry Project Golden Triangle, BC
summary: Sanatana Resources plans a 3,000-metre drill program starting mid/late July 2024 at its Oweegee copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia. The drilling targets an untested IP anomaly interpreted as likely linked to earlier Cu-Au-Ag-Mo mineralized breccias. This is exploration activity without near-term supply impact.

title: Stillwater Critical Minerals Drills Wide and High-Grade Nickel, Platinum, and Palladium Mineralization in Resource Expansion Drilling at Stillwater West in Montana, USA
summary: Stillwater Critical Minerals announced final drill results from resource-expansion work at its Stillwater West Ni-PGE-Cu-Co project in Montana. The company highlights high-grade nickel and copper sulphide intersections and broader NiEq interval potential, supported by ongoing Glencore investment and technical involvement, improving sentiment toward nickel and copper supply prospects.

title: Premium Nickel Reports 52.45 Metres of 2.02% NiEq or 3.59% CuEq (1.26% Ni, 1.17% Cu, 0.06% Co) & 35.60 Metres of 2.45% NiEq or 4.35% CuEq (1.54% Ni, 1.38% Cu, 0.08% Co) at Selebi North Underground
summary: Premium Nickel Resources reported additional high-grade Ni-Cu-Co drill intercepts at the past-producing Selebi North underground mine in Botswana and said these are the last holes for its initial NI 43-101 compliant Mineral Resource Estimate, expected soon. The release implies continued resource confidence but no immediate production or market supply impact.

title: Africa Finance Corporation (AFC)  / Press release | Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) invests in Africa's largest copper complex, driving mineral beneficiation on the continent
summary: Africa Finance Corporation closed a US$150 million senior loan to Kamoa Copper for Phase 3 expansion of the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The project targets a 33% increase in capacity to over 600,000 tpa and includes a large copper smelter and renewed hydro power generation.

title: EQS-News: Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) invests in Africa's largest copper complex, driving mineral beneficiation on the continent
summary: Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) closed a US$150 million senior loan to expand the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC. Phase 3 includes a 33% production-capacity increase to over 600,000 tpa and construction of a large smelter. The project also restarts hydro power generation to support operations.

title: BASF decides against investment in nickel-cobalt refining complex in Indonesia
summary: BASF said it will not proceed with its nickel-cobalt refining complex in Weda Bay, Indonesia, citing a changing global nickel market and evolving supply options for battery-grade nickel. The company will stop ongoing negotiations and evaluations, lowering expected incremental refining supply for nickel.

title: Vedanta in talks with IHC unit, investors for Zambian copper stake sale
summary: Vedanta is in talks with IRH (an IHC unit) and other investors over buying into its Zambian KCM copper assets. The stake sale aims to raise about $1.2 billion to revive operations and boost copper output, while Vedanta seeks to retain a majority stake and use funds to settle creditors.

title: Lundin Mining to up stake in Caserones copper mine to 70%
summary: Lundin Mining will raise its ownership of Chile’s Caserones copper-molybdenum mine to 70% by buying an additional 19% for $350 million. The move increases its exposure to the mine’s expected 120,000–130,000 tonnes of annual copper output and boosts operator-related cash flows under a revised agreement.

title: BASF to cancel $2.6 billion nickel-cobalt refining project in Indonesia
summary: BASF said it will cancel its $2.6 billion Indonesia nickel-cobalt refining project, citing growing battery-grade nickel options and near-term oversupply in the nickel market. The planned HPAL/BMR unit would have supplied nickel for nickel sulfate production. Cancellation may tighten expectations for nickel intermediates supply.

title: Parliament ratifies Ghana Bauxite Company's mining lease
summary: Ghana’s parliament unanimously ratified the mining lease for Ghana Bauxite Company’s Awaso bauxite mine. The government links the project to building an integrated aluminium industry via GIADEC, including plans to expand the mine and develop a refinery to refine local bauxite, supporting jobs and socio-economic benefits.

title: Small businesses facing a new threat—copper thieves tearing apart their AC units
summary: A local ice cream shop in Louisville closed after thieves tore apart its rooftop AC unit and stripped copper wiring. The post highlights growing theft risk for small businesses and suggests scrap value incentives, but it does not provide evidence of large-scale copper supply or inventory changes affecting near-term copper prices.

title: Exclusive-Codelco copper output falls behind target in May, document shows
summary: Reuters reports that Chile’s Codelco produced 103,100 tonnes of copper in May, 8.6% below its target of 112,800, and remained 6.1% behind target in the first five months. Output challenges follow an incident-related stoppage and delays, sustaining near-term copper supply concerns.

title: Copper Fox Announces Upsize to Non-Brokered Private Placement
summary: Copper Fox Metals upsized a non-brokered private placement to C$1.125 million, issuing shares and warrants, and says proceeds will fund exploration and development at its copper projects (Van Dyke, Eaglehead, Mineral Mountain, Sombrero Butte, and interests in Schaft Creek). The release is a financing update without immediate supply impact.

title: Bahrain Business: Aluminium rod maker makes foray into food security push
summary: Conexus Resources says its Konexus Aluminium International subsidiary has started a $100m aluminium rod plant in Bahrain, processing liquid aluminium from Alba with 32,000 tpa capacity. The firm frames expansion as downstream aluminium and includes partial solarisation plans, but no clear immediate global aluminium market shock is cited.

title: Trading ideas: IJM, Samaiden, CN Asia, Kuchai, Sapura Energy, Amanah REIT, Hextar Industries, IHH, Poh Huat, LB Aluminium, Northern Solar, Well Chip
summary: The recap includes corporate updates, notably LB Aluminium reporting a 62.7% year-on-year rise in 4QFY24 net profit to RM9.43mn, citing higher contributions from both its aluminium and property segments. Other items are mainly unrelated to industrial metals or are solar/office related.

title: Copper hovers near two-month low as demand woes linger
summary: Copper futures hover near a two-month low as lingering demand worries and uncertainty about China’s recovery weigh on prices. A firmer US dollar limits buying interest. TD Securities cites surging copper inventories in China and low local premiums, indicating weak physical demand support for copper rallies.

title: Freeport Indonesia launches $3.7 bln Gresik copper smelter
summary: Freeport Indonesia launched its $3.7 billion Gresik copper smelter in East Java. The plant has 1.7 million tonnes of annual copper-concentrate input capacity and is expected to produce about 650,000 tonnes of copper cathode, plus small quantities of gold, boosting Indonesia’s refined output potential.

title: MPs laud Lands Minister for ratifying Ghana Bauxite Company's mining lease
summary: Ghana’s parliament unanimously ratified a new mining lease for the Awaso bauxite mine operated by Ghana Bauxite Company. The lease is tied to government plans for an integrated aluminium industry, including expansion and refinery development. The decision enables operations, jobs, and potential future aluminium supply and investment.

title: Freeport Indonesia launches $3.7 bln Gresik copper smelter to meet renewables demand
summary: Freeport Indonesia launched its $3.7 billion Gresik copper smelter, targeting 650,000 tons of copper cathode capacity. First production is due in August at 50% rates, reaching full output in December. The project supports Indonesia’s post-export-ban smelting requirements, with permits and extension discussions ongoing.

title: Freeport Indonesia Launches $3.7 Billion Gresik Copper Smelter
summary: Freeport Indonesia launched its $3.7 billion Gresik copper smelter in East Java. The plant is designed to process 1.7 million tonnes of copper concentrate annually and produce about 650,000 tonnes of copper cathode, along with gold output. The expansion targets greater domestic processing capacity for copper feedstock.

title: BASF and Eramet Withdraw from $2.6 Billion Nickel Smelter Project in Weda Bay
summary: BASF and Eramet canceled a $2.6 billion nickel-cobalt refining project in Weda Bay, citing significant changes in the global nickel market and sufficient/altered supply options for battery-grade nickel. The withdrawal reduces incremental future refining capacity expectations, potentially supporting near-term nickel prices.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Appoints World-Renowned Economic
summary: First Atlantic Nickel Corp. appointed a nickel-iron (awaruite) technical advisor and a strategic capital-markets advisor and reported a $2.1 million financing to support a planned 5,000m drilling campaign at its Atlantic Nickel Project in Newfoundland. The update is sentiment-supportive for nickel but lacks immediate supply impact.

title: Copper slips to more than two-month low on high stocks and weak demand
summary: Copper prices fell to a more than two-month low as LME inventories rose above 500,000 tonnes, bullish positions were unwound, and Chinese demand stayed weak. Data showed slowing industrial profit growth in China and rising local inventories/premiums staying low. Aluminium slipped, while nickel rose modestly.

title: Vedanta in talks for Zambian copper stake sale
summary: Vedanta is in talks with IRH (IHC subsidiary) and other investors to buy stakes in its Zambian copper mines (KCM). The deal is part of Vedanta’s plan to raise ~$1.2bn to rejuvenate operations and secure funding to settle KCM debts, boosting near-term copper supply prospects.

title: Spot activity slows across global copper market
summary: Spot activity for copper cathodes is limited as traders leave for LME Asia Week and sentiment stays subdued. Sources cite weak China demand, quiet European conditions, disrupted European import liquidity, and high borrowing costs. Copper cathode premiums are mostly unchanged, while LME copper inventories surged 51% in June, weighing on prices.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd: Aston Bay Announces Planned Exploration Program at its Epworth Sediment Hosted Copper-Silver-Zinc-Cobalt Project, Nunavut, Canada
summary: Aston Bay announced a planned 2024 exploration program at its Epworth copper-silver-zinc-cobalt project in Nunavut, funded by over $2 million in flow-through money. The work includes a large airborne TDEM/magnetic survey plus mapping and sampling to define drill targets. No production or immediate supply changes were reported.

title: LNG plan for Guinea to fuel alumina exports [Gas in Transition]
summary: Guinea’s government is exploring an LNG build-out to fuel a new alumina refining sector, aiming to expand alumina exports. By improving energy supply for refining, the plan could lower costs and support alumina/aluminium production economics, which may translate into modest near-term bullish sentiment for aluminium markets.

title: TNR Gold Corp.: TNR Gold NSR Royalty Update - Los Azules Copper, Gold and Silver Project - McEwen Copper Announces $70 Million Financing
summary: TNR Gold says it holds a 0.4% NSR royalty on the Los Azules copper project in Argentina. The operator, McEwen Copper, announced a US$70 million private placement financing to fund work toward a bankable feasibility study scheduled for end-Q1 2025. No direct near-term market supply impacts are stated.

title: TNR Gold NSR Royalty Update - Los Azules Copper, Gold and Silver Project - McEwen Copper Announces $70 Million Financing
summary: TNR Gold discloses an update from McEwen Mining on the Los Azules project in Argentina, where TNR holds a royalty interest. McEwen Copper announced a US$70m private placement financing to advance a bankable feasibility study for the copper deposit, supporting development prospects.

title: Vale expects to regain Onca Puma and Sossego copper mine licences
summary: Vale says it has reached a deal with the state of Para to reinstate operating licenses for its Onca Puma nickel mine and Sossego copper mine within 48 hours. The state had suspended licenses earlier due to environmental-report irregularities and non-compliance. Vale plans to resume operations and implement agreed socio-environmental measures.

title: Uzbek copper producer will spend $15 bln to more than double output
summary: Uzbekistan’s AGMK plans a $15 billion expansion to more than double copper cathode output to 400,000 tons per year by 2030, including upgrades to mining/ore processing and a new smelter. The company will finance the project via loans and a state development fund. Current market data suggests a yearly surplus.

title: Delayed and Penalized, Freeport's Copper Smelter Now Enters Operational Phase
summary: Freeport Indonesia began operational phase at its new copper smelter in the JIIPE Industrial Zone in Gresik, East Java. The project spans 100 hectares and involves about US$3.7 billion investment. Start of operations expands Indonesia’s copper refining capacity, which can improve supply expectations for refined copper.

title: EV Minerals Announces Strategic Entry into Copper Exploration
summary: EV Minerals announces a strategic entry into copper exploration, citing rising copper demand tied to renewable energy and electric vehicles. It also references its Quebec McNickel nickel-copper-cobalt deposit and plans to evaluate recovery methods for nickel, cobalt, and copper. No production or supply changes are announced.

title: Freeport completes US$3.7 billion copper smelter  - Companies
summary: Freeport Indonesia said it has completed a US$3.7 billion copper smelter in Gresik, expected to start producing first copper cathode in August after a six-to-10 week commissioning period. Cathode output is projected to rise to over 900,000 tonnes annually versus 300,000 tonnes, with full production by year-end.

title: U.S. GoldMining Commences Drilling at the Whistler Gold-Copper Project, Alaska
summary: U.S. GoldMining began 2024 diamond drilling at its Whistler gold-copper project in Alaska, focusing on confirmatory infill and step-out drilling at the Whistler and Raintree West deposits. The release highlights gold-copper mineralization and planned delineation, but does not indicate any immediate copper production or supply disruption.

title: Freeport Indonesia opens $3.7bn copper smelter in Gresik
summary: Freeport Indonesia commissioned its $3.7bn Gresik copper smelter in East Java. The plant targets about 650,000 tonnes of copper cathode, ramping from half capacity by August 2024 to full output by December. It supports Indonesia’s raw-mineral export ban timeline via extended concentrate permits.

title: Sonoran Desert Copper Corporation Successful Remediation Testing Results on Brazil Copper Slag Tailings
summary: Sonoran Desert Copper Corporation reports successful TCLP results for remediation testing of copper slag tailings in Brazil, with leaching below detection limits/landfill standards. The company plans to commercialize its polymer remediation solution. Financing details are included, but no immediate impact on copper supply or traded inventories is stated.

title: Camino Minerals Corp.: Camino and Nittetsu Secure Exclusive Rights to Negotiate Copper Mine Acquisition in Chile
summary: Camino Minerals and Nittetsu secure exclusive rights to negotiate the acquisition of the construction-ready Puquios copper project in Chile. The proposed 50:50 JV includes 50% shared copper off-take, with financing and approvals pending. Because it targets near-term production potential, sentiment for copper may improve despite conditional timelines.

title: Miners seek answer to pressing question: Why do nickel prices 'suck'?
summary: The piece argues nickel prices are falling because supply and demand are not matching. Higher inflation and sluggish growth reduced commodity demand, creating surpluses. It also cites a flood of Indonesian nickel increasing supply. Uncertainty about EV nickel chemistry adds demand-side doubt.

title: Indonesia pledges nickel industry decarbonisation as social and biodiversity concerns linger
summary: Indonesia, producing nearly half the world’s nickel, is pursuing aggressive downstreaming and plans a nickel decarbonisation roadmap to cut emissions from smelting. Regulatory debates—including captive coal plants being classified as “green”—and concerns over biodiversity and governance raise uncertainty, but no immediate production disruption or clear price-moving event is specified.

title: London copper set for biggest monthly fall since May 2023
summary: London copper firmed on the day but was on track for its biggest monthly fall since May 2023, down nearly 5% in June. The decline was attributed to patchy economic growth in China, weak demand concerns, higher inventories, and uncertainty over U.S. interest rates.

title: Norsk Hydro : Hydro pursuing zero-carbon aluminium by testing green hydrogen technology with global potential
summary: Norsk Hydro says it is piloting green hydrogen in aluminium recycling at its Høyanger facility, replacing natural gas for one remelting furnace. The pilot is supported by Norwegian funding and aims to develop fuel-switch technology, improve metal quality, and reduce CO2 footprints of recycled aluminium, potentially supporting future low-carbon aluminium demand.

title: Copper rebounds on rate cut hopes, technical buying
summary: Copper prices rose on the LME on June 28, supported by hopes of U.S. rate cuts ahead of the PCE inflation release and technical buying after price held above $9,480. The piece notes copper’s June weakness but highlights near-term upside from a softer-rate outlook catalyst.

title: RT to install carbon free aluminium smelting cells | Company Announcement
summary: Rio Tinto will install carbon-free aluminium smelting cells using ELYSIS technology at its Arvida smelter in Québec, backed by state and company investment. The demonstration facility aims to produce up to 2,500 tonnes/year by 2027 with GHG-free primary aluminium. Commissioning of larger prototype cells is underway in 2024.

title: Rio Tinto to install carbon free aluminium smelting cells using first ELYSISTM technology licence
summary: Rio Tinto will deploy ELYSIS’ carbon-free aluminium smelting cells at its Arvida smelter in Québec, with a demonstration plant designed to produce up to 2,500 tonnes/year. The project is supported by Québec and aims to strengthen low-carbon aluminium output, potentially supporting aluminium demand sentiment and pricing.

title: Arizona Supreme Court gives Resolution Copper a win in wastewater discharge appeal
summary: Arizona’s Supreme Court ruled in favor of Resolution Copper regarding its wastewater discharge appeal. The decision lowers legal/regulatory uncertainty around water disposal for the copper project, reducing the risk of operational disruptions and potentially supporting short-term expectations for copper supply.

title: John West tuna introduces recyclable aluminium strip in industry collaboration
summary: John West, via collaborations with Schubert Packaging Systems, CCL Label and Touch Design, introduced a recyclable aluminium strip to replace plastic shrink wrap in ambient tuna multipacks. The Smartstrip stays attached to the can and is kerbside recyclable in the UK. The change is positioned as reducing plastic use and emissions.

title: Billionaire Agarwal Set to Regain Control of Zambia Copper Mine
summary: The piece’s headline says billionaire Agarwal is set to regain control of a copper mine in Zambia. A shift in ownership can influence expectations for mine operations and copper supply. Without operational specifics, the likely near-term impact is modestly supportive for copper prices.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp.: Flying Nickel Provides Update on Acquisition of Nevada Vanadium
summary: Flying Nickel provides an update on a court-approved share arrangement to acquire Nevada Vanadium and hold an AGM vote on July 10, 2024. The transaction narrative emphasizes diversification into vanadium for energy storage, without any disclosed immediate nickel production or supply changes affecting near-term nickel markets.

title: Miners seek answer to low nickel prices
summary: Miners and analysts at PDAC discuss why nickel prices remain depressed despite expected long-term demand from electrification. They cite a demand/supply mismatch amid sluggish global growth, resulting surpluses, and rising Indonesian nickel supply that pressures producers’ margins. Investors also doubt EV nickel usage and pace of electrification.

title: Miners seek answer to low nickel prices | Elliot Lake Standard
summary: Miners and analysts say nickel prices remain weak despite expectations of rising EV-related demand. They cite a macro “economic hangover” that leaves commodities in surplus and supply challenges, including more nickel from Indonesia potentially affecting U.S. trade incentives. Funding for Canadian nickel projects is harder at current prices.

title: Miners seek answer to low nickel prices | North Bay Nugget
summary: The article examines why nickel prices have stayed weak despite forecasts of rising EV-related demand. Analysts cite a demand-supply mismatch from sluggish growth and surpluses, plus a flood of Indonesian nickel affecting eligible demand. It also notes investor uncertainty about nickel use and difficulty raising project finance.

title: Miners seek answer to low nickel prices | Mid-North Monitor
summary: The article explains why nickel prices remain weak despite expectations of rising EV-related demand. It cites global demand softness causing surpluses, “downward pressure” on commodity prices, and a reported surge of Indonesian nickel supply that increases oversupply. It highlights funding difficulties for nickel projects under current prices.

title: Miners seek answer to low nickel prices | Cochrane Times-Post
summary: The piece says nickel prices have fallen sharply in 2023-2024 despite rising long-term EV expectations. Analysts cite weaker global demand and resulting surpluses, plus increased Indonesian nickel supply, which has pressured the market and made projects harder to finance. It suggests nickel remains under downward pressure for now.

title: LMEWEEK-Copper the most bullish base metal for H2, market players say
summary: Reuters reports market participants expect copper to be the most bullish base metal in H2, citing tight concentrate/raw material supply, improving Chinese demand, and fund inflows. It highlights expectations of copper smelters cutting output and notes smelter treatment charges in Chile falling sharply, alongside possible refined destocking in July.

title: Vedanta Resources gets control of Zambian copper mine to capitalise on future copper demand for AI and EVs
summary: Vedanta Resources has taken control of Zambia’s Konkola copper mine after a court sanctioned a $250 million debt settlement and the government resolved prior disputes. Vedanta plans to invest about $1.3 billion and expand capacity to lift copper output, targeting 250,000 tons over the next few years amid rising AI/EV-driven demand expectations.

title: Alta Copper Corp.: Alta Copper Announces Annual General Meeting Voting Results
summary: Alta Copper reported voting results from its June 28, 2024 AGM, including auditor appointment and approval of an equity incentive plan. It also discusses director resignations related to Fortescue’s withheld votes and mentions potential board reconstitution to accelerate development of its Cañariaco Norte copper project in Peru.

title: Southern Copper to restart development of Peru mine on Monday -document
summary: Southern Copper will restart development of the long-delayed Tia Maria copper project in Peru on Monday, confirmed by an internal memorandum seen by Reuters. The mine had been held for years due to community and environmental concerns. The project is expected to produce about 120,000 tons of copper annually.

title: Southern Copper To Restart Development Of Tia Maria Copper Mine…
summary: Reuters says Southern Copper will restart development of the Tia Maria copper mine in Peru on Monday. The announcement points to progress toward bringing future copper supply online. Near term, the production effect is limited until output ramps, but expectations for supply are incrementally improved.

title: Harita Nickel eyes participation in national EV supply chain - Companies
summary: Harita Nickel’s president director says the company aims to stay competitive by being a low-cost nickel producer in Indonesia, leveraging coastal logistics and proximity to processing. It notes Indonesia’s expanding nickel supply has disrupted global production, including closures of processing plants abroad, while referencing declining nickel prices.

title: London copper falls on inventory pressure
summary: London LME copper eased 0.7% as LME-approved inventories rose, pressuring prices. At the same time, China’s physical demand is improving and import appetite is strengthening. However, CRU expects third-quarter upside could be limited as smelters ramp up supply after maintenance and tube-sector demand weakens seasonally. Aluminium slipped; nickel edged up.

title: Mitsubishi Materials : First Copper Concentrate Production at Mantoverde Copper Mine in Chile
summary: Mitsubishi Materials said copper concentrate production has started at its Mantoverde copper mine in Chile, where it holds a 30% interest. Construction of a concentrator is completed, ramp-up is underway, and full-scale production is expected in the second quarter. MMC also has offtake rights for 30% of output.

title: Oaktree trading house squares off against shareholders for nickel mine
summary: Commodities trader Hartree Partners, backed by Oaktree Capital, is trying to take control of Tasmanian nickel miner Mallee Resources, operator of the Avebury mine, after it entered receivership when debt payments were missed amid slumping nickel prices last September. Minority shareholders oppose the takeover attempt and claim alternatives were spurned.

title: Aluminum prices likely to fall amid poor fundamentals  | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: The report expects Chinese aluminium prices to soften, citing growing supply (resumption of electrolytic cell output), weak downstream demand in the off-season (construction materials, auto, PV) and production cuts from inspections. With profitability declining and inventory destocking slow, bearish fundamentals outweigh any demand-support efforts.

title: Rio Tinto to deploy carbon-free aluminium smelting tech in Canada
summary: Rio Tinto plans to deploy ELYSIS carbon-free aluminium smelting cells at its Arvida smelter in Québec, with a demonstration plant funded jointly with the Government of Québec. The facility would produce up to 2,500 tonnes annually and start commissioning in 2027, reinforcing low-carbon aluminium investment sentiment.

title: Vedanta set to regain control of Zambia copper asset
summary: Vedanta received Zambian court approval to regain control of the Konkola copper project after sanctioning a debt-settlement plan, including a $250m payment. The company aims to restart and expand output, potentially enabling significant copper production, after output collapsed. Discussions on stake sales also continue.

title: Rio Tinto: strengthens position in low-carbon aluminum
summary: Rio Tinto will install carbon-free aluminium electrolysis cells at its Arvida plant in Quebec using Elysis technology, investing USD 285 million with the Quebec government. The demonstration plant targets 2,500 tonnes per year with no direct GHG emissions by 2027, supporting Rio’s low-carbon aluminium strategy rather than near-term supply changes.

title: Peruvian copper production to be flat in 2024, due to blockades and unfavourable weather conditions
