summary: BHP will temporarily suspend its Western Australia Nickel operations, including the Kwinana refinery, Kalgoorlie smelter and Mt Keith/Leinster, starting October, citing global nickel oversupply and falling prices. A transition begins July, with review by February 2027. The move reduces supply expectations from a major producer.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc and Freeport Commence Extensive Drilling a Joy Copper-Gold District, British Columbia
summary: Amarc Resources announced that two drilling rigs have started at its 100% owned JOY Cu-Au district in British Columbia, with Freeport funding an earn-in. The program targets multiple porphyry copper-gold systems identified by IP anomalies and prior drill intercepts. It’s an exploration catalyst, not a near-term supply change.

title: Fathom Nickel Inc.: Fathom Announces Mal Lake Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Mineralization - Further Evidence of Blue Sky Potential at Company's Gochager Lake Property
summary: Fathom Nickel reports review of historic Mal Lake core showing nickel-copper-cobalt sulphide mineralization, with pXRF scans indicating elevated Ni and Cu and possible Co tenor similar to its Gochager Lake deposit. The company plans further drilling next winter, but no production or inventory changes are announced.

title: BHP puts thousands of jobs in limbo as it suspends nickel operations amid global oversupply, plummeting prices
summary: BHP announced it will suspend nickel operations from October 2024 after a global oversupply, driven in part by Chinese-backed Indonesian output, pushed nickel prices sharply lower. The halt should reduce supply from BHP’s Nickel West assets, potentially supporting short-term nickel pricing.

title: Biden imposes 'melt and pour' requirement for Mexican steel, aluminium imports
summary: The US will apply “melt and pour” rules and increase Section 232 tariffs on Mexican steel unless processing occurs in Mexico/US/Canada, while aluminium imports from Mexico face a tariff if primary aluminium was smelted/cast in China, Russia, Belarus or Iran. US-Mexico enforcement aims to block circumvention and curb unfair metal imports.

title: Hydro, Porsche sign agreement for green aluminium in auto industry's latest effort to decarbonize
summary: Hydro and Porsche signed an agreement to supply low-carbon primary aluminium plus recycled aluminium with at least 75% post-consumer scrap, and to test using even higher recycled content. They will collaborate on new high-recycled-content alloys and integrate Hydro’s decarbonization and emission-free smelting plans into Porsche’s supply chain.

title: Zambia says China's JCHX will invest $300 mln in Lubambe copper mine
summary: Zambia said China’s JCHX plans to invest $300 million in the Lubambe Copper Mines it recently acquired. The spending is meant to extend mine life, improve a loss-making operation, and support output increases via works such as a new shaft. The announcement links directly to prospective copper supply.

title: Canada Nickel : Investor Presentation July 2024
summary: Canada Nickel’s investor presentation emphasizes a positive bankable feasibility study for its Crawford nickel sulphide project, citing strong NPV/IRR and long-life output. It also argues the nickel market remains fundamentally short outside Indonesia/China and forecasts rising demand, factors that could bolster nickel price expectations.

title: BHP to temporarily halt nickel operations in Australia
summary: BHP will temporarily suspend Western Australia Nickel operations (including the Nickel West and West Musgrave projects) from October 2024 after citing global nickel oversupply and a sharp decline in forward consensus prices. The move will pause the Kwinana refinery and smelter, with a later review and continued care-and-maintenance.

title: Sprott says new copper fund is too small to pose a market risk
summary: Sprott says its newly launched copper fund is too small to pose a market risk. The implication is that any incremental demand for copper exposure from the fund is unlikely to be large enough to sway near-term copper pricing, suggesting limited impact on market expectations over the next days to weeks.

title: Mining jobs: BHP shuts down Nickel West, threatening 3000 jobs
summary: BHP plans to temporarily suspend its Nickel West operations in Western Australia, including the Kwinana nickel refinery and Kalgoorlie smelter, affecting about 3,000 jobs. BHP cites global nickel oversupply and sharply lower forward nickel prices. The major shutdown risk could reduce near-term supply and support nickel.

title: US prioritises Aluminum sector under Uyghur Forced Labor Act while EU urged to take stronger action
summary: US authorities are prioritizing the Aluminium production sector under the Uyghur Forced Labour Prevention Act amid concerns about forced labour in Xinjiang’s aluminium industry. Human Rights Watch urged the EU to act more strongly. US enforcement could restrict or delay imports, tightening aluminium supply and supporting prices.

title: Sprott says new copper fund too small to pose a market risk
summary: Sprott launched a physical copper trust and plans to raise more capital. The fund would hold over 10,000 tonnes initially and could add about 50,000 tonnes at current prices. Sprott says its scale is too small to materially affect global copper availability, so near-term price impact should be limited.

title: Cymat's SmartMetal wins contract to supply aluminum foam kits - Canadian Manufacturing
summary: Cymat Technologies’ SmartMetal division received its first serial production order for stabilized aluminum foam underbelly kits for an Asian military vehicle manufacturer. The contract value is expected at $4M–$5M, with 24 kits initially and growth toward 350 kits over three years, targeting an estimated 700-vehicle fleet.

title: Copper Prices Bounce Back On Market Optimism
summary: Copper prices rebounded in early July as demand signals improved. China’s Yangshan premium briefly turned positive, U.S. construction power spending rose, and the EBCI strengthened. Inventories at CME looked depleted and supply remained tight. Rate-cut optimism and higher investor longs further supported bullish near-term copper prices.

title: BHP suspends nickel mining operations in Western Australia
summary: BHP announced it is suspending nickel mining operations in Western Australia. A halt in mine output typically lowers near-term nickel supply availability, raising expectations of tighter inventories and potential upward pressure on nickel prices over the following days to weeks.

title: Bonnell Aluminum Commenting on Proclamation to Strengthen the Rules to Qualify for Trade Benefits Between the U.S. and Mexico
summary: Bonnell Aluminum comments on a Biden administration proclamation that strengthens rules for aluminum to qualify for relief from U.S. Section 232 tariffs in trade with Mexico. Imports must meet “smelted and cast” criteria excluding Belarus, China, Russia and Iran. The company frames it as addressing unfair processing of subsidized metal.

title: World needs 55% more copper mines to meet EV transition goals: study
summary: A new study says electrifying transport is impractical because copper mine supply cannot match EV-driven demand. It estimates far more new copper mining is required than historically occurred, highlighting copper’s role in batteries, motors, wiring and charging infrastructure. The article supports expectations of tighter copper supply.

title: Live updates: US rate cuts likely in September after inflation falls, S&P 500 and Nasdaq drop, BHP shuts nickel business, ASX to rise
summary: BHP announced it will suspend its Australian nickel mining and smelting operations for several years, from October, citing global nickel oversupply and weaker prices. The closure triggers mixed analyst reactions: some note alternative regional processing routes, but others expect the downward nickel price trend to continue.

title: BHP to shut WA nickel operations
summary: BHP says it will shut its Western Australia nickel operations for the next few years, indicating government support for the embattled Australian nickel industry has not prevented production curtailments. The move reduces expected nickel supply, likely tightening balances and supporting higher nickel prices near term.

title: Expeditors International of Washington : DHS Publishes UFLPA Strategy with a Focus on Aluminum, PVC, and Seafood
summary: DHS published an updated UFLPA strategy identifying new high-priority enforcement sectors, including aluminum. The policy increases scrutiny of imports linked to forced labor in China, potentially causing delays, refusals, or higher compliance costs for aluminum shipments, which may disrupt near-term supply expectations for aluminum markets.

title: Copper weighed down by rising inventories, China trade data in focus
summary: Copper prices slipped as LME inventories rose to their highest since October 2021, doubling since mid-May, reflecting weaker demand and more incoming cargoes, including from China. Markets also looked to upcoming Chinese trade and metals import data, including export growth possibly linked to tariff anticipation.

title: ASX BHP: BHP nickel woes hit Lynas, Glencore in ripple effect
summary: Glencore said the outlook for its Australian nickel and cobalt operations depends on keeping labor and energy costs contained and securing infrastructure access. It is monitoring conditions around the Murrin Murrin mine in Western Australia, which employs ~1,500 people and is a major cobalt source, adding uncertainty for nickel output.

title: ANALYSIS: Difficult Future Ahead After BHP's Nickel Shutdown
summary: The analysis says BHP will mothball its WA nickel mines and processing plant for at least three years, citing oversupply in the global nickel market. The planned shutdown reduces nickel output and should support nickel prices by improving expectations for supply tightness over the coming weeks.

title: BHP suspends nickel operations until 2027
summary: BHP will suspend Nickel West operations in Western Australia—two mines plus a refinery and smelter—until at least 2027. Management attributes the decision to a global nickel oversupply, including a glut from Indonesian supply, alongside weak EV demand. The supply cut should tighten market expectations for nickel prices.

title: World would need 55 per cent more copper mines to meet EV transition goals: study
summary: A new study says EVs cannot scale without substantially more copper mining, estimating electrifying the global vehicle fleet would require 55% more new copper mines than historically mined. It attributes the gap to underinvestment in new mines, highlighting copper needs for batteries, motors and charging infrastructure.

title: China June unwrought copper imports at 436,000 metric tons
summary: China’s unwrought copper and copper product imports fell 3% year-on-year to 436,000 metric tons in June, customs data showed. Imports were up 6.8% for the first half of the year at 2.76 million tons. The monthly decline may indicate softer near-term Chinese demand for physical copper.

title: BHP to suspend Western Australia nickel operations amid Indonesia's supply glut - Companies
summary: BHP said it will temporarily suspend its Western Australia Nickel West operations and West Musgrave project from October, citing global nickel oversupply and weak economics. Management plans a review by February 2027 and continued investment for a potential restart. Nickel prices have recently recovered but remain down year-on-year.

title: China June unwrought copper imports slide to 14-month low
summary: China’s June unwrought copper imports fell to a 14-month low of 436,000 tons, down from May and earlier year levels, as high global prices and contracted manufacturing weakened demand. Slow consumption lifted SHFE stocks to a four-year peak, and weaker buying appetite likely adds bearish pressure for copper prices.

title: Braddon MP calls for West Coast Avebury Nickel Mine sale probe | The Advocate
summary: Australia’s Braddon MP urges FIRB and ASIC to investigate and potentially block the proposed sale of the Avebury nickel mine after the company Mallee Resources went into receivership and the mine closed. Shareholders argue the sale price is far below prior bids and due diligence/process were insufficient.

title: BHP's Nickel West closure could mark end of Australian nickel industry, analyst says
summary: BHP will suspend operations at its Nickel West nickel assets—Kwinana refinery, Kalgoorlie smelter and mines at Mt Keith and Leinster—impacting about 1,600 workers from October. Analysts cite oversupply, including cheaper Indonesian nickel, and expect nickel’s downward trend to continue, despite hopes of possible restart.

title: China's June imports of crude oil, unwrought copper drop y/y | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
summary: China’s June imports data showed unwrought copper imports at 436,000 mt, down about 3% y/y. Commentary cited weak demand, high inventories in China, and high copper prices discouraging purchases, alongside broader evidence manufacturers are front-loading orders ahead of potential tariffs. This supports bearish near-term copper sentiment.

title: US slaps 25% tariffs on steel and 10% on aluminium not smelted in Mexico, US or Canada
summary: The Biden administration introduced 10% tariffs on aluminium imported from Mexico when it was not smelted in Mexico, the US, or Canada, alongside 25% on steel. The measure targets Chinese-origin metal routed via Mexico. Because a portion of Mexican aluminium is smelted outside North America, supply to the US may tighten.

title: China's June imports of crude oil, unwrought copper drop y/y | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Reuters reports China’s June imports of unwrought copper fell 3% year-on-year to 436,000 mt. Analysts attribute weaker buying to poor domestic demand, high copper inventories, and high prices deterring import demand. The overall data point suggests softer near-term demand conditions for copper.

title: BHP nickel shutdown: Anthony Albanese, WA Premier Roger Cook blamed as workers drown their sorrows at Palace Hotel in Kalgoorlie
summary: Workers at Kalgoorlie’s Palace Hotel are gathering after BHP’s nickel operations were mothballed and other mines reportedly shut down. The hotel owner criticizes federal and WA governments for not acting quickly enough. The news points to an immediate nickel supply disruption risk from BHP’s operations.

title: US slaps 'symbolic' tariffs on China steel, aluminum
summary: The US imposed “symbolic” tariffs on steel and aluminum products originating from China via Mexico, closing a loophole that allowed Chinese suppliers to evade US tariffs since 2018. Aluminum imports routed this way face higher tariff costs, likely dampening demand and adding near-term bearish pressure to aluminium prices.

title: BHP's nickel shutdown is a sobering reminder of commodity fortunes
summary: BHP plans to mothball its Nickel West operations, citing discipline after losing about $50m a month and a nickel market disrupted by Chinese investment into cheaper Indonesian supply. The shutdown underscores the difficulty of sustaining production amid oversupply pressures, pointing to continued near-term downside risk for nickel prices.

title: Stanislav Kondrashov Telf AG: Mexico sets duties on steel, aluminum and ferroalloys — consequences for world markets — Пресс-релизы
summary: Mexico has introduced 20%–35% import duties on steel, aluminum sheets/coils, and ferroalloys, with exemptions for partners in Mexico’s free trade agreements. The piece highlights potential trade tensions and reduced global market stability. The aluminum tariffs are the most direct driver potentially pressuring aluminum prices in coming days.

title: Oracle Power announces copper findings at Australian project
summary: Oracle Power announced assay results showing copper mineralisation at its Blue Rock Valley Copper & Silver project in Western Australia, with reported copper grades ranging from 8.56% to 25.7%. The company plans further geophysical work for definition drilling, while also evaluating potential gold and uranium opportunities.

title: The "death knell" for the nickel industry
summary: Mining analysts say Australia’s nickel sector faces collapse and that 1,600 jobs are at risk. BHP plans to suspend operations at its nickel mines from October, citing a global nickel glut. Analysts attribute excess supply to rapid Indonesian output growth, implying tighter supply expectations going forward.

title: Prismo Metals Inc.: Prismo Metals Secures Permit Approval for Deep Drilling Program at Hot Breccia Copper Project in Arizona
summary: Prismo Metals said it received BLM permit approval for ten drill pads and has posted a bond to proceed with a planned deep 5,000-metre drilling program at its Hot Breccia copper project in Arizona. Preparatory road work will start road maintenance before drilling begins in Q3 2024.

title: Softer China demand outlook sets copper on track for a weekly loss
summary: Reuters reports copper prices edged up on Friday but were set for a weekly loss as China’s demand outlook weakened. Imports fell to a four-month low while exports rose, property stress persisted, and LME stocks remained near multi-year highs, suggesting bearish near-term pricing pressure.

title: Russia's Nornickel to restart furnace at key smelter in early August
summary: Reuters reports Nornickel will restart one of two furnaces at its Nadezhda smelter in early August after major repairs. The repairs, delayed by Western sanctions-related equipment import issues, should help stabilize the plant’s output. Nornickel is a major refined nickel producer, so this affects nickel supply expectations.

title: China's JCHX to invest $300m in Zambia's Lubambe Copper Mine
summary: JCHX Mining plans to invest $300m to revive Zambia’s Lubambe Copper Mine and extend its operational life. The underground mine holds an 80% stake by JCHX and 20% by ZCCM-IH, with new commercial terms expected. The update is a direct positive for anticipated copper supply.

title: Gold, silver and copper had a banner first half
summary: The piece says copper rose strongly in the first half of 2024 and frames the move as driven by expectations of Fed interest-rate cuts after US labor-market cooling and Powell’s comments. It argues the dollar/treasury-yield outlook is the key near-term driver for commodity prices, including copper.

title: United States Imposes Section 232 Requirements for Imports from Mexico: "Melt and Pour" for Steel; "Country of Smelt and Recent Cast" for Aluminum | White & Case LLP
summary: The US issued Section 232 proclamations for aluminum imports from Mexico, replacing prior tariff exclusions with “country of smelt” and “most recent cast” rules. If smelt/cast is linked to China, Russia, Belarus, or Iran, the 10% tariff is reinstated and the 200% Russia-related tariff can apply, effective immediately.

title: New Certification Requirements For Steel and Aluminum From Mexico To Avoid National Security Tariffs | BakerHostetler
summary: Biden’s July 10 orders introduce stricter certification and smelt/cast origin requirements for U.S. aluminum imports from Mexico to qualify for Section 232 tariff exemptions. Imports containing aluminum smelt/cast in China, Russia, Belarus, or Iran face higher duties, aimed at curbing transshipment and excess supply.

title: Lundin to pitch BHP on joint bid for copper miner Filo
summary: The piece centers on a potential bid involving BHP and Lundin for the copper miner Filo. While any acquisition could influence expectations for future copper supply, the provided information lacks deal specifics and immediate production impact, so a clear bullish or bearish near-term move is not evident.

title: Copper thieves increasingly targeting telecom equipment in Canada
summary: Global News reports rising copper telecommunications cable thefts across Canada, including cuts that disrupt Bell and Telus internet and cell service. Thieves target copper cables feeding internet and cell towers, with multiple incidents over the past seven months. Telecom firms are switching to fibre, but theft persists as copper remains expensive.

title: Workers and residents in WA Goldfields reeling over BHP's decision to mothball Nickel West operation
summary: BHP will place its Nickel West operations into care and maintenance, affecting around 1,600 workers and local towns reliant on nickel mining and refining. While communities face job losses, the market implication is reduced near-term nickel supply, which can provide short-term price support.

title: Lundin Mining, BHP weighing joint bid for copper miner Filo Corp, sources say
summary: Lundin Mining and BHP are reportedly weighing a joint bid for copper miner Filo Corp. Talks are early and may not lead to an offer, but the news lifted Filo shares. The rationale is consolidation and merging project infrastructure for Filo del Sol and Lundin’s Josemaria.

title: Expeditors International of Washington : United States and Mexico Announce Plan to Strengthen North American Steel and Aluminum Supply Chain
summary: The U.S. and Mexico announced measures to protect North American steel and aluminum markets from “unfair trade.” Mexico will raise tariffs on steel imports from non-FTA countries, while the U.S. will require melt-and-pour and smelt-and-cast processing for certain aluminum imports from Mexico, tightening eligible supply.

title: LTR BHP ASX: Liontown lithium supply test of faith for Tesla after BHP nickel halt
summary: The piece contrasts Liontown’s plan to deliver lithium to Tesla earlier with BHP’s decision to shut down nickel mines, despite a long-term supply contract. While lithium is not tracked here, the nickel halt implies curtailed production and shifting supply expectations, which can pressure nickel prices downward over the near term.

title: London copper slips on firmer dollar; China data in focus
summary: London copper fell 0.3% as the dollar firmed, reflecting reduced appeal for non-USD buyers and concerns over China demand amid high inventories. Investors awaited China GDP, retail sales and industrial output data. In parallel, LME aluminium slipped slightly and nickel edged higher, indicating mixed, limited FX-driven pressure.

title: China June aluminium output climbs on higher profits
summary: China’s primary aluminium output rose 6.2% in June to 3.67 million tonnes as producers increased runs on higher profits. Inner Mongolia added capacity and Yunnan resumed output supported by summer hydropower. Reuters cites record monthly production and higher industry margins, implying near-term supply pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Copper steadies as soft China data raises stimulus bets
summary: Copper steadied as softer China data increased bets for additional stimulus ahead of a key Communist Party meeting. While surging inventories and strong production capped gains, investors still expected improved demand. The piece also shows mild mixed moves in aluminium and nickel alongside copper as the dollar firmed.

title: Chinese Firm JCHX to Invest $300 Million in Zambia's Lubambe Copper Mine
summary: Zambia’s ZCCM-IH confirmed JCHX’s purchase of an 80% stake in the Lubambe copper mine from EMR Capital and said JCHX will invest about $300 million to operate and extend the mine. The move is aimed at boosting Zambia’s copper output and reinforces supply expectations.

title: HOCHTIEF : PYBAR to deliver underground services for Jericho Copper Mine
summary: PYBAR won a four-year underground services contract (with an optional extension) for AIC Mines’ Jericho copper deposit within the Eloise complex in Queensland. The scope includes a 3 km underground link drive and additional development for stockpiles, with mobilisation starting in July 2024 and works underway for Jericho.

title: Constellium Advances Decarbonization Efforts with the World's First Successful Industrial-Scale Production of Aluminium Slab Using Hydrogen Combustion
summary: Constellium said it completed the first industrial-scale hydrogen casting at its R&D center, producing a 12-ton aluminium slab with no observed quality impact. The hydrogen method replaces natural gas in casting and supports decarbonization efforts, with the slab slated for EV-related aluminium processing in France.

title: Atalaya Mining lowers guidance as copper grades miss expectations
summary: Atalaya Mining reported Q2 copper production fell 18% to 11,583 tonnes as grades missed expectations. The company adjusted full-year copper grade guidance down to 0.34%–0.38% from 0.39%–0.41% and reduced production estimates to 45,000–50,000 tonnes. It still expects improved grades in H2.

title: China data and inventories weigh on copper
summary: Copper prices fell as weak Chinese economic data and higher LME-approved inventories weighed on demand expectations. LME stocks rose to the highest since Oct 2021, and a firmer dollar added pressure. The article also highlights weaker aluminium pricing tied to higher China primary output and reports nickel down.

title: Osisko and Franco-Nevada Acquire a Gold Stream on SolGold's Cascabel Copper-Gold Project
summary: Osisko and Franco-Nevada entered a gold stream with SolGold tied to production from the Cascabel copper-gold project. Osisko will fund US$30m pre-construction and up to US$195m for construction (staged). The project’s 2024 PFS highlights large planned copper output, supporting copper development expectations.

title: Franco Nevada : and Osisko acquire a gold stream on SolGold's Cascabel Copper Gold Project
summary: Franco-Nevada and Osisko acquire a gold stream financing package for SolGold’s Cascabel copper-gold project in Ecuador, with $750 million total funding including pre-construction payments and staged construction funding subject to milestones and permits. The Cascabel project is described as a large copper-gold development, supported by Ecuador approvals.

title: Osisko, Franco-Nevada to Buy Gold Stream on SolGold's Cascabel Copper-Gold Project
summary: Osisko Gold Royalties and Franco-Nevada will invest $100 million initially and $650 million later to fund pre-construction and construction costs for SolGold’s Cascabel copper-gold project in Ecuador. The prefeasibility study projects multi-decade copper and gold output, but timing is future, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Taseko Mines Reports Second Quarter Copper Production and Operational Update for Gibraltar Mine
summary: Taseko reported Q2 production of 20 million pounds of copper at its Gibraltar mine, but output was impacted by concentrator downtime, maintenance at concentrator #1, and an 18-day union strike in June. Repairs resumed after the strike; concentrator #1 is ramping. Full output is expected to recover later in 2024.

title: Osisko Gold Royalties Ltd.: Osisko and Franco-Nevada Acquire a Gold Stream on SolGold's Cascabel Copper-Gold Project
summary: Osisko Gold Royalties and Franco-Nevada entered a gold stream agreement funding SolGold’s Cascabel copper-gold project in Ecuador, with US$100 million initially and additional US$650 million for development milestones. The 2024 PFS estimates multi-decade output of copper and gold, supporting progress toward copper project execution.

title: Taseko copper and molybdenum output at Gibraltar mine falls
summary: Taseko says copper and molybdenum output at its Gibraltar mine fell materially in Q2 2024. Molybdenum declined 20% and copper dropped 29% to 20 million pounds, blamed on concentrator mill downtime, maintenance, and a June workforce strike. Guidance was slightly reduced for 2H copper output.

title: Portugal's mining strategy may favour copper over lithium
summary: Portugal’s environment and energy minister said a new strategic plan for green-transition critical raw materials may give copper a more important role than lithium, highlighting copper’s relevance for electric vehicles. Portugal already has the EU’s largest copper mine and may pursue new concessions, supporting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Nornickel to restart furnace at Nadezhda Smelter in early August
summary: Nornickel says it will restart a furnace at the Nadezhda Smelter in early August after Rbs30bn repairs delayed by equipment sourcing problems under Western sanctions. The smelter is critical for refined nickel output. Separate LME and US/UK measures continue restricting Russian copper, aluminium and nickel flows.

title: Russia became leader in nickel production last year — Putin
summary: Putin said Russia became a top producer of high-grade nickel and a leading producer of aluminum last year, citing expert estimates. The statement frames ongoing development and advanced alloy production, but provides no immediate policy or operational changes that would clearly shift near-term nickel or aluminum supply expectations.

title: Teck Resources (TECK) Exits Coal to Focus on Copper, Stock Up
summary: Teck Resources sold its 77% stake in coal unit Elk Valley Resources to Glencore for $7.3 billion, planning to reduce debt and reinvest in copper. The company expects copper output to roughly double to ~600,000 tons with ramp-up at Quebrada Blanca and to fund multiple copper projects.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Announces First Shipments of Copper Concentrates to Anglo-American PLC for Smelting
summary: Battery Mineral Resources announced first shipments of copper concentrate (503.74 DMT, ~288,500 pounds of contained copper) to Anglo American’s Chagres smelter in Chile. Production at its Punitaqui flotation plant is ramping up toward 1,400 DMT per month near term, boosting copper supply expectations.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Announces First Shipments of Copper Concentrates to Anglo-American PLC for Smelting
summary: Battery Mineral Resources announced first shipments of copper concentrate—503.74 dry metric tonnes containing about 288,500 pounds of copper—from its Punitaqui flotation plant to Anglo American’s Chagres smelter in Chile. Production is being ramped toward higher monthly output, signaling improved copper concentrate sales and near-term cash flow.

title: Rio Tinto releases second quarter production results
summary: Rio Tinto’s Q2 results show mined copper production at 171 kt, up 18% year-on-year, with Oyu Tolgoi underground ramp-up and higher head grades supporting output. Aluminium output was slightly higher (824 kt) and Rio Tinto secured long-term renewable power for New Zealand’s Tiwai smelter, supporting continuity of supply.

title: China Copper Smelters Bracing for Shortage of Vital Scrap Metal
summary: The article title says Chinese copper smelters are preparing for a shortage of key scrap metal feedstock. If scrap availability tightens, secondary copper supply to smelters may be constrained in the near term, which typically supports bullish price expectations for copper.

title: IGO ASX: IGO Limited braces for another hit on nickel as it warns of a $275 million writedown
summary: IGO expects a further writedown of up to $275 million tied to nickel asset impairment as Australia’s critical minerals sector deteriorates. The news cites fallout from BHP’s decision to suspend its large-scale nickel mining and processing operations, raising concerns about ongoing production disruption and weaker market fundamentals.

title: Nickel Hub 'Apocalyptic' For Uncontacted Indonesia Tribe, Say NGOs
summary: NGOs allege deforestation and heavy-metal pollution at Indonesia’s Weda Bay nickel hub are endangering the O’Hongana Manyawa Indigenous people. Weda Bay began operations in 2019 and continues, with no shutdown reported; only a proposed BASF-linked refinery project was scrapped for market conditions.

title: Copper eases on rising inventory, weak China data
summary: Copper prices eased as weak China economic data lowered demand expectations and inventories rose across LME, Comex, and Chinese bonded/energy warehouses. Reuters cites lower LME and SHFE copper prices and notes China accounts for about half of annual copper demand. Speculative positioning improved, but pressure from inventories dominated.

title: Nickel hub 'apocalyptic' for uncontacted Indonesia tribe, say NGOs - Society
summary: NGOs allege Weda Bay nickel operations in Indonesia’s North Maluku are stripping forests and polluting local waters, threatening the O’Hongana Manyawa Indigenous people. The piece highlights environmental concerns and campaigning for protections, implying potential regulatory or operational risks for a major nickel hub.

title: Copper: A Key Step on the Road to Net Zero, if It Can Be Mined Sustainably
summary: Copper demand for the net-zero transition is rising sharply, with prices near a 15-month high amid supply constraints. A study warns of a looming shortfall without accelerated mining, and the DRC has seen production cuts, including a 6.5% quarterly reduction at Kamoa-Kakula. Tenke Fungurume’s Copper Mark supports responsible supply and potential premiums.

title: Copper prices under pressure from rising inventory, weak China data
summary: Copper prices fell as weak economic data from China, the world’s largest consumer, weighed on demand outlook. Rising inventories across LME-approved, Comex, and Chinese bonded/SHFE-linked warehouses increased through July, indicating softer physical demand. Reuters reported declines in LME and SHFE copper contracts during the session.

title: Trending : Rio Tinto Iron-Ore Shipments Rose, Narrows Copper Guidance Downward
summary: Rio Tinto said it shipped 2% more iron ore in Q2 and received approvals for Guinea’s Simandou mine, but it narrowed its copper-output guidance downward. The weaker copper guidance points to reduced near-term supply expectations, which can pressure copper prices over the next several days to weeks.

title: Aluminium hits three-month low on heavy supply, copper slips
summary: Aluminium prices hit a three-month low on fears of oversupply after China boosted aluminium output, including resumed Yunnan production with more hydropower. Copper also slipped, pressured by weak Chinese economic data and rising inventories indicating softer demand. The piece cites concurrent declines in LME copper and aluminium contracts.

title: Some Japanese buyers agree to pay Q3 aluminium premium of $172/T, up 16%-19% from Q2
summary: Japanese buyers agreed to pay a Q3 aluminium premium of $172/ton over the LME benchmark, up 16%-19% from Q2 and above April-June levels. The increase reflects tighter regional supplies as some metal diverted to Europe and stronger demand. Talks with producers like Rio Tinto and South32 continued.

title: Aluminium hits three-month low on heavy supply, copper slips
summary: Aluminium prices fell to a three-month low as oversupply concerns grew, with China producing at the highest pace in nearly a decade after resuming output in Yunnan aided by heavy rains and hydropower. Copper also declined on weak Chinese economic data and rising inventories, pressuring demand expectations.

title: Marimaca Copper Announces C$68 Million Strategic Investment by Assore International Holdings (AIH) Including Private Placements Totaling C$30.3 Million led by AIH
summary: Marimaca Copper said Assore International Holdings will invest C$68 million through share purchases and a private placement to fund the Marimaca Project in Chile, including DFS, engineering, permitting, and exploration. This is issuer-level financing for a copper producer, without direct evidence of immediate copper supply or demand shocks.

title: Miner Barrick's second-quarter gold, copper output rises sequentially
summary: Barrick reported its second-quarter copper production increased sequentially to 43,000 tonnes from 40,000 tonnes in Q1, aided by higher grades and recoveries at Lumwana in Zambia after a planned maintenance shutdown. Gold output also rose, but the only tracked-metal price linkage here is higher copper supply expectations.

title: Canadian miner Barrick's second-quarter gold, copper output rises sequentially
summary: Barrick Gold said its second-quarter copper output rose to 43,000 metric tons from 40,000 in the first quarter, helped by higher grades/recoveries at Lumwana after a planned maintenance shutdown. It also notes gold output and cost guidance. Mali contract talks are noted but the immediate quantified item is copper supply.

title: Vertiv and ZincFive Collaborate to Deliver Safe and Reliable Nickel-Zinc Battery Energy Storage for Data Center UPS in North America and EMEA
summary: Vertiv will add ZincFive’s BC Series nickel-zinc UPS battery cabinets to its data center backup power portfolio, offering compatibility with select Vertiv UPS models in North America and EMEA. The NiZn chemistry is positioned as safer and lower-maintenance, with deployments already underway at major data centers.

title: Northern Shield Resources Inc. Earns 100% Interest in Root & Cellar Gold-Silver-Tellurium and Copper Porphyry Project, Newfoundland
summary: Northern Shield Resources says it earned a 100% interest in the Root & Cellar property in Newfoundland, exploring epithermal gold and an associated copper porphyry system. Work includes drilling results, IP anomalies, and trenching. The update is exploratory with no production or immediate supply impact, likely limiting short-term copper price reaction.

title: Alcoa Corporation Announces Stockholder Approval in Connection with the Proposed Acquisition of Alumina Limited
summary: Alcoa reported preliminary stockholder approval for issuing shares to complete its proposed acquisition of Alumina Limited. The transaction targets expanded bauxite and alumina ownership and is expected to close around August 1, after further Australian court approval. The deal may modestly support near-term aluminum market expectations by improving upstream supply control.

title: Alaska Energy Metals Corporation Announces Drilling Program at the Nikolai Nickel Project in Alaska
summary: Alaska Energy Metals Corporation began a drilling program (three holes, 1,200 meters) at its Nikolai Nickel Project’s Canwell block and plans bench-scale metallurgical testing on mineralization at the nearby Eureka deposit. The project is described as a large nickel accumulation with copper and other byproducts, with results aimed at process development.

title: EU faces green dilemma in Indonesian nickel  – DW – 07/16/2024
summary: The piece says Germany’s BASF and France’s Eramet withdrew from Indonesia’s $2.6 billion “Sonic Bay” nickel-and-cobalt refinery after criticism that mining threatens Indigenous land and causes pollution. It links the pullout to EU due-diligence rules and broader push for cleaner nickel, which could reduce near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: China has critical minerals assets: Copper and nickel
summary: The article says China is extending control over critical minerals, including copper refining and nickel processing. It highlights China’s rising copper production/refining influence and large nickel investments in Indonesia (smelters/HPAL projects). It also states these nickel investments disrupted the market and contributed to a collapse in nickel prices.

title: BHP joins the lengthening list of nickel price casualties: Andy Home
summary: Reuters reports BHP is suspending its Western Australia nickel operations from October amid a prolonged nickel price slump. The backdrop includes Indonesia-led output growth, rising LME nickel inventories, and market oversupply, while battery demand disappoints. US/EU engagement is discussed, but near-term price recovery appears limited.

title: China has critical minerals assets: Copper and nickel
summary: The article argues China is securing upstream critical-minerals control, emphasizing nickel and copper supply chains. It details large Chinese investments in Indonesia’s nickel HPAL/smelting to produce battery-grade material, claiming this disrupted the nickel market and drove price declines. It also notes China’s growing copper refining dominance by 2030.

title: Miner Barrick's quarterly gold and copper output edges higher
summary: Barrick Gold said second-quarter copper output rose to 43,000 metric tons from 40,000 tons, helped by higher grades and recoveries at its Lumwana mine in Zambia after a planned maintenance shutdown. Markets may also watch copper guidance alongside expected updates from contract negotiations in Mali.

title: Northern Shield Resources : Earns 100% Interest in Root & Cellar Gold Silver Tellurium and Copper Porphyry Project, Newfoundland
summary: Northern Shield Resources announced it has earned a 100% interest in the Root & Cellar project in Newfoundland, targeting epithermal gold and a potential porphyry copper system. Drilling and trenching are ongoing, with tellurium and copper-associated alteration reported, but no production or supply impact details are provided.

title: Australian nickel – 60 years old and the funeral arrangements are being considered
summary: The article highlights a sharp decline in nickel prices and reports suspensions/closures of Australian nickel projects, including BHP’s decision to suspend operations until at least February 2027 after impairing its nickel assets. It also cites care and maintenance at other producers, reflecting stress in nickel supply and investment sentiment.

title: BHP Annual Iron Ore, Copper Production Rises -- Update
summary: BHP said annual production of iron ore and copper rose, with copper output at the highest level in over 15 years and guidance for further growth. It also reported a 2% rise in nickel production but noted plans to shut Australian nickel operations later this year amid a global glut. Wet weather hurt coal output.

title: BHP ASX: The miner's iron ore exports surge, bullish on copper
summary: BHP reported record iron ore export volumes, but its outlook highlights growth from its copper business. Copper production rose 9% after the OZ Minerals acquisition, and BHP forecast copper output could increase up to 10% next year as Chile’s Escondida mine transitions into higher-grade material.

title: Copper rises after sell-off, firmer dollar caps gains
summary: Copper, aluminium and nickel gained in London on Wednesday after a prior sell-off, with LME three-month copper up 0.3% and LME aluminium up 0.5% and nickel up 0.3%. Gains were capped by a firmer U.S. dollar following stronger U.S. retail sales, while China demand stayed weak.

title: BHP's Iron Ore, Copper Production Rises
summary: BHP reported higher production of copper (and iron ore). The increase in copper output can signal greater near-term supply to the market, potentially softening price expectations. With no countervailing demand, disruptions, or supply risks cited in the snippet, the immediate impact is seen as mildly bearish for copper.

title: Copper holds in tight range as supply concerns counter weak China demand
summary: London copper held in a tight range as supply concerns countered weak China demand and pressure from a firmer U.S. dollar. Reuters cited plans by Chinese smelters to cut output due to raw material shortages. LME aluminium edged up while nickel was listless, indicating muted net direction for nearby prices.

title: Antofagasta expects 2024 copper output at low end of yearly forecast
summary: Antofagasta said 2024 copper output is expected at the low end of its 670,000–710,000 tonne guidance range due to lower ore grades. First-half output fell 3.7% year-on-year, while net cash costs rose. Capex guidance was unchanged, keeping 2024 supply expectations subdued for copper markets.

title: Rio Tinto names former Shell executive Katie Jackson as new copper boss
summary: Rio Tinto appointed Katie Jackson, formerly a Shell executive, as head of its copper operations. She will join Sept. 1 and oversee ramp-up of the Oyu Tolgoi mine in Mongolia, a major copper deposit. The Reuters item is a management change without cited near-term production policy impacts.

title: Antofagasta eyes higher copper production in 2024 despite fall so far
summary: Antofagasta said first-half copper production and sales fell, but expects 2024 full-year output to beat 2023. Q2 production surged on Los Pelambres expansion ramp-up and higher sales. Management also cited Centinela recovery impacts and expects guidance at the lower end, still above 2023 levels.

title: Marimaca Copper secures nearly $50m infusion from Assore
summary: Assore’s subsidiary AIH invested about C$68m (~$49.7m) in Chile’s Marimaca Copper via share purchases and a private placement to fund project development and exploration. The deal increases AIH’s stake to roughly 15%–18% and supports longer-term copper production potential, but no near-term output is specified.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Extends Porphyry Trend at Mineral Mountain
summary: Copper Fox reports sampling results and progress in the Environmental Review permitting process for its Mineral Mountain porphyry copper property in Arizona. Fieldwork found secondary copper and hydrothermal indicators and extended the prospective mineralized trend, but it provides no production or reserve/throughput updates, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Copper firms slightly as dollar slump counters China demand fears
summary: Copper prices edged higher as a weaker U.S. dollar supported LME-traded contracts, but concerns over soft Chinese demand and rising inventories capped the move. LME copper inventories have increased, signaling excess supply. The same session saw modest gains in aluminum and nickel, though overall sentiment looked fragile.

title: Usha Resources Ltd.: Usha Resources Options Southern Arm VMS Property from Abitibi Metals with ~7.3 km Copper-Gold Trend
summary: Usha Resources announced an option to acquire full interest in Abitibi Metals’ Southern Arm property, described as a ~7.3 km copper-gold trend with VMS-style potential and nearby high-grade copper/zinc references. The news is exploration-focused, with no near-term supply or demand impact indicated for copper, nickel, or aluminium.

title: Copper Fox Extends Porphyry Trend at Mineral Mountain
summary: Copper Fox reports sampling results and progress on the Environmental Review/BLM permitting process for its 100%-owned Mineral Mountain porphyry copper property in Arizona. The company highlights increased prospective trend length and reports elevated copper indications in samples, but no production or supply-impact decisions are announced.

title: Drop in European manufacturing tightens aluminium scrap availability
summary: Fastmarkets and BIR report a summer-driven slowdown in European manufacturing and reduced scrap inflows, leaving recycled material still scarce despite a drop in official aluminium ingot prices (DIN 226) and lower LME aluminium cash levels. Competition for scrap is tough, pushing scrap support upward and squeezing alloy makers’ margins.

title: United States - International Trade & Investment - Closing The Southern Border To Indirect Chinese Imports: U.S. Proclamations On Steel And Aluminum Imports From Mexico
summary: Biden issued July 10, 2024 proclamations tightening Section 232 tariff exclusions for steel and aluminum imports from Mexico. A steel “melt and pour” rule restricts duty-free origin, while aluminium faces a “country of smelt/most recent cast” requirement. Importers must submit origin certificates, increasing compliance and potentially shifting aluminium supply routes.

title: FIRST ATLANTIC NICKEL RECEIVES DRILLING PERMITS OVER MULTIPLE AWARUITE NICKEL ZONES ALONG 30 KM DISTRICT TREND
summary: First Atlantic Nickel announced drilling permits for 26 sites across multiple awaruite nickel zones along a 30 km trend in central Newfoundland and says a 5,000 m multi-zone drill program will begin this summer. The company also plans road upgrades to reduce costs and focus drilling on priority targets.

title: "Apache Tribe Challenges EPA Copper Smelter Rule"
summary: The San Carlos Apache Tribe is suing to challenge updated EPA air-toxics regulations covering two copper smelters near its reservation. The tribe argues compliance could shift pollution and potentially increase copper production to meet electric-vehicle demand, while EPA expects toxic-metal emissions to be halved and the groups asked for stricter limits.

title: BHP suspends Western Australia Nickel operations, affecting 3,000 jobs
summary: BHP will suspend its Western Australia Nickel operations, closing Nickel West and stopping mining, processing and the Kwinana refinery and Kalgoorlie smelter, risking thousands of jobs. The shutdown reduces near-term nickel supply while the market remains oversupplied from Indonesia, but supply expectations should still support nickel prices.

title: Copper: Humanity's first and most important future metal
summary: The piece discusses copper’s critical role in electrification and renewables and claims a structural supply deficit versus rising demand. It also cites Citi expecting China stimulus tied to grid and renewable upgrades in mid-July, suggesting near-term price support for copper despite risks from ore grade declines and labor issues in major producing countries.

title: Aluminum Prices Face Downward Pressure as Tariffs Influence Market Trends
summary: Aluminium prices are described as facing ongoing downward bias, with the Aluminum MMI down 4.7% and prices at their lowest since mid-April. The U.S. imposed a 10% tariff on certain Mexican aluminium imports to close a trade loophole, but the affected volumes are small. Chinese primary aluminium output hit a record high, reinforcing deflationary pressure.

title: Aluminium hits 3-month low on rising supply, nickel hits 4-month trough
summary: Aluminium prices fell to a three-month low as primary output rose in major producing countries, with Shanghai LME inventories climbing to the highest since April 2023. Shanghai nickel also hit a four-month trough on increased production, including Indonesia’s output, pressuring an over-supplied market.

title: China's June aluminium imports up 16% on-year, customs data show
summary: China’s unwrought aluminium imports rose 16% year-on-year in June to 240,000 tonnes, with first-half imports up sharply. Bauxite imports also increased 15.4% in June. Strong inflows of primary metal and feedstock suggest higher near-term supply, potentially pressuring aluminium prices.

title: Aluminium hits 3-month low on rising supply, nickel hits 4-month trough
summary: Aluminium prices hit a three-month low on rising primary output in major producing countries, particularly China, and higher SHFE inventories. Shanghai nickel also fell to a four-month trough as supply increased, including from Indonesia, contributing to an over-supplied market and downward pressure across short-term contracts.

title: 40 copper downspouts stolen from San Luis Obispo shopping center
summary: Forty copper downspouts were stolen from an Irish Hills Plaza shopping center in San Luis Obispo, with an initial estimated value of about $10,000. Copper is described as high-value but costly and volatile, and the police are seeking the suspect. The incident is localized and unlikely to move copper prices broadly.

title: Noronex and South32 join forces to accelerate large-scale copper exploration in Namibia
summary: Noronex and South32 agreed an earn-in and strategic alliance to fund copper exploration in Namibia’s Kalahari copper belt. South32 will pay $15 million over five years, starting with a $3 million first-year program of surveys and drilling. The deal targets new copper discoveries but does not change near-term output.

title: Anglo American Cuts Coal Target Following Fire Incident; Backs Copper, Iron Ore Views
summary: Anglo American cut its coal target after a fire led to suspending output for the rest of the year, and reported lower copper production in Q2 (196,000 tonnes vs 209,000 a year earlier) due to lower throughput and grades. The company backed guidance for copper, but the output drop is near-term bearish.

title: RTG Mining Inc.: Multiple Finance and Offtake Offers Secured for Development of Mabilo Copper-Gold Project
summary: RTG Mining announced multiple debt finance and offtake offers to fund 100% of Stage 1 CAPEX for its Mabilo high-grade copper-gold project in the Philippines. The DSO startup is expected to mine ~100,000t of high-grade chalcocite (about 21% copper), generating near-term cashflow on market terms.

title: Anglo American Cuts Coal Target Following Fire Incident; Backs Copper, Iron Ore Views -- Update
summary: Anglo American cut its coal target after a fire incident, suspending a major mine for the rest of the year. It reported 6% lower copper output in Q2 and reiterated 2024 copper guidance, citing lower throughput and grades. Nickel output rose slightly, with the restructure still targeting future sales.

title: MRAI Urges for Duty-Free Aluminium Scrap Imports
summary: India’s Material Recycling Association (MRAI) urges the government to remove the 2.5% import duty on aluminium scrap, arguing recycling cuts carbon emissions versus smelting. The group asks for duty-free imports until enough quality domestic scrap is available, potentially improving scrap supply for aluminium recyclers.

title: Anglo American Backs Copper, Iron Ore Targets After In-Line Performances -- Commodity Comment
summary: Anglo American said its Q2 production dipped for copper, but it kept 2024 copper guidance unchanged, citing Chile and Peru throughput and unit cost levels. Nickel production was broadly flat with unchanged 2024 guidance and lower unit costs. Aluminium was not discussed, and no new disruption was announced.

title: Japan buyers agree to pay higher Q3 aluminum premiums, sources say
summary: Japan buyers agreed to pay a higher Q3 aluminum premium of $172/mt, up 16%-19% from the prior quarter, citing tighter regional supply as some metal was diverted to Europe and the US. Negotiations ended below initial offers, while Japanese demand stayed lackluster and port stocks rose modestly.

title: Chilean copper output to grow by 5% in 2024, supported by output from Quebrada Blanca
summary: Chile’s copper production is forecast to rise 5% in 2024 to about 5.5 million tonnes, supported by ramp-up at Teck’s Quebrada Blanca and higher contributions from other established and upcoming mines. Some declines and disruptions are noted, but overall supply growth remains the dominant theme.

title: Canada Nickel Company Announces Initial Deloro Nickel Sulphide Project Resource
summary: Canada Nickel Company reported an initial resource for its 100% owned Deloro nickel sulphide project near Timmins, Ontario, including 81 Mt at 0.25% Ni (202kt contained) plus an inferred portion. Seven exploration rigs are drilling the Timmins Nickel District, but no near-term production impact was stated.

title: Canada Nickel Company Inc.: Canada Nickel Company Announces Initial Deloro Nickel Sulphide Project Resource
summary: Canada Nickel filed an NI 43-101 technical report supporting an initial mineral resource estimate for its 100% owned Reid nickel sulphide project near Timmins, Ontario. The release specifies the effective date of the estimate and notes no material changes from prior results, reinforcing the project’s potential to expand nickel supply outlook.

title: PAN GLOBAL INTERSECTS 6.5M OF 1.22 G/T GOLD AND 14M OF 0.46% COPPER, EXPANDING MINERALIZATION AT CAÑADA HONDA DISCOVERY, ESCACENA PROJECT, SOUTHERN SPAIN
summary: Pan Global reports assay results from additional holes at its Cañada Honda Cu-Au discovery in Spain’s Iberian Pyrite Belt. Drilling confirms down-dip continuation of copper mineralization, including 14m at 0.46% Cu, and suggests stronger sulphides up-dip. The company plans further step-outs to test extensions and higher grades to the west.

title: Indonesia to Launch Nickel, Tin Online Tracking System Next Week
summary: Indonesia will launch the SIMBARA online tracking system next Monday for nickel and tin shipments to improve mining governance and boost government revenue. The system, first used for coal in 2022, is being expanded to other minerals. Tighter shipment oversight could affect near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: Indonesia to launch nickel, tin online tracking system next week
summary: Indonesia will launch SIMBARA, an online tracking system for nickel and tin shipments, next week. The system links smelters’ purchases to mine registration and bars unloading ore from mines that have not paid royalties. It is tied to RKAB quota records and aims to boost revenue and improve mining governance.

title: Exclusive-Nornickel in talks to build China nickel plant for battery sector, sources say
summary: Nornickel is reportedly in talks with Chinese battery companies such as CNGR and CATL-linked Brunp to build a plant producing nickel sulphate from Russian nickel matte. The goal is to ship guaranteed nickel output into China while navigating Western sanctions. China demand could strengthen sentiment for nickel.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon & Circulor Announce Partnership for Tracking Responsibly Sourced Domestic Nickel
summary: Talon Metals will use Circulor’s traceability technology to digitally track its nickel and copper concentrates, including provenance and CO2 intensity, through processing and recycling. The company says it aims to reduce reputational and compliance risk for battery makers under the US IRA and EU Battery Regulation. Immediate effects on metal supply appear minimal.

title: Copper falls on lack of impetus from China and switch to gold
summary: Copper prices fell toward three-week lows as China offered no new stimulus, with Beijing communique lacking details, and Chinese copper imports slipping to a 14-month low. LME copper inventories rose to a 33-month high, while investors rotated into gold on expectations of Fed rate cuts. Aluminium also hit a recent low.

title: Fathom Nickel Inc.: Fathom Provides Gochager Lake Exploration Update
summary: Fathom Nickel provided an exploration update from its Gochager Lake property, reporting preliminary pXRF findings that indicate elevated nickel (up to ~2.06% Ni) and meaningful copper (up to ~0.69% Cu) in outcrop samples. The company says signals match drill-core patterns, suggesting a larger open magmatic system.

title: First Atlantic's Newfoundland nickel project gets drilling permits
summary: First Atlantic Nickel secured drilling permits for its Atlantic Nickel Project in central Newfoundland, enabling a planned 5,000m multi-zone drill programme to start this summer. The company plans to test promising awaruite nickel zones and is mobilising equipment to upgrade roads, with an emphasis on sulphur-free processing advantages.

title: Peruvian copper production to grow by just 0.6% in 2024, linked to disruptions
summary: Peru’s copper production growth is forecast to slow to 0.6% in 2024 due to mining disruptions from blockades and unfavorable weather. Las Bambas was blocked until April 11 and produced less in Q1. Despite this, overall Peru copper output rose 3.6% YoY in Q1 on other mines’ gains.

title: International Business: Indonesia to launch nickel, tin online tracking system next week
summary: Indonesia will launch SIMBARA next week, an online tracking system for nickel and tin shipments, linked to mining quotas (RKAB). Smelters must register nickel purchases and cannot unload ore unless royalties are paid. The government expects higher revenue and tighter control over nickel flows from mines to smelters.

title: Six suspected copper cables thieves appear in Gqeberha court
summary: Six suspects appeared in court in Gqeberha after authorities recovered about 300kg of Telkom copper cables valued at R600,000. Police followed a tip-off about a vehicle carrying copper, seized the cables and vehicle, and kept the suspects in custody pending bail. The incident is copper-related but localized.

title: Copper output from Chile's Codelco this year to top 2023, chairman says
summary: Codelco Chairman Maximo Pacheco said the company expects its 2024 copper production to surpass 2023, with improvements coming in the second half of the year. Chile’s state miner is the world’s major supplier, and the update is likely to lift market expectations for copper availability.

title: Biden Administration Issues Steel, Aluminum Tariff Proclamation
summary: Biden issued proclamations refining Section 232 tariff exclusions for aluminum imports from Mexico. New “country of smelt” and “most recent cast” requirements require certificates of analysis to prove primary aluminum is not from China, Russia, Belarus, or Iran for duty-free treatment, with tariffs reinstated otherwise.

title: Southern Copper's restart of contentious Peru project sparks protests
summary: Southern Copper restarted construction on the long-stalled Tia Maria copper mine in Peru, prompting protests and road blockages near the site. Activists cite environmental concerns and warn tensions could escalate. Company statements say construction continues, with production expected in 2027.

title: Construction of Southern Copper's Peru Mine Sparks Protests
summary: Protests in Peru’s Tambo Valley have erupted over Southern Copper’s long-stalled Tia Maria mine construction. Locals cite environmental concerns, recalling past unrest that involved fatalities. While protests are said not to affect construction and production is targeted for 2027, potential escalation could threaten future copper supply planning.

title: Copper hits three-month low on lack of Chinese stimulus
summary: Copper hit a more than three-month low after China’s political meeting failed to deliver further stimulus measures, reducing expectations for metal demand. Weekly losses widened. Aluminium also fell to multi-month lows amid rising output, and nickel reached a four-month low, reflecting increased supply and weaker sentiment.

title: Vedanta Resources pays $246 million dues to help revive operations at Zambian copper mine
summary: Vedanta settled about $245.75 million in dues to creditors to help revive Konkola copper mines in Zambia after regaining control in 2023. The mine’s smelter also comes under Vedanta’s plans, though an additional ~$1 billion is still needed for operations and deep mining investment.

title: SMM Analysis: Copper Smelters Face Diverging Strategies of Production Cuts and Expansions
summary: SMM reports Chinese smelters plan to reduce copper smelting capacity from next year because spot and long-term treatment charges for copper concentrate are unfavorable. Some smelters already adopted “passive” cuts. Others pursue expansions, but forecasts point to a widening concentrate supply gap and potential capacity consolidation, supporting copper tightness expectations.

title: iTWire - Panasonic Energy to collaborate with Australia's National Science Agency CSIRO to develop Nickel Laterite Processing Technologies for Lithium-ion Battery Applications
summary: Panasonic Energy will work with Australia’s CSIRO to develop new processing technologies to recover nickel from nickel laterite for lithium-ion battery applications. The collaboration targets lower-cost, lower-environmental-impact supply chains and aims to strengthen Australia’s nickel industry to meet growing battery demand, supporting nickel market sentiment.

title: Vedanta restarts Zambian copper mine after $246 million debt settlement
summary: Vedanta agreed to pay about $246 million in debts to reclaim and restart operations at Zambia’s Konkola Copper Mines, which had been seized by the government and held in legal dispute. The move supports renewed copper production, although further funding is still needed for deep mining and full advancement.

title: Nornickel in talks to build China nickel plant for battery sector, sources say
summary: Reuters reports Nornickel is in talks with Chinese battery firms to build a plant in China producing nickel sulfate for EV batteries from Russian nickel matte, potentially supplying 50,000 tons/year. The project is conditional with sanctions risks and no final decision, suggesting limited near-term effect on nickel prices.

title: Aluminum: Social inventory of aluminum ingots increased to a new high in H2, further suppressing spot and futures prices
summary: SMM reported social inventory of aluminum ingots rose to 797,000 mt in H2, including 671,000 mt available for sale, lifting supply and suppressing spot and futures. Inventory increased mid-week and reached a new high, reflecting weaker northwest processing demand and reduced shipments to south China.

title: Nornickel in discussions to set up nickel plant in China
summary: Nornickel is in talks to build a China nickel plant that would process Russian nickel matte into nickel sulphate for EV batteries. The project targets supplying about 50,000 tonnes of nickel annually and relocates some processing to bypass sanctions-related sales disruptions, though Chinese firms are cautious.

title: Surge Copper Commences 2024 Field Program and Closes Top-Up Subscription by ARM
summary: Surge Copper Corp. announced the start of its 2024 field program, with two rigs drilling at the Berg copper-molybdenum project in British Columbia, using funds raised through a top-up offering. The financing supports exploration activity but does not imply immediate changes to copper supply or inventories.

title: Copper extends downturn to three-month low on China gloom
summary: Copper prices fell for a fifth session to a three-month low as markets stayed bearish on China’s weak economy and the absence of additional stimulus. SHFE copper also dropped. Aluminium and nickel hit multi-month lows, weighed by higher output in Indonesia and China, reinforcing overall downside momentum.

title: ACG Acquisition sets reverse takeover of Turkey copper mine
summary: ACG Acquisition agreed a reverse takeover of Turkey’s Gediktepe polymetallic mine, planning a sulphide expansion to enable copper production starting in 2026. The USD290 million deal includes cash and shares, with funding arranged in principle. ACG frames the asset as a first step in copper consolidation, but timing is long-dated.

title: Alcoa ready for more potential M&A as Alumina deal nears close, CEO says | Hotter Commodities
summary: Alcoa’s CEO says the Alumina Ltd acquisition is on track to close August 1 and will simplify the company’s structure. The deal timing is influenced by elevated alumina prices amid supply disruptions, including refinery curtailments, gas pipeline problems affecting cargoes, and issues at Nalco, supporting aluminium cost expectations.

title: Copper Extends Downturn to Three-Month Low on China Gloom
summary: Copper prices continued their downturn, falling for a fifth straight session to a three-month low. LME three-month copper slid about 0.5% to roughly $9,343/t after earlier hitting the lowest since early April. The move was attributed to disquiet over China’s weak economy and lack of stimulus announcements.

title: Southern Copper : SCC reports 2Q24 results
summary: Southern Copper reported 2Q24 results with copper sales volume up 5.5% and copper production up 6.6% QoQ to 242,474 tons, driven by higher ore grades. Net sales and income rose sharply, and management cited higher copper prices/realizations contributing to results, which can support near-term copper sentiment.

title: "Continued Deterioration": Goldman Sees "Surplus Market" In Copper, Pushing Prices Lower In "Short-Term"
summary: Goldman’s view, as reflected in the headline, points to a copper “surplus market” in the near term. That assessment generally translates into expectations of more available supply than demand, which should weigh on copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Aluminum associations sall for fair trade practices amid subsidy disparities - Canadian Manufacturing
summary: Aluminum industry associations from the US, Europe, Canada and Japan back an OECD effort to quantify subsidies and state-enterprise roles. The report argues Chinese aluminium firms receive most subsidies and below-market energy/finance. Associations urge governments to apply trade defence measures for a fair, level playing field in aluminium markets.

title: Ferndale aluminum plant sued for air quality violations by EPA
summary: An EPA lawsuit alleges air quality violations at the Ferndale aluminum plant. Enforcement actions such as mandated corrective measures, operating restrictions, or potential downtime could affect near-term aluminum output, which would likely be bearish for aluminium price expectations over the coming days to weeks.

title: Copper Demand Surge Drives Consolidation Wave in Mining Sector
summary: London-listed ACG says it has bought Turkey-based Polimetal, securing the Gediktepe open-pit copper mine, as the start of a “global copper consolidation strategy.” The deal is justified by sustained copper demand for EVs and renewables, following other bid activity in copper mining.

title: Capella Announces Termination of Agreement with Polar Transition for the Sale of its Central Norway Copper Assets
summary: Capella Minerals said it and Polar Transition agreed to terminate a previously announced sale of Capella’s central Norway copper portfolio after the long-stop date passed. Capella regains 100% ownership of its copper-cobalt projects and will pursue alternative advancement strategies, including drill-ready targets at Åmot and Hessjøgruva.

title: Goldman Sachs Sees Downside For Copper in The Short Term
summary: Goldman analyst Adam Gillard warns copper could fall in the short term as the market shifts toward a surplus. The piece cites record Chinese unwrought cathode and product exports, rising Asia LME deliveries, built Chinese inventories, and weaker June apparent demand, implying continued downside despite long positioning.

title: Bauxite in the Republic of Guinea
summary: Guinea is described as the world’s largest bauxite producer, with 2023 output up 11% year-on-year and exports also up 11%, largely to China. Guinea’s bauxite share is cited at 28% of global production, with continued but slower growth expected, supporting aluminium supply expectations.

title: South32 to Take $554 Million Worley Alumina Impairment
summary: South32 will record a US$554 million impairment and cut Worsley Alumina fiscal 2025 guidance after Australian environmental regulators recommended additional conditions and the project faced challenging operating conditions. Alumina production fell to 5.06 million tonnes, and 2025 volume guidance drops, potentially weighing on aluminium supply expectations.

title: South32 to Take $818 Million in Alumina, Nickel Impairments -- Update
summary: South32 plans $818 million in impairments, including $554 million for its Worsley Alumina unit and $264 million for Cerro Matoso due to global nickel glut and pressure on nickel prices. It cut Worsley guidance, reported flat aluminium volumes, and noted lower copper output from grade/recovery issues.

title: South32 to recognise $554 mln charge against Worsley Alumina in FY24
summary: South32 will record a $554 million impairment charge tied to its Worsley Alumina operations after WA EPA recommendations could impose conditions that make the project harder to operate. The company said the conditions may affect long-term viability, potentially tightening alumina-linked supply and supporting aluminium expectations.

title: South32 to Take $818 Million in Alumina, Nickel Impairments -- Update
summary: South32 will book $818m impairments, including $554m tied to its Worsley Alumina business amid added regulatory conditions and weaker operating outlook. It also takes a $264m impairment for Cerro Matoso as a global nickel glut pressures prices. The firm cuts alumina guidance and reports lower copper production, adding downside sentiment for nickel, aluminium, and copper.

title: South32 Shares Tumble Almost 10% Amid Worsley Alumina Impairment
summary: South32 shares fell ~10% after the company warned environmental conditions could affect the long-term viability of its Worsley Alumina project. It recorded US$818m impairments and cut Worsley production guidance, citing lower 2024 output from a bauxite conveyor outage and regulator-recommended conditions.

title: Vedanta Limited: Vedanta Regains Control of Konkola Copper Mines in Zambia
summary: A press release from Makor Resources highlights progress toward advancing the Muli Copper Project in Zambia’s Central Province, within an emerging copper corridor near the Kitumba Copper Project. It emphasizes Zambia’s mandate to expand copper output and investor interest in electrification-related demand, but provides no immediate mine-production figures.

title: Vedanta Regains Control of Konkola Copper Mines in Zambia
summary: Vedanta says it has paid USD 245.75 million under the KCM scheme in Zambia, enabling the reinstatement of the KCM board and full return of management control. The company plans to ramp up KCM copper output to 300ktpa, which should ease near-term copper supply uncertainty.

title: Four arrested in copper theft investigation in Scott City — an estimated $13,000 worth stolen
summary: Scott City, Missouri police arrested four residents for stealing about 3,000 feet of copper from Union Pacific Railroad, allegedly worth around $13,000. The stolen copper was reportedly sold at recycling locations across southeast Missouri. The charges include stealing and damaging critical infrastructure facility.

title: South32 Tumbles After $818 Million Alumina, Nickel Writedown
summary: South32 shares reportedly fell after an $818 million writedown linked to alumina and nickel. The market read-through is weaker outlook for production economics and possible supply impacts along the alumina-to-aluminium chain and in nickel operations, which can weigh on near-term price expectations for both metals.

title: Tiwai Point aluminium smelter to cut back its power use
summary: New Zealand’s Tiwai aluminium smelter will cut electricity demand by 185 MW (about 4% of national energy use) under a contract with Meridian Energy due to low hydro lake levels. The smelter will stop and restart about one-third of operations until April, tightening aluminium supply.

title: The macro impact and fundamentals intertwine, and the downward trend of nickel prices remains unchanged.
summary: SHFE nickel prices fell about 3.58% MoM, with the downturn driven by weaker macro sentiment amid US election/tariff uncertainty and by supply-side disruptions. Philippines weather delayed shipments, while Indonesia’s SIMBARA integration aims to improve nickel supply-chain compliance but its net effect on ore availability is unclear. Downstream demand remains limited.

title: Indonesia launches nickel, tin online tracking system
summary: Indonesia launched an online tracking system to monitor nickel (and tin) flows from mines to domestic processing facilities, with links to miners’ production quota records. The stated goals are improved accountability and government revenue. The policy could affect operational compliance, but no clear near-term supply shock is mentioned.

title: London copper heads for sixth day of loss on China demand worries
summary: London copper is set for a sixth straight day of losses as China demand worries persist and policymakers provided no new stimulus details. LME copper inventories hit the highest since Sept 2021, while China bonded stocks rose to a May 2023 peak. SHFE prices also hit lows, despite some physical buying.

title: EV Resources ramps up Queensland copper porphyry hunt
summary: EV Resources says new rock chip results at its Khartoum project in Queensland show high-grade copper (up to 71% copper mentioned) and strong silver, suggesting potential for large-scale copper-moly-silver porphyry targets. The company plans further sampling, geophysics, and drilling, boosting copper-focused market sentiment.

title: S32 ASX: South32's Worsley alumina refinery threatened by environmental rules
summary: South32 warns the Worsley alumina refinery in Western Australia may be threatened by stricter environmental approval requirements. The company recorded a $US389 million impairment and cut production forecasts for Worsley and two other assets. The concern is potential alumina supply disruption, weighing on aluminium-linked sentiment.

title: South32 to take USD554 million hit from Worsley Alumina woes
summary: South32 warned it expects a USD554 million hit from regulatory uncertainty affecting its Worsley Alumina refining operation in Western Australia. The company faces tougher EPA conditions and an appeal process. Alumina production was slightly lower and the impairment signals higher risk to aluminium supply viability.

title: Indonesia expands online tracking system to nickel, tin-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia broadened its Simbara online tracking system to include nickel (and tin), building on efforts that helped curb illegal mining and generate state revenues. Given Indonesia’s large nickel production and reserves, stronger enforcement could constrain near-term nickel supply, supporting nickel price expectations over coming days to weeks.

title: Indonesia expands online tracking system to nickel, tin
summary: Indonesia expanded its Simbara online tracking system to include nickel (and tin) to curb illegal mining via risk profiling and automatic blocks. The program has boosted state revenues since 2022. With Indonesia producing about half of global nickel output, tighter enforcement may reduce illicit supply and support nickel prices.

title: Planning Institute of Jamaica reports major growth in bauxite production
summary: Jamaica’s Planning Institute reports that the local bauxite sector nearly doubled output in 2023, driving a sharp rebound in mining growth versus 2022. It also cites supportive government policy under the National Mineral Policy aimed at meeting global mineral demand, which could be interpreted as supportive for aluminium supply expectations.

title: Vedanta Resources Limited: Vedanta Regains Control of Konkola Copper Mines in Zambia
summary: Makor Resources is advancing the early-stage Muli Copper Project in Zambia’s Central Province, highlighting its prospective district-scale copper potential and Zambia’s supportive investment framework. While it underscores long-term copper supply relevance and nearby copper development progress, it provides no immediate production or supply-change figures affecting prices.

title: Copper, aluminium hit 3-1/2-month low on demand concerns
summary: Copper and aluminium prices fell to 3-1/2-month lows as investors worried about China’s prolonged property slump and demand outlook after a key political meeting failed to deliver further stimulus. Prices also weighed on by high LME warehouse inventories. Lower interest rates offered limited offset, keeping bearish sentiment.

title: Copper, aluminium hit 3-1/2-month low on demand concerns
summary: Copper and aluminium prices dropped to multi-month lows on Monday as China demand worries intensified amid the property slump and high warehouse inventories. A lack of additional stimulus from a key political meeting and elevated LME stock levels weighed on sentiment, while rate cuts only partly supported physical buying.

title: Solaris Reports In-Pit Mineral Resources Including Higher Grade Mineralization; Over 30,000m Drilling in H2/24 Targeting Open Extensions and Infill to Upgrade Resources; Concurrent District Exploration for Epithermal Gold/Silver and Porphyry Copper Discoveries
