summary: Solaris Resources reported an updated in-pit Mineral Resources estimate at its Warintza copper project in Ecuador, with extensive drilling planned in H2/24 to support a PFS in H2/25. The release also describes district exploration for epithermal gold/silver and porphyry copper targets, but no near-term supply changes.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Continues Drilling Program and Announces Encouraging Drill Results from Its Punitaqui Copper Mine in Chile
summary: Battery Mineral Resources reported encouraging assay results from underground drilling at its Punitaqui copper mine complex in Chile and said it resumed mill operations, producing and shipping copper concentrates. The drill intercepts confirm and better delineate copper grades and mineralized extent, supporting near-term expectations for copper production ramp-up.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp. Signs Letter of Intent to Sell Minago Assets to Norway House Cree Nation
summary: Flying Nickel Mining signed a binding letter of intent to sell its Minago nickel project and related assets in Manitoba to Norway House Cree Nation, with consideration including cash and Flying Nickel shares. The transaction is subject to definitive agreement and regulatory/court/shareholder approvals, with no immediate production impact described.

title: Aluminium slips to almost four-month low on demand concerns
summary: Aluminium prices slid to a near four-month low on Monday as traders pared bullish positions and base metals weakened amid concerns over China’s demand, with no new stimulus outlined after a key political meeting. LME three-month aluminium fell to $2,308.50, while copper and nickel also eased on the softer outlook.

title: Aussie's Selloff Deepens as Copper Prices Plunge
summary: Copper prices are falling sharply, with the worst week since 2022, tied to disappointing Chinese demand signals. The People’s Bank of China’s surprise short-term rate cut and weaker Q2 growth are cited as reminders of persistent economic trouble, reinforcing bearish near-term copper sentiment.

title: Ero Copper and Vale Base Metals Execute Definitive Earn-In Agreement on the Furnas Copper Project
summary: Ero Copper and Vale Base Metals executed a definitive earn-in agreement for Ero to earn a 60% interest in the Furnas Copper Project in Brazil’s Carajás Mineral Province. The deal follows a prior term sheet and is intended to support development of the copper resource, modestly improving supply expectations.

title: New tracking system to prevent fraud in nickel, tin mining - Regulations
summary: Indonesia expanded its Simbara online tracking system to cover nickel shipments from mines to domestic smelters. The government says it targets fraud/illegal mining and aims to raise state revenue, building on results for coal. Since Indonesia is a major nickel producer, this could tighten effective supply and support prices.

title: Closure of Sterlite copper smelter plant in Thoothukudi put India at mercy of China: Vedanta
summary: Vedanta said the closure of its Sterlite copper smelter in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, leaves India dependent on China. The shutdown reduces domestic copper refining supply and raises concerns about near-term availability and trade flows, which can influence expectations for refined copper prices over coming weeks.

title: Is nickel down but not out?
summary: The piece argues nickel remains under pressure due to persistent oversupply. It forecasts a 2024 surplus (production 3.7Mt vs usage 3.4Mt) and a 2025 surplus, while Indonesian supply expansion and a shift from NMC to cheaper LFP batteries reduce incremental EV demand support. BHP’s shutdown offers only partial offset.

title: Panasonic Energy and CSIRO collaboration aims to develop new nickel recovery methods
summary: Panasonic Energy and CSIRO will collaborate on studies to develop new processing technologies to recover nickel from Australian laterite resources for lithium-ion battery supply. The initiative is positioned as a way to create low-cost, lower-impact nickel and bolster a nickel industry hit by oversupply and falling prices, but it is primarily R&D with limited immediate effects.

title: Aluminium producer Norsk Hydro's Q2 core profit falls below expectations
summary: Norwegian aluminium producer Norsk Hydro said Q2 core profit fell 18% to 5.84 billion crowns, missing analysts’ expectations. The decline was attributed to lower volumes and margins, even though alumina prices were higher. The result suggests weaker operating conditions for aluminium markets near term.

title: China's rate cuts fail to revive iron ore and copper: Russell
summary: China’s first major interest-rate cuts in 11 months failed to lift commodities sentiment. Copper futures fell—London down about 1% and Shanghai down 0.86%—to the lowest closes since early April. The piece adds that Chinese copper trade flows are being driven more by global price/arbitrage than by stimulus expectations.

title: Column – China's rate cuts fail to revive iron ore and copper: Russell | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: China’s first interest-rate cut in 11 months produced a muted reaction in commodities, with copper futures slipping. London copper ended down 1.0% and Shanghai contracts also fell to their weakest closes since April 8. The piece attributes limited stimulus impact and notes lower copper arrivals and higher refined exports.

title: Indonesia to extend online tracking system to copper, gold and bauxite
summary: Indonesia plans to broaden its Simbara online tracking system beyond earlier rollouts to cover additional commodities. The government has already expanded Simbara to include nickel and tin, with copper and other minerals such as bauxite expected next. Officials say the system helps curb illegal mining and supports state revenues.

title: Indonesia to extend online tracking system to copper, gold and bauxite
summary: Indonesia plans to broaden its Simbara online mineral tracking system to additional commodities, following Monday’s inclusion of nickel and tin. The minister said copper and bauxite (plus manganese and others) will follow. Officials cite state revenue gains from preventing illegal mining, but no immediate production change is specified.

title: 91 tonnes of copper stolen at Chirundu border post
summary: Zimbabwe Revenue Authority seized three trucks after 91 tonnes of copper disguised as in-transit goods were stolen at the Chirundu border post. A court ruled against Nashfreight, citing failure to prove proper delivery to Zimra’s custody and evidence the copper was consumed in Zimbabwe after illegal entry.

title: Indonesia to extend online tracking system to copper, gold and bauxite-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia plans to expand its SIMBARA online tracking system for minerals and coal to cover additional commodities including copper, after it was broadened to nickel and tin. The system targets illegal mining through risk profiling and automatic blocking, contributing state revenues. No immediate production or aluminium-specific impact is detailed.

title: Indonesia to extend online tracking system to copper, gold and bauxite-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia’s energy ministry plans to extend its Simbara online tracking system to additional commodities. It already broadened Simbara to cover nickel and tin and now intends to add copper, bauxite, manganese and others. Simbara helps curb illegal mining via risk profiling and automatic blocking, contributing to state revenues.

title: Porsche lowers forecast - supply bottlenecks for aluminum slow down production
summary: Porsche lowered its annual forecast after aluminum-alloy supply bottlenecks. A flooding incident at an important European supplier triggered force majeure, disrupting production of special aluminium alloys used across Porsche vehicle series. Porsche expects impairment for several weeks, potentially delaying model-series output and deliveries, which can reduce short-term aluminium demand.

title: London's FTSE 100 falls as copper miners, automobile stocks weigh
summary: London’s FTSE 100 fell slightly as copper miners slid, tracking pressured copper prices. The decline was attributed to heightened concerns that Chinese demand will remain weak after recent policy announcements disappointed investors. Rio Tinto and Glencore fell more than 1% each, reinforcing near-term bearish sentiment on copper.

title: Indonesia's online monitoring system now covers nickel, tin commodities
summary: Indonesia expanded its Simbara online mineral/coal tracking system (launched in 2022) to include nickel and tin. Finance Minister Sri Mulyani said it has helped prevent leakage of state revenues from illegal mining. Authorities expect added income from better compliance, implying tighter nickel supply.

title: LYC ASX: Lynas says Labor should help fund supplies after BHP halts nickel work"
summary: Lynas Rare Earths urged Australia’s government to help fund a plant supplying sulphuric acid after BHP halted nickel work and ended acid supplies in Australia. Lynas said it may need to produce its own acid for a planned rare-earths processing plant at Kalgoorlie, citing input availability concerns.

title: Porsche shares fall as automaker cuts 2024 outlook on aluminium alloy shortage
summary: Porsche’s shares fell after it cut its 2024 outlook, blaming a significant shortage of special aluminium alloys. The shortage is linked to flooding at a key European aluminium supplier’s facility, disrupting aluminium body components across vehicle series. Porsche expects production impairments for several weeks and possible series shutdowns.

title: Copper hits multi-month low on growing Chinese demand fears
summary: Copper prices fell for a seventh straight session to the lowest in three and a half months as fears of softer Chinese demand grew. Reuters cited disappointment over China’s third plenum, sell signals from trading models, record Chinese shipments raising LME stocks, and a wider refined copper surplus, weighing on sentiment. Aluminium bucked the trend.

title: Lifezone Metals Produces First-Ever Nickel, Copper and Cobalt from Kabanga Nickel Project
summary: Lifezone Metals says its Simulus laboratory produced the first-ever refined nickel and copper cathode samples from Kabanga Nickel Project flotation concentrate during semi-continuous pilot hydromet testing. Results support design criteria for the planned Kahama refinery, but assays and commercial timing remain pending.

title: Bmw: Aluminium Shortages Affected Production But Had Contingency…
summary: Reuters reports that BMW experienced aluminium shortages that affected production, but the company had contingency plans. BMW said there was no impact on overall output or its outlook. The news signals temporary aluminium supply tightness affecting manufacturers, but with limited broader demand implications in the near term.

title: BMW: no interruption to production from aluminium shortages
summary: BMW said an aluminium alloy supply shortage also affected its supply chain, but it compensated for the lost supply and production was not interrupted. The shortage previously influenced Porsche’s outlook, implying some stress in aluminium alloy availability, but BMW’s mitigation limits immediate additional upside risk for aluminium prices.

title: Lifezone Metals Produces First-Ever Nickel, Copper and Cobalt from Kabanga Nickel Project - Iberonews
summary: Lifezone Metals says it has produced its first-ever nickel and copper from the Kabanga Nickel Project. The milestone indicates early development of future supply from the project, which can modestly lift market sentiment for nickel and copper. Immediate price impact depends on the scale and ramp-up timeline beyond the initial production.

title: Ero seals deal to earn 60% of Furnas copper project in Brazil
summary: Ero Copper agreed to earn in for a 60% stake in Vale Base Metals’ Furnas copper project in Brazil’s Carajás region. The deal includes a phased drilling program to deliver scoping, pre-feasibility and DFS studies, supporting longer-run supply prospects and improving development momentum for copper.

title: Southeast Asian lawmakers urge govt, region to consider nickel mining impacts - Politics
summary: Southeast Asian lawmakers urged Indonesia and regional governments to better assess environmental and social costs amid a nickel boom tied to EV battery demand. Indonesia is highlighted as the largest nickel producer. The inquiry called for stricter compliance, but the article doesn’t announce specific near-term regulatory actions.

title: Speira boosts aluminium recycling with advanced furnace upgrades for contaminated materials
summary: Speira is investing €11m to upgrade two German aluminium recycling plants with tiltable rotary furnaces capable of processing heavily contaminated low-grade scrap and dross. The upgrades include automatic charging and more efficient burner/afterburner systems, aiming for higher aluminium yield and lower energy use, with production targeted from May 2025 onward.

title: In search of the elusive green nickel premium: Andy Home
summary: Reuters discusses BHP’s plan to put its Nickel West green nickel sulphate push on care and maintenance later this year, after years of investment and a Tesla-linked supply deal. It argues that nickel oversupply from Indonesia and China has crushed “green premiums,” keeping market pricing depressed despite new low-carbon contract efforts.

title: Novelis notified customers about Swiss aluminium plant shutdown
summary: Novelis notified automotive customers of a force majeure that led it to shut a Swiss aluminium plant after late-June flooding. The disruption meant it could not fully deliver aluminium supplies in Europe. Porsche also cut its sales forecast after another European aluminium supplier declared force majeure.

title: Speculative interests in copper driving base metals narratives, says Sucden Financial
summary: Sucden Financial’s head of research says copper’s recent upside was driven mainly by re-engaged speculative long positions, with markets watching COMEX/LME arbitrage. Copper strength is expected to lift the wider base-metals complex, with aluminium following closely, while nickel may diverge due to Indonesia supply and inventory growth.

title: Flying Nickel plans to divest Minago project in Canada to NHCN
summary: Flying Nickel signed a letter of intent with Norway House Cree Nation to divest the Minago nickel project and related assets in Manitoba. Consideration is $7.3m–$8m cash plus share surrender, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. Minago contains significant nickel resources, but timing is uncertain for production impact.

title: Artificial Intelligence Is Sparking a Copper Boom in Zambia
summary: KoBold Metals says it made the largest copper discovery in over a decade in Zambia, with potential output of hundreds of thousands of tonnes annually once developed. The piece links rising clean-tech and data-center demand to copper shortages, citing forecasts of higher copper prices. It frames Zambia’s mine growth as bullish for copper sentiment.

title: EuroPacific Announces Drill Assay Results Targeting High-Grade Copper Zone to 350m at Miguel Vacas Confirming Significant Mineralization at Depth
summary: EuroPacific Metals announced assay results from an additional 350m undercut hole at the Miguel Vacas copper project. Results include broad breccia intersections and high-grade copper intervals (e.g., 10.5m at 2.56% Cu, plus sections up to 7.49% Cu). Management says the system is open at depth and along strike.

title: First Quantum reaches agreement with major Chinese shareholder Jiangxi Copper to curb its power
summary: First Quantum agreed with its major Chinese shareholder Jiangxi Copper to curb its ability to add or sell significant stakes and to limit its influence on board decisions for three years. Jiangxi Copper is a leading copper smelter and is linked to First Quantum’s copper prepayment/offtake arrangements, slightly affecting copper supply sentiment.

title: Intalco Aluminum agrees to $5.25 million penalty for hazardous pollution violations at Ferndale
summary: Intalco Aluminum agreed to pay a $5.25 million penalty for hazardous pollution violations at its Ferndale location. The settlement highlights increased environmental compliance scrutiny and potential costs or operational constraints, which can slightly pressure near-term aluminium supply expectations and prices.

title: Copper slides on China demand worries
summary: Copper prices fell toward a three-and-a-half month low as concerns about weakening demand in top consumer China weighed on the market. Reuters cited dampened physical demand from price surges and China’s prolonged property crisis and limited stimulus after a political meeting. Other LME/SHFE metals showed minor mixed moves.

title: Philippine Laterite Nickel Ore Exports in Q2 2024: Dominated by the Chinese Market? [SMM Analysis]
summary: Q2 2024 Philippine exports of nickel laterite ore increased sharply, with shipments to China rising from about 80 to 106 ships between April and May. Low-nickel cargo dominated, while medium-grade demand weakened on NPI price fluctuations. Frequent June rainfall reduced loading rates temporarily, but most ships still loaded.

title: Strickland zeroes in on red-hot Serbian copper-gold target
summary: Strickland Metals reports preliminary IP survey results at its Obradov Potok target within Serbia’s Rogozna project, suggesting a potential new deposit with associated gold and base-metal indicators. Drilling is ongoing and copper is mentioned among soil geochemistry, but there’s no production or market-moving supply data. Aluminium is not addressed.

title: Copper around 3-1/2-month low on demand concerns, risk-off sentiment
summary: Copper prices fell again, hovering near a three-and-a-half month low on demand concerns in China and risk-off sentiment. Lower-than-expected Q2 growth and limited stimulus to support the property sector drove sell-off. Investors also weighed potential U.S. tariff risks to global demand.

title: Department of Defense Awards $23 Million to Augment the United States Domestic Aluminum Casting Supply Chain
summary: The U.S. DoD awarded $23 million under the Defense Production Act to Constellium Muscle Shoals to add up to 300 million pounds of annual aluminum casting capacity. The project is intended to secure supply for U.S. mills, increase recycled input, reduce reliance on primary metal, and strengthen defense-related aluminum supply resilience.

title: The City of Chapais and QC Copper & Gold Establish a Framework for Collaboration on Opémiska
summary: Chapais, Quebec and QC Copper & Gold created a City/Mine Group framework to oversee exploration and eventual development of the Opémiska project. The company highlights a large copper resource inventory and local procurement commitments, while indicating further work for a preliminary economic study. The update is mainly procedural, with limited immediate supply impact.

title: Copper falls to 3-1/2-month low on high inventory, selling by funds
summary: Copper prices fell to a 3-1/2-month low as LME inventories rose to a 34-week high, climbing 28% since early July, suggesting weaker consumption. Managed futures/CTA funds also continued selling copper, adding downward pressure. Other metals were mixed, but copper showed the clear negative move.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd.: Aston Bay and American West Metals Confirm Expansion of High-Grade Copper Zones at the Storm Project, Nunavut, Canada
summary: Aston Bay and American West update drilling at the Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, reporting thick visual copper sulfide intervals across prospects (notably Thunder and Cyclone) and planned receipt of assays within two weeks. The results suggest lateral and depth continuity, though grades remain unconfirmed and no immediate production change is stated.

title: Demand for aluminium in green transition supporting otherwise challenging downstream markets: Norsk Hydro CEO
summary: Norsk Hydro’s CEO said aluminium demand in Asia is “quite good,” citing rising Chinese demand for grid infrastructure and solar panels, outweighing weak construction. Primary aluminium production in China hit a decade high. While European extrusion demand fell year on year, green-transition demand supports the globally traded aluminium market.

title: ACG's Gediktepe deal first step in creating mid-tier copper producer | Hotter Commodities
summary: ACG’s SPAC move centers on acquiring Turkey’s Gediktepe mine and expanding it into primary copper production. The sulfide expansion is expected to add up to 25,000 tonnes/year of copper from 2026, with a longer potential life. The deal signals active investment and supply growth expectations for copper.

title: Core Nickel Announces Completion of Airborne Geophysical Surveys at Halfway Lake and Resting Lake Projects in the Central Thompson Nickel Belt, Manitoba
summary: Core Nickel reports completion of airborne geophysical surveys and receipt of an exploration work permit for its Halfway Lake and Resting Lake nickel projects in Manitoba. The company plans ground geophysics and diamond drilling into high-priority targets through April 2025. The news is exploration-focused without near-term production impacts.

title: World Copper Ltd. and CEO Provide Corporate Update
summary: World Copper Ltd. provided a corporate update and progress overview for its Zonia copper project in Arizona, citing a large copper resource, planned SX-EW cathode production, and potential pre-production revenue from stockpiled material. The article is a development narrative without immediate supply or demand shocks for copper.

title: Kobrea Receives Exploration Permits for Upland Copper Project
summary: Kobrea Exploration received permits from the British Columbia Ministry of Energy, Mines and Low Carbon Innovation to conduct exploration at its Upland Copper Project, including passive seismic work, trenching, and diamond drilling. The copper-dominant VMS deposit is described as open for expansion, but no production timelines are given.

title: Osisko Metals Provides Update at Gaspé Copper
summary: Osisko Metals provided an update on summer work at its Gaspé Copper project, including 11 drill holes totaling ~2,600 metres, additional 4,500-metre drilling at Copper Mountain, and extensive surface-water sampling to assess pit-water quality and downstream impacts. The company reiterates PEA timing for early 2025.

title: Teck cuts copper forecast as it experiences more bumps with QB2 mine ramp-up
summary: Teck cut its full-year copper forecast by just under 7% after grade issues at its QB2 open-pit mine in northern Chile. Geotechnical instability and pit dewatering are limiting access to higher-grade ore, prompting production guidance reductions and investor concern early in the mine ramp-up.

title: China Starts Work On Afghan Copper Mine Long Stalled By War
summary: China and the Taliban government began ground-breaking on an Afghan copper mine that has been stalled for 16 years due to war. The project targets the world’s second-largest copper deposit, potentially improving future supply prospects. Near term, physical output is unlikely to start immediately, but sentiment may turn supportive for copper.

title: Net-Zero Targets Could Double Yearly Copper Demand by 2035
summary: The article says Vedanta has paid $245.75 million to complete its “KCM scheme” arrangement, potentially reinstating KCM’s board and restoring full management control. That could help boost production at the major Zambian copper mine, supporting copper supply expectations while demand growth driven by net-zero targets remains a bullish backdrop.

title: Teck Resources achieves record copper output as QB mine project continues to ramp up
summary: Teck says it achieved record copper output in Q2, with production rising 71% year-on-year and ramp-up continuing at Chile’s Quebrada Blanca project. The firm lowered its 2024 copper forecast after geotechnical and port filter issues, but expects full capacity later this year.

title: First Quantum Minerals announces commercial production at Africa's biggest nickel miner
summary: First Quantum Minerals announced commercial production at its nickel project in Zambia’s northwest and reported second-quarter nickel output of 6,147 tonnes versus 4,031 tonnes in the first quarter. The company plans to complete a smelter plant by mid-2025, supporting future ore processing and supply continuity.

title: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Reports Second Quarter 2024 Financial Results
summary: Kaiser Aluminum’s Q2 results showed lower shipments and conversion revenue, with management revising its 2024 outlook due to reduced commercial jet build rates and an extended outage at its Warrick facility. The company also highlighted continued hedged exposure to aluminum alloy costs tied to the Midwest Transaction Price.

title: Chinese engineers, Taliban break ground on Afghanistan's copper mining project after 16-year delay
summary: Chinese engineers and the Taliban broke ground on Afghanistan’s Mes Aynak, a major copper deposit, after a 16-year delay. Surveyors estimate 11.5 million tonnes of copper ore. While demand is strong, first extraction is expected in about two years, so near-term copper price pressure is likely limited.

title: First Quantum Minerals announces commercial production at Africa's biggest nickel miner-Xinhua
summary: First Quantum Minerals announced commercial production at its nickel mining project in northwestern Zambia, reporting nickel output rising to 6,147 tonnes in Q2 from 4,031 tonnes in Q1. The company says ramp-up is meeting expectations and cites plans to complete a smelter by mid-2025.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp: Nickel 28 Announces TSXV Acceptance of Normal Course Issuer Bid
summary: Nickel 28 Capital Corp. announced TSXV acceptance of a normal course issuer bid to repurchase up to 7.15 million shares over 12 months. The company is a nickel-cobalt producer via its interest in the Ramu operation, but the release does not change production, supply, or demand fundamentals for nickel.

title: First Quantum Announces Commercial Production at Enterprise Nickel Project
summary: First Quantum declared commercial production at its Enterprise nickel mine in Zambia and reported Q2 output rising to 6,147 tonnes from 4,031 tonnes in Q1. It also lifted 2024 contained nickel guidance to 17,000–20,000 tonnes, signaling stronger near-term nickel supply prospects.

title: Liquidator for Clive Palmer's former company Queensland Nickel says creditors paid in full
summary: The liquidator of Queensland Nickel says creditors have been paid in full after the Yabulu nickel refinery collapse in 2016. While most coverage is legal wind-down, it also cites BHP idling WA nickel mines because of global oversupply and volatile pricing, implying near-term bearish pressure on nickel sentiment.

title: Copper falls below $9,000 level on China demand concerns
summary: London copper fell below $9,000/t for the first time since early April, down 1.9% to $8,933.50, amid worries over China’s demand after a political meeting produced no targeted support for growth or property. Physical demand stayed weak with high inventories, pressuring also nickel and aluminium.

title: Centaurus Metals: Nickel sulphides – A$175m cash flow a year for 18 years – that will do!
summary: Centaurus Metals’ managing director discusses the company’s recent feasibility study for its nickel sulphide project. The article emphasizes a projected A$175m annual cash flow for 18 years and frames the project as positioned to benefit from the current “battery metals” cycle, supporting positive nickel sentiment in the market.

title: NST ASX: Gold miner Northern Star sees silver lining in BHP nickel woes
summary: Northern Star’s CEO says labor-cost pressures in Australian resources may plateau as the nickel industry in Western Australia runs into trouble following BHP’s nickel collapse. He also cites weaker lithium and shutdowns of high-cost iron ore operations. The remarks imply nickel supply disruption could support nickel pricing.

title: Two workers critically injured replacing stolen copper lines
summary: Two Las Vegas public works workers were critically injured replacing stolen copper lines. The county says 184 miles of wire were stolen since 2022, prompting work to replace copper and switch some streetlight wiring to overhead aluminum wire. The story implies local replacement demand, but no market-wide supply shocks.

title: Copper falls below $9,000 level as bleak demand outlook weighs
summary: London copper fell below $9,000 for the first time since early April, down 1.4% to $8,981.5/t, driven by investor risk-off sentiment and weaker China demand expectations after no supportive policy measures. Weak physical demand and high inventories were cited, alongside equity losses. Nickel and aluminium also fell.

title: Kincora Copper Limited: Kincora Copper Announces ANT and Gravity Geophysical Surveys at the Nyngan Project
summary: Kincora Copper announced ANT and gravity surveys at its Nyngan Project with Fleet Space Technologies, aimed at identifying and refining copper porphyry targets ahead of upcoming drilling under an earn-in and joint venture with AngloGold Ashanti. Surveys are set for early to mid-August, with interpretation targeting faster drill planning.

title: Copper falls below $9,000 level prompting Chinese buying
summary: Copper slipped below $9,000 on LME as funds sold after an overshoot, while breaking technical support. The move triggered stronger Chinese physical interest: import premiums rose to the highest in over three months and rod plants in Jiangsu increased output on incoming orders, partially offsetting bearish sentiment.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Intersects 0.62% Copper Over 29.08 Metres Within 190.25 Metres at 0.23% Copper Near Surface at the Prada Breccia in the American Eagle Area
summary: Faraday Copper reported additional drill results from the Copper Creek Project in Arizona, including a 29.08m intercept at 0.62% copper at the Prada breccia and other near-surface mineralization. The company says results could support open-pit resource growth, as Phase III drilling continues.

title: Coppernico Metals begins drilling at Sombrero project in Peru
summary: Coppernico Metals has begun a 6,500m core drilling program at its Sombrero copper-gold project in Peru, targeting copper-rich skarn mineralisation at the Ccascabamba area. The program includes 16 diamond drill holes in Phase I, with Phase II planned for 2025, aiming to confirm resources.

title: Copper sinks below US$9,000 threshold as metals selloff deepens
summary: Copper is reported to have fallen below the US$9,000 level as the metals selloff intensifies. This suggests investors are reducing exposure to industrial metals, creating short-term downside pressure on copper prices over the coming days.

title: Kobrea gets exploration permits for Canadian copper project
summary: Kobrea Exploration secured permits from British Columbia for work on its Upland Copper Project, including diamond drilling and trenching. The copper-dominant VMS deposit shows depth and expansion potential based on historical drilling and anomalies. Activities this year will further define mineralisation, but no production is indicated.

title: Electra Identifies New Copper Showing in Idaho and Extends Redcastle Agreement
summary: Electra Battery Materials said it identified a new copper surface showing (Malachite Hill) on Idaho’s Redcastle Agreement area, with grab samples reporting elevated copper (up to 2,660 ppm) and plans for follow-up mapping and sampling between the showing and its Ruby target, subject to financing. Agreement dates were extended to 2028.

title: Brixton Metals Provides Initial Assays from the 2024 Drill Program at its Thorn Project with 1467.73m of Copper-Gold-Silver-Molybdenum with Several Sub-intervals
summary: Brixton Metals reported initial 2024 drill assay results from its Thorn Project, highlighting long broad copper-dominant porphyry intervals with associated Au, Ag and Mo, and noting mineralization remains open at depth. The company is awaiting additional hole results; no nickel or aluminium supply-demand drivers were cited.

title: Taliban start building road for huge Chinese copper mining project
summary: Afghanistan’s Taliban began building a road to the remote site of MCC’s planned large copper mine, a project long delayed by instability and infrastructure gaps. Officials and China representatives attended. MCC expects to push for operations but timing remains unclear, yet progress can improve near-term supply expectations for copper.

title: Amman Mineral Secures Export Permit for 534,000 Dry Metric Tons of Copper Concentrate
summary: Indonesia’s Amman Mineral Nusa Tenggara received a government export permit for 534,000 dry metric tons of copper concentrate through Dec. 31. The permit follows completion of smelter construction by its affiliate Amman Mineral Industri, and the company expects first copper cathode output in Q4 2024.

title: China Breaks Ground On Massive Afghan Copper Mine After 16 Years Of Delays
summary: China’s state-owned MCC has broken ground on the Mes Aynak copper mine in Afghanistan after 16 years of delay, including building a road to the site. First copper is expected in at least two years. The restart follows improved security and growing China-Taliban ties, potentially supporting copper market sentiment despite short-term constraints.

title: US copper supply to grow by 4% in 2024
summary: US copper mine production is forecast to rise 4% in 2024 as output improves at major operations like Robinson, Pinto Valley, and the ramp-up of Pumpkin Hollow. The article cites higher recovery rates, richer ore, and throughput expansions, increasing supply expectations and weighing on copper prices.

title: 7 Best Copper Stocks to Buy According to Analysts
summary: The article argues copper remains supported by supply constraints and rising demand expectations tied to AI, electric vehicles, and electricity growth. It cites steep declines in LME and global copper stocks, the Cobre Panama suspension and other producers’ guidance cuts, and notes strong recent copper price gains.

title: Brixton Metals Corporation Provides Initial Assays from the 2024 Drill Program At Its Thorn Project with 1467.73M of Copper-Gold-Silver-Molybdenum with Several Sub-Intervals
summary: Brixton Metals announced initial 2024 drill assays from its Thorn Project in NW British Columbia, describing copper-dominant porphyry Cu-Au-Ag-Mo mineralization, with multiple higher-grade sub-intervals and extended mineralization in hole THN24-290. The company is running two rigs and continuing geophysics and geochemistry.

title: South Pacific Metals Corp. Announces Mobilization for Its First Multi-Stage Exploration Program of 2024 At Its Anga Gold-Copper Project
summary: South Pacific Metals Corp. mobilized a three-week exploration program at its Anga gold-copper project in Papua New Guinea’s Kainantu District. Work will include soil sampling and mapping targeting lode-gold and base-metal mineralization, with a reported nearby copper-rich float sample. No production or supply impact is announced.

title: Global spot copper markets mixed; China ticks up, US tight, Europe quiet
summary: Fastmarkets reports that China’s copper cathode premiums (cif Shanghai and in-whs) jumped on improved LME–SHFE arbitrage and stronger import buying. It also cites shipment delays from Africa that reduce spot availability. The US Midwest premium narrowed, while Europe and Southeast Asia stayed quiet, implying net near-term bullish copper support.

title: Freeport-McMoRan's Kathleen Quirk says copper scarcity means companies are buying rather than building new supply
summary: Freeport-McMoRan CEO Kathleen Quirk says copper supply is scarce: actionable new projects are limited, permitting and development lead times are long, and new discoveries are difficult. With uncertainty around building new supply, companies may seek copper exposure by buying existing material, reinforcing near-term tightness.

title: Gold Price Sinks as Shanghai Premium Vanishes, Copper Falls with Silver
summary: Gold prices fell as the Shanghai gold premium collapsed, removing incentives for bullion imports into China amid a lack of stimulus. The stronger US GDP data and worsening risk sentiment pushed industrial commodities lower, and the article notes copper also declined alongside silver.

title: DHS' Second UFLPA Strategy Update: Aluminum, PVC, and Seafood Enter the UFLPA's Purview for Scrutiny and Enforcement | ArentFox Schiff
summary: The DHS UFLPA Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force published its second strategy update, expanding the entity list and naming aluminum as a new high-priority enforcement sector. The move implies more detentions, heightened importer scrutiny, and release-form/addendum requirements, which can tighten near-term aluminum supply and weigh on prices.

title: Eramet lifts profit outlook on manganese rally, says nickel market tough
summary: Eramet raised its full-year earnings outlook on a manganese ore rally but warned the nickel market remains tough. The firm cited a 27% first-half EBITDA drop pressured by weaker nickel prices and a supply surplus. Violence in New Caledonia disrupted SLN nickel output, adding downside risk for nickel sentiment.

title: Copper still an attractive long-term investment despite recent selloff: analyst
summary: An analyst says global copper fundamentals are still weak: China demand is soft, especially tied to the property market, while supply appears “pretty strong,” leaving markets oversupplied. Copper has fallen ~20% from mid-May highs, and the analyst expects near-term volatility and continued spot weakness.

title: First Quantum copper mine not on government agenda this year, Panama's Mulino says
summary: Panama’s President Mulino said the government will not address issues around First Quantum’s shuttered Cobre Panama copper mine until early 2025, with higher-priority matters taking precedence. The mine was shut in November after a court ruling voided the contract. First Quantum says it does not expect reopening this year, suggesting ongoing copper supply risk.

title: China Begins Work on Massive Afghan Copper Mine
summary: Chinese engineers began construction on the Mes Aynak copper mine in Afghanistan under a MCC concession. A road is being built to the site, with first copper extraction likely in about two years. The start follows years of conflict and may boost expectations for future copper supply despite ongoing security risks.

title: EPA flags Huntington as area of concern for toxic air pollutants from nickel emissions
summary: The EPA flagged parts of Huntington, West Virginia, as an area of concern for toxic air pollutants tied to nickel emissions from Special Metals’ Huntington division. Officials highlighted health risks from long-term nickel exposure and workers’ exposure. WVDEP will hold a public meeting to discuss the findings, potentially prompting tighter controls.

title: Vale S.A. (VALE): The Best Copper Stock to Buy According to Analysts?
summary: The piece highlights strengthening copper prices and a tight physical market, citing sharp declines in LME warehouse stocks and broader supply constraints from mine suspensions/reduced guidance, including Cobre Panama. It also points to rising demand linked to AI-driven power/energy infrastructure, implying supportive near-term expectations for copper.

title: Flying Nickel Announces Voting Results from Annual General and Special Meeting
summary: Flying Nickel Mining Corp. announces strong shareholder approval of its arrangement with Nevada Vanadium, subject to court, stock exchange, and regulatory approvals, with expected completion in August 2024. The company is an exploration-stage nickel sulphide developer advancing its Minago nickel project; no immediate production or supply changes are stated.

title: Panama Delays Action on First Quantum Copper Mine Until 2025
summary: Panama’s President said the government will not address issues around First Quantum’s shuttered Cobre Panama copper mine until early 2025. The Supreme Court invalidated the contract, and the mine is unlikely to reopen this year amid ongoing environmental protests. The delay suggests sustained copper supply disruption risk.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp.: Flying Nickel Announces Voting Results from Annual General and Special Meeting
summary: Flying Nickel Mining Corp. reports overwhelming shareholder approval of an arrangement with Nevada Vanadium and expects to complete closing in August 2024, subject to regulatory and court approvals. It also notes its Minago nickel project. The announcement is deal/process-focused with no stated immediate effect on nickel supply or demand.

title: Hudbay Minerals Inc. (HBM): Hedge Funds Are Bullish on This Copper Stock Right Now
summary: The article argues for bullish copper prospects, highlighting tight LME copper inventories and supply constraints tied to mine disruptions such as the suspension of Panama’s Cobre Panama. It also points to potential demand growth from AI/data centers, EVs, and electricity infrastructure, using these themes to justify optimism on Hudbay’s copper exposure.

title: Why Is Ivanhoe Electric Inc. (IE) the Best Copper Stock to Buy Right Now?
summary: The piece is an analyst-stock roundup but uses copper market context to argue for upside. It cites LME copper gains since ChatGPT’s release, tightening warehouse stocks, and supply constraints from mine disruptions and reduced producer guidance (including Cobre Panama-related shutdowns). It also points to rising demand drivers like data centers and EVs.

title: Southern Copper : SCC Conference Call 2Q 2024 transcript
summary: Southern Copper’s earnings call discusses the copper market: LME copper is up year-on-year and the company expects a ~217,000-ton 2024 deficit based on producer cuts. It also highlights resilient demand despite weak China real estate. The call focuses on its copper production and costs, but the market outlook is supportive.

title: Southern Copper : 2Q24 Conference Call transcript
summary: Southern Copper’s 2Q24 call discusses a stronger copper backdrop, citing LME copper rising and a projected 2024 supply deficit (~217,000 tons) alongside production growth at its Peru and Mexico assets. Management also reiterates cost guidance and Tia Maria project progression, supporting near-term copper market sentiment.

title: NorthWest Copper Announces Results of 2024 AGM
summary: NorthWest Copper reported results of its 2024 AGM, including re-election of directors, auditor reappointment, and approval of an equity incentive plan. The company is a copper-gold explorer, but the update contains no material information on output, major project milestones, or supply-demand conditions for copper in the next few weeks.

title: London copper edges lower as China demand outlook weighs
summary: London copper was subdued, slipping slightly as worries about demand in China, the top consumer, weighed on prices. Support came from better-than-expected U.S. data that reinforced expectations for a September Fed rate cut, keeping the dollar steady and lifting some other base metals including nickel and aluminium.

title: Indonesia moves to reduce China's investment in nickel projects
summary: Indonesia is seeking to cut Chinese investment in new nickel mining and processing projects to help qualify for US tax breaks under the Inflation Reduction Act. The incentives exclude EV batteries and critical minerals sourced from entities of concern with substantial Chinese ownership, prompting Indonesia to adjust project participation.

title: Chinese firms seek to cut stakes in new Indonesian nickel smelters
summary: The article says Chinese firms are trying to reduce their stakes in new Indonesian nickel smelters. Such moves can imply less committed investment and possible delays or adjustments in processing capacity, which may support tighter nickel supply expectations and help underpin nickel prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Chinese Firms Seek to Cut Stakes in New Indonesian Nickel Smelters
summary: Chinese firms are negotiating to cut stakes in Indonesian nickel smelters and HPAL projects so U.S. buyers can qualify for IRA EV tax credits under the 25% foreign-entity-of-concern rule. Indonesia is also working with Washington to include its nickel supply chain. These steps may boost near-term nickel demand sentiment.

title: Luhut to pitch nickel projects to Elon Musk - Companies
summary: Indonesia’s Luhut Pandjaitan says he will invite Tesla CEO Elon Musk to invest in Indonesia’s nickel industry during a US meeting next month. He provides no project specifics and notes Tesla has no near-term EV-plant plans, but Indonesia’s importance to Tesla’s nickel supply keeps sentiment supportive for nickel.

title: Copper set for third weekly decline on Chinese demand woes
summary: Copper is set for a third straight weekly decline as China’s economic weakness raises doubts that renewed physical buying will last. Three-month LME copper is slightly higher on the day but down sharply on the week. Analysts note short-term support near $9,000, yet downside persists into a quieter second half.

title: World-famous blue NIVEA Creme tin now made from 80% recycled aluminium
summary: Beiersdorf’s NIVEA Creme tin will use at least 80% recycled aluminium, developed with supplier Novelis, aiming to cut about 8,000 tons of CO2e emissions by 2025. The move highlights reduced energy use versus virgin aluminium, but also notes recycled material availability as a key constraint.

title: Scotiabank's top picks in copper miners as the commodity price corrects
summary: Scotiabank revisits its copper price assumptions, noting copper miners embed an implied price above spot despite heightened volatility, and it recommends selected copper stocks. Other sections discuss macro-driven portfolio repositioning, including liquidation of crowded “long copper” trades and key copper futures levels to watch, implying mixed near-term pressure.

title: NPI and refined nickel show mixed performance. Will the discount narrow again?
summary: SMM reports NPI prices rose on tight supply: laterite ore shortages in Indonesia persist, smelter inventories remain low, and July NPI output is expected to decline. Chinese stainless demand is stable, with spot prices firm. Refined nickel fell amid US-election risk, yet cost support limits downside and narrows the NPI discount.

title: Copper Price Set to Rebound Amid Supply Shortages and EV Demand Surge, Miners Respond
summary: Copper is seen rebounding after a recent sharp decline, with analysts pointing to a Chinese smelter supply shortage and constrained mine supply that could tighten availability. The piece also highlights EV-driven demand growth and ongoing miner investment/asset moves supporting future supply.

title: USA News Group; Energy Metals News: Copper Price Set to Rebound Amid Supply Shortages and EV Demand Surge, Miners Respond
summary: The piece says copper has hit record highs and argues the rally can continue due to potential supply shortages and accelerating demand from EVs, renewables, AI data centers and major grid upgrades. It frames these factors as increasingly tight copper fundamentals, implying bullish near-term price pressure.

title: Cyprium, Glencore tie up to resurrect Nifty copper production in WA
summary: Cyprium and Glencore have signed agreements to restart copper production at the Nifty complex in Western Australia. Glencore will buy 100% of cathodes produced and support operations via technology, sulphuric acid options, and concentrate sales arrangements. The deal provides start-up revenue certainty and supply input flexibility, supporting copper sentiment.

title: 'We Can't Even Open The Window': Residents Grapple With Pollution from Chinese Copper Mine In Serbia
summary: Residents and officials in Bor, Serbia complain that Zijin’s Chinese-backed copper mine and smelter expansion has not materially improved pollution and health impacts. The operation has faced fines, a prior order to pause work for environmental non-compliance, and continued allegations of harmful emissions tied to increased output capacity.

title: Copper trades in tight range as investors assess economic outlook
summary: Copper prices were range-bound after three weeks of declines as investors assessed the global economic outlook ahead of the Fed meeting and multiple U.S./Eurozone data releases. Copper, aluminium, and nickel quotes in the article showed only small day-to-day moves, suggesting muted net price pressure in the near term.

title: New Caledonia's mothballed nickel plant starts mass sackings process
summary: New Caledonia’s mothballed Koniambo nickel plant (KNS) has begun mass layoffs as Glencore seeks an exit and the 31 August timeline nears without a finalized buyer. Ongoing unrest has targeted nickel sites, while New Caledonia’s nickel sector faces collapse amid a weak global nickel market dominated by low-cost Indonesian supply.

title: Copper slides as investors assess demand outlook
summary: Copper prices fell on Monday as investors reassessed China’s demand outlook. Three-month LME copper slid to about $9,055/ton and September SHFE copper dipped slightly. The market is waiting for the Fed meeting and upcoming U.S. and Eurozone data, but current demand worries are weighing on prices.

title: Indonesia pushes for lowering Chinese stake in nickel projects
summary: Indonesia is restructuring nickel mining and processing deals to reduce Chinese ownership in projects to qualify for US IRA incentives tied to critical minerals. The government is pushing new smelter investments with China holding minority stakes (<25%), aiming to sustain or expand nickel processing eligibility and production expectations.

title: Community Scoop » New Caledonia's Mothballed Nickel Plant Starts Mass Sackings Process
summary: New Caledonia’s Koniambo (KNS) nickel plant has begun mass lay-offs ahead of the end of a six-month respite, leaving only maintenance staff for a “cold” sleep. The decision follows Glencore’s earlier exit plans and persistent unrest that has damaged/targeted nickel sites, worsening the already weak global nickel market.

title: Indonesia pushes for Chinese stake decrease in nickel projects
summary: Indonesia is reportedly pushing for Chinese stakeholders to reduce their stakes in nickel projects. The move could alter project development and financing dynamics, influencing expectations for near-term nickel output and supply availability. That supply-effect potential can shift sentiment in nickel pricing over the coming days to weeks.

title: New Caledonia's Mothballed Nickel Plant Starts Mass Sackings Process
summary: New Caledonia’s Koniambo (KNS) nickel plant began mass layoff processes after being mothballed, with a deadline for a “cold” sleep state as ownership and buyer options remain unresolved. The country’s unrest has also targeted nickel sites, adding supply disruption amid a broader nickel-price crisis.

title: Aluminium Bahrain B S C : Alba Secures Capral Aluminium as First Customer for Groundbreaking EternAl Low-Carbon Aluminium
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) says it has secured Capral Aluminium as the first customer for its EternAl low-carbon aluminium primary billet, launched in May 2024. The product targets 15%–30% recycled content with DNV verification. Capral completed successful trials, enabling wider supply to Australian manufacturing sectors.

title: Canada Nickel Provides Update on Crawford Project Optimization and Commencement of Pilot Plant Operation
summary: Canada Nickel reported improved testwork at its Crawford East Zone, including a locked-cycle result delivering 47% total nickel recovery and 60% nickel sulphide concentrate, with open-circuit tests averaging 28% higher recovery than modelled. A 130-tonne pilot plant began commissioning and will run until September to generate concentrate samples.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Hosts Strategic Investor Site Visit, Expands Geological Team, and Reports Milestones on Infrastructure Upgrades at Atlantic Nickel Project
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reports progress at its Atlantic Nickel Project in Newfoundland, including a completed investor site visit, a bridge installed for year-round access, permits filed for additional road work, and expanded geological activity targeting awaruite nickel occurrences. The updates support ongoing exploration that may bolster longer-term nickel supply expectations.

title: Copper loses ground on weak Chinese demand, high stocks
summary: Reuters reports copper fell on Monday due to concerns over weak Chinese demand and elevated inventories. LME three-month copper dropped about 0.7% to $9,045/ton, with LME stocks more than doubling since early June. Macro expectations around Fed rate cuts also influenced sentiment across metals.

title: Copper Loses Ground on Weak Chinese Demand, High Stocks
summary: Copper prices fell on Monday as market participants grew concerned about weak Chinese demand and noted high inventories. Three-month LME copper dropped 0.7% to about $9,045/ton. The move followed a large pullback from late-May highs, with traders waiting for Fed and U.S. data for direction.

title: Royal Road Minerals Announces Results of Infill Soil Geochemical Sampling and Updates on Drill Permitting: Alouana Copper-Gold Project, Kingdom of Morocco
summary: Royal Road Minerals reported infill soil geochemical sampling results and progress on drill permitting for its Alouana copper-gold polymetallic project in Morocco. The company refined copper anomaly zones and plans scout drilling, but the release does not mention production volumes or any immediate supply change.

title: Russia's Nornickel sticks to production outlook despite furnace repairs
summary: Nornickel reported a 1% nickel output drop in H1 due to furnace repairs at the Nadezhda smelter but kept full-year nickel guidance at 184,000–194,000 tonnes. It also noted lingering constraints from delayed Western-sourced equipment and the US/UK nickel/aluminium/copper trading and import bans, with repairs resuming early August.

title: Funds dump copper as rising stocks dampen bull spirits: Andy Home
summary: Funds have sharply reduced long exposure to copper on the back of rising inventories and increased Chinese exports into LME warehouses. LME stocks are at a three-year peak and ShFE stocks remain high, dampening the scarcity narrative and contributing to price retreat, despite forecasts for recovery later in 2024.

title: Pan Asia Metals signs exclusivity deal on Chilean copper project
summary: Pan Asia Metals signed an exclusivity agreement to conduct due diligence on Chile’s Rosario Copper Project and may move toward an option acquisition. The project is near existing copper infrastructure and reports high-grade results. However, it is still an early-stage development step, unlikely to materially shift near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Funds dump copper as rising stocks dampen bull spirits
summary: Funds cut long exposure in copper as inventories rise. China’s property drag keeps demand weak, while Chinese smelters export larger volumes into LME warehouses, lifting LME stock to a three-year peak and pushing the LME three-month price down. Analysts warn copper may struggle for direction in coming weeks.

title: China's nickel sulfate price edges down on slow demand
summary: Fastmarkets reports China nickel sulfate prices edging down, citing slow demand, weaker liquidity, and continued declines in the three-month LME nickel cash price. It also links softer international nickel sulfate activity to BHP’s suspension at Nickel West and West Musgrave, weighing on market sentiment.

title: Vedanta Nico Partners with AEsir Technologies to Propel Next-Gen Nickel-Zinc Batteries
summary: Vedanta Nico, a Vedanta subsidiary, partnered with US battery technology firm AEsir Technologies to supply nickel for next-generation nickel-zinc batteries for EVs, 5G telecom and critical infrastructure. The move highlights growing nickel demand for battery cathodes, potentially supporting near-term nickel price sentiment.

title: Copper-Gold Miner Royal Road Minerals (TSXV: RYR) Announces Results of Infill Soil Geochemical Sampling and Updates on Drill Permitting
summary: Royal Road Minerals reported infill soil geochemical results at its Alouana copper-gold project in Morocco and said drill permitting is advancing for a planned 2,000-meter scout program. The news refines near-surface copper anomaly targets but does not indicate immediate production changes or supply shocks.

title: MAX RESOURCE : ANNOUNCES THE 2024 EXPLORATION PROGRAM FOR THE SIERRA AZUL COPPER SILVER PROJECT, FUNDED BY FREEPORT MCMORAN EXPLORATION CORPORATION
summary: MAX Resource announced a US$4.2m 2024 exploration program for the Sierra Azul copper-silver project in Colombia, funded by Freeport-McMoRan under an earn-in agreement. Work includes regional sampling, mapping, geophysics, and target drilling preparation, aiming to delineate copper drill targets across multiple districts.

title: ASX BHP: BHP buys copper darling Filo
summary: BHP will invest $US2.1 billion to expand its South American copper business through a 50:50 joint venture in Chile–Argentina’s Vicuna district with Filo Corp and Lundin Mining. The project targets multiple copper prospects near BHP’s Escondida area, signalling growth plans rather than an immediate supply change.

title: BHP advances copper ambitions with acquisition and JV
summary: BHP and Lundin Mining agreed to buy Filo Corp, which owns the Filo del Sol copper project, and to form a 50/50 JV to progress the Filo del Sol and Josemaria projects in Argentina/Chile’s Vicuña district. BHP plans a $2.1bn cash payment; closing is expected in Q1 2025.

title: Tanzania to Pay $90m to Australian Firm in Nickel Mining Dispute
summary: Tanzania agreed to pay US$90 million in instalments to Australia’s Indiana Resources to settle an ICSID dispute over cancellation of its Ntaka Hill nickel licence. The article describes the project’s nickel sulphide potential but offers no concrete near-term production impact, implying minimal effect on global nickel pricing.

title: China demand concerns, risk-off sentiment drag copper below $9,000/t
summary: Copper extended its third straight drop on concerns about demand in top consumer China and uncertainty over when interest-rate cuts will arrive. Chinese stimulus aimed more at consumers than infrastructure and property weakness weighed. The piece also reports aluminium fell as risk-off sentiment dragged industrial metals.

title: Kenorland Minerals Ltd.: Kenorland Enters Definitive Agreement to Sell the South Thompson Project to Evolution Nickel
summary: Kenorland Minerals entered a definitive agreement to sell 100% of its South Thompson nickel project to Evolution Nickel, receiving Evolution shares and a 2% net smelter return royalty. Closing is expected before end-2024 and depends on Evolution raising at least C$4m. The release is about exploration development, not production.

title: Battery Mineral Resources Corp.: Battery Mineral Resources Announces Second Shipment of Copper Concentrates to Anglo-American for Smelting
summary: Battery Mineral Resources announced its second shipment of copper concentrates (751.65 DMT) to Anglo American’s Chagres smelter in Chile, totaling 1,255 DMT delivered in July. The company says Punitaqui flotation output is ramping after refurbishing processing capacity, projecting higher monthly concentrate deliveries.

title: BHP swoops on Filo in US$3 billion South American copper deal
summary: BHP has agreed a US$3 billion South American deal to acquire Filo, a copper-related asset. The announcement is likely to support sentiment around future copper supply and mining investment, which can translate into modest near-term upside pressure for copper prices over the coming days.

title: Trigon Metals Reports Q4 2024 Financial Results, Operating Costs Fall to $3.35/lb Copper Produced at Kombat Mine, Namibia
summary: Trigon Metals reported Q4 operating results for its Kombat copper mine in Namibia, stating C1 cash costs fell to $3.35/lb from $3.96/lb and production increased with higher ore tonnage and underground contribution. The firm attributes gains to operational improvements and Namibian dollar weakness.

title: BHP and Lundin Mining to jointly acquire FDS copper project owner in $3bn deal
summary: BHP and Lundin Mining agreed to acquire Filo, owner of Argentina’s Filo del Sol copper project, in a ~$3bn deal and then form a 50-50 JV to develop FDS alongside Josemaria. The transaction includes BHP buying Josemaria’s 50% stake and aims at phased development, subject to approvals.

title: Rail News - Copper-wire thefts impact Denver's light-rail service. For Railroad Career Professionals
summary: RTD in Denver reported multiple copper-wire thefts along light-rail and commuter-rail lines, causing signal problems, train delays, crossing arm issues, and bus shuttles. Most thefts targeted copper wiring tied to rail power and signaling systems. RTD is investigating additional cases and has used anti-theft measures previously.

title: Aluminum Prices Plummet Despite Green Energy Hype
summary: Aluminum prices have continued to fall on both the LME and China’s SHFE since early June, despite earlier bullish hopes tied to EVs, renewables, and grid spending. The decline is linked to weak Chinese demand, sluggish Europe/U.S. activity, rising inventories, record Chinese production, and high Russian/cheap imports creating oversupply.

title: FPX Nickel slashes carbon intensity by 50% for Baptiste project - Canadian Manufacturing
summary: FPX Nickel reports value engineering at its Baptiste project reduced estimated carbon intensity by 50% (to about 1.2 tCO2e/tNi), driven by trolley-assist haul trucks cutting diesel use ~50%. It also secured BC Hydro funding for electrification studies, improving economics and expected nickel operating competitiveness.

title: Miningnewsbreaks  Battery Mineral Resources Corp. (TSX.V: BMR) (OTCQB: BTRMF) Reports Second Shipment Of Copper Concentrates To Anglo-American
summary: Battery Mineral Resources says it has completed a second shipment of copper concentrates to Anglo-American. It projects near-term copper sales will come from its Punitaqui mine operations and additional third parties, aiming to build consistent cash flow from copper. The update is supportive for the company’s supply outlook, not clear macro pricing impact.

title: Cameroon signs bauxite deal with Canyon Resources
summary: Cameroon signed a bauxite mining agreement worth at least $2 billion with a subsidiary of Canyon Resources for the Minim-Martap project. The plan includes producing alumina from bauxite, transporting via existing rail to ports, and exporting the output. Mining is projected to begin in about two years.

title: Rio Tinto 1st Half Earnings Rise, Helped by Higher Copper Output, Prices
summary: Rio Tinto reported first-half profit up 14% as higher copper production and copper prices helped offset weaker performance from its iron-ore business. The miner said net profit rose to $5.81 billion and announced a dividend aligned with underlying earnings, reinforcing positive near-term copper market sentiment.

title: Codelco is working very hard to boost copper output, CEO says
summary: Codelco CEO Ruben Alvarado said the state-run producer is “working very hard” to recover copper output after an 8.4% drop in the first half of 2024, with production at a 25-year low. The company targets a turnaround in coming months to finish 2024 slightly above last year.

title: PTX Metals Inc. Announces Additional Wide Zones of Near Surface Copper Nickel Pge Mineralization At W2 Project
summary: PTX Metals reported additional near-surface drill results from its W2 Cu-Ni-PGE project in Ontario, citing higher confidence in continuity of mineralized zones and new intersections with disseminated to massive sulphides. The update is exploration-focused and does not signal near-term production impacts. Gold assays are also pending next week.

title: PTX Metals Inc. Announces Additional Wide Zones of Near Surface Copper Nickel Pge Mineralization At W2 Project
summary: PTX Metals released additional diamond-drill assay results from its 100%-owned W2 Cu-Ni-PGE project, expanding and confirming near-surface sulphide mineralization across several zones. Results increase confidence in continuity of historical zones. The release is exploratory and does not mention production, shipments, or new supply disruptions affecting prices.

title: Analysis: Govt expands Simbara system to tackle illegal nickel, tin practices - Academia
summary: Indonesia expanded its Simbara mining tracking system to cover nickel (and tin), following a corruption case and to improve governance. The move links production, sales, exports, royalties, and port clearance, targeting Rp 5–10 trillion in additional nickel-related royalties/PNBP. It should tighten oversight and reduce illegal supply.

title: Codelco Strives to Recover Copper Production Amid New Partnerships
summary: Chile’s Codelco said it is taking steps to recover copper production after output fell to a 25-year low. CEO Ruben Alvarado discussed efforts and suggested potential collaborations with Saudi mining officials, while talks referenced the Maricunga lithium project. Overall, investors may view improved copper-supply prospects as supportive for near-term prices.

title: BHP and Lundin Mining forge $4.5b deal to develop Filo del Sol copper project
summary: BHP and Lundin Mining agreed to buy Filo Corp for $4.53 billion and form a 50:50 JV to advance the Filo del Sol copper project in Argentina and Josemaria in Chile. The transaction includes interim financing and reflects growing commitment to the Vicuña copper district.

title: Police task force has success in fighting Los Angeles copper wire theft
summary: Los Angeles Police Department’s Heavy Metal Task Force says it has recovered over 2,000 pounds of stolen copper wire and made 82 arrests since early in the year. The city highlights copper theft from the 6th Street bridge, proposes stricter telecom-wire possession rules, and seeks measures to etch/brand public copper wiring.

title: Merdeka Copper Gold Makes Decarbonization Efforts for a Net-Zero Indonesia
summary: Merdeka Copper Gold (MDKA) is shifting its mining energy use from coal to renewables such as solar, alongside B35 biodiesel for vehicles and feasibility work for hydropower and wind. The transition is tied to operations including the Wetar copper mine and MDKA’s nickel assets, framed as cost-efficient ESG that may support output continuity.

title: Regional copper theft task force tackles crime across the Las Vegas Valley
summary: A newly formed task force in Las Vegas targets copper theft from streetlights and public utilities, citing nearly 971,000 feet of copper wire stolen since early 2022. Officials aim to pass local and state laws to curb sales of stolen copper, potentially reducing theft volumes and streetlight-related losses.

title: NIC ASX: Nickel boss says Indonesia trying to distance itself from China
summary: Indonesia’s Nickel Industries managing director said Indonesia may limit further Chinese investment in its nickel sector to avoid reliance on China and attract more Western capital. This policy risk can influence expectations for Indonesia’s nickel supply and near-term project development, offering support to nickel prices over the next weeks.

title: Rio Tinto logs H1 2024 profit growth on copper boom
summary: Rio Tinto reported H1 2024 net profit rising to $5.8bn, largely driven by higher copper production and higher copper prices, offsetting lower iron ore prices. It also reiterated copper-equivalent production growth on track for the year. The results signal supportive expectations for copper over the coming weeks.

title: Barminco extends stay at Khoemacau copper mine
summary: Perenti’s Barminco has finalized terms to continue its five-year underground mining services contract at MMG’s Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana until June 30, 2025, with remaining contract value about $240 million. The mine will execute the current plan while MMG assesses potential expansion to meet copper demand.

title: Queensland Government offers $13.5m for Harmony's Eva copper mine
summary: Queensland’s government granted Harmony a conditional A$20.7m for preparatory works at the Eva copper mine under a mining acceleration programme, helping infrastructure and early development toward production. The grant requires a positive FID by January 2026, but signals improved project momentum and support for future copper supply.

title: Canyon signs mining convention for Cameroon bauxite project
summary: Canyon Resources signed a mining convention for its Minim-Martap bauxite project in Cameroon, contingent on a mining permit, with government officials present. The step adds certainty to advance development work—especially port and rail access. It is a progress milestone, not an immediate supply change.

title: Copper theft causes Telus outage in Ogden affecting landlines, 911 service
summary: Copper wire theft at Telus damaged telecom cables in Calgary’s Ogden, disrupting landlines and potentially 911 service. Telus says TV/internet were restored and teams are working to restore phones. The incident follows multiple thefts across Canada, prompting calls for harsher penalties and improved security.

title: Bastion Minerals to acquire three copper assets in Canada
summary: Bastion Minerals agreed to buy three copper projects in Canada (ICE in Yukon, and Mariner and Harley in the Northwest Territories) from Arcus Resources. It will pay cash, issue shares, and grant options/performance shares tied to drilling and resource targets. The ICE resource is historical and high-grade.

title: Rio Tinto Eyes Copper Takeover as First-Half Profit Rises
summary: Rio Tinto reported slightly higher first-half profits and said it would consider a large acquisition in the copper business only if it offers value. The company is targeting modest copper output growth and analysts cited renewed takeover talk. Mentioned copper price strength and deal speculation are supportive for copper sentiment.

title: Aluminium Curtain Wall Market Size Projections Exhibit a
summary: The news is a market research outlook for the aluminium curtain wall industry, forecasting growth from USD 43 billion (2023) to USD 92.83 billion by 2033. It cites infrastructure spending, urbanisation, and technology upgrades driving construction demand, which could support aluminium demand and prices modestly.

title: Intalco aluminum plant fined $5.25 million for air pollution
summary: U.S. DOJ fined the closed Intalco aluminum smelting plant $5.25 million for repeated Clean Air Act violations, including illegal emissions monitoring and heavy-metal releases. The facility ceased operations as Alcoa curtailed output in March 2020 and permanently closed later, implying reduced aluminum supply and tighter regulatory risk for any future capacity.

title: Copper slides on China demand concerns
summary: Copper prices fell at the start of August as concerns grew over weakening Chinese demand, supported by a private survey showing manufacturing contracted and an official PMI hitting a five-month low. Despite some support from a narrower export parity and retreating inventories, higher exports boosted inventories. Powell’s rate-cut hint offered limited offset.

title: Mineral production sees robust growth in Q1, India 2nd largest aluminium producer in world
summary: India’s Ministry of Mines said primary aluminium output rose 1.2% in Q1 FY25 to 10.43 lakh tonnes versus 10.28 lakh tonnes a year earlier. The government also cited robust growth in iron ore and limestone. Continued aluminium production growth supports expectations of steady near-term supply.

title: Copper Miners Expand Operations to Address Global Supply Shortages
summary: Energy Metals News says copper miners are expanding and restarting operations to address global supply shortages. It highlights exploration and ramp-up at projects including Southern Copper’s Tia Maria restart, production increases at various mines, and new drilling updates. Overall messaging is that added near-term supply can ease tightness while demand grows.

title: Copper Falls on Soft Chinese Factory Data, Higher Inventories
summary: Copper prices fell as China’s factory data came in weaker than expected, reducing near-term demand expectations for the top metal consumer. At the same time, rising LME inventories pointed to excess supply. As a result, three-month LME copper declined 1.9% to around $9,048/ton.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Reports Second Quarter 2024 Results
summary: Capstone reported Q2 2024 results including 40,937 tonnes of copper production and improved profitability driven by a higher realized copper price versus the prior year. Mantoverde’s new concentrator produced first saleable concentrate in June and is expected to reach nameplate in Q3, supporting near-term copper output guidance.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Reports Second Quarter 2024 Financial Results
summary: Faraday Copper reports Q2 2024 financial results and provides ongoing drilling updates from its Copper Creek project in Arizona, including multiple copper intercepts and positive metallurgical testwork. It also notes the company’s need for continued financing and that it remains an exploration-stage entity without revenue or production.

title: Ero Copper Reports Second Quarter 2024 Operating and Financial Results
summary: Ero Copper reported Q2 2024 operating results, including first saleable copper concentrate from the Tucumã Project and continued ramp-up toward commercial production. The company produced 8,867 tonnes of copper in concentrate in Q2 and expects lower H2 copper C1 cash costs. Results were boosted by stronger metal prices and tight concentrate markets.

title: Indonesia identifies over 100 new potential nickel reserve sites-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia’s Geological Agency says it has identified more than 100 additional potential nickel reserve sites for further exploration. The government’s findings reinforce Indonesia’s role as the leading nickel producer, important for EV batteries. With output and export revenues already large, new prospective supply may ease supply concerns.

title: Indonesia identifies over 100 new potential nickel reserve sites
summary: Indonesia’s Geological Agency says it has identified over 100 additional potential nickel reserve sites for further exploration. The findings reinforce Indonesia’s role as the leading nickel producer used in EV batteries, but the report does not point to near-term production increases or export changes, suggesting limited immediate price pressure.

title: London copper gains but set for flat week amid dour demand outlook
summary: London copper rose 0.4% but was set for a flat week as investors await US jobs data while China’s demand outlook remains downbeat. Copper inventories stay high. LME aluminium edged down. Nickel prices were supported by tight Indonesian ore supply, but overall the week’s direction appears muted.

title: China sets renewable energy targets for aluminum production
summary: China’s state planner set renewable-energy targets for aluminium production in key provinces. Shandong is targeted for renewables to supply 21% of production energy, while Inner Mongolia and Yunnan face 29% and 70% respectively. The policy could affect production costs and supply timing for aluminium.

title: Indonesia Identifies Over 100 New Potential Nickel Reserve Sites
summary: Indonesia’s Geological Agency says it has identified more than 100 new potential nickel reserve locations and will continue exploration. The update strengthens Indonesia’s position as the leading global nickel producer used in EV batteries. With large existing output already, new prospects may support expectations for longer-term supply, mildly bullish for nickel.

title: Copper bounces on potential U.S. rate cuts
summary: Copper prices edged higher as markets increasingly priced potential U.S. interest-rate cuts, supporting the metal via a softer USD backdrop. Physical demand in China improved slightly, with the Yangshan copper premium rising to a three-month peak and SHFE deliverable inventories down, though investors stayed cautious on weak macro data.

title: Goldrea Expands Cannonball Project and Now Controls All Advanced Copper Gold Prospects Adjoining Seabridge's Iskut Project
summary: Goldrea Resources announced LOIs to acquire 50% interests in additional mineral claims adjoining its Cannonball Project, which hosts multiple porphyry copper-gold and copper-gold prospects. The company says the geology matches Seabridge’s Golden Triangle corridor and highlights recommended drilling. No production volumes, inventories, or near-term supply changes are reported.

title: Aluminium producer Alcoa closes acquisition of Alumina
summary: Alcoa has closed its all-stock acquisition of Alumina, expanding its upstream bauxite and alumina position and gaining full control of the AWAC JV. AWAC holds bauxite mines, alumina refineries and a smelter stake. The deal is framed as value creation and operational flexibility, implying limited immediate pricing impact for aluminium.

title: Iran's aluminum output hits record
summary: Iran’s IMIDRO said four major smelters produced a record 169,141 mt of aluminum ingots in the three months to June 20, up nearly 1.5% year on year. Growth was driven by smelter upgrades and better feedstock availability from domestic alumina and bauxite production.

title: Indonesia seeks to limit Chinese investments in nickel to qualify for U.S. tax breaks
summary: Indonesia plans to limit Chinese ownership in new nickel mining and processing projects so they qualify for U.S. tax incentives under the Inflation Reduction Act, which penalizes sourcing from “foreign entities of concern.” Indonesia is negotiating deal terms and smelter ownership thresholds, seeking U.S. trade agreement compliance.

title: London copper edges up after sell-offs, global demand concerns weigh
summary: London copper edged up 0.2% after prior sell-offs, as some dip-buying emerged, but global demand concerns capped upside. The U.S. jobs report and weaker China activity fueled recession worries while expectations of Fed cuts supported industrial demand. LME aluminium and nickel rose slightly, showing mixed sentiment.

title: China's CMOC and other miners of Congolese copper seek LME listing
summary: CMOC and other miners in the Democratic Republic of Congo have applied for their copper brands to be registered for delivery against LME contracts. If approved, DRC copper could enter LME warehouses from next year, supporting financing and exchange fee revenue. ESG oversight for DRC sourcing is also discussed.

title: Review and Outlook: China's Copper Rod H1 Earnings Results Released, H2 Consumption Highlights Preview!
summary: Article reviews China’s H1 2024 copper cathode rod market, linking moves in copper prices to RRR cuts, smelter processing-fee drops and production cuts, weak real-estate/infrastructure demand, and later a price correction that loosened order pressure.
