It previews H2 policy support and gradual demand release, but growth remains limited.

title: Global growth angst hits copper prices
summary: Copper prices tumbled as worsening China and U.S. demand outlooks sparked a sell-off. Weaker U.S. jobs data and technology earnings reinforced recession fears, while rising LME warehouse inventories weighed near term. The risk-off move also pushed aluminium and nickel modestly lower alongside copper.

title: Copper 360 Limited Announces Commencement of Underground Production at Rietberg Mine
summary: Copper 360 Limited began underground mining at the Rietberg copper mine in South Africa’s Northern Cape. Ore is processed at a newly acquired modular flotation plant, targeting 12,000 tonnes per month in the first month and rising as additional capacity is commissioned. This adds near-term incremental copper supply.

title: Metal Bank secures copper exploration rights in Jordan
summary: Metal Bank secured surface exploration rights for Jordan’s Area 47, identified via remote sensing and limited data as a prospective copper-bearing intrusion. Field sampling found anomalous multi-metal geochemistry and rock chips with up to 0.7% copper, supporting plans to advance projects to drill-ready status.

title: Indonesia's 100 new potential nickel reserve sites promote its leading position
summary: Indonesia’s Geological Agency reported at least 100 additional, currently unexplored sites with potential nickel reserves. It said the findings strengthen Indonesia’s position as the leading global nickel producer, with nickel being used in EV batteries, and that further exploration will continue.

title: Global Growth Angst Pushes Copper to More Than 4 Month Low
summary: Copper prices fell to more than four-month lows as concerns over weaker demand in China and the United States triggered a selloff. The Reuters report links the decline to signs of stalled industrial activity in China, weighing on copper used in power and construction, with prices down about 20% from May records.

title: Gold, copper and oil prices fall as stock market contagion spreads
summary: Copper fell sharply (up to 3.8% on the LME) as global financial contagion triggered a risk-off rush to cash out and turn bearish amid fears of a US recession. The selloff pressured other industrial raw-materials, reflecting weaker growth expectations and tighter financial conditions.

title: Executive Column: Eramet seeks bigger stake in Indonesia's nickel industry - Companies
summary: Eramet Indonesia’s director says the company, via PT Eramet Bumi Sulawesi, is looking to expand its role in Indonesia’s nickel sector and build partnerships for an end-to-end EV battery value chain. Eramet plans new mining-site work and permits, positioning against Chinese dominance amid Western EV supply concerns.

title: Kalamazoo welcomes new eco-friendly aluminum processing center
summary: Kalamazoo, Michigan welcomed a new eco-friendly JP Processing Center from Schupan to recycle obsolete aluminum into usable raw material. The company says the process cuts carbon footprint and is more efficient and cost effective. Output is aimed at green aluminum products used in items like pop cans and home siding.

title: Copper-gold in Utah and lithium in Brazil
summary: Alderan Resources discusses exploration progress at Utah’s Frisco copper-gold district, including permit approval and a two-stage drilling plan for the New Years prospect, plus follow-up work at the Cactus area. The company also reports lithium exploration in Brazil, but the only tracked metal mentioned is copper.

title: Asian Battery Metals uncovers new copper-nickel system within Yambat project
summary: Asian Battery Metals reported interim reconnaissance results from Mongolia’s Yambat project, including evidence of an expanded magmatic copper-nickel system and new targets such as Copper Ridge. Mapping and geophysics guided sampling and a Phase 1 drilling campaign. Results are preliminary and plan further scout drilling, implying future supply potential.

title: Indian miner Vedanta tops Q1 profit estimates on higher aluminium, zinc prices
summary: Vedanta reported Q1 profit above estimates, citing higher global prices—especially aluminium and zinc—amid supply worries. The firm said pre-tax profit at its aluminium unit rose 14%, with aluminium contributing about one-third of group profit and revenue. The update reinforces short-term positive sentiment for aluminium prices.

title: City of Las Vegas councilman vows to curb rising crime of copper theft
summary: Las Vegas officials are proposing tighter controls on scrap-metal sales and purchases to curb copper theft. The city has already replaced targeted street lighting wiring, including with aluminum-based wiring, but theft persists into wider areas. Penalties include fines and possible jail, with a council discussion scheduled for Aug. 7.

title: Copper deepens losses on investor disquiet about potential slowdown
summary: LME and Shanghai copper prices extended losses as speculators stayed pessimistic about global growth and reported weak demand in China. Three-month copper fell to about $8,798/t and the Shanghai September contract hit a fresh low for the period. Commentators cited reduced long exposure and CTA selling amid recession fears.

title: Copper 360 restarts Rietberg underground mining in South Africa
summary: Copper 360 has restarted underground mining at South Africa’s Rietberg Mine in the O’Kiep Copper District after decades. The company plans to process ore at Nama modular flotation plants and expects output of about 45,000t per month at 1.6% copper, moving from producing plate to copper concentrate.

title: Clarification needed for required aluminium import certificate between Mexico, US
summary: The White House announced that some Mexican aluminium imports into the US will lose Section 232 tariff exemptions unless importers provide proof that first/second smelter and casting are not China, Russia, Belarus or Iran. Affected goods face a 10% tariff (and higher for already sanctioned material), increasing compliance uncertainty.

title: Brixton Metals Provides Assays from the Second Camp Creek Drill Hole of the 2024 Exploration Program with an Upper 61.5m Gold Dominant Zone and a Lower 1126.05m Interval of Porphyry Copper Dominant Zone
summary: Brixton Metals reported assay results from its second Camp Creek drill hole at the Thorn Project, including a 1,126m copper-dominant porphyry interval (CuEq up to ~0.67%) and higher-grade sub-intervals. The findings expand the copper-gold system footprint, but no near-term production changes are stated.

title: Nickel hydrometallurgy intermediate products in Indonesia saw a production decline due to weather impact, down 12.06% MoM in June [SMM Analysis]
summary: Indonesia’s nickel hydrometallurgy intermediate product output fell 12.06% MoM in June due to abnormal weather, which reduced transportation efficiency of ore and materials and caused delayed raw material supply. August output is forecast to rise 9.73% MoM as weather improves, though levels remain below normal.

title: Six key trends in the copper market
summary: The piece argues the copper market is under intense strain: copper prices are pushing to all-time highs while treatment and refining charges (TC/RCs) have fallen to record lows. It attributes pressure to disrupted supply and weaker concentrate investment, with demand growing from energy transition sectors.

title: Copper Recovers, But Investors Wary About Economy, China
summary: Copper prices moved into positive territory as central bankers’ comments eased recession concerns, lifting broader financial markets. The piece notes zinc fell after inventories rose, pointing to oversupply pressure. No direct supply or policy shock for copper is cited beyond macro sentiment.

title: London copper slips on firm dollar, Shanghai up
summary: London copper fell 0.5% to a more than four-and-a-half month low as a firm dollar and looming U.S. recession fears pressured prices, alongside weak China demand concerns. LME aluminium also slipped 0.3% and nickel fell 0.5%, while Shanghai contracts were mixed, reflecting catch-up activity.

title: China July unwrought copper imports at 438,000 metric tons, customs says
summary: China’s July imports of unwrought copper and copper products fell 2.9% year-on-year to 438,000 metric tons, according to customs data. First-seven-month imports rose 5.4% to 3.2 million tons, but the month-on-month dip suggests softer near-term physical demand.

title: China July copper imports decline on weak demand
summary: China’s July unwrought copper imports fell 2.9% year-on-year to 438,000 tonnes as demand stayed subdued and inventories were high. Weak manufacturing and a property downturn coincided with elevated Shanghai deliverable stocks around 300,000 tonnes. Antaike expects slower refined copper consumption growth this year.

title: London copper slides on firm dollar, Shanghai up
summary: Reuters reports LME three-month copper fell 0.5% to a four-and-a-half-month low due to a firm dollar and worries about U.S. and Chinese growth. Shanghai copper rose 0.3% as higher prices spurred Chinese exports and narrowing spreads attracted cargoes. LME aluminium and nickel slipped slightly while SHFE aluminium rose and nickel edged down.

title: South32's Worsley Alumina expansion condemned by Boddington, Wandering, Williams residents
summary: South-west WA residents and groups oppose South32’s Worsley Alumina bauxite project expansion, citing alleged environmental harm, changing hydrology, dust mitigation water use, and inadequate consultation. Over 130 appeals were lodged against the expansion’s approval, creating potential near-term uncertainty around operating and expansion timelines.

title: ESG Focus: The Little Big Things - 06-08-2024
summary: ESG-focused coverage includes Macquarie’s notes that several nickel mines are being suspended/closed amid weak pricing, which may tighten near-term supply. It also reports South32 is appealing WA EPA conditions at its Worsley alumina mine, potentially influencing aluminium supply/costs. Other sections are largely macro/energy/ESG themes.

title: SK Nexilis, Lotte Energy Materials delay construction of European copper foil plants amid EV glut
summary: Lotte Energy Materials and SK Nexilis delayed construction of copper foil plants in Spain and Poland after European EV battery makers scaled back expansion plans amid demand weakness. LEM cut investment sharply and expects a delayed business turnaround, while SK Nexilis pushed back completion and operations due to uncertain demand and policy risks.

title: SMM Analysis Of China Aluminum Production In July And Forecast For August
summary: SMM reports China’s aluminium output rose in July as Yunnan smelters resumed full production and additional capacity came on in Inner Mongolia and Sichuan. It expects August operating capacity and output to keep increasing, with aluminium liquid proportion recovering toward 73%, suggesting higher supply despite improving downstream demand.

title: Armenia's copper concentrate production up 15% in the first half of the year
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate production rose 15% in January–June 2024 to 144,630 tonnes versus the same period a year earlier, according to the National Statistical Committee. Zinc and molybdenum concentrate output also changed, but the headline implies modestly higher copper supply with unclear near-term pricing effects.

title: Aruma finalises purchase of copper and uranium assets in Australia
summary: Aruma Resources has completed the purchase of NHM Holdings’ copper exploration assets in South Australia and Queensland, including the Fiery Creek and Bortala projects. The company cites high copper assays in rock chips and plans additional geophysical surveys and drilling, but provides no near-term production or supply changes.

title: Zambia's Minerals Law: Potential Impact on Copper Investment
summary: Zambia’s proposed Minerals Regulation Commission Bill is criticized for potentially deterring mining investment by increasing regulatory discretion and “free carry” risks, with concerns about property rights and corruption. Industry groups warn it could undermine efforts to raise copper output toward 3 million tonnes, pressuring near-term copper growth expectations.

title: Aluminium Bahrain B S C : Alba and Daiki Aluminium Forge Strategic Partnership to Establish Sustainable Aluminium Dross Processing Plant in Bahrain
summary: Alba (Aluminium Bahrain) and Daiki Aluminium sign an MoU to establish a sustainable aluminium dross processing business in Bahrain. The facility will use state-of-the-art technology to recover aluminium metal from dross, lowering waste and supporting circular-economy and ESG goals. The move modestly strengthens near-term aluminium supply sentiment.

title: First Quantum to trim work hours at stalled Panama copper mine
summary: First Quantum says it will cut work hours at its stalled copper mine in Panama. The move indicates ongoing production disruption and potential reductions in near-term copper output, likely tightening immediate supply expectations and pressuring copper prices lower in the short term.

title: Sustainability at every step: AMAG AL4® ever now also offers certified, low carbon primary aluminium
summary: AMAG Austria Metall AG expands its AMAG AL4® ever portfolio by adding certified low-carbon primary aluminium from its Alouette smelter in Canada. The smelter uses exclusively renewable hydropower, limiting energy-related CO2 and targeting up to 4.0 t CO2 per tonne of aluminium. A certificate verifies Scope 1–3 footprints.

title: Copper Plating Solutions for Semiconductor Manufacturing Market Size to Grow USD 830 Million by 2030 at a CAGR of 8 %
summary: PRNewswire/Valuates describes a market forecast for copper plating solutions used in semiconductor processes (e.g., Damascene, TSV). It attributes growth to semiconductor miniaturization and performance gains requiring copper interconnections. The piece is about industry expansion but contains no immediate supply, trade, or pricing catalysts for copper.

title: Tertiary, First Quantum sign Zambia copper exploration deal
summary: Tertiary Minerals and First Quantum signed a letter agreement for the Mukai copper exploration project in Zambia, with $1.5m minimum exploration funding over 24 months and potential earn-in to up to 80% contingent on meeting copper resource thresholds. The deal is mainly early-stage, so near-term copper prices may see limited effect.

title: Indonesia's Net Zero Nickel Boom Is A Toxic Disaster, Destroying Rainforests And Coral
summary: The piece argues Indonesia’s nickel boom—driven by EV and battery demand—has caused major rainforest and coastal damage, citing relentless smelting smoke, mining craters, and pollution at processing hubs like IMIP. It notes Indonesia’s leading nickel output and smelting capacity, raising the risk of disruption or tighter oversight affecting near-term nickel supply.

title: Alba and Daiki Aluminium Forge Strategic Partnership to Establish Sustainable Aluminium Dross Processing Plant in Bahrain
summary: Alba, Bahrain’s major aluminium smelter, and Japan’s Daiki Aluminium have formed a strategic partnership to set up a sustainable aluminium dross processing business in Bahrain. The initiative focuses on recycling dross into usable materials, potentially improving secondary metal supply and supporting aluminium availability expectations.

title: BHP Seeking Buyer for Gold, Copper Mines in Brazil
summary: BNN Bloomberg notes that BHP is seeking a buyer for its gold and copper mines in Brazil. Such divestment can influence copper supply expectations near term, but without specifics on operational continuity or production curtailments, the immediate price impact is likely limited or unclear.

title: Bahrain Business: Alba ties up with Daiki for sustainable aluminium dross processing business
summary: Alba and Japan’s Daiki Aluminium Industry have signed an MoU to establish a sustainable aluminium dross processing business in Bahrain. The facility will use state-of-the-art technology to recover aluminium metal, reduce waste, and support ESG and circular-economy goals. This could incrementally tighten aluminium supply expectations.

title: Marimaca Copper Announces Closing of Private Placements Totaling C$30.3 Million led by Assore International Holdings
summary: Marimaca Copper announced closing C$30.3 million in private placements led by Assore International Holdings, plus a related acquisition of shares from an affiliate. The funds relate to developing its Antofagasta, Chile oxide heap-leach copper project, with warrants exercisable at C$5.85 over 18 months.

title: Copper wire, machete, untaxed cigarettes seized by RCMP
summary: RCMP in Innisfail arrested a repeat offender and seized more than 1,500 pounds of stripped copper wire from a truck and trailer. Police also found tools and untaxed cigarettes. The case is a local enforcement action on stolen copper, with no clear implication for broader copper supply or pricing.

title: Copper wire, machete, untaxed cigarettes seized by RCMP  - Okotoks & Foothills News
summary: RCMP in Innisfail arrested a repeat offender suspected of stealing copper wire from industrial/commercial/oilfield sites and seized over 1,500 pounds of stripped copper wire, along with tools and other contraband. The police are locating owners of the seized property. The event is local and unlikely to affect broader copper prices.

title: A look at Gov. Tim Walz's stance on copper-nickel mining over the years
summary: The article reviews Minnesota Governor Tim Walz’s approach to copper-nickel mining and highlights that Twin Metals’ leases were pulled by the Biden Administration, effectively halting a planned mine near the BWCA. Walz is portrayed as hands-off and emphasizing federal environmental review, keeping project timing uncertain.

title: Copper Slumps As China Dumps Base Metal Into Asian Warehouses
summary: The piece reports that copper prices are slumping because China is said to be dumping base metals into Asian warehouses. If additional warehouse inflows raise short-term availability and increase inventory pressure, market expectations for near-term copper supply tighten, usually weighing on spot copper prices in the following days.

title: LME copper rebounds on soft dollar; outlook remains murky
summary: Copper edged up slightly on a softer U.S. dollar, but broader sentiment is weak as LME inventories jumped and global growth expectations deteriorated. Commentary notes rising TC/RCs suggest improving concentrate supply. Aluminium and nickel prices were also lower in the same session, indicating mixed but generally pressured industrial metals.

title: Jubilee Metals starts operations at new Roan copper plant in Zambia
summary: Jubilee Metals says it has begun operations at an upgraded Roan copper concentrator in Zambia, reaching a critical stage of production ramp-up. The new front-end module adds processing capacity, lifting Roan’s capacity toward 13,000 tonnes of copper per year, supporting higher copper concentrate supply and potentially bullish copper expectations.

title: Copper steadies as gloom on global growth hits demand
summary: Copper prices steadied but remained under pressure as pessimism on global growth and risk-off sentiment weighed on base metals. LME copper inventories surged nearly threefold to 294,750 tons. Aluminium and nickel also fell on the day, reflecting weaker demand expectations outweighing improving spot refining charges.

title: Does copper have the mettle?
summary: The IEF warns that copper is central to energy transition but faces a looming global shortage. It cites sluggish supply versus rapidly rising clean-energy demand and notes the closure of Panama’s Cobre Panama mine. Despite some surplus forecasts, the article stresses a need for new capacity to meet demand growth.

title: Golden Arrow Drilling Hits Greater Than 0.4% Copper Over More than 100 metres in Two New Step-Out Holes at the San Pietro Iron-Copper-Gold-Cobalt Project, Chile
summary: Golden Arrow reported new step-out drill intercepts at its San Pietro IOCG project in Chile, including long intervals grading about 0.43–0.44% Cu with associated gold and cobalt. The release is an exploration update with no production or reserve change stated, so any near-term effect on copper prices is likely limited.

title: Expectations for improved aluminium demand supported by automotive recovery
summary: Traders expect improved Japanese automotive demand to support aluminium in the latter half of 2024 after Toyota certification and recall-related production suspensions. Toyota models resume in September following compliance confirmation, while Japan Aluminium Association data shows aluminium usage in transportation. Fastmarkets also moves the Japan spot premium publication to daily to improve liquidity.

title: Koryx Copper Intersects 72 METERS at 0.38% CuEq; 80 Meters
summary: Koryx Copper announced additional assay results from the Haib copper project in Namibia, including multiple drill intersections with grades above 0.3% CuEq over significant widths and potential for higher average deposit grade. The company plans an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate and further metallurgical test work, with fieldwork expected in August 2024.

title: CEO.CA Technologies Ltd.: CEO.CA's Inside The boardroom: Faraday Copper Encountering Near-Surface Mineralization During Phase III Drilling
summary: CEO.CA interviewed Faraday Copper’s CEO (Paul Harbidge) on updates from the Copper Creek project. The discussion notes Phase III drilling encountering near-surface mineralization. While no production or resource numbers are provided, the news is supportive for perceived future copper supply potential.

title: US Copper Corp.: US Copper Corp Initiates an Updated Preliminary Economic Assessment on Entire Moonlight-Superior Project
summary: US Copper Corp retained Global Resource Engineering to complete an updated PEA for its 100% owned Moonlight-Superior copper project in Northeast California. The study will incorporate revised NI 43-101 resources and new oxide resources and is expected by year-end, potentially improving project economics.

title: Steel and aluminum producers urge tariffs to combat Chinese dumping
summary: Canadian steel and aluminum producers are urging Ottawa to impose tariffs on Chinese steel and aluminum, arguing current measures have not stopped dumping and market overcapacity. The push follows recent U.S. tariff increases on Chinese metals and concerns Canada could become a trade backdoor via Mexico, risking job losses and potential price pressure in aluminum markets.

title: Steel, Aluminum Makers Push Trudeau Government on China Tariffs
summary: Aluminum producers are pressing Canada’s Trudeau government to act on China-related tariffs. The move would likely raise the cost of importing Chinese aluminum into Canada, potentially reducing near-term supply and supporting domestic prices as markets price in a stronger tariff-driven import barrier.

title: meviy Announces a 30% Price Reduction on CNC Milling Aluminum Products
summary: Meviy (MISUMI Group) said it will cut the sales price of its CNC milling aluminum products by 30% effective immediately, covering aluminum alloys 6061, 5052, and 2017 with no surface treatment. The move targets lower customer costs and competitive pricing, likely signaling local pricing pressure on aluminium products rather than metal prices broadly.

title: McEwen Copper Update, Excitement in Argentina: Milei Magic
summary: McEwen Copper reported strong Los Azules infill drill intercepts, including multiple long intervals above ~0.8% Cu, confirming and extending a high-grade enriched zone ahead of the feasibility study. The update also cites Argentina’s new mining investment incentives and a US$4.4B BHP/Lundin copper-deposit acquisition in San Juan.

title: Mitsui : Capital increase in the Brazilian aluminum smelting business
summary: Mitsui underwrites a capital increase in Nippon Amazon Aluminium (NAAC), raising its stake in the Albras smelter joint venture to about 46% (direct and indirect). The deal also increases annual offtake of primary aluminium ingots from ~80,000 to ~140,000 tons, strengthening green aluminium supply access.

title: No 'Dumping Ground': Steel and Aluminum CEOs Urge Ottawa to Impose Tariffs on China
summary: Canadian steel and aluminum CEOs urge Ottawa to impose tariffs on China to prevent North America from becoming a “dumping ground” for Chinese overcapacity. They seek trade protection aligned with the U.S. and Mexico. If implemented, reduced Chinese import pressure could support aluminium pricing in the near term.

title: Copper rebounds on US jobs data, still heads for weekly decline
summary: Copper rose Friday after U.S. jobless claims came in better than expected, easing recession-demand fears and supporting rate-cut optimism. It still faces a fifth straight weekly drop, with LME inventories at a high since 2019 limiting upside catalysts. Aluminium and nickel also climbed amid the broader rebound.

title: North Little Rock Police Athletic League faces setbacks after ballpark copper theft
summary: North Little Rock’s ball fields were damaged after a copper thief stole underground wiring and electrical components, shutting down parts of the complex. Police estimate the stolen copper value at about $25–$50 but repairs could cost $40,000–$50,000. A $2,000 reward is offered for information leading to an arrest.

title: Japan's Mitsui lifts aluminium ingot offtake in Brazil
summary: Mitsui increased its stake in Nippon Amazon Aluminium (NAAC) to expand purchases of low-carbon aluminum ingots from Brazil’s Albras. Offtake rises to 140,000 tonnes/year from 80,000 tonnes/year, mainly for Japanese buyers. NAAC/Albras use renewable power, and Mitsui expects tight low-carbon supply and rising demand.

title: 2,300 homes without internet after copper theft plunges Victorian town Woodend into NBN darkness
summary: Vandals stole copper from telecom infrastructure in Woodend, Victoria, causing a major NBN service outage for about 2,300 customers and disrupting phone service. Police are investigating the theft and ask for footage. The report signals continued copper-targeting, but offers no quantity or market-wide supply impact.

title: Los Angeles boosts copper wire theft crackdown effort with additional $200,000
summary: Los Angeles City Council approved an additional $200,000 for its police-led “heavy metal task force” targeting copper wire theft from public infrastructure. The initiative has led to arrests and recovered copper wire. Critics argue outages are often maintenance-related and prefer preventative streetlight solutions like LED or solar power.

title: Investee Company Update: Peak Nickel Ltd | Company Announcement
summary: Ormonde notes Peak Nickel has resumed a 2024 drill programme at its Rodburn Ni-Cu-Co project in Scotland, targeting further definition and potential expansion of mineralization. The announcement includes Ni, Cu and Co grades used in Ni-equivalent assumptions, but provides no new price-driving results or production impacts.

title: Strong Outlook for High-Grade NPI Prices Amid Tight Nickel Ore Supply and Rising Demand
summary: SMM reports high-grade NPI (8–12% nickel) prices rose WoW on tight nickel ore availability and higher ore-driven smelter costs, limiting short-term supply increases. Easing rainfall in Weda Bay supports logistics, while stainless-steel peak-season demand lifts inquiries. Nickel prices consolidated with a rebound and upside bias, though fundamentals remain weak.

title: Drilling campaign confirms high-grade copper at Loz Azules in Argentina
summary: McEwen Copper says drilling at the Loz Azules mine in Argentina confirmed high-grade copper and that the feasibility study remains on track. An updated PEA targets large-scale annual copper cathode output, while Argentina’s RIGI incentives could improve project economics. Near-term copper price impact appears modest.

title: Poilievre Promises Tariffs on Chinese Electric Vehicles, Steel, and Aluminum
summary: Pierre Poilievre said he would implement tariffs on Chinese exports, including aluminum, alongside electric vehicles and steel, citing protection of Canadian jobs from “economic predation” by Beijing. He made the remarks at the Stelco steel plant, arguing tariffs would encourage new mining and steel investment.

title: Coal Tar Pitch Market size is set to grow by USD 618.2 million from 2024-2028, Increasing use of aluminum across various industries boost the market, Technavio
summary: Technavio projects growth in the coal tar pitch market from 2024–2028, citing increasing use in primary aluminum production. Coal tar pitch is used as a binder/anode component in the Hall-Héroult process and electrode demand. Regulations limiting coal tar pitch due to PAHs are noted as a constraint, limiting clear short-term aluminum price impact.

title: Century Aluminum Company (NASDAQ:CENX) Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Century Aluminum’s Q2 call cites rising LME and regional premiums driven by stronger global demand and tight inventories, while noting alumina supply constraints and high alumina-to-aluminium ratios. The company highlights additional U.S./EU trade actions supporting domestic extrusion demand and improved U.S. pricing conditions, implying near-term bullish aluminium pressure.

title: Congo and Zambia Begin Talks to Reopen Key Copper Export Border
summary: DRC and Zambia began negotiations after Zambia closed their shared border, disrupting DRC’s copper exports through the Kasumbalesa crossing. The closure followed protests tied to Zambia responding to DRC’s ban on imported soft drinks and beer. Talks aim to reopen the border and restore copper shipment flows quickly.

title: Copper slips as investors assess economic uncertainty
summary: Copper prices opened the week softer as investors weighed ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty and awaited data for demand signals. Reuters cites economic worries including recession fears, with copper down on both LME and Shanghai. Nickel also slipped, while aluminium was steadier, reflecting cautious industrial demand sentiment.

title: Bangkok Post - Over 14,000 tonnes of hazardous aluminium dross seized near Bangkok
summary: Thai police and industrial works officials seized about 14,400 tonnes of hazardous aluminium dross at two smelting-related sites near Bangkok after stopping an unauthorized truck. Authorities found hot aluminium bars and illegal operations, including a prior April closure order that was allegedly ignored. Possible production disruption could support near-term aluminium prices.

title: East Star Resources plc Provides Copper Porphyry Exploration Update
summary: East Star Resources reported early exploration progress at its Ayagoz and Snowy licences in Kazakhstan, prospective for copper porphyry deposits. The company completed soil sampling (2,800 samples) and is running ICP-MS assays, using satellite imagery to map hydrothermal alteration and refine targets.

title: Copper rallies, eyes on China, U.S. data
summary: Copper prices rose as traders covered shorts and looked to upcoming China and U.S. data for demand and rate-cut timing. LME copper was up about 0.9%, with cancelled warrants increasing and warehouse inventories still elevated. The report also said aluminium and nickel climbed on the same risk-on backdrop.

title: India's NALCO's reports 76% jump in profit on shrinking costs, higher aluminium prices
summary: NALCO reported a 76% jump in Q1 profit, attributing gains to lower costs (coal and bauxite) and higher global aluminium prices. Reuters notes base-metal prices rose sharply on supply concerns and stronger demand, while domestic aluminium demand is expected to stay steady from power and construction sectors.

title: The True Cost Of China's Hold On Indonesia's Nickel
summary: US and Indonesia discussed a possible Critical Minerals Specific Free Trade Agreement to increase access to Indonesian nickel for EV batteries. However, nine US senators sent a bipartisan letter urging scrutiny over labor, environmental issues, and Chinese dominance, potentially slowing or complicating the agreement and dampening near-term nickel sentiment.

title: Share of Russian aluminium in LME warehouses rose to 65% in July
summary: LME data show Russian-origin aluminium’s share in LME-approved warehouses rose to 65% in July (from 50% in June), while Indian-origin fell. Total on-warrant aluminium stocks fell 23% in July. Russian copper and nickel shares declined. The piece also references the LME’s earlier ban on sanctioned Russian output.

title: Outflows of Indian aluminium boost share of Russian metal in LME warehouses
summary: LME data show Russian-origin aluminium’s share of on-warrant stocks rose to 65% in July while Indian-origin fell to 33%, alongside a 23% decline in total on-warrant aluminium stocks. The May Russian ban remains cited, with similar share changes for copper and nickel inventories.

title: Kincora Copper Limited: Kincora Secures Funded, Successful and Motivated Partner for Mongolian Assets
summary: Kincora Copper announced a funded earn-in arrangement with Woomera Mining for Mongolia’s Bronze Fox copper-gold project, including up to US$4m of exploration spend, drilling starting in September, and potential acquisition of remaining interest or free-carry to a final investment decision. The terms mainly affect future copper supply expectations, not near-term volumes.

title: Jiangxi Copper's subsidiary halts production after fatal accident
summary: Jiangxi Copper’s subsidiary Shandong Humon Smelting halted production in Shandong after a fatal accident involving an unexpected spill from a side-blown copper furnace. Three workers died and 14 were injured. The plant remains closed during an investigation; Humon produced 203,023 tonnes of copper last year.

title: UK firm drills at nickel laterite project site in Oman
summary: Knights Bay Oryx’s Oman subsidiary has completed initial drilling at its nickel laterite project in Mineral Block 21, targeting nickel continuity and staged resource definition. The company has not yet released lab results, but sampled ore near small mines showed ~1% nickel and shipped material for metallurgical testing.

title: Nickel Prices Plummet as Stainless Steel Demand Remains Weak
summary: Nickel prices continued to plunge through July, with early August stabilizing near early-2024 levels. Stainless steel distributors report weak demand, and lower nickel-driven stainless surcharges reduce buyer incentives. U.S. manufacturing PMI stays in contraction, reinforcing soft end-use conditions. Outokumpu sees growth QoQ but still down YoY.

title: Pan Asia triggers option on Chilean copper chase
summary: Pan Asia Metals converted an exclusivity agreement into a binding option to buy the Rosario copper project in northern Chile, with fees paid over a three-year option and a final purchase fee. The company plans IP geophysics and further sampling/trenching, citing high-grade historical rock-chip results and proximity to major facilities and El Salvador.

title: LME copper falls on caution ahead of key US, China data
summary: LME copper snapped a three-session rally, falling about 0.6% to near $8,973/ton as investors turned cautious ahead of forthcoming US CPI and China data that could influence Fed rate-cut timing. China demand indicators and lower prices provided some support, but net near-term pressure was bearish.

title: Roan Front-End Module's First Copper Concentrate | Company Announcement
summary: Jubilee Metals reports first copper concentrate from the Roan Front-End Module in Zambia, targeting previously mined material. The concentrate will be refined at the upgraded Sable refinery to copper cathode, adding to existing sulphide concentrate production. The Front-End Module will ramp up during Q3 2024.

title: SMM Analysis: Copper prices fell, and the price difference between primary metal and scrap narrowed significantly. The operating rate of copper cathode rod in China rebounded as expected in July.
summary: SMM survey data show China copper cathode-rod operating rates rebounded to 70.52% in July. Copper prices fell, yet the primary–scrap price spread narrowed markedly, drawing orders back from secondary rods to cathode rods and lifting cathode-rod output. August operating rates are expected to rise only slightly to 72.71%.

title: Jubilee Metals produces first copper from upgraded facility
summary: Jubilee Metals says it has produced first copper concentrate from the newly upgraded front-end section of the Roan concentrator plant in Zambia. The concentrate will be refined at its Sable refinery to make copper cathode, with the Zambian operation now spanning concentrator plus refinery upgrades for over 25,000 tpa.

title: Terrain heats up search for 'Nova-style' nickel lookalike
summary: Terrain Minerals reports airborne geophysics at its Lort River project in Western Australia, identifying five conductors that may indicate “Nova-style” magmatic nickel-copper sulphide mineralisation similar to IGO’s Nova-Bollinger deposits. The company plans ground EM, soil geochemistry, and reconnaissance drilling, seeking a new nickel discovery.

title: Material Matters: Nickel, Copper & Gold
summary: Morgan Stanley flags nickel may be near its pricing floor: inventories are surging and demand remains challenging, limiting upside and keeping prices range-bound. For copper, spot has retraced and Macquarie cuts short- to medium-term demand and price forecasts, pointing to renewed near-term downside pressure despite M&A activity.

title: Material Matters: Nickel, Copper & Gold
summary: Morgan Stanley says nickel’s “bottom” may be near but elevated nickel inventories and challenging demand constrain sustained rallies, implying range-bound pricing. Macquarie expects copper volatility, cuts 2025–27 forecasts on weaker demand, and lowers 2024 Chinese and North American growth estimates. Overall, neither metal faces a clear immediate breakout.

title: Copper retreats on rising inventories, sluggish demand
summary: Reuters reports copper prices fell as LME inventories climbed to near five-year highs and China demand remained sluggish. Traders cited exports of surplus copper into Asian LME warehouses and weaker Chinese macro data. Purchases from some physical consumers and hopes of a BHP Escondida strike limited losses, but overall sentiment stayed bearish.

title: RIO ASX: Rio Tinto prepared to sell stakes in Winu copper project
summary: Rio Tinto says it is prepared to sell stakes in its Western Australia Winu copper project, after earlier plans for alternative partnerships. The move could trigger more consolidation in the Paterson Province, with Newmont also seeking to exit. The news is about project ownership, not immediate output.

title: BHP workers at top copper mine go on strike after talks fail
summary: The report says BHP workers at its top copper mine went on strike after talks failed. The stoppage raises the risk of reduced copper output and near-term supply tightness expectations, typically weighing on copper sentiment and prices over the coming days as the market assesses duration and restart prospects.

title: Grid Metals Corp.: Grid Metals Corp Provides Activities Update on Donner Lithium and MM Copper Nickel Projects
summary: Grid Metals provided a permitting and exploration update for its Manitoba projects. Donner’s advanced exploration permit for lithium was approved but bulk sampling is deferred due to lower lithium prices. For MM, the company plans to resume a ~5,000 m drill program targeting Cu-rich sulfide mineralization near the New Manitoba deposit.

title: BHP Workers at Top Copper Mine Go on Strike After Talks Fail
summary: BHP workers at its top copper mine reportedly went on strike after failed negotiations. The stoppage threatens near-term copper production and increases supply-risk perceptions. With output disrupted at a major source, traders typically expect tighter physical availability and volatility, influencing copper prices.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Secures 100% Ownership of Mineral Rights at its Santa Cruz Copper Project with Final Option Payment
summary: Ivanhoe Electric said it completed a final US$10 million option payment to acquire 100% ownership of mineral and surface rights for its Santa Cruz copper project in Arizona. The company frames it as consolidating rights over a large, high-grade undeveloped copper resource, potentially strengthening long-term supply expectations, though near-term output is unchanged.

title: New Presidential Proclamations – Section 232 Duties On Certain Steel And Aluminum Products From Mexico - Export Controls & Trade & Investment Sanctions - International Law
summary: The U.S. issued proclamations modifying Section 232 trade treatment for certain steel and aluminum products from Mexico. For aluminum, importers must document smelt/cast countries; otherwise an additional 10% duty applies. This raises costs for some Mexico-origin aluminum shipments, likely reducing near-term demand and weighing on aluminum prices.

title: Workers strike at world's largest copper mine in blow to BHP
summary: Workers began a strike at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile after pay talks failed. The union represents most frontline operational staff and replacement workers are prohibited by law, raising the risk of reduced output from the world’s largest copper producer and likely tightening near-term supply.

title: BHP union launches strike at world's largest copper mine
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile began a strike after contract talks failed, potentially disrupting production at the world’s largest copper source. The stoppage could affect concentrate supply to Chinese smelters, raising short-term supply risk. Markets initially stayed calm, but analysts warned broader labor-dispute contagion.

title: BHP strike: Workers at Escondida world's biggest copper mine walk off the job in Chile
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile began a strike after rejecting a wage deal proposal following five days of mediation. About 2,400 union members walked off the job, creating risk of major production disruption at the world’s biggest copper operation, which can tighten short-term supply.

title: Strike Commences at World's Largest Copper Mine Amid Pay Dispute
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile began a strike after failed wage negotiations. The walkout could disrupt operations at the world’s largest copper producer, echoing 2017 supply impacts. The union seeks higher profit sharing while BHP recalls contingency plans as settlement hopes persist.

title: BHP workers at largest copper mine on strike
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile began a strike after wage talks failed, potentially shutting output from a site producing over one million tons annually and about 5% of world copper mined. The disruption is expected to tighten near-term supply and support bullish copper price pressure.

title: Workers Strike At World's Biggest Copper Mine In Chile
summary: Workers are striking at Chile’s Escondida, the world’s biggest copper mine, after BHP pay talks failed. The strike could disrupt output beyond a week or two even as copper stockpiles are high. BHP says scaled-back operations will continue with non-union staff and contingency plans.

title: Labor Strike Jolts World's Biggest Copper Mine
summary: A labor strike started at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile after wage talks ended without agreement. The walkout involves most operations and maintenance staff at the mine (~5% of global mined copper). Disrupted sales could tighten supply and support higher copper prices while negotiations resume.

title: Labor Strike Jolts World's Biggest Copper Mine -- Update
summary: A labor walkout at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile began after wage negotiations failed. Escondida supplies about 5% of global mined copper. Any disruption could tighten a market already softening on China/U.S. demand concerns, putting upward pressure on LME copper expectations as talks resume.

title: FIRB green-lights Japanese investment in Ardea nickel plan
summary: Australia’s FIRB approved Japanese investors (Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi) to participate in Ardea Resources’ Goongarrie Hub within the Kalgoorlie Nickel Project. The decision removes a JV condition, enabling continued feasibility-study funding and engineering work, supporting bullish sentiment for nickel development.

title: How did the YoY performance of China's copper cathode rod production fare in July as copper prices continued to decline?
summary: SMM reports China’s copper cathode rod production rose in July with higher operating rates, supported by a narrowing spread versus scrap copper that encouraged orders. Copper prices continued declining through July, with the average #1 cathode price down MoM. The rebound in deliveries is linked to lower price-triggered order releases.

title: Could a union halt production at the world's biggest copper mine? | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: A Reuters report says a union strike at BHP’s Escondida mine in Chile—about 5% of 2023 global copper output—could disrupt the world’s largest copper supply. Negotiations over profit-sharing and dividends are at a standoff, with analysts noting prices haven’t surged yet but could if action hardens.

title: Copper catastrophe: Copper wire thefts continue to cost victims thousands of dollars
summary: Copper wire thefts in Fresno have disabled traffic signals and damaged/affected school and campus infrastructure. Victims report significant repair costs and delays because stolen copper wiring must be replaced, sometimes costing tens of thousands. The problem is concentrated locally and does not indicate a market-wide copper supply shock.

title: Kincora Copper Limited: Kincora and AngloGold Ashanti's First Drilling Program
summary: Kincora Copper plans a first drilling program at its Nyngan Project in NSW in partnership with AngloGold Ashanti, testing up to eight untested intrusive Cu-Au targets (“Ace of Spades”) with 6–8 holes totaling about 4,000–5,000m, subject to permitting and weather.

title: Copper gains on hopes for US rate cuts, Escondida strike
summary: Copper rose on hopes for U.S. interest-rate cuts as weaker inflation data lifted expectations of earlier Federal Reserve action. Gains were further supported by a strike at Chile’s Escondida, the world’s biggest copper mine, raising prospects of reduced output. China’s weak economic data capped advances.

title: Ivanhoe Electric takes sole ownership of Santa Cruz Copper mineral rights
summary: Ivanhoe Electric paid the final $10m to obtain 100% mineral-rights ownership of its Santa Cruz copper project in Arizona, consolidating mineral and surface control. The underground project is described as small-scale with 1.6m tonnes projected over 20 years, but no immediate production change is indicated.

title: Workers strike at world's biggest copper mine in Chile - Companies
summary: Workers struck at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile after pay talks failed. The mine provides about 5% of global copper, and operations were expected to continue with contingency staffing, but scaled-back production raises near-term supply risk. Analysts cite existing stockpiles that may soften impacts.

title: Workers strike at world's biggest copper mine
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in northern Chile are striking after pay talks failed. The mine produces around 5% of global copper, so a production slowdown could reduce near-term supply. Analysts note stockpiles may soften the immediate effect, but longer disruption could push prices higher.

title: Workers launch strike at world's largest copper mine in Chile
summary: Workers struck at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile after pay talks failed. The mine supplies about 5% of global copper, so even partial shutdown risk can affect near-term output. Analysts note stockpiles may cushion the shock, but longer stoppages could push copper higher.

title: TNR Gold Corp.: TNR Gold NSR Royalty Update - Los Azules Copper, Gold and Silver Project: Los Azules Infill Drilling Confirmed High-Grade Copper Zone
summary: TNR Gold reports that McEwen Copper’s Los Azules project in Argentina delivered infill drilling intercepts confirming a high-grade enriched copper zone and supporting the feasibility study timeline. The release also highlights Argentina’s new investment incentives and a major BHP/Lundin deal for nearby copper assets, boosting sentiment.

title: NewRange Copper Nickel to focus on four new studies about tailings, water science and more
summary: NewRange Copper Nickel said it will run four studies to upgrade tailings storage design, modernize water treatment (with $100 million planned), improve efficient production to potentially raise throughput, and explore electric ore transport. The copper-nickel project uses existing processing infrastructure and faces permitting work, but most permits remain active.

title: Jubilee produces first copper concentrate from Roan front-end module in Zambia
summary: Jubilee Metals Group says it has produced its first copper concentrate from the Roan front-end module in Zambia, with concentrate to be refined at its Sable refinery into copper cathode. The front-end module and Roan upgrade aim to boost processing capacity in-country and increase total copper output potential.

title: Global copper smelter capacity activity remains below normal seasonal levels
summary: Earth-i data shows global copper smelter inactivity averaging 17.1% in July versus about 20% in June, with China driving the changes (inactivity 9.9% at end-July vs 12.4% mid-month). Some China and European restarts occurred, but outside China stayed stable. Tight concentrate market and planned 2025 output curbs suggest firm copper prices.

title: EGA ships bauxite cargo using LNG-fuelled ship
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) says it has shipped bauxite from Guinea to China on an LNG-fuelled, dual-fuel capesize vessel, aiming to cut transport emissions versus traditional marine fuel. Bauxite is the feedstock for aluminium, but the news does not indicate changes to bauxite volumes or aluminium production schedules.

title: Developers of stalled Minnesota copper-nickel mine plan studies that may lead to significant changes
summary: The report says developers of a stalled Minnesota copper-nickel mine plan studies that could result in significant changes. Such actions can influence market expectations for near-term copper and nickel supply. However, the provided text lacks details on whether production will resume, delay, expand, or be canceled, limiting direction.

title: Union Clash at World's Largest Copper Mine Impacts Global Market
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile rejected a proposal to pause their strike, halting formal talks. The strike has shut down key processing and electrowinning facilities and could reduce production. Given Escondida’s scale, the disruption raises near-term supply risk and supports higher copper prices.

title: Chilean miners' strike threatens world copper supply
summary: Workers union action threatens output at Chile’s Escondida copper mine, a facility producing about 5% of world copper in 2023. Negotiations over profit sharing raise the risk of production disruption, which would likely tighten near-term supply and support higher copper prices.

title: Kincora Copper Limited: Kincora Participation in the Sharewise Webinar
summary: Kincora Copper Limited announced it will participate in a Sharewise webinar where its CEO will update investors on the company’s copper asset portfolio, partner strategy, milestones, and upcoming catalysts, including planned drilling. The release is investor-focused and does not indicate immediate market-moving changes in copper supply or demand.

title: Rio Tinto Inks Deal With Queensland State to Safeguard Australia's No. 2 Aluminum Smelter
summary: Rio Tinto signed an agreement with Queensland to safeguard its Boyne aluminum smelter in Gladstone, backed by the state Energy and Jobs Plan as the plant shifts to renewable power. Queensland support from 2029 and Rio’s investment to keep capacity above 500,000 tonnes, plus more bauxite shipping, bolster aluminum supply expectations.

title: Law enforcement, scrap yards team up to combat copper theft in Fresno
summary: Fresno police, county sheriff and local scrap yard Bruno’s coordinate efforts to deter copper wire theft. Scrap yards require customer verification and delay payment, while security and surveillance aim to stop stolen copper entering resale. Theft persists, targeting farms and industrial areas, with law enforcement investigating weekly.

title: China July aluminium output rises to highest monthly total in over 20 yrs
summary: China’s July primary aluminium output rose 6% to 3.68m tonnes, the highest monthly total in over 20 years, as smelters ramped up due to still-profitable operations. While prices recently fell and demand stayed weak, analysts expect profits to remain steady and output to rise further, weighing on aluminium sentiment.

title: New, improved highway lights illuminating US 95 after copper wire theft
summary: Nevada’s NDOT restored streetlights on US 95 after theft caused outages; officials said stolen copper wiring was removed and the repairs were bundled into ongoing road work. Crews also added protective lids and security measures. The new LED lighting is more energy efficient and requires less maintenance, but the impact appears localized.

title: Developers of stalled MN copper-nickel mine plan studies that may lead to changes | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: NewRange Copper Nickel (PolyMet) developers say they will run studies over the next year on redesign options to improve environmental safeguards, reduce carbon emissions, optimize waste storage and water treatment, and change ore transport. Environmental groups argue the plan is flawed. No decisions or production timing changes are announced.

title: Developers of stalled MN copper-nickel mine plan studies that may lead to changes | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: NewRange Copper Nickel (PolyMet) developers said they will run studies on environmental safeguards and cost/energy efficiency, potentially changing the open-pit mine and processing design. Any major changes would require additional reviews and permitting. The project’s further delays/uncertainty are likely a modest negative for near-term copper and nickel sentiment.

title: Global spot copper markets quiet, Asian markets slow amid unfavorable import conditions
summary: Fastmarkets reported copper cathode premiums in China rising week over week, but spot buying slowed as import arbitrage conditions worsened and liquidity thinned after recent price gains. EQ premiums saw steadier demand, while supply was constrained by shipping delays from Africa. Southeast Asia demand was muted, keeping spot quiet.

title: BHP removes striking workers from world's largest copper mine
summary: BHP began removing striking workers from its Escondida copper mine in northern Chile after pay talks collapsed. Although mine operations continue on “minimum services,” reports say BHP has not detailed output cutbacks. Investors fear production reductions, recalling a past strike that materially affected copper prices.

title: Copper hits 10-day high on technical support, supply risks
summary: Copper rose to a 10-day high after breaking key technical levels on the LME and amid potential supply disruptions from a strike at BHP’s Escondida mine in Chile. Trading volumes were low, but workers rejected BHP’s request to pause the strike, keeping supply-risk expectations elevated for copper.

title: Rio Tinto & Queensland Gov partner on renewables to secure aluminium smelters
summary: Queensland partnered with Rio Tinto to secure the future of the Boyne/B2L aluminium smelter (BSL) and support renewable energy and grid upgrades. Economic support is set to safeguard the smelter’s financial viability and power contracting for decarbonised, green aluminium production, supporting supply continuity into the coming years.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd.: Aston Bay and American West Metals Announce Assays Confirm Additional Near-Surface, High-Grade Copper at the Storm Project, Canada
summary: Aston Bay and American West reported assay results from ongoing drilling at Canada’s Storm Copper Project, confirming thick, high-grade copper sulfide intervals at Cyclone and Chinook and initiating drilling at additional targets. The company expects remaining assays in coming weeks, supporting optimism for expanding near-surface and potentially deeper copper resources.

title: Aston Bay and American West Metals Announce Assays Confirm Additional Near-Surface, High-Grade Copper At the Storm Project, Canada
summary: Aston Bay and American West Metals reported assay results from the Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, confirming additional near-surface, high-grade copper sulfide mineralization at Cyclone and Chinook. Drilling is ongoing toward 20,000 meters, with results suggesting potential for new horizons and lateral extensions at depth.

title: BHP strike in Chile enters third day, buoying global copper price
summary: BHP’s Escondida copper mine strike in Chile entered its third day without a breakthrough, raising supply concerns. The union says plants are offline and force majeure has been used in past strikes. LME three-month copper rose sharply, and related mining shares moved higher on expectations of tighter copper supply.

title: Battery weakness weighs on nickel market | Latest Market News
summary: Nickel prices have fallen sharply, reflecting a supply glut in Indonesia and, increasingly, weaker EV battery demand. Europe and the US are seeing EV incentive cutbacks and slower downstream uptake of nickel-rich chemistries (NCM/NCA). Producers are impairing and delaying battery materials investments, reinforcing bearish sentiment for nickel.

title: Strike at world's largest copper mine exposes Boric government and union apparatus in Chile
summary: Workers at Chile’s Escondida copper mine, producing about 5.4% of global output, went on strike after contract talks with BHP failed. The 99.7% vote targets wages, benefits, and automation-related layoffs. BHP activated contingency plans using non-union labor to keep “basic operations,” implying supply disruption risk for copper.

title: Copper set for first weekly gain in six on supply risks, US data
summary: Copper prices are set for their first weekly gain in six, supported by mine supply worries after a strike at BHP’s Escondida in Chile and stronger-than-feared U.S. retail sales and jobs data easing recession fears. Aluminium and nickel also ticked higher, reflecting improved base-metals sentiment.

title: Replacing China in copper supply chain is 'unfeasible,' warns WoodMac
summary: Wood Mackenzie says efforts to replace China’s dominance across the copper supply chain are unfeasible, requiring hundreds of billions of dollars in new processing and fabrication capacity. With limited smelting plans in North America/Europe and mine/project gaps by 2030, the risk of tighter copper availability and higher costs rises as energy transition demand grows.

title: Copper eyes first weekly gain in six on Chile strike, fading US growth concerns
summary: Copper prices were set for their first weekly gain in six as a strike at BHP’s Escondida mine in Chile raised supply disruption worries. Prices also found support as U.S. recession fears eased with positive retail sales and jobs data, prompting traders to reduce bearish positions.

title: Supply risks set copper on track for first weekly gain in six
summary: Copper in London is set for its first weekly gain in six weeks as markets worry about a potential strike at BHP’s Escondida mine in Chile, which could tighten supply. The move is tempered by rising LME warehouse stocks, but supportive macro data and technical support underpin prices.

title: BHP says strike ends at huge Escondida copper mine
summary: BHP said it reached an agreement with a striking union at its Escondida copper mine in Chile, calling off a three-day strike after failed pay talks. The suspension reduces fears of near-term supply losses from the world’s largest copper producer, likely supporting copper sentiment and prices.

title: BHP reaches agreement with striking union at Escondida copper mine in Chile
summary: BHP and the main union at the Escondida copper mine in Chile agreed to a revised wage/bonus offer, suspending the strike after it began on Tuesday. The settlement eased fears over disruptions to global copper supplies. Copper prices initially fell on the news, then recovered slightly.

title: BHP Strikes Deal with Escondida Union, Halting Copper Mine Strike
summary: BHP reached a settlement with the union at Chile’s Escondida copper mine, ending a three-day strike over pay. The agreement suspends the strike from Friday, easing fears of global copper supply disruption given Escondida’s scale as the world’s largest copper mine.

title: Chinalco Is Said to Eye Stake in Biggest Philippine Copper Mine
summary: Chinalco is reportedly considering a roughly $2 billion stake in the Tampakan copper mine via Indophil Resources. The deal could also involve buying some output, improving project funding. While production is not expected until 2026, the move supports near-term sentiment around future copper supply expansion.

title: Strike at world's largest copper mine owned by BHP suspended
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in northern Chile suspended a strike and restarted talks with management, according to union and management announcements. The disruption had been launched earlier in the week, making near-term supply risk a key factor for copper market sentiment over the next days.

title: No one believed in you, yet you rose to the top...——Laterite nickel ore prices surged strongly [SMM Analysis]
summary: Philippine laterite nickel ore prices increased over the past week, with medium-grade ore rising from about $45/wmt to ~$48/wmt. Demand from Indonesia, tight ore supply, and smelter restocking needs are cited, while policy rewards and expectations of further quota tightness could keep prices rising short term.

title: Workers at world's biggest copper mine in Chile suspend strike
summary: Workers at Chile’s world’s biggest copper mine have suspended a strike, according to the article. The move likely reduces the immediate risk of lost output and supply disruption, which can pressure short-term copper prices as market participants adjust toward improved near-term availability.

title: Police arrest suspect in $20,000 copper downspout theft
summary: Police arrested a suspect for stealing about 40 copper downspouts worth about $20,000 from a shopping center in San Luis Obispo. Investigators say the suspect sold over 1,000 pounds of copper downspouts and insulated copper wiring to a scrap yard and may have additional victims.

title: Workers At World's Biggest Copper Mine In Chile Suspend Strike
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile suspended a strike and restarted negotiations after reaching consensus on a new collective bargaining contract. The move lowers the risk of continued production loss at a top global supplier, supporting expectations for steadier near-term copper supply and prices.

title: Miners down tools at two Chilean copper mines, as majors struggle to maintain production levels
summary: Strikes at Chile’s Caserones and Escondida mines are expected to disrupt copper production after failed collective bargaining. With Chile the world’s largest mined copper supplier, the labor actions add to already tight supply conditions, supporting expectations for higher copper prices in coming days.

title: European automotive aluminium demand set to slow: Fastmarkets analysts
summary: Fastmarkets says European automotive aluminium demand is weakening as cost-of-living pressures keep consumers cautious and vehicle output remains depressed. Primary foundry alloy premiums (PFA), mainly used in car parts, have fallen to $500-520/t in Germany. Vehicle sales and production declines and postponements reinforce bearish near-term sentiment.

title: Nevada Copper has potential buyer
summary: Nevada Copper Corp. signed an agreement with Southwest Critical Materials LLC (an affiliate of Kinterra Capital) to buy substantially all of its assets for $128 million as a “stalking horse” bidder. If the deal proceeds, Southwest would also pay specified cure costs, subject to liability adjustments.

title: Escondida: Strike at BHP-owned copper ends as workers win $48,000 bonus
summary: Workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile suspended their strike after agreeing to a sweetened wage/bonus offer. The settlement ends a disruption at the world’s largest copper mine and eases concerns over near-term global copper supply, which had been supporting higher copper prices.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Reports Fatality at the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said a fatal accident occurred underground at the Kansoko mine within the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in DRC. Mining was temporarily suspended for investigation and has since restarted after securing the incident area. The company is reviewing safety protocols with DRC authorities.

title: Workers at world's biggest copper mine in Chile call off strike
summary: Workers at the world’s biggest copper mine in Chile have called off a strike. With the labor action no longer threatening halted production and shipments, near-term copper supply disruption risk falls. This can improve market expectations for inventories and support a firmer outlook for copper prices over coming days.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp.: Flying Nickel and Nevada Vanadium Complete Merger
summary: Flying Nickel Mining completed its merger, acquiring 100% of Nevada Vanadium, creating a wholly owned subsidiary. The company is primarily focused on advancing its Minago nickel project and a vanadium project. The corporate combination may affect longer-term sentiment, but no near-term production or supply changes are stated.

title: Workers At World's Biggest Copper Mine In Chile Call Off Strike
summary: Workers at the world’s biggest copper mine in Chile called off a strike after reaching a pay agreement with BHP. By resolving the labor dispute before any prolonged shutdown, the move lowers short-term disruption risk and supports expectations for uninterrupted copper supply in coming days.

title: A trip to El Teniente, the largest underground copper mine in the world
summary: The piece profiles Codelco’s El Teniente, the world’s largest underground copper mine, noting 2023 output fell 8.4% due to mine interruptions and delayed investment. It describes a $40bn plan to lift production and green operations (electric buses, electric rail, tire pyrolysis), but gives no clear immediate supply shock.

title: Can the West Afford to Build Its Own Copper Industry?
summary: The piece argues that copper prices may need to rise as electrification accelerates, but copper mines and—more critically—refining/smelting capacity are concentrated in China. Wood Mackenzie estimates tens of billions in needed non-China processing investment, noting little new capacity in Europe/North America, supporting a tighter outlook for copper.

title: Union at BHP's Escondida copper mine warns it could relaunch strike
summary: A union at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile warned it may relaunch a strike later on Sunday unless BHP addresses contract issues promptly. After a strike earlier this week over payment disputes, a preliminary agreement was reached to end it, but renewed action could again disrupt global copper supply.

title: Union at BHP's Escondida copper mine warns it could relaunch strike | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: BHP’s Escondida copper mine union in Chile warned it could relaunch a strike if the company does not address contract talks quickly. After a strike began Tuesday over payment disputes, a preliminary agreement was reached Friday to end it, but renewed action could disrupt copper supply again.

title: A recent overview of nickel sulphate prices | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM reports the battery-grade nickel sulphate index at 27,826 yuan/mt on Aug 16, down WoW. Demand is subdued because downstream cathode material firms are not at restocking peaks, though some buying improved. Inventory is relatively low and sentiment is supportive, but costs remain inverted, limiting upside; a modest rebound is expected into early September.

title: Great Bear Project delivers further outstanding Copper, Gold & Silver assays
summary: White Cliff Minerals announced additional rock-chip assay results from its Great Bear Project in Northern Canada, including multiple high-grade copper grades (up to 42.2% Cu) alongside gold and silver. The findings suggest expanded IOCG/epithermal copper potential, but they are early exploration data and unlikely to materially affect near-term copper pricing.

title: Union at BHP's Escondida copper mine in Chile signs new deal, ending risk of strike
summary: A union at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile has agreed to a new deal, ending the risk of a strike. The resolution lowers the probability of output disruptions at one of the world’s largest copper sources, which should be supportive for near-term copper pricing.

title: Copper climbs as US recession fears fade, China inventories decline
summary: Copper prices rose as U.S. recession fears eased after strong U.S. data and China’s copper inventories fell. LME three-month copper climbed 0.9% and SHFE September gained 0.5%. The report also cites easing supply concerns at BHP’s Escondida after a wage deal, alongside gains in aluminium and a modest nickel rise.

title: QLD Gov't set to secure Boyne Island aluminium smelter - Manufacturers' Monthly
summary: Queensland will partner with Rio Tinto to secure the Boyne Island aluminium smelter’s long-term operation, including full-capacity requirements until end-2040 and renewable energy support to protect competitiveness. The deal also includes demand response to reduce electricity demand during tight supply. Overall, it supports aluminium supply stability.

title: Strike Averted: Escondida Copper Mine Union Reaches Deal with BHP
summary: Chile’s Escondida union signed a deal with BHP, ending the threat of another strike. After an initial strike over payment disputes, a preliminary agreement was reached, and the looming disruption risk to global copper supplies was neutralized, supporting market sentiment for near-term copper prices.

title: Copper gains on waning US recession fears, China demand
summary: Copper prices opened higher as U.S. recession worries faded after strong macro data, while improving demand in top consumer China supported purchases. Deliverable SHFE stocks fell to a five-month low. Operations at China refined-rod producers picked up, and a strike at BHP’s Escondida was suspended.

title: Union at BHP's Escondida copper mine in Chile signs new deal, ending risk of strike | WKZO | Everything Kalamazoo
summary: Chile’s Escondida union signed a new deal with BHP, ending the threat of a further strike. The union had warned members could call another walkout over contract talks after a Tuesday strike over pay disputes, followed by a preliminary agreement on Friday. The resolution lowers risk to global copper supplies.

title: Historic Deal Reached at Chile's Escondida Copper Mine
summary: Escondida’s union in Chile signed a three-year agreement with BHP after ending a strike tied to payment disputes. The labor deal adjusts work conditions, shift changes, and bonuses, averting potential disruption at the world’s largest copper mine and lowering short-term supply risk for global copper.

title: China demand hopes, lower dollar lift copper prices
summary: Copper prices climbed to a 2-1/2 week high as signs of improving demand in China encouraged physical buyers and a sliding dollar made dollar-priced metal cheaper. ShFE copper stocks were at five-month lows, while LME inventory overhang remained. Aluminium also rose on declining LME stocks and cancelled warrants.

title: Flying Nickel finalises purchase of Nevada Vanadium
summary: Flying Nickel Mining has finalized the acquisition of Nevada Vanadium, making it a wholly owned subsidiary. The company is an exploration-stage miner focused on nickel sulphide and vanadium, including development of its Minago nickel project in Manitoba. The article details share issuance and governance changes, with no stated output timing changes.

title: The role of bauxite in Australia's geostrategic competitiveness
summary: Australia’s FMIA bill will fund “critical minerals” but excludes bauxite from the Critical Minerals List, though aluminium is treated as a strategic/green material. The Australian Aluminium Council argues this omission may weaken investment in the bauxite–alumina pathway. The piece highlights competitive pressure and energy costs for mining and refining.

title: Power Nickel Caps Off Impressive Lion Zone Winter Drilling Program With Cueq Results Of Holes 50 And 60 Ranging From 1.23% To 7.36%
summary: Power Nickel reported final results from a winter drilling program at its Nisk project’s “Lion Zone,” saying the mineralized zone increased over 94% and providing assay intercepts. The company is pursuing further summer drilling to test depth and continuity, aiming to expand high-grade nickel-copper mineralization.

title: BHP workers at world's largest copper mine claim pay dispute 'victory' - News
summary: Union workers at BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile have called off a strike after reaching a pay agreement. The dispute follows earlier expectations of a high daily output loss. With Escondida/Pampa Norte central to Chilean and global supply, the resolution lowers immediate copper supply risk and supports prices.

title: Aluminum Prices Continue to Slide
summary: Aluminum prices have continued to slide, with monthly declines after a brief mid-year stabilization. The piece highlights bearish factors including rising Chinese primary output, large inventories, wide contango versus spot, tepid Chinese demand, and investment funds cutting longs and adding shorts—together weighing on near-term aluminum sentiment.

title: Progress on Diversifying From Chinese-Backed Copper Sources Slow: Research
summary: Research says progress diversifying away from Chinese-backed copper sources is slow. Wood Mackenzie warns that a scenario without China in the copper supply chain would require a substantial increase in processing capacity to hit green-energy targets. The implication is higher perceived supply/refining constraints and potential price support for copper.

title: Strike at Lundin's Caserones copper mine showing no signs of resolution after a week, union says
summary: Workers at Lundin Mining’s Caserones copper mine in Chile have been on strike for over a week after contract talks failed. The union says there are no signs of resolution and that output is running at less than half of capacity. The stoppage could extend beyond 40 days, pressuring near-term copper supply.

title: London copper prices fall on short-covering
summary: London LME three-month copper fell 0.4% as the previous rally was attributed to short-covering rather than new demand. Open interest declined and analysts noted limited contract rollover. Chinese physical demand improved slightly, and an Escondida strike was averted, easing supply fears. LME aluminium and nickel also declined.

title: Bougainville Copper and Rio Tinto sign deal to clean up mining site
summary: Bougainville Copper Ltd and former parent Rio Tinto signed an MoU to remove ageing infrastructure at the long-closed Panguna mine to address safety risks. The cleanup will target old pumping and bridge assets and workshop/storage infrastructure, starting in November 2024 over several months, with legacy assessment results due Q4 2024.

title: BHP's quick strike fix sets tone for labor talks amid copper rally
summary: BHP’s Escondida copper mine in Chile settled a six-day strike after unions won a higher bonus and interest-free loan, avoiding a prolonged disruption like 2017. The deal, backed by high copper prices, may influence upcoming labor negotiations across Chile’s mines. Unions argue strong profits justify higher pay.

title: BHP's Swift Deal at Escondida Copper Mine Sparks Industry-Wide Implications
summary: BHP rapidly resolved a six-day strike at Chile’s Escondida copper mine, granting workers bonuses and interest-free loans after an earlier offer. The settlement may influence forthcoming labor negotiations at other Chilean mines. Analysts link the deal to strong demand tied to EVs and AI.

title: Weir Group plc Receives Redefined Flowheet Contract for Reko Diq Greenfield Copper-Gold Project
summary: Weir Group won a £53 million contract to supply energy-efficient grinding, separation and tailings equipment for the Reko Diq greenfield copper-gold project in Balochistan. The contract supports phase one processing, with first production targeted for 2028, implying little immediate impact on near-term copper fundamentals.

title: Copper miners, energy stocks pull FTSE 100 lower
summary: FTSE 100 edged lower as energy and copper miners fell. Energy shares declined with oil prices. Copper miners were down slightly because copper prices fell following short-covering after a prior rally. The market is also awaiting Fed Chair Powell’s Jackson Hole speech and upcoming PMI data.

title: Kobrea secures option for Argentina copper portfolio
summary: Kobrea Exploration secured an exclusive option to acquire up to 100% of Argentina’s Western Malargüe copper projects, covering 73,334 hectares. The deal includes a 1.5% NSR and cash/share payments up to 2029, but the projects have no drilling to date, implying limited near-term supply impact.

title: Analysis of Nickel Ore Import Data for July 2024 [SMM Data] | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: SMM cited China Customs data showing China’s nickel ore imports fell to 3.4851 million wmt in July (-30.6% YoY), with laterite down sharply. Philippines shipments dipped due to weather, though constraints are easing and supply is shifting toward Indonesia. August is expected to see room for laterite growth despite domestic demand.

title: Aluminium Hits 5-Week High on Fund Buying, Alumina Shortage
summary: Aluminium rose to a five-week high on the LME as fund buying increased and China faced a shortage of raw material (alumina). Three-month aluminium touched about $2,482/ton, the highest since mid-July, and last traded around $2,470, up roughly 1%.

title: Sterling Metals Corp.: Sterling Metals Provides Update on its Phase 1 Exploration Campaign at the Copper Road Project
summary: Sterling Metals provides an update on Phase 1 exploration at its Copper Road copper-molybdenum project in Ontario, reporting soil anomalies, airborne geophysical inversion, LiDAR interpretation, and new surface copper sulphide showings. The company plans further geophysics, assays, and preparation for a maiden drill campaign.

title: China's rare copper export boom signals more than weak demand
