summary: China’s refined copper exports surged in June, shipping 158,000 tons despite softening manufacturing activity. The move is attributed to higher Chinese output, strong imports (including Congolese supply), and prior CME delivery constraints creating an export arbitrage window. With demand not matching supply, premiums and prices weakened, pushing copper lower.

title: World Pumps - Weir wins £53mn contract for greenfield copper-gold project in Pakistan
summary: Weir won a £53mn contract to supply grinding, separation, tailings and related process equipment for Barrick’s Reko Diq copper-gold project in Pakistan. The tier-one project targets first production in 2028, implying long-dated capacity additions and minimal immediate effect on copper prices.

title: Falcon Gold Corp.: Falcon Reports the Status of Drill Program at Great Burnt Copper Project, Newfoundland
summary: Falcon Gold reported delays from high water levels at its Great Burnt Copper Project in Newfoundland and the need for additional permitting to build 8 km of road. Equipment mobilization is pending completion by week-end, after which drilling will test multiple copper geophysical anomalies. No nickel operational changes were reported.

title: Miner Antofagasta's half-year profit up on strong copper prices
summary: Chilean miner Antofagasta reported a 5% rise in half-year profit, driven by higher copper prices that outweighed lower sales. It also highlighted ongoing mine and processing expansion, expected copper output near the low end of guidance due to lower ore grades, and referenced LME copper strength before a later decline.

title: Falcon Gold Corp. Reports the Status of Drill Program At Great Burnt Copper Project, Newfoundland
summary: Falcon Gold reports delays and permitting for drill access at its Great Burnt Copper Project in Newfoundland, with roadwork expected to finish by week-end. The property is contiguous to Benton/Homeland Nickel’s Great Burnt Copper Zone. Reported past and recent drilling shows high copper grades, but no immediate production impact.

title: Peru likely to mine up to 2.8-million tons of copper this year, SNMPE says
summary: Peru is expected to mine 2.7–2.8 million tonnes of copper in 2024, below the government’s 3 million ton goal. Output is also down versus last year, with additional June weakness tied to a two-week Toromocho stoppage. Antamina output is expected steady, with ongoing investment plans.

title: Bangkok Post - Agency probes aluminium dumping
summary: Thailand’s Foreign Trade Department is probing and has issued an affirmative preliminary determination in an anti-dumping case against Chinese aluminium extrusions, prompted by complaints of import surges harming domestic producers. If dumping is confirmed, anti-dumping duties could be imposed for five years, potentially tightening supply and supporting prices.

title: Zeb Nickel Corp.: Integrated Environmental Authorisation Granted to Zeb Nickel Project
summary: Zeb Nickel Corp. said South Africa’s DMPR granted an Integrated Environmental Authorisation for its Limpopo Zeb Nickel Project, clearing a major permitting phase after a lengthy EIA process. The approval supports progressing toward a mining right for nickel extraction, with additional associated copper mineralisation mentioned.

title: BHP in discussions with Indonesian government on nickel: Reports
summary: Reports say BHP is discussing potential investment with Indonesia’s government to expand/participate in Indonesia’s rapidly growing nickel processing industry. The backdrop is BHP suspending WA nickel operations due to global nickel oversupply from Indonesia’s export ban. Such investment talks may support longer-term nickel supply balance expectations near term.

title: ACT police warn of fatal risks after CSIRO copper theft | The Canberra Times
summary: ACT police warn that copper thieves cut down live power lines at a CSIRO facility, leaving exposed wires that could be fatal. Police also cite other copper-theft incidents causing damage to heritage buildings. The report provides no supply policy or production impacts, suggesting limited direct effect on copper prices.

title: Indonesia's president-elect should get real on nickel | News | Eco-Business
summary: Eco-Business says Indonesia’s nickel push faces major hurdles: low-grade product focus, ore supply gaps, heavy captive-coal emissions, and environmental/labor controversies. EU and US rules may reduce appeal of Indonesian processed nickel, and a $2.6 billion BASF–Eramet project was cancelled. The article warns of China dependence and possible nickel price weakness.

title: ACT police warn of fatal risks after CSIRO copper theft | Braidwood Times
summary: ACT Policing warned about fatal risks after copper theft at a CSIRO facility, where live power lines were allegedly cut and left exposed. Police also cited additional copper-stealing incidents in Lawson causing extensive damage. The report signals ongoing theft activity but gives no copper volume, so market impact is uncertain.

title: Copper thieves spark outrage with Tweed Heads General Cemetery gravestone robberies
summary: Around 100 copper plaques were stolen from Tweed Heads General Cemetery, prompting council replacement costs estimated at $30,000–$40,000. The story links copper theft incentives to current scrap prices and notes past evidence that higher copper prices can coincide with more theft, though the incident is local and unlikely to move global prices.

title: New Xanadu resource lifts Mongolian copper-gold potential
summary: Xanadu Mines increased the contained copper at its Kharmagtai project in Mongolia by 463,000 tonnes (plus higher gold), driven by new drilling and refined pit-shell modeling for an upcoming prefeasibility study. This suggests improved longer-term copper potential, but no immediate output changes, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Tweed Heads: More than 100 copper plaques stolen from Tweed Heads cemetery
summary: More than 100 copper plaques were stolen from a cemetery in Tweed Heads. The council suspects they were taken to be resold as scrap metal and says the scrap value is about $1,500, though replacement could cost $30,000-$40,000. Local recyclers were alerted and police are seeking information.

title: Weir lands Reko Diq copper-gold project contract in Pakistan
summary: Weir Group won a £53m contract to supply grinding, separation, and tailings-management equipment for Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper-gold project. The mine is expected to start production in 2028 and has a long mine life. The deal is for equipment delivery and progressive revenue recognition.

title: Zeb Nickel's South Africa mine gains environmental authorisation
summary: Zeb Nickel received integrated environmental authorisation from South Africa’s Department of Minerals and Petroleum Resources for its Bushveld complex project. The approval supports progress toward a mining right and allows activities under the approved EIA, with plans for further drilling to improve nickel grade and project economics.

title: 'Copper volatility reveals growing demand for the metal'
summary: The piece argues copper demand is accelerating from AI/data centres, solar/wind and rising per-capita consumption, while refined supply growth has been limited since 2016. It cites prior supply deficits, constrained reserves/discovery challenges, and ongoing import dependence, suggesting near-term upward pressure on copper prices due to potential shortages.

title: Faraday Copper Corp. Announces the Results of Two Drill Holes from its Ongoing Phase III Drill Program at the Copper Creek Project, Located in Arizona, U.S
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. reported assay and geological results from two Phase III drill holes at its Copper Creek project in Arizona, confirming near-surface copper mineralization potential (chalcopyrite, breccias/porphyry, sericite alteration). The update is exploration-stage and does not indicate near-term production or supply changes.

title: Benton Resources Inc.: Benton Stakes Strategic Land at Great Burnt and Provides Exploration Update - Channel Sample Assays 3.79 g/t Gold, 0.68% Copper & 4.10 g/t Silver Over 5.10 m at South Pond
summary: Benton Resources announced staking new ground near its Great Burnt Copper Deposit and provided channel-sampling results at South Pond, including ~0.68% copper over 5.10 m and up to 1.60% copper over 5.10 m. The company plans further drilling to expand these copper-focused deposits, with assays pending for new sampling.

title: Western Metallica Announces Successful Renegotiation of Caña Brava Copper Project Option Agreement
summary: Western Metallica renegotiated its option agreement to acquire a 100% interest in Peru’s Caña Brava copper-(molybdenum) project, adjusting the transfer price payment schedule through 2028. The company also dropped the Turmalina option and plans a near-term copper drilling program. No immediate production impacts are stated.

title: Faraday Copper Intersects 1.01% Copper Over 117.90 Metres within 269.65 Metres at 0.64% Copper, Discovering the High-Grade Mineralized Banjo Breccia in the American Eagle Area
summary: Faraday Copper reported new drill results from its Copper Creek Project in Arizona, including 1.01% copper over 117.9 m at the Banjo breccia and 0.39% copper over 88.2 m at the American Eagle breccia. Management says mineralization is open and continues delineation drilling.

title: Western Metallica Resources Corp. Announces Successful Renegotiation of Caña Brava Copper Project Option Agreement
summary: Western Metallica Resources announced it renegotiated the option agreement to acquire a 100% interest in the Caña Brava copper project in northern Peru, including revised flexibility on the term and payment schedule. The company also dropped interests in a separate Turmalina project, with holders confirming no amounts owed.

title: Flying Nickel Mining Corp. Enters an Arrangement Agreement to Sell its Minago Assets to Norway House Cree Nation
summary: Flying Nickel Mining entered a definitive arrangement to sell its Minago nickel assets in Manitoba to Norway House Cree Nation for C$8 million cash plus shares. The transaction is expected by mid-October 2024 and requires shareholder and regulatory approvals. The announcement is asset-specific and not linked to broader nickel supply or pricing changes.

title: Pacific Ridge begins drilling at Canada copper-gold project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration has begun its first diamond drilling at the Chuchi copper-gold project in British Columbia, targeting potential porphyry copper-gold mineralisation at depth. The 2024 program is limited to about 3,000m across several holes to confirm historical results. It is exploration, not production, so near-term copper prices are unlikely to move meaningfully.

title: Times of Zambia   |  Long wait over! KCM handover thrills Copperbelt
summary: Zambian officials say President Hakainde Hichilema will officially hand over Konkola Copper Mine (KCM) assets to Vedanta Resources during a Copperbelt visit. Stakeholders express optimism, implying a positive resolution for operations and copper supply prospects from the key producing region.

title: Lion Copper and Gold Corp.: Lion Copper and Gold Announces Yerington Bear Deposit Diamond Drill Results, Hole B-056A Encountered 2,376 ft of 0.40% TCu
summary: Lion Copper and Gold reported 2024 diamond drill results from its Bear deposit in Nevada, including hole B-056A intersecting 0.40% TCu over 2,376 ft (with higher-grade sub-intervals). The company frames results as expanding the deposit footprint, but no near-term production changes were announced.

title: Breaking Mining Stock News: New Destiny Mining (TSXV: NED) Drilling Update: Hole 6 Intersects Copper Mineralization and Porphyry Dikes
summary: New Destiny Mining reported drilling at its Treasure Mountain project, completing six holes and intersecting a mineralized interval with chalcopyrite and pyrite within an altered porphyry system near the Railroad copper-silver zone. The company highlights copper soil anomalies and planned follow-up holes, but no production or supply changes are announced.

title: Canada Reliant on China for Copper to Achieve Lower Carbon Emissions Goals: Report
summary: A Wood Mackenzie report says Canada can’t meet its emissions targets without relying on China, and it frames copper as critical for electrification. By stressing the country’s dependence on Chinese copper supply for the energy transition, the article can bolster near-term expectations for copper demand and pricing.

title: New Destiny Mining Corp.: New Destiny Mining Drilling Update: Hole 6 Intersects Copper Mineralization and Porphyry Dikes
summary: New Destiny Mining reported drilling at its Treasure Mountain project, intersecting a mineralized interval with chalcopyrite/pyr­ite and altered felsic porphyry dikes, along with copper soil anomalies. The company is targeting a possible porphyry feeder to a Railroad copper zone. No production or supply changes are announced.

title: Solar-powered street lights coming to East Las Vegas as a solution to copper wire thefts
summary: East Las Vegas Valley is installing 12 solar-powered streetlights to deter copper wire thieves that have damaged public lighting since 2022. Officials say the units contain hardly any copper and outline additional efforts like ordinances and a potential state law targeting sales of stolen copper.

title: Copper Rises on Falling Inventories, Improving Demand
summary: Copper prices rose as inventories declined, reducing supply tightness concerns. The report also points to improving demand momentum in China and less fear of a U.S. recession, supporting buying interest. LME three-month copper and SHFE September copper both edged higher in early trading.

title: Thailand launches anti-dumping probe on Chinese extruded aluminium
summary: Thailand’s Department of Foreign Trade opened a nine-month anti-dumping investigation into Chinese extruded aluminium after local producers complained of injury from imports. The authorities may impose duties for five years if dumping is confirmed and can extend measures if damage persists, potentially tightening supply.

title: Material Capex Reductions for BKM Copper Project | Company Announcement
summary: Asiamet reports substantial capex reductions for its BKM copper project following engineering optimisation, including initial savings of over $26m and total pre-production capex savings of $50–80m. The company also advances permits for limestone supply and progresses biomass power plans, improving financing prospects for copper SX-EW development.

title: Flying Nickel seals deal to offload Minago project
summary: Flying Nickel Mining signed a definitive deal to sell its Minago nickel project in Manitoba to Norway House Cree Nation, receiving $8m cash and a 11.4% share stake transfer. The company plans a rebrand and remains active in its Nevada vanadium interests. The transaction is unlikely to meaningfully shift near-term global nickel balances.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd.: Aston Bay and American West Metals Announce Large-Scale Copper Targets at Depth Take Shape at the Storm Project, Nunavut, Canada
summary: Aston Bay and American West report deep diamond drilling at the Storm Copper Project in Nunavut intersected thick intervals of visual copper sulfides, including native copper, and EM surveys defined a large deep anomaly for follow-up drilling. The update is copper-focused exploration progress, without any immediate supply or refining impact.

title: Namibia's only refined copper plant restarts operation after four-year hiatus-Xinhua
summary: Namibia’s Consolidated Copper Corp restarted operations at the Tschudi copper plant after a four-year hiatus. The facility is Namibia’s only LME-grade refined copper processor and previously produced over 80,000 tonnes annually. Restart funding was secured via TRP debt financing, supporting local beneficiation and refined supply.

title: NewRange Copper seeking to advance new mine plan
summary: NewRange Copper Nickel advances permitting-critical studies for a potential NorthMet copper-nickel mine near Hoyt Lakes, including tailings, water treatment, and efficiency upgrades. The company is examining higher throughput (32,000 to 40,000 tons/day) to increase domestic copper and nickel supply, which could lift near-term price sentiment.

title: Midland and Soquem Identify on Nachicapau New High-Grade Mineralized Occurrences and Expand the Footprint of the Copper-Gold-Silver Hydrothermal System
summary: Midland Exploration and Soquem report new high-grade copper-gold-silver showings at the Nachicapau project in Quebec, including copper-bearing veins with strong grades and extended surface footprint. The work includes geochemical sampling and surveys, but remains exploration with no production timeline or immediate impact on copper supply.

title: Atacama Copper to Become Fuerte Metals
summary: Fuerte Metals (formerly Atacama Copper) changed its name and TSXV symbol to FMT and outlined upcoming drilling. The company emphasized copper exploration at Placeton/Caballo Muerto in Chile and planned drilling at Yecora in Sonora, plus continued work at its Cristina project. No production or inventory changes were disclosed.

title: Aston Bay and American West Metals Announce Large-Scale Copper Targets at Depth Take Shape at the Storm Project, Nunavut, Canada
summary: Aston Bay and American West report further deep diamond drilling success at the Storm Copper Project in Nunavut, with thick intervals of visual copper sulfide and a defined deep EM anomaly (1,300m x 500m) now being drilled. The results strengthen expectations for large-scale copper mineralization at depth.

title: Namibia's only refined copper plant restarts operation after four-year hiatus
summary: Namibia’s Consolidated Copper Corp restarted the Tschudi copper plant after a four-year shutdown, following refurbishment. The restart is expected to create jobs and involves significant local contracting. The operational return raises expectations for additional refined copper output in the near term, supporting copper sentiment.

title: Coppernico Metals Inc.: Coppernico Metals Announces the Voting Results of its 2024 Annual General Meeting
summary: Coppernico Metals reported voting results from its 2024 AGM, including director and auditor reappointments. The CEO also said the company is actively drilling the fourth hole at its Sombrero Project in Peru, which targets copper-gold deposits, and highlighted a strong cash position. No immediate production or supply impact is disclosed.

title: Deputy notices suspicious vehicle, circles back, busts man suspected of stealing copper
summary: A Rankin County deputy arrested a man suspected of multiple copper wire thefts and burglarizing commercial property and a semi-truck trailer. Authorities say copper thefts have increased and cite copper wires and tools found in the suspect’s SUV. The report is localized, with no broader market supply impact stated.

title: Li3 Lithium Corp: Li3 Lithium Announces Shareholder Approval of Name Change to Reflect its Focus on its 100%-Owned Northern Lights Copper Project Located in Nevada
summary: Li3 Lithium shareholders approved a name change to Global Copper Corp. The company also initiated soil and rock sampling and plans EM and reverse-circulation drilling at its 100%-owned Northern Lights Copper Project in Nevada. Historic and new surface sampling show copper mineralization, but no production changes are announced.

title: New solar streetlights installed in Las Vegas to stop copper wire thefts
summary: Clark County in Las Vegas is installing 12 solar streetlights in a neighborhood plagued by copper wire theft. The pilot replaces older poles using copper wiring with solar panels and batteries, after thieves stole nearly 1 million feet of copper wire since 2022. The change reduces local copper demand.

title: Copper asset in Zambia a true gold mine
summary: JCHX Mining Management says it will upgrade technology and improve efficiency at Zambia’s Lubambe Copper Mine after acquiring it in June. The mine targets 2.5 million tonnes of copper-ore capacity annually. The piece frames this as part of China’s push to secure critical mineral supplies as copper demand rises.

title: Noronex deploys gravity to unravel Kalahari copper mysteries
summary: Noronex began a large gravity survey over its Humpback-Damara copper exploration projects in Namibia to refine drill targets under Kalahari sand cover, with drilling planned later this quarter. South32 committed funding via an earn-in alliance. The update supports exploration prospects but does not change current supply materially.

title: What is the reason of "sky-high coefficient" for high-grade nickel matte? [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports the coefficient for high-grade nickel matte versus LME nickel rose to 87–88 as nickel prices fell and refining costs increased. It also cites weak downstream demand, substitution pressure from MHP due to high coefficients, and producers shifting toward NPI for better margins, leaving transactions sluggish.

title: BHP's return to Argentina marks new hope for untapped copper mines
summary: Reuters reports Argentina’s RIGI incentive regime has revived interest from major miners such as BHP, enabling financing and development planning for several copper projects along the Andes. Analysts and company executives expect valuations to rise and more deals to follow, potentially boosting future copper supply outlook over coming months.

title: Argentina's Copper Surge: Major Investments after New Incentive Regime
summary: Argentina’s new RIGI incentive regime is driving a renewed wave of copper mining investment, including major commitments from BHP and Lundin Mining. The government expects production expansion toward the end of the decade, though Argentina’s economy remains volatile. Overall, near-term copper supply impact appears limited.

title: CEO.CA Technologies Ltd.: CEO.CA's Inside The Boardroom: American Eagle Continues to Discover High-Grade Copper and Gold at NAK
summary: CEO.CA’s “Inside the Boardroom” features American Eagle Gold’s CEO discussing latest results at the NAK project and the copper and gold grades encountered so far. While the piece is promotional and lacks detailed assay or production timelines, the reported copper exploration progress can modestly support bullish copper sentiment.

title: Half-year Report | Company Announcement
summary: BlackRock World Mining Trust’s half-year report notes heightened volatility from macro and geopolitics, but says base and precious metals were buoyant, with copper breaking out to new all-time highs. It also points to softer Chinese property-related demand weighing on some bulk commodities. Nickel and aluminium are not specifically discussed.

title: Times of Zambia   |  FQM buys $6m copper cables from ZAMEFAthat
summary: First Quantum Minerals (FQM) is purchasing US$6 million of copper cables from ZAMEFA for construction of its S3 copper processing plant at Kansanshi Mine in Zambia. FQM says the 546 km of local copper cables represent over half of the project’s total cable requirement, indicating near-term copper demand.

title: Hindalco Announce Major Expansion Plans to Boost Aluminum Production Capacity
summary: Hindalco and Novelis announced a $10 billion investment plan to expand aluminium production and the recycling value chain. Hindalco plans a major Aditya smelter and flat-rolled products expansion in Odisha and a new alumina refinery at Rayagada. Novelis will add rolling and recycling capacity in the US and expand UBC recycling in the UK.

title: Copper thefts from utility poles raise concerns for Farmers RECC
summary: Farmers RECC in Glasgow, Kentucky says copper thefts from utility poles are compromising lightning protection and grid reliability, forcing additional repairs and straining line workers. The utility urges residents to report suspicious activity. The incident removes copper from distribution equipment but appears too localized to materially shift copper prices.

title: Russian mining giant Nornickel's first-half profit slumps on weak prices
summary: Nornickel reported a 22% profit drop, blaming weak nickel prices, logistics disruptions in the Red Sea, and harder cross-border payments. Maritime restrictions caused nickel and copper stock accumulation and reduced sales. The firm cited a 28% LME nickel price fall in H1 and forecast a 2024/25 nickel surplus.

title: Africa's Copperbelt and the Atlantic - Geopolitical Futures
summary: The planned Lobito Corridor rail links the DRC and Zambia to Angola’s Port of Lobito, aiming to cut export costs and improve access to EU and U.S. markets for copper-bearing mining areas. While still early and financing-dependent, it signals improved logistics for copper supply and potential upward price expectations.

title: As Russia Feels Effects of Multilateral Sanctions Campaign, Treasury Takes Further Action Against Russia's International Supply Chains
summary: The U.S. Treasury and State Department announced new OFAC/G7-aligned sanctions targeting nearly 400 individuals and entities involved in Russia’s military-industrial base supply chains, including entities tied to Russia’s metals and mining sector. Designations also cover Nornickel-related entities, potentially disrupting nickel-related trade and supply channels.

title: Gold and Copper Markets Respond to Powell | Live Wire
summary: Powell’s remarks suggesting a September rate cut lifted gold via a weaker dollar and falling Treasury yields, while copper was described as seeking a comeback after a slump. Copper had been pressured by moderating manufacturing demand, slower buying, and surplus stock exports, but prices have begun to recover.

title: Striking union workers at Lundin's Caserones copper mine in Chile accept contract deal
summary: Lundin Mining said union workers at its Caserones copper mine in Chile accepted a new 36-month contract after a strike lasting nearly two weeks. The deal includes wage increases and incentives, and Chilean court action ended road blockages. Caserones produced 139,520 tonnes of copper in 2023.

title: Lundin Mining Resolves Strike with Chilean Union at Caserones Copper Mine
summary: Lundin Mining said it settled a nearly two-week strike with Chilean union workers at the Caserones copper mine. The deal includes a 36-month contract with a 2.5% salary rise, bonuses, and incentive improvements after a court ordered road blockages to stop. Caserones produced 139,520 tonnes of copper in 2023.

title: Will China's Stimulus Measures Revive Copper Demand?
summary: The article discusses copper’s downtrend and a temporary boost from the Escondida mine strike ending. It argues China’s property-driven demand softness has weighed on consumption, but continued stimulus/rate-cut hopes could revive growth and copper demand, potentially supporting prices despite uncertainty and inventory dynamics.

title: Times of Zambia   |  FQM targets 21,000 tonnes of nickel
summary: First Quantum Minerals says its Enterprise Nickel mine in Kalumbila is expected to produce about 21,000 tonnes of nickel in 2024 and is poised to meet the set target. The mine was commissioned in 2022 and reached commercial production in June 2024, indicating stable near-term output.

title: Pan Asia launches copper oxide ore tests in Chile
summary: Pan Asia Metals has begun metallurgical bulk testing on copper oxide ore from its Rosario project in Chile to assess amenability to heap leaching and SX-EW to produce copper cathode. The company is also planning an IP geophysical survey and follow-on drilling to define copper targets.

title: India Aluminium Windows and Doors Market Forecast,
summary: The report highlights forecast growth for India’s aluminium windows and doors market, citing revitalized construction activity from government support for stalled housing projects and broader urbanisation trends. Increased residential and institutional investment points to higher near-term demand for aluminium building products, typically supportive for aluminium markets.

title: Fathom Nickel Inc.: Fathom Extends Geochemical Footprint of the Historic Gochager Lake Deposit Area by up to 25 Times
summary: Fathom Nickel reported final geochemical results from its Gochager Lake property, extending the Ni-Cu-Co+Cr-Mg soil and rock footprint and identifying additional anomalous trends. The release is focused on exploration work (pXRF, drilling context, and a MAG survey) without any production or supply-impact information.

title: CP NewsAlert: Canada to hit China with tariffs on electric vehicles, aluminum, steel
summary: Canada plans to raise tariffs on Chinese-made aluminum to 25% starting Oct. 15, aligning with North American partners’ trade actions against Chinese oversupply. Industry groups welcomed the move. By curbing imports, the policy can tighten near-term aluminum availability and support higher prices in the coming days.

title: Canada to hit China with tariffs on electric vehicles, aluminum, steel
summary: Canada plans higher tariffs on Chinese-made aluminum and steel, with aluminum tariffs rising to 25% (from lower levels) effective Oct. 15 after a product list is finalized Oct. 1. This likely curbs Chinese aluminum import flows into Canada, tightening supply expectations and supporting aluminium prices near term.

title: Canada Matches US Tariffs on Chinese-Made EVs, Adds 25% Charge on Chinese Steel and Aluminum
summary: Canada announced a 25% tariff on Chinese-made steel and aluminium, alongside a 100% tariff on Chinese EVs. The tariff move mirrors similar U.S. and EU actions aimed at reducing Chinese imports. By restricting aluminium inflows, the policy is likely to support near-term aluminium prices.

title: Canada to impose tariffs on Chinese-made EVs, aluminum and steel
summary: Canada will impose a 25% tariff on Chinese-made aluminum imports starting Oct. 15, alongside a 100% tariff on Chinese EVs. By restricting aluminum supply and increasing landed costs, the policy can tighten regional availability and support aluminum prices over the coming weeks despite potential downstream demand effects.

title: Feds impose tariffs on Chinese EVs, aluminum, steel - MRO Magazine
summary: Canada announced 25% tariffs on Chinese aluminum (and steel) alongside a 100% tariff on Chinese EVs. The move targets “unfair” Chinese non-market practices and aims to protect domestic manufacturing. By increasing the cost of Chinese aluminum inflows, the tariff is expected to support aluminum prices in the near term.

title: Canada to hit China with tariffs on electric vehicles, aluminum, steel | iNFOnews
summary: Canada announced steep new tariffs on Chinese-made EVs and also increased tariffs on Chinese-made steel and aluminum products to 25% from mid-October. Canadian industry groups welcomed the aluminum protection, while China warned of retaliation, adding near-term uncertainty for aluminum trade flows and pricing.

title: Russia's Nornickel examining impact of latest US sanctions
summary: Nornickel said it is assessing new U.S. sanctions affecting some subsidiaries and the Bystrinsky copper and gold project it controls indirectly. While core production/sales units are not directly listed, sanctions have previously led Western buyers to avoid Russian metal and complicated payments, potentially impacting nickel and copper supply flows.

title: Alucam More Than Doubles Aluminum Exports to France in Three Years
summary: Cameroon’s Alucam more than doubled aluminum exports to France over 2021-2023, with shipments to France rising to 15,879 tons in 2023. A new memorandum and commercial contract with Proalu SA is set to bring 30,000 tons of annual raw-aluminum orders for processing, supporting Alucam’s revenue and demand outlook.

title: Sault MP Terry Sheehan supports surtax on Chinese steel, aluminum and EV's
summary: Canada will impose a 25% surtax on Chinese-made steel and aluminum, effective Oct. 15, with the aim of countering unfair dumping and oversupply. The Sault MP Terry Sheehan supports the move to protect domestic producers and jobs. The policy directly targets aluminum import competition.

title: Canada to hit China with tariffs on electric vehicles, aluminum, steel - Canadian Manufacturing
summary: Canada announced tariffs targeting China: 25% duties on Chinese-made aluminum (and steel) alongside a 100% tariff on electric vehicles. The move is intended to protect domestic manufacturing as Chinese imports have surged, including via Tesla’s China-based Canadian EV production. Broader U.S. tariffs on China are cited as context.

title: USW statement shows support for federal tariffs on Chinese steel, aluminum - Canadian Manufacturing
summary: The USW supports Canadian federal tariffs on Chinese steel, aluminum and EVs, urging Canada to expand tariff authority to steel and aluminum under Customs Tariff section 53. It frames the move as countering dumping and excess capacity and protecting domestic industry, which can increase aluminum-related price support in the short term.

title: Junior Copper Miner from Down Under CopperCorp Resources Inc. (TSXV: CPER) (OTCQB: CPCPF), Gains on Project Updates
summary: CopperCorp Resources updates its Razorback project in western Tasmania, reporting new 3D inversion modeling, historical channel sampling with high copper grades, and scheduling drilling access at the Jukes zone. While bullish for the company and potential future production, it does not signal immediate global copper supply or demand changes.

title: Tariffs on aluminum, steel and electric vehicle imports
summary: United Steelworkers says Canada will impose tariffs on steel and aluminum imports from China (and electric vehicles). The union argues this will protect domestic steel and aluminum sectors and respond to Chinese dumping and excess capacity. Polling shows strong public support for similar tariff action.

title: Canada imposes 100% tariff on imports of Chinese EVs, 25% on aluminum, steel
summary: Canada announced a 25% tariff on imports of Chinese steel and aluminum, alongside a 100% tariff on Chinese EVs. The aluminum surtax starts Oct. 15 and follows US pressure and earlier US duties. By restricting Chinese aluminum inflows, the move may reduce supply and support aluminum prices.

title: Canada to hit China with tariffs on EVs, aluminum, steel
summary: Canada plans to impose tariffs on EVs along with aluminum and steel in retaliation against China. The direct mention of aluminum tariffs links the policy to aluminum trade costs and availability, which can affect near-term market expectations and add downside pressure to aluminium prices over coming weeks.

title: Las Vegas Arts District businesses hit by back-to-back copper wire theft
summary: Las Vegas Arts District businesses report back-to-back theft of copper from rooftop A/C units and compressors, with owners estimating nearly $100,000 combined losses. Metro Police increased overnight patrols and security assessments. The report is localized theft and offers no clear signal of broader copper supply or pricing impacts.

title: BHP Shifts Focus To Strengthening Copper Portfolio After Seeing 2% Profit Increase
summary: BHP reported a 2% rise in annual underlying profit and said it will strengthen its copper business. It is ramping projects in South Australia to raise copper output above 500,000 tonnes and expanding global copper assets in Chile and Argentina. Management cites strong copper positioning and growth expectations despite iron-ore challenges.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Accelerates Exploration at Atlantic
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reports completion of Phase 1 infrastructure upgrades and ongoing sampling over a 30 km awaruite (nickel-iron alloy) trend in Newfoundland, ahead of a planned 2024 drilling program. The release highlights awaruite’s easier concentration versus sulfide nickel and potential to ease North American nickel concentrate shortages.

title: Copper prices: Saxo bank says the worst of the correction is over
summary: Copper rose to an almost six-week high as investor demand returned and hopes grew for imminent U.S. interest rate cuts. Saxo Bank said the worst of the correction may be over, with further upside tied to improving demand fundamentals and falling warehouse stock levels as funding costs ease.

title: BHP Sees Copper Surplus in Short Term Before 'Fly-Up' Prices
summary: The article headline says BHP expects a short-term copper surplus, suggesting supply outweighs demand in the near term. That condition is generally bearish for copper prices over the coming days, even if the statement also references a later “fly-up” in prices beyond the immediate surplus period.

title: Benton Resources Inc.: Benton Expands The Great Burnt Copper Deposit Down Plunge Through Recent Drilling Results from Phase 3 Exploration
summary: Benton Resources reported Phase 3 drilling results from its Great Burnt copper project in Newfoundland, including 12.3 meters of 1.72% Cu and higher-grade intercepts up to 6.12% Cu. The company has started Phase 4 drilling targeting deeper extensions, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Lifezone Metals Initiates Process for Risk Insurance with U.S. International Development Finance Corporation for the Kabanga Nickel Project in Tanzania
summary: Lifezone Metals said it is starting an evaluation with the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation for political risk insurance for future investments in the Kabanga nickel-copper-cobalt mine and Kahama hydromet refinery in Tanzania. The project is expected to produce LME-grade nickel and copper, with a feasibility study progressing.

title: Northern Copper Zone and Garth Daniel Zone, update | Company Announcement
summary: Anglesey Mining reported updates from drilling at its Parys Mountain Cu-Zn-Pb-Ag-Au deposit, including traced mineralization continuity in the Northern Copper Zone and Garth Daniel Zone and new litho-geochemical results defining ore horizons. It supports geological modeling, but offers no near-term production change or supply disruption.

title: Torr Metals Reports Robust Copper-Gold Grades, Expands with
summary: Torr Metals reported final assay results from 2024 rock grab reconnaissance at its Kolos copper-gold project, including discovery of the Sonic Zone with anomalous copper and gold and higher copper values in multiple zones. The findings expand target areas but do not affect near-term mine supply, inventories, or logistics.

title: Congo opposes Chemaf's copper-cobalt assets sale to Norinco
summary: DRC authorities have halted or recommended stopping Chemaf Resources’s planned sale of its copper-cobalt mines to China’s Norinco, citing violations of Gecamines’ lease and farm-out contract terms. The dispute may disrupt near-term copper supply expectations from the DRC, though the final outcome is uncertain.

title: BHP sees copper surplus in short term before 'fly-up' prices – BNN Bloomberg
summary: BNN Bloomberg’s headline says BHP sees a copper surplus in the short term before a potential “fly-up” in prices. That framing suggests near-term supply will exceed demand, which would likely pressure copper prices over the next days to a few weeks until any later tightening emerges.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Accelerates Exploration At Atlantic Nickel Project with Expanded Crew, LiDAR Survey, and Infrastructure Upgrades
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reported Phase 1 infrastructure upgrades at its Atlantic Nickel Project in Newfoundland, including road/bridge improvements and expanded nickel sampling along a 30 km trend. The firm is also using LiDAR for better geological targeting and sending initial samples for analysis, aimed at developing awaruite nickel-iron resources.

title: Tech Innovation Set to Help Fuel Sustainable Copper Mining Amid Soaring Global Demand
summary: KoBold Metals says AI-driven exploration in Zambia likely found a major new copper deposit, estimating at least 300,000 tons of annual output. The article also highlights production ramp-ups in the DRC by CMOC and increased Chile output from BHP, alongside efficiency investments, supporting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: South Pacific Metals Corp.: South Pacific Metals Reports Exceptional Surface Trenching Results at Osena Gold-Copper Project, Including 8.82g/t Gold Sample at Ontenu Prospect, Kainantu District
summary: South Pacific Metals reports exceptional surface trench assay results at its Osena gold-copper Osena project in Papua New Guinea, including 79 m averaging ~981 ppm Cu and localized higher copper grades. The findings support potential expansion of a porphyry system, but are early-stage exploration with limited near-term impact on copper prices and none on nickel or aluminium.

title: European refined copper demand weak; German demand particularly challenged
summary: Fastmarkets reports very slow refined copper demand in Germany and across Europe, with manufacturing, automotive and construction sectors hit and industrial hours reduced. Copper cathode premiums in Germany and cif Rotterdam stay at multi-month lows, while sellers have ample material, indicating bearish near-term pressure despite some energy-transition demand.

title: China's nickel sulfate market rangebound; global nickel sulfate assessed at wide range
summary: Fastmarkets reports China nickel sulfate prices are rangebound but generally supported. Tight nickel MHP supply (and firm MHP payable terms) and low salt production inventories help hold prices firm, while slower NCM cathode precursor demand limits gains. Higher LME nickel cash prices lifted the all-in nickel sulfate range.

title: Breaking Mining Stock News: New Destiny Mining (TSXV: NED) Drilling Hole 7 Intersects Porphyry Dikes and Copper Mineralization at Treasure Mountain Silver Project, Hope BC
summary: New Destiny Mining reports drilling at its Treasure Mountain project in BC, with Hole 7 intersecting altered porphyry dikes and copper-bearing minerals. Portable XRF readings show copper (0.34%) and antimony within mineralized intervals. The release supports exploration potential but provides no supply or mine output change.

title: Norilsk Nickel may move copper production plant to China. Does Russia need it?
summary: Nornickel said it plans to transfer part of its copper-plant capacities from Norilsk to China via a joint venture, aiming to resolve market-access and sanctions-related issues. Experts warn this could disrupt Russia’s industrial base and concentrate flows. The relocation can affect near-term expectations for copper supply and related nickel-linked outputs.

title: Beijing decries Ottawa's tariffs on EVs, steel, aluminium
summary: Chinese government departments criticized Canada’s announcement of additional tariffs and other restrictive measures against Chinese exports, including electric vehicles, steel and aluminium. They called it protectionism and urged Canada to reverse the measures. The tariff threat is likely to disrupt aluminium trade expectations and pressure aluminium prices near term.

title: Aluminum Prices Defy Expectations
summary: The piece argues that despite ample primary aluminium supply signals (declining inventories, rising Chinese production), physical delivery premiums keep climbing. It attributes the move to sanctions-related deliverability issues (Russian supply) and cost/congestion constraints: higher freight rates, tight container capacity, Suez traffic disruptions, and port strikes in Germany delaying shipments into Europe and Japan.

title: Los Angeles cracks down on copper wire thefts, warns of more arrests
summary: Los Angeles announced a crackdown on copper wire thefts, warning residents and offenders of more arrests. By reducing stolen copper from local distribution and scrap flows, the policy is likely to slightly improve short-term copper availability and sentiment, potentially offering modest upward support for copper prices in the near term.

title: LAPD issues citations, arrests Valley suspects in copper wire thefts
summary: Los Angeles police conducted a crackdown on copper wire thefts, recovering 16,000 pounds of copper and arresting/fining recyclers. Officials also mention reclaimed aluminum cable and batteries. The enforcement targets illegal recyclers and upstream sourcing to prevent street lighting and service disruptions. More arrests are expected.

title: Parys Mountain: Copper works reopening hits milestone
summary: Anglesey Mining says it has submitted an initial Environmental Impact Assessment Scoping Report to restart underground mining at Parys Mountain, historically a major copper producer. The plan would process concentrate (~30% copper) for export, but requires significant investment and further approvals, making near-term copper impact uncertain.

title: Bezant Resources plc Provides Hope & Gorob Copper-Gold Project Permitting Update
summary: Bezant Resources said it received an Environmental Clearance Certificate for Namibia’s Hope & Gorob Copper-Gold Project (Licence EPL7170), extending validity to August 2027 and enabling continued exploration. The project sits on prospective geology associated with prior resources, with further exploration results expected as work progresses.

title: Sellafield failed to manage risks of nickel nitrate, ONR finds
summary: The UK nuclear regulator (ONR) issued improvement notices to Sellafield after breaches of hazardous chemical controls involving nickel nitrate in an effluent facility. Contamination outside a glovebox could have exposed workers. The issues must be corrected by late 2024 and March 2025, without compromising nuclear safety.

title: Anglesey Mining hit 'significant milestone' in reopening copper mine
summary: Anglesey Mining submitted an environmental scoping report to restart the Mynydd Parys copper mine at Parys Mountain in north Wales. The company cites densely populated deposits and expects future underground mining and an on-site processing plant, but final approvals and major $100m investment are still required.

title: Zambia: Copper Producers Turn to Renewables Amidst Power Crisis
summary: Zambia’s copper industry is hit by a drought-induced electricity shortage, with ZESCO increasing rationing to 17 hours of planned cuts per day from September 1. Jubilee Metals signs a renewable power purchase agreement to mitigate disruption, but firms still face higher energy costs and production risk.

title: Closure of Glencore's Mount Isa copper mine leaves city on economic cliff
summary: Glencore plans to end copper mining at Mount Isa in 2025, with the smelter’s operation dependent on government support until 2030. As other nearby projects likely won’t reach production until after 2026, the closure raises near-term concerns about copper supply and smelting throughput. Local workforce and investment risks are emphasized.

title: Aluminium giant Rusal's first-half profit rises nearly 42%
summary: Rusal reported a 41.6% jump in first-half profit as it increased production of primary aluminium and alumina and boosted shipments to China to record levels. It also notes the LME broad ban on Russian aluminium, copper and nickel amid U.S./UK sanctions. Improved volumes and rerouting are mildly supportive for prices.

title: Aluminium giant Rusal's first-half profit jumps 42% on strong prices, deliveries
summary: Rusal’s first-half adjusted net profit rose 41.6% as it increased production and shipped record volumes to China. The firm faced demand pressure as Western buyers avoid Russia-made metal after Ukraine. The article notes April LME bans on Russian aluminium, copper and nickel and links improved output to higher prices for aluminium and alumina.

title: Corella Resources (ASX:CR9) discusses novel flowsheeting for high-purity alumina
summary: Corella Resources discusses government funding for R&D aimed at improving high-purity alumina (HPA) flowsheeting from kaolin, including reducing high-temperature calcination to lower energy intensity. The work is expected to take about six months, but the update is primarily technical and early-stage, with no near-term supply change stated.

title: WA EPA sets Alcoa a deadline for bauxite mining approvals in the south-west
summary: WA EPA has set a deadline for Alcoa to submit information required for bauxite mining approvals in the jarrah forest, warning it could take a cautious approach or impose stricter conditions if information is not provided. Water and environmental agencies opposed the plans, citing risks to drinking water and ecosystems.

title: Carnaby, Latitude 66 record more Queensland copper-gold hits
summary: Carnaby Resources and Latitude 66 reported further reverse-circulation drilling results at the Greater Duchess JV near Mt Isa, including multiple high-grade copper intersections and accompanying gold. The findings support prefeasibility work and additional surveys, but they are exploration updates rather than near-term production impacts.

title: Sierra Gorda Copper Mine Declaration and Update | Company Announcement
summary: South32 reported a first-time ore reserve life of 16 years for the Sierra Gorda copper mine and confirmed a sulphide stockpile mineral resource update. It also outlines plant debottlenecking and a fourth grinding line expansion targeting higher throughput and lower operating costs, supporting future copper production growth.

title: CopperString project blowout sparks council concern
summary: Queensland is considering an extra $1.2 billion for the CopperString high-voltage transmission line after costs rose to an estimated $6.2 billion. The project is expected to support mining development and help supply cheaper power, likely boosting near-term expectations for grid metals, especially copper, with possible spillover to aluminium.

title: London Copper Rises on Rate Cut Expectations, China Demand Worries Cap Gains
summary: London three-month copper rose 0.3% to $9,287/mt as markets priced in U.S. rate cut expectations for September, supporting sentiment. However, a firm U.S. dollar and concerns about China’s demand limited the upside, leading to capped gains after early losses.

title: An explosion at an aluminium smelter in Inner Mongolia had minimal impact on production
summary: An explosion at an aluminium smelter in Inner Mongolia disrupted three aluminium electrolytic cells. The company resolved the issue quickly, and the affected tanks resumed production that afternoon. The update characterizes the production disruption as minimal, suggesting limited near-term impact on aluminium supply expectations.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd.: Aston Bay Announces Initiation of Airborne MobileMT Geophysical Survey and Expanded Claims Holdings at the High-Grade Copper-Silver Epworth Project, Nunavut, Canada
summary: Aston Bay says an 8,105 line-km helicopter-borne MobileMT EM survey is underway and it staked additional claims at its Epworth copper-silver project in Nunavut, after sampling and mapping. Results are expected to guide targeting for anticipated drilling in 2025, not near-term production.

title: Aluminum Leads Base Metals Down on Dim Supply and Demand Balance
summary: The article reports that aluminium is leading base metals lower as market conditions point to a weaker supply-and-demand balance. This suggests reduced support from physical or demand fundamentals, contributing to downward price momentum in aluminium relative to other base metals over the near term.

title: Argentina betting on lithium and copper projects to overcome recession
summary: Argentina’s minister says the pro-business mining incentive regime (RIGI) should attract major foreign investment and help new lithium and copper projects start later this year. Copper is framed as crucial for EVs and AI, with large capex needs for projects, implying improved near-term supply/export expectations.

title: Omani innovation 'Greenlium': A breakthrough in sustainable aluminum  I  Times of Oman
summary: Times of Oman reports Omani project “Greenlium,” using lignin extracted from palm waste to convert commercial aluminum into a more sustainable “organic” aluminum. It claims lower environmental impact and potential applications in packaging and electronics. The article does not indicate commercial scale or near-term supply/cost changes for aluminum prices.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp.: Cordoba Minerals Receives Approval of Mining Technical Work Plan (PTO) Application for the Alacran Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals announced Colombia’s National Mining Agency approved the PTO for the Alacran copper-gold-silver project. The permit is required to license the mine for construction, moving the project closer to an anticipated Q2 2025 start, subject to financing, which may modestly support copper supply expectations.

title: Grid Battery Metals Inc.: Grid Battery Expands Land Holdings by Adding a Copper Project in Northern Central British Columbia
summary: Grid Battery Metals acquired 100% interest in 17 mineral claims (27,525 ha) in northern-central British Columbia, adding a new copper property. The release describes regional copper-gold geology and adjacent projects but includes no drilling results, production changes, or supply-chain disruptions, suggesting minimal short-term impact on copper prices.

title: Cordoba Minerals Corp. Receives Approval of Mining Technical Work Plan Application for the Alacran Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Colombia
summary: Cordoba Minerals said Colombia’s National Mining Agency approved the Mining Technical Work Plan (PTO) for its Alacran copper-gold-silver project. The PTO is a key permit toward mine construction, expected to start in Q2 2025 if financing is secured. The update is a milestone, not near-term output.

title: US Steel and Aluminum Industries and the United Auto Workers Urge USTR to Expand Section 301 Tariff Rates on Certain Steel and Aluminum Articles from China
summary: US steel and aluminium groups and the UAW urged the USTR to expand Section 301 tariff rates, including proposals to target third-country imports that incorporate Chinese-origin aluminium. The Aluminum Association argues current trade diversion undermines US producers, seeking added tariff coverage. USTR reviews comments for a final decision in August.

title: Quetzal Copper Limited: Quetzal Copper Update on Drilling and Geophysics at the Cristinas Project, Chihuahua Mexico
summary: Quetzal Copper provided an update on drilling and geophysical work at its Cristinas Project in Chihuahua, Mexico, completing a downhole InfiniTEM survey and planning to recommence drilling in September 2024. It highlights the presence of historic shallow copper oxide mineralization and aims to model results for next drill targets.

title: Madagascar: Operational Issues Push Sumitomo to Cut Nickel Output Forecast at Ambatovy Mine
summary: Sumitomo’s Ambatovy nickel mine in Madagascar missed output targets after malfunctions, prompting an 89 billion yen write-down and a restructuring plan with a British court. Annual output was 31,000 tonnes vs 40,000 targeted. The company expects costs and production to improve once operations stabilize.

title: Hudbay Receives Aquifer Protection Permit for Copper World
summary: Hudbay said Arizona’s ADEQ has issued the aquifer protection permit for its Copper World project. The permit completes one of three key state prerequisites, de-risking advancement toward feasibility work and potential sanctioning. Copper World is expected to produce about 85,000 tonnes of copper annually.

title: CopperString funding: Mayor Peddle urges unconditional support | North Queensland Register
summary: Queensland Treasurer Cameron Dick says an extra $1.2 billion for the CopperString 840-kilometre transmission project would be provided only if the government is re-elected. The project’s costs have reportedly risen more than 20%. The mayor argues conditional funding could destabilize confidence and affect financing and timelines.

title: Expeditors International of Washington : Canada Announces Tariffs on EVs, Steel, and Aluminum from China
summary: Canada’s Department of Finance announced 100% tariffs on Chinese-made EVs and a 25% tariff on certain steel and aluminum products from China, with measures starting in October. The aluminum tariff can tighten supply from China into Canada, offering near-term support to aluminium prices.

title: Arizona approves key permit for Copper World Mine
summary: Arizona approved a key aquifer protection permit for Hudbay’s Copper World open-pit copper mine, with additional monitoring wells and conditions to protect groundwater. The approval enables construction to proceed subject to one remaining air-quality permit. The news is project-progress positive but lacks near-term production timing, limiting immediate copper-price pressure.

title: Hudbay Minerals Inc. Receives Aquifer Protection Permit for Copper World
summary: Hudbay Minerals said Arizona ADEQ issued the Aquifer Protection Permit for its Copper World project, a key state requirement for sanctioned development. Copper World is expected to produce about 85,000 tonnes of copper annually, but production is targeted for later (around 2026). The permit advances feasibility and project planning.

title: The Overnight Report: Ex-Nvidia Shares Are Up
summary: The Overnight Report links overnight weakness in industrial metals to a stronger USD and specific aluminium factors. It says aluminium led metals lower as worries persist over China’s demand recovery, while ample supply grew. Rusal’s record first-half aluminium shipments lifted China inventories to their highest levels since 2019.

title: BHP moves ahead with expansion of South Australia's Olympic Dam copper refinery
summary: BHP said South Australia has begun the application and assessment process for expanding the Olympic Dam copper smelter and refinery. The move supports plans to grow copper cathode output in coming years, with a final investment decision in 2027. The news could influence future supply expectations but timing limits immediate price pressure.

title: Alvance Aluminium agree inflation-bursting two-year payrise
summary: Unite union workers at Alvance Aluminium’s Lochaber smelter near Fort William agreed a two-year pay rise above inflation, including 5%/4% increases in 2024 and additional scheduled raises in 2025. The deal covers smelter and administrative staff and follows no reported production disruption; a recycling and billet project is planned.

title: Camino Minerals Corp: Camino and Nittetsu Extend by One Week Exclusive Rights to Negotiate Copper Mine Acquisition in Chile
summary: Camino Minerals and Nittetsu extend by one week their exclusive rights to negotiate the acquisition of the Puquios Project, a construction-ready copper mine in Chile. The deal remains subject to approvals and cannot be assured. The update may modestly boost copper sentiment by improving prospects for future supply.

title: Camino and Nittetsu Extend by One Week Exclusive Rights to Negotiate Copper Mine Acquisition in Chile
summary: Camino Minerals and Nittetsu extended their one-week exclusive rights to finalize negotiations for the acquisition of Chile’s Puquios Project, a construction-ready copper mine. The news is a progress/contracting update with no stated change to near-term production, but it may modestly influence copper supply expectations.

title: First Quantum seeks damages in Panama as its copper facility sits idle
summary: First Quantum is seeking damages from Panama after its Cobre Panama copper mine was shut following a Supreme Court ruling of unconstitutionality. A stockpile of about 120,000 tonnes of copper ore remains on site pending arbitration, with claims tied to letting the material leave or compensating at market value.

title: BHP's Olympic Dam Expansion Moves Forward, Aiming To Boost South Australia's Copper Output
summary: BHP says it is advancing plans to expand the Olympic Dam copper smelter and refinery in South Australia, with state approval pending. The project targets higher refined copper cathode output, potentially rising from 322,000 tons to 500,000 tons by the early 2030s, amid broader copper demand expectations.

title: Copper Claws Higher on China Hopes, Set for Monthly Gain
summary: Copper prices rose on optimism that China, the top metals consumer, may receive further government support for its economy. Investors also increasingly believe prices bottomed earlier in the month. The move put copper on course for its first monthly gain since May, when it hit a record above $11,100/t.

title: US Trade Chief Hails New Canadian Tariffs on Chinese EVs, Steel, Aluminum
summary: U.S. Trade Representative Katherine Tai said Canada’s new high tariffs on some Chinese imports are an important step for fair competition in electric vehicles and the steel and aluminum industries. By targeting Chinese aluminum imports, the measure is likely to tighten supply and support near-term aluminum prices.

title: Weir awarded £53m redefined flowsheet contract for Reko Diq greenfield copper-gold project in Pakistan's Balochistan Province
summary: Weir was awarded a £53m redefined flowsheet contract for the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Pakistan’s Balochistan, including ENDURON HPGRs, wet screens, slurry pumps and hydrocyclones. £26m is booked in Q3 with remaining orders in late 2024/early 2025, with production targeted for 2028.

title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Union's Appeal Against CETSTAT Order Allowing Vedanta's Plea To Levy Anti-Dumping Duty On Aluminium Imports
summary: India’s Supreme Court is reviewing the Union’s challenge to a CESTAT order involving countervailing/anti-dumping treatment for aluminium primary foundry alloy ingot imports from Malaysia. The dispute centers on whether the government can avoid imposing duties despite the authority’s recommendations, affecting import costs and near-term aluminium pricing.

title: Aluminum Prices Rise 15.7% in H1 2024, Boosting Cameroon's Alucam
summary: BEAC’s Q2 2024 commodity report says global aluminium prices jumped 15.7% between Q1 and Q2 2024. The article links the surge to improved export revenues for Cameroon’s Alucam, the region’s sole aluminium producer, which sells most output abroad and supplies sheets and cable-related inputs locally.

title: Bell Copper Corporation: Bell Temporarily Suspends Big Sandy Drilling, Presents Big Sandy Science in Anaheim
summary: Bell Copper temporarily suspended diamond drilling at its Big Sandy porphyry copper project due to stuck tooling and insufficient funding, planning to resume after additional capital is secured. It highlights encouraging copper-bearing mineralized gravel/clasts and ongoing studies, but the work is still early-stage with no resource yet defined.

title: Would more import taxes revive Pennsauken's Aluminum Shapes complex?
summary: U.S. aluminum extruders seek expanded import tariffs, citing dumping and government-subsidized competition from China and other countries. After prior penalties and a federal case over mislabeled Chinese shipments, new ITC/Commerce findings indicate material injury and potential “less-than-fair” trade, with a decision pending Oct. 1.

title: Port Kembla Copper smelter site for sale as it remediates contamination
summary: Port Kembla Copper is selling its former smelter site after finding hundreds of nearby homes still contaminated with toxic dust, including lead and cadmium. The company will use sale proceeds to fund ongoing investigation and remediation. The work relates to the disused copper smelter but does not change near-term production materially.

title: Tindo partners with Capral Aluminium in Australian PV supply chain
summary: Tindo partnered with Capral Aluminium to supply extruded aluminium frames for Australian-made solar panels, with a pathway to sourcing from Capral’s domestic facilities as Tindo scales output toward 1GW. The collaboration is aimed at strengthening Australia’s PV supply chain and could increase near-term aluminium demand.

title: Japanese giants ink commitment to Ardea nickel project
summary: Ardea Resources executed a binding shareholders’ agreement with a Japanese consortium (Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi) to fund a $98.5m definitive feasibility study and advance FEED for the Goongarrie Hub nickel-cobalt project in Western Australia. The step supports potential FID but does not change near-term nickel output.

title: Lotte in copper foil deal with Stellantis battery JV
summary: Lotte Energy Materials signed an agreement to supply copper foil for StarPlus Energy’s first EV battery plant in Indiana. The Stellantis–Samsung SDI JV is building two plants with total investment of $6.4bn, aiming for 33 GWh capacity per year from the first plant in 1Q2025. Copper foil demand outlook improves.

title: White House Issues Two Proclamations On Section 232 Requirements For Aluminum And Steel - Export Controls & Trade & Investment Sanctions - International Law
summary: The White House issued updated Section 232 proclamations covering aluminum imports. New “smelt and most recent cast” origin rules for Mexico-linked aluminum and higher duties apply when smelt/cast is reported in China or other listed countries, raising compliance costs and reducing duty-free inflows into the US.

title: US Steel And Aluminum Industries And The United Auto Workers Urge USTR To Expand Section 301 Tariff Rates On Certain Steel And Aluminum Articles From China  - Export Controls & Trade & Investment Sanctions - International Law
summary: US steel and aluminum groups and the Aluminum Association urged USTR to expand proposed Section 301 tariff rates to cover Chinese-origin aluminium embedded in third-country products re-exported to the US. AISI also sought broader steel rules of origin. USTR will finalize changes in August, taking effect shortly after publication.

title: Golden Deeps flies on massive NSW copper-zinc sulphide hit
summary: Golden Deeps shares surged after intersecting an 80m zone of semi-massive copper–zinc sulphides at its Havilah NSW project, with field results showing up to 18.5% copper and 34.8% zinc. Management believes it may indicate a large porphyry-sulphide system, pending lab assays.

title: Alpha HPA begins stage two construction at Gladstone alumina facility
summary: Alpha HPA began stage two construction at its Gladstone, Queensland high-purity alumina facility, building on stage one and planning over 10,000 tonnes annually of high-purity aluminium products. The expansion is funded with government debt and additional equity and targets electronics for the energy transition, supporting aluminium supply expectations.

title: New alumina inferred index reflects Indonesia's growing global significance
summary: Fastmarkets launched new FOB “alumina index inferred” assessments for Indonesia (and also Vietnam/India), reflecting rising Indonesian influence. The piece links Indonesia’s growing alumina output to capacity constraints in Australia, where refinery outages and force majeure have disrupted alumina supply.

title: Goldman Cuts Copper Forecast by $5,000 as Bullish Bet Closed
summary: The article headline says Goldman cut its copper price forecast by $5,000 after closing a bullish position. That signals weaker near-term expectations for copper demand and/or pricing, which can weigh on copper futures and related market sentiment over the next days to weeks.

title: ICBC hits back at ING's copper loss suit | Global Trade Review (GTR)
summary: ICBC denies liability in a dispute with ING over alleged trade-finance losses tied to documents against payment copper shipments routed through Maike Metals. The Hong Kong court rejected ICBC’s bid to move the case to mainland China, citing deviation from URC collection instructions. Maike later collapsed amid a liquidity crisis.

title: Orestone Mining Corp.: Orestone Options Copper Gold Porphyry Systems in Argentina
summary: Orestone Mining optioned the Las Burras-Incahuasi copper-gold-molybdenum porphyry property in Argentina, citing prior drill intersections up to 0.42% copper over 112 metres and planning an AirMT survey and further drilling. The update is about exploration advancement, with no near-term production affecting copper prices.

title: Global Copper Cathode Stocks: Increasing or Decreasing Post-Price Swings?
summary: The piece reviews copper cathode inventories: SHFE stocks rose post–Chinese New Year, while LME/COMEX were historically low before turning higher on continued exports. Despite exchange visible-stock buildup, SMM shows China social and smelter inventories declining. It concludes global inventory growth may slow as China continues destocking into peak season.

title: New Caledonian nickel firm KNS awaits new investor after furnace shutdown
summary: KNS, a New Caledonian nickel producer involving Glencore, shut its furnaces over the weekend, moving into care and maintenance and laying off most of its 1,200 staff. The wider local nickel sector has been hit by unrest, with Eramet’s SLN operating minimally and Prony Resources suspending operations.

title: ERG Announces Pre-Export Finance Facility Agreement Based on Metalkol Copper Supply
summary: ERG announced a $150m pre-export finance facility backed by a copper cathode supply agreement from its Metalkol operation. Glencore and Bank of China are counterparties, supporting working capital and ongoing exports from the DRC, where copper production is emphasized for global customers.

title: Breaking Mining Stock News: New Destiny Mining (TSXV: NED) Discovers New Spokane Vein - Outcrops Sampled 35 Meters Apart 6.6% Copper and 100 G/T Silver Using XRF Spot Analysis
summary: New Destiny Mining reported prospecting at its Treasure Mountain project in BC, identifying a Spokane quartz vein with up to 6.6% copper (plus 100 g/t silver) from handheld XRF spot measurements. Samples are being sent for lab assays and ICP, with further prospecting and permitting planned.

title: Materials Slide as Goldman Warns on Copper Price - Materials Roundup
summary: Producers of metals slid after Goldman Sachs warned that China’s economy remains listless, with ongoing copper demand likely to weaken more than supply concerns. Copper futures fell about 2.6% to $8,978/ton, roughly 20% below the May peak, reflecting the renewed demand outlook.

title: Air Enforcement: Alabama Department of Environmental Management and Baldwin County Secondary Aluminum Recycling Facility Enter into Consent Order | Mitchell, Williams, Selig, Gates & Woodyard, P.L.L.C.
summary: ADEM and Ecovery entered a consent order over alleged air-permit violations at an Alabama secondary aluminum recycling facility. The plant processes aluminum-copper radiators and had visible particulate emissions linked to south dust collector maintenance. The firm replaced filters and seals; later stack tests showed compliance. A $15,000 civil penalty was assessed.

title: New Electronics - Electroninks unveils copper MOD ink for advanced semiconductor packaging
summary: Electroninks launched copper MOD ink for advanced semiconductor packaging, targeting fine-line metallization/RDL seed layer printing. The company says ink-based printing can displace some electroless copper plating and PVD tie layers while improving throughput and reducing water/energy use. The report highlights copper as a standard in electronics but gives no production volumes.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Filing of Technical Report for Previously Announced Deloro Project Initial Resource
summary: Canada Nickel filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Deloro nickel sulphide project, confirming an initial mineral resource estimate effective July 17, 2024 with no material differences from earlier results. The update is a regulatory disclosure tied to future exploration progress, but no near-term production changes are stated.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Confirms High-Grade Nickel at Langmuir #2 Intersecting Nickel Grades from 1.07% to 5.11%
summary: EV Nickel Inc. reported drill-hole results from its Langmuir #2 nickel zone, including intersections from 1.07% to 5.11% Ni and higher-than-expected nickel sulphide tenor (~12% to >40% Ni). The company plans further drilling to expand the mineralized envelope and advance its nickel strategy toward battery supply.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Announces Kamoa-Kakula Achieved Record Copper Production of 40,347 Tonnes in August
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said its Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC produced a monthly record 40,347 tonnes of copper in concentrate in August and a daily record 2,096 tonnes on Aug. 31. Hot commissioning of Phase 3 fine-grinding mills is expected to finish in coming days, lifting recoveries toward 86% and supporting 2024 guidance.

title: Copper miners down but not cheap, says Scotia analyst
summary: Scotia’s Orest Wowkodaw says copper miners still look expensive, estimating miners imply an average copper price of about $5.06/lb versus spot near $4.00/lb (a ~27% premium). The premium is attributed to strong investor appetite and M&A speculation, alongside lower by-product prices. Macro NFP risk is noted but not copper-specific.

title: Mink Ventures Corporation Reports Positive Base Metal Assays From Sampling Program at Warren Copper Nickel Cobalt Project, Timmins, Ontario
summary: Mink Ventures reported positive results from a summer sampling program at its Warren nickel-copper-cobalt project in Ontario. Reference samples confirmed mineralized zones with meaningful nickel grades and significant copper assays, supporting drill targeting for a planned diamond drilling phase after freeze-up.

title: Mink Ventures Reports Positive Base Metal Assays From Sampling Program at Warren Copper Nickel Cobalt Project, Timmins, Ontario
summary: Mink Ventures reported positive grab-sample assays from the summer sampling program at its Warren nickel-copper-cobalt project in Ontario, highlighting multiple zones with copper and nickel grades. The company plans winter access and diamond drilling after freeze-up to test refined IP/EM targets. Near-term impact on metal prices appears limited.

title: ERG turns to trading market for US$150mn copper pre-export finance facility
summary: Eurasian Resources Group secured a US$150mn pre-export finance facility with Glencore and Bank of China, backed by copper cathode supply from its Metalkol plant in Kolwezi, DRC. The deal supports working capital and ongoing copper deliveries, reinforcing near-term supply expectations as DRC copper output underpins global demand.

title: Osisko Provides Select Asset Updates | Financial Post
summary: Osisko’s asset update includes a major copper focus via its interests in the CSA Mine, where Metals Acquisition reported record quarterly copper production of 10,864 tonnes and record monthly output in June, alongside stronger grades and new drilling intercepts. This supports expectations of steady copper supply.

title: Aluminium premiums in Europe remain well-supported; Japanese spot reference edges lower
summary: European aluminium premiums in Rotterdam and Italy remain well-supported, with the duty-unpaid premium edging higher amid tight regional supply, concerns over unpaid stock safety, low inventories, and high costs to source replacements. Japanese spot premiums narrowed on bearish sentiment and contango dynamics, while US activity stayed sluggish.

title: Key global nickel talking points ahead of the International Critical Minerals & Metals Summit
summary: Fastmarkets highlights Indonesia as the core of global nickel supply and processing, with expanding intermediate and refined capacity and rising ore imports. It links this supply build-out to much lower nickel prices, citing the LME three-month contract down 47% since January 2023 and Western producer closures in a low-price environment.

title: Iran to speed up giant copper project in impoverished Sistan
summary: Iran’s newly appointed industries minister said the government will accelerate the Janja copper-and-gold project in Sistan to boost regional jobs and investment. Authorities plan extra funding for faster development by contractors. The mine is sizable, but first-year copper cathode/concentrate output is scheduled for 2028.

title: Las Vegas City Council approves new ordinance to stop copper wire theft
summary: Las Vegas City Council approved an ordinance to curb copper wire theft, making it illegal to buy scrap metal without transport by motor vehicle and limiting purchases of burned scrap insulation unless sellers provide proof of legal origin. Local businesses like Good Pie and Cork and Thorn were victims, but no market-wide copper impact is quantified.

title: Domestic Aluminum Operating Capacity Hits New High, August Aluminum Production Up 1.8% YoY [SMM Data]
summary: SMM data show China’s August 2024 aluminum output rose 1.8% YoY to 3.69 Mt, supported by new capacity in Inner Mongolia and little disruption from Sichuan power rationing. Operating rate reached 95.88%. September output is forecast stable near 3.57 Mt amid improving downstream billet activity.

title: New Las Vegas ordinance cracks down on copper theft
summary: Las Vegas passed an ordinance to curb copper theft, raising misdemeanor fines and restricting cash transactions for recycling. City leaders say stolen copper from infrastructure delays repairs and costs millions. Businesses report tens of thousands in losses when thieves strip wiring, while recycling yards help implement the regional crackdown.

title: R20m worth of stolen copper cables recovered in KZN scrapyard
summary: Police in KwaZulu-Natal recovered about R20 million of stolen copper cables from a scrapyard in Queensburgh after an investigation and operation involving the Hawks. The eThekwini municipality said much of the copper belonged to it. A scrapyard manager was arrested, following prior cable theft recoveries in Durban.

title: Key highlights from the global aluminium industry, August 2024 | Shanghai Non ferrous Metals
summary: An August 2024 wrap-up for aluminium highlights a moderate price increase on LME and SHFE, attributed to supply chain constraints and selective demand strength, despite volatility from geopolitics and weaker European foil deliveries. It also covers power/production factors (China output, renewable power caps) and supply chain initiatives affecting aluminium costs.

title: Kyrgyzstan increases export of aluminium to China 4 times
summary: Kyrgyzstan has increased aluminium exports to China fourfold. The report indicates a large jump in outbound shipments, which can raise near-term supply availability in China. In the absence of offsetting demand or cost factors, such export growth is generally associated with downward pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Glencore still in talks to sell stake in the New Caledonian nickel firm
summary: Koniambo Nickel SAS said negotiations for Glencore’s 49% stake are continuing, but its furnaces were shut over the weekend and operations were already halted. Employees were laid off, and other New Caledonia nickel players are running at minimal capacity or suspending. These disruptions point to near-term nickel supply weakness.

title: BHP ASX: Copper 'mega bulls' throw in the towel
summary: Investors are reducing copper forecasts and unwinding bullish positions as concerns grow over short-term oversupply and weakening Chinese demand. Goldman Sachs exited a long position and cut its 2025 copper target by about one-third to an average of $10,100/tonne, signaling softer price expectations.
