The scheme targets large users like Tomago Aluminium, where power costs are about 40% of costs, supporting aluminium production prospects.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | The Macleay Argus
summary: Prime Minister Albanese announced green production credits aimed at supporting Australian aluminium smelters, including Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone, to encourage shifting to renewable and cleaner energy and reduce costs. Critics argue offshore production could rise, while Rio Tinto praised the investment certainty for aluminium.

title: $2 billion aluminium investment to aid AUS manufacturing - Manufacturers' Monthly
summary: Australia’s federal government is investing $2 billion in the aluminium industry via a “Green Aluminium Production Credit,” supporting smelters to switch to renewable electricity and receive support per tonne of clean, locally made aluminium over 10 years. The policy aims to expand Australia’s aluminium output and secure jobs.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | The Maitland Mercury
summary: Prime Minister Albanese says green production credits will secure Australia’s aluminium industry, targeting support to smelters including Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone to help them shift to renewable energy and lower costs. Coalition critics argue renewables policies will hurt reliability and push production offshore, while Rio Tinto welcomed the funding.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | Newcastle Herald
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced green production credits to support Australian aluminium smelters at Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone, aiming to lower energy costs and enable a shift to reliable renewable power. Rio Tinto welcomed the plan, while critics argued it would undermine industry, highlighting near-term costs and competitiveness.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | The Advertiser - Cessnock
summary: Anthony Albanese announced “green production credits” to support Australian aluminium smelters, including Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone, enabling investment in renewable and clean energy. The Coalition criticized the policy as unreliable and energy-costly, while Rio Tinto welcomed the commitment as securing manufacturing and jobs, potentially supporting aluminium supply economics.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | Great Lakes Advocate
summary: Prime Minister Albanese said Australia will provide green production credits to support aluminium smelters including Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone, aiming to help investment shift to renewables and lower energy costs. The Coalition critic said renewables-only policy would hurt industry, while Rio Tinto praised the commitment.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Anthony Albanese says Australia will use green production credits to secure the future of aluminium smelting, targeting support for smelters at Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone to shift to renewable and clean energy while lowering costs. Rio Tinto welcomed the commitment. Critics argue renewables raise power reliability/cost risks.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | Manning River Times
summary: Prime Minister Albanese says Australia will back aluminium smelters with “green production credits” to help firms invest in renewables and lower costs, highlighting support for Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone. Opposition claims renewables risk reliability and offshore production, but Rio Tinto applauds the commitment to the industry.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | Port Macquarie News
summary: Prime Minister Albanese said green production credits will support Australian aluminium smelters including Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone to help them shift to renewable power and lower costs. Industry leaders welcomed the funding, while opponents argued energy policy could harm reliability and drive production offshore.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | The Singleton Argus
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced green production credits for Australian aluminium smelters, including Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone, aimed at helping firms shift to renewable/clean energy while lowering costs and sustaining jobs. Opposition argues the policy undermines reliability and competitiveness, but Rio Tinto welcomed the support.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | The Scone Advocate
summary: Prime Minister Albanese announced green production credits aimed at supporting Australian aluminium smelters, including Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone, to help companies invest in renewable and cleaner energy and reduce costs. Opposition claims the policy would hurt industry, but Rio Tinto welcomed the commitment, supporting aluminium production outlook.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | Muswellbrook Chronicle
summary: Prime Minister Albanese says Australia’s green production credits will secure the future of the country’s aluminium industry, targeting support to smelters such as Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone. The policy is framed as reducing costs by enabling the shift to renewable power, protecting jobs and investment certainty.

title: Labor commits to 'green aluminium'
summary: Australia’s Labor government is offering billions in tax credits to help the aluminium sector shift smelting operations toward renewable energy sources. The proposal targets the energy-intensive nature of smelting, with claims of job security for workers in NSW’s Hunter region and sector confidence that renewables can meet demand.

title: Federal Election 2025: Albanese government's $2 billion aluminium boost faces torching as experts say it proves renewables aren't low cost
summary: Australia’s Albanese government announced $2 billion in incentives/production credits to help aluminium smelters (e.g., Tomago) move to renewable energy. Opposition critics argue wind/solar can’t supply reliable, low-cost baseload power and would raise bills. Overall, the funding directly supports aluminium production economics, likely supportive for near-term sentiment.

title: Australia to spend $1.2bn on green aluminum efforts
summary: Australia announced $1.2bn in support for its aluminum industry via a 10-year production credit program aimed at reducing emissions and boosting domestic “green” supply chain capabilities. The policy is intended to spur cleaner production and capacity planning, which can support market expectations for aluminum demand/supply balance.

title: Albanese says green production credits will secure the future of Australian aluminium | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Prime Minister Albanese announced green production credits to secure the future of Australia’s aluminium smelters, including Tomago, Bell Bay and Gladstone, by providing support throughout the supply chain to help firms shift toward renewable power and reduce costs. Opposition warned renewables could push production offshore, while Rio Tinto welcomed the plan.

title: Copper market sees half chance of 10% US tariff by first quarter-end, Goldman says
summary: Goldman Sachs says the copper market is pricing about a 50% chance of a 10% U.S. tariff on copper by end of the first quarter. Traders will watch Trump’s inauguration for policy signals. Three-month copper on the LME fell slightly, reflecting tariff-related demand concerns.

title: Government announces new funding for 'green' aluminium production
summary: Australia’s government announced $2 billion in “Green Aluminium Production Credit” funding to subsidize smelters for each tonne of aluminium produced using renewable energy. The credits aim to support Tomago and other operators in switching from coal power, improving competitiveness amid rising aluminium demand tied to EV growth.

title: Billions pledged for green aluminium push
summary: Australia pledged billions to support a “green aluminium” push, including per-ton government backing/production credits for low-carbon aluminium produced at Rio Tinto and Alcoa smelters. The plan aims to improve competitiveness amid higher costs and regulatory delays as the country increases renewable power.

title: Codelco and Saudi Arabia discuss copper investment opportunities
summary: Codelco said it is discussing joint copper investment opportunities with Saudi Arabia and expects 2025 production to rise by about 70,000 tonnes to around 1.4 million tonnes. Talks include potential technology transfer and partnership efforts aimed at boosting copper supply, with possible announcements later this year.

title: Australia to invest A$2bn in aluminium industry to bolster manufacturing
summary: Australia’s government will invest A$2bn in the domestic aluminium industry and launch a Green Aluminium Production Credit. The credit supports Australian smelters producing each tonne of clean, reliable, low-carbon aluminium for ten years, aiming to secure smelting capacity via renewable electricity and boost jobs. Rio Tinto and the Aluminium Council welcomed it.

title: Anglo American plans Brazil nickel mines sale in H1 2025
summary: Anglo American plans to sell its Brazil nickel assets, Barro Alto and Niquelandia, by H1 2025 as part of a restructuring after BHP’s takeover bid. Analysts expect obtaining a good price will be hard given a weak nickel price, implying continued bearish sentiment for nickel.

title: Ramp Metals Inc.: Ramp Metals Confirms New Rush Copper Discovery, Announces Mobilization for Geophysics Ahead of Drill Program
summary: Ramp Metals announced a new “Rush” exploration target within its Rottenstone SW property, reporting rock copper up to 1.61% and soil copper up to 798.5 ppm, alongside other gold/silver results. The company is mobilizing for a large airborne EM survey and plans drilling in February, but no production impacts are described.

title: Openreach ramps up copper switch-off
summary: Openreach has expanded “stop sell” coverage, halting the sale of legacy copper-based phone and broadband services in exchange locations where ultrafast full fibre is available to over 75% of premises. The move should push customers to fibre upgrades and reduce ongoing copper telecom demand in the affected areas.

title: Trigon's Kalahari Copper Project Wins EU Funding via UNDERCOVER Project
summary: Trigon Metals said its Kalahari Copper Project was selected for EU funding under the UNDERCOVER research initiative (€5 million total). The project targets exploration of critical raw materials in Namibia/Botswana, building on copper (0.7% Cu) intersections. Management also discusses progress on the Kombat Mine sale and an insurance claim.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc Announces Additional Drill Results From the AuRORA Copper-Gold-Silver Deposit Discovery in Collaboration With Freeport at the Joy District, British Columbia
summary: Amarc reported additional drill assay results from its AuRORA porphyry Cu-Au-Ag discovery at the JOY district in British Columbia, highlighting continuity and near-surface high-grade copper alongside gold and silver. Freeport is funding to earn an interest. The update is exploration-focused, without direct near-term supply impact for copper.

title: Column-Global aluminium market faces a year of trade turbulence: Andy Home - 2025-01-20
summary: Reuters columnist Andy Home says aluminium traders face trade turbulence in 2025, including possible U.S. tariffs on Canadian and Mexican aluminium, a potential EU ban on Russian supplies, and tighter alumina costs reducing output at Rusal. With falling LME stocks and higher prices, he expects heightened upside volatility in aluminium.

title: Will U.S. Tariffs Disrupt Copper and Aluminum Markets?
summary: U.S. tariff expectations under the new Trump administration appear to be lifting Comex copper prices, with traders pricing possible tariff impacts despite a stronger U.S. dollar. Aluminum shows a tighter LME–Comex spread, but the Midwest Aluminum Premium has risen since late October, signaling tariff-related risk and potential upside.

title: Will U.S. Tariffs Disrupt Copper and Aluminum Markets?
summary: The article says traders are pricing potential U.S. tariffs ahead of Trump’s inauguration, lifting Comex copper to its highest level since early November and widening LME–Comex spreads. For aluminum, LME and Comex stay closely correlated, while the Midwest aluminum premium trends higher. A strong U.S. dollar and Fed uncertainty cap gains.

title: BHP's 2Q Copper, Iron Ore Output Rises
summary: BHP said its second-quarter copper output rose 17% to 510,700 mt as a production record at Escondida outweighed a weather-related power outage at copper operations in South Australia. BHP reiterated its copper guidance for the year but pared expectations for the South Australia unit after a storm-driven outage.

title: Capstone Copper Announces 2024 Production Results and Provides 2025 Guidance
summary: Capstone Copper reported 2024 copper production of 184,458 tonnes and issued 2025 guidance for 220,000–255,000 tonnes, up 19–38%, with C1 cash costs falling to $2.20–$2.50/lb from 2024. It attributes growth to ramp-ups at Mantoverde/Mantos Blancos and outlines capex plans and hedging.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Announces 2024 Production Results and Provides 2025 Guidance
summary: Capstone Copper announced 2024 production results and 2025 guidance, citing record 184,458 tonnes output and lower C1 cash costs. It expects 2025 copper volumes of 220,000–255,000 tonnes (up 19–38%) and C1 costs $2.20–$2.50/lb (down 10–20%), driven by ramps at Mantoverde and other sites.

title: ASX 200 LIVE: Australian shares poised to rise as Trump takes office.Wesfarmers winds down Catch. Liontown lithium output leaps. BHP copper output jump; Capstone Copper misses guidance. Australian dollar rallies.
summary: Australia’s ASX rebounded after Trump tariff rhetoric initially hit markets, though later headlines showed possible 25% tariffs on Mexico and Canada. Copper-linked shares rose as BHP reported a bumper copper production result, while Fortescue also gained. Other mentions are equity-specific (banks, gold, iron ore) rather than nickel or aluminium.

title: Albanese's $2 billion boost secures Aussie aluminium's future | The Standard
summary: The Australian government will provide $2 billion in production credits to help aluminium smelters switch to renewable power before 2036. Alcoa says it secures the Portland smelter’s future and supports competitiveness and jobs. By easing energy-transition burdens and stabilizing supply expectations, the policy is modestly supportive for aluminium prices.

title: BHP's Copper, Iron Ore Output Rises -- Update
summary: BHP reported a 17% jump in second-quarter copper output to 510,700 metric tons, driven by a 33% year-over-year surge at Escondida, which hit a 10-year production high. South Australia was hit by a storm and a two-week power outage, but group copper guidance stayed intact.

title: BHP boosts copper production in second quarter
summary: BHP said copper production rose 17% year-on-year to 510,700 tonnes in the second quarter, with Chile’s Escondida delivering a 22% increase to a ten-year record. However, guidance for copper South Australia was lowered after a weather-related power outage. BHP also noted a USD300m impact from WA nickel following temporary suspension.

title: BHP chases copper as China's steel appetite flattens
summary: BHP said it boosted copper output 17% in the three months to Dec 31 versus a year earlier, beating analyst expectations. The strength was mainly attributed to its Chile-based Escondida mine. While iron ore prices fell, the company’s copper ramp-out improved near-term market sentiment for copper.

title: BHP copper output jumps as electrification era ramps up
summary: BHP reported a decade-high H1 copper production result, with output rising 10% to nearly 1 million tonnes, driven mainly by Chile’s Escondida. The piece ties electrification demand growth to the transition metals theme and notes consolidation discussions, leaving near-term copper price direction mixed between higher supply and stronger demand.

title: Albanese's green subsidy secures aluminium smelter jobs | The Advocate
summary: Australia’s government announced a $2 billion green subsidy program for aluminium smelters, intended to keep Rio Tinto’s Bell Bay plant producing and transitioning to renewable electricity. Officials say the plan secures electricity-intensive manufacturing via lower power costs and may stimulate new renewable contracts in Tasmania.

title: Albanese's green subsidy secures aluminium smelter jobs | The Examiner
summary: Australia’s federal government will provide a $2 billion green subsidy to aluminium smelters, aimed at keeping smelting jobs and ensuring cheap, reliable electricity for Rio Tinto’s Bell Bay plant as operations shift to renewable energy. The policy is intended to secure continued aluminium output and link smelters with new renewable power contracts.

title: IG Asia Recon Drilling Intercepts 50 Meters of 1.16% Copper
summary: IG Asia reported encouraging reconnaissance drilling results at Kazakhstan’s Pribrezhniy Cu/Mo porphyry trend, including a 1.01% copper intercept over 50m at Yuzhnaya Ploschad and copper mineralization in most holes. The findings support further exploration to expand resources, which is mildly bullish for copper sentiment.

title: Strategic Metal, Strategic Action: 6 Steps to Secure the Future of Aluminium in Europe
summary: The article argues Europe’s aluminium industry is threatened by high energy prices, carbon leakage, scrap exports, and unfair trade. It urges policies to cut electricity costs, strengthen CBAM, limit scrap exports, and bolster trade defence and financing for decarbonisation. These steps would likely support near-term aluminium producer outlooks.

title: Noronex drills big copper-silver grades at Namibia Fiesta project
summary: Noronex reported multiple strong copper-silver drill intercepts at its Fiesta project in Namibia, including 16m at 1.3% copper equivalent and other wider, higher-grade hits. The company also highlights silver’s potential to improve concentrate payability. Overall, the news is positive for copper sentiment but unlikely to affect near-term market prices materially.

title: Making aluminium uses 10% of Australia's electricity. Will tax incentives help smelters go green?
summary: Australia’s federal government proposes tax funding for aluminium producers to generate output using renewable electricity (2028–2036). The article notes smelting is power-intensive and currently coal-based, so reliable low-carbon power could improve competitiveness versus Asia. It frames incentives as supporting green aluminium demand while stabilizing smelter economics.

title: BHP's iron ore, copper production increases due to efficiency improvements
summary: BHP said its copper production rose 17% to 510,700 tonnes in the December quarter, mainly from efficiency gains at the Escondida mine in Chile. While BHP also talks about a potential future copper deficit and plans further investment, the reported uptick in production may weigh on short-term copper price expectations.

title: Jubilee Metals to re-start copper facility after power deal
summary: Jubilee Metals says it has secured regulatory approval for a new power supply agreement in Zambia and power delivery began Monday. The Roan copper concentrator had been disrupted by electricity outages. The added, multi-source power base should allow the plant to restart and improve near-term copper concentrate production.

title: Infinico Metals Corp.: Infinico Announces the Start of Fixed Loop Surface Electromagnetic Survey at the Nicobi Nickel, Copper and Cobalt Property
summary: Infinico Metals announced the start of a fixed loop fluxgate electromagnetic survey at its Nicobi Ni-Cu-Co property in Québec to refine conductive targets for future drilling. The company cites prior drilling results showing nickel-copper sulphide mineralization, but no production or operational changes are reported.

title: Infinico Metals Corp.: Infinico Announces the Start of Fixed Loop Surface Electromagnetic Survey at the Nicobi Nickel, Copper and Cobalt Property
summary: Infinico Metals began a fixed-loop fluxgate surface electromagnetic survey at its Nicobi property to refine conductive targets for potential Ni–Cu sulphide drilling. Prior drilling at Showing A intersected nickel and copper mineralization, but follow-up closed it off. The release focuses on exploration targeting rather than production or supply changes.

title: Alaska Energy Metals Corporation: Alaska Energy Metals' 2024 Surface Exploration Program Reveals Multiple Nickel - Copper Targets at The Angliers
summary: Alaska Energy Metals reported 2024 exploration results at its Angliers-Belleterre project in Quebec, outlining multiple undrilled VMS and Cu-Ni targets with anomalous copper and nickel in soil, rock, and VTEM results. The company plans further geophysical modeling and diamond drilling to test mineralization at depth.

title: BHP Headlines - BHP reports solid Q2, copper shines amid coal weakness
summary: BHP reported solid Q2 results, with the article emphasizing that copper pricing remains favorable. This strong copper performance helps offset weaker results in coal. Analysts cite BHP’s diversification benefits, particularly its exposure to copper, which continues to perform well.

title: Fathom Nickel Inc.: Fathom Provides 2024 Year in Review and Outlook for 2025
summary: Fathom Nickel reported 2024 exploration results expanding the historic Gochager Lake nickel sulphide footprint and validating magmatic mineralization at Albert Lake, plus plans for further EM surveys and drilling in 2025. The company expects improving nickel prices and notes Indonesia production curbs, but no near-term supply disruption occurs.

title: Surge Copper Expands Copper-Gold Mineralization at Ootsa Intersecting 108 Metres Grading 0.35% Copper Equivalent
summary: Surge Copper reported assay results from two 2024 exploration drill holes at its Ootsa Cu-Au target, including 108m of 0.35% CuEq and wider copper-gold mineralization at depth. The company says results could expand resources, but there is no immediate production or supply adjustment, limiting near-term copper price impact.

title: Surge Copper Expands Copper-Gold Mineralization At Ootsa Intersecting 108 Metres Grading 0.35% Copper Equivalent
summary: Surge Copper reported new drill results from its Ootsa Cu-Au target, including 108 metres grading 0.35% copper equivalent (0.25% Cu) and additional higher-grade copper-equivalent intervals. The company says results support potential expansion of copper resources at the Cu-Au target, improving copper development outlook.

title: Metso to deliver copper concentrator plant equipment to Mazoon Mining
summary: Metso signed a US$30m deal to supply processing equipment for Mazoon Mining’s Yanqul copper concentrator plant in Oman. The package includes crushing, grinding, flotation, thickening, filtration and monitoring systems. The project targets 115,000 tpy of copper concentrate, with most orders booked in 4Q24/1Q25.

title: Teck Resources expects copper production to rise this year
summary: Teck Resources said it expects 2025 copper production to rise to 490,000–565,000 tonnes, helped by increased output at Quebrada Blanca and Highland Valley Copper. The forecast is higher than 2024 production of 446,000 tonnes. The update is mainly company-level supply guidance for copper.

title: Teck Resources expects copper production to rise this year | iNFOnews | Thompson-Okanagan's News Source
summary: Teck Resources expects 2025 copper production to rise to 490,000–565,000 tonnes, supported by higher output at Quebrada Blanca and Highland Valley Copper. The guidance is above 2024 production of 446,000 tonnes. The article also updates forecasts for zinc, lead, and molybdenum, plus 2025 capex.

title: Metso to deliver copper-concentrator plant equipment to Mazoon Mining in Oman - Chemical Engineering
summary: Metso signed a $30 million deal to supply key crushers, mills, flotation cells, thickeners and filters for Mazoon Mining’s new copper concentrator plant at Yanqul, Oman. The project is planned to produce copper concentrate from five open pits, but the announcement implies future capacity rather than near-term supply changes.

title: Indonesia plans to cut nickel production for higher prices — newspaper
summary: Indonesia’s mineral authorities are considering cutting domestic nickel production so supply better matches domestic and export needs and avoids further sustained price declines. As the world’s leading nickel miner, Indonesia’s potential quota reductions could tighten supply expectations and support international nickel prices, amid recent sharp losses.

title: Material Matters: Gold, Copper, Oil & Coal
summary: Citi expects copper to soften after strong pre-tariff front-loading in late 2024. With tariff-driven growth headwinds, payback of temporary consumption support, and modest/reactionary China stimulus, Citi forecasts LME copper easing toward US$8,500/t in Q1 2025 from about US$9,000/t recently.

title: Copper Market to grow by USD 70 Billion (2024-2028), Driven by Strong APAC Demand, Report with Insights on AI's Impact on Market Trends
summary: Technavio forecasts the global copper market to grow by USD 70 billion (2024-2028), driven by strong APAC demand and technology trends like 5G/IoT, improved extraction and recycling. It notes copper price volatility from broader supply-demand and macro/geopolitical factors, but provides no near-term catalyst.

title: Saudi Arabia to get 20pc stake in Pakistan's Reko Diq Copper and Gold Project: report
summary: Saudi Arabia’s Manara Minerals via the Saudi Development Fund plans to buy about a 20% stake in Pakistan’s Reko Diq, a major undeveloped copper-gold mine. The Financial Times report cites potential production of up to 400,000 tonnes of copper. Talks aim to finalize within months, supporting sentiment toward copper supply prospects.

title: Australian Labor government pitches for business backing with huge aluminium subsidies
summary: Australia’s Labor government pledged $2 billion in “Green Aluminium Production Tax Credits” over 10 years for operators of four surviving Australian aluminium smelters, linked to renewable electricity use and additional transmission infrastructure. The subsidies are positioned as preventing closures and boosting output, implying near-term support for aluminium supply and sentiment.

title: Greens want ban on bauxite mining in WA forests
summary: The WA Greens propose banning new bauxite mining and expansions in native forests if they gain upper-house balance of power, with additional exclusion zones around conservation areas and reservoir protection zones. Premier Roger Cook and Alcoa argue it risks jobs and hampers aluminium’s role in the green transition. Demand for policy clarity could affect aluminium supply expectations.

title: Rio Tinto bets Trump will give green light to US copper mine, FT reports
summary: Rio Tinto believes President Trump may approve its stalled Resolution copper mine in Arizona. The project, developed with BHP, is described as potentially supplying more than a quarter of U.S. domestic copper needs. The prospect of regulatory progress improves near-term supply expectations for copper.

title: Zambia's 2024 copper production rises 12%, mines minister says
summary: Zambia’s copper production increased 12% in 2024 to about 820,670 metric tons as key mines recovered. Output gains came from Barrick’s Lumwana ramp-up, Vedanta’s Konkola Copper Mines resuming, and improved Mopani operations after ownership changes, despite electricity shortages. Zambia is Africa’s second-largest copper producer.

title: Rio Tinto thinks Trump will approve Arizona copper mine - FT
summary: Rio Tinto Chief Executive Jakob Stausholm told the Financial Times it believes the Trump administration will approve its long-delayed Arizona Resolution copper mine. The fully developed project could become North America’s largest and potentially supply about 25% of US copper demand, subject to permitting talks and ongoing legal challenges.

title: Zambia copper output up 12% last year as key mines recover
summary: Zambia’s copper output rose 12% in 2024 to about 820,670 tonnes as production recovered at major mines including Barrick’s Lumwana and Vedanta’s Konkola (KCM), alongside Mopani. Output increased despite electricity shortages from drought-linked hydropower issues, supporting copper supply outlooks.

title: Highland Copper Commences Drilling Program for Metallurgical Testing of Ultrafine Flotation Technology
summary: Highland Copper commenced a drilling program to collect samples for metallurgical testing of ultra-fine flotation technology as part of FEED work for its Copperwood and related projects. Results are expected by mid-March 2025, aiming to improve grade-recovery and reduce plant footprint, but no immediate output or supply changes are stated.

title: Koryx Copper Announces Transformative 2025 Drill and Study
summary: Koryx Copper announced a C$20M 2025 drill-and-study program at its Haib copper project in Namibia, including >55,000m of drilling, metallurgical testwork, and plans for an updated PEA by mid/late 2025 and PFS by year-end. The work targets higher grades/resources and flotation plus heap leach processing feasibility.

title: Camino Minerals Corporation Commences Copper Discovery Exploration Drilling At the Los Chapitos Project in Peru
summary: Camino Minerals said it has begun exploration drilling at its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, targeting copper oxide zones and potential copper sulfide mineralization. The 11-hole, 1,200m campaign is funded via an earn-in payment from partner Nittetsu. Results are not provided, so near-term supply impact is minimal.

title: Australia invests A$2bn to 'supercharge' green aluminium industry - News
summary: Australia is introducing a A$2bn production credit to encourage energy-intensive aluminium smelters to produce “clean” aluminium using renewable power. The scheme will incentivize extra output of clean metal and support domestic supply chains and jobs, backing investment in new smelting technology including at Rio Tinto sites.

title: Trigon gets N$100 million from EU for 'ambitious' copper project - Business Home 2
summary: Trigon Metals received about €5 million from the EU to fund the three-year Undercover research initiative, with its Kalahari Copper project in Namibia selected as one of the funded efforts. The program aims to improve exploration methods for deep, covered critical raw materials, potentially supporting future copper supply.

title: Column-Only Indonesia can help nickel recover from price bust: Andy Home -January 22, 2025 at 11:20 am EST
summary: Reuters column says Indonesia’s nickel sector has flooded markets and drove nickel to four-year lows, but Jakarta plans to cut 2025 ore mining quotas to 200 Mt from 240 Mt. The quota outlook has coincided with a modest LME 3-month nickel rebound (+3% since early January), though inventories remain elevated.

title: Trump's America First Trade Policy on Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: Trump’s administration launched an “America First Trade Policy” investigation under Section 232 focused on imported steel and aluminum. The review assesses exclusions/exemptions and could lead to adjusted tariffs or import restrictions after scheduled reports. The announcement is conditional and timing is uncertain, limiting immediate directional impact.

title: Only Indonesia can help nickel recover from price bust: Andy Home -January 22, 2025 at 06:59 pm EST
summary: Reuters columnist says Indonesia is pivotal for nickel’s recovery after 2024’s price bust. The Indonesian mining ministry plans to cut nickel ore quotas to 200m tons from a planned 240m, helping lift LME 3-month nickel by ~3% since early January, though rising inventories and weaker EV battery demand limit follow-through.

title: Zambia's copper output rises by 12% in 2024
summary: Zambia’s copper production rose 12% in 2024 to about 820,670 tonnes as production recovered at major mines including Barrick’s Lumwana and KCM after restart efforts. Mopani also improved output, though drought-related electricity shortages persisted. Zambia plans further expansion and permit transfers for investment.

title: Alcoa Sees Higher Aluminum Shipments in 2025 Despite Looming Tariff Threats
summary: BNN Bloomberg’s item says Alcoa expects higher aluminum shipments in 2025 even as tariff threats loom. The prospect of stronger shipment volumes may improve near-term supply expectations, but potential tariffs could also curb demand or lift trade costs, likely offsetting directional pressure on aluminum prices.

title: Cyprium Metals, Macmahon partner for Nifty Copper Complex redevelopment in WA
summary: Cyprium Metals and Macmahon signed a heads of agreement to speed up bankable feasibility study work for the redevelopment of the Nifty copper complex in Western Australia. Macmahon will lead engineering and project management to restart copper production and shorten construction timelines, targeting earlier time-to-revenue.

title: Freeport-McMoRan's profit beats estimates due to rising copper prices
summary: Freeport-McMoRan reported profits above analysts’ estimates, with the outperformance attributed to rising copper prices. That connection suggests market expectations for copper improved in the near term, providing supportive price momentum for copper within the coming days and weeks.

title: Columbia Falls Aluminum cleanup plan draws criticism over waste removal
summary: EPA approved a Superfund cleanup approach for the former Columbia Falls Aluminum smelter, choosing on-site containment via a reinforced concrete “slurry wall” to limit groundwater contamination. A local group criticizes the plan and wants toxic soil removal by the site owner, Glencore. The cleanup is expected to take 2–4 years.

title: Trump Initiates Investigation of Tariffs on Imported Steel and Aluminum Products | Pierce Atwood LLP
summary: The Trump administration has launched an investigation under Section 232 into whether to adjust tariff restrictions on imported steel and aluminum, reviewing exclusions and potential new import limitations tied to national security. Prior 232 tariffs included 10% aluminum in many cases, with possible further changes.

title: Zambia records increased copper production
summary: Zambia’s mines ministry said copper production rose to 820,676 metric tons in 2024 from 732,583 metric tons in 2023, a 12% increase. The minister attributed gains to investments and the resumption of operations at Konkola and Mopani Copper Mines. Production growth targets continued expansion toward 2031.

title: School electrician arrested after thousands in copper stolen from campuses
summary: A school electrician in Palm Beach County was arrested after police said copper wire was stolen from multiple schools, with about $779,000 in losses estimated over two years. Investigators allege he sold large quantities of copper and brass to a local scrapyard, typically shortly after burglaries. Damage claims include electrical component replacement costs.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Positive Regional Exploration Results Including Best Regional Exploration Result To Date At Midlothian
summary: Canada Nickel announced positive exploration drill results from its Midlothian and Deloro properties, with multiple holes intersecting shallow, mineralized ultramafic rocks and reporting nickel grades (e.g., 0.27% over 371m including 0.30% over 39m at Deloro). It also describes ongoing infill work at Nesbitt. This supports bullish nickel sentiment for the near term.

title: Alcoa sees higher aluminum shipments in 2025 despite looming tariff threats
summary: Alcoa forecasts record-high aluminum demand in 2025 but warns that a potential 25% U.S. tariff on aluminum imports from Canada could suppress American consumption. The company estimates the tariff would hurt consumers by $1.5–$2 billion, with weeks left before tariff clarity, while also discussing broader trade restrictions.

title: [SMM Analysis] Weekly Review of the Indonesian-1.24 Nickel Market for the second Week of 2025
summary: SMM reports Indonesia’s 2025 RKAB quota for nickel ore at 298 million wmt and active ore trading, with smelters starting February procurement. High-grade NPI FOB/inland prices recovered on tighter circulation ahead of Chinese New Year, but quota approval and rising LME nickel inventories restrained refined nickel gains, implying mixed near-term direction.

title: Upward Trend in High Nickel Pig Iron Prices Amid Supply and Demand Shifts
summary: High-nickel pig iron prices increased this week, with the Indonesian NPI FOB index also rising. Supply was slightly tightened by weaker domestic production due to smelter losses, while tight circulating resources and long-term contract coverage supported demand. The NPI-to-electrolytic nickel discount narrowed, implying buoyant nickel sentiment.

title: Noronex refocuses Namibian copper hunt on Damara project
summary: Noronex has begun an RC drilling program to test gravity and magnetic targets across its Damara copper project in Namibia, funded via a South32 JV. The company is also highlighting prior Fiesta drilling results with copper-equivalent grades. It signals potential copper prospectivity but no immediate supply changes.

title: Koryx Copper revs up drilling at Haib
summary: Koryx Copper says it is accelerating drilling and technical studies at its Haib copper project in southern Namibia to expand and upgrade resources and produce updated PEA and PFS before year-end. The plan aims to reach bankability faster and involves plans for copper concentrate and refined cathode production.

title: Battery Materials and Solutions Provider COBCO Takes a Major Step Forward with the Commissioning of its First Batch of Precursor Cathode Active Materials Nickel Cobalt Manganese Production Lines in Morocco
summary: COBCO commissioned its first batch of NCM precursor cathode active materials lines in Jorf Lasfar, Morocco, targeting 120kT/year PCAM capacity. The NCM (nickel-containing) production ramp-up and planned closed-loop recycling expansion point to higher near-term demand for nickel materials used in battery cathodes.

title: BT urges UK's Critical National Infrastructure providers to move off outdated copper network this year as fault rate increases
summary: BT urges UK Critical National Infrastructure providers to accelerate migration away from legacy analogue copper landlines due to rising PSTN fault incidents and an end-of-life retirement timeline (end-January 2027; actions by end-December 2025). It cites 60% of CNI customers lacking migration plans and highlights digital stability benefits. No explicit copper quantity changes are given.

title: Environmental group concerned about freshwater impact of nickel mine
summary: An environmental group says Canada Nickel’s proposed Crawford Project could harm freshwater by releasing effluent into the North Driftwood River, a relatively small stream. The group is reviewing the large impact statement and has concerns about long-term effects over a 41-year mine life, prompting ongoing scrutiny.

title: Core Nickel Corp. Provides 2024 Year-End Review and Outlines 2025 Exploration Plans
summary: Core Nickel Corp. published its 2024 year-end review and outlines 2025 exploration plans for its Thompson Nickel Belt projects, including planned VTEM, re-sampling, and a 4,000–5,000 m drill program at the Mel and Halfway Lake areas. The update targets resource expansion and does not affect near-term nickel supply directly.

title: JSW to invest $301m in two copper mines in Jharkhand, India
summary: JSW Group plans to invest about $302m to develop two copper mines in Jharkhand and build a concentrator plant via a 20-year contract with Hindustan Copper Limited. The project targets partial operations in 2026–27. JSW cites rising copper demand and aims to reduce India’s reliance on imports.

title: AT&T CEO outlines copper retireme... - Mobile World Live
summary: AT&T says it has FCC approval to begin discontinuing legacy voice services in 1,300 central offices and expects to retire most copper lines by 2029. Additional FCC filings will stop selling legacy copper in those sites. The shift to fiber/FWA is expected to lower copper network operations costs.

title: Trump Vows To Put Tariffs On Computer Chips, Drugs, Steel And Aluminum
summary: The headline reports a plan to impose tariffs on computer chips, drugs, steel and aluminum. An aluminum tariff would likely increase costs for import-dependent buyers and reduce near-term demand expectations, creating bearish pressure for traded aluminum prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Cygnus Metals nails 9.1 per cent copper in new Quebec lode
summary: Cygnus Metals announced drilling results from its Chibougamau copper-gold project in Quebec, including a standout 2.5m intercept grading 9.1% copper. The company describes a newly identified copper lode supported by electromagnetic conductors, suggesting upside for additional lode extensions and resources.

title: Copper Extends Losses After Trump Threatens Tariffs on Metals
summary: Copper prices are extending losses following reports that Trump threatened tariffs on metals. The tariff threat increases trade and demand uncertainty for industrial inputs, which can weigh on copper market sentiment in the near term, keeping downward pressure on prices over the following days to weeks.

title: Trump's copper, aluminium tariffs may raise costs for U.S. consumers
summary: Reuters reports Trump’s vow to impose tariffs on U.S. imports of copper and aluminium, arguing domestic production shortfalls and lengthy capacity restart timelines would raise costs for U.S. users. Analysts expect tariffs to alter trade flows and keep interim supply tight, supporting upward pressure on both copper and aluminium prices.

title: Trump's copper, aluminium tariffs may raise costs for U.S. consumers
summary: Reuters reports Trump’s vow to impose tariffs on U.S. copper and aluminium imports, citing limited domestic production and long lead times to restart smelting. Analysts expect the costs to be passed to U.S. manufacturers and consumers, with potential near-term supply-demand and trade-flow impacts for both metals.

title: Trump's Copper, Aluminium Tariffs May Raise Costs for U.S. Consumers
summary: The article reports that Trump vowed tariffs on U.S. imports of copper and aluminium (and steel) to encourage domestic production, citing a domestic supply shortfall and slow industry restart. Analysts expect higher costs for U.S. consumers, implying upward near-term pressure on copper and aluminium prices.

title: Trump's Copper, Aluminium Tariffs May Raise Costs for U.S. Consumers
summary: The article says Trump vowed tariffs on U.S. copper and aluminium imports, arguing the U.S. lacks enough domestic production and that restarting output would take time. Analysts expect the measures to raise costs for U.S. consumers, with copper and aluminium needed for military hardware.

title: JSW Group Enters Copper Mining with ₹2,600 Crore Investment
summary: JSW Group said it won a 20-year (extendable) MDO contract from HCL to develop two copper mines in Jharkhand, including installing a copper concentrator plant. The Rs 2,600 crore investment targets 3 MTPA ore capacity on full ramp-up, with operations expected in 2H FY2026-27.

title: Trump's copper, aluminium tariffs may raise costs for US consumers - Regulations
summary: Trump’s proposed tariffs on imported copper and aluminum would raise costs for US consumers because domestic production is short and restarting smelter capacity would take time. Analysts expect tariff charges to be passed through to manufacturers and automakers, potentially tightening near-term effective supply for both metals.

title: Trump's copper, aluminium tariffs may raise costs for US consumers - Regulations
summary: Donald Trump’s planned tariffs on imported copper and aluminium are expected to raise costs for US consumers because domestic production and restarting smelters would take time. Analysts say costs would be passed down the supply chain, and trade-flow uncertainty could affect demand, with copper especially painful meanwhile.

title: How artificial intelligence will boost demand for copper
summary: The piece says AI adoption will expand data centres, electronics, robotics and connected/automated vehicles, all of which use copper in wiring, power distribution, chips and circuit boards. It estimates substantial incremental copper demand and suggests supply constraints could push copper prices higher, with possible strategic stockpiling.

title: Vedanta's Rs 1 lakh cr aluminium refinery project to come up in Odisha's Raygada
summary: Vedanta said it will build a Rs 1 lakh crore aluminium refinery (6 MTPA) and aluminium smelter (30 lakh tonnes) in Odisha’s Rayagada. Initial commissioning is expected within three years, with later expansion. The project is tied to the firm’s Sijimali bauxite mine development, indicating growing aluminium capacity.

title: BBA to provide detailed design engineering for Troilus Copper-Gold Project in Canada
summary: Troilus Gold awarded BBA a contract for basic and detailed engineering for the Troilus copper-gold project in Quebec. BBA will design on-site infrastructure and an optimised process plant, including crushing, grinding, flotation and gold recovery, and coordinate power, tailings and water systems. Work starts in early February 2025.

title: World Pumps - KSB GIW wins major pump contract for a copper mine in British Columbia
summary: KSB GIW won a major pump contract for Teck’s Highland Valley Copper Mine Life Extension project in British Columbia. The upgraded infrastructure is expected to process additional ore and yield about 1.95 million extra tons of copper, supporting ongoing/expanded copper output and demand expectations.

title: Federal government invests $41 million in Foran mission to produce net-zero copper
summary: Canada’s federal government will invest $41 million to expand Foran Mining’s McIlvenna Bay project to produce net-zero copper. The funding adds 400 jobs and complements prior $20 million support to connect the mine to net-zero hydro. The copper is intended for EV batteries and related technologies.

title: MAC Copper Limited Announces December 2024 Quarterly Report
summary: MAC Copper’s December 2024 quarterly report highlights record quarterly copper production (11,320 tonnes) and a 12% QoQ reduction in C1 cash costs to US$1.66/lb. It also notes improved safety metrics and a positive 2025 C1 outlook from lower TC/RC benchmarks and exchange-rate effects.

title: Fire at Niles aluminum facility under investigation
summary: The news headline reports a fire at an aluminium facility in Niles and says the incident is under investigation. Production disruptions from fires can reduce near-term aluminium output, tighten supply, and lead to downward price pressure until the extent of damage and restart timeline are clarified.

title: EU to Propose Russian Aluminum Ban in Sweeping Sanctions Package
summary: The EU is expected to propose a sweeping sanctions package that includes a ban on Russian aluminum. If implemented, the measure would likely disrupt or reduce Russian metal flows into Europe, tightening near-term supply expectations and supporting higher aluminium prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: EU prepares sanctions against Russian aluminium, 15 banks and shadow fleet, Bloomberg reports
summary: Bloomberg reports the EU is preparing sanctions targeting Russian aluminium, involving measures such as action against 15 banks and the shadow-fleet network. If implemented, sanctions could disrupt payments, shipping and trade flows for Russian metal, tightening supply and affecting near-term aluminium market expectations.

title: EU Considers Russian Aluminum Ban
summary: The European Union is considering a phased ban on imports of Russian aluminium as part of a new sanctions package. EU imports about 8% of aluminium from Russia, with quotas during the transition before the ban fully takes effect. The proposal adds supply uncertainty for Europe’s aluminium market.

title: EU to propose phased ban on Russian aluminium in new sanctions package, Bloomberg reports
summary: Bloomberg reports the EU plans to propose a phased ban on Russian aluminium in a new sanctions package. If implemented, the measure would reduce Russian metal flows into European markets, likely tightening near-term supply and supporting higher aluminium prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Midnight Sun Mining Corp.: Midnight Sun Intersects High-Grade Oxide Copper at Kazhiba Target
summary: Midnight Sun Mining reported high-grade oxide copper intercepts from drilling at its Kazhiba target in Zambia’s Solwezi Project, including multiple multi–tens-of-metre copper-rich zones. The company plans additional drilling in April 2025 and awaits ionic leach and IP survey results, aiming to advance toward a resource.

title: EU Commission proposes ban on Russian aluminium in new sanctions package
summary: The European Commission proposed adding Russian primary aluminium imports to its 16th sanctions package against Russia. The proposed ban would cover aluminium alloys as well, with a one-year phase-in and an exemption for “necessary” imports up to 275,000 tonnes. Discussions among EU states are set to begin soon.

title: EU to propose Russian aluminum ban in sweeping sanctions package
summary: The EU is preparing a sanctions package that would include a phased ban on imports of Russian aluminium. If implemented, the measure would reduce Russian supply reaching European buyers, potentially tightening short-term availability and supporting higher aluminium prices as markets reprice replacement sourcing and logistics.

title: Oman resumes copper exports after 30 years
summary: Minerals Development Oman says it will export its first copper concentrate shipment from the Lasail mine after nearly 30 years of dormancy. Lasail produces copper concentrate (18%-22% purity) and has planned follow-on development at the Al-Baydha mine. Oman aims to expand copper exports amid rising global EV demand.

title: Novacium Files A Provisional Patent Application For Transforming Black Aluminum Dross
summary: Novacium/HPQ Silicon filed a provisional patent on a process that uses black aluminum dross to produce green hydrogen and convert remaining material into a valuable solid by-product. It targets improved recycling yield versus current alkaline methods. Potential savings of about C$900–1,500 per tonne are cited, but no near-term supply impact is specified.

title: Copper burglar jailed after stealing wiring from Huawei building
summary: A burglar jailed for involvement in thefts of over £2 million of copper wiring from an empty Huawei office in Reading. Several burglaries occurred in 2023, including cabling taken from voltage rooms and transformers. Loss estimates are local property damage; there’s no indication of wider supply disruption to copper markets.

title: Rampant copper theft drives up demand for aluminum cables in Japan
summary: Japan is seeing a wave of thefts targeting copper electrical cables as copper prices rise, making theft profitable. Solar farm operators and other businesses are reportedly switching to aluminum cable alternatives. The demand shift is likely supportive for aluminum while weighing on copper prices near term via disrupted flows and reduced consumption.

title: Rampant copper theft drives up demand for aluminum cables in Japan
summary: Japan is seeing a wave of thefts targeting copper electrical cables as copper prices rise, making stealing profitable. Solar farm operators and other businesses are switching to aluminum cable alternatives. The reported theft-driven disruption tightens effective copper availability, while substitution may boost aluminum demand, partially limiting copper downside.

title: Terra Metals Inc. Advances Copper and Cobalt Operations in Zambia Amid President Trump's Pro-Mining Policies
summary: Terra Metals said it is re-commissioning its copper-cobalt acid leach plant by end-Q1 2025 and advancing a 1 million tonnes/year flotation plant by end-Q2 2025 in Zambia. The company links progress to Zambia’s announced copper production growth and new pro-mining policy support.

title: Terra Metals Inc. Advances Copper and Cobalt Operations in
summary: Terra Metals says it will re-commission its copper and cobalt acid leach plant by end-Q1 2025 and commission a 1 million tpa flotation plant by end-Q2 2025 in Zambia. It also plans 400 MW solar capacity to power operations. The expansion improves copper production outlook and supports bullish near-term pricing.

title: King County crackdown on copper wire theft leads to arrests and felony charges
summary: King County and Woodinville police report arrests and felony charges for copper wire theft, including damage to wires used for 911, internet, alarms, and cell towers. Detectives describe repeated theft tactics and call for more public reporting. The piece is enforcement-focused without market-wide supply or inventory figures.

title: Rio Tinto and Hydro partner on carbon capture technologies for aluminium smelters
summary: Rio Tinto and Hydro will invest about $45 million over five years to evaluate and develop carbon capture technologies for aluminium electrolysis flue gas. The partnership covers lab work through on-site pilots to speed commercialization. It aims to reduce emissions from existing smelters as part of each company’s net-zero roadmap.

title: Core Nickel Corp.: Core Nickel Commences Property-Wide Airborne Electromagnetic Surveys on its 100%-Owned Mel and Odei River Projects and Grants Stock Options
summary: Core Nickel Corp. started helicopter-borne VTEM electromagnetic surveys on its Mel and Odei River nickel projects in Manitoba and plans further drilling after survey results. The news updates exploration targeting deeper nickel sulphide potential, with no changes to production, exports, or supply affecting near-term nickel markets.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces 2025 Schaft Creek Program
summary: Copper Fox announced its 2025 program for the Schaft Creek porphyry copper-gold-molybdenum-silver project in British Columbia, focusing on advancing studies from scoping to preliminary feasibility, completing geotechnical/environmental work, and conducting additional drilling for TMF and RSF sites. It also notes pre-production costs milestone status under the JV.

title: Tanzania, Burundi sign deal with China to build nickel-carrying railway
summary: Tanzania and Burundi signed an agreement with two Chinese firms to build a $2.15 billion railway connecting the two countries and carrying metals, including battery-mineral nickel, to Dar es Salaam port. The 282 km line is expected to move about three million tonnes of minerals annually, improving nickel transport capacity.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Intersects 47.95 metres at 0.74% Copper within 304.40 metres at 0.35% Copper in the American Eagle Area
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. reported results from six Phase III drill holes at its Copper Creek project in Arizona, including multiple near-surface intervals of copper mineralization (e.g., up to 0.74% Cu over 47.95 m). The release outlines continued drilling and planned studies, but provides no operational or supply-chain changes.

title: Geologica Resource Corp.: Geologica Discovers Copper Showing at Topley
summary: Geologica Resource Corp. reports discovery of a copper-bearing “Ruby” showing at its Topley property, including outcrop copper grades around 0.40–0.60% Cu and historic anomalous copper from prior geochemical and IP surveys. The release expands claims to cover the outcrop but does not imply near-term production impacts.

title: Aftermath Silver Ltd.: Aftermath Silver Reports Near Surface High Grade Silver and Copper Results
summary: Aftermath Silver reported Phase 2 diamond drill assay results from the Berenguela silver-copper-manganese project in Peru, including intervals with copper grades around ~1.8% Cu alongside silver. The company says results extend mineralization, but the news remains exploration-stage with no production changes, limiting near-term copper price impact.

title: New copper deposits unearthed in Block 8 in North Al Batinah Governorate
summary: Power Metal Resources said its subsidiary found new copper mineralization in Block 8 at Oman’s Awtad Project, reporting copper assay results from recent fieldwork. While the discovery reinforces Oman’s growing exploration and export ambitions for copper, no immediate production or shipment impact is described.

title: Rio Tinto and Hydro collaborate on carbon capture in aluminium electrolysis process
summary: Rio Tinto and Hydro will invest about $45m over five years to assess and accelerate carbon capture technologies for aluminium smelters, targeting reductions in process CO2 emissions from electrolysis. The firms will work with suppliers and also develop carbon-free smelting options, supporting aluminium’s net-zero transition by 2050.

title: Chile orders Lundin to shut small copper mine after causing massive sinkhole
summary: Chile’s environmental regulator ordered Lundin to permanently shut its Alcaparrosa copper mine after a sinkhole linked to unauthorized operations and aquifer water infiltration. Lundin faces a fine and will review the ruling. The company said its Candelaria project is unaffected and expects 2025 copper output elsewhere.

title: 'That can't really be happening,' copper theft hitting businesses in Pueblo
summary: Pueblo police are investigating incidents of copper theft and vandalism affecting businesses, including Global Callcenter Solutions. Thieves cut and removed small chunks of copper piping from rooftop HVAC units, causing extensive property damage. Police say it targets HVAC systems, but amounts are modest, implying limited influence on overall copper prices.

title: Experts and advocates warn of nickel mining's risk to precious marine region of Indonesia
summary: A report and experts warn that expanding nickel mining in Raja Ampat, Indonesia, is damaging a UNESCO-protected marine region. Satellite data show mining pit area grew sharply since 2020. Despite a March 2024 court ruling requiring extra protection for small islands, permits continue, raising risks to nickel production timelines.

title: Freeport expects green light for copper concentrate exports in Q1 - Companies
summary: Freeport-McMoRan said Freeport Indonesia has received government approval to resume copper concentrate exports after a late-2024 smelter fire and a temporary export closure. The company expects final approval in Q1 and is working on regulatory changes for continued exports during 2025, supporting copper supply expectations.

title: Rio Tinto Group (RIO) Faces 6% Stock Decline Amid Copper Tariff Concerns and Slower AI Chip Demand
summary: The article on Rio Tinto highlights concerns that the Trump administration may impose tariffs on US copper imports, pressuring European copper-linked equities. It also attributes part of RIO’s ~6% decline to softer AI and chip demand after DeepSeek. It frames copper as key for AI data center electronics.

title: Chile's copper output jumps in December
summary: Chile’s copper output increased 14.3% year-on-year in December to 566,547 tonnes, according to INE. The report also notes manufacturing production rose 8.4% from a year earlier. The higher copper production from the world’s largest supplier could pressure near-term copper prices.

title: Glencore's 2024 metals production declines, copper output falls 6%
summary: Glencore reported 2024 output declines across several commodities, including copper. Copper production fell to 951,600 tonnes, down 6% from 2023 and at the low end of its guidance. Management expects to provide 2025 guidance in February, with improved H2 performance supporting some offset.

title: Africa's big copper countries set their sights on the profits of trade
summary: Congo and Zambia, major copper producers, are negotiating deals to gain exposure to copper trading. Gecamines is close to finalising an allocation deal with Glencore, while Zambia and Mercuria plan copper purchases from local producers. Governments aim to control sales and capture profits amid strong demand.

title: Assays Confirm High-Grade Copper at Kinusi  | Company Announcement
summary: Marula Mining reports assay results from its Kinusi Copper Mine confirming high-grade copper concentrate specifications (average 21.54% Cu). The findings allow previously agreed initial shipments and up to 1,000 tonnes of sales to be finalized, after a delay, and support optimization and scheduling of the Phase 1/2 processing plans.

title: Chinese firms to build $2bn nickel-carrying railway linking Tanzania and Burundi – Medafrica Times
summary: Burundi and Tanzania agreed with Chinese firms to build a $2.15bn 282 km railway to Dar es Salaam to move minerals, including battery nickel. Financed with African Development Bank support, the line is expected to haul three million tonnes annually. Improved export logistics could lift near-term expectations for nickel supply.

title: China's Goodsense to establish $100 mln aluminium factory in Egypt: Minister
summary: China’s Goodsense plans to invest $100 million in Egypt to produce aluminium composite panels in a new Ataqa industrial zone facility. It will partner with WellBond, which already supplies about 8–9% of local needs. The project increases regional aluminium panel supply/demand but signals limited immediate price pressure.

title: Auto sector fuelling India's aluminium demand jump
summary: India’s secondary aluminium demand is forecast to rise 7-9% CAGR, with autos contributing an increasing share. Scrap purchasing remains firm, though importers face margin pressure from weak semi-finished demand. Meanwhile, stronger US and Thailand consumption reduces supply to India. Analysts expect aluminium prices to improve from February/March, citing potential China stimulus.

title: Nickel mining risks Indonesia marine region
summary: A report says nickel mining expansion in Indonesia’s Raja Ampat region has rapidly increased land use and raised fears of deforestation and sediment pollution harming coral ecosystems. Although mining is still operating, growing scrutiny and backlash around nickel projects could threaten near-term supply continuity, supporting nickel prices.

title: BHP awards EPCM contract for copper smelter expansion in South Australia
summary: BHP awarded an EPCM contract to Fluor Australia and Hatch for phased expansion of its Olympic Dam copper smelter and refinery in South Australia. The work starts with A$40m+ in strategy and study phases, supporting a later final investment decision in H1 2027 and higher refined copper cathode output.

title: NorthX Nickel Corp.: NorthX Nickel Announces Non-Brokered Subscription Receipt Financing
summary: NorthX Nickel Corp. announced a non-brokered subscription receipt financing to fund general working capital and to support a proposed acquisition of its Sudbury Basin nickel and base-metal assets. The escrow release depends on transaction conditions. The update is corporate/financing-focused with no direct production or pricing details, implying limited near-term nickel price effect.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces 2024 Year-End Operating and Financial Results
summary: Copper Fox reported audited financial results and progress advancing several copper projects, including exceeding a Schaft Creek pre-production cost milestone and ongoing permitting and technical work at other assets. The company reiterates planned 2025 programs and funding structures but provides no near-term production or supply disruption details.

title: Opponents appeal Arizona air permit for Copper World
summary: Opponents are appealing Arizona’s approval of an air quality permit for Hudbay’s $1.7 billion Copper World open-pit copper mine, arguing it lacks stricter controls and properly scoped emissions limits. The permit is a prerequisite for construction, and ongoing litigation could delay output, weighing on near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Capral Aluminium | Architecture & Design
summary: The piece says the Middle East conflict is disrupting the global aluminium market. It notes recent volatility but highlights analyst expectations for aluminium prices to rise, reflecting near-term supply-chain and market disruption dynamics relevant to aluminium demand and pricing.

title: US tariffs on Canadian aluminium: Major impacts on American workers and consumers
summary: The Aluminium Association of Canada says the US administration’s 25% tariffs on Canadian and other imported aluminium are highly disruptive and will immediately increase aluminium prices for American consumers and manufacturers. The group argues the US should keep Canadian aluminium exempt and highlights measures to prevent circumvention of trade rules.

title: Aluminum Assoc. of Canada: US Tariffs on Canadian Aluminium WIll Disrupt Industry, Drive Up Costs
summary: The Aluminium Association of Canada says 25% U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminium will immediately lift aluminium costs for U.S. manufacturers and consumers. It notes the U.S. relies heavily on imports and Canada supplies much of the shortfall, implying near-term upward price pressure for aluminium.

title: Greenwave Technology Solutions, Inc. Poised for Explosive Growth Amid New Steel, Aluminum, and Copper Tariffs
summary: Greenwave says President Trump plans significant tariffs on steel, aluminum, and copper imports. The company expects the measures to boost demand and raise prices for domestically sourced metals, benefiting its recycled, mill-ready supply. Its customers include major U.S. steel and metals producers and scrap buyers.

title: Greenwave Technology Solutions, Inc. Poised for Explosive Growth Amid New Steel, Aluminum, and Copper Tariffs
summary: Greenwave’s press release says President Trump announced sweeping tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper imports. It argues the tariffs should raise prices for domestically sourced metals and increase demand for mill-ready recycled scrap. The message is explicitly tied to aluminum and copper tariff-driven price pressure.

title: Zanaco CEO Chibesakunda Says Trade War Effect on Copper Muted
summary: Zanaco CEO Mukwandi Chibesakunda said the US trade war has not yet caused a major move in Zambian copper prices. Speaking to Bloomberg at the African Mining Indaba, she suggested near-term pricing remains more tied to underlying demand, with effects expected to play out over time rather than immediately.

title: The EU Competitiveness Compass – views from the Nickel industry
summary: The Nickel Institute comments on the EU “Competitiveness Compass,” arguing that EU regulatory inconsistencies—particularly revisions to nickel environmental quality standards proposed under the Water Framework Directive—could harm producers by constraining investment and competitiveness. It calls for streamlined permitting, reduced regulatory burden, and affordable energy to sustain EU nickel supply for batteries and the energy transition.

title: Canada expected to divert aluminium to Europe after US tariffs
summary: Europe’s physical aluminium market has seen duty-paid premiums fall after expectations that Canadian shipments diverted from the U.S. will arrive in Europe due to new U.S. tariffs. Traders report the COMEX duty-paid aluminium premium dropping over 10% to about $322/ton, indicating weaker near-term aluminium pricing.

title: Aluminium Association Of Canada Releases Statement Against Tariffs
summary: The Aluminium Association of Canada says US-announced 25% tariffs would be highly disruptive and immediately raise aluminium prices, harming US workers and consumers. It calls for Canadian aluminium to remain exempt, citing Canada’s role in North America’s integrated aluminium value chain, and urges action against unfair subsidized Chinese competition.

title: City of Prince George reports increase in theft of copper wire
summary: Prince George reports a sharp rise in theft of copper wiring from streetlights, with roughly $25,000 in repair costs since October. The city says thieves cut underground wiring via handholes, disrupting lighting and creating safety concerns. The report references local copper prices but is mainly a municipal theft update.

title: Sarytogan jags three new copper zones near Kazakh graphite site
summary: Sarytogan Graphite reports soil sampling near its Baynazar project in Kazakhstan identified three copper-emphasized anomalies (Aminbay AN-01 to AN-03) with geochemical and aeromagnetic signatures consistent with a possible porphyry intrusion. It cites artisanal trench copper assays but provides no confirmed deposit or production.

title: Assay Results Extends Copper Mineralisation    | Company Announcement
summary: Arc Minerals reported diamond-drill assay results from its Anglo American JV in Zambia, extending near-surface copper mineralisation at Cheyeza East (including 40.60m @ 0.61% Cu). Oxide and sulphide mineralisation were intersected, with further drilling planned to test extents.

title: Copper Theft: Crackdown on copper thieves with tough new South Australia laws
summary: South Australia is introducing tough laws to curb copper theft, citing major losses to the construction industry and safety risks from stolen copper leaving live wires exposed. Proposed rules require scrap dealers to register, record transactions, and allow police inspections, aiming to deter selling of stolen copper during a three-week consultation.

title: Column-Aluminium is base metals analysts' bull pick for 2025: Andy Home -February 04, 2025 at 10:08 am EST
summary: Reuters column citing a January base-metals analyst poll expects aluminium to lead in 2025 on a projected supply deficit, with cash prices set to rise. Copper upside is tempered by tariff-driven macro risk, especially for China demand. Nickel remains bearish on ongoing oversupply and rising stocks, limiting near-term net impact.

title: NV Energy: Attempted copper wire theft causes partial power outage to Las Vegas airport
summary: An attempted theft of copper wire at an NV Energy substation in Las Vegas caused a partial power outage affecting 12 customers, including Harry Reid International Airport’s Terminal 3. Backup power engaged, restoration began about 4:44 p.m., and the outage caused minor flight delays until power returned to some doors.

title: EU Targets Russian Aluminum, LNG and Shadow Fleet in New Sanctions Round
summary: The EU Commission proposes a new sanctions round targeting Russia and Belarus, including an import ban on primary aluminum from Russia and broader restrictions on Russian aluminum products entering the bloc. With energy measures limited and other logistics/logistics sanctions included, the aluminum trade restriction is the main near-term driver.

title: NV Energy Crews work to repair substation after copper wire theft cause outages near Las Vegas Strip
summary: NV Energy reported that attempted copper wire theft at a substation near Las Vegas Strip damaged equipment, leading to outages at Harry Reid Airport, Allegiant Stadium, and nearby areas. Crews repaired the substation the next morning while police investigated. NV Energy said security reviews may follow; no arrests were reported.

title: Changes in the Metal Supply Chain: How Does the New Energy Industry Influence the Global Market of Cobalt, Lithium, and Nickel?
summary: The article argues that rapid EV and renewable-storage growth is tightening global battery-metal supply chains. It highlights strong demand for nickel sulfate for NCM/NCA cathodes and notes irregular supply from producers such as Indonesia and the Philippines, alongside environmental and production-quote constraints. It implies continued nickel price volatility and upside bias.

title: New Energy Age: In the Era of Soaring Copper, Aluminum, and Nickel Prices, How Will the Volatility Help Guide Your Buying Decisions?
summary: The piece frames the energy transition as long-run support for copper, aluminum, and nickel and cites SMM’s January 20, 2025 price levels. It notes copper premiums weakening ahead of Chinese New Year due to softer consumption, while nickel premiums fall on abundant supply and reduced activity, implying mixed short-term pressure.

title: Power outage at Harry Reid Airport linked to copper theft case
summary: A power outage at Harry Reid Airport was linked to suspected copper theft at an NV Energy substation. Metro is investigating a grand larceny case, and NV Energy is repairing damaged equipment while assessing security. Clark County tightened scrap-wire rules, and crews have used aluminum to deter theft elsewhere.
