Management expects a near-term demand recovery supported by interest-rate cuts and China’s pro-growth measures, alongside continued copper investment.

title: Freeport Indonesia Requests Copper Concentrate Export Permit
summary: Freeport Indonesia asked the Indonesian government to relax its copper export ban and permit exports of 1.3 million tonnes of copper concentrate until December. The request is linked to its new smelter repairs after a fire in October. Easing the ban could lift concentrate supply expectations, pressuring copper prices.

title: Anglo American to sell nickel business for up to $500 million
summary: Anglo American said it will sell its nickel business to MMG for up to $500 million, including $350 million at completion and potential earnouts/cash tied to project development. The divested assets produce about 38,000 tonnes of nickel annually. The restructuring targets a focus on copper and iron ore.

title: Antofagasta celebrates copper demand as profit grows in 2024
summary: Antofagasta reported higher 2024 earnings, citing stronger copper demand and a higher realized copper price. Production rose slightly to 663,950 tonnes, while costs increased modestly. The company expects demand to remain strong and says supply is constrained by factors like grade decline and ore hardness.

title: Anglo American: sale of its nickel business to MMG -February 18, 2025 at 04:40 am EST
summary: Anglo American agreed to sell its nickel business to MMG, covering two ferronickel operations in Brazil and related growth projects, for up to $500 million (including an initial $350 million on completion and contingent payments). Management framed it as portfolio simplification, implying limited near-term effect on nickel output.

title: Anglo American to sell nickel business to MMG for up to USD500 million
summary: Anglo American agreed to sell its nickel business to MMG for $350 million on completion, plus a $100 million price-linked earnout and $50 million contingent payment tied to final investment decisions. The assets include ferronickel operations in Brazil and greenfield projects, as part of a portfolio simplification.

title: Anglo American to sell nickel business to China's MMG for up to US$500 million
summary: Anglo American said it will sell its nickel business to China’s MMG for up to US$500 million. The transaction could shift long-term nickel supply ownership and production strategy, but it is not an immediate disruption or demand shock, so near-term nickel price impact is likely limited.

title: The country that helped build Quebec's aluminum industry now threatens its survival
summary: The article highlights Trump’s planned 25% tariffs on all steel and aluminum imports and notes Quebec supplies about 65% of U.S. aluminum imports. That could disrupt Canada’s export-oriented aluminum smelting industry despite claims that cheap hydro power offers some resilience.

title: China's nonferrous metals industry association opposes U.S. additional tariffs on aluminum-Xinhua
summary: China’s nonferrous metals industry association said it is strongly dissatisfied with and opposes the U.S. decision to impose additional tariffs on aluminum products. The statement highlights an immediate trade policy risk for aluminum shipments between the two countries, which can influence near-term aluminum supply expectations and prices.

title: Trump Administration Issues Section 232 Tariffs On Steel And Aluminum: U.S. Considerations
summary: Trump’s administration reinstated and expanded Section 232 tariffs, including raising aluminum import tariffs to 25% from March 12, 2025 and revoking most country exemptions and product exclusions. The change directly affects aluminum import volumes and supply into the U.S., likely tightening availability and supporting prices near term.

title: Anglo American to sell nickel business for up to $500m
summary: Anglo American said it will sell its nickel business to MMG for up to $500m as part of restructuring away from nickel and toward copper and iron ore. The divested assets produce about 38,000 t/year of nickel. The company expects cash at completion plus earnouts tied to development.

title: China's copper imports from Congo climb by 71% year-on-year in 2024
summary: China’s refined copper imports from the DRC jumped 71% in 2024 to 1.48 million tonnes. Reuters attributes the rise to expanding Congo output, with Chinese operators dominating the copper belt and CMOC increasing production. The influx into China can weaken copper price outlook by boosting near-term supply expectations.

title: Carolina Rush Corporation: Carolina Rush Provides Exploration Update on Brewer Gold-Copper Project
summary: Carolina Rush provided an exploration update for its Brewer gold-copper project in South Carolina. In 2025 it plans a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate and a deep IP/MT geophysical survey, followed by deep drill targeting of porphyry copper-gold potential. It also evaluates critical minerals such as tellurium and gallium.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Pacific Ridge Plans to Drill RDP Copper-Gold Project Which Returned 107.2 metres of 1.39% Copper Equivalent or 2.06 g/t Gold Equivalent Within 497.2 metres of 0.66% Copper Equivalent or 0.97 g/t Gold Equivalent in an Earlie
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration announced plans to drill its RDP copper-gold project in B.C., following 2022 results including 107.2 m at 1.39% copper equivalent and 2023 follow-up drilling. The company cites improved permitting efforts tied to a tariff threat and raised financing for exploration; it provides no near-term supply changes.

title: Anglo American agrees $500m sale of nickel business
summary: Anglo American agreed to sell its nickel division to MMG Singapore Resources for up to $500m, including $350m upfront and price-linked payments. The deal follows nickel selling near a four-year low, blamed on Indonesia/China supply oversupply, a stronger US dollar, and softer electric-vehicle demand.

title: Quetzal Copper Limited: Quetzal Copper Announces Closing of Third Tranche of Financing
summary: Quetzal Copper closed the third tranche of a private placement to fund drill activities at its Princeton copper project in British Columbia, with proceeds from flow-through units renounced for exploration expenditures. The release includes financing details and does not signal any near-term production or supply disruption for copper beyond exploration spending.

title: Indonesia to develop nickel-based EV battery recycling plant by 2031-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia Battery Corporation (IBC) plans to build a nickel-based EV battery recycling plant by 2031, targeting recycling over 99% of components. The company says recycled nickel can be reused and should improve nickel availability and sustainability. While relevant to nickel, the long timeline suggests minimal near-term price impact.

title: Anglo American to sell nickel business for up to US$500-million
summary: Anglo American will sell its nickel business to MMG for up to $500 million, including Brazil ferronickel and development projects producing about 38,000 tonnes of nickel per year. The deal supports Anglo’s shift toward copper and iron ore, but the transfer is unlikely to immediately change physical nickel supply.

title: Philippines' planned nickel ore export ban raises concerns for RI smelters - Markets
summary: Indonesia relies heavily on Philippine nickel ore (about 97% of its imports). A proposed Philippines raw nickel export ban aimed at boosting domestic processing would threaten feedstock supply for Indonesian smelters. Experts urge diplomacy to secure alternative sources, but logistics and trade challenges could destabilize nickel supply and weigh on prices.

title: Chinese industry association opposes additional US tariffs on aluminum
summary: A Chinese industry association has publicly opposed additional US tariffs on aluminum. The stance suggests efforts to avoid further trade frictions and potential disruptions to aluminum flows between the US and China. This is likely to soften tariff-related downside risk for aluminum prices in the coming days.

title: Anglo to sell Brazilian nickel business to MMG
summary: Anglo American agreed to sell its Brazilian nickel operations (Barro Alto, Codemin, and greenfield projects) to MMG for up to $500mn, with expected closing by September. The deal includes cash, earnout, and development contingents. It signals portfolio shifts amid weaker Brazilian ferronickel imports to China.

title: How aluminum tariffs might impact local brewers
summary: The podcast discusses President Trump’s planned 25% tariffs on all aluminum (and steel) imports starting next month. Local craft breweries fear higher input costs, especially for aluminum cans used as taproom demand remains weak. Brewers expect they may need to absorb some margin pressure rather than fully pass costs to customers.

title: Argentina's Mendoza province open to mining and will build country's first new copper mine since 1997
summary: Argentina’s Mendoza province says it is open to mining and aims to develop copper projects, aided by the national RIGI investment incentive. The article cites an improving business environment and a pipeline of large copper projects, including the planned San Jorge mine expected to operate by 2027.

title: National Security Tariffs On Steel And Aluminum Imports
summary: The article says Presidential Proclamations reimpose and expand Section 232 national security tariffs on imported steel and aluminum starting March 12, 2025, increasing derivative aluminum duties and adding higher rates for Russia. It also removes product exclusion processes, potentially reducing imports and raising costs for fabricators in the near term.

title: Citi revises down 6-12 month copper forecast amid tariff concerns
summary: Citi lowered its 6-12 month copper forecast to $8,500/ton from $9,000, shifting expected price weakness later amid tariff uncertainty. The bank sees a small 2025 deficit, higher COMEX-LME one-year arbitrage, and modest end-use growth tempered by tariff and restrictive monetary policy headwinds.

title: Anglo American's strategic divestment: Nickel business sold to MMG Singapore
summary: Anglo American said it has agreed to sell its nickel business to MMG Singapore Resources for up to $500 million, covering two ferronickel operations in Brazil. The deal follows other divestments and is framed as cash generation, with no immediate evidence of reduced nickel output.

title: The Return of Steel and Aluminum Tariffs: Prelude to a Trade War? | Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP
summary: The U.S. issued new Section 232 proclamations raising/renewing import duties on aluminum and steel products to 25%, effective March 12, 2025, and ending many prior exemptions and exclusion processes. Trading partners may retaliate, but near-term the tariff change likely tightens U.S. aluminum availability and supports prices.

title: Trump's tariffs on aluminum, steel could crush San Diego's struggling craft breweries
summary: The article says Trump’s across-the-board 25% tariffs on imported aluminum (and steel) could financially “crush” San Diego craft breweries by raising costs for aluminum cans and other packaging. It notes aluminum can prices have already risen since earlier tariffs and supply shortages, increasing pressure on small producers’ margins.

title: White House Updates Section 232 Tariffs On Steel, Aluminum
summary: The White House issued an order adjusting Section 232 tariffs, reinstating a 25% tariff on steel imports effective March 12, 2025, and previewing similar action for aluminum. It ends exemptions/exclusions, expands coverage to more downstream derivatives, and tightens standards, potentially reducing import supply and supporting prices.

title: President Trump Modifies Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs | Arnall Golden Gregory LLP
summary: The article says President Trump issued updated Section 232 proclamations that modify existing steel and aluminum tariffs, changing duty rates, product coverage, and exemptions effective March 12, 2025. Higher or broadened aluminum import duties are likely to pressure near-term aluminum trade flows and U.S. aluminum prices.

title: Australian aluminium manufacturers brace for impact of Donald Trump's tariffs
summary: Australian aluminium producers are bracing for Donald Trump’s proposed 25% tariff on all aluminium and steel imports into the US by March 12. The firms fear disrupted trade flows, possible China dumping into alternative markets, and demand for anti-dumping duties or floor-price measures, creating near-term uncertainty for aluminium pricing.

title: BHP Interview: Dividends, Copper & M&A
summary: BHP’s CFO discusses weakening earnings and a trimmed dividend, while reaffirming a minimum 50% payout ratio. She highlights BHP’s copper growth plans, including Prominent Hill capex reassessment and increased copper volumes, arguing copper is central to future value creation. She also cites supportive India/China macro demand for metals.

title: The Impact of President Trump's Steel and Aluminum Tariffs on the Construction Industry | Gray Reed
summary: President Trump signed an order imposing 25% tariffs on all US steel and aluminum imports starting March 12, targeting major exporters including Canada. The construction industry—key consumer of both metals—faces higher input costs, supply chain disruption, and potential shortages, affecting bids and negotiations in coming weeks.

title: Indonesia's Amman Mineral Seeks Flexibility to Export Copper Concentrate
summary: PT Amman Mineral Nusa Tenggara asked Indonesia for flexibility to export copper concentrate. The miner says it has about 200,000 metric tons of concentrate inventory available, while its smelter runs at roughly 48% capacity. The request could affect near-term supply and shipment expectations for copper.

title: Freeport 'ready' to export 1.3m tonnes of copper concentrate this year - Companies
summary: Freeport Indonesia says it is ready to export about 1.3 million tonnes of copper concentrate this year, worth roughly $5 billion, but it is awaiting a government export permit extension after the prior permit expired. The ministry supports the extension, while noting it was delayed due to a recent smelter fire.

title: Australian fertilizer, copper, zinc rail line to reopen
summary: Flood-damaged Mount Isa rail line in Queensland is scheduled to reopen after earlier closure due to heavy rains. The route links phosphate and copper/zinc operations to the Port of Townsville. Glencore’s copper shipments via the line resume, easing transport bottlenecks that disrupted mine-to-port flows in early February.

title: EU envoys agree ban on Russian aluminium imports in new sanctions package
summary: EU envoys agreed on a new sanctions package that includes a ban on Russian aluminium imports. The measure is intended to reduce access for Russian metal to the EU market, tightening regional supply and shifting near-term pricing expectations for aluminium as buyers seek alternative sources.

title: How will Trump tariffs affect the Australian aluminium and steel industry?
summary: The report examines how Trump’s planned 25% tariffs on US steel and aluminium imports could disrupt global aluminium trade flows. Australian smelters and manufacturers fear margin pressure and risk of cheaper Chinese aluminium being redirected and potentially dumped. Tariff timing is March 12, with impacts uncertain but near-term uncertainty high.

title: Trump's aluminium tariff may force Coca-Cola to use more plastic bottles
summary: Trump’s 25% tariff on imported aluminium is expected to raise aluminium packaging costs for Coca-Cola. Management says it could increase use of PET bottles if aluminium cans get too expensive, although it downplays the overall cost impact. The change implies weaker near-term demand for aluminium packaging.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Corp.: First Atlantic Nickel Extends RPM Zone Discovery with a 400 Meter Step-Out Hole North, Intersecting 402 Meters of Visibly Disseminated Awaruite Nickel
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reports a 400-meter step-out drill hole (402 meters) intersecting continuous, disseminated visible awaruite nickel-iron alloy at its RPM Zone in Newfoundland, expanding the footprint and leaving mineralization open. The company also states Phase 2 is fully funded and permitted, targeting further step-outs.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Extends RPM Zone Discovery with a 400
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reports that RPM Hole 4 intersected 402 meters of continuous visible awaruite nickel-iron alloy mineralization, extending the RPM Zone to at least 400 meters long and 500 meters wide, with mineralization remaining open. Phase 2 drilling is fully funded and permitted, supporting further expansion.

title: Hayasa Metals Inc.: Hayasa Metals Announces Initial Drill Results and Final IP Sections at Urasar Copper-Gold Project
summary: Hayasa Metals reported initial geochemical results and final IP sections from drill holes at its Urasar copper-gold project in Armenia. Results show anomalous gold and copper and ubiquitous sulfide mineralization, though grades were below expectations. The company plans follow-up drilling that may target higher-potential zones north/upslope.

title: NiWest: the Australian project looking to defy the nickel downturn
summary: Alliance Nickel’s NiWest project in Western Australia has published a definitive feasibility study and claims low-cost, low-carbon nickel sulphate production with a ~10% premium over LME nickel. Despite a depressed nickel market tied to Indonesian supply, FID is not until ~Aug 2025, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Anglo American to sell nickel business to MMG for $500m
summary: Anglo American agreed to sell its Nickel Brazil ferronickel business (Barro Alto and Codemin) to MMG for up to $500m, with part of the consideration linked to future nickel prices. Operations are expected to transfer by Q3 2025 subject to approvals, implying limited short-term supply impact.

title: New EU sanctions package targets Russia's aluminum, shadow fleet
summary: EU envoys approved a 16th sanctions package targeting Russia, including a phased ban on primary aluminum imports into the EU. The measures also expand restrictions on circumvention through Russia’s shadow fleet and add more entities and individuals. The aluminum import ban is expected to tighten supply and support aluminum prices.

title: Koryx Copper Recognized as a Top 50 TSX Venture Exchange
summary: Koryx Copper was recognized on the TSX Venture Exchange “Top 50” list after strong 2024 share and market-cap growth. The release reiterates Koryx’s focus on its Haib copper project in Namibia and notes it is fully funded and executing a work program, but provides no new production or supply metrics.

title: EU's 16th package of sanctions targets aluminium, shadow fleet
summary: EU envoys agreed a 16th sanctions package on Russia that includes a ban on imports of primary Russian aluminium from a future effective date, with a limited 275,000 tonnes phase-in. The measures also tighten shipping and oil-related restrictions, but the aluminium ban is the key near-term price driver.

title: World Copper Ltd.: World Copper Enters into Letter Agreement to Sell Zonia Project
summary: World Copper announced a binding letter agreement to sell its interest in the Zonia copper project in Arizona for CAD $26 million, subject to due diligence, financing, and regulatory approvals. The transaction is expected to proceed via sale of shares of an Arizona subsidiary and includes staged payments and escrow provisions.

title: Proposed nickel export ban expected to help Philippines boost domestic processing industry
summary: The Philippines is considering a ban on exporting raw nickel ore to build domestic processing capacity, potentially starting after a five-year transition. Experts say this would concern Indonesia’s smelters, as most Indonesian nickel ore imports come from the Philippines, potentially tightening supply and raising international nickel prices and processing input costs.

title: Final Results | Company Announcement
summary: Rio Tinto reported strong 2024 financial results, noting that lower iron ore prices were partly offset by higher prices for LME copper and aluminium and improved volumes. The company also highlighted ongoing copper development at Oyu Tolgoi and benefits from portfolio diversification, supporting a constructive near-term sentiment for copper and aluminium markets.

title: Steel and Aluminum Tariff "Derivative Articles" Defined | Amundsen Davis LLC
summary: Federal registrar notices published Feb 14, 2025 define “derivative articles” covered by U.S. presidential proclamations imposing an extra 25% duty on imported steel and aluminum products. Annex I specifies HTSUS-based coverage and embedded-metal duty rules, with duties beginning March 12 after compliance system confirmation.

title: Steel and Aluminum Import Tariffs of 25% to Take Effect March 12; Reciprocal Tariffs Announced | Insights
summary: The U.S. will impose a 25% tariff on global aluminum imports effective March 12, reinstating Section 232 measures and terminating prior exemptions/exclusions. Coverage extends to aluminum derivative articles and may reach products tied to Russian smelting/casting with higher 200% duties. The new costs should support higher aluminum prices.

title: Top leadership changes in New Caledonia's nickel stakeholder
summary: Eramet announced leadership changes, with Christel Bories stepping down as CEO while remaining chair, and Paulo Castellari taking over. The focus includes Eramet’s SLN nickel mine/smelter in New Caledonia, where the group stated it is no longer financing SLN. Prior remarks questioned SLN’s competitiveness versus Indonesia.

title: President Trump Increases Tariffs On Steel And Aluminum
summary: Trump issued new Section 232 proclamations expanding U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs and tightening enforcement. Aluminum exemptions and exclusions are removed, downstream products are added, and the aluminum tariff rate is raised from 10% to 25%, effective March 12, 2025. Broader cost pressures could favor non-ferrous pricing.

title: President Trump Raises Steel and Aluminum Tariffs to 25%
summary: Trump signed proclamations raising U.S. steel and aluminum Section 232 tariffs to a flat 25% and eliminating exemptions, effective March 12, with potential stacking on other tariffs. The broad scope and lack of carveouts increase costs for downstream manufacturers and can pressure industrial demand, typically bearish for metal prices.

title: Family-owned businesses in Utah brace for impact of new steel, aluminum tariffs
summary: Utah family businesses say a 25% tariff on imported steel and aluminum is already prompting supplier price increases and may be passed through to their costs. A steel container maker highlights large steel input expenses, while a brewery buys many aluminum cans annually and expects higher beer pricing and tighter margins.

title: U.S. Aluminum Industry Navigates Tariff Changes
summary: U.S. aluminum prices have been rangebound on LME, but U.S. Midwest premiums have surged ahead of new tariff enforcement. A 25% tariff on aluminum/steel imports from Canada and Mexico is set to start March 1, with a broader 25% tariff on all steel and aluminum imports from March 12.

title: Copper region will drive the economy, Prime Minister says, yet mines stalling
summary: North-west Queensland copper operations are stalling, with several junior mines shut or mothballed after companies entered administration. Jobs and local businesses have been hit, while the government plans to streamline approvals. Separately, Glencore’s Mount Isa mine closure is imminent, highlighting looming copper supply risks.

title: Argentina's Milei likely to discuss US aluminum tariffs in Washington
summary: Argentina’s Milei is likely to discuss newly announced U.S. tariff hikes on steel and aluminum during a Washington visit. A Chubut governor said the 25% aluminum tariff (up from 10%) “doesn’t make sense,” arguing it harms Argentine industry and Aluar. U.S. imports under 4% of aluminum from Argentina.

title: RIO ASX: Fate of Rio Tinto's Tomago aluminium smelter uncertain after 2028 because of 'extremely expensive' power
summary: Rio Tinto said Australia’s Tomago aluminium smelter may be uneconomic beyond 2028 because offered power contracts are “extremely expensive,” and it wants a decision on the smelter’s fate within six months. The report also notes Glencore’s warning that high power prices threaten Queensland’s copper smelter.

title: Freeport Indonesia to pay higher duties on copper concentrate exports, Jakarta Post reports
summary: Freeport Indonesia is reported to face higher export duties on copper concentrate. The additional cost is likely to discourage some export volumes and reduce near-term concentrate supply availability, supporting tighter market expectations for copper within the coming days to weeks.

title: Govt to hike copper export levy after Freeport smelter fire - Companies
summary: Indonesia’s government says it will increase the export levy/penalties on PT Freeport Indonesia’s future copper concentrate shipments following a late-2023 fire that halted smelter operations. Exports may resume in stages, but with higher duties than before, with the final rate to be set later this month.

title: Strategx Elements Corp.: StrategX Discovers High-Grade Copper at East Arm, Great Slave Lake, Northwest Territories, Canada
summary: StrategX Elements Corp. announced high-grade copper discovery at its East Arm project after surface sampling returned up to 10.1% Cu, plus elevated silver, and added 6,425 hectares of claims. The company plans petrography, geochemical/geophysical surveys, and drill target definition, signaling potential new copper supply.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers' strike escalates over pay deductions | Newcastle Herald
summary: Workers at Rio Tinto-backed Tomago Aluminium are preparing additional stoppages after contract talks broke down. The AWU alleges extra docked pay from a prior action. The smelter produces about 600,000 tonnes and is highly electricity intensive, so ongoing disruptions raise short-term supply concerns for aluminium.

title: Tariff threat: US had asked Australia to ship more aluminium, says Rio Tinto CEO
summary: Rio Tinto CEO Jakob Stausholm says the US asked Australia for more aluminium exports after Russia’s supply was curtailed post-Ukraine. The risk is a proposed 25% tariff on imported aluminium, which could reduce US-bound supply and weigh on near-term aluminium prices. Copper and nickel are not discussed.

title: Rio Tinto propels profits with strong copper sales
summary: Rio Tinto reported higher 2024 net profit, attributing resilience in part to stronger copper sales as copper LME prices averaged about 8% higher. The company contrasts this with weaker iron ore amid China’s property slowdown, and it plans to ramp copper output at Oyu Tolgoi in Mongolia.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers' strike escalates over pay deductions | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Workers at Tomago Aluminium in Australia are escalating a dispute over pay deductions and enterprise agreement terms. Another six-hour strike is planned from 2am Sunday and a three-hour stoppage next Tuesday. Tomago produces about 600,000 tonnes annually and is a major power consumer, so interruptions can affect near-term aluminium supply.

title: Update on Konkola West Copper Project  | Company Announcement
summary: Tertiary Minerals provides a drilling update on the Konkola West Copper Project in Zambia, where KoBold is earning into the right to explore and drill deep copperbelt targets. Hole KWDD001 has advanced to 2,600m with planned 3,000m depth, and timing for a second hole is extended by four months.

title: Can Trump's Steel, Aluminum Tariffs Revive US Manufacturing Dominance?
summary: The article says Trump imposed 25% steel and aluminum tariffs to protect domestic producers and restore trade “fairness.” With US duties directly targeting aluminium imports, market participants may expect tighter supply and higher domestic aluminium prices over the coming days as import costs rise.

title: How Trump's tariffs on steel and aluminum could hit you at the grocery store
summary: Trump’s planned 25% tariff on imported aluminum—paired with removal of prior exemptions—could raise the cost of making U.S. aluminum beverage cans. Industry experts warn manufacturers will face higher input prices and pass them to consumers at the grocery store, tightening supply expectations for aluminum.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers' strike escalates over pay deductions | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Tomago Aluminium workers at the Rio Tinto-backed smelter plan further six-hour and three-hour stoppages after negotiations for a new enterprise agreement broke down. The AWU alleges management docked extra pay during prior action. The smelter is electricity-intensive and supplies large volumes, making disruptions plausibly bearish for aluminium in the near term.

title: Canada's Teck beats fourth-quarter profit estimates on strong copper production
summary: Teck Resources beat fourth-quarter profit estimates, driven by higher copper production volumes at its Quebrada Blanca mine in Chile. Output rose to 122,100 tonnes (+19% y/y), and the company expects 2025 copper production of 490,000–565,000 tonnes with potential further throughput gains of 10–15% from debottlenecking.

title: METLEN secures long-term deals with Rio Tinto for bauxite and alumina
summary: METLEN signed long-term agreements with Rio Tinto for 14.9Mt of bauxite from Guinea and 3.9Mt of alumina offtake to 2037/2027-35. The deals support METLEN’s expanded Agios Nikolaos refinery, with alumina production ramping from 2027, boosting perceived alumina supply security for aluminium.

title: Teck Resources tops fourth-quarter profit estimates on strong copper production
summary: Teck reported a sharp swing to profit, citing record copper production (122,000 tonnes) helped by strong performance at Quebrada Blanca in Chile. The firm said potential U.S. tariffs would be managed via rerouted trade flows, with management expecting demand support from electrification and urbanization.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Announces Positive Metallurgical Results and Confirms High Copper Recovery Through Coarse Grind and Flotation
summary: Faraday Copper reported positive metallurgical test results for its Copper Creek project, including ~95% sulphide rougher copper recoveries using coarse particle flotation and potential reductions in grinding energy and higher throughput. The company plans to use the data for future technical studies, but no near-term production changes are indicated.

title: Koryx Copper Announces Multiple Higher-Grade Drill Results
summary: Koryx Copper reported multiple higher-grade Cu-equivalent drill intersections from its Phase 2 program at the Haib copper project in Namibia, including several long, near-surface intervals. Remaining assays are expected within weeks and drilling rigs are expanding. The release is exploration-focused, suggesting improved resource potential, not immediate supply changes.

title: Gold-Rich Cobalt-Copper Mineralization at CAS Property
summary: Electra Battery Materials updates exploration results at the CAS property in Idaho’s cobalt belt, describing historical drilling with gold plus cobalt, and stating recent sampling found multiple anomalous gold, copper, and cobalt zones. The news supports potential future copper resources but does not imply immediate production or supply changes.

title: VR Resources Completes Drilling at Silverback Copper-Gold
summary: VR Resources reports completion of its first winter drill program at the Silverback copper-gold project, intersecting shearing, alteration, veining and sulfide-bearing textures, and planning follow-up once assays arrive. The geological model also references nickel mineralization in mafic-ultramafic dykes, but no copper/nickel results or supply changes are provided.

title: Sundaram-Clayton to divest aluminium die-casting bizz
summary: Sundaram-Clayton said its board approved plans to divest its aluminium die-casting business at the Hosur facility. High- and low-pressure die-casting operations will be bought by third parties, subject to approvals, but buyers and deal terms are undisclosed. The move could affect its aluminium processing footprint.

title: Steel And Aluminum Import Tariffs Of 25% To Take Effect March 12; Reciprocal Tariffs Announced
summary: The U.S. reinstated 25% tariffs on global steel imports and raised aluminum import duties from 10% to 25% effective March 12, ending prior exemptions and product exclusions. The tariffs apply to derivative products and can add duties atop existing AD/CV charges, likely weighing on aluminum-related demand expectations near term.

title: Teck Resources reports Q4 profit and record copper production
summary: Teck reported a swing to profit and record copper output (122,000 tonnes) alongside reduced debt. Management said possible U.S. tariffs would prompt it to reroute some refined products’ trade flows, but expects limited overall impact. Demand outlook remains supported by electrification, keeping copper bias modest.

title: Teck Resources reports Q4 profit and record copper production | iNFOnews | Thompson-Okanagan's News Source
summary: Teck Resources reported a $385 million Q4 profit and record copper production of 122,000 tonnes. CEO Jonathan Price said potential U.S. tariffs would be mitigated through alternative trade routes for copper concentrates and other refined products. The update supports copper output sentiment, but no direct near-term supply cut is indicated.

title: Teck open to deal with Glencore around combining Chile copper mines
summary: Teck’s CEO said the company is open to combining its QB2 copper mine in Chile with Glencore’s neighboring Collahuasi. The tie-up could generate large cost savings and improve processing and ramp-up efficiency. QB2’s output is expected to rise, and markets may react positively to improved copper economics.

title: Trump aluminum tariffs to hit 123 areas, including chip equipment
summary: Additional U.S. aluminum tariffs are scheduled to begin on March 12 and will cover 123 aluminum-related products, including parts used in chip equipment and aircraft components. The move is expected to hurt Japanese exporters supplying the U.S., likely weighing on near-term aluminum demand expectations and prices.

title: Aluminium exports to US may drop due to 25% tariff
summary: The US may impose a flat 25% tariff on aluminium imports from March 12, ending lower levies and country exemptions. India’s aluminium exports to the US could fall as buyers shift to local secondary/scrap. Indirectly, India’s imported US scrap supply also faces pressure, affecting secondary alloys output.

title: Across-the-Board 25-Percent Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum | DLA Piper
summary: The article says the US will impose across-the-board 25% tariffs on steel and aluminum imports under Section 232, revoking prior country and product exemptions effective March 12, 2025. Aluminum’s duty rises from 10% to 25% and exclusions are eliminated, aiming to address excess capacity and national-security concerns.

title: Trump's steel and aluminum tariffs | A&O Shearman
summary: Trump issued Section 232 steel and aluminum tariff proclamations effective March 12, 2025, revising duty rates and limiting relief/exclusions for covered derivative products. The measures are aimed at imported aluminum articles and can reduce import inflows and increase landed costs in the U.S., potentially supporting aluminum prices over the next weeks.

title: Trump's Steel And Aluminum Tariffs
summary: President Trump issued Section 232 proclamations reimposing blanket additional tariffs on imported aluminum (and derivative aluminum) into the US, with effects slated for March 12, 2025. The measures rescind prior exemptions/quotas and limit Commerce’s ability to grant relief, increasing uncertainty and import costs for aluminum supply.

title: Anglo American signs $5bn deal with Codelco for Chilean copper mines
summary: Anglo American signed an MOU with Codelco to jointly optimise adjacent Los Bronces and Andina copper mines in Chile. The plan targets efficiency gains and higher fine copper production (about 120,000 tonnes annually), with shared profits and limited additional capex. Final agreements depend on permits and approvals in H2 2025.

title: Announcement on the Quotation of New 8mm Oxygen-Free Copper Rod Export Processing Fee (FOB) [SMM Price Release Announcement]
summary: SMM announced that it will launch weekly quotations for the export processing fee (FOB) of 8mm oxygen-free copper rods (TU1/TU2) starting March 7, 2025. The notice explains the methodology, price ranges, and publication timing, following changes in copper semis export tax rebates.

title: Copper Cathodes Export Window Rapidly Open： How Does the Environment Differ from 2024?
summary: LME copper spreads returned to backwardation, worsening SHFE import margins for copper cathodes and reopening the export profit window versus May 2024. With copper concentrate supply tight and negative treatment charges, arbitrage and smelter hedging should raise electrolytic copper exports, likely smaller than last year, weighing on copper prices.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market-2.21
summary: SMM reports Indonesian nickel ore domestic trade premiums rising, with supply disruptions from rainy season, Ramadan timing, and SIMBARA enforcement tightening compliant ore flows. Active procurement after incomplete inventories is lifting premiums. Higher ore costs support high-grade NPI prices and narrow smelter losses, while refined nickel supply ramps continue.

title: High-Grade Nickel Pig Iron Prices Surge Amid Supply Constraints and Improved Market Sentiment
summary: High-grade nickel pig iron prices rose sharply amid supply constraints: nickel pig iron smelters operate at losses and some Indonesian lines run at low capacity. Demand sentiment for stainless steel is improving, traders are buying as the NPI discount versus electrolytic nickel narrows, and macro signals support pure nickel, though downstream demand remains soft.

title: Marula Mining updates on Kinusi copper mine operations
summary: Marula Mining provided an update on Tanzania’s Kinusi copper mine, saying preparations are underway for sales of high-grade copper concentrates. The company will take additional check samples and review QA/QC, while a trading group and logistics providers finalize transport to a bonded warehouse in Dar es Salaam ahead of potential sales.

title: China's Norinco sweetens bid for Congo copper mines as deal stalls, sources say
summary: Norinco has sweetened its bid for Chemaf’s Congo copper assets by offering terms that raise the DRC government’s stake, keeping Norinco majority interest, and sharing metal proceeds. The deal has stalled amid Gecamines’ competing bid, but revised terms could help finalize financing and mine expansion.

title: The Impact of U.S. Steel and Aluminum Tariffs: What You Need to Know | Mintz - ML Strategies
summary: The U.S. signed proclamations to close steel and aluminum tariff exemptions, restoring a 25% tariff on steel and elevating the aluminum tariff to 25%. The administration says this will curb loopholes, deter dumping, and support national security, with potential retaliation and higher imported input costs.

title: Southern Copper : 4Q24 Conference Call transcript -February 21, 2025 at 11:38 am EST
summary: Southern Copper’s 4Q24 call updated views on the LME copper market: it expects demand growth ~4%, supply growth ~3%, and a market deficit of about 250,000 tons with inventories covering roughly one week of demand. summary: Trump reinstated Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum imports, raising the aluminum duty to 25%. A derivative tariff list followed in the Federal Register, but aluminum printing plates were excluded, so no new tariffs apply to those plates from other countries beyond existing Kodak-related measures.

title: Mass. craft breweries worry costs of new steel, aluminum tariffs could shift to consumers
summary: Massachusetts craft brewers say a new 25% tariff on foreign steel and aluminum will raise their material and equipment costs, especially for aluminum beer cans. Brewers expect they’ll pass higher costs to customers via higher beer prices. They cite aluminum added per can and annual expense increases tied to the tariff.

title: Việt Nam still has a chance to export steel and aluminium to US despite tariffs
summary: The US imposed 25% tariffs on imported steel and aluminium, but Vietnamese shipments remain resilient. Experts expect limited changes to competitive dynamics, though exporters may face margin pressure and adjust pricing, costs, and product origin compliance. Aluminium exports to the US grew in 2024, yet tariffs still signal softer short-term demand.

summary: Gogebic County and multiple local bodies continue backing Highland Copper’s Copperwood Mine project. Highland argues the project is fully permitted and environmentally stringent, supporting future copper supply expectations.

title: EU Sees €28 Billion Hit From Trump's Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The piece (based on the title) reports the EU expects a major economic impact from Trump’s steel and aluminum tariffs, citing a €28 billion hit. title: Copper Bottom review – a green marvel in every sense
summary: A review of “Copper Bottom,” a house clad almost entirely in recycled copper, highlighting solar panels, a heat pump, and copper’s long life and thin application. title: U.P. Communities Stand Behind Proposed Copperwood Mine
summary: Local communities and county bodies in Michigan’s western Upper Peninsula reaffirm support for Highland Copper’s Copperwood mine, citing economic benefits and improvements to roads and broadband. title: Workers strike at Tomago aluminium smelter as tariffs loom
summary: Workers at Australia’s Tomago aluminium smelter (Rio Tinto) began an 8-hour strike stoppage on Sunday. The walkout adds to existing stress in the aluminium industry as the US considers potential tariffs. Reduced smelter output can tighten near-term supply expectations and pressure aluminium prices.

title: Noronex JV kicks up significant Namibian copper-silver hits
summary: Noronex and South32 have extended mineralisation at the Fiesta copper-silver project in Namibia, reporting multiple high-grade copper intercepts including 33m at 0.8% copper. summary: Bloomberg discusses BHP’s shift toward copper, citing a looming deficit and energy-transition demand. summary: Hindalco signed an MoU with Madhya Pradesh to invest Rs 15,000 crore over two years, expanding its aluminium presence in the state. summary: Hindalco signed an MoU with Madhya Pradesh to invest Rs 15,000 crore over two years to expand aluminium smelting capacity. summary: Barrick outlined plans to expand Zambia’s Lumwana copper mine, targeting higher output capacity over time. summary: First Quantum hopes Panama will approve the mine’s preservation and safety plan so it can export about 120,000 tonnes of copper concentrate accumulated since the Cobre Panama shutdown in late 2023.
