title: Internet, phone service restored in Greene County after copper theft causes outage
summary: Greene County internet and phone service for 520 residents was restored after thieves stole telecommunications fiber and copper cable, disrupting network connectivity. The report notes prior copper thefts and includes a snapshot of copper at $4.62/lb. It also references an inquiry into copper imports for possible tariffs.

title: Mine copper without destroying the planet? London-based project gives scientists hope
summary: A London-based research centre funded by Rio Tinto will develop “responsible” ways to source and extract copper, including geothermal-powered brine mining and plant-bacterial systems to recover copper from contaminated soil. The piece highlights copper’s role in electrification and net-zero, but offers no immediate production or trade change.

title: Canadian homebuilders say U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminum would hurt more than they did in 2018
summary: Canadian homebuilders warn that new U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum could revive pandemic-era construction cost spikes. The levies, potentially layered to higher rates, would raise prices for materials and fixtures sourced across North America, worsening an already weak preconstruction market and likely dampening near-term metal demand.

title: Why Trump's aluminum tariffs won't raise the price of your can of Coke
summary: The article says Trump’s 25% aluminum/steel import tariff is unlikely to significantly raise consumer soda prices because large beverage firms can adjust packaging mixes, shift production lines, and absorb margin impacts. It notes aluminum prices rose over 4% after the announcement, but suggests effects on aluminum pricing are limited and manageable.

title: Weekly Ratings, Targets, Forecast Changes - 28-02-25
summary: FNArena’s broker ratings roundup includes Chalice Mining commentary on a Gonneville metallurgical breakthrough. Morgans says saleable copper and nickel concentrates can now be produced from low-grade composites, removing a complex hydromet process and reducing development risk and expected costs. The target was cut, but the project outlook improved.

title: Navarro targets Australia in US aluminium tariff debate | Stock & Land
summary: US trade adviser Peter Navarro argues Australia’s aluminium exports benefit from unfair dumping and supports lifting tariffs to 25% for broader application. The article notes negotiations over possible exemptions for Australian steel and aluminium ahead of March 12. Uncertainty around import restrictions adds downside pressure to aluminium pricing sentiment.

title: Navarro targets Australia in US aluminium tariff debate | Farm Weekly
summary: US trade adviser Peter Navarro argues Australia’s aluminium exports are dumped below cost, ahead of March 12 when Trump’s planned 25% aluminium tariffs are set to start without exemptions. Negotiations over potential carve-outs remain uncertain. The prospect of tighter US import supply supports near-term bullish aluminium price expectations.

title: Navarro targets Australia in US aluminium tariff debate | North Queensland Register
summary: White House adviser Peter Navarro argues Australia’s aluminium smelters sell below cost, pushing for tougher US treatment as 25% aluminium tariffs are set to start March 12. Australia seeks an exemption but US officials and negotiations appear uncertain, which could reduce supply into the US market.

title: Navarro targets Australia in US aluminium tariff debate | The Land
summary: White House adviser Peter Navarro argues Australia has an unfair dumping advantage in aluminium and criticizes a carve-out debate ahead of scheduled US 25% aluminium tariffs on March 12. Negotiations are uncertain, with officials warning a potential lack of exemption could restrict imports and affect the US market.

title: Navarro targets Australia in US aluminium tariff debate | Queensland Country Life
summary: Peter Navarro argues Australia benefits from unfairly priced aluminium dumping and urges tougher US action as 25% aluminium tariffs are set to take effect March 12. Negotiations over possible exemptions are uncertain, with officials citing industry survival and recent export surges, raising immediate aluminium price and import-flow expectations.

title: Navarro targets Australia in US aluminium tariff debate | Stock Journal
summary: Peter Navarro argues Australia has an unfair advantage in selling below-cost aluminium and supports Trump’s move to raise US aluminium tariffs to 25% from March 12, removing country exemptions. Uncertainty around whether Australia gets a carve-out could tighten perceived US supply and support aluminium price expectations.

title: Trump tariffs: US trade chief slams Australia for 'frontal assault' on US aluminium sector
summary: Trump trade adviser Peter Navarro criticises Australia for subsidised aluminium dumping and argues for 25% US tariffs on steel and aluminium. The US seeks to limit imports before charges start next Wednesday, while Australia negotiates an exemption. The tariff outlook and import cost pressure are supportive for aluminium prices.

title: LME copper rises on weaker dollar and strong China data
summary: LME copper rose after the dollar weakened and data from China came in strong. The Reuters note links the gain to improving demand expectations for industrial metals and a more favorable currency backdrop for dollar-priced commodities, supporting upward near-term price momentum for copper.

title: US Initiates an Investigation Under Section 232 of Trade Expansion Act on Effect of Copper Imports on National Security
summary: The US initiated a Section 232 investigation into the impact of copper imports on national security, covering mined copper, concentrates, refined copper, alloys and scrap. The Commerce review could recommend tariffs, export controls and domestic incentives. Expectations of restrictive measures are likely to support near-term copper prices.

title: Worried Trump's aluminum tariffs will raise prices on canned drinks and metal appliances? Here's what to expect.<!-- -->
summary: The article says Trump’s new 25% tariffs on steel and aluminum from all countries, effective March 4, could raise costs for products such as canned drinks and metal appliances. An economist expects limited consumer price impact depending on implementation, but the tariff directly pressures aluminum supply costs and pricing expectations.

title: JP Morgan sees copper prices at $11,000/mt in 2026, 10% tariffs by late 3Q25
summary: JP Morgan expects the refined copper market to remain in deficit and forecasts copper averaging about $11,000/mt in 2026. It also expects U.S. copper import tariffs of at least 10% by late 3Q25, with risk of 25%, noting possible U.S. pre-tariff inventory builds could tighten supply elsewhere.

title: [SMM Nickel Ore Real-Time Market] Adjustment to the Calculation Method of Indonesian Nickel Ore HPM Price
summary: Indonesia’s ESDM issued decrees revising the HMA/HPM benchmark-price calculation method for metallic minerals, including nickel ore, NPI and MHP, effective March 1, 2025. The first-period March reference nickel HMA and resulting HPM nickel-ore prices for various grades were published, with potential second-period prices later in March.

title: Junior explorer Kingsrose acquires Jakon nickel project in Finland
summary: Kingsrose completed a 100% acquisition of the Jakon nickel-copper-cobalt project in Finland from Rio Tinto, expanding its position in the Kotalahti belt. The project is near the former Hitura nickel-copper mine and has historical nickel-copper sulphide intercepts. Payments are mostly deferred and contingent on a future FID.

title: Panama's $10 Billion Copper Mine Faces Tough Road to Restart
summary: The piece focuses on Panama’s large copper mine and highlights difficulties in getting the project restarted. If restart timelines slip, copper supply expectations can be reduced in the near term, potentially weighing on prices as traders reassess availability versus demand.

title: Why Trump's move to boost the U.S. copper market is a 'pipe dream' that could raise prices<!-- -->
summary: An executive order directs the U.S. Commerce Department to investigate whether copper imports pose a national security threat and to recommend mitigating actions such as tariffs, export controls, or incentives to expand domestic mining. With much of U.S. copper sourced from Chile, Canada, and Mexico, the prospect of restrictions could lift copper prices.

title: New GIADEC CEO optimistic about the aluminium industry's contribution to economic recovery
summary: GIADEC’s new acting CEO in Ghana said the integrated aluminium industry can significantly support the economy and emphasized developing the full aluminium value chain, including refiners, to fully harness bauxite resources. While focused on long-term integration and partner selection, it supports bullish expectations for aluminium.

title: Trump Initiates an Investigation Into Potential National Security Threat of Copper Imports | Snell & Wilmer
summary: President Trump issued an Executive Order initiating a Section 232 national-security investigation into copper imports due to U.S. reliance on foreign smelting and refining capacity. The review will assess demand, domestic supply capability, and risks such as export restrictions and “suppressed” prices from dumping/overproduction, with potential recommendations for tariffs or quotas.

title: Anglo American sells off nickel business for US$500m
summary: Anglo American sold its Brazilian nickel operations and developing projects for $500m, citing a highly competitive market dominated by Indonesia’s growing ferronickel output. The piece notes nickel prices have fallen for two years due to oversupply. Despite the transaction, it signals portfolio change more than immediate market supply disruption.

title: U.S. Investigates Copper Imports Under New Trump Executive Order
summary: A new U.S. Trump executive order directs a Section 232 investigation into copper imports (including scrap and derivative products). The review will assess domestic capacity, demand, subsidies/dumping, and risks from export restrictions by concentrated smelting supply. Possible import curbs could tighten supply expectations and support copper prices.

title: President Trump Announces 25% Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum | Torres Trade Law, PLLC
summary: Trump administration proclamations reinstate 25% tariffs on all steel and aluminum imports from all countries under Section 232, effective March 12, 2025, with expanded coverage to certain downstream derivative products. The measures revoke prior exclusions, add CBP enforcement, and may delay imports, supporting aluminum prices while indirectly influencing copper demand expectations.

title: Doug Ford threatens to stop nickel shipments to U.S. on eve of trade war
summary: Doug Ford threatened to stop nickel shipments to the U.S. on the eve of a trade war. The move implies potential disruption of cross-border nickel supply flows into the U.S., increasing trade risk and uncertainty for near-term nickel availability and pricing.

title: Decoding aluminium's carbon challenge
summary: The piece argues aluminium’s smelting emissions are difficult to capture because CO2 is highly diluted, driving pressure for low-carbon product differentiation. It notes procurement policies requiring carbon footprints and downstream demand from auto makers. It suggests companies will compete to meet constraints, potentially tightening low-carbon aluminium supply.

title: Indonesia's Nickel Boom Is Forcing Its Own Smelters to Shut Down
summary: The report says Indonesia’s “nickel boom” has pushed conditions such that local nickel smelters are being forced to shut down. This implies lower near-term nickel refining volumes and potentially tighter market supply, which typically supports nickel prices in the following days to weeks.

title: Doug Ford says he will stop nickel shipments if U.S. imposes tariffs
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Ontario will stop nickel shipments to the U.S. if the U.S. imposes proposed tariffs on Canadian goods. He also mentioned stockpiling nickel and potential additional retaliation measures. The threatened disruption is directly linked to near-term nickel supply flows to the U.S.

title: 'It will shut down manufacturing': Ontario will stop nickel shipments to U.S. if tariffs imposed, Doug Ford says
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford said the province would stop nickel shipments into the U.S. if U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods take effect, adding nickel stockpiling and retaliatory procurement legislation. The threat implies an immediate reduction in nickel supply available to U.S. buyers, likely tightening balances and pressuring prices higher for nickel.

title: Strickland picks up big sniffs of Serbian copper-gold porphyry find
summary: Strickland Metals says its drill rig intercepted ~493m of porphyry-related veining and alteration at Jezerska Reka in Serbia, including a 412m interval averaging 130 ppm copper from 300m depth. The company is planning further drilling to define a large-scale copper-gold system, which can support copper sentiment.

title: Addressing The Threat To National Security From Imports Of Copper (Trump EO Tracker)
summary: A Trump executive order directs a Section 232 investigation into the effects of copper imports on U.S. national security, including scrap and refined copper. The Commerce Department must assess demand in defense/energy/infrastructure, domestic smelting capacity, and supplier risks, with recommendations that may include tariffs or quotas within months.

title: Copperwood Mine secures updated air quality permit — with more testing, limits | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Michigan’s environment agency issued an updated air-quality permit for the proposed Copperwood underground mine, adding stricter testing and emission limits for mine vents and natural-gas emergency generators. The approval lets the project continue moving forward, supporting expectations for future copper supply, though funding remains uncertain.

title: 148m Copper Intersect at Mont Agoma | Company Announcement
summary: Rome Resources reports assay results from Mont Agoma showing a 148m copper-rich intercept averaging 0.35% Cu (with multiple higher-grade sub-sections) alongside tin and zinc. The update strengthens perceived copper prospect scale and continuity, potentially improving near-term market expectations for future copper supply, though production impact is not yet realized.

title: Uganda signs maiden production sharing deal to revive copper mine
summary: Uganda signed its first production sharing agreement to redevelop the mothballed Kilembe copper and cobalt mine near the DRC border. The deal targets production of copper cathodes and cobalt, following past shutdowns due to low copper prices and instability. Restart prospects may modestly support copper sentiment despite limited immediate output.

title: Canada Nickel signs agreement with First Nations for Crawford Nickel Project
summary: Canada Nickel announced an agreement with Wabun Tribal Council First Nations for the Crawford Nickel Project, including an early Impact Benefits Agreement framework and priority access for First Nations businesses. The company also released FEED outcomes, revising initial capital costs and adjusting the mining schedule to bring forward higher-value East Zone ore.

title: PAN GLOBAL COMMENCES DRILLING AT BRAVO TARGET IN THE ESCACENA COPPER-TIN PROJECT, SPAIN
summary: Pan Global Resources started drilling at the Bravo target within its Escacena copper-tin project in southern Spain, using gravity and IP geophysics to test for VMS mineralization. Up to eight drillholes are planned in a larger 7,000m multi-target program, with results to follow.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Corp.: First Atlantic Nickel Reports New Discovery at RPM Zone: Intersects 0.24% Nickel & 0.32% Chromium Over 383.1 Meters, 10km Downstrike from Super Gulp
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reported initial assays from its RPM Zone at the Atlantic Nickel Project, including 0.24% average nickel over 383.1 meters and consistent visible awaruite across a 500m x 400m area, with metallurgical testing underway. Phase 2 drilling is planned to expand depth and footprint.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Reports New Discovery at RPM Zone:
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reports initial assay results from the RPM Zone, including consistent nickel mineralization (up to 0.31% Ni over 383.1m; with chromium) and visible awaruite across a 500m x 400m footprint. Phase 2 drilling and DTR metallurgical testing are planned, supporting bullish nickel sentiment despite early-stage status.

title: Metals Creek Resources Corp.: Metals Creek Secures Diamond Drill for the Tillex Copper Project
summary: Metals Creek Resources says it has secured a diamond drill for its Tillex Copper Project and expects drilling to start mid-to-late March, targeting chalcopyrite-bearing mineralized units. The prior drill returned strong copper grades, but this is early-stage exploration with no immediate production impact.

title: Canada Nickel signs landmark agreement with First Nations for Crawford project
summary: Canada Nickel has signed a landmark agreement with First Nations for its Crawford project, prioritising First Nations businesses and recognising their role in the partnership. The article is focused on stakeholder inclusion and business participation rather than any immediate change in nickel production, supply, or inventories.

title: [SMM In-Depth Analysis] New Regulations Again? Impact of Numerous New Indonesian Policies on the Nickel Market
summary: Indonesia’s ESDM issued guidelines and March 2025 reference prices that change nickel-related benchmark calculations (HMA/HPM), including shifting to semi-monthly revisions and aligning valuation windows to LME spot. The rules may function as a floor for settlements and potentially affect export pricing via tariffs/tax, supporting near-term nickel expectations.

title: Ontario threatens to cut nickel and power over Trump tariffs
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he may cut nickel shipments to the U.S. and hints at reducing electricity exports after the U.S. announces 25% tariffs on Canadian and Mexican goods. Because Ontario supplies a large share of U.S. nickel needs, the threat implies potential short-term supply tightness and price support.

title: Copperhead Resources Inc.: Copperhead Resources Closes First Tranche of Private Placement
summary: Copperhead Resources Inc. closed the first tranche of a private placement, raising $92,250 via 1.23 million common shares at $0.075 per share for working capital. The release provides no project or production guidance or metal supply/demand changes, so near-term impacts on copper, nickel, or aluminium prices appear limited.

title: Bayhorse Silver Inc.: Bayhorse Silver Extends Bayhorse Breccia Zone From 90 M (300ft) Downhole to 318 M (1050 ft) Reports Anomalous Copper-Zinc Assay Results From The First 115 M Of The Breccia Zone, And Preliminary IP Results
summary: Bayhorse Silver Inc. reports drill results from hole BH24-01 showing continuous anomalous copper (up to 125 ppm) and zinc in the upper portion of a breccia zone, with chalcopyrite noted. Preliminary IP results highlight chargeability and low-resistance targets within VTEM anomalies, suggesting possible copper porphyry-related mineralization.

title: Trump's trade adviser says Australia is waging a 'frontal assault' on US aluminium markets. What's really going on? | Donald Trump
summary: Donald Trump’s trade adviser Peter Navarro criticized Australia’s “heavily subsidised smelters,” alleging unfair dumping and a “frontal assault” on the US aluminium market. The comments come as Australia seeks an exemption from new US steel and aluminium tariffs. Scrutiny of subsidies and exemption odds could pressure aluminium trade expectations and prices.

title: UBS Predicts More U.S. Copper Price Volatility Amid Tariff Uncertainty
summary: UBS notes a widening gap between U.S. copper prices and international benchmarks as tariff uncertainty increases. U.S. copper is reported up 13% versus an 8% rise on the LME, with U.S. premiums surging sharply, implying heightened local supply-demand tightness and volatility in the near term.

title: Harmony's gold, copper strategy aims for profitability and diversification
summary: Harmony Gold Mining says its diversification strategy—focused on gold and copper—aims to improve profitability, citing international copper (Eva project) and expansion/realignment of projects and investments (including Hidden Valley and other facilities). It argues strong copper and gold fundamentals support demand and margins, implying mildly bullish copper sentiment.

title: Quebec aluminum plant stops production after Trump tariffs
summary: A Quebec union says Alubar Métaux in Bécancour shut down after Trump’s 25% tariffs on Canadian goods, citing potential aluminum-rod tariff targeting effective March 12. The company calls it temporary maintenance, but the news signals near-term export-demand disruption risk from higher U.S. tariff costs, likely weighing on aluminum sentiment.

title: Doug Ford to withhold nickel from U.S. battery supply chain
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford said he intends to disrupt the U.S. battery supply chain by stockpiling Canadian nickel and stopping nickel shipments into the U.S., which he claims could shut down manufacturing. Canada is a major supplier to the U.S.; the implied supply cut is bullish for nickel prices.

title: Commerce Issues Modifications to Tariff Schedule to Implement Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce released Federal Register notices to modify the HTSUS to implement the President’s February 10 steel and aluminum tariffs. Notices publish March 5 and most tariff rates take effect March 12, with aluminium derivative products in Chapters 76/73 covered on that date.

title: Aluminum manufacturer to close Quebec plant following Trump tariffs
summary: A Quebec aluminum electrical cable maker (Alubar) temporarily closed its Bécancour plant after U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports took effect, with management later saying it would reopen. The plant’s output is largely shipped to the U.S., and the tariffs also add to planned aluminum-specific levies, raising short-term uncertainty.

title: Copper miner Teck seeking metal buyers outside U.S.
summary: Teck CEO Jonathan Price criticized U.S. inflation-fuelling tariffs on metals and said the curbs will push the industry to seek buyers outside the U.S., with Teck reserving port and warehousing capacity to export to Asia. Teck shares fell after tariff news, and Teck’s copper is largely shipped to Asia.

title: Copperwood Mine Project gets new air quality permit
summary: Highland Copper’s Copperwood Mine Project in Michigan received a new air-quality permit from EGLE, replacing one approved in 2018 and adding emissions testing conditions. The project still needs $50M in state funding before proceeding, so the near-term effect on copper supply and prices appears limited.

title: Canadian Critical Minerals Inc.: Canadian Critical Minerals Announces Increases of Indicated Metal of 11% for Copper and 17% for Gold at the Bull River Mine
summary: Canadian Critical Minerals Inc. reported an updated Mineral Resource for its Bull River Mine, including a reported increase in indicated copper content (10%/11% cited) alongside gold. The announcement expands resource estimates using stockpile material, but does not indicate immediate production changes, so near-term copper pricing impact is likely limited.

title: Recycled Steel and Aluminum Not Included in President Trump's Steel and Aluminum Tariffs | Gray Reed
summary: An executive order introducing tariffs on US steel and aluminum imports will take effect March 12, but a ReMA analysis says recycled steel and aluminum (scrap) are not covered. The US imports sizable volumes of iron/steel scrap and aluminum scrap, suggesting construction firms may use scrap to avoid delays and costs.

title: GSC Secures £1.57m Funding for Exploration Work | Company Announcement
summary: Great Southern Copper raised £1.57m to accelerate drilling and metallurgical test work at its Chile Mostaza Mine/Cerro Negro copper-gold projects. The company plans further diamond drilling and option/land holding costs, following strong assay results. The equity/convertible loan funding is Copper-development related and supportive for sentiment.

title: U.S. copper prices surge as Trump signals 25% tariff on imports
summary: U.S. copper prices jumped after Trump signaled a possible 25% tariff on imported goods. Such trade restrictions can affect metal import flows and availability, tightening near-term supply expectations. The move is reflected in the reported surge in copper prices.

title: India's small exporters seek import duty cuts to counter US steel, aluminium tariffs
summary: India’s small exporters asked for U.S.-linked import duty cuts after Trump’s planned 25% tariffs on steel and aluminium imports take effect March 12. Exporters expect fewer orders and higher costs affecting shipments to the U.S., while India also considers reciprocal tariffs, limiting near-term aluminium demand momentum.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Reports Strong Copper and Zinc Production in the First Two Months of 2025
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said Kamoa-Kakula produced near-record copper in January and February, running close to December 2024 rates. Power availability is improving with additional hydro discussions, supporting operations and smelter plans. The article also notes Kipushi zinc output, but aluminium and nickel impacts are not directly evidenced.

title: Furey Discusses Potential Nickel Impact at Toronto Mining Conference
summary: Premier Andrew Furey said Trump’s punitive tariffs on Canadian products are already affecting the mining sector, with repercussions for global nickel markets. He noted about one-third of Canada’s nickel comes from Newfoundland and Labrador, is processed in Canada, then shipped to the U.S. for manufacturing, where capacity is limited.

title: Trump's tariffs drive US physical market aluminium premiums to record high
summary: The article’s title says Trump’s tariffs have driven US physical market aluminium premiums to record highs. Such a move typically reflects reduced availability and stronger demand for prompt delivery, tightening physical supply and providing upward support to aluminium prices in the near term.

title: What Every Multinational Company Should Know About … The New Steel And Aluminum Tariffs (Part II)
summary: President Trump signed U.S. proclamations imposing 25% tariffs on aluminum (and steel), increasing the prior aluminum tariff and removing product-specific exemptions. Coverage expands to aluminum derivative downstream products to close perceived tariff evasion. Tariffs start for entries after March 12, 2025, with stricter customs classification and penalties.

title: New Section 232 Investigations of Copper and Timber - Background, Timeline, and Next Steps | Benesch
summary: The White House directed the Commerce Department to start Section 232 investigations covering copper imports, aiming to reduce U.S. reliance on foreign sourcing for national security and defense supply. The process may result in tariffs or other duties across all copper import forms, increasing near-term pricing and supply risk for buyers.

title: Nickel Asia, DMCI Mining to partner on nickel processing plant in PHL
summary: Nickel Asia and DMCI Mining said they are studying a Philippine nickel processing plant, tied to government consideration of banning raw nickel ore exports to boost local processing. The firms plan to secure stable ore supply and evaluate technology over 2–3 years, subject to approvals, amid oversupply and high local electricity costs.

title: Global aluminium producer seeks Q2 premium of $260/T from Japan buyers, sources say
summary: Global aluminium producers are seeking a Q2 premium of roughly $245–$260/ton from Japan buyers, according to sources cited by Reuters. The premium level indicates stronger pricing power and potential supply tightness in the Japan market, which is generally supportive for near-term aluminium prices.

title: LME copper hits near 3-week high on dollar pullback, China stimulus hopes
summary: LME copper moved toward a three-week high as the dollar pulled back and investors raised hopes for China stimulus. The headline suggests improved growth/demand expectations and easier currency conditions supported buying interest in copper, indicating near-term bullish pressure for prices.

title: RTG Mining Inc.: Binding Finance and Offtake Agreed for Development of High Grade Mabilo Copper-Gold Project
summary: RTG Mining announced a binding term sheet with Glencore to finance and offtake Stage 1 of the high-grade Mabilo copper-gold project, including up to US$30m in tranches. Stage 1 DSO is expected to mine ~100,000t of ~21% copper supergene chalcocite. Funding and offtake terms support commissioning progress.

title: US copper prices rise as Trump announces 25% import tariff
summary: US President Trump’s announcement and related executive actions on a potential 25% import tariff on copper (and aluminium) triggered a rapid rally in Comex copper, up over 5% in New York. LME three-month copper also rose, while Comex-LME spreads widened as traders rushed to source deliverable metal ahead of tariffs.

title: New Section 232 Investigations Of Copper And Timber – Background, Timeline, And Next Steps
summary: The White House directed the Commerce Department to initiate Section 232 trade investigations covering copper imports, citing rising reliance on foreign sourcing and defense-related copper needs. The process could result in tariffs or quotas, affecting near-term import costs and pricing expectations. The timber/lumber measures are separate.

title: Implementation Of Duties On Steel And Aluminum Products Pursuant To Proclamations 10895 And 10896
summary: The article says President Trump issued executive orders imposing new U.S. tariffs on products from Mexico, Canada, and China, effective Feb. 4, 2025, with no drawback or de minimis relief. It notes these duties add on top of other charges and do not provide exclusions, likely pressuring aluminum prices upward.

title: African Review - Ivanhoe Mines reshape DRC's copper and zinc future
summary: Ivanhoe Mines updated production at the DRC’s Kamoa-Kakula copper complex and Kipushi zinc mine. Copper output reached near-record monthly tonnes and annualized run-rates at the top of 2025 guidance, supported by improving hydro power and project progress. This signals stronger-than-expected copper supply momentum.

title: Lundin Mining to option Michigan nickel-copper targets from Talon Metals
summary: Lundin Mining agreed with Talon Metals to negotiate an earn-in for up to 70% of the Boulderdash and Roland nickel-copper exploration properties in Michigan, including a $5m advance to start drilling. The deal targets future nickel and copper resources, but it is not immediate production.

title: Lundin Mining to option Michigan nickel-copper targets from Talon Metals
summary: Lundin Mining agreed on an exclusivity/earn-in arrangement with Talon Metals to fund drilling (up to 30,000m) on Michigan nickel-copper exploration properties, including an initial $5m advance. The asset is adjacent to Lundin’s US nickel Eagle mine, but no production is yet confirmed, limiting immediate price impact.

title: Supply Chains to Face Global Impact From US Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum | Baker Botts L.L.P.
summary: US issued Section 232 proclamations adjusting imports of aluminum (and steel) effective March 12, 2025, with product-coverage determined by Commerce. The change alters trade flows for aluminum and steel-related derivatives, potentially tightening US availability. Copper is mentioned only indirectly via broader tariff policy and retaliation risks.

title: Trump Orders Investigation into Copper Supply Chain
summary: President Trump signed an order directing Commerce to investigate alleged national-security threats to the U.S. copper supply chain under Section 232, which could lead to tariffs and quotas on copper imports. While the action is investigative, the described likelihood of restrictions implies rising near-term copper price pressure.

title: Nickel CEO says Canada can ship its critical minerals 'anywhere' in the world amid U.S. tariffs
summary: Nickel CEO Mark Selby says Canada supplies roughly half of U.S. nickel and could redirect shipments to Europe if U.S. tariffs drive trade away from Canada. Ontario’s tariff dispute includes threats to halt nickel and electricity supply to the U.S., raising near-term supply uncertainty and supportive expectations for nickel prices.

title: NAC sees nickel prices rising on supply constraints - BusinessWorld Online
summary: Nickel Asia Corp. (NAC) expects nickel prices to face upward pressure due to limited future supply visibility beyond 2027, constrained ore availability and processing execution risks. It cites rising consumption from stainless steel and renewable energy, recent lows, and possible supply disruptions tied to Indonesia and the Philippines.

title: Trump Confirms Plan to Impose Steel, Aluminum Tariffs Next Week
summary: The headline reports that Trump confirmed a plan to impose steel and aluminium tariffs next week. Tariffs typically reduce imports and tighten available supply for the tariffed market, which can lift near-term aluminium price expectations, even if downstream demand could soften.

title: Executive Order Imposing Additional Duties On Aluminum Products
summary: An executive order modifies Section 232 aluminum tariffs by canceling allowances for several countries (e.g., Argentina, Australia, Canada, Mexico, EU, UK) and imposing an additional 25% duty on aluminum and derivative aluminum imports. It removes future product exclusions, broadens coverage for additional derivative articles, and increases CBP scrutiny.

title: Shanghai copper hits nearly five-month high on China stimulus hopes
summary: Shanghai copper rallied to a nearly five-month high as investors reacted to hopes for China stimulus. The move reflects expectations that additional fiscal or monetary support could strengthen industrial activity and copper demand, boosting sentiment and supporting copper prices over the near term.

title: China's January-February copper imports fall 7.2% y/y to 837,000 tons
summary: China’s unwrought copper imports fell 7.2% y/y to 837,000 tons in Jan–Feb 2025 as increased domestic smelting capacity reduced reliance on imports. Copper prices rose in China and globally following U.S. tariff threats. The report also shows higher SFE copper deliverable stocks by end-February.

title: Freeport secures permit for copper concentrate exports until mid-year - Companies
summary: Indonesia’s government granted Freeport Indonesia a permit to export copper concentrate through end-June, as its smelter is offline after a fire. The decision provides an exception to the since-December export ban and clears ~400,000 tonnes stuck in limbo, while warning of sanctions if repairs aren’t completed.

title: Upward Trend Continues: High-Nickel Pig Iron Prices Rise Amid Supply and Demand Dynamics
summary: High-nickel pig iron prices rose week-on-week, with domestic supply constrained by depleted nickel ore inventories and limited Indonesian smelter output during Ramadan. Demand firmed as stainless steel plants increased production and procurement. Smelter losses eased and weaker USD plus new Indonesian ore pricing formulas supported nickel-related prices, implying continued upside risk.

title: One in five small firms still 'analogue': BT calls on businesses to go digital by end of 2025 as historic copper network nears retirement
summary: BT urges UK businesses using analogue copper PSTN landlines to migrate to digital networks by end-2025, ahead of full retirement in January 2027. It cites a 45% rise in PSTN incidents and notes that PSTN-dependent equipment could be affected. The move supports a transition to more robust connectivity.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Announces Inclusion in the S&P/ASX 200 Index
summary: Capstone Copper announced its CDIs will be added to the S&P/ASX 200 effective March 24, 2025. The article focuses on index inclusion, trading liquidity, and investor visibility, without any updates to mine output, costs, supply disruptions, or demand. It is therefore unlikely to materially move copper prices.

title: After tariff victory, Mexico seeks win on aluminum, steel shipments to US
summary: After a U.S. tariff reprieve, Mexico is working to raise compliant exports, targeting that 90% of shipments meet U.S. requirements. The report highlights aluminum (and steel) shipments to the U.S., implying a near-term shift in exportable volumes and market supply expectations for aluminum.

title: Indigenous communities oppose Chinalco bauxite mine in Suriname
summary: Indigenous groups in Suriname sued to withdraw or suspend a government agreement with Chinalco to develop a bauxite mine near Bakhuis.
