summary: Australia’s federal Budget 2025 sets aside $2 billion for “green aluminium” under a plan to support Australian-made metals, alongside $1 billion for green iron. Green aluminium uses renewable energy to cut emissions, which may increase expected investment and supply activity in aluminium markets.

title: The US may impose tariffs on imported copper, a smelter under Glencore has suspended operations, and New York copper hit a record high [SMM Express].
summary: The report says the US may impose tariffs on imported copper, while a Glencore-linked smelter has suspended operations. It also notes New York copper reached a record high. Together, tariff risk and reduced refining supply point to near-term tightness and upward copper price pressure.

title: Tariff fears drive Copper to record in classic commodity fifth-wave extension
summary: US copper prices surged to fresh records as traders increased expectations that Trump may soon impose tariffs of up to 25% on copper imports. The Commerce Department’s review is seen progressing quickly, with a decision possibly within weeks, prompting defensive buying amid fears of supply disruption.

title: Copper Wire and Cable Exports Start the Year Strong with Stable Overseas Demand
summary: China’s copper wire and cable exports were 107,100 mt in January (+10.84% YoY) and 73,300 mt in February (-10.7% YoY), bringing Jan–Feb exports to 180,500 mt (+0.94% YoY). SMM expects March to stay high with stable overseas orders, supporting copper demand despite cautious trade sentiment.

title: Zeus North America Mining Corp. Applauds the Executive Order to Accelerate Critical Mineral Production, including Copper, in the USA
summary: Zeus North America Mining praises a U.S. executive order signed March 20, 2025 to accelerate domestic critical mineral production under the Defense Production Act, explicitly including copper. The order aims to expedite permits and create financing for domestic projects via a dedicated mineral production fund, supporting copper supply expectations.

title: Copper rises above $10,000 on speculation of US taxes
summary: Copper prices rose on the LME and Comex after reports that the US Commerce Department is investigating potential tariffs on copper imports. Traders accelerated moves of metal into the US to pre-empt duties, widening Comex–LME arbitrage. Additional support came from a Glencore smelter shipment pause in Chile.

title: Canada steel, aluminum plants lay off workers due to US tariffs
summary: Canadian steel and aluminum producers reportedly initiated layoffs after US tariffs reduced competitiveness and altered trade flows. The announcement points to weaker near-term operating conditions for aluminum plants, suggesting demand and/or production expectations may fall, adding downside pressure to aluminum prices in the short term.

title: Glencore declares force majeure on copper shipments from Altonorte smelter in Chile
summary: Glencore declared force majeure on copper shipments from its Altonorte smelter in Chile after production was suspended. Altonorte’s 350,000 mt/year anode capacity is a small share of global refined supply, but a long outage could worsen supply deficits. COMEX copper prices are already near record highs on shortage fears.

title: EU recorded a trade deficit of €11.1 billion in aluminium
summary: The EU recorded an aluminium trade deficit of €11.1 billion in 2024, with imports of €29.5 billion versus exports of €18.4 billion. Import and export values increased since 2019, mainly attributed to higher prices rather than volumes. Key import partners included Norway and China, while UK led exports.

title: Comex copper at record high as US import tariff fears mount
summary: Comex copper prices are reported at record highs as concerns about possible US import tariffs mount. Reuters suggests the tariff fears are influencing market expectations for near-term supply-demand balances and trade flows, contributing to upward momentum in copper pricing in the immediate term.

title: Goldman maintains copper price forecasts, says tariffs will avert US glut
summary: Goldman Sachs maintained its LME copper forecasts and said U.S. import tariffs would likely prevent a domestic copper stock glut in Q3. The bank warned that a trade-policy update effective April 2 could create near-term downside risk, but rising tariff certainty lifted COMEX premiums over LME prices.

title: Copper Futures Hit Record High on Report of US Tariffs Within Weeks
summary: Copper futures in New York surged to a record high after reports that U.S. tariffs on copper imports may arrive within weeks, earlier than the decision deadline. The Commerce Department probe launched under President Trump is reportedly expected to be resolved sooner, tightening the near-term supply outlook for copper.

title: Sterling Metals Corp.: Sterling Metals Commences Inaugural Drilling Program at Copper Road Project, Ontario
summary: Sterling Metals began a 2,000-metre diamond drilling program at its Copper Road Project in Ontario, targeting near-surface and deeper copper mineralization tied to geophysical anomalies. It also received a $200,000 Ontario Junior Exploration Program grant supporting critical minerals exploration, reinforcing project potential but not affecting near-term supply.

title: Hundreds of Canadian workers in steel, aluminum sectors laid off due to U.S. tariffs
summary: Hundreds of Canadian workers in steel and aluminum sectors are laid off after the U.S. imposed tariffs on March 12, with more possible tariffs on April 2 and an expected end to a 30-day tariff reprieve. Firms cite reduced orders and hiring freezes, pointing to near-term demand disruption that can weigh on metal prices.

title: Trump to expedite tariffs on copper
summary: The article headline says Trump will expedite tariffs on copper. Expanding tariff implementation can increase costs for buyers and disrupt cross-border trade, potentially weakening near-term demand expectations for copper and putting downward pressure on copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Go Metals Corp.: Go Metals Sets Drill Targets at Monster Copper Project
summary: Go Metals Corp. reports planning for a 2,500m drill program at its Monster IOCG copper-cobalt project in Yukon, following high copper and cobalt values in samples and geophysical targets. The article is primarily exploration-focused with no stated production or supply changes, likely limiting near-term price impact.

title: Search for copper underway north of Sault Ste. Marie
summary: Sterling Metals has begun drilling for near-surface copper mineralization at its Copper Road Project near Sault Ste. Marie, with work continuing until late April. The company cites geophysical anomalies and historical copper mines nearby, funded partially by an Ontario exploration grant. The news is exploration-focused, not output-related.

title: 1 dead and 2 missing in sludge collapse at Chinese-fund nickel plant in Indonesia
summary: A sludge collapse at a Chinese-funded nickel plant in Indonesia has reportedly killed one person and left two missing. The accident is likely to disrupt operations at the nickel facility, increasing short-term supply uncertainty and potentially pressuring nickel prices lower over the coming days to weeks.

title: Can Trump's critical minerals drive pass the copper test?
summary: Trump’s executive order aims to speed permitting for domestic minerals, which could help stalled U.S. copper projects like Resolution, Pebble and Twin Metals. However, new mine output would take years and U.S. processing capacity and smelter margins are tight. Recycling expansion may help later, limiting near-term copper price impact.

title: Sludge collapse kills 1 at a Chinese-funded nickel plant in Indonesia
summary: The article title reports a sludge collapse that killed one worker at a Chinese-funded nickel plant in Indonesia. Such an incident can halt or delay operations and maintenance, reducing near-term nickel output. That supply disruption risk is bearish for nickel prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: New Nevada bill creates penalties for stolen copper, causing massive outages
summary: Nevada’s new Assembly Bill 503 would increase penalties for possessing stolen municipal-grade copper wire and for causing outages or damage to infrastructure such as streetlights and substations. Officials say copper theft has driven major outages, prompting tougher enforcement that could tighten effective copper availability.

title: Copper hits all-time high on report that tariffs are weeks away
summary: Copper futures hit an all-time high after a report said US copper import tariffs could be imposed in weeks, not months. The tariff threat sparked fast-tracked US shipments and widened US-London price spreads. Analysts expect demand-supportive stimuli, but warn trade-war risk could hurt later.

title: Gold Down, Silver Firm, Copper Jumps
summary: The piece reports gold slipping and silver firm, while copper jumped about 1 week from Trump’s “Liberation Day” trade tariffs. The headline framing suggests the tariff outlook affected market expectations and provided bullish momentum for copper over the immediate trading window.

title: Copper Analysis Today 26/03: Record Highs Glimmer (Chart)
summary: Copper prices rallied to record highs, then pulled back slightly, trading near the upper support/resistance band. The article links the surge to President Trump’s statements on protecting U.S-origin copper production and tariff negotiation speculation that boosts positioning by large market participants. It warns of high volatility into early-April deadlines.

title: Is $5/lb Copper the New Normal?
summary: Copper is reported trading above $5/lb for the second time recently, with record prices driven by strained inventories, rising demand linked to renewables and grid investment, and concerns that mine output and supply development cannot keep pace. The construction segment faces higher wire costs and theft risk, prompting substitution toward copper-clad aluminum.

title: Nevada bill would up penalties for possessing copper wire
summary: A Nevada bill (AB 503) would stiffen penalties for possessing and stealing copper wire, including higher misdemeanor/felony thresholds and additional charges if theft interrupts electrical service. It also restricts possession of used utility wire without permits or documentation, potentially curbing theft and scrap diversion locally.

title: Copper prices have soared as the US threatens tariffs on the metal and China boosts its economy
summary: The article headline says copper prices have surged as the US threatens tariffs on the metal and China boosts its economy. The combination of policy risk around imports/flows and stronger growth expectations is presented as lifting near-term sentiment and pricing for copper.

title: Copper prices have soared as potential U.S. tariffs and China's economic stimulus program spur demand
summary: Copper prices hit record highs as tariff threats between the U.S. and trading partners raise expectations of tighter supplies and buyers stock up ahead of possible import levies. China’s stimulus is expected to lift demand further. The piece also links the rally to broader industrial and clean-energy demand.

title: Trump: copper prices increase amidst tariff threat on metal
summary: Copper prices are reported to have surged as the U.S. threatens to impose tariffs on the metal. The move is also attributed to China boosting its economy, supporting demand expectations. Together, the tariff risk and firmer demand outlook increase the likelihood of near-term copper price strength.

title: Trump Weighs Imposing Copper Import Tariffs in Weeks
summary: The article reports that the US could impose copper import tariffs within several weeks, earlier than the previously expected decision timeline. Such tariffs would likely increase the cost of imported copper into the US, affecting short-term supply expectations and supporting upward pressure on copper prices.

title: Why are domestic steel and aluminum prices rising, too?
summary: The article explains that tariffs raise the cost of imported steel and aluminum, which in turn gives domestic producers “a green light” to increase their own prices. A supplier increased U.S. steel costs by ~20%, and the domestic aluminum price is expected to rise after tariffs, despite weak demand.

title: US gears to slap tariffs on copper imports
summary: The headline says the US is gearing up to impose tariffs on copper imports. Such measures would increase the cost of importing copper into the US, potentially lowering near-term import demand and market sentiment, which could weigh on copper prices over the following days to weeks.

title: Copper prices surge to record high amid tariff anxiety
summary: Copper prices are reported to have surged to record highs as “tariff anxiety” escalates. The headline suggests investors are re-pricing near-term risks around trade policy that could affect copper flows and demand/supply expectations, supporting upward momentum in copper prices over the next days.

title: China expands carbon trading market to steel, cement, aluminum smelting sectors-Xinhua
summary: China will expand its emissions trading scheme to include steel, cement and aluminium smelting, adding 1,500 enterprises. The aluminium smelting inclusion may increase compliance costs for smelters through higher demand for emission permits, pressuring aluminium supply and pricing in the near term.

title: $944K settlement filed in class-action lawsuit against Lowcountry aluminum plant
summary: A $944,000 settlement was filed in a class-action lawsuit involving the Mt. Holly Century Aluminum plant in South Carolina over alleged alumina dust emissions. The company was also fined $360,000 for emissions test failures and EPA violations, with consent-order evidence of repeated exceedances. Additional filings and court approval are pending.

title: Copper prices hit record highs as trade war and demand surge
summary: The article headline claims copper is reaching record highs, attributing the rally to trade-war developments and a surge in demand. If sustained in coming weeks, these factors would likely lift market expectations for copper supply-demand balance and reinforce upward near-term pricing momentum.

title: China expands carbon trading market to steel, cement, aluminum smelting sectors
summary: China plans to expand its national carbon trading market to cover steel, cement, and aluminium smelting, adding about 1,500 enterprises and covering roughly 3 billion tonnes of CO2e annually. By pricing emissions in smelting, compliance costs are likely to rise, affecting aluminium production economics within weeks.

title: Brightspeed to replace copper wires with fiber optics amid ongoing service issues
summary: Brightspeed customers in Virginia have faced unreliable landline service due to wear and storm damage to copper wires and contractor cuts. The company plans to install fiber optic lines to replace copper, though no firm timeline is given. Regulators are investigating multiple customer complaints and discussing ongoing reliability issues.

title: London copper edges up, stronger dollar caps rise
summary: A Reuters note reports London copper edging up while a stronger U.S. dollar and related factors (described as “caps rise”) restrained gains. The headline suggests competing forces—slightly supportive copper pricing but capped upside by currency strength.

title: Lotte Energy Materials to Seek Copper Mark Certification for Malaysian Plant
summary: Lotte Energy Materials says it will seek copper market certification for its Malaysian plant. The move is intended to formalize the plant’s copper market eligibility/quality status, which may support sales and trading over time, but the article provides no immediate supply disruption or demand shock. Near-term copper price pressure appears limited.

title: Citi trims 3-month copper price forecast to $9,500/t
summary: Citi reduced its 3-month copper price forecast to $9,500 per tonne, according to Reuters. While the change is a market view rather than immediate physical disruption, it can weigh on copper sentiment by lowering expected prices over the coming weeks.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Exports Slightly Increased in January-February 2025, Expected to Grow MoM in March
summary: China’s customs data show copper plate/sheet and strip exports rose 28.4% MoM in January and were still supported on a cumulative Jan-Feb basis. February fell MoM but increased YoY. Trade flows and improving manufacturing PMI support demand, and SMM expects a March MoM rebound, keeping exports high.

title: [SMM Analysis]Refined Copper Rod Exports Showed Steady YoY Growth in January-February: Is Processing Trade a Flash in the Pan or the Future Mainstream?
summary: SMM cites customs data showing refined copper rod (>6mm) and copper wire (≤6mm) exports rising sharply in January–February 2025, with most volume shifting to processing trade. Exports grew MoM and YoY and are expected to remain high if the export window stays open.

title: Amid the tariff storm, copper prices in the US hit a historic high, and institutions predict that the era of copper shortage may have begun.
summary: US NYMEX copper futures hit a historic high above $5.22/lb, up more than 2.5%. The surge is linked to expected Trump tariffs on imported copper, with reports of ports overwhelmed by pre-tariff shipments. Analysts expect the NYMEX–LME spread to stay elevated and global copper tightness to worsen.

title: Citi cuts copper price forecast, sees 25% US import tariff in second quarter
summary: Citi lowered its copper price forecast and expects the US to impose a 25% import tariff in Q2. The downgrade signals weaker near-term demand or pricing assumptions for copper, and the tariff outlook is treated as part of that bearish outlook by the bank.

title: Rudi's View: Coal, Copper, Car Group & More
summary: The piece argues that US import tariffs could spill over across commodities. For copper, Morgan Stanley expects a 25% tariff on US imports to create a premium for US buyers, but also to reduce demand for imports from the rest of the world, likely pulling down London-traded copper contracts.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Intersects 0.25% Nickel and 0.29%
summary: First Atlantic Nickel announced assays from drill hole AN-24-03 at its RPM Zone, reporting an average 0.25% nickel over 216 meters (including 0.27% nickel in the final 21 meters) with visible awaruite mineralization. The company plans higher-powered Phase 2 drilling to test deeper/westward extensions, implying favorable nickel potential.

title: Copper slips on Trump auto tariffs, uncertainty
summary: Reuters reports copper prices slipped as markets reacted to potential Trump auto tariffs, with uncertainty over the policy’s impact. Traders appeared to reassess near-term demand expectations for auto manufacturing, which typically supports industrial metal usage, contributing to the immediate downward move in copper.

title: Copper Is Worth More in New York Than London — Just Like Gold
summary: Copper rallies to record highs in New York while London prices dip, driven by fears of imminent US tariffs on copper imports. The piece cites a US supply squeeze from stockpiling ahead of tariffs, with analysts expecting a growing supply-constrained market. It also points to rising defense budgets and EV/data-center demand.

title: PAN GLOBAL SAMPLES 5.2% COPPER OVER 5m AT PROFUNDA TARGET, CÁRMENES PROJECT, SPAIN
summary: Pan Global Resources reported underground channel samples at the Profunda target in Spain’s Cármenes project, including 5.2% copper over 5m and other high-grade Cu intervals. Nickel is also present in several samples (up to 0.53% Ni over 1m), supporting bullish sentiment for copper and some nickel.

title: Goldman Weighs In On Accelerated Copper Import Tariff Timeline
summary: The piece references Goldman’s view on an accelerated timeline for copper import tariffs. Such policy expectations can shift short-term supply/demand balance by affecting incoming copper flows, potentially tightening availability and supporting prices in the near term as markets adjust to higher trade frictions and prospective costs.

title: SPIC launches the construction of alumina refinery in Guinea
summary: SPIC has begun full construction of a planned alumina refinery in Guinea, targeting initial output of 1.2 million metric tons per year. The project is expected to deepen China-Guinea mining cooperation and expand local industrial capacity, with potential to improve upstream alumina availability supporting aluminium sentiment.

title: Hudbay Minerals To Buy Mitsubishi Materials's 25% Stake In Copper Mountain Mine (BC) Ltd.
summary: Hudbay agreed to buy Mitsubishi Materials’ 25% stake in the Copper Mountain mine in British Columbia from Mitsubishi Materials. The purchase includes an upfront payment plus installments and contingent payments, and Hudbay will assume related debts. Copper Mountain is targeted to rise production toward 60,000 tonnes by 2027, boosting Hudbay’s copper exposure.

title: Class 1 Nickel Updates Resource Estimate on Dundonald North
summary: Class 1 Nickel reported an updated NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate for the Dundonald North nickel sulphide deposit, citing higher tonnage and contained nickel, plus increases in contained copper and cobalt. The update is based on historical drilling and remains inferred/out-of-pit, with no near-term production timeline.

title: The operating rate of downstream aluminum sectors showed a slight increase[SMM Weekly Downstream Survey]
summary: SMM’s weekly survey shows downstream aluminum operating rates rising to 63.4% (+0.6pp WoW), led by power-grid-driven wire and cable orders and PV extrusion deliveries. Primary/secondary alloy rates tick up but remain constrained by inventory and losses. Overall conditions support a gradual increase next week, though high prices may suppress demand.

title: Firering Strategic drives Zambia's copper expansion
summary: Firering Strategic says its Limeco quicklime production for Zambia’s Copperbelt smelters started in late Feb 2025, with 600–800 t/d targeted by 1Q26. By supplying smelting-critical quicklime domestically, it should reduce costly imports and support Zambia’s copper industry as copper demand strengthens.

title: Copper Wire Thefts Surge in Downtown London
summary: London has reported 23 copper wire theft incidents since November, mostly in the downtown core and occurring between 2 a.m. and 5 a.m. Authorities warn thefts target hydro, buildings, and active sites, causing disruption and safety risks. Public guidance emphasizes reporting suspicious activity and managing scrap dealer oversight.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Royalty Partner, Zijin Mining, Provides an Update on a New Copper and Gold Discovery in Serbia
summary: EMX says its partner Zijin increased copper resources/reserves at Serbia’s Timok (Cukaru Peki) and completed preliminary exploration at a new Malka Golaja copper-gold deposit. The discovery is described as high-grade and open for further drilling, supporting incremental positive sentiment for future copper supply.

title: VTA strike: Copper wire theft 'skyrocketed' in last two weeks, service delayed until Monday
summary: A VTA strike halted service, and when workers returned, track and equipment inspections took longer because of copper wire theft, mainly along the Green Line. VTA said thefts increased during the strike, though the sheriff’s office later clarified reported thefts were lower than the previous year.

title: U.S. Copper Import Tariffs May Arrive Sooner Than Expected
summary: The U.S. may impose Section 232 copper import tariffs sooner than expected, with the Commerce timeline shifting to mid-May. Analysts expect faster U.S. shipments into April, followed by declining U.S. inventories from mid-to-late Q2, reducing stock-glut risk and supporting tighter global balance conditions, keeping copper prices bid.

title: How new aluminum and steel tariffs affect the brewing industry
summary: New US tariffs are taking effect, including a 25% duty on imported aluminum and a 25% duty on steel. Glacier Tanks, which ships aluminum and stainless-steel parts for brewers, says costs are already rising and will hit smaller breweries more. The added tariff cost is expected to lift aluminium-related input prices.

title: Analysis: Freeport copper ore export permit against downstream policy. - Academia
summary: Indonesia granted Freeport Indonesia an extended exemption to export copper concentrate through June 2025 after a October 2024 fire damaged its Gresik smelter’s sulfuric acid unit. With ~400,000 tonnes of concentrate stockpiled, the government raised export taxes while allowing shipments to prevent losses.

title: London copper edges lower as US tariff unease weighs
summary: London copper edged lower to a nearly two-week low as uncertainty over possible US tariffs weighed on sentiment. The report links the move to tariff-related unease, which can dampen expectations for industrial demand and metal trade flows, leading traders to price a softer outlook for copper.

title: London copper hits nearly two-week low as US tariff unease weighs
summary: London copper fell to a nearly two-week low as investors grew uneasy about potential US tariff measures. The reported tariff uncertainty weighed on sentiment, increasing concerns about near-term industrial demand and leading to weaker copper pricing in the immediate market session.

title: China to promote high-quality development of aluminum sector, actively respond to trade frictions: plan
summary: China plans to promote “high-quality development” of its aluminium sector and to actively respond to existing trade frictions. The policy intent suggests potential adjustments to industry output or trade stance that could influence near-term aluminium market expectations, but details are not specified in the article.

title: The spot market showed some improvement. The aluminum ingot inventory approached the 800,000 mt mark at month-end.
summary: Domestic aluminum ingot inventories fell mid-week by 25,000 mt to around 802,000 mt, with tradable stocks down, driven by higher outflows and reduced arrivals. Restocking demand from automotive and PV/NEV increased and discounts to the April contract narrowed, supporting near-term upside for aluminium.

title: 【SMM Announcement】Official Launch of New Price for SMM's Indonesia Local Laterite Nickel Ore
summary: SMM launched new weekly price points for Indonesia local laterite nickel ore (1.3%, 1.4%, 1.5%), with values published every Friday. This week, multiple nickel ore grades increased WoW, including 1.4% and 1.5% ex-factory and FOB assessments, suggesting firmer nickel ore pricing.

title: Romanian copper mining project shortlisted by EU for fast tracking faces environmental issues
summary: An EU fast-tracked Romanian project (Rovina) has had its environmental permit cancelled and needs new approval, including Hungary’s consent. The permitting timeline under the CRMA may still be challenging, with legal and ecological concerns cited. The project would have produced about 9,000 tonnes of copper annually in early years.

title: Lancaster County sees uptick in copper wire thefts from center pivots
summary: Lancaster County reports two recent cases of copper wire theft from center pivot irrigation systems, including $18,000 in losses. Authorities say the theft pattern is unusual for the area and suggest it may be driven by rising copper prices, citing a 30% increase this year.

title: China's Unwrought Aluminum Alloy Imports Slightly Declined YoY in the First Two Months of 2025 [SMM Analysis]
summary: Customs data show China’s unwrought aluminum alloy ingot imports fell in January (-4.9% YoY) and February (+3.6% YoY) but both months were below 100,000 mt, with cumulative imports down 1% YoY. Exports also declined sharply. Falling domestic prices compressed import margins, reducing demand; March may rebound slightly.

title: Copper Pipe & Tube Imports and Exports Both Increased YoY, January-February.
summary: China’s copper pipe & tube imports rose 8.8% YoY in Jan–Feb 2025, while exports increased 12.8% YoY. February exports fell MoM amid US tariff uncertainty, but March imports may tick up as air-conditioner demand strengthens, while exports to Southeast Asia could keep rising on a low base.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market-3.28
summary: SMM reports continued tight Indonesian nickel ore supply, with pyrometallurgical ore prices and April premiums expected to rise, aided by low smelter inventories and strong PNBP policy expectations that lift miners’ costs. Rainy-season disruptions and flooding constrain supply. NPI remains supported by higher costs, while refined nickel projects ramp up gradually.

title: LME copper falls with muted risk appetite ahead of bumpy next week
summary: LME copper is reported to be under pressure as risk appetite remains muted ahead of a potentially volatile next week. The move suggests investors are taking less exposure to cyclical metals, creating near-term bearish sentiment for copper prices on the LME.

title: China's GEM assumes control of nickel processor BNSI - Companies
summary: China’s GEM becomes the majority owner of Bahodopi Nickel Smelting Indonesia (BNSI) via a Rp 1 trillion share subscription, diluting PT Vale Indonesia to 49%. BNSI develops a nickel processing facility in Morowali. The report says operations and business continuity won’t be affected.

title: Amid Loss Pressure, Production Cuts and Maintenance Emerge Simultaneously, China's Metallurgical Alumina Operating Capacity May Further Decline in April
summary: China’s metallurgical-grade alumina output rose year-on-year in March, but operating rate fell to 84.64% as losses led producers to cut production and schedule maintenance. Spot alumina prices are expected to keep declining, with exports limited. April capacity is forecast to fall further, keeping alumina supply loose.

title: China Unveils 2025–2027 Aluminium Industry Action Plan
summary: China’s MIIT and other ministries released a 2025–2027 Aluminium Industry Action Plan. It boosts bauxite security and recycled aluminium, tightens approvals for new/expanded alumina refineries, and maintains a capacity ceiling for primary aluminium with cleaner-energy conditions. Analysts expect potential near-term tightening in deliverable aluminium ingots as volumes shift to processing.

title: High-Nickel Pig Iron Prices Continue to Rise Amid Cost Pressures and Supply Constraints in Domestic and Indonesian Markets
summary: High-nickel pig iron prices (SMM8-12%) rose WoW, supported by cost pressures from higher nickel ore and improved cost support amid tight feedstock availability. Indonesian flooding in Morowali is expected to increase pure nickel costs. The piece expects continued strong NPI and upward nickel price correction.

title: Helix Resources to acquire copper-gold tenements in Arizona, US
summary: Helix Resources signed conditional agreements to acquire the White Hills copper-gold tenements in Arizona, adjacent to an existing porphyry copper operation. The deal requires payments, equity issuance, and exploration spending, with potential feasibility milestones and Newmont royalty terms. No production is expected immediately, limiting near-term copper price impact.

title: Canada One Mining expands Copper Dome project landing holdings in BC
summary: Canada One Mining expanded its Copper Dome project land position in British Columbia by 1,728ha, adding “Copper Dome East” contiguous claims targeting porphyry copper and molybdenum mineralisation. The firm is awaiting a drill permit and cites historical copper-silver and molybdenum anomalies. No near-term production changes are stated.

title: Chile copper miner Codelco swings to profit in 2024
summary: Codelco, Chile’s state copper miner, is sending more copper to the United States after a tariff threat. The Reuters report suggests the company is front-loading shipments to avoid potential costs or disruptions from proposed tariffs, altering near-term copper trade flows and market expectations.

title: Gold surges past $3,100, copper hovers near record as Trump tariffs send metals soaring
summary: The headline reports that gold has surged past $3,100 and copper is hovering near record levels as Trump tariffs are described as sending metals higher. This indicates near-term positive sentiment and upward price pressure for copper tied to tariff-driven market expectations.

title: TOMRA reveals AI technology for upgrading wrought aluminium scrap
summary: TOMRA unveiled AI-based GAINnext technology to upgrade wrought aluminium scrap by recovering low-alloy cast from the wrought fraction and reducing silicon and other alloying elements. Integrated after X-TRACT and optionally refined with Dynamic LIBS, it targets higher-purity aluminium fractions for recyclers, improving scrap quality but not signaling near-term market supply shifts.

title: Key talking points Bauxite & Alumina 2025
summary: Fastmarkets reports alumina prices fell in 2025 amid excess supply and weaker demand, while bauxite remains influenced by Guinea supply security. It also notes a US move to impose 25% tariffs on imported aluminium, lifting domestic sentiment and aluminium premiums. Market participants watch further tariff signals and trade-flow impacts.

title: First Quantum Halts Public Tours of Closed Panama Copper Mine
summary: First Quantum said it will suspend public tours of its closed Cobre Panama copper mine after Panama’s president stressed the site should not appear operational and noted no progress on resolving the dispute. The government also ties future steps to suspending arbitration, including export of 120,000 tonnes of copper concentrate left at the site.

title: Two Arrested for Stealing 6,484 Meters of Copper Cable from a Mining Site
summary: Spanish authorities arrested two men accused of stealing 6,484 meters of copper cable from a mining site in Marina Alta. The theft removed electricity wiring, leaving the plant inoperative and halting operations for months. Investigators say high replacement costs can delay site restart and worsen sector supply losses.

title: Hundreds of workers laid off as Trump imposes steel, aluminium tariffs on Canada
summary: Trump imposed tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium products, prompting layoffs at MPG Canada and others. The reported job cuts and expectations of further disruptions after a 30-day reprieve end suggest weakening demand/trade conditions for aluminium into the US, creating bearish near-term sentiment for aluminium prices.

title: During this period, supply increased while demand decreased, leading to an inventory buildup of bauxite compared to the previous period.
summary: SMM estimates China’s March bauxite output rose, while port bauxite inventories climbed to 16.06 million mt (+1.5 million mt m/m) driven by higher imports. At the demand side, metallurgical alumina operating capacity fell amid losses, with further reductions expected in April, implying temporary weaker bauxite demand.

title: SMM Downstream In-Depth Analysis: Structural Recovery in Aluminum Processing PMI for March—Peak Season Demand Fails to Mask Concerns Over High Aluminum Prices and Export Pressures
summary: China’s aluminium processing PMI rebounded in March (61.6%), with strength in plate/sheet, foil, construction and cable segments. However, high aluminium prices and export pressure—along with weak terminal demand for recycled output—are constraining procurement. Forecasts for April depend on PV and grid delivery peaks, but prices above 21,000 yuan/ton may cap upside.

title: Copper prices have soared as the US threatens tariffs on the metal and China boosts its economy | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: AP reports copper at record highs as U.S. tariff threats (up to 25% on copper imports) spur buyers to stock up ahead of potential measures. It also cites China’s stimulus as demand support, contributing to tightening supply expectations and a strong rally in the most traded copper contract.

title: India Expands Copper Mining Interests in Zambia
summary: India’s government has acquired land in Zambia to explore copper (and cobalt), and Vedanta is also linked to a large copper investment via an MoU with Saudi Arabia. While these moves could improve longer-term copper supply security, the exploration/greenfield nature implies limited immediate tightness or disruption within weeks.

title: India's aluminium production sees modest rises to 38.36 LT in FY24-25
summary: India’s aluminium production increased 0.9% to 38.36 lakh tonnes during April–February FY24-25, based on provisional Ministry of Mines data. The modest output rise suggests slightly higher supply expectations going into subsequent weeks, which can be mildly bearish for aluminium prices.

title: India Sees Modest Rise in Aluminium Production FY24-25
summary: India’s Ministry of Mines data show aluminium output rose 0.9% to 38.36 lakh tonnes in April-February FY24-25, while refined copper production increased 7.1% to 4.97 lakh tonnes. The article also discusses tariffs and India’s growing aluminium scrap imports, plus demand outlooks and broader mineral production growth.

title: The Latest News Regarding the Panama Cobre Copper Mine
summary: Panama said it has not authorized visits to First Quantum’s shuttered Cobre Panamá copper mine and is commissioning an audit to evaluate operations and environmental impact. The dispute follows the mine’s shutdown after a court ruling. The government worries visits could affect analysis and copper concentrate supply.

title: China Aluminum Wheel Exports Hit a Three-Year High in January, but Faced a "Waterloo" in February [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s exports of aluminum alloy wheel hubs rose in January (a MoM surge) on “rush to export” expectations of tariff hikes, but fell sharply in February. SMM links the pattern to North American tariff/trade policy uncertainty and expects H1 2025 export volumes and demand to trend downward.

title: India's copper demand set to rise 7% amid renewable energy boom | Indiablooms - First Portal on Digital News Management
summary: India’s copper demand is projected to rise about 7% as renewables, EVs, and infrastructure expansion accelerate under government schemes like PLI. With domestic refined output still below consumption, India relies on large copper imports, widening the demand-supply gap and supporting bullish copper price expectations.

title: Hot Chili unveils blockbuster PFS in booming copper-gold market
summary: Hot Chili released a prefeasibility study for its Costa Fuego copper-gold project in Chile, highlighting 95,000 tpa copper in early years, low unit costs, and materially higher NPV at spot prices. The update supports bullish sentiment for copper development and near-term supply outlook.

title: London copper hits two-week low on trade war concerns
summary: London copper fell to a two-week low as trade war concerns intensified. The headline suggests markets are pricing heightened trade barriers and potential slowdown in industrial activity, which can reduce expected copper demand. The move is presented as a near-term price reaction to geopolitics and tariff risk.

title: Are tariffs the answer to save America's declining aluminium industry?
summary: The article says the US aluminium industry is in decline and argues Trump’s proposed tariff plan (25% on aluminium) aims to rebalance unfair global competition. It quotes Constellium saying imported aluminium to its Ravenswood plant will cost 25% more, suggesting short-term aluminium price support despite broader supply-chain disruption risks.

title: China smelter group agrees not to set Q2 copper TC/RCs guidance, sources say
summary: Reuters reports that a China smelter group has agreed not to set Q2 copper TC/RCs guidance, citing sources. Copper TC/RC benchmarks influence refining charges and concentrate supply-demand expectations, which can feed into short-term copper market sentiment, though the article does not indicate the direction or magnitude of changes.

title: China's smelter group agrees not to set Q2 copper TC/RCs guidance, sources say
summary: Reuters reports that China’s smelter group has agreed not to issue Q2 copper TC/RCs guidance, citing sources. Because TC/RCs are a key input to copper refining economics, the decision affects market expectations for refining cost conditions and can increase near-term uncertainty for copper pricing.

title: Inalum to finish study for 2nd phase of alumina smelter project this year - Companies
summary: Indonesia’s Inalum plans to finish a feasibility study and final investment decision for the second phase of its smelter-grade alumina refinery in 2026 in West Kalimantan. It follows completion of the first phase, aimed at raising alumina capacity to two million tonnes per year, supporting future aluminium supply.

title: Japan Q2 aluminium premium set at $182/T, down 20% from Q1 -sources
summary: Japan’s Q2 aluminium premium for April–June was set at $182/ton, down 20% from Q1, citing weak demand. The premium is the first quarterly decline in five quarters and is used by Japan as a regional pricing benchmark above the LME cash price for primary aluminium shipments.

title: Exclusive-Commodity traders Gunvor, Vitol queue to stock up on Russian aluminium from LME storage, sources say
summary: Gunvor and Vitol are waiting to withdraw large volumes of Russian-origin aluminium from LME-approved warehouses at Gwangyang in South Korea. LME data show long delivery queues and prior warrant cancellations, implying more aluminium will exit the exchange system. The move adds near-term sell/flow risk for LME aluminium prices.

title: South Pacific Metals Corp.: South Pacific Metals Successfully Completes Warden's Hearing on Renewal of Exploration Licence for Kili Teke Copper-Gold Project
summary: South Pacific Metals reports successful completion of a Papua New Guinea warden hearing renewing exploration licence EL 2310 for its Kili Teke Cu-Au project and plans to begin on-ground exploration. The update is copper-linked via project development, but no production or supply change is announced, limiting near-term price impact.

title: The resumption of aluminum production has been observed, and the proportion of liquid aluminum has rebounded to normal levels [SMM data].
summary: SMM data show March 2025 domestic aluminum production rose (up 3.7% YoY and 11.2% MoM) as smelters gradually resumed output and the liquid aluminum ratio returned toward normal (74.2%). Operating rates increased to 95.8%, implying higher supply. April may see a slight ratio correction despite demand/price pressures.

title: Aluminium reliant industries not spared from the impact of tariffs
summary: The article reports that the US 25% tariff on imported steel and aluminium (effective March 12) is raising costs for aluminium-reliant industries. It covers unwrought aluminium and many aluminium products, with sources noting cost pass-through into cans, construction, automotive and aerospace components.

title: Horizon Copper Highlights Pre-Construction Investment Advancing Hod Maden Project, Hugo North Extension Drilling, and Other Updates
summary: Horizon Copper updates progress on its 30% Hod Maden interest in Türkiye, where SSR Mining plans $60–$100 million of early-works construction in 2025 toward a formal investment decision. It also reports additional copper-gold drilling results from Entrée’s Hugo North Extension and Heruga deposits at Oyu Tolgoi.

title: Copper Stocks are on Fire!
summary: The piece argues copper is in a strong uptrend, citing demand growth (AI/data centers, EVs) and forecast supply tightness. It also highlights a Bloomberg report that U.S. copper import tariffs could be coming within weeks, implying tighter near-term copper availability and bullish price pressure.

title: Belararox Identifies Copper Targets in Botswana
summary: Belararox identified over 20 copper exploration target areas on Botswana’s Kalahari Copper Belt using soil geochemistry and existing geophysical data. The company plans AMT, gravity, and airborne EM surveys to refine drill sites, with a 2,000-meter RC drilling program scheduled for July 2025. No production changes are cited.

title: Bellezza process could replace copper with graphene in ICs
summary: Bellezza claims a patented “fusion” process could enable graphene interconnects in CMOS chips at low temperatures, potentially replacing copper circuits as copper interconnects reach size limits. The method uses iron/nickel plating substrates treated to form martensite crystals. The article provides technology claims but no market-scale deployment.

title: Chinese Blister Copper RCs Rose Above 1,000 Yuan/mt, Market Supply Faces New Variables in April [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says Chinese blister copper refining charges (RCs) rebounded sharply in late March and moved above 1,000 yuan/mt in April, driven by increased availability of secondary scrap raw material after copper price gains. Early-month price pullbacks may reduce scrap selling, risking future supply tightening if copper does not keep rising.

title: Versamet Royalties Corporation: Versamet Acquires a Copper Stream from Endeavour Silver on Its Acquisition of Compañia Minera Kolpa
summary: Versamet Royalties agreed to buy a copper stream from Endeavour Silver’s Kolpa polymetallic mine in Peru for $35 million, with ongoing payments tied to 10% of the spot copper price per tonne delivered. Kolpa produced copper in 2024 and the transaction is expected to close within 60 days.

title: Ceibo Appoints Darryl Steane as Chief Development Officer to Accelerate Copper Technology Commercialization
summary: Ceibo appointed Darryl Steane as Chief Development Officer to accelerate commercialization of its copper extraction technology, claiming up to 80% copper recovery from sulfide ores using on-site processing. The company says the move supports scaling to meet rising electrification-driven copper demand, though no near-term production increase is confirmed.

title: BRP selling Australian aluminum boat maker Telwater to Yamaha Motor Co.
summary: BRP is selling Telwater, Australia’s biggest aluminum boat maker, to Yamaha’s subsidiary and selling Alumacraft to Bryton Marine Group. The deals follow BRP’s shift toward powersports. Financial terms are undisclosed and approvals are required, with closes expected by mid- and early-2025.

title: 1844 Resources Inc.: 1844 Resources Announces Extension of Option Agreement with Nickel North
summary: 1844 Resources announced an extension of the outside date on its option agreement with Nickel North for the Hawk Ridge nickel/copper project, citing delays in preparing an updated geological report. The unit private placement details are also provided, subject to exchange approvals. No production or supply changes are described.

title: Copper giant Codelco secures US$666mn facility
summary: Japan’s JBIC approved a US$466mn loan (total US$666mn with a private lender) to Chile’s Codelco to secure stable imports of Chilean copper concentrates for Japanese manufacturers. JBIC cites rising copper demand from decarbonisation and notes Japan’s reliance on imports, using export finance to ensure supply.

title: First Quantum pulls back from arbitration on Panama copper mine
summary: First Quantum reportedly pulls back from arbitration related to its Panama copper mine. This suggests reduced near-term legal and operational uncertainty around copper supply in Panama. With disruption risk easing, market expectations for copper availability could improve, providing modest support to copper prices in the coming days and weeks.

title: Copper market grows wary of what follows its U.S. tariff rush
summary: News focuses on impending U.S. Section 232 copper import tariffs and uncertainty over the timing/level. Traders race to clear physical copper before tariffs, while LME stocks have fallen and arbitrage tightness may be shorter-lived. Analysts disagree: some expect higher copper, others warn of a rapid price crash.

title: First Quantum backs off Panama arbitration claims, opening door to reopening copper mine
summary: First Quantum agreed to drop/suspend arbitration claims against Panama and its related free-trade proceedings, keeping the door open to a resolution that could eventually reopen the Cobre Panama copper mine. The move follows improved government relations and export authorization for stockpiled copper, supporting positive copper supply expectations despite ongoing legal uncertainty and protests.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.02% Lower at $5.0190 — Data Talk
summary: The piece is a brief market data update stating Comex Copper futures settled 0.02% lower at $5.0190. The change is minimal, implying no strong new bullish or bearish catalyst signal. It mainly reflects routine session price movement rather than a substantial shift in demand, supply, or risk.

title: Nebraska deputies see spike in copper wire stolen from irrigation systems
summary: Nebraska sheriff’s offices report a spike in thefts of copper wire from center-pivot irrigation systems, citing higher copper prices—up about 30% since early 2025—as well as rising tariffs. Thousands of feet of wire were stolen in multiple counties, with losses totaling tens of thousands of dollars. No arrests reported.

title: Chile's Codelco to supply copper concentrate to India's Adani Group-owned smelter
summary: Codelco said it will supply copper concentrate to Adani Group’s Kutch Copper smelter in Gujarat, with deliveries starting this year. The Reuters report notes India’s copper imports have risen since the 2018 Sterlite closure. The smelter began operating a year ago and is expanding into wires and cables.

title: Hyundai Mobis secures low-carbon aluminum to boost green manufacturing
summary: Hyundai Mobis agreed to buy 15 kt of solar-powered, low-carbon aluminum from Emirates Global Aluminum in a $42.3m deal. The lower-emissions metal is intended for lightweight auto components and to help meet carbon-neutral goals and EU CBAM requirements. Adoption timing is not yet set.

title: Energy Capital & Power  / Press release | Zambia Bolsters Copper Exploration Ahead of 2031 Target
summary: Zambia announced initiatives to accelerate copper exploration toward a 2031 production target, including a digital mining licensing system, repossession and reallocation of mining licenses, aerial geophysical surveys, a minerals investment vehicle, and cooperation agreements. It also highlights renewed drilling and expansion plans by major industry players, which may support copper sentiment.

title: Overseas Secondary Copper Raw Material Imports Decline, How Do Import Traders Do?
summary: Customs data show China’s secondary copper raw-material imports fell in January-February 2025, driven by tariff uncertainty in US-China trade and widening SHFE/LME price spreads hurting hedging economics. Malaysia and Thailand tightened scrap import standards and inspections for environmental reasons, shifting flows and weighing on volumes. Overall copper feedstock inflows look weaker.

title: Trump administration adds beer, can imports to 25% US aluminum tariffs
summary: The Trump administration added beer imports and empty aluminum cans to a list of aluminum-derivative tariffs, imposing a 25% duty collected from April 4. Reuters says the policy could raise costs for beer imports worth $7.5 billion in 2024 and influence short-term aluminum-related demand via can supply chains.

title: Trump tariffs on steel, aluminum could squeeze Illinois apartment developers, leading to higher rents
summary: Chicago apartment developers may delay new projects because newly imposed tariffs on steel and aluminum raise costs amid high interest rates and labor expenses. The article links these tariff-driven cost pressures to slower construction starts, which can weaken near-term demand outlooks for aluminum used in building materials.

title: Novelis aluminum plant in Chesterfield to close May 30
summary: Novelis’ aluminum plant in Chesterfield is set to close on May 30. The stoppage is likely to reduce near-term output and availability tied to aluminium supply chains, potentially tightening supply conditions for aluminium products and supporting prices over the next days to a few weeks.

title: China Aims to Maintain Leadership in Aluminum Sector
summary: The article says China’s MIIT plan aims to green and restructure aluminum production but comes as China nears its capacity ceiling and production growth is expected to slow. It suggests export cutbacks and higher reliance on recycling may shift supply, while US tariffs on aluminum imports add uncertainty, likely weighing on prices.

title: Breweries React to Trump Tariffs Impact on Aluminum Prices
summary: Breweries and packaging suppliers say Trump’s 25% tariff on imported aluminum, effective March 12, is already feeding through to can costs. Reported increases are small per can but likely larger for high-volume can orders. Firms also cite aluminum price volatility and supply-timing uncertainty from tariff headlines.

title: Glencore announces closure date for Mount Isa Mines' copper operations
summary: Glencore confirmed it will close Mount Isa Mines’ underground copper operation in about 12 weeks, with the last ore pulled on July 29–30. The move cuts jobs and production from a major Australian copper producer, while the smelter/refinery future is also under review amid weak global smelting economics.

title: US Excludes Steel, Aluminum, Auto from Reciprocal Tariff
summary: The article says the US excluded steel, aluminum, and automobiles from reciprocal tariff measures. By keeping aluminum out of the tariff regime, importers and downstream users should face less cost pressure and fewer supply disruptions, which can support near-term aluminum price sentiment over coming days.

title: How Trump tariffs on steel, aluminum may impact funeral expenses
summary: A March 12, 25% tariff on aluminum and steel is raising production costs for items commonly used in funerals, including caskets. Some funeral homes expect vendor price increases and anticipate passing higher costs to consumers as information arrives, even though effects are still early (about three weeks).

title: Australian Aluminium Council welcomes new Fed Gov't statement
summary: Australia’s Aluminium Council welcomed a new Government Statement of Expectations for the Anti-Dumping Commission and noted multiple aluminium industry cases are before the Commission. The AAC argues anti-dumping action can reduce trade diversion and protect domestic manufacturers. New downstream members reinforce industry representation across the aluminium chain.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | Newcastle Herald
summary: Maintenance workers at Tomago Aluminium have nearly unanimously endorsed the right to industrial action after rejecting the company’s offer. The dispute centers on a proposed 15% pay rise over three years and leave provisions. Negotiations will resume, with a potential production disruption risk for the plant.

title: Canadian steel and aluminum suffer Trump's ire while mining sector spared for now
summary: Trump’s executive order largely spares Canadian USMCA-compliant mining from new reciprocal tariffs, easing near-term tariff risk for many minerals. However, existing 25% U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum remain. Copper is said to be exempt for now but under study, leaving uncertainty ahead.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | Manning River Times
summary: About 160 maintenance workers at Tomago Aluminium nearly unanimously voted for industrial action after rejecting the company’s offer. The dispute centers on wages and conditions, including a proposed 15% pay rise over three years. The risk of work stoppages may disrupt aluminium output, affecting short-term supply sentiment.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | The Macleay Argus
summary: Workers at Tomago Aluminium voted to support industrial action after rejecting the company’s enterprise agreement offer. The dispute centres on wages (seeking a 15% pay rise over three years), leave conditions and mental health days. Escalation could disrupt plant maintenance, tightening short-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | Port Macquarie News
summary: Maintenance workers at Tomago Aluminium voted nearly unanimously to support potential industrial action after rejecting the company’s latest enterprise agreement offer. They are seeking a 15% pay rise over three years and other leave and mental-health provisions. The dispute may affect plant operations, but no shutdown is confirmed.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | Port Stephens Examiner
summary: Workers at Tomago Aluminium endorsed the right to take industrial action after rejecting the company’s enterprise agreement offer. The dispute centers on a 15% pay rise over three years and conditions such as annual leave and mental health days. Potential industrial action could disrupt output and weigh on aluminium prices short term.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | The Scone Advocate
summary: Maintenance workers at Tomago Aluminium endorsed the right to take industrial action after rejecting a company offer, seeking a 15% pay rise over three years and improved leave/mental health provisions. The vote increases the risk of disruption at the aluminium smelter, potentially tightening short-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: China tightens regulations on new alumina plant construction to address overcapacity
summary: China’s MIIT issued an action plan to curb overcapacity in the aluminium value chain, tightening approvals for new alumina plant construction. Firms must secure adequate bauxite supply and projects in heavily polluted areas won’t be approved, aiming to slow alumina capacity expansion and help stabilise related alumina and aluminium pricing.

title: Japan's Q2 aluminium premium crashes to five-quarter-low as US tariff intervenes trade
summary: Japan’s Q2 2025 aluminium outbound premium fell to about USD 182/tonne, a 20% decline from Q1, the first quarterly drop in five quarters. Participants link the weakness to US 25% automotive import tariffs effective April 2, potentially weakening Asian demand and forcing suppliers to accept lower spot premiums.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Maintenance workers at Tomago Aluminium endorsed industrial action after rejecting a company offer. The dispute centers on a proposed 15% pay rise over three years and additional leave/mental health provisions. Tomago had negotiated a separate operators’ deal at 4% annually. Further industrial action could disrupt aluminium production near term.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | The Advertiser - Cessnock
summary: Maintenance workers at Tomago Aluminium voted nearly unanimously to support industrial action after rejecting the company’s enterprise agreement offer. The dispute centers on a 15% pay rise over three years and other conditions. Higher strike risk could disrupt output at the aluminium plant, supporting near-term price expectations.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | The Singleton Argus
summary: Workers at Tomago Aluminium endorsed the right to industrial action after rejecting the company’s latest enterprise agreement offer. The AMWU/ETU members are seeking a 15% pay rise over three years and improved leave and health provisions. Potential work disruption raises short-term aluminium supply risk.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Maintenance workers at Tomago Aluminium voted nearly unanimously to endorse industrial action after rejecting the company’s enterprise agreement offer. The dispute centers on a proposed 15% pay rise and leave/mental health provisions. Tomago’s maintenance labor disruption risk could reduce near-term aluminium output and pressure prices downward.

title: Tomago Aluminium workers vote for industrial action | Muswellbrook Chronicle
summary: Maintenance workers at Tomago Aluminium voted nearly unanimously to support industrial action after rejecting the company’s enterprise agreement offer. The dispute centers on a 15% pay rise over three years and other conditions like annual leave and mental health days. Potential work disruption could affect aluminium output in the near term.

title: Donald Trump tariffs on aluminum and steel could raise beer prices, affect SoCal breweries
summary: SoCal craft brewery suppliers warned that March tariffs could raise costs, with a 25% tariff on aluminum and steel cited. The brewery cans 40% of beer in aluminum and uses steel fermenters. Brewery owners expect potential pass-through to consumers if aluminum/steel costs rise further, affecting nearby material markets.

title: Revenues Received from Copper Concentrate Sales   | Company Announcement
summary: Marula Mining reported that payments due for its delayed initial trial copper concentrate shipment from the Kinusi Copper Mine in Tanzania have started and are now received for the first two trucks (~50 tonnes of a 250-tonne trial). A second shipment is also underway for longer-term offtake finalization.

title: Chile unveils plans to optimize copper and lithium extraction
summary: EU and Fraunhofer Chile launched the OPTIMINER project in Santiago to optimize extraction and processing of critical raw materials, including copper. Funded under Horizon Europe, it targets higher energy/water efficiency, better waste management, and sustainable mining tech, potentially improving copper production outlook and supporting prices.

title: US exempts steel, aluminium and copper from reciprocal tariffs
summary: The US declared a national emergency and announced new reciprocal trade tariffs from 5 April 2025. Copper and aluminium imports are exempt from the reciprocal tariffs, though other existing tariffs may still apply (e.g., Section 232). Exemption likely lowers near-term US cost risk for copper and aluminium.

title: US exempts steel, aluminium and copper from reciprocal tariffs
summary: The Trump administration declared a national emergency and will impose reciprocal tariffs starting 5 April 2025, but it exempts imports of steel, aluminium, copper and certain minerals not available in the US. These tariffs can be adjusted with retaliation. The move limits direct near-term tariff-driven pressure on copper and aluminium prices.

title: Ero Copper Corp. (ERO) Fell after a Cut in Copper Production Guidance
summary: Ero Copper Corp. shares fell after the miner cut 2024 copper production guidance, citing power disruptions that hampered the ramp-up of the Tucuma mine. With power issues resolved, management expects to meet 2025 guidance and double production. The guidance cut implies weaker near-term copper supply expectations.

title: The Operating Rate of Aluminum Downstream Terminated Eight Consecutive Increases[SMM Weekly Downstream Survey]
summary: SMM’s weekly survey shows aluminum downstream operating rates edged lower (62.6% WoW), with declines across primary alloy, plate/sheet, extrusion, foil, and secondary alloy, while wire and cable stayed steady at ~60% on strong power-grid tenders and PV installation demand. Orders remain weak in traditional end markets and exports face tariff/trade uncertainty.

title: The Price Of High-Nickel Pig Iron Has Slightly Increased, But May Face Downward Pressure In The Short Term
summary: High-nickel pig iron prices edged up to 1030.25 yuan per nickel point, supported by low smelter inventories and cost support. However, weak downstream stainless demand and rising raw material costs reduce procurement willingness. Indonesia policy delays and a stronger USD pressure pure nickel sentiment. Next week discounts may widen, implying bearish risk for nickel.

title: Indonesian nickel: new issue of MINE live now!
summary: MINE’s April 2025 issue reviews Indonesia’s rapid nickel growth and highlights upcoming challenges, including decreasing production quotas and plans to raise royalties. These policy shifts could reduce near-term nickel supply availability and influence market expectations, potentially providing upward support for nickel prices. No similar copper or aluminium signals are discussed.

title: ASX: Glencore seeks bailouts for Australian copper smelter and refinery
summary: Glencore is lobbying Queensland and federal authorities for a bailout for its Mt Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery, citing heavy losses. The move follows a broader industry crisis linked to rising primarily Chinese production that has pressured global metals markets.

title: Chile's Codelco to supply copper concentrate to India's Adani Group
summary: Chile’s Codelco plans to supply copper concentrate to India’s Adani Group. The deal directly relates to the physical flow of copper concentrate into the market, influencing expectations for near-term availability of refining feedstock and potentially copper supply premiums over the coming days to weeks.

title: Beer, aluminum can imports subject to 25% tariffs
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department posted notices for 25% duties on imported beer and empty aluminum cans, effective just after midnight Friday. These tariffs apply to shipments from any country and build on earlier aluminum tariff lists. Brewers and can suppliers expect higher costs and potential demand disruption, pressuring aluminium-related import expectations.

title: Comex Copper Settles 4.23% Lower at $4.8110 — Data Talk
summary: The report notes that Comex copper futures settled 4.23% lower at $4.8110. This settlement level reflects a sharp day-over-day decline, signalling bearish near-term market sentiment for copper prices.

title: No Arbitrage, No Rally: U.S. Aluminum Premium Stabilizes as Global Prices Weaken [SMM Analysis]
summary: Trump’s reciprocal tariffs extend the 25% duty on unwrought aluminium and aluminium products, including cans, raising estimated landed import costs above the U.S. Midwest premium threshold and squeezing margins. With weaker U.S. PMI and confidence, JIT buying replaces stockpiling, and risk-off trade uncertainty pushes LME 3M aluminium prices lower.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Turns to Zambia Following Copper Success in DRC
summary: Ivanhoe Mines secured exploration licenses in Zambia after success at DRC’s Kamoa-Kakula and plans environmental studies and drilling work to map copper targets. The move could broaden copper supply expectations across the Central African Copperbelt, but it involves early exploration with no near-term output impact.

title: European brewers' concern over US aluminium tariff move
summary: Brewers in Europe are concerned after the US moved to include beer and empty aluminium cans in aluminium-levied “derivative products.” The notice also follows broad US reciprocal tariffs, with a 25% aluminium-related tariff and a 20% EU-wide tariff. Breers seek clarification on which beer is captured.

title: Tariffs to Push Copper Prices 8%-10% Lower: Citi's Layton
summary: Citi’s commodities research head Max Layton says Trump administration tariffs are expected to pressure commodity markets, specifically copper. He forecasts copper prices could drop 8%-10%, implying weaker demand and/or less favorable trade flows from tariff measures. The note reflects near-term price risk for copper within coming weeks.

title: Robbie Katter slams Glencore over Mount Isa copper mine closure | North Queensland Register
summary: Glencore plans to close the Mount Isa copper mine by end-July, with last ore extracted July 29–30, risking further uncertainty around the Mount Isa smelter and downstream processing. Glencore cites weak global smelting margins and falling treatment/refining charges. Local stakeholders warn copper supply and jobs will be disrupted.

title: Glencore seeks Australian government bailout for local copper assets
summary: Glencore approached Australia’s federal and Queensland governments over the future of its Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery. It cited studies to end its Mount Isa mines in 2025 and said copper processing is under pressure from the biggest drops in treatment/refining charges in 25 years and heavy subsidies elsewhere.

title: Vedanta achieves record aluminium and zinc production in Q4
summary: Vedanta said it achieved historic highs in aluminium output in Q4 and FY ended March 31, 2025, with annual aluminium production up 2% and Q4 up about 1%. Alumina production rose 9% annually but saw temporary supply-chain disruptions that normalized by year end.

title: Jamaica Bauxite Mining aims to mitigate tariff impact through green port initiatives
summary: Jamaica Bauxite Mining says US import tariffs could pressure its bauxite exports because many buyers are in the United States. To mitigate costs and sustain shipments, it is converting ports into “green” sites, including installing solar PV to cut energy use, supporting bauxite outflows that feed aluminium.

title: Tariffs Take the Shine Off Copper
summary: London copper fell about 2% on the week after Trump’s broad tariff announcement raised fears of a trade war and slower global growth, weighing on metal demand. Even with copper initially spared, the US tariff investigation and potential for duties in weeks kept sentiment bearish.

title: 'I was sold': Venture capitalist describes how alleged nickel conman Ng Yu Zhi gained his trust
summary: A Singapore venture capitalist testified that he invested millions into an alleged nickel scheme run by Ng Yu Zhi after checking nickel prices and being assured returns. Prosecutors say there was no real physical nickel trading; investor funds paid earlier investors. The fraud unraveled in early 2021, damaging trust and nickel-related trading confidence.

title: Indonesia's nickel market stranglehold tightens, again
summary: Indonesia dominates global nickel supply, with rising production over 2018–2024 and major Chinese-linked investment. Despite a recent nickel price decline linked to faster supply growth and slower EV demand, the government is considering production quota cuts (and royalty increases), which could reduce supply and lift prices. Mentions recent support from tightening expectations.

title: Copper plunges more than 5% in the biggest drop since July 2022
summary: The article’s headline reports copper falling by more than 5%, describing the biggest drop since July 2022. While the excerpt doesn’t provide specific drivers, the magnitude and framing imply strong immediate downside pressure for copper prices in the coming days.

title: Copper Plunges Most in 5 Years as Tariffs Slam Metals and Miners
summary: Copper prices are reported to have fallen the most in five years after tariffs “slam” metals and miners. The headline suggests tariffs are quickly worsening expectations for copper demand and/or raising costs and uncertainty for mining and supply, likely driving urgent selling in the near term.

title: Kamoa Copper and CrossBoundary Energy partner for renewable mining power
summary: Kamoa Copper, one of the world’s largest copper mines in the DRC, signed a power purchase agreement with CrossBoundary Energy for 30 MW of renewable baseload power (solar PV plus battery storage). The deal replaces diesel generation, cuts emissions, and is expected to enhance cost and reliability at the mine.

title: ANDURAND CAPITAL CEASES TO RELY ON ALTERNATIVE MONTHLY REPORTING SYSTEM; URGES SPROTT TO FIX SPROTT COPPER VEHICLE
summary: Andurand Capital Management said it will stop filing under an Alternative Monthly Reporting System for its stake in the Sprott Physical Copper Trust and urged Sprott to adjust trust redemption terms to better align unit prices with physical copper. The units currently trade at an ~18% discount to NAV, reflecting liquidity issues rather than copper fundamentals.

title: APO Group - Africa Newsroom  / Press release | Kamoa Copper and CrossBoundary Energy sign agreement for a groundbreaking baseload renewable energy system in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
summary: Kamoa Copper signed a PPA with CrossBoundary Energy to supply 30MW baseload renewable power to the Kamoa-Kakula copper mining complex in DRC, including 222MWp solar PV and 526MWh battery storage. The deal is expected to reduce diesel generator use and supports forthcoming on-site smelter ramp-up in 2Q 2025.

title: Zambia projects 1-mln-ton copper production in 2025-Xinhua
summary: Zambia expects copper production to reach about one million metric tons in 2025, up from 820,676 tons in 2024, driven by expanding existing mines, reviving old ones, and starting new projects. The government plans $6 billion in investments, with supply growing further toward a three-million-ton target.

title: 10 Best Copper Stocks to Buy According to Wall Street Analysts
summary: The article highlights a 26% jump in U.S. copper futures by end-March 2025 and says it was driven by new U.S. tariff increases. It notes importers rushed to bring copper into the U.S. before higher duties, boosting physical deliveries and supporting higher domestic copper prices.

title: Copper Posts Biggest Weekly Drop Since Covid Crash As Tariff War Hammers Commodities
summary: The article headline says copper posted its biggest weekly decline since the Covid crash as a tariff war hammers commodities. The direct connection between tariffs and risk-off sentiment suggests weakening near-term demand expectations and downward pressure on copper prices over the coming days and weeks.
