Premiums assessed April 8 were unchanged, suggesting limited near-term price pressure.

title: ALRO Commissions Aluminium Plate Cutting Saw In Wake Of RON8M Investment
summary: ALRO Slatina commissioned a state-of-the-art aluminium plate cutting saw following a RON 8 million investment to strengthen its high value-added aluminium processing capabilities. The update signals incremental expansion of aluminium fabrication capacity, but it does not indicate a major immediate supply cut or demand surge, limiting near-term price pressure.

title: Northeast Wisconsin breweries prepare for potential rise in costs due to aluminum tariffs
summary: Wisconsin breweries that package beer in aluminum cans are monitoring 25% tariffs on foreign steel and aluminum, which started last month and were not fully paused. Breweries expect tariff charges and higher costs for imported can materials, with potential price pressure over coming months despite some domestic sourcing.

title: Low-carbon Aluminium: Guinea Must Go Green to Locally Process Its Bauxite
summary: Guinea’s bauxite producer position is being reshaped by a government push to develop local alumina and aluminium processing powered by renewable electricity. Low‑carbon aluminium has emerging premiums and new indices, driven by IRENA’s demand outlook, while Guinea expands hydro and solar capacity to meet carbon constraints.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Closes $1M Charity Flow-Through
summary: First Atlantic Nickel closed a C$1.07M charity flow-through private placement to fund Phase 2 drilling at its Atlantic Nickel Project in Newfoundland. The company highlights its nickel-iron alloy (awaruite) and proceeds timing/renunciation mechanics, but the financing itself is unlikely to materially move global nickel prices immediately.

title: India's Adani Enterprises to start copper smelter in four weeks
summary: Adani Enterprises says its Kutch Copper facility will start refining copper concentrate and produce anodes within four weeks, with capacity expansion approvals. The move comes as Asian smelters face negative TC/RCs due to tight concentrate supply. Copper prices rebounded sharply on tariff pause, but the new smelter adds supply expectations.

title: Copper output from Chile's Codelco slips 6% in February
summary: Cochilco data show Chile’s Codelco copper output fell 6% year-over-year in February to 98,100 metric tons. Output at Collahuasi dropped 62% to 17,000 tons. While BHP’s Escondida rose 16%, the overall Chile supply picture is skewed toward lower copper volumes.

title: New Caledonia's nickel mine shutdown leaves ghost towns behind
summary: New Caledonia’s Koniambo nickel mine and factory shut down in August after Glencore exited the operation, with smelters turned off last year. The closure halted production of high-grade nickel (up to ~60,000 tonnes/year) and leaves thousands unemployed. Buyers may not emerge soon, extending the supply shock.

title: Hudbay, unions sign agreement on Copper World construction
summary: Hudbay Minerals and several unions signed a letter of commitment to provide union contractors an opportunity in building the Copper World open-pit copper mine near Tucson. While permits are in place, lawsuits could still challenge approvals. The agreement signals progress toward construction workforce planning and potential copper supply continuity.

title: Hydropower surge sparks new copper phase at Kamoa-Kakula
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says Kamoa-Kakula has entered a new growth phase after starting its on-site copper smelter. Additional imported hydropower (rising from 70MW to 100MW) supported record March copper production and higher concentrator throughput, enabling more anode output and improved cost performance.

title: Three Cantonment Men Charged With Theft, Sale Of Nearly Two Tons Of Phone, Copper Wire : NorthEscambia.com
summary: Three men in Cantonment, Florida were charged with stealing and selling nearly two tons of phone cables and uninsulated copper utility wire. The wire, tied to AT&T and Pike Electric, was burned to remove insulation and sold as scrap to a yard in Alabama. Additional fiber lines were reportedly damaged.

title: High-Nickel Pig Iron Faces Largest Single-Week Decline This Year Amid Macro and Market Shifts
summary: High-nickel pig iron prices (SMM 8-12%) fell RMB 19.35 per nickel point week-on-week to RMB 1,010.9, the largest decline this year. The drop is linked to weaker stainless-steel demand on macro concerns from reciprocal tariffs, cautious procurement, and expectations of continued nickel price pressure despite some supply and cost factors.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market-4.11
summary: SMM’s Indonesian nickel market review says global nickel prices fell sharply on renewed Trump tariff policy and PNBP expectations, dragging down high-grade NPI prices and pressuring profits. Indonesian nickel ore premiums are stable due to tight supply, but demand weakens. Refined nickel supply also continues ramp-up.

title: Future of copper mining: global demand, strategic alliances
summary: Anglo American’s CEO says the world needs around 80 large copper mines by 2040 and highlights Chile’s copper supply outlook. Los Bronces production fell in 2024 due to care and maintenance, while a joint mine plan with Codelco is expected to improve output mainly from 2030, subject to permitting delays.

title: Impact of tariffs on Freeport-McMoRan copper production
summary: Freeport CEO Kathleen Quirk said US tariffs and possible Section 232 measures could slow economic growth and keep copper prices weak, putting US production growth at risk. She noted higher costs likely pass through the supply chain and that demand impacts are already appearing, despite long-term copper fundamentals remaining intact.

title: New Steel and Aluminum Tariffs in Effect | Troutman Pepper Locke
summary: The alert details new U.S. Section 232 tariffs effective March 12, 2025 that raise and expand duties on imported steel, aluminum, and certain downstream derivative products, including removal of most exclusion processes and added documentation requirements. It targets steel/aluminum supply chains, with no stated copper linkage.

title: AFCMA APPLAUDS U.S. INTERNATIONAL TRADE COMMISSION DECISION REGARDING IMPORTS OF DISPOSABLE ALUMINUM CONTAINERS FROM CHINA
summary: The U.S. International Trade Commission issued a unanimous finding that unfairly traded imports of disposable aluminum containers from China materially injured U.S. producers. The case will move to Commerce for antidumping and countervailing duties. Industry expects reduced low-priced imports and relief for domestic manufacturers.

title: Ghost towns left, in the wake of New Caledonia nickel mine shutdown
summary: New Caledonia’s Indigenous-controlled nickel mine has closed, leaving local communities facing uncertainty. The article ties this to Indonesia boosting global nickel supply with lower prices, suggesting immediate pressure on nickel demand-supply balance. It implies bearish sentiment for nickel as market participants weigh both supply loss and oversupply elsewhere.

title: Billion-dollar nickel scam: Singaporean Ng Yu Zhi spent S$7mil on luxury cars he gave to wife, girlfriends
summary: Singapore court testimony described a nickel-trading scam accused fraudster Ng Yu Zhi used to attract S$1.46 billion from investors. A liquidator said the nickel business allegedly did not exist, and funds were used for luxury car purchases. A witness also noted limited personal investment into the nickel scheme.

title: Steel and aluminium shipments being warehoused in Windsor
summary: Tariffs aimed at U.S.-bound goods are causing steel and Canadian aluminium shipments through Windsor to be warehoused or rerouted to avoid a 25% charge. Backlogs already exist for U.S. aluminium coming from Canada, and the diversion is expected to disrupt automotive supply chains.

title: Copper prices continued to rise, and traders' cargo pick-up speed rebounded.
summary: Secondary copper rod enterprises’ operating rate rebounded to 40.18% in March, helped by rising copper prices and widened spreads that encouraged trader arbitrage ordering. Inventories increased only slightly and finished goods digestion was limited, but restocking demand supported improved order-taking. April forecasts point to weaker activity after Sino-US trade tensions hurt prices.

title: Blast at Nagpur aluminium plant kills 5, injures 10 in massive fire outbreak
summary: A blast and large fire at MMP Limited’s aluminium plant in Nagpur’s Umred MIDC killed five workers and injured 10. The explosion occurred in a polished tubing/foil unit using raw aluminium powder, which is highly flammable. Multiple fire brigades took 15–16 hours to control the blaze, disrupting operations.

title: Alumina Market Faces Downward Pressure Amid Bauxite Price Discrepancies
summary: Alumina prices have declined sharply since late 2024, outpacing the slower drop in bauxite. SMM’s cost-profit model shows the industry shifting from profits to losses. With reduced margin and weaker-cost pass-through, producers are expected to expand production cuts, increasing near-term aluminium supply tightness concerns.

title: Iran's aluminum output down by nearly 5% in year to March
summary: IMIDRO data show Iran produced about 604,526 mt of aluminum ingots in the year to March 20, down from 635,596 mt a year earlier, with output declines across major smelters including SALCO. The same report notes higher alumina, aluminum hydroxide and bauxite production.

title: Trump tariffs: Commodity super cycle could boost gold, silver, copper
summary: CNBC discusses whether Trump’s reciprocal tariffs could trigger a commodities “super-cycle.” It cites higher copper front-month prices but warns tariffs may raise slowdown risks that pressure copper short term. It says nickel is unlikely to surge, while aluminium is among materials expected to be repriced upward as trade tensions persist.

title: S. Korea Requests Favorable Treatment as Copper Products Face Potential US Tariffs
summary: South Korea is reportedly requesting favorable treatment because copper products may face potential U.S. tariffs. If implemented, the tariffs would likely raise end-user costs and curb near-term demand expectations for copper, creating downward pressure on copper prices in the coming days to weeks.

title: Infill drill testing firms up Ardea high-grade WA nickel deposit
summary: Ardea Resources completed 287 infill reverse circulation drill holes at its Goongarrie Hub nickel project in Western Australia, reporting multiple high-grade nickel intercepts at Big Four and Scotia Dam. Management says results support potential resource upgrades and pit optimization work in its ongoing definitive feasibility study, which can strengthen near-term nickel sentiment.

title: Korea says copper tariffs risk jobs, investments in US battery sector
summary: South Korea urged the US to avoid imposing Section 232 tariffs on Korean copper products, arguing the imports are small and not a national-security threat. It warned tariffs could raise US domestic copper prices and disrupt copper foil supply for battery makers, threatening investments and jobs amid an ongoing Commerce review.

title: [SMM Analysis]Copper Market Changes Under the Cloud of Sino-US Tariffs, Refined Copper Rod Production in April May Exceed Expectations
summary: SMM reports refined copper rod operating rates rose in March but missed expectations, with consumption suppressed by secondary copper rod and some destocking-related maintenance. Copper prices fell sharply after trade-war tariff concerns. However, new orders and on-hand orders increased, supporting improved consumption and an April operating-rate forecast of 71.44%.

title: The supply of secondary copper raw materials decreased, and the operating rate of copper anode producers using scrap is expected to decline in April【SMM Analysis】
summary: SMM reports March 2025 copper anode producer operating rates rose MoM overall, but expects April to fall to 48.80%. Ore-based rates are projected to edge up, while scrap-based rates drop sharply to 38.35% due to reduced scrap supply after copper’s mid-April price fall, import gaps, and producer losses.

title: Goldman Sachs cuts aluminium price forecast on weaker growth outlook
summary: Goldman Sachs lowered its aluminium price forecast following economists’ downgrade to global growth after Trump’s tariff plans. The bank expects aluminium prices to fall toward $2,000/t in Q3 2025 and sees a larger 2025 surplus, citing weaker demand growth, despite expecting prices to recover later.

title: U.S. Steel and Aluminum Tariffs Reinstated Amid Broader Trade Shi
summary: The piece outlines U.S. reinstatement of full tariffs on steel (25%) and aluminum (25%) with a higher China rate and a 90-day pause that excludes steel and aluminum. It emphasizes continued elevated tariff burdens until at least July 9, 2025, likely weighing on aluminum-linked demand and prices near term.

title: Canadian steel, aluminum to be used in Canada's military: Liberals
summary: Canada’s Liberals announced a defense procurement plan that prioritizes buying Canadian raw materials, including steel and aluminum, to rebuild and rearm the military. The initiative includes streamlining procurement rules and expanding naval assets, implying increased demand for domestic aluminum supplies in the near term.

title: Copper gains on tariff exemptions and China stimulus hopes
summary: Copper prices rose about 0.6% as markets benefited from U.S. tariff exemptions on some electronics, hopes for additional Chinese stimulus, and a weaker dollar. The piece also cites technical support after copper’s prior drop and notes China’s loan growth and TSF acceleration, boosting near-term demand expectations.

title: Clean Energy Transition Inc.: transition.inc Files Technical Report for Aurora Nickel Project Updated Mineral Resource Estimate
summary: Clean Energy Transition Inc. filed an NI 43-101 Technical Report supporting an updated Mineral Resource Estimate for its Aurora Nickel Project in Ontario. The Indicated Resource totals 10.06 Mt at 0.42% nickel, with open-pit and underground deposits. The company frames the update as strengthening the low-carbon nickel opportunity.

title: Romanian aluminum producer Alro warns of imminent cheap imports from China
summary: Romanian aluminum producer Alro warns that U.S. tariffs could push cheap Chinese and Indonesian aluminum exports into Europe, overwhelming domestic supply. The firm says it may gain a small U.S. quota advantage, but expects dumping-priced imports from the east to “suffocate” the European market in the near term.

title: How copper producers are responding to tariff chaos
summary: Copper producers in Chile discuss tariff “chaos” after reciprocal US tariffs that temporarily exempt copper, while a Section 232 investigation could impose future copper duties. The piece links tariff uncertainty to falling copper prices, rising Comex inventories near 112,000 tons, weaker arbitrage, and tight concentrate-driven record-low TC/RCs.

title: Rio Tinto Copper CEO says tariffs create volatility in market
summary: Rio Tinto’s copper CEO said US tariffs are driving copper market volatility but viewed as edge adjustments rather than a fundamental demand/supply shift. She cited copper exemption from a continuing 10% tariff, potential tailwinds for domestic US operations, and challenges because tariffs also affect Rio Tinto’s US-bound aluminium business.

title: Kincora Copper Limited: Kincora Copper: Investor Briefing Webinar - Sixth Asset Level Agreement
summary: Kincora Copper said it will hold an investor webinar after amending an earn-in and joint venture agreement with AngloGold Ashanti to pursue a second joint venture in Australia’s Northern Junee-Narromine Belt. The partnership supports total exploration expenditures up to $100 million, but remains exploration-stage and not an immediate production change.

title: U.S. GoldMining Inc. Announces Plans to Commence an Initial Economic Assessment At Whistler Gold-Copper Project, Alaska
summary: U.S. GoldMining plans to start an initial economic assessment for its Whistler gold-copper project in Alaska. Management cites strong metal prices and recent drilling results as justification for moving forward, including use of a higher gold price assumption. No production timing or supply changes are announced.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Drills Significant Nickel-Copper Mineralization Intercept at Tamarack During Feasibility Study Drilling
summary: Talon Metals said drill hole 25TK0561 at its Tamarack nickel-copper project intersected 16.09 meters of mixed massive sulphide with 10%–80% sulphide content, potentially extending mineralization at depth. Management links the result to earlier BHEM modeling success and suggests potential tonnage addition as feasibility work progresses.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Drills Significant Nickel-Copper Mineralization Intercept at Tamarack During Feasibility Study Drilling
summary: Talon Metals announced a mixed massive sulphide intercept (16.09m) at its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project, with sulphide content indicating higher nickel grades. The company frames results as extending the CGO East Zone below the current resource and supporting potential early tonnage, but it remains feasibility-stage exploration news.

title: Kincora Copper: Second Major Earn-In Secured with AngloGold Ashanti
summary: Kincora Copper announced an expanded earn-in/JV with AngloGold Ashanti to broaden drilling across the Nyngan, Nevertire and Nevertire South projects in NSW, targeting copper-gold porphyry systems. The update notes ongoing scout drilling and prior anomalous copper results, but remains exploration-focused with no production or logistics changes.

title: Chile pushes back against Trump copper tariff probe
summary: Chile, Canada and Peru told the U.S. not to apply Section 232 copper tariffs, arguing copper imports support U.S. supply-chain and defense needs. The probe was launched in February but has no detailed findings yet. The suppliers and Freeport-McMoRan oppose duties, warning tariffs could benefit China.

title: Surge in Bauxite Arrivals and Shipments Indicates Strong Import Outlook
summary: Port data show bauxite arrivals at Chinese domestic ports jumping to 5.7141 million mt in the latest week, while departures from Guinea and Australia indicate continued inbound flow. Analysts expect stronger imports in May-June, but declining alumina demand could create a bauxite surplus and lift inventories at refineries and ports.

title: President Trump Expands Section 232 Tariffs On Steel And Aluminum
summary: President Trump issued expanded Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum, closing tariff loopholes and terminating exclusion processes. Aluminum tariffs rise from 10% to 25% and apply to additional aluminum derivatives, with no new or renewed product exclusions considered. The change is intended to counter excess capacity and national security risks.

title: Nickel production disruption in Indonesia raises supply concerns
summary: Bloomberg reports a production halt and investigation around Indonesia’s Morowali nickel hub after a landslide at a tailings area tied to PT QMB New Energy. Fatalities occurred, traders expect reduced output, and nearby producers cut production. Indonesia’s large share of global nickel supply raises immediate bullish pricing pressure.

title: Chile, Canada and Peru push back against Trump's copper tariff probe
summary: Chile, Canada and Peru told the U.S. Commerce Department that copper imports do not threaten U.S. security and should be excluded from potential Section 232 tariffs. The probe follows Trump’s earlier steel/aluminium tariffs and could affect U.S. buying demand and pricing, while suppliers warn it may benefit China.

title: U.S. Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum: Navigating the Changing Landscape in 2025 | Bradley Arant Boult Cummings LLP
summary: The article highlights that U.S. reciprocal tariff pauses for most goods will expire July 9, 2025, but exclusions for steel and aluminum imports remain. Aluminum tariffs stay at 25% overall, while China-related tariffs are 125%, with no expected change, likely lifting U.S. landed costs and supporting aluminium prices.

title: Citi sees copper prices falling slower as U.S. tariffs ease
summary: Citi said copper prices should decline more gradually over the next three months after Trump eased tariffs in the past week, while China bought on dips and U.S. scrap supply stayed tight due to stockpiling. Citi lifted its three‑month copper forecast and also raised its aluminum forecast on expected pricing support.

title: USITC rules Chinese imports of aluminium containers harmful to US industry
summary: USITC ruled that imports of Chinese aluminium containers are harmful to US industry. Such findings typically pave the way for trade remedies that curb imports and tighten supply into the US market. Reduced availability for aluminium container demand can support aluminium prices in the near term.

title: Destiny Copper Announces Partnership With BMI Group To Expand Operations At Bioveld Niagara
summary: Destiny Copper announced BMI Group purchased a minority stake to help expand operations at Bioveld Niagara, aiming to scale its copper recovery to copper powder (CR-to-CP) production. The financing supports commercialization and potential new uses, increasing expectations for incremental copper supply and processing capacity in Canada.

title: 7 Countries Oppose US National Security Review on Copper Imports
summary: Seven trade partners (Chile, Canada, Peru, Indonesia, South Korea, China and the EU) filed comments against a U.S. national security review of copper imports, urging the Commerce Department not to impose tariffs or quotas. Their pushback highlights the risk of restrictive policy that could disrupt copper trade flows.

title: China's unwrought aluminum and aluminum semis exports by month
summary: China’s March 2025 exports of unwrought aluminum and aluminum semis rose 24% month-on-month to 506,000 tonnes, but cumulative Jan–Mar volumes remain down 7.6% year-on-year. Export competitiveness is weakened by trade-war pressure and margin compression, with April exports expected to decline as tariff changes remain uncertain.

title: Focusing on the Enamelled Copper Wire Industry: Peak Season in Progress, How Will Tariff Policies Impact? [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports that frequent tariff-policy changes in April have driven large swings in copper prices, while enamelled copper wire remains in peak season. Many firms cite strong April orders and little immediate tariff impact, though concerns persist that US-bound home appliance and power tool demand may be delayed or canceled.

title: Prospect secures $9.5m from First Quantum for Mumbezhi copper project in Zambia
summary: Prospect Resources raised about A$15.2m ($9.5m) from First Quantum Minerals via an equity placement for its Mumbezhi copper project in Zambia. FQM becomes a 15% shareholder and a technical partner, supporting exploration and phase-two drilling. Total proceeds aim to strengthen working capital; no immediate production changes are outlined.

title: Asia-Pacific Low-Carbon Aluminum Market Analysis and
summary: The piece promotes an Asia-Pacific report forecasting growth in low-carbon aluminum demand driven by EV adoption and government emissions regulations, alongside advances in smelting and recycling using renewable energy. It notes high costs and supply-chain interruptions, but does not cite any immediate changes to aluminum supply or spot pricing.

title: Workplace risks loom over Indonesia's Chinese-funded nickel and steel smelters · Global Voices
summary: The piece describes repeated deadly incidents and alleged systematic safety shortcomings at Tsingshan’s IMIP nickel processing and stainless steel facilities in Indonesia, including a December 2023 nickel-plant explosion and another fatal smelter accident in February 2025. Despite production resuming quickly after one death, the accidents heighten perceived supply-risk and oversight concerns.

title: Chile, Canada, Peru oppose US copper tariff probe
summary: Chile, Canada and Peru—supplying most US refined copper—oppose a US Commerce probe that could impose Section 232 national-security tariffs on copper imports. Industry and traders warn tariffs could damage the global economy and potentially benefit China, while alternatives like export controls are discussed.

title: Kincora Copper: Investor Briefing Webinar - Sixth Asset Level Agreement
summary: Kincora Copper said it will host a briefing webinar after amending its earn-in and joint venture agreement with a subsidiary of AngloGold Ashanti for a second copper-gold exploration joint venture in the Northern Junee-Narromine Belt. Total expenditures could reach up to $100 million, supported by renewed partner funding.

title: Zambia consumer body says U.S. tariffs on agriculture, copper to hurt economy-Xinhua
summary: Zambia’s consumer advocacy group warns proposed U.S. tariffs—including a 25% tariff on copper imports—could reduce the competitiveness of Zambian copper exports to the U.S. It expects greater global copper price volatility, worsening foreign-exchange shortages, and added economic strain as the kwacha weakens and costs rise.

title: Navigating Aluminum Market Volatility After Tariffs
summary: MetalMiner reports aluminum prices turned more volatile after tariff announcements, plunging from a mid-March peak and breaking below the prior range. Tariffs were seen as raising demand risks amid global economic uncertainty, and the later reciprocal-tariff pause did not fully stabilize expectations. The domestic market is described as more resilient than in 2018.

title: Duties coming on aluminum containers from China following US trade ruling
summary: The headline says the US will impose duties on aluminum containers coming from China after a trade ruling. Such tariffs can increase the cost of imported aluminum packaging, potentially weakening near-term demand and weighing on aluminium prices over the next days to weeks.

title: BHP 3Q Copper Production Up 10% On-Year, Iron Ore Output Flat
summary: BHP said its third-quarter copper output rose 10% year on year to 513,200 tonnes, boosted by 16% higher production at Escondida in northern Chile. Iron ore output was flat as operational improvements offset earlier tropical cyclone disruptions. The copper rise points to near-term supply support.

title: Alcoa CEO appeals to Trump administration to drop tariffs on Canadian aluminum imports
summary: Alcoa’s CEO urged the Trump administration to remove 25% tariffs on Canadian aluminum, arguing the U.S. lacks primary smelting capacity and would strain electricity grids to replace imports. The tariffs already increased Alcoa’s costs and are expected to weigh further, while uncertainty around trade policy remains.

title: Correction to aluminium P1020A premium, ddp Midwest US, rationale on April 16
summary: Fastmarkets issued a correction to its MB-AL-0020 Aluminium P1020A premium (ddp Midwest US) rationale for April 16. The contango level was misstated as $0.15/tonne, and it is corrected to $37/tonne. The pricing database has been updated accordingly.

title: BHP iron ore output dips on cyclones, copper gains with Escondida boost
summary: BHP said escalating U.S.-China trade tensions could hurt the economy, but its direct tariff impact was limited. It reported a slight iron ore output dip from cyclones, while copper production rose 10% to 513,200 tonnes, boosted by improved Escondida operations. The company expects Chile copper output in the upper half of guidance for 2025.

title: BHP clinches copper and iron ore records - Australian Mining
summary: BHP says Chile’s Escondida mine lifted copper output by 20%, delivering a record nine-month production total of 1.5 million tonnes. BHP also increased copper production in South Australia. The company additionally outlined a major investment to expand copper operations over the next decade.

title: Rio Tinto signs deal to explore low-carbon aluminium project in India
summary: Rio Tinto signed an MoU with AMG Metals & Materials to assess a low-carbon aluminium project in India, potentially including renewable-powered primary aluminium smelting and alumina production. The first phase would study a possible 500,000 tpa smelter site. No financial or confirmed production timelines were provided.

title: Rio Tinto partners with Indian firm to explore low-carbon aluminium project
summary: Rio Tinto signed an MoU with India’s AMG Metals & Materials to study a low-carbon aluminium and alumina project in India. The proposal includes up to 1 mtpa primary aluminium smelting and renewable-powered operations, with initial work on a 500,000 tpa smelter site. No financial details were disclosed.

title: AM Green: Rio Tinto and AMG Metals & Materials to assess low-carbon aluminium project in India
summary: Rio Tinto and AMG Metals Materials signed an MOU to assess a low-carbon aluminium project in India, potentially including up to a 1 Mtpa primary aluminium smelter and 2 Mtpa alumina production powered by renewable energy. The study may evaluate phased capacity and smelting/commercial solutions, impacting expectations for aluminium supply.

title: BHP Cautions on Tariff War Risks While Posting Higher Copper Output -- Update
summary: BHP cautioned that a tariff war could slow global growth and fracture trade flows, but it reported higher copper output. Third-quarter copper volumes rose 10%, driven by increased Escondida mine production in Chile. BHP also signaled plans to extend Escondida’s life, keeping output in the upper part of guidance.

title: BHP Signals Plan to Boost Escondida Copper Output Later This Decade -- Commodity Comment
summary: BHP said third-quarter copper output at Escondida rose 10% versus a year earlier, driven by stronger material mined and higher concentrator feed grade. Guidance for FY25 copper remains unchanged but is expected to land in the upper half of the range. BHP also plans extensions to the Los Colorados concentrator beyond FY29.

title: BHP Signals Plan to Boost Escondida Copper Output Later This Decade — Commodity Comment
summary: BHP said Escondida copper output rose 10% year on year, aided by stronger mined material and higher concentrator feed grade. FY25 guidance remains 1.18–1.30 million tonnes, expected in the upper half due to operational strength offsetting strikes, sea swells and a Chile power outage. BHP also plans growth beyond FY29.

title: BHP warns on tariffs as copper output hits records after nine months
summary: BHP said US tariffs have a limited direct impact on its business but may weigh on demand via slower growth and fragmented trade. It reported record copper output for the first nine months and reiterated 2025 copper production guidance of 1.84–2.04 million tonnes, implying mixed near-term effects for copper.

title: Sinomine targets 2026 production at Kitumba copper mine in Zambia
summary: Sinomine Resource Group says it has started stripping at its Kitumba copper mine in Zambia and targets copper production to begin in September 2026. The company plans to invest about $560 million in the project, according to a WeChat post cited by Reuters. Near-term effects on copper prices appear limited due to the long timeline.

title: Greenko founders' firm teams up with Rio Tinto to explore low-carbon aluminium project
summary: Rio Tinto signed an MoU with AMG Metals & Materials to assess a low-carbon aluminium project in India, including up to 1 mtpa primary aluminium smelting and 2 mtpa alumina, powered by renewables and storage. The initial phase studies a 500,000 tpa smelter. It’s exploratory, with no financial details.

title: The domestic supply of aluminum billets is showing seasonal recovery. What is the current willingness of billet enterprises to resume production?[SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports a seasonal recovery in China’s primary aluminum billet market. After post–Chinese New Year production cuts and weak demand kept fees low, destocking during “Golden March and Silver April” improved processing fees and boosted operating rates. March output and utilization rose, and April production is expected to be stable to slightly higher.

title: Alcoa anticipates $90m impact from tariffs on Canadian aluminium imports in Q2
summary: Alcoa says US tariffs on Canadian aluminium imports will cost it about $90m in Q2 after costing $20m in Q1, with additional annual cost increases. Despite some alumina cost benefits, the company expects a large net negative result and highlights US capacity shortfalls and trade disruption risks.

title: Camino Minerals Corp: Camino and Nittetsu Complete Acquisition of Permitted Puquios Copper Project in Chile
summary: Camino Minerals completed its acquisition of Cuprum Resources Chile, which owns the construction-ready Puquios copper project in Chile, co-developed with Nittetsu in a 50/50 JV. The release discusses permitting, project economics and next financing steps, which are copper-specific but not linked to near-term production changes.

title: Indonesian nickel smelter group asks for royalty hike delay until prices rise
summary: Indonesia’s nickel smelters association asked the government to delay higher mineral royalty fees until LME nickel prices reach $17,000/ton, above current levels (~$15,600). The new royalties (14%–19% on ore; higher rates on nickel pig iron and matte) would raise costs amid weakening nickel prices.

title: EBRD helps to boost production of copper cables in Uzbekistan
summary: The EBRD plans to lend up to €20 million to Uzbekistan’s Artikul Aziya Kabel to expand production of copper cable and wire, including specialist solar cables, and to boost exports. The project supports grid enhancements and renewable deployment, potentially lifting near-term expectations for copper demand.

title: Indonesia raises royalties for nickel and other metals to fund national policies
summary: Indonesia plans higher nickel royalties, replacing a flat 10% levy on nickel ore with a variable rate of 14%-19% linked to government-set price levels. Lower-grade ore for battery-grade nickel faces a reduced 2% royalty. The change takes effect shortly, while miners warn of margin strain and output cuts.

title: Local business hit twice by copper thieves
summary: A Rio Rancho business says thieves broke into transformers twice in three months, stealing copper wiring and causing outages and losses. Owners estimate major damage in January and smaller losses during the second theft. The story is about local theft with no reported impact on broader copper supply or pricing.

title: AMNS India Flags Concerns Over Impact Of US Tariffs On Domestic Steel, Aluminium Industry -
summary: AMNS India warned that proposed US tariffs could disrupt trade flows and hurt India’s steel and aluminium industry, noting China may divert exports if it loses access to the US market. India expects safeguard measures, but current uncertainty around US tariff implementation could reduce aluminium demand prospects.

title: World's second largest miner Rio Tinto inks deal with AMG M&M for green aluminium project in India: Report | Indiablooms
summary: Rio Tinto signed an MoU with India’s AMG M&M to explore a large low-carbon aluminium project, evaluating up to 1 mtpa of primary aluminium and 2 mtpa of alumina powered by renewables and pumped hydro. A first phase targets a 500,000-tonne smelter, with potential bauxite supply from Rio Tinto’s Australia mines.

title: Steel and aluminum tariffs may impact rent prices in key US housing markets
summary: Realtor.com reports that Trump’s 25% tariffs on steel and aluminum imports could raise construction costs for newly built residences. Builders may pass higher costs to consumers or delay finishing construction, reducing housing supply. This could push rents higher in multiple US metros as tariffs dampen development plans.

title: USFS Issues 60-Day Notice of Final Environmental Impact Statement Republication for Resolution Copper Project
summary: The U.S. Forest Service issued a 60-day notice to republish the Final Environmental Impact Statement for the Resolution Copper project in Arizona. The company frames the step as progress toward permitting for a major potential underground copper mine, improving near-term expectations for copper supply.

title: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd.: Aston Bay Files Technical Report for Storm Copper Project Initial Mineral Resource Estimate

summary: The US Forest Service issued a notice related to a land transfer connected to an Arizona copper mine. summary: The U.S. is proceeding with a land exchange enabling Resolution Copper to develop a major mine at Oak Flat on sacred Apache land while a Supreme Court case is pending. summary: The US told the WTO that its Section 232 tariffs on imported steel and aluminium are justified by national security and not safeguard measures, after India requested consultations. title: The supply of copper raw materials falling short of expectations has led to the continuous depletion of the inventory of copper anode. [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports China’s March imports of copper concentrate rose but still fell short of what smelters required, leading to ongoing depletion of copper anode inventories. title: Trump team set to approve copper mine on sacred Native American land
summary: The headline says Trump’s team is set to approve a copper mine on sacred Native American land. If approved, the decision would be interpreted as enabling additional copper supply, which typically pressures copper prices by improving the outlook for future production and availability in markets.

title: Forest Service issues notice on land transfer for major Arizona copper mine
summary: The U.S. Forest Service issued notice of a final environmental review and draft decision to transfer Tonto National Forest land (Oak Flat) to Resolution Copper, clearing a path for a large Arizona copper mine despite Native American legal challenges. Advancing approval raises near-term supply expectations for copper.

title: US Forest Service issues notice on Oak Flat land transfer for Arizona copper mine
summary: The U.S. Forest Service issued notice it will publish a final environmental review and draft decision on transferring Oak Flat land to Resolution Copper, enabling a major Arizona copper project. summary: The article says Trump is putting the Oak Flat copper mine on a fast-track permitting process, while tribes and opponents vow to fight. summary: Russia’s state development bank VEB plans to invest $13.4 billion (1.1 trillion roubles) to develop the Baimskaya copper deposit in Chukotka. title: Resolution Copper Welcomes Inclusion in Federal Transparency Initiative
summary: Resolution Copper said the White House designated its project as a critical-mineral “transparency” initiative under the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council. The company frames this as increased permitting predictability for its proposed underground copper mine, supporting expectations of domestic copper supply development in the U.S.

title: Rio Tinto And AMG Metals Materials To Assess Low-Carbon Aluminium Project In India
summary: Rio Tinto and AMG Metals & Materials signed an MoU to assess a low-carbon aluminium project in India, including up to a 1 Mtpa primary aluminium smelter and 2 Mtpa alumina capacity powered by renewables. The study evaluates smelting and energy options and could shape expectations for future low-carbon supply.

title: Russia invests $13.4bn in Baimskaya copper mine
summary: Russia plans to invest $13.4bn in the Baimskaya copper mine. The announcement relates directly to copper supply development, which can increase market expectations for greater future output. Any near-term price reaction may be modest, since construction and ramp-up take time and current supply tightness may dominate.

title: Israel to phase out copper networks as fiber-optic transition gains momentum
summary: Israel’s communications ministry plans staged shutdown of copper and cable networks as fiber-optic coverage expands, including exemptions for Bezeq and HOT from deploying new copper lines and eventual dismantling once fiber reaches 85% of users in an area. The transition reduces future copper cabling needs.

title: China's copper anode imports in March 2025 dropped 47.8% YoY, hitting a five-year low [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s March 2025 copper anode imports fell to 50,176 mt, down 47.8% YoY (five-year low). Cumulative Q1 imports were also sharply lower. title: 12,508 mt! Copper Enamelled Wire Exports Hit a New High in March
summary: China’s exports of copper enamelled wire rose sharply in March 2025 to a record 12,508.09 mt (+29.53% YoY, +70.57% MoM), driven by strong shipments to Vietnam, Japan and others. Exports to the US fell (-10.24% YoY), with tariff policies possibly further reducing US-bound volumes.

title: "Trump Admin Reveals Timeline For Approving Resolution Copper Mine"
summary: The Forest Service said it will advance the Resolution Copper project in Arizona, releasing within 60 days a final environmental impact statement and draft record of decision tied to a land swap needed to transfer federal acreage for the underground mine. The project faces legal challenges, but the agency is moving forward.

title: India Flags US Tariffs On Steel, Aluminium Ahead Of Trade Talks -
summary: India has raised concerns with the US over re-imposed duties on steel (25%) and aluminium (10%), calling them a breach of a WTO settlement. India expects discussions in Washington next week. title: In March, the import profit/loss of aluminum narrowed, while the net import of primary aluminum surged MoM
summary: China’s March primary aluminium imports rose 10.9% MoM to ~222,000 mt, while the import loss narrowed to ~957.9 yuan/mt by April 18. title: Industrialization of "Safe and Cost-Reducing" Composite Current Collectors Accelerates amid Volatile Copper Prices
summary: The article links volatile tariff- and trade-policy-driven copper price swings to downstream impacts and battery inventory management. It then highlights AMTech’s €composite current collector project using metal–polymer–metal structures that reduce copper/aluminium usage via “one-step” vacuum evaporation, aiming to lower costs and improve battery safety.

title: Nuclear power could take the shine off Aussie aluminium
summary: A new study says a proposed shift toward nuclear power in Australia could leave several aluminium smelters “at severe risk of closure,” due to higher energy costs and gaps between current coal-fired electricity contracts and nuclear availability. With three smelters relying on coal power, the potential supply hit could weigh on aluminium prices.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Exports Were Generally Optimistic in March, While Exports to the US Halved YoY
summary: China’s copper plate/sheet and strip exports rose to 10,543 mt in March (+40.5% MoM, +5.2% YoY), with cumulative growth of 2.65%. Exports to the US fell 57% YoY, but SMM says tariffs haven’t directly hit orders. April exports may stay high, though downstream demand is suppressed.

title: Indonesia's Nickel Gambit From Raw Exporter to Battery Hub – Who Wins and Loses
summary: Indonesia dominates global nickel output and is pushing downstream processing after a raw ore export ban, building smelters and HPAL capacity. Nickel’s role in EV cathodes underpins demand growth from automakers. However, expanded refining could also increase refined supply, making the net near-term price effect uncertain.

title: Copper gains defy gloomy outlook
summary: Copper rose to a two-week high as a weaker U.S. dollar encouraged CTA/fund buying and traders covered shorts, breaching key moving averages. However, sentiment remains cautious because Trump’s import tariffs threaten growth and industrial metal demand. Aluminium and nickel were also up, but driven largely by macro flows.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Completes Phase 1 Construction on the Kenbridge Nickel Project All-Season Access Road
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. said Phase 1 construction is complete on an all-season restricted access road to its Kenbridge nickel-copper-cobalt project, replacing floatplane/ATV logistics with year-round road access. The company is starting Phase 2 and plans further upgrades and 2025 next steps to expand resources, potentially improving future supply prospects.

summary: Glenstar Minerals announced it has hired Midnight Sun Drilling to conduct the first-ever drill program at its Green Monster nickel-copper-cobalt property in Nevada. title: Glenstar Minerals Inc.: Glenstar Minerals Hires Midnight Sun Drilling Inc. for First Ever Drill Program on Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Green Monster Property
summary: Glenstar Minerals hired Midnight Sun Drilling to run the first-ever drill program on its Green Monster nickel-copper-cobalt property in Nevada. summary: Alaska Energy Metals filed an updated NI 43-101 technical report for its Eureka deposit at the Nikolai nickel project in Alaska, raising tonnage, metal content, and nickel-equivalent grades versus the prior 2024 estimate. summary: CEO.CA’s “Inside the Boardroom” interviews Vizsla Copper’s CEO on its exploration strategy for a major copper-gold discovery in B.C. summary: CEO.CA interviews Yukon Metals’ CEO about upcoming drilling plans at Star River and AZ targets, highlighting accessibility and high-grade surface samples. summary: Barrick Gold plans to rename itself Barrick Mining Corp. to better reflect its focus on growing gold and copper operations. The change is subject to shareholder approval in May and involves a NYSE ticker update. The news is supportive for copper sentiment but lacks specific near-term supply changes.

title: Lindian Resources secures full ownership of Lelouma Bauxite project in Guinea
summary: Lindian Resources has acquired full ownership of Guinea’s Lelouma bauxite project by purchasing the remaining 25%. The JORC resource totals 900mt with 45% aluminium oxide, targeting DSO production near Kamsar port. The update reduces ownership-dilution risk, supporting future aluminium feedstock prospects.

title: Nickel 28 Capital Corp: Nickel 28 Releases Ramu Q1 Operating Performance
summary: Nickel 28 reported Q1 2025 Ramu operations: contained nickel in MHP fell to 6,970 tonnes and nickel sales to 6,133 tonnes, driven by production curtailment from an acid plant blower fan failure. Unit costs rose to $3.61/lb. It notes lower Q1 LME average nickel price at $7.06/lb.

title: Tariff Wars Impact Copper Prices and Market Stability
summary: The piece attributes copper’s early-2025 volatility to tariff-related uncertainty, then highlights signs of stabilization: copper inventories are pressured, China’s refined output rose in March, and smelters are leveraging higher by-product prices. It argues copper may have found a floor and could resume upward movement soon.

title: SMM Outlook: More Scrap to Flow into Copper Smelting amid Ore Shortages
summary: SMM says China’s copper ore/concentrate shortages are pushing smelters to seek supplements. Scrap-derived anode copper supply is expanding, with higher scrap flows into smelting. It also notes concentrate TCs weakness and reduced anode imports, plus operational factors like maintenance, shaping feedstock availability.

title: SMM Global Copper Foil Industry Landscape and Market Outlook for 2025
summary: SMM’s outlook for global copper foil highlights rising overcapacity in lithium battery copper foil, cut-throat competition, and falling processing fees. It forecasts operating rates recovering in April/May, but US reciprocal tariffs are expected to impact end-use demand and prolong inventory buildup, likely weighing on copper foil-related copper consumption.

title: Aluminium producer Norsk Hydro's Q1 core profit lags forecast, cuts extrusions outlook
summary: Norsk Hydro reported Q1 profit growth but slightly missed forecasts and cut its 2025 outlook for its aluminium extrusions segment due to weaker downstream demand and rising uncertainty. The article notes headwinds in recycling margins and aluminium trade disruptions from renewed U.S. tariffs that have roiled flows and premiums, adding cost pressure.

title: Aluminium producer Norsk Hydro core profit lags forecast, cuts extrusions outlook
summary: Norsk Hydro reported higher core profit but cut its 2025 extrusion outlook on weaker downstream demand and compressed recycling margins. The return of U.S. 25% aluminium tariffs has roiled trade flows and pushed physical premiums to record highs, raising import costs and tightening regional pricing. Chinese surplus and weaker demand temper.

title: Hydro signs billion-euro deal to supply NKT with low-carbon aluminium for EU grid
summary: Hydro signed a long-term, ~1 billion euro deal to supply low-carbon aluminium wire rod to NKT for power cable production supporting Europe’s grid upgrades. The contract runs 2026–2033 (option for more) and follows Hydro’s planned Karmøy smelter expansion, reinforcing aluminium demand and supply expectations; aluminium can substitute copper in grids.

title: Aluminium producer Norsk Hydro core profit misses forecast, cuts extrusions outlook
summary: Norsk Hydro reported sharply higher core profit on higher aluminium prices and currency gains, while cutting its extrusion outlook due to weaker downstream demand. Renewed U.S. 25% aluminium tariffs roiled trade flows, pushing physical market premiums to record highs and increasing costs for U.S. buyers, supporting near-term aluminium tightness.

title: Star Copper Corp.: Star Copper Appoints Veteran Company Builder Brad Nichol as Chairman
summary: Star Copper Corp. appointed a new chairman and announced a $6 million non-brokered private placement, including flow-through proceeds earmarked for exploration, drilling, permitting, and related work on its British Columbian copper projects (Star and Indata). The funds support asset development but do not signal immediate supply changes for markets.

title: Indonesia imposes new nickel royalty rates | Latest Market News
summary: Indonesia implemented new non-tax royalty (PNBP) rates for nickel products effective 26 April. Rates vary by HMA-based nickel reference price for ore and are set for NPI, ferronickel, matte, and newly introduced MHP. The change is expected to raise longer-term costs but likely has limited immediate price impact.

title: CCIE 2025: New Capacity Exacerbates Oversupply in Chinese Copper Rod Industry
summary: SMM’s CCIE 2025 analysis expects China’s copper cathode rod capacity to keep rising to about 17.67Mt by end-2025, worsening overcapacity. Supply surplus is pressuring copper rod processing fees, contributing to lower operating rates amid weak consumption. It also notes uncertain export rebate effects and a shift toward anodes.

title: Aluminum Premiums Surge After New Tariffs Imposed
summary: U.S. aluminum import costs have surged after new tariffs (including 20% from the EU and 10% from the UK) took effect, driving Midwest delivery premiums for physical shipments toward record highs. Supply chain disruptions, shipping delays, and higher freight/risk premiums are pushing domestic aluminum prices near multi-year peaks.

title: MAC Copper Limited Announces March 2025 Quarterly Report
summary: MAC Copper Limited reported Q1 2025 output of 8,644 tonnes with a 4.1% Cu grade from its CSA mine, noting the quarter as seasonally lowest. C1 increased to $1.91/lb due to lower volumes, while 2025 TC/RC benchmarks are lower, improving outlook. Overall, it’s company-specific without major new supply shocks.

title: Codelco chairman says April copper output up, sees strong US and China demand
summary: Codelco said April copper output rose 22% year-on-year to about 105,000 tonnes, after recovering from a prior production low. Chairman Maximo Pacheco expects strong demand across Asia, especially China, and the US, noting tariff-driven shipment shifts and renewed smelter investment plans.

title: Glencore reports 30% drop in first-quarter copper production
summary: Glencore reported a 30% drop in first-quarter copper production. The reduction signals weaker near-term mine output versus the prior period, tightening supply expectations and typically weighing on copper prices in the short term as markets reassess available inventories and production timelines.

title: Power Metallic Expands the Lion Zone - Exceptionally High Copper & Gold Grade Kicks on Deep Eastern Margin of Zone
summary: Power Metallic reported drill results from its Lion Zone at the Nisk polymetallic project, including copper-dominant massive sulphides and assays containing nickel. While the high-grade results may improve investor sentiment for future Cu/Ni resource potential, the article does not imply immediate production changes, so near-term price impact is likely limited.

title: The hidden cost of Indonesia's nickel boom – DW – 04/30/2025
summary: DW reports leaked internal documents alleging systematic chromium-6 contamination from Harita Group’s Obi Island nickel mining and smelting complex, including claims made during the 2023 IPO due diligence. Residents lack clean water. IRMA is reviewing the site for certification, and legal scrutiny may follow, but no immediate supply cut is stated.

title: Glencore keeps annual guidance, but copper output starts year slowly
summary: Glencore kept most 2025 production guidance unchanged, but copper operations had a slow start. Q1 copper output fell to 167,900 tonnes, down 30% from a year earlier, due to lower ore mining rates, grades, and recoveries at Collahuasi, Antapaccay and KCC. The firm expects stronger performance later in 2025.

title: Erongored loses N$5 million from copper theft
summary: Erongored says it loses nearly N$5 million a year from copper theft, citing repeated incidents including theft of power poles at Swakopmund and Henties Bay. The vandalism disrupts electricity and affects water supply facilities. The utility warns perpetrators and works with police to prosecute.

title: Record gold prices help keep China's copper smelters going despite losses
summary: Record gold prices and valuable smelting byproducts are offsetting losses from deeply negative copper concentrate treatment/refining charges in China. Despite tighter concentrate availability and worsening profitability, smelters are unlikely to cut major output, helping refined copper production growth this year.

title: High-Nickel Pig Iron and Pure Nickel Markets Face Continued Downward Pressure Amid Supply-Demand Imbalances
summary: High-nickel pig iron prices in China fell again, though the weekly decline slowed, amid continued weak finished-product demand and cautious stainless steel buyers. Pure nickel also faced pressure from tariff/macro uncertainty and a surplus supply-demand balance, with downstream nickel plate transactions weak. Cost support limits downside somewhat.

title: Zambia copper production up 30% year on year in Q1, minister says
summary: Zambia’s Mines Minister said copper production in Q1 2025 rose about 30% year on year to roughly 224,000 tonnes, up from around 173,000 tonnes in Q1 2024. The increase was attributed to higher output from Konkola Copper Mines and Mopani Copper Mines.

title: Jubilee Metals in advanced stages to finish copper ore tests
summary: Jubilee Metals says it is in the final stages of trials at its Roan copper concentrator in Zambia. Initial results suggest the plant can boost copper production rates from high-grade ore, and delays were due to process adjustments. Jubilee also expects its Munkoyo open-pit ramp-up to reach 8,500 tonnes/month.

title: Basildon Alcotes copper theft probe sees appeal issued
summary: Police in Basildon issued an appeal in an investigation into the theft of copper pipes from a property in Alcotes last May. The theft reportedly caused damage to homes and neighboring properties. Officers are seeking information on a suspect’s whereabouts; no broader supply or market impact is mentioned.

title: North America Copper Tubes Market worth $3.44 billion by 2030 - Exclusive Report by MarketsandMarkets
summary: MarketsandMarkets forecasts North America’s copper tubes market will rise from USD 3.18 billion in 2024 to USD 3.44 billion by 2030, citing construction, HVACR demand, and energy-efficient/green building trends. It attributes growth to copper’s thermal conductivity, durability, and recyclability, but provides no near-term market disruption details.

title: Mining company excited about hydrogen potential in NL nickel deposits
summary: First Atlantic Nickel says early drilling at Newfoundland ophiolite projects returned strong results, including a new “RPM zone” discovery, with metallurgical recovery testing underway. The company highlights processing awaruite nickel without smelting (lower energy, no sulfur removal). It also explores geologic hydrogen tied to the deposits, funded by researchers and U.S. support.

title: Glencore posts 30% drop in first-quarter copper production
summary: Glencore reported first-quarter copper output down 30% to 167,900 tonnes, despite keeping full-year 2025 production guidance unchanged. Nickel production fell 21% as well. The company cited tariff-driven uncertainty and potential trade-flow dislocation, while analysts reacted to the weaker quarterly physical supply.

title: NKT signs deal for Hydro low-carbon aluminium wire rods
summary: NKT signed a roughly €1bn agreement with Hydro to secure low-carbon aluminium wire rod supply through 2033, with first rights to Hydro’s REDUXA grades. Hydro is investing €140m in a new casthouse to expand output locally. The deal supports aluminium demand and supply expectations, especially for European low-carbon material.

title: Aluminum Premiums Diverge Across Global Markets
summary: U.S. aluminium tariffs are lifting U.S. aluminium premiums while depressing European premiums, as metal imports are diverted abroad and U.S. demand remains constrained by limited primary output. With duties and logistics restricting arbitrage, U.S. buyers face higher costs likely to persist for months, barring policy relief.

title: Hudbay Completes Transaction to Consolidate 100% Ownership in the Copper Mountain Mine
summary: Hudbay completed its acquisition of Mitsubishi Materials’ 25% interest in the Copper Mountain Mine in British Columbia, bringing ownership to 100%. The company said the added attributable production supports its strategy to increase copper output in tier-1 jurisdictions, reinforcing its position as a major Canadian copper producer.

title: Materials Decline Alongside Copper Prices - Materials Roundup
summary: Metals and raw material producers fell in tandem with copper as fears of economic fallout from the U.S.-China trade war intensified. Copper futures tumbled 5.5% on weak U.S. Q1 data and a drop in Chinese export orders in April, ending May delivery at $4.56/lb and down 9.2% for the month.

title: Mount Lyell mine revival latest, with vast copper resources | The Advocate
summary: Sibanye-Stillwater’s Mount Lyell Mine in Tasmania has been out of production since 2014, but resource mapping and updated mineral resource estimates indicate large remaining copper resources. The company is continuing a feasibility study and may build a new concentrator plant if it restarts mining, potentially improving future supply outlook.

title: NYSE: AA Alcoa boss says midwest aluminium premium to soar
summary: Alcoa’s CEO Bill Oplinger says the Midwest aluminium premium is set to soar, with no plan to shut the Portland aluminium smelter for the next decade. He argues batteries won’t fully firm variable wind/solar supply, implying continued reliance on gas and potentially nuclear support for renewables.

title: Hopes of progress in US trade talks lift copper after sharp sell-off
summary: Copper rose on the LME after a sharp sell-off as traders gained confidence that U.S. trade talks with China could progress and ease tariff uncertainty. The move followed weak prior demand signals and was supported by continuing inventory outflows, with COMEX and China premium metrics indicating tighter near-term supply conditions.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Talks Next Steps at the Kenbridge Critical Metals Project Including an Airborne Geophysical Survey and Greenfields Exploration Program
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. says it has started a 4-week airborne geophysical survey and a greenfields exploration program at its Kenbridge nickel-copper-cobalt project in northwestern Ontario. The work aims to refine subsurface targets for future prospecting, sampling, and drilling. No production or supply change is announced.

title: Shrinking Economy, Sliding Copper, and Gold's Outlook
summary: The piece argues copper’s downturn is accelerating, citing a drop of more than 6% in the U.S. session and technical moves below key retracement levels. It links the move to weaker economic indicators (ADP employment and GDP) and risk-off sentiment, suggesting the “big slide” in copper may resume soon.

title: Versamet Royalties Corporation: Versamet Completes Minera Kolpa Copper Stream Acquisition and Upsizes Revolving Credit Facility
summary: Versamet completed a US$35 million copper stream acquisition on the Huachocolpa Uno (Kolpa) mine following Endeavour Silver’s acquisition of the mine operator. Versamet also upsized its secured revolving credit facility to US$60 million, lowering interest costs. The deal adds near-term copper exposure and can modestly bolster copper sentiment.

title: In Brief: Telstra Re-Rating, MinRes & MAC Copper
summary: The piece focuses on MAC Copper’s March quarter performance, noting copper production progress (including 4kt in March), improving costs with higher volumes, and ongoing ventilation and Merrin development milestones. Analysts cite stronger metrics and assign Buy ratings, supporting constructive near-term sentiment for copper-linked supply outlooks.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Confirms Kamoa-Kakula Achieved a Record 50,176 Tonnes of Copper Production in April
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says its Kamoa-Kakula complex produced a record 50,176 tonnes of copper in concentrate in April, with Phase 3 recovery and throughput exceeding design. The company also reports rising imported hydropower to support operations and smelter commissioning aimed at first anode production in July, supporting copper output growth.

title: Government designates NewRange Copper Nickel as a project important to national, energy security
summary: NewRange Copper Nickel announced the NorthMet project was designated a “Transparency Project” by a federal council aimed at expanding domestic critical-mineral supply. The move signals prioritized permitting progress for a major undeveloped copper and nickel resource. The company reports most state permits secured and plans to update Section 404 filings.

title: Government designates NewRange Copper Nickel as a project important to national, energy security
summary: NewRange Copper Nickel said the federal NEDC designated its NorthMet project as a “Transparency Project,” prioritizing permitting for critical minerals. The firm holds most required permits and plans to update its Clean Water Act Section 404 application. The designation is intended to speed development of domestic copper and nickel supply with environmental safeguards.

title: Representative Markkanen requests Michigan's budget includes support of the Copperwood development
summary: Michigan Representative Markkanen requests earmarked 2026 state budget funding to support the Copperwood Mine development in Gogebic County. The funds would upgrade roads, power, and telecommunications to improve site readiness, helping the project move toward production. The article notes prior funding was deferred and an air permit was approved with conditions.

title: Lundin Mining Corporation: Lundin Mining Announces Initial Mineral Resource at Filo Del Sol Demonstrating One of the World's Largest Copper, Gold, and Silver Resources
summary: Lundin Mining announced initial mineral resource estimates for the Filo del Sol and Josemaria deposits within the Vicuña project, reporting contained copper of 13 Mt M&I plus 25 Mt inferred and expansion potential at depth. This can modestly improve near-term expectations for future copper supply, supporting sentiment.

title: Morgan Stanley rates NIC as Equal-weight
summary: Morgan Stanley upgraded Nickel Industries (NIC) to equal-weight and lifted its valuation, citing higher EPS forecasts after reviewing the 1Q25 production report and revised cost-of-production estimates. It also noted delayed payments related to investment in the Excelsior nickel-cobalt project. The target price rises to 65c from 55c.

title: Medallion Metals annonce que Co & IGO Limited ont convenu de modifier les conditions d'acquisition des activités nickel de Forrestania
summary: Medallion Metals announced that CO and IGO Limited agreed to modify the acquisition terms for Forrestania’s nickel assets. The update concerns the transaction structure and proposed deal conditions, but the article does not indicate immediate changes to operating output, refining supply, or near-term nickel availability.

title: A future of Aluminium made in Australia - Manufacturers' Monthly
summary: The article says U.S. tariffs could disrupt Australia’s aluminium exports and increase the risk of dumped, subsidized aluminium entering Australia at low prices. Capral Aluminium warns this may intensify unfair competition and harm local producers, implying near-term downward pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Mining Major Hails Massive Copper Discovery
summary: Lundin Mining, with BHP, says its Filo del Sol discovery in Argentina-Chile contains about 13 million tons of copper and large gold and silver resources. The piece highlights copper’s importance for the energy transition and rising long-term demand, but offers no immediate production start, limiting short-term price impact.

title: Medallion Metals, IGO amend acquisition terms for Forrestania Nickel Operation
summary: Medallion Metals and IGO amended terms to acquire 100% of the Forrestania Nickel Operation’s processing facility and infrastructure, excluding nickel and lithium mineral rights that IGO retains. Medallion plans to use the existing assets to develop a Ravensthorpe gold-copper pathway, extending exclusivity to Aug 2025 and targeting completion in late 2025.

title: Copper-cable thefts in Spain leave passengers trapped in trains overnight
summary: Copper thieves stole cables in multiple areas of Spain’s high-speed rail network, causing train service suspensions and leaving passengers stranded overnight. Infrastructure operator Adif said staff are working to replace the stolen cables. The theft highlights ongoing vulnerability of rail cabling, implying incremental copper replacement demand.

title: Lundin announces largest greenfield copper discovery at Filo del Sol project
summary: Lundin announced what it describes as its largest greenfield copper discovery at the Filo del Sol project. The announcement can lift market expectations for future copper supply, providing modest near-term support to copper prices as traders reassess potential output growth.

title: Copper cable theft in Spain delays thousands of high-speed rail passengers
summary: Copper cable theft in Spain has disrupted high-speed rail service and delayed thousands of passengers. The incident suggests damaged or stolen copper cabling will need replacement and repair, potentially supporting near-term copper demand. While likely localized, the replacement requirement can add incremental short-term support to copper prices.

title: BHP partner says Filo copper discovery is largest in 30 years
summary: BHP’s partner says the Filo copper discovery is the largest in 30 years, boosting expectations for additional future copper supply. If investors view the find as meaningful and potentially timely, it can improve market sentiment and create mild upward pressure on copper prices over the coming days.

title: Spain opens probe after copper theft halts dozens of high-speed trains
summary: Spain opened a probe after coordinated theft of copper cabling disrupted high-speed trains between Madrid, Seville and other southern cities, affecting over 10,000 passengers and at least 30 trains. Authorities cited growing copper theft incentives after high prices, but the disruption appears localized and unlikely to sway global copper markets.

title: Venus locks in $52,500 grant for Murchison copper drilling program
summary: Venus Metals secured a $52,500 WA government exploration grant to help fund drilling at its Pincher copper-zinc project, with a pre-collar and follow-up diamond tail to test a modeled 400m conductor. It also has CSIRO support to map potential gold-copper alteration zones, but the funding is modest for price impact.

title: Copper wiring stolen from Carroll County athletic fields
summary: Copper wiring thefts in Carroll County, Maryland have damaged light structures at athletic fields, requiring costly repairs and field downtime. Officials estimate replacement costs of about $18,000 in one case and consider measures like burying components and adding cameras. The theft reduces local copper availability but is unlikely to affect broader copper markets materially.

title: Miners slam Chinese smelters for buying bauxite below benchmark price - Markets
summary: Indonesia’s bauxite association (ABI) says many Chinese smelters refuse to pay the government-set benchmark for bauxite ore, forcing several miners to stop producing. With Indonesia banning bauxite exports to feed domestic alumina/aluminium, weaker miner output could tighten bauxite supply for smelters and support aluminium prices.

title: Lundin mining announces South America's largest copper discovery in 30 years
summary: Lundin Mining, with BHP, announced what it calls South America’s largest copper discovery in 30 years at the undeveloped Filo del Sol project on the Chile-Argentina border. Estimated copper resources are about 13 million tons, with gold and silver. Development will likely take years, limiting immediate price effects.

title: AICE 2025: Impact of New Alumina Production in Indonesia and Global Alumina Market 2024-2025
summary: SMM’s AICE 2025 forum covers how new alumina production in Indonesia could affect China’s alumina market, alongside a 2024-2025 review. It highlights alumina price declines on surplus fundamentals and expects 2025 to remain oversupplied, implying lower feedstock costs for smelters and supporting aluminium profitability.

title: Xanadu triggers Mongolian copper-gold sale vote as JV deal stalls
summary: Xanadu Mines let its exclusivity agreement with Zijin lapse and triggered a vote on a put option to sell its remaining 25% stake in Mongolia’s Kharmagtai copper-gold project. The move may draw third-party suitors and alter JV funding plans, but it does not change near-term output immediately.

title: Why is copper theft on Spain's railways so common now and who's behind it?
summary: Spain has seen a sharp rise in railway copper cable thefts, including on the Madrid–Seville high-speed line, disrupting sensors and forcing trains into safety mode. Theft is driven by scrap economics and reported flows to global buyers. Preventive measures may include replacing some copper with aluminium or fibre optics.

title: The supply of China's imported bauxite remains high while demand declines, April saw over 4 million mt inventory buildup at ports.
summary: SMM reports China’s imported bauxite port inventories rose sharply by 4.13 million mt in April to 20.19 million mt, amid high import supply and declining demand from alumina refineries undergoing maintenance/production cuts. Refiners also shift toward cheaper domestic bauxite, reducing import purchases and sustaining bauxite price pressure.

title: Tariffs, tensions and tonnage: Three words primarily influencing US aluminium prices soar in 2025
summary: The US imposed additional aluminium tariffs on April 9, lifting effective EU duties to 45% (plus the existing 25% Section 232 base). The Midwest Premium surged to above 33 cents/lb, near 2018-2019 highs. Middle East-driven shipping reroutes and port constraints further raise logistics costs for US aluminium.

title: Market Conditions Expected to Tighten in May, with Significant Declines in Blister Copper RCs [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports blister copper and copper anode refining charges (RCs) in China fell sharply into May, with spot transactions largely absent due to unfavorable producer margins and tighter scrap flows from reduced US scrap imports. While supply-demand may tighten if copper prices don’t rebound, the immediate RC trend is bearish for copper sentiment.

title: Copper cable thefts bring key Spanish rail route to a standstill
summary: Copper cable thefts disrupted Spain’s high-speed rail signalling, stranding thousands of passengers. Authorities said stolen copper cables were taken at multiple sites, and the transport minister expects repairs to restore schedules by late afternoon. The report notes copper prices are high, boosting scrap value incentives for theft.

title: Israel Imposes Anti-Dumping Tariffs on Aluminum Imports From China
summary: Israel will apply anti-dumping tariffs of up to 146% on Chinese aluminum imports after launching an investigation into allegedly underpriced shipments. The government moves to impose levies before the investigation ends, aiming to protect local producers from “flooding” by 25 Chinese companies.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Discovers Blind Winchester Breccia, Expands Near-Surface Mineralization in the American Eagle Area and Provides Copper Creek Project Update
summary: Faraday Copper reported results from five drill holes at its Copper Creek Project in Arizona, including discovery of the blind Winchester breccia and multiple near-surface copper intercepts in the American Eagle area. The company also expects an updated MRE/PEA near end-Q3 2025 based on expanded drilling, supporting longer-term supply potential.

title: Brixton Metals Provides Exploration Plans for Gold and Copper Drill Targets for its Fully Funded 2025 Program at its Thorn Project
summary: Brixton Metals announced 2025 exploration plans at its Thorn copper-gold project, including shallow drilling for gold mineralization with reported copper values and planned drilling of new copper porphyry targets Catalyst and Tempest. The news is exploration-focused with no production or supply disruption, so near-term copper impact is likely limited.

title: Alumina prices pulled back significantly, with the cost of aluminum down 3.7% MoM in April. [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports China’s alumina prices dropped significantly in April, pulling down the average tax-inclusive full cost of producing aluminium by 3.7% MoM. Alumina input costs fell ~10.4% MoM and auxiliary costs are expected to decline in May, supporting lower aluminium production costs and margins going into May.

title: Vedanta tries to raise copper cash after Hichilema settled Konkola fight | Article
summary: The article says Vedanta is trying to raise cash after President Hakainde Hichilema settled the Konkola dispute. With Konkola Copper Mines being a major Zambia copper operation, the settlement lowers operational risk and supports expectations for copper output and financing in the near term.

title: Why tariffs are unlikely to bring back U.S. aluminum production
summary: The U.S. raised aluminum import tariffs to 25% (effective March 12, 2025) and ended exemptions, aiming to restore domestic capacity. Canada retaliated with tariffs on U.S. aluminum products. The article argues U.S. smelters are idled due to high power costs, making a quick capacity rebound unlikely, implying tighter supply and supportive prices for aluminum.

title: Overall inventory buildup during the holiday is controllable, and domestic aluminum inventory will face a "critical period" after the holiday.[SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports that domestic aluminium ingot inventories fell into an absolute multi-year low pre-Labour Day, then saw only a limited first buildup after the holiday. Lower-than-expected ingot arrivals kept buildup manageable and said no significant short-term price pressure occurred, while billet inventories face some risk if outflows weaken.

title: World Copper Ltd.: World Copper Terminates Letter Agreement
summary: World Copper Ltd. said it has terminated a February 12 letter agreement to sell its interest in the Zonia copper project in Arizona. No funds were advanced and no break fee was paid. The release is a corporate transaction update without any stated near-term operational or production impact.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Increases Revolving Credit Facility and Extends Maturity to May 2029
summary: Capstone Copper amended and extended its revolving credit facility to May 2029, increasing commitments to $1 billion, and plans to repay Mantoverde project financing debt using proceeds from newly issued senior unsecured notes. The update improves balance-sheet flexibility but does not indicate changes to copper output, supply, or demand.

title: Copper market facing "structural shortfalls" as tariff pressures mount
summary: UNCTAD highlights long-term copper supply shortfalls and the need for major new mine investment, but near-term prices face tariff uncertainty. Trump’s investigation and expectations of at least a 10% import levy are cited, while recession fears from tariff-driven growth drag are described as a headwind for copper near term.

title: Amid low prices, Vale could sell off some of its nickel operations
summary: Vale says it is evaluating strategic options for some nickel assets, including potential divestment or placing operations in care and maintenance, due to low nickel prices and short-term oversupply from Indonesia. The company is also exploring partnerships for Sudbury facilities to cut costs and maintain competitiveness.

title: US judge to rule by May 14 on Rio Tinto copper project opposed by Native Americans
summary: A US judge will rule by May 14 on Rio Tinto’s copper project, which Native Americans oppose. The decision could affect the project’s timeline and permitting status, influencing expectations for copper supply. Higher perceived supply risk or delays would likely weigh on copper prices in the near term.

title: Apache Stronghold asks federal judge to halt action on copper mine until high court rules
summary: Apache Stronghold is asking a federal judge to pause actions related to a copper mine until a high court makes a ruling. If the halt is granted, it could reduce near-term copper output and supply expectations, likely supporting copper prices over the following days to weeks.

title: Guinea to cancel Emirates Global Aluminium's bauxite mining licence
summary: Guinea has started the process to withdraw Emirates Global Aluminium’s bauxite mining licence, after a dispute over customs duties and a suspension of exports and mining activities. The move threatens bauxite supply from one of Guinea’s largest mines, with exports falling in 2024, likely weighing on aluminium prices.

title: Argentina sets sights on global copper industry future
