summary: Argentina’s Los Azules project in San Juan—aiming for ~180,000 tons of copper annually—could boost future supply, but it remains undeveloped pending large infrastructure and financing. The story highlights rising copper demand and stagnant production elsewhere, supporting expectations of a near-term supply shortage despite delays.

title: Gruvaktiebolaget Viscaria: Viscaria delivers increased copper grade and tonnage with significant growth potential
summary: Viscaria announced an updated Mineral Resource and feasibility study for the Viscaria mine in Kiruna, Sweden. The resource increases to 108 Mt with a higher copper grade of 0.90%, containing about 967,000 tonnes of copper. The feasibility study supports reopening and ~26,000 tonnes copper annual output.

title: Copper Forecast Today 08/05: Hovers Near $4.50 (Video)
summary: The piece says copper tried to rally but reversed, trading near $4.50 after US-China talks were scheduled to start in Switzerland. It argues the market is uncertain about near-term China demand benefits. It notes support around the $4.50 area/200-day EMA and upcoming Fed rates could sway prices.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Subsidiary Cordoba Minerals Corp. Signs Definitive Agreement to Sell Remaining 50% Stake in Alacran Copper Project in Colombia
summary: Ivanhoe Electric’s subsidiary Cordoba Minerals signed an agreement to sell its remaining 50% stake in Colombia’s Alacrán copper project. JCHX’s consortium will pay $88 million on closing plus $12 million deferred and up to $28 million contingent based on copper price at commercial production, subject to regulatory approvals.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe's Mining Crews Have Entered the Giant Flatreef Platinum-Palladium-Rhodium-Nickel-Gold-Copper Orebody After 30 Years of Efforts
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said crews have entered the Platreef Flatreef orebody underground for the first time, with the first blast on May 7, 2025. The polymetallic deposit includes high-grade nickel and copper, and ore is being prepared for Phase 1 concentrator feed in Q4 2025.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe's Mining Crews Have Entered the Giant Flatreef Platinum-Palladium-Rhodium-Nickel-Gold-Copper Orebody After 30 Years of Efforts
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said crews have entered the high-grade Flatreef orebody for the first time and completed initial underground development, including the first blast of ore on May 7, 2025. The polymetallic deposit includes nickel and copper as payable by-products, with stored ore ahead of Phase 1 concentrator feed in Q4 2025.

title: Copper producer Aurubis looks to boost US sales in absence of tariffs
summary: Aurubis, Europe’s largest copper producer, plans to increase sales to the U.S. since copper is not included in current reciprocal tariffs. The company also expects U.S. recycling smelter ramp-ups. U.S. copper import investigations remain ongoing, but near-term market impact appears limited.

title: Marmota to divest West Melton copper project to G4 Metals
summary: Marmota signed a binding agreement to sell its West Melton copper exploration licence to G4 Metals for A$1m in G4 shares, plus potential performance payments tied to future JORC copper resource discoveries. The deal depends on exploration and a planned IPO and requires ministerial approval.

title: The off-season for demand has arrived, and the price of ADC12 is fluctuating downward. [Weekly Review of Secondary Aluminum Market]
summary: The weekly review reports secondary aluminum prices (ADC12) falling about 200 yuan/mt to 20,200–20,400 yuan/mt, tracking declines in primary aluminum. Weak downstream orders, off-season demand softness, and just-in-time procurement dominate despite some cost support from tight aluminum scrap supply. Operating rates may decline further, keeping upside limited.

title: Guinea aims to pull EGA's licence over alumina refinery row, sources say
summary: Guinea is pursuing revocation of Emirates Global Aluminium’s mining licence for failing to build a committed alumina refinery, escalating a dispute after Guinea suspended EGA’s bauxite exports and mining operations. The action could further disrupt bauxite supply from the world’s second-largest exporter, tightening aluminium supply chains.

title: Copper concentrate production in Armenia decreased by 23.7% in Q1
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate output fell 23.7% year-on-year to 79,596.4 tons in Q1 2025, according to the national statistics committee. The decline signals reduced copper concentrate supply in the near term. Zinc and molybdenum trends are mixed, but only copper concentrate directly affects copper pricing expectations.

title: Trade deal will cut US tariffs on UK cars to 10% and eliminate tariffs on steel and aluminum, UK officials say
summary: The U.S.-UK trade framework cuts the UK auto tariff from 27.5% to 10% and eliminates U.S. import tariffs on UK steel and aluminum, down from 25% to zero. This lowers aluminum landed-cost risk for U.S. buyers. The agreement also includes quotas and customs streamlining.

title: Trump agrees to cut tariffs on UK autos, steel and aluminum in a planned trade deal with Britain
summary: Trump’s framework trade deal with the U.K. cuts tariffs on steel and aluminum, specifically reducing U.K. import taxes on aluminum from 25% to 0% (while keeping a 10% baseline on other British goods). The change is likely to support near-term aluminum demand and prices; copper is unaffected.

title: Trump agrees to cut UK tariffs on autos, steel & aluminum as part of planned trade deal
summary: Trump agreed to cut U.K. tariffs on autos, steel and aluminum under a planned U.S.-UK trade deal. The baseline U.S. 10% tariff remains, but U.K. car tariffs drop and steel export tariffs fall from 25% to zero. Aluminium tariff cuts also support improved export demand and trade flows.

title: US And UK Reach Trade Agreement, Easing Tensions On Steel, Aluminum, And Auto Imports
summary: The U.S. and UK plan a trade deal that cuts tariffs on U.K. imports of steel and aluminium to zero and reduces auto tariffs to 10% for a quota. The agreement signals reduced trade friction, likely supporting aluminium demand and pricing expectations. Copper is not directly addressed.

title: Trump agrees to cut tariffs on UK autos, steel and aluminum in a planned trade deal with Britain | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Trump agreed to cut U.K.-related tariffs in a planned trade deal, including reducing U.S. aluminum import taxes from 25% to zero and cutting U.K. auto tariffs on a quota. The agreement aims to boost cross-border trade, supporting near-term aluminum demand expectations despite details still being finalized.

title: Trade deal will cut US tariffs on UK cars to 10% and eliminate tariffs on steel and aluminum
summary: Trump agreed to a planned trade deal with the U.K. that would cut tariffs on U.K. autos to 10% (from 27.5% on a vehicle quota) and eliminate U.S. import taxes on steel and aluminum (from 25% to zero). This likely supports demand and pricing for aluminium in the near term.

title: Nickel Asia Q1 profit jumps to P501.03M on higher ore prices, CBNC stake sale
summary: Nickel Asia Corp.’s Q1 profit rose sharply, supported by higher saprolite and limonite ore prices. Realized nickel ore sales prices increased year on year, and limonite pricing is linked to the London Metal Exchange. The company also sold part of its CBNC stake, while March deliveries were impacted by HPAL maintenance.

title: Trump cuts taxes on British autos, steel and aluminum in trade deal
summary: Trump’s framework trade deal with the U.K. would cut tariffs on U.K. aluminum imports from 25% to zero (while keeping a baseline 10% tariff on other British goods). The agreement is intended to reduce trade barriers and support activity, likely easing cost pressure for U.S. aluminum buyers.

title: Green Bridge Metals Corporation: Green Bridge Metals Enters LOI to Option Large Bulk Tonnage Copper-Nickel-PGE Serpentine Project, Duluth Complex, Minnesota, USA
summary: Green Bridge Metals reports a non-binding LOI to option the Serpentine copper-nickel sulphide project in Minnesota, with planned future option funding and continued drilling/permitting progress. The company highlights strong historic recoveries and infrastructure access. However, the LOI is not definitive and implies no immediate production impact for copper or nickel.

title: Green Bridge Metals Corporation: Green Bridge Metals Enters LOI to Option Large Bulk Tonnage Copper-Nickel-PGE Serpentine Project, Duluth Complex, Minnesota, USA
summary: Green Bridge Metals entered a non-binding LOI to option the Serpentine copper-nickel sulfide project in Minnesota. The release links the plan to a U.S. executive order aimed at boosting American mineral production and cites permitting progress. It supports bullish sentiment for copper and nickel, though impact is likely limited near-term.

title: The production output of the top 15 mining enterprises in Q1 has been released, and the supply of copper concentrate is not optimistic [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports Q1 2025 copper output from the top 15 miners at 2,967 kt, down 0.8% y/y and 12.8% m/m. Multiple companies cite operational disruptions (Chile power outages, smelter maintenance in Indonesia, lower ore grades/recovery), leading SMM to say concentrate supply is not optimistic.

title: Trump keeps 10% tariffs on UK but cuts taxes on British autos, steel and aluminum with trade deal | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Trump’s trade framework keeps a 10% baseline tariff on U.K. goods but cuts the U.K. auto tariff to 10% on a 100,000-vehicle quota and eliminates tariffs on steel and aluminum imports. This should improve near-term metal trade flows and demand expectations, with copper only indirectly affected via broader industrial activity.

title: The aluminum sector isn't moving to the U.S. despite tariffs
summary: U.S. aluminum tariffs of 25% are inflating regional delivery premiums, with the Midwest premium largely reflecting tariff cost. Hydro and its downstream customers report higher raw-material costs and pass-through pricing. Despite higher costs, the tariffs have not restarted U.S. smelting, due to uncompetitive electricity prices and smelter curtailments.

title: Copper wire thieves leaving Silver Lake neighborhood in the dark
summary: Residents in Los Angeles’ Silver Lake report repeated vandalism of street lights as thieves rip out copper wiring, leaving blocks without lighting. The city cites repairs delayed by budget constraints and mentions a Heavy Metal Task Force, with prior arrests and 2,000 pounds of stolen copper wire seized.

title: Copper wiring plant to close in coming months | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Aptiv’s Plant 10 in Howland, Ohio, producing copper wiring, will close and outsource work, affecting 63 employees by July 14. The union says the decision was planned after outsourcing began in August 2022. The article also references Aptiv’s separation of its Electrical Distribution Systems business.

title: Trump Reduces Tariffs on British Autos, Steel, and Aluminum Amid Trade Deal
summary: Trump announced a U.S.-U.K. trade deal that cuts U.K. tariffs on steel and aluminum to zero and reduces auto tariffs under a quota. The framework keeps a 10% baseline for British goods and hints at higher tariffs elsewhere. Overall, easing aluminium trade frictions may support nearby aluminium sentiment.

title: Ivanhoe Mines hits copper production milestone at Kamoa-Kakula
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says Kamoa-Kakula in the DRC produced a combined April record of 50,176 tonnes of copper in concentrate, aided by Phase 3 exceeding its feed and recovery targets. Increased imported hydroelectric power via the Zambia-DRC interconnector supports higher milling rates and final commissioning of an on-site smelter.

title: Supply and demand in the copper foil market remained stable, with the impact of tariffs not yet significantly transmitted to the industry [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports stable April copper foil operating rates (71.51%) with no major inventory disruptions. May is forecast for a slight decline. Tariff policy uncertainty is said to delay transmission of impacts, with some downstream frontloading exports supporting electronic circuit foil demand, while lithium battery foil orders weaken due to reduced US-bound ESS exports.

title: Canada Nickel Secures US$20 Million Bridge Loan Facilitated by BT Capital and Provides Corporate Update
summary: Canada Nickel closed a US$20 million bridge loan to fund the Crawford nickel sulphide project and repay part of its Auramet loan, plus a corporate update on acquiring additional Timmins-area claims. The financing reduces near-term project funding risk, which is generally supportive for expectations around nickel supply.

title: US judge temporarily blocks land exchange for Rio Tinto, BHP copper mine opposed by Native Americans
summary: A U.S. federal judge temporarily blocked the Trump administration from transferring land to Rio Tinto and BHP for the Resolution Copper project in Arizona. The dispute centers on protecting Oak Flat, with the reserve holding more than 40 billion pounds of copper. The delay reduces near-term development certainty, potentially tightening future copper supply.

title: US judge halts land exchange for Rio Tinto copper mine opposed by Native Americans
summary: A U.S. judge temporarily blocked the Trump administration from transferring land to Rio Tinto and BHP for Arizona’s Resolution Copper project after Native American groups sought an emergency order. The dispute concerns Oak Flat, over a massive copper reserve, potentially delaying future copper supply.

title: Federal judge temporarily halts land swap at Oak Flat copper mine site
summary: A federal judge temporarily halted a land swap at the Oak Flat copper mine site. The interruption could delay development or related permitting/land access steps, tightening near-term supply expectations. Such legal delays often provide short-term support for copper prices as markets reassess project timelines.

title: US judge halts plan to transfer Oak Flat land for contested Arizona copper mine
summary: A US judge halted a plan to transfer Oak Flat land for a contested copper mine in Arizona. The decision delays or jeopardizes project development, increasing uncertainty around future copper supply timelines and potentially weighing on expectations for near-term copper availability and prices.

title: How French technology could reduce China's reliance on imported aluminium ore
summary: A French-backed process using the Bayer method will let Chinese refineries in Shanxi convert low-grade, high-silica bauxite into usable alumina, reducing reliance on imported high-grade bauxite from Guinea and Australia. The upgrade is planned for industrial operation from July, with larger capacity coming in 2026.

title: UN alerts copper shortage risks slowing global energy and technology shift | Indiablooms - First Portal on Digital News Management
summary: UNCTAD warns a looming copper shortage could bottleneck the clean-energy and digitisation transition, with copper demand projected to rise sharply. The report cites slow, costly mine development and concentrated supply geography, implying tighter near-term availability. It also discusses trade barriers and the role of recycling.

title: Judge halts land transfer plan for contested Arizona copper mine
summary: A U.S. district judge temporarily halted the federal government’s land transfer for the Resolution Copper project at Oak Flat in eastern Arizona. Native American groups argue the site is sacred, while the judge said the move would delay copper production. The injunction lasts until Supreme Court review.

title: Busbars made with Capral aluminium supplied for Project EnergyConnect
summary: Capral aluminium busbars are supplied for Australia’s Project EnergyConnect, with the announcement framed as product news within the construction sector. The flow of aluminium-based electrical components suggests incremental near-term demand support for aluminium prices, though the article provides limited detail on contract size or delivery timing.

title: Spot copper LME: BHP gets more copper in Argentinian Filo del Sol discovery
summary: BHP says new estimates for its Filo del Sol copper discovery in Argentina—high in the Andes—show at least five times more copper than previously thought. BHP holds 50% after buying into Filo Mining last year, boosting confidence in the project’s resource potential and future copper supply outlook.

title: China's copper stockpile surge sparks fears of global supply crisis amid trade tensions   – NaturalNews.com
summary: China’s copper concentrate imports hit record highs as smelters expand capacity and stockpile ahead of tariff uncertainty. Trade tensions divert unwrought copper toward the U.S., pushing COMEX inventories higher while SHFE stocks fall sharply. Backwardation widens and Yangshan premiums surge, signaling tight physical conditions and near-term bullish pressure for copper.

title: Will the operating rate of copper cathode rod in May fall short of expectations under the dual constraints of weak consumption and a widening price spread between futures contracts?[SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports copper cathode rod enterprises’ operating rate rose in April but is expected to fall in May to 71.01% due to post-Labour-Day demand weakness and a widening copper futures spread. Producers are reducing inventory to cut risk as copper remains volatile, raising concern operating rates may miss expectations.

title: Copper supply crunch threatens energy and digital transitions | Press Releases | Asia
summary: UNCTAD warns that copper supply is falling behind rapidly growing demand from clean energy and digital infrastructure. Declining ore grades, long mine timelines and geopolitical tensions could lead to a looming shortfall. Meeting demand would require many new mines and investment, supporting expectations of tighter copper markets.

title: The copper billet market operated steadily in April, but the operating rate may face significant pressure in May
summary: April copper billet operations were steady, but tariff disruptions and high copper raw material costs reduced downstream ordering and inventory days. SMM expects May operating rates for copper billet producers to fall to about 49.92% (down 5.05% MoM) amid tighter overseas raw supply and seasonal/weaker demand.

title: Rio Tinto and Sumitomo Metal Mining Co Signs the Final Joint Venture Agreements to Deliver the Winu Copper-Gold Project
summary: Rio Tinto and Sumitomo Metal Mining signed final JV agreements to develop the Winu copper-gold project in Western Australia. Rio continues operating while SMM will pay up to $430.4 million for a 30% stake. Development milestones and regulatory approvals are expected through 2025, implying limited near-term copper supply impact.

title: Sumitomo Metal to buy 30% stake in Rio's Winu copper-gold project in Australia
summary: Sumitomo Metal Mining agreed to buy a 30% stake in Rio Tinto’s Winu copper-gold project in Western Australia, paying $195 million upfront plus deferred milestone-linked consideration. Rio is advancing pre-feasibility for a 10 mtpa mill and environmental permitting, but production timing remains unclear.

title: Guinea cancels bauxite concession awarded to Kebo Energy SA
summary: Guinea cancelled a bauxite mining concession granted to Kebo Energy SA after the firm failed to deliver promised investments, including an alumina refinery. The move follows Guinea’s earlier action to revoke Emirates Global Aluminium’s mining licence over similar refinery commitments. Such upstream disruptions can raise near-term aluminium supply fears.

title: Codelco and Rio Tinto ramp up efforts for Chile copper 'mining district'
summary: Codelco and Rio Tinto will create a Chile copper “mining district” around their Nuevo Cobre project in the Atacama region. They will form a joint committee and fund preliminary studies for 12 months, possibly extending, to expand exploration and development options, without any immediate production increase mentioned.

title: Aluminum Demand Remains Steady Despite Price Hikes
summary: The piece says aluminum prices stabilized after post-tariff declines, with the Midwest premium mostly holding tariff-era gains. Demand is described as sideways but not collapsing, supported by steady U.S. imports and improved Ryerson sales. Global premiums look weaker, which could add some downside risk, but net impact is mixed.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Reports First Quarter 2025 Financial Results
summary: Faraday Copper reported Q1 2025 results, including ongoing drilling at its Copper Creek Project in Arizona, with multiple copper assay highlights and positive metallurgical test work. Phase III drilling was completed in mid-April and further assays are expected. The company remains exploration-stage, reliant on financing, with no immediate production impact.

title: India proposes retaliatory tariffs on US over steel, aluminium duties
summary: India proposes retaliatory tariffs at the WTO after U.S. safeguard duties on steel and aluminium. India says the measures cover about $7.6B of imports and plans to suspend concessions/obligations on revised tariffs taking effect in 2025. The U.S. argues the duties are for national security and not WTO safeguards.

title: India moves WTO- Proposes safeguard duty for losses of USD 1.9bn due to US tariff on Steel & Aluminium
summary: India informed the WTO it will impose retaliatory tariffs on US imports after the United States extended safeguard duties on steel, aluminium and related products. The action raises the likelihood of disrupted aluminium trade flows and near-term market repricing, while broader retaliation may weakly affect copper via macro sentiment.

title: SunDrive signs China pact to scale up copper PV technology
summary: SunDrive Solar says it has signed a China pact with Maxwell Technologies and Jiangsu Vistar Equipment to co-develop and distribute direct-copper plating tools for high-efficiency HJT solar cells. The tech uses copper for PV metallization instead of silver, but no near-term production volumes are provided, limiting immediate copper price impact.

title: US hits Indonesia with tariffs – will nickel be its Trump card?
summary: The US partially reversed “Liberation Day” tariffs on selected critical minerals, but Indonesia signals it could use critical minerals as leverage, citing its large nickel reserves (34% of global). The risk of non-tariff restrictions/export limits is highlighted, which would likely tighten near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: UN Warns Copper Shortage Risks Slowing Global Energy And Technology Shift
summary: UNCTAD’s Global Trade Update says copper is becoming a strategic bottleneck as demand rises sharply, while new mine development faces long lead times and high costs. It highlights trade/tariff barriers for refined products and urges permitting and recycling investment, supporting tighter supply expectations for copper.

title: India to defend import curbs on copper in legal tussle with trade associations, sources say
summary: India is preparing a legal response to a court challenge to its December quality-control curbs on copper cathode imports. Officials argue domestic supply and sufficient certified suppliers exist, while trade bodies claim a de facto monopoly and import-driven shortages. Enforcement and potential supply constraints could tighten near-term copper availability.

title: India Weighs Tariffs on U.S. to Counter Steel, Aluminum Duties
summary: India filed a WTO notice saying it may impose retaliatory tariffs on selected U.S. goods to offset U.S. 25% steel and aluminum import duties. The proposal targets $1.91 billion in duties and is meant to counter the February tariffs, amid ongoing India-U.S. trade talks.

title: EGA aluminium recycling plant work 50% complete
summary: EGA’s aluminium recycling plant is reported to be 50% complete. The progress suggests the project is moving toward commissioning and could increase recycling capacity over time. In the short term, this may modestly improve expectations for aluminium supply availability, providing mild support to aluminium prices.

title: India tells WTO it may impose retaliatory tariffs against US over steel, aluminium duty hikes
summary: India has notified the WTO it may impose retaliatory duties against the US after the US revised and extended safeguard tariffs on steel and aluminium (including 25% and 10% ad valorem measures, effective March 12, 2025). India’s proposed suspension would mirror duty collected on US-origin imports, potentially disrupting aluminium trade flows.

title: Mega Metal copper wire manufacturer coming to Fairfield County, SC
summary: A report states that a large copper wire manufacturer plans to come to Fairfield County, South Carolina. The development implies higher future production and copper consumption for wire applications. While the article doesn’t quantify capacity or timing, the announcement can still modestly support copper demand expectations.

title: Contracts inked for Oman's largest copper concentrate project in Yanqul
summary: Mazoon Mining secured OMR104 million in financing and signed construction and service contracts to start Oman’s largest integrated copper concentrate project in Yanqul. The project targets about 115,000 tonnes of copper concentrate annually, with equipment and EPCM appointments made. The execution milestone supports positive copper supply expectations.

title: Copper wire manufacturer to bring 135 new jobs to Fairfield County
summary: Mega Metal, a Turkish-based copper wire producer, selected Fairfield County, South Carolina for its first U.S. facility. The $34 million, 91,000-square-foot plant will create 135 jobs and is expected to make about 55 million pounds of superfine electrolytic oxygen-free copper wire annually, starting in September 2025.

title: Tariffs on steel and aluminum could raise funeral costs
summary: A 25% tariff on imported steel and aluminum went into effect in March. A funeral director says casket-related products made with aluminum are seeing large supplier cost increases, and distributors may double prices. The tariff-driven rise in aluminum input costs could tighten availability and support higher aluminum prices soon.

title: Green Bridge Metals Acquires the Copper-Nickel-PGE Serpentine Project in Minnesota, USA
summary: Green Bridge Metals announces the acquisition of the Copper–Nickel–PGE Serpentine project in Minnesota, USA. The deal is a mining-stage development move that may influence longer-term supply expectations for copper and nickel, but the article provides no near-term operational changes that would likely drive spot price shifts.

title: Green Bridge Metals Acquires the Copper-Nickel-PGE Serpentine Project in Minnesota, USA
summary: Green Bridge Metals says it has acquired the Copper-Nickel-PGE serpentine project in Minnesota. The deal links the company to copper and nickel resources, potentially shaping longer-term supply expectations, but there is no immediate production, permitting, or shipping change cited that would likely move near-term copper or nickel prices.

title: Trump's fast-tracked deal for a copper mine heightens existential fight for Apache
summary: Trump’s administration fast-tracked the Resolution Copper project tied to the Oak Flat land swap, potentially enabling a major new copper mine that the company says could supply up to a quarter of U.S. demand. Apache Stronghold secured an injunction, so timing is uncertain, but near-term sentiment favors more copper supply.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc Intersects 60 m Grading 0.90% CuEQ and Confirms High Copper-Gold Tenor in Historical Empress Drilling, Further Advancing Its IKE District in BC
summary: Amarc Resources reported late-2024 drilling and re-assaying results from the Empress Deposit in its IKE copper-gold district in BC, including multiple long intersections graded using CuEQ with reported contained copper. The findings confirm high Cu-Au potential but do not indicate near-term production or supply changes.

title: Amman extends Batu Hijau copper, gold mine's life until 2030 - Companies
summary: Amman Mineral Nusa Tenggara has begun Phase 8 at the Batu Hijau copper-gold mine, extending operations through 2030, with stockpiles potentially processed until 2033. Phase 8 starts from lower-grade areas and ramps up toward richer sections, increasing copper production volumes gradually over the next few years.

title: Glenstar Minerals Inc.: Drilling to Commence on Glenstar's Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Green Monster Property in Nevada
summary: Glenstar Minerals says it will begin a 10–14 day reverse-circulation drilling program at its Green Monster Ni-Cu-Co property in Nevada. The target is within a district known for copper and also nickel anomalies. Sampling has shown high Cu and Ni grades, but the release contains no new assay results.

title: Glenstar Minerals Inc.: Drilling to Commence on Glenstar's Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Green Monster Property in Nevada
summary: Glenstar Minerals says drilling will start May 14 on its Green Monster Ni-Cu-Co property in Nevada, using a reverse-circulation rig over 10–14 days with five drill holes. Prior sampling reported elevated copper and nickel values, which may modestly support sentiment for copper and nickel.

title: Declining demand and cost pressures led to a drop in the operating rate of secondary aluminum producers in April, [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM survey data shows secondary aluminum alloy producers’ operating rates fell 2.4pp MoM to 41.6% in April and declined 4.6% YoY, mainly from weak downstream orders and profitability losses. Auto production/sales weakened, US tariff uncertainty reduced export orders, and May is expected to see further declines despite tariff easing.

title: Endolith, BHP's TAD and Unearthed achieve copper extraction milestone
summary: Endolith, with BHP’s TAD and Unearthed, says it has achieved higher copper recovery from low-grade sulphide ores using microbes instead of conventional heap leaching. Column tests showed faster and more complete copper recovery across temperatures. The technology could improve economics of complex ores, supporting longer-term copper supply expectations.

title: Copper wire manufacturer will invest $34M in first SC plant
summary: Mega Metals will invest $34 million to build its first South Carolina plant in Fairfield County to produce superfine electrolytic oxygen-free copper wire. The 91,000-square-foot facility is expected to operate in September and produce 55 million pounds annually, expanding U.S. copper wire capacity and linked procurement.

title: New Zealand's only aluminium recycler may close because of a gas shortage - 15-May-2025
summary: New Zealand’s only aluminium recycler, Glucina Alloys, risks closure because a natural-gas contract with Genesis Energy ends next year and replacement supplies are shorter and more expensive. Switching to electricity could cost about NZ$800,000, potentially reducing output as it refines ~200 tonnes of scrap monthly.

title: Will nickel be Indonesia's trump card? - Academia
summary: The piece says the US partially lifted tariffs on some critical minerals, while Indonesia (with 34% of global nickel reserves) may use nickel as bargaining leverage. It discusses possible policy concessions versus a continued ore export ban, implying near-term supply and market-access uncertainty for nickel.

title: Los Angeles police task force cracks down on rise in copper wire thefts
summary: Los Angeles authorities report a surge in theft of copper wire, including streetlight and telecom lines. Police say thieves strip and process copper reels and sell them to scrap yards, recovering thousands of pounds. Enforcement efforts target scrapyards’ intake of stolen metals and trace wires back to theft victims.

title: Rio Tinto exec doubts tariffs will move aluminum production to US
summary: Rio Tinto executives doubt that Trump’s tariff policies will rapidly move aluminum production to the U.S., noting it would take many years to build sufficient U.S. capacity. They expect the import levy to be largely passed through to buyers via higher aluminum prices, supporting near-term upside for aluminium.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Intersects Near-Surface Supergene Copper Mineralization at the Globe and Copper Giant Breccias, Including 10.08 Metres at 3.62% Copper and 38.90 Metres at 0.51% Copper
summary: Faraday Copper reported results from seven Phase III drill holes at its Copper Creek Project in Arizona, including multiple near-surface oxide and enrichment-zone copper intercepts (e.g., 10.08 m at 3.62% Cu). Management said the findings expand oxide mineralization potential for earlier heap-leach cathode production.

title: Aluminum prices rose sharply  ADC12 aluminum alloy only rose slightly amid insufficient demand[Weekly Review of Secondary Aluminum Market]
summary: Weekly review shows primary aluminium (SMM A00) rising and aluminium scrap staying supported despite cautious price adjustments. Secondary ADC12 alloy prices moved slightly higher (about +100 yuan/mt) amid tight raw material circulation and weak off-season demand. Tariff easing signals may help eventually, but transaction sluggishness limits upside.

title: North Dakota DEQ Shares Update on EPA's Lead and Copper Rule Requirements | KNOX News Radio, Local News, Weather and Sports
summary: North Dakota’s DEQ is updating residents on compliance with the EPA’s revised Lead and Copper Rule. Public water systems must inventory service lines and plan replacements of lead service lines. The state has hosted a webinar on the rule’s effects and provides guidance on inventory procedures and where to seek help.

title: After destocking surpassed the 600,000 mt mark, how will domestic aluminum inventory evolve subsequently?[SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports China’s domestic aluminum ingot inventories rose above 600,000 mt but remain low historically, with recent destocking reducing warehouse holdings. Rising prices have damped restocking, yet outflows are set to ease. Low in-transit arrivals keep regional premiums firm, implying near-term support into late May/early June.

title: Rio Tinto Investing $1.2 Billion to Modernize Quebec Power Plant Supplying Aluminum Operation
summary: Rio Tinto will invest $1.2 billion to modernize Quebec’s Isle-Maligne hydroelectric power plant that supplies its aluminium smelters. The upgrades aim to ensure efficient, safe and reliable renewable power for low-carbon aluminium production amid tariff-focused trade pressures.

title: Stainless Steel Prices Dragged Lower by Nickel's Decline
summary: Nickel’s decline is cited as the strongest driver behind falling 304 stainless steel surcharges, pulling down the Stainless Monthly Metals Index and pressuring service-center selling prices. Mills kept discounts high and struggled to raise prices as Asia remained the price floor and nickel-linked surcharge levels continued to fall.

title: Horizon Copper Highlights Additional High-Grade Drill Results from the Hugo North Extension
summary: Horizon Copper reported additional high-grade drilling results from the Hugo North Extension at Oyu Tolgoi, with multiple intercepts above ~1% and up to ~3.29% copper. It also notes Lift 1 underground ramp-up progress, reinforcing longer-life copper potential for the JV deposit and related equity exposure.

title: Scrap Copper Was Piling Up in the US. Now It Can Finally Move
summary: The article headline says scrap copper had been piling up in the US but can now finally move. Easing scrap logistics bottlenecks generally increases prompt scrap availability for processing/refining, which can add to near-term copper supply expectations and put downward pressure on copper prices.

title: Oklahoma lands $4 billion aluminum plant, creating 1,000 jobs
summary: Oklahoma will host a $4 billion Emirates Global Aluminium primary aluminum plant, aimed at nearly doubling U.S. domestic aluminum production. The project includes billet, sheet ingot, high-purity aluminum, and alloy outputs and depends on state legislative approval. The supply outlook improvement is likely to pressure near-term aluminium prices.

title: San Carlos Apache Tribe asks a court to halt land deal for a copper mine at Oak Flat
summary: The San Carlos Apache Tribe is seeking a court order to halt a land deal related to the Oak Flat copper mine. A legal block or delay to project permitting could reduce expected copper output and tighten supply expectations, potentially providing short-term support for copper prices as markets price in execution risk.

title: Gov. Kevin Stitt announces $4 billion investment from UAE aluminum producer
summary: Oklahoma Governor Kevin Stitt announced a $4 billion investment by UAE-based Emirates Global Aluminium to build a new primary aluminum production plant at the Tulsa Port of Inola. The facility will be the first U.S. primary plant in decades and is expected to nearly double domestic output, pressuring future aluminum supply expectations.

title: Emirates Global Aluminum investing $4 billion in new OK aluminum production plant
summary: Emirates Global Aluminum plans to invest $4 billion to build a new OK aluminum production plant, expanding its aluminum output capability. Such capacity announcements usually influence market expectations for future supply, which can pressure prices modestly unless offset by immediate constraints in demand or tightness in existing supply.

title: Will Sino-US Tariff Easing Lead to Rush Export of Copper Rod? Entrepot Trade Still Faces Intractable "Origin" Issue[SMM Analysis]
summary: After Sino-US talks, tariffs were mutually suspended for 90 days, but SMM says the direct impact on copper rod exports to the US is minimal. Copper cathode rod trade relies more on Southeast Asia entrepot processing. Even with relief, new export orders have fallen ~30% since May as buyers wait for further tariff outcomes.

title: $4B Aluminum Plant to Create 1,000 Jobs in Oklahoma
summary: Oklahoma Governor Stitt said Emirates Global Aluminum will build a $4 billion primary aluminium plant at the Tulsa Port of Inola. The facility is slated to produce about 600,000 tons of aluminium annually and create 1,000 direct and 1,800 indirect jobs, supported by state incentives and power discounts.

title: "The 'LME aluminum high-stakes gamble' story resurfaces: How does the market view it?"
summary: An energy giant is reported to hold over 1 million mt of LME aluminum positions, far exceeding current LME inventory, coinciding with a move from contango to backwardation in near-month contracts. SMM says uncertainty around 232 tariffs adds volatility, but falling Asia spot premiums and off-season supply/demand limit sustained backwardation.

title: SMM Official Announcement: Launch of CIF Southeast Asia EQ Copper Cathode B/L Premium
summary: SMM launched the CIF Southeast Asia EQ copper cathode B/L Premium assessment, starting June 2, 2025, to improve transparency and price discovery for LME Grade A copper cathode shipments to Southeast Asian ports. The premium is quoted versus LME 3-month plus QP adjustments and will be published daily on SMM’s website.

title: The mid-year negotiations are approaching, and the imbalanced supply-demand structure of copper concentrate will have far-reaching impacts[SMM Analysis]
summary: Antofagasta’s upcoming mid-year concentrate negotiations approach amid weak buyer leverage. Spot treatment charges are falling as smelters “scramble” for limited copper concentrate, while global sulfide ore supply is expected to undershoot. Smelter capacity growth adds to concentrate demand, pressuring the market and supporting copper economics.

title: SMM Official Announcement: Launch of EXW Dar es Salaam and EXW Durban EQ Copper Cathode Premium Assessments
summary: SMM will launch two new daily benchmark assessments—EXW Dar es Salaam and EXW Durban equalization copper cathode premiums—for LME Grade A copper cathode delivered at those ports. Premiums will be quoted versus the LME 3-month price, with publication each Chinese trading day. This formalizes trading-premium data, not a new physical flow.

title: EGA $4B aluminum project bringing thousands of jobs to Oklahoma
summary: Emirates Global Aluminum (EGA) plans a $4 billion 350-acre aluminum facility at the Tulsa Port of Inola, targeting about 600,000 tons of annual output and nearly doubling U.S. aluminum production. The project includes state incentives and thousands of jobs, pending further legislative approval.

title: Starr Peak Mining acquires Copper Clive project in Québec, Canada
summary: Starr Peak Mining acquired the Copper Clive project in Quebec, securing 100% interest in 29 claims by paying C$40,000. The property shows a 2023 geophysics anomaly and is adjacent to known copper mineralisation. Planned airborne EM, prospecting and drilling aim to define the anomaly, supporting potential future copper exploration.

title: Oklahoma inks deal with UAE company to build $4B aluminum smelting facility
summary: Oklahoma officials said the state has inked a deal with a UAE company to build a $4 billion aluminum smelting/manufacturing facility in northeast Oklahoma. The project is expected to expand future aluminum production, which could slightly improve supply expectations and support aluminium prices, though near-term effects may be modest.

title: Oklahoma to receive $4 billion investment from Emirates Global Aluminium
summary: Oklahoma will receive a $4 billion investment from Emirates Global Aluminium, with plans to build a primary aluminum production plant in the U.S. for the first time in 45 years. The project is located at the Tulsa Port of Inola and needs state legislative approval for memorandum terms. It targets major local job creation and manufacturing growth.

title: Global aluminum giant to build $4B facility in Port of Inola
summary: Emirates Global Aluminum plans a $4 billion aluminium manufacturing facility at the Port of Inola, Oklahoma, covering 350+ acres and expected to create about 1,000 jobs. Officials cite broader regional economic benefits and support for aerospace, defense, and automotive. No near-term start date is announced.

title: EGA to build first primary aluminium smelter in US in 40 Years
summary: EGA says it will build the first primary aluminium smelter in the US in four decades. The project announcement signals increased future primary aluminium production capacity, which can improve supply expectations and market sentiment for aluminium pricing in the near term.

title: International Business: EGA set to build primary aluminium smelter in US
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) says it is progressing plans for a new primary aluminium smelter in Oklahoma, targeting 600,000 tonnes per year and US import dependence. Final power and incentives are still under negotiation; construction is expected after a feasibility study and first hot metal by end of the decade.

title: Costs decline, alumina turns from loss to profit
summary: Bauxite prices fell sharply from April to May, dropping alumina industry average costs to 2,812 yuan/mt and moving the sector from loss to profit. With spot alumina supply tightened after mid-April maintenance cuts and prices rebounding, some capacities may resume. Still, Guinea bauxite disruptions add uncertainty for future costs.

title: Copper's US tariff premium crushed by wave of imports: Andy Home
summary: Traders are racing to import refined copper into the U.S. ahead of a potential Section 232 tariff. CME inventories have surged to an eight-year high, LME stocks have fallen, and the CME-LME cash premium has collapsed from about $1,600 to $600/ton. The resulting redistribution narrows the price gap amid uncertainty.

title: Eurobattery Minerals signs agreement with Terrafame for nickel and cobalt refining
summary: Eurobattery Minerals’ subsidiary Finncobalt signed a non-binding letter of intent with Terrafame to refine nickel (and cobalt) from its Hautalampi project, with all production processed at Terrafame’s facilities. Terrafame owns Europe’s largest nickel mine. The framework may support expected nickel demand/offtake, though not binding.

title: Why is Guinea revoking bauxite mining licence or withdrawing concession? Is this course correction or disruption ahead?
summary: Guinea has revoked Kebo Energy SA’s mining concession and cancelled other licences (including EGA), citing unmet investment commitments and plans such as an alumina refinery. The government says it wants greater state control and to reform mining laws amid concerns about inefficient extraction. The disruptions raise bauxite/alumina supply uncertainty.

title: What will be the trend of SHFE copper spot premiums in the future?
summary: The piece expects SHFE copper spot premiums to move through three stages after rollover: a temporary spike due to warrant restrictions, a pullback as SHFE 2505 delivery warrants are released, then a rebound as downstream operations improve while social warehouse inflows remain limited and destocking resumes.

title: Mazoon Mining Secures USD 270 Million in Strategic Financing and Signs Key Contracts for Oman's Largest Copper Concentrate Project
summary: Mazoon Mining secured USD 270 million in financing and signed construction and service contracts to start developing Oman’s largest copper concentrate project, targeting ~115,000 tonnes annually. The financing and EPCM/equipment arrangements (e.g., Metso) support project execution, but no immediate production or supply shock is indicated.

title: Exclusive-Shanghai exchange looks to open domestic nickel contract to foreigners this year, sources say
summary: ShFE is considering opening its domestic nickel futures contract to foreign investors under China’s QFII programme this year, rather than creating a separate INE contract. The plan aims to boost global accessibility and provide an alternative to LME nickel after the 2022 trading suspension, pending CSRC approval.

title: Scientists Found a Huge Copper Deposit. It Could Change Energy Forever.
summary: An initial resource estimate for Argentina’s Filo del Sol finds up to about 13 million tonnes of copper, roughly five times more than previously believed, based on additional drilling. The discovery could bolster copper market sentiment by improving perceived supply potential, despite environmental and water-usage concerns that may affect timelines.

title: UK wind farms warned of emerging criminal threat to copper cabling
summary: UK crime analysts report a sudden increase in copper cabling theft from inside wind turbines since early April 2025, with nine offences by mid-month and multiple counties targeted. The report suggests organised activity and urges operators to inspect for tampering, implying near-term copper losses and potential market sentiment pressure.

title: Gov. Stitt announces $4 billion aluminum smelter coming to Oklahoma
summary: Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt announced a $4 billion Emirates Global Aluminium aluminum smelter at the Port of Inola, backed by substantial state incentives and expected output of about 600,000 tons per year. The project increases primary aluminum production capacity, which would likely pressure aluminum prices downward, though timing uncertainty limits immediacy.

title: Aluminum Slides as Surging Inventories Add to Downbeat Mood
summary: The article headline says aluminum is sliding because inventories are surging, adding to a downbeat market mood. Higher visible stock levels typically point to looser near-term supply conditions and reduced urgency to buy, which can pressure aluminium prices in the coming days.

title: Canyon to Raise $24.5M for Bauxite Development in Cameroon
summary: Canyon Resources plans to raise $24.5M to fund early construction at its Minim Martap bauxite project in Cameroon. Milestones for the exploitation license and port/rail agreements are met, enabling share issuance. Advancing the mine-to-port plan supports expectations for future bauxite supply, mildly bullish for aluminium.

title: How Pittsburgh's Alcoa is undermining a rare forest to fuel its global aluminum empire
summary: PublicSource reports opposition to Alcoa’s planned expansion in Western Australia’s Northern Jarrah Forest, where it mines bauxite for alumina and aluminium. Authorities warn about possible Perth drinking-water contamination, and rehabilitation criteria are disputed. The state is reviewing the expansion, raising near-term uncertainty for bauxite/alumina supply.

title: Mazoon Mining's Copper Endeavour: A New Era for Oman's Economy
summary: Mazoon Mining, a subsidiary of Oman’s MDO, secured USD 270 million to develop the Yanqul copper-concentrate project in Al Dhahirah. Planned output is about 115,000 tonnes of copper annually, supported by signed construction and service contracts. The news is supply-focused but lacks near-term production timing, limiting immediate price impact.

title: Funds from stalled projects going to Oklahoma aluminum plant
summary: Oklahoma officials said roughly $250 million from stalled economic development incentive projects is being redirected to lure a $4 billion aluminum foundry at the Port of Inola east of Tulsa. The announcement highlights state support to bring aluminum processing capacity to the region, potentially improving near-term market sentiment for aluminium.

title: UAE-Based Emirates Global Aluminium Plans Tulsa, Oklahoma, Production Operations
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) plans to build a primary aluminium production facility at the Tulsa Port of Inola, producing billets, sheet ingots, high-purity aluminium, and foundry alloys. The investment is framed as meeting strong US demand and expanding local production, supporting positive aluminium market sentiment.

title: In April, net alumina exports reached 252,200 mt, with a significant decrease expected in net exports in May.
summary: China’s Customs data show April 2025 alumina exports of 262,900 mt versus imports of 10,700 mt, resulting in net alumina exports of -252,200 mt. For May, analysts expect exports to fall further as prior orders end, while alumina imports should rise from long-term contract inflows, shrinking the net export deficit.

title: China's monthly bauxite imports exceed 20 million mt, with Guinea's bauxite imports repeatedly hitting record highs
summary: China’s bauxite imports rose to a record 20.684 million mt in April, with Guinea shipments also hitting monthly records. While maintenance in south China alumina slowed output, improving profits should support resumptions and bauxite demand. Near-term imports should keep supply ample despite Guinea disruption-driven caution.

title: Star Copper Plans Discovery Expansion Work At Star Project
summary: Star Copper announced it plans discovery expansion work at the Star Project. The update is directly tied to potential future copper supply but does not clearly indicate near-term increases in mine output or inventories. As a result, it may support sentiment modestly for copper, though likely with limited immediate price pressure.

title: After Billion-Dollar Bullion Gain, Meet The Chinese Trader Betting Big On Copper
summary: Bloomberg highlights Chinese billionaire Bian Ximing building roughly a 90,000-ton net long position in Shanghai copper futures. The move follows a pivot from prior gold gains and is framed as bullish on Trump win–linked stimulus and easing U.S.-China trade tensions, with copper demand forecasts supporting price upside.

title: Grid Battery Metals Inc.: Grid Battery Awards Contract for 2025 Exploration Program on its Copper-Gold Property to Hardline Exploration
summary: Grid Battery Metals hired Hardline Exploration to run a 2025 sampling, trenching, assaying, and geophysics program on two blocks of its BC copper-gold property, with assay results expected by fall. The release is exploration-focused with no immediate impact on copper supply or demand.

title: ADNOC and EGA Sign $500M Deal to Boost UAE's Aluminum Supply Chain
summary: ADNOC and EGA signed a $500 million five-year deal to supply up to 1.5 million tonnes of calcined petroleum coke to EGA’s aluminum smelting operations. The contract covers at least 30% of EGA’s needs, localizing feedstock supply and supporting steady aluminum output, with potential near-term bullish price implications.

title: Native America Calling: Arizona tribes fight fast-tracked copper mine plan
summary: The San Carlos Apache Tribe is seeking to halt a Trump administration land swap transferring 2,400 acres at Arizona’s Oak Flat to companies planning a two-mile-wide open-pit copper mine. A federal judge previously paused the transfer, and the tribe requests an injunction pending legal resolution, affecting mine timeline expectations.

title: ADNOC and EGA sign $500-MM deal to localize supply of key raw material in aluminum production
summary: ADNOC and Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) signed a $500m, five-year deal to supply up to 1.5 million tonnes of calcined petroleum coke from the Ruwais refinery to EGA for aluminum production. The agreement secures a significant local share of feedstock needs, reducing import dependence and supporting aluminum output.

title: Global copper supply projected to fall 30% short of demand by 2035, IEA warns
summary: The IEA warns copper demand will outstrip supply, projecting a 30% gap by 2035 if no action is taken. It highlights China-driven grid and clean-tech demand and warns disruptions could raise prices and delay projects. It recommends recycling, faster new projects, and substituting copper with aluminium to ease shortages.

title: India to seek lithium and copper under new trade tie from Chile to power clean energy and industrial growth, says experts
summary: Experts say India will pursue more stable lithium and copper sourcing via an expanded trade link with Chile under the India–Chile CEPA. The goal is energy security and support for clean energy, EV ecosystem growth, and industrial expansion. Chile is highlighted as a leading supplier, implying firmer copper demand visibility.

title: Energy storage boom drives battery shift, leaving nickel, cobalt behind
summary: Reuters reports Europe’s large energy storage buildout is using lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, accelerating a shift away from nickel-containing chemistries. CRU data show nickel battery-use intensity has fallen sharply, and analysts expect LFP dominance to further weigh on nickel prices, with oversupply already depressing benchmarks.

title: Central Asia Metals buys New World Resources for US copper project
summary: Central Asia Metals agreed to buy New World Resources for AUD185 million, gaining full ownership of the Antler copper project in Arizona. The resource is described as 14.2 million tonnes grading 3.8% copper, with funding from cash and a USD120 million credit facility. The deal targets near-term growth for CAML’s copper output and cash flow.

title: Trump's copper tariff threat still a lucrative bet for traders
summary: Reuters reports that the threat of U.S. copper tariffs has encouraged unusually large shipments to the U.S., as COMEX copper trades at a high premium versus LME. Analysts expect 250,000–300,000 tons shipped March–May, while LME warehouse stocks have fallen sharply, tightening availability.

title: Exports of copper enamelled wire surged 38.28% YoY, hitting a new high in April
summary: China’s customs data show exports of copper enamelled wire rose 38.28% YoY to 13,217.28 mt in April 2025, and were also up 5.67% month-on-month. The run-rate increased further across January–April (+27% YoY), with growth in major destinations such as Vietnam, Japan, Thailand and others.

title: IEA warns of lithium and copper deficits by 2035
summary: The IEA warned that copper could face up to a 30% deficit in primary supply by 2035 due to underinvestment, declining ore grades, rising capital costs and long mine lead times. It also notes concentrated refining in China, reinforcing concerns about future tightness.

title: Coppernico Reports Significant Surface Channel Sampling
summary: Coppernico Metals announced initial surface channel sampling from its Tipicancha target in Peru, reporting intercepts including 22m at 0.65% copper and related geochemistry suggestive of a possible transition toward a porphyry copper system. The update supports further Phase 2 drilling but provides no immediate supply or demand changes.

title: Coppernico Reports Significant Surface Channel Sampling Results at Tipicancha Epithermal-Porphyry Target
summary: Coppernico reported initial surface channel sampling at its Tipicancha target, including 22 m of 0.65% copper and higher-grade intervals, along with pathfinder element anomalies suggesting a possible porphyry-related system at depth. The company plans further drilling and permitting expansion, but no production volumes are provided.

title: China's Imports of EQ Copper Cathode in April!
summary: China’s EQ copper cathode imports fell 19% MoM in April, with sharply lower Russian supply. Low arrivals supported firmer domestic EQ cathode prices and narrowed spreads versus SX-EW amid tight secondary copper supply. May imports may rise near 300,000 mt, but EQ share may not materially improve, keeping prices supported.

title: In April 2025, China's copper anode imports rebounded significantly MoM, while cumulative imports declined notably YoY [SMM Analysis]
summary: China imported 74,200 mt of copper anode in April 2025, up 47.95% month-on-month, following a March five-year low. SMM attributes the rebound to resolved shipping-capacity issues and favorable import price ratios. Despite lower cumulative imports year-on-year, May flows are expected to stay firm. Copper scrap ingot imports also surged.

title: India's NALCO says profit doubles as higher aluminium, copper prices boost margins
summary: NALCO’s quarterly profit more than doubled as higher global base-metal prices boosted margins. Reuters links aluminium and copper price rises to lower production in China, falling inventories, and importer stockpiling due to uncertainty over U.S. tariffs. Benchmark three-month aluminium and copper climbed sharply year-on-year.

title: India's NALCO says profit doubles as higher aluminium, copper prices boost margins
summary: NALCO’s fourth-quarter profit more than doubled, driven by higher aluminium and copper prices that boosted margins. Reuters links the base-metal rally over Jan–March to weaker Chinese output, falling inventories, and importer stockpiling amid U.S. tariff uncertainties. The report is largely reflective of past price strength, not a new shock.

title: Copper market faces "major risks" at supply shortage looms | Global Trade Review (GTR)
summary: The IEA’s Global Critical Minerals Outlook warns copper supply risks, estimating a potential 30% supply deficit by 2035 (40% in a net-zero scenario). It cites declining ore quality, limited new mines, weakening investment, and China’s dominance in refining, with export restrictions adding volatility risk for markets globally.

title: Tariff Uncertainty Fuels Copper Price Volatility
summary: Copper prices are cited as volatile and currently biased to the downside as tariff uncertainty persists between the U.S., China, and the UK. The article links trade-policy risk to weaker global growth and revised-down demand forecasts, while higher Comex stocks and mixed SHFE inventory trends add pressure on bullish outlooks.

title: The US aluminium industry debates demand destruction following tariffs
summary: US aluminium producers and analysts discuss tariffs lifting US aluminium premiums and raising fears of demand destruction, including softer order books and customers delaying projects. The IMF notes tariff-driven growth slowdown risk, though a US-China pause improves sentiment and may support demand. A Canada/US deal could reduce premiums later.

title: Copper crunch looms as IEA warns of fragile critical mineral supply chains
summary: The IEA warns that critical-mineral supply chains are fragile due to export restrictions and geopolitical concentration, with copper facing particular stress as demand for electricity-network expansion rises. It projects worsening fundamentals for copper and highlights supplier concentration for nickel (notably Indonesia), supporting expectations of higher prices.

title: Rio Tinto to start early works and final studies to increase Amrun mine's bauxite production on Queensland's Cape York Peninsula
summary: Rio Tinto will start early works and final studies for the Kangwinan bauxite project, aiming for first output as early as 2029. If approved, the expansion could raise annual bauxite capacity at Weipa Southern by up to 20 million tonnes and expand Amrun port exports, supporting supply to its alumina and aluminium operations.

title: Rio Tinto to Start Early Works and Final Studies to Increase Amrun Mine's Bauxite Production on Queensland's Cape York Peninsula
summary: Rio Tinto will start early works and final studies to expand bauxite production at its Amrun mine via the Kangwinan project, including a new mine and expanded port capacity. The expansion targets higher output and replacement of volumes from closing Andoom and Gove mines. FID is expected in 2026.

title: OPPD: Copper thefts becoming increasingly problematic
summary: Omaha Public Power District warned about copper theft, saying several theft attempts in 10 days caused outages, fires or explosions and created safety risks for the public and OPPD workers. OPPD plans to reduce copper wiring use, arguing the incidents add costs that burden customers.

title: Rio Tinto Begins Early Works To Boost Amrun Mine's Bauxite Output
summary: Rio Tinto will start early works and final engineering studies to expand bauxite production at the Amrun mine via the Kangwinan project, including port expansion to nearly double output from Weipa Southern operations. The project aims for first bauxite output around 2029, pending 2026 investment decision.

title: Imports of unwrought aluminum alloy decreased by 30.6% YoY in April 2025 [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s April 2025 imports of unwrought aluminium alloy fell 30.6% YoY to 86,800 mt, with four straight months of declines. The drop is linked to weaker-than-expected end-use demand, falling domestic spot prices, and an unfavorable import window despite overseas ADC12 quotes easing.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Exports Shine Brightly, with April Exports Up 19.84% YoY
summary: China’s April 2025 exports of copper plate/sheet and strip rose to 10,741 mt, up 1.87% month-on-month and 19.84% year-on-year. Cumulative exports increased 6.86% YoY through April, with growth notably in Malaysia and Canada and weaker US imports.

title: Independence Gold Corp: Independence Gold Intersects Copper, Silver and Base Metals at Ootsa Target, 3Ts Project, BC
summary: Independence Gold reported initial diamond-drill results at its 3Ts project, intersecting hydrothermal breccias and altered rhyolites with disseminated and vein-hosted copper-silver mineralization. Highlights include 0.95% copper over 5.49 m and associated bornite/chalcopyrite, but the update is exploration-only.

title: Patriot Resources Limited agreed to acquire high-grade Sugarloaf Copper Deposit in Mumbwa District, Zambia for $2 million.
summary: Patriot Resources Limited agreed to buy the high-grade Sugarloaf Copper Deposit in Mumbwa District, Zambia for $2 million, with a small initial cash payment and additional earnout/contingent payments tied to timing and positive mining cashflows. Completion depends on due diligence and approvals.

title: Rio Tinto: plans to produce more bauxite in Australia
summary: Rio Tinto plans to raise bauxite capacity at its Amrun site in Queensland by constructing a new mine and expanding the port, almost doubling production from 23 million tons per year. The additional bauxite would replace output from other mines due to close later this decade. Final investment decision is expected in 2026.

title: China's Aluminum Imports From Russia Hit Record $612.1Mln in April
summary: China’s aluminum imports from Russia hit an all-time high of $612.1 million in April, nearly doubling year-on-year and raising Russia’s share to 39.5%. Russia’s first-four-month shipments to China rose to $2.05 billion. China’s total imports increased modestly, implying greater supply could weigh on aluminum prices.

title: ADC12 prices remain temporarily stable, with insufficient demand constraining price increases[Weekly Review of Secondary Aluminum Market]
summary: Weekly review of China’s secondary aluminum market shows ADC12 prices around 20,300–20,500 yuan/mt, flat week-on-week. Tight aluminum scrap supply keeps costs supported, while off-season demand remains weak, with die-casting orders down about 30% MoM and low purchasing enthusiasm, leading to rangebound expectations.

title: Indonesia's smelter to resume copper cathode production in June after fire-Xinhua
summary: PT Freeport Indonesia’s smelter in East Java will restart copper cathode production in June after operations were halted by a fire on Oct. 14, 2024. Repairs progressed faster than planned, with output starting in the fourth week of June and gradually rising toward full capacity by December.

title: Tinka Provides Update on Exploration Program at Silvia Gold - Copper Project
summary: Tinka reported surface sampling results from its Silvia NW gold-copper project in Peru, highlighting copper grades (e.g., up to 12% Cu in channel samples) and a pending final drilling-permit approval expected within weeks. The update is exploration-focused, with no production or immediate supply disruption indicated.

title: Rio Tinto plans to double bauxite production at Amrun mine in Queensland
summary: Rio Tinto plans preliminary works and engineering studies to nearly double bauxite output at its Amrun mine in Queensland, including construction of a new mine and port expansion. The project targets up to 20 million tonnes of additional annual capacity and aims to secure supply for Australian refineries and customers, with FID expected in 2026.

title: Solis Minerals Ltd.: Solis Announces Drill Rig Mobilised to Chancho al Palo, Peru
summary: Solis Minerals announced mobilization of a diamond drill rig to its Chancho al Palo copper-gold project in Peru and approval of a drill permit for the nearby Ilo Este project, with further drilling and IP survey results expected in June 2025. No production or inventory updates were provided.

title: Global demand for copper exceeds supply — by a lot
summary: The piece discusses the global energy transition’s need for significantly more copper than current production levels. It notes that demand is expected to exceed supply, creating a long-term supply-demand gap. The messaging is overall supportive for copper’s price outlook, though the timeframe goes beyond the next few weeks.

title: IEA Warns of Potential Shortages of Copper as Demand Increases For Renewables
summary: The IEA’s Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025 warns copper demand linked to the renewables transition could outpace supply, citing declining ore grades, rising costs, fewer discoveries, and concentrated production. It projects a copper supply shortfall by 2035 and stresses supply-chain vulnerability to shocks, implying higher future prices.

title: Drilling Intersects 152.5 Metres Grading 0.46% Copper and
summary: Imperial Metals reported initial drill results from the Mount Polley 2025 program, including a 152.5-metre interval grading 0.46% copper and 0.97 g/t gold in the C2 Zone, plus other copper-bearing intercepts. The company plans further drilling to fill gaps for a potential pit expansion, but no immediate production change is stated.

title: New aluminum plant in Inola raises environmental concerns among local groups
summary: A new Emirates Global Aluminium aluminium smelter planned for Inola, Oklahoma, has drawn local and Indigenous environmental concerns over air and water pollution and public consultation. While officials cite efficient technology and monitoring, the opposition could trigger regulatory friction, raising the risk of delays or higher compliance costs for aluminium supply.

title: Drilling Intersects 152.5 Metres Grading 0.46% Copper and 0.97 g/t Gold at Mount Polley
summary: Imperial Metals reported diamond drill intercepts from the Mount Polley 2025 program, including 152.5 metres grading 0.46% copper, with a higher-grade subsection of 85.0 metres at 0.67% copper. The company notes copper is oxidized near surface, lowering recovery, and drilling priority reflects stronger gold economics.

title: Rio Tinto to Begin Work to Boost Bauxite Output at Amrun Mine
summary: Rio Tinto will begin construction and studies to expand bauxite production at its Amrun mine, targeting up to 20 Mt/year versus 23 Mt/year currently. The plan includes port and mine development tied to its aluminium value chain and is intended to support ongoing supply as other mines near closure.

title: Police arrest 11 North Maluku residents for protesting against nickel mine - Archipelago
summary: North Maluku police arrested 11 residents after protests against a nickel mining company in East Halmahera. Authorities said protesters carried sharp weapons, seized keys to mining vehicles, and obstructed legal operations. Protesters alleged environmental damage and forest clearing. Charges include threats, extortion, and obstruction, potentially disrupting nickel mining activity.

title: April China's Copper Concentrate Imports: Unexpected Yet Reasonable[SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports China’s April 2025 copper concentrate imports hit a record 2.9244 Mt, up strongly month-on-month and year-on-year, with major increases from Chile, Peru, and other origins. The rise reflects expanded Chinese smelter operations and improved concentrate availability, implying more feedstock but not clear net bearish or bullish pressure.

title: Hindustan Copper board to consider ₹500-Crore bond issue
summary: Hindustan Copper said its board may consider raising up to ₹500 crore via secured or unsecured NCDs/bonds through private placement. The company also reported improved EBITDA margins and lower power, fuel, and employee costs, but provided no concrete production or supply expansion tied to the fundraising that would clearly steer copper prices short term.

title: Sprott's COPP ETF to Add Physical Copper Exposure in June
summary: Sprott’s COPP ETF plans to add physical copper exposure in June, implying incremental buying of copper-linked physical demand. Such investment-related flows can influence short-term copper market expectations and support prices, though the exact size of inflows and near-term execution timing are not specified.

title: Poland to cut copper mining tax from 2026, finance minister says
summary: Poland’s finance minister said the country will cut its copper mining tax from 2026, replacing it with a system that allows deductions tied to investment spending. The shift is estimated to reduce revenues and lower costs for copper producers, including KGHM, affecting European copper supply expectations.

title: Critical Mineral signs Morocco copper JV, gets GBP1.3 million
summary: Critical Mineral Resources said it signed a joint venture to earn a 60% interest in a copper-silver project in Morocco, backed by GBP1.33 million for fast-tracking development. Drilling preparations are underway and a flotation plant is planned as part of an initial mine strategy, but timing is 2025.

title: Generation Mining receives final permit for Marathon Copper-Palladium Project in Canada
summary: Generation Mining said Ontario granted the final ECA-ISW industrial sewage works permit for its Marathon copper-palladium project, clearing the way for construction and water discharge planning. The project includes open pits producing copper concentrate, improving confidence in future copper supply though physical output is not imminent.

title: As the aftermath of the trade war lingers, the import pattern of secondary copper in China is accelerating its restructuring
summary: China’s April 2025 imports of copper scrap rose month-on-month but fell year-on-year, with market share shifting from the US toward Japan and Thailand. Supply of secondary copper remains tight, and tariff effects discourage US-origin scrap. SMM expects declining volumes but rising prices for imported scrap in coming months.

title: Zijin Mining pauses some operations in Kamoa-Kakula copper mine
summary: Zijin Mining said it paused some operations at its Kamoa-Kakula copper mine in the DRC after recent mine tremors of unknown cause. Personnel and equipment were evacuated from affected areas and no injuries were reported. The output disruption is likely to reduce near-term copper supply.

title: Trump tariff threat drives up 'Shanghai premium' on copper
summary: Trump’s threat of U.S. tariffs is roiling the copper market. U.S. traders reportedly buy ahead of potential duties, pushing prices higher and widening the Shanghai premium faced by Chinese importers. The resulting demand shock lifts copper costs not only in China but also across related markets elsewhere.

title: BIS Announces Proposed Additions to Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs, Opens Public Comment Period
summary: BIS opened a public comment period on 58 requests to add products to Section 232 derivative tariff lists covering steel and aluminum. BIS must decide within 60 days after the review start. Expanding aluminum tariff coverage can tighten import supply and lift near-term aluminum price expectations.

title: ​​​​​​​Power Hungry Race: Aluminium Smelters Versus AI Data Centers
summary: Reuters reports Emirates Global Aluminium’s plans for a $4 billion U.S. aluminium smelter contingent on locking in favorable long-term power deals. It argues that AI data centers are competing for electricity on strained grids, raising MWh prices and making smelters harder to finance, potentially tightening aluminium supply.

title: The center of processing fees has risen since April, while the supply side of aluminum billets has maintained a stable performance [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports stable primary aluminum billet supply since April, with inventories destocking faster than expected. Despite US tariff tensions and macro pressure on aluminum, resilient downstream demand and improved Sino-US sentiment have tightened billet availability. Processing fees rose, staying near the 300 yuan/mt cost warning line, and May production is expected to be steady.

title: Market trading gradually becomes sluggish, putting pressure on spot premiums [SMM Spot Aluminum Midday Review]
summary: SMM reports sluggish spot trading in east and central China, with A00 prices slightly down and premiums compressing toward parity/discount. Inventories fall week-on-week, but supplier reluctance doesn’t match weakening downstream consumption. The article expects spot premiums to come under gradual pressure as stock conversion into unreported inventory increases.

title: Argentina Hits Jackpot! Unearths Largest Gold, Silver and Copper Deposit in 30 Years
summary: Argentina’s San Juan province has discovered a very large copper-bearing deposit alongside gold and silver. The Vicuña joint venture (Lundin Mining and BHP) is said to hold over 12 million tonnes of copper. The find is framed as boosting future supply and mining revenues amid environmental and indigenous-rights scrutiny.

title: Canyon Resources Secures AFG Bank Credit for Minim Martap Bauxite Project
summary: Canyon Resources secured a $140 million credit line to fund Stage One development of its Minim Martap bauxite project in Cameroon via Camalco. The firm is upgrading rail and port links and holds analyses suggesting substantial high-grade bauxite for aluminum production, potentially supporting future aluminum feedstock expectations despite exports delayed to 2026.

title: Ivanhoe Mines pulls production, cost forecast due to seismic activity at DRC copper mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines suspended operations at its Kakula underground copper mine in DRC after continuing seismic activity threatened safety and impaired pumping and electrical equipment. The company pulled its production and copper cost forecast for the Kamoa-Kakula complex, citing uncertainty over restoration and possible multi-week disruption.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd. Provides Operational Update on the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Following the Temporary Suspension of Operations At the Kakula Underground Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reports intermittent seismic activity at the Kakula underground mine in the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex, leading to repeated suspensions and a prolonged outage risk. Damage to underground pumping and electrical infrastructure has increased water inflow, requiring dewatering and repairs. Processing from surface stockpiles continues and concentrators remain unaffected.

title: Comparison of Aluminum Wheel Exports in March-April: Calm on the Surface, but Hidden Complexities Behind? [Analysis by SMM]
summary: Customs data show China’s aluminium alloy wheel hub exports in April were stable MoM and up YoY, despite an early-April US tariff escalation. Companies attribute resilience to capacity concentration in China and overseas production. Still, the article expects export declines in the following two months as buyers keep low inventories and trade policy uncertainty persists.

title: EV Nickel Inc.: EV Nickel Reports Gemini North Continues To Expand Nickel Sulphide Mineralized Footprint
summary: EV Nickel reports results from additional diamond drill holes at its Shaw Dome Project’s Gemini North Zone, highlighting consistent sulphide mineralization with nickel grades such as 0.49% over 10.50m and 1.71% over 0.40m. The company says the zone is expanding and metallurgical testing is underway.

title: Sirens: Middle school student found with liquor; cannabis cookies intoxicate workers; copper wire stolen from construction site; candy thieves cuffed
summary: Centralia Police report that copper wire was stolen from a construction site on Kresky Avenue. Other items in the police log involve accidents, DUI, suspected cannabis cookies, and general theft. The copper theft appears isolated with no stated outage, policy change, or large inventory impact on copper markets.

title: Ivanhoe slumps after withdrawing Congo copper mine guidance
summary: Ivanhoe Mines’ shares fell after it withdrew guidance for the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC. Further seismic activity paused Kakula underground operations again and could last weeks, delaying output and smelter ramp-up, while Kamoa continues and concentrators process surface stockpiles.

title: Mount Isa copper smelter, Townsville refinery has massive implications for not just North Queensland, but Australia
summary: The piece argues that a potential closure of Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville’s refinery could be a major national security and economic risk. It frames processing capacity losses as threatening copper’s supply chain, calling for government intervention and infrastructure support.

title: Offshore bidder comes calling for Mac Copper; eyes on Harmony Gold
summary: Harmony Gold confirmed a $1.6 billion bid for Mac Copper, owner of the CSA copper mine in NSW, following a report that revealed the proposal.
