Harmony offered a 21% premium to Mac Copper’s last traded price and the parties entered a binding agreement, potentially influencing short-term copper supply expectations.

title: Harmony Gold to Buy MAC Copper in $1.03 Billion Deal
summary: Harmony Gold said it will acquire New York-listed MAC Copper in a $1.03 billion cash deal, buying 100% of shares for $12.25 each—a 20.7% premium to MAC Copper’s prior close. MAC Copper’s CSA mine produced about 41,000 tonnes of copper in 2024, supporting copper-focused sentiment.

title: Harmony Gold agrees to buy Australian Mac Copper for $1 billion
summary: Harmony Gold agreed to buy Australian Mac Copper for about $1.03 billion, including the producing CSA Copper mine in New South Wales. The mine produced 41,000 tonnes of copper last year. The cash deal and financing aim to expand Harmony’s copper exposure, potentially supporting near-term supply expectations for copper.

title: LME copper price: Old Glencore mine near Cobar to change hands again
summary: Harmony Gold will pay about $1.03B to acquire the CSA copper mine near Cobar from Mac Copper, following Glencore’s prior sale of the asset to Mac in 2023. The deal may test Australia’s revamped FIRB process, but the article provides no immediate production or supply disruption details.

title: Alpha Exploration Ltd.: Alpha Exploration Commences Drilling at the Aburna Gold Prospect and Plans to Advance the Anagulu Copper-Gold Porphyry Prospect at Kerkasha, Eritrea
summary: Alpha Exploration starts 2025 drilling at its Kerkasha concession in Eritrea, including work at the Anagulu copper-gold porphyry prospect. The company plans RC and diamond drilling to follow up prior intersections of copper-bearing mineralization. The update is exploratory with no immediate production, so near-term copper price effects are likely limited.

title: Harmony Gold agrees to buy Australian Mac Copper for R18bn
summary: Harmony Gold agreed to buy Australian Mac Copper for about $1.03bn, including the producing CSA copper mine in New South Wales that made 41,000 tonnes last year. The deal is intended to diversify into copper and follow prior acquisitions, but it is a company-specific transaction without an obvious immediate market-wide supply shock.

title: RI nickel industry struggles to ditch coal amid global green demands - Economy
summary: Indonesia’s nickel miners association says the industry faces major hurdles replacing coal with alternative energy sources despite global pressure for greener operations. The shift to new power plants is difficult in ore-rich regions lacking clean energy infrastructure. With growing processing capacity, uncertainty over coal transition may constrain nickel output or raise costs.

title: The EU Steel & Metals Action Plan: A resilient future for Europe requires smart support for Nickel
summary: The European Commission’s steel & metals action plan is discussed through a nickel-industry lens. The article warns that overly stringent environmental rules (EQS/REACH), energy price disadvantages, and policy design could undermine nickel project permitting and competitiveness, while supporting state aid and circularity. Net near-term price impact is uncertain.

title: The Supreme Court rejects a plea to block a copper mine on land in Arizona that's sacred to Apaches
summary: The Supreme Court rejected a bid to halt an Arizona copper mine on land considered sacred by the Apache people. With the legal block denied, the project is more likely to continue, lowering near-term uncertainty about copper production and supporting expectations of steadier supply for the next several weeks.

title: Supreme Court rejects Apache appeal in Arizona copper mine case
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected Apache’s appeal in a legal dispute tied to an Arizona copper mine. The ruling reduces Apache’s options to change the case outcome, which could delay or constrain mine-related activity and support short-term copper supply expectations, potentially lifting copper prices.

title: Supreme Court turns down Apaches' bid to block copper mine on sacred site
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected a challenge to stop transfer of Oak Flat, a sacred site in Arizona, to Resolution Copper. By leaving a lower-court ruling in place, the decision allows the copper mine project to proceed. The company plans panel-carving to extract the deposit.

title: Supreme Court spurns Native American religious claim over copper mine on sacred land
summary: A Supreme Court ruling rejected a Native American religious claim tied to a copper mine located on sacred land. By spurning the challenge, the decision likely removes a legal barrier to the project, improving expectations for copper supply and weighing on copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: US Supreme Court rejects Native American case against large copper mine
summary: The US Supreme Court rejected an Apache Stronghold bid to stop construction at Oak Flat, clearing a key legal path for Resolution Copper’s mine. The decision keeps lower-court approval in place for the land transfer, which could enable development of a major deposit, supporting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: EGA's Guinea unit hopes for talks as bauxite stockpile nears 2 million tonnes
summary: EGA’s Guinea unit faces a standoff with Guinea’s government after authorities suspended its bauxite exports and mining operations over refinery commitments. Bauxite stockpiles have neared 2 million tonnes at the port. EGA hopes talks resume to lift the measures, while Guinea reviews licence actions.

title: Supreme Court rejects plea to block copper mine on Arizona land sacred to Apache tribe
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected Apache Stronghold’s plea to block a land transfer that would allow Resolution Copper to proceed with the Oak Flat project in Arizona. The decision sustains approvals for mining a major copper deposit, reducing permitting uncertainty and supporting near-term expectations for copper supply.

title: Supreme Court refuses to hear Oak Flat case, clearing a roadblock for huge copper mine
summary: A Supreme Court decision to refuse hearing the Oak Flat case clears a key legal obstacle for a large copper mine. Removing the block improves expectations for copper output and supply continuity, which can lift near-term market sentiment and add upward pressure to copper prices.

title: Supreme Court clears way for massive copper mine on Apache sacred land
summary: A Supreme Court decision has cleared the way for a massive copper mine on Apache sacred land. By reducing legal barriers to development, the ruling improves expectations for higher copper supply over time, which can weigh on copper prices as markets adjust their near-term supply outlook.

title: Supreme Court clears way for copper mine on Apache sacred land
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear an Apache challenge to the planned Resolution Copper mine at Oak Flat in Arizona, leaving lower-court rulings intact. The decision allows the Forest Service to finalize environmental steps and transfer land, keeping project development on track for a major copper deposit.

title: Supreme Court rejects a plea to block a copper mine on land in Arizona sacred to Apaches
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected Apache challenges to halt the Oak Flat land transfer to Resolution Copper, enabling the development of a major Arizona copper mine. The company says the deposit could be among the world’s largest, with the Forest Service set to re-issue an environmental review, supporting project progress and copper supply expectations.

title: The Supreme Court rejects a plea to block a copper mine on land in Arizona that's sacred to Apaches | iNFOnews
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected an Apache request to block a land transfer for Resolution Copper’s Oak Flat project in Arizona. The decision keeps the path open for the company to mine what it says is a world-scale copper deposit. The ruling lowers legal uncertainty around supply, potentially weighing on copper prices.

title: Supreme Court refuses Apache plea to save Oak Flat from copper mining destruction
summary: The Supreme Court rejected Apache’s attempt to preserve Oak Flat, paving the way for the area’s destruction for copper mining. The decision removes a legal delay risk for the project and can lift expectations for future copper supply, which is typically bearish for near-term copper prices.

title: Harmony Gold to Acquire MAC Copper in $1.03 Billion Deal, Boosting Copper Exposure
summary: Harmony Gold announced an all-cash $1.03 billion acquisition of MAC Copper to increase its copper exposure. The CSA Copper Mine produced about 41,000 tonnes in 2024 with a long reserve life. The transaction involves contingent copper payments and debt/stream obligations but no immediate production change.

title: Rio Tinto copper mine boosted by US Supreme Court decision
summary: The US Supreme Court rejected a Native American group’s appeal blocking a federal land transfer needed for Rio Tinto’s Resolution Copper project in Arizona. The decision clears the way for the 2,422-acre Oak Flat mine site, reducing permitting risk and improving expectations for future copper supply, supporting copper prices.

title: Copper thieves are targeting air conditioning units in Oshawa, police say
summary: Durham police warn that copper thieves in Oshawa are targeting outdoor air conditioners and heat pumps, reporting 22 incidents this year involving copper piping and wiring. Similar copper line theft is reported in rural Nova Scotia affecting Bell Canada services. Officials say copper wire theft is rising but hard to curb.

title: Supreme Court rejects appeal from Apaches, to halt a copper mining project
summary: The Supreme Court rejected Apache Stronghold’s appeal to halt the land transfer for Resolution Copper’s Oak Flat project in Arizona. The ruling keeps lower-court approvals, allowing the U.S. to proceed with environmental review steps and support the start of a major copper mine.

title: Canadian aluminum trader blames its bankruptcy on trade war
summary: Canadian aluminum trader Sinobec filed for bankruptcy in the US and Canada, blaming Trump-era trade tariffs. The firm said sharply higher costs and halted supply-chain payments from American trade friction damaged receivables and prevented refinancing. It buys aluminum ingots and finished products from multiple countries, mainly serving North America.

title: Harmony makes $1.6bn play for leading copper mine
summary: Harmony Gold plans to acquire MAC Copper’s CSA mine in Australia for about $1.03bn ($1.6bn), paying a 32% premium to MAC’s prior NYSE VWAP. CSA produces roughly 41,000 tonnes of copper in 2024. The transaction is recommended by the board, pending approvals for Q4 2025 completion.

title: Supreme Court Declines to Take Up Challenge to Big Arizona Copper Project
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to review a challenge to Rio Tinto and BHP’s Resolution Copper project in Arizona. The decision clears an obstacle to the federal land transfer and environmental steps needed for the mine’s approval, potentially enabling supply that the companies say could reach up to a quarter of U.S. demand.

title: Supreme Court Declines to Take Up Challenge to Big Arizona Copper Project -- Update
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge to Rio Tinto and BHP’s Resolution Copper project in Arizona. The decision clears a legal obstacle to a federal land transfer and environmental review for Oak Flat. Supporters see it enabling potential large-scale U.S. copper supply, while opponents vow to continue legal efforts.

title: Canadian aluminum trader blames bankruptcy on tariffs
summary: Canadian aluminum trader Sinobec filed for bankruptcy, blaming U.S.-imposed tariffs on Chinese goods. The company says receivables collections stopped as its supply chain ground to a halt, and even reduced tariff rates remained above market absorption. Sinobec sources aluminum from multiple countries but sells mostly in North America.

title: Hindustan Copper Q4 Net Profit Rises 52% to ₹189 Crore
summary: Hindustan Copper Ltd’s Q4 FY25 net profit rose 51.8% year-on-year to ₹189.48 crore and net sales increased 38.9% to ₹3,923.6 crore, attributed to higher operational activity and better realization. The company is India’s vertically integrated copper producer, with mining and smelting/refining assets.

title: Harmony Gold Mining to buy MAC Copper for $1.03bn
summary: Harmony Gold agreed to buy MAC Copper, owner of Australia’s CSA underground copper mine, for $1.03bn, implying a sizeable premium. The mine is described as high-grade and producing about 41kt copper in 2024. Funding is via a bridge facility and cash, with completion expected in Dec 2025.

title: Jubilee Provides an Update on the Implementation of Its Copper Projects in Zambia
summary: Jubilee reports successful processing trials at its Roan concentrator in Zambia, confirming it can treat shallow transitional “waste” copper ores with ~65% copper yields. Based on results, it signed a long-term feedstock supply agreement for Roan, with production commencing this week, alongside mining and refinery delivery plans.

title: Supporting Nickel Downstream Industry in Indonesia,
summary: Indonesia’s Danantara Indonesia, INA, and Eramet signed an MoU to explore an investment platform for nickel, targeting an integrated EV battery raw-materials ecosystem from upstream to downstream. The parties will conduct preliminary assessments and prepare a collaboration roadmap, with Eramet contributing technical expertise and financing structures.

title: Discovery of the largest gold, silver and copper deposit of the millennium: more than $337 billion
summary: Lundin Mining and BHP’s Vicuña joint venture announced a major greenfield discovery at the Filo del Sol project in Argentina, estimating at least 13 million tons of copper plus sizable gold and silver resources, with expansion potential. While environmental concerns exist, the headline primarily supports copper supply expectations.

title: Copper rises on signs of tighter nearby supply
summary: Copper prices rose as LME-registered warehouse stocks fell 43% since mid-February and the cash-to-three-month spread widened, signaling tighter nearby supply. Ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions kept copper in a tight range, while a potential U.S. copper tariff is under investigation.

title: WESTERN COPPER FORMALLY EXTENDS INVESTOR RIGHTS AGREEMENT WITH MITSUBISHI MATERIALS
summary: Western Copper and Gold said Mitsubishi Materials completed a precondition to extend their investor rights agreement after buying about 2 million shares to raise ownership to ~5%. The extension runs to May 30, 2026, supporting continued advancement of the Casino copper-gold project. No operational or production changes were announced.

title: Brixton Metals Commences Drilling at its Thorn Copper-Gold Project
summary: Brixton Metals says drilling has commenced at its Thorn project in Northwest British Columbia and plans to test new near-surface copper porphyry mineralization at the Catalyst target. The article cites quartz-chalcopyrite-molybdenite vein exposures and rock/soil assay results with up to 0.56% Cu, supporting a bullish copper sentiment impact.

title: Glenstar Minerals Inc.: Glenstar Completes Successful Initial Drill Program on Flagship Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Green Monster Property
summary: Glenstar Minerals reports completion of an initial reverse-circulation drill program on its Green Monster Ni-Cu-Cobalt property in Nevada under budget. Drilling found oxide and sulfide mineralization and dolomite veining hosting fine-grained sulfides across targets. Samples are being shipped for assay, with no new results released yet.

title: Glenstar Minerals Inc.: Glenstar Completes Successful Initial Drill Program on Flagship Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Green Monster Property
summary: Glenstar Minerals reports completion of its initial reverse-circulation drill program on the Green Monster property in Nevada. Drilling intersected oxide and sulfide mineralized sequences and dolomite veining with local sulfide mineralization, targeting nickel-copper and anomalous cobalt. Assay results from these new samples were not yet provided.

title: South32 receives ARENA grant to study steam electrification in alumina refining
summary: South32 received an A$4.4m ARENA grant to study partial steam electrification at its Worsley Alumina Refinery, aiming to reduce fossil-fuel steam use and greenhouse emissions. The announcement is focused on a pre-feasibility study and decarbonisation research, not immediate alumina output or cost changes.

title: US Supreme Court declines land swap challenge for Resolution Copper project
summary: The US Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge to the land swap underpinning Rio Tinto and BHP’s Resolution Copper project in Arizona. With the land transfer process continuing and a republished environmental report due in 60 days, the ruling lowers permitting risk for a major copper mine.

title: IGO pulls out of WA copper mining JV with Encounter Resources
summary: Encounter Resources has reacquired full control of the Yeneena copper-cobalt project in Western Australia after IGO exited the JV. Encounter will use accumulated exploration data and focus on reassessing the BM1 high-grade copper zone and follow-up drilling at BM5. The move supports future copper exploration but signals no immediate supply change.

title: EGA's Guinea unit hopes for talks as bauxite stockpile nears 2-million tonnes
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium’s Guinea unit has built nearly 2 million tonnes of bauxite after Guinean authorities suspended its mining and exports amid a dispute over downstream refinery commitments. The firm hopes to resume talks to lift blocking measures. Guinea says it will enforce contractual compliance and clean up mining.

title: Another Round of RKAB Approvals? Market Sentiment Around Nickel Remains Volatile
summary: Rumors that Indonesia may ease RKAB (mine quota) approvals have made nickel market sentiment volatile. Even so, ESDM officials reported no major supplemental quota approvals in two weeks, and Indonesian nickel ore prices remained firm. Weather disruptions and weak NPI economics cap upside for fire-grade ore, while hydromet demand improved after April outages.

title: North Dakota coal mine to become processing site for Minnesota nickel
summary: The headline says a North Dakota coal mine will become a processing site for Minnesota nickel. That suggests changes to nickel processing operations that could affect near-term supply and refining economics. The article text is largely missing, so the magnitude and timing of any nickel price impact are uncertain.

title: Nickel plant coming to former North Dakota coal mine
summary: A retired North Dakota coal mine is being repurposed into a nickel processing plant. The development suggests upcoming additional nickel processing capacity, which could gradually improve supply availability and weigh on nickel price expectations over the coming weeks, depending on commissioning timeline and throughput.

title: North Dakota Coal Mine to Become Processing Site for Minnesota Nickel
summary: North Dakota’s Beulah will host a processing facility operated by Talon Metals to process Minnesota-mined nickel ore, shipped by rail to the site. Tesla is contracted to buy roughly half the processed nickel, with Defense Department use also expected. The project supports U.S. critical-mineral sourcing away from China.

title: Eramet, Danantara agree to explore nickel supply chain projects - Companies
summary: Eramet and Indonesia’s Danantara/Indonesia Investment Authority signed an MoU to explore investments across the nickel supply chain, from upstream mining to downstream processing for EV battery materials. The deal, framed as part of a broader France-Indonesia economic push, centers on Indonesia’s large nickel reserves and production potential.

title: Lifezone Metals Announces Filing Dates for Kabanga Nickel Project Technical Report Summaries
summary: Lifezone Metals announced filing dates for technical report summaries for the Kabanga Nickel Project in Tanzania, including an Initial Assessment filing before market open June 2 and a Feasibility Study in July. The studies cover staged development and hydrometallurgical refinery plans, including the project’s first mineral reserves disclosure.

title: Sterling Metals Corp.: Sterling Metals Intersects 359.3m of 0.36% CuEq from Near Surface with Multiple Zones of Bornite Across Preserved Porphyry Copper Deposit in its First Drill Hole at the Newly Renamed Soo Copper Project
summary: Sterling Metals announced first-hole drilling results at its Soo Copper Project, intersecting a long near-surface bornite/chalcopyrite copper zone with meaningful CuEq grades across hundreds of meters. The company frames the find as a preserved porphyry copper system open at depth. Assays for remaining holes are pending; no production timeline is provided.

title: "Supreme Court Rejects Bid To Stop Arizona Copper Mine"
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected a bid by members of the San Carlos Apache Tribe to stop construction of the Oak Flat copper mine in Arizona. The decision keeps the project on track, lowering the chance of near-term supply disruption and modestly supporting expectations for future copper availability.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc and Freeport Are Planning a Significant 2025 Drill Program in Their Joy District, Including at the High Grade Copper-Gold-Silver Aurora Discovery
summary: Amarc Resources and Freeport plan a 2025 drill program in British Columbia’s JOY District targeting high-grade porphyry Cu-Au-Ag at the AuRORA discovery, plus Twins, Canyon, PINE and other Cu-Au targets. Freeport will fund work under an earn-in agreement, potentially boosting near-term copper upside expectations.

title: Insufficient downstream inventory stocking before the holiday, weak demand support for secondary aluminum alloy[Weekly Review of Secondary Aluminum Market]
summary: Weekly review shows secondary aluminum alloy prices (ADC12) easing while demand remains weak as holiday-related inventory stocking is limited. Social inventory of secondary ingots rose sharply and shipping pressure increased, but aluminum scrap supply is tight and cost support persists. Outlook is rangebound with upside capped by orders.

title: Import Window Closed, Net Imports of Aluminum Hit New High in April [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM cites customs data showing April 2025 net primary aluminium imports rose to about 236,800 mt, with net imports at a new high, and expects May inflows to remain elevated. It attributes this to loss-making overseas supply, weak demand, destocking, and increased processors’ willingness to take manual processing orders.

title: Nickel and Copper minerals processing facility announced for Beulah
summary: Talon Metals, owner of a taconite mine in Minnesota, plans to build the Beulah Minerals Processing Facility in North Dakota with Westmoreland Coal. The plant is designed to process nickel and copper minerals, using local energy and fly ash byproducts. Start is planned for 2027, with operations by 2029.

title: Nickel and Copper minerals processing facility announced for Beulah
summary: Talon Metals plans to build the Beulah Minerals Processing Facility on a former coal site in North Dakota, partnering with Westmoreland Coal. The project is described as advanced processing for nickel and copper minerals, using energy, rail transport, and coal fly ash. Construction is targeted for 2027, startup 2029.

title: Copper thefts could cause outages, price hikes for Farmers RECC members
summary: Farmers RECC in Kentucky says repeated copper thefts from utility poles could cause outages and force extra repairs, including restoring removed copper wire grounds. The cooperative urges residents to report suspicious activity. Replacement and remediation demand for copper can support short-term copper price expectations, though impact magnitude is uncertain.

title: Copper thefts threaten safety and power reliability in rural Kentucky
summary: Farmers RECC in Kentucky reports copper wire thefts from utility poles, with incidents tied to copper’s rising scrap value. Officials say stolen grounding conductors increase safety and reliability risks and can delay storm restoration. The story is locally supply/demand related but not a clear market-wide copper price driver.

title: Examining Alcoa's proposed bauxite mining expansion in WA's jarrah forests
summary: Alcoa is seeking approvals to expand its bauxite mining and alumina production in Western Australia near Perth’s water catchments, prompting environmental and drinking-water contamination concerns. The WA EPA is taking public submissions on multiple mine proposals. If regulatory outcomes delay capacity, aluminium supply expectations could worsen.

title: Casting Ingot Production in North China Declined Significantly in May, While Proportion of Liquid Aluminum Rose Sharply [SMM Data]
summary: SMM data show May 2025 aluminum casting ingot production fell 6.15% YoY to about 913,000 mt as smelters in north China increased the share of liquid aluminum to 75.5% (+1.48 pp MoM). Operating rates stayed stable, but the shift may reduce ingot arrivals into mainstream demand areas.

title: Outlook for Shanghai Spot Copper in June
summary: Shanghai spot copper premiums rose then fell as elevated futures prices weakened downstream buying and arbitrageurs/speculators closed positions. Month-end inflows from cancelled LME warrants and bonded imports reduced premiums to ~100 yuan/mt. June is expected to face further warrant cancellations and weak demand, limiting any premium recovery.

title: Manufacturing - Analysis: UAE largely shielded from US tariffs on steel and aluminium
summary: A Betterhomes report says the UAE is largely shielded from Trump-era US tariffs’ impact on its industries. It cites 350,000 tonnes of UAE aluminium exports to the US in 2024 and notes potential trade talks and Dubai’s transshipment capacity, implying limited immediate downside for aluminium pricing.

title: Exclusive-Miner Vale misses deadline for power to expand Brazil nickel complex
summary: Brazil’s ONS denied Vale’s request to increase power supply to its northern Onca Puma nickel complex after Vale missed a deadline to contract additional electricity. The second furnace for the $555 million expansion is still targeted for the second half of 2025, but approval uncertainty raises near-term nickel supply/ramp risks.

title: Trigon to Sell 80% Stake in Namibia Copper Mine for $24mln
summary: Trigon agreed to sell an 80% stake in Namibia’s Kombat copper mine to Horizon for $24 million, pending shareholder approval on June 11. Kombat remains suspended since January 2025 due to underground mine issues. Trigon plans to use proceeds to fund further copper exploration projects.

title: Panama says First Quantum copper mine maintenance plan is not a restart
summary: Panama approved First Quantum’s maintenance plan for its copper mine, while clarifying it is not a restart after the operation was shut following protests. By keeping the site closed, the decision likely sustains or worsens near-term supply expectations for copper, weighing on prices in the coming days.

title: Panama Sets New Path for Shelved Copper Mine
summary: Panama approved a maintenance plan for First Quantum Minerals’ inactive copper mine to ensure environmental safety after its 2023 shutdown. The mine remains closed, but First Quantum will manage the site under Environment Ministry oversight, while discussions continue and talks resumed after arbitration suspension in March. Resumption is estimated in three to six months.

title: Panama Government to Implement the Donoso Copper Mine Preservation Plan
summary: Panama’s MICI approved Cobre Panamá’s Donoso copper mine preservation and safe management plan after a Supreme Court ruling suspended mining. Authorities stressed it is maintenance only, not reactivation, to prevent environmental damage while deciding the mine’s future. The decision addresses upkeep of power, port and tanks without restarting production.

title: Commerce Department Considers Applying Section 232 Duties on Steel and Aluminum to More Construction Materials | Cozen O'Connor
summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce’s BIS is seeking public comment on adding more construction-related materials into the scope of existing 25% Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs. If inclusions are approved, additional aluminum imports could face higher costs, affecting construction demand and input procurement. Comments are due June 4, 2025.

title: In May, the surplus pattern of bauxite continued, with inventory buildup of bauxite both in alumina refineries and ports.
summary: SMM reports China’s bauxite output rose in May and inventories increased at alumina refineries and nine ports, showing a continuing surplus. While refineries’ operating capacity may rebound in June and demand could rise, imported bauxite supply remains high, so bauxite inventories are expected to keep building in the near term.

title: Harmony's $1bn (R18bn) copper deal a 'sweet spot' for the company
summary: Harmony Gold agreed to buy Australia’s Mac Copper for about $1bn, adding the CSA Copper mine producing ~40,000 tonnes of copper annually from day one. The company frames the deal as enhancing profitability and reducing risk. It may affect Harmony’s output mix, but no broad market supply disruption is indicated.

title: Trump says he will double tariffs on steel and aluminum imports to 50 per cent
summary: Trump said U.S. tariffs on aluminum imports will be doubled to 50% next Wednesday, after raising steel duties. The move follows earlier Section 232 tariffs and has already lifted steel product prices. Canada and industry groups warn of market disruption and retaliatory steps, but near-term import costs should rise for aluminum.

title: Trump says will double steel, aluminum tariffs to 50%
summary: Trump said he would double steel and aluminum tariffs to 50%. Higher tariffs can disrupt aluminum trade flows by raising delivered costs and changing demand for imports, which typically pressures short-term aluminum pricing expectations as markets reassess supply availability and purchase incentives.

title: Trump says he will double steel and aluminum tariffs to 50 per cent
summary: Trump says the U.S. will double steel and aluminum import tariffs to 50% starting next Wednesday. The piece notes prior tariff hikes pushed steel product prices up about 16% and references economic estimates of job and cost impacts. Aluminium supply costs are likely to rise quickly; copper influence is indirect.

title: Trump accuses China of violating trade deal, doubles steel and aluminum tariffs
summary: Trump accused China of violating a tariff rollback deal and ordered a doubling of worldwide steel and aluminum tariffs to 50% in the U.S., effective next week. The move renews trade-war risk with China, and signals slow progress on critical-minerals export licenses, pressuring aluminium sentiment and copper demand outlook.

title: Trump says he plans to double steel, aluminum tariffs to 50%
summary: Trump says he plans to raise U.S. import tariffs on steel and aluminum to 50% from 25% under Section 232, effective Wednesday. Markets expect higher domestic prices and benefits for some producers, while trading partners warn of retaliation and higher costs for consumers.

title: US to double tariffs on steel and aluminium imports to 50%, Trump says
summary: The US will double tariffs on steel and aluminium imports from 25% to 50% starting Wednesday. The move is intended to boost domestic production and reduce reliance on China.
