Canada supplies about half of U.S. aluminium imports, raising concerns for near-term aluminium trade and pricing.

title: No Violation Found in PT GAG Nickel's Raja Ampat Mine, Says Energy Ministry
summary: Indonesia’s Energy Ministry said a recent site visit found no violations at PT GAG Nikel’s nickel mine on Gag Island, with limited sedimentation observed and reclamation judged “pretty good.” Inspectors will conduct a deeper review after an earlier suspension tied to environmental concerns. This lowers near-term disruption risk.

title: Tougher penalties for copper wire theft passed by Nevada legislature
summary: Nevada lawmakers have passed tougher penalties for copper wire theft. By discouraging theft and diversion into scrap markets, the measure is expected to improve the availability of copper for legitimate supply chains, potentially weighing on nearby copper prices modestly as theft-related supply tightness eases.

title: China's copper boom under threat as miners test bargaining power
summary: China’s rapid smelting capacity expansion has pushed copper treatment charges deeply negative, with spot minus-$60/t and even proposed negative terms for contracted supplies. Smelter economics are deteriorating, prompting shutdown talk and past closures, while China’s state-backed output remains resilient, reshaping global ore and refined-copper expectations.

title: Raja Ampat's nickel paradox: When green ambitions threaten blue paradise - Academia
summary: The piece warns that Indonesia’s expanding nickel mining in Raja Ampat—cited as necessary for the green transition—has cleared forests and coastal areas and threatens coral ecosystems. Multiple companies are under investigation for environmental permit violations and improper waste handling, raising the risk of enforcement or operational disruption and supply uncertainty for nickel.

title: CopperString investment boosts Queensland growth | The North West Star
summary: Queensland’s Treasurer announced a record A$2.4bn state investment to advance the CopperString transmission project, including $225m for the Hughenden Hub and procurement of transformers, lines, and tower steel along the eastern link. Local leaders want faster rollout, but overall the spending supports anticipated demand for electrical conductor metals.

title: Indonesian nickel ore prices rise on tight supply
summary: Indonesia’s tighter domestic nickel ore supply has pushed up in-country nickel ore prices and premiums, with rainy weather disrupting Sulawesi operations and the government ordering Antam to suspend mining in a protected area. Ore buyers are seeking more imported supply. Downstream NPI and stainless prices fell, but upstream tightness is bullish for nickel.

title: Calls grow for nickel mining in Raja Ampat to end permanently - Archipelago
summary: Lawmakers and celebrities, backed by environmentalists, are urging Indonesia to permanently end nickel mining on Gag Island in Raja Ampat. The push follows outcry and Greenpeace Indonesia videos alleging environmental damage. Officials are calling for a moratorium or permanent ban and permit revocations, raising near-term nickel supply risk.

title: Exclusive—Ken Blackwell: Selling Out Religious Freedom to Give Copper to China
summary: The article argues that the Supreme Court’s decision allows the Oak Flat land transfer to Resolution Copper, a mining project described as tied to Chinese Communist Party-linked ownership through Rio Tinto and Chinalco. It contends the deal will enable extraction of copper that could ultimately be controlled by Beijing.

title: Northern Dynasty Minerals Ltd. (NAK): A Bull Case Theory
summary: The piece presents a bullish thesis for Northern Dynasty Minerals’ Pebble project, citing Trump-era executive orders prioritizing domestic critical minerals, including copper, and faster permitting. It also claims a growing copper supply deficit. Overall, it frames improved prospects for copper supply as supportive for prices.

title: INDONESIA Indonesia halts nickel mining in Raja Ampat because the environmental risk is too high
summary: Indonesia’s energy minister ordered a temporary suspension of nickel mining in Raja Ampat, after inspections found serious environmental-law violations and protesters raised concerns about ecosystem damage. The halt applies pending field verification of PT Gag and relates to multiple mining sites on small islands, potentially tightening near-term nickel supply.

title: How rising steel and aluminum tariffs are affecting a longstanding Salem manufacturer
summary: The Trump administration doubled tariffs on imported steel and aluminum from 25% to 50%, raising the cost of foreign-sourced inputs for the Damon Company. The firm reports increased spending on aluminum and steel and delays/derails export deals, contributing to uncertainty and potential pricing pressure for metal-intensive manufacturers.

title: Terra Metals Inc. and Lunda Resources Confirm 96.5% Copper
summary: Terra Metals and Lunda Resources report a metallurgical breakthrough at Zambia’s Kalaba Copper Project, with independent testing confirming 96.5% cumulative copper recovery and high concentrate grades. The result is enabled by new flotation chemistry addressing high talc content, improving leaching economics and supporting future copper output plans.

title: Attorneys get more time to argue over contested copper mine on land sacred to Apaches
summary: A U.S. judge denied a halt to the federal land exchange for the Oak Flat copper project but barred the Forest Service from proceeding for 60 days pending an environmental review. Native American and environmental groups seek to stop the transfer, while Resolution Cooper says the project complies and has local support.

title: Canada Fights Back: Aluminum Tariff Could Spark Supply Shock
summary: The U.S. Trump administration imposed a 50% tariff on aluminium, targeting Canadian supply. Canada’s Aluminium Association argues the tariff will make U.S. exports unviable, suppress demand across North America, disrupt defense and construction, and force redirection toward the EU, raising uncertainty for near-term aluminium trade and prices.

title: Copper wire theft continues to leave residents in the dark
summary: Bakersfield and California officials say copper wire theft is still causing damage and repair costs. The city has replaced numerous utility fixtures and is shifting some wiring to aluminium to deter theft. State and law-enforcement efforts highlight ongoing scrap-driven theft, supporting sustained copper scrap demand.

title: Possible rural copper network phase-out a concern for remote NZ communities
summary: RNZ reports concerns in remote New Zealand communities if Chorus phases out its copper broadband network and replaces it with fibre. The Commerce Commission has closed submissions on draft recommendations to deregulate the rural copper network. The prospect of copper substitution points to weaker copper demand expectations near term.

title: BLM seeks input on revived Antler copper mine proposal near Yucca
summary: BLM is seeking public comment on a proposal by Antler Operations Inc. to redevelop the historic Antler copper deposit near Yucca. The plan would build a new underground mine and related support facilities, including a powerline, with most work on private land and a small portion on public land.

title: New Tariffs Shake Up Steel and Aluminum Markets, Local Industry Responds
summary: A 50% tariff on imported steel and aluminum begins this week, replacing a prior 25% rate. Louisiana manufacturers say aluminum is their main input and costs are rising. The article cites a ~30% aluminum price increase from March to early June, inventory restocking effects, and expectations of higher prices for weeks.

title: Copper thefts rise in West Texas amid heatwave
summary: Copper thefts are rising in West Texas amid a heatwave, increasing losses of physical copper and tightening local availability of copper scrap/materials. That potential near-term supply disruption could lift expectations for copper prices over coming days as buyers compete for limited inventory.

title: Pathfinder Tonopah Receives Letter of Interest From U.S. EXIM Bank for $896 Million Financing to Advance Domestic Copper Mine
summary: Pathfinder Tonopah said the U.S. EXIM Bank sent a non-binding indicative Letter of Interest for $896 million to finance development of its Nevada copper (and molybdenum) mine. The funding proposal would accelerate construction of processing facilities, improving the investment and supply outlook for copper in the U.S. timeline.

title: Australia's biggest aluminium smelter on verge of collapse
summary: Australia’s Tomago aluminium smelter is in emergency talks with federal and state governments after crippling electricity bills threaten operations and up to 6,000 jobs. As a major domestic aluminium producer, potential output loss raises short-term supply concerns. The news follows Trump doubling tariffs on Australian aluminium to 50%.

title: Cascadia to acquire Granite Creek Copper, enhancing copper-gold exploration in Yukon
summary: Cascadia Minerals agreed to acquire Granite Creek Copper to expand its copper-gold exploration portfolio, combining the Carmacks Project in Yukon with additional projects. The deal includes a premium share exchange, a C$2.5m cash position, and a private placement/bridge loan to fund near-term drilling, subject to approvals.

title: International Wire Group Acquires Hussey Copper
summary: International Wire Group agreed to purchase Hussey Copper, a U.S. copper products supplier of busbars and electrical components. The deal aims to expand presence in electrical infrastructure, data centers, power generation, EVs and renewables, with closing expected in Q3 subject to approvals. Impact on near-term copper prices appears limited.

title: Indonesia aims to boost downstream investment in high-value copper sector-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia’s ministry is working to attract more downstream investment in the high-value copper sector. The country already produces copper cathodes and plans to expand into derivative products such as copper foil and slabs. Incentives include tax holidays and allowances, aiming to move beyond limited tier-one processing.

title: Indonesia revokes mining permits of 4 nickel firms over environmental violations-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia revoked mining permits of four nickel mining firms in Raja Ampat, Papua, citing environmental regulation breaches and violations related to protected geopark areas. The minister said one company (PT GAG) remains unaffected due to its distance from the geopark and compliance planning, but others face permit loss.

title: Star Copper Corp.: Star Copper Commences Drill Campaign in BC's Golden Triangle
summary: Star Copper Corp. begins an upsized 2025 drill program at its Star Project in British Columbia’s Golden Triangle, targeting expansion of a near-surface oxide zone and deeper porphyry copper-gold mineralization. The program covers ~4,000 meters across six holes to test modeled magnetic/chargeability anomalies and fault-controlled structures.

title: Ausenco to conduct initial study at Whistler gold-copper project in Alaska
summary: Ausenco was selected to run a preliminary economic assessment for U.S. GoldMining’s Whistler gold-copper project in Alaska, including updated resources and metallurgical testing. The study targets an open-pit mine and processing facility, but no near-term production or supply disruption is indicated, limiting immediate copper price impact.

title: Govt stops short of halting all nickel mining in Raja Ampat - Companies
summary: Indonesia’s government revoked mining business licenses for four nickel operations in Raja Ampat (Southwest Papua) but allowed PT Gag Nikel to keep its permit. The move follows environmental concerns and regulatory violations, and comes before RKAB approvals are obtained for mining activities.

title: Indonesia stops nickel mining operations at top tourist diving destination
summary: Indonesia suspended four nickel mining operations in Raja Ampat after an environmental investigation found permit violations. The companies had not started due to missing work-plan approval, while one remaining operator (Gag Nikel) continues outside the geopark. The move raises near-term concerns about nickel supply from Indonesia.

title: Copper slips on uncertainty over trade talks, demand
summary: Copper prices fell as investors avoided the market amid uncertainty over U.S.-China trade talks and the trade war’s impact on demand. LME three-month copper was down 0.3%. Comex futures dropped too, while LME stocks continued to fall, and aluminium and nickel also eased.

title: Copper market shows tariffs put traders and businesses in a bind
summary: CNBC reports that copper is being pulled by tariff uncertainty: U.S. companies may “front-load” purchases ahead of potential new levies, while LME inventories deplete quickly as copper is drawn to the U.S., lifting prices. Offsetting factors include weakening China signals, continued exports, and possible slower solar/U.S. demand.

title: Mount Isa copper smelter's planned closure prompts fears production will move overseas
summary: Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter faces potential earlier closure if government support isn’t secured, with experts warning Australian copper processing could shift offshore. Queensland officials cite sovereign risk and ongoing efforts to fund continued operations. Replacement capacity would be costly and slow, raising concerns about near-term refining tightness.

title: Indonesia Revokes Nickel Ore Mining Permits in Raja Ampat After Protest
summary: Indonesia’s energy minister said the government revoked nickel ore mining permits for four firms in Raja Ampat, Papua, after environmental concerns triggered public protests. The decision risks cutting near-term nickel ore supply from a major producing country, which can support nickel prices over the next days to weeks.

title: Choking hazard: How North Maluku nickel industry suffocates local villagers - Environment
summary: A Jakarta Post report says nickel mining and processing at PT Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park (IWIP) near Gemaf village in North Maluku causes persistent health problems, with dust and ash blamed on the plant and its coal-fired power units. The social and regulatory risk could pressure nickel operations.

title: Commodities: Copper nears its annual high
summary: Copper prices are edging toward an annual high, boosted by revived US-China trade dialogue and expectations for improved growth, while LME stocks are falling. The piece also links the move to tariff-related uncertainty following a trade truce, implying near-term demand/supply tightness supportive of copper.

title: Pathfinder receives $896m LOI from US EXIM to develop copper mine
summary: Pathfinder Tonopah said the US EXIM Bank issued a non-binding $896m letter of interest to help finance development of its Tonopah, Nevada copper mine. The support is aimed at strengthening domestic critical-minerals supply chains. The plan includes modern processing to produce copper cathode and molybdenum concentrate, but LOI is not final.

title: Minister dismisses claim Jokowi involved in Raja Ampat nickel mining - Economy
summary: Indonesia’s energy minister denied claims that former President Joko Widodo and his wife were involved in nickel mining in Raja Ampat and said permits were not issued by the former administration. The episode followed viral allegations of nickel-ore shipping tied to vessel names resembling Jokowi’s initials.

title: President Trump Increases Steel And Aluminum Tariffs To 50%
summary: Trump’s June 4, 2025 proclamation doubles Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum (and covered derivatives) from 25% to 50%, tightening US import economics and potentially boosting near-term aluminium prices. It also clarifies tariff treatment rules and stacking priority versus IEEPA tariffs, with refunds for some retroactive overpayments.

title: CBAM is coming – can steel and aluminium supply chains bear the costs?
summary: The article argues the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism will start generating liabilities within months and impose large compliance costs on importers of carbon-intensive goods, with aluminium facing meaningful added costs. It emphasizes certificate-price and policy-design uncertainty, which is already dampening forward contracting and could pressure prices via cost pass-through and demand shifts.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Initial Resource at Mann West Nickel Sulphide Project
summary: Canada Nickel reported an initial resource estimate for its Mann West nickel sulphide project near Timmins, Ontario, including indicated and inferred nickel tonnes plus palladium/platinum resources. The company framed Mann West as a larger resource and part of multiple new nickel resource updates expected in 2025, boosting nickel supply expectations.

title: Zeus North to acquire 90% interest in copper-gold properties in Nevada
summary: Zeus North America Mining plans to acquire a 90% stake in Nevada’s Delker and Bulls Eye copper-gold properties from Nedeel, with milestone-based cash/share payments and JV arrangements. The move targets future resource definition and drilling, with no immediate production impact cited, limiting short-term copper price effects.

title: Thieves target Niagara hydro utilities for copper: NRP
summary: Niagara Regional Police said thieves broke into electricity distributor yards in St. Catharines and Thorold to steal copper sold to scrap. Police announced arrests and multiple related charges tied to incidents reported in February and March. The report is copper-specific but the volume appears limited and local.

title: 232 Duty Increase Updates | Steel and Aluminum Tariffs - Impact and Timeline of President Trump's Proclamation | Benesch
summary: The article summarizes Trump administration Section 232 actions raising U.S. tariffs on imported aluminum from 25% to 50% effective June 4, 2025, with reduced exemptions and more aggressive CBP enforcement against misclassification. The expanded scope and higher landed costs are expected to tighten aluminum supply for U.S. buyers and support prices.

title: Uncertainty Dominates Copper Market Outlook
summary: The piece says copper prices have been stable in early June after prior tariff-driven volatility. It highlights ongoing U.S.-China and wider U.S. trade negotiations, with unresolved potential copper tariffs affecting Comex-LME premiums and U.S. inventories. It notes strong demand but rising Comex stocks could pressure prices.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | Newcastle Herald
summary: Newly appointed NSW industry minister Tim Ayres said governments must support the energy-intensive Tomago Aluminium smelter as rising power costs threaten viability. Reports say Tomago is in talks for billions in support, including production tax credits and electricity contract terms for 2026-2029, to keep output competitive.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Tomago Aluminium says rising electricity costs threaten its viability and reports it is seeking billions in NSW and federal support, including electricity-contract and production tax-credit design for 2026-2029. The government has already pledged $2 billion in credits to keep local aluminium production competitive globally.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | Muswellbrook Chronicle
summary: Tomago Aluminium says its future is threatened by high electricity prices and is seeking billions in state and federal support to manage energy-transition costs, including help for 2026–2029 power contracts and production tax credits. The government has already pledged $2bn credit support for Australian smelters.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | The Macleay Argus
summary: Australia’s Tim Ayres discusses measures to keep Tomago Aluminium viable as energy transition costs and high electricity prices threaten operations. Reports say NSW and federal support and production tax credits are being considered to manage 2026–2029 power contracts, supporting continuity of aluminium supply.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | The Scone Advocate
summary: Tomago Aluminium is seeking billions of dollars in NSW and federal support to manage rising electricity costs and secure its 2026–2029 power contract. The smelter produces about 600,000 tonnes annually and warned high energy prices threaten operations. Governments are offering production tax credits to keep aluminium competitive.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Australia’s Tomago Aluminium is seeking billions in state and federal support to manage rising electricity costs amid the clean energy transition. The smelter produces about 600,000 tonnes of aluminium and warned high power prices threaten operations. Officials reference large production tax credits aimed at keeping output competitive globally.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | The Advertiser - Cessnock
summary: NSW industry minister Tim Ayres says he is optimistic about Tomago Aluminium’s viability as the smelter seeks billions in government support to manage rising electricity costs. The plant produces 600,000 tonnes annually and is power-intensive. Talks focus on its 2026-2029 power contract and production tax credits design.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | The Maitland Mercury
summary: Tomago Aluminium is seeking billions in NSW and federal support to manage rising electricity costs amid the clean energy transition. The smelter’s high power needs make it vulnerable to energy pricing. The government has already pledged $2bn in production tax credits for aluminium smelters to keep local output competitive globally.

title: US copper group seeks tariffs, export ban | Latest Market News
summary: A US copper trade group filed with the Bureau of Industry and Security asking for tariffs on imported semi-fabricated copper and copper alloys, while exempting certain feedstocks like copper cathodes and scrap. It also seeks a ban on US copper scrap exports to limit supply access by China and others.

title: Tomago Aluminium seeks support amid energy transition costs | The Singleton Argus
summary: Tomago Aluminium is seeking billions in state and federal support to manage rising electricity costs that threaten smelter viability. The government has already pledged production tax credits for Australian aluminium smelters to keep local output competitive during the clean energy transition. The focus is on electricity contracts and credit design.

title: Hot Chili taps into seawater to unlock copper-rich north Chile
summary: Hot Chili says its Huasco Water project—building pipelines and modular seawater/desalination capacity—could solve water shortages for its Costa Fuego copper project and other mining users in Chile’s Atacama region. A signed MoU and positive feasibility economics support expectations for future copper output growth.

title: Apache lament loss of sacred Oak Flat site as Resolution Copper mine nears reality
summary: A federal judge denied an effort to temporarily block the land transfer for the Resolution Copper project at Oak Flat in Arizona, granting opponents only a 60-day wait after the final environmental impact statement. The mine targets a massive copper resource, but the delay tempers any immediate supply-price shock.

title: Chris Minns confirms majority Rio Tinto-owned Tomago aluminium smelter seeks federal and NSW bailout
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns says governments are discussing an “effective intervention” to prevent closure of Rio Tinto-owned Tomago, citing crippling power bills and a requested bailout potentially costing billions. The talks signal efforts to protect aluminium supply, offering near-term support for aluminium prices despite cost pressure.

title: Hindustan Copper to inject ₹2,000 Crore over 5-6 years
summary: Hindustan Copper said it will invest about ₹2,000 crore over the next 5–6 years to expand capacity to 12.20 MTPA by FY31 and pursue acquisition of new copper deposits. It also collaborates with CODELCO on mining and beneficiation. The update signals higher future copper supply expectations.

title: GIADEC to unlock the full potential of Ghana's bauxite: A New Era for the Integrated Aluminium Industry
summary: GIADEC received six mining leases to develop Ghana’s bauxite into alumina and aluminium, with plans to feed VALCO and expand capacity. It also discusses refinery/smelter partnerships, port and rail infrastructure, and potential modernization. The news supports bullish sentiment for aluminium by signaling progress toward integrated supply growth.

title: Philippines axes planned ban on nickel ore exports
summary: The Philippines dropped a planned ban on exporting unprocessed nickel ore, reversing a Senate-approved measure aimed at promoting domestic processing by 2030. Philippine ore exports rose in 2024, and dynamics in China/Indonesia are mixed, but the policy change supports continued ore supply and may weigh on nickel prices.

title: GT Resources Inc.: GT Resources - Copper - Palladium - Platinum (PGE) Project Updates
summary: GT Resources provides exploration updates for its North Rock (Canada) and LK (Finland) copper–PGE–nickel projects, including BHEM survey results and discussion of historic and 2022 resource figures (notably large contained copper and nickel). The news is exploration-oriented with no immediate supply or demand change, limiting price impact.

title: Northstar Gold Corp.: Northstar Reports High-Grade Copper Exploration Target at Cam Copper Mine
summary: Northstar Gold reported a high-grade exploration target at its Cam Copper No. 2 Zone, projecting 75,000–140,000 tonnes grading 9–18% copper, and said Novamera is incorporating results into a proposed development/surgical mining evaluation study. The company also notes the figures are conceptual pending further work.

title: Steel and aluminum tariffs add eight to 12 per cent to bottomline
summary: Canadian contractors report delays and higher bids after Trump doubled steel and aluminum tariffs to 50% and added further hikes. Firms cite rising end costs (about 8–12%) and inability to lock prices amid tariff changes. Reduced construction activity and postponed projects may curb near-term demand, weighing on aluminum prices.

title: American Pacific Mining Corp.: American Pacific Completes Phase I Drill Program at Madison Copper-Gold Project in Montana
summary: American Pacific Mining said its Phase I 2025 reverse-circulation drilling at the Madison copper-gold project in Montana is complete. Eight holes totaling 1,795 meters targeted porphyry and skarn zones, with assay results expected in July. No production changes or copper price-affecting decisions were announced.

title: Copper-nickel mining: Trump administration moves to lift mining restrictions near Boundary Waters in Minnesota
summary: The Trump administration announced it will lift Biden-era restrictions on copper-nickel mining near Minnesota’s Boundary Waters, advancing the Twin Metals Minnesota project. The decision reverses a 20-year mineral withdrawal/moratorium upstream of the proposed mine site, improving prospects for additional domestic copper and nickel supply.

title: Copper-nickel mining: Trump administration moves to lift mining restrictions near Boundary Waters in Minnesota
summary: The Trump administration moved to lift Biden-era restrictions on copper-nickel mining near Minnesota’s Boundary Waters, reinstating/accelerating leases for the proposed Twin Metals Minnesota project. Supporters cite environmental safeguards and domestic critical-minerals supply; critics warn of acid drainage and plan legal challenges.

title: Material Matters: Oil, Gold, Copper, And More
summary: RBC highlights copper’s strong YTD performance near $4.37/lb, attributing price support to US-bound inflows ahead of a potential copper tariff and tightening conditions as demand and supply weaken. Supply disruption from Ivanhoe’s Kamoa-Kakula outage and reduced Chile 2025 growth estimates raise the odds of a deficit in H2 2025.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns confirms talks to save Australia's biggest aluminium producer Tomago amid crippling power bills
summary: NSW confirms talks to keep Rio Tinto-owned Tomago operating as crippling electricity costs and limited renewable availability threaten its viability. Tomago uses 10% of NSW power and produces 37% of Australia’s primary aluminium. Aid and tax-credit discussions aim to prevent collapse, implying tighter aluminium supply.

title: LME intervenes as Mercuria's massive aluminium June position sparks supply concerns
summary: The LME ordered Mercuria to loan out part of its outsized June aluminium position because it exceeded available LME warehouse (on-warrant) supply, raising delivery-squeeze concerns. The move aims to prevent a corner or disorder in monthly aluminium contracts, easing immediate June delivery risk.

title: Donald Trump's 50% tariff: A boon or blow for US aluminium companies?
summary: The article says the US raised aluminium import tariffs to 50%, which US producers expect to tighten supply and lift prices, with LME aluminium and US Midwest premiums already surging. It also notes scrap imports are tariff-exempt, potentially adding cheaper supply and dampening demand.

title: IFC and World Bank back $700 million loan to Pakistan's Reko Diq copper‑gold venture
summary: IFC and the World Bank approved a concessional $700 million loan for Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan. The deal is expected to unlock additional private investment and includes revised throughput and higher phase-one costs. Production is slated for 2028, implying limited immediate output impact.

title: 232 Duty Increase Updates | Steel And Aluminum Tariffs – Impact And Timeline Of President Trump's Proclamation
summary: The article outlines strengthened U.S. Section 232 steel and aluminum tariff actions, including a June 4, 2025 increase in the aluminum tariff rate from 25% to 50% for subject imports, with fewer exclusions and stricter CBP enforcement. It also notes effective dates and derivative product scope expansion.

title: Feds expected to release final review of a plan to open Oak Flat site to copper mining
summary: The article headline says U.S. authorities are expected to publish the final review of a plan to open the Oak Flat site to copper mining. If the review clears the way for development, it would likely lift expected copper supply over the coming weeks, putting downward pressure on copper prices.

title: DRC's Kamoa-Kakula copper smelter to launch in September, Ivanhoe confirms
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said the Kamoa-Kakula copper smelter in DR Congo will start operations in September 2025, with first anode production in October, at 50% capacity initially. The project adds 500,000 t/year processing capacity, backed by additional power, despite a lower 2025 mine output forecast after a seismic event.

title: IFC to provide $400 million loan for Pakistan's copper-gold Reko Diq mine
summary: IFC will provide a $400 million subordinated loan, adding to prior commitments, to help finance Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper-gold mine. The disclosure brings IFC financing to $700 million. The project is expected to start production in 2028, but improved funding supports development sentiment for copper supply prospects.

title: Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd. Announces Progress on the Temporary Interruption of Partial Underground Mining At the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Mine in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
summary: Zijin Mining announced seismic activity at the Kakula portion of the Kamoa-Kakula copper mine in DRC caused underground flooding and a temporary interruption of partial underground mining. Pumping infrastructure damage required emergency dewatering, with production guidance for 2025 revised significantly downward, signaling reduced copper supply.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - 6.13
summary: SMM’s weekly review reports a rise in Indonesian hydrometallurgical laterite nickel ore delivered prices (up ~3.8% WoW) amid weather-driven supply tightness and delayed quota approvals. Demand strengthened after Morowali resumed production, keeping hydrometallurgical ore prices firm. Meanwhile, NPI smelters face cost inversions as finished stainless prices fall.

title: Velux Group Signs Agreement with Novelis to Supply Low Carbon Aluminum
summary: Velux Group signed a multi-year agreement with Novelis for high recycled-content flat-rolled aluminium (>70% recycled) to be used in roof windows and accessories. The deal targets cutting aluminium’s carbon intensity to 3 kg CO2e/kg or below by 2030 and supports decarbonization through recycled material use.

title: Outrage over Raja Ampat nickel mining: Between virality and solidarity - Academia
summary: Greenpeace and local youth protested nickel mining at Raja Ampat, where mining is legally banned but licenses were issued. Social media backlash pushed the government to revoke permits for four of five companies operating there, leaving PT Gag Nikel under supervision. The risk of curtailed supply may support nickel prices short term.

title: Copper theft leaving Perth roads in darkness, streetlights without electricity
summary: Perth metro areas face nighttime blackouts as copper thieves strip wiring from the power grid, leaving about 65 km of streetlights and 14 km of pathway lights non-operational. Authorities say theft has risen since 2018, costing millions annually, and scrap-licensing laws have fueled an underground resale market for copper.

title: Railway bells, copper cable stolen from rail bridge
summary: Police report that thieves stole over 750 meters of copper cable from a Hawke’s Bay railway bridge and removed four crossing bells. Authorities warn tampering could cause fatal accidents and vow enforcement against scrap yards handling stolen materials. The event signals copper scrap theft but is unlikely to affect copper prices materially soon.

title: Two Minot men sentenced for copper theft | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Two Minot men were sentenced for participating in a copper-wire theft scheme at Falkirk Mining Company near Underwood. The theft involved multiple incidents totaling about 980 pounds of copper tubing/wire, with proceeds from selling scrap in Minot and reported losses exceeding $500,000 to replace and repair materials.

title: The spot market remains sluggish, with the premium in east China narrowing rapidly [SMM spot aluminum noon review]
summary: SMM reports sluggish aluminium spot trading in East and Central China, with transactions often at discounts versus SMM prices and premiums narrowing rapidly. Downstream purchase willingness remains weak despite ongoing long-term contracting. Domestic aluminium ingot inventories are slightly lower, but higher casting ingot output and production cuts keep demand soft. Spot premiums are expected to keep narrowing.

title: Copper prices remain high amid off-season, cooling demand! Operating rates of cable producers declined significantly MoM in June【SMM analysis】
summary: SMM reports copper wire and cable enterprise operating rates fell to 70.18% (down 3.08 pp MoM, 12.66 pp YoY) and finished-product inventories rose after weak end-use demand followed April’s price volatility. Copper prices stay above 80,000 yuan/mt, but operators reduce rates to curb inventory risk.

title: Commodity prices: Platinum, gold and silver lead commodity markets, while alumina, bauxite and coal lag
summary: The piece notes strong performance in precious metals like platinum and silver, contrasting it with a “brutal reversal” in bauxite and alumina prices late last year. Because alumina is a key input to aluminium refining, the drop implies softer near-term aluminium cost expectations.

title: How Paid Family and Medical Leave Benefits Families and Businesses
summary: Hindalco (Aditya Birla Group) will acquire US specialty alumina producer AluChem for $125 million, adding three US facilities and raising annual alumina capacity in North America by 60,000 tonnes. The deal expands Hindalco’s downstream specialty alumina portfolio for high-tech and industrial refractory uses, supporting aluminium-linked supply and growth expectations.

title: Hindalco to acquire US specialty alumina manufacturer AluChem for $125 million
summary: Hindalco has agreed to acquire US specialty alumina producer AluChem for $125 million, aiming to expand North American specialty alumina production capacity by 60,000 tonnes. With facilities in Ohio and Arkansas, the acquisition strengthens supply for aluminium-related downstream uses and supports bullish near-term aluminium sentiment.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Receives Bureau of Land Management Approval for Exploration Plan of Operations at its Copper Creek Project
summary: Faraday Copper said the U.S. Bureau of Land Management approved its Exploration Plan of Operations for the Copper Creek Project in Arizona, enabling up to 67 drill pads and a Phase IV program likely starting in Q3 2025. The company plans updated resource and economic studies later in 2025.

title: Intrepid Metals Corp.: Intrepid Metals Secures Additional Mineral Rights Adjacent to Rio Tinto at Corral Copper
summary: Intrepid Metals acquired additional state leases and a patented mining claim to expand its Corral Copper Property near Rio Tinto’s adjacent claims in Arizona. The land package increased by 2,195 acres. The release is an exploration and development positioning update with no production or supply impact stated.

title: Gladiator Metals Corp.: Gladiator Completes Gravity Survey and Identifies Multiple Large-Scale, Untested Copper Skarn Targets at Little Chief
summary: Gladiator Metals reports gravity survey results at the Little Chief Trend within its Whitehorse Copper Project, identifying multiple undrilled copper-gold skarn anomalies and planning two diamond rigs to drill in the coming weeks. The news is exploration-focused with no production or reserve changes.

title: India sends geologists to Zambia to explore copper and cobalt
summary: India has sent geologists to Zambia to explore potential copper and cobalt deposits under a large government allocation. The initiative spans three years and aims to inform potential future mining leases. Because exploration is early and not affecting near-term supply, any impact on copper prices is likely limited.

title: Alumina costs are expected to drop back slightly in July
summary: SMM expects China’s weighted average alumina production costs to fall slightly in July. June costs were largely flat. The outlook reflects stable-to-lower imported bauxite contract prices and falling caustic soda contract prices in Henan/Guangxi, with lower July caustic soda levels. Overall cost range: 2,850–3,050 yuan/mt.

title: In H1, bauxite port inventory buildup reached nearly 10 million mt
summary: SMM data show China’s bauxite port and refinery inventories rising sharply in June, with total port inventory at 23.35 million mt and a large year-to-date buildup. Production slipped MoM due to inspections, but imported shipments stay high. Overall bauxite remains in surplus, supporting continued inventory accumulation and pressuring aluminium sentiment.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc Launches $10 Million 2025 Duke Copper-Gold District Drilling: Provides District Update
summary: Amarc Resources says it has started a $10 million 2025 drilling program at its DUKE copper-gold district in central British Columbia, funded via Boliden earning-in. The work targets multiple porphyry Cu-Au targets (JO, C4, Svea), expanding on prior scout drilling that returned copper and gold mineralized intercepts.

title: CATL-led nickel, battery project breaks ground in Indonesia
summary: CATL’s consortium with ANTAM and IBC broke ground on a $6 billion Indonesia project covering nickel mining, smelting, cathode materials, recycling, and battery manufacturing. Planned production includes about 142,000 tonnes of nickel annually. The integrated rollout should raise near-term expectations for nickel feedstock demand.

title: India Launches Cobalt and Copper Exploration in Zambia
summary: India is launching copper exploration in Zambia by acquiring greenfield land and sending geologists to assess copper deposits. Zambia’s economy relies heavily on copper exports, so the move signals India’s intent to secure critical mineral supply. It may provide mild near-term support to copper sentiment, though production impact is not immediate.

title: Aluminum tariffs weigh on results of Corona producer Constellation Brands
summary: Constellation Brands reported weaker-than-expected quarterly results, citing aluminum tariffs as a key driver of lower profitability. Beer packaging requires aluminum, and higher aluminum costs reduced margins. The company reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance despite earlier share declines tied to concerns over tariff hikes.

title: Protesters block Peru copper route used by large miners
summary: Informal miners in Peru have blockaded parts of a key copper transport corridor in Chumbivilcas, disrupting trucking used by major producers including MMG’s Las Bambas, Glencore’s Antapaccay and Hudbay’s Constancia. Companies reportedly began to be affected after days of protest, adding near-term supply risk and weighing on copper prices.

title: Copper looking good for rest of 2025
summary: The article argues copper will stay strong through 2025, citing tariffs that shift stocks into the US and tighten ex-US availability, lifting LME premiums and forecasts (e.g., Goldman’s higher December 2025 outlook). It also describes active M&A/offtake bidding for ASX copper projects, reinforcing bullish sentiment.

title: Austral Resources Australia acquires Rocklands Copper Mine near Cloncurry
summary: Austral Resources has agreed to acquire Queensland’s Rocklands copper mine near Cloncurry, which has been in care and maintenance since November and has been reopened multiple times since 2016. Residents are cautious due to prior unpaid wages and closures, but Austral expects upcoming production to support the town.

title: Key Takeaways from Aluminum Forum of Indonesia Critical Minerals Conference & Expo 2025
summary: The Aluminum Forum of Indonesia reports forecasts for a sizable global bauxite surplus (~12mn mt) and an alumina surplus in 2025 (notably China), implying sustained downward pressure on prices. It also discusses demand growth but stresses near-term risks from oversupply conditions and weak sector outlooks.

title: Aluminium Forging Market Share Analysis, Industry Trends &
summary: A ResearchAndMarkets report forecasts growth in the aluminium forging market, citing increased use of lightweight aluminium in automotive and other industrial sectors, especially in Asia-Pacific. It also acknowledges “fluctuations in aluminum prices” as a restraint, but gives no specific near-term supply, policy, or inventory details to drive prices immediately.

title: Erdene Enters Agreement to Acquire  Tereg Uul Copper-Gold
summary: Erdene signed an option agreement to acquire up to 80% of the Tereg Uul copper-gold porphyry prospect near Mongolia’s Oyu Tolgoi. The deal includes staged exploration spending and payments, with exploration expected to start in late Q3. No production is mentioned, suggesting only a modest copper-supportive sentiment.

title: Ero Copper Achieves Commercial Production at the Tucumã
summary: Ero Copper said its Tucumã Operation in Pará, Brazil reached commercial production effective July 1, after commissioning and plant modifications improved throughput to above 75% of design capacity in June. The mine produced about 6,400 tonnes of copper in Q2, including ~2,000 tonnes in mid-June, and expects throughput growth into year-end.

title: Erdene Enters into an Agreement to Acquire Tereg Uul Copper-Gold Porphyry Prospect
summary: Erdene Resource Development agreed to an option to acquire up to 80% of Tereg Uul, a copper-gold porphyry prospect near Mongolia’s Oyu Tolgoi corridor. The deal requires milestone payments and about USD 3 million of exploration spending within 12 months, with potential later stake purchases. Near-term copper supply impact is minimal.

title: Ero Copper Corp Achieves Commercial Production At Tucum Operation
summary: Ero Copper Corp said its Tucum operation in Brazil reached commercial production effective July 1, 2025. Commissioning of a third filter press and process plant modifications helped sustain throughput above 75% of design capacity in June. Q2 output totaled about 6,400 tonnes, including 2,000 tonnes in late June.

title: Ero Copper Achieves Commercial Production at the Tucumã Operation
summary: Ero Copper said its Tucumã operation in Pará, Brazil achieved commercial production effective July 1, 2025. After completing commissioning of a third filter press and plant modifications, throughput exceeded 75% of design capacity in June. The firm produced about 6,400 tonnes of copper in Q2 and expects throughput and sequential copper growth into year-end.

title: Indonesia nickel miners urge government to maintain three-year mining quota
summary: Indonesia’s nickel miners’ association APNI urged the government to keep mining quotas valid for three years rather than cutting RKABs to one year. The ministry said shorter quotas aim to better control supply and support prices amid revenue concerns. APNI warned shorter periods could cause approval bottlenecks for miners, raising supply uncertainty.

title: India to attract foreign copper firms with overseas mining ties, gov't document shows
summary: India unveiled steps to boost copper output, including encouraging foreign firms to build smelters and refineries in exchange for overseas mining investments. With domestic reserves limited, India expects to import most concentrates by 2047 and plans trade links and subsidies to expand 4–5 million tonnes of smelting/refining capacity, supporting copper supply expectations.

title: India to woo foreign copper miners, expand ties, gov't document shows
summary: India unveiled steps to increase copper output, including encouraging foreign firms to build smelters and refineries in exchange for Indian state-owned companies investing overseas in mining. The document highlights reliance on imported concentrates and rising demand, supporting expectations of tighter copper supply and potential near-term bullish pressure.

title: Aldebaran Reports Infill Drilling Results from Eleven Holes at the Altar Copper-Gold Project in San Juan Argentina
summary: Aldebaran reports infill diamond drilling results (11 holes) at the Altar copper-gold project in Argentina, focused on zones intended to upgrade inferred resources to measured/indicated. Drill intercepts include multiple long copper-bearing sections reported as CuEq, supporting continuity and potentially strengthening the project’s development outlook.

title: Second Drill Hole at Potro SE Extends Polymetallic Mineralization at Mirasol's Flagship Sobek Gold-Silver-Copper Project in the Vicuña District, Chile
summary: Mirasol reports a second drill hole at its Sobek (Vicuña, Chile) Potro SE target, extending a hydrothermal breccia system with gold, high silver, and zinc/lead plus copper indications. The company plans follow-up drilling to test the fault corridor southward, but no near-term production impact is given.

title: Canada announces new measures to protect steel and aluminum
summary: Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney announced new protective measures for domestic steel and aluminum, including a tariff-rate quota for foreign steel imports, aluminum-focused procurement preference changes, and possible additional tariffs. The policy response targets fallout from U.S. steel tariffs, with trade diversion into Canada potentially addressed via quotas.

title: High Nickel Pig Iron Prices Continue to Weaken, Macroeconomic Policies Aid Market Recovery
summary: High-grade nickel pig iron prices (SMM 8–12% NPI and Indonesian FOB NPI) fell week-on-week and are expected to stay weak. Elevated Philippine nickel ore CIF costs and Indonesia smelter maintenance/retooling reduce output and worsen smelter losses. Demand is steady but inventories don’t destock strongly; macro support offers only limited lift.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - 7.4
summary: SMM’s weekly review finds Indonesian nickel ore and NPI prices weakening: nickel ore delivered prices eased and NPI averages fell, while rain disrupts logistics and smelters struggle with high ore costs (cost inversion), prompting maintenance/production shifts and reduced procurement. Despite some potential quota approvals, short-term nickel prices face downward pressure.

title: Copper theft growing at alarming rate across Eastern Canada
summary: Bell reports copper theft incidents across Eastern Canada have risen 23% year-over-year, with over 500 cases reported in the first half of 2025 and concentration in Ontario, New Brunswick and Quebec. The company says theft damages telecom infrastructure and urges stronger penalties, implying greater replacement needs for copper wiring.

title: Kishan Reddy releases Copper & Aluminium Vision Documents to boost India's clean energy infrastructure
summary: India’s coal and mines minister released Copper and Aluminium Vision Documents to support the energy transition. The copper plan targets added smelting/refining capacity, scaling secondary refining and recycling. The aluminium roadmap aims to expand bauxite and production capacity and increase recycling and low-carbon tech. This may affect sentiment, but details are long-term.

title: Major Quebec aluminum smelter announces $1.5-billion investment with new electricity deal
summary: Quebec’s Rio Tinto-related aluminum sector faces crushing U.S. aluminum tariffs, prompting federal liquidity talks with Rio Tinto and measures to protect jobs. Separately, Aluminerie Alouette announced a $1.5-billion investment in Sept-Îles, tied to long-term hydro electricity rate terms until 2045, aimed at maintaining competitiveness when aluminum prices fall.

title: Quebec aluminum smelter announces $1.5B investment
summary: A major Quebec aluminum smelter operator (Aluminerie Alouette) announced at least $1.5B of investment in its facilities, supported by a long-term agreement with Hydro-Québec on electricity rates until 2045. The government says it helps the industry offset U.S. tariff impacts and remain competitive as aluminum prices move.

title: H&H Aluminium Launches India's Largest Advanced Aluminium Solar Frame Plant in Rajkot – Bilkul Online
summary: H&H Aluminium launched India’s largest solar aluminium frame plant in Rajkot with 24,000 mtpa capacity, supporting up to 6 GW of solar installations. The firm cites high import dependence for solar frames and a five-year anti-dumping duty on Chinese anodized aluminium frames, indicating supportive domestic demand conditions for aluminium.

title: Kishan Reddy Unveils Copper Aluminium Vision for Clean Energy Push
summary: India’s coal and mines minister released “Copper Vision” and “Aluminium Vision” documents to support the energy transition. Plans include adding copper smelting/refining capacity and scaling secondary refining and recycling, and expanding aluminium production and bauxite capacity. These are long-term roadmaps focused on raw-material security.

title: Kishan Reddy Unveils Copper Aluminium Vision for Clean Energy Push
summary: India’s coal and mines minister released Copper and Aluminium Vision Documents to support the clean-energy transition. The copper plan targets added smelting/refining capacity by 2030 and more secondary refining and recycling, while aluminium aims to expand production and bauxite capacity and raise recycling. Impact is mainly long-term.

title: Major Quebec aluminum smelter announces $1.5B investment with new electricity deal
summary: A major Quebec aluminium smelter announced a $1.5B investment tied to a new electricity agreement. The electricity deal can influence smelter operating costs and the availability of aluminium production. The news is likely to support aluminium market expectations for steadier or improved margins, providing modest near-term price uplift.

title: G.pivaudran announces entire product range now available in 'low-carbon' aluminium | Article
summary: G.pivaudran says its full product range can now be offered in “low-carbon” aluminium produced with renewable-powered, optimized processes, claiming lower CO2 per tonne than standard aluminium. It also references recyclable-aluminium packaging innovations and ASI-certified can materials, potentially supporting CSR-driven aluminium demand.

title: Destruction caused by theft of copper results in jail | Wallaceburg Courier Press
summary: A Brantford man was sentenced after stealing copper from air-conditioning units, causing about $45,000 damage to one business and $2,500 to another while seeking copper to fund drug addiction. The piece highlights rising copper-theft impacts on firms’ insurance and finances, but remains localized with no clear market-wide copper supply shock.

title: Persistent demand to fuel copper prices to rally to Rs 980-Rs 1,020 per kg: Report
summary: A Motilal Oswal report expects copper to rally further, citing shortages of copper stocks and strong backwardation (cash–3M spread above $100, LME warehouse stocks below 100,000 tonnes). It links the squeeze to lower immediate availability and trader activity ahead of possible US import tariffs, alongside a weaker US dollar and rate-cut expectations.

title: Copper Prices May Rally to Rs 1,020 per kg Amid Demand Surge
summary: The report expects copper to rally further, pointing to a near-term shortage: falling LME warehouse stocks (below 100,000 tonnes), strong backwardation, and a widened LME cash-3M spread. It attributes tightness to lower inventories and traders rushing ~400 kt into the US amid potential tariff risks, plus a weaker US dollar and rate-cut expectations.

title: Hindustan Copper shifts to underground mining, plans to double output amid surge in infra demand
summary: Hindustan Copper has transitioned its Malanjkhand mine from open-cast to fully underground operations and plans to double output. The move is framed as supportive of India’s growing infrastructure demand, potentially improving copper production expectations and market sentiment over the coming weeks.

title: Canada could financially back aluminum producers if 50% U.S. tariffs persist, trade group says
summary: Canada is considering financial backing for its large aluminium producers if the U.S. maintains a 50% tariff on aluminium imports. Reuters reports early talks with the industry amid negotiations. With roughly half of U.S. aluminium imports coming largely from Canada, persistent tariffs imply weaker demand and price pressure for aluminium.

title: Canada could financially back aluminum producers if 50% US tariffs persist, trade group says
summary: Canada is discussing financial backing for major aluminum producers if the US maintains a 50% tariff on aluminum imports. About half of US aluminum demand is imported, largely from Canada. The tariff has been in place since June 4, and talks aim to support cash flow and investment amid trade-war pressure.

title: Appeal after copper cable thieves target Aberdeenshire wind farms
summary: Police in Scotland appealed after copper cable thieves targeted two wind farms near Laurencekirk and Stonehaven, forcing open turbines and removing copper cables. Break-ins occurred overnight and over several hours. The stolen cable is believed to be worth tens of thousands of pounds, but likely too small for broader copper pricing impact.

title: Copper cables stolen in wind farm break-ins
summary: Copper cables were stolen from two wind farms in Aberdeenshire, with police believing the incidents are linked and likely involved a large vehicle. Turbines were forced open and the value is estimated in tens of thousands of pounds. Police are appealing for information; the theft affects copper supply locally.

title: Australia's South32 to take $130 million hit on Colombian nickel asset sale
summary: South32 said it will record a $130 million impairment charge tied to selling its Cerro Matoso ferronickel operations in Colombia to CoreX. The move reflects a sustained nickel market downturn, with producers cutting spending as Indonesia boosts output and prices collapse. South32 also reports declining planned nickel grades.

title: Rich ore discovered in drilling at Selebi copper-nickel mine in Botswana
summary: NexMetals Mining said drilling at the Selebi North deposit in Botswana hit “rich ore,” including multiple intervals with copper grades up to 2.87% and nickel grades up to 1.85%, while extending the orebody down-dip by 315 meters beyond the modeled boundary. The update is generally supportive for copper and nickel sentiment.

title: Rich ore discovered in drilling at Selebi copper-nickel mine in Botswana
summary: NexMetals reported rich results from initial drill holes at its Selebi North copper-nickel deposit in Botswana, including 13.5 meters with 1.13% copper and 1.25% nickel and additional intercepts extending ore down-dip and beyond the modeled resource boundary. Improved resource potential supports bullish sentiment for copper and nickel.

title: Kwinana Freeway, Old Coast Road left in the dark for months after thieves steal copper cable
summary: Thieves have stolen millions of dollars of copper cabling from streetlights and road infrastructure in WA, leaving areas without lighting for months. Main Roads says about 800,000 metres of cable were stolen over five to six years and replacement costs are about $2–$3 million annually, prompting investigations and prosecutions.

title: 'Nail in a coffin': Trump's steel, aluminum tariffs bleed Indian foundries | Trade War
summary: Trump’s planned/implemented higher US tariffs on steel and aluminium are squeezing Indian metal exporters and foundries. Orders have slowed and nearly 30% were cancelled after tariffs rose to 50%. With a 26% reciprocal tariff on India in play and market uncertainty, aluminium-linked supply and demand weaken, bearish for prices.

title: S$1.5b nickel fraud trial: Accused swindler Ng Yu Zhi declines to testify, defence closes case
summary: A businessman in Singapore is on trial over an alleged S$1.5 billion nickel investment fraud, with claims that purported physical nickel trading was fictional and investor money was diverted to personal spending. The defence closed its case after the accused declined to testify, while the verdict is pending later.

title: Indonesian minister seeks support to allow Amman to export copper concentrate
summary: Indonesia’s minister asked mining authorities to consider easing the copper concentrate export ban for Amman Mineral International until its smelter reaches full capacity. Amman holds about 200,000 mt of concentrate inventory and production exports are restricted since mid-2023. The smelter is running but not yet at full output, prompting policy flexibility.

title: Major step forward for the Resolution Copper Project | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: The U.S. Forest Service posted the final environmental impact statement and draft record of decision for the Resolution Copper Mining Project. The step supports advancing a proposed U.S. copper mine, though federal land transfer is not expected until Aug. 19, 2025, limiting immediate supply timing effects.

title: Weak traditional support coupled with the impact of substitute materials may lead copper billet producers' operating rates to hit bottom again in July
summary: SMM data show copper billet producers’ operating rate fell to 46.15% in June and is expected to drop to 43.82% in July. Demand is weak in the traditional off-season as high copper prices suppress downstream buying, pushing brass-billet buyers toward substitutes like stainless steel.

title: $1.46b nickel scam: Ng Yu Zhi opts to remain silent after judge calls for his defence
summary: A Singapore court trial ended for Ng Yu Zhi, accused of masterminding a $1.46b nickel-trading scam. Prosecutors said purported physical nickel trades never occurred and early investors were paid with funds from others. The case centers on alleged cheating and forged documents, not real nickel market flows.

title: Canada Nickel Reports Continued Exploration Success at MacDiarmid, Provides Exploration Update
summary: Canada Nickel says 2025 drilling at its MacDiarmid project intersected sulphide mineralization with multiple multi-hundred-metre nickel intervals (e.g., 0.25% Ni over 363 m) and plans to resume drilling at Midlothian and publish additional resources. The update is exploration-focused and unlikely to change nickel supply near term.

title: Copper theft is getting so bad Bell Canada is sounding the alarm
summary: Bell Canada warns copper theft is surging in eastern Canada, with incidents disrupting phone/internet and 911 access. Copper theft is up 23% year-on-year and Bell reports 2,270+ incidents since 2022, prompting accelerated shift to fiber and calls for tougher penalties. The story centers on copper theft impacts.

title: Crisis in the copper chain: innovation, geopolitics and Australia
summary: The article argues copper faces a growing supply-demand gap driven by EVs, grids and renewables, while US tariff threats and potential import restrictions add uncertainty and could disrupt supply chains. It also notes smelter intake constraints and concentrate shortages, tightening the market and pointing to price support despite longer-term technological solutions.

title: India announces initiatives to boost domestic copper production
summary: India announced incentives to attract foreign firms to build copper smelters and refineries, aiming to cut refined copper import dependence. The plan includes subsidies and customs duty exemptions, concentrate procurement strategy via trade talks, and notes tighter concentrate supplies. It also outlines aluminium demand and production strategies, but mainly longer-term targets.

title: Indonesia's nickel miners seek to maintain three-year quota validity
summary: Indonesia’s nickel miners (APNI) urged the government to keep mining quota validity at three years rather than shorten it to one. APNI argues yearly reapplications could create bureaucratic bottlenecks and reduce operational certainty. The ministry says quota adjustments aim to regulate supply and support commodity prices, alongside potential environmental sanctions at IMIP.

title: Bell warns copper theft on the rise, hotspots in Ontario, N.B., Quebec
summary: Bell warns copper theft is rising in Ontario, New Brunswick, and Quebec, with 500 cases in 2025 and a reported 23% year-on-year increase. The telco says thefts target copper telecom power wiring for resale, prompting calls for tougher penalties and added surveillance.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Announces $5 Million Listed Issuer Financing Exemption (LIFE) Private Placement
summary: Gunnison Copper announced a non-brokered private placement raising up to C$5.0 million to fund follow-on work at its Gunnison Copper Project, including long-lead drilling and metallurgical testing for a pre-feasibility study, plus 12 months of U.S. general and administrative costs. Closing is expected mid-July 2025.

title: Gunnison Copper Announces $5 Million Listed Issuer Financing Exemption (LIFE) Private Placement
summary: Gunnison Copper Corp. announced a C$5 million listed issuer financing exemption private placement to fund additional and follow-on work at the Gunnison Copper Project, including long-lead drilling and metallurgical testing for a pre-feasibility study, plus US head office G&A. Closing is expected mid-July 2025.

title: Operating rate of copper plate/sheet and strip continued to decline in June; "off-season test" continues
summary: SMM reports June operating rates for copper plate/sheet and strip producers fell to 67.44% as off-season demand stayed sluggish. Orders dropped MoM and firms cut production, while finished inventories rose. With wait-and-see sentiment amid high copper prices, SMM expects further July rate decline to 63.44%.

title: Third of chip production could face copper supply disruptions by 2035, PwC report says
summary: PwC said 32% of global semiconductor production could face copper supply disruptions by 2035 as drought risk rises in key chip-supplying countries. It highlights water stress already affecting Chile and Peru copper output, estimating 25% of Chile’s production at risk today, rising sharply over coming decades.

title: Operating rates of copper foil enterprises continue to rise, with lithium battery sector demand becoming the growth engine [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says China’s copper foil enterprises’ operating rate rose in June and is expected to climb in July, driven largely by lithium battery copper foil demand. Payment-term regulation improved cash flow, and finished/raw inventory ratios fell. Copper price strength later in June also boosted stockpiling, supporting tighter supply.

title: The long, suspenseful journey to Indonesia's nickel 'paradise' - Society
summary: A Jakarta Post report details conflicts around nickel mining in Indonesia’s Raja Ampat region, where environmental and indigenous concerns have sparked controversy. The mining operation on Gag Island (PT Gag Nikel) was allowed to continue, but the ongoing dispute highlights potential disruption or uncertainty for nearby nickel activities, a factor that can weigh on nickel prices.

title: Star Copper Corp.: Star Copper Confirms Two Prospective Copper Zones and Identifies Large Magnetic Anomaly as Daily Drilling Continues
summary: Star Copper Corp. provided updates from drilling at its Star Project in British Columbia, reporting continued near-surface copper oxide mineralization and deeper targets for porphyry copper-gold. The company also identified additional prospective zones (Star North/East/West) based on soil and IP signatures, with further assays pending.

title: Supreme Critical Metals Inc. Announces Amendment to Uranium Property Option, Relinquishes Nickel Property
summary: Supreme Critical Metals amended a uranium property option and, separately, relinquished its interest in the Saguenay Nickel Project in Quebec after a strategic review. While the release is not about nickel prices directly, dropping the nickel project can slightly weaken market expectations for future nickel supply.

title: The operating rate of copper pipe & tube producers will continue to decline
summary: SMM data show copper pipe & tube enterprise operating rates falling to 73.65% in June (down sharply MoM/YoY), with reduced production driven by weaker air-conditioner schedules and slower OEM cargo pick-up. July operating rates are projected to decline to 69.18% and further to 60–70% later as inventories remain high.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Reports 112,009 Tonnes of Copper Produced by Kamoa-Kakula in Q2 2025
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reported Kamoa-Kakula’s Q2 2025 copper output of 112,009 tonnes (+11% y/y) as concentrators ramp to ~85% of design and western-side mining restarted. Stage 2 dewatering pumps are progressing, and on-site smelter start is slated for September with first anodes in October.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Receives Mantoverde Optimized Permit
summary: Capstone Copper said it received the DIA environmental permit for the Mantoverde Optimized project in Chile. The permit clears the last major requirement for the brownfield expansion, raising throughput and extending mine life, with an expected additional ~20,000 tpa of copper production. Orders for long-lead items were also approved.

title: Glencore to sell struggling copper refinery to Filipino billionaire, Bloomberg News reports
summary: Glencore agreed to sell its Philippines copper refinery Pasar to the Villar family after putting the plant on care and maintenance during a severe copper pricing crisis. The valuation was not disclosed. While details are limited, the ownership change may affect expectations for near-term copper refining supply.

title: NGEx Minerals Ltd. Announces the Final Drill Results from the Phase 3 Program at its 100% Owned Lunahuasi High-Grade Copper-Gold-Silver Project in San Juan, Argentina
summary: NGEx Minerals reported final Phase 3 drill results from its Lunahuasi high-grade copper-gold-silver project in Argentina, including intervals with substantial copper grades and high associated gold/silver. The company completed 25,003m of drilling and will refine the deposit model before announcing Phase 4 plans later.

title: Capstone Copper Receives Mantoverde Optimized Permit
summary: Capstone Copper said it received the required environmental impact (DIA) permit for its Mantoverde Optimized project in Chile. The permit clears the last major authorization, allowing a brownfield expansion that lifts concentrator throughput and extends mine life, which could improve expected copper supply prospects.

title: Indonesia's minister requests copper concentrate export ban exemption for Amman
summary: Indonesia’s minister has requested an exemption from an export ban on copper concentrate for Amman. Granting such an exemption would likely allow more concentrate to ship from Indonesia than a full ban scenario, improving near-term supply expectations and weighing on copper prices.

title: Guinea Nearly Matches 2022 Bauxite Exports by Mid-2025
summary: Guinea exported 99.8 million tons of bauxite in H1 2025, up 36% year-on-year, nearly matching its 2022 full-year total and reinforcing its role as the top global supplier. China buys ~60% of exports. Guinea is also building new alumina/refinery capacity.

title: Sitka Gold Corp.: Sitka Commences the First Drill Program Ever to Be Conducted at Its Coppermine River Project in Nunavut Where up to 41.54% Copper and 13.45% Copper Have Been Identified in Volcanic-Hosted and Sediment-Hosted Target Areas
summary: Sitka Gold commenced its first diamond drilling at the Coppermine River Project in Nunavut, targeting sediment-hosted Copper Leaf and volcanic-hosted WIN copper showings. Surface grab samples previously returned up to 13.45% Cu (Copper Leaf) and up to 41.54% Cu (WIN). Initial results from drilling are pending.

title: Torr Metals Inc.: Torr Metals Advances Kolos Project with IP Survey Underway at High-Grade Bertha Copper Target
summary: Torr Metals reports an induced polarization survey underway at the Bertha Zone of its Kolos copper-gold project, citing historical supergene-style high-grade surface copper (up to 8.48%) and conducting recent rock sampling (assays pending). The release is exploratory, with no immediate production or supply impact for metals markets.

title: Semi-annual Review of Bauxite: Supply Surges Amid High Prices, Continuous Inventory Buildup Puts Pressure on Prices, Pulling Them Back
summary: SMM reports that bauxite supply surged on higher Guinea shipments, pushing port and refinery inventories up and turning alumina profitability to losses. Imported bauxite CIF prices fell from mid-January highs to about $74/mt by June 30. With buyers bargain-buying and surplus evident, bauxite prices pulled back.

title: Timmins news:  Four men charged with $100K copper wire theft in Coleman Township
summary: Ontario Provincial Police charged four men over the theft of 33 hydro poles’ copper wire, worth about $100,000, in Coleman Township between May 1 and May 7. Investigators linked the crime to a road connecting Cobalt and the Hound Chute hydro generating station. The case is local, not market-moving.

title: Trump to Impose 50 Percent Tariff on Copper
summary: Trump said he will impose a 50% tariff on copper, making “we’re doing copper” the focus of the policy announcement. Such a large tariff is expected to affect import pricing and demand, worsening near-term trade conditions and likely pressuring copper prices downward in the coming weeks.

title: What higher steel and aluminum tariffs mean for Washington state businesses, shoppers
summary: Trump’s higher tariffs on imported steel and aluminum (50% vs 25%) took effect, prompting expectations that costs for U.S. importers and manufacturers will rise and be passed along the supply chain. Businesses using aluminum cans report immediate shipment price increases, indicating bullish near-term pressure for aluminium prices.

title: Trump says he will impose 50% tariff on copper imports on Tuesday
summary: Trump said the US will impose a 50% tariff on copper imports on Tuesday. Reuters reports copper futures jumped on the announcement, implying immediate expectations of reduced imports and tighter US supply. The measure is likely to support copper prices in the near term by raising landed costs for foreign material.

title: Copper Soars To Record High As Trump Unleashes 50% Tariff
summary: Copper futures surged to a record high after Trump said he plans a 50% tariff on copper imports under looming sectoral tariffs and a potential Section 232 investigation. The move followed tighter Chinese inventories and higher COMEX stocks, but the tariff expectation boosted immediate US copper prices.
