summary: Southern Hemisphere and FMR have completed a binding earn-in JV for Southern Hemisphere’s Llahuin southern concessions in Chile, with FMR funding exploration and drilling. The project is copper-gold-molybdenum and includes a deep Cu-Au target. The deal increases exploration activity but does not imply immediate copper production changes.

title: New secondary aluminum projects surged in H1 of 2025[SMM analysis]
summary: SMM data show 20 new secondary aluminium projects in China in H1 2025, adding 3.31mn mt of planned capacity. Most are still in environmental assessment or construction, so limited capacity is currently operational. Secondary wrought aluminium is expanding faster than cast, improving economics via recycling and lower costs.

title: SMM Analysis On China Blister Copper Supply-Demand Dynamics In August
summary: SMM reports blister copper RCs in China rebounded in early August after earlier tight supply in July. It cites declining anode supply from lower concentrate availability, limited imports, reduced scrap inputs from tariffs, and procurement pressure from “reverse invoicing.” Demand for anodes remains strong for cathode production, suggesting continued tightness and supportive copper prices.

title: Mitsubishi Materials looks to scale down copper concentrate processing
summary: Mitsubishi Materials is looking to scale down its processing of copper concentrate. If implemented, this would reduce refined copper output from concentrate feed, potentially tightening near-term supply expectations and supporting copper prices over the next days to four weeks.

title: 50% Duty Imposed On Copper
summary: President Trump issued a proclamation imposing a 50% tariff on imports of semi-finished copper and intensive copper derivative products from Aug. 1, applied to the copper-content value. The duty is under Section 232 for national security, stacking on other potential tariffs and restricting trade-zone treatment, potentially tightening near-term copper input supply.

title: Donald Trump news: Beer maker Molson Coors forecasts downbeat annual profit on aluminum tariff impact
summary: Molson Coors cut its annual profit outlook, blaming weak U.S. beer demand and aluminum tariff impacts. The company’s guidance suggests higher aluminum-related costs and softer use of aluminum packaging, which can dampen near-term demand expectations and weigh on aluminium prices over coming days to weeks.

title: Aluminum can maker Ball Corp lifts annual profit forecast buoyed by strong global demand
summary: Ball Corp lifted its annual profit forecast, attributing the upgrade to strong global demand. As an aluminum can manufacturer, higher expected sales and improved demand outlook for aluminum packaging can boost near-term market sentiment toward aluminum prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Torr Metals Inc. Secures Drill Permit for the Kirby, Lodi, and Clapperton Targets at the Kolos Copper-Gold Project
summary: Torr Metals announced it received a five-year drill permit for copper-gold targets (Kirby and Lodi) and a copper-silver-molybdenum target (Clapperton) at its Kolos project in British Columbia. The release focuses on permitting and surface geochemical/geophysical signals, with no immediate supply or market flow changes.

title: Lion Copper and Gold Corp.: Lion Copper and Gold Announces Pre-Feasibility Study Results for Brownfield Yerington Copper Project and Maiden Mineral Reserve
summary: Lion Copper and Gold reported pre-feasibility study results for its Yerington, Nevada heap-leach copper project, targeting ~120 million pounds per year of refined cathode. The release details reserves/resources, recovery assumptions, capex/operating costs, and sensitivity to copper prices, but no immediate production or supply shocks were announced.

title: Trump Administration Issues Proclamation Imposing 50% Section 232 Tariffs, Export Controls On Some Copper Scrap
summary: The Trump administration issued a proclamation applying 50% Section 232 tariffs and export controls on some copper scrap and on specified imported semi-finished copper and intensive copper derivative products. The measures are effective Aug. 1, 2025. The U.S. duty and controls likely reduce copper availability and lift near-term copper price expectations.

title: New Tariff Actions Announced Back-to-Back From The White House: Copper 232, Brazil Tariffs, And De Minimis
summary: The White House issued executive orders imposing a 50% Section 232 tariff on imports of semi-finished copper and copper-intensive derivative products effective Aug 1, while excluding copper ores, cathodes and scrap. It also adds tariffs on Brazil effective Aug 6 and suspends de minimis entry, likely pressuring demand and pricing for imported industrial inputs.

title: First American Nickel Refinery Marks Industrial Milestone
summary: Westwin Elements says it is building the first major US nickel refinery, signing two large long-term offtake agreements with Traxys and Golden Age and selling most of its projected commercial output. The deals secure feedstock and buyers for high-purity nickel over seven years, but near-term production impacts are not specified.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Pacific Ridge Announces Initial Mineral Resource Estimate for Kliyul Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration announced an initial inferred mineral resource estimate for the Kliyul Main Zone of its Kliyul copper-gold project in British Columbia. The resource totals 334.1Mt at 0.15% copper and 0.33% copper equivalent. The estimate uses defined metal prices and assumes no metallurgical testing yet.

title: Molson Coors forecasts lower annual profit because of U.S. tariffs on aluminum
summary: Molson Coors cut its profit and sales outlook, citing softer U.S. demand and higher can costs from U.S. tariffs on aluminum. The company expects incremental costs of $20m–$35m in the second half as levies lift the U.S. Midwest Premium used for aluminum pricing, pressuring near-term aluminum-related economics.

title: Tariffs Imposed Pursuant To U.S. Section 232 Copper Investigation
summary: The U.S. issued a Section 232 presidential proclamation imposing a 50% tariff on the copper content of imported semi-finished copper products and copper-intensive derivative products, effective August 1, 2025. Ores, concentrates, cathodes, anodes and scrap are excluded. No exemptions are indicated, with compliance guidance issued by CBP.

title: Molson Coors cuts financial forecasts on softening U.S. demand, aluminum tariffs
summary: Molson Coors cut its forecast, citing softer U.S. consumer demand and higher costs from aluminum tariffs. The brewer expects incremental costs of $20m–$35m in the second half as levies boost the Midwest Premium used for U.S./Canada aluminum pricing. Aluminum price expectations are mentioned as potentially reverting later.

title: Molson Coors forecasts profit drop on aluminum tariff impact
summary: Molson Coors cut its annual profit outlook, citing higher costs from Trump’s aluminum import tariffs. Aluminum duties doubled to 50% since June, raising the price of the metal the company uses for beer cans. The tariff spike also pressures demand and net sales as consumers reduce spending on alcohol.

title: PyroGenesis To Supply Plasma Torch Technology For Constellium's Aluminum Remelting Furnace
summary: PyroGenesis will supply plasma torch technology for Constellium’s demonstrator aluminum remelting furnace as part of a decarbonization initiative to replace traditional heating sources with all-electric plasma torches. Terms are undisclosed and commissioning is expected by Q1 2026, suggesting mainly longer-dated technology development.

title: Chile's Copper Giant Mourns Five Miners Lost to El Teniente's Deepest Danger
summary: Codelco’s El Teniente in Chile suffered a deadly 4.2-magnitude rockburst that killed six miners and trapped five. Operations were suspended in the affected area and over 3,000 workers evacuated, with a scrapped earnings report and intensified investigation. The event raises short-term copper output risk.

title: A tale of two supply chains: Comparing Trump's new copper tariffs and rare earth investments
summary: The article says the US launched sweeping Aug 1 copper policies, including a 50% tariff on semi-finished copper products plus domestic sales requirements and tighter export controls on copper scrap. It argues the measures miss the smelting bottleneck and could raise downstream costs for sectors like auto and construction.

title: Canadian aluminum, steel products dealt biggest blow from U.S. duties in June, data show
summary: Canada’s exports of unwrought aluminum to the U.S. fell more than 11% in June after the U.S. doubled Section 232 tariffs on aluminum to 50%. The article notes aluminum accounted for about 60% of U.S.-collected duties on Canadian imports, signaling near-term pressure on aluminum trade flows.

title: Diversifying partnerships in Indonesia's nickel downstreaming strategy - Academia
summary: Indonesia’s nickel downstream strategy is highlighted, including an MoU between INA, Danantara and Eramet to build a platform across the nickel value chain. The piece also notes heavy dependence on China for MHP and nickel sulphate exports and calls for fair rules and higher environmental standards, aiming to diversify risks.

title: Chhattisgarh: Nickel-Copper-PGE deposit discovered in Mahasamund district
summary: Chhattisgarh’s Mahasamund district has reported a new Ni-Cu-PGE mineral deposit, following exploration and a licence award to Deccan Gold Mines Limited. A mineralised zone and sulphide mineralization are cited as promising. The government frames it as strategic supply progress, but no near-term production volumes are given.

title: Chhattisgarh: Nickel-Copper-PGE deposit discovered in Mahasamund district
summary: Chhattisgarh’s government says a new Ni-Cu-PGE deposit was discovered in Mahasamund district, with preliminary exploration indicating a mineralised zone and sulphide potential. DGML received a composite licence to explore and mine the area. The development supports India’s critical-minerals self-reliance, but no near-term output is stated.

title: Glencore Earnings Fall on Lower Coal Prices, Copper Production Challenges
summary: Glencore’s first-half adjusted earnings fell, blamed on weaker coal prices and lower copper output after operational challenges in its copper business. The report also notes widened impairments from Colombian coal operations. Copper production weakness may be mildly supportive for copper expectations, but the story is earnings-focused, not a clear immediate supply shock.

title: Copper Rises With US Tariffs, Codelco Mine Stoppage in Focus
summary: Copper is rising as investors focus on US tariffs and a Codelco mine stoppage. The stoppage implies tighter near-term supply of refined copper, supporting prices, while tariff-related policy signals contribute to overall industrial metals sentiment in the short term.

title: Bahrain: Alba reports $65.3mln profit for Q2; alumina prices hit gains
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) reported Q2 2025 profit of $65.3 million, down sharply YoY, while revenue rose. The company cites higher landed alumina costs as a key drag. It notes LME aluminium averaged about $2,447/t in Q2, dipping earlier on tariffs but recovering, remaining volatile.

title: Zambia Copper and SA Business Proposed Sale Update | Company Announcement
summary: Jubilee Metals Group updated shareholders on its Zambia integrated copper strategy, highlighting Roan concentrator restart performance (384t copper units in July), drilling progress for Munkoyo, and ongoing cathode refining expansion at Sable. It also discusses processing third-party feedstocks and tailings monetisation, supporting stronger near-term copper output guidance.

title: Trump's copper tariff u-turn sparks US oversupply as metals take a breather: Saxo Bank
summary: The piece discusses how Trump’s copper tariff reversal has helped create US copper oversupply, leading metals to “take a breather” after a strong start to the year. It suggests the tariff u-turn has reduced price support and shifted supply expectations, weighing on copper near-term sentiment.

title: 【SMM Daily Review of Nickel Sulphate】 Wanhua Chemical listed 64 mt of battery-grade nickel sulphate for sale on the Anhuida platform of the Shanghai Metals Market Metal Trading Center
summary: SMM’s daily review notes that Wanhua Chemical listed 64 mt of battery-grade nickel sulphate for sale on the Anhuida platform of the Shanghai Metals Market trading center. The new offer quantity can influence short-term expectations for nickel sulphate availability and thereby affect nickel-linked price sentiment.

title: Kyrgyzstan doubles unprocessed aluminum exports to China in H1
summary: Kyrgyzstan significantly increased its unprocessed aluminium shipments to China in the first half of 2025, with exports more than doubling in both value and volume. The data, cited from China’s customs administration, suggests greater incoming supply to China, which can weigh on aluminium price expectations over the next few weeks.

title: C3 Metals Inc.: C3 Metals Geophysical Program Significantly Enhances Khaleesi Copper-Gold Drill Target, Peru
summary: C3 Metals announced ground geophysical surveys (Mag, IP, MT) at its Khaleesi copper-gold project in Southern Peru, refining copper targets beneath glacial till and scheduling a maiden 14-hole, 6,000m drill program for Q3 2025. The update is exploration-led and not a near-term copper supply disruption.

title: Magna Mining Inc.: Magna Mining Reports 17.9% Cu, 0.6% Ni and 28.1 g/t Pt + Pd + Au over 1.8 Metres in the 700 Footwall Copper Zone at McCreedy West Mine
summary: Magna Mining reported new underground drill results from its McCreedy West mine, including high-grade copper and nickel intersections within the 700 Cu-PGE footwall zone. Management says the data supports production planning and potential up-dip/east-west expansion, but results are for definition drilling with no immediate market supply change described.

title: Gold Hart Copper Corp.: Gold Hart Copper Second Drill Hole at Tolita Asset Intercepts Long Gold Copper & Molybdenum Intervals Including Higher Grades Than First Hole
summary: Gold Hart Copper reported results from a second diamond drill hole at its Tolita gold-copper-molybdenum project in Chile, highlighting longer porphyry-style intercepts including a section with 0.34% copper and molybdenum. The news supports ongoing exploration continuity but does not imply any near-term supply change.

title: Glencore's Net Loss Widens on Low Coal Prices and Copper Output
summary: Glencore reported a wider first-half net loss, attributing weaker performance mainly to weaker coal prices and reduced copper output. It said copper production was 26% lower year-on-year in the first half, driven by lower grades and recoveries and other operational constraints, which could weigh on near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Guinea revokes Emirates Global Aluminium's bauxite mining concession
summary: Guinea revoked Emirates Global Aluminium’s bauxite mining concession and moved assets to a state-backed entity, citing non-compliance with refinery-planning requirements. EGA’s Guinea operations had already seen export and mining suspensions. The action threatens bauxite supply from a major producer (about 2–3% globally), supporting aluminium prices.

title: Unearthing US Vulnerabilities: President Trump Outlines Steps To Strengthen The US Copper Industry
summary: The Trump administration issued a Copper Section 232 investigation and then a proclamation imposing universal 50% tariffs on over 70 categories of semi-finished copper products and copper-intensive derivatives effective Aug. 1, 2025. Copper ores, concentrates, cathodes, and anodes are exempt. Policies aim to strengthen US domestic copper supply.

title: 'It's insulting': Feds decline to review approval of drilling at planned copper mine
summary: U.S. federal authorities refused to review approval related to drilling for a planned copper mine. The decision introduces regulatory uncertainty and potential delays to planned mine development, which may reduce near-term expectations for copper supply and place downward pressure on copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Guinea revokes Emirates Global Aluminium concession, transfers assets to new local firm
summary: Guinea revoked Emirates Global Aluminium’s bauxite concession for alleged mining-code violations and transferred the assets to a state-backed firm without compensation. The move escalates a dispute over a planned alumina refinery. Despite ongoing uncertainty, analysts said the quick transfer could calm short-term bauxite supply fears, muting near-term aluminium price impact.

title: Copper Mines Close in on Western Apache Sacred Site and Protected Forest
summary: Federal action tied to land offsets and appeals is moving forward for copper mining in Arizona, including a Resolution Copper project enabling a major new copper mine and BLM-approved exploratory drilling for Faraday’s Copper Creek. The tribe and environmental groups challenge approvals, but progress can still raise supply expectations.

title: Market grapples with surprise US announcement on copper tariffs
summary: The US exempted refined copper from the planned 50% tariffs that would apply mainly to semi-finished and derivative products. The policy shift collapsed the US refined copper premium, driving a reported 19% intraday drop in US copper prices and prompting expectations of re-export and storage for LME deliveries.

title: Announcement on the European P1020A aluminium premium price [SMM Price Announcement]
summary: SMM announces the methodology and launch timing (8 August 2025) for its European Aluminium P1020A Rotterdam duty-paid and duty-unpaid spot premium assessments. The premium is defined versus LME official cash. Data collection and publication mechanics are detailed, supporting physical contract settlement and risk management expectations.

title: Rio Tinto approves US$180 million Norman Creek project, securing long-term future for Amrun bauxite operations on Queensland's Cape York Peninsula
summary: Rio Tinto approved a US$180 million Norman Creek access project at its Amrun bauxite mine and is progressing early works on the Kangwinan capacity expansion. The projects aim to increase and secure long-term bauxite supply and port export capacity for Weipa operations, supporting future aluminium raw-material availability.

title: Trump Wants Copper Smelted in America—But It's a 30-Year Wait
summary: Trump announced a 50% tariff on imported copper, with limited exemptions that include cathode, ore, and concentrate. Traders reportedly rushed to stockpile, pushing up New York copper prices, while forecasters later expect a premature U.S. glut. The broader push to reshore smelting faces cost and timing constraints.

title: Rio Tinto Approves $180 Million Australian Bauxite Investment
summary: Rio Tinto approved a $180 million investment for its Norman Creek bauxite area within the Amrun operations in Queensland. The project includes building infrastructure such as a haul road and worker accommodation, with first production expected in 2027. Rio says the investment supports future bauxite output and confidence in operations.

title: Demand in the lithium battery sector remains strong, with China's copper foil industry's operating rate hitting a new high for the year [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says China’s copper foil makers’ operating rate rose to 77.28% in July and is forecast to reach 78.24% in August. Lithium-battery copper foil demand is the key driver, with higher ESS orders and increased US export shipments during a tariff window. Inventories fell as shipments surged.

title: In July, the operating rates of copper billet producers declined both YoY and MoM, with inventories continuing to shrink
summary: SMM data show July copper billet producer operating rates falling to 44.82% (down MoM and YoY), with small/medium firms hardest hit amid off-season demand and tight raw material supply. Inventories of raw and finished goods decreased. August may improve slightly for large firms but remain tough for smaller producers; tariff impact is expected limited.

title: India, Russia to deepen cooperation in aluminium, fertilisers, railways, mining
summary: India and Russia signed a protocol to deepen cooperation, explicitly including aluminium, along with mining technology and railway transport. The working group discussed capacity building and technology transfer in mining and other areas. The aluminium cooperation could influence short-term market expectations for supply and trade, though details are not provided.

title: Indonesia promotes nickel-based EV battery production
summary: Indonesia is urging EV manufacturers to switch from lithium-based batteries to nickel-based ones through proposed regulations and incentives. The government highlights SOE projects and partnerships to grow midstream battery investment and secure supply-chain efficiency. The strategy is framed around rising global EV battery demand through 2040.

title: India, Russia to deepen cooperation in aluminium, fertilisers, railways, mining – Bilkul Online
summary: India and Russia signed a protocol to deepen cooperation in aluminium, along with fertilisers, railways and mining technology. The working group discussed capacity building and technology transfer in mining and industrial waste management. The aluminium focus could influence near-term supply/trade expectations, though no volumes or timelines were specified.

title: ZCCM-IH Further Cautionary Announcement_ Court Petition Relating to Mopani Copper Mines Plc Transact-SENS
summary: ZCCM-IH says it has been joined in a constitutional court case challenging the 2024 Mopani Copper Mines transaction involving International Resources Holdings. The petitioner argues it should have required prior parliamentary approval as a state asset disposal. ZCCM-IH contests the claim and will update as proceedings progress.

title: 'Milestone' moment as UAE produces low-carbon aluminium using Barakah nuclear plant
summary: The UAE says it has delivered its first batch of low-carbon aluminium (MinimAL) produced by Emirates Global Aluminium using electricity from the Barakah nuclear plant. EGA/ENEC partnership and early supply to Egypt’s Canex aim to expand low-carbon aluminium availability, supporting demand for lower-emissions aluminium and potentially supporting prices.

title: Indonesia's copper export to the US gets zero tariff
summary: Indonesia’s minister said the US will apply a 0% import tariff to Indonesian copper under the ongoing trade arrangement, improving export economics and near-term demand expectations. Negotiations continue to lower US tariffs on other commodities, including nickel, potentially from 19%.

title: EGA delivers UAE's first low-carbon aluminium using nuclear energy - Technical Review Middle East
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) delivered the UAE’s first low-carbon aluminium batch using 24/7 electricity from the Barakah nuclear plant, certified under I-REC protocols. The material, MinimAL, will be supplied to CANEX Aluminum for infrastructure and solar uses. The move supports decarbonisation and low-carbon aluminium demand.

title: Sterling Metals Corp.: Sterling Metals Commences Phase 2 Drilling and Provides Exploration Update at the Soo Copper Project
summary: Sterling Metals commenced Phase 2 drilling and expanded soil sampling at its Soo Copper Project in Ontario, aiming to test near-surface and down-dip extensions of copper-bearing porphyry dyke targets and related geophysical anomalies. The update provides drill targeting details and recent outcrop/soil findings but no immediate production or supply impact.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: SLAM IP Survey Expands Deep Conductive Target East of Granges and Logan Copper Nickel Cobalt Zones at Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration reports additional IP survey results over its Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt zones, extending deep conductive targets and identifying chargeability/resistivity anomalies east of the Granges and Logan zones. It also references prior drilling with 1.49% copper-equivalent over 64.9 meters. The update supports future potential but isn’t a current supply change.

title: METALS-Copper rises on upbeat Chinese trade data
summary: Copper prices rose as China’s July trade data beat forecasts, lifting sentiment for industrial metals. Chinese exports and copper/copper concentrate imports increased, supporting smelter demand. Optimism around a potential U.S.-China trade deal also helped, while aluminium and nickel prices advanced in tandem.

title: Chile posts unexpected July trade deficit as value of copper exports falls
summary: Chile’s central bank said the country exported $3.99 billion of copper in July, down 0.4% year over year. Chile recorded a $62 million trade deficit versus a $525 million surplus expected by economists, reflecting lower copper export value. The data can weigh on near-term copper sentiment and prices.

title: Aldebaran Resources Inc. Reports the Results from Seventeen Infill Holes at the Altar Copper-Gold Project in San Juan Argentina
summary: Aldebaran Resources reported results from the remaining 17 infill holes at the Altar copper-gold project in San Juan, Argentina, targeting an upgrade from Inferred to Measured & Indicated resources. The company highlights copper-equivalent grades and notes the updated resource estimate from drilling through 2023-24. This is a localized progress update, not a major supply shock.

title: Copper concentrate production in Armenia decreased by 9.3% in the first half of the year
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate production fell 9.3% year-on-year in the first half of 2025 to 131,178 tons, according to the national statistical committee. Reduced concentrate output can imply tighter copper supply expectations, which may weigh on copper prices in the near term. Other outputs (zinc, molybdenum) are also cited but less directly relevant.

title: ADC12 aluminum alloy prices rose, supported by the shortage of aluminum scrap[SMM analysis]
summary: SMM reports ADC12 secondary aluminum prices rose sharply as aluminum scrap supply tightened and scrap prices climbed with primary aluminum. Despite weak end-use demand from seasonal off-season holidays and limited new orders, cost pressure and improved theoretical margins supported upward bias. Inventory is flat-to-slightly destocking, keeping prices well supported.

title: Operating rates of copper pipe & tube producers further declined
summary: SMM data show copper pipe & tube producers’ operating rates falling to 68.94% in July, with expectations of further decline to 64.20% in August. Domestic orders weakened, secondary-market stocking motivation is low, and copper pipe exports dropped. US 50% tariff pressure on copper semis and Mexico-U.S. tariffs further suppress export demand.

title: The price of high-grade NPI is expected to be generally stable with slight rise, and the discount against refined nickel may narrow
summary: The article forecasts refined nickel prices to remain range-bound in August, citing off-season downstream demand and stable yet constrained nickel supply. High-grade NPI is expected to hold steady with a slight rise as stainless steel fundamentals improve. The NPI-to-refined-nickel discount is expected to narrow due to shifting costs from Indonesia quotas.

title: President Trump Orders 50 percent Section 232 Tariff on Copper Imports | White & Case LLP
summary: The US will impose a 50% Section 232 tariff on the copper-content value of semi-finished copper and intensive copper-derivative imports effective Aug 1, 2025, with CBP entry guidance and no in-transit exceptions. Raw copper (anode/cathode/scrap) is excluded, pressuring copper-linked supply and landed costs for US buyers.

title: Zambia dismisses US health warning after toxic spill in Kitwe's copper mining area
summary: Zambia dismissed a US embassy health warning after a tailings dam collapse at Sino-Metals mine in Kitwe spilled hazardous waste into the Kafue River. The US alleged widespread contamination, while Zambia said lab tests showed pH normal and water safe. The incident may still heighten short-term copper supply and risk concerns.

title: Indonesian copper exports to US enjoy free tariff | Vietnam+ (VietnamPlus)
summary: Indonesia’s minister confirms Indonesian copper exports to the US will receive a zero-percent import tariff, with talks ongoing to extend tariff exemptions to other commodities. Negotiations with the USTR also target reductions for nickel (currently 19%). The US reduced reciprocal tariffs from 32% to 19% under the July agreement.

title: As clock ticks on Oak Flat copper mine, judge considers late plea to block land swap
summary: A judge is weighing a late request to block the land swap associated with the Oak Flat copper mine. If the swap is halted or delayed, it could prevent or slow mine development, tightening prospective copper supply and supporting higher near-term copper price expectations as the court decision approaches.

title: American Primary Aluminum Association Applauds President
summary: APAA praised President Trump for imposing a Section 232 aluminum tariff, claiming it helps U.S. primary aluminium producers. Century Aluminum, the largest U.S. primary producer, plans to raise output by 10%, invest $50 million, and return its Mt. Holly facility to full capacity, creating over 100 jobs.

title: American Primary Aluminum Association Applauds President Trump's Leadership and Century Aluminum Ramping Up Domestic Aluminum Production by 10%
summary: The American Primary Aluminum Association praises President Trump’s Section 232 aluminium tariff, saying it enables Century Aluminum to increase U.S. primary production by 10% after a capacity restoration at its Mt. Holly facility. The announcement cites a $50 million investment and job creation, signaling improved domestic aluminium supply conditions.

title: The Overnight Report: Tariffs Rattling Markets
summary: Tariffs and Fed/FX volatility set a risk-off tone, but the copper subsector is supported. China’s July refined copper imports rose to the highest level this year, helped by a refined copper tariff exemption. Copper concentrate shipments increased and multiple mine disruptions (Codelco, Kamoa-Kakula) raise near-term supply tightness expectations.

title: ANALYSIS-Argentina's copper dreams need infrastructure - but who will build it?
summary: Reuters says Argentina’s copper resurgence depends on financing and building roads and power lines for projects in the Andes. With the government assessing needs and provinces allowing royalties to repay infrastructure, developers like BHP, Rio Tinto and others seek workable solutions. The prospect of higher copper output supports near-term bullish sentiment.

title: Analysis-Argentina's copper dreams need infrastructure - but who will build it?
summary: Reuters reports Argentina’s copper deposits could drive a major expansion, but projects need roads and high-voltage power lines that the government is not fully funding. Proposed royalty-based infrastructure repayment and private financing plans (including for BHP/Rio Tinto’s Vicuna) aim to restart copper production after 2018.

title: MAC Copper Limited Announces SARB Approval Received
summary: MAC Copper Limited says Harmony Gold has received written confirmation from the South African Reserve Bank indicating no objection to implementing the proposed acquisition scheme and Harmony’s funding. This satisfies one regulatory condition precedent; the deal remains subject to additional shareholder, court, and other approvals.

title: Aluminum importers use Port of Oswego's Foreign Trade Zone status to cushion tariff blow
summary: A Port of Oswego FTZ allows aluminum importers to temporarily cushion the impact of Trump’s 50% tariff on Canadian raw aluminum. Companies previously stockpiled ahead of tariff increases and use bonded handling and storage solutions. Importers order less due to logistical limits, but FTZ relief helps sustain supply access.

title: Copper infrastructure needed for Argentina mountain deposits
summary: Argentina’s government is assessing infrastructure needs to enable new copper mines in the north, with miners like BHP and Rio Tinto facing gaps in power and roads. Measures such as royalty repayment for public-utility infrastructure and plans to share infrastructure aim to speed investment. Production would restart after copper output ended in 2018.

title: Three charged in theft of more than 7,000 pounds of copper in Raleigh County, deputies say
summary: Raleigh County, West Virginia authorities charged several men after alleged theft of thousands of pounds of copper wire from Frontier Communications, with additional charges related to receiving stolen property at a recycling center. Investigators cite a recent spike in thefts. The event is localized and unlikely to affect broader copper prices.

title: Louisville ramps up efforts to combat copper thefts with new law, regulations
summary: Louisville charged seven people in a copper wire theft ring targeting critical infrastructure, including traffic signs and phone/911-related assets. The city and Kentucky passed tougher laws and enforcement, including a felony for tampering with critical infrastructure and tighter penalties. The report highlights ongoing theft impacts but lacks market-wide copper supply details.

title: Century Aluminum Mount Holly plant to increase production to full capacity
summary: Century Aluminum will raise production at its Mount Holly aluminum smelter from 75% to full capacity by June 30, 2026, restarting over 50,000 metric tons and investing $50 million. The company attributes the plan to a new 50% aluminum import tariff and highlights increased domestic output.

title: Suspects in Louisville copper wire theft ring appear in court
summary: Louisville authorities arrested suspects in a copper wire theft ring after a task-force crackdown. Theft involved about 3,600 feet of copper wire from a TRIMARC sign and city/AT&T-related communications equipment, with evidence coming from a scrap yard. Kentucky upgraded copper theft charges to felonies.

title: Aluminum Producer to Invest $50M in US Jobs as 'Direct Result' of Tariffs
summary: Century Aluminum plans a $50m investment to restart its partially idled South Carolina plant, citing tariffs on imported primary aluminum as the direct trigger. The move is expected to raise U.S. aluminum output by nearly 10% and add about 100 jobs, potentially reducing import pressure.

title: Gold Soars on Tariff Shock as Copper Holds Steady | Live Wire
summary: Gold surged on tariff headlines and rate-cut expectations, while copper traded more cautiously. U.S. exempted refined copper from planned tariffs (applied to semi-finished forms), easing near-term pressure, but 50% duties on other types remain looming. Mining executives warn tariffs won’t restore U.S. smelting and may strengthen China’s role.

title: A £115 clip-on power meter that claims "pro-level" accuracy is set to hit Kickstarter, plus Trek's "industry-first shift" to low-emission aluminium, a fancy new Chris King headset patent + more
summary: Trek says that from October nearly all its aluminium bike frames will use aluminium sourced from facilities powered by renewable energy and/or include recycled content, covering over 1 million bikes annually. Other items in the roundup (power meter, headset patent, saddle colour) are unrelated to industrial metals.

title: India plans tariff response to US over steel, aluminium levy
summary: India is preparing WTO-legal grounds to retaliate against US 50% duties imposed in June on steel and aluminium from India. The planned response targets selected US commodities, depending on trade negotiations after tariff escalation. Timing is near-term, but effects are mostly tariff-driven rather than immediate supply disruption.

title: India tariff news LIVE updates: India considers tariff response for US' steel, aluminium duty
summary: The article covers US tariffs of 50% on steel and aluminium (and derivatives) from India and India’s consideration of counter-tariffs in retaliation. It also notes the tariff dispute dynamics and lack of negotiations until resolution, implying tighter aluminium trade flows and potential upward pressure on aluminium prices.

title: Chile's Codelco gets regulatory approval to reopen part of El Teniente copper mine
summary: Codelco received Chile’s mining regulator approval to reopen approved sections of the El Teniente copper mine after a weeklong suspension following a fatal collapse. Final restart timing depends on labor inspection sign-off. The regulator said approved areas show no damage or imminent risk, while monitoring seismic activity.

title: In July, secondary copper rod plants still failed to reverse losses, and the operating rate pulled back as scheduled.
summary: July secondary copper rod operating rates remain low/declining amid weak demand from wire and cable buyers during the off-season and negative theoretical gross profits for refiners. Recycled scrap prices stayed firm versus copper, making raw-material procurement difficult. Smelters reduced spot procurement for anode plates, further limiting output; copper prices retreated.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Tomago Aluminium workers were told the smelter will likely close in 2028 unless it can secure affordable power. The plant rejected a renewables-based contract proposal after its current AGL supply deal ends in 2028. Government production credits and talks with stakeholders continue, as the project’s status remains uncertain.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Tomago Aluminium was told its smelter could close in 2028 if it cannot secure an affordable power contract after its AGL deal expires. It rejected a renewables-based supply quote as too expensive, warning previous price hikes added over $100 million to power bills. Government and credits discussions continue.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Newcastle Herald
summary: Tomago Aluminium, producing about 600,000 tonnes of aluminium, faces potential closure by 2028 if it can’t secure affordable energy for power beyond its AGL contract expiration. Workers say a recent renewables-based quote was rejected as too costly. Government production tax credits are intended to support smelters’ energy transition.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | The Advertiser - Cessnock
summary: Tomago Aluminium, a major Australian smelter producing about 600,000 tonnes, has been told it will close in 2028 unless it secures an affordable post-2028 renewable power contract. It rejected a renewables quote as too expensive. Government support is under discussion, keeping aluminium supply risk elevated.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | The Maitland Mercury
summary: Tomago Aluminium has been told it will close in 2028 if it cannot secure an affordable energy contract after AGL’s deal expires. It rejected a renewables-based power offer as too costly. Ongoing talks with government aim to secure production tax credits and power supply, but no agreement is reached.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Port Stephens Examiner
summary: Tomago Aluminium told workers it may close in 2028 unless an affordable renewables-based power contract is negotiated. The plant produces about 600,000 tonnes of aluminium and needs a steady 950 MW. A proposed post-2028 energy quote was rejected as too expensive, with government credits under discussion.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Camden Haven Courier
summary: Tomago Aluminium was told it will likely close in 2028 unless it secures an affordable power contract. A proposed renewables-based supply quote was rejected as too expensive, adding to concerns about high electricity costs. A $2 billion aluminium production-credit pledge is intended to support the energy transition.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | The Singleton Argus
summary: Tomago Aluminium was told it will close in 2028 unless it can negotiate an affordable energy contract beyond its expiring AGL deal. The plant rejected a renewables-based supply quote as unfeasible, warning high power prices threaten operations. Government talks and production credits aim to keep the smelter running.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Manning River Times
summary: Tomago Aluminium told workers it may close in 2028 unless it secures an affordable post-2028 energy contract. The smelter’s 600,000 tonnes output depends on continuous power and the latest renewable quote was rejected as too expensive. Government production tax credits and ongoing talks aim to keep operations running.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | The Macleay Argus
summary: Tomago Aluminium warned it could close in 2028 unless it reaches an affordable long-term energy deal for its large smelter. It rejected a renewables-based power quote and faces a contract ending in 2028. The Australian government is offering $2 billion in aluminium production tax credits as talks continue.

title: Tunnel collapse kills 6, leaves 9 injured at Chile's El Teniente copper mine
summary: A tunnel collapse killed six subcontract workers at Codelco’s El Teniente, disrupting underground copper production. The report says Chile’s mining regulator approved reopening part of the mine after the shutdown, amid concerns that delays would worsen tightening copper supplies and cost millions per day.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Port Macquarie News
summary: Tomago Aluminium told workers it may close as early as 2028 unless it can negotiate an affordable renewable-based power contract after its AGL supply agreement ends. The current operator rejected a renewables quote as too expensive, risking higher costs and potential downtime, while government credits are discussed.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Muswellbrook Chronicle
summary: Tomago Aluminium told smelter workers it may close in 2028 unless it can negotiate an affordable renewable-based power contract after its AGL deal expires. The company rejected a renewal quote as infeasible, citing high energy prices that could add over $100 million to bills, while government transition credits are discussed.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | Great Lakes Advocate
summary: Tomago Aluminium warns it may close in 2028 without an affordable post-2028 renewable power contract. The smelter relies on a large, steady power supply and has rejected a high renewables pricing offer. Government support via production tax credits is discussed, but no deal is reached.

title: Tomago Aluminium to close in 2028 without affordable energy deal | The Scone Advocate
summary: Tomago Aluminium told workers it likely will close in 2028 unless it can negotiate an affordable renewable power contract. It rejected an offer for post-2028 supply as too expensive, and high electricity prices are jeopardizing the plant. The smelter produces 600,000 tonnes annually, with government credits discussed.

title: Nickel king Indonesia relies on China's CATL for EV supply chain ambitions
summary: Indonesia’s EV battery ambition increasingly depends on Chinese firms such as CATL as other investors exit amid a slowing EV market and technology changes. The risk is that Indonesia’s large nickel reserves may not translate into an integrated battery supply chain, potentially reducing near-term expectations for nickel demand.

title: Govt expects investment in mines, export of refined copper to US - Pakistan
summary: Pakistan’s commerce minister says a US reciprocal tariff deal will be more favorable for exporting refined, value-added copper because refined copper is exempt from the earlier 50% tariff. He expects US interest to invest in Pakistan’s copper mining and processing, supported by regulatory and infrastructure upgrades.

title: Chile copper mine to restart operations after deadly collapse
summary: Chile’s El Teniente copper mine in the world’s largest underground copper system was ordered to halt work after a seismic event triggered a tunnel collapse that killed one miner and left five missing. Operations were suspended for over a week and are set to resume, tightening near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Alvance takes delivery of alumina powder tank wagons
summary: Alvance British Aluminium took delivery of 20 refurbished powder tank wagons to improve alumina transport from Blyth port to its Fort William smelter. The higher-payload wagons and upgraded loading facility aim to reduce journeys and support predictive maintenance, ensuring uninterrupted 24/7 smelting operations.

title: Capstone Copper sanctions Mantoverde Optimised project
summary: Capstone Copper sanctioned the MV Optimised sulphide concentrator expansion at the Mantoverde copper-gold mine in Chile. Throughput is set to rise from 32,000 to 45,000 tpd, with incremental copper production targeted and ramp-up in Q4 2026 and sustainability from early 2027. 2025 capex guidance increases.

title: How to Offset Trump's Aluminum Tariffs: Recycle Your Beer Can
summary: A report explains that Trump’s 50% aluminum import tariff has pushed U.S. aluminum prices to record premiums over the global LME price. It argues recycling and scrap supply can’t quickly replace lost imports, so higher costs will likely persist as stockpiles deplete and firms pass through expenses.

title: Grid Metals Corp. Announces Grassroots Nickel Sulfide Surface Discovery at Makwa
summary: Grid Metals announced a grassroots surface discovery of semi-massive nickel sulfide (“Pavo” anomaly) at its Makwa Ni-Cu-PGE project, with grab samples up to 1.1% nickel and plans for follow-up EM surveys and drilling in Fall 2025. The update is exploration-stage with no immediate supply effect.

title: Guinea nationalizes UAE bauxite mine amid regional push for resource sovereignty – Medafrica Times
summary: Guinea nationalized UAE-linked bauxite assets by terminating GAC/EGA’s Boké concession and transferring it to a state entity, citing legal violations including failure to build a promised refinery. The government also seized stockpiled bauxite and signaled new partner talks, disrupting expected bauxite supply continuity for aluminium markets.

title: Winshear Enters Option Agreement on the Portsoy Nickel –
summary: Winshear Gold signed an arms-length option agreement to earn 100% of the Portsoy Project in Scotland, targeting near-surface high-grade nickel–copper sulphide mineralisation. The plan includes TSX-V approval, a 1,000m drill program and metallurgical testwork. It’s an exploration milestone, not production.

title: Miner Freeport-McMoRan will benefit from Trump copper tariffs, says Morgan Stanley
summary: Morgan Stanley upgraded Freeport-McMoRan to overweight, arguing President Trump’s 50% copper import tariffs should benefit the miner. The note says the U.S. is a net importer of copper rod and Freeport can raise rod contract pricing for 2026, with the market underestimating tariff-driven benefits.

title: Why Copper Prices Just Soared to Record Highs and Then Crashed
summary: U.S. copper tariff expectations first surged prices, with Comex copper peaking July 25, then reversed after the White House watered down duties and exempted refined copper and some input materials. The change sparked a rapid sell-off, with Comex prices falling roughly 24.56% from the peak within days.

title: Solis Announces: Drilling Commenced at Ilo Este Copper Gold Project, Peru
summary: Solis Minerals announced that diamond drilling has started at its 100%-owned Ilo Este copper-gold project in Peru, targeting magnetic anomalies and follow-up of historical copper-gold intercepts. The initial ~5,000m program aims to test known mineralisation and new targets; results are pending and could influence copper sentiment.

title: Solis Minerals Ltd.: Solis Announces: Drilling Commenced at Ilo Este Copper Gold Project, Peru
summary: Solis Minerals began diamond drilling at its 100%-owned Ilo Este copper-gold project in southern Peru, targeting historical porphyry-style copper-gold mineralisation and new geophysical targets. The initial program covers about 5,000 metres. This is exploratory work and does not signal near-term production changes.

title: Copper output from Chile's Codelco climbs 17% in June
summary: Chile’s Codelco copper production rose 17% year-on-year to 120,200 tonnes in June, based on Cochilco data. Reuters also noted output declines at BHP’s Escondida (-33%) and Glencore/Anglo’s Collahuasi (-29%). The Codelco increase supports near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Aluminum orders down after 50pc tariff: Bonnell
summary: Bonnell Aluminum reported a 20% decline in US extrusion orders after Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum rose to 50% from 4 June. Customers paused orders to evaluate the higher tariff, while Bonnell implemented Q3 price increases to offset related cost increases. Lower extrusion demand drove the order fall.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Reports Second Quarter 2025 Financial Results
summary: Faraday Copper reported its Q2 2025 financial results and provided updates on the Copper Creek Project in Arizona, including BLM approval of its exploration plan, new near-surface copper assay results, and progress in metallurgical testing. The company plans further drilling and a near-term resource/PEA update later in Q3, with no production changes.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Market: Operating rate declined in July but better than expected, with a rebound expected in August
summary: SMM reports copper plate/sheet and strip operating rates at 65.63% in July, down MoM/YoY but above expectations, helped by a copper price pullback and stronger orders in new energy, power, and high-end electronics. August is expected to rebound to 66.92%, despite weak home appliance/PV demand and fierce brass strip competition.

title: Atalaya's first-half profit and revenue rise on higher copper output
summary: Atalaya Mining reported a sharp rise in H1 profit and revenue driven by higher copper production (27,466 tonnes vs 22,249 tonnes). It narrowed 2025 copper guidance to 49,000–52,000 tonnes and lowered cash cost and AISC outlook, ending June with higher net cash.

title: Lifezone Metals secures $60m bridge loan for Tanzania nickel project
summary: Lifezone Metals secured a $60m bridge loan to fund early-stage infrastructure work at its Kabanga nickel project in Tanzania, supporting progress from feasibility study completion toward final investment decision. The deal affects project development funding but provides no near-term supply or disruption signal. Nickel is mentioned most directly.

title: MMG Limited: MMG Announces 2025 Interim Results, Profit, Earnings and Cash up on Strong Copper Growth
summary: MMG reported a sharp rise in interim profit and cash flow, driven by higher copper output across its mines and stronger copper (and other metal) prices, alongside lower unit costs at Las Bambas. It also cited record payable copper sales. Nickel is referenced for an acquisition, with no immediate impact detailed.

title: MMG Announces 2025 Interim Results, Profit, Earnings and Cash up on Strong Copper Growth
summary: MMG reported 2025 interim results with a large jump in profit driven primarily by higher copper production across its mines and improved costs at Las Bambas amid stronger market prices for copper. It also references work to complete a Nickel Brazil acquisition, but no near-term nickel operating impact is specified.

title: Uncertainty Looms for U.S. Aluminum Trade Deals
summary: U.S. aluminum tariffs have lifted the Midwest premium to record highs, but investors are cautious as trade talks with key suppliers (especially Canada) remain unresolved. Any duty rollback could cut the premium substantially. Separately, aluminum demand is soft, with sluggish service-center buying and weaker ISM manufacturing conditions.

title: 12 Best Copper Stocks to Buy According to Hedge Funds
summary: The article claims Trump imposed 50% tariffs on copper, driving a 13% surge in CME copper September futures and prompting analysts (Bank of America, Citi) to expect a further U.S. price spike and reduced U.S.-bound shipments. It frames copper producers as beneficiaries due to higher realized revenues.

title: UC Rusal moves to recover alumina after Bog Walk Gorge train derailment
summary: UC Rusal is repairing damaged rail infrastructure in Bog Walk Gorge to retrieve derailed rail cars used for alumina extraction operations linked to its Windalco bauxite plant. The incident also caused a temporary gorge closure and power outages. Authorities ordered investigations and safety measures. Repairs may disrupt alumina supply logistics in coming days.

title: Track repairs ongoing after Windalco bauxite train derailed in St Catherine
summary: A bauxite train operated by Windalco derailed in St Catherine’s Bog Walk Gorge, prompting track and utility repairs and a temporary closure of the area. UC Rusal and JPS crews are restoring rail infrastructure so vehicles can extract alumina from submerged cars while investigations into the derailment continue.

title: Trump's aluminum tariffs impact Wisconsin Foundry
summary: A Wisconsin aluminum foundry says Trump’s 50% tariffs on imported aluminum are raising costs because it relies on imported primary aluminum as a key input. The higher tariff-driven price reduces demand, leading to layoffs and slower hiring, indicating near-term bearish pressure for aluminum markets.

title: Discovery of Copper Mineralization in 400 Metre Step-Out
summary: Imperial Metals reported discovery of significant new copper mineralization at its Mount Polley property from diamond drilling in a 400-metre step-out. Drill hole FP-25-01 returned 7.0 m grading 0.70% Cu and 20.0 m grading 0.25% Cu, with native copper highlighted. Drilling continues elsewhere; Mount Polley drilling is suspended for now.

title: Environmental risk from derailed bauxite train low - NEPA
summary: NEPA said its assessment of UC Rusal’s derailed bauxite train in Jamaica found low environmental risk: minimal alumina spillage confined near the embankment, no hazardous materials, no oil contamination, and no fish deaths. Cleanup is ongoing and investigations will determine the derailment’s cause and safety improvements.

title: Discovery of Copper Mineralization in 400 Metre Step-Out Drill Hole, Four Kilometres North of the Mount Polley Mill
summary: Imperial Metals says a step-out diamond drill hole north of its Mount Polley mill intercepted hydrothermal breccia with visible native copper. Results include 7.0 metres at 0.70% Cu and 20.0 metres at 0.25% Cu, indicating new copper mineralization, though no immediate production changes are announced.

title: Canadian Lifezone Metals secures $60mn bridge loan to advance Kabanga nickel project in Tanzania
summary: Lifezone Metals secured a $60mn senior bridge loan to fund early works and infrastructure at Tanzania’s Kabanga nickel project. The financing supports progress toward a mid-2026 FID, amid Lifezone’s consolidation of ownership. Development of a large planned nickel sulphide operation can lift expectations for future nickel supply.

title: Lessons learned from the nickel downstreaming policy - Markets
summary: Indonesia’s nickel downstreaming program has boosted exports, but the lack of a long-term plan has created a nickel ore supply shortage. The article notes that required demand based on capacity up to 2025 is 261.3 million tonnes, while the 2025 RKAB may be reduced from 270 to 150 million tonnes.

title: Rods are turning for Norfolk as big Chilean copper targets loom large
summary: Norfolk Metals is restarting drilling at its Carmen copper project in Chile, targeting shallow oxide copper for potential heap-leach cathode production and planning further oxide infill plus wildcats in sulphides. The piece highlights encouraging historical grades, recent funding, and copper price strength, but is largely project-level news.

title: Investee Company Update: Peak Nickel | Company Announcement
summary: Ormonde Mining reports that Peak Nickel Limited has entered an option agreement allowing Winshear to earn a 100% interest in the Portsoy nickel (Rodburn) project in Scotland by funding drilling and metallurgical testwork and issuing shares over five years. Ormonde notes the deal offers value without additional exploration exposure.

title: The operating rate of secondary aluminum producers rose in July and may pull back in August [SMM analysis]
summary: SMM survey data show secondary aluminium alloy producers’ operating rate rose to 42.2% in July, helped by stronger orders (e.g., NEVs, motorcycle parts) and aluminium futures-triggered buying of ADC12. For August, demand is weaker with off-season conditions and high-temperature holiday breaks, expected to pressure operating rates.

title: AriZona's iconic 99-cent price could end due to Trump aluminum tariffs
summary: AriZona’s founder says the brand’s 99-cent can price may rise for the first time in 30 years if proposed U.S. aluminum tariffs take effect. The company uses aluminum in its tallboys, with part imported from Canada that would face a 50% tariff, increasing costs and potentially supporting higher aluminum prices.

title: Japanese Trading Company Mitsubishi Buys 30% Stake in Hudbay Minerals' Arizona Copper Project
summary: Mitsubishi Corporation is buying a 30% stake in Hudbay Minerals’ Arizona Copper World copper project for $600 million, forming a long-term joint venture. The investment supports about $1.5 billion of U.S. critical minerals supply chain spending and targets roughly 85,000 tonnes of U.S. copper output annually over the next two decades.

title: Granite Creek Copper: Cascadia and Granite Creek Complete Business Combination
summary: Cascadia Minerals completed its acquisition of Granite Creek Copper, combining copper-gold exploration and development assets in Yukon. The company plans a fall drill program and ongoing prospecting while awaiting results from prior work. The release discusses copper resources and PEA pricing assumptions but no immediate supply or trade disruption.

title: Japan's Mitsubishi Corp. to invest $600m in US copper mine
summary: Mitsubishi Corp. plans to invest $600 million in a U.S. copper mining project, including a 30% stake in an Arizona copper asset, aiming to satisfy growing copper demand from electric vehicles and data centers. The move highlights continued supply-chain investment amid tariff-related shifts.

title: Presidential Proclamation On Adjusting Copper Imports Into The United States
summary: A U.S. presidential proclamation adjusts copper trade under Section 232, finding copper imports threaten national security. It orders a 50% tariff on semi-finished copper products and copper-intensive derivatives from Aug. 1, while keeping copper inputs and scrap outside the tariffs, and it directs further tariff-schedule reviews within 90 days.

title: Hudbay Minerals to sell 30 per cent stake in Arizona Copper World project to Mitsubishi
summary: Hudbay said Mitsubishi will buy a 30% stake in the Copper World Arizona project, committing US$600m and supporting U.S. critical-minerals goals. The news also references a White House move imposing a 50% tariff on imported semi-finished copper products, potentially tightening near-term domestic copper-intensive supply.

title: Hudbay Minerals sells Copper World stake, reports Q2 results, shares up
summary: Hudbay shares rose after selling a 30% stake in its Arizona Copper World project to Mitsubishi, which committed US$600 million and expects 85,000 tonnes/year of copper. The deal is linked to U.S. national security following a 50% tariff on imported semi-finished copper products, boosting bullish sentiment.

title: Wells Fargo Backs Teck Resources as Top Copper Play Despite Sector Caution
summary: Wells Fargo reiterated an Overweight rating on Teck Resources, citing strong liquidity and attractive risk/reward, with “valuable exposure” to long-term copper demand. Other brokers are more cautious due to operational challenges and softer near-term expectations. Overall, the note is supportive for Teck’s copper outlook and may buoy copper sentiment modestly.

title: Eagle Mine to use Allonnia's technology for nickel purification
summary: Eagle Mine will pilot Allonnia’s D-Solve mobile unit at its Michigan nickel site to reduce magnesium impurities in concentrate and improve nickel recovery. Eagle expects the trial to test performance and scalability under continuous onsite processing. A prior test showed lower impurities and higher nickel grade, supporting nickel supply quality prospects.

title: Chile's El Teniente copper mine resumes operations after fatal collapse
summary: Chile’s El Teniente mine partially resumed after a collapse triggered by a July 31 earthquake. The halt caused damaged tunnels and the closure costs are estimated at 800–900 metric tons of refined copper per day, with multi-month recovery and potential large overall losses, implying near-term copper supply tightness.

title: BHP Group Limited (BHP) Targets Incentives in Argentina for Vicuna Copper Project
summary: BHP, with Lundin, is reported to seek Argentina’s Large Investment Incentive Regime to back development of the Vicuna copper project. The scheme offers tax breaks and access to international dispute courts for large investments, which could support copper project timing and economics.

title: Southern Copper's (SCCO) Cost Reductions Payoff as Net Income Grows
summary: Southern Copper reported Q2 2025 net income up 2% despite 2% lower net sales, with sales pressured by lower copper prices. Cash costs fell 17% and operating costs dropped 3%, while production slipped slightly. The firm also approved projects to add 156,000 tons of copper capacity.

title: More drilling for copper underway at Batchawana Bay
summary: Sterling Metals has begun a second phase of drilling at its Soo Copper Project in Ontario’s Batchawana Bay area, planning 3,000–5,000 metres across four target areas. The firm highlights lower drilling costs and ongoing development after an initial phase earlier this year, but no near-term output is reported.

title: MAC Copper (MATL) Acquisition Gains Momentum with Key Regulatory Approval
summary: Harmony Gold’s proposed acquisition of MAC Copper gained regulatory approval from South Africa’s Reserve Bank, following transaction structuring under Jersey law. Shareholder approval, Australian FIRB clearance, court sanction, and streams-deed conditions remain. The deal targets copper-focused assets tied to electrification, but no near-term supply impact is specified.

title: Freeport-McMoRan's (FCX) Q2 Results Impress amid Copper Production Ramp-up
summary: Freeport-McMoRan reported stronger Q2 financials and copper output, and it started up a large-scale copper smelter in Indonesia. The company produced 963 million pounds of copper in the quarter and is on track to sell 1.3 billion pounds from U.S. operations, indicating improved near-term supply prospects.

title: Taseko Mines (TGB) Ramping Copper Production as Q2 Earnings Disappoint
summary: Taseko Mines says it is making progress on its Florence Copper project and continuing advancement at the Gibraltar Mine, with Florence production expected within six months. The company reported Q2 revenue and copper output (19.8 million pounds produced) while earnings disappointed versus expectations, but production ramp prospects are constructive for copper.

title: Ero Copper Corp. (ERO) Delivers Robust Earnings Growth on Operational Efficiencies
summary: Ero Copper reported Q2 results with higher production and improved operational efficiency, including 25% quarter-over-quarter increases at its Caraíba and Tacumã operations. Cash costs fell 7% to $2.07/lb due to maintenance and water management. Commercial production started at Tacumã on July 1.

title: Hudbay Minerals sells stake in Arizona copper mine to Mitsubishi
summary: Hudbay will sell a 30% stake in its Arizona Copper World project to Mitsubishi, which plans US$600 million of investment. The U.S. also imposed a 50% tariff on imported semi-finished copper products, boosting incentives for domestic copper supply. Copper World is expected to produce 85,000 tonnes annually.

title: Cardboard-wearing thief steals copper from Bonshaw build site | The Advocate - Hepburn
summary: A thief stole construction equipment including electrical copper wiring worth about $40,000 from a Bonshaw building site. Police also cite another break-in where about $4,000 of copper was taken, and a water outage caused by copper pipe theft. Copper scrap is described as valuable.

title: Mitsubishi Corporation to acquire shares in Copper World copper mine project in the US
summary: Mitsubishi Corporation agreed to buy a 30% interest in Hudbay’s Copper World copper mine project in Arizona for $600 million, including development-cost contributions. The project is permitted to start around 2029 with peak output near 100,000 tonnes/year. The deal supports bullish copper sentiment through committed supply investment.

title: Proposed expansion to Alcoa's bauxite mining in WA jarrah forrests could produce 1.3 billion tonnes of emissions

summary: Ontario launched a $1 billion loan program for firms affected by increased U.S. tariffs under Section 232, focusing on auto, steel and aluminum supply chains. summary: The article headline says the US imposed new 25% tariffs on steel and aluminium that are affecting UK businesses. For aluminium, the tariff is likely to change import demand and trade flows into the US, potentially tightening market supply and supporting near-term aluminium prices.

title: Trump Administration Expands Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs to 407 Additional Products | Baker Botts L.L.P.
summary: BIS added 407 HS codes covering steel and aluminum derivative products under U.S. Section 232 tariffs effective Aug. 18, applying the 50% rate to steel/aluminum content (25% for UK-origin) with no transit exemptions. The expansion increases tariff coverage and may reduce import flows, weighing on aluminium prices near term.

title: Court Puts The Brakes On Contested Land Transfer For Arizona Copper Mine
summary: An appeals court temporarily blocked the transfer of federal forest land in Arizona (Oak Flat) to companies planning to mine one of North America’s largest copper deposits. The injunction was granted after appeals by a Native American tribe and environmentalists. The delay is expected to affect job prospects and domestic copper access.

title: Nickel Glut Weighs on Stainless Steel Despite U.S. Tariff Support
summary: The piece says stainless mills received tariff support but demand remains weak at service centers. It emphasizes that nickel prices are still soft amid exceptionally high inventories and a global supply glut, with Indonesia’s strong output expected to face demand slowdown and some smelter idling. Overall, nickel recovery looks unlikely.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Mid-Year Review and Second-Half Outlook for Indonesia's Nickel Ore Market in 2025: Spotlight on Policy Developments and Macro Factors
summary: SMM reviews Indonesia’s 2025 nickel ore market, showing Q1 saprolite tightness and restocking supported prices, while Q2 diverged as royalties rose (PNBP nickel rate 10%→14%), lifting mining costs. Limonite demand weakened after a Morowali HPAL tailings accident, then recovered. 2H depends on RKAB revisions, weather, and HPAL/RKEF output changes, with volatility and limited upside.

title: New 25 per cent US tariffs on steel and aluminium hit UK business
summary: The news reports that new US tariffs of 25% on steel and aluminium have begun hitting UK businesses. Higher import costs and potential trade disruptions are expected to reduce near-term aluminium demand and pricing sentiment, creating downside pressure for aluminium markets over the coming days.

title: Star Copper Corp.: Star Copper Announces Completion of $4 Million LIFE Offering
summary: Star Copper Corp. announced completion of a C$4 million LIFE (flow-through) offering, selling FT units to fund Canadian flow-through critical mineral exploration expenditures at its Star Project. The release describes the terms and use of proceeds, with no changes to production or project output. Immediate price impact on copper appears limited.

title: U.S. appeals court stalls land transfer for Arizona copper mine
summary: An appeals court in the U.S. has temporarily stalled a land transfer tied to an Arizona copper mine. The legal delay could postpone mine development or operational approvals, raising the risk of slower copper supply progress in the near term and putting downward pressure on copper price expectations.

title: Trump Criticizes Court Decision to Block Major Arizona Copper Mine Land Transfer
summary: A federal appeals court temporarily blocked a congressionally mandated land exchange that would transfer control of land in Arizona’s Tonto National Forest to Rio Tinto and BHP for a major copper mine. Trump criticized the decision. The injunction adds near-term uncertainty over mine development, weighing on copper supply expectations.

title: Trump's expansion of steel and aluminum tariffs could raise these prices
summary: Trump expanded U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs by adding 400 products effective Monday, extending 50% levies on aluminum/steel-containing items. The Commerce Department said it blocks workarounds and supports domestic metals industries. Analysts expect some cost pass-through into consumer and producer prices, modest so far.

title: US backs Aust-led copper project despite tribe concerns
summary: Trump backs BHP and Rio Tinto’s joint push for the Resolution Copper project in Arizona, targeting a large domestic copper source. A Native American tribe and environmentalists secured a temporary injunction blocking a scheduled federal land transfer over Oak Flat. Trump warned delays would harm jobs and domestic copper access.

title: BHP boss secures meeting with Trump, advocating for biggest copper mine in North America
summary: BHP’s CEO met Trump to lobby for support for the Resolution Copper joint venture in Arizona, but a US appeals court issued a temporary order blocking transfer of the sacred Oak Flat site, delaying the project by about two months. BHP sees potential success later and cites cautious China demand optimism.

title: Prolonged Freeport smelter shutdown frees up scarce ore for copper market - Companies
summary: Freeport’s Manyar smelter in Gresik faces extended downtime after repairs to an oxygen plant, limiting intake of Grasberg copper concentrate. The unprocessed concentrate—about 100,000 tonnes—is offloaded/sold to the global market, providing short-term relief amid a shortage and affecting copper supply expectations for smelters.

title: Windtech International - US Commerce Department expands steel and aluminium tariffs to cover wind turbines
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department expanded steel and aluminium tariffs to add 407 product categories, including wind turbines and components. For covered items, 50% tariffs apply to the steel and aluminium content, while other materials face country-specific rates. The change took effect immediately after Federal Register publication.

title: How to Become Peru's Largest Copper Mine? Only by Mining for Progress [SMM Analysis]
summary: MMG’s interim 2025 report projects total copper production to rise to 520,000 tonnes, with Las Bambas expected to reach 400,000 tonnes and deliver 210,000 tonnes already in H1. The mine’s C1 costs are reported as low as $1.05/lb and ramp-ups/expansions elsewhere also continue.

title: Sandvik secures mining equipment order for copper mine in Botswana
summary: Sandvik won an order from JCHX to supply underground mining equipment and remote monitoring for MMG’s Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana. The deal is tied to ongoing underground operations and expansion work, but deliveries start Q3 2025, limiting near-term effects. Copper supply expectations are supported long-term.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Drills 0.46% CuEq Over 111 m from Surface at the South Zone; Confirms Continuity over 950 m of Strike Length
summary: Kodiak Copper reported first 2025 drill results from its MPD copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia, including multiple reverse-circulation intercepts with copper grades up to ~0.39% and long strike-length continuity. Results will be used for a mineral resource estimate later in 2025. The release is exploration-focused and not a near-term supply event.

title: Marimaca Copper Announces Option to Acquire 150ktpa
summary: Marimaca Copper says it has executed an option to acquire a used sulfuric acid plant in Chile with up to 150ktpa capacity to supply its Marimaca oxide deposit. The move aims to reduce volatile acid input costs and lower operating costs from 2028-2029, improving project economics rather than changing short-term supply.

title: Supreme Critical Metals Inc. Acquires An Option on the Silver Vista Silver-Copper Property, Smithers, BC, Announces Financing
summary: Supreme Critical Metals announced an option agreement to acquire a 100% interest in the Silver Vista silver-copper property in British Columbia. The project has reported copper grades up to 2.57% Cu from prior drilling and plans further permitting and drilling, with financing for exploration. No production or immediate supply impact is stated.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: SLAM IP Survey Expands Target Beneath Farquharson Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Zone At Goodwin
summary: SLAM reports new induced polarization (IP) survey results on its Goodwin claims in New Brunswick, suggesting potential extensions at depth of the Granges and Farquharson copper-nickel(-cobalt) zones. The company plans a 4,000m drilling program to test targets, with prior drill intervals reporting CuEq grades.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: SLAM IP Survey Expands Target Beneath Farquharson Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Zone At Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration reported IP survey results identifying chargeability targets beneath its Farquharson and Granges copper-nickel-cobalt zones and plans a ~4,000 m drilling program to test extensions at depth. While the work may influence expectations for future resources, it provides no immediate production or inventory impact.

title: Pacific Empire Minerals Corp.: Pacific Empire Retains Omineca Drilling for September Diamond Drill Program at Trident Copper-Gold Property
summary: Pacific Empire Minerals announced it retained Omineca Drilling for a ~2,500-metre diamond drill program at its Trident copper-gold property, with road clearing underway and a multi-year permit allowing drilling from multiple sites. The release is exploration-focused and does not signal near-term copper supply changes or trade disruptions.

title: Azimut and KGHM Resume Drilling on the Perseus High-Grade Nickel-PGE Discovery at Kukamas, James Bay Region, Quebec
summary: Azimut and KGHM have started a 4,000-metre diamond drilling program at the Kukamas property to expand the Perseus high-grade nickel-PGE zone (often >3% Ni) and test additional targets. The release discusses nickel-copper potential but provides no production, permitting, or inventory changes, implying limited short-term price pressure.

title: Barrick's Pakistan copper-gold project to get $410-million package from ADB, sources say
summary: The ADB plans to provide a $410 million package to support development of Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper mine operated by Barrick. The project is expected to begin copper production in 2028 (200,000 mt/year first phase, up to 400,000 mt/year later), with additional financing from other agencies discussed.

title: Customs details of China's copper foil for July 2025 Both imports and exports increased YoY and MoM [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s July 2025 copper foil imports rose 6% YoY and nearly 5% MoM, while exports also increased (13% YoY). The report attributes strength to rapid AI-related orders boosting demand for high-end copper foils and partial reliance on imports due to production barriers, supporting copper demand sentiment.

title: UK manufacturers face 25% US steel and aluminium tariffs
summary: The UK reports new US Section 232 tariffs extending a 25% duty on exports containing steel and aluminium, with 50% rates for some non-UK exporters and duties applying to goods already in transit. Compliance complexity may raise costs further, potentially affecting aluminium trade flows more directly than copper.

title: Glencore targets 1 million tons of copper in Argentina over coming decade
summary: Glencore said its planned El Pachon and Agua Rica copper projects in Argentina could reach close to 1 million tons annually over the next decade, following $4 billion and $9.5 billion investment applications under RIGI. Argentina currently produces no copper, with no output timeline provided, but the scale supports bullish copper sentiment.

title: U.S. Department of Commerce Announces That More Than 400 Products Containing Steel And Aluminum Will Now Be Subject To Section 232 Tariffs | Morris, Manning & Martin, LLP
summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce announced that over 400 products containing steel and aluminum will be subject to Section 232 tariffs. While focused on steel broadly, the inclusion of aluminum-containing products can reduce U.S. demand for imported aluminum and related downstream supplies, weighing on near-term aluminum prices.

title: Court stops sacred Oak Flat land transfer to Resolution Copper in emergency order
summary: An emergency court order halts the land transfer of Oak Flat for Resolution Copper. The stoppage increases uncertainty about progress and timing for a copper project, potentially delaying future supply. Such supply-development setbacks can weigh on copper sentiment in the near term, especially over the coming weeks.

title: Trafigura denies Gupta allegations it benefitted from nickel fraud scheme
summary: Trafigura denies allegations that it benefited from a nickel fraud scheme involving cargoes shipped as LME-grade nickel but reportedly containing worthless or unidentified materials. The dispute includes claims about boosting reported nickel holdings and trading/derivative activity. Proceedings are ongoing as the case heads toward a November trial.

title: Local contractors feel the impact of steel and aluminum tariffs
summary: The article says Trump tariffs on steel and aluminum are raising costs for contractors and consumers, with Home Depot also increasing some prices in response. Contractors report material-price uncertainty, especially where components are imported (e.g., steel). It suggests near-term upward pressure for construction inputs, including aluminum, though copper is not directly discussed.

title: US Adds Steel, Copper, Lithium To High-Priority List Under Uyghur Forced Labor Law
