summary: The DHS announced under the UFLPA that the US will add steel and copper to its high-priority import restriction list, alongside other products, and expand enforcement under the Forced Labor Prevention Act. Shipment blocking and denied-entry actions may reduce near-term copper (and related metal) supply from affected China-linked sources.

title: Trump backs huge Arizona copper mine as Apache win late reprieve to halt it
summary: The article headline says Trump is backing a major Arizona copper mine and that Apache won a late reprieve to halt the action. The implication is a change in near-term copper supply disruption risk, which would tend to support expectations for steadier output and help underpin copper prices.

title: 'ADB to provide $410m package to help develop Reko Diq copper mine'
summary: ADB has approved a $410m financing package for Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper-gold mine, including $300m in senior loans and a $110m partial credit guarantee. The project is expected to produce copper concentrate from late 2028, supporting expectations of future copper supply and improving market sentiment.

title: Trump Criticizes Court Decision To Block Major Arizona Copper Mine Land Transfer
summary: A federal appeals court temporarily blocks a congressionally mandated land exchange needed for Rio Tinto/BHP’s Resolution Copper mine in Arizona. Trump criticized the delay and highlighted copper import tariffs on semi-finished products and derivatives. The injunction preserves the status quo pending legal review, with potential near-term supply disruption.

title: Trump backs Arizona copper mine as Apache win lifeline in court
summary: Trump and Interior Secretary Burgum backed the Resolution Copper project after a court reprieve on transferring federal land for the Oak Flat copper mine. The administration argues the U.S. needs copper urgently and meets with BHP and Rio Tinto executives, while opponents continue to challenge the land swap.

title: Steel, aluminum tariffs take effect
summary: President Trump’s 50% tariff on steel and aluminum imports has started, making hundreds of categories containing steel or aluminum more expensive to bring into the U.S. Importers facing higher duties may pay more on in-transit goods or cancel shipments and take losses, tightening availability.

title: JCB warns US tariffs on steel and aluminium will cost it 'hundreds of millions of pounds'
summary: JCB says expanded US tariffs on steel and aluminium will cost it hundreds of millions of pounds and could force it to reconsider US trade. The 25% levy on UK metal exports and broader tariff coverage for finished goods raise compliance difficulty and likely dampen aluminium demand/imports in the near term.

title: Copper tariffs could benefit Northwestern BC
summary: The piece discusses U.S. Trump tariffs, focusing on Northwestern BC. It claims copper exports remain viable because unrefined copper goes to China and returns refined, avoiding tariff impact. It also argues tariffs spotlight global copper shortages, supporting expectations for substantially higher copper prices despite the trade measures.

title: Donald Trump's mining dream cops reality check in Rio Tinto, BHP copper saga
summary: The article says Trump met executives from Rio Tinto and BHP in the Oval Office, aiming to coincide with the transfer of Arizona public land to the companies. The land transfer is described as a major milestone toward getting a large copper mine up and running, potentially boosting near-term copper project confidence.

title: ADB approves financing for Pakistan's Reko Diq copper-gold mine-Xinhua
summary: The Asian Development Bank approved up to $410 million in financing for Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper-gold mine, including senior loans and a partial credit guarantee for equity support by Balochistan. The project is expected to become a major copper producer, potentially improving confidence in future copper supply.

title: The nickel dilemma: A false binary between geopolitical power and a just transition  - Academia
summary: The piece argues Indonesia should act to support a nickel-based EV battery supply chain, noting it is the world’s top nickel producer and that nickel-processed exports are a growing share of earnings. It highlights US tariff package negotiations and Trump comments about access to the Indonesian nickel market, implying near-term demand sensitivity.

title: ADB approves $410m financing for Reko Diq copper-gold mining project
summary: The Asian Development Bank approved $410m in financing for Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper-gold mine, including senior loans and a partial credit guarantee aimed at leveraging private capital. The project is expected to become a major future copper producer, supporting positive sentiment for copper markets.

title: U.S. Greatly Expands Section 232 Steel And Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The U.S. expanded Section 232 tariffs, applying a 50% ad valorem duty on hundreds of additional imported goods effective Aug. 18, 2025. Tariffs specifically apply to the steel and aluminum content within those products, increasing import costs and likely tightening supply, supporting aluminum prices near term.

title: July China's Imports of EQ Copper Cathode Exceed 70% Again!
summary: China imported 296,900 mt of copper cathode in July, slightly lower month-on-month but higher year-on-year, with non-registered sources again exceeding 70% of imports. DRC inflows hit a July peak despite tighter shipping capacity, while August scrap-related demand narrowed price gaps and US tariffs affected refined copper expectations.

title: [SMM Nickel Analysis] The nickel intermediate product market is tight, with the overall payable strengthening.
summary: SMM reports tightness in the nickel intermediate product market, with strengthening payables and rising MHP prices this week as supply remains constrained and refined producers actively procure. High-grade nickel matte is weaker on low downstream acceptance, while rising Indonesian sulfur prices support nickel input costs, underpinning broader nickel price support.

title: ADB approves 410 mln USD financing package for Pakistan's copper-gold mine-Xinhua
summary: ADB approved a $410 million financing package for Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper-gold mine. The project aims to support critical-minerals supply and development, with copper concentrate production starting in late 2028. While it supports longer-term supply expectations and investment sentiment, it is unlikely to move copper prices in the next few weeks.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Provides Update on Geophysical Program at Eaglehead Porphyry Copper Project
summary: Copper Fox reports completion of a 3D DCIP geophysical survey at its Eaglehead porphyry copper project, expanding anomalous chargeability zones linked to mapped copper mineralization. The company plans to merge 2014–2025 geophysical data to refine drill targets and potential mineralized envelopes, with no immediate production impact described.

title: Canada's Aldebaran plans $1.5 billion capex for Argentina copper project
summary: Aldebaran Resources said it needs at least $1.5 billion capex to develop its Altar copper project in northern Argentina. The company will include the figure in a September preliminary economic assessment, with two copper production scenarios. It is uncertain whether project funding qualifies for Argentina’s RIGI incentives.

title: CMOC Posts Record H1 2025 Net Profit of USD 1.21 Billion, Driven by Strong Copper Performance
summary: CMOC reported record H1 2025 net profit of USD 1.21 billion, with copper driving results. Copper mining revenue rose to USD 3.59 billion and production reached 353,570 tonnes, with strong output from TFM and KFM in the DRC. The company also highlighted ongoing expansion and power project progress.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Aug 22
summary: SMM’s weekly review shows a slight decline in Indonesian nickel ore reference prices, with premiums and delivered prices largely stable. RKAB quota progress and abundant ore supply keep ore fundamentals soft, while NPI rises on firm costs but end-user stainless demand is weaker, capping upside and limiting gains next week.

title: US Commerce Adds 428 HTS Codes to Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariff List | ArentFox Schiff
summary: The US Commerce Department expanded Section 232 to add 428 steel/aluminium derivative HTS codes, effective Aug. 18, covering downstream products like fasteners, wire and tubular components. The duties increase costs for imported aluminium-containing derivatives with limited mitigation via FTZs, likely weighing on near-term aluminium and some copper-linked demand.

title: Kinetic Offers $10,000 Reward for Information Leading to Arrests for Copper Thefts
summary: Kinetic, a fiber internet provider, is offering a $10,000 reward for information leading to arrests over theft or vandalism of its copper and fiber infrastructure in North Carolina. The company cites multiple cable-cut incidents since Aug. 10 disrupting 911 access and services, but provides no direct data on copper market volumes.

title: Falcon Copper Corp. Projects Added to FAST-41 Transparency Dashboard
summary: Falcon Copper announced its Blue Copper and Schell Creek projects were added to the Federal FAST-41 Transparency Dashboard, aimed at accelerating federal permitting for critical minerals development. The projects target copper among other minerals, but the release provides no near-term production changes, making likely copper price impact limited.

title: Antofagasta Reports Strongest Profit Margins Since 2021 with Higher Copper Output and Rising Metal Prices
summary: Antofagasta reported its highest profit margins since 2021, citing an 11% rise in copper output and lower operating costs alongside stronger copper pricing. Copper sales increased 17% to reflect both higher volumes and market prices. The company also declared a larger interim dividend, highlighting copper’s ongoing price support.

title: Section 232 Tariff Developments: Hundreds of Steel and Aluminum Derivatives Added and Pharmaceutical and Semiconductor Tariffs Are Expected | Baker Donelson
summary: Commerce expanded Section 232 tariffs by adding 407 new HTS codes, covering many goods with embedded aluminum. The aluminum portion of covered products faces a 50% duty effective immediately for consumption entries. Importers must adjust customs reporting and supplier valuations, potentially tightening aluminum availability and supporting prices.

title: Canada eases trade tensions with US -- maintains tariffs on autos, steel, and aluminum
summary: Canada will remove most retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods covered under USMCA but will retain 25% tariffs on autos, steel, and aluminum. The change is seen as easing uncertainty for Michigan’s auto sector, yet aluminum remains tariffed, potentially affecting aluminum supply expectations into September.

title: Mark Carney announces Canada will restore free trade with the U.S., while targeting steel, aluminum, autos for ongoing talks
summary: Canada and the U.S. will restore free trade for most goods under CUSMA, removing tariffs on U.S. covered products from Sept. 1. However, Canada will keep targeted tariffs on steel, aluminum and autos during ongoing talks. The approach aims to preserve competitiveness while negotiations proceed and an industrial strategy is planned.

title: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Announces Second Quarter 2025 Financial Results
summary: Kaiser Aluminum reported solid Q2 2025 results with higher realized prices across its segments and 288.4 million pounds shipped. The company raised its full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA estimate, citing favorable metal pricing and strong operational fundamentals. This supports a short-term bullish read-through for aluminum prices.

title: Introducing the Offshore Refined Copper Spot Market Sentiment Index
summary: The article introduces SMM’s Offshore Refined Copper Spot Market Sentiment Index, updated daily and built from spot volume, quotation activity, and buy-sell willingness. It notes rising intraday volatility in offshore copper spot trading and frames the index as a tool to guide procurement and sales decisions, not as a new market shock.

title: Global Copper Market Tightens Further Despite Tariff Shock and Inventory Surge
summary: Despite a tariff shock that exempted copper cathodes, US refined copper inventories have surged to a 21-year high after front-loaded imports. LME Asian inventories have also built and nearby spreads have weakened since June 2025, easing prompt tightness. Demand growth and a deficit persist, but near-term sentiment is cautious and volatility elevated.

title: China's Refined Copper Imports Slip Slightly in July While Exports Surge Beyond Expectations
summary: China’s refined copper imports slipped slightly in July while exports jumped sharply. Inflows exceeded expectations, including via de-registered Russian copper and shipments after Ilo smelter maintenance. A 50% US tariff on semi-finished copper ends LME/COMEX arbitrage, but improving relative pricing and a likely August import window reopening support bullish copper sentiment.

title: SMM Unveils Offshore Refined Copper Spot Market Sentiment Index
summary: SMM introduced an Offshore Refined Copper Spot Market Sentiment Index, updated daily, using a multi-factor model based on spot trading volume, quotation activity, and buy-sell willingness. The index aims to signal abnormal fluctuations and guide procurement and sales decisions. It is informational, not a reported supply or demand change.

title: Lanjigarh MLA bats for opening bauxite mines in Kalahandi
summary: A local MLA in Odisha backed protests calling for the immediate opening of bauxite mines in Kalahandi. The article notes India still imports large volumes of bauxite despite sizable reserves, implying potential future domestic supply. If realized, more bauxite availability would support alumina and aluminium markets near term.

title: American West pushes PFS work on near-term Canadian copper project
summary: American West Metals is accelerating pre-feasibility work for its near-term Storm copper project in Nunavut. Recent geotechnical drilling intersected thick visible copper sulphide zones beyond current resources, with assays expected in 2–3 weeks. Progress on permitting and metallurgical tests supports potential development expansion, boosting copper sentiment.

title: Additional Steel And Aluminum Derivative Products Included On Section 232 Steel And Aluminum Tariff List
summary: A BIS Federal Register notice adds 407 HTS codes to the Section 232 list of steel and aluminum derivative products subject to a 50% tariff on the steel/aluminum content. The change starts immediately, with exemptions for certain US-melted/smelted inputs. A new request window opens Sept. 1.

title: New Serbian mineralised zone rakes in 6.8% copper for Strickland
summary: Strickland Metals announced new diamond-drill results from Serbia’s Shanac deposit, including a 1.7m interval grading 6.8% copper and additional copper-gold zones at depth. The discovery improves perceived future copper resource potential for its Rogozna project, which can modestly support copper sentiment over coming weeks.

title: July alumina exports to Russia exceeded 200,000 mt, with a small net export pattern expected to be maintained in August.
summary: China exported 229,400 mt of alumina in July, with Russia taking 88.3% of shipments and volumes exceeding 200,000 mt (five-year high). For August, the export window is expected to stay closed and imports only partially offset exports, keeping alumina net exports negative, potentially tightening feedstock.

title: Evergold to acquire 100% interest in Copper King prospects in Canada
summary: Evergold signed an option agreement to acquire full interest in the Copper King copper prospects in British Columbia, Canada, covering four inlier claim groups. The property has prior reports of significant copper mineralisation and sampling results, but it is exploration-stage and subject to approvals, with no immediate output or supply change.

title: How a gamble in Texas paid off for this Chinese copper company
summary: A Chinese copper company, Wellascent, built a Texas factory to produce copper flat wire for U.S. clients. Local production shields buyers from 50% tariffs on imported copper wire, and demand is described as hot. The firm plans to scale output later this year, boosting copper-related supply expectations.

title: The U.S. could add copper to its critical minerals list
summary: The U.S. proposed adding copper to its 2025 critical minerals draft list. Inclusion could make copper projects eligible for federal funding, streamlined permitting, and potentially stronger competitiveness via import-related fees. The U.S. links copper to defense and power grid needs, aiming to reduce import dependence.

title: Chile regulator ups requirements to restart areas affected by copper mine collapse, document shows
summary: Chile’s mining regulator Sernageomin is raising requirements for Codelco to restart areas of the El Teniente copper mine after a July 31 collapse. The regulator will demand additional follow-up and monitoring plans across underground deposits not yet reopened. Codelco has reopened some sectors but keeps others closed and reduced its copper forecast.

title: Copper hopeful Cyprium Metals preps $60m cash call
summary: Cyprium Metals is preparing a $60m underwritten equity placement to restart its Western Australia copper mine and bolster its balance sheet. The term sheet names Tribeca as lead manager and other banks as advisers/co-managers. The fundraising is intended to support renewed copper production prospects.

title: Water rights transfer denied for reopening of a copper mine
summary: New Mexico denied a water-rights transfer required to reopen the Copper Flat Mine near Hillsboro, closed since 1982. The decision cites risks to future water supply and public welfare, including obligations with Texas. The denial likely prevents a restart, reducing near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Southern Hemisphere-FMR JV to drill big Chilean copper-gold targets
summary: Southern Hemisphere and FMR Resources have finalised a 4,000-metre phase-one drilling program at Chile’s Llahuin project to test undrilled copper-gold porphyry targets. The campaign starts late September with directional drilling and lab results expected weeks after each hole, potentially clarifying the system’s size and economic potential.

title: US Proposes Adding Copper, Potash, 4 Others to Critical Minerals List
summary: The US Interior Department proposes adding six minerals, including copper, to the national critical minerals list. The move is aimed at incentivizing domestic production and processing of strategic materials. The list will be formally posted in the Federal Register on Aug. 26, potentially boosting near-term copper sentiment.

title: Policy "Black Hole" Swallows 30% of Production! Secondary Copper Rod Industry Faces Major Transformation
summary: A policy notice standardizing investment incentives and implementing reverse invoicing changes the VAT/refund economics for scrap-based copper smelting and refining. Secondary copper rod and scrap anode plate producers in some provinces halt or cut output, reducing August supply. SMM expects higher copper cathode consumption in September, supporting copper demand sentiment.

title: Kincora Copper: Positive Drilling Results at Two Northern Junee-Narromine Belt Projects
summary: Kincora Copper reported positive early drilling at its Nevertire and Nevertire South projects in NSW, including encouraging anomalous copper mineralisation and favorable alteration/veining consistent with porphyry Cu-Au settings. Assays are pending, and follow-up geophysics and drilling are planned with partner AngloGold Ashanti.

title: First Quantum Decides to Keep Its Stakes in Zambian Copper Mines
summary: First Quantum Minerals will keep its full stakes in Zambia’s Sentinel and 80%-owned Kansanshi copper mines after dropping plans to sell minority interests. It raised $1 billion via a Royal Gold streaming deal on Kansanshi gold by-product output. Cobre mine exports resumed in Panama, but production remains halted.

title: Mavunde launches first 30bn/- Nickel, Copper plant project
summary: Tanzania’s minister laid the foundation for a USD 15m nickel and copper refining and processing plant in Dodoma, built by Zhongzhou Mining. The plant will need over 280,000 tonnes of raw material annually and is expected to start operations in Oct-Nov, boosting local processing demand for nickel and copper feedstock.

title: Mavunde launches first 30bn/- Nickel, Copper plant project
summary: Tanzania’s Minerals Minister laid the foundation for Zhongzhou Mining’s first nickel and copper refining and processing plant in Dodoma, valued at over USD 15 million. The plant is set to start operations between October and November, requiring over 280,000 tonnes of raw material annually and creating jobs, with demand expected to support local mining supply.

title: Solis Minerals Ltd.: Solis Announces: Extensive Copper Mineralisation Observed at Ilo Este
summary: Solis Minerals reported its first drill hole at the Ilo Este project intersected long porphyry-style mineralisation with copper (and molybdenum) observed visually. Four mineralised zones totalling ~350 metres are described, but laboratory assay results are expected in September 2025. No production or shipment impacts are mentioned.

title: Following Investigation of Copper Imports, Trump Administration Takes Actions Targeting Imports and Domestic Sales | Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman LLP
summary: Trump issued a Section 232 proclamation targeting copper imports with a 50% tariff on the copper content of semi-finished and derivative copper products, and ordered DPA-linked domestic sales requirements to preserve feedstock for U.S. producers. DHS added copper to UFLPA enforcement priorities, raising detention risk for Xinjiang-linked copper.

title: High-grade copper discovered in a promising new mineralized zone
summary: Camino Minerals reports trench/channel sampling at its Los Chapitos project in Peru uncovered a high-grade Mirador copper zone with strong copper-silver results (including intervals above 3% Cu) and bornite showings. The company plans further sampling and drilling in 2025, boosting copper exploration sentiment despite early-stage status.

title: [SMM Announcement] Adjustment to Weight Coefficient of Nickel Sulphate Price Index
summary: SMM said it will adjust the weight coefficient methodology for its battery-grade nickel sulphate price index, revising enterprise sample weights based on updated capacity distribution, spot vs long-term contract structure, and quotation accuracy. The revised weighting scheme takes effect August 26, 2025.

title: Are You Ready for $144 Silver and $9.00 Copper?
summary: The piece argues that adding silver to the U.S. critical minerals list is bullish because it can boost official demand via strategic stockpiling, subsidies, and faster purchasing ahead of policy implementation. It also notes copper was recommended for inclusion, implying a potentially supportive demand narrative for copper despite limited direct copper-specific details.

title: Hayasa Metals Inc.: Hayasa Metals Announces Option Agreement on Vardenis Copper-Gold Project
summary: Hayasa Metals announced an amended option/joint venture agreement for its Vardenis copper-gold project in Armenia, granting Teck a sole option up to 80% with funding obligations and specified exploration spending and drilling milestones. Teck would fund costs during the option period, supporting development expectations for copper.

title: Aterian eyes copper and silver potential at new Botswana licences
summary: Aterian PLC said two of three new Botswana prospecting licences show strong prospectivity for copper (and silver), citing historical world-class deposits in the D’Kar and Ngwaka formations. The company secured licences in August and is beginning further exploration planning. The update is exploration-stage and likely limited for near-term copper prices.

title: Maaden signs solar power deal for Al Baitha Bauxite Mine - Technical Review Middle East
summary: Maaden Bauxite and Alumina Company signed a long-term PPA with Emerge to build an 8 MWp solar plant plus 30 MWh battery for the Al Baitha bauxite mine. The system is designed to supply round-the-clock renewable power for decades, reducing emissions and improving sustainable operations. Focus is decarbonisation rather than volume output.

title: The future is at stake: How many years of copper reserves are left to power our technology?
summary: The article discusses global copper reserve depletion estimates and warns that copper shortages could trigger supply shocks, disruption to construction and technology, and “drastic” copper price spikes driven by supply-demand imbalance. It also suggests recycling expansion and wider aluminium use as partial substitutes during a copper-constrained period.

title: Lincoln police investigating copper wire theft from Cargill
summary: Lincoln police are investigating the theft of roughly $50,000 in copper wire from a construction site tied to Cargill. Authorities are still seeking information and suspects. The report is local and does not indicate any disruption to regional supply chains or trading markets for copper.

title: LPD: $50,000 of copper wire stolen from north Lincoln construction site
summary: Police are investigating an ongoing theft of copper wire from a construction site in north Lincoln, Nebraska. Officers say someone has been entering silos and stealing copper wire, with estimated losses of about $50,000. Investigators found fence and door damage; the case remains under investigation.

title: FPX Nickel Corp. Completes Drilling Programs In B.C. - Canadian Manufacturing
summary: FPX Nickel Corp. reports completion of the 2025 drilling program at its Baptiste Nickel Project in central British Columbia. Work supports feasibility study engineering and the environmental assessment process, including geomechanical, hydrogeological, and condemnation drilling, plus ongoing baseline studies. No near-term production or supply impact is specified.

title: Australia's South32 posts 75% rise in annual profit on alumina operations strength
summary: South32 reported a 75% jump in full-year profit, driven by stronger alumina operations and higher commodity prices. The firm said its aluminium division benefited from higher metal prices amid supply constraints and rising costs. It also discussed future production ramp-ups and a planned Mozal smelter care-and-maintenance date.

title: Danantara joins Vale, GEM for $1.42b nickel project - Companies
summary: Danantara signed a head of agreement with GEM to jointly develop a US$1.42bn HPAL smelting facility in Indonesia’s Morowali nickel hub, targeting 66,000 tonnes per year of nickel in mixed hydroxide precipitate. The project supports Indonesia’s EV downstream push alongside GEM’s Vale collaboration.

title: Vietnam Aluminum Powder Import Research Report 2025
summary: ResearchAndMarkets adds a report on Vietnam’s aluminum powder imports. It notes Vietnam’s mid-to-high-end aluminum powder demand is met largely through imports (US$5.25m in 2024), with China and Japan as major suppliers, and expects continued demand growth from construction, metallurgy, electronics, and new energy applications.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Completes Preliminary Geometallurgical Model on Van Dyke ISCR Copper Project
summary: Copper Fox reported completion of a preliminary geometallurgical model for its Van Dyke in-situ copper recovery project in Arizona, identifying mineralogical domains and metallurgical data gaps and recommending further leach testwork to support prefeasibility. The release does not indicate imminent production or supply changes, so near-term price impact is limited.

title: Multiple Regions Initiate Cleanup of Irregular Tax Rebates, Secondary Aluminum Market Hit Again [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s regulators are driving cleanup of irregular tax rebates, requiring termination of non-compliant exemptions and rebate-related clauses for some secondary aluminum projects. Anhui and Jiangxi see notices and suspended refunds, leading to production disruption. Aluminum scrap prices face pressure, while finished alloy ingot prices are supported, limiting downside from off-season demand.

title: Secondary Aluminum Market Remains Strong in Short Term Focus on Demand Recovery and Policy Implementation[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Weekly review notes tight aluminum scrap supply (especially shredded/tense) and fluctuating but higher SMM A00 prices. Cost pressure from rising scrap and aluminum input prices, plus tax-rebate policy uncertainty, is pushing ADC12 and related secondary aluminum alloy prices upward. Demand recovery is only mild; inventory is building.

title: Troilus enters copper-gold offtake agreement with Aurubis
summary: Troilus Gold signed a memorandum with Aurubis for long-term offtake of copper-gold concentrate from the Troilus Project in Québec. The MoA formalizes earlier indicative terms, covering a significant portion of planned concentrate output as the project advances toward financing and construction.

title: Koryx Copper Announces Further Drill Assay Results Extending Consistent Mineralization At Depth and Laterally At the Haib Copper Project, Southern Namibia
summary: Koryx Copper reported assay results from seven drill holes at its Haib copper project in southern Namibia, extending mineralization depth and lateral continuity. The company is re-logging core for geo-metallurgical modeling and plans to publish a September 2025 PEA based on an older resource, excluding recent drilling.

title: APO Group - Africa Newsroom  / Press release | Mercuria Strengthens African Presence Through Zambia Copper JV, African Energy Week (AEW) 2025 Bronze Partnership
summary: Mercuria partnered with Zambia’s IDC to form a 50:50 joint venture, Industrial Resources, focused on copper concentrate trading. With concentrate volumes secured and the first shipment underway, the state will gain direct copper marketing participation. The firm highlights rising smelter demand and record-low TCs/RCs, supporting copper economics.

title: Inside China's Zambian copper mine disaster – Channel 4 News
summary: Channel 4 reports on a copper mine disaster in Zambia where a toxic chemical spill entered a river used by millions. The story cites an independent report alleging the government and industry suppressed the accident’s true scale at a Chinese-owned mine, raising concerns over environmental and production impacts.

title: Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum Drive Up Commercial Real Estate Con
summary: The piece explains that rising US tariffs on imported steel and aluminum (25% then 50%, plus more tariffed product categories) lift construction input costs. Higher project costs can increase rents and delay investment, supporting near-term aluminum price sentiment. It also notes downstream effects on other metal components used in buildings.

title: Maritime authorities have detained 13 ships serving Limerick's Aughinish Alumina plant in five years – The Irish Times
summary: Irish maritime authorities detained 13 ships serving Aughinish Alumina, a major European aluminium refinery. Detentions were due to safety/crew-training deficiencies. The vessels were released after a few days to proceed to repairs. The plant is owned by Rusal and reportedly remains off international sanctions, limiting clearer immediate supply impacts.

title: Trade Policy Update: 407 New Products Added To Steel And Aluminum Tariff List
summary: The U.S. BIS expanded the Section 232 steel and aluminum tariff schedule by adding 407 HTS codes, with 50% duties applying to the aluminum content of covered imports. The update broadens the range of tariffed goods and signals tighter near-term aluminum supply for U.S. buyers, supporting prices.

title: South32 annual profit surges on alumina operations strength, higher prices
summary: The article headline says South32’s annual profit surged, attributed to strength in its alumina operations and higher prices. Stronger alumina performance can improve refining economics and supply expectations for aluminium-linked chains, which may support near-term aluminium price sentiment.

title: MEED | EGA starts nuclear-powered aluminium production
summary: MEED reports that Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) has started producing aluminium using nuclear power. The shift implies a change in electricity sourcing and potentially production economics versus conventional energy supplies. If output costs fall or supply becomes steadier, near-term sentiment for aluminium could turn supportive, though details are not provided here.

title: DNR investigating copper release from a broken pipe in Garner, Iowa
summary: Iowa DNR is investigating a copper release after a broken pipe at the Zinpro facility in Garner, Iowa. About 700 gallons of copper-containing liquid spilled into a storm drain and drainage ditch. Cleanup and damming are in place, and residents are warned to avoid contact with the water due to confirmed dead fish.

title: Brazil's aluminium market faces rising competition amid US tariffs
summary: Brazil’s aluminium market faces more foreign competition as US tariffs potentially redirect global supply toward Brazil. Import volumes have risen and traders say Vedanta and possibly Rusal increased sales. Fastmarkets assessed aluminium billet/extrusion premiums in Brazil falling or shifting since the March 12 tariff start, pressuring local prices downward.

title: Zambia's Copper-Fueled Stock Market Soars, Topping African Peers and Major Global Indexes
summary: Zambia’s LuSE surged on gains tied to elevated copper prices, with the article noting copper is 39% above its three-year average. It highlights major copper-linked firms’ soaring valuations and warns that copper falling below $8,200/ton would stall earnings growth, reinforcing a near-term bullish copper backdrop.

title: The End of Cheap Nickel: Reserves are running out and the cost of technology could skyrocket.
summary: The article argues nickel is nearing supply constraints, citing USGS reserve figures and showing a simplified depletion projection under a hypothetical Australia–Brazil-only supply scenario. It stresses that shortages would likely lift nickel prices, making previously uneconomic production and recycling more attractive, supporting bullish near-term expectations for nickel.

title: Aluminum Billet Inventory in August: Supply-Side Pressure Resurfaces, Peak Season Demand Yet to Arrive, Aluminum Billet Processing Fees Lack Support [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports Chinese aluminum billet inventory rose to 134,000 mt by Aug 28 as mid/late-Aug arrivals increased after producers resumed output. Demand has not entered peak season; downstream orders remain mixed, with real-estate weakness limiting recovery. With more supply expected in September and consumption likely stable, inventories may rebound to 140,000–150,000 mt.

title: Copper Finds Its Footing as Market Sentiment Improves | Live Wire
summary: Copper rebounded more than 1% to around $4.61/lb as market sentiment improved. Traders cited better manufacturing outlook, softer U.S.–China trade rhetoric, and relief from U.S. copper import tariffs after a cathode carve-out. Ongoing African mining delays and limited inventory recovery kept some downward pressure.

title: The PMI for Primary Aluminum Alloy Remained High in August, Exports of Aluminum Wheels Continued to Grow During the Overseas Peak Season [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says China’s primary aluminum alloy PMI stayed high in August (59.4%), with elevated production and new orders and a rising operating rate. It also notes continued growth in aluminum wheel hub exports as overseas peak season approaches, with improving trade conditions and resilient volumes, pointing to supportive near-term aluminum demand.

title: China's Imported Copper Market Active in August, Yangshan Premium Rebounds as Bonded Stocks Decline
summary: August saw firmer China imported copper pricing, with Yangshan premiums rebounding and TC/BL and EQ CIF premiums rising. Gains were attributed to higher LME inventories widening contango (supporting arbitrage), stronger-than-expected July exports, and expected September refined supply contraction. Bonded stocks fell, indicating demand resilience and supporting higher premiums.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Reports Temporary Production Interruption at Mantoverde Operation
summary: Capstone Copper says its Mantoverde Chile operation faces a four-week production interruption after failures of both ball mill electrical drive motors, with repairs expected to take about one month. The mine will run at roughly half capacity by bypassing the ball mill, with 3,000–4,000 tonnes of copper-in-concentrate impacted.

title: The Monthly Average Price of Alumina Is Expected to Decline, and China's Aluminum Cost Is Projected to Drop Back Slightly in September
summary: SMM data show China’s aluminum industry cost in August was influenced by higher alumina prices, though YoY costs fell. For September, SMM expects alumina to remain surplus-like with declining prices, lowering tax-inclusive full costs to 16,100–16,400 yuan/mt, despite higher auxiliary and electricity costs.

title: NZ-AU: Definitive Feasibility Study Results and Reserves Upgrade Confirms Minim Martap as a Tier-One Bauxite Operation
summary: Canyon’s DFS for the Minim Martap bauxite project in Cameroon increases ore reserves by 33% to 144Mt at 51.2% Al2O3 and low silica, with first production planned Q1 2026 and first shipment in H1 2026. Staged expansion targets up to 10Mtpa and cites strong project economics, supporting future alumina feed availability.

title: Chile's Mine Production Declined, Copper Prices Edged Lower Overnight [SMM Copper Morning Meeting Minutes]
summary: Chile’s central bank reported July mining shrank 3.3% YoY, with declines in copper production weighing on the world’s largest copper supply source. The market also notes weak downstream demand from high prices and ample supply, while inventories are only partly supportive. Copper futures/spot edged lower overnight.

title: Core Nickel Corp.: Core Nickel Announces Results from Property-Wide Airborne Electromagnetic Survey on the Mel and Odei River Projects and Provides Management Update
summary: Core Nickel reports successful airborne electromagnetic surveys covering its Mel, Hunter, and Odei River nickel projects, identifying drill targets and confirming correlations between geophysical responses and nickel sulphide mineralization. It also notes a management change (VP Exploration resignation). The release is exploration-focused, with no near-term production impact.

title: Middle Island share price soars on Serbian copper-gold acquisition
summary: Middle Island Resources jumped after announcing its acquisition of Konstantin Resources, which holds Serbian licences in the Western Tethyan copper-gold belt (including multiple copper prospects). The deal includes a $3.4m placement and plans for near-term exploration. No production or supply disruptions are described, so near-term copper price impact appears limited.

title: Orogen Royalties Inc: Orogen Royalties Creates a Royalty on the Camelot Copper-Gold Project
summary: Orogen Royalties announced it created a 1% NSR royalty (with option for an additional 0.25%) on the Camelot copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia, acquired by Prospect Ridge. The company cites historical copper/gold assays and plans drilling in 2025, but no near-term production changes are disclosed.

title: China's Sinomine Secures Path to Control Botswana Copper Project In A$9 Million Deal
summary: Sinomine agreed to acquire a 70% stake in Cobre Limited’s Okavango copper project in Botswana, funding exploration via an initial A$3m placement and an additional A$7m payment. The deal, pending approvals, would give Sinomine majority control of a copper-belt asset and expand its African copper footprint.

title: Capstone Copper reports temporary production disruption at Chilean mine - MRO Magazine
summary: Capstone Copper said its Mantoverde sulphide copper mine in Chile faces a temporary production disruption after two ball mill electrical drive motors failed. With no additional spare on site, the operation will run at about 50% capacity while repairs take roughly four weeks, reducing output by an estimated 3,000–4,000 tonnes.

title: [Latest] Global Aluminium Cables and Conductors Market
summary: The article promotes a market-research report on aluminium cables and conductors, citing rising power consumption, renewables integration, smart-grid and rural electrification programs, and urban infrastructure upgrades as demand drivers. It expects aluminium cable/conductor market growth in 2025–2034, implying supportive sentiment for aluminium demand.

title: EGA completes debottlenecking expansion at Al Taweelah alumina refinery
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium completed a debottlenecking expansion at its Al Taweelah alumina refinery, installing a third ball mill. The upgrade unlocks up to 50,000 tonnes per year of additional alumina capacity, improves reliability and throughput, and supports EGA’s alumina supply as it reorients away from Guinea.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.13% Higher at $4.5695 — Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures settled 1.13% higher at $4.5695, indicating upward near-term price pressure for copper. The move reflects improved sentiment or support in the futures market versus the prior session, which can influence expectations for physical demand and positioning over the following days.

title: The U.S. and China Are Battling for Control of the World's Bauxite Supply
summary: The U.S. and China are competing for bauxite supply, with Guinea revoking a bauxite concession tied to UAE refiner plans. The article links bauxite to alumina and then aluminum demand, noting stable but regionally higher bauxite prices amid logistics and regulatory constraints. Supply-risk could lift aluminum expectations.

title: Canyon Boosts Minim Martap Bauxite Reserves by 33% to 144 Mt in Cameroon
summary: Canyon Resources raised bauxite reserves at its Minim Martap project in Cameroon by 33% to 144 Mt, citing a definitive feasibility study and premium-quality ore. The company expects phased output starting Q1 2026. While it supports longer-term aluminum supply prospects, near-term impact on aluminum prices appears limited.

title: How can the Philippines turn nickel mines green again?
summary: The Philippines, the world’s second-largest nickel producer, is working on mine rehabilitation through reforestation and a bioremediation “greening” programme amid environmental concerns. Laws require restoration, but some abandoned mines remain unreclaimed. Risks like typhoons may hinder cleanup, affecting future nickel supply compliance.

title: Brazil opens probe into Anglo American's $500 million nickel business sale, FT reports
summary: Brazil’s CADE has opened an investigation into Anglo American’s planned sale of its nickel operations in the country to MMG for up to $500 million, following a complaint from CoreX. CADE said the probe does not imply the deal will be blocked. The sale is still pending.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Announces First Copper Production from Johnson Camp Mine
summary: Gunnison Copper announced first copper cathode production from its Johnson Camp Mine, following successful SX/EW start-up in late August 2025. The company says the plant is fully operational, with ramp-up toward 25 million lbs of annual cathode capacity. It cites Nuton’s leaching technology support and U.S. incentives.

title: Exclusive-Britain's FCA asks Mercuria about its LME aluminium holding
summary: Britain’s FCA has contacted Mercuria to question its very large LME aluminium warrant position, which Reuters says has distorted short-maturity aluminium contract prices and reduced transparency for physical users. Holdings exceeded 90% of warrants, while LME aluminium inventories have risen since late June. No rule breach is alleged.

title: First Copper at Johnson Camp Establishes Gunnison Copper as America's Newest Producer
summary: Gunnison Copper Corp. says first copper has been produced at its Johnson Camp project, positioning Gunnison as a new US producer. The company frames the outlook as extremely bullish on copper and notes incentives aimed at boosting domestic mining supply, which can improve short-term expectations for copper availability.

title: NexMetals Mining Corp.: NexMetals Announces Selebi Mines Metallurgical Breakthrough: Unlocks Ability to Produce Separate High-Grade Saleable Copper & Nickel-Cobalt Concentrates
summary: NexMetals reports improved metallurgical test results from its past-producing Selebi Cu-Ni-Co mines in Botswana, showing it can produce separate saleable copper and nickel concentrates and potentially avoid a full smelter/hydromet plant. The company sees lower energy needs and faster restart optionality, but no near-term output change is stated.

title: Canada Focused on U.S. Relief for Steel, Aluminum and Autos, Carney Says
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said he’s in talks with President Trump for bilateral trade relief covering sectors facing U.S. tariffs, including aluminum. Canada recently cut retaliatory tariffs and U.S. officials discussed Canadian aluminum tariff levels, despite a reported 50% tariff. Easing barriers could lift near-term aluminum price expectations.

title: Canada Focused on U.S. Relief for Steel, Aluminum and Autos, Carney Says -- Update
summary: Canada’s PM Mark Carney said talks with the U.S. aim to obtain relief from tariffs on steel and aluminum. Despite Canada cutting some retaliatory duties, the U.S. plans to keep a 50% tariff on Canadian steel and aluminum, sustaining cost pressure on imports and likely weighing on aluminum prices in the near term.

title: British firm launches major copper drilling program in Agadir – The North Africa Post
summary: Critical Mineral Resources PLC has begun a 6,000-meter diamond drilling program at its Agadir Melloul copper-silver project in Morocco to test for 150,000–200,000 tons of contained copper. The work aims to define resources for potential future mining, but no production increase is reported.

title: Golden Sky Minerals Corp.: Golden Sky and Boliden Sign $20 Million Earn-In Agreement for the Combined Rayfield-Gjoll Copper-Gold Property, South-Central British Columbia
summary: Golden Sky Minerals and Boliden signed a definitive earn-in agreement to jointly develop the Rayfield-Gjoll copper-gold project in British Columbia, with Boliden funding up to C$20 million for an 80% interest over six years. The release highlights copper-gold porphyry targets and geology, but no near-term production impacts.

title: Copper shortage is forcing faster aluminium adoption
summary: Hydro says copper-to-aluminium substitution is accelerating in the US HVAC and refrigeration market despite US tariffs. Customers still pay higher aluminium tariff costs because aluminium remains much cheaper than copper, with the LME copper/aluminium ratio supporting substitution. The piece also notes copper supply constraints increasing the incentive to switch.

title: Copper shortage is forcing faster aluminium adoption
summary: Hydro says the copper-to-aluminium substitution trend in industrial applications has not reversed despite US tariffs, with faster switching in the US HVAC market where aluminium remains cheaper despite a 50% tariff. The piece cites a high copper/aluminium price ratio and ongoing copper supply constraints, implying weaker copper demand and stronger aluminium uptake.

title: US Copper Corp.: US Copper Commences Metallurgical Studies on Its Moonlight-Superior Copper Project
summary: US Copper Corp. hired metallurgical consultants to review prior testwork and design additional metallurgy needed for a planned PFS at its Moonlight-Superior copper project in California. The update includes oxide/sulfide testwork planning, potential additional drilling, and references to prior PEA results, with no near-term production impact described.

title: Fastmarkets' new domestic aluminium billet premium benchmark in Brazil highlights market resilience, reduced import dependence amid tariff changes
summary: Fastmarkets launched a domestic Brazilian benchmark for aluminium billet premiums, aimed at improving transparency for local billet/extrusion transactions. The note highlights Brazil’s growing domestic output and reduced import dependence amid US tariff changes. It complements existing aluminium benchmarks and sets a reference for contracts.

title: Fastmarkets Launches New Domestic Aluminium Billet Premium Benchmark in Brazil
summary: Fastmarkets launched a new domestic aluminium billet premium pricing reference for Brazil. The benchmark is intended to standardize transactions for billet used in extrusions, supporting local price discovery as Brazil’s aluminium market becomes less import-driven. It references tariffs but provides no direct supply-demand shock.

title: CADE investigating Anglo American's planned $500m nickel operations sale in Brazil
summary: Brazil’s competition authority CADE has started an investigation into Anglo American’s planned sale of its Brazilian nickel operations to MMG for up to $500m. The probe follows a competitor complaint but CADE says it doesn’t automatically imply obstruction, leaving near-term nickel supply timing uncertain.

title: Copper prices surpass 10,000 usd/mt mark again! What fuelled the spike?Could it go even higher?
summary: The White House signed a proclamation imposing 50% tariffs on imported semi-finished copper products and copper-intensive derivatives from August 1, excluding copper inputs and scrap. The article says spreads narrowed and copper rallied further with expectations of Fed rate cuts, tighter smelter feedstock, and upcoming peak-season demand.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Announces Discovery of Copper Mineralization on Surface at Project Licences in Kazakhstan
summary: Ivanhoe Mines and Pallas Resources report outcropping copper mineralization at the Merke licence in Kazakhstan’s Chu-Sarysu Basin, including visible malachite, azurite and chalcocite and samples up to 5% copper. Follow-up mapping and a planned 15,000-metre drilling campaign have begun, but the discovery is not yet economic.

title: Electric Royalties Ltd.: Electric Royalties Reports Increase in Copper Royalty Revenues from Punitaqui and Provides Updates on Other Key Royalties
summary: Electric Royalties reports higher royalty revenues tied to the Punitaqui Copper Mine in Chile, citing concentrate shipments (including copper content calculations) and stating the operator is executing plans to increase production. It also notes environmental approval to extend operations at Los Mantos, implying steadier near-term copper supply.

title: Koryx Announces Updated PEA Results for the Haib Copper Project, Southern Namibia
summary: Koryx Copper reported updated PEA results for its 100%-owned Haib copper project in southern Namibia, projecting ~92 ktpa payable copper and detailing C1/AISC costs, capital needs, and NPV/IRR at a long-term copper price. The update supports project potential but does not imply immediate production impact.

title: Core Silver Corp.: Core Silver Samples 316 g/t Silver & 0.62% Copper at the Valley Zone as Drilling Continues
summary: Core Silver reported 2025 surface rock assay results from its Laverdiere copper project, including copper grades of 0.62–0.74% from Valley Zone samples and additional copper-bearing veining at Copper Creek. The company also outlines continued diamond drilling plans targeting the newly defined structures.

title: First Quantum copper production: Targets 1.5M tpy by 2035
summary: First Quantum CEO Tristan Pascall discusses Kansanshi’s S3 copper expansion in Zambia, citing $1.25bn investment, life extension by 20 years, and a broader goal of 1.5mn tpy copper capacity over the next decade. The piece emphasizes stable policy/investment conditions and copper demand themes, but offers no near-term supply shock.

title: Police recover R3 million worth of copper cable belonging to Transnet
summary: Police and Transnet recovered about R3m of stolen copper cable at an unregistered scrapyard and arrested additional suspects for critical infrastructure theft at a Transnet depot. Transnet also welcomed convictions for copper cable theft, suggesting tougher enforcement against copper theft syndicates, with limited evidence of broader supply impact.

title: Oscillate enters copper JV, plans hydrogen disposal to Pulsar Helium
summary: Oscillate PLC signed an earn-in/joint venture with La Miniere de L'Elephant to advance the Duekoue copper prospect in Ivory Coast, committing up to USD 650,000 over two years and funding early exploration. La Miniere earns a per-pound copper equivalent royalty, but no near-term production is indicated.

title: Tight Aluminum Scrap Supply Supports ADC12 Aluminum Alloy Prices[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Weekly review highlights tight aluminum scrap supply, especially shredded/tense scrap, keeping aluminum scrap prices firm. Unconfirmed policy changes and nationwide crackdowns on illegal tax rebates are expected to raise secondary aluminum production costs. ADC12 spot prices stay firm with cost support, while demand recovery is limited, capping upside.

title: Aurubis obtains 75,000 tpy Canadian copper concentrate from 2028
summary: Aurubis secured a partial offtake deal for 75,000 tpy Canadian copper concentrate from Troilus (about 10% grade, implying 8,000-12,000 tpy copper content). The agreement supports smelter throughput amid tight clean concentrate supply and deep-negative TC/RCs, with pricing to be finalized under long-term terms.

title: Highland Copper Announces Updated Process Plant Flow Sheet
summary: Highland Copper reported positive metallurgical test work for its Copperwood copper project, redesigning the process flowsheet with ultrafine flotation and an MF2 circuit. Results indicate higher expected copper recoveries (up to 87.6%) and lower power and reagent costs. This supports future project engineering, but offers limited immediate supply impact.

title: Marimaca Copper Announces A$80,000,000 Placement
summary: Marimaca Copper Corp. announced an A$80 million brokered placement, with net proceeds earmarked for detailed design and engineering at its Marimaca oxide copper deposit and for exploration at the Pampa Medina and Marimaca sulphide targets. The financing supports project advancement, which can be sentimentally bullish for copper.

title: Pecoy Copper Corp. Announces Closing of Reverse Takeover and Completion of Pecoy Project Acquisitions
summary: Pecoy Copper announced the closing of its reverse takeover and completion of acquisitions consolidating 100% control of the Pecoy copper-gold-molybdenum project in southern Peru. The company raised C$63.48M to fund exploration, metallurgical and engineering studies, and eventual development work, with no near-term output guidance.

title: How local businesses and the city are fighting back against copper theft
summary: Prince George is seeing a 68% increase in copper cable theft, including wire taken from street lights. City and RCMP coordination, tighter recycler rules under the 2012 Metal Recycling Act, and improved yard inspections aim to reduce buying of stolen copper. These measures may curb scrap monetization and near-term copper pressure.

title: Editorial: Stop looking away — copper theft in Prince George is costing us all
summary: The editorial says copper theft in Prince George and across Canada is rising, damaging 911 access, landlines, wireless services, streetlights and potentially hospital/alarms. It cites a TELUS-reported 68% jump in copper cable thefts and argues penalties are too light. It frames copper as a profitable black-market target, implying tighter effective supply.

title: Copper Billet Industry's August Operating Rates Drop Both YoY and MoM, Mediocre Start to September Peak Season
summary: SMM reports copper billet operating rates fell in August to 43.87%, dropping MoM and YoY, with weak order flow—especially extruded billets—and refrigeration sectors still in off-season. Policy uncertainty on recycled copper prompts production cuts and tight inventories, while firm imported recycled raw material prices raise costs. September may only rise slightly MoM.

title: Hot Chili rights issue raises $14.1M to fast-track Chile copper play
summary: Hot Chili completed a fully subscribed $14.1M entitlement offer to fund further drilling and development at its Chile Costa Fuego copper-gold project. The company plans a follow-up drill program at La Verde and continues financing studies and partnering efforts, reinforcing expectations for progress toward near-term copper production.

title: Mining: Milei is betting big on copper to 'Make Argentina Great Again'
summary: Argentina’s President Javier Milei unveiled reforms (RIGI) to attract large investors to develop copper projects, with major firms like BHP and Glencore engaging on benefits for specific ventures. The news frames potential supply growth amid electrification demand, but highlights policy and social-licence risks, limiting immediate near-term price impact.

title: Kansanshi S3: Zambia's biggest copper investment in a decade
summary: Zambia inaugurated First Quantum Minerals’ $1.25bn Kansanshi Sulphide-3 (S3) expansion, commissioning a new 25 mtpa processing plant that should lift Kansanshi output to about 280,000 tpa and increase total copper from Kansanshi/Sentinel toward 480,000 tpa by 2027. The project also extends mine life and highlights Zambia’s output ramp plans.

title: JX Advanced Metals to cut copper production and smelting capacity
summary: JX Advanced Metals, a major Japanese copper smelter, plans to slash electrolytic copper output by several tens of thousands of tonnes versus earlier projections because it can’t purchase enough concentrates under current terms. It also plans to reduce smelting capacity amid weak TC/RCs and tighter concentrate supply, supporting copper prices.

title: The "September Peak Season" Effect Begins to Emerge! Weekly Operating Rate of Aluminum Processing Rises by 1%, with All Sectors Showing Positive Recovery Trends【SMM Weekly Downstream Survey】
summary: SMM reports China’s leading aluminum downstream operating rate rose 1 ppt week-on-week to 61.7% as the September peak season emerges. Plate/strip, wire/cable, foil, extrusion, and secondary segments improved on order growth, restocking, and end of restrictions, implying firmer near-term aluminum demand and utilization.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Sep 5
summary: SMM reports stable Indonesian nickel ore benchmark and premiums for most grades, with some supply easing as weather improves and RKAB approvals near completion. Demand is slightly stronger, NPI prices continue rising, and high-nickel pig iron increases on cost support and seasonal demand recovery, implying upward near-term nickel pressure.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Provides Execution Plan for PFS on Van Dyke ISCR Project
summary: Copper Fox announced completion of an execution plan for a prefeasibility study on its Van Dyke in-situ copper recovery project in Arizona, including planned drilling, metallurgical testing, and permitting steps. The company notes prior economics sensitivity to copper prices but provides no near-term production or supply change guidance.

title: Marimaca Copper Corp.: Marimaca Copper Completes A$80,000,000 Bookbuild
summary: Marimaca Copper Corp. completed an A$80m bookbuild to fund exploration at the Pampa Medina project and work at its Marimaca Oxide and sulphide targets in Chile. The financing supports ongoing development but provides no immediate production, supply, or trade disruption information for near-term copper pricing.

title: Cost Push and Policy Disturbance Drove ADC12 Price Up in August, Demand Fulfillment in Focus for September[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: ADC12 (secondary aluminium) prices rose in August, tracking tight scrap supply and rising input costs, while tax rebate policy changes under “No. 770” increased cost pressure (via canceled refunds and back-tax risk). Demand was softer during summer breaks, but September peak-season expectations and recovery of orders provide support.

title: Would Refined Nickel Alter the Tight Supply-Demand Balance of Nickel Sulphate? — September Nickel Sulphate Market Outlook and Economic Analysis of Nickel Salt-to-Refined Nickel Conversion
summary: SMM reports nickel sulphate (battery-grade) prices rising in Q3 amid weak spot supply from maintenance and limited raw material availability, alongside strong demand/stockpiling for the September–October precursor peak season. Analysis indicates conversion between nickel sulphate and refined nickel is cost-uncompetitive now, so supply tightness should persist into September.

title: Great Southern Copper seeks Rule 9 waiver nod at AGM
summary: Great Southern Copper will seek shareholder approval at its AGM for a Rule 9 waiver so its largest shareholder can exercise warrants without triggering a mandatory offer. The company expects 6.3 million new shares from warrant exercise and plans further Chile exploration drilling, funded by the exercise and other financing.

title: iPhone 17 Pro to Ditch Titanium for Aluminum, Base Model to Get 6.3-inch ProMotion Display [Report]
summary: Bloomberg reports Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max will revert to aluminum frames instead of titanium, while a new iPhone 17 “Air” model is also planned. The change suggests higher aluminum demand and potentially weaker titanium-related demand, offering modest near-term support for aluminum prices.

title: Canada's Koryx Copper Prices Its Namibian Copper Project at $1.56Bln, Aiming for 23-Year Output
summary: Koryx Copper released a preliminary economic assessment for its Haib copper project in Namibia, estimating initial investment of $1.56B to produce 88,000 tonnes of copper per year for 23 years. The work is still pending licensing, funding, and a DFS in 2H 2026 before a final investment decision.

title: Key talking points ahead of International Aluminium Conference
summary: Ahead of the EU’s CBAM definitive period, Fastmarkets highlights uncertainty around carbon-cost calculations but notes emerging hedging and front-loading of duty-paid European aluminium purchases. Fastmarkets expects P1020 premiums to include additional CBAM costs from Jan 2026, alongside tight inventories and tariff-driven premium strength in the US.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Tight Supply-Demand Pattern for Nickel Intermediate Products Drives Upward Price Trend
summary: SMM analysis highlights a tight supply-demand balance for nickel intermediate products. This imbalance is described as the driver of an upward price trend, suggesting that market expectations for near-term nickel availability and conversion supply are strengthening and likely supporting nickel prices over the coming days.

title: Media advisory - Government of Canada to highlight new support measures for workers and businesses in the aluminum industry impacted by U.S. tariffs
summary: Canada’s Industry Minister will highlight new support measures for workers and businesses in Quebec’s aluminum industry affected by U.S. tariffs. The government action suggests efforts to cushion producer impacts and improve near-term viability, potentially supporting aluminum price expectations versus a tariff-driven demand/supply shock.

title: Policy Shock: Secondary Copper Rod Plants Suspend Production and Adopt Wait-and-See Approach
summary: Secondary copper rod plants in Jiangxi suspended production from August amid uncertainty over potential policy crackdowns on tax incentives and investment measures. Scrap/raw-material tightness and narrow spreads squeezed margins, but output cuts reduced supply. Selling prices rose and discounts to copper futures narrowed, supporting near-term bullish copper sentiment despite weak orders.

title: Bahrain's Alba signs agreement to explore alumina refinery in Egypt
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) signed a non-binding MoU with Egypt’s state-backed Metallurgical Industries Holding to explore developing an alumina refinery in Egypt. The MoU covers potential offtake and equity options but provides no further details, limiting immediate implications for near-term aluminium markets.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Market: Operating Rate in August Fell Short of Expectations, Recovery in September Expected to Remain Weak
summary: SMM says China copper plate/sheet and strip producers’ operating rate fell in August to 65.87%, below expectations, due to off-season/weak end-demand and reduced buying from higher late-August copper prices. Tight recycled-copper scrap supply raised costs. September recovery is minimal, implying limited near-term upside for copper prices.

title: End-User Demand Continues to Heat Up, China's Copper Foil Industry Operating Rates Keep Climbing [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says China’s copper foil enterprises’ operating rate rose to 78.44% in August and is forecast to climb to 79.05% in September. Growth is led by lithium battery copper foil and strong downstream orders, with lower finished inventories and added support from peak-season stockpiling and export demand momentum.

title: Pakistan copper-gold mine Reko Diq wins $6bn in pledges after Saudi pullout
summary: Pakistan’s Reko Diq project, a major prospective copper (and gold) mine, secured $6 billion in loan pledges after a Saudi investor withdrew. Barrick Mining is now seeking alternative funding from U.S. and other international lenders, which may influence project timelines and future copper supply expectations.

title: UK regulator seeks clarity on Mercuria's sway over LME aluminium stocks
summary: The UK FCA is seeking clarity on Mercuria’s dominant LME aluminium warrant position (over 90% of warrants, 421,000 tonnes+), which witnesses say has distorted near-term aluminium prices. The LME has intervened, ordering Mercuria to loan out part of its holdings, and inventories have risen sharply since late June.

title: Air Conditioner Production and Sales and Copper Pipe & Tube Operating Rate
summary: Copper pipe & tube producer operating rates fell to 65.70% in August, with lower production and inventories, largely due to off-season effects. A 50% tariff on imported semi-finished copper products and weak US copper-pipe export orders hurt some producers, though US processing demand may lift utilization abroad. Sep forecast rises modestly; H2 copper pipe rates grow mildly.

title: Noronex nails deep Namibian copper in latest drilling program
summary: Noronex reported deeper drilling results at its Fiesta copper project in Namibia, including multiple copper-bearing intersections and plans for a 7,000m reverse-circulation program. The program is funded through an earn-in alliance with South32. Assays confirm copper continuity at depth, but impacts are largely exploratory.

title: In Panama 'The Copper Mine has been Managed Environmentally' Well
summary: Panama’s Ministry of the Environment is conducting a comprehensive audit of the Donoso copper mine to verify compliance with environmental conservation standards. A biologist says past audits and rehabilitation/monitoring measures support the mine’s environmental management. The audit could last months, and no immediate production impact is mentioned.

title: Canyon seeks larger Camrail stake to cut costs on Cameroon bauxite exports
summary: Canyon Resources is negotiating to increase its stake in Camrail to gain more control of rail and port logistics for its Minim Martap bauxite project in Cameroon. The push follows reserve growth and includes financing for locomotives, wagons, and infrastructure upgrades, aiming to speed exports.

title: /R E P E A T -- Media advisory - Government of Canada to highlight new support measures for workers and businesses in the aluminum industry impacted by U.S. tariffs/
summary: Canada’s government plans to announce new support measures for workers and businesses in Quebec’s aluminum industry affected by U.S. tariffs. Such policy responses can influence short-term aluminum trade flows and producer margins, potentially cushioning domestic supply and downside price pressure in the coming days.

title: Copper concentrate production in Armenia saw a decline of 8% during the period of January to July
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate output fell 8% to 159,125.3 tons in January–July 2025 versus the same period in 2024. The National Statistical Committee of Armenia reported the decline. Zinc and molybdenum saw rises and declines respectively, but copper production weakened year-on-year.

title: Joly expects aluminum sector to receive 'hundreds of millions' in tariff relief
summary: Canada’s industry minister says Quebec’s aluminum sector is expected to receive “hundreds of millions” from a $5-billion tariff relief fund as U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum are 50%. Most Canadian production is exported to the U.S., so relief is intended to restore competitiveness and mitigate trade-war knock-on effects.

title: Tariffs aluminum: Joly expects hundreds of millions in relief
summary: Canada’s industry minister says Quebec’s aluminum sector is likely to receive hundreds of millions of dollars from a $5-billion fund aimed at helping industries hit by U.S. tariffs. With most Canadian aluminum produced in Quebec and largely exported to the U.S., tariff relief should bolster competitiveness.

title: Aluminum sector likely to receive hundreds of millions in tariff relief, Joly says
summary: Canada’s Industry Minister says Quebec’s aluminum sector is likely to receive hundreds of millions of dollars from a $5-billion tariff relief fund. Canadian aluminum exports face 50% U.S. tariffs, and most Quebec output is exported to the U.S. Support is intended to keep the sector competitive and maintain trade flows.

title: Joly expects aluminum sector to receive 'hundreds of millions' in tariff relief | iNFOnews
summary: Canada’s Industry Minister said Quebec’s aluminum sector is expected to receive “hundreds of millions” from a $5-billion tariff relief fund aimed at firms hurt by U.S. tariffs. With nearly all Canadian aluminum exported to the U.S., tariff support should bolster competitiveness and support aluminum market sentiment near term.

title: Que. Aluminum Sector May Receive 'hundreds Of Millions' In Tariff Relief: Joly
summary: Canada’s Industry Minister says Quebec’s aluminum sector is likely to receive hundreds of millions of dollars from a $5 billion tariff-relief fund to counter U.S. tariffs. With most Canadian aluminum exported to the U.S., support to keep producers competitive should be mildly bullish for aluminium prices.

title: Aluminum Imports to Israel Halved | Barnea Jaffa Lande & Co.
summary: Israel’s Ministry of Economy imposed a temporary, steep-rate guarantee on aluminum imports from China and effectively blocked Turkish supply for Israeli buyers. Orders from China reportedly fell 50%, and total imports dropped from about $19.5m in January 2025 to $9.3m by June. The shortage is expected to raise aluminum prices.

title: Venerable Ventures Ltd.: Venerable Ventures Announces Start of 50,000 m Drill Program at the Minto Copper-Gold-Silver Mine
summary: Venerable Ventures announced commencement of a 50,000 m diamond drill program at the Minto copper-gold-silver mine in Yukon. Drilling began August 23 after land-use permit approval, and the first hole of the 2025 program intersected mineralization, suggesting expansion potential at Minto North.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Inc. (IE) Earns Outperform Rating on Copper Potential and Tech Edge
summary: National Bank Financial initiated coverage of Ivanhoe Electric with an Outperform rating, citing its Santa Cruz copper project in Arizona expected to deliver domestic copper cathode for U.S. supply-chain goals. The piece highlights its technology for locating copper deposits and frames the outlook as supportive for copper development sentiment.

title: Guinea's License Review Stalls Niagara Bauxite Project, Miner Says
summary: Arrow Minerals has halted all activities at its Niagara bauxite project in Guinea because of unresolved permit status after the government revoked more than 100 mining licenses, including Arrow’s. The suspension delays a preliminary economic study and stalls an estimated 185 million tonnes of bauxite resources.

title: Miners Anglo American, Teck plan new copper giant
summary: Anglo American and Teck plan a multi-billion merger to form Anglo Teck, positioning the new group as a leading copper producer with major mining and processing assets. The companies cite booming copper demand from electrification, renewables, EVs, and AI/data centers, and shares rose on the news.

title: Miners Anglo American, Teck Plan New Copper Giant
summary: Anglo American and Teck announced a multi-billion merger forming a new copper-focused producer, expected to complete in 12–18 months. The deal positions the combined group as a top global copper producer and highlights strong copper-linked demand from energy transition and AI, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Anglo American, Teck to Merge, Creating Copper Giant -- 2nd Update
summary: Anglo American and Teck agreed to merge, forming a major copper producer expected to raise annual copper output and make copper over 70% of the combined mix. The deal could reshape M&A expectations in copper, with analysts noting potential bidding activity, supporting near-term bullish sentiment for copper prices.

title: Instant View: Anglo, Teck forge $53 billion mining giant in bet on surging copper demand
summary: The article headline says Anglo and Teck are forging a $53 billion mining giant based on expectations of surging copper demand. Such a move can strengthen market expectations for copper demand and support prices over the next days to weeks. No material information on nickel or aluminium is provided.

title: Transition Metals Corp.: Transition Metals Defines Multiple Drill-Ready Copper Porphyry and Epithermal Gold-Silver Targets at Pike Warden
summary: Transition Metals reports completion of an 8.9 km IP survey and defines 17 drill-ready targets at its Pike Warden project in Yukon, including porphyry copper targets. Mapping and sampling show pending assay results, with historical highlights including up to 7.49% Cu. The company plans drilling this fall.

title: Aeromag Results Identify Primary Copper Source | Company Announcement
summary: GreenX reports results from a 58km2 airborne magnetic/radiometric survey over its Tannenberg copper project in Germany. It identifies the Mid-European Crystalline Zone as the deep source beneath historic Richelsdorf mines and notes anomalies extending into Tannenberg 2, increasing exploration potential. No immediate production change is stated.

title: Viscount Mining Corp.: Viscount Mining Advances Next Phase of Exploration in Colorado: Expanded Work Programs at the Kate Silver Resource and Passiflora Copper-Gold Porphyry Deposit
summary: Viscount Mining outlines expanded exploration at its Colorado Silver Cliff project. For Passiflora, new deep drilling (PF-03A) confirms thick copper-gold porphyry mineralization with open depth and higher-grade intervals, and permits have started for follow-up drilling. This supports positive copper discovery sentiment, though supply impact is limited near term.

title: Anglo American, Teck Resources Mega-Deal Will Create "Compelling, Large-Scale Copper Business"
summary: Anglo American and Teck Resources agreed to merge to create a large-scale copper miner (“Anglo Teck”), targeting about 1.2 million tonnes of annual copper output, rising to 1.35 million by 2027. With most revenues linked to copper and investor interest rising, the news supports bullish copper sentiment near term.

title: Anglo American, Teck to Merge, Creating Copper Giant — 2nd Update
summary: Anglo American and Teck agreed to merge, creating one of the world’s largest copper producers with about 1.2–1.35 million tons of annual output and copper as the dominant production mix. Analysts viewed the deal as a potential start of a new wave of mining M&A, supporting expectations for copper supply and demand.

title: Freeport Resources Inc.: Freeport Resources Announces Results from Optimization Study at Its Large-Scale Yandera Copper Project, Papua New Guinea
summary: Freeport Resources reported results from an optimization study for its Yandera copper-gold project, evaluating phased high-grade, reduced-throughput development and revised economics using updated commodity pricing models. The release cites current and historical copper prices and recommends further test work, but provides no near-term production or supply changes.

title: Copper Standard Resources Inc.: Copper Standard Provides Portfolio and Corporate Update
summary: Copper Standard Resources issued a portfolio and corporate update, electing not to proceed with an option on copper-related claims at the Colpayoc project while retaining adjacent interests. It also reports exploration results mentioning enrichment values up to 3% copper at Capricho. The update is corporate and exploration-focused.

title: Europe sees flood of Canadian aluminum as U.S. tariffs bite
summary: Quebec aluminium exporters are shipping far more to Europe as Trump’s US aluminum tariffs raise American costs and divert volumes away from the US. Europe’s share of exports surged in Q2, while US Midwest premiums jumped and Rotterdam premiums eased on added supply.

title: Every Can Counts analysis: Return rate for aluminium beverage cans reached 78% this summer
summary: Every Can Counts analysis using RetuRo data says Romania’s aluminium beverage-can return rate reached 78% in July, up from 35% two years ago. The rise is attributed to the Deposit Return Scheme, more collection/recycling capacity, and public awareness campaigns. The study suggests recycling would improve further with more education.

title: Anglo American, Teck to Merge Into $53 Billion Copper Giant -- Commodities Roundup
summary: Anglo American and Teck agreed to merge into a $53 billion copper-focused producer. The article frames copper as in rising demand from electrification/AI while supply may not keep up, implying support for copper prices. A related market talk adds Canadian government review risk for critical-minerals deals.

title: Anglo American and Teck Agree to Create $53 Billion Copper Giant Amid AI Boom
summary: Anglo American and Teck agreed to merge into Anglo Teck, a $53bn copper giant with over 70% copper exposure, amid surging AI-driven data-center electricity demand. Copper has risen about 15% this year but recently pulled back after Trump’s 50% import levies started in August. Deal completion is expected in 12–18 months.

title: Historic Copper Alliance: Anglo American and Teck Join Forces
summary: Anglo American and Teck agreed to merge assets, a deal framed by Codelco’s chairman as reinforcing Chile’s role in the global copper market.
