The alliance is expected to boost productivity in extraction and processing and position Chile more strongly amid rising demand linked to technology and green energy.

title: Anglo-Teck Mega-Deal: A New Titan Emerges in the Copper Boom
summary: Anglo American and Teck Resources announced a $50 billion merger to form Anglo Teck, combining large copper mine portfolios and targeting production scale of over 1.5 million tons annually. The deal is positioned against a tight copper market with rising electrification demand and supply constraints, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Proalu SA Set to Begin Construction of CFA88 Billion Aluminium Processing Plant in Douala
summary: Proalu SA will break ground on an $88bn-CFA aluminium processing plant in Douala, targeting 30,000 tons of aluminium coils and pre-coated products annually and producing electric cables including several thousand tons of aluminium and copper. The plant will use raw materials from Alucam with guaranteed sales, supporting import substitution and boosting near-term demand expectations for aluminium and copper.

title: CEO.CA Technologies Ltd.: CEO.CA's Inside the Boardroom: Gunnison Copper Is Now Producing 100% American Copper, Says Market Hasn't Caught Up Yet
summary: CEO.CA interviews Gunnison Copper CEO Craig Hallworth after Gunnison began copper cathode production at the Johnson Camp Mine in Arizona. The company says it is now producing “100% American copper” with an on-site SX/EW refinery and cites its 2024 PEA economics. The news is intended to bolster investor confidence in copper output.

title: Anglo American to quit London HQ after agreeing £40bn copper mega- merger with Canadian rival
summary: Anglo American agreed a £40bn merger with Teck Resources, creating one of the world’s largest copper producers. The deal combines adjacent Chilean copper mines (Quebrada Blanca and Collahuasi) and includes cost savings. Analysts expect consolidation and possible counter-offers, boosting copper sentiment in the near term.

title: PHL urged to move up copper value chain - BusinessWorld Online
summary: PwC urged the Philippines to move up the copper value chain by investing in processing, refining, and manufacturing rather than only exporting mined ore. The piece highlights large copper and some nickel reserves and mentions a need for regulation and infrastructure, but offers no immediate supply or demand change.

title: Wodonga railway train line copper thief caught by police | The Border Mail
summary: A man in Wodonga allegedly cut out and stole about 50 metres of copper cabling from railway signalling, causing signal faults. Police estimated repair damage at $102,540, including materials and labour. The court heard the theft could have created safety risks, but the incident seems localized.

title: Anglo American goes big on copper - but will its rivals now look to get in on the act? asks ALEX BRUMMER
summary: Anglo American’s £40bn merger with Teck Resources is positioned as copper-focused, combining adjacent Chilean mines (Quebrada Blanca and Collahuasi) and making the group a top five copper producer. The piece notes potential efficiencies but also risk from heavy income exposure to a single, volatile metal source.

title: Anglo American and Teck Resources deal makes it harder for BHP or Rio Tinto to move on miners' copper assets
summary: Anglo American’s $85bn merger with Teck is framed as changing acquisition dynamics for other majors considering miners’ copper assets. The deal reduces the ease with which BHP or Rio Tinto could move on such holdings, but the excerpt doesn’t indicate immediate production or supply disruptions for copper.

title: Anglo American and tech merger: Mega deal kicks off the copper wars
summary: Opinion piece argues the ~$US50bn Anglo American–Teck Resources nil-premium merger could spur “copper wars” as major miners seek more copper exposure. It highlights Anglo and Teck’s large copper output, constrained new supply, and potential consolidation around related Chile assets, supportive for copper sentiment.

title: Anglo American and Teck merger: Mega deal kicks off the copper wars
summary: Anglo American and Teck’s $US50bn merger (nil-premium) would combine large copper producers (~1.2m tonnes/year) and put both firms in play for rival bidders. The piece frames copper demand as booming and new supply as constrained, suggesting the deal could trigger further copper-focused M&A and support prices.

title: Kingfisher Metals Corp.: Kingfisher Metals Reports 234 meters of 1.0% Copper Equivalent, within 558 meters of 0.64% CuEq at HWY 37 Project, Golden Triangle, British Columbia
summary: Kingfisher Metals reported initial 2025 drilling results from the HWY 37 copper-gold project in British Columbia, including 557.8 meters at 0.29% copper and 0.64% CuEq, with a higher-grade 234.35-meter subinterval at 1.00% CuEq. The company says results de-risk targets and justify more drilling.

title: Vedanta in process of acquiring land for 3 MTPA aluminium smelter in Odisha
summary: Vedanta said it is acquiring land in Odisha to build a 3 million tonnes per annum aluminium smelter and is aiming to expand capacity to 6 million tonnes. The company also plans an aluminium park in Jharsuguda and is investing in billet capacity, signaling continued aluminium capacity growth and industry momentum.

title: Penang Customs foils attempt to smuggle in 125 tonnes of copper scrap worth RM5mil
summary: Penang Customs intercepted an attempt to smuggle 125 tonnes of copper scrap worth RM5.29 million arriving from Thailand. The goods were misdeclared as used electronic components and were detained as prohibited imports requiring a permit. The incident reduces immediate copper scrap availability while investigations continue.

title: Business Brief: Teck's long copper-led road - The Globe and Mail
summary: Teck’s proposed merger with Anglo could move Teck toward a foreign listing while keeping Vancouver and copper operations central. The deal combines Chilean assets (including Collahuasi and QB2) and is pitched as offering about US$800 million/year in savings, subject to Investment Canada review, supporting copper-focused sentiment.

title: Industrial partnership aims to reduce copper imports
summary: Green Tech Mining Services and Nuhas Oman agreed to study localising copper cathode procurement under Oman’s Industrial Strategy 2040, aiming to reduce copper cathode imports. Oman’s imports rose to OMR25.7 million by June 2025 versus OMR45.3 million in 2024, highlighting the import dependence to be addressed.

title: Nation surprises the world with new copper and gold deposits
summary: Serbia’s Timok district discovery Malka Golaja is highlighted by Zijin Mining with preliminary JORC-style resource figures for copper (2.81m tons at 1.87% grade) and gold, with resources open at the edges. Since it’s early-stage resources, near-term supply impact is limited, but sentiment for copper improves.

title: Firms partner to localise copper cathode supply
summary: Green Tech Mining and Nuhas Oman plan to procure locally produced copper cathode under an MoU to reduce reliance on imports. Oman’s copper cathode import bill fell but remains sizable, and a planned Suhar processing plant is set to add capacity. The plan supports the local copper value chain and exports.

title: Dutch greenhouse builders hit hard by U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs
summary: Dutch greenhouse builders report demand disruption after U.S. tariffs on imported steel and aluminum. Clients are canceling orders and builders are securing fewer U.S. contracts as greenhouse construction becomes about 25% more expensive, with supply-chain uncertainty stalling activity. The article does not mention copper directly.

title: Copper Rod Market Concludes August with a Flat Performance Can the "Golden September" Peak Season a Turn-around?【SMM Analysis】
summary: SMM reports China’s August copper rod output rose slightly, driven by higher copper cathode rod operating rates, while secondary rod rates fell MoM. High copper prices suppress downstream procurement and keep demand weak, limiting upside for “Golden September.” September production is forecast to rise modestly on late-month stocking.

title: Alaska Energy Metals Corporation: Alaska Energy Metals Hosts Federal Agency Representatives at Nikolai Nickel Project, Alaska
summary: Alaska Energy Metals says senior EPA and FAST-41 officials toured its Nikolai nickel project and that Alaska signed an MOU with the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council to streamline permitting. The company frames this as improving predictability for developing domestic critical minerals, supporting sentiment for nickel and, to a lesser extent, copper.

title: The Shortage of Aluminum Scrap Intensifies, Costs Drive ADC12 Aluminum Alloy Prices to Accelerate Their Rise[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Aluminum scrap supply stayed tight, especially for shredded tense scrap, with regional recycling offers rising as high as 300 yuan/mt in a day. Higher scrap costs and improved though still limited downstream demand supported ADC12 spot and cast-aluminum alloy futures, keeping ADC12 premiums and pointing to high prices next week despite upside limits.

title: Dufferin OPP investigating increase in copper thefts across the region.
summary: Dufferin OPP is investigating an increase in copper thefts across the region, targeting telephone wires, utility lines, and cable boxes, often overnight or in daylight by impersonating utility workers. Police warn against tampering with live infrastructure. Authorities urge residents to report suspicious activity immediately.

title: Copper: Teck CEO discusses Anglo American merger
summary: Teck’s CEO discusses its merger with Anglo American, saying the combined company will focus on copper and invest $4.5 billion in Canada’s critical minerals sector. The deal includes $2.4 billion to extend Highland Valley Copper mine life and aims to improve Quebrada Blanca performance, boosting bullish copper fundamentals.

title: What Farm Equipment Manufacturers Are Saying About 50% Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: Farm equipment makers say high U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminium are squeezing them. Case IH notes most production and steel inputs are domestic, while Claas relies more on European-built equipment shipped into the U.S. Claas says it has absorbed much of the cost rather than fully passing it to customers.

title: Zambia presses China for more compensation after toxic spill in Kitwe copper mine
summary: Zambia’s government is seeking additional compensation after a Chinese-owned copper mine tailings dam collapse released highly acidic, heavy-metal pollution into the Kafue River system. While authorities imposed a fishing ban and used lime to curb acidity, firms dispute spill estimates. The event could affect expectations for copper output, with broader health impacts reported.

title: Sask. copper mine one of five major projects announced by Carney
summary: Prime Minister Carney announced federal fast-track approvals and $41 million in investment for Foran’s McIlvenna Bay copper project in Saskatchewan. The mine aims for net-zero copper via cleaner technologies and is expected to start commercial production in mid-2026. Construction reached 50% completion, with no material wildfire impact reported.

title: B.C. LNG, copper mine projects crack first pass of federal list
summary: Canada’s federal “nation-building” list fast-tracks LNG Canada Phase 2 and a major extension of the Red Chris copper-and-gold mine. The Red Chris expansion is expected to extend mine life by a decade and lift Canada’s copper production by about 15%. Officials say fast-tracking aims to speed approvals and execution.

title: B.C. LNG, copper mine projects crack first pass of federal 'nation-building' list
summary: Canada’s federal “nation-building” fast-track list includes a major extension of the Red Chris copper-and-gold mine, which could extend mine life and raise Canada’s copper production by about 15%. Officials say the goal is to speed approvals and execution. This improves expectations for copper supply project timelines.

title: Indonesia seizes 148 hectare area of Weda Bay Nickel
summary: Indonesia’s task force seized 148 hectares of land from PT Weda Bay Nickel due to missing forestry permissions needed to use designated forest areas, despite holding a mining permit. The crackdown suggests potential delays or disruption to nickel output, tightening near-term supply expectations.

title: Govt seizes part of nickel site over forest violations  - Regulations
summary: Indonesia’s authorities seized nearly 150 hectares of the Weda Bay Nickel concession over alleged forest and licensing violations. The company said the seized area is a quarry for construction materials and that mining operations are unaffected. While it raises compliance-related uncertainty, the small scale suggests limited immediate supply disruption.

title: Leviathan Gold to acquire Cura Botswana copper and uranium assets
summary: Leviathan Gold will acquire 100% of Cura Botswana’s Kalahari exploration portfolios, including copper prospecting licences in Botswana. The transaction is structured as a share exchange with potential milestone payments and future share issuance. It is contingent on regulatory approvals, with no immediate production or supply change stated.

title: Indonesia Seizes Part Of Nickel Site Over Forest Violations
summary: Indonesian authorities seized nearly 150 hectares within the Weda Bay Nickel concession on Halmahera for encroaching forest areas without permits. Eramet said the seized section is a quarry for construction materials and mining operations were not affected. The company and authorities are clarifying permits while broader scrutiny of forestry rules continues.

title: 【SMM Nickel Analysis】Nickel intermediate products were affected by the decline in nickel prices, showing a downward trend in prices.
summary: Weekly SMM analysis says nickel intermediate products (MHP and high-grade nickel matte) fell as LME nickel prices declined. The drop is attributed to increased refined nickel supply, high inventories weighing on nickel, and weak downstream buying. Tight spot availability wasn’t enough to support prices, leading to lower absolute quotations.

title: The American Primary Aluminum Association Criticizes Hundreds of Millions of Dollars in New Canadian Aluminum Subsidies
summary: The American Primary Aluminum Association criticizes Canada’s $5 billion tariff-relief fund, saying it will provide hundreds of millions in support to Canada’s aluminum sector. The group argues this distorts global competition and calls for the U.S. to keep its 50% aluminum tariff, pressuring aluminum imports.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Sep 12
summary: SMM reports slightly lower Indonesian nickel ore prices, while higher-grade premiums remain steady amid improved weather and tighter enforcement of mining compliance. NPI prices rose on higher tenders, but mills’ weak acceptance and slim margins reduced transactions. Analysts expect upward momentum to fade next week.

title: Correction to alumina index, fob Australia, plus derived prices, on September 11
summary: Fastmarkets issued a correction notice for several alumina benchmark indices and derived prices (FOB Australia, Indonesia, India, Vietnam, and Brazil). Each was adjusted downward by about $0.30–$0.39 per tonne from previously published values. The pricing database and rationales were updated accordingly.

title: The Panama Copper Mine is set to be Audited by a French Company
summary: Panama’s Ministry of Environment has started a comprehensive six-month audit of the closed Cobre Panamá open-pit mine operated by First Quantum Minerals, following a 2023 court shutdown. It also notes that around 120,000 tons of copper concentrate remained and was exported, and the president authorized related energy imports.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Indonesian Nickel Ore Premium Stable in Q3? Logic Explained
summary: SMM analyzes why Indonesia’s mainstream nickel ore premium is stable around $24–26 in Q3. It links prior movements to royalty hikes, improved rainy-season conditions, RKAB quota revisions ending July 31, and smelter losses that forced premium resets. Outlook suggests limited near-term decline.

title: Indonesia reopens nickel mine in dive hotspot despite outcry
summary: Indonesia allowed PT Gag Nikel to resume nickel mining on Gag island after a suspension was lifted and an environmental audit granted a “green” rating. The move follows earlier permit revocations and renewed activist criticism, but it signals higher near-term nickel supply from a key producer.

title: Nickel gains after Indonesia seizes part of giant Tsingshan mine
summary: Nickel prices rose after Indonesia seized about 148 hectares of PT Weda Bay Nickel, part of Tsingshan’s giant operation, citing alleged permit violations. While shareholders say operations may be unaffected initially, the action underscores supply risks as Indonesia tightens mining quotas and cracks down on illegal mining.

title: BKM Copper Project Limestone Drilling Update | Company Announcement
summary: Asiamet reported that its BKM copper project’s limestone resource drilling is 50% complete, with early assays confirming very high-quality limestone (>95% purity, >54% CaO). Locally sourced limestone is expected to lower processing consumption and import costs, supporting ongoing optimization to improve soluble copper recovery and power solutions.

title: MMG seeks EU approval for $500m Anglo American nickel assets deal
summary: MMG, backed by China Minmetals, seeks EU approval for a $500m purchase of Anglo American’s nickel assets. EU antitrust concerns about Chinese ownership remain, but MMG expects clearance, citing strong European demand and reduced competitive overlap. US industry groups criticize the deal for increasing China’s nickel control.

title: Zambia Seeks Greater Compensation After Toxic Copper Mine Spill – Medafrica Times
summary: Zambia says it will seek additional compensation for communities affected by February’s toxic spill at the Chinese-owned Sino-Metals Leach copper mine after a dam collapse. Reports claim far more hazardous waste than initially estimated, with health impacts and official alerts, raising accountability and potential disruption risks to copper operations.

title: King Copper Discovery Corp. Announces Closing of $15
summary: King Copper Discovery Corp. closed a $15m non-brokered private placement to fund exploration, including diamond drilling at its Colquemayo copper-gold project, plus working capital. The release details investor rights, related-party participation, and regulatory approvals. The financing may modestly improve perceived copper project prospects.

title: The Unforeseen Ripple: How a 50% Copper Tariff Could Skyrocket Silver Prices
summary: The article argues a hypothetical 50% tariff on copper imports would raise domestic copper costs, fragment trade, and potentially reduce global mining activity. It expects copper-intensive demand to soften and price divergence between domestic and LME/SHFE benchmarks to emerge. It also mentions limited substitution into metals like aluminium but focuses mainly on copper.

title: Proparco, local banks invest CFA54.4 bln in Cameroon aluminum plant
summary: Cameroon signed financing for Proalu SA’s Douala aluminium transformation plant, backed by local banks and Proparco. The project will produce 30,000 tons of aluminium-related products and electrical cables, including 2,000 tons aluminium and 6,000 tons copper, sourcing raw materials from Alucam. It supports import substitution and state revenue.

title: Copperwood Infrastructure Funding supported, protested in Wakefield
summary: Wakefield, Michigan residents backed a $50 million infrastructure funding package that could improve roads and telecommunications, aimed at enabling Highland Copper’s Copperwood mine. Protesters cite potential environmental risks from tailings leaching chemicals. Approval still requires passage through the state Senate before action by the governor.

title: Anglo American, Codelco finalise $5 billion Chile copper mines deal
summary: Anglo American and Chile’s state-run Codelco said they have finalised an agreement to jointly operate neighbouring Chilean copper mines, targeting at least $5 billion in value creation. The report describes a commercial operating structure but does not signal immediate supply disruptions or output changes.

title: Anglo American, Codelco finalise $5 billion Chilean copper mines deal
summary: Anglo American and Chile’s Codelco finalized a $5 billion deal to jointly operate neighboring copper mines Andina and Los Bronces. The plan targets higher output (+120,000 tonnes/year) and about 15% cost reduction per tonne, with potential long-run additional production. Investors may view improved supply/cost prospects as copper-supportive.

title: Anglo American, Codelco To Unlock At Least $5 Bln Of Value From 2 Copper Mines In Chile
summary: Anglo American and Codelco agreed a joint mine plan for neighboring Chilean copper mines Los Bronces and Andina, creating a jointly owned operating company. The plan targets value uplift of at least $5 billion and additional copper output of 2.7 million tons over 21 years (~120,000 tons/year).

title: Anglo American formally seals copper pact with Codelco in Chile
summary: Anglo American and Chile’s Codelco have signed a definitive agreement to implement a joint mine plan for the Los Bronces and Andina copper operations. The plan targets an additional 120,000 tonnes of copper per year once environmental permits are secured, expected in 2030, with cost advantages and a large NPV uplift.

title: AAL Share Price - Anglo American, Codelco seal $5 bln copper deal in Chile's Los Bronces and Andina
summary: Anglo American and Chile’s state miner Codelco have finalized a $5 billion plan to jointly develop the neighboring Los Bronces and Andina copper mines. The deal is expected to unlock value and improve development prospects, which can support market expectations for future copper supply.

title: First Quantum Minerals: A Copper Play Poised for a Rebound
summary: The piece discusses First Quantum’s Cobre Panama mine shutdown in Panama and the prospect of reopening under a new government, which could restore copper supply. It also highlights rising copper demand from EVs, renewables, and data centers, arguing copper markets stay tight and supportive for prices in coming weeks.

title: Copper Declared "Critical" as U.S. Considers Supply Chain Risks
summary: The U.S. USGS draft critical minerals list adds copper, citing supply-chain vulnerability and rising demand tied to electrification and green energy. The move implies future federal prioritization for permitting, mining, processing, and recycling, potentially strengthening near-term copper supply expectations. Tariff risks remain but are mostly deferred to later years.

title: Copper demand in data centers & future trends ahead
summary: Fastmarkets interviews industry bodies arguing that AI-driven data-center expansion is rapidly increasing copper requirements for power distribution, transformers/switchgear, grounding, and liquid cooling plates. Reports cited suggest high copper consumption growth, alongside policy-related uncertainty affecting copper sentiment and prices, supporting a broadly bullish outlook for copper demand.

title: Arizona Sonoran Reports 11 Billion Pounds of Contained Copper in updated Cactus Mineral Resource Estimate ...
summary: Arizona Sonoran Copper Company released an updated Mineral Resource Estimate for its Cactus brownfield copper project near Phoenix, reporting total contained copper of 11 billion pounds. The expanded estimate follows a conversion drilling program, potentially improving the project’s development outlook and supporting positive sentiment for copper supply potential.

title: Chinese-linked mining firms in Zambia sued by Copperbelt farmers over 'ecological catastrophe'
summary: Farmers in Zambia sued two Chinese-linked firms after a copper-mining tailings dam collapsed in February, spilling highly acidic waste and contaminating water, soil, and crops. A US health alert prompted wider concern. The case seeks large compensation and may increase perceived copper supply and regulatory risk.

title: How the merger of Teck's and Anglo's Chilean copper mines will work – or not work
summary: Teck and Anglo agreed to merge and integrate their neighboring Chilean copper mines, Quebrada Blanca and Collahuasi. The plan involves moving Collahuasi high-grade ore to the QB mill, boosting combined output by about 175,000 tonnes/year and raising operating earnings through shared mills, trucks and ports, despite technical and partner hurdles.

title: Anglo American, Codelco finalize $5-billion Chilean copper mines agreement
summary: Anglo American and Chile’s Codelco finalized a deal to jointly operate the Los Bronces and Andina copper mines in Chile. The plan targets higher production (+120,000 tonnes/year) and about 15% lower costs per ton, supported by synergies in extraction and processing, subject to approvals and permitting.

title: True North strikes high-grade copper-gold in Qld copper heartland
summary: True North Copper reported multiple high-grade copper intercepts from RC drilling at its Wallace North prospect and confirmed depth persistence of its Aquila copper-cobalt-silver discovery at Mt Oxide. The results suggest enlarged copper mineralisation potential, supporting bullish sentiment toward future copper supply expectations.

title: Dharmendra Pradhan Reviews Angul Aluminium Park and MCL Projects
summary: Dharmendra Pradhan reviewed the Aluminium Park project in Angul, Odisha, alongside MCL coalfield rehabilitation and land acquisition discussions aimed at boosting coal production. The minister said Angul may establish an Aluminium Industrial Park to support MSMEs and ancillary industries, indicating incremental aluminium demand/industrial activity.

title: Anglo, Codelco seal pact to unlock $5B in Chilean copper
summary: Anglo American and Chile’s Codelco agreed to jointly operate their neighboring mines Los Bronces and Andina, creating a new district outside Santiago. The pact is expected to unlock at least $5B in value and add about 2.7 million tonnes of copper over 21 years, subject to permits.

title: More than 20 fire departments respond to fire at Novelis aluminum plant
summary: A 3-alarm fire at Novelis’ Oswego County aluminum plant in New York halted production until further notice. Around 26 fire departments responded, with most effort focused on extinguishing the roof fire. Novelis says impacts are under investigation but production remains stopped pending assessment and restart planning.

title: Anglo American, Codelco sign deal to unlock $5bn from copper mines in Chile
summary: Anglo American Sur and Codelco signed an agreement to jointly plan their neighbouring Chilean copper mines Los Bronces and Andina. The plan is expected to add about 120,000 tonnes of copper per year with lower unit costs and aims to increase output after approvals, supporting copper supply expectations.

title: Giant Mining Continues Engagement with RESPEC to Integrate 2024-2025 Drill Data and Breccia Body into Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project 3D Model
summary: Giant Mining said RESPEC will integrate 2024–2025 drill core data into the 3D model for the Majuba Hill porphyry copper-silver-gold project over the next few weeks, refining breccia geometry and the exploration model and evaluating new targets. The release is technical and does not affect near-term production or supply.

title: Genomines Raises $45M Series A to Redefine Global Metal Extraction with Plant-Based Nickel
summary: Genomines announced an oversubscribed $45M Series A to scale genetically enhanced “hyperaccumulator” plants for battery-grade nickel via phytoextraction. The company says yields and productivity have improved and that it will accelerate South Africa pilot projects and seek commercial offtake. The raise could bolster expectations for nickel supply resilience.

title: Mitsubishi Corporation: Definitive agreement to implement a joint mine plan between Los Bronces and Andina copper mines
summary: Mitsubishi’s affiliate Anglo American has agreed with Codelco to implement a joint mine plan for the adjacent Los Brones and Andina copper operations in Chile. The project is expected to optimize existing processing with minimal incremental capex, adding 120,000 tonnes/year of copper from 2030 onward.

title: Romios Gold Resources Inc.: Romios Expands Size of Trek South Porphyry Copper-Gold Prospect in BC's Golden Triangle and Prepares for First-Ever Drilling in 2026
summary: Romios reports fieldwork expanding the copper-mineralized zone at its Trek South porphyry Cu-Au prospect in BC’s Golden Triangle, supported by alteration mapping and strong IP/magnetic anomalies. The company is preparing an updated NI 43-101 and plans first-ever drilling in 2026. No current output or supply change is stated.

title: Rice University Turns Toxic Red Mud into Aluminium
summary: Rice University researchers report a rapid flash-Joule heating process using a brief electrical pulse and small chlorine gas to vaporise iron and toxic species from red mud, leaving residue rich in aluminium. Claimed high recovery and scalability could improve aluminium recovery from waste and modestly support aluminium supply expectations.

title: Copper wire theft leaves Fairfax District neighborhood in the dark
summary: Streetlights and electrical boxes in Los Angeles’ Fairfax District and along the Sixth Street Bridge were left dark after thieves stole copper wiring, smashing covers and tearing out cables. Officials say the city’s streetlighting infrastructure is a prime target, with repairs expected to take months.

title: Australia offers support for Glencore's copper plants
summary: Australia and Queensland authorities have offered Glencore a support package aimed at keeping its Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville refinery operating. The deal is not final and a decision is expected soon, easing near-term copper processing supply risk and supporting prices. Details were not disclosed.

title: Hercules Metals Intersects 81 m of 1.5% Copper Within 346 m of 0.66% Copper in First 2025 Drill Hole Completed at the Leviathan Porphyry System in Idaho
summary: Hercules Metals’ first 2025 drill hole at the Leviathan porphyry in Idaho intersected high-grade copper, including 81 m at 1.5% Cu, plus broader zones up to 346 m grading 0.66% Cu, alongside strong MT conductivity results. Drilling continues to test extensions southward.

title: Definitive agreement to implement a joint mine plan between Los Bronces and Andina copper mines
summary: Mitsubishi’s affiliate Anglo American agreed with Codelco to implement a joint mine plan for Chile’s Los Bronces and Andina copper operations. The project targets an additional 120,000 tonnes of copper per year over 21 years, but execution begins in 2030, limiting immediate near-term supply impact.

title: Mexican aluminium industry in a changing market
summary: Mexican aluminium producers are seeking a US deal amid tariff uncertainty and possible new Mexican tariffs on certain imported products, including aluminium. Scrap exports to the US are rising, tightening local secondary supply. Market participants report low spot activity and pricing pressure, with companies slowing operations due to trade volatility.

title: Blue Gold Limited Signs Purchase Agreement for Gold & Copper Mining Lease, Marking First Step in Broader Planned M&A Growth Strategy
summary: Blue Gold Limited signed a definitive purchase agreement to acquire up to a 90% interest in the Mampon gold & copper mining lease in Ghana. The deal includes payments partly linked to verified resource upgrades, with copper valuation capped by tonnage. Nickel and aluminium are not mentioned.

title: Is Copper the Next Geopolitical Battleground?
summary: The discussion focuses on why copper prices have been volatile amid surging demand from EVs, semiconductors, AI/data centers, power grids, and arms manufacturing. It also highlights declining ore grades, refining/smelting bottlenecks, and upcoming U.S. tariffs on some copper imports, affecting near-term supply outlook and pricing sentiment.

title: BHP-Lundin JV to invest more than $400m in Argentine copper project
summary: BHP-Lundin’s Vicuña JV plans to invest over $400m in Argentina’s Josemaria copper project and is seeking approvals and investment-incentive benefits (Rigi). The JV is in pre-construction and will present progress to its board by end-March, aiming for operational production in the 2030s.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Identifies New Porphyry Copper Target at Mineral Mountain
summary: Copper Fox announced preliminary exploration results expanding a drill-ready porphyry copper target at its Mineral Mountain project in Arizona, detailing copper-rich quartz vein mineralization and alteration types consistent with a porphyry system. Whole-rock geochemistry is pending and maiden drilling is planned for October, with no production or supply impacts stated.

title: AAL Headlines - Anglo American's Brazil nickel sale to MMG gets antitrust approval
summary: Brazil’s antitrust authority CADE has dismissed its investigation into Anglo American’s planned sale of its nickel operations in the country to MMG’s unit. The approval clears a regulatory hurdle for the deal, but the article provides no clear, immediate signal of changes in nickel supply, production, or inventories.

title: As Zambia Aims to Triple Copper Output, a Skills Deficit Puts Jobs at Risk
summary: Zambia plans to triple copper output by 2031 to serve green technology and EV demand. The World Bank expects large job creation, but a reported skills gap exceeding 60% in critical areas could limit productivity and lead to foreign hiring. The piece calls for training reforms and curriculum upgrades.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Initiates Largest Ever Drill Program at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona
summary: Faraday Copper Corp. began its 40,000-m Phase IV drill program at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona after expanding approved drill pads on federal land. The work targets further oxide resource growth and additional copper mineralization. The release provides drilling plans and expects assay results as holes are completed.

title: St. Augustine Gold and Copper Limited: St. Augustine Shareholders Approve Amended and Restated Stock Option Plan and Private Placement with Nicolaos Paraskevas
summary: St. Augustine Gold and Copper Limited announced that shareholders approved an amended stock option plan and a private placement with Nicolaos Paraskevas. The company is developing the King-king copper-gold project, but the announcement mainly concerns financing governance rather than immediate copper supply or production changes.

title: Cast Aluminum Alloy Futures Fell During the Week, Warrant Generation Set to Begin May Introduce New Market Variables[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: The weekly review reports cast aluminum alloy futures and secondary aluminium/ADC12 spot prices edging lower, largely driven by weaker primary aluminium and macro volatility tied to intensified US Fed cut expectations. Despite improved supply circulation and some inventory build, pre-holiday stocking and rigid costs provide support, implying high short-term volatility.

title: Copper prices may regain steam on supportive fundamentals and bets on further US rate cuts
summary: The Fed cut rates as expected and markets now price higher odds of additional October/December cuts, providing macro tailwinds for copper. Despite recent weakness and fading confidence above 80,000 yuan/mt, spot demand and smelter/shipment activity increased as prices fell toward 79,500, with National Day procurement expected to improve.

title: Surge Copper Announces Closing of Strategic Private
summary: Surge Copper announced closing a C$4.5 million strategic private placement with African Rainbow Minerals, raising about C$10.4 million in total to advance the Berg Project pre-feasibility study and exploration. The company’s assets are copper-bearing, but no operational or production changes were disclosed, limiting near-term impact on copper prices.

title: Nexmetals Mining Corp. Announces Assay Results from 2 Holes of the 12 Hole Metallurgical Drilling Program Completed At the Past-Producing Copper, Nickel, Cobalt and Platinum Group Elements
summary: NexMetals reported assay results from 2 of 12 metallurgical drill holes at the Selkirk Cu-Ni-Co-PGE mine in Botswana. Core supports ongoing metallurgical testwork, flowsheet optimization, and variability testing at labs in British Columbia. Additional assays from the 2025 program are expected on an ongoing basis.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Pacific Ridge Announces Filing of NI 43-101 Technical Report for Kliyul Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Kliyul copper-gold project, outlining an inferred mineral resource at the KMZ target (including copper grades and CuEq totals) and noting pending assays from 2025 infill drilling. No metallurgical testing, production, or permitting changes were announced.

title: Mount Isa waits for '11th-hour' decision on financial support for copper smelter
summary: Glencore is negotiating with federal and Queensland governments for financial bridging support to rebrick and keep operating the Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville refinery. A decision is due within days; without funding, Glencore says it would stop production next year, risking copper supply.

title: Hazardous copper level at landfill
summary: City officials say fire debris dumped at Calabasas Landfill contained hazardous copper (3,400 mg/kg vs 2,500 threshold) and report related contamination concerns. The case focuses on disposal permits and legal proceedings with Los Angeles County, with no direct implications for copper production, trade, or inventories.

title: Noronex kicks off Namibian drilling program to chart copper horizon
summary: Noronex has begun a 7,000-metre drilling campaign at its Powerline project in Namibia’s Kalahari Copper Belt, targeting copper-bearing horizons identified from aeromagnetic data. Historical results showed low-grade copper intercepts, and South32 funds exploration under an earn-in deal, supporting potential future discoveries that may bolster copper sentiment.

title: Midas Minerals to raise funds for Namibian copper project acquisition
summary: Midas Minerals will raise A$11.5m via a share placement to acquire Namibia’s Otavi Copper Project and accelerate exploration at Otavi and South Otavi, plus working capital. The company expects acquisition completion next quarter and notes drilling already underway. The financing supports copper activity but not immediate supply changes.

title: Namibia Approves $24 Million Sale of Kombat Copper Mine
summary: Namibia’s Competition Commission approved Trigon Metals’ $24 million sale of its 80% stake in the Kombat copper mine to Horizon. Deal finalization depends on TSX Venture Exchange approval. Kombat, restarted in 2023 after being idled, was suspended in January; the buyer signals a restart/expansion phase.

title: BHP Group (BHP) Remains Cautious on Big Deals, Focuses on Copper Growth Amid Anglo-Teck Merger
summary: BHP is portrayed as cautious on large M&A but actively pursuing copper growth, including higher production at Chile’s Escondida and a $2 billion stake in Argentina’s Josemaria mine. It also notes the Anglo American–Teck merger targeting a copper-focused powerhouse, which could underpin near-term bullish copper sentiment.

title: Hindustan Copper Ltd, Oil India join hands to explore critical and strategic minerals
summary: Hindustan Copper Ltd and Oil India Ltd signed an MoU to collaborate on exploring and developing critical and strategic minerals, including copper, to improve India’s mineral self-reliance. The move follows Cabinet approval of a Rs 1,500 crore incentive under the National Critical Mineral Mission to expand recycling capacity from scrap sources.

title: 【SMM News】Nickel intermediate products were affected by both nickel prices and supply-demand dynamics, with prices showing an upward trend this week.
summary: SMM reports tight spot availability for nickel intermediate products (MHP) and scarce tradable high-grade nickel matte, boosting sellers’ bargaining power. Demand improved as downstream users entered peak procurement. Rising cobalt sulphate and sulphur prices increased cost coefficients, while macro factors lifted LME nickel. Overall, nickel prices rose week-on-week.

title: Hindustan Copper Oil India Partner on Critical Minerals Exploration
summary: Oil India and Hindustan Copper signed an MoU to collaborate on exploration and development of critical minerals, explicitly including copper, to support India’s mineral security goals. The government also approved an Rs 1,500 crore NCMM incentive scheme to expand recycling capacity for critical minerals from e-waste and scrap sources.

title: Administration Opens Process to Expand Section 232 Duties to Additional Steel and Aluminum Derivative Products and Automobile Parts | Polsinelli
summary: BIS opened a new process to expand U.S. Section 232 duties on downstream products made from steel and aluminum, continuing the 50% tariff scope effective Aug. 18, 2025. For the first time, it also includes additional passenger-vehicle and light-truck auto parts, potentially supporting aluminum prices.

title: Turning point emerges in the smelting acid market; sulfuric acid revenue may struggle to support high-load copper smelting. [SMM Analysis]
summary: Since early September, China’s 98% smelting acid prices have declined as fertilizer demand weakened due to falling grain prices, mandated fertilizer-use reductions, slow distributor stocking, and weak industrial compound fertilizer operating rates. Lower by-product sulfuric acid revenue is expected in Q4, pressuring copper smelter margins and operating rates.

title: Policy Watch and Secondary Copper Rod Market Amid Copper Price Volatility: Short-Term Pressure and Resilient Recovery
summary: The report describes secondary copper rod trading amid volatile copper prices after a US Fed 25bp cut. Copper dropped sharply, prompting supplier caution and tighter liquidity in Jiangxi/Anhui due to Document No. 770. Production rates rose on a widening primary-versus-scrap spread, but margins fell; next week may see mild circulation recovery if prices stabilize.

title: Argentina Eyes Copper Boom as Global Demand Surges
summary: Argentina is positioning its large copper reserves for expanded production, citing IEA warnings of a future supply shortfall and introducing the RIGI investment incentive. It notes major planned projects (including Glencore) and infrastructure barriers. The piece is supply-expectations oriented, but largely long-horizon, limiting immediate price pressure.

title: Policy and Market Game in the Secondary Copper Rod Industry: Short-Term Pain and Long-Term Restructuring
summary: Secondary copper rod operating rates have risen as production resumed in Tianjin and Anhui, but remained shut in Jiangxi amid policy uncertainty tied to NDRC Reform No. 770, potentially raising effective taxes. The supply gap tightened, narrowing discounts versus copper futures and lifting gross profit, while downstream demand stayed cautious.

title: Chinese Secondary Copper Rod Industry Faces Short-Term Pain and Long-Term Restructuring
summary: China’s secondary copper rod output is constrained as Jiangxi firms largely shut down pending policy clarity, while Tianjin/Anhui resume operations. The supply gap has tightened, narrowing the spread versus copper futures and lifting weekly gross profit, despite higher effective tax risk under the No. 770 policy cleanup.

title: 【SMM Analysis】190 Mining Companies Temporarily Sanctioned by ESDM: Current Impact and Updates Towards Nickel Ore Producers
summary: Indonesia’s ESDM issued administrative sanctions and temporarily suspended 190 mining companies over failure to provide reclamation guarantees, including multiple nickel producers. SMM says these specific firms’ quotas are small and current supply-chain impact is limited, but regulatory tightening and sentiment could support higher nickel ore prices near term.

title: Copper prices rise on Grasberg supply risks
summary: Copper prices edged higher as investors weighed potential disruption at Freeport-McMoRan’s Grasberg mine in Indonesia, where underground operations were suspended after an incident trapped workers. With Grasberg a key supplier, any prolonged halt could tighten a constrained market, supporting near-term bullish sentiment.

title: Copper thefts are soaring in Missouri, as Trump's tariffs drive up the price
summary: AT&T investigators say copper thefts are rising in Missouri because copper prices are soaring. The article attributes the jump to Trump’s 50% tariff on all copper imports, imposed Aug. 1, which helped push copper to a July record high. Prices later eased but remain above a year ago.

title: Special report: Is Oman's future paved with copper?
summary: A report highlights Oman’s Vision 2040 push to revive copper, including the first export of Lasail copper concentrates in 2025 and plans to restart other mines. It also describes upgraded logistics and a recycling facility producing copper cathodes, potentially affecting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Export Data for August: Exports Up 10.87% MoM
summary: China’s customs data show copper plate/sheet and strip exports rose 10.87% month-on-month in August 2025 to 11,675.75 mt, despite a 6.49% year-on-year decline. Shipments grew in key markets like South Korea and Malaysia, while others (Vietnam, Thailand, US) fell sharply.

title: US Copper Scrap Further Fades as Japan and Thailand Maintain Dominance
summary: The report says US copper scrap prices have “further faded,” while Japan and Thailand maintain dominance in the scrap market. Falling scrap values usually signal weaker scrap pricing/market conditions, which can weigh on near-term copper sentiment by influencing expectations for recycled copper availability and scrap-linked costs.

title: Glencore offered a taxpayer funded bail-out of Mount Isa copper smelter by Queensland and federal governments
summary: Australia’s federal and Queensland governments have offered a taxpayer-funded bail-out to Glencore to keep the Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery operating. The plan aims to preserve about 600 jobs and avoid forecast multi-year losses, influencing expectations for copper supply and refining availability.

title: Indonesia halts 25 nickel mines in southeast Sulawesi
summary: Indonesia’s energy ministry sanctioned and temporarily suspended 25 nickel mining firms in southeast Sulawesi for inadequate reclamation and post-mining guarantees, with licence suspensions across other minerals as well. The action is expected to be limited for active output but increases concern over Indonesia nickel ore supply, pressuring nickel prices.

title: Glencore explores sale of majority stake in Kamoto Copper Company
summary: Glencore is discussing selling its 70% majority stake in the Kamoto Copper Company in the DRC, a key copper and cobalt project with royalty disputes and operational challenges. Talks may reflect shifts in risk and sanctions complexity, but no sale is formalized yet, limiting immediate copper-price pressure.

title: Kincora Secures Full Rights to the Mongolian Copper-Gold Portfolio
summary: Kincora Copper resecured full rights to its Mongolian copper-gold portfolio after Orbminco withdrew from an earn-in agreement. With 100% ownership, it plans near-term value-adding steps including possible additional mining license submissions and fresh studies for an oxide resource and potential SX-EW copper cathode development. The Supreme Court case continues.

title: August refined-copper imports fell short of expectations, and export volumes dropped sharply
summary: China’s August refined-copper imports were 264,300 tonnes, down 10.99% MoM and below market expectations, with DRC volumes falling. Exports dropped 68.93% MoM, and arbitrage flows to the US effectively ended. September arrivals are expected to stabilize, partly offset by other sources.

title: Expert says Canada needs more copper as Creighton mine joins national plan
summary: Canada’s federal government included the Foran McIlvenna Bay (Saskatchewan) copper project in its critical minerals strategy, citing a copper deficit for electrification. The billion-dollar mine is 50% built, with mid-2026 production targeted. Geologist Kathryn Bethune says recycling won’t cover demand, highlighting supply tightness.

title: Investment funds bet price of nickel has hit rock bottom
summary: Nickel prices have been stuck near five-year lows amid a large oversupply from Indonesia, reflected in rising LME inventories. Despite the weak backdrop, investment funds have reduced shorts and built long positions since mid-April, betting on a potential recovery if Indonesia reins in production via regulation and quotas.

title: Three people arrested in connection with copper wire thefts
summary: Maryland State Police arrested three people tied to a series of copper wire thefts that cut copper telecom cable from active power poles in Cecil County. The thefts caused communication outages and about $66,000 in estimated losses and damages. Several related investigations remain ongoing, suggesting continued local incidents.

title: Ancient copper craftsmanship vs. the AI era: Sertodo fights tariffs while revolutionizing wellness with hand-hammered antibacterial vessels   – NaturalNews.com
summary: NaturalNews.com claims the U.S. faces looming 50% tariffs on imported copper and says this could “cripple” small artisans like Sertodo Copper. Because the tariff increases the cost of copper imports, the article implies near-term tighter supply and higher copper prices.

title: Aluminum Prices Hit 6-Month High as Supply Concerns Grow
summary: Aluminum prices hit a 6-month high as LME breaks out on supply deficit fears that China’s output is nearing its production cap. Despite soft Chinese domestic demand and rising production data, inventories remain low and Russian material supply is constrained by sanctions, supporting a near-term bullish tone.

title: Mining company says drilling confirms 'significant' copper, gold in Wisconsin
summary: GreenLight Metals reports early drilling at the Bend deposit in Wisconsin confirms significant copper-bearing sulfides and notable gold, with results on additional holes expected in 3–4 weeks. The company plans further drilling and permits, but no economic development or production timeline is set, limiting near-term supply impact on metals markets.

title: Mining Company Says Drilling Finds Copper, Gold in Northwoods
summary: GreenLight Metals’ preliminary drilling in northern Wisconsin found high-grade copper (plus gold and tellurium) at the Bend deposit, but environmental experts warn the sample is small and uneconomic potential is uncertain. Further results are expected in 3–4 weeks, with more drilling planned for later periods.

title: Queensland Alumina fined $1 million after caustic chemical release in Gladstone
summary: Queensland Alumina Limited (QAL) was fined $1 million after a high-pressure system rupture at its Gladstone alumina refinery released caustic chemicals in 2022, triggering over $800,000 in insurance claims. QAL apologised and upgraded equipment, suggesting improved prevention of similar operational disruptions.

title: Industry ministry discusses response to possible expansion of US tariffs on steel, aluminum derivatives with companies
summary: South Korea’s industry ministry met companies to plan a response to possible US expansion of 50% tariffs on steel and aluminum derivative products and further tariff scrutiny of auto parts. The US process to include additional items may close next week, potentially worsening export demand for aluminum-linked products and weighing on prices.

title: China's August Copper Anode Imports Pulled Back Sharply, Scrap Copper Ingot Imports "Surged" in 2025 [SMM Analysis]
summary: Customs data show China’s August 2025 copper anode imports fell 26.7% MoM (and 18.7% YoY) amid timing effects from the SHFE/LME ratio and smelter maintenance/demand. In contrast, scrap copper ingot imports rose 17% MoM and 75% YoY, suggesting more feedstock flowing to smelting and possible September rebound.

title: Mining company: Drilling confirms 'significant' copper, gold in northern Wisconsin | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: GreenLight Metals says early drilling at its Bend deposit in northern Wisconsin confirmed significant copper-bearing sulfides (with gold and tellurium). The company drilled six holes and expects more assay results in three to four weeks. Further drilling, permitting, and economic studies are needed before any potential development.

title: Kibaha copper, nickel industry nearing completion
summary: A copper and nickel sorting/processing plant by Coast Nickel Industry Limited in Kikongo, Tanzania, is nearing completion and is expected to start operations by January. The $7m project supports local value addition and cites issues like power reliability and road infrastructure, but it is not yet producing, limiting near-term price impact.

title: China's Copper Foil Customs Details for August 2025: Steady Growth in Both Imports and Exports [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s copper foil imports rose to 6,822.56 mt in August 2025 (+2.94% YoY, +5.41% MoM) and import value also increased. Copper foil exports climbed sharply (+28.96% YoY, +16.56% MoM) with higher export value, suggesting improving end-demand and supportive copper market balance.

title: Southern Copper eyes steady production in Peru, bets big on new projects
summary: Southern Copper said its Peru copper output is expected to remain roughly the same this year while it invests $800 million in projects. It operates Toquepala and Cuajone and is progressing planned developments like Tia Maria and Michiquillay, though some face delays from protests.

title: Global Copper Demand Projected to Outpace Supply by Over 500,000 Tonnes In 2025, Driving Upward Price Pressure
summary: The piece forecasts a copper market deficit in 2025, with demand expected to outstrip supply by about 400,000 tonnes due to persistent supply constraints and growing grid, electrification, renewables, and agricultural modernization demand. It also cites multiple copper project/drilling updates, reinforcing a bullish copper supply-demand outlook.

title: MarketNewsUpdates: Global Copper Demand Projected to Outpace Supply by Over 500,000 Tonnes In 2025, Driving Upward Price Pressure
summary: The piece says global copper demand is projected to exceed supply by roughly 300,000–500,000 tonnes in 2025 (about 400,000 tonnes), citing industry/ICSG estimates. It links the imbalance to grid, EV, renewables and agricultural electrification, forecasting higher copper prices versus 2024 and a trading range into October.

title: Rusal may participate in reconstruction of an aluminum smelter in Egypt
summary: Rusal says it is negotiating with EgyptAlum and Egyptian government representatives on cooperation, including technology transfer and assistance to reconstruct and modernize the 310,000-ton aluminum smelter in Egypt. The company cites its expertise in upgrading facilities, but no investment size or production ramp-up timeline is confirmed.

title: 3 arrested after copper wire theft prompts communications outages in Cecil County
summary: Maryland State Police arrested three people for stealing Verizon copper wire from power poles in Cecil County, causing communications outages and about $66,000 in losses. The investigation references similar regional thefts, but reported amounts are relatively small, suggesting limited immediate impact on broader copper pricing.

title: Copper Market Roiled by Tariff Twist: A Deep Dive into Price Volatility and Policy Impact
summary: Trump’s sudden exemption of refined copper from a planned 50% US import tariff overturned expectations that had driven heavy pre-tariff stockpiling. The removal of the arbitrage premium led to a record 22% COMEX copper futures collapse in one day, followed by partial stabilization in LME prices.

title: Copper Giants Unite: Anglo American and Teck Resources Forge "Anglo Teck" Amidst Surging Demand
summary: Anglo American and Teck Resources plan to merge into “Anglo Teck,” a copper-focused producer with over 70% exposure to copper. Management expects sizable annual synergies and higher copper output, aiming to address a projected supply deficit tied to energy-transition demand. Markets reacted positively to the deal announcement.

title: Copper's Crucible: Green Energy, AI, and EVs Ignite a Potential Super Cycle
summary: The piece links electrification, renewables, EVs, grid buildout, and expanding AI/data centers to sharply rising copper demand while supply is portrayed as constrained. It highlights tightening fundamentals and recent copper strength, suggesting markets are beginning to price a growing deficit and supporting upward price pressure.

title: Global Copper Supply in Crisis: El Teniente Halt Deepens Shortage Amidst Cobre Panama Closure and Codelco Woes
summary: Chile’s El Teniente mine was shut down after a fatal collapse, with an estimated immediate copper output loss and only partial restart by mid-August. This follows the Cobre Panama permanent closure. Combined disruptions deepen global copper deficits, driving LME price volatility and an upward trend on tight supply expectations.

title: Visionary Metals Corp.: Visionary Announces Closing of Private Placement of $1.22M to Advance Wyoming Nickel Sulfide Exploration
summary: Visionary Metals Corp. said TSXV approved a $1.22M private placement with Teck to fund initial exploration on its Granite Mountains nickel sulfide project in Wyoming. Teck subscribed for about 17.4M shares at $0.07, subject to a four-month hold. Proceeds will support early exploration activities.

title: AT&T offering a reward for copper thefts across Missouri
summary: AT&T is offering rewards up to $20,000 in Missouri to help stop copper theft targeting telecommunications infrastructure. The report cites thousands of copper-theft incidents nationwide in 2025 and $2.21 million in losses in Missouri, linking theft to service disruptions. It does not indicate broader supply shocks.

title: Visionary Announces Closing of Private Placement of $1.22M to Advance Wyoming Nickel Sulfide Exploration
summary: Visionary Metals Corp. announced TSX Venture approval for a $1.22M private placement with Teck Resources to fund initial nickel sulfide exploration in Wyoming. Teck buys 17.39M shares at $0.07, subject to a four-month hold. Proceeds support early exploration only, without any immediate supply change.

title: BHP, Brookfield's Neoen Sign New Renewable-Power Deal for Copper South Australia
summary: BHP signed a new renewable-power baseload deal with Neoen/Brookfield for 100 MW to supply its Copper South Australia assets, including Olympic Dam’s smelter and refinery. The agreement expands existing renewable supply, supporting lower emissions and expectations to meet ~70% of power needs with renewables by 2030.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Signs Letter of Intent with Defense and Mineral Exploration Tech Start-Up Lunasonde to Assess Its Revolutionary Technology to Explore for Copper, Other Critical Minerals, and Rare Earth Elements in Arizona's Cochise
summary: Gunnison Copper Corp. announced first copper cathode sales from its operational Johnson Camp Mine in Arizona, totaling 225,371 pounds at an average realized price of $4.64/lb, generating about $1.0m in gross proceeds. It also notes capacity up to 25 million lbs annually and future Nuton bio-leaching deployment.

title: Copper prices stable as supply risks from Peru mount
summary: London and COMEX copper prices are largely steady as investors weigh growing Peru supply risks. Political protests and road blockades have disrupted copper mines and smelters, prompting Hudbay to halt production at the Constancia mine, increasing concern over near-term copper availability and supporting a bullish bias.

title: Copper supported by supply tensions despite abundant stocks
summary: Copper rose 0.1% on Tuesday as supply tensions (Grasberg production suspension in Indonesia) outweighed stock accumulation. US Comex reserves jumped on tariff expectations, keeping the outlook fragile. A Fed rate cut improved sentiment. Nickel gained on Indonesia permit suspensions, while aluminium eased slightly.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: Slam Drilling for Copper, Nickel and Cobalt on Granges Zone at Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration reports diamond drilling underway at its Goodwin Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Project in New Brunswick, targeting an eastward extension of the Granges copper-nickel zone. The company cites prior drilling grades (not new results) and IP anomaly follow-ups, but the release does not provide fresh assay outcomes.

title: Freeport: Q3 Sales To Be Lower For Copper, Gold Than Prior Estimates
summary: Freeport Indonesia is investigating a mud-rush incident at the Grasberg Block Cave mine, and has issued a force majeure due to operational impacts. The company expects Q3 consolidated copper sales to be about 4% lower than prior July estimates, indicating near-term supply disruption and downside pressure for copper prices.

title: Copper and oil gains aid FTSE 100 after drab open
summary: FTSE 100 gained as miners and oil majors rose. Copper firmed 2.7% to about $4.70 per pound, lifting Antofagasta, Anglo American and Glencore. The move was supported by Freeport-McMoRan saying suspension of its large Indonesian copper mine will reduce output, tightening near-term supply expectations.

title: Copper and oil gains aid FTSE 100 after lacklustre opening
summary: FTSE 100 ended higher as copper and oil rose. The article attributes gains in miners like Antofagasta, Anglo American and Glencore to a copper price spike (up 2.7% to around $4.70/lb). It also cites Freeport-McMoRan suspending its Indonesian copper mine, implying lower output.

title: Copper Jumps as Freeport Declares Indonesia Mine Force Majeure
summary: Copper jumped after Freeport declared force majeure at its Indonesian Grasberg mine following an accident that sent about 800,000 tons of mud underground and left five missing workers. The company also cut quarterly copper and gold sales guidance, worsening near-term supply expectations. LME three-month copper rose 3.6% to $10,336.50/ton.

title: Freeport declares force majeure at Grasberg, expects lower copper, gold sales
summary: Freeport-McMoRan declared force majeure at its Grasberg mine in Indonesia after a wet-material blockage restricted underground evacuation routes. The company expects consolidated Q3 copper sales to be about 4% lower than previously forecast. Analysts said this could contribute to a tighter copper market, but guidance cuts imply immediate bearish pressure.

title: Freeport shares tumble, copper futures rise due to Indonesia mine accident
summary: Freeport shares fell after it cut guidance due to an Indonesia mine accident. Despite the equity selloff, the report states copper futures rose, reflecting market expectations of disrupted copper supply from the incident and potential tighter near-term availability for copper buyers.

title: Copper prices at 15-month high after Freeport declares force majeure at Indonesian mine
summary: Freeport-McMoRan declared force majeure at its Indonesian Grasberg mine after an accident and flooding killed workers and halted much of production. The miner expects lower third-quarter copper sales and phased restarts into 2026. Copper futures jumped about 4% to a 15-month high.

title: "A Black Swan Event": Copper Prices Soar After FCX Declares Force Majeure At World's 2nd Largest Mine
summary: Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) declared force majeure for contracted copper supplies from its Grasberg mine in Indonesia after an accident caused a major mud intrusion and fatalities. The halt and downgraded copper sales guidance tighten near-term supply, pushing LME three-month copper up about 3.7% intraday.

title: Copper's September Slowdown: A Bellwether for Global Economic Health
summary: September 2025 copper prices slowed amid tepid sentiment, weaker Chinese refined copper import data (August -10.99% MoM), and a policy reversal exempting refined copper from a 50% U.S. import tariff. Supply shocks (Freeport Grasberg force majeure, Hudbay Constancia halt) were outweighed, contributing to volatility and a major U.S. price fall.

title: Chile's Path to a Responsible 2026 Budget Amidst Codelco's Copper Recovery
summary: Chile’s Finance Minister Nicolas Grau outlined a “responsible” 2026 budget with moderate spending growth and higher investment in carbon-neutral projects. The government highlighted permitting reforms important for mining and energy, while state-run Codelco seeks to recover copper output with partnerships to address production gaps, supporting copper sentiment.

title: Three charged after copper-wire theft; one suspect at large, Adams County deputies say
summary: Authorities in Adams County, Mississippi charged three people after roughly 400 feet of 400-pair copper wire (and fiber lines) was stolen and linked to sale at regional recycling centers. The sheriff’s office says the copper had about a $2,800 retail value, with additional repair costs.

title: The Overnight Report: Copper Surges, Rally Pauses
summary: Copper jumped as supply risks resurfaced. LME three-month copper futures surged past $10,000/t after Freeport-McMoRan declared force majeure on contracted Grasberg mine supplies in Indonesia following a mud flow into underground levels. Freeport cut Q3 output expectations and signaled further 2026 production reductions.

title: BHP (ASX BHP), Rio Tinto soar with copper price after mud slide at Freeport-McMoRan mine hits supply
summary: BHP and Rio Tinto stocks rose with copper after Freeport-McMoRan declared force majeure on contracted supplies from its Grasberg mine in Indonesia following a mud slide. Copper jumped about 3.6% on the LME to above $10,300/ton, reflecting fresh short-term supply concerns.

title: Goldman Sachs downgrades copper supply forecast after Grasberg mine disruption
summary: Goldman Sachs lowered its 2025 and 2026 global copper mine supply forecasts after a disruption at Indonesia’s Grasberg trapped workers in September. The bank estimates a large copper supply loss, worsens the 2025 balance to a deficit, and notes upside risks to its LME copper price outlook, implying bullish near-term pressure.

title: Europe's Water Framework Directive and the Nickel Environmental Quality Standard risks undermining its Green Ambitions
summary: The article warns the EU could halve the Environmental Quality Standard for nickel in surface waters, setting limits below natural background levels. It claims this would penalize compliant industries and deter mining, refining, and recycling permits, reducing nickel supply and increasing uncertainty during Europe’s EV and battery push.

title: Nickel Mining Threatens Indonesia Coral Haven, NGOs Warn
summary: NGOs warn that nickel mining in Indonesia’s Raja Ampat could damage coral reefs and that rehabilitation is poor, despite Indonesia revoking permits for four of five mining companies. One firm was allowed to restart, but activists fear mining could continue or resume, implying possible nickel supply disruption.

title: Hot Chili chases copper-gold monsters in Chilean copper homeland
summary: Hot Chili is stepping up drilling at its La Verde copper-gold discovery near its Costa Fuego plant in Chile, targeting higher-grade extensions that could add open-pit ore. The push is framed by rising copper prices and tight supply sentiment following Indonesia’s Grasberg mudslide, which disrupted production.

title: Nickel mining threatens Indonesia coral haven, NGOs warn - Archipelago
summary: NGOs warn that nickel mining around Indonesia’s Raja Ampat threatens coral reefs via deforestation and sediment runoff, despite Indonesia revoking permits for four of five mining companies in Southwest Papua. One firm restarted after mitigation claims, but activists fear damage and possible further mining disruption, influencing nickel supply expectations.

title: Canyon Resources Raises CFA85.3B for Minim Martap Bauxite, Afriland Joins as Investor
summary: Canyon Resources secured A$215m to accelerate its Minim Martap bauxite project in Cameroon, including increased funding for the Camrail logistics link to the Port of Douala. The company plans staged development toward first shipments in 1H 2026, which can support expectations for future aluminum supply and sentiment.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Doubles RPM Zone Strike Length to 800
summary: First Atlantic Nickel reports a step-out drill hole (AN-25-08) extending the RPM Zone strike length to 800 meters and confirming long intervals of visibly disseminated awaruite. Metallurgical DTR testing shows magnetically recoverable nickel concentrates with stated average DTR nickel grade of 0.12%, supporting improved recovery expectations.

title: Copper Climbs as Freeport Mine Accident Worries Market
summary: Copper rose in early trading after Freeport-McMoRan issued force majeure on contracted supplies from its Grasberg mine in Indonesia. Analysts cited the mine’s large share of Freeport’s output and global supply. The supply disruption concern is driving near-term bullish expectations for copper prices.

title: China studies how to regulate copper smelting capacity, industry association says
summary: China is studying tighter regulation of copper smelting capacity after record-low concentrate processing fees squeezed smelters’ profits. The state-backed industry association cited destructive “involution-style” competition and proposed measures to limit capacity expansion. The report notes that LME copper rose on the day amid tighter concentrate availability concerns.

title: JP Morgan Predicts Further Rise in Copper Prices
summary: JP Morgan says disruptions at Indonesia’s Grasberg copper mine, including Freeport’s force majeure after a September landslide, are worse than expected and will tighten supply over coming quarters. The bank raises its copper price outlook, forecasting higher LME averages for late 2025 and early 2026 amid recent 3-month copper strength.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Announces First Copper Sales from Johnson Camp Mine
summary: Gunnison Copper announced first sales of pure copper cathode from its Johnson Camp Mine in Arizona, selling 225,371 lbs at an average realized price of $4.64/lb for about $1.0 million gross proceeds. The mine is ramping toward 25 million lbs/year capacity, supporting domestic supply.

title: Oscillate Plc - Kalahari Copper Limited acquisition expanded to include prospective copper portfolio in Namibia and Updated Heads of Terms
summary: Oscillate Plc said it expanded the Kalahari Copper acquisition to include additional prospective copper licences in Namibia, adjacent to existing copper operations. The update covers due diligence, licence renewals, royalty terms, and milestone payments tied to copper resource milestones and feasibility work.

title: Rudi's View: Don't Fight The Fed, Inflation, Gold, Copper & More
summary: The piece argues copper has risen sharply recently and points to emerging production problems at Grasberg, one of the world’s largest supply sources. That supply concern is presented as supportive for mining companies with copper exposure, with Shaw and partners highlighting multiple “pure play” copper names.

title: Copper Surges as Freeport Mine Accident Clouds Global Supply Outlook -- Commodities Roundup
summary: Copper prices extended gains after Freeport-McMoRan declared force majeure on contracted supplies from its Grasberg mine in Indonesia following a fatal mudslide. Analysts warned a prolonged disruption could lift copper further and worsen smelter feedstock shortages, with LME three-month copper rising in midday trade.

title: Southern Copper (SCCO) Hits Fresh High as Metal Price Soars to 15-Month High
summary: Southern Copper shares jumped to a fresh 52-week high as copper prices rallied to a 15-month high. The move followed Freeport-McMoran declaring force majeure at the Grasberg mine in Indonesia, raising expectations of tighter global copper supply. The LME three-month copper index rose sharply during the session.

title: Copper Surges as Freeport Mine Accident Clouds -2-
summary: Copper jumped after Freeport declared force majeure on contracted supplies from its Grasberg mine in Indonesia. The update revived supply concerns, citing Grasberg’s share of global supply and Freeport production. LME copper rose to the highest level in over a year, while related London miner shares also increased.

title: Gainers & Losers: Hindustan Copper among 6 stocks that moved most on Thursday. Here's why
summary: Indian markets ended lower, but Hindustan Copper shares jumped 6.25% after global copper prices spiked following the suspension of production at Grasberg, the world’s second-largest copper mine operated by Freeport-McMoRan. The news points to tighter near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Copper Surges as Freeport Mine Accident Clouds Global Supply Outlook — Commodities Roundup
summary: The commodities roundup headline says copper surged as a Freeport mine accident raised uncertainty about global supply. Such disruption risk can tighten near-term expectations for copper availability, supporting prices. The article itself appears unavailable, so details are limited beyond the stated supply-outlook effect.

title: Super Copper Forges Future: CEO Dolesky Unveils Ambitious Chilean Copper Strategy and Pioneering Crypto Treasury
summary: Super Copper CEO Zachary Dolesky outlined an aggressive Chile copper strategy, including acquiring and expanding the Castilla copper land package in the Atacama region. The company also plans to allocate up to 20% of excess cash to Bitcoin. The news is largely corporate and not tied to near-term copper supply changes.

title: Cameroon's First Bauxite Mine, Minim Martap, Secures Key $141M Financing Plan
summary: Canyon Resources secured about $141M to accelerate its Minim Martap bauxite project in Cameroon and increase investment in the rail link to the Port of Douala. The funding supports feasibility-backed reserve growth and logistics certainty, improving near-term supply expectations for aluminium feedstock.

title: Oscillate's Kalahari acquisition to include copper portfolio
summary: Oscillate PLC agreed revised terms to acquire 100% ownership of Kalahari Copper’s Namibian and Botswana copper exploration licences, including projects in the Kaoko Basin and the Kalahari Copper Belt. The company frames it as a strategic step toward becoming a mid-cap copper explorer, but no production is described.

title: KCUR Blames Prez Trump For Rise In Traditional Missouri Copper Theft
summary: The piece says copper wire thefts are rising in Missouri and Kansas City, arguing the surge is tied to a 50% Trump tariff on copper imports that has lifted the metal’s value. It also notes meth-related drivers and reduced ability to deflect blame, but the copper-price link is central.

title: Copper Miners Surge as Grasberg Force Majeure Rattles Global Supply Chains
summary: A force majeure after a mudslide shut Indonesia’s Grasberg copper mine, cutting supply from a major ~3% global output source. Freeport signals minimal copper sales in Q4 and prolonged disruption into 2026. LME copper futures jumped above key resistance, reflecting immediate bullish tightness expectations for copper.

title: Nickel mining legacy haunts coral haven
summary: NGOs warn that nickel mining in Indonesia’s Raja Ampat threatens coral reefs despite permit revocations for four of five companies and a partial restart by PT Gag Nikel. They cite poor rehabilitation, sediment runoff, and fear mining could resume, implying potential disruption risk for near-term nickel supply.

title: Arconic Corporation celebrates commissioning of new high purity aluminum facility
summary: Arconic commissioned a new high-purity aluminium facility at its Davenport Works plant, doubling onsite HPA capacity. The ramp reduces the company’s reliance on importing HPA from foreign smelters. The project was supported by a U.S. Department of Defense award under Defense Production Act Title III, for aviation and defense supply needs.

title: New Opportunities For Public Comments On Auto Parts, Steel, And Aluminum Tariff Inclusions And USMCA Review
summary: Federal Register notices opened processes to request inclusion of additional auto parts in 25% Section 232 tariffs and derivative steel/aluminum products in 50% tariffs, with deadlines in September/October 2025 and analysis following public comment. Expansion of tariff scope for aluminum-containing products could reduce aluminum imports and support US aluminum prices.

title: Thieves targeting copper are damaging fiber cables, leading to outages
summary: The report says California leads the U.S. in copper wire theft, with frequent incidents cutting communications infrastructure and causing service outages. It notes thieves often damage fiber lines to access copper wiring, increasing repair burdens for providers like Spectrum. The recurring theft can imply reduced copper end-use demand, though at local scale.

title: Freeport sees copper, gold output plunge after Grasberg landslide - Companies
summary: Freeport Indonesia reported a September landslide at its Grasberg Block Cave that damaged infrastructure and suspended operations. Near-term copper sales are projected to be ~4% lower in Q3 versus July estimates, with Q4 copper expected to be negligible. A phased restart is planned, supporting bullish prompt copper expectations.

title: 2025 National Day Holiday Copper Processing Enterprise Holiday Survey—Brass Billet
summary: SMM’s survey of Chinese brass billet producers finds production staffing reduced for 3–5 days and overall pre-holiday copper billet stockpiling was weak. Intensified customs checks tightened secondary brass supply, while rapidly rising SHFE copper (over 83,000 yuan/mt) reduced downstream buying, leaving a wait-and-see mood post-holiday.

title: 2025 National Day Holiday Survey on Copper Processing Enterprises — Copper Pipe & Tube
summary: SMM reports sluggish October output for copper pipe & tube firms, with more holidays and limited new orders amid very high copper prices. It attributes weaker H2 to falling air-conditioner domestic/export schedules and reduced US-bound pipe & tube exports after US tariffs, weighing on enterprise operating rates.

title: Copper prices projected to reach $11,700 per metric tonnes amid supply concerns
summary: Copper is projected to rise to about $11,700/tonne due to tightening supply.
