The surge is linked to a mudflow at Freeport-McMoRan’s Grasberg mine, force majeure on shipments, halted operations, and additional refining bottlenecks and lower China refined output, with inventories at multi-year lows.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Sep 26
summary: SMM reports Indonesian nickel ore prices stable, but high-nickel pig iron (10–12% NPI) started trending downward. Demand for stainless steel is weaker with slowed destocking, while upstream inventories rise and smelter margins decline. With seasonal support fading and higher coking coal/electricity costs, NPI prices are expected to keep easing near China’s National Day.

title: Antamina forecasts 20% rise in copper output by 2026
summary: Antamina’s Peru copper mine forecasts output rising 20% to 450,000 tonnes in 2026 from about 380,000t this year, with production stabilizing near 400,000t annually afterward. The company also plans a $2bn expansion approved by Peru, extending operations and processing from 2027.

title: Copper Prices Surge to $11,700 Amid Global Supply Crunch
summary: Copper prices are surging as a mudflow at Freeport-McMoRan’s Grasberg mine triggers force majeure and indefinite halt of blockcave operations, cutting expected mined output and tightening concentrate supply. Refining bottlenecks, lower China refined production, and multi-year-low inventories further support a strong bullish move in copper futures.

title: The charts indicate this aluminum producer is set for a jump, says Carter Worth
summary: CNBC Pro commentary says Alcoa is positioned for about a 10% stock pop, citing chart recovery room after a tariff-related sell-off low in April. The piece is aimed at trading the equity, not reporting new aluminium supply/demand or pricing fundamentals, so near-term aluminium price impact is uncertain and likely limited.

title: US Sen. Slotkin supports Copperwood Project | News, Sports, Jobs
summary: Michigan budget legislation would provide $50 million for infrastructure to support the Copperwood mine project, including road, power-grid, and telecom upgrades and public access related to the site. Supporters argue it enables job creation and development under Michigan environmental standards, potentially improving expectations for copper supply.

title: McEwen Copper's Los Azules Joins Argentina's Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI)
summary: McEwen Copper said Argentina approved Los Azules to enter the Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI), providing 30-year legal, fiscal and customs stability and tax advantages. The US$2.672bn project is positioned toward feasibility completion and construction, supporting confidence in future high-purity copper cathode output.

title: McEwen Copper's Los Azules Joins Argentina's Large
summary: McEwen Copper said Argentina approved Los Azules to enter the RIGI, providing legal, fiscal and customs stability for 30 years. The copper project in San Juan is positioned toward feasibility completion and construction, improving investment confidence and reducing development risk for future copper cathode supply.

title: Business targeted by copper theft is left reeling
summary: A Kansas City business reports multiple break-ins over recent months, with thieves cutting and stealing copper wiring and spools and selling it to recycling for quick cash. Repairs and damage are said to cost tens of thousands of dollars. The article focuses on theft mitigation rather than broader copper supply changes.

title: Japan Inc. faces broad impact of Trump's steel and aluminum tariffs
summary: The Trump administration expanded U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs to cover about 720 derivative products, including items such as construction equipment and utensils. Japanese companies face heavier compliance burdens as certain aluminum-linked goods become more expensive in the U.S., which can weaken demand and weigh on aluminum-related prices.

title: NSW opposition pushes Chris Minns' government to save Tomago aluminium smelter
summary: NSW opposition is urging the Minns government to keep the Tomago aluminium smelter operating. The move follows internal Labor debate over subsidies for a trade-exposed business. Opposition argues closure would damage the industrial base, suggesting support measures could prevent supply risk and buoy aluminium sentiment.

title: Grasberg Mine Accident Heightens fears of Copper Supply Disruptions [SMM Analysis]
summary: Freeport’s Grasberg slurry accident in Indonesia suspended operations at the world’s second-largest copper mine and may cut 2026 production estimates by up to 35%. While global concentrate balance impact is assessed as limited, concentrate supply disruption fears and resulting smelter demand shifts point to near-term bullish pressure for copper.

title: Survey on Holidays for Copper Processing Enterprises During the National Day Holiday in 2025—Secondary Copper Rod
summary: SMM surveyed secondary copper rod enterprises on holiday operations and stockpiling ahead of the National Day and Mid-Autumn holidays. It notes ample secondary raw materials but low finished inventories and bullish end-user buying. Copper price gains are linked to mine disruptions and expected tighter ore and scrap anode supply, supporting further price strength after the holiday.

title: Cameroon Pension Fund, Canyon in Talks for $36 Million Stake in Minim-Martap Bauxite Project
summary: Cameroon’s public pension fund CNPS and other institutions discuss investing in Canyon Resources’ Minim-Martap bauxite project. The funding would support infrastructure and project launch, with first production and exports expected in 2026. Bauxite quality (alumina-rich) could affect longer-term aluminium feedstock expectations, though near-term impact is limited.

title: The Campbell's Company (CPB) Faces 4% Cost Hit From Steel, Aluminum Tariffs in Fiscal 2026
summary: Campbell’s expects about a 4% cost hit in fiscal 2026 from tariffs on steel and aluminum used in canned goods production. Limited domestic capacity for key steel inputs like tinplate, plus reliance on imports, constrains mitigation. Management may raise prices to offset costs, highlighting near-term aluminum tariff pressure.

title: Ball Corporation : Global Leader in Aluminum Packaging Under Strain
summary: Ball Corporation’s aluminum can business is growing in volumes, but the company warns margins will stay pressured due to cost and pricing challenges, limited pass-through, and regional overcapacity. The news highlights reliance on aluminum packaging and input cost volatility, which can weigh on near-term aluminum demand sentiment.

title: Argentina approves McEwen's $2.7bn copper project under RIGI programme
summary: Argentina approved McEwen Copper’s $2.7bn Los Azules project for RIGI tax incentives, aiming to produce high-purity copper cathodes. The project is expected to restart domestic copper production after dormancy since 2018, but cathode output is targeted for 2029, limiting near-term effects on copper prices.

title: Unchecked nickel mining fuels environmental, social crises - Archipelago
summary: A report by Auriga Nusantara and Earth Insight describes extensive environmental damage linked to Indonesia’s nickel mining in Raja Ampat, including deforestation, coral destruction, and sediment impacts. Groups argue permits and environmental assessments are often rubber-stamped, raising prospects of stronger scrutiny that could disrupt nickel output and weigh on prices.

title: Copper producers await extension of concentrate export permits - Companies
summary: Indonesia’s major copper concentrate producers are seeking extensions/renewals of export permits. PT Amman Mineral Nusa Tenggara has operated since its permit expired Dec. 31, while PT Freeport Indonesia’s permit lapsed Sept. 16 without clarity on renewal. Officials evaluate requests, adding near-term supply uncertainty for copper.

title: Royal Road Minerals Unearths Game-Changing Gold-Copper Porphyry in Colombia
summary: Royal Road Minerals announced a 303.7m gold-copper porphyry intersection at its Güíntar-Margaritas project in Colombia, including a 62m zone assaying 0.6% copper. The discovery boosts investor confidence in a potential large copper resource, but it is unlikely to materially affect near-term copper supply or prices.

title: Copper's Ascent: 'New Gold' Nears All-Time High Amid Green Revolution Demand
summary: Copper prices are surging toward all-time highs, with LME settlements above $10,180/ton and CME futures near $10,640/ton. The move is driven by rapid green-energy/EV demand alongside ongoing supply shortages, including mine disruptions such as Grasberg and tighter regulations. Prices are expected to stay firm despite volatility.

LME three-month futures hit 16-month highs, reflecting accelerating supply deficit risks.

title: Five charged with gang robbery, abetment over copper ingot theft in Seremban
summary: Five people were charged in Seremban for gang robbery and abetment involving the theft of 62 copper ingots from a company. Two were charged with abetting the theft. Bail was set pending the next court mention, but the report provides no evidence of wider supply disruption.

title: Copper retreats after 16-month high amid profit-taking
summary: Copper retreated after hitting a 16-month high around $10,800/ton, with the benchmark contract down about 0.7% to $10,636. Profit-taking followed a Golden Week slowdown in China, while a stronger US dollar reduced demand. Despite ongoing mine disruptions, Goldman sees slight short-term oversupply limiting upside.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Reports 71,266 Tonnes of Copper Produced by Kamoa-Kakula in Q3 2025; Recovery Efforts Advancing Well
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reported Q3 2025 copper production of about 71,226 tonnes from Kamoa-Kakula, with copper guidance maintained. Stage-two dewatering is over 20% complete and expected to finish by end-November. Start-up of Africa’s largest direct-to-blister copper smelter is scheduled for early November.

title: NorthWest Announces First Drill Results from 2025 Program and Highlights 44 Metres of 2.81 G/T Gold and 0.66% Copper
summary: NorthWest Copper announced initial 2025 diamond drill results at the Kwanika project, including 44 metres at 0.66% copper (and associated gold). The company says results support a higher-grade target model and potential economics improvements. The update is exploration-only, with no near-term supply or trade impact.

title: Copper: Hudbay resumes operations at Peru's mine
summary: Hudbay has resumed operations at its Peru mine following protests that had disrupted activity. The restart improves near-term copper supply expectations compared with the disruption period, which can weigh on copper prices in the coming days as markets anticipate higher output and reduced supply risk.

title: Canadian North Resources Inc. Reports Extraction Rates of 99% Nickel, 98% Cobalt and 90.6% Copper in the Second Set of Bioleaching Tests for the Ferguson Lake Project in Canada
summary: Canadian North Resources reports high extraction rates from lab-scale bioleaching tests on its Ferguson Lake massive sulphides: ~90.6% copper and ~99% nickel (plus 98% cobalt). Tests show copper leach performance improves at 65°C with faster leaching, suggesting lower-cost processing, but no immediate production or market supply change.

title: Former chief investment officer of Singapore firm that invested in S$1.46bil nickel trading scam fined S$9,000
summary: A former Singapore chief investment officer was fined for not disclosing conflicts of interest linked to a S$1.46 billion nickel trading scam. The scheme involved buying nickel at a discounted price and reselling via forward contracts, but collapsed, causing investor losses. The case is regulatory and does not cite direct nickel market supply impacts.

title: In Armenia, copper and molybdenum concentrate production drop  from January to August, while zinc concentrate production ups
summary: Armenia’s National Statistical Committee said copper concentrate production fell 8.1% to 185,654.7 tons in January-August 2025 versus the same period in 2024. Molybdenum concentrate fell and ferromolybdenum production dropped sharply, while zinc concentrate rose, but only copper is tracked here.

title: Indonesian nickel firms to re-apply for 2026-27 permits
summary: Indonesia’s ESDM revised RKAB procedures and asked nickel mining licence holders to re-apply for 2026-2027 permits, cancelling previously approved RKABs for the next two years while leaving 2025 unchanged. The one-year validity change increases regulatory uncertainty around production and sales, potentially weighing on nickel sentiment.

title: UN experts express concerns over Serbia copper mining – Fian
summary: UN experts have written to Serbian authorities and Zijin Copper raising serious allegations of heavy-metal pollution from mining in Bor, including impacts on water, air, soil, and health. The government and company were given 60 days to respond. Potential compliance and operational disruptions could weigh on near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Ford Plunges as Aluminum Supplier Fire Ignites Production Fears, Shakes S&P 500
summary: A fire at Novelis’s Oswego, New York aluminum plant damaged the hot mill and is expected to keep capacity offline until early 2026. As Ford relies heavily on this supplier for aluminum-intensive vehicles, analysts forecast production cuts and higher costs, with potential tariff-driven import reliance. Broader industry aluminum shortages may tighten prices.

title: Ford Shares Hammered On Report Aluminum Plant Fire May Disrupt Ford F-150 Production
summary: A Reuters/WSJ report says a Sept. 16 fire destroyed Novelis’s hot mill in Oswego, NY, keeping sheet aluminum offline until early 2026. Ford’s Dearborn plant will pause F-150 Lightning EV production next week because Novelis supplies ~40% of U.S. auto aluminum sheet, with high tariffs complicating imports.

title: Fire At Key Aluminum Supplier Threatens Automotive Production Into 2026
summary: A late-night fire at Novelis’ Oswego, New York hot-mill facility has halted primary aluminum sheet production. The plant is expected to remain offline until early next year, disrupting supply to Ford and other major automakers. As the plant supplies about 40% of U.S. aluminum sheet demand, tightness may push aluminum prices higher.

title: Red Lake Gold Inc. Dives into Copper with Soo North Acquisition Amidst Historic Market Surge
summary: Red Lake Gold acquired 100% interest in Ontario’s Soo North Copper Project after Sterling Metals reported a high-grade discovery nearby. The piece frames this amid a bullish copper market with tight supply and strong energy-transition demand, supporting positive sentiment toward copper exploration assets. It notes Red Lake’s financial constraints but expects upside if drilling succeeds.

title: Aluminum Plant Fire Affects Ford, Toyota Vehicle Production
summary: A fire destroyed an upstate New York aluminum plant, and the facility is expected to be inoperable until at least 2026. The plant supplies roughly 40% of auto aluminum sheet, and major automakers like Ford and Toyota may face production delays. The supply disruption supports aluminium price upside near term.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Reports Results of Phase 1 Drill Program at Mantoverde
summary: Capstone Copper reported initial drill results from its Mantoverde Phase 1 program in Chile, highlighting copper intercepts with grades above the block model across multiple sectors and step-outs (Brecha Flores, Santa Clara Corridor, Animas). The company says results support potential resource growth and future expansion projects, implying bullish near-term sentiment for copper.

title: Glencore Mount Isa copper smelter: Australian government provides bailout to save jobs
summary: Australia’s government is providing Glencore a $600m bailout to keep its Mt Isa copper smelter and Townsville refinery running for at least three years, securing 600 jobs and lowering near-term supply disruption risk. The piece also notes continued energy-focused support sought by aluminium smelters, underpinning production sentiment.

title: Fire disrupts aluminum supply for Ford, other automakers
summary: A fire damaged Novelis’s Oswego, New York hot mill used to supply aluminum sheet to automakers, including Ford, taking a major portion of the plant offline until early next year. Auto producers are sourcing alternatives and monitoring output impacts, signaling near-term aluminum supply constraints.

title: Taxpayers ride to the rescue of ailing copper smelter
summary: Australia agreed to a $600 million taxpayer-funded lifeline for Glencore to keep its Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery operating after the company threatened to shut loss-making facilities. The deal protects significant smelting capacity and jobs, reducing short-term supply risk for copper.

title: Glencore Gets $395 Million Government Bailout to Keep Mount Isa Copper Smelter Afloat
summary: Glencore will receive a A$600 million (US$395 million) government bailout to keep its Mount Isa copper smelter operating in Queensland. Funding is split between Australia’s federal and state governments, with A$200 million paid in the first two years and the final portion contingent on obligations being met.

title: Glencore Gets $395 Million Government Bailout for Australian Copper Smelter, Refinery -- Update
summary: Glencore secured an Australian government bailout of up to A$600 million (US$395 million) to keep its Queensland Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery operating for three years. The company cited losses from China-led smelting oversupply and high energy costs. Payments are contingent on agreed obligations.

title: Fire at Aluminum Plant Puts Automakers in Supply Crunch
summary: A major fire at Novelis’ Oswego, New York plant—supplying about 40% of the aluminum sheet used by US automakers—has taken a key hot-mill area offline. The restart is expected in early next year, forcing automakers to seek limited alternative supply. A 50% US tariff on imports adds upward pressure to aluminum.

title: Australia launches $395 million rescue of Glencore copper smelter
summary: Australia announced a A$600 million rescue over three years for Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville refinery, reflecting strategic concerns about critical mineral supply and competition from China’s overcapacity. The payments help avoid potential shutdowns, supporting expectations for copper refining availability in the near term.

title: Glencore Gets $395 Million Government Bailout for Australian Copper Smelter, Refinery -- 2nd Update
summary: Glencore will receive up to A$600 million (US$395 million) to keep Australia’s Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville refinery operating for three years. The loss-making units faced closure risk due to China-led oversupply and high energy costs. The support covers operational continuity and reduces short-term supply uncertainty.

title: AT&T: Missouri ranks among worst states for copper wire theft
summary: AT&T says Missouri is a leading state for copper wire theft, with thieves cutting telephone lines, damaging telecom infrastructure, and even stealing buried wire. AT&T reports $500,000 in 2025 losses in Kansas City and offers a $20,000 reward, while partnering with police and recyclers to deter purchases of stolen copper.

title: Federal, State Governments Pledge $600 Million Lifeline to Save Copper Smelter and Refinery
summary: Federal and Queensland governments pledged about $600 million over three years to help keep the Mount Isa Copper Smelter and Townsville Refinery operational. The support is aimed at preventing disruptions at the facilities, reducing short-term refined copper supply risk and likely supporting copper prices.

title: Strickland nails colossal 191m copper-gold hit in Serbia
summary: Strickland Metals reported a 191.2m drill intercept at its Rogozna Copper Canyon project in Serbia, including multiple thick zones with copper grades around 0.5–0.6% and sections exceeding 1%. The company says results could expand its resource and strengthen copper growth prospects. Further assays are due soon.

title: Glencore's copper operations saved by $600m funding | North Queensland Register
summary: Australia has agreed to fund Glencore’s loss-making Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery with $600m over three years, preventing potential care-and-maintenance. The deal offers certainty for workers and preserves domestic processing capacity. The government cites copper’s role in energy transition assets like solar and wind.

title: Glencore's copper operations saved by $600m funding | Queensland Country Life
summary: Australia will provide Glencore $600m over three years to keep its Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery operating, after Glencore warned it could shut loss-making assets without subsidies. The deal preserves a major share of local smelting/refining capacity amid high energy costs and market uncertainty.

title: Goldman: $10,000 Is New Price Floor For Copper
summary: Goldman analysts say copper futures near record highs as mine disruptions (notably Freeport’s Grasberg force majeure) and structural demand from grids, defense and AI support higher prices. They lift 2026 forecasts and argue copper is resetting to a $10,000–$11,000/t range, implying a new price floor.

title: Australian gov't announces bailout for Glencore copper smelter-Xinhua
summary: Australia announced up to AUD 600 million in joint federal and Queensland funding to keep Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville refinery operating for three years. The bailout targets energy and maintenance cost pressures, providing a short-term lifeline and reinforcing copper supply amid potential shutdown risk.

title: Trump Sanctions Revive Barter Trade: China's Chery Trades Half-Built Cars for Iran's Copper
summary: The article’s headline says Trump sanctions have revived barter trade, with China’s Chery exchanging half-built cars for copper from Iran. If this enables Iran to export copper despite sanctions, it would raise near-term supply availability expectations and likely pressure copper prices downward over days to weeks.

title: Camino Minerals Corp: Camino Receives Approval for Waste Dump Expansion and Achieves Milestone at the Puquios Copper Project in Chile
summary: Camino Minerals said Chile’s Environmental Assessment Service approved an exempt resolution for modifications to the Puquios copper project’s waste dump location and volume, extending project lifespan and removing the need for a separate EIA. The approval supports efforts to secure financing and move toward a final investment decision to build the copper mine.

title: American Pacific Mining Corp.: American Pacific Mining Prepares to Drill High-Priority Porphyry and Skarn Targets at Madison Copper-Gold Project
summary: American Pacific Mining announces Phase II drill targets at its Madison copper-gold project in Montana after receiving a drill permit. The program will test beneath copper-gold skarn zones and expand high-grade skarn and feeder targets. Madison previously produced small-scale copper, and results are pending.

title: $600m for Mt Isa copper bailout
summary: Australian taxpayers and Queensland/ federal governments will provide about $600m to Glencore to keep the Mount Isa copper smelter running for three years. The bailout prevents mothballing and supports ongoing production/refining capacity. The piece also discusses Optus’s triple-zero outage unrelated to metals.

title: Fire at aluminum plant to hit Ford's bottom line by up to $1 billion, analyst says
summary: A fire at Novelis’ New York aluminum plant is expected to take much of the facility down for months, disrupting aluminum supply for Ford’s F-150 trucks through year-end. Analysts estimate a $500 million to $1 billion earnings hit. The supply-chain disruption is likely to tighten near-term aluminum availability.

title: Amerigo Resources Copper Production Declines In Q3
summary: Amerigo Resources said copper output at its Minera Valle Central operation in Chile declined to 14.6 million pounds in Q3 from 16.27 million pounds a year earlier. The drop was blamed on reduced fresh tailings after an accident at El Teniente, with tailings not received for 10 days in August. 2025 output guidance is slightly lowered.

title: Teck Resources lowers copper production guidance for 2025
summary: Teck Resources cut its 2025 copper production guidance to 415,000–465,000 tonnes from prior 470,000–525,000 tonnes. The company cited lower expected output at its Quebrada Blanca mine in Chile and Highland Valley Copper operations in British Columbia. The downgrade signals reduced copper supply expectations.

title: Copper: Teck Resources lowers production guidance for 2025
summary: Teck Resources lowered its 2025 copper production guidance. A weaker production outlook implies less copper supply coming to market, which can tighten supply expectations and support copper prices in the near term as traders reassess output risk and future supply availability.

title: San Diego-area bike shop hit hard with steel and aluminum tariffs
summary: A San Diego bike shop says announced steel and aluminium tariffs have already raised costs on largely imported products, leading suppliers to apply more pressure and some bike lines to be cancelled. The owner reports higher wholesale prices and squeezed margins, with ongoing uncertainty about future stock costs.

title: Morgan Stanley Boosts Alcoa's Price Target Amidst Soaring Aluminum Prices
summary: Morgan Stanley raised Alcoa’s price target and reiterated an Overweight rating, citing soaring aluminum prices, ongoing alumina supply disruptions, and an anticipated aluminum supply deficit outside China. The bank also referenced IRA production tax credits for Alcoa, reinforcing expectations that aluminum prices remain elevated and supportive for producers.

title: Koryx Files Updated PEA for the Haib Copper Project,
summary: Koryx Copper filed an updated Preliminary Economic Assessment technical report for its 100%-owned Haib copper project in southern Namibia. The company reiterates the PEA results and current copper and molybdenum resources. The update may shape sentiment toward future copper supply, but it does not signal near-term production changes.

title: Carney pitches Keystone XL restart in exchange for progress on aluminum, steel | iNFOnews
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney told the U.S. President Donald Trump his teams should pursue discussions on reviving Keystone XL, linking energy cooperation to progress on support for Canada’s steel and aluminum sectors. Observers say this could help negotiations and ease tariff pain, which would be mildly supportive for aluminum demand expectations.

title: Koryx Copper Inc. Files Updated PEA for the Haib Copper Project, Southern Namibia
summary: Koryx Copper Inc. filed an updated Preliminary Economic Assessment for its 100%-owned Haib copper project in southern Namibia. The technical report (NI 43-101) is dated effective Sept. 4, 2025. The update may affect longer-term supply expectations, but no near-term production or supply changes are stated.

title: Ford aluminum supplier Novelis suspends operations until 2026 after major fire
summary: Novelis, a key supplier of automotive-grade aluminum to Ford and other automakers, will keep its Oswego, New York hot-mill offline until the first quarter of fiscal 2026 after a September fire. The disruption affects aluminum sheet supply used in vehicles like the F-150, potentially tightening material availability.

title: Federal politics live: Minister defends $600m bailout of copper smelter as 'good use of public resources'
summary: Federal politics coverage includes a minister defending a $600m taxpayer bailout for Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter. The bailout is framed as keeping the smelter running amid international pressures. Support for continued smelting capacity can reduce near-term supply disruption fears for copper prices.

title: Carney says he had 'meeting of minds' with Trump on steel, aluminum
summary: Carney said he reached a “meeting of minds” with Trump on steel and aluminum. The headline suggests policy or trade frictions around aluminum could ease, improving near-term expectations for aluminum supply and market tightness. That typically supports prices over the coming days to a few weeks.

title: Copper thieves target MDOT project site along I-20
summary: Mississippi DOT says copper thieves are repeatedly stealing copper from interstate light poles, causing outages and delaying a $1.8 million project to install LED lights and security trigger systems along I-20 and other corridors. MDOT expects completion in one to two months once LEDs and the security system are installed.

title: Glencore, Mount Isa: Minerals expert urges Australia to capitalise on $600 million copper smelter bailout
summary: Australia pledged $600 million over three years to keep Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville copper refinery operating. The expert cites global copper tightness and China’s smelting dominance, arguing preferential trade/security deals could sustain supply. Maintaining processing helps prevent disruptions, supporting near-term copper sentiment.

title: Sky Gold Corp.: Sky Gold Announces Private Placement in Preparation for Drilling on the Tower Gold and High Life Copper Porphyry Targets, Evening Star Property, Mineral County, Nevada
summary: Sky Gold Corp. announced a non-brokered private placement to fund geophysics and drilling at its Evening Star property in Nevada, including the High Life copper-gold porphyry target. The release states Tower Gold is drill-ready and surveys (magnetic and deep IP) will be conducted before drilling begins.

title: Fire at Novelis aluminum plant disrupts auto industry supply chain
summary: A Sept. 16 fire damaged Novelis’ aluminum plant in Oswego, halting production and disrupting supplies to major automakers. Novelis provides about 40% of the aluminum used by large automakers, so the outage is expected to lift material costs and tighten availability in coming months, supporting higher aluminum pricing expectations.

title: Fertiliser plant uncertainty puts Mount Isa Copper Smelter future in doubt despite bailout
summary: Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter received a $600m bridging bailout, but its operation depends on Dyno Nobel’s Phosphate Hill fertiliser/acid plant. If Dyno Nobel cannot sell by March, the fertiliser acid supply could stop in September 2026, potentially ending smelter production despite government support.

title: Teck cuts copper output at mine key to Anglo deal
summary: Teck cut copper output guidance for its flagship Quebrada Blanca mine in Chile, reducing 2026 production forecasts to 170,000–190,000 tons from 210,000–230,000 tons, and also trimmed guidance for QB2 and Highland Valley. The move adds another supply shock as mine disruptions mount.

title: Bell Bay Aluminium's future hinges on power talks | The Advocate
summary: Bell Bay Aluminium’s 10-year power contract with Hydro Tasmania is unresolved; failure by December 30 could force the smelter to close, threatening jobs and raising statewide power, transmission, and freight costs. The dispute and uncertainty also create risk for other industrial energy users, affecting aluminium production outlook.

title: Carney puts Keystone XL on the table in hopes for progress on U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs in 'coming weeks'
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney discussed energy cooperation, including possibly revisiting the Keystone XL pipeline, as leverage to make progress on U.S. steel and aluminium tariffs. Both sides directed teams to conclude work in coming weeks, implying hopes for tariff relief or better terms that could support aluminium prices.

title: Thieves stealing copper from lights on the interstate around metro area
summary: Mississippi DOT says thieves are stripping copper from newly installed LED traffic lights and electrical boxes along Interstate 20 and Highway 18 near Jackson. Repairs require rewiring and replacing fixtures, raising costs and causing lights to be out. MDOT calls the thefts costly and recurring, implying incremental copper demand.

title: Which state is the Largest Bauxite Producing state?
summary: Odisha is identified as India’s largest bauxite-producing state, contributing over 50% of national output. High-grade bauxite from mines such as Panchpatmali in Koraput supplies domestic and export refineries, including major aluminium producers like NALCO, Hindalco and Vedanta, supporting ongoing aluminium production and supply.

title: Bell Bay Aluminium delivers 'unsettling news' to staff ahead of power deal expiry
summary: Bell Bay Aluminium warned staff it faces a significant risk after failing to secure a new 10-year electricity deal with Hydro Tasmania before the Dec. 31 expiry. Tasmania is seeking federal help, including the GAPC scheme, as negotiations stalled and a closure could follow.

title: Zambia's Record Copper Mining Output Meets a Red-Hot Market
summary: Zambia is expected to produce record levels of copper this year, strengthening its role as a major supplier. The piece notes that accidents and disruptions at major mines have previously squeezed supply and pushed copper up more than 20% this year. If Zambia delivers, output growth could support sustained tightness and prices.

title: Market wrap: ASX200 books small gain on copper-fuelled mining rally
summary: Australia’s ASX200 rose slightly, with materials leading, as copper prices jumped overnight and lifted major copper miners such as BHP and Rio Tinto. The rally coincided with strong gains in several copper-related stocks. The top gainer was Nickel Industries, which also surged, indicating broader bullish sentiment.

title: Market wrap: ASX200 books small gain on copper-fuelled mining rally
summary: Australia’s market rose as a copper-fuelled rally in big miners followed an overnight jump in copper prices. BHP, Rio Tinto, and other copper-linked producers gained. Nickel Industries also surged strongly on the day. Other sectors moved lower, suggesting copper and nickel sentiment were supportive.

title: Teck Resources lowers copper output guidance amid challenges
summary: Teck Resources cut its 2025 copper output guidance after challenges at Chile’s Quebrada Blanca mine and Canada’s Highland Valley Copper, citing extended tailings dam work, TMF development constraints, and lower ore grades. Costs also rose, reinforcing weaker near-term supply expectations for copper.

title: Post-Holiday Surge in Cast Aluminum Alloy Futures and Spot Prices: Focus on Costs, Inventory, and Demand Sustainability[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Aluminum scrap prices rose after the National Day holiday, driven by stockpiling ahead of the break, tight scrap supply, and a jump in spot primary aluminum. Cast aluminum alloy futures and ADC12 spot increased sharply, with costs up and demand gradually recovering, though inventory buildup may limit upside.

title: ICSG: Global Refined Copper Market to Face a Supply Deficit of 150,000 mt Next Year
summary: ICSG forecasts global refined copper balances of a surplus (~178,000 mt) in 2025 shifting to a supply deficit (~150,000 mt) in 2026. The deficit is linked to weaker-than-expected refined output constrained by tight concentrate supply, after accidents reduced 2025 mine growth and demand growth continues, led by China.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Indonesian Nickel Ore Market Update – Limited Impact from China's Independence Holiday, RKAB Uncertainty Persists
summary: China’s National Day holiday had minimal effect on Indonesian nickel ore operations. The Oct. 3 RKAB policy release saw few miners secure approvals under the new two-stage verification system. Smelters increased early procurement, while favorable weather and rising Indonesian NPI output support ore demand, keeping nickel ore prices elevated toward Q4 2025.

title: Anglo Asian Mining lowers gold guidance, raises copper target
summary: Anglo Asian Mining lowered its full-year gold production target but raised copper guidance, citing Demirli copper mine nearing design capacity and continued ore stockpiling at Demirli and Gilar. Copper output is guided at 8,100–9,000 tonnes versus 6,500–6,800 previously, with permit progress and planned concentrate sales in November.

title: Afghan forces foil attempt to smuggle over 52 tons of copper, arrest 19-Xinhua
summary: Afghan security forces in Helmand province foiled an alleged copper smuggling attempt involving 52.5 tons moved by four vehicles. Nineteen suspects were arrested in Marja district and referred to the judiciary. The disruption of copper outflows could marginally tighten nearby supply conditions and support copper prices.

title: Northstar Gold Corp.: Northstar and Novamera Execute Definitive Surgical Mining Services Agreement to Advance Cam Copper Project Evaluation
summary: Northstar and Novamera signed a Surgical Mining Services Agreement to evaluate extracting high-grade copper from the Zone 2 horizon at the Cam Copper Mine. The work is dependent on permits and financing and is aimed at a future pilot and NI 43-101 assessment. No production decision is made.

title: Ford F-150 Production Becomes the First Victim Of Aluminum Plant Fire - Automaker Expects A $1 Billion Hit
summary: A fire at Novelis’ New York aluminum plant on September 16 is expected to disrupt production for months and reduce aluminum supply used in Ford’s F-150 trucks through end-2025. Ford expects up to a $1 billion earnings hit, following a stock drop after the news.

title: Copper hits US$11,000 a tonne, nearing all-time peak, as investors bet on shortages
summary: Copper surged to about US$11,000/ton on LME as investors returned amid mine supply disruptions, including Freeport’s force majeure at Grasberg, and falling LME stocks signaled tighter near-term availability. Aluminium also climbed to a three-year peak on broader base-metals strength and positioning, before easing slightly.

title: Copper output from Chile's Codelco slides 25% in August after deadly mine accident
summary: Cochilco data show Codelco’s August copper output fell 25% after a July 31 fatal collapse forced El Teniente to halt production. The accident is estimated to have cut output by about 33,000 tonnes. Escondida stayed nearly flat, while Collahuasi fell 27% on lower-grade ore.

title: BIS Posts Requests for Expansion of Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Derivatives Products Lists
summary: BIS has published over 90 requests to add more HTSUS subheadings covering steel and aluminum derivative products subject to Section 232 tariffs of 50%, following a September submissions window. The expansion would broaden tariff coverage for aluminum-linked imports, potentially tightening supply and supporting near-term aluminium pricing expectations.

title: Steel and aluminum tariffs drive up costs for everyday nuts and bolts
summary: A 50% tariff on steel and aluminum products is raising costs for downstream goods like screws, nails, and marine fasteners. Distributors report large margin pressure and slower construction and electrical projects due to higher input costs and tariff-related uncertainty, which can support aluminium prices and indirectly affect copper-linked electrical demand.

title: Core Silver Corp. Unearths Significant Copper Potential at Laverdiere Project, Signaling Long-Term Supply Hope Amidst Global Deficit
summary: Core Silver Corp. announced high-grade copper-bearing results from its Laverdiere exploration project in British Columbia, extending copper-molybdenum-silver mineralization over a multi-kilometer corridor. The article frames the find as supportive for the market amid an ongoing global copper supply deficit, though it offers no immediate production relief.

title: Horizon Copper Shareholders and Warrantholders Approve Proposed Plan of Arrangement with Royal Gold
summary: Horizon Copper reports shareholder approval of a plan of arrangement under which Royal Gold (via AcquireCo) will acquire Horizon shares and Horizon will acquire outstanding warrants, with closing anticipated on Oct. 20 subject to conditions and court approval. The company is copper-focused, but no operational supply changes are specified.

title: Copper near price record as China buyers return
summary: Copper prices neared record highs as China buyers returned after a holiday, coinciding with bullish momentum and a tight market. The rally was supported by production downgrades at major mines, including Teck’s Chilean asset, and disruptions at Grasberg and Freeport-McMoRan’s Indonesia operations. Aluminum also rose as markets priced easing.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Promotes Robert Winton to Chief Operating Officer
summary: Gunnison Copper Corp. promoted Robert Winton to COO, citing his role in bringing the Johnson Camp Mine into production and enabling first copper production and sales in 2025. The release also notes continued work using Nuton LLC/Rio Tinto bio-leaching technology and upcoming production expansion, but no immediate market-moving change is specified.

title: Carney Pitches Keystone XL Restart To End Tariffs On Aluminum, Steel
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney discussed reviving the Keystone XL pipeline with U.S. President Donald Trump, aiming to support Canada’s steel and aluminum sectors and potentially ease aluminum tariffs. Observers describe the talks as a way to secure tariff reductions via linked energy and industrial negotiations, which could lift near-term aluminum sentiment.

title: CME : Copper futures rallied despite dollar strength.
summary: November copper futures rose for a fifth week despite a strengthening dollar. The move also reflects market reaction to Teck Resources cutting its production guidance due to issues at its Chilean mine, with recent output at 170,000–190,000 tonnes versus 210,000–230,000 previously.

title: How are steel and aluminum tariffs calculated on bikes?
summary: The article explains how Section 232 tariffs on imported steel and aluminum would be calculated for bikes and e-bikes, including proposed additions of bike frames and some e-bikes to tariff derivative lists. It emphasizes potential hundreds of dollars in added landed costs and uncertain tariff “stacking,” directly affecting aluminum-containing inputs.

title: Ivanhoe Electric (IE) Hits New All-Time High on Jump in Copper Production
summary: Ivanhoe Electric shares rose after the company reported a 57% year-on-year jump in copper output to 71,226 tons in Q3 and reiterated full-year guidance. The report also flags upcoming higher-grade mining at Kakula and first production at Platreef, which is linked to nickel and copper endowment.

title: San Joaquin County task force reduces copper wire thefts
summary: San Joaquin County’s sheriff task force has sharply reduced copper wire thefts, cutting incidents from 500+ to about 140 in 2024 and under 100 this year. Police say thefts disrupted communications dispatch systems and local businesses’ phone lines, but digital upgrades reduced impact. A separate theft was reported Monday in Stockton.

title: Arizona AG Mayes holds town hall over Benson aluminum plant
summary: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes held a town hall on a proposed Benson aluminium smelting facility after residents raised health and air-pollution concerns. She said nuisance law actions are “absolutely on the table” while ADEQ continues permit review. Any stoppage or delay could tighten aluminium supply expectations.

title: Marimaca Copper Files NI 43-101 Technical Report for the Previously Announced Marimaca Oxide Deposit Feasibility Study
summary: Marimaca Copper Corp. filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its Marimaca oxide deposit feasibility study in Chile’s Antofagasta region. The report supports previously announced study results and is an update to regulatory disclosure. No new operational changes, production impacts, or supply disruptions are stated.

title: Indonesia's Bauxite Gambit: How a Mining Policy U-Turn Aims to Control a Booming Sector
summary: Indonesia has changed its bauxite mining RKAB rules, moving from a three-year to a one-year approval cycle effective Oct. 3, 2025, supported by tighter digital reporting and quota adjustments. The article notes structural oversupply versus limited refining capacity, implying continued price pressure and potential bearish sentiment for aluminium-related supply.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Oct 10
summary: SMM’s Indonesian nickel market weekly review shows upward nickel ore benchmarks but declining high-grade NPI prices. After the National Day holiday, NPI fell due to margin pressure at downstream stainless steel mills, sluggish sales, higher costs, and continued oversupply. Downward pressure is expected to persist next week.

title: Codelco's August copper production falls to 20-year low
summary: Codelco said August copper output fell to a 20-year low after a July 31 collapse at El Teniente, halting work for over a week and reducing production by about 33,000 tonnes. August output dropped 25% year on year to 93,400 tonnes, tightening short-term supply outlook.

title: Rio Tinto (ASX:RIO)  in talks to keep Australia's biggest aluminium smelter open
summary: Rio Tinto is negotiating with federal and NSW governments to prevent closure of Tomago, Australia’s largest aluminium smelter, after a post-2028 electricity cost blowout threatens viability. The plant is energy-intensive, and a support deal would likely preserve aluminium output and employment, tightening near-term supply expectations.

title: TNR Gold Corp.: TNR Gold NSR Royalty Update - Los Azules Feasibility Study Confirms Economically Robust Copper Project With Leading ESG Performance
summary: TNR Gold highlights an updated feasibility study for the Los Azules copper project in Argentina. The study confirms low-cost, long-life production of high-purity copper cathodes, with permits approved and the project accepted into Argentina’s large investment incentive regime. Financing discussions with IFC and others are referenced.

title: UAE's IRH Trading targets 1 mln tonnes in copper expansion
summary: Abu Dhabi-based IRH Trading plans to grow copper trading volumes, aiming for about 1 million tonnes per year by 2030, backed by controlling ownership in Zambia’s Mopani Copper Mines. It also signals future expansion in aluminium trading, but the news is mostly long-term capacity and trading ambitions.

title: Copper Inventories Nationwide Below Expected Buildup After the Holiday, Shanghai Emerges as the Only Major Destocking Region.
summary: After the holiday, SMM mainstream copper inventories rose less than expected (+18,000 mt to 166,300 mt) and fell YoY (-37,300 mt). Shanghai is the only major region with a decline (-3,000 mt) as fewer imports arrived and smelter flows favored nearby Jiangsu. Demand stayed weak in Guangdong, but overall buildup remained constrained.

title: Zambia's Kwacha Hits Highest Since 2024 as Copper Demand Soars
summary: Zambia’s kwacha rose to a near two-year high as investors gained confidence in the country’s copper industry recovery following a drought. The article cites expectations for record copper production this year, which is driving the rally and suggests improving copper supply prospects.

title: Changes to Steel and Aluminum Duties are in the Wind
summary: The article says Commerce has released inclusion requests related to Section 232 duties for steel and aluminum, with EU and Canada taking steps to align their import rules with the U.S. It highlights proposed EU quota-linked duties on steel and Canada’s tariff-rate quota system, implying tighter aluminum imports.

title: Copper Volatility Cant Detract From Broader Supply-Demand Pressures
summary: The article argues copper volatility is outweighed by underlying supply-demand pressures. It cites potential mining disruptions causing a supply deficit, slightly revised 2025 output guidance at Kamoa-Kakula, and tariff-driven demand changes tied to electrification and data centers. Overall, it expects copper prices to remain supported.

title: Zambia's Kwacha Soars to 2024 Highs Amidst Copper Boom and Investment Influx
summary: Zambia’s kwacha surged as optimism returned to the country’s copper industry amid a broader global copper price boom. The article cites strong demand from EV and renewable energy, major mine expansion investments, and targets for higher output, reinforcing near-term expectations for copper.

title: Goldman Sachs expects copper price to remain in $10,000-$11,000/t price range in 2026/2027
summary: Goldman Sachs said copper is likely to trade within $10,000–$11,000/t in 2026/27 due to a surplus, citing potential weaker Chinese buying and U.S. inventory effects. It expects nickel prices to fall as Indonesian supply grows, and aluminium surplus to increase as Indonesian output ramps up.

title: Teck cuts copper output target again amid global supply concerns
summary: Teck Resources lowered its copper output targets again, citing continued difficulty ramping output at its Quebrada Blanca mine in northern Chile due to delays in a tailings facility. The cuts extend through 2028 and add to broader mine supply challenges, supporting expectations for tighter copper concentrate supply.

title: Gilroy copper wire theft knocks out power to Luigi Aprea Elementary School as reform bill sits on governor's desk
summary: Copper wire theft has knocked out power at a Gilroy elementary school, highlighting ongoing thefts in California. The state attorney general and lawmakers are pushing a bill requiring junk dealers to document sellers and metal details, with Governor Newsom deciding soon. The measure targets incentives behind copper theft.

title: Rumble Resources Inc.: Rumble Resources Expands Wilmac Copper-Gold Project to 11,504 Hectares with Addition of Lamont Ridge and Plume
summary: Rumble Resources announced an expansion of its Wilmac copper-gold project in British Columbia by adding Lamont Ridge and the Plume tenure application. The company highlights copper anomalies and porphyry-style targets near an operating copper mine, but provides no production changes or immediate supply implications.

title: Mexico's Industrial Output Misses Estimates, Raising Economic Alarms and Challenging Nearshoring Narrative
summary: Mexico’s industrial production fell more than expected in August 2025, with broad declines across mining, manufacturing, and construction. The slump raises concerns about weaker near-term industrial demand, pressuring base metals exposure in Mexico (copper mining and aluminium components). It also highlights tariff/USMCA uncertainty, adding further downside risk to demand.

title: Marginal Recovery in Copper Anode Supply Fails to Alter Rigid Demand Support, Overall Tightness from Supply-Demand Mismatch Yet to Reverse Fundamentally [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports September copper anode/blister copper markets were tight due to secondary copper policy uncertainty reducing scrap-derived supply, with imports down sharply. In October, prices rose modestly as recycled raw material releases eased gaps, but smelter maintenance and concentrates deficits keep demand firm, limiting the rebound.

title: Copper Zinc Aluminium Bullish Momentum to Sustain Motilal Oswal
summary: Motilal Oswal expects sustained bullish momentum in base metals, citing tightening inventories and electrification-led demand. Copper is boosted by US tariffs on copper imports and higher EV-related copper intensity. Aluminium sentiment improves on the Fed’s rate cut, China’s production cap, and sharply lower LME/SHFE inventories, though range-bound risks remain.

title: Copper Zinc Aluminium Bullish Momentum to Sustain Motilal Oswal
summary: Motilal Oswal expects sustained strength in industrial metals, citing tightening inventories and supply disruptions. Copper is seen supported by US copper import tariffs, electrification and EV demand, and persistent disruption risks. Aluminium sentiment is boosted by the Fed rate cut, lower LME/SHFE inventories, and China supply/import dynamics, though demand is uneven.

title: How Much Inventory Buildup Occurred During the Holiday? An Analysis of Aluminum Ingot and Aluminum Billet Inventory Accumulation During the 2025 National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival Holidays [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM tracked China’s aluminum ingot and billet inventories after the 8-day National Day/Mid-Autumn holidays. Ingot stock rose 57,000 mt (+9.6%) to about 649,000 mt and billet stock rose 24,000 mt to 139,000 mt. The buildup matched expectations, suggesting limited supply pressure and no clear net price move.

title: Post-holiday copper inventory builds less than expected, while Shanghai stands out as the only major destocking region
summary: SMM data show post-holiday copper inventories rising by less than expected (mainstream +18,000 mt to 166,300 mt) and falling YoY. Shanghai is the only major region with destocking (−3,000 mt), as imported inflows were not concentrated. However, demand weakness elsewhere keeps buildup pressure.

title: Marginal copper anode supply recovery fails to fundamentally alter the tight market [SMM analysis]
summary: SMM reports that September saw a tighter blister copper market in China due to secondary-sector policy uncertainty, which reduced scrap-derived anode and blister supply. October shows some marginal supply recovery and higher RCs, but demand support remains firm, so the overall tight balance is unlikely to reverse materially soon.

title: Evolving Nickel Market: Trends, Risks & Outlook – key takeaways from Shirley Wang's Speech at INSG Meeting
summary: The piece argues that nickel prices are supported in the short term by tight Indonesian MHP availability, rising MHP prices that increase refined nickel production costs, and Indonesia’s tightened ore policy regime. It notes smelters stockpiling in advance of 2026 RKAB changes, while liquidity and refined nickel’s LME trading help buffer declines.

title: Fire breaks out at Indonesia nickel hub, three injured
summary: A fire broke out at a facility in Indonesia’s Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP), injured three workers, and damaged a scrubber tower at one tenant under construction. The operator says overall IMIP operations were running normally as the investigation continues. The incident is therefore unlikely to materially disrupt near-term nickel output, but adds risk.

title: Post-holiday copper inventory buildup below expectations, while Shanghai stands out as the only major destocking region
summary: SMM reports post-holiday copper social inventories rose less than expected (+18,000 mt to 166,300 mt) and fell YoY, with Shanghai showing destocking (-3,000 mt) due to weaker imported arrivals and fewer cathode shipments. Elsewhere inventories rose, and high prices suppress demand, implying continued accumulation.

title: Combating copper theft amidst rising prices
summary: The article says copper theft in Australia is rising as copper prices climb. It quotes measures implemented through a regulated, monitored recycling/scrap-yard system aimed at discouraging theft, suggesting compliance with scrap-yard protocols helps keep theft under control. It does not indicate major sustained supply impacts.

title: Cassowary Tenement Copper-Gold Exploration Project | Company Announcement
summary: Artemis executed a land access agreement for the Cassowary copper-gold exploration project in Western Australia, enabling planned heritage surveys and initial diamond drilling in December (subject to approvals). The target is interpreted as IOCG-type copper-gold, but the news contains no production, reserves, or immediate supply impact.

title: Copper's rally needs China impetus to reach record
summary: Copper prices neared a record near $11,104/t but slipped after Trump threatened higher tariffs on China, raising concerns about demand. Analysts say further upside likely requires stronger China-led stimulus and demand growth. Inventories are mixed, suggesting surplus pockets in the US and uncertainty over whether supply deficits are real.

title: Codelco lifts El Teniente loss estimate, copper output target intact
summary: Codelco said losses from an El Teniente mine accident are likely 45% higher than previously estimated, while output is still targeted to rise slightly overall despite a planned 48,000-ton reduction for 2025. Together with other disruptions, supply tightness is cited as pushing copper prices near record highs.

title: Codelco El Teniente copper production loss: LME Week 2025
summary: Codelco said a rock-burst at El Teniente, started in July, will reduce output and hit earnings, with an expanded estimate of lower production. The incident worsens global refined supply tightness alongside other disruptions, contributing to a shift toward a 2026 deficit per ICSG revisions.

title: Copper concentrates benchmark uncertainty: LME Week 2025
summary: Market participants are preparing for LME Week with major uncertainty over the 2026 copper concentrates TC/RC benchmark, with many expecting it to settle at zero or deeper negative levels due to persistent concentrate tightness after disruptions at major mines. Spot TC indices are far below the current benchmark, widening seller-buyer gaps and driving contract re-pricing discussions.

title: Copper Prices Extend Gains Close to Record Highs, Improving Prospects for Zambia and the DRC
summary: Copper futures gained 3.45%, nearing record highs around $10,775/ton, driven by a weaker dollar and tight supply alongside mining disruptions. Analysts say durability depends on Chinese demand and inventory levels, with UBS constructive on future tightness while Goldman flags potential oversupply and demand caps above $11,000/ton.

title: Openreach ramps up copper switch out
summary: Openreach says it will activate Stop Sell in 94 more UK exchange locations covering about 960,000 premises, ending sales of legacy copper-based phone and broadband where ultrafast full fibre is available to most premises. Customers must upgrade to new full fibre services, reducing incremental copper-linked demand.

title: China's Commodity Imports Present Mixed Signals: Iron Ore and Copper Surge While Coal Plummets
summary: China’s 2025 import data show diverging commodity trends: copper imports jumped 24.4% year-on-year and overall imports rose to a 17-month high in September, indicating firmer Chinese industrial/infrastructure demand. Iron ore also rose, while coal imports fell sharply. The copper surge is the clearest near-term bullish signal for copper.

title: Copper Rally Soars on China's 2025 Demand Amidst Escalating Trade Tensions
summary: Copper is rallying near record levels on strong projected Chinese demand for 2025 and persistent global supply constraints, including flooding at Grasberg and production losses at Chile’s El Teniente. U.S.-China tariff threats add volatility, but recent tariff-related dips are followed by recovery signals, keeping near-term bias bullish.

title: Verity Resources Gains Full Control of Copper Assets in Botswana
summary: Verity Resources said it gained 100% control of a copper-silver exploration portfolio in Botswana by buying out its JV partner’s 66% stake for $206,060. The acquired assets include multiple high-grade copper prospects and a deposit reporting copper, nickel and PGM occurrences, but no new near-term production plans were announced.

title: Soaring copper prices fuel wave of vandalism against EV chargers, stranding drivers   – NaturalNews.com
summary: Britain’s EV charging network is being repeatedly vandalized as thieves target copper cables, disabling chargers and stranding drivers. The article links the theft wave to soaring global copper prices (cited at $11,000/tonne) and describes large replacement costs, suggesting stronger scrap/cabling demand for copper.

title: Century Aluminum Soars to 52-Week High Amidst Robust Market and Strategic Expansion
summary: Century Aluminum’s stock hits a 52-week high as the company secures long-term power and invests $50m to restart 50,000 tpa of idled capacity at its Mt. Holly smelter. The narrative cites rising, supply-tight aluminium markets and higher Section 232 tariffs, supporting bullish aluminium price expectations.

title: U.S. Aluminum Prices Remain High After Novelis Fire Hit Supply Chain
summary: A fire at Novelis’ Oswego hot mill reduces U.S. aluminum capacity, forcing a larger reliance on costlier offshore supplies amid a 50% import duty. The disruption lifts U.S. Midwest premiums to an all-time high and supports higher LME three-month aluminum prices, maintaining an uptrend despite weaker demand.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Announces up to $360 Million Investment from Orion for 25% Interest in Santo Domingo
summary: Capstone Copper said Orion will invest up to $360m for a 25% interest in the Santo Domingo and Sierra Norte projects, conditional on positive FID and followed by matching and contingent payments. Funds include exploration to advance copper resources and processing studies, de-risking development financing and supporting future copper output expectations.

title: Rio Tinto Q3 Pilbara Iron Ore Shipments Down; Upgrades FY Bauxite Production Guidance
summary: Rio Tinto reported slightly lower Pilbara iron ore shipments but improved production. It upgraded full-year bauxite guidance, citing better utilisation at Weipa/Amrun, suggesting stronger aluminium supply expectations. The firm also said copper production remains on track for the higher end of guidance, supporting copper sentiment.

title: 2025 Copper Supply Crisis: Disruptions Soar as Major Mines Cut or Halt Production [SMM Analysis]
summary: A nationwide power outage in Chile and several accidents—mine suspensions, mechanical failures, earthquakes, and tailings/processing disruptions—reduced output across major copper operations (Chuquicamata, El Teniente, Antamina, Kamoa-Kakula, Grasberg, Quebrada Blanca, and others). Guidance was repeatedly cut, worsening supply tightness for 2025 and likely lifting copper prices.

title: Ford Halts SUV Production After Supplier Fire Disrupts Aluminum Supply: Report
summary: Ford will temporarily suspend production of several SUV models, including the Expedition and Lincoln Navigator, for about one week at a Kentucky plant after a fire disrupted output from a key aluminum supplier. A UAW official linked the stoppage to aluminum supply challenges stemming from the incident, implying near-term aluminum demand/supply disruption.

title: Ford temporarily cuts SUV production at Kentucky Truck Plant after aluminum supplier fire
summary: Ford is temporarily cutting SUV production at its Kentucky Truck Plant after a fire at Novelis, one of its major aluminum suppliers. The Novelis plant is not expected to restart until next year, and the SUV pause is expected to last about a week, potentially reducing near-term aluminium sheet demand.

title: Report: Ford pauses Kentucky SUV production amid aluminum shortage
summary: Ford reportedly paused SUV production in Kentucky because of an aluminium shortage. This points to near-term tight availability of aluminium for manufacturers, which can support higher aluminium prices over the coming days as supply constraints worsen, despite the temporary reduction in demand from Ford’s production stop.

title: Capstone Copper Announces Up to $360 Million Investment from Orion for 25% Interest in Santo Domingo
summary: Capstone Copper said Orion Resource Partners will invest up to $360 million for a 25% interest in the Santo Domingo and Sierra Norte copper projects. Funds will support exploration and advance engineering/financing toward sanctioning. The transaction reduces Capstone’s funding burden and improves confidence in project execution, which can support copper sentiment.

title: Rio Tinto lifts production forecast for bauxite, hails Oyu Tolgoi mine
summary: Rio Tinto lifted its 2025 bauxite output guidance to 59–61 million tonnes and reported higher alumina and aluminium production. The company also said the Oyu Tolgoi underground ramp-up remains on track to boost copper output by more than 50% this year, supporting both aluminium and copper supply expectations.

title: Global copper output to grow modestly in 2025, amid supply challenges in Australia and Indonesia
summary: Global copper mine output is projected to rise modestly in 2025, but declines in Australia and Indonesia constrain expansion. Indonesian export bans on copper concentrate/anode sludge from Jan 2025 and disruptions at Freeport’s Grasberg add near-term supply tightness, partially offset by gains in Zambia, Chile, Peru, and the DRC.

title: Peak Season End-Use Demand Robust, Copper Foil Industry Operating Rate in China Rises for Fifth Consecutive Month This Year [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says China’s copper foil enterprise operating rate rose to 82.17% in September and is expected to increase to 83.72% in October. Growth was driven by higher shipments, especially lithium battery copper foil and electronic circuit foil, supported by robust NEV/ESS demand and stockpiling ahead of holidays.

title: Ford Cuts Production Of Even More Vehicles After Aluminum Supply Shock
summary: Ford is cutting production and idling multiple plants after a Novelis Oswego aluminum mill fire shut down hot-mill operations until early next year. The disruption is reducing vehicle output across several models due to “difficulties with aluminum supply,” tightening U.S. aluminum sheet availability for auto buyers.

title: Supply Shocks and Solar Shifts Drive Copper Prices Higher
summary: Copper prices rose sharply as Indonesia’s Grasberg mine suffered mudslide damage and fatal accidents, leading to force majeure and large output losses. The market shifted toward a deficit in 2026, while a weaker dollar boosted base metals sentiment. China’s solar subsidy rollback also caused short-term front-loaded copper demand.

title: Ford halts some production at Kentucky plant after fire at aluminum supplier
summary: Ford will pause production of some SUVs at its Kentucky plant for about a week after a fire disrupted operations at its aluminium supplier, Novelis. The supplier’s Oswego hot mill outage is expected to last months, constraining aluminium sheet supply used by U.S. automakers and increasing sourcing pressures.

title: BHP eyes reopening defunct US copper mines in response to Trump
summary: BHP’s CEO said the company is reviewing whether to reopen defunct mines in Arizona’s US copper belt after a major shift in US government policy. The policy change has encouraged BHP to increase exploration in the US, prompting a reassessment of options for restarting copper production.

title: Copper's Golden Decade: Global Market Set to Soar Beyond $450 Billion by 2034, Fueling Green Transition and Industrial Evolution
summary: The piece projects a major expansion in the global copper market through 2034, driven by electrification, renewables, and EV adoption, while noting supply frictions such as declining ore grades and slow mine development. It frames expectations for ongoing price volatility but suggests a supportive demand floor for copper in the coming weeks.

title: Tariff tensions and copper rally stir volatility in Canadian markets
summary: Renewed U.S.-China tariff threats reignited volatility, but copper was firm and reportedly bounced above US$5 a pound, with follow-through into copper equities. The interview ties the move to renewed interest in domestically produced copper, making previously uneconomic U.S. mines viable at current prices.

title: Trade group wants to ban export of scrap aluminum cans to China
summary: An industry trade group urged the U.S. to ban exports of used aluminum beverage cans to China, citing national security and a U.S. aluminum scrap supply gap. It says scrap is processed in China and returned as finished goods amid growing demand. The request follows recent aluminum tariff increases.

title: Suspected copper wire thief pulled from West L.A. manhole
summary: Authorities charged a man caught inside a manhole attempting to steal copper wire in West Los Angeles. The piece links recent thefts to service outages and infrastructure damage, citing AB 476 signed into law to strengthen penalties for illegal dealers. The events are local; no direct market-wide copper supply impact is stated.

title: Dearborn Truck Assembly could see layoffs after New York aluminum plant fire
summary: A major fire destroyed a Novelis plant in Oswego, New York that produces automotive-grade aluminium used by automakers, including Ford’s F-150 supply chain. Dearborn Truck Assembly may face work stoppages and layoffs. Reports suggest output may not resume until 2026, forcing costly alternative sourcing.

title: Wood Mackenzie: Copper demand set to surge 24% by 2035 as four key disruptors reshape global markets
summary: Wood Mackenzie forecasts copper demand rising sharply through electrification, data-centre growth, EVs, and emerging Asian industrialisation. It warns that insufficient mine investment and higher disruption assumptions could tighten supply, depleting inventories and increasing price volatility, with potential data-centre construction spikes of 15% or more.

title: Capstone Copper strikes deal to sell 25% stake in Chilean projects for $360m
summary: Capstone Copper said Orion Resource Partners will buy a 25% stake in Chilean Santo Domingo and Sierra Norte projects for about $360m, with payments tied to a positive FID and project milestones. Orion also buys Capstone shares for $10m to fund exploration. The transaction supports copper project development but lacks immediate output impact.

title: Camino Minerals Corp: Camino to Commence Drilling at its Los Chapitos Copper Project in Peru; Peru's Ministry of Energy and Mines Names Los Chapitos Among Top 15 Priority Exploration Projects
summary: Camino Minerals announced mobilization for discovery drilling at its Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, with MINEM naming the project among 15 priority exploration initiatives. The release details surface Cu-Ag trenching results and expects drilling to start in early November, but no production impact is indicated.

title: Taseko Announces Start of Wellfield Operations at Florence Copper and Third Quarter Gibraltar Operational Results | Company Announcement
summary: Taseko reports wellfield operations starting at its Florence Copper project with first copper cathode expected in about three months. It also cites strong Q3 Gibraltar operational results, including higher copper output and sales and improving recoveries. Company expects further production gains in Q4 and raised 2025 copper guidance.

title: NorthWest Copper Corp.: NorthWest Extends High-Grade Mineralization at Kwanika With 16.9 Metres of 1.37% Copper Equivalent in Second 2025 Drill Hole
summary: NorthWest Copper reported assay results from drill hole K-25-272 at its Kwanika deposit, including 16.9 metres at 1.37% copper equivalent and additional near-surface mineralization suited for open pit. The company says the intercepts extend higher-grade zones 50 metres down dip and remain open for further growth, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Taseko Mines Limited Announces Start of Wellfield Operations at Florence Copper
summary: Taseko Mines said it has received final regulatory approvals for its 100%-owned Florence Copper project in Arizona and is beginning wellfield operations, marking the start of commercial production. Construction is largely completed and commissioning will run in parallel with startup. The company also reported Gibraltar operations and copper sales of 26.3 million pounds in the quarter.

title: US aluminium price rise spurs deliveries from Canada
summary: Canadian producers have increased deliveries to the U.S. after higher U.S. physical prices reflected the 50% import tariff. Inventories have shrunk, lifting the Midwest premium to record levels and largely pricing in the tariff. Reduced Canadian pressure elsewhere has pushed European duty-paid premiums higher, too.

title: Policy Tightening and Supply Outflow: Malaysia's Copper Scrap Market Trapped in a Downward Cycle
summary: Malaysia’s SIRIM import supervision for copper scrap has tightened since 2021, raising inspection costs and driving trade diversion to Thailand, Vietnam, and the UAE. Malaysia’s copper scrap imports collapsed (2021–2022) and remain depressed in 2024, while local smelters cut output amid shortages and enforcement after smuggling cases.

title: Anglo American, MMG Offer Concessions to EU Merger Watchdog in Nickel Deal Probe
summary: Anglo American and MMG offered remedies to the EU Commission to secure approval for MMG’s purchase of MMG’s Brazilian nickel business from Anglo. The deal includes a five-year ferronickel offtake contract tied to current European sales. The commission set a Nov. 4 decision deadline.

title: Copper market price surges with 'animal spirits' reawakening
summary: Copper prices surged at the LME on renewed “animal spirits,” driven by fresh supply-constraint concerns. The ICSG cut 2025 mine growth forecasts due to major output incidents at Grasberg, Kamoa, and Chile’s El Teniente. Concerns over constrained concentrate availability and negative treatment charges support a bullish tone.

title: Copper smelters face tight margins but stay resilient in 2025
summary: Panelists said copper smelters are coping with very negative TC/RCs, but the concentrate market remains tightly supplied. Another large concentrate deficit is expected, inventories are declining, and scarcity premiums are showing in copper concentrate pricing. China’s focus on secure copper supply is cited as adding ongoing pressure on availability.

title: Chinese Copper Export Avalanche Reshapes Global Markets Amidst Arbitrage Frenzy
summary: Chinese smelters are exporting a large volume of refined copper due to arbitrage between high LME prompt prices and softer domestic benchmarks in China. The surge targets LME-monitored depots and bonded warehouses, potentially replenishing prompt supply and easing tightness, which should pressure near-term copper pricing.

title: Copper and Gold Are Driving a Mining Renaissance
summary: The piece argues mining is in a “renaissance,” driven by energy-transition demand and tighter supply expectations. It specifically highlights the IEA view that countries need much more copper and says investors expect strong deal activity in gold and copper, reinforcing bullish sentiment toward copper prices.

title: WoodMac Warns Copper Demand to Surge 24% by 2035
summary: Wood Mackenzie forecasts global refined copper demand rising 24% by 2035, with major needs for additional mine capacity and more recycling. It warns supply discoveries and permitting may fall short, risking deficits. The piece links bullish sentiment to rising benchmark copper prices as investors anticipate tighter availability from electrification and data centers.

title: High-grade copper and gold intersections extend known
summary: FireFly Metals reports step-out drilling at its Green Bay (Ming) copper-gold project, extending known mineralisation by 430–650m beyond prior drilling and confirming a long DHEM anomaly. Reported intersections include 49.0m at 6.1% CuEq, plus additional high-grade copper-rich zones, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: New California law targets copper theft with tougher rules and fines starting in 2026
summary: California’s Newsom signed AB 476 to tighten rules and raise fines for metal buyers and sellers amid copper wire theft crackdowns. The law expands documentation requirements and restricts ownership of certain scrap copper. Local enforcement citing/arresting theft suspects follows earlier ordinances, supporting improved scrap supply security.

title: Cobre Advances Botswana Copper Ambitions with Ngami Pilot Plant
summary: Cobre Limited began the environmental impact assessment for an in-situ copper recovery pilot plant at its Ngami project in Botswana, following ministry approval of its work plan. The study supports permitting for construction, after tests showed 82% average copper recovery, and could improve outlook for future copper production.

title: Creighton copper mine on track for commercial production for mid-2026
summary: Saskatchewan’s McIlvenna Bay copper project is 60% complete and on track for commercial production by mid-2026, with a $1 billion investment. The mine will produce copper and other metals and relies on green power/hydrogen-related infrastructure and planned global shipping, but output timing is still future.

title: Comments Due October 21 On Requests To Add Hundreds Of Products To Steel And Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The US Department of Commerce issued 95 new requests to add additional steel and aluminum derivative products to Section 232 tariffs, potentially covering nearly $300 billion of imports. Public comments are due October 21. If approved, broader tariff coverage would likely increase aluminium-related costs and weigh on metal-intensive activity.

title: BHP considers reopening defunct Arizona copper mines
summary: BHP is reportedly reviewing whether to reopen four dormant Arizona copper mines and reprocess tailings, citing higher copper prices and more supportive US government policy (tariffs and expedited permitting). The company is stepping up exploration and drilling in the Globe-Miami area, potentially boosting future US copper supply expectations.

title: Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd.: Pacific Ridge Intersects 112.2 m of 1.35% Copper Equivalent or 2.02 g/t Gold Equivalent at the RDP Copper-Gold Project
summary: Pacific Ridge Exploration announced drill hole RDP-25-011 intersected 112.2m of 1.35% copper equivalent at its RDP copper-gold project in British Columbia, including several higher-grade sub-intervals. Results are exploration-focused, with other holes pending, and no immediate supply or trade disruptions are cited.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Market: Slight Increase in Operating Rate in September Amid High Copper Prices, October Unlikely to Reach Peak Season Levels of Previous Years
summary: SMM data show copper plate/sheet and strip enterprises’ operating rate rose slightly in September but fell sharply year-on-year, missing peak-season expectations. High copper prices restrained end-use orders and slowed downstream procurement, raising inventory days. October operating rates are projected to drop further, indicating weaker near-term copper demand momentum.

title: Guinea bauxite exports jump 23% in 3rd quarter despite rains, regulatory pressure – Channel Africa
summary: Guinea’s bauxite exports rose 23% year-on-year in Q3 to 39.41 million tonnes despite rains and licence revocations. Shipments averaged 13.14 million tonnes per month and mostly went to China. The rebound supports expectations for aluminium feedstock availability, though regulatory pressure may limit sustained growth.

title: Freeport copper concentrate contracts 2026: LME Week
summary: Freeport is negotiating 2026 copper concentrate contracts for about 1.7–1.9 million tonnes, with TC/RC floor-and-cap levels higher than last year’s benchmark.
