Talks may extend into Asia Copper Week in November. The pricing framework aims to balance concentrate scarcity against smelter viability, with some volumes already agreed for 2026.

title: Anglo Asian copper production rises, backs guidance
summary: Anglo Asian Mining said Q3 copper output jumped to 2,287 tonnes from 654 tonnes, citing first production at Demirli and a full quarter from Gilar, and reaffirmed/revised full-year guidance of 8,100–9,000 tonnes. The update suggests improved near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Guinea's Bauxite Exports Defy Odds with 23% Surge, Solidifying Global Dominance Amidst Operational Hurdles
summary: Guinea’s bauxite exports rose 23% y/y in Q3 2025 to 39.41 Mt, with shipments exceeding 2025 targets despite rains, labor disruptions, and stricter local-processing rules. The article links the surge to stronger Chinese demand but notes supply loosening for bauxite, implying pressure on aluminium prices near term.

title: Harmony (HMY) Acquires MAC Copper for AU$1.08B to Diversify Into Copper
summary: Harmony Gold will acquire MAC Copper in a AU$1.08B cash deal, gaining control of the high-grade CSA copper mine in New South Wales that produced about 41,000 t of copper in 2024. The article frames copper as diversification for electrification but provides no immediate global supply or demand disruption.

title: Indonesian nickel industry harming local communities, environment, report says
summary: A report says Indonesia’s rapidly expanding nickel industry, driven by EV and battery demand, is causing major environmental damage and health problems in mining areas. It criticizes captive coal use and calls for decarbonization and enforcement against abuses. The pressure could influence near-term expectations for nickel production and supply practices.

title: Harmony Gold Shines Bright: Gold Rally and Strategic Copper Acquisition Propel Stock to New Heights
summary: Harmony Gold shares rose on record gold prices and the completion of Harmony’s acquisition of MAC Copper, including the CSA copper mine in Australia. The article highlights expected copper output and timing of operational control, but provides no clear immediate market supply or demand shock for copper that would drive near-term price moves.

title: Japan Q4 aluminium talks drag out in effort to bridge gap, say sources
summary: Japan’s quarterly aluminium pricing talks for Oct-Dec are unusually prolonged as buyers and global producers struggle over primary shipment premiums. Buyers cite weak demand and high inventories, keeping bids in the $80s versus producer offers near $97-$103. Port stocks rose in late September, and talks may extend into late month.

title: Trump's latest China trade spat offers lessons for the copper market amid AI boom
summary: A new U.S.-China trade flare-up is discussed as a reminder of supply-chain fragility for copper. The piece argues that copper demand should rise, supported by AI-driven electrical/compute buildout and increased European defense spending. It also notes renewed focus on diverse delivery and smelting reinvestment, affecting near-term supply expectations.

title: Nickel mining threatens Raja Ampat ecosystems, communities and conservation in Indonesia
summary: Marine activists and a report urge Indonesia to restore Raja Ampat and enforce a ban on coastal/small-island extraction, citing risks from expanding nickel mining. It describes overlapping concessions with reefs and forests and references June 2025 concession revocations and a temporary halt at Gag Nikel, resuming operations later.

title: HSBC upgrades shares of Freeport-McMoRan on higher copper prices
summary: HSBC upgraded Freeport-McMoRan shares to Buy, citing higher metals price assumptions. The analyst said recent volatility and supply disruptions—especially in copper—have lifted outlooks. The firm expects FCX to benefit from strength in copper (and gold), with copper up strongly year-to-date.

title: Bell Copper Corporation: Second Government Critical Mineral Study Begins at Bell Copper's Big Sandy Porphyry Copper Project in Arizona, USA
summary: Bell Copper says Arizona Geological Survey research has started at its Big Sandy porphyry copper project, using company core samples to assess potential critical minerals and supergene profiles. The company also plans to resume drilling (BS-4) after a suspension, but no immediate production or supply changes are mentioned.

title: MTB Metals Corp.: ExGen Resources and MTB Metals Enter into Arrangement Agreement to Merge, Creating a Well-Funded Copper, Gold And Lithium Exploration and Development Company
summary: ExGen Resources and MTB Metals announced an arrangement to merge, creating a better-funded copper-gold and lithium exploration/development company. The deal consolidates MTB’s Telegraph copper-gold assets and adds ExGen’s 20% carried interest in the Empire copper-gold mine, but provides no immediate operational supply change for copper.

title: Bauxite exports surge 23% in Q3 despite challenges in Guinea
summary: Guinea’s bauxite exports rose 23% YoY in Q3 2025 to 39.41mt, despite heavy rains disrupting mining and ports and tighter regulation. Most shipments went to China, reinforcing feedstock supply. While monthly averages fell versus H1 and alumina exports were minimal, net bauxite supply looks supportive for aluminium.

title: Stellantis Follows Ford And Halts Truck Production After Fire At Only Aluminum Supplier For The Industry
summary: Stellantis halted production at its Warren Truck Assembly Plant for at least three weeks after a Sept. 16 fire disrupted output at Novelis’s Oswego aluminum supplier. The shortage is expected to keep production down through end of month, following an industry-wide pattern seen after Ford’s similar action.

title: A Fire at an Aluminum Supplier Is Hurting Ford Big Time
summary: A fire at Novelis’ aluminum sheet plant in Oswego, New York, has disrupted deliveries to multiple automakers. Ford and Stellantis have idled or cut production of several models while prioritizing aluminum parts. The supplier is not expected to fully reopen until 2026, likely tightening near-term aluminum availability.

title: 7 On Your Side Investigates: Cable copper thieves hit AT&T underground vault in South Los Angeles
summary: AT&T reports extensive copper cable theft in South Los Angeles, cutting dozens of cables and disrupting service. The story attributes the theft surge to copper’s higher price and cites a newly signed California bill tightening scrap/junk-dealer rules on penalties and identity verification, aiming to curb stolen-copper recycling. Reward offered for arrests.

title: President Trump's aluminum and steel tariffs strengthen US national security
summary: The piece promotes Trump’s Section 232 aluminum (and steel) tariffs, citing a reinstatement and a raised 50% rate to deter subsidized Canadian imports. It claims the tariffs helped avert aluminum smelter shutdowns and encouraged new domestic smelting and capacity expansions, supporting U.S. aluminum supply and prices.

title: Relief for North QLD: Glencore copper smelter saved | North Queensland Register
summary: The article says a deal has been reached to keep Glencore’s Mount Isa copper smelter and Townsville refinery operating, ending months of uncertainty for workers and local suppliers. It frames the outcome as safeguarding Australia’s refined-metal capacity, implying reduced immediate supply risk for refined copper.

title: Policy Watch and Price Volatility in the Secondary Copper Rod Market: Regional Divergence and Resilient Survival
summary: Secondary copper rod activity weakened as copper prices fell sharply and policy uncertainty (Notice 770) prompted Jiangxi producers to suspend or limit operations. Recycled copper feedstock demand softened due to subsidy fears and delayed customs clearances, while regional order diversion only partially offset the slump. Inventory and cautious procurement kept pressure on pricing next week.

title: Reko Diq copper project to generate $2.8b in first-year: FinMin
summary: Pakistan’s finance minister projects the Reko Diq copper and gold project’s first year of commercial operations could generate $2.8 billion in copper exports, raising the export base by about 10%. He also says more mines and concessions will follow and notes IFC and potential US EXIM participation. Smelting plans are also mentioned.

title: Crisafulli's CopperString plan stirs debate | The North West Star
summary: Queensland’s government says it remains committed to the CopperString transmission project’s eastern link, with early works on a $225m Flinders substation and an expanded community benefits fund. Critics argue funding for the western link to Mount Isa is vague, raising concerns about potential delays affecting grid connection and copper-linked investment timelines.

title: True North Copper appoints new MD for Queensland growth push
summary: True North Copper appointed a new CEO to push development of its Queensland copper assets, including drill-out of the Mt Oxide/Aquila discovery and restart assessments for the Cloncurry project. The company cites strong copper assay intercepts and potential upgrades to restart economics, referencing a recent rise in copper prices.

title: September Enamelled Copper Wire Exports: Down MoM but Up YoY, Industry's High-Growth Trend Remains Unchanged
summary: China’s September copper enamelled wire exports rose 21.17% YoY to 12,248.48 mt, despite a 4.35% MoM drop. Cumulative exports for Jan–Sep were up 24.91% YoY. Growth was strong in India and Turkey, while demand stayed weak in the US and Indonesia.

title: Imports of Recycled Copper Raw Materials Continued to Grow in September, with Supply Landscape Showing Notable Diversification
summary: China’s customs data show imports of copper scrap and shredded copper rose in September 2025 (up 2.63% MoM and 14.8% YoY) and climbed in the first three quarters. Japan and Thailand increased shipments, while the US share stayed low, implying steady demand for recycled copper feedstock.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Exports Increased Both YoY and MoM in September, with India's Growth Rate Reaching 107%
summary: China’s copper plate/sheet and strip exports rose in September to 11,946.39 mt, up 2.32% MoM and 10.84% YoY, with growth also across key destinations like South Korea and India. Total Jan–Sep exports increased 1.22% YoY, while Vietnam and the US declined.

title: Core Silver Corp.: Core Silver Discovers New Copper Porphyry Veins at Laverdiere
summary: Core Silver reports a new copper-bearing porphyry vein system at the Laverdiere Copper Project, with surface assays up to 1.35% Cu and accompanying silver and molybdenum. The company says the confirmed Cu-Mo-Ag mineralized footprint now spans about 4.5 km and remains open for expansion, supporting bullish copper sentiment.

title: Michigan Jeep plant temporarily shuts down over aluminum shortage
summary: A Jeep assembly plant in Michigan will pause production for about three weeks due to an aluminum supply chain issue, with similar cuts at Ford’s Kentucky plant. The shortage stems from a Novelis Oswego hot-mill fire in September that disrupted automotive-grade aluminum sheet supply.

title: Trump tariffs: Ottawa offers relief for steel, aluminum
summary: Canada’s finance ministry granted tariff remission and exemptions for specific aluminum products imported from the U.S. and China, effective Oct. 15, aiming to protect downstream supply chains. The move follows tariffs imposed by the U.S. on Canadian steel and aluminum and should ease near-term aluminum import costs.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Receives Extension from Kennecott Exploration to Ensure Alignment of the Tamarack Nickel Copper Project's Feasibility Study with Environmental Review
summary: Talon Metals said Kennecott Exploration granted a 12-month extension to deliver a feasibility study and make an additional US$10m payment to earn up to 60% of the Tamarack nickel-copper project. The company aims to align the study with Minnesota’s H1 2026 scoping environmental review, supporting permitting timelines.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Receives Extension from Kennecott Exploration to Ensure Alignment of the Tamarack Nickel Copper Project's Feasibility Study with Environmental Review
summary: Talon Metals says Kennecott Exploration granted a 12-month extension to deliver a feasibility study for the Tamarack nickel-copper project, plus a US$10 million payment for an additional 9% earn-in. The company aims to align the study release with Minnesota scoping environmental document timing in H1 2026.

title: BHP Posts Higher First-Quarter Copper Output -- Update
summary: BHP reported first-quarter copper production of 493,600 tons, up 4% from a year earlier, citing record concentrator throughput and improved recoveries at Escondida. BHP also noted resilient commodity demand, but the key market-relevant item for prices is the increase in copper output.

title: Solis Announces $5.9M Placement to Advance Peruvian Copper Portfolio
summary: Solis Minerals announced a $5.9 million placement to fund acquisition and exploration of Peruvian copper projects, including drilling at Ilo Este and planned drilling at Cucho and Cinto. Proceeds will cover exploration and working capital. The release is primarily corporate financing, with no immediate production or supply disruption impact.

title: Solis Minerals Ltd.: Solis Announces $5.9M Placement to Advance Peruvian Copper Portfolio
summary: Solis Minerals announced a $5.9 million placement to fund acquisition and exploration of its Peruvian Cucho copper project, plus drilling at Ilo Este and Cinto. Proceeds are earmarked for drilling and working capital. The update is copper-specific but reflects company-level exploration financing rather than immediate market fundamentals.

title: Star Copper Corp.: Star Copper Reports Drill is Turning at Copper Creek Target in Golden Triangle of BC
summary: Star Copper Corp. says drilling has started on its Copper Creek satellite target within the Golden Triangle, BC, with two ~400m first-pass holes to test copper-gold structures. The release describes geologic targeting and QA/QC, but provides no assay results, implying minimal near-term impact on copper prices.

title: Copper contracts rebound, supported by industrial recovery in China
summary: London Metal Exchange copper contracts rose 0.9% to about $10,700/ton after better-than-expected Chinese industrial production data. The upbeat demand outlook and LME Week supply discussions supported broad base-metal buying, with nickel also up and aluminium slightly lower, reflecting tighter supply concerns.

title: After Platinum Spinoff, Anglo American Exits Zambia Copper Project
summary: Arc Minerals and Anglo American mutually terminated their Zambia Copperbelt exploration joint venture. The termination followed a long period of no drilling activity in 2025 and leaves Anglo American with a smaller African mining footprint. Anglo American cites broader restructuring toward copper exposure, but the Zambian exit dampens copper-linked activity sentiment.

title: KEFI Gold and Copper - The finish line comes into sight
summary: KEFI says it has successfully closed US$240m of senior debt for Ethiopia’s Tulu Kapi project (70% of total debt), and is now moving to finalize an oversubscribed ~US$100m equity risk portion with shareholder meetings in November. Resettlement, access roads, and grid connection continue.

title: Lara Exploration Ltd.: Lara Reports Results of Preliminary Economic Assessment for its Planalto Copper-Gold Project
summary: Lara Exploration reported results of a Preliminary Economic Assessment for its Planalto copper-gold project in Brazil’s Carajás district, estimating multi-decade copper concentrate production and project economics based on assumed copper prices. However, the project is not yet in production, limiting any immediate supply effect on copper markets.

title: Atalaya backs annual outlook as third-quarter copper production rises
summary: Atalaya Mining reported third-quarter 2025 copper production up 1.9% to 12,123 tonnes and said output remains consistent with its full-year guidance of 49,000–52,000 tonnes. It cited strong plant availability and favourable cost trends, alongside higher realized copper prices, while maintaining optimism on growth projects.

title: China's Copper Foil Customs Details for September 2025: Both Imports and Exports Recorded Year-to-Date Growth YoY [SMM Analysis]
summary: China customs data show September 2025 copper foil imports at 6,508.93 mt (+7.28% YoY, -4.60% MoM) and exports at 5,174.88 mt (+44.69% YoY, -0.98% MoM). Export values also rose sharply. The report links stability/exports to AI server and 5G buildout and capacity expansion.

title: Romios Gold Resources Inc.: Romios Begins New Round of Fieldwork on the Kinkaid Copper-Gold-Silver Project, Walker Lane Trend, Nevada
summary: Romios Gold began a 10-day geological mapping and sampling program on its Kinkaid copper-gold-silver project in Nevada to advance PM Skarn and Bismark Hill targets toward drill readiness. Prior assays include high copper values in quartz veins; however, no production or supply changes are announced.

title: Gold Hart Copper Corp.: Gold Hart Copper Launches New Geophysics Survey on Flagship Tolita Gold-Copper-Molybdenum-Silver Asset in Vicuña Chile
summary: Gold Hart Copper Corp. launched additional geophysical surveying at its Tolita gold-copper asset in Chile and expanded drill pads for upcoming drilling. At its Nessa properties, new road construction enabled the discovery of additional visible copper-bearing surface showings and historic pits, with further surveys planned.

title: US primary aluminum growth a 'function of energy'
summary: US President Trump expanded Section 232 tariffs on aluminium imports, aiming to boost US primary smelting. Industry sources say the bigger limiter is affordable, long-term low-cost electricity—power dominates aluminium smelting costs. The Midwest aluminium premium rose but was steady late September, reflecting tariff-supported support amid energy-driven capacity uncertainty.

title: Los Angeles copper wire theft is leaving communities in the dark. Here's how a new law could fix the problem
summary: Los Angeles reports widespread copper wire theft that has disabled streetlights and increased repair backlogs. City and business leaders urge Gov. Newsom to sign AB 476, which adds verification and penalties for recyclers buying stolen scrap and restricts possession of certain public-infrastructure wire. A reward program is also approved.

title: Why is a US bike brand asking the Trump administration to include bicycles in proposed 50% aluminium and steel tariff?
summary: A US bike manufacturer lobbied to include bicycles in a proposed 50% Section 232 tariff on steel and aluminium content. Industry groups argue the tariff would raise costs on imported bikes, requiring metal-content declarations, but the actual impact on aluminium demand and prices is indirect and depends on whether the request is granted.

title: MMG Reports Increase In Total Copper Output In Q3
summary: MMG said Q3 total copper output rose 11% to just over 127,000 tonnes, mainly driven by Las Bambas. This implies higher near-term copper supply. While the company cited financial milestones, the production update is the main factor likely to weigh on copper prices over the next days to weeks.

title: PPX Mining Corp.: PPX Mining Intersects High-Grade at Callanquitas Sulfide Zone with up to 49.52 g/t Gold, 11,597 g/t Silver and 11.1% Copper
summary: PPX Mining reported assay results from four underground drill holes at its Igor Project in Peru, including strong copper grades in sulfide zones (up to 11.1% Cu) alongside high gold and silver values. The update is exploratory and does not indicate production changes, limiting immediate copper supply impact.

title: Century Aluminum Reports Electrical Equipment Failure Affecting One Potline at Grundartangi, Iceland Smelter
summary: Century Aluminum’s Norðurál Grundartangi smelter in Iceland temporarily stopped one of its two potlines after an electrical equipment failure. Output is reduced by roughly two-thirds while replacement equipment and recovery timelines are assessed. The other potline remains at full production; losses are expected to be insured.

title: Century Aluminum Reports Electrical Equipment Failure
summary: Century Aluminum’s Norðurál Grundartangi smelter in Iceland shut one of its two potlines due to an electrical equipment failure, cutting production at the site by about two-thirds. The other potline runs full production. The company is assessing replacement timelines; losses are expected to be insured.

title: Politics Insider: Canada-U.S. trade deal on steel, aluminum and energy could come this month, sources say
summary: Sources say Canada and the U.S. may sign this month a trade deal covering steel, aluminum and energy. The potential agreement would offer relief to Canada’s metals industry battered by U.S. tariffs, likely easing tariff-driven bearish expectations for aluminum prices in the short term.

title: Citigroup: Bullish on Copper and Aluminum in the Medium Term, Copper Prices to Reach $12,000/mt in the Next 6–12 Months
summary: Citi says it remains bullish on copper and aluminium, projecting copper to reach $12,000/mt over the next 6–12 months and aluminium to hit $3,500/mt by 2027. The near-term discussion focuses on gold and the US shutdown, with no direct short-term catalyst for these metals.

title: BHP starts FY strong as copper and iron-ore output lift in tightening markets
summary: BHP reported a strong start to the year, with group copper production up 4% to 494,000 tonnes due to record throughput at Escondida and stable output across other assets. It reaffirmed full-year copper guidance and cited competitor disruptions tightening supply, alongside higher average realized copper prices.

title: Boosted by Extensive Use in AI Data Centers, Copper Demand is Expected to Soar; Undervalued Mogotes Metals Inc. (OTC: MOGMF | TSXV: MOG) is a Great Way to Profit From Copper's Unique and Growing Role in the Economy
summary: Sponsored article claims copper demand is set to soar as AI data centers, EVs, and power-grid modernization expand, citing expected higher copper intensity and data center buildouts. It also notes production curtailments from mine disruptions. Overall, it frames a bullish near-term copper demand/supply outlook.

title: Steel Dynamics Expands Amid Improving Aluminum, Steel Market | Industrial Info Resources
summary: Steel Dynamics reported stronger Q3 results and plans to expand capacity in aluminum, including its aluminum flat-rolled mill and a proposed aluminum-recycling plant in Arizona. Management cited reviving demand for aluminum products and improving market conditions, suggesting supportive near-term sentiment for aluminum supply and pricing.

title: Hercules Metals Corp.: Hercules Metals Intersects 273 m of 0.60% Copper, within 379 m of 0.50% Copper, Including 35 m of 1.01% Copper and 6.2 g/t Silver at the Leviathan Porphyry System
summary: Hercules Metals reported long copper-bearing drill intersections at its Leviathan porphyry target (e.g., 273 m of 0.60% Cu) indicating grade continuity and potential scale. The update supports exploration expectations but does not change near-term production. Aluminium is not addressed beyond unrelated context.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc and Freeport Successfully Complete 2025 Aurora Expansion Focused Drill Program at Joy Copper-Gold District
summary: Amarc and Freeport report completion of a 2025 expansion-focused drill program at the AuRORA Cu-Au-Ag project in BC’s JOY District, including step-out and infill drilling and expectations of further assays. Freeport funds the 2025 program. The news is exploration-focused, with limited near-term implications for copper supply and prices.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.63% Higher at $4.9610 — Data Talk
summary: Comex copper finished up 0.63% to $4.9610, according to the data talk. The move reflects modest short-term strength in copper futures, which can influence near-term expectations for the metal’s spot and related pricing, though the size suggests no major shock.

title: Copper prices save Teck Resources despite setbacks at Chile copper mine
summary: Teck reported Q3 profits aided by higher copper prices, even as its Chile Quebrada Blanca copper mine struggles after an expansion. Tailings drainage problems raised costs and delayed ramp-up, prompting a production guidance cut. Analysts cite multiple mine disruptions totaling 5–6% of global supply, tightening copper expectations.

title: ALLEN WEST: Trump's Aluminum And Steel Tariffs Are Vital To Protect Homeland
summary: The commentary argues that Trump’s 50% Section 232 tariffs on foreign aluminum imports are restoring U.S. aluminum production. It cites declines in U.S. primary aluminum output after an earlier Canadian exemption, smelter shutdowns, and claims renewed smelter expansion plans in Alabama, Oklahoma, and South Carolina.

title: Teck seeks to ease investor concerns around copper joint venture with Anglo as shareholder vote looms
summary: Teck sought to ease investor concerns ahead of a Dec. 9 shareholder vote on its all-stock acquisition by Anglo, which would potentially combine Teck’s Quebrada Blanca and Anglo’s Collahuasi copper operations into Anglo Teck. Regulatory approvals in Canada/China and joint-venture ownership details remain uncertain.

title: Sterlite back in Thoothukudi with green copper. Will it get the red carpet?
summary: An exclusive report covers protests around Sterlite’s Thoothukudi copper plant, where a feasibility study recommends recycled copper use, closing some polluting sections, and a CSR corpus. It also notes ongoing counter-protests, leaving uncertain timing and capacity changes that could influence near-term copper supply expectations.

title: DRC, Zambia bring in Mercuria to build copper trading
summary: DRC’s Gecamines and Zambia’s IDC are partnering with Mercuria to trade copper cathode and concentrates, using trading capacity to monetize rising production and manage smelting constraints. Gecamines traded ~88,000 tonnes via Mercuria in 2024 and expects higher volumes as output ramps up. Zambia’s IRL has sold 200,000+ tonnes of concentrates.

title: Canada Drops Tariffs on U.S. Aluminum After Vowing to Fight Trump
summary: Canada’s government removed tariffs on certain U.S. and Chinese steel and aluminum imports, with the Finance Ministry order dated Oct. 15/confirmed Oct. 17. The move is intended to ease pressure on Canadian industry and follows prior tariff actions. Analysts may view it as supportive for near-term aluminum sentiment.

title: Copper theft surge impacts Phoenix businesses and neighborhoods
summary: Phoenix police report copper theft cases more than doubling, with thieves targeting utility boxes, street lights and construction sites. Losses include cut internet/phone service and risks to hospital connectivity. Authorities cite rising copper prices as a driver, but the impact described is local infrastructure disruption.

title: [SMM Analysis] Global Copper Scrap Restructuring: From Policy to Resources Rebalancing
summary: SMM describes a restructuring of global copper scrap flows after China’s 2018 solid waste import ban and subsequent tightening by Southeast Asian countries. Scrap trade shifted from China-led processing toward regulated hubs like India and the Middle East. Compliance and traceability requirements reduce low-quality supply, potentially supporting higher copper prices.

title: Angola to commence production at first major copper mine
summary: Angola’s Mines Minister said the Tetelo copper mine will begin production soon. The first major large-scale copper venture is a $250m investment and is expected to yield about 25,000 tonnes per year of copper concentrate initially, potentially adding supply ahead of broader expansion.

title: Antofagasta cuts cost guidance but says copper output to be at low end
summary: Antofagasta cut 2025 guidance for cash costs and capex, expecting net cash costs of USD1.20–1.30/lb versus the prior USD1.45–1.65 range. Copper output is guided to the low end of 660,000–700,000 tonnes amid rising unit costs and weaker copper sales.

title: Magna Mining Inc.: Magna Mining Reports Multiple Copper, Nickel and Precious Metal Rich Intersections from the R2 Target at the Levack Mine in Sudbury, Ontario
summary: Magna Mining reported new assay results from drillhole FNX6083-W2 at the Levack Mine in Sudbury, including copper-rich chalcopyrite veins (up to 19.3% Cu) and nickel-rich pentlandite-pyrrhotite veins (up to 12.4% Ni), alongside PGM and silver. It is an exploration update with assays pending for other holes.

title: Fathom Nickel Inc.: Fathom Announces Extension of the Historic Gochager Lake Deposit Host Rock over a 3.5+ km Strike Length
summary: Fathom Nickel reported updated mapping and pXRF/geochemical results extending the Gochager Lake project’s Ni-Cu sulphide “container rock” along a 3.5 km strike length. The company highlights disseminated and vein-hosted pyrrhotite/pentlandite with potential for further high-grade discoveries, but provides no production or confirmed new reserves.

title: Freeport-McMoRan profit beats as higher copper prices cushion production drop
summary: Freeport-McMoRan reported better-than-expected profit as higher copper prices outweighed lower output after a mudflow forced a shutdown at the Grasberg mine in Indonesia, leaving seven workers dead. Realized copper prices rose about 9% year-on-year, supporting results, while Q4 copper sales guidance declined.

title: Antofagasta lowers its annual copper production forecast
summary: Antofagasta reported Q3 output of 161,800 tons and revised its annual copper production outlook to the lower end of 660,000–700,000 tons. Nine-month production rose 2.8% year-on-year, but weaker annual expectations and reduced investment, amid tense supply conditions, pressured the stock and sentiment near-term.

title: Angola Set to Launch Aluminium Production in December Amid Industrial Expansion – Medafrica Times
summary: Angola plans to launch large-scale aluminium production in December 2025 at a new facility in the Barra do Dande Free Zone. The $1.6 billion, China-linked project aims to produce aluminium ingots, alloys, and sheets for export, boosting domestic capacity and employment as the country diversifies away from oil.

title: Copper project north of Sault gets chief geologist | Elliot Lake Standard
summary: A chief geologist was appointed for Sterling Metals’ Soo Copper Project north of Sault Ste. Marie. The company highlights the high-grade copper discovery and ongoing drilling at priority targets, plus a new exploration agreement with the Garden River First Nation covering related claims in the area.

title: Green aluminium deficit looms in Europe
summary: Electricity failures at Nordural’s Icelandic aluminium smelter cut output by two-thirds, including a full potline shutdown, while Mozambique’s Mozal faces power-supply stalemate that could limit production. With Europe’s duty-free ‘green’ P1020 supply tight into 2026, premiums rise and traders warn of a potential deficit.

title: Nornickel reduces nickel and copper output by 4% over nine months
summary: Nornickel said its nickel output fell 4% to 140,000 tons in January–September 2025 and copper output fell 4% to 313,000 tons. The company cited changes in ore quality and the need to replenish work-in-progress inventories. Q3 nickel rose but Q3 copper declined to 100,000 tons.

title: Nornickel reduces nickel and copper output by 4% over nine months
summary: Nornickel said its nickel output fell 4% to 140,000 tons and copper output fell 4% to 313,000 tons in Jan–Sep 2025. The company attributed declines to a higher share of disseminated ores, fewer rich ores, and replenishing work-in-progress inventories. Q3 nickel rose vs Q2, while copper fell slightly.

title: Tight Aluminum Scrap Supply Lifts Price Center, Highlighting Resilience in ADC12 Cost Support[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Weekly review reports a slight rise in primary A00 aluminium and a stronger ADC12 spot market, driven mainly by tight aluminium scrap supply. Scrap procurement prices increased, spreads between primary and scrap widened, and destocking reduced secondary alloy ingot inventory. Costs remain rigid despite minor pullbacks in silicon/copper, supporting aluminium bids.

title: Copper Wire Theft Hits LA EV Chargers Hard
summary: Copper wire theft is disrupting Los Angeles EV charging expansion as thieves cut and hack chargers’ copper cables. The story says rising copper prices are making theft more common, while repairs cost $650–$1,500 per incident. California’s AB 476 increases penalties and companies add anti-theft hardware and cable designs.

title: Angola Throws Its Hat in Africa's Copper Ring with Tetelo
summary: Angola’s Tetelo copper project, a $250 million mine led by China’s Shining Star Icarus, is expected to start production soon, Reuters reported. The move would add new supply from Angola alongside other African copper producers. Although no date is given, the announcement is supportive for copper prices in the near term.

title: Rural Women NZ calls for protection as copper network phase‑out considered
summary: Rural Women New Zealand urged that members be considered in a telecommunications sector review as a copper network phase-out is contemplated. While the piece focuses on inclusivity in services, it signals potential reduction in copper-based network use, which can weigh on copper demand expectations.

title: Alumina Index Correction Rocks FOB Brazil Market, Sending Ripples Through Global Commodity Benchmarks
summary: Fastmarkets issued upward corrections to the FOB Brazil inferred alumina index (MB-ALU-0010) in October 2025, citing procedural methodology lapses. The revised higher alumina price boosts producer revenues but raises immediate raw-material costs for aluminum smelters, likely pressuring aluminum margins and near-term aluminum sentiment.

title: Alcoa: High U.S. aluminum prices offset Trump tariff costs
summary: Alcoa says U.S. tariffs on Canadian aluminum cost it an extra US$69 million versus the prior quarter, with further increases expected. However, rapidly rising U.S. aluminum prices—driven by declining inventories and imports and a wider Midwest premium—have largely offset the tariff hit, leaving overall pressure mixed.

title: Canadian Critical Minerals Inc. Strikes Gold (and Copper, Silver) with Bull River Revenue Boost
summary: Canadian Critical Minerals Inc. said it earned USD $167,000 from a provisional payment for 942 dry metric tonnes of stockpiled mineralized material sold to New Gold’s New Afton operation. The material averaged 2.02% copper, supporting permitting funding. Impact on wider copper prices is likely minimal due to scale.

title: Australia's Cobre Starts New Drilling Campaign at Ngami Copper Project in Botswana
summary: Cobre Limited began a drilling campaign at the Ngami Copper Project in Botswana, targeting the Cosmos zone near the existing Comet deposit. Two diamond holes will test anomalous copper-silver mineralization to refine resources and guide further exploration, with potential implications for project economics but limited near-term market impact.

title: Novelis aluminum plant fire could cost Ford $1 billion, report says
summary: A fire at Novelis’ aluminum plant in Oswego halted production and prompted Ford to work with Novelis to source substitute aluminum for its still-operational cold-rolling section. Ford estimates up to $1 billion in earnings impact and other automakers also rely on Novelis, implying near-term aluminum supply tightness.

title: Aluminium producer Norsk Hydro's Q3 core profit lags expectations
summary: Norsk Hydro reported weaker Q3 core profit due to lower alumina prices and a stronger Norwegian crown, partially offset by higher volumes. Reuters notes U.S. aluminium tariffs have disrupted trade flows, driving record physical premiums and higher costs for American buyers, while global supply is rerouted and Western barriers support regional premiums.

title: Noronex fires up rigs for Botswana copper push with South32

title: Copper Prices in London Hit Record High on Supply Fears -- Commodities Roundup
summary: London Metal Exchange copper prices hit record highs, driven by supply worries. LME three-month copper rose to around $11,173/ton as mine disruptions were reported and producer forecasts weakened. Glencore trimmed the upper end of its copper output guidance after lower production, while Anglo American flagged reduced output from Collahuasi.

title: Southern Copper Corporation Reports Production Results for the Third Quarter and Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025
summary: Southern Copper reported Q3 and nine-month production results. Copper output fell to 234,892 tonnes in Q3 from 252,219 tonnes a year earlier, and to 714,098 tonnes over nine months from 734,963 tonnes. Other mined metals rose, but copper is the key tracked input.

title: Copper's Historic Ascent: London Prices Shatter Records Amidst Unprecedented Supply Squeeze
summary: London LME copper surged to a record $11,146/ton, driven by acute supply outages at major mines, sharply lower LME inventories, and forecasts of a growing refined deficit in 2026. Supportive macro factors (weaker USD, US-China trade optimism) further bolster near-term demand expectations, keeping upward price pressure.

title: Morgan Stanley Bets Big on Commodities: Gold and Copper Shine Amidst Inflationary Pressures
summary: Morgan Stanley signals a major shift toward commodities, highlighting a bullish view on copper. It projects the copper market could face its largest deficit in over two decades by 2026, citing tight physical supply, dwindling inventories, and strong demand. The strategy may steer institutional flows toward copper-linked assets.

title: Copper hits all-time high, but analysts warn rally could be poised to cool
summary: Copper surged to a record high as renewed mine-supply concerns and expectations of a US-China trade deal boosted sentiment. Glencore cut copper production guidance and the ICSG sees a refined deficit next year. Analysts warn gains may cool if demand doesn’t strengthen and much of the macro catalyst is priced in.

title: The Secondary Copper Rod Industry Under the Impact of Notice No. 770: Policy Uncertainty and Market Restructuring
summary: Policy Notice No. 770 standardizes investment/tax incentives and removes irregular refund/subsidy practices for secondary copper rod makers, increasing effective tax burden. Enterprises in key Jiangxi clusters suspended production and August output fell ~30% (≈48,800 mt supply impact). Limited September restarts and slower recycled-material clearance keep supply tight; costs rise.

title: Copper's Green Gold Rush: Demand Soars Amidst Global Energy Transition
summary: Copper demand is surging on the green energy transition, driven by EVs, wind and solar buildout, grids, and electrification. Supply growth is constrained by falling ore grades, fewer large discoveries, and long mine lead times. A US 50% tariff on unrefined copper adds local volatility, supporting expectations of higher copper prices and tightness.

title: Hunter businesses concerned about future of Tomago Aluminum | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Hunter businesses worry Tomago Aluminum may become commercially unviable, after a consultation process found no sustainable operating pathway beyond 2028. Proposed cost increases for coal-fired and renewable options from January 2029 raise closure risk, threatening export metal shipments and local jobs, creating potential aluminium supply concerns.

title: Hunter businesses concerned about future of Tomago Aluminum | Newcastle Herald
summary: Local businesses warn that Tomago Aluminum may become commercially unviable beyond 2028, with costs for coal-fired or renewable options under market proposals expected to rise sharply from January 2029. Possible closure would disrupt jobs and export shipments, implying reduced aluminium supply.

title: Hunter businesses concerned about future of Tomago Aluminum | The Macleay Argus
summary: Hunter businesses fear Tomago Aluminium may not remain viable beyond 2028, with costs of coal-fired or renewable options rising significantly from January 2029. A potential closure would impact freight and regional manufacturers. The smelter is described as important for grid stability, and no final decision has been made.

title: Hunter businesses concerned about future of Tomago Aluminum | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Local businesses worry Tomago Aluminium in Australia may not remain commercially viable beyond 2028 after failed efforts to secure sustainable cost pathways. Consultation with employees follows proposed costs for coal-fired or renewable power from January 2029. Potential closure could disrupt freight and regional customers, implying aluminium supply risk.

title: Cameroon's Aluminum Output Drops 40% in Q1 2025 Following Alucam Technical Failure
summary: Cameroon’s aluminum output fell 40.8% in Q1 2025 after Alucam shut down more than half of its electrolysis cells due to a technical failure. The decline cut ingot and slab production by the same percentage, contributing to lower turnover and ongoing losses while the firm seeks a strategic investor.

title: Copper Study Group highlights impact of mine supply hits - Academia
summary: ICSG says several large copper mines suffered accidents (Kakula seismic flooding, El Teniente collapse, Grasberg mud inflow), cutting 2025 mine supply growth and tightening mined concentrate availability. It projects a 2026 refined deficit risk (150,000 tonnes short) versus earlier surplus expectations, supporting copper price firmness.

title: First Quantum Q3 Copper Output Drops 9% as Zambian Mines Underperform
summary: First Quantum reported Q3 2025 copper output of 104,626 tonnes, down 9% year-on-year, largely due to weaker performance at its key Zambian mines Sentinel and Kansanshi. The company also cut its 2025 production forecast to 410,000 tonnes from 440,000 tonnes, implying tighter near-term copper supply expectations.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | The Maitland Mercury
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide the fate of the plant. Owners including Rio Tinto, CSR and Hydro have rejected government offers, citing that post-2028 power costs—coal or renewables—would sharply raise operating costs. The smelter may cease at contract end, risking major job losses.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | The Advertiser - Cessnock
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged Tomago Aluminium owners (Rio Tinto, CSR, Hydro) to decide on the plant’s fate after previous government offers were rejected. Tomago cites rising energy costs for 2029, potentially making operations unviable and prompting consultation about possible closure after end-2028.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Camden Haven Courier
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged owners of the Tomago Aluminium smelter to decide its fate. The plant may shut end-2028 after market proposals implied much higher electricity costs, making operations unviable. The potential closure threatens jobs and would be a major industrial loss in the Hunter, supporting tighter aluminium supply expectations.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | The Singleton Argus
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged Tomago Aluminium’s owners (Rio Tinto, CSR, Hydro) to decide on the plant’s fate. The smelter may cease at end-2028 because power costs under new market proposals from 2029 would rise sharply, making operations unviable. Uncertainty increases in a potential aluminium supply shock.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Great Lakes Advocate
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on the plant’s fate. The joint venture (Rio Tinto, CSR, Hydro Aluminium) says rising electricity costs under proposals threaten viability, with potential closure around end-2028. If the smelter shuts, thousands of jobs would be lost, heightening aluminium supply concerns.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Manning River Times
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged owners of Tomago Aluminium to decide on the plant’s fate after Rio Tinto, CSR and Hydro Aluminium rejected government offers. The smelter may become uneconomic because energy costs rise from 2029, prompting consultation and expectations it could close after current contracts, risking job losses and output.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | The Scone Advocate
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged Tomago Aluminium’s owners (Rio Tinto, CSR and Hydro) to decide on the smelter’s future. The plant may cease operations after its electricity supply contract ends because energy proposals would raise costs materially, making the smelter unviable, with consultation ongoing until November 21.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Muswellbrook Chronicle
summary: NSW Premier Minns urged Tomago Aluminium owners (Rio Tinto, CSR, Hydro) to decide on the fate of the Tomago smelter. The company says higher energy costs from Jan 2029 would make operations unviable and is consulting workers about potential cessation by end-2028. Closure risk may tighten aluminium supply expectations.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Newcastle Herald
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on the plant’s future. The smelter faces higher electricity costs after its supply contract expires, making both coal and renewable options more expensive and operations unviable. Consultation continues, but workers expect closure by end-2028.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Port Macquarie News
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged Tomago Aluminium owners (Rio Tinto, CSR and Hydro) to decide the plant’s fate. With existing power contracts ending, the company says available market options would greatly increase costs and render the smelter unviable, contemplating closure and consulting workers.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Port Stephens Examiner
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on the plant’s fate after rejecting government offers. The smelter says energy cost proposals for January 2029 would raise costs significantly, making operations unviable and forcing it to contemplate ceasing at contract end. Closure fears could reduce aluminium supply expectations.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | The Macleay Argus
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on the plant’s fate. Owners Rio Tinto, CSR and Hydro reportedly rejected government support. Tomago says rising electricity costs from 2029 could make operations unviable, prompting consultation on potential closure and potential job losses.

title: Tribeca Resources signs option agreement for Jiguata Copper acquisition
summary: Tribeca Resources signed a definitive option agreement to acquire a 100% interest in the Jiguata porphyry copper property in northern Chile, with staged payments and at least 3,000m of drilling over the coming years. The company plans to start fieldwork soon, but no near-term production impact is described.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Dungog Chronicle
summary: NSW Premier Minns pressed Tomago Aluminium owners (Rio Tinto/CSR/Hydro) to decide on the plant’s fate after rejecting government offers. Tomago says higher energy costs from Jan 2029 could make operations unviable, prompting consultation on possible closure by end-2028, threatening jobs and output.

title: Friel's EGT eyes potential sale of Swedish copper project
summary: European Green Transition (EGT) signed a six-month option to sell its Pajala copper project in northern Sweden. The buyer would fund due diligence, but no transaction is guaranteed. The piece frames copper demand as supported by electrification and EU critical minerals policy, yet offers no production impact or pricing terms.

title: Camino Minerals Corp: Camino and Nittetsu Commence Proprietary Leaching Studies for Growth Opportunities at the Puquios Copper Project in Chile
summary: Camino Minerals and Nittetsu Mining will start proprietary leaching studies at Nittetsu’s Tokyo facility to assess scalability of the Puquios copper project in Chile. The mine is permitted for construction and uses SXEW leaching. The company is pursuing financing and evaluating scale-up opportunities for deeper copper.

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns urges Tomago Aluminium owners to decide on plant's fate | Gloucester Advocate
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns urged owners of the Tomago Aluminium smelter to decide its fate. The joint venture (Rio Tinto, CSR, Hydro) says electricity proposals would raise costs significantly after current contracts expire, making operations unviable. Consultation with workers runs until Nov 21; closure would reduce aluminium supply.

title: Benton Resources Inc.: Benton Resources Drilling Continues to Delineate the South Pond Gold-Copper Deposit with Shallow
summary: Benton Resources reported encouraging drilling results from its South Pond gold-copper deposit, noting chalcopyrite in many holes and base-metal assays still pending. The company highlighted intersections with copper values, including previous reported copper grades, and stated the mineralized horizon continues north and remains open for expansion.

title: Copper Quest signs definitive agreement to acquire Kitimat copper-gold project
summary: Copper Quest Exploration agreed to acquire 100% of the Kitimat copper-gold project in British Columbia, highlighting infrastructure and historical drilling showing copper grades around 0.5% and gold results. The deal requires due diligence before final share issuance in January 2026, with no near-term output impact.

title: Abitibi Metals 150m Step-Out Extends B26 Western Copper-Gold Zone With 8.16% CuEq Over 3.2m Within 11.0m at 3.93% CuEq, Highlighting Significant Expansion Potential
summary: Abitibi Metals announced drill results showing a 150-metre step-out extension of the high-grade Western Copper-Gold zone at B26 in Quebec, including multiple copper-rich CuEq intercepts and a new copper-gold discovery to the west. The update supports continued expansion potential but does not indicate immediate supply impacts.

title: Abitibi Metals Strikes Gold (and Copper) with Major B26 Western Zone Extension
summary: Abitibi Metals announced strong drill results from its B26 Western Copper-Gold Zone, including 8.16% CuEq over 3.2 meters with reported copper grades and broader mineralized continuity. The step-out expansion de-risks the project and boosts expectations for future copper supply, likely supporting near-term copper sentiment.

title: Anglo American Targets Full Recovery at Chile's Collahuasi Copper Mine by 2027
summary: Anglo American said Chile’s Collahuasi copper mine will recover toward full capacity by 2027, but output is currently constrained by lower-grade ore and operational issues. The company cautioned near-term production may be lower than expected, adding pressure to a tight market where supply disruption fears are already supporting record copper prices.

title: Gold and Copper: The Unseen Forces Powering Market Returns – BlackRock Unveils Overlooked Opportunities
summary: BlackRock and other strategists argue copper is surging due to a growing supply deficit (declining ore grades and aging mines) against resilient demand from electrification, EVs, renewables, and AI/data centers. Morgan Stanley’s deficit forecast and claims that copper must reach ~ $12,000/t support expectations of further price strength.

title: BlackRock Sounds the Alarm: Are Investors Missing the 'Bigger Picture' in Gold and Copper?
summary: BlackRock says copper is indispensable for the energy transition and AI build-out but that mined ore supply is severely constrained. It argues copper prices may need to rise substantially (toward an incentive level) to fund new mines, expecting a demand-supportive backdrop despite localized construction softness.

title: Comex Copper Settles 3.04% Lower at $5.0780 — Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures settled 3.04% lower at $5.0780. The move signals bearish near-term price pressure for copper, reflecting weaker sentiment or demand expectations driving settlement losses into the latest trading session. No comparable data is given for nickel or aluminium.

title: Runoff from Atalco alumina refinery into Mississippi River raises environmental concerns
summary: Runoff from Atalco/Atlantic Alumina’s drainage pipe exceeded permit limits and showed caustic, discolored plumes into the Mississippi River. Regulators are pursuing violations linked to “red mud” handling and wastewater outfalls, with potential penalties and further permit requirements. As a key U.S. alumina producer, disruption risk could affect aluminium supply.

title: Rio Tinto warns of closure of Tomago aluminium smelter without long-term cheaper power deal
summary: Rio Tinto warns the Tomago aluminium smelter may shut unless it secures a long-term cheaper power deal. The Albanese government and Rio remain in a stalemate after Rio rejected a proposed federal-NSW bailout reportedly exceeding $1 billion, with the minister signaling openness to options like new ownership to keep output running.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Reports Third Quarter 2025 Results
summary: Capstone Copper reported Q3 2025 results showing record adjusted EBITDA driven by higher sulphide output and lower C1 cash costs, with copper production and sales exceeding prior year. The company also sanctioned its Mantoverde expansion and reiterated 2025 guidance, reinforcing positive near-term copper margin and production expectations.

title: Dr. Copper is Quietly Crushing the S&P 500 - The Daily Reckoning
summary: Copper is presented as rallying to a new all-time high above $11,200/ton, with the Indonesian Grasberg mine disaster (mudslide) allegedly shutting ~70% of production indefinitely. The piece also argues ongoing demand growth (data centers, EVs) plus a supply deficit is reinforcing tightness and upside for copper prices.

title: Panama President Mulino Strengthens Control Regarding Copper and Calms the Waters with Minera Panamá
summary: Panama’s president says the government has strengthened oversight of the Cobre Panamá mining project, with the environment ministry starting an environmental audit while the company hires staff for authorized mine maintenance and partial reactivation. Tensions with First Quantum have eased through dialogue, reducing near-term disruption risk for copper supply.

title: Emerald Horizon pitches its technology as a solution for Tomago Aluminium's energy crisis | The Singleton Argus
summary: Emerald Horizon pitches its ADES technology to provide long-term, zero-emissions baseload power to Tomago Aluminium, estimating enough capacity to support the smelter with multiple 15 MW modules. It argues the model would stabilize industrial power supply amid high energy prices, potentially improving aluminium production economics and market sentiment.

title: Emerald Horizon pitches its technology as a solution for Tomago Aluminium's energy crisis | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Emerald Horizon is pitching its accelerator-driven, thorium-based energy technology as a solution to Tomago Aluminium’s energy crisis. It claims the system can deliver containerized baseload power for 20 years and estimates enough units to power Tomago. The company is lobbying regulators and offers power-purchase agreements to reduce upfront costs.

title: Emerald Horizon pitches its technology as a solution for Tomago Aluminium's energy crisis | Camden Haven Courier
summary: Emerald Horizon is pitching its Accelerator-Driven Energy Source (ADES) technology as a zero-emissions baseload power solution for Australia, estimating enough modules could supply Tomago Aluminium. The firm plans to provide “energy as a service” via power purchase agreements, potentially easing Tomago’s energy-price and supply pressures that affect aluminium output costs.

title: Emerald Horizon pitches its technology as a solution for Tomago Aluminium's energy crisis | The Advertiser - Cessnock
summary: Emerald Horizon is pitching its ADES zero-emissions power technology as a way to supply long-term baseload energy to Tomago Aluminium amid Australia’s high power prices. The company estimates many modules could run for decades under power-purchase agreements. If adopted, lower energy costs could support aluminum output and sentiment.

title: Opposition Leader Sussan Ley takes aim at Albanese over Tomago aluminium smelter's 'uncertain future'
summary: Opposition Leader Sussan Ley criticizes Prime Minister Albanese over the ‘uncertain future’ of the Tomago aluminium smelter. The dispute implies possible risk to ongoing aluminium production in Australia, which could affect near-term supply expectations and support aluminium prices as markets weigh disruption probabilities.

title: Indonesia's Alumina Power Play: Leveraging Price and Policy to Redraw the Global Map
summary: Indonesia’s alumina FOB prices have fallen sharply (down from ~$730/mt in Oct 2024 to ~$325/mt in Oct 2025) alongside accelerated declines in China’s alumina benchmark. It also cites multiple Indonesian alumina capacity expansions driven by the bauxite export ban, implying improved feedstock availability and competitive production economics for aluminium.

title: Emerald Horizon pitches its technology as a solution for Tomago Aluminium's energy crisis | Great Lakes Advocate
summary: Emerald Horizon says its accelerator-driven, zero-emissions energy modules could supply long-duration baseload power for Tomago Aluminium, potentially improving affordability amid Australia’s power-price crisis. The company estimates enough units to power the smelter and is lobbying for technology approval, using power-purchase agreements for 20 years.

title: Sussan Ley advocates nuclear power as an option for Tomago Aluminium . | Newcastle Herald
summary: Opposition Leader Sussan Ley says Tomago Aluminium’s energy-cost pressure threatens closure and argues nuclear power should be part of Australia’s future energy mix by lifting the moratorium to enable private-sector investment. The piece links rising energy prices to a cost-price squeeze affecting smelting and related regional manufacturers.

title: Sussan Ley refused entry to Tomago Aluminium, says Anthony Albanese playing 'games'
summary: Opposition leader Sussan Ley was blocked from touring Rio Tinto’s Tomago Aluminium smelter. The company says competitively priced electricity is the key challenge and that market proposals for 2029 power would raise costs, potentially making the smelter unviable and requiring it to contemplate ceasing operations after its current supply contract.

title: Sussan Ley advocates nuclear power as an option for Tomago Aluminium . | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Opposition Leader Sussan Ley visited Tomago Aluminium amid concerns the smelter may close due to high energy costs. She urged lifting Australia’s nuclear moratorium to provide affordable baseload power for industry. NSW Premier Minns also pressed owners Rio Tinto and others for clear future plans to avoid delays.

title: Not Only Tariffs On Trucks: Trump Administration's Proclamation Amends The Tariff Landscape On Automobiles, Steel, And Aluminum
summary: The Trump administration’s Section 232 proclamation expands new tariffs on medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and parts starting Nov. 1, adding complexity for importers. It also offers limited USMCA-linked reductions in steel and aluminum tariffs for qualifying Canada/Mexico producers, but overall tariff expansion is likely a near-term headwind for aluminium prices.

title: Sussan Ley advocates nuclear power as an option for Tomago Aluminium . | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Opposition Leader Sussan Ley argues nuclear power could help provide affordable baseload electricity for Tomago Aluminium, which is nearing closure because it can’t secure sustainable long-term energy costs. NSW’s Premier urges owners (including Rio Tinto and Hydro) to clarify plans as high power prices squeeze costs across the region.

title: In October, the Aluminum Processing PMI dropped to 48.9%, re-entering contraction territory. [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s aluminum processing composite PMI fell to 48.9% in October, back into contraction, with most sub-sectors weakening. Causes cited include weaker construction and industrial demand, high aluminum prices reducing downstream purchases, holiday/seasonal disruptions, and inventory pressure. November PMI is expected to remain below 50.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Plans Angola Copper Drill Program by Q4 2025
summary: Ivanhoe Mines said it will start a 6,400-meter copper drilling campaign in Angola by end-2025 on an exploration license acquired in 2023. The move is part of expanding Africa’s copper footprint and follows strong demand narratives, while Angola prepares its first large copper mine, Tetelo.

title: Aldebaran's Altar copper-gold project PEA reveals 48-year mine life
summary: Aldebaran Resources released a PEA for its Altar copper-gold project in Argentina, targeting a 48-year mine life. The base case forecasts sustained copper output (about 108,579 t/year in the first 20 years) and positive economics, with NPV and IRR improving at higher spot copper prices.

title: China's industry association recommends capacity cap for copper, lead and zinc
summary: China’s non-ferrous metals industry association recommends capping capacity for copper (and others) to curb overbuilding that has crushed smelters’ profitability and processing fees. It notes copper concentrate processing fees have hit record lows. The piece also says aluminium is an exception, implying comparatively steadier conditions for aluminium.

title: China's Oct Alumina Output Dipped   Further Cuts Expected in November
summary: China’s metallurgical-grade alumina output rose in October but operating rate slipped to 83.09%, driven by calciner maintenance and constrained bauxite supply. October prices approached cost, squeezing profits. November is expected to stay in surplus with further production cuts and cost-pressure, potentially easing supply gradually and supporting aluminium expectations.

title: Debut use for Tadano lattice boom at Peruvian copper mine
summary: San Lorenzo used a newly delivered Tadano lattice boom crawler crane to install a 247-tonne conveyor belt section at Peru’s Cerro Verde copper mine. Tadano trained the crew during a six-week setup, using an auxiliary crane and extensive transport. The conveyor build will be repeated to complete 900 meters over time.

title: EPA clears 'major milestone' for Lisbon Valley copper mine expansion
summary: The EPA approved an exemption lifting drinking-water protections for part of the Burro Canyon aquifer, enabling Lisbon Valley Mining’s in-situ recovery expansion at its Utah copper mine. Together with prior BLM approval, the decision supports additional domestic copper supply, though operations still require further filings and monitoring.

title: US copper smelting equation: gap or glut? | Hotter Commodities
summary: The piece argues the US is pushing to build or restart primary copper smelters despite weak global smelting margins. Grupo México’s Hayden restart, Falcon’s new smelter, and expansions at Kennecott and Miami are cited. Policy is supportive: copper is a critical mineral and an EPA rule rollback adds permitting flexibility.

title: Tech Titans Ignite Futures: Apple and Amazon Rallies Signal Shifting Sands for Commodities and Market Mood
summary: U.S. stock futures rose on strong earnings from Apple and Amazon, with AWS growth driven by AI. The piece argues AI infrastructure build-outs imply higher copper demand for wiring, cooling, and power transmission, alongside generally optimistic capex sentiment. It expects crude oil weakness but highlights copper as a potential beneficiary.

title: Cameroon's Aluminum Output Falls 40.8% in Q1 After Electrolysis Failure at State Producer Alucam
summary: Cameroon’s aluminum output fell 40.8% in Q1 2025 after a technical failure forced Alucam to shut down over half of its electrolysis cells. The shutdown reduced ingot and slab production similarly and worsened cash flow and losses, while management seeks a new investor to stabilize output.

title: Mexico's Tariff Barriers Escalate, Resilience and Challenges Coexist in China's Aluminum Semis and Aluminum Products Exports to Mexico [SMM Analysis]
summary: Mexico’s Senate approved the 2026 budget plan that escalates tariffs on thousands of Chinese goods, including aluminum products and aluminum semis (rates up to 50%) and links the policy to USMCA rules of origin. Combined with existing anti-dumping probes, higher costs should reduce import volumes and weigh on aluminum demand.

title: Domestic Aluminum Rod Market Trapped in Oversupply Dilemma, Processing Fees Expected to Linger at Low Levels in Short Term and Expectations for Production Cuts Intensify[SMM analysis]
summary: SMM reports oversupply in China’s aluminum rod market: inventories at plants rose to 7.6 days and in-factory inventory ratio increased, while processing fees stayed low due to loose supply and weak end-use demand. SHFE aluminum prices hit a yearly high but demand remains subdued, prompting expectations of further production cuts.

title: Iran's rise as global copper powerhouse
summary: Iran is positioning itself as a larger global copper supplier, citing large copper reserves and multiple ongoing projects at mines such as Sarcheshmeh, Miduk, and Sungun, plus plans to expand cathode and downstream refining capacity. The push to increase exports and processing capacity supports improving expectations for supply competitiveness.

title: Weaker Raw Material Prices to Drive Further Decline in Alumina Production Costs in November
summary: SMM reports alumina production costs are set to fall further in November as bauxite costs weaken and caustic soda contract prices decline across regions. Weighted average full alumina cost should drop slightly to 2,900–3,000 yuan/ton, with cash cost at 2,710–2,810 yuan/ton. Alumina margin pressure eases.

title: Japan to dig into Pakistan's Reko Diq mine amid copper deficit fears
summary: Japan Bank for International Cooperation and other Japanese entities are preparing to finance Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper mine. The move reflects Japan’s interest in securing critical minerals as expectations grow for a future copper supply shortage. Additional project support can improve near-term copper market sentiment.

title: Copper Prices on Track to Climb Further in 2026, Backed by Growing Optimism and Robust Fundamentals:【Takeaway from SMM Copper Conference】
summary: SMM’s copper conference takeaway argues copper prices have support from weakening USD expectations and Fed easing, while fundamentals remain tight: record-low China spot treatment charges, multiple mine disruptions lowering 2025 concentrate supply, and very low LME inventories. Tariff uncertainty and resource reallocation toward the US are expected to keep prices firm into 2026.

title: Aluminium industry urges govt to slap 15 pc customs duty to check surge in imports
summary: India’s Aluminium Association urged the government to impose a flat 15% customs duty on aluminium products to counter a more than 50% rise in imports from surplus countries. It argues the measure would prevent dumping of poor-quality scrap, protect domestic manufacturing, and encourage investment, potentially supporting aluminium prices.

title: Anglo Asian Mining agrees sales deal for Demirli copper
summary: Anglo Asian Mining says it has secured licenses to operate the Demirli copper mine’s processing plant and tailings dam and has agreed a copper-concentrate sales deal with Trafigura, backed by a revolving prepayment facility up to $25 million. The company expects its first concentrate sale in mid-November.

title: Costs Down and Prices Up, Aluminum Industry's Average Profit Broke Through 5,000 Yuan/mt in October
summary: SMM data show China’s aluminium industry costs fell in October as alumina prices declined, lifting average tax-inclusive profits to about 5,022 yuan/mt. Operating capacity was fully profitable. Alumina surplus and open import windows support lower costs, though anodes and fluoride salts diverge. November costs are forecast slightly lower.

title: Improved Supply-Demand Mismatch in Blister Copper in China, Q4 Market Structure Expected to Ease [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports blister copper treatment charges in China rose in October and are expected to keep rising in November as the market shifts from tight to loose. Higher copper prices boosted sellers of recycled feedstock and supported smelter processing demand patterns, especially with primary smelter maintenance affecting blister versus anode plate output.

title: Glencore plans to shut Canada's largest copper metal operation over costs
summary: Glencore plans to close Canada’s Horne smelter, citing high costs for environmental upgrades, with no closure date yet. Horne is Canada’s largest copper smelter and is estimated to produce over 300,000 tonnes annually. The shutdown would intensify expectations of refined copper shortages amid existing supply disruptions.

title: Glencore considers closing Canada's largest copper smelter
summary: Reuters reports Glencore is considering closing its Horne copper smelter in Quebec, citing environmental issues and more than $200m needed for upgrades. Industry sources estimate output over 300,000 tonnes. The potential reduction in refined supply could deepen shortages, supporting copper prices amid existing mine disruptions.

title: Guardian Metal Unearths High-Grade Gold, Silver, and Copper at Garfield Project, Sparking Market Excitement
summary: Guardian Metal Resources reported high-grade polymetallic mineralization at its Garfield Nevada project, including rock chip copper assays (e.g., 14% copper) alongside gold and silver. Shares rose sharply on the news. However, as an exploration update at a junior scale, it is more likely to affect copper sentiment than global prices.

title: Alcoa (AA) Soars as Aluminum Prices Hit 17-Month High Amidst Green Energy Boom
summary: Alcoa’s shares rise as LME aluminium hits a 17-month high near $2,900/t. The move is attributed to tighter global supply from China’s production/environmental caps, outages, lower inventories, and a surge in green-energy-linked demand (EVs, solar, grids), supporting further bullish near-term aluminium pricing despite higher downstream costs.

title: Guinean Bauxite Exports to Remain Strong in 2026
summary: Guinea’s bauxite exports rose to 48.6 million tons in Q1 2025 (+39% y/y) as Chinese aluminum production recovered and port capacity expanded from five to nine export-ready facilities. Government shipping mandates and refinery-related initiatives support continued growth, implying stronger bauxite availability for aluminum markets in 2026.

title: Energy Capital & Power  / Press release | Guinean Bauxite Exports to Remain Strong in 2026
summary: Guinea exported 48.6 million tons of bauxite in Q1 2025, up 39% year-on-year, driven by stronger Chinese demand and expanded port infrastructure. The article connects the boom to rising Chinese aluminium output and expects continued growth in 2026 supported by logistics upgrades and government policy on value-chain management.

title: Aluminium Industry Seeks 15% Import Duty to Curb Rising Imports
summary: India’s Aluminium Association of India has asked for a flat 15% basic customs duty on imported aluminium products to counter a 50%+ rise in imports over five years and concerns about poor-quality scrap inflows. The proposal aims to protect domestic smelting, attract investment, and reduce dumping pressures, which could be price-supportive.

title: True North boosts QLD copper strike to more than 500m
summary: True North Copper extended the Aquila copper-silver-cobalt discovery at its Mt Oxide project, reporting thick, higher-grade drill intersections and more than 500 metres of strike along the Aquila trend. Management says results strengthen continuity and growth potential for the copper system, with further assays pending.

title: Material Matters: Energy Demand, Copper, Aluminium & Gold
summary: The piece argues US energy demand growth and electrification/AI data centres underpin a copper “super-cycle,” citing recent mine disruptions, declining grades, and expectations of falling inventories and tighter supply. It also links strategic policy support—grants, reshoring, and high import tariffs—to improving aluminium fundamentals, implying higher prices ahead.

title: Material Matters: Energy Demand, Copper, Aluminium & Gold
summary: The piece links US energy-demand growth and electrification/AI data-centre and EV buildouts to higher copper demand, while citing recent mine disruptions and rising expectations of falling inventories and tighter supply. For aluminium, it highlights critical-minerals policy, tariffs and government funding for new smelting, suggesting firmer deficits and higher prices.

title: From Utah to China, where in the world could Arizona copper sitting under an Apache holy site go?
summary: KJZZ reports on Resolution Copper’s stalled Oak Flat project and disputes over whether its future copper will be refined abroad, potentially in China, amid political concerns and tariff threats. It also cites broader U.S.-China trade actions affecting commodity risk sentiment, but no immediate production or policy change is confirmed.

title: Mining Right Granted and Executed for Zeb Nickel | Company Announcement
summary: URU Metals announced South Africa granted and executed a 30-year mining right for its Zeb Nickel Project (Bushveld Complex, Limpopo). The company is completing registration formalities and will start ground EM and gravity surveys to refine drill targets. The update reduces project risk but does not indicate imminent nickel output.

title: Star Copper Corp.: Star Copper Kicks Off Inaugural Drilling at Star North Target
summary: Star Copper Corp. began drilling the first hole at its Star North copper target, designed to test geophysical anomalies beneath Cu-in-soil trends. The company highlights prior 2025 rock sampling with chalcopyrite-bearing units and elevated copper grades. The update is exploratory and is not linked to immediate supply changes.

title: Pacific Nickel Mines to sell Kolosori nickel project to Green Rock
summary: Pacific Nickel Mines says it will sell its Kolosori nickel project to Green Rock. Such transactions can influence expectations for future nickel supply and development progress. However, the available article text provides no information on output, ramp-up timing, or operational changes, so near-term price impact is uncertain.

title: Report links nickel mining in Dinagat, Surigao Sur to environmental damage, rights abuses
summary: A report by Climate Rights International links nickel mining in Dinagat Islands and Surigao del Sur to water pollution, deforestation, mangrove loss, livelihood destruction, and alleged rights abuses. It urges the Philippine government to halt new nickel permits until standards are met, increasing near-term nickel supply and regulatory risk.

title: Stuhini Exploration Unearths High-Grade Copper-Gold Porphyry at Ruby Creek, Igniting Multi-Metal Potential
summary: Stuhini Exploration announced a new “Ruffner” copper-gold porphyry target at its Ruby Creek project in British Columbia. Grab samples reportedly include assays up to 8.1% Cu and 36.8 g/t Au, with geophysical data suggesting a sizable system. The news boosts copper sentiment but does not alter near-term supply.

title: Poor towns near nickel mines pay the price of energy transition – report
summary: A report by Climate Rights International describes environmental and social impacts in Philippine towns hosting nickel mines, and calls on the government to halt new permits and suspend operations that violate regulations. With the Philippines a major nickel producer, the allegations could increase near-term supply risk and regulatory uncertainty.

title: EU Merger Watchdog Deepens Investigation into $500 Million MMG, Anglo American Nickel Deal
summary: The European Commission deepened its investigation into MMG’s $500 million purchase of Anglo American’s Brazilian nickel business, citing competition concerns. It fears the deal could divert ferronickel supplies from Europe, tightening availability for European stainless steel demand. A March 20 deadline follows earlier concession offers deemed insufficient.

title: EU Merger Watchdog Deepens Investigation into $500 Million MMG, Anglo American Nickel Deal -- Update
summary: The European Commission will deepen its review of MMG’s $500 million purchase of Anglo American’s Brazilian nickel business. Regulators have competition concerns that the deal could divert ferronickel supplies from Europe, raising prices and affecting stainless-steel quality. A March 20 deadline was set; concessions were deemed insufficient.

title: Chile's Codelco cuts copper output guidance for 2025 despite higher production through September
summary: Chile’s Codelco cut its 2025 copper output forecast to 1.31–1.34 million tonnes from 1.34–1.37 million, despite higher production through September. The update follows an El Teniente accident that temporarily halted mining and smelting. The guidance cut may reinforce near-term concerns about copper supply.

title: MMG's Anglo American deal may divert nickel from Europe, EU warns
summary: The EU Commission opened an in-depth antitrust probe into MMG’s planned purchase of Anglo American’s Brazilian nickel business. Regulators warned MMG could divert ferronickel supply from Europe, hurting stainless steel production and affecting price and quality due to limited alternative sources. A decision is expected by March 20.

title: Rio Tinto aluminium smelter Bell Bay gets 12-month reprieve from Tasmanian government
summary: Tasmania granted a 12-14 month reprieve for Rio Tinto’s Bell Bay aluminium smelter by temporarily extending its power supply contract, originally set to expire Dec 31. The extension gives time to negotiate a federal rescue package and avoids a near-term supply cut risk.

title: Comex Copper Settles 2.40% Lower at $4.9260 — Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures settled 2.40% lower at $4.9260, signaling a clear decline in the near-term copper price. The item appears to be a “data talk” recap focused on the latest settlement move, implying bearish momentum for copper markets going into the next sessions.
