title: Anglo Asian (LON:AAZ) Signs $25 Million Trafigura Deal as Demirli Copper Mine Enters Full Operation
summary: Anglo Asian Mining signed a $25 million Trafigura prepayment-backed sales agreement for copper concentrates from its Demirli mine in Azerbaijan, which is now fully operational after commissioning and permits. First shipments are due mid-November, with production expected to reach ~4,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate in year one and rise later.

title: Australian Gold and Copper Forges Dominant Foothold in South Cobar Basin with Strategic Acquisitions
summary: Australian Gold and Copper (AGC) expanded its South Cobar Basin landholdings through acquisitions of EL9012 and the Browns Reef Project, including copper-bearing polymetallic targets and increased planned drilling. While this can support copper/bullish exploration sentiment, there is no immediate production, inventory, or logistics change, limiting short-term price impact.

title: Bell Bay Aluminium and Hydro Tasmania 'buy time' with short-term power deal
summary: Tasmanian authorities announced Hydro Tasmania has agreed, in principle, a one-year power deal with Rio Tinto’s Bell Bay Aluminium as its previous electricity arrangement was due to expire. The extension prevents potential care-and-administration, supporting continued aluminium smelter output while negotiations and federal green-aluminium credit eligibility are finalized.

title: Copper thefts surge in Jackson County as prosecutors crack down on crime wave
summary: Copper thefts in Jackson County have surged, with prosecutors charging cases at a much higher rate than the national average. Businesses report significant losses from stolen copper wiring and damage. The crackdown may reduce theft, but the surge itself highlights tightness and elevated local demand for copper wire.

title: South Africa grants mining right for Uru Metals' Zeb nickel project
summary: South Africa granted Uru Metals a mining right for its Zeb nickel project. The development may improve the project’s path toward production and raise expectations of additional future nickel supply. Because it is not an immediate start of output, any near-term impact on nickel prices is likely modest.

title: GeologicAI and Edge Copper partner to boost Zonia copper project in Arizona
summary: GeologicAI partnered with Edge Copper to advance the Zonia copper project in Arizona, including drill-hole optimization, remote core logging, and geometallurgical modelling to support a feasibility study. Edge Copper targets shovel-ready status in 3–4 years. The news is positive for future development but unlikely to move near-term copper prices materially.

title: EU initiates Phase II investigation into MMG-Anglo nickel deal
summary: The EU launched a Phase II merger investigation into MMG’s planned $500m purchase of Anglo American’s Brazilian nickel business, citing risks to continued, reliable ferro-nickel access for Europe’s stainless steel industry. Regulators could require remedies or block the deal by a March deadline, adding near-term supply uncertainty.

title: Mercuria, ERG close US$100mn pre-payment facility for copper supply
summary: Eurasian Resources Group agreed a US$100mn prepayment facility with Mercuria to support copper supply from ERG’s DRC mines under a three-year agreement. The funding strengthens ERG’s financing and commercial portfolio, signaling confidence in ongoing copper offtake and near-term availability for global buyers.

title: Hayasa Metals Inc.: Hayasa Metals Completes Vardenis Copper-Gold Project 2025 Drilling Campaign
summary: Hayasa Metals reports completion of a 2025 drilling campaign at the Vardenis copper-gold project in Armenia under Teck’s option/joint venture. Ten diamond holes intersected significant quartz-sulfide veining and potassic/sericite alteration. The company will receive assay results later, with no near-term production or supplies change disclosed.

title: Nine Mile Metals Ltd.: Nine Mile Metals Announces Phase 3 XRF High-Grade Results up to 26.14% Copper with 1.03% Antimony from the Upper Pre Drill Area at the Wedge Copper
summary: Nine Mile Metals reported Phase 3 XRF results from the Wedge Copper Gold Critical Minerals Project, with select samples returning up to 26.14% copper and 1.03% antimony, including visible covellite. Samples were shipped for certified assays. This is exploration news with limited immediate effect on copper pricing and no aluminium linkage.

title: Trafigura floods LME Malaysia warehouses with aluminium, sources say
summary: Trafigura delivered large quantities of LME-approved aluminium into warehouses in Port Klang, Malaysia, increasing registered stocks by nearly 100,000 tonnes to 366,850. Most was placed on LME warrants as part of rent/incentive arrangements, where rent is higher than non-warrant storage, increasing near-term supply signals.

title: 1844 Resources Inc.: 1844 Resources Launches Strategic Financing to Advance Vortex/Sullipek Copper Project Adjacent to Osisko's Gaspe Copper Mine Project
summary: 1844 Resources announced a $500,000 non-brokered private placement to fund advancement of its Vortex/Sullipek copper project in Quebec, adjacent to Osisko Metals’ Gaspe copper mine. The company cites permits secured and plans a targeted drill program, pending regulatory approvals and closing.

title: Pershing Resources : Sets Plans For Exploration Programs on its Mohave Gold Property and its New Enterprise Copper/Gold Project in Northern Arizona
summary: Pershing Resources reports it has paid U.S. BLM maintenance fees and designed a three-phase $2.3M exploration program for its New Enterprise copper/gold project near two producing copper mines. The company plans field work, geophysics and drill testing, but provides no production or volume changes, limiting any short-term copper impact.

title: FM spokesperson urges European Commission to honor openness pledge amid probe into nickel business acquisition by China-backed MMG
summary: A spokesperson urges the European Commission to honor an openness pledge amid an investigation into a nickel business acquisition by a China-backed MMG. Separately, the piece notes improving China–EU trade and talks nearing a solution on eliminating tariffs for Chinese EV imports. Details of any nickel outcome are not provided.

title: Base Metals Explained: Nickel vs Lithium Iron Phosphate
summary: Vale executives and Fastmarkets sources say nickel’s battery demand has slowed, with LFP now about 50% cheaper and potentially taking share from NCM cathodes. Nickel supply is abundant, but demand growth has not followed. Copper is described as having solid demand, though the article’s key near-term risk centers on nickel.

title: Resolution Copper Completes Deepening and Rehabilitation of Historic No. 9 Shaft
summary: Resolution Copper announced completion of a $200 million rehabilitation and deepening of its historic No. 9 Shaft in Arizona, extending it to nearly 6,900 feet and connecting it to No. 10 for ventilation and access. The milestone supports continued underground development plans for future copper production, despite ongoing litigation.

title: Lundin Mining Corporation: Lundin Mining Reports Third Quarter 2025 Results and Increases Full-Year Copper Production Guidance and Lowers Cost Guidance
summary: Lundin Mining reported Q3 2025 results and increased/tightened full-year copper production guidance to 319,000–337,000 tonnes while lowering consolidated copper cash cost guidance to $1.85–$2.00/lb. The update reflects stronger performance at Caserones and Chapada, supporting near-term copper market expectations.

title: Kenadyr Metals Corp.: Kenadyr Provides Operational Update on the Adelita Copper-Gold-Silver Project and Status Update of Reactivation Transaction
summary: Kenadyr/Algo Grande provides an operational update on the Adelita Cu-Au-Ag project, noting full permits and planned November exploration, alongside progress toward TSXV approval and financing tranches to reactivate the transaction. The release is development-focused and does not affect near-term copper supply or demand directly.

title: What is the future of aluminium in Australia?
summary: Tasmanian officials announced Hydro Tasmania reached an in-principal one-year power agreement with Bell Bay Aluminium. The previous 10-year power contract expires December 31 after weeks of industry uncertainty. The update improves short-term outlook for aluminium smelter electricity costs and operational stability in Australia.

title: Copper thefts on the rise in Portland, resulting in millions in losses and damages
summary: Portland police report a surge in copper thefts, with more than $2 million in losses and damages over six months. Suspects cut phone/communication lines and sell the copper cables, sometimes by burning insulation. Thefts occur frequently since September and raise safety and environmental hazards, but the impact appears local.

title: The demand for copper is huge
summary: Copper rallied above $11,200/t as supply tightened sharply after a mudslide forced Freeport-McMoRan to stop mining for about a month at Grasberg. The piece notes very low LME warehouse stocks and tariff-related US buying/arbitrage, alongside ongoing electrification and EV demand, supporting bullish expectations near term.

title: Santa Cruz Copper Project, USA
summary: Ivanhoe Electric’s Santa Cruz copper project in Arizona advanced through a published PFS, projecting 1.4 million tonnes of copper cathode over 23 years and targeting construction in 2026 and first production in 2028. The article also cites EXIM Bank debt financing interest, supporting longer-term copper supply expectations rather than immediate market moves.

title: Prospect Resources Sells Zimbabwe Lithium Stake to Focus on Zambian Copper
summary: Prospect Resources agreed to sell its 90% stake in Zimbabwe’s Step Aside Lithium project and use proceeds to fund drilling at its Zambia copper asset, Mumbezhi. The article also notes bullish copper fundamentals, citing projected global deficits amid mine disruptions in DRC and Indonesia and rising LME copper prices.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Another Restrictions on Nickel Supply? Indonesian Nickel Market Uncertainty Continues
summary: Indonesia’s PP 28/2025 adds OSS-based administrative moratoriums and declaration requirements limiting new nickel smelter projects producing NPI, FeNi, Nickel Matte and MHP. Firms face ambiguity over retroactive application, creating regulatory uncertainty and potential project delays, likely tightening Indonesian nickel supply and supporting prices.

title: Adani subsidiary Kutch Copper joins Caravel Minerals to fast-track key Australian copper project
summary: Caravel Minerals and Kutch Copper (Adani subsidiary) signed a non-binding MoU to collaborate on the Caravel Copper Project in Western Australia, including engineering, joint procurement, and concentrate offtake feeding Kutch Copper’s $1.2 billion smelter in Gujarat. It targets an FID in 2026 and aims to accelerate development.

title: Adani unit signs deal with Australia's Caravel Minerals copper project
summary: Adani Enterprises said its Kutch Copper Ltd signed a non-binding deal with Australia’s Caravel Minerals to accelerate a copper project in Western Australia, with initial capex of A$1.7 billion and options for equity participation. It also highlights Kutch Copper’s capacity and an LME listing application. The announcement is not an immediate production change.

title: Adani subsidiary Kutch Copper joins Caravel Minerals to fast-track key Australian copper project
summary: Caravel Minerals and Adani’s Kutch Copper signed a landmark (non-binding) MoU to fast-track Australia’s Caravel Copper Project, targeting an FID in 2026. The deal explores investment and offtake, including up to 100% of concentrate output feeding Kutch Copper’s Gujarat smelter, via joint engineering and procurement.

title: Caraga face environmental damage from nickel mining
summary: The report describes environmental degradation and human-rights abuses linked to ongoing nickel mining in Caraga, Dinagat Islands and Surigao del Sur. It notes nickel ore largely goes to China and cites changes in export destinations tied to nickel shortages. Despite risks from typhoons and pollution, no immediate supply stoppage is reported.

title: Venerable Ventures Ltd.: Selkirk Copper Announces Award of Trade-Off Study and Engineering Work Packages
summary: Selkirk Copper announces Hatch and SRK consulting engineering work packages to advance trade-off studies for a potential restart of the former Minto copper-gold-silver mine, targeting an early-2027 decision. The release is focused on planning and environmental/water/tailings design, not near-term output changes.

title: Vedanta Resources Limited: Vedanta Resources Launches CopperTech Metals to Bolster U.S. Copper Security and Advance Technology and Infrastructure Transformation
summary: Vedanta launched CopperTech Metals, which will own and operate Zambia’s Konkola Copper Mines. The company plans an additional $1.5 billion investment to expand production capacity, leveraging existing smelting and concentrator infrastructure. It targets increased copper cathode output to support U.S. supply security amid strong demand from data centers and grid modernization.

title: NorthWest Intersects 27.7 Metres of 1.23% Copper and
summary: NorthWest Copper reports assay results from drill hole K-25-271 at its Kwanika project in British Columbia, including a 27.7m intercept at 1.23% copper and additional higher-grade copper-gold zones (up to 2.63% CuEq). The findings strengthen confidence in expansion potential, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Interior Department adds coal and copper to critical mineral list in bid to boost production
summary: The Interior Department updated the USGS 2025 critical minerals list to add copper (and metallurgical coal), making these materials eligible for funding and faster permitting. The administration says the change strengthens domestic supply chains for national security and could feed into future policy tools like incentives or tariffs.

title: CBA CEO signals Brazilian aluminium export shift
summary: Brazil’s CBA CEO says US 50% aluminium tariffs have not hurt volumes, but demand in Europe is rising with CBAM-related stockpiling ahead of December. US Midwest primary aluminium premiums hit a record on inventory depletion. CBA plans to restart idle capacity and shift product mix toward ingots, supporting near-term aluminium tightness.

title: American Pacific Mining Corp.: Copper Added to New USGS Critical Minerals List Highlighting Increased Support for US Copper Projects Like American Pacific's Madison & Palmer Projects
summary: American Pacific Mining highlights that copper was added to the USGS 2025 critical minerals list as the Trump Administration expands critical mineral priorities. The company says this is expected to boost government funding and streamline permitting for US copper projects, providing “tailwinds” for its Madison and Palmer copper assets.

title: U.S. adds silver and copper to 'critical minerals' list
summary: The U.S. Department of the Interior added copper to its critical minerals list, raising the chance copper could be covered in upcoming Section 232 tariff reviews and domestic support programs. While this can be supportive for sentiment around copper supply chains, the article provides no immediate production or inventory impact.

title: Carmaker Stellantis pulls plug on supply deal with Australia's Alliance Nickel
summary: Stellantis will end its battery-grade nickel and cobalt supply deal with Alliance Nickel’s NiWest project from Dec 3 after missed milestones. Alliance attributes delays to difficult global nickel market conditions and financing constraints as prices have stayed under pressure. The termination supports renegotiation, but implies limited immediate market-wide nickel shock.

title: Caraga faces environmental damage from nickel mining
summary: A report says nickel mining in the Caraga region (Dinagat Islands and Surigao del Sur) has caused severe environmental degradation and community impacts, while describing nickel ore shipments largely going to China. It does not mention immediate mine closures or policy actions, so near-term nickel price effects are uncertain.

title: Enamelled Wire: High Copper Prices Constrain Demand, Operating Rates Struggle to Match Year-Ago Levels
summary: SMM reports enamelled wire industry operating rates fell in October, citing weak end-use demand and holidays. After holidays, copper prices rose more than expected, reducing end-user acceptance of finished-product price increases and delaying orders. Inventory remains high despite destocking. November is expected to rebound, but high copper prices keep demand suppressed.

title: Aluminum hits two-week low, penalized by declining equity markets
summary: Aluminum on the LME fell to a two-week low, settling near $2,843/mt, dragged by declining US technology-linked equities and broader risk-off macro concerns including a potential US government shutdown. Fundamentals in China remain solid with tighter supply and rising European premiums, but short-term sentiment is bearish.

title: Tasmania seeks federal help for green aluminium | The Examiner
summary: Tasmania is seeking federal help to ensure Bell Bay Aluminium can access Australia’s $2bn Green Aluminium Production Credit, aimed at supporting smelters’ shift to renewable energy. Federal officials say the scheme is still being designed with major owners, but keep working toward a fair outcome, supporting aluminium production economics.

title: Adani's Kutch Copper inks MoU with Caravel Minerals for Australia project
summary: Adani’s Kutch Copper and Australia’s Caravel Minerals signed a non-binding MoU to collaborate on the Caravel Copper Project in Western Australia, with potential up to 100% offtake of copper concentrate to Adani’s Gujarat smelter. The deal supports development toward a 2026 FID, lifting copper sentiment despite being preliminary.

title: US expands critical minerals list to include copper and metallurgical coal
summary: The US expanded its critical minerals list to include copper, enabling more federal incentives, permitting and stockpiling decisions tied to domestic supply resilience. Reuters notes it could unlock tax credits for producers such as Freeport. The move signals strategic backing that may support near-term copper price expectations.

title: Overview of Q3 Copper Production of the Top 20 Global Mining Companies in 2025 [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM data shows Q3 2025 output from the top 20 copper miners fell 4.1% QoQ and 6.5% YoY to 3,455 kt, driven by production disruptions. Notably, PT FI suspended mining after a mudslide and Codelco reduced output after a rock burst, with smelters awaiting concentrate, implying bearish near-term copper supply.

title: Southern Copper : Company Presentation - 3Q25, Production and Capex Guidance - 3Q25
summary: Southern Copper’s 3Q25 company presentation highlights copper fundamentals, citing an expected ~100k tonne 2025 market deficit and low inventory levels (about six days). It argues demand support from China, resilient US growth, and energy-transition/AI themes, while supply faces development challenges, implying bullish copper sentiment.

title: Brazilian green aluminium to command premium, says Hydro CEO
summary: Norsk Hydro CEO says markets will not accept aluminium from producers without renewable energy and that low-carbon aluminium can command premiums. Hydro highlights decarbonization steps at Alunorte (natural gas, electric boilers, solar) and notes Brazil’s policy discussions are still early. The piece also references stable or ongoing low-carbon aluminium differentials.

title: Copper's Green Revolution: Electrification Fuels Unprecedented Demand and Market Volatility
summary: The article says electrification and renewables are boosting copper demand sharply (EVs, solar/wind, smart grids, data centers), while supply development is slow. It highlights tight refined markets, inventory/logistics stress, and volatility, with copper reaching record highs and analysts forecasting further upside.

title: Trump Expands Critical Minerals List to Copper, Met Coal, Uranium
summary: Trump’s administration expanded the U.S. critical minerals list to include copper, alongside metallurgical coal and other minerals. The list guides federal incentives and permitting and is intended to boost domestic production and reduce import reliance, potentially supporting near-term sentiment for copper supply and investment.

title: Copper-gold ratio is bent but not broken: Taosha Wang
summary: The piece explains the copper-gold ratio’s decline as a distortion from U.S. trade policy but stresses copper demand strength from electrification (EVs, renewables, grid upgrades, data centers) and some supply fragility. It notes disruptive tariff effects but ultimately highlights supportive fundamentals for copper.

title: Copper prices: Investments in copper
summary: BNN Bloomberg reports Canadian copper outlook looks stronger, citing higher output since 2023, multiple mine expansions and ramp-ups, and a “historic” federal budget that improves critical-minerals tax incentives and funds infrastructure. Electrification/EV and renewable demand are highlighted as supportive, despite U.S. copper-import tariff concerns for refined products.

title: Aluminum's Unprecedented Ascent: Record Bull Bets Signal a New Era for Industrial Metals
summary: Investment funds have taken record net long positions in aluminium, coinciding with multi-year price highs above $2,900/t. The rally is attributed to China’s government capacity ceiling, tighter supply from environmental compliance constraints, firm demand from renewables and EVs, and reduced alumina/ingot inventories, implying continued upside momentum.

title: Hindalco to Build Rs.586 Cr Aluminium Plant in Chittoor for iPhone Chassis
summary: Hindalco plans to invest ₹586 crore in an aluminium extrusion plant in Kuppam (Chittoor) to supply high-grade aluminium used in iPhone chassis. The announcement cites supportive policy incentives and renewable energy advantages, implying added incremental aluminium demand, though timelines and volumes are not detailed.

title: Ma'aden Profit Jumps 91% on Phosphate, Aluminium Strength | The Middle East Observer
summary: Ma’aden reported a 91% jump in nine-month profit, attributing gains to higher volumes and stronger pricing in its phosphate and aluminium units. In aluminium, FRP sales rose ~15% and average realised aluminium prices improved ~11%. The company frames this as benefiting from a favourable aluminium pricing environment.

title: Copper prices fluctuated downward, and the supply-demand pattern in the secondary copper market underwent changes—awaiting direction amid policy observation.
summary: Copper prices fell sharply this week, with Guangdong bare bright copper down to 77,800–78,000 yuan/mt. The macro event “vacuum period” dampened sentiment, reducing secondary scrap suppliers’ shipments. Secondary copper rod operations rose slightly, but weekly profits fell and inventory dropped, suggesting bearish near-term pressure and a wait-and-see stance.

title: CopperTech Metals: Bridging America's Critical Mineral Needs with Zambia's Legacy
summary: Vedanta Resources launched CopperTech Metals Inc to run Zambia’s Konkola Copper Mines. The venture plans to boost annual copper production to about 300,000 tonnes by 2031 and invests $1.5 billion in AI-driven exploration and extraction. The focus is meeting US critical mineral needs, supporting copper supply expectations.

title: Vedanta to invest $1.5bn in Zambia's expanding copper sector
summary: Vedanta reorganized its Zambia operations and plans to invest an additional $1.5 billion at the Konkola copper mine to raise output toward 300,000 tons by 2031. The plan supports Zambia’s broader production targets, though near-term (2026) output guidance suggests limited immediate supply impact.

title: Salzgitter says it has no plans to exit copper producer Aurubis
summary: German steelmaker Salzgitter said it has no plans to exit its 29.99% stake in copper producer Aurubis, citing the asset’s contribution to EBITDA. The update follows an October plan to sell €500 million of exchangeable bonds that reduced takeover speculation. Overall, it’s more company-specific than a copper fundamentals move.

title: SA government unveils crackdown on costly, dangerous copper theft
summary: South Australia announced proposed legislation to curb copper theft, targeting scrap metal dealers with licensing, bans on cash transactions, and mandatory transaction records. The government cites rising construction-site damage and safety risks, estimating industry costs at about $70 million annually. The bill is set for introduction to parliament tomorrow.

title: High Copper Prices Weigh on Copper Plate
summary: SMM reports October 2025 operating rates for copper plate/sheet and strip enterprises fell to 64.97%, with seasonality weaker than usual. Rapid post–National Day copper price rises dampened downstream procurement and orders, lowered processing fees, and slowed inventory turnover, suggesting soft demand and limiting a near-term seasonal boost.

title: In Armenia, copper and molybdenum concentrate production decreased in three quarters, while zinc concentrate increased
summary: Armenia’s Statistical Committee data show copper concentrate production fell 13% to 202,155.3 tons in January–September 2025 versus the same period of 2024. Molybdenum and ferromolybdenum output also declined, while zinc concentrate increased. The copper reduction may tighten supply expectations.

title: Trade war: Aluminum premium hits record in U.S.
summary: The article says the U.S. aluminum premium hit a record high, attributing the jump to tariff-driven trade friction and a broader global squeeze in aluminum availability. The premium increase points to tight spot supply in the U.S., supporting expectations for firmer near-term aluminum pricing.

title: Southern Copper : 3Q25 Conference Call transcript
summary: Southern Copper’s Q3 call highlighted rising LME and COMEX copper prices and estimated a ~400,000-ton global copper deficit amid negative production effects in Indonesia and Chile. The company also reported lower copper output but stated byproduct strength and improved metal prices supported results, reinforcing near-term copper market tightness.

title: Aluminium premium hits record in US on tariffs, global squeeze
summary: The article says the US aluminium premium reached a record high, attributing the move to tariff-related pressure and a global supply squeeze. A rising premium typically reflects tighter US availability versus international benchmarks, creating near-term upward support for aluminium prices as buyers compete for limited supply.

title: Gold, Oil, and Base Metals Soar as US Shutdown Hopes and Soft Economic Data Fuel Broad Commodity Rally
summary: Markets rally as hopes for an end to a US shutdown and soft US data boost expectations for Fed easing and a weaker dollar. The article links this dovish shift to higher industrial-metals prices, highlighting copper and aluminium gains supported by energy-transition and infrastructure demand expectations.

title: US turns down India's request on WTO talks over copper tariff hike
summary: The US rejected India’s request for WTO consultations over a 50% US tariff on copper and copper derivative imports, arguing the duties are not WTO safeguards. The tariff, imposed under Section 232, has been in effect since Aug 1 and applies indefinitely, potentially dampening US copper import demand and price expectations.

title: Guinea's Alumina Ambition: A Pivotal Shift from Raw Export to Value-Added Processing
summary: Guinea is expanding alumina refining to capture more value from its bauxite, including a major SPIC plant and stricter local-processing enforcement that previously triggered a jump in alumina prices. While greater processed output could eventually affect aluminium sentiment, the article also cites a 2025–2027 global alumina oversupply, limiting near-term price clarity.

title: Guinea's Alumina Ambition: A New Dawn for West African Mining
summary: Guinea is pushing domestic alumina refining, suspending GAC bauxite exports in 2024 and revoking GAC’s mining license in August 2025 after missed refinery commitments. The disruption has reportedly lifted global aluminium prices. Construction of the SPIC-Boffa alumina refinery is underway, with more projects negotiated.

title: West Africa's Mineral Bonanza: Guinea Spearheads a New Era in Global Commodity Production
summary: The piece highlights Guinea’s dominance in bauxite and the government’s push to add value domestically via new alumina refineries. It cites concession revocation for non-compliance and export/shipping disruptions tied to refinery plans. These policies can alter bauxite and alumina supply near term, supporting aluminium price expectations.

title: Lara Exploration Ltd.: Minsur Terminates its Option to Acquire the Lara Copper Project in Peru
summary: Lara Exploration said Minsur notified it of an intention to relinquish its option to acquire Lara’s 45%-owned Lara Copper Project in southern Peru. The project hosts partly defined copper-molybdenum porphyry mineralization based on drilling results. The option termination reduces prospects for near-term development.

title: Materials Up With Gold, Copper -- Materials Roundup
summary: A Dow Jones materials roundup reports that producers of raw materials rose after the U.S. government reopened, boosting risk appetite and commodity prices. It specifically notes copper futures gaining about 3%, alongside strength in gold, with sector movers including Barrick’s Nevada review.

title: CEO.CA's Inside the Boardroom: Midnight Sun Confirms Copper at Dumbwa Target Within 20km Anomaly Zone, Fast-Tracks Drilling – IT Business Net
summary: CEO.CA interviews Midnight Sun Mining’s leadership, stating it has confirmed copper at the Dumbwa target within a defined anomaly zone and is fast-tracking drilling. While aimed at junior exploration rather than immediate production, the update can improve short-term sentiment around copper supply prospects.

title: International Business: Aluminium premium hits record in US on tariffs, global squeeze
summary: US physical aluminium premiums have hit record highs after Trump doubled aluminium import tariffs to 50% on June 4. Duty-paid Midwest premiums surged to 88.10 cents/lb amid tight global supplies, falling US stocks, and expectations of a sizable market deficit as non-China availability declines.

title: US Denies India WTO Consultations Over Copper Tariff Hike
summary: The US rejected India’s WTO request over its 50% tariffs on copper and copper derivative imports, imposed since Aug 1 under Section 232. The US argues the duties are not safeguard measures. India is an exporter of copper products to the US, raising potential demand and price pressure concerns.

title: U.S. Aluminum Prices Surge To Record Highs As Tariffs Squeeze Supply
summary: U.S. aluminum prices jumped to record highs as Trump’s steel and aluminum tariffs tightened supply. Imports from Canada fell after tariffs rose to 50%, while U.S. inventories shrank sharply. The Midwest premium and LME price extended gains, alongside higher aluminum futures open interest, signaling strong near-term upward pressure.

title: Barrick's Zambian Copper Output Jumps 41% by September 2025
summary: Barrick said its Lumwana copper mine in Zambia produced 109,000 tonnes in the first nine months of 2025, up 41% from a year earlier, helped by higher ore grades and better recovery. The company expects 125,000–155,000 tonnes in 2025 and is investing to expand capacity.

title: Although the pace of domestic primary aluminum billets production continued to increase in October, a retreat from highs is expected in November [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM expects domestic primary aluminum billet production to retreat from October highs in November as peak-season demand fades. Persistently high SHFE aluminium prices curb downstream purchasing, orders decline, and processing fees face pressure. Production is forecast to fall slightly and operating rates drop, with inventories still elevated.

title: China's Copper Foil Industry Operating Rate Continues to Climb, Full-Year Prosperity Expected [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says China’s copper foil enterprises’ operating rate rose to 84.22% in October and is forecast to climb to 84.49% in November. Lithium battery and electronic circuit segments show improved utilization and shipments, inventories decline, and end-use demand (NEVs, ESS, AI servers) remains strong.

title: [SMM Analysis] When Southeast Asia Shuts Its Doors:Can the Middle East Take Over the Role of Copper Scrap Processing Hub?
summary: The article argues that tightened waste-metal import rules in Southeast Asia have stranded low-grade copper scrap, pushing traders to seek new processing/transit hubs. The Middle East—especially UAE and Oman—offers open regulations, low energy costs, and port infrastructure, potentially tightening copper scrap availability and supporting copper prices near term.

title: Mining Titans Unite: Teck and Anglo American Forge Copper Colossus in $70 Billion Merger
summary: Teck Resources and Anglo American plan a $70bn “merger of equals” to form Anglo Teck, targeting a copper-centric portfolio (over 70% exposure) and synergies from Chile’s Quebrada Blanca and Collahuasi mines. The deal highlights strong copper demand drivers and expected output growth, supporting bullish near-term copper sentiment.

title: Latin American Assets Soar to Multi-Year Highs on Commodity Boom
summary: Latin American equities and currencies are rising as global commodity prices climb, with the piece explicitly citing strong copper prices as a key driver—especially for Chile. It frames this as continued demand tied to electrification/energy transition and links copper-producer performance to improved expectations.

title: Copper's Historic 2025 Rally: A Global Economy in the Red Metal's Grip
summary: The article reports copper reaching record prices (~$11,200/t) on supply tightness from mining disruptions and a strong demand surge linked to the green transition and AI/digital infrastructure, reinforced by tariff-driven inventory shifts. It highlights profit gains for copper miners and cost pressure for consumers, with some substitution toward aluminium possible.

title: Copper's Unstoppable Ascent: ASX Miners Poised for Green Energy Boom
summary: Copper prices are described as surging to multi-year highs on demand acceleration from EVs, wind/solar grids, and AI data centers, while supply is constrained by mine disruptions (including Cobre Panamá closure and Grasberg mudslide), declining ore grades, slow project ramp-ups, and low inventories. The piece expects continued bullish price momentum.

title: SMM Aluminium P1020A (MJP) Quarterly/Spot Premium, CIF Japan Price Release【SMM Announcement】
summary: SMM announced the Aluminium P1020A (MJP) quarterly and spot premiums for CIF Japan ($/tonne), describing them as key benchmark prices used for settlement across Asia. The release also notes Japan’s reliance on aluminium imports and major end-use sectors like autos and construction, but provides no explicit market shock details.

title: Aluminium Bahrain Q3 profit up 23% to $179m
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) reported Q3 2025 profit up 23% YoY to about $179m, with gross profit and sales revenue rising, despite softer demand. The piece also notes LME aluminium prices averaging $2,617/t (+10% YoY) and falling inventories, suggesting improving near-term aluminium sentiment despite ongoing trade-tariff headwinds.

title: Aluminum Rod Production Cut Wave Hits: Nearly 800,000 mt of Capacity Undergoes Concentrated Maintenance Shutdowns in November! 【SMM Analysis】
summary: SMM says China’s aluminum rod operating capacity fell as maintenance shut capacity of about 792,000 mt in November, near 10% of sampled production. Cuts were driven by inventory buildup and funding pressure, while downstream wire/cable demand and power-grid ordering stayed weak and processing fees deteriorated.

title: Guinea to fast-track alumina, iron ore processing, mines minister says
summary: Guinea’s mines minister says the country will fast-track alumina refinery and iron-ore processing to end raw ore exports. Guinea ships much of its bauxite to China for aluminium; new alumina projects aim to shift exports from bauxite to alumina. Current timing suggests limited immediate disruption to aluminium supply.

title: EMX Royalty Corp.: EMX Acquires a Royalty on a Development-Stage Copper Asset in Chile
summary: EMX Royalty Corp. acquired a 1.25% NSR royalty over the Puquios development-stage copper project in Chile and subscribed to concurrent financing to advance it toward construction and a final investment decision. The project has permits, reserves (~0.494% Cu), and forecasts of substantial copper production over 14 years.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Prepares for Phase 1 Drill Program at the Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. said it is preparing a ~3,600-meter Phase 1 diamond drill program at its Kenbridge nickel-copper-cobalt project in Ontario. The work targets extensions of high-grade Ni-Cu mineralization and upgrading inferred resources toward measured/indicated categories to support a potential PFS.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Prepares for Phase 1 Drill Program at the Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. announced it is preparing a ~3,600-meter Phase 1 diamond drill program at its Kenbridge nickel-copper-cobalt project in Ontario. The drilling aims to convert inferred resources to Measured/Indicated categories and test down-plunge extensions of high-grade Ni-Cu mineralization, supporting potential future PFS work. No production impacts are stated.

title: Lands Minister inaugurates Investor Selection Committee for VALCO modernisation and alumina refinery development
summary: Ghana’s minister inaugurated an investor selection committee for GIADEC to choose partners for VALCO modernisation and Ghana’s first alumina refinery. Officials say the refinery will supply the smelter and strengthen the aluminium value chain, reducing dependence on imported alumina and supporting future output and competitiveness.

title: Trump's Tariffs Send U.S. Aluminum Prices to Record Highs
summary: U.S. aluminum prices hit record highs as tariffs tighten domestic supplies: inventories are shrinking and Canadian shipments fall after the U.S. imposed and then doubled aluminum tariffs. The Midwest premium rose, LME prices extended gains, and aluminum futures open interest surged amid constrained supply and stronger demand expectations.

title: Lawmakers spike $50 million request for copper mine
summary: Michigan lawmakers sought a $50 million earmark to prepare infrastructure in Wakefield Township to attract Highland Copper’s proposed Copperwood copper mine. The request was not approved in the final 2026 budget. Critics called taxpayer subsidies inefficient, arguing roads, grids, and telecom upgrades could help investment and future copper production.

title: Nickel Asia Q3 profit jumps to P3.09B on higher ore prices, exports
summary: Nickel Asia reported a sharp Q3 profit increase driven by higher nickel ore prices and strong exports. The company cites elevated nickel ore pricing due to tight supply, expecting persistence as Indonesia enforces stricter production-permit policies. Export volumes and prices also rose notably in the quarter.

title: European Aluminum Premium Soars to Nine-Month High of $324/Tonne Amid Supply Disruptions and CBAM Anticipation
summary: European duty-paid aluminum premiums surged to about $324/t (nine-month high) after a Grundartangi smelter outage cut production and importers front-loaded purchases ahead of CBAM carbon costs. Logistical frictions and tight duty-free supply intensified demand, raising delivered costs for European industrial users.

title: Copper Elevated to Critical Mineral Status: A Strategic Imperative for the Green Transition
summary: The USGS added copper to the U.S. critical minerals list, published in the Federal Register on Nov. 7, 2025. The designation is expected to spur policy and investment measures to strengthen domestic supply chains, including possible permitting/incentive changes and trade-policy discussions, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Silver Rockets to Record Highs Amid Historic Squeeze, Gold and Copper Shine Bright
summary: The piece describes a historic squeeze and surge in silver alongside robust gains in gold and copper, driven by industrial demand from the green energy transition, supply tightness, physical-market liquidity issues, and macro/geopolitical uncertainty. It reports copper rising to record levels, implying near-term bullish price pressure. Aluminium drivers are not covered.

title: Indigenous Community Pushes Back Against Peru's Largest Copper Mine
summary: Indigenous Pumamarca community members in Peru protest Las Bambas, citing alleged illegitimate land sale and expansion that encroaches on ancestral grazing lands and threatens water sources with mining contamination. The community seeks restitution and accountability from MMG, creating risk of operational disruption at a major copper producer.

title: The Trump Trade: How Silver and Copper Became America's New Gold Rush
summary: Wealth Daily argues that U.S. policy reclassifying copper as a critical mineral will accelerate domestic mining via faster permitting, funding and DPA prioritization. It links copper to AI/data-center and electrification demand and claims supply constraints could tighten, supporting higher copper prices.

title: Copper rises on hopes of a resolution to the budget crisis in the US, with markets awaiting Chinese data
summary: Copper gained 0.9% to $10,924/ton on hopes of resolving the US budget crisis and ending the government shutdown, which would allow key US data releases for Fed rate decisions. Markets also await China credit figures as weaker financing forecasts cloud industrial demand, supporting a softer-dollar bullish tone.

title: Mining Lease Application at Big One Copper Deposit | Company Announcement
summary: New Frontier Minerals lodged a mining lease application for the Big One copper deposit within its NWQ Copper Project in Queensland. The company outlines an initial plan for an open-cut operation with ore hauled to Austral’s Mt Kelly processing facility, targeting first production in Q1 2027.

title: St-Georges Eco-Mining Corp.: High-Grade Nickel and Platinum Group Metal Discovery Expands Manicouagan Critical Minerals Potential
summary: St-Georges Eco-Mining announced first revenue from its subsidiary and identified a new high-grade nickel-copper-PGE target zone at its Manicouagan Project in Québec. Surface grab samples returned up to 2.28% Ni and 0.37% Cu, prompting plans for further surveys and future drilling, but results are early and selective.

title: ADC12 Aluminum Alloy Price Hits Yearly High, Aluminum Scrap Cost Exceeds 90%[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Domestic primary aluminium and aluminum scrap prices rose week-on-week, with ADC12 spot and futures hitting yearly highs. Tight scrap supply and strong cost support (scrap >90% of secondary costs) continued to lift quotations. Downstream procurement turned cautious due to high prices and environmental restrictions, but overall expectations remain “hold up well,” limiting downside.

title: Australia eyes Indonesia's nickel in its play for critical mineral supremacy
summary: Australia and Indonesia highlight critical minerals cooperation after the Australia-Indonesia Climate and Infrastructure Partnership, with strong focus on nickel. Indonesia is described as the dominant, surplus-producing nickel supplier, but policy moves on nickel quotas and continued downstreaming support shape expectations for near-term supply, investment, and pricing.

title: Vulcan Minerals, Inc.: Vulcan Minerals Inc. - Colchester Copper-Gold Update in Central Newfoundland
summary: Vulcan Minerals provided an update from the Colchester Project’s McNeily drill program, reporting multiple copper-bearing intersections (including up to ~1.01% Cu over 5.2m and 0.48% Cu over 13.7m) and extended strike continuity. It is an exploration reconnaissance update with no production or trade implications stated.

title: Rio Tinto and Alcoa develop low-polluting method for aluminum production
summary: Rio Tinto and Alcoa said their Elysis inert-anode technology achieved the first commercial-scale implementation at Rio Tinto’s Alma, Quebec smelter, producing aluminum with no direct carbon emissions. Testing will continue and scaling is planned over coming years, amid rising pressure to cut aluminum’s greenhouse-gas footprint.

title: 【SMM Analysis】PP 28/2025 Update: Implications for Indonesian Nickel Smelters
summary: SMM outlines Indonesia’s PP 28/2025 risk-based licensing rules affecting nickel smelters. OSS notices require firms to submit statements that they will not produce nickel intermediates unless exemptions are granted. System instability and difficulties for projects not yet under construction add uncertainty, potentially weighing on near-term nickel supply expectations.

title: Carney's latest major projects include LNG terminal expansion, nickel mine
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney listed new energy and mining projects for expedited review, including Ontario’s Crawford nickel project, described as the world’s second-largest nickel-sulphide reserve. Officials say the referral can speed approvals, attract investors, and potentially support construction next year, improving near-term nickel supply outlook.

title: Where does all the stolen copper wire go? ABC7 goes on raid with investigators
summary: Investigators in Lynwood raided an alleged backyard scrap operation tied to stolen copper wire, including communications and structural wiring. The report says copper theft has grown alongside soaring scrap prices and rogue recyclers, contributing to outages. It notes narcotics and firearms but no direct market supply shock.

title: Man behind nation-building nickel project has spent decades waiting
summary: Canada Nickel CEO Mark Selby tours the proposed Crawford nickel mine site near Timmins as the federal government’s Major Projects Office fast-tracks the project. The article frames it as a step toward creating a new nickel district amid stronger EV battery demand. It suggests improved prospects for future nickel supply.

title: Copper's Resurgence: China's Economic Optimism Ignites Global Industrial Metals Market
summary: Copper prices are surging on renewed China economic optimism, alongside persistent supply constraints from mining disruptions, declining ore grades, and limited new capacity. LME and COMEX levels have climbed sharply, with analysts forecasting further upside. Higher copper prices raise input costs for manufacturers, but boost sentiment for producers.

title: Rio Tinto Inks Wind-Power Deal For Kennecott Copper Operation
summary: Rio Tinto agreed to a 15-year wind-power supply deal with Terra-Gen for its Kennecott copper operation, buying 78.5 MW of power from a newly completed Texas wind farm. The company aims to cut Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 50% by 2030 and is expanding onsite solar at Kennecott.

title: Critical Minerals Update: USGS Finalizes 2025 Critical Minerals List, Adding Copper, Silver, And Eight Others
summary: USGS finalized its 2025 Critical Minerals List, expanding it by 10 and retaining the prior 50, including adding copper. The designation may trigger expedited federal permitting (FAST-41), Defense Production Act funding, and tax incentives. The policy aim is to reduce reliance on foreign supplies and accelerate domestic projects.

title: Saudi Arabia surprises with major gold and copper discoveries
summary: Saudi Arabia’s Ma’aden says early drilling in the Arabian Shield found promising gold and copper mineralization, including copper-bearing gold at Jabal Shayban and additional gold at Wadi Al Jaww. Results are preliminary and could support future mines, but timelines and reserves are not yet confirmed, limiting short-term price pressure.

title: Ivanhoe Electric receives $200m in financing for Santa Cruz copper project
summary: Ivanhoe Electric announced it has secured $200 million in financing for its Santa Cruz copper project. Additional funding typically improves project momentum and future production outlook, which can lift market expectations for copper supply and support short-term copper price sentiment.

title: [SMM Analysis] The nickel market was under pressure overall this week, and domestic inventory continued to accumulate.
summary: The report says nickel prices stayed under pressure this week: SHFE fell below 120,000 yuan/mt and closed at 117,080 yuan/mt, while LME weakened to about $14,860/mt. Spot nickel also declined and inventories built domestically, with end-users more cautious as prices kept dropping.

title: CopperTech market expansion | Hotter Commodities
summary: CopperTech, backed by Vedanta, said it has political support and resources to expand output from Zambia’s KCM mine, aiming to lift integrated copper production to 300,000 tonnes by 2031. It highlights improved power/infrastructure prospects and US import reliance (~45% of refined copper), implying stronger near-term copper supply expectations.

title: Canada Nickel Announces the Referral of the Company's Crawford Project to the Major Projects Office by the Government of Canada
summary: Canada Nickel said the Government of Canada has referred its Crawford Nickel Project to the Major Projects Office, a step aimed at accelerating national-significance permitting and financing. The company expects progress toward construction by end-2026, supporting near-term optimism for future nickel supply.

title: Erdene Resource Development Corporation: Erdene Files Updated Resource for the Zuun Mod Molybdenum-Copper Project
summary: Erdene announced it has filed an updated NI 43-101 technical report for its Zuun Mod molybdenum-copper project in Mongolia, following an updated mineral resource estimate. The release updates project technical information but does not indicate production, outages, or definitive supply changes. Sentiment for copper may improve modestly.

title: CEO.CA Technologies Ltd.: CEO.CA's Inside the Boardroom: Aeonian Resources Targets Sedimentary Copper in Overlooked Area of B.C.
summary: CEO.CA features an interview with Aeonian Resources’ CEO describing the company’s plans to target sedimentary copper in an overlooked area of B.C. While this is directly related to copper exploration, the release contains no assay, resource, or production figures that would clearly drive short-term copper price moves.

title: Feds pick Timmins nickel mine to be a nation-building project
summary: Canada’s federal government referred Canada Nickel’s Crawford project to a Major Projects Office, expected to accelerate permitting and financing for the planned open-pit nickel mine and mill. The government frames it as nation-building/critical-minerals support, which should bolster nickel supply expectations.

title: Nelson Mandela Bay residents left frustrated as copper thieves target water pipes
summary: Nelson Mandela Bay residents report a sharp rise in copper theft targeting municipal and residential water pipes and meters. Security firms cite dozens of incidents involving copper pipes and cables in recent months. Police and municipal operations are underway to curb the Second-Hand Goods Act violations and stolen copper flows.

title: Snowy Hydro deal in mix to save Tomago Aluminium smelter
summary: Federal Labor is considering a power deal between Snowy Hydro and Rio Tinto-controlled Tomago Aluminium to secure cheap renewable electricity for the troubled smelter. The move is intended to prevent output disruption after Rio rejected a federal–NSW bailout offer, improving near-term aluminium supply expectations.

title: Policy Uncertainty and High Arbitrage Inventories: The Dilemma of the Secondary Copper Market
summary: Copper prices in China rose this week, with SHFE up and Guangdong bright copper following. Secondary copper rod firms cut operating rates due to weak orders and unclear local incentives (Notice 770), while primary–secondary spreads widened and arbitrage increased hidden warehouse inventory. Outlook: copper may stay supported if futures remain strong, but recycled demand is constrained.

title: Existing investors demand exemptions from nickel smelter restrictions - Regulations
summary: Indonesia’s risk-based licensing rules impose a moratorium on new smelter projects aimed at producing intermediate nickel products, enforced via the OSS platform. Existing investors are demanding exemptions if they secured licenses before the rules. The regulation is intended to accelerate downstream nickel processing, potentially tightening future intermediate supply.

title: South32 invests in Richards Bay aluminium beneficiation
summary: South32 plans to invest R200m in Bingelela Alloys at Richards Bay to promote local beneficiation of liquid aluminium. The concessional financing, backed by the Automotive Industry Transformation Fund, is intended to support production of rim alloys. The project may modestly improve near-term aluminium processing expectations.

title: Zambia, a Copper Prize, Becomes the Stage for a Global Rail Race
summary: The EU and Zambia agreed to fund upgrades to the Livingstone–Ndola railway and support logistics corridors such as the Lobito route. The article links these improvements to faster copper exports from Zambia and the DRC via Angola. It also cites competing corridor upgrades backed by China and others, reflecting strategic focus on copper supply.

title: Indonesia Grants Copper Concentrate Export Permit Again – Can It Quench Immediate Thirst? [SMM Analysis]
summary: Indonesia has agreed to issue a renewed copper concentrate export permit to Amman Mineral International (480,000 tonnes for six months). Exports are expected to rise sharply to China, improving concentrate options for smelters in China, Japan, and South Korea and strengthening bargaining power in upcoming long-term contract talks.

title: Mining with integrity to advance sustainable nickel downstreaming
summary: Indonesia’s downstreaming strategy for nickel—accelerating domestic smelting and processing after the 2020 ore export ban—is highlighted as key to capturing higher value from nickel for battery materials. With Indonesia holding ~42% of global nickel reserves, the policy and new processing focus can support near-term nickel price expectations.

title: Around 30 people killed in Congo copper mine incident, officials say
summary: A bridge collapse at the Kalando semi-industrial copper mining site in Congo’s Lualaba province killed around 30 people, with several others hospitalized. Officials attribute the panic to reported gunfire by security forces amid artisanal mining. The incident underscores risks at unregulated copper sites but provides no clear output disruption data.

title: Over 30 Reported Dead In Congo Copper Mine Incident, Toll Rising
summary: Reuters reports dozens of deaths and many injuries after a landslide/collapse at the Kalando artisanal copper mining site in DR Congo’s Lualaba province. Officials report differing fatality counts, reflecting uncertainty. The incident underscores persistent safety and regulatory weaknesses that can disrupt copper supply and raise risk premiums.

title: U.S. tariffs: Impact on automotive, steel and aluminum industries
summary: The piece says U.S. tariffs act like consumption taxes, raising import costs and pressuring buyers, with Canada still facing tariff-driven trade friction. It links reduced car and parts purchases to closures/paused production, citing impacts on steel mills and aluminum smelters that supply the automotive industry.

title: Mining With Integrity to Advance Sustainable Nickel Downstreaming
summary: Indonesia’s 2020 nickel ore export ban has driven downstreaming, requiring companies to build smelters and process nickel into battery materials. The article cites Indonesia’s large nickel reserves and notes PT Vale’s nickel matte production and emission-reduction investments. Overall, it supports expectations for tighter nickel supply and stronger processing demand.

title: Dozens feared dead as section of copper mine collapses in DR Congo
summary: A section of a copper mine site in DR Congo collapsed after an overcrowded makeshift bridge failed, killing at least 32 people (reports up to ~70). The provincial interior minister blamed hasty crossing and flood/landslide conditions, with illegal diggers entering despite a ban. Rescue and investigations are ongoing.

title: Dozens killed in DR Congo after bridge collapses at copper, cobalt mine
summary: A bridge collapsed at the Kalando copper and cobalt mine in DR Congo after wildcat miners entered despite a rain/landslide ban, killing at least 32 (possibly 40). Authorities suspended operations on Sunday amid reports of military gunfire and panic. Disruption is localized, with no production figures given.

title: At least 32 dead in DR Congo after bridge at copper mine collapses
summary: At least 32 people died when an overcrowded makeshift bridge at the Kalando copper mine in DR Congo collapsed into a flooded ditch. The provincial interior minister blamed illegal “digger” crossings despite a ban during heavy rains. Investigations and search-and-rescue efforts continue, potentially disrupting copper operations short term.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | Newcastle Herald
summary: Australia’s federal government is considering a power-purchase agreement via Snowy Hydro to keep the Tomago Aluminium smelter viable after its coal contract expires. Without cheaper electricity/renewables-backed pricing, Rio Tinto has warned it may shut. Securing power would support aluminium production and near-term supply expectations.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Australia’s federal government is considering power-purchase arrangements via Snowy Hydro and a scheme financial vehicle to lock in financially sustainable electricity for the Tomago aluminium smelter. The current coal contract ends 2028 and higher post-2029 power costs could make the plant unviable. Keeping it operating supports aluminium supply expectations.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | The Macleay Argus
summary: The federal government is considering a power-purchase agreement with Snowy Hydro to provide financially sustainable electricity to Tomago Aluminium. With the existing coal contract expiring in 2028 and proposed post-2029 power costs higher, Rio Tinto has warned the smelter may cease operations without cheaper power.

title: Litchfield lands 91m Northern Territory copper hit
summary: Litchfield Minerals reports a strong 91m copper intersection at its Oonagalabi prospect, strengthening the case for a large polymetallic system. More importantly for prices, the piece cites disruptions at major copper mines in West Papua, the DRC and Peru and argues the market may move into a supply deficit.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | The Singleton Argus
summary: Australia’s federal government is considering a power-purchase agreement with Snowy Hydro to keep the Tomago Aluminium smelter supplied with financially sustainable electricity as its coal contract nears expiration in 2028. Rising post-2029 power costs could make the plant unviable, so support could help sustain aluminium supply and output.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | Manning River Times
summary: The federal government is considering a power-purchase agreement with Snowy Hydro to supply electricity to Rio Tinto’s Tomago Aluminium, whose coal contract ends in 2028. Without cheaper clean power, operating costs from 2029 could make the smelter unviable. A scheme could keep production running and avoid closure.

title: Dozens killed in DRC after bridge collapses at copper, cobalt mine
summary: A bridge collapse at DRC’s Kalando copper-and-cobalt mine killed dozens, with authorities citing wildcat miners forcing entry despite a ban due to heavy rain. Gunfire sparked panic, and the resulting rush caused fatalities. Operations were suspended, raising immediate supply and operational-risk concerns for copper markets.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | Great Lakes Advocate
summary: Australia’s federal government is considering power-purchase agreements via a scheme financial vehicle to keep Rio Tinto’s Tomago Aluminium smelter supplied with affordable electricity after its coal contract expires. The aim is to avert potential closure and preserve aluminium output, supporting supply expectations.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | The Scone Advocate
summary: The federal government is considering a power-purchase agreement using Snowy Hydro to secure stable, financially sustainable electricity for the Tomago Aluminium smelter. The current coal power contract ends in 2028, and higher 2029 energy costs could make operations unviable. The proposal seeks to avert closure.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | The Maitland Mercury
summary: Australia’s federal government is considering a power-purchase agreement with Snowy Hydro to ensure Tomago Aluminium can obtain affordable electricity after its coal contract ends. Without support, rising 2029 energy costs could make the smelter unviable and Rio Tinto may close it, threatening aluminium supply.

title: Bridge Collapse at DR Congo Copper Mine Leaves at Least 32 Dead
summary: A bridge collapse at a copper mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo killed at least 32 people, with reports of up to 70 deaths and missing miners. Officials say illegal diggers entered despite warnings of heavy rains and landslide risk. Rescue and investigations are ongoing, potentially disrupting copper output.

title: Government considers using Snowy Hydro's keep Tomago Aluminium open | Dungog Chronicle
summary: The federal government is considering a power-purchase agreement via a scheme financial vehicle with Snowy Hydro to keep the Tomago Aluminium smelter running as its coal contract ends in 2028. Rising post-2029 power costs threaten viability. A stable clean-energy deal would reduce closure risk and support aluminium supply.

title: 'Around 30 people killed in DRC copper mine incident' – Channel Africa
summary: About 30 people were killed after a bridge collapsed at the Kalando semi-industrial copper mine in southeastern DRC, according to SAEMAPE. Reports suggest panic triggered by gunfire from military securing the site. The incident highlights risks at unregulated artisanal operations, potentially affecting short-term copper supply expectations.

title: Converting Refined Nickel to Nickel Sulphate?—Supply-Demand Pattern and Price Outlook for Nickel Sulphate
summary: SMM reports nickel sulphate prices easing in early/mid-November as refined nickel prices weaken and producers expect refined output cuts. While demand from ternary cathode makers stays high, cost pressure eases and integrated/smelters ramp nickel sulphate supply. Potential conversion of refined nickel into nickel sulphate could further loosen the market, weighing on prices into December.

title: [SMM Analysis] Bears Dominate as Nickel Prices Weaken: An Analysis of Recent Macro and Fundamental Pressures
summary: Nickel prices have fallen sharply since late October, breaking multiple SHFE and LME support levels. The report cites weak China data, delayed US easing expectations, large refined nickel and LME inventories, and Indonesian regulatory actions affecting smelter investment/ore quotas. Near-term signals suggest oversold conditions, but surplus pressures dominate, keeping downside bias.

title: Rusal Plans Major Aluminum Smelter Investment in Ethiopia
summary: Ethiopian Investment Holdings and Russia’s Rusal signed an MoU to build a 500,000-ton-per-year aluminium smelter in Ethiopia, targeting multi-year development. The project would expand Africa’s limited smelting capacity dominated by a few large plants. The news is sentiment-supportive for aluminium prices.

title: Ball Corporation invests $60m in Indian aluminium packaging plant
summary: Ball Corporation plans to invest $60 million in an aluminium packaging plant in India. The expansion points to increased production capacity for aluminium packaging products, which can lift expectations for aluminium demand. The impact on near-term global aluminium prices is likely modest but positive.

title: 32 People Killed After Bridge Collapses at a Copper and Cobalt Mine in DRC
summary: A bridge collapsed at a copper and cobalt mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo after overcrowding and panic triggered by gunfire from soldiers. The incident killed at least 32 people. As the operation is a copper producer, the disruption could impair output and logistics, adding near-term supply risk for copper markets.

title: Nickel pivot sparks legal debate in mining sector
summary: Indonesia introduced PP 28/2025, enforcing an administrative moratorium on new smelter projects producing intermediate nickel products via the OSS licensing system. Industry groups debate exceptions for already-investing firms, but the policy is justified as a response to expected 2025 nickel oversupply. The market effect is supportive for nickel prices.

title: DRC copper mine bridge collapse claims lives
summary: A bridge collapse at the Kalando semi-industrial copper mine in Lualaba, DRC, reportedly killed dozens and left others injured after panic reportedly triggered by gunfire from military securing the site. Authorities cited overcrowding and militaries’ role, with calls for investigation into mine security and safety conditions.

title: Policy change in Argentina may boost Copper mining
summary: Argentina’s president is considering loosening the Glaciers Law by shifting perimeter-setting authority to provinces, potentially reducing protected glacier areas and improving legal certainty for mining. The change could unlock copper deposits near the Andes and aid foreign investment, which may lift expectations for copper supply and output.

title: Tribeca Investment Fund Backs Botswana's Emerging Copper Industry
summary: Tribeca Investment Partners invested AUD 4 million in Cobre Limited to help fund a copper demonstration plant at the Ngami project in Botswana’s Kalahari Copper Belt. The financing targets well-field development and exploration using In-Situ Copper Recovery, supporting expectations for future copper supply growth.

title: America's next coin casualty: Soaring metal prices put the costly nickel on notice
summary: The U.S. Mint ended penny production due to metal costs exceeding face value and warned it may target the nickel next. Nickels are made from a copper-nickel alloy, and rising copper and nickel prices have widened Mint losses, while advocates push for a cheaper “new” nickel composition within a year.

title: Rio Tinto to reduce production at Yarwun Alumina Refinery to extend operational life
summary: Rio Tinto will reduce production at the Yarwun alumina refinery by 40% from October 2026, lowering annual alumina output by about 1.2 million tonnes to extend the site’s life until 2035. Bauxite mines and aluminium smelters will keep running at full capacity, but alumina supply tightness risk rises.

title: Pecoy Copper to Commence Drilling Activities Shortly
summary: Pecoy Copper Corp. said drilling is scheduled to begin in coming weeks at its Pecoy copper-gold-molybdenum-silver project in Peru after renewed permits and environmental approvals. The company aims to expand the mineralized footprint. The news is exploration-focused and does not signal immediate supply changes.

title: Rio Tinto to cut production at Gladstone Yarwun Alumina Refinery, impacting 180 jobs
summary: Rio Tinto will curtail alumina output at its Gladstone Yarwun refinery by 40% from October next year, cutting annual production by about 1.2 million tonnes and affecting roughly 180 jobs. The firm says the change preserves the refinery’s tailings viability and keeps aluminium/bauxite operations running at full capacity.

title: FireFly Metals announces Mineral Resource increased by 51% at Green Bay Copper Gold Project, Canada
summary: FireFly Metals said the Green Bay Copper-Gold Project mineral resource rose 51%, including a higher-grade core zone and higher contained copper equivalent. Contained copper in M&I and inferred categories increased substantially, but the update is for resources and future feasibility work, not near-term production.

title: Rio Tinto axes 180 jobs at Queensland's Yarwun aluminium refinery at Gladstone
summary: Rio Tinto will axe 180 jobs and scale back operations at its Yarwun aluminium refinery in Gladstone, cutting production by 40% from October 2026. The move is intended to extend refinery life to 2035 and reduce annual alumina output by about 1.2 million tonnes, amid weak alumina economics and higher costs.

title: True North lands 7m at 7.9% copper hit in northwest Queensland
summary: True North Copper reported standout drilling at its Mount Oxide Aquila discovery in northwest Queensland, including a 7m intercept at 7.9% copper and other thick, high-grade copper-cobalt-silver zones. The company says strike has been extended over 700m and remains open, supporting bullish sentiment toward copper.

title: Kincora Copper Limited: Kincora Commences Drilling at the Wongarbon Porphyry Project
summary: Kincora Copper commenced its first ~650m hole to basement at the Wongarbon porphyry project in NSW to test a magnetic anomaly interpreted as a copper-gold porphyry target. The program is supported by an NSW grant and aims to optimize follow-up exploration, but no production or confirmed new supply is reported.

title: Canadian Copper Inc.: Canadian Copper Provides Murray Brook Project Update
summary: Canadian Copper Inc. updates its Murray Brook Project: SGS metallurgical testwork on drill-core samples, ongoing permitting discussions for an EIA registration, and continued project financing talks. While the core geology includes chalcopyrite (copper) and other sulphides, no production timing, supply impact, or policy change is announced.

title: Midnight Sun Mining Corp.: Midnight Sun Intercepts 1.0% Copper over 22 Metres and 0.98% Copper over 15 Metres at Dumbwa
summary: Midnight Sun Mining reported drill results from its Dumbwa target in Zambia, including copper intercepts around 0.79%–1.0% Cu over 5.25–22 metres, plus continued drilling through the rainy season. The update strengthens exploration confidence but does not indicate immediate production or inventory impacts.

title: African Rainbow Minerals considers Papua New Guinea copper venture with Newmont Corp
summary: Harmony Gold chairman Patrice Motsepe said the firm is evaluating a large copper venture in Papua New Guinea with Newmont that could require $4-5 billion. The plan is described as long-term, with funds potentially used in copper regions. No immediate production or policy changes are reported.

title: EU Plans to Curb Aluminum Scrap Exports Next Year -- Commodities Roundup
summary: The European Commission plans preparatory work for a “balanced” measure to curb aluminum scrap exports, aiming to limit scrap outflows that could leave Europe short of a key input for decarbonisation. The news flow also includes Rio Tinto’s plan to cut Yarwun alumina output, tightening upstream supply.

title: EU ramps up efforts to fight aluminium scrap leakage
summary: The EU Commission said it will prepare new measures to curb aluminium scrap “leakage” as exports of scrap to Asia and the US drain feedstock from European recyclers. Scrap leakage has intensified amid the US tariff on value-added aluminium exports. Measures aim to improve access at competitive prices without fully blocking exports.

title: EU plans to limit exports of aluminium scrap
summary: The EU plans to restrict exports of aluminium scrap after exports hit a record 1.26 million tonnes in 2024. The Commission argues scrap “flooding out” leaves EU industry short of feedstock as decarbonisation relies on recycling. Monitoring began in July and preparatory work for a measure follows.

title: Rusal's $1B aluminium smelter in Ethiopia | Hotter Commodities
summary: Rusal and Ethiopian Investment Holdings plan a $1B aluminium smelter in Ethiopia powered largely by low-cost hydropower. The project could make Ethiopia a major African producer and shift regional aluminium supply, supporting demand for smelting capacity and export flows. Risks include power variability and feedstock import needs.

title: Rio Tinto to cut Yarwun alumina refinery output by 40%
summary: Rio Tinto will reduce production at its Yarwun alumina refinery in Gladstone by 40% from October 2026, cutting alumina output by around 1.2 million tonnes per annum. The company says it will maintain customer requirements via other operations, while pursuing tailings and decarbonisation options to extend site life.

title: CME : An Options Strategy to Target Lower Copper Prices
summary: CME’s note uses Ichimoku and MACD technicals on front-month copper futures, stating the three-year uptrend has held despite tariff-related volatility and that the weekly MACD turning higher points to continued strength. It presents this as a basis for options positioning aimed at copper.

title: Trump opens door to easing some steel and aluminum tariffs
summary: The U.S. executive order gives Commerce discretion to reduce tariffs on some Canadian and Mexican steel and aluminum imports by up to half if companies expand U.S. production and shipments are destined for U.S. auto manufacturing. This limited relief could ease aluminum supply-cost pressures versus the earlier 50% tariff.

title: Nagoya Moves to Stop Illegal Collection of Aluminum Cans
summary: Nagoya is considering an ordinance to stop unauthorized collection of aluminum cans and other recyclables from designated points. City officials say scavenging has risen as recovered aluminum becomes more valuable due to higher prices. The measure would use warnings, orders, and fines to protect recycling operations and community routines.

title: AGFC seeks tips after copper wire theft, vandalism impacts wildlife management area
summary: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission is seeking tips after copper wire theft and vandalism at a wildlife management area, causing habitat loss. Damages exceed $50,000 and key electrical components, including a custom variable frequency drive and motor wiring, were stripped and require repair before duck season.

title: Copper falls amid doubts about tech stocks and the market's wait-and-see attitude
summary: Copper continued falling for a third straight session on the LME, with the three-month contract down about 0.8% to $10,690/t. The drop reflects risk-off sentiment from tech-stock valuation doubts and weaker expectations for further Fed easing. China demand looks moderate as premiums soften, while supply pressure appears limited on spot spreads.

title: Leaked CBAM provisional benchmarks largely in line with market expectations for aluminium and steel
summary: A leaked CBAM annex details provisional embedded-emissions benchmark calculations for EU imports of aluminium, including route-based distinctions between primary and secondary (scrap-heavy) material. The benchmarks are largely aligned with expectations, and market reaction was muted due to remaining uncertainty around default country values, so near-term impact on aluminium prices appears limited.

title: Copper: Investment in Project Involving Harmony Gold in Papua New Guinea Estimated at $5 Billion
summary: Harmony Gold and partners are developing Papua New Guinea’s Wafi-Golpu copper project, with total investment estimated up to $5 billion, but no final investment decision yet. African Rainbow Minerals signals funding readiness and renewed focus on copper tied to the energy transition, supporting near-term bullish sentiment.

title: Aluminum Bare Wire Conductor Market to Reach $19.1 billion, Globally, by 2034 at 5.5% CAGR: Allied Market Research
summary: The PRNewswire piece on the aluminum bare wire conductor market cites tariffs that pushed primary aluminum prices higher, raising input costs for wire manufacturers and affecting trade flows (reduced imports from China, shifts in Canadian exports). It also notes some domestic smelter/refinery gains, but aluminum remained above pre-tariff levels by 2025.

title: Stäubli Enhances its BosCon Connector Product Line for Large-Format PV Aluminum Cable
summary: Stäubli Electrical Connectors launched an enhanced BosCon connector for large-format aluminum PV trunk cables in utility-scale PV systems, including eBOS connections to combiner/disconnect boxes and inverters, plus BESS. The cULus-listed 1500V-rated connector targets safer high-current outdoor installations using 4/0 AWG through 600 MCM aluminum.

title: Aluminium Scrap Exports: EU's New Regulations Coming
summary: The European Commission is preparing measures to restrict aluminium scrap exports due to record outflows and domestic recycling feedstock shortages. EU scrap exports hit 1.26 Mt in 2024, aided by US primary aluminium tariffs that favor scrap. Producers seek export duties; alternatives include licensing or recycled-content targets.

title: Highland Copper highlights wetland restoration and stream diversion work with new drone footage
summary: Highland Copper says it has completed wetland restoration and stream-diversion mitigation at its Copperwood project, including thousands of trees planted and drone-documented works. Environmental groups oppose a proposed mine-waste dam holding toxic materials. Michigan’s 2026 budget excludes a related infrastructure grant, leaving timeline impact uncertain.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Announces President of South Africa, Cyril Ramaphosa, Officially Opens the Platreef Platinum-Palladium-Nickel-Rhodium-Gold-Copper Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines announced that South Africa’s president officially opened the Platreef mine and that the Phase 1 concentrator produced first concentrate on Nov. 18, 2025. The project targets significant platinum-group output plus payable nickel and copper by-products. Faster ramp-up supports incremental supply expectations for copper and nickel.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Announces President of South Africa, Cyril Ramaphosa, Officially Opens the Platreef Platinum-Palladium-Nickel-Rhodium-Gold-Copper Mine
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reports the official opening of its Platreef mine in South Africa and that Phase 1 concentrate production began on November 18, 2025. The orebody is platinum-palladium-nickel-rhodium-gold-copper, with nickel and copper expected as by-products, indicating incremental near-term supply support for those metals.

title: Harmony Gold considers Papua New Guinea copper venture with Newmont Corp
