summary: Harmony Gold said it is evaluating a large copper venture in Papua New Guinea in partnership with Newmont, potentially requiring $4-5 billion in investment. The chairman linked funding to copper regions in Australia and Papua New Guinea. However, the project is discussed as long-term strategy, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Cochilco Raises 2025–2026 Copper Price Outlook to Record Levels as Supply Pressures Persist
summary: Chile’s Cochilco lifted its 2025 copper forecast to $4.45/lb and 2026 to $4.55/lb, both record highs, citing weaker production at Collahuasi and Anglo American Sur and an accident at Codelco’s El Teniente. It expects supply constraints to outpace moderated demand growth.

title: Nippon Light Metal  to import recycled aluminum from India
summary: Nippon Light Metal Holdings will develop an aluminum supply chain using recycled scrap sourced from its partner in India, shipping the material to its Kambara complex in Japan. The firm targets mass production using scrap-derived aluminum in fiscal 2026 for auto parts, implying longer-dated supply adjustments rather than immediate price moves.

title: Dr. Copper's Pulse: A Robust Signal for Global Economic Health Amidst Green Transition
summary: The piece reports strong upward momentum in copper prices (around $5/lb; LME highs earlier in November) and attributes it to accelerating demand from electrification and grid/renewables plus persistent supply constraints from disruptions and delayed mine development. It also cites policy support and China optimism, reinforcing bullish short-term outlook.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Makes Final Land Acquisition Payment at the Santa Cruz Copper Project in Arizona
summary: Ivanhoe Electric says it has fully paid $39.3 million in remaining land acquisition costs for the Santa Cruz copper project in Arizona, meeting terms before major mine construction. Management expects initial construction in early 2026 subject to permits and first copper cathode production by late 2028.

title: Devon RCMP advises public of copper wire theft
summary: Devon RCMP warns property owners about copper wire theft, especially at isolated well sites. Police say thieves target copper for its resale value, causing repair costs, production downtime, safety and environmental risks. RCMP urges security measures and quick reporting. The theft risk implies reduced copper availability.

title: £2.5million Equity Funding to Expand Exploration | Company Announcement
summary: Great Southern Copper plc raised £2.5m equity funding to expand exploration at its Especularita project in Chile, including a high-grade copper-silver target. The funds finance additional drilling and prospect testing, but the company remains in exploration with no immediate production or supply change signaled.

title: Nifty Copper Project Update | Company Announcement
summary: Ecora Resources reported Cyprium Metals’ board approval of the Nifty Copper Complex cathode restart plan in Western Australia. First production of copper cathode is expected mid-2026. Ecora holds a 1.5% realized value royalty, but payments require 800kt cumulative copper.

title: Ecora Resources PLC Announces Nifty Copper Project Update
summary: Ecora announced Cyprium Board approval for a restart plan at the Nifty Copper Complex in Western Australia, targeting first copper cathode production in mid-2026. Ecora holds a 1.5% realised value royalty, with payments only after 800kt cumulative copper production, expected to take years to reach.

title: Aluminum Scrap Followed the Decline During the Week, Short-Term Tight Supply Supports Prices[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Weekly review says aluminum scrap prices followed primary aluminum lower, shifting the scrap price center down. Despite softer primary prices and weaker wrought demand, low scrap-yard inventories and tight supply limited downside. Secondary ADC12 costs eased but tight raw material supply and cautious buyers support consolidation near 21,200–21,600 yuan/mt.

title: China's 2025 Copper Anode Imports Hit Multi-Year Low, Down 15% YoY in Jan-Oct [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s copper anode imports totaled 55,200 mt in October 2025, up MoM but down YoY, with Jan–Oct cumulative imports down 15.01% to 634,000 mt and full-year expected at a five-year low. Zambia drove the MoM rebound after maintenance, but logistics and import price ratios remain unfavorable, with potential Q4 shipment delays.

title: Benton Resources Inc.: Benton Discovers Additional High-Grade Gold and Delineates Large Copper Soil Anomaly South of the Great Burnt Copper Deposit
summary: Benton Resources reported additional high-grade gold results and soil sampling that delineated a multi-line copper anomaly at its Great Burnt project, alongside ongoing drilling intersecting copper-gold mineralization. While copper-related discoveries can affect sentiment, the update is exploration-focused without immediate supply impacts, likely limiting near-term price movement.

title: Trump's executive order to reduce tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium would impact ArcelorMittal's EBITDA by $300 million maximum
summary: Trump signed an executive order that could allow Commerce to reduce Canada’s steel and aluminium import tariffs from 50% to 25% if conditions are met. Renta 4 estimates the tariff cut could improve ArcelorMittal’s EBITDA by up to $300 million annually, supporting a more constructive near-term outlook.

title: Another fire ignites at Ford aluminum supplier Novelis
summary: Another fire broke out at Novelis’ aluminum plant in Oswego, New York, which supplies Ford’s aluminum-intensive F-150 truck line. The plant had largely halted production after an earlier blaze, and Ford already revised forecasts for a gross hit of up to $2 billion. Restart plans may be delayed.

title: Osisko Metals reports new copper intercepts at Gaspé project
summary: Osisko Metals reported new drill intercepts from its Gaspé porphyry/skarn copper project, including 64.5m at 2.70% Cu within a larger 138m at 1.45% Cu. The results support an ongoing resource upgrade and expansion, with an updated MRE expected in early 2026.

title: Novelis aluminum plant catches fire again after costly disaster in September
summary: A five-alarm fire hit Novelis’ aluminum sheets facility in Scriba, New York, with dispatch audio indicating the cold mill as the source. The plant supplies 40% of U.S. automaker aluminum sheet demand, and this is the third fire in two months, compounding production disruption risk for the sector.

title: Peru's Commodity Sector Ignites with 9% Investment Surge, Fueling Export Boom
summary: Peru’s private investment in commodities rose over 9% in early 2025, with mining investment up and exports surging 14.2% in Q1 2025, led by copper. The government and investors plan major capital for copper projects, improving expectations for supply/output momentum in the near term.

title: Man accused in Tucson copper wire theft spree
summary: Tucson police arrested a man accused of a copper wire theft spree targeting neighborhood street lights. Investigators say more than a half-ton of copper wiring was removed and sold to scrap yards, prompting multiple burglary and theft counts. The report suggests localized copper diversion but likely minimal effect on prices.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.97% Lower at $4.9595 — Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures settled 0.97% lower at $4.9595, signaling bearish near-term price pressure for copper. The “Data Talk” format suggests the move is driven by the latest trading session pricing rather than policy or supply details, but it still directly concerns copper market performance.

title: Cascada Silver Corp.: Cascada Signs MOUs to Acquire Three Advanced Copper-Gold Porphyry Properties in Chile
summary: Cascada Silver signed non-binding MOUs to acquire three advanced copper-gold porphyry properties in Chile’s Totora cluster, citing historical drilling and copper grades (plus gold). It outlines multi-year option payments and next steps to update resources, but no immediate production or supply change is announced.

title: Second fire erupts at Ford supplier Novelis' aluminum plant in Oswego, New York
summary: A second fire broke out at Novelis’ Oswego, New York aluminum plant after prior blazes that suspended operations and affected Ford output. The facility supplies automotive-grade aluminum for vehicles like the F-150. Although the latest fire is out, damage assessment is pending, raising short-term aluminium supply risk.

title: Future Made in Australia: US aluminium producer Century Aluminum complains to Donald Trump about Australian subsidies
summary: Century Aluminum, a major US aluminium producer, has urged Trump’s trade official to list Australia’s $22.7 billion “Future Made in Australia” industrial policy as a foreign trade barrier. The company argues the subsidies unfairly help Australian rivals and could shift competition in global aluminium markets, potentially affecting near-term expectations.

title: True North Copper: Is this the best copper drill hole this year?
summary: ASX-listed True North Copper highlights its most recent Queensland drilling program, featuring a standout copper drill result. The managing director discusses the achievement on the Bulls N’ Bears Report, suggesting stronger prospects for copper resources, which can modestly lift copper sentiment in the near term.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Exports Fell MoM in October, with the Thai Market Recording a 30.3% YoY Decline
summary: China’s exports of copper plate/sheet and strip in October fell 18.16% MoM to 9,776.79 mt and were 8.28% lower YoY. While exports rose to several markets, Thailand’s shipments dropped 30.3% YoY, signaling weaker outward demand momentum for copper sheet/strip products.

title: Jubilee Metals copper production soars 65% in first quarter
summary: Jubilee Metals said its copper production jumped 65% to 938 tonnes in the first quarter, helped by expansion at the Molefe open-pit mine and plants running at full capacity. Ore deliveries to Sable refinery rose to 1,122 tonnes, with further ramp-ups targeted into October and November.

title: EBRD provides €10 million to finance copper pipe production in Uzbekistan
summary: EBRD is providing up to €10 million to MaxCopper to fund working capital and ramp-up of a new copper pipe and fitting plant in Uzbekistan. The financing includes purchases of raw materials such as copper cathodes and aims to expand output for domestic HVAC use and exports, potentially boosting short-term copper demand expectations.

title: Amid Expectations of Copper Concentrate Shortages, How Are Smelters Adjusting Their Operating Strategies?
summary: SMM reports spot copper concentrate treatment charges (TCs) have stayed deeply negative into late 2025, with 2026 contract TC expected to remain negative. Concentrate tightness is worsening due to limited new supply, mine disruptions, and diversion from ramp-ups in Indonesia and Africa. Smelters respond via aggressive tenders and higher prepayments, supporting copper tightness.

title: Europe eyes copper shortage unless EU halts scrap exports
summary: European copper semi-fabricators warn they may face a critical refined-copper cathode shortage unless the EU curbs copper scrap exports. They cite surging EU scrap exports (up 31% since 2022) and refined copper shipments to the US tied to tariff expectations. Companies urge similar action to EU aluminium restrictions.

title: [SMM Analysis] Nickel Prices Trended Lower Unilaterally This Week, with Weekly Inventory Declining Slightly
summary: Nickel prices fell on both SHFE and LME as the nickel market’s surplus widened: inventories rose to near five-year highs and SHFE broke key support around 114,050 yuan/mt. Weaker rate-cut expectations, a stronger USD, and risk-off sentiment further pressured prices, outweighing some oversold signals.

title: AIP plans sale or listing of French aluminium plant, union says
summary: American Industrial Partners plans to sell or list Aluminium Dunkerque, France’s largest aluminium smelter producing about 300,000 tonnes/year. A union official links interest to the plant’s 10-year power contract with EDF, improving cost visibility. Potential offers from major firms are cited, but no deals are confirmed.

title: Questions Arise About Supply Chain Robustness After Second Fire Breaks Out At Key Aluminum Plant That Supplies Automakers
summary: A second fire broke out at Novelis’s aluminum factory in Oswego, New York, supplying automakers, after an earlier fire had already interrupted Ford pickup and SUV production. The plant said the morning fire is under control with workers evacuated, but crews remain onsite, indicating possible continued output disruption.

title: Jubilee Metals reports 65% increase in copper production
summary: Jubilee Metals reported a 65% increase in copper production. The announcement points to higher near-term mine supply, which generally raises market expectations for available copper and can weigh on copper prices in the following days or weeks, assuming no offsetting demand or export constraints are mentioned.

title: Argentina emerges as global copper hotspot after Maser Group's entry
summary: Maser Group’s CEO met Argentina’s mining minister in Abu Dhabi and the company formally committed to invest in copper mining in Mendoza. The government also offered a role in a future national mining trust and discussed value-added processing to produce refined copper for EV, renewables, and electrification demand.

title: Critical Metals Corp: CRML Secures One of the Largest Strategic Stockpiles of Ultra-High-Purity Copper Powder in a US$20M All-Share Acquisition Issued at a 40% Premium to Market
summary: Critical Metals Corp said it acquired a US$20M strategic stockpile of ultra-high-purity copper powder (99.96%) for advanced defense, aerospace, and semiconductor applications. The deal improves Western, traceable supply access currently dominated by Russia/China. The announcement may support near-term copper-related sentiment, but effects on benchmark copper likely limited.

title: Fire Strikes Novelis Aluminum Plant Again in Scriba
summary: A major fire struck Novelis’ aluminum plant in Scriba for the second time in recent months, disrupting production in the hot mill and roll shop sections. Firefighting crews worked for hours and damage assessment is pending. Given Novelis’ role supplying sheets to automakers, further delays could worsen near-term aluminum supply tightness.

title: 5-alarm fire at Novelis aluminum plant NY raises new concerns for auto industry supply chain
summary: A five-alarm fire struck Novelis’ aluminum hot mill and roll shop in Scriba/Oswego County, forcing evacuation and fire-watch operations. Damage is not yet fully assessed, and the article notes it follows a September fire that disrupted auto supply chains and sheet production. Restart timing may slip, affecting near-term aluminum sheet supply to automakers.

title: Monster faces modest tariff impact from aluminum costs
summary: Monster Beverage said US tariffs on imported aluminum for beverage cans have raised the Midwest aluminium premium and increased supplier can costs. The 50% Section 232 duty is cited as the main driver of record premiums. Monster expects only modest tariff impact on earnings, using price actions and mitigation strategies.

title: Ford reaffirms annual EBIT guidance after latest aluminum supplier fire
summary: Ford reaffirmed its annual EBIT guidance after a new fire at Novelis’ New York aluminum plant. The September blaze had already disrupted production of Ford’s aluminum-bodied trucks and led to a prior profit forecast cut. Ford paused F-150 Lightning output and expects partial offsets next year, but timelines remain unchanged.

title: Comex Copper Ends the Week 0.81% Lower at $5.0085 — Data Talk
summary: Comex Copper front-month futures for November delivery ended the week down 0.81% at $5.0085/lb. It lost 4.10 cents on the week but saw a daily bounce of 0.99% today, with the week tracking three down weeks out of four.

title: Novelis reopens after fire at Oswego aluminum plant, resumes supplying Ford Motor
summary: Novelis reopened its Oswego County aluminum plant after a five-alarm fire damaged a hot mill section, resuming cold mill and heat-treatment operations and restarting shipments to Ford. The outage had disrupted automotive supply chains, and the company is using alternate sources while rebuilding the hot mill.

title: Ford Faces Another Blow As Key Aluminum Supplier Suffers Third Fire
summary: Novelis’ Scriba, New York aluminum-sheet plant suffered another fire, its third in two months, starting in the hot mill. The facility supplies about 40% of US automotive aluminum sheets and may stay offline until next month. Automakers, including Ford, face further production delays.

title: Anti-Dumping Levy on Aluminum Profiles from China | Barnea Jaffa Lande & Co.
summary: Israeli competition authorities oppose proposed anti-dumping levies on aluminum profiles imported from China, arguing the conditions for dumping, injury, and causal link are not proven and that falling demand likely explains local damage. The dispute may affect final policy; if levies are avoided, pressure for higher aluminum-related construction costs should ease.

title: Operations resume at Novelis aluminum plant one day after third fire in two months
summary: Novelis resumed operations at its aluminum plant in Scriba after a fire on Nov. 20, following two earlier fires in September and October. The plant supplies Ford’s aluminum for F-150 pickups, and supply constraints may raise costs and reduce availability. Repeated disruption increases short-term aluminum supply risk.

title: Stolen copper wire often ends up in underground scrap market
summary: Investigators in Los Angeles say copper wire theft is surging and that stripped copper is sold through unlicensed scrapyards, then shipped overseas to be melted and reused into new copper wire, potentially returning to local markets. Authorities highlight enforcement gaps and compliance efforts by legal recyclers.

title: Imports of Unwrought Aluminum Alloy in October 2025 Plunged YoY to 76,400 mt [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s October 2025 imports of unwrought aluminum alloy fell 33.8% YoY and 7.1% MoM to 76,400 mt, while exports rose. The decline is attributed to persistent inversion of domestic/overseas aluminum alloy spreads and tighter scrap supply abroad raising prices. Imports are expected to stay low in Nov–Dec.

title: Charges laid in copper wire theft from northwest new home construction site
summary: Police charged two men for stealing copper wire from a new home construction site in Livingston, after a security company tracked the wire’s electronic device and located the suspects. The recovered wire suggests localized theft prevention, but there’s no indication of wider supply disruption affecting copper prices.

title: Motoring: Ford reaffirms annual EBIT guidance after latest aluminum supplier fire
summary: Ford reaffirmed annual EBIT guidance after another fire at Novelis’ New York aluminum plant. The September blaze previously hit Ford’s gross profit and disrupted F-150 Lightning and gas F-150 output. With Novelis restart timing still pending, renewed supply uncertainty can pressure near-term aluminium availability and prices.

title: Angola seeks investors for copper and rare earths sector
summary: Angola plans to cut administrative steps and digitize the mining permitting process to attract more non-diamond investment, targeting copper growth. It cites copper exploration agreements and an imminent start of production at its first industrial copper mine, aiming for higher copper and rare-earth contributions by 2027.

title: MMG, Anglo American to Extend Deadline on Brazilian Nickel Deal
summary: MMG and Anglo American agreed to extend the deadline for MMG’s purchase of Anglo’s Brazilian nickel business after the European Commission prolonged its competition review and escalated it to Phase II. The review could delay closing from Nov. 18 to June 30, 2026, with concerns about ferronickel supply diversion to Europe.

title: Alcoa shelves plans to explore Perth Hills for bauxite mining expansion
summary: Alcoa withdrew part of its Perth Hills bauxite exploration plans after community and stakeholder opposition focused on drinking water security and jarrah forest impacts. The company still has other mine and alumina-expansion proposals before the WA EPA, but the decision reduces near-term potential incremental bauxite/alumina supply.

title: BHP ends copper group chase, remains biggest producer
summary: BHP ended talks on a proposed merger with Anglo American after its $49 billion bid failed, leaving Anglo free to pursue a deal with Teck. While the outcome may influence expectations for copper market structure, the article mainly reiterates already-tight copper fundamentals and recent supply disruption-driven price strength.

title: Limited Commissioning of New Projects Leads to Slow Growth in Aluminum Production in 2025
summary: SMM reports China’s aluminium operating capacity growth in 2025 is limited, though production still expected to rise modestly (1.7% YoY) after resumption from technological transformations and prior cuts. Globally, several smelter restarts add capacity, but temporary outages (e.g., Iceland power/equipment failure) offset. Overall impact on prices is mixed.

title: Export Growth of Copper Enamelled Wire Slowed in October, High YoY Growth Continued
summary: China’s October 2025 exports of copper enamelled wire were 10,764.88 mt, up 10.72% YoY but down 12.11% MoM, continuing a prior decline. Cumulative exports rose 23.46% YoY, with strong growth to India and Turkey, while shipments to South Korea and Thailand fell.

title: Harmony Gold to Proceed With Eva Copper Mine Project in Australia
summary: Harmony Gold said it has made a final investment decision to proceed with its Eva copper mine in Queensland, Australia, after an updated feasibility study. The project targets about 60,000 metric tons of copper annually and expects production in 2H 2028, funded via cash and debt.

title: Harmony Gold Mining Limited Approves High-Marin, Long-Life EVA Copper Project
summary: Harmony Gold Mining approved the high-margin, long-life EVA Copper project after completing feasibility study updates and FEED. First production is estimated for 2H 2028, framed as supportive of a structural copper supply gap and higher prices. The project is expected to boost Queensland’s economy, but timing is distant.

title: The Brief Off-season and Long-term Changes in Southeast Asia's Secondary Aluminium Market
summary: SMM reports Southeast Asia secondary aluminium scrap and recycled alloy prices rose through October-November alongside LME aluminium strength, while flooding from the northeast monsoon restricted scrap trading in Thailand and Malaysia. Higher scrap costs raised ADC12 production costs, reducing purchases. Traders increasingly stockpile for 2026 CBAM/tariff-driven price expectations.

title: [SMM Analysis] 2026 Raw Material Battle: MHP Payables Under Pressure, High-Grade Nickel Matte Window Hard to Find
summary: SMM analysis argues that rising Indonesian MHP supply (and sulphur-driven cost variability) will likely loosen MHP payable indicators and weaken nickel-sulphate cost support. It highlights refined nickel oversupply suppressing prices and notes conversion to nickel sulphate may further drive expectations of a looser nickel sulphate market, pressuring nickel.

title: Gimme Credit LLC: As Penny Production Ends, Copper Bonds Show Selective Strength, Says Gimme Credit
summary: Gimme Credit says copper is entering a pivotal phase with rising long-term demand, tightening supply, and improving producer balance sheets. It highlights progress at major miners (e.g., Kansanshi/Cobre Panamá) and generally constructive credit outlooks, despite some operational setbacks and tariff-related disruptions, implying supportive near-term copper sentiment.

title: As Penny Production Ends, Copper Bonds Show Selective Strength, Says Gimme Credit
summary: Gimme Credit says the copper sector is entering a pivotal phase as U.S. retires the penny. The note cites rising long-term demand from electrification, tightening supply fundamentals, and improving producer balance sheets/refinancing progress. Despite some operational setbacks, it maintains a generally constructive view on copper.

title: France deploys drones to fight copper cable theft on railways
summary: SNCF is deploying drone surveillance to curb frequent theft of copper cables along France’s rail network. Copper thefts have been costly and disruptive, with gangs cutting and selling wiring. SNCF says drone monitoring and deterrence have helped neutralize several theft gangs since September.

title: Manufacturing - EGA marks milestone with 50mn tonnes of aluminium produced
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) said it has produced 50 million tonnes of cast aluminium since 1979 and sold 2.74 million tonnes in 2024. It also highlighted future recycling and planned new US primary capacity, but provided no immediate supply or demand disruption.

title: Harmony Gold to invest R30bn in Australia's Eva Copper
summary: Harmony Gold approved development of its Eva Copper project in Queensland, targeting average copper production of about 60,000 ounces per year and up to 100,000 tonnes of copper annually once fully commissioned. The company frames it as added exposure to copper fundamentals, but first output is expected in 2H 2028.

title: With 85 per cent done, Tanzania's copper, nickel smelting nears completion
summary: Tanzania says construction of a new nickel and copper processing and smelting plant is 85% complete and targets first production in February 2026. The government wants value-add before export and urges small miners to supply ore, aiming for a structured market and finished exports. Near-term price impact is limited by the delayed start.

title: With 85 per cent done, Tanzania's copper, nickel smelting nears completion
summary: Tanzania’s nickel and copper processing/smelting plant is reported to be 85% complete, with first production line commissioning expected in February 2026 and initial capacity to process 300 tonnes of ore per day. The government aims to add value domestically before export, creating a more reliable local supply channel for feedstock.

title: Work advances on Oman's biggest copper concentrator project
summary: Oman’s Minerals Development Oman is accelerating construction on a $270 million copper concentrator at Yanqul, built by Mazoon Mining. The 2.5 Mtpa plant will produce about 115,000 tonnes of copper concentrate annually, targeting Q1 2027 operations. Logistics and EPCM contractors are named, but near-term supply change is minimal.

title: Mining Sector Shake-Up: BHP's Retreat Paves Way for Anglo Teck Copper Giant
summary: BHP withdrew its bid for Anglo American, clearing the way for an Anglo American–Teck “merger of equals” expected to create a top-five copper producer. The deal is seen as strengthening copper market positioning and raising expectations for supply competitiveness, supporting a bullish near-term bias for copper prices.

title: Ford holds to annual outlook after second fire at aluminium supplier
summary: Ford reiterated its full-year EBIT outlook after a second fire at Novelis’ Oswego, New York aluminium plant. The earlier October incident had implied up to $2bn impact, with planned recovery via higher truck output. The latest fire on 20 November was contained and operations resumed, but mitigation relies on alternate supplies and may affect aluminium deliveries.

title: BHP's Retreat Paves Way for Anglo Teck: A New Copper Giant Emerges Amidst Mining Sector Shake-Up
summary: BHP withdrew from its pursuit of Anglo American, clearing the way for a proposed Anglo American–Teck Resources merger (“Anglo Teck”). The deal could create a top copper producer with ~1.2 Mt annual capacity. Markets will react to the Dec. 9 shareholder vote and regulatory approvals, affecting copper expectations.

title: Industrial Metals Navigate Divergent Paths Amidst Global Economic Shifts and Green Transition
summary: The piece forecasts aluminum moving toward a 2025 deficit due to China capacity constraints, recovery in demand from renewables and EVs, and US tariffs supporting domestic prices. It also expects nickel prices to face pressure from a large 2025 surplus driven by Indonesian production and softer battery-driven demand, leading to mixed metal signals.

title: Industrial Metals Navigate Divergent Paths Amidst Global Economic Shifts and Green Transition
summary: The piece forecasts aluminium trending toward a 2025 deficit, supported by China capacity constraints, recovering demand from renewables and EVs, and US steel/aluminum tariffs boosting domestic prices. It also expects nickel prices to face pressure from a large 2025 surplus driven by Indonesia and softer battery-sector demand.

title: Cloncurry copper mine set to inject $17 billion into Queensland's economy
summary: Harmony Gold has approved the Eva Copper Project in Queensland, projecting over A$17 billion in economic benefits and producing about 60,000 tonnes of copper per year over 15 years. Construction starts in late 2026 with first production targeted for late 2028. Near-term copper supply impact is limited.

title: Lion Copper and Gold Corp. Secures US$31M Milestone Funding to Advance Feasibility Study and Mine Permitting for the Yerington Copper Project
summary: Lion Copper and Gold says Nuton (a Rio Tinto subsidiary) exercised an earn-in option and will fund up to US$31M for Stage 3, advancing the Yerington, Nevada project’s definitive feasibility study, mine permitting and engineering. The work targets copper cathode production using Nuton bio-heap-leach technology.

title: Ford hit again by layoffs as a second major fire erupts at critical aluminum plant in New York state
summary: A fire at Novelis’ Oswego, New York aluminum plant shut down the hot mill, suspended shipments of finished aluminum sheet, and disrupted supply to Ford and other automakers. The facility makes about 40% of US automotive-grade specialized aluminum sheet, idling Ford plants and risking revenue while recovery delays persist.

title: American Pacific Mining announces new agreement with Vizsla Copper
summary: American Pacific Mining said it finalized a major deal with Vizsla Copper under which Vizsla will take over Alaska’s Palmer Project. In return, American Pacific receives $15 million in equity and $15 million in bonus payments. The piece is focused on corporate transactions, not near-term supply output.

title: DOE launches nickel recovery inquiry at Paducah site
summary: The U.S. Department of Energy issued an expression of interest to commercially extract about 9,700 one-ton ingots of contaminated nickel stored at the Paducah site. If pursued, the project would convert hazardous nickel into sellable commodity and help fund cleanup, potentially influencing expectations for nickel supply.

title: Adani's Kutch Copper smelter in Gujarat caught up in global ore shortage
summary: Adani’s Kutch Copper smelter in Gujarat is operating with less than a tenth of the copper concentrate it needs to reach full capacity, reflecting a broader global ore/feed squeeze. Mine disruptions and China’s rapid smelting expansion have tightened supplies and pressured treatment/refining margins, indicating potential near-term copper support.

title: Aquila prospect heats up as True North strikes copper again in QLD
summary: True North Copper reported new, high-grade intercepts at its Aquila copper-cobalt discovery in Queensland, extending mineralisation beyond 900m and refining targets for further drilling. While results are bullish for the company’s project outlook and long-run copper supply expectations, there is no immediate production impact signaled for the next few weeks.

title: US copper inventories hit all-time high amid trade uncertainty
summary: US Comex copper inventories hit an all-time high at 402,876 short tons, up sharply this year as traders stockpile amid uncertainty over potential US tariff policy. Positive LME–Comex price arbitrage keeps shipments flowing despite prior exemptions, suggesting greater short-term availability and downward pressure on copper prices.

title: Star Copper Corp.: Star Copper Advances Satellite Target Located 1.5 Km from Star Main Deposit; Arranges Non-Brokered Flow Through Private Placement
summary: Star Copper Corp. reports completion of an inaugural drill hole at the Star North satellite target, defined by a copper-in-soil anomaly and an IP chargeability high, with chalcopyrite and alteration observed but assays still pending. The company also announces a C$2.5m flow-through private placement to fund further exploration at its BC copper project.

title: Harmony approves development of Eva Copper Project in Queensland
summary: Harmony Gold approved development of its Eva Copper Project in Queensland after an updated feasibility study and board FID. The open-pit mine is forecast to produce about 60,000 tpa of copper on average (65,000 tpa in first five years) in concentrate, with major capex and construction starting later.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: SLAM Extends Strike Length of Farquharson Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Zone to 300 Meters at Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration announced an additional 100 m extension of the Farquharson copper-nickel-cobalt zone at its Goodwin project in New Brunswick, reporting a 51.2 m mineralized interval with pyrrhotite and chalcopyrite. Assays are pending, and the company is preparing geophysics for 2026 drilling.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: SLAM Extends Strike Length of Farquharson Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Zone to 300 Meters at Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration reports drilling intersected a 51.20 m interval of mineralized gabbro with pyrrhotite and chalcopyrite, extending the Farquharson copper-nickel-cobalt zone to 300 m at its Goodwin project in New Brunswick. Assays are pending and there are no immediate supply or demand shocks.

title: JW Aluminum wins against insurers after Goose Creek fire
summary: A federal jury awarded JW Aluminum $112 million after insurers denied coverage for a 2020 fire at its Goose Creek aluminum mill. Jurors found insurers breached an all-risk policy, including $32.3 million for repairs and $80 million for business-interruption losses, with possible appeal expected.

title: Canada One Mining Corp.: Canada One Provides Exploration Update at Flagship, Copper Dome Project
summary: Canada One Mining provided a Phase 2 exploration update at its Copper Dome project, reporting visible copper sulphides (bornite, chalcopyrite) and potassic alteration consistent with a potential porphyry system. Rock samples were submitted for multi-element assay, with results pending, and no production or reserve changes were announced.

title: Barrick committed to Pakistan's Reko Diq copper project, says interim CEO
summary: Reuters reports Barrick’s interim CEO says the company remains committed to Pakistan’s Reko Diq copper project despite earlier reports of possible withdrawal or asset splitting. The $7 billion mine is expected to start production by end-2028, with large planned copper output, easing near-term supply and country-risk concerns.

title: Smart Grids and EVs Fuel Massive Growth in the Copper Connector Market
summary: A market report says growth in EVs, fast-charging, and smart-grid upgrades is driving demand for copper alloy connectors, projected to nearly double over the next decade. It notes rising connector imports and mentions copper price volatility and higher mining/refining costs, framing copper demand as supportive despite supply-side uncertainty.

title: Why Aluminum Scrap Is Europe's Hottest Critical Mineral
summary: Europe is exporting record volumes of aluminum scrap, accelerated by higher U.S. tariffs on primary aluminum (scrap is exempt). Scrap shortages and idle recycling furnace capacity in Europe suggest reduced local availability. Higher demand for high-purity scrap strengthens the feedstock crunch, supportive for aluminum prices over coming weeks.

title: Indonesian coastal villages in the dark over nickel pollution
summary: Villagers near Indonesia’s Morowali IMIP nickel processing complex report severe air and water pollution and tailings-related disasters. Indonesia’s environment ministry found violations and announced administrative sanctions and fines, but locals and NGOs say enforcement and transparency remain lacking. Ongoing risks could increase near-term operational and compliance costs for nickel.

title: Barrick committed to Reko Diq copper project, says interim CEO
summary: Barrick’s interim CEO said the company remains committed to the Reko Diq copper mine in Pakistan despite reports the board discussed splitting assets, potentially including a sale. The $7bn project (with government partnership) is expected to start producing copper concentrate by end-2028, with extensive security and financing needs.

title: Copper pipe & tube exports continued to decline MoM in October, with a YoY drop of nearly 20%!
summary: China’s customs data show copper pipe & tube exports fell 18.57% YoY in October and remained weak for the year despite peak season. The decline is linked to US tariffs and slower US capacity ramp-ups, keeping fees elevated. Imports rebounded MoM but stayed low YoY, with domestic demand expected to keep declining.

title: Commodities Prices - Deutsche Bank raises 2026 copper price forecast amid supply squeeze
summary: Deutsche Bank raised its 2026 copper price forecast, pointing to a tightening supply outlook as industry consolidation accelerates and mine supply is expected to remain constrained. The update suggests improved expectations for copper market balance versus the bank’s prior view, supporting a bullish tone for copper prices.

title: Inomin Mines Inc.: Inomin Drilling Intersects 161.5 Metres Grading 0.19% Nickel, 0.011% Cobalt, 0.36% Chromium, and 22.7% Magnesium Starting 30 Metres from Surface
summary: Inomin Mines reported initial 2025 drilling at its Beaver-Lynx project, intersecting substantial near-surface polymetallic mineralization including grades around 0.19–0.20% nickel across large drill intercepts. The release also notes copper among other metals seen in prior work, but provides no production or reserve updates.

title: Buncombe County: Spike in copper, construction thefts
summary: Buncombe County authorities report a rise in breaking-and-entering cases targeting construction sites, including theft of copper and other materials. Three suspects have been charged and more investigations are ongoing. The sheriff’s office urges contractors and property managers to improve security and notes coordination with recycling businesses to track stolen copper.

title: Trafigura accuses Gupta of hiding involvement in nickel fraud scheme
summary: Trafigura’s lawyers accuse Prateek Gupta of suppressing or destroying messages tied to a fraudulent nickel trading scheme, alleging containers marketed as LME-grade nickel contained near-worthless material, causing large losses. Gupta denies involvement, claiming he followed instructions from Trafigura’s nickel desk and knew little of the details.

title: The Painful Impact of the Steel and Aluminum Tariffs
summary: The article argues that new U.S. tariffs—especially 50% duties on steel and aluminum—raise input costs for manufacturers. It says U.S. steel prices have doubled versus other markets and aluminum prices have “soared in lockstep” with the tariffs, with no exemptions or carveouts, tightening supply and lifting near-term prices.

title: Anglo American's (LON:AAL) Quellaveco Mine Reaches 1 Million Tonne Copper Output Milestone
summary: Anglo American said its Quellaveco copper mine in Peru surpassed 1 million tonnes of cumulative output and expects 2025 production of 310,000–340,000 tonnes. The company attributes performance to renewable power and automation. The milestone and guidance reinforce expectations of copper supply ramping toward steady output, amid rising demand narratives.

title: Noronex sells Witvlei Copper Project in Namibia for N$50 Million, shifts focus to core Kalahari Belt assets
summary: Noronex has agreed to sell its non-core Witvlei copper project in Namibia for about N$50 million in staged payments, including a portion tied to a 2% NSR royalty on recovered minerals. Proceeds will fund other exploration and portfolio focus, shifting resources to core Kalahari Copper Belt assets.

title: iTWire - Copper Thieves Cause Major Optus Outage, Disrupting Triple Zero Access for 14,500 Customers
summary: Optus says vandals stole and damaged copper cabling at a network site, disrupting mobile and fixed-line service for about 14,500 customers and preventing some access to emergency “Triple Zero.” Police are investigating. The piece notes a growing trend of copper scrap theft driven by rising scrap metal prices.

title: Hot Chili jags monster 529m copper, gold hit in Chile
summary: Hot Chili says it hit a 529-metre intercept at its La Verde copper-gold porphyry discovery in Chile’s Atacama, with drilling expanding the mineralised core and identifying additional targets. The company links La Verde to adding to its Costa Fuego copper inventory and improving project economics based on copper pricing assumptions.

title: Solus signs major copper foil deal with Chinese battery maker
summary: Solus Advanced Materials signed a major five-year deal to supply 20,000 tons of ultra-thin copper foil to a leading Chinese EV battery maker, likely CATL. Deliveries begin next year from its Hungarian plant, supporting EV battery output for European automakers. The news boosted Solus shares, reinforcing copper demand expectations.

title: First Diamond Drillhole Confirms Gold-Rich Major Copper Discovery in Coastal Chile
summary: Hot Chili Limited announced that its first diamond drillhole at the La Verde discovery in coastal Atacama, Chile confirmed gold-rich copper-gold mineralisation. Reported results include 529 m at 0.41% Cu, with several higher-grade intervals, and drilling continues with assays pending. This strengthens copper discovery outlook.

title: Prices of Secondary Aluminum Alloy Stop Falling and Stabilize, Supported by Both Costs and Demand[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Secondary aluminum alloy and aluminum scrap prices stabilized at high levels this week, tracking primary aluminum. Tight scrap supply (low yard inventories, difficult recycling, and a sharp import drop) plus steady casting demand and year-end auto order front-loading supported prices. Import windows remained costly and constrained, keeping sentiment firm and volatility elevated.

title: The Copper Mark and SSI sign agreement
summary: The Copper Mark and the Solar Stewardship Initiative signed an MoU to collaborate on responsible copper sourcing across the solar energy value chain, including chain-of-custody pilots from mine site to end user. The framework aims to improve transparency and ESG assurance, but it does not signal immediate supply or demand changes for copper.

title: Gupta company tried to use "friendly" inspection agency for fake nickel cargoes, Trafigura says
summary: Trafigura alleges Prateek Gupta’s team tried to use a “friendly” inspection agency for nickel cargoes, after which inspections revealed worthless material instead of LME-grade nickel. The dispute cites failed repurchases, port container buildup, and large losses, but no clear immediate supply shock.

title: NorthWest Reports Results from Two Holes at Its Kwanika Property Highlighted by 26 Metres of 0.72% Copper and 1.30 g/t Gold (1.91% CuEq) from 268 Metres
summary: NorthWest Copper reported new drill results at its Kwanika property, including an intercept of 26 metres at 0.72% copper and additional copper-gold mineralization. The company says results improve confidence in higher-grade zones for future PEA work and potential starter pit. No production or supply impacts are announced.

title: LME Aluminium Prices Hit a Three-Year High in 2025 – Overseas Views on 2026 Outlook
summary: The piece reviews 2025’s volatile rally in LME aluminium, noting prices have reached the highest since the 2022 Russia–Ukraine surge. It attributes support to tight primary supply near China’s ceiling, scrap supply pressure from CBAM and potential tariffs, and steadier demand, while expecting short-term upside.

title: Rewiring India's future - The strategic case for a cleaner, stronger copper ecosystem
summary: The article argues India’s copper demand has risen sharply while domestic refined output has fallen, leaving imports over 40%. It focuses on proposals for a “green restart” of Sterlite Copper, citing upgraded emission controls and transparency, which could restore refining supply and reduce import vulnerability, supporting copper sentiment.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Nov 28
summary: SMM reports Indonesian nickel ore prices largely stable but notes potential downward pressure for pyrometallurgical ore as early-December HMA prices are expected to weaken. Nickel pig iron (10–12% NPI) prices fell sharply, with weak end-user stainless demand. Indonesian Navy intercepted vessels shipping nickel ore, signaling tighter oversight.

title: AI data centers' massive demand for aluminum is crushing the US aluminum industry
summary: The headline argues that AI-driven data centers are generating massive demand for aluminum, overwhelming the US aluminum industry. It suggests aluminum availability and production are being strained by rapid demand growth, which would typically support higher near-term aluminum prices as buyers compete for limited supply.

title: Hot Chili announces update on La Verde copper-gold drilling in Chile
summary: Hot Chili reported an update from drilling at the La Verde copper-gold discovery in Chile, including a 529m intercept with 0.41% copper and multiple wider, higher-grade sections. The programme extends the mineralised system to about 600m depth, improving prospects for further copper mineralisation; assays for remaining holes are pending.

title: 2026 CESCO Week Copper Long-Term Contract Landscape: Potentially the Most Chaos Market in a Decade
summary: Asia Copper Week concluded without clarity on 2026 copper long-term contracts. SMM reports sharply higher cathode and concentrate premiums, wider negotiation gaps, and small-volume EQ offers, while negative TCs persist. Codelco premiums rose versus 2025 and DRC FCA offers improved. Tight availability and weak expected parity raise short-term support risk for copper.

title: Copper Market Outlook 2026: Key Predictions Ahead
summary: Fastmarkets’ webinar panelists warn 2026 copper benchmark negotiations will be “tough,” with US tariff policy seen as a key threat. They cite deeply negative treatment charges, aggressive concentrate bidding, and projected concentrate deficits, suggesting tight availability and heightened volatility likely supportive for copper prices.

title: Manufacturing - EGA leads UAE aluminium decarbonisation drive
summary: EGA, TAQA, DUBAL and EWEC signed agreements to decarbonise Abu Dhabi aluminium production. TAQA and DUBAL acquire Al Taweelah power and water assets, while EWEC purchases electricity under long-term PPAs and transmission capacity rises. EGA expects growing output of low-carbon “CelestiAL/MinimAL” aluminium, supporting supply and demand outlooks.

title: Indonesia's Newly Commissioned Project Gradually Ramps Up Production; Daily Average Aluminum Production Outside China Expected to Rise MoM Next Month
summary: SMM data show overseas aluminium production rising and December operating rates projected to fall. The Indonesia project (PT Kalimantan Aluminium Industry) is ramping up after commissioning electrolysis cells, adding capacity and diluting global operating rates. This suggests increasing near-term aluminium supply pressure despite an Iceland smelter line outage earlier in the year.

title: The Great Commodity Divide: Oil Plunges While Green Metals and Gold Soar in a Bifurcated Market
summary: The piece highlights divergence where oil falls but industrial metals rise. It says copper is leading, with aluminum and nickel also supported by supply disruptions and years of underinvestment in mining, alongside demand from electrification, grid upgrades and data centers. It forecasts continued strength into early 2026.

title: BHP dropped second attempt to buy Anglo American, but the copper takeover game isn't over
summary: BHP withdrew from a proposed cash-and-share bid for Anglo American after previously attempting to buy it with conditions. The focus of the talks was consolidating Anglo–Teck copper operations in northern Chile ahead of a Dec. 9 vote. Outcomes could shape near-term copper supply expectations, but no new capacity change is confirmed.

title: Bus crashes on way to B.C. copper mine
summary: A bus transporting workers to Taseko’s Gibraltar copper mine in B.C. crashed near the site, injuring seven people. The cause is under investigation. The incident follows a prior fatal accident at the Gibraltar mine where operations were halted pending investigation, raising near-term disruption risk for copper supply.

title: Chile's copper output, manufacturing production fall in October
summary: Chile’s copper output fell 7% year-on-year in October to 458,405 metric tons, according to INE, the statistics agency. Manufacturing production in Chile was slightly down 0.4% on a yearly basis. The report signals weaker copper supply from the world’s largest producer.

title: SPECIAL REPORT: Nickel mining threatens Mati's protected areas
summary: A Philippine nickel mining project near Pujada Bay is facing mounting local and regulatory pressure after claims of deforestation, runoff, and protected-area risks. Authorities and community groups call for suspension or closure, with formal complaints filed. The potential disruption to nickel supply elevates near-term downside risk for nickel prices.

title: Copper breaks $11,000 on LME – Shafaqna English | International Shia News & Fatwas
summary: Copper on the LME surged to new highs above $11,200, surpassing $11,000. Reuters links the rally to a declining US dollar, reduced copper output from Chile in October, and expectations of further production cuts by Chinese smelters, reinforcing near-term supply tightness and bullish sentiment.

title: Copper Thieves Are Wreaking Havoc Across America
summary: The report says copper thefts across the U.S. are surging as copper prices near record highs, prompting criminals to raid and strip communications and electrical wiring. Telecoms face outages, disruption costs, and heightened enforcement. Copper demand is tied to wiring for EVs, wind and data centers, supporting near-term copper price pressure.

title: SPECIAL REPORT: Nickel mining threatens Mati's protected areas (2)
summary: MindaNews reports local opposition to Hallmark Mining’s Pujada Nickel Project in Mati, Davao Oriental, citing threats to protected areas, environmental destruction, and concerns over under-declared output and royalties. Officials say the province is better off without mining, with plans to shift toward road and tourism. The dispute could constrain nickel supply.

title: Split in 2026 Domestic and International Copper Cathode Long-Term Contract Negotiations: Can China's Copper Cathode Export Volume Continue Its Success?[SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports 2026 long-term copper cathode contract premiums are rising in both domestic and foreign markets amid expected US tariffs. Foreign premiums are high for COMEX-deliverable brands; Chinese non-COMEX brands face narrower arbitrage. Export volumes are forecast to fall, with constraints from processing-trade handbooks and possible stricter controls.

title: Attempted copper theft halts train traffic to and from northern Netherlands
summary: An attempted copper theft near Zwolle disrupted rail traffic in northern Netherlands, halting trains between specific stations and affecting a detour route. ProRail says no copper was stolen but “considerable” damage requires repairs until mid-afternoon. Limited buses were deployed, but no broader copper supply impact is indicated.

title: Approaching the Dry Season, Power Costs Rise, Weighted Average Cost of Aluminum Expected to Increase MoM in December
summary: SMM expects China’s aluminum industry full costs to increase slightly month-on-month in December as electricity costs rise with the approaching dry season in hydropower-heavy regions. Prebaked anode costs are also projected to rise, offsetting a slight alumina cost decline. Power costs are forecast to dominate the increase.

title: Copper Holds Near Record High as Supply Fears Grip Global Market
summary: The article headline says copper is holding near record highs as supply fears grip the global market. Such concerns typically reduce expectations for near-term availability, supporting bids for copper and keeping prices elevated versus recent levels in the coming days.

title: EGA, Taqa, Dubal in deal to decarbonise UAE aluminium production
summary: EGA, Taqa and Dubal signed agreements with EWEC to decarbonise aluminium production at Al Taweelah by expanding renewable and cleaner power generation, including a new power purchase arrangement and grid interconnection capacity. The changes support future CelestiAL/MinimAL low-carbon output, but ramps begin from Q4 2025.

title: PTX Metals Inc.: PTX Metals Launches 5,000m Drill Program at W2 Copper-Nickel-PGE-Gold Project as Metallurgy, Geophysics, and Infrastructure Agreements Strengthen Outlook
summary: PTX Metals began a 5,000m diamond drilling program at its W2 Cu-Ni-PGE project in Ontario. The company aims to test and expand sulfide-hosted targets using updated geophysics and preliminary metallurgy, while also citing regional infrastructure and metallurgy progress. No production or shipment figures are provided.

title: PTX Metals Inc.: PTX Metals Launches 5,000m Drill Program at W2 Copper-Nickel-PGE-Gold Project as Metallurgy, Geophysics, and Infrastructure Agreements Strengthen Outlook
summary: PTX Metals launched a 5,000m diamond drilling program at its W2 Cu-Ni-PGE project in Ontario, aiming to delineate mineralized zones and support resource and metallurgical work. It highlights ongoing surveys, geophysics, and infrastructure progress, but provides no immediate production or supply disruptions.

title: TMC the metals company (TMC) Rockets 19% Higher as Copper Hits Record High
summary: The article headline reports TMC shares jumping 19% as copper reaches a record high. This points to strong current demand/sentiment for copper and suggests upward near-term price pressure for copper. The rest of the text shown appears unrelated cookie/consent material.

title: Section 232 Steel & Aluminum Derivative Products Inclusion Process Expands Scope Of The National Security Purpose Of Section 232 Investigations
summary: The article explains how the U.S. expanded Section 232 coverage through an inclusion process for steel and aluminum derivative products, starting in April/May 2025. It argues most additions are likely approved, increasing tariff reach on aluminum-bearing articles and thereby supporting aluminium-related pricing expectations through reduced import attractiveness.

title: Tariffs, Deals, Steel, Aluminum And AI – Oh My!  Welcome To The New Normal
summary: The piece argues that tariffs and trade measures are changing with short notice, including detailed duties assessed on steel, aluminum, and their derivatives. It focuses on customs compliance and AI tooling for classification and enforcement, but the repeated aluminum tariff updates imply higher landed costs and likely near-term downside pressure for aluminium.

title: KGHM Shares Soar as Silver and Copper Ignite a Commodity Boom
summary: KGHM shares rally sharply as silver and—most importantly for tracked metals—copper prices surge to new highs. The piece attributes strength to expectations of US rate cuts, a weaker dollar, and robust industrial demand from solar, EVs, grid modernization, AI, and data centers, implying continued bullish copper price pressure.

title: Midas starts Otavi copper drilling in Namibia amid acquisition
summary: Midas Minerals has started drilling at Namibia’s Otavi Copper Project, mobilizing diamond and RC rigs to test the T-13 deposit and Spaatzu prospect, supported by XRF screening and pending commercial assays. The work is exploration-focused ahead of acquisition completion, with no near-term production implications detailed.

title: The Red Metal Rush: Copper Market Braces for Structural Deficit Amid Green Transition and AI Boom
summary: Copper is portrayed as facing a widening structural deficit driven by rapid demand growth from EVs, renewables and AI data centers, while mine supply gains remain limited. Disruptions, low ore grades, concentrate shortages and smelter output cuts (due to weak TCRCs) are tightening physical markets, keeping prices elevated.

title: Taseko (TGB) Climbs 24% on Gold, Copper Boost
summary: Taseko Mines shares rose 24% week-on-week, attributed partly to higher gold and copper prices. The company reported copper-driven revenue, with 26 million pounds of copper sold and improved Gibraltar production and recoveries. The article does not introduce new copper supply disruptions, demand shifts, or policy changes.

title: Northern Dynasty (NAK) Jumps 28% on Copper, Gold Rush
summary: Northern Dynasty Minerals shares jumped 28% as investors bet on copper (and gold) miners. The piece cites copper rising 2.28% to about $11,189/t and notes expectations for a 25-basis-point Fed rate cut, typically weakening the dollar and supporting commodity prices, including copper.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Repays US$7.3 Million of Nebari Secured Debt, Fully Eliminating Non-Convertible Portion of Second ARCA
summary: Gunnison Copper Corp. repaid US$7.3 million of the non-convertible principal under its Nebari secured credit agreement, leaving only a smaller convertible balance. The company frames this as strengthening its balance sheet. It also reiterates plans for on-site copper cathode production, but gives no new supply or demand metrics.

title: Alumina Costs to Edge Lower in December Supported by Elevated Energy Costs
summary: SMM reports November alumina costs fell (full cost ~2,949 yuan/ton, cash ~2,779 yuan/ton). Entering December, alumina full costs are projected to slightly decline to 2,850–2,950 yuan/ton and cash costs to 2,700–2,800 yuan/ton, supported by weaker bauxite/caustic soda prices, but constrained by higher winter energy and a stronger USD.

title: Copper theft is hitting building sites, street lights – and now phones. How do we stop it?
summary: The piece describes rising copper theft driven by higher copper prices and cites state bills and tighter scrap-metal rules aimed at stopping copper theft. It also notes electricity operators are replacing thousands of kilometres of copper cabling with aluminium due to theft costs. These factors can dampen copper demand expectations short term.

title: AGL continues talks with Tomago Aluminium on energy supply | Gloucester Advocate
summary: AGL says it continues discussions with Tomago Aluminium over energy supply as governments negotiate a plan to keep the Tomago smelter open beyond 2028. A long-term energy contract currently runs to end-2028, and an announcement is expected this month. New adjacent battery and power upgrades support supply reliability.

title: AGL continues talks with Tomago Aluminium on energy supply | Newcastle Herald
summary: AGL says it continues talks with Tomago Aluminium to secure the smelter’s energy needs beyond current supply arrangements ending in 2028. With governments negotiating a plan to keep the plant operating past 2028, the discussions reduce closure risk and support expectations for aluminium output.

title: Vale Base Metals and Glencore Canada agree to evaluate development of Sudbury copper deposits
summary: Vale Base Metals and Glencore Canada agreed to evaluate a brownfield copper development at Sudbury Basin properties using existing Glencore underground infrastructure. The project is proposed to produce about 880 kt of copper over 21 years, with final investment decision expected in 1H 2027 and engineering/permitting in 2026. Nickel would also be produced as part of polymetallic output.

title: DPM Metals Announces Inferred Mineral Resource Estimates of 2.6 Million Gold Ounces and 1.9 Billion Pounds of Copper at the Rakita Camp
summary: DPM Metals announced inferred mineral resource estimates at the Rakita camp in eastern Serbia, including 1.9 billion pounds of contained copper at ~1.02% grade across several prospects. Metallurgical testwork suggests recoverable copper concentrates, but the results are Inferred resources with no near-term production, limiting immediate copper price effects.

title: Copper Scrap Supply Increase + Demand Adjustment Keep Blister Copper RCs Rising [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports blister copper refining RCs rising MoM in both south and north China, with imports also higher. The rebound is attributed to copper price strength widening the primary–scrap spread, encouraging more scrap-derived anode output, partly offset by smelter maintenance and later-year inventory control. Overall, copper supply/demand loosening is expected.

title: Hot Topics in International Trade - December 2025 -  Section 232 Steel & Aluminum Derivative Products Inclusion Process Expands Scope of the National Security Purpose of Section 232 Investigations | Braumiller Law Group, PLLC
summary: The article explains how the U.S. implemented an expanded Section 232 inclusions process for steel and aluminum derivative articles. BIS began accepting requests in May 2025 and is likely to add more aluminum derivative HTS codes to the tariff scope. Broader tariff coverage can reduce import competition and support aluminum prices.

title: Copper Hits Record High; Goldman Warns A "Circular Melt-Up" Is Now Driving Global Market
summary: Copper futures on the LME and Comex surged to record highs as traders rush supplies into the U.S. ahead of potential import tariffs. The article attributes the move to a “circular melt-up” where tighter global stocks and LME backwardation intensify the U.S. arbitrage, draining inventories and raising prices further.

title: DPM Metals Unearths "Tier One" Gold and Copper Bonanza at Rakita Camp, Reshaping Precious Metals Landscape
summary: DPM Metals announced inferred resources at Serbia’s Rakita Camp of 1.9 billion pounds of copper and 2.6 million ounces of gold. The copper addition is important for future supply expectations, but with first concentrate targeted for 2029 it is unlikely to materially move near-term copper prices over days to weeks.

title: Copper is the new oil
summary: The piece forecasts copper prices rising sharply, driven by rapidly expanding AI data-center power infrastructure and broader energy-transition grid buildout. It claims refined supply growth is insufficient, with 2026 balance flipping to a sizable deficit, while mine grade decline, long development times, and recent disruptions constrain supply.

title: Vale Base Metals and Glencore Canada to evaluate copper project in Sudbury Basin
summary: Vale Base Metals and Glencore Canada agreed to jointly evaluate a brownfield copper project in Ontario’s Sudbury Basin. The plan would use existing shaft and infrastructure at Glencore’s Nickel Rim South Mine to access nearby copper deposits. Engineering and permitting are expected next year, with a final investment decision in 1H 2027.

title: Vale, Glencore to study $2-billion Sudbury copper joint venture
summary: Vale and Glencore are studying a framework for a potential $2-billion copper joint venture in Sudbury, using infrastructure at Glencore’s Nickel Rim South Mine. The plan could produce substantial copper over decades, but engineering and final investment are not until 2027, implying limited immediate supply impact.

title: Foreign imports threaten Trump's 50% aluminum tariff
summary: The piece argues Trump’s 50% aluminum tariff is being undercut by importers using undervaluation and mislabeling to pay duties only on raw material rather than the full value of manufactured aluminum articles. It calls for enforcing the tariff based on weight to protect domestic aluminum jobs, implying reduced imports.

title: Aluminum Market Navigates Volatility as China's Output Concerns Meet Mixed Industrial Demand
summary: Aluminium prices are volatile but supported by supply tightening tied to China: output is near its capacity cap, export tax rebates were removed to cut shipments, and SHFE inventories are falling. The piece notes mixed industrial demand and some short-term easing, yet expects firm-to-rising prices from structural constraints.

title: Copper's Descent: A Stronger Dollar and Faltering Demand Drag Down the Red Metal
summary: Copper prices are under downward pressure, driven by a stronger U.S. dollar that raises costs for overseas buyers and a weak global demand outlook. The article also highlights U.S. tariff actions on semi-finished copper products as a key catalyst for turbulence and near-term selling.

title: AGL continues talks with Tomago Aluminium on energy supply | Dungog Chronicle
summary: AGL says it is still in discussions with Tomago Aluminium over its energy supply, as governments negotiate a plan to keep the Tomago smelter open beyond 2028. Tomago previously flagged potential closure without an economically sustainable long-term power contract. An energy battery project near the plant is also progressing.

title: 50% Copper Tariffs Have Tennessee Small Business on Edge
summary: A Tennessee manufacturer says 50% tariffs on semi-finished copper shipments have made some imports too costly, delaying or rejecting bonded copper deliveries. The firm expects it will eventually pass higher costs through to customers, but warns the tariff burden could force closures if sustained.

title: Vale, Glencore agree to $2B joint venture copper project
summary: Vale and Glencore agreed on a framework for a $1.6–$2.0 billion brownfield copper project in the Sudbury Basin using Glencore’s existing infrastructure, targeting 880 kt of copper over 21 years. The work is set for 2026 with a final investment decision in 2027, implying limited immediate near-term supply impact.

title: Haib Copper Project, Namibia
summary: Koryx Copper’s Haib project in Namibia advanced to a PEA stage, outlining 23 years of potential production (about 92 ktpa payable copper in early years), with ongoing ESIA work toward environmental clearance in early 2026. The update is mainly longer-term supply planning, not a near-term disruption.

title: Growing Scrap Supply and Softening Demand Push  Blister Copper RCs Higher [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports blister copper treatment/ refining return (RCs) in China rose MoM in November, supported by a wider primary–scrap price spread after copper prices rallied. Scrap-derived anode output increased as smelters took more secondary feed, while some anode maintenance tempered demand. December expected to stay high on supply but softer demand.

title: Vale and Glencore consider joint venture to mine copper in Canada
summary: Vale says it is in advanced discussions with Glencore to form a copper-focused joint venture in Canada’s Sudbury basin, targeting ~900,000 tonnes of copper over 21 years. Investment is estimated at $1.6–$2bn with a decision expected in H1 2027. Nickel is mentioned via Vale’s broader base-metals strategy.

title: Copper declinesfrom historic high, on dollar's strength and market caution
summary: Copper fell from an all-time peak on the LME, down 0.8% as a stronger dollar and risk-off caution weighed on dollar-priced commodities. Other base metals also declined, including aluminium and nickel. The retreat is viewed as temporary, with supply-squeeze worries and copper support above $11,000.

title: Raw Materials: Chile raises its forecasts for copper prices
summary: Chile raised its copper price forecasts for this year and next, attributing the revision to supply disruptions and lower interest rates. In London, three-month copper delivery stabilized near $10,777. Price upside is limited by a strong US dollar and weak Chinese demand.

title: Camino Minerals Corp: Nittetsu Mining Provides Final $1.5 Million Earn-in Payment for Camino's Los Chapitos Copper Project in Peru
summary: Camino Minerals says it received the final CAD$1.5 million earn-in payment from Nittetsu Mining for the Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, completing expenditure requirements. The project will convert to a joint venture, with drilling continuing on high-grade copper targets. The news also notes a finder's fee via share issuance.

title: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.: Ivanhoe Mines Announces Kamoa-Kakula Copper Production Guidance for 2026 and 2027 as Recovery Plan Advances
summary: Ivanhoe Mines updated Kamoa-Kakula guidance: Kakula dewatering is progressing (Stage 2 ~60–70% complete) enabling higher-grade mining; 2026 copper production is guided at 380,000–420,000 tonnes and 2027 at 500,000–540,000 tonnes. With smelter ramping and destocking of unsold concentrate, 2026 copper sales are expected to exceed production.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces Strategy to Advance Van Dyke Copper Project to PFS Stage
summary: Copper Fox announced plans to advance its 100% owned Van Dyke in-situ copper recovery project to the PFS stage, updating the prior PEA with new technical studies, permitting activities, and revised cost/economic models. The company cites USGS critical mineral designation and demand tailwinds but provides no near-term production update.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: SLAM Reports Copper, Nickel and Cobalt Assays and Extends Farquharson Zone Strike Length to 360 Meters at Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration announced assay results from its Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt project in New Brunswick, including copper-equivalent intercepts and an extension of the Farquharson Zone strike length. The company is still drilling and planning further geophysical work; no production or inventory changes are reported.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: SLAM Reports Copper, Nickel and Cobalt Assays and Extends Farquharson Zone Strike Length to 360 Meters at Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration reported early 2025 drilling results from its Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt project, extending the Farquharson Zone to 360 meters and highlighting copper-equivalent grades. As copper/nickel prices are used to compute Cu Eq, the news is relevant but remains exploratory with no production or resource update.

title: Nittetsu Mining Provides Final $1.5 Million Earn-in Payment for Camino's Los Chapitos Copper Project in Peru
summary: Camino Minerals reports receiving the final CAD$1.5 million earn-in payment from Nittetsu for the Los Chapitos copper project in Peru, after completing current drilling and converting the project into a joint venture. The news describes ongoing exploration drilling but no immediate production or supply impacts.

title: Glencore Restructures Operations in Bet on Copper Production -- Update
summary: Glencore restructured operations to bet on rising copper demand, targeting about 1.6 million tons of annual copper capacity by 2035 and setting a higher capex plan through 2028. It cut 2026 midpoint guidance to 840,000 tons due to Collahuasi issues but plans to restart Alumbrera in late 2026, with production starting in 2028.

title: Global Supply Woes Push Copper Past $11,400 Per Ton
summary: Copper surged above $11,400/ton as supply tightness worsened. The article cites mine accidents in Chile and Indonesia reducing output, rising South Korea and Taiwan orders, and record LME warehouse withdrawal requests. Traders also positioned for future deficits amid tariff uncertainty, boosting demand for physical copper.

title: Futures Rise As Bitcoin Extends Rally For 2nd Day, Copper Hits Record
summary: US equity futures rise and markets watch macro data, but commodities highlight copper. Copper reached a fresh record above $11,350/ton after the largest surge in orders since 2013. The demand impulse is likely to reinforce expectations for tighter near-term copper fundamentals.

title: Copper Continues to Surge – Now Above $11,500
summary: Copper prices continued climbing to new record highs, topping $11,500 per ton, up about 3.5% on the day. The rally was attributed to a weaker dollar and supply concerns. Analysts at JP Morgan, cited via Bloomberg, expect copper could reach about $12,500 in early next year.

title: Hot Topics in International Trade - December 2025 -  Tariffs, Deals, Steel, Aluminum and AI – Oh My!  Welcome to the New Normal | Braumiller Law Group, PLLC
summary: The piece describes frequent changes to US tariffs and trade deals with short notice, including detailed duties on steel and aluminum derivatives. It explains how customs brokers and CBP must rapidly update classifications and enforcement. These measures can increase landed costs for aluminium imports in the near term.

title: Copper Smashes Records as Supply Fears Intensify Amidst LME Withdrawal Surge
summary: Copper surged to record highs as supply fears intensified: LME inventories fell sharply, warehouse withdrawals increased, and cash premiums widened alongside mine disruptions, lower output guidance, and coordinated Chinese smelter reductions. It also cites potential aluminium substitution in some power applications, but the dominant driver is tight copper physical supply.

title: Glencore Tapped by Codelco for Landmark Chilean Copper Smelter Amidst Surging Global Demand
summary: Codelco said it selected Glencore to lead a new 1.5 million tpy copper-concentrate smelter in Chile’s Antofagasta region, with concentrate supply up to 800,000 tpy. The project is not expected to start until 2032–33, but the announcement coincided with a new copper price record and bullish market sentiment.

title: Copper theft causing problems with Telus infrastructure
summary: TELUS reports a 39% year-over-year increase in copper cable thefts, including multiple incidents in Wetaskiwin over recent weeks causing outages and risking 911 and internet services. TELUS and CPKC cite widespread theft/damage to copper lines, with repairs often lengthy, and call for tighter enforcement.

title: Recycled Aluminum Market Set for $91 Billion Boom by 2032
summary: Recycled aluminum demand is rising as energy costs keep primary smelting expensive and EU/automotive policies push higher recycled content. Producers including Novelis and Hydro are expanding recycling capacity, while China’s primary smelting cap increases reliance on scrap. These factors support aluminium market sentiment and likely near-term price strength.

title: Copper theft causing problems with Telus infrastructure | Drayton Valley Western Review
summary: TELUS and RCMP report a sharp year-over-year increase in copper cable theft in Alberta, causing outages and public-safety risks. Repairs are prolonged and thieves also damage fibre lines. While this reflects disruption in local copper cable supply, the article provides no market-scale volume effects.

title: LME Copper Hits Another Record; Goldman Trader Pinpoints Driver Behind Move
summary: LME copper futures reached another record as requests to withdraw metal from London Metal Exchange warehouses surged sharply—the biggest increase since 2013. Withdrawals were driven mainly by Taiwan and South Korea, indicating copper being pulled toward China rather than the Comex system, tightening near-term LME availability.

title: Copper theft causing problems with Telus infrastructure | Fort Saskatchewan Record
summary: TELUS and CPKC report rising copper cable thefts in Alberta, with outages affecting wireline voice, internet and potentially 911 service. Incidents increased year over year and require extensive repairs. The thefts target copper lines and can also damage generators and other cables, raising replacement and security costs.

title: CME : Gold and Copper futures rallied on rate hopes and supply.
summary: Gold rose on weaker labor data and increasing expectations for a December Fed rate cut, aided by central bank buying and a weaker dollar. Copper futures also rallied sharply, attributed to supply tightness, while silver moved higher in sympathy. The report frames these as near-term market moves.

title: Copper hits record high in London
summary: London LME copper surged to record highs as a weaker dollar and tight on-warrant availability drove prices higher. The LME showed large net warehouse cancellations in Asia, pushing stocks to the lowest since July. Supply worries were reinforced by Glencore cutting 2026 copper guidance, alongside gains in other metals.

title: Grijalva introduces bill to repeal Oak Flat land swap and block copper mine
summary: A U.S. bill would repeal the Oak Flat land swap and halt Rio Tinto and BHP’s Resolution Copper project in Arizona. The mine is estimated to produce up to 40 billion pounds of copper over four decades. Pending lawsuits and legislative action raise near-term copper supply risk.

title: Prospect Resources Identifies New High-Grade Copper Zone at Mumbezhi Project in Zambia
summary: Prospect Resources reported new high-grade copper intercepts at its Mumbezhi project in Zambia, including 34m at 0.88% copper and other supporting results at Nyungu Central, plus metallurgical assay updates at Kabikupa. Assays remain pending for additional holes. Results are framed to support future resource updates.

title: Chinese Mining Stocks Rise as Copper Futures Surge to Record
summary: Chinese mining shares rose as copper futures hit record highs. The rally reflects mounting supply concerns, mine disruptions prompting producers to cut forecasts, and traders increasing U.S. shipments ahead of potential copper-related tariffs. Expectations of a December Fed rate cut also supported copper demand, lifting sentiment for copper-linked miners.

title: Rio Tinto lifts 2025 copper production forecast
summary: Reuters reports Rio Tinto lifted its 2025 copper production forecast, citing a ramp-up at the Oyu Tolgoi project in Mongolia. It now expects 2025 output of 860,000–875,000 tonnes versus the prior 780,000–850,000 range. The company also guided 2026 copper production of 800,000–870,000 tonnes.

title: Rio Tinto's Nuton technology produces first copper
summary: Rio Tinto says its Nuton bioleaching technology has produced the first copper cathode at the Johnson Camp mine in Arizona, using microorganisms to leach primary sulphide ore without conventional concentration or smelting. The company targets ~30,000 tonnes over a four-year demonstration and highlights cleaner, lower-water, lower-carbon copper.

title: Rio Tinto lifts 2025 copper production forecast on Oyu Tolgoi ramp-up
summary: Rio Tinto outlined a strategy day and lifted its 2025 copper production forecast, citing stepped-up operations at Oyu Tolgoi in Mongolia. It now expects 2025 copper output of 860,000–875,000 tons versus 780,000–850,000 previously, supporting a bullish sentiment for copper demand/supply balance.

title: Metso Secures Major Order for Australian Copper Project
