summary: Harmony selected Metso to supply key equipment and analytical solutions for the Eva Copper project in Queensland, valued at about €55m, alongside a multi-year support contract. The news signals ongoing investment and development momentum for copper supply, but it is unlikely to materially shift near-term copper price expectations.

title: Rio Tinto?s Nuton Technology Produces First Copper
summary: Rio Tinto says its Nuton Technology produced the first copper cathode from the Johnson Camp mine in Arizona via on-site bioleaching. The project will supply a heap leach pad technology package aimed at about 30,000 tonnes of refined copper over four years, with engagement of U.S. customers to support the domestic copper supply chain.

title: Glencore to raise global copper production by 2035
summary: Glencore said it expects to expand copper output long-term, but short-term guidance has been cut. It lowered 2026 copper production to 810,000–870,000t and kept 2025 at the lower end after operational and ore-grade issues. Collahuasi output fell in July–September due to lower grades.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Market: Operating Rates Improved MoM in November, High Copper Prices Constrained Production Increases in December
summary: SMM reports copper plate/sheet and strip operating rates improved in November on a phased copper price pullback and downstream order release, with finished inventories slightly lower. December year-end production plans face resistance as copper hit new highs, and aluminium substitution demand increased, shrinking some cable shielding strip orders.

title: Rio Tinto sees profit boost from cost cuts, asset sales, copper growth
summary: Rio Tinto outlined productivity and capital discipline plans alongside upgraded 2025 copper production guidance (860–875 kt) and lower unit cost guidance, implying improved supply outlook and margins. The company also targets aluminium & lithium as core businesses and expects higher output from its ramp-ups, supporting both copper and aluminium sentiment.

title: Codelco, signs MoU with Glencore for Chile copper smelter project in Antofagasta
summary: Codelco and Glencore signed a MoU to develop a copper smelter in Antofagasta, with Codelco supplying up to 800,000 tpa of concentrate for at least ten years. The project needs pre-feasibility and major permitting, with operations only expected in 2032-33, implying limited near-term price pressure.

title: Rio Tinto advances Nuton copper processing technology at Johnson Camp mine
summary: Rio Tinto says it produced the first copper cathode from Arizona’s Johnson Camp mine using its Nuton bioleaching technology, with a technology package aimed at ~30,000 tonnes of refined copper over four years. Nuton improves recovery from difficult sulphide ores and is positioned to strengthen US domestic copper supply.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Announces That Rio Tinto's Nuton Technology Produces First Copper
summary: Gunnison Copper announced that Rio Tinto’s Nuton bioleaching technology produced first copper cathode from the Johnson Camp mine in Arizona. The project will deploy a modular heap-leach/bioreactor package aimed at ~30,000 tonnes of refined copper over four years, with cleaner water and carbon metrics.

title: Gainers & Losers: HindustanCopper, Indigo among 6 stocks that grabbed eyeballs on Thursday
summary: Indian shares ended higher after a rupee slide boosted IT stocks, but Hindustan Copper gained 7.8% after it said it signed an MoU with NML to jointly bid for copper/critical-minerals block auctions and develop exploration, mining and processing. The news is a copper supply-positive signal.

title: Western Copper and Gold Corporation: Western Copper and Gold Partners with Little Salmon Carmacks First Nation to Support School and Daycare Meal Programs
summary: Western Copper and Gold will contribute $75,000 to Little Salmon Carmacks First Nation to support school and daycare meal and nutrition programs in Carmacks amid uncertainty from changes to federal funding. The release also reiterates advancement of its Yukon copper-gold Casino Project, but provides no production or supply-impact details.

title: Year-end consumption weakened coupled with high aluminum price suppression, the operating rate of aluminum processors came under pressure and pulled back to 61.9% ——SMM Aluminum Processing Weekly Survey
summary: SMM’s survey shows China’s aluminum downstream operating rate falling WoW (to 61.9% overall; plate/sheet 65.0%; wire/cable 62.4%; extrusion 52.0%). High aluminum prices above 22,000 yuan/mt suppress spot orders and year-end stockpiling, while environmental restrictions curb output, keeping demand weak into December.

title: Copper giant Freeport's CEO won't count on mergers for growth
summary: Freeport-McMoRan CEO Kathleen Quirk said the company is not counting on mergers and acquisitions for growth, instead expecting to grow its U.S. business through internal, organic expansion by up to 50% over five years. No immediate production or supply changes were announced.

title: Goldman Warns Copper's Parabolic Breakout Lacks Stability
summary: LME copper futures opened the week with a breakout to record highs, driven by US warehouse buying ahead of potential tariffs and strong Asia demand tied to power and AI buildouts. However, Goldman warns the parabolic move above $11,000/ton lacks stability and may not persist due to stretched speculative length and limited near-term tightness.

title: Policy Watch and Off-Season Demand Intertwine in Secondary Copper Rod Market: Weak Close in November, Fluctuating at Lows in December
summary: Secondary copper rod operating rates stayed low amid policy uncertainty and weak wire/cable and appliance demand. As copper prices rebounded, downstream restocking faded. Rising public-warehouse inventory and active physical-futures arbitrage tied up resources, creating hidden supply pressure. Profitability fell and transactions showed “rising prices but thin volume,” suggesting bearish near-term tone for copper.

title: Aftermath Silver Ltd.: Aftermath Silver Berenguela Silver-Copper-Manganese Project: Contained Silver in Measured and Indicated Resources Increases by 21% to 122.5 Moz, with 22.0 Moz of Silver in Inferred Resources
summary: Aftermath Silver reported a new NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate for its Berenguela silver-copper-manganese project in Peru. Measured and Indicated resources increased, including copper to 717.1 Mlb (with additional inferred copper). The release is resource-focused with no production timeline changes.

title: Copper producer Freeport would pursue M&A only if 'stars and moon' align, CEO says
summary: Freeport-McMoRan’s CEO said the company would only pursue acquisitions if “stars and the moon” align, while focusing on organic growth and new in-situ leaching technology. She also urged U.S. incentives as current copper tariffs help Chile/Peru. Grasberg output should largely recover next year.

title: Elemental Royalty Corporation: Elemental Executes Option Agreement to Sell the Hachita Porphyry Copper-Gold Project
summary: Elemental Royalty announced an option agreement with First Quantum to explore the Hachita porphyry copper-gold project in New Mexico, with staged payments and work commitments over five years. Elemental would receive a 3% NSR and milestone/annual advanced royalty payments upon earn-in, subject to further exploration and study milestones.

title: Copperbelt Energy to raise funds for African expansion
summary: Copperbelt Energy, which supplies electricity to Glencore Xstrata and Vedanta in Zambia, plans to raise about US$150mn via development loans and a smaller rights offer to expand operations in Africa and refinance debt. Funding could support power availability for copper mining, but near-term price impact is unclear.

title: Askari Metals Secures Strategic Funding to Launch Maiden Drilling at Nejo Copper-Gold Project
summary: Askari Metals secured A$1.15m to fund maiden drilling at its Nejo copper-gold project in Ethiopia, allocating ~A$800k for a 3,000–5,000m program targeting copper and gold prospects. It also plans further copper exploration at the Katta target using geophysics and historical datasets. Impact on copper prices is likely limited.

title: SMM Weekly Survey: Aluminum Processing Industry Strained by Off-Season and High Aluminum Prices, with Structural Divergence Persisting
summary: SMM reports falling operating rates across aluminum downstream processing: primary alloy steady but spot demand cautious; wire/cable, extrusion, and plate/sheet lower on weak orders and winter/off-season conditions. Aluminum prices surged above 22,000 yuan/mt, and environmental restrictions in Henan re-emerged, constraining production and deliveries.

title: Policy Uncertainty and Off-season Suppress Secondary Copper Rod Market in November, with Downturn Lingering into December
summary: Secondary copper rod operating rates in November fell and remained pressured by weak end-demand, copper price rebounds that reduced buying interest, and policy uncertainty dampening production in key areas. Arbitrage between physical copper and futures increased, lifting warehouse inventories and creating hidden supply pressure, keeping volume thin despite slightly higher price centers.

title: [SMM Analysis] Nickel prices were in the doldrums this week, with domestic inventory increasing slightly.
summary: SMM reports SHFE nickel moving sideways after failing to hold a brief 118,000 yuan/mt push, closing near 117,790 yuan/mt. LME nickel ranged roughly $14,700-$14,900/mt. Spot prices and premiums rose modestly, but downstream demand stayed weak and inventories were mixed (domestic buildup, LME still high). Prices expected to remain range-bound.

title: Sulphuric Acid Rises Sharply to Boost Costs, Aluminum Fluoride Prices Increase by 250-300 Yuan/MT in December [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports aluminum fluoride prices jumped 250–300 yuan/mt in early December after downstream aluminium enterprise tender prices were finalized at 10,200–10,300 yuan/mt. The increase is mainly cost-driven by rising sulfuric acid prices, while fluorite fell, slightly easing profitability pressure. Demand remains mediocre, keeping procurement weak.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Dec 5
summary: SMM’s Indonesia nickel market review shows domestic nickel ore benchmarks and some delivered laterite prices falling, while NPI prices (10–12% grade) eased week-on-week. Upstream smelters/traders supported prices amid contract talks, but stainless demand is weak with production cuts, limiting upside momentum. Premiums provide some support; near-term declines are restrained.

title: Copper Hits Fresh Record on Fears of Global Supply Squeeze -- Commodities Roundup
summary: Copper prices hit fresh record highs as traders feared a global refined supply squeeze. The article cites U.S. inventory stockpiling, continued pull of refined copper into the U.S., and a large withdrawal from LME warehouses earlier in the week, alongside optimism for upcoming Fed rate cuts.

title: Thai national arrested in Japan for massive solar farm copper theft
summary: Japanese police arrested a Thai national linked to 248 copper wire thefts from solar farms in Ibaraki and Chiba prefectures between May 2022 and March this year. Damage was estimated at about 310 million yen. Copper wire was cut from sites and sold to scrap dealers, prompting the investigation’s conclusion.

title: Copper hits record high, heads for weekly jump
summary: Copper jumped to a record high, with LME three-month prices up about 1.5% and earlier near 2.2%. Citi raised its copper outlook, expecting prices to keep climbing on soft-landing positioning, a weaker dollar, and a widening supply shortage. Analysts said funds are increasingly buying amid developing deficits.

title: Why are copper prices soaring?
summary: Copper prices are rising sharply due to a tightening supply-demand balance. Supply has been reduced by disruptions at Indonesia’s Grasberg mine and operational issues at a major Chilean mine. Demand is increasing from AI-driven electricity use and electrification, with concerns that production will lag demand.

title: Gold, Silver Hit New Weekend Records as Copper Market 'Fractures'
summary: Copper is trading at fresh LME record highs amid a “tug of war” between bullish and cautious views. The piece cites tariff uncertainty leading to physical stockpiling and a major drawdown of LME inventories, tightening balances. Investors also debate whether elevated inventories elsewhere offset the squeeze.

title: Ndayishimiye Courts U.S. Company Lifezone Metals to Invest in Burundi's Nickel Reserves
summary: Burundi’s President met Lifezone Metals to discuss expanding investment in the country’s mineral sector, focusing on large-scale nickel extraction. Burundi is estimated to hold about 6% of global known nickel reserves, particularly the Musongati laterite deposit. The government stressed transparency and local value creation amid rising nickel demand for batteries.

title: Aluminum Scrap | Argus Webinar
summary: Argus hosted a webinar on its newly launched US aluminium scrap price assessments for key auto scrap grades (baled clips). It states primary aluminium prices in the US have risen to record highs and that supply constraints, tariffs, and disruptions are increasing volatility in the automotive aluminium supply chain.

title: Copper's Unprecedented Ascent: Citigroup's Bullish Call and the Green Revolution Fuel Record Run
summary: Copper prices are hitting record levels, helped by Citigroup’s bullish forecasts and the energy-transition demand narrative. The article cites tightening supply from disruptions in Chile and Peru, declining ore grades, delayed projects, and inventory buildup ahead of tariffs, supporting expectations for an extended market deficit and further price strength.

title: EU risks slow demise of aluminium industry if carbon tax not scrapped, Constellium CEO says
summary: Constellium CEO warns the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) could inflate costs for aluminium consumers and raise European physical premiums to a 10-month high. While not immediate, he argues the higher premiums could pressure competitiveness and eventually lead to gradual capacity decline in Europe.

title: Codelco signs MoU with Glencore for Chile copper smelter project in Antofagasta
summary: Codelco signed a memorandum of understanding with Glencore for a copper smelter project in Antofagasta, Chile. The announcement is connected to copper refining capacity and treatment of concentrates, but being an MoU and likely longer-dated, it is unlikely to drive immediate spot-price pressure.

title: 10 Best Copper Stocks to Buy Right Now - Insider Monkey
summary: The piece says copper prices have been rising to record highs due to supply fears: mine output is lagging and tariff expectations are prompting large shipments to the US, potentially draining inventories. It cites JP Morgan’s view of a refined copper deficit ahead, supporting further near-term strength.

title: A Global Copper Crunch Is Looming
summary: IEA expects a major copper deficit to emerge as demand rises, warning supply is hard to scale quickly due to declining ore grades, higher costs, and long project timelines. The International Copper Study Group also cut its 2026 refined copper outlook to a deficit, reflecting slower production growth.

title: Enamelled Wire: Marginal Improvement in November Demand Supports a Weak Recovery, Record-High Copper Prices Hinder the Rebound in December Operating Rates
summary: SMM reports enamelled wire operating rates rose in November but are expected to only edge up in December. The rebound was supported by a copper-price pullback and improving downstream acceptance, while record-high copper prices around 91,000 yuan/mt and weaker end-use orders are cited as limiting further recovery.

title: KAIST unveils cause of performance degradation in electric vehicle high-nickel batteries
summary: KAIST researchers found that the electrolyte additive succinonitrile (CN4), used to improve battery stability, excessively bonds to nickel ions on high-nickel cathodes. This disrupts the protective electrical double layer and accelerates cathode damage and nickel migration, worsening battery degradation and motivating new additives.

title: Strong Demand Across Multiple Sectors Sustains High Prosperity in China's Copper Foil Industry [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says China’s copper foil enterprises’ operating rate rose to 86.3% in November, the seventh straight monthly increase, and is expected to climb to 87.78% in December. Shipments were up MoM, particularly lithium battery and electronic circuit foil, supported by EV/ESS and electronics demand.

title: Derailment closes Australian fertilizer and copper line
summary: A derailment in Australia has closed the Mount Isa rail line, with trains suspended until repairs are completed. Freight carrying zinc and copper concentrates from Glencore’s Mount Isa operations is being held, and spillage was limited. The shutdown follows prior weather closures and may disrupt near-term copper concentrate flows to port.

title: Koryx to Launch First Zambian Drilling in 2026 as Copper Prices Climb
summary: Koryx Copper said it will start its first drilling programs in Zambia in 2026 at Luanshya West and Mpongwe, supporting Zambia’s broader push to triple copper output. The update comes as copper prices have risen sharply earlier in the year, reinforcing positive market sentiment around copper.

title: Weda Bay rejects allegations of nickel smuggling through private airport - Companies
summary: Weda Bay Industrial Park (IWIP) rejected claims of nickel smuggling through its private airport in North Maluku. The firm said the shipments were permitted alumina samples sent to Jakarta for lab testing, detained temporarily due to missing documents. No seizures or investigations occurred, and samples remain under aviation security supervision.

title: Copper and molybdenum concentrate production in Armenia drop over 10-month period
summary: Armenia’s statistical committee reported that copper concentrate production fell 9.1% to 235,036.6 tons in January–October 2025 versus the same period in 2024. Molybdenum concentrate declined 14.1%, while zinc concentrate rose. The report does not indicate immediate policy or export changes.

title: Multiple Factors Constrain, Operating Rate of Secondary Aluminum Alloy Expected to Slightly Decline in December [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM survey data shows secondary aluminum alloy operating rates rose in November but are constrained by tight aluminum scrap supply, high procurement costs, and cautious operations amid regional policy uncertainties. In December, stable demand may be offset by lower winter dismantling volumes and reduced imports, keeping scrap tight. A slight rate decline is expected.

title: Alba signs two-year deal with Gulf Aluminium Rolling Mill Company
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) signed a two-year collaboration with Bahrain’s GARMCO to second technical staff for hands-on training at Alba’s facilities, focused on hydraulic and pneumatic systems. The deal is aimed at workforce development and knowledge sharing rather than changing aluminium production or trade flows.

title: Glencore Copper Output Forecast Decreases for 2026
summary: Glencore lowered its 2026 copper production forecast to about 840,000 tonnes from 930,000 planned, citing ongoing challenges at Chile’s Collahuasi mine, including lower grades and inadequate water. The expected tighter concentrate supply and supply concerns are supportive for near-term copper prices.

title: Rio Tinto Copper Output Increase at Oyu Tolgoi
summary: Rio Tinto increased its 2025 copper output target to 860,000–875,000 tonnes after Oyu Tolgoi ramp-up from completed underground development. The revision lowers projected cash costs and follows higher 2024 output. Production guidance implies improved near-term supply visibility, which can pressure copper prices.

title: Mercuria's African Copper Initiative with Gecamines
summary: Mercuria formed a joint venture with DRC state miner Gecamines, backed by the US DFC, to market copper (and cobalt) from Congolese mines with transparent benchmark-based pricing. The deal includes logistics, market access, and pre-financing/offtake funding. It should improve Gecamines’ control over sales rather than signal a near-term supply disruption.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Announces Rodren Drilling has Commenced Drilling at the Kenbridge Nickel Copper Cobalt Project, Sioux Narrows, Northwestern, Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. said drilling has started at its 100%-owned Kenbridge nickel-copper-cobalt project in Ontario. The program aims to convert resources, test extensions of nickel-copper sulphide zones, and gather data for engineering and development studies. It is an exploration milestone with no production figures or immediate supply change.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Announces Rodren Drilling has Commenced Drilling at the Kenbridge Nickel Copper Cobalt Project, Sioux Narrows, Northwestern, Ontario
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. says drilling has commenced at its Kenbridge nickel-copper-cobalt project in Ontario. The program aims to convert resources, test potential extensions of high-grade nickel-copper sulphide zones, and gather technical data for future engineering and development studies. No results or production changes are reported.

title: Gungnir Resources Inc.: Gungnir Resources' Lappvattnet Nickel Project Designated a Property of National Interest in Sweden
summary: Gungnir Resources said Sweden’s Geological Survey (SGU) designated its Lappvattnet nickel project as a “Property of National Interest,” offering protection from competing land uses and potentially easing future permitting. The release details nickel resources at Lappvattnet and Rormyrberget but provides no near-term production impact.

title: Aluminium deficit will support prices in 2026
summary: ING expects aluminium to remain in deficit in 2026, supporting prices. China’s output is near its 45 mt capacity cap, limiting net exports, while outages and power-contract difficulties constrain restarts abroad. US inventories are very low after tariff-driven destocking, reinforcing tightness. Faster Indonesian ramp-ups are the main downside risk.

title: How to play further gains in copper using options on this mining stock
summary: CNBC Pro discusses trading further gains in copper, arguing that easy monetary policy and regime risk support demand for hard assets. It highlights copper’s strong YTD performance and key industrial uses (wiring, transmission, motors, and computer chips/servers). It suggests copper miner Southern Copper options as leveraged exposure.

title: Global Copper Shortage Risk Grows as Citi Projects Prices Above $13,000 a Ton
summary: Citigroup forecasts copper prices above $13,000/ton by Q2 2026, citing supply cuts and tariff-driven stockpiling. Record LME prices near $11,620 accompany disruptions at major mines (DR Congo, Indonesia, Chile) and slower global supply growth, supporting a bullish near-term copper market despite some policy and timing risks.

title: Copper May Exceed $12,000 per Ton in 2026
summary: LME three-month copper rose to a record, with further gains linked to Chinese calls for stronger domestic demand for 2026. Price pressure also reflects supply issues at major mines, including Grasberg’s accident and force majeure, plus rising U.S. inventories and import expectations around potential refined copper tariffs.

title: What Retiring Copper Phone Lines Means
summary: The article says telecom providers, with FCC approval, are moving away from legacy copper phone lines toward fiber-to-home, VoIP, and cellular. It highlights faster, more reliable service and concerns from older adults who rely on landlines for 911 and health monitoring, especially in rural areas.

title: BIS Steel & Aluminum Derivative Decision Pushed to 2026
summary: BIS will issue its decision in 2026 on nearly 100 requests to expand U.S. Section 232 national security tariffs to additional steel and aluminum derivative products. The decision was previously expected within 60 days, but multiple deadlines were missed, citing prior approvals and EU trade discussions. Near-term aluminium price impact appears uncertain.

title: Break-Out For Capstone Copper Shares
summary: The piece provides a technical outlook for Capstone Copper Corp. shares, arguing the stock has broken out of consolidation and may trend higher. It also comments on Australian GDP and inflation concerns, but offers no concrete copper fundamentals (production, inventories, pricing). Impact on copper prices is indirect and limited.

title: Rio2 transforms into dual producer with Peru copper mine deal
summary: Rio2 agreed to acquire Peru’s Condestable underground copper mine for US$217 million, instantly adding copper production (27,000 tonnes copper equivalent/year) and expected cash flow. The company plans possible throughput expansion using renewable hydro power. While it increases a copper supply storyline, the deal is not likely to move near-term copper prices materially.

title: Kodiak Copper Corp.: Kodiak Reaches Key Milestone with Initial Mineral Resource Estimate at the MPD Copper-Gold Project
summary: Kodiak Copper reported an initial mineral resource estimate for its MPD copper-gold project in southern British Columbia, totaling 82.9 Mt indicated and 356.3 Mt inferred resources at ~0.39% and 0.32% CuEq (cut-off 0.2% CuEq). The release outlines future drilling and metallurgical work in 2026.

title: Teck Resources, Anglo American shareholders to vote on deal to create copper giant
summary: Anglo American and Teck shareholders overwhelmingly approved their “merger of equals,” paving the way to form Anglo Teck, a top-five global copper miner with over 70% exposure to copper. The deal still faces Investment Canada Act review and some South African resistance, but approval may bolster copper supply expectations.

title: Solis secures drilling permits for Cinto copper project in southern Peru
summary: Solis Minerals said it has received drilling permits from Peru’s Ministry of Energy & Mines for its fully owned Cinto copper project and will begin a diamond drilling campaign after rig mobilisation this month. The project is near major Peruvian copper operations, but remains exploration with no near-term output disclosed.

title: Teck, Anglo shareholders to vote on deal to create copper giant
summary: Anglo American and Teck shareholders have overwhelmingly approved their merger plan to form Anglo Teck, a major copper miner with over 70% exposure to copper. The deal is still subject to Investment Canada Act review. Resistance in South Africa is noted, but votes indicate broad support for the copper-focused consolidation.

title: Copper Smelters and the Supply Gap Challenge
summary: Copper industry speakers at the Resourcing Tomorrow conference highlighted deeply negative treatment charges expected through Q1–Q2 2026, persistent supply-gap concerns, and policies restricting US copper scrap exports to China. Smelters outlined efficiency and recycling initiatives, while Fastmarkets reported the cif Asia-Pacific concentrate TC index edging lower.

title: Maxus Mining Announces Positive Results from 2025 Exploration Program at Penny Copper Project in British Columbia
summary: Maxus Mining reported positive 2025 exploration results at its Penny Copper Project in British Columbia, including confirmed copper anomalism from soil sampling and a rock sample assaying 0.34% Cu. The update is mainly geophysical and sampling-focused, with no production or near-term supply change indicated.

title: Brazil's Aluminium Market Faces Increased Competition
summary: Fastmarkets reports intensified competition in Brazil’s primary aluminium billet market as wider domestic supply and more imports enter amid stable demand. High interest rates are slowing construction, reducing billet demand pace. The CIF billet premium fell through 2025, while near-term market momentum is expected to soften further, limiting upside.

title: The Rising Costs of Zambia's Copper Boom
summary: A major spill of 1.5 million tons of acidic mine waste into Zambia’s Kafue River has triggered contamination warnings, NGO demands for stricter enforcement, and references to suspensions/continued operations by implicated mining firms. These incidents and potential legal/regulatory responses add near-term supply risk for Zambia’s copper output, despite stated production ramp-up plans.

title: GARMCO signs up as Sustainability Forum Middle East partner
summary: Sustainability Forum Middle East announced GARMCO as a 2026 Forum Partner. The piece highlights the company’s “Green Initiative,” including recycling and energy-efficient production, plus a clean-energy deal to build a 6 MW solar power project at its Bahrain facilities, supporting decarbonization and potentially easing aluminium production economics.

title: Cloncurry's future: Harmony Gold's Eva Copper project | The North West Star
summary: Harmony’s Eva Copper project (a $2.3–2.6bn mine) is expected to produce about 60,000 tonnes of copper annually. The piece focuses on community incentives and local commitments in Cloncurry, including jobs and power/water arrangements, but the major takeaway is confidence in a significant new copper supply pipeline.

title: Wash Spot Laundromat Lucas hit by copper pipe theft twice | The Courier
summary: A laundromat in Lucas had copper piping stolen twice, costing about $2,000 each time and delaying opening. Police say copper theft is widespread and targets infrastructure, with criminals selling stolen copper to scrap dealers. Authorities link theft activity to rising copper prices, adding support for copper sentiment.

title: Wash Spot Laundromat Lucas hit by copper pipe theft twice | The Advocate - Hepburn
summary: A Lucas laundromat in Victoria says copper piping was stolen twice, costing about $2,000 each time and delaying opening. Police urge reporting as copper theft damages infrastructure and drives costs for businesses, and investigators note higher copper prices can increase theft activity for scrap.

title: Commodities: Copper gets its rally too
summary: Copper prices jumped to a new LME record around $11,635/ton, attributed to a weaker dollar and lower output in Chile, the leading producer. The piece frames this as an ongoing rally, implying near-term bullish price pressure from improved sentiment and tighter supply expectations.

title: Argentina: Mendoza Province Senate approves copper mining project amid intense protests
summary: Mendoza’s provincial senate approved the Environmental Impact Statement for the PSJ Cobre Mendocino copper project near Uspallata, despite major protests about potential water contamination and flaws in the study. The decision also included related environmental and royalty measures, potentially improving the project’s chances to proceed and lift copper supply expectations.

title: Aluminium Import Duties in Mexico: Previewing Possible Upcoming Changes
summary: Mexico’s Chamber of Deputies and Senate approved reforms to its General Import and Export Tax Law that change aluminium tariff schedules. Duties on some primary aluminium HS codes are removed, while new levies are added for various aluminium bars, wires and structures (often around 35%). Implementation is set for 2026, affecting trade flows.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc and Freeport Continue Expanding High Grade Aurora Copper-Gold-Silver Deposit
summary: Amarc and Freeport report additional 2025 drill results from the AuRORA Cu-Au-Ag deposit, extending mineralization north, east and southeast. Assays include intervals with ~0.27–0.44% Cu over significant lengths. The company frames the results as expansion potential for a future porphyry copper-gold district.

title: Copper Resumes Gains Back Toward Record on Tight Supply Outlook
summary: Copper prices are described as resuming gains and moving back toward record highs on a tight supply outlook. The framing suggests improving near-term market balance for copper—supporting physical availability expectations and bid strength—making an upside price reaction likely over the next days to several weeks.

title: Fluor Awarded Engineering, Procurement and Integrated Construction Management Services Contract for Teck Resource's Highland Valley Copper Mine Life Extension Project
summary: Fluor was awarded engineering, procurement and construction management services for Teck’s Highland Valley Copper mine life extension near Logan Lake, Canada. The brownfield project includes plant and processing upgrades and is scheduled to begin immediately, extending mine operations from 2028 to 2046 and supporting copper supply prospects.

title: Solis Minerals Ltd.: Solis Announces Drilling to Commence at Cinto Copper Project
summary: Solis Minerals announced that Peru has granted drilling permits for its Cinto Copper Project, enabling a maiden diamond drilling campaign targeting IP and geochemical anomalies. The article cites high-grade surface channel assays and proximity to Toquepala and Quellaveco, but it remains exploration-focused with no production impact.

title: Cloncurry's future: Harmony Gold's Eva Copper project | North Queensland Register
summary: Harmony Gold’s Eva Copper project near Cloncurry is being pitched to secure local incentives and commitments. The mine is forecast to produce about 60,000 tonnes of copper per year and create substantial jobs. Council seeks local housing and shared power/water infrastructure, while Harmony outlines community investment frameworks.

title: Three people before the courts following copper thefts, Waikato
summary: New Zealand Police report arrests of three people over commercial burglaries targeting reels of copper in Waikato, with more than 200 kilograms allegedly stolen and on-sold in Auckland. The police describe multiple break-ins and security warnings. The report is largely a local crime update with limited market-wide copper price impact.

title: Auckland.Scoop » Three People Before The Courts Following Copper Thefts, Waikato
summary: New Zealand Police report arrests of three people after commercial burglaries targeting reels of copper in Waikato. Investigators say over 200 kilograms of copper was allegedly stolen and subsequently on-sold in Auckland. The police press release focuses on security and reporting, with no broader supply or trade disruption noted.

title: Three People Before The Courts Following Copper Thefts, Waikato
summary: Waikato Police arrested three people tied to commercial burglaries targeting copper reels. Investigators say over 200 kg of stolen copper was allegedly on-sold in Auckland after multiple break-ins in August 2025. Charges relate to burglary, and police stress security measures; the theft appears localized rather than market-moving.

title: Waikato trio accused of copper thefts
summary: Police in Waikato arrested three people accused of burglary after investigations into recurring copper thefts. Raids followed reports of a commercial property being targeted and about 200kg of stolen copper reportedly resold in Auckland. The piece notes broader thefts from infrastructure but provides no price impact.

title: A copper-paved  road to the promised land
summary: Glencore outlined $14bn–$24bn of new copper investment and targets rising output, while confirming 2026 production would be lower than previously forecast. The company links growth to a steady copper price trend amid supply-tightness expectations, but analysts cite execution risk and limited medium-term targets.

title: Norfolk confirms shallow copper in Chile
summary: Norfolk Metals reports standout shallow copper intercepts at its Carmen project in Chile’s Huasco Province, including 53m at 1.1% Cu and higher-grade zones within the oxide and emerging sulphide mineralisation. The results underpin follow-up drilling and potential future resource upgrades, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Rudi's View: Copper, Aluminium & Technology (!)
summary: The piece is investment-strategy commentary, not a discrete supply event, but it references broker upgrades to base-metal outlooks and a more constructive stance. It highlights copper exposure as having strong fundamentals and notes Citi is most bullish on copper and aluminium, supporting near-term bullish sentiment.

title: Aluminium Import Tariffs in Mexico: Previewing Upcoming Changes
summary: Mexico’s legislature approved reforms to its import and export tax law that will change aluminium import duties starting in 2026. Tariffs on some primary aluminium HS codes are removed, while many downstream product codes face new duties (often 35%, with some at 5%). This reshapes trade flows with China, the US and others.

title: La Verde copper drilling confirms large, near-surface core
summary: Hot Chili says phase-two drilling at its La Verde copper-gold discovery in Chile confirmed a larger, higher-grade core near the surface. Assays from DKP005D show additional copper-gold mineralisation, with other holes visually confirming wide, continuous porphyry copper. Remaining assays are pending for six holes.

title: Cost Support and Weakening Marginal Demand Intertwined, ADC12 Price Fluctuates at Highs in the Short Term[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Weekly review shows aluminum scrap tracking primary aluminum with prices near highs. Tight imported and domestic scrap supply and continued cost support underpin ADC12, while environmental-protection production restrictions in regions like Chongqing/Henan reduce alloy operating rates and curb downstream procurement. Result: ADC12 likely remains in a high, highly volatile trading range.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: Slam Drills 74.80 meter Copper, Nickel Cobalt Core Interval at Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration announced a 74.80m drill core interval at its Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt project, grading 0.96% copper equivalent, and noted the Farquharson zone remains open for extension. The release outlines upcoming geophysical EM work for future drilling, supporting incremental bullish sentiment for copper/nickel.

title: SLAM Exploration Ltd.: Slam Drills 74.80 meter Copper, Nickel Cobalt Core Interval at Goodwin
summary: SLAM Exploration announced a 74.80 m core interval grading 0.96% copper equivalent from the Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt project in New Brunswick, extending the Farquharson zone to 360 m strike length. The company plans further geophysical surveys for 2026 drilling; the update is primarily sentiment-level for copper and nickel.

title: Orogen Royalties Inc: Orogen Royalties Notes Initial Resource Estimate on Kodiak Copper's MPD Copper-Gold Project
summary: Orogen Royalties highlights Kodiak Copper’s initial Mineral Resource Estimate for the MPD copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia. The MRE includes substantial copper contained resources (including within Orogen’s NSR royalty area). While not production, the update can modestly lift near-term copper sentiment.

title: BHP Group: Mining marvels and copper dreams
summary: The piece discusses BHP’s recent output, noting copper production up 4% to 494 kt and frames company performance as sensitive to commodity price swings. It also describes decarbonization and other projects (potash, power network) without any aluminium-specific developments that would likely move metal prices immediately.

title: Orogen Royalties Notes Initial Resource Estimate on Kodiak Copper's MPD Copper-Gold Project
summary: Orogen Royalties notes Kodiak Copper’s initial Mineral Resource Estimate for the MPD copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia, including copper ounces attributable to Orogen’s royalty area. The release provides resource quantities and grades but does not indicate near-term production changes, limiting immediate copper price impact.

title: New all-aluminum solar carport from France
summary: Gamme Telco, part of Mitjavila, launched the Electra Design 3 all-aluminum solar carport for residential and commercial use. The structure fits nearly all standard PV modules without special panels and includes concealed wiring and rainwater management. The announcement suggests incremental aluminium demand but provides no volume data, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Argentina aims to mine more than 1 million tons of copper in 10 years
summary: Argentina’s government incentives under the RIGI mining regime are reviving copper project development after years of near-zero production. The planned restart of Glencore’s Alumbrera and progress toward approvals for other large mines could lift future copper supply prospects. Improved regulatory clarity supports bullish sentiment for copper prices.

title: Three people before the courts following copper thefts, Waikato | infonews.co.nz New Zealand News
summary: Waikato Police arrested three people for commercial burglaries targeting and stealing reels of copper in Frankton. The investigation links the thefts to an alleged resale in Auckland, involving more than 200 kilograms of copper. No broader production or market-wide disruptions are cited; it’s a law-enforcement update.

title: Challenges of demand & supply in copper – Shafaqna English | International Shia News & Fatwas
summary: Copper demand is described as rising, driven by clean technologies and growing data-center electricity/AI activity. However, supply is portrayed as uncertain due to recent production setbacks and delays or challenges in developing new mines or expanding existing ones. Bloomberg frames the tension as a potential support for copper prices.

title: TSX hits another record high as gold, copper prices climb
summary: Reuters reports Canada’s TSX rose to a fresh record as upbeat domestic data and improving trade figures lifted investor sentiment. It notes the materials sector advanced sharply “as gold and copper prices climbed,” signaling supportive market expectations for copper over the near term.

title: The Overnight Report: Copper & Silver New Highs
summary: The Overnight Report says copper hit another new high. It links the move to a softer monetary outlook after the Fed cut rates and raised its US growth forecast, boosting expected demand. It also notes traders’ concerns about supply being diverted into the US around a potential tariff on refined metal.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | The Singleton Argus
summary: The PM says federal and NSW governments are finalising a multibillion-dollar support deal to keep the energy-intensive Tomago Aluminium smelter operating beyond 2028. The plan includes a long-term Snowy Hydro-linked power purchasing arrangement for competitive electricity, helping protect jobs and sustain output of about 600,000 tonnes annually.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | Newcastle Herald
summary: Australia’s PM says talks are finalising a multibillion-dollar scheme to secure Tomago Aluminium’s future beyond 2028 via long-term power purchasing with Snowy Hydro. The smelter requires continuous electricity; guarantees on pricing and renewables/storage are expected to keep production around 600,000 tonnes annually.

title: Tomago Aluminium Smelter: Deal secures 1000+ jobs beyond 2028
summary: Australia’s PM says a rescue deal is being negotiated to keep the Tomago aluminium smelter operating beyond 2028 by securing a 10-year power purchasing agreement with discounted electricity. It addresses the planned doubling of energy costs, supports jobs, and aims to keep production internationally competitive.

title: BC Hydro reveals how thieves are getting to valuable copper
summary: BC Hydro says copper theft from maintenance holes has surged, with cables described as essential for underground electricity between circuits and substations. It reports dozens of cases since January 2024 and estimates costly repairs. The incidents are tied to copper cable value on the scrap market and raise safety risks.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Australia’s PM says federal and NSW talks with Tomago Aluminium are advancing to finalize a multibillion-dollar, 10-year energy deal via Snowy Hydro to keep the Tomago smelter operating beyond 2028. The plant needs large, stable power, and the agreement aims to secure affordable renewable electricity and storage.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | Gloucester Advocate
summary: Australia’s PM said governments are finalising a multibillion-dollar deal to secure the Tomago Aluminium smelter’s future beyond 2028 by underwriting renewable generation, storage and transmission via a Snowy Hydro scheme. The plan aims for competitively priced electricity, keeping output running and supporting regional jobs and supply.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | The Advertiser - Cessnock
summary: Australia’s PM says governments and Tomago Aluminium are finalising a multibillion-dollar scheme-backed power deal with Snowy Hydro to keep the energy-intensive Tomago smelter running beyond 2028. The agreement would underwrite renewable generation, storage and transmission at a competitive electricity price, protecting output and jobs.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | Port Stephens Examiner
summary: Australia’s PM says federal and NSW talks with Tomago Aluminium are advancing to finalise a multibillion-dollar, 10-year energy deal via Snowy Hydro to underwrite renewable generation and storage. The move aims to keep the Hunter smelter operating beyond 2028 by securing affordable, stable electricity.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | Camden Haven Courier
summary: Australia’s PM says governments are finalising a multibillion-dollar arrangement to keep the Tomago aluminium smelter running beyond 2028. The deal underwrites renewable generation and storage for long-term, competitively priced power, addressing Tomago’s inability to secure a sustainable electricity contract and reducing supply disruption risk.

title: Government deal to ensure Tomago Aluminium smelter remains open beyond 2028
summary: The federal government is finalising a deal to keep the Tomago Aluminium smelter open beyond 2028 after the firm warned rising energy prices would make operations unviable. A long-term power purchase agreement is being negotiated to lower electricity costs. The outcome is expected to support Australia’s aluminium output and jobs.

title: Anthony Albanese confirms deal to keep major aluminium smelter open
summary: Australia’s federal government agreed to keep Rio Tinto’s Tomago aluminium smelter operating by funding cheaper power amid spiralling energy costs. The deal secures over 1,000 jobs and stabilizes output from the plant producing a large share of Australia’s aluminium, reducing short-term supply disruption risk.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | Muswellbrook Chronicle
summary: Prime Minister Albanese says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium’s future are moving forward, finalising a multibillion-dollar energy deal to keep the smelter open beyond 2028. The project targets long-term renewable power and storage via Snowy Hydro, protecting output and thousands of jobs.

title: Tomago aluminium smelter: Rio Tinto to keep smelter open with Snowy Hydro deal
summary: Rio Tinto agreed to keep its troubled Tomago aluminium smelter running after a Commonwealth-backed deal would provide subsidised electricity from Snowy Hydro and other renewables, firmed by gas. The arrangement reduces the likelihood of near-term shutdowns, supporting aluminium supply expectations and near-term sentiment.

title: Resources funds: Precious metals and copper price surge fuels massive returns
summary: Resources-focused funds reported major gains, citing a sharp rise in copper and precious metals. Terra Capital’s Natural Resources Fund doubled investors’ money after riding rallies in gold, copper and “critical minerals” stocks. The piece frames optimism for a renewed, longer commodity boom, implying supportive copper sentiment.

title: Australia unveils rescue bid for Rio Tinto's Tomago aluminium smelter
summary: Australia has unveiled a rescue bid for Rio Tinto’s Tomago aluminium smelter, signaling efforts to avert potential shutdown or prolonged disruption. By supporting production and containing near-term supply risk, the move is likely to be supportive for aluminium prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | The Scone Advocate
summary: Australia’s PM says talks to secure a multibillion-dollar energy deal for the Tomago Aluminium smelter are progressing, aiming to keep the plant operating beyond 2028. The energy-intensive facility would receive long-term power via a Snowy Hydro-linked structure, improving input cost certainty and reducing shutdown risk.

title: PM says talks to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter's future are moving forward | The Maitland Mercury
summary: Australia’s PM says talks to secure a multibillion-dollar energy deal for Tomago Aluminium are moving forward, aiming to keep the Hunter smelter operating beyond 2028. The scheme would underwrite renewable generation and storage for about 10 years, protecting output and industrial jobs and supporting electricity affordability.

title: Copper edges past silver to take gold
summary: Prospects for additional stimulus from China lifted Shanghai copper futures to a record high, putting industrial metals in focus. A weaker U.S. dollar after the Fed rate cut also supported real-asset trades. Broader risk sentiment was positive in Asia, reinforcing a near-term bullish bias for copper.

title: Rushed replacements for copper cable theft could be non-compliant
summary: South Africa’s infrastructure is hit by copper cable theft, with Eskom reporting hundreds of transformer failures from vandalism and illegal connections. SOEW warns emergency repairs rely on cheap, non-compliant Chinese cable imports, potentially worsening blackouts and raising calls for anti-dumping and enforcement, with stolen copper often sold to foreign buyers.

title: Copper Theft Ring Arrested | Fukuoka Now
summary: Fukuoka Prefectural Police arrested five Vietnamese trainees suspected of breaking into scrap yards across Kyushu and Yamaguchi and stealing about 41 tons of copper and copper wire in 22 incidents from June 2024 to January 2025. Police cited earlier theft of 3.3 tons in Tagawa City and questioned a social-media-linked network.

title: Tomago: More than 1000 jobs saved after government strikes deal to sustain largest aluminium smelter
summary: Australia’s federal and NSW governments struck a deal to keep Rio Tinto’s Tomago aluminium smelter operating beyond 2028 by securing clean energy and energy price guarantees after the coal power contract ends. This avoids likely closure and preserves supply, supporting aluminium market expectations in the near term.

title: Albanese government strikes deal to keep Rio Tinto's Tomago aluminium smelter open, saving more than 1200 jobs
summary: The Albanese government agreed to underwrite a power deal from Snowy Hydro to keep Rio Tinto’s Tomago aluminium smelter open long-term despite high electricity costs. The agreement reduces risk of closure after 2028, supporting ongoing production from Australia’s largest aluminium smelter.

title: Government reveals taxpayer-funded deal to keep Australia's largest aluminium smelter open. How long we will pay?
summary: Australia’s federal government announced a taxpayer-funded electricity supply deal to keep Rio Tinto’s Tomago aluminium smelter operating beyond 2028, citing high energy costs for aluminium. The subsidy via Snowy Hydro and renewables aims to prevent closure, but details on long-term competitiveness and risks remain uncertain.

title: Jiangxi Copper raises takeover bid for SolGold to $1.13 billion
summary: Jiangxi Copper increased its takeover offer for SolGold to value the copper-gold miner at about $1.13 billion, citing a global race for copper assets. The bid covers the Cascabel project in Ecuador and would require Chinese outbound approval. Despite the higher offer, SolGold shares fell amid deal skepticism.

title: More than 1000 aluminium jobs saved
summary: Australia’s government stepped in with a deal that saved more than 1,000 jobs at the country’s biggest aluminium smelter. By averting operational disruption and potential capacity loss, the news is supportive of near-term aluminium supply expectations, which can underpin aluminium pricing over the next few weeks.

title: In December, home appliances remained sluggish, dragging down the operating rate of copper pipe & tube.
summary: SMM data shows copper pipe & tube enterprise operating rates rebounded MoM in November/expected higher in December, but remain sharply lower YoY. The slowdown is attributed to weaker air-conditioner production schedules, high end-October copper prices limiting OEM scheduling, and unsatisfactory exports amid US tariff hikes. With no export improvement, rates are seen unlikely to rise.

title: EU aluminium and cement imports to face higher emissions costs, draft shows
summary: EU draft plans would tighten the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), raising expected CO2-related costs for certain imports, including unwrought aluminium. From 2026, benchmark emissions for aluminium would be set at 1.423 tCO2 per ton, increasing charges under default values for major suppliers and pressuring import demand.

title: Gold, Silver Soar to Record Highs, Copper Hits All-Time Peak as Federal Reserve Cuts Rates
summary: Following the Fed’s December 10 rate cut and dovish easing stance, copper prices in LME/three-month futures hit record highs, alongside a weaker US dollar and improved growth expectations. The piece also cites robust demand tied to the energy transition and supply disruption risks from Chile and Peru.

title: Australia, NSW plan to secure Tomago Aluminium smelter beyond 2028
summary: Australia and NSW plan to secure Tomago Aluminium’s smelter beyond 2028 by arranging reliable, competitively priced power through a long-term fixed-price PPA and concessional financing for renewables and storage. Tomago’s 590,000 tpa capacity faces electricity contract expiry, so the move reduces supply and cost uncertainty.

title: How tight supply, AI demand propelled copper towards $12,000
summary: Copper is nearing $12,000/ton as investors expect soaring data-centre/AI-driven demand colliding with tight global supply. The piece cites mining disruptions, production cuts, surging exchange warehouse stocks toward historically low availability, and tariff-related US trading flows, reinforcing a large market deficit forecast for 2025–2026.

title: Thieves steal about $470,000 of copper wire from R.I. highways
summary: Rhode Island DOT says thieves stole about $470,000 worth of copper wire used for highway and street lighting, cutting power to some locations. Officials are investigating and planning anti-theft covers. The incident highlights copper being diverted to scrap, but the scale is unlikely to materially move copper prices.

title: Copper explodes towards US$12,000 on AI
summary: Copper prices are nearing $12,000 as investors expect AI- and data-center-driven demand growth while supply remains tight. Exchange stocks are sharply lower, with miners’ guidance cut and warehouse inventories rising. U.S.-focused flows reflect tariff-related pricing dynamics despite partial tariff exemptions, reinforcing bullish sentiment.

title: Copper and Gold: Which Commodity is the Better Investment Heading into 2026?
summary: HSBC analysts project copper may face a structural deficit in 2025-26, driven by demand growth from renewables, green investment and EVs. They also point to supply disruptions and negative mine revisions, including accidents at Freeport’s Grasberg and a Codelco mine, reducing supply growth expectations.

title: Official Launch of the Winning Consortium Alumina Guinea (WCAG) Alumina Refinery Project 2025
summary: Guinea’s government officially launched construction of the WCAG alumina refinery in Dobali, Boké Prefecture. The planned 1.2 million tonnes/year facility, backed by over USD 1.2 billion investment, aims to move the country downstream into the aluminium value chain by producing alumina rather than exporting only bauxite.

title: Idled mill at Novelis plant reveals critical weakness in aluminum supply chain
summary: Two fires in September and November idled the Novelis hot mill at its Oswego plant, reducing production of aluminum sheet used heavily by automakers like Ford. With limited domestic automotive aluminum excess capacity, Novelis must rely on overseas output, facing a 50% import tariff and higher air-freight costs, tightening supply.

title: Secondary Copper Market Amid Soaring Copper Prices: Tight Supply-Demand Balance and Intensified Regional Divergence at Year-End
summary: Domestic secondary copper prices rose to record highs amid tight recycled-copper supply and “price rise but thin volume.” Traders held inventories and procured only after receiving delivery orders. Secondary rod operating rates improved but remain low. Regional invoice quota shortages tightened working capital, likely keeping copper prices supported into year-end despite weaker trading.

title: Latest Copper Concentrate Supply-Demand Balance Results: Annual Contract Negotiation Outcomes Imminent [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM estimates the global copper concentrate market ends this year with a ~170,000 mt deficit, improved from a prior 530,000 mt outlook, and expects the deficit to widen next year. Year-end BM negotiations for 2025 are progressing better, likely settling around $0 to -$5/t, supporting copper sentiment.

title: China's 2025 Copper Concentrate Imports Show Significant Increase in Inland Mining [SMM Analysis]
summary: China imported 2.526 million dmt of copper concentrate in November (+3% m/m, +12.5% y/y), with imports January–November up 8% y/y. Growth is driven by Mongolia and Russia, while Indonesia’s Grasberg accident reduces output. Tariffs reduce US-origin demand; a Kaz Minerals safety incident reduces shipments to China.

title: Fortescue to Take Full Control of US$101 Million Copper Miner Alta
summary: Fortescue agreed to buy the remaining 64% of Alta Copper for about US$101 million, paying C$1.40 per Alta share. Alta’s Canariaco Copper Project in Northern Peru is the key asset. Fortescue expects to close in Q1 2026, supporting its critical minerals strategy.

title: Opposition wants 'transparency' around the details of Tomago Aluminium deal
summary: Australia’s government is finalising a deal to keep the Tomago Aluminium smelter operating in New South Wales. This follows the company saying in October it struggled to see operations as commercially viable beyond 2028. The announcement precedes a gas-market review expected within weeks, relevant to smelter costs and supply.

title: Taruga Minerals to Acquire High-Grade Gold and Copper Projects in Papua New Guinea
summary: Taruga Minerals entered a 12-month option to acquire two projects in Papua New Guinea, including the Kol Mountain copper/gold porphyry prospects. The company plans drilling and modern geophysics and will fund activity via a $1.5m placement. No operational disruption or near-term supply change is indicated.

title: Fortescue (FMG ASX) to acquire Alta Copper's Canariaco copper project in Peru for $151.7 million
summary: Fortescue will pay $151.7 million to acquire Alta Copper’s undeveloped Canariaco project in Peru, subject to Alta shareholders’ approval on Jan. 26. The deal follows years of local community opposition. The transaction may influence expectations for future copper project development and sentiment.

title: China aluminium production up 2.5 % to 3.79 million metric tons in Nov - stats bureau
summary: Reuters reports China’s aluminium production rose 2.5% year-on-year to 3.79 million tonnes in November, and output for nonferrous metals including copper and nickel increased as well. Higher aluminium supply from China’s dominant producer can pressure nearby aluminium prices as markets anticipate greater availability.

title: Copper prices could hit new highs as traders rush metal into the U.S.
summary: CNBC reports copper hitting record highs as traders hoard refined copper into the U.S. amid worries of future tariffs, boosting U.S. inflows and tightening supply outside the U.S. LME inventories are lower and more stocks are tied up in canceled warrants. Mine disruptions and downgraded 2026 output forecasts add to the deficit outlook.

title: SolGold Board Backs Sweetened $1.13 Billion Takeover Bid From Jiangxi Copper
summary: Jiangxi Copper has secured SolGold board support for a revised $1.13 billion takeover bid, increasing the offer price to 28 pence per share. SolGold specializes in gold and copper mining. Shareholders representing nearly 41% plan to back the deal, tightening copper-related supply expectations.

title: JV Partner Sought for Kalahari Copper Belt | Company Announcement
summary: Kavango Resources says it is evaluating strategic options, including seeking a JV partner, for its Kalahari Copper Belt interests in Botswana. The portfolio is on-strike from MMG’s Khoemacau and Sandfire’s Motheo. Early diamond drilling at Karakubis intersected copper mineralisation in all seven holes.

title: Africa Advances New Projects to Expand Alumina Production Capacity
summary: Guinea and other African countries are starting multiple alumina refinery projects to expand refining capacity beyond existing bauxite supply. New builds in Boké, Boffa and planned initiatives in Ghana and Cameroon aim to grow alumina output, supported by higher aluminum demand expectations. LME alumina is cited above bauxite prices.

title: Fortescue to buy remaining 64% of Alta Copper
summary: Fortescue plans to buy the remaining 64% of Alta Copper, implying a change in ownership of a copper project. The provided text does not mention production changes, ramp-up delays, supply disruptions, or new offtake terms, so any near-term impact on copper prices is likely limited.

title: Cheap copper imports under FTAs threaten domestic manufacturing, industry body warns
summary: India’s primary copper producers warn that duty-free copper imports, especially from the UAE under the India-UAE CEPA and an allegedly inflated TRQ, are surging (340%) and undermining domestic smelters. They seek a 3% safeguard duty and stricter quotas. Continued import inflows could pressure copper prices.

title: AKFA Aluminum Solutions to establish first U.S. manufacturing facility in Bowling Green
summary: AKFA Aluminum Solutions plans its first U.S. plant in Bowling Green, Kentucky, a full-cycle aluminum production hub with extrusion, anodizing and finishing. The facility will use recycled aluminum billets and energy-efficient systems, expanding U.S. processing capacity and likely supporting near-term aluminum demand expectations.

title: Four Manufacturing Sites Earn The Copper Mark
summary: Southwire announced four manufacturing sites (including copper rod and building wire plants) received The Copper Mark assurance for responsible production. The Copper Mark covers responsible practices across the copper value chain. The release highlights compliance and sustainability but provides no data on production volumes or market-altering supply-demand changes.

title: Nornickel expects global nickel market surplus in 2025-2026
summary: Nornickel forecasts the global nickel market will stay in surplus at over 200,000 tonnes of Ni in both 2025 and 2026, driven by rising Indonesian supply outpacing demand growth. Indonesia’s recent licensing and quota adjustments may help but are expected to have limited short-term effect, keeping bearish pressure on nickel prices likely.

title: Copper Prices Surge Toward $12,000 on AI Demand and Supply Chaos
summary: Copper prices are surging toward $12,000, driven by supply disruptions (Grasberg accident and Chile issues) and U.S. tariff/trade-policy fears that have prompted stockpiling and record Comex inventories. Analysts link the rally to AI-driven demand alongside a looming copper deficit, tightening the market further.

title: Volta Energy Solutions Canada secures funding for battery copper foil plant in Quebec
summary: Volta Energy Solutions Canada secured about US$140 million from Korea’s Supply Chain Resilience Fund, plus additional financing totaling up to US$300 million, to build a battery copper foil plant in Quebec. The facility is under construction and targets initial output in 2H 2026, with capacity expanding by 2027.

title: Japan's JX says its Pan Pacific Copper unit sells stake in Peruvian mine to Glencore
summary: JX Advanced Metals’ Pan Pacific Copper sold its entire stake in Peru’s undeveloped Quechua copper project to Glencore for an undisclosed price. The asset is close to Glencore’s Antapaccay operations and could support future output, but no near-term production or supply change is indicated.

title: Accelerating North American Expansion: Volta Energy Solutions Canada Secures 'Supply Chain Resilience Fund' for Battery Copper Foil Plant
summary: Volta Energy Solutions Canada secured USD 140 million in Korea’s Supply Chain Resilience Fund and additional financing totaling USD 300 million for a Quebec battery copper foil plant. The project targets EV and growing ESS demand, using copper as the key raw input. It strengthens expectations for sustained battery-material demand in North America.

title: 2026 Aluminum Ingot Long-Term Contract Prices Stable with Adjustments, Multiple Factors Lead to YoY Decline in Order Signing[SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports 2026 aluminum ingot long-term contract prices are broadly stable versus the SMM A00 benchmark but with regional premiums/discounts and generally lower order-signing willingness. Factors include high aluminum price volatility, weaker downstream construction demand, and limited incremental global supply, leading to tighter seller terms and declining contract volumes.

title: Mozal Aluminium Update  | Company Announcement
summary: South32 said Mozal Aluminium in Mozambique will move to care and maintenance around 15 March 2026 after failing to secure a new electricity supply agreement at an internationally competitive price. The drought and power constraints from HCB and Eskom are cited. This reduces primary aluminium supply prospects and may pressure prices lower.

title: Metal Energy Corp.: Metal Energy Completes Right of First Refusal Agreement on NIV Copper-Gold Project in British Columbia
summary: Metal Energy completed a right of first refusal to acquire the remaining 20% interest in the NIV and West NIV properties in British Columbia. NIV is a fully permitted drill-ready copper-gold-(molybdenum) project. The company issued shares as consideration and plans drilling in 2026. No immediate production or copper market impact is stated.

title: [SMM Analysis] Nickel Prices Plunge Over 2% in a Single Day, Hitting a New Low—Where Is the Short-Term Bottom?
summary: Nickel sold off sharply, with SHFE nickel down about 2.36% and LME nickel down about 2.22% to around $14,295/mt. Spot premiums stayed high but trading was sluggish as downstream buyers turned cautious after prior stockpiling. Social inventories rose and production cuts failed to relieve inventory pressure.

title: Guinea, EGA in bauxite supply deal talks, sources say
summary: Guinea is reportedly in talks with Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) for a bauxite supply agreement via Guinea’s Nimba Mining after Guinea revoked EGA subsidiary Guinea Alumina’s licence. A deal could avert threatened litigation. EGA is seeking alternative ore supply; Nimba has shipped and plans renewed bauxite exports.

title: $30 Million from Copper Sale is Promised for Social Projects by Panama's President Mulino
summary: Panama’s President Mulino says $30 million from royalties tied to copper concentrate exports from the disabled Cobre Panamá mine will fund social projects. The government claims some 120,000 tons are being exported in July, helping cover preservation costs and sustaining near-term copper supply flow expectations.

title: New Zealand's Aluminium Smelter
summary: Rio Tinto describes its NZAS Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in New Zealand and electricity arrangements using renewable hydroelectricity that secure continued operation and low-carbon aluminium output. It also notes the smelter is largely exported. The supply outlook for aluminium is therefore more stable in the near term.

title: Guinea, EGA in bauxite supply deal talks – Channel Africa
summary: Guinea’s military-led government revoked EGA subsidiary GAC’s licence and transferred assets to Nimba Mining amid a refinery dispute. Supply-deal talks could avert threatened litigation and help secure bauxite/alumina feedstock for EGA, whose UAE refinery is engineered for GAC ore, supporting aluminium supply expectations.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.96% Lower at $5.2870 — Data Talk
summary: Comex Copper front-month for December delivery settled 0.96% lower at $5.2870 per pound, losing 5.15 cents. The contract fell on the day and was down on two of the past three sessions. It remains up on the month and year versus prior lows.

title: CME : March Copper futures fell as global industrial data softened.
summary: March copper futures fell 2.64% over three sessions as global industrial data softened. Manufacturing indicators in China, Germany, and the Euro area missed expectations, weakening the demand outlook for industrial metals. The EU’s plan to replace its 2035 combustion-engine ban with softer emissions targets also dampened longer-term copper needs for EVs.

title: True North heats up QLD with standout Aquila copper hits
summary: True North Copper reports high-grade assay results from its Aquila prospect at Queensland’s Mount Oxide, including multiple strong copper intervals and extended mineralised strike and depth. The company also secured $12.5m in funding to accelerate exploration across the broader project, with further drilling and surveys planned.

title: Norfolk crafts Christmas copper permit push in Chile
summary: Norfolk Metals says environmental permitting and baseline studies for its Carmen copper project in Chile are advancing with no major hurdles, aiming to lodge a DIA early next year. The company is also commissioning water studies for potential heap-leach processing and completing RC drilling, supporting future development rather than near-term supply.

title: Nickel groups push back over 'unfair' illegal mining fines - Regulations
summary: Indonesian nickel industry groups APNI and FINI object to a new ministerial decree imposing nearly $400,000 per hectare per year in administrative fines for illegal mining in forest areas, specifically targeting nickel. They argue the fines are unfair and could distort costs, prompting pushback amid regulatory enforcement changes.

title: AustruckX launches lightweight all-aluminium curtainsider for electric trucks
summary: AustruckX has launched the AXCS-EV, an all-aluminium curtainsider truck body engineered for electric trucks. By using lightweight aluminium alloys and replacing some steel components with alloy hardware, it cuts tare weight and increases payload. The company says orders are now open for compatible electric truck models, supporting incremental aluminium demand.

title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Congratulates Teck and Anglo American as Canadian Regulatory Approval Is Received
summary: Copper Fox said Canada has approved the Investment Canada Act review for the Teck–Anglo “merger of equals,” clearing the way toward forming Anglo Teck. The deal includes commitments to invest in Canada, including advancing the Schaft Creek copper project (where Copper Fox holds a 25% carried interest). Other antitrust reviews continue abroad.

title: Jubilee's first-quarter copper output surges as Zambian expansion takes shape
summary: Jubilee Metals said its first-quarter copper output rose 65% to 938 tonnes after recovering from earlier power outages at its Zambian operations. Management attributes gains to stable power and investments, and set 2026 production guidance of 4,500–5,100 tonnes. The firm targets a pure copper profile after asset sales.

title: US Presidential Deals Reshape Global Metals Markets: A New Era of Strategic Competition
summary: The piece links U.S. policy to near-term metals price pressure, citing higher aluminium import tariffs and proposed copper tariffs, plus sanctions that prohibit Russian-origin aluminium, copper and nickel imports from mid-April 2024. It also highlights infrastructure “Buy America” demand for copper and aluminium, boosting expectations of tighter supply and higher prices.

title: Global Turmoil Fuels Commodity Divide: Safe Havens Soar as Energy Wanes Amidst Geopolitical Tensions
summary: The piece describes a “great divergence” in commodities where industrial metals tied to the green transition outperform. It highlights copper’s strong 2025 rally driven by EVs, renewables and data centers, notes a structural aluminium deficit, and points to rising nickel demand from EV and storage growth, all supporting bullish near-term price sentiment.

title: Operational recovery means growth in DRC copper output in 2026
summary: DRC copper production is expected to rise moderately in 2025 and then strongly in 2026 as flooding disruptions at Kamoa-Kakula normalize, Phase 3 ramps deliver capacity, and Mutanda, TFM, and Kinsevere maintain steady output. Mutoshi starts production and Kipushi contributes, lifting overall supply.

title: EU expands carbon tax on imports to cover steel and aluminium products
summary: The EU expands its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism to cover 180 steel and aluminium-intensive downstream products. Importers must declare embedded CO2 and buy EU emission certificates if above EU standards. CBAM aims to level competition versus lower-standard producers and is expected to raise €1.4bn annually, with part funding for EU makers.

title: Viewpoint: Copper supply tightness beckons in Europe
summary: A viewpoint piece says Europe enters 2026 with copper supply tighter than global balances imply, as US tariff risk widens the LME–CME premium, drawing metal into CME warehouses. LME stocks fell earlier in 2025 and European cathode premiums have surged, with producers pricing Europe as “second in line.”

title: Vedanta Aluminium expands Lanjigarh refinery to 5 MTPA, boosts India's global rank
summary: Vedanta Aluminium expanded its Lanjigarh alumina refinery in Odisha from 2 to 5 MTPA and reported a record 254 kilotonnes in November, with strong month-on-month growth. The increased alumina supply supports domestic smelting and reduces import dependence, improving near-term expectations for aluminium availability and costs.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.45% Higher at $5.3635 — Data Talk
summary: Comex Copper front-month (December delivery) settled 1.45% higher, up 7.65 cents to $5.3635. It was the largest one-day dollar and percentage gain since Dec. 11, rising on four of the past six sessions and still down versus the July 23, 2025 settlement high.

title: Aluminium Price Surge Expected in Market
summary: South32 plans to put its Mozal aluminium smelter in Mozambique into care and maintenance around March 15, 2026 after failing to agree electricity pricing with key power suppliers. Market participants expect tighter duty-free “green” supply for Europe, pushing European aluminium premiums higher as traders bid up Rotterdam and U.S. Midwest levels.

title: Outback town has 'zero' rental stock as new copper mine is set to increase housing pressure
summary: A Queensland town Cloncurry is facing a rental shortage as Harmony Gold’s Eva Copper Project gets the green light. The mine is forecast to produce 60,000 tonnes of copper annually and create jobs, but local housing is insufficient, raising concerns about FIFO. The approval is mildly supportive for copper sentiment.

title: Woman is fourth and final copper theft ring suspect arrested in Jasper County
summary: A woman was arrested as the fourth suspect in a copper theft ring in Jasper County, Texas. The group allegedly stripped and sold hundreds of pounds of copper from equipment and substations to local scrap yards over the past month. Officials say replacement wiring costs thousands and damage customers, with the investigation ongoing.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Corp.: First Atlantic Announces a No Warrant Private Placement Financing to Advance the Pipestone XL Project
summary: First Atlantic Nickel Corp. announced a non-brokered, fully allocated private placement of flow-through shares to raise up to about C$2.94m, with proceeds earmarked for drilling and metallurgical testing at its Pipestone XL Nickel Alloy Project in Newfoundland. The company says work will advance exploration targets and processing recovery.

title: Vedanta Aluminium scales Lanjigarh Refinery to 5 MTPA; Sets new Alumina production record
summary: Vedanta Aluminium said it ramped up its Lanjigarh refinery to 5 million tonnes per annum and set a new alumina production record. The company framed this as strengthening India’s aluminium self-reliance. Increased refining output can support near-term aluminium supply expectations and pricing.

title: Price Spread of Copper Cathode Rod Processing Fees Exceeds 500? — Analysis of Industry Profit Logic and Breakthrough Strategies
summary: SMM reports that copper cathode rod processing fees in east China fell to around 430 yuan/mt in Dec 2025, with trader quotations turning negative and widening to 500–600 yuan/mt at times. The driver is oversupply versus weak downstream demand, lowering operating rates and intensifying margin pressure.

title: As the off-season deepens, the proportion of liquid aluminum continued to decline
summary: SMM data show China’s proportion of liquid aluminium fell for six straight weeks to 76.34%, driven by policy-driven local alloying and limited holiday downtime, while consumption weakens in the off-season. With spot discounts widening and production expected to rise, supply gains and softer demand point to aluminium prices under pressure.

title: FLSmidth A/S: FLS wins order to supply key comminution technologies to a greenfield copper concentrator in South America
summary: FLSmidth said it won a DKK 405 million order to supply comminution equipment (gyratory and cone crushers, SAG/ball mills, and cyclones) for a greenfield copper concentrator in South America. The project is copper-focused and booked in Q4 2025, signaling ongoing copper project development, albeit with delivery in 2027.

title: India's AM Green and Japan's Mitsui explore potential investment, offtake for green aluminium
summary: India’s AM Green and Japan’s Mitsui signed a non-binding agreement to explore investment and offtake for low-carbon green aluminium. AM Green plans a 1 MTPA solar/wind/hydro-powered smelter and a 2 MTPA alumina refinery in Andhra Pradesh. The pact is expected to support green aluminium demand signals.

title: ASEAN's EV surge runs on untraceable Philippine nickel
