summary: A CRI–Empower investigation says politically connected Philippine nickel exports are hard to trace after leaving the country, with limited safeguards at Chinese processing hubs in Indonesia. Communities report pollution-linked harm amid ASEAN EV growth and rising nickel demand. The piece raises compliance and reputational risks rather than immediate nickel supply disruption.

title: Copper price: BHP CEO, investment banks see bull run in 2026
summary: Copper prices have surged to record highs and are nearing $12,000. The article cites ongoing mining disruptions, persistent supply shortages, and uncertainty around U.S. tariffs as key drivers lifting prices. BHP’s CEO and investment banks expect these pressures to continue into 2026.

title: Canada Nickel Announces Initial Resources at Midlothian and Bannockburn Projects
summary: Canada Nickel announced initial mineral resource estimates for its Midlothian and Bannockburn nickel sulphide projects near Timmins, Ontario, reporting inferred and indicated resources totaling substantial contained nickel. While this improves the company’s long-term resource base, it is unlikely to materially alter near-term nickel supply expectations within weeks.

title: Aluminum scrap resists declines and supports costs, with ADC12 prices continuing to hover at highs. [Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Weekly review reports aluminum scrap prices hovering at highs, with tight supply and CNY pre-stocking supporting seller pricing despite some demand weakening from environmental production restrictions. ADC12 spot prices remain cost-supported and range-bound amid volatile primary aluminum and cautious downstream die-casting procurement, suggesting high-level fluctuation rather than a clear directional move.

title: Intrepid Metals Corp.: Intrepid Metals Announces Strategic Investor: Teck to Acquire a 9.9% Equity Interest to Fund Exploration on the Corral Copper Project in Arizona at $0.45 per Share
summary: Intrepid Metals announced Teck’s $3.96m investment for a 9.9% stake to fund a 24-month exploration program at its Corral Copper Project in Arizona. Planned work includes IP surveying, mapping, sampling, permitting, metallurgical studies and follow-up drilling. The news is financing-led and not a near-term production or supply change.

title: AM Green and Japan's Mitsui explore potential investment, offtake for green aluminium
summary: AM Green and Mitsui signed a non-binding agreement to explore investment and offtake for AM Green’s green aluminium value chain. AM Green is developing a 1 MTPA solar/wind/hydro-powered aluminium smelter and a 2 MTPA alumina refinery in Andhra Pradesh, India, targeting low-carbon aluminium demand.

title: Aurubis to Source Copper from Sweden in New Supply Deal
summary: Aurubis signed an MoU to source about half of the output from Viscaria’s copper mine in northern Sweden, supplying roughly 25,000 tons of concentrate annually. Deliveries to Germany are expected to start after the mine begins operations in late 2027. Volume is small versus Aurubis’s total sourcing, suggesting limited short-term price impact.

title: Northstar Gold Corp.: Northstar Commences Diamond Drill Program at Cam Copper Mine
summary: Northstar Gold commenced a 1,200m definition diamond drill program at its Cam Copper Mine to support an NI 43-101 resource estimate for the Zone 2 copper lens. The company also outlines a potential near-surface surgical mining pilot (~116,000 tonnes) but remains contingent on studies and permitting.

title: Euro Sun Mining Inc.: REPEAT -- Euro Sun Enters Into Multi-Facility Agreement With Trafigura to Secure Up to US$200m for Development of Rovina Valley Copper-Gold Project
summary: Euro Sun announced an amended multi-facility agreement with Trafigura to secure up to US$200m for development of its Rovina Valley copper-gold project in Romania. A further tranche may be drawn later, subject to conditions and authorizations. The financing reduces project funding risk and supports copper development sentiment.

title: FinancialContent - Red Metal Resilience: Why Copper is Defying Gravity Despite China's Economic Headwinds
summary: Copper is described as resilient near record highs despite worries about China’s property sector. The rally is attributed to inventory tightening and major supply disruptions (Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula), plus a weaker US dollar and tariff-driven COMEX warehouse inflows. China’s stimulus and NEV/tech demand are also supporting consumption.

title: Goldman Upgrades Copper Price Forecast Weeks After Warning About "Circular Melt-Up"
summary: Goldman analysts upgraded their LME copper 2026 price forecast to $11,400 from $10,650, citing a lower probability of a refined copper tariff being implemented by H1 2026. The change follows earlier warnings about a “circular melt-up” as copper futures hit new LME records near $11,700/ton.

title: PHL may miss green shift gains sans nickel reform - BusinessWorld Online
summary: The ILO warns the Philippines could miss green-transition benefits without reforms to improve “decent work” and domestic value creation in its nickel supply chain. While nickel demand should rise, the industry says further processing is limited by low LME nickel prices and higher costs versus Indonesia/China.

title: National Transmission Company South Africa provides update on Mozal, Mozambique, aluminium smelter new electricity supply agreement negotiations – Unabridged
summary: South Africa’s NTCSA says it is still negotiating a new electricity supply agreement for the Mozal aluminium smelter in Mozambique, due to expire on 15 March 2026. Mozal needs a substantially lower electricity price to remain competitive. NTCSA is working with stakeholders to avoid cost impacts on consumers while keeping talks open.

title: BGFD responds to structure fire at Kobelco Aluminum
summary: Bowling Green Fire Department units responded to a structure fire at Kobelco Aluminum early Thursday morning. The fire has been brought under control, with causes and damage still under investigation. If production was affected, the incident could tighten near-term aluminum supply expectations.

title: AM Green Mitsui MoU for Green Aluminium and Low-Carbon Investment
summary: AM Green and Mitsui signed an MoU to explore investments in low-carbon aluminium, including a 1 million tpa aluminium smelter and a 2 million tpa alumina refinery powered by wind/solar and pumped hydro. The pact includes potential trading of low-carbon aluminium, but production timing is not specified.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.06% Higher at $5.3665 — Data Talk
summary: Comex copper futures for December delivery settled 0.06% higher at $5.3665/lb, gaining 0.30 cent. The contract rose for two straight sessions, up 1.50% over the last two sessions and up five of seven sessions, marking the highest settlement since Dec. 11, 2025.

title: $200K worth of copper stolen from trailer: Police | The West Elgin Chronicle
summary: Police say a tractor-trailer loaded with more than $200,000 worth of scrap copper was stolen in Strathroy on Nov. 29. The trailer was recovered, but the copper cargo remains missing. The theft is a localized supply loss reported by police, with limited likelihood of affecting broader copper prices.

title: $200K worth of copper stolen from trailer: Police | The Woodstock Sentinel Review
summary: Police say a tractor-trailer loaded with over $200,000 of scrap copper was stolen from a business in Strathroy on Nov. 29. The trailer was later recovered, but the copper cargo remains missing. Police are seeking information and witnesses to locate the stolen material.

title: Lundin Mining Corporation: Lundin Mining Announces Sale of the Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill to Talon Metals to Create a Pure Play American Nickel-Copper Company
summary: Lundin Mining agreed to sell its Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill to Talon Metals for Talon shares, creating a U.S. nickel-copper producer. Eagle is described as the only operating primary U.S. nickel mine and historically produces nickel and copper. The transaction aims to leverage shared processing infrastructure rather than stop output.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals to Acquire Lundin Mining's Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill Operations, Creating a Multi-Asset U.S. Nickel-Copper Company
summary: Talon Metals will acquire 100% of Lundin Mining’s Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill, combining them with Talon’s Tamarack nickel-copper project and its Beulah processing facility. The agreement is positioned to extend mine life and accelerate exploration, supporting domestic nickel-copper supply narratives.

title: Lundin Mining Corporation: Lundin Mining Announces Sale of the Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill to Talon Metals to Create a Pure Play American Nickel-Copper Company
summary: Lundin Mining agreed to sell its Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill to Talon Metals in exchange for Talon shares, creating a U.S. nickel-copper pure play. Eagle is the only operating U.S. primary nickel mine. Humboldt mill processing and potential mine-life extension are highlighted, with no immediate output shutdown stated.

title: BHP CEO: Copper Supply Tightness Hard to Resolve, High-Price Era May Last for Years
summary: BHP CEO Mike Henry said constrained copper supply is hard to resolve, with the market shifting into deficit and remaining tight. He cited record London and strong year-to-date price gains driven by mine disruptions and tariff concerns, arguing high prices are likely to persist as new, smaller, lower-grade mines take time to develop.

title: Talon Metals to acquire Lundin Mining, will create the only operating nickel-copper company in U.S.
summary: Talon Metals has signed an agreement to acquire 100% of Lundin Mining’s producing Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill in Michigan. The combined entity would be a primary nickel-copper producer with expansion potential, aiming to extend mine life, advance permitting, and progress Tamarack project development.

title: Talon Metals to acquire Lundin Mining, will create the only operating nickel-copper company in U.S.
summary: Talon Metals agreed to acquire 100% of Lundin Mining’s producing Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill in Michigan. The company says the combination creates the only operating primary nickel-copper producer in the U.S. and will use Eagle’s cash flow to support mine-life extension and advance its Tamarack nickel-copper project.

title: European Companies Call for More Copper Mines in the EU
summary: European companies Viscaria and Aurubis urged for more EU copper mines and are working to reactivate a copper mine in northern Sweden, targeting output later in 2027. They stressed Europe imports substantial copper and recycling cannot meet rising demand, supporting a tighter-supply narrative and bullish copper sentiment.

title: Viewpoint: Indonesia's MHP surge to hit nickel prices
summary: Indonesia is expected to expand mixed-hydroxide-precipitate (MHP) capacity further in 2026, deepening an already oversupplied nickel market. Argus estimates show falling MHP and Class 1 nickel prices in 2025, while EV demand growth cools and non-nickel battery chemistries gain. Nickel surplus is projected to rise in 2026.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Enters into Collaboration Framework Agreement with Lunasonde to Perform Initial Survey for Critical Minerals in Arizona's Cochise Mining District
summary: Gunnison Copper entered a collaboration with Lunasonde to run initial airborne georadiotomography surveys to image subsurface anomalies across its Cochise Mining District, which contains multiple known copper deposits. The release is exploration-focused with no immediate production or supply change, making any near-term copper impact likely limited.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Dec 19
summary: Indonesia’s domestic nickel laterite ore benchmarks and delivered prices edged down, with rainy-season disruptions at mines and softer procurement from NPI smelters. NPI prices fell again amid weak end-user stainless demand, high inventories, and sparse transactions. While 2026 benchmark/RKAB revisions are discussed, near-term tone stays bearish.

title: Rescue Plan for Australia's Largest Aluminum Smelter
summary: Australia’s federal and NSW governments agreed a rescue plan for Rio Tinto’s Tomago primary aluminium smelter, threatened by rising energy costs. The plan targets a fixed-price power purchase agreement and financing for renewable energy and storage ahead of the current contract expiring in 2028, avoiding potential closure and output loss.

title: Copper nears record high as supply tightness back in focus
summary: Copper rose toward record highs as analysts pointed to tight mine supply constraints, with Goldman reiterating a bullish long-run view and Commerzbank expecting a move toward $12,000 over the next month. Nickel gained on Indonesia’s proposed ore output reduction, while aluminium climbed after South32 said it would shut Mozal.

title: Nickel 28 Files Fiscal Q3 2026 Financial Statements
summary: Nickel 28 reported Q3 2025 financials and Ramu production/sales (contained nickel and MHP) and stated quarterly results were interruption-free. It notes nickel prices remain flat and payables are improving, while Indonesia’s announced fines for illegal mining may tighten ore supply in the short term.

title: Anglo American on track to sell nickel and steelmaking coal businesses
summary: Anglo American reported it is on track to complete the sale of its nickel business, restarting/continuing processes to dispose of remaining steelmaking coal assets after a failed bid. The company is simplifying its portfolio and expects regulatory approvals in the nickel/coal transactions, but near-term nickel output changes appear limited.

title: Customs Act | CESTAT Mumbai Quashes Aluminium Metal Scrap Valuation Enhancement; Says Rule 12 Safeguards Mandatory
summary: CESTAT Mumbai set aside customs orders that enhanced the declared assessable value of imported aluminium scrap using NIDB comparisons and a DGoV valuation circular. The tribunal held Rule 12 requires proper notice and substantiated evidence, and the circular is only a guideline. The enhancement was quashed, benefiting the importer.

title: Sego Resources Inc.: Sego Resources Discovers Copper Porphyry Within the South Gold Zone
summary: Sego Resources reports that drilling at the Miner Mountain Project discovered a new copper porphyry within the South Gold Zone. Three of four drill holes intersected chalcopyrite-associated potassic alteration. Results will be followed by extensive drilling and lab assays, with no quantified resource or immediate production impact stated.

title: ABB advances electrification, automation at Boliden's Aitik copper facility
summary: ABB upgraded electrification and automation at Boliden’s Aitik copper mine in Sweden to support expansion of tailings and improved water recycling, storage and monitoring. The modular systems improve energy-flow control and predictive maintenance. Boliden aims to scale output amid rising copper demand, supporting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: DRC and Zambia Set to Dominate Global Copper Production | IR Global
summary: The piece argues that DRC and Zambia are increasing copper production and investment, with Zambia’s Q2 output up nearly 18% and DRC overtaking Peru as a top producer. It links this with modest global supply growth projections and rising demand for grids and EV batteries, supporting a bullish copper price outlook.

title: Talon Metals to buy Eagle Mine and its Michigan nickel processing mill
summary: Talon Metals agreed to acquire Lundin Mining’s Eagle Mine and Humboldt processing mill in Michigan, consolidating U.S. nickel-copper production and refining capacity. The purchase supports domestic “critical minerals” supply focus and may improve near-term expectations for nickel and, to a lesser extent, copper feedstock and processing.

title: CBP Issues Guidance on Valuation of Steel, Aluminum and Copper Content for Section 232 Tariffs
summary: U.S. CBP issued guidance on calculating Section 232 tariffs by valuing embedded steel, aluminum, and copper content. For mixed products, tariffs apply to the invoice value paid for the metal content, with limited deductions for fabrication and treatments. Copper alloying value can’t be deducted, potentially increasing landed costs and dampening demand.

title: CBP Issues Guidance on Valuation of Steel, Aluminum and Copper Content for Section 232 Tariffs
summary: CBP issued guidance on valuing steel, aluminium and copper content under U.S. Section 232 tariffs. For mixed products, duties are based on the invoice value of the contained metal, with fabrication/labor costs generally not deductible. Copper alloying elements also can’t be deducted, raising uncertainty and potentially increasing effective costs for importers.

title: Market seeks price transparency for Guinea bauxite amid cost pressures, rising demand
summary: Guinea’s bauxite exports to China surged to 127.11 million tonnes in the first 10 months of 2025. Growth in bauxite supply to alumina refineries has left them facing oversupply and depressed alumina prices, expected to persist. Market pressure is pushing cost transparency and FOB pricing for Guinea bauxite.

title: Kutcho Copper Corp.: Kutcho Copper Announces $1,000,000 Flow-Through Financing
summary: Kutcho Copper Corp. announced a non-brokered $1,000,000 flow-through financing to fund exploration on its Kutcho copper-zinc property in British Columbia. Proceeds will be used for Canadian exploration and critical mineral mining expenditures through Dec. 31, 2026. The release focuses on capital raising rather than near-term production changes.

title: Minnesota requires copper sellers to have a state-issued license, but is it helping to reduce theft?
summary: Minnesota’s new law requires a state license for selling copper wire for recycling, aiming to reduce theft profits. St. Paul reports copper wire theft complaints fell 34% year over year between January and September 2024. Officials still cite ongoing theft and observe illegal sales of insulated wire at some recyclers.

title: 'Giant' potential possible for copper project north of Sault
summary: Sterling Metals’ year-end letter highlights promising early drill results for the Soo Copper Project near Sault Ste. Marie, citing widespread copper mineralization and potential for scale and grade. Management frames copper markets as structurally strong with demand and protected supply needs, reinforcing bullish sentiment toward copper.

title: WATCH LIVE: Funeral for the penny as the mint ends the copper coin
summary: The U.S. Treasury decided to suspend production of the one-cent (penny) coin because it is no longer deemed necessary and because costs have risen from 1.42 cents to 3.69 cents per penny. The change implies reduced domestic copper coin demand but likely limited effect on overall copper prices.

title: Weekly Review of the Secondary Copper Market: Price Stability and Volume Contraction Persist, Year-End Invoice Constraints Dampen Trading Activity
summary: The weekly secondary copper market review reports stable copper prices but shrinking volumes, driven by weak end demand and tightening invoice/tax quotas in Guangdong and Jiangxi. Secondary rod operating rates fell sharply with production cuts. Supply pressures and inventory accumulation increased, while near-term copper price sentiment remains range-bound.

title: SMM Analysis: The Two-Month Low-Price War Concludes, Aluminum Rod Processing Fees Reach an Inflection Point
summary: SMM reports falling inventory at domestic aluminum rod plants and a slight WoW dip then rebound in aluminum prices after testing the 20-day average. Processing fees have moved off lows but remain range-bound as end-use demand and wire/cable operating rates weaken, with holiday-related export slowdown offering short-term pressure.

title: Copper nears US$12,000 a tonne as base metals rally
summary: Copper neared US$12,000/t as base metals rallied alongside renewed US tech stock strength. The move was supported by tightening supply from mine outages and higher US imports, with AI-related usage optimism. Aluminium hit a recent high on smelter shutdown worries in Mozambique, while nickel rebounded on reduced-supply expectations.

title: Red Metal inks JV to fast-track copper hunt in WA
summary: Red Metal signed a joint venture with Artemis to fast-track drilling at the Sharon Dam IOCG copper-gold target in Western Australia. Artemis can earn up to 60% by funding over three years, starting with a $400,000 program partly co-funded by a WA government exploration grant. Drilling is planned for March.

title: Copper Enamelled Wire Exports Rose Both Year-on-Year and Month-on-Month in November, with Egypt Showing Prominent Growth and Entering the Top 10
summary: China’s exports of copper enamelled (winding) wire rose 22.6% YoY in November 2025 to 12,814 mt, though down 19.0% MoM. Shipments reached 144 markets, with sharp YoY gains to India and Egypt and declines to some destinations, indicating uneven demand but overall supportive copper export momentum.

title: Prospect Ridge Updates Diamond Drill Program at 100% Owned Camelot Copper-Gold Project in B.C.'S Cariboo Mining District
summary: Prospect Ridge reported visual and pXRF spot results from the final four drill holes at its 100% owned Camelot copper-gold project in B.C., detecting disseminated pyrite and chalcopyrite and copper across holes. Wet-chemical assay results are pending for late December, limiting any immediate impact on copper prices.

title: Silver And Copper Are Both Flashing The Same Signal — And That Is Setting The Stage For Widespread Panic On Wall Street
summary: The piece argues AI and data-center expansion are driving heavy copper demand (including claims of up to 50,000 tons per hyperscale site) and links rising prices to supply pressure from copper theft and infrastructure disruptions. It also discusses silver shortages and battery-related silver use, but only copper is directly price-relevant here.

title: Up MoM but down YoY, China's copper plate/sheet and strip exports reached 10,887 mt in November.
summary: China’s customs data show copper plate/sheet and strip exports of about 10,887 mt in November, up 11.35% month-on-month but down 10.07% year-on-year. Total exports to 98 destinations fell on a YoY basis, with weaker shipments to Malaysia, the US and Japan partially offsetting gains elsewhere.

title: Bitcoin trails polar opposites, Gold and Copper, as the 'fear and AI' trade lifts tangible assets
summary: The piece argues investors are favoring tangible assets, citing copper’s strong year-to-date gains. It attributes copper strength to electrification and digital infrastructure tied to AI, alongside slower supply growth and geopolitical tension. This framing suggests expectations of firmer copper demand in the near term.

title: China's Copper Anode Imports Remain Low in 2025, 2026 RC Benchmark Finalised [SMM Analysis]
summary: China imported only 692,300 mt of copper anode in Jan–Nov 2025, down 15% YoY, with November volumes still low versus prior years due to tight ore supply and logistics/political constraints. Global demand for anodes is expected to rise as overseas refining expands, while the 2026 blister RC benchmark settled at $85/mt.

title: 【SMM Analysis】250M Ton RKAB Quota Gamble: Is Indonesia About to Break the Global Nickel Market?
summary: SMM reports Bloomberg citing APNI sources that Indonesia may cut its 2026 nickel ore RKAB quota by about 34% to ~250 million tons to tighten supply and support nickel prices. While Indonesia’s 2025 output already ran below quota, rising HPAL/processing demand and declining ore grades could lift ore needs.

title: Eastport Critical Metals Corp.: Eastport Provides Drilling Updates at Matsitama Copper, Semarule REE and Foley Uranium
summary: Eastport Critical Metals Corp. reports drilling updates for its Botswana projects, with Matsitama Copper work focused on infill and exploration drilling across multiple copper targets. All programs paused for the holiday season and are scheduled to resume mid-January 2026. No assay results are provided in this release.

title: Xinjiang Shipments See Recovery, How Will Year-End Aluminum Ingot Inventory Play Out? [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports that aluminium ingot shipping backlogs in Xinjiang have largely eased, but concentrated arrivals triggered phased inventory buildup in warehouses, especially Gongyi, where withdrawals are weak due to environmental protection-related production cuts. Supply chain costs normalize after highway transport ends. Late-December inventories may rise above 600,000 mt, pressuring aluminium prices.

title: Refined Copper Net Imports Plunge in November; Monthly Exports Hit Second-Highest on Record
summary: China’s refined copper net imports fell sharply in November, while exports rose strongly, driven by widening LME-COMEX spreads and expanded export windows. However, the surge in exports and weaker apparent consumption imply demand missed expectations. Seasonal demand weakness is expected to persist into year-end, with December imports still low YoY.

title: FinancialContent - Copper Fever: Is Lundin Mining's 130% Surge a Fundamental Breakthrough or a Speculative Bubble?
summary: The piece argues copper is in a historic rally, trading near $12,000/tonne, driven by Lundin’s expansion in Chile and a new BHP-Lundin JV with major copper resources. It highlights AI/data-center and energy-transition demand as supportive, while noting valuation risks and potential macro cooling.

title: FinancialContent - Metals Mania: Gold, Silver, and Copper Hit Historic Highs as Robust GDP Data Damps Stock Futures
summary: U.S. Q3 GDP grew 4.3% versus 3.3% forecast, keeping “higher for longer” rate expectations elevated. Meanwhile, copper surged to a record $12,031.50/ton on LME amid supply deficits from disruptions in Chile and Peru and importers stockpiling ahead of potential tariffs. Precious metals also rose sharply.

title: FinancialContent - The Triple Crown: Gold, Silver, and Copper Hit Historic Peaks in Unprecedented Metals Supercycle
summary: The piece reports LME copper above $12,000/ton on a “triple metal” rally. It links copper strength to tight inventories near historic lows, multi-year supply deficits, and accelerating AI data-center and grid modernization demand, reinforced by geopolitical risk premiums and reduced expected real yields.

title: The Daily Chase: Copper in record territory
summary: Copper prices pushed above US$12,000 per ton on the London Metal Exchange, extending a rally with about a 37% gain this year. The move is attributed to severe mine outages and tariff agenda-related trade disruptions, even as China’s underlying usage weakens.

title: Supply and Tariff Woes Send Copper Prices to Record High above $12,000
summary: Copper prices hit record highs above $12,000/t as supply disruptions in key producing countries (mine accidents in Chile and Indonesia) tighten the physical market. U.S. trade-policy/tariff uncertainty has increased import worries and encouraged Comex hoarding, supporting a market deficit narrative and boosting demand expectations.

title: Congo halts artisanal copper and cobalt processing amid corruption crackdown
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo suspended artisanal copper processing and ordered entities to halt operations and certify mineral origins amid a corruption crackdown. The decree aims to improve transparency and prevent illegal exports. While cobalt supply issues are prominent, the article provides no quantified estimate of copper output changes or price effects.

title: Gold, Silver, and Copper Hit New Highs
summary: Gold and silver hit fresh all-time highs as geopolitical tensions escalated and markets priced in more US rate cuts. Copper also climbed above $12,000 a ton for the first time. The move suggests strong near-term bullish momentum for industrial and precious metals, supported by lower-rate expectations and heightened risk appetite.

title: Copper hits $US12,000 for first time as tariff trade upends market
summary: Copper broke $12,000/t on the London Metal Exchange, rising about 2% to $12,159.50. The rally is linked to severe mine outages reducing supply and tariff-related trade dislocations disrupting market flows tied to Trump’s trade agenda.

title: 'Do Not Consume' order issued for Granisle water supply due to aluminum contamination
summary: Northern Health issued a ‘Do Not Consume’ order for Granisle’s water after tests found aluminium concentrations above Canadian guidelines. The authority says aluminium likely comes from coagulant leaking from treatment equipment into distribution lines. Repairs and flushing are required, with no clear timeline, and testing continues.

title: Uzbekistan-Based AKFA Aluminum Solutions Plans Bowling Green, Kentucky, Production Operations
summary: AKFA Aluminum Solutions plans a full-cycle aluminum production hub in Bowling Green, Kentucky, including extrusion, anodizing and finishing. The firm expects up to 100,000 tons annually and received Kentucky tax incentives to support the investment. The expansion can influence short-term aluminum supply expectations, though the ramp timeline is unclear.

title: Police: Copper wire theft led to traffic light outage, contributed to deadly Portland crash
summary: Portland Police say copper wire theft damaged traffic light wiring at the I-205/Northeast Airport Way intersection, causing non-operating signals that contributed to a deadly Dec. 11 crash. Officers investigated wire cutting in a traffic transfer box and asked for witnesses; the report is local and not linked to copper markets.

title: Gold, silver and copper prices surge to record highs on dollar worries
summary: Gold, silver and copper prices hit record highs as investors worried about a weakening U.S. dollar shifted toward commodities. Copper in particular rose on “tight supply,” described as lifting demand and supporting higher copper futures prices in the near term.

title: China's Copper Foil Customs Details for November 2025: Both Imports and Exports Increased, Trade Deficit Narrowed [SMM Analysis]
summary: China’s November 2025 copper foil imports rose to 6,653.5 mt (+11.8% YoY, +9.2% MoM) with import value up 21.8% YoY. Exports also increased to 5,994.2 mt (+14.1% YoY, +11.5% MoM), narrowing the trade deficit. The shift suggests firmer copper-linked demand and trade activity.

title: Chile loads its copper cannon with 13 projects for a bullish 2026
summary: Chile expects 13 copper projects to reach key milestones in 2026, with several starting operations and expansions that could raise output. The outlook is framed by rising supply-squeeze fears, a projected refined deficit, US cathode stockpiling, and a 10% Chinese smelter output cut—supportive for copper prices.

title: Cobalt and Copper: A New Regulation in the DRC Redraws the Winners of the Copperbelt
summary: The DRC abruptly tightened regulations on artisanal copper processing and re-certification to curb illegal exports, freezing parts of the supply chain. It mainly affects informal/artisanal circuits (around 20–30% of output), creating a short-term supply squeeze, redirecting trade, and likely supporting higher copper prices and risk premiums.

title: SolGold agrees to $1.2 billion takeover by top investor Jiangxi Copper
summary: SolGold agreed to a roughly $1.17 billion takeover by its largest shareholder Jiangxi Copper, granting control of the Cascabel copper-gold project in Ecuador. Reuters frames it amid demand growth for copper. Because it concerns an undeveloped project, near-term refined copper supply effects are likely limited.

title: SolGold recommends shareholders support Jiangxi Copper offer
summary: SolGold PLC agreed to an all-cash acquisition by Jiangxi Copper’s investment arm at 28 pence per share. The deal is an increased offer versus prior bids and requires shareholder approval. While it links to copper via the buyer and target, no immediate supply-demand changes are specified.

title: FinancialContent - The Great Metal Super-Surge of 2025: Gold, Silver, and Copper Hit Historic Peaks as Economic Clouds Gather
summary: The piece describes 2025 as a “copper crunch,” with copper peaking near historic highs amid mine-related supply setbacks (including Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula) and accelerating demand from AI data centers and green-energy infrastructure. It frames current backwardation as evidence the supply squeeze persists into early 2026.

title: FinancialContent - Copper's Red Metal Revolution: Prices Target $12,000 Milestone Amid Supply Shocks and AI Demand
summary: Copper prices are surging toward $12,000/ton on the LME amid tight physical supply: inventories at multi-year lows, mine outages/production drops (Cobre Panama closure, lower Codelco output), and a U.S. 50% tariff on refined copper that triggered front-running and record premiums. The market expects persistent tightness and some substitution toward aluminum.

title: "Critical Mineral Bauxite Boom Pollutes Water And Crops In Guinea"
summary: Villagers in Guinea’s Kindia region accuse an Indian company operating a nearby bauxite mine of polluting local water and reducing crop yields. With Guinea holding the world’s largest bauxite reserves, the reported environmental harm could prompt scrutiny or disruptions that affect near-term bauxite/aluminium supply expectations.

title: Copper prices rise to more than 30% in the U.S.
summary: Copper prices in the U.S. have surged more than 30% this year. JPMorgan links the rally to new data center construction growth and tariff speculation from the Trump administration. The higher prices have also coincided with increased copper-wire thefts, leading to infrastructure disruptions and higher utility replacement costs.

title: Materials Up as Copper, Gold, Silver Test Record Highs -- Materials Roundup
summary: Producers of raw materials rose as recent weakness in the U.S. dollar pushed metals futures to record highs. Copper topped $12,000 a ton in London for the first time, linked to tariffs and currency-market moves. The roundup also highlights record-testing gold and higher silver, citing geopolitical hedging demand.

title: South Korea-Based ALUKO Group Plans Halls, Tennessee, Aluminum Manufacturing Operations
summary: ALUKO Group plans an integrated aluminum manufacturing facility in Halls, Tennessee, repurposing a former Tupperware building. The plant will serve EV, solar, and construction customers and create 285 jobs, supported by state and TVA. The new capacity/demand outlook is supportive for aluminum market sentiment.

title: Chinese state miner to buy Ecuadorean copper project in $1.2bn deal
summary: Jiangxi Copper, a Chinese state miner, agreed to buy all shares of London-listed SolGold for $1.2 billion. The acquisition is expected to give Jiangxi control of Ecuador’s Cascabel project, with output planned for 2028. Near-term copper supply changes appear limited, implying limited immediate price pressure.

title: [SMM Analysis] Review of the Nickel Market in 2025 and Outlook for 2026
summary: Nickel prices fell through 2025, with SHFE/LME turning lower to near multi-year lows before a brief surge tied to Indonesia’s planned RKAB ore quota cuts. The article highlights accumulating LME/SHFE and domestic inventories and projects ongoing 2026 oversupply from China and Indonesia, implying a further downward nickel price bias.

title: Resonance of Seasonal Demand Recovery and Raw Material Disruptions: 2025 Review and 2026 Outlook for Battery-Grade Nickel Sulphate
summary: SMM reviews nickel sulphate’s 2025 tight supply-demand due to raw material constraints and notes strong prices during seasonal ternary demand recovery. It expects Q1 2026 to be an off-season for ternary procurement, with continued tight intermediate supply but weaker nickel sulphate demand, leading to generally weak prices with only intermittent rebounds.

title: GIADEC dismisses claims gov't plans to award Nyinahin Bauxite concessions to Ibrahim Mahama
summary: Ghana’s GIADEC denied claims that the government would grant bauxite concessions in Nyinahin to a private businessman, reiterating that GIADEC will remain the leaseholder under a new policy. It says it secured six bauxite mining leases, including Nyinahin, in June 2025 pending Parliament ratification.

title: Cost and Demand Game Continues, Secondary Aluminum Prices to Hover at Highs in the Short Term[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: Secondary aluminum and aluminum scrap prices remained at high levels, with SMM A00 up WoW and shredded/tense scrap holding firm. Supply is constrained by environmental protection-driven production restrictions, while secondary alloy buyers stock ahead of Chinese New Year. Growing imports and weak die-casting demand could limit upside, but the near-term bias is supportive.

title: Net Primary Aluminum Imports Dropped to Below 100,000 mt in November
summary: China’s net primary aluminium imports fell to about 94,000 mt in November, down 58% month-on-month and 29% year-on-year, the lowest for the year. Exports rose sharply. SMM attributes the drop to wider import losses, tighter Asia supply, and high European/U.S. ingot premiums diverting global flows to those regions.

title: FinancialContent - The Red Gold Rush: Copper Shatters $12,220 as AI Supercycle and Supply Shocks Reshape the Global Economy
summary: Copper futures are described as surging to an all-time high near $12,220/t on AI-driven electricity/data-center demand and copper supply disruptions, including the Grasberg mudflow and ensuing concentrate shortages that forced Chinese smelter cuts. The piece flags short-term volatility and potential aluminium substitution, but expects a strong copper price floor.

title: Unpacking Copper's Phantom Deficit
summary: The piece claims the LME copper rally reflects a logistics/tariff-driven “phantom deficit,” with hundreds of thousands of tonnes economically trapped in the US and held back by rumored 15% tariffs. If tariffs are lighter, it expects the inventory to return and pressure copper prices. It also highlights substitution pressure toward aluminium.

title: Copper Prices Tempt Thieves: How to protect your home, business
summary: The story says copper prices have risen sharply and attract thieves to scrap yards. It notes a prior Indonesia mine landslide that tightened supply and pushed prices higher, and describes local regulations and security measures to deter theft. It provides no new supply disruption in the near term.

title: Copper to Hit $13,500/ton by 2026 Amid Supply Crisis
summary: Analysts expect copper to extend its rally, citing persistent supply constraints from mine disruptions in Indonesia/Chile/Peru, planned Chinese smelter output cuts, and tighter concentrate markets. They also point to improving physical demand and premiums, weaker dollar support, and pre-emptive US stockpiling tied to tariff uncertainty, projecting higher LME and domestic prices into 2026.

title: Detained mining tycoon Joseph Sy resigns from Global Ferronickel
summary: Detained mining tycoon Joseph Sy resigned as director of Global Ferronickel Holdings, a top Philippine nickel ore exporter with a major producer unit in Surigao del Norte. Sy’s citizenship case and ongoing detention could add uncertainty to operations and shipments to China, where nickel ore feeds stainless-steel intermediates.

title: China to rein in copper, alumina capacity expansion under next five-year plan
summary: China’s NDRC said it will tighten approvals and feasibility reviews for new copper and alumina projects to curb “irrational investment” and overcapacity risks. The guidance also promotes mergers to increase concentration and supports overseas mining. Reuters notes copper and aluminium prices rose on the news.

title: China to rein in copper, alumina capacity expansion under next five-year plan
summary: China’s NDRC said it will tighten oversight of new copper and alumina capacity expansions from 2026-2030 to curb overinvestment and disordered growth. It urged stricter project feasibility reviews and more industry restructuring. The move follows prior copper smelting-capacity suspensions and coincided with higher copper and aluminium prices.

title: [SMM Analysis] Nickel Intermediate Product Market Under the Dual Impact of Indonesian Policies and Supply-Demand Situation—2025 Nickel Intermediate Product Annual Review
summary: SMM reviews 2025 Indonesian nickel intermediate product markets (MHP and high-grade nickel matte). It links quarterly output disruptions (holidays, Indonesian flooding, maintenance) and policy effects (RKAB/SIMBARA/HPM/PNBP) to MHP/high-grade payable and final prices, while LME nickel moves from tariffs, USD strength, and inventories partially offset demand-driven increases.

title: [SMM Analysis] Nickel prices surged strongly this week, with a slight destocking on a weekly basis.
summary: Nickel prices surged this week as Indonesia-related rumors of tighter nickel ore quotas by 2026 boosted expectations of supply contraction. SHFE nickel 2602 rose about 9% and LME 3M nickel increased about 5%. Spot premiums improved, inventories were broadly stable, and liquidity easing supported sentiment.

title: China tightens oversight on Copper, Alumina projects – Shafaqna English | International Shia News & Fatwas
summary: China’s top economic planner said it will tighten supervision over new copper and alumina projects from 2026-2030 to curb “reckless investment” and chaotic expansion. By potentially delaying or reducing new capacity plans, the policy could support firmer expectations for copper supply and aluminium fundamentals via alumina feedstock.

title: China tightens oversight on Copper, Alumina projects – Shafaqna English | International Shia News & Fatwas
summary: China’s top economic planner said tighter oversight will apply to new copper projects and alumina projects from 2026 to 2030 to curb reckless investment and “chaotic expansion.” While this could constrain future supply, it is not tied to immediate shutdowns or policy affecting prices in the next few weeks.

title: Copper Hits Record in China, Jumps in New York on Supply Concern
summary: Copper prices reportedly hit records in China and increased in New York, with gains attributed to supply concerns. The headline suggests perceived near-term copper tightness, which can raise expectations for reduced availability and support buying interest across physical and futures markets.

title: Copper prices change daily, making companies hesitant to accept orders! Downstream factories are forced to cut production and "lie flat."
summary: Sharp copper price increases are linked to ore supply tightness (mine disruptions, declining grades), low concentrate treatment charges that constrain cathode supply, and imbalanced COMEX vs LME inventory distribution. Demand expectations from energy transition/AI and weaker USD add financial support, while downstream wire/rod producers cut output under high costs.

title: FinancialContent - BHP Group Hits $61.53 Milestone: Copper Supercycle and Resource Sovereignty Drive Global Mining Surge
summary: BHP reached a $61.53 52-week high, driven largely by copper’s rally to record levels amid a structural deficit. The article points to grid expansion and AI/data-center demand, plus U.S. copper import duties and stockpiling effects that lift domestic pricing expectations. Overall, it implies near-term bullish pressure for copper prices.

title: Chinese Domestic Copper Cathode Premium Has Began to Widely Offer
summary: SMM reports that Chinese copper cathode and concentrate contract terms for 2026 are being widely quoted, including historically low TC/RC and first-round cathode premium offers in various regions. Downstream buyers remain cautious due to high copper prices and elevated premiums, with expectations for more variable fixed-price contracting.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Dec 26
summary: SMM’s Indonesian nickel market review shows nickel ore prices broadly stable/slightly down, with production disrupted by rainy season and constrained shipping from forestry enforcement. However, nickel pig iron/NPI sentiment turned positive: high-grade NPI prices rose WoW on macro support and higher stainless steel, alongside year-end restocking and stronger upstream pricing.

title: Hindustan Copper Shares Surge to 52-Week High – Chennaionline
summary: Shares of Hindustan Copper jumped as much as 8.65% to a 52-week high, with analysts attributing the move to rising global copper prices and stronger demand. The piece notes that record-high copper prices are boosting companies involved in mining, refining and trading and could support continued gains in coming weeks.

title: Bitcoin price news: BTC stumbles as gold, silver and copper soar to new records Friday
summary: Bitcoin falls below $87,000 while metals surge. The article says copper gained about 5% to new record highs alongside gold and silver on “debasement” trading and geopolitical tension. It attributes the capital rotation away from crypto to safe-haven/hedging demand. Platinum and silver also rise sharply.

title: FinancialContent - Dr. Copper's Diagnosis: What the Red Metal's Record Surge to $12,000 Tells Us About the Global Economy
summary: Copper surged over 20% in Q4 2025, topping $12,000/t on the LME, driven by mid-2025 supply shocks (Indonesia’s Grasberg force majeure, Chile’s Codelco disruptions) and acute physical tightness. Negative Chinese TC/RCs triggered a 10% smelting production cut, pushing cathode availability and spot premiums higher.

title: Shanghai copper hits record high on signs of tight concentrate supply
summary: Shanghai copper surged to record highs, driven by signs that copper concentrate supply will remain tight next year. Chinese smelters reportedly refrained from setting next-quarter processing fees, reflecting feedstock shortages and record-low charges. A weaker U.S. dollar boosted broader metals sentiment, with aluminium higher and nickel slightly up.

title: Copper prices hit record as investors bet on tighter times coming next year
summary: Copper prices surged to record highs in Shanghai and New York as investors priced tighter global supplies next year and a weaker US dollar boosted affordability. Comex and LME reopenings are noted, and tariff-related review expectations added to volatility and buying interest, sustaining strong bullish momentum.

title: Soaring Copper Prices Widen the Price Difference Between Primary Metal and Scrap, Yet Market Performance Deviates from Historical Trends
summary: Copper prices have surged since late September 2025 to record levels, widening the tax-inclusive spread between primary cathode and scrap beyond 5,000 yuan/mt. Despite supply-theoretic expectations of higher scrap flows, secondary rod operating rates fell, while anode plate output rose. Delayed procurement and stable cathode output increased spot cathode inventories.

title: India's Aluminium Sector: Urgent Call for Import Duty Hike
summary: India’s aluminium industry panel urges the government to raise import duties on primary and downstream aluminium to 10% and add a 7.5% duty on aluminium scrap to stem a surge of cheap imports. Imports are said to cover 56% of domestic demand, potentially pressuring domestic producers.

title: MMG to Spend $900 Million Toward Copper Mine Expansion in Botswana
summary: MMG, a Chinese state-owned miner, said its board approved a $900 million expansion of the Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana. The project would raise concentrate output to about 130,000 tonnes of copper and cut expected C1 costs. It includes new processing capacity and additional deposits.

title: [SMM Analysis] 2025 Recycled Copper Raw Material Import Market Review & 2026 Outlook
summary: China’s recycled copper scrap imports rose in Jan–Oct 2025 and jumped in October, recovering after earlier trade-friction dips. Scrap prices moved with LME copper, peaking in Q4 amid tighter raw-material supply from accidents and expectations of smelter production cuts. Policy protectionism may further fragment flows ahead.

title: [SMM Analysis] Latest Chemical Policies Rattle Copper Sector: Shrinking Sulfuric Acid Revenues & Inadequate Storage Capacity
summary: SMM says copper concentrate spot TCs collapsed, boosting the importance of sulfuric acid revenue for Chinese copper smelters. New policies emphasize fertilizer supply stability via reduced sulfuric acid exports and sales-price caps. The article warns this may harm smelters’ acid economics and create storage-capacity stress, lowering copper smelting utilization.

title: Nickel price soars after Indonesia signals production cuts
summary: Nickel prices rose to a seven-month high after Indonesia signaled it would cut nickel supply. Indonesian media cited Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil Lahadalia confirming production cuts, while an industry group expected Jakarta to enforce a 34% reduction in volumes next year, supporting higher prices.

title: Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) Climbs 8% on Copper Jump to Fresh High
summary: Freeport-McMoRan shares surged about 8% as copper prices jumped to a new high. The market move suggests improved near-term expectations for copper, likely reflecting tighter conditions or stronger demand sentiment, and it aligns with higher physical or benchmark copper pricing. No nickel or aluminium effects are indicated.

title: Axis International seeks $28.9 billion from Guinea over revoked bauxite permit
summary: Axis International is seeking $28.9 billion in arbitration after Guinea revoked its bauxite mine permit. Guinea has tightened control over mining permits for higher revenue and local processing. The dispute highlights potential near-term disruption to bauxite supply from a major reserve holder, which can affect alumina and aluminium markets.

title: Copper pulls back from record rally as investors take profits
summary: Copper surged to record levels near $13,000/t before paring gains on Monday as investors took profits and the LME reopened after a holiday. The rally reflects shortage worries, weaker dollar, and risk-on sentiment, with tighter US stocks and mine disruptions cited. Aluminium and nickel moved only marginally.

title: Gainers & Losers: Hindustan Copper, Hindustan Zinc among 7 stocks that dominated on Monday
summary: Indian markets fell, but Hindustan Copper shares gained about 2.6%, citing a surge in copper prices as the driver. The piece attributes strong gains and a near-term rally to copper price strength, suggesting supportive near-dated sentiment for copper demand and pricing.

title: Building an Aluminum Giant: Indonesia's 2025 Strategy of Control, Compliance, and Captive Demand
summary: Indonesia’s 2025 reforms keep the bauxite export ban in place while adding annual RKAB output quotas, SIMBARA monitoring, and stronger enforcement in forest areas with sizable per-hectare fines. It also cites surging domestic demand from EV, renewable energy, and national infrastructure programs, supporting expectations for higher aluminum demand and supply discipline.

title: Copper Rallies to Record Near $13,000 in London on Supply Fears
summary: Copper prices are reported to be rallying toward record levels near $13,000 in London on supply fears. Such concerns about tighter near-term availability usually increase expectations of deficits, supporting upward price pressure in the copper market over the next days to weeks.

title: Copper price on track for biggest rise in 15 years amid global shortage fears
summary: Copper is set for its biggest annual rise in 15 years as traders price global shortage risks. Gains are linked to US tariff uncertainty and hoarding that tightens availability, along with concerns over mining accidents disrupting supply. China also prioritizes securing stocks for electrification demand.

title: Copper Prices Are Having a Banner Year -- Commodities Roundup
summary: LME three-month copper futures rose about 2%, reaching near-record levels. Coverage attributes gains to supply disruptions at major mines and expectations of looming U.S. tariffs on refined metal imports, which have encouraged faster shipments, alongside supportive rate-cut expectations for industrial metals.

title: Copper prices surge to near record high
summary: Copper prices surged to near record highs as London caught up with China and US gains. The rally was attributed to shortage worries, tighter US inventories, mine disruptions, a weaker dollar, and risk-on sentiment. SHFE also got support from reports China will curb copper capacity growth. Aluminium slightly dipped; nickel rose.

title: FinancialContent - The Copper Super-Squeeze of 2025: How AI and Trade Wars Created a 'Perfect Storm' for the Red Metal
summary: Copper prices are described as surging to record levels in 2025 due to AI-driven demand, tariff policy shocks (including a 50% tariff on semi-finished products with refined cathode exemptions), and supply disruptions from mine outages, earthquakes, mudslides, and labor blockades. Smelter margins collapse (TC/RCs to zero) intensify refined supply tightness; aluminium substitution is mentioned as limited.

title: FinancialContent - Copper's Red-Hot Supercycle Ignites African Currencies: Zambia's Kwacha Leads Global Gainers
summary: The article argues copper is in a “red-hot supercycle,” supported by a large global deficit and structurally stronger demand from EVs, renewables, and AI-driven data centers. Copper is described as holding above ~$10,500–$10,800/ton, with Zambia and DRC benefiting via currency gains and mine expansions.

title: FinancialContent - The Great Metal Squeeze: Structural Deficits Propel Copper and Silver to Historic Highs
summary: The piece argues that copper prices have surged due to structural deficits: a Grasberg mine force majeure reduced output, ore grades are declining, and AI/data-center plus grid modernization demand has accelerated. LME stocks reportedly fell below 110,000 tonnes, indicating physical tightness. It suggests continued shortage-driven strength into 2026.

title: FinancialContent - Tariff Madness: How Trade Protectionism Ignited a Historic Surge in Copper and Silver Markets
summary: The article attributes 2025’s sharp copper rally to trade protectionism, including a blanket 25% U.S. tariff and a July 8 2025 50% tariff on copper imports of semi-finished products. These duties disrupted flows, triggered an inventory grab, widened Comex-LME pricing, and pushed Comex copper futures to record highs.

title: Peru's copper output could double with large-scale projects
summary: Peru’s central bank projects copper production could rise further if large-scale mining projects proceed, potentially adding about 3.2 million metric tons. Growth depends on substantial investment and faces risks from social conflicts, protests, and environmental/permitting delays. The outlook supports longer-term supply expectations but is conditional.

title: Suspected copper wire thieves disable parking enforcement radios in Los Angeles
summary: Copper thieves damaged a communications tower in Elysian Park, disabling Los Angeles transportation officers’ radios for two days. The city and technology agencies repaired the tower, and officials highlighted ongoing copper theft. The article also cites a newly signed state law increasing penalties for illegal scrap metal dealers.

title: Mining Stocks Slip Near the End of Stellar Year
summary: Mining shares slipped as a rally in gold, silver and copper paused. The decline was linked to weaker metals prices, with copper down about 4.6% Monday. CME Group increased margin requirements on metals contracts due to volatility review, adding short-term downward pressure.

title: Materials Shares Follow Silver and Gold Lower -- Materials Roundup
summary: Mining-related stocks fell as gold, silver and copper prices reversed lower late in 2025. The article also says CME Group increased margin requirements for metals contracts after a normal volatility review, effective Monday. Shares of Newmont, Barrick, Freeport-McMoRan and Southern Copper declined as copper dropped 4.6%.

title: From Glencore trader to Indonesia's nickel king
summary: Bloomberg profiles Arif Kurniawan, a dominant Indonesian nickel ore trader with stakes across multiple concessions and an estimated large share of domestic ore trade. It links Indonesia’s rising role in global nickel supply to battery demand and notes potential political shakeups and export-banning risks, but provides no fresh immediate policy action.

title: Mining M&A 2026: behind Fortescue's bid for Peru's Alta Copper
summary: Fortescue’s executives’ visit to Peru preceded a four-year bid that would bring it to buy Alta Copper for more than $151 million. Alta shares rallied sharply during negotiations. The deal news is supportive for copper sentiment, though no immediate production or supply change is specified.

title: Hindustan Copper soars again! Stock jumps 7% after massive copper price rally | Indiablooms - First Portal on Digital News Management
summary: Hindustan Copper shares jumped nearly 7% in early trade after both domestic and LME-linked copper prices rallied. The move followed a 15% gain on Monday and reflects broad bullish sentiment, with copper up over 40% year-to-date and LME prices near $13,000 per tonne.

title: Critical Mineral Resources rises on Moroccan gold, copper samples
summary: Critical Mineral Resources said drilling at Morocco’s Agadir Melloul prospect produced encouraging near-surface assays, including 1.1% copper over 10 metres and up to 1.69% copper over one-metre intervals, alongside gold results. The update is early exploration, with further results expected in Jan–Feb.

title: Copper prices: What next for the red metal as LME prices hit record
summary: Copper prices are rising to record highs on the LME, with strong year-to-date gains. The article links the move to supply disruptions, a weakening U.S. dollar, improved Chinese growth expectations, and accelerating AI-driven data center demand, which tightens inventories. Analysts largely expect further upside into early 2026.

title: Kutcho Copper Corp.: Kutcho Copper Announces Closing of Flow-Through Financing
summary: Kutcho Copper Corp. closed a non-brokered flow-through financing to fund exploration on its Kutcho copper-zinc property in British Columbia. The release details unit terms, use of proceeds, commissions, and option grants. It does not report changes to production, shipments, or copper market fundamentals in the near term.

title: 2 arrested, charged with stealing copper from sites across Virginia: Police
summary: Police in Virginia arrested two men accused of stealing and causing property damage through a string of copper thefts across multiple jurisdictions. The investigation involves several local agencies and mentions recycled materials as part of the case, but provides no evidence of large-scale supply disruption beyond local theft losses.

title: Nickel hits nine-month high
summary: Nickel prices rose to a nine-month high after Indonesia signaled it will cut nickel supply to support prices. The Energy and Mineral Resources Minister said output in 2026 will be reduced and mining quotas (RKABs) tightened. Indonesia’s rising production has pressured LME stocks, but policy guidance is bullish for nickel.

title: Suspected copper thieves caught on camera
summary: Jackson Police are seeking suspects after copper thieves stole a large amount of copper from the Entergy Hinds Plant on Beasley Road around 3:30 a.m. Dec. 30. The investigation is ongoing and the public is asked to provide information; no copper price details are given.

title: Alara Resources Dispatches 32nd Copper Concentrate Shipment
summary: Alara Resources said it dispatched its 32nd shipment of copper concentrate from the Al Wash-hi–Majaza mine in Oman, departing Sohar Port on Dec. 30. The parcel totaled 1,378.6 WMT of concentrate, carrying about 252.6 MT of copper. Output is described as steady, with ongoing exports.

title: New Aluminum Projects in Indonesia Ramp Up, Boosting Daily Average Aluminum Production Outside China
summary: SMM data show overseas aluminium production rose in December as Indonesia’s new smelter projects began ramping up, lowering the overall operating rate dilution effect. The Indonesian PT Kalimantan Aluminium project started commissioning in late November. Rio Tinto secured a post-2028 energy approach for Tomago, while Mozal faces a planned maintenance shutdown around mid-March.

title: Ovoca Bio seals reverse takeover to become copper explorer Talisman
summary: Ovoca Bio will complete a reverse takeover to become Talisman Metals, refocusing on copper exploration in Morocco via Tadeen International’s permits (Tizert and Argana projects). The company will consolidate shares and raise GBP 1.2m for field work, but the deal size suggests limited immediate impact on copper prices.

title: Alarm Sounded! Domestic Social Inventory Surges by Over 70,000 mt in 9 Days, Copper Demand Frozen Amid High Prices
summary: SMM says high copper prices (LME peak, SHFE >100,000 yuan/mt) are freezing demand: operating rates across copper rod, wires/cables, sheet/strip and pipes/tubes fall, while social inventory of copper cathode surges from 159,000 mt to 238,900 mt in nine days (+70,500 mt). Aluminium substitution is beginning to be discussed.

title: Abitibi Metals Corp.: Abitibi Metals Issues Year-End Shareholder Letter as Copper Hits Record Highs
summary: Abitibi’s year-end letter notes copper is at record highs and describes progress at its B26 copper-gold project, including high-grade copper intercepts, increased ownership steps, and upcoming drilling and scoping-study milestones for 2026. It frames these developments within a supportive copper supply-demand backdrop and acquisition interest.

title: Tartisan Nickel Corp.: Tartisan Nickel Corp. Closes $1,000,000 Financing at $0.24 per Share
summary: Tartisan Nickel Corp. closed a C$1.0m flow-through financing at $0.24/share to fund Canadian exploration expenses and continue drilling at its Kenbridge nickel-copper-cobalt project in northwestern Ontario. The firm says assays are pending from a first completed hole and expects to update results as available.

title: Year-End Aluminum Ingot Inventory Alert Sounded! Domestic Inventory Buildup in Q1 2026 a Foregone Conclusion? [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports domestic aluminium ingot inventories rising sharply in late December and expects continued slight increases into early January 2026. Causes include resumed Xinjiang shipping, higher electrolytic production/casting volumes, traditional off-season demand weakness, and tighter environmental controls slowing warehouse withdrawals. High prices further suppress restocking, limiting inventory digestion.

title: Nickel Prices Jump After Top Producer Indonesia Signals 2026 Output Cut
summary: Indonesia’s Energy and Mineral Resources minister said the government will adjust nickel miners’ production quotas in 2026 to curb an oversupplied market and reduce environmental impacts. Following the signal, LME nickel inventories rose but nickel prices jumped, with spot and three-month contracts climbing sharply.

title: LNG, Mahenge Graphite, Kabanga Nickel lure US investors to Tanzania
summary: Tanzania and the U.S. held talks in Dar es Salaam focused on deepening economic cooperation, including U.S. interest in investing in the Kabanga Nickel project. While LNG and graphite are also mentioned, the nickel element could improve sentiment around future nickel supply, supporting near-term price expectations.

title: FinancialContent - Metals Maintain Bullish Momentum: Gold, Silver, and Copper Defy Year-End Retreat to Hold Key Support Levels
summary: The piece argues that copper remains supported into year-end, holding above its 50-day moving average near $5.20/lb and trading around $5.67/lb. It attributes the resilience to a widening structural supply deficit, boosted by AI data-center demand and grid electrification, maintaining an upward near-term bias.

title: FinancialContent - The Red Metal's Golden Year: Unpacking the 2025 Copper Super-Rally
summary: The article attributes copper’s 2025 “super-rally” to AI-driven demand growth, supply disruptions including a Grasberg force majeure removing about 250,000 tonnes, labor/grade issues at Escondida, and late-year policy moves tightening refined output. It highlights depleted inventories and a likely continued deficit into 2026.

title: China's Refined Copper Exports Expected to Remain Above 100kt in January 2026
summary: China’s refined copper cathode exports are expected to remain above 100kt in January 2026, with 100,000–110,000 tonnes projected. Elevated shipments reflect negative copper concentrate TCs squeezing smelters and continued demand for spot supplies, while US-bound volumes are set to decline and Middle East/SEA/Europe increase.

title: Metso seals Grupo Mexico copper plant contract
summary: Metso won a major contract to supply cone crushers for Grupo Mexico’s La Caridad copper concentrator in Mexico and booked further equipment and services for Almalyk MMC’s new copper smelter in Uzbekistan. These orders support copper processing capacity development and associated near-term supply expectations.

title: Copper records biggest annual gain since 2009 on supply bets
summary: Copper’s best year since 2009 is linked to tighter near-term supply bets. Traders ship copper to the US ahead of potential tariffs, tightening ex-US availability and narrowing the price spread. Additional supply strain comes from accidents and floods at major mines in Indonesia, DRC, and Chile, despite some demand softness in China.

title: Year-End Volatility in the Copper Scrap Market: The Supply-Demand Dilemma Amid High-Price Suppression and Policy Uncertainty
summary: Copper scrap prices softened after a rapid earlier rise, with sluggish trading and overseas holiday disruptions halting imports of recycled inputs. Domestic secondary copper rod demand stayed weak as firms deferred restocking under high copper prices, year-end cash pressures, and policy/subsidy uncertainty plus tighter reverse-invoicing scrutiny. Prices and spreads narrowed mid-week.

title: Copper's Big Year—Best Since 2009—Ends on a Low Note
summary: Copper ended 2025 slightly lower, with prices falling about 2% to roughly $5.67 per pound on Dec. 31. The move is described as part of a broader decline across the metal market after a strong year for the red metal.

title: FinancialContent - Institutional Rebalancing Amidst Record Metal Prices: Ninety One UK Ltd Trims Stake in Freeport-McMoRan
summary: Ninety One UK Ltd trimmed about 879,341 shares of Freeport-McMoRan after the Grasberg Block Cave mudslide triggered force majeure and ongoing litigation. While the wider disruption supports a copper supply tightening narrative and strong copper prices, the share sale itself is mainly portfolio rebalancing, suggesting limited immediate copper-price pressure.

title: Capstone Copper Corp.: Capstone Copper Provides Update on Labour Negotiations at Mantoverde Operation
summary: Capstone Copper said Union #2 at its Mantoverde mine in Chile will strike effective Jan. 2, 2026, after failed collective bargaining talks. During the strike, Mantoverde output is expected to fall gradually to as high as 30% of normal production. The firm continues negotiations and legal procedures.

title: SpaceX nickel supplier buys into ASX-listed metals group's $3.6 billion Indonesia project
summary: Sphere Corp, a key nickel supplier to SpaceX, will take a 10% stake in Nickel Industries’ Excelsior nickel-cobalt project in Indonesia, valuing it at $3.6 billion. Sphere has also signed a 10-year SpaceX supply deal worth about $1 billion and will receive nickel cathode output with volume options at market prices.

title: Capstone Copper Provides Update on Labour Negotiations At Mantoverde Operation
summary: Capstone Copper said Union #2 at its Mantoverde operation in Chile, covering about half of employees in that union group, will strike starting Jan. 2, 2026. Capstone expects to keep output at up to 30% of normal during the strike, gradually reducing some mine activities.

title: [SMM Analysis] The Paradox Behind the Stagnation of EU Internal Copper Scrap Trade and the Surge in Outflows
summary: EU copper scrap flows are falling sharply within the bloc, with internal trade declining more than exports. The drop is driven by weak European demand and higher smelter costs, plus a front-running effect as stricter EU customs monitoring and a future export ban approach. Industry groups warn the recycling market may collapse.

title: Copper keeps on rising, aluminium hits three-and-a-half year top
summary: London copper rose nearly 1% to $12,537/tonne, continuing into the new year after a record 2025 rally. LME aluminium was little changed but reached its highest since May 2022 near $2,998/tonne. The piece attributes support to a weaker US dollar and firmer China demand signals.

title: 2026 Metals Outlook: Copper, Aluminium Deficit; Iron Ore to Fall
summary: ING expects 2026 to be characterized by tightness in copper and aluminium. Copper is forecast in a large deficit due to disruptions at Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, and El Teniente plus tariff-related trade distortions. Aluminium should also remain in deficit from China’s capacity cap and power constraints, while nickel stays surplus.

title: 2026 Metals Outlook: Copper, Aluminium Deficit; Iron Ore to Fall
summary: ING’s Metals Outlook for 2026 expects a refined copper deficit (~600kt) from high demand and outages/disruptions in Indonesia, DRC and Chile, alongside tariff-driven trade flow distortions. Aluminium is also projected in deficit (~200kt) due to China’s capacity cap and power constraints. Nickel is seen in surplus, with regulatory scrutiny and softer demand.

title: Copper keeps on rising, aluminium hits three-and-a-half year top
summary: London copper rose nearly 1% to about $12,537/tonne, after a strong 2025 and record levels, supported by a weaker US dollar and demand from AI and renewables. LME aluminium was little changed but reached its highest since May 2022 around $2,998/tonne, indicating bullish near-term sentiment.

title: FinancialContent - Yields on the Rise: The 2026 Bond Sell-Off and the New American Economic Reality
summary: The article links the 2026 Treasury yield sell-off to higher cost of capital, but highlights a divergence where industrial metals—especially copper—benefit from electrification. It argues AI-driven data-center build-outs and grid modernization are boosting power demand, supporting copper prices trending toward ~$13,000/tonne.

title: FinancialContent - South Korea's Sphere Secures $2.4 Billion Foothold in Indonesian Nickel as Global Supply Chain Bifurcates
summary: Sphere Corp bought a 10% stake in Indonesia’s Excelsior Nickel Cobalt (ENC) HPAL project for about $2.4B, securing proportional offtake tied to high-purity nickel cathode. The deal reinforces tighter Indonesian quota expectations and could affect market pricing if commissioning or output is delayed.

title: Aluminum hits $3,000 on supply concern
summary: Aluminium rose above $3,000/ton for the first time since 2022 as investors priced tighter supply after China capped smelting capacity and Europe faced output constraints from higher electricity prices, drawing down inventories. The piece also notes copper gains on tight supply and nickel strength following a Vale Indonesia mining halt.

title: Miners go on strike at Capstone Copper's Mantoverde mine in Chile after talks fail
summary: Hundreds of miners at Capstone Copper’s Mantoverde mine in northern Chile began a strike after labor contract talks failed. The union expects losses up to $160 million and says it can sustain the strike for at least two months. Capstone expects output to run at up to 30% during the stoppage.

title: Ivanhoe Mines begins copper anode production at new Congo smelter
summary: Ivanhoe Mines began producing copper anodes at Kamoa-Kakula’s DRC direct-to-blister smelter, with first output in late December and ramp-up toward 500,000 tpa capacity. The company expects anode production to complete by year-end, alongside further mine dewatering progress supporting future copper supply.

title: Aluminum Hits $3,000 for First Time Since 2022 on Supply Concern
summary: Aluminum prices reportedly hit $3,000 for the first time since 2022, with the move attributed to supply concerns. Tighter expected availability in the near term would reduce prompt supply and typically supports higher aluminium benchmarks as traders adjust for a potential supply shortfall.

title: Copper, Aluminium Rally to Drive Up Appliance Prices
summary: Industrial metals surged as supply tightened and demand stayed robust. Aluminium broke above $3,000/t for the first time in over three years on smelting caps and high power costs, while copper neared record levels due to disruptions in Indonesia, Chile and the DRC plus Chilean labour unrest. Nickel also rose on Indonesia supply concerns.

title: Copper, Aluminium Rally to Drive Up Appliance Prices
summary: Copper, aluminium, and nickel surged sharply as supply tightened and demand stayed robust. Copper pushed above $12,000/ton with major Chile mine unrest, Indonesian/DRC/Chile disruptions, and accelerated US-bound shipments. Aluminium rose above $3,000/ton on China smelting caps and high European power costs. Nickel advanced on Indonesia output cuts and PT Vale halt.

title: Somany: Rising Copper Prices to Drive Up Costs for Consumers in 2023, ETRetail
summary: Copper prices have surged to record highs, prompting appliance, cookware, and bathware brands to announce 5–7% and other price hikes due to higher input costs. The piece also links broader industrial-metal strength, including aluminium, to cost pressure, citing MCX gains and company margin protection.

title: Bullion rally! Which metal stock to buy amid ongoing surge in gold, silver and copper rates?
summary: Copper is reported firm on MCX, with strength attributed to structural electrification and an estimated global deficit in 2025–26, suggesting supportive near-term expectations. Silver is also discussed, while aluminium appears mainly via Hindalco’s outlook with assumed aluminium price ranges, offering weaker, indirect signals.

title: Nickel Industries says S Korea's Sphere to buy 10% stake in Indonesian project
summary: Nickel Industries said South Korea’s Sphere Corp will buy a 10% stake in its Excelsior nickel-cobalt HPAL project in Indonesia at a $2.4 billion valuation. Sphere will offtake nickel as cathode material. The deal aligns with ongoing Indonesia supply support plans, boosting nickel sentiment.

title: Open to Vedanta to File Plea Before Authorities Over Green Copper Plant: Madras HC
summary: Madras High Court told Vedanta’s Sterlite Copper unit it may file a fresh application with Tamil Nadu authorities regarding its proposed “green copper” plant and process changes. The court noted earlier consent/violation-based closures and Supreme Court challenges. It allowed recommencement through formal approvals, with decisions pending.

title: Open to Vedanta to file plea before authorities over green copper plant: Madras HC
summary: Madras High Court said Vedanta can file a fresh application with competent authorities for its proposed “green copper” plant in Tamil Nadu. The court noted earlier consent/breach issues and emphasized proper applications. While no production restart is confirmed, the ruling supports process advancement for Sterlite Copper.

title: Policy-Driven Path to Scale, Intensification and Green Growth in China's Alumina Sector
summary: China’s NDRC policy urges tighter regulation and faster consolidation in resource-intensive sectors like alumina and copper smelting. The article describes China’s alumina overcapacity, high inventories, and rising energy/environment compliance costs, with stricter approvals and integration expected. Near term, surplus and inventory pressure point to weaker aluminium sentiment, and any copper effect is indirect.

title: Mining Lease Application at Big One Copper | Company Announcement
summary: New Frontier Minerals reports its mining lease application for the Big One Copper Deposit has progressed into the technical assessment phase in Queensland. The deposit hosts copper resources and has test-work supporting conventional sulphuric-acid leaching via Austral Resources’ Mt Kelly facility, but no immediate production is indicated.

title: Ivanhoe Mines begins copper anode production at smelter in Africa
summary: Ivanhoe Mines reportedly started copper anode production at a smelter in Africa. The ramp-up of anode output implies additional copper supply moving toward refinement in the near term, which can strengthen expectations for available refined copper and provide mild upward pressure on copper prices over the coming days.

title: Overview of Venezuela's Aluminum Industry Chain
summary: The article discusses Venezuela’s aluminum chain amid a U.S. strike on Caracas on Jan 3 and concerns about supply disruption. Venezuela has very low operating rates and minimal exports, so even if localized disruptions occur in the bauxite/alumina/smelting cluster, near-term global aluminum impact is expected to be limited and mainly sentiment-driven.

title: China's Blister Copper RCs Surge, Supply Growth as Core Driver [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports China’s blister copper refinery charges (RCs) rose MoM in both south and north regions, with supply expansion from wider primary-vs-scrap spreads boosting scrap-derived blister copper and copper anode availability. Smelters reduced year-end procurement, loosening secondary inputs; January is expected to stay loose despite gradual restocking demand.

title: DR Congo partially lifts suspension on copper-cobalt processing after compliance review-Xinhua
summary: The DRC Ministry of Mines partially and temporarily lifted a Dec. 19 suspension on copper-cobalt processing after a compliance review in Lualaba Province. Processing entities operating exclusively in Lualaba can resume, and Haut-Katanga firms may process stockpiled minerals under supervision, pending inspections. The move targets OECD due-diligence compliance and traceability.

title: Copper climbs to record high above $13,000 after strike at Chilean mine
summary: Copper surged above $13,000/t, with the rally driven by intensifying supply concerns after a strike at Chile’s Mantoverde mine, expectations of deficits, and a sharp fall in LME-approved warehouse stocks. Aluminium also rose on worries about shortages, including China’s output cap.

title: Global Copper Smelting: What to Expect in 2026
summary: Fastmarkets reports copper smelters face worsening profitability with record-low (and often negative) concentrate TC/RCs and negotiations still unresolved for 2026 supply. It expects higher volatility and potential production cuts/disruptions, which should tighten refined supply and support further rises in LME copper prices, even as TC/RCs fall.

title: Record copper price signals accelerating race for supplies
summary: Copper prices surged to records above $13,000/t as traders and analysts flagged tightening supply.
