News around potential tariff risks for U.S. imports, rapid U.S. warehouse stock gains ahead of levies, and recent mine disruptions (Grasberg and Capstone) reinforced shortage fears amid strong AI/data centre and EV demand expectations.

title: Viewpoint: US copper faces uncertain 2026 outlook
summary: US copper outlook is expected to stay volatile as tariff-related spreads and high US CME inventories influence near-term trading. Market participants largely expect stronger 1H 2026 prices supported by AI/data-center demand, a weaker dollar from Fed easing, and tighter mine supply, though some doubt sharp gains due to ample stocks and slower growth risk.

title: Chile's $14.8 Billion Copper Pipeline Faces 2026 Test as Prices Hit Record Highs
summary: Chile’s copper project pipeline totaling $14.8 billion faces a 2026 test as analysts warn supply may not keep pace with demand. Some projects may start producing next year, but timing risk remains from permitting and community issues. Investors also expect President Kast’s pro-investment stance could speed approvals, supporting prices.

title: Major Chilean Copper Mine Slows Production Amid Strike
summary: Workers at Capstone Copper’s Mantoverde mine in Chanaral, Chile, began a strike on Jan 2. The operation is running at up to 30% of normal capacity while talks/mediation are pending. With large portions of staff on strike, near-term copper supply is reduced, supporting prices.

title: Commodities: Record copper price signals accelerating race for supplies
summary: Copper prices rose to record levels above $13,000/t amid fears of shortages and supply-chain risk linked to Venezuela and broader critical-minerals themes. Analysts cite mine disruptions, a refined copper production deficit estimate, and uncertainty around possible U.S. import tariffs that have driven anticipatory stock movements.

title: Cashing in on illegal copper trade
summary: Malaysia reports a surge in copper theft and vandalism linked to higher copper prices, with thieves targeting telco and power cables and other public infrastructure items. Unlicensed foreign scrap collectors offer higher cash prices, complicating enforcement and potentially tightening copper scrap supply. Aluminium scrap collection is also referenced but less directly.

title: Northern B.C. copper-gold mine to increase production
summary: British Columbia approved Mount Milligan’s nine-month environmental review, allowing the copper-gold mine near Fort St. James to expand production and operate until 2035. Ore output is expected to rise from 60,000 to 66,500 tonnes per day, supported by pit deepening and tailings dam modifications, with permits expected soon.

title: Alumina Production Costs Continue to Decline in December Yet Nearly Half of Plants Face Cash Cost Pressure
summary: SMM says alumina full costs fell 1.93% month-on-month in December, helped by a weaker US dollar, lower caustic soda prices, and slightly cheaper thermal coal. Bauxite inventories rose and long-term ore contract prices fell. January is expected to bring further cost declines, easing cash-cost pressure for many plants.

title: Kamoa-Kakula smelter produces first copper anodes
summary: Ivanhoe Mines says its Kamoa-Kakula smelter in the DRC has produced the first copper anodes, following heat-up and initial concentrate feed. The facility is ramping to 500,000 tonnes/year of high-purity anodes, supporting copper sales as concentrate inventories decline during 2026.

title: Copper Extends Rally, Bursting Through $13,000 a Ton
summary: Copper prices extended their rally, breaking above $13,000/ton as markets priced tighter supply from mine disruptions, including a strike at Chile’s Mantoverde, and heightened U.S. tariff uncertainty. Traders increased refined copper shipments to the U.S., raising concerns about supply squeezing and reduced availability elsewhere.

title: European Midday Briefing : Oil Prices Slide, Copper Hits Record High
summary: Copper prices climbed to a record high above $13,000/mt, driven by concerns over tightening supply and uncertainty around U.S. tariffs. The piece links tariff-related contract shifts to supply tightening outside the U.S. Overall market coverage also notes miners rising alongside copper and precious metals gains.

title: Copper, gold and BTC: A macro signal to watch
summary: The article argues that the copper-to-gold ratio has broken out, signaling a shift toward risk-on economic momentum. It points to copper pushing above $6/lb and gaining about 18% over three months, implying improving growth expectations. It extrapolates this macro shift to potential bitcoin strength into 2026.

title: Copper thefts cause $30K damage to Pittsylvania phone towers
summary: Virginia authorities arrested two men for stealing copper from phone towers in Pittsylvania County, taking an estimated $3,000 worth of copper and causing about $30,000 in damage. The sheriff linked the theft motive to increasing copper prices, but the scale is small and local, limiting market impact.

title: Copper Extends Rally, Bursting Through $13,000 a Ton -- Update
summary: Copper prices surged to record highs above $13,000/ton on worries about tighter supply and U.S. tariff uncertainty. Mine disruptions, including a strike at Chile’s Mantoverde, and U.S. heavy stockpiling ahead of possible refined copper duties have squeezed supply and supported bullish momentum into the June 30 tariff decision.

title: Alba hits record 1.623MT aluminium production in 2025
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) said it produced a record 1.623Mt of aluminium in 2025, slightly above 2024, surpassing its annual target despite an industrial fire. The company also reported two consecutive years of LTI-free operations and plans to build on performance.

title: Copper strides to record high after fresh mine disruptions
summary: Copper hit record highs and nickel jumped to a 19-month peak as supply disruptions and delays raised concerns about near-term tightness. A strike at Capstone’s Mantoverde mine in Chile and delays to Tongling’s Ecuador project were cited. Nickel gains were reinforced by Indonesia plans to cut ore output. Aluminium rose as well.

title: FinancialContent - Copper's "Red Gold" Era: Prices Breach $13,000 as Global Supply Chains Fracture
summary: Copper prices surpassed $13,000/t on the LME amid acute physical scarcity and deep backwardation. The rally is attributed to supply cuts from Chilean and Indonesian mine disruptions, output guidance reductions in DRC, and tariff-linked pre-shipment hoarding that left regional inventories tight. The market expects a sizable 2026 refined deficit.

title: FinancialContent - Aluminum Breaks $3,000 Barrier as Base Metals Super-Cycle Intensifies; NALCO and Hindalco Hit Record Highs
summary: Aluminum surged above $3,000/t on the LME, with buyers citing enforced China primary output caps, high European smelter energy costs, and “green aluminum” premiums tightening LME-grade availability. The rally is echoed by record copper and improved nickel prices, reflecting electrification-driven demand and a carbon-border-driven supply vacuum.

title: Copper Extends Rally, Bursting Through $13,000 a Ton -- Commodities Roundup
summary: LME three-month copper futures extend their rally, topping $13,000/ton and reaching new records. Gains are attributed to tightening supply from mine disruptions and heavy U.S. stockpiling, alongside uncertainty that U.S. tariffs on refined metal imports could be introduced this year. Other commodities in the roundup move higher as well.

title: FinancialContent - The Great Convergence: Gold, Copper, and Equities Shatter Records as 2026 Opens with a Geopolitical Jolt
summary: Early January 2026, the article links a U.S. extraction operation in Venezuela and broader monetary easing to a surge in commodities. Copper breaks $13,000/ton as AI-driven data center demand is said to have depleted inventories and left a projected 400,000-ton deficit, indicating bullish near-term price pressure.

title: FinancialContent - The Red Metal Revolution: How Copper is Replacing Silver in the Global Solar Race
summary: LONGi and other solar players are commercializing copper-metallized PV cells to replace volatile, expensive silver paste. The shift is framed as solving a 2025 silver supply/demand squeeze and reducing module costs. Copper demand is expected to rise as plating lines scale, though major ramp is later in 2026.

title: B.C. approves extending life of Mt. Milligan copper and gold mine to 2035
summary: British Columbia approved an amendment extending the Mt. Milligan copper and gold mine to 2035 and expanding its footprint by 80 hectares. The approval is expected to increase ore output by 6,500 tonnes per day and raise tailings dam height. Further permitting decisions are expected soon, supporting copper production continuity.

title: UBS: "Copper Is The Commodity Everyone Wants To Own"
summary: UBS and Goldman highlight a sharp rally in LME copper, with three-month futures hitting record levels above $13,000/t. Traders are pricing tighter global supply due to tariff uncertainty over US imports of refined copper, causing inventory imbalances, speculative positioning, and support from ongoing mine setbacks and strong end-demand.

title: Targeting $14K For Copper: Max Layton
summary: Copper extended its rally, breaking above $13,000/ton for the first time. Citi commodity research head Max Layton said he remains bullish in the near term and now targets copper around $14,000/ton. The commentary is presented as part of a market outlook discussion on Bloomberg.

title: Nickel price surge: Vale Indonesia halts operations sending nickel to 15-month high
summary: Nickel prices surged to a 15-month high after Vale halted operations in Indonesia. The stoppage tightens short-term supply from Indonesia, a key low-cost nickel producer used in stainless steel. With oversupply previously pressuring the market, the disruption provides immediate support, boosting price expectations for nearby weeks.

title: Nickel prices hit 15-month high on robust sentiment
summary: Nickel prices surged on 6 January, with LME nickel above $18,000/t and SHFE hitting its daily limit, supported by robust sentiment and possible changes to Indonesia’s mining plans. Market discussion centers on an RKAB cut and potential export-benchmark/tariff mechanisms, while copper strength also lifted nickel.

title: How Will Mining Giants Adapt as Copper Tops $13,000?
summary: Copper prices have surged above $13,000/t on the LME amid severe physical scarcity, sharp drops in inventories outside the US, and deep backwardation. Tariffs on semi-finished and possible refined copper increases are redirecting shipments to the US, worsening regional imbalances. Supply disruptions and labor risks further tighten near-term availability.

title: Arizona Sonoran Copper Company Inc. Grants Dust Permit for the Cactus Project
summary: Arizona Sonoran Copper Company said it received a dust permit for its Cactus copper project, the first post–pre-feasibility permit. The PFS targets about 113,000 short tons of copper cathode annually for the first 10 years. The company plans to re-apply for amended permits ahead of a feasibility study.

title: What's Behind Copper's Rally to a Record High?
summary: The piece reviews the factors behind copper’s move to a record high above $13,000/ton for the first time, citing Morgan Stanley’s metals strategist. It is focused on explaining the rally rather than describing a clear new immediate supply, demand, or policy event that would independently pressure prices in days.

title: Mercuria & Glencore Seal Major Copper Offtake Deals
summary: Mercuria signed a copper-concentrate offtake deal with Geotechmin for Ellatzite mine output in 2026, including a $250m prepayment facility. Additional copper-of-take/financing efforts involving Glencore (via Orion) are discussed. The coverage frames a tightening copper market and lower concentrate TC levels.

title: FinancialContent - Metals in Retreat: Silver and Copper Cool as Wall Street Hits Record Milestones
summary: On Jan 7, industrial metals declined as CME raised margin requirements for precious metals futures, triggering leveraged deleveraging. Investors rotated from “safe havens” into equities as AI-driven risk-on sentiment grew and the US dollar strengthened, pressuring dollar-denominated commodities including copper (notably around $4.50/lb).

title: Aluminum surges as AI data centers strain power supply
summary: Aluminum prices are rising as AI-driven data centers intensify electricity demand, pushing up power availability and costs. The report cites smelter concerns, including operations at major producers facing challenges due to soaring electricity prices. Given aluminum’s heavy electricity requirements, the market anticipates supply disruptions.

title: Comex Copper Settles 3.35% Lower at $5.8090 — Data Talk
summary: Comex copper for January delivery settled 3.35% lower at $5.8090, down 20.15 cents per pound. The move was the largest one-day dollar and percentage decline since Monday, Dec. 29, ending a three-session winning streak and pulling prices 3.35% below the Jan. 6 2026 high.

title: August: Copper theft putting lives at risk | Mayerthorpe Freelancer
summary: The Wetaskiwin area has seen more than a dozen incidents of theft and vandalism on CPKC Rail properties, including generators and cables being cut for the copper wire between Ponoka and Wetaskiwin in 2025. The theft is described as putting lives at risk, signaling disruption and extra costs.

title: August: Copper theft putting lives at risk | Edmonton Examiner
summary: The Edmonton Examiner reports more than a dozen incidents of theft or vandalism on CPKC Rail properties in 2025, including cutting generators and copper-wire cables between Ponoka and Wetaskiwin. The theft is framed as a safety risk, but the disruption is localized with unclear material impact on broader copper supply.

title: Cable thefts amid rising copper prices having wide impact in local communities
summary: Rising copper prices are driving increased theft of copper cables in Kentucky, leading to 911 and internet outages. Incidents include 1,500 feet stolen in Laurel County and thousands of destructive attacks nationwide over the past year. Kinetic urges vigilance and offers rewards to deter theft.

title: AI to boost copper demand 50% by 2040, but more mines needed to ensure supply, S&P says
summary: S&P Global says AI and defense will lift global copper demand by about 50% by 2040, but supply may fall short by more than 10 million tonnes annually without more recycling and mining. It links demand to electrification and new data centers and defense spending, supporting expectations of future tightness.

title: Global copper squeeze set to intensify on AI, defence spending
summary: S&P Global warns the copper market could tighten further as AI, data centres and defence spending boost demand while mine supply faces structural limits. Copper has already hit record highs above $13,000/t on mine outages and US warehouse stockpiling ahead of possible tariffs, reinforcing bullish near-term expectations.

title: Nalco, Hind Copper shares fall up to 5% to hit one-week low as global metal prices retreat
summary: Shares of Nalco and Hindalco slid up to 5% after a six-day rally as investors booked profits and global metal prices retreated. The Nifty Metal index dropped 3% for a second day. The move followed declines in other metals such as gold and silver, signaling weaker sentiment toward copper and aluminium.

title: The world's copper squeeze is set to intensify on AI and defence spending: S&P
summary: S&P Global says AI spending and surging defence demand could intensify a projected copper shortage as mine supply hits structural constraints. Copper is at record highs, with additional US stockpiling ahead of potential tariffs. The study highlights accelerating demand from data centres, EVs, grids and robotics amid long supply timelines.

title: Copper Plate/Sheet and Strip Industry: Operating Rate in December Falls Short of Expectations, Downward Pressure Intensifies in January
summary: SMM reports copper plate/sheet and strip operating rates fell to 68.21% in December and are expected to drop further to 67.2% in January. The sharp rise in copper prices reduced downstream order volumes and raised inventory days, with additional pressure from secondary-copper policy impacts on specific bronze production.

title: [SMM Analysis] Nickel's Counter-Seasonal Spike Opens Arbitrage Opportunities: Catalysts & Outlook for High-Grade NPI Price
summary: SMM reports nickel and SHFE nickel futures have risen, creating structural arbitrage versus non-standard high-grade NPI prices. Despite off-season stainless demand and high NPI inventories, upstream and downstream are executing more high-priced trades (980–995 yuan/mtu). With ore costs lower and potential stainless price recovery, NPI acceptance may rise toward 980 yuan/mtu within a month.

title: Copper demand: AI and defence spending to widen supply gap for the red metal
summary: The piece argues that copper’s supply deficit will worsen, driven by rising demand tied to electrification, electric vehicles, renewables, AI, and defence spending. It notes major miners are competing for copper exposure, suggesting expectations of tighter supply and stronger competition among producers.

title: Copper theft causes blackout in Newcastle suburbs | Muswellbrook Chronicle
summary: Suspected copper theft is blamed for a blackout affecting 1,500+ homes in Newcastle suburbs after damage to Ausgrid’s 11 kV lines. Police are investigating possible attempted theft. Ausgrid warns theft leaves powerlines exposed and notes heatwave conditions could further stress the grid into the weekend.

title: Copper theft causes blackout in Newcastle suburbs | The Scone Advocate
summary: A suspected copper theft is blamed for a blackout affecting over 1,000 homes in Newcastle suburbs. Damage to Ausgrid’s 11 kV lines at Cooks Hill was found during investigation. Crews restored power gradually while the network also prepared for heatwave grid pressure, but the copper theft is local.

title: AI Set to Drive 50% Rise in Copper Demand by 2040
summary: Oilprice.com cites an S&P Global report saying AI could lift global copper demand and contribute to a long-run supply gap by 2040. It argues electrification and data centers require significant copper, potentially raising demand from 28 million tons (2025) to 42 million tons (2040). The article implies future tightness, not near-term shocks.

title: Aluminium Price Surge Forecast for 2026 on Supply-Demand Gap
summary: Analysts forecast aluminium prices to remain firm in 2026, citing China’s output cap at a 45-million-tonne ceiling that restricts supply growth. Demand support from EVs, renewables and infrastructure is expected to rise, while Europe smelter shutdowns and Guinea raw-material bottlenecks limit offsetting supply.

title: Copper theft causes blackout in Newcastle suburbs | Dungog Chronicle
summary: Suspected copper theft is blamed for a blackout affecting about 1,500 homes across Newcastle suburbs, with damage found to Ausgrid’s 11 kV lines at Cooks Hill. Power was restored by Friday morning. Ausgrid warns copper theft creates lethal hazards, amid heatwave grid stress.

title: Perseverance Metals Inc.: Perseverance Metals Intersects High Grade 4.07% Nickel over 2.1m with 0.69% Copper, 0.12% Cobalt, and 1.86g/t PGEs from Baseline Zone Discovery, Lac Gayot Project, Québec
summary: Perseverance Metals reported additional drill assays from the Baseline Zone at the Lac Gayot project, including a 2.1m massive sulphide intersection with high nickel and copper grades, alongside cobalt and PGE values. Management highlights expanding conductive targets for follow-up drilling. The update may modestly support sentiment for nickel and copper.

title: JPMorgan downgrades Alcoa following strong run, sees aluminum pricing 'leveling out'
summary: JPMorgan downgraded Alcoa to underweight, citing valuation risk after a 74% stock rally and expecting aluminum prices to ‘level out.’ The note points to higher Chinese aluminum inventories versus December averages, resistance to higher prices, Indonesia supply risks, and tariffs as near-term overhangs.

title: ADC12 Weekly Increase Exceeds 1,200 yuan/mt, Market Competition Intensifies Amid Caution Over Correction Risks[Weekly Review of Aluminum Scrap and Secondary Aluminum]
summary: The report says secondary aluminum scrap and ADC12 spot prices surged in line with sharp primary aluminum gains, but downstream buying resistance increased as costs outpaced finished alloy prices. Secondary producers’ operating rates declined, transactions slowed, and pre–Chinese New Year stocking weakened. It expects prices to fluctuate at highs with correction pressure.

title: Core Silver Corp.: Core Silver Extends Porphyry System 450 Metres South At Laverdiere Copper Project
summary: Core Silver reported drill hole LAV25-012 intersected additional copper-bearing intervals, confirming a 450-metre southern extension of the Laverdiere Cu-Mo-Ag porphyry system. While the results may modestly support copper-focused market sentiment, there is no indication of near-term changes to mined output, inventories, or refined metal flows.

title: Tariffs and low stocks propel aluminium costs to records for US consumers
summary: Reuters reports US aluminium consumers facing record high prices as Trump’s doubled 50% tariff on imports and low US inventories amplify supply tightness. LME aluminium is up more than 20% over 12 months, while US premiums and shipments adjust, shrinking stocks below 300,000 tons, raising costs for manufacturers and inflation concerns.

title: The World's Copper Squeeze Is Set to Intensify on AI and Defense Spending, S&P Says
summary: S&P expects the global copper market’s supply-demand balance to tighten further as AI and defense spending increases demand. With a worsening “copper squeeze,” the market may anticipate more limited near-term availability, supporting higher copper prices over the coming days to weeks.

title: Copper theft causes blackout in Newcastle suburbs | Port Stephens Examiner
summary: Suspected copper theft caused damage to Ausgrid’s 11 kV power lines in Newcastle suburbs, leading to a blackout affecting over 1,000 homes, with service restored overnight. Authorities say the damage is consistent with attempted theft and warn about safety risks. The grid is also facing heatwave pressure.

title: Copper theft causes blackout in Newcastle suburbs | Camden Haven Courier
summary: Suspected copper theft is blamed for a blackout affecting more than 1,000 homes across Newcastle suburbs after damage to Ausgrid’s 11 kV power lines. Police said the damage looks consistent with attempted theft. The utility warns copper thieves create lethal hazards, and crews restored power by Friday morning.

title: GIADEC secures strategic investors for VALCO modernisation and alumina refinery project
summary: GIADEC says it has secured strategic investors for VALCO’s modernisation and an alumina refinery in Ghana. The projects are framed as interdependent: the refinery would feed the smelter and support downstream aluminium manufacturing, with plans to raise VALCO output substantially from 2026 onward.

title: FinancialContent - Strategic Pivot: American Lithium Minerals Stakes Claim in Chile's Silver and Copper Corridors
summary: American Lithium Minerals secured exclusive options to acquire 100% of two Chile projects, including the Furano copper-gold porphyry, which reported 0.9% copper equivalent in shallow drilling and is located near BHP’s Cerro Colorado. The deal closes in Q1 2026 after faster permitting, boosting expectations for future copper supply.

title: Copper theft causes blackout in Newcastle suburbs | The Singleton Argus
summary: Suspected copper theft was blamed for an Ausgrid blackout affecting about 1,500–1,200 homes in Newcastle suburbs. Crews found damage to 11 kV power lines, with police suggesting attempted theft. Ausgrid warned copper theft endangers public safety and noted heatwave pressure on the grid.

title: FinancialContent - Gold and Copper Rally Propels Centerra Gold to 22% Revenue Surge Amid Global Metals Boom
summary: Centerra Gold reported a 22% year-over-year revenue rise, attributing it to record-high gold and copper prices plus improved mine throughput and recovery at Mount Milligan. With copper testing about $5.80/lb, the article frames strong cash flow and operational upgrades as boosting copper producer sentiment in early 2026.

title: FinancialContent - Copper's Red-Hot Ascent: Bernstein Forecasts $11,500 Peak as AI and Supply Shocks Collide
summary: Bernstein forecasts copper averaging $11,500/tonne in Q1 2026 after record highs, attributing gains to major supply disruptions, a sizable ICSG deficit, and strong AI data-center demand. The report warns of possible later momentum fade and notes substitution toward aluminum if copper stays elevated.

title: Koryx Copper seeks to raise N$300m for Haib Project
summary: Canadian company Koryx Copper plans to raise C$25 million via a share offering to fund technical studies, exploration, working capital, and general purposes for its Haib copper project in Namibia. The company also holds copper exploration licences on the Zambian Copperbelt. No near-term production changes are stated.

title: FinancialContent - Tariffs and Toasts: Constellation Brands Beats Estimates Amid Surging Aluminum Costs
summary: Constellation Brands reported a Q3 beat but warned that a 50% U.S. aluminum import tariff keeps pressuring packaging costs. The tariff has pushed the Midwest Premium to record levels, driving higher can prices. Management and peers discuss lightweighting and possible shifts from aluminum cans to PET/glass if premiums stay elevated.

title: Comex Copper Settles 1.08% Lower at $5.7465 — Data Talk
summary: COMEX front-month copper for January delivery settled 1.08% lower at $5.7465 per pound, down 6.25 cents. It marked the second consecutive session decline and was off about 4.39% over two sessions. The contract remains up versus the prior year lows but below recent highs.

title: [SMM Analysis] The global nickel market experienced a roller coaster ride this week, while domestic inventory continued to increase significantly.
summary: The report describes sharp volatility in global nickel prices driven by expectations around Indonesia’s 2026 nickel ore quotas, then undermined by weak downstream demand and a sudden LME inventory surge (+20,000 mt in one day). Nickel prices corrected late in the week as sentiment shifted to caution.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Completes Previously Announced Acquisition of Lundin Mining's Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill Operations Creating a Multi-Asset U.S. Nickel-Copper Company
summary: Talon Metals completed its acquisition of Lundin Mining’s producing Eagle Mine and associated Humboldt Mill in the U.S., positioning Talon as an operating primary nickel-copper producer. The release highlights ongoing mine life extension, permitting, and exploration acceleration, which could support near-term expectations for nickel and copper supply.

title: Talon Metals Corp.: Talon Metals Completes Previously Announced Acquisition of Lundin Mining's Eagle Mine and Humboldt Mill Operations Creating a Multi-Asset U.S. Nickel-Copper Company
summary: Talon Metals announced completion of its acquisition of Lundin Mining’s producing Eagle Mine and the associated Humboldt Mill in Michigan. The deal positions Talon as a multi-asset U.S. primary nickel-copper operator and supports ongoing production and processing, potentially improving short-term expectations for nickel and copper supply.

title: Copper supplies set to peak just as tech needs more
summary: A study warns copper supply will peak around 2030 at 33Mt while demand rises toward 42Mt by 2040, leaving a sizable deficit. Demand growth from electrification, EVs, renewables, datacenters, and transmission contrasts with declining ore grades, costlier mining, slow new mine timelines, and insufficient recycling.

title: FinancialContent - The Red Gold Rush: Why 2026 is the Year Copper Becomes the Global Economy's Most Critical Asset
summary: Copper prices on the LME are described as hitting record highs above $13,000/mt, driven by tight inventories, mine and regulatory supply setbacks, and a surge in AI/data-center demand. A projected 2026 deficit and “copper gap” reinforce bullish expectations, while substitution toward aluminum is discussed as a possible ceiling on copper gains.

title: Copper Prices Extend Last Year's Gains as S&P Warns of Global Supply Deficit
summary: Copper prices rose about 2% to roughly $5.91/lb, extending last year’s gains. The move is linked to S&P Global’s warning that the copper market faces a widening supply deficit. With expectations of tighter availability, traders lifted copper futures, reflecting bullish sentiment.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Jan 9
summary: SMM’s weekly review says Indonesian nickel ore prices eased slightly, but logistics and regulatory constraints disrupted mining/shipping, while demand from NPI smelters remained soft. LME nickel strength is expected to boost the next HPM cycle and support ore premiums. NPI prices rose on stronger high-grade sentiment and arbitrage that tightens supply short-term.

title: The future depends on copper, but a coming shortage makes it a 'systemic risk' to the economy
summary: S&P Global warns global copper demand could surge while supply shrinks, potentially creating a large deficit and “systemic risk.” It notes copper prices have already risen sharply amid Trump tariffs and mining disruptions, emphasizing electrification, data centers, and security demand and vulnerability to trade and geopolitical disruptions.

title: Premier slams 'low life' copper thief as thousands of Queenslanders ordered to take shelter NOW as cyclone looms
summary: Queensland’s premier condemned a person accused of cutting a telecommunications cable near Townsville to steal the copper inside, disrupting Telstra/Optus/NBN services ahead of a Category 2 cyclone. Residents were ordered to shelter as dangerous winds and flooding were forecast, potentially driving urgent telecom repairs and copper-related demand.

title: Suspected copper thieves cut telecommunications to thousands in cyclone warning zone
summary: Authorities in Townsville say suspected copper thieves cut fibre/telecom cables at a mobile site, disrupting phone and internet services as Cyclone Koji approached. Technicians restored some services after removing damaged fibre. Police investigate, with officials condemning copper theft during the disaster.

title: High Copper Prices, High Policy Pressure, and Low Demand: The Triple Pressure on the Secondary Copper Rod Market in December 2025
summary: Secondary copper rod operating rates fell into a year-end “high prices, high policy barriers, low demand” trap. Tax-related policies and funding constraints drove production suspensions and invoice shortages, while downstream wire/cable buyers delayed orders. Hidden inventory from unsold stock may pressure near-term copper physical pricing into early 2026.

title: Wave of Costly Copper Thefts Threatens Public Safety, Experts Say
summary: The article says that with copper at new highs, copper thefts from communications and power networks have increased sharply. Telecommunications companies, power suppliers, and construction firms report heightened risk and disruption. It notes copper traded around $6/lb (~$12,000/ton) on Jan. 7, up more than 30% year over year.

title: Police find drug filled cars while investigating $40k copper wire theft in Ballard
summary: Seattle police recovered hundreds of pounds of stolen copper wire after investigating a $40,000 copper theft at a Ballard construction site. Tracking devices led officers to impounded vehicles with copper-stripping equipment and narcotics. The incident suggests localized copper loss, but scale appears unlikely to affect broader copper prices.

title: Five Copper Miners Leading the Commodity Rally as Producers Post Explosive Monthly Returns
summary: The headline claims five copper miners are leading a commodity rally after reporting explosive monthly returns for producers. This implies improving near-term outlook for copper supply or earnings momentum, which can support copper prices. The article text provided contains mostly cookie/privacy content, limiting confirmation of fundamentals.

title: Enamelled Wire: High Copper Prices Suppress Operating Rates, Resulting in Year-on-Year and Month-on-Month Declines in December
summary: SMM reports enamelled wire operating rates fell in December, citing an unexpected surge in copper prices as the core factor suppressing production and slowing downstream cargo pickups. Inventories rose and demand was constrained, with orders scarce early after New Year and some customers selling below cost.

title: Start of Drilling at Eureka Gold & Copper Project  | Company Announcement
summary: Ajax reports the start of a fully funded drilling programme at the Eureka Gold and Copper Project in Argentina, targeting copper-focused geochemical and IP anomalies near the historic Mina Eureka mine. Historical samples cited up to 6.1% Cu, but no assay results are provided yet, limiting immediate market impact.

title: Copper shortfall widens the AI race
summary: S&P Global’s study warns that accelerating electrification—powered by AI data centres, defense spending, and broader demand—will outpace copper supply. With primary output projected to peak in 2030 and deficits growing by 2040, plus constrained mining and concentrated smelting, markets face higher risk of copper tightness.

title: Journeo wins orders; MicroSalt sales beat forecast
summary: The news roundup highlights copper-focused exploration updates. Great Southern Copper reports successful completion of drilling and “high-grade copper-silver hits” at Cerro Negro, while Ajax Resources begins drilling at its Eureka project near a historic copper mine. These positive developments may modestly support near-term copper sentiment.

title: Chinese Copper Foil Maker Defu Slumps After Luxembourg Stymies Plan to Take Over Circuit Foil
summary: Chinese copper-foil maker Defu scrapped a takeover of Circuit Foil Luxembourg after Luxembourg imposed restrictions allowing only a minority stake. Defu’s shares fell sharply and it plans instead to buy a majority stake in a domestic electrolytic copper-foil producer to expand capacity. The move affects copper-foil supply expectations, but not broader copper pricing materially.

title: Southeast Asia's Secondary Aluminum Industry Trapped in "Margin Squeeze": Raw Material Surge Forces ADC12 Plant Cuts, Industry May Enter "Lunar New Year Mode" Early
summary: SMM reports LME aluminium cash prices jumped in late 2025/early 2026, lifting regional scrap costs in Malaysia and Thailand. Raw material prices for ADC12 feedstock surged faster than finished ADC12 ingot prices, compressing margins. Multiple producers plan January cuts or early Lunar New Year downtime, reducing output ahead of demand recovery.

title: Operating Rate Rises for 8th Consecutive Month, Copper Foil Industry Ends 2025 on a High Note [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM says China’s copper foil enterprises’ operating rate rose to 88.20% in December and is forecast to reach 88.72% in January 2026. Shipments increased, with strength in lithium battery and electronic circuit foil. Demand support comes from energy storage performance and restocking before Chinese New Year and holiday orders.

title: Wave Of Costly Copper Thefts Threatens Public Safety, Experts Say
summary: Copper at new highs is fueling a wave of thefts from communications and power networks, causing major service disruptions. The piece cites thousands of incidents and notes scrap dealers/resellers as a key outlet for stolen copper, while new laws target tighter identification and recordkeeping for scrap sales.

title: BMO analyst reveals his top picks in copper mining as its price hits new records
summary: A market roundup highlights copper hitting new records and RBC’s analyst expects continued upward momentum. It cites supply disruptions, elevated US inventories, and demand growth, with copper stocks outperforming. The piece also notes mine ramp-ups and possible sanction decisions as potential near-term catalysts for further price strength.

title: FinancialContent - The Great Copper Consolidation: Rio Tinto and Glencore in Talks as BHP Watches from the Sidelines
summary: Rio Tinto and Glencore have confirmed preliminary talks for a mega-merger, with a Feb. 5 deadline to announce a firm offer. The deal is portrayed as consolidating Glencore’s large copper pipeline and expanding dominance in copper and nickel, potentially tightening near-term supply expectations. Antitrust scrutiny in China is a key risk.

title: Market Factors: Top picks in the record-breaking copper sector
summary: The piece highlights copper’s record-breaking rally, up 52% since early 2024 and near $6/lb, driven by electrification and rising power demand, including data centers. It also cites temporary supply disruptions at Freeport-McMoRan’s Indonesian site and Hudbay’s Manitoba project, supporting bullish near-term price expectations.

title: Thieves targeting copper cables disrupt 911 service, internet, and power for millions across the U.S.   – NaturalNews.com
summary: The article reports a surge in U.S. copper cable thefts that disrupt 911, internet, power, and transportation communications for millions. It states copper has risen above $6/lb and cites large incident counts and company costs. New security measures and scrap-dealer verification laws aim to reduce copper supply to scrap markets.

title: BHP Expected to Wait Out Rio Glencore Deal Talks as Copper M&A Heats Up
summary: BHP is expected to wait out Rio Tinto’s and Glencore’s proposed merger talks. The deal is framed as a way to build a dominant copper player, combining Glencore’s copper assets with Rio’s operations as markets anticipate possible copper supply shortfalls and rising transition-metal demand. Antitrust scrutiny remains a key risk.

title: Theft of copper wire causes $260K damage, man charged: Chatham-Kent police
summary: Chatham-Kent police charged a man after copper wire was stolen from a Tilbury business twice in the same week, causing about $260,000 in repair damage. Police recovered the wire and equipment. The incident is local and focused on theft rather than industry supply or market-wide copper constraints.

title: RBC analyst reveals his top picks in copper mining as commodity price hits new records
summary: The article reports copper hitting new records and quotes RBC Capital Markets’ strategist on a constructive outlook. Drivers cited include supply disruptions, elevated U.S. inventories, and growing demand. It also notes potential “too far too fast” consolidation, but expects continued focus on mine ramp-ups and production-related decisions.

title: Theft of copper wire causes $260K damage; man charged: Police | The Stratford Beacon Herald
summary: Chatham-Kent police charged a man after copper wire was stolen from a Tilbury business twice in one week, causing about $260,000 damage to equipment housing the wire. Police recovered the wire and equipment and continue investigating copper wire thefts that threaten local infrastructure.

title: Freeport Resources Reports PNG Government in Support of Yandera Copper Project and Closes Final Tranche of $3.5 Million Private Placement
summary: Freeport Resources says the Papua New Guinea government supports its Yandera copper project and reports closing the final tranche of a $3.5 million private placement. The update is mainly a positive signal for project momentum and financing, which can modestly support expectations for copper supply and sentiment over coming weeks.

title: Clean Air Metals Announces 2026 Strategic Objectives in Historically Strong PGE and Copper Markets
summary: Clean Air Metals announced 2026 objectives for its Thunder Bay North Critical Minerals Project, citing substantial increases in platinum and copper spot prices versus prior study assumptions. It also highlights resource grades and contained copper and nickel quantities, but provides no immediate production or supply disruption details that would likely move metals in days-to-weeks.

title: Star Copper Corp.: Star Copper Reports Balance of Phase 1 Drill Results Extending Supergene Zone Southwest
summary: Star Copper reports Phase 1 drill results at its Star Project, including long intercepts of copper mineralization and expansion of the supergene zone southwest. The company provides Cu grades and CuEq calculations and discusses ongoing Phase 2 drilling results pending. The news is exploration-focused, with limited direct near-term supply implications for copper.

title: Whisky distillery investigates replacing glass bottles with aluminium
summary: A Scottish whisky distillery is testing whether aluminium can replace glass bottles, with university researchers examining chemical interaction, safety/contamination, and sensory outcomes. Results are promising for flavour, but liners must prevent aluminium leaching. The work is exploratory, suggesting only limited near-term aluminium demand impact.

title: Public–private partnership investing $450m in ATALCO's alumina refinery and USA's first large-scale primary gallium production
summary: Atlantic Alumina Company (ATALCO) announced a $450m public-private investment to expand its Gramercy, Louisiana alumina refinery, the only operating US alumina plant, and to build the country’s first large-scale primary gallium production circuit. The deal aims to raise domestic alumina output and reduce reliance on China-driven supplies.

title: Star Copper Reports Balance of Phase 1 Drill Results Extending Supergene Zone Southwest
summary: Star Copper Corp. released Phase 1 drill results from its Star Project in British Columbia, reporting long copper-rich intercepts and expanding the near-surface supergene oxide footprint to the southwest. The company cites chalcopyrite mineralization and CuEq-based grades, with Phase 2 results pending, but no production or trade changes are announced.

title: Pumpkin Hollow Project, a copper-gold deposit in Nevada, US
summary: Nevada’s Pumpkin Hollow copper-gold project was acquired after Nevada Copper’s Chapter 11 filing. In 2025 Kinterra/Kinterra Capital raised equity financing to restart underground copper production, with plans for engineering, updated resource modelling, and offtake-linked financing. Development and restart expectations are supportive for copper sentiment.

title: Copper, Aluminum, and Zinc "Surge Ahead," While Die-Casting Zinc Alloy Profits Are "Eroded"?
summary: SMM reports that copper prices rose by 1,455 yuan/mt and aluminium by 1,570 yuan/mt versus the prior trading day, citing strong copper and aluminium performance above key levels. Raw material cost pressure and narrowing zinc-aluminium spreads accompany higher die-casting alloy processing fees, supporting continued near-term strength.

title: Taseko Provides Update on Florence Copper Ramp-up and Gibraltar 2025 Production Results | Company Announcement
summary: Taseko reported that Florence Copper construction is complete and SX/EW commissioning is progressing without significant issues, with wellfield operations and higher recovered solution grades; first copper cathode is expected within weeks. At Gibraltar, 2025 copper sales were 99 million pounds and Q4 output rose despite November downtime.

title: DRC Gecamines to Sell Copper to US in 2026
summary: Gecamines, via its stake in Tenke Fungurume Mining and partner Mercuria, plans to sell 100,000 tonnes of DRC copper to the US in 2026, with support from the DFC. The company is expanding marketing and securing sales rights, while TFM output ramps up under CMOC.

title: FinancialContent - The 2026 Aluminum Squeeze: Why This Industrial Metal is Outperforming the S&P 500
summary: The piece argues early-2026 aluminum prices are surging on a “price squeeze,” citing depleted LME inventories, China’s output ceiling, weak exports, power-driven smelter outages in Europe, and high U.S./Mexico import tariffs. It expects continued backwardation and higher costs for downstream users, while smelters benefit.

title: PM Pushes to Restart Slovalco Aluminium Plant - News -  Rádio RSI English
summary: Prime Minister Robert Fico wants to restart aluminium production at Slovakia’s Slovalco plant after three years of shutdown. The idle period followed soaring electricity prices after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and costly emissions allowances. He is seeking an EU-level pause on carbon permits, aiming to resume production at the site.

title: Ontario fast-tracks Canada Nickel's Crawford mine permitting in response to U.S. trade war
summary: Ontario is fast-tracking permitting for Canada Nickel’s Crawford mine, which holds the world’s second-largest nickel reserve, to reduce regulatory friction linked to U.S. trade-war concerns. The company plans construction before year-end and a processing plant in Timmins, but financing gaps remain, suggesting limited immediate supply relief for nickel markets.

title: Gramercy alumina plant to get $450 million upgrade | Business
summary: Private equity and the U.S. government will invest $450 million to upgrade the Atlantic Alumina (Gramercy) refinery. Officials say the project will raise alumina production capacity toward 1 million tons and improve problematic red-mud waste handling. As alumina is central to aluminum output, the plan is likely supportive for aluminum prices in coming weeks.

title: Norfolk locks in $2.1M funding as Chilean copper play grows teeth
summary: Norfolk Metals secured $2.1M for a placement and says fresh drill assays at its Chilean Carmen copper project confirm rich primary sulphide mineralisation and continuity, with further drilling planned. The report links the timing to copper’s surge to record highs on renewables and defence demand, reinforcing bullish copper sentiment.

title: Power, corruption and reprisals: How Filipino communities, rivers pay the price for nickel mining boom
summary: An investigative report describes alleged environmental and social damage from Marcventures nickel mining in Cantilan, Philippines, and claims political connections helped sidestep regulations. It notes a court ruling in favor of the company after years of litigation. The outcome may reduce near-term fears of supply disruption for nickel.

title: Copper cable theft suspect arrested, cutting 50 feet of cable at South San Francisco Caltrain station, causing $5,000 in damage
summary: A suspect was arrested for cutting about 50 feet of copper cable beneath Caltrain tracks in South San Francisco, causing an estimated $5,000 repair cost. Officials emphasize public safety risks, though service disruption was limited. The case reflects localized copper replacement demand but is unlikely to move broader copper prices.

title: Bryan County residents show support for potential nickel refinery
summary: Bryan County, Georgia residents and leaders heard support for Westwin Elements considering Richmond Hill as a site for a major nickel refinery. Few specifics were shared, but backers cited 800 jobs and economic benefits. Commissioners want more research due to pending lawsuits and national security concerns.

title: Ontario expedites Crawford Nickel Project under 1P1P framework
summary: Ontario selected Canada Nickel’s Crawford Nickel Project to proceed under its 1P1P streamlined permitting framework. The nickel-cobalt sulphide mine is advanced and Ontario expects construction to start by year-end. Faster regulatory progression improves confidence in future nickel supply, offering modest near-term support to nickel prices.

title: [SMM Analysis] China's December copper concentrate import data guide the future supply-demand balance of copper concentrate in China.
summary: China’s customs data show copper ore/concentrate imports rose 7% m/m to 2.704 million dmt in December 2025 and reached 30.365 million dmt for 2025, with repeated record highs. SMM expects increased domestic concentrate potential, anode supply from Kamoa-Kakula, and rising recycled copper use supporting electrolytic copper.

title: MEED | Construction begins on Yanbu copper rods plant
summary: Construction has started on a SR550m copper rods manufacturing plant in Yanbu, targeting 130,000 tonnes/year. The project, backed by Elsewedy Electric and Alfanar, is intended to supply electrical cables and grid infrastructure while reducing copper-rod import reliance for Saudi utilities under Vision 2030.

title: Arizona Sonoran Copper Company Inc. Initiates 2026 Work Plan to Advance Cactus, and 2025
summary: Arizona Sonoran Copper outlines its fully funded 2026 work plan for the Cactus brownfield project, including engineering, permitting/financing progress, and long-lead procurement for power infrastructure. The company targets first sustainable copper cathode production in second half 2029 and expects a feasibility study in H2 2026.

title: Copper hits an all-time high amid speculation and doubts over demand
summary: Copper hit a record on the LME at about $13,407/t, easing to around $13,240, after speculative buying amid monetary concerns. The rise is supported by strains on global supply, mine and logistics disruptions, and potential tariff expectations. However, weaker Chinese imports suggest demand may be lagging.

title: FinancialContent - Copper Prices Hit Record Highs: The 'Super-Squeeze' Driven by AI and the Global Grid Overhaul
summary: Copper prices are trading above $13,200/t on the LME, driven by a “super-squeeze” from rapid AI data-center and power-grid demand and a sudden supply pullback from mine closures and disruptions. Warehouse inventories are reportedly critical, with multi-decade delivery premiums, reinforcing a near-term bullish price outlook.

title: GIADEC, Metalloid and GIBDLC secure $60m facility to advance Nyinahin bauxite project
summary: GIADEC, Metalloïd Resources Investment and GIBDLC secured a US$60m medium-term facility to accelerate mining at Ghana’s Nyinahin bauxite concession. Funding will support early mining across hills one to three, scaling production progressively to develop a more integrated aluminium value chain from bauxite extraction.

title: IIT Bhubaneswar researchers develop satellite-based bauxite exploration technology
summary: IIT Bhubaneswar researchers developed hyperspectral satellite-based technology to prospect bauxite in Odisha’s Koraput and Rayagada districts. Since bauxite is the primary ore of aluminium, the work aims to make exploration faster and cheaper and support sustainable resource planning. It does not signal near-term output changes.

title: Exclusive: NSS under scrutiny for alleged $5m scrap copper sale
summary: Investigations by Radio Tamazuj say South Sudan’s NSS allegedly seized and sold scrap copper wire worth about $5.2 million despite customs and tax clearances. Court documents show an ongoing civil lawsuit demanding damages. The dispute highlights local supply diversion, but no clear signal of wider copper price moves.

title: Rising copper prices fuel theft surge in Springfield
summary: Springfield police report a jump in copper thefts as copper prices hit decade highs. A local recycler says it is paying record rates for bare bright copper, tied to daily COMEX pricing. Theft focuses on AC units and phone/cable wiring, with AT&T citing major nationwide costs.

title: Suspect charged, another wanted after copper wire theft
summary: Toronto police charged a suspect after a break-in where about $10,000 worth of copper wire was stolen in North York, with another suspect sought. The report is a localized theft event, implying minor near-term disruption, but no clear impact on broader copper supply or inventories.

title: Clark County continues to battle copper wire theft leaving neighborhoods in dark
summary: Clark County in Nevada is responding to widespread copper streetlight wire theft that has left neighborhoods without lights. Officials expanded repair crews, allocated funding for replacement, and introduced measures including tighter recycling rules and a switch toward aluminum wiring and solar streetlights in some areas.

title: Positive Study Results – Kalahari Copperbelt  | Company Announcement
summary: Aterian plc reported positive independent geophysical study results for its wholly owned Botswana Kalahari Copperbelt licence, identifying favourable structures, copper-in-soil anomalies, and conductive horizons near the Motheo copper mine. The company plans further surveys and drill targeting. The update supports optimism for future copper supply prospects.

title: Police crack down on copper theft as main roads, telecommunication networks targeted
summary: North Queensland police are cracking down on copper theft, with suspected thieves cutting copper cables that disrupted mobile and internet services ahead of ex-Tropical Cyclone Koji. Officers say copper is targeted for scrap trading and have charged dozens of people, but the report doesn’t show global supply or demand shifts.

title: MEED | PIF signs agreement to develop Yanbu aluminum complex
summary: PIF and Riyadh-based Red Sea Aluminium Holdings sign an agreement to build a fully integrated aluminium complex in Yanbu. RSAH will bring advanced smelting and casting technologies and develop large downstream processing facilities. Construction of phase one is already under way by China Minmetals’ contractor, with a total expected cost of SR38bn.

title: Copper thieves cause $1.5 million in light pole damages in Jefferson Parish
summary: Jefferson Parish reports widespread streetlight thefts, with copper wiring stolen from roughly 300 light poles over eight months and repairs estimated up to $1.5 million. Authorities are ordering parts, refurbishing poles, and moving some wiring to aluminum, which is cheaper and less valuable as scrap.

title: Weather disrupts Australian copper, coal logistics
summary: Queensland weather has disrupted roads and rail links in Australia’s mineral-rich region, limiting Glencore’s ability to supply copper concentrate to its smelter for several days. Mount Isa rail line sections remain closed with no confirmed reopening timeline. The disruption supports tighter near-term copper concentrate availability.

title: PIF in deal to set up integrated aluminium complex in Saudi Arabia
summary: Saudi PIF agreed with Red Sea Aluminium Holdings to develop an integrated downstream aluminium complex in Yanbu, including advanced smelting technologies and a major continuous casting facility. The project aims to produce high-value downstream aluminium products for global and local demand, supporting expectations of expanded aluminium supply.

title: Gunnison Copper Corp.: Gunnison Copper Announces That Rio Tinto and Amazon Web Services Collaborate to Bring Low-Carbon Nuton Copper from Gunnison's Johnson Camp Mine to U.S. Data Centers
summary: Gunnison Copper says Rio Tinto and AWS will use Nuton’s low-carbon copper produced at the Johnson Camp mine in AWS data centers. The bioleaching process yields high-purity copper cathode and is intended to reduce water and carbon. AWS provides analytics to optimize recovery and scale production.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Corp.: First Atlantic Nickel Highlights Relevance of Pipestone XL Awaruite Nickel-Cobalt Alloy Discovery to Address U.S. Critical Mineral Supply Chain Vulnerabilities Identified in January 14, 2026 White House Proclamation
summary: First Atlantic Nickel links its Pipestone XL awaruite nickel-cobalt alloy discovery to a January 14 White House proclamation targeting U.S. processed critical-mineral import vulnerabilities, highlighting nickel’s downstream processing dependence. The company argues awaruite could be beneficiated without smelting into nickel sulfate feed, potentially easing near-term nickel processing constraints.

title: Taseko (TGB) Climbs 11.8% on Looming Copper Site Operations
summary: The piece is mostly promotional about AI, but the headline says Taseko shares rose 11.8% due to looming copper site operations. That suggests investors expect copper production/supply conditions to improve soon, which can translate into near-term bullish sentiment for copper prices.

title: Rio Tinto and Amazon Web Services Collaborate to Bring Low-Carbon Nuton Copper to U.S. Data Centres
summary: Rio Tinto and AWS agreed a two-year deal to supply Nuton low-carbon copper for U.S. data centre components and to use AWS analytics to optimize bioleaching at Johnson Camp. The modular process produces 99.99% copper cathode without conventional concentrators/smelters, targeting ~30,000 tonnes over four years, with lower carbon and water intensity.

title: AWS To Use Low-Carbon Nuton Copper In U.S. Data Centres Under Rio Tinto Deal
summary: Rio Tinto announced a two-year collaboration with Amazon Web Services where AWS will become the first customer of its Nuton Technology. AWS will use copper produced via modular bioleaching in U.S. data-centre components and support digital analytics to improve copper recovery at the Johnson Camp mine.

title: Amarc Resources Ltd.: Amarc Builds on Disruptive AuRORA Discovery Success and Advances Pipeline of High Demand District-Scale Copper-Gold Assets in British Columbia During 2025
summary: Amarc reports expanded drilling results and continued advancement of its copper-gold projects in British Columbia, including the AuRORA discovery within the JOY district and progress at the DUKE and IKE districts. It highlights staged JV funding with Freeport and expects transactions. No aluminium-specific developments are mentioned.

title: Ivanhoe meets 2025 copper, zinc output targets as Kamoa-Kakula smelter ramps up
summary: Ivanhoe said its Kamoa-Kakula copper complex met 2025 output guidance, producing about 388,838 tonnes of copper in concentrate, and is ramping a new smelter that is averaging 500 tonnes/day of 99.7% anodes with first exports expected imminently. De-watering progress should improve 2026 production.

title: Sterling Metals Expands Bornite Zone within Large Porphyry Copper System ...
summary: Sterling Metals reported new assay results expanding continuous porphyry copper mineralization and a high-grade bornite core at Ontario’s Soo Copper Project. Wide, higher-grade copper equivalent intervals were intersected and the zone’s footprint was extended, with additional assays pending. The news is supportive for long-term development, but likely minimal for near-term copper pricing.

title: FinancialContent - The Copper Crunch: Why the "Impossible" Math of the Green Energy Transition is Sending Prices to New Stratospheres
summary: The article argues copper is in a structural supply deficit, with LME inventories at decade lows and further upside risk from production disruptions (e.g., Grasberg mud accident) and rising demand from AI data centers and power-grid expansion. It forecasts continued parabolic copper prices and discusses some substitution toward aluminium, but stresses copper scarcity.

title: Osisko Metals Incorporated Announces New Drill Results from the Gaspe Copper Project
summary: Osisko Metals announced new drill results from its Gaspe Copper Project in Quebec, reporting multiple mineralized intercepts with average copper grades (e.g., 0.27% to 0.55% Cu) from infill and expansion holes. The company aims to upgrade resources and potentially expand future copper supply.

title: Armenia's  copper and molybdenum concentrate production down over 11 months, while zinc concentrate production up
summary: Armenia’s copper concentrate production fell 4.7% to 267,542 tons over January–November 2025 versus the same period in 2024, according to the Statistical Committee. Molybdenum concentrate and ferromolybdenum also declined, while zinc concentrate rose. The copper output drop can tighten supply expectations.

title: Amazon buys first American-mined copper in a decade — Arizona mine to fuel AWS AI data centers in seismic two-year deal
summary: Amazon agreed with Rio Tinto to buy copper from Gunnison Copper’s restarted Johnson Camp Arizona mine, including output using Nuton Technology that reduces processing steps. The contract is small relative to Amazon’s total copper needs but boosts expectations for U.S. copper supply and supports demand from expanding AI data centers.

title: Anglo Asian Mining in green as copper production surges
summary: Anglo Asian Mining said copper output surged, with 2025 production rising to 7,915 tonnes from 377 tonnes in 2024 and Q4 rising 94% to 4,439 tonnes. The company slightly missed guidance due to Demirli ball mill maintenance but expects it back in operation by end of Q1. Sales and prices were favourable.

title: FinancialContent - The Impossible Wire: Why 120 Years of Mining History Says the EV Revolution Is Out of Copper
summary: A University of Michigan study claims the EV and grid transition will require far more copper than can be produced under current mining and permitting timelines, creating a structural supply deficit. With copper near record levels and an added demand boost from EVs and AI data centers, the article implies continued upward price pressure and volatility for copper.

title: Midas Minerals hits high-grade copper-silver at Otavi
summary: Midas Minerals reported early high-grade copper and silver intersections at the Spaatzu Prospect within Namibia’s Otavi Copper Project, including 2.55% copper over 16 metres (with silver). The drilling is ongoing and only part of results are assayed. It is supportive for exploration sentiment, but preliminary for near-term supply.

title: Sterling Metals Expands Bornite Zone within Large Porphyry Copper System
summary: Sterling Metals reported new assay results from expanded drilling at Ontario’s Soo Copper Project, extending porphyry copper mineralization and identifying a wider bornite-rich, high-grade core. Intercepts include long copper intervals with high CuEq and multiple high-grade chalcopyrite/bornite zones, supporting stronger future resource development potential.

title: Amazon secures Arizona mine copper supply for data center expansion needs
summary: AWS signed a two-year agreement with Rio Tinto’s Nuton venture to secure copper cathode from the Johnson Camp mine in Arizona for AWS data center growth. The supply covers about 14,000 tonnes over four years, reinforcing expectations of rising copper demand from AI infrastructure.

title: Rio Tinto Copper: Amazon becomes first buyer of Arizona copper made by Rio's Nuton
summary: Amazon Web Services signed a deal with Rio Tinto to source copper from an Arizona mine for use in US data centres. Rio said AWS will be the first customer for copper produced via its Nuton bioleaching technology. No contract terms or quantities were disclosed, but it adds demand visibility for copper.

title: Rio Tinto Group (RIO) Balances $207B Merger Speculation With Cost Reduction and Copper Production Goals
summary: Reuters reported Glencore is in takeover discussions with Rio Tinto that could form a $207B mining group. Rio is also pursuing cost reductions and targeting higher copper production. These developments may affect market sentiment around copper supplies, but the article lacks concrete near-term supply or demand shocks for aluminium.

title: Venezuela Aluminium: An Overview of Current Issues
summary: Venezuela’s aluminium smelting is operating well below its installed capacity because of technical and infrastructure problems, leading to high off-spec production. This likely constrains exports and could alter flows between Brazil, Europe and the US, but traded volumes in Brazil are small, implying limited near-term aluminium price impact.

title: Middle East, Copper and the Energy Transition Strategy
summary: Fastmarkets reviews the Middle East’s copper industry and energy transition. It links electrification and rising electricity demand to increasing copper use and tightening supply, citing extreme 2025 market conditions, high loss-making premiums, and limited refined stock availability. It also flags Red Sea/Suez disruptions raising transport costs.

title: Arizona mine to supply copper for Amazon data centers
summary: Rio Tinto said Amazon Web Services will buy copper from its Johnson Camp Mine in southern Arizona under a two-year supply agreement. The mine uses a bioleaching process to reduce water and emissions and has capacity of about 25 million pounds of copper cathode per year for U.S. data-center needs.

title: High copper prices are good for Butte mining
summary: Montana Resources says its Butte copper operation is benefiting from record-breaking copper prices just over $6/lb. The piece links strength to green-economy demand (EVs, wind) and recent supply disruptions, including an Indonesia copper mine disaster and labor strikes at mines in Chile, tightening global supply.

title: Metals correct: Is the uptrend over? Silver (XAG/USD), Gold (XAU/USD) and Copper (XCU/USD) Outlook
summary: The article argues the metals rally may be slowing due to crowded long positioning, reduced speculative leverage (CME margin changes), and fading rate-cut support. For copper specifically, it cites rejection near the monthly channel high and potential RSI exhaustion/divergence, implying a pullback risk toward $5.40–$5.90 support.

title: First Quantum backs Panama's plan to allow stockpile processing at shut copper mine
summary: First Quantum said it supports Panama’s plan to remove and process stockpiled ore at the shuttered Cobre Panama mine while awaiting approvals. The processing is intended to mitigate acid rock drainage risks and secure feed material for tailings management, potentially offsetting some copper supply disruption until a June decision on the mine’s future.

title: Rio Tinto plugs AWS into innovative copper process
summary: Rio Tinto will use AWS data and analytics to optimize its Nuton micro-organism-based copper recovery process at Johnson Camp, and AWS will be the first customer using the copper in US data-centre components. The deal is aimed at improving predictions and reducing acid and water use, with copper already produced at industrial scale.

title: More drilling for copper and gold in northern Wisconsin may begin next month
summary: GreenLight Wisconsin plans to begin additional exploratory drilling in northern Wisconsin next month at the Bend deposit, estimated to contain copper-bearing sulfides and gold. Permits are still under review, including stormwater/dewatering and wetlands access. The project is exploration only, with any potential mine years away, limiting near-term copper price impact.

title: Rising Metal Prices Back Prospect Resources' Copper-Gold Push In Zimbabwe
summary: Prospect Resources reported new exploration intercepts at its Mumbezhi copper project in Zambia, confirming gold by-product potential. The article notes copper prices have firmed above $13,000/t and gold is near records, with plans to update resources and begin early studies. It signals potential longer-term value, not immediate supply changes.

title: Bungled copper theft leads to possible prison time | The Courier
summary: A man was arrested after attempting to steal copper from a substation at Bacchus Marsh Grammar. Police caught the pair during the break-in and chase. The story focuses on court proceedings and sentencing, not on any broader supply disruption or market-wide factors for copper prices.

title: High Costs and Weak Demand Converge, Operating Rate of Secondary Aluminum Producers Expected to Remain Weak in January [SMM Analysis]
summary: SMM reports China’s secondary aluminum operating rate fell to 44.1% in December amid weaker demand after mid-month, tight scrap supply and high costs, and environmental-related production restrictions. With demand still soft into January and high aluminum prices limiting cost pass-through and stockpiling, January operating rates are expected to drop further.

title: [SMM Analysis] Nickel prices closed higher after experiencing sharp fluctuations this week, while domestic inventory still increased significantly.
summary: Nickel prices rose sharply after Indonesian officials reiterated expectations of tighter nickel ore production quotas (RKAB) for 2026, boosting bullish sentiment and driving a rebound in SHFE nickel toward its weekly high. This was tempered by high global inventories and weak downstream demand, keeping volatility elevated despite China easing liquidity support.

title: XXIX Metal Corp.: XXIX Advances Thierry Copper Project with Comprehensive Validation and Reinterpretation of 210,000 Metres of Drilling
summary: XXIX Metal reported updated geological models for its Thierry copper project, combining 210,000 metres of drilling with new IP survey results suggesting sulphides between K1 and K2. The company also notes that higher copper prices since its 2021 resource assumptions improve potential economics, but no near-term market supply changes are described.

title: FinancialContent - Metals Mania: Gold, Silver, and Copper Shatter Records as Global Stability Cracks
summary: Copper surged to LME record highs on Jan 14, driven by a reported physical deficit (~400,000 metric tons) from mine closures and production hurdles in key regions, alongside faster-than-expected AI data-center copper demand. The piece frames copper as entering “vertical price discovery,” implying strong bullish pressure.

title: FinancialContent - Copper's Bellwether: A Deep-Dive into Freeport-McMoRan (FCX)
summary: The piece frames 2026 as a copper crunch, noting copper rebound to above $6/lb alongside expectations of supply deficits driven by electrification and AI-linked power demand. It highlights Freeport-McMoRan’s recovery efforts in Indonesia, including leaching technology and a new smelter, and positions potential contract/production milestones as catalysts.

title: FinancialContent - The Fragile State of Aluminum: How Operational Decay and Geopolitical Shifts in Venezuela are Reshaping Regional Markets
summary: Venezuela’s state smelters (CVG Venalum and CVG Alcasa) have largely shut down amid political turmoil and severe infrastructure/technology failures, leaving mostly off-grade output. With imports constrained by tariffs and quality issues, the U.S. and Brazil face a supply vacuum, lifting regional aluminum premiums and supporting higher prices.

title: SMM Analysis: Sellers and Buyers Are Evenly Matched, Aluminum Rod Processing Fees Remain Stable
summary: SMM reports weaker December aluminum rod production and declining in-factory inventories, with processing fees largely bottoming and returning to more reasonable regional levels. Downstream demand remains cautious due to high aluminum prices, and plants expect slower January operating rates. Wire/cable output is stable, with modest near-term recovery potential.

title: SMM Analysis: Processing Fees for Aluminum Billets Remain "Negative"! When Will the Discounted Pricing End?
summary: SMM reports aluminum billet processing fees across Chinese regions fell into negative territory after A00 aluminum prices surged post-holiday, reflecting profit-realization and faster destocking by billet producers and traders. By mid-January, fees began rebounding toward parity, but remained negative in parts, with a forecast return to 0–200 yuan/mt.

title: Is the U.S. Tariff Delay a Turning Point for Copper Market Structure?
summary: The article says the U.S. will not impose copper tariffs for now, narrowing LME-COMEX spreads and easing expectations for tight supply. With high U.S. inventory and 2026 COMEX-related contracts priced above spot, some copper is redirected to Asia and discounted, potentially making Q1 2026 slightly oversupplied.

title: FinancialContent - The Red Metal Renaissance: Middle East Projected to See 40% Copper Demand Surge by 2035
summary: The piece argues the Middle East will drive a large copper demand surge as electrification, renewables, and grid buildouts accelerate, with Saudi NEOM and other GCC projects increasing expected electricity needs. It links this to constrained supply forecasts and notes copper prices near record highs, implying bullish near-term sentiment.

title: Hudbay Announces Preliminary 2025 Production Results and Achieves 2025 Consolidated Copper and Gold Production Guidance
summary: Hudbay reported preliminary 2025 results showing consolidated copper production around 118,188 tonnes, meeting guidance despite wildfire evacuations and other interruptions. Fourth-quarter output was about 33,069 tonnes. The company also expects operations to be normalized after weather disruptions, supporting near-term copper supply expectations.

title: EU Imposes Anti-Dumping Duties on Chinese Fused Alumina Imports
summary: The European Commission imposed anti-dumping duties of 88.7% to 110.6% on Chinese fused alumina imports and added a quota for duty-free volumes. The EU says the move addresses unfair dumping harming domestic supply and protects downstream industrial risks. The restriction is likely to support aluminium-linked input prices.

title: Stronger Iron Ore, Copper, and Aluminum Prices See Rio Tinto's Fair Value Estimates Increased
summary: Rio Tinto said its fair value estimates rose as copper and aluminium prices strengthened. The company’s sales are heavily tied to China, and it expects earnings could decline if commodity demand softens after the China boom. Nonetheless, the update signals near-term support from higher copper and aluminium pricing assumptions.

title: Stronger Iron Ore, Copper, and Aluminum Prices See Rio Tinto's Fair Value Estimate Increased
summary: Rio Tinto’s fair value estimate rose as market prices for copper and aluminum strengthened. The piece notes Rio’s heavy exposure to China demand and suggests that after the earlier China boom, commodity demand may soften, but the immediate catalyst cited is the increase in copper and aluminum prices.

title: Copper, AI & America's Supply Risk
summary: Copper is trading near record highs on rising demand from AI-driven computing, data centers, EVs, and grid expansion. The article cites Amazon’s deal with Rio Tinto to buy copper produced with new technology, alongside discussion of US copper supply risk. Overall, it supports bullish expectations for copper.

title: Stronger Iron Ore, Copper, and Aluminum Prices See Rio Tinto's Fair Value Estimates Increased
summary: A Business Strategy and Outlook note says Rio Tinto’s fair value estimates rose as copper and aluminium prices strengthened. It highlights Rio Tinto’s exposure to these metals and that earnings expectations depend heavily on global, especially China, demand. The cited catalyst is the recent firming in copper and aluminium prices.

title: Raising Anglo American's Fair Value Estimate, Driven by Increased Iron Ore and Copper Prices
summary: Anglo American is restructuring after BHP’s failed bid, refocusing on copper (alongside iron ore) while exiting other businesses. The article says the company’s fair value estimate is being raised because copper prices have increased, implying improving near-term sentiment for copper markets even as China demand risks are noted.

title: Raising Teck's Fair Value Estimate Due to Stronger Copper and Zinc Prices
summary: The article says Teck Resources’ fair value estimate is being raised due to stronger copper prices. It also notes China’s role as a major buyer and discusses a shift from investment to household consumption, which could weaken demand growth for investment-oriented commodities and lower prices versus 2023 levels.

title: Stronger Iron Ore, Copper, and Aluminum Prices See Rio Tinto's Fair Value Estimate Increased
summary: Rio Tinto’s fair value estimate was raised as copper and aluminium prices strengthened. The piece highlights Rio’s major exposure to China demand and notes earnings sensitivity to global growth. While it discusses a longer-term demand slowdown after the China boom, the immediate catalyst is higher copper and aluminium prices.

title: Copper slips to a one-week low as traders book gains and China demand worries resurface
summary: Copper fell to a one-week low as traders booked gains after a strong run. Price action also reflects renewed worries about consumption demand in China, the world’s largest copper user. The report highlights how quickly sentiment can shift when demand expectations deteriorate.

title: Hessmer man accused of stealing AT&T copper wire in Rapides Parish
summary: Authorities report a Hessmer man accused of stealing AT&T copper wire, cutting phone service lines and damaging poles. The thefts allegedly involved about $100,000 in copper over a week, plus $30,000 damage. Police also found aluminum sheathing and wires at the scene, posing a railroad hazard.

title: Chinese-invested electrolytic aluminum plant inaugurated in Angola-Xinhua
summary: Angolan President inaugurated a Chinese-backed electrolytic aluminum plant in the Barra do Dande Free Trade Zone. The first phase is a $250 million investment aiming to produce 120,000 tonnes of electrolytic aluminum annually. The project is planned in phases with job creation and workforce training for local industry.

title: Amazon is buying bacteria-harvested copper for its data centres
summary: Amazon’s AWS is reported to become the first customer for Rio Tinto’s Nuton Technologies, which reopened the Johnson Camp copper mine in Arizona using bioleaching microorganisms. The process targets low-grade ore with less water and lower emissions and could improve throughput from older sites. The AI/data-centre boom underpins demand for copper.

title: Chinese-invested electrolytic aluminum plant inaugurated in Angola
summary: Angola’s president inaugurated a Chinese-backed electrolytic aluminium plant in the Barra do Dande Free Trade Zone. The first phase involves $250 million and aims to produce 120,000 tonnes of aluminium annually. Industry park construction and jobs/training are part of broader economic diversification, implying higher future supply.

title: Industry captains hail Madras HC verdict on Sterlite green copper plant
summary: Madras High Court allowed Vedanta’s Sterlite Copper unit to file a fresh application for its proposed green copper plant in Tuticorin. Industry groups say the move could enable cleaner, more efficient production and support India’s growing copper demand, including via a hybrid system using a share of recycled copper.

title: AFASL says policy gap creates 'uneven playing field,' undercuts local Aluminium industry – The Island
summary: AFASL warns a policy gap in Sri Lanka’s BOI Negative List allows duty-free imports of fully fabricated aluminium doors, windows and façade systems, while duty protection applies mainly to raw extrusions. The resulting import undercutting is said to threaten local jobs and reduce domestic value-chain demand, pressuring expectations for aluminium.

title: Budget Infrastructure Focus to Drive Aluminium Demand: NALCO
summary: NALCO expects India’s aluminium demand to stay strong as upcoming budget thrusts on infrastructure and power sector expansion boost consumption of conductors, cables and construction-linked uses. The firm is scaling up alumina output and is ahead of targets, with steady aluminium production plans despite subdued prices.
