If dumping and injury are found, provisional anti-dumping duties could be imposed within about 7-8 months, tightening imports.

title: World's top single-site aluminum smelter in Bahrain shuts down 3 production lines amid regional crisis-Xinhua
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) in Bahrain has begun shutting down three primary production lines, representing about 19% of its total aluminium smelting capacity, citing a regional crisis. The company says it will use inventory and develop alternatives to reduce near-term supply volatility as tensions around Iran escalate.

title: Bahrain's Alba to cut 19% of aluminium production capacity amid Hormuz disruption
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) has started a controlled shutdown of roughly 19% of its production capacity because disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has halted most transit for two weeks. The move targets closed lines while maintaining output elsewhere and is expected to tighten supply, keeping aluminium prices elevated.

title: Hormuz Chokepoint Claims Next Victim: World's Largest Aluminum Smelter Cuts Capacity
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba), the world’s largest single-site aluminium smelter, cut output by about 20% after disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. It shut three reduction lines to preserve raw-material inventory amid muted tanker traffic. With the cut affecting ~19% of Alba’s output, the article expects aluminium prices to rise.

title: Bahrain starts output cuts at world's top aluminum smelter
summary: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) began a phased shutdown of three production lines at the world’s largest single-site aluminum smelter, taking out about 19% of capacity. The cut is attributed to Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions affecting raw materials and outbound shipments, deepening supply concerns and pushing LME prices higher.

title: Iran to hold funeral for killed warship sailors, Aluminium Bahrain cuts output
summary: The article links disruption in the Strait of Hormuz with industrial supply curtailment in Bahrain. Aluminium Bahrain will gradually shut down nearly one-fifth of capacity because exports remain blocked, citing inability to meet obligations. A phased reduction could keep global aluminium supplies tight and support higher prices despite reopening hopes.

title: South32 puts Mozal Aluminium into hibernation after no power deal
summary: South32 said it put Mozal Aluminium in Mozambique on care and maintenance after failing to secure affordable electricity beyond the current supply agreement. The 63.7%-owned smelter near Maputo will have its alumina redirected to third parties. The move signals reduced aluminium production and tighter supply expectations.

title: South32 puts Mozal Aluminium on care and maintenance amid power woes
summary: South32 will place its Mozal aluminium smelter on care and maintenance after failing to secure affordable power beyond March. The decision follows unsuccessful negotiations over electricity supply terms and highlights high Eskom costs. Idling primary aluminium capacity should tighten near-term supply expectations for aluminium prices.

title: Gulf Rivers: Rio Tinto propose 100 copper exploration drill sites
summary: Rio Tinto has proposed a short-term copper exploration drilling program in Queensland’s Gulf Rivers region, seeking feedback on up to 100 drill sites within specific exploration permits inside an environmental area. The work is subject to regulatory approvals and aims to test potential copper mineralisation, not to produce metal.

title: Hormuz crisis: Middle East aluminium supply disruption
summary: The Hormuz crisis is disrupting shipping routes and forcing/triggering delivery constraints for Gulf aluminium producers. Qatalum is running at 60% capacity after reduced gas supplies and issued force majeure. Alba and other smelters face commercial constraints, tightening physical supply. Aluminium premiums in Japan and Europe have surged quickly.

title: Alba initiates shutdown of aluminium smelting lines
summary: Alba has initiated the shutdown of aluminium smelting lines. This cuts aluminium production and reduces near-term supply availability, which can tighten the market and lift expectations for higher aluminium prices over the coming days and weeks.

title: Rio Tinto And Prysmian Partner To Deliver Innovative Low-Carbon Aluminium Solutions For The Data Centre Market
summary: Rio Tinto and Prysmian are running an industrial trial to produce low-carbon aluminium cables for data centres, using Alma hydropowered aluminium and ELYSIS technology that eliminates direct smelting emissions. The partners cite growing data-centre cable demand and increasing aluminium share, aiming to accelerate lower-carbon supply.

title: Mozambique's Mozal aluminum smelter halts production over power supply constraints-Xinhua
summary: Mozambique’s Mozal aluminium smelter stopped producing and exporting aluminium ingots after electricity tariff talks failed. The plant entered “care and maintenance” because power supply at competitive prices can’t be secured, with hydropower constrained by drought and South Africa’s Eskom unable to help. Restart may take up to 12 months.

title: FinancialContent - The Great Metal Chokehold: Strait of Hormuz Closure Paralyzes Global Copper and Aluminum Supplies
summary: A military escalation shut the Strait of Hormuz, stopping shipping and trapping refined copper cathode and Iranian copper exports in the Gulf. Middle East aluminum supply faces gas-related smelter curtailments and export disruptions. LME copper surged above $13,000/t and aluminum hit four-year highs as inventories tighten through end-March.

title: FinancialContent - The Great Metal Chokehold: Strait of Hormuz Closure Paralyzes Global Copper and Aluminum Supplies
summary: A military blockade effectively closes the Strait of Hormuz, suspending maritime transits and trapping significant refined copper cathode and other base-metal cargoes. It also disrupts aluminum exports and forces gas curtailments that lead to smelter shutdowns. Copper and aluminum prices have already surged, with further upside risk if the blockade continues.

title: Lifezone signs Burundi Musongati nickel deal
summary: Lifezone Metals signed a 14-month exclusivity deal with Burundi to assess the Musongati nickel deposit, with planned finished nickel production using hydromet technology at the Kahama multi-metal facility in Tanzania. The facility is expected to generate nickel with copper and cobalt by-products, supporting regional beneficiation and logistics.

title: Centaurus inks Glencore deal for Jaguar nickel output
summary: Glencore signed a binding five-year offtake agreement worth about $450 million for nickel output from Centaurus Metals’ Jaguar project in Brazil. The deal supports progress toward a final investment decision, improving visibility on contracted nickel supply and demand expectations, which can be mildly supportive for nickel prices.

title: World's Top Aluminium Smelter Cuts Output Due to Shipping Chaos
summary: Aluminium Bahrain began a controlled shutdown of three reduction lines, cutting output about 20% amid disrupted tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The disruption reflects shipping chaos and aims to preserve raw-material inventory. Given potential supply tightening, the article expects higher London aluminium prices.

title: Guinea weighs bauxite export quotas as prices slide and freight costs rise, sources say
summary: Guinea, the world’s top bauxite supplier, is weighing export quotas for mining projects after bauxite prices slid 20%-35% and freight costs rose. With Guinea providing over 40% of global bauxite and shipping largely to China, quotas would tighten supply expectations for aluminium feedstock.

title: Hormuz shipping crisis forces major aluminum production cut, threatening global supply   – NaturalNews.com
summary: Shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz forced Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) to conduct a controlled shutdown, cutting production by 20% by idling three of six lines because alumina imports became unreliable. The supply tightness risk has driven LME aluminium to nearly a four-year peak, supporting further price increases.

title: Core Silver Corp.: Core Silver Intersects High-Grade Copper-Molybdenum Veins up to 7.31% Cu & 1.01% Mo Confirming Large Porphyry System at Laverdiere
summary: Core Silver reported 2025 drilling assays at its Laverdiere copper project showing widespread copper-molybdenum porphyry mineralization, including localized copper grades up to 7.31% Cu and other high-grade intercepts. Results are intended to confirm a large porphyry system, but they do not indicate immediate production changes.

title: United States Forest Service and Resolution Copper Complete Land Exchange
summary: The U.S. Forest Service and Resolution Copper completed a required land exchange that enables development of the Resolution Copper project, described as one of the largest untapped copper deposits. The court upheld the exchange and additional ~$500 million spending is planned for enabling works and drilling, supporting eventual copper supply prospects.

title: Correction to FOB Australia alumina index, inferred prices on March 13
summary: Fastmarkets issued a correction to its FOB Australia alumina index and several inferred alumina prices (Indonesia, India, Vietnam, Brazil). The published errors were small, with values adjusted by roughly $0.67/tonne (and a minor Brazil change). These alumina indices feed into aluminium refining but the correction is unlikely to shift aluminium prices materially.

title: Cheaper, cleaner copper technology offers a lifeline as Mount Isa weighs uncertain future
summary: Australia’s Mount Isa copper smelter faces potential closure, threatening concentrate economics for mines in Queensland. Researchers and Banksia Minerals are developing a furnace-free hydrometallurgical process using saline solutions and electricity, claiming ~half the energy of conventional smelting and lower emissions. A pilot is planned for 2028.

title: Rio Tinto gains control of Resolution Copper acreage after years-long court fight
summary: Rio Tinto says it has gained access to acreage in Arizona needed for the Resolution Copper mine after appeals court rulings and no Supreme Court emergency stay. The land swap unlocks a 5,400-acre/2,400-acre exchange covering a large copper deposit and prompts a $500 million drilling campaign.

title: Apache women seek court intervention as federal land is turned over for copper mining
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court request follows the completion of a federal land transfer in Arizona to Resolution Copper (Rio Tinto/BHP) for development of a major copper deposit at Oak Flat. Courts lifted an emergency injunction, and officials said the project supports energy independence and defense-related copper supply, despite tribal and environmental concerns.

title: Rio Tinto and BHP's legal win over Resolution Copper mine in Arizona
summary: A U.S. court denied requests to stop a land exchange enabling Rio Tinto and BHP’s Resolution Copper to move forward with its planned Arizona mine after more than a decade of legal disputes. The ruling cuts regulatory/project risk tied to developing a major underground copper deposit, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Rio Tinto, BHP Complete Land Swap for Big U.S. Copper Project
summary: Rio Tinto and BHP completed a land swap that grants control of federal land needed for the Resolution Copper project near Superior, Arizona. The companies say the project could supply up to a quarter of U.S. copper demand for decades, improving prospects for domestic copper supply.

title: Sacred Apache site moves closer to becoming copper mine after decade of legal battles
summary: A federal land transfer finalized, moving the Resolution Copper project closer to developing the Oak Flat area into one of the nation’s largest copper mines. An appeals court rejected efforts to block the move. Officials cite domestic copper supply benefits, though opponents warn of environmental and water impacts.

title: BHP, Rio Tinto secure US land exchange for Resolution Copper venture
summary: BHP and Rio Tinto said Resolution Copper completed a federal land exchange with the US Forest Service in Arizona, transferring 2,400 acres near the Magma Copper mine in return for conservation land. The milestone moves the project toward technical studies and planning for a potential major US copper mine.

title: Rio Tinto, BHP Complete Land Swap For Big U.S. Copper Project -- Update
summary: Rio Tinto and BHP completed a land swap enabling the Resolution Copper project near Superior, Arizona. The deal gives the JV control of land over a copper-rich orebody and removes a major permitting obstacle after court challenges. Resolution plans $500 million of drilling over two years, signaling progress toward U.S. copper supply.

title: US transfers sacred Oak Flat site to Resolution Copper, dealing blow to tribal opponents
summary: The U.S. Forest Service finalized the transfer of Oak Flat to Resolution Copper after court setbacks for opponents. The government and company frame it as unlocking a major domestic copper source for defense and energy, while tribes and activists argue it threatens sacred land and may face further litigation.

title: Dramatic spike in copper thefts sparks reward
summary: MainPower says copper earthing wires have been repeatedly cut and stolen across its North Canterbury network, with costs exceeding $1 million and over 200 thefts this year. Orion reports similar copper-wire thefts in Selwyn. The utility offers rewards due to safety risks and network disruption.

title: True North eyes more Queensland gold-copper growth
summary: True North Copper plans to expand exploration at its Queensland Cloncurry projects, highlighting historic drilling that intersected copper-gold mineralisation outside the current resource model and geophysical conductors at depth. The company is also progressing a pre-feasibility study to develop contained copper resources, but near-term production impacts are not stated.

title: The West's last aluminum smelter is coming down, taking a way of life with it
summary: The article argues that the West’s last aluminum smelter is being shut down. This implies reduced primary aluminum output in the near term, potentially tightening supply and supporting higher aluminum prices as the market adjusts to the loss of smelting capacity.

title: Litchfield builds momentum across Northern Territory copper hunt
summary: Litchfield Minerals reports continued drilling momentum at its Oonagalabi project in Northern Territory, including completed diamond and RC holes, new drill pads, and pending assays. The company previously reported thick, stacked copper and zinc mineralization and plans additional RC holes if weather and rig access improve.

title: Lines company offers reward to help reduce copper theft
summary: MainPower (Canterbury) is offering a $5,000 reward after a rise in copper theft from earthing wires on power poles. The company reports more incidents since January and disruption and replacement costs of about $1,000–$2,000 per theft. Copper is cut and removed for safety grounding.

title: Apache Women Seek Court Intervention Against Copper Mining
summary: A U.S. appeals court lifted an emergency injunction and the federal government completed the land transfer to Resolution Copper, aimed at developing the Oak Flat copper deposit in Arizona. Apache women and Native groups seek Supreme Court intervention, but authorities cite “energy independence,” supporting expectations of continued copper project progress.

title: Centaurus, Glencore sign nickel supply deal in Brazil
summary: Centaurus and Glencore reportedly signed a nickel supply deal in Brazil. Such agreements can affect near-term nickel supply expectations and contract availability. In the absence of details on volumes, pricing, or disruptions, the likely near-term effect is modest bearish pressure on nickel as the market anticipates steadier supply.

title: Resolution, USFS conclude land exchange for copper deposits
summary: Resolution Copper (Rio Tinto 55%, BHP 45%) says it has concluded a land exchange with the US Forest Service after a Ninth Circuit ruling. The deal enables further planning and development of a major Arizona copper deposit and includes about $500m of additional investment, supporting mining activity and future copper supply outlook.

title: FinancialContent - Copper's Standoff: $13,000 'Price Rejection' in China Paralyzes Physical Market
summary: Copper is seeing a “price rejection” in China after LME futures surged above $13,000/t. Chinese buyers withdrew, physical transactions collapsed, and SHFE/visible inventories hit multi-decade highs. Smelters face $0 TC/RCs and cut output. With Yangshan premiums near $34/t and substitution toward aluminium accelerating, copper faces near-term downside risk.

title: New Alloy Could Vastly Expand Automotive Use Of Recycled Aluminum
summary: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Laboratory developed an alloy (“RidgeAlloy”) that makes remelted recycled aluminium strong enough for structural automotive parts. The piece argues recycled aluminium can drastically cut processing energy and may reduce need for primary aluminium despite tariffs, potentially lowering new car material costs.

title: Pre-FOMC Metals review: Platinum (XPT/USD) outperforms its peers, Copper (XCU/USD) struggles
summary: Ahead of the FOMC, the piece reviews metals price action and notes copper has lost momentum after an early breakout attempt. It is stuck in a $5.50–$6.00 range, but has crossed back below its 50-day moving average and is showing bearish short-run cracks, risking a test of lower supports.

title: Guinea Weighs Bauxite Export Quotas Amid Falling Prices and Rising Costs – Medafrica Times
summary: Guinea is reportedly weighing export quotas for bauxite producers this month as global bauxite/aluminium feedstock prices have fallen 20–35% and shipping costs have risen. With Guinea supplying over 40% of world bauxite, reduced exports would likely tighten feedstock availability and support aluminium prices.

title: EGA to export aluminium via Oman amid Gulf disruption, sources say
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium plans to import alumina and export aluminium via Oman’s Sohar port because conflict has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz. Around 7 million tonnes of Gulf aluminium output rely on exports, so trucking reroutes signal potential short-term logistical shortages. Aluminium prices surged last week on shortage fears.

title: Russia's Rusal swings to annual loss on rising costs, lower aluminium output
summary: Rusal posted a net loss as costs rose from sanctions-related impacts, FX and higher debt servicing, while output fell slightly. However, analysts cited a sharp rise in aluminium prices since the Iran-linked war disrupted shipping and blocked ~8% of global output, plus supply constraints from Russia-related trade frictions.

title: Red Metal, Chalice Mining link up in hunt for next copper-gold frontier
summary: Red Metal and Chalice Mining formed an earn-in JV to drill underexplored Callabonna ground in South Australia for potential IOCG copper-gold systems. The plan includes minimum basement drilling spend over four years, aimed at testing magnetic and gravity targets. The update is exploratory, with limited immediate impact on copper supply expectations.

title: BHP taps copper division chief for top job amid pivot to red metal
summary: BHP appointed Brandon Craig as its new CEO. Craig previously led BHP’s Americas business, where the company has expanded copper (and potash) production. The miner said it will increasingly look to the Americas for growth as it pivots to copper and potash fertilizer projects.

title: Tell the coppers about copper crime | LiveNews.co.nz
summary: New Zealand Police say Southern District investigators are looking into multiple copper theft cases, noting that both theft reports and scrap copper values have risen over the past month. Thefts target cylinders, copper wire stripped/burnt off, and copper taken from buildings and power companies. Police ask for information on suspicious scrap origins.

title: BHP Americas chief to become new CEO as copper tops profits
summary: BHP announced Brandon Craig as its new CEO, saying the company will increasingly look to the Americas for growth as it pivots to copper and potash fertilizer projects. Reuters notes Craig currently leads BHP Americas, where it has been expanding copper production, underpinning a positive copper outlook.

title: Salazar Resources Limited: Salazar Resources Consolidates Ecuador Copper-Gold Portfolio While Maintaining 25% Carried Interest in the El Domo Mine
summary: Salazar Resources closed an acquisition that consolidates its Ecuador copper-gold exploration portfolio, taking full strategic control over several projects and retaining a 25% carried interest in the El Domo copper-gold mine under construction. The company plans further drilling in 2026, with no immediate production or supply shock indicated.

title: First Atlantic Nickel Corp.: First Atlantic Nickel Announces New Alloy Max Zone Discovery - A Second Large-Scale Awaruite (Ni3Fe) Target Area Extending 7 km North from the RPM Zone at the Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt Alloy Project
summary: First Atlantic Nickel announces discovery of a second large awaruite (Ni3Fe) target area (“Alloy Max”) at its Pipestone XL nickel-cobalt project, extending 7 km from the RPM zone. The zone is fully permitted and funded for drilling, supported by favorable DTR surface grades and geophysics, reinforcing district-scale nickel potential.

title: Mining giant BHP names new boss as it shifts focus to eco-friendly copper
summary: BHP named Brandon Craig as CEO, signaling continued and increased focus on copper as it moves away from coal. The company’s latest results showed copper contributed the largest share of earnings over six months to Dec. 31, and Craig has run copper assets in Chile and Argentina. The shift boosted shares after the announcement.

title: New Almalyk Mining copper plant begins work with 60 million tonne capacity
summary: Uzbekistan inaugurated a new Almalyk copper processing plant (Processing Plant No. 3), with 60 million tonnes annual ore processing capacity and output up to 900,000 tonnes of copper concentrate. Officials say concentrate output could rise from 2,400 to 5,000 tonnes daily after ramp-up, alongside further smelter and processing plans.

title: Talisman concludes sampling at Fougnar Copper-Silver Project
summary: Talisman Metals has completed stream sediment sampling and much of its geophysical surveys at the Fougnar copper-silver project in Morocco. Two trenches show visible malachite, and additional RC scout drilling is planned. The company is processing geophysical and geochemical data to refine copper targets.

title: Guinea to curb bauxite exports by April to stabilize prices, minister says
summary: Guinea says it will reduce bauxite export volumes by early April to support prices and protect smaller producers, not through an outright ban. The move targets margins squeezed by weaker Chinese demand and higher shipping costs. As bauxite is aluminium feedstock, tighter supply expectations are likely to lift aluminium prices.

title: Plastics, aluminum, and microchips: What the closure of the Strait of Hormuz costs the world economy beyond oil and gas
summary: Closure of the Strait of Hormuz sharply reduces maritime flows of refined products and industrial inputs. The article notes vessel traffic down ~95% and highlights cascading effects on petrochemicals and industrial raw materials. It specifically points to ING’s scenario where aluminum could surge to $4,000/ton amid Gulf smelting supply concentration.

title: FinancialContent - Doctor Copper's Fever Breaks: Record Highs Give Way to Reversal Amid Goldman Sachs Warning
summary: Copper prices have reversed sharply from January record highs as China’s manufacturing cools (PMI ~49), a ‘buyer strike’ emerges, and LME/SHFE inventories build. Goldman Sachs warns a mid-2026 copper surplus and a looming US refined-copper tariff decision could trigger further downside; aluminium and nickel show correlated weakness.

title: FinancialContent - The "Solidified Electricity" Crisis: Iran Conflict and Energy Spikes Send Aluminum Markets into Turmoil
summary: Escalation of Iran-related conflict and an effective Strait of Hormuz closure has halted shipments of primary aluminium, triggering force majeure and shutting/stranding millions of tonnes of capacity. Natural gas prices in Europe and Asia surged, making smelting uneconomic. LME aluminium prices exceeded $3,400/tonne with risk of $4,000 if disruption persists.

title: Mitsui locks 40% Josemaria copper concentrates offtake
summary: Mitsui secured rights to offtake 40% of copper concentrate from Argentina’s Josemaria deposit, via a tender from JOGMEC. Fortescue also completed its Alta Copper acquisition, adding the Cañariaco project. The piece notes concentrate remains tight, with TC indices declining recently, supporting bullish sentiment for copper.

title: Guinea to curb bauxite exports by April to stabilize prices: Minister – Channel Africa
summary: Guinea says it will curb bauxite exports by early April (not a ban) to support prices and protect smaller producers. The country’s bauxite shipments to China face weak demand and higher freight costs, squeezing margins. Officials are reviewing miners’ multi-year plans before sector-wide export curbs.

title: McEwen Copper plans $300 million IPO to finance Los Azules project in Argentina, executive says
summary: McEwen Copper plans a roughly $300 million IPO to help finance the Los Azules copper project in Argentina. The project has completed feasibility work and received Argentina’s RIGI tax-break approval. The company aims for board approval in late 2026 and construction in early 2027, boosting forward copper supply expectations.

title: Resolution Copper clears land hurdle after years-long legal fight
summary: Rio Tinto secured control of the land in Arizona needed to advance its Resolution Copper project after U.S. authorities completed a long-contested land exchange. The resolution of this legal hurdle is described as a turning point for the project, which can lift expectations for future copper supply.

title: KoBold Metals targets early-2030s copper output at Zambia project
summary: KoBold Metals began development of its Mingomba copper project in Zambia, moving into permitting with shaft sinking expected in 2027 and production in the early 2030s. The project is designed for 300,000 tonnes of annual copper. KoBold also conducts nickel exploration in Namibia, but effects appear long-dated.

title: New Frontier Minerals shares rise as the Big One copper project gets a key greenlight
summary: New Frontier Minerals’ shares rose after a key greenlight for its “Big One” copper project. The approval improves expectations for future copper supply and supports investor sentiment around the project’s development prospects, which can lift near-term copper price outlook, though timing and scale remain uncertain.

title: Southern Police are appealing for information following a spike in copper thefts - 19-Mar-2026
summary: Southern Police say copper thefts have risen, targeting water cylinders and stripped wires from buildings and power companies. Constable Craig Colyer attributes the uptick to increased scrap copper values over the past month. Police urge reporting of scrap copper from suspicious origins. The note suggests scrap-market sensitivity but no broader supply figures.

title: Apache Women Ask SCOTUS to Stop Copper Mine
summary: Apache women, representing Apache Stronghold, have asked the US Supreme Court to halt Resolution Copper’s plan to mine the Oak Flat site in Arizona. The land transfer followed an appeals court denial. Supporters say the project boosts domestic copper supply, while opponents cite sacred sites and environmental and legal concerns.

title: Fake MTNL crew hires crane to steal copper cables in Mulund; 9 held
summary: Police in Mulund arrested nine people for allegedly posing as MTNL workers and stealing underground copper cables using a crane and labourers. Investigators said high copper prices have driven a surge in cable thefts, with Mumbai scrap copper nearly ₹1,200/kg and theft incidents up about 30% recently.

title: Material Matters: Rare Earths, Aluminium, Coal, Gold, Copper & Lithium
summary: The piece links Middle East conflict to higher near-term aluminium prices, citing energy input cost risks, potential Strait of Hormuz-related smelter closures, steep backwardation, and low LME on-warrant inventories. It also notes RBC Capital materially raising copper (and other metals) price forecasts for 2026, supporting bullish sentiment.

title: Material Matters: Rare Earths, Aluminium, Coal, Gold, Copper & Lithium
summary: The piece links the Middle East conflict to higher thermal coal and aluminium prices via energy cost pressures and potential Strait of Hormuz disruption. It highlights aluminium force majeure shutdowns, falling LME inventories and steep backwardation. It also reports RBC Capital raising 2026 copper forecasts on expected deficits.

title: Demolition of last Northwest aluminum smelter marks end of era
summary: Alcoa has begun demolishing the Intalco aluminum smelter in Washington, the last remaining Northwest facility, following closure in 2020. The multiyear teardown and environmental cleanup eliminate hopes of restarting production. Regulators are drafting cleanup steps for PCB and other contamination, with hearings in April.

title: Former Holt Manufacturing manager charged with stealing more than $1 million worth of copper wire with false invoices
summary: A former Holt Manufacturing manager in Texas was charged with allegedly stealing $1.18 million worth of 4/0 heavy-duty copper wire using more than 200 questionable invoices. Investigators say the wire could not be found at Holt sites or returned to the supplier after being ordered and picked up on Holt’s account.

title: Tomago Aluminium smelter bailout could see taxpayers face $300m annual subsidy in complex power deal
summary: Australia’s governments are negotiating a bailout for the Tomago Aluminium smelter, potentially locking taxpayers into at least a $300m annual subsidy for a decade. The plan hinges on providing affordable long-term renewable power, reducing closure risk and supporting smelter operations. This can affect aluminium supply expectations and sentiment.

title: Copper theft drops in Louisville amid crackdown despite record prices
summary: Louisville police report a sharp drop in copper thefts after a coordinated infrastructure task force and stricter scrap-metal rules (licensing, ID/vehicle records, no cash, tracked payments). Dealers say they buy less copper as attempts slow. Authorities cite reduced theft at targeted sites and continued investigations.

title: Guinea Plans Export Curbs to Lift Bauxite Prices Amid Market Slump
summary: Guinea’s Mines Minister says the country will curb bauxite exports by early April to reduce oversupply and support slipping prices. Guinea supplies about 40% of global bauxite, and rising Middle East tensions have raised logistics costs. Details and possible producer offsets remain uncertain, but the policy is price-supportive for aluminium.

title: Albanese government's $300 million plan to save Tomago aluminium smelter
summary: Australia’s Albanese government announced a $300 million plan aimed at saving the Tomago aluminium smelter in NSW. The facility is a large, troubled producer and uses significant electricity. Government support is likely to reduce immediate risk of shutdown or reduced output, supporting expectations for aluminium supply.

title: SA's transmission network faces copper cable quality dilemma
summary: South Ocean Electric Wire warns South Africa’s transmission and energy projects face risks from dumped, inferior non-compliant imported cables, citing overheating, insulation breakdown, fires and downtime. It urges utilities to buy SABS-certified, locally tested cable and reconductoring materials to support grid expansion and renewable integration.

title: How Trump's steel and aluminum tariffs impact prices one year later
summary: A year after Trump’s steel and aluminum tariffs were imposed (and while steel/aluminum tariffs remain), industry reports mixed outcomes and higher costs for downstream users. Import competition is reduced, but aluminum producers see strong price gains. The Producer Price Index shows domestic aluminum up nearly 40% versus a year ago.

title: FinancialContent - Copper's Red Metal Rally: Why $5.94 Holds Firm Despite Global Market Tremors
summary: Copper holds near $5.94/lb despite global equity volatility, attributed to a smelter squeeze from near-zero TC/RCs, low LME/COMEX inventories, and ongoing mine/refining disruptions including Grasberg’s force majeure. The piece argues a structural deficit and strategic demand (AI/energy transition) underpin tight near-term supply.

title: Copper joins gold in broad commodities sell-off. There's a worrying reason behind it
summary: Industrial metals sold off broadly as investors worried that higher oil prices from the U.S.-Iran conflict will keep inflation elevated and interest rates higher. With stronger rates and a firmer dollar, copper fell about 2% as recession risk and demand destruction concerns for industrial activity grew.

title: Copper futures plunge on macro-economic pressure, demand concern
summary: Copper futures fell to their lowest level in months as cautious Fed guidance lifted US yields and pressured risk sentiment. Escalating Middle East tensions raised energy prices, heightening inflation and growth worries. LME inventories surged above 334,000 tonnes, suggesting abundant supply, while China demand remained subdued despite some production resilience.

title: Strategic investment in Chilean copper developer | Company Announcement
summary: Power Metal Resources plans to invest US$1 million (2.6% stake) in Chile’s Next Minerals to fund development of the mine-ready Comahue underground copper project in Antofagasta. Next Minerals targets phase 1 production of copper cathode after permitting and engineering, but the investment size suggests limited immediate market impact.

title: Clarendon Alumina Partners to lose $7.6b even as partners push efficiency drive at Jamalco
summary: Clarendon Alumina Partners expects continued operating losses through 2027 at its stake in Jamaica’s Jamalco alumina refinery. The filing cites alumina revenues below operating costs, with power/steam expenses central to the turnaround plan and ongoing efficiency and incorporation efforts. CAP is investing to lower energy costs despite losses.

title: Atalaya's copper moment
summary: Atalaya reported sharply higher 2025 earnings and cash, citing higher realized copper prices and improved costs at its Riotinto mine, where production and throughput hit upper guidance. However, heavy rainfall in early 2026 has disrupted mining conditions and lowered grades, threatening near-term output despite maintained guidance.

title: Botswana Minerals looks to raise €1.3m to further copper prospecting
summary: Botswana Minerals plans to raise about £1.15m (€1.3m) via a share placing to fund copper-focused prospecting licences in northwest Botswana, following a shift from diamonds. Directors cite phased work programmes and optionality. The announcement supports copper exploration activity, but is unlikely to affect short-term copper prices materially.

title: READY, FIRE, AIM: Copper Dreams.. or Nightmares – Pagosa Daily Post News Events & Video for Pagosa Springs Colorado
summary: The piece cites analysis from The Conversation that copper demand is rising with new technologies while supply struggles to keep up due to financing risk, permitting complexity, and labor constraints. It argues that even at current record prices, shortages could worsen, implying copper prices may face strong upward pressure.

title: FinancialContent - Copper Supply Crunch Intensifies: Impact on Global Renewable Energy Sector
summary: The piece argues that a structural copper supply deficit is worsening, driven by mine disruptions (Grasberg force majeure, flooding at Kamoa-Kakula, and Cobre Panama shutdown) and smelter cutbacks due to near-zero TC/RCs. It links tight inventories to higher LME copper prices and discusses aluminium substitution for grid transmission.

title: Prysmian Eyes New Texas Copper Mill Amid Data Center Boom
summary: The headline reports Prysmian is considering a new copper mill in Texas, linked to rising data-center construction. If investment proceeds or signals strong near-term copper consumption, it can boost expectations for copper demand and prices over the coming days to weeks. The rest of the provided content is cookie/privacy text.

title: Century Aluminum CEO Sells 150000 Shares as Aluminum Prices Soar
summary: Century Aluminum’s CEO sold about 150,000 shares, while the report notes aluminum prices have surged. The main market signal is the stated rise in aluminum prices, implying strong near-term bullish sentiment. The insider transaction is unlikely to materially change aluminium supply or demand on its own.

title: Asia's EVolution: Indonesia's nickel powers global electric vehicle boom but at what cost to the country?
summary: The CNA report describes how Indonesia’s Weda Bay has become a major nickel hub after the export-bans and refinery build-out tied to EV demand. It details heavy coal power use, pollution, and a government decarbonisation roadmap. Despite strong supply expansion, it offers limited near-term signals for nickel pricing.

title: Regional Aluminum Premiums Surge May Impact China's Primary Aluminum Net Imports
summary: China’s primary aluminum net imports rose in Jan-Feb, but SMM expects net imports to weaken as regional aluminum premiums outside China surge. Japan, US, and Europe premiums jumped sharply. The move is attributed to Middle East supply contraction from Qatar and Bahrain shutdowns and potential logistics disruption via the Strait of Hormuz.

title: 【SMM Analysis】Weekly Review of Indonesian Nickel Market - Mar 20 - Shanghai Metals Market (SMM)
summary: SMM reports Indonesian nickel ore prices and premiums rising, supported by smelter restocking demand and pessimism around RKAB quota reductions, with Eid holidays expected to delay approvals. At the same time, high-grade nickel pig iron shows periodic retracement as stainless steel and futures prices weaken, limiting upside but also containing downside.

title: Ardea WA nickel project grabs Japanese-US attention
summary: Ardea Resources’ Kalgoorlie nickel project was included in a Japan-US Critical Minerals joint fact sheet, backed by policy cooperation after a Trump-Japan summit. The company is progressing its nickel project DFS with Japanese consortium funding and potential EFA/EXIM support, boosting confidence in future nickel supply prospects for Western markets.

title: Copper stocks on sale, says Scotiabank analyst
summary: Scotiabank argues copper fundamentals are bending but not broken, maintaining a sizable deficit outlook while updating for weaker near-term demand and higher fuel-cost impacts from the escalating Middle East crisis. Despite valuation discounts in copper miners, the note cautions copper prices may not have bottomed, suggesting near-term bearish pressure.

title: FinancialContent - The Silver Squeeze: Aluminum Surges Past $3,000 as 2026 Supply Crunch Hits Global Markets
summary: LME aluminum is surging past $3,000/tonne, reaching roughly $3,220, amid a 2026 supply crunch. Drivers cited include China’s enforced capacity ceiling creating net imports, Strait of Hormuz shipment disruptions, and EU CBAM levies increasing scarcity of “green” metal. Analysts expect further volatility.

title: FinancialContent - The Aluminum Renaissance: A Deep-Dive into Alcoa's (AA) 2026 Strategic Pivot
summary: The piece is a deep dive on Alcoa’s 2026 strategy, emphasizing its alumina and aluminium smelting operations and its low-carbon product positioning. It notes LME aluminum price sensitivity, expected competitiveness from EU CBAM/IRA policies, and potential site monetization, but provides no immediate supply disruption signal.

title: FinancialContent - The Copper "Perfect Storm": Prices Breach $14,500 as Global Deficit Deepens to 330,000 Tonnes
summary: Copper prices have surged above $14,500 on the LME amid a cited 330,000 tonne global supply deficit, tight warehouse inventories, and production disruption from Indonesia’s Grasberg mine. The piece expects demand to remain largely inelastic short term due to electrification and AI data-center buildouts.

title: FinancialContent - The Copper Squeeze: How a Midstream Meltdown is Redrawing the Global Energy Transition
summary: The piece argues that copper prices are high while smelter processing economics have broken: treatment charges have fallen to near $0 and China smelters plan a 10% output cut. A potential continued concentrate deficit threatens refined cathode supply, supporting a bullish outlook for copper in coming weeks.

title: NGEx hits 6.8% copper at Argentina's Lunahuasi - The Northern Miner
summary: NGEx reported high-grade drill results from its Lunahuasi copper-gold-silver project in Argentina, including 335 metres grading 2.25% copper and standout intervals such as 6.83% copper and a 21.65% copper bonanza sample. The update supports expectations of resource upside, boosting copper-focused sentiment.

title: Freeport-McMoRan confident in copper demand despite Iran conflict, CEO says
summary: Freeport-McMoRan CEO Kathleen Quirk said copper demand for electrification, data centers and high-tech uses should remain resilient despite market jitters linked to the Iran conflict. She argued “Dr. Copper” drivers are largely secular. Copper has dropped nearly 10% since late-Feb strikes, but outlook stays constructive.

title: Deputies spot men cutting pole wires; two arrested in Tulsa County copper theft probe
summary: Tulsa County deputies arrested two men for allegedly cutting wire from a telephone pole and charging them with larceny of copper and conspiracy. The report is limited to a local theft probe with no indication of wider supply loss, production impact, or market-wide effects on copper prices.

title: War in Iran drives up aluminum costs, impacting Berwick boat builder
summary: War in Iran is causing supply disruption fears and higher shipping/transport costs for aluminum moving through the Strait of Hormuz. A Louisiana boat builder reports aluminum input costs up ~10% since January, expecting another 10–12% increase. Aluminum is tied to LME/global and regional indices, plus logistics.

title: From the Shannon to Siberia: How alumina from a Limerick refinery enters Russia's weapons supply chain – The Irish Times
summary: The Irish Times investigation says Aughinish Alumina in Limerick ships growing volumes of alumina to Rusal-owned Russian smelters, where it becomes aluminium supplied via trader ASK to Russian defence manufacturers. It highlights EU-scooped alarm and ongoing debate over sanctions, even though alumina is currently not sanctioned.

title: The Irish Times view on Aughinish Alumina: revelations pose urgent questions
summary: An investigation by the Irish Times and OCCRP alleges that alumina processed at Aughinish Alumina in Co Limerick is entering Russia’s military supply chain via Russian smelters and an arms-linked trading company. It highlights export growth to Russia and raises pressure for enforcement or further restrictions affecting aluminium markets.

title: How alumina from a Limerick refinery enters Russia's weapons supply chain – The Irish Times
summary: An Irish Times investigation traces exports from Aughinish Alumina’s Limerick refinery, showing links to Russia’s weapons supply chain. The article notes alumina’s role as feedstock for aluminium and discusses why the EU previously allowed the industry a “pass” amid possible sanctions related to the war in Ukraine.

title: Faraday Copper Corp.: Faraday Copper Continues to Intersect Near-Surface Copper Mineralization at American Eagle and Expands Keel Laterally
summary: Faraday Copper reported results from Phase IV drilling at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona, highlighting multiple near-surface copper intercepts at the American Eagle area and an expanded northeast extension at Keel. Drilling is ongoing, aimed at improving open-pit potential and collecting hydrogeological and geotechnical data.

title: The copper crisis: Overcapacity in China and underinvestment in America
summary: The piece claims China’s state-backed overcapacity in copper smelting and dumping has given it dominant fabrication control and recently pushed bulk copper prices to 16-year highs. It calls for U.S. measures—new tariffs, export controls, and scrap feedstock restrictions—plus reliance on foreign refined supply until U.S. smelting returns.

title: Rio Tinto targets broader aluminium footprint, division CEO says
summary: Rio Tinto’s aluminium division CEO says the company is expanding its low-carbon aluminium footprint via AP60 smelter technology and new projects in Finland and India, plus further investment in Brazil through a joint acquisition of CBA and growth in recycling. The plans, though some pending approvals, reinforce aluminium supply/capex expectations.

title: The Great Copper Squeeze: Why Smart Money is Hoarding Hard Assets
summary: Commentary argues global refined copper supply is tightening, citing analysts’ forecasts for a 2026 refined deficit above 150,000 tonnes. It attributes demand growth to grid electrification, AI data centers and defense spending, plus sovereign “critical minerals” funding, and references copper-focused drilling updates.

title: Nickel catalyst enables high-performance fuel cell free of precious metals
summary: Researchers at Cornell report a nickel-on-carbon catalyst that enables high-performance alkaline fuel cells without precious metals like platinum. By improving nickel’s stability in alkaline media, the work could eventually expand fuel-cell applications using nickel. However, it does not signal near-term deployment, so short-term price impact is likely limited.

title: FinancialContent - Copper's Red Sea: Technical Bear Market Wipes Out Billions in Mining Valuations Amid Chinese Price Rejection
summary: Copper has entered a technical bear market after peaking in late January, with LME prices down nearly 20% to around $11,700. The sell-off is tied to China’s price rejection, swelling Shanghai/LME inventories, plummeting treatment charges to near zero, and mandated smelter production cuts—reinforcing bearish near-term sentiment.

title: Comex Copper Settles 0.31% Lower at $5.4225 — Data Talk
summary: Comex copper front-month futures for March delivery settled 0.31% lower at $5.4225 per pound, losing 1.70 cents. The contract fell eight of the past 10 sessions, placing today’s settlement among the lowest of the year, and remains down month-to-date and year-to-date.

title: Latin America's Lithium, Copper Boom
summary: The piece forecasts copper prices staying high as electrification, EVs, and AI data-center infrastructure raise demand while physical inventories remain low and a future production deficit is expected. It highlights investment momentum in Latin American copper projects and potential implications of Panama’s Cobre Panamá mine reopening and US-China trade uncertainty.

title: Rio Tinto, Queensland and Commonwealth secure long-term future for Boyne aluminium smelter at Gladstone
summary: Rio Tinto, Queensland and the Commonwealth agreed to fund and finalize long-term power arrangements for the Boyne aluminium smelter at Gladstone, keeping it cost-competitive beyond its current contract. The governments will invest A$2 billion over 10 years, supported by new renewable PPAs and battery capacity.

title: Federal and state governments announce $2b bailout for Rio Tinto's Boyne aluminium smelter
summary: Federal and Queensland governments will each invest $1 billion to support Rio Tinto’s Boyne aluminium smelter, funding renewable energy and grid assets to enable continued production beyond its 2029 power contract. Officials cite jobs and lower electricity costs, reducing shutdown risk and supporting aluminium supply.

title: Multibillion-dollar bailout for major aluminium maker
summary: Australia’s federal and Queensland governments are defending a $2 billion bailout for Rio Tinto’s Boyne aluminium smelter in Gladstone, aimed at saving jobs and lowering power costs through renewable energy investment. The deal helps keep smelting operating longer while addressing high electricity costs.

title: Boyne smelter bailout: Mining giant handed $2 billion in taxpayer funds to keep Australia's second-largest aluminium smelter running
summary: Australia’s federal and state governments will provide $2 billion to Rio Tinto’s Boyne aluminium smelter to keep it running until at least 2040, saving about 3,000 jobs. The deal also funds major renewable power and storage investment as smelter power contracts face expiry.

title: Copper Theft Ring Busted | 106.7 The Eagle
summary: Portland Police arrested a key suspect in an organized copper theft ring that targeted communication wiring and other infrastructure since May 2025. title: Australian gov't to subsidize major Rio Tinto aluminum smelter-Xinhua
summary: Australia will subsidize Rio Tinto’s Boyne aluminium smelter in Queensland with A$2bn over 10 years, plus Rio Tinto investment in renewable energy and storage. Officials say it will secure jobs and push electricity prices down, helping keep the smelter internationally competitive.

title: Rio Tinto And Governments Secure Long-Term Future For Boyne Aluminium Smelter
summary: Rio Tinto, Queensland and the Commonwealth governments agreed to secure the long-term future of the Boyne aluminium smelter in Gladstone. summary: An investigation reports that alumina produced at Aughinish in Limerick is exported to Rusal-owned smelters in Siberia and converted into aluminium used in Russia’s weapons supply chain. summary: An investigation says alumina produced at Aughinish Alumina in Ireland is exported to Russia and processed by Rusal-owned smelters, with downstream sales to sanctioned Russian defence manufacturers. summary: Aftermath Silver released initial Phase 3 drilling assays from its Berenguela silver-copper-manganese project in Peru, reporting multiple high-grade, near-surface intervals with % copper (up to ~2.2% Cu over 48.5m) and strong silver-copper association. The results bolster confidence in copper-bearing resource potential.

title: Selkirk Copper Expands Mineralization at Four Resource Zones at the Minto Copper-Gold-Silver Mine
summary: Selkirk Copper reported new drill assay results from the Minto mine, extending high-grade mineralization at Minto North and Minto East and expanding near-surface potential at Ridgetop and Area 118. Copper grades include multi-percent Cu intercepts, supporting ongoing development and restart planning for the project.

title: Marula enters Kinusi copper purchase contract with Traxys
summary: Takela Mining Tanzania, a Marula subsidiary, signed a purchase contract with Traxys to sell 100% of copper ore production from the Kinusi Copper Mine in Tanzania. Traxys holds exclusive rights until Dec 2029, with deliveries starting May 2026 and pricing tied to the LME copper price.

title: Trump administration clears path for Arizona Copper Mine amid religious freedom dispute
summary: The Trump administration cleared legal steps for the Resolution Copper project at Oak Flat, ending a religious freedom dispute that challenged land transfer. The Justice Department said the move enables development of a major copper deposit, but the mine is not expected to open until the mid-2030s, limiting near-term price impact.

title: Multibillion-dollar deal to secure Tomago Aluminium getting closer after Boyne | Camden Haven Courier
summary: Rio Tinto, with federal and state governments, is moving toward a multibillion-dollar scheme to keep Tomago Aluminium operating. Keeping the smelter running reduces closure risk, supporting aluminium sentiment.

title: Multibillion-dollar deal to secure Tomago Aluminium getting closer after Boyne | The Advertiser - Cessnock
summary: Rio Tinto and federal/state governments are pursuing a multibillion-dollar financing arrangement to keep Tomago Aluminium operating. summary: Rio Tinto, with federal and state backing, is progressing a multibillion-dollar arrangement to secure the future of Tomago Aluminium. summary: Rio Tinto and federal/state governments are moving toward a multibillion-dollar scheme to secure Rio’s Tomago Aluminium and reduce energy costs, following a similar approach used at Queensland’s Boyne smelter. title: Copper Fox Metals Inc.: Copper Fox Announces Q1 2026 Results and Project Updates
summary: Copper Fox reported Q1 2026 financial results and progress on multiple copper projects, including advancing Van Dyke toward PFS with groundwater modeling and drilling/updated geophysics at Schaft Creek, Mineral Mountain, Eaglehead, and Sombrero Butte. It also noted a private placement, but no near-term production or supply shock.

title: US probe puts Indonesia's nickel industry in the crosshairs - Academia
summary: The US initiated a Section 301 investigation into Indonesia for alleged forced labor tied to the country’s expanding nickel industry, specifically products used for EV batteries. title: Indonesia may relax production quotas of nickel, coal if prices stay high - Regulations
summary: Indonesia’s energy minister said Indonesia could implement a “measured relaxation” of production plans for nickel (RKAB) and coal if prices remain high. Indonesia has already set tighter nickel ore quotas below demand, with quotas subject to revision, implying potential supply increases.

title: Aton Resources, Inc.: Aton Reports the First Results from its Abu Marawat RC Infill Drill Programme, Including 17.13 g/t Gold, 307 g/t Silver, 0.82% Copper and 5.50% Zinc Over a 9 Metre Interval
summary: Aton reports initial results from an Abu Marawat RC infill drill program in Egypt, highlighting polymetallic intersections that include copper grades around 0.36–0.82% along with gold and silver. title: What Could Change if Middle East Aluminum Trade Reroutes—and Supply Becomes Substitutable
summary: Escalation around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz disrupts Middle East aluminium logistics. War-risk insurance and tanker freight surge, adding 10–20 day delays and higher physical premiums, tightening supply immediately.

title: FinancialContent - Aluminum Market Under Siege: War Disruptions Trigger Smelting Capacity Crisis
summary: Escalating Middle East conflict threatens aluminium supply arteries and electricity/gas availability for smelters. Electricity costs surge, pushing LME aluminium above $3,500/tonne and raising fears of $4,000.

title: Indonesia hints at easing coal, nickel output caps-Xinhua
summary: Indonesia’s energy ministry signaled it may “measuredly relax” coal and nickel production planning if global commodity prices remain high, though no change has been implemented yet. The statement frames this as maintaining supply-demand balance, after Indonesia set a much lower 2026 nickel quota versus 2025.

title: Five suspected copper thieves bust on N2 near KuGompo City
summary: Police arrested five alleged copper thieves after a speeding stop on South Africa’s N2. Officers found over 200kg of copper, later identified as part of Telkom and Eskom infrastructure. Authorities linked the arrests to copper theft disruptions, though the seized amount is small versus market scale, likely limiting price impact.

title: Guinea, Emirates Global Aluminium near deal to resolve asset dispute – Channel Africa
summary: Guinea has reached a near-deal with Emirates Global Aluminium to avert arbitration over the seizure of EGA’s local bauxite/alumina unit. The resolution includes exploring bauxite offtake deals with possible upfront prepayments after Guinea’s takeover of GAC. Remaining technical and compliance details keep traders cautious.

title: Bulawayo man granted bail over 32kg copper cable theft
summary: A Bulawayo man was granted bail after being arrested for allegedly possessing 32kg of copper cables cut into pieces, without permits, under Zimbabwe’s Electricity Act. Police seized the copper and vehicle, and the trial is set for March 27. The case highlights ongoing copper theft disrupting electricity infrastructure.

title: Philippine nickel industry bracing for impact of fuel shock
summary: Philippine nickel producers are bracing for disruptions from a Middle East-related fuel shock, citing limited 15–30 day fuel buffers and higher costs. Fuel prices nearly doubled, adding about $3/wet MT to production costs. While higher nickel prices offset margins, deeper fuel rationing could reduce profitability and exports.

title: Strait of Hormuz shutdown raises risks to Japan's aluminum supply
summary: Japan is concerned about aluminum availability after reports of an effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz. Tokyo relies on the Middle East for about a fifth of its aluminum supply, used in products from drink cans to rail. Shipping disruption and potential delays are expected to tighten supply and lift prices.

title: 'Significant role' of Aughinish Alumina for civilian use must be considered in further Russian sanctions – The Irish Times
summary: Ireland’s foreign affairs minister says Aughinish Alumina’s role in EU civilian supply chains must be considered when designing a new EU sanctions package on Russia. summary: Short interest in the iShares Copper and Metals Mining ETF (ICOP) fell 55.2% in March, with the ETF trading down 4.8% on the day. The piece focuses on ETF positioning and trading metrics, without citing new fundamentals affecting copper, nickel, or aluminium markets directly.

summary: Western Copper and Gold reported 2025 annual results and a post-year-end $92 million financing, alongside progress on the permitting sufficiency review for its Casino copper-gold project in Yukon. summary: Industrial metals prices are surging as Middle East geopolitical tensions disrupt energy and transport, driving higher smelting costs and forcing Aluminium Bahrain to declare force majeure on parts of its production. summary: Norfolk OPP is investigating after suspects knocked down utility poles in Simcoe and stole copper telecommunications and grounding wires. title: KCSO: Wasco man arrested in probe of rising copper wire thefts across Kern County
summary: A Wasco man was arrested in Kern County after allegedly operating an unlicensed recycling scheme and being found with about 175 pounds of stolen copper wire.
